payload.description:
Issue summary: Customers reported SSE/chat streams that begin producing tokens but then stop sending any bytes for >30s without an explicit error. The client stays connected; no socket close is observed from the client side. Impact: multiple NoteHub users experienced mid-generation stalls that required them to cancel and resend prompts, impacting product UX and causing increased token replays. Environment: production us-east, dedicated cluster for NoteHub (tenant-id nh-894). Occurred 2026-03-09 22:12 - 23:45 UTC during a small traffic spike.
1) Create a long-form chat request that triggers >1000 token generation using redwood-13b-v1 via SSE streaming API
2) Route through the customer's dedicated endpoint in us-east (note: route uses edge-proxy connection pooling to backend cluster)
3) Simulate intermittent 503 from one backend worker for ~200-400ms to trigger edge pool failover
4) Observe SSE stream: initial tokens arrive, then stream becomes silent for >30s while client socket remains ESTABLISHED
Stream emits partial content and then stops sending further chunks without socket close or 5xx. Server-side worker logs show coroutine cancellation followed by no explicit release of the per-session KV cache. Edge logs show backend connection pooled socket timed out and was re-used. Retry/resume attempts from client sometimes result in duplicate session IDs and permanently paused generator coroutine on the worker node.
If a backend connection is timed out or pooled away, the platform should either gracefully resume generation on an available worker or return an explicit error to the client so the SDK can retry. No worker coroutine should be left indefinitely paused holding KV cache/state.
edge-proxy(us-east) WARN 2026-03-09T22:12:17Z connection_pool: idle timeout, reassigning socket to new request
serving-runtime(worker-7) ERROR 2026-03-09T22:12:17Z stream-session: coroutine_cancelled_for_request_id=nh-894-req-1123 reason=backend_conn_reset
serving-runtime(worker-7) INFO 2026-03-09T22:12:17Z kv-cache: lock_acquired session_id=nh-894-1123
serving-runtime(worker-7) INFO 2026-03-09T22:12:20Z kv-cache: lock_timeout_waiting_for_cleanup session_id=nh-894-1123
edge-proxy(us-east) DEBUG 2026-03-09T22:12:20Z http2: pool_reuse socket_id=abc123 reused=true
token_latency_p50 increased from 120ms to 420ms during window
sse_stream_silence_count: 37 occurrences for tenant nh-894 between 22:00-23:00 UTC
backend_503_burst: 12 spikes of 100-400ms observed
2026-03-10 03:15 - Support: validated customer reproduction with NoteHub engineer; captured pcap and SSE timeline.
2026-03-10 06:40 - SRE: correlated silence events with edge connection_pool idle_timeout log lines; hypothesized interaction between HTTP/2 pool reuse and in-flight streaming coroutines.
2026-03-10 09:20 - Runtime team: observed coroutine cancellation path that does not always run the full cleanup routine if cancellation originates from connection reset at the edge; KV cache lock can remain held leading to generator pause state.
2026-03-11 14:00 - Reproduced locally with controlled socket reset; confirmed that when edge reassigns a socket mid-stream, worker might transition to a 'paused' coroutine state if the resume handshake from edge is missing the session handshake header X-RW-Stream-Session.
Hypothesis: a) Edge pool re-use causes RST/timeout followed by reuse without performing full stream handshake; b) Runtime's stream-resume path assumes either full reconnect or full close; intermediate state leaves coroutine paused and does not emit heartbeat leading to silent stall.
Alyssa Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Opened ticket after customer call. Attached client-side capture and timestamps. Customer reports 30-90s stalls where token generation resumes only after new request.
Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Initial triage suggests edge connection_pool config and runtime coroutine cancel path are involved. Escalating to runtime oncall.
Maya Gupta (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-11: Reproduced with harness. Adding instrumentation to mark session handed-off and ensure resume handshake includes X-RW-Stream-Session. Will push debug build to staging.
NoteHub Eng (customer) 2026-03-11: We're seeing this primarily during our peak ingestion where we have many concurrent long-chat streams. Happy to test changes in a staging mirror.
Workaround (applied 2026-03-11): 1) Edge: increased connection_pool idle timeout from 10s to 45s for NoteHub tenant to reduce mid-stream socket reassignments. 2) Support: advised customer SDK to fallback to non-streaming (polling) for long jobs as short-term mitigation. Permanent fix (in progress): Runtime patch to ensure coroutine cancellation triggers full session cleanup and to make resume handshake idempotent. Edge change to ensure any socket handed to a new request performs a full stream-session handshake or returns 409 if session mismatch. Target PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1874. Follow-ups: automated test for socket-pool reuse + streaming, postmortem document and rollout plan.
payload.summary: Edge connection pool timeout leads to orphaned SSE stream coroutine and mid-generation silence

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers on private deployment (CerebriX) reported intermittent 5xx control-plane errors and repeated model-serving node re-selection. Impact observed as increased tail latency for inference calls and occasional failed request routing to serving nodes.

Impact:
- ~10-15% of requests to Redwood API return control-plane 503 or experience >2s additional latency during spike windows.
- Serving node selection (by control-plane) flips between two AZ-local endpoints every ~90s causing in-flight connection resets and KV cache warm-up penalties.

Environment:
- Private deployment behind customer-managed split-horizon DNS forwarder and corporate firewall.
- Region: us-east-1, deployment: private VPC with VPCE to control-plane.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run continuous generation load against the API (100 rps) for 10 minutes.
2) Observe intermittent 503s and increased p99 latency.
3) On control-plane, tail logs show frequent health-check failures and node eviction/reattachment.

Observations / Logs:
- Control-plane logs show repeated cache-miss and re-resolve for serving nodes: "Resolver: received 2 different answers for service.redwood.svc - switching" every ~80-100s.
- tcpdump performed by customer on forwarder captured alternating A records from two resolvers with different TTLs (60s vs 300s).
- dig +short @10.0.0.2 service.redwood.svc returned IP set A, then B on subsequent queries; dig on port 53/udp sometimes returned "Truncated" and the forwarder fell back to TCP and returned a different IP order.
- Control-plane backoff logic (designed to avoid thrash) triggered and momentarily suspended sticky routing, causing selection to re-evaluate and pick different node.

Immediate customer impact: ongoing - customers report production errors and elevated latency.

1) Initial hypothesis: upstream split-horizon DNS forwarder is returning different IP sets due to inconsistent resolver responses; control-plane treats differing answer sets as topology change and triggers rebalancing.
2) Correlation observed between DNS TTL oscillation and serving-node flaps; when TTL decreased to 60s client-side re-resolve frequency increased and exposed alternating answers.
3) Packet captures show UDP responses occasionally truncated (EDNS0 buffer size mismatch). When truncation occurs, forwarder falls back to TCP and queries a different authoritative path (via corp DNS forwarder chain) which returns a different IP ordering and TTL.
4) Control-plane currently performs an answer-set comparison to detect endpoint changes; differing order or slight TTL variations are interpreted as a substantive change.
5) Customer's forwarder has a feature that performs parallel queries to two upstream resolvers (internal authoritative and corporate resolver) and races the earliest response. This racing combined with UDP truncation/TCP fallback created non-deterministic answers.
6) Metrics: elevated control-plane re-resolve count from 12/min -> 95/min during incident windows; correlated with increase in dig truncation events and tcp retransmits.

Key artifacts attached (copied into ticket):
- excerpt of tcpdump (udp/truncation timestamps)
- control-plane resolver debug logs (timestamps and answer-sets)
- customer dig sequence showing alternating answers and TTLs

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:22 - Customer (CerebriX - ops@cerebrix.com): Provided tcpdump showing multiple DNS responses with TC=1 followed by TCP answers with different ordering. Noted that corporate resolver was recently updated to an internal RPM that enforces EDNS adjustments.
Temporary workaround: pinned service.redwood.svc to a stable IP set on customer's forwarder and increased local DNS cache TTL to 300s to reduce re-resolve frequency.
Permanent actions planned:
- Short term (patch within 72h): Change control-plane resolver logic to treat answers as a set (order-insensitive) and tolerate TTL variance up to 5% before triggering topology re-eval. (PR #7842)
- Medium term: Add optional jitter and debounce window for re-resolve-triggered rebalancing to avoid reacting to transient DNS races.
- Customer ops recommendation: align EDNS buffer size with corporate resolver and disable parallel-racing feature on forwarder if split-horizon behavior is required.
Follow-ups assigned:
- INT-4421: validate resolver canonicalization across other private customers and run a canary.
- Networking team to publish runbook: "DNS split-horizon: detection and mitigations" on Confluence.
Status: workaround applied and monitoring in place. Patch in review. Customer notified and accepting timeline.
- Added metric: resolver.answer-set-change-rate for the affected customer to detect recurrence.
- Alert: if control-plane resolve-rate > 50/min for customer => page oncall.
- Dashboard: DNS truncation events and tcp fallbacks correlated with control-plane re-resolves.
Workaround applied; fix in PR review. Monitoring enabled; customer to confirm stability for 72h before closing.
payload.summary: DNS answer oscillation from split-horizon forwarder causes control-plane backoff and serving-node selection flap

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC Parkly Labs reported intermittent P99 latency spikes (3-7x baseline) and a 20-40% drop in sustained throughput on their dedicated capacity pool. The spikes are brief (30-90s) but frequent across a 6-hour window. Impact: customer-facing inference degraded for latency-sensitive endpoints; some user requests timed out and retried, increasing load. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool in us-east-1 serving redwood-open-7b-v2 for Parkly Labs; autoscaler configured with aggressive downscale cooldown (2m) and default min_replicas=2.
1) Call Parkly Labs' reserved model route during the reported window (prod us-east). 2) Observe transient p99 latency spikes and drop in throughput in Console > Routes > Parkly-Prod > Metrics. 3) Correlate with node-level GPU attach/detach events in infra logs. Note: spikes are intermittent and harder to reproduce outside the customer's traffic pattern (short, high-frequency small-stream bursts).
- Metrics snapshot (03:12 UTC): p50 120ms, p95 420ms, p99 2.6s (baseline p99 ~350ms).
- Node events: repeated ephemeral eviction events on gpu-node-ue1-042 and gpu-node-ue1-047 at 03:05/03:08/03:11 UTC.
- Scheduler trace: preemptive allocation request from tenant id=tenant-ephemeral-981; priority tag 'batch-job' unset, landed on same rack as Parkly.
- Autoscaler logs: scale_down executed at 03:06 UTC (from 6->3 rep), then scale_up at 03:09 UTC (3->7) matching spikes.
- KV cache metrics: sudden cache misses rose 3x during spike windows.

Additional notes:
SRE on-call (Liam O'Connor): Temporarily bumped Parkly's min_replicas to 4 and set autoscaler downscale cooldown to 10m as a mitigation; customer reports reduced p99 spikes after mitigation.
Timeline: 03:00–03:30 UTC repeated P99 spikes correlated with short-lived batch training jobs launched by tenant-ephemeral-981 that saturated GPU PCIe bandwidth and triggered CUDA context flushes on shared nodes. The scheduler allowed these jobs onto nodes with active inference slots due to a missing hard-affinity label on ephemeral tenant jobs. Autoscaler misinterpreted the load pattern: short bursts caused rapid scale-down (cooldown too short) then aggressive scale-up when requests queued, producing oscillation and increasing tail latency. Evidence: node GPU utilization logs show IO saturation concurrent with high packet drops on RDMA, and the GPU process list shows large ephemeral processes (data loader workers). Investigation links: Slack #support thread (https://slack.redwood.ai/support/p/CL7J9J2), infra dashboard panels (infra.redwood.ai/d/peaky-gpu), and scheduler trace (trace_id: b3f0a8a2).
A combination of: 1) ephemeral batch/training jobs scheduled onto shared nodes (no hard tenant affinity), causing noisy-neighbor PCIe/RDMA contention and intermittent CUDA context evictions; 2) autoscaler downscale cooldown set too short, leading to reactive oscillation; 3) KV cache churn from evicted contexts increasing per-request compute and amplifying latency.
Short-term mitigations applied 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC: - Bumped Parkly min_replicas to 4 and increased autoscaler downscale cooldown to 10m to avoid rapid oscillation. - Quarantined tenant-ephemeral-981 jobs by applying temporary hard-affinity (node isolation) and throttled their scheduling. Outcome: P99 spikes reduced to ~1.3x baseline; throughput stabilized. Long-term fixes in progress: - Scheduler patch to enforce tenant-affinity labels and prevent batch jobs landing on inference nodes (PR #4821). - Autoscaler tuning: increase default downscale cooldown and add short-burst detection to avoid scaling on sub-2m transients. - Add detection alert and automated temporary pinning when KV cache evictions exceed threshold. Rollout plan: Scheduler patch staged to canary cluster 2026-03-13, full rollout 2026-03-18 after validation. Autoscaler tuning merged 2026-03-11, will be monitored for 48h.
1) Postmortem draft assigned to Devon Chen (target 2026-03-18). 2) Add a conservative default for min_replicas for latency-sensitive dedicated pools (prod policy update). 3) Implement a monitor in Console to flag short-burst oscillation patterns (pager rule). 4) Notify affected customers and provide remediation guidance for noisy tenant detection.
Mitigation successful in reducing immediate customer impact. SRE and Scheduler teams collaborating on permanent fixes. Customer (Parkly Labs) acknowledged reduced errors and requested timeline for complete fix; provided ETA and will schedule a follow-up sync.
payload.summary: Unexpected P99 latency variance traced to ephemeral training job sweep impacting dedicated pool throughput

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers report that after we enabled the new fast_pack int8 embedding pipeline in front of the reranker, rerank responses intermittently return a large number of ties in top-k (many items with identical cosine scores) and reranker p99 latency increases from ~120ms to >2s. Impact: LexiSearch search quality degraded (user-visible duplicate results) and backend tail latency caused timeouts in their UI.

Observed behaviour:
- Endpoint returns candidate lists where many top-k items have identical similarity scores (to 6 decimal places) leading to unstable ordering.
- Reranker falls back to CPU ANN path on tie-handling code path causing p99 latency spikes and occasional 502s.
- Problem started after a staged rollout (fast_pack=true) of the embeddings-service on 2026-03-08.

Environment details:
- Customer on dedicated plan (enterprise) using model alias open-embed-1024.
- Traffic flows through api-gateway -> embeddings-service (quant pack) -> indexer -> reranker.
- Observed in us-west and eu-central production regions, intermittent (approx 0.5-2% of requests).
1) Use LexiSearch test account with their dataset (shared via secure S3 link in ticket).
2) Send batch of 256 document embeddings via embeddings endpoint with header X-Embed-Pack: fast_pack and algorithm=int8.
3) Call /rerank endpoint with those embeddings and same model alias. Observe top-k equal scores and slow responses on ~1% of requests.
4) Repeat without fast_pack header (server falls back to fp16 path) — behaviour not reproduced.
5) Reproduce reliably in a canary deployment when canary has mixed replicas (some still on old packing).
2026-03-10: Initial hypothesis - int8 packing algorithm reduces dynamic range for this customer's corpus (many near-identical vectors) causing cosine similarity quantization and ties.
Reproduced in staging when mixing packed-int8 replicas with fp16 replicas — tie rate increases when some upstream replicas return packed payloads with slightly different normalization handling.
Observed that the fast_pack pipeline applies a per-shard min-max scale before int8 quantization; small differences in scaling across replicas (floating point rounding) is producing identical integer vectors after packing for different originals.
Tie-handling code in reranker falls back to an expensive CPU-based stable-sort when more than 16 exact-equal scores are present; this is the immediate driver of p99 latency spikes.
Related linked issues: SUP-331210 (embed-timestamp-drift-cache-missstorms) — customer was part of same canary cohort; may have increased cache churn.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-10: Opened ticket after customer LexiSearch reported production impact. Provided initial logs and dataset slice to Eng. Customer experiencing duplicates in top-10, p99 latency > 1.5s.
Customer (LexiSearch SRE - Jordan Park) - 2026-03-10: We saw the issue surface after the new packing flag was enabled for our tenant; disabling it returned behavior to normal. Happy to provide traffic trace and emb payloads.
Eng (Marco Liu) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced in staging. Confirmed tie rate correlates with packed-int8 path. Hypothesis: per-shard quant scale rounding causing integer collisions. Investigating whether normalization is applied pre-pack consistently.
Eng (Priya Sharma) - 2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation: added server-side post-unpack epsilon jitter to break exact ties before tie_resolver threshold; added feature flag to disable jitter for testing. Preparing PR to make tie-resolver threshold adaptive.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-12: Communicated temporary mitigation to customer; LexiSearch enabled jitter on their tenant and reported reduction in duplicates. Requested ETA for permanent fix and rollout plan.
2026-03-09T18:12:03Z embeddings-svc[replica-12] WARN QuantPack: detected high-value clustering after pack -> variance=2.3e-9
2026-03-09T18:12:03Z reranker[replica-7] ERROR tie_resolver: candidate_scores all_equal_count=48, fallback_to_cpu=true, elapsed_ms=1876
2026-03-09T18:12:03Z api-gateway TRACE req_id=abc123 status=504 downstream_timeout=true
Temporary mitigation deployed to affected canaries: server-side epsilon jitter added after unpack to break exact integer collisions (feature-flagged). A code change was merged (reranker PR #980) to make the tie-handling threshold adaptive and avoid CPU fallback for moderate equality clusters. Embeddings team opened PR #2244 to harmonize per-shard scaling and ensure normalization occurs pre-pack consistently. Next steps: staged rollout of packing fix in embeddings-service, monitor tie-rate and p99 latency, and add an integration test that simulates near-colocated vectors to prevent regressions. Customer notified and will remain on monitor for 72 hours; support to follow up for SLA credits if issue recurs.
1) Embeddings: make per-shard scale deterministic across replicas and add pre-pack L2-normalization (PR #2244).
2) Reranker: remove expensive CPU fallback path for equal-score clusters <64 and replace with fast tie-breaker that preserves determinism (PR #980).
3) Add synthetic suite test covering pack->unpack roundtrip for corpora with low variance to CI.
4) Post-deploy: monitor tie-rate, p99 latency, and customer-reported duplicates for 7 days and report back to LexiSearch.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer running Redwood Private behind a customer-managed edge proxy + HSM for signing idempotency tokens reports duplicate external tool/function executions originating from function-calling requests. The idempotency token is produced by the customer's HSM-signing flow and attached as X-Idempotency-Sig header.

Impact:
- Duplicate function calls (webhook/post) observed intermittently for high-value payments related workflows.
- Duplicates occur across both Go and Python SDK clients used by the customer.
- Customer is on a Private deployment with an on-prem edge proxy that performs header processing.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) deployed in us-east
- Customer HSM: Vault HSM-backed transit/signing
- SDKs: go-sdk v1.8.2, python-sdk v2.1.0
- Customer edge proxy: Envoy v1.28 with custom header sanitizer filter

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Client generates idempotency payload: JSON blob (request_id, ts, action, args).
2) Customer code signs payload with HSM (RSASSA-PSS, signature length ~512 bytes) and base64url-encodes signature.
3) Signature is sent in X-Idempotency-Sig header to Redwood Private endpoint via Envoy.
4) On occasional requests, the downstream Redwood runtime receives a truncated header value (first ~256 chars) and treats it as a distinct idempotency token, allowing duplicate tool invocation when client retries.

Expected behavior:
- Signed idempotency tokens should be treated as opaque strings and never truncated by proxies or any inline middleware. SDKs and server should use the full header value for deduplication.

Observed behavior:
- Envoy filter appears to truncate/normalize long header values (observed limit ~256 characters) when forwarding requests to backend.
- When truncated, the token no longer matches the original HSM-signed value; server records a different idempotency key and executes the function call again.
- Duplicates are reproducible when customer forces long signatures by switching from RS256 to RSASSA-PSS (longer output).

Relevant logs (customer-provided):
- Client send: X-Idempotency-Sig: AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAABAQC3...<512-char base64url>
- Backend received: X-Idempotency-Sig: AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAABAQC3...<truncated to ~256 chars>
- Redwood runtime trace: dedup lookup miss -> function.exec id=fn-7623 created -> webhook POST sent -> external system processed twice

Attachments provided by customer: edge proxy config snippet, HSM signing config, request/response HAR samples.

Initial hypothesis and notes:
- Likely root cause: customer-managed Envoy header sanitization and/or internal header size limits on the proxy. Could also be an HTTP/2 header compression/continuation framing bug when large header values are present.
- Possible mitigation: recommend switching to short deterministic idempotency keys (e.g., HMAC-SHA256 of payload truncated to 64 chars) or pass signature in request body rather than header. However, customer requires header approach for routing.

Next steps (in-progress):
- SRE to reproduce locally with Envoy + HSM-signed long header values (INT-2022).
- Confirm server side will treat X-Idempotency-Sig as opaque and not perform internal normalization/truncation.
- Provide guidance to customer on Envoy config to allow long headers and ensure HTTP/2 continuation frames preserved.
- If Envoy behavior is unavoidable in their environment, propose SDK guidance and code samples to produce shorter canonical idempotency tokens that still provide collision resistance.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:02 - Engineering (Runtime): Confirmed runtime has no enforced truncation on X-Idempotency-Sig. Runtime stores the header verbatim for dedupe key calculation. Strongly suspect proxy-side limit or a middleware filter configured by the customer that canonicalizes headers.
2026-03-11 11:30 - Customer (FinNova - L. Chen): We can change proxy config; please provide explicit Envoy settings to accept long headers. We prefer not to change signing algorithm quickly due to compliance. Requested recommended config and test steps.
payload.summary: HSM-signed idempotency token truncated by edge proxy on Private deployment causing duplicate function-call executions across SDKs

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customers report intermittent stalls when Redwood private deployment attempts to download large model shard objects (range GETs) over a VPCE path that traverses an on-prem IPsec/MPLS tunnel. Impact: model pulls fail or hang for minutes causing serving nodes to fail healthchecks and autoscale. Root suspicion is DF-bit interplay and PMTU discovery being blocked by an intermediate firewall appliance, creating a blackhole for large TCP segments.

Impact: Several production serving nodes entered degraded state causing increased latency and two autoscale events. Customer observed repeated chunk retries and eventual fallbacks to smaller shards which increased latency and cost.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC + VPCE to S3), on-prem termination via IPsec to a third-party WAN appliance. Artifact downloader uses ranged HTTP(S) GETs for shard streaming. VPCE configured with prefix lists and NAT/Egress appliances on customer's transit path.

Observed behavior: TCP connections for large range requests establish successfully then stall after transfer hits ~1450-2800 bytes per segment boundary depending on egress path. Packet captures show IP header DF=1 and intermittent ICMP "Fragmentation needed" (Type 3 Code 4) being produced by an intermediate device, but those ICMP packets are not reaching the client (likely filtered). When ICMP is blocked, senders retransmit and eventually time out, causing the downloader to retry smaller ranges and ultimately fail if retries exceed thresholds.

Expected behavior: Path MTU discovery should either receive ICMP PMTU messages so endpoints lower MSS/fragment appropriately, or the tunnel/egress should allow fragmentation/clear the DF bit so large shards stream successfully.

Reproduction window: Issue reproduced during a controlled test using 256MB shard GETs while toggling WAN optimizer features on the customer's edge appliance.

Attachments: pcap snippets, traceroute --mtu output, downloader logs with byte offsets and retry counts are attached in ticket attachments.
1) Deploy private agent in customer VPC with VPCE to S3 and route default egress via customer transit (IPsec).
2) Trigger model download of large shard (256MB) via Redwood artifact-downloader using ranged GETs (concurrent ranges).
3) Observe transfer progress; capture tcpdump on serving node and on the VPCE/egress device.
4) Toggle WAN optimizer / IPSec fragmentation settings on the on-prem appliance and repeat transfers to see differences.
5) Run traceroute/mtr with packet sizes and check for ICMP Type 3 Code 4 responses.
artifact-downloader.log: 2026-03-09T14:12:03Z GET /bucket/shard-0001 Range=bytes=0-4194303 200 partial content; progress stops at ~1.5MB; retry count increments.
tcpdump-serving-node.pcap.gz: packets show IP DF=1 on outbound segments; no matching ICMP reaching node; several retransmits and dup acks.
egress-appliance.log: 2026-03-09T14:12:04Z 'Fragmentation needed' sent to 10.1.2.5 but dropped by firewall upstream (ICMP blocked by policy).
traceroute-mtu: shows first hop MTU 1500, then 1400 over IPsec tunnel (ESP+FRAG mismatch).

Additional notes:
Customer (NimbusHealth): Confirmed WAN vendor recently enabled 'DF-preserve' on transit firewall as part of an optimization; rolling back that change temporarily reduces failures.
Customer (NimbusHealth): Will coordinate with WAN vendor to either allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 or enable MSS clamping on the NAT/egress device.
Hypothesis: Intermediate firewall or WAN optimizer is blocking ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages and/or preserving DF bit across tunnel encapsulation, preventing endpoints from lowering MSS leading to packet blackholing.
Evidence: PCAP shows outbound TCP segments with DF=1 and subsequent 'Fragmentation needed' logged on egress appliance but no ICMP seen on serving node capture; traceroute-mtu exposes MTU mismatch on IPsec tunnel (1400) vs host (1500).
Triage steps: reproduced with jumbo ranged GETs; toggling DF-preserve setting on customer's WAN appliance made issue appear/disappear. Reducing range size or enabling MSS clamp fixes in tests.
Related config: VPCE uses prefix list + egress NAT device that does not perform MSS clamping. IPsec tunnel uses ESP without fragmentation support at vendor default.
Temporary workaround applied: configured customer's private agent to use smaller concurrent range window (1MB) and backoff retries; this restored shard downloads for the current deploys.
Customer applied immediate mitigation with WAN vendor: enabled MSS clamping on transit NAT/egress appliance and allowed ICMP Type 3 Code 4 from the IPsec egress to propagate back to the client side.
Permanent fix options presented: 1) Configure customer edge to perform MSS clamping at tunnel ingress/egress; 2) Update IPsec/ESP tunnel to allow fragmentation or to perform fragmentation before encapsulation; 3) Greenwood (artifact-downloader) change to adaptive chunking and fallback to smaller range sizes on DF=1 detection. Customer chose option 1 + partial 3.
Related PR merged: artifact-downloader PR #412 adds adaptive chunking when repeated stalls are detected (reduces default range size from 8MB to 1MB when PMTU signals are absent). Deployed to customer's agents on 2026-03-12.
Status: Customer confirmed stable downloads after combined mitigations; monitoring window started 2026-03-12 00:00Z.
PMTU blackhole caused by DF-bit preservation across IPsec + an upstream firewall blocking ICMP 'Fragmentation needed' messages, combined with artifact-downloader default large range sizes that exceeded the effective MTU on the encapsulated path.
1) Ops: Add a small PMTU detection check in private-deploy agent boot to detect obvious MTU mismatches and recommend MSS clamping if needed.
2) Engineering: Backport adaptive-chunking downloader logic to the stable agent channel and add a configuration flag 'force_small_ranges' for emergency support overrides.
3) Support: Create KB article outlining steps for customers and WAN vendors (MSS clamping, allow ICMP type3, IPsec fragmentation settings).
4) Security/Policy: Validate that recommending ICMP allowances is acceptable for enterprise security teams and provide hardened guidance (source-limited ICMP).
5) Postmortem: Draft incident postmortem and share with customer and internal stakeholders (owner: Marco Ruiz).
payload.summary: Large artifact (model shard) download stalls over VPCE + IPsec tunnel due to DF-bit/PMTU blackhole

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers (LexiDocs, dedicated) began reporting recurring p99 latency pulses and occasional 504s on text-generation endpoints. The pattern is periodic (roughly every 7-12 minutes) and correlates with increases in request queue depth for short requests. Impact: production user-facing latency spikes and failed responses for interactive flows.

Impact:
- Intermittent p99 spikes from baseline ~220ms to 1.8-2.2s for generation endpoints.
- ~0.3% increase in 504s observed over a 3-hour window for LexiDocs traffic.
- Affects short-sequence use cases (chat/assistant).

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (customer LexiDocs) in prod us-east.
- Serving runtime v1.42.0 with continuous-batcher enabled and default alignment snapshotting enabled.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Baseline low-latency traffic of small requests (~5-20 tokens) for 5-8 minutes.
2) System enters periodic alignment snapshot cycle tied to batcher metadata (every ~8 minutes).
3) During the snapshot window, multiple short requests queue while a larger snapshot I/O and KV alignment job runs, increasing per-request wait time and generating p99 pulses.

Observed behavior:
- Periodic p99 spikes aligned to snapshot window start times in metrics.
- Traces show requests waiting in the coalescer queue for 600-1800ms before entering a microbatch.
- Snapshot job logs show brief I/O stalls and a GC spike on the batcher worker during the same interval.

Expected behavior:
- Snapshot/metadata maintenance should not cause request queuing that elevates tail latency beyond configured SLO. Maintenance should be staggered or performed off the hot path.

Initial logs/metrics references:
- Grafana dashboard: /d/serve/continuous-batcher?orgId=1&view=lexidocs-prod (p95/p99 panels)
- Traces: jaeger/trace/7f8b2e... (examples attached by customer)
- Batch worker logs: /var/log/redwood/serving/batcher-0.log lines 12430-12490 (I/O snapshot start/finish entries)

Temporary workaround offered:
- Switched LexiDocs traffic to a dedicated tenant routing policy with lower snapshot frequency (config override) which reduced the amplitude of pulses by ~60% for the short term.

Next steps requested:
- Engineering investigation to confirm root cause and provide a patch or recommended configuration.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 01:38 - LexiDocs (Customer): Confirmed rollback to previous routing config stabilized UX but wants permanent fix. Attached additional traces where p99 jumps to ~2.1s.
Hypothesis 1: Snapshot/compaction job is running synchronously on batcher main loop, briefly blocking coalescer flush and increasing queue wait time.
Hypothesis 2: GC activity on batcher worker coincides with snapshot window due to increased allocation during compaction, amplifying pause time.
Evidence collected: Time-aligned logs show snapshot:start and p99 spike within <100ms. Heap profile sampled during pulse shows temporary retention increase and a STW GC mark phase lasting ~200-400ms on the batcher worker.
Experiment: Disabled compaction in a canary fleet; observed p99 pulses disappear in canary (0 instances) and persist in control group. This supports compaction as the main trigger.
Temporary mitigation applied: Reduced snapshot frequency and added tenant-scoped scheduling so LexiDocs snapshots are offset from global windows. Reduced but did not eliminate pulses.
Planned fix: Alter compaction to run off-thread (background worker) and add randomized jitter to snapshot start times per-tenant; add defensive backpressure so metadata maintenance yields to hot request path.
Related artifacts: INT-4021 (internal instrumenting of batcher compaction), PR #2843 implements background compaction and per-tenant jitter, Confluence runbook updated for postmortem.
Risk assessment: Low-risk change if compaction moved off hot path and controlled; however need canary validation on dedicated fleets to ensure no regression in memory stability.
Monitoring additions: Add an alert for 'batcher.snapshot_queue_wait' > 500ms for 5m on dedicated customers and create a dashboard tile showing alignment-phase overlap with p99.
Work in progress - patch authored to decouple compaction from main batcher loop and introduce per-tenant jitter. Patch under review (PR #2843). Plan: canary deploy to two dedicated fleets (including LexiDocs) 2026-03-17, monitor p99 for 48h, then schedule broader rollout if stable. Post-deploy summary and postmortem to be attached to this ticket.
We identified a periodic metadata compaction job in the continuous-batching subsystem that was running on the hot path and causing short bursts of queueing for small requests. We're moving that work off the hot path and adding jitter to snapshot timing; a canary rollout is planned and we'll follow up with results and recommended permanent configuration changes.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer Vela Health (Dedicated) reports intermittent mixed-model responses and unexpected fallback to an older model variant during ongoing streaming sessions. The customer pins requests to redwood-open-13b-v2 but ~3-5% of streaming chunks are served by redwood-open-13b-v2-quant (older fallback) without an explicit routing event in control-plane logs.

Impact:
- Customers observe degraded output consistency in streamed completions (semantic differences and tokenization deltas).
- Billing anomaly: spikes in 'quant' model usage metrics leading to cost allocation confusion for dedicated capacity.
- Affects live endpoints handling health-care insurance claim summarization (high sensitivity).

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: cluster-id d-vela-west-1
- Region: us-west-2 (primary)
- Traffic pattern: HTTP/2 long-lived streaming connections (gRPC-web over H2), keepalive enabled.
- Pin config: route-level version_pin: redwood-open-13b-v2 (explicit).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Open a long-lived streaming connection over H2 with multiplexing enabled (multiple concurrent streams per connection).
2) Send a pinned chat session that requests streaming tokens for ~30+ seconds.
3) Observe that some stream events contain tokenization differences and a change in latency profile mid-session.
4) Verify control-plane route mapping via /v1/routes/{route}/history — no explicit pin change recorded around observed time.

Observed behavior:
- ~3-5% of stream frames appear to be produced by the quantized variant (lower token width, slightly different detokenization).
- Edge logs show X-Redwood-Pin: redwood-open-13b-v2 on initial request, but downstream serving logs show a missing header on certain HTTP/2 stream IDs and a fallback decision in runtime.
- No orchestrator-promote/demote events in the same minute window.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming session pinned to configured model for entire session lifetime.
- Any fallback should be accompanied by a control-plane event and customer notification when pin is lost.

Relevant logs and traces (snippets):
- edge-proxy (us-west-2) trace id: trace-0ab3c7
  "stream_id=42 header_scope=connection X-Redwood-Pin=redwood-open-13b-v2"
- serving-runtime (gpu-02) log: "stream=42 missing pin-header; routing->fallback redwood-open-13b-v2-quant"
- billing metric: quant_model_tokens/hour rose +12% during incident window (03/10 16:12-16:18 UTC)

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Recommend switching to HTTP/1.1 streaming (no multiplex) for critical flows until fix is deployed.
- Force route config: add explicit per-stream metadata header X-Redwood-Force-Pin in client to reassert pin on each stream.

Investigation notes (internal):
- Hypothesis 1: HTTP/2 stream reuse with header scope=connection vs stream causes per-stream headers (X-Redwood-Pin) to be lost when the proxy reassigns stream IDs across backend connections during connection pooling.
- Hypothesis 2: Edge-proxy's header transform module normalizes pin header to connection-scoped metadata; when reused downstream the serving-runtime reads per-stream metadata and treats missing pin as eligible for fallback routing.
- Reproduced internally by running synthetic load with h2 multiplexing and toggling header scope (found reproducer at 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC).
- Reproducer shows ~4% of streams lose the per-stream header when the proxy merges multiplexed streams onto an existing backend connection.

Root-cause (preliminary):
- Edge-proxy optimization for backend connection reuse accidentally downgrades per-stream pin headers to connection scope in certain fast-path code paths, leading serving-runtime to interpret a missing per-stream pin as 'un-pinned' and invoke fallback routing.

Proposed fix:
1) Patch edge-proxy to preserve per-stream header delivery semantics for X-Redwood-Pin and X-Redwood-Force-Pin when multiplexing (hotfix branch edge-proxy/h2-pin-preserve).
2) Add defensive check in serving-runtime: treat absence of per-stream pin only if connection-level pin absent and control-plane indicates no explicit pin for that tenant.
3) Add observability: instrument edge-proxy to emit metrics: h2.streams_lost_pin_header, h2.streams_preserve_failures.

Next steps / rollout plan:
- 2026-03-12: Deploy edge-proxy hotfix to staging and run synthetic h2-multiplexing regression suite.
- 2026-03-13: Canary deploy to us-west-2 edge nodes with gradual traffic ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) monitoring h2.streams_lost_pin_header and quant model token % for Vela Health routes.
- 2026-03-14: If metrics stable, promote to all edge nodes in us-west-2 and communicate remediation to customer.

Audit / follow-up:
- Postmortem page scheduled: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INC/pages/H2+Pin+Leak+Postmortem (owner: Evan Brooks).
- Add automated regression to CI that simulates h2 multiplexing and asserts no per-stream header loss.


Additional notes:
2026-03-10 19:22 - SRE (Evan Brooks): Reproducer built using h2load; confirmed per-stream header loss when proxy reuses backend connection. Captured packet-level trace showing header scope mismatch. Marked as potential regression in edge-proxy h2 fast-path.
2026-03-11 11:10 - Support (Riley Chen): Communicated workaround to Vela Health — switch to HTTP/1.1 or include X-Redwood-Force-Pin per-stream. Customer accepted temporary workaround; they need timeline for a permanent fix.
2026-03-12 09:30 - SRE (Evan Brooks): Deployed edge-proxy/h2-pin-preserve to staging. Regression suite shows 0.1% failure compared to 4% baseline. Proceeding to canary tomorrow after additional monitoring hooks are added.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent DNS resolution failures from model-serving nodes in their Private deployment. Failures are transient and correlate with increased traffic spikes. Impact: model pulls and control-plane name lookups intermittently time out causing model download retries and elevated latency for inference (observed 95th percentile token latency spikes).
1) In customer VPC (Finlytics prod), run repeated DNS lookups for control-plane hostnames and S3 presigned hostnames from a serving node behind the TGW-attached subnet.
2) Simulate load with concurrent model-downloads or many concurrent inference requests to raise egress rate.
3) Observe intermittent NXDOMAIN/timeout or stale A answers for a subset of queries; behavior disappears when traffic volume drops.
- Intermittent DNS timeouts and stale UDP responses for ~0.5-2% of queries during traffic surges.
- Serving nodes retry over TCP/HTTPS and eventually succeed, causing client-visible latency spikes and extra egress.
- Customer sees increased model-download retry rates and occasional gRPC stream resets tied to DNS failures.
All DNS queries to control-plane and artifact endpoints should resolve reliably; UDP responses should be routed back to the original requesting ENI and not be dropped or mismatched.
Excerpts from tcpdump on serving node (src/udp dst mismatch):
- 10:12:23.456 IP 10.50.12.34.33333 > 172.31.8.10.53: 1234+ A? cp1.redwood.internal. (45)
- 10:12:23.457 IP 172.31.8.10.53 > 10.50.12.34.33333: 1234 1/0/0 A 54.239.26.90 (61)
- 10:12:23.457 IP 172.31.8.10.53 > 10.50.12.99.33333: 1234 1/0/0 A 54.239.26.90 (61)  <-- response delivered to different source port/ENI
Customer router logs show asymmetry: reply path traversed a different attachment and hit a NAT gateway with source NAT enabled, changing source IP and hitting customer's DNS cache which rejected the unsolicited response.
- Initial hypothesis: upstream DNS server (forwarder) sending responses that do not match original source tuple due to ECMP or TGW route table asymmetry.
- Pulled TGW route tables and attachment propagation logs: found a stale route originating from a prior maintenance change that created a longer, preferred path for the return traffic for the subnet range used by serving nodes.
- NAT devices observed performing source NAT for replies when they egressed via a different path; customer's DNS forwarder discards responses if the 5-tuple doesn't match an outstanding query.
- Packet captures show consistent pattern: DNS request leaves via ENI-A, response returns via ENI-B because TGW route propagation selected a different Transit Gateway attachment for that return prefix.
- Correlation with traffic spikes: when flow hashing changed (due to increased concurrent flows) packets were more likely to take alternate attachments and hit the stale propagated route.
Short-term workaround: customer removed source NAT on the affected NAT gateway and temporarily pinned route propagation to the intended attachment for the serving subnets. This reduced failed responses to near-zero while we prepared a permanent fix.
Operational workaround: disable aggressive ECMP on the TGW attachment or apply flow-affinity rules on the customer's edge to preserve symmetric routing.
Engineering (network team) prepared two changes: 1) Clean stale propagated route entries in the customer's TGW route table (completed 2026-03-14 09:20 UTC). 2) Added validation in the control plane to detect mismatched 5-tuples for UDP responses and trigger an alert when prevalence exceeds threshold.
Status: route cleanup rolled out and customer confirms reduction in DNS failures. Follow-up PR merged to add detection telemetry (PR #6287).
If issue recurs before full remediation: 1) Temporarily disable SNAT on NAT gateway for serving subnet egress to preserve original source IP. 2) Pin TGW route propagation for the affected prefix to the primary attachment. 3) Throttle connection churn on serving nodes to avoid flow-hash rebalancing during maintenance windows.
- Platform: add TGW route-propagation audit in daily infra health check.
- SRE: add dashboard showing mismatched DNS 5-tuple rate and alert at 0.1% baseline.
- CS: notify Finlytics when next maintenance window scheduled and validate after.
- Docs: update Private Deploy runbook with symmetric-routing checklist.
payload.summary: Intermittent DNS failures: stale UDP responses due to misrouted source routes on TGW

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 401s from the Redwood private API for requests proxied through their on-prem ingress. Impact: Customer's production integration cannot complete inference calls; errors began after a recent rollout that added a long service-account assertion header. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed control plane), prod, us-east-1. Observed behavior: Requests that include a long Authorization header (service-to-service bearer token which includes a long nested JWT) receive 401 Unauthorized from the identity-proxy. The token appears truncated in the proxy logs. Expected behavior: Identity proxy should forward the full Authorization header to the auth service and validate the token, returning 200 for valid tokens. Workaround: Short-term workaround was to reduce the size of the assertion header (customer-side) and use token introspection endpoint for smaller tokens.
1) Configure private deployment with customer ingress (NGINX/HAProxy) that proxies requests to Redwood identity-proxy. 2) Attach an Authorization header containing a long bearer token (>8192 bytes) produced by the customer's token service (includes nested claims). 3) Send standard generate/chat request to Redwood API route. 4) Observe 401 response and identity-proxy logs showing 'Authorization header truncated' or token decode error.
identity-proxy[2026-03-10T14:22:10Z] ERROR token_validation.go:86 invalid token: token parsing failed: unexpected EOF
nginx[2026-03-10T14:22:09Z] upstream sent invalid response while reading response header from upstream
-- captured truncated header (authorization): 'Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6Ij...' (length reported: 4096)
-- original token length reported by customer: 12048 bytes
2026-03-10 | Support (Maya): Opened ticket after initial CS report. Requested full proxy config, ingress type, and sample failing request headers. Asked for test token and timestamp of failures.
2026-03-10 | Customer (Aurelia Eng, Jordan): Provided nginx.conf snippet and sample token. Noted failures started after their auth pump that appended long trace metadata to assertions.
2026-03-10 | SRE (Daniel): Reproduced locally using customer's token shape. Observed header truncated by nginx default buffer size. Added hypothesis: ingress is dropping/truncating headers exceeding buffer limits, leading to corrupted tokens reaching identity-proxy.
2026-03-11 | Eng (SRE): Validated that identity-proxy can accept large headers (no hardcoded limit), upstream proxies are the culprit. Opened PR to docs and runbook recommending ingress config and updated onboarding checklist for private customers.
2026-03-12 | Support (Maya): Confirmed with customer that after adjusting nginx proxy_buffer_size and proxy_busy_buffers_size per recommended values and removing appended metadata, requests are succeeding. Customer validated end-to-end traffic in prod with no 401s for >24h.
Checked identity-proxy codepath: no arbitrary header length cap found; decoding libraries return EOF when token truncated.
Reproduced with a local nginx using default large_client_header_buffers (8k per buffer). Token >8k leads to truncation in proxy_pass path.
SRE test: increased nginx large_client_header_buffers and proxy_buffer_size to 32k, and upstream requests succeed.
Observed error pattern distinct from JWKS rotation or SAML issues: token was malformed due to truncation rather than signature mismatch.
Customer ingress earlier had a vendor default that strips header segments after a specific byte length; vendor docs confirmed this behavior for legacy builds.
Related internal ticket INT-4321 created to add an ingress checklist item and automated verification for private customer deploys to detect unsafe header truncation defaults.
Root cause: Customer's ingress (NGINX with vendor defaults) was configured with insufficient header buffer sizes which resulted in Authorization header truncation for very large bearer tokens. Remediation: 1) Provided documented recommended ingress settings (large_client_header_buffers and proxy_buffer_size >= token size). 2) Customer removed non-essential metadata appended to tokens and switched to compressed token format for long assertions. 3) Added runbook entry to private-deployment onboarding: verify ingress header buffer limits and run a synthetic request with oversized token. 4) Internal follow-up INT-4321 to add an automated check in deployment scripts.
Explained issue root cause (ingress header buffer limits) and provided step-by-step mitigation. Customer implemented recommended nginx config changes and validated success. Customer accepted the fix and requested the updated docs be added to their onboarding checklist.
payload.summary: Ingress header clipping truncates Authorization bearer token for private deployment, causing 401 errors

Issue summary:
Customer reported elevated 5xx (predominantly 504) responses during a large embeddings bulk upload. Error rate started at ~14:22 UTC and persisted for ~45 minutes, coincident with a spike in retry traffic from the customer's client. Impact: multiple embedding jobs failed, delays for downstream inference consumers, and increased costs due to amplification.

Impact:
- ~40% of the customer's requests returned 504 during the window.
- Other tenants on the same Dedicated pool saw latency bumps but lower error rates.
- Business impact: delayed ML pipeline runs for Noteable Analytics (non-prod downstream jobs also affected).

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (shared GPU pool)
- Region: us-west-2 (prod)
- Customer: Noteable Analytics (dedicated tier)
- Affected models: text-embedding-3-small (primary), fallback embedding-1b-quant

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Customer ran a bulk embeddings upload: 24k texts in 200-file parallel multipart batches with client concurrency=200.
2. Several individual batch requests hit 30s client timeout and retried immediately with exponential backoff but effectively very tight (no jitter).
3. Retries amplified request rate to the API gateway and upstream runtime; queues filled and connections entered TIME_WAIT.
4. Serving runtime threadpool reached saturation and started returning 504s as requests timed out waiting for worker availability.

Relevant logs / metrics / traces:
- APIGW 5xx rate graph: spike at 14:22 UTC from 1.2% -> 38% for the customer's route (link: https://dash.redwood.ai/apigw/graph?range=1h&panel=5xx).
- Runtime busy workers: worker_util peaked at 98%, queue_latency increased from 12ms -> 620ms.
- Kernel socket backlog (netstat): SYN_RECV queue grew; ephemeral port exhaustion warnings in edge proxies.
- Runtime logs: repeated "worker threadpool exhausted" entries and "dispatch timeout - returning 504".
- Customer-provided client logs show repeated immediate retries (no jitter) after 30s timeouts.

Initial hypothesis:
- Client-side retry amplification combined with heavy multipart batching overwhelmed the gateway and upstream runtime.
- Runtime inability to shed load quickly caused queue growth and timeouts rather than graceful backpressure.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Support requested that the customer back off concurrency to <= 16 and enable jitter on client retries (applied at 14:37 UTC).
- We applied a quick ingress rate cap for the customer's tenant on the API gateway (soft cap) at 14:40 UTC to reduce immediate pressure.
- Restarted two runtime workers on the affected Dedicated pool to clear threadpool leaks (rolling restarts 14:45–14:50 UTC).

Current state: partial stabilization as of 15:05 UTC. Error rate dropped to ~3% for the customer's route; background tail latency remains elevated while caches warm and connection pools recover.
2026-03-10T14:28:00Z - Aisha Khan (Support): Received alert from customer: their embedding job failures started at ~14:20 UTC. Attached customer logs. Investigating APIGW and runtime metrics.
2026-03-10T14:33:00Z - Miguel Torres (SRE): Observed APIGW 504 spike for Noteable tenant. Runtime threadpool shows sustained saturation. Opening INC-98765 to track infrastructure side. Pushing to triage and will look at ingress shedding options.
2026-03-10T14:38:00Z - Aisha Khan (Support): Recommended customer reduce concurrency and add jitter to retries; they implemented client change and reported transient improvement. Requested them to keep job throttled while we stabilize.
2026-03-10T14:42:00Z - Diego Rios (Runtime Team): Confirming we see "dispatch timeout" logs and socket backlog. Proposing rolling restart of two affected runtime pods and temporary per-tenant soft rate limit. Filing PR to adjust default keepalive/window settings for high-concurrency tenants (see related_github_prs).
2026-03-10T15:10:00Z - Miguel Torres (SRE): Post-mitigation check: APIGW 5xx dropped from ~38% -> ~3%. Still tracking lingering long-tail latencies and connection churn. Marking action items in ticket.
2026-03-10T15:45:00Z - Customer (Noteable Analytics): Confirmed bulk job mostly completed after lowering concurrency. Asking for guidance on recommended client settings and whether Dedicated pool needs resizing to avoid recurrence.
2026-03-11T09:20:00Z - Aisha Khan (Support): Follow-up: scheduled call with Noteable for 2026-03-12 to review best practices and propose autoscaler/tenant-quota adjustments.
14:25 UTC: APIGW trace shows hundreds of retries from the same source IPs; correlation with customer's upload job confirmed.
14:28 UTC: Runtime metrics indicate worker_pool.queue_length increased 50x compared to baseline; internal eviction policy not aggressive enough to shed excess requests before timeouts.
14:35 UTC: Edge proxy reports ephemeral port exhaustion warnings; increasing keepalive reuse would help but longer-term fix required.
14:40 UTC: Applied soft per-tenant ingress cap; observed immediate rate smoothing at APIGW layer.
Relevant links: APIGW dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/apigw/graph?panel=5xx; Runtime traces: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/abcd-embed-bulk
Workaround implemented: advised customer to reduce concurrency to <= 16 and enable exponential backoff with jitter; implemented soft per-tenant cap and rolled two runtime workers to clear threadpool state.
Fix plan (short term): Adjust default per-tenant ingress soft limits for Dedicated customers who run large bulk jobs; add client best-practice guidance to Support KB. Assigned INT-4412 to infra to evaluate ingress default caps.
Fix plan (medium term): Improve runtime load-shedding behavior so requests are rejected earlier (503) rather than queued to timeout; add metrics to detect retry amplification patterns and trigger automated throttles. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2794.
Follow-ups: 1) Call scheduled with Noteable Analytics on 2026-03-12 to review recommended client configuration and discuss Dedicated pool sizing. 2) Post-incident postmortem to be written in Confluence and linked here.

Issue summary:
Customers running long prompts with multi-cookie auth headers observe two correlated failures in prod us-west: (1) streaming responses stall after several seconds of tokens and client sees connection hang (no final chunk) and (2) some requests receive 431 Request Header Fields Too Large prior to any token being emitted. Impact: BrightChat reports degraded UX for chat sessions (timeouts and partial responses) impacting ~12 sessions/hour for the last 36 hours.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-west (ALB fronting nginx edge -> api-gateway -> regional edge proxy -> serving runtime). Dedicated capacity.
- Typical request: streaming chat completion, prompt size ~6k tokens, Authorization header includes multiple cookie-like fields from customer SSO reverse-proxy (~9kb total header size).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a streaming chat request with a long system + user prompt (~6k tokens) and include the same aggregated auth headers observed in customer requests (Authorization + X-Forwarded-Client-Cookies combining multiple cookies totaling ~9kb).
2) Observe connection behavior for streaming: tokens start streaming, then stall for >15s with no data; client eventually times out.
3) Re-run more times: some runs return 431 immediately instead of starting the stream.

Observed behavior & logs:
- nginx edge logs show 431 responses with "Request Header Or Cookie Too Large" for a subset of requests.
- ALB logs show intermittent 502s when the edge times out while proxying large streamed responses, but on analysis many 502s align with the streaming stalls (connection closed mid-stream).
- api-gateway and region proxy traces show long idle periods during streaming where no bytes are forwarded for ~10-20s before a TCP teardown.
- No errors in serving runtime application logs; runtime reports continued generation but with low bytes forwarded to the client.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Large aggregated headers are exceeding nginx buffer limits causing immediate 431 in some cases. Verified by adjusting client header sizes locally reproduces 431.
- Hypothesis 2: Proxy buffering settings (proxy_buffer_size / proxy_busy_buffers_size) + connection idle timeout on ALB cause mid-stream stalls. The proxy appears to buffer bursts; when buffer churn coincides with keepalive timeouts between edge and gateway, the upstream stream is torn down while runtime continues to produce.
- Correlation found between requests that initially pass header checks but produce >8KB of initial chunked headers and later stall; suggests header rewriting or cookie consolidation at the edge increases header footprint.
- Related internal ticket SUP-29412 documented a prior increase of default nginx proxy_buffer_size in a canary in Feb; that change may be insufficient for high-cookie auth patterns.

Workarounds already applied:
- Customer temporarily removed cookie aggregation so their auth header is smaller (reduced 431 rate).
- Support toggled keepalive timeout on a trial edge instance to 60s for a small cohort, which reduced stall frequency for that set but is not a safe global change without load testing.

Next steps / recommended remediation:
1) SRE to raise nginx large_client_header_buffers and proxy_buffer_size on edge for us-west canary; validate against load and memory footprint.
2) Add defensive guard: reject >8KB headers at api-gateway with a clearer 4xx and guidance to clients to shrink auth payloads rather than letting proxy buffering lead to stalls.
3) Investigate ALB idle timeout vs edge keepalive interplay; consider aligning to a higher value for streaming customers or enabling TCP-level keepalive for proxied connections.
4) Instrument proxy to emit per-request buffer-churn metrics and sample body/flow traces to correlate stalls with buffer thresholds.
5) Update runbook and surface guidance in onboarding docs for customers using SSO cookie consolidation.

Requested by customer: rapid mitigation and longer-term config changes to prevent regressions and clearer guidance on supported header sizes for streaming workloads.

Additional notes:
Mitigation in progress: canary buffer increases reduced incidents; customer routing test requested. Permanent rollout pending load testing and runbook updates.
Edge nginx default buffer limits combined with ALB/keepalive timeout interactions; large aggregated auth headers from customer SSO and proxy cookie consolidation pushed requests into buffer thresholds leading to 431s or mid-stream proxy resets.
Follow-ups: schedule phased rollout, implement header-size rejection with customer guidance, add metrics for buffer churn. Owner: Diego Rivera.
payload.summary: Streaming stalls mid-response and intermittent 431 responses when requests use large auth headers

Issue summary:
During an incremental canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 in us-west, the customer (BrightAssist AI) reported a rise in cross-variant fallback responses where traffic pinned to the new canary model intermittently routed to an older model. This coincided with our recent session-token rotation job running during the same maintenance window.

Impact:
- ~2% of requests from a subset of pinned sessions returned responses from the fallback model (open-llama-7b-q4_0) instead of the pinned canary.
- Customer reports degraded QA metrics for conversation continuity and higher token costs.
- Incident impacted a single dedicated region (us-west) and affected several long-running user sessions.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (BrightAssist AI) on prod us-west
- Serving runtime: v3.8.1
- Edge/session proxy: session-proxy v1.14
- Canary rollout: incremental (10% -> 25%) over 2026-03-10 02:00-04:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 with session-affinity preserved.
2) Trigger session-token rotation job (automated security task that rotates session tokens/leases).
3) Long-running sessions that received a pinned token experienced token refresh mid-stream.
4) Some edge nodes rejected rotated token headers causing a re-authorization path that did not carry the pin metadata.
5) Requests without pin metadata were routed by policy to the fallback (older) model under burst constraints.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent 200 responses that contained outputs inconsistent with the canary variant (style/stop-words matched older model).
- No 5xx errors; routing decision led to expected but unwanted variant responses.
- Session logs show header rewrite/drop on specific edge-proxy instances.

Expected behavior:
- Session-token rotation should preserve pin-coherence: rotated tokens must retain or re-associate the session-level pin metadata so requests remain pinned to the intended model variant.

Attachments/Logs:
- tail of session-proxy logs (errors showing header validation mismatches) attached in ticket thread.
- Route coordinator traces showing decision tree for sample session IDs.
- Customer provided transcripts highlighting semantic divergence.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 - SRE on-call (Arjun Patel): Reproduced header drop on edge-proxy instance ep-12. Suspect token rotation handshake timing race. Captured pcap and traces.
2026-03-11 - Routing eng (Lars Becker): Confirmed some requests lost pin metadata after token refresh; edge-proxy returned 200 but omitted x-session-pin header before proxy->coordinator hop. Investigating why proxy didn't reattach pin after reauth.
2026-03-12 - Session proxy eng (Nina Alvarez): Found a bug in session-proxy v1.14 where rotated-token code path mistakenly clears temporary metadata when auth returns 204 (no-body). Preparing hotfix branch.
2026-03-12 - Customer (BrightAssist AI - ops): Confirmed symptom window matches their internal maintenance window. They've applied a temporary mitigation (pause canary expansion) and requested ETA for fix.
2026-03-13 - Support (Maya Chen): Escalated to PM for coordination on patch rollout and asked customer if they can accept a staged patch on their dedicated nodes tonight.
2026-03-13 - Engineering (Lars Becker): Hotfix PR opened and smoke tests green in staging. Planning a targeted restart of session-proxy fleet in us-west for 2026-03-13 22:00 UTC. Scheduled rollback if regressions observed.
Hypothesis 1: session-token rotation handshake returns a 204 (no-content) path that clears ephemeral headers; session-proxy code treats 204 as success and does not rehydrate pin metadata.
Hypothesis 2: route-coordinator relies on x-session-pin header strictly from edge; if header absent, it applies fallback policies even when a server-side session store contains pin data. Some requests short-circuited coordinator lookup due to cache TTL mismatch.
Evidence: packet traces show auth response sequence where rotated token accepted but edge-proxy emitted downstream request without x-session-pin for ~15s window on ep-12 and ep-17. Route coordinator logs show fallback path invoked for those requests.
Repro steps validated in staging by invoking rotation job concurrently with simulated canary traffic; saw identical header loss on session-proxy image with v1.14 but not on v1.13.
Scope estimate: ~2-3% of active pinned sessions in rollout cohort experienced at least one fallback call in the observed window. No data loss or secret exposure observed.
Risk assessment: fix is low-risk code change to session-proxy rehydrate path but requires coordinated restart of edge nodes to pick up fix in dedicated customer environment.
Workaround (customer applied): Pause canary expansion and instruct client to reconnect affected sessions to force rebind; this immediately reduced cross-variant fallbacks to <0.1%.
Fix deployed: session-proxy hotfix v1.14.1 released that preserves and reattaches x-session-pin after token rotation when auth returns 204. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/session-proxy/pull/331
Rollout plan: staged restart of us-west session-proxy instances in waves of 5% to limit interruption. Completed 2026-03-13 23:15 UTC. Smoke tests and customer validation passed.
Verification: Post-deploy traces show no header loss during rotation; monitored pinned-variant hit-rate for cohort improved from ~98% to >99.9% within 30 minutes.
Follow-ups: (1) Add an end-to-end test for token rotation + pin preservation in our canary harness. (2) Update runbook to avoid running token rotation jobs during canary expansions for dedicated customers until automated canary-friendly rotation is implemented. (3) Add observability metric for x-session-pin drops at edge-proxy.
Communication: Notified customer of fix and closure steps; recommended resuming canary expansion after confirmation window. Ticket to be closed after 48h of stable metrics.
payload.summary: Session token rotation interferes with pin coherence during incremental canary causing cross-variant fallbacks

payload.description:
Issue summary:

Customer FinSight Labs reported intermittent mixed-generation outputs after a scheduled canary promotion on their dedicated capacity pool in us-east. Customer had pinned production route to open-llama-13b-quant-v1 but observed ~2-5% of requests temporarily routed to v2 and to a degraded fallback variant during the canary window.

Impact:
- Affecting ~3k requests/min for the customer during the canary window (P1 business impact).
- Some user sessions received inconsistent outputs (different model behaviors) and transient latency spikes (p50 doubled for affected requests).

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (g5dn-like) serving FinSight Labs tenant in us-east.
- Route config: model pin to v1, canary slice enabled (5% weight), prewarm probes enabled with immediate qualifier probe sequence.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Schedule a weighted canary promoting open-llama-13b-quant-v2 to 5% while keeping route pinned to v1.
2) Enable prewarm + qualifier probes (default immediate sequence).
3) Observe through customer telemetry and SDK traces over 10 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- During prewarm and qualifier window, some requests had model affinity flip to v2 or a degraded fallback for a short window (~20-90s) despite the explicit pin.
- Edge and orchestrator traces show qualifier probe ACKs arriving out-of-order relative to probe dispatch; snapshot commit for cohort reassigned before the pin handshake completed.

Expected behavior:
- Prewarm/qualifier probes should preserve explicit pin for pinned routes; probe ACK ordering should not cause a cohort snapshot commit that rebinds routing cohorts mid-handshake.

Logs / telemetry pointers:
- Orchestrator logs (orchestrator-2026-03-10-13:22) show probe_ack timestamps: 13:22:03 -> probe for v2, 13:22:02 -> probe for v1 (out-of-order), with commit id mismatch 0x1f4a/0x1f4b.
- Edge traces (edge-proxy-us-east-3) show X-Canary-Qualifier: seq=42, seq=41 for concurrent probes.
- Console: token-level latency spike correlated to probe window.
- Customer supplied SDK logs: request_ids: [finsight-req-00023, finsight-req-00047].
2026-03-10 13:35 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged receipt. Opening investigation with SRE and Eng. Provided customer temporary mitigation steps (disabled prewarm qualifier).
2026-03-10 14:10 - SRE (Marco Chen): Reproduced ordering anomaly in staging when prewarm probe fanout > 20. Observed ack reorder under burst probe fanout. Collecting orchestrator and edge pcap for root cause.
2026-03-11 09:02 - Eng (Lena Ortiz): Hypothesis: orchestrator probe scheduler uses parallel workers that don't preserve logical sequence IDs under retry/backpressure; snapshot commit path doesn't verify in-flight handshake for pinned cohorts. Creating PR to enforce in-order ack handling.
2026-03-11 16:40 - Customer (J. Alvarez, FinSight): Confirmed that disabling qualifier probe eliminated mixed outputs during the next canary test. Wants ETA for permanent fix and asks about retroactive billing impact from degraded fallback calls.
Collected packet captures and orchestrator trace logs from us-east nodes for the 13:20-13:25 window.
Found that when probe concurrency exceeded worker pool size, ack responses were processed by different ack-handlers without seq check, allowing later probes to commit earlier probe's snapshot (race).
(Related) observed prewarm mirror on standby nodes sometimes replied before primary edge due to cached mirror state, creating perceived out-of-order ACKs.
Reproduced in internal load test: enabled canary qualifier with 50 concurrent prewarm probes -> ~4% of traffic experienced transient cohort rebind and fallback to degraded variant.
Telemetry: cohort_snapshot_commit_rate increased with probe concurrency; commit rollback events tied to commit id mismatch logs.
Workaround applied (2026-03-10 15:00): disabled qualifier probes for FinSight route and set canary_weight to 0 temporarily. Patch deployed to staging (orchestrator PR 6789) that adds seq validation to probe-ack path and holds commit until handshake completion. Patch rolled to prod us-east on 2026-03-12 02:20 behind a staged rollout (staged by region). Monitoring shows no recurrence in follow-up tests. Billing: fallback requests were within committed reserved capacity; CS to coordinate with finance if customer requests credit. Follow-ups: full postmortem and recommended change to prewarm concurrency default (reduce default fanout and add in-order ack enforcement).
Complete postmortem and share with customer (owner: Marco Chen) by 2026-03-18
Adjust default prewarm qualifier fanout and add a config toggle to force sequential prewarm for pinned routes (owner: Release Eng)
Add automated test that simulates high probe concurrency and asserts commit id monotonicity (owner: Test Infra)
CS to open billing review if FinSight requests credit (owner: Rachel Moore)
Link permanent fix PR to changelog and release notes for Dedicated customers (owner: Product)

Issue summary:
Customer NimbusHealth reports that the 'User conversion' funnel panel on their org dashboard intermittently shows all zero counts for multi-hour ranges immediately after nightly retention compaction runs. This affects billing-tracked conversion metrics and has caused missing alerts for conversion-rate drops.

Impact:
- Several teams at NimbusHealth rely on the funnel card to measure daily onboarding conversion; values show 0s for windows that previously had non-zero traffic.
- Alerting tied to the funnel (conversion_rate < 3%) did not fire because the dataset collapsed to zeros rather than being marked as partial/unknown.
- Customer is enterprise tier and expressed operational impact to their analytics deliverables.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east region (org: nimbushealth-prod, console org id: org_8349)
- Affected dashboard: "Acquisition -> Onboarding Funnel" (panel id 42)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Open the funnel dashboard for org_8349 during UTC window immediately after nightly retention compaction (approx 03:30-04:30 UTC).
2) Select time range: Last 24h and apply event filters for "signup_completed" -> "account_verified" steps.
3) Observe counts displayed in funnel and check raw query via "View underlying query".
4) Compare same panel before compaction (e.g., previous day) and after compaction.

Observed behavior:
- Funnel card displays 0 for each step for some time after compaction.
- Raw underlying query returns empty rows in console despite ingestion metrics showing events present in storage and downstream billing counts.
- Alerts suppressed; no entries in alert history for the expected triggers.

Expected behavior:

Issue summary: Customer observed increased 95th/99th token latency and sporadic streaming disconnects immediately after we enabled an adaptive batching experiment for their tenant (coalesce_small_reqs=true, adaptive_grouping=aggressive) and a matched experimental quant profile (q8_dyn_prefetch). They requested guidance for a safe unwind: minimal customer disruption, no model-quality regressions, and a reproducible verification checklist.
Several production routes for BrightHealth AI show 95p latency up from ~180ms to 750-1200ms and periodic client stream resets. Traffic is on Dedicated pool assigned to the customer; estimated 12% of user-facing requests affected. Business impact: user timeouts and degraded UX for conversational flows; P1 SLA breach risk.
1) Tenant uses dedicated pool with tenant_id bhai-prod-42.
2) Apply optimizer profile: {coalesce_small_reqs: true, max_batch_wait_ms: 15, adaptive_grouping: aggressive, quant_profile: q8_dyn_prefetch}.
3) Replay synthetic production load (mix of short prompts and streaming long generations).
4) Observe that small concurrent requests are coalesced into heterogenous batches; KV cache thrash observed on serving nodes leading to tail amplification and occasional stream disconnects.
Excerpt from serving-runtime trace (us-east-1, node rwd-srv-11):
[2026-03-13T09:34:12.412Z] TRACE request-id=rcst-7b3a: batch-size 18 coalesced (heterogeneous seq lengths)
[2026-03-13T09:34:12.415Z] WARN kv-cache: evict: tenant=bhai-prod-42 key-prefetch-miss=0.86
[2026-03-13T09:34:12.419Z] ERROR stream: write error: upstream reset by peer (timeout)
[2026-03-13T09:34:12.422Z] PERF token-latency: p95=980ms p99=1.24s
Support captured a console trace and attached the tenant traffic sample in case file: rwd-trace-bhai-20260313.log
Initial hypothesis: the combination of aggressive coalescing and dynamic quant prefetching is causing cache eviction churn. Small requests are being combined with long-context streams producing heterogeneous batch padding; quant prefetch is populating ephemeral weights/kv entries that push hot KV entries out. This increases backend deserialization/rehydration costs and spikes tail latency.
Evidence: correlated spikes on kv-cache eviction metric and an increase in deserialization time in kernel selection traces. No model weights OOMs reported.
Triage steps performed: rolled traffic from 100% to 80% steady and split 20% to canary with conservative profile (coalesce_small_reqs=false, q8_static). Canary shows p95 back to normal.
Open hypothesis: async quant prefetch interacts with coalescing by prefetching per-batch quant tables for long-sequence items, causing eviction for recently-accessed short-context items. We need a safe unwind that avoids immediate mass rollbacks that could cause cold-start penalty for long-running conversations.
2026-03-13 10:02 - Support (Evelyn Carter): Received report from customer, reproduced in sandbox with replay. Noticed consistent kv-cache evictions when coalescing is enabled.
2026-03-13 11:10 - SRE (Ravi Menon): Recommended splitting traffic to canary and disabling coalesce_small_reqs for the tenant as quick mitigation. Prepared rollback checklist and snapshot plan.
2026-03-13 11:48 - Customer (BrightHealth AI, product lead - Anika Rao): Asked for minimal interruption plan; cannot take a full restart during business hours. Requests guidance for staged unwind and verification.

Monitoring shows p95 returning to ~210ms.
2026-03-14 09:00 - Customer (Anika Rao): Verified on their end; user-facing timeouts resolved for sampled flows. Asked for postmortem and follow-up mitigation to safely re-run experiment.
Workaround applied: staged unwind executed by SRE on 2026-03-14. Specific actions: (1) tenant-level toggle coalesce_small_reqs=false; (2) quant profile fallback to q8_static for new sessions via routing policy; (3) enabled transient traffic-split to keep 10% traffic on conservative canary for 2 hours for validation; (4) warmed KV cache using shadow replays for active conversations to avoid cold starts.
Outcome: p95 and p99 latencies returned to acceptable range; streaming disconnects stopped.
Follow-ups: (a) Engineering to instrument per-tenant KV eviction metrics more granularly and add alerting for eviction > 0.6 sustained over 5m. (b) Research to add coalesce-awareness to quant-prefetch (avoid per-batch prefetch for heterogeneous batches). (c) Support to prepare a tenant-facing runbook describing staged unwind steps.
