Issue summary:
Customer (DataSort Inc.) reports sudden 429 spikes for a subset of API keys over the last 18 hours. Spike correlates with a background service that refreshes signed URLs for archived embedding files. Impact: multiple ingestion pipelines see repeated 429s for short durations (~20-60s), causing downstream backfills to fail and triggering support SLA.

Observed behavior:
- 429s appear in waves across many clients that share the same tenant, not all API keys.
- Requests are clustered around file download and file-metadata endpoints used by the signed-url refresher.
- Throttle headers indicate token window exhaustion on the tenant layer (tenant token-bucket) despite per-key accounting showing low steady usage.

Customer impact:
- Backfill jobs fail with exponential retry amplification.
- ML feature pipelines lag by 2–6 hours.

Business impact:
- Enterprise customer on an SLA contract; needs root cause and mitigation within 48 hours.
1) Deploy a worker that calls PUT /v1/files/refresh-signed-url for N objects with no jitter in a tight loop.
2) Use 200 short-lived API keys (rotate per worker) tied to the same tenant.
3) Trigger a simultaneous refresh cycle across workers.
4) Observe 429s returned from API gateway and tenant-level throttle metrics incrementing in bursts.
Selected log excerpts (redacted keys):
- 2026-03-10T11:22:10Z api-gw[us-east] WARN tenant=dsinc tokens_left=0 window_ms=1000 route=/v1/files/refresh-signed-url status=429
- 2026-03-10T11:22:12Z rate-limiter DEBUG tenant_bucket_account tenant=dsinc added=+450 counted=+450 total_window=1000ms
- 2026-03-10T11:22:13Z proxy-pool INFO backend=fileservice node=files-12 request_id=abcd123 cohort_size=180
- 2026-03-10T11:22:50Z worker[dsinc-refresh] ERROR retry attempt=6 last_status=429 message="exponential backoff triggered"
Hypotheses considered:
- Health checks or monitoring probes incrementing tenant quota (low likelihood; probe traffic pattern doesn't match).
- Duplicate accounting from proxy pool fanout where a single logical refresh is translated into parallel backend requests and each is double-counted at tenant layer.
- Short-lived API key rotation causing many fresh keys to bypass per-key smoothing and hit tenant token window simultaneously.

Findings:
- Rate-limiter tracing shows the tenant-level refill is applied per proxy connection, and our proxy-pool spread (cohort_size ~180) produced near-simultaneous accounting updates.
- Auth logs confirm ~150 distinct ephemeral keys created by the customer's refresh service in a 15s window.
- Downstream backoff logic in the customer's worker is aggressive (no jitter), causing burst amplification.
- Console metrics: tenant_burst_count spike aligns exactly with signed-url refresh schedule (cron at HH:22).

Temporary mitigation performed:
- Applied a 30-minute tenant quota bump to prevent further production impact (noted in billing).
- Instructed customer to enable jitter and reduce parallelism to <=8 workers per refresh job.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:40 - Customer (DataSort platform): Provided architecture diagram and worker code snippets showing no jitter and 200 parallel refresh threads.
2026-03-11 09:12 - SRE (Priya Menon): Noted a proxy-pool accounting double-count path in logs; created github PR to add dedupe tag for proxy-originated internal fanout (see related PR).
Workaround and short-term fix:
- Customer implemented jittered backoff and reduced parallelism; immediate reduction in burst 429s observed.
- Support applied temporary tenant quota increase until permanent fix deployed.
Permanent fix and follow-up:
- Merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/1284 to ensure proxy-pool fanout updates aggregate for tenant accounting instead of naive per-connection increments (deployed to prod us-east 2026-03-12 02:45 UTC).
- Added server-side smoothing for ephemeral-key bursts (smoothing window increased from 500ms to 2s for tenant layer).
- Created runbook entry and a new alert rule for high short-window tenant bursts.
- Billing note: temporary quota bump recorded and will be reconciled with customer finance.
Follow-ups (action items):
- Engineering to verify no regression in per-route fairness after smoothing (owner: Priya Menon, due 2026-03-20).
- Product to propose console UX to show "ephemeral-key burst detection" for enterprise tenants (owner: Leila Chen, due 2026-04-01).

Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12 14:05 UTC, BeaconHealth's dedicated pool in us-west-2 experienced a sustained p50/p99 throughput plateau for 40+ minutes despite overall cluster capacity appearing sufficient. Impact: customer observed ~30% drop in completed token throughput for batched /generate requests and increased queueing. The problem correlated with many short-lived GPU attaches and fragmented slot allocation across hosts. Initial hypothesis: a noisy background workload (ephemeral debug/training jobs from another tenant) caused frequent small allocations and KV cache churn; autoscaler cooldown and min-replicas configuration prevented quick consolidation, causing slot fragmentation and prolonged throughput plateau.
1) Reproduce workload shape: submit a steady stream of medium-length batched inference requests (~1k requests/min, avg seq_len 1024) to a dedicated pool pinned to BeaconHealth's tenant.
2) Inject many short-lived attach/attach-release operations from a separate tenant (simulate ephemeral debug jobs with ~10s lifetimes, 50-100 parallel short streams) on the same dedicated cluster.
3) Observe allocator logs and slot distribution via /debug/allocator and Grafana (batch-slot-utilization, gpu-attach-rate). Expect slot fragmentation and small-slot holding behavior.
Selected artifacts: grafana: /d/redwood/dedicated-pool-usw2?from=2026-03-12T13:30:00Z&to=2026-03-12T15:00:00Z (panels: slot-fragmentation, attach-rate, kv-cache-evictions); allocator log excerpt: '2026-03-12T14:07:21Z WARN slot_manager: small-slot-hold host=usw2-host-17 slot_count=3 fragmentation=0.78 tenant=beacon-health'; autoscaler events: 'scale_down deferred due to cooldown, target_replicas=4 current=6 last_scale_event=2026-03-12T13:58:09Z'; request traces: increased queueing at queue-service p95 ~420ms -> 1.2s.
- Observed high attach/release churn from tenant 'dev-sandbox-7' coincident with throughput drop. Slack thread #support: tldr in thread (https://slack.redwood/support/threads/CFJ9kLq2).
- KV cache eviction rate doubled during event, causing many requests to re-run warmup phases and increasing effective per-request GPU time.
- Autoscaler had a 10m cooldown and min_replicas configured to 4 for the pool. When ephemeral attaches freed fragmented slots, autoscaler didn't consolidate because cooldown prevented downsizing/upsizing quickly; this left many hosts with underfilled slots.
- Host-level metric nvlink_io_wait spiked on 5 hosts, matching small-stream I/O bursts from ephemeral jobs. PCIe saturation signs noted on hosts running both debug jobs and customer streaming workloads.
- Hypothesis validated: noisy short-stream tenant caused I/O noise and slot fragmentation; autoscaler cooldown prevented rapid rebalancing; scheduler/allocator favored fairness per-tenant which prevented preemption of tiny attaches.
Mitigations applied during incident:
1) Temporarily isolated 'dev-sandbox-7' by moving its pods to a different reserved pool (config change + drain), eliminating the noisy background attaches.
2) Reduced autoscaler cooldown to 90s for the affected dedicated pool and increased prewarm worker target from 2 -> 6 to reduce warmup penalty.
3) Adjusted allocator tuning to prefer consolidation when fragmentation>0.6 and combined small-slot holders under eviction policy to free contiguous slots.
Outcome: throughput returned to baseline within ~12 minutes of isolation; p99 queueing returned to normal levels and KV-eviction rate normalized.
- Engineering action item: autoscaler: add 'burst-mode' override that temporarily relaxes cooldown when attach-rate delta > X for replicated dedicated pools (PR opened gh-redwood/autoscaler#209).
- Ops: add a Prometheus alert (attach_rate_churn > threshold) to trigger automated tenant isolation or notify SRE.
- Product: document recommended tenant best-practices for dedicated pools (avoid ephemeral training/debug loads on shared physical hosts).
- Runbook: update dedicated-autoscale-playbook with consolidation play and prewarm knobs.
For impacted customers: suggestion to set a minimum 'isolation' tag on critical tenants to ensure physical separation from ephemeral workloads; temporary fix applied for BeaconHealth by applying isolation tag.

Issue summary: Customer reports that a short, high-volume traffic spike at 2026-02-17T22:13:00Z did not surface as an alert in Console despite configured threshold (95th percentile token latency > 350ms over 5m). Impact: customer SLO was violated for a paid endpoint; on-call and customer engineers were not notified. Environment: production us-east ingestion cluster. Observed window is immediately after a scheduled retention compaction job.

What happened: LumenOps observed a 4-minute burst of requests generating heavy per-route metrics. Our evaluation job that computes windowed percentiles reported no spike for that 5-minute alert window. The customer provided exporter logs and console query snapshots indicating the raw events exist in the raw event store for the period but rollup data lacked the high-latency buckets.

Why this ticket: We need to determine whether retention compaction job evicted or temporarily aliased buckets used by the alert eval, and implement a fix or mitigation so short bursts are preserved or alert evaluation queries fall back to raw events when compaction boundaries overlap evaluation windows.
1) Simulate 4-minute burst of high-latency requests against a single org-scoped route in prod-us-east (token latency ~600ms).
2) Ensure retention compaction run is scheduled at the same minute (the customer's compaction cadence was hourly with boundary at :13).
3) Wait for hourly compaction to complete and then run Console alert eval (95th percentile over the immediately preceding 5m).
4) Compare raw event counts (raw-events API) to aggregated rollup buckets used by alerting service for the same window.
5) If rollup shows no high-latency bucket but raw events do, the compaction path likely removed detail needed by the percentile evaluator.
2026-02-17T22:12:59Z ingest-processor[writer]: wrote 3,412 events for org: lumenops route: /v1/generate
2026-02-17T22:13:23Z ingest-processor[writer]: event token_latency_ms=612 request_id=8a3c...
2026-02-17T22:14:05Z retention-compactor[cron]: started hourly compaction bucket=2026-02-17T22:00:00Z -> 2026-02-17T22:59:59Z
2026-02-17T22:14:07Z retention-compactor[worker]: merged 1.2M samples, evicted detailed percentile histogram shards: shard_ids=[3421,3422]
2026-02-17T22:15:01Z alert-eval[runner]: eval alert_id=AL-9876 window=2026-02-17T22:10:00Z-2026-02-17T22:15:00Z percentile(95)=128ms
2026-02-17T22:15:02Z alert-eval[runner]: eval finished status=ok actions=none
Initial hypothesis: compaction merged histogram shards and replaced high-resolution histograms with approximated rollup that smoothed out short spikes.
Checked raw-events API: raw-events returns 3,412 events in window with ~7% events reporting >500ms latency.
Checked rollup buckets: corresponding 5m rollup shows 0 events in >400ms bucket; histogram summary shows 95th=128ms.
Confirmed compaction job started within the 5-minute eval window; compaction replaced per-minute histograms with hourly aggregates before alert-eval ran.
Reproducer note: running alert-eval immediately before compaction correctly triggers alert (95th>350ms). Running after compaction returns smoothed result.

Additional notes:
2026-02-19 08:01 - LumenOps (Customer): This caused us to miss a critical SLA alert, lost visibility for about 20 minutes. Asking for ETA on fix and whether any credits will be issued.
Retention compaction job merged high-resolution histogram shards into coarse hourly aggregates while an alert evaluation job for a short 5-minute window ran after compaction but before raw-event fallback was implemented. The coarse aggregate smoothed short spikes, causing percentile-based alert eval to miss the spike.
Implemented an alert-eval fallback to query raw-events for percentile calculations when the rollup resolution is coarser than the alert window. This is enabled for prod:us-east canary and will be monitored.
In Progress - mitigation deployed to canary (prod:us-east). Next steps: 1) update compaction policy to keep minute-level histograms for the last 2 hours before compacting to hourly; 2) add unit/integration tests for compaction+alert-eval timing; 3) schedule rolling rollout and customer follow-up.
Related runbook: Retention compaction and alert evaluation ordering (Confluence) - linked above.
Similar tickets: SUP-991222 (alerting aggregation window misalignment after kafka backfill) - consulted during investigation.
Priority customer; recommended follow-up call scheduled 2026-02-22 15:00 UTC.

Issue summary: BrightDocs reported sudden elevated 5xx rates (502/503) across both embedding and chat routes starting 2026-03-13 20:02 UTC. Impact: multiple customer requests failed with upstream 5xx; latency spiked and streaming sessions dropped. Environment: prod us-east, dedicated tenant for BrightDocs. Hypothesis: edge rate-limiter token-bucket TTL eviction caused per-tenant token bucket state to reset simultaneously, producing a retry stampede that saturated the api-gateway accept queue and upstream runtimes, leading to 5xx and some runtime crashes. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and customer communication.
1) Send mixed traffic (short embed uploads plus chat streaming) at burst rate (~1200 rps) to tenant-alias belonging to BrightDocs in us-east.
2) Observe edge rate-limiter metrics: token_bucket_evictions rate spikes and per-tenant buckets show recent ttl expirations.
3) Client SDKs retried on 429 but misinterpreted response as transient, sending repeated hedged retries, amplifying load.
4) Api-gateway accept queue grows; upstream runtime threads hit prefetch locks and some runtimes restart with OOM-like symptoms.
Note: reproducing requires simulated ttl-eviction conditions and client retry heuristics; non-trivial in staging unless rate-limiter TTLs are reduced.
2026-03-13T20:02:14Z apigw[edge-3]: token_bucket_evictions{tenant=brightdocs}=312 increment
2026-03-13T20:02:15Z apigw[edge-3]: accept_queue_depth=912 latency_p50=220ms p95=1.8s errors=5xx:124
2026-03-13T20:02:17Z rate-limiter[rl-1]: TTL_EVICT tenant=brightdocs bucket_id=0x7f12 msg=evicted state=expired ttl_ms=0
2026-03-13T20:02:18Z runtime[rt-4]: prefetch_lock_wait average_ms=1350 threads_waiting=19
2026-03-13T20:02:20Z runtime[rt-4]: worker[11] terminated signal=SIGKILL reason=watchdog_timeout memory_usage=18.9GB
Support (2026-03-13 20:10) - Aisha: Customer BrightDocs reported a 10-15% error rate with 502/503 across both embeds and chat. Asked for tenant alias and recent request IDs. Provided request ids: rq_20260313_20_02_{a..f}.
SRE (2026-03-13 20:25) - Marco: Observed simultaneous spike in token_bucket_evictions for multiple edge nodes; accept_queue growing to >900 in us-east; pushed temporary soft-rate-limit to 200 rps for BrightDocs to throttle retries.
Customer (BrightDocs Ops, 2026-03-13 20:30) - Jenna: Confirmed traffic pattern: SDK batch uploader retried aggressively on 429. We had a scheduled cron that did chunked embedding uploads at 20:00 UTC.
Engineer (2026-03-13 20:45) - Priya: Correlated events: TTL rotation job for edge cache completed at 20:01 UTC (https://runbook.redwood/ttl-rotation). Hypothesis: eviction wave + client retries caused accept queue starvation and two runtime restarts.
SRE (2026-03-13 21:05) - Marco: Rolled out hotfix on edge rate-limiter: stagger TTL sweeps across nodes and added jitter to eviction loop; monitoring for 30m. Applied conservative retry-quarantine at api-gateway for repeated hedged retries.
Support (2026-03-13 21:35) - Aisha: Customer confirmed error rate dropped to baseline ~0.2% after hotfix and temporary throttling. Monitoring to ensure no recurring spikes.
SRE (2026-03-14 09:10) - Marco: Postmortem draft started; root cause is combination of synchronous TTL eviction across edge nodes + aggressive client retry semantics that interpreted 429s as transient  and retried without backoff, amplifying pressure. Next steps listed below.
Edge metrics show token_bucket_evictions aligned across NTP-synchronized nodes -> likely coordinated eviction job or TTL drift.
Accept queue growth first observed on edge-3 then propagated via load balancer to other apigw instances.
Runtime watch-dog triggered restarts after accept queue pressure and long prefetch lock waits.
Client SDKs (brightdocs-sdk v2.3.1) had a retry change in 2.3.0 that retries on any non-200 including 429; lacking exponential backoff in bulk upload path.
No config changes from BrightDocs on 2026-03-13; their scheduled batch likely tipped the system when eviction occurred.
Related signal: small but sustained increase in kernel softirq for network handling on apigw hosts during the spike.
1) Applied tenant-level soft-rate-limit (200 rps) to BrightDocs at 20:26 UTC to break retry loop.
2) Hot-fixed edge rate-limiter: added node-level random jitter to TTL eviction jobs and limited per-eviction bucket deletes to 50/s.
3) Configured api-gateway to detect repeated hedged retries and send 429 with Retry-After header for same client fingerprint for 10s.
4) Restarted two affected runtimes in a controlled drain to recover prefetch locks; observed stable memory after restart.
5) Notified BrightDocs of recommended SDK upgrade (v2.3.2) which includes exponential backoff for bulk uploads.
6) Added temporary alert rule to detect global token_bucket_evictions rate > 100/s per region.
1) Engineering: implement persistent per-tenant token-bucket state (avoid synchronous full-region eviction) - owner: Priya - ETA: 2026-03-21.
2) Product/SDK: coordinate mandatory backoff in SDK for bulk embedding uploads and document best-practices for retry behavior - owner: Diego - ETA: 2026-03-18.
3) SRE: harden api-gateway retry-quarantine heuristics and add synthetic test covering TTL eviction + client retry storm - owner: Marco - ETA: 2026-03-16.
4) Postmortem: complete RCA and publish on Confluence and share with BrightDocs - owner: Marco - ETA: 2026-03-17.
5) Follow-up: schedule canary of TTL rotation job with smaller window and node-level staggering - owner: infra-team - ETA: 2026-03-15.
Mitigated (temporary throttles, jittered eviction). Permanent fix in progress: per-tenant bucket persistence and SDK backoff. Customer impact resolved; monitoring remains active.
2026-03-13 21:45 UTC - We implemented temporary throttles and a hotfix in the edge rate limiter to address elevated 5xx for BrightDocs; traffic has returned to normal. Engineering is implementing a permanent fix to avoid coordinated eviction events and working with SDK teams to improve retry behavior.

Issue summary: Customer reports a gradual, sustained drop in dedicated pool throughput over several hours coincident with a high rate of short-lived connections from a single tenant. Impact: AcmeChat's p50 token throughput dropped ~35% and p99 latency increased from ~120ms to ~890ms on their dedicated reservations for several rolling windows. Environment: prod us-east, dedicated pool (reservation-id: res-84f3). Observed: high connection churn (>15k connects/min), unusually high prefetch requests per second, repeated KV cache warmups, frequent small eviction events and GPU-slot fragmentation. Expected: short streams should not starve longer batched work or cause repeated prefetch re-execution that fragments slots. This ticket captures triage, investigation notes, and mitigation attempts.
1) Provision a small dedicated reservation with mixed workloads: 20% steady long-batch traffic (seq len 1024) + 80% short chat streams (avg 4 tokens) from a single tenant.
2) Simulate high connection churn: open/close websocket connections at ~250 RPS per client for 60+ minutes across 100 parallel clients.
3) Observe scheduler allocation churn, repeated prefetch calls in serving-runtime, and falling p50 throughput on the dedicated pool dashboards.
4) Capture metrics from /metrics and /debug endpoints for prefetch_requests_total, evictions_total, gpu_slot_free_fraction.
5) Re-run with client-side keepalive (30s) to compare behavior — mitigation is expected if churn is root cause.
[2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] prefetch: tenant=acmechat req_id=8f7cd prefetch_start seq_id=312 ttl_ms=60000
[2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] scheduler: allocate slot gpu=gpux012 reservation=res-84f3 reason=short_stream
[2026-03-10T14:22:04Z] eviction: slot=slot-2 tenant=acmechat cause=prefetch_collision
[2026-03-10T14:22:38Z] serving-runtime: kv-cache-miss tenant=acmechat key=conv-9b1a miss_count=47
[2026-03-10T15:03:11Z] nvlink: peer-drop detected on gpux012 (kernel 0xffff) — transient IO errors, correlates with eviction spikes
p50 throughput baseline: 12k tokens/s -> degraded to 7.9k tokens/s over 2 hours
prefetch_requests_total: increased 5x from baseline during the incident window
gpu_slot_free_fraction: dropped from 0.28 -> 0.05 during sustained churn
evictions_total: saw periodic spikes aligned with connection bursts
Initial hypothesis: a dominant tenant generating a high volume of very short streams causes repeated prefetch attempts and frequent allocation/eviction cycles, which fragment GPU slots (slot erosion) and reduce effective batch sizes for other tenants. Support validated correlation between tenant X (AcmeChat) connection churn and pool-level degradation via dashboards: dedicated-reservation res-84f3. SRE captured serving-runtime traces showing prefetch_start events for conversation keys that are immediately abandoned when clients disconnect; these prefetches still consume slot attachments and KV cache warm-up GPU memory until eviction. Autoscaler reacts to transient drop in usable slots by attempting re-provisioning which amplifies allocation churn.
A: Churn causes prefetch re-execution -> confirmed by matching request ids and kv-cache misses
B: Autoscaler thrash increases fragmentation -> partially confirmed: autoscaler made 2 scale-down attempts in-window which coincided with additional eviction events
C: Underlying GPU IO errors (nvlink) are the root cause -> inconclusive; transient nvlink peer-drops observed but not clearly causal — further kernel-level logs requested from infra team
1) Temporary tenant throttling applied at edge to limit short-stream connect rate (reduced churn by ~60%) — immediate throughput improvement observed
2) Increased prefetch TTL to 2 minutes in the serving-runtime for this reservation to allow reuse across reconnects — reduced repeated warmups but increased short-lived memory hold times
3) Applied server-side keepalive guidance to customer SDK (recommended 30s) — pending customer rollout
4) Pinning the workload to a separate dedicated reservation as isolation short-term mitigation
Support (Asha): Asked customer for sample request ids, connection patterns, and traffic start/end timestamps.
Customer (AcmeChat - James Lee): Provided sample traffic trace and confirmed they launched a new client version yesterday that reduces connection pooling (likely cause).
SRE (Miguel): Collected serving-runtime heap profiles and scheduler allocation timeline; nvlink peer-drops seen but only during highest eviction windows. Attached metric snapshots to ticket.

Additional notes:
Support (Asha): Recommended customer enable client keepalive and provided SDK snippet; scheduled a call for 2026-03-11 to coordinate mitigation rollout.
1) SRE to gather kernel-level NVMe/NVLINK logs for gpux012 during the incident window (assigned to Miguel). 2) Engineering to prototype scheduler change that cancels prefetch attachments if client disconnects within X ms (PR sketch: runtime/prefetch-cancelation). 3) Customer to roll out client-side keepalive and connection pooling update; monitor p50/p99. 4) Consider short-term tenant isolation if churn persists.
In Progress - partial mitigations applied (tenant throttling and increased prefetch TTL). Awaiting customer SDK rollout and infra kernel logs to confirm or rule out hardware IO contribution. Follow-up actions: scheduler patch (PR linked), postmortem if repeats.

Add autoscaler hysteresis for dedicated reservations experiencing high short-lived-connection churn

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FinNova) reports that a subset of requests have been routed to an older model variant that they had explicitly pinned away from. The regression began during a customer traffic spike and a concurrent canary weight change.

Impact:
- ~18% of requests for one tenant are receiving outputs from the legacy variant (v1.8) instead of the intended pinned variant (v2.0-quant).
- Customer reports degraded result quality and elevated token usage leading to billing concerns.
- Problem started during a scheduled weighted canary adjustment and persisted despite control-plane restarts.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool (dedicated tenant pool, us-east region)
- Tenant: finnova-prod (dedicated)
- Affected model: redwood/oasst-7b-v2-quant (target), legacy fallback v1.8 (observed)
- Ingress path: edge-proxy -> orchestrator -> serving-runtime (quantized GPU nodes)

Steps to reproduce (from customer and support replay):
1) Customer increases concurrent sessions from ~1200 to ~3200 over 3 minutes (traffic surge window).
2) Support triggers canary weight shift from 5% -> 25% for v2.0-quant via Console rollout UI.
3) During the shift, certain sticky sessions begin receiving v1.8 responses; session affinity indicates a pin to legacy variant.
4) Attempts to refresh tenant pin via API return success but do not clear stuck affinity for affected sessions.

Observed behaviour:
- Sessions tied to a cohort continue to route to legacy variant even after pin-update and orchestration restart.
- Edge logs show the cohort affinity token is present, but orchestrator returns placement for legacy variant for that token.
- No 5xx errors; requests succeed but with unexpected variant.

Expected behaviour:
- Pin update should immediately route all new requests and existing sessions (subject to TTL) to pinned variant or trigger a clean handoff according to rollout policy.

Logs / Dashboards / Links:
- Support trace: https://console.redwood/support/traces/SUP-142357-rt-01
- Ingress sampling (edge-proxy): https://dash.redwood/edge/proxy/requests?trace=SUP-142357
- Orchestrator placement events: https://dash.redwood/orchestrator/events?range=3h
- Customer-provided transcript showing v1.8 outputs: attached as finnova_output_snippet.txt
- Related Slack thread: #support-finnova (slack.com/archives/C02XYZ/2026-03-12)

Initial hypothesis:
- During rapid weight change + surge, pin reconciliation logic failed to pick up the new placement snapshot and served an older placement for a subset of cohort tokens.
- Edge or sidecar cache may be returning stale affinity tokens that map to older cohort epoch.
- Orchestrator snapshot merge timing could create transient window where placement resolver prefers legacy nodes for tokens with intermediate epochs.

Impact assessment so far:
- Customer-facing but limited to a cohort (approx 18% of tenant traffic).
- No increased error rates or node OOMs; primarily correctness / quality and billing exposure.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Force pin-refresh for finnova via admin API (admin.routing.refresh_pins(tenant=finnova-prod)) — reported success but did not clear affected live sessions.
- Rolling restart of orchestrator worker behind tenant shard performed at 2026-03-12 15:40 UTC — did not rectify stuck cohort.
- Temporary rule applied on edge to reject affinity cookies older than epoch-245 to force rebind (edge config change ID: edgecfg-2026-03-12-1346). Observed 70% of stuck sessions rebind within 6 minutes, remaining ~30% persisted.

Next steps (in progress):
- SRE to instrument placement resolver trace for token->epoch mapping (assigned).
- Routing team to review snapshot merge logic and any prefetch/caching decisions during weight changes.
- Run targeted session reshard job to clear remaining stuck cohort (requires scheduled maintenance window with customer).
- Engineering to prepare a hotfix to make pin-refresh force-evict session affinity when requested by admin API.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 15:50 - Customer (FinNova - Ops): Thank you for partial mitigation. We still see some degraded outputs and would like a full remediation plan before next billing cycle. Asking for ETA on hotfix.
Reproduced in staging by simulating 3-minute ramp from 1.2k -> 3.2k concurrent sessions and applying a 5%->25% canary weight shift. Traced token->placement mapping; found ~27% of tokens referenced stale epoch (one snapshot behind). Orchestrator logs show snapshot merge fences executing but a race condition in the token resolver allowed lookups against an older snapshot until its TTL expired. Edge cookie expiry workaround reduces surface but does not eliminate tokens already materialized in downstream session stores.
In progress. Short-term: targeted session rebind job executed (2026-03-13) cleared ~98% of stuck sessions. Long-term: hotfix merged to routing (PR #1987) will add admin API flag to force-evict and strict snapshot fence during canary weight changes. Hotfix rollout scheduled to dedicated control plane next build window 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC. Post-rollout validation and customer billing reconciliation scheduled. Follow-up tasks: add unit + integration tests for snapshot merge race, augment runbook with guidance for forced-rebind, and instrument more granular metrics for epoch mismatch rate.
Preliminary rebind job successful; remaining items tracking in INT backlog. Customer notified and provided credit for degraded tokens. Will close once hotfix is live and post-validation is clean.

Issue summary: Customer reports persistent 429 responses when performing a large embeddings import immediately after transferring 5 subaccounts under a single organization billing pool. Impact: Import jobs failing with repeated 429s causing incomplete ingestion and downstream blocking of model-indexing pipelines. Environment: Dedicated tenancy on prod-us-east, dedicated pool id dp-42. Recent customer action: executed subaccount transfer and billing consolidation at 02:00 UTC before starting import.

Observed behavior: Multiple workers (50 parallel processes) receive 429s within 10-30s of start; headers show per-key token refill lag and inconsistent X-RateLimit-* headers across parallel requests. Console shows quota for the top-level org updated, but subaccount windows appear to have stale refill counters. Customer sees repeated retries with exponential backoff and still exhausts the window. Expected behavior: Post-transfer quota and refill windows should reconcile quickly and allow sustained throughput given dedicated commit.

Customer impact: High — scheduled migration/import must complete for production search indexing. Customer has deadline for compliance decommissioning and indicated potential business impact if import cannot finish within SLA.
1) Create organization with 5 subaccounts under a single billing pool. 2) Move the 5 subaccounts from separate billing pools into the target pool (simulate transfer). 3) Immediately start bulk embeddings import with 50 parallel workers using the existing API keys for the subaccounts. 4) Observe HTTP 429 responses within the first minute and inconsistent X-RateLimit headers returned. 5) Repeat with smaller concurrency to validate behavior changes.
- Sample response headers captured 2026-03-11T02:15:23Z: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests; X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000; X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0; X-RateLimit-Reset: 167; Retry-After: 8
- API gateway logs show token_debit failures tied to org_id=arcadia-876 and subaccount ids s-101,s-102,s-103.
- Console audit: billing_pool update event id bp-20260311-09, completed at 02:01:12Z.
- Worker client stack traces show retry loop attempts and backoff jitter up to 64s.

- Hypothesis 1: Refill window for per-subaccount token buckets was not atomically migrated leading to uneven starting credits.
- Hypothesis 2: Rate-limiter shard responsible for these subaccounts did not observe the billing-pool reconciliation event and is using stale refill state.
- Hypothesis 3: Dedicated pool tiering logic applied a short warmup (burst-limited) window after the transfer which is blocking sustained concurrency.
- Early checks: Confirmed billing event present in audit logs. Token bucket metrics show high debit rate and zeroed remaining counters immediately after transfer.
- Checked gateway traces: transfer event propagated to control-plane but rate-limiter shard commit timestamps lag by ~30s.
- Reproduced in staging with smaller scale: when transfer is followed immediately by parallel imports, 429s are observed until ~45s after transfer completion.

Additional notes:
SRE Team (internal): Found control-plane publish to 'quota-reconciler' succeeded but deliver to rate-limiter-kv-store delayed by 28s. Possible queue consumer lag on rl-sync worker.
Support (to customer): Suggested two immediate mitigations — staggered worker start (ramp up over 60s) or run import against a single API key tied to the org-level pool (avoid per-subaccount windows) until we confirm fix.
Workaround provided: customer accepted a staged ramp-up script and switched to a single org-level API key for the import; import completed with reduced failures. Engineering action: Opened internal task to harden quota-reconciler -> rate-limiter delivery with guaranteed-at-least-once semantics and backfill reconciliation for subaccount counters. Proposed fix: add a short 'post-transfer grace window' where org-level tokens are used until all shards confirm updated state. Related PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/342. Follow-up: schedule change to rate-limiter consumer to reduce lag and add observability alerts for reconciliation deltas. Customer to re-test a replica transfer next week and coordinate with SRE during the window.
1) SRE to add consumer lag metric and alert (ETA 2026-03-14). 2) Eng to implement grace-window fallback and add unit/integration tests (tracked in internal ticket INT-22018). 3) Support to coordinate a controlled re-test with Arcadia Health and monitor metrics in real-time. 4) Document recommended post-transfer importing pattern in KB article.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Nimbus Analytics reports intermittent 429 throttles for low-latency chat sessions that started immediately after they enabled the SDK 'session_replay' telemetry feature (client-side keystroke/interaction capture). Throttles coincide with periods of apparently low interactive traffic (user idle windows) and occur across multiple user sessions.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency and 429s on interactive chat endpoints for a subset (~3-5%) of active sessions during nightly hours and occasional daytime spikes.
- Affects multiple product users and prevents real-time typing UX for affected sessions.

Environment:
- Customer: Nimbus Analytics (enterprise) on Redwood Private (VPC) using a dedicated pool in eu-west.
- SDK: rust-sdk v1.6.2 with session_replay enabled and telemetry_endpoint configured to use same API key as production calls.
- Models in path: gpt-redwood-24k (primary), fallback to gpt-open-3b.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a chat session in the Nimbus web app with session_replay enabled.
2) Leave the session idle for 60-90s (SDK configured to flush buffered keystroke events every 30s).
3) Re-enter and start typing; observe occasional 429 on the next generation call.
4) Repeat with multiple browser tabs/orchestrated workers to increase concurrency.

Observed behavior:
- Telemetry flushes appear as short bursts of small requests (0-50 tokens each) originating from the SDK on the same API key used for generation.
- The bursts align with the token/token-window accounting in our rate-limiter and are depleting the per-tenant token/concurrency window leading to 429 responses on user-facing calls.
- Console shows tenant-level token-window exhaustion at the same timestamps as customer errors.

Expected behavior:
- Telemetry/diagnostic pings should not consume production token/concurrency quota or should be accounted separately to avoid impacting user-facing generation.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- SDK config snippet (session_replay: true, flush_interval_ms: 30000).
- Timestamps and sample request IDs for failed generations: req-6fc2a9, req-6fc2b1, req-6fc2e7.
- Sample telemetry flush logs showing hundreds of tiny POSTs during a 10-minute window.

Additional notes:
Confirmed telemetry endpoint calls are routed through api-gateway and pass through the same token accounting path as generation requests.
Rate-limiter uses per-tenant token windows that count all requests authenticated with the tenant's API keys; small telemetry requests still increment token accounting due to header metadata mapping to the same route.
Observed periodic flush pattern every ~30s from SDK; when many sessions/tabs are open, aggregated bursts coincide with window exhaustion in the short refill interval configuration.
No evidence of hardware or dedicated pool capacity shortage; this is purely quota accounting at the gateway/rate-limiter layer.
Edge-case: private VPC sidecars add a small amplification due to connection pooling and retries; increases apparent concurrency briefly during flush times.
Temporary mitigation test: instructing customer to set SDK flush_interval_ms to 300000 (5 min) reduced burst frequency and eliminated 429s in a small A/B test.
Workaround provided and roadmap fix identified. Actions taken:
1) Workaround (customer applied): Change SDK session_replay config to use an isolated telemetry API key or increase flush interval to avoid synchronized bursts. After the change, Nimbus saw immediate reduction in 429s during nightly windows.
2) Short-term platform mitigation: SRE added an exclusion rule for the customer's telemetry route in the rate-limiter config to stop counting telemetry pings against the tenant token window while we test. This is scoped to the customer's dedicated VPC and will be rolled back after full fix validation.
3) Long-term fix: Engineering to add route-level token-accounting flags so telemetry/endpoints can be marked non-consumptive or redirected to a separate quota pool. Patch PR created and under review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5821.
Follow-ups:
- Eng to add clearer SDK docs recommending use of separate telemetry keys for production traffic and provide sample config for flush intervals and batching.
- Product to evaluate telemetry as a first-class traffic class with separate quota allocation on Private/Dedicated deployments.
- SRE to monitor the customer's tenant quota telemetry for 72 hours post-mitigation.
Status: In Progress — workaround validated by customer; engineering PR in review; monitoring active.
ENG: Merge PR 5821 and deploy feature flag for route-level accounting (owner: Marco Ruiz, ETA 2026-03-18).
DOCS: Publish SDK guidance for telemetry keys and recommended flush settings (owner: DevRel - Priya Natarajan, ETA 2026-03-17).
SRE: Monitor quota consumption and reopen rate-limiter exclusion if any regressions (owner: Sofia Chen, monitoring window until 2026-03-15).
CS: Follow up with Nimbus on final validation and close ticket after 72h of clean telemetry (owner: Aisha Patel).

payload.description:
Customer runs a mixed workload in production: interactive realtime chat sessions (low tokens, high concurrency) and frequent background telemetry/heartbeat pings from a fleet of edge agents. Over the last week they started seeing a rising number of 429s that correlate with telemetry sweep windows. They want concrete guidance on whether to: 1) split refill windows (separate burst pools) for telemetry vs interactive lanes, 2) use separate API keys/routes for telemetry, or 3) tune smoothing/refill intervals to avoid synchronized tenant-level throttles.
~12% of interactive chat requests returned 429s during nightly telemetry sweeps; several customer-facing flows degrade (timeouts, retries). Affects production us-west region only. Billing unaffected but user experience degraded.
1) Deploy 1000 edge agents configured to send telemetry heartbeat (small POST) every 60 seconds. 2) Start 200 concurrent interactive chat sessions that send occasional messages (avg 30 tokens) over WebSocket/HTTP3. 3) Observe token usage and 429 spikes in request timeline around minute boundaries when many heartbeats align. 4) Toggle telemetry heartbeat jitter and re-run to see effect.
Sample throttle header from client: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 25s. Platform logs show tenant_token_window_exhausted events at 2026-03-09T03:00:00Z and 2026-03-10T03:00:00Z. Ingress traces show many short lived HTTP/3 connections from telemetry agents and long-lived websocket-like streams for chat. No 5xx accompanying errors.
Initial hypothesis: telemetry heartbeats are concentrated on the same refill epoch and are counted against the tenant-wide refill window used by interactive requests. HTTP/3 multipath and short connections may be causing preflight-like counting or connection-level aggregation anomalies. Possible contributing factors: (a) telemetry uses same API key/route and is not isolated, (b) refill interval (60s epoch) aligns with heartbeat cadence resulting in sawtooth token consumption, (c) smoothing parameters not tuned for high-cardinality short requests.
1) Recommend separating telemetry onto a dedicated API key and route that maps to a distinct burst pool (isolated burst lane) so background pings cannot exhaust interactive quota. 2) If separate key not possible, add jitter to heartbeat schedule to desynchronize pulses. 3) Temporarily increase tenant burst credits during sweep windows or configure a short-lived exception for telemetry route via Console as a stopgap.
Triage stage. Guidance prepared for customer; engineering inboxed to evaluate adding a Console UI path to create isolated burst pools for routes. If customer agrees, support will schedule a config change: create dedicated route + API key for telemetry and update docs with recommended jitter parameters. No code changes required immediately.

Issue summary: Customer reported repeated short-lived waves of 5xx (502/503) affecting streaming and short-poll generation routes for a single dedicated tenant. Impact: Several production endpoints returned 502/503 intermittently for ~10-30s pulses, causing dropped streams and failed request retries; observed by Nimbus Health as increased error rate and user-visible failures. Environment: Dedicated pool for customer in us-east-1; mixed embedding/chat traffic; model pinned to redwood/gptx-3.2. Initial symptom window: 2026-03-10 01:12–03:40 UTC.

Steps to reproduce: not reliably reproducible from a single synthetic test; reproduces under sustained concurrent tenant traffic + aggressive background prefetch for large prompt sets. Support template fields below contain logs, metrics, and timeline.
Send mixed streaming and non-streaming requests at 150 concurrent connections from single tenant with varied prompt lengths (200–400 tokens).
Trigger background model prefetch by submitting a large-batch evaluation job (customer internal test) to the tenant simultaneously.
Observe intermittent 502/503 on streaming sessions and short-lived elevated 5xx pulses in API gateway and runtime metrics.
2026-03-10T01:15:04Z runtime[pid=1843]: OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files
2026-03-10T01:15:04Z runtime[pid=1843]: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/opt/serving/prefetch/worker.py", line 412, in _open_prefetch_stream
2026-03-10T01:15:04Z apigw[edge-id=apigw-12]: upstream read error: EOF (502) for route /v1/chat/stream
2026-03-10T01:15:27Z runtime: worker watchdog triggered restart (reason=fd-limit-reached)
API gateway 5xx rate for tenant spiked from baseline 0.2% to 8.6% in 30s windows
Runtime open file descriptor count on host node climbed from ~2k to >65k before failures
Accept queue drop rate increased concurrently with runtime 'watchdog restart' events

Initial triage (support): Correlated apigw 502s to upstream runtime restarts and EMFILE in runtime logs. Tenant traffic patterns show high short-lived stream connects plus a background evaluation triggering prefetch activity.
SRE ran live diagnostics on affected runtime host: lsof snapshot showed thousands of TCP sockets and many /tmp/prefetch/*.tmp file handles left open by prefetch worker processes.
Hypothesis: Prefetch worker has a filehandle leak when prefetching large prompt embeddings; under high concurrency the leak climbs until process cannot open sockets/files, watchdog restarts the worker and upstream returns 502/503.
Temporary mitigation: increased ulimit -n for affected pods to 100k and disabled aggressive prefetch for the tenant via per-tenant config (rollback to conservative prefetch window). This immediately reduced recurrence of pulses.
Root cause identified by runtime eng: missing close() paths in prefetch worker error-handling when partial reads fail; also prefetch created temp files that were not removed on cancellation. See PRs referenced.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 02:22 UTC — SRE (Marta Delgado): Confirmed EMFILE traces on node runtime-ue1-34. Collecting lsof + pmap. Noted many /tmp/prefetch files. Temporarily bumped ulimit and paused tenant prefetch config.
2026-03-11 10:12 UTC — Customer (Nimbus Health contact: Rahul Mehta): Confirmed error rates returned to baseline and reported no further user-visible failures since mitigation. Asked for post-incident summary and corrective actions.
Hotfix applied: fixed missing close() paths in prefetch worker and added cleanup for temporary files. Emergency mitigation (increased ulimit, disabled aggressive prefetch for tenant) limited recurrence during rollout. Hotfix deployed to prod dedicated pool on 2026-03-11; metrics show 5xx back to baseline. Postmortem and follow-up tasks created (INT-2409) to add FD-growth alerting and integration tests. Issue summary: Around 18:20 UTC we observed a rapid elevation in 5xx responses for requests routed to the us-east serving pool for a single dedicated tenant (LexiSearch). Impact: Customer saw ~60% error rate on chat/streaming requests and ~30% on embedding uploads for 18:20-18:55 UTC. Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated capacity pool pinned to customer. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a mixed workload from LexiSearch that includes long-chat generation (>2k tokens) and bulk embedding upload concurrently. 2) Observe runtime worker thread crashes and subsequent 502/503 responses from API gateway. Logs & traces: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/dashboard/s/serve/tenant-us-east Lexi thread panic trace: logs-redwood://prod/us-east/runtime/worker-7/2026-03-10T18:22:31Z (see stack frames w/ tokenizer::segmenter::process). Slack thread: #support-lexisearch (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C12345/p164)
1) Use LexiSearch account to send a simultaneous streaming chat request (long prompt + function calls) and a bulk embedding upload of ~12k items.
2) Observe increased prefetch activity and repeated KV cache invalidations in serving-runtime logs.
3) Monitor API Gateway 5xx rate and runtime worker restarts during the burst.
Memory and GPU driver checks: NVML logs show transient GPU driver reset coincident with worker SIGABRT; GPU memory usage not at peak but post-reset fragmentation observed.
Stack traces point to tokenizer::segmenter::process -> tokenize_utf8_sequence -> std::vector resize in patched tokenizer library (new behavior introduced in runtime-hotpatch).
Prefetch/KV cache behaviour: Long streaming sessions caused frequent KV writes; combined with bulk embeddings, this created lock contention on kvcache shards causing coroutine queue growth and increased thread concurrency in runtime worker.
Amplification path: runtime thread panic leads to worker process crash -> Kubernetes restarts worker -> API gateway keeps retrying connections which temporarily increases connection churn and accept queue backlog -> additional 5xx from api-gateway while runtime pool recovers.
Correlation: error spike window matches customer activity (confirmed by customer logs and request-ids). No similar signals for other tenants in the same pool.
A recent runtime hotpatch updated the tokenizer library with an aggressive internal buffer resize which can trigger a stack corruption when combined with high concurrency on kvcache prefetch locks. The stack corruption produced thread-level panics and worker process SIGABRTs. Worker crash/restart churn amplified load at the API gateway (retries and accept queue saturation), producing the observed 5xx surge for the affected tenant.
1) Rolled back the runtime hotpatch to the previous stable tokenizer build (deployment rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6789). 2) Applied temporary per-tenant ingress throttle for LexiSearch to prevent immediate re-flood during restarts. 3) Increased api-gateway accept_queue and provisional connection backoff to smooth retry amplification. 4) Performed rolling restarts of affected runtime shards and monitored NVML/GPU health. Result: error rate returned to baseline by 19:22 UTC.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 18:42 - LexiSearch (Customer): We started a bulk import and several long conversation sessions; errors started ~18:20, please advise ETA to restore.
Rollback + throttles restored customer service quickly. Customer confirmed recovery and resumed operations with reduced concurrency while engineering prepares a patch. LexiSearch requested a 1:1 sync to understand timeline for a permanent fix.

Add a counter metric for tokenizer-exception-rate and alert when >0.1% for 5m in any tenant pool.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports that when using the Go SDK with multiplexed streaming sessions they observe duplicate external tool executions (webhook posts) in a narrow race where the client triggers a retry during the server-side retry window. Impact:
- Duplicate downstream side effects (payment webhook charged twice) in ~0.8% of long-running sessions for one major flow.
- Billing discrepancies and customer-facing incorrect behavior.
Environment:
- SDK: redwood-go v0.12.3 (custom wrapper)
- Service: Hosted Redwood Dedicated pool (us-east-1)
- Model: redwood-13b-v1 pinned to v2026-02-26
- Traffic pattern: multiplexed client with two concurrent logical streams per connection, median request time 18s, tail 90s
Observed behavior:
1) Client sends request A invoking external tool (payment POST) and receives partial ack for call queued but connection is swapped (connection migration) at ~17s.
2) Client times out locally, then triggers an immediate retry on the multiplexed session.
3) Server retries the in-flight tool call (because it had queued it) AND the client retry causes the tool to be enqueued again for the retried request resulting in two webhook posts.
Expected behavior:
- Server-side deduplication or explicit tool-confirmation should prevent duplicate external tool invocation in this race.
Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start redwood-go client with multiplexing enabled and two logical streams per TCP connection.
2) Use a handler that triggers a synchronous external webhook call during model generation.
3) Simulate transient connection swap (tcp reset) at ~15-20s on in-flight stream A.
4) Immediately retry the request on the same multiplexed session.
5) Observe two webhook calls for a single logical action.
Logs/trace snippets (redacted):
- correlation-id: bc-prod-9f3d
- server request id: srv-20260312-5031
- webhook upstream: https://payments.brightcart.com/charge -> 2x POST bodies with identical payloads timestamped 18.042s and 18.129s
- client side: "stream: moved, retrying request" followed by "retry-sent: idempotency-token=blank"

Temporary workaround requested by customer: guidance on short-term mitigations (headers, retry backoff, SDK flags).
See description steps; customer provided a minimal repro that toggles multiplex=true and forces a connection swap. They used an internal script to send SIGPIPE to the socket after 15s.
server-log-excerpt: [2026-03-12T15:14:10Z] srv-20260312-5031 streamA queued tool POST -> outbound webhook payment id X123; [2026-03-12T15:14:27Z] connection migration detected; [2026-03-12T15:14:27Z] client retried logical streamA -> queued tool POST -> outbound webhook payment id X123 (second)
2026-03-12 - BrightCart-Support: We saw two charges for order 98765. Both webhook bodies identical. This wasn't reproducible on non-multiplexed config.
2026-03-12 - Support (Ava Patel): Thanks for the report — tagging Runtime and SDK teams. Can you share connection reset sequence and SDK version? Any idempotency token being sent?
2026-03-12 - BrightCart-Support: Using redwood-go v0.12.3, our wrapper strips idempotency headers for tool calls to reduce payload size (we didn't realize they'd be needed). We attached server logs. Repro is included.
2026-03-12 - Support (Luis Moreno): Reproduced locally with repro. Observed same double-enqueue when client retries immediately after reset and idempotency header absent. Raising to Runtime eng for dedup policy review.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 - SDK Eng (Rajiv Kapoor): SDK change candidate: ensure SDK includes idempotency-token header for each tool request by default and preserve it across retries. Preparing PR for default behavior and docs update.
2026-03-13 - Support (Luis Moreno): Sent interim guidance to customer: enable `disable_multiplex=false` or add client-side deliberate 200ms jitter before immediate retry; both reduce duplicates pending fix.
Runtime logs show queued-tool entries survive connection swap because queue is per-worker, not per-connection.
Deduplication currently relies on client-supplied idempotency token; if missing, server treats each enqueue as unique.
Multiplexed sessions allow retries to reuse logical stream identifiers; client immediate retries currently do not re-use/forward original token in this customer's wrapper.
Hypothesis: two independent code paths enqueued the same payload: the original in-flight path and the retry path after client reconnect. Without token, server cannot collapse them.
Repro steps run in staging reproduces at ~0.7% of requests when artificial swap injected; higher with aggressive client retry logic.
Potential edge case: cleanup TTL for queued-tool dedupe map configured to 30s; race window may be shorter than cleanup frequency.
Workaround provided to customer on 2026-03-13: a) enable per-tool idempotency tokens in their wrapper; b) add 150-300ms backoff before immediate retry; c) disable multiplexing as a short-term mitigation.
Engineering action items: (1) SDK: default to attaching idempotency-token header for tool calls and preserve it across retries (PR prepared by Rajiv K). (2) Runtime: implement server-side short-term dedupe by (session-id || request-hash) with a 60s TTL to collapse duplicate enqueues when token absent (proposal by Maya C). (3) Docs: add best-practice guidance for long-running tool calls under multiplexing with examples for Go/TS/Python (tracked in GH issue).
Planned rollout: SDK change staged in next minor release (v0.12.4) after review; runtime dedupe gated behind config flag for dedicated pools and will be rolled out to us-east-1 in canary first.
Follow-up: After SDK patch deployed, ask BrightCart to re-run repro and confirm no duplicates. If duplicates persist, collect full traces and reopen.

Issue summary: Customer reports repeated partial paragraph fragments and missing final end-marker when resuming SSE streams after a corporate VPN (split-tunnel) path migration. Impact: Multiple generation outputs are duplicated mid-paragraph and sometimes the final JSON/terminal marker is not received by the client, causing downstream parsers to hang. Occurs intermittently during mobile/workstation VPN re-route or NAT rebinding events. First reported by FinGrid on 2026-03-09 14:20 UTC.
1) Start a long-running SSE generation request from FinGrid client behind corporate split-tunnel VPN.
2) Trigger network path change (disconnect/reconnect VPN or move machine to external network) while stream is active.
3) Client reconnects and attempts to resume the SSE session using existing session token/cookie and resume offset header.
4) Observe duplicated mid-paragraph fragments and/or missing closing event (no 'end' marker).
client-log: conn=abcd1234, resume_offset=23174, observed_duplicate_fragment='...the transaction will be processed' repeated
edge-proxy: session_id=fg-9987, NAT_rebind=true, client_ip=10.1.5.23->54.210.12.8, resume_offset=23174 forwarded
serving-runtime: resume_validation: expected_offset=23180, incoming_offset=23174, kv_cache_lookup=miss -> partial replay applied
auth: sso-cookie-rotate at 2026-03-09T14:21:03Z for user=finops@fingrid.com
(Support) 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Acknowledged receipt. We need network traces from the customer and the client-side SSE raw stream to confirm the offset negotiation behavior.
(Customer) 2026-03-10 - FinGrid Ops (J. Morgan): Attached pcap and client raw events. Happens ~15% of reconnects during VPN re-routes. Parser downstream fails on ~40% of affected requests.
(SRE) 2026-03-11 - Miguel Alvarez: Reproduced locally by simulating NAT rebind and resume header mismatch. Observed server applied delta-replay that overlapped by 6 tokens, causing duplicated text. Missing end marker appears when edge LB drops final keepalive event during handoff.
(Support) 2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Temporary mitigation suggested - client should fully close and re-open a new stream when moving networks. Customer confirms acceptable as short-term workaround.
(Eng) 2026-03-13 - Priya Desai: Patch ready that adds a tolerance compare on resume offsets and forces explicit reconciliation of KV cache by client id. Deploying to canary this evening.
Hypothesis 1: NAT port rebind combined with SSO cookie rotation results in the client being associated with a different edge session id; resume offset forwarded to a different serving worker whose KV cache is offset by a few tokens -> duplicate fragments.
Hypothesis 2: Edge LB handoff drop can remove the final 'end' keepalive/control event while the client assumes stream continues, leaving client awaiting terminal marker.
Repro steps validated in staging with netem causing path migration and auth cookie refresh - duplicate fragments reproduced consistently when resume_offset < worker_expected_offset.
KV-cache mismatch trace: serving-runtime returned 'partial-replay' path that concatenated overlapping tokens instead of de-duplicating overlap region.
Observed correlation with longer-lived streams (>45s) and enterprises using split-tunnel VPNs.
Mitigation (short-term): Advise customers to close and re-open stream on network change. Support provided a client SDK snippet that falls back to full reconnect when NAT or IP change detected.
Fix (deployed 2026-03-13): Canary edge patch adds resume-offset tolerance logic: if incoming_offset <= expected_offset && overlap <= 12 tokens, trim overlap on server side rather than replaying. Also added explicit final-event ack forwarding during LB handoff.
Follow-up: Roll out patch to all edge regions on 2026-03-14 with monitoring dashboard for 'resume_overlap' metric. Create runbook entry describing detection and manual mitigation steps.
Customer follow-up: FinGrid validated canary and sees reduction of duplicates from ~15% to <1% on test cohort. They will schedule wider validation next week.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer Acme Cloud observed a sudden and repeatable p99 throughput regression on their dedicated pool during midday windows. The dips correlate with waves of short-lived tenant spinups (many 5–30s streams) after a marketing campaign. Impact: sustained ~30% drop in batch throughput and elevated queueing for ~3-6 minutes per wave.

Impact:
- Customer-facing inference latency spikes and degraded SLAs for batch-heavy endpoints
- Autoscaler temporarily failed to instrument capacity (delayed upscales) leading to request queueing and budgeted fallback model routing

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (Acme Cloud reserve), prod, us-west-2
- Mix of models (13B, 7B) with batching enabled and prefix-KV cache warmups

Observation summary:
Metrics show short bursts of many short streams that cause the allocator to take ~200-700ms stalls when assigning slots; these stalls accumulate, causing batchers to miss assembly windows and p99 throughput falls. NVME/io and GPU memory not saturated; traces point to allocator RPC latency and a spin-lock path in the GPU-allocator daemon that scales poorly for high churn of ephemeral connections.
Simulate 1,200 short-lived streams (5-30s) across 100 tenants over 60 seconds targeting dedicated pool slot-prefetch route
Observe allocator pod logs and batcher assembly p99 in Grafana (dashboard: dedicated/pool/slot-alloc)
Reproduce locally on staging with same concurrency and confirm slot-assignment latency spike
11:40 - Initial triage: ruled out NVIDIA driver or GPU OOM; GPU metrics steady, memory headroom present.
12:05 - Hypothesis A: autoscaler metrics pipeline lag causes delayed node adds. Counter-evidence: nodes were added but slot allocator still stalling.
12:30 - Hypothesis B: allocator contention under connection churn. Recreated in staging with synthetic short streams; observed identical slot_assign RPC latency spikes.
12:55 - Found allocator thread stack trace showing a lock held during connection tear-down code path (prefetch cancel path). Suspect contention between prefetch cancellation and new assignment operations.
13:15 - Discovered increased goroutine counts in allocator pods correlated with each wave; GC/pause times negligible but mutex contention high.
13:45 - Quick mitigation tested: bumping allocator pod replicas from 3 -> 6 reduced per-pod in-flight RPC and brought p99 throughput back to baseline under same load in staging.
14:10 - Further hypothesis: short-lived streams cause many simultaneous prefetch cancellations which invoke a cleanup routine that takes a lock over shared slot-index. Need code-level fix to narrow lock scope.
Links: Grafana (dedicated/pool/slot-alloc): https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/slot-alloc, Slack thread: #support-acme (https://slack.com/archives/C0123456)
Related investigation: see SUP-271400 for prefetch-related throughput anomalies (similar cancellation path implicated).
2026-03-13T11:34:12Z allocator[pid=1294]: slot_assign_start tenant=acct-ACME shard=3 request_id=...
2026-03-13T11:34:12Z allocator[pid=1294]: rpc_latency=0.62s peer=allocator-2 (count=14 in-flight)
2026-03-13T11:34:13Z batcher[pid=2201]: assemble_missed window=50ms reason=slot-delay p99=0.67s
Aisha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-13: Customer reported first occurrence at 11:30 PDT after email campaign. They are seeing p99 increases and multiple model fallbacks. Asking for urgent triage.
Riley Chen (SRE) - 2026-03-13: Triage started. Running synthetic load to reproduce; initial signs point to allocator RPC queuing. Putting alloc pods into debug mode to capture stacks.
Mateo Alvarez (Infra Eng) - 2026-03-13: Confirmed high mutex wait times in allocator at peak. Recommending temporary scale of allocator replicas as mitigation while we prepare a patch.
Riley Chen (SRE) - 2026-03-13: Scaled allocator replicas 3->6 in prod dedicated pool for Acme (change id: infra/scale/ACL-881). Observed throughput recovery within two waves. Customer notified of workaround.
Priya Raman (Allocator Owner) - 2026-03-14: Root cause narrowed to prefetch cancel path holding global slot-index lock. Preparing PR to replace coarse lock with per-shard lock; will run canary on staging.
Aisha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-14: Customer acknowledges temporary improvement but requests ETA on permanent fix and asks for retro on how to avoid future recurrence during campaigns.
Workaround applied: scaled allocator replicas from 3 to 6 for the affected dedicated pool (action id infra/scale/ACL-881). This reduced per-pod in-flight RPC and mitigated p99 throughput regressions for the observed waves. Root cause: allocator global lock contention in prefetch cancel code path under high churn of short-lived streams. Permanent fix: replace coarse global lock with per-shard locking and refactor cleanup to be non-blocking; patch PR opened and under code review (github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/912).
Deploy PR with per-shard locks to canary staging and run synthetic churn test (owner: Priya Raman, due: 2026-03-18)
Add autoscale rule to proactively add allocator capacity when short-stream connection churn > 500/s (owner: Mateo Alvarez, due: 2026-03-20)
Postmortem draft in Confluence and customer-facing RCA to be prepared (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-19)
Add targeted alerting for allocator mutex contention and per-pod goroutine growth (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-16)
Customer follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-15 10:00 PDT (calendar invite sent)

payload.description:
Customers report 504s from Redwood Console when uploading large prompt bundles (~30–120MB). Failures only occur for users routing through their corporate ADC (F5/Big-IP) that applies TCP optimizations. Browser shows gRPC-web stream reset / PROTOCOL_ERROR; server-side logs show aborted streams and SETTINGS frame sequence anomalies.
Issue summary: Intermittent upload failures and 504s observed in Redwood Console for a Private deployment. Failures reproduce only when the user's traffic flows through their on-prem ADC which performs HTTP/2/TCP optimizations. Impact: uploads fail to complete, leading to customer inability to persist prompt datasets and occasional console timeouts; affects a subset of users behind the ADC, not all tenants.
Multiple engineering users at Nimbus Security cannot upload prompt bundles via Console; some retry loops create duplicate upload attempts and token churn. Estimated 10–20% of uploads from within the corporate network fail during nightly ingestion batches.
Private deployment (customer-managed VPC, VPCE to Redwood control plane). Customer frontends traffic through an on-prem F5 BIG-IP ADC which terminates TLS and proxies upstream to the VPCE. ADC configured with HTTP/2 multiplexing, TCP coalescing, and an application profile that rewrites some SETTINGS behavior to minimize handshake RTTs.
1) Login to Redwood Console from a client inside Nimbus Security network.
2) Start a large prompt bundle upload (~30–120MB) via the Console 'Dataset > Upload' flow (uses gRPC-web over HTTP/2).
3) Observe upload progress; in failing cases upload stalls and Console eventually shows a 504 or 'Upload failed: stream reset'.
4) Reproduce is consistent when client is on the corp network and routing through ADC; bypassing the ADC (direct internet or mobile tether) completes upload successfully.
5) Packet captures and ADC access logs were captured by the customer and attached below.
gRPC-web stream resets mid-upload, Console logs show 'STREAM_RESET' or 'PROTOCOL_ERROR'. Server logs report aborted streams, and HTTP/2 trace shows SETTINGS frames arriving out of expected order or with coalesced payloads. ADC logs show an optimization labeled 'http2-settings-coalesce' and TCP coalescing across small writes.
Uploads should complete without stream resets; HTTP/2 SETTINGS and WINDOW_UPDATE frames should arrive intact and in-order so the gRPC runtime can maintain the stream. Console should return success and persist the dataset.
Customer-provided tcpdump (snippet): frame 12345: TLS record: Handshake
    frame 12346: HTTP/2 SETTINGS (initial)
    frame 12348: HTTP/2 SETTINGS (ack) coalesced-with WINDOW_UPDATE
    frame 12350: DATA (partial) -> stream reset
ADC syslog excerpt: Mar 10 10:12:34 bigip1 INFO http2:settings-coalesce enabled profile=low-latency; coalesced_frames=12
Console client error (browser console): gRPC-Web: transport error; code=2; message=Stream reset (code=PROTOCOL_ERROR)
Server side trace id: trace-redwood-98231 (attached request ids across aborted uploads)
Customer-provided ADC config excerpt (redacted): http2 profile with 'coalesce-settings' and 'tcp-latency-opt' enabled

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 16:10 - SRE: Captured server-side HTTP/2 frame trace. Observed SETTINGS frames grouped and a WINDOW_UPDATE inserted before SETTINGS_ACK which triggers our gRPC runtime to treat the stream as out-of-order leading to PROTOCOL_ERROR.
2026-03-10 17:45 - Eng: Reviewed gRPC-web client behavior; client library expects SETTINGS/ACK handshake before application DATA on a new stream. ADC coalescing merges control frames and packets such that ordering is not preserved from server perspective.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Support: Requested customer to temporarily disable 'http2 settings coalesce' and 'tcp-latency-opt' on ADC; they agreed to test during a maintenance window.
2026-03-11 14:05 - Customer: Re-tested with optimizations disabled; upload success rate returned to baseline. ADC vendor notes indicate an optional patch that alters SETTINGS handling for legacy backend stacks.
2026-03-12 11:00 - Eng: Determined a safe client-side retry/backoff change can make uploads more robust to short control-frame reordering, but fix is non-trivial and may mask real protocol violations.
2026-03-11 - Customer (Nimbus): Disabled 'http2-settings-coalesce' during window and reported successful uploads. Customer will engage ADC vendor for a permanent patch.
On-prem ADC is rewriting/coalescing HTTP/2 control frames (SETTINGS/ACK/WINDOW_UPDATE) and delivering them to the backend in a combined TCP segment. The gRPC-web client and our HTTP/2 stack interpret the reordered/coalesced frames as a protocol error, leading to stream resets. Bypassing ADC shows success, disabling coalescing in ADC resolves the issue.
1) Ask customer to disable 'http2-settings-coalesce' and any TCP coalescing/latency optimizations on their ADC for paths to the VPCE.
2) If disabling is not possible, recommend bypassing ADC for uploads (split upload endpoint via direct egress subnet) during their migration window.
3) Console-side: implement a guarded retry for uploads that fail with PROTOCOL_ERROR (limited retries to avoid duplication).
- Engineering to evaluate robust handling of unexpected control-frame ordering in the HTTP/2 stack; prototype safe retry/backoff logic for gRPC-web uploads (Q2 work item).
- Docs: Add ADC/ADC-profile guidance to Private deploy runbook (confluence page) describing HTTP/2 profiles known to break gRPC-web.
- Support: Add a diagnostic check to onboarding checklist that flags 'http2-settings-coalesce' or similar ADC optimizations.
- Follow-up with customer: Confirm ADC vendor patch schedule and re-open if patch doesn't remediate.
- Add unit test in runtime to simulate SETTINGS coalescing to observe client behavior.
In Progress - temporary mitigation verified. Customer disabled ADC coalescing and reported upload success during maintenance window. Engineering to scope a resilient client-side mitigation and add runbook guidance. Pending verification after customer's vendor patch.
1) Eng to produce a small RFC for safe upload retry behavior and run it by security/rate-limiting teams (owner: Lara Chen, due 2026-03-19).
2) Support to update onboarding checklist and confluence guidance (owner: Maya Singh, due 2026-03-16).
3) Customer to confirm ADC vendor patch and provide test date; Support to revalidate.
4) Keep ticket open until customer's patched ADC validated in prod for 48h of normal ingestion cycles.

Issue summary: A scheduled payout for vendor 'NordPoint Shipping GmbH' was flagged by the bank on payout day due to a payee name mismatch and IBAN formatting concerns. Treasury put the transaction on hold to avoid rejection. Impact: vendor payment delayed, potential late-fee exposure and vendor escalation to Partnerships. This ticket coordinates AP, Treasury, and Vendor Ops to validate identity and release the payment.
1) Vendor submitted invoice INV-2026-334 via vendor portal on 2026-03-05 with payee 'NordPoint Shipping' (no legal suffix).
2) AP approved invoice and created a scheduled payrun for 2026-03-12 through NetSuite/Payments service.
3) Treasury submitted ACH/SEPA instruction to bank for execution; bank returned a reject/hold citing 'payee name does not match beneficiary records' and flagged IBAN formatting (extra non-ASCII characters).
4) Treasury placed payrun on hold, notified AP and Vendor Ops; vendor opened an escalation thread in #vendor-ops on Slack.

Vendor portal submission metadata: vendor_profile_id=VND-9082; payee_display='NordPoint Shipping'; attached_business_registry='Hand-signed PDF, company name: NordPoint Shipping GmbH'

Issue summary: After a customer-directed route weight adjustment this morning, Atlas reported a sustained rise in 5xx responses from the API (primarily 502/503). Impact: ~18% of requests for the tenant returned 5xx over a 22-minute window, causing user-facing failures in chat and embedding uploads. Environment: Dedicated tenant in prod (us-east) using pinned instances and prefetch enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Apply route weight change (route weight shifted from default pool -> new pool) 2) Resume normal traffic ramp for tenant 3) Observe elevated 5xxs and increased runtime restart counts Observed behavior: API gateway returns 502/503; serving runtimes show repeated model-prefetch evictions and KV cache miss storms. Runtime logs contain frequent "prefetch-lock-timeout" and "connection lease expired" messages. Expected behavior: Route weight change should redirect traffic without increasing 5xx floor; prefetch cache eviction should be graceful without triggering runtime crash/restarts. Initial hypothesis: Misrouted traffic landed on a small set of warm runtimes while a prefetch-eviction race left those runtimes with tainted kvcache states; combined with ingress prioritizer dropping lower-priority requests, this led to priority-queue starvation and upstream connection churn causing 5xx amplification.
13:02 UTC - Alert: tenant Atlas saw error-rate jump from baseline 0.6% -> 18%. Notified via #support and #incidents.
13:05 UTC - api-gateway metrics show surge in upstream 502s; 95th latency for successful requests increased from 220ms -> 1.4s.
13:08 UTC - serving-runtime team observed repeated "prefetch-lock-timeout" and kvcache eviction spikes on three nodes (node ids: s-ea-12, s-ea-15, s-ea-23).
13:12 UTC - ingress prioritizer logs show several priority-shed events for tenant traffic coincident with route weight change (link: slack://channel#incidents/clip-xyz).
13:18 UTC - Identified that connection leases to the runtime pool expired aggressively due to a stale client keepalive policy during the traffic handoff.
13:24 UTC - Correlated runtime restarts with a prefetch eviction bug where tainted entries triggered heavy KV lock contention (see runtime PR attempt: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4582).
Support (Ethan Myers) 13:10: Thanks for reporting, Atlas. We're triaging — can you confirm if you changed route weights or did this via the Console rollouts?
Customer (Atlas SRE - Maria Lopez) 13:11: We applied a 60/40 weight shift to a new pool at 12:58 UTC as part of a planned capacity migration. We saw errors within ~4 minutes.
Support (Priya Shah) 13:16: Noted. Engineering is looking at prefetch/kvcache metrics and ingress prioritizer traces. Posting initial investigation in #incidents: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/CINC12345/p164...
Eng (Jin Park) 13:22: Found repeated "kvcache:taint_detected" events on s-ea-15; runtime restarted after OOM fragmentation on driver. Hypothesis: eviction race left kvcache locks held causing downstream timeouts.
Eng (Priya Shah) 13:30: Applied short-term mitigation: temporarily pinned Atlas route to previous pool, increased connection lease TTL on the client side, and invalidated prefetch index for the tenant. Error rate dropped to 1.7% within 6 minutes.
Customer (Maria Lopez) 13:37: Confirmed traffic recovery and reduced user errors. Requesting postmortem and long-term fixes.
Support (Priya Shah) 13:55: Creating follow-ups: (1) fix eviction race in runtime (PR linked), (2) add graceful prefetch invalidation on route changes, (3) add ingress prioritizer backoff on rapid weight changes.
Workaround applied: rolled back route weight to original pool, increased client connection lease TTL, and issued a tenant-specific prefetch invalidation which reduced the 5xx rate to baseline. Permanent remediation planned: runtime patch to prevent tainted-kv eviction races (PR opened), change Console rollout to perform staged weight shifts with ingress backoff, and add a runtime-side guard to refuse prefetch invalidation storms. Postmortem scheduled and runbook updated.
Short-term: rollback weight + prefetch invalidate (13:30 UTC) — immediate decrease in 5xxs.
Medium-term: runtime PR to serialize prefetch evictions and avoid taint (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4582) — targeted deploy 2026-03-18.
Long-term: Console change to staged rollouts with minimum grace window and ingress prioritizer smoothing to prevent priority starvation during pool transitions.
Follow-up action: update dedicated-customer runbook for weight shifts and add automated tenant prefetch drain on route changes.
