payload.description:
Issue summary
- Northwind Commerce noticed an elevated p95 latency window on their Dedicated cluster while Marketing/SE were collecting performance numbers for a planned public case study.
- The spike was transient (~18 minutes) but would materially change any "single-window" p95 figure if captured during that interval.

Customer impact
- Endpoint: /v1/chat.completions (streaming + non-streaming)
- Impact: p95 increased from baseline ~430–520ms to ~1.6–2.1s; p99 peaked ~3.8s.
- Error rate: no sustained 5xx increase; brief uptick in 429s due to queue protection (max in-flight).
- User-visible symptoms: slower first-token latency on some requests; a few retries observed by Northwind.

Context (why ticket was opened)
- This was surfaced during case study preparation (interview + metric capture). We need to:
  1) confirm whether the spike was a platform issue vs workload change,
  2) ensure mitigations prevent recurrence during future measurement windows,
  3) document the event so published metrics are measured over an appropriate window (e.g., 7–30 days) and/or exclude known maintenance events.

Timeline (UTC)
- 2025-10-09 16:42: Northwind reports "latency feels off" in Slack via CSM; SE flags risk to published p95.
- 16:46: Support opens SUP-3812; on-call begins triage.
- 16:50–17:08: p95 elevated; queue depth rises; autoscaler events noted.
- 17:10: Tail latency returns to baseline without customer changes.
- 17:35: Initial hypothesis shared with SE/Marketing; agree to avoid quoting that window.

Observability / dashboards
- Dedicated overview (Grafana): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/ded-nw/northwind-dedicated-overview?from=2025-10-09T16:30:00Z&to=2025-10-09T18:00:00Z
- API p95 by route (Datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/3xq-9qk-7eu/northwind-api-latency?from_ts=1760027400000&to_ts=1760032800000
- Scheduler queue depth: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/sched-q/scheduler-queue-depth?var=cluster=northwind-dedicated-us-east
- Node events (maintenance/drain): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/k8s-ev/k8s-events?var=namespace=nw-dedicated

What we checked
- Workload: No evidence of a step-function traffic increase from Northwind; request rate remained within typical burst bounds (+8% vs same weekday baseline).
- Model/version: No model rollout; pinned model version unchanged.
- Platform: K8s events showed a single GPU node drain/replace in the Dedicated pool coincident with the spike.

Investigation notes (most likely cause)
- Root cause: transient capacity reduction during a node drain (kernel security patch) combined with conservative surge settings for the deployment, leading to fewer ready replicas for ~10–15 minutes.
- Contributing factors:
  - Warm-up for the replacement node took longer than expected (image pull + cache warm), increasing request queue depth.
  - Autoscaler reacted, but scale-up lag (GPU provisioning) meant tail latency increased before capacity stabilized.

Mitigation applied
- Short-term (same day):
  - Increased min_replicas for Northwind Dedicated deployment from 6 -> 8 during business hours.
  - Adjusted pod disruption budget to reduce simultaneous unready capacity during drains.
  - Coordinated with Infra to pause non-urgent maintenance on Northwind’s Dedicated pool during the case study measurement week.
- Follow-up hardening:
  - Added an alert on "ready replicas < desired" + queue depth correlation for Dedicated clusters.
  - Documented recommended measurement window guidance for Marketing/SE: use rolling 7-day p95 (excluding maintenance/drain events) or present a range with a footnote.

Customer comms
- We informed Northwind that we identified a transient capacity event (node drain) and applied safeguards to reduce the chance of recurrence. No action required on their side.

Resolution
- Latency returned to baseline at 2025-10-09 17:10 UTC.
- Preventative changes are in place (min replicas + PDB + maintenance pause).
- Guidance provided to Marketing/SE to avoid quoting p95 captured during the impacted interval; use an agreed measurement window for publication.

Next steps / action items
1) Infra: validate node warm-up time on Dedicated pools; ensure image pre-pull + model cache warm path for replacement nodes (linked PR: redwood-inference/infra#19344).
2) Runtime: add "pre-warm" hook to reduce first-request penalty after replica replacement (linked PR: redwood-runtime#8821).
3) Support Ops: add a checklist item for case study metric capture: confirm no maintenance/drain events in the selected interval.

Attachments
- Screenshots of queue depth + p95 charts saved in #support-internal thread (ref: Slack link in comments).

Additional notes:
Resolved after identifying a transient Dedicated pool capacity reduction due to a GPU node drain/replacement, which temporarily reduced ready replicas and increased queue depth. Applied mitigations (higher min_replicas during business hours, PDB tightening, temporary maintenance freeze) and documented guidance to exclude the affected interval from case study metric capture. No further customer action required.
payload.summary: Northwind Commerce (Dedicated): transient p95 latency spike during case study measurement/interview window

Issue summary:
Customer requires a formalized delivery and verification model for audit telemetry to satisfy a regulatory evidence request. They want an immutable handoff using scheduled SFTP batches, each accompanied by a signed manifest (HMAC per batch) and a deterministic resume token so they can stitch events across days. Key asks: per-batch HMAC and manifest, deterministic event IDs, proof of monotonic ordering (including handling of late-arriving events), timezone canonicalization to UTC with signed checkpoints, and a short sample package that demonstrates preservation of per-event context (tenant IDs, request_id, model_version). Customer also requests KMS entropy proof showing that per-batch signing keys are rotated and attestable for the audit window.
N/A - this is an onboarding / export specification request rather than a runtime bug. Customer provided examples of their ingest expectations and a small CDC feeder that produced out-of-order events when replayed into their SIEM; they need guidance to ensure Redwood's export ordering semantics satisfy legal-chain requirements.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - Customer: Attached sample CSV and desired manifest schema (sha256_hmac, first_timestamp, last_timestamp, batch_sequence, resume_token, record_count). Also included a short legal questionnaire excerpt asking for KMS rotation proof and HSM attestation.
2026-03-13 - Eng (Nina Koh): Confirmed we support per-batch signing via service key, but customer requests KMS-backed HSM attestation and rotation history which requires coordination with Security and KMS team. We recommend an initial iterative deliverable: (1) signed manifest with HMAC (service key), (2) deterministic resume token (sha256 of first+last+batch_seq+tenant), (3) sample replay and verification script for customer. KMS/HSM attestation will be scoped separately.
Support triage 2026-03-11: Determine whether existing SFTP export supports manifest generation and resume tokens. Found export pipeline supports contiguous snapshots but not explicit per-batch HMAC manifests. Current checkpoints use signed JWT tokens for internal resume only.
Eng 2026-03-12: Reviewed export codepath. Two extension points: batch manifest generator (worker) and post-process hook to upload manifest to same SFTP folder. Deterministic resume token can be derived from event envelope fields; must agree canonicalization (UTC timestamps, canonical JSON field ordering).
Eng 2026-03-12: Late-arriving events - Redwood export is eventually consistent; ordering guarantees are per-ingest-shard sequence, not global. For legal evidence, propose including event_serial (per-producer monotonic counter) and server_receive_ts to help reconstruct ordering. Documented reconstruction algorithm in draft Confluence.
Security 2026-03-13: KMS attestation path requires exposing rotation logs and signed key metadata (key_id, rotation_time, signer_fingerprint). We can provide rotation audit from KMS but full HSM attestation will need SOC/security engagement and likely a formal ATO amendment for export scope.
Support 2026-03-13: Customer sample replay found 12 events with timestamp skew >5s; propose normalizing timestamps to canonical UTC and including original_timestamp field for forensic tracing.
Proposed phased deliverable: Phase 1 (ETA 2026-03-20): generate per-batch manifest (JSON) containing batch_sequence, first_timestamp_utc, last_timestamp_utc, record_count, sha256_hmac (using service signing key), deterministic resume_token. Provide a verification script and sample 1-day bundle for customer validation. Phase 2 (scoped, ETA TBD after security sign-off): KMS-backed signed manifests with rotation history report and HSM attestation artifacts. Customer to confirm Phase 1 acceptance to proceed.

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightCart (dedicated) is asking for two things: 1) a visual heatmap in the Console showing token consumption by refill window over time so they can identify microburst hotspots, and 2) concrete guidance and option to configure a custom smoothing/refill window per-tenant to avoid short-lived 429 spikes during mixed realtime + bulk embedding workloads.

Customer note: They run a hybrid ingest pipeline: a continuous realtime chat surface (~5qps) plus intermittently scheduled bulk embedding batches (concurrent workers). They observe occasional identical short 429 spikes across many API keys in the org during batch start times even though overall token usage is under committed capacity. They want to both understand the traffic pattern (visual) and be able to reduce the short spike exposure without sacrificing steady throughput.
Intermittent 429s for a small percentage of chat flows during scheduled embedding job starts. Customer reports user-visible chat timeouts ~0.1-0.5% during batch kicks which impacts SLAs for certain pages. No billing discrepancies reported.
1) Customer schedules concurrent embedding worker job (200 parallel workers) to start at 02:00 UTC.
2) At the same time, realtime clients continue to send chat requests.
3) Observed behavior: a cluster of 429 responses for short windows (3-6s) immediately after batch jobs start.
4) Staggering the batch start by 30s reduces, but does not eliminate, the short bursts.
Attached: sample trace IDs from BrightCart (trace: bc-20260310-1, bc-20260310-2), token_bucket_refill Grafana panel link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rl_windows/token_bucket_refill?org=brightcart, sampling of request/response headers showing X-RateLimit-* for affected requests (pasted in comments).
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Logged with SRE and assigned Diego. Requested sample API keys, traces, and approximate batch start schedule.
Customer (BrightCart) 2026-03-10: Provided traces and schedule. Confirmed they're on a dedicated pool with reserved capacity and using default tenant smoothing settings.
SRE (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-11: Initial hypothesis: refill window alignment across edge proxies may be creating transient double-accounting when large fanouts happen at near-same second boundaries. Requested edge proxy logs and NAT mapping table snapshot for the batch start time.
SRE (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-11: Also asked engineering to check token-bucket refill algorithm and rounding behavior for short windows. Added link to internal runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/RateLimit+Debug+Runbook.
Customer (BrightCart) 2026-03-11: Asked if Redwood can temporarily increase burst window for their tenant to avoid user-facing errors while we investigate.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12: Confirmed temporary burst increase is possible as a stopgap. Scheduled a maintenance config change for 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC with planned rollback if no improvement.
SRE (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-12: Post-change note: short spikes reduced by ~85% in sampled window; still observed rare 429s when batch workers start with <5s skew.
Hypothesis A: Refill alignment skew at the edge. Our token refill runs on a 1s tick; edge proxies with slightly different clocks cause multiple requests to be counted in adjacent buckets leading to transient double-throttle signals.
Hypothesis B: HTTP/2 multiplexing and connection reuse from pooled proxies can cause per-connection accounting to be misattributed when worker fanout occurs, slightly amplifying the token draw in origin accounting.
Data: Grafana panel shows refill histogram spikes at 02:00:01 and 02:00:02 UTC with a tight cluster of high token consumption events. NAT table snapshot indicates 14k concurrent connections re-used by the bulk upload workers across 6 proxy nodes at start time.
Finding: Edge proxies were configured with a 250ms clock lead relative to origin, causing some refill events to be applied earlier at the edge. Combined with worker fanout starting within the same second, earliest requests are occasionally counted twice during the alignment window. This is amplified for dedicated customers using pooled proxy IPs and HTTP/2 multiplexing.
Temporary mitigation applied: increased tenant burst window to +50% for 24 hours and enabled a per-tenant smoothing flag on the rate-limiter. Observed ~85% reduction in user-facing 429s for the sampled job run.
Root cause summary: refill tick alignment + connection pooling + high-concurrency job start produces transient accounting artifacts that manifest as short 429 spikes for realtime flows overlapping batch starts.
Metrics and links: token_bucket_refill histogram, request qps overlay, and edge-proxy-clock-drift panel (links attached above).
Short-term workaround: Increased tenant burst allowance and enabled per-tenant smoothing. Customer to stagger batch starts by >=10s for best results until console visualization rollout.
Medium-term remediation: Engineering to add a 'refill-heatmap' panel to Console showing per-refill-window token usage (work started, PR referenced). This will let customers see microburst hotspots and choose smoothing windows intentionally.
Long-term fix: Scheduler change to make refill alignment origin-driven (single authoritative tick) and to add configurable per-tenant smoothing/refill-window sizes in the Console. Follow-up epic planned: INT-22098 (rate-limiter: per-tenant window config + UI).
Follow-up items: (1) Add a KB article for hybrid workload best practices and recommended smoothing settings; (2) Run a short experiment to enable origin-driven refill alignment for 10 dedicated tenants and measure effect; (3) Ensure documentation of recommended embed-worker start jitter in Quickstarts.
Status: Temporary config applied 2026-03-12; medium-term Console panel PR merged to staging. Customer confirmed reduced user impact and requested Console ETA - target Q2 2026 for GA of heatmap feature.
payload.summary: Rate-limit heatmap request and guidance for custom refill/window smoothing to avoid short spikes

payload.description:
Issue summary: FocusText.ai reports recurring spikes in rerank tail latency (~500-1200ms) and nondeterministic top-k ordering for a subset of requests. Spikes correlate with embedding cache TTL expirations which cause synchronous refetch + reranker CPU fallback. Impact: user-facing search ranking instability and increased P95/P99 latency. Environment: Dedicated customer pool in us-east, embedding cache is Redis cluster with per-namespace TTL. Temporal pattern: spikes appear when cache misses spike after periodic namespace TTL sweeps or backfills.
Search API P95 increased from 120ms to 700-1200ms for ~2-5% of requests during cache churn windows; reported customer-facing ranking changes and occasional 503s from the reranker with traceback referencing CPU fallback path.
1) Use customer dataset and send sustained 500 req/s embedding+rerank workload against dedicated pool in us-east
2) Set embedding cache TTL artificially low (simulate rolling TTL expiry) or trigger namespace backfill to induce mass cache misses
3) Observe reranker latency and top-k ordering for requests that miss cache vs warm requests
4) Capture logs from proxy, cache, and reranker services during TTL expiry window
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z reranker ERROR cpu_fallback_path.cpp:142 - fallback due to missing GPU kvcache, processing in FP32 CPU mode, request_id=aa3f4b
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z cache INFO redis: cache_miss namespace=focustext:docs key=embed:12345
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z proxy WARN proxy_manager: queue_growth - client_qsize=80, worker_qsize=0, backpressure=true
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z metrics gauge reranker.p99_ms=1120 tags:customer=FocusText.ai,region=us-east
Hypothesis A: Mass cache-miss events force synchronous embed recompute which then routes to GPU but falls back to CPU when kv cache unavailable leading to slower FP32 code path and nondet floating point ordering.
Hypothesis B: Embedding variant mismatch between cached vectors (embedder-v1-1536) and live model (embedder-v2-1024) triggers additional normalization path that runs on CPU. We found a small number of stale cache entries with legacy shape headers in redis during incident window.
Checked dashboards: saw correlated spikes on redis eviction rate and reranker.cpu_util; GPU nodes reported transient kv-cache connection errors (logs reference transient gRPC timeouts to kv-store).
Reproduced locally by expiring cache namespace and instrumenting reranker: observed FP32 path uses a different normalization routine which produces slight cosine differences leading to top-k order changes for near-tie candidates.
Related PR discovered that changed embedder alias routing two weeks ago: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/128 - it introduced alias fallback logic that may populate legacy-shaped embeddings into cache during a rollout.
Customer workload patterns: periodic nightly backfills from FocusText.ai coincide with the cache-sweep windows and increase miss storms.
Support (Asha): Initial triage with customer and asked for request ids and a short reproduction script. Customer provided sample request ids and their nightly backfill schedule.
SRE (Diego): Noted redis eviction burst and temporary gRPC kv-store timeouts between 14:11 and 14:15. Adding temporary autoscale to cache replicas for mitigation.

Additional notes:
Customer (FocusText.ai - Ben): Able to throttle backfills which reduces frequency of spikes; requests a long-term fix and SLA credit investigation.
Eng (Marco): Working on hotfix to avoid running CPU normalization for embed sizes we don't support and to enforce strict dimension validation on cache write/read.
Mitigations applied: 1) Temporarily increased cache replica count and adjusted eviction thresholds for the customer's namespace to reduce TTL churn. 2) Added temporary rate limiter on backfill ingestion for dedicated pools. 3) Deployed hotfix to router to reject writing legacy-shaped embeddings into active cache namespaces (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/140). 4) Added defensive check in reranker to prefer GPU normalization path or defer request with 429 to upstream when fallback would cause nondet scoring. Follow-ups: schedule permanent fix to normalization convergence on CPU/GPU parity, add alerting for cache-shape-mismatch, and prepare SLA credit proposal for customer. Currently status: mitigation live; working on code fix and permanent tests.
ENG: Complete parity tests for CPU/GPU normalization and land fixes to reranker normalization routines (owner: Marco) - target 2026-03-18
SRE: Add cache-shape-mismatch alerting and increase default cache replica autoscale for dedicated pools (owner: Diego) - target 2026-03-14
CS: Prepare SLA credit estimate and remediation communication for customer (owner: Priya) - target 2026-03-15

Issue summary: During a regional canary backfill (preemptive capacity warmup) tenant requests pinned to a specific model variant were partially redirected to standby nodes that did not preserve pin metadata. Impact: customers saw mixed-model outputs (tokenization/format deltas) and a transient billing spike because requests hit higher-cost standby variants. This affected interactive chat sessions for a subset of NovaChat users and caused confusion in their QA cohort runs.

Observed timeframe: 2025-11-04 09:10 - 2025-11-04 10:40 UTC in us-east region.

Expected: Prewarm/backfill should not reassign or migrate pinned cohort mappings until pin metadata and affinity tokens are carried to target pool, or should honor pin affinity and fall back gracefully.

Notes: Customer reports reproducible within their long-lived session tokens when traffic overlapped with our orchestrator's preemptive backfill window.

Mixed-model outputs for ~120 user sessions, intermittent 5xx rate increase for pinned endpoints, and a billing spike (~12% more inference units for affected tenant over 90 minutes). Business impact: customer QA runs invalidated; potential SLA breach for latency/consistency during canary window.
1) Customer pins tenant to redwood/gpt-medium-v2 via model_version pin header.
2) Trigger sustained traffic from pinned session while orchestrator runs scheduled preemptive backfill in us-east.
3) Observe session responses intermittently switching to the standby variant (higher-cost quantized build) and tokenization differences.
4) Check serving logs for cohort reassignment entries around backfill timestamp.
edge-proxy[2025-11-04T09:13:02Z] INFO request-id=abc123 cohort_lookup=COHORT:tenant-42 pin_token=tok-9a8b missing_on_target=true -- orchestrator assigned backfill-target=node-standby-07
serving-runtime[2025-11-04T09:13:02Z] WARN model_variant=redwood/gpt-medium-v2-quantized tokenization_delta=+2 bytes request_id=abc123 -- emitting fallback-log
billing[2025-11-04T09:14:05Z] INFO tenant=NovaChat units_charged=452 expected_baseline=404

Initial hypothesis: preemptive backfill job moved traffic to standby nodes without carrying cohort pin metadata (pin_token absent on target).
Telemetry shows orchestrator 'backfill-assign' path marks targets as warm but omits cohort-metadata copy when target state = 'standby'.
Edge logs show cohort_lookup succeeded on source but cohort token returned 'missing_on_target=true' for backfill target. Service mesh retry paths then routed to fallback variant under cost-tier ladder.
Reproduced in controlled staging by triggering scheduled backfill; confirmed cohort mapping not copied for nodes in 'standby' pool when prewarm job uses fast-path optimization.

Issue summary: Customer reports that new service account tokens cannot perform delegated admin ops (user management and billing read) after migrating to a private deployment token broker. Impact: Multiple automation jobs and SRE runbooks fail; customer-facing admin UI returns 403 when acting-as a service account. Environment: Private deployment (Aurora private VPC), prod - us-east, Redwood private control plane with identity-proxy v1.9.2 and token-broker v0.8.2. Observed start: 2026-03-09 18:20 UTC. Business impact: Blocks Aurora's automated onboarding and scheduled invoice exports; they are a HIPAA-regulated customer and cannot proceed with several tasks until impersonation works.
1) Create service account 'onboard-runner@aurora' in Aurora tenant. 2) Request token via Aurora's token-broker that exchanges internal long-lived key for a short-lived access token. 3) Call Admin API /v1/admin/users with X-Redwood-Impersonate header set to 'user:alice@aurora.com' and Authorization: Bearer <token>. 4) Observe 403 'insufficient_scope' returned. 5) Same call with the original human user's token succeeds.
identity-proxy (2026-03-09T18:21:12Z) WARN request_id=3fa2ed 'token scope mismatch: expected [admin:impersonate,admin:users] got [service:read,service:write]'; admin-api (2026-03-09T18:21:12Z) ERROR request_id=3fa2ed 'authorization failed for impersonation: missing permission admin:impersonate'; token-broker (2026-03-09T18:20:58Z) INFO 'issued token sub=svc:onboard-runner aud=redwood-api scope="service:read service:write" exp=2026-03-09T19:20:58Z'
Initial hypothesis: token-broker is attaching default service scopes rather than tenant-mapped impersonation scopes. Confirmed that tenant mapping rule set 'aurora-mappings' in token-broker was not applied after the private control-plane upgrade (v0.8.0->v0.8.2). Identity-proxy performs additional scope filtering: it strips any scope not in allowed_scope_table for service accounts. Allowed_scope_table for Aurora appears to be stale and only lists 'service:*' scopes. Replayed token exchange locally with debug flags: mapping step returned intended impersonation grant, but the token-broker's caching layer served an earlier cached token profile. Cache invalidation appears tied to last-deploy timestamp; deployment delta on 2026-03-08 likely left cache entries inconsistent. Cross-referenced with INT-4112 where SRE rolled out token-broker config but noted a missing cache-buster flag. Observed related PR that changed default scopes (see related_github_prs).
Temporary workaround provided to customer: 1) Use a human admin token for critical admin calls. 2) As short-term automated fix, update identity-proxy config to whitelist the service account 'onboard-runner@aurora' with an explicit mapping to include admin:impersonate and admin:users. Provided steps and a patch snippet to Aurora engineering. Note this bypass is allowed only in their private VPC and will be removed after full fix.
Investigating full fix: coordinated deploy sequence to invalidate token-broker cache and roll token-broker + identity-proxy together with a cache-buster flag. SRE to schedule an out-of-band config reload for Aurora's token-broker and then redeploy identity-proxy v1.9.3 which contains a protective check to reject stale cached scope profiles. After reload, verified token exchange returns token with scopes [admin:impersonate,admin:users] and admin API calls succeed. Resolution steps documented in confluence page and will be included in a postmortem. Customer notified and temporary whitelist removed. Planned follow-up: add integration test in CI to simulate config drift and prevent mapping cache staleness.
Support (Maya Chen) [2026-03-09T19:05Z]: Ticket created after Aurora CS reported 403 on impersonation endpoints. I requested logs and a live replay session. Assigned to Ethan from SRE.
SRE (Ethan Park) [2026-03-09T20:12Z]: Confirmed 403s in customer's request traces. Found token scope on exchanged tokens only has service:* scopes. Suspect token-broker mapping/caching. Pulling broker logs and cache state now.
Customer (Aurora - Priya Desai) [2026-03-10T01:33Z]: We saw this start right after you performed the private-control-plane upgrade last week. The automation jobs that create users are failing and we need a short-term bypass.
SRE (Ethan Park) [2026-03-10T03:00Z]: Provided a temporary whitelist patch and instructions to apply in their private VPC. We will not keep this as permanent; it's a stopgap. Planning coordinated cache invalidation and redeploy for 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC.
Support (Maya Chen) [2026-03-12T02:30Z]: Scheduled the deploy window and confirmed Aurora's approval for the maintenance window. Will notify when done.
SRE (Ethan Park) [2026-03-12T02:47Z]: Performed cache invalidation and rolled identity-proxy v1.9.3. Observed token-broker issuing tokens with admin scopes. Runbook verification: admin API calls now return 200 for impersonation tests.
Customer (Aurora - Priya Desai) [2026-03-12T03:10Z]: Confirmed our automation jobs are back to normal. Thank you. Please share postmortem and remediation steps for our auditors.
Support (Maya Chen) [2026-03-13T09:00Z]: Postmortem draft shared to confluence. Marking the ticket as In Progress until follow-up CI test is merged and temporary whitelist is removed.

Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running WebSocket chat streams periodically end with an unclosed JSON choice and duplicated partial tokens when the client is behind a corporate proxy/fanout. Impact:
- End users receive an incomplete JSON object and client SDK parse errors; conversations stop rendering and must be retried.
- Symptoms appear for ~8% of long streams (>30s) from the BrightDocs dedicated deployment.
Environment:
- BrightDocs dedicated account on prod us-east-1, API gateway + our edge proxy cluster in same region. Runs redwood-rlhf-7b model pinned at v2026-02-15. Customer using JS SDK v2.4.1 over browser WebSocket with multiplexed session mode.
Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Start a multiplexed WS session with two concurrent chat streams from a browser behind the corporate proxy; keep one stream open > 30s with streaming responses.
2) After intermittent network activity (edge probe or proxy rebind), the client receives what appears to be a fragmented binary frame sequence.
3) Client logs show partial JSON payloads (no closing brace) and duplicated token prefixes when reconnect/resume occurs.
4) The SDK fails to reassemble the final choice and throws a parse exception; UI shows partial sentence and stops.
Observed logs / errors from customer:
- "SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input" in SDK parser on final message.
- Client debug shows WS frames arriving with non-monotonic frame indices and duplicate prefix bytes.
- TCP-level traces show the corporate proxy coalescing and reordering SSE/WS fragments during a keepalive probe.
Additional notes:
- Customer reports workaround: switching to plain (non-multiplexed) single-session WS eliminated the failure in their tests.
- Problem occurs less frequently from non-corporate networks (home/other cloud), suggesting middlebox involvement.
Support (Aisha): Triage - Received from BrightDocs support rep on 2026-03-10 14:20. Reproduced once in staging using a local proxy shim that injects reorder/fragment behavior.
CS (Jordan Lin): Confirmed customer is on dedicated plan and provided request IDs for several failed streams: rq_20260310_87fd, rq_20260310_94ab. Asking SRE for edge proxy request logs.
SRE (Mateo): Pulling edge-proxy logs and TCP captures for the time windows. Initial look shows several FIN/ACK + keepalive sequences coalesced by the upstream corporate proxy leading to out-of-order WS fragments at our gateway.
Action: capture 1h of pcap for customer IP and correlate with request IDs.
Eng (Priya): Hypothesis - our WS multiplexing expects ordered binary frame delivery for chunk assembly; if upstream shuffles small TCP segments we can observe partial JSON reassembly failure. Suggest adding defensive reordering detection and buffer until a complete JSON message boundary is observed. Will spike patch to SDK and server-side parser.
Customer (BrightDocs): Confirmed we can reproduce reliably when using corporate proxy appliance A with aggressive connection pooling. Non-corporate networks do not reproduce. We can provide packet captures on request.
Support (Aisha): Requested packet captures and browser network logs. Provided runbook checklist for collecting pcap + HAR and steps to toggle to single-session mode as temporary mitigation.
Reproduced in internal staging by running a simple TCP proxy that reorders and coalesces segments: final JSON chunk occasionally missing closing brace when server's stream boundary arrives split across reordered frames.
Edge-proxy (v1.12.0) is seen forwarding WS binary frames with no additional per-message-sequence metadata; server assumes reliable in-order delivery from TCP but does not validate message-level completeness before handing to SDK assembler.
Client SDK (js v2.4.1) assembles frames eagerly into JSON and triggers parse when it sees what it believes to be end-of-message; if the end marker is delayed due to reordered frames, incomplete parse error occurs and resume logic can re-send previous prefix leading to duplicate tokens.
Sporadic correlation with our keepalive/probe timings on the edge: when upstream closes and reopens connection quickly, fragments can be replayed or delivered out of sequence to the gateway thread handling multiplexed sessions.
No evidence of model-side truncation or runtime OOM; logs show server emitted complete chunks but gateway delivered partial sequences to client on occasion.
Related internal ticket INT-420 tracked a separate proxy half-close case last quarter; concepts overlap but root here is binary-frame reorder at the corporate middlebox.
Proof-of-concept server-side mitigation: buffer binary frame bytes for a short, configurable reorder window (25ms) and validate JSON boundary before emitting to SDK assembly layer. Initial tests reduce failure rate from ~8% to <0.5% in synthetic workloads.
Client-side mitigation: SDK change to be lenient on parse errors for end-of-stream, attempt to re-request suffix or hold parse until next fragment arrives, and dedupe prefix on resume.
Edge proxy request IDs: rq_20260310_87fd, rq_20260310_94ab
S3 pcap upload (customer provided): s3://brightdocs-support/pcaps/SUP-159008/pcap-20260310-87fd.pcap
Gateway logs: https://logs.redwood/prod/edge-proxy/us-east/2026-03-10/87fd (redacted)
SRE: retrieve and attach full pcap for both failed request IDs and keep for postmortem (owner: Mateo, due 2026-03-11)
Eng: implement short reorder-buffer on gateway and add JSON-boundary validation in assembler (owner: Priya, spike by 2026-03-13)
SDK: implement parse-retry and prefix-deduplication on resume in js SDK (owner: Lillian, target 2.4.2 release)
Support: advise customer to use single-session WS mode as interim mitigation and collect HAR + pcap (owner: Aisha)
CS: schedule coordinated snapshot with customer to reproduce while we capture pcap (owner: Jordan, scheduled 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC)
Postmortem: prepare incident writeup if regression persists after fixes (owner: Mateo)
Follow-up: add a conformance test that simulates reordered TCP segments for streaming to prevent regressions (owner: Eng QA)
Communications: send interim status to BrightDocs and note workaround and ETA (owner: Aisha)
Related PR: runtime change referenced for tracking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891
Work in progress - mitigation patch merged to internal branch and SDK change under review. Customer using single-session WS as temporary workaround. Close after production rollouts and customer validation.
03/12: Gateway reorder-buffer spike showed <0.5% failure in staging; pushed internal canary to 5% of edge traffic for further validation.
03/12: BrightDocs validated single-session WS workaround; confirmed failure rate drops to near zero in their environment.
Next: Roll gateway fix to prod edge pool after QA; publish SDK 2.4.2 containing parse-retry and dedupe logic, and coordinate with BrightDocs to remove workaround.
If customer still observed issues after rollouts, escalate to network team for joint debug with their proxy vendor (customer requested vendor involvement if problem persists).
Link to follow-up PT: https://confluence.internal.redwood/streaming/postmortems/SUP-159008
payload.summary: WS binary-frame reorder behind corporate proxy leaves unclosed JSON chunk and partial tokens in multiplexed stream

Issue summary: Customer reports their single-shot generation requests (very large context + large max_tokens) are intermittently returning HTTP 504 or abruptly terminating the streaming connection after ~60-90s. Impact: VeraHealth has a nightly batch which processes long clinical transcripts and expects completions; jobs fail ~30% of the time causing downstream delays and billing anomalies. Environment: prod us-east using hosted API, API key scoped to customer account, observed on both redwood-13b-q4-8bit and open-llama-15b-quant. Observed since 2026-03-10 after a configuration change in the serving pool allocation.
1) Use customer API key and call /v1/generate with model redwood-13b-q4-8bit
2) Provide a single context concatenating ~180k tokens (multiple transcripts) in the input_text field
3) Set max_tokens to 40k and stream=true and await response
4) Repeat the request 10 times; observe 2-4 requests fail with HTTP 504 or stream close at ~60-90s
Requests with large context and large output budgets should either complete or hit documented per-request token limits with clear 4xx response; streaming connections should remain open until completion or graceful error.
Intermittent HTTP 504 from gateway and abrupt stream termination without structured error payload; customer sees partial token output and then connection close. Billing shows full request charged in some aborted cases.
customer-provided curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
gateway trace ID: gt-0a9f2c3b (2026-03-13T02:14:57Z) -> upstream served until 00:01:05 then 504
serving-runtime logs (approx): [2026-03-13T02:13:12Z] request-start id=rt-8912 tokens_in=179842; [2026-03-13T02:14:17Z] finalizer-queue wait=24s; [2026-03-13T02:14:57Z] connection-reset-by-peer
No consistent OOM or GPU eviction in the node logs; scheduler shows transient backlog spikes on the pool servicing this customer's traffic.
Maya Thompson (Support) 2026-03-12: Opened with customer logs and batch examples. Customer says failure rate increased after 2026-03-10. Requested sample payloads and timestamps.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-13: Initial triage — observed increased queueing and finalizer latency on pool-p-08. Hypothesis: burst of long-running generations caused finalizer/backpressure interactions with the streaming proxy leading to idle timeouts.
Customer (VeraHealth) 2026-03-13: Provided three failed request traces and confirmed identical behaviour across two models. Needs workaround to keep nightly jobs running.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-14: Reproduced locally with synthetic 160k token context and 30k max_tokens; when concurrent backlog >8, stream closed after 70-95s. Raising priority and involving runtime team.
1) Reproduction: Confirmed intermittent stream cutoffs with high-context, large-output single-shot requests when pool backlog and finalizer queueing exceed SLO thresholds.
2) Metrics: finalizer_queue_time and stream_idle_time spiked correlated with gateway 504s. No GPU OOMs; CPU and network within expected ranges except elevated proxy connection resets.
3) Hypothesis: The finalizer (post-tokenization flush and KV serialization) can be delayed by concurrent long generations; streaming proxy has comparatively low idle timeout leading to race where the client sees a connection close before the runtime completes last flush.
4) Billing anomaly: some aborted requests are being billed at full cost due to downstream accounting marking request as accepted early.
Workarounds provided to customer:
- Short-term: reduce max_tokens to <=16k or split the generation into multiple smaller streamed segments. This reduced failures to <2% in customer tests.
- Medium-term: request to use a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) to avoid cross-tenant backlog spikes; offered trial for two nights.
Platform actions underway:
- Runtime: adding an explicit keepalive/ping between finalizer and streaming proxy to prevent idle timeout races (PR linked).
- Gateway: increasing stream idle timeout for affected pools by config to 120s as stop-gap.
- Billing: engineering will patch accounting to only bill completed token counts for aborted streams in next billing cycle to correct customer charges.
Follow-ups:
- Postmortem to include telemetry knobs for finalizer queue depth and stream idle latency (assigned to Diego).
- Engineering change and rollout planned 2026-03-20 with canary in us-east before global rollout.
payload.summary: Intermittent streaming cutoffs and 504s for single-shot requests with very deep context + large output budget

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Dedicated customer reports that their tenant-level override for batching SLO tier (fast) is not being applied; effective behavior remains standard.
- Customer expectation (and internal design): customer override > route policy > tier default.
- Observed: route policy appears to override tenant setting (or tenant setting is ignored).

Customer impact
- Customer is attempting to force fast tier on a latency-sensitive streaming endpoint.
- They are seeing increased queueing and higher p99 compared to pre-tiered-defaults behavior.
- Impact limited to a subset of routes on their Dedicated cluster, but blocks their rollout of tiered defaults.

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: northlake-dedicated-03
- Region: us-east
- Runtime train: 1.22.0 (feature flag enabled for tiered defaults)
- Control plane: 2026.04.08 build (policy evaluation service)

What the customer configured
1) Tenant override (Dedicated Console > Cluster > Runtime overrides): batching_tier=fast
2) Route policy (Console > Routes > /v1/chat/completions): batching_tier=standard (set earlier during testing)

Expected behavior
- Requests on that tenant/cluster should run fast tier regardless of route policy.

Actual behavior
- Requests continue to use standard tier.
- Telemetry shows selection_reason=route_policy for the affected route.

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) In staging (or a dedicated test cluster), set tenant override batching_tier=fast at the cluster/tenant scope.
2) Set route policy batching_tier=standard on a specific route.
3) Send requests without request-level tier headers.
4) Observe effective tier via decision trace / metrics label.

Observed signals
- runtime.metric: redwood_inference_request_latency_ms{tier="standard",route="/v1/chat/completions"} increases.
- reason code emitted: profile_selection_reason="route_policy" even when tenant override is set.

Notes
- Customer also noted that toggling the tenant override off/on sometimes changes behavior after ~10 minutes, suggesting config propagation/cache involvement.

Requested outcome
- Fix precedence to match published behavior for Dedicated.
- Provide an immediate workaround + ETA for rollout to their cluster.

Additional notes:
Action: reproduce in staging with a route-tier set + tenant override set.
Fix plan: introduce dedicated precedence mode: customer_override > route_policy > tier_default. Also ensure request-level header remains highest precedence when allowed.
Workaround: customer can remove route-level batching_tier setting to allow tenant override to apply (confirmed in staging).
Resolved by correcting tier override precedence in Dedicated mode: customer/tenant override now wins over route policy, which wins over tier default. Fix validated in staging and dedicated canary; shipped in runtime-1.22.1 with accompanying control plane policy-eval hotfix. Customer verified behavior in prod us-east. Temporary workaround (prior to rollout) was to remove route-level batching_tier to allow tenant override to apply.

payload.description:
Issue summary: After a recent IdP change, tenant-scoped admin impersonation fails for Asterion customers on their private VPC. The Identity Proxy is returning role assertions but Redwood's RBAC lookup does not map them to tenant admin bindings due to claim canonicalization differences (casing and trailing suffix).

Technical background: Customer uses an on-prem IdP that recently started sending service role assertions in the claim 'serviceRoles' with values like 'TenantAdmin/Finance'. Redwood expects the normalized claim key 'service_roles' and lowercased role names without '/' separators. The mismatch causes the tenant admin lookup to return no bindings and results in 403s for impersonation and certain admin operations.
Customer reports that platform admins cannot impersonate users or perform tenant-scoped admin tasks (user invites, role grants). Affects all admin users for one tenant in their private deployment. Blocking day-to-day operations for Asterion's Platform team. Estimated 12 engineers impacted at customer side.
1) Configure IdP to emit service role assertion under claim 'serviceRoles' with value 'TenantAdmin/Finance'.
2) Perform a tenant-scoped admin impersonation request to the Redwood Private Admin API with the IdP-issued assertion exchanged via the identity-proxy.
3) Observe 403 response: 'rbac: no matching role binding for tenant'.
4) Confirm that the raw request headers into the serving runtime include 'x-assertion-serviceRoles: TenantAdmin/Finance'.
Identity proxy or RBAC layer canonicalizes incoming role assertions into the normalized form used by tenant bindings (e.g., 'tenantadmin:finance' or 'tenant_admin'). Tenant admin impersonation should succeed when a binding exists.
Requests are denied with 403. RBAC lookup logs show 'no bindings found for claim key service_roles' because the identity-proxy passed 'serviceRoles' and the runtime did not map it.
2026-02-20T09:13:21Z ident-proxy INFO incoming assertion keys: ["serviceRoles", "sub", "iss"]
2026-02-20T09:13:21Z rbac ERROR lookup failed: claim key 'service_roles' missing (trace=tr-9b3f2e)
2026-02-20T09:13:21Z admin-api WARN impersonation denied uid=alice@asterion.com tenant=asterion-finance reason='no role binding'
Initial hypothesis: IdP changed claim key casing and added a namespace separator '/'.
Reproduced locally against staging private image: identity-proxy forwarded raw claim exactly as IdP sent it (serviceRoles). RBAC canonicalization code currently only checks for snake_case 'service_roles' and lowercased values without '/'.
Trace tr-9b3f2e corresponds to customer request sample provided by support (attached).
Config mismatch discovered: customer had customized IdP mapping in their nextIdP release; they intended to keep old claim key but legacy outbound mapper now emits the new format.
Temporary workaround provided to customer: add a claim remap rule in their IdP (or in the identity-proxy 'claim_mapping' config) to emit 'service_roles' with lowercased, colon-separated values. Support provided sample mapping snippet. This restored admin impersonation for the tenant within ~10 minutes.
Engineering patch deployed to identity-proxy v1.3.27 that adds robust claim canonicalization: accepts camelCase, PascalCase, kebab-case and snake_case claim keys, strips trailing slashes, and normalizes separators ('/' and ':' to ':') and lowercases role names. A short migration job was run to re-evaluate cached role-bindings for affected tenants. Patch deployed to customer's private control plane on 2026-02-23. Post-deploy verification: impersonation succeeds and no further 403s reported for the tenant.

Follow-ups: (1) update RBAC docs with canonicalization expectations, (2) include a diagnostic check in the Private Console to show raw incoming claims for tenant owners, (3) add automated test coverage for common claim permutations.
Support (Priya Patel) 2026-02-20: Thanks for the report and the sample assertion. Can you confirm when the IdP change was rolled out and whether it affects other tenants?
Customer (Marcus Li - Asterion) 2026-02-20: Change was rolled yesterday as part of our security normalization. Only Finance tenant uses the new outbound mapper currently.
SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-02-21: Reproduced locally. Identity-proxy forwarded 'serviceRoles' verbatim. RBAC lookup expects 'service_roles'. Adding claim mapping in proxy fixed the request. Preparing small patch for canonicalization.
Engineering (Liam O'Connor) 2026-02-22: PR 482 adds normalization and unit tests. Scheduling deploy to customer's private control plane during maintenance window 02/23. Will run role-binding re-eval after rollout.
Customer (Marcus Li) 2026-02-23: Confirming impersonation works now for our Finance tenant. We'll keep the workaround mapping for 24h and then revert once we validate.
Support (Priya Patel) 2026-02-23: Closing loop with customer and adding doc links to ticket. Leaving ticket open until follow-up items completed.

Issue summary: LexaHealth reports that when multiple chat streams are multiplexed over a single websocket, and the platform performs session-token rotation (security refresh), some clients observe truncated final choices after a resume. Impact: In worst cases the assistant's last sentence is cut off or the final choice is missing, causing downstream UI to show an unfinished answer and triggering duplicate retry logic. Environment: Dedicated cluster for LexaHealth in prod/us-east; traffic uses Reed proxy and connection multiplexing at the customer side.
1) Start two concurrent websocket streams (A and B) to the Redwood hosted endpoint using mux session id. 2) Stream tokens from model redwood-rlhf-13b while sending keepalives. 3) Trigger token rotation by forcing a short-lived session key refresh (simulate by calling the rotate endpoint or wait for scheduled rotation). 4) Simulate a transient disconnect on stream A, allow client to reconnect and resume with resume_offset. 5) Observe that stream A sometimes resumes but final choice is truncated or missing while stream B continues normally.
On resume, the server should return a complete, stitched stream up to the final "end" event (or final choice) preserving ordering and producing no duplicate or truncated tokens.
Customer logs: [ws://lexa-prod-conn] resume_request: session_id=abc123, resume_offset=2452
Server logs (approx): 2026-03-05T14:11:10Z session-manager: rotating token for session abc123 -> token tkn_7G
2026-03-05T14:11:11Z mux-router: connection MUX-9: reassigning stream A to worker w-12
2026-03-05T14:11:11Z serving-runtime[w-12]: resume request offset=2452, kv-cache-hit=true, seq_start=2453
2026-03-05T14:11:11Z serving-runtime[w-12]: final-choice emitted (seq=2499) then connection tear-down during send
2026-03-05T14:11:11Z api-gateway: truncated send detected, client ack missing

Support (Aisha): Thanks for the report — we can reproduce locally with a muxed client. Collecting traces and asking SRE to check token rotation path.
Customer (LexaHealth): We see this intermittently during our 04:00-06:00 traffic spike. It's impacting user-visible answers ~0.8% of streams. Priority is high because product blocks on final token for analytics ingestion.
SRE (Marco): Reproduced on dedicated pool. Hypothesis: session token rotation triggers a short window where the mux-router rebinds stream to a different worker but resume_offset is applied relative to the old worker's streaming buffer, producing an off-by-one when KV cache pointer advances during rotation.
Eng (Priya Rao): Adding instrumentation to capture resume_offset, worker_id, and latest-kv-cache-seq in a single trace. Will also add assert checks on resume boundary handling.
Support (Aisha): Noted workaround for customer - disable client-side muxing for critical paths or increase resume window tolerance to 2s until patch rolled out.
Customer (LexaHealth): Applied the workaround and observed immediate drop to ~0.02% of affected streams. Thanks — will hold on full enablement until fix is deployed.
Initial triage (2026-03-05): Reproduced with synthetic mux client. Observed correlation between token rotation and worker rebind events. Trace show resume_offset=2452 but worker had advanced to seq_start=2453 causing first token after resume to be skipped (off-by-one). Hypotheses: (1) session-manager issues rotation broadcast after mux-router rebind causing stale offset semantics; (2) serving-runtime does not atomically remap resume_offset to new worker's cache base when reattach occurs; (3) network-level partial write during final-choice send leads to missing terminal event on client side. Further tests: instrumented resume path to log (resume_offset, cache_base_seq, worker_id, token_version) — logs attached to PR. Related Slack: #support (thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/thread/GPQ9x2), related incident stub INC-2026-03-05-LEXA.
Mitigation applied: Increase resume tolerance on mux-router (v2) to accept resume_offset +/-1 for same session; added guard in serving-runtime to re-align resume_offset to target worker's cache_base_seq when worker change detected. Deployed hotfix to dedicated cluster 2026-03-09 (runtime patch release v1.67.2). Post-deploy monitoring: affected streams dropped from 0.8% to 0.01% for LexaHealth in prod/us-east over 72 hours. Follow-ups: engineering to land full fix that ensures atomic token-rotation + rebind ordering (tracked in PR #2291). Customer workaround: disable client-side multiplexing for latency-sensitive flows (documented in runbook). Ticket status: In Progress until full end-to-end integration tests are green and customer approves re-enablement.
1) Eng to complete end-to-end test harness for rotation+rebind (owner: Priya Rao, due 2026-03-15). 2) Add automated end-to-end regression to CI for muxed resumes (owner: Runtime QA). 3) Confirm LexaHealth can re-enable multiplexing in staging and schedule a gradual rollout. 4) Update public runbook and customer-facing KB article summarizing workaround and expected behavior.
Potential root cause: non-atomic ordering between session token rotation broadcast and mux-router stream rebind which exposes resume_offset semantics that assumed single-worker sticky mapping. Postmortem should review token rotation ordering guarantees, mux-router handoff protocol, and add stricter invariants in serving-runtime. Include customer impact metrics and timeline.
payload.summary: Multiplexed session token rotation causes intermittent truncation on stream resume

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC we observed a sustained increase in 5xx responses for a set of enterprise customers (notably SparkDocs Inc) routed through the us-east-1 API gateway. Impact: ~12% request error rate increase for embedding and short streaming requests for ~3 hours; several tenant requests hit P1 SLA thresholds. Environment: prod (us-east-1). Symptoms: API gateway returned 502/503/504; upstream runtime logs show frequent worker restarts and OOMs; accept queue length spiked for affected frontends. Hypothesis initially: kernel fallback / nvml glitch; later investigation pointed to priority-shim eviction + UVM worker thrash amplified by hedged retries and a large embedding bulk retry loop from one tenant.
1) Send a mix of short text-gen and frequent small-batch embedding requests from a single tenant with high connection concurrency and hedged-retry enabled.
2) Simulate background large embedding bulk (30k vectors) prefetch on same tenant to cause long-running KV cache prefetch tasks.
3) Observe accept-queue growth on ingress and priority-shim evictions moving short requests to lower priority buckets.
4) Note runtime UVM worker CPU/memory thrash as prefetched jobs compete with real-time streams, causing OOM kills and hedged retry amplification.
5) Result: API gateway 5xx elevation and client-observed failures.
Correlation: apigw accept_queue growth precedes runtime OOMs by ~30-90s; hedged retries count spiked after accept queue hits threshold.
The long embedding prefetch was consuming UVM pinned memory and multiple worker threads without yielding; this caused GPU memory fragmentation and failed allocations for short-lived inference requests.
Ingress prioritizer's shim eviction logic was too aggressive: it dropped new short requests into low-priority pools instead of returning fast failures, which multiplied connections and kept sockets open.
Metrics consulted: apigw/accept_queue, ingress-prioritizer/shim_evictions, runtime/oom_kills, runtime/uvm_mem_free, hedged_retry/attempts. Dashboards: /d/ingress/accept-health; runbook: confluence/Runbooks/ingress-prioritizer.
Repro in staging: reproduced with a tenant-level background job generating KV-prefetch load + aggressive client hedged retry settings.
Combination of an unbounded tenant-scoped embedding prefetch workload monopolizing UVM worker resources and an ingress prioritizer shim eviction policy that demoted short requests into lower-priority buckets rather than failing fast. This created head-of-line blocking, hedged-retry amplification at the API gateway, and downstream runtime OOMs leading to elevated 5xx rates.
Immediate: Apply temporary cap to priority_shim_evictions (apigw feature flag) and throttle tenant prefetch concurrency for identified tenant (SparkDocs Inc).
Short-term: Deploy hotfix to ingress prioritizer that returns 429 for demoted requests under extreme accept_queue pressure instead of demotion, reducing stuck sockets.
Short-term: Add runtime guard to detect UVM worker pinned memory > 80% and pause new prefetch tasks until memory reclaimed.
Customer-facing: Notified SparkDocs support and provided recommended client hedged-retry configuration (increase backoff, reduce concurrent hedged attempts).
Hotfix rolled: ingress-prioritizer change to fast-fail demoted requests (returned 429 instead of demotion) deployed 2026-03-11 08:15 UTC; observed apigw 5xx rate return to baseline within 20 minutes.
Applied tenant prefetch concurrency limit for SparkDocs Inc (temporary) 2026-03-11 08:25 UTC.
Runtime patch to add UVM worker memory guard merged: PR gh/4201, rolled to canary 2026-03-12, full rollout 2026-03-13.
Post-incident: scheduled follow-up to revisit prioritizer eviction strategy and add synthetic checks for hedged-retry amplification during tenant bulk jobs. Confluence postmortem link: confluence/RWD/postmortems/SUP-286543 (pending).
[2026-03-11T02:12:34Z] apigw-frontend-12 accept_queue=352 backlog=110 priority_shim_evictions=42
[2026-03-11T02:12:36Z] runtime-worker-3 PID=4512 OOMKill invoked, nvml_free_mem=0.4GB, kv_cache_evictions=127
[2026-03-11T02:13:01Z] apigw-frontend-12 respond 502 conn_id=0x7fae, upstream_err=connection-reset-by-peer
[2026-03-11T02:14:10Z] ingress-prioritizer: demoted 18 sessions due to shim-eviction; hedged_retry_counter tenant=SparkDocs Inc = 23
Maya Chen (Reporter) [2026-03-11 03:05 UTC]: Customer reported sharp increase in 5xxs; provided example request IDs and timeline. Customer impact: dashboarding functions failed for 10% of queries.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee) [2026-03-11 03:20 UTC]: Triage started; pulled apigw and runtime metrics. Noted accept_queue spike correlated with long-running prefetch tasks from a single tenant.
SRE (Anika Rao) [2026-03-11 04:00 UTC]: Reproduced queue growth in staging with scaled embedding prefetch. Observed priority_shim counter incrementing and evictions causing head-of-line blocking.
Eng (Diego Morales) [2026-03-11 06:45 UTC]: Confirmed runtime OOMs caused by UVM worker threads pinned to large prefetches; hedged retries amplified ingress pressure. Opening PR to add eviction throttles and backpressure for prefetch jobs.
Liam O'Connor [2026-03-12 09:10 UTC]: Applied hotfix: reduce prefetch concurrency for tenant-scoped background jobs and add temporary priority_shim cap on apigw. Error rates dropped to baseline within 20 minutes.
SparkDocs Support Rep (J. Alvarez) [2026-03-12 11:02 UTC]: Confirmed customer saw degraded queries for ~2.5 hours. Customer accepted workaround and requested postmortem.

Issue summary: BrightDocs reported that their finalized invoice for 2026-02-28 shows a net negative payable (surplus credit) of $1,218.30 after hourly consolidation. Impact: Customer billing shows credit beyond what was expected, autopay attempted and then failed because final invoice reflected negative total and payment gateway rejected the autopay flag. Environment: Dedicated tenant on us-west. Customer uses seat-based metering overlay (per-seat seat-hour) plus reserved GPU capacity credits and a separate KV-cache warmup credit stream. Observed behavior: During the hourly consolidation run the reconciler applied a second set of provisional credits for the same subaccount usage window, resulting in an over-credit and a negative invoice line. Expected behavior: Deduplicated postbacks and smoothing algorithm should allocate exactly one set of provisional credits per hour window, not double-apply on merged subaccount overlays. Additional context: BrightDocs recently performed an org merge of two subaccounts and enabled a seat-split feature; that merge coincides with the hourly-run when the anomaly occurred. Customer reached out via support@brightdocs.com and posted in #support-billing Slack thread (linked below).
1) In prod, create two subaccounts under one parent org mirroring BrightDocs org IDs (org: bd-981, sub: bd-981-a, bd-981-b).
2) Send hourly postbacks for the same hour window from both sub accounts (postback payload includes reserved_hours, kv_warmup_credit, seat_hours).
3) Trigger the hourly-consolidation job (POST /internal/billing/reconcile/hourly?window=2026-02-28T00:00Z) with reconciliation flag force=true.
4) Observe billing service applying provisional credits and the duplicate allocation when both subaccount tags map to the consolidated billing namespace.
5) Finalize invoice-run via /billing/invoices/finalize and check resulting invoice lines.

2026-03-01T01:06:03Z billing.allocator INFO allocated provisional_credit id=pc_98013 amount=512.40 references=[bd-981-b-seat]
2026-03-01T01:06:10Z invoices.finalize ERROR final invoice total=-1218.30 invoice_id=inv_20260228_bd981 autopay=false reason=negative_total
2026-03-01: Initial triage by CS (Aisha). Confirmed customer-visible negative invoice and autopay failure. Requested logs and invoice PDF from billing team.
2026-03-02: SRE (Diego) reproduced duplicate provisional credits locally by forcing consolidation with merged subaccount mapping. Reproduction exact when seat-hour keys normalized to consolidated namespace but dedup key used subaccount-scoped identifier.
2026-03-03: Hypothesis: dedupe key generation used 'subaccount_id + metric' rather than 'consolidated_namespace + metric', so when org merge mapping returned two subaccount identifiers that canonicalized to same consolidated namespace after mapping stage, dedupe check ran earlier and missed collision.
2026-03-04: Investigated reconciler commit history; found a recent refactor (PR 211) that moved dedupe check after mapping step — regression introduced order-of-operations bug. Related PR listed in related_github_prs.
2026-03-05: Cross-checked the postback stream — there were no duplicate retries; both postbacks were valid distinct subaccount events that should have been collapsed by consolidator.

Additional notes:
Workaround: Billing Ops put affected invoice inv_20260228_bd981 in manual-review and set autopay=false; payments notified to skip charging BrightDocs. We issued provisional credit memo CP-20260301 to offset customer-facing negative total until reconciliation completes. Permanent fix: patch in postback-reconciler to compute dedupe keys using consolidated_namespace+metric after mapping stage, deploy hotfix v1.2.3 to staging (PR 217) and run test consolidation on snapshot of affected windows. Post-deploy actions: run backfill reconciliation for windows 2026-02-26 through 2026-03-02, re-generate corrected invoices (inv_corr_20260228_bd981), and issue final credit memo/adjustment. Follow-up items: add unit test coverage for merge/namespace mapping edgecases, add monitoring alert on negative-finalized-invoice events, and schedule a postmortem in Confluence (link in related_confluence_pages). Estimated ETA for code fix and reconciliation: 2026-03-11.

payload.description:
Issue summary: After upstream IdP update, a subset of FinSight users experience an interactive SSO loop when attempting to sign in to the Redwood Console on their private deployment. The browser repeatedly redirects to the IdP sign-in page and never lands back on the console. API keys and machine-to-machine auth are unaffected; only interactive web sessions are impacted.

Impact: ~12% of active console users (reported across two teams) cannot complete a login; they remain skirted out to the IdP and back repeatedly. This is preventing admin operations and delaying model rollouts.

Initial hypothesis: Identity proxy is setting a session cookie against an unexpected path due to URL normalization of encoded slashes in the IdP redirect_uri/relay_state. The IdP now returns a redirect with an encoded slash (%2F) in the relay path; some upstream ingress proxies normalize/decode that value when forwarding, causing the identity-proxy to see a different effective path vs. what the browser uses. The effect is two different Set-Cookie Path values across the handshake, which means the browser does not send the expected session cookie on the final console redirect, leading to repeated re-auth.

Notes: Customer reports this started after a routine IdP upgrade last Thursday. They are on the Private deployment (VPC) with our identity-proxy behind an internal nginx ingress that has allow_encoded_slashes off by default.
1) Configure private deployment with identity-proxy mounted at /sso/proxy/tenant-a
2) Configure IdP to include relay_state=apps%2Fconsole%2Ftenant-a (encoded slash in path segment)
3) From a new incognito browser, attempt console login and follow IdP redirect flow
4) Observe repeated redirects back to IdP and no persistent console session cookie being used on final redirect
identity-proxy (2026-03-09T14:02:07Z) INFO incoming SAMLResponse relay_state=apps%2Fconsole%2Ftenant-a
ingress-nginx (2026-03-09T14:02:07Z) DEBUG normalized path=/sso/proxy/tenant-a/apps/console/tenant-a -> /sso/proxy/tenant-a/apps/console/tenant-a (decoded)
identity-proxy (2026-03-09T14:02:07Z) INFO Set-Cookie: rw_session=eyJhbGci...; Path=/sso/proxy/tenant-a; HttpOnly; Secure
browser request to /sso/proxy/tenant-a/apps/console/tenant-a did not include rw_session cookie (cookie path mismatch)
identity-proxy (2026-03-09T14:02:08Z) WARN session not found for relay_state -> redirecting to IdP
Support reproduced locally with a minimal nginx ingress that had 'merge_slashes on' and 'allow_encoded_slashes off' — ingress decoded %2F into / before proxying to identity-proxy.
When ingress decoded the path, identity-proxy set Set-Cookie Path=/sso/proxy/tenant-a but browser final redirect used /sso/proxy/tenant-a/apps/console/tenant-a, which meant cookie did not match the requested path.
Captured curl traces and browser devtools show two Set-Cookie headers during SAML handshake in some flows (IdP-issued cookie via IdP domain + identity-proxy cookie). The important mismatch is the Path attribute differing because of decoding behavior upstream.
Hypothesis validated by toggling ingress to 'proxy_preserve_host on' and 'allow_encoded_slashes on' — with allow_encoded_slashes enabled, the path was not decoded and session cookie Path aligned with browser path, resolving the loop.
Customer's ingress had recently been upgraded by their infra team; change logs show a default change that disabled allow_encoded_slashes in the new image, explaining the regression timing.

Additional notes:
Alternative short-term: Configure identity-proxy to set session cookie Path=/ (root) as a temporary mitigation — reduces cookie scoping but resolves path mismatch.
If neither option available: IdP can be configured to avoid encoding slashes in relay_state (use a token or base64 blob instead of raw encoded path).
Engineering assigned: identity-proxy team (Lena Thompson, Marco Ruiz)
Hotfix plan: Add defensive logic in identity-proxy to canonicalize relay_state consistently (treat %2F and / equivalently when deriving cookie Path) and a feature flag to force Path=/ for affected deployments.
PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/584 (adds canonicalization and feature flag), tests added to simulate decoded/encoded relay_state variants.
Staging: Patch deployed to staging 2026-03-11; FinSight confirmed staging login success.
Rollout: Target production rollout for 2026-03-13 in a canary-first deployment. Customer advised to apply ingress config workaround if they cannot wait for the patch.
1) Complete code review and merge PR #584 (identity-proxy) — assigned Marco Ruiz
2) Run additional canary cycles in us-east and monitor session creation/console-login 10-minute windows
3) Customer to schedule prod ingress image update OR accept our patch and we will coordinate canary rollout
4) Postmortem doc linking root cause to ingress default change and steps to avoid future regression. Add an entry to the SSO runbook.
2026-03-09 18:02 - Customer (FinSight): Uploaded SAMLResponse and nginx ingress config; confirmed they rolled a new ingress image last Thursday.
2026-03-10 09:24 - Support (Lena Thompson): Confirmed reproduction and provided temporary mitigation steps to FinSight (see workaround).
2026-03-11 11:45 - Customer: Applied ingress config change in staging and observed successful logins; scheduling prod change window.
2026-03-12 08:30 - Support: Notified customer that an identity-proxy hardening patch will be released to make cookie Path assignment robust to decoded vs encoded relay_state.
payload.summary: Nonce replay + cookie path normalization causing interactive SSO login loop in private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
- Customer reports significant latency regression after Redwood serving runtime 1.18 rollout.
- Observed across Chat Completions and Text Generation (non-streaming and streaming), with biggest impact on longer outputs.

Customer impact:
- Aurora Search reports production SLO breach on end-user search-assistant flows.
- Symptoms: p95 latency increased ~40–80% depending on model; elevated tail latency spikes (p99) during peak.
- No material increase in 5xx, but increased client-side timeouts due to slower responses.

Scope / blast radius (initial):
- Regions: us-east (strongest), eu-west (moderate).
- Models most impacted: rw-llama-70b-instruct (highest), rw-llama-8b-instruct, rw-mistral-7b-instruct.
- Endpoints: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-02-13 17:52: Customer email + ticket opened. Customer notes issue began “shortly after” runtime update.
- 18:05: Support confirms internal dashboards show p95 regression coincident with runtime 1.18 deploy wave.
- 18:12: Slack bridge started in #support per playbook; moved to #incidents when multi-customer pattern confirmed.
- 18:25: SRE on-call (Sean Gallagher) engaged; Release on-call looped in via #eng-releases.
- 19:10: Initial mitigation: halt further rollout; shift traffic away from 1.18 pools where possible.
- 20:05: Partial rollback in us-east Dedicated/Hosted pools; latency begins recovering.
- 2026-02-14 00:40: Full rollback completed in us-east; eu-west rollback completed 02:10.
- 2026-02-14 03:00: p95 back to baseline (+/- 5%) on key dashboards; customer confirms recovery.

Environment details requested/received:
- Customer SDK: redwood-sdk-typescript 2.6.1
- Traffic pattern: mix of streaming and non-streaming; typical output 300–900 tokens
- Customer regions: us-east primary, eu-west backup
- Example request IDs (customer provided):
  - req_01HZZ9Z2S5KJ9A3FQ4VQ9K2E7W
  - req_01HZZB0P7R9ZQK8A6T6F1P3N2M

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) In prod, send chat completion to rw-llama-70b-instruct with max_tokens=700, temperature=0.2.
2) Compare identical prompt on runtime 1.17 pools vs 1.18 pools.
3) Observe time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-output-token (TPOT) deltas; tail increases on 1.18.

Diagnostics / investigation notes:
- Correlation: regression lines up with runtime 1.18 deployment window (deploy label runtime_version=1.18).
- Metrics: TTFT modestly worse (~10–15%), but TPOT and queueing latency increased notably under load.
- Hypotheses (SRE/Runtime):
  - Continuous batching behavior change causing smaller effective batch sizes (lower GPU utilization, higher scheduling overhead).
  - KV cache memory pressure leading to more frequent evictions / recompute under longer sequences.
  - Scheduler fairness changes increasing queue time for long generations.

Dashboards (internal):
- Latency overview: grafana://prod/inference-latency?var-region=us-east&var-model=rw-llama-70b-instruct
- TTFT/TPOT breakdown: grafana://prod/streaming-health?var-region=us-east
- Queueing and GPU util: grafana://prod/cluster-utilization?var-region=us-east&var-pool=hosted

Escalation/coordination:
- Support bridge started: #support-bridge-inc-2026-02-13-latency
- Incident channel: #incidents (INC-2026-02-13-ue1-euw-latency)
- Owner (technical): SRE on-call (Sean Gallagher) coordinating rollback with release on-call.
- Customer comms owner: Rachel Kim for enterprise cadence; Support to relay technical updates.

Customer comms notes:
- We acknowledged regression, avoided promising RCA until confirmed.
- Provided mitigation status updates while rollback in progress (approx hourly cadence during active mitigation).

Requested follow-ups:
- Runtime team to identify 1.18 change causing TPOT/queue regression and add guardrail / perf test.
- Docs/Support: add a short internal troubleshooting note for “latency regression after deploy” including how to quickly check runtime_version and pool routing.

Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 504/connection-timeout errors when requesting large max_output values and deep priming history in a single call. Impact: All generation requests that include an ~80k token context plus a 120k max_output budget are intermittently timing out after 90 seconds in the hosted Dedicated pool. Occurrence window: started 2026-03-11 09:15 UTC and recurred in bursts through 2026-03-12. Customer observed failures across multiple runs and client SDKs.
1) Use customer account API key in Dedicated pool (NimbleDocs dedicated namespace).
2) Send POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-open-v1-70b, temperature=0.2, max_output_tokens=120000, and include an application history ~80k tokens as the prompt.
3) Enable streaming in client and set client-side timeout to 90s.
4) Repeat 5-10 times in rapid succession (multi-tenant traffic present).
Expected: streaming begins and completes without server-side 504. Observed: request stalls, server-side finalizer times out and client receives 504 or connection reset.
Requests with very large prompt + large max_output consistently hit server-side timeouts in bursts. Tail latency climbs from ~2s to >120s for finalization steps, and streaming stalls with no progress before final disconnect.
Long-context requests should either be accepted and progress streamed until completion within SLOs, or fail fast with clear error (e.g., unsupported token budget) rather than silent stalls leading to 504s.
Initial triage (Support): validated customer reproduction, confirmed behavior isolated to dedicated pool in us-east-1 and to requests with combined very large context+max_output budgets.
SRE telemetry: observed sustained increase in finalizer queue length correlated with long-context requests. GPU kernel swap rate spiked during incident windows. Short low-latency requests continued to be served normally.
Hypothesis: recent scheduler change (dynamic batch coalescing v2) introduced heuristics that aggressively coalesced long-context requests into mixed batches with short requests. This caused long-running batches to occupy GPU for extended periods and produced priority inversion, causing finalizer/backpressure thrashing and KV cache evictions for queued long-context requests.
Further evidence: sampling of scheduler traces showed multiple mixed batches where a single long-context request queued with many short requests; mixed-batch kernel selection forced fallback code paths that perform additional KV materialization and repeated kernel swaps.
Related config change: rollout of dynamic batch coalescing v2 on 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC (PR r-infra#5483) — referenced in related_github_prs.

2026-03-11T09:23:44Z - finalizer - finalization_deadline_exceeded for request id=xyz; cumulative_gpu_time=86s
2026-03-11T09:23:44Z - http - responded 504 to client request id=xyz

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - SRE run: Rolled temporary rollback of dynamic coalescing heuristic in prod:us-east-1 for dedicated pool at 2026-03-12T04:30Z; observed finalizer queue length drop and no new 504s for same reproducer.
2026-03-12 - Customer (NimbleDocs): Verified with test harness; confirmed failures stopped after rollback. Customer requested follow-up and root cause analysis.
Root cause: scheduler dynamic batch coalescing v2 caused mixed batches that triggered fallback kernel paths and repeated KV cache reloads, leading to finalizer queue bloating and timeouts for long-context requests. Fixes applied: 1) immediate rollback of the aggressive coalescing heuristic in prod:us-east-1 dedicated pools (mitigation), 2) targeted scheduler patch to create dedicated long-request lanes and avoid mixed-batch kernel selection, 3) added telemetry and an alert for mixed-batch rate and finalizer queue length. Follow-ups: extend mixed-batch tests in CI, update rollout checklist for scheduler heuristics, and notify customers with recommended best-practices (reduce max_output or use dedicated pinned instances for extreme budgets). Customer notified and confirmed recovery. Ticket closed after verification by customer and SRE.

payload.description:
Customer reports intermittent mixed-model outputs and a spike in latency/errors during a staged canary migration in us-east-1. Symptoms started after we increased canary weight for their tenant as part of a scheduled promote. Impact: 8% of requests for tenant 'acme-health' were routed to a legacy variant for ~12 minutes, producing unexpected tokenization/formatting differences and a small increase in 5xx streaming disconnects. Root cause suspected to involve stale pin shard state not being fully flushed when orchestrator rate-shedding triggered partial migration retries.
1) In prod us-east-1, start a weighted canary promote for tenant acme-health from variant A -> variant B (10% -> 50% over 10m).
2) Apply autoscaler synthetic load to push nodes into rate-shed policy (simulate noisy neighbor by creating burst of short-lived streams).
3) Observe orchestrator logs for commit windows and pin-shard flush events; check edge-proxy routing decisions and cookie/affinity headers.
4) Reproduce client requests that rely on streaming and model-specific tokenization to detect mixed outputs.

2026-03-12T14:08:19Z edge-proxy[router] INFO route-decide tenant=acme-health shard=pin-3 resolved=variant-A ttl=0s (stale)
2026-03-12T14:08:29Z serving-runtime[model-allocator] ERROR stream 0x4b12: downstream stream reset while switching kv-cache
logs: https://logs.redwood.prod/us-east-1/streams?query=tenant:acme-health+commit-window+rate-shed
14:10 - Initial triage (Maya): customer reports quality regression and intermittent 5xxs starting exactly when canary weight was bumped.
14:20 - SRE (Liam) observed a cluster-wide rate-shed event from the autoscaler coincident with the canary promote window. Orchestrator shows commit-window retries where shard flush acknowledgement from edge was not seen before a migration retry.
14:35 - Hypothesis: when the orchestrator retried the commit due to rate-shed, it wrote a new pin-shard but the edge-proxy still served requests from an older pin-shard (TTL mismatch + cache not invalidated), creating a cohort split. Some streams followed new variant, some old -> mixed outputs.
14:50 - Confirmed via distributed trace that request X and request Y from same session were routed to different variants; trace ids: trace-a1b2 (variant-A), trace-c3d4 (variant-B).
15:05 - We reproduced locally by forcing rate-shed and observing commit-window retry path; edge cache invalidation was not issued on retry path due to a short-circuit return in coordinator code (PR suspected).
Findings link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/issues/4820
