Slack: #support (https://slack.redwood.com/support/p16234) and #sre (https://slack.redwood.com/sre/p4221) threads created.
Workaround applied: immediate edge-cache invalidation for tenant acme-health and manual flush of pin-shard entries across orchestrator replicas. Customer traffic returned to expected variant consistency. Long-term fix: code change to Coordinator.commit_retry to ensure cache-broadcast/invalidation is executed on retry paths even when rate-shed is active (PR 4821). Follow-up: add unit + e2e test to simulate rate-shed/migration and add monitoring alert for commit-window mismatches.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Retail) reports a gradual degradation in dedicated pool throughput during peak window that started ~2026-03-09 11:40 UTC and persisted for multiple hours. The degradation shows as a progressive fall in served tokens/sec and increased queueing despite apparent free GPU slots. Autoscaler did not scale up or rebalance for the affected shard for >18 minutes once p99 latency crossed the SLO.

Impact:
- Production API p50/p95 showed ~30% throughput loss for Acme's dedicated pool (customer-facing).
- Multiple requests were returned with 429s from route fallback logic when the system attempted to fall back to shared capacity.
- Customer-facing latency regressions caused degraded UX for product feature launched that morning.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id dp-usw-23 (Acme-reserved)
- Region: us-west-2
- Models: redwood-v2-7b (pinned), fallback: gpt-neo-instruct-3.5
- Platform: production, autoscaler enabled with predictive window and cooldown configured

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a steady burst of short inference streams (50–200 tokens) with high connection churn and frequent small attachments (customer's pattern).
2) Observe allocator logs and pool metrics during sustained start-of-minute flares.
3) Note that kv-prefetch IO increases on the scheduled shard followed by a drop in batch formation efficiency.

Observed behavior:
- GPU slots show as available in allocator state but batcher throughput stalls (p50 token generation drops).
- Autoscaler telemetry indicates belief that capacity is sufficient (no scale up event) while per-GPU IO (nvme read queues) and host CPU sys time increase.
- Prefetch subsystem shows erratic lease renewals; slot attach latency for new sessions climbs from ~60ms to 900ms.

Expected behavior:
- Batch formation remains efficient for short streams and autoscaler should add capacity or trigger rebalance when p99 latency crosses configured SLOs.

Logs / metrics / artifacts:
- Customer metrics (Acme dashboard): https://dashboards.redwood/acme/throughput/2026-03-09
- Allocator trace (shard dp-usw-23): https://logs.redwood/allocator/trace/2026-03-09-11
- Autoscaler event stream: https://logs.redwood/autoscaler/events/2026-03-09
- Kernel-level nvme/io-wait graphs: https://metrics.redwood/host/io-wait/dp-usw-23

Initial hypotheses:
- Cross-tenant I/O coupling: a tenant in the same host group is generating small, high-fanout writes that increase NVMe contention and postpone context switch for the serving process, reducing batch throughput.
- Prefetch/kv-cache lease churn causing slot reservation inconsistency: batcher sees slots as free but attach pipeline is delayed by prefetch backlog.
- Autoscaler configuration (smoothing window/cooldown) is too conservative for this workload pattern, so it fails to react to short-lived but sustained p99 regressions.

Immediate customer-facing workaround requested:
- Temporary increase of burst capacity for Acme's pool and enable aggressive fallback to warm shared instances for the next 2 hours while investigation continues.

Work items for follow-up:
- SRE to collect host-level IO stack traces and perf events for the impacted hosts.
- Scheduler/allocator team to correlate attach latency with nvme IO spikes and identify tenant causing heavy small writes.
- Autoscaler team to evaluate a shorter predictive window for dedicated pools flagged as latency-sensitive.

Priority: P1 (customer-facing degradation).

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 11:00 - Autoscaler team: The predictive model uses 5-minute smoothing with a 10-minute cooldown which allowed the p99 window to persist without triggering scale. Simulated faster window (1m) did trigger scale-ups but caused oscillation in unrelated pools.
Workaround applied: temporary burst reservation increase for Acme and warm shared fallback enabled for 3 hours (2026-03-10 15:20 to 2026-03-10 18:20). Canary allocator tweak deployed to limit prefetch backlog on affected hosts. Internal tenant (tenant-93) agreed to stagger snapshot jobs — INT coordination ticket created.
Planned permanent fixes:
- Autoscaler tuning: evaluate lowering predictive smoothing for latency-sensitive dedicated pools and add guardrails to avoid oscillation (task created for autoscaler team).
- Prefetch subsystem: add stronger visibility and backpressure metrics; implement faster orphan-handle GC and earlier attach-failure detection.
- Placement policy: better IO-affinity packing rules to avoid co-locating small-write-heavy tenants with low-latency dedicated pools.
Status: In Progress (deployments for autoscaler config and allocator GC improvements scheduled in next sprint).
1) Autoscaler team to run A/B with 1m predictive window for a subset of dedicated pools and monitor oscillation risk (owner: Priya Patel).
2) Scheduler/allocator to produce a host placement advisory and a flag to avoid snapshot-heavy tenants co-located with latency-sensitive pools (owner: Diego Alvarez).
3) CS to follow up with Acme on 2026-03-13 for final verification and close the incident once proof-of-fix deployed.
4) Postmortem and runbook updates to be authored after fixes (owner: Maya Chen).
payload.summary: Tenant I/O coupling causing gradual capacity bleed and autoscaler unresponsiveness

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer FleetPush reports a persistent spike of 429 responses across multiple webhook endpoints after a credential rotation they initiated. Impact: ~30% of webhook deliveries return 429s for ~10-30 minutes per rotation wave, causing backfill and duplicate deliveries on their side. Environment: production (dedicated pool) in us-west-2.

Observed behavior:
- FleetPush triggered a staged API credential rotation via our Console (rollout window: 03/10 02:00 UTC) with rapid overlapping activation waves from their CI.
- During and shortly after activation waves we see tenant-wide 429s on webhook routes and increased token-accounting events in rate-limiter logs.
- The customer uses a webhook orchestrator that opens many short-lived connections (HTTP/2 multiplexed clients) and aggressively retries.

Expected behavior:
- Staged credential rotations should not cause tenant-level token exhaustion or unexpected 429s for existing active sessions.

Notes: Customer believes rotation UI toggles were staggered locally but orchestration triggered near-simultaneous activation in our edge fleet due to webhook CI concurrency.

1) In dedicated pool, initiate credential rotation from console for tenant with multiplexed webhook clients.
2) Simulate webhook orchestrator starting 200 short-lived HTTP/2 streams that authenticate with the new credential at once.
3) Observe 429 rates on /v1/webhook/* routes and token-accounting increments in rate-limiter logs for the tenant.
4) Replay with staggered activation (1s to 60s jitter) to compare behavior.
Initial hypothesis: simultaneous activation across many edge proxies led to transient double-counting (preflight + activation) against the tenant burst pool. Correlated spike with user-initiated rotation window and high fanout from webhook orchestrator.
Actions taken:
- Pulled rate-limiter token accounting for tenant across edges; saw sharp refill / issue windows matching customer's activation timestamps.
- Replayed activation in staging with local orchestrator: reproduces elevated 429 when activation requests are batched within the same refill epoch.
- Confirmed that health-check and preflight probes from orchestrator contributed to accounting.
Pending: SRE to review edge-proxy activation path that increments token windows on credential handshake and preflight simultaneously.

2026-03-10 08:40 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Correlated tenant token events with edge logs. Observed multiple activation RPCs and preflight checks counted as separate grants. Proposed short-term mitigation: recommend customer enable client-side jitter (>=30s) and Service to apply a 45s smoothing window for credential activation accounting on dedicated pools.

Follow-ups: implement server-side dedupe for activation events (ENG-4578), update rotation runbook with recommended jitter and console UX to surface activation smoothing option, and add metric alarm to surface multi-edge activation spikes.

Issue summary:
BrightCart reports a sudden, sustained increase in trace ingestion from their account starting 2026-03-13 02:10 UTC. This coincided with a billing spike for observability usage.

Impact:
- High volume of traces (10x baseline) leading to elevated ingest and processing costs for the customer and increased CPU on tracing pipeline.
- Console trace explorer overwhelmed with many low-value spans, making debugging difficult.
- Customer concerned about unexpected invoice delta.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant for BrightCart in us-east.
- Tracing sampling configuration applied at org-level (target sample_rate=0.05) via Console > Observability > Sampling.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1. Send typical production traffic through BrightCart endpoints for 20 minutes.
2. Observe traces in Console and ingestion metrics in Usage.

Observed behavior:
- Tracing shows ~95% sampling for BrightCart requests during the window.
- Console displays per-request traces for many short-lived jobs that previously were not sampled.
- Billing usage report shows elevated "trace_ingest_units" for the timeframe.

Expected behavior:
- Org-scoped sampling policy should cap sampling at ~5% (0.05) for non-debug spans.

Quick logs/links:
- Usage dashboard snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/u/brightcart/usage?ts=2026-03-13T02:00Z
- Trace explorer example URL: https://console.redwood.ai/u/brightcart/traces/lsq-20260313-0210
- Related Slack thread: #support-brightcart (thread ts: 1710365400.000200)

BrightCart (2026-03-13 09:40 UTC): Provided tenant_id=brightcart-37 and sample trace ids: trace-8a2b, trace-8a2c. Noted issue began ~02:10 UTC after a scheduled job run.
SRE - Mei Chen (2026-03-13 11:03 UTC): Observed policy evaluation logs show rule matcher returned 'global' policy instead of org policy for several requests. Adding internal investigation notes.
Initial hypothesis: recent policy-evaluation optimizer rewrite (PR#4120) changed precedence order, causing global policy to override org-level policy when certain headers present.
Checked policy-eval logs (infra/tracing/policy-eval/2026-03-13) — lines show policy_selector returned 'global-default' for requests that should match 'org:brightcart-37'.
Found matching condition: requests with x-ro-routed=true header were evaluated by a fast-path that omitted org-scoped evaluation. This fast-path was added to reduce latency for internal routing but lacked org lookup.
Reproduction: Locally reproduced by sending requests with x-ro-routed header through staging pipeline; sampling rate applied was 1.0 instead of 0.05.
Mitigation: temporarily enabled enforcement flag at ingestion gate to respect org sampling rate. Root cause: policy-evaluation fast-path omitted org lookup after optimizer rewrite (see PR#4120). Permanent fix: landed PR#4227 to reintroduce org lookup in fast-path and added unit + integration tests. Billing: billing team opened internal charge review for BrightCart and applied a credit for the unexpected delta.
Follow-ups:
- INT-8150 to backfill missing policy-eval audit logs for 2026-03-13 window.
- Add e2e test for org+fast-path combinations (assigned to tracing team).
Confirm customer sees normal ingestion for 48 hours and close ticket if stable.
Coordinate with Billing to finalize credit adjustment and update customer with breakdown.
Monitor for regressions for 7 days across dedicated tenants with x-ro-routed-enabled headers.

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 'hangs' where inference requests appear stuck for 10-30s and then either return 429 or a late 200. This is occurring during predictable traffic bursts when their application fan-out increases (health-check and batch scoring).

Impact:
- Affects several production endpoints for Lumina Health (dedicated pool).
- Visible end-user latency spikes and elevated error rates reported by customer dashboards.
- Customer counts this as impacting critical patient-facing scoring flows.

Environment:
- Customer on Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool).
- Region: us-east-1, capacity pool: dedicated-us-east-lumina-01.
- SDK version: redwood-js 0.12.3 embedded in their Node service.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Warm model pool, normal traffic steady.
2) Trigger a scheduled batch: 300 concurrent short prompts (avg 40 tokens) over 30s.
3) Observe client-side retries kick in (initial 200ms, then 400ms, linear backoff misconfigured in their SDK).
4) Service shows bursts of 429s and many requests delayed or queued with increased tail latency.

Observed behavior:
- Sudden surge of 429s from the API gateway correlated to a narrow window (approx 60s).
- Customer SDK starts retrying aggressively (short initial backoff), creating a retry storm.
- Support traces show per-request server-side queueing and sporadic long tail that looks like 'hang' from the client perspective.

Expected behavior:
- Controlled throttling signals with Retry-After propagated to client and respectful backoffs.
- SDK should escalate backoff to avoid amplification on bursts.

Relevant logs/traces (excerpt):
- api-gateway logs: 2026-03-10T14:32:11Z 429 route=/v1/generate pool=dedicated-us-east-lumina-01 burst=true
- rate-limiter: threshold=750 rps window=1s tokens-exhausted=125
- serving-runtime: queue_depth spike to 82, avg_latency 180ms -> tail 6.2s
- customer SDK trace: seq=1345 attempt=3 backoff_ms=200

Attachments:
- Customer provided SDK traces and proxy logs (uploaded to ticket attachments).

Notes:
- Customer claims this is a regression vs last month where same batch pattern did not cause user-visible hangs.
- No full pool outage; capacity reports show GPUs healthy but with elevated scheduling waits.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
CuraSense reports intermittent requests that appear to 'hang' or return after tens of seconds. Customer observes wide tail latency spikes correlated to heavy traffic windows. They see client-side timeouts/retries and believe the serving runtime is slowing.

Impact:
- Several production customers of CuraSense saw elevated tail latency (p95->p99) during morning batch runs; product features that rely on sub-second responses degrade.
- Customer experienced increased error counts and duplicate charges from retries.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod-us-east) running dedicated pool for CuraSense.
- Customer uses SDK-js v1.3.6 with default retry policy.
- Affected model: redwood/rhine-13b-8k pinned at v2026-02-28.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Run 120 concurrent streaming requests with 1–2 token priming across 10 hosts from us-east ip range.
2) Observe ~3–8% of requests take >10s or appear to never return to the client (client eventually times out and retries).
3) Client logs show rapid immediate retries after perceived timeout; server logs show bursts of 429s.

Observed behavior:
- Server logs show many short-lived 429 responses (soft quota enforcement) with no Retry-After header present in most cases.
- Client SDK immediately retries on socket timeout/closed stream without exponential jitter. This creates retry amplification and increases load on the rate limiter, which in turn produces more 429 responses (feedback loop).

Expected behavior:
- Soft quota 429s should be communicated with Retry-After or gracefully degrade (503) so clients back off.
- SDK should implement exponential backoff + jitter and treat 429s as explicit signals to back off.

Relevant logs & links:
- Trace samples: trace ids: trace-20260310-7cf8b1, trace-20260310-7cf8d2 (linked to internal trace store)
- Rate limiter dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rate-limiter/soft-quota-bursts
- Customer's SDK logs (attached in ticket)

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 09:35 - Customer (CuraSense - eng@curasense.co): Sent sample logs and client traces. Confirmed they run concurrent short requests and see many client-side retries in quick succession.
2026-03-12 16:10 - CuraSense (Customer): Confirmed tail latency dropped in the observed window after mitigation; asked for next steps to avoid recurrence.
SRE reproduction: under sustained short-request concurrency the api-gateway's token-bucket enters a soft-quota state and begins returning 429s to some requests in microbursts.
Many 429 responses lacked Retry-After header due to codepath in legacy rate-limiter (relevant service: rate-limiter v2.4.1) that returns 429 in soft-deny mode without adding Retry-After. This makes it a non-explicit signal to clients.
Observed client behavior: SDK-js v1.3.6 treats socket close/timeouts as transient and retries immediately up to N attempts with no jitter; combined with short timeouts this amplifies traffic.
Correlation shows retry storms align with p99 latency spikes and increased 429 counts; root cause is interaction between soft quota enforcement and aggressive client retries (amplification).
Proposed server-side fixes: add Retry-After header for soft-429s, consider returning 503 for short cooldown with Retry-After, enable burst-smoothing and token refill tuning for dedicated pools.
Proposed client-side fixes: release SDK patch to honor 429 as a backoff signal, implement exponential backoff + jitter, and add configurable max-concurrency defaults for short streaming workloads.
2026-03-12 - Short-term mitigation: increased CuraSense soft quota by 25% for next 72 hours and enabled api-gateway rate-smoothing. Observed immediate reduction in tail latency during customer morning window.
2026-03-13 - Server fix (PR #1428) merged: rate-limiter now sets Retry-After header on soft-429s and exposes per-customer cooldown metric. Rolling out to prod-us-east.
2026-03-13 - SDK fix (PR #329) merged: sdk-js v1.3.7 will interpret 429s as backoff signals and uses exponential backoff with jitter; released to npm and sent customer patch instructions.
Follow-up actions: schedule postmortem and add runbook entry: 'Handling soft quota 429s' in Confluence; update dedicated pool autoscaling knobs to reduce soft-deny frequency; coordinate SDK minor release notes and notify customers about recommended concurrency settings.
Customer verified: CuraSense reported improved p99 behavior after mitigations and agreed to onboard SDK patch across clients.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During SapphireLine's nightly end-of-day batch (scheduled 02:00-03:30 UTC), a subset of inference requests experienced streaming truncation and intermittent 5xx spikes across us-east and eu-west. Customers reported partial transcripts and missing trailing tokens for streaming completions, plus repeated client reconnects. Impact: multiple business-critical batch jobs failed to reconcile logs and generated duplicate downstream processing attempts.

Impact:
- Affected ~7% of batch traffic for SapphireLine between 2026-03-11 02:07 and 2026-03-11 02:41 UTC.
- Streaming responses truncated mid-completion; clients saw final chunk missing.
- Several retries caused billing/usage anomalies and duplicate downstream webhooks.

Environment:
- Hosted Redwood API (enterprise tenant), dedicated routing for SapphireLine in us-east and eu-west.
- Smart-router service v2.3.1 deployed across both regions.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Run high-concurrency streaming job against redwood/gptx-13b-v2 with session affinity enabled and target traffic split across two availability zones.
2) Trigger a control-plane autoscaler event that drains one routing pool (simulated node removal).
3) Observe some streams where the handshake completes but the stream ends with no terminal chunk; client reconnects and receives a truncated resume offset.

Logs & traces:
- Correlation IDs attached in investigation notes.
- Streaming proxy logs show abrupt TCP FIN from nodes receiving requests after routing table change.
- Smart-router trace shows concurrent topology update and in-flight route reassignment in a 350ms window.
2026-03-11 02:18 - SapphireLine SRE (customer): 'We're seeing hundreds of truncated streaming completions in the EOD flush. It's causing reconciliation to drop the last line item. Can you confirm this is on your side?'
2026-03-11 02:21 - Support (Aisha): 'Acknowledged — investigating. We've opened a Major Incident and are pulling SRE/Serving on-call. ETA for first update 10 minutes.'
2026-03-11 02:31 - SRE (Liam): 'Preliminary: smart-router v2.3.1 performed a topology update while autoscaler issued drain signals. Some in-flight streams were redirected to nodes without the streaming plugin enabled (legacy-quant routing path) and the stream frame API returned early EOFs.'
2026-03-11 02:44 - Support (Aisha): 'Mitigation: rolled back smart-router to v2.3.0 in us-east and eu-west for SapphireLine's routes. Re-routed live traffic to stable pool. Customer reporting improved behaviour — truncated responses no longer observed after 02:42 UTC.'
2026-03-11 09:12 - SapphireLine Engineering: 'Thanks for the quick response. We did see jobs clear and our reconciliation completed for the remaining batches. Please advise on permanent mitigations and billing credits for duplicate downstream webhooks.'
2026-03-12 16:05 - Product (Lydia Chen): 'Documenting follow-ups: smart-router release gating, add e2e streaming resume tests, and ensure autoscaler drain window is extended for streaming workloads.'
Observation 1: The timing window where topology update overlapped with drain events was ~350ms; requests launched in that window were marked routed to new node but had backend handshake discrepancies.
Observation 2: Legacy routing path (metric name: routing.plugin.legacy_quant) lacked the streaming-frame-seq header enforcement introduced in 2.3.0 — result: resumed connections lacked monotonic seq and were treated as new streams.
Hypothesis: race in control-plane (smart-router v2.3.1) plus aggressive autoscaler drain timeout caused some streams to be reassigned mid-session to nodes missing streaming plugin; clients received early EOF and retried, producing duplicate downstream webhook events.
Evidence: tcpdump + streaming-proxy logs show FIN from reassigned nodes and subsequent new connections with identical client session-id but starting sequence at 0; correlation IDs show truncated transcript length matches shard assignment changes.
Timeline: 02:07 UTC first truncated stream observed; 02:18 customer escalation; 02:31 engineering identified routing race; 02:36 rollback started; 02:42 stable behaviour restored for affected routes.
Related telemetry: token-level cost spike correlating to retries between 02:10-02:45 UTC; approximate billing delta for SapphireLine ~0.9% of that day's usage (to be reconciled).
Immediate mitigation:
- Rolled back smart-router to v2.3.0 for SapphireLine routes in us-east and eu-west (02:36-02:40 UTC).
- Re-routed traffic to stable serving pool and disabled aggressive autoscale drains for streaming tenant for 24 hours.

Permanent fixes planned / completed:

Additional notes:
- Added monotonic sequence header enforcement for streaming resume so resumed streams are validated and duplicates are rejected.
- Autoscaler change: extend drain window by default for streaming workloads and add a drain-safe flag for routes with active streaming sessions.
Customer remediation & follow-up:
- Issued a 30% invoice credit for the affected billing window and committed to a dedicated post-incident review with SapphireLine engineering.
- Action items assigned: engineering to add e2e streaming failover tests in CI; SRE to add a dashboard alert for topology-change-in-flight > 100ms; support to coordinate with billing to reconcile webhook duplication charges.
- Post-incident exec brief scheduled 2026-03-16 with product, SRE, and SapphireLine (invite sent).

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightVoice AI reported intermittent flips from their pinned model (rw-infer-v2.1) back to the legacy variant during a staged canary promotion. The flips coincide with an edge priority reordering event triggered by a regional capacity rebalance.
Impact: Multiple customer sessions observed mixed outputs (some responses from rw-infer-v2.1, some from open-llama-65b-q4 legacy), session-level latency increased ~3x, and BrightVoice reported degraded quality affecting their chat product for several customer-facing sessions.
Environment: Production (BrightVoice tenant on Dedicated cluster), incidents observed in us-east and eu-west during 2026-03-10 03:20–06:00 UTC. Orchestrator version: 4.7.2-edge, Edge-proxy version: 2.13.7. Serving runtime: 1.12.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a staged canary promotion of rw-infer-v2.1 with 10% weight in eu-west and us-east. 2) Simulate a capacity rebalance: preempt a standby GPU in us-east region to force one orchestrator priority swap. 3) Send a burst of 200 tenant-scoped streaming sessions pinned to rw-infer-v2.1. 4) Observe routing headers and model variant in responses.
Observed behavior: During the orchestrator priority swap, edge-proxy queues reordered a subset of in-flight requests. Pin commit messages (control-plane -> edge commit) were delivered but not applied consistently: some edge nodes reported successful commit, others returned a 409-like response in logs and treated the commit as a no-op. Result: a window where requests for the same session hit mixed variants and some sessions fell back to the legacy variant.
Expected behavior: Pin commit should be applied atomically per-session across edge nodes or rejected in a way that preserves existing pin (no mixed-variant window).
Logs & traces:
- edge-proxy logs (us-east/edge-7): "pin_commit: id=tvk-3345 -> commit_failed: priority-mismatch-requeue"
- orchestrator trace (4.7.2-edge): "commit-broadcast delayed by 420ms for shard s72 during priority-reorder"
- serving-runtime logs: intermittent 502s during the same timeframe
Workaround taken: Immediately increased pin-commit timeout on customer's tenant to 3s and pinned at an account-level sticky token to force session affinity to a single edge node. This reduced mixed responses but did not eliminate them for long-lived streams.
Temporary mitigation: 1) Advise customer to enable tenant-level affinity override until a permanent fix is deployed. 2) Apply an emergency patch to edge-proxy to avoid reordering in-flight commit messages during priority swaps (rollbackable hotfix deployed to us-east on 2026-03-11 01:10 UTC).
Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Edge reordering combined with non-idempotent commit semantics allows a later-in-time commit to be applied on some nodes while earlier commits are dropped; this causes split-view across nodes.
- Hypothesis B: Orchestrator broadcast uses a best-effort shard fanout; priority swaps cause some shards to queue commits and apply them out-of-order relative to in-flight requests.
- Evidence: Correlated commit-broadcast timestamps show 300–600ms skew between shards. Edge nodes that reported "commit_failed: priority-mismatch-requeue" subsequently resumed normal routing once the emergency patch prevented message reordering.
Follow-up tasks created:
- INT-4421: Add idempotent compare-and-set for pin commits at the edge (planned SRV-Q2-375).
- ORCH-1290 (github PR): Ensure orchestrator commit broadcasts are ordered by commit-timestamp per-tenant.
- Add a canary test scenario to the release pipeline that simulates priority reorders while committing pins.
Customer communication: BrightVoice notified via #support-private and provided session ids and sample transcripts. We promised hourly updates until resolution.
Next steps: 1) Engineering to implement idempotent pin apply (INT-4421) and ensure commit ordering (ORCH-1290). 2) Expand edge-proxy hotfix to eu-west after validation (scheduled 2026-03-15). 3) Add observability: per-tenant commit-apply success rate metric and alert (SLO threshold 99.95%). 4) Postmortem to be written in confluence and shared with BrightVoice when complete.
Severity rationale: P1/Sev1 because pinned model behavior violated contract and produced mixed outputs for end users; impacts SLAs and quality.
1) Start staged canary promotion of rw-infer-v2.1 at 10% weight in eu-west and us-east. 2) Trigger regional capacity rebalance to force orchestrator priority swap (simulate preempt on standby GPU). 3) Issue a burst of 200 streaming sessions pinned to rw-infer-v2.1 using BrightVoice tenant tokens. 4) Monitor edge-proxy logs for 'commit_failed: priority-mismatch-requeue' and correlate with model variant in responses.
Initial triage: Support confirmed reports and collected traces. SRE reproduced message reordering during orchestrator priority swap in a staging cluster which led to inconsistent pin apply across edge shards. Engineering confirmed commit broadcast is not strictly ordered and pin apply is not idempotent, allowing split-state under concurrent priority reorders. Emergency mitigation reduced occurrence but permanent fixes require adding idempotent compare-and-set and stronger ordering guarantees from orchestrator.
Workarounds: tenant-level affinity override and increased pin-commit timeout reduced customer impact. Hotfix prevented message reordering on us-east and decreased incident frequency. Permanent fix: engineering to implement idempotent pin apply and ordered commit broadcasts (target release 4.8.0). Customer-facing timeline: planned eu-west hotfix 2026-03-15 and full rollout of fixes in 4.8.0 (canary + staged rollout) by end of March. Postmortem owner: Liam Chen.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 05:02 UTC - SRE (Marco Diaz): Reproduced in staging by inducing orchestrator priority swap; observed commit-broadcast skew between shards. Captured logs and trace ids: trace-7721, trace-7722.
2026-03-10 06:30 UTC - Eng (Priya Nair): Looked at commit path. Pin apply at edge is currently 'apply if commit id > local-id' without CAS; if reordering occurs commits can be lost. Proposed emergency patch to avoid reordering in-flight messages.
2026-03-11 01:05 UTC - Ops (Liam Chen): Deployed hotfix to us-east edge-proxy that adds ordering buffer for commit messages; monitoring for regressions.
2026-03-11 08:20 UTC - BrightVoice (customer): Noticed improvements after fix in us-east but still seeing occasional swaps in eu-west. Asked for ETA on full fix.
2026-03-12 11:45 UTC - Eng (Priya Nair): Created ORCH-1290 and INT-4421. ORCH-1290 PR for ordered broadcast is under review: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1289.
2026-03-14 09:15 UTC - Support (Aisha Gomez): Updated customer with planned eu-west hotfix date 2026-03-15 and target 4.8.0 rollout. Assigned Liam as postmortem owner.

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout for redwood-open-7B-v2 in the BrightHealth dedicated fleet, a staggered TTL commit across edge shards caused a small cohort of tenant sessions to lose pin-coherence. Impact: affected tenant sessions experienced repeated fallback between the canary variant and the stable variant, resulting in increased tail latency, duplicated token outputs for streaming sessions, and sporadic 5xx errors. Scope: limited to BrightHealth AI customers on the dedicated pool in us-east-1; first observed after a canary weight increase at 2026-03-10T09:22:00Z.
1) Configure a weighted canary rollout (10% -> 40%) for redwood-open-7B-v2 with edge shard TTLs set to staggered commit windows.
2) Initiate traffic from tenant with long-lived streaming sessions.
3) Observe routing logs on edge and control plane when canary weight crosses the health-window boundary.
4) Reproduce by simulating intermittent rate-limit 429 responses from a single edge shard while health probes continue to report 'healthy'.
[2026-03-10T09:22:15Z] edge-ash-12 INFO route-decide tenant=brighthealth sess=abc123 pinned=stable -> candidate=canary weight=0.10
[2026-03-10T09:22:18Z] controlplane-commit INFO commit-ttl tenant=brighthealth shard=ash-12 ttl=30s commit-window=2026-03-10T09:22:18Z
[2026-03-10T09:22:19Z] edge-ash-12 WARN request=xyz 429 rate_limit exceeded
[2026-03-10T09:22:21Z] edge-ash-12 INFO route-decide tenant=brighthealth sess=abc123 pinned=canary -> fallback=stable reason=fallback-on-retry
[2026-03-10T09:22:23Z] stream-xyz ERROR token-duplication detected tokens=+2 session=abc123
[2026-03-10T09:22:25Z] controlplane INFO reconcile tenant=brighthealth pin-consistency=unstable
Initial hypothesis: staggered TTL commit across edge shards allowed control-plane to see mixed pin states for same tenant during rapid weight adjustments.
Edge shard ash-12 returned intermittent 429s which triggered client-side retry logic and the edge route decision returned a fallback to stable variant while control-plane commit for canary was in-flight.
We observed pin metadata TTL differences by ~2-6s between ash-12 and ash-14 during the window; this matched the timing of the fallback loop.
No code-level bug in routing algorithm was found; the race is between commit propagation and edge retry/fallback heuristics under throttling.
Related config: control-plane commit-window default=5s, edge retry backoff=250ms x 3, pin-ttl=30s.
1) For affected tenants, set explicit model pin on the tenant route (pin: redwood-open-7B-v2-stable) to force stable serving while we remediate propagation timing.
2) Reduce canary weight ramp-up steps and increase commit-window to 15s to avoid in-flight mismatch.
3) Apply per-edge backpressure smoothing to prevent 429-triggered immediate fallback.
In progress: control-plane patch proposed to add commit monotonic fencing (PR linked) and edge fallback heuristic adjusted to wait for in-flight commit acknowledgement when commit timestamps are newer than local pin TTL. Long-term: add explicit pin-sync protocol between control-plane and edge to avoid TTL stagger races. Target: patch to be deployed to staging 2026-03-13 and prod 2026-03-14 after validation.

2026-03-10T10:22:30Z - SRE (Evan Coleman): Collected edge shard metrics and found short-lived 429 spikes on ash-12 correlated with commit windows. Reproduced locally with simulated 429s; fallback loop reproduced.
2026-03-10T11:05:12Z - Engineering (Priya Narang): Added instrumentation to control-plane commit path to log commit-timestamp and shard acknowledgements. Observed 4-6s propagation skew between shards in prod under current commit-window.
2026-03-10T11:45:00Z - Support (Mei Chen) -> Customer (BrightHealth AI): Applied temporary explicit pin and reduced rollout speed; customer reports immediate reduction in duplication. Asking customer for confirmation of service level for remainder of business day.
2026-03-11T09:10:00Z - SRE (Evan Coleman): Deployed emergency config change to increase commit-window to 15s for ongoing canaries in us-east-1. Rollout monitored; no further fallback loops observed in 6h post-change.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers observed a sustained increase in 5xx errors originating at the API gateway during large multipart streaming requests that included unusually large custom metadata headers. Impact: multiple streaming sessions failed with 502/503 and the serving-runtime pool for the affected tenant entered a thread-spin / high CPU state, causing progressive upstream failures and client timeouts.

Impact:
- LatticeHealth reported 12% of streaming calls failing with 502/503 between 2026-03-10T02:15 and 2026-03-10T03:40 (us-west).
- Elevated p50/p95 stream latencies and increased runtime CPU usage on 6 hosts in the dedicated tenant pool.
- Customer-facing sessions reported reconnect loops; some clients retried aggressively leading to amplified load.

Environment:
- prod | us-west (tenant: lattice-prod-dedicated)
- API Gateway (nginx-based front proxy), ingress parsing pipeline -> runtime proxy -> serving-runtime GPU workers.

Steps to reproduce (internal reproduction):
1) Send a multipart streaming request simulating client behavior: a 10MB payload split into chunks with ~200 custom metadata headers (each ~16KB).
2) Observe ingress accept log; API gateway stalls while parsing headers.
3) Requests either timeout at the gateway (502) or are forwarded but cause serving-runtime request handler threads to enter long spin cycles trying to read/assemble headers, producing high CPU and watchdog resets.

Logs & Observations:
- apigw error logs: "ingress: header parse delay > 1200ms, connection queued" (see apigw-logs lines: apigw-usw-12: /var/log/apigw/2026-03-10.log:line 4872).
- runtime syslogs: recurrent "request-handler: waiting on header assembly" and then "worker watchdog triggered" followed by runtime restart entries.
- tracing: distributed trace shows 90th percentile time spent in ingress header-parsing span (ingress.parse_headers) increased from ~3ms to ~1.2s for affected requests.
- metrics: p50 latency for streaming route increased from 140ms -> 420ms; 5xx rate jump to 12% for tenant.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis was a malformed chunk boundary or backend prefetch causing backpressure; however packet captures and trace spans showed the dominant delay in header parsing at the gateway layer.
- The specific trigger was a combination of high count of headers with large individual header sizes (common when clients attach extensive per-chunk metadata). The gateway's header parser used an O(n^2) path when handling very large header maps under the current config, which isn't exercised by normal traffic.
- While header parsing was stalled, connection accept backlog increased, and proxy worker threads held file descriptors open waiting for parse completion; downstream runtime handlers received partially-assembled requests and stalled while blocking on header assembly, leading to CPU spin and eventual watchdog resets.
- Reproduced locally with a synthetic client. Confirmed that reducing header count/size avoided the condition immediately.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Rate-limited the tenant's streaming route from the edge to reduce retry amplification (applied 2026-03-10T03:00).
- Added a temporary header count and aggregate header size limit at the API gateway layer for the tenant (soft reject with 413 when exceeded).
- Advised customer to stop including per-chunk large metadata and to aggregate metadata into the first chunk while we deploy a fix.

Root cause:
- An inefficient header parsing code path in the API gateway that degenerates under very large header counts/sizes, combined with downstream runtime handlers that assume quick header assembly and block on partial reads. This produced a feedback loop: parse stalls -> accept backlog -> proxy threads held -> serving-runtime threads blocked -> watchdogs restart -> 5xx wave.

Resolution & rollout notes:
- Patch deployed to API gateway ingress parser to short-circuit pathological header maps, move to linear-time parsing for header counts, and enforce configurable header parsing timeouts. Deployed 2026-03-11 01:30 UTC to canary pool and 2026-03-11 03:10 UTC to prod us-west.
- Serving-runtime patched to avoid blocking request handlers on header assembly by offloading header reads to async parsing goroutine and adding a parse timeout guard. Deployed 2026-03-11 02:45 UTC.
- Per-tenant soft header size/count limit implemented with clear 413 response and reason message.
- Rolling restart of 6 affected runtime hosts completed 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC.
- Post-deploy monitoring: 5xx rate for lattice-prod-dedicated returned to baseline (<0.5%) within one hour of full rollout.

Follow-ups / Action items:
- (ENG-5123) Add unit+fuzz tests for header parser edge cases (assigned to ingress team).
- (SRE-2981) Add circuit-breaker alert for ingress header-parse latency > 200ms sustained across hosts.
- Customer communication: CS sent detailed incident summary and recommended client changes.

Related links:
- Slack thread: #support-lattice / thread TS12345
- Traces: https://tracing.redwood.internal/trace/abcd-parse-span-20260310 (internal)
- Apigw logs excerpt: s3://redwood-logs/apigw/us-west/2026-03-10/apigw-usw-12.log:4872-4910
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/2345, https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/447

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:10 - LatticeHealth (Customer): Confirmed downstream errors resolved and no further replay storms observed. Thanked team for quick remediation.
Ingress parser and serving-runtime fixes deployed; tenant soft-limits applied; rolling restart completed. 5xx rates returned to baseline. Follow-up tickets created for tests and alerts.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer ScribeLabs reports that after our zero-downtime rolling cutover from text-redwood-v3.1 -> text-redwood-v3.2 (canary -> main), a subset of requests that were explicitly model-pinned by the customer started receiving fallback responses from older variants or 5xx errors. Impact begins ~2026-03-10 03:12 UTC during the canary -> cutover window.

Impact:
- ~12% of ScribeLabs' pinned requests returned model-incompatibility fallbacks or 5xx over a 22-minute window.
- Increased latency for pinned endpoints (p95 from 240ms -> 950ms) and user-visible failures for a production pipeline.

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated), us-east-1 region.
- Rollout performed via rollout-controller v1.14.2.
- Edge proxies: envoy 1.23 with route cache.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Customer pins route "scribe-annotate" to text-redwood-v3.1 using policy pin-by-model-version.
2) Initiate canary roll (v3.2) with 5% traffic to canary, then promote to 100% with zero-downtime cutover.
3) Observe routing logs for requests with header X-Model-Pin and cookie "rw-affinity" during cutover.
4) In affected timeframe, tailing router logs show successful pin update events but affinity headers still resolved to stale instance IDs that no longer advertise the pinned model metadata.

Observed behavior:
- Rollout-controller updates the model-version record for the pin but edge-proxy route cache retains an affinity mapping to instance IDs that were decommissioned as part of the cutover.
- When edge-proxy tries to route to the affinity instance and cannot find a matching model, fallback triggers and sends the request either to a backward-compatible variant (older model) or returns a 5xx when no compatible variant is available.
- Flushing route cache manually (SRE action) resolves the symptom for sessions that reauth or refresh affinity cookies.

Expected behavior:
- Pinned requests should continue to resolve to the customer's pinned model version (or a compatible promoted variant) through the cutover window without user-visible fallbacks.

Logs/trace evidence:
- Router log snippet (sanitized):
  - 2026-03-10T03:14:22Z routing: route_lookup pid=8742 affinity_cookie=rw-affinity id=inst-4b2a expired=yes model_meta_missing=true fallback=variant_old
  - 2026-03-10T03:15:01Z rollout: pin-update route=scribe-annotate model=text-redwood-v3.2 user=ScribeLabs status=committed
  - 2026-03-10T03:15:03Z routing: route_lookup pid=8750 affinity_cookie=rw-affinity id=inst-3f9c not_found -> fallback to variant_old

Temporary workarounds applied by Support/SRE:
- Manual flush of edge route caches and instructing ScribeLabs to re-open sessions which cleared affinity cookies. This reduced failures to <1% within 10 minutes.
- As a stop-gap, we advised ScribeLabs to temporarily unpin the route and re-pin post-cutover; this is disruptive and not acceptable long-term.

Notes:
- Customer requests a root-cause and durable fix; they are on a dedicated contract and expect a non-disruptive remediation path.

Initial hypothesis: routing affinity persisted to decommissioned instances due to a race between rollout-controller model-record update and edge-proxy route cache invalidation.
Findings so far:
- rollout-controller updates happen via control-plane notifications but edge proxies use a local route cache keyed by affinity instance id. There is no explicit invalidation event for affinityIds when an instance is drained; we rely on TTLs.
- In this incident the instance id referenced by active cookies was decommissioned quickly during cutover; the control-plane did not emit a specific affinity invalidation message, so edge proxies attempted to route and fell back.
- A secondary issue: new canary instances did not advertise the legacy affinity label "pin-group:v1" that older instances used, so automated compatibility matching failed and triggered fallbacks instead of routing to the new model variant.
- Reproduced in staging by creating pinned session + forced drain of an instance; observed identical behavior.
Hypothesis: two contributing bugs - (1) missing affinity invalidation on instance drain, (2) inconsistent pin-group metadata between old and new model variants after canary rollout.
Temporary mitigations validated: route-cache flush and ensuring new instances advertise compatible pin-group tags.

2026-03-10 04:05 - ScribeLabs (customer): 'We started seeing 500s for our annotate endpoint during your upgrade window. Many requests that were pinned to v3.1 are failing. Please advise.'
2026-03-10 04:09 - Support (Aisha Patel): 'Acknowledged. We're investigating and will provide a mitigation shortly. Can you confirm whether sessions are long-lived and whether you use rw-affinity cookies?'
2026-03-10 04:22 - ScribeLabs: 'Yes, sessions are sticky for up to 48h and we use the rw-affinity cookie. Unpinning temporarily reduced errors.'
2026-03-10 05:10 - SRE (Lena Ortiz): 'Flushed edge route caches in us-east-1 and recommended customer re-auth; errors dropped to baseline. Collecting router logs for analysis.'
2026-03-10 12:30 - Engineering (Marco Chen): 'Reproduced in staging with a forced drain. Filing small rollout-controller change to emit affinity invalidation events and adding backward-compatible pin-group label propagation for canaries. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-controller/pull/878'
2026-03-11 09:14 - Support (Aisha Patel): 'Customer notified of temporary mitigation and that engineering is working on a patch. Monitoring for any recurrence.'
1) Patch rollout-controller to emit explicit affinity invalidation events on instance drain and ensure edge-proxy config can subscribe and invalidate route cache entries immediately.
2) Add a rollout validation check that verifies pin-group labels are present on canary and promoted instances (backfill when missing).
3) Update docs/runbook with steps to handle pinned routes during cutover and add a monitoring alert for sudden spike in pinned-route fallbacks.
4) Schedule an after-action call with ScribeLabs once patch is staged.

Under investigation; likely a race between instance drain (edge affinity TTL) and lack of explicit affinity invalidation combined with missing pin-group metadata on canary instances

Customer requests a legally defensible delivery of audit events for a procurement security assessment. They require an ordered SIEM export with a signed SHA256 manifest, object-lock enabled artifact storage, attacker-resistant delivery receipts, and a sample chain-of-custody proving custody timestamps and KMS key fingerprints.
Issue summary:
Atlas FT (enterprise) is running a procurement security review and needs an evidence bundle containing: an ordered SIEM export (last 90 days), per-file SHA256 checksums plus a top-level signed manifest, timestamps with RFC3161-style proof, storage with object-lock/immutable retention in their region, and HSM/KMS key fingerprint attestation. They additionally ask for delivery receipts showing successful SFTP/HTTPS handoff with server-side verification, and a short explanation of the export process for their legal team.

Impact:
This is a compliance/contractual request from procurement causing a hold on onboarding until evidence is provided. It is time-sensitive (legal review meeting scheduled 2026-03-18).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod (us-east)
- Customer account: atlas-ft-prod (enterprise)
- Export target planned: Atlas-managed Azure Blob (object-lock) and fallback SFTP to their on-prem archive

Requested artifacts (customer-provided template attached via ticket):
1) 90-day chronological SIEM export (newline-delimited JSON) broken into daily archives.
2) SHA256 manifest per archive plus top-level manifest signed with Redwood KMS key (and copy signed with HSM attestation).
3) RFC3161-style timestamp token for the top-level manifest.
4) Delivery proof: SFTP server logs showing successful PUT with server-response codes and TLS session fingerprints, and HTTPS webhook delivery receipts with callback verification headers.
5) Short readme describing field mapping and redaction policy used during export.

Steps to reproduce / prepare artifacts (internal):
1. Generate daily export for last 90 days using audit-export job (date-window).
2. Normalize timestamps to UTC ISO8601 and canonicalize fields per Atlas template.
3. Compress and sign each archive: compute sha256sum, append to per-directory manifest.
4. Create top-level manifest listing files and checksums. Sign manifest using KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/redwood-audit-signing-key (customer requested key fingerprint).
5. Request RFC3161 timestamp from timestamping authority used by Redwood (or include local attestation chain).
6. Deliver on Azure Blob with object-lock enabled; if not possible in time, deliver via SFTP with signed delivery receipt.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sustained 429s for a subset of routes after a planned plugin reload that happened during nightly worker warmup. Impacted requests are both long-poll streaming and short embedding calls.

Impact:
- NeuroEdge reported 12% of requests returning 429 across their dedicated pool for ~18 minutes during their nightly scheduled workers window.
- End-users saw failed webhooks and stalled embedding backfills.
- Customer lost tail SLA for that maintenance window.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (dedicated) in prod-us-east running 4 G4dn hosts behind API gateway.
- Plugin reload was a config rollout of the telemetry-agent (v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0) rolled via canary.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start large scheduled worker fanout (500 short-run tasks) that performs embed calls and opens short-lived streaming sessions.
2) Trigger telemetry-agent plugin reload on pool during warmup (matched customer timing).
3) Notice a burst of telemetry pings + in-flight retry-drain messages that coincide with quota accounting updates.
4) Shortly after, API returns 429s with X-RateLimit headers indicating negative available tokens and refill windows misaligned.

Expected behavior:
Normal plugin reload should not increment tenant token counters or count telemetry heartbeats as consumer traffic. Rate accounting should remain stable across the canary swap.

Actual behavior:
Telemetry pings and drain/retry coordination messages were misattributed to customer request accounting for a short epoch, causing temporary token depletion and tenant-wide 429s.

Urgency:
Customer is on dedicated tier with SLA; production impact reported. Customer requests mitigation and a short postmortem explaining root cause and corrective actions.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 09:28 - Customer (NeuroEdge): Provided sample request_ids: nid-20260310-09-14-{a..f} and approximate window 2026-03-10T09:10:00Z - 2026-03-10T09:28:00Z. Noted they performed a telemetry-agent canary at 09:11Z.
2026-03-11 14:02 - Support (Aisha Khan): Posted workaround to customer: scheduled a quick config flip to mark telemetry-agent pin=\"exempt-from-quota\" and rolled restart on a subset of hosts. This restored available tokens within two refill cycles (~90s).
2026-03-12 08:30 - Customer (NeuroEdge): Confirmed workaround restored normal behavior. Asked for permanent fix and advisory to avoid during heavy scheduled workers.
High-level timeline: plugin canary started at 09:11Z -> telemetry-agent v2.5.0 exposed new debug handshake at 09:12Z that used same client socket path -> gateway token middleware increments for each handshake and for telemetry pings because the exempt flag was not set in PR-4182.
Hypothesis: during reload the agent emitted burst telemetry heartbeats while also issuing a drain/retry state sync which created duplicate counting for ephemeral handshakes and incremental telemetry. Those increments pushed tenant token balance negative inside the epoch, causing the limiter to return 429 until refill.
Evidence: token-service metrics show +6.8k increments labeled source=telemetry-agent in a 2 minute window that map to the customer pool. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/rl/tenant-token-balance?orgId=1&var-tenant=neuroedge. Linked PR: github.com/redwood/release/PR-4182.
Next steps: 1) Confirm code change that set exempt flag was reverted to canary until tests added. 2) Add unit tests to token middleware to ignore source=telemetry-agent and agent-handshake events. 3) Run canary traffic with mixed scheduled-worker load to validate.
Sample gateway log lines (redacted):
2026-03-10T09:12:13.342Z gateway-01 INFO request_id=nid-20260310-09-14-a source=telemetry-agent event=handshake token_inc=1 route=/internal/telemetry/handshake
2026-03-10T09:12:13.343Z gateway-01 INFO request_id=nid-20260310-09-14-b source=telemetry-agent event=heartbeat token_inc=1 route=/internal/telemetry/heartbeat
2026-03-10T09:12:13.345Z gateway-01 WARN request_id=nid-20260310-09-14-c source=ingest event=embed token_inc=1 route=/v1/embeddings status=429 x-ratelimit-remaining=-3 x-ratelimit-reset-in=72
2026-03-10T09:12:14.001Z token-svc INFO tenant=neuroedge increment=6800 window_epoch=2026-03-10T09:12:00Z
Workaround applied: set telemetry agent processes to \"exempt-from-quota=true\" on customer dedicated pool and roll-backed the canary on rolling hosts. This immediately stopped telemetry increments being counted. Customer confirmed restoration of normal request success within two refill cycles (~90s).
Permanent fix: reverted PR-4182 change and authored patch PR-4195 that ensures token-middleware rejects events with tag telemetry_exempt and differentiates handshake vs consumer traffic. Patch scheduled for staged canary and test rollout.
Follow-ups: add an automated regression test that simulates plugin reload with concurrent scheduled-worker traffic, update runbook 'telemetry-drain-runbook' with a section on marking agent traffic exempt, and advise customers to avoid rolling agent updates during high-volume warmup windows until patch is deployed.
Owner for follow-up: Marco Reyes. ETA for patch deployment: 2026-03-15.
Customer communication: emailed customer 2026-03-11 with workaround details and timeline for permanent fix.
Keep ticket open until PR-4195 is merged and we complete staged canary. Postmortem to be added to Confluence after closure.

payload.description:
Customer reports repeated duplicate side-effecting tool/function invocations when using function-calling with retries. The customer is on a dedicated plan behind a corporate reverse proxy that normalizes headers (lowercasing, truncation of long header values, and replacing spaces with hyphens). NimbusAI sees duplicate webhook/tool calls on retry even though they supply stable idempotency keys in the SDK. Hypothesis: the proxy is rewriting/persistently normalizing the Idempotency header in-flight, so Redwood's dedupe layer receives a different header value on the retry path and treats it as a new request.
1) Use Redwood Go SDK to create a function-calling request with an explicit idempotency header 'Idempotency-Key' set to a 64+ char UUID-like token.
2) Send request from a host behind an enterprise reverse proxy that enforces header normalization (lowercase, trims >64 chars, replaces spaces).
3) Force a network timeout on the client to trigger an SDK retry (retry logic enabled at default backoff).
4) Observe that Redwood service receives first request and executes tool call; on retry the gateway receives a mutated Idempotency-Key and executes the tool again (duplicate side-effect).
5) Validate on customer side: two webhook payloads delivered to downstream service with different idempotency header values seen by Redwood logs.
customer-proxy.log: 2026-02-24T15:03:22Z INFO incoming request headers: idempotency-key: abcdef1234567890-ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWX--(truncated)
redwood-gateway.log: 2026-02-24T15:03:22Z DEBUG recv headers: Idempotency-Key: abcdef1234567890-ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWX
redwood-gateway.log: 2026-02-24T15:03:25Z INFO request processed idempotency_key=abcdef1234567890-ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWX action=tool_call tool_id=extract-entities
redwood-gateway.log: 2026-02-24T15:03:28Z DEBUG recv headers on retry: Idempotency-Key: abcdef1234567890-abcdefghijklmnop (normalized/lowercased/truncated)
redwood-serving.log: 2026-02-24T15:03:28Z INFO executed tool call id=extract-entities request_id=xyz-998 duplicate_check=miss
SRE reproduced in staging by inserting a header-normalizing proxy that lowercases and truncates header values >48 chars; observed duplicate execution when idempotency key length exceeded truncation limit.
Go SDK by default sends Idempotency-Key with length ~72 bytes when using UUID+context suffix; short keys (~32 bytes) dedup correctly across retries.
Customer proxy team confirmed corporate WAF normalizes headers for policy reasons and will not preserve raw header values for long tokens.
Confirmed Redwood dedupe uses exact match on the received idempotency header value at gateway level; no canonicalization tolerance currently exists.
Idempotency keys mutated in transit by a corporate reverse proxy (lowercasing/truncation/character replacement). Redwood's dedupe mechanism requires exact-match on header value, so mutated retries are treated as new requests leading to duplicate tool executions.
1) Short-term: Use a compact idempotency key under 48 characters (e.g., SHA256-truncated hex or base64url of request payload) so the proxy does not truncate or mutate it.
2) Use request-body idempotency: include a stable 'request_id' field in the JSON body and perform application-level de-dup on your webhook receiver until gateway fix is released.
3) Configure corporate proxy (preferred): whitelist/preserve 'Idempotency-Key' header without normalization for Redwood endpoints. Proxy team can map header passthrough by host pattern.
4) For function-calling with side-effects, enable a server-side confirmation pattern: include a confirmation token in the tool payload and have downstream acknowledge (idempotent design).
Temporary mitigations agreed: NimbusAI will switch to generated 32-char hex idempotency keys and apply a receiver-side dedupe for 72 hours. Internally created INT-4820 to implement header canonicalization strategy and logging to detect mutated idempotency headers at ingress (PR referenced). Engineering will add a warning to SDK docs recommending short idempotency tokens for environments that may normalize headers. Planned follow-up: implement tolerant dedupe that compares a normalized fingerprint (SHA256 of header value) as a fallback within 30 days.
1) INT-4820: Add normalized-fingerprint fallback in ingress dedupe (owner: ingress team) - ETA 2026-03-18.
2) Docs task: update SDK idempotency guidance for proxy environments (owner: devx) - ETA 2026-03-05.
3) Customer follow-up: NimbusAI to confirm proxy whitelist change or confirm short-key rollout in 72h.
4) Monitoring: add detection alert when same request path executes >1 tool call within 10s with different idempotency header values (owner: observability) - ETA 2026-03-10.

Additional notes:
2026-02-26 08:22 - NimbusAI (Customer): Confirmed they can switch to shorter keys for now; proxy team prioritized a whitelist check but requested a workaround asap.
payload.summary: Cross-proxy normalization of idempotency header causing duplicate tool/function executions

Issue summary:
FluxAnalytics reported intermittent failures for control-plane operations and model shard fetches from their private deployment in us-west-2. Failures present as short-lived control-plane timeouts, followed by TLS certificate name mismatch errors on artifact fetches and some presigned URL 403s.

Impact:
- Customers' production inference routes intermittently fail (5-10% of requests) for ~30-90s windows.
- Observed during peak traffic; customers see degraded tail latency and occasional 5xx from SDKs.

Environment:
- Customer: FluxAnalytics (private deployment, VPC peering to Redwood transit VPC).
- Region: us-west-2.
- Nodes: private control-plane behind VPCE; serving nodes in customer's VPC.
- Private DNS: on-prem forwarder -> customer egress -> upstream resolver chain (reseller DNS + regional CDN GeoDNS).

Steps to reproduce:
1) From serving node in customer's VPC, resolve control-plane hostname repeatedly (dig +short) and observe A/AAAA answers over time.
2) Simultaneously tail control-plane TLS handshake logs and SDK errors.
3) Run dig +edns @<customer-forwarder> <control-plane-hostname> +short and dig +trace to observe EDNS client-subnet behavior.

Observed logs / outputs (excerpts):
- SDK error: "tls: certificate is not valid for requested name: controlplane.us-west-2.private.redwood.net (got cert for controlplane-eu-west.redwood-cdn.example.com)"
- Serving node syslog: "fetch shard: presigned GET https://s3-us-west-2.redwood... -> 403 signature mismatch"
- dig @10.1.4.2 controlplane.private.redwood.net +short -> 13.32.11.97 / 2600:1f18:xxxx::1
- repeated dig after ~40s -> 52.17.4.23 / 2a03:xxxx::23 (eu-west range)

Initial hypothesis:
On-prem DNS forwarder is rewriting EDNS Client Subnet (ECS) or otherwise normalizing the client subnet to an IP that maps to a different region in upstream GeoDNS. This causes the control-plane hostname to resolve to an external/cdn-backed endpoint in the wrong region intermittently. The client then attempts TLS to that IP and fails because the certificate presented matches the CDN host name not the expected private hostname, and presigned artifact URLs (which are region-bound) fail or return 403s when routed to the wrong origin.

Immediate customer impact: control-plane auth loops and model fetches fail until DNS answers stabilize.

Requested action: full root-cause investigation and mitigation steps + temporary workaround to restore stability while customer remediate on-prem DNS behavior.
2026-03-10 15:12 - Support (Aisha): Received initial report from FluxAnalytics. Customer noticing short 30-90s windows of control-plane auth failures. Asked for dig +trace output and SDK logs.
2026-03-10 15:45 - Customer (Ops Lead, Maya R.): Attached dig +trace and tcpdump from a serving node. Noting the IP answers flip between us-west and eu-west ranges. Can we route around until we fix our forwarder?
2026-03-10 17:10 - Support (Aisha): Confirmed certificate commonName observed belongs to a CDN edge (eu-west). Escalated to SRE. Opened temporary bypass guidance (hosts entry) while investigating.
2026-03-10 19:04 - SRE (Tomás): Ran parallel dig against customer forwarder and directly to upstream resolver. Found EDNS0 ECS option being rewritten to a /24 that maps to EU. Packet captures show on-prem forwarder rewrites client-subnet. Created pcap snapshot and uploaded to ticket.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Customer: We scheduled network team to check the forwarder; they reported a managed reseller appliance doing ECS normalization for privacy. Asking whether Redwood can prefer IPv4 or validate certname earlier to avoid falling back to wrong endpoint.
2026-03-12 11:23 - SRE: Implemented and tested a conservative fallback in staging to prefer IPv4 addresses when TLS cert name mismatch is detected and to re-query control-plane via alternative resolvers before failing. Not yet in prod; testing ongoing.
2026-03-13 08:43 - Support (Aisha): Customer applied a temporary /etc/hosts override for control-plane on a subset of nodes and reported stability improved over the previous 24h window. Work with customer network team on permanent disable of ECS rewrite or configured split-dns at forwarder.
2026-03-13 14:57 - Customer (Maya): Network team plans to deploy forwarder config change to stop ECS normalization; ETA 2026-03-15. Please keep ticket open until we confirm no recurrence.
Checked DNS answers over a 2 hour window: answers oscillate between IP blocks belonging to us-west-2 and eu-west-1 (ASNs differ).
tcpdump on serving node shows DNS queries leaving to 10.1.4.2 (customer forwarder) with EDNS0 present. Upstream responses reflect client-subnet /24 originating from forwarder, not the actual node source IP.
TLS handshake logs show sni=controlplane.private.redwood.net but presented certificate CN contains controlplane-eu-west.redwood-cdn.example.com, causing verify error.
Presigned URL requests forwarded to wrong CDN edge produced 403 from S3 due to region mismatch and signature host mismatch (signature V4 region-bound).
Tested resolving via 8.8.8.8 and cloud-resolver; always returned US-west addresses. Resolving via customer forwarder intermittently returned EU addresses.
Temporary workaround (hosts override) stabilizes control-plane connections; indicates DNS answer is root cause rather than routing/GW flapping.
Temporary mitigation provided: 1) Hosts-file override on serving nodes for control-plane host to pin to us-west-2 control-plane IPs; 2) Customer network team to disable EDNS Client Subnet normalization on their forwarder (reseller appliance).
Longer-term mitigations: 1) We will add a control-plane resolver fallback to detect geo-drift by validating certificate commonName vs requested host and re-querying via known-good resolvers before promoting error to client. 2) Add telemetry to detect EDNS-originated geo-drift and alert automatically.
Customer confirmed front-line stability after hosts override; they will roll forwarder config change on 2026-03-15 and monitor for recurrence. Keep ticket open until 2026-03-18 for verification.
Assigned internal follow-up: INT-21402 to add EDNS drift detection and retry logic in control-plane client library (owners: control-plane team).
On-prem DNS forwarder normalizes/rewrites EDNS Client Subnet to a range located in a different region. Upstream GeoDNS uses ECS to return region-specific endpoints so some queries resolved to eu-west CDN edges, causing TLS certname mismatch and region-bound presigned URL failures.
SRE: deploy certname validation + re-resolve fallback to prod routing library (target 2026-03-20).
Support: keep ticket open and monitor customer telemetry until 2026-03-18.
Customer: apply forwarder config change to stop ECS normalization (in progress, ETA 2026-03-15).
ENG: INT-21402 to implement EDNS-drift metric and auto-retry logic (owner: control-plane team).
payload.summary: EDNS client-subnet rewrite by on-prem DNS forwarder causes control-plane region misroute and TLS cert name mismatch on private deployment

Issue summary:
Sustained degradation in tokens/sec and increased 5xx/timeouts for tenant 'AcmeAI' on their dedicated pool (pool-id: pool-usw-41). Starts ~2026-03-10 02:15 UTC and persisted despite autoscaler activity.

Impact:
- Production inference latency increased from 60-80ms p50 to 900-2,500ms p50/p95 for typical chat requests.
- Request timeouts (gateway 504) and queueing observed. Affected approximately 20% of traffic for the pool; customer reported user-visible failures in multiple services.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated pool pool-usw-41 (US-West-2)
- Region: us-west-2
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Models in use: redwood-v2-large (primary), llm-13b-quant (fallback)
- Components engaged: dedicated-pool, autoscaler, scheduler, serving-runtime, api-gateway

Steps to reproduce (from load test):
1) Run sustained ramp to 350 concurrent requests over 30 minutes against redwood-v2-large route.
2) Observe tokens/sec drop at ~120 concurrent requests and growing request queue.
3) Increase to 420 concurrent requests; autoscaler triggers but pod additions lag >90s and throughput stays low.
4) Re-run after forcing min_replicas=4 and scale-up cooldown reduced: throughput recovers.

Observed metrics and logs:
- GPU utilization per-node: 98-100% on 2 nodes, 20-40% on newly added nodes.
- GPU memory fragmentation spikes; OOM kill events at kernel level in serving-runtime logs.
- Autoscaler events: frequent scale up requests at 02:18 and 02:21 UTC but only 1 new replica added due to cooldown and allocation constraints.
- Queue depth alerts: queue_depth > 800 requests for 7 minutes.
- API gateway logs: 504 timeouts correlated with peak queue depth. Sample log line: "2026-03-10T02:19:12Z ERROR gateway request_id=... status=504 latency_ms=30000"

Hypothesis:
1) Autoscaler configuration has undersized min_replicas and long cooldown which causes delayed capacity addition (autoscale undershoot).
2) One node in the pool is saturated by a noisy tenant job (high-intensity batched throughput) causing GPU contention; scheduler did not rebalance quickly because of allocation constraints.
3) Serving runtime encountering memory fragmentation with the current quantization path for llm-13b-quant under certain sequence lengths leading to elevated kernel times.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Forced min_replicas from 2 -> 4 for pool-usw-41 at 2026-03-10T03:02 UTC; observed tokens/sec recovery within 60-90s.
- Drained the suspected noisy node and cordoned it for investigation (node-id: g4-usw-node-117).
- Temporarily disabled mixed-batch allocation for redwood-v2-large on the pool to reduce intra-node contention.

Next steps and action items:
- Engineering to patch autoscaler: reduce scale_up cooldown from 60s -> 20s and adjust target queue depth thresholds. (PR created)
- Add per-node tenant isolation signals to scheduler to avoid mixing heavy batch jobs with latency-sensitive routes.
- Run stress tests across sequence length distributions to reproduce memory fragmentation; optimize serving-runtime kernel selection for affected quant paths.
- Add alerting rule for sustained queue_depth > 200 for > 2m and GPUs with 90%+ utilization for >1m.

Attachments provided:
- Grafana snapshots: URL(s) included in linked_confluence page.
- Gateway logs sample and serving-runtime logs attached to ticket.

2026-03-10T02:45Z - Maya Lopez (Support): Customer reports increased 504s and slow p95. Asked for pool id and recent request ids.
2026-03-10T02:58Z - Ethan Park (SRE): Found queue_depth spike and autoscaler activity; initiating forced min_replicas bump.
2026-03-10T03:05Z - Maya Lopez (Support): Customer validated reduced error rate after forced scale; monitoring for recurrence.
2026-03-11T09:12Z - Priya Singh (Platform Eng): Investigating node g4-usw-node-117 for high batch job; kernel traces being collected.
Timeline:
- 02:15 UTC: Customer alerts from monitoring and Support.
- 02:20 UTC: Autoscaler logged multiple scale_attempt events but effective replicas increased slowly.
- 03:02 UTC: Manual change to min_replicas; throughput recovered.
Findings:
- Allocation logs show scheduler repeatedly trying to place new pods but failing due to packing heuristics and reserved GPU memory.
- Node g4-usw-node-117 had a large batch job consuming most GPU memory and sustained SM utilization leading to eviction pressure.
- Cooldown and target thresholds in autoscaler were tuned for cost efficiency; this incident shows they are too conservative for bursty workloads.

Temporary: increased min_replicas and reduced cooldown; drained and quarantined noisy node; disabled mixed batching for sensitive routes.
Permanent/Follow-up: autoscaler configuration PR merged to adjust cooldowns and thresholds; scheduler change to improve tenant isolation is in design. Added alerts and a confluence runbook for similar incidents.
payload.summary: Sustained throughput drop on dedicated GPU pool due to autoscaler undershoot and cross-tenant GPU contention

Issue summary: Customers receive scheduled dashboard exports (PDF and CSV attachments) from the Console scheduler, but the links embedded in exported reports (View in Console / Trace links) have tracehook tokens stripped when the job is run by a service-account via impersonation. Links land on a generic 404 or a listing page without trace context, breaking runbook workflows.

Impact: Multiple enterprise customers (reported by LexiHealth) are unable to use scheduled emails to navigate to alert-linked traces or annotate dashboards. This affects on-call workflows (missed context) and compliance evidence collections that rely on tracehook parameters.

Environment: Production, us-east, scheduler v2.4, console 1.19.1, auth-service 3.2.

1) Create a dashboard with a tracehook-enabled panel (uses route param 'route_id' and customer-level aliasing).
2) Configure scheduled export (PDF and CSV) to run hourly using a service-account with impersonation scope (org-scoped).
3) Wait for job to run or trigger manually via scheduler UI.
4) Open emailed PDF/CSV and click 'View in Console' or trace links inside exports.

Expected: Links should include tracehook tokens or redirected permanent tokens so recipients land directly on the annotated dashboard/trace with preserved context.
Actual: Links arrive without tracehook query parameters or with an expired token; Console returns a generic 404 or the top-level project page.

Scheduler job ids: job-20260310-22a7, job-20260311-03f1. Example exported link from PDF: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/lexihealth/dashboards/78?view=export (expected ?tracehook=eyJhb...)
Auth logs: impersonation token minted: sa-lexi-scheduler@lexihealth; audit entry shows 'impersonation: true' for both jobs.
Console logs (trace): 2026-03-11T03:00:12Z WARN export:sanitizer - dropped 1 query param (reason=impersonation-strip); stack=...

Initial hypothesis: a sanitizer step in the scheduled export pipeline removes high-cardinality query params when exports are executed with service-account impersonation to avoid leaking org tokens. Evidence: 'impersonation-strip' warning in console logs. However, same sanitizer should preserve tracehook tokens by substituting with short-lived export-safe tokens (existing behaviour for user-triggered exports).
Engineer notes: Reproduced locally by running scheduler job under 'sa' token; export pipeline branches at export-service/handler.go line ~412. A related recent change merged in github.com/redwood-inference/console PR #2418 tightened query-param allowlist for impersonated jobs.
Next steps: confirm whether exporter is expected to token-swap for impersonated runs; if so, revert/disallow the overbroad sanitizer and add explicit tracehook handling. Track a fix PR and add e2e test.

2026-03-10 - Customer (LexiHealth) - Sarah Nguyen: We rely on scheduled reports during night shifts; links inside yesterday's PDF were opening to a generic page, losing incident context. Attaching example PDF.
2026-03-10 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Thanks Sarah — we've triaged and escalated. Can you confirm whether scheduled jobs run under an org service-account or a user? Also confirm whether exports triggered manually from the UI work as expected.
2026-03-11 - Customer (Sarah Nguyen): Confirmed: they run under org service-account (sa-lexi-scheduler). Manual exports include trace links correctly. Happy to provide audit logs.
2026-03-11 - Eng (Marco Ruiz): Reproduced in staging. Found console log entry 'export:sanitizer - dropped query param' for impersonated runs. Suspect PR #2418 tightened allowlist. Creating a targeted fix and unit tests.
(added linked PR github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2471)
2026-03-12 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Provided temporary workaround to LexiHealth to run manual exports or change scheduled job to run under an org user until fix is deployed. Customer accepted workaround but requests priority SLA.
Short-term: change scheduled job to run under a normal user account (not service-account impersonation) or switch scheduled job to call a webhook that triggers a server-side export in the customer's environment. Both options preserve tracehook tokens. Support has documented steps and shared with customer.
