payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 429 responses for production realtime API traffic after migrating from per-route token windows to a composite (per-second + per-minute) window configuration. Impact: production latency and request failures for user-facing search autocompletion; intermittent errors affect ~12% of requests during peak spikes. Background: VectorSearch is on a dedicated pool with mixed workloads: low-latency autocomplete (short model calls) and bulk backfill embeddings. They recently applied a composite window policy intended to smooth bursts but observed more 429s for short-lived realtime sessions. They are asking for clarification on how the composite windows are applied and guidance on splitting burst pools for realtime vs batch to avoid cross-traffic exhaustion.
1) Deploy configuration: enable composite token window (1s / 60s) on the tenant and make per-route weight 0.7 for realtime route and 0.3 for bulk route.
2) Start 200 concurrent short-lived websocket sessions (autocomplete) from a multihost orchestrator with rapid connect/disconnect (50 RPS sustained, microbursts to 400 RPS for 20s every 5 minutes).
3) Run a parallel bulk embed job that sends 8 large requests per second during the same timeframe.
4) Observe 429 responses on realtime route during microbursts and throttling headers indicating token window exhaustion.
2026-03-09T17:02:14Z ingress-proxy[host-34] INFO 429 route=/v1/realtime reason=token_window_exhausted tenant=vecsearch window=(1s=120/120,60s=1500/2000)
2026-03-09T17:02:14Z rate-limiter DEBUG refill: tenant vecsearch composite: 1s_bucket full=false next_refill=0.54s
2026-03-09T17:02:15Z serving-runtime WARN request-id=cc3a short-circuit fallback to small-quant model due to concurrency limit
2026-03-09T17:05:00Z dedicated-pool INFO autoscaler scale_event desired_gpus=12 current_gpus=10 reason=cpu_hotspot
We applied the composite window to reduce microburst throttles but the opposite happened for our websocket-based autocomplete. The 429s started after switching configs and correlate with our periodic backfill windows.
We prefer to keep bulk embedding jobs running during business hours but need autocomplete to remain reliable for customers.
Can we allocate separate burst capacity or are we misunderstanding composite window accounting?
Initial triage: 429s correspond to 1s bucket exhaustion even though 60s bucket shows remaining tokens — composite window logic enforces both buckets; exhaustion of any bucket triggers throttling.
Observed that ingress-proxy connection reuse (HTTP/2 multiplexing) and short-lived websocket reconnects cause rapid token consumption in the 1s window due to per-request preflight accounting. Healthcheck probes from orchestrator also contributed ~5% of 1s window usage during spikes.
Autoscaler events showed pool scaling lag (~90s) relative to microbursts, so capacity scaling did not assist 1s bucket exhaustion.
Hypothesis: per-route weight was not isolating burst credits as expected because tenant-level composite windows are applied before route weighting; route weights shift steady-state refill but do not prevent short-window cross-traffic exhaustion.
Test performed: created temporary separate route-level burst pool with dedicated burst credits (shadow mode) and observed 429s reduced by ~85% for realtime path during a replay of customer load.
2026-03-10 09:14 - Zendesk import: Customer initial report received (support@vectorsearch.com) - '429s spiked after enabling composite window; need guidance and a short-term workaround.'

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 15:22 - Customer (VectorSearch): Approved temporary shadow test and provided access to burst policy config in console.
2026-03-12 16:40 - Customer: Confirms reduced 429 rate in production after the shadow change, requests guidance for permanent setup and runbook entry.
Short-term: enabled route-level burst isolation (shadow mode) and exempted orchestrator healthchecks from per-request preflight accounting for 30-minute trial; immediate reduction in realtime 429s observed. Long-term recommendations: (1) Create separate burst pools for latency-sensitive realtime routes by configuring dedicated route burst credits or using a separate dedicated-pool node group; (2) keep composite windows if you want smoothing but bind per-route burst credits so the 1s bucket for realtime is not drained by bulk jobs; (3) tune autoscaler cooldown to 30s for dedicated pools handling mixed microbursts and set a small always-on headroom for realtime capacity; (4) avoid counting frequent healthcheck probes against token buckets (we will ship a config flag).
Create runbook entry for 'separating burst capacity for realtime vs batch' - owner: Marcus Reed - due: 2026-03-19
Add console toggle to mark probes as 'non-accounted' so healthchecks don't consume buckets - owner: infra-console team - ticket: INT-40233
Implement permanent route-level burst credits in policy engine and document in customer KB - owner: product-rt - due: 2026-03-26
Confirm customer wants dedicated node group for realtime; schedule account review call - owner: Evelyn Shaw - due: 2026-03-15
payload.summary: Clarify composite rate-window behavior and configure separate burst pools for realtime vs batch pipelines

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (DataMill Analytics, dedicated tenant) reports intermittent high p95 latency for inference calls from EU-based traffic. Tenant is pinned to eu-west pool but we are seeing a subset of requests routed via ap-southeast-1 which increases p95 from ~180ms to ~850ms.

Impact:
- Production traffic for DataMill analytics pipelines experiencing periodic p95 spikes (~0.5%–2% of requests during rolling windows).
- Errors are not increased; primary impact is latency and customer SLA concern.

Environment:
- Tenant: datamill-prod (dedicated gpu pool)
- Region: eu-west primary pin configured via tenant routing policy (strict_pin: false by default)
- Time window: first observed 2026-03-09 18:20 UTC, reproducible intermittently through 2026-03-10

Steps to reproduce:
1. Send batched generation requests for model redwood-1-large pinned to tenant datamill-prod from EU IPs.
2. Observe latency distribution in Console -> Per-route latency (p50/p95/p99).
3. Correlate request IDs that show p95 > 500ms with router decision logs.

Observed logs / snippets:
- Example request IDs (observed high p95): rqd_20260309_7a1b, rqd_20260310_10c3
- Router decision trace (extracted): route.decide(tenant=datamill-prod, geo=eu) -> selected_edge=eu-west-3 primary, fallback_path=[ap-southeast-1] -> chosen=edge=ap-southeast-1 due to available_capacity_low=true at timestamp 2026-03-10T09:12:18Z
- Network traceroute excerpt from selected host: 10 hops, transit via sfo -> ap-southeast-1 (unexpected)

Initial hypothesis:
1) Autoscaler or capacity scoring occasionally marks eu-west pool as low-capacity causing smart-router to choose apac pool as low-cost fallback, even when tenant pinned.
2) Sticky pin TTL or route-staleness in our control-plane allows short-lived multipath routing for dedicated tenants when strict_pin is not set.
3) Mis-evaluation of latency/cost scoring metric in smart-routing that underweights geo-penalty in edge cases.

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed: tenant routing policy shows pin to eu-west but strict_pin=false; that means fallback to compatible variants is allowed by policy.
- Checked autoscaler metrics for eu-west pool around timestamps: GPU utilization spiked to 92% for 30s windows; however capacity autoscaler added nodes but with a 45s startup delay. During that window routing score favoured ap-southeast-1.
- Router trace logs show a weight calculation: score = latency_est + cost_adj - pin_bonus; pin_bonus incorrectly set to 5 for dedicated tenants in recent config rollout (should be 20).
- Found related deployment PR that adjusted pin bonus to be dynamic: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3412 (author: infra/team). The change was merged 2026-03-08 and rolled out 2026-03-09.

Customer-provided context:
- They enforce EU data processing but rely on our documented routing policy that pin=tenant should keep traffic in-region except for strict_pin override. They do not have strict_pin enabled because they depended on cost-aware fallback being region-aware.

Temporary mitigation applied (2026-03-10 14:45 UTC):
- Flipped per-tenant override: set strict_pin=true for datamill-prod via control plane to force hard residency until fix. Notified customer of short maintenance (no downtime).
- Added routing metric alert for when >0.1% of tenant requests are routed outside pinned region.

Next steps (planned):
- Roll back the recent pin_bonus change in routing config (PR drafted) to restore stronger pin weighting for dedicated tenants. Owner: infra-routing team.
- Add a unit/regression test to assert pin_bonus minimum for dedicated and private tenants.
- Improve autoscaler warm-up smoothing to avoid transient low_capacity signals.
- Follow up with customer on SLA credits and permanent config options (allowing them to opt into strict_pin or dedicated hard-residency).

Resolution (partial):
- Temporary: strict_pin=true for tenant (workaround) which reduced outside-region routing to <0.01% during observation window.
- Permanent: PR to revert/adjust routing pin bonus pending review.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 08:40 UTC - Customer (DataMill Ops - Carlos Mendez): Confirmed that after strict_pin change p95 decreased and notebooks resumed. Asked for permanent config option and rationale note for audit. Asked about billing/SLA credits for impacted window.
Key finding: routing scoring change merged 2026-03-09 reduced pin influence for dedicated tenants. Combined with autoscaler warm-up delay, some requests were routed to APAC fallback, increasing p95. Verified by matching router decision logs and autoscaler metrics and the merge PR. Temporary strict_pin set for tenant reduced out-of-region routing. Next: revert pin change and harden tests.
Workaround: strict_pin=true applied for datamill-prod which eliminated the observed p95 spikes. Permanent fix: infra-routing to revert/adjust routing pin_bonus and add regression tests; autoscaler warm-up smoothing work item created. Customer to receive postmortem and SLA credit evaluation.
Revert pin_bonus config change (infra-routing) - owner: Priya Nair
Add regression test for pin_bonus floor - owner: infra-systems
Autoscaler warm-up smoothing - owner: scheduler team
Customer postmortem + SLA credit evaluation - owner: CS manager

payload.description:
Issue summary: TextFlow reported a sustained increase in 5xx responses (~8-12% error rate) for their tenant between 11:30-13:20 PDT on 2026-03-12. Impact: customer-facing inference calls returned 502/504 intermittently; streaming sessions dropped with incomplete chunks. Environment: Dedicated tenant, reserved pool in us-west-2. Immediate business impact: degraded UX, elevated retry traffic from the customer side causing amplification.
1) Customer traffic pattern: steady concurrent streaming sessions (~350 concurrent connections) with a sudden background model sync job kicking at 11:28 PDT
2) Issue reproduced in production under similar concurrent streaming load when model-sync overlaps with tenant connection throttling event
3) Observed API gateway returning 502/504 while serving-runtime logs reported repeated session-manager timeouts and worker restarts
apigw: 2026-03-12T11:31:02Z - upstream returned 502 - upstream: runtime-allocator-43 (http2 GOAWAY observed)
runtime: 2026-03-12T11:31:03Z - session_manager: write stalled for 12s; GPU worker pid=4123 killed (OOM-like memory fragmentation)
kv-cache: 2026-03-12T11:31:04Z - prefetch lock contention on tenant TextFlow (waiting_queue=14)
11:45 - Support triage: validated customer metrics and confirmed 5xx rate correlated with their tenant's reserved pool; other tenants in same pool showed minor increases but not as severe.
12:00 - SRE snapshot: concurrent worker restarts aligned with start of background model sync for a model snapshot refresh initiated by ops (internal job id: model-sync-20260312-60).
Hypothesis 1: Model sync induced temporary I/O and memory pressure on the host which increased scheduling latency and caused session-manager write starvation, leading to connection resets and 502s at API gateway.
Hypothesis 2: Tenant-level priority demotion/connection throttling logic ran concurrently (autoscaler scaling-down warm workers) and amplified prefetch lock contention for KV cache, producing retry storms.
Evidence: flamegraphs and GPU memory maps show fragmentation spikes during the window; kernel-level swap events were observed on host nodes servicing the tenant pool.
Correlation: A maintenance model-sync job was scheduled in the same availability zone at 11:28; rollback of that job coincided with error rate improvement.
Related signals: increased TLS handshake timeouts and http2 stream resets from apigw metrics; elevated queue depths on the runtime's incoming socket accept queue.
Samira Patel (Support) 2026-03-12T11:40: We observed TextFlow reporting client-side retries and partial responses. Triage with SRE requested.
Diego Ramirez (SRE) 2026-03-12T11:55: Noted model-sync job running at same time. Scheduling I/O and memory pressure visible. Kicking off temporary mitigation: pause model-sync on implicated hosts.
TextFlow Ops (customer) 2026-03-12T12:02: We can delay our internal snapshot if that helps. Please advise on expected ETA to recover.
Diego Ramirez (SRE) 2026-03-12T12:18: Paused model-sync job (model-sync-20260312-60), increased keepalive to 90s for tenant pool, patched session-manager to back off prefetch lock. Error rate fell from 11% to 0.8% over 20 minutes.
Samira Patel (Support) 2026-03-12T12:45: Customer confirms recovery and reduced retries. Providing follow-up plan and postmortem timeline.
Diego Ramirez (SRE) 2026-03-12T13:05: Short-term mitigation applied; preparing PR for permanent fix. Marking incident resolved pending postmortem.
Mitigation executed: paused internal model-sync job on affected AZs, increased HTTP keepalive timeout for TextFlow tenant pool, and applied session-manager config change to reduce aggressive prefetch concurrency.
Permanent fix: engineering produced PR #4521 to add bounded prefetch semaphore and to avoid large synchronous model-sync I/O on worker hosts. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521
Rollout notes: PR to be staged in canary cluster; monitoring alert added for session-manager write stalls > 5s. Autoscaler policy updated to avoid scaling-down during model-sync windows for dedicated pools.
Customer follow-up: Offered post-incident review with TextFlow and scheduled a remediation window to validate the runtime patch on their reserved pool.
Postmortem action items: (1) Add model-sync blackout window for dedicated pools; (2) instrument GPU memory fragmentation metrics; (3) add automated detection for prefetch lock contention and circuit-breaker to avoid cascade retries.
Status: Resolved (temporary mitigations applied, PR opened for permanent fix).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports provisional buffer credits (hourly buffer) were not applied to their org after an automated fallback from a quantized dedicated variant to a hosted non-quantized variant during a large mixed-queue batch run.

Impact:
- LexiChat saw ~18 hours of reserved/provisional buffer disappear from the console and a provisional invoice shortfall for the billing window.
- Customer-facing pipelines reported elevated token counts in hosted aggregation and a higher-than-expected final invoice.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: lexichat-dedicated-prod (us-west).
- Fallback target: hosted-us-west-primary.
- Time window: 2026-03-09 22:10 - 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Submit mixed-queue batch job (embeddings + chat-inference) with pin to quantized variant on dedicated.
2) Dedicated pool hit a transient GPU OOM; auto-fallback routed requests to hosted non-quantized variant.
3) Job completes; console shows hosted-metering for that window but provisional buffer credit line not consumed/allocated to customer ledger.

Observed behavior:
- Hosted postbacks recorded usage at hosted rates.
- Hourly provisional buffer count in account decreased in UI but was not translated to a billing credit in provisional invoice export.
- Console estimate stayed lower, causing customer confusion; finalized invoice reflected hosted consumption without buffer offset.

Expected behavior:
- When fallback occurs for capacity reasons, provisional buffer credits reserved for the customer's dedicated usage should be consumed/allocated to offset hosted fallback costs for that window (per SLA/credits policy).

Attachments:
- Customer-provided job IDs and timestamps.
- Console screenshot showing buffer counter drop and missing invoice line.
- Example of postback payload header (obfuscated keys).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:02 - LexiChat (Customer): Provided job IDs and redacted postback lines. Notes that fallback events show in the console 'fallback: hosted' tag at 22:23 UTC.
2026-03-11 08:30 - SRE (Miguel Torres): Found transient OOM on dedicated pool at 22:21 UTC; fallback routing triggered 3k requests to hosted. Posting trace links to internal dashboard: #support thread.
2026-03-12 10:05 - LexiChat (Customer): Appreciated quick updates; requested provisional credit line to be applied before invoice finalization. Asked for ETA and manual waiver if fix misses cycle.
Initial hypothesis: credit reconciler keyed on model variant id and queue type. During fallback, hosted postbacks used hosted-rate model_id but retained legacy 'quantized_meta' tag from client payload, creating a tag-combination not covered by reconciler rules.
Logs: reconciler logs show pattern 'skip_credit: unknown_combination' for ~2,843 postback lines within window. Stacktrace points to function map_credit_for_postback in reconciler service.
Reproducer: created synthetic postback with mixture of 'tool_calls' and 'embeddings' that mirrors customer's payload; reconciler skipped allocation in staging.
Patch approach: expand reconciler mapping to treat 'fallback_hosted' as equivalent to original dedicated model_id when provisional buffer exists within same hourly bucket. Add unit test for mixed-queue payloads.
Rollout plan: land PR to canary 03/13, monitor canary reconciler logs for skip reductions, then roll to prod with a midnight window to avoid mid-cycle churn.
Temporary: Applied manual ledger credit to LexiChat for the missing provisional buffer amount for the affected hours (credit reference CLR-2026-391827). Permanent: Merged reconciler patch (PR #1834) to include fallback_hosted mapping logic for quantized->hosted transitions and mixed-queue payload handling. Canary monitored for 12 hours; postback skip rate dropped to 0. Deployed to prod 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. Follow-up: scheduled a postmortem and a small billing policy doc update clarifying fallback credit behavior.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in end-to-end rerank latency after they performed a namespaced embedding migration last week. The reranker returns correct results but 99th percentile latency for batch rerank calls spikes to 6–9s (baseline ~300ms) and occasional 503s observed from the rerank endpoint.

Impact:
- Intermittent but customer-facing UX timeouts for search results in production (LexiSearch CDN observes >20% degraded sessions).
- Increased request retries causing downstream quota consumption.
- Supports enterprise SLA (high priority customer).

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east-1, dedicated project for LexiSearch (enterprise, VPC).
- Embeddings stored in namespaced index: "lexi_v2_migrated" and legacy namespace "lexi_v1" (migration executed 2026-03-05 03:10 UTC).
- Rerank route: /v1/rerank/batch -> routed to reranker-mini-1 behind router service.

Steps to reproduce (from customer guidance):
1) Call embedding upload API with namespace header set to "lexi_v2_migrated" (bulk ingest).
2) Trigger rerank endpoint using saved candidate ids referencing both namespaces (some documents still point to lex_v1 ids).
3) Observe higher tail latency and periodic 503s.

Observed behavior:
- Per-request traces show fanout to 3+ embed-store shard replicas for a single rerank request. We expect 1-2 shards based on sharding key.
- Router logs show repeated resolv/lookup queries for same document ids across namespaces, increasing I/O and queuing on embedding-store workers.
- KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% to 58% for customer's requests after migration.

Expected behavior:
- Deterministic routing to single shard per id and stable KV cache hit rate. Rerank p99 should remain below 800ms.

Initial logs & traces:
- Trace sample (request id 9b7f-...): router -> embed-store: lookup(keys: [d-143, d-144, d-712]) -> embed-store returned duplicate shard mapping: shards [shard-12, shard-18, shard-12] causing duplicate fetch attempts.
- Router debug: discovered two different namespace-to-shard mappings for "d-712" (lexi_v2_migrated -> shard-18, lexi_v1 -> shard-12). Migration script annotated some ids with both namespaces due to client-side duplicate-key retries.
- Metrics: embed-store queue depth +300% on shard-18 for a 30-minute window near migration completion.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Migration produced duplicate namespace labels on a subset (~0.6%) of document ids. When rerank receives mixed namespace candidate lists it attempts per-namespace resolution causing cross-shard fanout.
- Hypothesis 2: Router shard-mapping cache invalidation was delayed; stale mapping caused lookups to be sent to multiple shard endpoints until caches expired.
- We validated that embedding-store indexes contain duplicate keys across namespaces by running a sampling scan (internal tool: emb-index-inspect).
- Confirmed two client-side ingest retries (from LexiSearch bulk uploader) created duplicate records with slightly different metadata and namespace headers.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Support enabled per-request namespace-coercion at the router for LexiSearch (forces lookup to prefer lexi_v2_migrated) — reduced fanout and dropped p99 from ~7s to ~1.2s for affected fleet. Applied 2026-03-11 02:40 UTC.
- Increased router shard-mapping cache TTL temporarily to avoid oscillation while we clean duplicates.

Next steps / recommended remediation:
1) Customer action: Run a dedupe job using customer-provided id map and the 'emb-index-clean' helper to remove duplicate keys in lexi_v1 that now also exist in lexi_v2_migrated. We provided a safe migration runbook link.
2) Infra action: Run targeted index compaction on shard-12 and shard-18 during low-traffic window (proposed 2026-03-13 01:00–03:00 UTC).
3) Router: Add hard check to prefer per-request namespace header and fall back only when explicit flag is set (postmortem change).
4) Engineering: Add validation to bulk-ingest client to detect duplicate-id retries and surface warnings.

Notes/links:
- Slack thread: #support-lexi (https://slack.redwood/support-lexis)
- Related PR: github.com/redwood/embeddings-service/pull/98 (namespace-coercion at router)
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/namespace-migration-checklist


Additional notes:
2026-03-10 14:35 UTC - SRE (Maya Chen): Confirmed shard queue buildup on shard-18; capturing queue metrics and taking conservative throttle snapshot.
2026-03-11 09:10 UTC - LexiSearch (Carlos Ruiz): Customer ran dedupe scan and provided list of ~1.2k duplicate ids; asked for safe compaction window.
Mitigation in place: router-level namespace coercion reduced p99 from ~7s to ~1.2s. Scheduled index compaction and customer dedupe job. Pending engineering change to bulk-ingest validation and router preference logic. Will update to Resolved when compaction completes and p99 stabilizes under 800ms for 48h.
payload.summary: Embedding namespace migration produced cross-shard fanout and high rerank tail latency

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers (notably AtlasSearch Inc.) reported elevated 502/503/504 rates beginning ~2026-03-14T11:18Z on embedding upload and small generation routes. Errors surface primarily at api-gateway; traces show upstream connection resets and runtime process exits shortly after.

Impact:
- Multiple tenants in prod-us-east observed a 5xx increase from baseline ~0.2% -> 7% for ~20 minutes.
- Embedded file uploads (multipart) and small embed generation routes returned 502/504; streaming routes saw intermittent resets.
- Customer-facing degradation for dedicated tenants (AtlasSearch, MeridianAI).

Environment:
- prod-us-east (dedicated capacity pool and shared ephemeral proxies)
- Affected path: /v1/embeddings/bulk, /v1/generate (short payloads), streaming endpoints

Steps to reproduce:
1) Upload a large multipart embedding file (~1.2GB, 16 parts) via the bulk-embed API from a dedicated tenant.
2) Observe background checksum validator job start (storage service log shows checkpointing).
3) Within 2-5 minutes, ephemeral-proxy CPU spikes to 90-100%, accept queue grows, and api-gateway begins returning 502/504.
4) Upstream serving-runtime processes report watch-dog timeouts and occasional SIGTERM restarts.

Logs / evidence:
- api-gateway logs (sample): "upstream reset before response: connection reset by peer" at 2026-03-14T11:22:11Z.
- ephemeral-proxy metrics: cpu_user jumped from 12% -> 96%, accept_queue length +420 between 11:20-11:25Z.
- storage service logs: "checksum-scan: background validation started for multipart manifest id=mnf-78f2" at 11:19:58Z.
- serving-runtime stderr: "Watchdog: no-progress timeout, killing worker pid=4127" followed by OOM-killer messages in dmesg.
- Tracing link: https://traces.redwood.com/trace/xyz-embed-246801

Current workaround provided to customer:
- Ask customers to split large embedding uploads into time-separated batches and to enable client-side retry jitter.
- Temporarily paused non-critical background checksum scans in prod-us-east (manual action by storage ops).
Timeline & hypotheses:
- 11:18Z: AtlasSearch bulk-embed upload arrives. Storage starts multipart commit and triggers checksum validation.
- 11:20Z: Storage I/O increases (nvme iowait >80%), ephemeral-proxy CPU climbs; proxies are performing synchronous write/metadata operations on behalf of uploads.
- 11:22Z: Accept queue backlog causes api-gateway backpressure; gateway hedged retries amplify load and trigger runtime preemption.
- 11:24Z: Some serving-runtime pods hit memory pressure and the kernel OOM reclaims worker processes, causing 502/504.

Hypothesis validated by correlating storage IO spikes, proxy CPU, and runtime OOMs. Not a pure kernel bug or model kernel fallback: kernel selection logs show normal operation. Root cause appears to be combined: heavy multipart upload + synchronous checksum scan holding proxy threads while the I/O path causes CPU+io saturation, amplifying accept-queue and hedged retries.

Partial findings & artifacts:
- Sysstat (iostat) from node n-edge-17 shows nvme_avg_quque > 300ms during the window.
- Ephemeral-proxy traces show long-tail syscall blocks on fsync during checksum stage.
- No config change or deployment at 11:15; reproducible with a synthetic large multipart upload in perf cluster (staging) when background checksum enabled.

Next investigation steps:
- Reproduce in dedicated staging with storage perf flags and collect flamegraphs for ephemeral-proxy.
- Confirm whether multipart checksum runs on sync path; if so, move to async background worker.
- Audit rate limits and hedged-retry policy that may amplify backpressure.

Stakeholders looped: support (#support), sres (#sre-frontend), storage eng (#storage).

2026-03-14 13:10 - AtlasSearch Support Rep (customer): Confirmed drop in errors after your mitigation (pausing scans). Reported successful re-uploads with smaller batches. Asking for ETA on permanent fix.
(work in progress) Immediate mitigations applied: paused background checksum scans in prod-us-east and asked tenants to stagger large embed uploads. Temporary limit applied to concurrent multipart commits.
Planned fix: storage change to move checksum validation off the synchronous commit path into an async validator (PR #102) + limit concurrent checksum workers and add IO-throttling on background validation.
Operational follow-ups:
- Add alert for storage iowait > 50% that triggers auto-throttle of background validators.
- Update runbook with steps to pause checksum workers and recommended tenant ingestion best practices.
- Postmortem to be produced after rollback windows and canary validation (linked to INT-442).
Items to cover in postmortem: why checksum validation was synchronous; why hedged retry/backpressure amplified failure; capacity planning for embedding ingestion; customer communication timeline and SLA impact calculation.

Issue summary:
Customer reports streaming (SSE) chat sessions that produce initial tokens but then enter a silent stall mid-generation when we are performing a canary model rollout. The stall lasts 30–90s and often recovers with the client receiving the remaining tokens in a burst, or the connection ultimately closes with no final chunk.

Impact:
- Affects multiple sessions for a single enterprise customer (NimbleHealth) using dedicated capacity in us-east-1.
- User-facing streaming hangs during live chat flows, causing timeouts and poor UX.
- Observed during planned canary rollouts and when routing shifts traffic from old model to canary variant.

Environment:
- Production, dedicated pool (dedicated-nyc-pool-7) serving NimbleHealth.
- Canary rollout configured: 5% traffic to canary before automatic ramp.
- Affected model families: redwood-v2-chat-8k (quantized) and fallback to llama3-13b-chat.

Trigger a canary rollout for a chat-capable model in prod (example: increase canary to 5-10% via console).
Send a long streaming chat request that includes a ~2k token context and expects a multi-paragraph response using SSE client.
Observe token stream: initial tokens are received, then streaming pauses for 30-90s (silent period).
After delay either a burst of buffered tokens arrives or stream terminates with a 499/502 from gateway or client timeout.
Reproduce reliably when the canary routing decision causes some requests to be routed to a worker that is still performing model warm-up or KV cache priming.

2026-03-10T14:03:13Z host=worker-23 runtime DEBUG kvcache miss priming started for session=abc123

03/10 14:20 - Support triage: customer-sup reproduced with NimbleHealth traffic pattern; correlated with canary ramp activity in deployment logs.
03/10 15:05 - Observed pattern: streaming stalls map to requests routed to new canary workers that had a KV cache miss and were performing quantized model kernel lazy-initialization.
03/10 16:30 - API gateway logs show silence (no chunk sent) during model warm-up window; gateway connection health-checks allowed connection to remain open but client-side timeouts occur in some SDKs.
03/11 09:12 - SRE reproduced locally by forcing worker to simulate 40s model initialization in serving-runtime; SSE client showed identical silent window.
Aisha Patel (Support) [2026-03-10T14:25Z]: Customer reported multiple incidents during today's rollout. Asked for priority escalation and logs. Attaching sample request id=abc123.
Diego Morales (SRE) [2026-03-10T15:10Z]: Reproduced locally by toggling canary routing. Hypothesis: lazy kernel init + KV cache priming on quantized workers delays first token flush. Investigating whether runtime buffers until model ready and then flushes as a burst.
Maya Li (Runtime Eng) [2026-03-10T17:02Z]: Found worker code path that suppresses SSE flush calls until token generation buffer hits a threshold when model is in 'initializing' state. Opening PR to force periodic flush during warm-up: linked PR #2147.

NimbleHealth (Customer) [2026-03-11T10:05Z]: Appreciated the quick mitigation; reported fewer stalls after reroute. Asked for permanent fix and postmortem.
A combination of canary routing to freshly provisioned quantized workers and a runtime optimization that deferred SSE chunk flushes during kernel lazy-initialization and KV cache priming. This created silent windows while the worker completed warm-up, leading to client-side timeouts or upstream connection resets.
1) Roll back canary (set canary to 0%) for affected customers until fix is deployed. 2) Enable pre-warming for quantized model variants in dedicated pools (provision warm workers before routing traffic). 3) Increase client-side SSE keepalive/timeouts temporarily.
Merged runtime fix to flush partial token buffers periodically during worker warm-up (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2147). Deployed to canary cluster 03/12; observed immediate reduction in SSE stalls during subsequent rollouts. Also added a rollout checklist item to pre-warm quantized workers and an automated health probe to detect long warm-up windows.
Action 1: Add an orchestration step to pre-warm at least 2 workers of any canary model variant before shifting traffic (owner: infra/serving, due: 2026-03-20)
Action 2: Add metric 'worker_warmup_duration' and alert if > 15s for any worker in production (owner: observability, due: 2026-03-18)
Action 3: Update rollout runbook to include SSE behavior note and rollback thresholds for streaming endpoints (owner: ops, due: 2026-03-17)
Action 4: Customer follow-up: provide NimbleHealth with postmortem and recommended client-side timeout defaults (owner: CSM, due: 2026-03-15)

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sharp increase in tail latency and intermittent 5xxs after enabling a combined optimization profile (q4 quantization + adaptive batching + KV prefetch) on their dedicated workloads. The tenant is NovaraHealth (enterprise) running pinned model variants in prod us-east.

Impact:
- Elevated 95th/99th latency impacting API SLAs for critical patient triage flows (spikes to 2.5s from baseline ~300ms).
- ~5% request error rate (502/524) reported over last 3h.
- Customer requests stepwise, low-risk rollback guidance that avoids broad capacity churn.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: novara-prod-pool (reserved GPUs)
- Model variants: rw-gpt-3b-q4_8 pinned, fallback: rw-gpt-3b-fp16
- Autoscaling policy: conservative (no aggressive scale-up)
- Observability: Console traces + per-route latency graphs available (link in comments).

Steps observed / how the change was applied:
1) On 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC, customer applied an optimizer profile bundle that set: quant_profile=q4_8, adaptive_batching=enabled (max_batch=64, dynamic_threshold=120ms), kv_prefetch=aggressive
2) Within ~30–45 minutes, error rate climbs and tail latency regresses.
3) Customer toggled kv_prefetch off for a single route (canary) with partial improvement, but errors persisted across other routes.

Repro/Notes:
- Repro is intermittent; load shape correlates with bursty user arrivals causing large batches to form that time out on slower token-generation paths.
- KV prefetch appears to increase memory pressure on some GPUs when combined with quantized kernels, leading to OOM-like behavior surfaced as 5xx.
- Adaptive batching settings make rollback tricky: instant disable may drop throughput and cause queueing across tenants.

Customer asks:
- A clear, minimal-risk sequence to unwind optimizations that minimizes service disruption and avoids a full fleet restart.
- Confirmation of which knob to toggle first (kv_prefetch vs adaptive_batching vs quant_profile).
- Any temporary mitigations (timeouts, per-route limits) we can apply now.

Additional notes:
Staging replay with identical load shape reproduced 502s when kv_prefetch=aggressive + q4_8 present. GPU memory high-water marks hit ~95% at failure windows.
Heap and kernel logs show transient allocation failures in q4 kernel path; FP16 kernels did not show same behavior under identical load.
Per-route tracing indicates most 5xxs originate in decoder token generation stage (long sequences).
Staged unwind sequence agreed with customer (low risk):
  1) Reduce kv_prefetch intensity per-route to prefetch_items=1 (canary already applied) and observe 30–60m.
  2) If errors remain, set adaptive_batching to conservative (max_batch=16, dynamic_threshold=400ms) for affected tenant routes.
  3) If tail latency still unacceptable and errors persist, roll quant_profile back to fp16 for the largest-model route only (keep q4 on low-traffic routes).
  4) If rollback of quant_profile is required, do per-shard gradual switch to avoid immediate capacity pressure (1 shard per 10 minutes).
Applied: Step 1 and 2 completed by Novara SRE with Support assistance. Observed 72% reduction in 5xxs and P95 improved to ~420ms on critical routes.
Follow-ups: schedule a post-mortem with engineering to review q4 kernel memory behavior and add a guard that prevents kv_prefetch=aggressive from being enabled concurrently with q4_8 for dedicated tenants without explicit QA.
ENG: Create a short-term guard in the optimizer controller to block aggressive KV prefetch when q4_8 is active for dedicated pools (linked PR).
DX: Update docs for recommended rollback order and a troubleshooting checklist for optimizer bundles.
SRE: Run a capacity-replay test with mixed quant profiles and kv_prefetch settings to validate fix.
CS: Share post-mortem and recommended config templates with NovaraHealth by 2026-03-18.
payload.summary: Guidance for staged rollback of mixed quantization + adaptive batching + KV prefetch in prod

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate side-effects (duplicate job creations and webhook posts) when a chat session uses a combination of the TypeScript SDK for client-side streaming and a backend Python service that invokes tools via function-calling. Impact: NovaMaps sees duplicate jobs billed and double webhook deliveries causing downstream processing failures and user confusion. Environment: Dedicated plan, prod us-west, heavy multiplexed traffic from mobile clients.

Observed behavior: During intermittent mobile network flaps customers reconnect the streaming TS SDK. On reconnect the conversation resumes, but NovaMaps sees repeated tool invocations (same external job created twice, second with 409 race but still triggers webhook). The duplicates are intermittent (10-15% of reconnects) and often correlate with short reconnect windows (500ms-5s).

Expected behavior: Retries/reconnects should not cause duplicate externally visible side-effects; SDK and platform should provide clear guidance to implement at-most-once or idempotent patterns for tool/function calls.
1) Start a streaming chat with TS SDK (client sends partial tokens).
2) Backend (Python) receives function_call events and synchronously creates an external job (POST to customer API) without idempotency key.
3) Simulate a short network interruption and reconnect the TS stream; allow SDK to resume and resend buffered tokens.
4) Observe backend receiving what appears to be a replay or duplicate function_call and creating the external job a second time.
5) Repeat across multiplexed client connections to increase probability of race. Expected: single job created per logical user prompt. Observed: duplicates in ~1/8 attempts.
Initial logs show two function_call events with identical arguments separated by ~300-1200ms. The serving-runtime trace indicates both requests were routed to different worker shards (continuous batching enabled) and the second arrived after a short reconnect window. There is evidence of client-side buffered token replay: the TS SDK reopened the stream and replayed unacknowledged tokens. Python handler is synchronous and returns 200 quickly after creating job; no idempotency key used.

Hypothesis A: Client-side resume combined with lack of idempotency at the application layer allows duplicate tool side-effects.
Hypothesis B: Multiplexed batching + shard routing can reorder or duplicate function_call envelopes when SDK reconnection overlaps with prior in-flight request merge.

We reproduced locally by forcing a websocket close at the client after sending the function_call start token then reconnecting; backend saw two function_call webhooks. Enabling request logs on the serving runtime shows two separate request IDs but identical payloads.

Relevant traces and logs: link to internal trace: https://trace.redwood.ai/trace/abcd-190001; backend logs (redacted) show two POSTs to customer endpoint 2026-03-09T18:12:03Z and 2026-03-09T18:12:04Z.
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged receipt; requested sample client/handler code and approximate timestamps. Asked for a short repro repro script.
Customer (NovaMaps - Rafael Ortiz) 2026-03-10: Provided minimal repro (TS client + Python webhook handler) and sample webhook URL. Noted duplicates correlate with cell-network reconnections.
SRE (Evan Liu) 2026-03-11: Confirmed duplicates in traces. No platform-level 'exactly-once' offered; recommended idempotency keys at handler. Asked Eng if SDK should expose sequence-nonce helper.
Eng (Anika Shah) 2026-03-12: Noted that continuous batching and shard routing can cause same logical message to be processed twice if clients replay unacknowledged buffers. Suggested pattern: include client-generated idempotency token + sequence number on function_call metadata and server-side dedup map with TTL.
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-13: Shared a mitigation guide and a small code sample for generating per-invocation idempotency tokens from client-provided conversation_id + function_call_nonce. Customer testing scheduled for 2026-03-14.
Workaround provided: 1) Add a per-function-call idempotency token (UUIDv4) passed in function_call.metadata or top-level input metadata from the client. Backend must use that token when creating external jobs and perform a get-or-create (upsert) using the token as unique key. 2) For streaming resumes, SDK will be configured (client-side) to assign a monotonically increasing sequence number per partial function_call and attach the last-acked seq in resume messages. 3) Short-term recommended server fix: dedup table with 30s TTL keyed by idempotency token + customer id.

Long-term items: INT task to add optional SDK helper to auto-generate and attach idempotency tokens on function_call events (INT-4021). Engineering to evaluate providing explicit 'function_call_ack' event from runtime so clients can safely garbage collect buffered tokens (related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1198).
- Customer to test provided workaround and report results by 2026-03-14.
- INT-4021: Engineer owner assigned to evaluate SDK helper (ETA 2 sprints).
- Track related follow-ups in linked issues and update this ticket when SDK change PR is available.
Open: customer testing in progress; workaround accepted pending results. Engineering follow-up tracked via INT-4021 and serving-runtime PR.
payload.summary: Non-deterministic tool execution order & duplicate side-effects when mixing SDKs and streaming reconnects

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate side-effects (duplicate bank transfer hooks) when Redwood invokes their external webhook for function/tool calls. The external webhook occasionally times out; Redwood retries the webhook invocation which results in duplicate downstream actions because the webhook endpoint is not deduplicating on invocation id. Impact: customer observed 2-3 duplicate webhook hits for ~0.5% of calls during a 3-hour window, causing billing and operational risk. They have paused the integration and requested recommended idempotency patterns. Environment: Production: customer-private deployment (enterprise) in us-east. Using TypeScript SDK v1.8 to open streaming chat sessions with function_call hooks enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Configure a function in model manifest to call an external webhook URL. 2) Simulate occasional 5-10s processing delay on the webhook to force timeouts from Redwood side. 3) Observe multiple HTTP POSTs to webhook with different timestamps but same payload body. Expected: either a single invocation or a stable invocation identifier provided so receiver can dedupe. Observed: 1-3 POSTs, varying slightly in JSON body metadata leading to receiver not treating them as identical. Logs/IDs: customer provided sample webhook request bodies (anonymized) showing fields: "tool_name", "input", "timestamp", "attempt" (1,2), but no single stable invocation UUID in the payload. Customer asks: what is Redwood's recommended idempotency contract for function/webhook callbacks? Is there a header or field we can rely on? Can they configure the platform to include a stable invocation id?
Create model manifest with a function that uses webhook tool (url points to test receiver)
Start a chat session via TS SDK that triggers the function_call path
Add artificial 6-8s processing delay in receiver to trigger platform timeout/retry behavior
Inspect receiver logs for multiple POSTs and compare payloads/headers
Customer-provided sample 1: POST /webhook 2026-03-09T14:02:10Z body contains {"tool_name":"pay_transfer", "amount":100, "user_id":"redacted", "attempt":1}
Customer-provided sample 2: POST /webhook 2026-03-09T14:02:18Z body contains {"tool_name":"pay_transfer", "amount":100, "user_id":"redacted", "attempt":2}
Gateway logs: connection to customer webhook timed out after 5s, platform retried according to backoff policy
Customer: We saw duplicate bank transfer webhook posts. Our receiver doesn't have a dedupe key and the payload changes slightly between attempts, so we're getting double charges. Want a reliable unique id for each function invocation so we can make our webhook idempotent.
Support (Maya): Thanks for the report — assigning Diego from runtime to investigate. Can you paste a redacted example of the full request headers and body for both attempts? Also confirm whether you control the receiver code (yes/no).
Customer: Pasted headers. We control receiver (yes) and can persist request ids if provided. We do not want to rely on timestamps/attempt numbers.
Support (Diego): Initial hypothesis: platform retries webhook invocations on timeout/5xx and includes an "attempt" field but not a stable invocation UUID. We'll verify whether the runtime sends a consistent invocation_id header or field. If not, recommend receiver-side dedupe using stable id once we provide guidance or a workaround.
SRE (internal): We saw retries from gateway for pipeline X during the window. Retry logic uses exponential backoff and replays the original payload but currently does not inject a stable invocation_id header in older runtime builds.
Reproduced in staging with TS SDK v1.8 and runtime version 2026-02-28. Staging webhook receiver recorded two POSTs when simulating a 6s delay: both bodies identical except for 'attempt' field and timestamps. No 'invocation_id' present in headers or body.
Checked recent runtime change logs: a PR to add stable tool invocation ids landed behind a feature flag in 2026-03-04 but was not enabled for enterprise private deployments by default.
Confirmed that newer hosted deployments include header 'X-Redwood-Tool-Invocation-Id' and include 'tool_invocation_id' in payload; private deployments may need configuration or upgrade.
Risk assessment: Until stable invocation ids are present, receivers must dedupe on payload semantics or implement idempotency using business keys to avoid side-effects on retries.
Related items: linked internal ticket INT-1987 (runtime: enable toolkit invocation id feature flag for private deployments)
Related github PRs: PR-3456 (add invocation id header to webhook calls)
Workarounds provided to customer on 2026-03-11:
1) Make receiver idempotent using business-level keys (e.g., customer transaction id included in function input) and persist processed ids to ignore duplicates.
2) If feasible, add a short-lived dedupe store keyed by a hash of request payload and business key for the window of potential retries (e.g., 30s).
3) Temporarily increase webhook timeout threshold on receiver to avoid platform-side retries while we enable the feature, or return 200 quickly and process asynchronously (ack pattern).
Platform action items:
- Diego to coordinate enabling the stable invocation id feature flag for the customer's private deployment (INT-1987) and schedule an upgrade window (ETA 2026-03-18).
- SRE to confirm that once enabled, Redwood will include a header 'X-Redwood-Tool-Invocation-Id' and a top-level field 'tool_invocation_id' in webhook payloads for all subsequent invocations to support receiver-side dedupe.
Follow-up: After feature is enabled, customer should verify dedupe behavior and then re-open ticket if duplicates persist.
payload.summary: Webhook function-calls retried by platform on timeout leading to duplicate side-effects; guidance requested for idempotency

Issue summary:
A Boxleaf tenant experienced a sharp spike in 502/5xx responses across multiple routes beginning ~2026-03-13T18:05:00Z. API Gateway returned 502s and 504s, and upstream serving-runtime pods entered restart loops. Error window lasted ~45 minutes with highest error rate at ~18:20 UTC. Customer reported production impact: failed interactive requests and degraded throughput.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency/failures for Boxleaf production workload (dedicated capacity).
- Traffic loss estimated ~30% of requests for impacted tenant during the window.
- Boxleaf reported user-visible errors for their chat endpoints.

Environment:
- Deployment: dedicated cluster for Boxleaf (tenant id: boxleaf-prod).
- Region: us-east-1.
- Models: redwood/llama-13b-v2 pinned to v2026-02-28.
- Ingress: api-gateway cluster behind edge-proxy pool.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) High rate of concurrent short-lived connections from tenant between 18:04-18:22 UTC.
2) API Gateway hit connection queue and began returning 502 to new requests when upstream TLS handshakes timed out.
3) Serving-runtime processes showed repeated segfault-like exits followed by immediate restarts; OOMs not present.
4) Autoscaler attempted to spin up replacement pods, which joined but hit the same failure pattern.

Logs/metrics (selected):
- api-gateway/edge-proxy: connection_queue_length spiked to 12k; TLS handshake error rate increased (ERR_TLS_HANDSHAKE=3.2k/min).
- serving-runtime: process exit codes 139 (segfault) recorded on 6 distinct pods between 18:08-18:18 UTC.
- node exporter: no host OOMs or CPU saturation above 70%.
- kernel oops/oom logs: none.
- trace: request IDs see https://observability.redwood.ai/traces/INC-20260313-07 (internal link).

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Connection flood from a customer-side traffic pattern (short connections) overwhelmed the API gateway connection backlog leading to TLS handshake failures and wave of upstream disconnects. Evidence: edge-proxy socket backlog metrics correlate with 502 spike.
- Hypothesis B: A latent memory corruption bug in serving-runtime exposed under a particular request pattern, causing process crashes (exit 139). Evidence: core dumps present but limited; crash addresses point into the custom kernel-attention module linked in serving-runtime.
- Hypothesis C: Race in warmup/kvcache initialization during rapid new-connection storms causing invalid memory reads. Evidence: startup logs show repeated kvcache init warnings immediately prior to exits.

Actions taken so far:
- Support (Ava) opened incident, paged on-call runtime (Devon).
- Scaled down Boxleaf traffic to 20% via rate-limit hold at the edge to reduce error amplification at 18:25 UTC (mitigation reduced error rate by ~70%).
- Collected core dumps and uploaded to internal artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/incidents/INC-20260313-07/cores/.
- Disabled the most-recent runtime kernel optimization flag (kernel-opt=attn_v2) for new pods as an isolation step; new pods stayed healthy in short tests.
- Warmed an alternate dedicated pool with kernel-opt=attn_v1 and tested with synthetic short-connection burst; no crash observed in 30m test.

Open questions / next steps:
- Confirm root cause: memory corruption in attn_v2 kernel vs. edge connection backlog amplification.
- Run extended fuzzing of attention kernel in staging with short-connection workload.
- Roll forward a temporary fix: keep Boxleaf pinned to kernel-opt=attn_v1 while we complete PR and CI validation for mount/attn fixes.
- Post-incident: full postmortem + recommendation to add connection queue-based auto-throttle at gateway per-tenant.

Suggested owner and ETA:
- Runtime engineering (Devon) owner for root cause validation (ETA 72h).
- Support/CS (Ava) owner for customer communication and temporary routing policy (ETA 24h).

Customer communication:
- Notified customer at 2026-03-13T18:40Z with mitigation steps and ETA for full rollback to stable kernel. Boxleaf requested follow-up and impact quantification.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 19:05 UTC - Customer (Boxleaf SE): Thanks. Seeing substantially fewer errors. Please keep us posted on RCA and any data exports we should review.

Issue summary: Between 2026-03-09 18:10-19:05 UTC we observed a sustained degradation in throughput and a sharp rise in p95/p99 for GlideAI's dedicated reservation in us-west. Symptoms started after an evening traffic spike. Impact: production endpoints returned 504/stream timeouts and request throughput fell ~45% compared to baseline, causing customer LLM features to fail for end users. Environment: Dedicated GPU reservation (resv-glas-13b), single pool in prod-us-west serving mixed model variants. Observed at ~18:10 UTC when a tenant in the same pool exhibited a high burst of long-sequence requests.
1) Simulate 60-90s burst from a single tenant with interleaved long context (seq_len ~2048) and high token generation rate; 2) Run concurrent steady traffic from GlideAI baseline workload (shorter sequences, high qps); 3) Monitor serving runtime queue length, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and scheduler pending queue; 4) Observe tail latency elevation and 5xx/timeouts on baseline requests.

Multiple customers reported a sudden spike in 5xx responses beginning ~2026-03-10 02:12 UTC. High-rate streaming clients (websocket based) experienced disconnects and immediate 5xx responses. Metrics show sustained error-rate increase on several ingress nodes and correlated serving-runtime OOMs and restart cycles. Initial symptom: high CPU and memory on downstream batch route workers followed by process exits and upstream 502/503s. Customer payloads were streaming chat sessions but were being routed to a route configured for large, synchronous batch embedding jobs (batch handler), causing long-lived websocket sessions to occupy batch worker slots and trigger KV/prefetch lock contention and eventual OOMs.
1) Establish a websocket streaming session that sends small chat deltas every 50-200ms. 2) Observe topology: some sessions were incorrectly routed to /v1/batch/embed handler instead of /v1/stream/chat. 3) Under concurrent load (~500 concurrent streaming sessions) the misrouted batch workers accumulate many half-open streams, holding memory and prefetch resources. 4) After ~2-5 minutes, serving-runtime reports OOM and restarts; API gateway surfaces 502/503 to callers.
- apigw logs (us-east-1) show route rewrite: original_path=/v1/stream/chat, rewritten_path=/v1/batch/embed, reason=route-set-by-priority (2026-03-10T02:11:58Z)
- runtime stderr: 'Allocation failed: device out of memory' (2026-03-10T02:14:05Z)
- runtime supervisor: restart_count=3 within 2m (2026-03-10T02:16:20Z)
- metrics: error_rate(api_gateway)=12% (baseline 0.2%), pod_restarts(serving-runtime)=7 in 10m
- tcp traces: many KEEPALIVE half-open sockets to batch-handler backends, long time_waits
- Noticed a rewrite rule introduced in latest ingress ruleset (PR #gh-5721) that tightened route priority ordering. The rule deprioritized the streaming prefix in some edge nodes, allowing a catch-all batch route to match first.
- Correlated runtime OOM stack traces show cumulative KV cache growth with many small streams holding pointers; batch handler expects bulk upload patterns and delays releasing memory for streaming frames.
- Reproduction done in staging by replaying websocket traffic to batch endpoint -> reproduces leak within 3 minutes.
- Hypothesis: route priority change + difference in connection handling semantics between batch and streaming handlers produced sustained resource retention, amplifying under burst and leading to process OOMs.
- Customer impact: TextFlow reported ~40% of active streams dropped; affects dedicated cluster customers using streaming chat concurrently with batch embedding jobs.

Applied short-term patch to apigw to detect streaming websocket handshake on batch routes and reject with 4xx instead of forwarding. No code changes to serving-runtime required for mitigation; long-term fixes planned.

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightChat reports that a subset of streaming sessions (long-poll / SSE clients) began receiving responses from the fallback model during a rolling promote of redwood-7b-v1.2. Sessions were previously pinned to v1.2 but lost affinity mid-stream after an automated health-probe eviction on the canary pool.

Impact: ~120 active streaming sessions for BrightChat saw degraded model quality for ~11 minutes (users observed hallucinations and mismatched formatting). No tokens were billed incorrectly, but customer-facing feature quality was impacted.

Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod-us-east, canary rollout to a subset of GPU pool nodes. Health probe configuration: edge L7 probe with 5s interval, 2 failures to mark unhealthy. Rolling promote increased canary weight from 10% to 40% during the window.

Observed behavior: When a canary node returned transient 502 for probe traffic during the promote, the routing layer prematurely evicted pinned session state for active streaming sessions that had intermittent reconnects; upon reconnect the routing chose fallback model (openchat-13b-quant) due to fast-path fallback policy.

Expected behavior: Streaming sessions should preserve pin affinity until an explicit unpin or a sustained failure threshold (longer than short-lived probe blips). Short probe-induced evictions should not break active long-poll streaming pins.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the interaction between short health-probe failures, session reconnection behavior for long-poll clients, and the pin expiry/eviction logic in the router during weighted canary promotes.
1) Configure a dedicated route for tenant 'brightchat' pinned to redwood-7b-v1.2 with streaming enabled (SSE/long-poll).
2) Start 200 concurrent streaming sessions that maintain open connections with periodic partial messages.
3) Start a gradual promote from 10% -> 40% canary weight and simultaneously induce a transient 502 on one canary node by returning bad frames on probe path for ~10s.
4) Observe reconnects and routing decisions for sessions that briefly re-handshake during the probe window.
5) Expected: pins remain intact; Observed: ~10% of sessions rebind to fallback model and lose pin affinity.
[2026-03-13T18:12:07Z] edge-proxy: probe /health -> 502 (canary-node-7)
[2026-03-13T18:12:09Z] router: session_reconnect tenant=brightchat session_id=sn-7e4c pin=redwood-7b-v1.2 -> lookup returned no pin (ttl_evicted)
[2026-03-13T18:12:09Z] router: fallback_route tenant=brightchat session_id=sn-7e4c chosen_model=openchat-13b-quant reason=fallback_policy:probe_eviction
[2026-03-13T18:12:18Z] serving-runtime: model-load openchat-13b-quant on node=pool-2
[2026-03-13T18:23:00Z] edge-proxy: probe /health -> 200 (canary-node-7)

Initial hypothesis: pin eviction is tied to node-level health events and a short TTL on session-affinity metadata. Router code currently treats a node marked 'unhealthy' as a signal to evict any pins associated with that node immediately. For streaming clients, a transient reconnect during this window triggers re-evaluation and a fallback decision.

What we've checked:
- Verified routing logs show immediate TTL eviction behavior when node state flips unhealthy.
- Confirmed with BrightChat that affected clients were using long-poll with intermittent keepalive that triggered re-handshake within 5-12s windows.
- Replayed traffic in staging with injected probe failures reproduces the rebind to fallback model.

Potential root causes:
- Aggressive pin eviction on node failure events (policy is tuned for standard request/response but too aggressive for long-lived streams).
- Canary promote weight shift increases chance of clients reconnecting to different backend pools during promotion.
- Edge probe flaps caused by a minor bug in canary image returning 502 under high probe concurrency (tracked in PR 1829).

Additional notes:
BrightChat (Customer): Provided session IDs and user impact examples. Asking for mitigation and postmortem.
Mitigation applied: Temporary policy change deployed to prod-us-east at 2026-03-14T02:10Z that prevents immediate pin eviction for sessions marked as 'streaming' — instead escalate to a 60s grace window before unpin. This lowered rebind rate to <1% in the affected tenant.
Workaround for customer: BrightChat enabled 'session_pin_strict=true' on affected route to persist pins across short reconnects.
Planned permanent fix: Update router pin-eviction logic to be session-type aware (streams vs RPS) and to consult session reconnection semantics. Also include safety: do not treat single probe failure as immediate eviction for active streams. Target patch in serving-runtime PR#1837 and router PR#1838; rollout gated behind integration tests (staging) and a canary with explicit streaming workload.
Follow-ups:
- Postmortem to be authored and linked here after closure.
- Add test harness for long-poll + canary promote scenarios to catch regressions.
- Confirm billing/usage checks with finance (no token misbilling observed).
INT-9912: Router change to session-type aware eviction (assigned to Marco Liu)
PR-1837: Add integration test for streaming reconnection during canary promote (assigned to Evelyn Park)
OPS-RUNBOOK-UPDATE: Document streaming pin grace behavior in runbook
payload.summary: Long-poll streaming connections lose model pin after health-probe eviction during rolling promote

Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden rise in interactive-chat p95 latency (~300–450ms delta) for users routed to eu-west and eu-central after they turned on the "region-affinity" preference for their account. Impact: Production users of MuseAI (dedicated tenant) observe degraded interactive responsiveness for chat features; request rate unchanged. Environment: prod - eu-west, dedicated pool. Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer toggled 'region-affinity' in the Console for their tenant at 2026-03-08T14:12Z. 2) Observe interactive chat p95 on their service dashboard and external synthetic clients. 3) Toggle back to 'any-region' and re-measure. Observed behavior: With affinity enabled, p95 increased by ~320ms for eu-west requests and ~280ms for eu-central for ~45 minutes after the change. Toggling back to any-region returned p95 to baseline within 10 minutes. Logs & traces: Edge logs show intermittent additional NAT hops and occasional TLS handshake timeouts to backends in eu-west-2. Control-plane audit shows residency preference change propagated to two control-plane nodes at different times (2026-03-08T14:12Z and 2026-03-08T14:18Z). Customer timeline and screenshots attached to the ticket via email (not included in JSON).
Support (Liam): Received initial report and collected synthetic trace links and timestamps from customer. Escalated to SRE and assigned to Priya.
SRE (Priya): Started by checking control-plane propagation logs and edge-proxy routing tables; noted discrepancy in stamp propagation to eu-west edge cluster A vs B.
Customer (Nina, MuseAI): Confirms toggling affinity off returns performance to normal; can reproduce with our synthetic clients in eu-west.
SRE (Priya): Requested tenant ID and sample request IDs; asked customer not to toggle setting until we capture traces. Customer provided tenant:muse-428 and sample request ids.
Support (Liam): Logged internal INT-4412 to investigate edge stamp propagation race-condition. Linked PR to infra change that rolled out two days prior.
SRE (Priya): Noted known infra rollback candidate: PR #3283 touched control-plane caching TTLs; correlates with the timeframe. Will run packet captures and a short canary traffic test in eu-west-2.
SRE (Priya): Found that some edge nodes attempted fallback to secondary egress (us-west) for a subset of sessions during propagation window, adding cross-region RTT. Collecting full pcap and spans.
Support (Liam): Informed customer of active investigation and recommended a temporary rollback to any-region if immediate mitigation needed. Customer requested we attempt to fix before forcing config change on their side.
Hypothesis 1: Control-plane residency stamp update propagated non-atomically to edge clusters, causing mixed-ejection to secondary egress for sessions established during window.
Hypothesis 2: Edge proxy cache TTL reduced by infra change (PR #3283) resulting in stale residency states and more frequent TLS re-handshakes to fallbacks.
Finding: Correlated timestamps show control-plane wrote new residency stamp at 2026-03-08T14:12Z but global edge invalidation completed at 2026-03-08T14:17:45Z; during that 5m45s window, ~12% of requests were routed via a secondary egress in us-west, adding ~280–400ms RTT.
Trace excerpt: span IDs [span:0a3f, span:0a4b] show extra hop eu-west-edge -> nat-gw-us-west -> eu-west-backend; TLS handshake retries observed in 1.4% of affected requests.
Load/Capacity: Dedicated GPU pool healthy; no autoscale events or GPU contention observed during window.
Related change: PR https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3283 reduced control-plane cache flush parallelism, intended to reduce DB write pressure, but inadvertently increased propagation variance under low load.
SRE action: Collected packet captures and request-level traces; created filtered logs and uploaded to secure S3 for eng review (link provided to engineers only).
Workaround: Temporarily switching the tenant to 'any-region' restored baseline latency within ~10 minutes and is a validated mitigation. Permanent fix: Rollback or patch PR #3283 to reintroduce parallel invalidation for residency stamps and add a short 'grace' routing window while propagation completes to avoid cross-region fallback. Assigned to INT-4412 for engineering fix and to infra for a follow-up postmortem. Customer agreed to keep affinity off until patch is deployed. Follow-ups: add instrumentation to detect mixing of egress paths for a single residency-change event and SLA-facing notification if propagation exceeds 30s.

Issue summary: Customer LensAI reports a progressive degradation in tail latency (p95/p99) and throughput in their dedicated GPU pool during a nightly embedding sweep that issues many short-lived embedding requests. Impact: Customer's batch job (embedding sweep for 6M items) now runs 3x longer and stalls downstream pipelines. Environment: Dedicated pool (LensAI-reserved-3) in prod-us-west-2, routing to embedding-small-v2; issue first observed on 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run ~2000 concurrent short embedding requests (payloads ~512 bytes) with keep-alive disabled/closed quickly; 2) Observe allocator slot counts, connection table, and short-stream fanout; 3) Notice increasing queue depth and autoscaler failing to attach additional GPUs. Observed behavior: - p50 stable, p95/p99 and tail CPU/GPU attach times increase gradually over 1–2 hours. - Node/socket table shows many TIME_WAIT/FIN_WAIT entries. - Autoscaler metrics show attach attempts succeeding but effective usable slots falling due to connections occupying scheduler slots. Initial hypothesis: Customer client opens very high concurrency of short-lived connections without proper connection pooling/keep-alive, leading to ephemeral socket churn that ties up scheduler/sidecar resources (prefetch and per-connection state), causing allocator fragmentation and autoscaler misinterpretation (appears as slot capacity but unavailable). Attachments/Logs: - Support logs: /var/log/support/SUP-246801/support_debug_2026-03-10.tar.gz - Grafana dashboard snapshots: tail_latency_spike_2026-03-10.png - Packet capture excerpt available on request. Requested customer action: Provide client HTTP connection settings and a short reproducible script.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 14:21 - LensAI engineer (customer): Confirmed client used no connection pooling; their current SDK creates a new TCP connection per request. They attached a representative load generator (script). Asked whether Redwood can throttle per-tenant connection creation.
2026-03-12 11:02 - LensAI engineer: Reported partial improvement — job time reduced by ~45%, but p99 still elevated compared to baseline. Asked if Redwood will implement a durable fix.
Sidecar analysis: sidecar process holds per-connection prefetch metadata in memory for up to 30s after close; with high churn this accumulates and blocks slot reclamation.
Kernel socket state: large number of sockets in TIME_WAIT and FIN_WAIT2 observed on nodes; OS tcp_tw_reuse and ephemeral port exhaustion risk considered but not reached.
Autoscaler behavior: attach attempt rate healthy, but scheduler marks slots as in-use because per-connection prefetch leases exist; this prevents immediate reuse leading to effective capacity drop.
Customer pattern: high qps of very short requests (~10–50ms server time) with no pooling; SDK defaults identified as root trigger.
Load reproduction: synthetic generator reproduced p99 drift in lab at ~1800 concurrent short streams. Enabling HTTP/2 multiplexing eliminated drift in test.
Risk assessment: If left unmitigated, can cause other tenants in same reserved pool to observe intermittent p99 regressions during large short-stream campaigns.
Workarounds tried: per-pool soft-rate-limiter (reduced immediate impact), temporary increase of prefetch reclamation aggressiveness (reclaimed slots but raised minor p50 jitter).
Temporary mitigations applied 2026-03-11: per-pool connection soft cap and autoscaler sensitivity window increased. Customer validated ~45% job time improvement.
Planned actions: 1) Sidecar patch to aggressively free per-connection prefetch state and detect short-connection floods (PR linked). 2) Scheduler tweak to treat recently-closed prefetch leases as reclaimable under short-stream flood condition. 3) Add tenant-level guidance in docs and provide SDK patch sample to LensAI to enable persistent connections/HTTP/2.
Customer communication: Provided concrete SDK config recommendations and sample patch to switch to HTTP/2 multiplexing. Follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-13 to validate final throughput.
Owner: Miguel Santos (SRE) to own sidecar/scheduler changes; ETA for durable patch: 2026-03-19 (pending review).
Mitigated with soft-rate-limiter and guidance; durable sidecar/scheduler patches in progress. Customer to validate nightly run; postmortem and KB to follow once patch is deployed.

Issue summary:
StreamlineAI reports a persistent elevation in 'time-to-first-byte' (first token emitted) for chat completion requests after our runtime hotpatch (2026-03-11) and a load-balancer affinity change that rolled out the same morning. Impact is concentrated on their dedicated cluster in us-west-1 using rw-3.1-large (and the quantized variant).

Impact:
- P95 first-byte latency increased from ~120ms to ~540ms for short chat prompts (<=64 tokens).
- Customers observed occasional 30s client-side timeouts when initial token emission exceeded client thresholds.
- Affects ~12% of requests for the customer during peak (09:00-11:00 PST).

Environment:
- Customer: StreamlineAI (dedicated reservation)
- Region: prod-us-west (us-west-1)
- Models: rw-3.1-large (primary), rw-3.1-quantized (fallback)
- Runtime: rtx-runtime-2.1.7 -> hotpatched to rtx-runtime-2.1.8 on 2026-03-11 03:22 UTC
- LB config: affinity change (session stickiness tweak) rolled out 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use StreamlineAI account with dedicated pool and send 1k short chat requests (prompt length 10-40 tokens) at concurrency 20 from us-west region.
2) Observe latency distribution and connection logs.
3) Compare first-byte timings against baseline from 2026-03-10.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent but repeatable stalls between connection handshake and first token emission.
- Traces show increased time inside serving-runtime on 'KV cache miss + kernel selection' path for affected requests.
- Affected requests frequently land on a subset of hosts that show CPU spin waiting on a kernel JIT/compat check.

Expected behavior:
- First token emitted within 100-200ms for short prompts under dedicated SLA.

Logs & metrics links:
- Grafana (customer p95 first-byte): https://grafana.internal.redwood/a/graphs/streamlineai/first-byte?from=2026-03-10&to=2026-03-13
- Traces: https://jaeger.internal.redwood/trace/7a8f3c2a
- LB rollout audit: https://infra.redwood/audit/logs/2026-03-11/lb-affinity

Timeline and quick findings:
- 2026-03-11 03:22 UTC: rtx-runtime-2.1.8 hotpatch deployed cluster-wide (cherry-picked quant path fix).
- 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC: Load-balancer stickiness tweak rolled (goal: reduce cross-AZ tail latency).
- 03/11 04:15 UTC: StreamlineAI support ticket opened reporting spikes.

Hypotheses tested so far:
1) Kernel selection/quant path regression in 2.1.8: reproduced increased per-request setup time in staging with 2.1.8 when model variant uses quantized kernels.
2) LB affinity change concentrating traffic on a smaller hot pool exposing cold-Warmed worker state: correlation observed — affected hosts had higher number of cold model instantiations per minute.
3) KV cache priming race with new runtime path: traces show ~70ms extra spent waiting for KV cache population on misses when requests hit a recently-started process.

Findings:
- Canary tests show that mixing affinity change + runtime 2.1.8 increases probability of a request landing on a cold host (no warmed KV) by ~3x relative to previous setup.
- Those cold hosts take extra ~300-450ms before first token while JIT/compat checks and cache priming run.
- Rolling back LB affinity on a small subset reduced first-byte p95 back toward baseline for that slice.

Next immediate actions:
- Scoped rollback of LB affinity tweak for StreamlineAI dedicated pool (in progress).
- Scheduling a rollback of runtime hotpatch 2.1.8 on affected dedicated pools if rollback of LB affinity does not restore baseline in 30m.
- Instrument additional telemetry in kernel-selection path to capture precise JIT/cold-init counts (PR opened).

[2026-03-12 09:14 UTC] Lena Park (Support): Customer alerted that after morning deploy they observed a 4-5x increase in p95 first-token latency. They provided example request IDs and SDK logs. Attaching logs to ticket.
[2026-03-12 09:48 UTC] Priya Singh (SRE): Started correlation of host-level metrics. Noted subset of nodes with elevated 'model-initialization' time and high counts of 'kernel-compat-check' events. Marked nodes for deeper inspection.
[2026-03-12 10:05 UTC] Diego Morales (Serving Runtime): Reproduced locally with 2.1.8 + affinity change. Observed extra setup time from a new compat check path introduced to handle quantized kernels. Created PR to gate compat checks behind warmed-cache flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321
[2026-03-12 10:42 UTC] Lena Park (Support) -> StreamlineAI: Provided guidance to temporarily pin their workload to rw-3.1-large on runtime rtx-runtime-2.1.7. Customer agreed to test a routing pin for a 30-minute window and report results.
[2026-03-13 02:17 UTC] StreamlineAI (customer comment): After pinning to 2.1.7 first-byte p95 dropped back to ~140ms. Observed ~95% of requests within SLA now. Still seeing a few outliers.
[2026-03-14 08:22 UTC] Priya Singh (SRE): Rolling back LB affinity in StreamlineAI's dedicated pool as an intermediate mitigation. Monitoring metrics; will follow up with a plan for either full runtime rollback or a targeted runtime fix.
Temporary workaround provided to customer: pin their routing to runtime rtx-runtime-2.1.7 (pre-hotpatch) or route to rw-3.1-large on a warmed pool. Support created a routing pin for StreamlineAI and verified improvement within 20 minutes.
Short-term: keep LB affinity rollback in place for StreamlineAI and monitor for 24 hours. If metrics remain stable, schedule a targeted runtime patch that removes the opportunistic compat/JIT check on cold hosts (PR #4321).
Long-term: add startup warmup to dedicated pools during scale-up to ensure KV cache priming and kernel warm paths are executed before accepting steady traffic. Add gating for new compat checks behind an opt-in flag for dedicated customers.
