Issue summary:
Customer NimbusApps reports that cohort tiles on their main usage dashboard show zero counts for multiple metrics (active_sessions, token_count) intermittently after our nightly aggregation pass. The dashboard previously displayed expected values during the day and dropped to zero after the background compaction/aggregation job runs.

Impact:
- Customer cannot rely on cohort metrics for billing reconciliation and product telemetry.
- Affects 3 dashboard widgets across their org; spikes trust issues and blocked billing reconciliation for the past two compaction windows.
- Visible to customer admins and product analytics users; dashboards show zeros for historical buckets whereas raw event exports still contain rows.

Environment:
- prod cluster in us-west (dedicated tenant for NimbusApps)
- Console version: 2.14.1
- Retention engine: retention-engine v1.9.3 (compaction worker v3.2.0)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Log in as NimbusApps org admin in prod (us-west region).
2) Open "Product Usage" dashboard -> select cohort "Beta Testers (last 30 days)" and timespan last 7 days.
3) Observe cohort tiles for active_sessions and token_count show nonzero during daytime.
4) Wait for scheduled background aggregation/compaction run (00:15 UTC) or trigger compaction via internal job runner.
5) Refresh dashboard: tiles for those cohorts show 0 for all hourly buckets after merge completes.

Logs & artifacts:
- Query trace ID (console): trace:usw-3::0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h
- Retention worker logs (excerpt): "INFO compaction: merged 24h buckets into 1h; dropped 42 series due to label-scope collision"
- Export of raw events for cohort (CSV) attached by customer shows rows for same buckets.
- Screenshot: dashboard_before_and_after.png attached to ticket.
Login to NimbusApps org admin in prod (us-west).
Open Product Usage dashboard and select cohort Beta Testers (last 30 days).
Observe active_sessions and token_count show values pre-compaction.
Trigger/await background aggregation/compaction job (00:15 UTC).
Refresh dashboard and observe zeroed series for hourly buckets.
retention-worker[pid:8123] 2026-03-10T00:15:07Z INFO merged buckets
retention-worker[pid:8123] 2026-03-10T00:15:07Z WARN dropped series due to label-scope collision: org=nimbusapps,cohort=beta-testers
console-query trace:usw-3::0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h - query took 342ms, returned 0 series after merge
Initial hypothesis: aggregation merge incorrectly prunes series when label namespaces collide between transient prefix labels used by cohort join and persistent metric labels. Replayed compaction on staging with identical payload and enabled verbose logging: compaction step applied pruning rule 'drop-if-empty' earlier than the cohort-join step. Identified retention-engine PR that introduced an optimization to dedupe labels (PR #842) which may have reordered merge steps.
SRE reproduction: ran compaction with same dataset in a sandbox; confirmed 42 series are flagged as "dropped" though raw events remain. Query planner returns empty result because cohort join key was rewritten to a sanitized label that the downstream index doesn't have.
Next steps: add a canary change to compaction order and re-run for NimbusApps tenant only, add additional instrumentation around label-scope and series tombstone reasons.
Workaround provided: rolled back retention-engine to v1.9.2 for NimbusApps tenant and re-ran compaction to restore expected series counts. Engineering created hotfix branch reverting label-dedupe optimization and added an additional safety check to avoid pruning series referenced by cohort joins. Hotfix PR created and under review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/retention-engine/pull/848. Follow-up: schedule a full replay for affected windows and run reconciliation job to backfill any lost rollup counts.
Customer communicated workaround applied; they confirmed restored counts in two verification windows. Planned release of hotfix to production across dedicated tenants after QA signoff.
2026-03-10 | Support - Asha Patel: Acknowledged receipt from NimbusApps and escalated to SRE. Opened linked internal ticket INT-4120 for urgent investigation.
2026-03-10 | SRE - Diego Marquez: Reproduced in sandbox. Observed prune events during compaction mentioning label-scope collision. Collecting retention worker logs and running a replay.
2026-03-11 | Engineering - Priya Rao: Root cause looks tied to label dedupe optimization in retention-engine PR #842. Preparing rollback hotfix.
2026-03-11 | Support - Maya Chen: Shared temporary rollback plan with NimbusApps and requested confirmation window to run rollback. Customer approved immediate rollback for their tenant only.
2026-03-12 | SRE - Liam O'Connor: Rolled back retention-engine to v1.9.2 for NimbusApps and re-ran compaction job. Verified cohort tiles now show expected counts. Creating hotfix PR to revert optimization safely.
2026-03-12 | Customer - Jordan Lee (NimbusApps): Confirmed dashboard counts restored and billing reconciliation can proceed. Asked for ETA on global fix to prevent recurrence.

payload.description:
Issue summary: HelixCare reported intermittent 429s and p99 latency spikes on dedicated cluster during a morning activation window. Impact: Several routes backed by the customer's reserved pool experienced elevated token latency and transient request failures for ~40 minutes. Customer-facing symptoms included streaming disconnects and repeated retry errors.

Observed behavior: p50 latency normal, p95/p99 spiked; autoscaler did not provision additional nodes quickly enough; allocator showed many short-lived attachments from the customer's sidecars; GPU attach failures and slot exhaustion recorded in the allocator and scheduler logs.

Initial customer report: customer saw a synchronous activation burst from a scheduled job that bootstraps short lived model shims across many pods, creating ~10-15k ephemeral connections over 2 minutes. This coincided with spike in sidecar write amplification and NVMe IO wait on the dedicated hosts.
Initial triage (Support): collected request traces and error counts, confirmed 429s across multiple routes. Observed repeated 'slot-reserved' and 'attach-timeout' in allocator logs.

SRE analysis: correlated allocator metrics with NVMe iostat and kernel iowait. Found marked increase in sidecar log writes and metadata updates at 09:05 UTC, matching customer's activation window. Autoscaler metrics show scale decision delayed by 45s due to noisy telemetry from a background health-sweep (high IO causing heartbeat jitter).

Key log snippets:
2026-03-10T09:05:12Z scheduler INFO attaching slot tenant=helixcare slot_id=shard-117 status=queued
2026-03-10T09:05:28Z allocator WARN attach-timeout tenant=helixcare reason=nvme_iowait_high
2026-03-10T09:06:10Z autoscaler DEBUG decision=hold reason=telemetry-latency(1200ms)

Hypotheses considered: sidecar log flood triggering host IO saturation -> allocator heartbeat delays -> autoscaler misread (thinks nodes not under pressure) -> delayed provisioning -> ephemeral connection fanout causes slot fragmentation. Also considered network spike and model prefetch churn; NVMe IO correlated best with symptoms.
2026-03-10 09:02 UTC: HelixCare scheduled activation job starts.
2026-03-10 09:05 UTC: Spotty 429s and p99 jump reported by customer.
2026-03-10 09:07 UTC: Support opened incident, gathered traces.
2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: SRE observed NVMe iowait spike and allocator attach-timeouts.
2026-03-10 09:20 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied (throttle sidecar write rate for helixcare).
2026-03-10 09:30 UTC: Autoscaler headroom increased for affected reserved pool (manual bump).
2026-03-10 09:42 UTC: Error rate subsided and latency returned to baseline.
2026-03-12 14:00 UTC: Follow-up completed, permanent fixes scheduled.
Short-term mitigation: applied customer-scoped sidecar write throttling and small default rate-limit to prevent NVMe write amplification during activation waves. Manually increased reserved-pool headroom (added +2 nodes) while autoscaler logic was adjusted.

Long-term fixes scheduled: 1) autoscaler change to ignore short telemetry bursts from background health scans and require sustained pressure before deferring scale decisions (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/98). 2) allocator patch to aggregate rapid attach/detach from same tenant to reduce slot churn (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/204). 3) documentation & template for customers with large activation waves recommending staggered start or baked-in rate-limiting.

Customer communication: Support coordinated with HelixCare engineering; provided workaround to stagger activation and confirmation when root cause mitigations were scheduled. Issue marked Resolved after validation period of 48 hours with no recurrence.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 09:13 - HelixCare (customer): Activation kicked off at 09:02 UTC, it's a scheduled bootstrap across many small services. We saw retries and some 429s starting ~09:05.
2026-03-10 09:40 - HelixCare (customer): Metrics look normal now, thank you. We'll modify the activation to stagger starts while you roll fixes.
Attachment: diagnostic-sample-helixcare-2026-03-10.log attached to the incident in Jira (sanitized).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart is building a long-running orchestration service that drives a multi-step workflow where each step triggers a Redwood function/tool call. They want strong guarantees that each step is executed at-most-once across retries, client restarts, and region failovers.

Impact:
- Inconsistent downstream state when a step executes twice (e.g., duplicate charge, duplicated email send).
- Unclear recommended pattern for mapping 'action' idempotency onto Redwood's request-scoped idempotency key model.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (dedicated GPU pool) in us-east.
- Using Python backend orchestrator, TypeScript front-end for initiating workflows, and occasional Go workers for async processing.
- SDKs: python==3.12 redwood-sdk v1.4.2, @redwood/sdk 1.4.2, go-sdk v1.4.1.

Use case details and constraints:
1) Workflows are long-running (minutes to hours). Steps may be triggered from different processes (frontend initiates, backend polls, worker picks up).
2) Network partitions and client restarts are expected; BrightCart needs clear at-most-once semantics per logical action id (e.g., order-12345-step-payments).
3) They prefer not to add heavy external coordination (no central DB for every idempotency check) but are open to lightweight key-value store or Redis.

What they tried:
- Generating a per-action UUID and sending it in an X-Idempotency header on each funcall request; observed duplicate executions when stream reconnects or when a proxied connection stripped the custom header.
- Using tokens persisted in Redis with short TTL to gate downstream side effects; this reduced duplication but introduced race conditions during concurrent retries from multiple processes.
- Attempted client-side optimistic check: ask Clearwater webhook to verify idempotency state before calling; this added latency and still had race windows.

Specific questions (BrightCart asks):
1) Recommended schema/TTL for an idempotency store for long-running orchestration steps? Any rules-of-thumb for TTL vs workflow length?
2) Safe patterns for multi-process concurrency: should they use Redis SETNX + expiration and then confirm-on-success? Any examples in Python/TS/Go?
3) Guidance about header-based idempotency (X-Idempotency) vs body-scoped token vs per-action confirmation step. Which is resilient across proxy/CDN and HSM rotations?
4) Is there any planned Redwood server-side support for per-action idempotency (e.g., confirming a tool-run idempotency token separately from request-level idempotency)?
5) Any SDK helpers or middleware recommended for automatic dedup handling across restarts and multiplexed streams?

Desired outcome:
- Concrete, language-specific examples for safe at-most-once patterns that work with Redwood function/tool calls.
- Recommended Redis key schema + TTL guidance and concurrency pattern (e.g., SETNX flow + idempotency confirmation).
- Any platform limitations or recommended guardrails (headers stripped by proxies, max idempotency key length, signing considerations for private deployments with HSM).

Logs / Evidence:
- Sample request headers captured where duplicate occurred (redacted):
  - X-Idempotency: "action-uuid:85f4a1c2"
  - Authorization: "Bearer REDACTED"
  - Via: "edge-proxy-1"

- Example Server trace (reduced):
  - 2026-03-08T14:02:03Z [api-gateway] incoming request id=req-7a2
  - 2026-03-08T14:02:03Z [serving-runtime] funccall start tool=charge-hosted order=12345 idempotency=X-Idempotency=action-uuid:85f4a1c2
  - 2026-03-08T14:02:04Z [serving-runtime] funccall completed status=200 confirmation_token=confirm-3b9
  - 2026-03-08T14:05:11Z [api-gateway] retry request id=req-8f9 (replayed after reconnect) idempotency header missing
  - 2026-03-08T14:05:11Z [serving-runtime] funccall start tool=charge-hosted order=12345 idempotency=none
  - 2026-03-08T14:05:12Z [serving-runtime] funccall completed status=200 confirmation_token=confirm-4a2

Notes:
- There are signs the header was removed by an intermediate proxy on reconnect.
- BrightCart is sensitive to adding an extra round-trip but can accept a small confirmation call post-success.

Requested attachments: BrightCart included minimal flow diagram and code snippets in their initial support email (attached to the ticket).
Support (Lena Park) 2026-03-10: Thanks for the detailed write-up, Diego / BrightCart. This is a common pattern for long-running orchestrations. Short answer: X-Idempotency header alone is brittle across intermediaries; we recommend a hybrid pattern (persistent idempotency store + confirmation token). I'll outline language-specific recipes below and link to internal notes.
Support (Lena Park) 2026-03-10: Recommended pattern (high-level):
1) Generate a per-action ID (action-id).
2) Before issuing Redis SETNX action-id -> pending (TTL = workflow timeout + safety window).
3) Call Redwood func/tool with action-id in body (not just header).
4) On success, store the returned confirmation_token (or write a small record) and mark action-id -> confirmed.
5) On retries, check confirmed state first; if confirmed, return cached result; if pending and lock expired, treat as conflict and escalate to compensating flow.

Redis TTL guidance: set TTL = expected max workflow duration + 2x median network RTT + 30s safety. For very long-running flows (hours), prefer a longer-lived key with periodic heartbeats from the orchestrator to renew the TTL.
Support (Lena Park) 2026-03-11: Language snippets attached as inline examples: Python SETNX + confirm flow using redis-py; Node/TS using ioredis with compare-and-set; Go using redigo. Also note: prefer putting action-id in request body JSON field and signing the payload if going through untrusted proxies. Headers can be dropped; bodies are more likely preserved.

Python example sketch: Redis SETNX action:{action_id} -> "pending", TTL=ttl
call redwood.func(..., json={"action_id": action_id, ...})
if success: redis.set(action:{action_id}:confirmed, confirmation_token, ex=confirm_ttl)

Node/TS and Go examples follow same pattern.
Engineering (SRE) 2026-03-11: Internal note: platform currently returns a confirmation_token in responses for hosted charging tools; we don't yet expose a first-class confirm/claim API for idempotency tokens. Related GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7891 (adds optional response header X-Confirmation-Token for some tools). We should surface guidance in docs and consider a lightweight confirm endpoint in roadmap. Logging: we verified proxy logs showing header-stripping on reconnect via edge-proxy-1, which explains missing header scenario.
BrightCart (Customer) 2026-03-12: Thanks, this helps. A few clarifying Qs: 1) For multi-worker concurrent retries, is SETNX enough or should we use a Lua script for atomic check-and-write of both pending and worker-id? 2) For private deployments with HSM signing, are there constraints on payload size or header signing that we should watch for?
Support (Lena Park) 2026-03-12: Answers: 1) Use a small Lua script (GET + SETNX semantics) to avoid races when you need to store metadata (worker id, attempt count). SETNX alone is fine when you only need a lock token. 2) HSM signing: avoid large arbitrary headers; signed payloads (sign the action_id + timestamp) are safer. Private deployments sometimes enable edge proxies that rewrite headers; signing the body or using a confirmation token flow is more robust. I'll follow up with a sample Lua script and a short runbook link.
Actionable follow-ups (Lena Park) 2026-03-12: Attach Python/TS/Go code examples and the Lua script to the ticket; create short docs page for Best Practices for orchestration idempotency and loop in SDK team to consider adding middleware helpers. Linked engineering issue created: INT-4122 to track SDK middleware exploration.
Pending guidance attachments and SDK middleware follow-up. Support provided recommended patterns and engineering created internal follow-up INT-4122 for SDK helper work.
payload.summary: Best-practices for per-action idempotency in long-running orchestrations across Python/TS/Go SDKs

Issue summary:
Northridge Bank completed initial account setup and submitted Redwood's security questionnaire. They require a consolidated evidence bundle for their internal audit (KYC onboarding) that includes: 1) a timebound SIEM export (ordered events) for a three-hour window on 2026-02-26 with per-record HMAC; 2) a replayable forensic slice to demonstrate event fidelity and replay tools; and 3) proof of tenant-encryption key rotation and HSM-backed key attestation for the period covering the export.

Impact:
Customer cannot complete their procurement onboarding for production access until they receive a turnkey evidence package and a short replay demo for their security team. This is blocking their go/no-go decision for production traffic (estimated $15k/mo committed spend).

Environment:
Production (us-east primary, eu-west DR). Tenant ID: northridge-prod-7. Export time window requested: 2026-02-26T09:00:00Z to 2026-02-26T12:00:00Z. Desired formats: gzipped JSON lines (newline-delimited JSON), manifest with per-batch SHA256, HMAC per-record using customer-provided verification key, and an optional parq/avro translation. Delivery medium: SFTP (customer-managed gateway) with pre-authorized SSH key and optional presigned S3 link behind customer VPC.

Steps to reproduce / reproduce data selection:
1) Validate tenant export pipeline for northridge-prod-7.
2) Query audit store for the time window and event types: authentication, model-invoke, webhook-delivery, policy-evaluation, and admin-activity.
3) Produce ordered export with per-event timestamp, event_id, tenant_id, routing, and payload truncated to PI-neutral fields.
4) Generate HMAC per record using tenant envelope key and produce a signed manifest and a detached signature (RFC 7515 style).
5) Prepare a replay harness: a Docker image and small runbook that replays events to a sandboxed replayer with deterministic output and a checksum report.

Logs / evidence attached by customer:
- Security questionnaire PDF (uploaded to ticket).
- Customer SFTP public key and host fingerprint (provided).

Notes / customer constraints:
- Northridge requires HSM-backed key attestation (we must provide an attestation statement showing key rotation event GUIDs and Timestamps).
- They do not want raw PII fields; any PII should be redacted or pseudonymized in the export per their checklist.
- Replay must be demonstrable in a 20-minute video call for their security engineering team.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deliverable 1: Ordered, gzipped ndjson export for requested window with per-record HMAC and signed manifest.
- Deliverable 2: Replay harness and checksum report demonstrating deterministic playback.
- Deliverable 3: Key rotation attestation referencing KMS/HSM event IDs and a rotation timeline for the last 90 days.
- Deliverable 4: Runbook for how to reproduce export and redaction steps.

Requested by customer on 2026-03-09; customer needs final package and 20-min demo between 2026-03-15 and 2026-03-19.

Priority rationale: enterprise onboarding blocker with legal and procurement timelines.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:28 - SRE (Liying Chen): Investigation note: Live export for 3-hour window estimated compressed size ~18GB. Suggest using pre-signed S3 drop with multipart upload; SFTP delivery can be provided after we stage to S3. Also recommend prefix-level checksums and a manifest signed by platform KMS and include per-record HMAC using a tenant-wrapped envelope key.
Attached runbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Onboarding/pages/Replay+Runbook+Draft
2026-03-12 10:03 - Security (Samir Rao): We'll generate attestation. Provide us with the tenant key alias and the rotation window. We'll return a signed statement from the HSM CA and pointer to KMS audit log entries. ETA 2026-03-13 EOD.

SFTP handshake tested against provided host key in staging; host unreachable from our primary export runner due to customer-side firewall. Recommended option: provide presigned S3 and we coordinate with customer to pull into their SFTP gateway, or open source IP temporarily. Needs approval from customer ops.
Plan: produce ndjson export in staged S3 path: s3://redwood-temp-exports/northridge-prod-7/2026-02-26-09_12/ with manifest and detached signature; then copy to customer's SFTP. Create replay harness image and checksum report.
Await HSM attestation blob from Security (Samir).
Confirm delivery mechanism with customer: SFTP pull vs. presigned S3 push.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During the 09:00-10:00 UTC predictive-autoscale window on 2026-03-12, Nimbus Analytics reported a sustained p95/p99 throughput drop (30-60%) on their reserved pool. The pool reported full GPU slot allocation and started returning 429 throttles and occasional 503s for batched routes.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency p95 increased from ~90ms to ~320ms and p99 from ~420ms to ~1.2s for batched text-generation endpoints.
- Several short streaming requests were failing with streaming disconnects and batch cancellations.
- Billing not affected directly but SLA risk due to degraded throughput.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool (customer: Nimbus Analytics) in prod us-east-1.
- Autoscaler configured in predictive mode (lookback 6h, forecast horizon 1h).
- Pool had pinned model redwood-7b-v1 and fallback llm-open-13b-q4.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Synthetic traffic replay using customer's traffic trace (replay started at 09:00 UTC with same mix of long streaming + many small inference bursts).
2) Observe autoscaler behavior: predictive scale-up initiated ~08:55 UTC, scheduled new slots to be ready at 09:05 UTC.
3) At 09:07 UTC backlog of small short-lived streams increased queueing and slot allocation reached 100%.
4) p95/p99 throughput dropped and some batched inflight requests were cancelled.

Observed logs / traces:
- Grafana dashboard (reserved-pool/nimbus) showed the slot-allocation curve hitting 100% at 09:07 UTC and stayed within 98-100% until 09:40.
- Scheduler logs: "slot_alloc: fail reserve (no_free_slot)" repeated across many hosts.
- Autoscaler logs: predictive job executed and marked new nodes as available, but several allocations failed with "affinity_mismatch" in scheduler.
- Serving runtime logs: repeated "batcher: cancel_batch_inflight: victimous_short_streams" and KV-cache reports show high prefix-cache-built entries.

Notes: customer reported this is first time predictive mode was used at this scale with a mix of many short streams and a handful of long-context generation sessions.

2026-03-12 09:30 - Support (Ava Chen): Acknowledged. Collected initial logs and asked SRE to pull scheduler and autoscaler traces. SLA flagged and priority set to P1.
2026-03-12 10:02 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Initial hypothesis: slot exhaustion caused by many short-lived streams fragmenting slot capacity and predictive autoscale placing nodes with incompatible affinity. Pulling host-level GPU logs and kernel module messages.
2026-03-12 12:14 - Customer (Nimbus SRE - Rahul Patel): We confirmed traffic spike originates from a localized workflow with thousands of 50-200ms calls every minute; long-run sessions continued concurrently. We can throttle that workflow if needed for troubleshooting.
2026-03-12 15:05 - Eng (Maya Singh): Replayed customer's trace in staging. Reproduction succeeded: short-stream fanout saturates slots and causes the batcher to cancel inflight batches. Observed high KV-cache growth and increased NVLink IO wait on 3 hosts.
2026-03-12 18:30 - Support (Ava Chen): Temporary mitigations applied: 1) Enabled per-tenant short-stream isolation policy (route to separate slot pool) for Nimbus; 2) Increased autoscaler affinity relaxation window. Monitoring impact.
2026-03-13 09:00 - SRE (Diego Martinez): After mitigation, p95 returned to 110-130ms, p99 to ~240ms. Will keep ticket open to track permanent changes and postmortem.
2026-03-13 12:20 - Customer (Rahul Patel): Confirmed improved performance. Asked for guidance to avoid recurrence and whether predictive mode should be used going forward.
Findings:
- Root cause appears to be a combination of short-stream fanout and allocation affinity. Short streams create many small batches that fragment slot occupancy (slot-churn), preventing efficient high-throughput batching.
- Predictive autoscaler placed additional nodes, but scheduler reported "affinity_mismatch" for several allocations: the autoscaler offered nodes with constraints (gpu-type:gpuA, zone:a) while existing tenant affinity expected (gpu-type:gpuB or same host family) causing allocations to fail and leaving slots unavailable.
- KV-cache growth: small streams had a high diversity of prefixes; KV-cache eviction wasn't keeping up and memory pressure led to occasional host-level eviction cycles, correlating with small latency spikes.
- NVLink IO wait and GPU kernel queueing observed on 3 hosts; these hosts were running a mix of long-context sessions and many short batches.
- No hardware failures found; kernel messages show resource pressure but not OOMs.

Hypotheses tested:
1) Predictive scale-up nodes with strict affinity caused allocation failures -> validated in staging trace replay.
2) Short-stream isolation reduces slot-churn and should recover throughput -> validated with mitigation in prod for Nimbus.
3) KV-cache tuning (smaller per-tenant cache or different eviction policy) reduces memory pressure -> synthetic tests show lower memory churn but needs longer soak.

Logs / dashboards referenced:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/reserved-pools/nimbus?from=2026-03-12T08:30:00Z&to=2026-03-12T10:00:00Z
- Scheduler trace: https://kibana.redwood.com/app/discover#/doc/trace-id/trace-ff9a3c
- Autoscaler job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-autoscaler/actions/runs/72513

Temporary mitigation (2026-03-12):
1) Activated per-tenant short-stream isolation: moved high-fanout short streams for Nimbus into a separate slot pool (isolated small-stream pool) to prevent fragmentation of large-model slots.
2) Relaxed strict autoscaler affinity rules for predictive mode to allow heterogeneous node matches while preserving cost tags.
3) Applied KV-cache eviction tuning for tenant to cap per-tenant prefix entries to 25k (reduced memory churn).

Result: throughput returned to acceptable levels within ~3 hours post-mitigation. Customer confirmed improved p95/p99 metrics and reduced cancelled batches.

Permanent next steps (action items):
- ENG-1729: Update predictive autoscaler to surface affinity mismatch counts and automatically relax affinity when allocation failures exceed threshold. (linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-autoscaler/pull/498)
- ENG-1730: Add automatic short-stream isolation heuristic in serving runtime to detect high fanout tenants and route them to separate small-stream pools.
- OPS-881: Run a 72h soak in staging with customer's traffic trace to validate KV-cache eviction changes and measure impact on NVLink IO wait.
- Follow-up with Nimbus: provide best-practice configuration doc for mixed long/short workloads and recommendation to tune client-side batching where possible.

Ticket status: probing for permanent changes; leave open until ENG-1729 and ENG-1730 are implemented and soak completes.

Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden shift in how hourly usage was bucketed after a scheduled batch migration on 2026-03-09. Several hourly buckets for batch embedding jobs were reassigned to the subsequent hour, which caused a portion of usage to fall into a higher rate tier for that billing cycle.

Impact:
- BrightStore observed a ~12% increase in effective per-token cost for a two-hour window (01:00-03:00 UTC).
- Provisional overage alert triggered for their reserved-dedicated plan.
- Customer is requesting an explanation, provisional credit, and assurance this won't recur.

Environment:
- Org: BrightStore Inc. (dedicated pool: dp-us-east-07)
- Region: us-east primary; some jobs routed through eu-west for failover during the migration window.
- Job type: nightly batch embeddings (bulk-embed API, 16k sequence length), scheduled migration job id 'batch-mig-2026-03-09'

Steps to reproduce (from customer runbook):
1) Trigger the same batch job on prod during hourly rollover (01:58 UTC)
2) Observe metering events emitted by billing-pipeline at 02:00+
3) Compare hour buckets and rate tier assignment in the billing dashboard

Observed behavior:
- Metering pipeline shows a cluster of usage events stamped 01:59:xx that were routed into the 02:00 hourly bucket for aggregation and subsequently attracted higher tier pricing in the pipeline snapshot.
- Console shows a short-lived routing to eu-west for a subset of shards during the rollout.

Expected behavior:
- Usage should be aggregated into the hour corresponding to the request timestamp and rate-tier calculations should be stable across shard routing.

Attachments/Logs:
- Customer provided CSV of per-request timestamps and trace ids (attached in Jira).
- Linked billing snapshot and invoice preview in their account (screen grabs).
- Billing pipeline job logs: invoice-pipeline/consumer-20260309.log (internal link in investigation notes).

Requested outcome:
1) Clear explanation of why the hourly bucket reassignment happened.
2) Provisional credit for the delta while we investigate.
3) Fix or mitigation to prevent reoccurrence and confirmation of re-rating if credit is applied.
2026-03-10 09:12 - BrightStore (customer): We ran our nightly embed at 01:58 UTC and saw a spike in invoice preview. Support requested help — attaching CSV of timestamps and trace ids.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Maya Patel): Thank you. I've triaged this and opened a P1 ticket. We've applied a temporary billing hold on new overage notifications while we investigate. Assigning to SRE/Platform to look at metering pipeline behavior (assigned to Liam).
2026-03-10 11:30 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Initial look at invoice-pipeline logs: there were several rebalances in the batch scheduler between 01:58 and 02:02 UTC. Not yet sure if event timestamps were mutated by the rebalance. Pulling audit trail for consumer offsets and shard routing.
2026-03-10 14:02 - Finance (Elena Ruiz): Please note BrightStore has requested a provisional credit. Finance requests an initial delta estimate to approve temporary credit up to $6,000.
2026-03-11 08:47 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer confirmed they are okay with provisional credit while root cause is investigated. Waiting on SRE findings and precise usage delta calculation.
2026-03-12 16:20 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Found related consumer-offset race in consumer-v2; committing investigation notes to linked PR. Suspect timestamp normalization failed to account for shard-handback during rebalance. Preparing backfill plan.
Query: SELECT count(*) FROM metering.events WHERE org='brightstore' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-03-09T01:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-09T03:00:00Z' GROUP BY hour_bucket; result shows 24% of events with request_ts in 01:59 but hour_bucket=02:00.
Observed short-lived routing to eu-west for shards 12-14 at 01:59:55 UTC documented in cluster logs: scheduler_events/2026-03-09/rebalances.log#L342-L358.
Hypothesis A: consumer-v2 rebalance path re-emitted events without applying timestamp normalization, causing aggregator to compute hour_bucket from processing_time instead of request_time for a subset of events.
Hypothesis B: a recent change in invoice-pipeline (PR #889) adjusted buffer flush logic and altered offset boundaries for hour aggregation. Investigating PR diff and test coverage for hour boundary cases.
Evidence: consumer-v2 log lines show 'processed_ts' differing from 'request_ts' by 5-8 seconds for affected traces; aggregator currently uses 'max(processed_ts, request_ts)' in the presence of missing fields, which may bias toward processed_ts during rebalance.
Dashboard links: billing-dashboard.redwood/internal/org/brightstore/usage?window=2026-03-09T00:00:00Z..2026-03-09T04:00:00Z; metering-latency panels show spikes exactly at 02:00 UTC.
Temporary mitigation applied: billing hold for BrightStore to stop automated overage emails and prevent auto-charge while we compute a corrected rerate.
Next step: run re-aggregation backfill for 2026-03-09 01:00-03:00 and compute delta with current invoice preview. Backfill plan in progress; estimating 2 hours to run and validate.
Under investigation — preliminary evidence points to a consumer-v2 rebalance re-emitting events where aggregation used processed_ts instead of request_ts for hour bucketing; change in invoice-pipeline buffer flush (PR #889) may have widened the window for the race.
Partial mitigation: provisional billing hold applied and provisional credit approved by Finance up to $6,000 pending exact delta. Backfill job scheduled to recompute hour buckets for 2026-03-09 01:00-03:00. Final rerating and any additional credits will be applied after backfill completes.
Run re-aggregation backfill for 2026-03-09 01:00-03:00 and produce corrected invoice delta (owner: Liam, ETA: 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC).
If backfill confirms delta > provisional credit, submit for additional finance approval and apply credits to BrightStore billing account (owner: Elena).
Add unit/integration test for hour boundary in invoice-pipeline and increase test coverage for consumer rebalance scenarios (owner: backend team).
Create post-incident runbook entry describing rebalance→bucketing risk and mitigation (owner: Platform Ops).
Schedule follow-up call with BrightStore to review findings and confirm credit application (owner: CS).

Issue summary: Customers (notably Waveform Analytics, dedicated tenant) observed a sudden elevation in 5xx responses from the API gateway beginning 2026-03-12 20:13 UTC. Errors coincide with long TLS/ALPN handshake latencies and a subsequent cascade of runtime preemptions / supervisor restarts for serving-runtime processes assigned to the tenant. Impact: ~18% of requests returned 502/503 over a 25-minute window for the tenant; overall cluster error rate increased by ~3% during the window. Visible customer-facing symptoms: streaming sessions dropped mid-response, and bulk embedding uploads intermittently failed with 5xx. Timeline: - 2026-03-12 20:09 UTC: minor increase in ALPN negotiation latencies on a subset of edge proxies. - 20:13 UTC: api-gateway 5xx rate begins to rise; keepalive pool consumption increases. - 20:18 UTC: serving-runtime supervisors report CPU scheduling delays; OOM-like preemptions observed for tenant worker groups (preempt -> restart). - 20:32 UTC: mitigation actions (accept-queue increase, temporary rate limit applied for tenant) reduce error rate. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation and follow-ups.
Hypotheses considered: 1) ALPN/TLS handshake queuing on edge proxies caused long tail latencies -> backpressure to runtime. 2) Keepalive connection reuse semantics combined with HTTP/2 stream multiplexing caused head-of-line blocking. 3) The serving-runtime preemption logic misinterpreted high CPU scheduling latencies as hung workers and forcibly restarted them, amplifying failure rate. Findings: - Heatmap of alpn_neg shows a spike on edge nodes colocated with tenant's egress IPs. - Kernel-level tcp_tw_reuse and TCP backlog exhaustion correlated with accept queue growth. - Supervisor logs show preempt_count spikes tied to cpu_wait_ms > 1500. - No OOMs in dmesg; restarts were preemption-based by our watchdog (we killed workers to break perceived deadlocks). - A recent change in the edge-proxy TLS handshake loop (PR #241) introduced a tighter retry delay which increases active TLS worker retention under high backlog. Partial replication in staging: reproduced when artificially limiting ephemeral worker counts on proxies and simultaneously running cpu-heavy model in the runtime.
Mitigated: - Edge proxies rolled back the handshake retry delay change from PR #241 on affected hosts (rollback tag v2.3.7->v2.3.6). - Temporarily increased accept_queue and ephemeral TLS worker pool on egress-edge nodes in us-east-1. - Applied tenant rate limit for Waveform to protect shared capacity during remediation window. - Adjusted runtime watchdog preemption threshold to be more permissive for short CPU stalls. Permanent fix plan: optimize handshake retry backoff logic to prevent worker retention, introduce connection-shed behavior prior to forced runtime preemption, and add heuristics to correlate apigw backlog with runtime restarts.
Postmortem doc (owner: Liam) - due 2026-03-18; include timeline and metric charts
Edge-proxy change: implement adaptive handshake backoff (owner: Priya) - target 2026-03-20
Runtime: add correlation metric shipping apigw_backlog -> preempt_count (owner: Marco) - target 2026-03-19
Product: review tenant SLA and default burst protections for dedicated tier (owner: Nora) - target 2026-03-25
2026-03-12 20:24 UTC - Support (Aisha): Notified customer (Waveform) of elevated errors; applied temporary tenant-level rate limit to reduce tail pressure.
2026-03-12 20:42 UTC - SRE (Liam): Increased apigw accept_queue and bumped proxy ephemeral workers by +30% on affected hosts; error rate falling.
2026-03-13 09:15 UTC - Eng (Priya Ghosh): Reproduced in staging with scripted ALPN stall; PR identified that increases handshake worker lifetime under retry path (edge-proxy PR #241).
2026-03-13 11:02 UTC - Runtime (Marco): Watchdog preemption threshold adjusted in staging; reduced forced restarts for cpu_wait_ms < 3000 to avoid cascades.
2026-03-14 07:30 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed services stabilized after mitigations; provided notes for post-incident review.
1) Simulate sustained concurrent streaming + embedding workload from a single dedicated tenant (Waveform-like traffic profile: 40 concurrent streams + 8 embedding uploads).
2) Use HTTP/2 with ALPN; include TLS session reuse on long-lived connections.
3) Ramp concurrency over 5 minutes and observe accept queue, TLS handshake latencies, and runtime supervisor metrics.
4) Observe apigw 502/503 when handshake backlog + CPU contention align.

[2026-03-12T20:14:12Z] apigw-edge-3 keepalive_in_use=980/1024 pool_wait_ms=1200 502_count=17
[2026-03-12T20:17:08Z] runtime-supervisor tenant=waveform worker_group=22 preempt_count=3 cpu_wait_ms=2400 restart=1
[2026-03-12T20:18:02Z] runtime-22 stderr: "sched: long-sleep detected, killing worker to avoid deadlock"
[2026-03-12T20:20:15Z] metrics: cluster_5xx_rate=0.032 (baseline 0.005); tenant_waveform_5xx=0.18
[2026-03-12T20:30:45Z] mitigation: rate-limit applied tenant=waveform throttled=20%
[2026-03-12T20:31:10Z] apigw-edge-1 accept_queue=28 backlog_ms=45 alpn_neg=20

Goal
Ensure the correct PagerDuty group(s), schedules, and escalation policies exist for Support escalations and match the newly published escalation paths/coverage rules. This is required so Support can page the right on-call without bypassing #incidents or creating ad-hoc paging.

Background
During playbook refresh review, we found mismatches between the documented escalation contacts and what Support can actually page in PagerDuty (some services lack a Support-facing escalation policy; some schedules are named inconsistently; after-hours routing unclear).

Scope
- Create or update a PagerDuty escalation policy named “Support Escalations (Customer Impact)” that routes to the correct primary/secondary on-call per playbook.
- Ensure schedules exist and are populated for:
  1) SRE On-Call (customer impact)
  2) Platform On-Call (control plane/auth/SSO/audit logs)
  3) Runtime/Serving On-Call (streaming/runtime regressions) OR confirm SRE is the first hop with defined handoff.
- Verify Support can trigger paging via a single, stable PD target (group/policy), not individual users.
- Confirm coverage windows + handoff rules match the playbook (weekday vs weekend; after-hours expectations; follow-the-sun handoff if applicable).
- Update the internal directory (where Support looks up PD targets) and confirm the target is referenced from Slack bridge template automation.

Out of scope
- Changing actual on-call rotations/ownership beyond aligning naming/routing (those changes belong to Eng leadership).

Dependencies / related work
- INT-332 Update Slack automation for support bridges (should reference the final PD target)
- INT-333 Jira automation SLA reminders + required fields (will nudge to page via PD target)

References

Additional notes:
- Email thread (bridge template + Jira linking): sources/gmail/rafael_mendes/20260210-incident-bridge-template-and-jira-linking.json
Acceptance criteria
1) PagerDuty escalation policy exists and is discoverable to Support as the standard paging target:
   - Name: “Support Escalations (Customer Impact)”
   - Contains at least 2 levels (Primary + Secondary) with defined timeout/ack rules.
2) The policy routes to schedules (not individuals) owned by the right org(s) and matches documented escalation boundaries.
3) The PD policy is tested end-to-end (test incident) and results are documented in a comment (who received page, within what time, any gaps).
4) Support-facing doc/template is updated to reference the policy name (or PD shortlink) consistently.
Risk / notes
- Avoid creating a path that bypasses #incidents for Sev0/Sev1 events; this PD target is intended to get the right responders while following the incident process.
- Some customers are enterprise with strict comms cadence; paging must be reliable to prevent SLA misses.
Requested reviewers
- Rafael Mendes (SRE on-call/escalations owner)
- Priya Natarajan (Platform eng sponsor)
- Owen Phillips (Support incidents SME)
Proposed configuration (draft)
Level 1: SRE On-Call (customer impact) (15 min)
Level 2: Platform On-Call OR Runtime/Serving On-Call depending on tag/triage (15 min)
Level 3: SRE Manager On-Call / escalation (optional; confirm with Rafael)
Open questions
- Do we want separate PD policies per product area (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) or a single Support-facing policy that triages to SRE first?
- Is there an existing “Support Escalations” service/policy we should rename rather than create net-new (to preserve integrations)?
2026-02-06 (Dev Patel): Creating this as a blocker for playbook adoption. Support currently pages a mix of individuals + an old PD policy that doesn’t match the new routing/coverage. Need a single stable target that matches Confluence escalation paths. Tagging Benji for implementation and Rafael for SRE sign-off.
2026-02-07 (Benji Okafor): Started audit in PagerDuty. Found existing escalation policy “Support-Eng Escalations” pointing to a deprecated schedule (last populated 2025-10). Also found “Platform Primary” schedule exists, “SRE Primary” exists, but no dedicated Runtime schedule. Proposed approach: create new policy “Support Escalations (Customer Impact)” that goes to SRE Primary first, then Platform Primary, then SRE Secondary. Waiting on Rafael to confirm whether Runtime should be separate or handled via SRE triage/handoff.
2026-02-08 (Owen Phillips): +1 to single Support-facing PD target as long as playbook makes clear: if Sev0/Sev1 and broad impact, move to #incidents and let incident commander own. For isolated customer issues, Support can page via PD but still use bridge template + link SUP ticket. Please ensure the PD target name is copy/paste-friendly for macros.
2026-02-10 (Rafael Mendes): Confirmed: Support should page SRE first for customer-impacting prod issues; SRE will pull in Runtime/Platform as needed. We should not force Support to decide between Platform vs Runtime at page time. Recommend policy levels: L1 SRE Primary (10–15m), L2 SRE Secondary (10–15m), L3 SRE Escalation (manager) only for P0+ customer impact. Platform Primary should be added as subscriber/notification for specific services via incident process, not as default L2 in the Support policy.
2026-02-11 (Benji Okafor): Implemented new escalation policy draft:
- Policy: “Support Escalations (Customer Impact)”
- L1: SRE Primary (15m)
- L2: SRE Secondary (15m)
- L3: SRE Manager On-Call (30m)
Also created a PD shortlink in internal wiki: pd://support-escalations (internal). Next: run a test page during business hours w/ Rafael + document results. INT-332 can now reference the policy name in the Slack bridge workflow.
2026-02-12 (Benji Okafor): Test completed (13:20 PT): triggered a test incident via PD using the new policy; SRE Primary received page in ~30s, acknowledged in 2m, escalation did not proceed. Verified Support has permission to trigger the policy and can find it via PD search. Remaining: update internal Support directory reference + confirm no legacy policy is used in macros (coordinating with Dev Patel + INT-332).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a dedicated pool report a hard throughput ceiling plateau where p50/p90 remain fine but sustained throughput is ~40% below historical levels despite ample GPUs being shown as Available.

Impact:
- EdgeDocs experiences sustained lower tokens/sec on their dedicated pool during business hours (approx 09:00-18:00 PDT).
- Client traffic is not receiving 429s, calls succeed but tail latency and throughput are depressed, causing backlog on the customer side and increased internal queueing.
- Business impact: degraded user experience for their product search feature; potential SLA breach if not resolved.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id dp-ec-003 (EdgeDocs reserved cluster)
- Region: us-west-2
- Node type: A100-80GB heterogeneous blend (some older A100-40GB in same pool)
- Routing policy: latency-preferring with fallbacks to auto-quantized model variants

Steps to reproduce / Observed pattern:
1) Run sustained generation workload (many short streams, median context 512 tokens) from EdgeDocs tenant over 30+ minutes.
2) Observe that new allocations are accepted but placement time spikes from ~150ms to ~1200-3000ms intermittently.
3) CPU-side metrics show repeated preemption/handshake events with GPUs where KV cache warmups are happening then evictions re-triggered.
4) Throughput tops out and does not recover even after load stabilizes; pool reports Available GPUs in console but effective throughput remains capped.

Logs & traces (excerpt):
- scheduler.trace: allocation_request -> placement_ack delta: steady increase to 1.2s at plateau windows
- autoscaler.log: "placement_retry=3 backoff=200ms" seen repeatedly for same tenant slices
- serving-runtime: "kv_cache_evict start" logged concurrently with "gpu_handshake_timeout" in multiple pods

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Increased pool reserved capacity by +2 slots (temporary) — transient improvement then reversion to plateau after ~12 minutes.
- Pinned EdgeDocs tenant to a single host to reduce cross-host KV warmups — throughput improved by ~10% but still below baseline.

Sustain short-stream generation workload at scale for 30+ minutes
Observe placement time and allocation handshakes in scheduler traces
Monitor serving-runtime kv_cache and eviction logs concurrent with placement retries
Initial hypothesis: noisy-neighbor or GPU fragmentation. Evidence summary pointed elsewhere: repeated placement handshakes and delayed scheduler heartbeats appearing at the same time window.

Findings so far:
- Scheduler heartbeats to the placement coordinator intermittently delayed by up to 800ms during plateau windows. Heartbeat delay correlated with increased allocation round-trips and placement retries.
- Placement retries cause short-lived preemptions: an in-flight tenant slot is briefly relinquished and reacquired, triggering KV cache eviction/warmup cycles and increasing per-request overhead.
- Autoscaler debounce/backoff parameters allowed multiple near-simultaneous placement attempts for different tenants which amplified slot churn.
- Background GC activity on one older A100 host coincided with the largest heartbeat delays by timestamp correlation.

Hypotheses:
1) Non-deterministic heartbeat jitter from a combination of host-level GC and the scheduler's single-threaded coordinator loop is causing slow placement acknowledgements.
2) Autoscaler debounce settings are too aggressive for short-stream-heavy workloads; parallel placement retries cause unnecessary preemptions and slot churn rather than graceful queuing.
3) KV cache eviction on preemption is expensive enough to reduce effective tokens/sec such that apparent Available GPUs don't translate into usable throughput.

Evidence links:
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/cluster/dedicated-pools?orgId=1&var-pool=dp-ec-003
- Tracing: https://jaeger.redwood.ai/trace/0b8a9c2
- Sample logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/edge/274199/placements.zip
1) Forced tenant pinning to single host for testing (temporary) — gave ~10% immediate uplift.
2) Bumped scheduler heartbeat frequency temporarily on coordinator in us-west-2 canary — reduced observed heartbeat lag in canary by 60%.
3) Raised autoscaler debounce interval and introduced linear backoff for repeated placement retries in staging to validate impact.
4) Engaged infra to collect host-level metrics on suspected older A100 node for background processes and GC timings.
5) Asked customer to slightly reduce short-stream concurrency as a stopgap (customer accepted temporary throttling).
Work in progress: engineering patch prepared to harden scheduler coordinator and change placement retry behavior (PR linked). Planned rollout: canary in staging then gradual roll to us-west-2 dedicated pools.

Target fix details:
- Change scheduler to batch placement acknowledgements and add a small jitter to heartbeat processing loop to avoid synchronized delays.
- Increase autoscaler placement retry backoff and add a max retry cap that funnels excess requests into a queue rather than immediate preemption.
- Improve KV cache eviction policy to defer full eviction on very short preemptions (soft-evict).

Customer-facing mitigation: keep tenant pinned to a smaller host subset until patch deploy. Finance/CS notified of potential SLA credits if plateau persists.

Next steps:
- Deploy patch to staging and run customer workload replay by 2026-03-14.
- If staging looks good, roll canary to 2 nodes in us-west-2 on 2026-03-15 and monitor for 6 business hours.
- Postmortem/learnings to be written to Confluence after root cause confirms.
2026-03-10 09:42 - Support (Avery Chen): Received report from EdgeDocs; customer reports consistent throughput ceiling despite available GPUs. Asked for session IDs and traffic window.
2026-03-10 10:10 - Customer (EdgeDocs, Nora Singh): Provided session IDs and confirmed synthetic replay reproduces behaviour. Noted peak hours alignment.
2026-03-10 13:05 - SRE (Ravi Patel): Correlated placement traces with scheduler heartbeats; seeing 400-800ms jitter. Opening follow-up to infra for host-level metrics.
2026-03-11 08:22 - Infra (Marta Kozlowski): Found high GC pause events on a subset of older nodes during the windows; quarantined one node for deeper inspection.
2026-03-11 12:40 - Eng (Diego Alvarez): Created a prototype change to autoscaler backoff and soft-evict for KV cache (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/7321). Running unit + integration tests.
2026-03-12 16:05 - Support (Avery Chen): Customer accepted temporary pinning and reduced concurrency; saw slight improvement but still below baseline. Monitoring continues.
2026-03-12 17:00 - Eng (Ravi Patel): Scheduling coordinator patch merged to canary branch; scheduled staging run for 2026-03-13.
2026-03-12 17:15 - Support (Avery Chen): Notified CS and billing about potential SLA remediation schedule.

Issue summary:
Customer observed that after resuming a paused canary slice for a model rollout, a subset of traffic was routed to a compatibility/legacy variant instead of the pinned canary variant. This happened even though the customer had an explicit version pin for several long-lived sessions.

Impact:
- ScribeAnalytics reported degraded output quality for ~12% of in-flight requests for a 45 minute window.
- Requests received responses from a legacy compat variant that uses a different tokenizer and older prompt preprocessing, producing tokenization mismatches and downstream parse errors for structured output.
- No 5xx errors, but a quality regression and increased error rates in the customer's downstream parsers.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster in prod:us-west, tenant: scribe-analytics-prod, reserved pool rp-west-04
- Model targeted for rollout: redwood/opt-6.7b-quantized-v2 (canary slice id: cs-923)
1) Customer has model pin set via route with pinned_version=opt-6.7b-quantized-v2.
2) Start staged canary: create canary slice cs-923 with 7% weight and prewarm enabled.
3) Pause canary for manual checks.
4) Resume canary by increasing weight back to 7% via console/rollout API.
5) Observe a subset of previously pinned sessions routed to compat-legacy variant during the first 10 minutes.

Observed vs Expected:
- Observed: Some sessions dropped pin affinity and were served by redwood/opt-6.7b-compat-legacy after canary resume.
- Expected: Pinned sessions should maintain affinity to the explicitly pinned version across canary pause/resume cycles unless pin is explicitly modified.
Edge logs (excerpt):
[2025-11-02T10:14:02Z] ingress: tenant=s-022 session=abc123 route=/nlp/generate prewarm_handshake=START cs-923
[2025-11-02T10:14:03Z] orchestrator: session=abc123 pin_lookup=OK pin=opt-6.7b-quantized-v2 prewarm_status=IN_PROGRESS
[2025-11-02T10:14:04Z] prewarm-service: session=abc123 prewarm_commit=DELAYED reason=orchestrator-commit-race
[2025-11-02T10:14:04Z] routing: session=abc123 final_variant=opt-6.7b-compat-legacy fallback_reason=prefetch_commit_timeout

Trace notes:
- Prefetch handshake completed but prewarm commit to the routing snapshot was delayed by a race with the orchestrator epoch advance.
- When the orchestrator advanced the epoch, routing snapshot included compat fallback entries for new traffic; pinned affinity for long-lived sessions was not reapplied atomically during resume window.
- Immediate: Customer restarted affected streams (client reconnect) to re-establish pin affinity. That rebind caused subsequent requests to route correctly to the pinned variant.
- Short term: We set a temporary guard in the edge proxy to prefer explicit route pins over snapshot fallback for sessions with active session tokens. This reduces the blast radius for resumed canaries (rolled by SRE).
Timeline and root cause hypothesis:
- When canary was resumed, the orchestrator advanced epoch to include the canary slice. The prewarm-service had outstanding prewarm_commits for some in-flight sessions.
- Orchestrator epoch advance triggered a snapshot merge which included fallback routing entries for fresh allocation in case prewarm didn't complete quickly.
- Because the prewarm commit path was non-atomic with respect to pin rebind, sessions that had not completed prewarm_commit fell back to compat variant in the merged snapshot.
- Key contributing factors: (1) non-atomic commit ordering between prewarm-service and orchestrator, (2) no strong preference for explicit pins in the snapshot merge, (3) long-lived session model where reconnects are uncommon.

Reproducibility:
- Reproducible in staging with dedicated reserved pools when simulating a pause/resume and adding artificial latency to prewarm commit.

Next steps agreed:
- Engineering change to make prewarm commit idempotent and block epoch-advance until pin-affinity commits are acknowledged for sessions with active tokens (PR #1428).
- Add a snapshot-merge rule: prefer explicit pinned_version headers over fallback mapping when session token present.
- Run a canary of the fix in prod-labs, then staged rollout to prod with strict monitoring of affinity drift metrics.
(pending) Mitigation applied: edge-proxy guard prefers explicit pinned headers; customer reconnect workaround documented. Engineering PR submitted to make prewarm_commit atomic with orchestrator epoch commit (see PR #1428). Planned rollout: prod-labs canary on 2025-11-07, followed by gradual promotion. Permanent resolution requires successful canary and monitoring of pinned_affinity_loss < 0.1% over 24h.
2025-11-02 11:00 - Support (Asha Patel): Acknowledged. Eng and SRE looped in; open triage. Asking customer for session ids and sample request IDs.
2025-11-02 12:15 - Customer (ScribeAnalytics - Daniel Kim): Provided sample session ids abc123, def456 and examples of malformed structured outputs. Noticed the problem only for sessions active before the resume.
2025-11-02 14:05 - SRE (Omar Li): Captured routing snapshots and noticed commit_for_epoch failure around 10:14:04Z; prewarm-service reported DELAYED commit. Hypothesis: prewarm commit ordering can lose pin-binding if orchestrator advances epoch while commit pending.

Issue summary: Customer reports that for long-running SSE streams (>45s), when the client is slow to read (simulate high CPU or network jitter), the resumed stream after a transient disconnect is missing intermediate 'choice' chunks. Impact: Some end-users see partial completions (missing sentences) causing downstream application state to appear truncated. Environment: Dedicated account (DialogueAI), prod us-east region, using pinned model llm-redwood-13b-realtime on dedicated pool. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start generation with a prompt that produces ~1200 tokens (long narrative). 2) Simulate client-side backpressure by throttling the socket read or introducing 250-500ms pauses every 5s. 3) Force a short disconnect (TCP RST or browser tab backgrounding). 4) Reconnect and observe SSE stream resume events. Observed behavior: Resume occurs but intermediate choice chunks appear to be skipped; final choice present but continuity has gaps (missing sentences). Sometimes the reconstructed text contains duplicated fragments later in stream, as if fragments were re-ordered. Expected behavior: Resume should yield a stitched stream with no lost tokens and preserved order. Logs/trace: Edge proxy logs show repeated 503s then 200 on reconnect. Serving runtime trace shows successful KV-cache retrieval and a resume token match but there are gap warnings in the stitcher: "stitcher: missing-offset gap detected, dropping N fragments". Temporary workaround provided: Customer reduced concurrency and enabled application-level buffering (hold fragments until final event). Request: Support asked for an engineering investigation into whether edge-proxy backpressure triggers drop of partially-committed fragments and whether stitcher heuristics can be relaxed for dedicated pools.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:45 - DialogueAI (customer): Provided sample curl script and browser trace showing throttle; attached truncated output and timestamps.
2026-03-12 15:02 - DialogueAI (customer): Applied suggested mitigations; partial improvement but still seeing one in ~10 streams affected. Asked for ETA on permanent fix.
Hypothesis A: Edge proxy coalescing + upstream backpressure leads to partial fragment write that is GC'd by stitcher on reconnect. Check proxy buffer window and flush semantics.
Hypothesis B: Stitcher uses strict offset continuity; in dedicated pool with heavy KV-cache hits, re-attach can jump offsets and the heuristic treats the mismatch as duplication risk and drops fragments.
Actions taken: reproduced with supplied throttle script; captured runtime trace with debug stitcher logs; instrumented fragment-hold-time metric (pending PR).
Dashboards referenced: Streaming Latency (console/streams/us-east), stitcher-error-rate (grafana), edge-proxy-buffer-occupancy (grafana).
Related PRs/branches: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4218 (instrumentation); follow-up patch planned to tweak stitch_timeout and add tolerant reordering window.
Linked tickets: SUP-4721 (similar SSE resume truncation reported previously), SUP-72401 (orphan end-event after browser refresh behind proxy).
In Progress - Engineering to land a two-part change: (1) increase stitcher tolerance window from 150ms to 500ms on dedicated pools and expose feature flag; (2) modify edge-proxy to flush partially accumulated fragments when a resume/reconnect is detected. Temporary mitigation (customer applied): lower keepalive and enable buffer-forwarding on proxy which reduced incidence from ~10% to ~3%. Next steps: land PR 4218 for metrics, follow with PR to add tolerant stitching behavior, schedule patch in canary for us-east. If successful, roll to Dedicated pools. No customer data loss has been logged beyond truncated user-visible output.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We observed a regional throughput degradation in us-east for a dedicated customer (MapleMaps Inc.). The autoscaler did not provision additional GPU capacity despite sustained increases in queued requests from the customer's service. Root cause appears correlated with a pattern of many low-volume, long-lived prefetch/keepalive connections originating from the customer's SDK that suppress normal allocator heartbeats ("quiet fanout").

Impact:
- Customer MapleMaps reported elevated generation latency and a 30% drop in sustained throughput for their dedicated pool starting 2026-03-13 15:10 UTC.
- Platform p95 generation latency for affected routes rose from ~220ms to ~1.1s; p99 increased to ~2.6s.
- Autoscaler showed no scale-out events for ~28 minutes during increased queue pressure.

Environment:
- prod-us-east dedicated pool (reserved capacity cluster: dp-us-east-42)
- Tenant: maple-prod-01 (dedicated)
- Observed across two pinned models: gpt-3.5-redwood-v1 and llama2-13b-q4

Timeline (abridged):
- 2026-03-13 14:58 UTC: baseline (p95 ~220ms).
- 2026-03-13 15:10 UTC: customer reported degraded responsiveness.
- 2026-03-13 15:12 UTC: internal metric alert: allocator-utilization up, free GPU credits dropping, queued requests rising.
- 2026-03-13 15:20–15:40 UTC: autoscaler logs show repeated small connection heartbeats causing slot-marking with minimal payload; no scale decisions triggered.
- 2026-03-13 15:46 UTC: initial triage and mitigation steps applied (temporarily increased slot eviction aggressiveness).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1. Customer opens many long-lived prefetch or keepalive streams with low per-request token counts.
2. These streams maintain pinned lightweight reservations and suppress allocator heartbeat deltas used by autoscaler heuristics.
3. Real work requests queue behind many quiet streams; autoscaler does not perceive sustained CPU/GPU pressure and refrains from scaling.

Logs / Metrics / Evidence:
- Autoscaler decision log excerpt (15:22 UTC): "no_scale - heartbeat_delta < threshold - active_slots=128 - quiet_streams_detected=94"
- Allocator telemetry: GPU_credits_available fell from 82 -> 25 over 18 minutes; slot_reservation_failure rate increased.
- Traces: several client connection IDs repeatedly appear with keepalive pings and <32 token requests, holding slots for average 4.2s each.
- Customer-side SDK logs (sanitized) attached in support ticket bundle: repeated prefetches every 250ms from the same host group.

Hypothesis:
- The customer's SDK prefetch logic creates a high-count of persistent, low-throughput streams. These streams appear as active reservation slots but do not trigger autoscaler metrics for actual GPU utilization, causing a perception of capacity headroom while work queues. Result is effective GPU depletion (shortage) and noisy-neighbor symptom where quiet-fanout prevents scale-out.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Increased autoscaler sensitivity to queued-request growth for the affected cluster (temporary lowering of heartbeat_delta threshold).
- Adjusted slot eviction policy to free slots held by streams with <50 tokens processed and >30s idle.
- Engaged customer to throttle prefetch cadence (requested change in SDK).

Next steps / follow-ups:
- SRE to run a targeted autoscaler heuristic update: add explicit detection of high-count low-throughput connections and weight queued-request delta more heavily (tracked in GH PR #5483).
- Product to consult with SDK team about adding a prefetch rate limiter and an SDK flag to mark prefetch streams as low-priority (opt-in).
- Run a one-hour canary of the autoscaler heuristic tweak in us-east staging and measure p95/p99 improvements.
- Schedule a joint RCA with MapleMaps within 48 hours to review SDK changes and confirm remediation.

Customer impact and communication plan:
- Customer experienced degraded tail latency and lower throughput for ~40 minutes; no data loss.
- Support notified customer at 15:18 UTC and provided the temporary mitigation steps taken.
- Follow-up customer advisory proposed: recommended SDK change + config knobs for prefetch behavior and keepalive timeout defaults.

Status: Investigation ongoing. Working with SRE and SDK teams on a short-term autoscaler patch and a customer-side SDK fix.

2026-03-13 15:40 - SRE (Liam Chen): Observed high count of long-lived streams with minimal tokens. Hypothesis: quiet fanout holding slot reservations. Pushed temporary slot-eviction change to dp-us-east-42.
2026-03-13 16:05 - Support (Aisha Gomez): Informed MapleMaps that we applied a mitigation and asked them to throttle prefetch cadence. Customer replied they can toggle prefetch to 1s from 250ms as a test.
2026-03-13 18:02 - SRE (Liam Chen): Autoscaler sensitivity patch merged to internal canary branch (gh:5483). Observed p95 drop back to ~240ms in canary; will roll to staging for 1 hour.
2026-03-14 09:10 - Product (Sofia Martinez): Flagged SDK product owner to evaluate prefetch rate limiter and low-priority stream marker. Adding to SDK backlog with target s-1 release.
2026-03-14 12:40 - Support (Aisha Gomez): Customer confirmed improved behavior after throttling prefetch; planning SDK change and will monitor. Marking ticket In Progress until autoscaler patch fully validated.
Temporary mitigations freed capacity and customer-side throttling improved throughput. Autoscaler heuristic patch in canary; pending full rollout after staging validation. SDK change planned.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer ByteDock reported intermittent requests being served by the legacy model variant during a weighted-slice rollout that should have preserved per-tenant pinned versions. The symptom is sudden, short-lived 'fallback' occurrences where tenant sessions temporarily receive responses from the older variant (rw-inference-compat-1.2) despite an explicit pin to open-llama-70b-q4.

Impact:
- Affects a subset of tenants on ByteDock's dedicated capacity (prod-us-east).
- Visible as incorrectly routed responses for ~1-3 minute windows, recurring across a 48 minute rollout window.
- Customer reports quality degradation for affected requests; estimated 2-5% of requests for some tenants during windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated fleet: prod-us-east, reserved capacity pool rdw-ded-04
- Control plane: orchestrator v2.18.3; edge-proxy v1.5.9; serving-runtime v3.4.1
- Model variants: rw-inference-compat-1.2 (legacy) and open-llama-70b-q4 (new)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start weighted-slice rollout (50% -> 100%) for tenant group A using orchestrator promotion job.
2) Orchestrator writes snapshot to control-plane and pushes route update to edge-proxy.
3) Between snapshot_commit and edge propagation, some requests are observed hitting legacy variant for pinned tenants.

Logs / Evidence snippets:
- Edge routing log (03:12:07 UTC) - tenant t-8892: route_choice=legacy_variant, pin_lookup=explicit(open-llama-70b-q4), snapshot_version=20260310-0311
- Orchestrator commit timeline: commit_start=03:10:52 UTC, snapshot_write=03:11:01 UTC, snapshot_swap=03:11:19 UTC
- Metric: fallback_rate for tenant cohort jumped from baseline 0.3% to 4.8% between 03:11 and 03:14 UTC (dashboards/grafana/dashboard?id=fallback-rate&panel=7)

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:10 UTC - Eng (Orchestrator): Deployed staging patch to make snapshot swap atomic; scheduled canary to assess durability. Noted this ticket will be updated after canary results.
Hypothesis 1: Orchestrator snapshot write completed but edge propagation read an intermediate control-plane state before snapshot swap completed, causing a mismatch between pin map and active route mapping (observed 'slab gap').
Hypothesis 2: Edge-proxy cache TTL on route metadata is shorter than pin-lease acknowledgement window, enabling a brief window where the pin map read returns older cohort assignment.
Evidence: Correlated timestamps show a 18s window between snapshot_write and snapshot_swap. Multiple edge servers reported route metadata with snapshot_version equal to pre-commit value during that window. The fallback spikes align with that window across >3 edge instances.
Testing: Replayed orchestrator snapshot write with debugging instrumentation in staging; reproduced slab gap when snapshot swap used non-atomic replace. Reproduction steps attached in staging runbook (confluence link).
Customer-specific factor: ByteDock's tenant pin TTL had been shortened (custom config) which increased sensitivity to transient snapshot inconsistencies.
Workaround (applied 2026-03-10 05:02 UTC): Applied X-Force-Pin header at edge for affected tenants to override route selection until control-plane patch applied.
Immediate fix (2026-03-12): Deployed orchestrator change that makes snapshot publication an atomic swap operation, eliminating the observed 18s slab gap during our staging and canary tests.
Edge hardening: Increased route metadata read-retry window and added a short pin-lease grace (300ms) at edge to avoid choosing a legacy variant when snapshot_version is within swap window.
Rollout notes: Patch released to canary pool at 09:00 UTC 2026-03-12, monitored for 2 hours (no recurrence), then promoted to prod pool at 11:20 UTC 2026-03-12. Post-deploy monitoring shows fallback_rate returned to baseline (<0.5%).
Follow-ups: (1) PR #4421 to merge atomic-swap into main and add e2e test covering snapshot atomicity. (2) Add alert to control-plane that triggers when snapshot_swap_latency > 5s. (3) Document tenant pin TTL guidance in runbook and notify dedicated customers about recommended TTLs.
Status: Fix deployed to production; monitoring continuing. Customer ByteDock notified and confirm reduction in incidents. Ticket will be closed after 72h stable observation window.
payload.summary: Intermittent pinned-version flip during weighted-slice rollout due to orchestrator snapshot gap

Issue summary:
AtlasFin (enterprise customer) needs a custom, near-real-time Kafka-based audit export for their SOC and billing teams. Requirements: encrypted topic using customer-scoped KMS keys, per-event HMAC prefix (for independent integrity checks), each event must include a SAML session_id and user_handle mapping so AtlasFin can correlate sessions back to their IdP; produce a daily CSV reconciliation file that maps Redwood event offsets to AtlasFin invoice line items for the billing team.

Impact:
- SOC team cannot complete incident reconstruction exercises without session correlation.
- Billing team reports a ~0.6% discrepancy for a 7-day window that they believe is due to missing/incomplete event metadata.
- Customer requires SOC2 evidence for this deliverable within 48 hours.

Environment:
- Production tenant: atlasfin-prod (customer-scoped)
- Region: us-east-1
- Expected throughput: ~350 events/s during business hours (peaks up to 1k/s)

Detailed request/acceptance criteria:
1) Provide a Kafka topic endpoint (TLS+SASL) that AtlasFin can pull from, or allow Redwood to push to their Kafka cluster.
2) All events must be encrypted at rest and in transit; Redwood must sign per-event HMAC (first 8 bytes hex) computed with a KMS-backed key that AtlasFin can verify.
3) Each event must carry session linkage fields: saml_session_id, idp_assertion_id, user_handle, and an internal offset_to_invoice field that we will populate for reconciliation.
4) Deliver a daily CSV mapping file: [event_timestamp, kafka_offset, saml_session_id, user_handle, model_id(optional), token_count, billed_amount_cents]. CSV should be available in the customer's S3 bucket with a manifest and MD5 checksum.
5) Provide an audit evidence package (doc + sample of 10 signed events) showing key rotation policy and verification steps for AtlasFin audit team.

- Asked for a 24-hour dry-run with redacted PII before full delivery.

Notes on compliance:

Requested timeline:

- Dry-run delivery of 1000 redacted events + reconciliation CSV in 48 hours.

Action items: (1) add offset_to_invoice metadata during write path, (2) instrument HMAC header, (3) produce sample CSV for last 72h and reconcile against AtlasFin billing ledger. (C) Compliance evidence: Provide key fingerprints, HMAC verification script, and a 1-page attestation confirming key rotation cadence. Issue summary:
Customer ScribeAI reports sustained 429 responses across a subset of API keys immediately following a tenant credit reconciliation event (automatic refill) that occurred 2026-03-10 00:05 UTC. The tenant was simultaneously running a long-running bulk embedding backfill and high-frequency webhook-driven chat inference for low-latency UI actions.

- Real-time chat flows experienced user-visible failures; bulk backfill jobs retried and slowed throughput.
- Appears to affect only requests routed via the dedicated pool in us-east.

Requested outcome:
- Root cause analysis and mitigation to avoid recurrence during future credit refills and autosyncs.
- Guidance / recommended config to isolate bulk backfills from low-latency routes (rate classes, burst pools, or route separation).
1) On a dedicated tenant with scheduled midnight credit refill, kick off a large parallel bulk embedding job (1000 concurrent workers) against the embeddings endpoint.
2) At the same time, run simulated user traffic: 200 RPS of short chat requests (streaming) using multiple short-lived API keys and websocket sessions.
3) Observe behavior immediately after automatic credit refill / tenant reconciliation (00:00-00:10 UTC window).

Issue summary:
Customer reports that during long SSE streams the final closing delimiter ("[DONE]" metadata marker used by their client) is never received after an edge health-check swap. The response body contains the final sentence truncated in the middle of a paragraph.

Impact:
- Intermittent content loss for a small subset of long-running streams (estimated ~0.2% of streams for the affected customer)
- Customer application treats stream as incomplete and triggers retries which double downstream token costs

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod-us-east) hitting edge-gateway cluster behind FastEdge load balancer
- Customer using dedicated account with pinned model redwood-v1-large, streaming via SSE over TLS

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Open SSE connection using client X with keepalive every 30s
2) Start generation that runs for >45s and includes multi-paragraph output with final delimiter marker
3) Observe that when an edge health-check probe causes connection handover, the client does not receive the final marker and the last paragraph may be cut mid-sentence

Observed behavior:
- Final bytes of the stream appear truncated (cut after a punctuation mark)
- No end-of-stream metadata marker is seen in the SSE stream
- Server logs show connection teardown around the same timestamp as an HTTP/1.1 health probe on the edge node

Expected behavior:
- Stream should include all generated tokens and the closing delimiter metadata event even if the underlying edge connection is rotated or health-probed

Relevant logs/snippet (redacted):
- Customer client trace: "2026-03-12T18:07:12Z SSE CHUNK: "...and finally we recommend updating your policy.""
- Connection closed without [DONE] marker at 2026-03-12T18:07:12.342Z
- Edge proxy log: "probe=health path=/_edge/health reused_conn=false swap_to=10.3.4.22:443 RST_SENT"
- Serving runtime: "session_id=abc123 drain_timeout=0.150 connection_half_closed=true last_kv_commit=1598"

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Short term: switch to a short client-side timeout + polite retry that requests a small context resume (application-level fallback)
- Avoid edge path rewriting by using regional endpoint (us-east.direct.redwood.example) until fix is deployed

Notes:
- Customer supplied multiple traces and the timestamps correlate with edge health-checks that happen every 30s on a subset of our FastEdge fleet
- Not all probes cause the issue; looks correlated with probe that triggers a connection swap while there is in-flight buffered SSE data

Hypothesis B: Certain TLS session resumption / 0-RTT behavior on the FastEdge node can cause half-close semantics that our serving runtime treats as terminal before emitting the metadata marker. Investigating TLS handshake logs.

Root cause: Edge health-check swap could preemptively reset a connection mid-chunk flush. The aggressive connection rotation logic in edge-proxy v2.1.7 reduced the drain grace window; when probe coincided with buffered SSE data, the TCP shutdown semantics caused clients to miss the final metadata marker.
Fix implemented: edge-proxy patch (PR #512) increases drain grace window for streaming endpoints and ensures explicit flush of SSE chunk queue before any RST path is taken. Also added a probe-tag to stream logs for easier correlation.
