Customer (Lattice Financial) reports that during the 2025-11-07 us-east degradation they experienced elevated errors and streaming disconnects, but our public status page showed "Operational" for the relevant timeframe. Customer is requesting (a) confirmation that Redwood recognizes the outage and (b) clarification on why the status page did not reflect the impact.

Issue summary:
- Customer observed: intermittent 5xx/stream resets on streaming chat completions in us-east; elevated end-user error rates.
- Redwood status page observed by customer: "All Systems Operational" (no component marked degraded/outage until after their peak impact window).
- Customer concern: status page is too coarse (global/hosted API only) and/or incorrectly classified impact (streaming vs non-streaming, per-region impact not reflected).

Impact (customer-reported):
- Duration: ~20–30 minutes (approx 16:05–16:35 UTC per customer); residual retries for another ~10 minutes.
- Symptoms: SSE stream dropped mid-response; some requests returned 502/504; retries succeeded.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions (stream=true).

What we need to do:
1) Validate the timeframe and whether our internal incident timeline matches customer evidence.
2) Provide a customer-facing explanation for the status page mismatch without disclosing sensitive capacity/customer-specific details.
3) Capture action items feeding into the status page transparency upgrades project (component taxonomy + signal mapping + comms process).

Customer-provided artifacts (summarized):
- Request IDs: LF-7b2c1e, LF-7b2c33, LF-7b2c8a (sample)
- Error codes: 502/504; stream disconnect without final event.
- Region: us-east only (customer also has low-volume eu-west traffic not impacted).

Internal notes:
- Internal incident opened: INC-2025-1107-USE1-STREAMING (SRE).
- Public status page components at time were too coarse (Hosted API global), and our automated classifier did not mark the correct component/region promptly.
- Known gap tracked by SRE: inability to represent "Streaming (us-east)" separately from "Hosted API"; led to delayed and ambiguous external comms.

Requested outcome for closure:
- Provide written acknowledgement + corrected timeline to customer.
- Share our planned improvements: new component granularity (product surface + region), standard comms templates, and faster time-to-first-update goals.
- Confirm whether any post-incident summary will be published and when.

Additional notes:
Resolved customer dispute by providing verified internal incident timeline and acknowledging a status page mismatch due to overly coarse components and incomplete streaming/region signal mapping. Customer accepted explanation. Follow-ups captured for the status page transparency upgrades initiative: implement per-capability/per-region components (including Streaming us-east), improve signal-to-component mapping to prevent misclassification, and standardize incident update templates + approval flow for faster time-to-first-update.

Issue summary: Customer noticed a single, high-value embedding invoice line dated 2026-03-08 for ~1.2M tokens (~$4,200) attributed to their production org. Customer insists the load originated from a staging service that should be excluded from billing.\n\nImpact: One unexpected invoice line causing a customer-facing billing surprise and an open support escalation with finance. Customer paused automatic renewals pending clarification.\n\nEnvironment: LexiQ Health production org (org_id: org_lexiq_prod). Requests in question appear under api_key prefixes matching their historical staging naming convention (stg-*) but were recorded under the production org in postback logs. Region: us-east-1. Model: text-embedding-3-large.\n\nSteps to reproduce (customer-provided):\n1) Nightly batch job on 2026-03-08 ran an internal staging reindex using keys named stg-reindex-01 -> reported 2026-03-09 when invoice generated.\n2) Customer verifies the key was a staging key that had been deleted on 2026-02-25 and should not have been active.\n3) Customer sees the usage line on the monthly invoice for period ending 2026-03-08.\n\nObserved billing lines: Invoice ID INV-LEXIQ-20260308 line item: text-embedding-3-large, 1,204,320 tokens, charge $4,212.48, note: \"metered usage (postback reconciler v2)\".\n\nExpected behavior: Staging keys that are flagged as non-billable (stg- prefix & tag:environment=staging) should be ignored by the billing pipeline and not attributed to production orgs.\n\nInitial hypothesis: Postback reconciler v2 introduced a relaxed key-to-org mapping regex during the 2026-02-20 change, which may have allowed deleted / staging key signatures to remap to the most recent matching org.\n\nImmediate customer request: Temporary reversal of the invoice line while we investigate, and an explanation of why deleted staging keys were billed.

2026-03-10 10:05 — LexiQ Health (customer): Provided invoice PDF and the deleted key prefixes: stg-reindex-01, stg-reindex-02. Confirm key deletion timestamp: 2026-02-25 03:11 UTC. Asked for immediate provisional credit if possible.

Issue summary:
Customer reported that their Private deployment control plane entered a sustained authentication retry loop after a scheduled peering change between two AWS accounts. The control-plane agents show repeated 407 Proxy Authentication Required responses when attempting token refresh and artifact fetches, which triggers accelerated retry backoff and a surge of outbound attempts.

Impact:
- Agent heartbeats from ~40 serving nodes in customer us-east private deployment were intermittently marked unhealthy and cycled (30-60s).
- Model pulls timed out intermittently causing request errors (429/502 depending on path).
- Customer reports production traffic >5% error rate for 45 minutes during peak hours.

Environment:
- Customer: Nimbus Retail Inc. (private deployment, VPC peering between account A and B)
- Redwood Private control plane (managed) in us-east-1
- Agents running on customer-managed serving nodes in peered VPC (account B)
- Corporate egress proxy sits in account A and is expected to handle outbound web auth for peered subnets

Steps to reproduce (as observed):
1) Customer applied new route table to peered VPC (account B) that removed explicit propagation for the control-plane CIDR and replaced with a 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop to a customer appliance.
2) Agents attempted token refresh to control-plane endpoint (controlplane.redwood.internal -> resolved to IP in account A).
3) Packets from serving hosts in account B were routed to the appliance in account B (0.0.0.0/0) instead of traversing the peering path to account A, creating asymmetric path and hitting the corporate web-proxy cluster that expects requests to be authenticated via a different header exchange.
4) Proxy returned 407 responses; agents retried rapidly due to our token-refresh backoff being reset by the intermittent 407s, leading to a storm of auth attempts and control-plane retries.

Observed logs/snippets:
- Agent logs (serving-node-12): "token_refresh: received 407 Proxy Authentication Required; proxy-id=corp-proxy-7; content='Proxy-Authenticate: Negotiate'"
- Control plane logs: "auth: token invalidation from 10.12.5.20: excessive retries -> escalate"
- VPC flow logs: show SYN->RST from appliance IP for control-plane target IP; no direct peering path entries for account B->account A after route change.

Hypothesis:
Route table update in customer account B created a default route that diverted traffic destined for the control plane through a local appliance/proxy rather than the VPC peering path. The corporate proxy inserts/mandates an authentication handshake (407) that our agents don't perform, resulting in failed token refreshes and retry storms. Asymmetric routing also caused some TCP session resets for artifact downloads.

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed route table in account B now has 0.0.0.0/0 -> appliance ENI and no explicit routes for control-plane CIDR; peering connection still exists and routes were previously propagated.
- Customer's network team admits they toggled route propagation as part of a security baseline change; they believed traffic to account A would still prefer peering due to local route priority but omitted the explicit CIDR entry.
- Turned on DEBUG on agent token refresh path; agents do not attempt Proxy-Authenticate flows and treat 407 as a failure class similar to 4xx.
- Verified that when we manually injected a host route (control-plane CIDR -> peering ENI) from customer side, agent heartbeats returned to normal and token refresh succeeded.

Customer communications:
- 2026-03-10 10:22 UTC: Notified customer we are investigating; requested recent route table and peering acceptance logs.
- 2026-03-10 10:45 UTC: Customer confirmed they applied a baseline route policy 10:30 UTC.
- 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC: Provided mitigation steps to add explicit host route for control-plane CIDR; customer applied host route at 11:12 UTC.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Customer added explicit route for control-plane CIDR (172.20.64.0/21) -> peering connection.
- We issued a soft-throttle on agent token refresh backoff logic for customer cluster to avoid token-storm (configuration change on control plane to raise retry jitter for 20 minutes).

Root cause:
- Route-propagation change on customer's side removed explicit control-plane prefix route, causing asymmetric egress through corporate appliance that enforces proxy auth. Agents do not perform proxy authentication, so token refreshes fail with 407 and trigger retry storms.

Resolution / next steps:
1) Customer restored explicit route to peering for control-plane CIDR (immediate resolution).
2) Networking runbook updated (confluence) to require explicit CIDR route for Redwood control-plane prefixes when applying route propagation changes. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/5021/Peering+Runbook
3) Follow-up: engineering to add a defensive check in agent startup that validates direct reachability to control-plane IPs and warns if a proxy is in-path. Tracking PR: github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1482 (owner: @liamoc).
4) Recommend customer add an egress-scope ACL that allows peering CIDR -> control-plane CIDR priority above default appliance route.

Impact window and timeline:
- 2026-03-10 10:30-11:15 UTC: peak errors; mitigation applied 11:12 UTC, full healthy state by 11:25 UTC.

Notes for postmortem: include suggestion to extend agent telemetry to detect 407/407-like proxy signs sooner and surface a clear "proxy-in-path" alert in Console.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:47 UTC - Nimbus NetOps (customer): We made a route propagation change to tighten outbound routing; didn't expect it to affect peering to account A.
2026-03-11 09:15 UTC - Engineering (Liam O'Connor): Created PR to add early-probe reachability check in agent and a control-plane-side flag to slow refresh jitter if many 4xx/407 observed. PR link included in related_github_prs.
payload.summary: Peered VPC route-table propagation mismatch causes control-plane auth loop via corporate proxy 407 responses

Issue summary:
Customer reports that calls to the embeddings endpoint intermittently return responses whose metadata (embedding_id and "namespace") do not match the payload order. Downstream reranker sees out-of-order candidate metadata and falls back to a CPU path, causing 2-6x tail latency spikes.

Impact:
- Affected customer: NimbleDocs (dedicated).
- Production traffic: rerank latency tail increases from ~120ms to 800-2,400ms during incidents.
- Result: UX timeouts in their search UI and elevated error rates reported by customer monitoring.

Environment:
- Redwood prod environment (vpc-dedicated) servicing NimbleDocs dedicated pool.
- Observed in us-east primary region; cascade effects seen in eu-west for cross-region traffic.

Observed behavior:
- Embeddings API returns batches where embedding payload order does not match embedding metadata array order in the JSON response (embedding_id / namespace misaligned).
- Reranker logs show candidate-to-metadata mismatches and triggers CPU fallback which increases tokenization and scoring latency.

Why this is critical:
- Dedicated customers rely on deterministic mapping between embeddings and metadata for correctness. Out-of-order metadata breaks top-k stability and increases latency and 5xxs.

1) Use NimbleDocs account credentials and call POST /v1/embeddings with batch size 16 and client-supplied ids (embed_ids array) against prod us-east endpoint.
2) Immediately call POST /v1/rerank with the returned embeddings and matching ids in the same order.
3) Observe rerank score instability and tail latency >1s in ~1/200 requests.
4) Compare embedding_id order in embeddings response JSON to original request order; intermittently they differ.
5) Reproduce frequency increases when client uses parallelized client-side batching across multiple TCP connections.
6) Re-run traffic routed to eu-west after cross-region test to observe propagated latency.

[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] reranker: candidate-metadata-lookup mismatch for request id1 -> metadata id3; triggering cpu_fallback=true; score_path=cpu; latency_ms=1203

Maya Chen (Support) [2026-03-10]: Logged on behalf of NimbleDocs. Provided initial request/response body samples and a HAR capture. Customer seeing intermittent top-k noise and large latency spikes.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) [2026-03-10]: Assigned for triage. Initial hypothesis: parallel connection reuse + protobuf/gRPC muxing bug in embeddings-service response packing. Requesting pcap and exact client SDK version from customer.
NimbleDocs Support (customer) [2026-03-11]: Sent client SDK v0.9.3 and load pattern (16 concurrent workers, batches of 16). Observed peak on weekdays 09:00-11:00 ET.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) [2026-03-11]: Replayed traffic in staging using same SDK and concurrency. Unable to reproduce with single-region internal staging (no reorder). Enabled verbose logging in embeddings-service to capture response assembly ordering.
Priya Singh (Backend Eng) [2026-03-12]: Found a reassembly code path in embeddings-service that uses an async aggregator; under high concurrency a map iteration was non-deterministic. Patch PR prepared to enforce deterministic ordering by capturing original request index.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) [2026-03-12]: Deployed hotfix to canary in us-east. Observed reduction in reorder metric from 0.78% -> 0.02% in 2-hour window. Requesting extended verification from NimbleDocs on their traffic spike window.
NimbleDocs Support (customer) [2026-03-13]: Confirmed dramatic reduction in wrong-metadata events and tail latency; still seeing rare spikes (~1/20k). Customer requests RCA and long-term fix timeline.
Priya Singh (Backend Eng) [2026-03-13]: PR #8421 contains deterministic index tracking; additional integration tests added for parallel clients. Scheduling full rollout to dedicated pools after QA signoff.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) [2026-03-13]: Marking as in-progress. Need to verify eu-west replica behavior and update canary config to include a cross-region test. Linking to INT-1203 for router investigation.
Hypothesis: non-deterministic iteration over map/aggregation buffer in embeddings-service async aggregator produced response arrays with permuted order under concurrent writes.
Evidence: Staging replay with same SDK and concurrency produced identical symptom only after enabling interleaved response assembly; disabling connection pooling removed symptom.
Root cause seems to be a race in response assembly when multiple write goroutines append to a shared slice without preserving client-provided indices.
Related observation: envoy/upstream connection reuse and HTTP/2 stream multiplexing increased the window for concurrent assembly; router metrics show slight increase in stream resets for some backends.
Change introduced in commit ab12f3 (async aggregator refactor) likely introduced the bug; PR referenced below reintroduces stable ordering by tracking original request positions.
Residual rare spikes may be caused by cross-region replication lag when eu-west reranker pulls cached metadata and experiences transient inconsistency; further investigation with regional cache invalidation required.

Hotfix deployed to canary in us-east (2026-03-12): embeddings-service updated to preserve client-specified index positions during async aggregation. Canary metrics: reorder rate fell from 0.78% to 0.02%. Pending full rollout to all dedicated pools and cross-region verification. Follow-up work: INT-1203 to examine router connection pooling settings and an integration test added to CI for multi-connection client replay. Customer notified and will receive final RCA and change window for scheduled rollout.

Issue summary: Customer reports periodic sharp throughput drops in their dedicated pool (us-west) between 09:30-10:15 UTC. Symptoms include rising p50/p95/p99 latencies, increased 5xx errors, and transient GPU attach failures. Impact: production inference jobs observe a 40-60% p50 throughput collapse for 10-20 minute windows, affecting user-facing latency-sensitive endpoints. Environment: prod, dedicated pool us-west, affected cluster: redcap-prod-dc-05.
Customer-visible latency spikes and failed requests on chat and embed routes. Business impact: degraded UX for automated chat assistants and delayed embeddings ingestion for nightly jobs. No data loss observed but SLAs at risk during windows.
prod-us-west (redcap-prod-dc-05), dedicated pool for Nimbus AI, pool config: reserved nodes 8 (A100), autoscaler policy: balanced-latency, prewarm=true
1) Run sustained chat traffic at ~750 concurrent short streams for 15 minutes to the customer's pinned model (redwood-7b). 2) Increase a secondary analytics connector (customer-side collector) load on same tenant by starting long-running micro-batches that hold GPU memory. 3) Observe allocator backlog and GPU attach retries between 2-12 minutes after load begins.
[2026-03-10T09:37:12Z] allocator: attach-retry backoff for tenant=nimbus-123, reason=OOM-reserve-fallback
[2026-03-10T09:39:45Z] node-monitor: thermal-headroom drop detected on gpu0 -> frequency-capping -> fallback-mode=slow-path
[2026-03-10T09:41:02Z] serving-runtime: session-keepalive holding 3.2GB persistent alloc from sidecar-analytics (pid=8123)
- GPU utilization: nominal at 42% for compute but memory occupancy climbed to 92% on affected nodes.
- p50 latency increased from 60ms to 170ms; p99 spikes to 2.3s.
- allocator attach-failures increased (attach-error-rate +600% during window).
- autoscaler did not scale up due to short-lived oscillation window (scale-up hysteresis hit).
Initial triage by Tier-1 support found correlation between customer analytics connector rollout at 09:30 and onset of throughput degradation. SRE reproduced with staged load: a long-lived micro-batch process that performs vectorization on the node's sidecar was pinning GPU memory and preventing quick reallocation. Monitoring shows frequency capping due to thermal headroom losses, which forces the runtime into a slow-path that increases per-token latency. Autoscaler sensitivity combined with short windows prevented immediate scaling action. Hypothesis: a memory-occupancy leak from the customer's analytics side-process plus thermal throttling cascaded into allocation failures and autoscaler non-action.
Evidence: node-exporter traces, device-mapper logs, and the customer's process list show persistent allocations from a non-inference process. Device temperatures increased ~7C shortly before frequency capping events.
A customer-side analytics sidecar (long-lived micro-batch) intermittently holds persistent CUDA allocations on a shared dedicated node. Those allocations raise memory occupancy and cause thermal headroom reduction. The serving runtime detects reduced headroom and switches to a conservative slow-path; combined with autoscaler hysteresis tuned for longer windows, this produces ephemeral GPU thinness and attach failures. Not an issue in CPU-only or private deployments where processes are isolated.
1) Support applied a pool-level eviction policy to forcibly drain sessions flagged as non-inference for the Nimbus tenant during the window. 2) SRE increased autoscaler aggressiveness for the affected pool (shortened scale-up cooldown from 5m to 60s) as an emergency measure. 3) We requested the customer to disable the analytics sidecar or reduce its memory retention for the next 24h. These steps restored throughput within ~6 minutes of the intervention.
Workaround held: temporary eviction rules and autoscaler cooldown reduction prevented recurrence during the follow-up 48h monitoring window. For a long-term fix, engineering will: (a) add guardrails to detect and evict non-inference CUDA allocations in dedicated pools, (b) surface tenant-level memory-occupancy alerts in the Console with automated suggested actions, and (c) implement autoscaler policy that reacts to memory-occupancy signals in addition to request queue depth. Customer updated their analytics connector to use host-side batching (no persistent CUDA alloc) and confirmed stable throughput.
- ENG: implement non-inference allocation detection (ticket ENG-34521).
- SRE: create runbook for thermal-headroom-induced slow-path with kill/evict thresholds and emergency autoscaler override.
- DX: add Console alert with remediation steps for customers who run side-processes.
- CS: schedule postmortem call with Nimbus AI on 2026-03-16 to review changes and confirm SLA posture.
2026-03-10T10:02Z - Miguel Santos (SRE): Confirmed persistent CUDA allocations from a non-inference pid on node redcap-prod-05-gpu0. Captured process stack and sampled memory map.
2026-03-10T10:18Z - Nimbus AI (Customer): We've just rolled a new analytics agent this morning. We'll roll it back to the previous image and report back.
Customer provided stacktrace showing CUDA calls from their agent.
2026-03-10T10:43Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Applied emergency evict rule to remove processes with tag 'sidecar-analytics' from serving nodes for Nimbus tenant. Observed throughput return within 4-6 minutes.
2026-03-11T08:30Z - Erica Zhang (Eng): Scheduled implementation plan for allocator detection in ENG-34521. Will prototype detection algorithm that differentiates inference sessions from background CUDA allocators.
2026-03-12T15:12Z - Miguel Santos (SRE): Lowered autoscaler scale-up cooldown on redcap-prod-dc-05 as temporary safety net. Monitoring continues; no recurrences in 36h.
2026-03-13T09:05Z - Nimbus AI (Customer): Confirmed analytics connector update removed persistent allocations. Performance stable during morning peak. Thank you.

Issue summary: Around 02:00 UTC on 2026-03-10 SolarAxis observed duplicate billing callback completions for their daily reconciliation job. Impact: duplicate 'payment_succeeded' callbacks caused downstream ledger to create duplicate provisional credits for 186 customers in the 02:00-02:15 window. Customer escalated to CS at 09:05 local and requested immediate mitigation and crediting plan.
Customer-facing billing mismatch leading to incorrect provisional credits and two customers reporting incorrect available balance. Business impact: risk of financial exposure and loss of trust; immediate request for retroactive reconciliation and credits.
Customer alert via support portal and automated billing discrepancy detector (rule: duplicate callbacks within 60s with different request ids). Pager alert fired for scheduler error rate spike at 02:12 UTC.
Initial triage: scheduler replay path was triggered by a chronos time-synchronization window on one scheduler replica. Root cause hypothesis: scheduler considered the 02:00 job missing when NTP offset crossed threshold during a rolling restart and invoked replay logic. Secondary failure: idempotency key was generated from a monotonic timestamp rather than stable request fingerprint, so duplicates bypassed billing dedupe. We reproduced locally by inducing 1.5s NTP offset and restarting the scheduler replica.

comments: 2026-02-28T10:12:00Z Alicia Ramos: Customer reported that scheduled alert notifications in Slack contained ‘View trace’ links that resolve to empty pages. Provided logs and a sample CSV export where trace_id column was blank.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
A VertexAI Labs dedicated account observed that scheduled alert backfills for dashboard-derived queries sometimes emit alert payloads where tracehook parameters are empty or missing. This removes trace links in notifications and prevents customers from clicking through to traces from alerts/exports.

Impact:
- Alerts delivered without tracehook context (trace_id/span_id) for a subset (~3-7%) of backfill runs over the last 48 hours.
- Scheduled CSV exports have rows missing tracehook columns, causing downstream tools to mark rows as incomplete.
- Customer-facing SLO for alert trace link availability dropped below threshold for scheduled alerts.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated pool) in us-east-1.
- Console v2026.02.18, Alerting worker group v4.3.1, Query-cache service v2.7.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer has a dashboard panel with a saved query that includes runtime tracehook injection (e.g. SELECT ... , '{{tracehook.params.trace_id}}' as trace_id).
2) Panel is used as a scheduled alert (backfill window enabled).
3) During a maintenance window the customer edits the saved panel (minor metadata change) which triggers saved-query reindex and cache eviction.
4) Shortly after, the scheduled backfill job runs (overlapping with the cache invalidation).
5) Alerts produced for the backfill contain empty trace_id/span_id fields.

Expected behavior:
Backfill/alert runs should always evaluate the saved query with runtime tracehook bindings restored and include tracehook parameters in emitted payloads. Cache invalidation should not cause loss of runtime binding information.

Observed behavior:
A race condition between saved-query cache eviction and the alert backfill scheduler causes the backfill runner to execute a prepared plan that does not rehydrate runtime tracehook placeholders; alert payloads emitted in that window have tracehook fields set to empty strings.

Relevant logs and errors:
- QueryCache: "miss: saved_query:panel-4821 -> prepare(plan_id=0x7f2a)"
- AlertRunner: "backfill_run_id=bf-20260228-34 skip_reason=param_binding_failed bindings_missing=[trace_id, span_id]"
- Console metrics: alert.tracehook.success_rate dropped from 99.6% to 92.1% during incident window

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced on staging by creating a saved panel with injected tracehook parameters, editing panel metadata to force reindex, then running a scheduled backfill; identical missing-params symptom observed.
- Root cause narrowed to query-cache's prepared-plan lifecycle: when a saved-query is evicted, a concurrent backfill may pick up a prepared plan handle that lacks the runtime-binding layer used by the console to substitute tracehook parameters.
- Race occurs when cache eviction->plan eviction happens between plan handle lookup and parameter binding step in the AlertRunner code path.
- Found a dangling optimization: prepared-plan pooling assumes immutable parameter schema; saved query edits can flip placeholder tokens from inline templating to compiled placeholder indices which some older plan paths don't rehydrate.
- Related PRs identified that overlap with the fix: console#14567 (ensure parameter rehydrate on cache-miss) and query-cache#14568 (serializes eviction to prevent reuse of stale handles).

Workarounds (customer-facing):
- Avoid editing saved panels that are on schedules/backfills during active backfill windows.
- Restarting the alerting worker group clears in-memory plan handles and forces fresh plan compilation; this mitigates immediate emissions but is disruptive.
- Temporarily disable scheduled backfill for affected panels until fix is deployed.

Resolution and rollout notes:
- Implemented fix that forces rehydration of runtime templating at query-eval time when plan lookup hits an eviction window (PR console#14567). Added serialization around plan eviction to prevent concurrent consumers from using stale handles (PR query-cache#14568).
- Changes were unit tested and staged to staging (staging build 2026-03-03).
- Hotfix deployed to prod on 2026-03-07 to the us-east dedicated pool with canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
- Post-deploy monitoring showed alert.tracehook.success_rate returned to baseline (99.7%) and VertexAI Labs reported no further missing tracehook events for scheduled alerts.

Postmortem actions / follow-ups:
- Add an integration test for scheduled backfills + saved-query-edit sequence to CI.
- Instrument query-cache metrics for concurrent eviction consumers.
- Add an alert for alert.tracehook.success_rate < 98% for 10m in prod.
- Customer success follow-up scheduled to confirm remediation and offer credits for missed links.

Additional notes:

2026-03-01 09:24 - SRE (Mei Chen): Reproduced on staging using reproduction steps. Observed param_binding_failed in AlertRunner logs. Suspect query-cache race. Opening INT ticket for deeper runtime tracing.
2026-03-03 15:02 - Eng (Devon Park): Created fix patch that forces parameter rehydrate on cache-miss (console#14567). Added serialization in query-cache flush path (query-cache#14568). Preparing staging deploy.
2026-03-07 03:45 - Eng (SRE): Hotfix deployed to prod us-east canary. Monitoring metrics for 2 hours; tracehook success rate recovered to 99.7%.
2026-03-10 12:10 - CS (Alicia Ramos): Customer confirmed no further missing tracehook links and accepted credit offer. Marking ticket resolved and capturing follow-up actions in Confluence.
Hotfix deployed (console#14567, query-cache#14568). Canary -> full rollout completed 2026-03-07; monitoring shows tracehook metrics recovered. CI test and alerting follow-ups created.
Add scheduled integration test covering saved-query edit + backfill; implement eviction-consumer metric; owner: Devon Park; target completion: 2026-04-01
A race in saved-query cache invalidation could cause some scheduled alerts and exports to be emitted without tracehook context (trace_id/span_id). A hotfix was deployed and the issue is resolved; customers affected were contacted and credits offered.
payload.summary: Saved query cache invalidation race causes scheduled alert backfill to omit tracehook parameters

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent p95 latency spikes and unexpected cross-region egress immediately after an availability-zone (AZ) failover in their us-east region. They believe regional pinning should prevent routing to eu-west but see a subset (~2-3%) of requests egressing to eu-west for ~10-20 minutes after the failover.

Impact: Elevated p95 for token generation (from ~120ms to ~720ms) for a portion of traffic; affects user-facing inference latency for BrightHealth AI clinical triage flow. No request failures observed, primarily latency degradation and higher egress cost.

Environment: Dedicated capacity, strict residency enabled (customer pinned to us-east), model redwood/open-7b-v1, production. AZ failover was triggered by a cloud provider maintenance event noted 2026-03-11 22:30 UTC.

Observed behavior: After the AZ failover, about 2-3% of requests for ~15 minutes were routed to eu-west serving nodes resulting in ~600ms additional network RTT and increased token latencies. DNS lookups from our edge proxies showed mixed A records pointing to us-east and eu-west.

Expected behavior: With strict residency + pin, all inference requests should remain within us-east and never egress to eu-west.

Customer-provided artifacts: sample request IDs and timestamps included in logs section.

1) Customer has strict residency toggled to 'us-east' in their tenant config on Dedicated.
2) Simulate an AZ-level capacity degradation or mark an AZ unhealthy in the load balancer (internal staging).
3) Send steady inference traffic pinned to redwood/open-7b-v1 at 100 req/s and monitor per-request egress region and p95 latency.
4) Observe whether a small percentage of requests are routed out-of-region for short windows after failover events.

DNS edge logs: at 22:30:58Z cached A for service-proxy.us-east had TTL=18s; on cache miss resolver returned two A records (us-east, eu-west) due to backend rollout state
Proxy trace: sticky session cookie present for 98% of sessions; tie-breaker weight used for node selection was 'least-loaded' and returned eu-west node for some requests during AZ reconvergence
BrightHealth AI (customer) - 2026-03-12: 'We see short bursts of requests hitting eu-west immediately after the AZ maintenance window. Can you confirm why pinning didn't keep traffic in us-east?'
Support (Aisha) - 2026-03-12: 'Thanks for the report — we're collecting traces and DNS responses. Can you share a couple of example request IDs? Also confirm if you have any per-tenant DNS overrides.'
Customer - 2026-03-12: 'Provided three request IDs via secure attachment. No custom DNS overrides on their side.'
SRE (Marco) - 2026-03-13: 'I've pulled edge resolver logs and observed transient mixed A responses from our control plane during AZ reconvergence. Opening INT-3421 to validate controller's tiebreaker behavior.'
Support - 2026-03-14: 'We've reproduced similar behavior in staging with simulated AZ failover. Hypothesis: DNS pool population and the runtime's node-selection tiebreaker sometimes choose a geographically-different peer during a short window despite strict tenancy pin, when in-AZ capacity is temporarily below per-node thresholds. Working on mitigation.'
Hypothesis 1: DNS/Resolver race — control plane briefly advertises nodes from neighboring regions while reconciling healthy us-east nodes, causing some resolvers to receive multi-region A sets.
Hypothesis 2: Node-selection tiebreaker weight prioritizes 'least-loaded' rather than strict residency during reconvergence; if us-east nodes are reporting heavy ephemeral load, tie-breaker picks eu-west node even for pinned requests.
Hypothesis 3: Sticky pin metadata TTL mismatch between edge caches and control plane leads to a window where edge cache returns stale negative for local nodes and triggers fallback to broader pool.
Staging reproduction: Simulated AZ outage in staging produced ~1.8% cross-region egress during 10-20s windows; matches customer magnitude after scaling reconverge delays are introduced.
Captured traces and resolver outputs saved to INT-3421 for deeper debugger session.
Mitigation steps provided to customer: (1) Recommended temporary worked-around config: increase residency pin health check thresholds to delay failover selection and set per-tenant node-selection policy to 'prefer-local' in Dedicated console. (2) SRE rolled a control-plane config change to prefer strict-region nodes over 'least-loaded' tie-breaker during reconvergence windows (INT-3421). (3) Shorter-term: edge resolver TTL alignment patch scheduled.

Follow-up actions: (a) ENG to ship control-plane fix to enforce 'region-stickiness' during reconverge (tracking PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rt/commit/af3b2c1) (b) QA to run AZ-failover chaos test against Dedicated fleets (owner: Marco Diaz) (c) CS to confirm with BrightHealth AI after config change.

Status: Workaround applied and control-plane config rolled to canary; monitoring shows cross-region egress reduced to <0.1% in canary ring. Customer informed and asked to validate traffic after next maintenance window.
payload.summary: Unclear routing determinism after AZ failover causing cross-region egress and latency spikes

Issue summary: BrightCart reports that during streaming client shutdowns (app crash or SIGTERM during an open stream), some in-flight function/tool calls are not being finalized on their backend webhooks and occasionally re-executed after client reconnects. Impact: duplicate side-effects in customer systems (order confirmations) and uncertainty about whether calls were committed or rolled back. Observed pattern appears correlated with short shutdown windows and clients that rely on SDK graceful-shutdown hooks. Customer expects deterministic at-most-once semantics or clear confirmation tokens to reconcile duplicates.
1) Start a long-running chat generation with an attached funcall to POST /webhook/order-confirm on redwood-2.7-small in us-east-1
2) Trigger a SIGTERM in the client within 200-800ms after the funcall is delivered but before the stream ack is received by the client
3) Restart the client (or reconnect) and resend without an explicit idempotency key in the funcall payload
4) Observe webhook receiving duplicate POSTs or an initial POST with no final confirmation, followed by a replay from the client or platform fallback.

2026-03-10T14:08:24Z stream_connection=client-78 dropped_by_client=SIGTERM code=CLIENT_SHUTDOWN
2026-03-10T14:08:26Z serving-runtime: outbound-webhook POST /webhook/order-confirm status=200 body_digest=sha256:ab12... confirmation_token=tok_f_3e9
2026-03-10T14:08:26Z platform-replay: funcall_id=fcall-7c3 replay_trigger=client-reconnect reason=unconfirmed_ack
2026-03-10T14:08:26Z outbound-webhook POST /webhook/order-confirm status=200 body_digest=sha256:ab12... confirmation_token=tok_f_3e9 (duplicate)
trace: https://traces.redwood-infra.internal/trace/rc-9a2f (internal)
edge-proxy: connection-id=conn-4bg chunked-header-truncate=false
Initial hypothesis: graceful-shutdown path in SDK closes stream before platform acks are reliably persisted to funcall-confirmation store.
Correlates with short shutdown windows where client does not wait for final confirmation frame over the stream (observed on both Go and Python SDKs).
Serving runtime shows outbound webhook returned 200 and confirmation_token generated, but client did not receive the final confirmation frame before disconnect. Platform replay logic then re-enqueued the funcall because confirmation metadata was not yet durable in the request ledger at time of disconnect.
Possible contributing factor: write ordering between webhook confirmation persistence and stream frame push; if persistence is async and ack frame send is raced with client disconnect, we can observe "unconfirmed_ack" state.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1893 addresses making confirmation write synchronous (experiment branch).
Telemetry: increased incidence when dedicated GPU pools experience GC/eviction events and when clients use SDK shutdown-timeout < 1s.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:17 - BrightCart (Anna Patel): Workaround tested: client waits for confirmation_token frame up to 3s before shutdown -> duplicates gone in our trials, but unacceptable latency for some flows.
In Progress: short-term mitigation (feature-flag to make confirmation persistence synchronous) scheduled for canary on BrightCart's dedicated pool. Customer advised to add a client-side confirmation wait of up to 3s as a stopgap. Long-term design work underway to implement a hybrid 'stub-first' confirmation write + idempotent replay suppression to avoid latency regressions.
Client-side: after receiving funcall.delivery event, block shutdown for up to configurable timeout (default 3000ms) waiting for funcall.confirmation frame. Server-side: enable feature-flag 'sync-confirmation-write' on dedicated pools to ensure confirmation durability before stream frame is considered committed.

2) SDK team to publish guidance snippet and small helper that exposes 'await_confirmation(timeout_ms=...)' in Go/Python/TS SDKs (owner: Priya Nair)
3) Eng to design hybrid persistence approach and open RFC (owner: Priya Nair)
4) CS to monitor BrightCart for duplicate webhook events for 72 hours post-canary (owner: Jordan Lee)

Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 ~09:12 UTC customer reports elevated p95/p99 inference latency and several streaming sessions that never yielded data (client observed stalled SSE chunks and eventual 504). The impact was concentrated on requests from eu-west customers routed via US egress, and on the customer's dedicated pool (CartaHealth-dedicated-us-east).

Impact:
- Multiple customers experienced long tails (p99 increased from 420ms to 3.7s) and intermittent streaming disconnects.
- Customer-visible errors: streaming disconnects (client-side idle reads) and occasional 504 gateway responses.
- Affected customer: CartaHealth (dedicated) — production traffic.

Environment:
- Prod (managed hosted) with dedicated capacity for CartaHealth.
- Routes: default geo-affinity + recent routing-policy rollout (edge-policy-weight v2.4 deployed 09:05 UTC).
- Regions impacted: eu-west requests observed TO/RTT amplification as they traversed us-east edge nodes.

Steps to reproduce / Observed behavior:
1) Send a streaming chat request pinned to model gpt-open-13b from eu-west client IPs to the Redwood API.
2) ~10–20% of sessions show first chunk delayed >1s; p99 token latency spikes to 3–4s.
3) Some streaming connections time out at client after no chunks for 30s and show gateway 504 in server logs.

Logs/metrics and traces:
- Traces show routing decision attribute weight_shift=+0.65 to us-east for accounts with affinity=false between 09:05–09:28 UTC.
- TCP/TLS handshake RTTs on affected traces jumped from median 28ms to 120–240ms after extra cross-region hop.
- Edge logs: route-control service emitted WARN: policy-weight-rollout step mismatch (commit 2d8f7) followed by transient 5xx on proxy (upstream connect error).
- Observability snapshot: p50 120ms -> 200ms, p95 390ms -> 1.9s, p99 420ms -> 3.7s.

Initial triage notes:
- Correlated timing to edge-routing policy rollout at 09:05 UTC.
- Hypothesis: a misapplied weight override in the route-control plane caused non-affine requests to be redirected to a higher-weight (but cross-region) egress pool, producing additional network hops and serialization delays for streaming.
- Alternative: recent BGP peering metric changes. We confirmed AS path stable; BGP not the primary driver.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- At 09:30 UTC rolled back route-control weight override (reverted commit 2d8f7) and forced affinity rules for dedicated accounts.
- Restarted the proxy layer on the small set of impacted edge nodes to clear stuck upstream connections.
- Notified CartaHealth support contact and kept them informed.

Resolution summary:
- Root cause: a configuration rollout in route-control accidentally increased policy weight for a US egress pool for accounts without explicit affinity, created during a staged release that skipped a canary gate. This increased cross-region routing for a subset of customer sessions, adding extra network RTT and exhausting streaming idle time windows which led to client-side timeouts and gateway 504s.
- Fix: rollback of weight change, rollout of a corrected PR with canary gating and stricter affinity overrides (PR linked).
- Post-rollback metrics returned to baseline within ~7 minutes (p95 back to 410ms, p99 back to 460ms).

Follow-up actions / Postmortem TODOs:
- INT ticket to add a canary gate in route-control CI and block rollouts without active healthcheck results (linked INT-2045).
- Update runbook and add an explicit alert for sudden increase in cross-region hop count for streaming sessions.
- Add a short-term dashboard that breaks out routing weight changes by customer tier.
- Communicate RCA to impacted customers with timeline and assurance of mitigations.

This ticket involved dedicated tenant routing rules; the policy-rollout pipeline lacked an enforced canary check which allowed weight shift to reach production nodes briefly. Recommend a hold on manual weight edits until gating enforced.

Issue summary:
Customer requests guidance and configuration help to create distinct priority classes so interactive chat requests (low token, low-latency) are insulated from background embedding/bulk ingest jobs that generate 429 throttles during nightly backfills.

Impact:
- Intermittent 429 responses observed on chat endpoints during customer bulk embed pipelines (nightly backfill).
- Customer reports increased latency and degraded user experience for chat during weekend ingest windows.
- Risk of SLA breaches for key chat routes if mitigation not put in place.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (DataMesh dedicated lease) in us-east, running mixed workloads.
- Chat clients use short-lived ephemeral keys via an edge proxy. Bulk ingest jobs run from an internal orchestrator on scheduled window.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start bulk ingest job (10k small files, parallel workers 150) targeting /v1/embeddings.
2) Simultaneously open 50 chat sessions that stream short responses from /v1/chat/completions.
3) Observe increased 429s on chat route and periodic spikes in chat latency.

- Chat routes return 429 with X-RateLimit-Reason: tenant_quota_exhausted in bursts.
- Console shows token burn from bulk ingest consuming shared burst credits.

Expected behavior:
- Chat traffic should be prioritized, either via separate burst pools or priority classes so bulk background jobs cannot exhaust low-latency capacity.

What customer has tried:
- Reduced parallelism on workers from 150 -> 50; partial improvement but still occasional throttles.
- Enabled exponential backoff in client; not acceptable for chat UX.

Customer request:
1) Recommended configuration to create isolated burst/bandwidth pools for chat vs bulk on their dedicated lease.
2) Example per-route priority class and route-weight configuration for the api-gateway and rate-limiter.
3) Console/dashboard checks to validate the separation and tooling to alert when bulk jobs approach burst thresholds.

Initial hypothesis: bulk ingest consumes shared burst credits on the dedicated pool because route-level isolation is not configured for the customer. Observed token accounting in metrics shows large sustained token consumption from /v1/embeddings during backfill windows.

Issue summary: Customer BrightHealth AI reports unpredictable tail-latency spikes and occasional 5xx errors after applying a combined optimizer profile (aggressive async batching + KV-prefetch + per-layer quantization). They want guidance on a controlled, per-tenant demotion plan that avoids wholesale rollback and preserves capacity while restoring SLOs.

Impact: Intermittent increased 95p/99p latency for several mission-critical endpoints; error rate rose from 0.2% to ~1.8% during peak. Customer is on Dedicated plan with reserved capacity in us-east. Business impact: delayed user responses in production workflows; customer is requesting an SLA-safe mitigation within 48 hours.

Environment: prod, dedicated pool: bh-ai-pool-1, region: us-east, model pinned: open-7b-v1-q4a (tenant override present), runtime version: 2026.02.11, optimizer stack: async-batching:v3 + kv-prefetch:v2 + quant-profile:per-layer-mixed.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a mix of short- and long-sequence requests matching tenant's traffic profile (50% chat, 30% summarization, 20% embeddings) to tenant route /v1/tenants/bha/api/generate. 2) Observe 95p/99p latency spikes after traffic churn and cache-eviction windows. 3) Occasionally observe 503 from an allocator when KV-prefetch eviction collides with async-batch flush.

Logs / traces: Linked Grafana dashboard and sampled traces in comments. Key observation: tail spikes correlate with large mixed-sequence batches and concurrent KV-prefetch eviction events.

Requested outcome: A stepwise per-tenant demotion (soft-landing) plan that: - is safe to run live without full rollback, - preserves most throughput, - allows phased re-enable with gating metrics, - includes preflight checks and a clear handoff to SRE if manual rollback is required.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:42 - SRE Oncall (Maya Rivera): Requested exact tenant pool and pool occupancy stats. Pulled allocator and pod logs; saw 503s with message 'kv_eviction_in_progress, allocator busy'. Attached grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/opt/tenant-bh-ai?orgId=1
2026-03-12 22:57 - Customer (BrightHealth AI - infra team): Ran shadow traffic for 4 hours; saw 0.4% error rate and minimal accuracy delta on eval set. Requested go-ahead for phased traffic gate tomorrow morning US peak.
Hypothesis 1: Large async batches are extending enqueue time and overlapping with KV-prefetch eviction triggers, creating resource contention leading to allocator 503s.
Hypothesis 2: Per-layer mixed quantization increases CPU/GPU kernel variability for some sequence lengths, increasing variance under mixed workloads (contributes to tail latency).
Telemetry: 95p latency correlates with two signals: batch_size spikes and concurrent kv_eviction_count > 2. See trace sample: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/0a4f3b
Staging reproduction steps: Use tenant traffic generator (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/tenant-loadgen) with mixed sequence lengths 16/128/1024 distribution. Observed same 503 signature after simulated cache churn.
Preflight checklist performed: 1) Snapshot tenant optimizer config 2) Exported per-route token histograms 3) Validated eval prompt set for accuracy before demote 4) Captured current autoscale and allocator state
Decision: Proceed with 'Soft-demote' approach (per-tenant limited demote) rather than full rollback. This uses traffic-split + config overrides + gating metrics to re-enable parts gradually.
Workaround applied (phase 1): Per-tenant temporary overrides: async-batching max_window reduced by 30%, batch_size cap set to 64, kv-prefetch window set to conservative mode. Result: 95p latency reduced ~45% in first 2 hours and allocator 503s stopped.
Phase 2 (in progress): Gradual reallocation via traffic-split: 90% traffic to demoted profile, 10% to original for quality checks. Monitor gating metrics: 95p latency, 99p latency, error_rate, model_accuracy_delta. If gating thresholds breached, automatically shift back to 100% demoted profile.
Permanent fix plan: Team will iterate on tuned async-batching heuristics and update KV-prefetch eviction backpressure logic (linked PR above). Long-term: add a per-tenant preflight simulator to validate combined optimizer stacks under realistic token distribution before rollout.
Follow-ups: 1) Postmortem and runbook update scheduled (owner: Jordan Patel) 2) Add tenant-specific circuit-breaker thresholds for KV eviction events 3) Create a console UI quick-action to run 'soft-demote' and snapshot profiles for dedicated tenants.
Status: Monitoring continues; SRE standing by. Customer notified and engaged in phased plan.

Issue summary: Customer is seeing recurring 429 responses when uploading large batched embedding requests (payloads ~800-1200 records per request) during a nightly sync. Impact: Sync jobs are intermittently failing, causing index lag of up to 6 hours. Environment: Dedicated account on prod-us-east running a single reserved pool. Observed behavior: API returns 429 with x-rate-limit-retry-after headers in some batches; other batches succeed. Expected behavior: Large batched uploads should be accepted or throttled predictably with guidance on safe concurrency/throughput settings. Customer asked for prescriptive rate-limit configuration and any platform-side adjustments we recommend.
1) Prepare a CSV of 1,000 documents and send as 10 concurrent POST /v1/embeddings/batch requests with 100 items each.
2) Run five such job instances in parallel from a single IP to simulate the nightly sync concurrency.
3) Observe 429 responses returned for a subset of requests; check x-rate-limit-* headers.
4) Retry with exponential backoff using original client retry logic and note percentage of successful retries within 2 minutes.
2026-03-09T03:12:22Z - 429 POST /v1/embeddings/batch - request_id=rid_4a2c - x-rate-limit-limit=200 - x-rate-limit-remaining=0 - x-rate-limit-retry-after=15
2026-03-09T03:12:28Z - 200 POST /v1/embeddings/batch - request_id=rid_4a2d - x-rate-limit-remaining=197
2026-03-09T03:15:10Z - 429 POST /v1/embeddings/batch - request_id=rid_4a3f - client-ip=52.14.23.11

Luis Romero (SRE) (2026-03-11): Reproduced locally against a dedicated test pool with same quota settings. Observed token- and request-based rate limiter hit when multiple job instances coordinate bursts. Hypothesis: global per-customer request quota is being exceeded transiently due to synchronized job starts.
Customer (StreamlineSearch) (2026-03-12): Asked whether we can increase request quota for maintenance windows or provide a preferred backoff configuration for batches of 1k+ documents.
Checked quota-service metrics for customer account: observed short spikes in requests/sec that align with nightly job start times.

Issue summary: Customer (EuroBank Holdings, enterprise) requests a signed evidence package and SIEM export profile that demonstrates per-field redaction decisions together with attached legal-basis tags (e.g., consent, contract, legitimate_interest) and consent timestamps for EU-region tenant activity. Impact: This is a compliance block for an upcoming regulator audit (scheduled 2026-03-20) — customer needs proof of how PII was redacted, which legal basis applied to each record, and a cryptographically signed manifest for delivered artifacts. Environment: prod, eu-west region, single-tenant on Redwood Dedicated. Request: 1) A sample export (CSV and Parquet) for a 7-day slice (2026-02-28 to 2026-03-06) showing pseudonymized identifiers and the redaction_reason field per event; 2) A mapping document describing the redaction rules applied (field name -> rule id -> redaction level); 3) Per-record legal_basis tags and consent timestamps where available; 4) Signed delivery manifest (SHA256) and an RFC3161 timestamp of manifest creation; 5) A short runbook describing how to reproduce the same export via the Console or API, including parameter names and recommended query filters.
Customer reproduction intent: query audit stream for tenant eurobank-prod between 2026-02-28T00:00:00Z and 2026-03-06T23:59:59Z with fields: event_id, timestamp, actor_id, resource_id, changes, redaction_reason, legal_basis, consent_timestamp.
Support suggested API call: GET /v1/audit/exports?tenant=eurobank-prod&start=2026-02-28T00:00:00Z&end=2026-03-06T23:59:59Z&format=parquet&redaction=include_metadata
If export fails: capture exporter logs and console export job id, share with Support for investigation.
Customer-provided sample (anonymized): event_id=evt_01ab, timestamp=2026-03-02T14:12:03Z, actor_id=usr_xxxxx, resource_id=doc_9a8b, redaction_reason=phone_mask, legal_basis=consent, consent_timestamp=2025-11-12T09:22:11Z
Support collector note: export job 2026-03-11T08:45:22Z -> job_id=exp-7890 returned 206 partial content (missing redaction_reason column)
Exporter debug: 2026-03-11T08:45:21Z INFO starting export slice tenant=eurobank-prod start=2026-02-28 end=2026-03-06 format=parquet include_meta=true
Redaction engine trace: 2026-03-11T08:45:25Z WARN rule_lookup_timeout for field 'consent_timestamp' fallback=empty
Aisha Patel (Customer Success) 2026-03-10: Received audit request from EuroBank compliance lead (Sofia Lind). They specifically require legal_basis per event and proof that consent timestamps are retained when present. Audit date is 2026-03-20, asking for deliverables by 2026-03-13.
Evelyn Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Started triage to verify export feature flags and whether redaction metadata is included by default. Investigating exporter job behaviour in eu-west cluster.
SRE on-call (Marcus Lee) 2026-03-11: Confirmed exporter runs in dedicated pool for eurobank-prod. Found recent rollout of redaction-engine v1.9.2 on 2026-03-09 — noting a change that can omit optional metadata fields when rule backend times out.
Evelyn Chen 2026-03-11: Requested permission to run a controlled re-export and provide a signed manifest. Proposed approach: create export snapshot, pseudonymize actor_id/resource_id with salted HMAC, include redaction_reason and legal_basis columns, sign manifest with platform signing key and attach RFC3161 timestamp. Asked customer to confirm acceptance of salted HMAC pseudonymization as proof artifact.
Sofia Lind (Customer) 2026-03-11: Confirmed salted HMAC pseudonymization is acceptable provided we include mapping of hashing salt fingerprint and that the legal_basis and consent_timestamp are present as separate columns. Also asked for a short statement of chain-of-custody for the delivered artifact.
Hypothesis 1: Recent redaction-engine update introduced a race condition with the rule backend (rules-service) leading to missing redaction_reason/legal_basis values when rule lookup exceeds 250ms timeout.
Hypothesis 2: Exporter configuration for dedicated tenants had include_meta defaulted to false for performance; need to verify tenant config override for eurobank-prod.
Checks performed: 1) Reviewed export job logs (job_id=exp-7890) and saw WARN for rule_lookup_timeout. 2) Checked tenant config: export.include_meta = false (inherited from global defaults) for eurobank-prod. 3) Validated rules-service latency spikes around 2026-03-09 due to cache miss after rollout.
Partial finding: When rules-service returns late, exporter records an empty value for redaction metadata instead of retrying or marking record for manual review. This explains missing column in customer sample export.
Planned immediate workaround: run a controlled replay export with exporter param include_meta=true and increased rule_lookup_timeout=1000ms for the requested 7-day slice; pseudonymize identifiers via HMAC-salt provided by Support; generate SHA256 manifest and request RFC3161 timestamp from our timestamping service.
Planned follow-up engineering fix: create a patch to make exporter tolerate rule lookup timeouts by queueing records for async metadata enrichment and include a manifest flag 'metadata_partial=false' to fail exports that would otherwise omit redaction metadata. Triage ticket created: INT-33421.
Deliverable timeline: Controlled export + signed manifest to customer by 2026-03-13. Engineering patch targeted for 2026-03-20 with rollout to prod-eu after validation.
payload.summary: Field-level redaction mapping and legal-basis tagging for EU banking audit - evidence & export profile request

payload.description:
Customer is preparing a Redwood Private on-prem upgrade using the air-gapped upgrade bundle flow. Bundle download completes on a connected jump host, but verification fails when the bundle is moved into the offline environment.

Customer impact:
- Upgrade is blocked (cannot proceed past bundle verification).
- Maintenance window planned for 2025-06-05 is at risk.

Customer context:
- Northstar requires offline validation (checksum + signature) for all artifacts.
- They are following the draft runbook we shared for air-gapped upgrades.

Initial customer-provided error (redacted):
- "ERROR: bundle verification failed: signature verification failed" (no further detail)
- In a later run: "checksum mismatch for manifest" (unclear whether file corruption vs parsing vs key trust issue)

Goal for this ticket:
- Triage root cause (customer environment vs installer bug vs packaging issue).
- Provide immediate workaround.
- Track engineering fix for clearer/accurate error messaging and keying/compat behavior in the offline flow.
1) On connected host, download bundle:
   redwood-private-installer bundle download --private-version 1.9.0 --output /tmp/redwood-private-1.9.0.bundle.tgz
2) Transfer bundle to offline environment via approved mechanism.
3) On offline host, run:
   redwood-private-installer bundle verify --bundle /mnt/media/redwood-private-1.9.0.bundle.tgz
4) Observe verification failure; upgrade cannot proceed.
Bundle verifies successfully (signature + checksums) and installer proceeds to prechecks/plan generation.
Bundle verification fails with non-actionable errors (signature/checksum failure without identifying missing key vs corrupted download vs wrong file type).
Findings from support triage:
- Customer was using redwood-private-installer v0.13.4 in the offline environment.
- Bundle target version is Redwood Private 1.9.0 (beta build shared for design partner).
- Engineering suspects 1.9.0 bundles are signed with the new signing key (key rotation for Private offline artifacts). Older installers do not ship the updated trusted keyring, and the current error output does not clearly state "unknown signer" / missing fingerprint.

Additional hypothesis we ruled in/out:
- Partial/corrupted download: possible, but the bundle file size reported by customer matched expected size from the portal.
- Wrong content downloaded (HTML login page saved as .tgz): not the case here; `file` output showed gzip-compressed tar.
- Transfer corruption: customer used binary-safe transfer; repeated transfer yielded identical SHA256 of the outer bundle file.

Repro in Redwood lab:
- Using installer v0.13.4 to verify a 1.9.0 bundle reproduces "signature verification failed" with no key ID.
- Using installer v0.14.1 (internal) succeeds.

Conclusion:
- Primary root cause: installer keyring is out of date relative to bundle signing key.
- Secondary issue: error message is too generic and leads customers to suspect checksum issues rather than trust/key mismatch.
Short-term workaround provided to customer:
1) Upgrade the installer binary in the offline environment to v0.14.1 (provided via support secure link), then re-run:
   redwood-private-installer bundle verify --bundle <path>
2) If upgrading the installer is blocked by change control, use the provided keyring file (redwood-private-public-keys-2025-06.asc) and run:
   redwood-private-installer bundle verify --bundle <path> --keyring ./redwood-private-public-keys-2025-06.asc

Notes:
- We did NOT recommend skipping signature verification. Customer explicitly requires signature verification for change management evidence.
Resolved via workaround: customer upgraded installer to v0.14.1 in the offline environment and bundle verification succeeded. Customer proceeded with prechecks in a dry-run and confirmed they can schedule the maintenance window.

Engineering follow-up tracked for product fix:
- Improve error message to include signing key fingerprint / key ID and guidance ("upgrade installer" or "provide keyring").
- Add explicit compatibility check: if bundle requires signing key not present in installer keyring, fail fast with actionable remediation.
- Document required installer version for each Private bundle signing epoch.
1) Dev Patel to coordinate with Release Eng on backport/GA timeline for improved verifier messaging and keyring packaging.
2) Update external-ish docs/runbook snippet for air-gapped upgrades to include: "upgrade installer first" and "how to verify bundles offline".
3) Ensure the download command prints expected bundle size + SHA of the outer file and stores it alongside plan artifacts for audit.
4) Add a support macro for common air-gapped verification failures (missing key vs corrupted bundle vs wrong file downloaded).

Additional notes:
2025-06-04 08:27 PT — Customer (via Support, paraphrased): Outer bundle SHA stable across transfer. Installer v0.13.4. Verification fails with "signature verification failed". Upgrading installer may require internal approval but is feasible.
2025-06-05 07:52 PT — Customer (via Support, paraphrased): Upgraded to installer v0.14.1. `bundle verify` now passes. Proceeding with precheck dry-run today; maintenance window remains on schedule.
payload.summary: Air-gapped upgrade bundle fails verification (checksum/signature) during offline download/verify flow

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a scheduled SCIM provisioning run, a subset of users lost RBAC bindings in their private deployment. Affected users receive 403 when calling the private API even though they are still present in the IdP and in Redwood's user list. The drop appears intermittent and only affects groups that are provisioned via SCIM upsert (PATCH) sequences from the customer's IdP.

Impact:
- Multiple product teams at Knex Analytics unable to access model endpoints behind the private VPC.
- Several users report 403s for routine calls; customer is on a paid private plan and requires immediate mitigation.

Environment:
- Private control plane (customer-managed VPC) running agent v1.37.4
- Region: eu-west
- IdP: Okta acting as SCIM provisioning source

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Provision a new group in Okta with displayName "knex-analytics:research" and externalId "grp-334".
2) In a follow-up sync Okta sends a PATCH (SCIM upsert) with the same displayName but externalId "grp-334​" (zero-width char inserted).
3) Redwood SCIM client receives 200 for the PATCH but the provisioning engine later shows the group as "unbound" to the corresponding role mapping.
4) Users in that group get 403 on calls to private endpoints.

Observed behavior:
- SCIM logs show upsert sequences succeeded with HTTP 200/204 but reconciliation marks the group as duplicate and it is omitted from the role-mapping index.
- When support triggers a manual re-sync in the console the missing bindings reappear and users regain access.

Expected behavior:
- Upserts should be idempotent and preserve role bindings even when small metadata differences (e.g., invisible unicode characters) exist.

Additional context:
- Customer says the issue started after an Okta change that introduced a migration script; they suspect the script added non-printing characters to externalId in some groups.
- No other customers have reported identical failures but one internal customer ticket (INT-4102) shows a similar reconcile edge-case in staging.

Relevant log snippets (redacted):
- "2026-03-11T08:14:22Z scim-client: PATCH /Groups/grp-334 200"
- "2026-03-11T08:14:22Z provisioner: reconcile: found duplicate key 'knex-analytics:research' -> skipping binding"
- "2026-03-11T08:14:23Z rbac: lookup failed for group id 'grp-334​' -> normalized lookup returned null"

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - SRE (Alex Kim): Retrieved agent logs from private control plane; confirmed duplicate-detection path marked group as duplicate during reconcile. Requested agent debug build to surface normalization steps.
2026-03-12 - Support (Priya): Ran manual re-sync via Console for customer which restored bindings for the impacted groups. Recommended a temporary workaround (manual re-sync) while engineering investigates permanent fix.
2026-03-12 - Engineering (Rohit Malhotra): Reproduced locally with a test payload that included U+200B (zero-width space). Filed PR (see related_github_prs) to normalize group identifiers during SCIM upsert handling.
Root cause hypothesis: SCIM upsert sends logically identical identifiers but with non-printing unicode differences. The provisioning engine's duplicate detection compares displayName/externalId without normalization, causing 'duplicate' label in the index and subsequent omission from role-binding reconciliation.
Confirmed reproduction: Added U+200B into externalId in a staging Okta export; provisioning observed same behavior (200 responses, but reconcile omitted binding).
Edge case: SCIM client reports HTTP 200/204 so upstream looks healthy; error is in downstream reconciliation logic which treats de-duplicated entries as intentionally removed rather than normalized duplicates.
Related internal ticket: INT-4102 documents a similar reconcile edge-case on a non-production cluster using different unicode variations.
Telemetry: No increase in 5xx, but jump in 'rbac_missing_binding' events for customer-specific tenant id.
Workaround (customer-facing): Run a manual 'Reconcile groups' from the Redwood Console for the affected tenant; this will normalize and reattach missing bindings. Support performed this on 2026-03-12 and customer confirmed access restored.
Temporary mitigation (recommended): Instruct IdP admin to run a cleanup script to strip non-printing unicode from externalId/displayName fields prior to provisioning.
Permanent fix: Engineering merged normalization patch to SCIM upsert pipeline to trim and NFC-normalize identifiers (PR linked). Patch will be released as agent v1.38.1; rollout plan targets private agents first and then hosted fleet.
Post-deploy follow-up: Add an automated 'fuzzy-check' during reconcile to detect and reconcile probable unicode-only differences and surface warnings in the console. Create postmortem entry and update SCIM runbook.

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent increase in end-to-end latency after we rotated residency stamps for a subset of tokens during a control-plane reconciliation window. The increase appears only for requests that are routed through our CDN-prefetch path and then hand off to a different edge SNI than expected.

Impact:
- BrightHealth AI (Dedicated) reports p50 increased from ~120ms to ~420ms and p95 from ~900ms to ~2.6s for text-generation requests over a 20 minute window.
- Errors: no 5xxs reported from runtime; increased TLS renegotiation counts and handshake time recorded at edge.

Environment:
- prod, customer tenant on Dedicated pool in us-east-1 with eu-west failover.
- Residency mode: safe-residency (control-plane stamp rotation enabled).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send steady 10rps requests pinned to eu-west token that was recently rotated.
2) Observe client-side timing and server-provided X-Residency-Stamp header.
3) Occasionally requests route via CDN edge A (us-east) which has different TLS session cache for the customer, causing full handshake.

Observed behavior:
- TLS full-handshake durations spike for affected requests (200-800ms).
- Edge reports SNI flip between requests associated with same token within a short TTL window.
- Control-plane logs show residency-stamp update at 14:12:03 UTC, followed by route reconcilers pushing mapping at 14:12:09 UTC.

Expected behavior:
- Residency stamp rotation should not produce mixed-egress where same token alternates SNI/edge within session lifespan and cause new TLS handshakes.

Logs / artifacts:
- Edge TLS metrics link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/edge/tls-handshakes?orgId=1&var-tenant=brighthealth
- Control plane event: cp-event-2026-03-10-141203 (included in attachments).

Found CDN prefetch TTL of 60s (customer-configured). Our reconciler had 45s rotation cadence during recent control-plane repair, creating a window where two edge mappings were valid for short period.
Observed session-affinity headers differ between hits; when SNI flips, session cache lookup fails -> full TLS handshake. This explains latency delta without 5xxs.

payload.description:
Issue summary:

Customer reports that when a client cancels a long-running function call (tool invocation) then immediately retries the same logical operation, the downstream function can execute twice and produce duplicate side effects. This appears to be most common with long-running handlers (>30s) where the server acknowledges the funcall start, the client cancels (AbortController / context cancel) and retries; the first run completes later and the customer observes duplicate side effects (e.g., duplicate emails, duplicate database writes).

Impact:
- Observable duplicate side effects for critical actions (billing emails) for a small subset of requests (~0.2% of calls from the customer).
- Customer on Dedicated capacity; duplicates break idempotency expectations and require manual reconciliation.

Environment:
- Customer: NimbusAI (dedicated cluster)
- Region: us-east
- SDKs observed: Go v0.9.3, Python v1.4.1
- Server runtime: dedicated-serving v2026.02.14

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a function call that triggers a downstream action taking 40–90s (handler sleeps then writes to external DB).
2) After 2–4s, client cancels request using context.Cancel (Go) or AbortController.abort (TS) or requests.Session.close (Python) and immediately issues a retry of the same logical operation (new request, same business id).
3) Observe: new request completes successfully; later the original inflight request completes on server side and triggers the same downstream action again.

Expected behavior:
- Either the initial inflight execution should be safely deduplicated on completion (server-side dedupe keyed by idempotency/business id) or the retry should be rejected/queued until the server can confirm the original outcome. Customer expects at-most-once semantics for business operations when they provide a request-level idempotency key.

Logs / Traces (sanitized excerpts):
- Client (Go): context cancelled -> reconnect -> new request 202 Accepted -> result returned to client after 3s
- Server trace: funcall-start id=call-abc123 timestamp=10:01:12 -> func invoked on worker-17 -> no explicit commit recorded yet
- Server later: funcall-complete id=call-abc123 timestamp=10:01:58 -> downstream webhook POSTed
- New request trace: funcall-start id=call-def456 timestamp=10:01:15 -> func invoked -> func completed timestamp=10:01:18 -> webhook POSTed

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis A: client-side cancel only severs the connection but does not communicate intent to the serving runtime to cancel the already-scheduled work; the runtime continues and completes the task. If the retried request uses a different idempotency token or no token, the server treats it as a separate invocation.
- Hypothesis B: request-level idempotency is currently applied at request receipt (dedupe for identical token seen within a short window) but tokens supplied by customer are not always propagated to the worker execution metadata (race in header propagation during reconnection). That could allow duplicate executions.
- Reproducer built by Support using Go SDK (attached) shows deterministic duplicate when aborting after 2s and immediately retrying with a different generated request-id.

Immediate workaround suggested to customer:
- Include a stable idempotency key in the retried request (e.g., business-operation-id) that the server will normalize and dedupe on completion.
- As an interim: avoid issuing an immediate retry; wait for the first call timeout or configure a short server-side TTL for in-flight dedupe.

Recommended long-term fixes / follow-ups:
- Server-side: persist idempotency key to funcall execution metadata and perform dedupe on completion, not only on initial receipt. Consider storing key+status (inflight/completed) in the serving control-plane to reject or reconcile retries that occur while execution is inflight.
- SDK: surface a clearer pattern for client cancellation vs intent-to-abort (i.e., provide an explicit "cancel-and-abort-server-work" option) and add docs showing the safe retry pattern for long-running tool calls.

Next steps assigned:
- Engineering (runtime) to validate header propagation path and confirm whether idempotency keys are present on worker-side metadata. (Assigned INT-9923)
- Support to gather a minimal repro that includes headers and request bodies from customer.

Workaround implemented by customer:
- NimbusAI configured their orchestration to attach a stable business id in the metadata and the duplicates dropped to ~0.01% (still visible in narrow edge cases).

Resolution notes (in progress):
- Eng interim patch proposed: ensure idempotency key written to execution record at receipt and atomically used to dedupe completions. Patch PR: runtime#1824 (linked).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:42 - Customer (Nina Li, NimbusAI): Provided Go and Python repros and confirmed they did not set a stable idempotency key initially. Noted duplicates happen ~1 in 5000 calls but are high-impact.
2026-03-11 16:10 - Eng (Diego Morales): Debugging header propagation; saw cases where request-metadata is lost when connection is aborted and server requeues for execution. Hypothesis: worker execution receives a fresh execution context without idempotency token in edge abort scenario.
payload.summary: Cancel-then-retry race: long-running function-call confirmation mismatch causing duplicate executions

1) Send a burst of concurrent streaming generation requests (concurrency ~120).
2) When a subset of requests receive 429s or soft-quota HTTP headers, client SDK retries with exponential backoff but short initial backoff (100ms).
3) Observed behavior: SDK retries overlap with original traffic window causing repeated 429s and long queuing behind the serving runtime.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent 429 responses returned from gateway and occasionally 503 from upstream serving-runtime when queue grows.
- Client logs show retry storm patterns (batches of identical requests retried every ~200-800ms).
- Token-level cost spikes correlate with retry windows.

Expected behavior:
- Soft-quota signals should throttle politely without inducing retry storms that cascade into higher end-to-end latency.

- Console dashboard: route "nimbus-prod/summarize" shows latency percentiles and rate-limit counters (dashboard link in comment).
