payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicated chunks in streaming responses and occasional full requests egressing via us-east even though tenant is pinned to eu-west strict residency. This started after enabling automatic residency-lock refresh for their Private VPC deployment (toggle enabled 2026-03-10).

Impact:
- Intermittent duplication of streaming frames visible to client (duplicate partial tokens appearing ~0.5-2% of streams).
- P95 latency spikes (+30-120ms) correlated with duplicated streams.
- Some requests observed in packet captures and flow logs leaving eu-west and reaching us-east edge (unexpected cross-region egress).
- Customer workflow: bank transaction summarization via streaming; duplicates are causing downstream de-dup logic to reject some chunks, causing UI flicker and a small percentage of failed user flows.

Environment:
- VerityBank private deployment hosted in eu-west VPC with peered backup egress to us-east (configured per compliance).
- Residency mode: strict with residency-lock refresh enabled (automatic refresh window = 15m).
- Client: in-house web client using websocket streaming with keepalive 45s.
- Time window first observed: 2026-03-11 10:42 - 2026-03-12 09:00 UTC.

Observed telemetry/logs (snippets attached in comments):
- Edge flow logs show intermittent NAT translations to us-east edge IPs during refresh windows.
- Streaming server logs show duplicate chunk IDs generated by the same request ID but different connection IDs.
- Auth service logs show short-lived token rotation events (STS) coinciding with residency-lock refresh timestamps.

Other notes:
- Customer has packet captures, Cloud NAT logs, and conservative retry logic on the client (single in-flight request per session).
- No large-scale outage; behaviour is sporadic and low volume, but reproducible for this tenant under the lock-refresh schedule.
1) Use VerityBank Private deployment in eu-west with residency-lock refresh enabled (15m window).
2) Open websocket streaming session from a client behind the customer VPC (simulate same egress IP).
3) Trigger a streaming generation workload on rw-open-13b-v1 (moderate token length, ~400 tokens).
4) Observe server-side stream frames and client received frames around the residency lock refresh boundary (e.g., at minute 14-16 of refresh timer).
5) Repeat while collecting edge flow logs and auth token audit logs to correlate timestamps.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 13:15 UTC - VerityBank (Customer): Provided pcaps and noted that duplicates align with the residency-lock refresh (they can toggle to test). They can reproduce by enabling refresh every 5 minutes in staging.
- Reproduced locally in staging by toggling residency-lock refresh; duplication rate ~1.2% with 15m window, increases to ~3.8% when forcing 1m window.
- Packet captures show SYN/FIN from proxied connections where mid-stream rebind happens; new edge connection receives buffered messages and replays last N frames without ref counter, causing duplicates at client.
- Auth STS rotation timestamp correlated with edge routing update events in control plane logs (control-plane workflow: mark transferable -> update routing table -> edge subscribes -> rebind).
- Hypothesis: control plane currently treats token rotation and route refresh as independent events; when they overlap, edge proxy may accept ownership while previous session not fully drained, resulting in double-emit of buffered frames.
- Telemetry dashboards referenced: /dashboards/edge/rebind-events, /dashboards/streaming/duplicate-frames (internal links provided to eng team).
- Related runbook: Private VPC Egress Runbook — contains steps to disable automatic refresh and verify route sticky session (linked above).
Workaround applied: Customer agreed to temporarily disable automatic residency-lock refresh (manual refresh only) and increase websocket keepalive to 90s. This reduced duplicate frames to <0.1% in their staging tests.
Planned fix: engineering to land serialized rebind flow that ensures old edge proxy drains buffered frames and acks before new proxy replays any buffered content. PR branch: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4123 (under review).
Rollout plan: Canary in staging (complete), progressive rollout to eu-west Private clusters over 72 hours with monitoring for duplicate-frame metric and p95 latency regressions. Post-deploy verification with VerityBank capture set scheduled for 2026-03-18.
Follow-ups: add an alert for rebind-events > 0.1% and add documentation entry in Private VPC Runbook about recommended websocket keepalive/refresh window alignment.
payload.summary: Streaming session duplication and intermittent cross-region egress after residency-lock refresh in Private VPC

payload.description:
Issue summary: Percepta Labs reports they did not receive a partial credit for an hourly accumulator rollback that occurred during a mixed-quantization batch job on 2026-03-09 23:00-23:15 UTC. Impact: Customer expects ~$1,200 in prorated credits to be applied to their month-to-date invoice; currently the invoice shows full charge and no provisional credit. Environment: prod (us-west-2), dedicated tenant, reserved capacity + burst pool. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run mixed-quantization batch (jobs using rw-open-3b-v1 and gptx-compat-7b-quant) with autoscale policy set to allow burst. 2) Trigger manual scheduler rollback of hourly accumulator (internal operator action). 3) Observe billing postback window and invoice generated on March 10. Expected: Metering service deducts prorated hours/credits for the rolled back accumulator window. Observed: No credit applied; usage shows full token counts for the affected hourly window. Logs/IDs: tenant_id=percepta-34, job_ids=[J-9876, J-9877], postback_batch_id=PB-20260309-23, invoice_line_ref=INV-202603-Percepta-01. Additional context: Customer had previously received partial credits for similar rollbacks (SUP-721345). They raised this as an urgent credit appeal ahead of their EOM reconciliation.

Additional notes:
Checked postback logs for PB-20260309-23: consumer accepted events but metric 'accumulator.rollback' had timestamp drift of ~90s relative to batch window, causing it to fall into next hourly bucket.
Hypothesis: Hourly accumulator logic aggregates by fixed-window boundaries; rollback events with timestamp drift were not re-associated with the original bucket for crediting. Mixed-quantization microbatches produce non-deterministic commit timing, increasing chance of boundary drift.
Query run: SELECT * FROM metering.postbacks WHERE batch_id='PB-20260309-23' returns two entries for job J-9876; second entry had corrected_token_count but no rollback_flag set — possible duplicate event overwrote rollback-tagged record.
Dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/metering-postback?var=tenant=percepta-34, https://sentry.redwood.ai/organizations/redwood/issues/456789/
Related code area: metering consumer dedup + accumulator assignment (infra/metering/consumer.go). PR 4182 adds extra telemetry but does not fully address re-association logic.
Workaround applied 2026-03-12: Manually created provisional credit for Percepta Labs ($1,210.00) applied to account as a refund line item; finance notified and invoice INV-202603-Percepta-01 updated. Engineering action: follow-up ticket INT-330112 created to implement idempotent rollback re-association and timestamp-normalization for accumulator events. Planned rollout: patch to postback consumer (infra PR in review) and acceptance test covering mixed-quantization microbatch boundaries. Customer notified and confirmed acceptance of provisional credit; monitoring added to track similar rollbacks for 7 days.
payload.summary: Appeal: Partial credits missing after hourly accumulator rollback during mixed-quantization batch run

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers observed elevated 5xx rates for both long-poll and short-stream endpoints during a concentrated tenant traffic burst. Errors started at ~2026-03-12 08:30 UTC and persisted with periodic waves for ~6 hours. Downstream investigation shows repeated runtime process restarts and kernel-level GPU eviction messages. apigw exhibited queue growth and connection backlog leading to additional upstream resets.

Impact:
- NimbusHealth (dedicated tenant) experienced ~35% request error rate on streaming endpoints and ~20% on poll endpoints for ~6 hours.
- Several in-production features degraded: real-time transcription and message streaming.
- Customer has an active production incident with business impact.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment for NimbusHealth in prod (us-east-1) on dedicated GPU pool (3x A100 partial partition).
- Model mix: redwood-13b-v1 for heavy completions and redwood-7b-quant for some routing.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant sends high fan-in of mixed short/long streaming sessions (many connections with keepalive ~120s).
2) apigw accept queue and keepalive pool grow; some connections are queued >1s.
3) Serving runtime processes begin to show kernel eviction (nvml/gpu driver messages) and eventually restart.
4) apigw shows 502/503/504 spikes as upstreams become unhealthy or reset.

Observed behavior:
- Repeated runtime exits with logs showing "GPU eviction: kernel preemption" and then restart watchdogs.
- apigw metrics: accept_queue_length spike, per-route 5xx rate up to 40%.
- Autoscaler attempts scale-up but new pods fail with OOM-like driver errors until eviction pressure subsides.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant burst should be absorbed by autoscaler and prefetched KV cache without causing upstream process restarts or kernel-level GPU evictions.

Logs & metrics (examples):
- runtime.log excerpts: "[08:45:12] ERROR gpu_driver: kernel eviction triggered for device 0, nvml:page_fault"; "[08:45:13] INFO watchdog: restarting runtime (exit code 137)"
- apigw metrics: accept_queue_seconds P95 = 1.8s at peak; 5xx-rate per-route = 38%
- node metrics: GPU memory utilization oscillating 60->98% within seconds during long-stream fan-in.

Initial hypotheses considered: noisy-tenant GPU fragmentation, driver-level pagefaults triggered by long-pinned KV caches, and streaming keepalive amplification.
Findings to date:
- NVML traces captured frequent MMU page faults on device 0 during the peak.
- Kernel logs on host show driver preemption messages consistent with eviction under heavy migration.
- Prefetch/KV cache warmup coincided with bursts of long-lived streams which pinned memory and prevented efficient scheduler placement.
- Autoscaler added pods but new pods immediately experienced driver pagefaults when routing prefetched tensors due to memory fragmentation.
- apigw backlog amplified retries causing additional load.
Hypothesis: combination of long-lived streaming sessions + large prefetched KV caches for redwood-13b-v1 created transient high GPU memory fragmentation; driver preemption/eviction led to runtime restarts and cascading apigw 5xx.
Next steps planned:
- Coordinate with infra to collect full NVML dumps and host kernel traces for the affected hosts.
- Temporarily throttle prefetch windows for NimbusHealth and cap streaming concurrent sessions as a mitigation.
- Add a short-term scheduler pinning change to avoid packing heavy-prefetch and streaming workloads onto the same GPUs.

Applied temporary mitigations at 2026-03-13 01:10 UTC: reduced tenant prefetch window by 50% and set a per-tenant concurrent streaming cap to 300 sessions. Observed immediate reduction in runtime restarts and 5xx rate dropped to ~6% within 20 minutes. Note: customer-facing latency slightly increased for cold prefixes.

Mitigation in progress. Short-term cap and prefetch reduction stabilized the fleet. Engineering is implementing a medium-term fix: scheduler change to isolate heavy-prefetch model instances from long-lived streaming workloads and a runtime patch to handle driver pagefault backoff more gracefully. ETA for rollout of scheduler change to staging: 2026-03-18.

2026-03-12 09:05 Support (Aisha Raman): Customer reported elevated 5xx across streaming endpoints; provided initial telemetry and request traces.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:00 Engineering (Marta Liu): Confirmed NVML pagefault patterns; suspect memory fragmentation. PR to add additional NVML dumps in-flight: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4217.
2026-03-13 01:12 Support (Aisha Raman): Short-term controls applied (prefetch cap, streaming cap) — customer reports degradation reduced, monitoring continuing.
2026-03-14 14:05 Customer (NimbusHealth Ops): Thank you; incident impact reduced. Requesting follow-up on SLA credit process and long-term mitigation timeline.
payload.summary: Persistent 5xx across streaming and poll endpoints during tenant burst leading to runtime GPU eviction and apigw overload

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a sustained traffic spike on 2026-03-08 02:14 UTC Orpheus Media began seeing truncated streaming responses followed by session errors (401/invalid token) and a small set of unexpectedly billed retry completions. Impact: Live chat widget truncation for a subset (~7%) of user sessions in us-east-1, elevated 5xxs and token errors for Orpheus API keys, and a measured billing delta for requests that retried after token refresh failures. Timeline (high level): - 02:12 UTC: Orpheus reports first truncated stream in #support channel. - 02:14 UTC: Support triages -> escalates to SRE; incident declared. - 02:18 UTC: Initial mitigation (circuit limiting) applied at API gateway. - 02:30 UTC: Root cause hypothesis formed (session-store eviction race with KV-cache TTL bump). - 03:05 UTC: Hotfix deployed to session-store (atomic update and TTL alignment). - 03:22 UTC: Service stabilized and streaming resumes for most traffic. - 03:40 UTC: Billing review shows a small batch of duplicated completions from client-side retry loops; credits issued. Environment: prod us-east-1, Canary: none (customer on enterprise plan with dedicated routing). Steps to reproduce (attempts): 1) Replay a synthetic surge matching Orpheus traffic profile against their API key with concurrent streaming clients. 2) Force session-store TTL to roll over while concurrent requests are in-flight. 3) Observe streaming cut and subsequent 401s on reconnect attempt. Observed logs / key artifacts: - api-gateway logs: repeated "token validation failed: missing session" traces correlated with spike window. - session-store metrics: sudden TTL eviction spikes at 02:14:12 UTC. - serving-runtime traces: streaming chunk checkpoint shows truncation where backend returned EOF mid-chunk. - billing ledger snapshot: handful of completions marked as retries with distinct request_ids and same session_id. Attachments: links to dashboards (Grafana, Kibana) included in related_confluence_pages.

Additional notes:
2026-03-08 02:29 - SRE: 'Deployed opt-in circuit at API gateway restricting in-flight session refresh to 1 per session_id as mitigation. Preliminary reduction in 401s.'
Initial hypothesis: token refresh race causing ephemeral missing session keys in KV-store under surge.
Reproduced locally with a synthetic surge harness using Orpheus's concurrency profile; observed identical TTL eviction behavior when the session-store TTL refresh loop conflicted with garbage collection under load.
Tracing revealed that some in-flight stream handlers called token-refresh path after the session TTL had been evicted; client retry loop attempted reconnection which produced duplicate completions billed separately.
Root cause: session-store TTL refresh path performed non-atomic read-modify-write against cache; under high concurrency the GC path could evict a key between read and write windows (race). Secondary factor: a recent cache config change (TTL bump roll-out) widened the window for the race during heavy churn.
Metrics: session-store eviction rate increased by 420% during spike; 5xx rate for affected API keys rose to 6.3% (baseline 0.1%). Billing delta: approximately 0.14% of daily token volume for Orpheus (isolated batch).
Related signals: correlation with a feature flag rollout that adjusted KV-cache sync interval on 2026-03-07 21:00 UTC. Linked PR for the config change: https://github.com/redwood/config/pull/678
Reviewed recent releases: no serving-runtime kernel changes implicated; change set limited to cache sync parameters.
Applied hotfix (02:48 UTC) to session-store: convert TTL refresh to atomic upsert and add short backoff on contention. Deployed as emergency patch to prod us-east-1.
Rolled back the TTL-bump config to previous value while we validated the atomic upsert under load.
Added API gateway soft-circuit limiting to reduce concurrent refresh attempts per session_id during bursts.
Billing remediation: issued a credit equal to duplicated completions for Orpheus for the affected window; finance ticket created for manual audit (FIN-2026-0310-01).
Customer communication: sent incident summary and credits on 2026-03-09; scheduled a conference call for 2026-03-11 to review postmortem and action items.
(P0) Replace non-atomic TTL refresh with atomic update in session-store (complete).
(P1) Add telemetry to surface TTL-refresh contention metrics and expose in Console per-tenant dashboard (owner: Observability team) - target 2026-03-28.
(P1) Update runbook playbook for session eviction spikes with recommended mitigation steps (circuit limits and transient backoff) - runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood/runbooks/pull/93.
(P2) Add integration test that simulates KV eviction race under surge as part of CI for session-store component.
(P3) Revisit cache sync interval rollout gating for config changes; add canary and staged ramp to avoid wide TTL-window shifts.
(P2) Schedule follow-up with Orpheus CSM and Engineering to validate production behavior after config re-rollout (2026-03-25).
payload.summary: Orpheus Media - sudden session token loss during traffic surge causing truncated streaming and transient billing discrepancies

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when their corporate edge rewrites Streaming SSE to a long-poll fallback path, the last ~1-2 sentences of responses are consistently missing after a reconnect.

Impact: Intermittent data loss for streaming responses behind certain proxies; affects customer-facing assistant content (missing trailing sentences). Reported by a Dedicated customer (NimbusDocs) using the hosted API through a corporate proxy that downgrades SSE to HTTP long-polling.

Observed behavior: Client receives streamed tokens, then connection is torn down by edge for long-poll fallback. When the session resumes the service returns an early 204/OK and the final trailer event (closing marker/end metadata) is not delivered to the client. Result: truncated final paragraph and absent terminal metadata (choice.finish_reason).

Expected behavior: Fallback path should replay or proxy through the complete trailing chunks or the server should re-emit terminal events after reconstitution so the client receives the full final sentence and closing metadata.
1) Customer environment: desktop app behind corporate proxy that strips SSE and does long-polling; use proxy that rewrites HTTP/1.1 to HTTP/1.0 and closes keepalive after 15s.
2) Open a streaming chat session against the Redwood hosted API with Accept: text/event-stream and keepalive enabled; send a prompt that yields a 60-120 token final paragraph.
3) Trigger a controlled network interruption to force the proxy to close and re-establish the HTTP connection (simulate edge path change or probe).
4) Observe on the client: streaming resumes but final 1-2 sentences are missing; server logs show a short-lived long-poll request that returns without the closing trailer event.
5) Reproduce reliably by toggling the proxy keepalive interval in synthetic lab; behavior observed ~7/10 runs.
[2026-03-10T14:08:12Z] proxy edge: Upstream accepted, id=xyz-7
[2026-03-10T14:08:26Z] client -> proxy: Connection close by proxy (keepalive expiry) (15s)
[2026-03-10T14:08:26Z] proxy -> rt-proxy: new long-poll /v1/stream?session=abc returning 200 OK (early-close)
[2026-03-10T14:08:26Z] rt-proxy: stream-session abc resumed; last-kv-checkpoint=0x7f1; trailer_flag=false
[2026-03-10T14:08:27Z] serving-runtime: produced final-choice tokens, emitted trailer meta (choice.finish_reason=length)
[2026-03-10T14:08:27Z] rt-proxy: upstream write failed: client closed connection; skipping trailer emission on long-poll path
Hypothesis 1: Long-poll fallback path short-circuits trailer emission when client socket indicates close; race between runtime's trailer write and proxy long-poll response commit.
Hypothesis 2: Proxy/edge performs an extra connection-level close that causes rt-proxy to treat resumed session as ephemeral and drop final metadata to avoid blocking write (backpressure handling path).
Repro steps validated in internal staging with our test proxy (haproxy) reproducing 80% of runs when keepalive <= 20s.
Observed difference vs normal SSE: SSE code path uses chunked transfer with streaming flush; long-poll path uses buffered response commit and currently lacks explicit trailer re-synthesis when the client reconnection occurs.
Logs indicate serving-runtime did emit finish trailer but rt-proxy logged upstream write failure before it could sink to the client long-poll response body.
Amelia Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged ticket to customer, requested example session IDs and sample network captures. First response within SLA.
NimbusDocs (Customer) 2026-03-10: Provided tcpdump + proxy logs and one failing session id (abc). They confirm this happens behind their Palo Alto NGFW which downgrades SSE to polling for legacy clients.
Diego Morales (SRE) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally using haproxy rewrite script. Confirmed trailer emission race. Created scoped patch to add server-side retry to ensure trailers are replayed on resumed long-poll responses (branch: fix/long-poll-trailer-replay).
Product (Benita Arora) 2026-03-11: Asked for risk assessment and whether this impacts other fallback paths (ws->long-poll, http2->http1).
Diego Morales (SRE) 2026-03-12: Hotfix staged in canary (us-east staging). Observed full trailer delivery in 95/100 synthetic runs. Plan: backport hotfix to production proxy layer and release rollout with feature flag to disable fallback replay as kill-switch.
NimbusDocs (Customer) 2026-03-12: Requested ETA for production fix and whether there is a short-term client workaround.
Support (Amelia) 2026-03-12: Provided customer workaround: enable direct SSE passthrough for Redwood endpoints or increase proxy keepalive to >= 60s; both mitigate until patch is rolled out.
Workaround provided to customer (enable SSE passthrough or increase proxy keepalive). Hotfix implemented in rt-proxy to replay trailers on long-poll resume (branch fix/long-poll-trailer-replay). Canary results positive; production rollout scheduled with a config flag and canary wedge. Postmortem and formal remediation tracked on confluence page. Follow-up: add integration test for long-poll fallback path and update runbooks to include proxy keepalive guidance.
Hotfix PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-proxy/pull/542
Canary deployed to us-east staging 2026-03-12 08:30Z; 95% success in synthetic tests.
Prod rollout planned 2026-03-13 with feature-flagged rollouts per region.
Post-deploy: monitor streaming error rates and truncated-response alerts for 48h; add automated regression test in CI.
payload.summary: Long-poll fallback closes early, truncating streamed tail on reconnect

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a staggered pinned-version rollout for redwood/gptj-13b-v1 in us-east, a small cohort of NovaPay tenants were routed to the degraded quantized variant (gptj-13b-quantized-v1) unexpectedly. Impact: ~0.8% of their traffic received degraded responses for ~18 minutes, causing subtle hallucination regressions in production. Environment: production (us-east), dedicated pool for NovaPay. Observed at 2026-02-18T09:12Z. This appears correlated with prewarm handshake operations and a concurrent coordinator prewarm retry that produced a sticky prewarm session on the orchestrator, preventing the normal pin commit and triggering fallback routing paths.
1) Start a staged pinned rollout for redwood/gptj-13b-v1 with canary weight 5%
2) Trigger concurrent prewarm by sending prefetched requests to a small tenant cohort with long streaming sessions
3) Simulate an orchestrator prewarm retry (kill prewarm worker during handshake)
4) Observe routing decision and tenant affinity after orchestrator resync
Expected: tenant remains on pinned variant or cleanly falls back without sticky prewarm state. Observed: tenant affinity persisted to an unexpected degraded variant until explicit token refresh or edge reconnection.
2026-02-18T09:11:42Z orchestrator[controller]: prewarm handshake start tenant=nvpay-cohort-17 request_id=req-0a12
2026-02-18T09:11:43Z edge-proxy[edge-7]: proxied session created sticky_prewarm_id=stick-99 status=OK
2026-02-18T09:12:01Z orchestrator[controller]: prewarm worker crashed during kvcache init tid=1723 err=oom
2026-02-18T09:12:05Z orchestrator[reconciler]: prewarm retry created sticky_prewarm_id=stick-99 reason=retry-after-crash
2026-02-18T09:12:10Z routing[router-3]: decision tenant=nvpay-cohort-17 -> variant=redwood/gptj-13b-quantized-v1 reason=prewarm-sticky-affinity
2026-02-18T09:29:22Z support: customer reported increased hallucinations in transactions feature session ids examples=[s-77,s-81]

Additional notes:
2026-02-18 18:45 - NovaPay (Customer): Confirmed drop in degraded responses after 13:10Z. Requesting root cause and long-term mitigation.
Preliminary: The orchestrator prewarm retry path attaches the previous sticky_prewarm_id if the original prewarm did not complete cleanly. This sticky id is treated by the edge routing layer as an affinity token and exercised during the routing decision, which can prefer compatible degraded variants when the pinned variant prewarm isn't confirmed.
Reproduction: Local reproduction succeeded by killing prewarm worker mid-handshake; router resolved tenant to quantized variant due to sticky affinity header 'x-prewarm-id' being present and unresolved.
Scope: Affected ~0.8% of NovaPay traffic within the canary window; no other customers observed in initial triage. Root cause tied to concurrent prewarm crash + retry within dedicated pool for NovaPay.
Temporary mitigation: Forced routing override removed sticky prewarm header at edge for NovaPay; revert applied once patch shipped.
Code investigation: orchestrator/controller prewarm retry logic needs to generate fresh session ids and ensure pin_commit flag is re-evaluated on retry. Edge should avoid treating incomplete prewarm ids as authoritative for model selection.
Root cause: prewarm retry logic in orchestrator reused sticky prewarm ids after worker crash, and edge routing used that id to prefer a compatible quantized variant while pin commit was outstanding. Fix: change prewarm retry to generate new prewarm session ids and mark incomplete prewarm sessions as transient so edge ignores them for routing decisions. Deployed patch in orchestrator (PR 1298) and edge-proxy change (PR 447). Emergency override lifted 2026-02-19 03:12Z. Post-deployment verification: monitored for 48 hours; no recurrence. Follow-ups: add unit test for prewarm-retry behavior, add metric for sticky_prewarm reuse, update prewarm runbook.
1) Merge PR github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1298 to ensure fresh prewarm ids on retry
2) Backport fix to stable branch and deploy to dedicated pools (done 2026-02-19)
3) Edge change github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/447 to ignore incomplete prewarm ids for routing decisions
4) Add alert 'orchestrator.prewarm.retry-sticky-id' to PagerDuty, threshold >5/min
5) Update confluence runbook to include prewarm-retry checklist and verify pin commit after prewarm completes
payload.summary: Sticky prewarm race causes tenant diversion to degraded variant during pinned-version rollout

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart is seeing sporadic per-request stalls when using the Structured Output (JSON) mode. Requests look like they begin streaming tokens but the stream / HTTP response sometimes hangs for 10-60s at the end of generation and eventually hits client-side timeout. This behavior started after a traffic increase and after the model catalog rolled a minor model variant update last week.

Impact:
- High 95th/99th latency for calls with structured_output=true for this customer
- Several timed-out user-facing requests reported by BrightCart; conversion impact reported by customer CS team
- Occasional increased error rates (up to 2.3% 5xx and client timeouts) for affected routes

Environment:
- Redwood hosted Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated GPU cluster) in us-east-1
- Serving runtime v1.9.2 on dedicated nodes; api-gateway v2.1.0
- Customer requests use structured_output=true and streaming=true with a JSON schema for product_catalog responses

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) POST to /v1/generate with model=open-lama-13b-v2 and structured_output=true
2) Provide schema with nested arrays (catalog -> items[]) and ask for generation with max_tokens ~1024
3) Observe streaming SSE; in ~85% of requests the stream completes normally, in ~15% the stream outputs the closing bracket then stalls (no FIN or stream end) for 15-60s and client disconnects

Observed behavior:
- Token stream appears to emit final content but the HTTP connection remains open without a final stream termination event (SSE end)
- Server-side request remains in RUNNING state on runtime for additional 20-40s after last token emitted
- CPU on the worker spikes during the stall window and then drops when the request finally exits

Expected behavior:
- Stream should close promptly after generation completes and response should be marked as completed with < 2s of post-generation cleanup

Logs / snippets (customer and runtime):
- Customer trace: request_id=cust-BR-7721-20260312
- Runtime worker logs (excerpt):
  [2026-03-12T15:03:10Z] INFO request=cust-BR-7721 token_emit=last_chunk
  [2026-03-12T15:03:10Z] DEBUG json_validator: starting schema finalization
  [2026-03-12T15:03:10Z] DEBUG json_validator: validating 3 nested arrays
  [2026-03-12T15:03:25Z] WARN request=cust-BR-7721 decode_wait: waiting for downstream drain
  [2026-03-12T15:03:48Z] ERROR request=cust-BR-7721 worker=worker-7 hang_detected: blocking syscall in validator

Additional context:
- Customer reports flaky reproduction; not all requests with the same payload hang
- Quick mitigation (customer): disabling structured_output (returning plain text) stops the stalls
- No recent changes to the customer schema; model variant rollout occurred ~72 hours prior to first reports

Attachments:
- Customer's example prompt and schema (sanitized) attached to the ticket


Additional notes:
2026-03-12 18:40 - BrightCart (Customer CS - Emily Wong): Shared sanitized prompt + schema and noted that issue correlates with lists of >150 items in 'items' array. They can repro internally ~30% of the time with the shared payload.
2026-03-13 11:30 - Eng (runtime) - Sofia Alvarez: Investigating change in model variant that increased average token length in final chunks which triggers validator to re-scan the full response for schema anchoring. Opened PR to add streaming-validation short-circuit for final chunk when schema already satisfied (runtime PR #438).
Perf traces show blocking in python json_validator for ~10-30s in affected requests.
Reproduction successful with customer's sanitized schema + large item arrays under load (concurrency 20+).
Kernel-level profiling did not show syscall-level stalls; CPU bound on Python thread (GIL) and expensive string ops are primary suspect.
Model variant change increased average token length and introduced extra trailing whitespace tokens in final chunk; triggers validator to do full-buffer rescans instead of incremental checks.
Temporary mitigation validated: disabling structured_output eliminates the hang; switching to non-streaming also avoids the streaming-end hang.
Related tickets: SUP-7021 (schema validation regressions) and SUP-6012 (stream serialization backpressure) — share similar themes but different root causes.
Proposed permanent fix: implement streaming short-circuit in runtime validator and move heavy validation off the GIL-bound path (native C extension or offload to worker threadpool).
Customer workaround (accepted): set streaming=false for critical endpoints, which causes validation to be synchronous but avoids streamed hang behavior.
Alternative: set structured_output=false to return plain text and perform JSON parsing client-side.
Throttle concurrent structured-output requests (reduce concurrency below 10) as a temporary operational mitigation.
If using schema with very large arrays, consider paginating items or returning compressed/condensed representations to reduce validation work.
Eng (runtime) to merge PR #438 to add streaming-validation short-circuit and run internal perf tests (target: 2026-03-16).
If PR proves effective, schedule hotfix rollout to dedicated pools in us-east-1 (canary then full) — target window 2026-03-17.
Explore implementing C-based validator or offload path to avoid GIL-bound stalls in high-concurrency scenarios (RFC by 2026-03-20).
Postmortem and customer-facing RCA to be drafted after root cause and fixes are deployed; owner: Marcus Li.
In Progress - runtime PR opened to short-circuit streaming validation (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/438).
Customer accepted workaround and applied streaming=false for critical endpoints; reported immediate reduction in timeouts.
Waiting on performance validation and canary rollout results before marking Resolved.
payload.summary: Structured-output JSON mode causing sporadic token-decoding stalls and client timeouts

payload.description:
Issue summary:
- Customer BlueArc reports elevated 5xx rate (502/503) on streaming routes during evening business hours. Errors began ~2026-03-13 18:05 UTC and show repeated short spikes (1–3 minutes) with increased tail-latency for streaming sessions.

Impact:
- Multiple long-lived streaming client sessions observed disconnecting and failing to resume. Customer reports degraded UX for interactive analytics feature; estimated 12% of streaming calls in the hour experienced errors.

Timeline / Observed pattern:
- 2026-03-13 18:02 UTC: first error cluster; apigw error rate to this tenant increased to 5xx ~18%.
- 18:05–18:12 UTC: short oscillations of 5xx with concurrent rise in upstream preempt events and runtime worker restarts.
- 18:20 UTC: transient decrease, then another cluster at 19:10 UTC with similar pattern.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool serving BlueArc (tenant id: ta-9043) in us-east-1, running model variants redwood/gptx-7b and redwood/gptx-13b-int8.
- Streaming route: /v1/stream/chat (http2). TLS termination at edge, keepalive proxied through streaming-proxy.

Steps to reproduce (customer reproduction):
1) Establish 40 long-lived streaming sessions that send alternating short user messages (~100 tokens) and occasional large prompts (~2500 tokens).
2) Let sessions idle with periodic keepalive pings from the SDK (interval ~25s).
3) Observe intermittent 502/503 responses and session resets after several minutes.

Observed artifacts / logs:
- apigw logs show HTTP/2 RST_STREAM followed by 502 responses from the proxy.
- streaming-proxy metrics show a short surge in concurrent streams per worker followed by worker preempt and SIGTERM -> restart.
- runtime logs: NVML preempt events and 'worker: preempted due to scheduler pressure' entries; no explicit OOMs.
- TLS logs: occasional TLS renegotiation (client-initiated) at time of spikes; keepalive intervals for some clients drifted to 0–2s in traces (SDK bug suspected).

Initial triage notes:
- Pattern suggests amplification: large prompt fanout (long generation) ties up worker threads while many short heartbeats/keepalives increase scheduling overhead at proxy, causing accept/handshake queuing and eventual worker preempt.
- TLS renegotiation coincident with stream spikes appears to increase CPU overhead on proxy and apigw.

Immediate customer-facing message we sent:
- "We're investigating elevated streaming errors impacting some long-lived sessions. Engineering is triaging runtime preemption and proxy scheduling; we'll follow up within the hour with mitigation steps and ETA."
2026-03-13 18:25 - Support (Aisha): Collected initial logs from BlueArc tenant and escalated to SRE. Noted concurrent keepalive storm patterns in proxy metrics.
2026-03-13 18:40 - SRE (Marco): Attached flamegraph of streaming-proxy CPU during spike; saw frequent context switches and a rising accept queue. Hypothesis: short keepalive intervals from SDK + TLS renegotiation amplifies per-connection CPU.
2026-03-13 19:05 - Eng (Liang Chen): Runtime reports worker preempt events when per-worker concurrent streams exceed ~48. No NVML OOMs, but scheduler marks GPU as busy and signals preempt to reclaim cycles for other tasks.
2026-03-13 19:30 - Support (Aisha): Informed customer of temporary mitigation (client-side keepalive increase) and asked for replication script. Customer provided reproduction harness that generates 40 streams with intermittent large prompts.
2026-03-13 20:10 - SRE (Marco): Deployed a temporary apigw config change to increase accept queue depth for the affected route by 2x and turned on more aggressive connection backpressure in streaming-proxy. Observed reduction in 5xx rate for subsequent spike window.
2026-03-14 09:12 - Eng (Liang Chen): Opening follow-up task to add telemetry: per-tenant streaming concurrency gauge and TLS renegotiation counter to correlate with preempt events. Assigned to runtime team backlog.
2026-03-14 11:00 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed seeing fewer disconnects overnight after applying keepalive workaround and after our temporary edge config change. Asking to keep ticket open while eng implements durable fix.
Detailed traces show two contributing factors: 1) client SDK bug causing aggressive keepalive behavior (25s configured but observed bursts of 0-2s) leading to high syscall rates at proxy; 2) large prompt fanout holds GPU kernels open for long real-time durations, which reduces worker availability and triggers scheduler preempt signals. Combined, these create a short-lived amplification loop where proxy CPU and runtime scheduler interact and produce 5xx spikes. Correlated metrics: streaming_proxy.cpu_ns, apigw.accept_queue_depth, runtime.worker_preempt_count. No memory OOMs observed. Next steps identified: durable proxy backpressure improvements, runtime scheduler rate-limits per-tenant long-running generation, and customer SDK patch to fix keepalive jitter.
1) Customer: Increase client-side keepalive interval to >=60s and disable client-initiated TLS renegotiation in SDK (patch available in customer SDK v2.3.1). 2) Platform: Applied temporary apigw accept-queue increase and enabled streaming-proxy backpressure—monitoring for regressions. 3) Avoid concurrent large prompt fanout across many long-lived streams until fixes rolled out.
- Engineering to implement per-tenant streaming concurrency telemetry and a soft cap to avoid worker preempt cascade (tracked in runtime backlog).
- Runtime to add a graceful preempt backoff to avoid immediate SIGTERM on scheduler pressure.
- SDK team to publish recommended keepalive defaults and patch to avoid renegotiation.
- Support to coordinate customer validation and keep ticket open until fix rolled out and validated (aim target: 2026-03-20).
payload.summary: Intermittent evening 5xx surge from streaming fanout + keepalive mismatch causing upstream worker preemptions

payload.description:
Customer reports that rotating API keys via Hosted API returns 403 Forbidden. This started after their org was enabled for RBAC v2 (feature flag) and coincides with new gateway authz middleware behavior (deny-by-default).

Impact:
- Customer security team cannot rotate keys as part of their credential hygiene checks.
- Blocks their pilot readiness checklist and internal security review timeline.

Customer report (Ironbank Financial):
- Endpoint: POST /v1/api-keys/{key_id}/rotate
- Response: 403 Forbidden
- Behavior: Happens consistently for their Admin user/token; creating keys still works via Console, but rotation fails via API.

Initial hypothesis:
- Route missing/mis-mapped permission annotation OR legacy RBAC v1 -> v2 mapping does not grant rotate permission for their existing built-in role binding.
- Gateway is enforcing deny-by-default and returning 403 where previously service allowed.

Notes:
- Customer provided request IDs and timestamps (see Logs section).
- This appears limited to key rotation; other admin endpoints (list keys, create key) succeed.
2025-03-21 09:18 PT (Colin O'Donnell): Customer reports 403 on key rotation endpoint. They are in Hosted API prod (us-east). They can create/list keys but rotation is blocked. Asking for request IDs + exact endpoint/path.
2025-03-21 10:02 PT (Customer via Colin): Repro is stable. Example curl:
POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/api-keys/ak_01HRR.../rotate
Authorization: Bearer <admin token>
Returns 403 {"error":{"type":"permission_denied","message":"Not authorized"}}.
Request IDs: rwreq_7f3c2a9b8c, rwreq_7f3c2aa11d (around 2025-03-21 09:54 PT).
2025-03-21 10:25 PT (Amara Diallo): Pulled gateway logs for rwreq_7f3c2a9b8c. Denial is coming from gateway middleware (not upstream service). Denial reason code: MISSING_PERMISSION. Required permission recorded as rbac.api_keys.rotate (exact string in log). User has org role binding that includes rbac.api_keys.read + rbac.api_keys.create but not rotate.
2025-03-21 10:31 PT (Kaitlyn Nguyen): This looks like a gap in the default role template / v1->v2 mapping for legacy “Org Admin” for Hosted. Rotate permission was added later in the permission registry and didn’t get included in the legacy mapping table. Suggest: patch policy bundle mapping + confirm endpoint annotation is correct per API standards.
2025-03-21 11:05 PT (Amara Diallo): Confirmed endpoint annotation is correct and matches authorization-check-patterns (gateway enforced). The rotate route was recently added to sensitive coverage and is now enforced by deny-by-default. The missing piece is default permissions for role template + migration mapping.
2025-03-21 11:26 PT (Naomi Feldman): For enterprise pilots we should treat key rotation as critical. Please prioritize a safe fix that does not broaden permissions unintentionally. Also ensure denial reason is visible for org admins via debug header if they enable it.
2025-03-21 12:10 PT (Amara Diallo): Workaround for customer while fix rolls out: create a new API key via Console (or POST /v1/api-keys create) and revoke old key; rotation is blocked until permissions updated. If they require rotation semantics, we can temporarily grant rbac.api_keys.rotate via a custom role binding (Support-assisted) for their org.
2025-03-22 09:42 PT (Amara Diallo): Fix prepared: update role template for Hosted “Org Admin” to include rbac.api_keys.rotate and update v1->v2 migration mapping table so existing org_admin bindings inherit rotate. Added regression test to ensure rotate permission is included for org_admin. Rolling out behind RBAC policy bundle version bump. Tracking via RBAC v2 rollout dashboard deny spikes.
2025-03-22 16:05 PT (Colin O'Donnell): Informed customer of workaround + ETA for fix (next business day rollout). Customer requested confirmation once effective; they are running compliance tests for their SOC-aligned checklist.
2025-03-24 08:30 PT (Amara Diallo): Deployed policy bundle v2025.03.24-1 to Hosted control plane + gateway (us-east). Verified with internal test org in prod: org_admin can now rotate keys; read-only role still denied. Deny-by-default preserved for other sensitive routes.
2025-03-24 09:15 PT (Colin O'Donnell): Customer confirmed rotation now works (same endpoint) and 403 is resolved. Closing ticket.
1) Use an org with RBAC v2 enabled (feature flag).
2) Authenticate as a user/service principal with the built-in legacy-migrated “Org Admin” role binding.
3) Call POST /v1/api-keys/{key_id}/rotate against a valid API key in the org.
4) Observe 403 Forbidden from API Gateway with permission_denied.
Expected: 200 OK and rotated key material returned per API behavior; audit log entry emitted for key rotation.
Gateway log (rwreq_7f3c2a9b8c): decision=deny reason=MISSING_PERMISSION required_permission=rbac.api_keys.rotate subject=usr_01HT... scope=org:org_9pK... policy_version=rbac-bundle-2025.03.21-2
Response body (customer): {"error":{"type":"permission_denied","message":"Not authorized"}}
After fix verification (internal, 2025-03-24): decision=allow required_permission=rbac.api_keys.rotate policy_version=rbac-bundle-2025.03.24-1
Root cause: RBAC v2 deny-by-default enforcement at the API Gateway began enforcing the rotate API key route using permission rbac.api_keys.rotate. The built-in legacy-migrated Org Admin role mapping did not include the rotate permission, causing unexpected 403s for customers relying on RBAC v1-era admin bindings.

Fix: Updated the default role template and v1->v2 migration mapping to include rbac.api_keys.rotate for Org Admin (Hosted), and bumped the RBAC policy bundle version. Verified allow/deny behavior with regression tests and production smoke test in us-east.

Customer workaround during incident window: Create a new API key and revoke the old key (no rotation), or Support-assisted temporary custom role binding granting rbac.api_keys.rotate.
Add CI guardrail: any new api_keys.* permission must be reviewed against built-in role templates + migration mapping (owner: Naomi Feldman).
Add a console-side hint/CTA for admins when rotation is denied (link to permission viewer + 'request access') (owner: Tessa Morgan).
Add alert on sudden increase in denies for high-criticality permissions like api_keys.rotate post policy bundle release (owner: Logan Wright).
payload.summary: Hosted API: unexpected 403 Forbidden on API key rotation endpoint after RBAC v2 rollout (deny-by-default)

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports automated background jobs that rely on service-account token exchange are intermittently failing with 401 Unauthorized when talking to Redwood Private control-plane APIs. Failures started after WAF policy push last week.

Impact:
- Multiple scheduled sync jobs for Helios Therapeutics are failing (approx. 15% of runs) resulting in delayed model-rollout metadata updates and missed audit entries.
- Customer-facing UI unaffected, but background automation and admin tooling are impacted.

Environment:
- Private deployment (Helios Therapeutics VPC) behind customer-managed WAF + Redwood identity-proxy.
- Region: us-east-1.
- Affected paths: /v1/internal/token-exchange, /admin/audit/logs

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Trigger service account token exchange from customer CI (client_assertion JWT signed by customer service-key).
2) Request reaches customer WAF, then to Redwood identity-proxy which forwards to control-plane token-exchange endpoint.
3) Some requests result in 401 with message: "invalid_client_assertion: kid header missing or key not found"

Observed behavior:
- 401 responses correlate to requests that show modified JWT on the wire where the 'kid' header is absent.
- Replaying captured raw JWTs directly to control-plane (bypassing WAF) succeeds.
- WAF recent policy change includes header normalization and a custom header-scanning rule.

Expected behavior:
- Service-account JWTs forwarded intact; token-exchange succeeds regardless of WAF in path.

Logs / sample traces:
- identity-proxy logs show token exchange request ID: tx-31a7b. Error: "JWKS lookup failed for kid: null"
- WAF debug capture (provided by customer) shows incoming token has header {
  "alg": "RS256", "kid": "svc-prod-17"
} but forwarded token header lacks kid.

Initial triage:
- Support reproduced missing 'kid' when request passes through a specific WAF rule set (rule set id: X-WAF-2026-09).
- Hypothesis: WAF performs JWT canonicalization/inspection and strips certain header fields when forwardable header size or character set triggers normalization.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated timestamps between WAF captures and identity-proxy logs show exact requests that lost kid.
- Team verified identity-proxy and token-exchange service accept JWTs with and without kid, but our key-selection flow depends on kid for service-account projection. Without kid, the control-plane rejects the assertion rather than attempting key discovery for security reasons.
- Customer WAF vendor confirms that a header-sanitization subrule strips characters after policy update when header contains dash-separated tokens matching their suspicious pattern matcher. The 'svc-prod-17' kid matched that pattern and was removed.

Workaround applied:
- Temporary mitigation: customer disabled the specific header-sanitization subrule and added a WAF exception for Authorization header to stop stripping 'kid'.
- Support enabled a short-lived permissive path: token-exchange accepts kid-less assertions for Helios if a signed client-cert is presented (audit-flag enabled). This was rolled out with strict logging and expires in 48 hours.

Root cause:
- A customer-managed WAF policy update introduced a header-sanitization rule that strips header fragments matching a heuristic. The service-account 'kid' values produced by the customer's key management matched that heuristic and were removed, causing verification to fail.

Resolution plan:
1) Recommend permanent WAF exception for Authorization header parsing or adjust WAF rule to ignore JWT header structure.
2) Identity team to implement a safer fallback: if kid missing, attempt strict, logged key-discovery restricted to configured trusted issuers for private deployments (requires feature flag and security review).
3) Create a post-incident config checklist for private customers that includes WAF header exceptions for Authorization and preserve-kid.

Follow-ups:
- SRE/Identity to draft PR for controlled key-discovery fallback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/412
- Solutions Engineer to update Helios deployment runbook with WAF exception steps.
- Create KB article for customers about common WAF behaviors affecting JWT headers.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:22 - Helios ops (Customer): Rolled back WAF policy change and verified scheduled jobs recovered to normal run success rates. Requested permanent guidance and assistance to avoid reintroducing issue.
2026-03-12 16:05 - Support (Elena): Drafted KB for customer and internal runbook checklist. Linked PR for identity-proxy fallback and opened INT follow-up for security review.
WAF header-sanitization matched dash-separated kid patterns. Customer provided WAF capture confirmed modification. Identity code intentionally rejects kid-less JWTs for safety; fallback requires careful security constraints. Local reproduction through WAF test harness succeeded.
Customer disabled the header-sanitization subrule and added an Authorization-header exception in WAF. Support also temporarily enabled a client-cert gated acceptance path for Helios for 48 hours.
Customer-managed WAF sanitized Authorization header and stripped 'kid' values matching its heuristic after a policy push, leading to assertion verification failures in the private control-plane.
Temporary customer WAF rollback + identity-proxy temporary gated acceptance resolved the immediate impact. Next steps: permanent WAF guidance, code path for constrained key-discovery behind a feature flag, and customer runbook updates. Security review scheduled.
Ship WAF guidance KB to customer and update onboarding docs
Complete PR for key-discovery fallback behind feature flag and logging (PR #412)
Schedule security review for fallback behavior in private deployments
Add WAF exception checklist to private deployment runbook
payload.summary: WAF removes JWT 'kid' header during service-account token exchange in private deployment leading to 401s

comments: 2026-03-12T09:15:00Z Maya Chen: Customer reported first noticed at 08:40 UTC. Provided sample request and traces. Marked as P1 due to checkout timeouts.

2026-03-12T10:02:00Z Arjun Patel: Reproduced locally with AcmePayments request shape. Observed repeated schema.compile on every tool invocation. Opening investigation with runtime/validator teams. Linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1843.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer AcmePayments reports large increases in P95/P99 end-to-end latency for completions that include tool/function calls. The regression appears to correlate with a recent change in the function-proxy handshake and an aggressive per-invocation JSON schema compilation step in the validator. Impact: Several customer endpoints experiencing 2x-4x tail latency increases during peak hours, causing timeouts in the customer's checkout flow. Business impact: failed authorizations and elevated error rates for enterprise production traffic. Environment: prod, us-east-1, dedicated enterprise tenant for AcmePayments. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a completion request with 3 sequential tool calls (validate_card -> check_balance -> create_auth) using the customer's tool adapter config. 2) Observe traces via /trace endpoint and measure end-to-end latency for tool-enabled vs plain text completions. 3) Reproduce at scale by sending 1000 requests/min with a similar request shape. Observed behavior: median latency for tool-enabled completions is ~180ms higher than baseline; P95 increased from ~420ms to ~1.1s and P99 spikes up to 2.4s. Traces show multiple 50-250ms synchronous gaps attributed to function-proxy handshake and repeated "schema.compile" calls. Expected behavior: handshake should be <50ms and schema validation should be cached/reused to avoid per-call compilation. Logs/Traces: Attached (file references in ticket) - trace ids: trace-us-east-20260312-abc123, trace-us-east-20260313-def456. Validator logs contain repeated: "schema.compile: cache_miss=true, compile_time_ms=82" on every invocation. Function-proxy logs show handshake RTTs of 40-220ms during spikes. Additional notes: issue concentrated on requests with multiple short tool calls; single tool-call flows less impacted. Occurs during customer peak traffic and correlates with recent proxy validator deployment (2026-03-11).
Initial findings: 1) Histogram and flame graphs point to two dominant contributors: synchronous proxy handshake (blocking wait for tool adapter readiness) and per-invocation JSON schema compile inside the schema-validator process. 2) Schema validator recently changed from 'compile-on-first-use' with LRU cache to 'compile-every-request' due to a bugfix intended to enforce strict validation isolation for enterprise tenants. 3) The function-proxy handshake includes a synchronous SSL/TLS handshake and a metadata exchange; in our code path this is done inline on the request critical path. Data points: p95 latency delta = +680ms for affected requests; during one spike we saw 12% of requests with 2+ handshake events >150ms. Hypotheses: A) schema.compile is CPU-bound and when cache_miss=True it costs ~80-120ms and spikes under CPU contention; B) synchronous proxy handshake amplifies tail when combined with multiple sequential tool calls; C) lack of schema caching and blocking sync calls produce multiplicative effect for sequences of short tools. Temporary mitigations attempted: turned on schema_validator debug logs (no change), increased validator worker pool from 8->12 (reduced median slightly), enabled per-tenant adapter warm-up for a subset of routes (reduced handshake occurrences but not eliminated). Correlation with PR: serving-runtime PR #1843 touched proxy handshake retry logic and may have affected connection reuse behavior. Traces and flame graphs shared in ticket attachments.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 08:30 - AcmePayments (Customer): Customer notes that timeouts up to 3s caused a small % of transactions to be retried client-side; asking for ETA on fix and temporary workaround.
Workaround applied (2026-03-14 09:10 UTC): rolled out a targeted hotfix to function-proxy in us-east-1 for AcmePayments tenant that introduces an in-memory schema cache keyed by tool signature and an async handshake fast-path. Behavior: per-invocation compile cache hits eliminated for common tool signatures, and handshake now uses connection warm-pool to avoid blocking on first-request TLS handshake. Immediate effect: P95 for affected routes dropped from ~1.1s to ~520ms in canary. Planned next steps: 1) publish patch to all enterprise tenants in us-east (canary -> gradual rollout), 2) add metrics (schema.compile.cache_hit, proxy.handshake_time_ms) to monitoring and dashboards, 3) backport safe cache behavior to older runtime branches, 4) add automated perf regression test in CI that exercises multi-tool sequences. Timeline: canary applied 2026-03-14 09:10 UTC, global rollout planned for 2026-03-16 pending telemetry. If rollback needed we have rollback plan to disable cache and revert handshake changes via runtime feature flag.
Add synthetic workload to perf-suite that runs 3-sequential-tool scenarios and gates on P95/P99 (owner: Perf Eng, due: 2026-03-20)
Instrument schema-validator with per-tenant cache hit/miss metrics and expose in Console (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-18)
Backport schema cache fix to v1.2.x branch and cut release (owner: Runtime Eng, due: 2026-03-17)
Create runbook entry for diagnosing tool-proxy handshake latency and add to Confluence (owner: Support, due: 2026-03-21)
Follow up with AcmePayments on impact and confirm reduction in customer-side retries (owner: CSM, due: 2026-03-16)
payload.summary: Elevated tail latency for tool-enabled completions due to synchronous tool-proxy handshake and per-invocation schema compilation

comments: 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Aisha Khan: Initial report received from customer at 09:12 UTC. Attached their p99/per-route graphs and request IDs for one of the affected windows.

2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Ravi Menon: Triage started. I see correlated autoscaler scaling-up/spike logs for dp-nimbus-usw2-5 at 09:08-09:22 UTC. Opening investigation and pulling cluster allocation traces.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer Nimbus Analytics is observing repeated p50/p99 throughput degradation on their dedicated pool during mid-day windows. The degradation corresponds with a flurry of many short-lived, high-frequency client streams from a single tenant (internal batch job) that intermittently saturates slot allocation and triggers autoscaler churn.

Impact:
- Customer reports ~30-45% reduction in sustained throughput for their latency-sensitive routes for ~10-30 minute episodes.
- Affects production inference for multiple pinned models.
- Customer business impact: inference backlog and degraded feature availability for end users during peak window.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-nimbus-usw2-5 (reserved cluster)

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - SRE (Marta Lopez): Observed many ephemeral connections from tenant "nimbus-batch" with avg duration 9s and very high inter-arrival rate. Prefetch subsystem shows repeated prefetch/evict cycles; kv-cache growth for other tenants stalls during these windows.
2026-03-12 - Eng (Ravi Menon): Implemented temporary mitigation: throttled tenant via rate-limit rule and applied an emergency affinity soft-evict to rebalance slots. Early telemetry shows throughput restored to ~95% baseline within 8 minutes of the action.
2026-03-12 - Customer (Nimbus Ops): Confirming recovered performance in their dashboards. They request explanation and permanent fix options.
Timeline and observations:
- 2026-03-10 09:05 UTC: first small-stream flood starts. Client telemetry indicates a tenant job that spins up thousands of short streams to multiple routes.
- 09:07-09:12 UTC: autoscaler interprets higher request rate and attempts to expand GPU allocation; due to slot granularity new GPUs are attached and background prefetchers start filling KV cache for hot models.
- 09:12-09:18 UTC: eviction/rehydration thrash: ephemeral tenant streams frequently tear down slot affinity leading to serialization of batchers and GPU slot fragmentation. Other tenants (including Nimbus customer production routes) see increased queueing and a drop in realized batch sizes.
- 09:18-09:25 UTC: autoscaler overshoots and then retracts, leaving fragmented slots and temporary GPU attachment churn.
Key signals pulled:
- Serving-runtime logs: repeated "slot-unavailable" and "batch-flush-from-eviction" messages correlated to tenant id nimbus-batch.
Mitigation steps taken:
1) Applied tenant-scoped rate-limit to the offending tenant (nimbus-batch) to cap short-stream concurrency.
2) Executed emergency soft-evict for ephemeral tenant allocations to force consolidation and permit fair slot assignment.
3) Applied temporary autoscaler param adjustment: increased stabilization window from 30s to 90s for dp-nimbus-usw2-5 to reduce oscillatory attach/detach during short bursts.
Outcome:
- Post-mitigation telemetry (09:28 UTC onwards) shows customer throughput returned to ~95% of baseline and p99 latency improved. No longer triggering autoscaler rapid attach/detach loop.
Permanent follow-ups (action items):
- Ops: schedule tenant throttling rule in policy engine for all dedicated pools vulnerable to short-stream floods (ticket INT-43821, created).
- Eng: evaluate prefetch and KV-cache eviction heuristic to avoid aggressive fill during transient short-stream floods (RFC by 2026-03-20).
- Product: contact customer with options: quota limits, dedicated route rate-limits, or migration to a smaller-isolated pool for bursty batch jobs.
- Monitoring: add alert for slot fragmentation ratio > 0.25 and autoscaler attach/retract frequency > 3/min for dedicated pools.
We will keep this ticket open until permanent mitigation is scheduled or Nimbus accepts recommended changes.
Create follow-up ENG ticket for prefetch heuristics (due 2026-03-20)
Ops to roll global dedicated-policy for short-stream throttles (ETA 2026-03-18)
CS to schedule customer sync to review options and collect traffic samples (by 2026-03-15)
payload.summary: Intermittent dedicated throughput sag caused by ephemeral tenant spillover and slot unfairness

comments: 2026-03-05T10:05:00Z Aisha Rahman: Logged ticket with customer, requested tcpdump and SDK logs. Customer provided edge-proxy config and timestamped traces.
2026-03-08T08:55:00Z Aisha Rahman: Notified customer of canary testing and recommended temporary mitigations while patch is validated.
payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent truncated or duplicated final JSON arrays on websocket streaming sessions. Impact: Several production flows (web chat + background mobile sync) are returning partial outputs (missing closing array bracket or duplicated terminal 'end' event) causing downstream JSON parsing errors in their backend and mobile apps. Environment: MercuryForms runs on a Private deployment (VPC) with an HA edge proxy (customer-managed) in front of Redwood's VPC egress; they use our iOS SDK in background URLSession mode for mobile sync and a Node websocket client on server-side. Problem first observed after their edge proxy upgrade (transparent TCP pooler) on 2026-03-04.

Observed behavior: - Websocket sessions are established and begin streaming. - On ~0.6% of sessions the final frames arrive fragmented or interleaved: server emits close/terminal event but trailing JSON array is split across fragments in non-sequential order, producing either a truncated JSON or a duplicated trailing element. - Issue happens only when connection reseat occurs while stream is active (their edge proxies reuse TLS session tickets and perform connection pooling). - Reproduction appears more likely for longer streams (>= 1200 tokens) and when client reconnection uses a reused session ticket.

Expected behavior: Streaming websocket sessions should preserve frame ordering and terminal-event atomicity across TLS session-ticket resumption and upstream connection pooling. Terminal JSON structures (final array/object) should never be split into interleaved fragments that lead to invalid payloads.

1) Customer runs long-running streaming request against hosted websocket completion on model gpt-open-8k-v1 in prod us-east-1.
2) From their edge proxy, trigger a connection reseat by forcing TCP connection churn (e.g., rotate backend pool, short connection TTL) while stream is mid-flight.
3) Observe final messages on client: occasionally see truncated JSON array or duplicated trailing object leading to parse failures.
4) More likely when using iOS SDK background URLSession reuse or node ws client reusing TLS session tickets.
Notes: We were able to reproduce in a synthetic harness when simulating a proxy that re-orders small fragmented application frames during connection rebind.
Trace id: trace-20260305-73af | ws_conn_id: 7f3a9c | timeline: stream_start -> keepalive -> conn_rebind -> terminal_fragment_received (partial) -> parser_error
Server snippet: FRAME_SEQ: [1,2,5,3,4] detected for conn 7f3a9c before finalization (expected monotonic).
Customer-side stacktrace: SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input at parse (mobile-sync v2.3.1)
2026-03-05 09:20 PST - Initial triage by Support (Aisha): gathered client logs and reproduction steps; confirmed customer edge proxy upgrade correlates with start of errors.
2026-03-05 11:10 PST - Eng (Tomás) ran synthetic harness: simulated connection pooling + TLS session-ticket reuse; reproduced ~0.4% failure rate matching customer symptom set.
Hypothesis: edge proxy connection reuse + internal worker handoff combined with our websocket fragmentation logic can allow out-of-order assembly of small control and data frames when connection reseat happens during in-flight fragmented payloads.
Evidence: Server trace shows non-monotonic frame sequence numbers for affected sessions. Frame seq reordering occurs only when upstream connection id changes mid-stream (proxy rebind path).
Mitigations tried: 1) temporary customer-side workaround to disable aggressive TCP pooling at edge proxy - eliminated reproduction in their canary region. 2) toggling iOS SDK to avoid background URLSession reuse reduced mobile incidence significantly.
Next steps: Prepare runtime patch to make the websocket streaming reassembly tolerant to transient frame reordering at terminal boundary and ensure terminal-event atomic commit is idempotent. Add additional guard rails in edge-worker to buffer and reorder small terminal fragments by sequence id before handing to the parser.

Additional notes:
2026-03-05 11:30 - Tomás Ortega (Eng): Reproduced locally with harness. Assigned to streaming-runtime team for patching. Opening follow-up INT ticket for internal change (INT-4121).
2026-03-06 09:00 - Customer (MercuryForms SRE - Elena K): Confirmed disabling 'pool-keepalive' on proxy reduced errors in staging. Asking for ETA on permanent fix for production.
2026-03-07 14:20 - Tomás Ortega (Eng): Implemented candidate fix: buffer terminal fragments up to 200ms and reorder by sequence id before parse. Running canary on serving-runtime in our staging cluster.
2026-03-08 16:40 - Customer (Elena K): Canary results look good in staging; will coordinate production rollout window with their infra team.
Workaround: Customer temporarily disabled aggressive connection pooling on their edge proxy and switched iOS clients to non-background URLSession reuse; both reduced error rate to ~0.01%. Permanent fix: deployed runtime patch that buffers and reorders terminal websocket fragments by sequence ID and makes terminal-event delivery idempotent. Patch rolled out to 10% canary on 2026-03-07, 50% on 2026-03-08, 100% scheduled pending customer production window. Post-deploy validation: customer reported no parse failures in staging over 48h after patch. Follow-up: add e2e test that simulates connection reseat and reordering; update streaming runbook to include proxy pooling guidance.
payload.summary: Intermittent websocket fragment interleaving after TLS session-ticket resume behind customer edge proxy

comments: Aisha Patel: Received initial report and validated Redwood console health flaps. Asked customer for resolver query logs and SRV dig outputs.

Daniel Kim: Reproduced locally using dnsmasq + scripted SRV toggles; healthchecks flip after second probe failure. Proposed mitigation: treat SRV weight changes within a short window as noise and add a small debounce in healthcheck logic OR recommend customer increase TTL to >=30s during canary churn.
Aisha Patel: Asked product/infra teams to evaluate safety of debouncing weight changes for private deployments. Escalated to networking/serving-runtime for impact analysis.
Product Lead: Requested a risk assessment for changing healthcheck semantics; asked for telemetry on how many private customers use SRV split-horizon with sub-10s TTLs.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
FinTrust (private deployment) reports intermittent failures of Redwood control-plane health checks for serving nodes. Failures manifest as transient 'unhealthy' status and short-lived connection rebalances which trigger automatic fallback to older model variants. Impact: production request errors and increased latency for a subset of requests.

Impact:
- ~3-7% of requests during observed windows returned 502/504 or experienced streaming resets tied to node health flapping.
- Customer reports degraded p99 latency and occasional degraded user experience in app telemetry.

Environment:
- Private deployment using VPC Endpoint (VPCE) with split-horizon DNS (internal resolver returns SRV records pointing to internal LB by weight).
- Control-plane healthchecks (gRPC/HTTP) rely on SRV priorities and short TTL for fast failover.

Observed behaviour:
- DNS SRV responses for _redwood-control._tcp.example.internal return varying weights across repeated queries; TTLs observed oscillating between 5s and 180s from the customer's internal resolver cache during the same minute.
- When TTL collapses to 5s and weights flip, the control-plane marks nodes unhealthy until multiple probe retries succeed.

Expected behaviour:
- Stable SRV responses with consistent weights and TTLs consistent with the configured failover policy. Healthchecks should not flap solely due to DNS cache jitter.

1) From a node in customer VPC, run: dig +short SRV _redwood-control._tcp.example.internal at 1s intervals for 60s
2) Observe SRV weight and target changes along with TTL in responses
3) Trigger a synthetic traffic run that floods a single node (to force health probing and possible reroute) and watch control-plane healthcheck events in the Redwood console
4) Correlate timestamps with customer internal resolver logs and VPCE resolver metrics
2026-03-12T10:03:15Z control-plane: healthcheck_started node=node-12 region=us-west-2
2026-03-12T10:03:17Z resolver: SRV _redwood-control returned 3 entries with weights [100,0,0] ttl=5s
2026-03-12T10:03:20Z control-plane: probe_failed node=node-12 reason=connection-refused
2026-03-12T10:03:21Z resolver: SRV _redwood-control returned 3 entries with weights [0,100,0] ttl=180s
2026-03-12T10:03:24Z control-plane: probe_succeeded node=node-12
Initial hypothesis: split-horizon resolver returning inconsistent SRV weights due to internal orchestration (service discovery) churn and low TTLs causing cache thrash at VPCE resolver.
Customer confirmed they run an internal service registry that republishes SRV records with aggressive TTLs to accelerate failovers for their own services. We observed TTLs toggling between 5s and 180s corresponding to registry refresh events.
Control-plane healthchecks are sensitive to DNS SRV order/weight because our routing selection evaluates DNS weight at each probe when TTL is low. Rapid weight oscillation can cause our healthcheck to consider the endpoint unstable for the duration of probe retries.
Reproduced in lab by emulating SRV responses with varying TTLs using dnsmasq: when TTL<=5s and weights alternate, healthcheck state transitions occur within 10-30s matching customer behaviour.
VPCE local cache observed dropping entries on low TTL which triggers new upstream queries; internal registry momentarily returned different weight assignments during leader election windows.

Additional notes:
Customer (FinTrust SRE - Marco Rossi): Attached dig outputs showing frequent weight flips correlated with their internal deployment pipeline (canary rollout job runs every minute). Confirmed no firewall drops or packet loss.
Workaround: Customer increased SRV TTL to 60s in their service registry during an initial mitigation window; after TTL increase, control-plane health flaps stopped and p99 latency returned to baseline. Long-term fix options: (A) Implement a conservative debounce in control-plane SRV-weight handling to ignore weight-only changes within a short window (default 15s) for private deployments; (B) Document recommended SRV TTL/weight patterns in Private Deployment runbook. Action items: INT-442 create feature proposal for debounce; SUP-608007 to remain open until code review and rollout plan or final runbook published.
payload.summary: Intermittent control-plane healthcheck failures due to DNS SRV weight/TTL oscillation in customer split-horizon setup

payload.description:
Issue summary: Enterprise customer Ledgerly reports a spike in end-to-end inference latency and an increase in 504 Gateway Timeouts for requests that include function/tool calling. Impact: multiple production endpoints returned 504s and experienced >95th percentile latencies of 2.5s+ over a 30-minute window. Initial triage suggests the extra synchronous schema-check step added by the function-call path is creating per-request remote round trips and queueing under load.
Customer-facing endpoints intermittently returning 504s and high tail latency; several mission-critical pipelines delayed. Affects live customers using tool-calls with strict tail-latency requirements; billing and usage spikes observed due to retries.
Prod cluster in us-east-1. Customer uses enterprise plan with pinned model versions and function-calling enabled. Requests travel: api-gateway -> function-proxy -> schema-validator (sync HTTP) -> serving-runtime. Schema-validator runs in shared k8s namespace (validation-service-v1).
1) Use Ledgerly test payload with function_call present (schema definition included). 2) Send 100 concurrent requests from us-east-1 over 30s. 3) Observe e2e latencies and error rate. 4) Capture traces with x-request-id. (Observed in customer and in synthetic repro harness.)
Traces show a synchronous HTTP call from function-proxy to schema-validator that adds 120-380ms per request. Under concurrency, schema-validator pods experience CPU spikes and request queueing; waiting time grows non-linearly and the api-gateway begins returning 504 at the tail. Reproduced with synthetic load. Datadog trace example: https://app.datadoghq.com/trace/trace_id=abcdef123456 (private).
Schema validation should not add unbounded blocking on the critical request path; tool/function-call validation should be happy-path fast or executed asynchronously without increasing e2e tail latency to cause 504s.
Sample logs (redacted):
- function-proxy[2026-03-12T14:02:04Z] x-request-id=xx-123 calling schema-validator start
- schema-validator[2026-03-12T14:02:04Z] request queued (queue-depth=18)
- schema-validator[2026-03-12T14:02:04Z] validation-time=0.312s status=200
- function-proxy[2026-03-12T14:02:04Z] schema-validate-rtt=312ms
- api-gateway[2026-03-12T14:02:04Z] response-time=2580ms status=504
Full logs linked in ticket storage: s3://support-logs/ledgerly/SUP-84719/
1) Disable function-calling for the customer's high-throughput endpoints (config toggle in console) — immediate reduction in 504s. 2) Increase schema-validator replica count and CPU for short-term mitigation. 3) Enable client-side retry jitter and backoff on Ledgerly side to reduce thundering herd.
Initial hypothesis: new sync validation integration introduced in serving-runtime v1.18 creates extra round trips.
Traces show ~150-380ms additional latency per request on validation step; when concurrent requests exceed 30, queueing in validator increases tail to >1s.
Schema-validator uses Python Flask process on shared node pool; CPU syscalls spike under validation parsing of complex nested schema (customer uses large tool schema with many properties).
A/B testing: toggling validation off for a small percentage of traffic removed the extra hop and reduced 95th percentile latency to baseline.
Related PR added a sync remote validation call rather than local schema check: infra PR #3421.
No evidence of serving-runtime model inference slowdown; problem limited to validation path and resource contention on validator pods.
Checked RBAC and network: no failed DNS or TLS handshakes observed; successful responses but delayed.
Customer reported additional retries from their client which amplified load and caused cascading queue growth.
A code change introduced a synchronous remote schema-validation service call into the request path for function/tool calls. Under load the shared validator instances become CPU-bound and queue requests, causing added RTTs that drive gateway timeouts and client retries, amplifying the effect.
Hotfix: revert to local in-process schema validation path for function-call fast path (serving-runtime rollback or flag) — owner: Jonah (ENG) — PR in progress.
Mitigation: scale schema-validator replicas and increase CPU limit in us-east-1 for Ledgerly’s tenant — owner: SRE team — done (scaled x3).
Long-term: implement async validation with pessimistic fast-fail and background deep validation; add circuit-breaker around validator calls — owner: Platform/Runtime team — design ticket created.
Add validation complexity limits and server-side caching of previous schema validations per customer to reduce CPU work — owner: Runtime/Optimization team.
Add tracing and quota metrics for schema-validator latency and queue depth; alert when queue-depth > 10 for >2m — owner: Observability team.
Follow up with Ledgerly CS to review retry behavior and recommend exponential backoff changes — owner: CS team.
Post-incident: produce a short postmortem and update function-call runbook — owner: Support Lead.
Test surface: add load test with large schema payloads in CI to detect regressions early — owner: QA.
Schedule: hotfix rollout targeted for 2026-03-13 07:00 UTC; full async redesign Q2 roadmap item.
Work in progress. Temporary mitigations applied: validation scaled and customer advised to disable function-calling for high-throughput endpoints. Hotfix PR to revert to local validation submitted and under review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/210. Customer notified and monitoring shows error rate trending down after mitigation.
Aisha Patel (Support) [2026-03-12T15:10Z]: Assigned to Jonah. Customer impact high — they reported multiple timed-out production jobs. Putting high priority on hotfix.
