payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external side effects (webhook posts and database writes) for function/tool calls invoked via Redwood Go SDK. This occurs on their private deployment behind an mTLS terminator (F5 load balancer + edge TLS) which performs connection-level retries on upstream timeouts.

Impact:
- Multiple customers of StellarForms have observed duplicate order confirmation webhook posts (2x) within ~3s for the same user action.
- Customer reports financial reconciliation errors and asked to pause traffic to the Redwood endpoint while we investigate.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (VPC) deployment in us-east
- Edge TLS terminator: F5 BigIP (mTLS between edge and origin)
- Customer using Redwood Go SDK v1.8.3, configured to use function-calling with signed per-request idempotency header X-Idempotency-JWT
- Serving runtime version: 2026.02.12-build

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send a function-call request with X-Idempotency-JWT header signed by customer's signing key and include callback webhook URL in tool args.
2) Induce a transient upstream timeout at the edge (they used a test rule to delay the origin for 1.2s).
3) Edge performs a connection-level retry; second attempt reaches origin but X-Idempotency-JWT header is missing on the retried request.
4) Serving runtime accepts the retried request as a new request and executes the tool, causing duplicate webhook post.

Observed behavior:
- First attempt log (edge -> origin): request_id=req-6a2b, X-Idempotency-JWT present
- Second attempt (edge retry -> origin): request_id=req-6a2b-retry, X-Idempotency-JWT absent
- Serving runtime created two separate tool-run events: tool_run_id=tr-8271 and tr-8272 (different DB entries)
- Customer webhook received two identical POSTs 3s apart.

Expected behavior:
- Retries performed by the edge should forward or preserve the idempotency token (or the gateway should canonicalize retries) so the serving runtime can de-duplicate and avoid re-executing side-effecting tools.

Logs / snippets provided by customer:
- Origin access log (first): "req-6a2b - headers: X-Idempotency-JWT=eyJhbGci..."
- Origin access log (retry): "req-6a2b-retry - headers: (no X-Idempotency-JWT)"
- Serving runtime trace: "received function-call: request_id=req-6a2b, tool=post_webhook, idempotency_present=true -> tool_run_id=tr-8271"
- Serving runtime trace (retry): "received function-call: request_id=req-6a2b-retry, tool=post_webhook, idempotency_present=false -> tool_run_id=tr-8272"

Temporary mitigation by customer:
- Disabled edge auto-retry on their F5 pool (stop-gap)
- Enabled client-side retry=off in Go SDK (SetRetryPolicy none) which prevents duplicate tool runs while we investigate

Additional notes:
- Customer is on an enterprise contract and has requested an ETA for a permanent fix.
- They cannot permanently disable edge retries due to other traffic patterns; need a gateway-side solution or a recommended SDK pattern for private deployments behind mTLS terminators.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 09:58 - StellarForms (Customer): Uploaded edge logs to secure bucket s3://stellarforms-support/dup-req-0310.tar.gz. Confirmed temporary mitigation applied (disabled retries).
2026-03-11 12:03 - Support (Aisha Khan): Notified customer of workaround and proposed timeline: experimental gateway patch to be rolled to a canary pool by 2026-03-12 pending soak results.
Reproduction: We reproduced the duplicate tool execution using a test F5 config in staging (edge sim). The terminator's connection-retry path creates a fresh HTTP/1.1 re-request and omits ephemeral headers that were associated with the original TLS session. The Go SDK's per-request idempotency approach (signed X-Idempotency-JWT generated by the customer) is therefore not present on retried attempts.
Root cause hypothesis: Connection-level retries at the edge do not automatically preserve arbitrary client-supplied headers that are computed per-TLS-connection. Signed idempotency tokens in customer headers can be lost on re-issued requests. Because the serving runtime uses header-presence to determine de-duplication, the missing header causes re-execution.
Engineering notes:
- This is specific to private deployments with an edge terminator that performs active retries. Hosted API had versioned routing and our gateway already performs header-preservation for retries there; private edge config varies.
- Short-term gateway change: if X-Idempotency-JWT present on the first attempt, copy it into a stable header X-Idempotency-Forward and ensure retries add that header. Implemented as a middleware in the gateway (PR linked).
- Long-term: document recommended best-practice for enterprise/private customers: either use server-side idempotency keys (included in request body) or ensure edge config preserves request headers on retries; SDK guidance to set retry=off when the network path performs automatic retries.
Work in progress. Temporary customer mitigations accepted (disabled edge retries + client disable retry). Gateway patch merged to staging (PR 1456) and scheduled for canary deployment 2026-03-12. If canary passes, plan a controlled rollout for private deployments with a migration playbook. Post-deployment follow-up: update private-deploy runbook and add a note to enterprise onboarding docs about header-preserving retry requirements.
payload.summary: mTLS terminator connection-retry strips signed idempotency header leading to duplicate function/tool executions (Go SDK, private deploy)

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer (AtlasWrite, Dedicated) reports intermittent per-request latency spikes (1.8-2.5x baseline) and occasional streaming timeouts when users resubmit identical prompts or when client SDK retries a broken stream. Impact: Several customer-facing flows (autosummarize & chat history replay) experience user-facing slowdowns and ~5-10% request failures during peak traffic windows. Environment: prod/us-east, dedicated pool id d-pool-12. Observed primarily on gptx-13b-quantized and gptx-8b-finetune. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a multi-turn conversation with a repeated prompt token prefix. 2) Force a transient stream disconnect on the client to trigger retry logic (SDK exponential backoff). 3) Observe server-side logs and latency metrics for repeated prompt ID. Expected behavior: Repeat prompt should hit warmed prefix/KV cache and return near-baseline latency with streaming retry preserving KV cache. Actual behavior: First retry shows KV cache miss, full KV lookup or cold fetch (~150-300ms extra) and in some cases the retry path times out after streaming proxy backpressure, producing a 504 to the caller. Recent change: Queryable prefix indexing refactor (serving-runtime v2.8.0) rolled 2026-03-08 suspected to coincide with regression window. Attachments: customer traces, sample request headers, and timing graphs uploaded to ticket attachments.

Logs / snippets: Error patterns observed in logs (prod us-east): "kv-cache: prefix-miss for key=prefix_0x4f2a" followed by "kv-fetch: cross-pool fetch latency=210ms" and then "streaming-proxy: retry-forward - client-side disconnect, initiating retry path". Several entries show the serving node evicting prefix entries after background compaction even when traffic indicates hot prefixes.
2026-03-10 10:20 - Support: Confirmed customer reproducible with SDK simulated disconnect. Collected p95/p99 latency traces and raw streaming logs.
2026-03-10 12:05 - SRE: Correlated latency spikes to increased KV miss rate for prefix keys during retry windows. KV eviction rate spiked after compaction window in pool d-pool-12.
2026-03-10 14:30 - Eng (serving-runtime): Found that refactor introduced a race where prefix entries marked as 'candidate-for-evict' were eligible for eviction earlier, but retry path assumes presence of warmed prefix and skips prefetch.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 13:45 - Repro test: In staging, toggling eviction threshold + enabling pre-warm on retry reduced p95 from 420ms to 180ms for repeated prompts.
2026-03-12 08:00 - Risk: If rollout continues, more dedicated pools with high retry rates may see increased user errors; customer impact likely for high-frequency repeat prompts (chatbots, summarizers).
2026-03-11 16:35 - Customer (AtlasWrite, support@atlaswrite.example): Provided user impact report. They requested immediate mitigation or a config knob to reduce timeouts on their dedicated pool.
A race introduced in the prefix/KV cache refactor caused aggressive eviction of recently used prefix entries while the streaming retry code assumed warmed prefixes. Retry path did not trigger prefix pre-warm, resulting in cold KV fetches; the extra latency combined with streaming proxy backpressure caused retries to hit timeouts.
Temporary config change applied to d-pool-12: increase prefix TTL and enable explicit pre-warm on streaming retry path. This reduces cold fetches and drops streaming timeouts for the customer.
Patch accepted: serving-runtime PR #3124 adds explicit prefix pre-warm on retry path and tightens eviction gating for recently-used prefixes. Patch scheduled for canary in prod on 2026-03-13 and full rollout on 2026-03-14 after monitoring window. Post-deploy: confirm with AtlasWrite that their observed errors are resolved and close ticket.
Post-deploy: run 48h regression tests on dedicated pools with synthetic retry storms to validate no hidden perf regressions.
Add an observability alert: sustained increase in kv-miss-rate for hot-prefixes tied to streaming retry counts.
Confluence: Draft a short postmortem and add preventative checklist for future prefix refactors.
Customer communication: Schedule a 30-min review with AtlasWrite success team to walk through fix and confirm SLA satisfaction.
payload.summary: Intermittent timeouts and doubled latency for repeated prompts: stale prefix / KV cache misses during streamed retry path

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 07:40 UTC, Scriptly AI reported elevated p95 (~3.2s -> 7.8s) and intermittent 504/502 timeouts when calling our hosted endpoints backed by their dedicated pool (pool-rtp-03). Impact: customer-facing inference degraded for ~90 minutes; streaming sessions dropped; retries caused 429 bursts. Environment: dedicated pool pool-rtp-03, node group gpu-a100-1, region us-west-2. Observed behaviour: p95/p99 spikes coincident with high variance in request cost (mix of long-seq summarization and many short chat queries). Autoscaler config had min_replicas=1 and aggressive scale_up_threshold=0.85 leading to sustained high per-GPU utilization and head-of-line queueing. Expected behaviour: stable p95 < 800ms and no 5xx for in-reservation traffic.
1) Send a steady mix of long-sequence (seq_len ~ 4096) and short chat (seq_len ~ 128) requests at 350 rps against the model pinned in pool-rtp-03. 2) Observe per-GPU scheduler queue depth and token throughput. 3) Notice serialization on single CUDA stream and elevated GPU context-switches when long and short jobs overlap. 4) Retries from clients increase queue depth and surface 429/504s.
From Grafana dashboard: p50=210ms p95=3.2s (spike to 7.8s at peak) p99=12.1s; GPU util per-card: 92% average with 1 card at 99% bursting; CUDA context-switches increased 8x; inference RPS fell by 38% relative to baseline. Queue length at the runtime RPC layer jumped from 4 -> 26. API gateway 429 rate jumped to 18%.

[2026-03-10T07:42:13Z] kernel-trace: cuda_stream_wait: ctx=0x7f9e3c, pending_tasks=12
[2026-03-10T07:43:02Z] autoscaler: evaluate: replicas=1 avg_gpu_util=0.92 scale_up_threshold=0.85 time_above_threshold=420s - decision=NOOP (cooldown)
[2026-03-10T07:44:10Z] api-gateway: response=504 path=/v1/chat/complete customer=scriptly-ai pool=pool-rtp-03
07:45 UTC - Support triage: validated customer traces and confirmed increased p95 and 5xx; engaged SRE (oncall-inference)
07:52 UTC - Pulled GPU metrics and noticed high sustained utilization and elevated context-switch rates on node gpu-a100-1-12 in pool-rtp-03
08:05 UTC - Captured per-request histograms and saw long requests holding the CUDA stream for extended durations, blocking short ephemeral requests (head-of-line blocking)
08:20 UTC - Autoscaler logs indicate min_replicas=1 and a cooldown configured which prevented scale up despite sustained high utilization; scale up was suppressed due to cooldown policy from an earlier spike
08:35 UTC - Hypothesis formed: mis-sized autoscaler + mixed workload -> GPU serialization and kernel preemption leading to throughput collapse; noisy peer (another tenant in same pool) was running heavy long-seq batch jobs
08:50 UTC - Temporarily increased replicas to 3 and applied pod anti-affinity to separate the heavy job tenant; this immediately reduced p95 and cleared long queues
Aisha Kaur (Support) 2026-03-10 07:50: Customer reports streaming disconnects; provided initial trace and ETA for first response: 30m
Daniel Park (SRE) 2026-03-10 08:02: Oncall pulled GPU telemetry; seeing high context-switch count on node gpu-a100-1-12. Suspect kernel preemption and workload mixing.
Ravi Mehta (Infra) 2026-03-10 08:30: Autoscaler cooldown prevented scale-up after earlier burst; min_replicas=1 is too low for known mixed workloads. Increasing replicas as a stopgap.
Scriptly-AI (Customer) 2026-03-10 08:40: Thanks — we see latency improving after your change. Please advise long-term mitigation.
The root cause is a combination of: 1) Autoscaler misconfiguration (min_replicas=1 + aggressive cooldown) that left the pool undersized for mixed long/short workloads; 2) GPU-level serialization when long-sequence requests and short chat requests share the same CUDA streams leading to kernel preemption/serialization and KV cache thrashing; and 3) a noisy peer in the same reservation running high-duration micro-batch jobs that exacerbated scheduling unfairness.

Additional notes:
Medium-term: update autoscaler policy for dedicated pools to set min_replicas >= 2 for mixed-workload reservations and reduce cooldown for scale_up evaluations
Medium-term: introduce per-tenant scheduling class for long-duration micro-batch jobs so we avoid interleaving on same GPU stream
Long-term: instrument per-stream kernel timings and add runtime heuristics to route long-requests to isolated GPU slices or variant models (quantized/faster)
Applied emergency scale and anti-affinity which reduced p95 from 7.8s peak down to ~650ms within 12 minutes. Implemented gateway rate-limiting for long-seq requests to prevent immediate reoccurrence. Follow-up work created to adjust autoscaler defaults for dedicated reservations and implement scheduling isolation for heavy micro-batch workloads. Customer confirmed recovery and we provided post-incident notes and proposed mitigations.
2026-03-10 09:10 UTC - Recovery observed; 504s fell to 0. 2026-03-11 - Autoscaler policy PR opened (link above). 2026-03-12 - Confluence runbook updated with dedicated-pool sizing guidance for mixed workloads.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Between 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC and 2026-03-10 06:10 UTC Lyra Insurance observed intermittent failures for embedding requests that used Redwood's embedding endpoints. Errors manifested as 500/502 responses and stalled streaming for a subset of customer requests. The root trigger was a tokenizer component regression causing certain outlier input batches (multi-line policy documents with mixed encodings) to throw exceptions during tokenization.

Impact:
- ~18% of Lyra production embedding calls failed with 5xx for a 2.5 hour window.
- End-to-end embedding throughput for Lyra (dedicated pool) dropped by ~60% leading to request queueing and higher tail latency for other customers using the same Dedicated pool.
- Autoscaler reacted to apparent latency by rapidly adding and removing workers, causing increased GPU churn and billing anomalies for Lyra's reserved capacity.
- Customer reported increased errors visible in their app, automated retries led to duplicate events.

Initial detection:
- Lyra Support engineer opened a ticket and escalated to Redwood via priority channel.
- Alerts fired from per-customer error-rate dashboards and dedicated-pool SLO monitors.

Expected behavior:
Embedding requests for supported models should not fail tokenization for inputs that previously succeeded; dedicated pools should isolate CPU-level tokenizer failures and not cascade to whole-pool throughput degradation.

1) Customer payload: multi-line policy document with mixed UTF-8 and legacy Windows-1252 punctuation (example provided in ticket).
2) POST to /v1/embeddings with model=openlm-embed-1024-v2 and batch size 8.
3) Observe request sometimes returns 502 or times out; reproduced more often when inputs include long contiguous sequences of non-standard whitespace and soft-hyphen characters.
4) Repro rate ~20% in Lyra's sample corpus, not deterministic in small synthetic sets.
[2026-03-10T03:48:17Z] tokenizer-service.ERROR tokenization_exception input_index=3 error=UnicodeDecodeError('utf-8', b'\x96', 0, 1, 'invalid start byte')
[2026-03-10T03:49:02Z] serving-runtime.WARNING backpressure queue_size=312 pool_id=ded-pool-07
[2026-03-10T03:50:11Z] autoscaler.INFO scale_event add_workers=3 pool=ded-pool-07 reason=high_tail_latency
[2026-03-10T05:05:22Z] gateway.ERROR upstream-502 model=openlm-embed-1024-v2 request_id=rb-9f3b4
- Hypothesis 1: tokenizer library update (rev 2.1.4 -> 2.2.0) introduced stricter decoding behavior for non-UTF inputs.
- Hypothesis 2: Batch pre-processing path bypassed fallback sanitizer for dedicated-pool traffic under high concurrency.
- Correlation: Tokenizer errors spike aligns with commit github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizer@2.2.0 merged 2026-03-09 and deployment window 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC.
- Reproduced locally by feeding mixed-encoding snippets into tokenizer-service running 2.2.0; downgrade to 2.1.4 eliminated exception.
- Observed autoscaler thrash: short-lived latency spikes from tokenizer exceptions caused scale-up decisions; scale down occurred before workers processed cached warmup leading to oscillation.
- Customer tenancy isolation: Lyra was on a shared Dedicated pool (configuration gap) instead of a fully isolated pool; follow-up check flagged misconfiguration on account settings.
- Link to Slack thread: #support-lyra (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C04S2KJ1H), SRE postmortem draft link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/INC-2026-0310-01
Mitigation performed 2026-03-10 04:10 UTC:
1) Rolled back tokenizer library on serving nodes from 2.2.0 -> 2.1.4 for affected Dedicated pool.
2) Applied on-the-fly input sanitizer that normalizes legacy encodings to UTF-8 at the gateway for Lyra's tenant requests.
3) Temporarily increased min_workers for ded-pool-07 to provide capacity and disabled aggressive scale-down cooldowns.
4) Pinning: Lyra's account temporarily pinned to model-version=openlm-embed-1024-v2@2026-03-08 to avoid newer integration paths.

Issue summary: Customer runs a mixed workload from the same API key: low-latency websocket chat sessions plus large batch embedding imports. They recently changed the tenant's threshold ladder (burst credits and sustained window) to reduce cost, and since the change have seen a spike of 429 responses that look like tenant-level token exhaustion rather than per-route throttles. Impact: customer reports intermittent 429s that cause degraded UX for interactive sessions (timeouts, reconnects) and failed batch jobs. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1; single API key used by an orchestrator that fans out both chat and bulk workers. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start 150 concurrent websocket chat sessions, each sending short prompts every 1s. 2) Simultaneously start 10 parallel batch embedding jobs that submit 2k requests each over 10 minutes. 3) Observe tenant 429s on chat sessions after ~6 minutes; batch jobs see early failures and retries pile up. Logs / snippets: - ingress-rate-limiter [2026-03-10T14:21:04Z] token-window: tenant=Kestrel-99 available=0 refill_next=2026-03-10T14:22:00Z - gateway [2026-03-10T14:21:05Z] 429 POST /v1/embeddings 200ms xid=... reason=tenant_quota_exhausted - websocket-proxy [2026-03-10T14:21:08Z] disconnect user=chat-conn-73 code=429 message="rate limit exceeded" Additional context: Prior to ladder change they had a larger burst bucket and a longer sustained window. The customer changed two knobs: lowered burst_credits from 20000->6000 and reduced refill_smoothing_window from 60s->15s to reduce cost during quiet periods. They chose to keep routes unsegregated (chat + embeddings share same tenant quota).
Checked tenant-level token accounting: counters show rapid token depletion when batch importer begins; chat sessions contribute smaller per-request tokens but high concurrency leads to additional counting due to websocket connection keepalive probes.
Observed refill alignment artifact: with smoothing_window reduced to 15s, burst drawdown followed by a slower apparent refill cadence causing periodic hard 429s between refill ticks.
No sign of a bug in gateway code path; rate-limiter logs show expected behavior given configured ladder but customer expectation was different (they expected route isolation to prevent chat impact).
Checked dedicated pool utilization: GPUs not saturated; this is quota accounting behavior rather than serving capacity exhaustion.
1) Mixed workload is exhausting tenant burst credits because routes are not isolated; short high-concurrency chat spikes trigger repeated small token uses that, combined with batch job token usage, hit tenant window.
2) Shrinking smoothing_window created refill boundary effects (microbursts) that are leading to synchronized refill gaps across clients.
3) Health-check/keepalive probes are being counted towards tenant quota and amplify depletion under high connection counts.

Additional notes:
Config examples: - route_quota.chat.weight=0.2 - route_quota.chat.burst=8000 - route_quota.embeddings.weight=0.7 - tenant.refill_smoothing_window=60s
Operational: enable transparent throttle headers (X-RateLimit-*) so clients can backoff more gracefully and implement splay on retry waves to avoid synchronized retries.
Long-term: if cost is a concern, use dynamic routing to send low-latency traffic to a small dedicated pool or priority lane with smaller instance count but reserved burst credits.

Issue summary:
Customers experiencing intermittent 403 responses when a service account attempts token-refresh via the private control plane. Errors surface in production us-east and affect background job processing for BrightBank.

Impact:
- Several scheduled worker jobs (payment reconciliation) are failing to authenticate, causing near-real-time processing delays (~15-30 min backlog).
- Authentication failures are intermittent: ~1-3% of token refresh attempts return 403.

Environment:
- Private deployment (BrightBank VPC, Private control plane)
- Region: us-east
- Identity provider: customer's internal OIDC provider relayed by identity-proxy
- Affected clients: service-to-service token refresh (client credentials flow with id_token exchange retained for auditing)

Steps to reproduce:
1) From inside BrightBank VPC, call /v1/token/refresh with service account refresh token using identity-proxy as relay.
2) Observe 200 for most requests; ~1-3% return 403 with body: {"error":"invalid_token","detail":"subject mismatch"}.
3) Correlate with identity-proxy logs and control-plane token-exchange traces.

Expected behavior:
- Token refresh should succeed for valid refresh tokens and return new access tokens consistently.

Actual behavior:
- Intermittent 403 from token-exchange with message indicating id_token subject mismatch.

Relevant logs (redacted):
- identity-proxy: "WARN auth: id_token sub 'svc-ops-79' does not match cached subject 'svc-ops-hr' for client_id 'brightbank-payments'"
- control-plane: "ERROR token-exchange: incoming id_token subject prefix 'svc-ops-' differs from allowed prefix 'svc_reports-' -> reject"

Additional notes:
- This started after BrightBank rotated a naming prefix in their AD connectors the week of 2026-03-02. Not all service accounts were updated to the new subject namespace.
2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Priya Gupta): Acknowledged receipt. Triage P1 and engaged SRE. Requested customer logs and an example request ID.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Customer (BrightBank SRE - Carlos Mendes): Provided sample request IDs: req-20260310-87a, req-20260310-92f. Confirmed AD connector change on 2026-03-02. Not seeing consistent failures on their side.
2026-03-10 13:30 - SRE (Jordan Lee): Correlated request req-20260310-87a to identity-proxy pod id proxy-4. Found id_token.sub alternates between 'svc-ops-79' and 'svc_reports-79' for same client_id. Hypothesis: upstream token-issuance is inconsistent during rotation causing subject prefix variance and name-based auth policy rejecting when prefixes differ.
2026-03-11 08:45 - Eng (Aisha Khan): Reproduced locally by replaying token exchange with two id_tokens that only differ in sub prefix. Control-plane currently enforces strict subject-prefix policy during token refresh to prevent privilege escalation across namespaces. This is rejecting valid rotated tokens when subject namespace temporarily diverges.
2026-03-11 12:20 - Support (Priya Gupta): Shared mitigation steps with customer: (1) Ensure client refreshers update to new subject namespace; (2) Temporary allowlist change to accept both prefixes for the tenant on control-plane while rotation completes. Requested approval to apply allowlist change scoped to BrightBank tenant.
2026-03-11 15:05 - Customer (Carlos Mendes): Approved temporary control-plane allowlist change. Asked for rollback plan.
2026-03-12 03:10 - SRE (Jordan Lee): Applied tenant-scoped allowlist in control-plane for prefixes ['svc-ops-','svc_reports-']. Monitor shows 403 rate dropped to <0.1% in the last 12 hours. Planning follow-up fix to make subject-prefix policy tolerant during rotation windows and add signal to console.
2026-03-12 11:02 - Eng (Aisha Khan): Created PR to implement tolerant subject-prefix matching with explicit tenant rotation windows. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-auth/pull/298. Added unit and integration tests. QA scheduled for 2026-03-14.
2026-03-12 11:20 - Support (Priya Gupta): Updated ticket status to In Progress. Noted customer impact mitigated by allowlist; monitoring continues.
Hypothesis: The identity provider rotation changed the subject namespace for service accounts (prefix change). Control-plane subject-prefix policy rejects requests when id_token.sub doesn't match the expected tenant-scoped namespace. Evidence: identity-proxy logs show alternating subject prefixes for the same client_id during rotation window. Trace links: https://observability.redwood.prod/traces?trace=req-20260310-87a. Metrics: token-exchange 403 spike correlated to 2026-03-02 AD rotation event. Reproduction steps executed in staging with replay tokens replicated the 403 behavior. Root cause: strict enforcement of exact subject-prefix mapping without accounting for rotation windows and multi-prefix allowlist per tenant.
Workaround applied 2026-03-12: tenant-scoped temporary allowlist added to control-plane for BrightBank to accept both old and new subject prefixes. Observed immediate reduction in failures (<0.1%).

Permanent fix plan:
- Deploy tolerant subject-prefix matching logic that supports a short-lived rotation window per tenant and logs rotation diagnostics (ENG-2012). PR created: https://github.com/redwood/inference-auth/pull/298.
- Add console signal and alerting when subject-prefix variance exceeds threshold (OPS-894).
- Post-deploy: perform coordinated tenant rotation test with BrightBank to validate.

Follow-ups:
- Runbook update: add section for tenant prefix rotations and allowlist procedure.
- Customer communication: notify BrightBank when permanent fix is deployed and recommend schedule for future rotations.

Ticket outcome: mitigation in place; awaiting deployment of PR and QA.

Issue summary:
During a canary shadow (traffic mirroring) attempt for customer LexicoSearch in eu-west, tenant-bound requests briefly reverted from the pinned canary variant back to the primary variant. The tenant explicitly had a model pin set to canary for several days. The behaviour surfaced as ~10-30s windows where streaming responses came from the legacy model (different tokenizer leading to minor token differences) and request latencies spiked.

Impact:
- Customer: LexicoSearch (dedicated) observed degraded output quality for a subset of user sessions and a small billing spike due to fallback to larger primary variant.
- Scope: Intermittent, appears tied to long-lived streaming sessions and canary shadowing config in eu-west. Estimated <0.5% of total requests for the tenant during the window.

Environment:
- Prod, eu-west cluster, control-plane v3.24.1, edge-proxy v2.9.0, orchestrator v1.18.
- Canary config: mirror=true, weight=0 (shadow only), tenant pin -> model: redwood-v2-medium-canary-2026-03-08

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long-lived streaming session pinned to canary via the tenant pin API.
2) Enable canary shadow mirror (mirror=true) for route.
3) Under light-to-moderate traffic, observe streaming output for the session.
4) After a reconciliation window, some streaming chunks show tokens produced by primary variant.

Observed logs (edge/orchestrator snippets):
- edge-proxy[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] DEBUG route-resolver: tenant=lexico-001 pin-ts=2026-03-08T12:05:33Z source=orchestrator snapshot-id=8421
- orchestrator[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] INFO reconcile: tenant=lexico-001 last-pin-updated=2026-03-10T14:18:55Z applied-snapshot=8423
- edge-proxy[2026-03-10T14:22:12Z] WARN routing: pin-timestamp-skew detected (edge older than control-plane) -> snapback to primary variant
- serving-runtime[2026-03-10T14:22:12Z] ERROR model-resolve: route=lexico-001 variant=primary returned tokens mismatch md5_expected=7f4a... md5_actual=7f4b...

Notes: The key symptom is a timestamp skew between the edge-side cached pin metadata and the control-plane's most-recent pin. Because shadow mirror snapshots are reconciled on a short window, an older edge cache led the reconciler to interpret the tenant as ‘not pinned’ and therefore apply normal primary routing temporarily (snapback).
2026-03-10 15:00 UTC - Reproduced on staging by mimicking long-lived stream with mirror=true; confirmed edge cache TTL=120s and control-plane pin update time within that TTL.
Hypothesis: edge clock drift / async pin propagation + mirror reconciliation logic treats stale edge pin metadata as absence of pin and triggers snapback path.
Found evidence: edge log shows 'pin-ts' older than orchestrator last-pin-updated in ~12 occurrences across the eu-west pool during the window.
Checked prior related fixes: PRs that modified snapshot reconciliation in 2025 Q4 — behaviour differs when mirror=true vs weight>0.
Temporary mitigation: forced pin-refresh API call for the tenant caused immediate rebind to canary; restarting edge-proxy drained the stale cache and prevented further snapbacks.
Telemetry: added metric 'pin_ts_skew_count' to detect future events and alert threshold set to 5 in 5m for eu-west.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported streaming tokens diverging after enabling canary shadow. Created ticket and requested SRE look into edge/cache behaviour.
Marco Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-10: Confirmed timestamp skew in logs. Re-produced in staging with long stream. Proposed immediate mitigation: pin refresh + edge-proxy rolling restart in eu-west.
LexicoSearch (Customer) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged workaround is acceptable short term but asked for root cause and a permanent fix timeline.
Emily Zhao (Eng - Orchestrator) 2026-03-11: Noted that reconciler assumes authoritative source = control-plane; edge should not cause snapback if mirror=true. Opening follow-up PR to normalize logic.
Marco Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-12: Rolled edge-proxy restart across eu-west (canary group -> full). Post-restart telemetry shows no further skews for 48h.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-13: Customer confirmed no further incidents during business hours, requested a summary and PR link for audit.
Workaround applied: forced tenant pin refresh via control-plane API and rolling restart of edge-proxy fleet in eu-west. Customer-facing mitigation communicated. Permanent fix: engineering patched the reconciliation logic to ignore edge-side absent pin when mirror=true and to accept control-plane pin as authoritative even when edge cache TTL not expired; PRs referenced above. Monitoring: new metric (pin_ts_skew_count) and dashboard added; alerting configured for eu-west. Post-deploy verification: 72h silent period with no recurrence; customer confirmed restoration of expected behaviour. Follow-up action: backport fix to 3.23.x maintenance branch and schedule a postmortem note in Confluence.

Issue summary:
BrightCart reported that their consolidated invoice shows a 42% higher hosted usage line for the billing window 2026-02-28 00:00:00 to 2026-03-01 00:00:00 UTC. They believe excess usage was attributed to their production org after we decommissioned an older regional edge proxy (edge-us-east-3) last week.

Impact:
- Customer seeing ~3.8k USD unexpected hosted usage charge on finalized invoice for the period.
- Affects billing reconciliation for finance (BrightCart) and may trigger chargeback to their customers.
- Customer service and engineering time required to arbitrate.

Environment:
- Redwood prod, region us-east (primary), eu-west (secondary failover).
- Customer uses dedicated hybrid routing with private keys and multiple subaccounts under org-brightcart-prod.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Decommissioned edge proxy edge-us-east-3 on 2026-02-27 14:05 UTC (scheduled maintenance).
2) Post-decommission, queued postbacks for several API keys were replayed from retention buffer over a short window (2026-02-27 14:10–14:40 UTC).
3) BrightCart reports that the postbacks were attributed to their parent org rather than the original subaccount that produced them.
4) Metering pipeline aggregated those postbacks into hourly buckets and rerated them under hosted tariff, not reserved/dedicated tags.

Expected behavior:
- Postback replay should preserve original api_key and subaccount tags, maintain original rate/tariff mapping, and attribute usage to original org/subaccount.

Actual behavior:
- A subset (~18%) of replayed postbacks lost subaccount tagging during replay and were attributed to BrightCart parent org at hosted rates.

- Postback trace IDs: pb-ff7a1c, pb-ff7a1d, pb-ff7a4a (attached).
- Edge decommission runbook: Confluence page 'Edge decommission: edge-us-east-3' (link in related_confluence_pages).

Immediate customer request:
- Provide explanation and provisional credit for the unexpected hosted charge while we investigate attribution.

Workaround suggested to customer (temporary):

Retention-replayer lacked strict validation of X-Subaccount header when edge decommissioned; some proxies stripped header during graceful shutdown.
Metering service applied fallback routing that defaults to parent org if subaccount tag missing — this logic is correct for isolated events but unsafe for bulk replays.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
BrightVoice reports intermittent 429s immediately after a subaccount split/tenant reparenting. The pattern: long-lived SSE connections (keepalive pings every 30s) experience opaque 429s with no X-RateLimit headers, while a burst of webhook callbacks (signed URL POSTs) succeed concurrently.

Impact:
- Production user-facing chat widgets intermittently drop streaming updates for ~5-20s.
- Retry loops on the client escalate CPU and duplicate webhook deliveries.
- Observed by multiple BrightVoice accounts in the same dedicated GPU pool.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (dedicated-02), prod-us-west.
- Subaccount split performed 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC (BrightVoice initiated migrate-subaccounts v2).
- SSE connections established from browser clients via api-edge (http/2 -> origin).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run a large webhook fanout (200 concurrent signed-URL callbacks) to the same tenant after triggering the subaccount split.
2) Keep ~150 active SSE clients connected and emitting keepalives every 30s.
3) Observe sporadic 429s on SSE connections (no rate-limit headers) while webhook callbacks mostly succeed.

Observed behavior:
- SSE responses are rejected with 429 and connection reset. Client logs show no X-RateLimit-* headers.
- Server-side ingress metrics show a temporary drop in available burst credits for that tenant immediately after the split.
- Console shows route-level token counters not decreasing for webhook route (route reports normal usage) but tenant-level burst credit decremented.

Expected behavior:
- Long-lived SSE keepalives should be accounted against a separate long-lived/session pool or at least expose clear throttle headers telling client retry window.
- Webhook callbacks and SSE keepalives should not silently steal each other's burst credit in a way that produces opaque 429s.

Logs / trace identifiers provided by customer:
- TraceIDs: trace-20260310-3a7f, trace-20260310-3a8c
- Example client timestamp: 2026-03-09T22:27:14.523Z
- Customer attached packet captures and server-side sample logs (sse_connection_id=sv-7f2d).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:45 - BrightVoice Tech (customer): Provided curl samples, packet captures and the migration log. Says they saw 429s persist for ~18 minutes then subside.
Checked rate-limiter logs for tenant 'brightvoice-44' between 2026-03-09T22:05 and 2026-03-09T22:40. Observed a refill event where origin and edge both applied a partial refill, but the handoff left the tenant with an unexpectedly low effective burst budget.
Edge-proxy (http2) triggered connection reuse behavior: SSE keepalive frames were mapped to a generic /events path which shares token accounting with signed-url callbacks (POST /cb).
Observed lack of X-RateLimit headers for SSE rejections because the edge rejects early at the token-bucket layer (pre-auth) and the header propagation path is bypassed when reject happens in the pre-routing layer.
Staging reproduce: tenant-split flow + concurrent webhook burst + 150 simulated SSE keepalives -> SSE 429s observed. When we moved SSE keepalive to use a distinct client-id header, accounting separated and 429s stopped.
Hypothesis: tenant-split causes a short-lived mismatch in burst-credit ownership between edge and origin. Because SSE and webhook use different route selectors but same token bucket, the transient low-burst state results in opaque SSE 429s with header-less rejects.
Workaround implemented: temporary config change applied to dedicated-02 to grant 'long-lived-connection' exemption pool for BrightVoice for 24 hours and enabled verbose throttle headers on pre-routing rejects. Customer verified streaming recovery after change.
Planned fix: engineering will land the following in next sprint (PR linked):
- Isolate long-lived SSE/WS keepalive traffic into a distinct refill bucket at the edge so route-level and session-level traffic do not compete for the same burst credits. (Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/498).
- Ensure pre-routing rejects include X-RateLimit headers by plumbing header emission into the token-bucket reject path.
Follow-ups and action items:
- Postmortem note: schedule after next week to capture incident timeline and recommend tenant-split runbook additions. (Owner: Elena Ruiz).
- Add an automated check in the migration playbook to verify tenant burst credit parity between edge and origin before cutover. (Owner: Platform SRE).
- CS to follow up with BrightVoice on 2026-03-15 to confirm no recurrence and communicate planned fix timeline.
Status: Mitigated (temporary exemption applied). Engineering work in-progress for permanent fix.

Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in perceived inference timeouts and stalled streaming sessions across multiple hosts in their dedicated pool. Symptoms look like model hangs because client SDKs observe long tail blocking and retry heavily.

Impact:
- Multiple production customers of NimbleDocs saw 15-30% of streaming sessions stall for 10-30s during a 45-minute window on 2026-03-10.
- Automated client retries caused burst traffic and amplified queueing behind a server-side pacing window, making the issue look like a model regression.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: prod-us-east (gpu-pool-dedicated-42)
Initial triage (Maya):
- Collected SDK logs and streaming session traces from NimbleDocs. Observed rapid client-side retry loops (default SDK backoff disabled by customer).
- Observed a consistent server-side rate-window enforcement interval: short windows where new requests were queued and soft-429s returned.
- Serving runtime metrics: queue length spiked then drained in bursts. P95 latency increased during drain periods.
- No GPU OOMs or kernel faults. Kernel latencies stable per-host.

Hypothesis (Arjun):
- A pacing window (internal rate-window for per-customer fairness) starts returning soft 429s when tokens/requests exceed configured pacing threshold. Customers with aggressive retry behavior produce a request surge that pushes the queue into the pacing window, leading to visible stalls.
- The SDK did not implement jittered exponential backoff; retries were tightly clustered causing amplification.

Evidence:
- Nginx/gateway logs show 429 responses annotated with X-Rate-Window: true and Retry-After header values of 2-5s.
- Traces show client retries begin ~100ms after initial 429, causing a second micro-surge that re-triggers the same pacing window.
- Patchwork of short Retry-After values makes clients loop multiple times within a single pacing interval.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Recreate request pattern using the customer SDK with retries disabled vs aggressive retries.
2) Send 100 concurrent streaming sessions with payloads similar to production prompt sizes.
3) Observe gateway 429s and per-customer pacing annotation.

Next actions:
- Ask customer to temporarily enable exponential backoff with jitter (workaround).
- Adjust routing policy to apply per-route gradual backoff to reduce amplification while we investigate configuration defaults.
- Prepare a small runtime change to increase Retry-After for pacing windows so clients have time to back off.

Workaround and mitigation applied:
- Provided NimbleDocs with an SDK patch to enable jittered exponential backoff and recommended backoff parameters. Customer confirmed immediate reduction in perceived stalls (measurements show 90% drop in session stalls).
- On 2026-03-11 infra changed pacing window Retry-After from 2-5s to 6-12s for dedicated pools as a temporary server-side mitigation to reduce retry amplification.
- Engineering will ship a runtime change to expose pacing window metrics and make Retry-After adaptive based on current queue drain rate (target release 2026-03-18).

Follow-up items:
- ENG-OPS TODO: Add a customer-exposed telemetry flag so customers can see when they're in a pacing window.
- DOCS TODO: Update SDK docs and quickstart to strongly recommend jittered backoff; add example config.
- POSTMORTEM: Create a short postmortem if similar incidents occur after the runtime change.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:48 - Customer (NimbleDocs - Elena Ruiz): Deployed patch. Early metrics show streaming success rate increased from 78% to 95% for the test cohort.
payload.summary: Opaque pacing window causes perceived session hang during SDK retry surge

Issue summary: Customer performed a credit transfer between two subaccounts and upgraded billing plan while running a large ingestion. After the transfer, several of their long-lived legacy API keys received intermittent 429 responses for ~18 minutes. Throttle headers were inconsistent across connections and some streaming sessions dropped mid-session.

Impact: Customer ingestion pipeline stalled; ~180k embedding tokens rejected with 429s, causing retries and duplicate downstream writes. Business impact: delayed nightly import and customer escalated to Enterprise CS.

Environment: Production (us-east), enterprise plan, legacy API keys issued in 2024, ingestion workload uses parallel uploader (16 workers) and keeps long-lived SSE streaming sessions open.
1) On enterprise org with two subaccounts A and B, initiate a credit transfer from A -> B via console transfer API.
2) Immediately after transfer, trigger a heavy parallel ingest from multiple hosts using legacy API keys tied to subaccount A.
3) Observe 429 responses and inconsistent X-RateLimit-* headers; streaming SSE sessions may drop with HTTP/2 CANCEL or 5xx from edge.
4) Note that console shows credits moved but quota refill windows did not align for some legacy keys.

2026-03-10T03:20:05Z billing: credit-transfer completed tx=0x9bf3a ref=TR-20260310-77
Support triage: customer provided X-RateLimit headers and ingestion timeline; initial hypothesis - delayed refill application for legacy key windows after credit transfer.

Edge/gateway logs show mixed window_reset values for requests from the same API key - indicates transient split-brain between token-windows cached at edge and authoritative quota-store.
Confirmed customer was using a mix of long-lived SSE connections and new short-lived upload connections; SSE sessions kept old local cache while new connections hit updated but not-yet-refilled windows, causing double-counting and short-window exhaustion.
Repro script created in staging to simulate transfer + concurrent workers; reproduced 429 spike when refill-processor latency > 8s and when edge cache TTL > 10s.
Related code area: quota-service async refill path + edge cache invalidation. Investigated PR history and found a recent change that optimized bulk credit writes but did not force immediate cache invalidation for legacy-key windows (PR referenced above).
Dashboard links: RateLimiter queue depth: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ratelimiter/refill-queue?orgId=1 (observed spike at 03:12)

Evelyn Park (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging; noticed refill-processor backlog. Opening an engineering investigation and escalating to infra-oncall. Linked PR for quick fix.

Race between async credit-transfer refill path and edge cache TTL for legacy API keys. Bulk credit write optimized path did not trigger immediate cache invalidation, causing mismatched token-window state and transient 429s under concurrent connections.
Hotfix applied: synchronous cache invalidation for credit-transfer flow and immediate refill queue prioritization for affected subaccounts. Engineering merged permanent fix (PR 5487) to make refill + cache update atomic. Manual quota-sync executed for the customer's affected keys to restore normal windows. Customer ingestion completed without further 429s.

comments: 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z Priya Kapoor: Created ticket after NimbusDocs support rep @nimbus-support reported truncated final sentences and double metadata. Attached customer's sample websocket capture.
2026-03-10T10:05:00Z Liam Chen: Acknowledged; triaging with infra. Requesting LB config and client SDK version. Asked Nimbus for pcap and trace-id headers.
2026-03-12T08:21:00Z E: Confirmed proxy is performing 0-RTT resumption and observed duplicate write calls in gateway logs. Posted preliminary findings to #support and linked runbook.
2026-03-13T11:47:00Z Liam Chen: Deployed a gate in staging to suppress duplicate meta emission when we detect immediate re-transmit after KV cache flush. Need further validation under load.
2026-03-14T08:19:00Z Priya Kapoor: Customer verified that disabling 0-RTT entirely on their edge eliminated occurrences for 48 hours; monitoring continues.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a brief client-initiated half-close followed by a TLS 1.3 0-RTT retry, WebSocket streams to the Redwood API sometimes arrive with the final JSON choice split across two frames and duplicated 'meta' objects. The downstream client sees truncated final text and two metadata blocks, which breaks deterministic parsing in their SDK.

Impact:
- NimbusDocs chat-export feature sometimes misses the closing sentence of streamed responses or receives duplicated metadata blocks at the end of the stream.
- Affects enterprise customers on us-east region using persistent WebSocket sessions behind presigned TLS termination and aggressive 0-RTT retry policies.

Observed frequency:
- Intermittent: ~1 in 1200 streams during peak load for this customer. Reported first on 2026-03-09.

Expected behavior:
- Stream should deliver a single terminal JSON chunk with one metadata object and the complete final text. Reconnect/retry behavior should not produce duplicate terminal metadata.

Actual behavior:
- Final JSON object split across frames: first frame ends with a partial 'choices' array and a complete 'meta' block; second frame contains trailing tokens plus another 'meta' object. Client SDK reports a parsing error or concatenates metadata producing duplicate fields.
1) Establish a persistent WebSocket session to api.redwood.ai/v1/stream with standard event framing.
2) Start a long-running streaming generation (approx 800-1200 tokens) using model redwood-open-7b-v2 with streaming=true.
3) Simulate a client TCP half-close (FIN) immediately before a short network retry that triggers TLS 1.3 0-RTT resumption from the client side (this is observed behind certain load balancers and edge proxies).
4) Allow the client to reconnect and resume the stream; observe the last 1-3 chunks for duplicated 'meta' and a split final choice.
[2026-03-09T18:23:12.103Z] ws-session=abc123 state=streaming final_chunk_id=cf32 partial=true
[2026-03-09T18:23:12.106Z] tls=0rtt client_replay=true handshake=resume session=abc123
[2026-03-09T18:23:12.107Z] api-gateway: received FIN from client, transitioning to HALF_CLOSED
[2026-03-09T18:23:12.110Z] serving-runtime: flushed kv-cache for session=abc123; resume_token=rt-9f4
[2026-03-09T18:23:12.113Z] ws: sent frame(seq=912, last=false) payload_len=1024
[2026-03-09T18:23:12.117Z] ws: sent frame(seq=913, last=true) payload_len=128 meta_block_present=true
[2026-03-09T18:23:12.118Z] ws: sent frame(seq=914, last=true) payload_len=42 meta_block_present=true duplicate_meta_detected=true
Initial hypothesis: edge LB or client 0-RTT resumption triggers an aggressive session handoff where the last buffered frame is partially retransmitted, and the gateway/serving layer is re-emitting metadata on both fragments.
Parsed wire logs show two frames flagged 'last=true' emitted within 5ms with meta_block_present=true on both. Serving runtime logs indicate a flush of KV cache followed by a resumed transmit sequence using the same final-chunk id.
We reproduced a similar pattern in staging with a local proxy that performs 0-RTT reconnect simulation; reproduction requires precise timing: client FIN then immediate 0-RTT handshake reuse. Without 0-RTT we did not reproduce.
Potential root causes considered:
 - Double-emit from api-gateway during session handover (e.g., race between retry path and flush path).
 - Serving runtime mis-tagging a trailing fragment as terminal after partial flush.
 - TLS 0-RTT replay causing duplicate transmit of last queued frames by upstream LB.
Advise customer to disable 0-RTT retries on their edge/clients as a short-term mitigation, or increase client-side de-dupe tolerance for terminal metadata in SDK. We provided a patch to their SDK to ignore identical consecutive 'meta' blocks when parsing terminal choices.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11T14:33 NimbusDocs (Customer): Provided pcap and said they have 'enable_0rtt=true' on their F5 and see retries from client side during mobile flakiness window.
1) Instrument gateway to add a dedupe layer for terminal meta emission for 0-RTT/resume paths (short-term throttle guard).
2) Add unit/integration test simulating client FIN + immediate 0-RTT resumption and assert single terminal meta object. Link test to PR.
3) Work with infra to evaluate safe lifecycle for KV cache flush ordering to avoid double-finalization windows.
4) Coordinate with NimbusDocs to schedule a controlled repro in a canary window and verify fix.
Provided SDK patch to NimbusDocs to ignore adjacent duplicate 'meta' blocks for terminal chunks and recommended disabling TLS 0-RTT at the edge as immediate mitigation. Monitoring recommended for 72 hours before full rollout of gateway dedupe.
payload.summary: Client half-close during TLS 1.3 0-RTT retry causes websocket final payload split and duplicate metadata

comments: 2026-03-12T02:18:00Z Maya Chen: Ticket opened after ZenithSupport alerted via #support-escalations. Immediate mitigation requested and customer notified that engineering was triaging.

2026-03-12T02:25:00Z Rafael Ortega: Confirmed duplicate chunk pattern from traces (request replay observed when stream resumed after transient 503). Suspected interplay between autoscaler/node recycle and our prefix/KV cache warming logic.

2026-03-12T04:10:00Z Rafael Ortega: Applied temporary autoscaler cooldown (increase scale-down window to 10m) and enabled conservative rate-limiter policy for Zen pool. Duplicates and 5xxs subsided; monitoring green by 04:35.
payload.description:
Issue summary: During a nightly high-throughput batch ingest (10M tokens over 30 minutes) for ZenithAnalytics' dedicated pool in us-east, customers started seeing duplicate completion chunks and a rapid spike in token accounting. This triggered the platform autoscaler to aggressively add/remove nodes which in turn caused rate-limiter thrashing and elevated 5xxs for ~22 minutes.

Impact: Customer reported duplicate completions (some responses duplicated whole 300-token tails), inflated token consumption visible on observer, and temporary elevated latency and 5xx for ~2% of requests. Billing exposure estimated ~+8% token delta for the affected window. Zenith's downstream processors received duplicate payloads, triggering ingestion retries.

Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated), prod | us-east. ZenithAnalytics tenant id: ten-7721.

Steps to reproduce (summary):
1) Synthetic replay of Zenith's batch: 50K requests with 200–400 token completions using the customer's batching mode and prefix cache config.
2) Observe autoscaler triggers when tail latencies exceed 600ms and queued request backlog > 150.
3) Throttles/rate-limiter rules flip to more restrictive policy as nodes cycle and KV cache warms, causing partial replays and duplicated completions in resumed streams.

Observed behavior: Duplicated completion chunks (typically the last 50–100 tokens repeated), autoscaler rapid scale-up followed by scale-down oscillation, rate-limiter returning 429/503 cascades for short windows.

Expected behavior: Single, ordered completion per request. Smooth autoscaling with gradual capacity adjustments and stable rate limit enforcement.

Logs / artifacts: System traces attached to confluence page. Key traces show repeated request replays from gateway: request-id trace links in Confluence. Kernel selection logs show quantized kernel used for half the instances during window. KV-cache hit-rate dropped to 12% initially then recovered.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 03:05 - ZenithAnalytics (Customer): Confirmed duplicates are causing downstream ingestion to drop records. Asked for immediate temporary throttle reduction and refund window for affected tokens.
Initial triage: duplication correlated with stream resume after short-lived 503s; repeated writes from gateway session replay logic observed in traces.
Hypothesis 1: Gateway replay + resumed streaming interactions caused the serving-runtime to replay the last completion fragment due to missing idempotency checks on reattach.
Hypothesis 2: Rapid autoscaler churn caused inconsistent kernel selection and KV-cache warmup regressions leading to transient stream resets and gateway replay attempts.
Telemetry: KV cache hit-rate dropped to 12% at incident start, steady at ~85% after stabilizing. Autoscaler metrics: 6 scale events in a 9-minute window. Rate-limiter logs show policy flips from 'moderate' to 'restrictive' twice during the window.
Root cause (conclusion): Combination of (A) gateway-level request replay on perceived transient 503s during stream resumption and (B) aggressive autoscaler scale-down policy that enabled node churn before KV caches warmed, which together created a replay loop producing duplicate completion fragments.
Contributing factor: A recent change to the autoscaler aggressiveness feature flag (ASG-aggressive=true) rolled out to dedicated pools for cost optimization two days earlier; the Zen pool hit the new threshold under batch load.
Evidence links: Traces and histogram dashboards posted to Confluence page; kernel-selection and autoscaler event timelines captured there.
Immediate mitigation (2026-03-12 03:50): Increased autoscaler scale-down grace period to 10m for Zenith's pool; disabled 'ASG-aggressive' for the pool; applied conservative rate-limiter fallback rules to prevent replay amplification.
Code fix (2026-03-13): Backported a patch to gateway reattach logic to enforce idempotent stream re-entry: server now uses resume-token validation and discards duplicate completion chunks when sequence numbers overlap. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2291.
Config change (2026-03-13): Updated default dedicated-pool autoscaler profile to use smoother ramp (min step 10% / max step 40%) and KV cache pre-warm hook when scale events exceed threshold.
Customer remediation: Issued a billing credit for the affected window equivalent to estimated +8% token delta; customer notified and accepted the credit (credit applied on 2026-03-14 invoice).
Monitoring: Added alert 'dedicated.pool.duplicate-completion-rate' and dashboard tile for autoscaler-churn-rate; synthetic test added to nightly suite to replay Zenith-style batch and detect duplicates within 5 minutes of deploy.
Status: Fix deployed to prod for dedicated pools in us-east on 2026-03-13 22:10. Verified with customer-run replay and production telemetry.
1) Postmortem writeup to be published to Confluence by 2026-03-16 (owner: Rafael Ortega).
2) Rollout plan to remove 'ASG-aggressive' flag globally only after 2-week canary and additional load tests (owner: Platform Team).
3) Add resume-token idempotency unit/integration tests and include in CI gating for gateway (owner: Gateway Team, due 2026-03-20).
4) Review billing exposure calculation for batched workloads; create automated token-delta check that flags unusual deltas per tenant (owner: Billing, due 2026-03-24).
5) Schedule a customer-facing review session with ZenithAnalytics to go over root cause and safeguards (owner: Customer Success, scheduled 2026-03-18).
payload.summary: ZenithAnalytics: duplicate completions during batched ingest triggered autoscaler throttle cascade - post-incident action plan

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent high latency (~200-800ms increase at p95/p99) for in-region requests when their routing falls back off the primary us-west pool into an out-of-region egress path. Impact: user-facing timeouts for inference calls in production, elevated token cost due to retrying. Timeline: 2026-03-09 17:40 UTC - customer began seeing spikes; 2026-03-09 18:05 UTC - first support contact; 2026-03-10 - triage opened and routed to SRE and Routing owners. This ticket covers investigation of whether egress policy, TLS session reuse, or cross-region routing orchestration is the root cause.
Production inference calls for NimbusHealth show transient p95/p99 latency increases causing degraded UX during morning traffic peak. Estimated 8% of requests experienced >=200ms extra latency during incident windows.
1) Configure account with region-pin=us-west and low-tier fallback routing enabled
2) Send steady generation traffic (approx 30 requests/s) targeting rw-7b-instruct with short contexts
3) Simulate reduced capacity in us-west pool to trigger fallback routing
4) Observe end-to-end latency and trace headers (X-Trace-Id) for out-of-region routed requests
Representative traces: trace-id=trc_20260309_7f3a; see traces page https://console.redwood/instrumentation/traces/trc_20260309_7f3a. API gateway logs show 0.6s increase before streaming token emission. SRE packet captures (pcap) uploaded to s3://redwood-support/sup-20347/pcaps.tar.gz. No obvious 5xx errors in serving-runtime, but TLS handshake times increase for some connections (full handshake observed vs resumed session).

Additional notes:
Customer (NimbusHealth): We only observe impact for model rw-7b-instruct and when our internal autoscaler reduces us-west capacity. We can disable fallback if that helps.
Observations:
- Correlated spikes only on requests that were routed to out-of-region egress (us-east) after a brief us-west capacity shortfall.
- TLS metrics: session reuse dropped significantly for those requests; full TLS handshakes added ~120-350ms.
- Network path: out-of-region egress traverses a different edge NAT with distinct TLS session cache lifetime.
- No application-level 5xx; serving-runtime token generation time unchanged.
Hypotheses:
- Egress policy currently selects fallback region by availability, not by TLS session affinity; this can cause cold TLS handshakes adding latency.
- Edge-level session cache population is uneven across egress IP blocks.
- There may be an SRC IP NAT translation causing MTU differences that sometimes trigger additional packetization latency.
Next steps:
- Roll temporary preference to keep fallthrough egress in same region when available (done, monitoring).
- Add instrumentation to capture TLS handshake vs resumed percentages per egress IP block.
- Evaluate pre-warming/resuming TLS sessions for common customer pins during autoscaler events.
- Create runbook entry and customer-facing explanation about fallthrough latency tradeoffs.
Mitigation applied: temporary routing preference to select regional egress for pinned fallthroughs rolled out to NimbusHealth's account. Early metrics show p95 reduced by ~180ms for affected requests in the first hour. Final resolution pending: engineering change to ensure TLS session affinity and improved egress cache warm-up. Follow-ups: create a platform change to prefer TLS-session-affine egress when possible, update docs to call out expected latency delta for cross-region fallbacks, and add a config flag for customers to choose strict residency vs graceful fallback. NO final code PR merged yet; work tracked with linked PR and runbook updates.
Short term: we applied an account-level routing preference to keep fallthrough egress regional. Please monitor your 48-hour window and report any regressions. Long term: we will introduce TLS-session-affinity and a config toggle for strict residency fallback behavior. Documentation pointer will be provided once change is scheduled.
payload.summary: Intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes when region-pinned traffic falls back to out-of-region egress

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ShopRight Inc.) reports repeated user prompts take ~10-50ms normally but p99 jumps to 1.2-1.6s for repeat prompts after short idle (~20-60s). This started 2026-03-11 ~14:00 UTC and affects their dedicated pool in us-east.

Impact:
- Elevated p99 for identical prompts after ~30s idle causing timeouts for edge UI flows (error surfaced to end-users).
- Affects ~8% of requests from the customer's dedicated pool during observed windows.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (customer-scoped GPU pool) in us-east.
- Model: rw-open-7b-v2 pinned by customer.
- Serving runtime v2026.02.3, KV-store (metadata) v1.8.2.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From a dedicated API key tied to the customer's pool, send prompt A (short prompt, deterministic).
2) Wait 30-45s idle.
3) Re-send prompt A.
4) Observe latency distribution: p50 ~ 40ms, p95 ~ 120ms, p99 ~ 1.2s-1.6s.

Observed behavior:
- The follow-up (repeat) prompt triggers synchronous remote KV fetch for prefix metadata and blocks the request thread until KV returns.
- Logs show a KV "coherence lookup" and subsequent shard revalidation on the RPC path.
- Traces correlate the p99 spike to a 1.0s+ wait on kv-metadata.replica-read.

Expected behavior:
- Repeat prompt after short idle should hit local prefix cache / speculatively prefetch and return with ~baseline latency (no >1s waits).

Relevant logs / metric pointers:
- Trace: https://observability.redwood.internal/traces/trace-20260312-8342 (shows stall at kv-metadata.replica-read)
- Dashboard: https://observability.redwood.internal/dashboards/kv-coherence (spike at 2026-03-11 14:02 UTC)
Hypothesis: cache coherence window (soft TTL + lease refresh) allows a short period after idle where the local prefix cache marks entries stale and triggers synchronous revalidation with the central KV store. For hot keys this causes head-of-line blocking when several concurrent requests for the same prefix race to revalidate and the first revalidation path does not publish the new lease until completion, forcing others to wait.

Findings so far:
- Reproduced against a customerdedicated cluster in staging. Identical sequence produced p99 ~1.3s and traces match prod behavior.
- KV-store metrics show increased replica-read latency coincident with spikes; one node reported GC pause ~150ms in same interval.
- Hot-key contention observed: when multiple clients replay repeat prompts within coherence window, only one prefetch is allowed and others block.
- Prefetch is currently synchronous on cache miss by design; there is no request-level speculative background prefetch for identical prompts.

Temporary mitigations tested (staging):
- Increasing prefix_cache.soft_ttl from 30s -> 300s eliminated the repeat p99 spikes for test workload but increases memory footprint.
- Enabling speculative async prefetch (feature flag) caused follow-ups to hit warm cache and reduced p99 to baseline.

Next investigative actions:
- Correlate shard leadership changes and recent shard rebalance (possible contributing factor).
- Test async prefetch at scale and evaluate memory/cost tradeoffs.
- Check for other customers in the same pool experiencing same pattern.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 08:30 UTC - Support (Aisha Kumar): Customer confirmed noticeable improvement in their UI flows after mitigation. No user-facing errors reported in last 10 hours.
2026-03-13 12:00 UTC - Engineering (Liam O'Neill): Preparing PR with async prefetch and singleflight deduping to avoid head-of-line blocking (see related_github_prs).
Mitigation applied: prefix_cache.soft_ttl increased from 30s to 300s for ShopRight's dedicated pool in prod-us-east; speculative async prefetch feature-flag enabled for same pool.
Rollout notes:
- Hotfix applied 2026-03-12 14:10 UTC to customer pool only. Verified improvement via customer and dashboards.
- No regressions in baseline latency observed for other traffic during limited rollout.
Permanent fix plan:
1) Merge async prefetch + singleflight dedupe PR to prevent multiple concurrent revalidations (PR linked).
2) Add a local lease publish path so the first revalidation can publish new lease faster to peer caches.
3) Add alert for kv-coherence replica-read p95 > 200ms.
4) Post-mortem and adjust default soft_ttl algorithm to be workload-aware.
Follow-ups / action items:
- ENG-1287: evaluate memory/cost of increased soft_ttl across customer base.
- OPS-442: add runbook step to trigger async prefetch flag for affected pools.
- QA: add integration test that simulates hot repeat prompts after variable idle times.
Related slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.com/support/archives/C03KJ2H9); customer-provided request IDs: rq_20260311_140207_{a..c}.
payload.summary: Cache coherence window causing repeat-request p99 latency spikes after short idle

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after onboarding via SAML SSO, scheduled worker jobs and API impersonation calls for a particular service account are failing with 403 'insufficient_scope' or 403 'unauthorized_impersonation'. The same SAML assertion, when used to log in to the Redwood Console, shows the expected group memberships in the Console UI and admin role is visible. The failure appears only for API routes and scheduled worker impersonation, not interactive console sessions.

Impact:
- Several scheduled batch jobs (daily model scoring) failed to start for the last 6 hours.
- Customer's service account cannot be used for impersonation endpoints; operational impact to production analytics pipelines.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) running identity-proxy v1.18.2 behind HAProxy ingress in eu-west.
- SAML IdP: Customer on-prem ADFS 2019, sending Groups attribute as a single string with semicolon separators (e.g., "GroupA;GroupB;org-admins").

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Trigger SAML SSO via IdP, capture SAML Response (POST with Groups attribute as semicolon-delimited string).

4) Inspect headers arriving at identity-proxy for API path vs console path; API path contains header 'x-rw-groups: GroupA;GroupB;org-admins' (single header value), while console flow has header passed through as multiple header instances in the HTTP stack.

Observed behavior:
- API path: RBAC evaluation treats the entire 'GroupA;GroupB;org-admins' string as a single group label, no match to configured role bindings.
- Console path: framework shows parsed groups correctly (console route normalizes header by splitting on both comma and semicolon).

Expected behavior:
- Both console and API routes should parse group attributes similarly and match against role bindings so impersonation succeeds when the user is in any required group.

Relevant logs/traces (redacted):
- identity-proxy (api route) at 2026-03-11T09:17:22Z: "received header x-rw-groups=GroupA;GroupB;org-admins"
- rbac-evaluator (api route) at 2026-03-11T09:17:22Z: "no matching role binding for subject 'GroupA;GroupB;org-admins'"
- console-auth (same timestamp): "parsed groups [\"GroupA\",\"GroupB\",\"org-admins\"] for user uid=aurora"

- Updated IdP to emit groups as multiple attribute instances (not possible for all groups due to IdP config limits).

Customer (2026-03-11 11:15 UTC) - Helena Park (Aurora): Provided SAML response and HAProxy config snippet. Confirmed console flows show expected groups; API flows do not.
SRE (2026-03-11 14:43 UTC) - Diego Ramos: Verified ingress rewrites multiple header instances into a single header value for backend API routes due to 'http-request set-header' config in HAProxy. This explains why API path sees single header value. Will pair with identity team to confirm parsing difference.
Identity Eng (2026-03-12 08:22 UTC) - Liam O'Connor: Reproduced locally with a test IdP emitting semicolon-delimited groups. Found identity-proxy's header-splitting logic only splits on comma for API auth path; console path uses a shared middleware that splits on comma and semicolon. Preparing patch to unify parsing behavior.
Customer (2026-03-12 12:01 UTC) - Helena Park: Applied temporary role binding for the semicolon-joined literal and restored scheduled jobs. Requesting permanent fix and guidance to avoid future breaks.
2026-03-11: Packet capture shows HAProxy collapsing multiple Set-Cookie and multiple x-rw-groups instances into a single header string when using 'http-request set-header' with concatenation. This is common in their HAProxy config to normalize incoming headers for backend routing.

Temporary mitigation: created a customer-scoped role binding for the literal semicolon-joined group string to restore operations. payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sustained latency increase (200–800ms p50 delta) for requests pinned to EU region despite 'preferred-edge' routing configured. Customer expects all inference traffic for their account to remain in EU for residency reasons; however, some requests appear to egress via the US and show higher tail latency.

Impact:
- FinLedger (enterprise customer) sees elevated response times for model inferences used in customer-facing workflow (real-time risk scoring).
- Errors have not been reported, but tail latency breaches internal SLO and degrades UX.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod), customer account configured with region pin: eu-west-1 and routing policy: preferred_edge (not strict_residency).
- VPC peering + NAT gateway present on customer side; traffic egress patterns documented in their network team notes.
- Affected models: redwood-giant-v1 (default), fallback to llama-3-13b-q4 for capacity events.

Steps to reproduce (as performed by customer):
1) Issue repeated generate calls to /v1/completions with account API key and routing header X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1.
2) Observe p50/p95 latency over 10k requests during business hours (09:00–12:00 CET).
3) Compare traces where the request path shows egress to us-east-1 and where it stays eu-west-1.

Expected behavior:
- With preferred_edge, control-plane should route to eu-west-1 endpoints when capacity and health permit.
- No cross-region egress for request/response body when eu region has capacity.

Actual behavior:
- ~6% of requests are routed via a US egress path and show +200–800ms latency compared to EU-local requests.
- Routing logs include fallbacks to compatible model variants and occasionally show a route decision referencing 'preferred_region_unavailable -> fallback-region'.

Logs / Observations provided by customer:
- Sample trace IDs: trace-eu-0001, trace-eu-0145, trace-us-0991 (attached as headers in their support dump).
- Timestamped latency histogram CSV attached in ticket (customer_latency_2026-03-09.csv).
- Private note: their infra team reports NAT gateway scaling events aligned with some of the spike windows.

Customer asks:
1) Why did preferred-edge routing result in cross-region egress for a subset of requests?
2) Is there a toggle to enforce strict residency to guarantee no cross-region egress? What are trade-offs?
3) Can Redwood provide immediate mitigations or configuration changes to reduce tail latency while preserving residency requirements?

Requested next steps:
- Support to confirm exact routing decision logic and provide actionable config recommendation (strict_residency vs preferred).
- SRE to check platform-side capacity and fallback conditions for eu-west-1 during affected windows.
- Engineering to advise on an account-level setting that forces strict residency with documented performance and capacity implications.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 16:20 - FinLedger (Customer): Provided VPC flow logs for trace-eu-0145 and notes that strict_residency would be preferred if it avoids US egress. Asking about cost/latency tradeoffs for strict enforcement.
Findings so far:
- Routing behavior: 'preferred_edge' prioritizes pinned region but may allow fallback to alternate region variants when node health or serving capacity drops below thresholds. Fallback includes cross-region egress for request bodies if no compatible local variants are available.
- Platform signals: autoscaler and health checks showed short-lived degraded state in a small subset of eu-west-1 serving pools; related to an upstream kernel memory regression rolled in on 2026-03-09 (investigating with infra patch PR).
- Customer-side signals: NAT gateway scaling and increased egress latency coincided with some traces but not all; indicates mixed contribution (platform routing + customer network).
- Metrics: sampled 1k traces; cross-region requests had median +420ms and p95 +780ms compared to EU-local.
- Temporary config change 'strict_residency=true' would prevent cross-region fallback but may increase request failures or queueing under capacity pressure.
Next technical actions:
1) SRE to provision a small capacity buffer for FinLedger's account in eu-west-1 for peak hours as an interim (estimated 4x small GPU instances).
2) Engineering to evaluate adding an account-level knob that enforces strict residency with clear SLO degradations documented.
3) Request customer supply one full PCAP for a representative trace to finalize customer-side vs platform-side latency attribution.
4) Track infra PRs that may have caused memory pressure (linked PR in related_github_prs).
Work in progress. Interim mitigations proposed:
- Provision short-term capacity buffer for FinLedger (SRE action, scheduled 2026-03-13 allocation).
- Support to offer configuration guidance: set account routing.policy.strict_residency = true to eliminate cross-region egress; caution: may lead to increased 429s if local capacity is exhausted.
- Engineering to spec an account-level strict residency toggle with telemetry and failure-mode warnings (follow-up ticket planned).
Owner: Marco Gutierrez (SRE) for capacity buffer; Lina Chen for network correlation; Eng (routing) to owner follow-up ticket.
payload.summary: Clarify preferred-edge egress vs strict residency and observed latency spike for EU-pinned requests
