payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports an unexpected fee line labeled 'conversion-smoothing' on a finalized March invoice. At the same time hourly smoothing credits that usually offset microburst embed spikes were not applied for three separate bursts on 2026-03-02. The customer believes this is correlated with the org's recent rate-plan conversion performed by billing ops on 2026-03-01.

Impact: Finalized invoice USD 23,412.85 contains a new fee line of USD 412.50 and is missing -USD 375.00 in hourly-smoothing credits that NimbleDocs expected. Net unexpected charge ~USD 37.50. Customer is on enterprise contract and flagged as billing-impacting; they require an explanation and corrective credit.

Environment: prod, us-east; account id: org_009874; invoice id: INV-2026-03-009874; affected API keys: key-prod-ner-01 (masked).

Steps to reproduce / observation steps:
1) Run our standard invoice reconciliation for org_009874 for period 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07.
2) Inspect invoice line items and hourly smoothing ledger for the account in the billing UI and via /internal/billing/ledger API.
3) Observe presence of a one-off fee labeled 'conversion-smoothing' and absence of three expected smoothing credits that correspond to microburst windows (2026-03-02 02:00-02:15, 09:10-09:20, 17:45-17:50 UTC).

Observed behavior: A new fee line 'conversion-smoothing' (rate_type: conversion-fee) appears on finalized invoice. The hourly_smoothing ledger entries for those three microbursts show status 'pending' and were not promoted to 'applied' during finalization. Postback logs show smoothing job attempted, but the postback for those entries was rejected with a 400 error citing unknown rate_tag 'rp_conv_v2'.

Expected behavior: Hourly smoothing credits should have been applied before invoice finalization. No unexplained conversion fee should be billed to the customer; any rate-plan migration artifact should not create a positive fee without customer visibility.

Attachments: invoice PDF attached to ticket, extracted ledger CSV, postback log excerpt (billing-job-2026-03-02.log lines 412-436).

Requested action: Provide root-cause explanation, apply corrective credit if customer is owed one, and confirm fix to mapping so smoothing credits are applied for retroactive/converted rate plans.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:20 - SRE (Sophie Laurent): Found billing-worker container restarted during mapping deploy on 2026-03-01 23:59; mapping reload may have occurred with an incomplete diff. Saving container logs: billing-worker-logs-20260301.tar.gz.
2026-03-12 10:00 - Customer (NimbleDocs Billing Contact, Sara Lee): Acknowledged provisional credit; requests confirmation that this won't recur and asks for postmortem and any compensatory waiver for operational impact.
Initial triage: correlate rate-plan conversion deploy (rp-convert-20260301) with smoothing job failure. Observed error in smoothing-postback-service: 400 Bad Request 'unknown rate_tag rp_conv_v2'. Hypothesis: mapping table used by smoothing-postback-service was not updated atomically with rate-plan conversion and smoothing-service still expected pre-migration tags. Checked mapping delta: rp_conv_v2 introduced but smoothing mapping cache not reloaded due to a deploy race (billing-worker restarted mid-deploy). Logs indicate 2 smoothing postbacks for org_009874 were transitioned to 'pending' and later skipped during finalization because the credit reconciliation job treats pending entries with unrecognized rate_tag as non-applicable. Next steps: (1) Confirm mapping commit and exact deploy timestamps, (2) add idempotent cache-reload step in rate-plan conversion flow, (3) backfill smoothing credits for affected windows and regenerate invoice adjustments where appropriate.
In progress - provisional credit applied (CR-2026-03-752468). Engineering to patch mapping reload in conversion job and run backfill for pending smoothing entries. Final resolution will include an entry in the account ledger and a comment here when invoice adjustment completes.
Provisional credit posted on 2026-03-11 13:45 UTC. Billing engineering prepared a backfill script (github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1145) to mark pending smoothing entries as applied when mapping is available. Plan: schedule backfill on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC during maintenance window; if backfill succeeds we will generate an invoice credit note and close ticket. Customer requested a short postmortem; assigning follow-up to Billing Eng to produce a one-page action item list.
payload.summary: Hidden conversion-smoothing fee on finalized invoice; hourly smoothing credit not applied after rate-plan conversion

comments: 2026-03-12T00:00:00Z Aisha Patel: Initial report from customer attached; asked for telemetry screenshots and timestamps.
2026-03-12T00:00:00Z Marco Chen: Noted refill alignment looks suspicious; requested sampling from rate-limiter logs and tenant token refill metrics. Opened Slack thread #support-datasleuth.

2026-03-13T00:00:00Z Marco Chen: Found correlation between refill epoch boundaries and worker launch window; healthcheck OPTIONS counted as requests by edge; suggested immediate temporary mitigations.

2026-03-13T00:00:00Z Aisha Patel: Shared short-term mitigation steps with customer and asked if they can stagger jobs while we validate configuration changes. Customer agreed to test a small jitter change.
payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer observes repeated waves of 429s between 00:00 and 00:15 UTC each day for their production ingest pipeline. Impact: user-facing webhook retries and delayed embeddings ingestion for the DataSleuth pipeline; spikes correspond to scheduled batch jobs and orchestrator-coordinated warmup tasks. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod-us-east with a reserved Dedicated pool; orchestrator runs ~1,200 short-lived workers across 24 pods that perform scheduled pulls and embed calls.
1) Customer runs daily scheduled job that launches 1,200 short-lived worker tasks during midnight UTC window.
2) Each worker performs a preflight health check (OPTIONS) then initiates 3 parallel embedding calls.
3) Orchestrator warmup flag set to true, and service-sidecanary path performs lightweight model warmup requests at the same time.
4) Observe 429s in client telemetry and on Redwood console token/quota dashboards.
- Sawtooth pattern of 429s starting at 00:00 UTC peaking at 00:03–00:07 and decaying by 00:15.
- Rate-limit headers show per-tenant token window exhaustion (X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0) with Refill-Interval anchored at top-of-minute.
- Logs show many simultaneous short-lived connections reusing ephemeral keys and healthcheck probes counted as requests.
- Customer noticed console shows 'burst_pool' credit approaching zero during the window.
Scheduled background workers should not generate tenant-impacting 429s if burst credit and smoothing are configured for cron-style fanout; healthcheck probes ideally excluded from quota accounting or routed to a separate background pool.
[2026-03-12T00:02:01Z] ingress-proxy: src=10.8.2.14 tenant=ds-prod req=/v1/embeddings status=429 tokens=0 remaining=0 window_refill=60ms
[2026-03-12T00:02:02Z] orchestrator: launched-worker id=wk-9372 preflight=OPTIONS status=200
[2026-03-12T00:02:02Z] rate-limiter: debit tenant=ds-prod amount=3 reason=embed-call
[2026-03-12T00:04:45Z] console: burst_pool_credit=12 -> 0
Sampled tenant refill logs show refill anchor at 00:00:00.000 and refill bursts every 60s with tokens slotted to tenant windows; large synchronous debit causes immediate exhaustion.
Healthcheck and preflight (OPTIONS) are currently accounted at the same priority as interactive embed calls in the customer's routing configuration.
Orchestrator warmup and canary paths fire lightweight model probing requests concurrently with worker launches; these are not tagged as 'background' in the customer's request headers so they consume primary burst pool.
Dedicated pool has burst_pool enabled but configured with low credit for background flows; smoothing interval is 60s and does not absorb the instantaneous fanout.
No sign of dedicated pool autoscaler failing; capacity adequate but token accounting is the limiter, not GPU saturation.
Add randomized jitter (recommended 5–30s per worker) to scheduled job launches to avoid synchronized token drains.
Reduce preflight healthcheck frequency or mark preflight requests with X-Request-Purpose: background so they can be routed to a background-burst pool.
Temporarily increase tenant burst_pool credit for the midnight window via console (support-approved) while final config is validated.
Enable client-side exponential backoff with small randomized jitter for retry loops to avoid synchronized retry waves.
If using ephemeral keys, batch creation so not all workers create new keys at the same second (avoid credential churn double-counting).
Configure route-level quota separation: isolate scheduled/background job routes to a distinct burst pool with larger smoothing window.
Adjust refill granularity: move from top-of-minute anchor to sliding refill or add micro-refills to avoid epoch alignment across tenants.
Enhance orchestration guidance in SDK: include helper to mark background calls and attach a recommended jitter helper for cron fans-out.
Consider server-side exclusion rules for lightweight model warmup probes or tag them as diagnostic and route to low-priority quota.
Add telemetry alerting rule: detect >50% of tenant debits within 30s window and auto-suggest staggered rollout to customers.
2026-03-13: Agreed on a two-step plan with customer. 1) Short-term: DataSleuth added 10s jitter to job launches and reduced preflight to once per pod; Redwood Support temporarily bumped tenant burst_pool credits for two nights. Observed 70% reduction in peak 429 rate. 2) Long-term: SRE will onboard a route-separation config template for scheduled/background flows and open a follow-up internal ticket to evaluate sliding refill implementation. Customer satisfied with mitigation and will report back after full rollout.
- SRE (Marco Chen) to create internal follow-up INT ticket to prototype sliding refill (ETA 2 sprints).
- Support to follow up with DataSleuth on 48h observational window and close if no regressions.
- Document recommended cron jitter and background-pool config in public KB article.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - DataSleuth Support Rep (customer): Uploaded per-worker traces and confirmed orchestrator jitter was previously set to 0s. They confirmed >1k worker fanout at midnight UTC.
2026-03-13 - DataSleuth (customer): Performed staggered rollout with 10s jitter and reported reduced peak 429s but still observed some soft throttles at peak concurrency.
payload.summary: Orchestrator jitter alignment causing periodic tenant 429s; request config guidance and short-term mitigation

comments: 2025-01-09T03:55:00Z Hypothesis: During promote, added tracing IDs from canary-coordinator increased header size; sanitizer dropped X-Tenant-Pin, leading router to treat requests as unpinned and use fallback routing rules.
2025-01-09T03:30:00Z Grace Kim: Customer reported mixed outputs after promote with example request IDs and timestamps; requested rollback if variance persists.
2025-01-09T04:05:00Z Anika Patel: Attached correlation IDs and initial analysis showing header drops at edge-proxy; investigating sanitizer rules and sidecar behavior.
2025-01-09T05:15:00Z Marco Alvarez: Confirmed reproduction locally by increasing header length via tracing; preparing PR to whitelist pin header and add router guard.
2025-01-09T07:45:00Z Marco Alvarez: Deployed edge-proxy hotfix to us-west (PR #4120) that exempts X-Tenant-Pin; monitoring metrics and customer test traffic shows normalization.
2025-01-11T09:10:00Z Olivia Chen: Confirmed behavior returned to expected; thanked the team for quick response.
payload.description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled canary promote for LumenAI's dedicated pool in us-west, we observed ~12% of tenant requests routed to a different model variant (redwood-v2-medium-quant) despite the tenant being pinned to redwood-v2-medium. Impact: downstream quality alerts and customer request to rollback.

Environment: dedicated cluster tenant=lumenai-prod, edge shard=us-west-2, canary started at 03:14 UTC (5% -> promote to 100%) using canary-coordinator v1.8.2. LumenAI uses a sidecar proxy (lumen-sidecar v0.9.1) that appends tracing metadata and tenant-affinity headers.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Trigger promote from canary to full in console.
2) Customer concurrently ran a batch job increasing per-second requests by ~3x.
3) Edge logs show X-Tenant-Pin header present upstream but missing at router inputs for a subset of requests.
4) Router fallback logic selected older/quantized variant when header absent, causing mixed outputs.

Observed log example: "edge-proxy: header X-Tenant-Pin dropped connID=0432ef metadata_len=278 sanitizer_rule=header_length_regex"
2025-01-09 03:22 - Support triaged; initial staging attempts failed to reproduce because sidecar header trimming was not simulated.
2025-01-09 03:40 - SRE (Anika Patel) examined edge-proxy logs and found the header-sanitizer regex matched when header length exceeded 256 bytes (tracing + tenant metadata appended).

Additional notes:
2025-01-09 04:10 - Router analysis: when X-Tenant-Pin missing, router priority chain may pick a compatible variant (older or quantized) if promoted mapping is not committed atomically across route caches.
2025-01-09 04:45 - Reproduced in canary lab by crafting header payload >260 bytes; confirmed header was stripped and route fell back to prior model id.
2025-01-09 05:30 - Mitigation paths considered: 1) whitelist X-Tenant-Pin in edge-proxy sanitizer, 2) make router consult session-store pin before immediate fallback, 3) pause promote on traffic surge.
2025-01-09 07:00 - Short-term mitigation: disabled regex sanitizer for X-Tenant-Pin on us-west shard and prepared hotfix PR.
Root cause: a regex-based header sanitizer in edge-proxy dropped X-Tenant-Pin when sidecar tracing metadata made header length exceed a threshold during a traffic surge at promote. This caused router to consider requests unpinned and fall back to older model variants. Fixes deployed: 1) hotfix to edge-proxy to whitelist X-Tenant-Pin (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/4120) rolled to us-west at 07:45 UTC and staged for global rollout; 2) router guard change to consult session-store pin before fallback (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/289). Rollout notes: global edge rollout scheduled 2025-01-12 behind a feature flag with canary. Follow-ups: add automated canary-promote tests for large header payloads, add a runbook step to pause promotes on traffic spikes, and track a backlog task to remove header-length heuristics affecting routing headers (INT-1104).
payload.summary: Sidecar header sanitizer strips tenant pin during canary promote, causing mixed model routing

comments: 2026-03-12T08:15:00Z Jordan Phillips: Logged from customer call; they can reproduce reliably when Go and TS clients participate in same session. Provided sample traces and webhook timestamps.

2026-03-12T09:02:00Z Lina Ortiz: Investigating. Initial hypothesis: gRPC '-bin' metadata is base64-encoded by the proxy; HTTP client sends plain text UUID. Gateway dedupe logic compares canonical header string and does not decode base64 '-bin' equivalently.

2026-03-12T14:20:00Z Lina Ortiz: Temporary customer workaround: prefer consistent surface (both clients use HTTP or both use gRPC) or ensure Go SDK uses text header encoding (workaround patch attached). Will prepare gateway fix to canonicalize both encodings.
payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate downstream tool/function executions when a multi-service orchestrator mixes a Go gRPC client and a TypeScript HTTP client in the same session. Root cause appears related to different encodings/metadata keys used by gRPC (binary metadata) versus HTTP (text header) across our edge proxies.

Impact: Multiple customers using mixed-language orchestrators (Go + TS) see duplicated external webhook/tool calls on retries. Duplicates cause side effects (duplicate database writes, external webhook POSTs) and have led to one customer to temporarily disable automated retries.

Observed start: 2026-03-11 22:10 UTC. Reported via customer support ticket and linked Slack (#support-datasilo).
1) Setup an orchestrator with two client processes: a Go microservice using our Go gRPC SDK to call /v1/stream (gRPC) and a TypeScript worker using the HTTP SDK to call the same session via REST.
2) From TypeScript worker, send a function/tool-invocation request with idempotency key header 'x-redwood-idempotency' (text).
3) From Go gRPC client, send a matching request concurrently but the Go SDK attaches metadata key 'x-redwood-idempotency-bin' as binary metadata (raw bytes).
4) Induce a transient network error at the gateway (tcp reset) to force client-side retry of the TypeScript HTTP call.
5) Observe duplicated tool execution downstream (two webhook POSTs) despite both clients thinking they used the same idempotency value.
customer-observed: two webhook POSTs to https://hooks.datasilo.com/processor within 200ms of the retry attempt
gateway-request-log (ts-http): headers: { 'x-redwood-idempotency': 'B1f4c2b0-9e7a-4' }
gateway-request-log (go-grpc): metadata: { 'x-redwood-idempotency-bin': <binary 16 bytes> }
proxy-translation: grpc-proxy normalized '-bin' metadata into base64 string 'QjFmNGMyYjA...' and attached header 'x-redwood-idempotency: QjFmNGMyYjA...' while HTTP client used raw UUID string 'B1f4c2b0-9e7a-4'
serving-runtime trace: session_id=ses_03a2, trace_id=tr_9c4; tool_exec_id first=tool_112, second=tool_113; both had different idempotency canonical values, so dedupe check missed.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:40 - DataSilo (Customer): We confirmed two identical downstream POST bodies and different idempotency values in logs. We had to disable retries to avoid duplicates; this is blocking our production pipeline.
2026-03-13 07:30 - Eng (Gateway): Created draft PR to change gateway dedupe to decode '-bin' metadata into UTF-8 when possible, and to fallback to hex/base64 normalization. See PR #1284. Need security review for binary-to-text conversions.
2026-03-13 16:10 - Support (Jordan): Sent customer recommended temporary SDK patch for Go to set header 'x-redwood-idempotency' as text in addition to metadata (double-send) to avoid mismatch. Customer accepted patch; re-enabled retries under observation.
Hypothesis: mismatch between 'x-redwood-idempotency' (text) and 'x-redwood-idempotency-bin' (binary) resulted in different canonical values downstream; dedupe only matched exact header string.
Reproduced in staging by running concurrent TS HTTP and Go gRPC clients against edge-proxy with tcpkill induced transient resets. Confirmed two executions when binary metadata encoded as base64 differs from raw text UUID.
Examined gateway code path: grpc-proxy currently leaves '-bin' metadata as base64 without attempting reversible decoding into UTF-8 text; compare logic uses strict string equality against HTTP header value.
Security note: decoding arbitrary binary metadata into UTF-8 for canonicalization could be unsafe; need to whitelist expected idempotency header formats (UUID, hex, base64 of UTF-8).
Tested local gateway patch that normalizes both forms: 1) if header present and looks like UUID, use that; 2) if '-bin' present, attempt base64 decode and validate UTF-8/UUID; 3) compare normalized tokens for dedupe. Patch passes unit tests and reproducer.
Workaround delivered: customer applied a small Go SDK patch (attached) that sets both the text header 'x-redwood-idempotency' and the binary metadata 'x-redwood-idempotency-bin' with identical byte/UTF-8 encoding; after that, duplicates stopped.
Planned permanent fix: gateway PR #1284 will add normalization to accept and compare both text and -bin metadata by canonicalizing to UTF-8/UUID when safe. Security review scheduled and a canary rollout to prod us-east by 2026-03-18.
Follow-ups: update SDK docs with cross-language idempotency guidance, add an integration test in e2e suite that mixes gRPC and HTTP clients, and add a monitoring alert for duplicate tool executions per session above threshold.
payload.summary: Duplicate function/tool executions when mixing Go gRPC client and TS HTTP client: idempotency header encoding mismatch

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long streaming responses delivered over SSE occasionally end with a truncated final markdown/code block and a leftover HTML numeric entity (e.g. '👍') after a network path failover through their corporate proxy. The stream reconnects and resumes but the very last tokens are missing and a trailing entity is left in the last line, causing downstream markdown renderers to break.
Several API calls from BrightBoard production workloads return incomplete final paragraphs or malformed markdown on ~0.5% of streaming sessions during business hours, causing UI errors and automated parsing failures. Customer reports user-visible failures for their summary-generation flow.
1) Use SSE streaming endpoint with conversation length > 800 tokens and markdown output enabled
2) Put client behind a corporate proxy that performs an HTTP 100-Continue handshake and sometimes re-routes connections during idle probes
3) Start stream, simulate a path migration (NAT/idle-probe) from client network or trigger proxy connection splice
4) Observe resumed stream output for missing terminal tokens and presence of a trailing numeric HTML entity in the final line
5) Reproduce more reliably by adding a 1-3s intermittent packet loss during the final chunk window and by enabling aggressive proxy keepalive rebinds
Request-id: req_9a7c2b4d; client_ip: 54.235.12.87; proxy-conn-id: proxy-19; start: 2026-03-01T15:22:13Z
Serving runtime logs (excerpt): [2026-03-01T15:22:15.102Z] token-stream: chunk 0..N-1 flushed; [2026-03-01T15:22:17.438Z] connection: upstream splice detected; session-resume: true; resume_offset: 0x7f2
Edge proxy trace: proxynode-19 performed connection-rebind due to idle-probe (see /internal/traces/tn-19-20260301)
Client observed payload (final bytes): "...
- Summary: 3 bullets
> Note: confirmed by tests 👍" (missing trailing backticks for codeblock)
Proxy response headers (captured): Connection: keep-alive, Transfer-Encoding: chunked, X-Proxy-Splice: true
Initial hypothesis: proxy path splice is splitting a UTF-8 multi-byte emoji sequence across the final chunk boundary, and our reassembly logic for resume assumes chunk-aligned UTF-8 boundaries; trailing bytes are being interpreted as HTML entities during downstream JSON/markdown framing
Reproduced internally with synthetic proxy rebind using corp-proxy-sim v0.9 and observed identical orphaned numeric entity present only when rebind occurs in the middle of a multi-byte sequence
Observed that SSE resume uses byte-oriented offsets from runtime; however some edge proxies perform transparent header/body rewrites (100-Continue) which incrementally alter chunk boundaries leading to mismatch between resume_offset and actual re-streamed payload
Found related flaky unit in streaming parser: parser/streaming_assembler.go: line 278 does a 'if resumeOffset == savedOffset' fast path that doesn't validate UTF-8 tail bytes; added a failing test case locally
Checked model generation: final tokens include emoji or characters that encode as 4-byte UTF-8 sequences (e.g. thumbs-up). This interacts with chunking where a split can leave 1-3 continuation bytes orphaned
Edge note: customer uses an enterprise WAF that rewrites chunking on TLS termination; WAF adds '100-Continue' handling and sometimes re-chunks responses into smaller segments during spike backpressure
2026-03-01 16:10 - Customer (BrightBoard): We see the UI fail to render when the trailing '👍' appears. It happens intermittently and correlates with our corporate proxy cpu spikes.
2026-03-02 09:04 - Support (Aisha): Thanks, we are investigating. Can you share a HAR or tcpdump from the time window?
2026-03-02 11:30 - Customer: Attached tcpdump (sensitive) shared via secure link: https://files.brightboard.example/secure/tcpdump-20260301.pcap (access granted to redwood SREs)

Issue summary: QuantileAI reported sustained 429 responses for a subset of production requests starting 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC. Traffic pattern: high-cardinality microservice front proxy that shards requests across ephemeral API keys per upstream worker. Symptoms indicate token-bucket exhaustion on the tenant-level accounting caused by synchronized client retries and per-request key fanout.

Impact: ~12% of live inference requests return 429s intermittently across two services that share a forwarding proxy. Latency and throughput degraded for latency-sensitive features; customer reported increased errors in user-facing inference endpoints and alerted CSM.

Environment: Dedicated pool (QuantileAI-reserved), prod us-east, HTTP/2 between customer proxy and Redwood edge, customer uses short-lived API keys minted per worker.

Observed at: 2026-03-12 09:10–11:45 UTC.

Logs & snapshots: see logs_snippet field for representative lines. Rate limiter metrics show tenant token balance hit zero for 30–90s windows while per-key buckets still had tokens (indicating misaligned accounting).

Hypothesis: Customer-side retry library performs coordinated retries with limited jitter plus our edge proxy shards requests across multiple ephemeral keys. When a subset of requests hit transient backend 503s, clients retried aggressively causing multiple keys to be used in quick succession and amplifying token consumption at the tenant level. The combination of per-request key fanout + synchronized retries caused tenant-level token buckets to be exhausted leading to cascading 429s for unrelated requests.
1) Deploy small proxy that mints ephemeral API keys per outbound worker and multiplexes via HTTP/2 to Redwood edge.
2) Run 200 concurrent clients that call the proxy with a short timeout and a retry library configured with exponential backoff but no jitter (retries at 50ms, 100ms, 200ms).
3) Inject transient 503 responses at the serving-runtime for 2 minutes (simulate noisy GPU or model eviction).
4) Observe tenant token-bucket metrics and request traces in Console; expect tenant_quota_tokens to reach zero while individual key buckets report remaining capacity.
5) Observe surge of 429s across unrelated endpoints during retry window.
Initial triage: verified 429s were tenant-scoped (Console tenant view) rather than per-key; deduced accounting at the tenant layer dropped below zero while some per-key counters remained positive.
Checked dedicated-pool autoscaler logs: no scaling events during window; serving-runtime reported transient 503s consistent with a single host eviction (investigation INT-4421).
Replayed customer traffic in staging with their proxy config: reproduced tenant-level 429s when retry library had no randomized jitter and when ephemeral keys were minted per request.
Confirmed customer was using an internal retry strategy that retries up to 5x with minimal backoff, amplifying the original failure into N simultaneous attempts across multiple keys.
Identified missing smoothing at the token-refill layer for tenant-level accounting when key fanout is high; rate-limiter treats each key consumption equally but tenant refill pulse is coarse (60s).

Additional notes:
Instructed customer to switch proxy to a small pool of stable API keys (reuse across workers) for 10 minutes to absorb retry bursts.
Recommended enabling jitter in their retry library (random delay between 30–150ms) to avoid synchronized retries.
Applied a short-term rule at edge to exclude internal health-check endpoints from tenant accounting while we audit the probe list (edge rule id=EXCLUDE-qa-health-2026-03-12).
Combination of customer-side coordinated retries without jitter + per-request ephemeral API key fanout + coarse tenant-level token refill caused tenant token exhaustion and 429 responses across services.
Customer applied pooled-key reuse and jitter; Support deployed a temporary health-check exclusion rule. Engineering (rate-limiter team) scheduled a change to smooth tenant-level refills and add a configurable per-tenant short-window burst multiplier to reduce sensitivity to transient retry storms. Patch tracked in infra PR and linked runbook. Final follow-up assigned to INT-4421 for persistent fix rollout.
ENG: Implement tenant-level refill smoothing and a short-window burst allowance (owner: rate-limiter team, target: 2026-03-20).
SRE: Monitor dedicated-pool tenant_quota for QuantileAI for 7 days post-fix (owner: Luca Romano).
CS: Share best-practice guidance with QuantileAI (pooled keys, retry jitter, health-check exclusion) and capture config in account notes.
Monitoring in progress — customer reports normal error rates since 2026-03-12 11:30 UTC. Engineering follow-up scheduled.
payload.summary: Proxy retry amplification causing sharded API-key exhaustion and cascading 429s

Issue summary: customer reports repeated 403s for several service accounts after a scheduled IdP configuration change. Impact: administrators and service integrations cannot complete tenant-scoped operations; user-facing APIs that depend on correct tenant resolution are failing. Environment: private deployment (VPC) with our identity-service proxied by the customer's ingress. Observed after IdP updated client registrations.

Initial hypothesis: assertion claim format or audience values changed during IdP update, causing Redwood's tenant resolution to pick an incorrect tenant.

1) IdP issues SAML/OIDC assertion for a service account with multiple audience values (aud contains two client IDs: one for the customer's monitoring app and one for the customer's platform integration).
2) Submit assertion to Redwood private token-exchange endpoint behind customer's ingress.
3) Identity-service attempts tenant resolution and binds account to tenant A, while tokens were intended for tenant B.
4) Requests for tenant-scoped admin APIs return 403 with 'tenant mismatch' audit log entries.
When IdP assertion contains multiple audience entries that match client IDs across tenants, identity-service should either disambiguate using azp or another claim, or reject the assertion with a clear error indicating ambiguous audience values.
Identity-service accepted the assertion and selected the first matching client_id for tenant binding, resulting in incorrect tenant association and authorization failures for legitimate requests.
Audit trace: 2024-11-05T08:12:22Z identity-service tenant_resolution: matched_client=client-9f3a first_seen
Sample assertion (redacted): {"iss":"https://idp.example.com", "sub":"svc-account@greenwave", "aud":["client-9f3a","client-2b77"], "azp":"client-2b77"}
Authz error returned to caller: {'status':403,'message':'tenant mismatch: token resolved to tenant A, request target tenant B'}
Customer-provided SAML metadata snapshot and IdP client registration export attached in ticket.
2024-11-05 10:05 - Support (Aisha Khan): Opened with customer-provided assertion and sample logs. Customer says change occurred after IdP team updated client registrations on 2024-11-04.
2024-11-05 11:20 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Reproduced in a staging private deployment using customer's IdP export. Identity-service picks the first aud entry when mapping client_id -> tenant. Creating reproduce script and adding to ticket.
2024-11-05 14:03 - Customer (Greenwave SSO Admin, Maria Perez): Confirm IdP intentionally added an additional audience to support a new integration; expected azp to be authoritative. Sent full assertion examples and tenant mapping spreadsheet.

Additional notes:
2024-11-06 16:40 - Support (Aisha Khan): Informed customer of workaround to revert IdP change while we validate and patch behavior. Customer accepted temporary revert for next 24 hours and asked for ETA.
- Reproduced failure in staging using customer's IdP export and a mirrored tenant map.
- Identity-service tenant resolution flow: map aud entries to client_id -> tenant; currently selects first matching mapping without cross-checking azp.
- Customer's IdP emits aud as an array where position is not stable across rotations; reliance on array order is unsafe.
- Observed multiple customers with similar IdP configs in testbed; risk of wider impact if IdP rotates audience ordering.
Identity-service tenant resolution logic treated aud array position as authoritative and did not prefer azp when present. When IdP emitted multiple aud values spanning different tenants, the resolver bound requests to the wrong tenant instead of validating or rejecting ambiguous assertions.
Customer reverted the recent IdP client registration change to remove the additional audience entry. As a temporary mitigation, Support instructed customer to configure the IdP to put the intended client_id first in the aud array or populate azp consistently (if supported).
Deployed patch in identity-service that: 1) treats azp as authoritative when present and equivalent to aud target, 2) adds strict validation to reject assertions where aud array contains multiple entries that map to different tenants without an authoritative azp, 3) logs a clear validation failure with guidance for IdP teams. Hotfix PR merged and scheduled for private control plane rollout to Greenwave during maintenance window 2024-11-08 02:00 UTC.
1) Update tenant resolution runbook and confluence page with new validation rules and examples (owner: Identity eng).
2) Add unit + integration tests for aud/azp precedence in identity-service (owner: Identity eng).
3) Notify other private customers via security bulletin if their IdP configurations match the ambiguous pattern (owner: Customer Success).
4) Consider adding a preflight check in console that flags multi-aud assertions that map to multiple tenants (product/UX review).
payload.summary: IdP assertion with overlapping audience values leads to ambiguous tenant binding in private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden spike in HTTP 429 responses after switching to short-lived API keys (30m TTL) and enabling a parallel multipart uploader for large embedding jobs. This started approximately 2026-02-20 17:10 UTC immediately after the key rotation rollout.

Impact:
- CipherDocs ingestion jobs are failing at ~60% throughput due to intermittent 429s.
- Affects critical nightly syncs and causes downstream analytics delays.
- Errors are concentrated on the embedding endpoint and on a dedicated pool in us-east.

Timeline / Observed behavior:
- 2026-02-20 17:05 UTC: CipherDocs rotated to short-lived keys and launched a new uploader service configured for N=16 parallel upload streams per worker.
- 2026-02-20 17:10 UTC: Support alerted by customer about elevated 429 rates.
- Error patterns: bursts of 429s lasting 10–40s with recovery, correlated with large batches (300–1200 docs) and the uploader's reconnect/retry logic.

Environment:
- Customer: CipherDocs (dedicated pool)
- Region: prod us-east-1
- API: POST /v1/embeddings (batch)
- Client: in-house Go uploader (v1.4.2) using short-lived keys minted from customer SSO service

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Mint new short-lived key via their rotation service.
2) Start their uploader with 16 concurrent multipart streams, batch size 256.
3) Observe 10–40s bursts of 429s within the first 5–10 minutes of the run.

Logs / Evidence:
- Customer provided request_id samples: r_3f9a1c2e, r_3f9a1f4b, r_3f9b2d11 (attached).
- Platform metrics show token-bucket exhaust events on per-key buckets with sharp drops in allowed concurrency.
- Gateway logs show many short-lived connections from the same tenant but with different API key values within the same tenancy.

Initial hypothesis:
- Short TTL keys + parallel uploader cause effective burstiness at the tenant level: each rotated key gets its own per-key bucket, and the uploader cycles keys quickly, causing multiple buckets to be hit and the tenant-level aggregator to throttle more aggressively.
- Reconnect/retry timing creates synchronized spikes that exhaust the tenant concurrent-window.

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed that per-key buckets exist alongside a tenant-level concurrency window.
- Observed that key rotation rate was ~1 key per 2s per worker; with 10 workers and 16 streams the number of active keys increased rapidly during jobs.
- Reproduced locally by simulating rotation + 12 parallel clients; saw similar 429 burst pattern and token-bucket drain.
- Checked rate-limiter config on dedicated pool: tenant window = 200 concurrent tokens, per-key bucket = 20 tokens. With many keys active simultaneously the tenant window is consumed quickly.

Workarounds applied / Recommended immediate mitigations:
- Support recommended client-side smoothing: reduce parallel streams to 4 and increase batch size to 512 to amortize requests. Customer applied this and saw immediate drop in 429 rate.
- Temporarily increase per-tenant concurrency on the dedicated pool for CipherDocs by +30% while we tune rate-limiter behavior (SRE actioned a controlled increase).
- Ask client to align key rotation to non-overlapping windows (longer TTL or staggered rotations) as a short-term measure.

Root cause (interim):
- Interaction between short-lived key churn and per-key token buckets produced higher-than-expected aggregate concurrency consumption at the tenant level. The uploader's design (many parallel short connections) amplified this.

Next steps / long-term fixes:
1) Platform change: re-evaluate rate-limiter semantics for short-lived key churn. Possible approaches:
   - Make per-key buckets transient and have tenant-level smoothing that accounts for key churn.
   - Add short warm-up grace for newly minted keys to prevent immediate bucket exhaustion.
   - Implement a rolling aggregation that treats keys from the same tenant as a single logical bucket for a short interval.
2) Product guidance: publish a best-practices doc for key rotation + parallel upload patterns.
3) Client guidance: recommend exponential backoff with jitter plus reduced parallelism for uploaders that rotate keys frequently.
4) Follow-up: schedule a post-incident review with SRE, Platform, and the customer to finalize a config change.

Attachments: request_id logs, CPU/mem graphs, gateway traces (attached to ticket).

2026-02-20 18:02 UTC — Support (Priya): Logged initial report, requested request_id samples and uploader config. Assigned to SRE.
2026-02-20 18:35 UTC — CipherDocs (Customer): Provided request_ids r_3f9a1c2e,r_3f9a1f4b,r_3f9b2d11 and uploader config (parallel=16,batch=256,rotation=30m->30s for testing). Noted issue appears within first 2 minutes.
2026-02-20 19:10 UTC — SRE (Liam): Reproduced locally with a rotation simulator and parallel clients; saw tenant token window exhaustion. Proposed short-term tenant concurrency increase.
2026-02-21 02:15 UTC — Support (Priya): Applied client workaround recommendation (parallel->4,batch->512). Customer reports reduced 429s and resumed ingestion.
2026-02-21 09:00 UTC — SRE (Liam): Increased tenant concurrency by 30% for CipherDocs on dedicated pool as a controlled mitigation (will monitor).
2026-02-25 14:30 UTC — Product (Ava Chen): Drafting best-practices doc and guidance for short-lived keys + uploaders. Will include sample client backoff configs.
2026-03-02 11:20 UTC — SRE (Liam): Engineering action item created to evaluate rate-limiter change; tracking PR referenced in related_github_prs.
Mitigation in place: customer-side parallelism reduced and tenant concurrency increased temporarily. Engineering to implement rate-limiter change to better account for key churn. Pending follow-up postmortem and product guidance.
payload.summary: High 429 rates observed after migrating to short-lived API keys with parallel multipart uploader

Issue summary: After a planned cross-region failover exercise for the dedicated pool serving StorApp Inc., a subset of tenant sessions were routed to a degraded fallback variant even though the customer's tenant pin was expected to remain bound to the promoted model version. Impact: ~8% of production requests for StorApp (steady traffic) returned responses from the degraded variant (lower quality / quantized variant) for ~45 minutes; customers observed higher latency and quality regressions. Environment: Dedicated pool (prod us-west) performing cross-region failover to eu-west due to maintenance. Model: rwd-chat-7b-v2 pinned for tenant storapp-42. Observed behavior: control-plane signalled a successful promote to eu-west, orchestrator reported pin handoff completed, but edge-proxy continued to route a subset of requests to a fallback (quantized) variant. No explicit unpin event for the tenant was present in the control-plane audit log. The issue surfaced during a canary-weight adjustment window after the failover and persisted until manual remediation.
1) Configure tenant storapp-42 with model pin to rwd-chat-7b-v2 in us-west. 2) Initiate cross-region failover (simulate maintenance: drain us-west, promote eu-west). 3) Observe routing during canary weight shift (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and health probe smoothing. 4) Inspect edge-proxy routing logs and control-plane snapshot versions. 5) Note that a portion of sessions are served by the degraded variant despite pin remaining in control-plane state.
excerpt: [2026-03-12T08:21:02Z] orchestrator: pin_handshake tenant=storapp-42 seq=23134 status=COMMIT; [2026-03-12T08:21:04Z] control-plane: snapshot_publish id=23134 region=eu-west; [2026-03-12T08:21:10Z] edge-proxy[id=e-84]: route_eval tenant=storapp-42 pin_token=xxxxxx cookie_domain=redwood-internal trace=0x9f2 drop_to_variant=quantized-7b reason='route_cache_missing_snapshot' latency_ms=482; [2026-03-12T08:22:11Z] serving-runtime[node=sr-12]: variant_select tenant=storapp-42 selected=quantized-7b load=0.73
Initial hypothesis: edge-proxy cache TTL + cookie-domain rotation left some fronted proxies with stale snapshot index after orchestrator commit, causing route evaluation to fall back to a degraded variant when snapshot lookup failed. Key findings: - Control-plane audit shows commit sequence 23134 for tenant storapp-42 and no explicit unpin. - Orchestrator emitted pin_handshake COMMIT but the edge-proxy logs show 'route_cache_missing_snapshot' for the same tenant within the commit window. - There were concurrent health-probe smoothing events (canary weight adjust) that caused orchestrator to temporarily signal degraded-route eligibility. - Correlation with a small batch of edge-proxies that had not pulled snapshot 23134 due to a transient S3 read error caused route-cache misses. - Tokenization delta between rwd-chat-7b-v2 and quantized-7b exhibited increased latency for affected sessions. - No model-serving nodes reported errors; this is routing-level divergence. Open questions: whether edge-proxy should block-route until snapshot confirmation or enforce a stronger reconciliation on mismatch. Related historical tickets: links to pin-handshake races (SUP-314159) and route-cache issues (SUP-4721).
Workaround applied (2026-03-12 09:03 UTC): support executed control-plane forced-reconcile for tenant storapp-42 and restarted the 6 affected edge-proxy instances to flush stale cache. This returned routing to pinned model and reduced incidents. Root fix plan: 1) Deploy a reconciliation patch to control-plane/orchestrator that marks a pending commit as 'blocked' until a quorum of edge proxies confirm snapshot pull (implement optimistic commit backoff). 2) Add exponential backoff and retries for edge-proxy snapshot pulls and emit clearer metrics when pulling fails. 3) Extend canary handshake window by 30s during cross-region handoffs. 4) Add a short-term mitigation which will auto-reconcile pinned tenants if route_cache_missing_snapshot is observed more than N times. Rollout notes: patch targeted for canary on 2026-03-20 in control-plane; orchestration PR opened. Customer follow-up: StorApp notified and given post-incident summary. No billing adjustments required; CS offered credits as goodwill.
payload.summary: Stranded model pin after cross-region failover degrades routing to fallback variant

Issue summary:
BrightDocs reports elevated p95/p99 latency and intermittent 504 timeouts from their Dedicated reservation beginning 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. The impact aligns with our cluster nightly maintenance window (22:00-23:30 UTC).

Impact:
- Customer-visible: increased request latency (p95 up from ~120ms to 1.1s, p99 spikes to 3.4s) and 504s for synchronous streaming requests.
- Affects production traffic for BrightDocs' reserved capacity in us-west-2 (dedicated pool ID: dp-56f9).
- Business impact: degraded UX during evening peak for customer; BrightDocs billing tier and SLAs flagged this as P1.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-56f9 (3 reserved nodes, GPU: A10G equivalent), auto-scale policy: min=3 max=6 scale_cooldown=300s, preemptible=false.
- Node image: node-agent-v2.14.1 (includes nightly maintenance agent).
- Models in use when issue observed: redwood-2.7b (chat), mistral-7b (reranking).

Steps to reproduce / Observed pattern:
1) Customer runs bursty workloads starting ~2026-03-09 21:45 UTC.
2) At ~22:00 UTC nightly maintenance jobs begin (node-agent orchestrates OS package updates, kernel GC, background log rotation and node-level checkpoint consolidation).
3) Within ~5-12 minutes of maintenance start, telemetry shows increased scheduler queue length and longer wait times for GPU contexts.
4) Customers see streaming disconnects and 504s; requests are retried by client at higher rates which amplifies the queue.

Logs / Metrics (examples):
- grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serve/dedicated-pool-dp-56f9?orgId=1&from=2026-03-09T21:30:00Z&to=2026-03-09T23:30:00Z
- p95 latency (redwood-2.7b): baseline ~120ms -> spike to 1.1s at 22:07 UTC.
- p99 latency: baseline ~450ms -> spikes 3.4s, correlates with GPU context switch rate increase.
- node_exporter: write_iops spikes on /var/lib/checkpoints starting 22:02 UTC.
- nvidia_smi: transient GPU utilization drop and higher kernel launch latency reported on node-03 which is running the maintenance agent.

Expected behavior:
- Nightly maintenance should not interfere with serving-critical processes on reserved nodes; scheduling should prefer off-host maintenance or drain with graceful workload evacuation.

Additional notes:
- Customer has routing pinned to pool dp-56f9. Failover routing to other pools is possible but not enabled in their config.
- Similar timing pattern has been observed in other reserved pools in us-west during the same maintenance window (see linked issues).
2026-03-10 02:12 — Support (Aisha Patel): Opened ticket after BrightDocs support call at 23:00 UTC. Collected initial logs and confirmed correlation with nightly maintenance window.
2026-03-10 03:05 — SRE (Marco Li): Confirmed increased queue length and GPU context latency on node-03. Noted disk IO activity on /var/lib/checkpoints concurrent with spike. Hypothesis: maintenance agent performing checkpoint consolidation is contending for CPU/io and causing kernel/GPU latency.
2026-03-10 05:20 — Customer (BrightDocs - Emma Zhou): Provided request traces and mentioned they did not configure cross-pool fallback because they wanted data locality. Asking for mitigation options tonight.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 09:15 — SRE (Marco Li): Actioned temporary disable of maintenance on dp-56f9 (change-id CHG-7882), increased min nodes to 4. Monitoring for next maintenance window.
2026-03-12 11:02 — Support (Aisha Patel): Customer confirmed improved p95 and no 504s during subsequent maintenance window after mitigations. Follow-up engineering work assigned for root cause and permanent fix.
Telemetry aggregated from Grafana and node logs indicates the main contention vector is node-level IO and scheduler preemption during checkpoint consolidation; this increases kernel launch latency observable in CUDA profiler traces.
nvprof sample (node-03, 2026-03-09T22:05): average kernel launch latency increased 6x vs baseline; GPU occupancy transiently drops suggesting CPU-side stalls rather than GPU load saturation.
Autoscaler behavior: min=3, observed burst increased active pods but autoscaler cooldown prevented quick scale up while nodes were blocked by maintenance-related IO, causing queue to back up.
Hypothesis 1: maintenance agent not respecting cgroup/ionice limits, performing high-priority IO on shared checkpoint disk, causing host CPU and I/O contention and delaying serving threads.
Hypothesis 2: node-agent triggers lightweight local checkpoint compaction on same disk backing model cache; compaction uses synchronous fsyncs that block the serving process's pagefault handling, increasing kernel scheduling latency.
Reproducibility: reproduced in staging by enabling maintenance job on a 3-node reserved pool while running a synthetic bursty workload; observed same p95/p99 drift within 6-10 minutes.
Cross-reference: SUP-642113 observed similar p99 patterns but was attributed to vram paging; this ticket differs because we see host IO spikes rather than GPU OOM activity.
Action items taken so far: disabled maintenance on customer pool for 48h, bumped min nodes to 4, queued autoscaler config change (PR referenced) to allow faster scale up when queue depth exceeds threshold.
Next step: instrument node-agent to respect ionice and CPU shares and implement a 'maintenance-drain' mode that triggers graceful evac prior to IO-intensive work.
Workaround (applied 2026-03-10): Disabled nightly maintenance on dp-56f9 (CHG-7882), increased pool min nodes to 4 to provide immediate headroom, and offered enablement of routing fallback to BrightDocs. Customer accepted these temporary mitigations.
Permanent fix (planned): 1) Update node-agent to run background consolidation at low IO priority (ionice -c3) and within a cpuset/cgroup that avoids core serving processes. 2) Implement maintenance-drain mode that sets node to cordon and migrates active contexts before heavy IO. 3) Adjust autoscaler thresholds so scale-up can preempt maintenance windows if queue depth rises rapidly. 4) Add a monitoring alert for 'maintenance+queue correlation' to auto-trigger mitigations.
Deployment plan: node-agent change scheduled for canary on 2026-03-18, full rollout 2026-03-25 after performance validation. Autoscaler tuning PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/98 (in review).
Follow-up: Postmortem and runbook update to be published to Confluence (link to be added). Assign owners: Diego Morales (node-agent), Priya Raman (autoscaler).
payload.summary: Reserved pool latency drift and elevated timeouts correlated with nightly background maintenance jobs

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several customers (initially Finlyx Payments) reported SSE/WebSocket streaming sessions that stall mid-generation for long-form responses (~1k+ tokens). The stream remains open but no additional chunks are emitted for 10–90s before either resuming or the client timing out. Impact: Enterprise customer experienced degraded end-user experience during business hours, multiple sessions timed out and impacted SLAs. Environment: prod, eu-west; Hosted API behind our NLB + per-region nginx proxy layer; serving runtime on dedicated pools with mixed kernel versions. Observed: stalls correlate with spikes in kernel-swap events on serving-worker hosts and with sustained HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE backpressure on the edge proxy. Expected: continuous token stream with <200ms token inter-arrival for these responses.
Streams remain open but no tokens are emitted for extended periods. Some sessions resume after system recovers; others time out client-side. Stall probability increases under bursty concurrent streams and when serving-worker kernel preemption occurs.
Streaming responses should continue to emit tokens without multi-second gaps; short internal backpressure should not cause 10s+ silent stalls.
1) Use customer prompt that triggers long-form generation (approx 800-1200 tokens) against redwood/open-chat-medium-v1 in eu-west.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a staged canary rollout initiated by LinguaTech (dedicated pool), several requests observed unexpected fallbacks to the older pinned model after initial routing to the canary variant. Root cause appears correlated with duplicated outbound requests from the edge sidecar into the rollout coordinator queue leading to out-of-order processing of health and commit events.

Impact:
- Intermittent mixed-model responses for ~1-3% of requests from a set of tenant sessions during the rolling window.
- Affects inference determinism for LinguaTech production traffic (low-volume bursty traffic pattern).
- Customer reported content mismatch and regeneration loops in chat flows.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: pool-dedicated-us-east-3 (GPU: A100)
- Sidecar version: v1.8.2
- Canary coordinator: v2.3.0
- Serving runtime: rtm-4.7.1
- Observed between 2026-03-10T10:23:00Z and 2026-03-10T12:10:00Z

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Trigger a staged rollout: promote model redwood/opt-13b-quant (canary) at 10:05 UTC with 5% weight.
2) Send parallel tenant sessions that maintain long-lived session tokens and high inter-request concurrency.
3) Edge sidecar enqueues health/commit events to rollout-coordinator queue; under transient congestion the sidecar re-emits the same event (duplicate) due to a non-idempotent retry path.
4) Coordinator processes duplicates interleaved with later commit events, causing the commit to be applied then immediately shadowed by an earlier stale event that triggers fallback logic for the affected session cohort.

Observed behavior:
- Some sessions returned canary responses followed by older pinned-model responses within the same conversational session.
- Traces show duplicate enqueue timestamps from the sidecar and matching dequeue times separated by unrelated commits.
- Canary coordinator logs include repeated "apply_pin" and "revert_pin" for the same cohort-id within seconds.

Expected behavior:
- Sidecar emits each coordination event exactly once (or with idempotent dedupe in coordinator).
- Coordinator applies events in logical order and ignores stale duplicates, ensuring session-affinity/pin consistency during rollouts.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Pause the staged rollout for LinguaTech and promote via an atomic cutover in a maintenance window.
- Increase session affinity TTL to reduce susceptibility to transient rebinds.

Notes on reproducibility and severity:
- Repro is intermittent and workload dependent (high concurrency/long sessions increase probability).
- Classified as Sev1 due to customer production impact and correctness of responses.

Attachments/Artifacts:
- Traces: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/abcd-20260310
- Coordinator log excerpt: coordinator-logs-2026-03-10.txt (attached in ticket)
Initial hypothesis: duplicate message emission from sidecar retry path. Evidence: identical event IDs with multiple enqueue timestamps in the edge logs and coordinator receiving duplicate events without idempotency checks.

Findings so far:
- Sidecar v1.8.2 contains a change in the outbound queue client which switched from at-least-once to best-effort retry for performance (PR referenced below). Under transient queue pressure it will re-send events without attaching stable request-id.
- Coordinator has defensive logic for dedup by event-id but relies on client-supplied idempotency-token which was not present for these events.
- When duplicates interleave with commit ordering, fallback logic triggers because the coordinator treats the duplicate as an explicit revert by an older controller state.

Action items:
- Engineer to add server-side dedupe based on event fingerprint (cohort-id + event-type + sequence) within the coordinator (short-term patch).
- Backport sidecar change to include stable idempotency-token for all coordination events (long-term fix).
- Add e2e integration test that simulates duplicate-delivery interleaving.
- Notify customer of deployment schedule and confirm rollback mitigation is acceptable.

Additional notes:
Workaround applied and coordinator dedupe patch deployed to staging. Sidecar PR opened to restore stable idempotency tokens. Planned production rollout for coordinator patch on 2026-03-13 with monitoring; follow-up ticket will track sidecar backport and full regression test coverage.
Merge sidecar PR to re-add idempotency tokens and backport to v1.8.x branch
Promote coordinator dedupe patch to production during low-traffic window
Add integration test covering duplicate-event interleaving and session-affinity preservation
Coordinate with CS to validate customer after production rollout and close ticket

payload.description:
Issue summary: After NovaHealth promoted open-qa-3b-v2 to 100% for their tenant, a subset (~1.8% of sessions) continued to be routed to the legacy variant for up to 45 minutes. Impact: Customer reports mixed outputs in production (safety filter differences and tokenization mismatch) causing a spike in quality complaints and elevated error reports to their internal QA. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-nyk-3), customer tenant: novahealth-prod, region: us-east, workload: chat completions with streaming enabled. Observed behavior: During the canary -> promote transition the cohort-affinity cache on several edge nodes held a stale affinity snapshot and served requests to the old variant despite the control plane showing the new variant as active for the tenant. Expected behavior: Once promote commit completes and the control plane publishes the new routing snapshot, cohort-affinity should invalidate and all new requests for the tenant should target the promoted model within the promote_grace_window (default 30s). Steps to reproduce (internal): 1) Create a canary for a tenant with streaming sessions and a long-lived keepalive (60s) 2) Promote to 100% using the standard rollout path 3) Observe traffic on edge nodes with prewarm enabled and a traffic-mirroring sidecar 4) Reconnect keepalive streams and monitor cohort-affinity cache hit rates Observed logs/telemetry: - Edge node e-nyk-12 shows affinity_snapshot:v3 TTL=180s, last-refresh=2026-03-10T02:11:04Z - Control plane commit for tenant novahealth-prod at 2026-03-10T02:12:10Z - Serving logs show routing decision: variant=legacy_openqa for request ids: req-8f3a, req-8f48, req-8fb9 - Stream disconnects coincident with prewarm probe at 02:13:05Z Investigation notes: - Hypothesis A: Affinity snapshot persisted because prewarm-sidecar merged mirrored session metadata and prevented TTL eviction. - Hypothesis B: Edge replay latch delayed application of control-plane snapshot due to in-flight prefix cache warmups on a handful of nodes. - We reproduced locally by artificially extending snapshot TTL and saw routing continue to legacy until manual cache purge. Workaround implemented: Instructed customer to force a tenant affinity flush via support action (edge-affinity-flush tenant=novahealth-prod) which immediately switched routing back to the promoted variant. Customer confirmed degraded outputs stopped after flush. Temporary mitigation: We pushed an automated job to sweep edge nodes for stale affinity snapshots older than control-plane commit_time + 30s while a fix is prioritized. Proposed fix: 1) Ensure control-plane commit increments snapshot_version and edge-initiated prewarm merges do not block snapshot activation. 2) Add an edge-side quick-check that compares snapshot_version against control-plane leader and triggers soft-invalidations for out-of-date snapshots when promote events are received. 3) Short-term: reduce default affinity snapshot TTL during canary windows for dedicated tier customers with streaming. Next steps / owner: - Engineering (Liam Chen) to triage kernel in runtime that merges mirrored session metadata — ETA patch: 2026-03-16. - SRE (internal) to monitor sweep job effectiveness and escalate if residuals > 0.1% of tenant traffic. - Product to review rollout prewarm merging docs and surface guidance for dedicated customers. Customer communication: apologetic note sent and mitigation instructions delivered; customer requested postmortem and a timeline for a permanent fix. Attachments / references: links to edge logs and commit: https://logs.redwood.corp/edge/e-nyk-12/2026-03-10-02 and PR above.

2026-03-10 09:05 NovaHealth Ops (Customer): Confirmed that ~1.8% of sessions returned legacy outputs; provided example request IDs and timestamps. Asked if there was an immediate rollback option.
2026-03-10 14:40 Engineering (runtime team): Reproduced locally with long TTL and prewarm mirror enabled. Cause appears to be merge path in sidecar that accepts stale snapshot if mirrored session metadata presents conflicting version info.
2026-03-13 11:22 Product (Marisol Gomez): Requested that rollout docs include explicit guidance on streaming sessions and affinity TTL during canary for dedicated customers. Added to roadmap for docs update.
Temporary mitigation: edge sweep job reduced incidents to near zero. Permanent fix in progress: change to edge quick-check and safe-invalidation logic; patch targeted 2026-03-16 with controlled rollout. Postmortem scheduled after patch verification. SLA credit request filed with finance if recurrence within 30 days.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported large number of 429 responses for in-flight streaming websocket sessions following an organization-level quota bump (quota increase applied via admin console at ~2026-03-09T22:15Z). The increase shows in the console and new API keys/sessions are able to consume higher throughput, but long-lived connections that were open prior to the change continued to receive 429s until they disconnected and reconnected.

Impact:
- HorizonMaps (dedicated) experienced elevated 429 rates on streaming endpoints for ~2 hours during a heavy mapping tile backfill.
- Multiple long-lived sessions for their ingestion workers received repeated 429s and stalled, causing a backlog and delayed processing of ~80k events.
- Customer reports this caused missed SLAs for downstream pipelines.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-west-2 (cluster id: dp-32a1).
- Token bucket based rate limiter with per-tenant windowing (default window 60s) and session-affinity for established websocket sessions.
- Customer was using multiplexed websocket connections (4 workers per host) and persistent session tokens renewed every 12h.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long-lived streaming session connected before quota change.
2) Trigger org-level quota adjustment in Console (increase throughput).
3) Keep existing session open and observe 429s returned on subsequent requests for ~1-2 hours until session reconnect.

Observed behavior:
- New sessions established after quota change consume tokens at the new higher rate without 429s.
- Existing sessions appear to be limited by a stale snapshot of the token-bucket allocation taken at session start.
- Rate-limiter metrics show the tenant allowance increased, but per-session counters remained at pre-change levels.

Expected behavior:
- Quota increases applied in Console should be reflected immediately for all active sessions (or there should be clear documentation stating reconnect is required).

Immediate workaround provided to customer:
- Recommend reconnecting long-lived streams to pick up the new quota allocation (customer did and throughput resumed).
- As interim mitigation, we suggested horizontal scaling of worker hosts to spread per-connection quotas.

Investigation notes (support/SRE):
- Reproduced in staging with dedicated-tenant test harness. Observed token-bucket state stored in a session-scoped in-memory cache which is only refreshed on session handshake.
- Admin quota changes update the tenant-level bucket in Redis, but we do not push updates to active session caches. Long-lived sessions therefore continued to consult stale in-memory values until reconnect.
- Rate limiter implementation contains optimization to avoid frequent cross-node reads for performance; this optimization introduced the reconciliation lag on quota mutation.
- Relevant logs: rate-limiter debug shows "session_bucket_snapshot" timestamps matching session start time, and "tenant_quota_update" entries after the snapshot time.
- Dashboard links: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/rls/rate-limiter?org=dp-32a1 (customer-visible metrics sanitized).

Root cause hypothesis:
- Session-scoped bucket snapshots are not invalidated when tenant-level quotas change. The design assumed quotas are stable or that sessions are short-lived; it did not account for admin-driven quota mutations during heavy long-lived streaming workloads.

Short-term remediation plan:
- Add a reconciliation path: when tenant-level quota changes are detected, publish an invalidation event on the quota-change channel so session nodes refresh snapshot for affected tenant IDs.
- Deploy a hotfix to staging that subscribes to quota-change channel and forces snapshot refresh for active sessions (PR reference provided).

Long-term fix considerations:
- Evaluate cost/perf trade-off of always consulting tenant-level bucket in Redis for every packet vs. periodic background refresh vs. event-driven invalidation.
- Update docs/console to indicate that quota changes may require reconnect for streaming clients until reconciliation is implemented.

Customer communication notes:
- Notified HorizonMaps via email (marcus@horizonmaps.com) of the workaround and that we are prioritizing a fix.
- Offered credits for the processing delay while fix is rolled out.

Next steps / owner action items:
- (Liam) Validate hotfix in staging and run the customer reproducer (due 2026-03-12).
- (SRE) Roll out event-driven invalidation to canary nodes and monitor 429 rate.
- (Docs) Add Console note about reconnect behavior for streaming sessions after quota modifications.

Resolution notes (so far):
- Hotfix deployed to staging 2026-03-12. Reproducer showed immediate refresh of session snapshots on quota change.
- Canary rollout started 2026-03-13 to 10% of dedicated pool nodes; initial telemetry shows ~90% reduction in sustained 429s for pre-existing sessions after quota change.

Follow-up references:
- Slack thread: #support-horizonmaps (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05ABC9)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rls/pull/412
- Confluence runbook: Rate Limiter Reconciliation (link above)

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 17:38 UTC - SRE (Marta Chen): Confirmed snapshot behavior. Tenant-level Redis shows updated tokens but per-session memory still reads old allowances. Adding instrumentation to identify affected node ids.
2026-03-13 07:22 UTC - SRE (Marta Chen): Canary rollout to 10% started. Monitoring dashboards show 87% drop in 429s for pre-existing connections post-change. Moving to 50% if stable.
2026-03-13 12:05 UTC - Customer (Marcus - HorizonMaps): Appreciative of quick mitigation; asked if there will be a change to client SDKs to handle this without reconnects. Forwarded to Product for consideration.

Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports a sudden increase in 429 responses during normal traffic after enabling a short smoothing window on the dedicated pool rate limiter. They observe tenant token depletion spikes that align with healthcheck probes from their internal orchestrator.

Impact:
- Multiple realtime endpoints returning 429s for ~2–3 minute bursts every 15 minutes, affecting checkout personalization and search ranking features.
- Customer reports ~8% error rate for low-latency routes during bursts, increasing e2e latency and causing retries in their service.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (BrightCart lease id: lease-91b7) in prod/us-east.
- Rate limiter config rolled out yesterday: smoothing_window=10s (reduced from 60s), healthcheck sampling enabled on route /_hc, priority routing enabled for low-latency lane.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Use a small fleet of workers (16) to send steady interactive traffic (~12 rps) to /v1/chat with pinned model redwood-open-7b.
2) Run a healthcheck loop that pings /_hc every 30s from a separate monitoring agent (3 probes concurrently).
3) Observe 429 spikes on interactive endpoints when the healthcheck cluster performs concurrent probes and when smoothing window is short.

Observed behavior:
- Healthcheck requests appear to be counted toward tenant token bucket immediately and trigger short, intense token consumption peaks.
- Smoothing window reduction causes refill accounting to be more granular, exposing short bursts rather than smoothing them out.

Expected behavior:
- Healthcheck traffic should be accounted in a way that does not amplify microbursts for interactive lanes (either sub-sampled or mapped to a separate background pool).
- Short smoothing windows should not cause periodic ~2–3 minute tenant-wide 429 waves for typical monitoring patterns.

Workaround so far:
- Customer temporarily disabled healthcheck sampling and reverted smoothing_window to 60s which reduced 429 frequency.

Additional context:
- Customer provided request IDs and timestamps (attached). They noted the bursts always correlate with their monitoring agent schedule.
- BrightCart is on a dedicated contract and requests guidance for a conservative default and an explicit option to exclude internal health probes from the interactive quota.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 02:12 UTC - BrightCart Support (Elena Rojas): Provided additional logs and confirmed reverting smoothing window reduced errors. Requests option to have healthcheck path mapped to background pool or be exempt in dedicated pools.
Hypothesis 1: Short smoothing window reduces the effective refill blur so small periodic probes appear as sharp token drains at refill boundaries.
Hypothesis 2: Healthcheck requests are treated as interactive by default and counted against the same token bucket as user requests; concurrent probes multiply apparent concurrency.
Data: Token refill logs (token-service) show refill intervals at 10s after config change; token consumption graph attached in PR #214 shows spike alignment with probe timestamps.
Staging tests: Sub-sampling healthcheck requests (1 in 3 accepted) in staging reduced peak token draw by ~68% and eliminated the tenant-wide 429 wave in our 4-hour run.
Edge case: If customer uses many monitoring agents across multiple IP pools, sub-sampling alone may not be enough; recommend mapping healthchecks to a background/burst pool.
Related runbooks: See Rate Limiter Design and Priority Pools (confluence link) for background-pool mapping and dedicated-pool config knobs.
Implemented route-level pool mapping toggle and healthcheck sub-sampling option for dedicated pools. Ran canary on BrightCart lease-91b7; reverted smoothing_window back to 10s without reintroducing 429 spikes when healthcheck mapping is enabled.

Canary window: 2026-03-12 02:00–04:00 UTC on lease-91b7. Metrics: 429 rate dropped from 8% bursts to <0.2% and average latency stable.
Workaround documented: Console toggle for dedicated customers to map /_hc to background pool and set healthcheck.subsample_rate default to 0.33.

2026-03-14 - Customer (Priya Rao): Confirmed tests — pinning to corporate egress IPs makes exchanges succeed consistently. Dynamic runners show intermittent failures.
Mapped failure timestamps to Azure sign-in audit logs; Azure shows 'Conditional Access' denial entries that match failing exchange attempts.
Redwood token introspection returns 403 only after Azure indicates policy blocked issuance — Redwood is not inventing denial.
Customer's Conditional Access policies restrict token issuance to 'Named locations' (corporate office IPs). Their app registration for Redwood was not listed in the 'trusted apps' exclusion list, so tokens issued to the app are subject to the policy.
Ephemeral CI runners egress from variable IP pools; sometimes those IPs fall outside Customer's Named locations causing Azure to refuse to issue tokens for OIDC flow.
We verified that interactive web login succeeds because interactive flows use different Conditional Access rules (e.g., MFA+Allow for browser sessions) and often come from whitelisted locations.
Auth-proxy changes: none identified. No evidence of bug in Redwood Private token handling.
Azure AD Conditional Access policy prevented token issuance for OIDC requests originating from dynamic CI egress IPs. Redwood Private correctly rejected the token exchange after Azure returned a denial. The customer app registration was not excluded from the Conditional Access policy and their Named locations did not include CI egress ranges.
Workaround (customer): Configure CI runners to originate from a stable, whitelisted egress IP range or route token requests through a corporate NAT/VPN so Azure Conditional Access sees a trusted IP.
Workaround (quick): Add the Redwood OIDC application or the specific client ID to the Conditional Access policy 'Exclude' list for the token issuance policy if acceptable to customer security policy.
Permanent guidance: Customer to review Conditional Access Named locations and app exclusions. Documented recommended patterns in Confluence: using service principals with 'trusted app' exclusions for machine-to-machine OIDC exchanges, or using static egress IPs for CI workloads.
Redwood action items: Add a KB article in Support portal that describes this failure mode and Azure Conditional Access interaction with OIDC token exchanges for private deployments. Link from private SSO runbook.
Follow-up: Support scheduled a 1:1 runbook review with NexusHealth SRE on 2026-03-17 to help apply recommended configuration changes and validate fixes.

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC, ClipStream observed a large increase in tail latency (p95/p99) and recurring client timeouts (504/524) for text generation requests. Impact: Production traffic for their dedicated deployment experienced spikes in per-request latency and occasional 5xx responses, degrading user-facing ingestion pipelines. Environment: prod, us-east. Initial triage indicated the platform routed a subset of requests to a canary variant that was still initializing, producing cold-start delays and failed requests. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and follow-up actions.
1) Send steady client traffic to ClipStream production route (tokenized chat completion workload, ~15 req/s per client).
2) Trigger platform canary rollout for model variant redwood/fp16-compat-7b-canary-2026-03 with default fallback policy (weight-based, allow-initializing).
3) Observe backend routing decisions and per-request latency for requests redirected to the canary variant.
4) Note intermittent 504/524 from gateway and increased p95/p99 on request traces that hit initializing replicas.
- Around 09:10 UTC, p95 increased from ~120ms to ~1.8s and p99 hit 6-8s for the customer route.
- 1.2% of requests returned 5xx (mix of 504 and 524) during the peak period.
- Traces show requests routed to a variant with logs indicating 'variant_state=initializing' and long kernel load times (cold-start).
- Autoscaler attempted to spin up replicas but new pods remained 'initializing' for ~45-90s due to model quantization hotload.
Customer route: total_rps: 220 -> 210 (steady), error_rate: 0.2% -> 1.2% during incident
Platform: route_fallbacks: 18 per minute to canary variant during 09:10-09:40 UTC
Latency: p50 95ms -> 110ms, p95 120ms -> 1800ms, p99 350ms -> 7600ms
2026-03-12T09:12:03Z serving-runtime[replica-7b-canary-02]: INFO variant_state=initializing kernel_load=12400ms kv_cache_rehydrate=300ms
2026-03-12T09:12:04Z router[smart-routing]: WARN routing-to-variant variant_id=fp16-canary-2026-03 reason=fallback_policy evaluated_weight=0.12 allow_initializing=true
2026-03-12T09:12:04Z api-gateway: ERROR upstream_response=504 upstream_host=10.2.4.19:8080 path=/v1/generate customer=ClipStream
2026-03-12T09:17:22Z autoscaler: INFO requested_replicas=2 pending_provision=2 provider=dedicated-gpu wait_time=65s
Initial hypothesis: increased latency due to model runtime change in canary causing cold starts. Confirmed: canary image introduced a lazy-quantization step that extends first load time by ~12s per replica.
Routing policy review: smart-routing evaluation allowed 'initializing' variants to receive fallback traffic when stable variants breached latency budget. This behavior is intentional in policy but unsafe for large dedicated customers.
Autoscaler logs show capacity requested but provider API returned delayed GPU provisioning (provider-side laged by ~40s), compounding cold-start impact.
Health checks: readiness probe for canary variant only passes after model weights are fully loaded; during that window some replicas still accepted TCP connections from router because of race in readiness registration.
Maya Patel - 2026-03-12: Customer reported spikes and timeouts, attached trace IDs and replay bundle. Asked for immediate mitigation.
Diego Martinez - 2026-03-12: Scoped to routing + runtime. Reproduced in staging by enabling canary with lazy-quantization. Opening temp rollback for customer pin.
SRE (Evan Li) - 2026-03-12: Provider reported delayed provisioning for GPUs in us-east; working with infra partner to surface capacity metrics. Recommended pinning to stable variant and disabling canary for the route.
Support (Aisha Kumar) - 2026-03-12: Applied customer-side mitigation: pinned ClipStream to redwood/open-llama-7b-v2 and set fallback policy to 'avoid-initializing'. Observed p95 returned to baseline within 6 minutes.
Diego Martinez - 2026-03-13: Confirmed root cause and deployed temporary guard in router to exclude variants with state 'initializing' from fallback selection for high-tier customers. Follow-up ticket created for permanent fix.
Workaround applied: Pinned ClipStream to stable variant redwood/open-llama-7b-v2 and disabled automatic canary traffic for their route (09:25 UTC).
Temporary platform mitigation: Router guard added to treat 'initializing' variants as ineligible for fallback selection for customers with dedicated/reserved capacity (rolled 09:40 UTC).
Customer impact resolved: p95/p99 returned to normal by ~09:31 UTC after pin + routing guard; no data loss reported.
Permanent follow-ups: INT-4399 created to change fallback policy evaluation to de-prioritize initializing variants globally; INT-4402 created for runtime change to pre-warm quantization layer during rollout; update rollout docs and canary config defaults.
Communication: Sent incident summary and mitigations to customer (ClipStream CS contact) and to #support and #incidents Slack channels with postmortem draft.
