Issue summary: During a scheduled model minor-version upgrade in the customer's Dedicated pool, a narrow race in the rollout commit window caused the tenant's session tokens to be routed to a fallback (smaller-quant) variant rather than the pinned primary model. Impact: Intermittent mixed-model responses (some requests returned quantized outputs with subtle tokenization differences) for a subset of BrightForms tenant traffic for ~8 minutes. No data leak; correctness impact limited to degraded generation quality and increased tokenization mismatches.

Background: BrightForms has a pinned model version for their route. We initiated a scheduled minor upgrade on 2026-03-10 02:05 UTC that touched the rollout-manager commit path and the router's pin cache TTL. During commit, some session leases were truncated by a retry path which cleared pin metadata before the router could persist the new pin. The router then fell back to its fallback mapping (quantized variant) for those sessions until the pin reconciler repaired state.
Provision a dedicated pool with a pinned model version and a fallback quantized variant
Start sustained session traffic with session-lease extension enabled and a median latency of 70ms
Trigger a scheduled minor upgrade which performs a commit across rollout-manager and router within the same 30s window
Introduce an artificial retry on the rollout commit (simulate transient DB timeout) that runs commit twice with truncated lease metadata
Observe that some sessions lose their pin and are routed to the fallback variant until the reconciler runs
2026-03-10T02:05:11Z rollout-manager INFO commit start rollout_id=rl-7784 tenant=brightforms
2026-03-10T02:05:11Z router WARN session-lease truncate session=tok_3h2a flags=retry-path
2026-03-10T02:05:12Z rollout-manager ERROR commit retry due to transient-db-timeout: write failed (code=504)
2026-03-10T02:05:14Z router INFO route-evaluate tenant=brightforms resolved_variants=[quantized:0.0, primary:0.0] (fallback applied)
2026-03-10T02:13:21Z pin-reconciler INFO repaired 142 sessions for tenant=brightforms duration=00:08:07
Hypothesis 1: Commit retried while router persisted a partial state resulting in pin key being cleared on edge caches
Hypothesis 2: Session-lease truncation on retry path emitted an empty affinity token which bypassed pin-resolution heuristics
Finding: Correlated errors in rollout-manager (transient DB 504) with router session-truncate events. Reconciler timestamps align with the time window where mixed responses were observed.
Edge-proxy TTL configuration allowed stale negative cache entries for up to 45s which extended the window where fallback mapping was used after the transient error
Customer traffic pattern (highly-sustained with long sessions and lease extensions) increased probability of hitting the retry path during the commit window
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Initial report from BrightForms: 'We saw weird shorter outputs and tokenization edge cases starting at 02:05 UTC for about 8 minutes. Many requests appeared to come from the same session ids.'
SRE (Diego Ramirez) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged and started trace collection. Observed rollout-manager commit retries and router session-lease truncates. Marked as P1 given tenant production impact.
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Notified customer of investigation and provided temporary mitigation: avoid scheduling upgrades during BrightForms heavy usage windows and to use shorter lease-extension TTLs as a stop-gap.
SRE (Diego Ramirez) 2026-03-11: Reproducer run in staging with injected retry confirmed race. Created PR to add idempotent commit semantics to prevent lease truncation on commit retry. See PR #4212.
Product (Ava Chen) 2026-03-12: Requesting a follow-up to add an observability alert for 'pin-loss-rate' during rollouts and to reduce edge negative-cache TTL to 10s for dedicated pools as a protective default.
Short-term: Disable long session-lease auto-extension for the affected tenant and schedule upgrades during low-traffic windows. Operational: manual reconcilation (pin-reconciler) run completed which repaired sessions. Applied edge negative-cache TTL patch at the edge-proxy config level for the dedicated pool to 10s.
In progress: hotfix merged to rollout-manager to make commit idempotent and preserve lease metadata on retry (PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-manager/pull/4212). Edge negative-cache TTL lowered for dedicated pools (router PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/3051). Pin-reconciler run repaired affected sessions; monitoring added to alert on 'session-pin-loss-rate'>0.5% during rollouts. Scheduled follow-up: make reconciler aggressive for first 5 minutes post-commit and add a canary-runner test that injects commit failures during staged upgrades.
Ship rollout-manager idempotent-commit to production (canary scope: 5% of dedicated upgrades) - responsible: Diego Ramirez - target: 2026-03-16
Add alert for session-pin-loss-rate and a dashboard panel - responsible: Observability team - target: 2026-03-15
Update runbook to recommend edge negative-cache TTL <=10s for dedicated customers with long session leases - responsible: Product Ops - target: 2026-03-18

Issue summary: After a partial canary rollback initiated for redwood-7b-v1.2, a subset of tenant sessions that had pinned model versions experienced route reversion to a legacy variant and intermittent mixed responses. Impact: customer saw mixed model outputs for live sessions, some requests routed to an older variant without pin being explicitly changed. Environment: production (dedicated) in us-east-1 for NimbleScribe. Observed starting 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC during canary rollback window.

Expected behavior: pinned sessions should retain their pinned variant during rollbacks, or fall back deterministically to configured fallback policy. Actual behavior: a cohort (~0.8% of active sessions for the tenant) lost pin affinity and were routed to legacy variant (llama2-13b-quant), producing inconsistent outputs and causing a short-term quality regression for customer traffic.
1) Start with tenant using pinned model redwood-7b-v1.2.
2) Initiate canary promote to redwood-7b-v1.3 for 10% traffic, wait for health probes.
3) Run partial rollback to revert canary at 09:58 UTC (abort promote, commit rollback).
4) Observe session affinity map and edge headers for affected tenant cohort.
5) Reproduce by replaying traffic from recorded session IDs through edge (see attached session list).
Timeline reconstruction shows a narrow window where three events coincided: (1) operator-initiated partial rollback commit on control-plane, (2) a burst of health-checks hitting edge sidecars which triggered header sanitizer rule, and (3) control-plane snapshot merge code applied snapshots out-of-order for ephemeral commit IDs. Logs show 'commit-order-mismatch' warning immediately before edge removed X-Redwood-Pin for a subset of sessions. Session lease renewal traces indicated delayed lease refresh due to reconciler holding a lock while merging snapshots. The combination produced transient entropy in the routing decision: sessions without X-Redwood-Pin were evaluated by route-engine and matched fallback variant ruleset that selected a legacy model.

Hypotheses tested: header-stripping during health probes (confirmed), reconciler commit-ordering race (reproducible in staging with canary scripts), session lease TTL renewal delay under lock (observed in traces).
A race during partial canary rollback where control-plane snapshot merge applied snapshots with commit-order mismatch while edge-sidecar health-probe sanitization removed pin headers for requests. The reconciler's commit application path temporarily blocked lease renewals, leading to pin eviction for a small session cohort. Combined, this produced non-deterministic routing and fallback to legacy variants.
Immediate: re-applied pin metadata for affected tenant sessions from control-plane snapshot backups and forced lease renewal. Added a temporary rule to disable header sanitizer for X-Redwood-Pin during rollback windows.
Medium-term: deployed reconciler patch to enforce strict commit-serial application and prevent snapshot reorders. Deployed edge-sidecar patch to treat X-Redwood-Pin as protected header (not removed by health-probe sanitizer). Added metrics/alert to detect header removals and commit-order warnings.
2026-03-10 11:20 UTC: Reapplied pins for 142 affected session IDs (script: tools/reapply_pins.sh --tenant nimble-123 --file sessions.csv).
2026-03-10 13:45 UTC: Disabled legacy header sanitizer rule in prod for edge cluster us-east-1.
2026-03-11 22:30 UTC: Reconciler patch merged and rolled to canary (PR #4203).
2026-03-12 02:10 UTC: Edge-sidecar patch rolled (PR #3891) and protected header behavior enabled.
Patch to control-plane reconciler and edge-sidecar released. Backfill script reapplied pins and forced lease renewals. Customer confirmed that mixed outputs stopped within one hour of mitigation. Monitoring dashboards show no recurrence for 48 hours post-deploy. Ticket marked Resolved pending postmortem follow-ups.
2026-03-10 09:20 Support (Maya): Customer reported mixed model outputs after canary rollback; attached sample request/response pairs.
2026-03-10 09:40 Eng (Liam): Initial hypothesis: edge health-probe or sidecar header sanitizer stripped X-Redwood-Pin during in-flight rollback commit, causing routing to recompute and select fallback variant.
2026-03-10 10:05 Customer (NimbleScribe): Confirmed roughly 0.6-1.0% of requests returned legacy outputs; business impact limited but visible in QA channel.
2026-03-10 14:02 Eng (SRE - Priya): Found control-plane snapshot merge ordering warnings around rollback commit. Prepared quick mitigation to reapply pin on active sessions.
2026-03-12 02:14 Eng (Liam): Patch deployed to reconciler and edge-sidecar to preserve pin headers during health-probes and enforce commit serial ordering. Backfilled pins for affected sessions. Monitoring shows no further regressions.
Add an automated integration test that simulates canary rollback + health-probe storms to catch header-preservation regressions.
Instrument 'X-Redwood-Pin' header removal with a dedicated metric and alert threshold (SLO: zero removals during rollouts).
Revise runbook: during rollback operations, disable aggressive header sanitization rules or run sanitizer after pin re-assertion step.
Consider reducing lock duration in reconciler snapshot merge path and introduce async lease refresh where safe.
We re-applied pinned-model state for affected sessions and deployed fixes to prevent header stripping and commit reordering. We will run a post-change verification on next scheduled canary and share the test run results. If you see any further anomalies, please open a new ticket and include sample request_ids.
payload.summary: Pinned-session entropy and route reversion after partial canary rollback

Issue summary:
- Customer on Dedicated reports that users with their “Dedicated Admin” role can no longer edit routing policies in Console after RBAC v2 was enabled.
- Save action fails with a 403 Permission Denied.

Impact:
- Customer cannot update routing rules (fallback/model pinning behavior) for production traffic.
- Blocks planned rollout of routing changes tied to a model update.

Customer context:
- Company: Aegis Insurance Group
- Deployment: Dedicated
- Auth: SSO group mapping -> built-in role template “Dedicated Admin”

Environment:
- prod / us-east
- Console + Control Plane API

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Console -> Routing -> Policies
2) Open existing policy
3) Change target model or traffic split
4) Click Save
5) Error banner: “Permission denied”

Observed behavior:
- Console request returns 403
- Customer reports this workflow worked prior to RBAC v2 migration/enablement.

Expected behavior:
- Dedicated Admin should be able to edit routing policies (within the org/project scope they administer).

Artifacts provided by customer:
- Timestamp: 2025-03-11 16:22–16:30 UTC
- Request ID (from Console network panel): rwreq_9f3c0b1a1b2a
- User: (redacted) in IdP group mapped to Dedicated Admin

Support notes:
- Likely RBAC v2 deny-by-default enforcement + role template missing required permission for routing policy update endpoint.
- Please confirm permission string required by the endpoint annotation and whether “Dedicated Admin” template includes it in the policy bundle version currently deployed to this customer.
2025-03-11 16:41 UTC — Colin O'Donnell (Reporter)
Customer (Aegis) escalated during Dedicated pilot: admin cannot edit routing policy. They are blocked from changing fallback behavior ahead of a model version pin change. They confirmed they’re in the “Dedicated Admin” group in their IdP. Attaching request id: rwreq_9f3c0b1a1b2a.
2025-03-11 17:05 UTC — Benji Okafor (Assignee)
Pulled logs for rwreq_9f3c0b1a1b2a from Control Plane. Response 403 with structured denial. Denial reason code: RBAC_DENY_MISSING_PERMISSION. Required permission (from endpoint annotation): controlplane.routing_policies.update. Subject had roles: [template/dedicated_admin] scoped to org: aegis-prod. No matching permission found in evaluated policy bundle.
2025-03-11 17:22 UTC — Marcus Lin
This looks like a template gap, not a runtime bug: endpoint was recently annotated and now enforced deny-by-default. Action item should be to add controlplane.routing_policies.update to the dedicated_admin role template (and any operator template that previously had access). Also confirm read vs write split (list/get vs create/update/delete).
2025-03-11 17:40 UTC — Naomi Feldman
+1 template gap. For least-privilege, Dedicated Admin should include routing policy write. We should not broaden other roles by default. Please also add an integration test that validates dedicated_admin can update routing policies (to avoid regressions when we add new sensitive permissions).
2025-03-11 18:10 UTC — Benji Okafor
Workaround for customer: created a temporary custom role “RoutingPolicyEditor” with permission controlplane.routing_policies.update and bound it to their admin group at org scope. Customer confirmed they can now save policy edits in Console. Next: patch built-in template and roll out updated policy bundle.

Notes:
- This is consistent with deny-by-default behavior working as intended.
- The permission exists in the registry; it’s missing from the role template YAML used to generate built-ins.
2025-03-12 10:15 UTC — Connor O'Brien
Release coordination: once policy bundle is updated, we can roll out to Dedicated tenants via standard policy bundle sync. Please confirm expected bundle version and whether any cache invalidation is needed (role template changes should take effect after policy bundle refresh; no code deploy required).
2025-03-12 14:05 UTC — Benji Okafor
Template patch prepared and merged in policy bundle repo (internal). Deployed policy bundle refresh to Aegis Dedicated org at 2025-03-12 13:52 UTC. Removed temporary custom role binding after verifying built-in role now includes permission. Customer retested successfully.
2025-03-14 09:30 UTC — Colin O'Donnell
Customer confirmation: routing policy edits are working again; no additional 403s observed. They proceeded with planned routing change. Closing ticket.
Root cause:
- RBAC v2 endpoint annotation for routing policy update introduced a new required permission (controlplane.routing_policies.update).
- Built-in role template “Dedicated Admin” did not include this permission in the deployed policy bundle for the customer.
- With deny-by-default enforcement, requests to update routing policies correctly returned 403 with RBAC_DENY_MISSING_PERMISSION.

Fix:
- Added controlplane.routing_policies.update to the “Dedicated Admin” role template in the policy bundle.
- Refreshed policy bundle for the customer’s Dedicated tenant.

Workaround used during mitigation:
- Temporary custom role granting controlplane.routing_policies.update bound to the customer’s admin group; removed after bundle refresh.

Follow-ups:
- Add/extend integration coverage to assert built-in dedicated_admin can edit routing policies.
- Audit other routing-policy-related endpoints (create/delete) to ensure templates match intended access.

Customer-facing outcome:
- Customer can edit routing policies in Console and via API again; no change required to their IdP group mapping.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent WebSocket streaming sessions that appear to resume after a short gap but the conversation misses the final token(s) and client-side shows last chunk unacknowledged. Behavior started after they enabled multiplexed connections and moved workload onto a dedicated pool.

Impact:
- Several end-user chat sessions lose the final portion of generated messages (often the last sentence) after a 5–30s silent period.
- Client sees socket resume (code 1000) or a short reconnect, but server-side logs show last chunk delivered and not marked acknowledged by the multiplex layer.
- Customer reports impact on UX for long-turn responses and higher risk for partial instructions being delivered.

Environment:
- Customer: ParcelScale (dedicated)
- Region: prod us-east-1 (dedicated pool id dp-87)
- API mode: WebSocket multiplexing enabled, single socket transporting multiple chat sessions
- Model: redwood-7b-v2 pinned at v2026-02-28

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1. Open a multiplexed WebSocket connection and initiate 6 concurrent chat sessions using long-system prompts (~1.5k tokens) that trigger KV-cache growth and fallback to longer context execution.
2. Trigger a long-generation request on one session (expected ~60–90 tokens).
3. Observe that after ~12–25s of generation the socket shows short silence (no events) and then a reconnect event on the client.
4. After reconnect the session resumes but the final token(s) from the previous generation are missing; server-side trace shows final chunk emitted but not confirmed by multiplexing layer.

Observed behavior:
- Server-side: last chunk logged as "stream_chunk_sent" with offsets; multiplex layer logs a "partial-ack timeout" for that session id.
- Client-side: sees a short disconnect/reconnect and final message ending abruptly.
- No explicit 5xx from runtime; no model crash; CPU/GPU utilization within pool normal.

Expected behavior:
- Multiplex layer should guarantee in-order delivery and durable acknowledgement; on transient reconnection the final token should be replayed or redelivered such that client receives a complete message.

Initial logs attached by customer:
- ws_trace.txt (client side): shows disconnect at 2026-03-09T22:14:05Z and reconnect at 2026-03-09T22:14:09Z with no application-level gap markers.
- session_events.json: server sent chunk id 32 at 22:14:04Z; multiplex "ack" event for session id 7 missing.

Temporary workaround provided by customer:
- Reduce multiplexing concurrency to 2 sessions per socket and disable aggressive keepalive coalescing. This reduces frequency but is not acceptable long-term.

Priority/Customer ask:
- Customer requests root cause and mitigation within 48 hours; restoration of end-to-end guarantees or a recommended configuration to avoid data loss on multiplexed sockets.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 18:40 - ParcelScale (Customer): Uploaded ws_trace.txt and session_events.json. Provided dedicated pool id dp-87 and sample request IDs: req-7c9b2, req-7c9b3.
Multiplexing layer has a race when two chunks are coalesced and an in-flight KV-cache eviction triggers a slight delay in persistence ack path; subsequent TCP/TLS micro-reconnect does not replay the unacked chunk back through the mux dispatcher.
Streaming-proxy keeps a 5s window for replayable chunks; however coalesced frames are collapsed into a single buffer and the replay index is not updated when eviction occurs—leads to final chunk marked sent but not present in replay buffer.
Observed that explicit keepalive coalescing optimization (introduced 2026-01) merges tiny chunks to reduce network overhead; this increases chance of coalesced loss on reconnects.
No evidence of model worker faults or GPU preemption. CPU spikes on proxy host correlated with bursts of other multiplexed sessions but within SLOs.
In progress - holding until mux replay logic fix is validated in staging. Temporary mitigation: disable coalescing and limit sessions-per-socket for affected pools.
Patch multiplexing dispatcher to maintain independent replay buffers per logical chunk (PR referenced above).
Deploy fix to staging dp-staging-12 and run the customer's reproduction harness with KV-eviction enabled.
If validated, schedule hotfix rollout to dp-87 with feature-flagged toggle and monitor ack/replay metrics for 24h.
Customer follow-up: propose configuration adjustments for immediate relief (disable coalescing, sessions-per-socket=2) and share ETA for hotfix.
payload.summary: WebSocket multiplexing: unacknowledged mid-stream chunks and missing final token on reconnection

payload.description:
Customer reports duplicated downstream function executions when using the TS SDK's streaming client combined with a Step Functions style serverless orchestrator that replays sessions after client disconnects.
Issue summary:
The customer (Nimbus Analytics) is seeing duplicated invocations of external tool endpoints (webhook-based function calls) when their orchestration retries a streaming session after an abrupt client disconnect. This is occurring for streaming responses with partial acknowledgements (per-message confirm) enabled in the TS SDK.

Impact:
- Duplicate side effects observed in production: duplicate billing events and duplicate downstream job runs.
- Affected ~3% of long-running orchestrations (~120/week) for this customer.
- Customer considers this a P1 due to data correctness and downstream cost impact.

Environment:
- Redwood prod region: us-east-1
- TS SDK version: 2.7.1 (customer-run), orchestration: AWS Step Functions invoking serverless workers via webhook endpoints behind CloudFront.
- Webhook consumer acknowledges function calls and performs idempotent checks, but duplicates still pass through due to varying confirmation tokens.

1) Start a streaming chat session from TS SDK with per-message partialConfirm enabled.
2) During a long response (~>45s), simulate client network interruption (client process kill or ephemeral edge outage).
3) Orchestrator detects incomplete session, attempts replay/resume by creating a new client session and re-sends the same user prompt.
4) Streaming runtime delivers partial tool call confirmations; one instance shows confirmation token A, the resumed session presents token A' (token normalization/truncation) and the orchestrator re-sends the tool invocation to the webhook.
5) Consumer receives two distinct invocations and processes both (duplicates).
- Duplicate POST requests to customer's webhook within a 2-5s window for the same logical tool call.
- Confirmation tokens differ in length/encoding between original stream and resumed stream (example tokens in logs).
- Server-side logs show the Redwood streaming runtime generated two separate funcall records labeled with different stream session IDs.
- When a streaming session is resumed, the runtime should normalize idempotency/confirmation tokens so resumed requests are recognized as the same logical invocation and not re-delivered to webhooks.
- At most-once delivery semantics for tool/function calls within the bounds of the session's idempotency scope.
Excerpt from request log (timestamps truncated):
- 2026-03-08T16:22:03Z /stream A -> funcall webhook POST idempotency_token=eyJr...X (session s-123) -> 200 OK
- 2026-03-08T16:22:45Z client disconnect detected (session s-123)
- 2026-03-08T16:22:49Z orchestrator starts resume -> new session s-456
- 2026-03-08T16:22:50Z /stream A (resume) -> funcall webhook POST idempotency_token=eyJr...X~ (different encoding) -> 200 OK
Note: tokens differ by trailing modulus and a compressed header byte in the resume path.

- Slack thread: #support (link: slack.com/archives/C04SUPPORT/p167839) where Nimbus first reported duplicates.
- Dashboard check (console): per-route token counts show retry spike at 2026-03-08 16:22 UTC correlating to customer's reported window.
- Captured raw streaming frames from runtime show original funcall frame included 'confirm_token' field as base64url, while resumed stream replaced header with a hex-encoded prefix.
- Replayed requests through local staging with TS SDK 2.7.1 reproduced duplicate POST when using CloudFront+Lambda@Edge in front of webhook (header normalization by edge appears to mutate multi-part confirm header).
- No evidence this is a consumer-side mishandling; webhooks log distinct tokens.

1) Edge/Proxy (CloudFront + Lambda@Edge) rewrites or splits idempotency/confirmation header during resume path leading to token normalization mismatch.
2) TS SDK generates a resume-compatible token but runtime path that handles resumed streams applies an alternate encoding (hex vs base64url) for confirm tokens.
3) Downstream idempotency checks fail because token canonicalization isn't consistent across original/resume paths.
- Customer temporary workaround: disable automatic resume/replay in the orchestrator (fail-open to the original session) and let client retry from scratch, or have webhook add a dedupe layer using a broader composite key (user_id + prompt_hash + approximate timestamp).
- Recommended short-term: enable strict canonicalization on customer edge (avoid header rewrites for confirm headers), or run webhook behind an ALB (avoids CloudFront Lambda@Edge rewrites).
- Eng (ts-sdk) created a small reproducer and opened PR to add instrumentation around confirm token generation and normalization (see related PR).
- Ops added extended logging around confirm_token headers in prod route for Nimbus for the incident window.
- Support engaged Solutions Engineering to advise customer on temporary request dedupe pattern.
- Engineering to add deterministic canonicalization logic in streaming resume code path (TS SDK + runtime) to ensure confirm tokens use a single encoding across original/resume flows. Target: patch in 2.7.2.
- Ops to validate that edge proxies (CloudFront Lambda@Edge) are not normalizing headers; if they are, publish guidance for customers in the runbook.
- Customer to test the workaround removing Lambda@Edge manipulation and report results.
- Set follow-up check: verify no duplicates for 72 hours after patch/mitigation.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:03 - Nimbus SRE (customer): We can reproduce by killing the client mid-stream. Sending access to sample logs and CloudFront config.
payload.summary: Streaming partial-ack cascade causing duplicate tool/function invocations in serverless orchestration

payload.description:
Customer (Northbridge Healthcare) reports that audit log export started failing with 403 PermissionDenied immediately after enabling RBAC v2 on their Private deployment. They are attempting to export audit logs to their SIEM integration for daily compliance review.

Impact:
- Security team cannot export audit logs from Redwood Console or via API.
- Blocks compliance evidence collection for internal audit window (customer stated deadline: end of week).

Notes:
- Customer indicates exports worked the prior week.
- They recently upgraded their Private deployment and enabled RBAC v2 feature flag per rollout guidance.
- Customer uses SSO group mappings -> built-in role templates; no custom roles yet.
1) Log into Console as a user in customer IdP group mapped to their auditor role (customer calls it "Compliance-Auditor").
2) Navigate to Console -> Security -> Audit Logs -> Export.
3) Select time range (e.g., last 24h) and destination (download CSV / SIEM push).
4) Click Export.

API variant:
- POST /v1/audit/exports with payload {"from":"2025-02-26T00:00:00Z","to":"2025-02-27T00:00:00Z","format":"jsonl"}
Export job is created successfully and either (a) produces a downloadable artifact, or (b) pushes events to the configured SIEM exporter. Console shows job status and a success event is written to audit logs.
Console shows "You don't have permission to perform this action" and the export job is not created.

API returns:
- HTTP 403
- error: PermissionDenied
- message: "Missing permission: audit.export" (when debug header is enabled for admin users)

Customer sees the failure for both download exports and SIEM push exports.
Customer-provided (redacted) Console network trace:
- request_id: req_9c7f2b2c0c4c
- POST https://<redacted-private-domain>/v1/audit/exports
- status: 403
- response: {"error":"PermissionDenied","message":"permission denied"}

Server-side (Support reproduced via customer-provided request_id in their cluster logs):
2025-02-27T18:22:51.931Z audit-exporter INFO request_id=req_9c7f2b2c0c4c subject=user:<redacted> org=org_nbhc action=audit.export scope=org:org_nbhc decision=deny reason=SUBJECT_MISSING_PERMISSION policy_version=rbac-bundle-2025.02.21

Control plane authz debug (from customer admin session with debug header enabled):
X-RW-Authz-Deny-Reason: SUBJECT_MISSING_PERMISSION
X-RW-Authz-Policy-Version: rbac-bundle-2025.02.21
X-RW-Authz-Action: audit.export
X-RW-Authz-Scope: org:org_nbhc
Initial hypothesis: role template used by customer (auditor/read-only) does not include the new audit export permission introduced/required by RBAC v2 for export job creation.

Findings:
- In Private deployment, customer is using built-in role template derived from the policy bundle artifact.
- The policy bundle version deployed in their cluster (rbac-bundle-2025.02.21) contains audit.read permissions but not audit.export.
- The export flow is correctly enforcing deny-by-default at the service layer and is returning 403 (expected behavior when permission missing).
- This appears to be a role template gap/mismatch rather than a regression in the exporter service code.

Root cause:
- Role template intended for auditors (and/or deployment operators) did not include audit.export after RBAC v2 permission catalog expansion.
- Customer’s group mapping therefore omitted audit.export even though the user’s responsibilities include export for compliance.
Immediate workaround (customer-admin action):
1) Create a custom role (or clone the auditor template) and add permission: audit.export
2) Bind that role at org scope to the IdP group used for auditors.
3) Wait up to 60s for authz cache TTL to expire (or trigger cache invalidation by re-saving the binding).
4) Retry export.

Alternate workaround (least recommended but acceptable short-term): bind the built-in Security Admin role to a small subset of compliance users who need export, then remove once the proper auditor role is updated.

Support offered to run a screen-share to validate permissions via the Console permission viewer once enabled in their build.
Fixed by updating the Private policy bundle role templates to include audit.export in the appropriate built-in roles (Auditor / Security Admin variants for Private), then rolling the updated bundle to the customer’s Private deployment.

Customer actions completed:
- Upgraded policy bundle from rbac-bundle-2025.02.21 to rbac-bundle-2025.03.01 (delivered via their standard Private update process).
- Re-synced IdP group mapping to the updated role template.

Verification:
- Customer confirmed exports succeed from Console and via POST /v1/audit/exports.
- Support validated new audit log entries include authz context for the export action (decision=allow) and the SIEM push succeeded.

Follow-ups logged:
- Ensure role template matrix explicitly calls out audit.export vs audit.read separation and applies consistently across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
We confirmed RBAC v2 is enforcing a new fine-grained permission (audit.export) for creating export jobs. Your current auditor role template includes audit viewing but not export. We provided a safe workaround (custom role add audit.export) and delivered an updated policy bundle so your existing group mapping can continue to use a built-in role template. After the update, exports are working again.
2025-02-27 (Colin O'Donnell): Opened on behalf of Northbridge after POC admin reports they cannot export audit logs. Customer suspects RBAC v2 change; started immediately after upgrade/flag enablement. Asking for quick workaround due to audit deadline.
2025-02-27 (Kevin Osei): Acknowledged. Requesting: policy bundle version, Private platform version, whether export is Console-only or also API, and one request_id for correlation. Also asking customer to confirm which IdP group/role mapping is in use.
2025-02-27 (Colin O'Donnell): Customer provided request_id req_9c7f2b2c0c4c and confirmed it fails both in Console and direct API call. Policy version shown in debug header: rbac-bundle-2025.02.21. Group mapped to "Read-only Auditor" template.
2025-02-27 (Kevin Osei): Found deny log in audit-exporter with reason SUBJECT_MISSING_PERMISSION for action audit.export. This looks like expected enforcement + missing permission in role template. Coordinating with Security Eng to confirm intended role coverage.
2025-02-28 (Marcus Lin): Confirmed audit.export is intentionally separate from audit.read for least privilege; however the built-in auditor template should include export for most enterprise setups. We should update role templates and document recommended split (Auditor vs Auditor-NoExport).
2025-02-28 (Kevin Osei): Provided workaround to customer: create custom role with audit.export at org scope and bind to their IdP group. Customer will apply immediately while we prep updated policy bundle.
2025-03-01 (Kevin Osei): Role template change landed in policy bundle; advising customer to update to new bundle artifact and resync. Noting cache TTL up to 60s; may need to re-save binding to trigger invalidation. (Related: cache TTL discussion in #eng-platform thread 1739808400.)
2025-03-03 (Colin O'Donnell): Customer upgraded bundle and confirmed exports are now succeeding; SIEM push also successful. Requesting confirmation that audit log entries include authz context for their SOC evidence.
2025-03-04 (Kevin Osei): Confirmed exporter emits authz context fields (decision, action, policy_version, reason codes) aligned with the authz decision schema. Closing ticket.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Edge CDN (conditional GET / If-None-Match probe) is intermittently issuing a 304-ish probe/teardown while an SSE stream to a long-running generation is active. The downstream behavior observed by the customer: the stream abruptly ends mid-markdown block (no explicit terminal event), and on immediate reconnect the new stream begins with a repeated system/preamble message and a duplicated short token prefix. This results in partial content, duplicated system content, and a broken markdown code block for some sessions.

Impact:
- PaperTrail Analytics (enterprise) reports ~12% of long-form streaming calls truncated or duplicated over last 24h from us-east.
- Affected flows are interactive summarization and long-code-generation where the client depends on a consistent stream boundary and finalization marker.
- Customer sees degraded UX (broken markdown/code fences) and increased downstream parsing errors.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east edge region fronted by third-party CDN (conditional caching + revalidation enabled).
- Requests are to /v1/stream?model=redwood/ranger-7b with SSE.

Observed timing:
- Typical timeline: initial SSE open -> ~30–90s of streamed tokens -> CDN issues conditional revalidate (If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since) -> TCP/HTTP teardown from CDN side -> client reconnects and resumes -> duplicated "system" preamble and missing closing fence.

Notes: Customer is on enterprise plan with dedicated routing rules. They provided sample client logs and a session id (session_id: pt-9a7f).

1) Configure a client to open SSE to /v1/stream?model=redwood/ranger-7b with Accept: text/event-stream and keep the connection open for >60s.
2) Put a caching CDN in front (simulate conditional revalidation on TTL expiry). Set CDN to send conditional GETs (If-None-Match) periodically for long-lived connections.
3) Trigger a long generation (300–800 tokens). Observe stream through client until CDN issues conditional probe.
4) When CDN sends revalidation (or the edge issues a FIN), observe whether origin emits terminal marker (data: [DONE]) or connection closes silently, then reconnect the client and inspect the leading tokens on the resumed stream.
5) Repeat with smaller and larger keepalive/heartbeat intervals to reproduce frequency variance.
Partial output: stream ends without explicit terminal event; client reconnect receives a fresh initial 'system' message repeated, followed by a short duplicated token prefix. Final markdown code block frequently lacks closing backticks, causing downstream parser failure.
If the origin marks the stream finished the SSE should include an explicit terminal event (e.g., data: [DONE]) before close. If CDN revalidation occurs mid-stream, edge should hold or proxy the request such that clients either receive the terminal marker or can resume without duplicating system-level messages.
----- client.log (excerpt) -----
[2026-03-13T11:22:41.123Z] SSE open session pt-9a7f: received token 'defense'...
[2026-03-13T11:23:08.907Z] keepalive: data chunk...
[2026-03-13T11:23:12.002Z] tcp RST from CDN-edge (conditional-get probe) - connection closed without terminal event
[2026-03-13T11:23:12.120Z] client reconnect session pt-9a7f: receives 'system: <preamble>' then 'system: <preamble>' (duplicate), then content starts mid-sentence
----- origin-edge access log -----
GET /v1/stream?model=redwood/ranger-7b 200 - 11.22s "SSE"
CDN revalidate: If-None-Match: "etag-abc123"
CDN->edge: conditional probe triggered at 2026-03-13T11:23:11Z
2026-03-13 12:00 - Initial triage by Support (Ava T): reproduces with internal simple CDN config and logs show connection FIN from CDN during revalidation.
2026-03-13 13:30 - SRE (Diego M) observed that origin runtime does not always emit finalization marker when connection is closed by a close-from-proxy; it relies on TCP graceful close to trigger emitter flush.
Hypothesis: Edge/proxy or CDN is issuing conditional GETs that cause a half-close path; origin flush path is skipped leading to silent-close. On reconnect the session handshake includes system preamble generated by the server-side conversation snapshot; session resume logic currently prepends the system preamble unconditionally which creates duplication.
Checked recent deploys: no recent changes to resume/preamble code in last week; CDN config changed yesterday (shorter revalidate TTL) per customer support notes.
Relevant links: Slack #support (thread PT-9A7F), runbook: https://confluence.redwood/internal/runbooks/streaming-edge-cache-handling
Captured pcap between CDN and edge to inspect FIN timing; awaiting redacted pcap from customer for timeline correlation.
Applied short-term workaround: disable CDN revalidation for SSE endpoints for PaperTrail's routing rule (edge rule updated at 2026-03-14T02:14Z). Customer implemented a client-side heuristic to wait 200ms for terminal marker before treating the stream as complete. This reduced incidence to ~1.8% in initial sampling.
1) Engineering: add logic in serving-runtime to emit terminal marker immediately on SIGPIPE/connection-abort to avoid silent close. 2) Platform: add edge rule to detect conditional GET on live SSE and hold revalidation until stream finalizes or use cache-bypass for active connections. 3) QA: add integration test simulating conditional revalidation to prevent regressions. 4) Follow up with CDN provider to understand conditional-get behavior on long-lived SSE streams.
In progress: temporary edge rule applied and customer workaround accepted. Engineering action item created (ENG-STREAM-678) to ensure runtime always flushes finalization marker on abrupt upstream close. Target fix in next minor release.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 16:22 - PaperTrail Support (customer): We can confirm behavior reduces when TTL bumped from 30s -> 5m. Happy to accept workaround but want permanent fix.
payload.summary: edge-cache-conditional-get-teardown-splits-stream-and-repeats-system-preamble

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovusDocs, dedicated) reported a sharp increase in 5xx responses and streaming disconnects during an evening traffic burst. Error spike correlated with sustained prefetch activity and tenant-specific concurrency ramp. API gateway queue lengths grew, upstream runtimes began returning 502/503 and several runtime processes restarted under GPU watchdog.

Impact:
- ~18% of NovusDocs' inference requests returned 5xx during the incident window (18:10–18:40 UTC on 2026-03-10).
- Streaming sessions dropped and reconnects triggered retry amplification.
- Customer reported degraded UX for a critical document-generation flow; business impact: several thousand failed docs.

Environment:
- Production (us-east), dedicated pool for NovusDocs.
- Prefetcher enabled for tenant-level hot prompt caching.
- Autoscaler configured with ephemeral worker pool min=4, max=40.

Steps to reproduce (at high level):
1) Enable tenant prefetch and pin model open-7b-v2 to a dedicated pool.
2) Simulate 800 concurrent streaming sessions with long prompts (avg 6k tokens) and bursty arrival (ramp 0->800 in 30s).
3) Observe API gateway queues grow and runtime prefetch locks increase; runtime GPU watchdog restarts under backlog.

Observed logs / traces (highlights):
- apigw: accept_queue_depth jumped from 30->450 within 45s.
- apigw: upstream 502/503 rate increased; proxy reported "upstream response timeout" and "connection reset by peer".
- runtime: repeated "KVCacheLock: prefetch cancel failed" warnings followed by "GPU watchdog: termination requested" and tidy restart logs.
- metrics: p95 latency for failed requests ~ 3.2s; error budget for tenant exceeded.

Initial hypothesis:
A combination of aggressive prefetching and the tenant's rapid concurrency ramp created a backpressure loop: the prefetcher holds locks and inflates request latencies which amplifies queue depth at the API gateway; the gateway's retry/fanout logic then increases load on runtimes, leading to GPU watchdog-triggered restarts and a cascading 5xx wave.

Support triaged and confirmed elevated 5xx stories across tenant routes at 18:10 UTC
SRE added short-term ingress rate-limit to tenant at 18:20 UTC, which reduced immediate pressure but did not fully stop runtime restarts
Captured runtime stacks and prefetcher lock stats; discovered a prefetch cancellation race under high concurrency leading to stale locks
Heap and GPU memory telemetry showed fragmentation spikes before watchdog terminations
Reproduced locally with a synthetic harness; confirmed prefetch cancellation semaphore could deadlock when cancellation and new prefetch intersect
Short-term: Applied tenant ingress rate-limit and disabled background prefetch for NovusDocs pool (18:20 UTC) which reduced queue growth and halted restart spiral.
Medium-term: Deployed runtime patch that fixes the prefetch cancellation race and adds an LRU cap for pending prefetch requests (PRs merged: serving-runtime#2894, apigw#512).
Long-term: Added an inbound backpressure policy to apigw to drop oldest pending requests under sustained queue pressure, tuned GPU watchdog thresholds, and added a prefetch telemetry dashboard and alert.
Customer remediation: Disabled prefetch in tenant config for now; rolling back to prefetch after patch verification. Provided customer with usage credit for failed requests and scheduled a postmortem review with engineering and CS.

Create a runbook for prefetch-induced backpressure (owner: infra eng)
Add automated test for prefetch cancel race in CI (owner: serving-runtime team)
Tune apigw backpressure thresholds and enable alerts for fast queue growth (owner: apigw team)
Coordinate with CS to contact affected customers and reconcile failed requests billing (owner: support)
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10T18:18Z: Initial report from NovusDocs — they see ~20% 5xx on streaming route. Escalating to SRE.
Marco Rinaldi (SRE) 2026-03-10T18:21Z: Applied temporary ingress rate limit and disabled prefetch for tenant to reduce pressure. Will collect traces for analysis.
Elena Moreno (Eng - serving runtime) 2026-03-10T20:03Z: Found race in prefetch cancellation codepath; preparing hotfix. Repro harness validated the failure mode.
Marco Rinaldi 2026-03-11T02:47Z: Hotfix deployed to prod (canary -> rollout). Observed error rate back to baseline for NovusDocs.
Martin (NovusDocs) 2026-03-11T09:00Z: Thanks — impact mitigated. Would like confirmation before re-enabling prefetch.
Aisha Patel 2026-03-12T14:15Z: Post-deploy verification complete; re-enabled prefetch for NovusDocs during low-traffic window and monitored for 24h with no regression. Marking incident resolved and scheduling postmortem.
Root cause: prefetch cancellation race + aggressive tenant prefetch combined with sudden concurrency ramp created a self-amplifying backpressure loop. Fixes deployed: cancellation race patched, prefetch caps introduced, API gateway backpressure policy hardened. Customer impact mitigated via temporary rate limiting and prefetch disablement; full rollback validated. Follow-ups scheduled to harden telemetry and CI coverage.
This ticket captured a backpressure pattern not previously codified in runbooks; it surfaced the need for an inbound request dropping policy under sustained queue growth for dedicated tenants.
payload.summary: Backpressure loop causing elevated 5xx and runtime restart spiral during tenant prefetch burst

payload.description:
Issue opened by SomaHealth CS: after enabling the new adaptive async batching policy (per-request grouping) together with the new 4-bit quantization profile and the kv-cache TTL eviction (LRU-timeout=30s) for tenant somahealth-prod, several endpoints show increased semantic errors and hallucinations for a critical clinical extraction prompt set. Customer observed sudden mismatch between human-labeled expected extraction values and model outputs starting 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC after a config rollout. They want guidance for immediate safe rollback and root-cause investigation.
Customer reports ~15 percentage point drop in exact-match extraction accuracy on their 250-example evaluation set (from 91% -> 76%). Production traffic includes ~1200 requests/min for affected routes; some requests are latency-sensitive (95th p50-95 target 200-500ms). Business impact: triaged as P1 due to potential clinical safety risk and SLA exposure.
1) Tenant somahealth-prod has optimizer profile 'adaptive-async-batch-v2' enabled, quant-profile 'q4-dense-agg', and kv-eviction 'lru-ttl=30s'.
2) Send the customer's canonical extraction prompt with patient note payload (attached in logs).
3) Compare token-level outputs and structured extraction fields to expected gold labels.
4) Re-run against the same model with quant-profile 'q8-normal' and batching disabled — outputs align with expected labels.
Attached snippets from request IDs: req-20260312-11a, req-20260312-11b. Example mismatch: expected 'medication_dose: 5 mg' returned 'dose: 5mg twice' causing parser mismatch. Console traces show 'batch_group_id' assigned, 'kv_cache_hit=false' in many failing requests. No 5xxs reported. Latency profiles show slight increase in p95 (~+40ms) during incident window.
Hypotheses: 1) Quantization to 4-bit changed tokenization/post-decoding behavior for rare clinical tokens leading to extraction errors. 2) Adaptive async batching combined with short KV TTL may produce stale/misaligned KV contexts for requests that relied on prefix cache warmups. 3) Race conditions in batch packing could reorder prompt segments for this tenant due to payload chunking. Current telemetry: precision drop correlates with rollout time; failing requests largely show kv_cache_hit=false and grouping into larger async batches. We inspected PR #6124 which enabled new packing heuristics and found a non-deterministic padding path that may affect token alignment for long clinical notes.
Apply temporary traffic-split: 95% -> hf/soma-med-13b-v1 (q8-normal), 5% -> current variant for warm monitoring. Disable kv-eviction for tenant somahealth-prod (set lru-ttl=600s) to avoid repeated cold-cache misses. Disable adaptive-async-batch flag per-tenant until controlled verification.
1) Snapshot current config: redwoodctl config snapshot create --tenant somahealth-prod --name pre-rollback-20260312
2) Create traffic gate: redwoodctl traffic split set --tenant somahealth-prod --route /extract --split 'variant_q8:0.95,variant_q4:0.05'
3) Disable adaptive async batching: redwoodctl optimizer set --tenant somahealth-prod --profile adaptive-async-batch-v2 --enabled false
4) Revert quant profile: redwoodctl model pin --tenant somahealth-prod --model hf/soma-med-13b-v1 --quant q8-normal
5) Increase kv-cache ttl: redwoodctl cache set --tenant somahealth-prod --kv-ttl 600
6) Monitor 5m rolling accuracy on customer's evaluation set via console/dashboard and hold changes if regression persists
(TBD) Initial mitigation applied: traffic-split and increased kv-ttl. Early telemetry shows accuracy improved to 89% on customer's eval within 30 minutes after rollback steps 2-4. Ongoing root-cause: engineering to instrument kernel dequant path and packing order. Will plan full rollback if improvement not stable. Postmortem scheduled if confirmed causal link to packing heuristics and 4-bit quant interactions.
Customer (SomaHealth CS): 'We validated on a mirror and see divergence only when q4 + adaptive async batching is on.'
Support (Ava): 'Collecting failing request IDs and creating snapshot. We'll validate rollback steps; assigning to runtime team.'

Issue summary: Customers observed intermittent end-to-end request latency spikes and occasional 120s request timeouts for calls that use external tool invocation. Root cause traced to the new dynamic tool discovery / capability negotiation flow which performs a synchronous per-request capability check against the tool registry when a tool URL is present in the request. Impact: Multiple customers on Dedicated tier (BeaconHealth first reported) experienced increased p95/p99 latencies for requests that include tool invocation metadata. This caused some long-running customer calls to hit application-level timeouts and surface as 504/timeout errors. Environment: Prod (us-east-1), dedicated cluster for BeaconHealth. Regression window began ~2026-03-09 04:30 UTC, correlated with a router rollout that enabled dynamic negotiation by default.
1) Use customer account on dedicated cluster with a request that includes a tool invocation (tool_url header + tool_schema omitted).
2) Send 50 concurrent generation requests with short prompt (~40 tokens) that trigger tool capability negotiation path.
3) Observe per-request traces and latency; p95 often spikes >800ms and tail >1.2s. Some requests hit client-side 60s/120s timeouts depending on caller config.
4) Toggle router feature flag 'dynamic_tool_negotiation' to false and repeat: p95 returns to baseline (~120-150ms).
Service traces show synchronous RPC to tool-registry/service-discovery for capability negotiation on every request when a tool_url is present. Each negotiation adds 120-350ms depending on cache miss. Because negotiation is synchronous and blocking the request flow, overall request latency increases and tails spike. Customers reported 504/timeouts for long-running sessions and increased error rates on routes that combine short LLM generation with tool calls.
Capability negotiation should be cached or executed asynchronously so that per-request overhead is minimized. On cache hit the latency overhead should be negligible (<10ms); on cache miss negotiation should use async prefetch or background warm-up without blocking the generation path.
Initial triage: BeaconHealth reporting spikes 2026-03-09. Support ingested trace and found negotiation RPCs chained before generation start.
Distributed trace snippets show negotiation RPCs originate in router pre-handler and block the request path until capability resolution completes.
Perf profiling: cache hit latency ~8-12ms, cache miss latency 120-350ms due to remote schema fetch and TLS handshake to external tool endpoints.
Change correlation: router v2.14.0 rollout (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/112) enabled feature 'dynamic_tool_negotiation' by default on 2026-03-09 04:20 UTC.
Hypothesis: enabling negotiation by default exposed many requests with previously-unused tool_url header to synchronous negotiation path, dramatically increasing per-request hops and tail latency.
SRE confirmed increased 5xx/timeouts on dedicated clusters that had non-empty tool_url traffic patterns (coincides with BeaconHealth usage).
Customer provided sample request and agreed to run AB test toggling the flag; toggling off returned latencies to baseline within 5 minutes.
Related: SUP-99231 shows a similar symptom but was traced to preflight serialization—linked for follow-up harmonization of negotiation and preflight logic.
Workaround: For immediate relief customers can disable dynamic negotiation via router feature flag 'dynamic_tool_negotiation=false' or include tool_schema in request payload to avoid negotiation. Permanent fix: rolled out router v2.14.1 which adds an in-memory negotiation cache with TTL 10m and background prewarm on first tool discovery; also introduced a new header 'x-rw-tool-negotiation-mode' to opt into async-negotiation mode. Patch deployed 2026-03-12 09:40 UTC to affected dedicated clusters. Follow-ups: (1) extend cache to shared cache layer for multi-instance warm hits (INT-1124). (2) Add metrics for negotiation cache hit rate and per-request negotiation latency to Console dashboards (task created: ENG-ops backlog). Customer confirmed resolution on 2026-03-12.

Additional notes:

Issue summary:
Acme AI reports that token usage on invoice preview is higher than their own aggregation of the Usage API for the same time window. They believe they are being billed twice when (a) their client retries after timeouts/5xx and/or (b) Redwood performs a server-side fallback retry during streaming.

Impact:
- Customer-reported overcharge risk and trust hit; potential credit request.
- Meter integrity risk: duplicate usage events on retry/fallback path may skew billing, pricing experiments, and gross margin model.

Customer evidence (from Support):
- Spike in billed tokens on 2026-02-06 around 19:00–21:00 UTC.
- Correlates to elevated 502/timeout errors and client retry behavior.
- Requests primarily via OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions with stream=true.

Environment:
- Prod, region us-east
- Models: llama-3.1-70b primary, fallback variant enabled by routing policy

Suspected failure mode:
Usage event dedupe/idempotency for streaming retry/fallback path is insufficient. When an initial attempt emits partial tokens and then triggers an internal retry/fallback (or when the gateway retries before completion), both attempts may be marked billable and included in the billing aggregation, resulting in double-counting for a single logical client request.

Initial triage links:
- Slack: sources/slack/support/1770083321-customer-reporting-double-charged-retries.json
- Related Eng work: pr-27463 (retry double-count fix), perf-canary metering scenarios (pr-912)

Requested outcome:
1) Confirm whether double-counting occurred for Acme AI in the reported window.
2) If confirmed, identify scope and provide remediation recommendation (credit vs forward-only fix) per Finance/Legal.
3) Ensure fix is deployed with validation and no regressions (shadow billing compare + canary).
2026-02-08 09:14 PT — Monica Patel (Support) — Customer escalation from Acme AI. They are seeing ~8–12% higher tokens on invoice preview than their daily usage export rollups. They specifically suspect retries are being counted twice. Attaching customer-provided request IDs in the Slack thread: sources/slack/support/1770083321-customer-reporting-double-charged-retries.json
2026-02-08 10:02 PT — Cole Summers (Billing Hooks) — Acknowledged. This matches an open hypothesis from telemetry: streaming retry path can emit two usage events with different attempt_ids but same logical request correlation. Looping in Nadia Rahman + Logan Wright for metering semantics + event dedupe.
2026-02-08 11:18 PT — Nadia Rahman (Metering) — Meter spec intent: if Redwood performs internal fallback retry for a single client request, we should bill once for tokens delivered to the client (not sum of partial + retry if both are recorded as final). If client retries without idempotency, they may legitimately pay twice; if they use Idempotency-Key / request_id semantics, we should dedupe. Need to confirm what headers Acme is sending.
2026-02-08 11:45 PT — Monica Patel (Support) — Follow-up from customer: they are sending an idempotency key on retried requests ("Idempotency-Key" header) and expect dedupe. They also note the double-count only appears on stream=true requests; non-streaming seems fine.
2026-02-08 13:10 PT — Logan Wright (Telemetry) — Quick check in Snowflake: elevated duplicate usage_event rows for Acme AI where (account_id, idempotency_key) repeats with different event_id, and both have billable=true. Duplicates cluster around stream_disconnect + fallback_retry reasons. This looks like us, not customer misuse.
2026-02-09 08:06 PT — Cole Summers (Billing Hooks) — Root cause found: on stream retry/fallback, we emit a usage event on the first attempt when the stream aborts, then emit another usage event on the retry attempt. Downstream billing aggregation does not enforce "single billable event per (account_id, idempotency_key, api_operation)" and treats both as billable. We should mark the first attempt as non-billable (or billable=false, attempt_status=aborted) and ensure the final successful attempt is the only billable event under idempotency.
Plan: ship fix under PR pr-27463 and validate with shadow billing compare (pr-27518) + perf-canary scenario update (pr-912).
2026-02-09 09:22 PT — Monica Patel (Support) — Sent interim update to Acme AI: We confirmed a suspected metering bug on streaming retries that may overstate billed tokens. We’re working on a fix and will quantify impact. Asked them to share 5–10 representative request IDs and confirm whether they saw 502/timeout spikes client-side.
2026-02-10 14:30 PT — Leila Farouk (Perf Canary) — Added regression scenario locally reproducing: stream partial tokens -> server fallback -> stream completes. Asserting only one billed_tokens aggregation per idempotency key. Will land via pr-912 after pr-27463 merges.
2026-02-11 10:05 PT — Cole Summers (Billing Hooks) — PR pr-27463 merged to main. Change: do not finalize billable usage event for aborted streaming attempt if a retry/fallback is triggered and an idempotency key is present; instead, emit attempt record with billable=false and tie to retry_chain_id. Also tightened dedupe key (account_id + idempotency_key + operation + request_start_minute).
2026-02-12 16:48 PT — Aisha Bello (SRE/Observability) — Deployed to staging and ran shadow-billing compare: delta went from +6–10% (old > new) on reproduced dataset to <0.3% expected variance. No increase in missing usage events observed.
2026-02-13 09:37 PT — Connor O'Brien (Release) — Rolled out to prod us-east (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with shadow-billing enabled for 48h. Monitoring duplicate rate + drift dashboards; no alert triggers so far.
2026-02-14 12:20 PT — Cole Summers (Billing Hooks) — Quantification for Acme AI window 2026-02-06: estimated overstatement 7.9% of billed_tokens for streaming chat requests in us-east only. Scoped to retry/fallback path; non-streaming unaffected. Recommending Finance-approved credit; not doing retroactive invoice re-issue unless required. Looping in Emily Stone for credit guidance.
2026-02-14 15:05 PT — Emily Stone (RevRec/Accounting) — Approved: issue customer a one-time service credit equal to estimated overbilled amount for the impacted period, documented as "metering correction credit". Do not re-open posted invoices. Attach query evidence and PR references to the internal audit trail per playbook.
2026-02-15 09:12 PT — Monica Patel (Support) — Informed Acme AI: bug confirmed + fixed; credit will be applied on next invoice. Shared customer-safe explanation: duplicate token charge could occur when streaming request aborted and Redwood retried/fell back; fix ensures a single billable event per idempotency key and bills only the final successful stream. Customer acknowledged and asked for a short written note for their finance team.
2026-02-16 11:40 PT — Cole Summers (Billing Hooks) — Closing as resolved. Follow-ups: (1) ensure usage API exposes billed_tokens vs raw_tokens and retry attribution consistently (tracked in related PRs), (2) add alert on duplicate billable events per idempotency key (owned by telemetry).

Fix shipped via pr-27463 with shadow-billing validation and perf-canary regression coverage. Customer remediation: Finance-approved service credit for estimated overbilled amount (no retroactive invoice re-issue).

23:30 UTC - Runtime team observed repeated kernel-probe failures when a memory/CPU scheduling jitter occurred; runtime switched execution path to slower scalar kernels which increased latency and triggered watchdog no-progress timers.
23:35 UTC - Feedback loop: increased latency led apigw backpressure and stream window stalls; stalled streams accumulated, causing connection reset amplification and client-visible 502/503.
Root cause (combined): a) tenant's high-multiplexing streaming pattern exhausted HTTP/2 stream/window resources at apigw and b) a recent runtime kernel probing change (PR 12634) caused intermittent fallback to slower kernels under brief memory pressure which amplified tail latency and then triggered watchdog restarts.
Evidence: correlated timestamps between apigw RST_STREAMs, runtime kernel-fallback logs, and watchdog restarts; CPU and heap traces from the affected runtimes captured rapid kernel-probe activity.
Reproducibility: reliably repro'd in staging when simulating multiplexed long-lived streams and toggling kernel-probe experimental flag.

2) Send sustained traffic with ~80% of requests using long-lived streaming (keepalive interval > 60s)
3) Observe that after ~2 minutes the apigw reports increased stream resets (RST_STREAM) and client sees 502/503

2) 02:10 UTC: apigw keepalive pool utilization climbed to 98% (accept queues increased).
3) 02:12 UTC: several runtime workers logged GPU thermal throttling and subsequent NVIDIA driver resets on nodes hosting the customer's dedicated pool.
4) 02:14-02:50 UTC: API gateway returned a mix of 502/503/504; streaming sessions reported half-open sockets and heartbeats dropped.
5) After 02:50 UTC: autoscaler and kube-level restarts reduced concurrency and error rate slowly returned to baseline.

Observed logs / metric excerpts:
- apigw.keepalive_pool.active: 3125 (pool capacity 3200)
- apigw.accept_queue.length: spiked from 12 -> 490 in 3m

- Root cause appears to be a combination of three factors: (1) aggressive tenant-driven long-lived streaming sessions causing keepalive pool saturation in api-gateway, (2) amplified backpressure to serving runtime leading to high sustained GPU utilization in a small set of nodes, and (3) GPU thermal events triggering driver resets which cause upstream runtimes to exit and return 502/503 until recoveries occur.
- Keepalive pool shrink behavior: healthcheck/keepalive reaper aggressively reclaimed idle connections during the spike, which resulted in churn and additional connection setup under load causing accept-queue growth and proxy head-of-line blocking.

- API gateway team to audit keepalive reaper heuristics and add a soft-failback to avoid aggressive reclaim under stream-heavy workloads.
- Product -> Customer Success: recommend SDK guidance for backoff/hedging on long-lived streams and provide suggested heartbeat interval (>= 60s) for heavy multiplexing clients.
- SRE runbook update: include GPU-thermal + keepalive pool interplay as a trigger for automated mitigation (temporary throttle + node reshuffle).

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightLens (dedicated tenant) reports intermittent high tail latency and streaming disconnects during sustained inference traffic. Impact: Customer seeing 5-10% of requests hit 10s+ latencies and some streams terminate with TLS handshake retries, causing client-side reconnects and token duplication. Environment: Production, APAC region behind our edge POPs; Dedicated pool in apac-south-1. Observed start: 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.
1) Customer sends sustained streaming generate requests (chunked SSE) to /v1/streaming with region unset (default routing).
2) Traffic volume ~120 rps from multiple BrightLens app instances over 10–15 minute windows.
3) Observe intermittent failures: client logs show TLS handshake errors and server logs show 499/504 and backend timeouts.
edge-pop logs (apac-south-1) around 2026-03-09T22:04Z: upstream TLS handshake failed: EOF from upstream (envoy ssl) trace_id=trx-8b3f
gateway metrics: 502 spike at 22:04-22:07 UTC; p99 latency jumped from 180ms -> 11.3s
serving-runtime logs: kv-cache miss + extended GC pause observed on worker-17 at 22:05:12 (duration 320ms) but not sufficient to explain 10s tails

2026-03-09 22:10 UTC - SRE engaged; initial checks of Dedicated pool show normal GPU utilization
2026-03-09 22:20 UTC - Edge team observes transient certificate renegotiations between edge proxy and a west region egress proxy
2026-03-09 22:45 UTC - Temporary mitigation: advised customer to set region_hint=apac-south-1; immediate reduction in TLS retries noted
2026-03-11 09:30 UTC - Deeper traces show requests from APAC routed to us-west-2 via a translation proxy during BGP flap window
Hypothesis A: Intermittent BGP path changes caused upstream route to flip to a us-west transit, introducing an additional TLS proxy hop and occasional MTU/mss translation anomalies leading to handshake retransmits.
Hypothesis B: Edge POP affinity snapback (anycast rebalancing) caused some connections to be proxied through a legacy TLS-terminating fleet that lacks the new keepalive tuning, exposing long tail due to TCP/TLS retransmit timeouts.
Trace analysis: Collected 27 traces with trace_id prefix trx-8b3f..trx-8b5a. 7/27 showed an extra hop: edge-pop -> translation-proxy-us-west -> dedicated-gw -> serving-runtime. The extra hop correlates with 9–12s tail latencies.
Packet captures: SYN/SYN-ACK retransmits observed where MSS option dropped after translation-proxy; some clients retried TLS handshake, leading to duplicate streams at application layer.
Config review: The translation-proxy had an older OpenSSL build and a different keepalive/tls-opts profile; also had Nagle enabled and default TCP_USER_TIMEOUT which aggravated the symptom.
Customer impact: Requests that hit the translated path either succeeded after long retry or failed client-side with TLS handshake timeout; roughly 5-10% of active streaming sessions were affected during peak windows.
A transient cross-region routing event routed a portion of APAC tenant traffic through a legacy TLS translation proxy in us-west-2. That proxy's TCP/TLS stack and MSS handling caused handshake retransmits and long tail latencies, resulting in streaming disconnects and timeouts for some requests.
Mitigation: 1) Applied a routing policy change to prefer local apac-south-1 egress for dedicated tenants with region_hint unset; 2) Decommissioned traffic path through legacy translation proxy for affected ASNs; 3) Updated translation-proxy TLS config and enabled keepalives + MSS passthrough. Post-rollback: p99 for BrightLens streams returned to baseline within 45 minutes. Follow-up: full fleet OpenSSL upgrade scheduled, and a permanent route-affinity rule for Dedicated tenants to reduce cross-region translation risk.
Schedule OpenSSL rebuild for translation-proxy fleet (ENG-4278)
Add route-affinity test to Chaos/QA that simulates BGP path flips and validates TLS path invariants
Add metric: percent_of_requests_with_extra_proxy_hop (edge->translation->gw) and alert when >0.5%
Update runbook: when customer reports TLS handshake retries, check for translation-proxy hop via traces and advise region_hint as immediate workaround

Additional notes:
2026-03-09 22:48 - Support (Aisha Khan): Advised customer to set region_hint=apac-south-1 as immediate mitigation. Customer confirmed reduced failures in 20 minutes.
2026-03-11 10:05 - Networking (Rajiv Menon): Correlated to a BGP flap on peer ASN 64512 between 22:03-22:27 UTC; routes temporarily preferred the transit path through us-west translation cluster.

Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden increase in cost for embedding calls after they started routing traffic through their staging proxy. They observe embeddings charged at the hosted "hourly" embed rate instead of the expected dedicated reserved rate. Impact: Unexpected invoice increase for current billing period and confusion over credit application. Environment: Production requests proxied from customer staging host into Redwood api-gateway via our reverse proxy (forwarded X-Request-Origin headers).
Customer reported +18% invoice delta on the last 48h for embed usage; affects billing reconciliation and may trigger finance escalation if not resolved within SLA.
1) Customer routes embed requests through their staging proxy to Redwood API endpoint with header X-Forwarded-Host set.
2) Requests hit the api-gateway and are routed to usage-postback service.
3) Postback records metering tags based on origin header mapping.
4) Observed: meter recorded as hosted-hourly-embed instead of dedicated-reserved-embed for same API key.
Postback trace snippet (us-east, 2026-03-11T22:14:02Z): request_id=8f7a1c, api_key=live-lyra-01, origin_header=staging.lyra.internal, resolved_org=lyra-prod, selected_rate=hosted-hourly-embed, kv_cache_hit=true
Initial hypothesis: staging proxy rewrites or omits the original origin->tenant header leading postback to fallback to default hosted rate.
Checked routing logs: requests identified with api_key correctly mapped to LyraSearch org.
Postback mapping: we prioritize X-Client-Region + origin tag; if origin tag matches a staging domain pattern we apply hosted fallback (legacy behavior introduced 2025-09).
Search of past incidents: SUP-314777 touched postback heuristics for unrecognized hostnames.
Correlation: all affected requests in the sample were proxied and had X-Forwarded-Host set to staging hostname which matches our staging pattern and triggers fallback to hosted rate.
Repro on internal staging: able to reproduce using curl with X-Forwarded-Host=staging.lyra.internal — postback selected hosted-hourly-embed rate.
Root cause: heuristic in usage-postback that treats any origin hostname containing "staging" as non-production and forces hosted rate; staging proxy preserved that hostname in forwarded headers.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - SRE (Jordan Lee): Confirmed logs show X-Forwarded-Host contains 'staging'. Postback code path in prod branch checks 'staging' substring. Created hotfix branch to relax heuristic and prioritize api_key org mapping first. See PR #742.
2026-03-13 - Finance (Elena Rossi): Requested provisional credit estimate and that we notate invoice until fix is deployed. Will hold escalation to billing team until resolution.
Workaround applied: updated usage-postback heuristics to prefer api_key->org mapping over origin-hostname heuristics and deployed hotfix to canary. Full rollout to us-east prod scheduled 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC after monitoring window.
Customer remediation: no changes required on their side; they may optionally strip 'staging' from forwarded host to avoid previous heuristic.
Follow-up: engineering to remove substring-based 'staging' rule and add explicit allowlist for known staging domains; add unit tests and a migration plan for postback config. Finance to apply provisional credit outlined below.
payload.summary: Staging proxy causes embed requests to be billed at hosted hourly rate (metering tag misattribution)

Issue summary:
Customers report intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional request timeouts that correlate with periods of low traffic followed by a resumed stream. The spikes show up as single-request tail latency events (10s-20s) and intermittently as 504s for short streaming requests.

Impact:
- Affected customer: Clipr AI (dedicated).
- Intermittent user-facing timeouts and visible p99 latency regressions for short requests (single-turn chat / completion calls).
- Start time: ~2026-03-09 22:30 UTC, recurring during quiet windows and on tenant handoff events.

Environment:
- Production, us-east region, dedicated pool assigned to Clipr AI.
- Traffic profile: mostly short sequences (<=128 tokens), mix of streaming and non-streaming.

Steps to reproduce (observed patterns):
1) Let dedicated pool run idle for ~5-15 minutes.
2) Resume with a burst of short streaming requests (QPS ~5-15 across a few connections).
3) Observe occasional single-request p99 spikes and rare 504s.

Observed behavior:
- Continuous batcher emits a "small" flush (1-2 requests) almost immediately after resume, but the request experiences high end-to-end latency compared to baseline.
- Traces show additional scheduler wait before GPU load begins and an extra 100-300ms of pre-processing that appears correlated with a cache/kv-sync operation.
- When multiple tenants are being reweighted (tenant-handoff), these spikes increase in frequency.

Expected behavior:
- Smooth low-latency handling for short requests after idle periods; no large single-request tail latency events.

Logs/metrics attached:
- p95/p99 timeseries for request latencies (streaming/non-streaming) from 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-11.
- Traces sampled from affected requests (span timeline included).
- Grafana: serving-runtime CPU/GPU utilization around spikes.

Immediate customer-visible mitigation requested: temporary routing to a pool variant with conservative coalescing and KV-cache-prewarm enabled.
2026-03-10 10:00 UTC: SRE captured flamegraphs for two representative p99 traces. Extra overhead concentrated in: (a) batcher pre-flush decision path, (b) kv-cache coord sync, (c) scheduler ticket acquire for GPU slot.
Heap of evidence suggests a "ghost flush" phenomenon: batcher tick aligns with tenant-weight recalculation during quiet periods, producing an early flush with insufficient batching and triggering additional coordination paths that add fixed overhead per-request.
Observed correlation between tenant-handoff events (resharding/weight update) and increased frequency of spikes. Metrics: tenant-reshard-rate spikes match p99 spikes with ~10-30s lag.
KV-cache invalidation occurs occasionally during weight updates; affected requests see an extra ~120-280ms for KV sync (confirmed via span annotations).
Hypothesis 1: Timer alignment bug — coalescer flush timer and tenant-weight recalculation tick fall into resonance under low QPS, causing ghost flushes that bypass some fast-paths and force expensive coordination.
Hypothesis 2: Cold path in scheduler when preempted by a very small batch leads to extra lock contention and sequentialization on GPU ticket acquisition for that request.
Test performed: simulated quiet period and replayed tenant weight update in staging; reproduced single-request p99 tail in 3/10 runs. Added debug logging for batcher tick and tenant weight update boundaries.
Temporary mitigation trialed: route Clipr AI traffic to a pool with batcher.min_batch_size=1 disabled and kv-cache prewarm set; observed 70% reduction in p99 spike rate over a 12-hour window.
Next steps: instrument more precise timing metrics around batcher tick, add jitter to tenant-weight recalculation schedule, and create a patch to ensure batcher fast-path for tiny flushes avoids KV-sync path when possible.

2026-03-10 11:22 — Customer (Clipr AI - Elena R.): Provided 6 request IDs and sample logs; impact seen across two application instances. Noted that spikes affect end-users intermittently.

Workaround applied: customer traffic routed to a conservative-pooling configuration reducing spike frequency. Engineering patch proposed: (1) add jitter to tenant-weight-recalc schedule, (2) make batcher flush fast-path avoid KV-sync for tiny flushes, (3) add a dedicated-pool flag for conservative coalescing during low-util windows. PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892. Planned rollout after tests across canary pools.
Routed Clipr AI to conservative pool variant; enabled KV-cache prewarm and disabled aggressive micro-batching for their dedicated pool.
Ship PR 1892 with tests and enable canary rollout (owner: Ethan Chen).
Add monitoring alert: sudden increase in tenant-reshard-rate correlated with p99 spike rate (owner: Lara Nguyen).
