Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 03:04 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses (502/503) for requests routed to tenant Acme Analytics. The API Gateway entered repeated backoff cycles and a subset of serving runtimes for the tenant showed accelerated fd growth and accept-queue saturation. Impact: customer-facing API calls returned 5xx at ~8-15% for a 25 minute window; streaming sessions experienced resets; some low-latency requests timed out. Scope: limited to prod-us-east and predominantly customers with scheduled tenant snapshot sync enabled (dedicated tenants).
1) Ensure a dedicated tenant with scheduled snapshot sync configured (tenant flag snapshot-sync=on). 2) At ~03:00 UTC trigger tenant snapshot via internal admin API POST /admin/tenant/<tenant>/snapshot/sync. 3) Generate concurrent small-embedding and streaming requests (~200 rps) against the tenant for 5 minutes. 4) Observe API Gateway 502/503 increase and runtime fd growth in /proc/<pid>/fd and accept_queue metrics.
- apigw: 2026-03-12T03:05:12Z WARN upstream reset for tenant=acme-analytics route=/v1/embeddings status=502 count=120/min
- serving-runtime: 03:06:01 UTC fd_count=16384 (baseline ~512) for prefetch-worker threads
- netstat/snippets: many sockets in TIME_WAIT and CLOSE_WAIT associated with 10.20.5.*; accept_queue length peaked at 256 for runtime-ephemeral-34
- tracing: high retry amplification from hedged-retry policy, observed backoff loops between apigw and runtime proxies
- dashboards: 5xx-rate (tenant filter) peaked at 14.2% between 03:05-03:30 UTC
- Correlated spike start time with scheduled tenant snapshot sync (snapshot process opens many transient connections to shard-aware prefetcher).
- Heap/CPU metrics of runtime processes stable; kernel fd exhaustion and accept queue backlog were primary failure mode.
- Prefetch worker did not close socket on some code paths when snapshot worker returned early (hypothesis: error path missing socket.close()).
- Apigw configured hedged retries + aggressive retry window; retries amplified load when upstream started dropping connections, causing backoff loop.
- Quick mitigation: temporarily disabled scheduled snapshot sync for Acme Analytics and increased runtime connection backlog limits to reduce immediate 5xx. This reduced 5xx-rate to <1% within 7 minutes.
- Affected code area likely runtime prefetcher: snapshot streaming path. Created internal INT-18290 to track runtime patch and load test changes.
1) Disabled tenant snapshot sync for Acme Analytics (admin toggle) at 2026-03-12T03:12 UTC. 2) Increased runtime accept queue and ulimit for affected shards. 3) Temporarily relaxed hedged-retry policy at API Gateway for tenant routes to avoid amplification. 4) Restarted 2/3 runtime replicas for the tenant during low traffic window to reclaim leaked fds.
- Merge runtime fix to ensure sockets are closed on all prefetch error paths (PR referenced above).
- Add unit/integration test to simulate snapshot cancellation and assert fd usage returns to baseline.
- Add liveness check to detect fd growth and restart affected runtime automatically.
- Review hedged-retry policy defaults for tenants with scheduled background jobs; add per-tenant retry profiles.
- Run controlled load test with snapshot sync enabled to validate fix before re-enabling for Acme Analytics.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 03:40 - Customer (Acme Analytics): Thank you — our production jobs were failing during the window. Please confirm when safe to re-enable snapshot sync.
2026-03-12 09:12 - Support (Asha Mehta): Customer notified of temporary workaround and impacted window. SLA response satisfied. Waiting on ENG PR and staged deploy.
Postmortem will capture timeline, root cause (socket leak in prefetch snapshot stream), mitigation efficacy, and action owners. Target postmortem doc to be published to Confluence within 72 hours after incident closure.

Issue summary: At ~19:05 UTC on 2026-03-10 BrightVoice (enterprise tenant) reported a sustained elevation of 5xx responses and unusually long tail latencies for short chat requests. Impact: ~20% of calls returned 502/503 over a 30-minute window, causing client-side retries and downstream timeouts. Scope: impacts a single enterprise tenant in us-west region during a scheduled model shard rebalance.

Environment: prod-us-west (us-west-2), Redwood hosted inference, API gateway version v2.17.3, serving-runtime v1.9.2, autoscaler v0.8.

Observed behavior: API gateway logs show repeated TLS handshake failures between the gateway and runtime proxies. The gateway enters a backoff loop, reduces concurrent dialing, and many requests fail fast with 502. Simultaneously, runtimes log NVML/gpu watchdog resets and process restarts after short-lived connections are established and torn down repeatedly.

1) Simulate a tenant warmup: start 200 small streaming sessions to prod-us-west that open TLS connections to runtime and immediately send short prompts.
2) Trigger a model shard rebalance to force ephemeral runtime restarts.
3) Observe handshake failure rate between apigw and runtime proxies and monitor 5xx rate on the tenant route.

Expected: transient retries but no sustained 5xx floor or runtime watchdog resets. Actual: handshake thrash results in sustained 5xx floor and repeated NVML resets on several GPUs.
apigw: [2026-03-10T19:06:12Z] tls: handshake error: remote error: unknown cipher
serving-runtime: [2026-03-10T19:06:14Z] proxy: short-lived connection established; nvml: watchdog reset triggered
apigw: [2026-03-10T19:07:01Z] backoff: dialing runtime (retrying) count=7 route=brightvoice-usw
serving-runtime: [2026-03-10T19:07:25Z] runtime: signal: SIGABRT (reason: gpu-watchdog)
stack traces and additional logs attached in internal artifact (s3://redwood-logs/sup-908172/).
- Initial triage (Aisha): tenant traffic spike coincided with a scheduled shard rebalance; apigw observed TLS errors referencing 'unknown cipher' which is odd since server cipher lists were unchanged.
- Eng (Marco): reproduced locally by forcing mismatched TLS client/server cipher priorities during rapid connection churn; observed repeated older cipher suites being negotiated then rejected by runtime process leading to short connections and GPU watchdog resets.
- Hypothesis: a recent library update in the runtime proxy (PR linked) changed cipher ordering and introduced a regression when connection churn is high, resulting in repeated handshake attempts and CPU/GPU stress.
- Observed autoscaler: concurrent scale-downs were aggressive during rebalance, producing a window where many connection attempts hit a small set of warm runtimes causing connection storms and thrash.
- Cross-ref: Slack #support-incidents thread (https://slack.redwood/support-incidents/CH12345) and PRs above.

Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Reported elevated 5xx from BrightVoice, opened incident, added on-call SRE.
Marco Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced handshake errors in staging with cipher reorder; escalated to runtime team and opened PR to revert cipher change.
Leah Ortiz (Runtime) 2026-03-11: Confirmed regression introduced in runtime-proxy v1.9.2 (PR#3421). Preparing hotfix cut for v1.9.3.
Customer (BrightVoice) 2026-03-10: Notified of degradation, asked for ETA on mitigation. Provided recommended temporary limit changes.
Marco Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-11: Deployed temporary rate-shim for tenant (concurrency cap) and adjusted autoscaler cooldowns; immediate 5xx rate dropped to baseline.
Leah Ortiz (Runtime) 2026-03-12: Hotfix v1.9.3 deployed to prod-us-west; monitoring normalizing.
A code regression in serving-runtime proxy changed TLS cipher ordering which, under high connection churn during a model shard rebalance, caused repeated failed negotiations. Aggressive autoscaler scale-down amplified pressure onto fewer runtimes, turning transient handshake failures into a sustained 5xx floor and GPU watchdog resets.
Workaround: applied tenant-level concurrency cap and increased autoscaler cooldown to prevent aggressive scale-down during rebalance. Hotfix: reverted cipher-order change in runtime proxy and released v1.9.3. Post-deploy monitoring showed 5xx rate returned to baseline for BrightVoice and no further GPU watchdog resets observed in the window. Customer notified and incident closed.
- Runtime: add CTS (connection-thrash) test to CI that simulates rapid new-connection churn across TLS stacks. (owner: Leah, due 2026-03-20).
- Infra: add a safety floor to autoscaler to avoid aggressive scale-down during tenant warmup and rebalance windows; add telemetry to detect handshake-thrash early. (owner: Marco, due 2026-03-18).
- Observability: add dashboard panel for apigw<->runtime TLS error rate and a paged alert when sustained >5% for 5m. (owner: Observability team, due 2026-03-17).
- Postmortem doc: publish detailed postmortem and remediation steps to Confluence and link to customer support note. (owner: Aisha, due 2026-03-15).

Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10 20:40 UTC Scriptly Inc reported a sustained spike in 5xx responses for streaming requests. The spike correlated with runtime worker restarts and delayed GPU warmup on a subset of Dedicated capacity nodes. Impact: customer streaming sessions experienced frequent disconnects and ~20-40% increased error rate for ~18 minutes. Several long-running streaming sessions were dropped and retried, amplifying downstream load. Environment: production, dedicated cluster serving Scriptly Inc tenant in us-east primary and failover in us-west.
20:37 UTC - first customer report via support chat: multiple 502s on long-lived streams
20:39 UTC - automated alert: api-gateway 5xx rate > 15% for tenant Scriptly (threshold 5%)
20:41 UTC - SRE escalated, began attaching runtime and GPU-manager logs
20:45 UTC - temporary mitigation applied: scale up ephemeral worker pool (+50%) and increase accept-queue depth
20:55 UTC - error rate dropped back to baseline after autoscaler completed warmup and prefetch timeouts adjusted
1) Use a long-lived streaming session against redwood/gpt-medium-v1 with sustained token output (avg response chunking every 200ms)
2) Trigger a graceful restart of serving-runtime on a subset (simulate rolling deploy) and attempt to resume streams
3) Observe keepalive/handshake failures and 5xx responses as clients attempt reconnection while GPU warmup is still ongoing
4) Note increased retry loops from client and higher prefetch cancellations leading to worker respawns

[2026-03-10T20:40:14Z] runtime: worker-17 exit(137) reason=oom_after_prefetched_kv shard=12

Initial hypothesis: rolling restart combined with prefetch cancellation caused a tight respawn loop on ephemeral workers which in turn delayed GPU warmup and caused apigw to surface 502s/503s
Correlated metrics: prefetch cancellation rate spiked from baseline 0.2% to 18% for affected tenant; worker restart rate climbed from 0.01/s to 0.6/s
Observed pattern: long-lived streaming clients reconnected repeatedly while runtime was still initializing model KV and GPU; apigw then hit upstream timeouts and returned 5xx
Reproducer confirmed in staging when inducing prefetch timeout = 50ms during concurrent worker restarts
No evidence of hardware failure on GPU hosts; warmup latency increased due to serialized prefetching and KV lock contention
Scriptly reported client-visible disconnects and a 35% reduction in successful streaming completions during the window
Attachments: customer provided sample request ids: abc123, def456, ghi789
Billing impact: elevated retries noted; potential overcharge concerns — flagged for finance review

Additional notes:
Customer (Scriptly Ops): Confirmed stream stability improving after mitigation; requested root cause and timeline for a permanent fix.
Mitigations applied: 1) Temporarily increased ephemeral worker pool to absorb reconnect storms; 2) raised prefetch abort timeout for affected tenant from 100ms -> 400ms to prevent immediate cancellation during warmup; 3) adjusted autoscaler cooldown to 120s to avoid churn. Result: 5xx rate returned to baseline within ~10 minutes. Current status: monitoring for recurrence; not yet a complete fix.
Schedule runtime change to serialize per-shard prefetches with backoff to avoid global warmup stalls (ENG-#),
Patch autoscaler to detect prefetch-induced respawn loops and temporarily increase warmup concurrency (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/334)
Add tenant-level prefetch telemetry to console dashboards and alerting for sustained prefetch cancellation >5%
Coordinate post-incident postmortem and customer-facing RCA within 72 hours
payload.summary: Burst of 5xx errors during streaming shutdown propagation causing downstream runtime respawns and GPU warmup delays

Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 in us-west (customer AcmeHealth) a subset of tenant traffic silently switched to a degraded fallback variant. Impact: ~2-5% of requests from the tenant were routed to the cheaper/degraded variant for several minutes, causing altered completions and a spike in cost for the tenant due to duplicate retries. Environment: prod-us-west, dedicated tenant on enterprise plan. Observed window: 2026-03-10 18:20 - 18:35 UTC.

Observed behavior: Requests that previously held a model version pin were routed to a degraded secondary variant without explicit pin removal in the control plane. Control-plane logs show pin eviction events with reason=header_mismatch and orchestrator marked cohort as unhealthy, triggering fallback policy. Expected behavior: Pins should survive transient edge header mutations (or be reconstructed via session cookie) and not trigger fallback except for true health failures.

Steps to reproduce (internal repro):
1) Use customer tenant token + pre-existing session cookie for pinned version.
2) Send burst of parallel streaming requests (approx 300 RPS for 30s) from a client that simulates an upstream proxy that truncates the X-Tenant-Session header to 64 chars.
3) Observe in routing logs that requests where X-Tenant-Session was truncated show pin-lookup failures and are routed to fallback variant.

Immediate customer impact: Silent degraded outputs observed by AcmeHealth product team; ticket opened after they saw inconsistent model outputs affecting an automated triage flow.

Initial hypothesis: A recent edge proxy configuration change on the customer's side (header size enforcement) started truncating the header used by our pinning algorithm. The pinning logic treats a header mismatch as a lease/affinity violation and triggers cohort eviction during canary weight surge. The canary window's health smoothing then marked the cohort degraded and applied fallback routing.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 19:05 UTC - Correlated client-side header truncation events seen in edge logs with pin_eviction events in routing logs.
2026-03-10 19:20 UTC - Reproduced locally by running a synthetic proxy that truncates X-Tenant-Session to 64 bytes. Confirmed that truncated requests hit fallback path immediately after orchestrator's pin check fails.
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Engineering review: pin check currently requires exact header match; there is no length-normalization or signed-cookie fallback for this header in the orchestration handoff.
2026-03-11 13:40 UTC - Found recent customer-side change: AcmeHealth rolled out a new gateway filter at 2026-03-10T18:00 which enforces header size limits. Customer confirmed the change during call.
2026-03-11 15:20 UTC - Canary health smoothing logic amplified the effect during a weight increase at ~18:22 UTC, turning transient pin misses into cohort degradation and fallback.
2026-03-12 10:10 UTC - Patch proposal accepted: add header-canonicalization + graceful pin ttl extension, and fall back to signed session cookie when header length mismatch occurs.
Support (Aisha): Thanks for reporting, AcmeHealth team. We're seeing matching pin_eviction events on our side and are investigating. Could you confirm whether you changed any gateway filters around 18:00 UTC?
AcmeHealth (product-ops): Confirmed — we deployed a gateway config that enforces maximum header lengths at 18:00 UTC. We did not expect it to affect your session header. We can roll back but would prefer a platform fix if possible.
SRE (Diego): I've reproduced with a truncated header locally and can see immediate eviction. Short-term workaround: we can enable an explicit tenant-level routing_override to pin the tenant to the promoted variant while engineering implements a fix. Would you like us to enable?
AcmeHealth: Yes please enable the routing_override for the tenant for the next 48h while we test a gateway hotfix. We'll coordinate rollback after you confirm the platform patch.
Eng (Lina Chen): Investigating patch. Two options: 1) accept header canonicalization (normalize/truncate to canonical form) before pin check, 2) change pin-check to tolerate header-length mismatch when a signed session cookie is present. We'll implement 2) to be conservative. PR drafted: routing/pull/4543.
Support (Aisha): Applied customer-requested routing_override at 2026-03-11T17:05 UTC. Observing metrics: pin_eviction events dropped to zero for that tenant and outputs stabilized.
Workaround applied: tenant-level routing_override pinned AcmeHealth to the primary variant (manual override) at 2026-03-11T17:05 UTC — mitigated customer impact.
Permanent fix: engineering to deploy change to pin-check logic to accept signed-session cookie fallback and relax strict header-length equality. Patch PR #4543 created; target staging rollout 2026-03-15, prod rollout 2026-03-17 pending canary verification.
Follow-ups: update docs to recommend header canonicalization guidance for self-hosted gateways; add automated alert when header-length-truncation spikes for pinned-tenants.

[2026-03-10T18:21:04Z] edge/proxy: WARN truncated header X-Tenant-Session from 128 -> 64 client_ip=203.0.113.45

Issue summary:
Customer reports a sustained 30-50% drop in dedicated-pool throughput for their reserved capacity window starting 2026-03-10 10:40 UTC. The drop correlates with elevated attach latency and increased prefetch retries. Impact: multiple production jobs saw increased tail latency and several 504s to the customer-facing service.

Impact:
- Customer-visible p95 token latency increased from ~220ms to ~620ms.
- Throughput for pinned route fell by ~45% for a 90 minute window.
- Some requests returned 504/timeout during autoscaler attach backoff.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool (tenant: veridian-prod-dedicated).
- Region: us-east-1.
- Model routing: pinned rwd-llama2-13b-q4 primary, fallback to open-7b-q8_0.

Steps to reproduce / Observed sequence:
1) 10:38 UTC: periodic background "health-scan" job (snapshot integrity + weight-validate) started on several nodes in the reserved pool (operator-initiated maintenance).
2) 10:40-10:45 UTC: allocator attach latencies rose (logs show 500ms -> 1.8s attach handshake delays).
3) Autoscaler observed rising attach latency and classified capacity as constrained -> increased scale-up attempts and then triggered conservative cooldowns.
4) Prefetcher started thrashing KV cache entries due to snapshot read IO causing NVMe contention on two GPUs; this produced noisy-neighbor symptoms (per-node IO wait spikes).
5) 10:45-12:15 UTC: sustained throughput loss (~45%) with intermittent request timeouts.

Relevant logs and traces referenced below.

Observed behaviour vs expected:
- Expected: background maintenance runs to be IO-throttled and not reduce tenant throughput below SLA.
- Observed: maintenance caused elevated host IO wait leading to attach timeouts and autoscaler misclassification, which in turn reduced throughput and increased request errors.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Support temporarily disabled the non-critical health-scan on the affected nodes at 11:05 UTC (operator rollback).
- We moved the tenant traffic to a warm spare GPU stripe at 11:12 UTC (manual routing) which gradually restored throughput.
- Customer was notified and put on high-touch status.

Examined allocator traces: multiple attach attempts per request increased attach handshake retries from avg 1.1 to 3.6 during peak window.
NVMe io_wait correlated with prefetcher eviction spikes measured via metrics.prefetch.evictions which spiked 6x.
Autoscaler telemetry showed a decision boundary flip: attach_latency > 800ms -> treat as scarcity and throttle new routing. This threshold triggered conservative behaviour during noisy IO.
Node-level dmesg contained repeated nvme timeouts on node-ue1-d-14 during window (investigating firmware counters).
Prefetcher currently lacks backpressure when underlying storage signals sustained io_wait. Hypothesis: add reactive backoff to prefetcher and schedule health-scan with IO cgroup limits.
Looked at tenant traffic patterns: Veridian has many parallel short streams that are sensitive to attach latency. This amplified noisy-neighbor impact compared to long-batch tenants.
2026-03-10 11:07 - Support (Aisha Khan): Confirmed with SRE that health-scan was scheduled and running on two reserved nodes. We recommended pausing the job and monitoring attach latencies.
2026-03-10 11:20 - SRE (Daniel Park): Paused health-scan across affected nodes. Noted NVMe io_wait spikes in node metrics (node-ue1-d-14, node-ue1-d-18). Initiating node-level io diagnostics.
2026-03-10 11:35 - Customer (Veridian SRE - Priya Rao): Noticed token p95 coming down slowly after re-routing. Appreciate quick response. Please advise whether this will reoccur.
2026-03-10 12:05 - Support (Marta Lopez): We are keeping the node scans off for now. Next step: patch prefetcher to back off under elevated nvme_io_wait; scheduling with infra team. ETA 2026-03-12.
2026-03-11 09:15 - SRE (Daniel Park): Root-cause hypothesis: background health-scan read pattern created large sequential NVMe bandwidth that competed with prefetcher small-random IO, causing NVMe scheduler starvation and elevated GPU attach times. Working on a limiting PR.
2026-03-12 14:02 - Engineering (Samir Patel): Submitted PR to add IO throttling and health-scan niceness: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4789. Patch includes prefetcher backoff threshold tied to node io_wait metric.
2026-03-12 16:45 - Support (Marta Lopez): Notified customer of planned fix and scheduled controlled rollout to canary nodes on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.
Temporary and permanent mitigations: (1) Immediately paused health-scan and re-routed tenant to warm-stripe to restore throughput. (2) Engineering delivered PR to rate-limit health-scan IO and add prefetcher backoff tied to node io_wait metrics (PR #4789). (3) Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-13; full rollout after 24h canary with monitoring. (4) Recommended changes to runbooks: schedule heavy maintenance jobs outside reserved windows or use IO-cgroup throttling.
payload.summary: Dedicated throughput fingerprint shift caused by background health-scan impacting autoscale behavior

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports frequent failures for long-lived streaming responses when clients use HTTP/3 (QUIC) to the private deployment endpoint. Failures start ~30-90s into a stream and manifest as QUIC packet decryption errors and abrupt stream termination. Impact: Active users in production experience broken streaming completions for chat/streaming endpoints; user-facing error rate ~8% for affected customers, causing perceived instability in product demos.

Environment: Private deployment in Acme Ads' VPC peered to Redwood Private control plane via Transit Gateway. Traffic path includes customer on-prem -> transit GW -> redundant DirectConnect links -> cloud TGW -> Redwood VMs behind GWLB. ECMP is enabled across two upstream transit links. QUIC/HTTP3 is allowed through firewalls and load balancers.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Client establishes HTTP/3 connection to private endpoint and begins a streaming completion.
2) Stream proceeds normally for ~30-90s with many packets exchanged (large responses, long-lived).
3) Suddenly client logs show QUIC error: PACKET_DECRYPTION_FAILURE / CRYPTO_ERROR and stream terminates; server records connection close with QUIC_ERROR(0x1d).
4) Restarting client session usually succeeds for a short period then may fail again after similar duration.

Observed logs and captures:
- Server-side QUIC logs: "connection 0x7f...: received undecryptable packet, dropping (PACKET_DECRYPTION_FAILURE)" (multiple occurrences).
- Client debug: "quic: received PACKET_DECRYPTION_FAILURE, stateless reset?"
- tcpdump from customer edge shows significant packet reordering and out-of-order UDP datagrams for the same QUIC connection around the failure window (sequence gaps and >200ms reorder).
- VPC flow logs and traceroute show that traffic for the same 5-tuple is traversing two different upstream physical links after a transient ECMP hashing change correlated with a load rebalancing event on the transit router.

Hypothesis: QUIC is sensitive to packet reordering and path rebalancing; ECMP across unequal-latency/congestion paths is causing reordering/out-of-order delivery leading to QUIC decryption errors because packet-level reassembly/crypto state gets disrupted. Traditional TCP streams tolerate reordering; QUIC (UDP + crypto) exhibits packet drop/decrypt failures under this pattern. The rebalancing appears tied to transit gateway flow hashing when upstream link metrics changed.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced with tcpdump and pcap analysis from customer edge and Redwood egress node; timestamps show packets for the same connection arriving at different egress points with >100ms skew.
- No signs of middlebox tampering or SNI stripping; TLS cert validation passes on fresh connections.
- When customer temporarily forced a single egress path (disabled one DirectConnect), QUIC streams remained stable for the same traffic and load pattern.

Impact assessment: Affects customers using HTTP/3/QUIC to private endpoints or going through multi-path ECMP topologies. Streaming completions are most impacted (long-lived flows). Not all customers are affected — those with single-path or consistent per-flow hashing see no issues.

Temporary workaround applied: Support requested customer to pin egress to a single active path (disabled one DirectConnect) and asked Redwood to apply similar per-flow affinity at gateway where possible. Workaround reduced observed failures to ~0.2% during test window.

Next steps / remediation plan:
- SRE: propose configuration change on Redwood transit routers/GWLB to prefer per-flow hash that uses 5-tuple rather than symmetric hashing that can flip on path metric changes. (Assigned INT-4021).
- Support: coordinate with customer networking team to avoid transient ECMP rebalancing during peak usage windows.
- Product: add a note to Private deployment networking guide warning about QUIC sensitivity to ECMP rebalancing and recommend sticky egress or single-path for high-stability streaming.
- Engineering: evaluate adding more tolerant QUIC implementation knobs (reordering thresholds, larger decryption window) in serving runtime if safe.

References: PCAP excerpts, VPC flow logs and traceroute attached to ticket (see links in comments).

Additional notes:
Link: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/issues/INT-4021
Workaround in place: customer pinned egress to a single path; SRE proposed per-flow hashing change (INT-4021) for a safer long-term fix. Product to document QUIC/ECMP guidance. Engineering to evaluate runtime-level mitigations.
payload.summary: ECMP path rebalancing triggers HTTP/3 (QUIC) packet decryption failures for streaming responses in Private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexaHealth reported that after they started a canary rollout (adjusting canary weight from 0% to 10%) for gpt-medium-v3.1, a subset of requests that had explicit model version pins continued to route to the fallback quantized model (gpt-medium-v3.1-fallback-quant) instead of the pinned version. This occurred even though the pinned version remained healthy and dedicated pool capacity was available.

Impact:
- Some pinned requests from LexaHealth experienced output format changes and slight regressions because the fallback model is quantized and tuned differently.
- Customer telemetry and downstream processing saw ~7% degraded correctness on pinned workloads during the window.
- Business impact: potential SLA blip for Dedicated customer.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated cluster: prod-us-east
- Customer workspace: lexah-health-prod (dedicated pool)
1) Customer pins requests in their integration header: X-Redwood-Model-Pin: gpt-medium-v3.1
2) Start a canary via Console: set canary weight for gpt-medium-v3.1 -> 10% with fallback variant configured (gpt-medium-v3.1-fallback-quant)
3) Observe routing logs and sampled traces for pinned request IDs in the time window when weight was adjusted

Observed behavior:
- 6:42:12 UTC: weight change applied in console
- 6:42:12-6:43:05 UTC: ~7% of pinned requests routed to fallback variant
- Traces show routing decision path: route-eval -> weight-based assignment -> fallback-path selected (unexpected)

Expected behavior:
- Requests with explicit model pin must always route to the pinned model if the pinned model is healthy and has capacity, regardless of canary weight adjustments or fallback configuration.
- Example request ids: req_0a7f3c, req_0a9d12, req_0b3f88
- Traces: trace.us-east.0a7f3c -> routing_decision: pin=true, runtime_decision=fallback_selected
- Console change audit: /api/rollouts/12345 PATCH by lexah-admin at 2026-03-10T06:42:12Z
- Metrics: routing_rule_mismatch{project=lexah,region=us-east} count=83 in 53s window
- Heapster logs: routing-engine INFO "evaluated candidates; preferred:fallback; reason:score_override"
- Screenshot of Console rollout adjustment attached (not in JSON)

Initial hypothesis: capacity-driven fallback - rejected. No capacity shortage or 5xxs in serving logs.
Routing engine logging showed a new field 'score_override' which was set when canary weights were updated; comparator ordering allowed 'score_override' to win over explicit pin flag in rare interleavings.
Reproduced in staging by applying a weight change and firing pinned requests in the exact ordering; root cause reproduced deterministically with a pause between write to routing-config and config-index update.
Code area: routing/decision/comparator.go - pin precedence check occurred after score override logic rather than before; comparator is non-atomic with concurrent config refresh path.
SRE confirmed no impact to other customers in the cluster; effect limited to requests using explicit model pin headers during canary weight adjustments.
Added additional telemetry to measure 'pin-honored' boolean on routing decisions to monitor regressions.
Fix and workaround:
- Immediate workaround used by Support: requested customer to pause canary weight changes until hotfix applied, or temporarily set explicit model-pin lock via Console that enforces 'pin_lock=true'.
- Hotfix applied: routing comparator change and additional unit + integration tests merged in PR #6123 and deployed as routing-service v1.23.4 to prod-us-east on 2026-03-11 at 12:50 UTC.
- Post-deploy verification: replays of sampled traffic and customer test suite show 0 mismatches in subsequent 24h window.

Follow-ups and action items:
- Add automated e2e test covering pin + canary weight change race (assigned to Diego).
- Instrumentation: emit gauge 'routing.pin_precedence_violations' and alert if >0 in 5m window (assigned to SRE).
- Console UX: add warning when starting a canary if active pinned routes are detected (product ticket created).
- Postmortem recorded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEV/2026-03-10+LexaHealth+canary+routing+postmortem

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 07:18 - Customer (LexaHealth - lexah-admin): Provided sample request ids and said approximately 80 of 1200 pinned requests affected over ~1 minute window.
2026-03-10 10:10 - SRE (Priya Raman): Checked dedicated pool capacity and found no GPU pressure; autoscaler did not trigger in window.
2026-03-12 09:15 - LexaHealth (lexah-admin): Customer acceptance: observed restored behavior and accepted fix. Asked for postmortem and tests.
payload.summary: Fallback routing supersedes active version pin during canary weight update (priority inversion)

Issue summary: During an unanticipated tenant traffic surge for NovaChat, the API gateway applied an adaptive rate-shedding policy that mis-evaluated backend capacity, triggering widespread 5xx responses and a client-side retry cascade. Impact: multiple tenant requests returned 502/503 over a 22 minute window; customers reported stream disconnects and elevated latency. Environment: production us-east cluster serving Dedicated pools with mixed prefetch and streaming workloads.
1) Simulate sustained connection burst with many long-lived streaming sessions against tenant NovaChat on prod us-east
2) Force a mixed prompt workload where many requests trigger prefetch and cold KV cache misses
3) Observe API gateway rate-shedding decisions and how upstream runtimes are selected for fallback
4) Watch for client retry behavior and whether retries are amplified by gateway responses (502/503).
2026-03-13T12:07:12Z apigw[edge-12] WARN shed_decision=adaptive action=drop tenant=novachat sessions=842 backlog=3700
2026-03-13T12:07:13Z runtime[pool-7] ERROR upstream=worker-77 status=exit reason=oom_estimated kernel_swap=false
2026-03-13T12:07:14Z apigw[edge-12] ERROR proxy_response status=502 upstream=worker-77 latency_ms=412
2026-03-13T12:16:02Z apigw[edge-12] INFO shed_decision=adaptive_reenable action=allow tenant=novachat sessions=128 backlog=80
Initial hypothesis: adaptive rate-shed policy overreacted to transient backlog signals from the ingress prioritizer and marked a whole tenant as overloaded instead of applying fine-grained shedding. This caused many requests to be rerouted or dropped, prompting heavy client retries and producing a cascading 5xx wave.
Correlated events: a parallel autoscaler jitter event (documented in SUP-214567) reduced warm workers briefly, increasing prefetch latency and inflating backlog signals to the prioritizer.
Telemetry: trace sampling shows increased queue latency on apigw edge nodes between 12:05-12:28 UTC. Heap / memory metrics for several runtime workers show short-lived spikes but not sustained OOMs; a small subset of workers did crash (see logs).
Behavioral note: retry headers from client (Retry-After absent) caused immediate retries; lack of coordinated backoff amplified load on already stressed upsteam workers.
Repro attempt: synthetic load reproduced shed decision when backlog > 1500 and average runtime response time > 250ms. Adjusting shed threshold to 3000 avoided the misfire in test harness but increases risk of degraded latency under real overload.

Additional notes:
Mitigated via staged rollback of aggressive adaptive shed thresholds and temporary enforcement of conservative client backoff recommendations. Engineering deployed a hotfix to scope shed decisions per resource-class instead of tenant-wide, which prevented subsequent 5xx cascades.
Hotfix deployed 2026-03-13T16:40Z on apigw edge fleet: adaptive_shed.thresholds.tenant_critical increased from 1500 to 3000 and decision granularity changed to resource-class. No further 5xx waves observed after 16:45 UTC.
Runtime team patched memory accounting in the prefetch cold path to avoid transient worker crashes; rollout completed to Dedicated pools by 2026-03-13T18:10Z (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-registry/pull/289).
Customer communications: NovaChat notified of mitigation and recommended to implement exponential backoff with jitter. Support will monitor tenant for 48 hours.
1) Postmortem scheduled: owner Luis Ortega, doc link to be attached to related_confluence_pages. Due 2026-03-20.
2) Add conservative default client backoff guidance to API docs and insert Retry-After header where appropriate within apigw responses.
3) Enhance shed policy tests in chaos harness to include autoscaler jitter scenarios and cold-KV prefetch bursts.
4) Monitor NovaChat dedicated pool for 48 hours and collect SLI deltas; report to CS and product.
payload.summary: Rate-shedding policy misfire during tenant surge leading to 5xx retry cascade

Issue summary: During a scheduled canary weight sweep + bulk promote that ran concurrently, one NovaChat tenant observed that their per-request explicit model_version pin was ignored and requests were routed to a legacy/degraded variant. Impact: customer-facing sessions saw mixed outputs and 15-20% of streaming sessions were served by a deprecated variant for ~18 minutes, causing a quality regression and billing inconsistency. Observed at ~2026-03-12T14:05-14:23 UTC in us-east (prod).
1) Customer submits requests with explicit request header X-Model-Version: redwood/gptx-7b@v1.4.2.
2) Orchestrator receives a parallel bulk promote job and a canary weight sweep (internal schedule).
3) Control-plane snapshot merge and edge cookie rewriting occur in overlapping windows.
4) Some requests evaluate routing before the final promote snapshot commit and pick a fallback (legacy variant).
Expected: explicit per-request model_version pin must always take precedence and not be evicted by concurrent promote mechanics.

Issue summary:
Customer observed a visible p99 throughput regression (~2.5x increase) and multiple failed attaches in their dedicated pool after an automated cross-region failover window. Symptoms appeared 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC and persisted as a sustained throughput plateau for ~90 minutes.

Impact:
- NimbusHealth saw degraded end-to-end latency for inference routes pinned to their dedicated pool, p99 increased from ~420ms to ~1.1s.
- Some requests returned 503/504 or experienced long attach times (10-45s).
- A fraction of their short-stream workloads timed out and auto-retried, increasing burst pressure.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved) in us-east-1 with cross-region DR routing to eu-west-1 during the window.
- Models in use: redwood-rlhf-8k (primary), openlm-gptj-6b (fallback).
- Autoscaler configured with predictive warmup and 15s heartbeat tolerance.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Triggered DR failover for a subset of tenant routing (automated by routing policy at 09:10 UTC).
2. Shortly after, allocator heartbeats for some GPU slots began reporting delayed heartbeats (15s expected -> 60-90s observed).
3. Autoscaler saw these delayed heartbeats and interpreted as unhealthy, initiated scale-in decisions for several nodes.
4. Meanwhile prefetch / KV-cache backlogs increased and many short micro-batches flooded the remaining GPUs, causing attach contention and p99 regression.

Observed metrics and logs (high level):
- Allocator heartbeat latency spike at 09:12 UTC (median 18s -> 72s).
- Node detach + scale-in loop: 09:13 - 09:25 UTC (3 rapid shrink events).
- GPU attach failures trace shows NVML timeouts and increased driver attach latency.
- Autoscaler decision traces: multiple shrink signals flagged due to heartbeat window violation during region routing events.

Immediate asks from customer:
- Explanation of cause and short-term mitigation.
- Request to avoid repeated scaling events and to return to pre-incident throughput SLA.

2026-03-10 09:22 UTC — Support (Aisha): Acknowledged. Opening investigation with SRE. Please provide request IDs where you saw the 503s and any SDK logs from 09:10-09:30 UTC.
2026-03-10 09:28 UTC — Customer (NimbusHealth - ops@NimbusHealth): Attached sample request IDs: nh-req-5591, nh-req-5592, nh-req-5603. We saw retries spike; this is impacting patient-facing flows.
2026-03-10 09:34 UTC — SRE (Liam): Noted heartbeat window expansion on allocator metrics. Kicking off node-level checks and checking autoscaler decision logs. Pinning this to dedicated pool ID dp-84b.
2026-03-10 10:00 UTC — SRE (Liam): Temporarily disabled predictive shrink heuristic for dp-84b to prevent further rapid scale-ins. Observing whether attach failures reduce. Update in 15m.
2026-03-10 10:18 UTC — Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed partial recovery of successful attaches but p99 still elevated compared to baseline. Continuing monitoring.
2026-03-11 14:05 UTC — SRE (Liam): Postmortem note: driver-level NVML attach latency correlated with node-level IO wait during failover window. Autoscaler misinterpreted heartbeat gaps as unhealthy nodes and shrank, amplifying the impact.
09:12-09:20 UTC: Heartbeat jitter amplified during region routing change; correlation with control-plane RPC retries across regions.
Autoscaler logs: scale-in triggered by consecutive heartbeat misses (threshold 3) — in this event heartbeats were delayed (not lost) due to cross-region RPC tail latencies, causing false unhealthy signals.
Observed KV-cache prefetch queue depth increased x3 for tenant dp-84b after shrink; remaining GPUs experienced microbatch serialisation and NVML attach timeouts.
Node-level iostat and dmesg show increased block IO wait for ephemeral checkpoint write during the window on 2 nodes (node-7f, node-9a).
Hypothesis: cross-region control-plane RPC latency spike + background ephemeral snapshot activity -> heartbeat delay -> autoscaler shrink -> concentrated micro-burst on remaining GPUs -> attach timeouts and p99 regression.
Test run: Replayed traffic against a staging pool with simulated 80s heartbeat latency; autoscaler performed scale-in repeatedly and produced same attach contention pattern.
Dashboards referenced: Dedicated Pool DP-84b allocator-heartbeat dashboard, autoscaler-decision-trace, nvml-attach-latency histogram (links provided to internal dashboards).
Mitigation tested: Raised heartbeat tolerance to 120s in staging reproducer; autoscaler refrained from premature shrink and p99 impact was reduced by ~60% in replay.
Affected tenants observed a doubled retry rate during incident window, indicating client-side retry amplification played a role in increased burstiness. Recommend client-side backoff tuning as defensive measure.
Short-term: Prevented further scale-in oscillation by disabling predictive shrink for dp-84b and temporarily increasing allocator heartbeat tolerance to 120s for the pool. Evicted the background ephemeral snapshot process from the two affected nodes and triggered a controlled rebalance to restore KV-cache distribution.

Outcome: Attach failure rate dropped to baseline within 25 minutes after mitigations; p99 improved to ~480ms (near baseline).

Long-term actions (tracking):
- INFRA-2125: Add cross-region-aware heartbeat logic to autoscaler to distinguish delayed heartbeats from node failure.
- INFRA-2126: Harden control-plane RPC paths during DR routing with prioritized heartbeats.
- OPS-9002: Add guardrail to prevent autoscaler scale-in if recent cross-region routing event detected.
- Recommend customer (NimbusHealth) to apply client-side exponential backoff for short-stream retries to reduce microburst amplification; provided SDK config snippet.

Follow-up: Post-incident review scheduled 2026-03-14 16:00 UTC. Assigned owners: Liam (SRE) for INFRA tickets, Aisha (Support) to coordinate customer communication.

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightLens reports that streaming chat responses (SSE) frequently abort mid-token during sustained traffic bursts. The client receives an abrupt end-of-stream after 3–10s of no tokens, even though the inference job eventually completes on the backend.

Impact: Several BrightLens customers see truncated assistant replies inside the product. User sessions are not recoverable without a full request retry. This affects multiple customer endpoints and is causing ongoing support escalations.

Environment: prod cluster servicing BrightLens (dedicated pool) in us-east-1. Autoscaling group of 8 A100 GPUs with dedicated serving-runtime instances behind an Envoy API gateway and AWS ALB. Model pins: redwood-vicuna-13B (quantized) for assistant endpoints.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer and reproduced by Support):
1) Start a chat session with a 2k token context that triggers long-form generation.
2) Fire a burst of concurrent streaming requests (10–15) from separate client machines.
3) Observe one or more streaming connections close with no closing token or error body; client sees connection close or SSE malformed event.

Observed behavior: The SSE connection terminates abruptly during generation. Server-side logs show the inference worker continuing to generate and finish the output 5–15s after the client observed the abort. No explicit 5xx logged at the app layer for the aborted connection. Envoy metrics show increased upstream timeouts and connection resets around the same timestamps.

Relevant logs & excerpts:
- Envoy upstream log snippets: "upstream reset: connection_failure" and repeated "upstream headers timeout" entries around 2026-03-11T18:22:xxZ.
- ALB access log example: "request_processing_time=0.05 target_processing_time=12.34 response_processing_time=0.00 elb_status_code=504 target_status_code=502"
- Serving-runtime worker log (inferred): "[2026-03-11T18:22:12Z] generate_stream: started request id=abc123" then "[2026-03-11T18:22:24Z] generate_stream: finished request id=abc123 duration=12.0s" with no associated error.
- Client telemetry: SSE event stream closed with WebSocket/HTTP client code 1006 / ECONNRESET in customer traces.

Hypothesis / initial investigation notes:
- Load balancer idle or target timeout (ALB/Envoy) is closing connections when backend generation exceeds configured thresholds under bursty concurrency. The serving runtime continues producing tokens but the connection path is torn down by middleboxes.
- There is evidence of Envoy dropping upstream connections when concurrency crosses a threshold causing queueing delays; this manifests as upstream resets in Envoy logs.
- Client heartbeats are not enabled by default for SSE flows, so multi-second gaps between tokens are treated as silent and result in connection closure by intermediaries.

Customer impact workaround provided to BrightLens:
- Short-term: Recommend client implement automatic retry with conversation state on stream close and reduce per-request max_new_tokens to keep generation chunks < 6s.
- Platform workaround: We increased ALB and Envoy idle/timeout thresholds for the BrightLens dedicated pool to 120s and temporarily scaled the serving pool from 8->12 GPUs to reduce queueing.

Next steps already taken:
- Eng oncall (Diego) created INT-4512 to run a reproducer load test and capture pcap/trace.
- Added enhanced Envoy debug logging for the BrightLens target group for 24h.
- Engineering set a short-term config bump on ALB/Envoy timeouts and informed BrightLens.

Proposed longer-term fixes:
- Add periodic SSE keepalive/heartbeat frames from the serving-runtime to prevent intermediaries from treating gaps as idle.
- Improve real-time metrics for token emission latency per-request so autoscaler and routing can detect sustained per-request stalls and redirect to higher-throughput nodes.
- Tune queueing/backpressure behavior in the serving-runtime to prioritize steady token emission under concurrency.

Open questions:
- Is the Envoy idle timeout bump safe across other tenants in the same VPC? (Security/infra to advise).
- Can we add configurable keepalives in the runtime without regressions on memory/CPU?


2026-03-11 18:40 — Support (Ava): Initial triage with customer; reproduced with 12 concurrent streams. Noted ALB 504s and Envoy upstream_reset patterns.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:20 — BrightLens (Customer): Confirmed fewer truncations after change but still seeing ~1 in 50 aborts under peak.
2026-03-12 11:10 — Product (Maya): Flagging as product/backlog item for keepalive and token-metrics; may impact roadmap prioritization.
Reproducer (INT-4512) shows correlation between concurrent request queue depth and Envoy upstream_resets. Token emission SLO violation occurs when per-request generation >8–10s combined with 10+ concurrent streams. No serving-runtime OOMs or worker crashes observed.
Temporary mitigations applied: ALB/Envoy timeouts increased and serving pool scaled. Customer instructed to implement retries and smaller generation chunks. Permanent fix planned: runtime keepalive + token-latency metrics work.
Middlebox timeouts (Envoy/ALB) closing idle streaming connections during sustained token-generation delays caused by bursty concurrency and queueing in the dedicated serving pool.
Mitigation in place; engineering backlog item created for runtime keepalive and improved token emission metrics. Monitoring remains active; ticket will be updated with code PRs and rollout plan.
payload.summary: SSE session aborts mid-response when inference latency spikes under burst load

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Northwind AI reports that the Redwood TypeScript SDK is retrying requests that return HTTP 400 (Bad Request). They observed multiple request IDs for what they believe is a single client call, and raised concern about duplicate billing and/or duplicated side effects in their application.

Impact:
- Customer observed 2–3 identical requests sent for a single application action when the API responds with 400.
- Customer concerned this could lead to duplicate charges and/or duplicated downstream actions (they log each attempt and tie it to billing / user-visible behavior).
- Support + on-call had difficulty triaging because TS error surface did not clearly indicate whether the error was retryable and what triggered the retry.

Customer report (from email + support portal):
- SDK: @redwood-ai/sdk (TypeScript) v2.8.0 (customer-reported)
- Runtime: Node 18
- Pattern: calling chat.completions.create() with a request that sometimes returns 400 (validation failure). SDK appears to retry anyway.
- Evidence: logs show 3 request_id values within ~2 seconds, all 400, same payload.

Environment:
- Region: us-east-1
- Endpoint: api.redwoodinference.com

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Use TS SDK v2.8.0.
2) Send an invalid request that triggers a gateway/service 400 (e.g., missing required field or invalid parameter type).
3) Observe SDK retry loop (backoff) and multiple requests emitted.

Expected behavior:
- 400s should not be retried by default.
- The SDK should return a non-retryable, typed error and include request_id if present.

Actual behavior:
- In certain 400 responses, the retry middleware treats the failure as retryable and retries up to the default max attempts.
- Customer sees multiple request IDs (one per attempt).

Notes / hypotheses:
- The retry middleware appears to misclassify some 400 responses as “network errors” due to an exception during error body parsing (e.g., non-JSON error body or unexpected content-type). When parse fails, status is not propagated to the retry classifier.
- This is aligned with other parity findings: different SDKs handle “error parsing failure” differently; TS path can drop status_code and request_id.

Billing clarification (preliminary):
- Platform billing is token-based for successful generations/embeddings. 400 responses should not bill tokens; however, the customer may still see request counts and/or gateway logs that look like “multiple attempts”, and they may have internal metering tied to request volume.
- Independently of billing, duplicate attempts can create duplicate application side effects if the customer couples the API call to a non-idempotent operation.

Request IDs provided by customer (example set):
- rw_req_01HNTW9VZ9J2R3… (400)
- rw_req_01HNTW9W1P8K5A… (400)
- rw_req_01HNTW9W3F0M2C… (400)
(These were within one client action window; exact IDs stored in the private Zendesk attachment, not reproduced here.)

Ask:
- Confirm whether TS SDK is retrying 400s and under what conditions.
- Provide workaround to customer ASAP.
- Align with SDK parity initiative: retryable codes + typed error taxonomy + conformance tests to prevent regressions.
2026-01-29 09:18 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Acknowledged customer escalation. Asked for: TS SDK version, snippet showing retry config (if any), and 3 request_ids + approximate timestamps. Noted that SDK retries are expected on 429/5xx, but not on 400. Opened as P1 due to billing concern.

Shared immediate workaround: set maxRetries: 0 in client config until we confirm behavior.
2026-01-29 10:02 PT — Customer (Northwind AI) via support portal
Confirmed @redwood-ai/sdk 2.8.0, Node 18, running behind a corporate proxy. They see 3 attempts on a single call when the error is 400. They associate retries with possible double-charging because their internal cost dashboard counts requests. They asked whether Redwood bills for failed requests.

They provided logs showing three request IDs and identical payload hash.
2026-01-29 10:30 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Escalation Eng)
Pulled gateway logs for the provided request_id set. Confirmed: all three requests returned HTTP 400 with ~5–20 ms service time. No streaming involved. Response size small. Error body for at least one attempt was not JSON (content-type text/plain) due to an upstream validation error path.

Conclusion: the client truly sent 3 requests. Not a duplicate server-side processing artifact.
2026-01-29 11:15 PT — Ibrahim Khan (SDK TL) (internal note)
This matches a known parity issue: TS retry middleware can treat “failed to parse error response” as retryable because it throws before constructing the HttpError with status_code. If the retry classifier sees a generic error without status, it goes down the network-retry path. Need to ensure status is captured even if body parsing fails, and never retry 400.

Flagging Dana Lo to investigate in TS repo; also aligns with ENG-5126 error taxonomy work.
2026-01-29 13:05 PT — Dana Lo (TS SDK Owner)
Reproduced locally with v2.8.0:
- When error response is JSON, status=400 is preserved and shouldRetry=false.
- When error response is text/plain (or JSON parse throws), the SDK throws a generic error prior to wrapping it, so our retry middleware sees “unknown error” and retries.

Plan:
1) Refactor error parsing so we always preserve HTTP status + headers and build a typed error even when body parsing fails.
2) Tighten shouldRetry to require an explicit retryable classification (429/5xx/408/504 + network timeouts) rather than defaulting unknown errors to retry.
3) Add conformance coverage: 400 with non-JSON body must not retry.

ETA: patch release within a week; will link PR.
2026-01-29 14:10 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Responded to customer with billing clarification:
- Redwood does not bill tokens for requests that fail with 4xx before generation.
- They may see multiple request records because the client retried.

Provided mitigation until fix is released:
- Configure client retries off (maxRetries: 0) or restrict retryableStatusCodes to [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].
- Log request_id + retry_count for correlation.

Asked whether they rely on any side-effectful behavior tied to request submission; recommended idempotency keys where applicable (even though chat/embeddings are typically safe, their surrounding workflow might not be).
2026-01-31 16:42 PT — Dana Lo
Opened fix PR and requested review: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-1298-unify-retry-middleware-and-error-shapes.json
Key changes:
- Ensure HttpError is constructed even when response body parse fails.
- Attach status_code, request_id (if present), and retryable flag.
- Update retry classifier: do not retry when status_code is 400–499 (except 408/429), regardless of parse failures.

Also added tests for non-JSON 400 response body.
2026-02-02 09:05 PT — Allison Grant (SRE/Standards)
Reviewed retry classification against standard. Confirmed retryable defaults should include 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 + network errors/timeouts, and must not include 400. Requested one additional guard: if Retry-After is present on a 4xx that is not 429, ignore it for retries.

Suggested adding telemetry fields (retry_count, status_code, request_id) to align with the parity logging plan.
2026-02-03 11:20 PT — Dana Lo
Merged fix + follow-up for Retry-After parsing/jitter alignment: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-1307-retry-after-parsing-and-backoff-jitter.json
Cut release v2.8.2.
Release notes include: “Fix: do not retry HTTP 400 when error body parsing fails; improved typed errors with request_id + retryable flag.”
2026-02-03 12:00 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Informed customer of v2.8.2 and provided upgrade guidance + confirmation steps:
- Upgrade @redwood-ai/sdk to 2.8.2.
- Run a controlled invalid request; verify only one request_id appears and retry_count remains 0.
- Keep maxRetries: 0 in prod until upgrade completes.

Re-answered billing question: token billing not incurred for these 400s; if they need an invoice-level confirmation, we can route to finance but logs indicate no successful generations on those request_ids.
2026-02-06 15:37 PT — Customer (Northwind AI)
Upgraded to 2.8.2 in staging. Confirmed no retries on 400 anymore. Their internal request counter is now consistent. Asked for a short written statement they can share internally that 4xx validation failures do not incur token charges.

No further issues.
2026-02-10 10:12 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Provided final billing statement and closed ticket. Customer confirmed resolved in production after rollout.

Follow-ups:
- Ensure conformance suite covers “400 + non-JSON body” across SDKs.
- Ensure docs/migration notes mention the retry classifier change and how to tune maxRetries.
2026-02-10 10:20 PT — Ibrahim Khan (internal)
Logged as an input to SDK parity effort: this bug is a concrete example of why error taxonomy must preserve status_code/request_id even on parse failures. Will reference in parity matrix and conformance fixtures.
Resolved in TypeScript SDK v2.8.2 by ensuring HTTP status/request_id are preserved even when error-body parsing fails, and by tightening retry classification so 400 is never retried by default. Customer mitigated by disabling retries until upgrade. Billing concern addressed: 4xx validation failures did not incur token charges.
Customer upgraded to TS SDK v2.8.2; confirmed 400 responses are not retried and internal metering no longer shows duplicate attempts. Provided written clarification that 4xx validation errors do not incur token billing.
payload.summary: TypeScript SDK retries on HTTP 400 responses, causing duplicate request + billing concern

They require per-batch RFC3161 timestamps, per-event SHA-256 checksums, and a manifest signed using their BYOK KMS key (AWS KMS key alias: alias/citadel-byoj). Impact: regulatory audit must be submitted by 2026-03-18; missing or unverifiable handoff delays compliance filing. Environment: production tenant for citadel-health (tenant id: th-04512) in us-east-1. Acceptable alternatives include presigned S3 URL with time-limited access + signed manifest. Request includes sample mapping (.csv) of 10 representative events and full manifest for the slab. 5) Sign manifest metadata with customer's BYOK key (alias/citadel-byoj) via KMS signing workflow, and produce an overall slab-level checksum
6) Deliver slabs to customer SFTP and provide confirmation envelope with resume token and delivery receipt
7) Customer verifies checksums and RFC3161 timestamps; support to provide verification steps and sample verification script

payload.description:
Customer AtlasSearch reports repeated 429 responses across a subset of their interactive routes during a scheduled rolling credential refresh. Errors began shortly after a control-plane-initiated key rotation for ephemeral session tokens. Requests appear to be accepted by the gateway then rejected with 429 at the rate-limiter during refill windows for the priority (low-latency) lane.
Customer reports elevated error rates for live search and query-autocomplete endpoints affecting ~12% of interactive traffic during the rotation window. No data loss but increased user-facing failures and retries; customer SLAs at risk for the dedicated contract.
1) Use a dedicated tenant with priority and background lanes configured (priority weight 80, background 20).
2) Schedule a rolling credential refresh of ephemeral credentials across multiple edge ingress hosts.
3) Start 500 concurrent low-latency requests (chat/search) pinned to priority lane while background batch flushers run.
4) Observe transient 429s returned from /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings endpoints around the refresh windows.

Checked config: tenant had explicit priority-band isolation enabled and a small dedicated burst pool; burst pool shows no exhaustion but weight reallocation logs show 'temporary fallback' events during key refresh.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer DatumHealth reported that scheduled background workers that perform service-account impersonation are receiving 403 when calling Redwood admin APIs even though user SSO logins succeed and interactive admin sessions are fine. The failure started after DatumHealth upgraded their on-prem IdP to a patch that changed the SAML AuthnContext value from the short alias 'password' to the full URN 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:PasswordProtectedTransport'.

Impact:
- Several scheduled jobs that use a service-account flow to impersonate tenant admins are failing to obtain elevated calls to the admin API.
- Affects production region us-west for DatumHealth only (private deployment).
- Customer reports increased job error rate and downstream processing delay; business reports delayed patient record synces.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) in us-west region.
- Redwood runtime v1.24.2, auth-service v3.7.0, sso-adapter v2.4.1.
- DatumHealth IdP: OnPremSAML v5.2.4 -> upgraded to v5.2.5 prior to incident.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure IdP to emit AuthnContextClassRef as the full URN (urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:PasswordProtectedTransport).
2) Trigger service-account token exchange: service -> POST /v1/admin/impersonate with SAML assertion to the token-exchange endpoint.
3) Observe token-exchange response from auth-service and follow-up admin API call.

Observed behavior:
- Token-exchange returns 200 OK and issues a session token, but the subsequent admin API call returns 403 Forbidden with RBAC deny: "role_resolution_failed: authn_context_mismatch" in the authz logs.
- Support logs show assertion parsed successfully but our internal claim 'authn_context' equals the full URN; RBAC layer has a strict equality check against configured alias 'password' for impersonation grant.
- Edge logs sample:
  auth-service[login] INFO assertion parsed subject=svc-scheduler@datumhealth tenant=datumhealth
  authz[rbac] WARN role_resolution_failed subject=svc-scheduler reason=authn_context_mismatch got="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:PasswordProtectedTransport" expected="password"

Expected behavior:
- Impersonation should succeed as long as the equivalent AuthnContext class is provided by IdP, regardless of aliasing or URN form.

Initial investigation notes:
- Confirmed with DatumHealth that only the AuthnContext value changed during their IdP upgrade.
- We parse AuthnContextClassRef verbatim and store in claim authn_context. RBAC impersonation rule uses a tenant-configured value 'authn_context_alias' that historically has been 'password' (short form).
- Our service did not include normalization logic to map known URNs to aliases, which previously worked because most IdPs sent the short alias.
- Determined that the token-exchange flow and assertion verification are otherwise successful; the deny occurs at role resolution where we match allowed_authn_context == authn_context_claim.

Temporary workarounds provided to customer:
- DatumHealth reverted IdP to send the short alias 'password' (config change) — immediate mitigation.
- Alternatively, configured an Assertion Transform rule on their IdP to rewrite AuthnContext to 'password'.

Root cause:
- Strict string equality check for authn_context in RBAC role resolution. No canonicalization or known-URN whitelist applied. Recent IdP update started emitting the URN form which is semantically equivalent but failed the equality check.

Fix implemented:
- Auth-service patch: add AuthnContext normalization layer that maps well-known URNs to canonical aliases (e.g., URN PasswordProtectedTransport -> 'password'). Implemented a tolerant matching fallback that checks last path segment of URN if exact match fails.
- Configurable tenant override: allow tenant admins to define additional acceptable authn_context values per impersonation-role in tenant RBAC config.
- Unit and integration tests added to cover URN and alias variants.
- Backport: hotfix rolled to v3.7.1 for auth-service in private control plane.

Rollout / mitigation:
- Hotfix deployed to customer's private control plane on 2026-03-11 02:15 UTC.
- Verified scheduled jobs resumed and 403s dropped to zero.
- Customer kept an IdP assertion-transform disabled after verifying fix.

Follow-up actions / docs:
- Documentation update: 'AuthnContext compatibility and recommended mappings' page added to ops runbook.
- Enhancements: introduce fuzzy matching preferences and log sampling to surface future authn-context mismatches more clearly in Console.

Attachments:
- Redacted authz logs, assertion samples, and correlation IDs were uploaded to the ticket.

Lena Morales (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer opened ticket after noticing scheduled job failures after IdP upgrade. Assigned to auth on-call.
Arjun Patel (Auth Eng) 2026-03-10: Reproduced locally by sending URN AuthnContext, observed RBAC deny at role resolution. Hypothesis: equality check against alias. Will prototype normalization patch.
DatumHealth (Customer) 2026-03-11: Confirmed reverting IdP to send 'password' restored jobs; will keep reverted until fix applied. Provided assertion sample and upgrade notes.
Arjun Patel (Auth Eng) 2026-03-11: Deployed hotfix v3.7.1 to the customer's control plane at 02:15 UTC. Monitored job queue for 3 hours. No recurrence observed. Patching changelog: add authncontext normalization and tenant override support.
PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1268

Lena Morales (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer confirmed tasks completed and asked for closure. Documentation link provided. Closing ticket.
Hotfix deployed (auth-service v3.7.1) that normalizes SAML AuthnContext values and adds tenant-configurable accepted values; customer reverted IdP temporarily and verified fix; docs updated.
payload.summary: SAML AuthnContext URN vs alias mismatch prevents service-account impersonation in private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent gRPC stream disconnects (server-initiated RST / RESET) for long-polling requests from private deployment when traffic routes through their corporate TLS-inspecting forward proxy.

Impact: Production streaming endpoints drop ~3-10% of user sessions during business hours; affects inference continuity for chat features. Customer sees elevated error rates and has paused canary rollout.

Environment: Private deployment in customer VPC (FinLite) peered to Redwood control plane. Egress via corporate forward proxy (explicit HTTP CONNECT) performing TLS interception and ALPN rewriting. Client SDK uses HTTP/2 over TLS to connect to Redwood ingress (grpc).

Steps to reproduce:
1) From customer app hosts behind corporate proxy, establish streaming gRPC call to Redwood endpoint with keepalive enabled (interval 20s).
2) Let stream remain idle >90s, then send prompt.
3) Observe server-side reset and client gRPC error UNAVAILABLE / HTTP/2 GOAWAY in logs.

Observed behaviour: Streams terminate with HTTP/2 GOAWAY or RST_STREAM; connection resets coincide with proxy idle timer and rewritten ALPN tokens. TCP remain open but HTTP/2 layer fails to negotiate. No client TLS certificate issues.

Expected behaviour: Long-lived gRPC streams should survive through proxy with transparent CONNECT and keepalive preserved; graceful keepalive probes should be proxied and not trigger shutdown.

Relevant logs/observations:
- Customer tcpdump: repeated TLS renegotiation attempts and ALPN advertised as "http/1.1" after proxy re-write.
- Redwood ingress (nginx sidecar) logs: proto negotiation mismatch: expected h2, got h1 upgrades; recorded GOAWAY with code NO_ERROR immediately prior to user-facing error.
- Packet capture shows proxy injecting TLS payload inspection frames and altering ALPN list.
- No model pull errors; only streaming termination.

Attachments: customer-provided pcap (s3 link), proxy config snippet, ingress logs excerpt.
Initial hypothesis: corporate proxy is rewriting TLS ClientHello ALPN during re-key/idle timeout, causing mismatch when ingress expects h2. Alternative hypothesis: keepalive probes are converted to HTTP/1.1 pings by proxy, causing nginx to signal GOAWAY.

Actions taken:
- Reproduced failure in staging with a simulated forward proxy that rewrites ALPN -> reproduced GOAWAY within 2 minutes.
- Verified Redwood ingress accepts HTTP/2 and honours ALPN; when ALPN changed mid-connection, HTTP/2 is torn down.
- Captured tcpdump on customer-host and ingress; confirmed proxy inserts TLS rewrap and advertises only http/1.1 in rekey handshake.
- Tested forcing HTTP/1.1 fallback: client switched to HTTP/1.1 and resumed unary calls (non-streaming), but streaming unavailable.

Temporary mitigation identified: configure SDK to enable HTTP/1.1 fallback for non-streaming paths, and/or set proxy to preserve ALPN/h2 in TLS rewrap. Longer-term: document proxy configuration requirements and add health-checkable header to detect ALPN rewriting and auto-failover.

Open questions:
- Can we detect ALPN rewrite at connection start and present actionable error to customer?
- Should we implement a graceful downgrade path that proxies streaming over websocket when h2 unavailable?

Next steps assigned to SRE and SDK teams.
[2026-03-13 09:12] Support (Jordan Patel): Logged initial ticket after customer call. Attached pcap and proxy config. Requesting SRE assist  suspect TLS rewrap.
[2026-03-13 11:03] SRE (Miguel Santos): Reproduced in staging with mitmproxy configured to strip h2 ALPN. Confirmed GOAWAY from ingress. Adding ingress-side logging to show ALPN on accept.
[2026-03-13 14:45] Customer (FinOps Lead - Emily Chen): We've pushed a proxy change earlier this week; can revert to previous image to test. Will try overnight and report.
[2026-03-14 07:31] Support (Aisha Nguyen): Customer reverted proxy config; observed connection stabilised in limited test. Requesting formal workaround and guidance for permanent fix.
[2026-03-14 10:05] SDK (Lara Kim): Adding feature request to SDK to surface explicit ALPN mismatch warning and automatic websocket streaming fallback. Filed PR referenced above.
Workaround: Customer reverted proxy TLS rewrap policy to preserve ALPN and increased proxy idle timeout to 15 minutes. This reduced streaming disconnects to <0.1% during monitoring window.

Permanent fix / follow-up:
- SRE to publish runbook on ALPN preservation for corporate forward proxies (confluence link included).
- SDK team to prototype websocket fallback for streaming clients where ALPN/h2 unavailable.
- Add detection logic in ingress to log ALPN mismatch and return a clear error (400 with guidance) instead of silent GOAWAY.

Status: Mitigation applied by customer; monitoring continues for 72 hours. Owner for follow-up: Aisha Nguyen (Support) / Miguel Santos (SRE) / Lara Kim (SDK).
payload.summary: gRPC long-poll disconnects behind corporate TLS-inspecting forward proxy on private deployment

Issue summary:
Customer BrightLearn Inc. reports a promotional waiver (30% overage credit, promo code: SPRINGENTERPRISE-30) intended to offset a disputed overage on the invoice for the current billing cycle (INV-2026-03-BLE-7301). Instead, the waiver line appeared as a provisional credit scheduled for the next invoice period, resulting in a short-term overcharge and an autopay failure for the current cycle.

Impact:
- Immediate financial impact: customer account temporarily charged $12,345.67 more than expected; autopay attempted and failed, triggering billing alerts.
- Business impact: customer procurement flagged the charge and paused integrations until billing is corrected.
- Affects BrightLearn production inference workloads in us-east and eu-west.

Environment:
- Tier: enterprise (dedicated GPU pool)
- Regions: us-east primary, eu-west fallback
- Components implicated: billing postback pipeline, dedicated-fallback routing logic, invoice finalization job

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1. BrightLearn performed a capacity-heavy training-inference burst on 2026-03-02 that exceeded reserved buffer on us-east.
2. Traffic routed to eu-west dedicated fallback for a 1.5-hour window (03:12–04:42 UTC).
3. BrightLearn submitted billing support request for promo waiver (SPRINGENTERPRISE-30) on 2026-03-04 referencing the current invoice.
4. On invoice finalization (2026-03-05), billing shows the overage charge applied; the promo waiver did not offset the current invoice but shows a provisional credit pending for the next billing cycle.

Observed behavior:
- Waiver appears in billing ledger as a provisional credit with effective_period starting 2026-04-01.
- Postback logs show waiver acceptance event processed at 2026-03-04T18:23:47Z but linked to a future period idempotency key.
- Autopay attempted on 2026-03-06 and failed due to mismatch between expected balance and posted charges.

Expected behavior:
- Waiver requested and accepted before invoice finalization should be applied to the current open invoice and reduce the total due immediately.

Attachments / Logs:
- Customer provided invoice PDF (INV-2026-03-BLE-7301.pdf) and billing support request email thread.
- Extracts from postback-processing logs attached to the ticket (postback-2026-03-04.log).

Additional notes:
2026-03-09 11:10 - SRE (Harper Singh): Found that dedicated-fallback window overlapped with a scheduled pricing migration job that ran at 03:00 UTC on 2026-03-02. Suspecting race between pricing-tag-update and postback assignment. Pulling logs from routing service.
Initial hypothesis: postback-reconciler attached waiver to billing period based on pricing_tag at time of ingestion. The dedicated-fallback caused a pricing tag refresh which flipped period mapping for in-flight postbacks.
Confirmed: postback-2026-03-04.log shows promo_accept event with idempotency_key=promo-BLE-20260304-0xa7 and assigned billing_period_id=2026-04 (future) instead of open period 2026-03. Event ingestion timestamp is 2026-03-04T18:23:47Z. Pricing-tag-change event logged at 2026-03-04T18:23:11Z during a reconciliation retry window.
Reproducer: running reconciler locally with identical sequence of pricing-tag-update + ingestion reproduces wrong assignment when reconciler processes pricing snapshot older than realtime routing snapshot.
Edge condition: dedicated-fallback routing emits region_override that caused postback pipeline to recalculate period using region-local timezone rounding logic. This interacts poorly with cross-region pricing tag migration that was in-progress.
Temporary mitigation implemented: manual invoice credit and adjustment to autopay; added compensating rule to reconciler to treat promo acceptances before invoice_finalization_ts as current-period credits if customer explicitly requested current-cycle application.
Permanent fix planned: PR #2012 updates idempotency key generation to include invoice_period_candidate and forces reconciliation to use invoice_finalization_cutoff when evaluating promos. QA + canary scheduled for 2026-03-15.
2026-03-12 - Temporary workaround: Applied manual adjustment of $12,345.67 to INV-2026-03-BLE-7301 and retried autopay; autopay succeeded on 2026-03-12T10:52Z.
2026-03-12 - Customer notified and provided written confirmation of credit and refund timeline. Customer accepted workaround and requested PM follow-up to avoid recurrence.
2026-03-15 - Planned permanent fix: Merge PR #2012, run reconciliation job with new idempotency behavior, and monitor next invoice finalization for similar customers who had region/fallback overlap during promo windows.
Postmortem items: add test case for pricing-tag migrations during postback ingestion, instrument metric for 'promo_applied_period_mismatch', and update runbook to escalate any autopay failures for enterprise customers immediately.
