payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports opaque 429s from batch import jobs that run intermittently (10–20 RPS bursts for ~30s every 10 minutes). Console shows available burst credits and per-route quota sufficient, but requests are being rejected at the edge with 429s.

Impact: Several import jobs fail mid-window; retries are escalated into large backoff waves and increase job completion time from minutes to hours. Affects one enterprise dedicated tenant during nightly processing.

Environment: dedicated deployment, prod-us-west, private VPC peering to customer ingress. Model: redwood/gpt-medium-v1.

Observed behavior: Customer sees 429 responses from edge-proxy with header X-RateLimit-Reason: window-exhausted. Console credit graph does not decrement corresponding to the rejections and shows available credits. Edge logs show short refill interval (5s) while control plane policy is configured for 60s refill.

Expected behavior: Console and edge should agree on refill interval and token accounting so that transient low-frequency bursts are absorbed by burst credits and not prematurely rejected.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use a single API key tied to the customer's dedicated pool.
2) Post a burst of 12 concurrent embedding/generation calls (short payloads) for ~25s, spaced every 10 minutes.
3) Observe 429 responses from the edge after ~18–22s into the burst for ~8–12s windows.
4) Check console quota UI and timing; console shows credits still available.

Logs / excerpts:
EDGE LOG: [2026-03-10T03:12:22Z] conn=28 path=/v1/generate key=cus-XXX status=429 reason=window-exhausted refill_interval=5s
CONTROL PLANE POLICY: tenant_refill_interval=60s policy_version=v3.4.2
CONSOLE: burst_credits_available=1200 last_refill=2026-03-10T03:11:00Z

Authenticate with the tenant's API key
Trigger 12 concurrent short generation/embedding requests for ~25s
Observe 429s surfaced from the edge at ~20s into burst
Compare console burst_credits and edge logs for refill_interval and reason header
Initial hypothesis: edge-proxy config drift after a recent hotfix left a legacy refill schedule (5s) active on the edge nodes while the control plane operates on 60s windows. This creates misaligned token buckets where edge depletes local window tokens faster and returns 429s without consulting the central burst pool. Correlated with a deploy on 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC that updated edge-side rate-limiter binary to 1.8.1-hotfix.

What we've checked so far:
- Pulled edge-proxy config from a sample node; refill_interval=5000ms found (should be 60000ms).
- Console policy in DB shows correct 60s setting.
- No tenant-level rate-rule overrides in console.
- Replayed traffic in staging with aligned windows reproduces no 429s.

Next steps: coordinate with infra to push corrected edge config or rollback the hotfix; add a one-off metric to count edge-vs-control refill_interval mismatch; examine if stale config can survive node restarts or requires a rolling restart.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:30 - Customer (CloudScale Analytics): Able to pause and shift job schedule. They reported business impact as delayed analytics but no data loss. Asked whether this will impact other tenants sharing same edge cluster.
2026-03-12 08:05 - Support (Aisha Khan): Followed up with the customer, suggested gradual job resume and recommended client-side exponential backoff with jitter as interim. Customer asked for confirmation that billing/credit counts will be reconciled; escalated to Billing (linked SUP-71234).
In Progress: SRE rolled back the edge hotfix override by updating EDGE_REFILL_MS and performing staged restarts; affected edge nodes now match control plane policy. Temporary mitigation: customer paused scheduled retries and resumed at lower concurrency. Follow-up action: add automated config drift alert and add an end-to-end test that exercises refill sync between control plane and edge on deploys. Billing reconciliation request opened (SUP-71234).
Pause high-frequency retries and resume imports at lower concurrency (<=6 concurrent connections) until edge nodes confirm correct refill interval. Implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter to avoid synchronized retry waves.
Add CI gating test to validate EDGE_REFILL_MS parity with control-plane policy on deploy
Create an alert when edge-config-refill != control-plane-refill for any tenant
Coordinate with Billing to reconcile perceived credit consumption (SUP-71234)

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent diversion of requests away from a tenant-pinned model to a fallback variant during the nightly canary health probe window. Impact: ~3-7% of requests for the tenant observed returning responses from the unpinned variant for ~30-90s intervals, causing subtle output differences and an increase in quality alerts. Environment: prod/us-east, Dedicated cluster (enterprise plan).

Observed behaviour: During the automated canary health probe window (03:00-03:10 UTC), some sessions bound to the tenant's pinned model temporarily route to the canary variant. This occurs without the tenant changing any pins or routes. The issue began on 2026-03-09 after a routine canary rollout for the redwood-open-7b-v2 family.

Expected behaviour: Tenant sessions pinned to a specific model/version should maintain affinity and continue to route to that pinned model except for explicit failover conditions (unhealthy instance, capacity exhaustion, or manual override).

Steps to reproduce (customer): 1) Tenant sends steady requests with session token/tenant header to prod endpoint in us-east. 2) Wait for scheduled canary health probe period. 3) Observe 200 responses signed by fallback model (version mismatch in response metadata) while pin remains configured in tenant settings.

Key logs and traces (sanitized): - edge-proxy: cookie-lease refresh at 03:02:14 from health-probe service, set Path=/, Domain=redwood.ai, SameSite=None
- routing-agent: route-resolve[pinned-token=tenant-abc] -> target=canary-redwood-open-7b-v2-20260309-1 at 03:02:15 (decision reason: probe-priority-preempt=true)
- serving-runtime: kv-cache-miss for session-lease token at 03:02:15
- api-gateway: x-tenant-pin header present in request, value=redwood-open-7b-v2@2026-03-08

Customer impact notes: Output variance triggered quality monitors; customer paused a subset of production traf fic and opened this ticket. No data leakage or model-execution errors observed, only routing divergence and output semantics differences.

Hypotheses so far: 1) Health-probe traffic (internal service) is being prioritized by the canary coordinator and temporarily preempts pin reconciliation for overlapping session tokens. 2) Edge cookie/lease refresh from the health-probe modifies affinity state, causing the edge to consider the session ephemeral and eligible for canary routing. 3) A race between the pin-coherence reconciler and canary weight adjuster leaves a short window where fallback policy (probe-priority-preempt) takes precedence.

Initial investigation steps performed: - Verified tenant pin configuration and pin TTLs remain unchanged. - Pulled routing decision logs and correlation IDs for affected requests (samples attached in comments). - Replayed probe traffic in staging with header mutation reproduces diversion consistently when cookie-lease refresh happens immediately before request. - Checked autoscaler and capacity metrics: no GPU shortage or eviction events during windows. - Reviewed recent canary coordinator PRs — two merged changes adjust probe preemption thresholds (PR referenced above).

Immediate mitigations applied: - Disabled probe-priority-preempt for the affected rollout in us-east (temporary guardrail). - Added conservative pin-coherence backoff to delay canary weight shift until existing session leases reconcile (hotfix patch deployed to canary coordinator).

Next steps: - SRE to run additional long-tail tests for cookie-lease refresh + probe timing across region. - Engineering to instrument pin-reconcile latency metrics and add a metric-level alert. - Rework canary coordinator policy to respect pinned-session affinity until TTL expiry unless explicit unhealthy condition is present. - Customer success to monitor customer quality alerts and confirm reduction in diverted requests.
2026-03-10 12:15 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer first reported ~4% of requests returning unpinned model output during the 03:00 canary window. Provided initial logs and sample response IDs.
2026-03-10 12:42 - Eng (Arjun Patel): Pulled routing logs; saw routing-agent decision reason 'probe-priority-preempt'. Tentatively reproduced in staging by replaying health-probe cookie refresh. Opening a hotfix on canary coordinator to disable preemptive probe routing in target region.
2026-03-10 13:10 - SRE (Lina Gomez): Confirmed no capacity issues or GPU evictions. Edge cookie-lease refreshes from internal health-probe service appear in ~2.2% of session windows during canary. Also saw KV-cache misses for those sessions at the time of diversion.
2026-03-10 15:05 - Eng (Arjun Patel): Deployed guardrail disabling probe-priority-preempt to us-east canary jobs. Observed a drop in diversion events in the first two windows post-deploy (samples attached). Keeping monitor active for 72h before re-enabling a revised policy.
2026-03-11 09:20 - Customer (BrightData AI - S. Rao): Thanks for rapid response. We saw the percentage of diverted responses drop to <0.2% last night. We'll keep monitors and report if anything recurs.
2026-03-12 10:00 - Eng (Arjun Patel): Creating a follow-up engineering task to change canary coordinator logic: require explicit health/unhealthy signals (not probe-only) before preempting pinned sessions. ETA for design + PR: 2026-03-19. Linking internal design doc in related_confluence_pages.

Issue summary: Customer reports repeated drops in throughput and elevated p99 latency for their reserved pool between ~11:30-12:15 UTC on weekdays. The effect is transient (10-40m) and correlates with sudden GPU slot exhaustion. Impact: Noteable Analytics observed ~70% drop in sustained throughput for their model routes and increased 5xx rate for batched routes. Business impact: realtime inference pipelines degrade; internal SLAs at risk. Environment: Dedicated capacity (reserved pool rsv-3492) in us-east-1. Observed across multiple models pinned in the pool.

Observations:
- Starts as a spike of many short-lived streaming sessions (0.5-2s) from a small set of tenant API keys.
- Slot allocation logs show rapid allocate/deallocate churn and ephemeral batch sizes of 1.
- Autoscaler reacts by reducing scale (interpreting churn as idle), then later ramps back, creating a sawtooth in capacity and causing p99 spikes.

Initial ask: Customer requested explanation and a short-term mitigation to avoid further SLA breaches.
Monitor dedicated pool rsv-3492 during a weekday midday window (11:00-13:00 UTC).
Replay small-stream traffic generator that opens 200-500 very short streams (0.5-2s) distributed across many keys at t=0.
Observe slot allocation churn in scheduler logs and p99 latency in console dashboard for affected routes.
Verify autoscaler decision logs for scale-down events immediately after the burst.
scheduler.log lines (us-east-1, rsv-3492): 'slot_alloc: tenant=noteable-123 request_id=... slot=12 allocated; duration=0.8s; dealloc'.
autoscaler.log sample: 'policy=utilization_smoothing window=60s observed_util=0.12 -> scale_down target_replicas=2 -> execute'.
serving-runtime: 'batcher: created batch size=1 repeated 430 times in 300s; kv-cache hit rate stable'.
console trace: 'p99 err rate increase from 180ms -> 2.1s at 11:37 UTC; throughput drop 68%'.
11-Mar: Confirmed burst source is internal to customer (tenant keys). Customer later confirmed recently enabled an internal health-checker for their fleet that opens short streaming probes every minute across many endpoints.
11-Mar: Identified autoscaler smoothing misinterpreting high churn as low utilization because of short-lived connections; scaling policy uses 60s window and min_replicas=1 for this pool, allowing undersize after a scale-down.
11-Mar: Observed GPU slot fragmentation: ephemeral streams prevented effective batching, causing increased per-token overhead and reduced GPU throughput efficiency.
12-Mar: Correlated with sidecar heartbeats — sidecars that attach to user streams were triggering prefetches and then immediately releasing, magnifying slot churn.
Hypothesis: Short, high-concurrency probes from the customer's health-check flood the scheduler with allocation requests, causing slot exhaustion and triggering hysteresis in autoscaler decisions.
Mitigation applied (12-Mar): Added temporary tenant-level filter in serving-gateway to reject requests with health-check user-agent pattern 'NoteableHC/1.0' and return 204; this immediately stabilized the pool and restored baseline throughput.
Hotfix PR merged (infra#4821) to increase autoscaler min_replicas to 3 for this reserved pool and to lengthen utilization smoothing window from 60s -> 120s for pools with high short-stream variance.
Follow-up tasks created: implement explicit per-tenant short-stream quota and add metric 'short_stream_rate' to the console; runbook updated to include guidance on blocking synthetic probes in dedicated pools.
Customer action: Noteable Analytics will move internal health-checks to a low-priority route on a separate non-dedicated project and will throttle probe concurrency pending long-term configs.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged and escalated to SRE. Asked customer for timeframe and traffic samples.
Noteable Ops (customer) 2026-03-10: Provided pcap and list of internal health-check IPs. Confirmed they rolled out a new probe last week.
Diego Ramos (SRE) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with traffic generator; confirmed autoscaler incorrectly dropping replicas after burst. Linked infra PR to adjust smoothing. (See github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821).
Ava Patel (Platform) 2026-03-12: Deployed tenant filter as hotfix and monitored for 45 minutes; p99 returned to baseline. Advising follow-up telemetry and stricter short-stream quotas.
Finalize and deploy autoscaler config changes to all dedicated pools with similar usage patterns (scheduled 2026-03-15).
Ship per-tenant short-stream quota enforcement and a UI toggle for customers to mark synthetic traffic (Q2 work).
Work with customer to validate their probe redesign and confirm no residual failures for one week before closing ticket.
Create alert: 'short_stream_rate > 200/s for 5m' -> page SRE and notify support.
payload.summary: Intermittent p99 throughput collapse during midday caused by bursty internal health-checks exhausting dedicated slots

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403s for admin and scheduled worker calls immediately after we rotated ingress nodes for their private deployment. Failures correlate with users hitting the identity provider single-logout (SLO) endpoint during or shortly after the rotation. Some sessions appear to be orphaned and cannot be rehydrated, requiring the user to fully reauthenticate.

Impact:
- Multiple Finterra engineers observed 403s on console and API calls for ~7–12 minutes after the ingress rotation window.
- Two scheduled background workers failed retries due to auth failures and missed one data sync job.
- Potentially blocks admin tasks until manual reauth for affected users.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed ingress) behind our private control plane.
- Region: prod/us-east (customer's VPC peering).
- Auth flow: SAML SSO with the customer's IdP (Okta) configured for both SSO and SLO endpoints.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1. Rotate ingress (kubectl cordon/drain + replace node pool) during quiet window.
2. IdP SLO webhook is invoked as existing sessions are terminated by the ingress.
3. Some requests arrive at new ingress nodes where auth-proxy has an empty/inconsistent session cache and triggers an SLO confirmation flow.
4. Subsequent API calls return 403 with X-Auth-Reason: session-orphaned or missing-assertion.

Observed behavior:
- 403 responses include trace-id and auth-proxy logs showing 404 to local session lookup and a follow-up POST to IdP SLO endpoint that times out or returns 200 without the expected sessionid payload.
- Session-store metrics show transient spike in cache-misses and a later burst of full-session creations.

Expected behavior:
- Ingress rotation should not trigger session invalidation across nodes; SLO calls must be correlated to the originating session and not create orphaned state.

Logs / Traces (redacted):
- auth-proxy: "session-lookup: key not found: s-7a3b2f, falling back to idp-slo: invoked"
- idp-slo: "POST /slo callback 200 OK (body empty) - missing session_ref header"
- session-store (redis): "GET s-7a3b2f -> nil; SET s-7a3b2f ..."
- ingest trace-ids: us-east-ingress-rot-2026-03-10T03:22Z

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Avoid performing ingress node rotations during high-idle windows until we deploy fix.
- Manual re-auth: users can clear affected sessions by logging out via the console and re-initiating SSO; we've provided a script to delete local session keys for affected workers.

Next steps requested:
- Investigate correlation between ingress lifecycle hooks and auth-proxy session cache invalidation.
- Add guard to ignore idp-slo callbacks that do not include a valid session_ref header.
- Add automated retry/backoff for idp-slo handler and fallback path to gracefully force a reauth without returning 403 in the intermediate window.
Timeline: 2026-03-10 03:15 — ingress rotation started by customer ops. 03:22 — first 403 reported to support. 03:24 — our SRE reproduced by cordoning one ingress node in staging with identical auth-proxy configuration. Root cause hypothesis: ingress node drains trigger connection termination that causes the IdP to receive SLO messages for sessions that are simultaneously being migrated; new ingress instances' auth-proxy instances have a cold cache and no way to reconcile an in-flight SLO callback that lacks session context.

Findings:
- auth-proxy expects SLO callbacks to include session_ref; some SLO payloads from the customer's IdP are missing the session_ref when logout was initiated via front-proxy connection termination.
- session-store TTLs are short (30s) for in-flight handoff path; during rotation, TTL expiry plus missing session_ref leads to orphaned requests.
- Race identified: idp-slo callback processed before session replication completes across stores during node failover.

Reproduced in staging with scripted ingress drain and simultaneous IdP SLO POSTs.

Hypotheses considered and rejected:
- Network MTU or proxy truncation causing missing session_ref: logs show full SLO payloads when routed directly.
- IdP misconfiguration: Okta team confirms SLO payloads include session_ref when initiated from UI; missing only during abrupt TCP connection terminations.

Action items created:
- Add session_ref validation and Nack/Retry to idp-slo handler (ENG-4721).
- Increase session replication window on session-store to 2m for private deployments (OPS-3821).
- Harden ingress drain lifecycle to wait for auth-proxy graceful shutdown (DEPLOY-2198).

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:02 - SRE Lead (Aisha Khan): Deployed short-term config change to increase session replication window to reduce race probability for Finterra. Monitoring for recurrence.
Workaround documented and temporary session replication window increase applied on 2026-03-11. Engineering implemented idp-slo handler changes to validate session_ref and return 202+retry when session context is not found; deployed to staging and merged to main on 2026-03-12. Planned canary for Finterra private deployment on 2026-03-13 morning. Postmortem to include changes to ingress drain lifecycle and session replication defaults for private customers.
payload.summary: IDP SLO race condition after ingress node rotation leaves orphaned sessions and intermittent 403s

Issue summary: Customer reports that after an intermittent network disconnect, SSE streams resume but the first resumed payloads are half-formed JSON fragments and the client parser fails. Impact: Several NexaHealth production workflows ingesting streamed clinical summaries are producing invalid partial objects; customer reports ~15% of resumed sessions encounter parse errors and drops. Environment: prod, us-east, edge-proxy path through third-party CDN probe that occasionally inserts synthetic TCP probe packets. Observed behavior: On reconnect the server sends a resumed chunk that starts mid-UTF8 sequence and omits the JSON array opener; client logs "JSON parse error: unexpected token". Expected behavior: Stream resume should deliver complete, well-delimited framing and finalization events so clients can stitch without parse errors. Business impact: High — downstream ingestion pipeline discards incomplete records, causing missing clinical notes in processing.

Initial customer-provided details: NexaHealth observed issue at approx 2026-03-13T20:12:34Z during a regional CDN reroute. They captured client-side SDK logs and network capture showing a tiny probe RST/ACK/half-close followed by resumed SSE payloads with missing leading bytes.

Required next steps: Confirm whether edge-probe or load balancer is splitting TCP segments or injecting probes that cause the serving runtime's resume framing to emit a partial fragment; reproduce with controlled probe injection; add defensive guarding in the server resume path to ensure framing re-sync before emitting resumed payloads.
1) Use NexaHealth production-like SSE client with auto-reconnect enabled and streaming enabled for model meta-llama-2-7b
2) Simulate network probe/hard-close from edge (TCP RST then immediate reconnect) or use a test CDN that injects health probes during an open connection
3) Allow client to reconnect and request resume token (client SDK send last-offset header)
4) Observe first resumed chunks emitted by the API and attempt to parse as JSON array of choices
5) Compare capture to baseline where reconnect occurs without edge probe injection
2026-03-13T20:12:34.112Z EDGE-PROXY INFO conn-id=abc123 probe: injected keepalive sequence
2026-03-13T20:12:34.115Z API-GW DEBUG resume_token=tok_9b8k resume_offset=4821 sending resumed-chunk bytes=128
2026-03-13T20:12:34.116Z SERVING-RUNTIME WARN resume: detected non-delimited-prefix, emitting chunk (len=96)
client-sdk: 2026-03-13T20:12:34.118Z ERROR JSON parse error at byte 0: unexpected token '\u00E2' (partial UTF-8)
Support triage: reproduced with lab harness by toggling kube-proxy socket keepalive causing half-close during SSE. Repro rate in lab ~20% when small probe inserted within a 10ms window.
SRE checked edge proxy logs and saw probe pattern matching third-party CDN health check (Path: /probe/health) correlated with symptom windows.
Serving runtime analysis: resume path currently trusts resume_offset and replays buffered bytes without an explicit framing resync; if TCP segment boundary aligns inside a UTF-8 multi-byte char or JSON token, client-side parser fails.
Hypothesis: The edge probe triggers a half-close that causes client reconnection path to request resume with an offset that points mid-symbol; server replays from that offset producing a chunk that is not aligned to logical framing boundaries.
Temporary mitigation tested: adding a small defensive resync on server (scan back up to 8 bytes for JSON array opener '[' or '{"') reduces parse errors to <1% in lab without further infra changes.
Repro notes: issue reproduced on both SSE and websocket fallback with binary frames when probe occurred at same timing window. Browser clients are more forgiving due to internal buffering; embedded SDKs fail more often.
Support (2026-03-13 21:02) - Ava Chen: Logged initial ticket after receiving NexusHealth incident report and analyst captures. Customer provided client SDK logs and pcap. Marked P1 due to data loss.
SRE (2026-03-13 22:10) - Priya Singh: Confirmed CDN probe pattern in edge logs. Captured server-side resume offset and observed chunk starting with 0xE2 (mid UTF-8). Hypothesis: resume offset pointing mid-codepoint. Requesting runtime team to review resume semantics.
Runtime Eng (2026-03-14 09:35) - Diego Marquez: Added local patch that scans backward from resume_offset up to 16 bytes to align to a valid UTF-8 boundary and to nearest JSON delimiter when feasible. Lab validation shows significant improvement. Preparing PR for serving-runtime.
Customer (2026-03-14 11:12) - NexaHealth Oncall (M. Jacobs): Confirmed that the mitigation reduced errors in their staging 12h soak. Requesting ETA for hotfix in prod and whether there is an edge configuration to avoid probes during active connections.
SRE (2026-03-14 13:00) - Priya Singh: Reached out to CDN support rep to ask about probe window settings; CDN acknowledged probes can be configured but requires change window and impact assessment. Escalating to account team.
Support (2026-03-14 15:20) - Ava Chen: Noted customer's appetite for a coordinated rollout: runtime hotfix + CDN probe config change. Scheduling maintenance window proposal.
Runtime Eng (2026-03-14 16:45) - Diego Marquez: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2892 includes defensive resync logic and unit tests covering UTF-8 boundary alignment and JSON delimiter resync. Marked for expedited review.
Workaround applied: enabled defensive resume resync in canary (serving-runtime v1.32.4-canary) which scans backward up to 16 bytes from resume_offset to align to valid UTF-8 and a JSON structural marker. Customer validated staging; errors dropped from ~15% to <1%. Permanent fix path: merge PR 2892, run canary across two us-east clusters, then promote to prod in maintenance window coordinated with CDN probe configuration change to avoid probe injection during long-lived streams.
Merge and deploy PR 2892 to prod canary cluster (assigned to Diego Marquez)
Coordinate with NexaHealth and CDN provider to shift probe timing/config for their traffic (assigned to Priya Singh)
Add unit/integration test that injects probe mid-stream and validates resume alignment (assigned to Runtime QA)
Document resume resync behavior in runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/streaming-reconnect-troubleshooting (assigned to Support)
Monitor production for 72h post-rollout; add a dashboard showing resume_parse_errors by region and model (assigned to Observability)

comments: 2026-03-13T18:30:00Z Aisha Patel: Acknowledged. Opening incident and escalated to SRE. Assigned Liam for investigation.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that during long streaming sessions (SSE) the client receives rapid duplicate heartbeat events ("heartbeat" event payload repeated), followed immediately by an extended silence where the final metadata/event that signals completion never arrives. The client SDK (atlashealth-web-sdk v2.1.3) treats the duplicate heartbeat as an idempotent keepalive but then drops into a reconnection backoff when no further framed events arrive, resulting in a missing final_chunk metadata and incomplete conversation state in the customer app.

Impact:
- Several AtlasHealth users see generated responses missing the final summary paragraph and end-of-stream metadata (conversation_id and token_count).
- Partial responses appear in the UI; customer re-requests cause duplicate content or incorrect conversation stitching.
- Affects a subset (~3-4%) of long-running sessions (>40s) in us-east production.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1) behind Redwood edge-proxy cluster ep-us-east-3
- Customer SDK: atlashealth-web-sdk v2.1.3 (browser: Chrome 114 on Linux)
- Models: gpt-4o-mini pinned by customer to v2026-02-15

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a chat stream using SSE with a multi-paragraph prompt (expected token stream > 60 tokens).
2) Let stream run for 45-120s. Occasionally the stream shows a repeated heartbeat event (two identical keepalive frames within ~200ms).
3) After the duplicate heartbeat, client experiences no more framed events; SDK triggers internal reconnect/backoff after its idle window and UI never receives final metadata block (closing markers).

Observed behavior:
- Logs show duplicate heartbeat events from the edge (two SSE comment/keepalive blocks back-to-back) followed by no further data for ~90s.
- Client logs: SDK sees keepalive twice, then raises IdleTimeout -> reconnect; on reconnect the resumed session returns a new conversation snapshot but missing previous final metadata.
- Redwood serving runtime traces show the worker completed token generation and sent final metadata to the edge upstream, but the edge cluster logs contain a short-lived connection handoff at the same timestamp as the duplicate heartbeat.

Expected behavior:
- Heartbeats should be single periodic keepalives that do not change resume state. Final metadata and end-of-stream markers should always be delivered once the worker completes generation, regardless of transient proxy/hand-off events.

Relevant logs/snippets:
- Edge-proxy trace (ep-us-east-3) at 2026-03-13T18:22:11.123Z:
  "SSE_KEEPALIVE id=xyz123 ts=2026-03-13T18:22:11.123Z"
  "SSE_KEEPALIVE id=xyz123 ts=2026-03-13T18:22:11.326Z"
  "CONN_HANDOFF id=xyz123 from=ep-us-east-2 to=ep-us-east-3 reason=upstream_rebalance code=1001"
- SDK log (client):
  "keepalive:received (ts=2026-03-13T18:22:11.326Z)"
  "idle_timeout:triggered (ts=2026-03-13T18:22:13.450Z)"
  "reconnect:attempt 1 (ts=2026-03-13T18:22:13.450Z)"
- Serving runtime (worker-42):
  "generation.complete: session=abc789 total_tokens=138 final_meta_sent=true ts=2026-03-13T18:22:11.190Z"

Initial hypothesis:
- Race between ep-proxy connection handoff and heartbeat emission causes the edge to send a duplicate keepalive while simultaneously tearing over the socket, which results in the handoff path not forwarding the final metadata. Edge logs show handoff and duplicate keepalive within a ~250ms window.
- Client SDK's idle/backoff timer is more aggressive than the end-to-end delivery guarantees in presence of connection handoff; duplicate heartbeat may confuse client-side reassembly logic in older SDK versions.

Immediate customer impact and workaround:
- AtlasHealth has implemented a temporary client-side patch (delay idle timeout to 6s from 2s) to reduce false reconnects. This reduces but does not eliminate missing finals.

Next steps proposed:
- SRE to correlate edge handoff logs with specific proxy instances and flag candidate misconfigured keepalive behavior.
- Runtime team to verify that final metadata is forwarded reliably across handoff.
- SDK team to add defend logic for duplicate immediate-heartbeat sequences (treat as single keepalive and extend local idle window for a short period).


Additional notes:
2026-03-14 10:00 UTC - Elena García (Edge team): Found edge config that emits keepalive on close path and also on scheduled interval; in race both were emitted. Preparing a config patch to deduplicate keepalive on close path and to buffer final telemetry until forward ACK.
Edge handoff events co-locate with duplicate keepalive frames in ~100ms window — strong correlate to observed client missing finals.
Serving runtime reliably marks final metadata as sent to upstream; problem reproduces when edge fails to forward final metadata after a handoff sequence.
Client SDK v2.1.3 reacts to repeated heartbeat then idle: SDK's internal reconnect threshold is 2s; raising helped but not complete mitigation.
Staging rebalancer test increased handoff rate and reproduced missing final metadata in ~4% of forced handoffs; suggests non-negligible race condition.
No evidence of model worker crash or retry — generation completes normally.
No billing discrepancies observed — token accounting is recorded on server side for affected sessions.
EDGE: rolling out a config patch to deduplicate immediate successive keepalive sends from the same connection context (edge commit https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/commit/abc123).
EDGE: adding a short buffering window (250ms) to wait for final metadata forwarding to finish before emitting connection-close on handoff. Controlled rollout to ep-us-east-3 beginning 2026-03-14T18:00Z.
SDK: created ticket INT-4555 for atlashealth-web-sdk v2.1.4 which will treat back-to-back keepalives within 500ms as a single event and temporarily extend idle window by 1.5x when duplicate keepalive seen. Patch is backward compatible.
Follow-up: monitor SUP-128001 for 72 hours after edge patch rollout; customer to confirm reduction to <0.2% incidence. If not resolved, plan deeper tcp socket lifecycle tracing on proxy (separate ticket).

payload.description:
Issue summary: First Meridian Bank legal team requests a timebounded, tamper-evident forensic export and playback package to satisfy an eDiscovery subpoena covering 2026-01-15 to 2026-01-22. They require chain-of-custody proof, HSM key-rotation attestations for the KMS keys used to sign manifests, and a sampling of raw events mapped back to customer user identifiers.

Impact: High — the export is required by the customer's legal hold with a court deadline. Customer cannot proceed without evidence of immutability and key custody.

Environment: Production (us-east tenant scoped).

Requested deliverables: 1) A resumeable forensic export (S3 presigned package) of ordered audit events for the date range, including raw event JSON and the internal redaction/pseudonymization map. 2) A signed chain-of-custody manifest (RFC-style) with per-file SHA256 checksums and an ed25519 signature. 3) HSM-backed KMS key-rotation audit (rotation events, attestations, and certs) that show key versions active during the range. 4) A small sample (100 events) translated to customer identity mapping for validation, with redaction applied per agreed policy. 5) A playback harness (script + instructions) and a short runbook for verifying checksums and signatures.

Steps taken: Customer submitted signed PO and legal letter on 2026-02-17. Support confirmed receipt 2026-02-18 and asked for tenant GUID and exact time windows. SRE asked for internal retention exceptions and whether there were archival snapshots.

Logs/Context: Log retention TTL for tenant is 365 days. No prior legal holds on the date range. Potential large export size (~120GB) estimated by retention sizing tool.
2026-02-18 - Customer (legal): Please confirm you can produce a tamper-evident export and include proof of key custody. Court date: 2026-03-10.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated streaming chat sessions that 'sputter' (short pauses of 2–6s) and then abruptly terminate with connection reset during long generations (>1,000 tokens). These events began after a backend runtime change deployed 2026-03-09 and affect multiple sessions concurrently on the customer's dedicated pool.

Impact: Multiple customer agents experience truncated assistant responses; some downstream systems treat the aborted stream as a failed generation and retry, causing increased cost and user-visible timeouts. Customer reports 12% of long-session streams either stall then drop, or end prematurely without the final token.

Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (acme-health-dedicated-01) in prod/us-east, running redwood-serving-runtime v1.34.2 (deployed 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC). Edge routing via api-gateway fleet egw-prod-eus1. Observed on both SSE and WebSocket clients.

Observed symptoms: repeated short "quiet gaps" during generation followed by websocket close (1006) or server-side 502/504 logged near time of termination. Some sessions show a short sequence of keepalive/EMPTY frames immediately prior to drop.

1) Customer calls /v1/chat/stream on dedicated endpoint with model=redwood-1.2-large and a prompt that results in ~1k+ token output.
2) Use SSE or WebSocket streaming client; observe partial tokens arriving.
3) After ~20–90s of generation, client logs either a 1006 close or an abrupt socket reset.
4) Repeating with shorter prompts (~200 tokens) does not reproduce reliably.

Notes: Reproducible more frequently when concurrent traffic on dedicated pool >75% of provisioned throughput.
Excerpted logs (redacted):

[2026-03-12T14:22:07.832Z] req=abc123 trace=tr-7f9a serving-runtime: start stream generation; seq=0 ctx_tokens=128
[2026-03-12T14:22:19.904Z] req=abc123 worker=w-22 kv-cache: prefix cache hit; continue seq=42
[2026-03-12T14:22:22.110Z] req=abc123 edge-proxy: keepalive probe sent
[2026-03-12T14:22:24.345Z] req=abc123 client_conn: received WINDOW_UPDATE
[2026-03-12T14:22:26.721Z] req=abc123 serving-runtime: stall detected, scheduler wait=3.9s, reason=worker-oom-eviction?
[2026-03-12T14:22:30.124Z] req=abc123 edge-proxy: downstream close: ECONNRESET
[2026-03-12T14:22:30.126Z] req=abc123 api-gateway: responded 502 to client

Additional traces show short GC-like pauses on the worker and a concurrent batch rebalancing event logged at the same timestamps. Full trace file: trace-7f9a-20260312.json (linked in investigation notes).
Timeline:
- 2026-03-09: runtime v1.34.2 deployed (kernel selection change + adaptive batching tweak).
- 2026-03-10: first customer reports of intermittent truncation.
- 2026-03-11..12: spike in streaming errors for long contexts correlates with dedicated pool CPU steal and increased worker preempts.

Hypotheses tested:
- Hyp1: network edge (proxy) keepalive misconfiguration causing midstream drop -> replayed traffic through alternate edge fleet; reproduction still occurred.
- Hyp2: kv-cache checkpointing causing short sync pause -> identified several checkpoint operations coincident with observed stalls. Checkpoint frequency unchanged, but new lock acquisition order in v1.34.2 may introduce transient waits.
- Hyp3: adaptive-batcher reshuffle under high concurrency causes in-flight batch cancellation; observed batch reschedule events in scheduler logs.

Initial findings:
- Worker logs show "evict:quantize_swap" and short kernel swap events at the same timestamps as stalls.
- Edge logs contain ECONNRESET for the client socket immediately following worker stall.
- Reproduction rate rises with concurrent sessions and when KV cache miss rate increases (more prefix mismatches).

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Disabled adaptive batching on a canary host (runtime flag disable-adaptive-batch=true): canary shows ~90% reduction in stalls for long contexts.
- Increased worker reservation for Acme pool by +10% to reduce preempt frequency: partial improvement.

Open questions:
- Is the kernel-selection path in v1.34.2 introducing non-cooperative blocking during cache checkpoint/quantize swaps?
- Is there a timing window where edge-proxy keeps the connection open but worker is blocked, leading to downstream ECONNRESET?

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 10:05 - Customer (Acme Health): Provided additional capture showing websocket close code 1006 and appended full client trace logs.
Short-term: increase worker reservations for customer dedicated pool (+10–20%) and disable adaptive batching flag on runtime for the pool. This reduces reproduction rate. For customers, recommend breaking very long generations into segmented calls (application-level chunking) until root cause resolved.
Under investigation — leading hypothesis: a lock ordering regression introduced in runtime v1.34.2 interacting with quantize/kernel-swap code path and adaptive batching reshuffle; this can cause transient worker blocking and downstream socket resets under high-concurrency long-context workloads.
Finish code review and run canary of lock-ordering fix for kernel/quantize swap (Marco) — target canary 2026-03-15.
If canary shows improvement, schedule a rollback of adaptive-batching tweak or hotfix release v1.34.3 to customer pools (SRE + Release).
Coordinate with Edge team to add more graceful retries/backoff so client sockets are less likely to be reset during transient worker stalls.
Postmortem to capture timeline and long-term mitigation (reduce blocking paths during cache checkpoint, increase observability for in-flight batch cancellations).
TBD
payload.summary: Chat streaming 'sputter' and abrupt termination during long-generation for Acme Health (dedicated)

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403 Authorization failures for their private deployment when users are connected over company VPN configured with split-tunnel. Impact: Several internal apps using Redwood API return 403s intermittently for a subset of users; affects ability to call inference endpoints and admin console access. Environment: Private deployment (VPC peering), identity-proxy v1.9.3, ingress ALB, customer uses corporate VPN with split-tunnel routing where traffic to some hostnames routes inside tunnel and some goes directly to internet.
1) Customer logs into Redwood Console through private deployment (via SSO).
2) From inside corporate VPN with split-tunnel, open app that calls Redwood inference endpoints on /internal-api/* paths.
3) Repeat requests from a machine on VPN and a machine off-VPN; observe intermittent 403s only from some on-VPN sessions.
4) Capture request headers and cookie presence for failing vs successful requests.
Auth cookie set by identity-proxy is included on subsequent requests from users in the same browser session, allowing authorized calls to inference and admin routes.
Requests intermittently missing the auth cookie when routed over VPN split-tunnel to certain internal host/path combinations, resulting in 403 Unauthorized from the authz layer.
authz service logs: 403 - missing session cookie (session_id)
ingress (ALB) access logs: cookie not present on failed requests; same client IP shows cookie present on successful requests
identity-proxy logs: Set-Cookie sent with Path=/customer/tenant123/internal-api but later requests arrive at /internal-api (path mismatch)
tcpdump from customer: client is not sending cookie on requests that hit internal route rewrite
Customer (Vireo): We only see this for users on VPN and only for our internal app paths. Workaround that helps is forcing all traffic through the VPN (disable split-tunnel) or using a browser private window.
Customer: We cannot disable split-tunnel for all users; need a server-side fix or config change.
2026-03-10 - Initial triage (Marina): Collected ingress logs, identity-proxy Set-Cookie headers, and customer tcpdumps. Observed Set-Cookie path was scoped to a tenant-prefixed subpath and not a root path.
2026-03-10 - SRE (Diego): Confirmed failing requests originate from same client IPs as successes; cookie present on some requests but absent on others from same session. Hypothesis: split-tunnel route causes requests to be rewritten/normalized by corporate proxy or by ALB path rewriting, causing cookie path mismatch and client not sending cookie.
2026-03-11 - Eng (Priya): Reproduced locally by setting identity-proxy to emit Set-Cookie with Path=/tenant/abc/internal-api and then requesting /internal-api; browsers do not send cookie when path scope excludes the request path after rewrite. Also found some corporate proxies strip path prefixes in upstream requests which breaks cookie path semantics.
Additional checks: SameSite and Secure flags were set correctly; domain matched. Problem is specifically Path scoping combined with network path rewrite due to split-route behavior.
Applied temporary workaround for customer on 2026-03-11: identity-proxy configuration override to emit Set-Cookie Path=/ (root) for tenant tenant123 in their private deployment. This restored cookie sending for on-VPN clients and removed 403s.
Opened engineering task to implement configurable default cookie path for private deployments and to add a flag preserve_cookie_path=false to avoid tenant-prefixed paths by default.
Requested customer to validate workaround during business hours and confirm 24h stability.
2026-03-12 - Resolution: Permanent fix merged to identity-proxy to default Set-Cookie Path=/ for private deployments unless explicitly overridden by tenant config (PR: https://github.com/redwood/identity-proxy/pull/412).
Deployed patch to customer's private control plane during maintenance window 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC; customer confirmed reduced 403s to zero in subsequent 48-hour window.
Follow-up: Added runbook entry advising customers using split-tunnel VPNs to prefer root cookie paths and documented configuration knob in private deployment docs. Linked confluence page updated.
1) Ship backport to v1.9.x line for customers still on older identity-proxy releases (Engineering).
2) Notify CS/Onboarding to request customers using split-tunnel to validate cookie path behavior during install checks.
3) Add automated test in e2e suite simulating path rewriting to prevent regressions.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - Customer (Vireo Support Contact - Jason Morales): Applied your temporary change and can confirm auth flows look stable for the last 6 hours. Will monitor overnight.

Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 02:14 UTC Lexa Health reported a sudden spike in 502/503 and aborted streaming sessions from their inference endpoints. Impact: ~35-45% of requests returned 5xx over a ~45 minute window; customer-facing app reported large retry storms and timeouts. Environment: prod-us-east, customer on Dedicated pool 'lexa-dedicated-pool-3' with autoscaling disabled.

Observed behavior: Short text-generation calls (<=64 tokens) frequently received upstream 502 with body 'upstream unavailable' and streaming sessions dropped mid-response with TLS reset. Runtime logs show repeated worker exits (exit code 137) and watchdog restarts around the same timestamps. Edge proxy metrics show an unusual imbalance in route weight assignments: the prefetch route for lexaprefetch/* was fanouting significantly more connections than expected and consuming a high percentage of keepalive slots on the edge proxy.

Steps to reproduce:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.prod.lexa/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"gptx-6b-q4","input":"short prompt"}' --repeat during a busy tenant period
2) Observe intermittent 502/503 and streaming disconnects after ~200-400ms.

Initial hypothesis: Edge route assignment mismatch allowed prefetch-style requests to be elevated to a higher fanout path without respecting per-tenant concurrency bounds. This created connection pool starvation at the edge proxy which cascaded back to the serving-runtime, causing queue growth and out-of-memory worker restarts under load.

Evidence collected:
- Edge proxy keepalive occupancy spike (keepalive_in_use 93% -> 99% for 02:10-02:55 UTC).
- Per-route connection histogram showing lexaprefetch/* opened 4-6x expected concurrent sockets.
- Runtime logs: repeated "worker killed by OOM" and NVML logs showing GPU memory fragmentation and allocations failing around same timestamps.
- API gateway traces show heavy retry storms from SDK clients.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Applied temporary rate limit on lexaprefetch/* at the edge (reduced burst size from 300 -> 40).
- Scaled dedicated pool 'lexa-dedicated-pool-3' +1 node to absorb backlog.
- Rolled a hotfix to edge proxy config to enforce per-tenant keepalive caps.

Result: Error rate returned to baseline (~<1.5% 5xx) within 20 minutes of mitigations. Customer reported resumed normal operation and accepted temporary limit while we implemented a permanent fix.

Additional notes:
Correlation between edge-proxy keepalive slots and runtime OOMs indicates the issue originated at route assignment layer. Edge config allowed lexaprefetch to be assigned to an experimental high-fanout weight during recent routing reshuffle. That experimental path did not enforce per-tenant caps. Investigation traced change to routing rollout PR #4679 (route-weight-sweep) which mis-tagged lexaprefetch.
A recent routing weight reshuffle accidentally escalated a prefetch route into a high-fanout path without enforcing per-tenant concurrency and keepalive caps. This caused the edge proxy to exhaust keepalive slots, leading to connection queueing backpressure on serving runtime and worker OOMs, producing elevated 5xx responses.
Merged PR #4821 to add enforcement of per-tenant keepalive/concurrency ceilings and fixed route tagging logic. Deployed hotfix to prod-us-east 2026-03-13 04:10 UTC. Added an alert that triggers at 75% keepalive utilization per-proxy and a prefetch circuit-breaker that soft-limits fanout for any single tenant.
Schedule rollback-safe canary for routing-weight sweeps and require per-route cap unit tests (owner: Platform Eng, target: 2026-03-20)
Add SLO-based runbook step to auto-apply per-tenant soft-rate-limit when keepalive utilization > 80% (owner: SRE, target: 2026-03-17)
Re-run tenant-level chaos tests that simulate heavy prefetch fanout (owner: QA, target: 2026-03-18)
payload.summary: Edge fanout routing mismatch causing priority starvation and elevated 5xx rate for dedicated tenant

Issue summary: Between 2026-03-12 10:40 and 2026-03-12 11:05 UTC the customer's dedicated GPU pool experienced repeated p99/p50 throughput regressions (~40-60% drop) and elevated queue lengths. Impact: NovaMaps reported degraded inference latency for user-facing routing features and elevated error retries. Environment: Dedicated pool backed by rtx-a6000 instances in us-east-1, autoscaler configured with predictive_window=60s, scale_up_cooldown=90s, max_nodes=12. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send sustained short streams (50-200 requests/sec) from a synthetic tenant that creates many small streams with heavy KV-cache churn; 2) Observe autoscaler behavior and GPU attach/detach events. Observed behavior: sudden IO bursts from an ephemeral tenant caused host-level NVMe I/O saturation and delayed GPU attach operations; autoscaler observed perceived capacity shortage and began aggressive scale-up attempts which repeatedly failed due to transient node provisioning delays; meanwhile higher-priority tenant requests were queued which led to throughput collapse. Logs/metrics: - Serving runtime p99 latency spike 10:41 -> 10:47 UTC (from 180ms -> 720ms) - Autoscaler scale_up_attempts: 7 in 6 minutes, 5 timeouts - Node attach error: "attach_timeout: nvme_wait_io_blocked" - NVMe utilization on affected hosts reported at 95% for ~90s - Per-tenant slot occupancy showed one tenant (tenant-id: t-nm-119) occupying many short-lived streams. Impacted customers: NovaMaps (reported), adjacent tenants on same pool experienced reduced throughput but no 5xxs. Temporary workaround: We moved NovaMaps traffic to fallback pool (dedicated-fallback-3) at 11:10 UTC which restored throughput to expected levels.
Run synthetic client that opens 60-120 short streaming sessions/second with frequent small token outputs (1-8 tokens)
Observe autoscaler logs and pool attach events under same load pattern
Monitor host NVMe and PCIe latency metrics while load is running

11:00 UTC - SRE (Arjun) observed pattern: IO-heavy prefetch + frequent short sessions correlated with NVMe queues spiking on a subset of hosts leading to attach timeouts
11:05 UTC - Hypothesis A: short-lived streams with aggressive prefetch are causing host IO saturation and blocking the attach path for new GPU containers. Hypothesis B: autoscaler predictive window too short causing over-aggressive scale attempts that collide with provisioning limits.
11:20 UTC - Corroboration: kernel logs show repeated blk-mq timeouts and dmesg entries 'nvme_io_timeout' on hosts h-us-e-042..047; correlated to tenants with >200 small streams/minute.
11:35 UTC - Investigated scheduler allocation: packing policy allowed many short streams to multiplex into same GPU slot which increased IO fanout; eviction metrics show frequent micro-evictions for background checkpoint writer on same hosts.
12:10 UTC - Reproduced in staging by replaying customer's traffic pattern; reproduced NVMe saturation and attach_timeout within 30s of traffic starting.
12:30 UTC - Temporary mitigation: increased autoscaler scale_up_cooldown to 180s and throttled prefetch_count for suspected tenant via per-tenant config. Observed immediate reduction in attach failures but throughput still suboptimal until traffic migrated.
13:00 UTC - Follow-up action items documented and handed to infra team for longer-term fixes (see related PRs and runbook updates).
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-12 10:55: Collected metrics and pprof link https://console.redwood.ai/d/dash/tenant-throughput?from=2026-03-12T10:30&to=2026-03-12T11:30 - observed NVMe spikes on hosts 042-047.
Arjun Patel (SRE) 2026-03-12 11:05: Spinning up investigation. Initial guess is IO saturation causing GPU attach timeouts. Will attempt to reproduce in staging.

Workaround: We migrated NovaMaps off the contaminated host set to dedicated-fallback-3 which restored throughput. Short-term mitigations applied: throttle prefetch_count for tenant t-nm-119, increased autoscaler scale_up_cooldown to 180s to reduce thrash, and temporarily disabled background checkpoint writer scheduling on serving hosts. Long-term actions: (1) infra PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1428 to add NVMe-aware placement constraints and avoid scheduling heavy IO background jobs on serving nodes, (2) autoscaler change: add request-rate aware predictive windowing and backoff on repeated attach failures, (3) per-tenant prefetch/IO quota enforcement and telemetry to detect noisy-tenant patterns early, (4) update runbook at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Dedicated+Pool+Noisy+Tenant+Runbook. Owner for infra fixes: Sophie Nguyen. Owner for autoscaler tuning: Arjun Patel. Expected follow-up timeline: infra PR to land by 2026-03-20, autoscaler tuning staged in canary by 2026-03-18.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightReply reports that a subset of their hourly usage is appearing as separate invoice line items under two different subaccount IDs after a scheduled multi-queue batch run. The split appears to map identical usage timestamps to two 'meter namespaces'.

Impact: BrightReply sees duplicated-looking (split) charges on last billing run that together equal expected usage but are attributed to different subaccounts. This breaks their internal chargeback and forecasting; they request a provisional credit and a root-cause explanation.

Environment: prod, multi-tenant org with subaccounts; observed in us-west and eu-central billing runs for date range 2026-03-07 00:00 - 2026-03-07 08:00 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start a multi-queue batch embedding job that fans out to two worker pools (pool-a and pool-b) using the same API key with subaccount header set.
2) Job retries on queue handoff for a small fraction (~2%) of microbatches.
3) After job completion, BrightReply runs reconciliation and sees some hourly usage posted to subaccount A and some to subaccount B with the same origin request IDs and identical token counts.

Expected behavior: All usage for a given request ID and subaccount header should be attributed to one subaccount and one meter namespace.

Actual behavior: The usage is split between two meter namespaces, creating two invoice lines that sum to the expected usage but are split across subaccounts, causing incorrect chargeback.

Logs/attachments: Customer provided CSV of sample request IDs and corresponding invoice lines, timestamped postback logs, and request-level trace IDs (attached to ticket). They also shared a short Slack thread linking #billing and #support.
2026-03-10 Support - Sofia Patel: Acknowledged. First response sent to customer, asked for CSV of sample request IDs and the raw postback payloads. Requested the billing window and any retries they observed. Promised update within 24 hours.
2026-03-10 Customer - BrightReply (account lead: Aaron Delgado): Uploaded CSV of 34 sample request IDs. Notes: the requests were originated from a single submit endpoint; internal logs show a transparent retry between worker pools. They attached the retry trace and IDs.
2026-03-11 Support - Sofia Patel: Triage complete. Escalated to Metering team. Added labels and opened linked internal ticket INT-3398 for scheduler handoff investigation.
2026-03-12 Engineering - Daniel Kim: Initial investigation: found that when a microbatch is handed off between queues, our postback reconciler can reuse an internal meter namespace token if the subaccount header is present in one handoff but lost in the retry path. Reproducer in staging created. Marking potential root cause as 'namespace token reuse on cross-queue retry'.
2026-03-13 Engineering - Daniel Kim: Confirmed repro: in multi-queue handoff scenarios, the 'meter_namespace' field in the outgoing postback can be computed from the in-flight worker context; if the handoff loses the explicit subaccount header, reconciler falls back to a computed default namespace (derived from org ID vs subaccount ID), causing split attribution. Patch proposed in PR 4521.
2026-03-14 Support - Sofia Patel: Informed customer: provisional credit offered for affected invoice lines while engineering prepares fix. Requested permission to apply temporary centralized billing mapping to combine the two namespaces for BrightReply's billing cycle. Customer accepted provisional credit and mapping.
Collected 34 sample request IDs and traced postback sequences across the scheduler and reconciler component logs.
Observed two distinct meter_namespace values in postbacks for identical request IDs: one namespaced by subaccount header, the other defaulting to org-level namespace.
Reproduction steps confirmed in staging: forcing a queue handoff without propagating X-Subaccount header leads to computed fallback namespace during postback emission.
Hypothesis: race condition in handoff code path where context propagation middleware does not guarantee subaccount header preservation when retrying between worker pools. The reconciler aggregates hourly buckets based on meter_namespace, causing split invoice lines.
Impact estimate: approximately 1.8% of BrightReply's hourly usage during the window; some customers with high fanout/multi-queue jobs may see similar symptoms at low frequency.
Related code area: scheduler/handshake middleware, postback emission path, meter namespace derivation logic. See PR 4521 for proposed fix to always preserve explicit subaccount header in handoff metadata.
Linked internal issue INT-3398 tracks adding end-to-end unit tests to prevent regression.
Data retention note: collected reconciler logs and CSV samples stored in secured S3 bucket s3://redwood-support-artifacts/SUP-820419/ (access limited to billing and engineering).
Temporary workaround applied (2026-03-14 by Billing Ops): centralized billing mapping rule added to treat the two detected meter_namespace values as a single namespace for BrightReply for the affected billing window. This produces combined invoice lines in the provisional invoice export.
Provisional credit: Finance approved a provisional credit equal to the smaller of the two invoice lines for the affected window. Customer accepted credit and requested final reconciliation after permanent fix.
Permanent fix: merged PR https://github.com/redwood/usage-reconciler/pull/4521 contains code to ensure subaccount header is preserved across queue handoffs and adds a reconciliation check that rejects ambiguous namespace postbacks. Targeted rollout to prod on 2026-03-20 with canary in us-west first.
Post-deploy action items: run a replay job over 2026-03-07 to validate no further split attribution; update billing run reconciliation to flag namespace collisions; backfill credits where necessary.
Customer communication: Support to send final reconciliation note and updated invoice on 2026-03-21. Recommend closing ticket when customer confirms final invoice matches expectations.

payload.description:
Customer runs a single chat turn that contains a batch of intended tool invocations (a multi-action response). They observe duplicate side-effects when the client retries at the request level. They want explicit guidance and a recommended pattern to achieve per-tool at-most-once semantics.
Issue summary:
SonderAI calls Redwood with a single chat turn that asks the model to return an ordered list of separate actions (e.g., "[{call: \"create_ticket\", payload: {...}}, {call: \"send_email\", payload: {...}}]"). The model returns a multi-action response and the customer's runtime executes each action sequentially. When the initial request hits a transient network error, the customer's client library retries the whole request which causes the same set of tool calls to be executed again, producing duplicate side-effects.

Impact:
- Duplicate external side-effects (duplicate tickets, duplicate emails).
- Hard to dedupe because the actions are generated inside the model response (no built-in per-action idempotency token currently).
- Customer is using Dedicated tier and is sensitive to side-effect correctness.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (prod-us-east)
- SDKs: Python 1.8.2 and Node TS 2.0.1 in separate services
- Server runtime executes tool calls as HTTP webhook POSTs to internal services

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Send a chat request that instructs the model to produce multiple actions in a single structured response (JSON list).
2) Client receives response but the network connection fails before client ack; SDK retries the request at the HTTP level.
3) Backend returns same model response and the runtime executes the same sequence of tool calls again.

Observed behavior:
- Two tickets created in downstream system with different global IDs but same payload content.
- No per-action idempotency token present in the function_call objects returned by the model.

Expected behavior / ask:
- Guidance on recommended patterns (client + server + SDK) to ensure per-action at-most-once semantics when the model returns multiple actions in a single response.
- Suggested SDK changes or patterns to carry idempotency through retries without changing model generation prompts significantly.
Example prompt: 'Return a JSON array of actions to take. Each action is {name:string, args:object}.'
Run Python SDK call: client.chat.create(...) with prompt above and target model redwood-instruct-v1
Cut network immediately after first HTTP response to trigger a retry in the SDK (or simulate transient 5xx on first attempt).
Observe downstream actions executed twice by the service that consumes the model output.
Request ID: req-6a9f2b (first attempt) - HTTP 200 body: {actions: [{name:"create_ticket", args:{title:"..."}}, {name:"send_email", args:{...}}]}
Request ID: req-6a9f2b-retry (second attempt) - HTTP 200 body: identical actions array
Downstream system logs show two POSTs to /tickets separated by 3s with different downstream ids: ticket_1832, ticket_1840
Initial hypothesis: SDK-level retry replays whole model response which contains the action list. Customer does not currently supply per-action idempotency tokens in the generation prompt or in the action metadata.
Checked SDK behavior: both Python and TS SDKs retry transparently on idempotent HTTP errors; retries are at the request granularity and replay the same request body unless the application injects unique tokens.
Serving runtime: does not currently synthesize per-action dedupe tokens for list responses. Runtime exposes function_call payloads as-is to the customer's action execution layer.
Reproduced locally with a minimal script and confirmed duplicate side effects when retry occurs.
No built-in per-action idempotency tokens are produced by the model by default when returning arrays of actions.
Customer replay occurs because SDK retries re-send the same request body and server responds identically; without unique per-action ids downstream cannot dedupe reliably.
Two practical mitigation strategies are available: 1) application-level per-action ids injected by the client at request time; 2) runtime/SDK-assisted tokenization where runtime returns stable call IDs alongside function_call objects.
Short answer: adopt per-action idempotency tokens scoped to the action executor and generated by the client or SDK. Long answer and recommended pattern below:
1) Client-side: Before sending the chat request, generate deterministic per-action tokens. If you expect N actions, pre-create N stable uuids (call_uuid_1, call_uuid_2, ...). Include these tokens in the prompt so the model returns them embedded in each action object, e.g. {name:'create_ticket', token:'call_uuid_1', args:{...}}. This keeps tokens stable across retries.
2) Executor-side: When executing an action, persist an execution record keyed by (customer_id, action_name, token). If an execution with that token already exists, skip re-execution and return the stored result. This ensures idempotency even when the same model response is re-run.
3) SDK helper: Short-term you can implement a small helper that generates tokens and injects them into the prompt or into the top-level metadata field of the request. We'll follow up with an SDK feature suggestion below.
4) Alternative (runtime-assisted): For customers that cannot modify prompts, we recommend a small change: ask the runtime to return a per-action call_id alongside function_call objects. We've logged an internal feature request (INT-4021) to evaluate exposing stable call IDs from the serving runtime; this would let executors dedupe without client prompt changes.
5) Edge cases: If the model may reorder or merge actions, include both token + intended position index to make matching robust. If actions contain non-deterministic generated content, store a hash of the payload in the executor record as additional validation.
Python (client-side token injection):
from uuid import uuid4
call_tokens = [str(uuid4()) for _ in range(3)]
prompt = f'Return an array of actions. For each action include a token field that must match one of {call_tokens}.'
resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-instruct-v1', messages=[{'role':'user','content':prompt}])
# executor can now use resp.actions[i]['token'] as dedupe key
TS (executor-side dedupe sketch):
async function executeAction(action, customerId) {
  const key = `${customerId}:${action.name}:${action.token}`;
  const existing = await dedupeStore.get(key);
  if (existing) return existing.result;
  const result = await callDownstream(action.args);
  await dedupeStore.put(key, {result, ts: Date.now()});
  return result;
}
Note: If the model doesn't include token field, use client-generated tokens and include them in the prompt in a predictable sequence so the model can echo them back.
Embedding tokens in prompts slightly changes model conditioning and could affect output format if not constrained; use explicit formatting instructions (e.g., JSON schema) to avoid drift.
If you pre-generate tokens but the model returns fewer actions than tokens provided, map tokens by position rather than name to avoid mismatches.
Runtime-assisted approach requires an internal change and rollout on Dedicated/private deployments — this is a longer-term fix.
Customer to try client-side token injection pattern and confirm behavior: due by 2026-03-16.
Support to provide a small SDK snippet helper package for token generation and injection (internal ticket INT-4067 opened).
Product/Serving to review INT-4021 (runtime per-action call_id) and schedule feasibility assessment.
If customer confirms fix, update public docs with a new section: 'Per-action idempotency for multi-action responses'.
2026-03-14 - Provided explicit pattern and code samples to customer. Recommended immediate adoption of client-generated per-action tokens plus executor-side dedupe store.
Customer acknowledged they will test token-injection pattern in staging. If successful, they will roll to prod and close this ticket.
Support created internal follow-ups (INT-4021, INT-4067) to evaluate runtime/SDK improvements for longer-term ergonomics.
2026-03-12 10:15 - Customer (SonderAI) description: 'We need a pattern that stops duplicate emails/tickets when the SDK retries. Is there a way to get per-action ids from the model or a change in SDK behavior?',
2026-03-12 12:01 - Support (Aisha): 'Thanks — we're investigating. Can you share a minimal request/response (sanitized) and whether you control the action-executor? Also what SDK versions are in use?',
2026-03-13 09:40 - Customer: 'Sent sanitized payloads and examples. We control the executor and can persist dedupe metadata if we receive any unique token per action.'
2026-03-14 08:22 - Support (Marco): 'We've got a recommended pattern below. We can also open an internal follow-up to add SDK helper primitives.'
payload.summary: Per-action idempotency guidance for batched / multi-call function-calling requests

Issue summary:
Customer BrightWave IoT reports sudden, sustained 429s for webhook callback endpoints after enabling an edge-level CDN prefetch rule + Lambda@Edge that retries on origin 5xx. The 429s started ~2026-03-12 06:00 UTC and affected their dedicated pool (us-east-1).

Impact:
- ~30% of webhook callbacks are rejected with 429 for ~45 minutes during morning traffic spike (reported customer-facing errors and downstream job failures).
- Affects background telemetry and critical device state updates for BrightWave fleet (thousands of small IoT devices).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer provisioned) in us-east-1
- Ingress via customer CDN (Edge) with Lambda@Edge that performs prefetch and rewrite for signed URLs
- Client traffic: many short-lived connections (IoT devices) + webhook fanout to 200k endpoints

Observed symptoms / Timeline:
- 2026-03-12 05:58 UTC: Customer enabled CDN prefetch rule to warm signed URLs.
- 2026-03-12 06:02 UTC: Burst of 429s begins for callback route /v1/webhooks/callback, correlating with CDN edges performing prefetches.
- 2026-03-12 06:20 UTC: Customer rolls back some CDN retry settings; 429 rate drops but remains above baseline.
- 2026-03-12 07:30 UTC: Support engagement opened.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Configure CDN to prefetch signed webhook callback URLs via HEAD/GET to our endpoint with a short TTL (10s).
2) Enable Lambda@Edge that rewrites auth headers and retries up to 2 times on 5xx.
3) Bulk trigger webhook fanout (simulated device update) over ~2 minutes.
4) Observe 429s returned from our API gateway and increased rate-limiter counters for that tenant.

Relevant logs / metrics (excerpt):
- rate-limiter: tenant_token_exhaustion spikes at 2026-03-12T06:02:12Z -> 06:10:00Z
- edge-proxy: incoming HEAD requests from multiple edge IPs, 10k/s aggregated for 90s
- auth-service: signed URL validation success, but repeated requests increase per-route counts
- sample access log lines:
  2026-03-12T06:02:13Z edge-34-... GET /v1/webhooks/callback 200 - cache-miss lambda-retry=1
  2026-03-12T06:02:13Z edge-54-... HEAD /v1/webhooks/callback 200 - cache-miss
  2026-03-12T06:02:14Z origin-01  POST /v1/webhooks/callback 429 tenant_quota_exhausted=1

Investigation notes:
- Rate accounting is currently counting HEAD and GET the same against the per-route token bucket. Prefetch HEADs from many edge nodes look identical to real client calls and are consuming burst credits.
- Lambda@Edge retries amplify the fanout: when an edge gets a 5xx from origin, lambda retries, so the origin sees duplicate requests from the same edge IP within a short window.
- CDN TTL of prefetch responses is very short (10s) so many edges revalidate concurrently, forming a microburst.
- Because BrightWave uses short-lived signed URLs and the CDN revalidates them frequently, cache-hit ratio is low leading to repeated origin requests.

Hypothesis:
1) Prefetch HEADs + short TTL + lambda retries caused a synchronized microburst across many edges that exhausted the customer's per-route burst quota and tripped tenant-level 429s.
2) Our current rate-limiter does not deduplicate/ignore HEAD prefetches and counts per-connection retried requests separately, which amplifies the apparent traffic.

Immediate mitigation / workaround applied:
- Support temporarily classified /v1/webhooks/callback as a high-burst route and enabled a short-lived emergency burst pool for BrightWave (dedicated) to keep critical callbacks through while we investigate.
- Recommended CDN config changes to customer: stop prefetching signed URLs OR increase TTL on prefetch responses; disable client-side lambda retries for origin 5xx during warmup.

Engineering actions planned:
- Rate-limiter change: implement configurable ignore-list for HEAD/OPTIONS for customers who use CDN prefetch (patch submitted, see related PR).
- Edge-proxy: add logic to tag requests with X-Edge-Prefetch when Lambda@Edge indicates prefetch so rate-limiter can apply different accounting. (Design doc linked.)
- Add telemetry: expose prefetch vs client metrics in console to help customers identify prefetch amplification.

Next steps / owner:

Additional notes:
- Customer (BrightWave): roll back CDN prefetch temporarily or increase TTL and confirm behavior.
- Support: monitor tenant quota usage for 48 hours after changes and coordinate incident follow-up.
Desired resolution criteria:
- No unexpected 429s for the callback route under similar prefetch settings, or documented config guidance that prevents recurrence.
Temporary dedicated burst pool added for BrightWave; advised to disable CDN prefetch or raise TTL and turn off lambda retries on origin 5xx.
(in progress) Engineering PR created to tag prefetch requests and to allow HEAD/OPTIONS exclusion from account counting. Once canary passes, will roll out to prod and update customer config guidance.

2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - Product (Monica Ruiz): Asked that we surface prefetch metrics in Console as a short-term visibility improvement.

Issue summary: Customer migrated a set of workers from a bulk batch ingestion flow to a low-latency streaming flow in their dedicated pool. Shortly after migration they observed repeated 429 responses for a subset of API keys while other keys on the same tenant remained healthy. Impact: production traffic serving low-latency chat experiences saw 15-20% of streaming requests receive 429s for ~2 hours, user-facing errors and increased retries. Hypothesis: disparity in token accounting between batch and streaming route layers combined with per-key burst smoothing is causing uneven refill behavior after the migration.
1) Use InsightMetrics prod tenant in us-east dedicated pool
2) Start sustained batch embedding job using api key A at 300 rps for 10 minutes
3) Rotate a subset of worker clients to streaming protocol using api key B and open multiplexed websocket connections (50 concurrent streams)
4) Observe 429s returned from /v1/streams/start and intermittent 429s on text generation endpoints within 2 minutes of switch
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z - 429 - x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 - x-rate-limit-window: 60 - route: /v1/streams/start - key: key-B (truncated)
2026-03-10T09:12:07Z - 200 - x-rate-limit-remaining: 128 - route: /v1/completions - key: key-A
Gateway logs show health-check probes from edge-proxy ip 34.82.11.9 incrementing tenant counters during warmup window
Dedicated pool autoscaler log: scale_event at 2026-03-10T09:11:30Z - no capacity change
Support reproduced locally against a staging replica with a dedicated-pool config; observed that multiplexed websocket sessions consume per-connection concurrency windows plus per-key token refill accounting.
Rate-limiter team: smoothing algorithm uses a 60s refill window and a short 'burst credit' bucket that is applied per-route and per-key; when clients move from a bulk delayed-retry pattern to many short-lived stream starters the burst credit is consumed unevenly and refill appears skewed due to fractional accounting rounding.
Edge proxy health-checks: confirmed that default health probes on some customers were routed through the tenant's route and incrementing token counters; recommended disabling tenant-scoped probes or routing them through a dedicated health route.
Confirmed that key-A (batch) retained large steady token consumption but batch path marks tokens as 'sustained' which allows smoothing to re-balance; streaming path marks tokens as 'interactive' and immediate accounting leads to earlier exhaustion of the burst bucket for key-B.
Observed mismatch between console quota readout and runtime: console displayed updated quotas after tier changes but runtime token refill used cached window config for ~90s due to config propagation TTL; potential contributing factor during this migration window.
Short-term workaround: recommended InsightMetrics stagger startup of streaming clients (5s jitter) and raise streaming per-key burst cap via console for the tenant while we push a runtime fix.
Applied a temporary config change at 2026-03-11T02:04Z: increased per-key streaming burst allowance from 200 to 600 for tenant InsightMetrics; reported 429s fell below 1% within 8 minutes.
Medium-term fix: rate-limiter team to deploy a patch that aligns per-route accounting semantics for batch vs interactive paths and reduces rounding skew for fractional token refills. Patch PR: github.com/redwood/rate-control/pull/231 (pending review).
Follow-ups: create console indicator for 'pending config propagation' TTL and add runbook step to route health checks off tenant token counters.
