Issue summary: Customer reports chat streaming sessions abruptly stall ~2-3KB into the response. The LLM continues generating (tokens advance in runtime traces) but client receives no further SSE chunks and the HTTP/2 stream remains open until client reconnect. Impact: customers experience partial responses and delayed reconnection workarounds; higher-cost repeated requests. Environment: prod (us-east-1), requests from enterprise dedicated account using dedicated tenancy and edge ingress via our managed envoy fleet. Observed patterns: stalls correlate with responses that emit many small token frames (lots of short chunks), and with clients behind corporate proxies. This is not a model decoder crash — tokens complete on the worker but are not delivered to the client due to transport-layer flow control behaviour.
1) Use a small-chat prompt that causes many short tokens (e.g., tables/markdown with many small emits).
2) From a client that negotiates HTTP/2 (curl --http2 -N), open SSE streaming request against /v1/chat/stream with streaming=true and observe bytes delivered.
3) Observe that ~2-3KB of content arrives then no further bytes for >15s while backend still shows active token generation.
4) Reconnect the stream: subsequent connection often resumes generation with duplicate or truncated content depending on client resume logic.
edge-envoy: stream_id=1345 stalled: no WINDOW_UPDATE from downstream for 18s; upstream keepalive OK
ingress-proxy: connection_id=9fd3 closing? last_frame_received=RST_STREAM?=false; flow_control_window=0
serving-runtime: request_id=rq_7f8a tokens_emitted=312 last_token_time=2026-03-10T07:12:23Z final_write=OK
Initial hypothesis: client-side read blocking or corporate proxy coalescing. Reproduced with curl without corporate proxy: no stall. Reproduced when routing through corporate-like proxy that enforces small initial window sizes.
Envoy debug shows the HTTP/2 connection's flow-control window on the downstream side hitting zero and not receiving WINDOW_UPDATE until client sends additional frames or reconnects.
Serving runtime continues generating tokens and writes to upstream connection successfully; bytes are buffered in envoy connection and not forwarded due to exhausted window.
A quick experiment increasing the initial_window_size and stream_window_size on an envoy canary removed the stall in 90% of test cases.

Additional notes:
Product Ops: File follow-up to consider default window tuning and add server-side periodic keepalive churn to avoid stalls for small-chunk-heavy streams.
Canary change applied to ingress envoy: increased HTTP/2 initial_window_size and enabled more frequent WINDOW_UPDATE flushes for streaming routes (gh/infra/5521). Customer confirmed no stalls after canary; change rolled to production 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC. Follow-up: task created to add periodic zero-byte keepalive chunk from gateway for SSE streams and add tests for low-window proxies.
payload.summary: HTTP/2 flow-control window exhaustion causes SSE/WebSocket stream to stall mid-generation

Issue summary: After a customer-initiated org merge (org B merged into org A), several users in BrightRoute Labs report that their saved dashboard favorites and alert subscriptions were reassigned to user accounts that no longer exist in the org (stale user entries). The console still shows the favorite/alert metadata but the target user is unreachable and notifications are being dropped.

Observed behavior: Favorites & alert subscriptions list the old email/uid (pre-merge) in UI tooltips and in the API payloads. Attempts to edit or transfer ownership fail with 'user not found' errors. Some alerts are not firing because the subscription endpoint resolves to the stale user and fails delivery, but audit logs indicate the alert evaluation ran successfully.

Expected behavior: After org merge, favorites and alert subscriptions should be re-mapped to existing members when possible, or show a clear orphaned state in the UI and surface remediation steps. Alert notifications should fall back to org-level owners/teams rather than silently dropping when subscription targets are invalid.
Multiple dashboard owners (5+ dashboards) and ~12 alert subscriptions are currently orphaned. Customer reports missed alert notifications for two production jobs overnight. Business impact: delayed on-call response and degraded trust in alerting. Workload: BrightRoute is an enterprise customer with SLA expectations.
1) Perform org merge: import/migrate users from source org (B) into destination org (A) using org-merge tool
2) Observe that pre-merge dashboard favorites and alert subscriptions retain original owner metadata in console UI and via GET /api/v1/alerts?org=
3) Attempt to reassign ownership via console -> Dashboard -> Share -> Transfer ownership, receive 'user not found' error
4) Review audit logs: alerts evaluated but delivery errors recorded with 'recipient id does not exist'
Sample alert delivery error (prod-us-east, 2026-03-09T03:14:22Z): 'delivery.failure: recipient_not_found uid=usr-824283-premerge'. Console API GET /api/v1/favorites returned owner_id: usr-824283-premerge and owner_email: 'ingesta+old@brightroute.example'
Initial triage by Support: confirmed via API that favorites/alerts stored owner_id strings that were not in destination org's user table post-merge. Audit trail shows org-merge job wrote metadata without running identity reconciliation. Related internal ticket INT-7842 tracks an earlier migration job that had 'retain_original_ids' flag enabled. Hypothesis: org-merge process only copied references to original owner IDs and did not invoke post-merge canonicalization job.

Evidence: DB snapshot (prod-redwood-01) shows favorites.owner_id values pointing to deleted_user_ids table. Alert subscription delivery attempted to enqueue webhook to user-specific channel using owner_id; delivery service rejects unknown owner ids at enqueue time. Also observed retention compaction prune job has compacted some historical identity mappings; the canonicalization job relies on those mappings and is failing for oldest records.

Potential risk: If canonicalization job is re-run blindly it could overwrite live ownership metadata for dashboards that were intentionally transferred; need safe-merge plan.
Support (Maya Thompson) 2026-03-09: Customer reports 12 stuck alert subscriptions and 5 dashboard favorites orphaned after org merge. Provided temporary workaround: export alert definitions and create org-level team subscriptions.
SRE (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-10: Confirmed owner_id references to deleted_user_ids. Created INT-7842 to track migration flag investigation. Will not run ad-hoc canonicalization without engineering plan.
Eng (Priya Nair) 2026-03-11: Hypothesis: org-merge retained 'external_id' instead of mapping to new internal uid. Proposed approach: run id-resolution job with dry-run to produce remap list. Need customer approval and backup snapshot. Blocking: retention compaction removed some legacy mapping rows (see compaction-window-2026-02).
Customer (Alex Reynolds, BrightRoute) 2026-03-12: We need alerts restored or re-routed to team channels ASAP. Willing to accept manual reassignments for impacted dashboards. Asked for ETA on canonicalization run.
Support (Maya Thompson) 2026-03-13: Scheduled a maintenance window with customer for 2026-03-15 02:00-03:00 UTC for a controlled id-resolution dry-run. Requested DB snapshot and acceptance of risk statement.
Eng (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-14: Dry-run completed in staging against a scrubbed export; remap suggested 12 owner_id -> uid mappings and 3 orphaned subscriptions requiring manual rebind. Preparing runbook and rollback plan.
In Progress: runbook drafted. Next steps: (1) take DB snapshot, (2) run id-resolution in prod during agreed maintenance window, (3) for any orphaned subscriptions, create org-level team bindings and notify customer. Post-action follow-ups: add org-merge canonicalization to pipeline and add pre-merge validation to prevent future writes with stale owner_ids. Customer has been offered a manual reassignment support pack free-of-charge.
1) Finalize rollback playbook and testing checklist. 2) Execute prod dry-run during 2026-03-15 window if customer approves. 3) Post-mortem and add a blocking validation to org-merge tool to fail when identity mapping cannot be resolved.
Related to retention: older mapping rows were removed by retention compaction (policy retention=90 days) which contributed to inability to auto-resolve. Engineering to propose retention exception for identity-mapping table for 7 days around run.

Issue summary:
On 2026-03-01 11:18 UTC Cybershore reported widespread streaming resets and large increases in per-tenant token billing for their private deployment. Initial symptoms: burst of 5xx and cancelled streams from client side, followed by a rapid series of new connections from the same tenant that correlated with backend auth failures. Impact: degraded throughput for Cybershore's customer-facing chat tier (~40% error rate at peak), elevated costs due to repeated model cold-starts and failed completions, and customer SLA exposure.

Impact:
- Customer streaming sessions truncated and retried, causing duplicate partial responses and billing anomalies.
- Autoscaler for the tenant oscillated (scale-up then immediate eviction) causing GPU churn and cold-cache penalties.
- Several retries were routed to fallback larger model variants, increasing cost.

Environment details:
- Private deployment (VPC peering + PrivateLink) in us-east-1.
- Control plane on private cluster (v2.8.3).
- Auth service (token validation) running version 1.14.
- Customer uses client library with aggressive keepalive and immediate reconnect on stream terminate.

1) Using a PrivateLink-configured tenant, configure the client SDK with keepalive interval 10s and immediate reconnect on error.
2) Force the control plane auth service to return transient 503s (simulated in staging via fault injection).
3) Observe repeated reconnects, auth failures, and autoscaler activity.

Selected log excerpts (redacted):
- 2026-03-01T11:17:45Z auth-service ERROR token-validate failed: upstream: unavailable (timeout) tenant=cybershore request_id=abc123
- 2026-03-01T11:17:46Z proxy INFO connection closed by client: keepalive=10s tenant=cybershore
- 2026-03-01T11:17:46Z autoscaler INFO scale_up tenant=cybershore pool=gs-priv-small -> 4 replicas
- 2026-03-01T11:17:50Z serving-runtime WARN kv-cache miss: new replica cold-start tenant=cybershore
- 2026-03-01T11:18:02Z billing NOTICE repeated-charge: session aborted, attempt=3 tenant=cybershore amount=+0.63

2026-03-01T11:18 UTC - Cybershore reported customer-impacting streaming resets via support channel (#support-private).
2026-03-01T11:25 UTC - On-call SRE (Sanjay) triaged, identified auth-service transient errors and correlation with client reconnects.
2026-03-01T11:40 UTC - Escalated to Platform Engineering; incident declared (INC-20260301-01).
2026-03-01T12:05 UTC - Implemented emergency mitigation: disabled aggressive immediate reconnect policy server-side (introduce 2s jitter, exponential backoff at proxy), and applied temporary token-validation cache backstop for authenticated sessions.
2026-03-01T12:30 UTC - Streaming error rate for Cybershore dropped from 40% to <5%.
2026-03-01T13:00 UTC - Hotfix PR merged: add auth retry budget and exponential backoff enforcement at proxy (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821).
2026-03-01T13:45 UTC - Hotfix rolled to prod private control plane for affected region; customer confirmed restoration of normal traffic patterns.
2026-03-03T09:00 UTC - Post-incident review scheduled with Cybershore and internal stakeholders; action items assigned.
Hypothesis 1: Control plane auth-service transient upstream latency caused token validation failures; client SDK's immediate reconnect behavior amplified load and triggered autoscaler scaling loops.
Hypothesis 2: Token validation has low caching TTL for PrivateLink tenants, so every reconnect forced an auth-path call causing thundering herd when many clients reconnect simultaneously.
Finding: Auth-service introduced a regression in 1.14 where a dependent upstream (internal cert verification service) had reduced concurrency under load leading to 503s; combined with client reconnect patterns this produced the observed oscillation.
Telemetry: Traces show auth validation latency tail rising to >2s during peak, median 40ms. Autoscaler reacted to CPU/Queue length signals within 6s, scaling up and causing cold-cache penalties visible in serving-runtime metrics.
2026-03-01T11:30 UTC - Acknowledged receipt; informed customer we are triaging and provided initial ETA 60 minutes. (Leah)
2026-03-01T12:10 UTC - Informed customer of temporary mitigation (backoff/jitter) and expected reduction in retries; requested that they hold off client-side SDK updates until stability confirmed. (Sanjay)
2026-03-01T13:50 UTC - Notified customer that hotfix is deployed and asked to validate traffic. Customer reported downstream errors resolved and provided sample logs. (Leah)
2026-03-03T09:30 UTC - Sent post-incident brief with root cause, mitigations, billing remediation plan, and next steps. (Leah)
Customer response: Appreciative of fast mitigation; requested credit for duplicated token charges during incident window and asked for long-term solution timeline.
Root cause: a concurrency regression in cert-verification upstream of auth-service (introduced in 1.14) caused intermittent 503s. This combined with customer SDK's immediate reconnect semantics and low token-cache TTL produced a feed-forward reconnect-amplification loop that triggered tenant autoscaler oscillation and cold-start billing spikes.

Fixes applied:
- Emergency server-side mitigation: enforce server-side reconnect backoff + 2s jitter to prevent reconnect storms.
- Hotfix to auth-service: increase upstream concurrency limits and fail faster with clearer retryable error classification (PR merged and deployed).
- Added token-validation backstop cache for PrivateLink tenants to allow 30s cache during auth upstream errors.
- Billing remediation: finance to issue credit for duplicate charges during incident window (see linked internal billing ticket INT-44012).

Status: Hotfix deployed 2026-03-01 13:45 UTC, customer traffic stabilized. Monitoring retention 72h; no regressions observed as of 2026-03-03.
Action 1: Platform - revert auth-service regression in next patch release and add capacity tests for upstream cert-verifier (owner: Platform Eng, due 2026-03-10).
Action 2: Developer Experience - update Private SDK default reconnect policy to include exponential backoff and jitter; publish patch to SDK (owner: DevX, due 2026-03-12).
Action 3: SRE - add tenant-level autoscaler damping factor for private tenants to avoid rapid oscillation under short auth blips (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-08).
Action 4: Billing - review affected invoices and issue customer credit; coordinate with CS and Finance (owner: Billing Ops, due 2026-03-05, linked INT-44012).
Action 5: Docs - publish post-incident runbook outlining PrivateLink auth failure mitigation patterns and recommended SDK settings for private customers (owner: Solutions Eng, due 2026-03-09).
payload.summary: Cybershore PrivateLink: auth retry-thrash causing tenant autoscaler oscillation, streaming resets, and billing spike

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple dashboard alert rules that were muted via the Console UI reverted to unmuted state after an hourly metrics compaction/retention job. Impact: AcmeRetail teams received repeated low-severity alert notifications and PagerDuty escalations during a time window when they expected silence. Scope: Observed for two dashboards and one inherited monitor across two application teams.

Observed behavior: Console shows 'Muted until <timestamp>' immediately after the admin action. The Alerts API and internal alert-evaluation service returned mute=false after the compaction job completed and evaluated the rule, causing notifications to be dispatched. The event is intermittent and reproducible when a compaction/rollup job runs shortly after the mute operation.

Expected behavior: Mute state set from Console or API should be durable across background retention/compaction operations and honored by the alert evaluation pipeline. No notifications should be fired for muted rules until the expiry time or user unmute action.
1) Login to Console as org-admin for the customer org.
2) Select an alert rule and choose 'Mute' for 1 hour.
3) Verify Console UI shows the mute TTL.
4) Call the Alerts API: GET /v1/alerts/{alert-id} and confirm mute=true.
5) Trigger or wait for the next metrics compaction/retention job.
6) After compaction, call GET /v1/alerts/{alert-id} and inspect alert-engine evaluation logs; observe mute=false and notification dispatch.
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] console: user=acme-admin action=mute alert_id=aler_22f4 status=success
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] console: mute_ttl=3600s stored_key=alerts:aler_22f4:mute org=acme-retail
[2026-03-10T14:59:58Z] scheduler: trigger retention_compaction shard=12 org=acme-retail
[2026-03-10T15:00:05Z] metadata-store: compaction write shard=12 blob_id=cmp-20260310-150005 overwritten_keys=120
[2026-03-10T15:00:06Z] alert-engine: load_rule alert_id=aler_22f4 mute=false eval=trigger -> notify(pagerduty)
[2026-03-10T15:00:07Z] api: GET /v1/alerts/aler_22f4 returned {"mute": false} source=metadata-store
[2026-03-10T15:02:00Z] notification: pagerduty incident created for rule aler_22f4
Initial hypothesis: Console UI didn't persist mute flag to the metadata-store. UI logs showed write success so issue looked upstream.
Reproduced in staging by running a compaction on a snapshot of the customer org. Observed compaction write replacing a shard blob that did not include ephemeral mute metadata.
Root cause: the retention/compaction job reconstructs a compacted alert_rules blob but did not merge ephemeral per-rule metadata (mute flags live in an ephemeral map). Write-back overwrote the ephemeral map with an older snapshot missing mute entries.
Timeline: 14:02 mute set -> 14:59 compaction reads older snapshot -> 15:00 compaction writes blob without ephemeral_meta -> 15:00 alert evaluation reads mute=false -> notifications sent.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 02:45 - DevOps: Patch deployed to canary in us-east; canary observed through two compaction windows with no regressions for test orgs.
Workaround: Avoid triggering compaction within minutes of applying a mute; if compaction is imminent, re-apply mute via API after compaction. Permanent fix: merged change to compaction write path to merge ephemeral per-rule metadata (mute flags) instead of overwriting. Deployed to canary then prod on 2026-03-12. Added a post-compaction validation job that samples muted rules and asserts mute=true; created migration script 'reconcile-mute-flags-2026-03-12' to repair any orgs that lost mute entries during the incident. Follow-ups: add unit/integration tests, update compaction runbook, and publish postmortem.
payload.summary: Muted rules reset after metrics compaction leading to unexpected notifications

Issue summary: Customer running a Redwood Private deployment behind a corporate edge is seeing intermittent control-plane authentication failures and artifact pull timeouts. Root cause appears to be a mid-path NAT64 gateway performing IPv6->IPv4 translation that rewrites the source address to a NAT64 prefix. The customer's internal DNS resolver uses DoT (DNS-over-TLS) and has ACLs allowing only the original VPC CIDR; when requests arrive with the NAT64 translated source the resolver drops the TLS handshake. Impact: control-plane sessions and model artifact fetches fall back and retry, producing cascading retries and increased latency for long-running gRPC streams. This is customer-visible as higher token latency and occasional 5xx artifact fetches for nodes in the private deployment.
1) Customer deploys Redwood Private in their VPC (eu-west) using standard VPC routing through their transit/edge.
2) Traffic to the corporate resolver is routed via a NAT64 appliance that translates egress to an IPv4 resolver.
3) Redwood node attempts name resolution via DoT to resolver.example.corp:853; TLS handshake fails intermittently.
4) Control-plane reports auth timeout and artifact downloads fall back to retries and eventual failure after multiple backoffs.
- Control-plane TLS session to resolver stalls during handshake (client hello sent, no server certificate) or immediately closed.
- Repeated control-plane retries in logs with exponential backoff.
- Artifact downloads occasionally fail with gRPC UNAVAILABLE after control-plane auth fails.
- Debug traces show source IP at resolver is in 64:ff9b::/96 (NAT64 prefix) rather than customer VPC CIDR.
DoT handshake should succeed using original VPC source address or resolver ACL must accept translated NAT64 prefix so that control-plane auth and artifact fetches proceed normally.
2026-03-09T14:12:05Z control-plane: tls_connect: client_hello sent to resolver.example.corp:853
2026-03-09T14:12:06Z control-plane: tls_connect: handshake timeout after 5s
2026-03-09T14:12:11Z artifact-fetch: retrying download (attempt 3) due to control-plane auth failure
tcpdump: src=64:ff9b::1 dst=2001:db8::7 port=853 - TLS client hello observed, no server response
- Customer provided tcpdumps and flow logs showing source addresses rewritten by NAT64 appliance.
- Resolver team confirmed ACLs only allow original VPC IPv4 CIDR and drops traffic from NAT64 prefix.
- Reproduced in staging by inserting an IPv6-to-IPv4 translator that rewrites source to a NAT64 prefix and observed DoT handshake failure.
- Hypothesis: NAT64 device strips or mangles TLS client-source information (SNI preserved) and resolver's ACL+TLS policy rejects handshake because source IP not allowlisted.
- Additional observation: when resolver is reachable over plain UDP/53 (not allowed in customer's policy) DNS would succeed; only DoT is affected due to ACL behavior and strict TLS session handling.
- Temporary workaround accepted by customer: add the NAT64 prefix (64:ff9b::/96) to the resolver allowlist so TLS handshakes from translated addresses are permitted.
- Alternative workaround: configure the NAT64 gateway to use source IP preservation or static NAT mapping for Redwood nodes so original VPC addresses are presented to resolver.
- Short-term Redwood-side mitigation: enable UDP fallback for name resolution in the node config (not preferred for security policies), and increase control-plane retry window to reduce artifact churn.
In progress. Customer applied resolver allowlist for NAT64 prefix as stop-gap on 2026-03-11 which restored control-plane stability. Engineering is coordinating a permanent approach: options are (A) documented config + validation for customers using NAT64 to preserve source IPs or allowlist NAT64 prefixes, (B) implement smarter resolver fallback with DoT retry heuristics inside Redwood Private that will surface clearer alerts when resolver ACLs block translated sources. Owner: Liam O'Connor. Target: publish KB and config checks by 2026-03-19.
- Engineering: draft KB article + deploy node validation that checks resolver ACL compatibility with NAT64 (Liam) by 2026-03-19.
- Customer success: confirm rollback plan and monitor for reoccurrence over next 72 hours (Maya).
- SRE: investigate whether control-plane should surface a specific error code when DoT fail due to source IP allowlist (Triage ticket linked).
Customer (DataBridge): 'After adding the NAT64 prefix to our resolver ACLs the errors subsided immediately — thank you, we can keep this as a temporary fix while we plan a cleaner network change.'
Support (Maya Chen): 'Thanks for the update — we've escalated this pattern to the Private deploy runbook team. Liam to take engineering action items.'
Engineering (Liam O'Connor): 'Confirming reproduction in staging. We'll prepare a KB and a new node check that warns when NAT64 is detected in traceroutes.'
Resolver team (internal): 'Resolver maintains strict source IP allowlist. We recommend customers either preserve original source or explicitly allow any NAT translation prefixes in their DNS policy.'

comments: 2026-03-12T09:15:00Z Jordan Miles: Logged by ClearSight after they saw duplicated webhook posts for the same funcall. They are on dedicated plan and route via the CDN-backed edge.
2026-03-12T11:02:00Z Priya Nair: Assigned. Reproduced locally with edge emulation toggle. Flagged possible header encoding mutation. Notifying edge team (INT-3321).
2026-03-13T13:30:00Z Runtime Eng: Implemented provisional decoding path to normalize percent-encoded idempotency headers. Rollout to ClearSight's dedicated pool under feature flag.

payload.description:
Customer reports duplicate downstream tool/webhook executions after an intermittent network hiccup. ClearSight observed two identical webhook POSTs for the same funcall within ~10s, despite supplying an idempotency token. The pattern only occurs when requests traverse our edge proxy path that performs HTTP/2 <-> HTTP/1.1 translation (edge-side connection downgrade).
We saw duplicate webhook invocations for the same function call when our clients hit the Redwood endpoint through our CDN-backed edge. This started after a bandwidth spike in their region. We consistently send X-Idempotency-Key header and only expect one webhook per funcall. Can you advise why the dedup didn't work?
1) Use Go or Python SDK to initiate a streaming funcall with header X-Idempotency-Key: A1+b/9==token (base64-like with plus and slash)
2) Route traffic through the edge proxy configured to terminate HTTP/2 and proxy to origin over HTTP/1.1 (typical CDN config)
3) Simulate a transient connection reset on the edge (e.g., terminate upstream connection mid-stream) so client retries using SDK exponential backoff
4) Observe downstream webhook receiver logs for duplicated POSTs for the same logical funcall id within rollback window (~30s)
5) Capture raw request headers at edge and origin and compare X-Idempotency-Key values
edge capture (raw): X-Idempotency-Key: A1+b/9==token
origin capture (after downgrade): X-Idempotency-Key: A1%2Bb%2F9%3D%3Dtoken
downstream webhook received (first): id=fn-98321 payload=... ack=200
downstream webhook received (second, ~7s later): id=fn-98321 payload=... ack=200
sdk debug (go): retry attempt=2 replacing connection, idempotency_header_sent=A1+b/9==token
sdk debug (python): retry attempt=1 header_transport=%22A1%2Bb%2F9%3D%3Dtoken%22 (note: URL-encoding observed)
nginx-ingress log: proxy_protocol backend chunked transfer applied; header rewrite enabled: true
Initial hypothesis: dedup table keys differ because edge rewrites/percent-encodes special characters (+, /, =) when downgrading HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 or when manipulating header frames.
Confirmed with packet captures: clients send raw token (plus/slash/equals). Edge transforms token to percent-encoded representation when converting header from HTTP/2 pseudo-headers frame to HTTP/1.1 header string in the upstream request.
Go SDK sends header as-is; Python SDK underlying requests library appears to quote/encode header intermittently when connection pooling is torn down mid-stream and a new connection starts over HTTP/1.1 path.
Serving runtime dedup key normalization expects canonical token (raw bytes) and currently treats percent-encoded and raw string as different keys which bypasses dedup check.
Edge configuration has a legacy flag 'encode_non_ascii_headers' set to true for historical infra compatibility; this flag appears to be the culprit for token mutation.
Reproduced locally by toggling edge flag: with encoding flag ON, origin sees percent-encoded token and duplicates observed; flag OFF origin sees raw token and dedup works as expected.
Scoped to dedicated customer's edge path; created INT-3321 to validate edge config change impact across tenants
Temporarily advised customer to URI-safe base64 their idempotency token (replace +/ with -_) as mitigation while we fix server-side normalization
Added logging in serving runtime to decode percent-encoded idempotency tokens to canonical form for dedup-key lookup as short-term protective measure (feature flagged)
Opened runtime PR to canonicalize idempotency header decoding and normalizing both raw and percent-encoded forms (see related PR)
Requested edge team to evaluate disabling header encoding for idempotency header or to preserve original header bytes during HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translations
Workaround provided and server-side normalization feature-flag enabled for ClearSight. Pending permanent fix: runtime PR merged and scheduled for deployment in next minor (042). Edge config change will be coordinated with infra/edge teams under INT-3321. Marking customer ticket for monitoring; closing after 72h of no duplicates observed.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 08:47 - SRE (Kai Chen): Confirmed nginx layer has 'encode_non_ascii_headers' behavior that percent-encodes + and /. Will test safe toggle on staging for this header only.
2026-03-14 07:05 - Customer (ClearSight): We saw no duplicate webhooks in the last 24h after the workaround. Will continue monitoring and report back if it recurs.
payload.summary: Idempotency token re-encoding after HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 downgrade causes duplicated funcall callbacks

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer DataSift Labs reports recurring sharp throughput drops (~40-60%) for their dedicated pool during sustained, bursty batch inference jobs. The pattern begins 2-3 minutes after a high burst and recurs on subsequent bursts. Autoscaler appears to reduce active replicas aggressively then fails to recover capacity quickly, causing queued requests and higher p95 latency.

Impact:
- Customer sustained throughput reduction -> user-facing timeouts for downstream services.
- Affects a single dedicated pool (DataSift-prod-us-west) with reserved capacity and predictive autoscaling enabled.
- Incidents seen across multiple model variants used by the customer; highest impact on larger-quantized models.

Environment details:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) in us-west region.
- Pool config: predictive_autoscale: enabled, min_replicas: 2, max_replicas: 12, target_utilization: 0.7, warmup_seconds: 30.
- Workload: large-batch inference bursts (batch size 32-128), short TTL between bursts (~45-90s).

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler scales down after burst completion to baseline (2 replicas) within ~35-50s.
- When a new burst arrives, autoscaler starts scale-up but scheduler cannot place pods quickly: GPU allocation delays 30-95s.
- During this window, serving-runtime falls back to a lower throughput mode and KV cache miss rates spike, leading to token-level latency increases and client timeouts.

Expected behavior:
- Predictive autoscaler should maintain buffer capacity for rapid re-bursting patterns or use faster warmup paths; scale-up should meet target within warmup_seconds or trigger fallback to pre-warmed GPUs.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Submit repeated batch inference jobs against dedicated pool with a 60s cadence: each job uses batch sizes between 64 and 128 and holds KV cache locality.
2) Observe throughput and latency in first 3 minutes after a burst, then across the next 5 bursts.
3) Collect autoscaler events and node allocation timestamps.

Relevant logs/metrics (samples):
- autoscaler:event: 2026-03-10T14:12:42Z scale_down from 6->2 reason=predicted_low_utilization
- scheduler:pod_binding_delay average=42.7s p95=88.3s pool=DataSift-prod-us-west
- serving-runtime:kv_cache: miss_rate window=5m => 0.63
- api-gateway:429 count spike during 14:13-14:15 UTC

Immediate customer impact: high — production degradation observed for ~18 minutes across repeated bursts.

Initial customer-provided artifacts:
- snapshot of pool config (attached in ticket)
- k8s event export and autoscaler history CSV
- sample request traces showing streaming disconnects

Temporary workaround implemented by Support (Mar 10):
- Increased min_replicas to 4 for DataSift pool (manual override).
- Disabled predictive_autoscale for the pool to force conservative scaling behavior.
- These changes reduced p95 latency and eliminated 429 spikes during subsequent bursts.

Request from customer:
- Root cause for why predictive autoscaler mispredicted and why scheduler placement delays are so high during rapid re-bursting.
- Recommended config adjustments or runtime changes to avoid manual overrides.
03/10 15:00 — Replayed customer workload in staging: autoscaler used predictive signal to scale down aggressively after burst; confirmed scale-down timeline matches customer logs.
03/10 16:10 — Observed pod scheduling contention in us-west: cluster reported short-term GPU resource fragmentation due to recent evictions and node-level reserved workloads (noisy tenants).
03/11 09:24 — Scheduler p95 binding delay correlates with node reclamation events in the dedicated pool's node group. This increases cold-start time for new replicas and degrades throughput during re-bursts.
Hypothesis: predictive model underweights burst-recurrence probability for this customer's traffic pattern. Combined with node fragmentation/noisy-tenant eviction, warmup path exceeds warmup_seconds and leads to queueing and 429s.
Manual increase of min_replicas to 4 and disabling predictive_autoscale for the pool. Recommend keeping pool on conservative autoscale until a fix is deployed.
Adjust predictive autoscaler model to consider inter-burst interval distribution (short-TTL bursts) when computing predicted_utilization
Introduce 'burst-buffer' parameter for pools that hold a small number of pre-warmed replicas for rapid re-bursting
Short-term: add heuristic to prevent scale-down below N replicas if recent burst frequency > threshold
Investigate scheduler placement: reduce node fragmentation by improving bin-packing for dedicated pools and applying soft anti-affinity for noisy tenants

Additional notes:
1) Engineering to evaluate predictive autoscaler training signals and add burst-buffer heuristic (owner: infra-autoscale). 2) Scheduler team to run node fragmentation audit and propose improved bin-packing for dedicated pools (owner: infra-scheduler). 3) Create a canary test for bursty-batching workloads that replicates customer's cadence. 4) Keep customer updated weekly until a permanent rollout is scheduled.
In progress — temporary workaround applied. Permanent fix planned: autoscaler heuristic update + scheduler placement improvements. ETA TBD after infra teams estimate.
payload.summary: Predictive autoscaler misprediction causing tiered throughput drop during bursty batch workloads

Issue summary: Aurora DataHub reported a burst of stale/low-recall embedding search results following a scheduled control-plane maintenance window. Customer saw query vectors matched to previous index snapshots causing mismatches with recently ingested content.

Impact: Production search for Aurora DataHub customers returned stale embeddings for a subset of queries (~5-8% of traffic for the tenant), causing incorrect recommendations and a measurable drop in user engagement metrics. Customer escalated to enterprise SLA channel and requested immediate rollback or mitigation.

Environment: prod (us-east-1) using Redwood hosted inference + managed embeddings indexing (open-embed-2.5 quantized variant enabled). Maintenance window completed at 2026-03-10T11:05Z. First customer reports at ~2026-03-10T11:20Z.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Use Aurora DataHub test tenant and submit ingestion job A (document batch) with embedding write-through enabled. 2) Run search queries Q1..Q10 before and after a checkpoint. 3) Observe that post-maintenance queries sometimes return vector matches from checkpoint N-1 despite successful acknowledgement of ingest. Intermittent and not 100% reproducible in our sandbox; appears related to checkpoint/compaction ordering during maintenance.

Logs/Observations: - Control-plane maintenance altered the index checkpointting job run order across two nodes. - Index compaction logs show occasional "checkpoint-swap" events where the active pointer moved back to previous snapshot for tenant aurora-datahub-org-17. - KV cache hit metrics for embeddings show unexpected evictions at 11:10Z. - No 5xxs or throttles reported; request success rates unaffected, but similarity scores and top-k returned differ.

Preliminary mitigation applied: - Forced a recheckpoint of Aurora DataHub's active embedding index (manual compaction) at 2026-03-10T12:05Z which restored expected results for ~70% of impacted queries. - We put a temporary routing policy to pin the tenant to the node that completed compaction successfully while we investigate cross-node checkpoint pointers.

Requested by customer: full validation that all recently ingested documents are present in the active index, audit evidence for their SLA credits, and a permanent fix to avoid checkpoint pointer regressions during maintenance.
2026-03-10T11:25Z - Aurora support contact (Lena Ortiz): We started seeing search mismatches immediately after your 11:00 maintenance. Some recent docs are not appearing in top results. This is affecting a live feature. Please advise ETA and mitigation.
2026-03-10T11:28Z - Support (Maya Chen): Acknowledged, opening Major Incident. Triage team and SRE paged. We'll provide updates every 30 minutes or sooner with findings. (first_response_due met)
2026-03-10T11:42Z - SRE (Ravi Patel): Initial hypothesis: checkpoint pointer update race during maintenance compaction. Pulling index compaction logs and KV cache eviction traces for tenant aurora-datahub-org-17. Creating temporary routing pin to avoid cross-node reads.
2026-03-10T12:08Z - SRE (Ravi Patel): Manually triggered recheckpoint/compaction on replica node-3. Post-compaction sampling shows restoration for many queries. Continuing wide sampling and consistency checks across other replicas.
2026-03-10T12:40Z - Aurora (Lena Ortiz): Thank you — some queries look better now but several still show older embeddings. Will continue to monitor and escalate if anything else appears.
2026-03-11T09:10Z - SRE (Ravi Patel): Found race in checkpoint-swap logic introduced in PR #2145. Under certain maintenance ordering, active pointer could be moved to previous snapshot if compaction jobs overlap with pointer flips. Drafting a patch to add a compare-and-swap guard and an extra verification step post-maintenance.
2026-03-12T16:45Z - Engineering (Nina Gomez): Patch merged to main (PR 2190), rolling canary to serving-runtime in us-east-1 for non-critical tenants. Added a post-maintenance verification job to reconcile pointers with compaction logs.
2026-03-13T10:05Z - Support (Maya Chen): Customer requested audit bundle showing the affected time window and proof that recheckpoint restored documents. Generating export and will share via secure S3 with access logs. Also coordinating SLA credit request to billing ops.
2026-03-13T14:10Z - Aurora (Lena Ortiz): Received audit bundle and partial confirmation. Pending full reconciliation. Appreciate daily check-ins until fully verified.
Hypothesis: A race in the control-plane checkpoint-swap logic (introduced during recent maintenance orchestration change) allowed the active index pointer to briefly revert to a previous snapshot when two compaction/merge jobs overlapped across replicas. Evidence: checkpoint-swap log entries at 11:06-11:12Z showing pointer moves, KV eviction spike at 11:09Z, and correlation with maintenance job ordering. Repro: Simulated overlapping compaction jobs in staging and observed pointer revert in 1/25 runs. Mitigation: 'pin routing' and manual recheckpoint; long-term fix is a CAS guard and post-maintenance reconciliation job. Linked INT-4021 for orchestration config hardening.
Workaround: manual recheckpoint and temporary tenant-node pinning restored service for majority of queries. Permanent fix: merged patch (PR 2190) adds compare-and-swap guards and a verification pass after any maintenance that touches compaction/checkpointing. Rollout plan: canary in us-east-1 non-prod (2026-03-12), staged prod rollout (2026-03-13 through 2026-03-14) with enhanced monitoring.

Customer communication: provided audit bundle and step-by-step explanation of root cause. Billing ops engaged to evaluate SLA credit request.

Follow-ups (action items):
- INT-4021: orchestration config defaults to disable overlapping compactions for single-tenant critical namespaces (owner: SRE).
- Add automated per-tenant index-consistency checks to Redwood Optimize (owner: Applied ML infra).
- Update runbook for maintenance window choreography and include pointer reconciliation checklist (owner: On-call SRE).
Production search degraded for Aurora DataHub tenant for ~3 hours (11:05Z-14:10Z) with impact to a subset of queries. Enterprise SLA channel engaged; billing ops evaluating credit.
payload.summary: Aurora DataHub — embedding index checkpoint drift after maintenance leading to stale search results (customer escalation)

Issue summary:
FinBank (Private / VPC) is requesting an official, supportable backup/restore runbook for Redwood Private control plane and a DR checklist suitable for internal audit. They are in late-stage security + reliability validation and need a customer-facing guidance doc (or an approved interim runbook) to proceed.

Customer ask / urgency:
- Provide "official" Redwood guidance for: (1) consistent backups, (2) restore into a clean cluster, (3) DR procedure (single-region) with validation steps.
- Confirm what is included/excluded (Kubernetes objects vs Redwood control plane state; secrets handling).
- Provide encryption + key management expectations (customer-managed KMS key, rotation expectations, behavior if KMS unavailable).
- Provide recommended storage backend patterns (S3 + KMS + least privilege IAM).
- Provide evidence artifacts they can keep for audit (backup manifest, checksum, restore validation report).
- Timeline: they want this within 1 week to meet an internal gate for their MAP.

Environment details provided by customer:
- Deployment type: Redwood Private (VPC) on AWS EKS
- Region: us-east-1
- Topology: single-region, multi-AZ
- Object storage permitted: S3 (preferred). NFS is not preferred; GCS not applicable.
- Key management: customer-managed AWS KMS CMK; no external egress from cluster other than to AWS endpoints
- Compliance: requires encryption at rest + documented retention policy; wants clear statement on whether backups include secrets

What we have today (internal / draft):
- Internal Confluence drafts exist for control-plane backup/restore and DR plan, but not yet published as customer-facing docs.
- Installer work in progress adds `backup create` / `restore apply` and an encrypted artifact manifest.

Requested outcome:
- Provide customer-approved interim runbook + caveats, and confirm ETA for customer-facing docs publication.
- Coordinate with Security (encryption/secret handling language), SRE (validation + cadence suggestions), and Docs (publish location).

They are OK with an interim PDF/export from Confluence if we mark it as "Draft" and add support boundaries + prereqs. Can Support/SRE align on what we can safely share this week?
2025-02-03 10:01 (Sean Gallagher): Triage: this is effectively a docs/supportability request, but we need to ensure the steps match current installer + helm behavior. Assigning to me for coordination. I’ll pull in Kira (docs) + Marcus (security) for wording and what’s in/out of scope. Target: share a vetted interim runbook by EOW.
2025-02-04 14:26 (Kira Thompson): Docs status: customer-facing guide is in progress (redwood-docs PR-812). For interim sharing, we can export the Confluence runbooks + add a front-matter section: supported versions, prerequisites, and explicit exclusions. Please confirm the minimum supported Private version for `backup create` / `restore apply` so we don’t overpromise.
2025-02-05 11:40 (Ethan Park): Current behavior: `backup create` produces a manifest + encrypted tarball of control-plane state. Restore ordering expects CRDs present and helm releases installed to the target version before applying state (PR-489 covers validation/report). Not ready to claim it’s fully self-serve without operator familiarity. Recommend we provide a "supported with Redwood assistance" note for restores until after the game day hardening.
2025-02-05 13:18 (Marcus Lin): Security guidance for customer-facing language: 1) backups must be encrypted at rest; 2) do not include raw secret material in backup artifacts unless explicitly configured; default is to back up references/metadata and rely on KMS/HSM + secrets manager as the source of truth; 3) include checksum + signature verification steps where applicable; 4) state retention is customer-configurable and should align to their policy. Also include behavior guidance if KMS is unavailable during backup/restore (fail closed).
2025-02-06 09:07 (Sean Gallagher): Proposed interim package to send FinBank:
- Confluence exports: Overview + Control Plane Backup Runbook + Control Plane Restore Runbook + DR Plan (VPC single-region)
- ADR excerpt for backup format/encryption rationale (sanitized)
- Short support boundaries note: we support backup creation as self-serve; restores should be performed in a planned window with Redwood on call for first run.
Please confirm if we should include Velero integration guidance or keep it out to avoid confusion.
2025-02-06 09:44 (Colin O'Donnell): For FinBank specifically, keep Velero as "optional" with clear include/exclude list. They asked whether they can just rely on cluster-level backups; we should emphasize application-level restore for Redwood control plane state, and that etcd snapshot restore is last resort. If we include it, include the coordination point: do not snapshot secrets as plain YAML, and align timing so control-plane snapshot is consistent.
2025-02-07 16:22 (Sean Gallagher): Sent interim runbook package to FinBank via Markus (SE) including Confluence exports + a 1-page cover note with:
- Scope: control-plane state + critical configuration; excludes model weights/caches; dataplane is stateless.
- Storage: S3 + KMS; least privilege IAM; retention suggestions.
- Validation: smoke test checklist + restore report expectations.
- Known caveats: restore requires matching target version + CRDs present; Redwood assistance recommended for first restore.
Awaiting customer feedback.
2025-02-10 08:53 (Markus Klein): Customer feedback: acceptable, but they asked for two clarifications in writing:
1) RPO/RTO targets we recommend for single-region VPC (even if "best effort")
2) Explicit statement that backup artifacts do NOT contain plaintext secrets by default.
Can we add a short appendix + send?
2025-02-10 10:15 (Sean Gallagher): Yes. I’ll add a short appendix referencing our internal target matrix (without overcommitting SLA). We’ll phrase as "reference targets" contingent on storage backend and operator readiness. Security statement: "no plaintext secrets by default; backups include secret references/metadata; customer secret store remains system of record". Will send today.
2025-02-10 17:02 (Sean Gallagher): Appendix sent to Markus for forwarding. Also pointed them to the upcoming customer-facing docs publication path and noted we’ll notify when PR-812 lands. Internally tracking doc publication and version compatibility under ENG-9828/ENG-9830.
Provided FinBank with a vetted interim backup/restore + DR runbook package (Confluence exports) plus an appendix clarifying reference RPO/RTO targets and default secret handling (no plaintext secrets in backup artifacts by default). Set expectation that customer-facing published docs are forthcoming (tracked in docs PR-812 / ENG-9828) and that first restore should be performed with Redwood assistance until hardening/game day outcomes are fully incorporated. Issue summary:
Customer reports that their negotiated per-seat discount (contract #ACME-ENT-2025) did not apply to a surcharge line on their finalized invoice for 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07. The surcharge line is labelled 'scheduled-toolcall-surcharge' and corresponds to multiple scheduled nightly batch jobs that invoke tools (OCR and document-summarization). Impact:
- Customer was charged $4,125.00 where expected net was $2,975.00 after negotiated seat discounts and an agreed tool-invoke waiver for scheduled batches.
- Finance flagged a negative balance alert at AcmeSlides and Customer Success escalated.
Environment:
- Production (us-east); nightly scheduled job window 02:00–04:30 UTC; jobs run under org API key org_ACME_94; scheduled via Console -> Jobs -> "Document Summarizer - nightly".
- Customer on enterprise tier with seat discount mapping tag: seat_discount:enterprise_acme_20pct.

Steps to reproduce / investigation steps taken so far:
1) Customer provided invoice PDF and ID INV-2026-03-07-ACME.
2) Support reproduced postback entries for the period and filtered by tag 'scheduled-toolcall' and API key org_ACME_94.
3) Confirmed meter records show tool-invoke rate applied (toolcall.rate_id=tool-surcharge-v2) and line was generated by billing job run at 2026-03-07T07:12:02Z.
4) Queried rate-lookup cache at billing service and found lookup returned base tool-surcharge rate (no discount ladder) during finalization window.
5) Confirmed customer discount tag existed on account metadata in Account DB as of 2026-02-28.

Observed logs and artifacts:
- billing-finalize.log excerpt: "2026-03-07T07:12:02Z billing.finalize INV-2026-03-07-ACME - applied_rates: [base-tool-surcharge-v2] - discount_lookup: MISS - applied_lines: [scheduled-toolcall-surcharge: 412500 cents]"
- postback records: 87 events aggregated into scheduled-toolcall-surcharge (aggregate_tokens: 1,250,000).
- scheduler audit: 'Job run completed, tag applied: scheduled-toolcall'.

1) Locate scheduled job 'Document Summarizer - nightly' in Console for org_ACME_94.
2) Inspect executed job logs for 2026-03-02 through 2026-03-07 and confirm tool-invoke events count.
3) Query Billing service rate-lookup for tool-surcharge-v2 over finalization window (2026-03-07T06:50:00Z to 2026-03-07T07:15:00Z) to check discount resolution.
4) Re-run discount resolution flow with customer's seat_discount tag and force a simulated finalize to see expected lines.

Hypothesis 1: Rate-lookup cache TTL expired and billing finalizer ran against stale rate cache without discount mapping.
Hypothesis 2: Scheduled-job postback tag 'scheduled-toolcall' was stripped during intermediate aggregation, causing mismatch in discount selector that relies on tag namespace 'scheduled-*'.
Checked account metadata and discount tag exists and is valid; account-level feature flag 'apply_scheduled_toolcall_waiver' is ON for ACME.

Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reported sustained elevated 5xx error-rate (502/503) and high p50/p95 latency for API requests during a sustained tenant ramp. Symptoms correlate with a tenant burst between 2026-03-13T13:40Z and 2026-03-13T14:10Z.

Impact:
- Multiple production requests returned 502/503 to BrightCart (affects checkout and search flows).
- Error rate increased from baseline ~0.2% to ~6% for the tenant's traffic slice in us-east.
- Customer reports increased tail latency and occasional streaming disconnects.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (us-east-1)
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-42 (tenant pinned)
- Model in use: redwood/gpt-3-small-v1 (pinned)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) BrightCart runs parallel bulk-embedding upload followed by high-concurrency prompt traffic (spike to 700 RPS).
2) Autoscaler warms new runners but routing layer assigns a disproportionate fraction of sessions to a small subset of runtimes (hot striping).
3) Affected runtimes experience KV-cache churn, prefetch thrash and then OOM-like GPU evictions leading to upstream 5xxs.

Logs / Evidence (snips):
- apigw-prod us-east accept-queue: "WARN accept_queue.go:214 hot-shard detected: tenant=brightcart sessions=312 target_pool=dp-us-east-42"
- runtime dp-us-east-42 node-13: "ERROR runtime/serve.go:487 kvcache eviction spike -> prefetch_failure: retry_count=6"
- runtime node-13 nvml: "WARN nvml: gpu_mem_fragmentation high, device-reset initiated"
- apigw 502 sample: "502 upstream reset: upstream=runtime-node-13 conn_status=closed reason=eviction"
2026-03-13 14:05 - Support (Maya): Opened ticket after receiving BrightCart alert and logs. Notified SRE channel #sre-prod-us-east.
2026-03-13 14:12 - SRE (Omar): Observed uneven session distribution across dp-us-east-42; one host (node-13) serving ~40% of sessions. Added temporary routing weight adjustment to reduce load on node-13.
2026-03-13 14:25 - Support (Maya): Customer confirms slight reduction in 5xx but still elevated errors. Providing workaround: retry with exponential backoff and 10s jitter.
2026-03-13 15:00 - Infra (Priya): Autoscaler logs show scale-up completed but new instances joined in the same AZ and were immediately assigned to the same shard due to stale striping table. Investigating striping sync path.
2026-03-14 09:30 - Eng (Lena): Identified race in striping controller where newly provisioned nodes received default shard assignment before striping rebalance. Drafting patch to delay join until shard rebalance event completes (PR linked).
Preliminary hypothesis: 'resource-striping misalignment' — routing/striping controller assigned new capacity without triggering a global rebalance, creating a hot shard. Hot shard caused sustained KV-cache thrash on node-13 -> prefetch failures -> GPU memory fragmentation -> runtime evictions and upstream 5xxs. We observed: 1) accept queue skew metrics, 2) high kvcache eviction rates on node-13, 3) nvml warnings and soft-resets.

Data points collected:
- routing metrics: shard_load_percentile: node-13=0.42 vs median=0.07 during spike
- kvcache eviction rate: node-13=172 ev/s (baseline 12 ev/s)
- runtime restart count: node-13=3 restarts in 30m
- apigw 502 rate for tenant slice: peak 6%

Actions taken so far:
- Manual routing weight adjustment to rebalance sessions away from node-13 (mitigated immediate saturation).
- Temporarily increased autoscaler target to add capacity in another pool and started failover routing to dp-us-east-43 (cold).
- Collected heap/proc maps and nvml logs for node-13 and pushed to /var/archives/sre/314271/ for post-mortem.

Open investigation items:
- Confirm root cause of striping controller race and fix window where new nodes are given default shard assignments.
- Validate kvcache eviction thresholds and whether prefetch cancellation logic amplified thrash.
- Determine if tenant-level routing affinity should be relaxed during large bursts to avoid hot-sharding.
Status: Partial mitigation applied (2026-03-13). Manual routing rebalance and cross-pool failover reduced tenant 5xxs to ~0.6% by 2026-03-13T16:00Z.

Workaround provided to BrightCart: temporary routing to dp-us-east-43 and recommend client-side retry/backoff for affected endpoints.

Planned permanent fix (next steps):
- Engineering to land striping controller patch to ensure global rebalance occurs before new nodes accept tenant sessions (PR #4821). Target rollout: canary 2026-03-16, full rollout 2026-03-18.
- Add guardrails in routing to detect shard-load imbalance and trigger automated reweighting earlier.
- Tune kvcache eviction thresholds and add early-shed policy to avoid OOM-triggered evictions.

Follow-up: Postmortem and runbook update scheduled (owner: Omar Singh). Customer follow-up scheduled for 2026-03-15 to confirm stability and share mitigation plan.
payload.summary: Resource-striping misalignment causes hot-shard overload and elevated 5xx baseline in us-east during tenant burst

payload.description:
Customer DataWave reports intermittent 10-30s tail latencies and occasional request timeouts when using streaming JSON/structured-output mode against our hosted API. Issue appears only for prompts that request deeply nested arrays/objects (e.g., multi-level tokenization outputs, nested 'chunks' arrays). The problem is surfaced as: (a) streaming connection remains open but no 'complete' event is emitted, causing client timeouts, and (b) individual requests occasionally hit the platform timeout (upstream 30s) with serving-runtime showing high decode CPU and GC spikes. Impact: Several production features at DataWave are degraded; they are on an enterprise contract and report customer-facing outages.
1) Create a request with streaming=true and output_format=json (structured mode).
2) Prompt that requests nested arrays, example: 'Return analysis as {"batches": [ {"chunks": [ {"tokens": [ ...nested 7-10 levels... ] } ] } ] }'.
3) Use max_tokens=1024, temperature=0.0, and chunk_size=256, with client set to 30s request timeout.
4) Send 50 parallel requests from us-west; observe percent of requests finishing vs timing out and tail latency distribution.
Expected: streaming incremental JSON chunks arrive and finalization within SLO (<2s median for small responses, <1s tail increase).
Observed: many requests show steady streaming then stall for 8-30s while server CPU and memory allocation spike; some requests time out without final JSON close token.
[2026-03-12T15:03:21Z] serving-runtime: stream-id=abc123 decode-buffer=1.2MB state=parsing depth=9 cpu_ms=12345
[2026-03-12T15:03:22Z] api-gateway: upstream response stalled for 18.4s, client_timeout=30s, route=/v1/generate
[2026-03-12T15:03:23Z] runtime: GC pause 340ms; total_alloc=1.8GB; ctx=stream-json-decoder
[2026-03-12T15:04:05Z] s3-upload: attempt delayed due to request timeout; linked_incident=INC-2026-03-12-77
Support - Riley Chen (2026-03-12): Opened after receiving multiple escalations from DataWave CSM. Customer provides sample payloads; they can reproduce locally against our hosted endpoint.
Customer - DataWave (2026-03-12): 'We see 15% request timeouts when processing nested token arrays. Non-streaming JSON mode returns slowly but completes; streaming seems to hang.'
Eng - Miguel Torres (2026-03-12): Confirmed reproduction in staging with the sample prompt. Profiling shows long pauses in the JSON incremental decoder and large temporary buffers created when encountering deep nesting. Assigned SRE to monitor memory churn.
SRE - Aisha Patel (2026-03-13): Grafana: rx latency p95 jumped from 1.1s -> 7.6s for affected route; correlates with increased allocator churn on nodes running the streaming decoder. Investigating potential pathological recursion or iterative parsing fallback.
Support - Riley Chen (2026-03-13): Provided temporary client workaround: set stream=false or request flattened output to avoid deep nesting. Customer asks for ETA to full fix.
Initial hypothesis: streaming incremental parser accumulates buffer per top-level array but does not flush partial objects when deeply nested arrays are present; causes O(n^2) reserialization in worst case.
Reproduced in staging: increasing explicit nesting depth from 3 to 9 increases decode CPU ~linearly and increases GC pauses superlinearly (observed 3x GC time at depth 9).
Heap profile indicates many short-lived allocations during decoder's 'emit_chunk' path; copy-on-emit creates transient strings repeatedly when nested containers are closed.
Observed a lock contention on streaming write queue on nodes with high load; decoder backpressure not applied early enough, causing upstream batching to grow.
Quick local patch: avoid full serialization on partial emits and switch to incremental token emission reduces tail latency in reproducible test by ~60%.
Related prior ticket SUP-7021 shows schema validation path can also add latency when combined with nesting — possible compound effect.
Workaround: customer advised to use stream=false or request flattened JSON until fix is deployed. Mitigation: deployed hotfix to staging that reduces transient allocations in streaming decoder; fix PR is under review (runtime PR #1984). Next steps: run canary, validate with DataWave test payloads, and schedule rollout to prod-us-west. No full prod rollout yet; ETA for rollout 2026-03-18 pending canary results.
1) Complete PR review and run 24h canary in prod-us-west with traffic mirror of 5% (owner: Miguel Torres).
2) Add additional unit tests targeting deep nesting and large array streaming to prevent regressions (owner: Runtime team).
3) Update client docs to recommend flattened outputs for streaming heavy nested data and document known limitation until fixed.
4) Post-mortem if rollout required more than two attempts; include memory allocation and decoder design notes.
payload.summary: Deeply nested structured-output causes long-tail decode latency and intermittent request timeouts (streaming JSON mode)

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports sharp increase in end-to-end latency for streamed responses when prompts include tool calls. The stream starts but streamed chunks are delayed ~2-8s mid-response, occasionally leading to client-side timeouts.

Impact: Affects multiple production customers (enterprise tier). Intermittent but reproducible with tool call enabled; increases tail latency and causes streaming sessions to abort after client-side timeouts.

Environment: prod cluster in us-east, streaming route /v1/chat/stream with toolcall preflight enabled and schema-hydration flag set to speculative=true. Observed for rw-open-7b-v1 and rw-llama-13b-v2.

Observed behavior: Initial tokens stream normally for ~200-400ms, then a stall of 2-8s while server emits heartbeats but no content chunks. Traces show a synchronous preflight/schema hydration step invoked mid-stream for tool metadata.

Expected behavior: Preflight/schema validation should either complete before the first chunk is sent or be performed asynchronously without blocking chunk emission. Streaming should not stall due to synchronous schema hydration after initial token emission.
1) Create a chat request against prod us-east with tool calling enabled and speculative schema hydration toggled on (speculative=true).
2) Use a prompt that will trigger a tool call path (e.g., include a tool signature in assistant instructions and a callable tool in the request).
3) Request streaming response (transfer-encoding: chunked) and observe timeline of chunks in client.
4) Repeat with speculative=false and compare latencies and stall behaviour.
Hypothesis: speculative=true path triggers a synchronous schema hydration call that blocks the stream when tool metadata is not already cached. The hydration executes in the request critical path rather than as a background fetch.
Trace analysis: spans show preflight-validator span executing between token spans; blocked the emission of content chunks until schema returned. Trace link: https://traces.redwood.local/trace/trc-9f3b2a
Cache hit/miss correlation: incidents correlate with cold cache entries for tool schemas after model rollout events or cache eviction windows (~30m).
Rate/queue impact: When many concurrent streams hit cold schema hydration, thread-pool saturation leads to broader tail latency increases and occasional 504s from the proxy under load.
Temporary mitigation applied: disabled speculative=true for FinSight via per-customer flag; preliminary telemetry shows streaming stalls resolved for their traffic.
Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-12T15:05Z: Acknowledged customer report; reproduced with FinSight test payload. Escalating to SRE. Slack: #support -> thread https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0123XYZ/p1678707900000
SRE (Liam Patel) 2026-03-12T16:10Z: Confirmed synchronous hydration span present in traces. Created workaround to flip speculative=false for affected customer. Observed immediate latency improvement in their requests.
Eng (Maya Rodriguez) 2026-03-13T09:20Z: Looking at codepath in preflight-validator; speculative branch currently awaits schema resolution to populate tool invocation metadata. Propose changing to async hydration with placeholder metadata and patching runtime to apply schema when available without blocking chunk emission.
Customer (FinSight Support) 2026-03-13T11:02Z: Thank you — turning off speculative mode reduced timeouts. Requesting permanent fix and timeline for rollback to speculative mode once safe.
SRE (Liam Patel) 2026-03-14T08:35Z: Filed PR to make speculative hydration non-blocking and to instrument cache warmers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4387. Running canary in staging now.
Workaround: per-customer toggle set speculative=false for FinSight, which removed mid-stream stalls. Temporary cache warmers enabled for critical tool schemas.
Permanent fix plan: change speculative hydration path to schedule an async schema fetch and continue emitting chunks; apply schema to toolcall metadata when available without blocking streaming. PR #4387 submitted and under canary. Deploy to prod targeted 2026-03-18 after staging validation.
Follow-ups: add cache-warming on model rollouts, increase preflight-validator thread pool elasticity, add a streaming-specific SLA test to CI to detect regressions early.
payload.summary: Speculative tool-schema hydration causing delayed streamed chunk delivery and mid-stream timeouts

2024-10-15T10:03:00Z Liam O'Connor: Confirmed reproduction from our lab using a simulated header-stripper appliance (mod_security config). Observed header removal pattern: appliance strips headers containing the substring 'redwood' when combined with comma-separated values.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403 Forbidden responses for calls to the Redwood Private inference endpoint. Root cause appears to be an intermediary edge appliance in the customer's network path removing the x-redwood-roles header that our authz-service relies on for RBAC resolution.

Impact: Affects a subset of API calls from CarmenHealth production VPC; results in failed admin and service-account operations and user-facing errors when role-bearing requests are required. Approximately ~2-4% of requests in a 24h window returned 403 with no downstream error payload. Customer reports impact to nightly ingestion job and web console users.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed edge appliance -> customer firewall -> Redwood private ingress). Region: us-east. Customer tenants: carmen-prod.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run curl against private endpoint via customer network funnel (through customer's Citrix/bluecoat appliance used at edge).
2) Include a valid bearer token and x-redwood-roles: admin,ingest header.
3) Observe intermittent 403 responses (approx every ~25th request) with no change to token or request body.

Observed behavior: 403 Forbidden, authz-service logs show missing role claim (roles array empty). In ingress-proxy logs we see upstream request arrives with x-redwood-roles present but the request received by authz backend sometimes lacks the header.

Expected behavior: Header preserved end-to-end and authz evaluates roles successfully, returning 200 where permissions allow.

Relevant logs / traces:
- TraceID: 8f3a2c9a-7b1e-4c2f-9a2e-11b3b2f5c9d1 (example of successful request).
- TraceID: a4d2b7f1-2c3d-4e5f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b (example of 403 where header missing).
- Ingress proxy capture (tcpdump) shows initial client packet includes header: x-redwood-roles: admin,ingest
- HTTP request at authz-service for failed trace shows no x-redwood-roles present.

Workaround: Customer can configure edge appliance to pass-through unknown headers or configure appliance header-whitelist to include x-redwood-roles. We provided temporary instructions and a suggested ACL change.

Request: Investigate whether our ingress-proxy can be made tolerant to missing headers by falling back to token-embedded role claims, and provide recommended configuration for customers using middleboxes that rewrite headers.

Additional notes:
Action: collecting ingress-proxy access logs and tcpdumps for correlated traces.
2024-10-15 14:45 - CarmenHealth (Customer): We pushed a temporary rule to allow x-redwood-roles but still see intermittent failures; attaching appliance debug logs showing a firmware hotpatch at 03:00 UTC.
Summary of findings: 1) Customer edge appliance is intermittently rewriting or stripping headers that contain the substring 'redwood' when the header payload includes multiple comma-separated roles. 2) Authz-service logic currently treats any presence of x-redwood-roles header (even if empty string) as authoritative and skips token-based fallback. 3) Ingress-proxy and our TLS termination do not introduce header loss in controlled tests; mismatch only occurs when simulating customer's appliance behavior.
Evidence and next steps: - Replayed captured pcap through controlled appliance and reproduced. - Created unit test to assert fallback behavior when header is empty or malformed. - Created PR to authz-service to treat empty or whitespace-only x-redwood-roles as absent (see related_github_prs). - SRE to propose ingress-proxy logging change to surface header-length and presence for quick debugging. - Recommend runbook update for private customers to include 'allow-list x-redwood-roles' for appliance whitelists.
Temporary mitigation: Provided CarmenHealth with appliance ACL change and explicit configuration snippet to whitelist x-redwood-roles; they applied and saw immediate reduction in failures.
Permanent fix: Authz-service patch merged to treat empty/whitespace x-redwood-roles as absent (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/authz-service/pull/331). Patch deployed to private control plane canary on 2024-10-17; rollout plan: canary (10%), monitor 24h, full rollout if no regressions.
Follow-ups: - Update private-deploy runbook and onboarding checklist to include guidance on header-whitelisting for common middleboxes. - Add an automated check in our onboarding verifier that warns if edge path contains appliances known to rewrite headers. - Engineering story INT-3321 created to add ingress-proxy instrumentation for header-length and header-count metrics.
Deployed authz patch and customer appliance config reduced incidents to baseline. Continue to monitor traces for 7 days. Customer success to schedule follow-up call to finalize long-term compliance configuration. Logged post-deployment metrics to console dashboard: authz.header_fallback_rate dropped from 3.7% -> 0.1%.
payload.summary: Edge-proxy strips x-redwood-roles header causing intermittent 403s for private VPC customers

comments: 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Aisha Patel: Thanks for the detailed reproduction steps and pcap. I can confirm patterns look like a delivery gap rather than model truncation. Starting triage with edge team.

2026-03-11T00:00:00Z Olga Novak: Able to reproduce at ~4% locally with a stress harness. Captured pcaps show server final frames transmitted but client reassembly drops them when multiplexed. Opening INT ticket for proxy seq state investigation.
