payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports repeated partial streaming outputs when their client performs websocket multiplexing and a connection migration (upstream proxy/ALB rebind). Instead of receiving the final delta tokens, the client sees a short ‘stale-ack’ fragment and the stream stops without the usual closing metadata.

Impact:
- Several user-facing generation requests for BrightCart chat flows are missing the final sentence(s) ~10-15% of the time during bursts.
- Affected feature: live product-recommendation snippets in the BrightCart web checkout (high commercial impact).
- Occurs only on their Dedicated tenancy during peak traffic and after upstream path changes (ALB handoff / proxy connection reuse).

Observed behavior:
- Client receives a short delta (usually 1-4 tokens) identified as a stale-ack, then the websocket stream emits a normal keepalive, but the final closing metadata ("event: end"/json envelope) is not observed by the client.
- When the client reconnects and re-requests the session, the server returns the expected final content (so not a model generation fault), indicating partial delivery rather than model truncation.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Use BrightCart SDK with multiplexing enabled (multiple concurrent streams on same ws connection).
2) Start 20 concurrent generation requests targeting redwood/gptx-1.2b with short prompts (~80 tokens target).
3) Simulate upstream ALB rebind by toggling a TCP drain on a path (they used an internal test harness to induce connection migration).
4) Observe ~10-15% of streams deliver a short stale fragment and then never observe terminal envelope.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming session should deliver full deltas followed by closing metadata (end-of-stream marker). Reconnect/resume logic should not lose trailing tokens.

Temporary workaround provided by customer:
- Disable client-side multiplexing (use single-stream-per-connection) which reduces incidence to <1%.
- Implement server-side poll-on-reconnect for missing terminal metadata (application-layer workaround).

Logs / sample traces (sanitized):
- 2026-03-09T18:02:11Z ws-client[bc-123] -> SEND: start_stream id=stream-91
- 2026-03-09T18:02:11Z ws-proxy[edge-12] -> UPSTREAM: attach worker-17
- 2026-03-09T18:02:11Z serving-runtime[worker-17] -> GENERATION: stream-91 partial=..."The recommended item is a RedWidget..."
- 2026-03-09T18:02:12Z ws-proxy[edge-12] -> CLIENT: delta tokens: 1-4, flagged as stale-ack
- 2026-03-09T18:02:12Z ws-proxy[edge-12] -> CLIENT: keepalive
- 2026-03-09T18:02:12Z ws-proxy[edge-12] -> UPSTREAM: connection handoff (ALB rebind)
- 2026-03-09T18:02:14Z ws-client[bc-123] -> RECONNECT: start_stream id=stream-91
- 2026-03-09T18:02:14Z serving-runtime[worker-18] -> GENERATION: stream-91 final payload sent on reconnect

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Multiplexing conflates per-stream ack windows in the websocket-proxy during an upstream connection migration. A stale-ack tag is emitted when the proxy believes a downstream socket has acknowledged the tail, but the original upstream still had outstanding buffered payloads.
- Hypothesis 2: The serving-runtime sends closing metadata but the proxy's per-stream frame mapping loses the final envelope when multiple streams share a single underlying TCP connection and a path change occurs.
- We reproduced a lower-frequency case internally by running a multiplexed client against a test ALB and forcing connection drain; captured pcap shows final TCP segments being retransmitted but client-side frame reassembly stops at keepalive.

Next steps (assigned):
- Network/edge to add per-stream frame counters and assert end-envelope delivery across migration boundaries (Liam Chen).
- Runtime to add end-of-stream explicit flush on detection of upstream handoff (SRE pair: Olga Novak + runtime team).
- SDK/Client team to ship a temporary patch to disable multiplexing by default for Dedicated customers until a fix is in place (PR opened).

Attachments:
- pcap snippet: https://s3.redwood.com/brightcart/pcap/1003456.pcap (customer-provided)
- Internal trace: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/streams/trace/stream-91

- Reproduced locally at low frequency by enabling multiplexing in our internal sdk and toggling connection drain on ALB.
- Packet capture shows server final frames transmitted but not reassembled client-side; proxy logs show stale_ack flag set immediately before rebind.
- Reviewed ws-proxy code path: per-stream window bookkeeping relies on a single seq counter that gets reset on connection rebind. Probable race between rebind cleanup and in-flight frame drain.
- Quick patch idea: persist per-stream sequence state across rebinds for N seconds and hold rebind completion until outstanding frames are acked or TTL expires.

In progress: workaround (disable multiplexing) accepted by customer. Engineering to implement proxy-side per-stream sequence preservation and explicit end-of-stream flush on handoff. Estimated fix ETA: 2 sprints (priority patch + canary).

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - BrightCart (customer): Disabling multiplexing reduced errors to near-zero. We can keep multiplexing off short-term but need a fix since multiplexing is critical for our scaling model.
[serve] 2026-03-09T18:02:12.111Z INFO worker-17 stream=stream-91 partial_sent=48 tokens
[proxy] 2026-03-09T18:02:12.117Z WARN edge-12 streammap=0x7ff stale_ack=true rebind_detected=true
[client] 2026-03-09T18:02:14.201Z INFO reconnect success code=200
payload.summary: WebSocket multiplexing + upstream migration produces stale-ack partial delta and missing trailing tokens

comments: 2026-03-10T09:15:00Z Platform Eng: Collected thread dumps, heap profiles and gateway rate-limiter logs. Noticed threadpool queuing rising sharply when hedged retries active. Preparing hypothesis writeup.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a mid-morning traffic spike for a dedicated customer (TextLoop Labs) we observed a rapid rise in 5xx responses from the API gateway beginning ~2026-03-09T10:12:00Z. Error rate climbed from baseline ~0.3% to ~7% within 6 minutes and remained elevated for ~45 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer saw failed requests for both chat and embeddings routes; several upstream calls returned 502/504 and streaming sessions were reset.
- Affected customer workflows experienced degraded throughput and multiple retry storms.
- Business impact: degraded SLA for dedicated tenant; support ticket opened by account team.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: tenant pinned to a reserved GPU pod group in us-east-1.
- API Gateway: fronting runtime with per-tenant soft rate-shedding configured at 450 rps.
- Serving runtime: version rtx-2026-02-20 (threadpool v1.4).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1. Tenant ramps from steady 120 rps to ~600 rps over ~3 minutes initiating many concurrent short requests.
2. API gateway hit soft rate-shedding threshold and began returning 429s to some callers while also issuing hedged retries for slow responses.
3. Hedged retries amplified upstream load, driving serving-runtime thread saturation and watchdog timeouts; runtimes started soft-restarting (SIGTERM -> restart).
4. Restarting runtimes caused in-flight KV/prefetch invalidations and transient failures which propagated as 502/504 back to API gateway.

Observed logs/metrics (high level):
- API gateway 5xx rate: spike to 7.1% (10:12–10:57 UTC).
- Upstream runtime restarts: ~22 restarts across 5 pods between 10:14–10:30 UTC.
- Thread pool utilization: sustained 98%+ during peak on affected pods.
- Hedged retry rate: increased by 12x compared to baseline; retry latency dropped for some requests but net throughput reduced.
- Error signatures: repeated watchdog timeouts, worker-thread-queue-overflow, and OOMKill absent (no OOM), NVML resets not observed; GPU driver logs clean.

Initial mitigation implemented:
- Support temporarily disabled hedged retries for the tenant at 10:22 UTC and increased soft-throttle ceiling to 900 rps to allow smoother ramp while engineering investigated.
- This reduced hedged retries and stabilized runtimes; 5xx rate fell back to ~0.6% by 10:40 UTC.

Notes on uniqueness of this incident:
- Unlike classic prefetch or NVML reset incidents, this failure chain appears to be driven by a combination of soft-throttling behavior in the API gateway and hedged retry logic amplifying load to the serving runtime until threadpool saturation triggered watchdog restarts.

Timeline reconstructed from traces and metrics: first gateway 429s at 10:12 -> hedged-retry scale at 10:13 -> runtime thread saturation at 10:14 -> restarts 10:14-10:30.
Hedged-retry implementation (gateway v2) issues: retries are started on perceived latency rather than on explicit upstream errors which can double-request load if tens of outstanding requests exist.
Serving runtime threadpool sizing: v1.4 uses fixed worker thread count configured by tenant profile. Under sustained concurrent short requests, queueing increased rather than shedding gracefully.
No evidence of GPU driver resets or OOMs; crash pattern consistent with watchdog-triggered restart due to task queue starvation/timeouts.
Staging reproduction: enabling hedged retries + rapid burst reproduced worker exhaustion at ~4x baseline concurrent short requests. Disabling retries prevented restart chain.
Potential root cause: race between gateway soft-shedding + hedged-retries amplification + conservative threadpool behavior in serving runtime leading to exponential load amplification and watchdog kills.

Issue summary: After a planned IDP attribute release on 2026-03-09, some users receive an 'organizationUnit' claim using a pipe (|) delimiter instead of the expected colon (:) delimiter. Impact: token-to-role mapping in the RBAC service fails to match these altered claims, resulting in 403s when accessing internal tools (feature-flag console, runbook editor, and analytics portal). Current behavior: tokens present correctly but role resolution returns empty set when the orgUnit claim contains the pipe delimiter. Expected behavior: RBAC claim parser should accept either delimiter (legacy colon or new pipe) or the IDP should continue emitting the colon-delimited value. Workaround (temporary): Manual role grant to affected accounts via the admin console until a fix is deployed.
1) Authenticate via Okta/IDP for a user with orgUnit attribute set to 'engineering|backend'
2) Request access to /console or /runbooks with the issued session token
3) Observe 403 from RBAC service and 'no roles resolved' in token resolution trace
4) Compare token claim payloads between a working user (engineering:backend) and failing user (engineering|backend)
TOKEN_PAYLOAD: {"sub":"U12345", "orgUnit":"engineering|backend", "exp":1710000000}
RBAC: resolve_roles(request_id=req-9f3b) -> matched_rules=0 -> returning 403
IDP: user-provisioner: emitted orgUnit=engineering|backend (deploy 2026-03-09 02:18 UTC)
Hypothesis: IDP provisioning change introduced a new delimiter for composite orgUnit values. RBAC regex expects '(.+):(.+)' and fails on '|'.
Checked token traces for ~12 affected users; all show consistent '|' in orgUnit. Legacy users provisioned before 2026-03-09 continue to have ':' and work normally.
Confirmed IDP release notes (internal) mention change to 'composite attribute separator' to support downstream systems, but RBAC was not included in scope.
Ran local unit tests: updated parser to accept /[:|]/ and role resolution succeeds with both separators.
Risk assessment: broad rollout of parser change is low-risk but we must ensure no accidental collision with existing role naming conventions that use '|' in other contexts.

Additional notes:

2026-03-12 17:10 - Coordinated with IDP team to temporarily revert attribute emission to ':' for new provisioning windows while patch deploys to staging.

Issue summary:
Customer ScalePilot Inc. reports intermittent 429 responses for a subset of requests after switching to a multiplexed ingress proxy that mixes short low-latency 'flash' calls (chat completions) and large batch embedding uploads.

Impact:
- Production traffic experiences sporadic throttles affecting latency-sensitive paths (chat) while long-running batch uploads continue.
- Customer observes ~1-3% error rate on chat endpoints during nightly bulk ingest windows, increasing customer-facing latency and user-visible errors.

Environment:
- Dedicated account in prod across us-east and eu-west.
- Ingress: multiplexing proxy that reuses HTTP/2 connections for both chat (short-lived requests) and bulk embedding uploads (long-lived, chunked POSTs).
- Rate-limiter: tenant-scoped token window with separate burst smoothing enabled.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Start a bulk embedding import pipeline that opens 24 concurrent HTTP/2 streams for chunked upload.
2) From a different client, send 50-200 short chat generation requests spread across the same API key over the same connection pool.
3) Observe 429s returned on chat requests after several minutes; bulk uploads remain accepted (but slower).

Observed behavior:
- 429s are returned with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and Retry-After varying between 3 and 12 seconds.
- Console shows tenant credit usage spiking during the ingest window but total token usage does not exceed committed quota.
- Rate-limiter logs show many small increments tied to each small chat request but larger accounting spikes from chunk ACK heartbeats for uploads.

Expected behavior:
- Priority-splay or separate bucketing for latency-sensitive chat requests should prevent short-lived requests from being throttled by long-running chunked uploads, or a clear documentation note about how to configure isolated burst pools for those flows.

Customer-provided logs and artifacts:
- Provided example request IDs: ch_20260310_aa34bb, up_20260310_cc77dd (uploaded to ticket attachments).
- Snippet of proxy trace showing multiplexed stream IDs and timestamps.
- Console screenshots of tenant rate window and per-route charts.

Initial investigation notes (support):
- Hypothesis: ingress proxy reuse of connection + HTTP/2 stream accounting causes token attribution to the same token window and spill-over into chat route weight.
- Noticed health-check heartbeats (from upload coordinator) are counted as tokens when they touch /v1/uploads chunk endpoints; these heartbeats create periodic refill spikes that misalign smoothing.
- Confirmed that the tenant-level burst pool is shared by default for this dedicated account; per-route isolation was not configured.

Workaround suggested to customer:
- Temporarily separate the embedding pipeline onto a different API key (or route) to isolate token accounting while we investigate.
- If immediate separation is not possible, reduce concurrent upload streams to limit chunk-heartbeat frequency.

Next steps / Action items:
1) Support to reproduce in a staging mirror using same multiplexing proxy configuration (assigned to Riley).
2) SRE to review rate-limiter token attribution for HTTP/2 stream reuse and check if chunk-heartbeat increments should be excluded (requested to Diego Mendez).
3) Product to draft console guidance on when to use per-route isolation and how to configure separate burst pools for latency-sensitive routes.
4) Customer to test separating uploads to a different API key and report results.

Resolution notes (placeholder):
- Pending SRE analysis and customer verification of the key-split workaround.

2026-03-10 12:30 - ScalePilot Inc. (Customer): Split pipeline to a second API key as requested. Error rate on chat dropped to ~0.1% during same load window. Will keep second key for now but requests permanent fix/guidance.

Issue summary: During a staggered canary rollout with a rolling prewarm slope, a subset (~1.8%) of tenant sessions lose their explicit model-version pin and are routed to the fallback variant. Impact: Customers observe mixed-model outputs and occasional quality regressions for affected tenants; PaperTrail AI reported multiple user complaints and an invoicing discrepancy due to unexpected token counts. Timeline: 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC - Canaries rolled with slope 5% -> 25% over 30m. 2026-03-09 03:21 UTC - PaperTrail first reported mixed outputs. 2026-03-09 03:30-04:00 UTC - Support observed spike in 5xx/fallback routing for tenants pinned to gptx-neo-13b-q4. Environment: prod us-west-2, dedicated pool, orchestration version v2.7.1, prewarm-scheduler version v1.3.2. Observed behavior: Certain tenant sessions that had explicit model pins (via route metadata) were receiving responses from the degraded fallback variant during the rolling prewarm window. The effect is intermittent: affected sessions often reconnect and resume pinned behavior after 2–8 minutes. Expected behavior: Pins should be respected during rollout; prewarm activity must not evict or clear tenant pin state. Severity rationale: Customer-visible quality regressions and billing anomalies with repeat occurrences.
1) Deploy a staged canary with a rolling prewarm slope (example: 5% -> 25% over 30m) to prod us-west-2.
2) Ensure the target cohort includes tenants with explicit model version pins (e.g., tenant config: model_pin=gptx-neo-13b-q4).
3) Issue long-lived streaming requests from pinned tenants and keep-alive connection churn (simulate reconnects).
4) Observe routing decisions in request traces and look for fallbacks to compatibility variant during the prewarm ramp.
Expected result: Model pin persists for session lifetime.
Actual result: ~1-2% of sessions show pin lost and are routed to fallback variant for several minutes.
2026-03-09T03:23:11Z [edge-proxy] tenant=papertrail-82 route_hint=pin:gptx-neo-13b-q4 -> routed_to=compat-legacy-6b (fallback) session_id=svc_4b32ef
2026-03-09T03:25:02Z [orchestrator] prewarm-scheduler: started prewarm wave slope=0.05->0.25 window=1800s cohort_slice=14%
2026-03-09T03:26:47Z [serving-runtime] kvcache: lease-refresh failed for tenant papertrail-82 key=pin-session:svc_4b32ef err=ETIMEDOUT (retries=3)
2026-03-09T03:29:03Z [edge-proxy] session-reconnect detected, cookie=rtk_... mutated_by=ingress-middleware header=traceparent missing
Hypothesis A: prewarm-scheduler is interleaving probe/handshake traffic with tenant pin lease refresh and causing lease expiry on the orchestrator side under keep-alive churn.
Hypothesis B: edge-proxy header normalization on reconnect strips the pin-claim header during certain H2 stream reuse scenarios leading to controller interpreting session as unpinned.
Telemetry: observed concurrent kv lease refresh failures correlated with prewarm waves; 95th percentile kv latency increased from 45ms -> 380ms during slope window.
Partial repro: synthetic load reproduces 1.6% pin-loss when introducing reconnects at 30s intervals + prewarm slope active.
Related code area: prewarm-scheduler handshake logic and session-lease reaper in orchestrator v2.7.1.
Blocked: need a reproducer with full request traces and kvcache debug enabled (requires customer opt-in).
Aisha Malik (Support) 2026-03-09: Customer reported 'mixed outputs' and attached two example conversations showing variant mismatch.
Miguel Santos (SRE) 2026-03-10: Captured orchestration traces and observed kv lease refresh spikes. Opening deeper trace capture for cohort slices. (see PR request)
Priya Patel (Eng - Runtime) 2026-03-11: Hypothesis B plausible — we found an H2 stream reuse path where header rewrite order can drop custom routing headers. Adding a reproduction to the integration test suite.
Alex Chen (Customer Success) 2026-03-12: Notifying PaperTrail AI of mitigation step and asking for permission to enable kvcache debug in their tenant for 1 hour.
PaperTrail AI (Customer) 2026-03-12: Confirmed willingness to enable debug window; reports a slightly higher than usual reconnection rate due to mobile clients.
Miguel Santos (SRE) 2026-03-13: Temporary mitigation applied: reduce prewarm slope aggressiveness to 3% and extend kvcache lease TTL to 90s for affected dedicated pool. Observed pin-loss rate drop to 0.05% in first hour.
Temporarily reduced prewarm slope from 5%->25% to 3%->15% and increased kvcache session lease TTL from default 30s to 90s for PaperTrail's dedicated pool; requested customer to postpone heavy reconnect experiments during canary windows.
1) Backport H2 header normalization fix to edge-proxy and add test for header preservation on H2 stream reuse (ENG-PR #1892).
2) Harden orchestrator session-lease refresh to tolerate prewarm-induced contention: implement jittered retry/backoff and bump default TTL.
3) Schedule a canary for the edge-proxy fix + orchestrator patch in staging, include synthetic reconnect load and prewarm slope replication.
4) Follow-up with PaperTrail AI after fix deployment and run a 24h validation window.
5) Postmortem doc and runbook updates to Prewarm Handshake Runbook.
In progress - mitigation in place. Awaiting edge-proxy patch and orchestrator lease hardening.

Issue summary
- Northstar Search reports higher p95 latency on a single Dedicated chat route after enabling a Quantization Profile Library profile.
- Regression is most visible on decode latency (streaming token cadence slower); p50 mostly unchanged.

Customer impact
- Customer reports p95 latency increased from ~1.3s to ~2.1s end-to-end on their main chat route.
- They are running near their throughput target; tail latency is causing user-visible delays.

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: nsr-dedicated-prod-01
- Region: us-east
- Route: chat-prod (route_id: rte_9b1d3a)
- Model: rw-llama3-70b-instruct
- Quantization setting change: quantization_profile_ref set from "default" to "qpl://rw-llama3-70b-instruct/int8w-fp16a/v1.2.0" at 2025-02-22 18:42 UTC

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Send streaming chat requests (typical prompt length 6–10k tokens; max_new_tokens 300–700) to rte_9b1d3a.
2) Compare baseline (quantization_profile_ref=default) vs enabled profile.
3) Observe p95 decode time and p95 time-to-first-token (TTFT).

Initial triage observations
- Onset aligns with route-level enablement of the INT8 profile.
- No concurrent deploys on the dedicated cluster besides the config change.
- Error rate unchanged (no 5xx spike), but queueing time increased under load.

Dashboards / logs (internal)
- Dedicated route overview (latency): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-route/dedicated-route-latency?var=cluster=nsr-dedicated-prod-01&var=route=rte_9b1d3a
- Runtime breakdown (TTFT/decode): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime-latency/runtime-latency-breakdown?var=model=rw-llama3-70b-instruct&var=cluster=nsr-dedicated-prod-01
- Quant profile panels (applied/fallback rates): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quant-profiles/quant-profile-rollout?var=route=rte_9b1d3a
- Trace search (quant_profile_id tag): https://traces.redwood.ai/search?service=runtime&tag.route_id=rte_9b1d3a

Investigation notes
- Quant profile was applied (not fallback) for the majority of requests; however we saw an elevated "profile_apply_slow_path" counter correlated with long-context prompts.
- KV cache metrics show higher VRAM pressure and increased "kv_cache_evictions" after enabling the profile, likely due to changed memory layout + smaller headroom for long-context sequences.
- Under the customer’s traffic mix (long prompts), the INT8 profile shifts us into a kernel path that is optimal for throughput at moderate contexts but increases tail latency at ~8k–12k context due to additional staging / dequant overhead and more frequent cache pressure.
- Batching remained enabled; p95 queue time increased because decode took longer, reducing effective throughput.

Mitigation taken
- Rolled back route-level setting to "default" precision (baseline) at 2025-02-22 22:17 UTC.
- Confirmed p95 recovered within ~15 minutes (after in-flight requests drained and cache stabilized).

Resolution
- Root cause: profile qpl://rw-llama3-70b-instruct/int8w-fp16a/v1.2.0 is not suitable for Northstar’s long-context workload on their dedicated GPU SKU; it increases VRAM pressure and triggers a slower decode path at high context lengths, worsening p95.
- Customer kept feature enabled on a lower-traffic staging route for continued evaluation, but production route is baseline.

Next steps / follow-ups
- Applied ML to publish an updated profile variant with a stricter max_context constraint and/or alternate kernel preference for this GPU class.
- Runtime team to add a guardrail/compat warning for this profile when typical_context_len > 8k on the relevant SKU class (doc + console warning).
- CS to provide customer with an eval plan: run A/B at 1–5% traffic with long-context prompt set and monitor kv_cache_evictions + decode p95 before re-enabling.

Customer-facing summary (for email)
- We confirmed the latency regression was caused by the newly enabled quantization profile on your production route. We rolled back the profile on that route and latency returned to baseline. The profile is performing worse for your long-context workload on the current hardware; we’re working on a revised profile/compat constraints before recommending re-enable.

Additional notes:
Rolled back route-level quantization_profile_ref to baseline precision on the customer’s Dedicated prod route. Latency p95 returned to baseline. Determined the enabled INT8 profile increased tail latency for the customer’s long-context workload due to VRAM pressure and slow-path decode behavior; awaiting updated profile/constraints before re-enablement.
We identified the regression as tied to the quantization profile enabled on your production route and reverted that route to the default (baseline) mode. Your p95 latency recovered shortly after. The profile is currently not a good fit for your long-context traffic on the current hardware; we’re working on an updated profile with improved compatibility constraints and will advise on a safe staged re-test when ready.

Issue summary:
MediLedger Labs reported generation quality regressions immediately after we enabled an optimizer bundle for their tenant. The change combined adaptive-batching v5, prefix-KV aggressive prefetch, and a newly promoted quant profile q8_perchannel_v3. The customer sees more variable casing on medical entities, occasional unanchored hallucinations in lists, and a ~9% increase in token length for a canonical set of prompts. The rollout to 100% completed at 2026-03-08T05:04:12Z.

Impact:
- Customer automated regression checks show a 9% token inflation and a 7% drop in entity-exact-match on a 200-prompt canonical set.
- Application-level complaints from production users about formatted IDs and extra annotations appearing in generated notes (business impact: potential manual triage workload increase).
- Tail latency 95p increased by ~40ms in the affected shard.

Environment details:
- Dedicated tenant: medi-ledger-prod, us-west cluster, runtime v3.8.0, optimizer profile id: bundlex-adv-20260308.
- Normal traffic ~90 req/s with bursts to 160 req/s at peak.

Desired behavior:
- Optimizer changes should not materially change sampling distribution for tenant canonical prompts (we agreed on an entropy-delta guard of 0.03).

Observed signals:
- token_entropy_delta rose to 0.082 at rollout completion.
- sampling_entropy_shift correlated with the canary -> 100% step.
- GPU telemetry shows increased small-kernel retries on nodes servicing tenant (gpunode-3, gpunode-7).
1) Apply optimizer bundle 'bundlex-adv-20260308' via Console rollout (canary 30% at 2026-03-08T04:50Z -> 100% at 2026-03-08T05:04:12Z).
2) Execute customer's canonical prompts (200 prompts) against redwood-compat-13b pinned for medi-ledger-prod and compare entity-exact-match to baseline snapshot.

2026-03-08T05:04:12Z INFO rollout-api: canary -> 100% completed bundlex-adv-20260308 tenant=medi-ledger-prod
2026-03-08T05:06:28Z WARN telemetry: token_entropy_delta=0.082 threshold=0.03 tenant=medi-ledger-prod
2026-03-08T05:07:10Z WARN serving-runtime: observed 95p latency increase +40ms on shard us-west-a

Additional notes:
SRE on-call (2026-03-08): Recommended staged rollback with session-affinity preserved: 40% -> 70% -> 100% with 3-minute observation windows to monitor entropy and latency signals.
Customer (MediLedger Labs) (2026-03-08): Confirmed they will pause downstream processing for 20 minutes during the rollback window to reduce user confusion if any partial differences appear.
Hypothesis: q8_perchannel_v3 applies per-channel scaling that, when combined with adaptive-batching fast-merge, can subtly alter logit dynamic range leading to higher sampling entropy on certain prompt shapes.
Telemetry correlation: token_entropy_delta spike aligns with canary escalation; internal dry-run on a mirror tenant reproduced similar entropy shift when enabling q8_perchannel_v3 with prefix-KV aggressive prefetch enabled.
Perf counters: increased small-kernel execution retries and slightly higher warp divergence on a subset of kernels on gpunode-3 (see perf logs).
Serving traces: some requests experienced additional batch-merge latency (~1.5-2ms) causing different batching boundaries for a subset of short prompts; this can change softmax normalization windows and affect low-probability token emission.
Difference from previous incidents: this is primarily an entropy/logit-scaling interaction rather than an outright correctness bug in model outputs.
Immediate mitigation: performed staged router rollback to previous optimizer snapshot at 2026-03-09T02:12:00Z (40% -> 70% -> 100% over 14 minutes).
Result: token_entropy_delta returned to baseline within the 70% step and entity-exact-match recovered to within customer acceptance thresholds after 100% rollback.
Safe-flipback mechanics: used router-level policy to change per-request routing; in-flight requests continued to completion on existing runtime to preserve session continuity.
Permanent/next steps: blocked q8_perchannel_v3 promotion for tenants with aggressive prefix-KV unless preflight entropy-sanity checks pass.
1) Add 'entropy-sanity' gate to rollout pipeline: compute token_entropy_delta on tenant canonical prompts during canary and block escalation if > 0.03 for 3 consecutive minutes (owner: DX/Product).
2) Extend console preflight to accept tenant-provided canonical examples and run a fast token-level simulation for optimizer bundles (owner: Product/Optimize).
3) Engineering: add an RPC-level flag to disable aggressive prefix-KV for a single tenant as a safe compatibility toggle (owner: Serving Runtime).
4) Instrument additional perf counters for small-kernel retries and surface alerts when spikes correlate with entropy shifts (owner: Infrastructure).
5) Produce a short KB for customers that explains when quant profiles can affect sampling and the recommended guidelines for tenant-level preflight.

- Dedicated capacity pool (enterprise).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Tenant has an active explicit pin to redwood/open-7B-v2 (cookie+X-Model-Pin header in Client).
2) Canary expansion triggered across regions; sidecar health probes roll out to new edge proxies.
3) Upstream edge proxy rewrites health probe headers (strip/normalize custom headers) causing the orchestration layer to see the cohort as unhealthy during probe handshake.
4) Router triggers fallback routing policy which prefers a compatible quantized variant to keep latency SLOs.
5) Subsequent requests for pinned sessions are served by fallback variant until pin is re-established.

Observed logs / snippets:
- edge-proxy: "probe-received: client_id=finlytics-42 probe_id=hk-7; headers=[Host, User-Agent, Accept]"
- router: "pin-check: cookie present=true header:X-Model-Pin missing=false decision=ROUTE_TO_FALLBACK reason=probe-unhealthy"
- control-plane: "cohort-health: us-east->eu-west: snapshot-mismatch: 18s"

Notes: the edge proxy rewrote the probe exchange such that the X-Model-Pin header did not correlate to the shard health window, producing transient pin loss at the routing layer.

Tenant with explicit pin pinned to open-7B-v2
Trigger canary expansion to eu-west
Observe edge health probe rewrite in edge logs
Watch router decisions revert sessions to fallback variant
Hypothesis 1: Edge health probe normalization strips or rewrites custom headers causing control plane to evaluate cohort as unhealthy — confirmed by header audit logs.
Hypothesis 2: Pin TTL (default 30s) is too short for cross-region canary probe window; combinatorial effect with probe rewrite creates gap — observed pins expiring while control plane awaiting health confirmation.
Logs show a narrow window (~12-22s) where router lacked consistent pin info for specific session cookies leading to fallback decision path.
SRE reproduced locally by simulating probe rewrite and observed router flip to fallback when pin replay did not occur before health confirmation timeout.
Confirmed that fallback routing is functioning as designed; root cause is loss of pin signal at probe/edge boundary, not serving runtime mismatch.
Applied a two-part mitigation: (1) Hotpatch to edge-proxy config to preserve X-Model-Pin and other custom routing headers on probe handshakes in prod-us-east and eu-west; (2) Increased pin reassertion TTL for enterprise tenants during canary windows and added a router guard to prefer explicit pin cookie over temporary probe-unhealthy flag for up to 60s if cookie is present. Deployed targeted reassert for Finlytics sessions.

Follow-up actions: create a control-plane check that treats explicit pin cookie as authoritative unless explicit unpin command is received; add automated pre-canary checklist to ensure probe header pass-through; update runbook and notify customer.

Issue summary
Hexagon Support Systems (Dedicated) is seeing repeatable queue depth increases and p95 latency spikes during a predictable daily traffic ramp. They are requesting a “predictive” scaling mode (or scheduled pre-warm) so capacity is available before the ramp begins.

Impact
- Customer-visible latency degradation during the ramp window. Their application retries amplify load and increase queueing.
- Observed: p95 latency increases from ~700–900ms baseline to ~3.5–5.0s for ~10–20 minutes while the autoscaler catches up.
- Queue depth increases significantly, leading to intermittent request timeouts on the client side (customer reports ~0.5–1.2% timeout rate during the peak window).

Customer context / why now
- Traffic pattern is consistent: weekday ramp aligned to their business open (customer local time), lasting ~45–60 minutes.
- Customer is expanding usage and wants guardrails + predictability; they specifically asked for “predictive scaling based on time-of-day ramps.”

Environment
- Dedicated deployment: hexagon-prod-dedicated-01
- Region: us-east
- Model: llama-3-70b-instruct pinned; fallback disabled per customer policy
- Autoscaling: platform default reactive signals; customer currently has no min baseline set beyond current config

Time window / reproduction
- Occurs daily (Mon–Fri) roughly 13:30–15:00 UTC.
- Most severe between 13:45–14:10 UTC when request rate increases quickly.

What we checked (Support/TAM)
- Dedicated dashboard review shows:
  - Queue depth climbs first, then GPU saturation follows, then autoscaler increases replicas after a lag.
  - Scale-up events occur, but ramp is faster than our current reaction + warm-up time.
  - No evidence of platform-wide incident or regional networking issues.
  - Error breakdown: elevated 504/timeouts are customer-side; Redwood-side 5xx not significantly elevated.

Links (internal)
- Grafana: Dedicated / Autoscaling overview (us-east) — panel “queue_depth + desired vs current replicas” (shared in Slack #support and with SRE)
- Traces: last 3 ramp periods sampled; see support attachment notes in Salesforce/CS workspace (request IDs available on request)

Request from customer
1) Short-term: a way to pre-scale before their known ramp.
2) Longer-term: predictive scaling (time-of-day + historical patterns) with clear safeguards.
3) They want to cap spend; any approach must respect their internal budget guardrails.

Current mitigation proposal (pending customer confirmation)
- Set an increased baseline min replicas ahead of ramp window (manual/temporary) while we validate predictive mode.
- Optionally adjust cooldown / scale-up aggressiveness (within safe limits) if it doesn’t risk oscillation.
- If needed, enable limited burst capacity for the ramp window.

Next actions
- [TAM] Confirm customer’s acceptable lead time (e.g., scale 10–15 minutes before ramp) and acceptable overshoot.
- [Support] Provide customer with recommended interim min baseline for the ramp window and a rollback plan.
- [Internal] Nominate Hexagon for predictive scaling pilot; create/route enablement request (INT-9412) once approved.
- [Eng/SRE] Validate whether queue depth is the best primary trigger for this model/workload, and confirm we’re not bottlenecked on cold-start image pull / model load time.

Comments / timeline
2025-06-11 (Dev Patel - Support)
Customer reports repeatable daily ramp causing queueing; requesting predictive scaling or scheduled pre-warm. Added Liam (TAM) and looping SRE for signal review.

2025-06-12 (Liam O'Rourke - TAM)
Confirmed pattern: ramp begins ~13:30 UTC. Customer can provide their daily schedule and historical request rate. They do not want fallback routing enabled.

2025-06-13 (Rafael Mendes - SRE)
Reviewed metrics: scale-up triggers fire but lag is dominated by warm-up (new replica ready time). Suggest interim: increase baseline capacity and/or earlier scale-up bias. Recommend pilot for predictive mode with bounds, plus alerts for max-bound saturation.

2025-06-17 (Allison Grant - Observability)
Shared dashboard panels to monitor: queue depth, desired vs bounded desired, scale event timeline, saturation. Noted we should avoid high-cardinality labels in customer-shared views.

2025-06-20 (Dev Patel - Support)
Proposed interim: increase baseline by +2 replicas during ramp (customer to confirm acceptable cost). Also offered to enroll in pilot for predictive scaling once enabled.

2025-06-24 (Liam O'Rourke - TAM)
Customer agrees to pilot, pending written summary of safeguards (never exceed max, never below min, reactive overrides when prediction wrong). Opening internal request to enable feature flag (INT-9412) after PM approval.

Open questions
- What min baseline provides stable p95 < 1.2s during ramp without significant overprovisioning?
- What lead time is required to account for model load + health checks in us-east?
- Are there any regional capacity constraints that would prevent meeting a proposed min during busy periods?

Proposed resolution criteria for this support ticket
- Customer has an agreed interim configuration that mitigates ramp queueing.
- Customer is enrolled (or scheduled) for predictive autoscaling pilot with clear communication of semantics and known limitations.
- Monitoring/alerting for max-bound saturation is configured for their deployment (or CS/SRE can interpret the standard dashboards during pilot).

Issue summary:
Customer BrightWrite reports intermittent malformed streaming responses from our chat endpoint when a client experiences HTTP/3 path migration (typical on cellular -> WiFi handoff or multi-path routing). The stream begins correctly but in ~1/8 sessions the JSON array that frames choices is malformed: an opening token/choice prefix is duplicated at the start of the resumed stream and the final closing bracket (""]") is missing, causing the client SDK to throw a parse error and the UI to show an incomplete response.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat sessions drop finalization in ~12% of observed path-migrations; customers see truncated output and JSON parse failures.
- Affects enterprise BrightWrite (high usage, multiple concurrent long-running streams).

Environment:
- prod | us-east-1 behind our edge-proxy fleet running HTTP/3 (quic) and HTTP/1.1 fallback.
- Client: BrightWrite mobile app v3.7.1 (iOS 17), they report network path migration events frequently when returning to foreground.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer + internal repro):
1) Start a long chat streaming call against /v1/chat/stream using redwood-chat-v1.
2) Induce path migration on client (cellular -> WiFi, or simulated QUIC path change).
3) Observe the client resumes connection via HTTP/3 with path migration.
4) In approx 1 in 8 attempts the resumed stream payload contains duplicated opening JSON choice tokens and the final closing bracket is not present.

Representative logs (trimmed):
- edge-proxy: "quic: path_migrate event id=0x7fa3, conn=0x2b1f; probe ack duplicate=1"
- api-gateway: "resume: session_id=br-abc123, resume_offset=1024, ack_window_conflict detected"
- serving-runtime: "stream(write): prefix='[
  {\"delta\":\"Hello'""
- client error (BrightWrite): "JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 485 (char 484)"

Observed pattern:
- When the QUIC stack performs a path migration there can be a short period where both old and new ACK windows overlap. In that overlap we observe the edge re-sending a small control frame and the gateway resuming the application stream while the runtime still has a partially-flushed buffer. The result is a duplicated opening fragment (client receives two leading '[' or repeated first token) and the stream termination path is not reliably firing the final '""]" to the resumed connection. The combination yields a syntactically invalid JSON stream.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced in staged environment by forcing a QUIC path migration in lab (NRF hardware + iOS network switch). Repro rate ~10-14% with the current edge-proxy QUIC config.
- Packet traces show two separate ACK sequences where the server-side writecall is executed twice during the handoff window.
- The runtime's flush/commit callbacks rely on a single finalization event that can be dropped if the connection object is torn down mid-flush and a resumed stream is established with a resumed session token.
- No evidence of model-level truncation: token generation continues, it's the framing/finalization that is missing or duplicated.

Hypothesis:
- Race between QUIC path migration ACK handling and our streaming finalization code causes double-send of an opening fragment and loss of final close marker when one of the flush paths is pre-empted.

Short-term mitigation suggested to customer:
- Ask BrightWrite to enable a client-side lightweight reassembly fallback: if stream parse fails, attempt a single re-request with resume=true to fetch trailing tokens (non ideal but reduces impact).
- Turn on connection affinity to avoid QUIC path migration during active streams (if feasible on client).

Next steps (engineering):
1) SRE: add monitoring for malformed-stream-rate across edge-proxy QUIC path-migration events (alert threshold 1%).
2) Edge team: investigate guard to serialize application-layer resume writes until in-flight flushes have deterministically succeeded or timed out (avoid dual-ack overlap).
3) Runtime: make finalization idempotent and resilient to mid-flush connection teardown (ensure final bracket always emitted or persisted to resume log).
4) QA: add fuzz tests simulating path migration and delayed ACKs to catch regressions.

Related artifacts:
- Packet captures and reproducer script uploaded to customer share (link sent to BrightWrite).
- See linked GH PRs for an initial edge-proxy patch that introduces a resume-write mutex.


Additional notes:
2026-03-14 08:10 - Support (Sofia): Shared recommended temporary client workaround with BrightWrite (attempt single re-request on parse failure). Customer accepted workaround and provided business impact details: ~3% of end-user messages affected leads to confusing UX for editors working on long documents.
payload.summary: HTTP/3 path migration + dual ACK race duplicates opening tokens and drops closing JSON bracket on streaming responses

Issue summary: After BrightLens enabled the new 'rate-smoothing' toggle for their dedicated pool and turned on per-route isolation via Console, they reported an increase in 429 responses for long-polling / SSE chat sessions. Impact: ~8% of active chat websocket/SSE connections experienced early 429s over a 45-minute window, causing degraded UX for real-time dashboards. Environment: Dedicated pool allocated to BrightLens, prod clusters in us-east and eu-west. Recent change: Console toggle 'rate-smoothing=v2' rolled out to their pool at 2026-03-13T09:12 UTC; canary rollout completed across both regions by 09:30 UTC. Steps to reproduce: 1) Open ~300 concurrent SSE sessions to the /v1/chat/stream endpoint with keepalive pings every 20s. 2) Send periodic user messages (avg 1 msg per session / 30s) with small-response models (redwood-chat-7b). 3) Observe token/accounting headers and response codes. Observed behavior: At ~09:35 UTC, 429s start appearing after 20-40s of activity; throttle headers indicate per-route token window exhausted despite overall tenant credits available. Expected behavior: Long-lived SSE sessions should see smoothing applied without premature per-route exhaustion; route-isolation should prevent unrelated bulk uploads from affecting live streams. Logs/snippets: - gateway logs show 429s with X-RateLimit-Reason: route_window_exhausted - token accounting snapshot (excerpt): route_window: 120/sec, tenant_remaining: 1.2M tokens, route_remaining: 0; several connections had keepalive pings counted as requests. Temporary workaround applied: Support recommended disabling 'per-route isolation' for this pool which reduced 429s (rolled back by BrightLens at 10:05 UTC).
1) Configure a dedicated pool with per-route isolation and enable rate-smoothing=v2. 2) Start 200-400 SSE connections to /v1/chat/stream with periodic keepalives. 3) Send message bursts (~1 msg per session / 30s). 4) Monitor X-RateLimit-* headers and gateway logs for 429s.
Short-lived 429 spikes for long-polling/SSE clients; headers indicate route_window_exhausted even when tenant credits remain. Keepalive pings appear in accounting and are being double-counted when smoothing transitions are active.
Requests from long-lived sessions should be smoothed such that keepalive heartbeats do not prematurely deplete route windows; per-route isolation should only isolate heavy bulk ingestion routes and not penalize persistent SSE chat traffic.
- Timeline: 09:12 UTC toggle enabled -> 09:30 UTC canary complete -> 09:35 UTC first 429s observed -> 10:05 UTC customer rolled back per-route isolation, 429s decreased. - Hypothesis 1: Rate-smoothing rollout changed refill algorithm; keepalive pings are treated as full weight (not lightweight) during transition window causing token bursts. - Hypothesis 2: Route isolation policy created narrow per-route windows and smoothing added an additional refill delay, causing temporary negative drift. - Evidence: Gateway trace shows keepalive (HTTP 200) followed by immediate token decrement; smoothing actor log includes a 'reconcile_delay' event around 09:34:58. - Repro on staging: Dev reproduced a version of the problem with synthetic SSE connections when using smoothing=v2 and route_min_window set < 200/sec. - Related: INT-4402 contains notes on smoothing reconcile logic and a patch in flight.

2026-03-13 09:55 - Customer (BrightLens, Emma Zhou): We're seeing 429s in our real-time dashboard users; the errors started shortly after enabling the smoothing toggle — can you confirm? Attached sample request IDs: req_7f4a, req_7f5b.
2026-03-13 10:02 - SRE (Tomas Rivera): Investigating. Initial traces show route_window_exhausted flagged. Asking Eng to check smoothing reconcile; filing INT-4402.
2026-03-13 10:08 - Support (Aisha Malik): Workaround suggested: Disable per-route isolation for the pool while we investigate. Customer applied rollback and reported reduction in 429s at 10:12 UTC.
2026-03-13 11:20 - Engineering (Priya Nair): Reproduced in staging with synthetic SSE connections when smoothing=v2 is combined with route_min_window < 200/sec. PR for a reconcile fix created (see github PR).

Under investigation. Current leading cause is a transient negative interaction between new rate-smoothing refill timing and narrow per-route windows that causes keepalive heartbeats to be accounted at full weight during reconciliation windows, depleting route token windows prematurely.
Disable per-route isolation for the affected pool or increase route_min_window to >= 500/sec; reduce keepalive frequency for SSE clients (e.g., 20s -> 60s) to reduce accounting churn.
1) Engineering to merge reconcile timing fix for smoothing actor (PR in review). 2) Run canary hotfix in staging against dedicated-pool simulation. 3) If verified, schedule emergency patch deployment to production with coordinated customer notifications. 4) Postmortem + console guidance: update UI to warn about combining route-isolation with smoothing=v2 for small route windows.

Issue summary:
During a regional proxy reshard (edge-proxy rolling update) that coincided with a small canary weight increase, a subset of tenant sessions lost their in-memory session affinity keys and were silently routed to an older model variant (redwood-beta-1.2) instead of the pinned redwood-beta-1.3.

Impact:
- Customer TextWave Labs (dedicated) reported subtle quality regressions for ~2% of requests over a 22 minute window in us-east.
- Requests were not returning explicit 5xx; responses came from a lower-version model causing semantic mismatch for production prompts.
- No rate-limits or errors logged at edge; routing decision mismatch is root symptom.

Environment:
- Prod - us-east cluster (edge-proxy 1.4.7 -> 1.4.9 rolling update at 2026-03-12T09:03Z)
- Routing service v2.9.1, canary-coordinator v0.18.4
- Affected customer on dedicated pool with model pin redwood-beta-1.3 pinned at route level

Timeline (UTC):
- 09:03: rolling update of edge-proxy started (reshard to reduce connection hot-spots)
- 09:07: canary weight bumped 1% -> 5% for redwood-beta-1.3 per automated rollout
- 09:10: TextWave CS reported intermittent semantic regressions via support channel (#support-textwave)
1) Have a tenant with model pin to redwood-beta-1.3 and active sessions.
2) Start a rolling reshard of edge-proxy in same region.
3) During reshard, adjust canary weight up by small increment (~1-5%).
4) Observe routing logs and session-affinity mappings for that tenant.
5) Reproduce by replaying live traffic through routing simulator capturing session cookie headers and routing decisions.
A fraction of sessions lost their affinity token mapping at the routing layer and were routed to variant redwood-beta-1.2 (older variant) without triggering clear errors. The edge logs show success 200 but model variant header indicates older model. No explicit pin-removal event was recorded; session token was present on the request but not resolved to tenant binding on a subset of edge proxy instances.
Pinned sessions should preserve variant affinity regardless of edge-proxy reshard. If mapping cannot be resolved, routing should fall back to safe failure mode (reject / route to fallback with explicit log/metric) rather than silently routing to older variant.
- edge-proxy access sample: tenant=twl-378 path=/v1/generate model-header=redwood-beta-1.2 x-session-token=abc123 status=200 latency=88ms
- routing-service trace: request_id=rq-9a4f, affinity_lookup: MISS on proxy-12, HIT on proxy-9
- canary-coordinator audit: weight-change by automated-rollout (operator=auto, change=+4%) at 2026-03-12T09:07Z
- no 5xx or quota logs during window
(Full log bundle attached to ticket in support portal: twl-831905-logs.tar.gz)
Hypothesis: an edge-proxy reshard caused transient eviction of in-memory affinity cache on a subset of proxies. The routing-service uses multi-hop affinity resolution: edge -> local cache -> global state. During the reshard, local cache was cleared but the proxy continued to forward session tokens without waiting for coherent state, and the routing policy allowed routing to any compatible variant. Canary weight change exposed the race by creating new eligible variant set (1.2 and 1.3), where missing affinity resolved to lowest-priority compatible variant (1.2).
Investigation steps taken:
- Replayed sample traffic through staging with proxy versions and observed affinity cache miss behavior on proxies upgraded with sharded config.
- Confirmed routing service recently changed tie-breaker behavior when affinity lookup fails (recent PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-service/pull/907 changed fallback ordering).
- Reproduced in lab by forcing local affinity cache flush during weight change: observed routes to older variant consistent with customer reports.
Applied temporary mitigation for TextWave: pinned at tenant-level in routing service (force-route to redwood-beta-1.3) and paused automated canary weight adjustments for that tenant's route. Notified customer and increased monitoring on model-variant headers. Deployed a proxy-side hold-before-forwards patch to stagger request forwarding until local affinity store warms (~5s).
1) Roll a backward-compatible fix to routing-service tie-breaker to prefer pinned variant when affinity token present (PR in flight).
2) Add explicit guard in edge-proxy to treat affinity cache misses as 'degraded' and consult global state synchronously for pinned tenants.
3) Add canary-runbook step: avoid simultaneous proxy reshard + canary-weight changes in same window.
4) Postmortem and runbook update; coordinate with rollout team to prevent concurrent operations.
5) Notify TextWave of timeline for permanent fix and offer extended monitoring window.
Priya Nair (Support) 2026-03-12T10:02Z: Customer reported semantic regressions; attached sample requests and timestamps. Escalated to SRE due to cross-service behavior.
Liam Chen (SRE) 2026-03-12T11:15Z: Investigating — initial traces point to affinity lookup misses on a subset of edge-proxy instances. Reproducing locally by simulating cache flush + canary bump.
Ava Martinez (Routing Eng) 2026-03-12T13:04Z: Found related change in routing-service fallback ordering (PR #907). Looks like tie-breaker now picks the lexicographically first compatible variant when affinity absent. Working on a patch to prefer pinned variant if token present.
Customer (TextWave Ops) 2026-03-12T14:30Z: Thank you — impacts are small but we see visible model drift on production prompts. Please prioritize tenant-level mitigation.

Issue summary: Customer reports an elevated and sustained 429 error rate when their ingestion system performs parallel webhook retries after transient failures. The pattern appears only during coordinated retry waves from many short-lived workers, not during steady-state traffic.

Impact: Several of LuminaSearch's ingest pipelines see 20-40% of requests returning 429 for 10-45 minutes during a retry storm. This causes backfill queues to balloon and downstream indexing to lag. Customer is on a Dedicated pool and needs guidance to avoid reoccurrence.

Environment: Dedicated capacity (pool id: ded-us-east-17), prod, region us-east. Customer uses short-lived API keys (rotated every 6h) and a fan-out webhook retrier that spins up hundreds of parallel workers on failure.

Request: Customer asks what combination of backoff, concurrency, and tenant-level rate/quota settings will prevent tenant-wide token exhaustion and whether Dedicated pool configuration can be tuned to isolate their burst without impacting other tenants.
1) Configure an ingestion runner to fan out 300 parallel short-lived workers.
2) Each worker issues a POST /v1/generate request to the Redwood API using a short-lived key, then on any non-2xx retries immediately with jitter disabled for the first 2 attempts.
3) Introduce a transient 503 from an upstream dependency for 30s to cause simultaneous retries.
4) Observe 429 rate across the tenant shortly after upstream flakiness and lasting until token buckets refill or traffic reduces.
[2026-03-10T09:14:02Z] ingress-fanout-187 POST /v1/generate 200ms -> 503 upstream; worker retries (ID wkr-129)
[2026-03-10T09:14:04Z] gateway rate-limit check tenant TID-449 token-bucket remaining: 0
[2026-03-10T09:14:04Z] gateway respond 429 x 1200 (approx over 90s)
[2026-03-10T09:25:10Z] rate-limiter refill heartbeat +300 tokens (window delta mismatch noted)
Initial hypothesis: Short-lived keys + parallel retry fanout causes per-key and per-tenant accounting to misattribute tokens, creating sudden token-bucket exhaustion.
Checked rate-limiter logs: refill cadence matched config but observed larger-than-expected drain events coinciding with key rotation windows.
Observed that health-checks and some internal monitoring probes from customer hosts were counted towards tenant quota during the spike (see gateway logs).
Confirmed dedicated pool capacity was healthy (GPUs not saturated) and serving-runtime latencies were nominal — issue is quota accounting rather than compute shortage.
Short-term: Have customer reduce parallel worker fanout to <= 50 concurrent callers and enable exponential backoff with base 200ms and jitter for 3 attempts. Avoid coordinated key rotations during active backfills. We suggested pause-and-stagger pattern for retries. Support provided a sample retry wrapper.
Mid-term: Support can enable a temporary burst allowance for tenant TID-449 while we tune quotas.
Enable per-route isolation for heavy ingestion routes (route-level token buckets) to separate webhooks from interactive traffic.
Increase tenant burst window temporarily (burst_tokens + burst_window_ms) on dedicated pool for scheduled backfills.
Switch customer to use longer-lived ingestion keys for worker pools and rotate using a rolling scheme to avoid synchronized expiries.
Recommend client-side exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter (Full Jitter) and capped concurrent workers per host.
Pending: engineering to review quota accounting when short-lived keys are presented in high fanout scenarios. Support to coordinate a one-off burst increase. No code fix yet; configuration guidance provided. Marking as In Progress until engineering validates long-term config options.
2026-03-10T12:02:14Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Logged initial reproduction and asked for sample traffic pattern and sample keys. Customer provided payloads and a small reproducer script.
2026-03-10T15:38:22Z - Diego Ramos (SRE): Confirmed that serving hosts were healthy. Attached rate-limiter debug traces and noted token-bucket delta events around 09:14Z. Asked customer to reduce fanout as immediate mitigation.
2026-03-11T08:10:41Z - LuminaSearch (Customer): Implemented reduced fanout and observed immediate drop in 429s. Asked about significance of short-lived keys vs per-tenant accounting.
2026-03-11T10:05:03Z - Diego Ramos (SRE): Explained that short-lived keys amplify per-key windows in our accounting and recommended longer-lived pool keys + rolling rotation. Opened ENG ticket to review per-key accounting logic.

Issue summary: BrightNote AI (dedicated tenant) reported intermittent 5xx responses on streaming chat routes during a three-hour window on 2026-03-12 evening. Impact: degraded streaming sessions and user-visible failed tokens for ~120 requests. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool, small sustained concurrency (~2-4 long-lived streams). Observed behavior: 5xxs are interleaved (not a continuous wave) and correlate with ephemeral-worker CPU surge and very short-lived runtime restarts, but only for this tenant and only when traffic is low.
Customer saw ~0.6% error rate spike on streaming endpoints across a three-hour window; a handful of user sessions experienced dropped streams and reconnect loops. Customer reported immediate business impact for a subset of paying users during evening hours. They requested root cause and mitigation; account-level SLA at risk for repeated incidents.
Observed in prod: query streaming.chat.start with a single short prompt and keep streams open for ~60s; repeat with 2-3 concurrent small sessions
Reproduced locally in staging by enabling ephemeral-proxy debug flags and lowering keepalive to 20s; rate of 503s increased when an accept-queue drain coincided with prefetch cancellation
Test harness used: loadgen script (internal) that emulates BrightNote traffic pattern (3x long-lived small-payload streams)
[2026-03-12T20:11:03Z] runtime-ephemeral-42 CPU 97% hotloop detected: poll() -> prefetch_cancel -> retry() -> backoff(0ms)
[2026-03-12T20:11:04Z] apigw-178 502 upstream reset: grpc: upstream terminated unexpectedly
[2026-03-12T20:11:05Z] ephemeral-proxy-acceptqueue overflow: accept_queue_depth=84 threshold=80
[2026-03-12T20:12:12Z] runtime-ephemeral-42 watchdog: restarting worker due to live-loop (reason=hotloop-detected)
Initial triage (Support): validated error spike for tenant BrightNote AI in us-east between 20:05-23:15 UTC; spike is small but customer-visible.
SRE triage: CPU profiles show a tight spin between two code paths in the runtime: prefetch cancellation and keepalive handling. Hotloop occurs when a cancellation and an accept-queue re-entrant callback race.
Correlated metrics: ephemeral worker CPU, short-lived process restarts, accept_queue_depth spikes, and apigw 502/503 increments align within seconds of each other.
Hypothesis 1: a scheduler/ephemeral-proxy timing regression introduced a reentrant callback leading to a busy-wait in certain low-concurrency workflows (reproducible when keepalive < 30s).
Hypothesis 2: tenant-specific prefetch settings cause a path that bypasses usual backoff, amplifying the hotloop on low traffic where long-lived streams are present.
Staging reproduction: toggling prefetch off for the tenant eliminated hotloop; reproducer shows accept_queue oscillation is the triggering condition.
Related: linked to previous ticket SUP-412987 which had a keepalive drift fix; rolling window of changes likely exposed a race in the runtime (see PR 4892).
Immediate: Support applied account-level mitigation by disabling request prefetch for BrightNote AI (temporary) — reduced 5xxs to baseline.
Operational: SRE added an ephemeral-proxy rate limiter and bumped accept-queue threshold for the affected host pool to reduce transient overflow.
Follow-up workaround: for any dedicated tenant seeing similar symptoms, we recommend toggling prefetch to "off" and increasing keepalive threshold to >= 45s while patch is applied.
Support (2026-03-12T15:40Z) - Aisha Patel: Customer reports intermittent 5xx on streaming routes; attached traces and timestamp range. Assigned to SRE for root cause.
SRE (2026-03-12T16:10Z) - Marcus Lee: Observed ephemeral worker CPU spin in metric profiles. Adding ephemeral-proxy and runtime owners to investigate. Reproducing in staging now.
Customer (BrightNote AI) (2026-03-12T17:01Z): Appreciate the quick response. We're seeing failed messages in production logs; any ETA on fix?
SRE (2026-03-12T18:25Z) - Marcus Lee: Applied tenant-level prefetch disable as a short-term mitigation. Please confirm if errors drop (Support to validate with customer).
Support (2026-03-12T18:34Z) - Aisha Patel: Customer confirmed errors dropped to baseline after mitigation. Continuing investigation for permanent fix.
Runtime Eng (2026-03-13T09:12Z) - Elena Gomez: Identified race in prefetch cancellation path; preparing a targeted runtime patch (hotfix branch).
SRE (2026-03-14T08:05Z) - Marcus Lee: Hotfix deployed to canary pool (runtime v1.4.7-hotfix); monitoring for recurrence.
Partial mitigation: tenant prefetch disabled to stop immediate errors. Permanent fix: runtime patch v1.4.7 will include a guarded cancellation path and backoff to prevent busy-wait; scheduled rollout to prod canary on 2026-03-14, global rollout pending validation. Customer notified and workaround documented.
Hotfix details: PR #4892 contains the guarded cancellation + exponential backoff change; avoids tight retry loops when accept_queue oscillates.
Canary rollout plan: 10% pool for 2 hours -> monitor CPU and 5xx telemetry -> 50% -> full rollout. Abort criteria: >0.2% increase in 5xx or CPU anomaly on non-related tenants.
Post-incident follow-up: add automated regression test in staging that simulates low-concurrency long-lived streams with prefetch enabled; add alert on ephemeral-worker spin metrics and small-tenant 5xx elevation.
Customer follow-up: Provide BrightNote AI with postmortem summary and recommended tenant config defaults (prefetch=off for now; keepalive>=45s).
Monitor canary runtime v1.4.7-hotfix for 24 hours and collect CPU/5xx trend for the affected host pool.
If canary is stable, schedule progressive rollout and notify support teams of expected windows.
Update BrightNote AI with the postmortem and timeline for full rollout (target completion 2026-03-16).
Add a smoke test and alert rule that triggers when ephemeral-worker CPU > 80% for >1m with correlated 5xx bump for a single tenant.
Create INT ticket to review scheduler timing changes introduced in previous keepalive fix to avoid regressions (INT-2220).
