Issue summary:
We observed an elevated and oscillating 5xx rate impacting a single enterprise tenant (AuroraMaps) in us-east. Error patterns correlate with API Gateway throttling spikes and upstream runtime processes being forcibly reclaimed / OOM-killed. The symptom set looks like a misprediction in the adaptive throttler combined with memory pressure in a subset of runtime pods serving mixed embedding and chat workloads.

Impact:
- ~15% of AuroraMaps requests in the window returned 502/503/504 intermittently (streaming and non-streaming routes).
- Latency for successful requests increased (p50 -> +120ms, p95 -> +800ms).
- Customer reported degraded user experience for map annotation features using chat + embedding mix; ticket raised via support channel.

Environment:
- prod-us-east cluster (k8s), mixed node types (A100 and T4 pools).
- Affected model variants: rwd-13b-quant-v2 (embedding-heavy), rwd-chat-7b-compat (chat sessions).
- Traffic pattern: sudden concurrent embedding bulk uploads + many long-lived chat streams from same tenant.

Timeline (local times):
- 2026-03-13T14:18Z: First alert from Grafana (error-rate spike on apigw-us-east).
- 2026-03-13T14:20Z: Support alerted SRE and customer; initial triage started.
- 2026-03-13T14:25Z: Observed runtime pod restarts; kernel messages show memory_reclaim invoked and killer invoked on cgroup tasks.
- 2026-03-13T14:40Z: Temporary mitigation applied (see Mitigation).

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) From a single tenant in prod-us-east, start a mix: concurrent embedding bulk upload (small-batch parallelized) + ~200 concurrent long-lived streaming chat sessions.
2) Observe accept-queue growth at apigw and throttler marking more aggressive shedding policy.
3) After throttle engages, backpressure causes hedged retries and request fanout that drives certain runtime pods into heavy memory churn and kernel reclamation.

Observed logs / metrics / traces:
- Grafana panel: apigw error-rate spiked to 18% at peak; upstream 502/503 logs show short-lived connection resets and 504 timeouts. (link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/alerts/apigw-us-east?from=...)
- Kernel logs on impacted runtimes: "kswapd0 high memory reclaim" and repeated "oom-killer: Kill process 14231 (runtime_worker) score 912" entries.
- Runtime logs: repeated GC-like pause messages, KV-cache eviction thrash, and the serving runtime logged "memory pressure: reclaim fallback" before exit.
- Traces show high queueing delay at apigw (acceptqueue length) and hedged retry amplification for streaming routes.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Support/SRE advised customer to throttle embedding bulk upload parallelism for AuroraMaps. Customer applied application-side rate-limit (reduced concurrency by 60%).
- We muted hedged retries at apigw for the tenant route to avoid retry amplification (config change rolled to canary then to entire us-east apigw pool at 14:38Z).
- Increased autoscaler warm headroom for the A100 runtime pool serving the tenant by +2 replicas to provide extra memory capacity during warmup.
- Marked two runtime nodes as drained and rotated them after kernel-level memory reclaim evidence.

Investigation notes / hypothesis:
- Hypothesis A: Adaptive throttler mispredicted working set because it used short-window token-rate features; sudden mix of embedding + streaming caused acceptance heuristic to swing too low, causing apigw to enforce harsh shedding. That shed traffic into retry loops which amplified demand on the runtime pool.
- Hypothesis B: Long-lived chat sessions pinned KV-cache slots while embedding bulk created burst memory allocations (for batched tokenization / embedding tensors). Combination caused host OOM reclaim of cgroup slices and killed some runtime workers.
- Evidence: correlated kernel OOM lines with times of bursty embedding operations; heap profiles from one runtime show transient large allocations around embedding batching code paths.
- Alternate contributing factor: hedged-retry policy at the gateway caused duplicate work to be sent to runtimes when latency spiked, magnifying memory footprint.

Immediate next steps (owner: Ravi Patel):
- Collect full heap profiles from a surviving runtime pod and upload to S3 for heapdiff analysis (tasked, ETA 2026-03-14 11:00Z).
- Reproduce in staging with synthetic mixed workload (owner: SRE QA) and validate throttler prediction smoothing changes.
- Instrument toggles to disable hedged retries per-tenant as a short-term safety valve (dev ticket created).
- Add a quota guard on embedding batch concurrency per-tenant in apigw (product follow-up).

Longer-term actions:
- Adjust adaptive throttler to include longer-window memory-pressure signals and a smoothing window for sudden bimodal payloads.
- Add per-tenant memory-accounting in scheduler to avoid overcommitting runtime node memory when multiple heavy-tenants run mixed workloads.
- Postmortem runbook and customer communication template (owner: CS/Support).

Customer communication status:
- AuroraMaps notified via support email at 14:30Z; they confirmed reduced throughput is acceptable as temporary workaround. They requested a root-cause summary and ETA for permanent fix.

2026-03-13T14:22Z - Maya Chen (Support): Notified SRE on #support and opened this ticket. Customer experiencing 5xx on embedding and chat routes. Asked for immediate triage.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13T14:33Z - Ravi Patel (SRE): Observed OOM-killer traces on 3 runtime pods. Suspect memory reclaim. Isolating pods and pulling heap profiles now.
2026-03-13T14:38Z - Maya Chen (Support): Applied mitigation with customer: reduced client-side embedding concurrency and disabled hedged retries. Error-rate dropped to ~4% after config change.
2026-03-13T15:05Z - Dev-Lead (Infra): Recommending throttler smoothing and per-tenant concurrency guard. Logged infra ticket: INFRA-9204.
2026-03-14T10:45Z - Ravi Patel (SRE): Uploaded heap profile to S3 (s3://redwood-debug/prod/heap/720720-20260313.prof) and submitted analysis PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5427.
Mitigated: customer-side concurrency reduced, hedged retries disabled for tenant, autoscaler headroom increased. Ongoing: collecting profiles and running staging repro for throttle tuning.
payload.summary: Oscillating 5xx surge from adaptive throttle misprediction and runtime memory reclamation during mixed-embedding/chat traffic

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightHealth AI reports a reproducible scenario where a long-running function/tool invocation initiated from their Go backend results in the external webhook being executed twice after an HTTP/2 connection migration. The call itself is a user-supplied webhook (external billing service) that performs an irreversible charge. They are seeing duplicate charges in the customer's logs when clients are migrated between edge proxies during an extended tool run.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream billing charges observed for ~2% of long-running tool calls (approx 120 events/day).
- Affects production traffic on BrightHealth's Dedicated pool in us-west.
- High customer severity: financial double-billing and support escalations.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated - us-west cluster
- Go SDK (v1.14.2) running on customer app servers behind a cloud load balancer
- Dedicated pool config: keepalive 90s, stream_idle_timeout 120s
- External webhook is synchronous (customer waits for 200 OK) and performs the charge on first receipt

Observed behavior:
- Client starts a function/tool call that takes >25s to complete (external processing time).
- During the long execution, client connection gets migrated (HTTP/2 GOAWAY + reconnect) by an edge proxy under normal scale events.
- Redwood runtime does not see a tool-level confirmation before connection drop; SDK retries the request which causes Redwood to re-dispatch the tool call to the webhook endpoint.
- Webhook endpoint receives two near-duplicate deliveries: the first eventually times out on the SDK-side because the original TCP stream was closed without a final acknowledgement being persisted; the second delivery completes successfully. Customer backend records both deliveries as separate charges.

Customer asks:
1) Is there a recommended at-most-once pattern for long-running tool/webhook calls using the Go SDK?
2) Any SDK configuration or console settings that reduce probability of this race?
3) Recommended server-side webhook acknowledgment semantics to avoid duplicate charges?
1) In Go SDK v1.14.2 start a function call that performs an external POST and intentionally sleeps >20s before responding.
2) During the in-flight request simulate connection migration by issuing an HTTP/2 GOAWAY on the client-side edge (or kill client TCP and reconnect).
3) Observe SDK behavior: it retries the request after connection loss and Redwood serving runtime dispatches a second webhook invocation.
4) Verify external webhook received two near-identical POSTs and both were processed as independent charges.
2026-03-10T14:12:03.121Z serve-12345 INFO incoming request: client_id=bhai-51, call_id=call-0a9f
2026-03-10T14:12:28.456Z edge-proxy WARN GOAWAY initiated: draining streams
2026-03-10T14:12:28.460Z go-sdk WARN connection lost, retrying call call-0a9f attempt=2
2026-03-10T14:12:29.012Z runtime INFO dispatch tool webhook: target=payments.brighthealth.ai charge_id=chg-233
2026-03-10T14:12:29.115Z webhook-server INFO received POST /charge request-id=chg-233 status=processing
2026-03-10T14:12:55.789Z webhook-server INFO completed charge req-id=chg-233 status=success
2026-03-10T14:12:56.002Z runtime INFO dispatch tool webhook: target=payments.brighthealth.ai charge_id=chg-234
2026-03-10T14:12:56.210Z webhook-server INFO received POST /charge request-id=chg-234 status=processing
2026-03-10T14:13:22.333Z webhook-server INFO completed charge req-id=chg-234 status=success

Note: call_id is the SDK-side call identifier. We did not observe a persisted server-level tool confirmation for call-0a9f before the GOAWAY.
Initial hypothesis: retries are triggered by the Go SDK after connection loss and runtime treats retries as new delivery attempts because no idempotency/confirmation handshake was completed. The serving runtime will re-dispatch a tool invocation when an SDK connection is lost and the request context does not include a server-side acknowledged execution token.

What we checked:
- Verified Go SDK version; found a known backoff/retry path that will re-send a request if the transport is reset and no final success envelope observed.
- Traced the runtime: when a tool call is in-flight the runtime expects either a tool-level ACK (persisted) or final response. If the connection terminates before ACK persistence, the request is considered incomplete and is eligible for replay.
- Customer's webhook is synchronous and has no idempotency protection (no idempotency-key header), so two deliveries are treated as unique.

Likelihood: High. The combination of long external processing time + connection migration is the root cause. This is not a bug in the serving runtime per se; it's an interplay between connection-level semantics and how customers implement webhooks.

Short-term mitigation candidates we evaluated:
- Reduce keepalive and increase client retry backoff windows (customer-side) to avoid aggressive resend during short transient migrations. Tradeoffs: increases latency and may reduce user experience for legitimately slow calls.
- Configure Go SDK to enable a client-side dedupe layer (per-call idempotency key header) so that resends carry stable idempotency tokens. SDK currently supports passing metadata/headers on tool invocation; recommend customers populate a stable per-tool-call idempotency header before invoking.
- Runtime-level ack: persist a lightweight 'receipt' earlier in tool dispatch path where possible so a second dispatch can be suppressed. This requires changes to runtime and guarantees around external webhook latencies; engineering cost medium.
2026-03-10 15:02 - Support (Aisha): Reached out to customer for sample request traces and webhook payloads. Asked for approximate fraction of long calls and business impact.
2026-03-10 16:10 - BrightHealth (Rachel, eng): Provided traces and confirmed two charge IDs; they cannot roll back the charge easily. Asked for immediate mitigation steps.
2026-03-11 09:20 - SRE (Marco): Confirmed runtime will re-dispatch when no tool-ack is persisted. Filed follow-up internal RFC to examine earlier persistence points for tool dispatch receipts (see related PR).
2026-03-11 11:40 - Support (Aisha): Suggested two immediate mitigations: (1) Add an idempotency header on the customer webhook payload that they check server-side to dedupe; (2) Configure Go SDK to increase initial retry delay to avoid flapping resends during short migrations. Provided sample code snippet for setting metadata headers in the Go SDK.
2026-03-11 15:55 - BrightHealth (Rachel): Implemented idempotency check on payments endpoint and rolled to 10% of traffic; duplicate charges dropped to ~0.1% during the canary. Asked for long-term platform guidance.
Workaround and recommended steps (customer-facing):
1) SHORT-TERM (immediate): Implement a per-call idempotency token on your webhook side (e.g., X-Redwood-Tool-Idempotency). Populate that token from the Go SDK metadata for the tool invocation. If you see duplicate deliveries, abandon second delivery if idempotency token already consumed. This was confirmed to reduce duplicates in the customer's canary.

2) SDK CONFIG (customer): In Go SDK v1.14.x, set a conservative retry/backoff for long-running calls (example: initial_backoff=500ms, max_backoff=10s) and consider increasing keepalive to reduce mid-flight migrations during normal operation. We provided example code in comment (sent to customer).

3) SERVER/PLATFORM: We will investigate an improvement to the runtime dispatch path to persist a lightweight 'dispatch receipt' earlier (ack-on-dispatch) so that a reconnect-induced retry can be suppressed. Owner: SRE/Serving runtime team (internal RFC opened, see github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1678).

4) LONG-TERM PATTERN: For irreversible side-effects (billing, provisioning), require idempotency semantics at the webhook receiver and use confirmation tokens for finalization. Recommended runbook: Confluence page 'stream-retry-and-ack-contracts' updated with a code sample and step-by-step migration checklist.

Follow-ups created:
- ENG task to scope runtime early-ack persistence (internal ticket INT-80921).
- Documentation task to publish Go SDK example and recommended headers (DOCS-345).

Ticket status: In Progress. Customer confirmed temporary mitigations and will monitor for 72h. Engineering work to address runtime changes is in discovery.
payload.summary: Go SDK long-running tool call: connection handoff causes webhook to be re-executed; asking for at-most-once patterns and recommended SDK config

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled canary weight increase for OrbitApps (dedicated tenant in prod-us-east), a subset of commit events for the rollout were applied out of order at the rollout-coordinator. This produced transient mismatch between tenant pin state and edge routing cache, triggering fallback routing to the legacy model variant and intermittent 5xx for some streams.

Impact: Customers (OrbitApps) observed 10-15% of requests being served by the older model variant for ~8 minutes during a weight shift. Some streaming sessions dropped with 502/504. Business impact: degraded user experience for production traffic; OrbitApps flagged as P1.

Initial hypothesis: ingress event queue (SQS-like) reordering combined with non-idempotent commit handling allowed a later rollback/health-check event to be applied before the successful commit, causing the coordinator state machine to transiently revert and then reapply commits in a way that left edge caches inconsistent.
1) Create a staged canary rollout for a dedicated tenant pinned to gpt-open-13b-v2.
2) Generate ~2000 rps of traffic from multiple edge nodes to exercise distributed commit propagation.
3) Inject synthetic small delay and reorder on one ingress instance (simulate slow ACK from queue consumer).
4) Trigger health-check probe failure on canary instance, then restore, then increase canary weight.
5) Observe routing decisions at edge and check tenant pin state in rollout-coordinator and edge cache.

Expected: commits applied in causally consistent order leading to consistent pin state across edge and coordinator.
Observed: coordinator logged commit IDs in non-monotonic order and edge returned older variant for subset of tokens until cache TTL expired or explicit invalidation applied.
[2026-03-10T14:02:10Z] rollout-coordinator: commit_id=abc123 applied weight->20% for tenant=orbitapps
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] ingress-gateway-3: dequeued event commit_id=abc125 (rollback healthcheck)
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] rollout-coordinator: commit_id=abc125 applied weight->5% for tenant=orbitapps (healthprobe-triggered)
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] ingress-gateway-1: dequeued event commit_id=abc123
[2026-03-10T14:02:13Z] edge-proxy-9: cache miss tenant=orbitapps, routing->legacy-variant, response=502
[2026-03-10T14:09:20Z] support: received customer alert: "Some sessions are being answered by older model, intermittent errors"

- Reproduced locally by adding artificial dequeue jitter; confirmed reordering risk when multiple ingress consumers read from an at-least-once delivery queue and do not coordinate commit sequence.
- Coordinator lacked strict commit-sequence enforcement: commits applied based on arrival timestamp without verifying monotonic commit sequence IDs.
- Edge cache TTL (30s) combined with delayed invalidation allowed older routing to persist beyond coordinator reconciliation window.
- Autoscaler/drain events create additional churn that increases likelihood of reordered deliveries.
- No evidence that serving-runtime served wrong weights; root cause is orchestration/commit ordering gap between ingress and coordinator.
- Telemetry shows spike in commit_out_of_order counter between 14:02-14:10 for tenant orbitapps.
- Related previous tickets SUP-31147 and SUP-4721 surfaced similar pin inconsistency patterns but were tied to cache warmup; this one differs due to explicit queue reordering and commit application race.
2026-03-10T14:15:00Z - Support (Aisha Fernandez): Notified SRE and assigned to Eric. Customer reported degraded UX; asked for steps being taken and ETA.
2026-03-10T14:27:12Z - SRE (Eric Liang): Confirmed logs show commit_id ordering mismatch. Immediately increased edge cache invalidation frequency for orbitapps route as a stop-gap. Asking infra to preserve delivery ordering for rollout events.
2026-03-10T15:02:45Z - Customer (OrbitApps - product lead Jenna Park): We see intermittent fallbacks; appreciate quick action. Can you provide a rollback plan if issue persists?
2026-03-10T15:10:02Z - Support (Aisha): Provided manual pin override steps to force tenant to desired commit and initiated a canary pause. Shared temporary rollback playbook.
2026-03-11T09:04:33Z - Rollout eng (Marta Kaur): Patch proposed to coordinator to enforce monotonic commit sequence validation and make commit application idempotent. Preparing PR and integration tests.
Temporary workaround: Applied targeted edge cache invalidation for tenant routes and performed manual pin override to re-establish desired model variant while investigation continued. This reduced fallback rate to <1% within 3 minutes.

Permanent fix (in progress): 1) Add monotonic-sequence guard in rollout-coordinator: reject or queue commits with lower sequence numbers than last_applied for that tenant. 2) Make coordinator commit application idempotent (store commit_id and short-term dedupe). 3) Improve ingress consumer to tag events with global sequence numbers sourced from coordinator when possible, and otherwise persist ordering in a lightweight sequence log. 4) Update edge cache invalidation to accept explicit invalidation events tied to commit_id. 5) Add new telemetry metric commit_reorder_count and dashboard alerts.

Planned rollout of fix: merge PR -> canary deploy to staging -> dedicated tenant pilot (not affecting public tenants) -> prod canary -> full rollout. Target ETA for prod fix: 2026-03-20.
Create a runbook for manual pin override and edge invalidation (owner: support) - due 2026-03-13
Merge coordinator monotonic-sequence PR and add unit/integration tests (owner: rollout team) - due 2026-03-17
Instrument commit_reorder_count metric and add alert for >0.1% reorders per minute (owner: telemetry) - due 2026-03-15
Perform chaos test simulating ingress consumer jitter on staging to validate fix (owner: reliability) - due 2026-03-18
Postmortem and customer communication once fix is live (owner: SRE+CS) - due after prod rollout

Issue summary
Aurora Search is reporting that Structured Output (JSON-schema / strict schema validation) returns validation errors that are hard to interpret and sometimes inconsistent across request types (streaming vs non-streaming) and SDKs. Errors frequently lack:
- Which field/path failed validation
- Whether the failure is due to schema shape vs model output vs response_format configuration
- A copy/paste-ready example of a valid output for the given schema

Customer impact
- Increased time-to-triage for what should be a simple client-side fix
- Multiple repeat tickets from different engineers on the same team (same symptom, different prompts)
- Customers are turning off structured output or adding brittle post-processing, increasing failure rate and Support volume

Customer request
1) Improve error message clarity (field path + constraint + example)
2) Docs: add a troubleshooting section + guidance on common mistakes (arrays vs objects, required fields, enums, additionalProperties)
3) SDKs: ensure the error surfaces request_id and a stable error code that Support can search

Environment
- Hosted API (prod), regions observed: us-east + eu-west
- Models: redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct and redwood/qwen2.5-32b-instruct
- Customer reports the issue in both Python SDK and TypeScript SDK; we reproduced with raw HTTP as well

What the customer sees (anonymized)
A) Non-streaming request returns 400 with vague message
- HTTP 400
- message: "Structured output validation failed" (no field path)
- sometimes includes: "schema invalid" even when schema is accepted on other calls

B) Streaming request fails mid-stream with an SSE error event that does not contain validation details
- stream ends with an error
- customer cannot tell whether partial output was invalid JSON, missing required keys, wrong types, etc.

Example schema (customer-provided, lightly anonymized)
- Object with required fields: {"id": string, "confidence": number, "tags": array<string>}
- Customer reports that if the model returns confidence as a quoted string ("0.82"), the error does not indicate which field is wrong

Support reproduction (internal)
- Using curl against /v1/chat/completions with response_format set to JSON schema.
- When forcing the model to return an invalid type for a required field, we see a generic validation error without a pointer (e.g., "confidence") and without the offending value.

Expected
- Error response should include:
  - Stable error code (e.g., structured_output.validation_failed)
  - request_id (already in headers; ensure included/propagated in SDK exceptions)
  - JSON pointer / field path (e.g., $.confidence)
  - Expected type/constraint + actual type (e.g., expected number, got string)
  - Actionable guidance ("return a number, not a quoted string")

Notes / constraints
- Do not include customer prompts verbatim in broadly visible docs.
- If we include snippets, use short, generic examples and clearly label them.
- Ensure error payload is safe to log (avoid echoing full model output; consider truncation and redaction).

Ask / next steps
- Eng: confirm current validation layer (gateway vs runtime) and what details are available to surface safely.
- Docs/DevEx: draft a structured output troubleshooting page + add to known-issues index if we want Support deflection.
- Support: add a macro for "Structured output validation" that requests schema + minimal failing output + request_id and links to docs once published.
2026-02-20 (Priya Shah): Customer reports repeated confusion with structured output errors. They are getting "validation failed" without the failing field. Asked for 3 request_ids and their response_format payload (schema only, no prompt).
2026-02-20 (Owen Phillips): Confirmed we should treat as P2/Sev3 (no platform outage). Tagging as deflection candidate for known-issues sprint. Added to Support macro refresh list.
2026-02-21 (Customer - Aurora Search, via Support email): Provided request_ids: rwreq_01HSO8V7Y3QK2..., rwreq_01HSO8W1N9J0A..., rwreq_01HSO8W6TQ0F7... (full IDs in private note). Reports both Python 1.18.2 and TS 0.9.4. Says error is "schema invalid" on some calls, "validation failed" on others for same schema.
2026-02-21 (Owen Phillips): Reproduced with curl using an internal test prompt. Observed response is 400 with generic message; no JSON path. In streaming mode, error arrives as SSE event "error" with message only. Looping in Platform for error payload consistency guidance.
2026-02-22 (Ethan Park): Took a look. We currently collapse validator errors to a single message at the API boundary to avoid leaking output. We should be able to safely include JSON pointer + expected/actual types without including full output. Agree this is a gap. Suggest creating a small structured error object and truncating any sample value to N chars if we include it.
2026-02-22 (Wei Chen): From docs side: we don’t have a dedicated troubleshooting section for structured output beyond the basic guide. I can draft a short page with common failures (required fields, enums, type mismatches, additionalProperties) and recommended prompt patterns. Need final error codes/payload shape to document.
2026-02-23 (Owen Phillips): Created follow-up items in Linear: ENG-4861 (error payload improvements) + ENG-4862 (docs troubleshooting). Will keep this ticket open until we have (1) committed plan + (2) published docs link we can use in macros.
2026-02-25 (Mina Haddad): One nuance: fallback routing can change model family; structured output adherence differs by model. We should make sure docs mention pinning models + using stricter prompts for smaller models. Not suggesting that we blame the model; just set expectations and provide mitigations.
2026-02-28 (Owen Phillips): Proposed customer-facing interim guidance (until errors improve): recommend including an explicit example JSON in the prompt and instructing "do not quote numbers" / "output must exactly match schema"; also suggest testing in non-stream mode to capture full error response for now. Pending Eng confirmation if any near-term patch can add JSON path to the error message.
Unresolved. Tracking improvements via Linear ENG-4861 (add JSON path + expected/actual types + stable error code; ensure request_id propagation) and ENG-4862 (publish structured output troubleshooting docs and link from known-issues index + Support macros). Interim workaround sent to customer: add explicit example output; avoid streaming while debugging; capture request_id + schema for Support.

Issue summary: Since ~2026-03-14T02:20Z LexiAI has observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses from our hosted API. Errors surface mostly as 502/504 at the API gateway and increased SIGABRT/exit events on serving runtime workers downstream. Early telemetry shows long TLS handshake latencies on a subset of edge nodes which caused connection queueing and amplified retry storms against the runtime fleet.

Initial impact: Customer reported degraded request success rate for live inference routes and several dropped streaming sessions. Latency and failure spikes coincide with tenant traffic bursts during daily model prefetches.
- Customer-facing errors: 18% error rate at peak for LexiAI routes in us-east-1 (normal <0.5%).
- Observable symptoms: 502/504 at API gateway, increased runtime worker restarts, transient OOMs and connection reset logs.
- Business impact: Live features degraded for paying dedicated tenant; potential SLA breaches if not remediated.
1) Target LexiAI tenant routes in prod us-east-1 during scheduled prefetch window (observed at ~02:15-02:35Z).
2) Send concurrent inference traffic at historical high-concurrency profile (approx. 1200 rps sustained for 3 minutes).
3) Observe API gateway 502/504 rates and runtime worker restart counts in monitoring dashboards.
4) Capture tcpdump/tls handshake timing on affected edge node and inspect upstream connection resets from runtime proxies.
api-gateway: [2026-03-14T02:22:11Z] upstream_connection_error: TLS handshake timeout after 12.1s (edge-node-7b)
edge-proxy: [2026-03-14T02:23:03Z] conn_queue_exceeded: pending_conns=450, accept_rate=18/s
serving-runtime: [2026-03-14T02:23:18Z] runtime_manager: worker_pid=1248 exited SIGABRT (oom="false") - last_request_duration_ms=15423
serving-runtime: [2026-03-14T02:24:01Z] runtime_proxy: upstream_reset_by_peer during response write code=RST_STREAM
Telemetry: TLS handshake p95 on ~20% of edge nodes in us-east-1 rose from 40ms -> 5-12s starting 02:15Z; these nodes show increased system load and elevated open file handles.
Correlation: Spikes align with LexiAI prefetch job and tenant burst on dedicated capacity pool; dedicated pool autoscaler not scaling fast enough and queued connections accumulated at edge layer.
Hypothesis 1: Edge TLS handshake slowness (likely userland crypto or kernel throttling) caused accept backlog and proxy queueing, leading to API gateway timeouts and fanout retries to runtime causing resource pressure and runtime restarts.
Hypothesis 2: A small percentage of clients reusing incompatible TLS session parameters triggered expensive handshake paths on a subset of edge nodes (observed client hello metrics).
Quick checks done: validated node-level kernel dmesg (no obvious OOM), checked ip_vs conntrack counts, verified no recent deployment to edge fleet in the 24h window, compared metrics with other regions (not affected).
2026-03-14T03:05Z - Ethan Morales: Reached out to SREs to isolate edge-node cohort. Spun up new edge instances with connection reaper changes to test traffic routing.
2026-03-14T03:20Z - SRE on #support: Temporarily throttled LexiAI prefetch traffic at the API gateway per-tenant policy to reduce pressure. Notified customer via support channel.
2026-03-14T03:45Z - Customer (LexiAI): Confirmed immediate reduction in observed errors after throttling but reported longer end-to-end latency for some requests.
2026-03-14T04:10Z - Aisha Patel: Adding linked incident SUP-720304 for historical autoscaler-liveness context; opening runtime PR to guard against successive retries.
A subset of edge nodes experienced pathological TLS handshake latencies (5-12s) under burst load, causing connection queueing at the API gateway. The queueing amplified fanout to the serving runtime, overwhelming worker pools and triggering unstable behavior/resets. The underlying trigger appears to be expensive handshake paths combined with insufficient edge connection reaping and a lagging dedicated autoscaler for the tenant pool.
Mitigation performed: 1) Applied emergency per-tenant rate-limiter to LexiAI prefetch routes to cap concurrent prefetches. 2) Re-routed new traffic away from the affected edge cohort and performed rolling restart of 6 edge nodes in us-east-1 to clear handshake state. 3) Increased API gateway short-circuit timeout from 10s -> 6s for handshake phase to fail fast and prevent long queue retention. 4) Deployed temporary change to connection reaper aggressive mode on edge proxies.

Observed result: 5xx rates dropped from 18% -> 0.8% within 20 minutes and runtime restarts subsided. Customer notified of mitigations and workaround while permanent fix is delivered.
1) Engineering: Ship PR to add per-connection TLS handshake timeout and more aggressive session resumption checks on edge (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/2896).
2) Platform: Adjust dedicated autoscaler warmup thresholds for prefetch patterns (task assigned to infra squad).
3) SRE: Add synthetic TLS handshake healthchecks and an alert when p95 handshake > 500ms on >10% of edge nodes.
4) Product/CS: Coordinate with LexiAI to smooth prefetch schedule or provide a recommended concurrency cap for dedicated tenants during model warmups.
5) Runbook: Update confluence page with steps for per-tenant throttling and edge cohort isolation procedure.
Postmortem to include timeline of events, edge kernel/userland metrics around handshake, autoscaler timings, and a proposal for default keepalive and handshake timeouts. Recommend a test plan to reproduce handshake path costs with client hello variants.
payload.summary: Elevated 5xx rates traced to slow TLS handshakes on edge causing connection pile-up and upstream runtime resets for a dedicated tenant

Issue summary:
OptimaThera (private deployment) experienced a surge of 5xxs and missing transcript fragments between 2026-03-10 01:12 UTC and 2026-03-10 02:04 UTC. Root cause was a multipath fanout change that increased parallel RPCs to the message broker, producing an ack backlog (broker ack debt) which caused the streaming runtime to drop final transcript fragments under load and created a billing delta for retried requests. Impact: customers observed truncated responses and a spike in per-request token billing due to retries and duplicated delivery attempts.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: ~12% of streaming sessions for OptimaThera had missing final chunks (transcript truncation) during the window. Several downstream transcript consumers reported partial messages and duplicate delivery attempts.
- Billing exposure: there was an unplanned increase in billed token counts for OptimaThera due to client retries and server-side duplicate deliveries, estimated ~1.8x baseline token usage for affected sessions during the window.
- Operational: increased broker queue depth and sustained CPU pressure on serving-runtime instances in the private cluster.

Environment:
- Private deployment (OptimaThera-managed VPC) using private control plane, region: us-east-1, cluster: optima-prod-3.2
- Components: serving-runtime v2.18.3, router v1.9.0 (multipath fanout enabled), broker: redwood-eventbus v4.6.1, billing pipeline v1.2.0

Steps to reproduce (investigation procedure):
1) Simulate client fanout: send 50 concurrent streaming sessions with typical OptimaThera prompts and enabled multipath routing to three replicas.
2) Monitor broker ack rate and unacked messages (redwood-eventbus metrics).
3) Observe serving-runtime logs for "final_chunk_dropped" and stream finalization timeouts.
4) Verify billing pipeline duplicates by correlating request_id across ingested tokens.

Observed logs / snippets:
- serving-runtime: "WARN final_chunk_dropped request_id=opt-89ef ctx=stream-finalize reason=broker-ack-timeout"
- broker: "ERROR subscription:ack_debt=312 unacked_messages=1248 ack_latency_ms=1532"
- router: "INFO fanout:parallel=3 route=replica-set-7 latency_p95=420ms"
- billing: "WARN duplicate_token_stream request_id=opt-89ef duplicates=2"
2026-03-10 01:20 - Support (Aisha Carter): Initial customer report received via CS escalation channel. OptimaThera reported truncated transcripts for multiple streaming sessions. Asked customer to provide request_ids and timestamp window.
2026-03-10 01:27 - SRE (Diego Morales): Observed broker queue depth spike on optima-prod-3.2; ack latency > 1.5s. Confirming correlation with router fanout increase at 01:12 UTC. Tagging engineering.
2026-03-10 01:35 - Engineering (Hannah Kim): Hypothesis: enabling multipath fanout caused N times more inflight deliveries to broker, broker became the bottleneck and started delaying acks. Suggested immediate mitigation: reduce router fanout to 1 and apply broker backpressure throttling. Preparing emergency PR to router config and broker flow-control thresholds.
2026-03-10 01:42 - Support (Aisha Carter) -> Customer (OptimaThera SE contact, Dr. Marcus Lowe): Thank you for reporting. We believe this is an internal routing change that increased parallelism. We're applying a temporary mitigation and will follow up within 30 minutes with status and rollback details.
2026-03-10 01:50 - SRE (Diego Morales): Mitigation applied: router fanout set to 1 for OptimaThera tenant; broker flow-control re-enabled (windowing throttles). Broker ack latency dropping back toward baseline by 01:58 UTC.
2026-03-10 02:10 - Engineering (Hannah Kim): Deployed hotfix: router now respects tenant-specific max_parallel_fanout and brokers have adaptive ack pacing. Added logging for "ack_debt" threshold crossing. Monitoring for duplicate deliveries and billing deltas.
2026-03-10 10:15 - Customer (Dr. Marcus Lowe, OptimaThera): Confirmed transcripts look complete in the morning. Concerned about billing — noticed unexpected credits needed. Asked for detailed token/activity report for the incident window.
2026-03-11 09:03 - Support (Priya Shah): Shared preliminary token accounting report and offered a scheduled call to review credits and remediation steps. Customer requested an itemized list of duplicate deliveries and how they will be credited.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 11:05 - Support (Aisha Carter): Ticket moved to Resolved after credits applied and customer accepted post-incident report. Follow-up actions assigned to Eng and SRE teams are tracked in INT-4098.
Timeline and root cause summary:
- 01:11 UTC: automated rollout enabled router multipath fanout flag cluster-wide for a subset of tenants (canary->gradual).
- 01:12 UTC: OptimaThera private router picked up new config and began parallelizing deliveries to 3 replicas.
- 01:14 UTC: broker redwood-eventbus observed sharp increase in in-flight messages; ack latency rose >1s and unacked message counts climbed.
- 01:20 UTC: serving-runtime began logging final_chunk_dropped events when broker ack did not arrive before stream finalization window. These dropped final chunks caused apparent truncated transcripts.
- Contributing factors:
  * Broker ack debt: the broker lacked tenant-specific flow-control for aggressive multipath; a single tenant’s parallelism could saturate broker IO.
  * Stream finalization timeout: serving-runtime had a fixed short finalization timeout that did not account for transient broker ack latency.
  * Billing pipeline idempotency gap: billing ingestion relied on per-token events without robust de-duplication across rapid retries/duplicates; duplicates were billed before downstream dedupe job completed.

Metrics and dashboards referenced:
- Eventbus: redwood.eventbus.consumer.unacked_messages (spike to 1.2k)
- Router: redwood.router.fanout.parallel (changed 1 -> 3 at 01:12)
- Serving: redwood.serving.final_chunk_dropped.count (12% of active streams during window)
- Billing: billing.tokens.ingested_per_min (2x baseline during incident window)

Temporary mitigation implemented:
- Immediate rollback of multipath fanout for OptimaThera tenant (fanout=1).
- Re-enable broker tenant-level flow-control and reduce per-tenant concurrency.
- Increase serving-runtime finalization timeout by 800ms in the private cluster for affected tenants.

Longer-term remediation planned (tracked in INT-4098):
- Add tenant-scoped broker backpressure and circuit-breaker to prevent single-tenant saturation.
- Implement server-side stream finalization that tolerates broker ack latency via graceful fallback (emit finalization marker and queue late chunk replays).
- Improve billing pipeline dedup stage to perform stronger cross-batch de-duplication before token billing is finalized.
- Add canary gating to router multipath rollouts: require broker ack-rate baseline checks before increasing fanout per tenant.
Root cause: router multipath fanout caused an unexpected increase in parallel deliveries to the message broker (ack debt), which delayed broker acks and led serving-runtime to drop final stream chunks under its tight finalization timeout. Duplicate deliveries and client retries led to a billing delta.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: rolled back router fanout for OptimaThera, re-enabled tenant broker flow-control, increased finalization timeout. These steps restored normal ack latency and eliminated transcript truncation by 01:58 UTC.
- Billing: reconciled duplicate-token billing for the incident window (42,000 tokens) and applied a full token credit plus 10% goodwill credit on the affected invoice. Finance approval obtained and customer notified on 2026-03-12.
- Long-term: see INT-4098 for engineering work: tenant-scoped broker guards, improved billing de-duplication, and safer canary gating for multipath rollouts.

Customer outcome: OptimaThera confirmed transcripts are restored and accepted the credits and action plan. Customer rated the follow-up call as satisfactory and will accept closure pending completion of INT-4098 remediation items.

Post-incident things to track (owners):
- INT-4098 (Eng/SRE) - tenant broker guards and router gating - owner: Hannah Kim - target: 2026-04-05
- Billing de-dup (Billing) - owner: Evan Patel - target: 2026-03-29
- Customer follow-up review (Support) - owner: Aisha Carter - target: 2026-03-20

Applied immediately: revert router fanout to 1 for affected tenant; re-enable and lower broker per-tenant concurrency; temporarily increase serving-runtime finalization timeout for private tenants until code fix deployed.
Credits issued on 2026-03-12. Customer acceptance recorded 2026-03-13. Incident classified as Sev1 and post-incident actions tracked as INT-4098. No regulatory data exposure identified; only delivery and billing impact.
INT-4098: implement tenant-scoped broker circuit-breaker and safe fanout gating
Billing-2026Q1: add cross-batch token de-duplication and faster reconciliation jobs
Support-Action: schedule 1:1 technical remediation call with OptimaThera on 2026-03-20

Issue summary: After enabling the experimental control-plane 'mirroring' sync for NovaHealth's private VPC control plane (intended to mirror control-plane events to a standby region), they observed opaque 429 throttling on production API requests. Impact: Customer reports widespread 429s across mixed realtime/chat and bulk embedding routes for ~90 minutes during the sync window; user-facing latency and request failures for critical clinical ingestion pipelines. Environmental notes: Private deployment (self-hosted control plane) behind our private API gateway image; control-plane mirroring was enabled via flag: CP_MIRROR_SYNC=true. Mirroring streams pass through the customer's VPC peering path and an internal HAProxy layer that rewrites headers. Observed behavior: 5–15% of requests return 429 with no X-RateLimit-* headers visible to the customer; server-side rate-limiter logs show tokens being consumed twice for a subset of incoming requests when mirrored control-plane traffic is present. Expected behavior: Mirrored control-plane events should not cause duplicate accounting against tenant token buckets or per-route burst pools.

Temporary customer impact/workaround: Support recommended temporarily disabling CP_MIRROR_SYNC on the private control plane while SRE investigates. This restored normal traffic for the customer within 10 minutes.
1) On a private control plane deployment with CP_MIRROR_SYNC enabled, configure mirror target to a standby region.
2) Route production API traffic through customer's HAProxy layer configured to preserve X-Client-ID and X-Forwarded-For.
3) Trigger a small-scale model rollout to warm the standby region (causes short burst of control-plane events).
4) Observe 429s on mixed chat/embed routes and check server rate-limiter accounting.
03/11 03:00 - Initial triage: customer saw opaque 429s with no throttle headers; suspected token accounting mismatch.
03/11 03:20 - Correlated 429 spike with control-plane mirroring start; control-plane emitted duplicate route-update events for a 15s window.
03/11 03:40 - Captured VPC flow logs and ingress HAProxy logs: mirrored events were re-injected to API path with preserved X-Client-ID, resulting in duplicate token accounting by the token-bucket service.
03/11 04:10 - Reproduced locally in staging by enabling mirroring and a simple header-preserving proxy; confirmed token_delta recorded twice for the same request-id when mirror replay occurred within same refill epoch.
03/11 05:00 - Hypothesis: control-plane mirror replay + header-preserving proxy leads to identical client-id + request signature being accounted twice because the dedupe layer relies on origin-request-id which is not preserved across mirror flow.
2026-03-11T02:09:12Z | rate-limiter | tenant=novahealth | route=/v1/chat | token_delta=-2 | window=60s
2026-03-11T02:09:12Z | proxy    | src=10.21.5.3 dst=10.8.0.12 | headers=[X-Client-ID:abc123 , X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.45]
2026-03-11T02:09:12Z | control-plane-mirror | event=route-update | orig-request-id=req_9A3B | mirrored=true
2026-03-11 03:15 - NovaHealth (customer): 'We started seeing 429s exactly when we flipped mirroring on. No changes to our app. Requests just started failing.'
2026-03-11 03:50 - Support (Priya): 'We're investigating. Can you confirm if HAProxy rewrites any X-Request-ID or origin headers? Any preserved request-id would help us correlate.'
2026-03-11 04:05 - NovaHealth: 'HAProxy is set to preserve X-Client-ID and X-Request-ID for tracing. We can toggle preservation if needed.'
2026-03-11 04:45 - SRE (Marisol): 'We see double token deltas in the rate-limiter for requests that have mirrored control-plane events within the same epoch. We're testing a fix to dedupe mirrored accounting by checking mirror flag + origin timestamp.'
2026-03-12 09:00 - Support: 'Recommend disabling CP_MIRROR_SYNC temporarily while we push a mitigation to edge-proxy and token-bucket for dedupe. Customer confirmed disabling resolved issue.'
Slack thread: #support-private (link): https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C02SUPPORT/p1615567890123
Control-plane mirroring caused replayed control events to be re-injected to the API path with preserved client identifiers. The token-bucket accounting pipeline lacked adequate deduplication for mirrored events when origin request IDs were preserved, leading to double-counting against tenant and per-route burst pools.
Mitigation deployed: quick patch to token-bucket service to detect mirrored-control flag and ignore mirrored replay events for accounting when origin-request-id matches a recently recorded request (10s window). Deployed to staging on 2026-03-11 08:30 and to private deployments as a config patch 2026-03-12 07:15.
Customer action: Disabled CP_MIRROR_SYNC during investigation; re-enabled after patch verification and saw no recurrence during a 2-hour soak in canary region.
Follow-ups: (1) Update control-plane mirroring runbook to include guidance on not preserving origin request ids across mirror replay flows or tagging mirrored events with a unique mirror-origin header. (2) Add a token-bucket test case to simulate mirror replay and ensure dedupe holds across refill epochs. (3) Schedule postmortem with NovaHealth and internal ops team (confluence page link added).
1) Engineering to harden dedupe in token-bucket: extend detection window to 30s and add metrics for mirrored-accounting-suppressed.
2) Documentation: add paragraph to Private deployment checklist about header-preservation and mirror configs.
3) Customer follow-up: schedule a runbook review call with NovaHealth for 2026-03-16.
4) Create an automated integration test that simulates mirrored-control-plane playback and asserts no duplicate accounting.

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403/Integrity errors when the serving nodes fetch large model shard ranges via presigned range GETs through their corporate WAN optimizer / TCP offload appliance. Failures correlate with large-range requests (>8MB) and only happen from the customer's VPC endpoint to S3-like storage.

Impact:
- Model pulls fail intermittently during startup, causing node rollout delays and degraded capacity.
- Partial shard reads cause checksum/integrity verification failures, triggering retries and slower cold-start times.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC endpoint + on-prem WAN optimizer in path)
- Customer-managed egress appliance with TCP segmentation offload (TSO) and MSS clamping enabled
- Observed from serving nodes in us-east-1 retrieving model shards from artifact storage using presigned range URLs

Observed behaviour:
- S3 GETs with Range: bytes=... return 403 or incomplete content on validation, or the object is fetched but fails checksum validation on the serving node.
- When requests are retried from a different IP/path, they sometimes succeed.

Expected behaviour:
- Presigned range requests should be fetched intact; serving nodes should validate checksums and proceed to load model shard without content mismatch or 403s.
1) Deploy a private cluster connected via customer-managed egress appliance with TSO enabled.
2) Trigger a cold start that causes serving nodes to download a large shard (>8MB) via a presigned range GET through the customer's VPCE.
3) Observe the artifact download logs and checksum validation on the serving node.
4) Repeat with TSO and MSS clamping disabled on the appliance (if possible) for control test.
- Serving node logs: checksum mismatch for shard model-2026-03-09-8mb.part at byte range 0-8388607; computed sha256 != manifest.
- HTTP trace: 200 OK but Content-Length mismatch reported by the node, subsequent validation fails.
- Packet capture summary (customer-provided): TLS records split such that application-level range boundaries do not align with expected chunking; occasional retransmit and sequence reassembly differences.
- VPCE access logs: successful GETs with status 200, followed by application-level checksum failure on node side.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:05 - Customer (FinWave): We confirmed disabling the WAN optimizer TSO feature reduced failures in a short test window (not fully validated across fleet). Attached pcap and node logs.

Issue summary: BrightDocs reports that long-running SSE streams (chat completions) are consistently losing the final choice when the mobile client switches network (cell <-> wifi) and reconnects. The client reconnect flow uses the resume token and expects the final '\n' framed 'end' event.

Impact: Multiple customers using BrightDocs' mobile app see truncated final sentences or missing final choice metadata, leading to confusing user-facing outputs. Affects production traffic in us-east-1.

Environment: prod API endpoint behind ALB and Fastly CDN; streaming endpoint path /v1/streams, gzip allowed at CDN edge; clients are Android app versions 5.3.1 and 5.3.2.

Observed behavior: On network handover, client reconnects with previous resume token but server sends a chunk that appears to merge the terminal event into an earlier chunk boundary. Client receives duplicated partial tokens then an immediate EOF from the CDN edge; final choice is not reconstructed.

Expected behavior: Resume should re-send missing tokens and terminate with a clear 'end' event/EOF; no partial duplication or dropped terminal events.

Temporary workaround: BrightDocs disabled aggressive client retry and implemented a 500ms backoff before resume to reduce overlapping connections; also disabled CDN gzip for streaming paths as a stopgap.

1) Start a long streaming chat completion (>6s output) against /v1/streams using SSE from Android 5.3.1 on mobile network.
2) While stream is mid-output, toggle device from mobile data to wifi (or simulate poor network causing transient TCP close).
3) Client reconnects immediately with last resume token; observe SSE frames received at client and any duplicated partials or missing 'end' event.
4) Capture edge logs from Fastly and ALB, and a tcpdump of the server-facing connection for correlation.
[client] recv: data: {"delta":"...the final par"}

[client] recv: data: {"delta":"t of the sentence"}

[fastly] 2026-03-12T14:08:32Z edge-close chunked-bytes=140 gzipped=yes connection-id=ch_8a9
[alb] 2026-03-12T14:08:32Z idle-timeout; client-ip=22.54.11.7 keepalive=0
[server] resume validation: token=tok_ghjkl offset=10240 accepted=true session=brdoc-432
[server] stream_end emitted but last_event_boundary=offset(10176) < resume_offset(10240) => possible split

Additional notes:
Hypothesis: resume offset validation assumes raw chunk boundaries from origin; CDN/ALB rewrites (gzip compression and chunk aggregation) can move event boundaries so offset points inside a compressed block -> client receives truncated token set.
Evidence: Fastly edge logs show gzipped=yes and early edge-close immediately after last server chunk. tcpdump from origin shows server emitted correct 'end' event but ALB/Fastly coalesced it into prior packet; gzipping at edge changed byte offsets.
Repro: Reproduced locally by introducing gzip at reverse proxy and toggling connection; client resume-side code fails to find 'end' marker when resume_offset > actual boundary due to recompression, producing partial duplicate deltas.
Mitigation tested: disabling gzip at CDN for streaming paths yields correct resume behavior; adding conservative client-side backoff reduces overlap-caused races but doesn't fix boundary mismatch.
Root cause candidate: mismatch between origin's resume offset semantics and CDN/proxy transformations (gzip, chunk coalescing, keepalive close timing).
Mitigation applied: Disabled gzip at Fastly for /v1/streams in us-east-1 for BrightDocs; customer confirmed immediate improvement in sample tests.
Short-term action: Add resume-offset validation in API gateway (detect if requested offset falls inside a transformed chunk) and return 409 with suggestion to re-fetch from safe offset if mismatch detected.
Long-term action: Runtime/Serving team to implement chunk-normalization: ensure server emits canonical, gzip-safe chunk boundaries or include explicit resume markers separate from byte offsets. Also add integration test that runs through CDN gzip path.
Next steps: Create INT ticket for runtime work (INT-9012) and add e2e test in CI that simulates CDN gzip/ALB behavior. Notify platform/console teams to show resume-failure metrics in Redwood Console.
payload.summary: SSE stream truncated after mobile network switch; final tokens lost on reconnect

Issue summary:
Customer reports sudden increase in egress to ap-south-1 for a tenant pinned to eu-west-1 following routine GPU pool rebalancing. Behavior began intermittently on 2026-03-12 after an autoscaler rebalance window.

Impact:
- Observed 2x token cost bump for a subset (~12%) of requests over 24h for FableAI's dedicated pool.
- P95 latency increased from ~110ms to ~270ms on affected requests.
- No explicit configuration changes from customer side.

Environment:
- Customer: FableAI (dedicated capacity)
- Region: primary eu-west-1 serving; anomalous egress seen to ap-south-1
- Models: rw-inference-v1 for most traffic; llm-opt-13b for heavy queries

Steps to reproduce (customer observed):
1) Send steady traffic (~200 rps) pinned to tenant pool in eu-west-1.
2) During autoscaler scheduled rebalance window (03:00–04:00 UTC), intermittent requests route out-of-region.
3) Cost and latency for those requests spike.

Observed behavior:
- Affected requests show two-phase path: edge -> eu-west control plane -> ap-south serving node (multi-hop).
- Logs contain session-affinity refresh events immediately prior to hop.

Expected behavior:
- Sticky session affinity to tenant's eu-west pool should keep egress in-region unless a hard failover/fallback triggers.

Relevant logs/links:
- Customer-provided traces: https://s3.redwood.ai/fableai/traces/2026-03-12-eh2q.zip
- Kibana dashboard: https://kibana.redwood.ai/d/fableai/egress-hop-analysis
- Billing spike window: invoice line items 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-13

Notes: customer is concerned both about data residency (they must keep egress in EU) and the unexpected billing delta.
Control-plane correlates: during pool rebalances the scheduler moves fraction of GPU-allocated containers to new hosts; ephemeral token used by routing to refresh session-affinity may be issued on a control-plane instance in a different region causing path flip.
We observed affinity refresh requests hitting a metadata endpoint that resolved to a global control-plane VIP which returned a region-ambiguous stamp when the local scheduler was in state TRANSITION.
Heap of affected requests share same short-lived client hint header (X-Req-Sticky=short). Hypothesis: short TTL + scheduler movement => affinity refresh races with host eviction and control-plane instance selection, producing stale residency stamp.
Billing analysis: average egress cost per affected request increased by 0.004 USD; multiplied by traffic proportion explains reported invoice delta.
Related internal ticket INT-1402 tracks a recent scheduler change to host drain semantics during rebalance (PR #2184 referenced).

Additional notes:
Customer uploaded traces and a billing snapshot.
2026-03-13 14:22 - FableAI (Customer): Confirmed they saw the same time windows. Asked whether strict region pinning can be enforced immediately for legal compliance.
Mitigation applied: increased session-affinity TTL for tenant 'fableai-tenant-42' from 30s to 5m to reduce race window during rebalances. Customer notified. Next steps: engineering to land a control-plane fix to ensure affinity refreshes inherit explicit region stamp (work tracked in INT-1402 / PR #2184). Post-mortem and a billing credit proposal pending after verification.
payload.summary: Session-affinity refresh vs GPU-pool rebalance causing intermittent region egress and cost bump

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer's Private deployment intermittently fails tenant resolution during SSO flows. We see the IdP metadata XML being fetched by the identity-proxy but the entityID element is truncated. The proxy then fails to match the IdP entity to the configured tenant, resulting in immediate 401/403 responses for new SAML logins.

Impact:
- FinBank Analytics (private) unable to create new SSO sessions for some users; existing sessions remain valid.
- Affects onboarding and new user logins only; no data plane inference impact.
- Around 30% of IdP metadata fetches in the last 24h contained truncated payloads.

Environment:
- Private VPC deployment (FinBank Analytics) in us-west-2
- Identity-proxy v1.12.0 behind customer-managed ingress (NGINX)
- IdP endpoint: https://idp.finbank.example.com/metadata (IdP managed by customer)

Observed behavior:
- identity-proxy logs show SAML metadata parse errors and missing entityID.
- Error pattern correlates with upstream responses that include Transfer-Encoding: chunked.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run a curl -v against the customer's metadata endpoint via the same path the proxy uses (through the ingress).
2) Intermittently the response headers contain 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' and the body is cut off mid-entityID.
3) Trigger SAML login flow; identity-proxy logs: 'metadata parse error: unexpected EOF while reading entityID' and the request returns 403 with tenant resolution failure in the response body.

Logs / excerpts:
- identity-proxy: "WARN metadata: parse failed: unexpected EOF at byte 312"
- ingress (NGINX): "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream"
- curl capture: Response headers: Transfer-Encoding: chunked; Body length reported by client does not match parsed XML length.

Temporary workaround:
- Customer routing change: configure their IdP to serve metadata via Content-Length header (static file) or disable chunked responses on the IdP side. This reduces failures immediately.

Notes:
- This only appears in the private deployment where customer ingress terminates TLS and proxies to their IdP; hosted customers have not reported this.

1) curl -v --location 'https://idp.finbank.example.com/metadata' via customer ingress path
2) Repeat until Transfer-Encoding: chunked appears in response headers
3) Attempt SAML login through the identity-proxy; observe 403 and metadata parse error in proxy logs
identity-proxy WARN: metadata parse failed: unexpected EOF at byte 312; NGINX: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header; curl: <truncated XML showing incomplete <EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.finbank.example.com/sso/"...>
Initial hypothesis: chunked transfer-encoding combined with ingress upstream behavior is causing partial reads by the identity-proxy HTTP client. Reproduced locally by instrumenting a mock IdP that returns chunked responses with occasional premature connection close.

Findings so far:
- identity-proxy HTTP client (Go net/http) was using default Read behavior; when upstream closes connection mid-stream the body reader returns EOF and the XML remains incomplete.
- Customer's ingress (NGINX) intermittently emits 'upstream prematurely closed connection' when backend IdP rotates worker processes during metadata generation.
- Linked to SUP-61502 (idp metadata fetch timeouts) as both involve metadata fetch instability, but root cause differs (timeouts vs chunked truncation).

Short-term mitigation applied:
- Instructed customer to set 'proxy_buffering off' and enable 'proxy_http_version 1.1' with 'proxy_set_header Connection ""' to avoid NGINX closing upstream prematurely. Customer applied change and saw immediate drop in truncation events.

Longer-term fix options:
- Harden identity-proxy metadata fetcher to retry and reassemble chunked responses, validating XML completeness before parsing. (PR created: related_github_prs).
- Add post-fetch validation and automated re-fetch on parse failure with exponential backoff.

Workaround: customer modified ingress settings to reduce upstream connection closes; this reduced errors. Engineering drafted a patch to identity-proxy to validate and retry on incomplete chunked responses (PR #482). Target: rollout patch to private branch and offer customer a hotfix deployment. Final verification pending after canary in customer's staging cluster.
payload.summary: IdP metadata served with chunked transfer-encoding leads to truncated entityID and tenant resolution failures in private VPC

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During scheduled retention compaction on March 12 we observed an event-join failure surface in the Console that breaks trace-to-dashboard linking for a subset of streaming and ad-hoc queries. The compaction job appears to rewrite event join keys for high-cardinality session events which causes the Console's join layer to miss trace anchors when building links to trace spans.

Impact:
- Customers (enterprise tier) reported missing 'View trace' links from dashboard panels and query results for queries executed within a ~3 hour window (approx 02:15-05:25 UTC).
- Estimated affected query rows: ~37k distinct query rows across 4 orgs; 2 orgs reported active customer-facing alerts firing without trace anchors.
- No generation/serving API customer requests were impacted; this is isolated to Console DB join index used for trace linking.

Environment:
- prod/us-east-1 Console and ingest clusters
- Retention compaction job v2.7.3 (nightly rolling compaction)
- Consoles affected: web-console-v3, trace-indexer-v1

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Query a dashboard time range that includes 2026-03-12 02:30 UTC.
2. Click on the trace anchor column or 'View trace' link on affected rows.
3. Console returns an empty trace link (no trace id) or a 404 when resolving the anchor.

Logs / Observations:
- trace-indexer logs (03-12T03:02:14Z): "WARN joiner: missing_key_after_compaction shard=17 key=org-8032-session-0x7f2a tombstone=true"
- ingest-worker (03-12T03:02:15Z): "INFO compaction: rewrite_summary keys_rewritten=2745 duration_ms=1203"
- console-api (03-12T03:04:08Z): "ERROR trace-linker: anchor_resolution_failed query_id=Q-89f1 org=8032 err=KeyLookupNotFound"
- Metrics: spike in joiner_miss_rate from 0.2% -> 6.9% between 02:10-05:30 UTC on 2026-03-12.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: retention compaction produced tombstones or changed canonical join keys that the Console join layer didn't account for during index reconciliation.
- Reproduced by re-running compaction on a staging shard and validating that rewritten keys no longer matched active trace anchor references.
- Related to a recent change in compaction key canonicalization (ingest PR linked) that normalized event session IDs by trimming leading zeros. That normalization is incompatible with older trace anchors that keep the original session id format.
- Supports cross-reference: SUP-412589 (route token attribution missing-prefix cache) appears to have overlapping code paths for join key normalization.

Workaround / Mitigation applied:
- Immediately disabled the nightly v2.7.3 compaction on affected shards at 2026-03-12T06:40 UTC to prevent further rewrites.
- Ran a reconciler job (console-reconciler v0.9) to rehydrate missing join keys from write-ahead logs for highest-priority orgs (Nimbus Health and two others). Rehydration restored trace links for ~60% of affected rows for those orgs.

Next steps / Proposed fix:
- Engineering (ingest + console) to coordinate a two-part fix: (1) revert canonicalization change in compaction or add backwards-compatible mapping layer, (2) add a reconciliation run to restore trace anchor keys for all affected shards.
- Add alerting on joiner_miss_rate > 1% to catch regressions earlier.
- Postmortem to be drafted after full reconciliation.

Desired customer communication:
- Notify Nimbus Health that we have a temporary mitigation in place and that partial restoration has completed; full restoration ETA pending reconciliation run (target: 2026-03-16).

Status:
- In Progress: engineering rollback + reconciliation is scheduled; SRE monitoring added to track rehydration progress.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:05 - SRE on-call (Linh Tran): Disabled compaction job for affected shard groups and started reconciliation for top orgs. Partial restoration reported.
Investigating; temporary mitigation applied: nightly compaction disabled and partial rehydration completed for high-priority orgs. Engineering patch and full reconciliation scheduled.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several customers on dedicated accounts (first reported by Arcadia HealthTech) are observing intermittent loss of pinned-model affinity during weighted canary rollouts. When affinity drops the request is routed to a fallback variant which increases error rate and token cost for affected tenants. Impact: customer-facing sessions see mixed-model outputs and increased latency/cost. Customer reports impact on live inference for scheduled traffic windows. Environment: prod, us-west-2, dedicated GPU cluster. Observed behavior vs expected: observed affinity drops when tenant session cookie is present but path attribute differs between initial request and edge rehydration. Expected: session/tenant cookie should be preserved across edge and sidecar hop and not cause unpin. This appears correlated to a client-side SDK that writes a tenant cookie with a root path and the edge-side sidecar rewriting cookies without preserving the original path attribute, causing downstream host/path mismatches and the routing mesh to treat the session as new (losing model pin).
1) Configure a tenant on dedicated capacity and pin to rw-7b-instruct-v2 via route configuration.
2) Use a client that sets a tenant cookie at path '/' while initial edge handshake uses '/api/v1' path on the gateway (Arcadia SDK behavior).
3) Send a steady stream of chat/infer requests while a weighted canary is active for the pin's route (10% weight).
4) Observe that after a subset of requests the session affinity token changes and requests are routed to fallback variant; the model pin is effectively lost for that session.
5) Reproduce by toggling the client cookie Path attribute or by introducing a path-normalizing header rewrite at the sidecar to simulate the condition.
[2026-03-10T14:22:03Z] edge-proxy.INFO tenant=arcadia uid=abc123 cookie=(tenant=arcadia; Path=/) routed=pin(rw-7b-instruct-v2)
[2026-03-10T14:22:07Z] sidecar.DEBUG session=abc123 set-cookie=(tenant=arcadia; Path=/api/v1) header-sanitizer=applied
[2026-03-10T14:22:08Z] router.WARN session=abc123 affinity-mismatch detected: cookie-path-mismatch -> fallback-route selected=rw-legacy-6b
Initial triage by support: verified customer traffic and captured request/response headers; confirmed cookie Path attribute differs between client and sidecar-set cookie.
Hypothesis A: sidecar cookie rewrite (pre-commit sanitizer) removes or normalizes Path to the upstream route, causing the edge lookup to miss the tenant cookie on subsequent incoming requests routed by path.
Hypothesis B: client SDK sets cookie with domain/path that is incompatible with edge host rewrite during canary mirror, resulting in two different cookie values and session split.
Correlated with recent sidecar release (sidecar v1.9.2) which added stricter cookie Path normalization: see PR github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar/pull/1198.
Reproduced internally by replaying capture with synthetic client that flips Path between '/' and '/api/v1' and saw router selecting fallback when header mismatch occurs.
Edge-proxy metrics show spike in routing decisions to fallback variant exactly when cookies differ; no GPU OOMs or autoscaler events observed during window.
Support (Aisha): Thanks Arcadia for logs and HAR. We've isolated cookie path mismatch as likely cause. We've escalated to sidecar and routing owners. (2026-03-10)
SRE (Miguel): Assigned and reproducing locally. Creating a test harness to simulate path rewrite and cookie behavior. Will instrument router to emit full-cookie-match diagnostics. (2026-03-11)
Customer (Arcadia): We rolled back sidecar agent on our hosts to prior version; issue frequency reduced but not eliminated — still seeing occasional affinity drops. (2026-03-11)

Additional notes:
Support (Aisha): Temporary mitigation suggested: configure client SDK to set cookie Path explicitly to match gateway mount (/api/v1) or enable 'preserve_cookie_path' in route config for affected tenant. Asked for confirmation from engineering if 'preserve_cookie_path' is safe at scale. (2026-03-12)
In progress. Short-term mitigation recommended (customer-side change to cookie Path or route config 'preserve_cookie_path') reduced incidents for Arcadia. Engineering to deliver a sidecar patch that will preserve original cookie Path or standardize pin lookup to be path-agnostic. PR planned to update router pinning lookup logic and sidecar sanitizer to include original Path in a dedicated header for robust matching. Follow-up steps: (1) sidecar fix (target hotfix v1.9.3), (2) router change to perform path-agnostic cookie match, (3) rollout canary for patch to 5% then 25% then 100% with monitoring. Expected next update 2026-03-15.
payload.summary: Tenant cookie path collision from client-side override causes pinned-model affinity to drop and fallback routing

Issue summary: Over the last 6 hours BrightFields observed repeated mixed-model responses for the same tenant/session during our staged canary promote. Impact: Customer request traffic intermittently routed to baseline model (redwood-3b-v1) instead of pinned canary variant, impacting output consistency and evaluation metrics. Environment: Dedicated pool for BrightFields in us-west (prod).
1) Use BrightFields tenant api key against production endpoint for route /v1/complete with canonical multi-turn payload
2) Send 30 requests rapidly from the same client behind the customer's load balancer using varying outbound source IPs (simulate NAT/egress churn)
3) Observe model selection in response metadata: some requests go to canary variant (redwood-3b-quant), others go to baseline (redwood-3b-v1) despite tenant pin expected to hold
4) Reproduce more consistently by toggling X-Forwarded-For header between original IP and a proxied IP; model selection changes correlate with header surface change
2026-03-13T08:12:04Z edge-proxy[proxy-3b]: request id=6a1b ... tenant=brightfields route=nlp/complete xff='203.0.113.42' chosen_variant=redwood-3b-quant pin_hash=0x7f4a ttl_ms=43200
2026-03-13T08:12:05Z edge-proxy[proxy-3b]: request id=6a1c ... tenant=brightfields route=nlp/complete xff='34.201.55.10' chosen_variant=redwood-3b-v1 pin_hash=0x2c11 ttl_ms=43190
2026-03-13T08:12:05Z orchestrator[leader]: pin-lookup tenant=brightfields key=route:nlp/complete client_shard=0x2c11 cache_hit=false
2026-03-13T08:13:22Z serving-runtime[gpu-12]: fallback-route invoked tenant=brightfields reason='pin-mismatch' target=redwood-3b-v1
Initial triage: customer reports mixed outputs; metrics show session-level variance in model selection correlated with changes to client IP observed at the edge.
Hypothesis A: Pin key derivation includes client_ip shard (by legacy design) and BrightFields' egress NAT churn changed client_ip surface, causing different pin hashes and split routing.
Hypothesis B: Edge proxy normalizes X-Forwarded-For / Forwarded header and sometimes rewrites to internal egress IP under high concurrency; this rewriting is intermittent and not reflected in pin cache TTL logic, producing brief split-pinning windows.
Checked orchestrator snapshot: canary slices configured to use 'cohort_key=client_ip_hash' for staged promote (confirmed), which increases sensitivity to XFF changes.
Confirmed TTLs: pin TTL set at 12 hours for dedicated tenants; however pin assignment depends on hash computed at request time, so different client_ip values produce distinct pin entries instead of reusing the canonical tenant pin.
Edge logs show two different client_shard values for consecutive requests from same session where only XFF changed — supports Hypothesis A+B.
No evidence of control-plane rollback or orchestrator epoch bump during the window; no autoscaler events correlated.
Customer provided sample pcap showing NAT churn frequency ~3s between connections during their internal deploy; this is higher than typical and explains high rate of pin splitting for their traffic pattern.

Issue summary:
Nimbus Health reports intermittent 429 responses (~0.8-1.2% of requests) for a single enterprise tenant during morning traffic warmups. Throttles present only during short, high-concurrency bursts immediately after their scheduled autoscaler cold-start window (07:45-08:05 PST).

Impact:
- Customer reports degraded UX for real-time patient triage flows (high priority SLA).
- Errors are transient but correlate with scheduled warmup/autoscaler events and a heavy mix of low-latency chat calls + background batch embed requests.

Environment:
- Tenant: Nimbus Health (enterprise account)
- Deployment: Dedicated pool pinned to us-west-2, priority-weighted routing enabled (weights: real-time=0.7, batch=0.3)
- Models: redwood-llama-70b-v1 (primary), rw-open-pt-20b-q4 (fallback)

Observed behavior:
- 429s appear only during the first 2-3 minutes after cold-start cycles and again during small autoscaler scale-ups.
- 429s carry throttle headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: ~22s, but token accounting dashboard shows tenant token balance not fully depleted.
- Console traces show surge of queued requests at the gateway and a short-lived spike of 5xx->429 conversions in the rate-limiter.

Expected behavior:
- Priority-weighted routing should preserve a reserve for low-latency routes during warmup and surface informative retry headers to the client.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Schedule load: 150 concurrent short chat sessions + 40 parallel batch embedding jobs that start within the same 60s window.
2) Ensure Dedicated pool has a cold-start (scale from 0 GPUs) at the start of the window.
3) Observe errors in the first 180s.

Logs/metrics attached below and in linked dashboard references.

Create a dedicated pool with autoscaler min=0 and scheduled warmup at 07:45 PST
Configure tenant to send 150 concurrent chat requests and kick off 40 parallel embedding uploads within 60s
Enable priority-weighted routing with real-time weight 0.7 and batch weight 0.3
Start traffic and observe rate-limit headers and console traces for 3 minutes
Gateway request logs: spike at 07:45:12 -> 07:46:00 with 80% of connections initiated by single IP range (customer orchestrator)
Rate-limiter metrics: instantaneous token-drain metric shows 90% consumption in 15s but refill reports delayed by ~12s relative to global refill tick
Serving runtime logs: first GPU warmup reported kernel load/start at 07:45:28, KV-cache priming at 07:45:40
Console traces: several requests converted 503->429 in rate-limiter fallback path between 07:45:35-07:45:58
03/10 10:15 (Lena): Reproduced in staging by simulating customer traffic pattern; saw 429s within first 90s of cold start when mixer prioritized batch workers concurrently.
03/10 15:43 (Samir Kapoor): Hypothesis A - refill tick misalignment between api-gateway token accounting and rate-limiter leads to short-lived negative token state reported to gateway; investigating clock/tick drift impact.
03/10 17:02 (Diego Morales): Hypothesis B - priority-weighted routing reserve calculation uses steady-state capacity estimates and does not account for initial GPU warmup delays, so reserved capacity not effectively protected during cold start.
03/10 19:30 (Lena): Added an experiment: introduce a small fixed reserve (5% tokens) for real-time route during cold-start window in staging; observed 429s drop to <0.1% in initial tests.
03/11 08:22 (SRE): Gathered relevant traces and CPU/GPU warmup timelines; linked PR that adjusted refill alignment in rate-limiter (github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4321) as potential fix.

03/10 11:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Logged initial ticket with customer, confirmed examples and provided requested request-ids.

Stagger batch embedding job starts to avoid co-located burst with chat starts (>=90s separation)
Apply client-side exponential backoff with jitter for immediate retries during warmup windows
Set pool autoscaler min=1 during high-schedule periods to avoid cold-start entirely
Engineering to validate PR#4321 refill alignment change in canary and measure token drift under mixed-priority bursts
Add a short-term server-side reserve policy for real-time routes during detected cold-starts (feature flag rollout for affected tenants)
Update runbook and our priority-weighting docs in Confluence with guidance for scheduled warmups and tenant configuration
Coordinate a follow-up with Nimbus Health to test canary and schedule a low-risk maintenance window if needed

03/10 16:00 - Samir Kapoor (Applied ML): Observed that model load and kv-cache priming lags the GPU kernel availability by ~10-15s; this likely widens the effective cold period.
