Issue summary: Several customers using sparse embedding payloads report intermittent empty candidate sets and large p95 rerank latencies after switching to client-side gzip compression. Impact: production traffic to the rerank endpoint returns empty candidate arrays for ~0.3% of requests and p95 token latency increases from ~120ms to ~1.3s during these windows. Environment: Dedicated cluster for Lexicon Labs (prod-us-east). This started after the customer's SDK rolled out gzip-by-default for embedding uploads two days ago. Observed with both open-embed-v1 and open-embed-sparse-v1.

Observed behavior: When client sends sparse CSR-like binary frames compressed with Content-Encoding: gzip over HTTP/2 multiplexed connections, the gateway's chunking layer miscalculates frame boundaries for small trailing chunks. The downstream ingest worker interprets a truncated sparse index block as zero-length or wrong-dimension vector, leading to either: (a) candidate suppression (empty result) or (b) a fallback path that converts to dense with zero-padding which causes ANN index fallback and queueing, increasing p95.

Expected behavior: Gateway should correctly decompress and reassemble gzip-compressed frames over HTTP/2 and hand a full, validated embedding payload to the ingest worker. Serving should reject invalid-length embeddings with a 4xx and clear error message rather than silently dropping candidates or falling back to expensive CPU paths.
1) Use the Lexicon SDK with sparse-embed flag enabled and gzip compression on.
2) Send a batch of mixed-size embedding uploads over HTTP/2 to the embedding endpoint with Content-Encoding: gzip and Accept-Encoding headers.
3) Immediately issue a rerank request referencing the new embeddings.
4) Repeat at 200 QPS for 5 minutes to reproduce tail behavior.
5) Observe 503s or empty candidate arrays in ~0.2-0.5% of requests and p95 spikes in serving-runtime.

Deterministic repro in staging: enabled SDK gzip + sparse flag against staging-gateway with http2 multiplexing reproduces sample within 1000 requests. Logs attached below include truncated frame offsets and decoder exceptions.
[2026-03-10T13:04:12Z] gateway-01 ERROR chunk_reassembly: expected 8192 bytes, got 6104, stream_id=0x7f2a
[2026-03-10T13:04:12Z] ingest-worker WARN sparse-decoder: index-block-truncated, fallback_to_dense=true, embed_id=lex-usr-3482
[2026-03-10T13:04:12Z] serving-runtime ERROR ann-fallback-queueing: worker-saturation, request=rerank/lex-usr-3482, p95=1270ms
[2026-03-10T13:04:13Z] api-gateway INFO request: client-ip=35.200.122.8, method=POST, path=/v1/embeddings, content-encoding=gzip, content-length=0

Note: logs show a content-length mismatch at the gateway (0 after decompress attempt) which correlates to how the HTTP/2 chunking layer interacts with our gzip streaming decoder for small final chunks.
Aisha Kapoor (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer reported sudden regressions after SDK change. Provided initial logs and sample request. Requested immediate triage.
Luis Morales (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging by toggling SDK gzip. Observed truncated index-blocks at gateway; suspect interaction between http2 chunk framing and our in-house gzip streaming wrapper. Kicked to serving-runtime and gateway owners.
Priya Nair (Serving Eng) - 2026-03-11: Found decoder state machine bug when final gzip block size < 1024 bytes under HTTP/2 multiplex path. Created local repro and unit test. Preparing patch to fully buffer final block before handing to sparse decoder.
Aisha Kapoor (Support) - 2026-03-11: Shared workaround to Lexicon Labs: disable SDK gzip or set X-Embed-Format: dense-fp32. Customer applied workaround and saw immediate reduction in empty candidates. Confirmed temporary mitigation acceptable while we push patch.
Luis Morales (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Hotfix PR opened and tested against staging with canary. No regression on dense endpoints. Planning production canary tomorrow (2026-03-13) during low traffic window.
Root cause: gzip streaming wrapper in gateway attempted to stream-decompress and incrementally hand bytes to chunk-reassembler for HTTP/2 streams. For sparse payloads (small index blocks appended at the end) the streaming decompressor reports available bytes but final flush sequence was invoked on a later HTTP/2 frame; our chunker considered the frame boundary complete and forwarded a partial payload to the sparse decoder. Sparse decoder treats truncated index blocks as either invalid (silently drop candidate) or attempts CPU fallback by padding to expected length.

Why it's customer-visible: Lexicon uses sparse embedding format that places small index metadata at the tail of the compressed stream; when tail fragments arrive in very small final frames the bug is triggered. Dense embeddings amortize the issue because final blocks are larger. The HTTP/1 path isn't affected; this is limited to HTTP/2+gzip+small-final-frame sequence.

Repro note: Adding an explicit flush in client (larger buffer) or disabling gzip prevents the race. Unit tests added to capture the <1024 byte final-block case for HTTP/2 streams.
Short-term mitigation: advised customer to disable client gzip and provided SDK flag to force dense format (X-Embed-Format: dense-fp32). Long-term fix: gateway patch to buffer final decompressed block until Content-Encoding flush confirmed and to validate embedding lengths before forwarding to ingest-worker. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3821 created by Priya Nair. Staging canary passed (2026-03-12). Production canary scheduled for 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC; rollback strategy documented in the linked Confluence runbook. Post-deploy actions: add monitoring alert for chunk_reassembly errors and a synthetic test that sends small-trailing-frame gzip-sparse payloads to staging/production canaries.
payload.summary: Sparse-embedding + gzip chunking causes truncated frames, dropped candidates, and elevated rerank p95

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent p95 latency spikes and region egress flips after our pin healthcheck runs. Impact: Notifyly experiences periodic p95 increases from ~120ms to ~450ms for requests that have a region pin to eu-west; spikes correlate with a router healthcheck window. Environment: Dedicated account on prod us-east control plane with residency pin set to eu-west for workspace 'notifyly-prod'. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady traffic pinned to eu-west from app clients in us-east. 2) Observe stable p95 ~120ms for 20-30 minutes. 3) Wait for the scheduled pin-healthcheck (runs every 30m). 4) Immediately after healthcheck completes, a subset (~7-12%) of requests switch egress via us-east edge then back within 20-90s. 5) During the flip p95 jumps to ~400-500ms for affected requests. Observed behavior: healthcheck completion appears to trigger routing path recompute that allows non-resident egress for pinned routes briefly. Expected behavior: pinned traffic should remain egressed from the pinned region unless a sustained failure is detected and routed by explicit fallback policy. Logs / traces: - Router trace sample (trace id: t-20260310-0a9c): shows route decision change at 2026-03-10T14:30:12Z. - Router debug: "pin_healthcheck: window=30s, result=OK, recompute_routes=true" - Edge connection logs show transient TLS renegotiation and elevated SYN/ACK RTTs to eu-west gateway during flip. Customer impact notes: affects production latencies for key API endpoints (inference and embeddings). Customer has asked for immediate mitigation and explanation.
2026-03-10 15:02 - Support (Aisha Patel): Opened ticket after receiving Notifyly report. Collected traces and asked for recent request IDs and sample timestamps. Escalated to SRE router team.
2026-03-10 16:10 - SRE (Marco Reyes): Reproduced with internal load test using dedicated workspace. Observed identical short egress flips immediately after pin healthcheck completes. Captured router decision logs. Hypothesis: healthcheck triggers a full route table recompute which temporarily relaxes residency constraints for pinned groups.
2026-03-11 09:23 - Networking (Evelyn Cho): Found increased TCP retransmits on eu-west gateway at the same time window. Possibly contributing to router treating eu-west as degraded and allowing fallback. No full outage observed on gateway.
2026-03-11 13:45 - Support (Aisha Patel): Shared findings with Notifyly and requested permission to apply a temporary workaround: suppress recompute-triggered fallback for their workspace for next 24h. Customer approved.
2026-03-11 14:05 - SRE (Marco Reyes): Applied temporary config to disable healthcheck-induced fallback for workspace notifyly-prod. Monitoring shows p95 stabilized back to baseline during the next healthcheck window.
2026-03-12 10:12 - Engineering (Rosa Martinez): Proposed permanent fix in router logic: require consecutive failed healthchecks (configurable N) and add a short backoff before allowing cross-region fallback for pinned routes. Draft PR created: redwood/router#4123.
2026-03-12 16:40 - Support (Aisha Patel): Notified customer of temporary mitigation and next steps. Customer requested an audit log entry showing the config change; provided the audit link.
2026-03-12 17:05 - Product (Omar Li): Requested additional metrics on pin-stability and egress-flip counts to be added to Console; added follow-up task to roadmap.

Initial hypothesis: healthcheck completion triggers route recompute which evaluates fallback rules and may allow non-resident egress briefly. Evidence: correlated timestamps between healthcheck job and router decision changes; increased TCP retransmits to eu-west at the same time. Reproduction: internal load test with pinned workspace reproduced flip within healthcheck window. Root cause candidate: recompute logic does not enforce pin-strong preference during transient gateway degradation; a single OK/ degraded signal from healthcheck is treated as sufficient to allow fallback. Additional signal sources (edge TCP metrics) influenced decision path. Impact scope: appears limited to dedicated workspaces with pin and healthcheck enabled; not widespread across hosted customers. Temporary mitigation successful: disabled recompute-triggered fallback per workspace. Longer-term: require N consecutive failed/healthy checks and add a cooldown before allowing cross-region fallback for pinned routes. Added metric: 'egress_flip_count' with tags workspace and region.
Workaround applied: configured notifyly-prod to ignore healthcheck-triggered fallback for next 72 hours; this stabilized p95. Engineering fix planned: patch router to require 3 consecutive healthcheck results and a 60s cooldown before allowing fallback for pinned routes. PR redwood/router#4123 created; queued for canary deploy in US staging on 2026-03-15 and full rollout week of 2026-03-22. Post-deployment actions: - Add Console alert for 'egress_flip_count' > 5/min per workspace. - Update regional egress runbook to include steps for pin-healthcheck anomalies. - Notify affected customers and provide audit of temporary config changes. Linked follow-ups: infra/egress-gw#198 to review gateway retransmit behavior. Ticket will be updated when PR is merged and deployed.

Customer reports sudden increase in reranking tail latency (P95) and intermittent partial/empty candidate lists from the /v1/rerank endpoint. Issue began after a quiet client-side rollout of batch prefetching in the customer's SDK. Top-level symptom: rerank requests return 200 but with fewer than expected candidates or truncated lists; end-to-end P95 jumps from ~120ms to 750-1200ms for affected calls.
Impacts subset of QleverSearch's production queries using Dedicated capacity in us-east-1. Customers report search relevance degradation when top-k results are missing. Estimated 18% of their rerank traffic is affected; revenue-affecting for search product. No token billing discrepancies observed.
1) Customer uses SDK version 2.14.0 with client-side embedding prefetch enabled (prefetch=true).
2) Simulate high QPS (~400 req/s) with mixed-length queries and 4 concurrent worker threads per client instance.
3) Observe /v1/rerank responses: intermittent candidate counts < requested top_k and tail latency spikes to 750-1200ms.
4) Disable prefetch on client or reduce client worker threads to 1 and re-run - issue frequency drops significantly.
[2026-03-11T14:22:03Z] proxy: upstream request /v1/embeddings id=7b2c... routed to embed-replica-3
[2026-03-11T14:22:03Z] embed-replica-3: prefetch-worker-1 blocked on I/O for 450ms (epoll wait)
[2026-03-11T14:22:03Z] rerank-pool: worker-11 queue length 24, wait-time 520ms, returned candidates 3/10
[2026-03-11T14:22:03Z] scheduler: cpu-steal increased on node gke-rw-us-east-12, throttling cpus for pod serving-runtime-7
[2026-03-11T14:22:04Z] customer-sdk: sending batch prefetch=on count=16

Initial triage: symptoms correlate with client's rollout of prefetch behavior (customer provided canary config).
Heap and thread profiles on affected replicas show an increased number of prefetch threads entering blocking syscall in close proximity to batch ingestion spikes.
Observed CPU steal and cgroup throttling on nodes hosting serving runtime + embed processes during high prefetch bursts; kernel reports high iowait to local block device used by ephemeral index cache.
Hypothesis A: aggressive prefetch threads performing synchronous disk reads for embedding warmup cause worker starvation in the rerank pool, increasing queue waits and sometimes timing out partial merging of ANN candidates.
Hypothesis B: interaction between prefetch-induced I/O and kube node autoscaling leads to transient packet loss between embed and rerank replicas causing partial candidate lists to be returned while the system falls back to best-effort merging.
Reproduction in staging with local index mirrored: enabling prefetch with 12 concurrent workers reproduces p95 spike; disabling prefetch returns baseline latency.

Additional notes:

Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler fallback to hosted for ~12 minutes should have generated a single hosted-fallback prorate that gets normalized against reserved-hours; an edge-case rounding path emitted both a fallback prorate and a smoothing-adjustment prorate because of timestamp normalization at 00:00 UTC boundary.
Query run: billing.postback_rows where invoice_id = 'invoice_2026_03' and tenant = 'aurelia-health' returned two contiguous proration rows with identical usage_hash but different reason_codes (reserved_prorate, smoothing_timezone).

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightHealth AI reports a spike in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions with occasional streaming disconnects after a scheduler parameter tuning that rolled out on 2026-03-09. Impact: Affected customer (dedicated) is experiencing degraded UX for interactive chat flows: median TTFB increased from ~120ms to ~900ms for short prompts, and ~10% of streaming sessions hit client-observed timeouts (30s) before first token. Production impact is customer-visible; business-critical for the customer's in-product chat feature. Environment: Production (dedicated pool) in us-east. Recent changes: scheduler tuning (session-placement affinity / bin-packing thresholds) + runtime microkernel scheduler patch (PRs linked).
1) Use BrightHealth AI org credentials to create a chat completion request with streaming enabled against the dedicated endpoint in us-east.
2) Send a short user prompt (<50 tokens) with model pinned to redwood-chat-3b-quant.
3) Observe initial latency until first token and any streaming disconnects.
4) Repeat across ~100 requests to reproduce elevated median TTFB and intermittent timeouts.
Note: Issue is intermittent — amplify by running parallel clients at 20-40rps to match customer traffic pattern.
- Median TTFB increased from ~120ms (baseline) to ~900ms for short prompts.
- ~10% of streaming sessions fail to receive first token within 30s (client timeout).
- 5xx errors were not consistently present; many requests completed successfully but with long stall before initial token.
- Spike correlates with times of scheduler rebalancing and when new GPU workers join the pool.
Median TTFB should remain close to historical baseline (<250ms for short prompts) and streaming should deliver first token within the customer's client timeout window.
Representative logs attached (obfuscated):
- api-gateway request IDs: rQk-9a1, rQk-9a2, rQk-9a7 show 28s stall before first token.
- serving-runtime traces: long wait in `kv_cache_lookup` + `worker-queue-wait` for requests routed to node gpu-12.
- scheduler logs: rebalance cycle triggered and moved 18 sessions at 2026-03-09T22:14:03Z.
- nginx upstream times do not indicate client-level network stalls.
(Full logs uploaded to attached artifacts: s3://support-artifacts/SUP-17583/)
Initial hypothesis: scheduler tuning changed session placement causing some requests to queue behind heavy priming work on newly provisioned GPUs.
Repro attempt in staging with identical scheduler flags reproduced median TTFB increase when simulated priming traffic present.
Tracing shows increased `worker-queue` latency specifically when requests land on nodes that recently received large KV cache loads (priming / prefix caching).
Correlation observed between rebalance events (scheduler) and TTFB spikes; nodes that accepted moved sessions show transient high queue times for ~30-90s after rebalance.
No widespread memory pressure or GPU OOMs found. CPU utilization on affected nodes spikes during rebalance window (related to cache materialization).
Potential secondary cause: runtime microkernel changed scheduling quantum causing fewer background cache materialization threads — prolonging priming time.
Customer-side telemetry: traffic pattern includes bursts of short interactive sessions which are sensitive to first-token latency.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12T08:05 - Ops: Temporary mitigation deployed — throttle rebalance frequency and prefer warm-hosts; monitoring for regressions.
Rolled back aggressive bin-packing scheduler flag on the customer's dedicated pool and applied a conservative rebalance cooldown (60s). Additionally re-enabled opportunistic cache materialization setting on affected runtime nodes. These mitigations reduced median TTFB back toward baseline in canary tests.
Scheduler rebalance interaction with recent runtime microkernel change: rebalance moved sessions to nodes that required KV/prefix cache materialization while runtime deprioritized background cache work, causing a window where new requests queued behind cache warm-up and increased first-token latency.
1) Patch runtime (PR incoming) to restore opportunistic KV materialization threads during rebalance.
2) Revert aggressive scheduler bin-packing by default; introduce rollout gate and per-customer opt-in.
3) Add instrumentation to detect rebalance-induced cache-warm windows and auto-warm hot keys for moved sessions.
4) Postmortem and update runbook for rebalance + cache interactions.

Hotfix (scheduler cooldown + cache materialization toggle) applied to BrightHealth AI dedicated pool on 2026-03-11; customer confirmed marked improvement in TTFB by 2026-03-12. Follow-up runtime patch queued and slated for patch release. Postmortem will be published to Confluence after release.

Add automated alerting for TTFB regressions tied to rebalance events (owner: SRE on-call).
Update scheduling runbooks and gating for bin-packing flags (owner: Scheduler team).

Customer ask: Provide immediate re-run of March export including the missing rotation events, provide signed manifest and SHA256 of the export, explain why events were truncated and confirm retention/encryption controls requested in their security questionnaire (retention window, KMS key usage, access controls, log integrity checks).

Requested artifacts: sample CEF file for March 3-4, signed manifest (SHA256), export configuration for GigaHealth (filters, include_system_events), retention policy statement, KMS key id used for S3, access ACLs and IAM role used for delivery.

1) Customer submitted export request via support portal for March 1-7, format=Cef, destination=s3://gigahealth-redwood-exports, include_system_events=false
2) Support reproduced by triggering ad-hoc export for same range using internal export tool (redwoodctl export run --account 112233 --start 2026-03-03 --end 2026-03-04 --format cef --dest s3://internal-test-exports)
3) Examined resulting CEF and noticed missing events with event_type=service_account_rotation; compared against control-plane audit stream which contained the rotation events
4) Observed several heavy events (>900kB) that in CEF conversion were split and ended with '[TRUNCATED]'.
2026-03-03T14:12:09Z INFO log-exporter: converting event id=evt-7f4a to CEF size=1.2MB -> emitted chunk 1/2, chunk 2 ends with '[TRUNCATED]'
2026-03-03T14:12:10Z WARN s3-delivery: upload failed for object=evt-7f4a-cef-part2 size=340k error=kafka message too large
control-plane: 2026-03-03T13:59:55Z EVENT service_account_rotation id=rot-992 customer=112233 actor=system

Additional notes:
Hypothesis 1: include_system_events filter was unintentionally set to false for this customer during a prior compliance mapping change (see SUP-48099). Verified configuration value in customer export profile: include_system_events=false.
Hypothesis 2: Kafka broker max.message.bytes default (1MB) caused large CEF-converted events to be rejected/trimmed. Observed broker logs with 'Message too large' for topic redwood-exports and corresponding s3-delivery warnings.
Evidence: Control-plane audit stream contains service_account_rotation events; those events are absent from initial export. Rerun with include_system_events=true returned the missing rotation events.

Workaround implemented: re-ran March export with include_system_events=true and enabled multipart S3 delivery; uploaded signed manifest (SHA256) and provided to customer. Runbook updates: add explicit step to verify include_system_events flag for compliance exports. Follow-ups: scheduled technical walkthrough on 2026-03-15, provide final attestation document for SOC2 by 2026-03-18, and close once customer confirms receipt to auditors.

Issue summary: BrightHealth reported an increase in per-request cost and a small but measurable NLU accuracy drift after an on-prem tenant-specific optimizer toggle deployed on 2026-03-10. The toggle enabled mixed-precision + aggressive KV prefetch for tenants on Dedicated pools. Impact: ~12% increase in token billing for the tenant's top route, 3–5% drop in exact-match on a customer regression prompt set, and increased 95th-percentile tail latency (from 320ms to 580ms) for sequences >512 tokens. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east serving tenant brighthealth-prod; deployment applied via tenant optimizer profile v1.3. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send canonical regression prompt set (attached) to model redwood-neo-7b-v2 pinned to profile v1.3. 2) Observe and record per-token billing and EM metrics from console. 3) Compare latency distribution using span traces from the console. Observed behavior: billing spike appears within 10 minutes of a rolling optimizer toggle; accuracy degradation is small but consistent on the provided regression set and correlates with the switch to mixed-precision + prefetch. Hypothesis: aggressive KV prefetch is evicting critical prefix cache entries and interaction with quantized kernels is causing slight numerical divergence (quantization-induced rounding) that manifests as measurable EM drops on edge cases. Billing rise is likely due to increased token re-generation in client flows (retries) and longer GPU time due to fallback/inefficient kernel paths at certain sequence lengths. Temporary mitigations applied by customer: reverted the tenant's traffic to a shadow profile and rate-limited high-token routes. Supporting artifacts: console traces (link in comment), billing spike screenshot attached, regression prompt set attached.
2026-03-11 10:25 - Preliminary checks: SRE verified no node OOMs or GPU throttling in the dedicated pool. 2026-03-11 11:00 - Reproduced EM drop locally against the same model and profile under synthetic traffic; observed higher KV eviction counts during peak sequences. 2026-03-11 13:30 - Confirmed that fallback to fp32 kernels occurs intermittently for sequences >1024 when mixed-precision path encounters a misaligned tensor shape — increasing per-token latency. 2026-03-12 09:15 - Cross-checked billing records: top route showed 11.9% token cost increase month-over-month correlated with optimizer toggle time window.
1) Scoped traffic split: moved brighthealth-prod 100% back to stable profile v1.2 for latency-sensitive routes. 2) Applied per-route token limit of 2048 for the affected endpoint to prevent fallback kernel path. 3) Enabled extra telemetry for KV cache hits/evictions for the tenant. These reduced 95p latency to ~360ms and billing impact to ~+2% during mitigation window.
High-level: perform a conservative, staged rollback that preserves safety for other tenants and allows for forensic capture. Step 1 (preflight): create a snapshot of optimizer profiles and deploy a tenant-scoped snapshot archive (snapshot id: bh-rollback-0326). Export last 2h of KV-cache telemetry and capture a full request archive for the regression prompts. Step 2 (quarantine): route new traffic for brighthealth-prod to a dedicated stable host pool (if available) or to a latency-priority lane to limit blast radius. Step 3 (stepwise revert): (a) disable KV prefetch flag only, monitor 30m for latency and EM; (b) if stable, disable mixed-precision and switch to fp32 kernels for the tenant; (c) if EM/latency/ billing metrics recover, promote changes to stable. Step 4 (validation): run regression harness (provided) against 1k synthetic and 200 real requests and verify EM and latencies within ±1% of baseline. Step 5 (post-restore telemetry): keep elevated KV and kernel traces for 48h. Rollback notes: avoid global toggles; perform tenant-scoped toggles. If any step increases error rates or latency, abort and escalate to Eng duty (on-call scheduler).
1) Add a preflight optimizer compatibility test to CI that runs mixed-precision + kv-prefetch across sequence length ranges. 2) Implement a tenant-level circuit breaker that auto-reverts aggressive optimizer flags when EM or latency degrade beyond a threshold. 3) Update runbooks and add a ‘safe-revert’ API that atomically restores profile snapshot for a tenant. 4) Engineering to file follow-up PRs to make mixed-precision kernel fallbacks cheaper (github PR referenced).
- ENG: add preflight CI test — assigned to @marco (due 2026-03-24)
- OPS: build safe-revert script and document in Confluence (due 2026-03-19)
- CS: run customer validation call and confirm acceptable regression baseline (scheduled 2026-03-14)

- The UI still shows the pre-rollforward escalation list for ~5-10 minutes until a full refresh, but the backend evaluates the empty list and does not send notifications.

Steps to reproduce (attempted by Support and reproduced in staging):
1) Create a composite alert on console using a high-cardinality metric with an attached tracehook (org token).
2) Configure an escalation chain: webhooks -> PagerDuty -> email. Save rule.
3) Wait for the scheduled hourly retention rollforward job to run (simulate by running rollforward script in staging).
4) Trigger the alert condition.
5) Observe that no webhooks/PagerDuty notifications are sent and dashboard trace link returns 403 or trace ID missing.

Initial logs and evidence:
- API audit entry (alerts service) before rollforward: alert_config_id=abf-12ec; escalation_targets=[pd:PD-abc, webhook:https://hooks.example.com/bf]
- API audit entry after rollforward: alert_config_id=abf-12ec; escalation_targets=[]
- Console UI trace: GET /api/alerts/abf-12ec returned escalationTargets: [] at 2026-03-10T01:03:14Z
- Customer-reported incident ID: BL-INC-20260310-01

Notes about scope:
- This is not the same as missing alert deliveries caused by transient downstream failure; the persisted rule state itself is mutated.
- Affected customers are limited to orgs that have had historical index compactions and hourly rollforward enabled (enterprise/dedicated accounts with high ingestion).
Create composite alert with tracehook and escalation recipients in prod/staging console.
Ensure hourly retention rollforward job is scheduled or run the rollforward script manually in staging.
Trigger the alert and observe notification delivery and trace link behavior before and after the rollforward run.
Compare alert_config documents in the alerts service DB pre- and post-rollforward (watch escalationTargets and tracehookParams fields).
2026-03-10T00:59:02Z alerts-service INFO Persisted alert abf-12ec with escalationTargets=[pd:PD-abc, webhook:https://hooks.example.com/bf]
2026-03-10T01:02:47Z retention-worker INFO Starting hourly rollforward for org=brightlens, index=usage-v2
2026-03-10T01:03:12Z alerts-service WARN Updated alert abf-12ec: escalationTargets=[] (source=rollforward job migration)
2026-03-10T01:04:05Z console-proxy ERROR Tracehook lookup failed for token=null for alert abf-12ec
Support reproduced behavior in staging by running hourly rollforward script against a copy of customer's alerts DB snapshot.
Hypothesis: rollforward migration job applies a schema normalization step that overwrites nested recipient arrays when encountering high-cardinality target metadata; related to recent retention compact rewrite (PR #2289).
DB diff shows that migration pipeline writes a transformed alert document where 'escalationTargets' is initialised from an intermediary map that is empty for webhook+pd entries when non-legacy target metadata present.
Retention worker logs show 'migration:normalize_targets' step executed at 2026-03-10T01:03:10Z for org brightlens - correlates with updated_at on alert document.
Tracehook tokens are stored as namespaced parameters on the alert document; migration attempted to dedupe repeated tokens and dropped them when it encountered duplicate token hash collision.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 08:13 - Customer (BrightLens Support Contact - Mark Ellis): Confirmed we received a test notification post-fix and trace links restored. Requesting timeline of root cause and mitigation for production.
Mitigation: Rolled back migration step 'normalize_targets' in production retention worker and applied a patch to preserve existing 'escalationTargets' and 'tracehookParams' arrays (PR #2334). Workaround for impacted customers: re-save affected alert rules in console to repopulate UI caches. Root cause: migration assumed a flattened target mapping and dropped nested recipient lists when encountering non-legacy metadata shapes. Follow-up: postmortem and hardened migration tests added to pipeline; add guards in retention worker to avoid in-place mutation of alert documents without a transactional backup. Production rollback scheduled on 2026-03-13 01:00 UTC; customer notified.
Create postmortem page and link to incident BL-INC-20260310-01
Add unit + integration tests for migration pipeline covering compound escalation targets
Run an org-scoped dry-run on retention jobs that output delta report before applying changes (build feature request)
Notify customers in similar cohorts and provide remediation script to restore tracehook tokens if needed
payload.summary: Alert escalation chain and tracehook parameters cleared during hourly retention rollforward

Issue summary: Customer reports that when their iOS app is backgrounded and later resumed, SSE streaming resumes but the returned stream contains a duplicated opening sentence and an unclosed Markdown codeblock (triple-backtick). Impact: renders assistant output unusable for downstream rendering (NoteStream shows hanging codeblocks and repeated leading text). Environment: production, SDK iOS v1.4.2, mobile carriers and wifi observed in us-west region.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a streaming chat via iOS SDK (v1.4.2) using SSE transport to redwood endpoint in us-west.
2) Allow stream to produce a partial response that includes a codeblock (```js).
3) Background the app (iOS suspend) for ~30s.
4) Bring app to foreground and allow SDK to resume connection/handshake.

Observed behavior: On resume the client receives a replayed opening sentence at the top of the resumed chunk (duplicate of earlier prefix) and the final codeblock fence is missing on the stream end, leaving markdown unclosed. In some sessions the server emits the final end-event, but the SDK's recomposition appears to drop the trailing backticks.

Expected behavior: Resume should continue from the last emitted token without re-emitting already-received tokens; final markdown fences should be preserved so output parses as valid markdown.

Recent changes: Customer updated to SDK 1.4.2 last week; server-side recent change was an idle-keepalive tweak rolled 2026-03-08 (serving-runtime heartbeat window tightening).

Logs / sample traces: Customer attached SDK logs showing session id and resume handshake. Key excerpt:
[2026-03-10T15:12:02Z] SSE:onmessage {chunkId: "c-7f3a", text: "Here is a helper function...
```js
function add(a, b) {"}
[2026-03-10T15:12:34Z] App:backgrounding
[2026-03-10T15:13:04Z] SDK:reconnect attempt
[2026-03-10T15:13:05Z] SSE:onmessage {chunkId: "c-7f3a-resume", text: "Here is a helper function...
```js
function add(a, b) {
```"}
(Notice duplicate opening sentence and missing closing fence in the first message before a subsequent small patch message closes fence intermittently.)

Temporary workaround: Customer downgraded to SDK v1.3.8 and reports no duplication in their tests. Workaround also: avoid backgrounding during active streaming sessions or add client-side post-processing to dedupe repeated prefix and append closing fence when missing.

Customer impact: NoteStream has ~120 active users hitting this flow daily; rendering bug blocks note previews and causes UX regressions.

Investigation notes (engineer):
- Initial hypothesis: session resume logic in SDK treats resume as a fresh partial and replays buffered prefix rather than deduplicating overlap.
- Alternative hypothesis: serving-runtime keepalive/heartbeat change shortened idle window causing the client to reattach to a slightly different resume offset, resulting in server re-sending range that overlaps.
- Repro attempt on prod-us-west with internal test client reproduced duplicate prefix when using iOS SDK v1.4.2 and iOS suspend; reproduction rate ~40%.
- Server logs for session show resume requests with range header window [tokens 0..N] instead of [N+1..]. Need to correlate token offsets across client/server.
- No evidence of proxy tampering; connection observed to reestablish directly to edge instance.

Next steps:
1) Engineering to add additional debug logging on resume offset negotiation in serving-runtime (trace token-offsets) and coordinate with SDK team to log client-side last-received-offset before reconnect. (Assigned to @Ethan Liu)
2) SDK team to audit v1.4.2 resume assembly path and dedupe logic; consider backporting v1.3.8 resume behavior if regression confirmed. (Assigned to SDK)
3) Provision a canary with extended resume-window tolerance on one us-west edge to validate server-side mitigation.

Resolution plan: TBD — awaiting SDK hotfix or server resume-offset clamp.

References: Slack thread #support-note-stream (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C02SUP123), test run log: s3://redwood-support/sup-424242/traces.log
2026-03-10 Priya Patel (Support) - Logged initial report and requested full SDK logs and reproducer steps. Noted customer downgraded to v1.3.8 as temporary validation.
2026-03-10 Customer (NoteStream Labs) - Provided SDK log bundle and short screen capture showing markdown rendering freeze in app. Reports repro only on iOS, not Android.
2026-03-11 Ethan Liu (Eng) - Reproduced locally with iOS simulator and SDK v1.4.2 using a background/foreground script. Observed the duplicated prefix. Created internal trace request: TRACE-98132.
2026-03-11 Jane K. (SDK Lead) - Investigating resume assembly path; suspect race where client buffers suffix and on reconnect both client and server replay overlapping token windows. Preparing patch to dedupe on assembly.
2026-03-12 Ethan Liu (Eng) - Correlated server token-offsets; server accepted resume-range starting from 0 for ~12% of resumed sessions in last 48h (likely tied to heartbeat change). Raising a serving-runtime change to clamp resume ranges.
Pending - engineering patch planned. SDK team to release v1.4.3 with dedupe-on-resume; server will also apply a resume-range-clamp canary in us-west. Customer workaround: continue using v1.3.8 or avoid backgrounding during active streams.
payload.summary: iOS SDK background-suspend -> SSE rehandshake produces duplicate opening sentence and leaves markdown codeblock unclosed on resume

Issue summary: Customer reports multi-step tool call workflows intermittently exceed end-to-end timeouts. Root cause suspected to be a synchronous schema-prefetch/handshake for every tool invocation introduced in SDK v2.7.
Impact: Several long-running customer workflows with 3+ sequential tool calls see 30-80% increase in tail latency; some requests hit application-level timeouts (30s) and fail. This affects customer-facing production traffic for ScribeAI (dedicated pool).
Environment: Production (us-east), dedicated capacity, SDK v2.7.1 pinned. Behavior not reproducible on staging because of different traffic multiplexing and disabled schema-prefetch flag there.
1) Deploy ScribeAI workload against Redwood prod endpoint (prod, us-east) with SDK v2.7.1 and tool-call flow enabled.
2) Issue a request that triggers a chain of 4 tool calls (e.g., parse -> enrich -> db_write -> notify) with streaming disabled.
3) Observe end-to-end latency per request in customer logs and in Redwood Console route-level dashboard.
4) Compare traces: look for a ~60-200ms synchronous round trip per tool call with tag 'schema-prefetch' or 'validator-ping'.
2026-03-12T14:21:03.512Z function-proxy[req-0ab4]: start tool-call parser (reqId=abc123)
2026-03-12T14:21:03.578Z schema-validator[conn-9f3]: prefetch/handshake-> validator v2 (latency=132ms) (reqId=abc123)
2026-03-12T14:21:03.712Z function-proxy[req-0ab4]: parser finished (processing=35ms) total-hop=200ms
2026-03-12T14:22:10.004Z api-gateway[req-7f1c]: request closed by client after 30s timeout (reqId=def456)
Note: traces show a near-linear increase ~130ms per tool call for affected traces.
Initial triage by Support: correlated customer error spikes with SDK v2.7.1 rollout on 2026-03-10; no infra changes in Dedicated pool around that time.
SRE (Elena) ran p99 latency queries on route: toolcall-heavy routes show +120ms p99 delta vs baseline for consecutive days.
Tracing indicates a synchronous HTTP gRPC call from function-proxy to schema-validator for every tool invocation; the validator is configured in SDK to 'prefetch' schemas when tool metadata flags are present.
Hypothesis: schema-prefetch handshake was added to improve validation correctness but was implemented synchronously on the hot path without caching across a request lifecycle.
Reproduction: Disabling SDK prefetch flag at client side reduces per-tool hop by ~110-140ms in controlled test (ScribeAI test harness).
Risk: Disabling prefetch may re-expose certain schema mismatch errors; need to ensure validation is performed asynchronously or cached per-request.
Related internal ticket INT-4031 raised to look at schema-validator scaling and potential batching options.
Observed no excess CPU/GPU saturation; validator latency appears to be the add-on hop (not serving runtime token generation).
Customer reports workflows with streaming off are worst affected because SDK waits for handshake before issuing next call.
Support - Aisha: Logged after customer report. Attached sample traces and asked ScribeAI for a minimal repro payload.
ScribeAI - Daniel (engineer): Provided two failing request IDs and a local repro using SDK v2.7.1. Noted failure rate ~6% during business hours.
SRE - Elena: Confirmed p99 increase; created INT-4031 to investigate validator behavior and whether batching could help.
Eng - Marco: Investigating SDK change that added 'schema-prefetch' handshake. Drafting quick mitigation to short-circuit handshake when a cached schema exists.
Support - Aisha: Proposed temporary client-side workaround (set REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH=false) and asked eng to validate implications.
ScribeAI - Daniel: Applied client-side workaround on a small percentage of traffic and observed significant drop in timeouts (from 4.2% to 0.5%).
Mitigated and rolling fix. Temporary mitigation: customer set REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH=false which removed synchronous handshake and reduced timeouts. Engineering pushed SDK patch v2.7.2 that makes prefetch asynchronous and adds per-request schema cache; serving-runtime PR added a short-circuit for cached schemas.
2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation validated by customer (client-side flag) — immediate reduction in timeouts observed.
2026-03-13: SDK v2.7.2 released (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/987) — makes schema-prefetch async and adds per-request LRU cache (TTL 2m).
2026-03-13: Serving-runtime PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2314) added tracing tags and a bypass when schema present in cache to avoid validator round-trip.
Follow-up: INT-4031 assigned to Validator team to evaluate persistent caching, batching validations for high-tool-count requests, and a longer-term TTL/consistency plan.
Customer follow-up: ScribeAI confirmed they will roll SDK v2.7.2 to 100% in 48 hours and requested a post-deploy verification window for latency regressions.
Postmortem/Action: Create Confluence postmortem and update SDK release notes indicating change in default behavior and guidance for customers on schema-heavy flows.
payload.summary: Per-tool schema-prefetch handshake adds 60-200ms per tool call, causing multi-tool sequences to time out

comments: 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z Aisha Kapoor: Initial ticket from FinSecure Labs. They attached sample artifact-checker logs and a screenshot of the serving node stacktrace. They report ~8% failure rate during peak batch jobs.

2026-03-10T10:04:00Z Noah Chen: Acknowledged. Asked for pcaps, proxy vendor+version, and whether bypassing the proxy removes the issue. Asked customer to provide control-plane request IDs that failed.

Issue summary:
Customers on a private deployment report intermittent artifact integrity check failures during model shard downloads. The serving node logs show successful HTTP range 206 responses but later hash checks fail and streaming sessions reset with TLS errors. Impact: at peak, ~8% of shard fetches for gptx-13b-quant-v1 in us-east fail, causing retries, increased latency, and transient request errors for end users.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peered to Redwood control plane)
- Customer egress via corporate forward proxy that performs TLS interception for inspection and also acts as an HTTP range coalescing/splitting device.
- Redwood artifact storage: presigned S3 URLs fetched over HTTPS via customer egress.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Start several concurrent generation requests against pinned gptx-13b-quant-v1 on dedicated serving nodes.
2) Watch serving logs: artifact-fetcher requests presigned range downloads for shard parts (range headers present).
3) Intermittently one of the range responses is returned as 206 but the returned payload length is shorter than the byte-range requested (proxy split/trim behavior).
4) Artifact integrity check fails (hash mismatch) and the serving node logs: "artifact validation error: invalid shard hash".
5) Serving runtime retries, attempts full-range re-download, which sometimes succeeds after fallback to a different presigned URL, but adds 300–1200ms latency per request.

Observed runtime logs (sanitized):
- artifact-fetcher: "GET https://s3-presigned... Range: bytes=1048576-2097151 -> 206 Partial Content, content-length: 1048576"
- net/transport: "read: unexpected EOF after 842312 bytes"
- artifact-checker: "validation failed: expected sha256=... got sha256=..."
- tls: "client handshake aborted: tls: unexpected message"

Hypothesis: The customer's forward proxy is performing two problematic behaviors in combination: (1) rewriting TLS SNI for outbound connections to a local inspection name which causes the presigned URL hostname to receive a certificate chain that does not match the original S3 name (benign for some clients but can break HTTP/2 connection pooling and lead to connection reuse anomalies); and (2) the proxy splits/coalesces Range requests (to optimize caching) and occasionally truncates returned ranges or closes TCP connections mid-response during aggressive keepalive recycling. When a partial response is truncated but the proxy still returns 206 with an incorrect content-length, the artifact-checker receives fewer bytes than expected and flags integrity errors. The TLS rewrite can exacerbate connection reuse causing the client to see truncated TLS records or handshake errors on resume, leading to more unsuccessful replays.

Temporary workaround attempted by customer:
- Bypass egress proxy for S3 hosts (route via direct internet egress) — this eliminated failures in their environment (confirms proxy involvement).
- Increase artifact-fetcher retry to more attempts — reduced impact but not acceptable long-term due to increased latency and cost.

Impact to customer: Production traffic experiences increased latency and occasional 5xx errors when shard integrity fails; customer has paused a subset of high-throughput workloads.

Requested from customer: capture tcpdump of failing fetch (pcap) and proxy debug logs showing range-splitting behavior, and confirm whether proxy rewrites SNI for S3 hostnames.

Recommended internal next steps: see investigation_notes.


Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:30 - FinSecure Labs (support@finsecure.example): Provided pcap and proxy vendor: 'PerimeterInspect v3.7'. Confirmed bypassing proxy for s3.amazonaws.com stops failures.
2026-03-12 16:40 - FinSecure Labs: Confirmed vendor opened ticket and will disable range-splitting for presigned URLs as interim fix. Asking Redwood for guidance to detect and surface these failures in Console automatically.
2026-03-11 07:50 - Captured pcap analysis: multiple GETs with Range header followed by 206 responses where actual TCP payload length < advertised Content-Length. Several TLS sessions show handshake resumed after server send close, producing 'unexpected EOF' in client read.
2026-03-11 08:12 - Compared working vs failing flows: when proxy bypassed, content-lengths match and no truncated reads. When proxy active, some ranges are returned in multiple TCP segments with final segment missing and FIN injected by proxy.
2026-03-11 10:00 - Kernel/TCP analysis: no retransmissions from origin; truncation occurs at proxy which likely re-maps ranges to cached objects and fails to assemble full body when caching window hits eviction during concurrent fetches.
2026-03-11 11:30 - TLS SNI rewrite check: proxy changes SNI to internal hostname 'inspect.local' resulting in cert name mismatch for s3.amazonaws.com. Client TLS config in artifact-fetcher ignores hostname mismatch for direct S3 but HTTP/2 connection pooling fails leading to reused connections with partial states.
2026-03-11 13:45 - Repro in lab: Enabled range-splitting + sni-rewrite in PerimeterInspect. Observed same artifact hash mismatches and increased 'tls: unexpected message' errors in client, matching customer logs.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Short-term mitigation validated: bypassing proxy for presigned S3 domains eliminated failures in customer environment.
2026-03-12 11:20 - Long-term options: (a) detect truncated range responses in artifact-fetcher and automatically retry full-range or re-request presigned URL; (b) add explicit Host header validation and verify TLS cert commonName before accepting pooled connection; (c) surface a console alert when a threshold of artifact validation failures occur per deployment to guide customers toward proxy bypass.
2026-03-12 12:30 - Open action: engineering to propose runtime changes to be resilient to proxy range-splitting (see linked PR for initial code sketch).
Workaround accepted by customer: disable range-splitting/cache-coalescing for presigned S3 URL patterns or configure egress bypass for s3.amazonaws.com. Engineering will implement improved detection and a safer retry strategy: on content-length mismatch or unexpected EOF, artifact-fetcher will attempt a full-range re-download from a fresh connection before failing integrity. Planned rollout: patch to artifact-fetcher in platform v1.78.0 and console alert to surface artifact-integrity spikes. Target ETA for patch: 2026-03-26. Customer will keep workaround until vendor patch is applied.
This ticket documents an intersection of application-layer proxy behavior and TLS interception causing artifact-integrity failures. Related to prior tickets about range/rewrite issues but unique due to combined SNI rewrite + range-splitting behavior. Consider adding guidance to private-deploy runbook about exempting presigned URLs from range-munging proxies.
payload.summary: Private deploy: intermittent artifact integrity failures when egress proxy rewrites TLS SNI and splits range requests

Issue summary: Customer reports an unexpected invoice line labeled 'edge-cache-probe' and 'tool-invoke:warmup' that consumed ~120k tokens and was billed at reserved rates after a model canary alias swap. Impact: BrightLens sees a $4,200 unplanned line on their monthly invoice; finance team is asking for explanation and reversal. Environment: Dedicated cluster (BrightLens dedicated pool), production, us-west region. Suspected correlation with a canary alias swap that happened 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC during a routine model variant rollout.
1) Customer performed a canary alias swap from redwood/llama-3b-8bit -> redwood/llama-3b-quantized at 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC.
2) Immediately after swap, automatic edge warmup probes were triggered by regional edge agents to populate KV caches and run prefix warmup heuristics.
3) Probes appear to have been routed through the hosted fallback path due to transient capacity pressure in the dedicated pool, but were billed at the customer's reserved rate in billing backfill.
4) Invoice shows 'edge-cache-probe' and 'tool-invoke:warmup' line items for 2026-03-10 02:14-02:30 UTC totaling ~120,345 tokens billed at reserved/dedicated rates.
5) Customer claims they did not intentionally run any batch or embed jobs during that window.
billing-backfill.log excerpt 2026-03-10T03:05:12Z: backfill job #87622 processed postbacks for org: brightlens-org-07, tag=edge-warmup, tokens=120345, rate_id=reserved-us-west-1
metering-service audit 2026-03-10T02:15:01Z: probe request id=probe-0a9f, route=hosted-fallback, origin=edge-agent-us-west-3, model=redwood/llama-3b-quantized
router logs 2026-03-10T02:14:58Z: dedicated pool saturated, fallback triggered to hosted pool; fallback policy: use-compatible-variant
kv-cache metrics 2026-03-10: high prefix miss rates observed 02:10-02:20 UTC, edge warmup triggered by autoscaler heuristics
2026-03-11 09:00 - Initial triage by Support (Sofia): identified invoice line and matched backfill job. Notified Billing Eng and SRE.
2026-03-11 11:20 - Billing Eng (Anika) noted tokens were attached to reserved rate_id despite router showing hosted-fallback path. Hypothesis: backfill pipeline reconciled postbacks by org tag and applied reserved billing tag during merge step.
2026-03-11 15:45 - SRE (Evan) reproduced scenario in staging: canary swap triggers edge warmup probes that may traverse fallback path under saturation. Repro shows probes emitted with probe tag but postback processor normalizes tag -> reserved when org has reserved_pool:true. Edge agent postbacks contained origin tag that should have prevented reserved rate application but metadata lost during async pipeline handoff.
2026-03-12 08:30 - Found reconciliation code path in metering-service (metering-reconcile.go) that overwrites route metadata when postback arrives with warmup tag; code path added in commit github.com/redwood-inference/metering-service@commit=ab3c5f2 to prioritize reserved mapping for dedicated orgs. That commit didn't account for edge-origin probes which should be treated as free warmup (no-charge) per edge warmup policy.
2026-03-12 13:00 - Confirmed produced tokens in backfill are genuine probe tokens (short sequences with warmup prefix). Customer tests confirm no manual traffic.
Support - Sofia Martinez (2026-03-11 09:12): Hi BrightLens team — we're investigating the unexpected line on your invoice. I've cross-referenced the invoice id INV-2026-03-10-BL and located a backfill job that posted tokens. We'll loop in engineering and billing. (Assigned to Evan)
Customer - Aaron Lee, BrightLens Finance (2026-03-11 10:03): Thanks Sofia. The line is marked 'edge-cache-probe' on the invoice and our finance team needs a reversal if it's a warmup probe. We did a canary swap but did not launch any traffic. Please advise ETA.
Billing Eng - Anika Rao (2026-03-11 11:45): I've pulled billing-backfill logs. Backfill applied rate_id reserved-us-west-1 for the org. Need metering team to confirm classification of these postbacks (probe vs real usage).
SRE - Evan Burke (2026-03-11 16:05): Reproduced behavior in staging. Postback pipeline normalizes routing metadata and reserved flag is overriding 'probe' tag. Sketching fix: preserve edge-origin or warmup tag through reconciliation step. Will open PR and attach link once ready.
Support - Sofia Martinez (2026-03-12 14:12): Update for BrightLens: engineering identified the reconciliation bug that caused warmup probes to be billed. We're prioritizing a fix and will submit a provisional credit for the charged amount while code change is validated.
Customer - Aaron Lee (2026-03-12 15:03): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please confirm when credit appears and whether similar events can be suppressed in future rollouts.
Root cause: metering reconciliation logic overwritten probe/origin metadata for postbacks coming from edge warmup probes, causing reserved rate assignment. Fix: metering-service PR #1423 updates reconciliation to preserve 'edge-warmup'/'probe' tags and enforce zero-charge policy for probe tokens. Action taken: provisional credit of $4,200 issued to BrightLens (credit memo CM-2026-03-13-BL) pending finalized billing backfill correction. Deployed hotfix to staging 2026-03-13 and scheduled production rollout 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC after smoke tests. Follow-ups: add e2e test to prevent metadata overwrite, update runbook to include warmup postback detection, and create alert for large warmup token spikes tied to canary swaps.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
FinEdge reports that when their internal client reuses a single TCP/WebSocket connection to multiplex multiple user sessions (separate logical streams) and performs retries on transient network errors, some downstream tool/function invocations are replayed more than once. This leads to duplicate side effects (e.g., duplicate database writes and double webhook calls).

Impact:
- Customer is seeing duplicated external side effects in production for ~3% of streaming sessions that experience a reconnect/retry.
- Affects enterprise plan workloads in us-east; customer has strict audit requirements.
- Immediate risk to data correctness; customer paused specific workflows while we investigate.

Environment:
- Customer uses SDKs: python 1.2.0, ts 0.11.3, go 0.8.1 (server-side multiplexing client).
- Server receiving multiplexed streams via our streaming-proxy service (version 3.4.1).
- Production region: us-east-1.

Steps to reproduce (from customer test harness):
1. Create two logical streams A and B over a single websocket connection using the client-side multiplexer library.
2. Issue a streaming chat message on stream A that triggers a function/tool call (e.g., POST to /execute-action).
3. Simulate transient network blip causing the websocket to reconnect and the client to replay in-flight messages for stream A only.
4. Observe that the external tool endpoint receives the invocation 2-3 times for some reconnects.

Observed behavior:
- Function/tool invocation is executed twice or thrice for a single logical request.
- SDKs attach an idempotency header in some flows (x-idempotency-key) but the key value is reused per WebSocket session rather than per logical invocation in the multiplexed scenario.

Expected behavior:
- Retries/replays from the client should be deduplicated server-side using a per-invocation idempotency key, or clients should provide unique idempotency keys per logical invocation even when multiplexing streams over one connection.

Customer request:
- Immediate mitigation: guidance on how to configure client SDKs and server-side settings to avoid duplicate side effects.
- Long-term: ensure SDKs and proxies handle multiplexed replay safely or document required client behavior.

Additional notes:
2026-03-09 12:45 - Customer (FinEdge) - Nora Patel: Uploaded sample logs and a small repro harness. Noted that the client multiplexer keeps per-stream sequence numbers but the idempotency key is derived from the websocket session UUID + stream id; when the client replays queued frames it reuses the same idempotency key across replay attempts.
2026-03-12 16:22 - Customer (FinEdge) - Nora Patel: Applied the per-invocation idempotency key change in their workaround. Reported initial verification: no duplicates in 48-hour smoke test.
2026-03-12 17:05 - Support (Ava Martinez): Noted next steps with customer: postmortem and permanent rollout, plus a checkbox for customers building multiplexed clients indicating requirement for per-invocation idempotency keys.
Streaming-proxy v3.4.1 log patterns show request replay loops during websocket reconnect for multiplexer clients.
Dedupe store (redis) TTL set to 5m; in-flight replay can happen within that window but keys were being generated at the session scope, not at invocation scope.
SDK Python 1.2.0 multiplexing helper derived idempotency key as session_uuid + stream_id when using convenience helper; explicit idempotency_key param was optional and not enforced.
Go and TS SDKs have similar convenience helpers; behavior differs across languages leading to cross-lang customer confusion.
Canary of PR 412 added check to streaming-proxy: if x-idempotency-key present, honor it; otherwise generate a server-scoped strong nonce per-invocation when handler sees a function call frame. This reduces accidental reuse.
Runtime team: need to add telemetry to count 'replay-dedupe-misses' to catch future regressions automatically.
Suggested SDK change: make per-invocation idempotency key required for multiplexing helper with a clear runtime error when omitted.
Related internal ticket INT-418 tracks SDK changes and docs updates across python/js/go SDKs.

Workaround applied by customer: update client to generate an explicit per-invocation UUID and set x-idempotency-key on every function/tool call when using multiplexed streams. Runtime change (PR 412) to streaming-proxy to prefer explicit x-idempotency-key and to generate server-side per-invocation nonces when missing was canaried in us-east w/ no regressions.
Next steps:
- Merge PR 412 and roll out to all regions (runtime).
- Patch SDK helpers to require/auto-generate per-invocation idempotency keys for multiplexing helpers; raise an API error if not provided (SDK teams).
- Publish support note and SDK snippets for Python/TS/Go showing recommended pattern (Support/Docs).
- Add telemetry alert for replay-dedupe-misses and an internal runbook (SRE/Runtime).
Merge streaming-proxy PR 412 and release v3.4.2

Docs: publish support article and code snippets for per-invocation idempotency for multiplexed clients
Monitoring: add replay-dedupe-misses metric and alert in Console

Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring short windows (30s–3m) of severe throughput collapse in their dedicated pool. Behavior appears as staged or ‘phased’ bursts from multiple client instances that coincide with degraded p50/p95 token throughput and a spike in per-GPU queue serialization.

Impact:
- Customer’s production routes experience 60–90% drop in effective tokens/sec during each window.
- End-user latency p95 increases from ~120ms to >2s, and p99 can go to 6–8s.
- Affects several model routes and causes downstream request timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity reserved in prod-us-east (pool id: pool-09b7).
- Customer: Maple Analytics (dedicated plan).
- Observed across models: redwood/gpt-6b-open, mistral-instruct-7b.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1. Run 400 short streaming requests per minute from 12 ephemeral client instances (each opens/closers streams every 5–12s) targeted at the reserved pool.
2. Observe throughput and GPU allocation metrics in the console.
3. Reproduce windows align with external scheduled batch jobs the customer runs (not directly on Redwood).

Observed logs & metrics excerpts:
- serving-runtime logs: repeated entries showing small-batch reservations followed by delayed KV-cache pin release ("kv_cache: delayed_release timeout=30s tenant=maple-33").
- scheduler metrics: gpu_fragmentation_ratio spiking to 0.63 during events; free_slot_count dropping by 70% in 45s.
- autoscaler events: incremental allocations then immediate fragmentation warnings; no immediate scale-down because of transient high queue depth.
- network: no TLS or L7 errors observed.

Initial hypothesis:
Phased short-stream bursts from many ephemeral clients cause frequent microbatch reservations that do not fully release at the same cadence, which leads to fragmenting GPU slot allocation into islands that cannot efficiently coalesce. This produces queue serialization (requests waiting on a small set of active slots) and triggers autoscaler behavior that both over-allocates and then fails to improve throughput due to fragmentation and delayed KV-cache releases.

Requested by customer:
- Immediate mitigation to reduce event frequency and restore baseline throughput.
- Longer-term fix to avoid fragmentation from short-lived streams and ensure autoscaler uses fragmentation-aware placement.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:15 UTC - Correlated customer request patterns with timing of throughput collapses; events line up with ephemeral client restarts and a nightly batch in their infra.
2026-03-11 02:30 UTC - Observed repeated 'delayed_release' kv-cache warnings in serving-runtime. KV cache pins persist ~28–35s after stream close during events (expected ~5s).
2026-03-11 08:10 UTC - Reproduced locally in staging by simulating 10–15 clients with 5–12s short streams. Replication resulted in slot fragmentation and similar p95 increase.
2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - Temporary mitigation trial: lowered per-tenant short-stream reservation TTL from 30s to 8s in staging autoscaler config; fragmentation metrics improved in staging without immediate regressions.
2026-03-12 16:40 UTC - Noted customer SDK version 2.1.4 used; this SDK aggressively reopens streams without keepalive and can create microbursts. Requested they test a connection pooling patch.
2026-03-13 10:05 UTC - Eng added placement telemetry to scheduler for deeper analysis; confirmed small allocation islands caused by alternating microbatches that prevent large-batch packing.
2026-03-12 16:55 UTC - Customer engineer (Maple Analytics): We pushed a quick client patch to add connection pooling and saw fewer short-lived opens. Throughput improved during a short window; will run more tests overnight.
Temporary workaround provided: customer applied client-side connection pooling to reduce short-lived stream churn which restored throughput during validation windows. Support staged an autoscaler/serving runtime config change in staging to reduce short-stream reservation TTL (30s -> 8s) and added fragmentation-aware placement hints in the scheduler. Next steps: schedule a controlled canary rollout to pool-09b7, monitor fragmentation_ratio and p99 closely for 48 hours, then promote fix to production if stable. Engineering follow-up: implement scheduler-level microbatch coalescing and make short-stream TTL adaptive based on observed fragmentation metrics (tracked in related PR https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2289).

Issue summary:
During the midday traffic window on 2026-03-10, LuminaSearch observed a 30–60% reduction in steady-state throughput for their reserved dedicated pool in us-east. P50 latency increased modestly but p99 and token throughput showed periodic collapse for short bursts (~2–7 minutes). Impact: customer-facing search features experienced slowdowns and occasional 5xx fallbacks.

Impact:
- Affected customer: LuminaSearch (dedicated)
- Window: ~2026-03-10 12:10–13:05 UTC with recurring micro-wobble through the afternoon
- User-visible: search ranking queries retarded; fallback model invocations triggered

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) – prod-us-east
- Model: redwood/gpt-medium-v2 pinned by customer
- Autoscaler config: target_utilization=0.75, cooldown=120s, min_replicas=2, max_replicas=10

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Customer traffic reproduces normal bursty search pattern (many short single-token prompts, many concurrent connections).
2) At roughly 12:10 UTC, internal validator-sweeper jobs started a background sweep that spawns ephemeral validation requests against pinned models for telemetry.
3) Within 60–90s of sweep start, autoscaler trimmed new allocations and observed slot scarcity; throughput collapsed transiently and customer routes fell back to slower variants.

Observed metrics / logs:
- scheduler.allocation_miss rate spiked by 4x at 12:11 UTC
- autoscaler.decisions shows repeated shrink events followed by rapid grow (thrash) between 12:11–12:18 UTC
- GPU_slot_utilization per-node dropped 10–40% while pending_queue_length rose
- Validator-sweeper emitted many short-lived connections with keepalive=false (seen in sidecar logs)
- Sidecar metrics flagged many ephemeral attachments with small compute duration (<200ms)

Additional notes:
- No driver crashes or node reboots during window
- No direct network partition; control-plane health green


12:15 - Support: alerted by LuminaSearch CS about repeated p99 spikes and fallback to smaller model variants.
12:20 - Observability: found correlation between validator-sweeper runbook schedule and start of throughput wobble (internal cron at 12:10 UTC).
12:28 - SRE hypothesis: ephemeral validator jobs create many short attachments that soft-reserve allocator credits and compress heartbeat signals, confusing autoscaler sampling windows.
12:35 - Instrumentation: captured sidecar logs showing 8k ephemeral attach/detach events in a 6-minute span, avg lifetime 180ms; many from internal service validator-sweeper@infra.
12:48 - Confirmed: autoscaler sampling window uses decayed moving averages that underweight short-lived attachments, leading to repeated shrink decisions during the sweep. Shrink then starves longer-lived customer streams that get queued, causing throughput drop and grow oscillation.
13:00 - Experiment: disabled validator-sweeper in us-east staging. Immediate reduction in attach/detach churn and stabilization of autoscaler decisions in 2 mins.
13:20 - Found related config: validator-sweeper had recently been updated to increase concurrency from 5->40 without registering with resource-controller; change merged in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/582.
13:35 - Root-cause working theory: combined effect of (a) high-frequency ephemeral validator attachments that consume allocator credit in short bursts, and (b) autoscaler cooldown and sampling heuristics that misinterpret short-lived spikes as capacity release, causing under-provisioning for steady customer load.
13:50 - Cross-team sync: SRE, Serving, and Platform scheduled a mitigation and longer-term fix planning session.
Support (Amelia): Logged customer impact and opened incident. Notified on-call SRE.
SRE (Devon): Looking at autoscaler logs; seeing shrink/grow oscillation coincident with high attach churn. Investigating whether allocator credit accounting treats ephemeral attaches as 'free' and then releases too quickly.
Customer (LuminaSearch-SA): Observed search latency issues beginning 12:10 UTC; provided sample request IDs and traces (trace 8b3f7d). Asking for ETA on mitigation.
Platform (Marta): Disabled validator-sweeper schedule in us-east at 12:30 UTC as a test. Noted immediate improvement. Will roll back change if additional impact seen.
SRE (Devon): Temporary mitigation applied — throttled validator-sweeper concurrency and enabled attach debouncing in allocator config. Monitoring for 30 minutes.
Temporary mitigation: throttled internal validator-sweeper concurrency in prod-us-east, and applied attach-debounce (10s) in allocator to prevent credit thrash from sub-second attaches. This stopped the autoscaler oscillation and restored steady throughput for LuminaSearch by 12:35 UTC.

Permanent plan: (1) change validator-sweeper to use non-reserved telemetry path (no GPU attaches) or run sweeps on dedicated validation capacity; (2) update autoscaler sampling to weight longer-lived streams more heavily and add a short attach-debounce window before allowing shrink decisions; (3) add a safety circuit to prevent shrink if pending_queue_length > threshold. Owners: infra-team (sweeper changes) and autoscaler-team (sampling/decisions). Target ETA for permanent fixes: 2026-03-24.

Follow-ups: postmortem and config changes tracked in Confluence (see related page). Customer compensation request: LuminaSearch CS to engage commercial team if credit remediation is requested.
payload.summary: Midday reserved-capacity wobble caused by validator-sweeper ephemeral reservations and soft-reserve contention

Issue summary: After a scheduled optimizer experiment ramp (aggressive batching + PTQ quant profile) for tenant MapleAI, some long-lived streaming sessions saw sustained p95 latency spikes and occasional 5xx stream disconnects. An automated rewind script was run to restore the previous optimizer profile but the script returned success while the serving runtime continued to use the new profile for in-flight sessions. Impact: customer 95th percentile latency doubled on several routes; several high-value customers reported streaming disconnects during video ingestion workflows. Risk of SLA breach.

Environment: production, dedicated pool (MapleAI-reserved), us-west-2, runtime version rw-runtime@2026.03.01, optimizer-config v3.5.

Requested outcome: restore pre-experiment optimizer profile for both new and existing streaming sessions (or gracefully drain affected sessions) and provide a reproducible fix for the rewind script so it truly reconciles in-flight session config state.

1) In dedicated pool with tenant pin to optimizer-config v3.5, create a long-lived streaming session (>60s) that uses async incremental batching and prefix KV caching.
2) Trigger an optimizer feature ramp: enable aggressive-batching and ptq-evict-heuristics via feature flag for that tenant.
3) Observe p50/p95 latency baseline for streaming routes for ~10m, then initiate the automated rewind script that toggles optimizer profile back to v3.4 snapshot.
4) Note that API indicates script completed successfully, but in-flight streaming sessions still observe increased p95 and occasional stream disconnects; new sessions may or may not pick up the older profile depending on worker reuse.
runtime logs: rw-runtime WARN optimizer: attempted profile revert for tenant=mapleai tenant_snapshot=v3.4 returned success but session router did not evict worker cache (worker-id=gw-12f4)
scheduler logs: scheduler INFO drain: initiated drain for worker gw-12f4 but drain timed out after 120s while sessions remained active
console metrics: p95 for /v1/stream/generate increased from 210ms -> 520ms between 2026-03-10T14:02Z and 2026-03-10T14:12Z
customer telemetry: MapleAI ingest pipeline reported 2.1% stream disconnect rate during the window
Scoped traffic split: moved MapleAI traffic to a fallback routing policy that targets a compatible non-experimental model variant (rw-optimized/8b-compat) and throttled aggressive-batching flag for that tenant. This reduced p95 to ~280ms for most routes while we investigate.
Initial hypothesis: the rewind script updated tenant config in control plane but did not force worker-side KV eviction for in-flight sessions. Worker reuse and persistent KV caches mean sessions continued using PTQ-compiled kernels. Evidence: worker process gw-12f4 retained kv_cache_hits and used quantized kernel paths after revert. Repro on staging by running revert without explicit 'session-evict' call reproduces behaviour.

Next steps: add explicit worker eviction step to revert script, validate idempotent session drain procedure, add reconciliation check that queries worker process for active optimizer profile. Confirm changes in staging with long-lived sessions before prod redeploy.
1) Applied emergency traffic split to fallback model variant for MapleAI (completed 2026-03-10T15:04Z).
2) Manually forced a graceful drain on 3 workers showing inconsistent optimizer state (gw-12f4, gw-18a9, gw-2d7c).
3) Rolled back the revert script in control plane to block further automatic rewinds until fix is merged.
4) Captured detailed worker debug traces and uploaded to internal S3 for analysis (link: s3://redwood-debug/mapleai/rewind-2026-03-10.tar.gz).
Patch revert script to perform three-phase revert: (1) update tenant control-plane config, (2) query active workers and force-evict or gracefully drain sessions tied to old optimizer state, (3) verify worker reports new profile before allowing new sessions. Add a safe fallback that routes traffic away if drain does not complete within configured window. Add automated test that runs a long-lived streaming session in staging and validates profile reconciliation.
In progress: Runtime PR #1428 implements worker reconciliation and forced-evict API. After successful staging validation (long-lived streams test passed), we will schedule a controlled rollout. Temporary mitigations restored service levels while fix is validated. Final resolution will include a customer-facing postmortem and the updated revert script deployed to prod.

2) Add unit & integration tests for revert script (owner: Runtime Tools, due: 2026-03-14).
3) Draft customer postmortem and share timelines with MapleAI CS contact (owner: Aisha Malik, due: 2026-03-15).
4) Update Confluence runbook with new forced-evict procedure and safe timeouts (owner: SRE Docs, due: 2026-03-16).

Additional notes:
SRE (Diego Ramos): Confirmed worker-level KV cache persisted after control-plane revert. Proposed adding 'force-evict-sessions' and 'reconcile-worker-config' steps to revert script.
Customer (MapleAI - Priya Singh): Reported downstream ingest back to normal after traffic split but asked for permanent fix and explanatory postmortem.
Eng (Runtime Team - Mei Chen): Will prepare PR to add worker reconciliation check and make revert script atomic and idempotent. Targeting patch in staging by 2026-03-12.
