Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated short-lived websocket sessions from browser clients after high-volume multiplexed fanout (server-side sends same delta to ~40 clients). Affected sessions show a trailing 1-3 byte partial JSON fragment followed by an immediate silent reconnect loop (client reconnects but receives duplicate prefix tokens). Impact: several of customer's chat widgets display incomplete final sentences or duplicate prefixes, causing UX corruption and elevated error rates in their monitoring.

Impact:
- Partial outputs (incomplete last sentence) for ~12% of streaming requests during peak traffic windows (spikes to 1.2k RPS).
- Clients disconnect and reconnect automatically, resulting in doubled token consumption for a subset of flows and billing concerns.

Environment and constraints:
- Customer on enterprise Dedicated plan using private VPC egress through their edge appliance (A10/F5 managed by customer).
- Connections use websocket upgrades via our API gateway with HTTP/2 termination at the edge appliance and h1 to our gateway in the backend.

Observed behavior:
- Server sends well-formed JSON choice end event but client receives a final partial chunk (1-3 bytes) that cannot be parsed by the SDK JSON stream assembler.
- Client SDK shows an immediate reconnect with identical session-id; on reconnection the first chunks re-play the duplicated prefix tokens then stream continues (duplicate content + missing final clause).

Expected behavior:
- Client should receive full terminal chunk and not auto-reconnect due to malformed framing. No duplicate prefix replay on subsequent reconnects.

1) Customer configured multiplexed fanout: single model response broadcast to ~40 web clients using websocket multiplexing IDs.
2) Send long-running generation with trailing punctuation and multi-sentence finale (~400 tokens).
3) Observe on some clients: final JSON choice event arrives truncated by a few bytes, SDK JSON parser fails to finalize and triggers reconnect logic.
4) Reconnect receives prefix replays and duplicated token sequences before normal continuation.
edge-proxy (customer) tcpdump: observed HTTP/2 HEADERS + multiple DATA frames coalesced and then forwarded as single HTTP/1.1 chunk sequence to our gateway
gateway access log: ws upgrade successful -> stream id 0x7f3a; final write to socket shows 3 bytes less than server-side payload size
serving-runtime trace: choice-end event emitted at 2026-03-10T16:02:34.752Z size=312 bytes; low-level socket write returned size=309 bytes (on connection path with appliance).
client SDK logs (customer): JSONStreamAssembler error: Unfinished token at EOF. Triggering reconnect. SDK v1.14.2.
metrics: customer saw 2.1x reconnect rate for streaming connections between 16:00-16:20 PDT on 2026-03-10.
Initial hypothesis: gzip/Brotli or proxy buffer coalescing at the appliance is trimming or splitting chunk boundaries leading to incomplete final frames.
Reproduced in-house by inserting an HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 conversion proxy (nginx with http2 upstream) and high-fanout payloads; saw final DATA frame coalesced with keepalive and truncated by 1-4 bytes under certain buffering flags.
Correlation observed: issue only when customer's appliance performs HTTP/2 termination and uses 'http2-max-concurrent-streams' lower than our gateway defaults; reassembly window misaligned leading to drop of tail bytes on edge rewrite.
SDK behavior: on partial final JSON the assembler marks stream as corrupt and triggers immediate reconnect (no exponential backoff configured in customer's integration).
Not reproduced when bypassing appliance (direct path) or when using SSE long-poll fallback.
2026-03-10 19:05 - Support (Aisha): Asked customer for tcpdump from their egress appliance and full client SDK logs. Provided temporary instrumentation snippet for more detailed ws frame logging.
2026-03-10 20:30 - Customer (L. Chen, Northbridge): Uploaded tcpdump and confirmed appliance vendor support will review h2->h1 translation settings.
2026-03-11 09:12 - SRE (Tomás): Reproduced locally with nginx proxy config; created minimal repro harness (link to test harness in repo PR).
2026-03-11 11:40 - SRE (Tomás): Deployed temporary mitigation in gateway: added toleration for trailing partial fragment by buffering up-to 12 bytes and attempting JSON resync. Reduced observed client disconnects in controlled test from 18% to 2%.
2026-03-12 08:47 - Customer (L. Chen): Appliance vendor identified configuration option 'proxy_buffering on' + HTTP/2 coalescing as likely root cause and will apply a patch to preserve DATA frame boundaries.
2026-03-12 15:20 - Support (Aisha): Recommended customer apply appliance vendor patch and also update their client SDK to implement a short exponential backoff (500ms -> 1s) to avoid back-to-back reconnect storms.
2026-03-13 10:05 - SRE (Tomás): Noted follow-up: adjust gateway buffering change into a feature flag for controlled rollout. Created INT-4122 to track gateway code change and tests.
Workaround applied: gateway buffering tolerance enabled for affected connections (feature-flagged); attempted to silently reassemble small trailing fragments up to 12 bytes and deliver final event when valid JSON can be reconstructed.
Customer action: applied vendor patch to edge appliance to preserve HTTP/2 DATA frame boundaries and disabled aggressive coalescing. Vendor confirmed patch will be rolled to prod on 2026-03-14.
Client recommendation: upgrade SDK to v1.15.0 which includes safer reconnect backoff and a parser fallback that attempts a one-shot small-buffer reassemble before reconnecting (decreases duplicate-prefix replay).
Root cause: appliance HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation + buffer coalescing/truncation produced 1-4 byte tail loss on final DATA frames for high-fanout websocket payloads. SDK immediate reconnect logic amplified the impact by replaying prefixes and doubling token usage.
Follow-ups: INT-4122 (gateway buffering feature) for bounded reassembly; QA tests added to streaming regression suite to simulate h2->h1 conversion appliances; postmortem checklist entry to include advising enterprise customers on appliance configs for websocket paths.

Issue summary:
Customers behind a Finova Health integration report intermittent increases in p95 latency (~50-120 ms additional) for requests that should be routed to the us-east residency. Traces show occasional single-request hops to us-west (secondary) for short windows during traffic bursts; these hops correlate with a TLS handshake and an extra NAT hop, adding observed latency.

Impact:
- Intermittent p95 latency spikes for a subset (~0.8%) of requests from Finova's tenant.
- No increased 5xx rate observed.
- User-visible slowdowns in conversational features (web and mobile) during peak periods.

Environment:
- Customer Tier: enterprise (Finova Health)
- Redwood prod region: us-east primary for this tenant (residency pinned)
- Time window: recurring during peak traffic bursts (13:00-14:30 UTC last three days)

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Send 30 concurrent streaming generation requests pinned to tenant-residency us-east.
2) Repeat load in 1-minute bursts for 20 minutes.
3) Observe ~0.5-2% of requests with higher-than-normal p95 and a single cross-region hop visible in the trace.

Observed behavior from Redwood traces/logs:
- Trace IDs attached by customer show an extra TLS handshake and NAT source IP change for the subset of affected requests.
- Control-plane routing logs show pin refresh events around the same timestamps for the tenant but no explicit routing policy change.
- Edge LB logs show occasional 504s retried successfully (no customer-requested retries).
- Autoscaler metrics show ephemeral GPU pool pressure in us-east during the bursts; capacity autoscaled up within ~30s window.

Hypotheses so far:
- Short-lived capacity pressure in the primary us-east GPU pool triggers transient routing to the nearest compatible region (us-west) as a best-effort fallback.
- During fallback, a different egress path/NAT is taken, incurring TLS handshake + NAT traversal latency.
- Pin refresh and routing control-plane race during scale-up may allow a small number of in-flight requests to be routed to the fallback before sticky affinity is restored.

Investigation notes (engineering):
- Confirmed autoscaler events in us-east aligning with customer timestamps.
- Verified control-plane emitted fallback decisions; however, policy should prefer queuing or traffic shaping rather than immediate cross-region egress for enterprise-tenants with residency pins.
- Edge team observed that a small subset of front-proxy workers resumed routing to fallback region while control-plane signaled new pins — likely a timing window.
- No misconfiguration found in customer's residency settings.

Temporary mitigation/workaround provided to customer:
- Scoped rate-limiting on bursts at the proxy layer (applied for Finova) to reduce autoscaler pressure while we fix routing behavior.
- Recommend enabling a short request-queueing policy for pinned tenants (configurable) to avoid cross-region fallback during transient capacity shortages.

Next steps / action items:
1) Engineering: Add guardrail in routing decision path to prevent immediate cross-region egress for tenants with residency pins when autoscaler is scaling (ETA 2026-03-17).
2) Serving-runtime: Add tracing metadata to annotate control-plane pin version used for each request (ETA 2026-03-18).
3) SRE: Run load test reproducing burst pattern in dedicated staging to validate fix (ETA 2026-03-16).
4) CS: Keep customer updated, extend temporary rate-limiting if needed.

Attachments/logs referenced:
- Traces: trace-ids provided by customer (list attached in comments).
- Autoscaler logs: us-east autoscale events (internal link).
- Edge LB sample logs: 2026-03-12/13 window (internal link).

Resolution: (pending)
Root cause: (investigating currently; likely routing timing window during autoscaler scale-up)

Issue summary: Customer (AcmeDocs) reported reproducible truncated streaming responses when their clients switch network paths (Wi-Fi -> Cellular) while using SSE. The final JSON array terminator or closing object is missing in ~20% of reproductions, leaving the client-side parser hanging.

Impact: Customer reports production users see partial answers or clients that never receive the closing "end" marker for streamed choices; manifests as stuck UI and increased support tickets. Affects enterprise tier; customer needs a reliable streaming experience for their editor feature.

Environment: prod, us-east region, requests proxied through our edge (NGINX w/ TLS offload at CDN provider), fronted by Redwood API gateway, model: redwood-chat-v1 (streaming SSE).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open SSE stream to /v1/streams with long output (multi-paragraph).
2) Start on Wi-Fi. After ~3s of tokens, toggle to cellular (iPhone, or use iptables to emulate).
3) Observe stream: intermediate chunks arrive. In failing runs the last JSON chunk containing the terminal metadata and closing array/object is absent; the connection shows a short TLS-close from the CDN and the downstream SSE connection is left half-closed.

Observed behavior: Final closing JSON token ("event: done" + closing JSON) not received by client; server-side logs show the runtime emitted the terminal frame and then a short TLS record with FIN, but edge traces indicate the TLS record was split by TLS offload/inspector and reassembled differently by the CDN, leading to the closing delimiter being delivered in a separate segment that is dropped/reordered during the path migration.

Expected behavior: All stream terminal markers and closing JSON should reliably reach client even across network handoffs; stream reconnect/resume should preserve final marker or emit an explicit "terminal-missing" diagnostic if lost.

Attachments/logs: Provided below are trimmed excerpts from customer and edge traces (timestamps redacted):
- Client console: "SSE open, received chunk id=341, chunk id=342, ... hung"
- Edge proxy trace (hex of TLS record lengths): [0x16/0x03/0x03 len=2048] -> [0x16/0x03/0x03 len=128] -> (path-migrate) -> [0x17/0x03/0x03 len=24]
- Server runtime emit log: "choice_id=abc123 emitted final_event=done bytes=112"
- Upstream ack: "tcp retransmit, segment out of order"

Notes: Customer supplied PCAP showing that the closing JSON (final 112 bytes) is split across two TLS records and the CDN's TLS termination appears to coalesce different upstream segments when migrating the connection, resulting in a dropped tail when the client socket is rotated.

Priority justification: P1 because enterprise customer production UX affected and reproducer provided.

03-01: Support triaged with AcmeDocs. Initial hypothesis: proxy idle/keepalive teardown during path migration (similar to SUP-310999 patterns) but customer trace shows explicit TLS record boundary change.
03-01: SRE obtained edge NGINX + CDN termination logs; observed short TLS close immediately after runtime reported final emit. CDN records show two TLS records for the final payload that land across the path migration window.
03-02: Reproduced internally using a network-path-migration script (iperf+tc+ip rule) against staging with identical edge config; observed ~18% failure where final chunk not delivered to client-side SSE parser.
03-02: Instrumented runtime to include 'terminal-seq' tokens in final emit and added per-chunk sequence numbers; server sees final chunk emitted and acked by upstream TCP, but downstream SSE socket reports half-close before final delimiter reaches app layer.
03-02: Hypothesis refined: TLS offload device at CDN re-segments or coalesces TLS records and during path migration the CDN's socket handoff drops the last small record (common failure when 0-RTT or early-data path migration is enabled).
03-02: Correlation: failures cluster when final payload size < 256 bytes and when path change occurs within 1-2 RTTs after final emit.
03-03: Discussed mitigation: force runtime to send explicit keepalive/flush + larger trailing padding so terminal delimiter sits in an earlier/larger TLS record; or make the streaming protocol emit a separate guaranteed-final 'end-of-stream' event on reconnect if missing.
03-03: Linked to PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2291 (add terminal padding / explicit terminal marker) for testing; engineering to validate in staging with CDN offload enabled.
Workaround (short-term): Engineering released a staging build that appends a 512-byte padding block to the final SSE chunk so it is coalesced into a larger TLS record less likely to be dropped by CDN offload. Customer validated in their environment; failure rate dropped from ~18% to <1% in reproducer runs.

Planned permanent fix: (1) Add explicit durable terminal handshake: when client reconnects after an interrupted SSE, the runtime will return an explicit "terminal-missing" diagnostic and a pointer to fetch the final delta via REST. (2) Work with CDN partners to disable aggressive TLS early-data coalescing on streaming routes and add tests for segment boundary behavior. (3) Upstream runtime change (PR #2291) to optionally pad final chunk and add sequence numbers for integrity checks.

Rollout notes: Hotfix padding enabled behind a feature flag for affected enterprise customers. Will roll out to additional customers after partner config validation and synthetic test coverage added.

Additional notes:
2026-03-03 08:55 - Customer (AcmeDocs): Confirmed temporary padding workaround reduced incidents in their field test. Concerned about performance impact but accepts for now.
payload.summary: TLS offload segment-boundary shift causes SSE stream to lose terminal JSON delimiter after path migration

Issue summary: After enabling a tenant-level optimizer profile that enables aggressive KV prefetch (window=32) and a 4-bit quant profile (q4_mixed) the customer reports intermittent 5xx errors and a noticeable P99 tail latency increase for interactive chat routes.

Impact: Intermittent 5xx responses (approx 0.6% of requests during peak) and P95->P99 jump from ~450ms to ~1.2s for the tenant's primary chat route. Customer reports visible user complaints and warned they may revert to a competitor if unresolved.

Environment: Dedicated pool in prod-us-east serving BrightPost Health tenant. Traffic is primarily short-turn chat (avg seq len 80 tokens). The change was applied during a low-traffic maintenance window two days ago and rolled to 100% tenant traffic 90 minutes after initial canary.

Observed behavior: 1) Spikes of 502/503 with upstream serving-runtime logs showing 'KV_CACHE_MISS' thrashing followed by 'INFERENCE_TIMEOUT' entries. 2) Node-level GPU memory pressure observed on 2/6 nodes in the tenant pool with ephemeral OOM logs during the same window. 3) Error rate correlates with a rise in 'async_batch_queue_time' metric and increased packet-drop on egress links.

Expected behavior: Stable error rate (<=0.01%) and tail latencies within baseline SLO (P95 < 500ms, P99 < 800ms).

Attachments: telemetry snippets, trace ids, and sample request/response pairs included in logs field below.
1) Apply optimizer profile: kv_prefetch.window=32, enable async_batching=true, quant_profile=q4_mixed on tenant.
2) Route steady chat traffic that matches customer's seq length distribution (avg 80 tokens, 95th 330 tokens).
3) Observe tail latency and error rates over 30 minutes.
4) Check serving-runtime logs for KV eviction/rehydration patterns and scheduler for batch queue buildup.
Sample traces: trace-id: bp-20260309-1a2b (P99 1.32s, 503). Serving logs: 'kv_cache: eviction_count=456, prefetch_errors=12', 'scheduler: async_batch_wait_ms=1200', 'gpu0: mem_used=33000MiB / 34000MiB', recent Kubernetes pod events show transient OOMKilled on node-tn-04. Full log bundle uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/bpprod/sup-836201/log-bundle.tar.gz
Initial hypothesis: aggressive kv_prefetch expanded resident KV working set combined with q4_mixed memory layout caused increased GPU memory pressure and cache thrash, leading to longer queue times and timeouts. Alternate hypothesis: async batching combined with variable sequence lengths produced long-tail batching delays.

What we checked: recent rollout timeline, per-host GPU metrics, KV cache hit ratios, async batch queue histograms, tenant-specific traffic split. No code changes to serving runtime at rollout time besides optimizer config toggles. No infra events in cluster except the OOMs on two nodes pinned to tenant pool.

Immediate actions taken: 1) Scoped traffic split: we reduced the tenant rollout from 100% to 50% on the original snapshot to reduce pressure. 2) Created short-term circuit: lowered kv_prefetch.window to 8 for the tenant as a canary. 3) Temporarily pinned tenant to q8 quant profile for 30 minutes during the investigation which brought P99 back to ~780ms and reduced 5xxs to ~0.05%.

Next investigative steps: correlate per-request KV size distribution, run a tenant replay in staging with identical seq distribution, and test progressive kv_prefetch window sizing to identify inflection point.
2026-03-09 - Support (Ava Chen): Raised by customer at 09:12 UTC. Created ticket and escalated to SRE. First-pass suggested rollback options and asked for logs. (Assigned to Diego)
2026-03-09 - SRE (Diego Morales): Performed quick gating: rolled traffic back to snapshot-2026-0309-09 for tenant and temporarily set kv_prefetch.window=8. Observed immediate drop in 5xx. Requesting confirmation from customer on user-visible impact.
2026-03-10 - Customer (BrightPost SE - Maya Patel): Confirmed reduced errors after kv_prefetch window change and quant pin to q8. Reports slightly higher per-token cost but acceptable for now. Asks for recommended long-term safe rollout pattern so they can re-enable q4 in the future.
2026-03-11 - Support (Ava Chen): Proposed conservative staged rollout: (1) q8 -> shadow q4 traffic with 5% sampled traffic; (2) incremental kv_prefetch window increases 8->16->24 with 1-hour observation windows and automatic rollback on P99 or 5xx thresholds; (3) enable async_batching only after prefetched KV working set is stable. Suggested adding a circuit breaker that auto-demotes quant when per-node GPU mem_used > 90%.
2026-03-12 - SRE (Diego Morales): Implemented a tenant gating rule and created a safe rollback runbook (link in related_confluence_pages). Scheduling a staged replay in staging on 2026-03-13 to verify thresholds and collect exact inflection points for kv_prefetch window size.
Short term: Pin tenant to q8 quant profile and reduce kv_prefetch.window to 8, or temporarily disable kv_prefetch if memory pressure persists. Use traffic split to move 30-50% of traffic back to a known-good snapshot.

Medium term: Run a shadow q4 profile with sampled traffic and compare memory + latency metrics. Introduce an auto-demote policy that switches to q8 when GPU memory utilization >85% or P99 latency > 1s for more than 5 minutes.

Commands / config snippets (operator):
- rctl tenant update --id brightpost --optimizer kv_prefetch.window=8 --quant-profile=q8
- rctl traffic split --tenant brightpost --target-snapshot snapshot-2026-0309-09 --percent 40
- monitor: alerts for tenant.bp.p99_latency > 1s OR tenant.bp.5xx_rate > 0.2%
In progress: temporary mitigations applied (kv_prefetch.window reduced and quant pinned to q8). Customer confirmed reduced UX impact. Awaiting staging replay to recommend a safe staged rollout plan for re-enabling q4 and increased prefetch. Follow-up runbook link: confluence.redwood.com/display/SUPPORT/kv-prefetch-playbook.
payload.summary: Conservative opt-tuning safety net: tenant sees intermittent 5xx and elevated tail latency after enabling kv-prefetch + q4 quant profile

Issue summary:
Customer BrightChat has an explicit tenant-level model pin to redwood/open-7b-v2-quant for an SLA-sensitive route. During a streaming reconnect (client retried after a transient 502), the resumed stream was attached to an existing prewarm session owned by a canary cohort. The routing layer applied the prewarm session's metadata and routed the resumed request to the canary variant instead of honoring the tenant pin.

Impact:
- BrightChat observed degraded quality responses for ~6 minutes for ~1200 requests (partial sessions) while their tenant pin was effectively bypassed.
- Cost spike: routed to a larger variant intermittently causing token billing increase.
- Customer-facing latency and content regressions; they opened an incident citing production impact.

Environment:
- Production, us-east cluster (region: us-east-1).
- Dedicated capacity pool id: ded-nyc-3 (BrightChat).
- Canary rollout active for redwood/open-7b-v2-quant: weight 7%.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Configure tenant TID-992 with explicit model_pin=redwood/open-7b-v2-quant via Console.
2) Trigger a streaming generation that prewarms canary pods (small warmup traffic).
3) Cause a transient 502 on the edge for the client and have the client reconnect the same stream id.
4) Observe routing decision in logs and confirm model id selected.

Observed behavior:
- Resumed stream was routed to canary variant (redwood/open-7b-v2-quant-canary-2026-02-09) despite tenant model_pin setting.
- Edge trace id: trace-us-east-0a-8f7c9b2d.
- Orchestrator decision log snippet: "selected_session=prewarm-session-cc33, effective_model=canary-variant, tenant_pin_present=true"

Expected behavior:
- Tenant model_pin must override ephemeral prewarm-session attachments; resumed streams should respect the tenant-level pin and route to the pinned variant or fallback according to explicit routing policy.

Logs & artifacts attached (provided by customer and support):
- Edge traces: trace-us-east-0a-8f7c9b2d, trace-us-east-0a-8f7c9b3f.
- Orchestrator decision dump (sanitized): decision-2026-02-10-14-22.log (attached).
- Customer sample prompts + responses showing quality delta (attached).

Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-02-10: Filed on behalf of BrightChat. Attached edge traces and decision logs. Customer reports immediate quality regression and cost bump. Requesting SRE triage and a short-term mitigation to prevent further user impact.
SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-02-10: Acknowledged. Reproduced locally using a simulated streaming reconnect. Initial hypothesis: routing priority comparator incorrectly ranks active prewarm session metadata above tenant pin when both are present on a resumed stream. Collecting more traces and adding debug logging in routing-mesh decision path.
Customer (BrightChat, Elena Rivera) 2026-02-10: Impact confirmed. We can temporarily stop canary traffic but prefer a hotfix to ensure pins are authoritative. Provided request IDs and session ids on our side.
SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-02-11: Found comparator behavior in routing-mesh: prewarm sessions set session_priority='session' while tenant pins set session_priority='pin' but comparator logic treats non-empty strings with lexical precedence so 'session' > 'pin' in current implementation. Posting proposed fix to override comparator to check explicit_pin boolean first. Preparing PR and test cases.
Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-02-11: Communicated workaround to BrightChat: (1) disable canary weight for the impacted model in us-east, (2) create a CLI-level model override for tenant route via route.override_model_id until the patch is deployed. Customer applied workaround and reports traffic reverted to pinned model; monitoring continues.
Summary of findings:
- Reproducible: yes, with streaming reconnect flow.
- Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by log inspection): priority comparator in routing-mesh used lexicographic ordering on a small set of session_priority tokens rather than explicit flag semantics. Because 'session' sorts after 'pin', prewarm session metadata won when both present.
- Secondary contributing factor: resumed streams reattach session metadata before pin reconciliation runs, so the mid-path comparator had to disambiguate and it currently doesn't check explicit_pin boolean early.
- Risk: any resumed streaming clients that reconnect to a prewarm session may temporarily bypass tenant pins during a rollout window.
- Test coverage gap: no unit test validated session vs pin precedence with streaming reconnect semantics.

Next steps:
- Create PR to change comparator to: if explicit_pin present => choose pin; else consider session metadata. Add unit tests for streaming-reconnect scenarios. (PR opened in routing-mesh repo).
- Backfill a small reconciler job to find tenants whose live sessions are attached to prewarm canary pods and reassign or evict sessions if tenant_pin exists. This mitigates already-affected customers until roll-out of fix.
- Post-deploy: run a Canary simulation harness for streaming reconnect permutations.

Applied by customer: temporarily set canary weight for redwood/open-7b-v2-quant in us-east to 0% and created a route.override_model_id for tenant TID-992. Support recommended restarting affected prewarm sessions (or blocking reuse) as a short-term mitigation. This restored pinned routing and prevented further regressions.
Fix in progress: routing-mesh comparator patch authored and under review. Reconciler plan drafted for immediate remediation. Target patch deployment to prod us-east: 2026-02-12 (pending review and QA).
PR review and merge: routing-mesh comparator fix (https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-mesh/pull/891)
Deploy reconciler job to us-east to evict/rewire prewarm sessions that conflict with explicit tenant pins
Add unit/integration tests covering streaming reconnect + pin precedence
Communicate root cause and postmortem to BrightChat when incident closed
payload.summary: Streaming reconnect resumes on prewarm session and overrides explicit tenant model pin, causing fallback to canary variant

2026-03-14T10:03:00Z Miguel Santos: Confirmed intermittent header drop on eu-west edge for multipart/form-data fanout paths when proxy layer performs canonicalization. Reproduced locally with a synthetic fanout and slow webhook responder.

2026-03-15T08:41:00Z Miguel Santos: Shared temporary mitigation steps (disable auto-retry for funcalls or increase ack window). Opening linked PR in SDK to add stronger header preservation and optional server-side dedupe for webhook fanout. See related_github_prs.

Issue summary:
Customer observed duplicate side-effects (duplicate downstream payments and duplicate job dispatches) when using function-calling with an external webhook confirmation flow. The application fans out function call completions to a third-party webhook endpoint in multiple regions via our webhook fanout feature.

Impact:
- Two customers reported doubled transactions within a 2-hour window (FinSaaS staging -> prod migration).
- Duplicates are intermittent (~1 in 1,200 requests) but high severity for finance workloads.

Environment:
- Customer: FinSaaS Inc. (enterprise)
- SDKs in use: python-sdk v1.8.3 (server worker), ts-sdk v1.9.0 (edge orchestrator)
- Platform: Redwood hosted prod, multi-region fanout (us-east, eu-west)
- Model: rw-3.8b-chat pinned in config

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Client issues function call that triggers external webhook fanout to third-party payment processor.
2) SDK sends funcall request with idempotency token in X-Redwood-Id header.
3) Webhook endpoint experiences a transient spike (100ms->1200ms processing) in eu-west resulting in delayed 200 OK confirmation.
4) SDK (python worker) does an automatic retry after ack window expires (default 750ms configured by customer on worker pool).
5) Downstream processor receives two separate POSTs; their payloads are semantically identical but have slightly different Redwoods request ids and the idempotency header is missing in the second POST due to proxy rewrite on the eu-west edge.

Expected behavior:
- Client retry should not produce duplicate external side-effects when webhook confirmation eventually succeeds; idempotency token should be preserved end-to-end or the platform should suppress duplicate fanout if confirmation arrives late.

Actual behavior:
- Duplicate side-effects observed when confirmation latency exceeds client ack window and one of the edge routes strips or rewrites the X-Redwood-Id header.

Logs/IDs attached:
- Customer request ids: rwd-cust-20260314-9a1, rwd-cust-20260314-9b2
- Edge traces: trace-us-2247, trace-eu-7832
- Slack thread: #support-fintech (link provided in related_confluence_pages)

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 13:27 - FinSaaS Ops (customer): Noted that setting client ack window to 2s reduced duplicate rate but did not eliminate duplicates. Asked whether platform can guarantee 'at-most-once' semantics for webhook fanouts.
Hypothesis:
- The root cause appears to be a race between client-side retry driven by ack-window expiry and an edge proxy path that rewrites/sanitizes headers for multipart fanout routes. When the second request loses the idempotency header, downstream sees it as a distinct invocation.
Evidence collected:
- Packet traces show the original request arriving at eu-west with X-Redwood-Id present. The same request, when re-sent by the sdk-backed worker, goes through the us-east edge route for that retry and passes through a different sidecar that normalizes header casing and drops unknown headers for multipart content.
- Router logs (trace-eu-7832) include a 502 transient between edge and webhook, followed by a successful 200 for the re-sent request.
- SDK logs: python-sdk v1.8.3 shows a retry at +820ms after initial send due to ack timeout configured at 750ms by customer. ts-sdk orchestration logs show coordinated fanout to two regions; eu-west returned late.
Candidates for fix:
1) Server-side dedupe for webhook fanout using a canonical idempotency token computed from body+signature when X-Redwood-Id missing.
2) Ensure edge proxies preserve X-Redwood-Id for fanout routes and stop header canonicalization on multipart paths.
3) Expose SDK option to mark particular funcalls as "external-confirmation-required" and disable automatic retries for those calls, leaving retry responsibility to application logic.
4) Increase default ack window in our python-sdk for enterprise worker pools or make it configurable from Console per-route.
Related artifacts:
- Local reproducer: synthetic slow-webhook script + fanout test corpus (internal repro link in INT-412).
- Slack thread: #support-fintech (internal)
Short-term mitigation steps provided to customer:
- Set the ack window to 2500ms on server worker pool (python) to reduce accidental retries.
- Disable automatic retry for funcalls that fan out to external payment processors.
- Add a per-call idempotency token in the webhook body payload (in addition to X-Redwood-Id) so downstream can dedupe when headers are missing.
These are documented to the customer; they reported fewer duplicates after increasing ack window but requested a platform-side fix for hardened at-most-once behavior.
In Progress: engineering is preparing a two-part fix: (1) edge proxy config change to stop header canonicalization for multipart fanout routes, and (2) server-side dedupe on webhook fanout that falls back to body-signature-based idempotency when header absent. ETA for staged rollout: 2026-03-22.
payload.summary: External webhook confirmation delayed during multi-region fanout causing duplicate function-side effects

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Helios Health is reviewing a draft public case study and requested exact technical details for audit log export formats and retention so their Legal/Compliance team can approve any security-related statements.

Customer questions to answer (for public write-up accuracy):
1) Export format: Are audit logs available as JSON/CSV? Is it JSONL? Is the schema documented and stable?
2) Export transport: Can Redwood export to customer-controlled storage (e.g., S3) and/or SIEM? Is it pull (API) or push (delivery job)?
3) Timestamping: Are timestamps UTC? Is there an ingestion timestamp vs event timestamp?
4) Fields included: Do events include actor identity, action, resource, source IP, request ID/trace ID?
5) Retention: What is the default retention in Redwood Console? Can it be configured (e.g., 90/180/365 days)?
6) Private deployment nuance: In Helios’s VPC deployment, do audit logs stay in the VPC and can they be exported without traversing public internet?
7) Wording constraints: What claim language is acceptable for public case study (avoid over-precise commitments / avoid implying certifications)?

Impact:
Blocked on approval of the Helios case study security section and architecture diagram callouts (audit logging + KMS).

Context:
This ticket is specifically to provide accurate, supportable answers and pre-approved claim language for Marketing to use. Any final customer-facing phrasing still needs Helios review/approval.

Requested output:
- Answer set for Helios (can be shared in email)
- Proposed public-safe wording + caveats (metrics/retention ranges) for case study draft

Owner / involved:
- Solutions Engineering: Markus Klein, Simran Kaur
- CS / reference liaison: Miguel Santos, Rachel Kim
- Security review: internal Security & Compliance (async via #security-help)

Links:
- Draft case study section referenced in Helios approval thread (internal)
- Support ticket created to ensure statements align with actual product behavior

Additional notes:
- Audit events are recorded in the Private control plane and visible in the Redwood Console (customer tenant).
- Export is available via API (customer can pull) and via scheduled delivery to customer-controlled object storage when configured (commonly S3-compatible). For Helios’s deployment, delivery stays within the customer’s VPC networking path (no public endpoint required) assuming VPC endpoint / private routing is configured on their side.
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL). We can also generate CSV via the API for ad-hoc pulls, but the canonical export is JSONL.
- Timestamps: event_time is emitted in UTC (RFC3339). delivery_time is included for delivery jobs.
- Fields: event_type, actor (user/service account), action, resource_type/resource_id, result (success/failure), source_ip (when available), region, and request_id for API-originated events.
I’m drafting a short ‘public-safe’ blurb (no hard numeric retention claims) and a more detailed appendix for Helios internal approval.
Proposed public case study language (approved internally):
“Helios runs Redwood Private in a VPC and uses Redwood audit logs to track administrative and API events. Audit events can be exported in JSON format to customer-controlled storage for compliance and retention needs.”
Optional technical appendix for Helios internal reviewers:
- Export format: JSONL (newline-delimited JSON)
- Time format: UTC (RFC3339)
- Typical fields: actor, action, resource, result, request_id, source_ip (when available)
- Retention: configurable in the Console; for long-term retention customers export to their own storage/SIEM
I will send this to Miguel to forward to Helios.
“...exported in JSON format to customer-controlled storage, where it can be forwarded into existing security and compliance tooling.”
This avoids promising a first-party SIEM integration. Marking ticket resolved unless Helios requests additional details or a schema doc link.
Provided Helios Health with confirmed audit log export details (JSONL canonical export; API pull + optional scheduled delivery to customer-controlled storage; UTC timestamps; common event fields) and internally-approved public-safe case study wording emphasizing configurable retention and export to customer-controlled storage. Avoided claims of immutability, specific retention maximums, or native SIEM connectors without customer-specific confirmation.
payload.summary: Helios Health: audit log export format + retention wording confirmation for public case study write-up

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer Novara Health observed a class of requests that had been explicitly pinned to redwood-v2-13b-quant-muted during a staged canary roll that were suddenly served by the fallback variant redwood-v2-13b-fallback. The transition coincided with heavy client-side HTTP/2 multiplexing and a burst of keepalive/reconnects from a downstream proxy.

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints returned lower-quality outputs for ~8 minutes for a small cohort (~0.6% of their traffic), causing a product regression and one elevated support alert.
- Observed token-cost increase due to fallback variant having a different batching/quantization profile.
- Customer reporting incorrect inference outputs in clinical summarization tests.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: novara-dedicated-1 (prod-us-east)
- Canary variant: redwood-v2-13b-quant-muted (pinned for cohort via per-tenant policy)
- Edge: client -> customer-proxy -> redwood-edge-proxy (h2 multiplexing enabled) -> api-gateway -> orchestrator -> serving-runtime

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer traffic with persistent connection and HTTP/2 multiplexing active.
2) Large number of concurrent keepalive PINGs and a reconnect wave from customer-proxy at 2026-03-13T16:07:12Z.
3) Orchestrator logs show two session IDs merged for the same tenant during the canary traffic-slice reconciliation window.
4) Pin-handshake trace shows a partial commit (pin_assign -> pin_ack) followed by a separate session completing the request without the pin metadata, which triggered routing policy to pick fallback variant.

Relevant logs / telemetry snippets (sanitized):
- edge-proxy: 2026-03-13T16:07:12Z INFO keepalive burst from 10.12.34.56: 102 concurrent streams
- orchestrator: 2026-03-13T16:07:13Z WARN session-merge detected tenant=novara-h tenant_id=tn-9032 merge_candidate_ids=[s-12121,s-12122]
- orchestrator: 2026-03-13T16:07:13Z DEBUG pin-handshake tenant=tn-9032 stage=assign trace_id=tr-0a1b pin_variant=redwood-v2-13b-quant-muted status=partial_commit
- api-gateway: 2026-03-13T16:07:13Z ERROR routing-fallback tenant=tn-9032 selected_variant=redwood-v2-13b-fallback reason=pin-missing

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis A: HTTP/2 multiplexing plus edge-level session coalescing caused pin metadata to be lost when two streams were combined. The orchestrator currently assumes per-session pin metadata is monotonic and not re-seen across merged streams; merge produces a race.
- Hypothesis B: Keepalive/reconnect wave caused a timing window where the pin_cohort assignment was written to the control-plane snapshot but not yet visible to the edge shard; combined session then routed by local decision to fallback.
- We identified a correlation between a specific edge-proxy middleware change (h2 stream reuse optimization, PR referenced above) and the timing of the first occurrence; rollback of that middleware in a staging environment reproduced a session-merge warning but did not reproduce a pin loss unless we forced a reconnect storm.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Support applied a short-lived sticky-route override for the affected tenant to force explicit variant selection for 30 minutes (manual policy) at 2026-03-13T16:20Z; customer traffic returned to pinned variant.
- Increased observability: enabled trace-level pin-handshake logging for the tenant and edge shard for the next 24 hours.

Open questions and next steps:
1) Reproduce in a controlled staging load test that uses h2 multiplexing + reconnect bursts to confirm the merge->pin-loss path.
2) Determine whether the orchestrator should tag per-request pin tokens (instead of per-session) for safety when session merging is enabled.
3) If root cause is edge stream reuse optimization, plan a targeted fix or a compatibility flag to disable stream coalescing for tenants with pinned rollouts.
4) Run retrospective across other tenants to surface if this was an isolated incident or a systemic risk.

Desired outcome:
- Root cause identified and fix shipped (edge or orchestrator) to prevent pin metadata loss when session merges occur.
- Automated detection rule added to alert on session-merge + pin_partial_commit patterns and immediately throttle pin-sensitive decisions or enforce conservative routing.

Tentative patch to ensure per-request pin-token is carried in header when merge detected. Planning a canary patch to edge-proxy with disable flag for coalescing.

Issue summary: Customer LexaForms applied a combined optimization profile (q4f16 quantization, increased dynamic batch_size to 256, and aggressive KV prefix caching TTL=30s) to their Dedicated pool last night. After the change they report increased hallucination rate on rw-chat-lg-1 and a spike in tail latency for long-response (>512 tokens) requests. They want step-by-step assistance to safely revert or adjust config without downtime and to introduce guardrails for future tune-ups.

Impact: User-visible quality regressions and tail latency spikes impacting 2 services: chatbot and document summarization. Traffic is routed through their dedicated pool in us-east with occasional failover to eu-west. Estimated affected traffic: ~12% of requests (higher for long-form endpoints).

Environment: dedicated prod pool (lexaforms-dedicated-us-east). Redwood Console traces and latency SLOs attached.

Initial hypothesis: The q4f16 profile likely reduced numeric fidelity on specific attention heads causing token-level degeneration in rw-chat-lg-1; increased batching raised per-request scheduling latency under high concurrency (long tail due to mixed short/long seqs); aggressive prefix cache TTL caused cache churn and frequent KV cache miss amplification under traffic patterns with many distinct prefixes (multi-turn sessions). The combination amplified tail effects and exposed model sensitivity to lower-precision arithmetic.

What customer has tried: They rolled the profile live at 2026-03-12T22:45Z, monitored for 40 minutes, then observed issues and patched batch_size back to 64 in the console at 2026-03-12T23:35Z. They did NOT revert quantization or cache TTL. No infra or node changes were made.

Requested outcome: 1) A short safe revert plan that minimizes downtime, 2) A checklist for canary testing future optimization changes, 3) Concrete config suggestions (quant, batch, caching) tuned for rw-chat-lg-1 and how to codify guardrails in Console.

Attachments/Links: Console traces: https://console.redwood.ai/lexaforms/traces/incident-11827, latency heatmap: https://console.redwood.ai/lexaforms/heatmaps/11827, slack thread: #support-lexaforms (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05XXXXXX), relevant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3421

Suggested safe revert plan (short):
1) Enter maintenance mode for the dedicated pool in Console (non-disruptive routing: set drain=false and reduce new-session percentage to 10% to limit blast radius).
2) Create a canary route: duplicate current route and pin to previous model variant (rw-chat-lg-1@v1.13) without q4f16 quant. Target 5% of production traffic for 15 minutes.
3) If canary passes (no hallucinations, tail latency within baseline), promote previous model variant to 30% for 30 minutes.
4) Revert cache TTL to conservative value (300s) on the canary and measure KV hit-rate and downstream tail latency.
5) If stable, roll back quantization to v1.13 across pool during a low-traffic window with staged increments (30% -> 60% -> 100%).
6) Once reverted, restore batch_size policy to adaptive mode (max_batch=128, max_concurrency=8) and enable per-route batching thresholds based on median sequence length.

Quick verification checks (what to watch during canary):
- End-to-end latency p50/p95/p99 for the route and distribution across sequence lengths.
- Token-level log sampling for hallucination signals (flapping facts, low-confidence tokens).
- KV cache hit rate and cache fill churn rate.
- Serving runtime errors / NaN/overflow events.
- Heap/GPU utilization and scheduling queue lengths.

Backout commands / Console actions (examples):
- Re-pin model variant: `redwood route update --route-id lr-chat-main --model rw-chat-lg-1@v1.13`
- Set cache TTL: `redwood pool update --pool lexaforms-dedicated-us-east --cache-ttl 300`
- Adjust batching policy: `redwood config set --route lr-chat-main batching.max_batch=128 batching.max_concurrency=8`

Longer-term guardrails to implement (recommendations):
1) Always run combined-change canary: never change quantization + batching + cache at the same time. Split into sequential canaries and keep one axis constant.
2) Add automatic model-quality hooks: baseline token-level metrics (per-prompt test suite) that fail deployments if KL divergence or F1 drift exceeds threshold.
3) Add preflight synthetic load tests for mixed short/long seq distributions using the customer's traffic replay (stored in S3).
4) Require a rollback playbook attached to any Optimize profile that changes both precision and batching.
5) Console policy: disallow q4f* quant profiles on rw-chat-lg-1 unless explicitly whitelisted for the customer pool.

Follow-ups requested from Engineering (recommended):
- Run a focused eval of q4f16 on rw-chat-lg-1 using customer prompt set (assigned to Applied ML) and share a small report.
- Add a dashboard tile showing KV cache miss amplification (per-prefix miss rate) and correlate it with tail latency.

Resolution target: Provide step-by-step assist today, complete canary, and schedule follow-up for hardening in 72 hours.

2026-03-13 10:45 - SRE (Liam Chen): Confirmed pool is healthy at infra level; no node restarts. Will coordinate safe canary steps with customer at 12:00 UTC.
2026-03-13 12:05 - Customer (Maria Gomez, LexaForms): Agreed to the canary window 12:30-13:30 UTC; provided a 1k-sample prompt set and consent to route 5% traffic for canary.
2026-03-13 13:00 - Support (Ava Patel): Executed canary route targeting rw-chat-lg-1@v1.13 (no quant) at 5% and set cache TTL to 300s for canary; monitoring p99.
2026-03-13 13:20 - Customer (Maria Gomez): Reports initial signs of improvement in hallucination rate; p99 latency improved from 2.3s to 1.1s for long responses.

In Progress - canary showing positive results. Recommended full revert of q4f16 across pool in staged rollout pending Applied ML eval. Customer to confirm low-traffic window for final rollback.
1) Complete Applied ML evaluation and post short findings. 2) Schedule final rollback window with LexaForms for 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC. 3) Create Optimize profile guardrail in Console and add preflight checks.

Customer request (Helio Health, Private):

They require:
1) Ability to pin Redwood Serving Runtime to an exact version (no floating tags / no implicit upgrades) across both Private installer and Helm-based installs.
2) Verifiable release artifacts for audit/change-control: SHA256 checksums for images/binaries, signed provenance (preferred), and an SBOM or equivalent bill-of-materials artifact.
3) Documentation that maps an artifact to the originating commit/tag + release notes, and a procedure to verify integrity offline.

Business impact:
- Blocker for production approval. Their security/compliance team will not sign off on a deployment where runtime images can drift or where artifact integrity cannot be independently verified.

Current state observed by customer:
- Installer defaults to channel-based latest (or documentation implies latest) without a hard pin.
- Helm values allow specifying image tag, but they want a first-class 'LTS channel' selection/pinning and a documented checksum verification step.
- Release notes exist but do not currently include checksums/provenance references for the exact artifact they pulled.

Asks / questions:
- What is Redwood’s supported mechanism to pin runtime to 1.18.x LTS patch (e.g., 1.18.1-lts) in Private installer and Helm?
- Can Redwood provide checksums/signatures and an SBOM for the runtime artifacts used in Private?
- Where is the official documentation and how will this be maintained for future LTS patches?

Requested deliverable:
- Written guidance + example commands/values, and confirmation that this is supported/maintained as part of Runtime LTS channel.

Notes:
- Customer referenced internal change-control policy requiring: (a) immutable version identifier, (b) checksum verification, (c) traceability to release notes and CVE advisories.
- Customer is OK with LTS cadence (monthly patches + out-of-band security) as long as each patch is optional unless flagged mandatory.

Support triage:
- This aligns with Runtime LTS initiative and Private packaging workstreams. Routing to Release Eng + Private installer/Helm owners.

Attachments:
- Customer security questionnaire excerpt (stored in Zendesk attachment; not copied here)
- Screenshot of their internal approval checklist (stored in Zendesk attachment; not copied here)

Looping in Release Eng (Connor O’Brien) and Private packaging (Bruno Silva) to confirm exact supported flags/values and artifact verification path. Linked to SUP-18421 (LTS availability request) for context.

We can provide per-release checksums and provenance metadata as part of the LTS artifact publish step. We’re landing repo changes under runtime artifact provenance + checksums (PR-23305) and SBOM generation (PR-23402).
2025-02-12 08:07 (Owen Phillips, Support): Clarifying questions back to customer: Are they using Private installer, Helm, or both? Do they need offline verification (air-gapped) or can they fetch checksums from an HTTPS endpoint at install time? Do they require signatures (cosign) or is SHA256 + provenance sufficient?
2025-02-12 13:26 (Customer, Helio Health): They use both (installer for base platform, Helm for runtime upgrades). Primary environment is not fully air-gapped, but verification must be possible without calling out to public registries at runtime. They prefer signatures (cosign/sigstore) but will accept SHA256 + attestation if Redwood documents the process. They need a stable URL pattern to retrieve checksums for a given patch and a retention statement (how long artifacts remain available).
2025-02-13 10:03 (Sahana Iyer, CI/Build): Build pipeline can publish: (1) artifact manifest, (2) SHA256SUMS, (3) provenance JSON referencing git SHA + build workflow run, and (4) optional SBOM artifact. Signing keys access is being set up for release branches (see INT-3302). For now, SHA256 + provenance is immediately available; signature rollout is in progress but not guaranteed for the first patch.
2025-02-14 16:55 (Bruno Silva, Private installer/Helm): Private installer changes are in redwood-private-installer PR-663 to support pinning runtime image to an LTS patch and validating checksums. Helm chart work is in PR-388 to expose an explicit LTS channel/tag value and surface release notes URL annotation. Once merged, we can provide customer with examples:
- Installer: set runtime.image.tag=1.18.1-lts and enable verifyChecksums=true with provided SHA256 file.
- Helm: values.yaml sets runtime.image.tag=1.18.1-lts plus releaseNotesUrl annotation.
2025-02-18 11:20 (Hanae Suzuki, Vuln response coordination): From security/compliance perspective, the recommended customer-facing guidance should include: artifact-to-commit mapping, how CVEs are communicated in LTS notes, and the security patch SLA for LTS. For now, direct them to the reproducible builds + artifact signing doc and LTS release notes format; we’ll follow up with signature details once finalized.
2025-02-20 09:37 (Owen Phillips, Support): Sent customer interim guidance: pin exact runtime tag (1.18.1-lts) and verify SHA256 checksums published alongside the release artifacts. Provided a draft snippet for verification (sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS) and advised to store SHA256SUMS internally for audit. Noted signatures are in-flight, SBOM support pending merge of PR-23402.
2025-02-28 15:04 (Connor O’Brien, Release Eng): Confirmed first LTS patch publish includes checksums/provenance; release notes will include a dedicated 'Artifact verification' block referencing SHA256SUMS and the provenance artifact. Asking Support to ensure customer sees that the pin is per-patch and not automatically updated.
2025-03-04 10:11 (Owen Phillips, Support): Customer confirmed the documented pinning + checksum workflow meets their immediate change-control requirement, pending SBOM availability for final compliance review. Marking ticket resolved; keeping an internal follow-up to notify once SBOM is GA for LTS artifacts.
Provided supported approach to pin Redwood Serving Runtime to an exact LTS patch in Private deployments (installer + Helm) and documented artifact verification steps using published SHA256 checksums and provenance metadata.

What we delivered to customer:

- Verifiable artifacts: per-release SHA256SUMS and provenance mapping artifacts to git SHA/tag; guidance to verify integrity and retain manifests for audit.

- Helm chart LTS values + release notes URL surfacing: redwood-helm-charts PR-388

Issue summary: Multiple customer requests from NovumHealth are terminating with a 504/backend timeout while generating with very large prefixes and high max_tokens. Impact: customer-facing API calls fail intermittently during long-context generations, causing feature degradation for batch summarization and legal-document completion jobs. Behavior first observed after the recent KV cache eviction tuning rollout (2026-03-08).
1) Use customer workspace with pinned model redwood-13b-8k in us-east.
2) Submit a generation request with prompt length ~120k tokens (multipart upload) and max_tokens=20k, streaming=true.
3) Observe initial token stream for ~30s, then connection resets and API returns 504.
4) Repeat with same prefix: sometimes completes if retried after ~60s.
- Multiple backend traces show sudden KV cache eviction around request time, followed by a spike in model cold-starts and kernel re-selection.
- Serving-runtime logs: repeated 'kv:evict shard' entries shortly before request starts.
- Scheduler trace: request queued behind a burst of large-context warmups.
- API gateway: upstream responded with 504 after 90s.
- Client-side: streaming socket closed with ECONNRESET, no final chunk arrived.
- No increase in 5xx rate for small-context requests in same window.
Hypothesis A: Aggressive KV eviction policy combined with large max_tokens causes repeated cache misses and sequential re-warming cost, pushing request beyond gateway timeout.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler temporarily rebalanced GPUs triggering model weight reloads during request (noisy neighbor plus eviction).
What we checked: KV eviction config change (2026-03-08) increased aggressiveness for prefix memory reclamation. Review of recent PRs shows change in eviction LRU threshold.
Preliminary reproduction on staging: reproduces when eviction threshold lowered to 40% and concurrent prefix warmups >= 6.
Telemetry: median latency for affected large requests increased from 35s to 110s in the incident window.
Next steps: instrument per-request KV-hit metrics, add a short-circuit to avoid eviction during in-flight long-context generations, and add a temporary model pin to maintain warmed weights for NovumHealth workload.
Customer workaround: reduce max_tokens to <=8k or split the prompt into smaller chunked requests. Temporary platform mitigations applied: raised eviction threshold for customer namespace in us-east, increased API gateway upstream timeout to 180s for the customer's API key, and temporarily reserved one warm GPU for pinned model. These reduced failures but are not permanent fixes.
(In Progress) Engineering is preparing a targeted fix: avoid triggering KV-eviction for prefixes with active in-flight generations and add batching-aware eviction windows. Plan to roll an opt-in config for dedicated/enterprise customers within 2 weeks. Final resolution will include rollback of the aggressive eviction change and a controlled rollout with additional telemetry.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:22 - SRE Team (Jorge Martinez): Found correlation between eviction events and increased cold-starts. Reproduced locally with lowered eviction threshold. Adding per-request kv_hit metrics to staging.
2026-03-12 08:40 - Support (Aisha Patel): Applied temporary upstream timeout and raised eviction threshold for NovumHealth namespace. Customer reported drop in failures to ~3% but some requests still time out under heavy concurrency.
2026-03-13 16:05 - Eng (Maya Chen): Working on patch to mark prefixes as "protected" while active generation ongoing; will open PR and schedule canary in prod us-east next week. Linking PRs in ticket.
2026-03-13 16:25 - Customer (NovumHealth SRE): Confirmed they can live with split-request workaround for now; would prefer a server-side fix.

Issue Summary
- Customer (Quartz Commerce) reported receiving unexpected sales outreach referencing “Dedicated/Private options” shortly after they viewed pricing/security content.
- Customer is currently self-serve, not in an active evaluation, and explicitly stated they were “just browsing” and felt the outreach was intrusive.

Customer Report (verbatim-ish)
- "We got a sales email right after we read your security FAQ. We weren’t asking for a sales conversation and it feels like you’re tracking us. Please remove us from sales outreach."

Impact
- Reputational risk and churn risk for self-serve cohort.
- Indicates signal pipeline is generating false-positive intent signals that route directly to HubSpot tasks without sufficient confidence/guardrails.

Environment
- Signal router: prod
- CRM: HubSpot (NA pilot workflow)

What likely happened (initial hypothesis)
- An intent-only signal (docs/pricing/security page views) met the current routing threshold and created an AE task.
- No explicit opt-in (demo/contact form) and no meaningful usage threshold (token/spend) to justify sales outreach.

Steps to Reproduce (for investigation)
1) In a self-serve workspace, view /pricing and security FAQ pages (and/or Dedicated docs) within a short window.
2) Confirm if a PLG Signal is created with type=INTENT_* and score >= routing cutoff.
3) Confirm HubSpot workflow creates follow-up task to AE without suppression.

Requested Outcome
- Apologize, clarify what data we use (high-level, privacy-aware), and stop outreach.
- Fix signal routing rules so intent-only browsing does not create sales tasks unless combined with stronger indicators or explicit opt-in.

Notes on data/privacy
- We should ensure comms do not imply tracking individuals. If we reference activity, keep it at company/account level and avoid page-level detail.

Owner/Workstream
- Support/CS: manage customer comms, ensure suppression (DNC) applied.
- Growth/Ops + Eng: adjust suppression rules and scoring thresholds; document change and rollout.

This matches the false-positive pattern we saw in #sales (Quartz example). Recommendation:

Please ensure comms do not say “we track your browsing”. 2025-05-21 15:55 PT — Priya Natarajan (Eng sponsor)
Eng update: we’ll implement a routing change so INTENT_* signals cannot create HubSpot tasks unless:
- signal.confidence >= 0.85 AND signal has “explicit_request=true”, OR

2025-05-23 17:08 PT — Grace O'Connor
Customer replied acknowledging apology, asked: “Can you confirm you won’t contact us again unless we reach out?” I confirmed DNC flag set and we’ll only respond if they request assistance.

2025-05-27 16:22 PT — Grace O'Connor

- Added suppression: “false_positive_disposition” blocks re-notification for 30 days.

Implemented routing/suppression guardrails to prevent intent-only browsing from auto-creating sales tasks unless combined with stronger product-led thresholds or explicit request. Issue summary:
Customers running Redwood Private (EdgeFin Analytics) report a sudden spike of 403s from internal background jobs that use service-account token exchange to perform tenant-scoped admin operations. Jobs started failing after an IdP certificate rotation and an upgrade to the corporate reverse-proxy in front of the customer's ADFS instance.

Impact:
- All scheduled model-management and dataset-ingestion jobs for EdgeFin are failing (no retries succeed).
- Customer is on a regulated cadence; missed jobs cause data staleness and SLA exposure.
- Affects only private deployment behind customer's ADFS+corporate proxy. Hosted customers unaffected.

Observed behavior:
- Token exchange succeeds (200) but the exchanged token presented to Redwood lacks the impersonation scope required (redwood:impersonate / act_as).
- Redwood authorizer rejects admin API calls with 403 "missing required scope: redwood:impersonate".
- SCIM / role bindings are correct; service account still has roles in our DB.

Environment details:
- Private deployment (EdgeFin) on-prem, prod-us-east.
- IdP: ADFS 4.0 behind a corporate reverse proxy (TLS termination + SNI rewrite).
- Recent changes: customer rotated IdP signing cert 2026-03-10 and upgraded proxy (adds request body normalization / form rewriting) 2026-03-11.

1) Configure a service account in customer's ADFS (SAML->OAuth exchange flow) with scope redwood:impersonate.
2) Use Redwood's token-exchange endpoint to exchange SAML assertion for a service token.
3) Present exchanged token to admin API (e.g., /admin/models/:id/rollout).
4) Observe 403 and validate token via /introspect shows missing scope claim.

Note: Repro is reliably seen only when requests are routed through the customer's proxy configured with request body/form normalization.
[2026-03-12T08:41:22Z] token-exchange: incoming_assertion=sha256:... status=200 asserted_scopes=[openid profile email]

payload.description:
Customers on Acera Health private deployment reported periodic control-plane API requests experiencing 5-10s latency spikes and occasional 504s. Investigation pointed to stale DNS answers being served by an on-prem DNS forwarder with aggressive negative/positive TTL skew, causing the Redwood control plane to continue routing requests to an unreachable (cached) NAT egress path for ~12 minutes.
Issue summary:
- Control-plane control APIs for Acera Health (private deployment) intermittently returned high latency and occasional 504s between 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC and 2026-03-11 04:30 UTC.
- Customers reported model request retries and degraded streaming stability.

Impact:
- Affected tenant: Acera Health (private). Approximately 12% of control-plane requests during windows experienced >5s latency; 1.3% returned 504.
- Application-facing token issuance and route resolution were delayed, causing downstream model-serving requests to hit fallback/ejected backends.

Environment:
- Private deployment in us-east connected via customer-managed VPN + on-prem DNS forwarder
- Redwood control-plane endpoints: control.acera.redwood-inference.internal (resolved via customer forwarder)
- Customer reported they run a DNS forwarder that conditionally forwards to their internal resolvers and upstream public resolvers with custom TTL handling.
Trigger control-plane list-models call repeatedly from within customer VPC while toggling their internal resolver to return NXDOMAIN for a temporary internal hostname (simulated)
Observe control-plane health-checks and route-resolve latency in the Redwood Console for the tenant
Capture DNS answers from customer's forwarder and from public resolver to compare TTLs and negative TTL behaviour
flow-logs: s3://redwood-support/acera/flowlogs/2026-03-10_flow.log -> shows identical queries answered by forwarder at t=22:12 and t=22:18 with cached IP and TTL zero returned
tcpdump: /support-drops/acera/tcpdump_controlplane.cap -> shows repeated SYNs to old egress IPs with successful 3-way but no application response
dig-output.txt: control.acera.redwood-inference.internal @10.0.0.2 -> shows TTL 7200 at 22:10, TTL 0 (SOA negative caching) at 22:14
redwood-console-trace: trace_id=rdw-ctl-115879-0001 -> shows DNS_resolve step 9.2s at 2026-03-10T22:14:03Z
Initial hypothesis: transient NAT gateway outages. Flow logs showed egress IPs reachable, so not NAT outage.
Observed DNS answers from the customer forwarder had inconsistent TTLs: positive answers returned long TTLs (2h) but when the internal resolver returned NXDOMAIN for certain control-plane helper hostnames the forwarder persisted a negative cache entry with a 12 minute retention and then continued to return the negative entry to us even after the internal resolver recovered.
Control-plane repeatedly attempted to resolve service-relevant hostnames which returned (via the forwarder) a stale CNAME chain during rolling network experiments. The control-plane's resolver cached the forwarded negative responses which delayed fallback to alternate routing policy.
Correlation between DNS negative cache windows and latency spikes is strong (Pearson r=0.82 over event windows).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 23:05 - Acera network team (Maria Gomez): Provided dnsmasq/infoblox configs. Confirmed they have an explicit 'min-ttl' policy and custom NXDOMAIN caching script.
Root cause: Customer on-prem DNS forwarder applied a negative-caching policy that created a multi-minute negative cache for internal control-plane helper hostnames after a transient internal resolver outage. The forwarder continued returning those negative answers to the Redwood control plane, which then cached the negative responses for the control-plane process and did not immediately failover to alternate routing. Result: control-plane route resolution delays and fallback triggering causing high latency and some 504s.
Applied temporary customer-side workaround at 2026-03-11 02:40: disable NXDOMAIN negative caching and reduce min-ttl to 30s for control.*.redwood-inference.internal zone
Redwood support pushed a short-lived control-plane resolver override for the tenant to ignore negative answers for 120s while the forwarding policy was corrected (rolled back 2026-03-12 08:00)
Customer disabled negative-caching and reduced min-ttl for the control-plane domain. Redwood applied a tenant-scoped resolver safety patch to ignore NXDOMAINs for critical control-plane helper names for a 2-minute window while the customer remediation completed. Post-fix monitoring shows latency restored to baseline: <1% requests >2s and 0.1% 504s in the 24h after remediation.
Docs: Add guidance to Private Deploy runbooks about on-prem forwarder negative caching behavior and recommended TTLs for control-plane zones
Product: Implement resolver-configurable per-tenant negative-cache-ignore list (EPIC created INT-402)
SRE: Add an alert for sustained DNS NXDOMAIN rate >20% for a tenant over 5m (create alert rule)
2026-03-11 00:12 - SRE (Lena Ortiz): Added temporary grafana panel to show per-tenant NXDOMAIN ratio and TTL anomalies.
This ticket highlights an operational mismatch between customer DNS policies and Redwood control-plane resolver assumptions. Recommend adding explicit preflight checks for TTL/negative-cache behavior during Private deployment onboarding.
payload.summary: Control-plane request latency and intermittent timeouts due to on-prem DNS forwarder TTL drift and negative-cache retention

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that rerank responses intermittently omit expected top candidates after a bulk embed backfill. Symptoms include missing candidate IDs, a persistent -1 offset between embed IDs and metadata IDs, and an increase in rerank latency when the service falls back to a CPU-based verification path.

Impact:
- AtlasSearch results show 15-40% missing top-k items for certain queries after nightly backfill.
- Production traffic (dedicated cluster) experiences elevated tail latency on rerank routes when mismatch detection triggers extra verification work.
- Business impact: user-facing search degradation and customer escalations.

Environment:
- Dedicated account in prod us-west-2 running embed-ingest v0.9.3 and serving-runtime v2.4.1.
- Reranker configured to accept batched embedding uploads and run nearest-neighbor on 1M doc index.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Run nightly backfill job uploading embeddings in 10k batches with the embed-upload endpoint (multipart/protobuf).
2) Observe backfill logs that report 200 for ingest but rerank queries afterwards return fewer candidates than expected.
3) Run diagnostic call to /v1/rerank with known query id; compare returned candidate ids to expected metadata list.
4) Re-run same batch but with smaller batch_size=512; issue does not reproduce consistently.

Expected behavior:
- Rerank should return top-k consistent with stored embeddings and metadata.
- No id offsets or missing candidates after successful ingest responses.

Actual behavior:
- Rerank returns N-3 (or variable) candidates; missing ids cluster around segment boundaries (every ~4096 embeddings).
- Temporary increase in rerank latency (~200-800ms) while the verification fallback runs.

Relevant logs / error snippets provided by customer:
- embed-ingest logs show repeated "decoded payload length mismatch" warnings immediately after the nightly backfill windows.
- Reranker audit log: "candidate_id_lookup failed for id=1024003 -> offset -1" (multiple occurrences).
- No 5xx errors returned to the customer; API returned 200 but with missing results array entries.

Additional notes:
- Customer attached sanitized sample batch and an MD5 of pre/post-ingest metadata mapping.
- This appears specific to large batched uploads and to the combination of embed-ingest v0.9.3 + packer config used by AtlasSearch.
- Customer is on a Dedicated cluster and has an active support SLA.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - AtlasSearch (Customer): Provided sample payloads and confirmed issue reduces when batch_size <= 512. Noted that they use an internal packer that emits a zero-byte delimiter between segments.
Summary of findings:
1) Reproducer created using customer packer + embed-ingest v0.9.3. Failure occurs when compressor strip/trims trailing zero byte at segment boundary during chunked upload.
2) Protobuf decoder expects fixed delimiter bytes between segments; trimming leads to byte-shift in subsequent message parsing which manifests as an ID offset (-1) at the boundary.
3) Reranker has a defensive verification path that detects id-metadata mismatches and triggers a CPU-based rescan/verification; this explains the latency spike but not the silent omission.
4) Root cause: a change in embed-ingest v0.9.3 that added an aggressive payload size optimization which erroneously removed zero-byte delimiters from multi-segment uploads packed by certain packers.
5) Related PR discovered: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embed-ingest/pull/972 (optimizations to payload trimming).
6) Reproduction notes: flakiness correlated with upstream packer behavior and batch alignment at 4096-boundary. Smaller batches avoid alignment and therefore avoid the trim case.
7) Additional cross-check: no evidence of index corruption; the issue is at ingest-time decoding and mapping between embedding buffer indices and metadata ids.
Next steps performed:
- Built hotfix branch (embed-ingest@hotfix/restore-delimiter-guard) that reinstates strict delimiter checks and rejects suspect payloads with 422 and clear diagnostic.
- Coordinated rollback plan to revert embed-ingest to v0.9.2 on AtlasSearch dedicated cluster during a 10-minute maintenance window.
- Prepared a reingest/backfill plan to replay any rejected batches and to run an id-consistency check script before re-enabling traffic.
- Added unit tests for multi-segment packing and a fuzz-test harness for common packers used by customers.
In-progress remediation and temporary mitigation applied:
- On 2026-03-13 at 03:00 UTC we rolled embed-ingest back to v0.9.2 on the AtlasSearch dedicated cluster. Preliminary checks show rerank candidate counts returned to expected levels for sample queries.
- Hotfix branch added additional validation to detect missing delimiters and fail-fast with 422, preventing silent id offsets. Hotfix PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embed-ingest/pull/984.
- Backfill replay plan: AtlasSearch to re-run nightly backfill for affected windows after we mark those batches as rejected and provide the sanitized artifacts. Support to validate with id-consistency script pre-cutover.
- Follow-ups: mandatory unit tests for delimiter-preserving compressors in CI, runbook update to flag embed-ingest version changes to customers with large-batch workflows, and a postmortem scheduled (owner: Elena Park) to document root cause and prevention steps.
Customer communication: customer notified of rollback and reingest plan; will validate and confirm by 2026-03-15. Ticket remains open until reingest completes and customer confirms full resolution.
Postmortem and RCA (owner: Elena Park)
CI unit tests for multi-segment packing
Add telemetry for delimiter-trim warnings
Run reingest and confirm id-consistency by 2026-03-15
payload.summary: Embedding segment-boundary trim causing ID offsets and partial rerank suppression
