payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that after a short network interruption and SSE resume, the final metadata event ("id":"session_end", "status":"complete") is missing from the resumed stream. Impact: downstream client never receives final metadata which triggers end-of-response processing; customers observe truncated final sentence and no end-of-stream payload. Environment: prod us-east, Dedicated instance for LuminaDocs, model pinned to redwood-2-medium.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a long streaming completion via SSE against the hosted endpoint using the customer's proxy stack (CloudEdge + header-rewrite layer).
2) Simulate a short TCP-level disconnect (~1-3s) between client and edge by TCP RST or by toggling client network.
3) Allow the client to reconnect using the same session token and resume as normal.
4) Observe resumed stream payloads and check for the terminal metadata event ("event: metadata\ndata: {..session_end..}\n\n").

Observed behavior: In a reproducible subset (~12% of attempts), the resumed stream contains the final text but the separate metadata SSE event is missing. The last chunk of text is present but the terminal metadata event that client relies on to finalize the response is suppressed.

Expected behavior: Final metadata event should appear after resumed content in every successful resume sequence.

Relevant logs/attachments: Uploaded client capture (sse-chunk-trace-0311.log), edge proxy logs showing a rewrite step (edge-rewrite-0311.log), request_id: req-9b3f2c2a. Attached sample client trace shows CRLF sequences inserted by intermediary that appear to coalesce the terminal metadata event into the previous data frame and the event separator (blank line) is dropped.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 LuminaDocs (customer): Canary disables helped; we still see 1/50 failures. Customer requests durable fix and rollback prevention steps. Asked for timeline and patch plan.
Investigative summary: Reproducer built using customer proxy stack and SSE client. When an intermediary changes line endings from LF to CRLF across the event separator (i.e., transforms "\n\n" into "\r\n" + "\r\n" but collapses one of the separators), the SSE parser on the client sees the metadata event merged into prior data or loses the final empty line used to delimit events. The server runtime emits correct events in origin logs; loss occurs in the rewrite layer. See edge proxy logs: request_id req-9b3f2c2a shows transformation at byte offset 14321.
Hypothesis 1: Text-normalize filter in edge-proxy rewrites streaming payload boundaries, inadvertently removing the blank-line separator between SSE events when the reconnection resume produces a boundary that matches heuristic. This causes the client's SSE parser to consider metadata as continuation of previous event or skip it.
Hypothesis 2: In resumption path, small resume fragments result in event-buffer reassembly where the edge's chunking + LF->CRLF normalization recombines frames differently than expected, exposing a race between rewriter and connection drain.
Data: Canary change that disabled normalization reduced failure rate from ~12% to ~1-2% in LuminaDocs traffic for 48h. Origin logs (serving-runtime) show consistent event emission with session_end metadata present for every returned response. No change observed in model output; problem isolated to proxy rewrite behavior.
Logs & dashboards: edge-proxy/error-rate, streaming/late-metadata occurrences, request traces: https://grafana.internal/streams?var-request=req-9b3f2c2a
Repro notes: Created a synthetic client that toggles network for 1-3s and reissues resume. Reproducer attached as repro_crlf_resume.sh. Edge config disabled text-normalize filter in canary cluster 'edge-canary-3'.
Workaround: Disable text-normalize/line-ending rewrite filter on edge for affected customers or route dedicated instances to a non-rewriting path. LuminaDocs was routed to non-rewriting canary which reduced failures dramatically.
Permanent fix: Engineering (edge team) to update proxy rewrite logic to preserve SSE event separators. Patch will: (1) treat streaming responses as binary-safe and skip LF/CRLF normalization for Content-Type: text/event-stream and chunked Transfer-Encoding; (2) add a unit test to ensure blank-line separators survive boundary rewriting; (3) add an integration test that simulates resume boundary cases.
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/427 (edge: skip line-ending normalization for SSE streams) — currently in review by infra.
Rollout plan: Merge -> canary edge-canary-3 -> monitor for 72h -> gradual rollout to prod. Post-rollout monitoring: capture streaming/end-metadata-loss metric and reduce to 0 occurrences for 7d before closing ticket.
Follow-ups: Update runbook for streaming resume issues to include 'disable LF->CRLF normalization' as first mitigation. Consider adding a server-side 'resume-session' idempotent marker event that is tolerant to line-ending transforms.
Status: Fix in review; customer routed to canary and monitoring shows residual failure rate ~0.5% in 24h. Will keep ticket open until 7d stable post-prod rollout.
payload.summary: Trailing CRLF conversion by intermediary suppresses final metadata event after SSE resume

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightLens reports a finalized invoice that includes a prorated charge for a deprecated model variant (rlm-1.3-quant-depr) after they rolled back a canary deployment earlier in the billing cycle. Impact: Unexpected charge on finalized invoice amounting to $1,120. Customer reports the charge corresponds to a small percentage of inference traffic that was routed to the deprecated variant during the rollback window. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-west, reserved commit in place. Expected: When a model variant is marked deprecated and traffic is rolled back to previous pinned variant, there should be no prorated charges for deprecated variants once traffic is drained or rollback completes. Actual: Finalized invoice shows a prorated line for rlm-1.3-quant-depr with non-zero quantity and a reserved-rate applied instead of hosted-fallback rate. This appears linked to a short canary rollback where routing briefly split across variants.
1) Deploy canary variant rlm-1.3-quant-depr to 10% on dedicated pool us-west during billing window.
2) Detect quality regression and trigger rollback to rlm-1.3-quant-stable at T+45 minutes.
3) Observe routing logs showing a small fraction of requests still hitting the deprecated variant during the rollback window (approx 0.8% over 30 minutes).
4) Allow billing cycle to finalize.
5) Observe invoice line for rlm-1.3-quant-depr showing prorated reserved-hours and positive charge.
Invoice excerpt:
- Line 345: rlm-1.3-quant-depr | Reserved variant prorated hours | qty: 3.2 | rate_id: reserved-hybrid-usw | amount: $1,120.00
Routing trace snippet (2026-03-02T14:42:10Z - 2026-03-02T15:12:05Z):
- request-ids: [redacted] routed to rlm-1.3-quant-depr at 0.6-1.2% of total.
Postback delivery log: postback-id 8f7a: success -> reconciler accepted -> billed under reserved-hybrid-usw
Note: Postbacks for the same window include entries tagged with deprecated_variant=true and tag migration_policy=canary-rollback.
Support verified invoice line and correlated timestamps with customer's rollback window.
Billing team confirms postback reconciler accepted variant tag 'rlm-1.3-quant-depr' and applied reserved rate because reconciler matched variant to customer's dedicated commit id.
Serving/runtime team found brief KV-cache TTL mismatch: router continued to route a small percentage to deprecated pod replicas for ~27 minutes after rollback due to stale prefix cache on 2 edge nodes.
Rollback was executed correctly at control plane level, but edge drain handshake failed for a subset of connections causing late routed traffic that still generated postbacks.
Preliminary root cause hypothesis: race between route update + prefix cache invalidation and postback attribution logic which maps variant->rate at ingestion time. Late postbacks were not re-attributed when variant was marked deprecated.
Customer provided request IDs and export of their traffic which matched postback records; we validated 98% of those postbacks correlate to the timeframe in question.
No evidence of duplicate postbacks or retries that would inflate quantity; charge matches legitimately routed requests.
Billing policy note: When a variant receives traffic during a customer's reserved commit window and reconciler maps to that commit id, reserved rates apply even if variant is deprecated later in cycle. This policy needs clarification for canary rollbacks.
Related config: reconciler uses first-seen variant tag to pick rate unless a reclassification job marks it differently. Reclassification job runs daily and did not reclassify these postbacks because the finalization occurred before cron job ran.
Potential mitigations: (a) fast reclassification on rollback events, (b) ensure prefix cache invalidation propagates synchronously for rollback operations, (c) treat deprecated variants with special billing attribution rules during rollbacks.
Estimate impact: single customer $1.12k charge; could affect other customers who performed similar rapid rollback within billing window but magnitude expected low.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - BrightLens (customer): Thank you for quick triage. Please advise timeline for credit or next steps. They need resolution before 2026-03-18 for their internal accounting.
payload.summary: Deprecated model variant prorated charge appearing on finalized invoice after canary rollback

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several OpenEdu Labs users report that long-running SSE streams occasionally deliver partial JSON objects at the tail of responses (duplicated fields in mid-object and missing trailing '}' ). The client sees a seemingly valid prefix, then a brief stream pause, then resumed fragments that interleave from a previous short-lived session. Impact: downstream consumer fails JSON parse and abandons the response 15-30% of affected streams during heavy outbound TLS rekeying windows. Environment: prod-us-east, customer using enterprise dedicated connection via corp-proxy that performs TLS interception and occasional renegotiation. Observed on model gptj-6b using streaming SSE path with keepalive interval 25s.

Observed behavior pattern:
- Stream starts and emits well-formed JSON chunks for ~30-90s.
- A short TLS rehandshake / renegotiation occurs at edge proxy (customer side).
- Post-renegotiation the SSE stream continues but occasional chunks are interleaved from an older ephemeral session: repeated keys (e.g., "delta": "..."), partial tokens, and final closing brace '}' is missing.

Why we care: This causes application-layer parse failure and a bad user experience in production classrooms (live transcript sessions drop).
1) Establish SSE streaming conversation against api.redwood.example with keepalive=25s using gptj-6b in us-east-1.
2) Simulate TLS interception/renegotiation on the client-side proxy (we used corporate BlueProxy v3 with midstream rekey).
3) Let stream run for ~45-120s and trigger renegotiation. Observe stream delivery: look for duplicated keys, interleaved partial fragments, or missing trailing '}' in final chunk.
4) Reproduce reliably on high-concurrency (>100 concurrent SSE) to increase probability.
[2026-02-28T14:22:11.123Z] edge-proxy: TLS renegotiate from 192.0.2.45:4443 -> client connection id c-7f3a
[2026-02-28T14:22:11.210Z] api-gateway: SSE stream continue session_id s-98ad kv_snapshot=345 (keepalive ok)
[2026-02-28T14:22:11.218Z] serving-runtime: emit chunk -> '{"choices": [{"delta": "The capital of France is"',
[2026-02-28T14:22:11.340Z] serving-runtime: emit chunk -> ' "Paris"}, {"delta": "Next topic:"'
[2026-02-28T14:22:11.355Z] client: JSON parse error: unexpected token '{' at offset 128 (missing closing brace)
Short-term workaround provided to customer: reduce client-side keepalive to 10s and enable explicit session pinning (pin model version + set max-sse-lifetime to 60s) to force tear-down and re-establish a clean session across proxy renegotiation windows. Also recommended to whitelist Redwood endpoints on corporate TLS interceptors to avoid midstream rekey where possible.
2026-02-28 15:10 - Support (Ava): Confirmed multiple incidents from OpenEdu Labs affecting long transcripts. Customer provided PCAPs showing midstream TLS rekey calls from their BlueProxy appliance.
2026-02-28 16:00 - SRE (Ravi): Checked API logs; server emits monotonically increasing sequence numbers for SSE events and keeps KV cache snapshots. No server-side crash observed at renegotiate time.
2026-02-28 16:18 - Eng (Maya): Hypothesis: When TLS renegotiation happens at the proxy we observe a short TCP session teardown on the ingress path; the gateway rebind attaches a new HTTP/1.1 session to the old logical SSE session which can cause out-of-order chunk reassembly in the presence of buffered writes at edge-proxy.\nEvidence: we saw two different connection ids within 200ms for the same client_id and overlapping sequence numbers.
2026-02-28 17:02 - Eng: Reproduced locally by enabling TLS rekey in a test proxy and observed interleaved write buffers: proxy replayed a small buffered packet from the pre-renegotiation connection after the post-renegotiation stream resumed.
Approximately 1200 streams from OpenEdu Labs in the last 24h, ~18% experienced parse failures; user-visible in live classroom transcripts. Customer escalated to enterprise success. Potentially broader impact for customers using TLS interception middleboxes.

Issue summary:
Customers (BrightCart) experienced an abrupt spike in 5xx responses on several streaming and short-request endpoints beginning ~2026-03-10 08:12 UTC after a weighted-route rewrite was deployed to shift traffic between model variants. The API gateway returned 502/503s and a subset of upstream runtime pods crashed with SIGABRT / runtime OOM messages.

Impact:
- Elevated 5xx for ~18 minutes across multiple customers in us-east-1, notably BrightCart (dedicated capacity).
- Streaming sessions dropped with 'stream reset' errors, and short synchronous text-generation calls received 502s.
- Customer impact: degraded UX on live checkout assistant; BrightCart reported failed requests and increased latency spikes.

Environment:
- Production (prod-us-east) 
- Affected services: api-gateway (http2 frontend), serving-runtime (model-serving pods on dedicated GPU pool), ingress-prioritizer (weighted route controller).
- Recent change: rollout of "weighted-route rewrite" to shift 20% of traffic to quantized variant (2026-03-10 08:05 UTC).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Use short-payload synchronous requests with priority header set to 'interactive' while the weighted-route controller is in the middle of an update.
2) Open multiple long-lived streaming connections (chat sessions) simultaneously and maintain keepalive.
3) Observe api-gateway metrics: accept-queue depth grows, http2 active streams approaches configured max, and new connections begin to get 502/503.

Observed logs / snippets:
- apigw: "WARN http2: active_streams=240 max_concurrent_streams=250 accept_queue=512"
- apigw: "ERROR route: rewrite applied, recalculating weights -> delayed socket handoffs"
- runtime pod: "fatal error: runtime: out of memory" (several pods)
- runtime: "panic: net/http: connection closed by peer while writing response"
- kernel: "oom-killer invoked for process /srv/runtime/bin/worker"

Temporary workaround applied:
- Rolled back weighted-route rewrite at 08:18 UTC (immediate mitigation).
- Increased apigw http2 max_concurrent_streams soft-limit from 250 -> 400 for the us-east apigw pool to provide breathing room.
- Enabled short-term keepalive pruning on the apigw to reclaim half-open sockets.

Notes on customer communication:
- BrightCart notified at 08:25 UTC that we had detected the issue, actions were taken, and rollback was in progress. They confirmed partial recovery at 08:34 UTC.
- Customer asked for postmortem and whether variant rollouts can be throttled differently for dedicated customers.

Support: 2026-03-10 08:22 UTC - triaged by Asha: rolling back weighted-route rewrite and notifying SRE; elevated error rate confirmed via dashboards (5xx rate from 0.8% -> 12%).
SRE (Ethan): 2026-03-10 08:27 UTC - Observed accept-queue and http2 stream saturation. Found a correlation between the timing of the route rewrite and a spike in half-open streams (SYN_SENT/SYN_RECV). Attaching pcap and metrics pointers in GH ticket.
Customer (BrightCart): 2026-03-10 08:36 UTC - Confirmed that errors reduced after rollback but saw residual latency for ~10 minutes. Requested a timeline for permanent fix. Provided sample request IDs: rq_3b9f2a, rq_3b9f8c.
SRE (Ethan): 2026-03-11 10:12 UTC - Investigation shows an http2 stream-slot accounting bug in apigw when routes are reweighted rapidly; the code path that transfers accept-queue ownership to new worker occasionally leaves slots marked as 'in-use' without active stream objects. This slowly exhausts the available concurrent_streams count and triggers backpressure to upstream runtimes, causing prefetch thrash and eventual OOMs.
Support: 2026-03-12 09:05 UTC - Notified BrightCart of intended mitigation: throttle route-rewrite rollouts to 5% per minute for dedicated customers and schedule permanent patch during low-traffic window.
Metric correlation: 08:05-08:12 UTC window shows http2_active_streams jump +360% and accept_queue growth from 32 -> 512 across 3 apigw instances.
dmesg on runtime pods shows repeated allocations then OOM; memory growth correlated with multiple failed prefetch retries (kvcache fingerprints increasing).
tcpdump indicates many FIN/ACK pairs followed by RSTs around the same time as the rewrite; suggests sockets were torn down mid-handshake during weight recalculation.
Heap profiles on runtime pods (captured pre-oom) show increased goroutine counts stuck in Write loop waiting on net.Conn that returned EOFs. Hypothesis: apigw marked streams as 'occupied' but closed underlying conn -> runtime kept buffers and retried prefetch/kv operations until memory exhausted.
Config review: weighted-route controller allowed immediate weight commit; no staging gradual step for dedicated tenants.
Status: Partial mitigation deployed (rollback of rewrite + increased http2 soft limits + keepalive pruning) restored service for BrightCart. Root cause: http2 stream-slot leak in apigw triggered by rapid weighted-route changes; leak propagated backpressure to serving runtimes causing memory growth and crashes.

Immediate next steps:
- Ship hotfix PR to apigw that fixes stream-slot accounting (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5421 in review).
- Implement rollout throttling for weighted-route changes: default 5% per minute for dedicated/private tenants; allow opt-in fast rollouts with explicit approval.
- Add a safety circuit: if apigw accept_queue or active_streams > 75% for 30s, pause route reweight operations and surface alert to SRE.
- Postmortem: schedule Confluence postmortem doc and runbook update; assign follow-up INT ticket to track permanent guardrails.

Follow-up items: 
- INT-2201 (apigw http2 slot accounting deeper audit)
- INFRA-PR-5421 (hotfix -> canary -> prod rollouts)
- Confluence runbook update link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/accept-queue-drainplaybook

Issue summary: Multiple customers (notably ByteFlow Analytics) report that SSE/WebSocket-based streaming chat responses either disconnect abruptly or stall indefinitely during mid-generation when the user is on spotty mobile networks. Impact: Partial responses are being delivered, the finalization event ("response.complete") is missing in many cases leading to client-side timeouts and retries. Several customers report increased error rates starting after the 2026-03-12 midnight UTC deploy to streaming-proxy. Environment: Production (us-west primary), affected across us-west and eu-central customers, primarily on circuits with high jitter and intermittent packet loss.
1) Use the hosted chat API with streaming enabled (SSE or WebSocket) and model=redwood-chat-1.
2) Simulate an intermittent mobile network (high jitter, small packet loss) using network throttling (e.g., tc/netem or a mobile device with flaky signal).
3) Send a multi-paragraph prompt that triggers multi-chunk streaming (> 3 chunks).
4) Observe connection behavior and whether 'response.complete' or final event is received by client within expected timeframe.
Clients report connections either dropping with upstream errors (502/504) or streams freezing with no new events for >30s while server-side logs show partial chunk writes. In some cases the client eventually reconnects and receives duplicated tokens from server-side retries.
Streaming connections should deliver all chunks followed by a final completion event. On transient network blips the server should keep the stream alive long enough for client reconnection or gracefully terminate with a clear error so client can retry deterministically.
2026-03-13T13:42:11Z streaming-proxy[proxy-3] WARN upstream write timeout to serving-runtime/instance-12: 'upstream write failed: broken pipe'
2026-03-13T13:42:12Z api-gateway[gw-7] ERROR client 18.205.12.34 disconnected during SSE stream (session=abc123) status=UPSTREAM_ERROR
2026-03-13T13:45:05Z serving-runtime[svc-1] INFO partial response emitted for request req-9f3b, kv-cache-hit=false, batch-size=1
Initial correlation with 2026-03-12 deploy of streaming-proxy (PR #88) which adjusted keepalive and write timeout heuristics.
Reproduced locally by introducing 200-400ms jitter + 1-2% packet loss; observed same stall pattern where last chunk and completion event not flushed.
Hypothesis 1: aggressive upstream write timeouts in streaming-proxy close connection before kernel buffers are flushed under high jitter.
Hypothesis 2: batching/continuous-inference change in runtime (runtime PR #459) increased chunking frequency; combined with proxy change this results in more small writes causing buffer coalescing issues.
SRE ran an A/B with streaming-proxy rollback -> client reports decreased disconnects on test cohort.
No evidence of model runtime OOMs; GPU metrics stable.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 16:40 - Support (Asha Patel): Customer ByteFlow confirmed decreased failures after mitigation applied to test cohort (rollback proxy config). Customer requested follow-up and permanent fix timeline.
1) Temporary: Rolled back streaming-proxy keepalive/write-timeout changes for affected nodes (rolled to previous stable tag) which reduced disconnects for test customers.
2) Client-side: Recommend clients implement idempotent request IDs and resume logic that can handle replays (server currently does best-effort dedup for short windows).
3) For dedicated customers: advised to pin to a non-chunking config as short-term measure, if acceptable.
Mitigation applied: reverted streaming-proxy timeout changes and applied a conservative keepalive for mobile-region edge pools. Runtime team opened follow-up PR to batch-flush less aggressively (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/472). Monitoring alerts added for 'streaming_partial_finalize' and a synthetic mobile-net connectivity test. Next steps: coordinate a staged rollout of runtime PR, add end-to-end tests for intermittent networks, and schedule postmortem after full remediation.
1) Runtime team to land PR #472 and run canary for 48h.
2) SRE to instrument streaming success-rate by client-network-type and promote synthetic test to CI.
3) CS to notify impacted customers with ETA and postmortem link.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightQuant reported recurring midday throughput degradation in their eu-west dedicated pool over last 36 hours. Symptoms: p50 stable, p95/p99 inflating by 2-4x for short text-generation routes and a corresponding drop in sustained batch throughput. Impact: customer reports missed SLAs for latency-sensitive endpoints and falling behind ingestion windows.

Impact:
- Multiple customer routes (low-latency chat) see p95 from ~200ms to ~1s during 11:30-13:45 UTC windows.
- Batch pipelines (scheduled hourly) experience enqueue growth and 30-40% throughput drop while autoscaler remains stable (no scale events).
- Customer-facing errors: rare 5xx spikes (~0.3% of requests) tied to timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id d-pool-eu-09 assigned to BrightQuant (reserved capacity).
- Models serving: redwood/decoder-7B-v2 pinned.
- Traffic mix: many long-lived, low-CPU streams (analytics listeners) + short high-QPS chatlets.
- Observed on infra: prod eu-west; telemetry retained in Redwood Console (dash links below).

Steps to reproduce / Observed triggers:
1) In customer traffic during mid-day, dozens of long-lived connections with intermittent token generation overlap with a scheduled hourly batch of 128-sequence inference jobs.
2) Prefetch subsystem initiates KV warmup for long contexts; prefetch tasks consume HBM bandwidth and PCIe IO windows.
3) When batch sweep starts, scheduler attempts gang-attach for batch jobs; GPU handshake latencies spike (nvlink/PCIe handshakes delayed) causing serialized attach and temporary slot blocking.
4) Autoscaler metrics (slot utilization) remain within thresholds, so no immediate scale action; result is temporary queueing and degraded per-request latencies.

Logs / dashboards referenced:
- Console dashboard: /org/brightquant/dedicated/pool/d-pool-eu-09/perf (p95/p99 charts)
- Trace: trace-id 4f3a2b6c (example of serialized attach and prefetch overlap)
- Slack: #support (thread tD3kz9)

Initial hypotheses:
- Prefetch jobs (long-lived stream KV growth) are interfering with batch attach handshake windows (HBM + PCIe contention).
- Scheduler gang-preemption policy delayed eviction of long-lived streams, producing a blocking window where batch workloads are forced to serialize.
- Autoscaler sensor does not capture transient HBM/handshake latency, so it fails to scale preemptively.
Timeline & findings:
- 2026-03-12 12:05 UTC: BrightQuant reported first spike; Support created initial ticket and collected traces.
- 2026-03-12 12:15 UTC: SRE replicated with internal load generator combining 200 long-lived streams + scheduled batch; reproduced p99 spike and observed repeated GPU attach handshakes in node logs.
- 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC: Kernel-level NVLINK counters show short bursts of PCIe tx retries during batch attach (~30-80ms windows).
- 2026-03-13 09:20 UTC: Prefetch worker metrics show sustained KV cache churn and HBM bandwidth at 78-92% during window.
- 2026-03-14 06:40 UTC: Investigated autoscaler telemetry; slot-util metrics do not reflect handshake tail latency - autoscaler thresholds insufficient for this mixed-workload pattern.

Collected artifacts:
- node logs: /var/log/redwood/node-attach-2026-03-12-12.log (excerpt attached in ticket)
- sample traces: trace 4f3a2b6c, 66b1d1f2
- perf counters snapshot: /s3/redwood-debug/prefetch-hbm-snap-2026-03-13.json

Intermediate conclusion:
- Root cause likely multi-factor: prefetch-driven HBM pressure + serialized GPU attach (gang-scheduler behavior) causing temporary slot blocking; autoscaler blind spot for handshake latency allows the condition to persist for 60-180s windows.
Mitigation steps applied (temporary):
1) Disabled aggressive prefetch for BrightQuant pool during peak window via runtime flag (prefetch.max_concurrent -> 4). This reduced HBM pressure and eliminated attach serialization in test.
2) Updated gang-scheduler soft-eviction threshold to prefer preempting the oldest long-lived streams when a batch attach is pending for >500ms (hotfix rollout to eu-west pool).
3) Added autoscaler sensor patch to monitor GPU attach latency metric (attach_handshake_ms) and treat sustained >200ms as a scale trigger. Patch deployed as canary to two dedicated pools.

Planned follow-ups:
- Engineering to land comprehensive fix: improved prefetch backpressure + smarter gang-attach backoff (PR linked). Target sprint: 2026-03-21.
- Postmortem runbook update: document prefetch throttles for dedicated pools and standard mitigation steps.
- Customer follow-up: confirm SLA recovery and offer temporary additional capacity credit for impacted windows.

Status: ongoing. Mitigations reduced p99 by ~60% in canary and prevented queueing; monitoring continues.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 07:20 - Engineering (deploy-bot): Soft-eviction threshold patch rolled out to eu-west canary (nodes n-eu-132, n-eu-133). Monitoring p99.

Issue summary: Since the runtime queue-rebalance and scheduler tuning deployed 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC, several chat sessions for a high-volume dedicated customer show increased time-to-first-token (TTFB). Impact: Customer experiences 3-12s stalls before first token, occasional 504s for sessions that exceed request timeout. This is reproducible for short prompt+chat-init flows and appears more severe when KV cache is cold or when model pinning forces a model variant with different kernel selection.

Observed behavior: Conversations stall before streaming begins; first token latency spikes from baseline ~0.2-0.6s to 3-12s. Throughput for long-running token streaming is normal once streaming starts. Errors: sporadic 504s and 502s during peak.

Expected behavior: TTFB should remain at baseline (<1s) for dedicated capacity customer; no increase in 5xx rates after scheduler change.
1) Use NovaDocs dedicated account in us-west region with model pinned to rw-medium-1.5
2) Start new chat session with a short priming prompt (30-80 tokens), enable streaming, low concurrency (1-2 sessions),
3) Observe initial token emission time via client-side timing and server traces
4) Repeat with KV cache cold and with KV cache warm (observe difference),
5) Compare before/after times relative to 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC rollout window

03-10 10:00 - Support (Aisha): Validated multiple request-ids from NovaDocs showing high first-token latencies and some 504s. Captured sample traces and forwarded to SRE.
03-10 11:15 - SRE (Diego): Correlated latency spikes with runtime queue-rebalance rollout at 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC. Noticed increased slot_acquire_wait in traces for affected requests.
03-10 12:20 - Eng (R&D runtime team): Observed that the new scheduler attempts to rebalance work across fewer worker threads to improve throughput, which increases time waiting for a worker to be assigned for short, low-token requests leading to head-of-line starvation for chat kickoff.
Hypothesis 1: Scheduler rebalance introduced increased worker assignment latency for short-lived chat priming requests, particularly when KV cache is cold and kernel selection path takes fallback, causing TTFB inflation.
Hypothesis 2: A change in queue affinity (hot-path batching) reduced priority for low-token streaming requests; combined with recent kernel selection logic this delays first-token emission while batch windows form.
Correlation: Issues are concentrated in dedicated customers on older quantized model variants where kernel fallback triggers extra cache warmup and the scheduler waits for a worker matching GPU/quantization profile.
Repro attempt: Re-running workload on staging with scheduler toggled to previous policy reproduces median TTFB at baseline; enabling rebalance policy reproduces 3-8s stalls.
Related artifacts: linked PR https://github.com/redwood-infer/runtime/pull/1846 contains the rebalance logic and scheduler config changes. Slack thread #support-ttfb: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0123456

payload.description:
Issue summary: AurumHealth enabled an optimizer experiment (tenant profile 'exp/aggressive-mix-v2') that combined continuous batching heuristics, aggressive KV prefetch, and an 8-bit quantization profile. After the change we saw a sharp P95 latency regression and intermittent streaming disconnects for long chat workloads.

Impact: ~30% of tenant requests now have P95 ≈ 900ms (previously ~200ms). Several customer agents reported streaming truncation and occasional 5xx errors. This is customer-impacting during peak hours for AurumHealth's workflow.

Environment: Dedicated pool ded-us-east-3, prod-us-east region, tenant = AurumHealth (dedicated). Traffic shape: many mid-long sequences (avg seq_len 320, 95th 600). Model pinned to llama-3-70b, runtime variant redwood-mix-quant-8bit for the experiment.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Apply tenant optimizer profile 'exp/aggressive-mix-v2' via Console -> Tenant Config.
2) Run workload generator with seq length distribution matching customer production (burst 20qps sustained for 10m).
3) Observe P95 and streaming error rate via Console / Traces.
4) Check worker logs for KV cache eviction spikes and socket write errors.

Relevant logs (sample):
[worker-12] 2026-03-10T02:14:03Z WARN kv_cache: eviction=high prefix_hits=0.02 evict_rate=0.78
[worker-12] 2026-03-10T02:14:04Z ERROR stream: write failed: BrokenPipeError
[router] 2026-03-10T02:14:05Z INFO batching: grouped_batch_size=128 per_request_tokens=512 kernel_select=slow-path

Requested action: Provide a step-by-step safe step-down/rollback plan that can be executed during a customer maintenance window with minimal disruption, including: per-tenant snapshot restore of optimizer profile, ordered rollback of batching/kv-prefetch/quantization flags, traffic-splitting commands to shift 10/50/100% to stable variant, preflight checks to run before re-enabling experiment, and a short hotfix script we can apply now if immediate mitigation is required. Also request guidance for postmortem checks to avoid recurrence.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:35 - SRE (Zoe Patel): Observed elevated GPU memory pressure and high KV eviction on ded-us-east-3. Suggest disabling KV prefetch first as it appears to increase memory churn and forces fallbacks to slow-path kernels.
2026-03-11 09:10 - Customer (AurumHealth - ops@aurumhealth.com): Confirmed they can accept a 10-minute maintenance window tonight. Asked for order of operations and rollback verification steps.
Metric snapshot (prod-us-east/ded-us-east-3) between 2026-03-10T01:50 and 2026-03-10T02:20 shows GPU mem usage sustained at 92% + frequent GC cycles on worker pods.
KV cache eviction rate increased 6x after enabling 'exp/aggressive-mix-v2'. Eviction correlates with increased average grouped batch size (auto-grouping bumped to 128).
Kernel selection trace indicates a fallback to 'slow-path' for mixed quant profiles when grouped_batch_size > 64; this significantly raises per-token latency for long sequences.
Hypothesis: Combined effect of larger automatic grouping + KV prefetch increases memory pressure -> causes cache churn and forces slow kernel fallback for mixed quant workloads. The quant profile change in the experiment exacerbates kernel mismatch for sequences >512 tokens.
Temporary mitigation that reduced latency in a canary: (1) disable kv_prefetch on tenant via CLI, (2) set max_grouping_size=32, (3) pin quant_profile=fp16. Observed P95 drop from ~900ms -> ~260ms in canary traffic (10% split).
Need: 1) Operator-friendly step-by-step rollback instructions (CLI commands + Console steps) to unwind the experiment per-tenant; 2) A small hotfix script to disable kv_prefetch and cap group size without a full restart; 3) Traffic-split recipe to move 10/50/100% off the experiment profile to the stable profile; 4) Preflight checklist to validate before re-enabling the experiment (metrics to watch, safe traffic ramp rates).
In Progress - hotfix script being prepared by Runtime Eng. Planned verification on canary traffic then staged rollout back to tenant.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent high p99 latency and occasional 504 timeouts for identical conversational turns (repeat prompts) after short idle windows. Problem affects a subset of sessions that are 'hot' (high QPS on the same conversation id) and reproduces against the customer's dedicated capacity pool in us-east.

Impact:
- Multiple user-facing requests for NarrativeAI saw p99 generator latency climb from ~120ms to >2.5s, with some requests eventually 504ing.
- Customer reports degraded product experience for follow-up messages (idempotent repeated prompts) and increased error rates.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool) in us-east
- Production traffic from NarrativeAI (dedicated tier)
- Affected models: redwood-rlhf-13b (primary), fallback to open-llama-13b observed

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Start a conversational session and send an initial prompt that warms model and KV cache.
2) Send 3–6 identical follow-up turns spaced at ~200–500ms intervals.
3) Wait ~6–12 seconds idle.
4) Send the same follow-up turn again (identical tokens).
5) Observe p99 spike or 504 on the repeated turn in ~5–15% of sessions.

Observed behavior:
- The first repeated turns after a short idle often hit cold-path prefetching and trigger a small fan-out to KV shards, but when the same hot key is continuously requested the prefetch logic sometimes defers re-population, causing serialized misses across replicas and amplified latency.
- Logs show prefix lookup misses followed by sequential backoff/retry patterns. KV lease/lease-stale timings align with observed 6–12s window.

Expected behavior:
- Identical conversational turns should hit prefix/KV fast-path and return sub-200ms response in dedicated env.

Attachments / links:
- Support logs (redacted) attached by customer: s3://support-uploads/narrativeai/2026-03-09/payloads.zip
- APM traces linked in Confluence runbook

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:45 - SRE (Priya Desai): Confirmed correlation between miss_count and increase in per-request tail latency. Noted high contention on a small subset of KV shards (hot-key fanout). Suspect prefetch backoff/backpressure policy allows starvation when a key stays hot and re-population is delayed.
2026-03-11 08:30 - Customer (NarrativeAI - Eng Ops): Provided additional examples and confirmed issue frequency ~8% for active sessions during peak. Able to reproduce with a short test harness. Asked whether there's a config to make prefetch more aggressive.
2026-03-13 09:00 - Support (Aisha Khan): Applied temporary config change (kvcache.prefetch_hotkey_threshold=0.6 -> 0.3) for NarrativeAI pool to force earlier prefetch on hot keys. Early metrics show p99 dropped from ~2.5s to ~420ms for sample traffic. Monitoring for side effects.
2026-03-13 12:10 - SRE (Priya Desai): Noted slight increase in KV read operations (expected) but no capacity exhaustion. Continuing to monitor for CPU/GPU impact and tail latency across other tenants.
2026-03-13 17:32 - Customer (NarrativeAI - Eng Lead): Acknowledged improvement in recent tests. Requested permanent fix and rollback plan for config if regressions observed.
Metric correlation: prefix_lookup_miss and kvcache.backfill_queue_length spike aligned with p99 latency window.
Observed lease ttl mismatch: leases expire at ~8s, but prefetch re-enqueue uses a conservatively large backoff with a 10s floor for keys previously seen as 'hot', which allows a small window where client requests trigger serialized cache repopulation.
Hot-key fanout: single conversation id caused many in-flight requests; scheduler currently favors fairness across keys > this leads to repeated de-prioritization of the same key's prefetch in favor of new keys, causing reserialized cold-paths.
Reproduction harness: Customer provided a harness which simulates 50 sessions with repeated identical turns at 200–500ms spacing; reproduced p99 spikes locally using dedicated-sim mode.
Potential risk of aggressive prefetch: increasing prefetch aggressiveness could increase KV read QPS and burst costs; must ensure no impact on latency for other keys/tenants in shared path (but this is dedicated pool for customer).
Relevant linked tickets: SUP-34121 (cache-coherence window), SUP-78320 (session cache coherence delay) — similar symptoms but different root cause related to prefetch scheduling.
1) Ship and smoke-test runtime patch to reduce prefetch backoff floor for hot keys (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4129).
2) Deploy to NarrativeAI's dedicated pool during low-traffic window and monitor p99, KV read QPS, CPU/GPU utilization for 24h.
3) If stable, roll change into general dedicated-config with feature flag and add automated canary thresholds to detect KV QPS regressions.
4) Update kvcache runbook and create a telemetry dashboard showing prefetch re-enqueue counts, lease expirations, and hot-key contention alerts.
5) Follow up with customer for acceptance test and schedule post-mortem draft if needed.
Partial mitigation applied: temporary config change reduced prefetch backoff threshold for NarrativeAI's pool and produced immediate p99 improvement. A runtime patch (PR #4129) has been drafted to more robustly handle hot-key re-enqueue behavior and will be canaried to the customer's dedicated pool. Monitoring is in place; awaiting 24–48h stable signal before promoting to broader rollout. Documenting follow-up items in Confluence.
Reduced kvcache.prefetch_hotkey_threshold for the customer's dedicated pool to force earlier repopulation of hot-key prefixes. Customer observed lower p99 during testing. If recurrence happens, advise temporary traffic shaping to reduce hot-key QPS.
payload.summary: Intermittent p99 latency and timeouts for identical conversational turns due to KV prefetch starvation on hot keys

Issue summary: Customer reporting a $4,312.57 discrepancy across three invoice line items after they changed reserved capacity and model variant pins mid-billing-window. Impact: Customer billing shows duplicate-looking microbatch line items with fractional token rounding that sum to an unexpected delta. Provisional credit that normally applies during postback reconciliation was withheld pending investigation.

Context: Novus Retail migrated a portion of traffic from mixlm-13b-v1 to redwood/quantized-medium-7b on 2026-03-08 at ~18:40 UTC to reduce cost. They are on a Dedicated contract with hourly reserved capacity. The pricing tier change happened roughly in the middle of the hourly accumulation window which led to blended per-token rates for the same API key. The customer expects the platform to attribute usage to a single effective tier and apply smoothing/rounding consistently; instead the invoice contains three separate lines for similar microbatch events and a withheld provisional credit labeled "auto-reconcile-hold".
1) Customer has Dedicated reserved capacity with hourly aggregation enabled.
2) At T0 (2026-03-08 18:40 UTC) customer changes model pin for route /v1/chat from mixlm-13b-v1 to redwood/quantized-medium-7b and reduces reserved GPUs by 20%.
3) Billing pipeline receives mixed postbacks during the hourly window with both pre-change and post-change tags blended by edge proxies.
4) Aggregator produces per-model microbatch rounding to 2 decimal places and emits three invoice lines instead of a single smoothed line.
5) Reconciler flags the blended window for manual provisional credit hold due to tier ambiguity.
Billing postback sample (2026-03-08T18:41:02Z): {api_key: redacted, model: mixlm-13b-v1, tokens: 1324.7, microbatch: 3, rate_applied: 0.0009}
Billing postback sample (2026-03-08T18:41:15Z): {api_key: redacted, model: redwood/quantized-medium-7b, tokens: 1401.3, microbatch: 4, rate_applied: 0.00075}

 - LINE_B: quantized-medium-7b interleaved microbatch $1,879.23

2026-03-10 09:30 - Initial triage by billing: confirmed three line items in finalized invoice CSV. Held provisional credit flagged by reconciler due to conflicting tier tags.
2026-03-10 11:10 - Correlated postbacks to edge proxy logs (edge-42). Observed that some postbacks lost 'reserved-tier' tag during resize event; others retained old tag. This created duplicate attribution for same token ranges.
2026-03-10 14:25 - Re-created aggregator run on staging with mixed postback order: reproduces multi-line output due to per-model rounding to cents before merging aggregated buckets.
2026-03-11 08:05 - Finance note: rounding is performed per model per microbatch and then summed; expected behavior is to sum raw token*rate then round. Current implementation introduces per-model rounding noise that is visible when tiers change mid-window.

Additional notes:

SRE (Jamal Ortiz) (2026-03-11): Edge proxy resize event at 2026-03-08T18:40:12Z shows some in-flight postbacks retried without metadata; likely root cause for lost tag. We need to add idempotent tag propagation on retry path.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Shopwise reports duplicate external side-effects (order creation) when using the TypeScript SDK from serverless functions behind an API gateway. The app calls a customer tool via function_call to create an order; sporadic retries from their serverless platform and the SDK lead to the tool being executed twice, creating duplicate order entries in Shopwise's systems.

Impact:
- Duplicate orders observed for ~0.8% of checkout requests during peak traffic (high revenue impact).
- Customer is enterprise (PCI scope) and needs clear guidance for at-most-once semantics and a safe remediation path.

Environment:
- TS SDK v1.4.2 (pinned)
1) Deploy a serverless HTTP function (AWS Lambda behind ALB) that forwards client requests to Redwood TS SDK (v1.4.2) and uses function_call to invoke a customer tool endpoint (POST /create-order).
2) The SDK client is initialized per-request inside the handler (no global connection reuse).
3) Simulate transient timeouts by dropping the ALB response for ~10% of requests (or have the backend sleep >4s).
4) Observe that the Lambda / API gateway retries the outbound HTTP request to Redwood and the SDK also retries (default retry policy), leading to duplicated tool webhooks arriving at customer service with different request IDs but identical payloads.
5) Inspect the Shopwise order DB and find duplicate rows with same cart_id and amount but different order_id.
[2026-03-11T15:02:01Z] lambda.handler requestId=abc123 - outbound to redwood: POST /v1/chat (function_call: create_order)
[2026-03-11T15:02:01Z] redwood response: 202 Accepted (processing) request_token=rtk-09a
[2026-03-11T15:02:05Z] lambda retry triggered by ALB after timeout
[2026-03-11T15:02:05Z] lambda.handler requestId=def456 - outbound to redwood: POST /v1/chat (function_call: create_order)
[2026-03-11T15:02:06Z] redwood response: 200 OK (tool webhook delivered) request_token=rtk-0b3
[2026-03-11T15:02:06Z] shopwise /create-order created order_id=ORD-1001 for cart_id=CART-87
[2026-03-11T15:02:06Z] shopwise /create-order created order_id=ORD-1002 for cart_id=CART-87
Initial hypothesis: idempotency key used for deduplication is scoped to a session or connection in the TS SDK when function_call triggers are converted into tool webhooks. In serverless deployments where SDK clients are ephemeral, the second request does not present the same idempotency token and the platform treats it as a fresh invocation.

Reproduction validated in staging with a small script that simulates Lambda cold starts and forced ALB timeouts. We observed distinct request tokens from the Redwood side for each retry when the SDK was re-initialized per-invocation. When we moved to a global SDK client instance and generated an explicit idempotency key per-customer-order (UUID attached to the chat request metadata), duplicates disappeared in tests.

Related: internal note suggests SDK should surface/allow a per-request idempotency header for function_call tool invocations (RFC in linked PR).
Short term: have the customer send a stable, application-level idempotency key (e.g., X-Shopwise-Idempotency) as part of the chat/tool request payload or in chat.metadata. Shopwise can generate the key at checkout (cart_id or UUID) and include it on every retry attempt; server-side tool should dedupe based on that key. Alternatively, reuse a global SDK client instance across invocations (pool) so the SDK's internal idempotency mapping is consistent across retries.
SDK change: expose an explicit 'idempotency_key' parameter on ChatRequest/FunctionCall payloads that is forwarded as a strong dedupe token for tool webhook delivery. Server change: accept idempotency keys for function_call deliveries and guarantee at-most-once delivery semantics when token is identical. Engineering has a draft PR for the TS SDK (see related_github_prs).
In Progress - agreed short-term mitigation with customer (application-level idempotency header). Engineering to implement SDK param and server-side mapping to dedupe tool calls. ETA: engineering sprint in two weeks, patch release targeted 2026-03-28.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 08:47 - SRE (Slack #incidents): Noted that API gateway retried due to 504s; asked customer to check ALB timeout settings as additional mitigation.
payload.summary: Session-scoped idempotency keys causing duplicate side-effect tool invocations in TS serverless integration

payload.description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 ~02:07 UTC Tidewave reported a sudden increase in request latency and streaming disconnects. Investigation found a fanout heartbeat storm originating from a misrouted scheduler retry loop which caused session coordinator congestion. Symptoms included long streaming resumption times (>30s), duplicate completions for idempotent requests, and a customer-visible invoice spike due to duplicate billing records.

Impact:
- Tidewave experienced ~18 minutes of degraded streaming for 60% of requests from their us-east endpoints.
- Approximately 1.2k requests were duplicated and billed.
- Customer-facing SLOs breached; Tidewave moved to high-severity escalation and notified their finance/comms teams.

Environment:
- prod | us-east (primary servicing pool), dedicated tenant: tidewave-enterprise-01
- Affected model slices: rwkv-14b quantized variant and redwood-v2-medium fallback

Steps to reproduce (reduced replay):
1) Replay subset of Tidewave traffic with controlled fanout concurrency (simulated 800 concurrent streams).
2) Inject a scheduler ACK delay to force client retry logic to trigger multiplexed heartbeats.
3) Observe coordinator task queue growth, streaming session reconnect bursts, and duplicated completions on the serving-runtime.

Observed logs and metrics (high-level):
- scheduler: repeated job requeue logs with exponential backoff suppressed (scheduler.log lines 02:06:45 - 02:08:00).
- session-coordinator: queue_depth spike from 120 -> 4,200 in ~90s; worker CPU saturated at 92%.
- api-gateway: 5xx rate up from 0.2% -> 6.8% and connection resets per second increased 12x.
- billing: duplicate completion webhook fired for 1,235 completions (billing-service audit stream).

Immediate mitigation taken:
- 02:15 UTC: Support applied emergency circuit-breaker rule to Tidewave tenant to limit parallel streams to 200.
- 02:22 UTC: Engineers pushed a scheduler patch to stop re-enqueueing heartbeats when coordinator backlog > 1,000.
- 02:30 UTC: Billing team paused duplicate-completion ingestion and began deduplication job on the outstanding invoices.

Current status and resolution summary:
- Root cause: scheduler retry logic failed to respect a new coordinator backpressure header introduced three weeks prior. A regression in scheduler task throttling allowed fanout heartbeats to escalate under high latency conditions, creating a positive feedback loop.
- Fix deployed: scheduler throttling conservative fallback (PR linked) and session-coordinator hard quota enforcement.
- Billing fix: retroactive dedupe job applied to outstanding invoices; customer credits calculated and applied for duplicated charges.

Notes on detection and monitoring gaps:
- Alerting thresholds did not consider combined queue_depth + heartbeat rate; only queue_depth had an alert. Heartbeat rate spikes were visible in metrics but not alerted.
- No synthetic replay detected the pattern because synthetic load used lower stream concurrency than Tidewave's production profile.

Required follow-ups (see action_items):


2026-03-10 02:10 UTC | Tidewave IT (Alex R.) - initial report: customers seeing streaming timeouts and duplicate responses; attached sample request IDs. Asked for ETA and immediate mitigation.
2026-03-10 02:18 UTC | Support (Maya Chen) - triage: escalated to SRE, applied tenant-level parallelism cap as short-term mitigation. Notified billing to hold ingestion of completion events for the tenant.
2026-03-10 02:25 UTC | SRE (Ravi Patel) - investigation note: observed scheduler requeue storm and session coordinator queue spike; rolling patch to throttle requeues underway (PR: runtime#4582).
2026-03-10 03:05 UTC | Billing (Lena Ortiz) - note: paused ingestion pipeline for tidewave-enterprise-01; starting dedupe scan. Initial estimate: ~1.2k duplicate events; preparing credit batch.
2026-03-10 08:14 UTC | Support (Maya Chen) - customer update sent: summarized mitigations, promised post-incident report and invoice credits. Customer acknowledged and requested timeline for permanent fixes.
2026-03-11 10:02 UTC | Engineering (Carlos Mendes) - follow-up: root cause confirmed; scheduler regression introduced in PR#4478 (task-throttling refactor). Patch merged and staged to prod; coordinator quotas added as defense-in-depth.
2026-03-12 16:22 UTC | Customer Success (Elena Karpova) - verified invoice credits applied and Tidewave finance confirmed receipt. Customer requested a follow-up postmortem and changes to SLA terms for high-concurrency streaming workloads.
Found scheduler change 2026-02-15 removed coordinator backpressure header propagation in the refactor. This allowed scheduler to continue requeuing when coordinator was saturated.
Reproduction succeeded with synthetic replays at 750-1k concurrent streams when ACK delays > 300ms.
Session-coordinator lacked an absolute hard-cap; queue growth overwhelmed worker pools which in turn increased ACK latency creating a feedback loop.
Billing duplicates traced to webhook fanout retries; dedupe key missing request_id in some older fallback paths which allowed duplicate invoice records to be persisted.
Immediate: tenant stream cap and scheduler patch stopped the heartbeat amplification. Billing dedupe job removed duplicate invoice records and credits were applied. Long-term: added coordinator hard quota, restored backpressure header propagation, added heartbeat-rate alerting, and expanded synthetic load tests to include high-concurrency streams. Customer received credits and a compensation plan for SLA exposure.
ENG-1: Restore backpressure header propagation in scheduler and add unit + integration tests (owner: Carlos Mendes) - due 2026-03-20
SRE-1: Implement session-coordinator hard quota enforcement and autoscaling guardrails (owner: Ravi Patel) - due 2026-03-18
OBS-1: Add composite alert for queue_depth AND heartbeat_rate for all tenants (owner: Priya Shah) - due 2026-03-16
QA-1: Add high-concurrency synthetic workload (>=800 concurrent streams) to regression suite (owner: QA team) - due 2026-03-22
BILL-1: Audit billing ingestion fallback paths to ensure dedupe keys always include request_id (owner: Lena Ortiz) - due 2026-03-19

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During an evening traffic surge on 2026-03-10 we observed a tight ~18-minute window where a subset of tenant traffic (Finora Health) triggered a sharp increase in 5xx responses at the API gateway. Upstreams (serving runtime) were reporting process-level errors and eventually OOM/FD-exhaustion-like failures.

Impact:
- Finora Health experienced ~9% request failure rate for generation/chat endpoints during the window.
- Elevated customer error alerts and automated failover to fallback model variants triggered additional capacity pressure.
- Production latency spiked for affected routes.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1) - dedicated tenant fleet for Finora Health on dedicated-capacity cluster.
- API Gateway version: apigw-1.9.3, Ingress proxy: envoy-2.4.1, Serving runtime: runtime-3.2.0
- Client SDK observed: finora-es-client v2.3.0 (newer behavior observed after rollout to some clients).

Steps to reproduce (approximate):
1) Simulate concurrent short-lived streaming sessions with frequent client-side half-close (RST) events and keepalive-negotiation churn.
2) Run a high fan-out of short generation requests (~600 req/s concentrated to the tenant shard) with the same client library behavior.
3) Observe connection table growth and rising FD usage on ingress/worker processes, then errors when FD limit reached.

Observed behavior:
- API Gateway returned 502/503/504 for requests routed to the impacted shard.
- Ingress and runtime logs show many connections in CLOSE_WAIT and a spike in open file descriptors.
- Kernel logs showed "EMFILE" type messages and runtime processes logged "failed to accept: too many open files" followed by worker restarts.
- Post-incident profiling indicated ~85% of FDs were sockets in TIME_WAIT/CLOSE_WAIT and not being reclaimed quickly due to client half-close behavior and short keepalive TTLs.

Relevant logs / excerpts:
- apigw: "error accepting conn: accept: too many open files" (multiple workers across nodes)
- ingress-proxy: "socket close-wait count=4123; max-fd=8192"
- runtime: "watchdog: process restart after uncaught OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files"
- kernel: "pid 4112: open files: 8765 (max 8192)"

Workaround applied during incident:
- Emergency increase of system FD limit on affected nodes (temporary) and rolling restart of ingress proxies to clear stale CLOSE_WAIT sockets.
- Activated tenant-level egress rate limiter to spread the Finora Health burst across longer window.
- Deployed a short-term apigw config change to lower concurrent connection per-worker acceptance rate to reduce FD growth.

Expected next steps / follow-up (see resolution):
- Root cause analysis and permanent mitigations completed (connection handling hardening + client coordination).
- Customer notified and incident postmortem published.

Initial hypothesis: generic 'thundering herd' causing runtime OOMs. However kernel-level EMFILE hints shifted focus to FD exhaustion. We observed correlation with Finora SDK version 2.3.0 rollout (client-side change in keepalive/close behavior).

Key findings:
- The client library started issuing aggressive TCP RST after streaming blocks in v2.3.0 for connection pooling efficiency. This produced many half-closed sockets on our side which lingered in CLOSE_WAIT.
- Ingress proxy (Envoy) configured with default delayed-close times and a relatively low worker FD budget led to resource starvation when hundreds of clients exhibited the new behavior simultaneously.
- The serving runtime did not enforce strict per-process FD reservation; combined with large model cache pages and logs this led to accept() failing and restarts.

Evidence collected:
- Packet captures show RSTs from client side immediately after upload shards.
- Node-level lsof and ss snapshots during the window showed >60% sockets in CLOSE_WAIT.
- Metrics show sudden jump in socket_open_count, fd_usage_percent, and worker_restart_count synchronized with increased 5xx.

Mitigation trials during incident:
- Increased process ulimit, restarted ingress to reclaim sockets: immediate drop in 5xx but not sustainable as long-term fix.
- Back-pressure via tenant rate limiter: reduced immediate FD pressure.
- Short-lived change to Envoy delayed_close to aggressively close sockets resulted in fewer lingering CLOSE_WAIT entries.

Post-incident reproduction notes:
- We reproduced locally using a synthetic client that closes streams with RST and observed identical FD accumulation in an Envoy+runtime composition.

Permanent mitigations implemented and validated on 2026-03-12:
1) Ingress (Envoy) config patch to tune delayed_close, aggressive_linger_timeout, and per-worker fd soft-reservations deployed to prod us-east-1.
2) Serving runtime hardening: added FD guard that refuses new accepts when fd_usage exceeds 70% and responds with 429s (back-pressure) instead of allowing accept()/crash.
3) Operator playbook: new runbook steps for detecting CLOSE_WAIT storms and graduated mitigation (rate-limit -> system ulimit bump -> safe-restart).
4) Coordinated with Finora Health: flagged client SDK v2.3.0 and requested a staged rollback / follow-on patch to change RST behavior; client agreed and released v2.3.1 with recommended keepalive behavior.
5) Added alerting rule on fd_usage_percent > 65% and new dashboard panels for CLOSE_WAIT counts per node.

Customer communication:
- Finora Health SRE and account team were notified within the incident window; a post-incident summary and recommended client changes were shared. Customer acceptance of fixes confirmed on 2026-03-13.

Status: Resolved. All mitigations validated and monitoring in place.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 20:05 - SRE Oncall (Priya Nair): Kernel EMFILE seen across three nodes; increasing ulimit as emergency step.
Track adoption of client SDK v2.3.1 by Finora Health and other large tenants (30-day window)
Roll out Envoy config adjustments to eu-west and ap-south after validation (scheduled)
Add automated simulation test for half-close socket storms to CI for ingress/runtime combos
Document recommended client SDK socket/keepalive settings in DevX guides

Issue summary:
During a scheduled nightly batch from AegisPharm (private deployment, eu-west), the Redwood private control plane entered a multipath failover loop causing amplified request fanout, repeated retries, and ordered-stream reassembly failures for streaming completions. Symptoms started at ~2026-03-10T01:12Z and lasted for ~90 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer observed duplicate completions and truncated streaming transcripts across ~18% of requests for the 90-minute window.
- Significant token accounting discrepancies led to a billing exposure (estimated 2.4x token inflation for affected requests).
- Several model variants in the customer's pinned rollout experienced high tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors.
- Business impact: AegisPharm paused nightly ingestion jobs and opened an escalation call.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane)
- Region: eu-west-1
- Cluster: aegispharm-prod-cluster-3 (dedicated GPU pool)
- Canary config: pinned redwood-quant-4bit behind routing policy with multipath failover enabled

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1. Customer ran concurrent batch job (fanout to 4k concurrent sub-requests) against the private endpoint with streaming enabled.
2. During transient scheduler pressure, router invoked multipath failover to secondary replicas.
3. Failover logic retried requests while upstream still delivered partial streams, causing duplicates and out-of-order stream segments.
4. Client resumed and reassembled streams but hit reassembly logic edge cases that truncated transcripts.

Logs / Observability pointers:
- Kibana: logs/aegispharm/prod/2026-03-10T01:00-03:30 (request-id examples: req-0a7f23e9, req-0a7f24b2)
- Metrics: dashboards/serving/runtime/eu-west/pool-3 (spike in retry_count, evictions, and request_fanout_ratio)
- Traces: jaeger/service/router?trace=req-0a7f23e9

Immediate customer-facing note: We acknowledged impact within first_response_due and opened an incident bridge with AegisPharm engineering and CS. Workarounds were provided (temporary reduce concurrency + disable multipath failover).
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10T01:22Z: Customer called in reporting duplicated and truncated streams from nightly ingestion. Opened incident bridge and notified SRE and on-call infra.
SRE (Sanjay Mehta) 2026-03-10T01:35Z: Initial triage indicates routing layer returned multiple successful ACKs while backend KV caches were still warming. Temporarily disabled multipath failover for aegispharm-prod-cluster-3 to reduce amplification. Requesting scheduler and router logs for 00:50-01:30Z.
AegisPharm (Dr. Lena Ortiz) 2026-03-10T02:05Z: Confirmed stop of duplicate completions after disabling multipath. Customer paused ingestion and asked for billing mitigation while investigation continues.
SRE (Riley Park) 2026-03-10T04:40Z: Observed elevated eviction_count on GPU pool and TLS renegotiation spikes aligned with retry bursts. Hypothesis: under high concurrency router retried prematurely due to false negative health checks.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-11T09:12Z: Provided customer with a temporary credit estimate and proposed next steps. Scheduled postmortem call for 2026-03-12.
Engineering (Priya Singh) 2026-03-12T14:00Z: Root cause identified in multipath backoff code; race between ack-path and retry-path under partial stream conditions. Preparing fix and tests.
Timeline and findings:
- 01:12Z: first increase in router retry_count and request_fanout_ratio.
- 01:15-01:45Z: scheduler reported intermittent slot evictions on pool-3 (GPU memory pressure flagged).
- 01:20Z: router healthcheck misclassification spikes (false negatives) correlated with short-lived TLS renegotiation events downstream.
- Root cause: conjunction of three factors: (1) a regression in multipath backoff (commit 8f3b2c) that could trigger rapid retries without exponential backoff on partial-success ACKs, (2) transient kernel-level scheduler evictions causing backend nodes to requeue requests, and (3) stream reassembly logic that assumed single-path monotonic segment ordering.
- Evidence: trace captures showing duplicate sub-request IDs, TTL on KV cache not honored for newly elected replica, and unit test coverage gap for partial-stream ACK semantics.
Short-term mitigations (applied 2026-03-10):
- Disabled multipath failover for aegispharm-prod-cluster-3 and rolled back router commit 8f3b2c.
- Instructed customer to reduce concurrency for nightly jobs and to switch the pinned rollout to the non-quant variant for the next 48 hours.
- Issued provisional billing credit estimate and paused invoicing for the affected window while we finalize accounting.

Permanent fixes (deployed 2026-03-12/2026-03-13):
- Backport fix to multipath backoff logic to gate retries on explicit final-ACKs and add jittered exponential backoff. (PR merged: serving-runtime #6123).
- Strengthened healthcheck debounce logic in router to ignore transient TLS renegotiations under 10s. (PR merged: router #204).
- Enhanced stream reassembly to accept out-of-order segments and re-request missing ranges instead of truncating.
- Added end-to-end integration tests simulating partial-stream ACKs and multipath failover.

Customer communication:
- 2026-03-11: Provided interim action plan and billing credit estimate.
- 2026-03-13: Shared final postmortem and confirmed credit applied to March invoice.

Follow-up commitments: see follow_up_actions field.
Engineering to add explicit unit and integration tests for partial-stream ACK semantics (owner: Priya Singh, due: 2026-04-02)
SRE to run a dedicated soak test of multipath enabled configurations at 4k+ concurrent sub-requests (owner: Riley Park, due: 2026-03-25)
Product to review default multipath_failover toggle for private deployments and set conservative default for enterprise/private tiers (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-04-08)
Billing team to reconcile the token accounting for aegispharm window and apply agreed credit (owner: Hannah Li, due: 2026-03-18)
Support to produce a short runbook for customers: recommended concurrency limits and failover toggle guidance (owner: Maya Chen, due: 2026-03-20)

Issue summary:
Customer reported sporadic P99 latency spikes and temporary 5xxs from their dedicated pool during lunchtime traffic on 2026-03-12. Symptoms included: increased attach time to GPUs, evictions from the pool, and sudden autoscaler shrink events followed by tenant request timeouts.

Impact:
- Customer (Acme AI) saw ~20% of their requests return 502/504 during a 14:20–14:35 UTC window.
- Throughput dropped for their pinned routes; internal dashboards showed brief reduction in live GPU attachments for the dedicated pool.
- Affected production flows: low-latency chatlets and short streaming sessions.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: pool-dedicated-us-east-3 (pinned to HW-family: gdx-48gb-mix)
- Models served: redwood/gpt-x-13b-fp16 (primary), fallback to fp32 when kernel hit frag or mem alignment issues
- Region: us-east-1, prod

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Run a short-stream workload with many concurrent, 2–6 token requests interleaved with occasional long requests (1:20 ratio short:long).
2) Force mixed-precision fallback on some requests by sending slightly misaligned sequence lengths and forcing attention patterns that trigger a legacy kernel path.
3) Observe GPU driver logs and autoscaler telemetry over a 15–30 minute window.

Observed behavior:
- GPUs reported repeated power capping events in driver logs (power_limit_changed / pwr cap applied) leading to clock down events and reduced TFLOPS per card.
- Serving runtime noted higher per-request latency due to lower clocks and more kernel retries; metric: kernel_retry_rate spiked 3x.
- Autoscaler observed sustained reduced utilization and fired a shrink (scale-down) decision; scale-down removed a small number of GPUs which led to request failures while attachments were rebalanced.
- Customer's short streams experienced serialized queueing and a rise in 502/504 until the autoscaler stabilized.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should not react to short-lived driver-level power events that transiently reduce clock speed; should consider thermal/power signals as unreliable for capacity shrink decisions.
- Serving runtime should prefer FP16 execution paths for pinned models without downgrading to fallback on short misaligned requests when avoidable.

Logs / telemetry snippets:
- GPU driver: "pwr_cap applied: 160W -> 120W; clocks throttled" (multiple cards, repeated ~every 30s for ~10min)
- Runtime metric: kernel_retry_rate: baseline 0.2 -> 0.65; attach_latency p95: 180ms -> 560ms
- Autoscaler decision trace: shrink triggered at 14:25:12 UTC with decision_reason: "sustained_utilization_below_threshold (5m)"

Attachments / Links:
- customer-provided logs: s3://acme-uploads/sup-250999/log-batch-14-20.tar.gz
- internal dashboard links: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/dedicated/pool-dedicated-us-east-3?span=15m

Immediate customer-facing summary (first response):
- Acknowledge impact, set customer status to "We are investigating", provide workaround to pin model to FP16 variant and reduce concurrent short-streams while we investigate.

2026-03-12 14:28 UTC | Aisha Patel (Support): Customer (Acme AI) reports 502/504 on pinned dedicated pool. Asking for logs, sample request ids, and timeframe. SLA first response due 2026-03-13.
2026-03-12 15:05 UTC | Diego Martinez (SRE): Got logs. Observed repeated GPU power cap events correlated with latency spikes. Triage to autoscaler and runtime. Escalating to runtime team; allocating on-call CPU/GPU help.
2026-03-12 16:10 UTC | Priya Singh (Runtime Eng): Initial hypothesis: mixed-precision fallback kernels cause hotter power draw due to less efficient memory layout leading to driver power capping on these cards under short-burst patterns. Suggest immediate mitigation: force FP16 path and suppress autoscaler shrink decisions for 10m if shrink is correlated with power cap signals.
2026-03-13 09:22 UTC | Diego Martinez (SRE): Applied mitigation in prod: updated pool autoscaler policy to ignore utilization dips that coincide with driver power_cap events and increased min-replicas by 1 for pool-dedicated-us-east-3. Also enabled 'prefer_fp16' flag for redwood/gpt-x-13b-fp16 for this pool.
2026-03-13 12:40 UTC | Aisha Patel (Support): Informed customer of applied mitigations and requested confirmation that errors have subsided. Customer confirmed reduced 5xxs and improved p95 within 2 hours.
2026-03-14 10:00 UTC | Priya Singh (Runtime Eng): Root cause analysis complete. Filed long-term fix PR to improve kernel selection and to add driver-signals-safe heuristics in autoscaler: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821. Scheduling rollout window in maintenance next week.
2026-03-14 11:15 UTC | Aisha Patel (Support): Closing customer ticket after customer confirms stable behavior and acceptance of planned rollout. Provided post-incident notes and contact for follow-up.
Hypothesis 1: Mixed-precision fallback kernels cause inefficient memory access patterns increasing instantaneous power draw -> driver power cap applied -> lower GPU clock -> throughput drop.
Hypothesis 2: Short-stream heavy fanout causes workload bursts that push card to peak power frequently; combined with fallback kernels, this breaches power envelope on older card revisions in pool.
Telemetry findings: Correlation found between driver power_cap events and autoscaler shrink timestamps. Power cap events preceded autoscaler shrinks by ~45-90s in most samples.
Kernel-level traces: Certain attention kernel variants used under fallback showed 18% higher GPU compute time on identical batch size compared to preferred FP16 kernel.
Autoscaler policy evaluation: current policy treats sustained_utilization_below_threshold over sliding 5m as reliable; however it does not cross-check driver telemetry (power/thermal) which made it act on transient hardware-level events.
Risk assessment: Without mitigation, repeated events could lead to unnecessary capacity churn and customer-visible errors for pinned dedicated pools under bursty short-stream workloads.
Related past incidents: see SUP-41258 (thermal throttle) for similar clock-down observations; however that incident was caused by ambient thermal conditions not kernel power draw patterns.
Mitigation applied 2026-03-13 09:22 UTC: (1) Set autoscaler to ignore utilization dips coincident with driver power_cap signals for pool-dedicated-us-east-3, (2) increased pool min-replicas by +1 as temporary buffer, (3) enabled prefer_fp16 execution path for redwood/gpt-x-13b-fp16 in that pool.
Customer impact after mitigation: 5xxs dropped from ~20% to <1% during comparable load windows. P95 latency returned to expected range within ~2 hours.
Long-term fixes: PR #4821 updates kernel selection logic to avoid costly fallbacks for short-stream patterns and adds autoscaler cross-check to filter shrink decisions when driver-level power/thermal events are present. Scheduled rollout: progressive canary starting 2026-03-21 with post-rollout validation dashboards.
Follow-ups assigned: Runtime team to complete kernel selection improvements (owner: Priya Singh), Autoscaler team to add driver-telemetry gating (owner: Diego Martinez). Notify capacity-planning for potential hardware refresh for pool-dedicated-us-east-3 in next quarter.
Customer communication: Sent post-incident summary and planned timeline for fixes. Customer accepted workarounds and will monitor during next week. Ticket closed with customer sign-off on 2026-03-14.

Issue summary: NorthStar Payments requests a short-term, customer-controlled webhook 'lease' for audit events covering a legal investigation window. They need each delivered event to carry a server-signed timestamped acknowledgement token and an HMAC of the payload. Deliverable should include a tamper-evident bundle (signed manifest) that proves delivery order and non-repudiation for the leased window.

Impact: Customer cannot complete an AML internal investigation and third-party pen test until they can ingest a provable stream. The ask affects a single production tenant and is time-sensitive (legal request, 72-hour window).

Environment: prod us-east (tenant ns-payments-prod).

Requested artifacts: 1) A timebound webhook lease that routes audit events for tenant ns-payments-prod to a customer-provided HTTPS endpoint for a 72-hour window. 2) Per-event acknowledgement tokens signed by Redwood's audit service (ed25519) and an HMAC header (sha256) keyed by the tenant envelope key. 3) A signed manifest at the end of the lease containing per-event sequence numbers, event hashes, and a canonical ordering proof. 4) Playbook text describing verification steps for the customer to validate the manifest and signatures.

Customer-provided constraints: endpoint supports mutual TLS. Customer requires no redaction of low-level fields during the leased window (they have legal basis). They also want resume tokens to allow replays within the 72-hour lease only.

Steps to reproduce / test harness: 1) On Redwood side, provision a temporary webhook route for tenant ns-payments-prod with mTLS and per-event HMAC headers. 2) Send a continuous stream of audit events from prod (sampling all write events) for 1 hour. 3) Confirm receipt of acknowledgement tokens and that the final signed manifest enumerates all sequence numbers in order and that the manifest signature verifies with our audit key.

Logs / artifacts provided by customer: initial request email thread, mTLS cert bundle from customer, endpoint URL, and a sample of 3 events they expect in the lease window.

Acceptance criteria: customer can validate per-event signatures and manifest, manifest shows contiguous sequence window for lease period, and customer can replay using resume tokens within the lease TTL.
2026-03-12: Intake call with CS and customer to clarify scope. Confirmed legal hold and explicit non-redaction consent. Customer provided certs and sample events.
2026-03-12: SRE reviewed streaming pipeline constraints; noted that current webhook infra supports per-event HMAC but not an end-of-window signed manifest natively.
2026-03-13: Proposed approach: create ephemeral lease record in routing service, turn on ordered delivery mode for tenant, enable per-event hmac header (X-Redwood-HMAC) and acknowledgement token header (X-Redwood-Ack). Implement manifest assembly in audit-archiver job which will compute sequence hashes and sign with audit key. Temporary keys to be rotated after lease.
Hypotheses: latency should remain within SLO since volume for tenant is moderate; main work is manifest generation and atomicity guarantees while archiver writes manifest at lease end.
Open risks: ensuring no partial manifests if archiver crashes; need abort/rollback behavior and a clear resume token hygiene policy to avoid replay outside TTL.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 - Customer (NorthStar Contacts): Provided mTLS certs and endpoint. Confirmed they will accept ed25519 signatures from Redwood audit key. Asked whether resume tokens include replay limits and whether we can provide sample verification code.
2026-03-13 - Legal/Trust (internal): Noted we must record an explicit consent log and attach the legal request to the ticket. Asked CS to collect signed authorization from the customer's legal team.
Create ephemeral webhook lease controller that can be scoped to tenant and TTL
Add per-event ack token (ed25519-signed) header generation in audit emitter
Add X-Redwood-HMAC header (sha256) using tenant envelope key
Implement manifest assembler job in audit-archiver that signs final manifest
Provide verification playbook and sample code snippets for customer
Run a 72-hour test window in staging and one 3-hour pilot in prod for ns-payments-prod
