payload.description:
Customer reports a surprise invoice where a single multi-model batch job (mixed short and long sequences) was billed using a nonlinear higher tier multiplier instead of the expected weighted per-token rate. The customer expects per-token weighting across model variants; instead, a peak-sequence tier was applied to the entire job resulting in ~3.8x higher charge than estimate.
Immediate unexpected charge on finalized invoice for March cycle. Customer has paused scheduled overnight batch runs. This affects billing reconciliation and forecasting for a large healthcare data-processing job (sensitive to month-end budgeting).
1) Customer runs mixed-model batch job 'synth-qa-2026-02-28' using two models: mixseq-embedder-v2 (short sequences ~32 tokens) and dialog-2b-multi (long sequences up to 6k tokens).
2) Job submitted through Dedicated queue (pool-dedicated-us-east-3).
3) Postback stream shows per-request token_count and sequence_length_bucket.
4) Finalized invoice shows line item with rate multiplier matching >4096 token tier applied to entire job instead of per-model weighting.
Postback sample (sanitized): request_id=rp_9f2a7, timestamp=2026-02-28T03:14:22Z, model=dialog-2b-multi, token_count=6120, sequence_length_bucket=">4096"; request_id=rp_9f2a8, model=mixseq-embedder-v2, token_count=28, sequence_length_bucket="<64".
Billing reconciler entries: postback_ingest_id=ing_2026_8721 (ingest window 2026-02-28T00:00-04:00), computed_rate_key=rate_tier:>4096 (applied_total_tokens=1,148,236).
Invoice line: invoice_2026_03_line_44: rate_code=hybrid-multi-tier, applied_multiplier=3.8x, description='Hybrid batch mixed - applied peak-tier'.
- Billing team reproduced mapping of postback->tier: mapping logic currently buckets per-job by max(sequence_length_bucket) rather than per-request aggregation.
- Postback replays show the reconstructor aggregated token counts across models but then looked up rate_tier using the single highest sequence bin seen in the job window.
- Potential contributing factor: an async ingest rewrite deployed 2026-02-20 (PR #487) that changed the order of per-request normalization and job-level aggregation.
- Tokenizer inconsistency flagged: dialog-2b-multi returns additional control tokens for tool-calls; these were double-counted in the aggregator during the ingest rewrite (token_count inflated by ~2-4% for long items).
The postback ingest change (PR 487) inadvertently changed the aggregation order: instead of summing per-request charges and weighting by model, the pipeline computed the job-level maximum sequence bucket and applied that bucket's rate to the whole job. This explains the non-linear 'peak-tier' application. Tokenizer control-token duplication exacerbated the bucketization for long sequences pushing the job into >4096 bin.
1) Temporary manual reclassification of invoice lines for job 'synth-qa-2026-02-28' to per-request weighted rate (billing adjustment).
2) Customer should re-run future jobs with an annotation header 'metering-mode: per-request' (we can accept this header and force the correct aggregation until fix deploys).
Revert aggregation order in postback-reconciler to compute per-request effective token units, aggregate costs by weighted sum, then map to invoice tiers. Add guard in pipeline to ignore job-level max-bucket lookups for mixed-model batches. Patch scheduled: 2026-03-05; rolling deploy with canary on a small set of dedicated pools.
Credits pending: provisional credit issued equal to delta between billed amount and expected weighted amount for invoice_2026_03 (credit memo CM-78291 created). Permanent fix scheduled and tracked in INT-9271. We will reprocess affected ingestion window and adjust any additional customers impacted before next billing cut.
- INT-9271: Postback aggregator order revert and unit tests (owner: infra-ingest).
- Billing: run reconciliation job to find other invoices with 'applied_multiplier>2' for Feb 20-28 window.
- DX: add customer-facing metering doc snippet describing mixed-model batch semantics.
Hi — thanks for flagging this. We traced the overcharge to a regression in our postback ingestion that caused a peak-tier to be applied at the job level. We've created a provisional credit for the March invoice and scheduled a fix to the invoicing pipeline. We'll notify you when the fix is deployed and after we've reprocessed the affected window. Apologies for the disruption and thank you for pausing the overnight jobs while we resolve this.

Issue summary: During PulseRx's morning ingest window (09:30-10:15 UTC, 2026-03-11) a subset of streaming completions returned interleaved token sequences and occasionally duplicated segments from concurrent requests. This produced garbled patient-facing summaries and inflated token counts on billing. Customer (NexGen Health Technologies, enterprise tier) needs a signed delivery of audit logs and a retention/chain-of-custody artifact bundle to satisfy a third-party compliance review (SOC 2 readiness). Impact:
Customer cannot complete their external compliance audit without: signed audit batches covering 2025-09-01..2026-02-28, a manifest for each batch, and a short runbook explaining how Redwood signs and stores these artifacts. This is blocking their audit engagement and procurement milestone.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FinScale Labs) using Redwood Private in eu-west reported truncated Markdown lists and duplicated system lead-ins after an SSE stream disconnect and reconnect. Impact: final list items and the closing Markdown fence are missing in ~60% of reconnects; clients see a duplicated system message at the top of the resumed stream.

Impact:
- User-visible: incomplete bulleted lists in generated responses, often missing last 1-3 list items and trailing punctuation.
- Functional: downstream parsers (JSON/Markdown consumers) fail to validate conversation boundaries.
- Scope: multiple instances in customer's VPC across two dedicated nodes; observed in production only.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployment (customer-controlled edge in their VPC) behind corporate TLS inspection appliance (vendor: NetInspect X).
- Client: browser and server SDKs behind the customer's corp-proxy.
- Model: redwood-llama-13b pinned v2026-02-10.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Start a streaming completion (SSE) with a prompt that yields a bulleted list and a final paragraph.
2) After ~30–90s, trigger an outbound TLS re-inspect (customer's security appliance emits a FIN/close as it rotates session internals).
3) Client reconnects using the standard stream-resume flow.
4) Resumed stream contains: duplicated system preface line ("SYSTEM: Resuming..." injected by runtime for resumed sessions) and the final 1–3 bullet items from the original completion are missing.

Observed logs (edge + app):
- edge-proxy.log excerpt (during incident):
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.912Z] conn: socket=0x7f4fd FIN received from upstream (inspector)
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.915Z] conn: half-close: pipeline flushed, keepalive pending
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.916Z] sse: session-id=9802 resume-token=rtk_7f4fd queued-resume

- runtime.log excerpt:
  [2026-03-10T14:12:07.918Z] stream: session=9802 state=HALF_CLOSED kvcache=warm
  [2026-03-10T14:12:08.120Z] stream: resume requested token=rtk_7f4fd last-offset=3472
  [2026-03-10T14:12:08.121Z] stream: emitted system-resume-envelope id=9802-preface
  [2026-03-10T14:12:08.122Z] stream: resume: rehydrate-kv start=3473 end=NNN

- client-side observation (customer): duplicated first "SYSTEM:" line and final bullet list items missing on DOM render.

Initial hypothesis:
- The TLS inspector's mid-stream FIN causes the edge-proxy to half-close the connection while the runtime believes the request is still in-flight. On resume, the runtime emits a system-resume envelope but does not reconcile the last in-flight token boundary properly; the reconstructor on the client sees the duplicated system preface and the final in-flight tokens are never re-sent (or are treated as already-delivered).
- Alternative: edge-proxy's flush during half-close clobbers the last fragment in the outgoing buffer and resume offset is computed using the flushed offset, not the truly delivered offset.

Logs/metrics links provided by customer:
- Edge dashboard: https://grafana.finscale.internal/d/streams/edge-latency
- Runtime trace: https://sentry.redwood.internal/trace/9802

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced in our lab when we simulated an upstream FIN from a TLS-inspector by sending a half-close during active SSE. Reproduction rate ~3/10.
- Observed that the runtime resume path re-emits a system-resume envelope unconditionally; client SDK prepends resumed fragments to the message buffer and treats the resume-envelope as a normal system message, resulting in apparent duplication.
- Verified that last-offset persisted by the edge component is sometimes one fragment lower than the runtime's internal last-seen-offset after a half-close. This mismatch correlates with missing trailing bullets.
- Correlated timing: if FIN occurs immediately after a chunk boundary, issue not observed; when FIN occurs mid-chunk (edge flush), final tokens are lost on resume.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Disable the TLS inspector's aggressive session rotation for flows to Redwood endpoints (they applied a policy to exempt the inference subnets). This reduced incidence to near-zero for their test traffic.
- Customer can increase client resume window: set resume_grace_period_ms to 5000 in client SDK to accept a wider offset delta while SDK merge logic is being upgraded.

Next steps and action items:
- Engineering (streaming/runtime) to add an idempotent marker to resume-envelope and ensure client SDK treats resume-envelope as a control-only marker (do not render). (PR referenced below).
- Edge team to align flushed-offset semantics with runtime last-seen-offset on half-close; add validation that resume offset <= runtime offset before marking resumed segments as delivered.
- Add telemetry to detect resume-offset mismatches and raise a metric/resume-offset-delta > 0.

Related artifacts:
- Repro harness used: tests/streaming/halfclose-repro (internal).
- Temporary client patch: sdk-js#v0.21.3-resume-control (customer applied locally).

Expected SLA commitments:
- Customer requested a live workaround confirmation within 24h (sla_due_at: 2026-03-11T16:00:00Z in their timezone).

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 12:45 - Customer (FinScale Labs): Applied exemption on their TLS inspector for Redwood subnets; initial test traffic shows marked improvement. Asked for permanent fix schedule and request for teleconference.
Simulated FIN reproduced missing trailing tokens; reproduction rate correlated with mid-chunk FINs.
Client SDK currently treats resume-envelope as a renderable system message; patch pending to treat as control-only.
Edge flush semantics differ between proxy implementations; added a test matrix for nginx, envoy, and the customer's NetInspect X appliance.
Temporary: Customer exempted Redwood egress from TLS inspector rotations, reduced incidents to near-zero.
Short-term fix (runtime): emit resume-envelope with explicit control header resume-control:true so SDKs ignore in-rendering (PR runtime#1289).
Medium-term fix (edge): add guard to compute resume-offset based on runtime last-seen token; reject resume if offset mismatch > 4 tokens and trigger re-emit of missing fragments.
Follow-up: Add telemetry alert (resume-offset-delta) and include into Console per-route dashboard for Private deployments.
payload.summary: Half-closed SSE session: early FIN from corporate TLS inspector leads to reconnect that drops closing list items and duplicates system preface

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A NoteWave customer reported that long-running SSE streams sometimes arrive to the client with the entire final segment missing (last ~1-3 sentences) and the client enters a repeated backoff/reconnect loop. This reproduces when keepalive timing aligns with an LB-induced TLS rekey/priority change.

Impact:
- Several API calls from NoteWave produce truncated outputs for ~10-30s windows, causing user-facing partial responses and automated retry storms.
- Affected subset: persistent SSE sessions (>60s) that experience a midstream TLS session update via the edge load balancer.

Environment:
- prod, us-east-1 region, Redwood-hosted API via ALB -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime pool.
- Customer uses enterprise integration with sticky sessions enabled at their edge.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start a long generation SSE stream using redwood-open-11b-v1 with a document length target > 120 tokens.
2) Maintain the stream open and wait for LB keepalive probe/rotation to occur (approx 30-90s).
3) Observe client-side logs showing a sudden 1006/ECONNRESET followed by immediate reconnect attempts. The resumed stream lacks the final concluding sentences.

Observed behavior:
- Final JSON chunk or closing paragraph is absent on resumed stream.
- Client backoff loop (rapid reconnect attempts) sometimes amplifies the window of missing output.

Expected behavior:
- Stream should either gracefully deliver final chunk before connection handoff or resume with deterministic resume marker so client can reassemble without losing terminal content.

Attached artifacts: request IDs, timing traces, and small pcap snippet from customer capturing the TLS rekey handshake timing.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 17:45 - NoteWave Support (Customer): Confirming resolution in production for multiple long-running streams. Thank you.
Captured timelines (server and ALB): keepalive probe at t=43s, ALB initiates TLS ticket rotation between t=43.1-43.3s, server worker receives FIN at t=43.35s while ~2 terminal JSON chunks were still buffered.
Reproduced deterministically by simulating ALB rekey at various offsets; failure mode correlated with rekey occurring while runtime flush is in progress and before application-level end marker is emitted.
Observed that the runtime's socket-priority state machine flips to a 'handoff' mode without waiting for the streaming-terminator to complete when an out-of-band connection event occurs.
Client behavior: default SDK reconnect logic attempts immediate reconnects (no jitter) leading to small client-side retry storms; this increases probability of hitting a subsequent rekey window.
Metric evidence: spike in 'stream-abort' traces aligned with ALB ticket rotation events; no corresponding increase in 5xx errors from runtime (connection-level closes only).
Temporary mitigation attempted: applied a 200ms drain delay in canary to allow end-marker flush; reduced missing-final events to ~0.2% from ~6% in test harness.
Root cause: race between ALB/TLS session ticket rotation (connection-level) and runtime stream finalizer; insufficient flush ordering on handoff path.
Related logs: server_worker_20260308.log lines 3492-3510 include 'PRIORITY_FLIP' then 'HANDOFF_DRAIN_ABORTED'.
Root cause fixed by ensuring the serving runtime performs a synchronous stream terminator flush on handoff events and by delaying ALB connection reuse for 250ms when a streaming worker indicates a pending termination. Patch deployed to canary (us-east) on 2026-03-11 and rolled to prod on 2026-03-12. Additionally, client SDK recommended change: add exponential jitter to reconnect attempts to avoid retry storms during transient handoff windows.
Schedule in next sprint: add end-to-end test covering TLS rekey during streaming handoff (owner: Runtime Eng).
Add observability alert: if streaming-abort rate > 0.5% over 5m for a region, trigger an ops page (owner: SRE).
Update public docs: note recommended client SDK reconnect jitter settings for long-lived streams (owner: DevX).
payload.summary: Socket priority flip during keepalive rotation causes truncated final segment and client retry loop

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports progressive silence on long-completions followed by connection resets after ~90-150s. Not a single hard timeout: client sees long periods of zero bytes, then a reset. Impact: production traffic for ScribeAI (dedicated) degraded; several live sessions dropped mid-completion; customer revenue impact reported.

Observed behavior: Sessions begin normally, tokens stream for first N seconds. After a sustained period of activity with large trace/cookie headers added by the customer's sidecar, the API gateway begins deferring flushes (write hysteresis). This leads to longer gaps between bytes (TTFB increases gradually), eventually the ALB resets the connection with a 504/connection reset during KV cache warmup for subsequent requests.

Environment: prod us-east-1, Dedicated pool rdx-dedicated-us-east-3, affected model redwood/gpt-2.7b, client SDK v1.9.2, sidecar version scribe-sidecar v0.7.5.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Initiate long completion request from ScribeAI app against hosted Redwood endpoint pinned to redwood/gpt-2.7b.
2) Ensure request path includes their sidecar trace cookie and rotating metadata header that grows with each token (customer-provided telemetry).
3) Observe initial streaming output for ~20-40s.
4) After multiple completions in same HTTP connection, notice gaps in streaming output widen and eventually the connection resets during a subsequent warmup.

Logs & evidence:
- Grafana panel: latency/ttfb spike starting 2026-03-12T09:14:00Z for customer's pool (link redacted in ticket).
- ALB logs: multiple 504s and connection closed entries correlated to same client IPs between 09:16-09:30 UTC.
- API gateway trace: write_coalescing metrics show increased flush_hold_count and bytes_in_headers growth.
- Sample request headers captured: Cookie size ~18KB after several requests, custom-trace header ~6KB.
- Packet-level capture from a repro run attached to internal S3 (s3://redwood-support/sup-53124/pktcap.pcap).

Investigation notes / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Sidecar header growth pushes request/response headers beyond proxy fast-path thresholds, forcing additional buffering and triggering write hysteresis in APIGW, increasing TTFB and causing ALB idle/keepalive heuristics to reset long-lived streams.
- Hypothesis B: Proxy flush suppression (optimization to reduce small writes) interacts poorly with our streaming runtime's KV cache warmup, creating windows with no bytes sent while the runtime is busy handling warmup. The combination looks like client-side silence, leading to upstream LB resets.
- Initial triage: Reproduced in staging when artificially growing headers and enabling coalescing at the gateway. Lowering header size or disabling write coalescing prevented the stagnation.

Timeline / comments: [see comments below for thread].

Current impact and mitigation: Customer traffic degraded intermittently; we applied a temporary mitigation at 2026-03-12T12:40Z: reduced APIGW write_coalescing hold time for the customer's route and increased ALB idle timeout for the dedicated pool to 180s. This reduced occurrence but did not remove the root cause.

Workaround: Request the customer to limit rotating metadata headers and compress/trim telemetry cookies on long-lived connections. We provided SDK patch guidance to batch metadata off the main request path.

Proposed permanent fix options:
- Short term: adjust gateway write coalescing thresholds per-customer when header sizes exceed X bytes and mark streaming routes to use immediate flush semantics.
- Medium term: add active header-growth detection and automatic flush enforcement plus early KV cache pre-warm for routes with high header churn.
- Long term: runtime-level backpressure handling that sends keepalive-chunks when no token output is produced for >10s to avoid LB idle heuristics triggering resets.

Next steps:
1) Eng infra to evaluate risk of per-route coalescing changes (assigned to Liam O'Neill).
2) Engage SRE to instrument fast-path thresholds and add alerting for flush_hold_count > 50 per-minute.
3) Work with Customer Success to onboard ScribeAI on recommended SDK changes.
4) Track change in a follow-up INT ticket for gateway config rollout.

Resolution notes: TBD - mitigation reduced incidents but full fix requires gateway change.

2026-03-12 09:28 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reports repeated mid-stream silence -> connection reset. Collecting headers and request IDs. Asked for sample request IDs.
2026-03-12 10:03 - On-call SRE (Rakesh Patel): Confirmed ALB 504s correlated to customer's IP; attached raw ALB logs. Hypothesis: proxy coalescing + header bloat. Reproduced in staging by inflating headers.
2026-03-12 11:15 - Eng (Liam O'Neill): Ran quick repro and confirmed gateway's flush_hold_count spikes when cookie+trace headers exceed ~12KB. Lowering coalescing threshold removes gap. Preparing mitigation plan.
2026-03-12 12:42 - Support (Maya Chen): Applied temporary route-level config to lower write coalescing for ScribeAI routes and increased ALB idle timeout to 180s. Customer reports fewer drops in the next hour.
payload.summary: Proxy write hysteresis combined with growing sidecar headers causes gradual stream stagnation and eventual connection resets

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 responses across a subset of their bulk ingestion jobs. The jobs use HTTP/2 chunked uploads with many short-lived streams and aggressive client-side retries. Behavior appears correlated with high write concurrency and client retry amplification during transient backend slowness.

Impact:
- Several bulk indexing pipelines at AcmeSearch are failing intermittently, producing ~10-15% job failures across concurrent workers.
- Customer is on a dedicated pool; they report increased latency and 429 spikes on specific time windows (heavy ingest windows) which have impacted downstream search indexing SLA.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool (customer-managed reservation) in us-east-1
- Ingest path: client -> edge-proxy (http/2) -> api-gateway -> ingest-service -> model/embedding pipeline
- Keys used: short-lived upload keys created by customer's pre-signed workflow

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start 120 parallel upload workers, each opening a short-lived HTTP/2 stream that sends chunked parts (8-16 chunks/stream).
2) Simulate transient backend delay (sleep 400-800ms) for ~10% of chunk writes on ingest-service.
3) Clients retry failed chunk segments with immediate exponential backoff (start 100ms), resulting in bursty retry fanout.

Observed behavior:
- Edge-proxy logs show a pattern of many concurrent half-open streams and FIN frames arriving in quick succession during the retries.
- API gateway logs return 429s for a subset of requests; throttle headers are inconsistent across parallel streams for the same API key.
- Customer observes bulk job failures and multiple retries that increase total request volume, worsening the 429 rate.

Expected behavior:
- System should avoid counting transient retry amplification in a way that creates a positive feedback loop; short-lived streams and chunked retries should not push tenants over quota quickly when retries are reasonable.

Logs / evidence attached:
- Provided request IDs: req-20260310-7a9f, req-20260310-7aa0, req-20260310-7b02
- Edge-proxy trace links and sample snippets attached in attachments array.

Additional customer notes:
- They are using an SDK that aggressively retries chunk uploads on any non-2xx or connection reset.
- They prefer not to reduce concurrency below current levels because of indexing latency requirements.

2026-03-10 | Support (Maya Chen): Acknowledged receipt and escalated to SRE. Asked for full ingress logs, sample request IDs, and client's retry policy. Customer provided SDK version and sample trace. Assigned to Diego.
2026-03-11 | SRE (Diego Ramirez): Initial triage: observed bursty retry amplification in api-gateway metrics (per-key token depletion pattern). Added temporary token smoothing rule on the affected tenant to limit immediate retries. Requested packet captures from edge-proxy team for HTTP/2 windowing behavior.
2026-03-11 | Customer (AcmeSearch - infra): Confirmed temporary smoothing reduced immediate 429s but some bulk jobs still see sporadic failures. Shared a timeline where most 429s cluster immediately after a transient backend delay. Asked whether we can change counting semantics for chunked streams.
2026-03-12 | SRE (Diego Ramirez): Noted follow-up: disabling per-stream quota increment on chunked uploads reduced the positive feedback in staging. Planning controlled change for dedicated pool with canary on two nodes. Requesting PM/Prod approval for rollout window.
2026-03-12 | Support (Maya Chen): Informed customer of proposed canary and requested maintenance window for low-impact rollout.
Checked api-gateway token accounting: saw per-request token increment at stream open and per-chunk accounting on write completion — this double-counts when clients retry chunks, amplifying quota usage.
Edge-proxy HTTP/2 behavior: connection reuse is high; many short-lived streams cause window updates that sometimes race with the retry logic in client SDK.
Metric snapshots: per-key request-rate and token-balance graphs show sawtooth spikes matching customer's retry events (dashboards linked in confluence page).
Hypothesis: chunk-level accounting + immediate client retries cause retry amplification that is incorrectly attributed to tenant token usage without smoothing or retry dedupe, leading to transient 429s and a feedback loop.
Ran staging experiment: added a server-side short grace window (200ms) to coalesce chunk retries and applied per-connection smoothing; staging saw 60% reduction in 429s for same workload.
Related issues: SUP-71234 (early 429s during mass concurrent upload throughput spike) had similar symptoms but different root cause (burst window sizing).
Workaround (short-term): Applied tenant-level retry-smoothing and brief grace period for chunked writes on the customer's dedicated pool. Instructed customer to stagger worker startup by 500ms and to update SDK to use a slightly longer initial backoff (300ms) to avoid synchronized retries.
Planned fix (scheduled): Change token accounting model for chunked uploads so that retries within a 250ms debounce window are deduplicated at the api-gateway layer. Implement per-connection smoothing at edge-proxy to avoid counting half-open/aborted streams as full quota units.
Rollout plan: Canary rollout to 10% of dedicated pool nodes in us-east-1, monitor per-key throttle-header consistency and 429 rate for 24 hours. If stable, ramp to 100% over 72 hours. Rollout ticket to be created in infra backlog with PR link.
Follow-ups: update docs with recommended client SDK retry parameters for chunked uploads; add automated health-check to detect retry-amplification patterns and trigger adaptive smoothing. Owner: Diego Ramirez. ETA for fix: 2026-03-19.
Customer communicated acceptance of workaround and agreed to the canary window.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported that long-running SSE responses occasionally reattach to a previously closed conversation snapshot after a rapid client network migration. The resumed stream contains duplicated assistant preamble messages and the final JSON object is truncated (closing brace missing), causing client-side JSON.parse failures.

Impact:
- Customer-facing streaming sessions for AtlasDocs are intermittently producing invalid JSON payloads on reconnect (~0.8% of long streams observed for this customer).
- Clients see duplicate assistant system lines and then a JSONDecodeError when attempting to parse the final chunk; in their app this results in a visible truncated paragraph or missing final bullet items.

Environment:
- Customer environment: Dedicated tenant on prod us-east (vpc egress through transparent envoy sidecar).
- SDK/Client: atlasdocs-js v2.14.1 using EventSource (SSE) with automatic reconnect.
- Affected model: redwood-open-rlhf-v1, typical sequence length 1k-3k tokens.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Open SSE stream and request a ~2k token completion.
2) During generation, simulate rapid network migration (cellular -> wifi) or trigger a transparent proxy rebind on the client path (we reproduced using an envoy reconfigure / conn-rebind).
3) Client reconnects and sends resume request referencing last acknowledged offset.
4) Server resumes stream but emits an earlier assistant preamble and then continues; final JSON payload ends abruptly without the closing '}' or final newline.

Observed behaviour:
- Duplicate assistant preamble lines ("assistant: ... [system]" block) inserted immediately after resume.
- Final chunk truncated: last bytes end with '..."choices": [{"delta": {"content": "..."}}]' (missing closing brackets/braces).
- Client-side JSON.parse throws and client drops the last paragraph.

Expected behaviour:
- Resume should continue from the latest committed KV snapshot for the active session, not a stale snapshot.
- No duplicate system/assistant preamble. All emitted JSON objects must be well-formed and terminate with proper braces and delimiters.

Temporary workaround (customer):
- Increase client-side resume verification: if parse fails, fall back to re-request full non-streamed completion. Not ideal due to increased cost.
- Customer downgraded auto-reconnect to add a 300ms jitter which reduced reproduction frequency.

Logs / snippets:
- Worker logs (redacted):
  [2026-03-10T14:03:21Z] conn-id=ab12 rebind from 10.11.1.5 -> 10.23.4.1; session=atlas-72; kv-snap=2026-03-10T14:01:08Z
  [2026-03-10T14:03:21Z] resume-request offset=48712 last-ack=48712
  [2026-03-10T14:03:22Z] resume-applied snap=2026-03-09T23:58:12Z (stale)
  [2026-03-10T14:03:22Z] emit delta: assistant-preamble
  [2026-03-10T14:06:03Z] emit delta: final-chunk bytes=+512 truncated=true

Attached artifacts:
- customer-provided HAR of reconnect sequence, sample truncated payload, and SDK logs (attached to ticket).
(see Description steps)
Reproducer notes:
- We used a Vagrant VM + controlled iptables to force a TCP migrate and envoys rebind. Repro rate ~40% under our test harness when forcing immediate client reconnect. Adding a 200-500ms client jitter reduced repro to <5%.
Initial hypothesis: race between conn-migration resume path and KV snapshot selection.
Findings so far:
- Worker logs show resume applied snapshot timestamp earlier than last-ack (snap=2026-03-09T23:58:12Z vs last-ack 2026-03-10T14:01:08Z) indicating stale snapshot selection during reattach.
- Edge-proxy (envoy) conn-handoff flow injects a rebind marker that our session-router treats as a new attach and occasionally performs a cold snapshot lookup instead of using in-memory committed offsets.
- The serving runtime will stream deltas taken from the snapshot; if the snapshot is stale, the preamble is emitted and token stream overlaps the previously delivered tokens.
- Truncated final chunk appears correlated with worker process performing an async flush while the resume was using a different buffer length; we saw an off-by-one length calculation in the delta-chunkizer for resumed streams (offending code path in runtime chunker module).

Next steps planned:
1) Add guard to session-router to prefer in-process committed offset if available when handling conn-handoff resume. (PR planned to edge-proxy/session-router boundary)
2) Add validation on emitted final JSON chunk to ensure object termination; if termination fails, trigger automatic re-emit of closing bytes or mark stream as failed and instruct client to retry.
3) Add targeted integration test simulating rapid conn migration with envoy rebind.
4) Coordinate with AtlasDocs to test patch in staging dedicated tenant.

Related artifacts:
- Replay trace id: trace-20260310-AL72
- Internal runbook referenced: SSE Handoff Runbook (see related_confluence_pages)

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 16:12 - AtlasDocs (customer): Confirmed workaround applied (client jitter) reduced frequency but still impacts some mobile users. Requested ETA for permanent fix and whether there will be a hotfix for dedicated tenants.
payload.summary: Rapid connection migration resumes stale SSE snapshot: missing closing JSON brace and repeated assistant preamble

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden surge of 429 responses for interactive traffic after performing a subaccount merge via the Console UI. Console showed the merged subaccount's quota as '0 / 0' (reset) for ~20 minutes while requests were being rejected with 429. This is confusing for the customer because the billing/usage dashboard later reported quota available and there was an apparent mismatch between control-plane display and data-plane enforcement.

Impact:
- PulseMetrics experienced ~18 minutes of elevated 429 errors affecting webhooks and real-time SSE clients (~30% of production traffic).
- Customer-facing dashboards showed quota reset to zero leading to an incident escalation to their SREs.

Observed behavior:
- Console shows quota as 0 immediately after merge.
- API returns 429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset headers that appear inconsistent across edge nodes.
- Backend token-bucket snapshots indicate tokens still present on origin, but edge caches returned a local 'exhausted' decision.

Expected behavior:
- Console should reflect an accurate post-merge quota state quickly (within the usual UI refresh window).
- Rate-limiter decisions should be consistent across edge and origin during merge operations and not produce opaque 429s for requests that should be allowed immediately after quota transfer.

1) Create two subaccounts A and B with non-zero burst credits in prod-us-east.
2) From Console, merge B into A using bulk-merge flow (subaccount transfer + quota reconciliation).
3) Immediately start concurrent SSE and webhook traffic that previously consumed B's burst credits.
4) Observe Console quota widget, API responses, and edge logs for 429s and rate-limit headers.
edge-proxy logs (example): 2026-03-13T16:02:18Z decision=REJECT reason=local_bucket_empty scope=subaccount id=subacct-9876 trace=trace-abc123
rate-limiter origin snapshot: subacct-9876 tokens=420 refill_ts=2026-03-13T16:02:10Z
console backend audit: merge-job=job-20260313-55 state=applied quota_transfer=+500burst
X-RateLimit headers observed from customer: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 2026-03-13T16:04:00Z

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 09:12 - Support (Aisha): Customer accepted workaround; provided instructions to toggle dedicated-burst-pool on merged route to bypass edge-local checks temporarily. Customer confirmed error rate dropped to normal.
Hypothesis: Merge job applies control-plane changes but does not actively invalidate edge-local rate-limiter caches. Edge nodes continue enforcing old local buckets until their TTL or a background refresh occurs, producing sticky 429s.
Observed that merge job emits 'quota_delta' event on topic 'control.quota.updates' but edge nodes listen to 'control.quota.cache' which is updated by a separate reconciliation pipeline with a 20-40s delay.
Found related race condition when merge occurs during peak refill epoch boundary; nodes compute local windows that cross over and round down to 0 for short interval.
Replayed merge in staging with increased cache invalidation and saw immediate consistency—edge rejects disappeared in <2s.
Workaround provided: advised customer to enable temporary dedicated burst pool on merged routes (steps shared) to bypass edge-local enforcement while we deploy the fix. Implementation fix: rate-limiter team will add explicit cache-invalidation event publish after subaccount merge and shorten the reconciliation TTL from 30s to 5s for quota updates. Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/482. Rollout plan: canary to us-east edge tier 1 tomorrow 03/15, global rollout over 24 hours. Post-deploy validation: run merged-subaccount merge replay job and monitor 429 rate and X-RateLimit headers. Follow-up: add metric to track 'quota-update-lag-ms' and an alert if >5000ms.
payload.summary: Misleading console quota reset after subaccount merge leading to opaque 429s

Issue summary:
Evening (2026-03-10 18:40 UTC) we observed a multi-tenant spike of 5xx responses originating at the API gateway with upstream runtime restarts and degraded throughput. Symptoms started after a staged model update for a dedicated customer; traffic for a subset of streaming routes was elevated and long-lived.

Impact:
- Multiple dedicated tenants experienced increased 502/503/504 rates for streaming and short-response routes for ~45 minutes.
- Observed request-level timeouts and degraded tail latency for inference.
- BrightForms Inc. (dedicated) reported failed streaming sessions and partial tokenization errors; business impact reported as user-facing failures.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (us-east-1)
- API gateway v2.1.8 (Nginx-proxy + internal prioritizer)
- Serving runtime release: runtime-2026-03-08-rc3 with prefetch changes
- Affected models: vicuna-13b-q4_0 (customer pinned), opt-6.7b-q4 (fallback pool)

Steps to reproduce (internal test harness):
1) Open ~3k concurrent streaming sessions with `x-priority-window: high` header and client keepalive every 10s.
2) Ensure ~1:20 ratio of long-lived streaming to short RPCs on same tenant route.
3) Trigger model reload on a subset of backends to simulate rollout.
4) Observe apigw accept queue, runtime threadpool, and prefetch metrics.

Observed logs / telemetry snippets:
- apigw metrics: accept-queue length spiked to 18k, accept-queue-accept-ratio dropped to 0.12 for low-priority routes.
- apigw error stream: "upstream prematurely closed connection (502)" repeated during accept-queue peak.
- runtime logs: repeated "worker-thread-starvation: waiting-for-pool" and then "watchdog: runtime-cold-reset" followed by OOM-like eviction messages.
- kvcache churn: eviction rate 9x baseline during spike.
- autoscaler: did not scale quickly due to burst detection thresholds (min-grace 90s).

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Temporarily capped per-tenant concurrent streaming sessions for BrightForms to 500 (apigw policy).
- Applied emergency ingress rule to prioritize keepalive ACKs and avoid long-lived connection hold on accept queue.
- Increased runtime threadpool soft-limit from 128 -> 192 for the affected pool to reduce backlog.

Current impact and status:
- Error rate reduced to baseline levels within 18 minutes of mitigation; downstream runtime restarts reduced.
- Customers still see intermittent reconnects; monitoring in place.
- Ticket escalated to Serving Runtime SRE for root cause analysis and longer-term fix.

Hypothesis 1: Priority-window logic in apigw is causing accept-queue unfairness when long-lived streaming sessions dominate, starving the worker threads that handle short RPCs and healthchecks. Evidence: accept-ratio collapse for non-priority routes and high keepalive hold time.
Hypothesis 2: Prefetch changes in runtime-2026-03-08-rc3 combined with increased kvcache churn amplified memory pressure and triggered watchdog resets. Evidence: kvcache eviction spike correlating with runtime reset timestamps.
Actions taken so far:
- Pulled logs and timeline from Kibana/grafana: panels apigw/accept-queue, runtime/threadpool, runtime/prefetch-evictions. Links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pg/accept-queue?from=2026-03-10T18:00:00Z&to=2026-03-10T19:00:00Z
- Replayed traffic in canary cluster reproducing accept-queue imbalance.
- Rolled back runtime-2026-03-08-rc3 on two canary nodes to observe changes; rollback shows drop in eviction rate.
- Opened PR to add backpressure guard in apigw prioritizer (see related PR).

Follow-ups planned:
- Instrument priority-window sliding algorithm for fairness metrics (owner: scheduler team).
- Tweak autoscaler burst detection to allow faster ephemeral scale-up for streaming long-tail (owner: autoscaler).
- Add kvcache throttling/async-eviction on prefetch hot paths (owner: runtime).
2026-03-10 19:02 UTC - Support (Ava): Initial triage: spike started ~18:40 UTC, raising to SRE. Actioned temporary stream cap and ingress rule. Notified customer BrightForms support contact.
2026-03-10 19:30 UTC - SRE (Ravi): Applied threadpool soft-limit bump and cap on per-tenant streams; monitoring shows error rate falling. Collecting detailed runtime stacks for resets.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 08:00 UTC - Support (Ava): Customer BrightForms confirmed reduced failures after mitigations; they requested a postmortem and timeline for permanent fixes.
Mitigations applied: per-tenant stream cap, ingress rule to favor keepalive ACKs, threadpool soft-limit increase. Root cause investigation in progress. Next steps: implement priority-window fairness guard in apigw, add kvcache prefetch throttles, and adjust autoscaler burst sensitivity. Planned owner reviews scheduled this week.
payload.summary: Evening 5xx surge: ingress priority-window imbalance leading to runtime thread starvation and proxy 502s

comments: 2026-03-05T09:12:00Z Asha Patel: Customer reported high P95 on calls to /v1/generate; attached sample traces and SDK logs. They see ~2-3x baseline P95 bursts and intermittent request errors from the client. Asked for request ids and pool details.

2026-03-05T10:01:00Z Marco Hernandez: Collected gateway metrics and CPU on dedicated hosts. Serving runtime shows consistent per-request token times. No obvious backend queueing. Requested tcpdump from customer and SDK config (keepalive, maxSockets, retry settings).

2026-03-06T08:46:00Z Marco Hernandez: Reproduced locally with their config. Observed that when retries back off and sockets are reused aggressively, client threads block waiting for socket availability. With maxSockets low and long keepalive, the SDK queues requests locally rather than opening new sockets due to ephemeral port exhaustion and TIME_WAIT growth from churn. Not a server-side backlog.

2026-03-09T15:20:00Z Marco Hernandez: Deployed mitigation to customer: recommended immediate client-side changes: set maxSockets=50, reduce keepAliveMsecs to 10000, lower initial retry delay to 100ms and cap maxRetries to 3. After these changes, customer reports P95 returned to baseline and no further client-side timeouts.

2026-03-10T10:05:00Z Mei Chen: Released Node SDK 3.2.5 with adaptive jitter and safer defaults; added explicit guidance to docs for connection pooling under high concurrency. Python SDK release planned next week.
2026-03-10T10:20:00Z Asha Patel: Marking as resolved. Follow-up task created to add a troubleshooting guide to Console KB and include recommended pool defaults in quickstart templates.
payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent spikes in end-to-end inference P95 latency (and some client-side request timeouts) beginning 2026-03-04. PineApps is on Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 and uses our official Node + Python SDKs. Impact: user-facing feature slowdown and sporadic 504-like timeouts from SDKs. Environment: prod (dedicated pool ID: ded-32-a), client SDK versions node 3.2.1, python 2.9.0. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run sustained bursty traffic from multiple client instances (50-200 concurrent connections) with short TTL per request, 2) Observe elevated client-side latency P95 and occasional SDK timeouts while server-side RT metrics (token generation time) remain normal. Logs/observations: SDK logs show repeated connection resets and retry backoff chains. Kernel traces on customer's side show many sockets in TIME_WAIT with keepalive probes. API gateway metrics: increased connection churn but stable generation latency on the serving runtime. Initial mitigation: recommended SDK version pin to latest (where we've changed default retry delays) and increased client-side connection pool size as a temporary workaround.

Additional notes:
2026-03-05 14:28 - PineApps (Customer): Attached tcpdump and SDK config. Node SDK set maxSockets=6, keepAlive=true, keepAliveMsecs=60000, retry policy: exponential with initialDelay=200ms, maxRetries=6. Multiple app instances behind a load balancer.
2026-03-07 11:02 - Eng (SDK team) - Mei Chen: Confirmed Node SDK prior to 3.2.5 had a bug where exponential backoff jitter was too conservative combined with agent keepalive behavior. Opened PR to change default maxSockets and add adaptive backoff jitter. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rumble/pull/456
2026-03-10 09:41 - PineApps (Customer): Confirmed fix holds under load tests (up to 500 RPS sustained). Happy to keep Dedicated pool but requested a formal SDK patch and release notes so their ops can update confidently.
Observed discrepancy between client perceived latency and backend token-generation time. Server-side P95 for generation stayed within SLOs while client-side P95 spiked.
Packet captures from customer showed many short-lived TCP connections and high TIME_WAIT counts; connection churn increased under bursts.
Customer's SDK maxSockets was low (6) which, combined with aggressive retry attempts, caused local queueing in the SDK when sockets were briefly unavailable.
Keepalive with long intervals meant idle sockets persisted, preventing ephemeral port reuse and causing the client to open/close sockets more frequently when pool size was exceeded.
Reproduction notes: With a synthetic client mimicking customer's concurrency and original SDK config, reproduces increased client-side P95 within ~10 minutes of sustained bursts. After changing pool/defaults reproduction stops.
Root cause: Interaction of conservative retry/backoff config + small connection pool + long TCP keepalive => client-side request queueing and exponential backoff retries that multiplied perceived latency. Secondary factor: some customer app instances had periodic restarts causing ephemeral port churn.
Server-side mitigations were unnecessary; issue fixed by SDK defaults and customer config changes. Confirmed no resource leaks in serving runtime.
Related symptoms: similar pattern referenced in SUP-12903 and SUP-8419 but root cause here was adaptive jitter + pool sizing rather than server throttling.
Root cause: misaligned client SDK defaults (small maxSockets, long keepalive, conservative retry backoff) causing local queueing and perceived latency increases. Resolution delivered: 1) Customer applied immediate config workaround (increase maxSockets, reduce keepAliveMsecs, cap retries). 2) Node SDK 3.2.5 released with adaptive backoff jitter and updated default pool sizes. 3) Added KB entry and Console quickstart note with recommended SDK connection-pool and retry settings for Dedicated pools. 4) Follow-up: Python SDK patch scheduled and outreach to all Dedicated customers about recommended SDK tuning. No server-side change required.
payload.summary: Aggressive SDK retry + socket reuse interacting with keepalive causing client-side queueing and elevated P95 latency

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports SIEM-ready audit export (Datadog destination) failing with HTTP 403 responses from Datadog Logs intake.

Impact
- Audit events are not being delivered to Datadog for Helio Health’s beta validation window.
- Customer cannot complete their security validation checklist until events appear in Datadog.

Customer context
- Helio Health (Enterprise). Using Datadog Logs for centralized audit collection.
- Beta feature: SIEM-ready audit export.

Environment
- Redwood: Hosted/Dedicated control plane; exporter running in prod (us-east).
- Destination: Datadog Logs intake.

What we saw (symptoms)
- Exporter adapter reports repeated 403s; retries occur but do not succeed.
- Export lag increases; destination health shows “Auth/permission error”.

Steps to reproduce (from customer)
1) In Redwood Console -> Audit Export -> Add destination -> Datadog.
2) Provide Datadog site = “us1” (datadoghq.com) and API key (redacted).
3) Enable export; within ~1–2 minutes destination health shows failures.

Relevant logs (redacted)
- 2025-04-18T16:22:41Z audit-exporter datadog_adapter request failed status=403 path=/v1/input error="Forbidden" dd_body="{\"errors\":[\"API key is not authorized to submit logs\"]}" tenant=*** dest_id=dd-***
- Note: customer only provided last-4 of key in ticket; full key not captured/stored by Support.

Investigation notes
- Initial hypothesis: wrong Datadog site (us1 vs eu1) or invalid key.
- Verified destination configured for datadoghq.com (us1). Customer confirmed their Datadog org is us1.
- Exporter uses Datadog Logs intake endpoint; 403 indicates key rejected at intake rather than network/TLS.
- Customer confirmed the key works for metrics API in another integration, but logs intake still 403.
- Eng (Logan/Caleb) noted Datadog now supports scoped API keys; if the key is restricted (missing logs ingestion/write scope) intake returns 403.
- Customer checked Datadog UI and confirmed the key was created as a restricted/scoped key intended for API usage, not log submission.

Root cause
- Datadog API key provided to Redwood was scoped/restricted and did not include the permission/scope to submit logs to the Logs intake endpoint, causing Datadog to return 403 Forbidden.

Resolution / recommended remediation (customer-facing)
1) In Datadog, create a new API key that is allowed to submit logs (unrestricted, or explicitly including the Logs ingestion/write scope).
2) Update the Redwood Datadog destination to use the new key.
3) Wait ~2–5 minutes and confirm:
   - Destination health in Redwood Console shows “Healthy”.
   - Audit events appear in Datadog Logs (search by service/source tags used by Redwood; see notes in comments).

Verification
- After customer rotated to a new (unrestricted) API key, exporter status transitioned to Healthy.
- Customer confirmed logs appear in Datadog (sample events: audit categories = authz, workspace, api_key).

Notes / improvements
- Current UI/error messaging shows generic 403; we should surface a clearer hint: “Datadog API key is not authorized for Logs intake (check API key scopes / logs ingestion permission / site).”
- Support guidance: do not request or paste full API keys in Jira; use secure channel if absolutely necessary; last-4 only.

Next steps
- Support: close ticket once customer confirms stable delivery for 24h.
- Product/Eng follow-up: improve docs + Console validation error message for 403 responses from Datadog intake (scope/permission guidance).
2025-04-18 16:11 (Miguel Santos): Customer (Helio Health) reports Datadog destination failing. Console shows repeated delivery failures, last error “403 Forbidden”. They are blocked on beta validation. Requesting Eng eyes on what 403 typically means for Datadog intake.
2025-04-18 16:26 (Colin O'Donnell): Taking. Can someone confirm whether this is site mismatch (datadoghq.com vs datadoghq.eu) or a key issue? Miguel—please ask customer which Datadog site/org they’re on and whether the key is newly created/scoped.
2025-04-18 16:44 (Miguel Santos): Customer confirmed Datadog site is us1 (datadoghq.com). Key was created by their security team recently; they mentioned they were trying to follow least-privilege and “restricted it to what’s needed.” They assumed logs intake uses same key permissions as other integrations.
2025-04-18 17:02 (Caleb Johnson): Datadog introduced scoped API keys; logs submission can 403 if key doesn’t include logs ingestion/write. Suggest creating an unscoped/unrestricted API key as a test. If that works, it’s definitely key scoping.
2025-04-18 17:19 (Colin O'Donnell): Agree. I’ll send customer steps: generate new API key in Datadog with logs write/ingest allowed, then rotate in Redwood destination. Also remind them to avoid pasting the key in this ticket—last-4 only.
2025-04-19 09:14 (Miguel Santos): Customer rotated to a new key (unrestricted) and updated Redwood destination. Export health flipped to Healthy in ~3 minutes. They can see new events in Datadog Logs. They asked how to filter quickly; I suggested searching by tags and sourcetype/source used by Redwood (I told them to look for “redwood” source/service).
2025-04-19 10:03 (Colin O'Donnell): Great. Marking resolved. Follow-up: our 403 surface is too generic; we should add a hint for scoped-key failures and a docs snippet under Datadog destination setup.
2025-04-20 13:27 (Miguel Santos): Customer confirms delivery stable through weekend test window (no further 403s). Closing.

payload.description:
## Issue summary
Vertex Legaltech reports audit log records are arriving >30 minutes late in eu-west. Customer is using audit logs for compliance monitoring + SIEM ingestion; late delivery causes their ingestion job to flag missing events and triggers internal alerts.

## Impact
- Customer-facing: perceived missing audit events for ~30–60 minutes, later backfilled.
- Business/compliance: enterprise account; security team expects near-real-time visibility and is escalating internally.

## Customer-reported symptoms
- "Audit log export shows gaps for the last ~45 minutes; older records appear eventually."
- Ingestion job errors when expected window is empty; retries increase.

## Environment
- Tier: Enterprise
- Region: eu-west
- Product area: Audit logs delivery pipeline

## What we need to confirm
A) Redwood audit log delivery pipeline backlog (queue/consumer lag), vs
B) customer-side ingestion assumptions (polling window too tight, lack of overlap/dedupe), vs
C) downstream sink throttling.

## Initial investigation (Support)
- Requested:
  - exact time range of observed lag
  - example event timestamp vs delivery timestamp
  - destination type (pull job cadence + lookback window)
- Checked internal metrics (Grafana → Audit Logs → Pipeline Health):
  - `auditlog_delivery_lag_seconds` elevated (p95 peaked ~2,700s) in eu-west
  - queue depth increasing then draining in sawtooth pattern
  - delivery error rate low (symptom consistent with backlog/consumer lag vs drops)

## Customer-safe mitigation (approved)
- Recommend widening polling/export window with overlap + dedupe by event ID.
  - Suggested: run every 5 minutes, pull last 60 minutes with overlap; dedupe.
- Recommend exponential backoff + jitter for retries.
- Avoid aggressive backfill loops that hammer small time slices.

## Escalation / workstream
- Paged SRE to confirm backlog and ETA to drain.
- Follow-up engineering work: add first-class audit log lag metric + alert thresholds aligned to enterprise expectations (ENG-4824).

Additional notes:
SRE confirmed audit log delivery pipeline backlog in eu-west; backlog drained and delivery latency returned to baseline by 2026-02-11. Support provided temporary mitigation (widen export/polling window with overlap + dedupe; retries with backoff). Follow-up engineering work opened to add first-class lag metrics/alerts and dashboards aligned to enterprise expectations (ENG-4824; observability-pack/pr-711).
ENG-4824: add audit log lag metric + alert thresholds; link runbook and Support-safe dashboard view
Update Support macros/snippets to include the overlap + dedupe guidance for audit log lag
Ensure status-page vs direct comms guidance is followed for any future region-wide lag events

Issue summary:
Customers on Dedicated in us-east (ChorusAI) reported intermittent p95/p99 spikes for short streaming requests after sessions resume from brief idle windows. Spikes started 2026-03-09 ~18:00 UTC and correlate with many short streams (single-turn prompts) that reconnect quickly.

Impact:
- Multiple production tenants observed p99 jump from ~120ms to 800-1200ms for short streaming requests.
- Client-side timeouts increased; several 504s reported by customer.
- Affects user-facing product features (chat quick-reply) for ChorusAI customers on dedicated capacity.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (us-east), serving runtime v2.8.3, continuous-batcher enabled with adaptive_linger and priority_decay settings.
- Traffic pattern: many short-lived streaming connections with pauses of 200-800ms between messages.

Steps to reproduce (customer recipe):
1) Open 200 short streaming connections at 10r/s total QPS, each sends a 10-token prompt then pauses 400ms and resumes.
2) Observe latency distribution using the request_id returned by the streaming handshake.
3) Reproduce with model gpt-small-v1 pinned.

Observed behavior:
- p95 and p99 increase in bursts when many streams resume concurrently.
- Traces show linger window decisions expanding for resumed connections (linger accrued to >120ms) before flush.
- KV-cache hits are high; not a cold-cache symptom.

Expected behavior:
- Short resume bursts should be flushed promptly, maintaining p95/p99 within baseline.

Logs & dashboards (examples):
- Metrics: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/continuous/batcher?orgId=1&from=now-6h&to=now
- Trace example: trace-id=3a8f7b2d (attached in upload)
- Sample worker log excerpt: "[batcher] adaptive_linger_ms adjusted from 12 -> 96 for tenant=chorusai request=..."

Initial hypothesis:
Adaptive linger algorithm plus priority_decay interacts poorly with stream-resume patterns. When a connection resumes after a short idle, the algorithm temporarily increases its linger estimate to favor coalescing; concurrent resumes create a feedback loop where linger amplifies across microbatches, causing delayed flushes and p99 spikes. Throttling/backpressure and per-connection rate smoothing exacerbate the effect.

2026-03-10 19:05 - Support (Asha Patel): Customer reported spike; triaged and requested traces + representative traffic replay.
2026-03-10 20:12 - ChorusAI (CS contact - Jordan Blake): Attached replay script and sample trace-ids. Impacting chat quick-replies in production.
2026-03-10 21:30 - SRE (Riley Chen): Reproduced locally with replay; confirmed linger growth on resume paths. Opening investigation. Linked infra dashboards.
2026-03-11 02:05 - Eng (Priya Singh): Profiled batcher decision path. Observed priority_decay_ms set to 3000ms and adaptive_linger_ms oscillation. Hypothesis: priority decay keeps resumed streams in a low-priority bucket causing them to wait longer for batch alignment.
2026-03-11 09:40 - Eng (Riley Chen): Deployed temporary mitigation: enforce max_linger_ms=30 for streaming routes in us-east. Customer reports reduction in p99 a few minutes after rollout.
2026-03-11 12:20 - ChorusAI (Jordan Blake): Confirmed mitigated impact; user-facing errors decreased from 2.1% to 0.2% during the observed window. Asked for a permanent fix and config recommendations.
2026-03-12 08:15 - Eng (Priya Singh): Preparing PR with improved adaptive_linger heuristic that decays linger estimates faster on resume and caps amplification across tenant bursts. PR: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2410
Reproduction: traffic replay with 200 concurrent short streams reproduced p99 from 130ms -> 1.1s in ~6 minutes.
Trace analysis: worker flush times increased; microbatch sizes were slightly larger than normal but not enough to justify the added latency.
Batcher config: adaptive_linger_enabled=true, adaptive_linger_base_ms=8, adaptive_linger_max_ms=200, priority_decay_ms=3000.
Root cause theory: adaptive algorithm increases linger when it detects repeated short pauses; priority_decay keeps resumed streams in lower scheduling priority long enough for their linger to compound across multiple resume cycles. When many streams resume concurrently the batcher amplifies the window to maximize coalescing, but this creates tail latency for short requests.
Additional contributing factors: per-connection token pacing and RPC backpressure signals delayed early flushes for streams resuming mid-window.
Temporary mitigation validated: setting max_linger_ms=30 and reducing priority_decay_ms to 800ms for streaming routes restored p99 to ~150-170ms under replay.
Telemetry: added a new gauge 'batcher.linger_amplification' to track how often adaptive_linger increases >4x over base for a tenant.
Related issues reviewed: SUP-93177 (staggered flush resonance) - similar amplification phenomenon but different trigger; SUP-9023 (idle threshold drift) - useful patterns for detection.
Workaround and permanent fix deployed. Workaround: applied configuration change in us-east dedicated pool on 2026-03-11 02:05 UTC - max_linger_ms enforced at 30ms and priority_decay_ms set to 800ms for streaming routes; customer confirmed reduction in errors. Permanent fix: merged PR github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2410 which implements a resume-aware adaptive_linger decay and global amplification cap. Rollout timeline: canary 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC -> regional rollout us-east 2026-03-12 05:00 UTC -> global 2026-03-13 01:00 UTC. Post-deploy monitoring shows p99 back to baseline for replay tests. Follow-up: add automated alert when batcher.linger_amplification > 0.05 for 5m and document recommended batcher config for dedicated streaming tenants in Confluence runbook. Closing notes: keep issue open for 72h of steady-state monitoring before final close.

Issue summary: Customers reported that long streaming responses (SSE and websocket) occasionally finish with a trailing ellipsis (...) and then, after the client reconnect/resume, a duplicated final clause or sentence is appended. Impact: user-visible duplicated suffix or hanging punctuation in final output that confuses downstream post-processing and fails strict JSON validators for structured responses. Observed with enterprise customer behind an aggressive corporate proxy and mobile webview clients.
1) Start a long multi-paragraph generation request using the streaming endpoint for redwood/ggml-7b-chat with temperature=0.7 and max_tokens=800.
2) Let stream emit for ~20–40s until the model returns the closing paragraph and likely a final punctuation mark.
3) Trigger a transient network change on the client (corporate proxy rebind or mobile network suspend) causing a keepalive gap of ~12–18s.
4) Client reconnects and sends resume token / session id; server emits remaining fragments and occasionally emits a duplicate of the last sentence or an extra ellipsis then duplicate suffix.
5) Reproduces reliably behind Acme Payments' corp-proxy which has an idle-teardown of 10s when reauthenticating.

2026-03-10T14:02:11Z TRACE session=abc123 client=10.5.4.3 keepalive=22s last_chunk='...'
2026-03-10T14:02:23Z WARN proxy=corp-edge rebind token-refresh teardown idle=10s connection-rst
2026-03-10T14:02:34Z INFO resume received session=abc123 resume_token=rt-789 trace_id=tx-5543
2026-03-10T14:02:34Z DEBUG serving-runtime choice-emit chunk_id=457 last_choice='final clause.'
2026-03-10T14:02:34Z DEBUG serving-runtime choice-emit chunk_id=458 duplicate_of=457 'final clause.'
2026-03-10T14:02:34Z ERROR parser detected unexpected trailing '...final clause.' in stream (tx-5543)
Links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/tx-5543 , Slack: #support-acme-payments-thread/ABCD1234
Initial triage (Support): confirmed multiple occurrences from same customer in us-east over 3 distinct days. Pattern: short-lived network gaps of ~10–20s followed by resume, duplicates only on longest streams.
Hypothesis A: KV-cache re-priming race where resumed worker replays buffered tail while prior worker also emits trailing fragment (double-emit).
Hypothesis B: Edge-proxy keepalive extension mismatch causes client to receive a heartbeat-only chunk (ellipsis) interpreted by SDK as content, then resumed content appended leading to duplication.
SRE reproduction: simulated proxy-teardown at 10s while streaming long responses; reproduced duplicate tail when proxy dropped connection and resume routed request to a different worker with overlapping session state.
Trace analysis: tx-5543 shows two downstream emits (chunk 457 and chunk 458) with same choice payload and consecutive sequence ids; both workers reported chunk emission for same session id due to race on resume-claim.
Root cause narrowed: race during resume claim across serving nodes when proxy rebind causes an ephemeral reconnect; resume path allowed a second worker to re-emit cached tail before exclusive resume-claim was fully reconciled in the control plane.
Customer environment note: Acme's corp-proxy performs TLS re-termination + 401 reauth flow which triggers connection close and immediate reconnects; their idle-teardown (10s) is shorter than our resume-claim lock timeout in some code paths.
Repro notes: duplication more likely when final chunk is small (ellipsis or short clause) because the SDK merges heartbeat-like fragments into content and treats them as partials.
Customer (2026-03-10T14:05Z) - Jordan L.: We're seeing truncated outputs followed by a weird repeated sentence when the user switches networks. It's intermittent but painful for downstream JSON parsing.
Support (2026-03-10T14:18Z) - Maya C.: Thanks Jordan — collecting logs, can you confirm whether clients are behind an edge proxy or using an SDK? Any screenshots of the duplicated text would help.
Customer (2026-03-10T14:22Z) - Jordan L.: They are behind a corporate TLS reauth proxy. Using in-house webview. Provided live request-id tx-5543.
SRE (2026-03-10T15:05Z) - Diego A.: Able to reproduce with proxy teardown @10s. Suspect resume-claim race on workers. Creating follow-up INT ticket for fix rollout. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1124
SRE (2026-03-11T09:40Z) - Diego A.: Deployed hotfix behind feature flag: enforce single-resume-claim via optimistic lock + short garbage-collection window for session tails. Enabled for us-east canary at 09:30 UTC.
Customer (2026-03-11T11:12Z) - Jordan L.: Verified on our side — duplicate tail no longer observed in 30+ test runs. Thanks!
Support (2026-03-12T08:00Z) - Maya C.: Closing ticket after monitoring 48h of no regressions. Follow-up: recommend customers behind aggressive proxies increase idle timeout or enable resume-delay client-side backoff.

Root cause: race condition in session resume where two workers could emit a cached trailing fragment when corporate proxy rebind closes the original socket. Fix: added an optimistic resume-claim lock in the control plane and tightened the session tail GC window; also added defensive de-duplication in the serving runtime for back-to-back identical tail emits. Rollout: hotfix canary in us-east on 2026-03-11 09:30 UTC, global rollout completed 2026-03-11 18:00 UTC. Customer instructed to adjust proxy idle teardown to >15s or enable client resume backoff as mitigation. Monitoring: alert created stream-resume-duplicate-rate >0.1% per minute with dashboard link.

Issue summary: During a customer-triggered concurrency increase (tenant scale-up) for Cortexa Labs' dedicated pool, they observed a sustained rise in 5xx responses from the public API and frequent streaming session disconnects. Impact: multiple generation requests returned 502/503 and long-lived streaming sessions dropped mid-response, causing user-visible failures in Cortexa's chat UI and automated ingestion pipelines. - API gateway 502/503 rate climbs from baseline ~0.2% to 8-12% during ramp.
- Streaming connections see half-close/h2 stream errors and client resets.
- Serving runtime shows worker preemption and repeated model load/unload cycles.
- TLS session cache invalidation spikes, resulting in handshake backlog at proxy layer.

Hypothesis: combination of (a) concurrency ramp, (b) autoscaler consolidation policy, and (c) TLS session eviction limits produced a feedback loop that amplified 5xx. 2) Engineering to add soft-stall for TLS session cache eviction during tenant warmup.

Issue summary:
During the customer evening peak (approx 19:00-20:15 UTC) Textly.ai observed repeated P99 throughput regressions for routes pinned to their dedicated pool. Symptoms included elevated request queueing, autoscaler throttles (rate-limit style rejection of new GPU allocations), and a short-lived shortage of free GPU slots that recovered after ~8-10 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency p99 increased from ~180ms to 1.2s for generation routes for ~35% of requests during the window.
- A subset of small, high-concurrency streams experienced preemptive queuing and a spike in 503s when allocation throttles triggered.
- Business impact: degraded UX for Textly.ai paying customers (estimated 1.2k affected requests in window).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-textly-prod-us-east (configured min_replicas=2, max_replicas=10, burst_capacity=2)
- Region: us-east-1
- Models: redwood-v2-large (primary), fallback to open-llama-13B for cost-tier routes
- Autoscaler: adaptive-burst (policy version 2026-02-18)

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) High rate of short-lived concurrent streams from customer traffic (many requests <200 tokens, duration <2s) starting 19:03 UTC.
2) Autoscaler began requesting new GPU allocation for additional slots; allocation requests hit quota soft-limit enforced by internal allocator for the dedicated pool.
3) Allocator returned throttled responses for ~6 minutes; requests were queued locally in the router.
4) Some queued requests exceeded route timeouts and returned 503/504.
5) Once some longer-running background workloads finished or preempted, allocations succeeded and queue drained by 19:11 UTC.

Observed logs and metrics (snippet):
- metrics/autoscaler/alloc_retries: spike from 3->47 in 3 minutes
- allocator/errors: rate_limit_exceeded (internal quota) 78 events between 19:04-19:08 UTC
- serving/runtime/gpu_util: per-GPU 92-98% during peak, but slot free-count reported transiently 0/64 for 7 minutes
- router/queue_length: p95 from 2 -> 18 requests
- customer reported 503s correlated with allocator throttle timestamps (see attached traces).

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should either succeed or fall back to graceful degradation policies (route-level fallbacks to cheaper model or enqueue into burst buffer) without triggering quota-throttle that causes abrupt 503s.

Initial triage:
- Hypothesis 1: Background scheduled batch/maintenance task on same dedicated cluster caused temporary GPU bank contention and reduced capacity; autoscaler escalated but was throttled by allocator quota.
- Hypothesis 2: Adaptive-burst autoscaler misestimated warmup time for additional GPU nodes leading to a cascade of allocation requests that tripped internal rate limits.
- Hypothesis 3: Noisy neighbor from other tenants in the same host-pool performing short high-concurrency streams causing slot fragmentation.

Attachments:
- packet: trace-Textly-2026-03-12-19-03.json (router traces)
- grafana: panels (autoscaler, allocator errors, gpu_util, queue_length)

Requested by customer:
Customer requests immediate mitigation (reduce p99 latency) and post-incident follow-up to avoid recurrence. They prefer isolation if needed (pin to reserved machines for peak hours).
2026-03-12 | Support (Ava Martinez): Ticket created after Textly support alerted #support. Collecting traces and metrics; escalated to SRE oncall.
2026-03-12 | SRE (Morgan Li): Confirmed allocator rate_limit_exceeded spikes in grafana. Opening temporary mitigation: increase allocator soft quota for dp-textly-prod-us-east by +2 for 1 hour. Applied at 19:22 UTC; queue drained by 19:30 UTC.
2026-03-12 | Customer (Textly.ai - Priya Shah): Thanks. We saw improvement after your change. Can we get a permanent fix? Peak hours are predictable for us (18:30-20:30 UTC).
2026-03-13 | Product (Diego Ramos): Suggest adding scheduled reservation window feature for dedicated pools or policy to pre-warm GPUs for customers with predictable peaks. Filing product follow-up.
2026-03-14 | SRE (Morgan Li): Running deeper analysis; correlating cluster maintenance events and background batch jobs. Found 1 host with nightly checkpoint writer that overlapped with peak and had I/O causing transient kernel backpressure.
2026-03-12 20:00 UTC - Found allocator throttle window aligns with a short burst of 120 small concurrent streams from tenant 'content-ml' sharing same host-pool.
2026-03-12 21:10 UTC - Node-level logs show kernel-level IO wait spikes on host xg-pool-13 causing slower container eviction and delayed slot freeing.
2026-03-13 09:00 UTC - Autoscaler policy 2026-02-18 uses conservative warmup timeout (45s) but issues parallel allocation requests; this interacts poorly with our allocator's per-minute allocation limit and causes aggregated throttles.
2026-03-13 11:40 UTC - Confirmed no scheduled cluster maintenance in region during that window; but a tenant scheduled checkpoint job started at 19:02 (cron job mis-scheduled).
2026-03-14 10:30 UTC - Reproduced high-concurrency short-stream load in staging and observed allocation throttling when allocator soft quota set to default. We reproduced queueing and p99 blips similar to production.
Mitigation applied (temporary): increased allocator soft quota for dp-textly-prod-us-east by +2 replicas at 19:22 UTC on 2026-03-12; removed after stability confirmed at 20:00 UTC.
Short-term plan: schedule tenant isolation for predictable peak windows (Textly advised to request reservation for 18:30-20:30 UTC) — SRE to create reservation for next 14 days.
Medium-term: autoscaler tuning - change parallel allocation backoff and add jitter to reduce simultaneous allocation fanout; target PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/489 (under review).
Long-term: product feature - scheduled reservation/pre-warm API for dedicated pools and allocator rate-limit control per-customer. Product to own roadmap item.
Follow-ups: 1) SRE to identify and quarantine noisy tenant 'content-ml' daily checkpoint job; 2) Reduce default allocator parallelism threshold for adaptive-burst policy; 3) Add alert for allocator.rate_limit_exceeded > 5/min.
Status: In Progress - mitigation successful, customer stable; implementing medium-term autoscaler change and creating reservation as requested.

Issue summary:
Customer (NimbleAI) on a Private deployment reporting intermittent failures while fetching model artifacts and spiky control-plane backoff. Failures manifest as partial TLS handshakes (client hello seen; server handshake aborted) from serving nodes to S3-presigned endpoints. Around same times, control-plane agents fall back to DNS-over-TLS (DoT) to an internal forwarder and show exponential backoff.

Impact:
- Artifact fetch retries and partial shard downloads cause model load failures (fast-fail or degraded quality) for a subset of requests (≈2-3% of fetches during peaks).
- Control-plane heartbeats recorded as intermittent timeouts; autoscaler triggered scale-downs then rapid scale-ups.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) peered to Redwood control-plane over VPCE in us-west-2.
- NAT arranged via customer-managed Transit NAT appliances with limited ephemeral port pools.
- Serving nodes on dedicated capacity pool; artifact storage on S3-compatible endpoint (presigned URLs).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Load test from serving nodes triggers many concurrent artifact fetches (model reloads + rolling restart).
2) NAT ephemeral port pool on egress appliance saturates -> source port reuse and port collisions.
3) Upstream TLS handshakes from different TCP flows appear to reuse five-tuple in NAT translation and result in server-side aborts (S3 returns connection reset or handshake abort).
4) Node agent falls back to DoT for DNS resolution (internal forwarder), DoT sessions hit rate-limit on forwarder -> DNS TCP/DoT latency spikes -> control-plane request timeouts -> exponential backoff.

Logs / Observations:
- Serving node tcpdump snippets (timestamps obfuscated):
  "Mar 10 14:11:22 tcpdump: SYN src=10.0.3.12:52321 -> dst=s3.example.net:443"
  "Mar 10 14:11:22 tcpdump: ClientHello src=10.0.3.12:52321"
  "Mar 10 14:11:22 tcpdump: RST id=..., server reset during handshake"
- NAT appliance metrics: ephemeral_port_utilization: 98% -> sudden drop to 45% after ephemeral reuse surge.
- Control-plane agent logs: "dns: fallback to dot://10.1.2.8:853 after udp timeout", repeated backoffs: 100ms -> 200ms -> 400ms -> 800ms.
- Cloudwatch: artifact-get 502/504 spikes correlate with NAT peak windows.

Hypothesis:
Primary: Ephemeral NAT port exhaustion / aggressive source-port reuse on the customer's egress appliance causes connection collisions leading to partial TLS handshake failures on presigned artifact downloads. The agent's DNS fallback to DoT increases latency and when DoT forwarder is rate-limited, causes control-plane backoff, amplifying the effect.

Temporary mitigations applied by customer:
- Increased ephemeral port range on transit NAT appliance (customer change) reduced immediate failure rate from ~2.7% to ~0.6%.
- Staggered model reloads across nodes to reduce burst fetch concurrency.

Proposed remediation plan / next steps:
1) SRE/Support to validate NAT ephemeral port exhaustion with customer (review conntrack and source port reuse behavior).
2) Recommend long-term: increase ephemeral port range and/or enable NAT port preservation heuristics; add source port hashing to distribute translations.
3) Add jittered artifact fetch retry/backoff logic in agent to avoid synchronized fetch storms (Engineering story).
4) Harden DoT forwarder rate-limits or add secondary DoT endpoints; recommend customer allow fallback to plain TCP53 for control-plane lookups when policy permits.
5) Follow-up: run coordinated load test with customer to reproduce and validate fix.

References / Crosslinks:
- Slack: #support-private-deploy thread (link posted)
- Runbook: confluence.redwood.internal/KB/egress-nat-churn-runbook

Customer requested outcome: permanent fix or recommended configuration for their NAT appliance plus a plan to change agent retry behavior to prevent synchronized fetch storms.
Aisha Malik (Support) 2026-03-10: Ticket created after NimbleAI reported repeated shard download failures during morning load test. Captured tcpdumps and NAT metrics attached by customer. Escalating to SRE for triage.
Tom Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-11: Initial triage - NAT ephemeral pool at 98% during window, conntrack shows many TIME_WAIT reuse entries. Hypothesis: port exhaustion + aggressive port reuse on appliance. Requested customer to expand ephemeral range and pause reload storm. Assigned to me for further validation.
NimbleAI Ops (customer) 2026-03-11: Increased ephemeral port range and applied temporary staggered restart script. Observed immediate reduction in failed fetches. Asking whether Redwood can provide agent-side debounce for artifact fetches and any recommended NAT sizing guidelines.
Tom Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-12: Next steps documented above. Filing Engineering story to add jittered fetch/backoff. Will coordinate test window with customer next week.
Mitigated - customer increased ephemeral port range and applied staggered reloads. Engineering story opened to add jittered artifact fetch backoff; follow-up load test scheduled.
ENG-4521 - Add jittered artifact fetch backoff (internal story)
SRE: coordinate test with NimbleAI 2026-03-16
Support: publish NAT sizing guidance KB entry
payload.summary: Ephemeral NAT pool churn triggers partial TLS handshakes for artifact fetches; DoT fallback causes control-plane backoff
