payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer EchoHealth reported a spike in tail latency and a rise in 5xx stream disconnects following a combined change that: enabled a new quantization profile, increased batching window from 8ms to 25ms, and enabled aggressive KV prefix caching for session replays.

Impact:
- Intermittent p95 latency regressions from ~120ms to 780-1,200ms for certain conversational workloads.
- Increased streaming disconnects (stream_close_rate +3.4%) and transient token generation 5xxs.
- Customers on dedicated pool are seeing increased request timeouts triggering client-side retries.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: echohealth-prod-gpu-a (us-east region)
- Serving runtime version: 2.9.1+opt (deployed 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC)
- Optimizer profile: hybrid-agg-v2 (batch_window=25ms, kv_prefetch=true, quant=amq8-approx)
- Traffic: 95% chat, 5% embeddings

Steps to reproduce:
1) Route a steady chat workload at production qps to the dedicated pool (we used the customer's canary).
2) Apply optimizer profile hybrid-agg-v2 via the Console rollout (applied to 100% of pool).
3) Observe p95 and streaming error rate over next 15-30 minutes.

Logs / metrics / traces referenced:
- Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/ops/echohealth-latency (p50/p95/p99 timeseries)
- Traces: linked trace ids in investigation notes below
- Recent rollout: Console rollout id ROLLOUT-2026-03-11-752

Customer request:
EchoHealth asked for prescriptive, stepwise guidance to safely revert to the previous stable optimizer configuration with minimal user-visible disruption and no data loss. They requested a temporary protection plan while we investigate root cause.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:35 - EchoHealth (Ops contact: Maya Chen): Confirmed canary and full pool had identical symptoms; attached a trace where kv_prefetch shows repeated cache miss thrash.
2026-03-13 02:05 - SRE (Diego Ramos): Prepared hotfix rollback playbook. Will coordinate with customer's on-call for maintenance window if needed. Recommended staged rollback (see investigation notes step sequence).
Hypothesis A: Combined effect - quantization profile 'amq8-approx' increases kernel path variability; when paired with larger batch windows the runtime generates larger execution kernels that increase memory working set causing GC/eviction thrash.
Hypothesis B: KV prefix caching with prefetch enabled caused a stampede on cache fill under elevated QPS since batch coalescing altered request ordering, producing hot keys and increased backend IO latency.
Checks performed:
- Node level: top/htop, GPU memory and utilisation, nvtop snapshots during spike windows.
- Runtime logs: looked for 'kv_cache_evict' and 'quant_fallback' messages.
- Telemetry: compared per-token CPU and wall-time distributions pre/post rollout.
- Canary revert: reverted quant profile only on 10% of capacity and observed metrics drop ~60% of the regression within 7 minutes.
Key finding: Reverting quant profile produced the largest immediate improvement on p95. KV cache invalidation helped but only after existing cache fill completed; batch window reduction reduced memory pressure but had slower effect on streaming disconnects.
Workaround and rollback plan applied and next steps:
1) Immediate staged revert (already started):
   - Monitor p50/p95/stream_close_rate for 30 minutes. If stable, proceed.
2) KV cache handling: Run coordinated KV cache drain on nodes that had prefetch enabled before toggling caching to avoid stampede (admin command: rwdctl cache invalidate --pool echohealth-prod-gpu-a --mode staged).
3) Batch window rollback (planned): Roll batch_window from 25ms back to 8ms in a separate staged rollout with 5-minute observation windows between stages; prefer a 10% -> 30% -> 100% stage progression.
4) Rollforward vs rollback note: We recommended revert quant first because it yielded largest effect; batching and caching to be handled after the quant change to avoid overlapping effects.
5) Postmortem actions: Create a canary test harness for hybrid profiles and add an automated alert if p95 increases >2x within 10 minutes of optimizer profile change.
Follow-up items assigned:
- Engineering (optimizer): add conservative fallback for 'amq8-approx' that disables prefetch when batch_window > 20ms (PR requested: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimizer/pull/5018).
- SRE: add dashboard panel that correlates batch_window, kv_prefetch, and quant profile usage with p95 and stream_close_rate.
- Support: produce a short runbook for customers introducing hybrid optimizer profiles with recommended rollout percentages and observation windows.
Status: Canary revert successful; full rollback in progress. Will update when full pool reversion completes and when follow-up PR merges.
payload.summary: Guidance for safely rolling back combined batching/caching/quantization profile changes after latency and error spikes

payload.description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12T13:20 UTC, a single dedicated-tenant (NarrativeLabs) observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses from the Redwood API. Impact: Customer facing failures for generation and embedding requests (~15-25% 5xx rate at peak) and elevated tail latency. Root-cause (short): Under sustained high concurrency to a pinned int8 quantized model, the runtime's kernel selector occasionally failed to pick the quantized kernel for long sequence lengths and fell back to a float kernel. The float fallback significantly increased per-request GPU memory, causing memory fragmentation and NVML watchdog resets on a subset of GPUs which in turn produced upstream runtime exits and amplified API gateway 502/503s. This ticket tracks the customer report, investigation, mitigation, and postmortem action items.
1) Pin tenant to model nl-vq-1.2-int8 in Dedicated pool
2) Send concurrent streaming generation requests with sequence lengths ranging 1k-4k tokens from 200 parallel clients
3) Observe runtime kernel selection logs and GPU memory footprints
4) Repeat with similar concurrency against fp16 variant for baseline comparison
API gateway returned elevated 5xx rates (502/503) and streaming disconnects. Runtime health checks recorded NVML watchdog resets (driver timeouts) on 2/12 GPUs in the tenant pool. Kernel-selector logs show intermittent 'kernel_not_found' events followed by 'fallback_to_fp32' for batches that earlier had quantized kernels. P99 latency increased from ~450ms to >3.2s at peak.

Issue summary: Customer requests a production-ready delivery method for tenant-scoped audit events to support an ongoing privacy investigation and SOC2 evidence collection. They need hourly bundled archives over SFTP in addition to an optional TLS syslog stream. Each audit event must be reversible-pseudonymized (escrowed key material) for lawful re-identification, include an ordered sequence number, and ship with a signed manifest that contains resume tokens and HMAC checksums.

Impact: This is blocking the customer's compliance filing. They cannot complete internal forensic review or provide auditors with reproducible evidence until deliveries are validated. Risk: high sensitivity PII present in some audit fields; customer requires cryptographic proofs and a minimal-change integration.

Customer request (deliverables):
- Hourly gzipped tar bundles (.tar.gz) dropped to a customer-managed SFTP endpoint with object names: AUREUS-audit-YYYYMMDD-HH.tar.gz
- Per-bundle manifest.json signed with Redwoods rotating KEK (signature metadata included) containing: start_seq, end_seq, per-file HMACs, resume_token for last event, count, event_schema_version
- Each event must be reversible-pseudonymized using a per-tenant key with HSM-backed escrow; deliver the key-escrow procedure and attestation steps for auditors
- Optional real-time TLS syslog stream with per-event envelope headers (tenant-id, seq, ts, stream-hmac) for parity with the SFTP feed
- Integrity and non-repudiation: hourly manifest must be verifiable offline; include sample verification CLI snippet and sample public key used for signature verification
- Retention and replay: customer needs guidance for replaying slices (resume semantics) and an index file for quick seek by timestamp

Acceptance criteria:
1) A customer test SFTP drop that matches naming and manifest schema for 3 consecutive hours without gaps
2) Manifest signatures verify using published public key; HMACs in manifest match files
3) Reversible pseudonymization flow documented with key escrow steps and timeline for reencryption requests
4) Minimal latency for syslog envelope delivery (<=10s median) when enabled

Attachments from customer: sample schema mapping (CSV), auditor contact info, SFTP host & SSH key (sensitive channel used), and a compliance questionnaire with requested answers.

Notes on scope: This is an enterprise-level compliance integration. Implementation will touch audit exporter, archive writer, SFTP uploader, and security/KMS teams for escrow documentation. Recommend dedicated engineer pairing with customer success and an SRE to run initial drops.
Initial triage (2026-03-12): Verified customer request form and attached schema. Confirmed SFTP host reachable from our staging egress. Hypothesis: existing hourly archive job can be extended with manifest signing and escrow hooks. Blockers: key escrow playbook and HSM procedure need security sign-off. Engineering estimate: 3 sprint-days for export changes, 2 days for KMS escrow docs and 1 day for SRE rollout and verification.

Technical checkpoints:
- Ensure per-tenant key material generation and store in customer-scoped KMS envelope.
- Implement resume_token as base64(seq||sha256(last_event)) to avoid ambiguity.
- Add manifest signer microservice to sign with current KEK; plan for rotation metadata in manifest.

Preliminary test plan: Test SFTP drops to customer-provided jumpbox, verify manifest signature and HMACs, run re-identification test in secured environment with escrow keys.

Additional notes:

1) Security to finalize KMS escrow runbook and provide required operator checklist (owner: Priya Rao)
2) Engineering to land manifest signer and wire into hourly archive job (owner: Miguel Alvarez)
3) SRE to schedule test drops to customer test SFTP and perform signature/HMAC verification (target: 2026-03-16)

Issue summary: During a staged canary wave for gptx-alpha-3.1 we observed a subset of tenant sessions that were explicitly pinned to 3.1 being demoted to a degraded variant (3.0-quant) without an explicit rollback or pin change. Impact: Affected tenant (AtlasSearch) saw inconsistent outputs and higher latency on ~2% of requests; downstream QA flagged semantic drift causing failed assertions in their processing pipeline. Environment: prod-us-east, Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-2 (4x A100), orchestrator v1.8.3, edge-proxy v2.2.1. Observed window: 2026-03-08 18:12 - 18:46 UTC. Expected behavior: Explicitly pinned sessions should continue routing to the pinned model until pin expiry or explicit unpin. Workaround applied: Triggered manual pin-refresh job which reasserted lease tokens for affected tenant and restored routing for most sessions.
Partial degraded routing for pinned sessions affecting AtlasSearch (dedicated). Approximately 2% of their traffic routed to quantized fallback, causing semantic divergence and a 60-120ms median latency increase for those requests.
AtlasSearch reported that their nightly QA jobs flagged content mismatches; they require a post-incident export of request IDs that hit fallbacks for compliance. Customer is on a dedicated plan and requested daily updates until fully resolved.
Initial hypothesis: autoscaler/prewarm interaction caused rapid prewarm invalidation which cleared pin tombstones on edge shards.
Telemetry shows a correlated spike in session-lease-renew RPC errors from the edge to control plane coincident with CDN connection resets (us-east-1).
Control-plane snapshot/epoch showed a narrow window where pin lease timestamp differed between orchestrator replicas by ~20s (we log timestamps at millisecond granularity).
Edge probe logic treats missing/expired lease as eligible for fallback; combined with a commit-latency race the fallback path executed before lease reconciliation could recover.
Reproduced in a staging REPLAY: windowed reconnection pattern + induced RPC latency reproduces transient demotion in ~3/50 trials (non-deterministic).

Issue summary:
Customer CloudPaper AI reports repeated timeouts (client 504) and elevated p95/p99 token latency for requests pinned to their dedicated GPU reservation between 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC and ongoing. Impact is intermittent but recurring during tenant-driven bursts.

Impact:
- Multiple production requests timing out (504) and streaming disconnects reported by the customer.
- Elevated p95 (2.3s -> 7s) and p99 tail spikes up to 18s for short text generation endpoints.
- Customer facing UX regressions and increased error rate; they asked for urgent mitigation.

Environment:
- Dedicated reservation: redwood-dedicated-cc-prod-09 (4x A100s), us-east cluster
- Customer traffic pattern: frequent long-sequence streaming jobs and a handful of concurrent long-stream sessions from a single tenant process.
- Autoscale policy: target based on pod GPU utilization (avg), min_replicas=1, max_replicas=6, cooldown=300s.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant issues a sudden burst of 30 concurrent long-seq streaming requests (seq_len ~ 2048).
2) Pods serving the tenant show near-saturation on SM% and kernel queuing increases.
3) Autoscaler does not scale quickly because average GPU util stays under threshold (due to a mix of idle short requests and a few saturated pods).
4) Scheduler queues requests, micro-batches overlap, KV cache thrash observed, leading to p95/p99 spikes and 504s.

Observed behavior:
- GPU SM% per-saturated pod >95% for sustained periods.
- Cluster-level GPU utilization averaged ~62% (below autoscale trigger).
- Request queue depth on the per-tenant routing queue climbed >200 for short windows.
- Streaming sessions aborted after client-side 30s timeout (customer SDK default).

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should react to per-pod saturation or queue length and bring up capacity fast enough to maintain p95 below 2s for this workload pattern.

Artifacts attached / logs referenced:
- Grafana dashboards: serving/runtime/p95, node/gpu-sm, autoscale/activity (links provided to customer and infra).
- Sample traces: trace IDs provided to SRE channel.
- Kernel logs: show repeated SM stalls and occasional nvlink retries.

Initial triage summary:
- Hypothesis: Autoscaler policy relying solely on average GPU utilization masks localized saturation caused by uneven traffic distribution (noisy tenant).
- Secondary contributor: Long-sequence streaming jobs hold GPU context and induce KV cache churn that increases effective per-request cost.
- Immediate mitigation options: temporary tenant isolation (soft reservation), add per-tenant queue-based scaling metric, or increase min_replicas for this reservation.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 Support: Notified customer we are investigating and proposed a short-term mitigation: increase min_replicas to 2 for the reservation and enable tenant soft-reservation. Customer approved temporary change.
2026-03-11 Ops (Automation): Applied temporary override: redwood-dedicated-cc-prod-09 min_replicas=2 for CloudPaper AI reservation. Observed immediate reduction in p95 from ~7s to ~2.4s during a smaller repeat burst. Metrics attached.
2026-03-12 Product (Platform): Proposed autoscaler enhancement RFC to consider per-pod latency and queue backlog as scaling signals. Referenced PR #4802 that adds a queue-based metric collector (staging validation in progress).
2026-03-12 CloudPaper AI (Customer): Confirmed temporary improvement but requested a durable fix. Asked for timeline for autoscale change or a recommended long-term reservation sizing guideline.
Checked serving-runtime logs for noisy-tenant markers: tenant_id=cloudpaper-42 shows high long-seq session counts at 2026-03-09 22:03-22:18 UTC.
Kernel telemetry: increased SM stalls and higher memory copy times on affected pods; nvlink errors transient but not primary root cause.
Autoscaler analysis: current metric is cluster_avg_gpu_utilization. This allowed saturated pods to be masked by idle or low-util pods in the same reservation.
KV cache observations: repeated cache misses when requests hit newly scaled pods, causing additional token latency for affected sessions.
Reproduction in staging: simulated 25 concurrent long-seq streams; observed same pattern when autoscale uses average util with long cooldowns. Changing scale signal to per-pod 90th percentile GPU latency reduced tail significantly.
Related historical tickets: see SUP-9271 (sustained throughput drop), SUP-48210 (pipeline saturation). Patterns overlap but root cause here is autoscale signal masking localized saturation.
Temporary mitigation applied: min_replicas increased to 2 for the customer's reservation and soft-reservation applied to reduce noisy-tenant spillover. Customer reports immediate improvement; p95 back to ~2s in observed windows.
Planned permanent fixes:
- Short term: provide CloudPaper AI sizing guidance (recommend increasing reserved GPUs for sustained long-seq workloads or using smaller per-stream batching) and update runbook. ETA: 48 hours.
- Medium term: implement autoscaler to include per-pod queue-length / p95 latency as a scaling signal and reduce cooldown for surge handling. PR #4802 implementing queue-based metric collector is in review; canary rollout scheduled for next sprint.
Follow-ups:
- Update Dedicated Autoscale Runbook to include noisy-tenant isolation steps.
- Consider per-tenant soft reservations for heavy long-seq workflows.
- Track action item ENG-OPS-1753 to validate autoscaler changes across 2 clusters.
2026-03-11: Temporary min_replicas=2 override rolled for customer reservation by ops-automation; watch metrics for 24h.
2026-03-12: Customer confirmed reduction in error rate; remaining action is product change to autoscaler and runbook update.
ENG-OPS-1753 created to track autoscaler enhancement and runbook updates.

Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart (private deployment) reports intermittent 504s and frequent gRPC stream resets for long-lived generation sessions. Symptoms correlate with increased KV cache misses on serving nodes and elevated control-plane auth retries. Preliminary tcpdump captured HTTP/2 PRIORITY frames inserted mid-stream by an intermediate egress proxy.

Impact:
- Generation streaming sessions abort after 30-90s, leading to degraded UX for end users (progressive text stops).
- Elevated token cost due to repeated replays and cache churn.
- Affects production workloads in us-east-1 for BrightCart only (private VPC with VPCE to Redwood control plane).

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering + VPCE) with customer-managed egress proxy/NAT in front of VPCE.
- Redwood control plane and serving nodes in us-east-1.
- Model: gpt-large-v1 pinned.

1) Launch long-lived streaming generation (streaming=true) against pinned model gpt-large-v1 from BrightCart private deployment.
2) Sustain a single stream for >60s by asking to continue generation.
3) Observe a gRPC GOAWAY or RST_STREAM from serving node and immediate client reconnect.
4) Correlate with egress proxy logs that show proactive HTTP/2 PRIORITY frame injection into existing connections.
- Customer tcpdump (extract): shows inbound client TLS -> VPCE; within decrypted HTTP/2 frames, packets with type 0x2 (PRIORITY) appear that were not sent by the client.
- Serving node logs: repeated 'stream reset: code=REFUSED_STREAM' followed by reconnects and KV cache invalidations.
- Control-plane auth logs: intermittent 'auth token expired' during reconnect sequence.
- Egress proxy logs (customer): 'rewriter: injecting priority frame: stream_id=0x7fd' at same timestamps.

- Hypothesis: Customer's egress device performs HTTP/2 frame rewriting to prioritize certain traffic classes (DPI-based QoS). This rewriting is breaking gRPC semantics for long-lived streams and causing the server to treat stream state as invalid.
- Verified with packet captures that frames are present mid-stream while client never issues them.
- Reproduced a similar failure in our lab by running a simple HTTP/2 frame injector in the egress path; gRPC reset behavior matched.
- Correlated increased KV cache churn with stream resets: each reset forces state rehydration and additional artifact/kv reads.
- Control-plane retries are side-effect of reconnects, not root cause.

Customer-facing streaming degradation (higher 5xx ratio), increased token costs due to replay, and potential control-plane rate spikes. Affects only BrightCart's private deployment in us-east-1 so far.

- Short term: Route outbound control-plane and serving traffic through a bypass NAT (customer-side) that does not pass through the DPI/priority rewriter. Customer report: adding a routing policy that sends VPCE-bound traffic via a dedicated egress (bypassing rewriter) dropped stream resets to near-zero.
- Alternative: Disable HTTP/2 frame rewriting feature on the customer's egress device if possible.

Triage in progress. Customer applied temporary routing bypass on 2026-03-13 which significantly reduced incidents. Engineering follow-up assigned to egress-proxy and serving-runtime teams to harden gRPC against mid-path non-spec frame injection where possible (defensive parsing and stronger stream validation).
Next steps: add detection telemetry in serving nodes to log unexpected frame types and surface to console, and work with customer to schedule a configuration change window to fully remove injector.

Additional notes:

Issue summary:
Customer reporting increased time-to-first-token (TTFB) on chat completion start after we rolled a runtime ABI compatibility change and a minor model packaging update. Problem appears across multiple clusters and is concentrated in US-EAST traffic for this customer's dedicated pool.

Impact:
- Arcadia Health (dedicated) reports 3–6x increase in median TTFB for chat sessions originating from us-east; occasional 504s when handshake exceeds 60s.
- Affects production traffic for two internal teams relying on low-latency responses for assisted triage flows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: arcadia-dedicated-us-east (prod)
- Runtime: inference-runtime v1.9.2 -> v1.10.0 (ABI compat change applied 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC)
- Model package: rw-io/gpt-medium-v2@2026-03-08-patch (packaging artifact updated same window)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open chat session using Arcadia API key against the Redwood hosted endpoint pinned to their dedicated pool.
2) Send short prompt (~10 tokens) to start a session.
3) Observe first token delay; sometimes stream handshake stalls for 20–60s before first chunk.

Observed behavior:
- Median TTFB for chat start rose from ~120ms to ~450ms; P95 from ~600ms to ~2.8s.
- Intermittent 504 gateway timeouts when handshake path exceeds proxy timeout (60s).
- Logs show long waits waiting for "kv-cache-init" and multiple negotiation retries between api-gateway and serving-runtime.

Expected behavior:
- Median TTFB < 200ms for pinned dedicated pool on these short prompts. No stream handshake timeouts.

Logs & metrics attached (summarized):
- api-gateway logs (us-east) show TLS reconnects and repeated "runtime capability mismatch" entries around 02:12–02:20 UTC.
- Serving-runtime traces show delayed kernel selection step: kernel-selection latency spikes during session init.
- KV-cache hit-rate unchanged; but KV cache warmup appears to block session until compat check finishes.

Temporary workaround:
- Customer unpinned model routing and forced fallback to a pre-upgrade model variant (rw-io/gpt-medium-v2@2026-02-27) which restored baseline TTFB within 30 minutes.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: ABI compatibility check introduced an extra synchronous RPC during handshake that blocks token generation until kernel/ABI handshake completes.
- Hypothesis 2: Model packaging update altered the runtime-compat metadata causing the serving runtime to perform a slow fallback resolution (checks across multiple kernel variants).
- Hypothesis 3: Gateway TLS renegotiation observed in logs indicates some clients hit a path that re-establishes connection prior to session start; correlated with a new keepalive config deployed 2026-03-09.
- Correlated events: runtime v1.10.0 deployment, model packaging push, gateway keepalive tuning — all within 18 minutes.

Next steps (ordered):
1) Lock down a repro on a staging replica of the customer's dedicated pool with traffic replay (assigned to Rafael).
2) Add debug flags to serving-runtime to log ABI negotiation timings (hotfix build).
3) Roll back gateway keepalive change in us-east to isolate TLS renegotiation hypothesis (SRE).
4) If ABI handshake proves blocking, revert runtime v1.10.0 or cherry-pick non-blocking handshake patch.
5) Coordinate customer communication and confirm they can stay on fallback model while engineering fixes the runtime.

Business impact note:
- Customer is in production; sustained latency regressions risk SLA breach and potential throttled usage. Finance/sales informed.

Workaround: customer temporarily routed to pre-upgrade model variant. Engineering patch prepared to make ABI/compat handshake asynchronous to avoid blocking kernel selection. payload.description:
Issue summary:
Users report that when they apply an ad-hoc time shift (e.g., shifting the dashboard to -7d) the annotation overlay begins to flicker and several annotations disappear entirely from the view. Behavior is intermittent but reproducible for large time ranges and when the dashboard contains more than ~400 annotations.

Impact:
- Customer GlacierDocs (enterprise) is unable to rely on annotations for post-deployment incident reviews; important markers dropped from charts.
- Affects any org-level dashboard with annotations + ad-hoc time shift; visibility regression for historical analysis.

Environment:
- Console web app (React) v4.8.1 served from prod in us-east region.
- Annotations backed by annotations-service v1.9 (Postgres), served through console API gateway.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login as a user with access to org dashboard that has >400 annotations in the last 90 days.
2) Open dashboard, confirm annotations visible at baseline (no time shift).
3) Open time selector and apply an ad-hoc shift (e.g., Last 30 days with "Shift by" -7d or use the time-shift quick selector).
4) Observe annotation layer flicker; some annotations disappear instantly and do not return when toggling layer visibility.
5) Refresh the dashboard -> sometimes annotations return; applying different shifts causes unpredictable losses.

Observed behavior:
- Flicker of the annotation layer (visual redraw) followed by removal of up to 30-40% of annotations for the selected range.
- Trace links from annotations occasionally break (link -> 404) after the shift.
- No 500s from API, but frontend console shows 'Range mismatch for annotation cache' warnings.

Expected behavior:
- Time shift should re-query annotations for the shifted window and render a stable annotation layer with all markers that fall in the shifted period.

Logs / artifacts attached:
- Console network timeline HAR (redacted) - link in comments.
- Screenshot: flicker and missing markers.
- Frontend console warnings: "annotation-cache: mismatch between server range and client range, invalidating partial cache" (repeated).

Initial triage (Support):
- Reproduced with GlacierDocs test org. Problem more likely when annotation count > ~400 and when time-shift window size increases tokenized query length to annotations-service.
- Client-side code path: time-shift triggers a new annotation query with range calculation; client attempts to merge incremental annotation pages into existing render layer. Merge logic likely drops annotations that fall outside a previously cached bucket due to inconsistent bucket boundary calculation.

Eng update (Lucas Rivera):
- Checked annotations-service logs for query patterns around 2026-03-10T15:xx. No 5xxs. Query payloads show overlapping but non-identical range parameters between client and gateway (off-by-one in millis conversion). Suspect rounding/UTC conversion bug in client-shift calculation.
- Found related flaky test in PR history that touched range normalization for ad-hoc shifts (see related_github_prs).

SRE note:
- No infra capacity issues. Memory and p99 latency for annotations-service normal. Not a DB timeout.

Hypothesis:
- Client calculates shifted range using timezone-naive timestamps, resulting in queries for ranges that straddle bucket boundaries. Client-side merge code then discards items that don't match exact bucket IDs. The net effect: flicker as layer re-renders and some items dropped permanently until full refresh.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 14:30 - SRE (Priya Nair): Checked annotations-service logs and DB queries. No errors; p99 latency 42ms. Not infra. Marking as app-level bug.
1) Merge PR (console) after QA: range normalization + full-reload fallback. 2) Deploy console hotfix to staging and validate with GlacierDocs repro org. 3) If green, deploy to prod during low-traffic window and notify customer. 4) Add e2e test for ad-hoc shift with >500 annotations. 5) Create a small migration note for annotation bucket IDs to tolerate near-boundary queries.
Customer workaround: Refresh the dashboard after applying time shift, or toggle annotation layer off and on. If lost annotations are critical, request Support to run a manual full-reload (Support has script to force annotation-page refresh).
payload.summary: Dashboard annotation layer flickers and drops annotations when applying ad-hoc time shift

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Aurora Bank (enterprise) requests a legally defensible audit export that preserves strict ordering, provides a per-event cryptographic signature (Ed25519), and includes resume tokens so exports can be resumed or replayed deterministically for legal-hold and eDiscovery. They require a sample delivery bundle and verification instructions for their internal auditors.

Background:
Customer ingests high volume of events (auth, prompt/response metadata, admin actions) and must produce an ordered archive for legal requests and SOC2 evidence. They want per-event signatures to prove non-repudiation and a small resume token that allows incremental replays without duplicating events. Customer also insists that user identifiers be pseudonymized with a deterministic HMAC using a rotating KEK, and that the export manifest includes checksums and attestation metadata (signer key id, timestamp, canonicalization method).

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
1) Export format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) gzip archive + manifest.json.
2) Each event object must include a top-level "sig" field containing an Ed25519 signature over the canonicalized event payload and headers. Signature format: base64url. Include "sig_kid" (key identifier) and "sig_ts" (UTC ISO8601).
3) Resume token: short opaque token (base64url) with a cryptographic anchor so that replay from token produces exact event sequence without overlap or gaps. Token TTL = 24h; tokens must be monotonic per-partition.
4) Pseudonymization: a deterministic HMAC-SHA256 of the subject identifier using customer-scoped KEK; provide sample mapping tool and rotation guidance. KEK rotation must allow backfill verification for previous KEKs via manifest.
5) Manifest must include: archive checksum (sha256), signer public key fingerprint, key attestation reference (HSM certificate chain link), canonicalization method (sorted keys, utf8 normalizing), and a per-archive signature (Ed25519) over the manifest.
6) Delivery options: S3 presigned (customer bucket) or SFTP with signed receipt. Provide both samples.
7) Verification guide: steps for auditors to verify per-event signatures and resume-token replays, including a small reference script and expected verification output.

Security & compliance constraints:
- Customer requires attested HSM signing (option A: Redwood HSM-signed keys with attestation; option B: customer-supplied public key and Redwood signs archives only).
- No cleartext PII may be exported; per-event payloads must contain pseudonymized identifiers only.
- All artifacts must be retained according to customer's legal-hold retention window (90 days initial request) and include a tamper-evident manifest.

Deadline:
Customer asks for an initial sample bundle and verification steps by 2026-03-18 to feed into their audit window.

Notes:
This request overlaps with prior audit export work but is distinct in asking for per-event Ed25519 signatures + resume tokens and a deterministic pseudonymization scheme that supports KEK rotation and verification.

1) Receive sample gzip JSONL bundle and manifest.json. 2) Run provided verification script against manifest to verify archive checksum and manifest signature. 3) For each event, verify the 'sig' field using the signer public key and confirm 'sig_ts' within expected window. 4) Use resume token with replay endpoint to request events after token; confirm sequence matches archive and tokens do not cause duplication. 5) Confirm no raw PII fields are present and that pseudonymization mapping verifies deterministically with provided HMAC parameters.

Additional notes:
Checked existing audit-export pipeline: supports JSONL gzip bundles, manifest signing at archive level (currently RSA-2048). No existing per-event signature path.
Evaluated signing approaches: (A) Sign inline at ingestion (higher CPU, deterministic), (B) Sign during export worker (less impact on ingestion, still per-event cost). Export-worker approach preferred to avoid affecting real-time SLOs.
HSM attestation: Redwood HSM supports Ed25519 signing via PKCS#11 shim; need to confirm certificate chain export format for attestation reference. Latency tests show ~3-6ms per sign when batched; for 100k events/hour export-worker signing is acceptable with worker autoscaling.
Resume token design sketch: token = base64url( HMAC-SHA256( partition_id || seq_no || epoch ) || truncation ) with server-side monotonic seq mapping. Will wrap token in MAC to prevent exposure of internal ids.
Pseudonymization: use HMAC-SHA256 with customer KEK; deterministic output hex/base64. Provide sample rotation table in manifest mapping previous KEK IDs with start/end times.
Dependencies: platform PR to add per-event signing (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6734). Need KMS/HSM team for attestation artifact and support for Ed25519 key material export (public key fingerprint only).
Triage complete. Engineering published initial design and opened PR. Awaiting engineering prototype of signed JSONL bundle and verifier script. Next steps: platform eng to deliver sample bundle by 2026-03-17; Support to coordinate secure delivery and auditor walkthrough. Follow-up item: confirm KEK rotation cadence with customer and produce runbook for verification steps.
ENG: Implement export-worker per-event signing prototype (owner: Elena Ruiz) - target 2026-03-17
KMS: Provide attestation artifact and public key fingerprint export - target 2026-03-16
SUPPORT: Prepare delivery checklist and auditor verification guide - target 2026-03-17
payload.summary: Request: Per-event Ed25519 signatures + resume tokens for ordered audit export (legal hold)

Issue summary:
We observed a sustained increase in 5xx responses for customer Vernon Analytics (dedicated tenant) originating from api-gateway and upstream serving-runtime restarts. Error rate spike started 2026-03-13 14:12 UTC and correlated with an automated priority rebalancing job executing across the ingress-prioritizer fleet.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests for the tenant returned 5xx over a 22-minute window; clients reported failing streaming sessions and aborted generation jobs.
- Customer reported production degradation for a data-processing pipeline (affects business analytics dashboards).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: prod us-east-1 (tenant pinned to a subset of GPU nodes).
- Components involved: api-gateway -> ingress-prioritizer -> serving-runtime pool (cuda nodes).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Priority rebalancer runs and recalculates per-tenant priority buckets based on recent QPS and SLA weights.
2) In-flight lower-priority requests are preemptively evicted to rebalance capacity.
3) Evicted clients retry immediately (no jitter) causing a rapid burst against api-gateway.
4) Api-gateway queues spike, backpressure increases, and several serving runtime workers exceed allowed KV cache thrash limits leading to watchdog restarts and OOM-like termination (SIGABRT).
5) Subsequent requests receive 502/503/504 depending on proxy path and timing.

Observed behavior & logs (selected):
- apigw logs (us-east-1, 2026-03-13 14:12:30 - 14:34:00): repeated upstream 502s; connection resets followed by 429s at the gateway when token buckets hit zero. Link: https://dash.redwood.com/apigw/errors?svc=us-east-1&window=2026-03-13T14:10:00Z_2026-03-13T14:40:00Z
- ingress-prioritizer: job "rebalance-cycle-2026-03-13-14:11" completed in 18s. Logs show mass eviction events for tenant id t-vernon-11 with reason PREEMPTIVE_REBALANCE.
- serving-runtime: repeated worker watchdog restarts with stack traces indicating rapid KV cache invalidation and repeated memory pressure before abort: "runtime: aborting worker due to kv-evict-loop". Kernel-level OOMs were not recorded, but process exit codes were non-zero.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Preemptive eviction without backoff caused retry amplification; retries hit the gateway burst limit and queue saturation triggered upstream timeouts.
- Hypothesis B: The rebalancer's immediate eviction approach did not signal the runtime to gracefully finish in-flight streams, causing partial state corruption of runtime's KV caches and subsequent instability when those requests retried.
- Correlated metrics: request retry rate increased 6x immediately after rebalance completion; average per-request queue time at apigw jumped from 12ms to 420ms.
- Cross-checks: No infra-level node interruptions recorded in cloud provider metrics; node CPU/GPU utilization increased but did not show sustained saturation prior to restarts.

Temporary mitigation performed (timeline):
- 14:25 UTC: Support escalated to SRE and Engineering.
- 14:32 UTC: Rolled back automated priority rebalancer for the us-east-1 ingress-prioritizer cluster to stop further evictions (hotfix toggle).
- 14:40 UTC: Applied short-term gateway rate-smoothing for tenant t-vernon-11 via dynamic token-bucket increase to allow graceful retries with jitter.
- 14:55 UTC: Performed rolling restart of 6 serving-runtime workers handling the tenant to clear the kv-cache thrash cycles; error rate began to fall.
- 15:10 UTC: Error rate returned to baseline for the tenant; monitoring shows stabilized queue times and reduced restart frequency.

Customer communication:
- CS notified customer at 14:36 UTC; provided update at 15:20 UTC confirming mitigation and next steps. Customer accepted working-with-engineering for root cause follow-up.

Next steps / recommended permanent fixes:
1) Add a grace-window in the priority rebalancer that avoids preemptive eviction of actively streaming sessions for X seconds and instead marks for low-priority tail-preemption.
2) Implement client-visible retry-jitter guidance and server-side retry token smoothing when eviction events are emitted.
3) Add a safety-check in ingress-prioritizer to not evict more than N% of in-flight requests within a single cycle.
4) Enhance runtime KV cache eviction metrics and add an automated alert when eviction storms correlate to worker restarts.
5) Postmortem & runbook update: record exact mitigation toggles and make hotfix toggle accessible to on-call without engineer approval.

Work items created:
- github.com/redwood/ingress-prioritizer/pull/129 (smoothing + grace window)
- ENG-TASK-1122: telemetry for kv eviction spikes and runtime restarts
- DOCS: update runbook confluence.redwood.com/KB/priority-rebalancer-runbook with emergency toggle steps

Resolution notes (so far):
- Root cause appears tied to the rebalancer eviction policy interacting poorly with streaming workloads and runtime cache behavior. Hotfix rollback and smoothing mitigations reduced customer impact; engineering will deploy a targeted code change to ingress-prioritizer to enforce eviction rate limits and grace periods.

Observed behavior: - Increased tail latency (95p to 99p) on tenant-pinned model variants. - Elevated token counts for identical prompts (tokenizer traces show repeated prefix re-encoding in some traces). - Streaming sessions entering stalled state and then resuming (connection logs show large gaps of inactivity from runtime).

1) Tenant configuration: apply optimizer profile 'tenant-opt-ldg-2026' via Console -> Tenants -> LumenDocs -> Optimizer Profiles -> Activate.
2) Use production request route 'summarize-v2' with payload size ~2k tokens and streaming=true.
3) Observe streaming: agent receives first few tokens then connection stalls for 2–6s before resuming; client may timeout if retry thresholds low.
4) Compare token accounting: run identical prompt through snapshot before and after profile; backend shows ~30% higher token count post-profile in subset of traces.

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent HTTP/2 stream resets and 502/stream-closed errors when fleet of serving nodes concurrently pull model artifacts over the cluster egress path. Impact: Model pulls fail (partial), causing cold-starts to time out and downstream inference requests to error or stall. Environment: Private deployment behind customer TGW and a pair of NAT gateways in us-east-1; TLS termination at Redwood control-plane; model artifacts served from S3 via VPC endpoint and from a hosted artifact proxy (HTTPS) over egress.
Multiple serving hosts experience simultaneous aborted model downloads during rollout/scale events. Symptoms include ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_CANCEL, repeated TLS rehandshakes, elevated retry rates in serving runtime, and increased inference latency leading to user errors in production.
1) Deploy a scale-up event for a model (llama-3-8b) to 50 replicas in the customer's private cluster.
2) Trigger parallel artifact downloads by restarting pods to force cold pulls.
3) Monitor egress NAT gateway connection table and serving runtime logs.
4) Observe duplicated source-port allocations and TCP connection resets between serving hosts and artifact proxy/S3 endpoint.
Concurrent downloads frequently fail with http2 stream resets; server logs show repeated TCP FIN/RST from remote and client-side 'stream cancelled' errors. Packet captures indicate multiple distinct internal IPs mapping to a small set of external source ports due to hairpinning/masquerade behavior, leading to collisions and stream demux failures in the artifact proxy or intermediate stateful device.
Each internal connection should be NATed to a unique (ip,port) tuple so concurrent HTTP/2 streams don't collide when translated across the egress path. No stream-level resets during parallel artifact pulls.
[2026-03-10T08:14:02Z] serving-node-17 fetch-artifact failed: ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_CANCEL, retrying...
[2026-03-10T08:14:03Z] nat-gw-01 conntrack: SNAT 10.0.5.23:51432 -> 54.239.0.12:443 reused for 10.0.6.11:51432
tcpdump excerpt: client 10.0.5.23:51432 -> proxy 54.239.0.12:443, then client 10.0.6.11:51432 -> proxy 54.239.0.12:443 with same src port observed within 10ms
Artifact proxy logs: 'http2: stream id 19 cancelled by peer (duplicate client port detected)'
Serving runtime: 'model-pull: permanent failure after 3 retries, error=http2: stream canceled'

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:30 - Customer (NovaCommerce): Confirmed they recently added a second NAT gateway in a different AZ and enabled route propagation through TGW. Issues started ~1 hour after change.
Conntrack entries show SNAT collisions where the external 5-tuple is identical for different internal IPs: this causes stateful middleboxes/artifact proxy to misassociate streams.
Artifact proxy implements per-(ip,port) demultiplexing for HTTP/2 streams and treats colliding src ports as duplicate sessions; upstream then cancels existing streams.
Issue is exacerbated when customer introduces multiple NAT gateways/ENIs and TGW routes create hairpin return paths where egressing interface differs from ingress.
Related prior ticket SUP-27654 documents ephemeral nat-port reuse patterns; this case differs because hairpinning changes which NAT device performs translation leading to identical port reuse across devices.
Packet-level timing shows collisions occur within <50ms during a burst of simultaneous connections, explaining why high-concurrency cold starts are affected.
Tested mitigation: enabling ephemeral port randomization and increasing source port range on customer NAT reduced collision rate in staging.
Short-term: Customer to stagger restarts by 5s per replica to reduce parallelism of model pulls.
Short-term: Increase NAT ephemeral port range on customer side (recommended 32768-65535) and enable source-port randomization where supported.
Medium-term: Route artifact pulls through single egress NAT path (disable hairpinning across TGW for artifact proxy origin) to ensure consistent SNAT device and port assignment.
Long-term: We will add a note in the Private Deploy runbook advising customers to avoid multi-NAT hairpinning patterns for large-scale parallel artifact pulls and provide recommended NAT settings.
2026-03-12 - Implemented customer change: set NAT ephemeral port range to 32768-61000 and configured TGW to prefer single egress attachment for artifact-origin routes. Observed zero stream-reset failures in subsequent scale test (100 concurrent pulls).
2026-03-12 - Infra PR merged to add guardrails in our on-agent egress configuration that detect high port-reuse rates and log a warning to Console (github PR #812).
Follow-up: Create a KB article explaining the NAT hairpinning failure mode and recommended network settings for private deployments (owner: Jonas Meyer, due 2026-03-20).
payload.summary: NAT hairpinning + source-port reuse causing HTTP/2 stream resets during parallel model artifact pulls

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 10-30s tail latency spikes and occasional 504s when using structured_output mode for tasks that emit long arrays (thousands of items). Impact: Production search-indexing pipeline using our hosted API experienced several failed requests and delayed downstream processing. Environment: prod us-east, requests via hosted API, structured_output=true, streaming disabled.

Observed behavior: Most requests complete sub-500ms, but ~1-2% of calls for large enumerations spike to >10s and sometimes time out. Spikes appear correlated with the model producing very long JSON arrays and payloads with many comma-separated items.

Expected behavior: Structured output decoding should not add long-tail latency; streaming responses or chunked parsing should emit tokens progressively and complete within normal percentiles.

1) Use hosted API endpoint with structured_output=true and streaming=false
2) Prompt the model to generate a JSON array of ~3000 short items (e.g., list of normalized entity objects)
3) Observe latency distribution over 500+ requests; identify 95/99/999p spikes
4) Re-run with streaming=true and compare latencies
5) Repeat with alternative models (redwood/chat-3b and openlm-llama-13b)
Notes: customer provided a sample prompt and corpus attached to initial support attachment (not stored here)
Request IDs: req-0372a, req-0375f, req-0419c
Proxy logs show upstream 200 from runtime at t=360ms, but response assembly held until t=11.2s for req-0375f
Runtime trace: parser buffer flush at offset 0x1f48 took 10.8s in parse_json_chunk()
Gateway reported backpressure spikes and repeated zero-byte writes to client socket before final flush
Relevant dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/structured-output-long-tail?from=now-24h
Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer says problem started after last runtime deploy (2026-03-08). They only see issues when the model produces very long flat arrays.
Luis Ortega (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with redwood/chat-3b. Initial hypothesis: incremental parser uses an internal boundary heuristic that defers buffer emission for comma-delimited sequences, causing blocking until a final close-bracket or flush is seen.
Aisha Patel (Eng - parser) - 2026-03-12: Confirmed parser path parse_json_chunk() uses a 'lookahead' that can wait for up to 8k tokens before emitting; this interacts poorly with streaming=false and large enumerations. Adding instrumentation to measure wait times.
Customer (MapleDocs) - 2026-03-12: Provided 12 sample prompts and 90 failing request IDs. Impact: indexing job fell behind SLA by 3 hours for one batch.
Luis Ortega (SRE) - 2026-03-13: Temporary mitigation suggested for customer: set structured_output_chunk_threshold=1024 OR enable streaming=true. Customer validated streaming=true reduces spikes but changes client-side handling.
Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-13: Will coordinate final patch rollout and schedule customer-facing communication about config option and timeline.
Hypothesis 1: Parser 'enumeration lookahead' heuristic waits for additional tokens to decide whether to emit a partial array item, causing delays when items are small and numerous.
Hypothesis 2: Gateway backpressure + runtime write coalescing leads to delayed flush when response body is primarily commas and braces (small tokens), exacerbated by streaming=false path.
Repro steps executed in staging: crafted PR that toggles lookahead to 256 tokens; median latency unchanged but 99.9p improved from 12.1s -> 0.9s in local test (3000-item array).
Perf trace: CPU usage steady; blocking is in parser IO path waiting on internal condition variable (cv) in parse_json_chunk().
Related signals: increase in socket write vfs_queue length for affected requests; no OOMs observed.
Cross-reference: See SUP-17821 for related final-chunk blocking behavior on structured output when unicode escapes are present.
Action items: create a small runtime hotfix to lower lookahead threshold and add an adaptive flush when array length > 512; add e2e test with large enumerations; add monitoring alert for parser_hang_seconds>2.
Workaround provided: customer set streaming=true for affected endpoints which eliminated the >10s spikes for their workload. Alternatively, set structured_output_chunk_threshold=1024 on request-level config to force earlier flush.
Fix implemented: PR #842 shortens enumeration lookahead to 256 tokens and adds an adaptive flush when array item count exceeds threshold. Test coverage added for long enumeration streaming and non-streaming paths.
Rollout plan: Canary rollout to 5% traffic in us-east on 2026-03-14, monitor 99.9p latency and socket queues. Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-16 pending no regressions.
Follow-ups: Update structured-output runbook with config knobs; add documented guidance in SDK docs about streaming vs structured_output tradeoffs; postmortem planned if customer sees further impact.
Status: Patch merged to main; canary deployed. Pending verification from customer that batch indexing recovered.

Issue summary:
Customer observed SSE streams from the Redwood API delivering garbled final choices after resuming a paused browser tab. The stream plays correctly initially; after leaving the tab backgrounded for ~20–30s and then returning, the final choice is split across fragments and then interleaved with a subsequent choice. This results in malformed structured output for the application and a user-visible truncated sentence.

Impact:
- Multiple end users at Streamly.ai report corrupted assistant responses in production for ~6% of resumed streams in us-west-2.
- Breaks downstream parsers that expect well-formed JSON or terminal choice markers.

Environment:
- Client: Chrome 106 on macOS Monterey and Chrome 106 on Linux. Also seen in Chrome-based embedded webview.
- Customer uses a client-side service worker which intercepts fetch events and applies range/rebuffering logic to improve battery/latency for background tabs.
- Redwood API model: redwood-v1-medium (pinned) via hosted endpoint behind Cloudflare + internal edge proxy.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer and reproduced by support):
1) Start streaming completion via SSE from UI in foreground tab (payload includes structured choices and "end" marker).
2) Let the stream run for ~2–3s, then background the tab (put to sleep) for ~20–40s.
3) The client service worker intercepts revalidation and issues range-style re-requests for the stream upon resume.
4) On tab resume, the browser/service-worker pipeline coalesces/reattributes incoming bytes and we observe out-of-order chunk delivery and partial event merges.
5) Client parses resulting SSE stream and fails to reconstruct final choice boundaries; final sentence fragments are split and interleaved with next-choice tokens.

Relevant request ids / logs (customer supplied):
- customer request-id: streamly-req-20260308-77a1
- edge request-id: rwd-edge-0a9f2b03
- approximate time: 2026-03-08T21:14:03Z

Initial investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally with Chrome 106 when using a synthetic service worker that rewrites range bytes and replays portions of the stream on resume.
- Observed that when Service Worker fetch handler returns a ReadableStream that performs byte-slicing and concatenation, the browser's framing of text/event-stream boundaries can be altered (Content-Type unchanged).
- Edge logs show no 5xx; connection remained open and returned 200 with transfer-encoding: chunked. No server-side errors recorded.
- Hypothesis: client-side rebuffering/replay by service worker changes the chunk boundary alignment; SSE event parsing in the browser then groups bytes differently leading to event frames that contain partial choices or multiple events merged.

Temporary workarounds suggested to customer:
- Disable service worker interception for streaming endpoints (simplest) or return a passthrough response for any URL matching /v1/stream/* to avoid client-side range reassembly.
- Use WebSocket fallback rather than SSE for clients that require aggressive SW caching.
- Shorten background pause deadline (keepalive pings) so the browser does not trigger service worker byte slicing on resume.

Engineering next steps / proposed fixes:
- Add guidance to SDK docs to set Cache-Control: no-transform and to avoid service-worker reassembly for streaming endpoints.
- Server-side: add an SSE-safe chunk boundary marker (internal event boundary) that clients can use to validate event framing when resuming. This requires a small runtime change to emit explicit end-of-choice markers on their own line.
- Intake a task to detect abnormal resume offsets and return 409/+Retry-After to force clients to reopen a fresh stream when we detect non-sequential byte offsets (P2 engineering ticket to spec).

Attachments provided by customer: sample HAR with SW handling, a client-side service worker snippet, and a screen recording of resumed stream showing interleaved tokens.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 - Streamly.ai (Customer): Implemented workaround to bypass SW for streams and confirmed immediate drop of corrupted resumes. Customer requests ETA for server-side marker fix.
Workaround accepted by customer (disable SW for streaming endpoints). Engineering to ship explicit SSE choice-boundary markers in serving runtime; PR planned for 2026-03-21. Follow-up tasks: create internal ticket to detect non-sequential resume offsets and update docs.
This ticket is high priority because it affects structured-output integrations. Related to prior proxy/utf8 boundary tickets but root cause here is client-side SW rebuffering in Chrome; coordinated mitigation will be both docs and runtime marker emission.
payload.summary: Chrome service-worker rebuffering after long tab pause causes SSE event boundary corruption and interleaved choices

Issue summary:
Customer LexiconMedia (dedicated pool) reported intermittent mixed-model responses during a staged rollout. A subset (~15–20%) of tenant requests that were explicitly pinned to redwood/open-13B-v1 were observed to be routed to the canary variant (redwood/compat-7B-q4) for short windows. This produced tokenization deltas and occasional quality regressions.

Impact:
- Approximately 18% of pinned tenant requests during the observed window returned responses from the canary variant, causing degraded output quality for LexiconMedia product flows (search summarization).
- Customer saw elevated error reports and alerted support; revenue-impacting session types affected.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: lexicon-dedicated-1 (prod-us-east)
- Platform components: orchestrator commit-queue, prewarm worker, edge-proxy cookie routing
- Canary rollout: weight progressed from 5% -> 25% over a 12m window with prewarm mirroring enabled

Steps to reproduce (observed consistently in lab after reproduction):
1) Configure tenant pin to model redwood/open-13B-v1 with rollout policy that includes a 15% canary weight and prewarm mirror enabled.
2) Push a burst of warm-up traffic (simulated 300 RPS sustained for 90s) to the tenant route to trigger prewarm and autoscaler interactions.
3) Immediately rotate the client keepalive (simulate reconnects) for a cohort of sessions to exercise handshake code paths.
4) Observe routing telemetry and model assignment for the tenant session IDs.

Observed behavior:
- Orchestrator shows elevated pin_commit_latency metrics (spikes to 600–800ms) and an internal queue backlog labeled "epoch-fence". During queue backlog windows the control plane acknowledged the pin but did not atomically publish the new routing snapshot to all edge shards.
- Edge proxy logs show cookie flag updates out-of-order and a small fraction of edge workers served the stale snapshot that still referenced the canary assignment.
- Result: mixed routing where some session handshake renewals landed on canary despite explicit pin on the control plane.

Expected behavior:
- Pin handshake should be committed and observed by all edge shards within the configured commit window (<=200ms). No session should be routed to a variant other than the pinned model unless an explicit fallback or compatibility policy applies.

Temporary workaround (applied with customer consent):
- Reduced prewarm mirror concurrency for lexicon-dedicated-1 to 0 to avoid prewarm-induced commit queue pressure.
- Increased orchestrator commit-window to force synchronous commit for the tenant route. Both actions reduced observed deviation to <1% within 10 minutes.

Investigation notes and hypothesis:
- Root cause hypothesis: a commit-queue spike in the orchestrator allowed acknowledgement of pin-handshake to return to control plane clients while the snapshot publish to edge shards lagged due to serialization order inversion. The publish path interleaves prewarm state reconciliation which can reorder epoch fence operations when prewarm mirror actors are busy.
- Secondary contributor: edge-proxy cookie write path applies routing snapshot updates asynchronously and lacks a pin-staleness check, so an edge worker that processed a keepalive during the lag window resumed session assignment using the old routing table.

Proposed remediation (short and long term):
- Short term: patch orchestrator to add fast-path synchronous commit when tenant is pinned and dedicated flag set. Deploy to prod-us-east as hotfix (PR linked).
- Medium term: add a pin-staleness detector on edge: if a session handshake sees a pin mismatch against control-plane TTL, force immediate revalidate before assigning variant.
- Long term: reorder prewarm reconciliation to publish routing snapshot first, then reconcile prewarm state to avoid interleaving that causes epoch-fence inversion.

Customer communication plan:
- Notified customer 2026-03-10 09:12 PST with initial observations and temporary mitigations. Planned follow-up with permanent fix ETA: 2026-03-16.
- Offer extended logging window and priority monitoring for the customer until fix is rolled out.

Next steps:
- ENG: land orchestrator hotfix PR #852 -> rollout to prod-us-east canary nodes 2026-03-13.
- SRE: enable additional tracing for pin_commit_latency and export granular per-shard snapshot-sequence logs.
- Support: schedule customer call to review mitigation and coordinate patch deployment windows.
Support (2026-03-10 09:12) - Logged by Maya: Customer reports mixed outputs when pinned. Escalated to SRE and ENG.
SRE (2026-03-10 09:28) - Initial triage: observed pin_commit_latency spike in prod-us-east; reproduction attempt in staging shows similar behaviour when prewarm concurrency high.
Customer (LexiconMedia admin, 2026-03-10 09:35) - "We started seeing 15-20% of sessions returning results that mismatch our expected tokenizer; this affects search relevance."
ENG (2026-03-10 11:02) - Jorge: Identified commit-queue ordering inversion; drafting PR to add fast-path sync commit for pinned tenants. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/852
Support (2026-03-10 13:40) - Temporary mitigation applied: prewarm concurrency set to 0; customer reports immediate improvement. Monitoring continues.
ENG (2026-03-12 08:20) - Deployed hotfix to canary ring; initial telemetry shows pin_commit_latency 80–120ms and no observed re-routes for 6h.
SRE (2026-03-12 09:05) - Action: schedule full rollout during low-traffic window 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLens reports that SSE chat responses repeatedly stall mid-generation during multi-minute conversations. This started after yesterday's auth rollout that introduced shorter session token TTLs and a synchronous revalidation path for streaming requests.

Impact:
- Intermittent but reproducible stalls mid-response for ~30-90s, then eventual connection close.
- Affects only dedicated customer pools in us-east; estimated ~6% of streaming sessions for BrightLens over the last 12 hours.
- Customers observe degraded UX in live agent assistant and automated reports.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: redwood-dedicated-us-east-3
- Edge/Proxy version: edge-proxy@v2.14.0 (released 2026-03-09 03:10 UTC)
- Auth service: token-rotation feature enabled (short-ttl mode)
- Serving runtime: rw-runtime@1.7.3

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer + reproduced by Support):
1) Start a long SSE chat request with an input that triggers ~600-900 tokens of generation (customer provided corpus).
2) Allow the session to run for ~2–6 minutes (token TTL window).
3) The client sends the next keepalive/chunk; at this point the auth token has rotated on the client side and a refresh flow occurs.
4) Server stops emitting generation tokens for 30–90s (no SSE chunks), then eventually the connection closes with a 502/connection-reset in the client.

Observed behavior:
- Worker logs show repeated auth-service calls with increased latency and intermittent 401/timeout responses.
- Edge-proxy reports: "authz-check: blocking verification for connection_id=<redacted>" followed by a backoff and no write to socket.
- Serving runtime continues CPU work but kernel output is not flushed to socket (socket write path is gated by auth middleware).

Expected behavior:
- Token rotation should not block in-flight streaming generation. If a revalidation is required, it should not cause stalls; a graceful 401 and reconnect or async verification should be used.

Relevant logs (excerpted):
- edge-proxy: [2026-03-10T09:14:22Z] authz-check start conn=<id> token_age=301s
- auth-service: [2026-03-10T09:14:22Z] verifyToken slow (p99=1.3s) backing-off to external-kms
- serving-runtime: [2026-03-10T09:14:24Z] flush-to-socket blocked waiting on auth for conn=<id>
- edge-proxy: [2026-03-10T09:15:45Z] authz-check failure: upstream timeout 10s

Workarounds attempted by Support/Customer:
- Increased keepalive frequency on client -> no reliable change in stall frequency.
- Customer rolled back client-side token refresh to refresh earlier than TTL expiry -> reduced occurrences but not practical as a long-term fix.
- Support temporarily increased token TTL for the impacted dedicated pool (mitigation).

Notes:
- This appears correlated with the auth rollout that made token verification synchronous on the streaming request path (edge-proxy). Previous behavior cached verification result per-connection for the token TTL and did not block streaming.
- The problem reproduces reliably against the dedicated pool when token TTL < ~5 minutes and when external KMS responses spike.

Additional notes:
Mitigation: Increased session token TTL for BrightLens dedicated pool and rolled back synchronous verification on edge-proxy (hotfix edge-proxy@v2.14.1). Permanent fix: implement async verification + per-connection positive cache; PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1198.
Rollout notes: v2.14.1 deployed to us-east dedicated pools 2026-03-11 22:30 UTC. Post-deploy monitoring shows stall rate returned to baseline. Customer notified and accepted workaround. Follow-up action: add unit/integration tests for streaming path under auth rotation and add a perf guard for auth-service latency to prevent blocking streaming worker threads. Postmortem page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Stream+Auth+Rotation+Postmortem
Add integration test for streaming + token rotation (owner: Edge Eng)
Instrument auth-service KMS fallback to alert when p95 > 500ms (owner: Auth Eng)
Add canary rollout gating for auth-related changes (owner: SRE)
Notify product about change in token TTL semantics and update docs (owner: Docs)
payload.summary: SSE streaming stalls mid-generation after short-lived auth token rotation

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer Finexa Payments is onboarding a per-tenant SIEM webhook and requires cryptographic evidence that: events are delivered in tenant-specific total order, each delivery is unique (no replay), and retention checksums are available for a 30-day window. They also want signed delivery receipts that can be sent to auditors.

Impact:
- Compliance: customer cannot complete SOC evidence package without proof of ordered, non-replayed delivery.
- Production: SIEM ingestion currently drops events when out-of-order is detected by their consumer; they require a signed ordered lane to avoid data gaps.

Customer environment / setup:
- Customer tenant id: finexa-prod-87
- Ingestion target: on-prem Graylog cluster via webhook endpoint (mutual TLS)
- Expected volume: ~1.2k events/minute (bursty peaks to 5k/min)
- Current Redwood config: audit-forwarder v2.1 (webhook delivery), per-tenant API key, default retry/backoff

Steps to reproduce / observed behaviour:
1) Finexa configured webhook with mTLS and provided CIDR allowlist.
2) Events with sequence meta generated by Redwood (x-redwood-seq) sometimes arrive out-of-order at the customer's collector during short Green/Blue deploys.
3) Customer's collector rejects out-of-order events, creating gaps in SIEM.
4) Customer requested a compliance artifact demonstrating non-repudiable delivery (signed receipt with nonce + sequence) for a rolling 30-day window.

Expected behaviour:
- Per-tenant monotonic sequence numbers (or vector clock) and a signed delivery receipt per HTTP 2xx acknowledging the canonicalized event ID and sequence.
- Retries should not create indistinguishable duplicates: replay protection via per-request nonce and server-signed replay-proof HMAC included in header.
- Proof-of-immutability manifest for daily bundles stored to customer-controlled S3 or via signed manifest JSON with timestamped checkpoints.

Actual behaviour:
- Current system sets x-redwood-seq but does not provide auditor-friendly signed receipts or a replay-proof header. Some sequences can be temporarily re-ordered across short deployment windows.

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- sample_payloads.json (10 events showing seq: 1203,1204,1206,1205)
- webhook_response_logs.txt (shows 200 OK from Redwood with no delivery-receipt header)
- curl_output_with_tls_handshake.txt

Customer asks (requested artifacts):
1) Specification of the delivered ordering guarantee and any deployment windows where ordering might be temporarily relaxed.
2) Short-term workaround to guarantee in-order delivery for Finexa's tenant (can disable canary routing or pin a single delivery engine).
3) An evidence bundle for auditors: signed receipts for the last 7 days (per-event small sample: 100 events/day) and a plan to produce rolling 30-day manifests showing daily checksums and signed checkpoints.
4) Example headers/verification steps and a small verification script they can run to validate receipts locally.

Priority/notes:
- Customer legal/compliance team has a deadline 2026-03-20 to submit preliminary evidence. They flagged this as time-sensitive.
- Recommend coordinated response with SRE/Serving runtime and Security for key attestation approach.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 14:22 - Support (Liam Chen): Acknowledged. Triage and will loop in SRE and Security. Requested immediate logs from customer's collector to confirm drop pattern.
2026-03-11 09:03 - SRE (Maya Patel): Noted that our current forwarder provides x-redwood-seq but ordering can be relaxed during rolling deploys if requests are routed across engines. Investigating single-engine pinning as a short-term workaround.
2026-03-11 16:45 - Security (Ethan Wong): Suggested HMAC over canonicalized event body + seq + nonce signed with rotating per-tenant key. Drafting attestation pattern for compliance teams.
2026-03-12 08:31 - Support (Liam Chen): Confirmed we can offer 7-day signed receipt export within 48 hours as interim deliverable; working on the extraction query and signing process.
2026-03-12 12:10 - Customer (Finexa - Rachel Liu): Appreciated the interim plan, asked for an example verification script and confirmation that signed receipts will include a timestamp and key-id for key rotation traceability.
Checked audit-forwarder logs (prod/us-east-1) for tenant finexa-prod-87 between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-10. Observed intermittent seq gaps coinciding with canary swap windows around 03:14 and 14:10 UTC.
Confirmed x-redwood-seq is assigned at ingestion time by the collector service, but the webhook dispatcher does not currently attach a signed receipt header. Retries are idempotent on event-id but indistinguishable from replay without nonce.
Short-term mitigation validated: modifying routing policy to pin tenant to delivery engine instance pool reduces out-of-order incidents in a 4-hour canary test (no reordering observed across 12k events).
Security proposed HMAC structure: HMAC-SHA256 over canonicalized JSON (sorted keys, UTF-8, no whitespace) + seq + nonce + iso8601 timestamp. Header: X-Redwood-Receipt: keyId=rot-2026-02, sig=base64(hmac), ts=2026-03-12T08:00:00Z, seq=1206, nonce=uuid-v4. This meets auditor needs for traceable key-id and time.
SRE notes: need a small feature in audit-forwarder to produce and persist receipts (and expose export job). Implementation estimated at 3-5 engineer-days to produce signed receipts for a historical window and to add runtime header emission for future deliveries.
Risk: per-tenant signing key lifecycle needs to be integrated with KMS for rotation and access logs. Security suggests a temporary signing key with HSM-backed attest for the 7-day export, then transition to long-term KMS-managed keys for rolling 30-day manifests.
SRE to provide a short-term routing config to pin finexa-prod-87 to a single delivery engine and monitor for 48 hours (owner: Maya Patel).
Security to produce signing spec and sample verification script (owner: Ethan Wong).
Support to produce 7-day signed-receipt export for customer (owner: Liam Chen) and deliver as tar.gz with verification instructions.
Product to evaluate longer-term feature request for persistent per-event receipts and manifest generation (owner: Priya Nair).
(pending) Interim export scheduled: Support to deliver signed receipts for 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-11 by 2026-03-14. Final resolution depends on product implementation of per-event receipts and manifest automation.
payload.summary: Per-tenant ordered webhook delivery with nonce and replay-proof evidence for SIEM ingestion

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent spikes in end-to-end inference latency and occasional timeouts during periods of high concurrent streaming traffic. Symptoms are more pronounced after short bursts of requests and persist even when the serving runtime shows healthy token throughput.

Impact: Several user-facing features at NovaScribe experienced degraded responsiveness for ~5-30s windows, leading to user timeouts and feature degradation. No model correctness regressions observed.

Environment: Customer uses Redwood Dedicated cluster in us-east, SDK v1.3.2 (Node and Python clients), requests over TLS through API gateway. Dedicated pool sized according to contract and reporting normal GPU utilization in CloudWatch dashboards.
1) Use SDK v1.3.2 with default client settings (maxConnectionsPerHost=2, aggressive retry strategy).
2) Start 30 concurrent streaming chat sessions that each send an initial prompt simultaneously.
3) Observe end-to-end latency for first token across sessions and any 504/timeout errors from the SDK.
4) Repeat with SDK config: increase pool to 8 and disable exponential retry to compare behavior.
Customer-provided SDK client logs (abridged):
[2026-03-10T14:21:03Z] WARN request_retry: attempt=1 host=api.redwood.example.com queue_time_ms=324 context=stream-init
[2026-03-10T14:21:03Z] ERROR request_timeout: request_id=abc123 elapsed_ms=15000 status=timeout
[2026-03-10T14:21:05Z] INFO socket_status: opened=2 in_use=2 idle=0 total_attempts=18
[2026-03-10T14:21:30Z] WARN retry_backoff: backoff_ms=8000 attempts=3 jitter=0.0

Gateway logs show many simultaneous TLS handshakes followed by TCP TIME_WAIT spikes on gateway hosts during the window. Serving metrics do NOT show corresponding GPU saturation; token service QPS remains within expected range.
Initial hypothesis: problem originated in serving runtime. Validation: serving runtime metrics (latency and token throughput) stayed normal, GPUs not saturated.
Conclusion: issue likely client-side or gateway-level resource exhaustion leading to request queueing before reaching runtime.
Observed SDK defaults: maxConnectionsPerHost=2 and aggressive exponential backoff without jitter in v1.3.2. Under bursty concurrency, the SDK serialized pending requests behind the small connection pool; combined with long backoff windows and no jitter, many clients retried in lock-step (retry bursts), causing transient queueing and perceived latency spikes.
Additional contributing factor: short socket idle timeout at the gateway + high connection churn produced many sockets in TIME_WAIT, causing ephemeral port exhaustion on gateway frontends and increasing TLS handshake latency for new connections.
Reproduction verified in-house using synthetic load: with SDK default settings we reproduced 5–20s tail latencies and request timeouts; increasing pool and enabling jitter eliminated most spikes.
Telemetry: traces show requests spending majority of time in SDK-level client queueing (queued_ms) and time in TLS handshake rather than in serving runtime.
Customer applied temporary mitigations: updated SDK config to maxConnectionsPerHost=8 and reduced retry maxAttempts to 2 with randomized jitter; enabled HTTP keepalive and increased OS ephemeral port range on their gateway. This eliminated the immediate 5-30s spikes.
Recommendation to ops: add connection reuse and tune gateway TCP TIME_WAIT reuse to reduce churn until SDK patch deployed.
Root cause: combined client SDK connection pool small default and non-jittered exponential backoff produced synchronized retry bursts, which—together with gateway ephemeral socket churn—caused queuing and perceived inference latency. Serving runtime was healthy.
Fix implemented: SDK patch released in clientsdk v1.3.5 that increases default pool to 8 for dedicated-class customers, changes retry policy to use full jittered backoff by default, and exposes clear doc strings for pool/timeouts. Gateway-side guidance added to recommendations.
Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood/clientsdk/pull/3421
Customer status: NovaScribe upgraded to v1.3.5 and confirmed latency spikes resolved in production. Follow-up monitoring window of 72 hours completed with no recurrence.
Postmortem tasks: update QuickStart docs to call out pool and retry defaults for streaming workloads; add guidance to Dedicated onboarding checklist; create alert rule for SDK queue_time_ms exceeding 200ms in API gateway metrics.
[Support - 2026-03-10] Asha Kapoor: Customer reports intermittent 5-30s latency spikes affecting streaming chat. They included SDK logs and screenshots of increased client-side queueing.
[Customer - 2026-03-10] NovaScribe SRE (Erik M.): We see the problem only during bursts. Serving looks fine. Please advise whether we need to scale Dedicated pool.
[Support - 2026-03-11] Liam Chen: Initial triage suggests client connection pool defaults + retry logic. Can you temporarily increase connection pool in SDK and report back?
[Customer - 2026-03-11] Erik M.: Increased pool to 8 and enabled keepalive per instructions — spikes disappeared in our test. Waiting for your SDK patch for long-term fix.
[Eng - 2026-03-11] Priya Nair (SRE): Observed TIME_WAIT spike on gateway. Recommend tuning ephemeral port range and enabling reuse as stopgap. Filed INT-3245 to track gateway OS tuning.
[Support - 2026-03-12] Liam Chen: Released clientsdk v1.3.5 (PR #3421) with default changes and jittered backoff. NovaScribe has validated in prod. Marking as resolved after 72-hour monitoring window.
payload.summary: Intermittent high inference latency during concurrent streams due to ephemeral socket exhaustion + retry bursts
