Issue summary:
Customer reports brief increases in p50 latency (50-120ms above baseline) across eu-west for requests pinned to EU residency. The spike correlates with background residency-refresh events and at times results in a short fallback to a US egress path for a subset of requests.

Impact:
- Intermittent p50 latency increases seen by NovusHealth web app users in EU region during business hours.
- No customer-observed 5xxs or lost responses; errors are not reported.
- Affects SLA-sensitive flows that must remain EU-e2e due to data residency constraints.

Environment:
- Tenant: novus-prod (enterprise/private deployment using Redwood Private control plane)
- Region: eu-west primary, failover to us-east seen in traces
- Models: redwood-v1-medium production pin
- Time window: recurring ~every 10-18 minutes for short bursts (30-120s).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send 50-100 small-chat requests pinned to EU residency over 5 minutes from NovusHealth frontend.
2) Observe p50 and trace egress path.
3) At ~10-18 minute cadence some requests show 150-220ms added latency and traces indicate egress hop to us-east for ~30-90s.

Observed behavior:
- Traces show control-plane residency-refresh job runs and a small fraction of tokens pick a route that resolves to a US edge before the pin refresh fully completes.
- Client-side retried requests are fine but initial p50 moves up.

Expected behavior:
- Pin refresh should be atomic for an active token or should prefer sticky existing egress until refresh window closes. No cross-region egress should be observed for enterprise tenants with strict residency.

Logs/links:
- Sample trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/novus/trace-20260310-1223
- Control plane job run logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/app/control-plane/2026-03-10-refresh

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 09:42 - NovusHealth (Customer): Provided several trace IDs and noted spikes correspond to internal token refresh cycles. Customer is concerned about EU egress during bursts due to compliance reviews.
2026-03-13 11:05 - NovusHealth (Customer): Customer accepted temporary mitigation if we limit any cross-region egress to under 0.01% and will await permanent fix. Asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether this needs a contractual change.
2026-03-10: Collected traces and control-plane job schedules. Identified correlation between residency-lock-refresh and p50 spikes.
2026-03-11: Replayed refresh job in staging. Confirmed staggered refresh can leave partial routing entries where edge selection falls back to default egress resolver (which in our setup can be US edge for some DNS answers).
2026-03-11: Rate of affected requests ~0.5-1% during window on replay for tenant with normal TTL; effect increases if client side pre-resolve behavior is present.
2026-03-12: Root cause hypothesis: control-plane worker stagger combined with DNS cache TTL and edge ip rotation causes a small race where egress resolution prefers a non-EU edge until the new residency stamp propagates to the routing layer.
2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation approach: set a 'refresh-sticky' flag for enterprise tenants so that in-flight tokens continue to honor previous routing entries until refresh completes, and reduce stagger window to 10s for tenants with strict residency.
2026-03-12: Code PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/412 (adds tenant-level refresh-sticky flag and configuration toggle)
2026-03-13: Verified in staging with NovusHealth-like footprint: p50 jitter eliminated in 5 test runs; fallback rate reduced to <0.01%.
2026-03-13: Risk assessment: low risk to broader fleet if gated by tenant flag; requires config push to Private control plane for Novus tenant.
2026-03-13: Linked INT ticket for Ops to perform config push: INT-2243.
2026-03-13: Temporary mitigation scheduled: set refresh-sticky=true and reduce worker stagger to 10s for novus-prod during maintenance window 2026-03-14 02:00-03:00 UTC. This is a config-only change for Private control plane.
2026-03-13: Customer notified and accepted maintenance window. Post-change verification plan includes 1 hour of synthetic traffic and sampling traces every 5 minutes.
Planned permanent fix: make refresh-sticky default for tenants with data-residency policy and add an atomic refresh propagation mechanism (tracked in backlog, target: next sprint).
Follow-ups: Update runbook for residency refresh (confluence link), add monitoring alert for cross-region egress rate for enterprise tenants, and include mention in Customer Release Notes for NovusHealth.
Status: Mitigation approved and queued; permanent fix scheduled.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightMetrics reported intermittent control-plane authentication failures from their private deployment. Calls from the customer agents to Redwood control-plane started failing TLS mTLS verification after a firewall/egress gateway change on their side.

Impact:
- Control-plane heartbeats from fleet agents bounce with mTLS errors, causing short-lived registration losses and transient task scheduling failures.
- Affects ~12 agents across two dedicated subnets. No model-serving requests were affected directly, but agent reconnections caused short scheduling delays.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC)
- prod-us-west region (us-west-2)
- Control-plane endpoint: cp-prod.redwood-internal.example.net
- Customer egress sits behind a corporate TLS-terminating gateway/proxy (appliance vendor: SquidCorp v4.1)

Observed at: 2026-03-10 07:43 UTC

1) Customer deploys agent with pinned control-plane cert verification enabled.
2) Egress gateway performs outbound TLS termination/inspection and re-initiates TLS to control-plane.
3) Agents attempt mTLS auth; control-plane rejects handshake with client-chain errors.

Note: Reproducible when gateway is on path; bypassing gateway (direct internet egress) makes the problem disappear.
[control-plane] 2026-03-10T07:43:12Z ERROR auth: client handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
[agent-17] 2026-03-10T07:43:12Z WARN heartbeat: control-plane rejected connection: client cert chain incomplete
[tcpdump] TLS ClientHello shows SNI: cp-prod.redwood-internal.example.net, ALPN: h2
[proxy-inspect] Re-originated TLS to cp-prod.redwood-internal.example.net; forwarded client cert length: 0 bytes (expected ~2.1KB)

- Initial hypothesis: corporate proxy is terminating mTLS and not forwarding the full client certificate chain, or it is stripping TLS client cert info when re-establishing TLS.
- Collected packet captures at agent and gateway; capture shows agent sends full client certificate chain in TLS ClientAuth, but the gateway's re-originated connection omits client cert (gateway performs TLS termination and re-init).
- Control-plane logs show 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority' followed by 'client cert chain incomplete'.
- Customer confirmed a recent gateway firmware update that enabled 'certificate rewriting' for outbound TLS inspection.
- Reproduction verified by toggling gateway to TCP pass-through mode: when pass-through is enabled control-plane auth succeeds immediately.
- Created internal INT-4451 to track engineering follow-up on control-plane behavior when client certs are absent/trimmed by middleboxes.

Workaround implemented: BrightMetrics reverted the gateway setting to preserve client cert information by enabling TLS passthrough for control-plane hostnames and whitelisting cp-prod.redwood-internal.example.net. After change, all agents re-registered and heartbeats stabilized.

Permanent guidance provided to customer:
- Configure egress proxy to either: 1) perform TCP passthrough for mTLS endpoints, or 2) if TLS inspection is required, configure the proxy to re-inject the original client certificate chain (some appliances support 'forward client cert' or 'proxy-cert-forwarding').
- Add control-plane hostnames to proxy whitelist where mTLS is required.

Internal follow-up:
- INT-4451 assigned to infra-auth team to harden control-plane error messaging and provide clearer telemetry when client certs are absent.
- Add a KB entry in runbook: 'Detecting and mitigating client cert truncation by egress proxies'.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 09:12 - Customer (BrightMetrics - infra): We've rolled a new firmware yesterday; enabling TLS inspection is the only change. We can toggle passthrough for a test subnet if needed.
2026-03-10 11:30 - BrightMetrics: Enabled TCP passthrough for control-plane hostnames as requested. Agents immediately re-registered; confirmed heartbeats healthy.
2026-03-11 14:20 - SRE (internal): Logged INT-4451 for infra-auth improvements. Suggested adding clearer control-plane metric for 'client cert missing' with a counter and alert threshold.
payload.summary: mTLS client certificate chain truncated by customer egress proxy causing control-plane auth failures on private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a midday window on 2026-03-10 LuminaAnalytics observed elevated p95/p99 latency for their dedicated routes backed by the us-west reserved pool. The symptom set looked like an intermittent GPU scarcity: short (~30–120s) periods where new attach requests failed or were delayed and throughput across their routes dropped by ~40% causing customer-facing request timeouts.

Impact:
- Customer reported multiple user-facing timeouts and elevated error rates across two critical routes for ML-driven recommendations.
- Observed p99 generator latency increased from ~220ms to 900–1400ms during windows.
- Service degraded for ~18 minutes total across a 3-hour window; impacted business-critical queries.

Timeline / Key events (high-level):
- 12:08 UTC: First alert from Lumina monitoring (elevated p99).
- 12:09 UTC: Support ticket opened and triaged.
- 12:10–12:15 UTC: SRE observed burst of attach failures (attach timeout) in allocator logs for us-west.
- 12:12 UTC: Autoscaler triggered a decision to shrink one overprovisioned slice; shortly after, attach latencies spiked.
- 12:18 UTC: Autoscaler re-expanded but with a ~40s cooldown; intermittent shortages continued until 12:26 UTC.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool: lumina-usw-reserved-1 (multi-GPU A100/NVLink mix).
- Region: us-west-2.
- Routes affected: /v1/generate (high throughput), /v1/chat (medium throughput).
- Models: gptx-13b-int8 (primary), redwood-chat-7b-v2 (fallback).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Sustained medium burst of short-lived sessions from customer test cohort (many short streams, 1–3s each).
2) Autoscaler observed drop in moving-average attach utilization (because short streams complete before sustained attach metrics reflect them) and shrunk a slice to reclaim capacity.
3) Immediately after shrink, a cohort of new attach requests arrives; allocator cannot attach into the reduced pool quickly enough -> attach timeouts and delayed batching -> p99 spike.

Observed behaviour & logs (excerpt summary):
- allocator logs (us-west): attach_timeout 2026-03-10T12:11:07Z tenant=lumina route=/v1/generate attempt=3
- autoscaler decision log: shrink slice id=slice-19 reason=util_moving_avg_below_threshold window=60s
- telemetry: moving_avg_attach_util=0.48 at 12:10, instantaneous_attach_rate spike to 2.4x baseline at 12:11
- serving-runtime: increased NVLink stall counters during the shortage windows (nvlink_io_wait++ in 12:11–12:20)

Hypothesis (triage):
- Autoscaler metric window/granularity (60s moving average) causes hysteresis: short-lived bursts drive instantaneous attach demand but do not raise the moving average quickly, triggering inappropriate shrink decisions.
- Shrink operations have a cooldown and require time to re-expand; this combination results in transient GPU scarcity during bursty short-stream workloads (noisy-cohort effect).
- Background snapshotter jobs on a subset of hosts also increased NVMe IO causing attach latency amplification during that window (secondary contributor).

Temporary mitigation / Workaround applied:
- Support requested emergency temporary override of autoscaler - disabled slice shrink for lumina-usw-reserved-1 for 30 minutes at 12:20 UTC (manual hold).
- Increased autoscaler moving-average window threshold and added a short-term rule to consider instantaneous_attach_rate spikes before shrinks.
- Customer applied client-side retry/backoff (exponential jitter) to reduce immediate fan-in of attaches.

Investigation next steps / planned remediation:
- Engineering to adjust autoscaler heuristic: add fast-path detection for high instantaneous attach rate to prevent shrink while short-burst demand is present (PR referenced below).
- Add a pre-shrink check: if instantaneous_attach_rate > 1.5x baseline in last 15s, block shrink or delay by X seconds.
- Improve telemetry: surface instantaneous_attach_rate and short-stream histograms in Console per-slice.
- Analyze background snapshot schedule on affected hosts and consider staggering to reduce IO coupling with peak attach windows.

Owner / Contacts:
- SRE owner: Daniel Kim (assignee).
- Support liaison: Aisha Patel (reporter).
- Customer contact: Maria Chen (Lumina analytics infra lead) via #support-lumina slack channel and lumina@contacts.lumina.com.

References and crosslinks:
- Slack: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SUPPORT/p167849xxx (internal triage thread)
- Allocator debugger trace: s3://redwood-alloc-traces/us-west/2026-03-10/trace-931999.log
- Related PR (short-term): github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1708
- Runbook consulted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/dedicated-autoscale-triage

Acceptance criteria for full resolution:
- No producer-initiated shrinks for lumina routes during short-burst patterns without a fast-path check in place.
- Autoscaler changes merged and rolled out to canary and us-west with monitoring dashboards for instantaneous_attach_rate.
- Post-deploy 72-hour observation window showing no recurrence for similar workload pattern.

2026-03-10 12:13 — Support (Aisha Patel): Initial triage complete, elevated p99 confirmed. Escalated to SRE. Notified customer of ongoing investigation.
2026-03-10 12:16 — SRE (Daniel Kim): Found autoscaler shrink event at 12:12 followed by attach timeouts. Temporarily pausing automatic shrinks for the reserved pool. Gathering allocator traces.
2026-03-10 12:22 — Customer (Maria Chen, Lumina): Confirmed temporary override reduced timeouts but we still saw a smaller spike at 12:21. Will enable client-side backoff in the interim.
2026-03-11 09:02 — Engineering (Priya Nair): Draft design posted for fast-path check to autoscaler. Test plan to be added and PR opened against autoscaler core. See PR 1708.
2026-03-11 16:40 — SRE (Daniel Kim): Instrumentation requested for instantaneous_attach_rate; dashboard ticket created and linked. Continuing investigation into snapshot scheduling overlap.
workaround_applied; engineering change in progress (autoscaler fast-path detection). Full resolution pending deploy and 72h observation.
payload.summary: Autoscaler metric granularity hysteresis leading to short-lived GPU scarcity in us-west dedicated pool

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 401/redirect-to-login immediately after SSO redirect completes. Issue started within an hour of our ingress controller (edge-proxy) upgrade (v2.8.1 -> v2.9.0) in customers private cluster.

Impact:
- Multiple end users are unable to complete SSO login to Redwood Console behind the customer's private deployment.
- Session creation appears to succeed on the identity provider side, but subsequent requests to the console return 401 and users are returned to IdP for re-auth.
- Affects all tenant admins and many user sessions intermittently.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) running Redwood Private 1.7.2
- Edge/ingress controller managed by customer (k8s) recently upgraded to v2.9.0 on 2026-03-12 08:15 UTC
- Region: us-west (customer region)

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Initiate SSO login via SAML to the company's IdP (Okta) from console.redwood.private
2) Complete IdP authentication and return to Redwood with SAML assertion
3) Observe final redirect to console and intermittent failure with 401 or immediate redirect back to IdP

Observed behavior:
- SAML assertion is accepted (IdP logs show successful assertion).
- Support logs show session cookie being set in the response, but browser does not send the cookie on subsequent requests in some cases.
- When cookie is not sent, API returns 401 and user is redirected to IdP.

Expected behavior:
- Session cookie should be set and included in subsequent browser requests, preserving the logged-in session.

Relevant logs/snippets (redacted):
- Identity-proxy set-cookie header: session_id=...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Domain=console.redwood.private
- Browser devtools (problematic flow): response sets SameSite=None was not present; subsequent request does not include cookie.
- Edge-proxy (v2.9.0) access log shows initial post-auth response 200, followed by GET to /api/me returning 401 with no cookie header.

Immediate workaround provided by Support:
- Customer rolled back ingress controller to v2.8.1 and reported immediate reduction in failures.
- Temporary mitigation: configure IdP-initiated login to include prompt=consent (not a reliable fix).

Attachments provided by customer:
- HAR files (redacted), ingress upgrade job logs, Okta SAML logs, screenshots of browser devtools

Initiate SSO login via SAML to console.redwood.private
Complete IdP authentication and return to Redwood with SAML assertion
Observe final redirect to console and intermittent 401 or redirect back to IdP
SAML assertion accepted by Redwood but browser does not send session cookie on follow-up requests intermittently
Identity-proxy sets SameSite=Lax on Set-Cookie header in responses when ingress v2.9.0 is in path
Edge-proxy logs show 200 on POST SAML callback then 401 on subsequent /api/me without cookie
Session cookie is set with attributes compatible with cross-site redirects from IdP and is included in subsequent requests
Users remain logged in after SSO redirect completes
03/12 10:05 UTC - Support confirmed timing correlation between ingress upgrade and spike in SSO failures
03/12 11:20 UTC - Reproduced locally in staging by deploying ingress v2.9.0; observed SameSite attribute being rewritten from None to Lax in the response path
Hypothesis A: ingress v2.9.0 adds or normalizes SameSite attribute on Set-Cookie headers when certain proxy annotations are present, causing the cookie to be blocked on the IdP->SP redirect flow
Hypothesis B: header sanitization in the chain (edge-proxy -> identity-proxy) strips SameSite=None or Secure attribute in cross-site flows in some browser/agent combinations
03/12 13:40 UTC - Confirmed rollback to v2.8.1 removes the behavior (customer verified)
03/12 15:10 UTC - Collected packet traces showing Set-Cookie header values at each hop (edge, identity-proxy). Edge shows SameSite=Lax after upgrade; identity-proxy initially sets None.
Customer (NimbleFin) - 2026-03-12: We're seeing about ~30% of logins immediately fail after SSO completes. We rolled back ingress and it seemed to get better. Please advise.
Support (Asha) - 2026-03-12: Thanks for the report. We're investigating a potential SameSite header rewrite in your ingress upgrade. Can you share ingress annotations and any header rewrite rules?
Customer (NimbleFin) - 2026-03-12: Shared ingress values and the helm release notes for v2.9.0. No custom cookie rewrites were configured but they use the default proxy annotations.
SRE (Mateo) - 2026-03-12: Reproduced in staging with v2.9.0. Edge is rewriting SameSite=None to SameSite=Lax for cookies set during cross-site POST when strict-csp annotation is present. Opening INT-5021 for tracking with infra team.
Eng (Lena Chen) - 2026-03-13: Confirmed identity-proxy sets Set-Cookie with SameSite=None for SAML callback as expected. The rewrite happens at the edge when the response passes through header-normalizer middleware introduced in v2.9.0.
Support (Asha) - 2026-03-13: Notifying customer of root cause and recommended rollback (which they performed). Planning patch guidance for private deployments.
Customer (NimbleFin) - 2026-03-14: After rollback the problem is largely resolved. We're standing by for a permanent fix or a recommended ingress config.
Engineer (Mateo) - 2026-03-14: Patch identified - add explicit passthrough for Set-Cookie SameSite=None tokens or disable header-normalizer for cookie-related responses. Drafting advisory for private customers.
Root cause: header-normalizer middleware in ingress v2.9.0 rewrites SameSite=None to SameSite=Lax for cookies on cross-site POST/redirect responses when the strict-csp annotation is present. This prevents browsers from including the session cookie on IdP->SP redirects, causing apparent authentication failures.
Immediate action: customer rolled back ingress to v2.8.1 which restored previous behavior.
Permanent fix path: coordinate with ingress vendor/maintainers to add an explicit opt-out for SameSite normalization or update middleware to honor Set-Cookie attributes on upstream responses for known SSO callback endpoints. Alternatively, document a recommended ingress annotation to disable header-normalizer for private deployments using SSO.
Follow-ups: create KB article for private customers (owner: Mateo Ruiz), add an automated check in Redwood Private deployer to warn when ingress v2.9.0+ is detected and SSO endpoints are present (owner: Platform), link to INT-5021 for infra work.
Status: customer verified rollback success; patch advisory being drafted and expected to ship to customers 2026-03-20 after upstream coordination.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer's SCIM provisioning creates service accounts whose displayName contains emoji (e.g., 'ExportJob❤️') and long text. The IdP appears to base64-encode the displayName when emitting the SAML assertion (attribute urn:custom:displayName). The customer's private deployment identity-proxy strips trailing '=' padding on attribute values during header normalization, which corrupts the base64 blob. This results in the RBAC role-mapper failing to parse the attribute and no tenant-scoped roles being granted to the service account.

Impact: Scheduled export workers (service accounts) provisioned via SCIM cannot assume tenant-scoped roles and receive 403 on the scheduled job endpoints. The customer reports ~100 failed jobs over the last 24 hours; business impact is delayed nightly exports.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC), prod-us-east region. SCIM provisioning originates from Okta (SCIM connector v2). Identity-proxy version: v1.8.3 (private bundle). RBAC service version: 2.1.0.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Provision a service account via SCIM with a long displayName containing emoji (example: 'nightly-export-batch-2026-03-09-🚀').
2) Observe SCIM create event in Okta; Okta sends to Redwood SCIM endpoint.
3) Confirm user/service account exists in Redwood console.
4) Trigger scheduled job that uses the service account credentials (or run token exchange).
5) Job fails with 403 and logs show RBAC mapping did not find tenant binding.

Observed logs/symptoms:
- On the IdP side, SAML assertion contains attribute urn:custom:displayName with value looking like base64 (example: 'bm...Zy0yMDI2LTAzL...==').
- Identity-proxy access logs show header X-Raw-Assertion: 'urn:custom:displayName=bm...Zy0yMDI6LT0' (note trailing '==' changed to '=0' after header normalization).
- RBAC service logs: "role-mapper: attribute decode failed: invalid padding" and subsequently "no-tenant-binding for principal service-account:nightly-export-2026".
- Customer console shows service account present but lacking tenant bindings.

Requested from customer: SCIM payload (redacted), a sample SAML assertion (base64), and a HAR/wire capture of the assertion flow.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:04 - DataHealth (Customer): Provided redacted SCIM create payload and the raw SAML assertion. Noted that only service accounts created after 2026-03-08 are affected.
2026-03-11 09:15 - DataHealth (Customer): Re-ran a job; got 200 for the job that previously failed (confirmed one successful night run). Customer requests permanent fix and asks for root cause and recommended action for existing service accounts.
Hypothesis: Okta SCIM/displayName is being base64-encoded by the IdP because it contains non-ASCII (emoji) characters. The SAML path then emits the base64 string as an attribute value. Our identity-proxy has a legacy header normalization step which assumed header values would be UTF-8 strings and, when encountering characters outside an allowed set or when length > 120, performs URL-decoding and trims padding '=' characters (bug introduced in v1.7.9). Trimming '=' corrupts base64 payloads and causes downstream role-mapper to fail base64 decode, so the attribute used for role resolution becomes invalid.
Evidence collected:
- Decoded SAML assert: urn:custom:displayName = 'bm...==', decoded -> 'nightly-export-2026-03-09-🚀'.
- Identity-proxy sanitized header: padding replaced/mangled, visible in canary logs: 'bm...=0'.
- Role-mapper error trace: 'base64: invalid padding at offset 248'.
- Reproduced locally by sending a synthetic SAML assertion with base64-encoded displayName and passing through identity-proxy v1.8.3; observed same mangling.
Temporary mitigation tested: disable header padding trim in identity-proxy and restart subset; immediate repro job succeeded when routed through updated proxy.
Open questions:
- Whether other attributes may be affected (e.g., urn:custom:jobLabel) — quick scan shows a few other attributes with non-ascii may be base64-encoded by IdP.
- Whether SCIM configuration at customer side can be adjusted to avoid IdP base64-encoding (customer prefers not to remove emoji).
Next steps and owners:
- SRE/Platform (Marco): propose a hotfix to identity-proxy to preserve header raw values and only perform normalization for known safe attributes. Draft PR created. (see related_github_prs).
- Support (Aisha): coordinate with customer on re-provisioning plan and bulk remediation for existing affected service accounts.
Mitigation applied: We deployed a canary config change to the customer's identity-proxy (disabled header padding trim) which restored correct attribute delivery for test jobs. Customer confirmed a single repro job succeeded.
Permanent fix plan: merge PR to identity-proxy to avoid trimming '=' from header values and add unit tests for base64-like attributes. Add detection/alerting when attributes look like base64 but decode to non-ASCII characters and document recommended SCIM mapping.
Workarounds for customer until fix is fully rolled out:
- Re-provision affected service accounts (fast but may be disruptive).
- Update SCIM template to populate a separate ASCII-only attribute (e.g., serviceName) without emoji and map RBAC to that attribute.
Follow-ups:
- Patch release scheduled for 2026-03-15 to identity-proxy v1.8.4 with hotfix and tests.
- Support to run a bulk remediation script (optionally) to repair attribute values for already affected service accounts; script to be delivered after customer signs off.
Status: Waiting on Customer to sign off on patch rollout plan and choose remediation approach.
payload.summary: SCIM displayName with emoji base64-encoding mangles SAML attribute, blocking service-account scheduled jobs

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports unexpected duplicate downstream webhook side-effects after client retry during intermittent network blips. Impact: DocuServe observed duplicate invoice webhook posts causing double-processing in their accounting pipeline for ~4% of requests during a 9:13–9:45 UTC window. Environment: prod (us-east), enterprise tenant on dedicated routing policy, SDKs in use: python (v1.12.0) and typescript (v0.9.4).

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Start long-running chat with function-tool enabled and external webhook target configured.
2) Simulate short TCP connection drop on client side (client reconnect/retry logic triggers).
3) SDK emits retry and resends the request without a clear semantic ack from Redwood for the previously-accepted func/tool execution.
4) Downstream webhook receives second POST (same payload idempotency semantics not enforced server-side).

Observed behaviour: External webhook receives the same callback twice (duplicate side-effect). Customer notes this happens more often when client network retry uses immediate reconnect (no jitter) and when requests route through an edge proxy that strips a custom X-Client-Nonce header.

Expected behaviour: One of the following: (a) SDK-level dedupe prevents resubmission when server acknowledged execution; (b) server returns a definitive non-retryable ack that client can rely on; or (c) server exposes a replay-suppression token that downstream can use to dedupe side-effects.

Temporary workaround requested by customer: Guidance on SDK configuration to add jitter/backoff, ensure client preserves nonce header, and recommend webhook-side de-dup keys until a platform-level mitigation is available.
Start chat session with function/tool calling and webhook target configured
Induce client TCP disconnect (short blip) and allow SDK to retry immediately
Observe duplicate POSTs to the webhook target within a 30s window
Confirm client sdk versions and edge-proxy header retention behavior
2026-03-10T09:14:03Z DEBUG sdk-python: resend request id=inv-7421 nonce= (header stripped)
2026-03-10T09:14:04Z INFO serving-runtime: tool-exec ack sent internal_id=tx-98213 status=completed
2026-03-10T09:14:05Z WARN edge-proxy: dropped header X-Client-Nonce for connection 10.3.44.2
Initial triage (Support): Reproduced scenario in staging with an edge sidecar that canonicalizes headers; when X-Client-Nonce was removed by proxy, SDK retry produced a new nonce and server treated request as distinct. SRE found serving-runtime wrote a completed ack for the first execution (internal_id=tx-98213) but the client did not observe it due to connection drop. There is no opaque replay-suppression token exposed in the current API; server relies on client-supplied idempotency keys. Edge proxy config in customer's infra is stripping that key preflight.

Hypothesis: The platform's current contract assumes idempotency keys are preserved end-to-end. When proxies mutate headers (or when API keys are rotated mid-stream), dedupe fails. SDKs currently recommend per-request idempotency but do not enforce persisted session-scoped nonces across reconnects for streaming sessions.

SRE quick test: enabling sticky header passthrough at proxy prevented duplicates in controlled test. Code reference: platform ingress normalization codepath at router/header_normalizer.go: lines 122-145 (linked PR provided).
Duplicates causing double ingestion of webhook events resulting in accounting reconciliation issues. Estimated duplicate rate 3–5% during intermittent network events. Customer has temporarily paused automated reconciliation and is seeking a long term mitigation.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:22 - DocuServe Ops (customer): Provided webhook server logs and confirmed they rely on X-Client-Nonce for dedupe but use Apache proxy that rewrites some headers. Asked for guidance on platform-side short term mitigation.
2026-03-12 12:04 - Product (Design): Noted need for a platform-level replay-suppression token and cross-SDK guidance. Raised as follow-up to product backlog (linked: INT-91200).
Workaround provided: (a) configure edge proxy to preserve the client's idempotency header or proxy metadata; (b) apply SDK setting to persist and reuse a session-scoped idempotency key across reconnects (snippet provided). Platform follow-up: Product/SRE to design an explicit replay-suppression token in the API and add server-side dedupe when idempotency header absent. Next steps tracked in INT-91200 and INT-84021.
If you run into duplicates on webhook side-effects during client retries: ensure your proxies preserve idempotency headers, add client-side jitter/backoff, and consider persisting a session idempotency key in your client until the platform-level replay token is available.
payload.summary: Clarify client/server replay-suppression and acknowledgement contract for cross-SDK retries and external webhook side-effects

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that several trace links ("trace_id" -> trace view) are not present on console heatmaps or in the segmented usage rollups after nightly retention compaction. The missing links are only for queries that include a segmentation filter (org_id + route) and older than the retention window but still within the expected rollup TTL.

Impact:
- Multiple customers (first reported by NimbleMaps) see dashboards with empty trace-links on heatmap cells for historical data.
- Alert cards that rely on trace linking are firing without being able to attach traces, causing noise in on-call.
- Affects troubleshooting (support and SRE) for production incidents where historical traces are needed.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1)
- Console version: v2026.02.3
- Retention compaction job: retention-pruner v1.8.2 running nightly 03:30 UTC

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Query console heatmap for route: "/api/v1/ingest" with segmentation by org_id for timeframe 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28.
2. Click some heatmap cells to view attached trace links.
3. Note that ~15-20% of the cells that historically contained trace links now show "No traces available".
4. Run same query for a non-segmented time range -> trace links present as expected.

Observed behavior:
- Traces are present in raw span storage (customer provided S3 snapshot with spans), but console heatmap tile metadata lacks the trace_id references for segmented rollups.
- The usage rollup object for segmented keys shows token counts and p95 latency but has empty "trace_refs" arrays.

Expected behavior:
- Rollups that include trace references to sampled spans should retain a pointer (trace_id) for the top few representative traces even after compaction, so console cells can link back to traces for historical troubleshooting.

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- Example heatmap screenshot (attached to ticket)
- Redacted span bundle (S3 link) with representative trace ids
- Console query id: q_2026-03-11_9861 (customer saved query)

Additional notes:
- Customer believes the issue began after a retention-pruner configuration change rolled out 2026-03-02 that aggressively removed per-segment metadata earlier than the rollup TTL.

Initial triage (03/12): Support confirmed customer query and verified missing trace refs in rollup documents for segmented keys. Indexing and raw spans present in S3.
SRE triage (03/13): Replayed retention-pruner job in staging against a snapshot and observed that when compaction prunes per-segment ephemeral metadata, trace_refs are not migrated into the persistent rollup summary for segments with low sample counts. Potential race between rollup-merge and retention-pruner.
Engineering hypothesis (03/13): Edge case occurs when: 1) a segment receives sparse traffic, 2) rollup flush occurs close to retention cutoff, and 3) retention-pruner marks ephemeral metadata as expired before rollup-merge migrates trace_refs into the persistent bucket. This leaves the persisted rollup without trace pointers.
Evidence: grep of persisted rollup documents shows null/empty trace_refs only for segments whose last-rollup-timestamp is within 2 hours of retention TTL boundary.

2026-03-11 - Customer first opened support chat reporting missing trace links.
2026-03-12 - Ticket created; Support gathered query ids and artifacts.
2026-03-13 - SRE reproduced issue in staging with replayed compaction run; hypothesis formed.
2026-03-14 - Engineering started a patch to ensure rollup-merge promotes trace_refs before retention-pruner deletes ephemeral metadata.

For impacted customers temporarily: disable aggressive retention-pruner rollout (rollback to pre-2026-03-02 config) or increase segment retention cutoff by 48 hours to avoid race with rollup-merge. Support can also run an on-demand backfill job to repopulate trace_refs for the affected date ranges using raw span snapshots.
Customer-facing workaround shared to NimbleMaps on 2026-03-12: increase query window and remove segmentation filter until backfill completes (reduces granularity but restores trace links).
TBD - engineering patch in progress (PR referenced). Targeting forward-fix deployment 2026-03-16 and a one-off backfill job for affected date ranges. Post-deploy we will validate with the customer's sample queries and provide remediation notes.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3245 (in review as of 2026-03-14).

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 16:30 - Support (Aisha): Communicated temporary rollback option and workaround to NimbleMaps. Customer accepted backfill but asked for ETA on forward fix.
2026-03-14 15:05 - NimbleMaps (customer): Confirmed they can wait for 48h rollback; requested notification when backfill completes so they can validate dashboards.

Issue summary:
Customer observed a sustained elevated 5xx error rate (~8-12% of requests) for the NovaCRM account starting 2026-03-13 22:10 UTC. Errors manifest as a mixture of 502 and 504 responses from the API Gateway, and multiple upstream runtime SIGTERM/restart events. The issue surfaced after an automated load-shedding reassignment job ran for tenant weight rebalancing.

Impact:
- NovaCRM reported degraded application performance and partial feature outages for their end users (churn risk).
- Error rate elevated for all chat and embedding routes for the committed dedicated pool.
- Multiple customer requests timed out or returned 5xx for ~55 minutes before mitigation steps.

Environment:
- prod: us-east (dedicated gpu pool cluster r-w-12)
- Route types: streaming chat (long-lived), non-streaming text generation, embeddings
- Models in-use: rw-inference-v2 pinned for the customer's dedicated pool

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Scheduled load-shed reassignment job initiated to redistribute tenant weights across ephemeral proxies and router groups.
2) Routing table updates started rolling; some proxy nodes received higher inbound fan-in during reassignment.
3) Keepalive pruning kicked in concurrently on a subset of proxies due to FD pressure.
4) Upstream runtimes serving the tenant logged repeated preemption and SIGTERM as their worker pools attempted to gracefully drain.
5) The API Gateway returned 502/504 to customers when proxy handoffs timed out or connections were reset.

Logs and metrics collected:
- api-gateway access logs: surge in 502/504 from 22:10–23:05 UTC (sample attached in ticket).
- proxy metrics: AcceptQueueDepth spiked from 12 -> 156 on two proxies, FD_use 92%.
- runtime logs: repeated "Received SIGTERM for graceful shutdown" followed by "Worker exit: code 137" around 22:18 UTC.
- scheduler events: reassignment job started 22:05, completed 22:40 with several retries on node-bind failures.
- Observed KV cache evictions increase and backend latency (p95 token latency) rising from 120ms -> 420ms during the window.

Initial mitigation performed by Support/SRE:
- Paused ongoing reassignment sweep at 22:28 UTC.
- Manually rebalanced a subset of heavy routes away from saturated proxies at 22:35 UTC.
- Increased keepalive window temporarily to reduce pruning by 22:42 UTC.
Result: error rate decreased to baseline over ~20 minutes.
2026-03-13 22:22 UTC - Support (Mariana Lopez): Customer reports 8-12% 5xx on chat and embed routes. Escalating to SRE. Logged initial request id samples.
2026-03-13 22:30 UTC - SRE (Ethan Patel): Observed accept-queue spike and FD pressure on proxy-7 and proxy-9. Paused reassignment job. Requesting routing table snapshot and runtime core dumps.
2026-03-13 22:40 UTC - Customer (NovaCRM - ops): Noted partial recovery after you paused the job. Please advise on root cause and next steps to prevent recurrence.
2026-03-13 22:52 UTC - SRE (Ethan Patel): Manually rebalanced heavy-weight routes off proxy-9; increasing keepalive helped. Collecting runtime restart traces for postmortem.
2026-03-14 09:10 UTC - Support (Mariana Lopez): Follow-up email to customer with incident summary and interim mitigations. Awaiting confirmation on whether additional rollouts impacted other tenants.
Hypotheses: (1) The reassignment algorithm momentarily concentrated high-weight streaming routes on proxies with stale keepalive state, amplifying FD pressure and triggering pruning. (2) Runtime preemption logic is too aggressive when signaled by proxy-side connection resets, leading to worker exit instead of graceful drain. Evidence: accept-queue spikes align with reassignment windows; runtimes show SIGTERM + OOM-ish exits (exit code 137) consistent with degraded host resources. Next checks: full thread and heap profiles from runtimes during the window; router table diffs pre- and post-reassignment; check kernel-level closed socket counts and ulimit settings on affected proxies.
Short-term: Paused reassignment sweep during high-traffic windows and increased keepalive thresholds to avoid mass pruning. Implemented manual route smoothing to distribute heavy streams across healthy proxies.
Medium-term: Engineering to adjust reassignment throttle to consider live accept-queue depth and FD utilization metrics before moving weights. Plan to update runtime shutdown handling to wait longer for active streaming sessions and avoid premature SIGTERM escalation.
Follow-ups: Create an INT ticket to add a pre-flight check to the reassignment controller (INT-4051). Schedule a postmortem runbook for dedicated pool rebalances and update customer-facing guidance for maintenance windows. Target ETA for medium-term changes: 2026-04-02.
ENG: Implement pre-flight health gating for reassignment controller (linked INT-4051).
SRE: Add alert for AcceptQueueDepth > 100 sustained for 2m on any proxy (owner: SRE-routing).
DX: Notify affected customers about revised maintenance windows and provide mitigation guidance.
Postmortem: Owner assigned to Mariana Lopez, due 2026-03-20.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent request timeouts and long-tail latency when using structured-output (JSON) streaming mode. Problem appears after ~20-60s for some requests; other requests complete normally. Impact is end-to-end timeouts surfaced to the customer application (HTTP 504 / SDK timeout).

Impact:
- Multiple failed inference calls for 10 active users at ClariFin Analytics (enterprise tenant on dedicated capacity).
- Estimated 2-5% of requests hitting timeouts during peak load window (13:00–15:00 UTC).
- Downstream data processing pipelines backpressure due to missing structured outputs.

Observed behavior:
- Request initiates, initial token stream begins as expected.
- Streaming stalls mid-response while server still reports active worker handling the request.
- After ~30–60s stall, client times out and request is marked failed. No 5xx returned from API gateway.
- Replaying identical requests in non-JSON mode (plain text) returns normally and quickly.

Hypothesis: eviction/flush of structured-output buffer or decoder finalization logic can block when certain metadata fields are present (multi-field arrays), causing long-tail stalls in the streaming decoder / postprocess step.

Notes: customer attached sample prompts and the failing request IDs in comments below.
1) Use customer tenant credentials and call /v1/chat/stream with mode=structured-json and schema that includes nested arrays and 4 'metadata' fields.
2) Observe initial tokens emitted, then wait — some requests stall after emitting ~80% of tokens.
3) Re-run identical request switching to mode=plain-text; observe normal completion within expected latency.
4) Run load test with 50 concurrent streams for 5 minutes to reproduce long-tail under sustained load.
5) Collect request IDs from customer logs and cross-check with serving-runtime traces.
Sample failing request ids: req-20260310-7a2f, req-20260310-7b9c
2026-03-10T13:12:04Z srv-01 streaming-decoder INFO request=req-20260310-7a2f tokens_emitted=182 status=streaming
2026-03-10T13:12:35Z srv-01 streaming-decoder WARN request=req-20260310-7a2f stall_detected=1 last_token_timestamp=2026-03-10T13:12:05Z
2026-03-10T13:12:40Z api-gateway INFO request=req-20260310-7a2f client_timeout=60000 returned_http=504
Worker traces show no OOM, CPU at 45-60%, and GPU util ~30% at stall time.
2026-03-10T14:20:12Z - Aisha Khan (Support): Opened ticket after customer escalation. Attached sample prompt and request IDs.
2026-03-10T15:05:43Z - Samir Gupta (SRE): Acknowledged. Will collect runtime traces and enable additional debug logging on the affected dedicated pool.
2026-03-10T17:02:01Z - Marco Liu (Platform Eng): Noted similar pattern to SUP-20345 where structured-output postprocessing held a mutex during finalization; adding hypothesis to investigation.
2026-03-11T09:30:22Z - Samir Gupta (SRE): Temporarily increased decoder flush timeout and verified reduction in observed customer timeouts (from 3% to ~0.5%) during a 2-hour window. Planning a safer hotfix.
2026-03-12T11:11:09Z - Priya Patel (Customer Success): Customer confirmed they can reproduce reliably with their schema that includes arrays of metadata and trailing optional fields. They provided sample schema and data (attached in customer portal).
2026-03-13T08:44:55Z - Samir Gupta (SRE): Added link to PR with instrumentation and a candidate fix for buffer eviction race: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/812
- Reproduced stall locally using customer's schema when structured-output contains nested arrays > 3 levels and > 500 total elements across fields.
- Thread dump shows streaming-decoder main loop waiting on eviction condition variable while postprocessor holds the output buffer lock for extended time.
- CPU profiling indicates a synchronous JSON serialization pass in postprocess that occasionally spikes to 500ms for large payloads; this coincides with stalls.
- Non-JSON streaming bypasses postprocess serializer; explains why plain-text mode unaffected.
- No evidence of GPU or memory pressure; issue localized to CPU-side finalization path.
- Candidate root cause: structured-output finalization path performs full in-memory JSON assembly under a global lock causing head-of-line blocking for other streams on same worker.
- Affected customers appear to be on dedicated pools with default worker concurrency=8 leading to head-of-line blocking when one request enters heavy serialization.
- Related to prior issue SUP-19862 but different trigger (large nested arrays vs. rare unicode causing decoder hang).
- Instrumentation added to measure per-request serialization time and lock hold time (PR linked above).
1) Customer: Reduce nested array sizes or paginate metadata into separate follow-up requests.
2) Temporary server-side mitigation: lowered default worker concurrency on affected dedicated pool from 8 -> 4 to reduce contention (rolled out 2026-03-11 05:00 UTC).
3) Increased per-request streaming flush timeout to avoid client hits for 60s windows while hotfix is validated.
4) Recommend customers use plain-text mode for extremely large structured arrays until fix is released.

Issue summary:
Acme Banking is requesting a supported integration to export Redwood audit logs into Splunk (preferably Splunk HEC) as part of their security monitoring + compliance program.

Customer impact / urgency:
- Customer has an internal security review and external audit window starting ~2025-03-15.
- They need a concrete plan for SIEM ingestion (what events, delivery guarantees, and an ETA) to unblock a broader rollout of Redwood.
- They are explicitly asking for "near real-time" export of admin and access events (config changes, key/credential changes, RBAC changes, login events, API key usage, etc.).

What customer is asking for:
1) A supported way to stream/forward audit events to Splunk (HEC preferred).
2) Guidance on field mapping (CIM-ish naming conventions) and deduplication expectations.
3) Clarification on delivery semantics (exactly-once vs at-least-once), retention/backfill window, and how they can prove completeness.
4) Timeline / access: whether they can be part of the limited beta.

Environment details (from customer):
- Redwood deployment: Dedicated (prod) in us-east.
- Splunk: Splunk Cloud.
- Security constraints: outbound allowlist required; they prefer TLS + token auth; no PII beyond user identifiers; they want source IP if available.
- Estimated volume: 2–5M events/day once enabled across all workspaces; bursty during deployments.

Current state:
- Customer has access to Redwood audit logs in Console, but no direct Splunk export.
- Customer attempted a workaround by scraping the Console UI export CSV, which is not acceptable for audit/compliance.

Request from Support:
- Confirm whether Splunk HEC export is supported (now or via beta), and what scope/limitations apply.
- Provide a short-term workaround if direct HEC is not available (e.g., S3 delivery + Splunk ingestion from S3, or periodic API pull if available).

Attachments/links:
- Customer email excerpt included in first comment.
- Internal reference: SIEM-ready audit export beta PRD + Splunk guide (linked above).

Notes:
- Please treat as high-touch due to enterprise deal dependency + audit timeline.
2025-02-21 | Liam O'Rourke (Reporter) | Customer (Acme) request received via email
"We need Redwood audit logs in Splunk (Splunk Cloud). Our audit window begins mid-March. Console visibility isn't sufficient—we need automated ingestion with reliability semantics documented. Is HEC supported? If not, can we get S3 delivery that Splunk can pull from?"
2025-02-21 | Colin O'Donnell (Assignee) | Initial triage
Thanks—looping in Security and Product. I believe Splunk HEC is part of the upcoming SIEM-ready audit export beta (feature-flagged). Need to confirm eligibility and target timeline for a beta tenant allowlist enable.

Actions:
- Ask customer for Splunk HEC endpoint format (event collector URL), index/source/sourcetype preferences, and whether they require client certs.
- Confirm their outbound allowlist requirements (domain/IP ranges) so we can validate exporter egress controls.
2025-02-22 | Marcus Lin (Security) | Security considerations
We can support at-least-once delivery with event_id for downstream dedup. Must be explicit that duplicates can occur and Splunk should dedup on event_id.
PII: IP/user-agent are "where applicable" and may be omitted depending on event type; we should not promise full IP coverage for all actions. Also ensure we do not include request payloads or prompt content.

Please use the beta security FAQ language for customer-facing statements.
2025-02-24 | Naomi Feldman (Product) | Beta access guidance
Acme is a strong candidate for the limited beta, but we need to confirm (a) volume expectations and (b) whether they can accept beta limitations (no Private/on-prem, limited backfill window, at-least-once semantics).
If Acme agrees, file internal enablement request with tenant ID and target destination (Splunk HEC).
2025-02-25 | Colin O'Donnell (Assignee) | Follow-up questions sent to customer
Sent questions:
1) Confirm Splunk HEC URL and whether you will use raw endpoint vs services/collector/event.
2) Confirm index/source/sourcetype and whether you want gzip compression.
3) Confirm expected steady-state events/sec and peak bursts.
4) Confirm whether you can accept at-least-once delivery (possible duplicates) with event_id-based dedup.
5) Confirm minimum acceptable backfill (e.g., 24h/72h) and whether you need replays.

Also shared preliminary workaround: S3 delivery (JSONL partitions) + Splunk S3 input, if HEC is delayed.
2025-02-27 | Liam O'Rourke (Reporter) | Customer responses
Customer confirms:
- Splunk Cloud HEC endpoint: https://http-inputs-<redacted>.splunkcloud.com/services/collector/event
- Wants index=redwood_audit, sourcetype=redwood:audit
- Can accept gzip.
- Peak bursts: up to ~2,000 events/sec during deploys; steady ~200–400 events/sec.
- At-least-once is acceptable if event_id is stable.
- Backfill: minimum 72 hours preferred; 24 hours acceptable for beta if clearly stated.
- Outbound allowlist: they will allowlist Splunk HEC endpoint only; no inbound requirements.
2025-02-28 | Colin O'Donnell (Assignee) | Internal enablement request
Filed INT-9012 to enable SIEM audit export beta for Acme tenant allowlist once approved. Requested Splunk HEC destination with:
- index=redwood_audit
- sourcetype=redwood:audit
- source=redwood
- gzip enabled

Also asked Platform team to confirm egress allowlist behavior and destination host validation requirements.
2025-03-03 | Rafael Mendes (SRE) | Operational expectations for beta
Please ensure the customer is aligned on:
- Delivery is at-least-once; duplicates possible.
- Export lag SLO is "minutes" under normal conditions; can increase under downstream 429s.
- If Splunk throttles (429), exporter backs off and retries; customer should monitor for lag rather than expecting strict real-time.
- We can pause exports as mitigation during extended downstream issues.

Support should set expectations that this is beta and subject to tuning.
2025-03-04 | Colin O'Donnell (Assignee) | Customer-facing update drafted
Draft sent to AM/CSM for review:
- Redwood will support Splunk HEC export via SIEM-ready audit export beta.
- At-least-once delivery with stable event_id; customers should dedup on event_id.
- Backfill window for beta: up to 24 hours (working to extend; GA target larger). Customer can request manual replay assistance if needed.
- Fields: actor/action/resource/tenant/workspace/timestamps, plus source IP/user-agent where applicable; PII minimized.
- TLS in transit; tokens stored securely; RBAC required for export configuration.

Pending: confirm exact beta enablement date.
2025-03-05 | Liam O'Rourke (Reporter) | Customer accepted beta limitations
Customer confirmed acceptance of beta limitations (at-least-once, 24h backfill for beta) and wants enablement by week of 2025-03-10 if possible.

Closing this support request as "Resolved" once enablement is tracked under INT-9012; will continue comms on INT ticket.
Provided customer with beta scope/semantics for Splunk HEC audit export, collected endpoint/index/sourcetype requirements, and initiated internal enablement via INT-9012. Customer accepted at-least-once + event_id dedup and beta backfill limitations. Ongoing enablement tracked separately.
1) Proceed with INT-9012 tenant allowlist enablement and destination configuration under feature flag.
2) Schedule validation session with customer: confirm events arriving in Splunk, sourcetype/index correct, and dedup on event_id.
3) Provide customer with the security FAQ language + brief integration notes (HEC endpoint, token rotation expectations).
4) Monitor lag/errors for first 72h post-enable; adjust batching/backoff if Splunk 429s are frequent.

Issue summary
- Customer reported intermittent 5xx responses from Redwood Private inference endpoints. Spikes correlate with KMS throttling errors during envelope decrypt.

Impact
- Symptoms: elevated 5xx at API gateway, increased p95 latency, sporadic request failures (non-deterministic).
- Customer impact: end-user facing errors during peak traffic windows; retries from upstream increased load and made spikes worse.
- Duration: recurring spikes over ~3 days; most acute on 2025-11-19 15:10–16:05 ET.

Environment
- Deployment: Redwood Private
- Region: us-east-1
- Cloud/KMS: AWS KMS (customer-managed key)
- Workloads: chat + embeddings, moderate concurrency with periodic burst traffic

Detection / signals
- Alert: "KMS dependency error rate" (new dashboard pack) triggered at 15:14 ET.
- Observed metrics:
  - redwood.kms.requests_total increased sharply with retries
  - redwood.kms.errors_total{error_category="Throttling"} spiked
  - api.gateway.5xx_rate correlated 1:1 with KMS throttling bursts

Dashboard links (internal)
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/kms-health/kms-dependency-health?var=env:prod&var=region:us-east-1
- Gateway errors: https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/api-gw/api-gateway?var=env:prod&var=region:us-east-1
- Trace sample (Honeycomb): https://ui.honeycomb.io/redwood/datasets/inference/trace?trace_id=2f6c3c9b6a7c4d9a

Investigation notes
1) Confirmed error mapping
- Logs show AWS KMS returning "ThrottlingException" on Decrypt operations. The errors propagate as 5xx due to decrypt failure on request path.
- Log fields (new-ish): kms.error_category=Throttling, kms.operation=Decrypt, kms.key_arn=.../key/xxxx, kms.request_id=...

2) Retry amplification hypothesis
- During throttling, our client retries with exponential backoff, but with multiple callers and burst traffic, total KMS QPS increased (retry storm). KMS throttling then worsened.
- p95 decrypt latency rose; some requests exceeded upstream budgets, contributing to gateway timeouts and 5xx.

3) Quota / provisioning
- Customer KMS account-level quota appeared near default for Decrypt TPS for their region.
- Customer had increased inference burst without revisiting KMS quotas.

Root cause
- Primary: AWS KMS Decrypt throttling at customer quota limits during burst windows.
- Contributing: retry policy lacked sufficient jitter + global throttle budget/backpressure, leading to request amplification under throttling.

Mitigation (immediate)
- Recommended customer actions (same day):
  - Submit AWS quota increase request for KMS Decrypt in us-east-1.
  - Reduce burst concurrency temporarily (if possible) or add upstream jittered retries with cap.
- Redwood config guidance (customer-approved):
  - Reduce max retry attempts for KMS Decrypt.
  - Enforce a retry budget so per-request decrypt does not exceed the end-to-end latency budget.

Mitigation (product / platform)
- Implemented throttle-budget/backpressure for KMS wrapper to avoid saturating KMS under load and to prevent retry amplification.
- Observability: confirmed dashboards and alerts include Throttling by region/key ARN and show request volume vs errors.

Customer communication
- Provided interim explanation: KMS throttling (not key mismatch) + recommended quota increase path.
- Provided runbook excerpt and troubleshooting steps from the Private operator guide; included sample AWS CLI command to validate key access and confirm throttling errors.

Resolution
- 2025-11-22: Customer confirmed AWS quota increase approved (Decrypt TPS). Error spikes reduced significantly.
- 2025-11-25: Redwood hotfix + wrapper improvements rolled to their deployment (backoff/jitter + throttle budget defaults). No further 5xx spikes observed for 24h under similar traffic.

Verification
- Post-change metrics:
  - redwood.kms.errors_total{error_category="Throttling"} near-zero
  - api.gateway.5xx_rate returned to baseline
  - p95 end-to-end latency back within expected range

Follow-ups
- [Eng] Ensure KMS wrapper safe defaults are enforced and cannot be overridden without explicit override in prod (guardrails).
- [Docs] Add operator-guide callout: KMS TPS/quota sizing guidance for bursty workloads + how to recognize throttling patterns.
- [SRE] Tune alert thresholds to avoid noise while still catching real throttling onset; split by env/region.

Customer reports "sporadic 500s" and elevated latency. Initial triage suggests decrypt path failures. Pulling logs + dashboards.
2025-11-19 15:41 ET — Rafael Mendes (Assignee)
Confirmed KMS ThrottlingException in dataplane logs. Correlates with gateway 5xx spikes. This looks like retry amplification: KMS request volume is higher than baseline during throttling windows.
2025-11-19 16:02 ET — Nadia Rahman
I’m seeing redwood.kms.errors_total{error_category="Throttling"} jump alongside redwood.kms.requests_total. Trace samples show multiple decrypt retries per request. Sharing a trace link in description.
2025-11-19 16:15 ET — Sean Gallagher
On-call view: this matches the pattern from the recent KMS timeout spike thread (#incidents). Suggest we advise quota increase + reduce retry attempts short-term; long-term fix is throttle budget/backpressure in wrapper.
2025-11-19 16:33 ET — Kira Thompson
Pulled relevant troubleshooting text from Private KMS Operator Guide draft. Adding a section proposal: "KMS throttling and quotas" with explicit AWS quota guidance + what metrics/log fields to look at.
2025-11-20 10:12 ET — Jordan Lee
Customer’s IAM looks fine (no AccessDenied). This is pure throttling. Recommended they request KMS Decrypt quota increase in us-east-1 and we should ensure our wrapper uses jitter on backoff to avoid sync retries.

Opened eng follow-up and linked PR plan: add KMS throttle budget/backpressure + cap retries. Also recommend enabling the new KMS dashboards pack for this customer.

Customer confirmed they submitted AWS quota increase request; temporary mitigation applied by reducing burst concurrency during peak windows.
2025-11-25 17:05 ET — Rafael Mendes
Rolled wrapper changes to customer deployment (throttle budget + improved jitter). Observed KMS throttling drop to near-zero. Monitoring overnight.
2025-11-26 11:22 ET — Tomáš Novák
24h verification complete: no recurrence of 5xx spikes, latency stable. Closing as Resolved with follow-up doc improvements.

Issue summary: HelixBio reported a sudden increase in request queue depth for their dedicated reserved pool starting ~2026-03-10T08:12Z. P99 generation latency rose from ~120ms to >2.4s for short inference requests, and the pool reported intermittent GPU allocation failures.

Impact: Customer's user-facing product experienced degraded responsiveness for ~45 minutes, causing failed UX flows and throttled retry storms. This affected a single reserved capacity contract (dedicated) and impacted two commonly used model routes.

Environment: prod us-east-1, dedicated pool: pool-helix-3, autoscaler: rebalancer-v2 (enabled), serving-runtime: 1.34.2.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Run many short, low-token inference requests from a noisy tenant simultaneously (observed from tenant id noisy-tenant-47).
2) Trigger scheduled rebalancer cycle (rebalancer runs every 60s by default).
3) Observe queue depth metric climb and GPU allocation latency metrics tick up within the same rebalancer cycle window.

Observed behavior: During rebalancer cycles, allocation churn increases (frequent GPU handoffs), concurrent short jobs from another tenant are scheduled onto the same nodes, runtime reports increased kvcache eviction and binding latency. The scheduler queues for HelixBio's routes grow rapidly and p99 latency spikes. We also saw a correlated rise in the rebalancer_cycle_count and gpu_alloc_failures metrics.

Expected behavior: Rebalancer should avoid causing immediate allocation churn under transient short-job pressure and preserve steady allocation for reserved tenants. P99 should remain within SLA thresholds for pinned model routes.

Logs / Dashboards:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/pool_metrics/pool-helix-3?orgId=1
- Allocation trace: s3://redwood-logs/pool-helix-3/2026-03-10/rebalancer-trace.log
- Serving runtime logs (sample): https://logs.redwood.ai/serving/runtime/pool-helix-3/2026-03-10

Attachments: heap of short traces attached to ticket (key traces: trace-20260310-0818.gz, trace-20260310-0820.gz).
2026-03-10 08:20 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Acknowledged. Opening incident and paging SRE. Contacted HelixBio to request traffic window info and ETA for a mitigation window.
2026-03-10 08:27 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Observed synchronous rise in rebalancer_cycle_count and queue_depth_per_pool. Initial hypothesis: rebalancer aggressively reallocated GPUs while a tenant produced many short-lived jobs, causing allocation thrash.
2026-03-10 08:33 - Customer (HelixBio - Lia Chen): Confirmed sudden surge of low-latency calls as part of a data-sync job. Reported elevated p99 and user-visible errors between 08:10-08:55 UTC.
2026-03-10 08:45 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Temporarily disabled automated rebalancer for pool-helix-3; pinned HelixBio's workloads to warm nodes as workaround. Observed queue depth drop within ~2 minutes and p99 latency reduced to ~150ms.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:12 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Deployed rebalancer soft throttle patch to staging; scheduled canary to prod if metrics stable.
2026-03-10 09:20 - Hypothesis 1: Rebalancer does not account for short-job churn and treats transient allocation pressure as sustained, triggering unnecessary reallocations.
2026-03-10 10:40 - Hypothesis 2: Scheduler affinity heuristics allow noisy short jobs to preempt reserved allocations if they match GPU capability labels; need stronger reservation enforcement during rebalancer windows.
2026-03-12 08:00 - Data: 72% of allocation churn events were attributable to a single tenant's short burst traffic; remaining 28% were noise from background housekeeping jobs.
Temporary mitigation: Rebalancer was disabled for pool-helix-3 and HelixBio routes were pinned to a warm subset of GPUs. This reduced allocation churn and restored p99 latency to acceptable ranges.
Permanent fix plan: Merged PR to add a soft-throttle and minimum-hold-time to rebalancer logic (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rebalancer/pull/412). Changes: (1) rebalancer will require two consecutive cycle signals before reallocating a GPU, (2) backpressure window added to scheduler to deprioritize short-lived jobs during rebalancer windows, (3) stronger reservation enforcement for dedicated pools.
Rollout notes: Patch has been deployed to staging and will be rolled to a single canary reserved pool on 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC for 2 hours before broader rollout. Monitoring checks include allocation churn rate, p99 latency for pinned routes, and rebalancer_cycle_count.
Follow-up: Postmortem scheduled, and customer will be offered 10% credit for the degraded window as goodwill.
Add alert: rebalancer_cycle_count > 3/min for a given pool
Add alert: gpu_alloc_failures > 0.5% for reserved pools
Add scheduler change: short_job_sampling flag to avoid co-scheduling with reserved workloads
Run postmortem and update dedicated pool SLO docs
Plan customer communication and credit approval

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightPost reports sharp tail-latency spikes (~95p to 99p) with intermittent 5xxs after a targeted optimizer rollout that enabled 'async_partitioned_batching' and a new quantization profile 'q8-dyn-lite'.
Impact: Customer-facing API errors for a subset of long-session chat requests; increased error rate from ~0.2% to ~3.7% for BrightPost traffic. Some streaming connections drop mid-response.
Observed behavior: Errors are concentrated on long sequences (>1k tokens) and large embedding+generation hybrid routes. Errors began at 2026-03-12T09:30 UTC shortly after a staged toggle of optimizer flags for the dedicated pool serving BrightPost.
Top-level ask: Provide a safe, stepped offramp to reduce customer impact (restore latency and eliminate 5xxs) while preserving telemetry to debug root cause.
1) Use BrightPost tenant credentials against prod us-east endpoint (tenant: brightpost-prod).
2) Run a mixed workload: 40% long-form chat (1k+ tokens), 40% short chat, 20% embedding+rerank calls using redwood-rl-13B pinned to optimizer profile 'alpha-experiment-2026-03-12'.
3) Observe tail latency and error rate over 10 minutes; compare to a control tenant pinned to 'stable-v2' profile.
4) Reproduce reliably by setting client-side concurrency to 12 connections and ensuring average input length > 600 tokens for long chat paths.
[2026-03-12T09:33:21Z] serving-runtime ERROR tenant=brightpost pool=dedicated-12 request_id=aa1b... status=500 runtime=0.12s reason=kv-cache-evict-failed
[2026-03-12T09:34:02Z] optimizer WARN optimizer_profile=alpha-experiment-2026-03-12 flag=async_partitioned_batching step=3 evicted=842 lat_p95=1.8s
[2026-03-12T09:34:02Z] telemetry METRIC tenant=brightpost tail_p99=3.4s increased_from=0.6s
[2026-03-12T09:36:10Z] api-gateway INFO request_id=bb2c... upstream_error=502 message=stream-closed-by-runtime
Hypothesis A: async_partitioned_batching interacts poorly with q8-dyn-lite quant profile on long-sequence KV cache patterns causing eviction churn and transient 5xxs.
Hypothesis B: The new quant profile reduces memory headroom on dedicated GPUs, triggering aggressive KV cache eviction and OOM-like failures surfaced as 5xxs rather than clear OOM logs.
Telemetry: GPU memory headroom dropped ~18% for impacted pods after 09:30 UTC; GC/eviction counters spiked in the same window.
Repro experiment: toggling async_partitioned_batching=false on a single replica reproduced tail latency improvement in 2/2 runs; error rate dropped to baseline.
Cross-checks: Other tenants on same pool but pinned to 'stable-v2' did not show errors, indicating tenant-level config gating is likely the trigger.
Immediate mitigation (live): disable async_partitioned_batching at tenant scope for brightpost-prod. Command: rwctl tenant update-config --tenant brightpost-prod --set optimizer.async_partitioned_batching=false --reason 'emergency-offramp-2026-03-12'
If command unavailable: apply traffic-split in router to route BrightPost to a fallback pool pinned to 'stable-v2' (rwctl router set-split --tenant brightpost-prod --default-pool=fallback-stable --weight=100).

Customer requests a certified delivery pattern for audit events used in regulatory forensics. They want incremental (delta) batches that are strictly ordered per-tenant with a manifest that proves sequence continuity, gap detection metadata, and TTL provenance for legal hold and retention verification. The deliverable should include a sample delivery to Azure Event Hubs and an S3 fallback with signed manifests (RFC 3161 timestamping or equivalent) and an explanation of how KMS-wrapped signing keys are rotated.
Customer's compliance team is unable to complete their inbound SOC or audit because they cannot demonstrate chain-of-custody and ordered delivery guarantees. They have paused a scheduled audit until we supply an attested sample. Business impact: potential delay in contract renewal and elevated legal scrutiny.
1) Customer configured tenant-level webhook to our audit export endpoint. 2) Expected strictly ordered event batches with sequence_number per tenant. 3) Observed reordering and occasional missed sequence numbers across two business days. 4) Customer attempted replays and saw duplicate offsets from our S3 fallback manifest. 5) Customer requests a reproducible sample and artifact demonstrating gap detection and reconciliation behavior.
Customer requests (a) 10-minute sample of delta bundles for tenant 'finovia-prod' in prod.us-east, (b) JSON manifest format with sequence_number, prev_hash, batch_hash, rfc3161_tstamp, and kms_key_id, (c) a redaction flag for PII fields and sample mapping for the customer's QRadar ingestion (field mappings and overflow policy). Provide the sample both as Azure Event Hubs push and as signed S3 objects.
Provided upload from customer (truncated):
- webhook_delivery.log: 2025-02-16T09:14:21Z tenant=finovia-prod seq=12534 status=200 latency_ms=48
- webhook_delivery.log: 2025-02-16T09:14:27Z tenant=finovia-prod seq=12536 status=200 latency_ms=62
- s3_fallback.log: 2025-02-16T09:18:04Z tenant=finovia-prod manifest_id=mf-20250216-0918 uploaded=true size=2.1MB
Note: customer attached CSV of observed sequence gaps (12535 missing) and Event Hubs consumer offsets for the same window.
- Initial triage: observed intermittent delivery backpressure in the webhook router during the time window; two 429 spikes recorded in the router metrics.
- Correlated with autoscaling events: dedicated delivery worker pool scaled from 4->2 briefly due to throttling logic threshold.
- Manifest generation job uses best-effort accumulation window; when delivery worker retries out-of-order, manifest prev_hash may not reflect final persisted order.
- Identified missing invariant: manifest creation currently assumes idempotent append but does not enforce strict sequence-lock during concurrent batch flushes.
- Reproduced locally by simulating concurrent batch flush with artificially delayed KVS persistence; observed the same gap pattern and duplicate offset in fallback manifest.
1) Temporarily enable per-tenant sequence-lock mode for finovia-prod to force a single writer path (console toggle). 2) Advise customer to hold audit replay until we provide attested sample. 3) Provide manual reconciliation manifest covering the requested window with signed timestamps and explicit gap markers.
(pending) Engineering has a prioritized patch to add a lightweight sequence-lock for manifest flushes and to include explicit gap-detection entries in manifests. SRE will generate the requested attested sample for 2025-02-16 09:10-09:20 window and deliver via secure S3 presigned link plus Event Hubs test push. Will include RFC-3161 style timestamping via our timestamping proxy and a key-rotation note. Target delivery: 2025-02-20.

Issue summary
Northbridge Analytics reports that Optimization Config rollback actions are not appearing in their audit log export / SIEM pipeline. Rollback itself succeeds (traffic returns to baseline), and they can see other Optimization Config lifecycle events (create/apply/promote) in the audit feed.

Impact
- Customer compliance/change-management requirement: all production rollbacks must be auditable with actor + scope + before/after.
- Procurement blocker for enabling Safe Apply + Rollback broadly across their org.
- No production outage, but compliance risk + inability to prove rollback action occurred.

Customer report
- They rolled back Optimization Config via Console (Rollback button) on 2026-02-11 ~18:40 UTC.
- They expected an audit event within ~1–2 minutes in their exported audit stream.
- They can correlate the rollback in Redwood Console history and via performance recovery, but there is no corresponding audit event in their feed.

Expected behavior
Audit event should be emitted and exported for rollback actions (Console + API) with:
- event_name matching taxonomy
- actor identity (user_id/email or service principal)
- request_id/correlation_id
- scope (tenant/model/region)
- config_version_from + config_version_to
- outcome (success/failure)

Actual behavior
Rollback event not present in exported audit feed. Apply/promote events show up as expected.

Environment
- Deployment mode: Dedicated (customer)
- Region: us-east
- Affected feature: Optimization Config rollback

Notes / attachments
- Customer provided: rollback timestamp, affected tenant slug, and SIEM query screenshots (not attached here). Support has them in the customer thread.

Initial triage checklist
- Confirm rollback happened in Console history and in control-plane event logs.
- Verify whether event was emitted but dropped by exporter (schema mismatch / missing required fields).
- Verify taxonomy match vs documented event names in Confluence.
- Confirm whether rollback endpoint path uses the same audit emitter as apply/promote.

Internal references
- Audit event taxonomy: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/optimization-config-audit-events.json
- Rollback endpoint PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-19902-add-rollback-endpoint.json
- Audit events PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-19941-add-audit-log-events-for-config-changes.json
2026-02-12 09:18 UTC — Kevin Osei (Reporter)
Customer escalation from Northbridge Analytics: rollback action does not appear in audit log export. They can see optimization_config.apply + optimization_config.promote events, but not rollback. Marking as P1 due to enterprise compliance blocker.

2026-02-12 10:02 UTC — Benji Okafor (Assignee)
Reproduced in staging with SIEM-export mode enabled. Rollback succeeds, history updates, but exporter shows 0 rollback events. Control-plane internal logs show an event emitted with name "optimization_config.rollback".

2026-02-12 10:27 UTC — Marcus Lin (Security)
The documented taxonomy page expects event_name "optimization_config.rolled_back" (past tense) with required field "action" and "result". If emitted name differs, exporter filter will drop. Please confirm exporter allowlist.

2026-02-12 11:05 UTC — Benji Okafor
Confirmed: audit-exporter allowlist includes "optimization_config.rolled_back" but not "optimization_config.rollback". The rollback endpoint is emitting the non-allowlisted name. Apply/promote code paths use the correct names.

2026-02-12 11:22 UTC — Jordan Lee
Also noticed rollback endpoint payload omits "previous_config_version" (it only includes target_version). Exporter schema validation requires both for optimization config changes, otherwise it drops the event.

2026-02-12 12:10 UTC — Benji Okafor
Fix plan:
1) Update rollback endpoint audit event name to taxonomy-compliant "optimization_config.rolled_back".
2) Include required fields: previous_config_version, new_config_version, scope.
3) Add integration test asserting exporter receives rollback events.

2026-02-13 16:44 UTC — Benji Okafor
Opened fix PR and requested review from Security + Console.

2026-02-14 09:30 UTC — Dr. Aisha Rahman
Approved taxonomy alignment. Please ensure request_id is always present and actor identity is captured for both Console and API rollbacks.

2026-02-17 14:12 UTC — Hannah Rivera (Console)
Verified Console rollback uses same endpoint; once backend emits corrected event, Console should be fine. Also asked to add UI note: audit event may be delayed by export pipeline.

2026-02-18 18:06 UTC — Benji Okafor
Fix merged and rolled to prod-us-east. Confirmed in internal SIEM test tenant: rollback generates event within 60–90s.

2026-02-19 15:40 UTC — Kevin Osei
Follow-up with Northbridge: asked them to re-run rollback in a low-risk scope and confirm event appears in their feed. Offered to provide sample payload and correlation_id for their query.

2026-02-20 10:05 UTC — Kevin Osei
Customer confirmed rollback event now appears with expected fields. Closing ticket.
Root cause: rollback endpoint emitted a non-taxonomy event name ("optimization_config.rollback") and omitted required schema fields, causing the audit-export pipeline allowlist/schema validation to drop the event. Fix: updated rollback audit emission to taxonomy-compliant event name ("optimization_config.rolled_back"), added required version-diff fields + request_id + actor, and added integration coverage to prevent regression. Deployed to prod us-east; customer verified audit feed includes rollback events.
We identified an issue where rollback actions were not being included in exported audit logs due to an internal event taxonomy mismatch. The rollback operation itself was successful, but the audit record was filtered out during export. We deployed a fix so rollback actions now generate the expected audit log event with the required fields. Please re-test and let us know if any additional fields are needed for your SIEM queries.
