payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer (AtlasMedia, Dedicated) reports intermittent increased p95/p99 latency and occasional cross-region egress after enabling 'residency_preference=strict' on their account. The behavior appears during policy refresh windows and correlates with bursty traffic from their ingestion workers.

Impact: Elevated p95/p99 for generation requests from eu-west users (~200-500ms delta) and occasional cross-region egress (requests routed from eu-west -> us-west) for short windows (~30-90s). Customer reports increased cost due to cross-region egress and user-facing latency spikes during peak times.

Environment: prod, Dedicated pool (atlas-dedicated-gpu-1), live since 2026-02-28.

Observed behavior: Requests normally route to eu-west serving nodes. During periodic policy refresh (~every 60s control-plane refresh), a subset of sessions are forwarded to us-west edges, causing TLS handshake and additional routing latency. This is intermittent and correlates with control-plane policy refresh timestamps seen in control-plane logs.

Expected behavior: With residency_preference=strict, traffic should remain pinned to eu-west and never egress to us-west unless explicit failover occurs or capacity is exhausted and fallback policy is triggered.
1) Customer sets residency_preference="strict" for tenant.
2) Send a steady stream of generation requests from eu-west clients (RPS ~40-60) with session affinity headers (X-Session-ID).
3) Observe routing in request trace and edge logs over 10 minutes.
4) Note any short windows where requests are routed to us-west and latency increases.

Expected: No cross-region hops when capacity is available in eu-west. Actual: transient cross-region egress coinciding with policy refresh cadence.
Control-plane log excerpt (2026-03-10T14:02:00Z):
[control-plane] refresh_policy tenant=atlasmedia policy_version=18 start
[control-plane] compute_affinity_changes tenant=atlasmedia changed=27
[edge-eu-west] session_lookup id=snip-abc result=PIN_EXPIRED last_seen=2026-03-10T14:01:58Z
[edge-eu-west] forward_to=us-west host=gw-us-west-03 reason=fallthrough
[edge-us-west] accept_request session_hint=snip-abc

Request trace (sample): trace_id=tx-77bbc latency=780ms path=edge-eu-west -> gw-us-west TLS_handshake=220ms

Grafana alerts: increased p99 for atlasmedia eu-west generation route starting 14:02:10Z for ~70s.
Initial hypothesis: race between control-plane policy refresh and edge pin refresh leads to temporary TTL/pin inconsistencies. Two possible vectors: (1) control-plane computes a micro-migration (rebalancing) while edges still see old pin metadata, causing fallthrough to fallback route; (2) DNS TTL reduction on control-plane side during refresh causing some edges to re-resolve to secondary edge set.

What we've checked so far:
- Validated control-plane logs show policy_version increments at same cadence reported by customer.
- Edge metrics show pin_cache_miss spikes aligning with policy refresh window.
- No GPU shortage or autoscale events in dedicated pool during incidents.
- Session affinity header present in requests; edge reports last_seen < 60s but pin considered expired due to race condition.
- Reproduced locally with a synthetic load: when we trigger a policy refresh while simultaneously rotating edge routing table, ~5-8% of sessions fall through to fallback path for ~20-60s.

Correlated artifacts: Slack thread #support (https://slack.redwood/archives/C03SUP), Grafana panel (https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/routing?orgId=1&var-tenant=atlasmedia), and a debug PR with instrumentation (https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/908).

Hypothesis refinement: The control-plane publishes routing deltas and a short 'refresh-window' where edges accept both old and new pins to avoid hard-cutovers. In this window, our TTL/expiry logic on the edge treats pins as stale if last_seen < configured_pin_refresh_threshold, which combined with a small DNS re-resolve leads to mixed egress.

Next diagnostic step: add higher-fidelity tracing to pin state transitions and bump pin_refresh_grace to observe effect. Also evaluate candidate fix to debounce policy refresh broadcasts and add a short 'pin-hold' on edges during refresh to prevent fallthrough.
2026-03-10 15:05 - Support (Ava Martinez): Initial triage complete. Escalating to SRE/Routing. Asking customer for request IDs and sample traces.
2026-03-10 16:20 - Customer (AtlasMedia - Ops Lead, Jorge Ruiz): Provided three sample trace IDs and noted spikes only during 14:02-14:04 windows. Attached internal load generator plan.
2026-03-10 18:12 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Reproduced locally with synthetic load. Pin-cache miss spikes coincide with policy refresh broadcast. Raising priority and opening router PR for instrumentation. See PR #908.
2026-03-11 09:34 - Support (Ava Martinez): Shared interim workaround with customer: enable 'strict_no_failover' flag (controls application-level) to prevent automatic fallback while we test. Customer will trial on a subset of traffic.
2026-03-12 11:07 - Customer (Jorge Ruiz): Trial applied to 10% traffic. Early results: p99 spike occurrence reduced but not eliminated. Awaiting SRE countermeasure rollout.
2026-03-12 14:55 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Deployed temporary config change to increase pin_refresh_grace from 3s -> 30s on eu-west edges. Monitoring for reduction in mixed egress events.
Workaround: Increased pin_refresh_grace on eu-west edges (temporary) and instructed customer to enable strict_no_failover for canary traffic. This reduced mixed-egress occurrences during the test window but did not fully eliminate them.

Planned permanent fix: Engineering to implement a debounce on control-plane policy broadcasts and implement a short 'pin-hold' period on edges where the existing pin is preferred for a grace window during version transitions. Add metrics for pin_state_transitions and add automated canary to validate behavior.

Follow-ups:
- Router team to land PR #908 (instrumentation) and follow-up PR for debounce (target 2026-03-24).
- SRE to run extended soak test for 48 hours post-merge.
- Support to coordinate with AtlasMedia to schedule a maintenance window for permanent rollout.

Status: In Progress. No final resolution yet; customer notified of workaround and planned timeline.
payload.summary: Residency policy refresh race condition causing mixed-egress paths and regional latency bump

Issue summary: Customer BrightCart Inc. reports an unexpected 'egress' line item (~€1,320) on their finalized March invoice for a private deployment. They assert that the organization's reserved hours contract for eu-west (monthly reserved pool) should have covered the traffic and that egress is included in their enterprise Private plan.

Impact: Finalized invoice shows a large one-time egress charge which has put autopay on hold. Customer finance is requesting an immediate explanation and provisional credit while we investigate. Affects billing for the whole org (all API keys associated with the private VPC connector).

Environment: Private control plane; dedicated private connector in eu-west-1; reserved hours contract active for March; deployment uses partner transit gateway (third-party peering).

What customer saw: Itemized invoice lines show:
- reserved-hours (applied)
- model usage lines (chat/embedding)
- new line: private-egress: euro-amount 1320.00 (no detailed tag or cost center)

Expected: No egress line (egress was contractualized in their Private plan).

1) Customer exports finalized invoice from Console -> Billing for March cycle. 2) Filter by cost-center 'private-vpc-connector' 3) Expand line items and click 'private-egress' line -> shows no origin tags. 4) Support attempted to reconcile postback logs and found egress postbacks tagged as 'hosted' for discrete windows between 2026-03-03 and 2026-03-04.
Billing postback fragment (redacted):
- 2026-03-03T22:11:12Z POST /postback {org_id: brc-001, route_tag: hosted, bytes_out: 12,345,678, tariff_id: egress-standard}
- 2026-03-03T22:11:12Z POST /postback {org_id: brc-001, route_tag: private-vpc, bytes_out: 12,345,678, tariff_id: null}
Console audit: api-key-tag-change by deploy-bot at 2026-03-03T21:59:02Z

Initial hypothesis: A transient tag-sync failure between Private connector service and billing postback pipeline caused a subset of egress events to be labeled 'hosted' and billed at egress tariff.

What we checked:
- Reserved-hours ledger shows credit applied for March. Credits reduce model usage lines but do not auto-offset mis-tagged egress tariff lines.
- Postback consumer logs (billing-consumer-02) show consumer restart at 2026-03-03T21:58:30Z, coincident with deploy-bot tagging event.
- Cross-checked network logs in Private control plane: transit gw reported sustained egress for that hour.
- Found one queued replayer job in billing-backfill that failed to map route_tag -> cost_center due to schema change in PR 9f3a4b2 (linked above). That PR was rolled out 2026-03-03.

Intermediate conclusion: Likely regression from recent billing schema normalization deploy (PR 9f3a4b2) that changed route_tag/connector mapping. A fraction of egress postbacks lost connector mapping and fell into default 'hosted' tariff during a 40-minute window.

Next steps planned:
- Ask Engineering to backfill mapping for 2026-03-03 21:50 -> 22:30 and recompute tariff assignment (ENG-allocator).
- If backfill succeeds, request billing to issue provisional credit and regenerate invoice lines.
- Add an alert to deploy-runbooks to block schema deploys without mapping validations for private connectors.

Additional notes:
Work in progress: Engineering to run backfill and recompute tariff assignments for affected windows. If mapping restored, Billing will issue provisional credit equivalent to the egress line and regenerate invoice lines. Follow-up actions: add pre-deploy validation for route_tag mappings and create a post-deploy reconciliation job to detect missing connector tags within 1 hour of schema changes. Owner for follow-ups: Priya Patel (SRE) and Diego Ramos (Billing Eng).

Customer (Acme AI) is requesting service credits due to a perceived SLA breach during the us-east streaming degradation on 2026-02-04 (ref SUP-1842 / INC-2026-02-04-us-east-streaming-degradation). They are asking for credits for the impacted window and requesting written confirmation of the timeline + mitigation steps.

This ticket is to (1) capture the comms log + timeline in one place, (2) document what we can/can’t promise in writing, and (3) run the exec escalation / approvals workflow for a credits decision.

---

Customer ask (as received)
- Credits for the impacted period (customer cited a 2–3 hour window of elevated stream resets/truncation).
- Confirmation whether this qualifies as an SLA breach under their Enterprise terms.
- Assurance that mitigations are in place to prevent recurrence.

Support/CS position (initial)
- We can acknowledge impact, provide a factual timeline, and share mitigations + follow-ups.
- We should not confirm “SLA breach” language in Support comms; route to CS + Legal/Finance approvals per exec escalation protocol.
- Credits decisions require VP CS approval; contract interpretation requires Legal review if customer requests a formal SLA determination.

Impact summary (customer-reported)
- Streaming responses disconnect mid-generation; some responses truncated.
- Increased retry load and higher token spend due to repeated attempts (customer claims).
- Business impact: customer cited degraded end-user experience for their demo workflow.

---

Evidence / internal references

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer QueryFlow reports sustained p99 latency regressions and sharp throughput drops for their dedicated pool during the 11:30-13:30 PST window. Symptoms look like a midday 'attach drought' where new allocation attempts fail or queue for long periods, causing request queuing and increased tail latency. Impact: Customer-facing endpoints see ~3-5x p99 increase and a 30-60% throughput reduction for routed model redwood/opt-1.3b. This is affecting production traffic and violating their internal SLOs.

Environment: Dedicated capacity (reserved cluster) in us-west-2. Autoscaling enabled with predictive warmup. No recent customer-side config changes reported.

Observed behavior: - New request attach attempts time out or backoff repeatedly for a sustained period. - Autoscaler does not return capacity quickly enough; cluster show high attach-retry counts. - Background prefetch/pin tasks spike CPU and NVMe I/O on a subset of hosts. - A small cohort of tenants exhibit long-lived handshake latency that holds allocator slots open.

Expected behavior: - Attach attempts should find free slots or trigger predictive spin-up within configured cooldown window. - Autoscaler should replenish capacity to keep p99 within targets.

Initial logs/metrics attached (snippets): - allocator.attach_retries: 842 spikes between 11:32-12:10 - prefetch_io_ops/s: host-rt-07: 12k -> baseline 900 - nvme_io_wait_ms: host-rt-07: p95 450ms - kernel_queue_depth: host-rt-07 elevated - per-tenant-conn-latency: tenant-queryflow-03: p99 1.2s (baseline 120ms)

Timeline: 2026-03-10 11:28: QueryFlow reports slowdown. 11:35: Support triage. 11:50: SRE review of allocator and autoscaler dashboards. 12:05: Temporary mitigation applied (soft cap on prefetch threads for the noisy tenant).

Notes: This looks different from classic noisy-GPU compute saturation: the hosts implicated show moderate GPU utilization but heavy NVMe IO and long attach handshakes. Hypothesis is that handshake resource contention (prefetch + metadata writes) is preventing slot recycling and causing allocator starvation across the pool.
1) Route synthetic steady-load traffic for redwood/opt-1.3b through a dedicated pool with autoscale enabled.
2) Simulate a tenant that opens many long-lived connections with prefix caching enabled and forces aggressive prefetch operations (high kv-cache churn).
3) Observe allocator.attach_retries and host nvme_io_wait metrics during the ramp to midday traffic levels.
4) Correlate p99 latency and attach queue lengths with host-side prefetch_io_ops spikes.
- Correlation found between per-host nvme_io_wait and global attach_retries count; host-rt-07, host-rt-09 most affected.
- No driver-level GPU errors observed; GPU SM/util consistent with moderate inference load (45-65%).
- Prefetch subsystem triggered high small-file NVMe writes (checkpoint-like behavior) from a single tenant's long-lived warmers.
- Allocator code holds a slot until metadata commit completes; when metadata IO is delayed, slot remains unusable and autoscaler sees high allocation pressure.
- Autoscaler telemetry shows spin-up latency within expected band, but attach handshakes still queue because existing slots are logically blocked.
- Reproduced with a synthetic client that issues aggressive KV-cache refreshes: identical attach drought observed in a scaled test cluster.
Mitigation applied (2026-03-10 12:03): Reduced prefetch concurrency for the noisy tenant which reduced nvme_io_wait and lowered attach retries by ~40%.
Short-term fix (2026-03-12): Rolled out autoscaler config change to add an allocator backoff fast-path: long metadata writes will fast-fail with retry backoff instead of holding slots indefinitely. Deployed to prod-us-west canary (20% of pool) during low-risk window.
Long-term remediation: Engineering to land PR to change allocator slot lifecycle so metadata commits are performed asynchronously and slot handoff occurs on logical commit acceptance. Also evaluating per-tenant prefetch rate-limiting at the scheduler layer and improving telemetry alerting on nvme_io_wait spikes.
Customer communication: Informed QueryFlow of temporary mitigation and that a short-term autoscaler change is rolling out to canary. Recommended customer to throttle internal warmers if feasible as a stop-gap.
Follow-ups: - Post-deploy verification window 2026-03-13 11:00-14:00 PST. - Create INT ticket to track allocator refactor (INT-90045). - Add NVMe IO wait alert to runbook.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:48 - Customer (QueryFlow - Alyssa Rivera): No config changes on our side. We did start a long-running batch that keeps many model contexts warm starting 11:00 PST but that's expected traffic.
2026-03-12 08:15 - Engineering (Priya Rao): Reproduced locally with synthetic prefetch client. Found allocator backpressure code path that holds slot while metadata write completes. PR suggested to fast-fail long metadata writes and let autoscaler supply warm slots earlier.
payload.summary: Tenant handshake throttle causing midday attach drought and degraded P99 throughput

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer Foresight Analytics reports intermittent spikes in time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and complete silence mid-request for long streaming completions. Symptoms started 2026-03-11 and escalated after traffic pattern changes (more tracing/metadata).

Impact: ~2–3% of in-flight streamed completions experience TTFB spikes (from ~200ms baseline to 2–8s) and occasional mid-stream disconnects resulting in 502/504 for user-facing requests. Affects dedicated tenant in prod us-east only. Customer reports degraded UX in their chat product and requested urgent mitigation.

Environment: Dedicated deployment, prod us-east-1, region routing through edge gateway cluster gw-us-east-02, backend pool on serving-runtime nodes pool-d-01. Observed on models: open-llama-13b and redwood-v1-qa.

Steps to reproduce (most reliable):
1) Send a long-completion streaming request (>40s expected) with a large set of custom metadata/tracing headers (~>20KB total) and client that uploads the request body in small slow chunks (~1KB every 100ms).
2) Observe initial handshake completes but first streamed bytes delayed (TTFB spike).
3) In some runs, stream goes silent mid-request and ALB/gateway issues a reset/502 after idle timeout.

Observed logs / signals:
- Edge gateway access logs show multiple requests with large header_size values and many small write events to upstream.
- Proxy (nginx/h2 proxy) error.log: repeated "upstream write timeout" and "client aborted" entries correlated with request ids.
- Serving runtime logs show no obvious CPU/GPU saturation; KV cache warmup patterns normal.
- Tracing headers (x-ctx, x-trace, baggage) grow on the wire when clients re-use connections leading to header table growth on HTTP/2.
- Metrics: 95th TTFB for tenant jumped from 350ms to 3s during incident windows; request count unchanged.

Initial hypothesis: Large aggregated metadata headers + slow client chunking cause the gateway/proxy to buffer writes and coalesce small upstream writes. That buffering combined with write hysteresis in the load balancer leads to delayed flushes (increasing TTFB) and sometimes triggers idle/reset timeouts mid-stream. HTTP/2 header compression (HPACK) growth and per-connection header table behavior exacerbate the issue for long-lived connections.

Actions already taken:
- Support asked customer to test with trimmed headers and faster client chunking; customer confirmed dramatic reduction in failures when headers <8KB.
- SRE performed a canary change on an internal gateway node disabling proxy_buffering for streaming route; preliminary tests reduced TTFB spikes on the canary.
- Ops increased ALB idle timeout from 30s to 90s for the affected pool as a temporary mitigation to reduce mid-stream resets.

Requested next steps:
- Short-term: Keep ALB idle at 90s for affected pool, deploy proxy_buffering=off for streaming endpoints across the cluster, and add an alert for sustained header_size growth per-connection.
- Mid-term: Harden gateway config: increase max header size, tune write buffer thresholds, and add explicit flush behavior for streaming responses.
- Long-term: SDK guidance/validation to compress or truncate tracing baggage and an automated header-size warning in the Console for customers.

Notes: This ticket overlaps with historical proxy/header growth incidents; see linked issues for similar patterns.
Timeline: 2026-03-12 09:12 customer ticket -> Support triage. 2026-03-12 11:00 SRE reproduced with internal harness mimicking slow-chunked client and large metadata; confirmed proxy write coalescing increased TTFB. 2026-03-12 14:30 applied canary proxy_buffering=off (gw-us-east-02-a) and saw median TTFB drop to baseline in canary. 2026-03-13 02:00 increased ALB idle timeout to 90s for pool-d-01. Root cause analysis points to interaction between large header frames and proxy buffering/write coalescing on HTTP/2 leading to delayed flush. HPACK table growth makes header frames larger on reconstructions, causing the proxy to spend more cycles and hold writes. No indication of serving-runtime CPU/GPU resource exhaustion.

Evidence: request ids r-20260312-6a1df, r-20260312-6a2b7 included in logs. Sample proxy error lines and ALB logs attached in internal ticket (attachment references).

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 03:12 - Ops (Jordan Lee): Temporarily increased ALB idle timeout for pool-d-01 to 90s and rolled proxy_buffering change to 10% of gateways. Monitoring for regressions.
Partial mitigation applied: ALB idle timeout increased to 90s for the affected pool and proxy_buffering disabled for streaming route canary. Customer-side header trimming confirmed effective. Permanent fixes planned: update gateway defaults (max header size, write buffer thresholds), route-level buffering exceptions, and Console/SDK guidance. Infra task created (INT-???) to roll changes to all gateways and add header-size alerting. Customer will be notified once config is fully rolled out.
Infra task to roll gateway config changes to all clusters and document rollback plan
Add Console alert for per-connection header_size > 16KB sustained for >5 minutes
SDK change to validate and compress tracing/baggage headers by default
Postmortem and runbook update referencing this ticket and linked incidents
payload.summary: Intermittent high TTFB and mid-request silence for dedicated tenant due to load-balancer backpressure from large custom metadata headers

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (LexicoHealth) reports intermittent high p99 latency and spike in 5xx (504/503) for inference requests served from their dedicated reservation in us-west during overnight windows. The behavior started 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC and recurred multiple times overnight.

Impact:
- Several production endpoints returned elevated p99 (1.2s -> 7s) and 5xx rate climbed to 8% for short intervals (~2-6 minutes).
- Business impact: LexicoHealth ingests inference results into user workflows; timeouts cause retries that fail end-user flows. They flagged this as production-severity for multiple services.

Environment:
- Dedicated reservation: lexicon-prod-resv-usw (dedicated GPU pool).
- Region: us-west.
- Models in use: starcoder-3b for long-code-completion paths; redwood-v2-medium for short chat.
- Autoscaler config: min_replicas: 0, max_replicas: 8, scale_target_cpu: 70%.

Steps to reproduce / observed pattern:
1) Schedule synthetic load that mixes long-sequence batch jobs (offline-embeddings/long-seq-batch) with online short chat traffic at similar time.
2) When long-sequence jobs enter the pool and overlap with online traffic, p99 for online requests jumps and 5xxs appear.
3) When long-seq jobs finish or are evicted, latency returns to baseline.

Logs / quick artifacts:
- Customer-provided timestamped traces: s3://lexicohealth-logs/2026-03-12/inference-traces/trace_20260312_0210.json (redacted link).
- Support trace snippet: "request_id=abc123 host=gpu-node-04 p99_ms=6400 backend_error=timed_out"
- Monitoring charts: heatmap of per-pod GPU context switches and memcopy stalls attached in investigation section.

Customer message (initial):
"We're seeing intermittent timeouts overnight. We didn't change workloads this week; this started when an internal large-embedding batch ran. Please advise; this is blocking our nightly ingest."

Timeline:
- 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC: Support triage; confirmed elevated p99 and 5xx spikes in LexicoHealth reservation.
- 2026-03-12 04:10 UTC: SRE noticed correlation with scheduled "offline-embedding-batch" (another tenant) running in same physical dedicated cluster due to pool labeling overlap.
- 2026-03-12 04:40 UTC: Captured NVML metrics and scheduler events; observed repeated GPU context-switch counts and spikes in PCIe memcopy time on affected nodes.

Hypotheses considered:
1) Noisy neighbor running long-sequence jobs causing KV cache thrashing and memory copies, increasing tail latency for co-located online inference.
2) Autoscaler mis-sized (min_replicas=0) allowed cluster to scale down overnight; when batch job arrived, scaling up lag + pod scheduling placed long-seq pods on same hosts as online pods causing contention.
3) Thermal/clock throttling on several GPUs due to sustained peak from the batch job leading to transient slowdowns.

Findings:
- GPU utilization profile shows high memcpy_util and lower compute_util during spike windows -> indicates memory-bound long sequences causing heavy host-device transfers.
- Node metrics: GPU power draw elevated, and dmesg contains a few nvlink timeouts on gpu-node-04 (nonfatal).
- Autoscaler logs: scale up triggered but new pods came up 45-90s after first performance degradation (scaling lag). With min_replicas=0 there was insufficient warm capacity.
- Scheduler placement: long-seq batch pods had no anti-affinity rules, so they colocated with LexicoHealth online pods.

Correlated artifacts:
- Slack thread: #support-lexicohealth (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C02ABCDEF/p1647043200000)
- Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood/prod/lexicohealth/panels/latency-2026-03-12
- Node metric snapshot (support): https://storage.redwood.com/tmp/node-snapshot-20260312.png

Interim mitigation attempted:
- At 2026-03-12 06:10 UTC we temporarily increased lexicon-prod-resv-usw min_replicas to 2 for LexicoHealth service and pushed pod anti-affinity for their online pods to prefer distinct nodes. Immediate p99 reduced but not fully back to baseline until long-seq batch finished.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 05:00 - LexicoHealth (Customer): We can schedule batch jobs outside of our online windows but need a long-term fix — this impacts SLAs.
Short-term: enforce min_replicas>=1 for dedicated reservations for customers with production SLAs and apply anti-affinity heuristics for online latency-sensitive pods.
Medium-term: introduce scheduling class for long-sequence batch jobs and a placement policy to prevent colocation with latency-sensitive online pods; add autoscaler warm pool / burst capacity options for dedicated.
Action Items:
- (SRE) Roll forward autoscaler minimum change to lexicon-prod-resv-usw across region (diego) — in progress.
- (Platform) QA PR #4182 for scheduler isolation and plan phased rollout (quentin).
- (Support/Product) Update onboarding checklist and recommended reservation templates for enterprise (maya/ava).
This ticket is intentionally technical and operational; runbook reference added. Recommend follow-up postmortem if customer requests formal RCA.
payload.summary: Intermittent p99 spikes and 5xxs on dedicated reservation during overlap with long-sequence batch jobs

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightPath Analytics reported an unexpected mid-cycle consumption of reserved credits after a scheduled multi-region batch embedding job. They observed a ~12% deduction from their reserved hourly credits window leading to a negative provisional balance and a flagged invoice variance.

Impact:
- Immediate: Customer's monthly provisional invoice shows a -$1,820 line attributed to 'usage adjustment' for the batch run on 2026-03-11 23:00 UTC. Customer reports they had sufficient reserved credits.
- Business: Customer is on a dedicated reserved plan; unexpected reserve consumption erodes trust and could trigger billing disputes.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: rh-dedicated-prod-1 (us-east)
- Batch job: nightly multi-region embed job (cron: 0 23 * * * in local time for customer)
- Model: openembed-v2-512 (quantized)
- Metering pipeline: batch-worker -> postback-service -> hourly-accumulator -> billing-reconciler

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Customer schedules a nightly batch of 1.2M texts at 2026-03-11 19:00 EST which corresponds to 2026-03-11 23:00 UTC.
2) Job completes and posts postbacks to our meter endpoint.
3) Next hourly reconciliation run attributes ~12% of the job to the previous hourly window due to a timestamp offset.
4) Customer sees reserve credits consumed mid-window and receives provisional negative balance notice.

Observed behavior:
- Postbacks from the batch worker contain X-Client-Timezone: "America/New_York" but timestamps are sent as local epoch_millis instead of normalized UTC. The postback service accepted the payload and used the received epoch to bucket into hourly-accumulator without normalization.

Expected behavior:
- All postbacks should be normalized to UTC in postback-service before hourly bucketing; reserved credits should be consumed only within the correct hourly window.

Relevant IDs / Logs:
- Customer job id: BP-embed-run-20260311-23
- Metering request examples (redacted): request_ids: [mtr-15f7, mtr-15f8, mtr-16a2]
- Billing line id: INV-PROV-20260311-1820

Customer note:
"We scheduled the job for 7PM EST; our billing team expected consumption in the 23:00 UTC window. The provisional invoice indicates part of the job consumed into the 22:00 window, which drained reserved credits and triggered an autopay hold. We need credits reapplied and guidance to prevent recurrence."

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:05 - Customer (BrightPath Analytics - billing@brightpath.com): Provided gzipped postback archive and their local scheduler cron. Noted that their batch library emits timestamps in milliseconds without timezone suffix.
2026-03-13 16:10 - Support (Sofia): Notified customer that engineering identified root cause (postback timestamp normalization bug) and that we will provisionally re-apply reserved credits for the affected window while a permanent fix is rolled out. Asked customer to confirm if they want immediate manual credit reallocation.
2026-03-14 09:30 - BrightPath (Billing contact): Confirmed they want immediate credit reallocation and asked for ETA on fix.
Hypothesis: Batch clients emitting local epoch_ms got interpreted as UTC, causing events to be bucketed into adjacent hourly windows during DST transitions.
Steps performed:
- Replayed sample postbacks to dev accumulator and reproduced mis-bucketing.
- Queried hourly_aggregate table: SELECT sum(tokens) FROM hourly_aggregate WHERE window_start BETWEEN '2026-03-11 22:00:00' AND '2026-03-11 23:00:00' AND org_id = 'org-brightpath'; observed +12% spike.
- Checked postback-service code path: no timezone header parsing; it trusts numeric epoch_ms and casts to UTC without client hinting.
- Confirmed dedicated cluster ingested messages unaltered (no proxy rewrite).
Temporary mitigation options considered:
1) Recompute hourly aggregates by re-normalizing postbacks to UTC and reapply credits (safe but expensive, impacts billing pipeline).
2) Apply a manual credit memo for the diff and leave metering data unchanged (fast, auditable).
3) Patch postback-service to normalize new incoming payloads and backfill past windows for the last 24-48h.
Partial workaround applied: Billing team issued a manual credit memo of $1,820 to BrightPath Analytics to offset the provisional negative line. Autopay hold cleared per customer request.
Engineering actions planned:
- Hotfix deployed to postback-service (v1.14.3) on 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC to always interpret incoming numeric epoch_ms as UTC (unless a timezone header is provided and canonicalized). Rollout went to prod-dedicated with canary. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/412
- Backfill job scheduled to re-run hourly-accumulator for the affected windows (2026-03-10 to 2026-03-13) to ensure historical aggregates align with credit memos. Backfill ETA: 2026-03-16 12:00 UTC.
- Billing reconciliation: once backfill completes, reconcile manual credit memo against any over/under-applied tokens and adjust final invoice if needed.
Follow-ups and notes:
- Customer requested a postmortem and list of needed client-side changes (we recommend: emit RFC3339 timestamps OR include X-Event-Timezone header for ambiguous epoch_ms).
- Task created to add unit tests for timezone normalization in postback-service and to add a monitoring alert for hourly-aggregate spikes >5% compared to running median.
Status: Manual credit applied; hotfix deployed; backfill scheduled. Engineering to update once backfill and reconciliation complete.
Apply timezone normalization unit tests in metering repository (PR#412 merged).
Add alert: hourly-agg spike >5% vs rolling 7-day median to PagerDuty component.
Document recommended postback contract (RFC3339 or timezone header) in developer docs and notify dedicated customers via email/console message.
Complete hourly-accumulator backfill and run billing reconciler; cross-check with manual memo and close adjustment loop.
payload.summary: Timezone offset during scheduled multi-region batch embeddings caused mid-cycle credit loss and invoice variance

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer Cobalt Health began reporting elevated 5xx rates for inference requests starting ~2026-03-11 03:20 UTC. Errors were mostly 502/503 returned by the Redwood API gateway. Customer impact: production traffic for 6 app routes experienced 30-60% failure rate for ~90 minutes during the window.

Impact:
- Affected customer: Cobalt Health (enterprise).
- Duration: ~03:20-04:50 UTC on 2026-03-11 (partial degradation continued intermittently until mitigations applied).
- User-visible: failed streaming sessions, aborted responses, HTTP 5xx to SDKs.

Timeline (initial):
- 03:15 UTC: Scheduled keystore rotation for platform-wide certs started (rolling across nodes).
- 03:18 UTC: First customer report via support channel (#support).
- 03:20 UTC: API gateway 5xx spike begins; alerts for apigw.error_rate and runtime.request_failures fire.
- 03:40 UTC: SRE engaged; initial mitigation attempts (temporary route drain) had limited effect.

Environment:
- prod, us-east-1 region, tenant pinned to dedicated pool.
- Runtime version: 2026.02.7-serv-rt
- API gateway: apigw-1.12.0

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Trigger keystore rotation (rolling cert refresh) during sustained traffic.
2) A subset of gateway->runtime mutual-TLS handshakes fail transiently for seconds on a node during rotation.
3) Failed handshakes cause connection resets; gateway retries; runtime prefetch queue continues to accept upstream prefetch work.
4) Runtime listener accept queue length and socket_fd count climb; new connections hit backlog limits and are rejected, resulting in 502/503 responses.

Observed behavior & evidence:
- apigw metrics: apigw.error_rate spiked from baseline 0.7% to 42% for affected routes (charts linked below).
- runtime metrics: runtime.listener.backlog_spike and runtime.fd_count rose concurrently with handshake failures.
- Kernel stats snapshot: somaxconn at default 128 on affected nodes; SYN backlog dropped; no obvious OOM.
- TLS logs from gateway show short windows of "handshake failure: certificate not yet available" and "remote closed connection" timestamps matching spike.
- No core dumps found for the runtime; no immediate memory pressure.

Logs and dashboards (links):
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/apigw/errors?from=2026-03-11T03:00Z&to=2026-03-11T05:00Z
- Kibana runtime logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/kibana/app/discover#runtime?query=SUP-233401
- Slack incident thread: #incidents -> message 1723

Temporary mitigations attempted:
- Disabled prefetch for affected tenant at 03:48 UTC (reduced downstream pressure).
- Put a routing rule to shift a portion of Cobalt Health traffic to a warm fallback pool at 03:52 UTC (partial recovery).
- Paused keystore rollout for the remainder of the region at 03:55 UTC.

Request from customer: Full post-incident analysis, permanent mitigation to prevent keystore rotations from causing availability loss, and guidance for tenant best practices during rotations.

Initial hypothesis: keystore rotation caused transient cert unavailability which produced TLS handshake failures between apigw and runtime. Unlike a pure TLS failure, runtime continued to accept prefetched work, so connection churn accumulated and hit accept/syn backlog limits.

What we checked:
- Verified rotation logs: keystore service restarted NodeAgent on each node to pick up new certs; restart window ~12s/node.
- Measured handshake failure ratio: ~7-12% of new handshakes to nodes in rotation window.
- FD counts: nodes under rotation showed fd_count climb from ~1200 to ~6600 over 10 minutes.
- somaxconn default 128 -> accept queue overflow.
- Autoscaler: did not trigger additional capacity because CPU and GPU utilization remained below scale-up thresholds; backlog buildup is a connection-level problem not CPU/GPU.

Hypotheses considered and ruled out:
- OOM or memory leak: no consistent memory growth; heaps stable.
- Model-level crash: runtime did not crash; returning 502s were at gateway/proxy level.

Actionable findings:
1) Keystore rotation implementation restarts local NodeAgent processes synchronously which interrupts TLS availability for short windows; when traffic is high, many nodes in quick succession produce repeated handshake failures.
2) The runtime's prefetch behavior accepts upstream work even while handshake failures are in progress, contributing to higher concurrent connections.
3) Kernel listen/accept backlog (somaxconn) is too low for the burst pattern produced by rotation failure/retries.

Suggested permanent fixes:
- Stagger keystore rotation: increase per-node delay and add health-check gating so NodeAgent only restarts after TLS socket drains.
- Treat handshake failures from internal mutual-TLS during rotation as 503-backoff signals to avoid aggressive retries in gateway.
- Add a temporary circuit-breaker on gateway for repeated "certificate unavailable" errors to fail fast and reduce connection churn.
- Increase somaxconn and ephemeral port tuning on runtime hosts as a safety buffer; coordinate with infra change window.
- Add a runtime config to refuse prefetch when inbound handshake error rate exceeds threshold.

Follow-ups created:
- ENG ticket to change keystore rollout logic and NodeAgent restart gating: INT-4367 (internal).
- Infra ticket to propose somaxconn bump and host tuning: INT-4419 (internal).
- Runbook update: add canary step and off-peak scheduling for keystore rollouts.

Mitigations applied during incident:
- Paused keystore rotation across us-east-1 and completed a controlled staggered rollout during low-traffic window (completed 2026-03-12 02:20 UTC).
- Disabled prefetch for the affected tenant for the remainder of the high-traffic period; customer traffic returned to normal error rates by 04:10 UTC.
- Deployed temporary apigw rule to limit retries on TLS handshake failures (rolled in via github.com/redwood-inference/apigw/pull/2917).

Permanent remediation plan (in progress):
- INT-4367: Update NodeAgent to perform graceful TLS handoff and gating before restart (owner: infra-security). ETA: 2026-04-05.
- INT-4419: Coordinate with infra to raise somaxconn and tune net.core settings for runtime hosts. ETA: 2026-03-28.
- ENG: Add prefetch backpressure threshold tied to handshake error rate; PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4392.
- Update keystore rotation runbook and schedule canary rollouts with traffic-aware windows.

Customer-facing resolution notes sent to Cobalt Health at 2026-03-13 09:12 UTC. Customer confirmed service stability and accepted temporary mitigations; requested post-mortem and timeline for permanent fixes.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 03:33 - SRE (Alex Ramos): Observed apigw error spike. Correlated with keystore rotation events. Investigating runtime fd_count and kernel backlog.
2026-03-11 03:48 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Disabled prefetch for tenant ID 'cobalt-prod' as emergency mitigation. Noted partial reduction in retry amplification.
2026-03-11 03:52 - Support (Maya Patel): Applied routing to fallback pool for 30% of traffic; customer reporting decreased errors but still intermittent failures.
2026-03-11 04:05 - Infra (Priya Singh): Paused keystore rollout. Will schedule staggered completion in maintenance window. Raised INT-4419 for kernel tuning.
2026-03-12 02:25 - Engineering (Rafael Gomez): Deployed apigw retry-limiter patch to treat handshake failures with fast-fail and exponential backoff (PR #2917).
2026-03-13 09:12 - Support (Maya Patel): Sent customer-facing incident summary and remediation plan. Customer acknowledged and requested follow-up tech review meeting.
payload.summary: High 5xx rate for tenant during keystore rollover causing runtime socket backlog and API 5xx wave

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC customers (notably Fathom Analytics on a dedicated pool) began observing a sustained increase in 5xx responses from the hosted API. Impact: ~18% of requests for the affected tenant failed with 502/503/504 over a 45-minute window during morning ramp. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated GPU pool, api-gateway fronting multiple serving-runtimes. Initial signal: Grafana alert for 5xx-rate > 8% for tenant route.
Initial triage: alerting showed 5xx spike started ~2 minutes after an automated control-plane healthcheck sweep and coincident with a cert-rotation job for the dedicated pool.
Correlation: TLS renegotiation rate tracked to a burst of control-plane heartbeats plus parallel cert-rotate operations that caused a flurry of short-lived TCP connections while runtimes were completing background model prefetchs.
Hypothesis 1: cert rotation + increased handshake rate exhausted accept queue on the runtime side causing socket churn and subsequent GPU watchdog timeouts.
Hypothesis 2: control-plane heartbeat fanout amplified to api-gateway when route weights were briefly rebalanced, causing accept queue pressure at ingress proxies and leading to runtime threadpool starvation.
Metric evidence: accept_queue_depth and halfopen_sockets correlated with 5xx spikes. Runtime GC/gpu-reset logs line up with top of spike. No single model code regression identified.
Customer impact: Fathom reported retries and timeouts in their ingestion pipeline; latency-sensitive clients observed tail latencies rise from ~120ms to >2s before failures increased.
Cross-links: Slack thread #support-incident-133337 captured early cross-team triage. See slack.com/archives/C01SUPPORT/p167847...
Short-term mitigation: throttled control-plane heartbeat fanout and paused the cert-rotation job for dedicated-pool-42. Applied a temporary apigw backpressure setting to limit concurrent handshakes per upstream. These actions reduced TLS renegotiations and stabilized accept_queue_depth; 5xx rate returned to baseline by 08:55 UTC. Long-term fix: runtime patch to better prioritize existing keepalives over new handshakes during high accept-queue pressure, and change cert-rotation orchestration to stagger operations per shard. Patch merged: runtime PR #2891; deployment scheduled and small canary validated on 2026-03-12.
1) Engineering to ship runtime handshake-priority patch and monitor for related regressions (owner: SRE)
2) Control-plane to update cert-rotation orchestrator to sequential/staggered mode (owner: Control Plane team, due 2026-03-20)
3) Add a permanent apigw handshake-rate limiter for dedicated pools (owner: API GW team)
4) Postmortem doc and runbook update for heartbeat-flood scenarios (owner: Incident Response)
5) Reach out to Fathom CS with RCA and mitigation steps applied (owner: Customer Success)
6) Consider adding tenant-level early-shed when accept_queue_depth > threshold (owner: Platform Reliability)
7) Monitor dedicated-pool-42 for a week for recurrence and report daily to SRE channel

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:05 — Engineering (post-deploy): Handshake-priority patch rolled to canary and validated; no regression observed on small workload. Will proceed with phased rollout.
Mitigated by pausing cert rotation and throttling control-plane heartbeat fanout; deployed handshake-priority runtime patch and updated rotation orchestration. Customer impact resolved; long-term fixes scheduled.

Issue summary: Customer reports repeated stalls and eventual client-side timeouts when making streaming generation requests that prime the model with 8-12 large documents and set max_tokens to 65k. Impact: Customer facing production outage for document summarization pipeline; multiple jobs failing and increased support load. Environment: prod, us-east-1, Dedicated edge routing to serving-runtime clusters.

Observed behavior: Streams start and return first few partial chunks (~1-2s), then stall for 40-90s and eventually client times out with HTTP 504 or streaming websocket disconnect. Server does not emit 5xx in API gateway logs but serving runtime shows long tail processing and repeated KV cache evictions.

Expected behavior: Streaming responses should proceed at consistent per-token latency for the configured max_tokens budget and large prefix, or fail fast with a clear 5xx that indicates resource exhaustion.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Upload 10 documents to prompt_context array (total ~180k tokens priming)
2) Call /v1/chat/stream with model redwood-3b-v2, max_tokens=65000, stream=true, temperature=0.2
3) Observe initial chunks emitted then stream stalls and client disconnects after 60s timeout.

Customer-provided artifacts: request/response HAR, websocket trace, sample prompt files, PMP job IDs.

Prepare 8-12 long documents totaling ~150k-200k tokens as multi-document primer.
Make a streaming generation request to /v1/chat/stream with max_tokens=65000 and stream enabled.
Watch for initial chunks then prolonged stall and eventual client-side timeout or 504.
Repeat with shorter primer (<10k tokens) to confirm requests succeed normally.

Multiple production jobs for GlobeDocs summarization pipeline are failing; customer reports >50% requests time out or disconnect. Revenue-impacting and blocking go-live for new enterprise integration.
Initial hypothesis: KV cache thrashing under heavy prime leading to repeated disk-backed reloads and large GC in worker process.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer's Python SDK client issues a function_call to an external tool (ledger.post_transaction). The tool immediately returns a 202 + deferred_id and promises a webhook callback to confirm completion. When the client experiences a client-side timeout and retries the original call, the runtime creates a second tool invocation because the deferred confirmation (deferred_id) from the first attempt is not being used to deduplicate the retry.

Impact: Duplicate ledger entries created at customer's downstream service, billing for two tool-invocations, customer saw inconsistent transaction state between UI and back-end until webhook arrived. Affects a small group of enterprise customers using deferred webhook confirmations with the Python SDK.

Environment: prod/us-east, Python SDK v1.8.2, server runtime v2.4.0, webhook endpoint behind customer's ALB (HTTPS).

Expected behavior: When the SDK retries a request that returned a deferred confirmation from the tool, the associated deferred_id or server-side acknowledgment should be attached/forwarded with the retry so the serving runtime can detect the in-flight async confirmation and deduplicate the second invocation.

Actual behavior: Retry path from Python SDK omits the runtime-provided "X-Deferred-Ack" header (or fails to attach the deferred_id into retry metadata). The serving runtime therefore treats the retry as a fresh invocation and forwards a second execution to the webhook target.

1) Configure a tool endpoint that accepts request and responds 202 with JSON {"deferred_id": "<uuid>"} and then posts final status to the configured webhook callback URL.
2) Use Python SDK v1.8.2 to call the tool using function_call semantics. Configure client timeout to a short window (e.g., 2s).
3) Make the tool intentionally delay final ACK (>2s) so the client times out locally and triggers SDK retry policy.
4) Observe two separate tool invocations at customer's service and two webhook sequences (one per invocation) arriving later, creating duplicate side-effects.

Client trace: python-sdk request id=req_0a8f2d, timeout triggered at T+2s, retry sent with new request id=req_0a8f2d_retry1. Server/runtime logs: received initial request req_0a8f2d -> tool forwarded, returned 202 with deferred_id=defer_b12; later received retry req_0a8f2d_retry1 -> forwarded as new invocation (no deferred_id present). Webhook sequence: callback/defer_b12 (first invocation) and callback/defer_c33 (second invocation). See runtime traces: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/txn/requests?var-request=req_0a8f2d (internal link).
- Reproduced internally with local tool that returns 202+deferred_id.
- Confirmed Python SDK v1.8.2 retry path uses the transport layer to re-issue the request but does not merge or propagate runtime-sent acknowledgment headers (we reproduced by printing outbound headers on retry).
- Serving runtime supports dedup via an "X-Deferred-Ack" header and a deferred registry keyed by deferred_id; this registry was never consulted for retry because header never present.
- Hypothesis: original design assumed deferred confirmations only arrive via webhook and that retries would be rare; the SDK's retry layer never receives or persists runtime response metadata for a partially completed call.
- Temporary mitigation is to increase client-side timeout to avoid retry window, or to disable client-side retries for deferred tool calls.

Workaround provided to customer: upgrade to Python SDK v1.9.0-beta which includes an interim change to persist response metadata to request-scoped retry state and forward deferred_id in subsequent retries. Added server-side guarding so duplicate deferred_ids are ignored if already registered (safe-guard).
Planned fix: PR #4821 adds persisted response metadata in the SDK transport layer and makes the default behavior to attach X-Deferred-Ack header on retry when present. Server-side: improve idempotency check to consult deferred registry on incoming retry if client-provided deferred_id header present. Target: roll SDK patch v1.9.0 stable and runtime guard in v2.4.1.
Follow-up: Add a section to the function-call runbook describing "deferred" semantics and recommended client retry configuration.

Additional notes:
2024-11-08 14:41 - SDK Owner (Sam Reed): Confirmed SDK does not preserve response headers across retries in v1.8.x. We have a quick patch to persist response metadata to memory for request-scoped retries. Will open PR.
2024-11-09 09:05 - Customer (Tabula Health - Integrations): Asked whether disabling retries is safe. Noted service cannot tolerate duplicate ledger entries; requested recommended settings.
2024-11-10 08:30 - SDK Owner (Sam Reed): PR #4821 opened and in review. Patch persists response headers on first response and attaches X-Deferred-Ack header for retries. Added unit tests and an integration test covering deferred webhook flow.
2024-11-10 12:00 - Customer (Tabula Health): Applied v1.9.0-beta; confirmed duplicates stopped on repeat test. Requested an official patch release schedule.
payload.summary: Deferred function confirmation (deferred_id webhook) lost when Python SDK retries, causing duplicate external side-effects

Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running SSE sessions from their mobile app frequently end with partial outputs (missing final punctuation or truncated last sentence) following a short network stall. After the stall, the client sometimes reconnects and receives duplicate prefixes but is still missing the terminal punctuation or closing sentence. This is blocking Parcelly's delivery-notification feature for ~5% of heavy users.

Impact:
- Intermittent user-visible truncation of generated messages (missing final sentence or period).
- Visible on the customer's dedicated deployment in us-east; affects mobile app behind enterprise SOCKS proxy.
- Occurs for long streaming responses (>12s), higher incidence on cellular+VPN.

Environment:
- Customer dedicated cluster (dedicated pool), region: us-east-1, prod.
- Client: Parcelly Android app v3.4.1, corporate SOCKS5 proxy + VPN.
- Server-side model: redwood-open-7b-v1, streaming SSE endpoint /v1/stream.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1. Start a long-form generation prompt that yields >250 tokens (~15s).
2. Put device onto cellular with enterprise SOCKS+VPN active.
3. Trigger a brief backgrounding or network flap (toggle airplane mode for 2-4s).
4. App reconnects and resumes the SSE session.

Observed behavior:
- Stream resumes but the final sentence is either truncated or the terminal punctuation is missing.
- Occasionally the client sees a duplicated prefix chunk (last 10-30 tokens) and then no concluding token.
- No explicit 5xx from API; connection shows FIN/ACK from intermediate proxy in some packet captures.

Expected behavior:
- Client should receive a complete finalization event (server-sent end marker or explicit choice 'finalized' frame) and full text for the choice, or the resumed session should produce the remaining tokens to close the choice.

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- Packet capture (pcap) showing mid-stream FIN from proxy: trace_id=tr-20260310-8f2a
- Client SDK logs with session id: sess-7a9f-22, timestamps and last-received-token-index=243.
- Example truncated output and original expected complete output.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:10 - SRE (Marta Higgins): Hypothesis: proxy or VPN teardown triggers a half-close where small buffered tail fragments are dropped. Client reconnect logic then replays prefix but server-side finalization event was lost and isn't retried due to idempotency semantics. Suggest adding explicit server-side finalize frame that can be requested by client on reconnect.
2026-03-12 16:40 - Customer (Parcelly): Accepts keepalive workaround short-term and requests ETA for permanent fix. Asking to retain session replay metadata in dedicated pool for 48h.
Findings so far: (1) No 5xx or application error logged in the Redwood runtime for trace tr-20260310-8f2a; logs show tokens streamed up to token index 246, then client-driven reconnect. (2) Packet captures demonstrate an intermediate proxy FIN/ACK sequence very close to the final tokens being emitted. (3) The server currently treats streaming as best-effort: if the connection drops before finalization event is ACKed, the model-generating worker does not automatically emit the remaining tokens to the resumed session because resume uses an idempotency token that assumes last ACK. (4) Client-side keepalive reduced occurrences in customer test. (5) Reproduced locally by inducing socket half-close and rapid reconnection via SOCKS.
Hypothesis: Enterprise proxy performs aggressive half-close or reassembly and drops last N small TCP segments containing finalization boundary; our resume protocol doesn't include a way for the client to request 'give me remainder since token #N' if server didn't persist remainder.
Workarounds: (1) Customer to enable application-level keepalives at 1s or enable SDK option 'stream_keepalive' to reduce proxy idle close behavior. (2) Recommend customer increase proxy idle timeout where possible.
Planned permanent fix: implement server-side finalization events combined with sequence numbers and idempotency bounds so resumed sessions can request missing token ranges. Patch PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-client-fixes/pull/142. Target: canary deploy to dedicated clusters in us-east by 2026-03-20.
Follow-ups: add monitoring for rate of truncated finalization events per cluster and expose metric in Console. Retain session metadata for 48h behind dedicated pool per customer request.
1) Communicate short-term workaround to Parcelly (Aisha): enable SDK keepalive and increase proxy timeout if possible. 2) Runtime team to review PR and schedule canary for dedicated clusters. 3) SRE to add alert for 'stream-finalization-missing' metric. 4) Track customer impact until permanent fix is deployed.
Parcelly's delivery-notification messages sometimes end mid-sentence for a small but meaningful subset of mobile users on enterprise VPNs. Workaround reduces occurrence; permanent server-side fix is being scheduled.
If PR is insufficient, expand to: (a) persist finalization buffer server-side for short window (48h) to allow client re-request, (b) ensure finalization frames are sent over multiple transport windows or marked for high-priority delivery. Include test harness that simulates proxy half-close and validates reassembly of finalization frame.
payload.summary: Partial stream outputs and missing terminal punctuation after mid-stream stall behind enterprise SOCKS proxy

Issue summary:
Customer reports that after SCIM provisioning from their on-prem Identity Provider (IdP) to Redwood Private, users in nested AD groups are missing expected RBAC role bindings. This started after a recent on-prem SCIM connector update on the customer side.

Impact:
- Several users cannot access model inference endpoints via the private VPC admin console and scheduled workers.
- Customer reports reduced platform functionality for internal automation (scheduled ingestion jobs failing with 403).
- Affects all users whose groups are exclusively assigned via nested group memberships (approx 18 accounts reported).

Environment:
- Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) in eu-west region
- Customer IdP: On-prem Active Directory with SCIM 2.0 connector (vendor: ForgeAuth v2.4)

Observed behavior:
- Provisioning payload contains a single string property 'memberOf' whose value is an escaped, semicolon-separated DN list inside quotes (i.e. a double-encoded string). Example payload snippet captured in access logs:
  \"memberOf\": \"\\\"CN=devs,OU=Groups,DC=acme,DC=corp;CN=platform-admins,OU=Groups,DC=acme,DC=corp\\\"\"
- Our SCIM parser expects either a JSON array of group objects or a semicolon-separated string (single-encoded). The double-encoded pattern is treated as a single raw string and not split, leading to no group matches against configured group-to-role mapping.

Expected behavior:
- Nested group DNs should be parsed and normalized into individual group identifiers that map to RBAC role bindings. Users in nested groups should receive expected roles and permissions.

Logs / Evidence:
- Inbound request recorded at 2026-03-11T15:12:03Z: content-type application/json; body contains memberOf: \"\\\"CN=devs,OU=Groups,DC=acme,DC=corp;CN=platform-admins,OU=Groups,DC=acme,DC=corp\\\"\"
- RBAC-service audit (2026-03-11T15:12:04Z): \"no_group_match: memberOf '\\"CN=devs,...' not found in map\"
- Admin console trace: provisioning processed, user created, role_assignments: []

Investigation notes:
- Replayed captured SCIM payloads to staging SCIM parser. Parser v1.8 splits on comma/semicolon only when field is a native array or unquoted string. It does not unescape an inner-quoted string, so double-encoded payloads remain a single token.
- Hypothesis: ForgeAuth 2.4 introduced a change in serialization for nested memberships, wrapping the semicolon-separated DNs inside an additional set of quotes.
- Quick patch attempted on staging: added a defensive unescape+split step before canonicalization which fixed mapping for replayed payloads. Patch is behavioral and requires test coverage for other IdP connector variants.

Workaround provided to customer:
- Customer temporarily modified their ForgeAuth SCIM connector to send groups as a proper JSON array (vendor docs exist) OR
- As alternate immediate mitigation, customer can add a custom mapping rule in Redwood Console that matches the entire double-encoded string to a role (not recommended long-term).

Next steps / Recommended actions:
- Ask ForgeAuth customer to confirm whether the connector change is intentional and if there is configuration to disable double-quoting.
- Ship a defensive fix in RBAC service to attempt to detect and unescape quoted membership strings, with unit tests across common IdP encodings.
- Add a Confluence runbook entry describing detection and short-term fixes for double-encoded SCIM group strings.

1) Configure ForgeAuth SCIM connector to send group membership to Redwood via POST /scim/v2/Groups or PATCH on Users.
2) Ensure nested group membership is encoded (group A is memberOf group B).
3) Observe provisioning payload captured by our SCIM endpoint.
4) Watch RBAC role mapping in console — expected roles are not created for these users.

Observed behavior:
- Provisioning payload contains a single string property 'memberOf' whose value is an escaped, semicolon-separated DN list inside quotes (i.e. a double-encoded string). Example payload snippet captured in access logs:
  "memberOf": "\"CN=devs,OU=Groups,DC=acme,DC=corp;CN=platform-admins,OU=Groups,DC=acme,DC=corp\""
- Our SCIM parser expects either a JSON array of group objects or a semicolon-separated string (single-encoded). The double-encoded pattern is treated as a single raw string and not split, leading to no group matches against configured group-to-role mapping.

Expected behavior:
- Nested group DNs should be parsed and normalized into individual group identifiers that map to RBAC role bindings. Users in nested groups should receive expected roles and permissions.

Logs / Evidence:
- Inbound request recorded at 2026-03-11T15:12:03Z: content-type application/json; body contains memberOf: "\"CN=devs,OU=Groups,DC=acme,DC=corp;CN=platform-admins,OU=Groups,DC=acme,DC=corp\""
- RBAC-service audit (2026-03-11T15:12:04Z): "no_group_match: memberOf '\"CN=devs,...' not found in map"
- Admin console trace: provisioning processed, user created, role_assignments: []

2026-03-12T17:04:00Z - Jordan Patel (Support): Logged after customer call. Captured sample payload and escalated to identity team.
2026-03-12T20:15:00Z - Marina Gomez (SRE): Replayed payload in staging. Confirmed parser does not unescape nested quotes. Temporary patch in staging fixed replay. Will prepare PR with tests.
2026-03-13T09:32:00Z - Customer (Acme Payments): We deployed a ForgeAuth hotfix earlier this week; we can toggle serialization settings but want Redwood to handle this edge-case to avoid future regressions.
2026-03-13T14:48:00Z - Marina Gomez (SRE): Preparing PR to add defensive normalization. Will include feature flag to gate behavior for private customers to review. Requesting customer permission to deploy patch to their private control plane during maintenance window.
2026-03-14T08:22:00Z - Jordan Patel (Support): Awaiting customer confirmation of maintenance window (status set to Waiting on Customer).
Workaround available (customer adjusted SCIM to send array) and staging patch validated; production fix pending customer-approved maintenance window.
1) Configure IdP SCIM connector to send group memberships as JSON arrays (preferred).
2) If not possible, create a targeted role mapping that matches the double-encoded string until patch applied.
PR#412 - add unescape+split normalization in rbac-service (testing required)
Update Confluence runbook with detection pattern and mitigation steps
Coordinate maintenance window with customer for production patch

Issue summary: Customer VeloxAI reports that single streaming generate calls are being split into multiple 'sessions' in the Console usage analytics, resulting in inflated session counts and mismatched per-session metrics in dashboards and billing exports. Impact: Overcounted sessions and per-session latency/length metrics; potential billing discrepancies for a major customer on Dedicated tier. Observed since 2026-03-08 after a streaming proxy rollout.

Context: VeloxAI uses long-lived streaming sessions for multi-turn generation. Console aggregates usage by a session_id field derived during request ingest. When their streaming client briefly reconnects (common under mobile networks), our pipeline currently creates a new session_id instead of continuing the existing logical session, creating multiple session records for one logical interaction.
Customer-visible: dashboards show 2–6x more sessions for streaming routes vs raw logs. Billing export shows session-count deltas for VeloxAI (estimated +18% sessions last 7 days). Business: Dedicated customer concerned about overbilling and product analytics integrity.
1) Customer starts a streaming generate request with a persistent client-side session token (client-session: abc123).
2) Simulate intermittent network blips causing the client to reconnect the stream (close and re-open WebSocket within 10s).
3) Observe Console > Usage > Sessions for the route: two distinct session entries appear with separate session_id values even though the client-session token is identical.
4) Export usage CSV for the timeframe and compare session_count vs raw request logs (requestid-level): raw logs show 1 logical session, Console shows multiple.
2026-03-09T17:02:41Z INFO ingest: message=received stream open request, client_session=abc123, websocket_conn_id=ws-789, request_id=req-1001
2026-03-09T17:02:47Z WARN streaming-proxy: connection dropped, websocket_conn_id=ws-789, reason=network_timeout
2026-03-09T17:02:49Z INFO streaming-proxy: connection re-established, websocket_conn_id=ws-812, client_session=abc123, request_id=req-1002
2026-03-09T17:02:49Z INFO usage-ingest: new_session_created session_id=sess-20260309170249, source_conn=ws-812, original_req=req-1001

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 - VeloxAI (Customer): Confirmed they include a client-session header in their SDK; reported that reconnects are frequent for mobile users. Customer requests urgent workaround and rollback option for the streaming proxy rollout.
Ingest pipeline stages: streaming-proxy -> kafka topic 'ingest-raw' -> sessionizer service -> analytics rollup. Sessionizer currently keys on websocket_conn_id when present, else request_token. Issue triggered when client sends persistent client_session header but websocket_conn_id changes on reconnect.
Correlation of request_ids shows that reconnect events keep client_session but generate a new websocket_conn_id. Sessionizer creates new session node because websocket_conn_id was considered authoritative.
Billing export job aggregates by session_id produced by sessionizer. Fix must preserve logical session continuity to avoid billing noise.
Tested quick patch in staging that checks for client_session header and if seen, attempts to reconcile with last session for that client_session within a 60s window. Staging results show sessions no longer split for reconnect scenarios.
Risk: naive reconciliation could join unrelated concurrent sessions if client_session is reused across different tabs or users. Need a safer tie-breaker (e.g., compare last activity timestamp + IP fingerprint + request sequence number).
Related past tickets: SUP-42188 (console usage unique-client-spike missing requestid) indicated edge cases in session attribution; learned patterns reused here.
Observed affected_models were the routes most used by VeloxAI (gptx-mini for chat, gptx-embedder-v2 for embeddings), but root cause is transport/sessionization logic and not model-specific.
Workaround (prod hotfix): Temporarily prefer 'client_session' header for session continuation when websocket_conn_id changes and last_activity < 60s. Hotfix deployed to us-east on 2026-03-14 (rollout id: rollout-20260314-psi).
Permanent fix: Platform Eng to land PR that enhances sessionizer to use a safe reconciliation heuristic (client_session + last_activity + IP_fingerprint) and adds an opt-in console toggle to control session merge behavior. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2894 (in review).
Customer communication: Sent VeloxAI a status note and temporary credits offer while we validate corrected billing exports. Customer accepted: credits capped at $5k for the affected billing period pending final audit.
Follow-ups: Add an automated analytics test for reconnect scenarios in the ingress e2e suite; update confluence runbook and alert thresholds to detect sudden session_count drift (>15% over 24h). Assigned to Lina Chen for rollout plan and Tom Reynolds for monitoring updates.
payload.summary: Console sessionization causing single streaming API call to be recorded as multiple usage sessions

Issue summary: Customer CortexAI reported an unexpected provisional overcharge on their hourly invoice for 2026-03-09 14:00 - 15:00 UTC. Impact: ~120k extra embedding tokens billed (provisional), causing a provisional negative balance and triggering a credit hold. Environment: production (us-east-1), dedicated pool org 4872. Steps to reproduce: 1) Not reproducible deterministically; appears after sustained async postback retries from edge proxies during a short network partition. 2) Check hourly-accumulator for duplicate postback IDs in the 14:00 window. 3) Inspect reconciler logs for repeated retry bursts. Logs: postback-reconciler lines show repeated POSTs for same postback_id with increasing retry_count within a 7s burst window. Customer impact: Billing line item shows doubled token count for a subset of embedding requests that used a prewarm kv-cache policy. Customer asked for provisional credit and explanation.
Simulate postback network flapping for 30s using edge proxy test harness
Trigger large batch embed job pinned to dedicated pool with kv-cache soft-warm enabled
Force postback worker to retry by returning 502 to initial POSTs and allow up to 5 retries per postback
2026-03-09T14:12:05Z postback-reconciler INFO received postback id=pb_8f3a retry=1 tokens=1200 org=4872
2026-03-09T14:12:07Z postback-reconciler INFO received postback id=pb_8f3a retry=2 tokens=1200 org=4872
2026-03-09T14:12:08Z hourly-accumulator WARN duplicate postback id=pb_8f3a not deduped due to race window
2026-03-10 | Aisha Patel: Customer reported spike on 2026-03-09 14:00 hour. Provided provisional invoice PDF and trace_id 7f9a-embed-20260309-14 to support team.
2026-03-10 | Marcus Lee: Triage assigned. Initial hypothesis: dedupe race in hourly-accumulator introduced by change to microbatch window (PR #414). Adding billing and infra oncall.
2026-03-10 | Priya Nair (Billing): Confirmed provisional charge appears as duplicate tokens in hourly rollup. Holding customer from manual charge until investigation completes.
2026-03-11 | SRE oncall (Diego Martinez): Replayed reconciler logs and reproducer in staging. Observed dedupe key absent when retries land within same batch boundary and arrival ordering changes due to proxy bursts.
2026-03-12 | Marcus Lee: Created hotfix PR to enforce idempotent reduction at accumulator ingress. Plan to deploy to staging 2026-03-12 16:00 UTC then to prod 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC with traffic ramp. Notifying customer of provisional credit timeline.
Hypothesis: recent change to postback batching window (microbatch size reduction) removed a delay that previously allowed dedupe metadata to load before accumulator ingestion; when a burst of retries arrives, duplicate postback IDs can be accepted into the hourly accumulator before dedupe check completes.
Confirmed by running synthetic flapping test in staging: when edge proxy returns 502 five times within 10s, postback worker retry loop sends identical postbacks with retry_count increments; accumulator inserted both events when processing concurrency > 4.
Billing analysis: token-level audit shows two entries with same original_request_id for ~2.3k requests, amounting to ~118,700 tokens double-counted for hour 14:00 UTC. This matches customer-reported delta on provisional invoice.
Related code refs: postback-reconciler commit 9f1a3b0 (changed batch window), hourly-accumulator indexing logic lacking CAS-based dedupe for near-simultaneous inserts.
Dashboards: billing/hourly-accumulator/inserts spike graph and postback/retry-rate show correlated spikes 2026-03-09T14:00-14:06Z (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/accum/accum-spikes?org=4872)
Temporary mitigation suggested: mark affected hour as provisional and block auto-finalize for that hour while fix is deployed; manual credit adjustment post reprocessing.
Race condition in hourly-accumulator dedupe path: when postback retries arrive in a tight burst the dedupe metadata load and insert can interleave, allowing duplicate inserts for the same original_request_id under high concurrency after a microbatch timing change.
Hotfix deployed: postback-reconciler PR#482 implements strong idempotency keys (CAS insert) at accumulator ingress and backfills a reprocess job for the 14:00 UTC hour to recompute hourly aggregates. Team processed the backfill and issued a provisional credit to CortexAI for the duplicated tokens. Prod deployment completed 2026-03-12 23:10 UTC. Billing adjusted and credit applied; customer notified and provisional hold removed.
2026-03-12 22:00 UTC: Deployed hotfix to prod behind feature flag. Verified staging reproducer no longer duplicates.
2026-03-12 23:05 UTC: Ran backfill to reprocess hourly-accumulator for org 4872 for 2026-03-09 14:00 window. Aggregate reduced by 118,700 tokens.
2026-03-12 23:15 UTC: Finance applied a manual credit line to customer's account and reissued corrected provisional invoice. Customer confirmed receipt and accepted credit.
Follow-up: schedule invariant tests for postback dedupe race and add an alert on hourly-accumulator duplicate-key rate. Owner: Marcus Lee. ETA for full test coverage: 2026-03-26.
Add unit and integration tests for CAS dedupe on accumulator ingress (owner: Marcus Lee)
Add Grafana alert for duplicate-key insertion rate crossing threshold (owner: SRE)
Run a one-week audit of recent hourly windows to find similar anomalies and proactively credit affected customers if found (owner: Billing team)
Document postback dedupe runbook and update confluence page (owner: Diego Martinez)

Issue summary: Customers observed intermittent p99 latency/throughput regressions for AtlasDocs' dedicated capacity pool across multiple small-stream workloads. Impact: Real customer-facing latency spikes causing API timeouts and increased request retries, visible as a 30% throughput drop for the tenant during spikes.

Observed window: 2026-03-04 23:10 - 2026-03-05 02:00 UTC. The pattern is transient (10-60s bursts) and correlates with a high number of concurrent short-lived streaming sessions from the tenant and a collocated neighbor tenant.

Impact details: - API p50 unchanged; p95 increased slightly; p99 increased up to ~2.8x baseline. - Customer reported 5xx retries from app logs and increased client-side backpressure. - No platform-wide outage; isolated to the dedicated reserved pool hosting the customer and a small set of other tenants.
1) In a dedicated pool with mixed tenants, start ~500 short streaming connections across two tenants (A = AtlasDocs workload, B = simulated neighbor small-batch streams).
2) Set stream length to 10-30 tokens per request with inter-request interval of 50-200ms to emulate high churn of small streams.
3) Observe p99 latency and GPU queue length via /metrics and per-tenant dashboards; repeat with tenant B removed to compare.
Support timeline: Grafana traces show p99 spikes coincident with abrupt rises in per-GPU kernel-preempt counts and scheduler wait queue growth.
GPU metrics: SM utilization dips from 78% to 54% during spikes while scheduler run-queue and kernel-preempt counters spike; PCIe enqueue latency shows 2-4x increase.
Serving runtime logs: repeated 'preempted_by_owner' and 'stream_coalesce_timeout' events for small-batch inference workers between 23:12-23:40 UTC.
Autoscaler: no scale-up during the first bursts due to cooldown settings; scale response happens after sustained queueing, which is too late for short bursts.
2026-03-05 00:15 - Initial triage by Support (Maya): correlated customer error traces with pool-level telemetry; opened INC-20260305-01.
2026-03-05 01:00 - SRE (Santiago) reproduced burst in staging using the small-stream harness; observed same p99 spike behavior when two tenants with many short-lived streams share GPU nodes.
Hypothesis: Gang-scheduling / rapid context-switching for many short-lived streaming connections is causing kernel preemption and inefficient packing on device, leading to transient throughput degradation for affected tenants.
Additional finding: Autoscaler cooldown and slot fragmentation allow bursts to persist; the scheduler's fairness heuristics cause alternating preemptions that reduce SM efficiency during churn.
Staging test: Enabling 'stream_coalesce' reduced p99 amplitude but increased tail of single-request latencies; increasing per-tenant min_batch and raising autoscaler sensitivity improved overall throughput.
Cross-references: Related to historical artifacts in SUP-33489 (fragmentation from small streams) but root cause here is scheduling interaction under short-burst workloads.
Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-05: Reached out to AtlasDocs with timeline and asked for peak request samples and client-side logs. Slack thread: #support-dedicated-pools.
AtlasDocs Ops (Priya Kaur) - 2026-03-05: Provided request_id samples and affirmed customer sees retries in their dashboards at the same timestamps. Shared a CloudWatch export and app-side retry logs.
Santiago Ruiz (SRE) - 2026-03-05: Ran controlled repro in staging (harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/67). Observed kernel preempt spikes and queueing pattern matching prod.
SRE (Santiago) - 2026-03-06: Applied temporary mitigation by moving AtlasDocs to a short-lived isolation reservation (warm-up nodes) and adjusted autoscaler cooldown to 30s in the affected pool. Customer reports immediate improvement.
Maya Chen - 2026-03-07: Notified customer of temporary fix and ETA for permanent scheduler patch. Opened follow-up operational ticket INT-900401 to track scheduler changes and rollout plan.
Temporary mitigation: migrated AtlasDocs' traffic to an isolation reservation within the dedicated pool and increased autoscaler sensitivity and reduced cooldown to 30s. Enabled stream_coalesce for the pool as an interim measure. Permanent fix: scheduler team to land fairness and preemption-rate limiting patch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/178) to avoid oscillatory preemptions for many short-lived streams. Post-deploy will include a staged rollout to dedicated pools and an update to the troubleshooting runbook. Follow-ups: INT-900401 (scheduler rollout), add automated test in perf-harness for short-stream gang scenarios, update RLHF-3b quantization packing doc where needed.
1) Scheduler: implement preemption-rate limiter and smarter packing heuristics for sub-100-token streams (owner: @scheduler-team, due 2026-03-20).
2) Autoscaler: add burst-mode tuning profile for pools with many short streams and reduce default cooldown in dedicated pools (owner: @autoscale-team, due 2026-03-14).
3) Observability: add a per-tenant 'kernel_preempt' alert and a short-stream pattern detector to trigger early autoscaler scaling (owner: @telemetry, due 2026-03-12).
4) Docs: update dedicated-pool runbook with mitigation steps to isolate noisy tenants and to use reservation warm-up (owner: @support-docs, due 2026-03-11).
