payload.description:
Issue summary:
When an embedded dashboard with multiple paginated panels is viewed while a recent retention backfill job is running, pagination on embedded panels resets to page 1 intermittently. This reset shifts the time windows used by the client-side alert evaluation UI, resulting in alert evals that skip recent buckets (missing 1–3 minutes) and therefore suppress expected alerts.

Impact:
- Customer reports missed threshold alerts for a production route used in BeaconHealth AI’s triage workflow; they missed three alerts over a 45m window.
- Affected customers on enterprise tier using embedded widgets and long retention backfills.

Environment:
- Redwood Console (hosted) prod cluster serving eu-west and us-east; issue observed in us-east region.
- Browser repros on Chrome 112 and Safari 16.

Observed behavior:
- Opening an org-embedded dashboard with paginated panels during a retention backfill occasionally causes the panel to jump back to page 1.
- The client-side alert evaluation code uses visible panel page offsets to compute alert windows; after a reset, the evaluation skips the most recent N buckets causing missed alerts.

Expected behavior:
- Pagination state for embedded panels should be preserved (or decoupled from backend retention maintenance) and alert evaluation windows should remain continuous across retention backfill events.
1) Customer loads an embedded dashboard iframe that contains 3 paginated panels (each panel shows time-series with 1m buckets).
2) Trigger or schedule a retention backfill in us-east (we reproduced via backfill job id retention-backfill-20260310-1730).
3) Observe panel pagination behavior in the guest org session while the backfill runs (5–20m).
4) Check alert timeline: open alert eval history for the alert rule connected to the panel’s route metric and compare gaps to server ingest timeline.
Console JS: Uncaught (at promise) Error: pagination-state-sync failed: 409 (conflict) — /api/console/embed/state (2026-03-10T17:42:03Z)
Browser network: GET /api/console/embed/state?org=beacon-health&pageToken=eyJ... returned 200 then 409 intermittently during backfill window
Server: retention-indexer: backfill job retention-backfill-20260310-1730 started at 2026-03-10T17:30:12Z, reindexed partition p-20260310-17-30; logs show short spikes of lock contention on embed_state table (see link)
2026-03-10 - Support (Maya Chen): Opened with BeaconHealth AI after they reported 3 missed alerts during a 45m window. Customer provided dashboard embed URL, alert rule id A-89321, and time of backfill. Asked for timeline and temporary mitigation steps.
2026-03-11 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Reproduced locally by running a retention backfill against a staging copy. Observed pagination state writes failing with 409s and client falling back to default page=1. Hypothesis: state writes are blocked by retention-indexer locks during partition repair which causes client fallback. Assigned to console team for fix + hotpatch.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 - Support (Maya Chen): Shared a screenshot and timestamp from BeaconHealth AI showing alert history gaps. Customer needs a workaround they can apply today; asked if an account-level toggle is possible to disable server-side pagination sync for embeds.
Checked DB traces for embed_state table during backfill: saw lock wait times up to 1400ms and repeated update retries from embed-sync workers.
Correlation: each 409 pagination reset lines up with a retention-indexer partition reindex event (retention-backfill-20260310-1730).
Repro steps successful on staging when artificially holding a table lock during pagination-state upsert. Client behavior falls back to page=1 when server signals conflict.
Related github PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-console/pull/7845 (client fallback fix).
Related internal ticket INT-44321 flagged for making embed_state upserts idempotent and removal of row locks during reindexing.
Temporary: client-side hotfix deployed to ensure local pagination token is preserved when server returns 409 conflict. Canary rolling in us-east (2026-03-14 22:00Z).
Permanent: engineering story created to change embed_state writes to conditional upsert and make retention-indexer reindex less disruptive (linked INT-44321). Also adding an org-level toggle to disable server-side pagination sync for embeds as a customer-facing mitigation.
Follow-up: postmortem and runbook update to include guidance for retention backfills impacting embed state (assigned to Priya Nair).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasDocs reported intermittent truncation of SSE streaming responses during a multi-minute window following an auth token refresh. The client observed the final sentence of generated responses occasionally missing and, in several cases, a duplicated metadata envelope (system messages / role attributes) inserted midstream after the client reconnected.

Impact:
- Affects a subset of production users of AtlasDocs in us-east using SSE for long-running generation.
- Truncated paragraphs lead to malformed documents in their ingestion pipeline; business impact: downstream docs missing closing paragraphs causing parsing errors.
- Intermittent, reproducible within token refresh scenario; not all streams are affected.

Environment:
- Production (us-east), hosted Redwood API endpoint behind edge-proxy + ALB.
- AtlasDocs is enterprise plan with pinned model redwood-llama-70b.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Start a long SSE generation with a conversation prompt (typical length 800-1500 tokens).
2) Let generation run until auth token rotation window (customer client configured to refresh tokens proactively around 55m).
3) Token refresh triggers an SSE reconnect path on the client; sometimes client attempts resume, sometimes full reconnect.
4) Observe the final 1-3 sentences of the response missing or the stream contains a repeated metadata envelope followed by a truncated tail.

Observed behavior:
- Server-side logs show a complete final chunk emitted for the generation id, but client-side captures show either a gap (no final tokens) or a duplicate metadata event inserted before the final tokens, effectively making the final tokens be dropped by the client parser.
- In metrics, a small spike in 5xx/stream-timeout correlates with the affected windows.
- Reconnect path varies by client SDK version; older SDKs more likely to fall back to full reconnect.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should stitch tokens idempotently without duplication and without losing the closing tokens.
- If client fully reconnects, server should send a consistent snapshot/resume payload that preserves the final tokens or include an explicit terminal marker.

Attachments / evidence:
- Customer-provided browser HAR and a trimmed SSE transcript (attached to ticket).
- Server trace snippets showing final emit at 2026-03-10T18:32:15Z for convo id conv_9a1b and subsequent ACK window logs.
- Grafana snapshots of stream success rate and auth rotation events in the 5-minute window.

Notes about scope:
- This appears specific to the interplay between token refresh, edge connection handoff, and our resume id mapping and is distinct from simple proxy truncation (we have separate tickets for ALB half-close patterns).
2026-03-10 09:14 - AtlasDocs Support: 'We see this ~1-2% of long streams. Often happens during our token refresh. Final paragraph missing or we get a repeated system JSON block.'

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:10 - SRE (Ana Ribeiro): 'Observed brief spike in edge connection migrations at 2026-03-10T18:32Z; logs show a keepalive jitter coinciding with token refresh. ALB did a circuit rebalance. Investigating whether session id is preserved across the rebind.'
2026-03-12 12:05 - AtlasDocs Support: 'Applied SDK bump and saw a drop in occurrences in our staging harness. Production monitoring will continue.'
Hypothesis 1: Edge rebind + token rotation leads to resume id mismatch. The server accepts the new session but our resume id mapping may point to a stale snapshot when rebind occurs during inflight streaming KV priming.
Hypothesis 2: Client parser behavior: when a metadata envelope appears midstream, older SDKs treat it as a message boundary and drop following tokens if ordering differs. New SDK includes a more tolerant parser.
Evidence: Server traces show final token batch emitted but the corresponding ACK window not observed from client prior to disconnect. Edge logs show connection handoff between two proxies within 500-1200ms of token refresh request.
Reproduction: Added test harness that simulates token refresh and randomized edge rebind; reproduced truncation consistently when rebind happened within 1.5s of resume window. Patch candidate simulated resolved the case in unit/integration tests.
Risk assessment: Patch small and scoped (resume id grace window + ordered ack handshake). Potential side-effect: slightly extended time where resume id is considered canonical (5s) — low risk for correctness, small additional state retention needed on edge nodes.
Related: PRs and runbooks linked; see github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4321 for code changes and confluence page for design notes.
Mitigation deployed (2026-03-12): v1.8.3 of serving-runtime plus edge proxy config change rolled to us-east. Changes: (1) 5s resume-id grace window after auth refresh, (2) ordered-ack handshake on resume envelopes, (3) additional logging on resume mismatch cases.
Customer remediation: AtlasDocs upgraded client SDK to v2.4.1 and added a 3s random jitter to token refresh timing. They reported a significant drop in truncation occurrences in staging and early production sampling.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sharp increase in end-to-end latency and intermittent 504 timeouts for requests that trigger multi-stage tool/function calls. Problem started after a catalog update rolled out last week (model routing + tool metadata changes).

Impact:
- ~8% request error rate (504) for tool-invoking flows during peak in us-east; elevated p95/p99 latency for affected routes (~700–1200ms increase).
- Affects production traffic for VennHealth (enterprise) and traces show repeated synchronous preflight/validation round-trips for each tool invocation.

Environment:
- prod us-east primary, some echoes in eu-west.
- Customer uses model rw-13b-v1 with a two-step toolchain: (1) schema validation + metadata lookup (internal RPC to schema-validator service) and (2) external tool proxy invocation (function-proxy).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Send a multi-turn chat request with tool invocation payload and complex tool schema (nested JSON with >6 required fields).
2) Observe server-side timeline: initial request -> schema validation RPC -> model scoring -> tool proxy handshake -> model re-score -> streaming response.
3) Repeat 50–100 times during peak and measure p99.

Observed behavior:
- Each request is incurring 2–3 synchronous RPCs before token generation begins.
- Schema validation RPC occasionally returns with 100–200ms variance; combined with the proxy handshake increases tail latency.
- Under load, some tool proxy handoffs time out and the platform surfaces 504 to the client.

Expected behavior:
- Schema validation should be cached when identical tool signatures are used by a single customer and not require full round-trip every request.
- Tool proxy handshakes should be optimized (async or background validation) to avoid adding to critical path for model token generation.

Initial hypothesis:
- A recent change in tool metadata propagation (catalog rollout) removed a short-lived local cache entry for schema-validator results, forcing synchronous validation on every request.
- Tool proxy handshake includes unnecessary synchronous capability checks that could be deferred.

Next steps / investigation plan:
1) Retrieve traces for SUP-26112 request IDs from us-east (request IDs provided by customer).
2) Check recent deploys to schema-validator and tool-proxy around 2026-03-09 -> 2026-03-11.
3) Reproduce load in staging with identical tool schema and measure per-request RPC counts and latencies.
4) If cache removal confirmed, re-enable validation caching for identical schemas and add a short TTL.
5) Consider changing handshake to background validation with optimistic execution path for known-good tool signatures.

Workaround provided to customer:
- Support recommended a short-term client-side batching to combine similar invocations (reduces per-call overhead) and temporarily pin to rw-13b-v1 replica set in another region (eu-west) while we investigate.

Resolution criteria:
- p95/p99 for tool-invoking routes back to baseline within 24h of mitigation and no new 504s from validation/proxy handoffs.

Links / artifacts:
- Customer-provided traces attached in ticket (trace IDs included in comments).
- Related runbook: Toolcall Diagnostics Runbook (confluence).

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:42 - On-call SRE (Marco Diaz): Acknowledged. Reproduced elevated p99 on a small sample against prod-us-east using the customer's payload. Observed repeated schema-validator RPCs before model invocation. Collecting full spans.
2026-03-13 07:37 - Support (Elena Park): Customer accepted temporary workaround to route to eu-west and implement client-side batching. Customer will keep us updated if 504s continue after routing change.
2026-03-14 03:10 - SRE (Marco Diaz): Hotfix (rollback cache change) deployed to canary in us-east. Early telemetry shows per-request RPC count reduced and p99 latency trending down. Will watch for 24h before closing.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer CogniWare reported repeated request timeouts (504s) and elevated p95 latency on their dedicated GPU pool in us-east. The drop started as intermittent spikes on 2026-03-09 and became sustained during business hours on 2026-03-10.

Impact:
- Customer experiencing 20-40% request failures for production inference routes (streaming and standard generate endpoints).
- End-user facing degraded UX for chat and batch scoring.
- Customer is on a committed Dedicated plan; business impact is high.

Observed behavior and quick indicators:
- Request queue lengths on the dedicated pool increased 6-8x during incidents.
- GPU SM utilization observed low (15-30%) while token service latency and PCIe wait metrics spiked.
- Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles roughly every 3-7 minutes for the pool.
- A single tenant in the pool was running many long-running small-batch synchronous requests that appeared to block scheduler fair-share and cause head-of-line queueing.
- External gateway returned 504s; internal serving runtime returned several kernel-timeout and connection-reset logs.

Environment:
- prod cluster: dedicated-pool-cogniware-us-east
- Node type: A100-40GB (mixed 1/2 config)
- Model variants: redwood-alpha-13b (quantized q4), llama-2-70b (fp16)

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Deploy a synthetic workload that mixes high-concurrency short streaming requests with intermittent large-batch scoring jobs to the same dedicated pool.
2) Run sustained bursts (5k reqs/min) for ~20 minutes.
3) Observe queue growth, autoscaler churn, and increases in token latency leading to gateway timeouts.

Relevant logs/metrics (links included below):
- Dedicated pool dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated/pool/dedicated-pool-cogniware-us-east
- Autoscaler event stream: https://logs.redwood.ai/autoscaler/streams/dedicated-pool-cogniware-us-east
- Recent SRE heap traces and kernel logs attached in internal storage.

Immediate customer impact: high. Customer reported lost queries and has asked for mitigation within SLA window.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:44 - Customer (CogniWare): Noted that latency improvements when we moved heavy batch jobs to a separate window — requesting temporary isolation.
2026-03-11 07:20 - Support: Provisioned isolated fallback pool for CogniWare and started migration trial for high-risk routes. Monitoring impact.
Metric correlation shows queue length growth preceded autoscaler actions by ~30-90s, indicating the autoscaler reacts to backlog but cooldown allowed immediate shrinkage before warmup completed.
GPU telemetry: low SM utilization with high page migration/PCIe wait suggests per-request serialization or NVLINK contention on colocated pods rather than GPU compute shortage.
Trace sampling shows scheduler granted many short-lived slots to the noisy tenant; their job mix favors sync requests which block preemption and queue fairness.
Reproduced core symptoms in staging by driving mixed workloads; observed autoscaler cooldown=3m, scale_step=1 node which caused oscillation and repeated GPU warmup overhead.
Checked node dmesg and driver logs — no OOMs or driver crashes. Found intermittent CUDA power-limit throttling messages for one host; flagged for infra to inspect power-capping policy.
SRE ran a controlled test: increasing autoscaler min_nodes to 2 and cooldown to 10m removed thrash and eliminated 504s during synthetic reproduction.
Hypotheses: (1) autoscaler configuration too aggressive for mixed workload; (2) lack of per-tenant admission/fairness; (3) noisy tenant request pattern amplifies warmup costs and causes head-of-line blocking.
Action items created for long-term fixes: autoscaler hysteresis tuning, per-tenant admission controls, prewarm heuristics, and improved telemetry to detect queue-starvation early.
Temporary measures applied 2026-03-11: moved CogniWare heavy routes to a reserved fallback pool and increased dedicated-pool min_nodes to 2 for 24 hours.
Autoscaler parameters adjusted in prod: cooldown extended to 10m, scale_step increased to 2 for pools with mixed workload labels, warmup prefetch increased to reduce per-node warmup latency.
Implemented short-term scheduler change: per-tenant concurrency cap to reduce head-of-line blocking for synchronous short requests.
Customer confirmed effective reduction in 504s to <2% and p95 latency returned to baseline on 2026-03-12.
Planned long-term: follow-up RFC for autoscaler redesign, per-tenant QoS, and telemetry alerts. Assigned to ENG roadmap Q2.
Post-action: create post-incident review and update runbook with detection query and mitigation steps.
payload.summary: Dedicated pool throughput drop: GPU queue starvation and autoscaler thrashing causing request timeouts

Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10T02:05 and 2026-03-10T03:30 UTC Axiom Payments reported duplicated streaming responses and a surge of 5xx errors plus client-observed throttling that caused ~18% of payment API calls to fail or be delayed beyond customer SLOs.
Impact: Transaction creation requests experienced duplicate model outputs (duplicate intents leading to double-charges in downstream processing) and elevated latency/timeouts across the us-east region. Customer reported immediate business impact (failed settlements).
Environment: Production (us-east) serving via Hosted API for enterprise tenant using model redwood-ggml-13B pinned version v2026-02-25. Customer on enterprise plan with dedicated routing policy.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a stream-based chat request with small initial prompt and repeated 'confirm' function call; 2) Observe two or more streamed final responses within 1s window for same request id; 3) Repeat under sustained concurrent load (~120 rps) and observe API gateway returning 429s or 502s.
Observed behavior: Streaming connection returned duplicate final chunks for ~12% of streams; API gateway returned 429s with message 'rate-limited' while backend showed no corresponding throttling in dedicated pool metrics.
Initial notes: Customer escalated to CS at 02:20 UTC. Triage opened and declared Sev1 due to financial impact. Temporary mitigation requested and SLA credit asked for.

Additional notes:
Timeline and evidence: At 01:58 UTC an infra routing config (PR 1045) introduced a new streaming multiplexer path intended to reduce cold-starts. At 02:03 UTC stream_ack_rate doubled and stream session state reconciliation lagged. Traces (trace ids: 7a1b3c, 7a1b4d) show api-gateway re-sending stream init frames when backend did not immediately ACK due to a lock contention in the multiplexer: this resulted in duplicate final chunks being emitted when the delayed original ACK arrived. Concurrently, a defensive token-bucket rate limiter in api-gateway had a regression that treated these duplicate frames as new requests and incremented counters, causing the gateway to return 429s even though dedicated pool metrics were below thresholds. Key logs: /logs/stream-multiplexer/2026-03-10.log lines 1124-1168; apigw metrics spike at 02:04. Root cause: a combination of (1) a non-idempotent stream init handshake in the multiplexer introduced by config change, and (2) a rate-limiter edge-case that double-counted retries. Evidence: reproducible with provided request ids when replayed in a staging environment with the problematic multiplexer enabled.
Immediate fixes applied: 1) Rolled back the multiplexer path (infra PR revert) at 02:45 UTC which stopped new duplicates; 2) Disabled the new token-bucket defensive code path causing double-counts at 03:00 UTC; 3) Temporarily routed Axiom Payments traffic to us-west cluster for the remainder of the window; 4) Increased dedicated pool headroom by +20% for Axiom until full fix is deployed. Permanent remediation: 1) Code fix PR #2387 removed the non-idempotent handshake and adds idempotency tokens for stream inits; 2) Rate limiter fix added de-duplication check for retry frames and a test harness; 3) Add a canary rollout guard for infra routing changes and telemetry alerts for stream_ack anomalies. Follow-ups and customer remediation: Postmortem meeting scheduled 2026-03-15; agreed SLA credit of one week of enterprise plan; instrumentation dashboard created (link below) and alerts added.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that users in their private deployment cannot complete SSO login. Requests to our auth proxy return 403 Authorization Denied.
Impact: All Aurelia Finance users in the eu-west private deployment are unable to sign in via SSO (affects web console and API token exchange for automation).
Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) running auth-proxy v1.8.1, auth-service v3.2.0. IdP: corporate SAML IdP configured to sign assertions with RSA-PSS (RSASSA-PSS with SHA256).
Observed behaviour: SAML assertion accepted by IdP and delivered to our endpoint, but auth-proxy logs show signature validation failure and downstream RBAC mapping is not performed, resulting in 403.
Expected behaviour: Our SAML verifier should validate IdP-signed assertions and proceed to role mapping; if algorithm unsupported, we should surface clear diagnostic and provide a compatibility path.
1) Configure a SAML IdP to sign assertions using RSA-PSS (RSASSA-PSS/SHA256).
2) Direct assertion consumer URL to private auth-proxy endpoint for the customer's control plane in eu-west.
3) Attempt SSO login from the Aurelia Finance console.
4) Observe 403 response and check auth-proxy logs for signature verification errors.
2026-03-01T09:14:22Z auth-proxy ERROR validate_saml_signature: signature verification failed: unsupported signature algorithm: rsa-pss
2026-03-01T09:14:22Z auth-proxy INFO inbound_assertion: saml_assertion_id=4b9f-... user=alice@aurelia.test status=REJECTED
customer-provided: Assertion: <Signature> Algorithm='http://www.w3.org/2007/05/xmldsig-more#rsa-pss'
IdP debug: Assertion issued at 2026-03-01T09:14:20Z; Verified by IdP logs as signed with RSASSA-PSS-SHA256
Initial triage: Support reproduced locally by generating assertions signed with RSA-PSS; our current saml verifier (xmlsec/java-saml wrapper) rejects rsa-pss algorithm tokens leading to signature verification failure.
Hypothesis: Underlying XML signature library does not advertise RSA-PSS support; auth-proxy treats the assertion as unauthenticated and returns 403 before RBAC mapping.
Corroborating evidence: Stack trace from auth-proxy points to xmlsec error path 'unsupported signature algorithm' and a unit test added locally fails on PSS-signed assertion.
Customer workaround tested: Aurelia Finance reconfigured IdP to sign with RSA-SHA256 (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5) and SSO resumed immediately—confirms algorithm incompatibility.
Related internal notes: This surfaced because a subset of enterprise IdPs have moved to RSA-PSS by default. Not previously present in other support tickets.
Workaround: Customer temporarily switched IdP signing algorithm to RSA-SHA256 (PKCS#1 v1.5) which restored SSO within minutes.
Short-term fix: Backported a permissive verification shim into auth-proxy to recognize RSA-PSS algorithm OIDs and route to updated xmlsec bindings. Deployed patch to customer's private control plane as auth-proxy v1.8.2-pss-fix (hotfix).
Long-term plan: Upgrade saml/xmlsec dependency across private control plane images to a release that fully supports RSASSA-PSS and add automated tests for rsa-pss assertions. Corresponding GH PR created (see related_github_prs).
Customer communication: Advised Aurelia Finance of the fix and recommended an IdP transition plan once the dependency upgrade is in stable release (target: v1.9.0).

Additional notes:
2026-03-02 08:17 - Customer (Aurelia SRE): We've temporarily switched our IdP to RSA-SHA256 and confirm logins work. We need a permanent solution as PSS is our policy.
2026-03-03 15:00 - Aurelia SRE: Confirmed SSO restored across their user population. Asked for timeline for full dependency upgrade in stable releases.
2026-03-04 09:20 - Support (Leah Park): Notified customer of planned release v1.9.0 target for full support; added to release notes and follow-up ticket if needed.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Analytics) reports intermittent streaming failures when using SSE to our hosted API from behind their CDN/edge proxy. Symptoms include duplicated metadata/control frames (e.g. ":meta" events) emitted at the beginning of the resumed segment, followed by a long silent tail (no final "[DONE]"-style event) even though the server logs show the request completed. There is no explicit 5xx/4xx returned to the client. Impact: ~8-12% of long-lived streaming sessions terminate without client-observed completion and exhibit repeated metadata frames; customer reports user-visible partial outputs and occasional UI hangs.

Impact:
- End-users see repeated prompt/metadata fragments and missing finalization (incomplete assistant messages)
- Affects production traffic for Acme Analytics dedicated cluster in us-west-2
- Customer reports spike after a recent CDN configuration change (enabled prefetch / HTTP/2 connection reuse)

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (dedicated cluster for Acme Analytics)
- Region: us-west-2
- Client path: browser -> CloudFront (custom origin) -> customer's edge proxy -> Redwood api-gateway -> serving-runtime
- Model: redwood-rlhf-small-v1

Steps to reproduce (reported):
1) Client opens SSE stream for a long-form generation (~30s+).
2) Client experiences transient network blip or local backoff (short sleep ~200-800ms) and reconnects with resume headers.
3) On reconnect, client receives a burst of small control/metadata SSE events that appear duplicated compared to the prior segment, then silence (no terminal event).

Observed behavior:
- Duplicated "meta" events (same sequence id) arrive immediately after reconnect.
- Server side logs show the original request completed successfully (full token count and no runtime error).
- No 5xx observed at api-gateway; HTTP connection between CF and origin shows normal 200s.
- Client never receives terminal event marking completion; user perceives partial output.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should not replay metadata that was already delivered, and the final terminal event should be delivered once server completes.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Disable CDN prefetch/early hints and disable HTTP/2 connection pooling between CloudFront and the customer's edge (reduce connection reuse)
- Enable websocket fallback for long-lived sessions for now
- Add jitter to client reconnect backoff to avoid tight reconnect loops

Notes: request IDs and sample trace IDs provided separately to ENG in investigation notes for privacy and trace correlation.
2026-03-12 09:14 - Customer (J. Rivera, Acme): We're seeing repeated "meta" events on reconnect and then the stream never finishes. This started after we flipped a CDN setting last week.
2026-03-12 09:38 - Support (Maya Patel): Acknowledged. Captured request IDs and asked for a full HAR and exact timestamps. Suggested temporary WS fallback and disabling CDN prefetch as quick mitigation.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Eng (Ethan Chen): Reproduced a similar failure in an internal staging harness when HTTP/2 connection reuse + server-side keepalive race occurs. Linked a tentative PR to add extra session markers on resume: see PR 843.
2026-03-13 08:22 - Customer (J. Rivera): After disabling prefetch, the issue frequency dropped dramatically. Still want root cause analysis and a permanent fix.
2026-03-13 12:00 - Eng (Ethan Chen): Implemented additional logging behind a feature flag and scheduled a targeted load test to exercise short backoff reconnects.
Hypothesis A: CDN/edge prefetch or HTTP/2 stream multiplexing causes a partial replay of buffered control frames during connection swap, resulting in duplicated metadata events on client reconnect.
Hypothesis B: api-gateway's resume path does not sufficiently dedupe control-frame IDs when a connection is torn down and re-established within short intervals; race with keepalive probes leads to a ghosted 'replay' slice.
Reproduction: Built a harness that simulates CloudFront + custom edge with connection reset after small pause; observed duplicated ":meta" frames and missing terminal event ~40% of runs under identical timing window.
Logs examined: edge-proxy access logs (trace ids: trace-prod-wnz-1425, trace-prod-wnz-1428) show two handoffs within 600ms; serving-runtime shows single inference completion for each trace id.
Dashboards referenced: streaming-tail-errors (SLO), api-gateway-conn-reuse, edge-proxy-pipeline-metrics. No increases in 5xx or CPU spikes were observed.
Mitigation test: Disabling connection reuse on the edge eliminated duplicates in the harness; suggests problem is in connection handoff + rebuffer logic between edge and api-gateway.
Next steps: add more structured resume markers to SSE frames, instrument idempotency checks in api-gateway, reproduce with customer's exact CDN settings, and evaluate PR 843 in canary.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/843 (adds stronger session markers and server-side dedupe).
Workaround applied: Customer disabled CDN prefetch and reduced HTTP/2 connection reuse. Incidence rate dropped to near zero for their traffic. Engineering deployed additional logging under feature flag and linked PR 843 to be tested in canary. Next steps: run extended load test against the canary change, add a small server-side dedupe window for control frames, and coordinate a rolling canary to Acme's dedicated cluster once validated.
Complete canary test for PR 843 (edge-proxy) against simulated CloudFront handoff pattern
If canary passes, schedule non-peak rolling deploy to Acme Analytics dedicated cluster with opt-in flag
Add permanent dashboards for resume-replay-rate and a one-minute alert if rate > 0.5%

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports duplicate POSTs to their external webhook after using the SDK offline/local-plugin mode. Symptom: while their app is offline (edge network outage), the SDK's local plugin accepts and executes tool calls locally. When network connectivity is restored, the SDK replays the queued tool calls to the Redwood control plane which in turn re-dispatches the webhook, causing duplicated external side effects (e.g., doubled order notifications).

Impact:
- Duplicate external side effects reported by customer (financial/notification duplication).
- Reproducible for long-running sessions that used local-plugin offline execution.

Expected behavior:
- If the SDK or local plugin executes a tool that has irreversible side effects, the execution should be marked/confirmed so the control plane does not re-run the tool post-reconnect. The idempotency/confirmation handshake should prevent duplicates regardless of offline execution path.

Actual behavior:
- Local plugin execution does not consistently persist the confirmation token/metadata into the SDK queue item. On reconnect, the control plane sees no confirmation and re-executes the tool, leading to duplicates.

Notes: customer is using Go SDK v1.8.2 with the optional local-plugin extension. They also have a TypeScript microservice that receives the webhook posts. The customer indicated the local plugin was developed in-house to forward tool calls to an on-prem subsystem when the device was offline.
1) Configure Go SDK v1.8.2 with local-plugin enabled. local-plugin accepts tool invocations and returns success without calling Redwood confirm endpoint.
2) Simulate offline network (block outbound to api.redwood.ai) and invoke a tool that triggers an external webhook (e.g., POST /orders).
3) Confirm local-plugin returns success and the SDK enqueues the tool call as 'locally-executed' in the offline queue.
4) Restore network connectivity. Observe SDK reconnect flow and replay of queued entries to the control plane.
5) Verify duplicate POSTs on customer webhook receiver and two separate tool-execution records in the control plane / logs (one local, one replayed).
2026-03-09T18:12:01Z [go-sdk] toolcall queued (offline) id=abc123 local_exec=true
2026-03-09T18:12:01Z [local-plugin] tool-run success, response_code=200, confirmation_token= (none)
2026-03-09T18:30:05Z [go-sdk] network restored, attempting reconnect to api.redwood.ai
2026-03-09T18:30:05Z [go-sdk] replaying queued toolcall id=abc123, idempotency_key= (absent)
2026-03-09T18:30:05Z [control-plane] webhook-dispatch POST /hooks/order-notify id=abc123-remote
2026-03-09T18:30:06Z [customer-webhook] received POST order-notify id=abc123-local
2026-03-09T18:30:06Z [customer-webhook] received POST order-notify id=abc123-remote
- Reproduced locally using provided repro harness and customer's local-plugin mock. Behavior matches customer reports.
- Root cause hypothesis: offline execution path does not attach/serialize the confirmation token or idempotency metadata into the SDK's persisted offline queue item. On reconnect the control plane treats the replay as a fresh invocation.
- Observed inconsistent presence of idempotency header in replayed requests; local executions sometimes include no idempotency key header because the local-plugin response path didn't propagate it back to the SDK persistence layer.
- Edge case: when the local-plugin returns a confirmation URL or token, the SDK still failed to persist that token for items created prior to v1.9.0 (regression introduced in v1.8.0 local-queue refactor).
- Querying webhook logs shows two distinct deliveries with different Redwood dispatch IDs; neither is suppressed by control-plane idempotency checks because the second request lacks the confirmation metadata expected by the dispatcher.

Additional notes:
Workaround: Instructed customer to do one of the following until patch is released:
- Disable local-plugin offline execution for tool calls that produce irreversible side effects (set allowLocalExecution=false for those actions).
- Modify local-plugin to call Redwood's confirm endpoint immediately after local execution (confirm URL + token) so control plane sees execution and suppresses replay.
Short-term fix implemented: Engineering produced a patch (PR linked above) that ensures confirmation_token is persisted alongside the offline queue item and that replay attaches idempotency/confirmation metadata for dispatch. Patch targeted for SDK rollouts: Go v1.9.0, TS v2.4.1.
Follow-ups: INT-92214 tracks audits and a test matrix to cover offline-plugin handshake, plus docs update in SDK offline-mode guide to call out explicit confirm behavior and recommended patterns for irreversible side effects.
BrightCart experienced duplicate external notifications during an outage window. Issue affects local-plugin offline execution without confirm calls and can lead to duplicated irreversible side effects.
1) Engineering to merge PR and schedule SDK patch releases (Go v1.9.0, TS v2.4.1).
2) CS to coordinate a migration window with BrightCart for SDK upgrade and to validate no further duplicates in a canary session.
3) Docs update to offline-mode best practices and explicit examples for confirm endpoint use.
4) Postmortem/lessons learned to be linked to the incident report if duplicates led to material customer loss.
payload.summary: local-plugin offline-queue replay duplicates external webhook posts on reconnect

Issue summary: During a staged (tiered) canary rollout for redwood-open-gpt-3.5-v1, a subset of tenant sessions that were previously pinned to the promoted variant unexpectedly reverted to the default fallback variant. Impact: customer-visible mixed-model responses for ~3% of requests from Meridian Analytics' production traffic in us-east; increased latency for affected requests due to additional routing and KV cache misses. Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:10 UTC - deploy start for tiered canary; 09:22 UTC - first customer report; 09:30-10:00 UTC - increased 5xxs and quality complaints; 10:15 UTC - Support triage. Observed behavior: some sessions lost model affinity and were routed to a fallback variant; this coincided with sidecar snapshot refresh events on a subset of edge pods. Expected behavior: pin affinity should persist across sidecar snapshot refreshes and control-plane rollouts until explicit unpin or pin TTL expiry. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create tiered canary rollout with staged weights and pin variant for a test tenant; 2) Trigger sidecar config refresh (simulated by restarting sidecar or pushing a SIGHUP); 3) Send session traffic with pinned token and observe routing; 4) Reproduce by toggling edge header rewrite feature flag. Logs & artifacts: edge-proxy logs show header rewrite events at same timestamps as routing flips; sidecar snapshot logs show a full snapshot replace (snapshot_id changed) and an applied config hash mismatch with control-plane; KV cache miss logs for pinned sessions; sample request IDs: rq-0a1f23, rq-0a1f98, rq-0b2c11. Attachments: packet captures and a short trace are in the ticket attachments (internal).
Initial hypothesis: sidecar snapshot replace caused pin metadata to be dropped locally on edge pods that applied new snapshot before pin reconciliation completed.
Correlated timing between snapshot replace and a partial control-plane propagation delay (10-14s window) in us-east region.
Found header rewrite rule that migrates legacy session-cookie to new token format; during rewrite the pin-token field was being stripped by an older sidecar build on ~7% of pods.
Reproduced in the staging cluster by applying an older sidecar image plus the header rewrite: pinned token removed on snapshot apply and route fallback triggered.
Checked rollout orchestration logs: canary weight adjust and snapshot distribution overlapped; reconciliation controller did not retry pin sync fast enough when snapshot applied mid-window.
No evidence of model-serving node eviction or GPU preemption; serving runtime healthy for promoted variant.

Additional notes:
Marcus Liu (SRE) (2026-03-10 11:20): Confirmed sidecar binary mismatch on ~6 out of 90 edge pods in us-east; those pods show snapshot replace events exactly at 09:18-09:24 UTC.
Elena Park (Control Plane) (2026-03-11 08:50): Found a timing edge in the pin-reconciliation backoff; filing PR to add a forced sync when snapshot ID increments during an active pin window.
A race between sidecar snapshot replacement and control-plane pin-reconciliation caused pin metadata to be stripped on edge pods running an older sidecar build that applied an incompatible header rewrite. The strip led to routing logic treating the session as unpinned, invoking fallback routing to a default variant.
Disabled the header rewrite flag for affected tenant during the canary window and ran a targeted pin-resync job against edge pods in us-east. This restored session affinity for affected tenants within ~30 minutes.
Short term: keep header rewrite disabled for Meridian until sidecar patch is deployed. Medium term: merge sidecar PR to preserve pin-token across rewrite and add a forced pin-sync when snapshot ID changes; add critical telemetry and an alert on pin-drop rates. Long term: adjust rollout orchestration to avoid snapshot distributions that can overlap with active pin windows or make reconciliation immediate on snapshot increment.
Customer is on a Dedicated contract; follow-up retrospective scheduled with product and infra teams to update the canary runbook and add explicit guidance about header rewrites during pin-sensitive rollouts.
payload.summary: Pinned session reverts during tiered canary: sidecar snapshot desync triggers fallback routing

Issue summary:
Customer requests a one-time, ordered audit export covering 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-28 with special formatting and cryptographic delivery proofs. They require: deterministic tenant pseudonymization (stable mapping across the export), timestamps normalized to Europe/Zurich timezone while preserving original UTC timestamps in metadata, per-batch HMAC-SHA256 checksums encrypted with a customer-provided wrapping key, and support for resumable delivery (opaque resume token per batch).

Impact:
CobaltBank uses the export to feed their forensic SIEM and eDiscovery pipeline. Delays or incorrect pseudonym mapping will block their compliance deadline and SOC2 evidence submission. This is an enterprise customer with legal review timelines.

Request details (high-level):
- Export range: 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z -> 2026-02-28T23:59:59Z (all tenants under org: cobaltbank-prod)
- Output format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with one top-level event per line
- Per-event fields required: event_id (UUID v4), tenant_pseudonym (deterministic), original_timestamp_utc, localized_timestamp_zurich, event_type, resource, raw_payload (redaction applied per rules in attachment)
- Deterministic tenant mapping: HMAC-SHA256 using customer-provided salt (they will provide base64 salt), output as 64-char hex digest prefixed with TID-
- Resume semantics: each file/batch must include a resume_token (opaque string) and resume_token must allow export to continue from last successfully ingested offset without overlap or skip
- Integrity: per-batch encrypted_manifest.json containing: batch_id, start_utc, end_utc, count, hmac_sha256_of_plaintext (hex) then encrypt the manifest with the customer's RSA-OAEP public key; also include a detached JWS (RS256) signed by Redwood release pipeline key to assert generation time
- Delivery: pre-signed GCS signed URLs to a customer bucket; prefer 2GB chunked files with index; optional SFTP fallback

Environment / notes:
Customer runs SIEM in eu-central and expects local timestamps in Europe/Zurich for correlation with on-prem systems. They require signed artifacts for legal chain-of-custody. This is not a repeating export; one-time bulk export only.

Attached to ticket: customer redaction matrix (attachment: cobalt_redaction_matrix_v3.csv) and HMAC salt placeholder (cobalt_salt_base64.txt).
Customer explicitly asked for: (A) stable pseudonymization across export so their correlation tables (tenant->internal id) remain valid, (B) localized timestamps in Europe/Zurich in ISO8601 without losing original UTC value (original_timestamp_utc field), (C) per-batch encrypted manifest using their RSA public key, (D) resume_token semantics to allow client to re-request incomplete batches, and (E) HMAC-SHA256 checksums of plaintext event arrays included in manifest and then encrypted. They also requested signed JWS generated by Redwood pipeline that ties manifest to a release tag.
1) Customer uploads request and attachments via support portal; includes redaction matrix and salt
2) Support confirms scope and generates export job request to export pipeline
3) Export pipeline should create ordered batches, generate deterministic tenant pseudonyms, produce per-batch manifest and encrypted checksum, and upload to customer-provided GCS signed URLs
4) Customer attempts to resume transfer by hitting the resume_token endpoint with last token; service must return next batch starting at correct offset

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403s from admin/impersonation and tenant-scoped admin console calls after an ingress-side 'claim whitelist' was enabled in their private deployment. Requests originate from the customer's edge proxy -> Redwood private control plane.

Impact:
- FormaHealth admin users and service accounts unable to perform tenant-scoped admin operations (403).
- Affects multiple teams; blocks immediate admin workflows and onboarding of new service accounts.
- Occurs intermittently when requests route through an updated backend claim filter.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) behind customer's ingress proxy.
- Region: prod us-east.
- Affected endpoints: POST /v1/admin/impersonate, GET /console/tenant/{tenant_id}/roles

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Create tenant service account and bind tenant-admin role via console/SCIM.
2) From their edge, send impersonation request: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <service-jwt>" -H "X-Forwarded-User-Claims: {\"rdw:tenant_bindings\":[\"tenant-123:admin\"]}" https://private.redwood-cp.example.com/v1/admin/impersonate
3) Observe 403. Same token via direct control-plane pod (bypassing ingress) succeeds.

Observed logs / artifacts (customer-provided):
- edge-proxy logs show: "claim-whitelist: dropped claim 'rdw:tenant_bindings' (not in allowlist) for request id=7a3f..."
- control plane audit-log: "authorization denied - no tenant_binding found" request_id=7a3f..., subject=service-account:forma-admin
- sample JWT (redacted) contains namespaced claim: "rdw:tenant_bindings": ["tenant-123:admin"]

Notes: The customer recently enabled a custom claim whitelist on their ingress (third-party WAF) to reduce header injection surface. After enabling, tenant-bound RBAC assertions are intermittently absent when requests pass through the modified path. When the customer re-routes traffic to bypass the claim whitelist, requests authenticate and authorize correctly.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 09:22 - Customer (FormaHealth): Provided WAF config snippet that enables claim whitelist: allow: ['sub','email','rdw:user_id'] (note: rdw:tenant_bindings missing). Customer says they intentionally tightened the allowlist yesterday.
2026-03-14 12:05 - Engineering: PR opened to add defensive logging and clearer audit message when namespaced tenant claims are absent: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4889
Hypothesis: Ingress-level claim whitelist/filtering removes 'rdw:tenant_bindings' and other namespaced claims required by RBAC evaluation, causing downstream control-plane to see an incomplete subject assertion.
Confirmed by reproducer: local proxy filter that removes namespaced claims reproduces 403 consistently; direct bypass or allowlist change allows success.
Observed that some customers namespace tenant bindings under 'rdw:' prefix; our control-plane RBAC matcher accepts both 'tenant_bindings' and 'rdw:tenant_bindings' but only when present in incoming token or header. If the header is removed, no fallback exists and authorization fails.
Edge case: Claims were present in the JWT; however the customer's WAF removes header-representations of them when proxying. Control-plane treats header-provided claims as authoritative when X-Forwarded-User-Claims present.
Workaround applied: customer updated the ingress/WAF allowlist to include the 'rdw:tenant_bindings' claim and confirmed admin workflows restored. Engineering patch in progress to improve audit messages and to add a defensive fallback log recommending claim whitelist updates for private deployments. No code-level RBAC change deployed yet.
ENG: Merge PR that emits clearer audit messages and guidance when tenant-binding claims are absent (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4889).
DOCS: Update Private Deployment runbook to include guidance on common claim names that must be preserved by ingress/WAF ('rdw:tenant_bindings','rdw:service_roles','tenant_bindings').
SE: Reach out to customers currently on private to recommend a quick checklist before enabling claim-whitelists on their ingress (due 2026-03-20).
OPS: Add an alert that correlates control-plane 'authorization denied - no tenant_binding' messages with recent ingress config changes for faster triage.
payload.summary: Tenant bindings stripped after backend claim whitelist filter causes 403s in private deployment

Issue summary: Nordic Bank is onboarding Redwood audit exports via our webhook bridge. They require an incremental delivery manifest that proves at-least-once delivery with per-batch signed ACKs and replay tokens, plus security questionnaire evidence (SAML assertions, KMS/HSM attestation sample, and retention policy). Impact: They cannot complete security review for escrow and incident response automation without cryptographic delivery proofs and sample resume tokens. Environment: prod-us-east; customer uses an on-prem SIEM behind a corporate firewall with an ingestion webhook that validates signed manifests. Request: 1) Provide a sample signed ACK manifest format for incremental webhook batches (including timestamp, batch_id, resume_token, hmac signature, signer_cert_fingerprint). 2) Deliver a 48-hour sample bundle (NDJSON) with two consecutive batches showing resume tokens and signed ACKs. 3) Provide redacted SAML assertion examples and the audit-exporter key attestation statement for their compliance pack. 4) Answer security questionnaire sections 3.1 (key management) and 4.2 (replay/resume guarantees).
1) Customer configured inbound webhook with mutual TLS and expects per-batch ACK header 'X-Redwood-ACK' containing signed manifest. 2) Send two test payloads (batch A then batch B) via the platform with resume tokens generated. 3) Observe that customer received two payloads but their SIEM reported duplicated event IDs when webhook retried. 4) Confirm whether the platform provided resume_token rotation and manifest for each batch and whether ACK signature verification would have prevented duplicate acceptance. 5) Reproduce by replaying batch A with previous resume_token and check consumer acceptance behavior.
Onboarding blocked for enterprise compliance review; inability to provide signed delivery evidence prevents SOC and IR teams from closing contractual controls. Potential risk to incident reconstruction if replay tokens are ambiguous. Customer reports small delta in event counts between our delivery logs and their SIEM (2-3 events per day) which they attribute to retries/duplicates.
Initial triage (2025-02-12): Audit-exporter is emitting per-batch resume_token and a detached JWS manifest. Webhook-proxy logs show successful mtls and ACK header verification for the sample window. Customer-provided SIEM logs show duplicate event ids after a retry window; hypothesis: consumer side replay handling accepts replays when resume_token not advanced or when dedupe keys differ. Checked signing key rotation: rotation window aligned with our documented 24h rotation; no gap found. Noted a mismatch: customer's ingestion pipeline de-duplicates based on 'event_uuid' while our retry may reingest with the same event_uuid but different envelope_id; recommend mapping guidance. Security evidence: can produce a signed manifest (JWS) example using current audit-exporter key, and produce an HSM attestation excerpt from our HSM provider (redacted).

Additional notes:
2025-02-13 08:20 - Nordic Bank SOC (Customer): Provided SIEM ingestion log excerpt showing duplicate event_uuid when retry occurred and asked whether our ACK manifests include both batch_id and envelope_id to allow deterministic dedupe.
2025-02-15 16:30 - Security (Elena Ruiz): Confirmed we can provide: (1) signed manifest JWS example with signer_cert_fingerprint, (2) HSM attestation excerpt from vendor (redacted), (3) redacted SAML assertion example. Drafted answers for questionnaire sections attached to this ticket.
2025-02-17 14:10 - Nordic Bank SOC (Customer): Confirmed manifest signature verified and that after switching dedupe key to event_uuid+envelope_id the duplicate counts resolved in test window. Asked for final evidence bundle for audit and signed statement for contractual appendix.
Workaround provided: guidance to dedupe on event_uuid+envelope_id and immediate sample bundle delivered. Final deliverables to include: (a) NDJSON 48-hour incremental sample with per-batch JWS manifests, (b) signed attestation excerpt from HSM vendor, (c) redacted SAML assertion samples, (d) filled security questionnaire sections 3.1 and 4.2. Delivery ETA 2025-02-18. Ticket remains open until customer confirms receipt and legal signs the appendix.
We supplied a signed manifest format and short-term workaround. Root cause: customer dedupe logic did not include envelope_id leading to duplicate acceptance on retry. Recommended dedupe change and provided signed proofs for compliance. Pending final signed evidence bundle and legal appendix.
Nordic Bank SOC confirmed verification of manifest signatures and successful test after dedupe change on 2025-02-17. Requested final signed packet for procurement appendix.

Issue summary: BrightLedger reported repeated windows of reduced batched throughput (p50 throughput drop ~30%, p95 latency increase 3x) on their dedicated pool in us-west-2 starting 2026-03-11T23:00Z. Impact: customer-facing inference endpoints saw elevated tail latency and reduced tokens/sec for multi-request batched routes. Scope: affects ~3 GPU nodes in BrightLedger's reserved pool, intermittent (2–10 minute windows) and correlated with transient ephemeral jobs scheduled in the same cluster. Timeline: 2026-03-11 23:01 – first alert from synthetic checks; 23:03 — customer report; 23:10 — support triage; 23:35 — mitigation throttle applied; 2026-03-12 — engineering investigation ongoing.
1) Deploy a dedicated pool with reserved GPUs (BrightLedger config).
2) Launch steady inference traffic using batched routes (batch target 8, max latency 250ms).
3) Submit short-lived ephemeral training/instrumentation jobs that create heavy CPU+IO on nodes concurrently (simulated background job in test harness).
4) Observe autoscaler and scheduler logs during bursts; monitor p95 latency and tokens/sec for the serving runtime.
- Short, repeated windows (2-10m) where token throughput drops ~25-35% and p95 latency rises from ~140ms to ~420ms for batched endpoints.
- GPU allocations show no OOMs, but scheduling logs contain preemption/eviction events for low-priority ephemeral pods (kube-scheduler).
- Node-level metrics show CPU steal and iowait spikes during windows; NVLink and GPU memory stable.
- Autoscaler response lags: new pods created but batching doesn't recover immediately due to KV cache warming and batch serialization.
Dedicated pool should preserve batched throughput for reserved tenants. Background ephemeral jobs on best-effort tenants should not induce intermittent p99/p95 regressions for reserved capacity customers.
kubelet evict events (2026-03-11T23:02:14Z): preempted pod ephemeral-ia-224 - reason: "Preemption by higher-priority burst"
serving-runtime trace (2026-03-11T23:02:18Z): batch_worker stall detected: wait_for_batch() duration 340ms (normal 40-60ms)
node metrics snippet (iowait): node-az3-004 iowait jump 0.4 -> 3.7 (23:02-23:05)
autoscaler log: scale_up triggered but new pods returned NotReady for 45s due to sidecar init and kv-cache restore
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-12T00:10Z: Acknowledged receipt from customer. Reproduced transient drop in staging by running bursty ephemeral jobs. Escalating to SRE for scheduler/autoscaler correlation.
SRE (Luis Ortega) 2026-03-12T01:05Z: Observed preemption chains in kube-scheduler; ephemeral jobs are not constrained and spike node CPU/IO. Scheduling preemption causes pod restarts on reserved nodes and disrupts surviving batchers.
Customer (BrightLedger - Alex Cho) 2026-03-12T01:30Z: We observed production errors during scheduled batch windows; requesting mitigation and ETA for fix. Impacting customer SLAs.
Infra (SRE) 2026-03-12T03:20Z: Temporary mitigation applied: added taint on dedicated nodes to repel best-effort ephemeral scheduling and set eviction thresholds; monitoring for recurrence.
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-12T04:00Z: Customer notified of temporary mitigation; asked to validate if throughput stabilizes during their peak window tonight.
Hypothesis A: noisy best-effort ephemeral jobs consume CPU/io bandwidth causing kubelet/cgroup contention and triggering preemptions that serialize batched requests.
Hypothesis B: autoscaler cooldown and kv-cache restore time combine to create a recovery hole; new nodes join but batchers are cold, lowering effective throughput.
Finding: Eviction logs match timing of throughput drops. Node iowait and CPU steal correlate with eviction windows. No GPU memory contention or thermal events found.
Supporting artifacts: correlated grafana dashboard panels (requests/sec, tokens/sec, node iowait, kube-scheduler preemption_rate) show tight coupling of events.
Attempted reproducer in staging: reproduced by running 10s ephemeral CPU+disk IO spikes; same pattern of eviction -> batch stall -> autoscaler lag observed.
Short-term mitigation verified in canary: tainting dedicated nodes prevented ephemeral pods from scheduling and removed the 10m windows in canary traffic.
Long-term options considered: (1) enforce node-level QoS/CPU and IO limits for best-effort tenants; (2) introduce preemption-aware placement (reserved instance isolation); (3) tune autoscaler to pre-warm nodes or reduce kv-cache restore time via checkpoint sharing.
Workaround applied (2026-03-12): added a dedicated-node taint + updated scheduler tolerations for BrightLedger's pool to prevent best-effort ephemeral jobs from landing on reserved GPUs. This eliminated recurrence in canary. Next steps: SRE and Scheduler team to implement a policy change: set soft-affinity for reserved pools, enforce CPU/iowait quotas on sidecars, and reduce kv-cache warm time by sharing checkpoints across pod starts. Follow-up action items created: GH issue infra#2246 for autoscaler prewarm, runbook update to prevent ephemeral job escalation. Target date for permanent mitigation: 2026-03-19.
INFRA-2246: autoscaler prewarm feature backlog entry (owner: Priya Nair)
SCHED-112: implement reserved-pool soft-affinity + taint automation (owner: Daniel Kim)
RUNTIME-89: investigate kv-cache checkpoint sharing to speed restore (owner: Marta Silva)
CS-Note: notify BrightLedger when permanent mitigation is live and offer a post-mortem call

Issue summary:
Customer (OmniScribe, Dedicated) turned on an aggressive optimizer profile (quantized model + KV-prefetch + increased async batching) for low-cost inference during business hours. Shortly after rollout they reported increasing 95/99th tail latency and intermittent streaming disconnects for a subset of keys.

Impact:
Persistent elevated tail latency (95p ~600ms -> 1300ms; 99p spikes >2s) and 0.2% increase in streaming disconnect rates affecting a production tenant with critical SLA. Traffic is steady; packet loss or infra-wide events not observed.

Environment and context:
- Dedicated pool (tier: reserved) in us-east-1.
- Model variants: redwood-7b-v2 (baseline) and a quantized 8-bit LLM build.
- Optimizer profile enabled: kv-prefetch=true, async_batching=aggressive, quant_profile=8-bit-mixed, prefetch_window=64.
- Rollout was tenant-scoped via config snapshot applied 2026-03-09 09:12 UTC.

Customer asks:
1) Provide a safe step-by-step 'quiet-window' procedure to pause optimizer features for this tenant with minimal disruption, including how to hedge traffic and reduce burstiness.
2) If rollback is required, provide the minimal safe rollback commands and any preflight checks to avoid cache inconsistencies.
3) Confirm what telemetry to capture during the quiet-window so we can validate rollback success and regressions.
1) Apply tenant optimizer profile: kv-prefetch=enabled, async_batching=aggressive, quant_profile=8bit-mixed via snapshot (console or API)
2) Run normal production traffic for 30-60 minutes (OmniScribe steady traffic pattern)
3) Observe 95/99p latency increase and occasional streaming connection resets for some request IDs
4) Reproduce: toggle only kv-prefetch off while keeping quantization to isolate impact
Telemetry review shows concurrent increased KV fetch latency correlated with p99 spikes; host-level memory pressure peaks on serving nodes assigned to tenant.
No infra-wide network anomalies; error logs show backpressure and occasional 'cache-evict' warnings at 09:20-09:30 UTC.
A/B isolation: when kv-prefetch=false in a short test for the same tenant, 95/99p latency returned near baseline within 3 minutes; async_batching still enabled but not enough to trigger spike in isolation test.
Quantization alone did not reproduce the full spike in lab tests; suspect incompatible interaction between large prefetch window and quantized KV cache memory layout on this GPU family.
A) Preflight checks (10 mins): verify snapshot ID, capture baseline p50/p95/p99, and note time ranges. Ensure a maintenance window with customer consent.
B) Quiet-window (hedged pause): create a tenant traffic split of 80/20 to a fallback non-optimized model variant to validate behavior before full change. Use the console traffic-split API: POST /v1/tenants/OmniScribe/traffic-split {primary: optimized, weight:80, fallback:baseline, weight:20}
C) Step 1 - disable kv-prefetch for tenant: apply config toggle kv-prefetch=false for tenant snapshot (do not touch quantization yet). Monitor p95/p99 for 5 minutes.
D) If latency improves, gradually increase primary weight back to 100 over 5-minute steps, validating SLOs after each step. Keep async_batching unchanged initially.
E) If latency does not improve, revert traffic split immediately and schedule full rollback of optimizer snapshot (see Rollback commands).
F) Rollback commands (minimal safe): use snapshot restore to previous known-good snapshot: POST /v1/tenants/OmniScribe/snapshots/restore {snapshot_id: opt-snap-20260308-1800} then trigger a soft drain of in-flight async batches for 90s and re-warm cache.
G) Post-rollback verification: capture p50/p95/p99, streaming error rate, and compare token costs. Keep an 1-hour observation period and keep snapshot backup until confirmed stable.
H) Follow-up: open a performance investigation ticket to analyze kernel-level memory layout incompatibility for quant+prefetch on this GPU family. Consider a targeted hotfix or adjusting prefetch_window defaults for quant profiles.
1) Confirm snapshot IDs and timestamp (customer provided: opt-snap-20260309-0912)
2) Ensure backup snapshot (opt-snap-20260308-1800) available and verified
3) Capture current traffic split and obtain IHOT trace samples
4) Confirm maintenance window and rollback owner
5) Ensure on-call SRE reachable and console/CLI access works
6) Validate monitoring dashboards (latency, stream-errors, host-memory, evict-warnings) are visible and linked
# disable kv-prefetch for tenant via API
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/OmniScribe/config -d '{"kv_prefetch":false}'
# restore prior snapshot (soft rollback)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/OmniScribe/snapshots/restore -d '{"snapshot_id":"opt-snap-20260308-1800","mode":"soft"}'
# traffic split API example
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/OmniScribe/traffic-split -d '{"groups":[{"variant":"optimized","weight":80},{"variant":"baseline","weight":20}]}'
p50/p95/p99 latency per route and per model-variant (1m resolution)
streaming disconnects and reconnect counts by request-id
host-level GPU memory allocation and cache-eviction events
async-batch queue length and average batch sizes
KV fetch latency distribution (per prefix)
Priya Menon (Support) - 2026-03-09: Received raw traces and asked for exact snapshot ID and rollout timestamp. Customer confirmed snapshot=opt-snap-20260309-0912.
Customer (OmniScribe) - 2026-03-09: We need a mitigation path - rolling back immediately may affect cost goals but latency is customer-visible and impacting users.
Carlos Vega (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Hypothesis: KV-prefetch is increasing memory pressure on GPUs under this tenant's prefix distribution, causing cache thrash and increased kernel stalls. Suggest quiet-window + disable kv-prefetch for tenant, then verify latency before touching quantization.
Priya Menon (Support) - 2026-03-11: Sent step-by-step 'quiesce' playbook draft to customer for approval before runbook execution. Waiting for customer to confirm a 10-minute maintenance window.
Customer (OmniScribe) - 2026-03-11: Approved maintenance window 2026-03-12 02:00-02:20 UTC. Also requested guidance for partial traffic hedge rather than full cutover.
1) Wait for customer confirmation of the 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC maintenance window (customer confirmed above).
2) SRE to run quiet-window procedure during maintenance window and report captured telemetry within 30 minutes after completion.
3) If rollback occurs, request customer to maintain observation for at least 60 minutes and then sign off.
4) Create a follow-up technical investigation ticket (INT-?) to root-cause quant+prefetch interaction and propose a permanent mitigation.
5) If confirmed, schedule a patch or optimizer profile change to avoid this interaction for similar tenants.
Pending: mitigation steps drafted and customer-scheduled quiet-window. No final rollback executed yet. If executed, we'll update this ticket with rollback snapshot IDs and post-rollback metrics.
Open an internal investigation (INT ticket) for kernel-memory layout and prefetch interaction
Consider adding an automatic 'prefetch guardrail' for quantized profiles to prevent prefetch_window > 32 on affected GPU families
Update public runbook with a 'quiet-window traffic split' example

Issue summary: Over the 11:40–13:20 UTC window on 2026-03-12 NimbusSearch observed sustained p50/p95 throughput loss in their dedicated pool while aggregate cluster-level metrics looked nominal. Impact: customer production traffic experienced 20–40% reduction in successful inferences per GPU and elevated p99 latencies (3x). Observed failures were primarily timeouts and 429-like throttles from the dedicated pool facade.

Environment: dedicated pool hosted in us-east (tenant: nimbus-prod, reserved capacity).

Timeline / key events:
- 2026-03-12 11:38 UTC: Customer reports increased application-side queue lengths to Support.
- 2026-03-12 11:45 UTC: Support escalates to SRE after brief check; core metrics (GPU count, cluster CPU) appear within usual ranges.
- 2026-03-12 12:05 UTC: Observability shows handful of GPUs at sustained 95–100% utilization while the rest underutilized. Autoscaler did not trigger new allocations for ~25 minutes.
- 2026-03-12 12:20 UTC: SRE notices a connection fanout pattern from a small set of customer session IPs -> affinity mapped to GPUs 8–11, leaving others idle (GPU islanding).

Steps to reproduce (internal / best-effort):
1) Replay a production traffic trace that preserves client connection affinity (keepalives + pinned sockets) into a dedicated pool with identical scheduler affinity config.
2) Simulate long-lived multiplexed short streams from a single client ID (10k concurrent sockets with low per-req tokens).
3) Observe allocation and batcher placement; look for persistent slot reservations on NVLink islanded GPUs and autoscaler non-reactivity.

Observed behavior:
- Asymmetric connection distribution caused repeated placement on a small GPU subset.
- Batching engine experienced slot serialization (many tiny batches) on those GPUs, increasing per-token overhead.
- Autoscaler metrics (aggregate free_slots / average_utilization) were masked because the majority of GPUs were underutilized; autoscaler thresholds were not met.

Expected behavior:
- The scheduler should spread short-stream fanout across GPUs and the autoscaler should be sensitive to per-GPU skew (not only cluster aggregate).

Logs & dashboards (pointers):
- Grafana: /d/redwood/dedicated-pool-tenant?var-tenant=nimbus-prod&from=167/ -- panel "per-gpu-utilization" shows skew.
- Kibana traces: trace ids included in comments.
- Customer-provided app logs attached to ticket.

2026-03-12 11:51 - Support (Aisha Patel): Received initial report from NimbusSearch. Customer reports timeouts and increased tail latencies. Asked for application logs and sample request IDs.
2026-03-12 12:10 - SRE (Marco Nguyen): Quick triage shows per-GPU skew; opening deeper investigation. Noting GPUs 8-11 pinned at high utilization while others idle. Suspect socket affinity/scheduler placement interaction.
2026-03-12 12:28 - Customer (Elena Morales, NimbusSearch): We pushed a short-stream optimization in our SDK last night that uses persistent multiplexed connections. Happy to provide trace captures. We do see lots of very short requests (avg 8 tokens) from a few hosts.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 12:55 - SRE (Marco Nguyen): Temporary mitigation applied: forced soft-eviction of affinity cache for affected tenancy and applied per-gpu-skew alert to trigger immediate autoscale override. Asking customer to throttle persistent connections while we prepare a targeted fix.
2026-03-13 09:10 - Customer (Elena Morales): After the mitigation, throughput recovered to baseline. We plan to ship an SDK patch to round-robin new connections by default; coordinating timing with Redwood.
2026-03-13 11:00 - Support (Aisha Patel): Noted recovery. Scheduling longer postmortem and follow-up implementation items for scheduler changes to avoid future islanding.
Affinity analysis: Scheduler uses source-ip hash + port to prefer stable placement. Combination of persistent multiplexed sockets and small request sizes favored repeated reuse of same batcher slots.
Autoscaler blind-spot: global_utilization based autoscale rule masked per-GPU hot spots. Add per_gpu_skew_ratio metric to detect imbalance.
Batcher behavior: tiny-batch overhead dominates when many short requests hit same GPU; continuous batching window rarely filled, producing many micro-batches.
NVLink/NUMA mapping: GPUs 8-11 share NVLink island, scheduler affinity prioritized placement there due to historical locality preference which in this case amplified the problem.
Customer SDK change: persistent connection reuse + high concurrency produced concentrated fanout. Customer will patch to more balanced socket distribution.
Reproduction: Successful in internal staging when reproducing same connection-fanout characteristics; validated mitigation (evict affinity cache) resolves skew temporarily.
Mitigation applied: evicted affinity cache for tenant nimbus-prod and enabled emergency per-gpu-skew override which forced autoscaler to provision 2 extra GPUs in us-east. Customer throttled new persistent connections briefly and rolled back SDK change. Result: throughput returned to baseline and p99 dropped to normal levels.
Permanent fix plan: scheduler change to include bounded placement randomness for highly multiplexed short-streams; autoscaler enhancement to consider per_gpu_skew_ratio and trigger earlier. Both items scheduled on SRE roadmap.
Rollout notes: we will deploy a scheduler tweak (canary) to staging on 2026-03-18 and to prod on 2026-03-20 behind a tenant toggle. Autoscaler metric addition targeted for 2026-03-25.
Create a per-gpu skew alert: SRE ticket INT-9876 (owner: Marco Nguyen)
Scheduler change PR: runtime#4128 (owner: Priya Singh) — add bounded randomness when request length < 16 tokens and connection count > 1024
Autoscaler change PR: autoscaler#221 (owner: Ravi Patel) — include per-gpu_skew_ratio and override policy
Customer SDK guidance: update NimbusSearch SDK recommendations to avoid single-host socket fanout; doc snippet to be added to support KB
payload.summary: Socket affinity fanout causing regional GPU islanding and autoscale blind-spot

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several Soteria Health users in a private VPC deployment report sudden 403 Authorization failures when calling Redwood admin APIs. The errors began after an internal network appliance upgrade. Impact: A subset of service accounts and admin users are blocked from performing operations that are gated by IP-based conditional RBAC rules (e.g., allow-listing corporate IP ranges). Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) fronted by customer edge proxy + Redwood identity proxy in us-east-1. Steps to reproduce: 1) Call admin endpoint with a request proxied through the customer's upgraded edge appliance. 2) Observe 403 with error 'denied by ip_condition'. 3) Repeat from same client but bypassing edge appliance (direct to Redwood ingress) — request succeeds. Expected behavior: Requests forwarded through trusted proxies should evaluate the original client IP and allow access when within allow-list. Actual behavior: Requests forwarded via the customer's upgraded edge appliance are being evaluated with a spoofed/misattributed client IP (X-Forwarded-For appears to contain internal hop IPs first), causing the RBAC engine's IP condition check to fail. Logs/Traces: AuthN logs show valid JWT and tenant; authZ logs show evaluated ip_condition set to "203.0.113.245" (edge appliance) rather than the original client IP. Ingress proxy provenance trace: received X-Forwarded-For: "10.0.0.5, 203.0.113.245". Identity proxy received the same header without a trusted-hop validation. Customer reports appliance upgrade changelog included "preserve-source-ip=false" by default.
2026-03-13 09:12 - Customer (Soteria): 'All of our automation that runs from on-prem IPs is failing with 403s after our edge appliance update.'
2026-03-13 09:47 - Support (Elaine Park): 'Thanks — investigating. Can you share a request-id and a sample X-Forwarded-For header from a failing request?'
2026-03-13 10:05 - Customer (Soteria): 'Request-id: req-7f3a; X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.5, 203.0.113.245'
2026-03-13 13:20 - Engineering (Marco Ruiz): 'Reproduced in staging by inserting a proxy hop that prepends a private RFC1918 address before the public edge IP in XFF. RBAC engine currently trusts the left-most XFF element as source IP when header present.'
2026-03-14 08:21 - SRE (Ivy Chen): 'We applied a workaround to verify proxy-hop trust and prefer the right-most public IP when intermediate hops are private. Rolling to canary.'
Hypothesis: Identity/ingress proxy accepts X-Forwarded-For without validating trust of upstream hop; upgraded appliance now prepends internal hop which pushes client IP to the right, altering evaluation if trust policy expects left-most client.
Observed authz decision traces: ip_condition evaluated against 203.0.113.245 (edge appliance) not 198.51.100.77 (client) because XFF order changed after appliance rewrite.
Reproduced: Created synthetic proxy that inserts '10.0.0.5' before public IP in XFF; RBAC check fails when trust policy is configured to treat left-most token as client IP.
Configuration review: Some private deployments configure 'trust-proxy=true' without restricting trusted hops; ingress should validate hop IPs against a configured trusted list or use right-most public IP when private hops present.
Related: linked INT-4219 tracks a planned auth library change to XFF parsing and trusted-hop config; PR opened to ingress-proxy to add explicit trusted_hops and to ignore RFC1918 tokens when selecting client IP.
Risk analysis: If we flip selection logic globally without per-tenant config, some customers who rely on left-most semantics may be affected. Need customer-scoped rollback/feature-flag.
Workaround (applied 2026-03-14): Deployed ingress-proxy canary to Soteria's private control plane that 1) validates X-Forwarded-For hop chain against configured 'trusted_hops' and 2) when private RFC1918 hops are present, prefers the nearest public IP for RBAC evaluation. This restored access for affected service accounts.
Fix plan: Merge PR https://github.com/redwood/ingress-proxy/pull/1124 which introduces tenant-scoped 'trusted_hops' config and a 'xff_selection_policy' parameter ('left-most', 'right-most-public', 'validated-trusted-hops'). Ship as opt-in for private deployments with follow-up migration docs.
Post-deploy actions: 1) Add runbook instructions to validate edge appliance XFF behavior during upgrades. 2) Notify customers in private tier with IP-based RBAC to review 'trusted_hops' config. 3) Schedule postmortem and update RBAC docs.
Customer follow-up: Soteria Health confirmed workaround fixed immediate blocking issue and will coordinate with their appliance vendor to preserve original-source-ip semantics or explicitly configure proxy to forward XFF in expected order.
Closure criteria: Fix merged and enabled in customer's control plane, runbook updated, automated tests added to prevent regressions.
payload.summary: Customers in private VPC seeing 403 from IP-based RBAC conditions due to untrusted X-Forwarded-For header from proxy chain

Issue summary: StreamlineAI reported recurring 10-30s waves where p99 latency spikes 2-8x baseline and intermittent 504s occur. Impact: user-facing timeouts on short prompt workloads, elevated error budget burn for the Dedicated pool. Environment: prod-us-east Dedicated nodes running serving-runtime v2.8.1 with continuous-batcher enabled. Observed: p95 stable while p99 shows periodic stair-step waves; batch size histograms show transient increases in microbatch size followed by queuing. Suspected root cause: drain scheduling jitter in continuous-batcher that sometimes aligns badly with arrival patterns, producing delayed flushes and head-of-line blocking.
1) Provision a Dedicated pool with continuous-batcher enabled and default linger_ms=20
2) Emit steady low-rate short requests (mean token count ~22) from ~200 concurrent connections
    observe p99 over 2-3 minute windows for episodic waves
3) Capture batcher.drain_delay_ms and batch_size histograms; compare boundaries of p99 waves to drain timer variance
4) As mitigation, route traffic to non-continuous flush path and confirm p99 reverts to baseline
Support triage: confirmed traffic profile dominated by short sequences and periodic background bursts
SRE: p99 wave boundaries align with increased variance in batcher.drain_delay_ms histogram on 3 nodes
Perf Eng: reproduced locally with synthetic traffic and traced drift to scheduling behavior under OS scheduling delay
No resource saturation observed: GPU and CPU utilization steady; queues grow only during wave windows
Additional finding: batcher reschedule used system clock, allowing positive drift when host scheduling latency occurred
