Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports intermittent high tail latency and mid-stream connection resets (clients see 504/connection closed) for long streaming completions. Problem correlates with sessions where their sidecar attaches large per-request metadata headers (X-RW-Meta-*).

Impact:
- Several customers' streaming sessions terminate after 20–40s of token generation resulting in degraded UX for chat flows.
- Observed in prod/us-east only; impacts enterprise accounts on shared ingress.
- Estimated ~2-3% of long-running sessions in the customer account on 2026-02-27 and 02-28.

Environment:
- Ingress: internal ingress-nginx v1.21 behind AWS ALB (idle timeout 60s).
- API gateway layer: Redwood API (hosted).
- Serving runtime: rw-instruct-v1 on shared dedicated pools.
- Customer sidecar: BrightCart telemetry sidecar v0.7.2 that appends X-RW-Meta-* headers per user event.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long streaming completion (>250 tokens) with verbose telemetry enabled in BrightCart webapp.
2) Sidecar appends repeated X-RW-Meta-* headers and multiple tracing headers on each request.
3) After ~15–35s of streaming, client receives connection reset or sees a keep-alive close and subsequent 502/504 from ALB.

Expected behavior:
Streaming should continue to completion without mid-stream resets; ingress should not drop connections due to header growth during an active streaming session.

Actual behavior:
Ingress logs show "upstream prematurely closed connection" and NGINX error lines indicating proxy_buffer overflow and failed header parsing when header size exceeds configured large_client_header_buffers. ALB shows idle resets for some streams after headers expand on re-negotiation.

Attached logs / traces:
- Sample request IDs: req-20260227-7a3c, req-20260228-1f8b
- Ingress error lines (nginx): "upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream" and "client sent too large header"
- ALB access logs show 502/504 for the same request ids and TCP resets around the time of buffer errors.

Immediate customer impact: UI-level streaming interruptions; customer has paused telemetry while we investigate.
2026-02-28 - BrightCart Support (Elena Morris): We're seeing streaming interruptions for ~15% of long sessions since Friday. Disabling telemetry appears to reduce failures. Attaching sample trace ids.
2026-02-28 - Support (Samira Khan): Acknowledged, creating ticket. Initial hypothesis: header growth from sidecar + ingress buffer limits. We'll loop in SRE to validate NGINX buffer errors.
2026-02-28 - SRE (Mateo Ruiz): Observed NGINX error lines for the sample requests. Headers per request can reach 80–120KB in these sessions (cookies + X-RW-Meta). Linked to large_client_header_buffers and proxy_buffering behavior. Reproduced locally with a synthetic header generator.
2026-03-01 - Engineering (Priya Patel): Confirmed that when proxy_buffering is enabled and header size grows mid-stream (sidecar re-attaches metadata on follow-up requests), NGINX enters a state where it attempts to re-buffer and then closes upstream if buffers exceed limits. ALB idle timeout amplifies the symptom.
2026-03-01 - Support (Samira Khan): Proposed customer workaround: 1) temporarily disable sidecar telemetry headers, or 2) reduce header size. Provided config options they could set. Asked SRE for ingress-side mitigations.
2026-03-02 - SRE (Mateo Ruiz): Implemented temporary ingress tweak in prod/us-east for BrightCart route: increase large_client_header_buffers and set proxy_buffering off for their location block as emergency mitigation. Monitoring for regressions.
2026-03-02 - BrightCart (Elena Morris): Confirmed immediate improvement after config change; streaming sessions complete normally in the test cohort. Will work with us on a longer-term fix.
2026-03-02 - Support (Samira Khan): Marking ticket In Progress while engineering owners draft a permanent solution and runbook updates.
Hypothesis A: Repeated metadata headers appended by the customer's sidecar increase overall header size above NGINX large_client_header_buffers leading to parsing errors and upstream close.
Hypothesis B: proxy_buffering combined with header growth during an active keep-alive stream causes NGINX to allocate temp files / exceed buffer limits, triggering upstream connection termination.
Reproduction: Synthetic test with incremental header append replicated the upstream closed behavior and produced identical nginx error messages. Buffer growth observed when successive requests included additional X-RW-Meta-* headers.
Metrics: 95th/99th latency spikes aligned with ingress error logs for affected request ids. Error rate for BrightCart routes dropped by 85% after temporary buffer and proxy_buffering changes.
Dashboards/links: #support-brightcart slack thread, ingress error dashboard (dashboards.redwood.internal/ingress/errors?from=2026-02-27), sample logs in S3 s3://redwood-support/brightcart/samples/
Workaround (applied 2026-03-02): increase NGINX large_client_header_buffers for BrightCart location and set proxy_buffering off for their upstream block. This mitigated mid-stream resets and reduced observed 502/504 errors immediately.
Customer workaround: BrightCart disabled verbose telemetry headers and rolled a patch to reduce X-RW-Meta-* footprint. This was a low-effort temporary measure while we finalize platform changes.
Permanent fix (planned): Engineering to implement conservative defaults in ingress for streaming routes (larger header buffer defaults or per-route buffer policies), add detection to reject/trim excessive metadata headers earlier in the gateway, and update the 'streaming' runbook to include header-size checks and clear guidance for sidecars.
Follow-ups / tasks: INT ticket to evaluate increasing ALB idle timeout for long-running streams by default for enterprise customers; add a linter in SDKs to warn about per-request header growth; update runbook at https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/ingress-header-bloat. Linked PR for runbook changes: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1428.
Status: Temporary mitigation in prod/us-east applied and customer reduction of telemetry confirmed. Engineering planning a staged rollout of runbook + config changes; next update scheduled 2026-03-05.
payload.summary: High inference latency and mid-stream resets caused by oversized sidecar metadata headers overflowing NGINX buffers

comments: 2026-03-10T15:02:00Z Aisha Patel: Received P1 escalation from Greenline CSM. Customer reporting intermittent long-tail stalls and client retries amplifying the issue. Provided request for traces and SDK logs.

2026-03-10T17:20:00Z Platform Oncall: Confirmed elevated 429s for Greenline pool in prod/us-east-1 between 2026-03-10T13:40 and 2026-03-10T19:05. Noted concurrent autoscale activity. Collected runtime logs and initial metrics.

2026-03-13T11:02:00Z Greenline: Confirmed improvement during the canary window; still seeing occasional stalls when burst pattern exceeds 3x baseline traffic per instance. Requested permanent mitigation plan and guidance for SDK retry settings.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Greenline Health reports sudden spikes in perceived inference timeouts and streaming stalls during sustained small-burst traffic patterns. Customer observes long-tail stalls (~10-45s) on a subset of requests, which trigger aggressive client retries and amplify apparent outages.

Impact:
- Multiple customer application endpoints report transient user-facing delays and increased error rates during a 6-hour window on 2026-03-10.
- Estimated 12% of requests from Greenline during the window experienced >10s latency, several timed out client-side before server responded.
- Business impact: mission-critical clinical triage workflows occasionally delayed; customer flagged as P1.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated cluster (Greenline dedicated pool) in us-east-1.
- Models: redwood-v1-large (primary), fallback gpt-open-7B.
- Client: Greenline NodeJS SDK v2.4.1 with default retry backoff.

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Run steady stream of small bursts: 5 requests every 12 seconds per app instance, sustained for 30+ minutes across ~20 app instances.
2) Observe that a small fraction of requests see tokens delayed or the streaming socket pauses mid-response.
3) Client SDK retries after 6s leading to concurrent duplicated requests.

Observed behavior:
- Serving runtime logs show soft per-customer pacing (windowed request pacing) kicking in when burst density exceeds threshold.
- Rate-limiter returns 429 with X-RateLimit-Policy=pacing-window or introduces queueing leading to extended head-of-line blocking for that customer pool.
- Client retries amplify load, causing further queue elongation and increased tail latency.

Expected behavior:
- System should either return a clear 429 quickly or maintain steady short latency for allowed throughput without long queue waits. Client retries should be avoidable when throttling signals are explicit.

Logs & artifacts provided by customer:
- Trace IDs: trace-us-17822a, trace-us-1782ab, trace-us-1782ac (attached).
- Example SDK logs showing retry loop starting at 2026-03-10T14:32:06Z and duplicates created at 14:32:12Z.
- Network capture showing intermittent TCP keepalive during streaming stalls.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 13:55 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Found that pacing-window uses a conservative window-size parameter (0.9 * configured_qps_per_customer) and performs head-of-line queueing instead of rejecting excess quickly. Proposed short-term rule tweak and long-term redesign.
Hypothesis: Per-customer pacing window algorithm is intended to smooth traffic but currently enqueues excess requests, causing head-of-line blocking and long-tail stalls when client retries occur.
Metrics: During incident window 95th->99.9th percentile latency jumped from 0.9s to 18.4s for greenline pool. 429s increased by 4.6x compared to baseline.
Staging repro: Reproduced queueing behavior deterministically with the customer's burst profile; observed identical pacing-window log markers and queue depth growth.
Root cause analysis: Conservative pacing implementation with long dequeue delay plus SDK default retry timing (6s) creates a feedback loop. Lack of explicit fast-429 for pacing-window allowed retries to pile up instead of failing fast.
Related config: Dedicated pool had custom qps_per_customer cap set lower than assumed by pacing algorithm, misalignment exacerbated head-of-line queueing.
Short-term mitigation validated: prefer immediate 429 (fast-fail) on pacing-window breach; OR surface X-Pacing-Delay header with expected retry-after to clients.
Long-term options: 1) change pacing implementation to token-bucket with immediate rejects beyond capacity; 2) expose clearer throttling headers and SDK changes to respect Retry-After and exponential jitter; 3) autoscale smoothing to absorb short spikes without triggering pacing.
Workaround / Temporary fix applied: Deployed canary config (2026-03-12) that converts pacing-window enforcement from head-of-line queueing to immediate 429 for overflowed requests in Greenline's dedicated pool. Observed 70% reduction in client duplicate requests and 80% reduction in 99.9th percentile latency for the canary group.
Permanent remediation plan:
- Short term (next 7 days): Roll out immediate-429 behavior to all dedicated pools with opt-in per-customer exceptions. Publish SDK guidance recommending exponential backoff with jitter and honoring Retry-After headers.
- Medium term (1-2 months): Implement token-bucket style enforcement at the gateway to avoid head-of-line blocking; update telemetry to surface pacing events in Console per-route charts.
- Long term (Q2 roadmap): Add automated detection that adjusts autoscaling headroom for dedicated pools showing sustained bursty patterns and incorporate adaptive pacing thresholds.
Post-incident follow-ups: Confluence runbook updated, PR created (#842) to change pacing behavior, and Customer Success to schedule a technical review with Greenline to review SDK settings and post-rollout verification.
payload.summary: Sustained small-burst traffic triggers per-customer pacing window causing long-tail stalls and client retry amplification

payload.description:
Issue summary: During an operator-initiated version-lock switchover (canary -> primary), a subset of client sessions retained a stale session pointer ('ghost session') that appeared to remain pinned to the previous model for several minutes and then silently lost the pin mid-request. Impact: Customers reported mixed responses (stylistic mismatch and hallucinations) as part of single user sessions; several LLM calls returned tokens from two different model variants in one stream. Environment: Dedicated cluster (MapleAI), prod-us-east, reserved pool: d-prod-nyc-4g, traffic routed through dedicated-proxy. Observed behavior: Session affinity initially held to the pinned version for affected sessions, then mid-utterance the routing layer diverted to the canary fallback path without a logged pin eviction event. Expected behavior: Sessions pinned by customer version-lock should remain routed to pinned model instance until explicit unpin or session expiry. Affected customers noticed user-visible incoherence and flagged as P1.
1) Customer creates a version-lock on route /chat to redwood/fastgen-1.3 for session_cohort A; 2) Initiate canary switchover via Console: promote canary weight from 10% to 70% over 2 minutes; 3) Replay recorded user session traffic at production QPS for 3-5 minutes; 4) Observe responses where prefix tokens map to fastgen-1.3 but suffix tokens are consistent with vicuna-13b-ggml; 5) Check routing logs and session-store for pin metadata. Note: reproduction requires dedicated-proxy + proxy-side autoscale event during weight change to be most reliable.
[2026-03-10T15:02:12Z] routing: session_lookup id=ses_8f7a123 found pin=fastgen-1.3 ttl=900; [2026-03-10T15:02:14Z] proxy: shard-02 reported backend-change model=vicuna-13b-ggml reason=canary-weight-adjust; [2026-03-10T15:02:14Z] serving-runtime: request resumed kvcache=hit session=ses_8f7a123 route=/chat -> routed_backend=vicuna-13b-ggml; [2026-03-10T15:02:15Z] audit: no explicit pin-eviction event for ses_8f7a123; [2026-03-10T15:02:17Z] trace: token-stream shows token_1..token_36 from fastgen-1.3 then token_37..token_120 from vicuna-13b-ggml.
- Initial hypothesis: race between dedicated-proxy shard failover and in-memory session-store leading to ephemeral loss of pin metadata under heavy prefix-preserving batching. - Confirmed that session-store uses local LRU cache with 30s heartbeat to central store; during proxy autoscale the local cache dropped entries before TTL refresh completed. - Found a path in routing code where on backend-change we call refresh_session_pin() but the call is best-effort and suppressed if proxy heartbeat is stale. That suppression path did not log an eviction event; this explains the 'silent unpin'. - Replayed traffic in staging with instrumentation: reproduced 18/200 runs (~9%) when autoscale event occurred within 250ms of a request completion. - Not correlated with auth tokens or customer pin APIs; appears purely routing+cache timing.
Short-term: advise customer to increase session_pin_ttl to 1800s and enable sticky-proxy=true for the route. Issue summary:
Nimbus Bank needs an on-demand, encrypted delta handoff for audit events with adaptive field-filtering so their SIEM retains only allowed fields per contract and we provide cryptographic evidence for regulatory review. They want an S3-based delivery option with per-batch encryption, resume tokens, and a small-scope test harness before a full production roll.

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete SIEM onboarding for compliance audit without field-filtering and encrypted delivery proofs.
- Potential audit escalation if evidence bundle is not accepted by their audit vendor.

Environment:
- Redwood prod (us-east). Tenant: nimbus-bank-prod.

Requested deliverables (customer):
1) Sample delta export that includes: a) gzipped ndjson, b) per-batch AES-GCM envelope encrypted with a KEK wrapped by customer KMS key, c) resume token in manifest.
2) Field-filtering policy support to apply an allowlist/denylist at export time with a pluggable transform hook (they will supply policy CSV).
3) Per-batch manifest with canonical timestamp, event count, compressed size, SHA256 checksum, and optional ed25519 batch signature for non-repudiation.
4) Playbook for legal hold / retention gating (how to mark slices as not deletable) and a short runbook for auditors to verify integrity.

Steps to reproduce (customer test case):
1) Customer requests a delta for last 24 hours through Console API with parameter field_policy=allowlist:v1.csv and delivery=s3-presigned.
2) Redwood prepares batches and posts manifest.json to presigned URL.
3) Customer verifies decryptability and checksum against manifest.

Attachments: customer supplied allowlist CSV (redacted) and security questionnaire excerpt attached via support portal.

2026-03-13 16:30 - infra-kms (comment): We can support KMS wrapping for a generated DEK per-batch, wrapped with customer CMK via cross-account grant. Need customer to provide ARN and grant. Also recommending envelope version v2 to include iv and aad metadata in manifest.
Checked previous similar exports (linked SUP-465432) — those used per-batch HMAC but not full envelope encryption. We need to extend exporter to produce AES-GCM envelope with wrapped DEK and include iv and tag in manifest.
Field-filtering: propose implementing a transform hook that can be applied at export time using a fast streaming redact/allow stream to avoid full-materialization. This preserves order and keeps memory bounded.
Resume tokens: will include a signed token (base64) containing last_event_id, last_event_timestamp, slice_sequence, and manifest_hash. Token signing will use Redwood signing key; customer requested optional ed25519 that they can verify themselves — engineering to confirm key distribution method.

Performance note: generating per-batch DEKs and wrapping via customer KMS will add ~150-300ms per batch due to KMS latency; recommend batching policy to keep batch count reasonable (e.g., 5–10 MB batches).
If KMS grant is delayed: provide temporary presigned S3 delta with client-side AES-GCM encryption key shared via secure support channel for the 48-hour test window. Clearly document this as 'temporary test key' and mark artifacts as test only; do not use for production compliance evidence.

Per-batch manifest.json with checksum, size, iv, tag, wrapped_DEK, resume_token

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexaSearch reports that after a nightly bulk embed upload, reranker queries return duplicate documents in the top-k and end-to-end query latency spikes by ~3-6x for affected queries. Behavior started after a large bulk ingest (1.2M rows) on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- Duplicate top-k results (same doc_id appears multiple times in results) causing poor UX for LexaSearch customers.
- Elevated rerank/recall latency for affected queries (p95 downstream latency from 120ms -> 450-700ms).
- Intermittent 503s observed in rerank service when merging duplicates under load.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east (dedicated for enterprise customers)
- Ingest pipeline: ingest-service v3.6.1 -> transform -> shard-write -> indexer
- Embedding model: embed-large-v2 (fp16 quant path)
- Reranker: rerank-light-v1 running on dedicated pool

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Upload bulk file via /v1/embeddings/bulk with payload containing 'doc_id' as alphanumeric strings: many short user-generated IDs (~8 chars).
2) Wait for indexing job to complete (indexer logs show completed for job 2026-03-09T02:00Z).
3) Run rerank query against rerank endpoint /v1/rerank with query ids that target the uploaded corpus.
4) Observe duplicate document entries in returned top-k and higher latency.

Observed behavior:
- Internal IDs in embeddings store show collisions: two different doc_id values mapped to the same internal_id (internal_id hashes identical).
- Reranker merge step returns duplicates because it indexes by internal_id; dedup logic is shallow and does not detect near-duplicate vectors.
- Indexer logs contain repeated warnings: "WARN indexer: duplicate internal_id detected, overwriting entry" around 2026-03-09T01:58:44Z.
- Dashboard: shard-12 write QPS spike and indexer GC increased during re-ingest (link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/ingest/dash?shard=12).

Expected behavior:
- Each uploaded embedding retains uniqueness; internal_id should be collision-resistant for customer-provided doc_id values.
- Reranker should not produce duplicate top-k entries for distinct documents.

Relevant logs / excerpts:
- indexer.log snippet:
  [2026-03-09T01:58:44Z] WARN indexer shard-12 duplicate internal_id=0x4f3a9b2c for src_doc_id=AB12 and src_doc_id=Q9X7
  [2026-03-09T01:58:45Z] INFO indexer shard-12 overwrite completed
- rerank service trace: trace_id=trc-9f8a3, p95_merge=610ms, merge_retries=3

Initial hypothesis:
- ingest-service uses a 64-bit non-cryptographic hash (murmur3_64) over doc_id for internal_id storage. At large scale with many short user-provided IDs there is a non-negligible probability of collisions. The duplicate internal_ids cause overwrites at index time and duplicate entries at query time.
- Dedup behavior in rerank expects dedupe by metadata and does not handle collisions at the internal_id layer.

Requested from customer:
- Full sample of original upload (already provided as anonymized CSV).
- Confirmation whether they use short, low-entropy doc_id values (customer confirmed ~80% of ids are 6-9 chars with limited alphabet).

Next steps planned: validate collision probability on current hashing strategy and implement mitigations (see investigation_notes).
Support - 2026-03-10: Thanks for the report, LexaSearch. We've escalated to SRE and Ingest owners. Can you share a sanitized sample of the uploaded CSV and a job_id?
Customer (LexaSearch) - 2026-03-10: Provided sample and job_id ingest-20260309-58. They confirm doc_id pattern: [A-Z0-9]{6,9} with heavy reuse of short prefixes.
SRE (Tomás Rivera) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally by fuzzing 6-9 char ids; murmur3_64 produced collisions at scale in our test harness (collision rate ~1 in 250k with this id distribution). Created reproduction job rep-20260311 on staging.
Support (Aisha Kumar) - 2026-03-11: Noted that indexer log contains explicit duplicate internal_id warnings. Raised ingest-service PR to add collision detection: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-service/pull/4298
Customer (LexaSearch) - 2026-03-12: Impact: duplicate results are actively surfacing in production and causing product complaints. They request a hotfix and a timeline for a permanent fix.
SRE (Tomás Rivera) - 2026-03-12: Applied temporary mitigation for LexaSearch: backfill job that re-wrote internal_ids by appending a short salt derived from upload timestamp for colliding entries. Deploying change to indexer-dedup-worker in us-east canary now. Monitoring for latency improvement.
Support - 2026-03-13: Can confirm customer saw reduced duplicate-topk in canary traffic (sampled queries show duplicates reduced from 12% to 0.8%). Still tracking stability and preparing a permanent ingest fix.
Reproduction: used a generator for 1.5M doc_ids with distribution matching customer sample; murmur3_64 collisions reproduced. Collision analysis: collisions cluster when doc_ids have low entropy and short length. Short-term mitigation options evaluated: (1) switch to 128-bit salted hash (xxh3_128) at ingest-time, (2) fallback to salted UUID when collision detected, (3) add post-write validation that checks for multiple distinct source doc_ids mapping to same internal_id and mark for re-ingest. We implemented option (2) as hotfix for this customer and are implementing option (1) as permanent fix in ingest-service v3.6.2. Also flagged rerank dedupe logic for improvement to detect duplicate vectors beyond internal_id equality.
Hotfix applied: ingest-worker backfill that detects internal_id collisions and rewrites colliding entries with a deterministic salt (upload timestamp + monotonic counter). Canary run for LexaSearch reduced duplicate-topk from ~12% -> <1%. Hotfix link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-service/pull/4298. Temporary mitigation will remain until ingest-service v3.6.2 rollout.
1) Finish ingest-service v3.6.2 change to use xxh3_128 for internal_id generation and add unit tests for collision detection (owner: ingest-team, ETA: 2026-03-18).
2) Harden rerank dedupe to check vector similarity if multiple results share internal_id or metadata (owner: rerank-team, ETA: 2026-03-20).
3) Run a one-off global scan for collisions for enterprise customers who used bulk uploads in last 30 days and schedule targeted backfills (owner: support-sre, ETA: 2026-03-22).
4) Postmortem and playbook update (owner: support-ops, ETA: 2026-03-25).
We will notify LexaSearch with a timeline for permanent fix and confirm when the global scan/backfill is complete. No customer-facing incident page created at this time; internal customers impacted only.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when their orchestration issues multiple function-calls (tool calls) in parallel from different regional clients, retries and server-side batching can cause the calls to be applied out-of-order at the downstream webhook. Impact: In a chat orchestration where calls represent financial operations (authorizations -> capture), out-of-order application produced a capture before the authorization for ~0.7% of requests during a high-retry window, causing failed reconciliation and manual refunds. Environment: Enterprise dedicated customer using SDKs in three services: Python v1.2.0 (orchestrator), Typescript v1.3.4 (frontend gateway), Go v1.1.8 (worker). Traffic through prod us-west and eu-west. Steps to reproduce, logs and minimal repro are included below.
1) Deploy three clients: python orchestration service performs two sequential funcalls per logical user action: POST /authorize -> POST /capture (function-calling to external webhook).
2) Simultaneously invoke 50 requests that the orchestrator parallelizes across 5 worker goroutines (Go workers use SDK streaming to dispatch first call), and intentionally drop ACK for 10% of streaming chunks to force retries from the edge.
3) On server side enable default batching (server automatically batches 10-20 requests per RT window).
4) Trigger transient error on api-gateway between us-west and eu-west (5xx for 1.5s) to cause cross-region fallback and retries.
5) Verify downstream webhook sequence numbers for authorize/capture pair; observe capture events arriving before authorize for a subset.
2026-03-12T08:04:11Z us-west api-gateway WARN request retry initiated trace=aa12f.. status=502 -> routed to eu-west
2026-03-12T08:04:11Z eu-west serving-runtime INFO batched 12 calls window=20ms batch_id=b-993
2026-03-12T08:04:12Z eu-west function-proxy WARN downstream webhook 429 for call_id=auth-4f2, retry queued
2026-03-12T08:04:13Z us-west sdk-go INFO stream reconnect chunk_ack_missing for call_id=capture-4f2, attempt=2
2026-03-12T08:04:13Z eu-west serving-runtime INFO dispatched call capture-4f2 to webhook with sequence=2 (batched order), but auth-4f2 queued on retry and applied later with sequence=5
2026-03-12 - EdgeChat support rep (Elena Morales): Customer reports 0.7% of transactions failing reconciliation. They attached webhook logs with sequence numbers showing capture before authorize. They requested immediate mitigation and guidance for SDK patterns to prevent out-of-order side-effects.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 - EdgeChat (customer): Implemented per-action idempotency tokens and saw immediate drop in reconciliation errors to <0.01% in a small canary. They requested a platform-level change to preserve per-request causal order or expose ordering guarantees for function-calls.
Hypothesis 1: Server-side batching is assigning dispatch order purely by batch arrival timestamp. When a retry from an earlier logical call arrives later, it enters a subsequent batch and is dispatched after later calls that were not retried.
Hypothesis 2: Some SDKs (TS v1.3.4) normalize idempotency tokens by truncation of long UUIDs, causing token collision and unexpected dedupe behavior that can hide replays — NOT primary cause for ordering but noted.
Findings: Reproducer run with verbose trace shows batch_id and per-call original_sequence metadata available in logs but not used when computing dispatch order. Batching code uses wall-clock enqueue timestamp only.
Reproducer: Added custom header x-rw-original-seq to outgoing funcalls in staging; batch dispatcher ignored header when sorting batch members. Patch locally shows reordering when dispatcher sorted by original_sequence instead of arrival timestamp.
Risk: Changing dispatcher sort order to honor original_sequence requires carrying that metadata for all requests (hosted + private) and validating across cross-region failover path; possible increased memory overhead in dispatcher and potential latency impact on throughput.
Short-term mitigation (applied 2026-03-12): Support instructed customer to set x-rw-batching: off for critical payment flows and to use explicit per-action idempotency tokens. Customer confirms reduction in incorrect ordering.
Medium-term engineering plan: implement 'preserve_logical_order' flag on function-calling API. When enabled, server will persist original_sequence metadata and prioritize it when assembling dispatch order across retry/batch boundaries. Initial RFC approved 2026-03-13.
SDK changes: Add opt-in helpers in SDKs to surface and consistently propagate an 'original_sequence' header and to avoid token normalization (TS SDK patch PR #118 prevents token truncation).
Planned release: Runtime patch to dispatcher (no user-visible API change) targeted for 2026-03-22 with rollout to non-bursting tenants first. SDK patches to be released: python 1.2.3, ts 1.3.5, go 1.1.9. Documentation update and runbook created in Confluence.
Permanent recommendation for customers with stateful side-effects: always model dependent function-calls as explicit ordered transactions (ack on success then schedule next), or enable preserve_logical_order for batched flows once available.
ENG-TRACK: Implement dispatcher ordering by original_sequence (RFC link above) - owner: Marco Nguyen - due 2026-03-20
SDK-TS: Prevent idempotency token truncation and add helper to set original_sequence - owner: Priya Shah - due 2026-03-18
DOCS: Publish best-practices for ordered function-calls and recommended headers - owner: DevRel - due 2026-03-19
SRE: Plan staged rollout for dispatcher change with feature flag and monitor reconciliation metrics for top enterprise tenants - owner: SRE Team - due 2026-03-22
payload.summary: Concurrent function-calls can be applied out-of-order after cross-region retry and batching - leads to inconsistent external side-effects

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer on Dedicated capacity reports that long chat sessions (5k+ token prompts) over SSE and WebSocket begin with normal streaming but after a period of elevated per-token latency (~300-600ms) the stream goes silent and the client observes a silent disconnect (no error frame) or abrupt close.

Impact:
- A single customer (Acme Health, dedicated) experiencing frequent user-facing interruptions in long interactive sessions across multiple regions.
- Estimated 20% of long sessions (>2000 tokens) affected during observed burst window.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-03) backed by redwood-13b-v1 workers.
- Fronting: Envoy edge -> NGINX LB -> internal API gateway -> serving-runtime.
- Observed regions: prod-us-east primary, affected sessions also seen proxied from eu-west clients.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Create a long chat prompt (instructions + 4 large context chunks; target output >3k tokens).
2) Open SSE subscription to /v1/chat/stream using customer API key and stream response.
3) After ~60-120s into generation, client reports heartbeat missing then connection close without explicit 5xx or 4xx.
4) Replays show same behavior roughly 1 in 5 attempts under burst load.

Observed logs & artifacts:
- Envoy edge logs show a 200 response for the request with a final FIN from client side shortly after a prolonged period of bytes silence. No application-level 5xx recorded.
- NGINX access log excerpt: "GET /v1/chat/stream 200 0.123 - - -" followed by upstream_disconnect
- Runtime stdout capture for worker: repeated "token-latency=0.45s" spikes and then worker reports "client closed connection".
- Client tcp dump (provided) shows keepalive window with no SSE comment lines for ~40s, then TCP RST from client agent.

Hypothesis (initial):
- Upstream proxy (NGINX) or intermediate idle timeout is closing connections after a threshold when streaming output is delayed due to transient model token-latency spikes (KV cache warm/thaw or kernel swap).
- Alternatively, when the serving-runtime pauses worker emission (prefetch/backpressure or kernel swap for quantized worker), Envoy/NGINX may not see periodic bytes and assume idle connection, closing it silently.
- There is also evidence of increased queuing at the router during autoscaling events which aligns with timestamps of affected sessions.

Notes:
- Customer reproduced against both SSE and WebSocket protocols; behavior is protocol-agnostic.
- Affected sessions often include model fallback events during which the server swaps a worker (observed canary-to-main fallback), which correlates with the silent period.

Attachments referenced:
- pcap: acme_health_sse_2026-03-12.pcap (attached to ticket)
- runtime traces: trace-2026-03-12-14-01.log
- dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/streaming/latency?range=2026-03-12

Additional notes:
Confirmed: behavior reproduces in lab when inducing token-latency spikes (artificial sleep in runtime emission path).
Envoy front door keeps connection open beyond 60s when periodic bytes are sent; NGINX upstream_read_timeout at 30s causes internal upstream disconnect when no bytes seen for that period.
Worker logs show KV cache migration events and occasional kernel swap for quantized workers at times that align with customer reports. These operations can pause emission for tens of seconds depending on sequence length and device warmup.
Autoscaler events: brief worker eviction/creation observed in dedicated pool at 2026-03-12T08:03Z which aligns with an uptick in incidents. Suggests combined effect: transient model warm + aggressive LB timeout -> client disconnects.
Heartbeat emission experiment indicates that keeping periodic zero-byte comments or tiny SSE comments prevents the proxy from closing the connection.
Mitigations applied: 1) Temporarily increased NGINX upstream_read_timeout to 90s for affected dedicated pools (rolled 2026-03-14 11:45 UTC). 2) Deployed runtime feature flag to emit configurable SSE comment heartbeats every 15s during long generations to survive proxy idle windows. 3) Created follow-up task for runtime team to reduce kernel-swap pause durations and improve warm worker handoff (see linked PR).
Next steps / permanent fix:
- Runtime: optimize KV cache migration path and make worker warmups non-blocking (owner: Elena Gomez, ETA: 2 weeks).
- Infra: review and align idle timeout semantics between Envoy/NGINX across clusters (owner: Marco Ruiz, ETA: 1 week).
- Product: update docs and SDKs to recommend client keepalive options and surface guidance for long streaming sessions (owner: Priya Menon, ETA: 3 weeks).
payload.summary: Streaming response jitter followed by silent SSE/WebSocket disconnect during long chat generation

payload.description:
Issue summary:
BrightBot reported a sustained drop in batch throughput and multiple 5xx fallback events for their dedicated pool in us-east-1 beginning ~2026-03-12T10:15Z. Symptoms included prolonged GPU attach latencies, bursty 429/504s on batched routes, and fallback to lower-tier model variants.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency/p99 for embedding and chat routes spiked to 6–12s for ~30% of requests.
- BrightBot reported visible user errors and loss of throughput on reserved capacity routes for ~45 minutes.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool (BrightBot-dedicated-us-east) running mixed workloads (short-stream chat + long-lived analytics keepalives).
- Platform: production, us-east-1.
- Autoscaler profile: predictive+reactive hybrid, cooldown 60s.

Timeline & observable triggers:
- 10:11Z: small increase in long-lived keepalive sessions from BrightBot analytics sidecars.
- 10:14Z: allocator heartbeats show increasing slot reservations with incomplete prefetch completes.
- 10:18Z: autoscaler issued a small scale-up, but attach latencies continued to climb and batchers started to serialize.
- 10:30Z: several in-flight prefetched KV leases exhausted, leading to short bursts of eviction and 5xx fallbacks.

Steps to reproduce (internal replication):
1) Create many long-lived keepalive streams with small periodic pings (10s) while also sending short chat bursts.
2) Configure predictive autoscaler with cooldown 60s; use dedicated-reserved pool.
3) Observe allocator slot attach times, KV prefetch success rate, and autoscaler decisions.

Observed behavior:
- Keepalive connections appear to "shadow" prefetched slots: long sessions hold soft leases preventing efficient batch coalescing.
- Prefetch pipeline enters a backpressure loop where incomplete prefetches block allocation of new batches (deadlock-like), causing GPU-credit counters to drop faster than autoscaler can replenish.
- Autoscaler scales up but new attachments take >45s and often fail to join batches, triggering immediate fallbacks.

Expected behavior:
- Short-lived and long-lived streams should coexist without prefetch starvation; autoscaler should respond to increased queued demand within configured SLO.

Relevant logs & traces (snippets):
- allocator.log @2026-03-12T10:16:02Z: "soft-lease hold: session=brightbot-analytics-321 lease_ms=120000 state=prefetch_pending"
- kv-prefetcher @2026-03-12T10:17:48Z: "prefetch_timeout model=redwood-v2-7b-instruct ctx=2048 pending=87"
- autoscaler @2026-03-12T10:18:05Z: "scale_request: +2 gpus reason=queued_duration_p90>threshold"
- serving-runtime @2026-03-12T10:19:32Z: "attach_timeout session=client-1983 err=attach_latency>30000ms retries=3"

Initial hypothesis:
- A cohort of long-lived keepalives with periodic small traffic holds soft prefetch/lease state that misleads the allocator and serializes batch formation (shadowing).
- Prefetcher backpressure + autoscaler cooldowns allow GPU-credit counters to drain, causing attach stalls and cascading evictions.

References and cross-links:
- Slack: #support (thread ts: 1647839200.000200), #infra-alerts.

Issue summary: During a staged model rollout for customer VerdeCommerce we observed repeated short-duration rollouts ('stutters') where a subset of tenant requests were intermittently rerouted to fallback variants despite an explicit model_pin. Impact: Customers reported mixed output quality and unexpected model variant responses for ~20% of requests to a single tenant. This is causing user-facing regressions in the customer's chat assistant and has been elevated by the CS team.

Impact: Mixed-model outputs for production traffic, increased error-monitoring noise, measurable QoE regressions in downstream application A/B checks (customer reported higher complaint rate). No data exfiltration. The behavior started after a canary weight increase that ran at 2026-03-10T08:12:00Z.

Environment: Dedicated pool for VerdeCommerce in prod:us-east-1 using pinned model redwood-v2.0-rc with orchestrator rollout configured as weighted canary (weights: 80 -> 100 over 30m). Edge tier uses header-based affinity and a short-lived session lease (ttl=90s).

Observed behavior: When canary weight increased stepwise, we see transient "stutter" windows (~5-30s) where requests belonging to the pinned tenant alternate between the pinned variant and a fallback variant (open-m-7b). These windows correlate with orchestrator snapshot commits and a flurry of health probe events. Requests during the stutter frequently contained identical session tokens but received different model variants.

Expected behavior: Tenant with explicit model_pin should remain routed to pinned variant for the life of the session lease and during gradual weight changes; fallbacks should be triggered only on persistent capacity or health failures, not during snapshot/commit churn.

Attachments: request-ids, sample payloads, and timing traces attached in ticket artifacts.
1) Configure a weighted canary rollout from redwood-v2.0-rc (pinned) to redwood-v2.0-rc promoted -> full in dedicated pool in us-east-1
2) Use a sustained low-throughput traffic generator with tenant header X-Tenant-ID set to VerdeCommerce and session cookie TTL=90s
3) Step canary weight from 80% to 100% in 10% increments every 5 minutes and observe routing decisions at edge and orchestrator during commit windows
4) Correlate routing logs with orchestrator commit timestamps and edge affinity lease renewals

Hypothesis A: Snapshot commit and route recompute is briefly dropping affinity for sessions whose lease is near expiry, causing edge to apply default fallback logic.
Hypothesis B: Orchestrator commit latency + in-flight connection reuse at edge leads to mixed routing decisions when route tables are being swapped (commit window race).

Mitigation steps: (1) Disable route recompute on snapshot commit for leases with remaining_ttl < 30s (temporary safeguard); (2) Orchestrator patch to apply commit atomically with graceful drain window (PR linked below); (3) Edge fix to prefer existing session route until lease expiry rather than recomputing mid-flight. Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 03:22 UTC Faraday Telecom experienced a partial service outage for inference requests. A scheduled maintenance window on a subset of Dedicated GPU pools triggered an automated drain of several nodes; the autoscaler inadvertently scaled down backup pools faster than expected, causing many customer requests to failover to hosted capacity in us-east. The hosted routing hit global soft rate-limits and a cascade of client retries produced a classic 'thundering herd' pattern.

Impact:
- 35% error rate (5xx/429) for Faraday's production traffic between 03:22–03:56 UTC.
- Increased tail latency for chat streaming; several streams truncated.
- Cross-tenant soft rate-limits engaged, affecting 12 other customers with transient 429s.
- Billing exposure observed due to repeated retries and duplicate completions for some requests.

Environment:
- prod us-east, Dedicated pools (dedicated-faraday-prod-pool) with fallback to hosted-api cluster-02.
- Model: redwood-rlhf-large-v2 pinned by customer.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Simulate drain of two dedicated GPU nodes serving a heavy prefix workload.
2) Force failover policy to routed-hosted when capacity under threshold.
3) Replay client behavior with aggressive retry (retry-after not respected).
4) Observe rate-limiter counters and queue saturation on hosted router.

Logs and traces referenced:
- Hosted router traces: trace-id 8b4f2a1b-03 (sample span links in confluence page).
- Autoscaler events: cluster-autoscaler logs 2026-03-10 03:20-03:40 UTC.
- Customer-provided SDK logs attached in support bundle (s3://support-bundles/faraday/128500/).
Timeline and primary hypothesis:
- 03:18 UTC: Scheduled maintenance job issued drain.
- 03:20 UTC: Autoscaler reconciler erroneously interpreted pool health as degraded and removed two warm spare nodes due to a config regression introduced in autoscaler PR 118.
- 03:22 UTC: Traffic overflowed to hosted-api cluster-02; global token bucket rate-limiter applied conservative per-customer limits.
- 03:24-03:40 UTC: Observed exponential retry patterns from Faraday SDK (client retry logic did not respect 'Retry-After' header due to older SDK version).
- 03:30 UTC: Queue depth spike on router and streaming connection resets.
Investigation confirmed via autoscaler leader logs and tracing. Key finding: autoscaler PR 118 modified drain behavior to prefer aggressive scale-down when average GPU utilization falls below 12% — in our scenario warm spares dropped below that threshold. Secondary contributing factor: SDK clients with aggressive retry policy and lack of exponential backoff.

Telemetry artifacts: grafana panels 'router-rate-limiter', 'autoscaler-reconcile', 'hosted-queue-depth' attached in incident runbook.
Mitigations applied during incident:
- 03:36 UTC: Support toggled fallback-policy to 'graceful' for Faraday, preventing further immediate failovers.
- 03:40 UTC: Temporary raise of per-customer rate-limit on hosted-api cluster-02 to accommodate inflight failovers while teams stabilized pools.
- 03:45 UTC: Autoscaler leader rolled back PR 118 and recomputed desired state; two warm spare nodes were restored.
- 03:50 UTC: Re-enabled normal routing; error rates and latencies returned to baseline by 03:56 UTC.
Post-incident actions implemented:
- Rollback of autoscaler PR 118 and a hotfix (PR 4331) to add safety gates to drain logic.
- Customer credits: applied a one-time invoice credit for duplicate-completion billing exposure (handled by Finance).
- Communication: sent customer-facing incident summary and remediation plan to Faraday CSM and engineering on 2026-03-11.
- SDK outreach: Customer engineering recommended to upgrade to SDK v2.3.1 which respects Retry-After and adds jitter to backoff.
Add autoscaler drain safety gate: require min-warm-spares >= 2 before aggressive scale-down
Add runtime circuit-breaker to prevent single-customer failover floods from consuming hosted router token buckets
Rate-limiter instrumentation: expose per-customer retry amplification metric to Console
Customer outreach: scheduled technical review with Faraday engineers on 2026-03-18
Create runbook: 'handling-dedicated-to-hosted-failover' and link in routing runbooks
payload.summary: Faraday Telecom: failover thundering-herd causing cross-tenant rate-limits and partial outage - post-incident follow-up

Issue summary: FastPay Solutions (enterprise PSP customer) requests a certified bundle of anonymized audit events and a SIEM index mapping to support an external penetration test scheduled by their security vendor. They require proof that delivered samples match production schemas and cryptographic provenance for ingest.

Impact: Customer cannot complete third-party penetration test without concrete audit evidence. This is blocking their compliance certification and go-live for a new payments integration. Customer expects delivery within 48 hours of first response.

Customer request (detailed):
- Provide an anonymized sample of ~5,000 audit events spanning account management, API keys, token usage, and model invocation logs.
- Deliver formats: ndjson and Parquet (gzipped).
- Provide a SIEM index mapping CSV mapping Redwood audit fields to common Splunk/Elastic fields.
- Include per-file HMAC-SHA256 signatures and a signed manifest (X.509 cert id reference).
- Supply a short playbook explaining pseudonymization rules applied (hashing salt rotation, which fields redacted vs truncated) and a delta manifest showing how samples were selected (time range, event filters).
- Answer a 12-question security questionnaire related to log retention, key management, and chain-of-custody.

Environment: Production tenant for FastPay (tenant-id: fpay-prod-004), us-east-1.

Steps to produce sample (requested by customer):
1) Query audit store for events between 2026-02-20T00:00:00Z and 2026-03-05T23:59:59Z filtered to tenant fpay-prod-004 and event types {auth.login, auth.token.create, model.invoke, keys.rotate, admin.account.update}.
2) Apply deterministic pseudonymization to user identifiers (sha256 with tenant-specific salt) and truncate IP addresses to /24.
3) Redact raw prompt text and replace with length buckets and model_id.
4) Export NDJSON and Parquet, compress, compute HMAC per file using a customer-shared verification key, and produce signed manifest referencing cert serial.

Acceptance criteria:
- Files contain exactly 5,000 events (allow +/- 2%).
- SIEM mapping covers at least the fields: timestamp, tenant_id, user_id_pseudonym, event_type, src_ip_trunc, model_id, request_id, http_status, token_id_hash, response_time_ms.
- Manifest signature validates with provided cert.

Deadline: Customer requests delivery no later than 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC.

Primary contact: Maya Chen (FastPay), security@fastpay.com. Redwood contact: Omar Patel (Support), o.patel@redwood.com.

Additional notes:
Audit store location: s3://redwood-audit-prod/tenant=fpay-prod-004/YYYY-MM-DD/*.ndjson.gz; query via internal export tool 'audit-exporter' v2.3.1.
Field mapping draft: timestamp->@timestamp, tenant_id->tenant, user_id_pseudonym->user.id.hash, event_type->event.action, src_ip_trunc->source.ip, model_id->service.model, request_id->trace.id, http_status->http.response.status_code, token_id_hash->token.id.hash, response_time_ms->metrics.latency.ms.
Pseudonymization approach: SHA256(hex(salt || user_id)) with tenant-specific salt stored in KMS (rotation policy applies). Salt access requires 'compliance-export' IAM role (temporary session requested).
HMAC signing: Using customer provided key for per-file HMAC-SHA256. We will include HMAC values in manifest.json and sign manifest with internal X.509 cert (CN=redwood-evidence-2026). Need to provide cert serial to customer for verification.
Privacy risk: Raw prompts redacted per customer instruction. Confirmed no PII remains in top-level fields; nested metadata checked via grep for email patterns during sample run.
Size estimate: 5k events ~ 12MB ndjson gzipped; Parquet gzipped ~ 8MB. Export job should complete in ~30 minutes for given date range.
Dependencies: Legal approval for redaction approach (INT-44102), temporary KMS grant (infra ticket INF-7832), and S3 presigned-upload configuration for customer bucket (ops ticket OPS-2291).
Status: In progress. Next steps: complete export job, compute HMACs, produce signed manifest, upload to presigned S3, and send verification instructions to customer.
If deliverable passes acceptance criteria, change status to Resolved and attach delivery manifest and checklist. If legal asks for additional redaction, create follow-up INT ticket for retention and policy updates.
Owner: Omar Patel (Support) to coordinate SRE export and Legal sign-off. Close plan target: 2026-03-13 or earlier depending on legal turnaround.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled canary weight increase for a dedicated customer (Lexicon Health) we observed multipart streaming requests that triggered a prefetch handshake to stall. Some sessions completed the handshake and retained a pinned model variant while others fell back to the baseline variant, causing mixed-variant responses for a single user session.

Impact:
- Several customer API calls returned inconsistent model behavior (different answer styles and tokenization) within the same conversation session.
- Customer reported degraded user experience for ~2% of requests in the affected cohort; no data loss reported.
- Billing spike observed due to unexpected re-runs on client side (~$220 additional tokens within the window).

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster for Lexicon Health in prod-us-west
- Rolling canary: target weight increased from 10% to 30% at 2026-03-10T02:15:00Z
- Models involved: redwood-open-7b-v2 (canary variant), redwood-open-1.3b (baseline)
- Edge and prewarm services: prewarm-service v2.11.0, edge-cache v1.9.1

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Send multipart streaming payloads (large prompt + attachments) pinned to the tenant route during a gradual canary weight increase.
2) Observe long-running prefetch handshake for KV cache warmup (timeouts between controller and prewarm-service).
3) During handshake stall, routing logic sometimes returns fallback route to baseline variant instead of waiting for pin commit.
4) Client receives first tokens from baseline; subsequent partial handshake completion rebinds subsequent requests to canary -> mixed responses.

Logs / Evidence:
- Edge request traces: trace ids available in comments below (e.g., trace: usw-req-20260310-7f2b4)
- Prewarm service logs: repeated "handshake: waiting on kvcache-warmup" followed by "handshake aborted: prewarm-timeout" for affected sessions.
- Orchestrator snapshot: commit for canary cohort delayed by 12s then partially applied on a subset of shards.

Initial hypothesis:
- Prefetch handshake timeout setting (default 10s) is too aggressive for multipart streaming with large attachment KVs; when handshake times out the routing fallback path is incorrectly taking precedence and not preserving explicit pin intent for in-flight sessions.
- Race between prewarm acknowledgment and edge routing cache eviction causes some requests to observe stale routing metadata.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced in staging by increasing multipart size and lowering prewarm timeout; observed same split behavior when handshake delay >8s.
- Traced request flow across edge -> prewarm -> orchestrator; observed orchestrator returning partial commit ack to some shards while others still report prewarm in progress.
- Orchestrator commit logic treats partial shard commit as success for route selection in the edge cache. This causes early routing decisions for subsequent requests.
- No evidence of tenant cookie corruption; session tokens were consistent.

Temporary mitigation applied (2026-03-11 04:30 UTC):
- Increased prewarm handshake timeout to 30s for Lexicon Health dedicated cluster to reduce aborts.
- Adjusted edge routing to prefer existing session affinity when handshake state is pending (suppress fallback-to-baseline for in-flight pinned sessions).

Resolution plan / next steps:
1) Engineering (serving-runtime) to add stronger guard: do not treat partial shard commit as route-commit until all shard acknowledgments are received or a deterministic quorum is met. (PR drafted, see linked PR).
2) Prewarm team to implement progressive backoff for KV warmup when multipart attachments are detected and surface warmup progress to orchestrator.
3) Edge caching: add short grace period for session-affinity preservation while handshake pending.
4) Post-incident: run a controlled canary with large-multipart test vectors to validate heuristics.

Customer communication:
- Notified Lexicon Health CS contact with interim mitigations and ETA for full fix. Customer asked for a postmortem and permanent fix timeline.

Additional notes:
Mitigation applied: prewarm handshake timeout increased and edge affinity suppression enabled for affected dedicated cluster. Permanent fix in progress: require shard quorum for commit and improve KV warmup backoff; target canary for 2026-03-18.
Race between prewarm handshake timeout and orchestrator partial shard commit; orchestrator treating partial shard ack as route commit caused routing divergence and fallback to baseline variant mid-session.
payload.summary: Prefetch handshake stall during multipart streaming splits model pin and causes mixed-variant responses

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reported intermittent streaming failures and fast client disconnects from Redwood Private agents. Impact: Live streaming endpoints (chat/streaming generate) experience repeated HTTP/2 RST_STREAM and full gRPC connection resets leading to truncated responses for ~10% of requests during peak. Symptoms started after a firewall rule update on customer's edge NGFW that enabled SYN cookie protection.

Context: Customer runs Redwood Private in a VPC peered to their on-prem via an edge NGFW. Traffic to the Redwood control plane and model-serving endpoints traverses the customer's firewall (stateful inspection) which recently had a policy change to harden TCP handshake handling (SYN cookie enabled).

1) From a client in the customer's network, open a streaming generation request to Redwood Private with HTTP/2 gRPC (long-lived).
2) Simulate connection churn by opening 20 concurrent streams and closing/reopening several to exercise connection reuse.
3) Observe periodic RST_STREAM errors and gRPC UNAVAILABLE followed by successful reconnects.
4) Disable SYN cookie feature on the firewall and repeat - streaming failures stop within 10 minutes.

- Agent logs: repeated 'HTTP/2 stream reset (RST_STREAM code 2)' and 'gRPC transport error: connection closed' around timestamps 2026-03-10T15:22:41Z - 15:40:12Z.
- tcpdump (customer capture): server-side SYN seen, SYN-ACK returned, then server retransmits SYN-ACK and client sends ACK twice leading to ambiguous handshake. Observed duplicate SYN/ACK retransmits around 1-2s after initial handshake.
- Firewall logs: entries showing 'SYN-cookie engaged' and 'TCP handshake revalidated' for connections toward Redwood control plane IP range.
- Console metrics: increased CONNECT_FAILURE and short-lived streams metric for customer in us-east-1 between 15:20-16:00 UTC.

Initial hypothesis: firewall SYN cookie mechanism rewrites or suppresses early SYN/ACK leading to server-side view of handshake state mismatch and spurious retransmissions; gRPC connection reuse and HTTP/2 multiplexing amplify the effect into stream resets.
Reproduced in lab by enabling SYN cookie emulation on a test NGFW - identical RST_STREAM patterns observed.
Root cause confirmed by vendor packet-inspection analysis: the NGFW treats certain SYN retransmissions as malformed and injects SYN-cookie responses, but does not consistently forward the subsequent ACK to the original server instance when pooling connections across HA pair, resulting in half-open or duplicate-seen handshakes.
Correlated with recent firewall policy rollout at the customer's edge on 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC.

Support (Maya): Logged by customer support after initial report; collected pcap and console metrics and escalated to SRE.
SRE (Sanjay): Confirmed patterns in packet capture; reproduced with vendor lab configuration. Opened ticket with customer's NGFW vendor: case #VENDOR-8821 and linked Slack thread #support-private-networking.
Customer (Ops lead, Aaron Li): Applied temporary rule tweak to disable SYN cookie on 2026-03-11 03:10 UTC; observed immediate reduction in stream resets. Customer requested a recommended long-term firewall config to maintain hardening without impacting gRPC streams.
SRE (Sanjay): Proposed mitigations: (1) disable SYN cookie for Redwood control-plane/model-serving IP ranges, (2) enable TCP connection tracking affinity on firewall HA pairs, (3) apply TCP keepalive and reduced idle timeouts on agents as defensive measure. Added runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.com/runbooks/private-networking-syn-cookie-workaround.
Root cause: customer NGFW's SYN-cookie implementation was interfering with TCP handshake tracking across HA nodes, causing spurious retransmits and gRPC connection flaps.
Fix/Workaround applied: Customer disabled SYN-cookie for the Redwood destination CIDR and enabled connection-affinity for the firewall cluster. We recommended keeping TCP keepalive on the agent side and added a defensive retry/backoff change in the serving-runtime (non-breaking) to reduce impact during transient handshake anomalies.
Follow-up: Vendor provided firmware patch addressing cross-node SYN-cookie behavior (VND-1.4.2). Customer scheduled staged rollout for 2026-03-20. SRE implemented a non-disruptive retry backoff change (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1487) to make streaming more resilient.
payload.summary: SYN-cookie enabled customer firewall causes gRPC connection flaps and HTTP/2 stream resets for streaming responses

- Affects scheduled exports across the org for dashboards that use nested variable resolution + sampling. Estimated ~12 scheduled jobs per day impacted for the customer.

Environment:
- Redwood Console (hosted), prod/us-east region, customer on Dedicated tier (VelaPay).
- Dashboards include panels with nested variables (org-level -> route regex -> tag). Query sampling at panel-level enabled (sample_rate ~0.1). Retention compacting enabled on org partition.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Create dashboard with two panels: A) raw events panel with nested variables in the WHERE clause; B) metric aggregation panel.
2) Enable panel-level query sampling on panel A (0.1).
3) Configure scheduled export (daily PDF and CSV) for dashboard with "attach tracehook" enabled.
4) Wait for scheduled job to run or trigger manual send.

Observed behavior:
- Scheduled PDF/CSV contains tracehook column values like "TRACEHOOK=;" or truncated urls missing runId and token.
- Live dashboard "Open trace" links on the same panels work and include full runId/token.

Expected behavior:
- Scheduled exports should preserve working tracehook links identical to the UI (or link back to the same runId/token namespace).

Temporary workaround:
- Customer disabled panel-level sampling and re-ran scheduled report; links returned. Not ideal due to cost/volume requirements.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 15:27 - SRE Team (channel #support): Observed that scheduled-run pipeline uses compacted rollup storage path for sampled queries which strips tracehook metadata during export join. Raising as suspected cause.
Logs: exporter logs show "tracehook_lookup_missing" entries correlated to scheduled runs that hit rollup store. Query planner uses plan hash H=0x7f4a when sampling_enabled=true and nested_vars_present=true; plan chooses 'rollup-scan' instead of 'raw-scan' to satisfy latency SLO for scheduled jobs. Retention compact deletes per-event runId mapping from older partitions; tracehook synthesis falls back to empty token. Hypothesis: planner changes plan under sampling+nested-vars and exporter doesn't rehydrate tokens from raw shards. Repro steps in staging confirmed: disabling sampling forces 'raw-scan' and tracehooks appear. Related to commit https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/commit/aa12b3 from retention compact reorder (recent).
Workaround provided to customer: disable panel-level sampling for affected dashboards or change scheduled export to run with parameter 'force_raw_scan=true' (internal flag) until fix deployed. Engineering action: patch query planner to prefer raw-scan for scheduled exports when tracehook export flag is set OR ensure exporter can rehydrate tracehook tokens from raw shards even when plan used rollup results. Patch PR opened and targeted for next canary: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4913. Planned rollout: canary -> us-east -> global over 72 hours. Post-deploy validation: run 5 scheduled exports across 3 dashboards with nested-vars + sampling and verify tracehook links. Follow-up: add unit test for scheduled-export tracehook preservation and add dashboard-level lint to warn when sampling will drop tracehooks.
payload.summary: Scheduled dashboard report strips tracehook links when panels use nested variables and sampling

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a sustained traffic peak on 2026-03-10 09:02-09:46 UTC MintLance experienced high rates of truncated responses (clients reported streaming connections closing mid-completion) and a subsequent unexpected billing delta attributed to duplicate acknowledgement accounting.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests from MintLance in us-east experienced truncated streaming completions (partial transcripts).
- Brief billing spike visible on customer's invoice preview window for the affected timeframe (~$480 extra before automated credit).
- Customer-facing producers reported degraded UX for chat features during morning traffic peak; no data exfiltration identified.

Environment:
- Redwood prod cluster in us-east serving MintLance dedicated pool (dedicated capacity, pool-id dl-mintlance-1).
- Models routed to rw/opt-6.7b-quantized-v2 with streaming enabled.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) High concurrency from MintLance runtime jobs starting at ~09:02 UTC.
2) KV prefix cache miss flood (many new conversation prefixes) increased per-request setup cost.
3) Serving runtime started shedding long-lived streaming connections under backpressure; some connections closed with 499/stream-reset.
4) Client retries combined with router-level partial-ack duplication produced duplicate billing events for a subset of short-lived retries.

Logs / evidence pointers:
- SRE dashboard: links to request-rate, tail latency, and streaming-reset graphs in Grafana (see related_confluence_pages).
- Example streaming trace: request-id 1a7b2f4d showing abrupt grpc stream close at 09:12:18 UTC (attached to internal trace).
- Billing ledger row samples in BigQuery: project redwood-billing.mintlance_tmp.billing_events_20260310 showing duplicate ack events for request-id hash range xxxxx..yyyyy.

Initial hypothesis: concurrent KV cache miss and a rare router backpressure path combined to close streaming connections without completing token accounting.

Timestamps and findings:
- 09:02 UTC: MintLance concurrent job window begins (customer reported a scheduled batch of user sessions).
- 09:07-09:20 UTC: KV cache miss rate spiked to 1400% of baseline for the dedicated pool; eviction churn increased CPU on serving nodes.
- 09:10 UTC: Router ingress observed queue growth; router began responding with RESET_STREAM to long-lived streams when per-node inflight tokens exceeded safety threshold.
- 09:12 UTC: Several clients retried immediately; retry logic created short-lived requests that completed quickly and created duplicate ack entries in billing pipeline due to idempotency gap for streaming-early-terminations.

Hypotheses validated by logs:
- We found router logs showing explicit RESET_STREAM events correlated with the same request-ids as truncated traces.
- Billing pipeline consumer acknowledged events twice when stream token accounting did not include retry-de-dup metadata (race between ack persistence and retry dedup token write).

Temporary mitigations applied during incident:
1) Increased per-router streaming inflight safety threshold for dl-mintlance-1 by 25% to reduce premature resets.
2) Applied a KV cache TTL bump and warmed common prefixes via a preheat job to reduce miss churn.
3) Issued a manual billing credit to MintLance while investigation proceeded.

Open risks noted:
- Similar mis-specified client retry windows could retrigger duplicate ack behavior unless idempotency tokens are enforced end-to-end.

Additional notes:
Root cause: a combination of KV cache miss storm causing serving node CPU pressure and a router safety path that reset long-lived streams when inflight tokens exceeded threshold. Client retry behavior plus a small idempotency gap in the billing ingestion pipeline produced duplicate ack/billing events.
Fixes implemented:
- Short-term: increased router threshold and warmed KV prefixes during the incident window; issued customer credit.
- Medium-term: patched billing ingestion to validate idempotency tokens on early-terminated streams (PR merged and deployed 2026-03-12).
- Long-term: engineering backlog items added to: (1) improve backpressure flow to allow graceful drain rather than immediate RESET_STREAM; (2) enhance KV warm-up heuristics for dedicated pools during scheduled batch windows; (3) publish SDK retry guidance and recommended backoff windows for customers.
Follow-ups / action items (owners and ETA):
- ENG-OPS: implement graceful stream-drain flow in router (owner: Ethan Cole, ETA: 2026-04-05).
- PLAT-DEV: KV preheat/runbook for scheduled batch windows (owner: S. Navarro, ETA: 2026-03-28).
- DX/Docs: SDK retry guidance and example configs for dedicated customers (owner: Lena Ortiz, ETA: 2026-03-20).
- FINANCE: reconcile credit in next billing run and confirm final adjustment (owner: M. Deng, ETA: 2026-03-20).
Status: Incident resolved; customer satisfied with remediation and credit. Postmortem published at related_confluence_pages.
payload.summary: MintLance concurrent session stall causing truncated completions and temporary invoice/billing delta during us-east peak

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring tenant-level 429 responses during large fleet rollouts and worker restarts. Behavior appears concentrated during a ~2-6 minute window after a portion of their uploader fleet resumes activity (we see synchronized warmups).

Impact:
- NimbleDocs ingestion pipelines observe 20-40% increased 429s for ~3 minutes after batches of uploader processes restart (~100s of clients).
- Processing latency and backlog grow; customer sees failed items and manual retries.
- Affects production workload (dedicated pool, us-west-2).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-42), prod us-west-2.
- Client SDK: nimble-uploader v1.3.2 (homegrown wrapper that performs exponential backoff with jitter).
- Observed on model routes: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings (mixed).

Steps to reproduce (from customer repro script):
1) Stop 250 uploader workers (simulate rolling deploy).
2) Bring them back up in groups of ~25 with 10s intervals using their orchestration tool.
3) Each worker immediately resumes sending batched requests (~50 concurrent requests each).
4) After ~30-90s the gateway begins returning 429s for the tenant.

Observed behavior:
- 429 rate spikes for tenant key across both generation and embedding routes; per-key token counts indicate burst window exhaustion.
- Rate limiter logs show many short-lived connections with similar timestamps (client-side jitter clustered bursts).
- Server-side token-bucket windows refilled at fixed intervals causing alignment with client bursts.

Expected behavior:
- Smooth admission across restart/warmup period; backoff/jitter should avoid synchronized bursts that exhaust tenant quota.

Initial hypothesis:
- Clients' backoff/jitter algorithm (uniform jitter applied to entire batch) plus coordinated rolling restarts align retries into micro-bursts.
- Tenant-level burst allowance and quota windowing on the rate-limiter are too tight for the customer's dedicated commit pattern, causing transient 429s even though sustained QPS is within contracted capacity.
- Per-route quotas and token-bucket refills are contributing to momentary alignment effects.

Additional notes:
2026-03-05 11:02 - NimbleDocs (Customer): Provided restart schedule, sample request timestamps (2000+), and confirmed they use an internal wrapper that applies uniform jitter at the batch level.
2026-03-06 11:05 - Support (Priya): Shared immediate mitigation steps and recommended client config changes (stagger start and per-worker random delay) while we prepare a server-side soft-fix.
2026-03-07 15:22 - Engineering (Ava Chen): Implemented temporary rate-limiter tweak in control plane to increase per-tenant burst allowance and add smoothing on refill for the dedicated pool. Deployed behind feature flag for NimbleDocs only.
2026-03-08 08:45 - NimbleDocs (Customer): Confirmed drop in transient 429 spikes after the flag was applied; reporting normalization during next rolling deploy. Customer requested a recommended long-term config and SDK guidance.
Findings:
- Token-bucket refill granularity aligned with minute boundary (refill event at 00s) which caused many client requests to arrive right after refill resulting in burst depletion.
- Client-side jitter implementation used per-batch seeding leading to near-simultaneous retries across many workers.
- Dedicated pool quota calculations assume smoothing over longer horizons; short transient bursts exceed burst tokens causing 429s even though 5-min average was within contract.
Telemetry checked:
- Gateway logs: connection timestamps clustered within 10-30s windows across restarted workers.
- Rate-limiter metrics: bucket depth dropped to zero for ~120s during incidents.
- No evidence of serving-runtime OOM or GPU shortage; CPU and GPU utilization remained nominal.
Hypothesis validated by staging repro where adding random per-process startup offsets removed the 429 spike.
Short-term mitigation applied (feature-flagged): increased per-tenant burst tokens from 50 -> 200 and modified refill to smooth over two sub-windows to reduce alignment.
Workarounds provided to customer:
- Stagger worker start with randomized delay (recommended 60-180s spread for 250 workers).
- Update uploader SDK to apply jitter per request rather than per batch and add a low-rate warmup ramp (start at 10% of steady concurrency and ramp over 2-5 minutes).
Long-term actions / follow-ups:
- (ENG) Add a tenant-specific smoothing policy in rate-limiter configurable from Console (ENG-4812).
- (DX) Publish a best-practice KB and a code sample for staggered restarts in our SDK docs (DOCS-129).
- (SRE) Add a metric/alert that flags >20% bucket depletion events in a 1-minute window for dedicated pools.
- (PRODUCT) Expose per-tenant burst config and simulation tool in Console for Dedicated customers.
Status: Mitigation confirmed; customer validated behavior during two subsequent rollouts. Scheduling follow-ups in sprint.
payload.summary: Staggered retry/warmup patterns from client fleet causing tenant-level 429 throttles
