Issue summary: After customer toggled strict-region routing for their tenant, production traffic for the tenant started showing intermittent latency spikes (p50 up by ~60ms, p95 up by ~400ms) and a pattern of 401 -> token refresh -> retry which increases tail latency. Impact: user-facing inference requests (chat streaming and short completion calls) have higher failure rate and slower perceived response for end users. Environment: Dedicated tenant running in eu-west with control-plane pin set to strict-region; some requests observed to be routed to a secondary us-east edge during short control-plane refresh windows. Expected: strict-region should prefer local eu-west edge and not cause auth re-negotiation or cross-region token churn. Actual: during control-plane pin refresh the edge routing flips briefly to a secondary edge which triggers token rotation and auth cache misses leading to additional TLS handshakes and request retries.
1) Tenant has strict-region routing enabled and is pinned to eu-west dedicated pool
2) Trigger a config refresh (simulate by toggling and re-enabling strict-region in console or via API),
3) Send a burst of streaming requests from client SDK that reuses a token scoped to the tenant
4) Observe a subset of requests route to us-east edge, see auth 401s and SDK churn / retries, and increased latency on those requests
2026-03-10T09:12:03Z edge-proxy[eid:edge-8792] WARN request_id=rx-9f2a auth: token validation failed: token-residency-mismatch
2026-03-10T09:12:03Z auth-service[svc-3] INFO token-swap: issued new token for tenant=fin50; issued_at=2026-03-10T09:12:03Z ttl=300s
2026-03-10T09:12:03Z edge-proxy[eid:edge-2911] INFO routing: selected secondary_edge=us-east-1 for tenant fin50 due to pin-refresh-window
trace: tc-20260310-0001 sample-span: handshake+auth 110ms; total-handler 510ms
Initial hypothesis: control-plane's pin refresh window is misaligned with token TTL leading to tokens that encode residency claims no longer matching selected edge during transient routing change.
Observed token change events correlate exactly with times of elevated p50/p95 and with edge selection logs showing temporary selection of us-east edge.
Auth service currently uses short token TTL (5 minutes) and token contains a residency stamp which is validated by the edge. When edge changes, validation fails and edge asks client to refresh.
SDK behaviour: client SDK retries on 401 by fetching a new token and reissuing the request. This is correct but adds extra round-trips if the edge flip happens mid-request.
We confirmed the issue reproduces in a controlled test where we force a pin refresh and stream 50 concurrent requests: ~12% show auth retry path and higher latencies.
No indication of model-serving timeouts or GPU shortage; CPU and GPU metrics on dedicated pool are normal during windows.
Network traces show additional TLS handshakes (full) for the affected requests indicating connection teardown between client and selected edge during the transition window.
Customer (Elena Petrova): We're seeing intermittent user-facing delay spikes and some requests fail with authentication errors right after we change residency policies. Is there a recommended workaround?
Support (Maria Chen): Thanks Elena — we've started an investigation. Can you confirm if your SDK is using token refresh on 401s? Also, do you have a reproducible script to simulate the policy toggle?
Customer (Elena Petrova): Yes the SDK refreshes on 401. We can provide a replay script that toggles the tenant pin every 30s. Will attach privately.
SRE (Olivia Park): We've reproduced with the provided script. Evidence points to a race between control-plane pin rotation and token TTL. Short-term mitigation: we can temporarily increase token TTL or stagger pin refresh to avoid flips during heavy client streams.
Support (Diego Alvarez): Applied mitigation for tenant fin50: increased pin-refresh-stagger to 5s and set control-plane to prefer same-edge for 30s post-refresh. Observed reduction in retries during a 30-minute test window.
Customer (Elena Petrova): After your mitigation we've seen p50 drop back to baseline and no 401s in the last 45 minutes. Thanks. Will keep monitoring from our side.
SRE (Olivia Park): Creating follow-up internal tasks to address root cause: change token/residency contract so tokens are valid across brief edge handoffs and align refresh window with token TTL.
Mitigation applied: pin-refresh-stagger increased for tenant fin50 and control-plane set to prefer sticky-edge for 30s post-refresh. Observed immediate reduction in auth retries and p50/p95 improved in customer tests. Next steps: SRE to implement a control-plane patch to add continuity headers during edge handoff and update token policy so tokens tolerate micro-handoffs. Follow-up internal story created (INT-570) to change default token TTL and add unit tests for handoff window. Customer monitoring to continue; we'll follow up with a post-incident note.
SRE: implement edge continuity header and ensure token validation tolerates short residence mismatch (INT-570)
SRE: increase default token TTL from 300s to 600s for dedicated tenants as an interim safety measure
Engineering: add e2e test that simulates pin refresh during streaming workload
Support: schedule a 1:1 review with FinSight SRE in 48 hours to confirm stability

Impact: Approximately 5-8% of requests for a high-volume rerank route return different top-10 ordering compared to historical baseline; customers notice relevance regressions and occasional 5xx retries. Latency spikes correlate with requests that include small payloads (~64 vectors) versus larger batches.

Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated), prod us-east, service route rerank-v1 pinned to open-rerank-1.1. Ingest pipeline uses SDK-js v2.4.0 on the customer side.

Observed on 2026-03-09 16:34:12 UTC and recurring.
1) Customer sends batched embeddings (payloads of variable shape) via POST /v1/embeddings with header 'Embed-Format: binary_npy' and Content-Type application/octet-stream.
2) Immediately issue rerank call using returned embedding IDs to /v1/rerank with same client.
3) Observe top-k ordering differences compared to a cached baseline response run against same inputs in staging.
4) Re-run with identical inputs but using SDK-js v2.3.1 (previous version) — behavior appears stable.

Note: The customer provided a small repro bundle in S3 referenced in attachments.
Sample log excerpt (redacted):

Issue summary:
Customer reports that when using the TypeScript SDK in streaming mode with function/tool calling enabled, the idempotency metadata (idempotency key/nonce) that the SDK sets on outgoing tool call requests is not being forwarded by our webhook relay to the customer's webhook endpoint. Impact:
- Customers observe duplicate side-effects: third-party webhooks called twice for the same logical tool invocation (e.g., duplicate order creations).
- Appears surface-level: tool call completes, external webhook receives 2 POSTs within <500ms.
Environment:
- StencilAI (dedicated account) on prod-us-east
- SDK: @redwood/sdk-js v2.7.4 (ts build)
- Relay: internal webhook-relay v1.9.0 behind api-gateway
- Model: redwood/gpt-6b, streaming via ws+chunked function_call JSON frames
Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Create a tool that posts to a webhook and requires an idempotency token header (X-Idempotency-Key) to dedupe POSTs.
2) In TS client, start a streaming generate with function_call enabled and include an explicit idempotency value in the tool_call options (sdk sets tool_call.metadata.idempotency_key).
3) Simulate a transient network interruption - disconnect the client briefly and allow the SDK to reconnect and re-send a resume request.
4) Observe webhook endpoint logs: two POSTs for the same tool execution ID but only the second POST contains the idempotency header (first POST lacking the header).
Observed behavior:
- Relay forwards the function_call body and invokes the webhook twice. The first invocation is missing the idempotency header, so the customer's webhook cannot dedupe and executes twice.
Expected behavior:
- Relay should preserve and forward idempotency metadata (either as header X-Idempotency-Key or a predictable webhook payload field) for every invocation of a tool call, including resumptions and replayed stream frames.
Temporary workaround:
- Customer added server-side dedupe by correlating tool_call.payload.order_reference with a store lookup. This mitigates duplicates but requires app changes.
- Recommended short-term: ask customer to enable "require-idempotency-header" on their webhook and reject calls without header (not ideal for them).
Notes: customer provided webhook logs and sample wire captures attached in comments.

Start streaming generate with function_call enabled using @redwood/sdk-js v2.7.4
Induce brief client disconnect to trigger reconnect/resume
Check webhook logs for duplicate POSTs and missing idempotency header on first call
2026-03-09T17:22:38.114Z relay: POST /webhook/invoke tool_call_id=tc_03a4a9 status=200 headers={Content-Type: application/json}
2026-03-09T17:22:38.520Z relay: POST /webhook/invoke tool_call_id=tc_03a4a9 status=200 headers={Content-Type: application/json, X-Idempotency-Key: abc-123}
Customer webhook: 2026-03-09T17:22:38.114 Received POST without X-Idempotency-Key order_ref=ORD-3942
Customer webhook: 2026-03-09T17:22:38.520 Received POST with X-Idempotency-Key: abc-123 order_ref=ORD-3942

Additional notes:

2026-03-12 12:15 - Customer: Acknowledged. Will keep temporary dedupe active and wait for fix. Please advise ETA for patch rollout.

Unit tests missed this scenario because they use non-resume flow

Patch prepared in relay to preserve/propagate tool_call.metadata.idempotency_key as X-Idempotency-Key for all outbound webhook invocations, including replay/resume flows. PR #88 created; integration tests added to cover resume + metadata propagation. Plan: deploy relay v1.9.1 to staging 2026-03-13 and to prod 2026-03-14 after 48h observation. Also working with SDK team to add explicit header mapping utility in @redwood/sdk-js v2.7.5 so customers can configure header name used for idempotency keys.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During the 14:00–15:10 UTC window on 2026-03-13 we observed a stepped increase in 5xx responses from the API Gateway for a subset of requests routed to dedicated pools serving AceroHealth. The increase coincided with an ephemeral-worker rebalance triggered by autoscaler activity and several upstream serving-runtime processes reporting OOMs and graceful shutdowns.

Impact:
- Customer requests returning 502/503/504; visible degradation across both sync generation and streaming endpoints.
- Customer-reported error rate ~18% peak (baseline ~0.6%).
- Some long-lived streaming sessions disconnected without retries succeeding.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east) dedicated pool for AceroHealth (tenant id: ac-7641).
- Autoscaler policy: aggressive scale-in with 5m cooldown.
- Model: gptx-1-large-v2 pinned by customer.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Autoscaler triggers scale-in due to aggregate metric dip at 13:56 UTC.
2) Ephemeral worker rebalance moves several sessions and drains connections from older proxies (14:02 UTC).
3) Serving-runtime observed KV cache eviction pressure and increased GPU memory allocation churn.
4) At 14:05–14:08 UTC multiple runtime workers hit GPU memory fragmentation thresholds and OOM, restarting.
5) API Gateway request fanout to upstreams encounters half-open connections, resulting in 502/503 and some 504 timeouts.

Relevant logs / excerpts:
[apigw] 2026-03-13T14:06:12Z WARN upstream reset for tenant ac-7641 route /v1/generate 502 conn-reset
[runtime] 2026-03-13T14:07:01Z ERROR gpu_allocator OOM while serving request shard=3 model=gptx-1-large-v2 pid=2245
[autoscaler] 2026-03-13T13:58:40Z INFO scale-in initiated from 12->8 replicas (cooldown enforced)

Initial mitigation applied:
- Support routed traffic away from affected dedicated pool to a warmed standby pool (14:12 UTC) which reduced 5xx rate to ~2.2%.
- Disabled aggressive scale-in policy for the pool (toggled to conservative) to prevent immediate reseed.
- Temporarily disabled prefetch eviction on the runtime for this tenant to reduce KV churn.

Current hypothesis:
- Aggressive scale-in caused ephemeral worker rebalance that exacerbated GPU memory fragmentation on a subset of workers; fragmentation led to OOM restarts which made upstreams intermittently unhealthy. API Gateway observed half-open connections and increased retry/backoff which amplified 5xx rates.

Next steps:
- SRE to collect full runtime nvml logs and heap/KV cache eviction traces (run: /opt/infra/bin/collect-runtime-traces --tenant ac-7641).
- Engineering to review GPU allocator changes in PR referenced below for potential regressions.
- Work with product to provide customers an advisory about pinning warm pool sizes or adjusting autoscaler cooldowns until fix is deployed.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 15:05 UTC - Engineering (runtime): Reproduced memory fragmentation locally with synthetic drain test. Confirmed allocator returns could be improved; preparing patch to reduce transient allocations during connection drain.
2026-03-13 15:25 UTC - Support (Aisha Patel): Notified AceroHealth of mitigation steps (traffic reroute, autoscaler policy change). Customer reports partial restoration; they will monitor and escalate if errors reoccur.
2026-03-14 12:00 UTC - Engineering (runtime): Canary results show stable memory metrics and no OOMs over 2h. Plan: schedule rolling hotfix to serving-runtime in next maintenance window (2026-03-15 01:00 UTC).
Temporary mitigations: traffic reroute to standby pool, disabled aggressive scale-in, turned off prefetch eviction for tenant. Long-term: runtime allocator patch to reduce fragmentation during drain and autoscaler tuning; update runbook to detect rebalance-induced OOM patterns. Hotfix scheduled and PR under review.
payload.summary: Afternoon sustained 5xx gradient after ephemeral-worker rebalance and upstream runtime OOMs

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLane reports intermittent long tail latency and completed requests returning 408/504 when sending large prompts via our REST API. Pattern only appears when the customer uploads the request body slowly (their mobile SDK on flaky cellular).

Impact:
- Several long-completion requests from one BrightLane workspace result in 408 at the gateway, followed by client retries that surface as 504 on our side.
- Affects ~2-3% of their generation traffic; visible TTFB spikes and partial streaming sessions closed mid-stream.
- Customer reports degraded UX and session-level errors in production.

Environment:
- Customer tier: self_serve (BrightLane)
- Region: prod (us-east) endpoint: api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Client: BrightLane mobile SDK v1.4.2 over HTTP/1.1, slow uplink (300-800 kbps intermittent)
- Our infra: API Gateway (Nginx fronting ALB), request body buffering enabled for default routes, streaming backend (serving-runtime) using long-lived connections.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Use BrightLane mobile SDK to send request with ~200kb prompt using chunked transfer / slow upload throttle to ~400 kbps.
2) Observe request stalls during upload for 6-12s, then gateway returns 408 Request Timeout or the connection is closed.
3) Client retries; second attempt sometimes gets 504 from our runtime after partial stream.

Observed logs / traces:
- API gateway access logs show "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)" for a subset of requests where request_time > 10s.
- Nginx error log lines referencing "client timed out (while reading client request body)".
- Serving-runtime side traces show no corresponding receive for some request ids (request body never fully delivered), KV cache warmup sometimes aborted.
- Customer provided packet capture showing slow chunk cadence and multiple small TCP segments with delayed ACKs.

Immediate workaround suggested to customer:
- Increase client-side upload concurrency or buffer request client-side so the SDK sends in a single burst instead of prolonged chunking.
- Customer temporarily increased client TCP keepalive interval to avoid connection tear-down; partial improvement reported.

Requested action / acceptance criteria:
- Confirm whether the API gateway buffer policy (wait for full request body) can be tuned to tolerate slow client uploads without closing upstream long-lived streaming connections.
- Produce a fix or configuration change that reduces 408s for slow uploads without degrading throughput for normal traffic.

Hypotheses tested:
- H1: API Gateway Nginx is configured to buffer the entire request body before proxying; slow uploads cause client_read_timeout and Nginx aborts (supported by logs).
- H2: When Nginx closes without forwarding, serving-runtime sees orphaned or partial sessions leading to downstream 504s on retry.
- H3: ALB idle timeouts and TCP keepalive mismatch between client proxy and ALB amplify the window where partial uploads are dropped.

What we've done so far:
- Reproduced with an internal test harness throttling request body upload. Observed identical Nginx "reading client request body" timeouts at ~10s.
- Verified our Nginx config uses client_body_timeout=10s and proxy_request_buffering=on for the route.
- Scoped incidence: primarily an issue when client upload stalls >8-10s; not correlated with model size beyond payload size.
- Ran a canary with proxy_request_buffering=off for a small percentage of traffic for the route; reduced 408s for slow-upload traffic but increased memory pressure on gateway pods by ~7%.
1) Coordinate with infra to roll a staged config change: increase client_body_timeout to 30s and selectively disable proxy_request_buffering for streaming routes for customers that opt-in (feature flag).
2) Add telemetry to count requests that exceed 5s upload time and correlate with 408/504 outcomes.
3) Discuss long-term: consider adaptive buffering that tails off buffering for clients with telemetry indicating slow upload patterns.
4) Follow up with BrightLane to test client-side SDK update as a short-term mitigation.
payload.summary: Slow client upload interacts with API gateway request buffering leading to 408 and downstream 504s for long completions

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BrightLens Analytics) observed mixed model outputs for a tenant pinned to gptx-3.7-quant during a rolling mirror prewarm. Traffic that should have remained bound to the pinned variant intermittently routed to the mirror candidate (redwood-rev1) and to a degraded fallback variant. Impact: downstream scoring pipeline received inconsistent embeddings and completions, causing elevated false positives in their analytics dashboard and a temporary billing spike due to requests replayed to fallback variants.

Impact:
- ~4% of requests for tenant T-7243 returned responses from the mirror or fallback variant during 2026-03-10 11:12-11:47 UTC window.
- Customer reported incorrect analytics summaries and asked for credits.

Environment:
- Production tenant on Dedicated capacity in us-east-1.
- Rolling mirror (traffic mirroring to redwood-rev1) was started by BrightLens via Console rollout API.

Observed behavior:
- Explicit tenant version pin present in route metadata, but orchestrator epoch handoff produced two competing route snapshots. Some edge workers evaluated the older snapshot while orchestrator completed commit, creating a transient cohort split. Requests from the same session sometimes hit different model variants and triggered fallback logic.

Expected behavior:
- During rolling mirror/prewarm we expect session affinity + explicit pin to enforce single-variant binding until an explicit promote is completed or pin is removed. No mixing of variants for pinned sessions.

1) On dedicated cluster in us-east-1, create a controlled tenant and pin to model gptx-3.7-quant.
2) Start a rolling mirror/prewarm to redwood-rev1 with mirror weight 10% using the Console rollout API and enable prewarm probes.
3) Simulate steady traffic from a tenant session (keepalive stream + intermittent short requests).
4) Trigger orchestrator snapshot replacement (force a config refresh) while prewarm is in progress to reproduce epoch overlap.
5) Observe response model variant ids returned in edge logs and platform trace — verify if any session received mixed variants.
2026-03-10T11:13:02Z EDGE[east-01] session_id=abc123 variant=gptx-3.7-quant route_epoch=512 request_id=rx-7a9
2026-03-10T11:13:12Z ORCH orchestrator.commit start epoch=513 prev_epoch=512 commit_id=commit-1984
2026-03-10T11:13:13Z EDGE[east-01] session_id=abc123 variant=redwood-rev1 route_epoch=513 request_id=rx-7aa
2026-03-10T11:13:15Z SERVING runtime fallback invoked variant=redwood-deg01 reason=prewarm-timeout request_id=rx-7ab
2026-03-10T11:14:05Z PROXY[vpc-ingress] retried upstream due to 502; original request_id=rx-7ac
Initial hypothesis: snapshot replacement race between orchestrator and edge snapshot cache TTL caused split-consensus across edge fleet.
Edge cache TTL configured to 2s; orchestrator commit window overlapped prewarm probe bursts leading to some workers loading new snapshot mid-session.
Observed edge logs show consistent epoch flip from 512->513 within ~1s for some workers but not others — indicates non-atomic snapshot activation across region shard boundaries.
Fallbacks triggered when a worker evaluated compatibility checks (model shape/tokenizer) against the new route and fell back to degraded variant. This suggests compatibility policy evaluation was applied atomically with snapshot load, but session affinity check used earlier in-memory token that didn't reconcile.
No evidence of auth or cookie mutation from customer side. Traffic patterns align with orchestrator commit timeline. Related PR that touched snapshot activation order: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1984 (still under review).
2026-03-10T12:05Z - Evan Park (assignee): Acknowledged. Reproducing in staging with identical rollout sequence to validate snapshot activation behavior.
2026-03-10T13:22Z - SRE oncall (Marisol Ortega): Found shard-level delay on snapshot propagation to edge pool 3; TTL expiry didn't trigger immediate refresh because cache heartbeat coincided with commit window.
2026-03-10T14:36Z - Aisha Kumar (reporter): Customer confirmed mixed responses for a 30-minute window and provided sample request_ids. Customer requests mitigation and billing credit consideration.
2026-03-11T09:18Z - Eng (Diego Ramos): Confirmed a window where snapshot activation order (compatibility checks then affinity binding) produced transient incoherence. Preparing a patch to reorder activation so affinity binding occurs after snapshot fully materializes.
2026-03-11T16:02Z - Support (Evan Park): Shared temporary mitigation steps with customer: pause mirror weight, drain affected shard, and apply an orchestrator commit with a quiesce window. Customer accepted mitigation and asked for timeline for permanent fix.
Workaround applied 2026-03-11 16:35Z: paused mirror traffic and performed orchestrator quiesce commit to force atomic snapshot rollout for shard pool 3.
Permanent fix in progress: reorder snapshot activation sequence so that session-affinity binding and explicit pin checks only evaluate after snapshot fully materializes across all regional shards. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1992
Customer impact mitigation: issued pro-rated credit for the 35-minute window and created follow-up billing ticket FIN-8842.
Status: monitoring post-workaround for 24h; no further mixed-variant reports from BrightLens.
1) Deploy orchestrator patch PR#1992 to staging -> canary -> prod (owner: Diego Ramos).
2) Add deterministic quiesce window option to Console rollout API (owner: product infra).
3) Update runbook to include shard-level snapshot propagation checks and a prewarm quiesce recommendation (owner: SRE).
4) Verify telemetry for session-affinity mismatches and add alert rule if >0.1% of pinned sessions see mixed variants for >5m.

Issue summary: Customers using structured JSON ("structured_output" mode) report large long-tail latencies (seconds to tens of seconds) when calling the streaming API under high concurrency. Impact: production traffic for a dedicated customer (NoteWave Labs) experienced 95th/99th percentile increases; real-time enrichment widgets timed out and degraded UX.

Environment: prod us-east (dedicated pool for NoteWave Labs). Occurs more often during traffic spikes (~500 concurrent streams). Models: rw-opt-13b-quantized primarily, but reproducible on open-7b-compat.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure a streaming chat request with structured_output enabled and a JSON schema that includes a final array field and optional trailing metadata field.
2) Send 400-600 concurrent streaming sessions with ~300 token generated responses each.
3) Observe that most requests stream tokens fine but a subset hangs for additional 5–30s waiting for the final chunk to arrive/parse.

Observed behavior: A fraction (~0.5–2%) of streams stall during finalization. Server-side logs show the model generating the final tokens and the runtime emitting final chunks, but the structured parser appears to block on stream termination/aggregate parsing. CPU on serving nodes shows short spikes on the parser thread; backlog on the runtime's completion queue increases. Requests eventually finish or time out at 30s.

Expected behavior: Streaming responses with structured_output should finalize within normal token latency bounds; the parser should incrementally validate/emit structured pieces without blocking other streams.

Customer impact: NoteWave Labs reported elevated error rates in their real-time UI; they were forced to route to a lower-fidelity non-structured mode as a workaround. Business impact is material for their product demos this week.

Temporary workaround: Disable structured_output or drop the final optional metadata field; reduce concurrency per client. Workaround reduces correctness guarantees for the customer but restores latency.

Enable structured_output with a schema containing a final array and optional metadata
Spawn 400-600 concurrent streaming requests against dedicated pool in us-east
Generate ~300 tokens per session and monitor stream completion times
Observe 95th/99th percentile long-tail delays and occasional 30s timeouts
2026-03-13T14:12:08Z runtime: stream-id=abc123 emitted final_chunk (len=128)
2026-03-13T14:12:08Z parser: stream-id=abc123 waiting on termination token, parsing stalled 12s
Node metrics: serving-node-7 cpu_parser_thread spike to 92% at 14:12:09Z
Trace: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/0f3a9b (sample with blocked finalization)
Initial hypothesis: incremental parser is performing a blocking full-JSON validation on final chunk under certain buffer boundary conditions.
SRE observed parser CPU spikes correlated with backlog in completion queue; queuing increases latency for subsequent streams.
Customer reproduction: NoteWave confirmed stable repro when sending schemas with final arrays > 50 items and optional trailing metadata fields.
Able to reproduce locally with load generator; enabling single-threaded parser reduces contention but does not eliminate stalls (indicates pathological code path).
No evidence of model generation stalls; model emits tokens on expected schedule.
Short-term: recommend disabling structured_output for NoteWave's high-concurrency endpoints or simplify schema (remove large final arrays).
SRE will provision a temporary extra serving pool for NoteWave to lower per-node concurrency while fix is developed.
ENG to triage parser implementation: add incremental/streaming-validate path that avoids full-document blocking on final chunk parsing.
Add targeted unit/integration tests with concurrent streams and large final arrays to CI.
Target: hotfix to runtime parser in 72 hours, followed by a canary rollout to dedicated pools.
(pending) Engineering assigned to implement non-blocking finalization for structured parser. Temporary pool and customer workaround applied on 2026-03-13 18:00Z.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-13: Customer NoteWave reports intermittent 30s timeouts when using structured_output in streaming mode. Escalating to SRE/ENG.
SRE (Luis Ortega) 2026-03-13: Reproduced at load; parser thread CPU correlates with blocked streams. Provisioning temp pool for customer.
Customer (Elena Ruiz, NoteWave) 2026-03-13: We see the UI freeze; switching off structured_output clears it — would like ETA on fix.
ENG (Priya Nair) 2026-03-14: Investigating parser code path. Suspect boundary condition when final array + trailing metadata present; working on patch to allow incremental emit/validation.
SRE (Luis Ortega) 2026-03-14: Temporary dedicated pool added (pool-id: tw-pool-22) and routing updated for NoteWave. Observed immediate reduction in 99th percentile latency.
payload.summary: Structured-output final-chunk blocking under high concurrency causes long-tail inference latency

Issue summary: Customer reports duplicated external webhook/tool/function invocations when using our Python SDK with a custom HTTP transport that emits chunked transfer-encoding. The duplicated executions happen only after a transient connection failure when the SDK's background retry thread re-sends the request.

Impact: NimbleDocs sees duplicate downstream jobs (billing+side-effects) for a subset (~2%) of long-running function calls. This is causing data duplication and customer-visible incorrect state.

Environment: NimbleDocs is on a Dedicated plan in us-east using Python SDK v1.8.2, custom requests.Session adapter that enables HTTP/2 multiplexing and chunked body streaming via iter_bytes. Edge sits behind an internal sidecar that rewrites some headers for routing.

Expected behavior: Retries should be safe and idempotent when an idempotency header is present; duplicate webhook/tool invocations should be prevented by the SDK or upstream dedupe.

Actual behavior: After a mid-request connection reset, SDK retries the request and downstream webhook receives two invocations with different idempotency-header representations. Edge/proxy treats them as separate requests and forwards both to the customer's job queue.

1) Create a Python client using Python SDK v1.8.2 and pass a custom requests.Session with an HTTP/2-capable transport and chunked streaming body (yielding small chunks).
2) Call the API with a function/tool that triggers an external webhook callback (long-running: 20-30s). Include X-Idempotency-Key header generated per logical operation.
3) Simulate a transient connection reset from the edge (tcp reset or short-lived proxy restart) during the streaming of the request body.
4) Observe client background retry logic: SDK re-sends the request (re-using session/transport) from a retry worker thread.
5) Inspect downstream webhook logs: two separate requests arrive; idempotency header values differ in byte representation (one split across chunk boundary), and the edge/proxy does not normalize them, so dedupe fails.
2026-03-09T14:12:04Z DEBUG python-sdk.transport: sending chunk size=1024 idempotency=XGK-abc123
2026-03-09T14:12:04Z WARN  python-sdk.transport: connection reset by peer during request-stream
2026-03-09T14:12:04Z INFO  python-sdk.retry_worker: scheduling retry attempt=1 request_id=req-34f2
2026-03-09T14:12:06Z DEBUG edge-proxy: received headers: host=n-docs-router x-idempotency-key="XGK-abc
2026-03-09T14:12:06Z DEBUG edge-proxy: received headers: (continuation) 123" chunked=true
2026-03-09T14:12:06Z INFO  webhook-nimble: job enqueued idempotency_key="XGK-abc123" source=req-34f2
2026-03-09T14:12:07Z INFO  webhook-nimble: job enqueued idempotency_key="XGK-abc-123" source=req-34f2-retry
2026-03-10 09:20 UTC - Support initial triage: reproduced with NimbleDocs test harness running local edge-proxy (sidecar) and custom chunk sizes. Duplicates observed when header bytes get split across chunk boundary and edge-proxy does not reassemble/normalize header canonicalization.
2026-03-10 12:45 UTC - Eng (Priya) note: SDK retry worker reuses the same transport and replays the request; requests library will stream chunks again. When the header is large or contains characters that result in splitting (some proxies limit header line length), the proxy may apply header folding which changed representation.
2026-03-11 02:10 UTC - Networking: Edge sidecar logs show header folding (RFC 7230 continuation) on h2-to-h1 translation. Downstream webhook endpoint treats the two different representations as distinct idempotency keys (one has an inserted hyphen during reassembly in our test).
Hypothesis: Combination of chunked transfer, custom transport, and edge/proxy header folding leads to byte-level idempotency-key mutation across the retry boundary. Downstream dedupe based on literal header string fails, causing duplicate processing.
Attempted mitigations run: 1) Reproduced with standard requests.Session (no custom transport) - no duplicates. 2) Reproduced with small chunk size and HTTP/2 prior-knowledge - duplicates. 3) Forcing SDK to send idempotency key in body (instead of header) prevents duplication but breaks some customers' orchestration.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Hector Alvarez): Hi NimbleDocs team — thanks for the report and repro steps. We're prioritizing this as P1 due to downstream side-effects. Can you share the exact custom transport code (or a minimized snippet) and an example idempotency key format you generate?
2026-03-10 11:30 - Customer (NimbleDocs - engineering): Sent snippet (attached in support portal). Idempotency key is a 12-char alphanumeric token (example: XGK-abc123). We confirmed behavior only on a dedicated edge setup that rewrites headers for routing. Using the public hosted API doesn't reproduce.
2026-03-10 13:05 - Support (Priya Nair): Reproduced locally with NimbleDocs snippet. Raising to runtime/edge team for advice on header canonicalization. Adding labels and linking to similar routing tickets.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 16:22 - Support (Priya Nair): Workaround tested: customer can set SDK flag 'idempotency_in_body=true' to place the token in JSON payload (server-side dedupe also checks payload). This prevents duplicates for their workflow. We documented steps and recommended short-term config change while we build a fix.
Workaround applied: NimbleDocs toggled idempotency_in_body flag to true (server accepts fallback payload key). Root cause: header byte fragmentation across chunk boundaries combined with edge h2->h1 translation that performs header folding/continuation, leading to mutated idempotency-key values. Fix plan: 1) Short-term: ship SDK update v1.8.3 that ensures idempotency header is sent as a single header frame (avoid chunked header emission) and adds optional header canonicalization helper. 2) Mid-term: edge-proxy change to normalize idempotency header (trim, remove inserted continuation markers) during translation. 3) Long-term: support canonical idempotency token in both header and payload with server-side normalized dedupe. Follow-ups: PRs created and tests added to SDK integration suite and edge translation unit tests.
SDK: small fix to ensure header emitted atomically in streaming path (PR 4123)
Edge: add canonicalization step for X-Idempotency-Key during h2->h1 translation
Create regression test in integration lab that simulates chunked header splitting
- Repro harness: use provided NimbleDocs snippet with adjustable chunk size; validate against local edge sidecar built from latest main.
- Consider normalizing idempotency key matching on the server: trim whitespace, collapse continuations, and optionally strip non-alphanumeric separators (configurable).
- Backport SDK fix to 1.7.x line for customers on older pinned versions.
payload.summary: Python SDK + custom transport (chunked) causes idempotency header split and duplicate webhook function-call

comments: 2026-03-10T11:05:00Z Hypothesis: ephemeral keys cause per-key warmups + health-check probes from the ingestion library to increment tenant-level counters (health probe stamps), accelerating aggregate consumption and creating 'invisible' accounting that isn't shown in per-key Console views.
payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports unexpected 429 throttles across multiple API keys belonging to the same top-level tenant and subaccounts during a scheduled backfill and real-time traffic spike. Impact: Production ingestion jobs intermittently fail with 429s, downstream feature extraction jobs delayed ~20-40 minutes, and customer reported potential SLA breach. Environment: prod, us-east-1, multiple API keys created under a single org with two subaccounts (ingest, realtime). Observed behavior: During a coordinated backfill (500 parallel workers) + burst of realtime chat sessions, several short-lived API keys and long-lived keys saw immediate 429 responses despite per-key quotas appearing available in Console. Expected behavior: Per-key quotas should allow parallel usage up to configured per-key limits when tenant-level aggregate is not exhausted.
1) Create a top-level tenant with two subaccounts and generate 4 API keys (2 long-lived, 2 ephemeral).
2) Start a backfill with 500 parallel workers issuing embedding batches (batch size 32) spread across 2 long-lived keys.
3) Simultaneously start 200 short-lived chat sessions using ephemeral keys that are rotated every minute.
4) Observe 429s beginning at T+30s of the spike and continuing for several minutes even though per-key dashboards show token buckets not fully depleted.
2026-03-10 10:24 - Initial triage by Support: verified 429s and captured sample request IDs (req_4a7f...).
2026-03-10 10:40 - SRE pulled rate-limiter metrics: tenant aggregate token bucket drained rapidly due to high concurrency from both backfill workers and many ephemeral key creations. Per-key buckets were not the limiting factor; tenant-level bucket was the bottleneck.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:35 - Reproduced in staging with synthetic traffic: rotating ephemeral keys at 1-min TTL + 300 parallel workers consumed tenant burst tokens much faster than anticipated and caused 429s for stable keys despite their visible buckets being non-empty.
2026-03-10 11:50 - Observed TTL collision: ephemeral key issuance triggered short connection handshakes that are charged at request start (prefix tokens) and do not always surface in per-key token counters due to aggregation windowing in the Console.
Support (Aisha): Thanks for the report. We can see 429s and sampled request IDs. Sharing logs and escalating to SRE for quota accounting review. (2026-03-10 10:29)
Customer (DataWeave - Javier): This is blocking nightly backfills. Console shows per-key limits ok; we need explanation of why tenant-level throttles occur. (2026-03-10 10:32)
SRE (Daniel): Investigating aggregate bucket behavior. Initial metrics point to tenant bucket exhaustion. Asking customer about ephemeral key rotation pattern and worker concurrency. (2026-03-10 10:45)
Customer (DataWeave - Javier): Ephemeral keys are rotated every 60s by our autoscaler; workers are short-lived. We also have a health-check that calls /v1/health every new session start. (2026-03-10 10:48)
SRE (Daniel): Confirmed health-checks + ephemeral key churn together cause rapid drain of tenant burst tokens. Proposed immediate mitigation: increase tenant burst allowance for DataWeave by 3x for 4 hours while we advise on config changes. (2026-03-10 11:15)
Support (Aisha): Applied temporary quota raise. Customer confirmed reduced 429s. Follow-up tasks assigned to Engineering for console UX clarifications and documentation updates. (2026-03-10 11:30)
Engineering (Priya - Rate Limiter): Added notes to a follow-up PR to expose tenant-level accounting and show ephemeral key warmup costs in Console. PR referenced below. (2026-03-11 09:22)
Customer (DataWeave - Javier): Verified backfills completed after mitigation, will adopt recommended warmup and key reuse patterns. Thanks. (2026-03-11 12:01)
Tenant-level aggregate token bucket was exhausted due to a combination of high parallel embedding backfill and many ephemeral key creations that trigger health-check and session-start charge events. The Console displayed per-key counters with slight aggregation lag and did not surface the immediate tenant-level burst accounting, causing a visibility gap.
Short term: Granted temporary tenant burst quota increase for 4 hours and advised customer to pause ephemeral key rotation during large backfills. Long term: Engineering to (1) make tenant-level accounting visible in Console, (2) adjust health-check accounting to not count lightweight probes toward burst tokens, and (3) publish guidance for ephemeral key patterns and warmup best practices. Customer confirmed recovery.
payload.summary: Clarify aggregate tenant quota behavior for subaccounts and why concurrent subkey requests return 429s

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightWrite Labs reports repeated occurrences where Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams appear to receive interleaved 'system' messages from a different conversation and the final paragraph of the assistant response is missing. This happens after a network path migration (cellular->wifi or carrier multipath) which triggers a multipath handoff and session rebind.

Impact:
- Customer-facing LLM responses occasionally contain unrelated system messages mid-stream and lose the final closing paragraph (important for code blocks and policy footers).
- Affects a subset of long-running streams under prod us-east-1 for the customer's dedicated pool.
- Reproducible for ~6% of handoffs observed over the last 24h for this customer.

Environment:
- Prod: dedicated GPU pool (dedicated tier, BrightWrite account) in us-east-1.
- Edge: our edge-sidecar fleet (node pool es-rtf-us-east).
- Client: mobile web (PWA) with SSE fallback; network path migrations tested via Charles proxy.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long generation (800-1200 token output) via SSE to rw-chat-v1 pinned on dedicated pool.
2) While streaming, trigger a network handoff (IPv6->IPv4 multipath or carrier switch).
3) Client reconnects and SSE receives a resume frame.
4) Stream resumes but contains an interleaved 'system' message and the last 1-2 paragraphs are missing.

Observed behavior:
- The stream shows a short run of tokens from a different recent session (system/assistant metadata), then resumes with the correct content but truncates the final closing paragraph.
- No 5xx from the serving runtime; gateway logs show two different worker IDs returning chunks for the same session-id during the handoff window.

Expected behavior:
- Exactly one backend worker continues the session after handoff; no mixing of content. The resumed stream should contain the full closing paragraphs.

Temporary workaround:
- Customer was advised to prefer websocket fallback for long-running streams while we investigate, and to set shorter keepalive probes on their mobile SDK to reduce probability of multipath.

2026-03-10 09:12 - Customer (BrightWrite support) - Report: 'We see corrupted footers and occasionally stray system messages mid-stream after users switch networks.' Included client-side logs and packet capture.
2026-03-10 09:40 - Support (Maria Gomez) - Acknowledged. Opened SUP-741258, asked for example request IDs; provided request ids: req-20260310-87a3, req-20260310-91b4. Escalating to SRE oncall.
2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Thomas Li) - Initial triage: saw two different worker IDs (worker-12 and worker-47) both stream-sending chunks within 150ms for same session-id during path migration. Gateway logs: 'session_lookup: cache_miss -> bind_to_worker(worker-47)'. Hypothesis: session mapping rebind race when ephemeral mapping is freed and reused during multipath stitch.
2026-03-10 13:22 - Engineer (Priya Sharma) - Reproduced locally with simulated multipath. Observed sidecar mapping table eviction at ~30s, and rebind code uses the ephemeral session token plus client-ip to key mapping; on path migration client-ip changed triggering a new bind before we drained previous worker's final buffer. Creating a patch to add a monotonic session epoch and drain handshake during rebind.
2026-03-11 02:15 - Engineer (Priya Sharma) - Deployed hotfix to edge-sidecar (v2.14.1) behind feature flag: enforce session epoch check and require previous worker to signal 'handoff-complete' or wait max 500ms before binding new worker. Rollout initiated to canary nodes in us-east-1.
2026-03-12 08:30 - Support (Maria Gomez) - Customer ran a controlled test and reported no interleaved system messages across 120 handoffs. Closing verification pending at 24h monitoring window.
Logs show that during multipath rebind the gateway sometimes rehashed session keys and immediately bound the session-id to a new worker while the old worker still had in-flight token buffers. The sidecar's session map eviction policy returned the mapping slot quickly; a new session epoch was not asserted in client resume frames so two workers treated resume as authoritative. Root cause: session binding was keyed insufficiently (ephemeral token + client-ip) and did not require a monotonic epoch or a drain handshake. The hotfix enforces an epoch in resume frames and a short drain window.
Referenced traces: trace-20260310-87a3 (worker-12 lastWrite at t, worker-47 firstWrite at t+120ms)
Impact estimate: affected ~0.5% of total handoffs cluster-wide, higher for clients undergoing IP family change.
Deployed fix in edge-sidecar v2.14.1 (commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-sidecar/commit/3a7f2b9). Fix details:
- Require monotonic session_epoch on resume frames and reject resumes with older epochs.
- Add a negotiated 'drain-ack' handshake: old worker must ack final buffer or max-wait 500ms before new bind.
- Add observability: 'handoff_conflict' metric and per-session handoff_trace_id in logs.
Rollout: canary us-east-1 -> full us-east within 3 hours. Post-deployment monitoring for 48h showed no recurrence for BrightWrite and cohort tests down to <0.05% handoff anomalies.
Follow-up actions: 1) Update streaming runbook with handoff mitigation steps. 2) Add integration test covering IPv6->IPv4 multipath rebind. 3) Consider increasing default drain-wait to 1s for high-latency mobile clients (RFC to product).
payload.summary: SSE session rebind to incorrect backend during multipath handoff leads to interleaved system messages and clipped closing paragraph

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightPost Health enabled an adaptive-batching profile alongside an INT8 quantization profile last night for a high-throughput route. Since then they report intermittent correctness drops (short hallucinations in structured outputs) and elevated p95/p99 latency spikes. No full 5xx outage, but a measurable degradation in tail latency and output accuracy for production traffic.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests for the affected API route show schema mismatches or truncated fields compared to baseline tests.
- p95 increased from 120ms to 520ms; p99 spiked to ~1.4s intermittently.
- Customer is on Dedicated with reserved GPU pool; business impact: downstream clinical alerts delayed.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity; prod | us-east region
- Route: /v1/generate/structured-alert
- Model pinned at redwood-open-7b-int8 (variant enabled via quant profile); fallback variant redwood-open-7b-ptq available
- Recent changes: adaptive-batching policy (aggressive max-batch-size + dynamic-queueing) + INT8 quant profile staged at 03:00 UTC 2026-03-13

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send 10k representative production requests to /v1/generate/structured-alert over 30 minutes.
2) Compare structured output schema pass rate vs snapshot from 2026-03-12.
3) Observe p95 and p99 latency deltas and intermittent truncated fields in JSON output.

Logs & Telemetry attached by customer:
- Sample request/response pairs included below in comments.
- Trace IDs: trace-20260313-07a9ef, trace-20260313-0b4d12

Requested outcome:
- A safe, stepwise rollback plan the customer can follow that minimizes live-request loss and provides a traffic-split fallback while engineering confirms root cause.
- If feasible, an automated toggle command or console steps the customer can use to ramp back to baseline without purging KV caches unnecessarily.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 09:05 - Customer (BrightPost): Provided two failing responses; one shows truncated JSON field 'clinical_note' and one with schema mismatch. Customer requests a non-disruptive fallback to previous quant profile while retaining batching settings if possible.
Telemetry: correlated latency spikes with times when batches exceeded 48 tokens and when adaptive-batcher coalesced heterogeneous requests (short + long sequences) into single batches. Kernel logs show a higher rate of fallback executions on the INT8 execution path (approx 0.8% -> 3.7% fallback invocations). Accuracy: post-quantization token probabilities shifted in specific tokens that generate structured delimiters, leading to truncation of trailing fields. No evidence of disk or network issues.
Repro: Small-scale replay of problematic trace (n=500) reproduced p95 increase when quant profile was active; disabling quant profile on the same host removed truncation behavior and reduced p95 by ~260ms.
Hypotheses: 1) INT8 kernels interacting with batching ordering produce occasional decode stalls/truncation. 2) Aggressive adaptive-batching increases effective sequence packing leading to edge-case tokenization timing that stresses the INT8 path.
Next steps: recommend stepwise rollback prioritizing correctness: demote quant profile per-host, then reduce adaptive-batcher max-batch-size, with traffic-split to fallback PTQ variant while telemetry is observed.
Planned mitigation steps provided to customer and ops: 1) Create a 90/10 traffic-split pushing 90% to fallback model redwood-open-7b-ptq and 10% to current INT8 path for 20 minutes. 2) On tenant's dedicated pool, demote INT8 quant profile to 'staged' on one instance group using optimizer-toggle --tenant brightpost --group ig-1 --quant-profile staged (ops-only). 3) Monitor p95/p99 and schema-pass rate for 15 minutes; if stable, progressively increase traffic migration in 10% increments every 10 minutes until 100% on PTQ. 4) If customer needs quicker rollback, run optimizer-toggle --tenant brightpost --force-quant-off which reverts quantization immediately but preserves batch cache. 5) If latency persists after quant demote, reduce adaptive-batcher max-batch-size to 8 and set dynamic_queue=false for the route. 6) Engineering to open root cause PR for INT8 kernel ordering and schedule a non-production repro and patch.
Follow-up: Engineering will test a quant-kernel fix; customer to be kept informed via thread. Ticket to be updated with postmortem link once fix merges.
payload.summary: Stepwise revert and traffic-fallback for correctness and latency regressions after enabling adaptive-batching + INT8 profile

comments: 2026-03-10T09:34:00Z Aisha Khan: Triage: Customer reported 502s and stalled streams. Captures requested; escalated to SRE and runtime teams.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 502 errors from the control plane and stalled model artifact downloads on their private deployment. Failures coincide with long-lived gRPC/HTTP2 connections used for artifact retrieval and serving node KV sync.

Impact:
- Artifact downloads (presigned URL -> S3 behind their egress path) fail with 502/ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR roughly every 15-30 minutes for a subset (~6%) of requests.
- Long-lived gRPC streams to serving nodes pause for 10–60s then recover, causing request latency spikes and several downstream user-facing errors.
- Affects production workloads for Neptune Analytics' private VPC deployment in us-west-2; customer reports increased error budget burn and consumer impact.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering -> customer on-prem MPLS -> WAN optimizer -> internet egress)
- Redwood control-plane + serving nodes in us-west-2 (prod)
- TLS: mutual TLS to control plane, ALPN h2 enabled for artifact fetches and gRPC traffic

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a model artifact download (large model shard ~350MB) via private deployment artifact fetch flow.
2) Open long-lived streaming session against serving nodes (simulate sustained inference with keepalive=15s).
3) Observe occasional 502/HTTP2 protocol errors and pauses in streaming throughput after ~10-30 minutes.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Control plane logs show repeated HTTP2_ERROR (PROTOCOL_ERROR) and RST_STREAM events during artifact GETs.
- Serving runtime metrics show periods of stalled outbound bytes and increased retransmits on TCP layer reported by the kernel.
- Packet captures (pcap from customer egress appliance) show out-of-order segments and reordered HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE frames where the window sequence appears inverted relative to stream data.
- WAN optimizer (third-party device) logs indicate aggressive re-segmentation and L7 buffering under bursts.

Investigation notes / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: WAN optimizer is reassembling/re-segmenting and replaying HTTP/2 frames in a way that inverts WINDOW_UPDATE ordering causing the receiver to enforce a protocol error.
- Hypothesis B: Intermediate box performs TCP-level rewriting (zero-window or MSS clamping) and triggers reordering leading to HTTP/2 flow control inversion.
- Hypothesis C: Path MTU/MSS and on-path buffering combine with parallel TCP sessions and selective ACKs causing TCP-level reordering large enough to violate expected HTTP/2 stream window semantics.

Evidence collected so far:
- PCAPs correlate customer-side reordering with time of observed 502s.
- Replaying packets in a lab (with a WAN optimizer in the path) reproduces the HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE inversion and RST_STREAM.
- Metrics show increased kernel retransmits and occasional dup-ACK spikes during incidents.

Temporary mitigations and workarounds:
- Customer disabled WAN optimizer HTTP/2/L7 acceleration mode last night and reported a drop in error rate (preliminary).
- Suggested temporary policy: route artifact downloads via an alternate egress path that bypasses the appliance (customer tested via split-eDNS and reported lower failure rate).

Next steps / action items:
- SRE: request full pcap for the failing time window and share a sanitized excerpt with runtime team (actioned).
- Networking: validate MSS/MTU settings across customer transit and ensure no clamping below 1280.
- Runtime: add additional defensive handling for out-of-order WINDOW_UPDATE sequences in the artifact-fetch HTTP2 client to avoid immediate RST_STREAM on borderline cases (low-risk patch candidate).
- Customer-facing: coordinate a maintenance window with Neptune to temporarily bypass the WAN optimizer for a 24h validation window.

Resolution: ongoing. Temporary bypass appears to reduce occurrences; root cause likely due to WAN optimizer re-sequencing HTTP/2 frames. Permanent remediation requires either appliance configuration change or runtime tolerance improvements.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent incomplete final metadata and a silent trailing paragraph when their websocket or SSE stream resumes after an edge failover/auth cookie rotation. The response body contains the content tokens but the final metadata envelope (terminal JSON object containing stream-level fields like 'id'/'usage'/'choices' metadata) is sometimes missing or cut and the last paragraph is not emitted, causing the client SDK to throw a parse error or appear to hang.

Impact:
- Several Inkwell Media users see a parse error or a UI spinner after a reconnect; last paragraph (summary) often never appears.
- Occurs ~0.5-1% of long-running streaming sessions for this customer during peak traffic.
- Affects critical editor flows where the final paragraph contains a license blurb.

Environment:
- Customer: Inkwell Media (dedicated account)
- Region: us-east
- Model: redwood-3b-v1 pinned
- Path: Streaming via websocket upgrade (wss) through edge-proxy cluster with header rewrite and cookie rotation set by customer-auth service
- Client: Browser webapp using Redwood JS SDK v1.4.2 behind corporate NAT/proxy

Steps to reproduce (attempted):
1) Start long-form streaming generation via websocket from the customer app with conversation payload > 800 tokens.
2) While streaming, trigger an auth cookie rotation (customer does so via SSO refresh) or simulate an edge failover by cycling one of the edge-proxy instances.
3) Client reconnects and requests resume using the session token; streaming continues but the final metadata object is missing or truncated and the closing paragraph is not emitted.

Observed behavior:
- Streaming tokens continue to arrive, and the last content tokens look complete, but no terminal metadata envelope (closing JSON with 'id' and aggregated usage) is present.
- Client SDK keeps waiting for the terminal event and does not surface the final paragraph. In some cases the SDK receives a small number of trailing bytes that appear to be a gzip fragment or partial header left by the edge-proxy layer, preventing parser completion.
- Reconnect sequences sometimes produce a duplicate initial system message, but not the terminal envelope.

Expected behavior:
- On resume, stream completes and the terminal metadata envelope is emitted exactly once; client SDK finalizes output and UI shows the concluding paragraph.

Logs / attachments provided by customer:
- 3 zipped websocket capture logs (wscat) showing trailing bytes on the final packet (attached to the ticket).
- Edge-proxy logs showing instance swap at 2026-03-10T17:12:34Z.
- SDK debug trace showing parser awaiting final 'end' event.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:10 - SRE (Maya Patel): Initial look — edge-proxy showed conn close with FIN prior to origin sending terminal metadata in ~2 of 6 captures. Also see truncated chunk with non-UTF8 suffix in one trace. Suspect proxy buffer flush on failover.
2026-03-12 15:30 - Customer (Inkwell Support): Confirmed they could reproduce on demand in staging by toggling SSO session rotation and that applying the temporary proxy setting stops the truncation.
Edge-proxy cluster shows conn handoff events matching customer timestamps; at handoff, some streams are sent a TCP-level RST to the midstream socket on one of the older edge instances.
One capture contains trailing bytes 0x1f8b (gzip magic) appended to the final data segment — likely proxy compression state incorrectly closed mid-stream.
Serving runtime logs (token emitter) show terminal envelope written to socket on origin at time T, but the sequence number mapping between socket write and TLS record on the egress path occasionally loses the final record if the proxy does an aggressive drain and rebind.
Reproduction in our lab by simulating cookie rewrite + immediate connection migration increases chance of missing terminal envelope from ~0.3% to ~5% when using the current edge-proxy config.
SDK parser currently waits for a clear 'stream_end' marker; if trailing garbage bytes appear after expected JSON close, it does not auto-trim and will throw a parse error rather than attempt best-effort completion.
SRE to deploy a canary edge-proxy build that preserves compression state and ensures graceful socket drain (rollback-safe toggle) — target ETA 2026-03-14.
Runtime team to add a defensive post-write flush acknowledgement for terminal envelope and emit a short retry if socket reports early close — experimental patch PR opened.
SDK team to ship a minor patch (v1.4.3) to tolerate small trailing non-UTF8 bytes when final JSON envelope is otherwise complete (best-effort parse fallback).
Coordinate with customer to run a controlled repro window and confirm mitigation on their dedicated cluster once canary is live.
(pending) Partial mitigations identified. Edge canary and SDK tolerance patch are in flight. No confirmed permanent fix yet; customer accepted temporary workaround (adjust proxy drain timeout) in staging and saw reproduction stop in their tests.
Customer-facing summary: We are actively investigating a rare streaming resume failure where the final metadata envelope may be dropped during an edge failover combined with auth cookie rotation. We're rolling out an edge canary and a short-term SDK tolerance patch; we'll follow up with a permanent fix after root cause validation.
payload.summary: Edge failover + auth rotation causes missing metadata envelope and trailing paragraph silence on streaming resume

Issue summary: Several ScribeAI tenants on a dedicated GPU pool reported repeat-prompt latency regressions and intermittent 504 gateway timeouts when sending sequences of previously seen prompts (chat history + short system prefix). Impact: Customer-visible slowdowns for repeating prompts (token emission latency increased ~4-6x) and occasional request timeouts causing degraded UX and retries. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool 'dedicated-us-east-42'. Observed start: 2026-03-13T13:10Z; correlated with autoscaler compaction and a config rollout to adjust prefix cache TTLs. Expected: Repeat prompts should be served from prefix/KV cache with sub-20ms amortized prefix retrieval; observed behavior shows full KV reload and serialization stalls on cache miss/eviction.
1) On prod-us-east dedicated pool, send identical prompt+context pairs at t=0 and t=+30s using customer ScribeAI traffic pattern. 2) Observe average first-token latency for the second request. 3) Repeat with increased concurrency (10-20 parallel sessions). 4) Check serving-runtime / kv-cache metrics and logs for eviction/compaction events.
[2026-03-13T13:12:02Z] serving-runtime: prefix_cache: eviction event: reason=compaction threshold exceeded, freed=14MB, entries_evicted=312
[2026-03-13T13:12:02Z] router: req_id=abc123 path=/v1/chat model=redwood/fast-7b-v2 latency=812ms status=200
[2026-03-13T13:12:03Z] serving-runtime: kv-serializer: snapshot-serialize took=620ms keys=312
[2026-03-13T13:13:40Z] router: req_id=def456 path=/v1/chat model=redwood/fast-7b-v2 latency=5048ms status=504
[2026-03-13T13:14:10Z] autoscaler: pool=dedicated-us-east-42 compaction_triggered=true reason=memory-pressure
Initial hypothesis: aggressive compaction/TTL change pushed earlier (config roll 2026-03-13T12:58Z) lowered prefix TTL and changed compaction thresholds; combined with a recently merged serializer change (commit ab12cd34ef) this caused long serialization pauses on eviction. Metrics show a spike in 'prefix_cache.evictions' and correlating spike in 'kv-serializer.serialize_ms'. Hot-path repro: when many small prefix keys are evicted, serializer consolidates them and blocks worker threads. We observed a cache key hash-clustering pattern causing disproportionate eviction of certain prefix namespaces (customer-specific prefixes). Additional signal: increased retries from upstream client leading to bursty warmup traffic, making eviction/warmup thrash worse.
Mitigations applied: 1) rolled back the TTL/compaction config change to previous stable values at 2026-03-13T14:05Z; 2) applied emergency patch to limit per-eviction serialization work (PR linked) and throttled serializer concurrency; 3) warmed hot-prefixes for affected customer via targeted pre-warm script. Customer-facing workaround: reduce concurrency and increase inter-request spacing for repeat prompts until warmup completes (~5 minutes). Long-term fix planned: PR #4520 to fix serializer batching logic, adjust compaction heuristics to respect namespace-aware quotas, and add instrumentation for per-prefix eviction impact. payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sudden, sustained 429 responses after they enabled automatic client retries using idempotency keys in their upload pipeline. Impact: batch ingestion jobs that previously completed within quota are now failing consistently with 429s and producing inflated token/billing counts.

Impact:
- ~20% of nightly ingestion worker runs fail with 429s and get delayed by retry loops.
- Customer sees apparent quota exhaustion on a single API key despite overall tenant quota headroom.
- Billing shows duplicate token accounting spikes around the same windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool, prod/us-east
- SDK: lexi-upload-sdk v2.3.1 (client-side retry enabled by default)
- Edge path: customer -> partner edge proxy -> Redwood API GW -> rate limiter -> serving nodes

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Configure client with automatic retries (exponential backoff) + idempotency-key header per request.
2) Start 50 parallel worker threads uploading small batches (1–5 requests/sec each).
3) Kill the partner edge proxy for 10s to trigger transient 502s.
4) On recovery, many requests are retried by client and some fail with 429s shortly after.

Logs / Evidence:
- Customer provided request traces showing repeated POSTs with same idempotency-key but different edge-proxy source IPs and different request IDs.
- Billing spike CSV attached (tokens counted doubled for window 02:00–02:15 UTC).
- Support capture of sample X-Request-ID headers: [rwd-req-1432, rwd-req-1433, rwd-req-1435] showing rapid retries.

Initial hypothesis:
- Retries are reaching different edge nodes after a partner edge proxy failover, and upstream normalization drops idempotency header or rewrites path, causing the rate limiter to count retries as separate requests instead of de-duping by idempotency key.

Workaround suggested to customer:
- Temporarily disable automatic retries in lexi-upload-sdk.
- Throttle concurrency and add client-side jitter until we confirm root cause.


Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:09 - LexiSearch Support (customer): Confirmed they saw retries with identical Idempotency-Key but different X-Forwarded-For entries; they have not observed header stripping in their proxy logs.
Confirmed that partner edge failover creates multi-path fanout causing retries to land on different api-gateway instances.
Rate limiter dedupe flow uses an in-memory 'in-flight' marker then commits to centralized dedupe store on success; race observed when second attempt arrives while first is still in-flight -> double-count.
Deduce root cause: dedupe store commit is asynchronous and TTL for in-flight marker (500ms) too short relative to inter-node routing jitter, allowing quick retries to bypass dedupe.
Reproduced with stresstest harness: emulate 100ms jitter + 600ms commit delay -> ~17% duplicate accounting on retries.
Billing spikes correlate with windows where partner edge performed rolling restarts (confirmed via partner logs).
Root cause: race in deduplication path within rate-limiter when idempotency-based de-dupe commit is delayed; quick client retries (enabled in lexi-upload-sdk) against multi-path edge lead to duplicate counting and 429s. Fix deployed in two parts: (1) rate-limiter change to use a short-lived centralized 'reserved' token that is set atomically on first receipt (https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/2043) and (2) backfill patch to extend in-flight marker TTL to 2s for dedicated pools. Rollout: Canary to us-east on 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC, full rollout 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.

Customer remediation: advised to re-enable retries only after full rollout and upgrade lexi-upload-sdk to v2.3.4 which adds optional "dedupe-safe" retry mode.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem and runbook update to document idempotency dedupe semantics across shards (owner: Dana Kim, due 2026-03-20).
- Add monitoring alert for duplicate token accounting >5% baseline in 15m window (owner: SRE team).
- Reach out to partner edge team to coordinate smoother handoff behaviour (action owner: Marco Ruiz).

Ticket status: In Progress (fix is deployed to canary; monitoring looks good).
payload.summary: Persistent 429s after enabling client-side automatic retries with idempotency keys

Issue summary: After a scheduled optimizer profile swap for tenant NexCommerce on 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC, we observed a spike in 5xx responses from the inference endpoint and a concurrent throughput regression for the tenant. Impact: ~18% of requests for this tenant returned 5xx over a 25-minute window; p95 latency increased from 210ms to 1.2s. This tenant is on Dedicated capacity; auto-scaling did not immediately mitigate. They are reporting production user-facing errors. We need guidance to perform a controlled exit of the new mixed-quant + prefetch profile while preserving session/kv state and avoiding mass evictions.
1) Tenant traffic routed to dedicated pool with optimizer-profile: mixed-quant-prefetch-v3
2) Trigger standard chat generation workload (short prompts, multi-turn) at 200 qps per-tenant shard
3) Observe serving runtime logs: increased kv eviction churn and 5xx errors (model load/cache miss path)
4) p95 and throughput regressions appear within ~3-5 minutes of deploy
5xx errors (502/503) returned from streaming endpoints
p95 latency regressed to 1.2s from baseline 210ms
throughput for tenant fell ~25% despite available GPU headroom
kv-cache eviction rate spiked and latency for first token increased
No increase in 5xx error rate after optimizer profile change
Throughput and latency within 10% of baseline for same workload
Graceful fallback to compatible model variant or demotion path without tenant disruption
[2026-03-12T02:03:14Z] serving-runtime ERROR tenant=nexcommerce request_id=3ff2b6 5xx model= gptx-7b-quantized-v2 kernel-failure: kv-evict-throttle

[2026-03-12T02:15:07Z] api-gateway ERROR upstream 502 connection-reset by peer
1) Temporarily pinned tenant to previous model variant (gptx-7b-fp16) via routing override
2) Throttled tenant to 150 qps to reduce eviction churn while we investigate
3) Enabled extended kv-cache TTL for the tenant as an emergency measure
- Initial hypothesis: mixed-quant layout interacts with prefetch/eviction heuristic causing aggressive KV eviction under short-turn workloads.
- Observed that prefetch triggered a wave of large KV allocations which evicted critical prefixes; next requests hit model cold path causing 5xx on kernel memory allocation failures.
- Autoscale did not kick synchronous with error window: scheduler delay and queueing contributed to client-facing 5xx.
- No changes to infra (nodes) at time of incident beyond profile flip; related PR referenced for optimizer heuristics (runtime PR #2145).
- Reproducer: synthetic replay at 180-220 qps with multi-turn prompts reproduces eviction/5xx pattern locally in staging with identical profile.
Root cause likely a resource allocation mismatch between mixed-quant kernel memory expectations and the prefetch eviction policy threshold.
Mixed-quant kernels have different KV sizing; prefetch assumed FP16 sizes and over-allocated internal buffers leading to eviction storms.
Edge-case: tenant workload has very short sequences with many small turns, which exacerbates thrash when prefetch pulls longer contexts.
Recommendation: coordinated demotion path that disables prefetch first and then rolls back quant profile rather than switching both at once.
A) Orchestrated safe-exit steps we can run for NexCommerce:
   1) Schedule a short maintenance window (5 mins) and enable routing pin to previous model variant to stop new sessions entering mixed profile.
   2) Disable prefetch feature flag for tenant (config: optimizer.prefetch.enabled=false) to stop further KV prefetch allocations.
   3) Drain existing prefetch allocations: run kv-evict-sweep with tenant-safe mode to free non-critical prefixes, preserving active sessions' prefixes.
   4) After evictions stabilize, roll model variant back to fp16 baseline and monitor p95/5xx for 15 minutes.
   5) If stable, gradually lift throttles and remove routing pin.
B) If above fails to restore within 30 minutes, follow emergency fallback: disable optimizer profile entirely for tenant and escalate to SRE for node-level memory allocation tracing.
1) Can NexCommerce accept a 5-minute maintenance window now (ETA to start provided)?
2) Are there any session-affinity constraints or long-running sessions we must preserve?
3) Do they have any traffic spikes scheduled in next 2 hours?

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 04:10 - Customer (NexCommerce - S. Patel): We see user-facing errors on checkout flows. Please prioritize. We can take a short maintenance window.
2026-03-14 01:20 - Product (Maya Rivera): Note: optimizer team will follow up with a long-term fix to prefetch sizing heuristics; linking an internal ticket INT-4382.
Action taken: Safely disabled prefetch for tenant, performed targeted kv-evict-sweep preserving active prefixes, rolled routing back to fp16 variant, removed throttles after stabilization.
Result: 5xx rate returned to baseline within 12 minutes of pinned rollback; p95 latency returned to ~230ms. Throughput restored to expected levels.
Follow-up: Engineering will publish an optimizer patch to correct prefetch sizing assumptions for mixed-quant kernels (tracked in INT-4382). Recommend staged rollout and tenant simulator preflight (templates attached).
Customer confirmation: NexCommerce verified checkout flows are healthy. Customer asked for runbook steps to avoid flip of quant+prefetch together in future.

2) Add a suggested maintenance checklist to Console UI when applying optimizer profile changes to Dedicated pools.
3) Coordinate a rolling test with NexCommerce in staging using tenant-simulator (task assigned INT-4382).

Issue summary: Customers observe that the last few tokens (often just trailing whitespace or the final punctuation) are missing after an SSE resume when requests route through Cloudflare Workers connection rotation. Impact: Final sentence fragments are getting silently trimmed in ~8% of resumed streams for Verbata's production traffic, causing truncated answers and user-facing UI glitches (cut-off sentences). This affects live-chat workflows and any flow that relies on the terminal event to mark completion. Environment: prod-us-east, SaaS customer using Redwood hosted API through Cloudflare Workers that performs header rewrites and connection pooling. Observed on redwood-chat-medium-v1 and gptj-6b-instruct. Occurs only when Worker routes cause a connection handoff / pool shuffle during resume pacing. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start an SSE streaming request to the Redwood API from a client behind a Cloudflare Worker with HTTP/1.1 keepalive enabled. 2) Let the server stream a long response (~4000 tokens). 3) Simulate a short disconnect (network blip or Worker-script triggered restart) and then re-establish the SSE resume request using the original resume token. 4) Observe that the resumed stream completes but final 1-6 characters (often whitespace or trailing period) are missing. Observed behavior differs depending on Worker caching and connection reuse. Logs & traces: see investigation notes below for excerpts. Notes: this is not a universal client bug (some clients receive intact stream). The pattern correlates with a connection rotation where the edge terminates the previous TCP session and a new one receives the remainder chunks. It appears to be sensitive to chunk boundary alignment and Cloudflare Workers' response buffering. Customer impact: high for Verbata chat flows (enterprise), intermittent for self-serve customers. Work-around in place: recommend short-lived client-side whitespace-tolerant heuristics (append missing punctuation if last chunk doesn't end with terminal marker) and temporarily route Verbata traffic around the Worker (bypass) while engineering investigates.
1) Deploy a minimal Cloudflare Worker that forwards requests to our API and preserves SSE headers. 2) Start a streaming chat call that yields a multi-kilobyte response. 3) After ~60-90s of streaming, force a Worker restart or force a connection pool rotation at the edge (can be simulated by rapidly re-deploying or toggling a keepalive setting). 4) Reconnect with the client's resume token and compare the final bytes of the stream to the original. Expected: resumed stream contains full final token/punctuation. Actual: final 1-6 characters are missing ~8% of the time.

2026-03-10 — Support (Aisha): Initial report from customer: truncated final punctuation on resumed streams. Asked for request IDs and sample replay.
2026-03-10 — Customer (Verbata SRE): Attached sample request id uid-9876 and indicated it's reproducible when Worker is configured to 'keep connections warm'. Provided traffic capture and Worker script.
2026-03-11 — SRE (Marco): Reproduced locally by enabling Cloudflare Worker connection rotation simulation. Observed consistent end-offset shortfall when the edge reported a mid-stream reset and resumed onto a different backend connection. Escalating to runtime team for kernel/kafka-like chunk boundary handling. Linked SUP-4721 for historical resume issues.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 — Support (Aisha): Informed customer of planned temporary workaround (bypass Worker) and requested permission to toggle routing for a 24h window to capture full network trace. Customer approved.
Initial triage focused on client SDK and server serializer; both passed basic tests. Reproduced in controlled environment by introducing an artificial mid-stream connection tear at the edge. The serving runtime logs show expected final-chunk length, but the resumable-offset reported by the edge is 4 bytes ahead of what the backend believes was acknowledged. Hypothesis: Cloudflare Workers (or CF's connection pooling) can coalesce and forward buffered bytes in a way that transiently masks the true boundary; when a connection is shuffled, a small trailing buffer remains at the Worker which the new connection doesn't replay, leading to missing trailing bytes after resume. Investigated HTTP transfer-encoding behavior, SSE chunk framing, and client-side reassembly. No evidence of corruption within our runtime; problem appears at edge/worker boundary. A patch to add an explicit final-chunk-hash in the resume handshake is being prototyped. Related historical tickets: SUP-4721 (sse-ws-reconnects) — similar resume mismatch patterns but different trigger (proxy chunking vs worker rotation).
Temporary mitigation: advised customer to route around Cloudflare Worker and to apply a client-side fallback that tolerates missing trailing whitespace/punctuation. Longer-term fix: landed a server-side resume-handshake enhancement (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2891) which adds a 16-bit checksum for the last N bytes and validates offsets on resume. This allows the server to detect the mismatch and request re-delivery from the client or trigger a conservative re-fetch from origin. Rollout plan: canary in prod-us-east on 2026-03-18, full rollout ~2026-03-22 pending metrics. Follow-ups: coordinate with Cloudflare AM to validate Worker pooling semantics and update docs with known edge behaviors.
