Issue summary:
Acorn Financial reports frequent disconnects when using streaming responses from Redwood (SSE) from within their corporate network. They are behind an enterprise HTTP proxy (Zscaler-like) and observe the stream terminating mid-response (partial output) with different error messages depending on SDK/language. They request explicit guidance on safe retry behavior for streaming and want request_id surfaced consistently for triage.

Impact:
- Production feature degraded: customers see truncated model outputs or UI hangs when stream ends unexpectedly.
- Retries are currently ad-hoc; customer concerned about duplicate side effects / duplicate billing when reissuing requests.
- Support unable to quickly correlate failures because request_id is not always present in SDK exceptions for streaming disconnects.

Environment:
- Customer tier: enterprise
- Region: us-east
- Network: corporate outbound proxy with TLS interception and idle connection policy
- Observed in: TypeScript SDK (Node 18), Python SDK (3.11), Go SDK (1.21)
- Endpoint: /v1/chat.completions with stream=true (SSE)

Customer-reported behavior:
- Stream runs for ~10–40 seconds then disconnects (no explicit error from API); client receives one of:
  - Node: "TypeError: fetch failed" / "ECONNRESET" or "socket hang up"
  - Python: "httpx.ReadError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer" or "RemoteProtocolError: Server disconnected"
  - Go: "unexpected EOF" while reading event stream
- Partial text is sometimes available in the UI, but the SDK throws and caller is unsure whether to display partial output or treat as failure.
- Customer notes that non-streaming requests are more reliable (but latency is worse).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Route outbound traffic through corporate proxy (CONNECT).
2) Run streaming chat completion with longer responses (max_tokens >= 800) and low temperature.
3) Observe intermittent disconnects; rate increases during peak proxy load.

Evidence/log snippets (redacted):
- Customer TS log:
  - "stream error: ECONNRESET" after receiving ~1200 chars; no request_id available in the exception.
- Customer Python log:
  - "httpx.RemoteProtocolError: Server disconnected"; request_id not printed.
- Customer captured response headers from successful calls show x-request-id present, but failures do not surface it.

Initial hypothesis:
- Proxy closes idle/long-lived connections or buffers SSE chunks; may terminate mid-chunk causing client-side protocol errors.
- SDK streaming implementations differ in how they parse SSE and how they attach request_id to raised errors.

What we need:
1) Clear docs guidance for streaming disconnects behind proxies (recommended timeouts, keepalive, proxy settings, partial output handling).
2) SDK behavior: on streaming disconnect, raise typed error containing request_id (if known), status_code if available, and include partial_output (or guidance on how to capture it).
3) Conservative retry guidance (streaming retries should not be automatic; document idempotency keys + request_id logging).

Success criteria:
- Customer can log request_id and provide it to Support for any failure.
- Docs provide recommended patterns: retry policy for non-streaming vs streaming; show safe resume/retry patterns.
- SDKs align on an error taxonomy so customers see consistent fields across languages.
2026-01-29 09:22 (Dev Patel): Ticket opened after CS escalation. Customer reports 5–15% of streamed responses end abruptly behind corporate proxy. Asking for guidance + request_id surfacing. Assigning to Owen for repro + coordination with SDK team.
2026-01-29 10:05 (Owen Phillips): Acknowledged. Requesting: (1) which proxy vendor/policy (idle timeout?), (2) whether they can bypass proxy to confirm correlation, (3) SDK versions + minimal repro, (4) confirm they can capture response headers for successful stream start (x-request-id).
2026-01-29 14:18 (Customer - Acorn Financial): Proxy is managed by IT; appears to terminate long-lived connections. Cannot fully bypass in prod, but can test in a separate network where issue disappears. SDK versions: TS 0.18.2, Python 0.14.7, Go 0.9.1. They can capture x-request-id on successful responses but failures throw before they can access it.
2026-01-30 09:02 (Owen Phillips): Repro attempt internally using a proxy simulator that cuts connections mid-chunk; observed similar errors: Node fetch fails with ECONNRESET; Python httpx raises RemoteProtocolError; Go returns unexpected EOF. Confirms we do not consistently attach request_id for streaming disconnects because headers are read at stream start but not retained/propagated in error path in some SDKs.
2026-01-30 10:21 (Allison Grant): From SRE perspective: do NOT auto-retry streaming by default. Encourage idempotency keys for non-streaming retries; for streaming, recommend application-level retry with explicit user confirmation or safe idempotent semantics. Also recommend exposing disconnect_reason and retry_count fields where possible for debugging.
2026-01-31 11:44 (Sabrina James): Python SDK: we can retain response headers at stream start and include request_id in any downstream stream iterator exception. Also can include a StreamingError that optionally carries partial_text collected so far (opt-in due to memory). Tracking under SDK parity work; will reference this ticket in PR.
2026-02-02 15:09 (Dana Lo): TS SDK: node fetch streaming loses access to headers after consumption in some paths; but we can capture request_id early and attach to a typed error when ReadableStream errors. Also clarifying cancellation semantics vs network disconnect in docs/examples.
2026-02-03 13:27 (Mateusz Zielinski): Go SDK: we can wrap scanner/decoder errors and include request_id captured from initial response. Will also document recommended retry pattern and that retries are caller-controlled for streams.
2026-02-05 09:40 (Owen Phillips): Sent interim workaround to customer:
- If possible, configure proxy to allow long-lived SSE and disable response buffering for the Redwood domain.
- Increase overall timeout and keep connection alive (TCP keepalive) where supported.
- For best reliability behind strict proxies, consider non-streaming mode for long outputs.
- For retries: avoid automatic retry on streaming disconnect; if retrying, log request_id and use idempotency keys for any side-effecting workflows; treat partial output as best-effort display only.
Customer acknowledged and will test proxy policy changes.
2026-02-07 16:12 (Owen Phillips): Internal: linked this issue to INT-1182 (request_id visibility in SDK errors). Also flagged as a concrete driver for SDK parity initiative (streaming edge cases + typed errors).
2026-02-10 12:33 (Wei Chen): Drafted doc updates for Streaming guide: new section "Behind proxies" + "What to do on disconnect" including sample code to log request_id and capture partial output. Will align wording across Python/TS/Go pages and add explicit warning that streaming retries are not automatic.
2026-02-14 10:50 (Owen Phillips): Engineering updates in flight:
- Python: add typed StreamingDisconnectError w/ request_id and partial output semantics.
- TS: attach request_id and normalize error shape on stream failure.
- Go: wrap unexpected EOF with typed error + request_id.
Docs + examples to include idempotency guidance and consistent logging fields.
Keeping ticket in progress until customer confirms improvements or docs are published.
2026-02-18 09:07 (Customer - Acorn Financial): Proxy team applied allowlist + disabled buffering for Redwood streaming endpoint; disconnect rate reduced significantly but not eliminated. They still want request_id in errors to speed up escalation and want clear guidance on when to retry.
2026-02-19 17:28 (Owen Phillips): Docs PR and SDK PRs merged/queued for release per parity rollout. Provided customer with preview link and recommended pattern:
- Always log request_id at stream start.
- On disconnect: show partial output (if acceptable) and present a "Regenerate" action rather than silent automatic retry.
- For background jobs: prefer non-streaming with idempotency key and standard retry policy.
Customer satisfied with plan; will upgrade SDKs when releases land.
2026-02-20 11:02 (Dev Patel): Closing as resolved via docs guidance + upcoming SDK changes (typed errors w/ request_id, clarified partial output + retry guidance). Follow-ups tracked in SDK parity epic and INT-1182. If customer sees ongoing high disconnect rate after proxy changes, we will re-open for deeper platform/proxy analysis.
Resolved via (1) published streaming docs guidance for enterprise proxies and safe retry patterns, and (2) SDK parity work to surface typed streaming disconnect errors including request_id and consistent semantics for partial output/cancellation. Customer implemented proxy allowlist/buffering changes as a mitigation and will upgrade SDKs to pick up improved error surfaces.

Issue summary: During a planned canary rollout of gptx-13b-redwood-v1 for AcmePayments (enterprise), some user sessions were routed to the canary while others observed the pinned model version. Impact: inconsistent responses for the same prompt across simultaneous user sessions (observed in 12 distinct request traces), causing incorrect transaction descriptions in customer QA. Environment: prod-us-east (hosted API, dedicated route pinned by AcmePayments).
1) Customer created a route with a pinned model version (gptx-13b-redwood-v1) for their /generate endpoint.
2) Redwood performed a canary rollout to add a quantized variant (gptx-13b-q4) with 10% weight in us-east around 2026-03-12T17:05:00Z.
3) Multiple simultaneous requests from the same customer session were sent before pin commit finished; some were answered by pinned variant, others by the canary.
4) Compare outputs for identical prompts; observe variance in phrasing and tokenization that affected downstream QA checks.
trace_id=trc_0a9f3e; timestamp=2026-03-12T17:05:12Z; route=acmepayments/txn-gen; backend=pool-7; model=gptx-13b-q4; decision=canary
trace_id=trc_0a9f3e; timestamp=2026-03-12T17:05:12Z; route=acmepayments/txn-gen; backend=pool-3; model=gptx-13b-redwood-v1; decision=pinned
edge-proxy logs show pin-commit event queued at 2026-03-12T17:04:59Z and confirmation delivered to routers at 2026-03-12T17:06:01Z
router debug: pin_state=deferred_commit; reason=concurrent-canary-update; affected_sessions=12
Initial hypothesis: routing cache TTL + deferred pin commit transaction allowing routing decisions to consult stale policy leading to split-cohort.
Checked console: pin create API returned 200 at 2026-03-12T17:04:58Z but commit coordinator log shows a deferred commit due to in-flight canary weight adjustment job.
Router logs show per-connection decision made from local cache when commit was still pending; subsequently the commit propagated and future connections consistently used pinned model.
No GPU OOMs or autoscaler evictions recorded in implicated pools during window (monitoring graphs attached to PR).
Related change: autoscaler scheduling job PR #2148 attempted a transient capacity shift that touched the canary allocation during commit window — likely exacerbated timing race.
Confirmed at least 12 customer request traces where different model ids are returned for identical session and prompt (sampled traces included above).
Customer side: AcmePayments reported downstream QA failures affecting nightly reconciliation; they provided example prompts and timestamps.
Mitigation applied 2026-03-12T18:00Z: forced pin-commit sweep issued (admin override) which reconciled router caches and set pin_state=committed across us-east routers.
Rollout paused for AcmePayments and canary weight rolled back to 0% until a safe commit path is implemented.
Hotfix deployed 2026-03-13T02:15Z: add gating in commit coordinator so pin commit cannot be marked 'queued/deferred' while concurrent canary-weight jobs are active; PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2154.
Follow-ups: add end-to-end test covering concurrent commit+canary update, increase routing cache TTL observability, and update runbook to include admin sweep command used in mitigation.
Customer communication: sent remediation note and workaround (pause canary) and scheduled postmortem with AcmePayments for 2026-03-15.
Status: workaround in place, long-term fix merged; monitoring alert created to detect 'deferred_commit' state during rollouts.

Issue summary: Several customers reported elevated end-to-end latency and streaming connection timeouts when using models that invoke external tool calls. Impact: Customer streaming sessions hit client-side timeouts (120s) and saw p95 generation latency increase by ~300-600ms per tool invocation. The customer (Parcelly) uses a dedicated route with tool-call enabled for address-normalization and observed degraded user experience in their checkout flow.
1) Use the Redwood streaming chat endpoint with a prompt that triggers a tool call to the address_normalizer tool (route: /v1/chat/stream).
2) Enable function/tool calling via the SDK and set max_stream_timeout=120s client-side.
3) Observe response times and streaming disconnects in the client after ~90-110s or abrupt streaming stop when tool invocation occurs.
4) Reproduce with curl using request-id header for trace: curl -i -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'x-request-id: rq_87af3d' -d '{...tool call...}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream

2026-03-10T14:08:03Z rq_87af3d orchestration: forward to tool-proxy schema-check=enabled sync=true
2026-03-10T14:08:03Z rq_87af3d tool-proxy: handshake start -> 120ms to auth, 200ms to schema-validator
2026-03-10T14:08:03Z rq_87af3d schema-validator: validation start, ruleset v2.1, elapsed=320ms -> result=pass
2026-03-10T14:08:03Z rq_87af3d tool-proxy: execute tool call, total blocking on validation and handshake 640ms, resume streaming
2026-03-10T14:09:55Z customer-observed: client streaming disconnect after cumulative delays during three consecutive tool calls
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported multiple streaming disconnects when invoking address_normalizer. Provided request-ids and sample payloads. Noted that the issue began 2026-03-09 after a runtime rollout.
Alejandro Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-10: Initial metric sweep indicates spike in p95 token latency on routes that hit tool-invocation path. Dashboard: /dashboards/latency/tool-invoke shows +450ms median extra. Flagged orchestration change on 2026-03-08 (deploy id: orch-2026-03-08-a) that enabled synchronous schema validation for tool responses.
Parcelly Support Rep (customer) 2026-03-10: Confirmed they saw increased latency in checkout address validation flow. They can reproduce consistently with their production dataset and want a mitigation ASAP.
Ravi Patel (SRE/Assignee) 2026-03-11: Temporarily backfilled a canary rollback for orch-2026-03-08-a on the customer's dedicated pool. Observed immediate reduction in p95 for the route. Working on a safer permanent fix.
Eng (Orchestration) 2026-03-12: Found that the new validation path performs sync call to schema-validator for every invocation and cache was accidentally disabled due to a key-salt change in PR 4123. Also, network retries to tool-proxy were set to 2 with 100ms backoff; combined this increased tail latency.
Ravi Patel 2026-03-12: Implemented workaround: re-enable cached schema results and set schema-validation to async-with-timeout=100ms with permissive fallback. Deployed to canary; Parcelly confirmed improvement. Planning full rollout after QA.
Maya Chen 2026-03-13: Customer accepted workaround as mitigation. Coordinated on release window and confirmed no further streaming disconnects after workaround applied. Closing as resolved but tracking follow-ups.
Note: Link to incident Slack thread: #incidents-tool-invoke-22401
Hypothesis 1: New orchestration change made schema validation synchronous, adding 200-600ms per tool call.
Hypothesis 2: Cache miss rate increased because of new cache-salt introduced in PR 4123; validation could not reuse prior results.
Hypothesis 3: Additional network retries and auth handshake added extra round-trips before tool execution.
Findings: Correlated deploy orch-2026-03-08-a with latency jump. Log traces show schema-validator end-to-end ~320ms on average, handshake/auth ~120-200ms. Cache miss exploded from 8% -> 72% on tool interface lookups.
Quantified impact: For a single tool-invocation, added median +420ms and p95 +780ms. Multi-invocation prompts multiplied impact leading to client streaming timeouts.
Temporary mitigation validated: Re-enabling cache and switching to async validation reduced p95 overhead to +60ms. Canary rollback matched pre-deploy baseline.
Testing notes: Added unit and integration tests for cache-key stability and a perf regression test to gate schema-validator changes.
1) Applied canary rollback of orch-2026-03-08-a on affected dedicated pools (parcelly's pool) 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC which restored baseline latency.
2) Implemented a permanent fix in orchestration: schema-validation runs async with a 100ms timeout and permissive fallback if validation does not complete in time (PR 4129).
3) Restored and stabilized schema-validator caching with consistent cache-salt semantics (PR 4130).
4) Reduced tool-proxy retry policy to 1 with exponential backoff starting at 50ms to avoid compounding latencies (PR 4131).
5) Deployed changes to canary 2026-03-12 and full rollout to production 2026-03-13 after QA validation. Monitoring shows p95 returns near pre-change baseline and customer reported fix.
6) Customer follow-up: Parcelly asked for a post-deploy verification window; SRE provided a 72-hour verification report and added the route to enhanced latency alerts.
Rollout notes: Added a feature flag (tool_call.async_validation=true) for safety and a perf regression test to the CI pipeline to block future synchronous validation changes without perf review.
Owners: Orchestration (Ravi Patel), ToolProxy (Dalia Nguyen). Action items: 1) Add regression test gating for schema-validator perf (due 2026-03-20). 2) Create runbook for tool-call latency complaints including quick rollback steps (due 2026-03-18). 3) Customer communications: follow-up note and SLA credit evaluation (Support to coordinate).
payload.summary: Tool invocation orchestration overhead causing streaming timeouts and elevated p95 latency

Issue summary: Customers observed an abrupt spike of 502/503 errors and elevated 5xx rates for streaming and short-chat calls immediately following a scheduled rolling deployment in us-east. Impact: Multiple enterprise customers on Dedicated capacity (including NimbusDocs) reported failed requests, higher tail latency, and partial runtime crashes. Initial symptoms indicated connection termination during node drain leading to request retries and downstream overload.
Approximately 8% of requests returned 5xx over a 12 minute window for the us-east pool. Several long-lived streaming sessions dropped mid-stream. No data corruption observed; primary impact is availability and degraded latency for affected tenants.
1) Schedule a rolling deploy against the us-east serving pool with default drain_timeout (30s).
2) Simulate a mix of short chat and long-stream requests at 60% of typical sustained throughput.
3) Observe that when nodes begin connection drain, in-flight requests to drained nodes are reset and the API gateway retries, amplifying load to remaining nodes.
4) Understood sequence: drain -> connection resets -> gateway retries -> remaining runtimes hit sudden concurrency -> some runtimes evict workers / hit alloc pressure -> 502/503s escalate.
2026-03-10T03:14:22Z apigw: client_conn_reset upstream=https://runtime-7.us-east internal_error=connection_drained
2026-03-10T03:14:23Z runtime-3 stderr: kvcache: failed to allocate buffer: out of memory
2026-03-10T03:14:24Z apigw: 502 from runtime-3 for request id=rq_89f0 - connection reset during body streaming
2026-03-10T03:20:01Z autoscaler: scale_up event triggered by elevated_reqs - launching 2 nodes (warmup)
Initial hypothesis: improper drain behavior caused abrupt connection closes rather than graceful handoff; gateway retries amplified remaining capacity and caused runtime worker eviction/ooms.
Checked autoscaler timeline: scale-up lag was ~3 minutes; warm-up CPU/memory usage peaked as newly launched nodes ramped, but too late to absorb burst.
Observed increased KV cache miss rate during window which magnified per-request compute as caching benefits were reduced.
Network telemetry shows SYN/FIN patterns consistent with in-flight connection termination rather than graceful keepalive shutdown.
Combination of aggressive connection drain policy during rolling deploy (drain_timeout too low) and unforgiving gateway retry amplification. Drained nodes cut live streaming connections instead of allowing graceful completion; gateway retried immediately, pushing more load onto remaining runtimes that then experienced memory pressure and partial OOMs.
Rolled back the rolling deploy controller to use extended drain_timeout for streaming-heavy pools (increase to 120s) and temporarily disabled immediate gateway retry for specific routes to reduce amplification.
1) Short term: Revert to previous deploy config and set drain_timeout=120s for prod-us-east streaming-capable pools.
2) Mid term: Implement streaming-aware drain that marks nodes as 'no-new-streams' before connection deadline to allow existing streaming clients to finish without hard resets.
3) Add a backoff window in API gateway retries for 5xx during deploy windows to avoid amplification.
4) Tune autoscaler warmup policies to reduce scale-up lag for heavy workloads and pre-warm cache for new nodes.
5) Create a runbook for deploys that adapt drain_timeout by workload type and register mandatory canary traffic windows.
Documented deploy drain change in runbook
PR opened to add streaming-aware drain logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1292
Dashboard alert created for rapid-5xx-change with auto-annotation of deploy events
Mitigation applied: rollback and adjusted drain_timeout. Immediate customer impact reduced to baseline within 9 minutes of mitigation steps. Longer-term fixes scheduled and tracked under INT-2109 and infra PRs.
Notified NimbusDocs support contact at 2026-03-10T03:22 with summary and ETA for mitigation. Follow-up update sent 2026-03-10T03:45 confirming rollback and partial fix. Offer extended support window for affected customers.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-10T03:18: Logged initial customer report from NimbusDocs; escalated to SRE channel #incidents.
SRE (Marcus Lee) - 2026-03-10T03:25: Confirmed spike in 5xx and runtime OOM traces. Rolling back recent deploy to halt additional drain events.
Infra (Helena Ortiz) - 2026-03-10T03:33: Observed autoscaler ramp lag. Will fast-track a change to pre-warm nodes for streaming profiles.
Customer (NimbusDocs - Rajesh Kumar) - 2026-03-10T03:40: Thanks, sessions resumed for most users. We saw a couple of dropped transcripts; please advise on follow-up.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-10T03:50: Offering to run a targeted re-run with extended drain_timeout in a canary and coordinate with NimbusDocs to validate stability.
SRE (Marcus Lee) - 2026-03-11T09:12: Added follow-up task INT-2109 to implement streaming-aware drain; assigned to runtime squad.

Issue summary: Customer reports that reserved burst credits (hourly burst capacity) were not applied to their subaccount after they downgraded a seat-level Dedicated plan in the middle of an hourly billing window. Impact: BrightCart observed a sudden unexpected invoice adjustment and a missing credit line for the subaccount, resulting in an overage alert and a triggered automated payment hold. Timeline: 2026-03-01 22:05 UTC - Customer changed plan (downgrade) on parent org. 2026-03-01 22:12 UTC - Scheduler ran hourly credit allocation job for burst capacity. 2026-03-01 22:20 UTC - Customer subaccount shows no burst credits applied; parent account shows partial allocation. 2026-03-02 08:00 UTC - Customer opened support ticket. Key question: why weren't burst credits allocated to the subaccount when the allocation job ran within the same hour as the downgrade?
1) Have parent org with Reserved Dedicated + hourly burst capacity enabled.
2) Create subaccount and assign some reserved capacity via console.
3) During an hourly billing window, downgrade seat-level plan on the parent org (reduce total reserved count).
4) Allow hourly burst credit allocator to run (scheduler job at minute xx:12).
5) Inspect allocation ledger: expected equal pro-rata burst credits to remain on subaccount but observed missing allocations.

2026-03-01T22:12:01Z billing-engine: compute_pro_rata(parent_org=brightcart, change_event=downgrade, effective=2026-03-01T22:05Z)
2026-03-01T22:12:04Z allocation: subaccount=bc-prod-analytics id=sub-63 allocation_delta=0 (expected >0)
2026-03-01T22:12:05Z allocation: parent_org=brightcart allocation_delta=+2 (unexpected)
2026-03-01T22:12:06Z billing-engine: wrote ledger lines to bucket hourly-burst-20260301-22
Hypothesis 1: Race between the downgrade event write and the credit-allocation job read window. Event timestamps recorded but the allocator might have used cached reservation totals from a previous snapshot.
Hypothesis 2: Allocation logic treats downgrades within the same hour as effective for the parent but not when deriving subaccount delta, causing parent to absorb credits instead of redistributing.
Query run: select * from hourly_allocations where org='brightcart' and window='2026-03-01T22' returned parent delta +2, subaccount delta 0.
Found telemetry: reservation_change_event handled by /events/ledger consumer at 22:05 but reservation indexer had last refresh at 22:00; allocator reads reservation index at 22:11 which did not include indexer update -> potential stale view.
Workaround issued: Manual allocation correction performed for BrightCart subaccount and credit memo created to reverse overage. Engineering action: add atomic coupling between reservation indexer and hourly allocator to ensure refresh-before-allocate for events in prior 15 minutes. Short-term hotfix: modify allocator to re-fetch reservation deltas if allocation mismatches parent/subaccount sums. Billing team issued provisional credit memo ID CM-2026-0047 to customer. Pending code fix landing and follow-up audit of hourly windows.

Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated 429 responses from a dedicated pool when a set of long-lived websocket connections maintain frequent keepalive heartbeats (every 15s) alongside low-rate interactive requests. Throttles are seen even though the token consumption for actual chat/embedding calls is well under the committed capacity.

Impact:
- AuroraMaps (dedicated) observes intermittent 429s affecting user-facing routing for ~7% of requests across a 20-minute window.
- Symptoms started after enabling an internal telemetry heartbeat (keepalive) that pings every 15 seconds to maintain session affinity.
- No billing discrepancy reported; the tenant's committed throughput is not exhausted according to console graphs.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated pool (dedicated) in us-west
- Runtime: redwood/gpt-large-v2 pinned at v2026-02-11
- Edge ingress: customer-managed proxy -> Redwood edge

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Establish 250 websocket connections scoped to a single api-key with keepalive pings every 15s.
2) From 10 of those connections, send lightweight chat requests (50-200 tokens) at ~1 req/min each.
3) Observe 429 responses on a subset of requests after ~5–10 minutes of steady state.

Observed logs / telemetry snippets (redacted):
- edge: "rate-limiter: token-window exceeded for api_key=auroracci-***; window=60s; used=1015; allowed=1000"
- serving: "connection keepalive: ignored-for-billing=true; heartbeat_count=1620"
- console: "dedicated-pool utilization 35% (tokens/sec), token-credits remaining: 2.1M"

Hypothesis / immediate ask:
- Customer suspects keepalive/heartbeat messages are being attributed to the token/quota window and contributing to the refill penalty that triggers sustained-window throttles. They want confirmation of how keepalives are accounted and guidance to avoid the 429s without disabling affinity.

Requested outcome:
- Clear explanation of which request classes count towards the sustained-window and per-window refill penalties for dedicated pools.
- Recommended config or mitigation (edge proxy keepalive configuration, route separation, or dedicated burst-pool adjustment) tailored for dedicated customers running many long-lived connections.

Investigation notes (support):
- Verified request headers and sample traces show keepalive requests hit the ingress path but contain no payload and are marked by the client as "ping/keepalive".
- Rate-limiter codepath currently classifies requests by route weight and connection metadata; there is a known refill alignment where small frequent requests can cause elevated per-window used counts even if token consumption is nominal (see linked PR).
- Dedicated pool metrics do not show token exhaustion but do show ephemeral window overrun events aligned with high heartbeat counts.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Reduce keepalive frequency to 60s where possible, or configure proxy to use connection-level TCP keepalives instead of application-layer pings for session affinity.
- Alternatively, create a separate routing path for telemetry/heartbeat and request a small background burst pool allocation from account team.

Next steps:
- Engineering to confirm whether application-layer keepalives should be excluded from sustained-window accounting or should be reclassified as non-billable health probes for dedicated pools.
- If code change needed, estimate impact and rollback plan.

2026-03-13 | Maya Chen (Support): Customer opened after seeing 429 spikes correlated with new keepalive telemetry. Provided traces and console screenshots. Asked for classification guidance and mitigation while we investigate.

Issue summary: Between 02:10-02:25 UTC on 2026-03-12, PixelProbe reported a spike in 502/504 responses from the Redwood hosted API for their tenant. Impact: ~45% of requests for the tenant returned 5xx during the window; customer embedding ingestion pipelines stalled and retried, causing downstream batch duplication. Observed pattern: a scheduled bulk embedding job (internal cron) started at 02:00 UTC with high concurrent subrequests, which saturated gateway keepalive sockets and triggered upstream runtime watchdog resets and subsequent 502/504s.
Customer schedule: submit embedding batch with ~1200 items split across 12 parallel worker threads starting at the same wall-clock time (simulate with test harness)
Ensure each embedding request uses long prompt context (~8k tokens) to exercise KV-prefetch and long-tail GPU memory usage
Run the batch against a dedicated tenant on us-west prod with current autoscaler and kernel-selection heuristic enabled
Observe API gateway metrics (accept queue, keepalive pool), runtime logs (watchdog resets), and downstream 5xx rates

2026-03-12T02:12:10Z runtime[worker-3]: watchdog: process reset due to long syscall (blocked on CPU fallback path) pid=32481
2026-03-12T02:12:11Z api-gateway[proxy]: upstream 502 returned from runtime-cluster-uswest tenant=pxp-58 request_id=abc123
2026-03-12T02:14:05Z autoscaler: scale_activity=warmup_delay observed_gpu_warmup=high scaling_decision=defer

SRE checked ingress: accept queue and keepalive pool exhausted in us-west frontends during the spike window. Connection churn increased by 8x relative to baseline.
Runtime team found watchdog resets on several worker processes. Core dump traces show thread stalls in the CPU fallback kernels triggered by a recent kernel-selection heuristic change (PR #1280) that aggressively prefers CPU fallback for mixed-length prompts on certain model shapes.
Hypothesis: concurrent long-context embedding requests from a single tenant saturated gateway socket resources (keepalive exhaustion + ephemeral port churn) causing increased latency, which pushed runtime into degraded kernel paths; those CPU fallback paths are single-threaded in current build and block for long syscalls, tripping the watchdog and causing abrupt upstream closure and 502/504 propagation.
Evidence: Watchdog reset traces correlate with the spike in accept_queue_full and a sharp drop in runtime healthy replicas. The recent kernel-selection change was rolled out to 20% of runtime pool in us-west earlier the same week (deploy on 2026-03-10).
Repro attempt in staging: Running a synthetic batch reproduces keepalive exhaustion and triggers 502s when the kernel-selection heuristic is enabled and gateway keepalive_pool_size is at default. Reproduced only when concurrency >=10 and average context length >5k tokens.

Issue summary:
Customer reported that long-running streaming responses (SSE and websocket) intermittently stop emitting the final closing tokens/paragraph when the client's apparent source IP changes mid-stream (observed during mobile carrier handoffs and corporate proxy rebinds). The stream appears to resume (client reconnect succeeds) but the final terminal chunk or closing metadata is missing, leaving partial output and a perpetually open client state.

Impact:
- Several TextFlow.ai jobs observed truncated summaries in ~2-4% of long streaming sessions (>= 60s).
- Affects user-facing text generation features (document summaries, long chat responses) for the customer; customers report incorrect UX (missing last paragraph).
- Customer is on a Dedicated plan; issue escalated because production traffic is impacted.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-east-1 (redwood-dedicated-us-east-4).
- Affected app: TextFlow.ai ingestion pipeline using streaming SSE for incremental updates.
- Observed on both SSE and websocket transports.
- Upstream load balancer: customer-facing ALB with source NAT and short session affinity cookie (60s).

Steps to reproduce (observed / test case):
1) Start a streaming generation request that produces ~75-120s of output from redwood-4-8b model via SSE.
2) Midway through the stream, simulate an IP path change (e.g., client moves from WiFi to cellular or a short proxy restart that changes downstream source IP).
3) Client reconnects using the same auth token and reconnect logic; server accepts new connection.
4) Observe that stream resumes but the final closing metadata event or last sentence is missing; client SDK remains waiting for termination marker.

Observed behavior:
- Client receives reconnect ack and intermediate chunks after rejoin but never receives the terminal "end" event / final metadata envelope.
- Server logs show a new connection accepted for the same session-id but no application-level resume token is associated with it; the worker treats it as a fresh session and drains partial generator state without sending closing envelope.
- No 5xx from API gateway; connection lifecycle shows ALB connection rebind and a new TCP connection to edge.

Expected behavior:
- After reconnect, server should reattach to existing stream state (via resume token or explicit session id) and re-emit pending chunks including the final closing metadata so client completes cleanly.

Relevant logs/traces:
- Trace IDs from affected customer runs: trace-20260310-73a1, trace-20260310-73a2, trace-20260310-73b9.
- Edge/worker logs excerpt (anonymized):
  - edge-conn: accepted new socket from 54.210.12.77 for session:none token:missing
  - sidecar: session-mapper: affinity=ip-cookie mismatch, fallback=false
  - runtime: generator-id=gf-19f stop-detected: partial-flush, no-terminal-envelope
- Grafana dash: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/stream-handovers?var=pool=redwood-dedicated-us-east-4 (spike in connection rebinds at 2026-03-10T14:43UTC)

Attachments:
- Customer-provided SDK log (trimmed): textflow_sse_log_20260310.txt
- PCAP from customer's edge-side proxy (shared privately)

Notes:
- Customer has implemented exponential reconnect/backoff and uses auth tokens per session; they do not supply an explicit session-id header by default (rely on token-derived mapping).
- Problem seems correlated with short ALB affinity cookie timeouts and NAT changes that present a new source IP to our edge within the same auth token window.
2026-03-10 15:02 UTC - Support (Maya Chen): Logged ticket after customer provided SDK logs and PCAP. Initial hypothesis: proxy/LB rebind is creating a new socket that our sidecar fails to map back to session state.
2026-03-10 16:18 UTC - SRE (Ravi Menon): Reproduced locally against staging ded pool by forcing IP rebind; saw same behavior. Worker logs show session mapping dropped when 'x-forwarded-for' changes and no explicit resume token present.
2026-03-10 18:05 UTC - Eng (Jordan Lee): Investigated sidecar session-mapper. Found code path where affinity=false branch early-returns without attaching resume token to new connection. Pushed a diagnostic change to log more details: PR #2891.
2026-03-11 09:21 UTC - Support (Maya Chen): Sent workaround to customer: advise setting explicit x-session-id header per streaming request to ensure deterministic reattach across IP changes while we validate fix. Customer confirmed they can add header and will test this afternoon.
2026-03-11 14:45 UTC - Customer (TextFlow.ai, Elena Rivera): After adding x-session-id header, we saw 0 truncated sessions in 1200 streams. Will keep monitoring for 24h. Thanks.
2026-03-11 18:50 UTC - Eng (Ravi Menon): Short-term fix merged to canary; changes ensure resume token is validated/attached on rebind even when affinity differs. Scheduled staged rollout to dedicated pools next 48h. Created follow-up INT-4510 to add integration tests and harden mapping logic.
2026-03-11 19:02 UTC - Support (Maya Chen): Updating ticket status to In Progress; assigned to Ravi for rollout and verification.
Hypothesis 1: ALB/NAT path change causes source IP mismatch and our session-mapper uses strict IP affinity when resume-token absent -> new socket not linked to generator state.
Hypothesis 2: Short affinity cookie triggers LB to route to a different edge instance; edge expects resume token in handshake but client SDK doesn't always send explicit session id, causing session to be treated as new.
Confirmed reproduction in staging with ip-move script that opens a second connection with different source port & NAT. Observed runtime generator state alive but detached from new connection (no terminal envelope).
Heap/worker dump analysis: generator state persisted (KV cache intact) and downstream flush executed but sidecar did not forward terminal envelope back to reattached socket due to missing mapping.
Temporary workaround: customer to include explicit x-session-id header on streaming requests; this forces deterministic reattachment across IP/path changes. Engineering change: relax strict IP-only affinity in sidecar session-mapper and ensure resume-token attachment path is executed when a valid resume token or explicit session-id header is present. A small change merged to canary (PR https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2891). Plan: rollout to dedicated canary -> progressively to all dedicated pools in 48 hours; monitor truncated-streams rate.
INT-4510: Add end-to-end test for IP-affinity change + session-id reattach in CI (assigned to QA)
Add dashboard alert: stream-terminal-missing-rate > 0.5% over 30m for dedicated pools (observability)
Postmortem/KB: write short KB for Solutions team with recommended client-side mitigation (session-id header) and link to SDK sample

Issue Summary
- Customer (Acme AI, route experiments beta) reports that experiment results in Console are inconsistent when using streaming responses. Specifically, p95/p99 latency and cost/token charts show a large percentage of traffic under “Unknown / unattributed” despite the route being under an active experiment.
- Customer verified they are receiving variant headers intermittently on streaming responses.

Customer Impact
- Console experiment dashboards appear incomplete/incorrect (variant comparison not trustworthy).
- Guardrail evaluation confidence reduced because unattributed traffic is excluded from per-variant aggregations.
- Customer is holding ramp from 10% -> 50% until attribution is reliable.

Environment
- Redwood Hosted API via Dedicated capacity.
- Regions: primarily us-east; customer also observed similar behavior after failover to eu-west.
- Endpoints: /v1/chat/completions with streaming enabled.
- Client: Redwood Python SDK + custom retry wrapper (retries on network disconnect / 5xx / upstream timeout).

Expected
- For every request routed under an experiment, experiment_id + variant_id should be present:
  - In response headers (for debugging) where applicable.
  - In request context so OTel spans + metrics emit {route_id, experiment_id, variant_id} consistently.
  - Persisted across streaming lifecycle and across retry paths (including internal re-attempts).

Actual
- Non-streaming requests show near-100% attribution.
- Streaming requests show missing experiment_id/variant_id in:
  - OTel spans for a subset of requests.
  - Aggregated metrics (rollups) feeding Console results.
- Missing rate increases when a retry occurs (disconnect mid-stream or gateway retry).

Steps to Reproduce (internal)
1) Enable a route experiment on a chat route (A=baseline model, B=variant model).
2) Send streaming chat completions with a forced intermittent disconnect (tcp reset or client cancel) to trigger retry logic.
3) Compare:
   - Gateway/router logs: request_id -> selected variant.
   - OTel traces: check for experiment_id/variant_id attributes on root span and streaming child spans.
   - Metrics rollups: attributed vs unattributed counts for the same time window.

Initial Triage Notes (Support + Telemetry)
- Hypothesis A: experiment_id/variant_id set on initial request context but lost when stream is handed off to async writer / span context changes.
- Hypothesis B: retry code path creates a new request context without copying experiment assignment fields.
- Hypothesis C: sampling / cardinality protections dropping tags (less likely; customer observes missing even in traces, not just metrics).

What we checked
- Console Results API confirms high “attribution drop rate” for streaming routes only.
- Router debug endpoint (internal) for same stickiness key shows stable assignment (determinism OK).
- Correlated unattributed spans with “streaming retry” logs; strong correlation.

Workaround (shared with customer)
- Temporary: disable client-side retries on mid-stream disconnects OR retry with a new request_id but include an explicit, stable stickiness key header to reduce confusing partial aggregates.
- Not a true fix; attribution still missing on some internal retry flows.

Engineering Escalation
- Owner: Telemetry/Tracing (Caleb Johnson) with Router context plumbing review (Vikram Singh / Jordan Lee as needed).
- Requested: verify request context propagation across streaming + retry, ensure experiment attribution fields are attached to:
  - Root request span
  - Streaming chunk spans (if present)
  - Any retry attempt spans

Resolution
- Fix implemented in github:redwood/pr-28622-fix-attribution-missing-on-streaming-retries.
  - Summary (from PR): ensure experiment dimensions persist across retry paths for streaming requests; copy experiment attribution fields into retried request context and ensure span attributes set before stream writer takes over.
- Rollout:
  - Deployed to staging: 2025-03-03
  - Deployed to prod us-east: 2025-03-05
  - Deployed to prod eu-west: 2025-03-06

Validation
- Post-deploy: attribution drop rate on Acme AI route experiments reduced from ~18–25% (streaming) to <1%.
- Customer confirmed variant headers now present consistently on streaming responses; Console results updated within the expected aggregation window.

Follow-ups
- Add regression test for streaming + retry attribution in ENG-9031 style E2E suite (suggested to Console/Platform).
- Ensure docs call out that variant headers may be omitted on certain error responses, but attribution should still be present in telemetry.

---
Comments / Timeline

2025-02-28 09:12 PT — Rafael Mendes (Reporter)
Customer report from Acme AI (beta). Seeing ~20% unattributed traffic on experiment results, only when streaming enabled. Non-streaming is fine.

2025-02-28 10:03 PT — Caleb Johnson (Assignee)
Ack. Pulling traces + comparing streaming vs non-streaming. Suspect context not being copied to retry attempt spans.

2025-03-01 14:20 PT — Logan Wright
Confirmed correlation with retry path. When stream reconnect/retry occurs, the new attempt span lacks experiment_id/variant_id. Routing decision logs still show variant selection.

2025-03-03 11:47 PT — Caleb Johnson
Fix up in PR: github:redwood/pr-28622-fix-attribution-missing-on-streaming-retries. Adds explicit context copy + ensures span attributes set pre-stream handoff. Staging looks good.

2025-03-05 16:05 PT — Rafael Mendes
Prod us-east rollout completed. Watching attribution drop dashboard; trending down.

2025-03-06 09:30 PT — Rafael Mendes
Customer confirmed. Closing as Resolved; leaving internal follow-up to add E2E test coverage.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent websocket sessions where, after an LB-induced connection handoff, the resumed stream contains duplicated metadata control frames (choice/metadata events repeated) and is missing the final terminal tokens for the last choice. This leads to downstream parsers seeing duplicate 'choice' blocks followed by a truncated final sentence.

Impact:
- Production traffic for a small set of enterprise customers experiences incomplete final output in ~0.2% of streams for long responses (>2k tokens).
- Downstream consumer logic de-duplicates metadata, which in some cases causes the last choice to be discarded entirely (customer-visible content loss).
- Customer has reported user-facing failures in a document-generation flow (FinSight Analytics) and is requesting urgency.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east region behind CloudFront -> NGINX LB (ephemeral connections enabled) -> websocket-proxy -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime.
- Customer traffic uses pinned model redwood-gemini-xt-1.2 and fallback to open-llama-13b-q4.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a long streaming generation (seeded prompt that produces ~3k tokens).
2) Force an LB connection flip (reproduce by toggling health check to trigger connection migration on the WB proxy or briefly cut TCP).
3) Client reconnects with existing session-token and resumes.
4) Server emits continuation events plus a small set of metadata/choice control frames; during some handoffs the client receives duplicate metadata frames followed by an abrupt end-of-stream with no terminal tokens.

Observed logs / snippets (redacted):
- websocket-proxy logs around handoff: "Handoff sessionToken=abc123 -> reused on new conn; old_conn_fd closed"
- api-gateway: "resume_request sessionToken=abc123 offset=2350"
- serving-runtime trace: "resume: emitted continuation chunk id=0..4; flushed meta-frame:choice-start" then "meta-frame:choice-start" (duplicate) then "EOS without terminal-token"

Initial investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: session-token reuse + non-idempotent resume path causes the serving-runtime to send both a leftover buffered meta frame and a fresh meta frame after reconnection (duplicate).
- Hypothesis 2: a race during handshake makes the gateway interpret the reconnection as a fresh session and also replay the tail of the old stream leading to overlapping fragments and truncated terminal tokens.
- Reproducible in canary when artificially inducing LB flips; rate is low and depends on exact timing of KV cache flush and handshake completion.
- Correlated with specific LB configuration that uses short keepalive and immediate connection teardown (NGINX proxy_running_v1.14 with upstream keepalive=1).

Immediate mitigation proposed:
- Add defensive deduplication in websocket-proxy: drop immediate back-to-back identical meta frames within X ms for the same session-token.
- Add a small grace window on resume to wait for any outstanding frames from previous connection (100ms) before sending fresh metadata.
- Customer workaround: enable short-term non-strict resume on client (client-side ignore exact duplicate meta frames) while we deploy server fix.

Next steps:
- SRE to reproduce reliably in staging with LB flip harness (assigned).
- Serving runtime team to add logging around resume idempotency (PR reference in linked PRs).
- Engineering to test metadata dedupe patch on websocket-proxy in canary for 48h before wider rollout.

Expected ETA for hotfix deployment: 2026-03-15 if tests pass.

Please see related PRs and runbook link for more artifacts.
Recreated locally with LB flip script; observed duplicate meta frames in pcap and runtime traces. KV cache eviction window aligns with race where both old connection flush and new resume send meta frames. Running an instrumented build of websocket-proxy (branch: ws-resume-dedupe) with 50ms suppress window eliminated duplicates in 200/200 test runs. Need further canary and backward-compat checks for heartbeat and multiplexed sessions.
Patch prepared for websocket-proxy to suppress identical metadata frames within a 100ms window for the same session-token (PR #4821). Serving-runtime will add a resume token monotonic counter to avoid replaying the same metadata frame (PR #4839). Planning canary deploy 2026-03-13; post-canary rollout if no regressions. Customer notified of workaround and will enable client-side dedupe in the interim.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 08:45 - Customer (FinSight Support Contact): Customer accepted temporary client-side dedupe; requested ETA for server-side fix and canary results.

Issue summary: After a recent behind-the-scenes schema change in how function/tool calls are encoded by the SDKs, a small subset of multiplexed streaming clients experienced duplicate external tool invocations. Impact: Customer reports duplicate downstream side-effects (duplicate job creations and webhook deliveries) for requests that were retried/resumed across SDK versions. Environment: Dedicated cluster in prod (us-west-2), customer uses multiplexed WebSocket streams with mixed clients (python 1.8.x and typescript 2.0.x). Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a multiplexed streaming session from a long-lived Node client (TS 2.0.1) and a Python client (1.8.4) to the same customer session.
2) Send a function/tool call that includes a confirmation ack expectation and an idempotency-derived key (default SDK behavior).
3) While the stream is in flight, trigger a client reconnect from the Python side (simulate flaky network).
4) Observe two downstream tool invocations for the same logical request id in the customer's system within ~15s.
Observed behavior: Two calls to the customer's webhook/service with equivalent payloads but different idempotency baggage values. Logs show the server accepted both as distinct invocations. Expected behavior: Retry/resume/reconnect should not produce duplicate external side-effects when idempotency keys or confirmation tokens identify the request as already-executed.
Additional notes: The customer is on Dedicated and has reserved capacity; traffic spike did not trigger autoscaling-related fallbacks. The duplicates correlate to sessions where client SDK versions were mixed (older Python + newer TS) and where a proxy (edge/ingress) performed a small payload rewrite (normalization of function argument field names).
Open a multiplexed session with mixed SDK versions (TS + Python)
Send a function call with default idempotency baggage
Induce a client reconnect/resume from one client
Observe duplicate downstream invocations in customer system
request_id=6f23b8a2-9c4a-4f2a-8d21-0b5c86f7e9d4 - server accepted invocation (stream seq 42)
request_id=6f23b8a2-9c4a-4f2a-8d21-0b5c86f7e9d4 - duplicate invocation (stream seq 47)
edge-proxy trace: header rewrite applied: func_name->function_name
customer webhook payloads: uuid=job_204, payload checksum matches

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:03 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Requested raw stream logs and request IDs. Asked customer to provide timeframe and sample request_id.
2026-03-10 11:20 - Customer (InstaDoc - DevOps): Provided request_id 6f23b8a2-... and said duplicates happen ~30% of reconnections. Using node-ts 2.0.1 and python-sdk 1.8.4 mixed in same session.
Confirmed mixed SDK versions produce different canonicalization outputs for identical semantic calls.
Edge proxy normalizer rewrote function argument key from 'func_name' to 'function_name' which changed canonical payload ordering in our serializer.
Idempotency baggage is computed as base64(sha256(namespace||canonical_payload)). Namespace includes SDK version for telemetry; older SDKs used 'sdk:py:1.8.4', newer used 'sdk:ts:2.0.1'.
Reproduced duplicate external webhook delivery in dedicated cluster when reconnect path resumed and server accepted both sequences as new invocations.
No sign of server-side dedup config being incorrectly applied; root cause is key derivation mismatch upstream of dedup check.
Customer-facing side-effects (duplicate job creation and webhook delivery). Affects customers using mixed SDK stacks and edge payload normalizers. Rate: ~20-30% of reconnect/resume events for affected sessions. No platform-wide outage; limited to sessions with mismatched SDK canonicalization and proxy rewrites.
Advise customer to: 1) pin SDK versions to a single major for all multiplexed clients in the same session; 2) disable edge payload rewrite for function call fields; OR 3) set explicit idempotency_key in tool call metadata (application-managed) until patch is deployed.
Engineering will: 1) land a patch to SDKs and server to decouple idempotency baggage namespace from SDK version (PR referenced below), 2) add tolerant canonicalization that ignores harmless key renames when computing dedup keys, and 3) add server-side heuristic that compares payload semantic equality if dedup keys conflict within a short window. Target patch: serving-runtime + SDK hotfix (python 1.8.5, ts 2.0.2).
In progress - PR opened. QA acceptance pending. After patch, we'll run a canary with the customer's traffic and monitor duplicates for 48h. Customer notified and asked to apply temporary workaround.
Merge PRs and release SDK patches (target 2026-03-14)
Coordinate with customer to roll patched SDK to all clients in their sessions
Add alert to detect increases in duplicate webhook deliveries per session

Issue summary:
MindfulAI reports a retroactive billing delta after a scheduled nightly embedding job (daily bulk embed) on 2026-03-09. Several hourly free-buffer credits that normally applied to warmup and microbatching were missing for multiple hourly buckets. The customer sees a +$1,240 provisional charge on the provisional invoice and requests a breakdown and corrective credit.

Impact:
- Customer billed unexpectedly for warmup/idle tokens normally covered by hourly free buffer for 8 hourly buckets on 2026-03-09 US-east run window.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:

2) Postbacks for hourly warmup credits were emitted by edge proxy and forwarded to postback-service.
3) Our postback-service stored tag metadata but later trimmed tag field to 128 chars during normalization. Customer uses long pipeline tags (org+dataset+job+region+user-agent) which exceeded the normalized limit.

When truncation occurs, system should fallback to a heuristic match (prefix search) or surface to reconciliation queue rather than drop credits.

Actual behavior:
Normalization truncates tag to 128 chars, matcher performs exact hash lookup and fails, credits are not reconciled. No automatic fallback or ticketing to reconciliation queue was triggered.

Issue summary: Customer reports sudden drop in rerank quality coincident with increased 5xx/504 responses from the /rerank endpoint. Impact: Search/rerank queries for several CipherHealth production routes are timing out or returning degraded ranking order. Observed after a model catalog update on 2026-03-09.

Immediate impact: Production user flows for clinical content ranking are failing, causing degraded UX and increased support tickets.

Wanted: Root cause analysis and a reliable mitigation path so customer can continue production traffic.
CipherHealth production search/rerank routes experiencing intermittent 5xxs and incorrect ranking ordering from 2026-03-09 14:00 UTC; estimated 12% of requests affected during peak windows, leading to degraded user workflows for clinicians.
1) Use CipherHealth production account to call /embed with model=rwd-embed-large-v2, receive embeddings (client observed length=1536).
2) Send embeddings to /rerank with model=rwd-rerank-v1 and top_k=10.
3) Observe 500/504 errors or a rerank response that places obviously irrelevant results at top (precision drop).
4) Repeat with pinned model rwd-embed-legacy-1 and rerank succeeds with expected quality.
[2026-03-11T16:02:43Z] api-gateway: request POST /rerank 200ms -> 504 upstream timeout
[2026-03-11T16:02:43Z] reranker-service: error validating vector dimensions: expected 2048, got 1536
[2026-03-11T16:02:44Z] serving-runtime: batch worker stalled on embed transform id=0x7f4a; kv-cache not updated
[2026-03-11T16:05:11Z] support: correlation found with model rollout rwd-embed-large-v2 (catalog rev 2026-03-09.3)
[stack snippet] File "reranker.py", line 214, in score_batch
  dot = np.dot(batch_matrix, query_vec)
ValueError: shapes (batch,2048) and (1536,) not aligned
Initial hypothesis: client-side embedding/model mismatch. We confirmed client reported embeddings length 1536 while reranker expects 2048. Timeline aligns with embedding model upgrade (rwd-embed-large-v2).
Deeper finding: the catalog entry for rwd-embed-large-v2 had changed canonical dimension metadata to 1536 but the rerank pipeline configuration (rwd-rerank-v1) cached an older compatibility table expecting 2048. Batching path did not validate dims until the dot-product op, causing upstream timeouts and failed batches.
We also observed a secondary effect: when the batch worker encountered a shape mismatch it retried at the serving-runtime layer, causing long queue hold times and cascading 504s for other requests in the batch pool.
1) Temporary mitigation applied 2026-03-11 19:20 UTC: reverted catalog alias for rwd-embed-large-v2 to previous manifest (pinned to legacy dims).
2) Customer advised to pin embedding model on client side to rwd-embed-legacy-1 until fix rolled.
3) Added an API gateway request validation rule to reject rerank calls where embedding length doesn't match model manifest (400 with clear error).
Deployed compatibility shim in reranker-service on 2026-03-12 04:15 UTC that: validates embedding vector length at ingestion, pads/truncates vectors in a deterministic way when compatible policy allows, and emits metrics when auto-adjustment occurs. Also updated model catalog and reranker config sync logic to invalidate caches on catalog rev increments. Verified CipherHealth traffic stable and rerank quality restored. Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/reranker-service/pull/427. Follow-up: add an alert for embedding-dim mismatch rate >0.1%.

Additional notes:
CipherHealth (Customer): We started seeing wrong top results and occasional timeouts; pinning to legacy embed helped temporarily. Please advise on timeline for permanent fix.
1) Add unit/integration tests to model-catalog CI that assert dimension and compatibility entries make backward-incompatible changes explicit.
2) Add an observable metric and PagerDuty alert for embedding-dim mismatch rate.
3) Postmortem to be published and shared with CipherHealth; include SLA credit evaluation as needed.

comments: 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z Asha Patel: Triage note - gathering logs and SDK versions from customer. Asked for pcap or hex dump of payloads; requested customer reproduce with verbose SDK logging.

2026-03-11T08:47:00Z Liam Chen: Reproduced locally with python-sdk v2.5.1 using simulated connection reset. Observed that the second attempt's protobuf bytes differ when the SDK reuses a pooled buffer in C-extension path. Filed an internal hypothesis and created INT-8891 to track root cause investigation.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that function/tool calls which use protobuf-encoded binary parameters are occasionally getting corrupted after client-side retries. The corruption leads to idempotency-key mismatches and duplicate downstream side-effects (e.g., two invoice creations).

Impact:
- Intermittent duplicate side-effects for production traffic for a subset of requests that send binary params via protobuf.
- Observed only for requests that were retried by the SDK (client-side backoff) and for which the server accepted and executed the original request but the client then retried and sent a mutated protobuf payload.

Environment:
- Customer: CleverDocs Inc. (enterprise, Dedicated cluster in us-east)
- SDKs in use: python-sdk v2.5.1, go-sdk v1.8.0, ts-sdk v3.0.2 (customer reports repro in Python and Go clients)
- API: production endpoint in us-east
- Models: redwood/gpt-compat-13b (function calling enabled)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Create a function call that takes a bytes param (protobuf field bytes attachment = <binary protobuf>).
2) Use python-sdk v2.5.1 with default retry/backoff policy and send a request that triggers a transient connection reset during streaming.
3) Client retries and the function is invoked again. The second invocation has altered binary contents (size off by small number of bytes).
4) Downstream system sees a different attachment payload and treats it as a distinct event, causing duplicate processing.

Observed behavior:
- The first server-side execution is recorded in logs but client sometimes still retries (timeout/EOF on client) and a second execution happens with subtly different protobuf payload bytes. Idempotency key either not matched or mismatched due to binary change.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should either be prevented from causing duplicate downstream effects (idempotent), or payloads should remain identical across retry attempts so idempotency keys remain stable.

Relevant logs/snippets (redacted):
- Client-side stacktrace: socket EOF followed by retry attempt idempotency_key="abc-123"
- Server-side first-exec log: function_call accepted idempotency_key=abc-123 payload_sha256=5f2b...
- Server-side second-exec log: function_call accepted idempotency_key=abc-123 payload_sha256=5f6d...
- Diff of decoded protobuf bytes shows a 3-byte shift near a repeated field boundary.

Workaround suggested by customer so far:
- Disable binary protobuf for parameters and use base64-encoded JSON strings instead. Not ideal due to size/latency and breaks streaming.

Customer impact statement:
- CleverDocs has temporarily throttled some customer flows and is requesting urgent mitigation guidance and a timeline for a fix.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:03 - CleverDocs (Customer): Provided hex dumps of two payloads and a repro script in Python. Customer also noted they can reproduce with Go by toggling the client's keepalive to trigger a connection reset.
2026-03-12 14:20 - Eng (runtime-team): Noted that api-gateway may perform HTTP/2 header coalescing and our gateway edge code path has a legacy protobuf streaming helper that mutates buffers when retries occur. Looking into safe-copy vs zero-copy behavior.
2026-03-13 10:05 - Support (to customer): Temporary mitigation: please use SDK flag REDWOOD_ENABLE_SAFE_BUFFERS=true in client config (available in python-sdk v2.5.2-beta) which forces copies on retry. We can provide a patched wheel. Also suggested switching to JSON-encoded payloads for critical flows.
2026-03-13 16:30 - CleverDocs: Applied the beta wheel, initial repro attempts did not reproduce duplication in 6k test runs. Customer requests a formal patch and postmortem once root cause confirmed.
Hypothesis 1: client-side SDK buffer reuse in C extension causes mutated buffers on retry; older SDK versions did not defensively copy when streaming resumed.
Hypothesis 2: api-gateway health check or HTTP/2 reset can cause partial frame consumption that our streaming helper tries to reassemble, and a race causes a shifted byte offset in repeated fields.
Reproduction: Created unit test that simulates connection reset between frames. With python-sdk v2.5.1 reproduced altered protobuf after retry. Upgrading to v2.5.2-beta with safe-copy flag prevented corruption in test harness.
Correlated evidence: payload_sha diffs consistently show a small delta near repeated field boundaries; binary inspection shows missing 0x08 marker occasionally (suggesting index shift).
Related artifacts: linked INT-8891 contains kernel traces and memory-slab diagnostics for the python native extension.
Short-term mitigation: Published python-sdk v2.5.2-beta with REDWOOD_ENABLE_SAFE_BUFFERS which forces copy-on-retry for protobuf payloads. Provided patched wheel to customer and advised rollout to affected clients.
Medium-term fix: engineering to land safe-copy in the SDK stable branch and add end-to-end tests that fuzz retries across HTTP/2 reset scenarios. Runtime team to harden gateway streaming helper to avoid in-place buffer mutation. Target stable SDK release 2.5.2 on 2026-03-20.
Long-term: add integration checks to CI that validate idempotency-key stability when retries occur, and expand observability to capture payload_sha256 at request intake so mismatches can be detected automatically and routed to a remediation flow (fallback to dedupe).
Follow-ups created: INT-8891 (infrastructure reproduction), INT-8902 (sdk-safe-copy-landing), and a Confluence runbook to handle binary-payload idempotency incidents.
Customer communication: Sent an interim incident summary and mitigation steps on 2026-03-13. Scheduled a follow-up call for 2026-03-15 to coordinate production rollout of the patched wheel.
payload.summary: Protobuf-encoded function-call payloads get corrupted after client retry, causing duplicate downstream side-effects

payload.description:
Customer Nimbus experienced elevated error rates (5xx) on their dedicated cluster during a large embedding upload that impacted production payment risk scoring. Approximately 8-12% of requests returned 5xx between 10:12–10:56 UTC, causing timeouts and failed batched scoring jobs.
Issue summary:
Nimbus Financial reported a sudden rise in 5xx responses for their dedicated deployment while performing a large embedding upload and concurrent chat/embedding traffic. The wave began ~2026-03-10 10:12 UTC and subsided after 10:56 UTC.

Impact:
- Enterprise customer production latency and error budget hit; some scoring pipelines failed and were retried by the customer's orchestrator.
- Customer reported degraded UX for internal dashboards tied to inference results.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster (tenant: nimbus-prod) in us-east-1
- Serving runtime version: 2026.02.3
- GPU image: rwinf/dedicated-gpu:2026-02-12 (NVML v460-driver)
- API gateway cluster version: apigw-3.1.1

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Customer uploaded a ~1.8M-vector embedding batch (multipart upload) at 10:10 UTC.
2) Simultaneous live chat traffic persisted to the same tenant (~120 concurrent streams).
3) Within ~2 minutes, apigw accept queue length increased and 502/503 responses started to spike.
4) Multiple serving runtime replicas reported NVML soft-resets and then restarts; apigw observed upstream resets and returned 502s.

Observed behavior:
- Apigw 502/503/504 spike correlated with GPU driver soft-reset spikes in telemetry.
- Keepalive counts dropped for upstream runtime sockets; accept queue grew.
- Prefetch cancellations and embedding shard rebalancer ran while the driver reset sequence occurred, leading to increased downstream retries and backpressure.

Expected behavior:
- Large embedding uploads should be rate-limited and isolated by the scheduler to avoid cascading soft-resets on shared GPUs. Runtime restarts should not cause sustained apigw 5xx floors.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- We advised the customer to stagger their large embedding upload and reduce chunk concurrency.
- Support temporarily pinned their tenant to a separate dedicated GPU pool while investigation proceeds.
[2026-03-10T10:14:02Z] runtime-42 NVML_SOFT_RESET detected GPU0
[2026-03-10T10:14:03Z] runtime-42 heartbeat lost, restarting worker
[2026-03-10T10:14:04Z] apigw-2 upstream-reset upstream=runtime-42 status=502 accept_queue=115
[2026-03-10T10:15:10Z] scheduler prefetch-cancel tenant=nimbus-prod shard=12 reason=worker-unavailable
[2026-03-10T10:16:30Z] kernel-selection-fallback: quant-kernel -> slow-path (incr latency)

Initial triage (Asha): correlated apigw 5xx spike with NVML soft-reset bursts across three runtime pods. Dashboard (grafana/embed-prod) shows NVML reset rate jumped at 10:13.
SRE (Diego): observed accept_queue growth on apigw and half-open upstream sockets; apigw timed out on hedged requests, amplified by client's retry logic.
Runtime team: driver logs show a pattern consistent with a long-running NVMe GC on host combined with a GPU watchdog throttle triggering soft-resets during heavy NVMe IO. Embedding upload triggered heavy NVMe writes for checkpointing embedding shards, which coincided with GPU driver scheduling delays.
Scheduler team: the dedicated scheduler allowed high multipart concurrency (default burst=20) for this tenant; this allowed many simultaneous GPU-intensive shard writes causing IO and GPU contention.
Hypothesis: a combined IO/GPU contention window caused NVML soft-resets; the restarts reduced available upstream capacity which pushed apigw into accept-queue saturation and 5xx responses. Hedged retries and the customer's upload concurrency amplified the backpressure.
Evidence: NVML reset timestamps align within 10s of apigw 502 spikes; NVMe iowait metrics increased ~5x during the window.
Next diagnostic steps: capture full runtime nvml logs, collect host dmesg, and reproduce with controlled embedding-burst in staging with same image and scheduler settings.

Additional notes:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-11):
- Temporarily moved Nimbus to isolated dedicated pool to restore production traffic.
- Reduced default multipart upload concurrency for dedicated scheduler to 6 for customers with >1TB shard activity.
- Released runtime image patch v2026.02.4 that adds guarded NVML watchdog backoff and better checkpoint IO yielding.
- Configured apigw to increase upstream keepalive timeout and reduce immediate hedged retry for affected tenant.
Status: Partial fix deployed (driver/ runtime patch + scheduler conservative defaults). Full RCA pending after host-level logs analyzed and NVMe mitigation validated. Follow-up owner: Priya Nair.
Backport runtime patch v2026.02.4 to all dedicated GPU images (owner: Priya Nair)
Add alert: NVML_soft_reset_rate > 3/min for any tenant -> paging SRE (owner: Diego Morales)
Audit scheduler burst defaults for dedicated clusters and create a safer default policy (owner: Scheduler team)
Run controlled embedding-burst test in staging with NVMe IO profiling and document threshold (owner: Runtime + Perf)
Confluence: write postmortem and guidance for customers on safe large-embedding uploads (owner: Customer Success)
Follow up with Nimbus on billing credits and confirmation their pipelines are healthy (owner: Samantha Kim)
payload.summary: Unexpected 5xx delta after large embedding upload: GPU driver soft-reset correlated with apigw overload

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasHealth reports that during a scheduled regional edge reshuffle (us-west), a subset of long-running sessions lost their model version pin and were routed to a fallback variant with degraded generation quality. The event coincided with a canary weight adjustment and an autoscaler preempt/rebalance in the region.

Impact:
- ~12 session streams (of a ~3k tenant cohort) observed abrupt model switch from gptx-8k-v1 (pinned) to gptx-16k-quant fallback.
- Customer saw quality regressions and 5 user-facing incidents (incorrect diagnoses in an internal triage flow).
- No billing disparity reported, but SLA risk for enterprise customer during scheduled maintenance window.

Environment:
- prod cluster: us-west primary, failover us-east
- Tenant: AtlasHealth (enterprise), requests use pinned_model header + session affinity cookie
- Canary rollout in same window: weight shift from 0% -> 10% for new variant of gptx-8k-v1

Observed behavior:
- Edge reshuffle triggered short-lived reinitialization of some sidecar connections.
- Affected sessions show token refresh and Set-Cookie mutation in edge logs immediately prior to pin loss.
- Orchestrator snapshots show that pin metadata remained in control-plane for tenant; however several front-line proxy nodes served traffic without pin-preserving cookie.

Expected behavior:
- Model pin should be preserved for session lifetime across edge node reshuffles and autoscaler rebalance events.
- Fallback routing should only occur when pin is explicitly unbound or when model variant is unavailable, with clear audit trail.

Steps to reproduce (attempted):
1) Start a long-running pinned session for tenant with pinned_model=gptx-8k-v1 and affinity cookie.
2) Initiate a regional edge reshuffle (simulate node drain) while canary weight shift starts.
3) Observe session cookies, Set-Cookie headers, and routing decisions on ingress nodes.
4) Replay identical requests through affected edge node to see if pin is honored.

Logs / Artifacts:
- Edge logs (us-west) attached in artifact: edge-reshuffle-uswest-2026-03-10.tar.gz (traces/headers for affected session IDs).
- Orchestrator snapshot: orchestrator-snap-2026-03-10-23:12
- Session-store traces showing affinity lease renewals for impacted session IDs.

Timeline summary:
- 2026-03-10 22:58 UTC: Canary weight adjustment started for cohort that overlaps AtlasHealth tenant.
- 2026-03-10 22:59 UTC: Autoscaler in us-west preempted two low-priority nodes (spot reclaim), triggering an edge reshuffle.
- 2026-03-10 23:00 UTC: Multiple sidecar reconnects seen; Set-Cookie header mutated in 7 of 12 affected session streams.

Hypotheses evaluated:
- Hypothesis A: Orchestrator unbound pins during snapshot merge. Rejected: control-plane shows pin metadata unchanged.
- Hypothesis B: Edge-proxy header sanitizer mutated or dropped the pin cookie during reconnect. Supported by logs showing sidecar rewrite of cookie domain and cookie attributes (HttpOnly -> missing).
- Hypothesis C: Health probe grace period mismatch allowed edge to declare variant unhealthy and trigger fallback routing for live sessions. Partially supported: healthcheck spike correlates with 429/5xx on a small subset of model backends.

Partial findings:
- The cookie mutation occurred only on nodes running edge-proxy v2.4.1 with new cookie normalization codepath. Older nodes preserved cookies.
- A small race between session-lease renewal and sidecar reattach meant the session-store marked the session as 'orphaned' momentarily, enabling fallback logic.
- Canary weight shift increased routing churn and made race window more likely.

Immediate mitigation applied (2026-03-11 00:30 UTC):
- Rolled back edge-proxy normalization flag on impacted nodes to preserve cookie attributes.
- Increased session-lease grace to 6s from 2s for affected fleet as emergency measure.

Next steps planned:
- Engineering to revert the cookie normalization changes or add explicit pin-preserve exceptions in edge-proxy. PR to follow.
- Adjust canary rollouts to avoid overlapping with regional rebalances for enterprise tenants by adding blackout window.
- Add stronger invariants: edge must consult control-plane pin store before allowing fallback for pinned sessions.

In progress: temporary mitigations (edge-proxy flag rollback + session-lease grace increase) restored pin stability for AtlasHealth sessions; full fix requires an edge-proxy code patch to preserve pin cookies during reconnect and a scheduler change to avoid canary-rebalance overlap. Engineering draft PR created and scheduled for staged rollout. Post-incident follow-up: propose new canary blackout window policy for enterprise tenants and update runbook to include cookie-preserve check.
Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer reported sudden model swaps during our scheduled window; provided session IDs and sample outputs. Logged as P1 given enterprise SLA.
Raj Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Initial triage points to edge cookie mutation during sidecar reconnect. Pulling edge logs and orchestrator snapshots.
Anika Verma (Eng - Edge) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced cookie rewrite on edge-proxy v2.4.1 when running cookie-normalization enabled. Preparing rollback and patch to skip normalization for "pin" cookies.
Raj Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Emergency rollback of normalization flag complete for us-west, observing pins stable in monitored cohort (10/10 sessions remain pinned after rollback).
Customer (AtlasHealth - Support Contact: Jorge Alvarez) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed that previously affected workflows are now returning to expected models; requested root cause and prevention steps.
Anika Verma (Eng - Edge) - 2026-03-12: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1123 adds explicit pin cookie whitelist and strengthens cookie attr preservation during reconnects. Scheduling staged rollout to canary subset next week.
Priya Das (Product) - 2026-03-12: Recommend we add enterprise blackout policy to canary scheduler and update customer-facing maintenance page to list blackout windows. Filing follow-up ticket to product backlog.
payload.summary: Unexpected model-pin eviction after regional edge reshuffle causing cascading fallbacks
