payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent stream stalls and downstream 504/502 responses during long-running streaming completions. Impact: Several of ByteCart's production endpoints experienced short periods where streaming sessions received no bytes for 10-40s and then aborted with 502 or 504; user-facing failures and cancellations increased ~4x during windows. Environment: Dedicated route in prod (us-east-1) serving redwood-chat-2b pinned model. Observed during peak morning traffic windows. Hypothesis: API gateway / LB is buffering/coalescing small chunks while per-connection header metadata (tracing/tenant headers) grows over time, hitting internal buffering thresholds or idle-send timers which then trigger resets.
1) Use ByteCart's production route in us-east-1 with long streaming completion (>60s) and client that sends frequent small chunked requests and rotates an X-Trace header per chunk. 2) Observe TTFB and streaming health via curl/wget with --no-buffer or via the SDK. 3) During load, watch for idle periods where no bytes are forwarded for 10-40s and then connection resets with 502/504. 4) Reproduction was confirmed on a canary traffic profile that mimicked ByteCart's chunking pattern.
[2026-03-10T08:43:11Z] apigw: conn=0x7ff3 buffer_len=8192 idle_send_timer=30s header_size=12KB route=bytecart-prod
[2026-03-10T08:43:51Z] apigw: conn=0x7ff3 idle_send_timeout fired, resetting downstream
[2026-03-10T08:43:51Z] alb-us-east-1: target returned 502 (net/http: connection reset by peer)
[2026-03-10T08:44:12Z] s-replay: client small-chunk 256B every 150ms; trace-id rotated every 2s
[2026-03-10T08:44:12Z] svc-serving: kv-cache-warmup in-progress, increased latency 2-3x

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:40 - Customer (ByteCart): We see user cancellations and some 502s on our dashboard. Can you confirm whether changing header rotation frequency is a recommended workaround?
Reproduced: Yes — reproduced in our canary environment when client rotated a 2KB tracing header every 1-2s and sent frequent 256B body chunks. When aggregated header metadata exceeded the apigw internal coalescing threshold, apigw deferred sends and triggered idle-send timers.
Observed correlation with serving-runtime KV cache warmup. During warmup latencies spike and request pacing increases; that combination increases buffering pressure in apigw, causing longer coalescing windows.
Heap/descriptor usage on apigw nodes peaked during the window but did not OOM. No 5xx at serving-runtime level; errors were introduced by proxy resets at the load balancer layer.
Config review: ALB idle timeout defaulted to 60s for customer route. Apigw had proxy_buffering enabled for performance; this interacts poorly with high-frequency small-chunk uploads and rotating headers.
Mitigation tested: disabling proxy_buffering eliminates silent periods in local repro. Increasing ALB idle timeout prevents premature connection reset but does not eliminate buffering-induced pauses.
Next steps: 1) implement route-level apigw config toggle for proxy_buffering per-customer, 2) add telemetry to measure header-growth and buffered bytes per-connection, 3) add note to runbook about interaction with KV-cache warmup and small-chunk workloads.
Mitigation applied: For ByteCart's dedicated route we disabled apigw proxy_buffering and increased ALB idle timeout to 90s (infra PR-4281). Short-term outcome: streaming failures dropped by ~90% in the monitored window; remaining stalls correlated with KV-cache warmup which we are investigating. Long-term plan: expose proxy_buffering toggle per-route, add per-connection buffered_bytes metric to Console, and update runbook. Follow-up owner: Mateo Ruiz (SRE) to validate changes over 72h and schedule a postmortem if residual customer impact persists. Customer will confirm closure after 72h monitoring.
payload.summary: API LB buffering + header growth causing in-flight streaming starvation and intermittent 504/502s

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent failures when fetching large model shard ranges from S3-backed presigned URLs using a private deployment behind a branch-office HTTP-CONNECT tunneling proxy. The customer's proxy rewrites HTTP responses and is observed injecting Alt-Svc/HTTP3/QUIC hints into 200 responses. Impact: Several tens of range GETs for large shards are returning 403/416/connection reset or large delays, leading to degraded warmup and increased token latency for hosted inference. Impact window appears correlated with branch-office work hours.

Environment: Private deployment (VPCE-connected nodes) in us-east-1, customers use a branch-office HTTP-CONNECT tunneling proxy for egress that performs response header rewriting and an ALPN/alt-svc cache. Customer reports the proxy is managed by their corporate networking team and is not under Redwood control.

Observed behavior: During incidents the client attempts to negotiate HTTP/3 (QUIC) to the S3 endpoint after seeing Alt-Svc. QUIC traffic is either blocked by an upstream firewall or misrouted by the customer's WAN optimizer. QUIC fail leads to connection resets and racey range re-requests, sometimes resulting in presigned host mismatch errors (403) when a follow-up attempt is routed via a different NAT public IP/ALPN mapping.

Expected behavior: The egress proxy should not inject Alt-Svc hints for presigned S3 responses passing through a CONNECT tunnel. Range downloads should remain over the established TCP/TLS channel or correctly fall back without losing auth or range semantics.

Reproducibility: Intermittent but reproducible under customer's branch-office network conditions. We can trigger by forcing large-range downloads from a client behind the proxy while the proxy's alt-svc cache is populated.
1) From a host behind customer HTTP-CONNECT tunneling proxy, request a presigned S3 range GET for a large model shard (multi-GB range or multipart range sequence)
2) Observe response headers returned by the proxy to the client (look for Alt-Svc: h3="" or Alt-Svc entries pointing to same host)
3) Watch client network stack: client attempts HTTP/3/QUIC handshake to S3 host after seeing Alt-Svc hint
4) If QUIC is blocked or rewriten mid-handshake by WAN device, note resulting behavior: TCP/TLS reset, 403 presigned host mismatch on re-request, or range reassembly failures (416)
Timestamp 2026-03-10T14:02:05Z serving-node-1234 curl -I "https://s3-us-east-1.amazonaws.com/fetch/presigned-obj?X-Amz-Algorithm=..."
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 1048576
Alt-Svc: h3=":443"; ma=2592000
---
Client-side quic log: connection failed: 0x2 (version_negotiation) after 62ms
Client retry via TCP: GET range -> 403 Forbidden (signature mismatch: request seen from different egress IP)
Initial triage: reproduced by engineering using customer-provided proxy VM image; proxy rewrites and injects Alt-Svc headers into CONNECT responses for caching/optimization reasons.
Network tracing: QUIC packets were sent but dropped by customer WAN optimizer; TCP fallback attempts performed but some retries used a different NAT mapping leading to presigned signature mismatch (403)
Serving runtime: no evidence of shard corruption on Redwood side; S3 logs show multiple short-lived QUIC SYN-like attempts followed by aborted GETs, then a small number of valid GETs that returned 403 due to signature mismatch (client IP changed)
Hypothesis: Proxy's Alt-Svc injection plus asymmetric NAT/NAT64 in branch traffic causes QUIC attempt followed by re-request with different source address/port, invalidating presigned URL signature window and range semantics.
Related: customer uses a corporate transparent proxy that caches Alt-Svc and rewrites host headers for optimization under heavy load; we suspect this optimization is intended for web traffic but breaks signed S3 range fetch semantics when used in CONNECT mode.
Ask customer to disable Alt-Svc/HTTP3 header injection for CONNECT-tunneled responses or add an exception for S3 endpoints / our artifact domain. If disabling globally isn't possible, whitelist presigned hostnames so proxy returns original headers. Alternatively, increase presigned URL enforcement tolerance by issuing presigned URLs bound to egress IP ranges (if acceptable to customer security), or ensure NAT stability for branch egress so retried requests retain same source address.
Aisha Rahman (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer opened after seeing repeated shard fetch failures during nightly warmup. Provided packet captures and proxy config snippets.
Carlos Mendez (Eng) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed Alt-Svc injection in proxy capture. Spun up test VM and reproduced QUIC handshake attempts followed by NAT translation changes on re-request.
Customer network lead (FinTechCo) - 2026-03-11: We see proxy logic that rewrites 200 responses and adds Alt-Svc for caching. We can toggle off the optimization but need guidance on safe config.
Carlos Mendez (Eng) - 2026-03-12: Requesting customer to disable Alt-Svc injection for any CONNECT tunnel traffic or exclude s3.amazonaws.com prefix. Proposed workaround documented below.
Support (Aisha) - 2026-03-12: Created INT-324 for internal runbook updates to detect Alt-Svc injected into CONNECT flows and add a diagnostic in our private-deploy health checks.
payload.summary: Branch office HTTP-CONNECT tunnel proxy injects Alt-Svc/HTTP3 causing QUIC fallback and intermittent presigned range fetch failures on private deploy

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers (notably BrightDocs, enterprise tier) reported intermittent 5xx errors on chat and embeddings routes from ~2026-03-10 02:30 UTC onward. Errors present as short bursts (~30s–3m) recurring every ~10–20 minutes. High-level symptoms: apigateway returns 502/503 to clients; runtime processes in the affected shard show recent process aborts with SIGABRT; ephemeral proxy (accept/handoff) shows long syscall latencies and accept-queue growth.

Impact:
- Multiple BrightDocs endpoints experienced degraded availability: ~6% p50->p95 error rate spike during bursts, impacting customer SLAs.
- Several other customers in us-east-1 saw transient elevated 5xx rates (non-global).

Observed timeline (local):
- 02:30 UTC: first client reports; apigw error-rate graph (dash/apigw/errors/us-east) shows spike.
- 02:33 UTC: runtime shard node-14 reported SIGABRT and restarted.
- 02:34–02:36 UTC: ephemeral-proxy accept-queue length increased from <50 to ~1200.
- 02:40 UTC: errors subside; runtimes stabilize after automatic respawn.
- Pattern repeated every ~12 minutes for the following 3 hours.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Simulate steady small-payload streaming + intermittent large-embedding bulk on a tenant in us-east-1.
2) Observe accept-queue growth when embed bulk starts at moderate concurrency (~100 concurrently).
3) After ~30–90s of accept-queue pressure, runtimes exhibit high thread creation latency and occasional aborts.

Key logs/snippets:
- runtime stderr: "pthread_create: Resource temporarily unavailable" followed by immediate abort/backtrace.
- dmesg: no OOM killer entries for GPU memory; kernel reporting short-lived thread creation failures.
- ephemeral-proxy metrics: "accept_queue_wait_seconds_p90" jumps to 8s.

Customer impact note: BrightDocs support rep escalated at 03:05 UTC (ticket #BD-221). They asked for ETA and suggested rate-limiting until root cause fixed.

Expected next actions requested by customer: temporary rate limit on heavy-embedding routes; patch and hotfix to runtime if allocator tuning required.
Initial hypothesis: not a GPU OOM or kernel-level fd exhaustion. Multiple signals point to userland thread allocator/backpressure:
- Repeated "pthread_create" errors inside the runtime process indicate a thread creation failure path rather than file-descriptor exhaustion. FD counts appear within normal ranges.
- Profiling (perf + pstack from coredump) shows runtime stuck in allocator_mmap/arena_lock in jemalloc build path when under accept-queue pressure.
- Ephemeral-proxy exhibited long handoff latencies which increased backlog and caused sudden bursts of concurrent short-lived work items in runtimes; combined with an aggressive thread-creation policy this appears to trigger a resource starvation loop.
- Stress test reproducer created with workload-mix script reproduces the SIGABRT within ~90s when threadpool target is set to 'unbounded' (current default on this shard).

Hypothesis: A combination of accept-queue surge + runtime threadpool unbounded growth + contention inside the chosen allocator (jemalloc) results in failed pthread_create and aborts. On restart, the runtime briefly recovers then the pattern repeats.

Evidence/Artifacts:
- Slack thread: #support (link: https://slack.redwood/support/thread/S-984)
- Dashboards: dash/apigw/errors/us-east (spike graphs), dash/runtime/thread-create-failures/node-14
- Collected coredump: /artifacts/coredump/node-14/2026-03-10-02-33 (uploaded to s3://rbw-incident-coreruns/707707/)
- Reproducer: scripts/reproducers/thread-surge-mix.sh (run under infra/sim cluster)

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 05:20 - CS Rep (BrightDocs): Requested immediate mitigation (rate limiting) and asked for ETA on hotfix. Logged in BD support portal.
Temporary mitigation: limited runtime worker_threads to 256 on affected shard families and applied an accept-queue backpressure parameter to ephemeral-proxy (handshake-window=30ms). This immediately reduced pthread_create failures and lowered 5xx burst amplitude.

Planned permanent fix: merge PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4212 which adds: (a) jemalloc tuning (reduced arenas + less aggressive trimming), (b) bounded threadpool policy with exponential backoff for short-lived tasks, (c) improved logging on thread_create failures to avoid immediate abort.

Rollout notes: hotpatch scheduled 2026-03-12 23:00 UTC; phased rollout across us-east-1 shards with canary on node-14 then +4 nodes. Post-deploy smoke tests include acceptance-scenarios/stream-embed-mix and 30m soak.

Customer follow-up: BrightDocs notified of mitigations and upcoming fix; offer of dedicated postmortem and longer-term SLA credit under review.
payload.summary: Periodic 5xx bursts caused by thread-allocator imbalance leading to runtime aborts

Issue summary: Multiple customers (initial report from BrightLedger) observe Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams that deliver the first 1-3 token chunks then become silent for 10s-90s and eventually time out. This started for BrightLedger after a routine edge proxy rollout on 2026-03-09. Impact: production chat features degrade (clients see partial responses followed by long silence or final 504). Affected sessions often involve clients sitting behind corporate HTTP proxies that re-establish connections (keepalive churn / pooled HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation).

Observed behavior: SSE connection appears open (200 OK) and initial chunks are delivered; server-side trace shows continued generation and token emission, but client-side receives no more chunk boundaries. Some streams complete silently with last_event_id unchanged; others close with connection reset after idle timeout.

Expected behavior: SSE streams should continuously deliver chunks as they are generated until a final event indicates completion or an explicit error.

1) Customer uses Redwood chat SSE endpoint (POST /v1/chat/stream) from behind a corporate proxy that does HTTP/2 fronting and translates to HTTP/1.1 to the edge.
2) Start a long response (context ~6k tokens) which triggers progressive token emission and KV cache usage.
3) Introduce an artificial client reconnect pattern (short socket recycle / proxy pool rotation) or wait for normal proxy churn.
4) Observe initial 1-3 SSE chunks delivered, then silence despite server-side active generation logs.
5) Reproduce reliably for BrightLedger client by toggling proxy keepalive to simulate pooling behavior (customer-provided steps attached).
Edge request id: req-0a3f9c (BrightLedger session) - 2026-03-09T18:12:33Z - initial chunks sent up to event id 2 then no further chunk frames observed on wire
Serving runtime trace: span srv-7234 - generator continued producing token batches for another 38s; last write syscall shows EPIPE after socket re-use
NGINX edge logs: 2026-03-09T18:12:33Z client 10.0.1.5 upstream prematurely closed keepalive connection (pool)
tcpdump capture (attached): shows downstream client acking initial packets then zero-window updates during later frames when server tries to send larger chunked frames
03/10 09:15 - Triage: Confirmed reproducible with BrightLedger repro steps. Behavior correlates with a recent edge-proxy change that enabled HTTP/2 connection coalescing for upstreams (rollout 2026-03-09).
Hypothesis A: Proxy pooling / HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation is causing flow-control window resets or connection re-use semantics that interrupt chunked SSE delivery even though server still believes socket is open.
Hypothesis B: Edge batching optimization aggregated small token frames into larger writev calls; when an intermediate proxy imposes backpressure the kernel leaves the socket in a state where subsequent writes return but are not delivered to client (zero-window), eventually causing stalls.
03/11 02:40 - Reproduced in staging by enabling the same coalescing flag; saw the same pattern. Disabling coalescing in staging returned normal continuous SSE delivery.
03/11 11:05 - Additional data: affected sessions have intermittent small gaps (<200ms) prior to stall, suggesting a timing-sensitive interaction with pool rotation. No evidence of model-side slowdown (generation CPU/GPU metrics normal).
Logs tied to upstream Nginx instance show KEEPALIVE resources returned to pool while server continues to write causing SIGPIPE in some worker connections.
Short-term mitigation suggested to customer: switch to websocket streaming endpoint (ws://) for affected clients or configure corporate proxies to preserve connection affinity and increase keepalive / idle timeout. Engineering recommended disabling HTTP/2->1 coalescing on edge for the customer routing policy as an immediate server-side mitigation.
1) Roll back HTTP/2 connection coalescing flag on edge for all affected routes (in progress). 2) Add additional socket write backpressure monitoring and a fast-fail path in the edge-proxy to surface broken pooled connections to the generator (RCA and code change ticket to follow). 3) Create automated test that exercises proxy pooling and HTTP/2->1 translation for SSE and websockets. 4) Postmortem and customer follow-up with timeline and permanent fix. Estimated ETA for rollback and customer confirmation: 2026-03-13.
Engineering to create code PR to detect stalled pooled sockets and force connection close: owner @edge-team (ETA 2026-03-17)
SRE to monitor SSE error rate and customer 5xx/timeout counts across us-west-2 for 72 hours post-rollback
Support to update BrightLedger with rollback confirmation and provide postmortem link

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:20 - BrightLedger Support (Elena Kovac): Provided proxy config, reproduction script, and a tcpdump capture. Customer requests a fast workaround as chat feature is used in demos.
2026-03-12 16:30 - BrightLedger: Applied websocket fallback and reported reduced incidence, but still asking for a permanent fix and postmortem.
SRE (03/11): Noted an increase in SSE idle timeouts correlated with edge change; setting up additional tcpdump captures for production validation.
BrightLedger - Elena (03/12): Confirmed websocket fallback reduces occurrences; awaiting full fix and postmortem.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when their Python client retries a streaming request that triggers function calling, the called external tool (webhook) is executed a second time despite supplying an Idempotency-Key. Impact: duplicate downstream charges and inconsistent external state for Acme AI customers. Environment: production, us-east region, Python SDK 1.6.2, network path includes their in-house proxy. Expected behavior: retries for retriable transport errors should be deduplicated by Idempotency-Key; the platform should not forward a duplicate function invocation. Actual behavior: second invocation observed after client reconnect/retry on transient streaming disconnect.
1) Use Python SDK 1.6.2 to send a streaming completion with function_call set to automatic and include header 'Idempotency-Key: <uuid>'
2) Simulate transient websocket drop on client after initial function request is received but before 200 ack from the customer's webhook (network-level disconnect)
3) SDK retries the request (built-in retry policy), server accepts retry and invokes configured function webhook again
4) Observe two calls to customer's webhook within minutes with identical payloads except for delivery metadata
2026-03-11T18:04:12Z [ingress] conn-reset from client 22.33.44.55 (partial request received)
2026-03-11T18:04:13Z [gateway] retry attempted for request id r_4a1b, client-id acme-123, Idempotency-Key=abc-123-uuid
2026-03-11T18:04:13Z [serving-runtime] function-invoke webhook acme-tool.example.com/payload status=200 duration=180ms attempt=1
2026-03-11T18:04:14Z [serving-runtime] function-invoke webhook acme-tool.example.com/payload status=200 duration=210ms attempt=2
Hypothesis A: API gateway is not forwarding Idempotency-Key to function-invocation subsystem on retry path due to header-normalization by the customer's proxy
Hypothesis B: SDK retry semantics for streaming requests re-issue a completely new request rather than attach the client-provided idempotency token in the retry envelope
Initial reproduction confirmed in staging when simulating websocket interruption behind Squid proxy — header was being stripped by proxy in some retry flows
Captured network traces from customer show Idempotency-Key present on first request, missing on subsequent TCP-level reconnect that triggered server-side retry handler
SRE note: our gateway has a separate code path for 'streaming reconnections' where we rehydrate request state; that path relies on a preserved header map from the original connection. If header missing on reconnect we treat as new request.
SDK engineering: Python SDK 1.6.2 did not attach X-Redwood-Idempotency on lower-level reconnects; newer SDK 1.6.3 includes a fix to carry header across retry envelope for streaming sessions (PR linked).
Workaround provided and fix in progress. Short-term mitigation: customer instructed to upgrade to Python SDK 1.6.3 (contains header-carry patch) or set server-side deduplication via 'Idempotency-Key' sent as part of function payload (redundant check). SRE applied gateway guard to reject retries that lack Idempotency-Key in the reconnect path for this tenant (Acme AI) as a temporary measure. Long-term: merged PR in sdk-python will make retries attach the original header and gateway will add defensive checks. Expected rollout: SDK patch released, gateway config rolled to canary on 2026-03-14, full rollout 2026-03-17.
Customer (Peter Nguyen): We saw two charges on our billing system and two records in our webhook receiver. We included an Idempotency-Key and assumed that would prevent repeats.
Support (Alice Wu): Thanks Peter — we are triaging. Can you confirm if you pass the Idempotency-Key in headers or in the request body? Also please paste any proxy logs if you have them.

Issue summary:
Customer reported that scheduled batch inference jobs started failing with 403 Authorization errors for ephemeral worker pods created after a config change on 2026-03-09. Failures began at ~09:10 UTC and affected all new workers; previously-provisioned long-running workers continued to operate normally.

Impact:
- Nimbus Analytics: recurring scheduled inference jobs (nightly batch) failing end-to-end, causing missed SLAs for data pipeline deliveries.
- Errors observed from worker -> /v1/infer requests: 403 with 'role binding not found' message.
- Estimated affected job runs: 42 in the first 3 hours.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) in us-west-2.
- Redwood Private control plane version: 2026.02.28.
- IdP: On-prem SAML (Shibboleth 3.5), group claim named 'memberOf'.
- RBAC: claim-to-group mapping using idp-mapper 'group_normalizer' regex.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Provision a new ephemeral worker via Nimbus scheduled job (same job definition as customer).
2) Observe worker pod logs showing successful token exchange with auth proxy.
3) Worker requests /v1/infer/* and receives 403 'no role binding for group: team' instead of expected 'worker' role.
4) Inspect idp-mapper output: groups emitted to Redwood are truncated to the first colon-separated segment.

Observed logs/snippets:
- auth-proxy: "token-issue: svcacct-ephemeral-123 accepted, groups=[team, infra, admins]"
- worker: "POST /v1/infer -> 403 {\"error\":\"role binding not found for groups: [team]\"}"
- idp-mapper debug: "raw memberOf: team:nimbus:workers, normalized: team"

Initial hypothesis: The group_normalizer regex was changed in the customer idp-mapper config during a maintenance change on 2026-03-09 to a simplifying pattern that strips everything after the first colon. This normalization removes tenant and role segments from namespace-qualified groups, so expected group 'nimbus:workers' (or 'team:nimbus:workers') no longer matches RBAC group patterns used by role bindings. Existing long-lived workers created before the change retained cached bindings and continued to function.

Customer-provided attachments: SAML assertion sample (redacted), worker pod logs, scheduled job run IDs.

Required next steps: immediate mitigation to restore batch jobs, followed by a configuration fix and a small code guard to prevent accidental destructive regex changes in idp-mapper.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:02 UTC - SRE (oncall): Applied customer-visible mitigation: added a temporary translation table at auth-proxy to map 'team' -> 'nimbus:workers' for Nimbus tenant, restoring scheduled jobs immediately.
Reproduced locally: apply regex '^([^:]+):.*$' to incoming 'memberOf' claim yields single-segment group names. Expected regex should capture tenant+role segments or preserve the last segment for role mapping.
Role-binding lookup in RBAC uses pattern 'nimbus:workers' and 'team:nimbus:workers' in different customers. The normalization removed the matching substring causing lookup to fail.
Cached role-bindings on long-lived workers prevented immediate failure; ephemeral workers always perform fresh token validation and therefore failed after change.
Auth-proxy logs show token exchange succeeded but downstream request-level authorization failed since token lacked expected group names understood by RBAC engine.
Quick mitigation implemented at auth-proxy via tenant-specific header translation. This is not ideal long-term because it masks normalization errors.
Root cause: idp-mapper configuration change without schema validation and insufficient unit tests for group normalization patterns.
Applied tenant-specific translation at auth-proxy to restore Nimbus batch jobs (temporary). Rolled back the customer-provided idp-mapper regex change in the control plane for Nimbus tenant and deployed a safer mapping implementation with explicit capture groups and unit tests (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/idp-mapper/pull/432). Added a validation step in the idp-mapper UI to warn on regexes that reduce group namespace segments. Customer confirmed nightly batch run success. Follow-ups: (1) Add automated canary checks for idp-mapper changes, (2) Publish runbook entry to surface group normalization effects to customers, (3) Offer migration assistance to other private customers who may have similar regexes.
payload.summary: Ephemeral batch workers fail authorization after IdP group-normalizer regex change

Issue summary: After a scheduled weighted-route migration (traffic shift) for a set of dedicated tenants in us-east-1, a single tenant (LexiconAI) observed a persistent elevated 5xx error rate (~12% of requests) for ~90 minutes. Impact: customer-facing API requests returned 502/503/504, streaming sessions dropped, and tail latency increased. Scope: observed across a 6-instance serving pool behind the same route weight group; not global.

Initial detection: LexiconAI support pinged #support at 2026-03-13T20:02Z noting a spike in 5xx and customer-facing errors. Alerting (apigw 5xx-rate) fired at ~20:01Z.
1) Trigger a weighted route migration that shifts ~30% of traffic from route A to route B for the us-east serving pool.
2) Observe increase in concurrent connection churn to runtime processes during in-flight model cache lookups.
3) Note repeated runtime thread stalls and watchdog restarts corresponding with API 5xx spikes.
4) Reproduce by replaying a 10-minute sample trace of LexiconAI traffic through canary routing (captured request IDs attached).
apigw: 2026-03-13T20:01:12Z - 502 upstream reset; runtime: 2026-03-13T20:01:13Z - ThreadPoolWorker[7] softlock detected at kv_cache.c:742; 2026-03-13T20:01:17Z - watchdog initiated graceful restart; container restart count incremented; dmesg shows no OOM; kernel logs show high scheduler wait times; network proxies returned ECONNRESET patterns during route handover.
Support triaged and validated customer impact; secured customer permission to triage live logs.
SRE observed runtime thread 'softlock' where workers spin waiting on a prefix-cache lock while new prefetch requests flood during migration.
Heap/CPU profiles show high user CPU from kernel-optimized attention kernels on 4/6 instances; one instance showed thread starvation with backlog growth in per-worker queue.
Autoscaler did not spin up additional dedicated instances because the route weight change occurred within the same instance pool and the autoscaler threshold was not breached.
Correlation between route-migration window and initial 5xx surge is strong; hypothesis: migration produced concentrated prefetch hotspots and lock contention on KV cache leading to per-runtime backpressure and upstream 502/503s.
2026-03-13T20:08Z - Diego Marquez (assignee): 'We're seeing repeated worker softlocks on two runtimes. Temporarily shifted LexiconAI traffic off the affected route to mitigate impact.'
2026-03-13T20:22Z - SRE: 'Mitigation in place — decreased weight to the failing route by 40% and bounced runtimes on the two offenders. Error rate dropped to ~1.2%.'
2026-03-13T21:10Z - Customer (LexiconAI): 'Thanks — we saw immediate improvement after your weight rollback. Please advise on root cause and long-term fix.'
2026-03-14T02:05Z - Runtime eng: 'Reproduced softlock locally with traffic-replay and a crafted prefetch burst; identified lock-order inversion when prefetch and eviction run concurrently.'
1) Emergency mitigation: partially rolled back weighted-route change for LexiconAI and diverted traffic to healthy pool. 2) Restarted two affected runtime containers and monitored for recovery. 3) Enabled additional request queue headroom for the tenant to reduce prefetch pressure. 4) Created a canary job to replay customer traffic to replicate state. 5) Notified customer and provided status updates.
Partial fix applied: rollback of weight migration + runtime restarts restored normal 5xx baseline. Root cause under active investigation (lock-order inversion in prefix/KV prefetch + eviction path). No data loss; customer satisfied with mitigation.
1) Runtime team to land PR that adds finer-grained cache locking and avoids global prefetch stall (PR referenced above).
2) Add route-migration throttling to limit concurrent prefetches across a pool (runbook task).
3) Update autoscaler thresholds for routing-induced prefetch hotspots so dedicated pool can scale proactively.
4) Postmortem and Confluence runbook update with clear mitigation steps and 'when to rollback' guidance.
5) Schedule 1:1 with LexiconAI CSM to review impact and SLA credits if requested.
payload.summary: Weighted route migration triggered runtime thread softlock causing sustained 5xx floor for tenant

Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 ~12:45 UTC PendulumHealth reported severe request latency and token cost spikes from their dedicated GPU pool. Customers observed large numbers of 5xx/429s followed by long tail latencies and partial completions. Impact: customer-facing application degraded, multiple transactions timed out.

Impact:
- PendulumHealth experienced ~40% request error rate and 8x token-cost spike during the window.
- Streaming responses truncated for ~18 minutes for a subset of requests.
- Potential billing exposure due to repeat retries and duplicate completions.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated GPU pool) in prod us-east
- Models: redwood-7b / redwood-7b-quant pinned by customer

Steps to reproduce (customer traces):
1) Customer sent a burst of long-sequence chat completions from a queued job agent at ~12:40 UTC.
2) Client observed repeated 429s and retried aggressively (no exponential backoff).
3) Serving requests consumed all hot worker slots; autoscaler did not immediately provision additional workers due to min_available_workers threshold mismatch.

Observed behavior and logs:
- Frontline logs show worker-slot exhaustion: "worker_pool: available_slots=0" repeated.
- Autoscaler logs: evaluation interval 30s, last scale event 12:10 UTC; recent scale decisions skipped due to perceived transient load (threshold set too high).
- Router traces show multiple retry loops with identical request IDs from PendulumHealth customer agent.

Customer report excerpt: "We saw the UI grind to a halt and then many failed completions; traffic was within our expected range and no backoff was applied on our side — we will investigate client retries but need a mitigation and credit for costs."
2026-03-10 13:00 UTC — Support (Sofia Martinez): Acknowledged. Triage started; contacting SRE and paging autoscaler owners. SLA first response met.
2026-03-10 13:10 UTC — SRE (Devon Clark): Observed worker slot exhaustion in pendulum pool; investigating autoscaler decisions and recent config changes. Punting to on-call infra lead if required.
2026-03-10 13:28 UTC — SRE (Anika Rao): Applied temporary mitigation: increased dedicated pool max-capacity by +30% and injected emergency routing headroom. Error rate reduced; streaming resumed for most flows.
2026-03-10 15:05 UTC — Support (Sofia Martinez): Customer confirmed service recovery and reported reduced error rates. Initiated billing review for duplicate completions and retry-cost exposure.
2026-03-11 09:30 UTC — PM (Liam O'Neal): Scheduled follow-up call with PendulumHealth for 2026-03-12. Action items assigned for autoscaler config audit and runbook updates.
Initial hypothesis: sudden client retry storm consumed hot slots and prevented new worker provisioning due to overly conservative autoscaler thresholds (min_available_workers set above intended value after recent commit).
Metric evidence: worker_pool.available_slots dropped to 0 at 12:42 UTC; queue_length spiked to 120; autoscaler decision log shows 'skip_scale=true' because 'scale_margin < margin_threshold'.
Traffic pattern: high-concurrency long-sequence completions from a single client agent creating head-of-line blocking and blocking the continuous batching optimization, increasing per-request GPU time.
Configuration change identified: 2026-03-08 deploy included autoscaler threshold change (PR #1287) that increased margin_threshold to avoid churn during short spikes — regression for dedicated, high-latency workloads.
Repro steps constructed in staging: replayed PendulumHealth traces (sanitized) with aggressive client retries and observed identical slot exhaustion and delayed scale-up behavior.
Temporary mitigation applied: emergency pool capacity increase (+30%) and dynamic route throttling for the customer's API key to smooth retry amplification.
Advised customer to implement exponential backoff on client retry logic; provided sample backoff config and recommended max_retries=3.
If immediate degradation observed again, customer can request manual pool expansion via dedicated-support channel.
Hotfix: reverted the autoscaler margin_threshold change from PR #1287 for dedicated pools (rollback applied 2026-03-10 14:20 UTC).
Permanent fix: updated autoscaler logic to consider long-request worker occupancy and introduced a secondary fast-path scale-up when queue_length > 50 for >30s. Change merged in runtime repo PR #1294 and scheduled for controlled rollout.
Operational changes: added dedicated-pool runbook section for retry storms, instrumented alert 'dedicated-pool-sustained-slot-exhaustion' with playbook steps, and created canary tests to exercise scale-up fast-path.
Customer remediation: applied a billing credit of $12,000 to PendulumHealth account to offset retry-related token costs and duplicate completions during the incident window. Customer accepted credit and escalated ask for an on-call postmortem review.
Communication: post-incident call scheduled and summary shared via the Confluence page. Follow-up actions assigned and tracked under INT-4412 and SUP-100721.
ENG-ALGO: Complete autoscaler fast-path rollout and validate in dedicated pools (owner: Devon Clark) — due 2026-03-20.
DOCS: Update dedicated runbook with retry-storm mitigation steps and include sample rate-limit policy (owner: Anika Rao) — due 2026-03-14.
CUSTOMER: Review PendulumHealth client retry config in joint session and share best-practice SDK patch (owner: Sofia Martinez) — meeting 2026-03-12.
BILLING: Finalize and document applied credit, add note to invoice and close billing dispute (owner: Maya Patel) — due 2026-03-13.

Issue summary:
Customer Bank of Nova is onboarding Redwood's on-prem syslog proxy to forward audit events into their SIEM behind an mTLS-only ingress. They also submitted a security questionnaire and require a signed evidence bundle showing field-level redaction controls, retention/immutable-export options, and proof of delivery for legal-hold slices.

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete internal compliance onboarding; integration is blocking certification for connecting Redwood audit stream to their SOC environment.
- Business: Onboarding delay for multi-region production usage, potential revenue hold on enterprise contract.

Environment:
- Customer environment: Air-gapped SOC cluster with a dedicated SIEM collector in eu-west.
- Redwood endpoints: on-prem agent v0.9.2, syslog-proxy service behind customer-managed NAT, handshake via mTLS certs issued by Bank of Nova CA.

Request from customer:
1) Step-by-step deploy guide for our on-prem syslog proxy that supports mTLS client auth + optional syslog-ng header enrichment.
2) Signed evidence bundle including: exporter manifest, sample redaction report for PII fields (account_id, user_email), RFC3161 timestamped manifest for a 7-day retention snapshot, and HMAC chain for delivered batches.
3) Answers for 25-question security questionnaire (attached) focusing on key rotation, HSM/KMS integration, and retention deletion guarantees.
4) Temporary retention override for a legal-hold slice (preserve events from 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-05) and confirmation of non-destructive export.

Steps to reproduce / reproduction notes:
1) Customer followed onboarding doc and attempted mutual TLS handshake — client cert fails during verification. Error observed in agent logs: "tls: handshake failure: remote error: bad certificate".
2) Customer attempted a fallback to plaintext for testing; connection is rejected by policy.
3) Customer uploaded questionnaire and evidence checklist via support portal (ticket created).

Logs and attachments provided by customer:
- agent-debug.log (2026-03-09) snippet: "verify error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"
- packet-capture.pcap (handshake)
- security_questionnaire_bank_of_nova_v1.pdf

Investigation so far:
- Support reproduced CA-trust issue in staging: our on-prem agent image v0.9.2 trusts system CA bundle; Bank of Nova uses a private root that needs to be added to agent trust store.
- Hypothesis: agent start-up does not accept additional CA mounted at /etc/redwood/extra-ca.pem when run under systemd with read-only root; onboarding container run as non-root did not pick up custom volume.
- Temporary workaround validated in staging: run agent with --extra-ca /etc/redwood/extra-ca.pem and restart; handshake completes and events flow.

Requested next steps (support/eng):
- Provide a hardened runbook for customer showing: how to mount extra CA into agent, systemd unit changes, and SELinux/AppArmor considerations for air-gapped installs.
- Produce signed evidence bundle (manifest + RFC3161 timestamp + HMAC chain) for the sample 7-day snapshot and the requested legal-hold slice.
- Complete security questionnaire answers with references to KMS/HSM pages and SOC2 controls.

Acceptance criteria:
- Bank of Nova completes an mTLS handshake with the on-prem agent and receives a signed delivery receipt for the preserved slice.
- Customer receives the signed evidence bundle and completed questionnaire answers within the SLA window.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 — Customer (Bank of Nova, SecOps): Confirmed they can provide the private root CA as PEM and provided their systemd unit. Asked if HSM-backed signing is available for the manifest.

Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running SSE streams from our hosted endpoint sometimes arrive to their client with all content except the final concluding chunk. Impact: Final sentence or closing JSON metadata is missing in 1-3% of sessions for a specific mobile app version, causing truncated completions and downstream UI to show a perpetual 'typing' indicator. Environment: Dedicated customer (Acme Retail) using Redwood hosted API via the mobile SDK v1.8.3 that runs a local sidecar process to multiplex network activity on flaky mobile connections.

Observed behavior differs from previous SSE truncation tickets because the server completes generation and emits the end event (visible in backend logs), but the client never receives the terminal chunk in a subset of reconnect/resume scenarios.
1) Install Acme mobile app with SDK v1.8.3 and enable sidecar multiplexing.
2) Start a long-running chat generation (~200-400 tokens) via SSE in us-east region.
3) Simulate intermittent network by toggling cellular data off/on twice quickly (to provoke socket handoff).
4) Observe stream resume; in affected runs the last 'end' event and final JSON metadata never arrive in the app while server logs show event emitted.
Backend excerpt (stream-id=stream-9a4f):
[2026-03-05T08:12:14Z] generation.complete event emitted seq=0 end=true metadata={duration_ms:3214}
Proxy/LB logs show FIN from client-side path at 08:12:14.108 and new connection at 08:12:14.210.
App-side sdk log snippet:
[08:12:14.205] sidecar: keepalive: sent incremental probe (12 bytes)
[08:12:14.208] sdk: resumed SSE session, last_seq=0
[08:12:14.300] sdk: no terminal event received - session closed by app after timeout.
Packets captured at edge indicate a pattern of interleaved tiny keepalive writes during the TCP handoff window.
Hypothesis: When the mobile sidecar emits very small keepalive writes during connection handoff, some ALB/proxy implementations coalesce or reorder micro-frames and the final zero-length termination marker (or small JSON payload) from server is merged with a client probe in a way that the server-side connection close race drops the packet. We reproduced locally by injecting 8-16B client-side writes during an h2->h1 fallback; reproduced ~2/50 runs.
Findings:
- Server runtime always queues and sends final event; logs confirm flush.
- Edge (customer-dedicated ALB) behavior changes when client sends a write within 40-120ms of server final chunk.
- SDK sidecar v1.8.3 intentionally batches keepalives as tiny writes (to reduce wakeups); this pattern increases the race window.
- Workaround trial: disabling sidecar keepalive batching prevents truncation in reproduced cases.
Related: INT-1122 flagged an ALB keepalive coalescing regression; added as linked issue for infra follow-up.
2026-03-05 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer reports truncated final chunk in ~1.7% of long SSEs. Provided initial request id and stream ids.
2026-03-05 - SRE (Liam Patel): Collected edge/rt logs and packet captures; initial hypothesis: proxy coalescing with client-side micro-writes. Asked customer to enable SDK debug logging and to try a short test with keepalive disabled.
2026-03-06 - Customer (Acme Mobile Eng): We toggled sidecar keepalive batching off and ran 1000 sessions; observed 0 truncations in that run. Re-enabled for subsequent tests and saw truncations return. Shared logs and a capture of client probes.
2026-03-06 - Infra (Nina Gomez): Noted an ALB change last month that altered small-write coalescing behavior; opened INT-1122 to investigate config. Will test with stricter Nagle settings and TCP_NODELAY variants.
2026-03-07 - Support (Liam Patel): Proposed two short-term mitigations and a long-term fix. Posted steps below. Customer accepted mitigation A and is running validation.
2026-03-07 - Customer (Acme Mobile Eng): Applying mitigation A now, will report back after 24h of traffic.

A) On customer SDK side: disable keepalive micro-batching (SDK config: sidecar.keepalive.batching=false) — immediate and low-risk.
B) On server/edge: add a 50ms grace flush after emitting terminal chunk at edge layer to allow in-flight client writes to settle (requires infra change).
C) Client-level: extend resume wait timeout to tolerate late arrival of terminal chunk while keeping UI tolerant.
Customer accepted A for now.
In progress: Customer applied SDK config change disabling keepalive batching and reported initial validation with no truncations in 24h sample. Infra team (INT-1122) to validate ALB behavior; plan is to add a conservative 50ms flush on the dedicated ALB for long-lived SSE endpoints if we cannot tune the ALB. Follow-up actions: schedule release notes for SDK v1.8.4 documenting recommended default for sidecar batching and include a mitigation flag in hosted console for dedicated customers.
1) Monitor Acme's traffic for 72h post-mitigation and collect metrics (support will follow up).
2) Infra to run controlled ALB small-write coalescing test and update INT-1122 with findings.
3) Ship SDK patch v1.8.4 with keepalive.batching default=false and add telemetry to detect suppressed terminal events.
4) If infra fix is not feasible, implement server-side 50ms flush for SSE final frames behind a feature flag for dedicated clusters.
payload.summary: SDK sidecar keepalive trickle results in suppressed final chunk for long-running SSE sessions

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers report repeated service discovery timeouts and long-tailed artifact fetch latency from on-prem Private deployment. Failures began after a recent scheduled maintenance window on the customer's edge appliances. Initial symptoms point to failed DNS lookups followed by many retries and fallback attempts, causing control-plane reconnects and occasional model pull timeouts.

Impact:
- Multiple inference nodes intermittently fail to resolve control-plane hostnames leading to 5-10s delays on startup and periodic reconnects.
- Artifact downloads fall back to presigned-URL retries and sometimes fail after exhausting retries, causing degraded throughput for FinNova's data-processing pipelines.
- Customer reported increased 429/503s in application telemetry during peak traffic windows.

Environment details:
- Private deployment (on-prem appliance) using VPX edge firewall + BGP to corporate WAN.
- Egress path goes through vendor-managed edge with NIC offload features enabled (hardware UDP checksum offload).
- Redwood agent version: 2.7.3-release, runtime 1.14.0.
- DNS: internal forwarder -> corporate recursive resolver -> public resolvers.

Observed timing: First reported 2026-03-09 02:17 UTC after vendor maintenance window.
1) From a serving node in the customer's on-prem cluster, run 'dig +tcp +time=2 example-controlplane.redwood.ai' repeatedly and measure response rates.
2) Simulate load by running parallel artifact prefetch requests for a medium-sized model (~6GB) and watch DNS/multi-retry behavior.
3) Toggle NIC UDP checksum offload on the node's egress interface (ethtool -K eth0 rx off tx off) to validate symptom change.
4) Capture tcpdump on egress interface while reproducing to compare UDP reply payloads vs in-kernel checksums.
5) Compare behavior across nodes behind different edge appliances (to rule out node-local misconfigurations).
Mar 09 02:18:11 agent[svc]: control-plane DNS lookup failed: timeout after 2s (retrying)
Mar 09 02:18:13 agent[svc]: artifact-prefetch attempt 3 -> presigned URL GET 504 (upstream timeout)
tcpdump sample (node-05 egress): UDP reply length=512 but UDP checksum 0x0000 (offloaded), payload contains truncated DNS answer at byte 476
strace of resolver: recvfrom returned 512 bytes, resolver marks as SERVFAIL due to bad RDATA (length mismatch)
Vendor edge appliance config excerpt provided by customer (anonymized) shows hardware-accelerated UDP checksum handling enabled on egress interface.
Packet analysis shows on-wire DNS UDP payloads that appear well-formed but include zeroed or mismatched checksum fields when the vendor offload + firmware optimization are active.
Userspace resolver receives buffer with truncated RDATA (length mismatch) and treats as SERVFAIL; application retries escalate to TCP fallback which is blocked at customer's perimeter, causing long tail and eventual artifact download failures.
Disabling NIC UDP checksum offload on host removes symptom immediately (local mitigation).
Reproduction in lab using a virtual NIC with checksum 'zeroing' reproduces resolver decode errors; confirms issue is in the offload/firmware layer rather than Redwood agent code.
Related configuration: EDNS0 with large UDP DNS responses for our control-plane SRV/TXT records and DNSSEC-signed resolver zones increase likelihood of >512B UDP responses.
Edge vendor acknowledged regression in firmware v3.12.8 introduced in maintenance; they have a patch pending but no ETA on customer timelines.
Workarounds considered: 1) Disable UDP checksum offload on all agent hosts (node-level) 2) Configure corporate perimeter to allow TCP53 to permit resolver fallback 3) Reduce EDNS0 advertised size (not ideal) 4) Use local DNS cache with TCP support (requires infra changes).
Customer reports production constraints: rolling restart of all nodes to flip offload is disruptive; customer prefers perimeter TCP53 exception short-term.
Added monitoring dashboard to track DNS SERVFAIL rate and artifact-prefetch retry counts; alert thresholds set to P1 paging.
Linked internal INT- tickets created for SRE playbook and vendor comms (see linked_issues).
Mitigation applied: Customer allowed temporary outbound TCP53 from agent subnets to corporate resolver (permitted 2026-03-13 22:00 - 2026-03-20), which immediately reduced timeouts and artifact failures.
Recommended short-term fix: Disable UDP checksum offload on egress-facing agent hosts where operationally feasible (ethtool -K eth0 rx off tx off). Customer will schedule a staggered maintenance window to apply this across nodes next week.
Long-term: Vendor to roll firmware patch to correct UDP coalescing behavior for large DNS responses. SRE to validate once patch available.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:45 - FinNova Network Ops (customer): Provided pcap + edge config. We toggled NIC offload on one host and timeouts stopped for that host. Other hosts still affected behind the vendor appliance.
2026-03-13 08:10 - Customer: Confirmed enabling TCP fallback in resolver mitigates but customer FW blocks outbound TCP53 at perimeter (corporate policy). They will allow temporary exception for TCP53 for validation window.
payload.summary: On-prem private deploy: egress NIC UDP checksum offload corrupts DNS responses -> service discovery timeouts

payload.description:
Customer requests an on-demand, incremental export from our audit stream into their S3 lakehouse. Deliverables must meet two specific constraints: (1) each S3 partition file must be wrapped in an opaque tenant envelope (customer manages tenant decryption) so raw tenant identifiers are never exposed in storage; (2) each incremental checkpoint must include an RFC3161-compliant timestamp token (time-stamp authority proof) and an accompanying SHA-256 manifest for non-repudiation. They also want an optionally signed KMS-wrapped key proof to show the envelope integrity was produced by Redwood's KMS.
Customer requires this bundle for an upcoming regulatory evidence submission. Delay > 5 business days will block their audit timeline and may escalate to legal review. No production API outage reported; this is an evidence/delivery request with medium urgency.
- Delivery cadence: hourly incremental deltas for the previous 24 hours as a single zipped bundle delivered to their customer-owned S3 bucket (s3://vaultbridge-evidence/redwood/).
- File layout: partitioned by year/month/day/hour with each file named <checkpoint_id>.<sha256>.enc.zip and accompanied by <checkpoint_id>.rfc3161.tst
- Tenant encapsulation: payload must be tenant-encrypted (opaque envelope). Redwood should not store the tenant decryption key; include envelope metadata that indicates KMS-key-id used and an HMAC over envelope with Redwood's signing key.
- RFC3161 timestamp: request includes a TSP token per checkpoint, signed by a recognized TSA. Customer provided example TSA: https://tsa.example.com
- Manifest: top-level manifest.json listing files, sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and RFC3161 token identifiers. Manifest must be checksumed and included in the signed bundle.
1) Customer provided a sample event range (2026-03-08T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-09T00:00:00Z) and sample bucket details.
2) Customer reports inability to map our standard audit export to their opaque-envelope format using the public docs (they need Redwood to produce the encapsulation at the source prior to S3 delivery).
3) Support should validate whether the export pipeline can insert an envelope layer and attach RFC3161 tokens per checkpoint.
Customer submitted a sample delivery log (delivery-log-20260309.txt) showing successful PutObject calls but missing envelope metadata and missing .rfc3161 tokens. Excerpt: 'PUT s3://vaultbridge-evidence/redwood/2026/03/08/00/checkpoint-0001.zip 200 OK' with no additional metadata headers. They attached CloudTrail and delivery receipts.
Initial triage: export pipeline currently supports JSON and Parquet partitioning with optional server-side encryption (SSE-S3 / SSE-KMS) but no opaque-tenant envelope abstraction at the object level.
Checked ingestion worker logs for hourly export jobs between 2026-03-08 00:00 and 2026-03-09 00:00: no evidence of envelope metadata injection. Worker version: export-service v1.12.4.
KMS: Redwood KMS keys available to support team. Need to confirm whether we can sign HMACs with existing service signing key or must route to dedicated evidence-signing KMS key (policy/legal constraint).
RFC3161: Our internal time-stamp service can generate RFC3161 tokens but currently not automatically attached to export checkpoints; requires TSP integration and packaging step (backend change).
Hypothesis: Deliverable requires a short-lived packaging job that pulls delta files, wraps each payload in the envelope format, requests RFC3161 token from TSA, generates manifest, signs manifest with KMS-signing key, and pushes zipped bundle to customer S3 with appropriate ACL and object metadata.
Potential blockers: cross-account S3 put permissions for their bucket, TSA whitelisting / fees, creation of a new packaging job with KMS-signing key and audit trail.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:18 - Customer (VaultBridge): Provided their TSA contact and asked if Redwood can provide TSA token cost estimate or if they will supply tokens externally.
2026-03-12 16:05 - Legal (external-comment): Requested to validate key usage policy and suggested a short contract amendment for evidence-signing services.
2026-03-12: Agreed next steps with customer: (A) Redwood will deliver a one-off prototype packaging job for the requested sample window within 5 business days; (B) packaging job will write to a pre-authorized, customer-owned S3 path and include per-checkpoint RFC3161 token and a signed manifest (signed with a dedicated evidence-signing KMS key after legal approval); (C) customer will supply tenant decryption public info and TSA service details.
Workaround: For immediate needs, customer can continue to ingest full audit export and run tenant encapsulation internally. Support provided mapping guidance and a sample Python script to perform envelope wrapping and generate RFC3161 tokens using their TSA.
Follow-up actions: create INT-40211 (internal task) to prototype packaging job; security to review KMS key policy and legal to prepare amendment; engineering estimate due by 2026-03-17.
Status: awaiting legal approval and security KMS review before moving to In Progress for engineering work.
Owner: Ethan Park (Support) to coordinate cross-team sync.
- Engineering to produce PR with prototype and integration tests: related_github_pr should be attached to this ticket.
- Security to produce a one-page summary of KMS signing key usage and rotation schedule to include in evidence bundle metadata.
- Once prototype validated, schedule a run for the customer's 24-hour window and provide the zipped bundle and verification steps.
Each checkpoint-level file is opaque to Redwood (tenant identifier encrypted inside envelope), Redwood provides non-repudiable RFC3161 tokens and a KMS-signed manifest proving file contents and delivery time.
Customer confirmed acceptance of prototype approach on 2026-03-12 and will await legal sign-off for Redwood-signed manifests.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightAnswers reports recurring elevated 5xx rates on their dedicated tenant during mixed workload periods (chat + embedding uploads). Errors surface as short 1–3 minute waves multiple times per hour.
Multiple production endpoints for BrightAnswers saw ~12-18% 5xx for short windows, causing higher latency and client-side retries. Customer reports downstream throttling and some failed long-running websocket sessions.
Dedicated cluster in us-west region. Tenant pinned to redwood-13b-v2 for chat routes and open-research-7b-quant for nightly embedding jobs. Observed during business hours and during scheduled bulk embedding uploads.
1) Customer issues high-concurrency websocket streaming sessions (keepalive enabled) to chat route.
2) Concurrently upload a large embedding batch (multipart) to embeddings route.
3) Monitor accept-queue depth on ephemeral proxies and api-gateway metrics (accept.queue_length, ephemeral_proxy_gc_cycles).
4) Observe elevated 5xx and runtime preemption logs when GC window aligns with incoming handshake bursts.
[2026-03-12T14:03:21Z] apigw: accept_queue=128 -> drop_rate=0.12, upstream=ephemeral-proxy-7 status=502
[2026-03-12T14:03:22Z] proxy: gc_cycle_start pid=2173 retained_fds=104
[2026-03-12T14:03:23Z] runtime: preempting-model-worker worker_id=42 reason=socket-half-open
[2026-03-12T14:03:24Z] runtime: OOM-avoid-reclaim triggered; restart-signal sent to worker
[2026-03-12T14:03:25Z] apigw: upstream_reset count=9 route=/v1/chat streaming=true
- Initial hypothesis: accept-queue pressure + ephemeral-proxy GC windowing is causing a burst of half-open sockets which escalate to the serving runtime preempting workers and triggering GPU reclaim attempts.
- Correlated apigw accept_queue spikes with proxy GC traces; GC cycles frequently align with incoming websocket handshakes during embedding upload contention.
- Observed that when GC cycles start, FD handoff latency increases ~4–8x leading to HTTP/2 stream resets and upstream restart loops.
- Heap and file descriptor stats from ephemeral-proxy show transient FD exhaustion during GC windows (avg open fds jump ~200).
- No immediate kernel-level OOMs; issue appears to be resource fragmentation and timing amplification across proxies and runtime watcher logic.
1) Temporarily throttle BrightAnswers embedding upload concurrency (request rate limit) and stagger uploads; recommended client-side backoff.
2) Increase ephemeral-proxy keepalive timeout to reduce socket churn during GC windows.
3) Apply rate limit on websocket handshake concurrency per-tenant in apigw as immediate mitigation.
Short term: deploy a hotfix to apigw that adds handshake-sidecar backpressure when downstream accept_queue exceeds threshold (canary to 10% of traffic in us-west).
Medium term: update ephemeral-proxy GC to perform incremental GC with smoother FD reclamation and emit early load signals to apigw.
Long term: refactor runtime preemption logic to avoid GPU reclaim on transient half-open socket bursts and improve keepalive pooling semantics for mixed embed/chat workloads.
- Owner: Runtime reliability team to implement preemption safety gate (ticket INT-2034).
- Proxy team to add incremental GC prototype and run load tests (PR submitted).
- DevX to update customer quickstart recommendations for embedding + streaming concurrency.
- Create synthetic test that reproduces GC-window handshake collision for future regression testing.
In progress: Canary patch to apigw backpressure deployed 2026-03-14 to 10% of us-west traffic. Early telemetry shows 70% reduction in 5xx wave amplitude for canary customers. Full rollout pending additional proxy GC mitigations and runtime safety checks.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 BrightAnswers Support Contact (Emily Zhang): Confirmed that after temporary concurrency limits and staggered uploads, immediate user visible errors dropped. Awaiting permanent fix timeline.

payload.description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 13:02 UTC GearboxAI reported application-side timeouts and streaming disconnects while using their Reserved Dedicated pool. Symptoms included repeated 5xxs from our API, automatic model fallback between gptx-7b-redwood-v1 and a quantized fallback variant (gptx-7b-q4b), and a billing spike from repeated retry loops. Impact: customer-facing API failures for GearboxAI's production traffic (~120 RPS) and degraded QA sessions for their internal users. Total outage window for the most severe errors: ~34 minutes.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-12 12:58 UTC: first alert from internal monitoring (elevated 5xx rate in us-west dedicated pool).
- 2026-03-12 13:02 UTC: GearboxAI escalates via support channel (severity P0 request).
- 2026-03-12 13:07 UTC: Support triage; SRE engaged and created INC-2026-0317.
- 2026-03-12 13:12 UTC: Observed autoscaler triggering double-scaling events and several node reconnects.
- 2026-03-12 13:20 UTC: Serving runtime started to route traffic to fallback quantized model due to transient OOM errors; fallback routing created retry loops for some requests.
- 2026-03-12 13:36 UTC: Mitigation applied: temporarily pinned GearboxAI routing to stable model on separate pool and disabled aggressive autoscale policy.
- 2026-03-12 13:50 UTC: 5xx rate subsided and streaming reconnect rate returned to baseline.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Use traffic generator with incremental RPS up to 150 against dedicated pool in us-west with model pinning unset.
2) Simulate instance pre-emption by restarting GPU worker while autoscaler configured with burst_policy=aggressive.
3) Observe serving-runtime logs for repeated fallback_to_quantized and request_requeue messages.

Logs/snippets: (excerpts pasted into ticket comments and log archive)
- serving-runtime: "ERROR request_handler - failed to allocate KV cache: OOM on GPU0 -> falling back to gptx-7b-q4b"
- scheduler: "WARN autoscaler - scale_up triggered twice in 15s for pool=gearbox-enterprise-pool"

Additional notes:
SRE-OnCall (2026-03-12T13:22:00Z): Observed repeated node reboots during the incident window; autoscaler double-fired after transient GPU agent heartbeat delay. Investigating heartbeat jitter causing duplicate scale events. See Slack thread #inc-2026-0317: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02INC/12345
Customer (GearboxAI - Alex Chen) (2026-03-12T13:30:00Z): Thanks for the rapid response. Please advise if we should throttle traffic or pin to a specific model while you investigate. We are seeing billing spikes due to retries; this is impacting customer SLAs.
Hypothesis A: Autoscaler double-scale due to heartbeat jitter caused brief worker churn -> worker reconnects triggered serving-runtime failover and fallback routing.
Hypothesis B: KV cache memory pressure (growth spike) caused OOM on some GPU workers for the non-quantized model; runtime fallback to quantized variant combined with client retry policy produced looping 5xxs.
Logs indicate both firing: autoscaler fired duplicate scale_up events (infra logs) and serving-runtime reported multiple OOM events within the same 90s window. CPU/memory metrics around 13:10-13:25 show KV cache growth correlated with request bursts. See monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/gearbox/dedicated-pool-oom
Reproduction on staging: reproduced using synthetic RPS with config burst_policy=aggressive + worker restart; fallback loop observed consistently. Fix candidate: mark fallback variants as non-retryable OR add short throttling cooldown on fallback events.
Root cause (post-analysis): combination of autoscaler heartbeat jitter + KV cache mis-sizing for observed request distribution. Autoscaler duplicate scale caused temporary overcommit and reconnect churn; during reconnect the runtime's KV cache allocation failed and triggered immediate fallback routing. Retry policy coupled with fallback produced request storms and billing leak.
Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/829 (add non-retry flag for fallback variants), https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/784 (debounce autoscaler triggers)
Related internal ticket: INT-4120 (autoscaler debounce investigation).
Mitigations applied during incident: (1) temporarily pinned GearboxAI to stable model on reserve node group, (2) disabled aggressive autoscaler burst policy for their pool, (3) emergency patch to mark fallback variants non-retry applied to serving-runtime and rolled to prod (PR #829). Long-term fixes scheduled: autoscaler debounce (PR #784) and KV cache sizing adjustment for enterprise pools. Customer confirmed recovery and error rate returned to baseline by 13:50 UTC.
Engineering: Merge and deploy autoscaler debounce PR (#784) across prod clusters by 2026-03-18.
Serving Runtime: Adjust default KV cache sizing heuristics for reserved pools and add proactive telemetry for KV growth by 2026-03-19.
SDK/Client: Update retry policy defaults to avoid retrying immediately after a fallback route; publish advisory for enterprise customers by 2026-03-20.
Customer Success: Scheduled 1:1 with GearboxAI on 2026-03-15 to review incident, share postmortem and discuss credits/compensation.
Billing: Investigate invoice exposure and prepare credit proposal for retry-driven overages; due 2026-03-16.
GearboxAI reported an estimated 12% overage on their daily usage during the incident window due to retry loops. Billing team to quantify token-level overcharge and propose credit. Temporary mitigation to prevent further charge accrual was applied by pinning routing and disabling retries on fallback variants.
Initial notification sent via support at 13:05 UTC. Real-time updates provided in support channel and Slack incident thread. After recovery, emailed customer a summary and next steps at 14:10 UTC. Follow-up 1:1 scheduled for 2026-03-15. Customer acknowledged and accepted the mitigation path; asked for formal postmortem and credit proposal.
Incident closed after targeted mitigations and two hotfixes deployed. Monitoring alert thresholds adjusted to detect duplicate scale events earlier. No further customer-impacting recurrences observed in 72h window.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer uses a hybrid embedding pipeline that concatenates a dense vector from redwood/embed-dense-1.2 with a sparse lexical vector (sparse/lexical-encoder-0.9) at ingest time. After a recent ingest pipeline change, the rerank endpoint started returning duplicate items in top-k responses and intermittently hitting CPU-fallback which causes 10-30s timeouts for some requests.

Impact:
- Affects AtlasSearch production queries that use the /rerank endpoint; ~12% of rerank calls in their workload observe duplicate IDs in top-10 and ~4% observe >10s latency spikes or 503s.
- Customer-facing search UX shows repeated results and slow page loads.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted Dedicated cluster in us-west-2 (customer-dedicated pool)
- Model versions: redwood/embed-dense-1.2, sparse/lexical-encoder-0.9
- Rerank service config: fusion_mode="concat_and_scale", batch_size=64, enable_kv_cache=true

Steps to reproduce:
1) Ingest a mixed corpus containing both lexically-rich short documents and long-form dense ones with the customer's mixing pipeline (dense vector + sparse vector stored as one fused embedding).
2) Call /rerank with a query that has high lexical overlap and expect top-10 unique document IDs.
3) Observe returned list and monitor request latency and CPU metrics on serving nodes.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate document IDs appear in the top-10 (same doc id repeated twice with slightly different scores).
- Rerank requests occasionally escalate to CPU-fallback path (serving-runtime logs show fallback trigger due to mismatch in vector handling) which increases latency to 10-30s and sometimes returns 503 when timeout occurs.

Expected behavior:
- Rerank returns unique top-k document IDs in descending score order.
- No unnecessary CPU-fallback for correctly-encoded embeddings.

Logs / Artifacts:
- Partial request traces and request IDs attached in comments below.
- Dashboard links: Observability -> rerank/topk-duplicates (https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rerank/topk-duplicates?customer=AtlasSearch)
Ingest mixed dense+sparse documents using AtlasSearch pipeline (dense vector + sparse vector fused)
Submit /rerank query with high lexical overlap against fused index
Observe top-k results and check serving node CPU fallback metric
req-id=8f9c3a2b trace shows vector-dim-mismatch warning: expected 512 but got 544
serving-runtime: fallback_triggered=true node=rerank-4 reason=embedding_fusion_unhandled
kernel-scheduler: batch=64 fallback-to-cpu latency_ms=12500

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 15:45 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer confirmed they recently turned on 'sparse-pad-auto' in their ingest pipeline. Working with AtlasSearch to disable as a temporary mitigation.
Initial triage: reproduce with customer's sample corpus; duplicates reproduced locally against rerank-4 node.
Hypothesis A: variable-length sparse padding leading to inconsistent fused vector shape (observed warnings about expected 512 vs 544).
Hypothesis B: batching reshuffle caused by scheduler when batch contains mixed-length fused vectors, leading to incorrect mapping of doc IDs to scores in postprocessing (less likely given logs).
Trace analysis: request 8f9c3a2b shows that the vector deserializer returned an extra 32 dims filled with small non-zero noise (not pure zeros). This triggered fallback path in kernel selector which then executed a slower CPU scoring routine that did not dedupe duplicate docs correctly.
Metric changes: rerank/topk_duplicate_rate climbed from 0.4% baseline to 12% during spike window; cpu-fallback-rate increased to 4% for AtlasSearch pool. Serving node CPU utilization spiked to 92% during fallback events.
Temporary mitigation: advise customer to disable 'sparse-pad-auto' (AtlasSearch applied revert) and we patched rerank deserializer to explicitly check and normalize fused-vector shapes on ingestion endpoint.
Longer-term: harden ingest validation and add contract tests to CI for hybrid fused shapes; add a rule in scheduler to reject batches with mixed fused-length embeddings rather than silent fallback.
Hotfix deployed 2026-03-14 08:10: rerank service normalizes fused embedding lengths and rejects malformed inputs with 400-level error instead of triggering CPU-fallback.
Customer rolled back the 'sparse-pad-auto' flag on 2026-03-13 16:20 as an immediate workaround.
Post-deploy metrics: duplicate top-k rate reduced to 0.6% within 2 hours and CPU-fallback rate returned to baseline <0.5%.
No data loss; affected requests were retried by customer or returned 503 - CS coordinated a partial retry plan for the customer to re-run critical batches if needed.
Mismatch between customer's sparse padding behavior and rerank's expected fused embedding contract: variable-length fused vectors with trailing non-zero noise caused rerank to take a CPU-fallback path and postprocessing dedupe to fail, producing duplicate top-ks and timeouts.
ENG: Add fused-embedding shape contract tests to serving-runtime CI (owner: @ethan_ross)
ENG: Add explicit ingest-time validation and sanitizer for fused embeddings (owner: @serving-team)
Support: Coordinate with AtlasSearch to run a backfill for affected critical queries and monitor for 48h (owner: Maya Patel)
Docs: Update embedding ingestion docs to call out padding and fusion best practices and examples for mixing sparse+dense (owner: Developer Experience)
payload.summary: Hybrid dense+sparse embedding fusion produces duplicate top-k results and triggers CPU-fallback timeouts on rerank

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that their synthetic monitoring probes (marked non-billable) were charged on the March 6 provisional invoice after an org merge on March 5. The provisional invoice shows a negative balance that triggered an automated payment hold and temporary service restrictions for some API keys.

Impact:
- NovaChat Labs observed $42.37 in unexpected charges for ~1,200 probe tokens flagged as billable.
- Provisional negative balance (-$42.37) caused automatic billing hold and a limited service state for two subaccount API keys for ~2 hours.
- Customer is concerned about downstream effects on SLAs and has asked for an immediate credit and root cause.

Environment:
- Dedicated account (org id: org-nova-1145) migrated into a consolidated billing parent on 2026-03-05 (merge job id: merge-2026-03-05-7).
- Affected keys are in prod (us-east).

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) 2026-03-05 03:12 UTC: Billing/merge job ran to remap subaccount org IDs into consolidated parent.
2) 2026-03-05 03:15 - 10:00 UTC: NovaChat synthetic monitors executed probe calls (identified by probe_user_agent and probe_tag=non-billable).
3) 2026-03-06 00:05 UTC: Hourly usage postbacks aggregated and forwarded to billing; some postbacks from probe keys were posted with parent_org_id instead of subaccount_org_id.
4) 2026-03-06 01:30 UTC: Provisional invoice generation applied charges; the probe-specific non-billable tag was not applied to ~1,200 tokens leading to $42.37 billable amount.
5) 2026-03-06 02:05 UTC: Automated billing rule detected negative provisional balance and placed account on hold (auto-hold policy triggered).

Relevant logs / links:
- Slack thread: #support -> https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02SUPPORT/p1678012345678
- Billing job logs: s3://redwood-ops/billing/merge-2026-03-05-7/logs/merge.log
- Postback samples: postback_ids [pb-99321, pb-99324, pb-99342] (see attached with ticket)
- Provisional invoice id: inv-prov-2026-03-org-nova-1145-03-06

Customer request:
- Immediate reversal/credit for the $42.37 and removal of the billing hold.
- Explanation of root cause and confirmation that synthetic probe traffic will not be charged going forward.

Additional notes:
2026-03-07 13:40 - Tomás Guerrero (Billing Eng): Confirmed probe tokens appear in usage table with tag 'probe' but their billing_tag column is NULL for ~1,230 rows. Suspect remap job may have stripped the non-billable tag during org id substitution. Added billing/backfill label.
2026-03-07 16:05 - SRE (Lena Huang): Collected merge job output. merge-2026-03-05-7 completed with 0 exit code but shows 4 warnings regarding org_id_remap table TTL; cross-checked with service-discovery. We will run targeted query to verify mapping consistency.
2026-03-08 12:10 - Customer (Elena Marquez): Thanks — hold lifted and services restored. Please advise on long-term fix and backdated billing adjustments if required.
2026-03-09 08:55 - Tomás Guerrero: Running backfill now (billing_recalc job). Expect recalculation to re-tag postbacks and adjust finalized invoice if needed. Will update when job completes.
Query run: SELECT count(*) FROM usage_postbacks WHERE org_id = 'org-nova-1145' AND billing_tag IS NULL AND probe_tag='non-billable' AND timestamp >= '2026-03-05' AND timestamp < '2026-03-07'; result: 1,237 rows.
Observation: postbacks were accepted by ingestion API with probe_tag preserved, but a downstream remap step that substitutes parent_org_id does a shallow copy and omits billing_tag if present. Code pointer: services/org-mapper/handler.go line ~312 (recent change in PR #4021 added shallow remap).
Hypothesis: org-merge job updated org_id on incoming postbacks using the org-mapper service which returned objects without the billing_tag field for some payload shapes (edge-case where probe_tag existed in headers but not in payload body).
Repro: replayed 10 sample postbacks through a staging replica of the remap service: 3/10 lost billing_tag. Root cause reproducible when header-based probe_tag is present but payload.billing_tag is null.
Related GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4021 (org-mapper shallow copy change, merged 2026-03-02).
Linked internal runbook: Confluence -> Billing -> org-merge-runbook (https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILL/pages/Org+Merge+Runbook)
Potential scope: Any org merges performed between 2026-03-02 and 2026-03-06 may have affected probe/non-billable tagging in postbacks.
2026-03-09 14:30 - Engineering: Deployed hotfix to org-mapper service to ensure billing_tag and probe_tag are preserved during remap (patch: org-mapper v1.3.2).
