Issue summary:
Customer QueryFlow reports sudden degradation in rerank relevance plus elevated p95 token latency from the reranking endpoint after an internal rolling change. Symptoms include: unexpected ordering changes in top-k results, higher tail latency for rerank requests, and intermittent 503s from the embed->rerank handoff. Impact: production traffic from QueryFlow (enterprise) sees 6-12% drop in expected top-5 recall for critical search flows and p95 latency jump from ~220ms to ~670ms.

Impact:
- Business-critical search feature experiencing visible quality regressions for end users (query samples attached).
- Elevated tail latency causing timeouts in QueryFlow application (some automated retries observed).

Environment:
- prod-us-east, customer tenant: queryflow-prod, routed via proxy-router cluster pr-us1.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/embeddings (text-embed-xl-v2), /v1/rerank (rerank-lite-v1).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send sample query set (provided in attachment) to embeddings endpoint pinned to text-embed-xl-v2 with tenant header X-Tenant: queryflow-prod.
2) Call rerank endpoint using returned embeddings without additional normalization.
3) Observe top-5 ordering vs baseline stored in QueryFlow eval set and check p95 latency on reranker traces.

Observed behavior:
- Non-deterministic top-k reordering compared to baseline; several queries show inversion of relevant candidates.
- Reranker logs show occasional fallback to CPU path due to upstream embed shape/metadata mismatch and router re-sharding events.
- Proxy-router logs show frequent 502/503s for the embed->rerank internal RPC during a 30m window.

Expected behavior:
- Stable top-k ordering for the same input and consistent p95 latency within SLOs (<=300ms).

Relevant logs/metrics (high level):
- spike in embed-service 500s at 2026-03-10T03:40Z correlating with router rolling update.
- reranker p95 increased to 670ms between 03:40Z-04:10Z.
- embed payload inspection shows alternating orientation flag values (row-major vs column-major) in metadata header on some requests.

2026-03-10 14:05 - Support (Asha Patel): Initial triage: asked customer for example queries, tenant headers, and whether they are pinning versions. Customer replied with sample bundle (attached) and noted they observed behavior starting approx 03:40 UTC.
2026-03-10 15:10 - Eng (Marcus Chen): Noted a router config rollout was executed in us-east around 03:35Z (PR referenced). Requested router and embed-service logs for 03:30Z-04:30Z. Assigned to serving-runtime and proxy-router oncall.
2026-03-11 09:22 - SRE (Leila Moreno): Found router hash ring change at 03:37Z that coincided with re-sharding events. Some embed requests had missing 'embed-orientation' header after proxy sidecar upgrade; these defaulted to legacy orientation interpretation and triggered downstream shape conversion and CPU fallback.
2026-03-12 11:41 - Customer (QueryFlow - James Lin): Confirmed that their client SDK did not include explicit normalization header; they rely on platform defaults. Asked for mitigation steps and whether hotfix can be provided.
2026-03-13 08:03 - Eng (Marcus Chen): Implemented a quick mitigation in staging to coerce missing orientation headers to the expected default and added a compatibility shim in proxy-router. Preparing canary in prod-us-east.
2026-03-13 12:50 - Support (Asha Patel): Communicated mitigation plan to customer and schedule for canary rollout at 2026-03-13T16:00Z. Requested that customer hold off config changes during canary window.
Hypothesis 1: Router hash ring change produced transient re-routing to replicas with older embed-service build that emits different orientation header formatting; this caused selective downstream CPU fallback and slight numerical drift in embeddings.
Hypothesis 2: Proxy sidecar upgrade inadvertently strips or renames 'embed-orientation' metadata header (observed in logs) for ~8% of requests, triggering a fallback normalization path in reranker that is slow and nondeterministic.
Evidence: Correlation between router rolling update time and spike in embed-service 500s and reranker p95. Packet capture and header dump show alternating presence/absence of 'x-embed-orientation' on affected requests.
Partial reproduction: Replayed affected customer bundle against staging proxy-router with the sidecar image from the rollout and reproduced top-k inversion on 3/25 test queries; enabling shim to add default header resolved ordering and reduced p95 back to ~240ms.
Next steps: schedule controlled canary in prod-us-east, roll forward proxy-router compatibility shim, and backfill integration tests for header preservation across router + sidecar.
Mitigation applied (2026-03-13): Canary deployment of proxy-router compatibility shim that injects missing 'x-embed-orientation: row-major' for unannotated requests. Canary metric snapshot shows reranker p95 returned to baseline (~230ms) for QueryFlow traffic and top-k recall recovered in sampled queries.
Planned permanent fix: Merge PR to router and sidecar to preserve embed metadata headers across re-shards and add explicit header requirement to embedding API; scheduled release 2026-03-18 after QA.
- Add non-regression test in CI to verify embed header propagation across proxy-router rolling updates.
- Notify customer of the permanent fix schedule and offer post-deployment validation run.
Follow-up: Create an internal post-incident note linking this ticket, the router PR, and the embed-service test failures. Recommend updating runbook to include header-preservation checks during rolling updates.
payload.summary: Embedding orientation mismatch combined with router-hash change causing degraded rerank quality and tail latency

Issue summary:
Customer KiteAnalytics reported intermittent mixed-model content inside long streaming responses for a pinned route. A single user stream would start returning tokens from the pinned version (growth-3b-v2) and midway through switch to the canary model (legacy-chat-7b) without an explicit fallback event in the application logs.

Impact:
- A small subset of long-running streaming sessions (approx 0.4% of requests during a 48h window) experienced content shifts mid-stream.
- Customer reported degraded coherence for long conversations and logged 14 high-priority support tickets internally.
- Affects production traffic in us-east-1 on dedicated capacity for KiteAnalytics.

Environment:
- prod us-east-1, Dedicated pool DK-11 serving growth-3b-v2 pinned routes.
- Fronted by API Gateway -> auth-proxy (session refresh service) -> streaming-router -> serving-runtime.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long streaming generate call with a pinned model version header (x-redwood-pin: growth-3b-v2).
2) Keep the connection open for >90s and generate multiple user messages (long conversation).
3) Trigger an auth token refresh (simulated by expiring session token) from the client side or wait for automatic refresh.
4) Observe that subsequent tokens in the same stream are produced by the canary model.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Router traces show initial route decision honored the x-redwood-pin header.
- At ~token N+48, logs show a header rewrite event at auth-proxy: Authorization header rotated and x-redwood-pin header absent in the rewritten request forwarded to streaming-router.
- Serving-runtime accepted the request and routed to canary because pin metadata was missing.
- No explicit fallback policy triggered in control-plane; router treated request as unpinned.
- Customer-provided transcript attached in comments (sensitive content redacted).

Hypothesis and root cause (investigation notes):
- The auth-proxy's session refresh path performs a conservative header sanitization pass when it swaps tokens; the code path intentionally removed unknown custom headers and reattached only whitelisted headers. x-redwood-pin was not on the whitelist and was dropped.
- Long-lived streaming requests that caused token refresh mid-stream got their pin metadata silently stripped, so routing fell back to default canary behavior.
- Short requests and non-streaming routes rarely hit the problematic path because token refresh happened client-side before request initiation.

Temporary mitigation / customer workaround:
- Immediately applied a proxy-side rule to preserve x-redwood-pin and x-redwood-session-id for streaming endpoints (hotfix ACL).
- Instructed KiteAnalytics to avoid client-side token expiry during a stream as a short-term workaround.
- Enabled request-level logging for affected customer routes to detect any further pin loss.

Permanent fix / next steps:
- Engineering (proxy team) to add x-redwood-pin and other inference routing headers to the proxy whitelist and add unit tests to prevent regression (PR opened: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/7241).
- Add integration test that simulates session refresh mid-stream and asserts pin preservation.
- Update runbook: streaming pin preservation and include checks in canary health verification.
- Roll out proxy hotfix to all regions; verify with synthetic streaming tests.

Status and timeline:
- Hotfix deployed to us-east-1 (mar 11) and confirmed to stop new occurrences for KiteAnalytics.
- Full rollout to eu-west and ap-southeast scheduled for mar 15 after automated test pass.

Resolution notes (work in progress):
- Auth-proxy whitelist adjusted in staging and prod us-east-1.
- Integration tests added to CI.
- Postmortem to follow once cross-region rollout completes.

Attachments: customer transcript excerpts, router trace snippets, auth-proxy logs (redacted).
2026-03-10 09:47 - Support (Aisha Kumar): Customer reported mixed-model tokens mid-stream. Initial triage suggests routing issue. Assigned to infra on-call.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:45 - Customer (KiteAnalytics - Ethan R.): Verified that new streams look stable after your change. Thanks — will report if we see more issues.
Note: affected several conversations started during morning ingest window.
2026-03-12 10:00 - Engineering (Miguel Santos): PR opened to include pin headers in proxy's canonical header set and added integration test. Scheduling prod rollout to remaining regions after CI green. PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/7241
Hotfix applied to preserve x-redwood-pin on auth-proxy for streaming endpoints; PR created to permanently whitelist pin headers and add regression tests. Full cross-region rollout pending CI verification.
Postmortem planned after rollout. Recommend adding header-preservation checks to canary test matrix to catch similar regressions in future.

Issue summary:
During automated HR->Okta SCIM sync for a remote new hire (employee_id: 105224), two Okta user objects were created: one with the canonical company email (jane.doe@redwood.ai) and a second temporary object with the HR alternate email (jane.d@contractors.redwood.ai). The provisioning pipeline created service accounts and provisioned a work laptop for both objects. One laptop was sent to the contractor address (incorrect) and VPN conditional access failed for the canonical account because group membership lived on the duplicate object.

Impact:
- New hire cannot complete first-day tasks due to VPN and GitHub access gaps.
- Unnecessary device shipped to wrong address (logistics + security risk).
- Excess service accounts created, increasing audit surface and license consumption.

Environment:
- Identity provider: Okta (SCIM mapping from Workday HRIS).
- Provisioning pipeline: onboard-scripts (k8s job in prod/us-west).
- Asset management: asset-shipper (US logistics partner).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create HR record with primary_email = jane.doe@redwood.ai and alternate_email = jane.d@contractors.redwood.ai and employee_id = 105224.
2) Trigger daily SCIM sync.
3) Observe Okta creates two user objects when SCIM mapping normalizes preferred_username differently and HRIS contains the alternate_email field.
4) Run onboarding pipeline which looks up by email and, failing to find a single unique match, creates per-object service accounts and kicks off asset order for both entries.

Logs / traces (examples):
- SCIM sync job run 2026-03-10T03:12Z: https://logs.redwood.tools/scim-sync/2026-03-10-03-12 (trace id scim-20260310-03-12-ff7b)
- Okta user objects: okta://org/00u7abcd/user/00u1primary and okta://org/00u7abcd/user/00u2alt (object ids redacted in ticket)
- Provisioning runs: onboard-scripts job id onboard-20260310-7f2a, asset-shipper order id ASH-77321

Investigation notes:
- IAM reviewed Okta objects and confirmed two distinct users exist. The canonical account (email jane.doe@redwood.ai) lacked the onboarding-group membership because the group assignment job matched on Okta object id that was attached to the alt object.
- Provisioning logs show onboarding-script chooses a match by querying Okta for email; because both objects listed emails (primary vs alt), the script returned both and proceeded to create separate service accounts rather than failing fast.
- Asset-shipper accepted two orders because it received two distinct device requests with the same employee_id missing from the payload. The package went to the address associated with the alt object (contractor address).
- Root cause: SCIM mapping allowed multiple user creation when alternate_email exists and preferred_username normalization differed. Provisioning lacked a unique employee_id check and relied solely on email matching.

comments: 2026-03-12T03:10:00Z Aisha Patel: Customer PXlMotif reported that ~2% of requests were returning mixed outputs after our canary rollback. They attached example request IDs: pxm-3921-reqs: [r-1001, r-1002, r-1007]. Asked for immediate mitigation and ETA.

2026-03-12T03:25:00Z Marcus Liu: Investigating orchestrator and metadata-sync. Noticed control-plane returned intermittent 503s during the weight flip window. Routing-mesh shows persistent hold attributes for affected sessions. Will attempt manual cache clear for pxm-3921.
payload.description:
Issue summary: After an automated metadata sync failed during a scheduled canary weight shift, a subset of tenant sessions observed a persistent 'version hold' that continued to route traffic to a degraded variant even after the canary was rolled back. Impact: Customer PixelMotif reports increased error rates and content-quality regressions for ~2% of their requests; billing spike observed due to unexpected fallback to an older model variant with higher per-token cost. Environment: Production (us-east-1), Dedicated pool for PixelMotif, canary rollout triggered March 12 02:30 UTC. Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger canary weight update for redwood/gpt-13b-quantized-v2 from 0% -> 15% via control-plane API.
2) Introduce transient metadata store error (observed in run: control-plane returned 503 for ~45s).
3) Retry commit rollback to previous weights.
4) Observe subset of session routing logs and responses for tenant pxm-3921.
Observed behavior: After the rollback completed, approx 1.8% of pxm-3921 sessions continued to be routed to an older variant (degraded-v1) and saw tokenization deltas. These sessions had a stale route attribute 'version_hold=true' persisted in the routing mesh cache. Expected behavior: After rollback or successful resync, session routing should clear ephemeral holds and respect the active variant selection. Logs / telemetry:
- Orchestrator: "commit: rollback success, epoch 2243" (03-12T02:33:12Z)
- Metadata-sync service: repeated 503s 03-12T02:31:05Z - 03-12T02:31:50Z
- Routing-mesh: session cache miss then stale attribute present: "session pxm-3921: hold=degraded-v1 ttl=3600 persisted=true" (03-12T02:35:40Z)
- Edge-proxy: 502 spikes for pxm-3921 (03-12T02:32:00Z - 02:33:00Z)
Hypothesis: The metadata-sync failure left partial writes in the routing-mesh's ephemeral cache. A subsequent rollback path did not invalidate a per-session 'hold' flag because the hold commit path depends on a successful control-plane acknowledgement. Failure to write the hold-clear event produced sticky routing affinity. Temporary workaround: A manual cache invalidation for the affected tenant cohort on the routing-mesh cleared the holds and restored normal routing. Next steps: 1) Reproduce in staging with injected metadata-store 503s; 2) Add stronger idempotent semantics for hold-clear commits; 3) Add a TTL eviction safety net so ephemeral holds older than X are forcibly cleared after rollback; 4) Post-incident patch to resync routing caches after any control-plane sync error.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 03:40 UTC - SRE (Hannah Ortiz): Performed targeted routing-mesh cache invalidation for tenant pxm-3921 at 03:36 UTC. Customer confirms degraded-v1 routing drops to 0% for those example request IDs. Monitoring for reappearance.
2026-03-12 04:05 UTC - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer reports service quality restored for provided samples. Billing team notified to investigate the cost delta from degraded variant token pricing during the window.
2026-03-12 10:15 UTC - Eng (Marcus Liu): Root-cause hypothesis drafted: hold-clear write path from control-plane to routing-mesh is not idempotent; transient 503s left routing-mesh in a semi-committed state. Added integration test plan to simulate 5xx during commit and rollback flows.
2026-03-13 09:00 UTC - Eng (Marcus Liu): Working on a hotfix to add a deterministic ack for hold-clear events and a safety TTL on ephemeral holds. Patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/4482. Staging runs scheduled.
Mitigated: manual routing-mesh cache invalidation performed for pxm-3921 restoring correct routing. Engineering implemented temporary guard: TTL-based eviction on ephemeral holds (configurable, default 10m) pushed to staging. Long-term fix: make hold-clear commits idempotent with control-plane acknowledgements; will land PR #4482 and run canary test with injected metadata failures. Billing adjustment: finance flagged for review of cost delta for affected window. Postmortem to be scheduled after rollback verification in multi-region runs.
payload.summary: Sticky version hold after control-plane metadata sync failure causes silent fallback to degraded variant

comments: Aisha Patel: Customer reported sustained throughput drop at 09:20 UTC and provided sample logs and collector config. Assigned to infra on-call.

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightVoice reported a sustained drop in P50/P95 throughput on their Dedicated pool beginning ~2026-03-10 09:20 UTC. Impact: customer experiences 30-60% lower completed requests per second for batched generation routes, increased request queueing, and occasional 504s. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated tenant) in us-east; running redwood-instruct-3b as primary pinned model. Observed behavior: batcher latencies climb gradually, followed by autoscaler scale-up attempts and then a cascade of short-lived evictions. We observed GPU scheduling stalls concurrent with high-frequency metrics snapshots from a background collector sidecar. Expected behavior: background telemetry should be asynchronous and not hold GPU resources while host inference is running.
1) Route synthetic batched traffic at the same QPS/mean request size as BrightVoice into their dedicated pool (prod us-east).
2) Enable the metrics sidecar with the same collection interval and full-kernel snapshot enabled (metrics-collector v1.4.2 config: snapshot_gpu=on, interval_ms=200).
3) Observe batcher/prefetch timing and GPU utilization over ~10 minutes.
4) Compare with same load but with collector snapshot_gpu=off to confirm regression disappears.
[2026-03-10T09:23:15Z] serving-runtime INFO batcher: batch assembled size=8 latency=120ms
[2026-03-10T09:23:15Z] metrics-collector DEBUG acquiring_gpu_lock for snapshot (tenant=brightvoice, pool=dedicated-us-east)
[2026-03-10T09:23:15Z] gpu-scheduler WARN gpu_lock_held duration=310ms src=metrics-collector (pid=7421)
[2026-03-10T09:23:16Z] batcher ERROR inference_timeout waiting_for_gpu after=300ms route=/generate
[2026-03-10T09:24:00Z] autoscaler INFO scale_up_triggered reason=queue_depth_threshold current_replicas=12 target=18
Initial hypothesis: a background telemetry process is synchronously acquiring a GPU resource or pinning the NVMe/GPU DMA path when taking full-kernel snapshots, blocking inference kernels for short windows and triggering cascading scheduling/backpressure effects.
Telemetry: high-frequency (200ms) snapshot configuration observed in customer deployment; collector binary is metrics-collector v1.4.2 (not yet hardened for dedicated pools).
Correlation: GPU lock events in serving logs align with batcher timeouts and immediate autoscaler scale-ups. When snapshots are disabled, throughput returns to baseline in lab repros.
Side-effects: autoscaler reacts to transient queue growth by adding replicas; because collector holds GPU briefly but repeatedly, added replicas experience identical behavior (eviction loops), causing oscillation and effective throughput loss.
Repro steps validated in staging with an instrumented sidecar; root cause narrowed to synchronous cudaMemcopy/trace capture in metrics-collector native shim.

Additional notes:
SRE (Lina Chen): Temporary mitigation: advising customer to set metrics-collector.snapshot_gpu=false and increase interval to 10s. Workaround reduced the lock frequency and restored throughput to baseline.
Eng (Ravi Iyer): Created internal issue INT-4182 to patch metrics-collector to use async GPU snapshots and fall back to lightweight telemetry for dedicated pools. Draft PR: github.com/redwood/metrics-collector/pull/214
Customer (BrightVoice - PM): Confirmed temporary workaround applied and throughput restored; requests permanent remediation and release timeline.
Investigating. Temporary mitigation recommended: set metrics-collector.snapshot_gpu=false and interval >= 10000 ms. Engineering working on async snapshot patch for metrics-collector (see linked PR).
payload.summary: Unexpected GPU locking by background metrics collector causing sustained dedicated throughput degradation

comments: 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z Aisha Raman: Customer provided traces and example curl commands. Observed correlation between ALPN=h2 negotiation and increased TLS handshake/route-change occurrences.
2026-03-10T11:04:00Z Tom Halpern: Assigned. Reproducing in lab with client SDK and curl. Created packetcapture on edge to inspect ALPN/SNI behavior.

2026-03-11T16:30:00Z Tom Halpern: Collected correlation dashboard: spikes align to ALPN=h2 sessions that landed on edge pool ep-12 which had transient auth token cache misses during specific control-plane rollout window.
2026-03-12T16:10:00Z Tom Halpern: Confirmed we'll provide clear remediation steps and schedule infra-side fix if required.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent increases in request latency (p50 -> p95 spikes) and occasional auth retries when their client libraries connect using HTTP/2. They observe that switching the client to force HTTP/1.1 (disabling ALPN negotiation) makes the problem disappear.

Impact:
- FinSight is seeing elevated end-to-end latencies for embedding requests originating in eu-west (~30-120ms additional latency on affected requests).
- A small fraction (~0.8%) of requests retry due to auth handshake/timeouts.
- This impacts nightly batch embeds and some low-latency product features.

Environment:
- Production (eu-west) primary, some requests routed to us-east as control-plane decides fallback.
- Customer uses managed SDK v2.4.1 with default HTTP/2 settings.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Run embedding batch from a vm in eu-west with SDK v2.4.1 (default HTTP/2/ALPN).
2) Observe p95 latency and occasional 401/504 auth retries in logs.
3) Re-run with SDK configured to force HTTP/1.1 (disable HTTP/2/ALPN) -> issue disappears.

Relevant logs/headers (redacted):
- Edge logs show initial connection negotiated with ALPN h2, SNI matches edge host, TLS handshake time higher by ~40ms on affected requests.
- Control-plane routing decision log snippets show route rules evaluated differently for connections marked as http2-capable (tagged by edge).

Customer ask:
They want clarification: does ALPN / HTTP/2 negotiation influence residency selection or fallback routing? Is there a known edge/control-plane behavior that prefers different egress pools for h2 vs h1, and could that cause cross-region fallbacks and auth handshakes? They also request a mitigation path for production: is disabling HTTP/2 a reasonable workaround?

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 14:22 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Noted that some edge pools tag incoming connections by protocol and route to different backend pools for performance isolation. Investigating whether backend pool for http2 had pending capacity/transient auth proxy errors.
2026-03-11 08:50 - Customer (FinSight): Confirmed forcing HTTP/1.1 in their SDK removes retries and latency; asked for a root cause and permanent fix.
2026-03-12 09:05 - Support (Aisha): Provided temporary mitigation to customer: pin SDK to force-http1 or set connection_reuse_timeout lower to avoid stale auth cache hits; customer accepted workaround while we investigate fix.
2026-03-12 12:00 - Eng (Lina Wu): Noted follow-up task to evaluate whether protocol-based routing tags should influence residency decisions. Filing INT ticket to capture infra change discussion.
2026-03-12 15:40 - Customer: Requested confirmation that forcing HTTP/1.1 is safe long-term and any production-side changes that would remove need for it.
Edge behavior: ALPN negotiation (client advertises 'h2') results in edge marking connection as http2-capable. Edge uses that tag to assign to an http2-optimized backend pool for efficiency (continuous streams, multiplexing).
Control-plane routing: residency decision is normally made using token-scoped residency stamp and region affinity. However, we observed an additional routing dimension: protocol-capability tag used by edge to select backend micro-pools (recent optimization rolled out to reduce http1/http2 tail latencies).
Auth/cache observation: the http2-optimized pool ep-12 was undergoing a token cache refresh sequence during a control-plane rollout; ephemeral token cache miss caused auth proxy to validate with KMS and added ~30-80ms and occasional 401/504 on timeouts.
Fallback flow: when auth proxy timed out or rejected, control-plane applied a fallback route to a different region (us-east) under our cross-region fallback policy — this explains occasional cross-region hops seen in traces.
Customer-side reproduction: forcing http1 bypassed http2-optimized pool assignment, so connections hit the stable http1 pool that didn't experience cache refresh, hence lower latency and no retries.
Risk assessment: Not all customers are impacted; effect surface depends on whether their edge-to-backend pool was in a transient state during rollout. Protocol-based micro-pooling increases variance during rollout windows.
Hypothesis: Recent optimization that splits pools by protocol capability + a control-plane rollout of auth-cache invalidation created a timing window where http2 pool had increased auth validation latency, triggering fallback and retry behavior.
Workaround provided to customer: configure SDK to force HTTP/1.1 for critical workloads (SDK flag example provided), or apply connection_reuse_timeout change to reduce probability of hitting an invalidated token cache entry.
Short-term infra fix: rolled back the protocol-based pool split for eu-west for a controlled subset of edges to reduce variance while auth-cache rollout completes (deployed 2026-03-12 14:00 UTC).
Medium-term changes: engineering to implement graceful cache refresh for auth proxies and avoid hard token cache invalidation windows; also track per-pool rollout status to avoid assigning new connections to pools undergoing cache migration.
Customer communication: Notified FinSight on 2026-03-12 16:00 that controlled rollback reduced p95 spikes and retries; asked to monitor for 48h and confirm. Customer acknowledged improvement.
Follow-ups created: INT-32791 (review protocol-based routing), INT-32792 (auth proxy cache safe-refresh design). Support to update public KB article about ALPN/protocol routing and recommended SDK settings for sensitive workloads.
Final status: Pending customer confirmation after 48h monitoring window. Recommend leaving ticket open until customer verifies stability; once confirmed mark Resolved with postmortem link.
payload.summary: Client TLS ALPN influencing control-plane routing selection and intermittent region selection latency

payload.description:
Customer reports that after a recent edge proxy rollout they observed (a) top-k candidate reordering for the same queries compared to prior baseline and (b) intermittent 200–800ms tail latency spikes from the rerank endpoint. Early signs point to an intermittent header that indicates embedding provenance being flipped/omitted between the embedding ingestion pipeline and the reranker, causing a fallback normalization path and extra serialization that both changes candidate ordering and increases tail latency.
1) Customer sends batch of 64 documents to /embeddings with header X-Embed-Provenance: origin-v2 (consistent payloads).
2) Immediately call /rerank with the same feature IDs and request top_k=10 under high-concurrency (QPS ~120).
3) Observe that responses intermittently have different top-3 ordering than previous baseline recorded 24 hours earlier for identical payloads.
4) Observe per-request latency for rerank spikes on a subset of requests (200–800ms extra) correlated with proxy logs showing X-Embed-Provenance missing or set to origin-v1.
5) Replaying the same traffic through a staging proxy (pre-rollout) does not reproduce the issue consistently.
2026-03-09T18:22:03Z proxy.us-east-1 INFO request_id=abc123 headers=X-Embed-Provenance: origin-v2
2026-03-09T18:22:03Z reranker.us-east-1 WARN request_id=abc123 fallback_normalization=fp32->fp16_cost+serialize_delay=220ms topk_diff_detected=true
2026-03-09T18:22:04Z proxy.us-east-1 INFO request_id=def456 headers=X-Embed-Provenance: origin-v1
2026-03-09T18:22:04Z reranker.us-east-1 WARN request_id=def456 applied_compat_path=true extra_latency_ms=510 topk_diff_detected=true
2026-03-09T18:23:11Z embedding-ingest.us-east-1 ERROR request_id=ghi789 missing_header=X-Embed-Provenance dropped_flag=false
2026-03-10 - Initial triage by Support (Maya): Pattern of header toggling observed in proxy traces. Customer provided request/response pairs and golden baselines.
2026-03-10 - CS Eng (Ethan) reproduced topk variance in a controlled replay when intentionally toggling X-Embed-Provenance between v1 and v2; reranker uses a fast path when provenance==v2 that avoids an extra normalization/quant-decoder, producing deterministic ordering.
2026-03-11 - Deeper trace: a recent edge-proxy image (rev 2026.03.05) contains a batching/jitter optimization that coalesces requests; under certain race windows it strips or overwrites X-Embed-Provenance when upstream connection pooling forwards to an older backend instance.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - Risk assessment: High — affects rerank determinism for dedicated customers with heterogeneous edge fleets; correlated with elevated tail latency reported by customer.
2026-03-12 - Temporary mitigation validated: Proxy config change to disable coalescing/jitter optimization for the customer's canary pool eliminated header flips in replays and restored baseline top-k and tail latency for 48k replays.
2026-03-12 - Engineering plan: roll back proxy optimization in affected pool, add strict header passthrough tests, and add guard in proxy to reject requests missing X-Embed-Provenance for embed/rerank flows (return 4xx) to avoid silent fallback.
Links: slack:#support (thread t12345), confluence:/runbooks/embed-rerank-provenance-checks, gh:/pull/enterprise-proxy-rollout-fix
2026-03-11 09:48 - Customer (Amir Haddad, DialogicSearch): We saw the issue ramp up after a Thursday night deploy. Rolling back that deploy made things better but we need a root fix.
2026-03-12 11:20 - Engineering (Ethan): Posting interim mitigation steps to Confluence and opening PR for proxy fix. Will schedule a full rollout with header passthrough tests.
2026-03-12 16:05 - Customer (Amir Haddad): Thank you — can we get an ETA for permanent fix and test coverage so we can be confident it won't reoccur?
Mitigation applied: disabled proxy coalescing in affected canary pool and customer confirmed restoration of baseline top-k order and reduced rerank tail latency. Long-term fix in progress: PR opened to ensure header passthrough across pooling logic and add unit/integration tests; proxy will return 4xx for missing X-Embed-Provenance on embed/rerank flows to force observable failure instead of silent fallback. Follow-ups: monitor for 72h post-rollout, add regression test to CI, and notify customers with guidance on how to surface provenance header on custom proxies.
payload.summary: Embedding provenance header flip leads to candidate index shift and sporadic rerank tail latency

payload.description:
Issue summary: ClearHealth reported a series of resumed conversational requests (user resumes session after short disconnect) that observe elevated tail latency (p99 ~4.2s) and occasional timeouts, compared to normal p99 ~250ms. This occurs after sessions have been inactive for ~30-90s. Impact: user-facing latency spikes and a small number of 504 timeouts causing degraded UX in production. Behavior is reproducible for certain session IDs and high-frequency resume patterns.

Context: This ticket was opened by Support after customer escalation. Initial triage indicates the serving runtime enters a blocking cold-path when a session key is considered "leased" by another backend shard due to a lease state that does not expire promptly. The behavior started after the kvcache lease change in release v2.18.

Customer-visible p99 latency increase to ~4s for resumed conversational turns; ~0.8% request timeout rate for affected sessions during the window. Affects ClearHealth production in us-east and may affect other enterprise customers using session pinning/lease feature.
1) Customer flow: create a long-lived chat session, send several turns until KV caching warm (baseline p99 ~200ms)
2) Allow session to be idle for 30-90 seconds
3) Resume conversation with a short prompt (identical to prior recent prompt), observe p99 latency spike and occasional 504
4) Reproduce by replaying traffic through our proxy with the same session_id and headers; behavior crops up intermittently for a subset of session_ids
2026-03-10T14:22:11Z [serving-runtime] session_id=ch-9a2 lease_check: found lease owner shard-7, lease_expiry=1970-01-01T00:00:00Z (infinite)
2026-03-10T14:22:12Z [kvcache] session_id=ch-9a2 warmup: blocking rehydrate sync (caller blocked for 3.9s)
2026-03-10T14:22:12Z [api-gateway] request_id=... status=504 latency=4207ms upstream_error=timeout

Additional notes:
Hypothesis A: Lease TTL regressed to 0 (infinite) for leases that experienced an RPC error during lease refresh, leaving keys marked as 'leased' indefinitely. This causes a new request to perform synchronous rehydrate under mutex, causing blocking latency.
Hypothesis B: Lease owner shard experiences GC pause and does not renew leases; other shards treat lease as active and synchronously attempt to take ownership using blocking backoff path introduced in v2.18.
Data: metric sticky_lease_count spiked from 0.02% -> 0.9% of session keys between 2026-03-10 02:00Z and 06:00Z. Correlates with increased p99 on serving-runtime for resumed sessions. Heap and GC traces on shard-7 show recurring short STW pauses ~200-400ms at times of spike.
Reproduction attempts: Ran a traffic replay tool that simulates 10k resumed-session requests across 5 shards; reproduced p99 spike only when replay included sessions that hit shards with sticky_lease_count > 0.6%.
Quick mitigation tested: Manually triggered eviction on shard-7 kvcache entries for 12 sample session_ids; resumed requests for those sessions returned to baseline latency.
Related artifacts: Slack thread #support link: https://slack.redwood/support/CK12345; Perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/s/dash/kv-lease; Erroring commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/commit/abc123
Workaround applied: manual eviction script run against affected shards (shard-7, shard-12) to clear sticky leases for impacted sessions; instructed customer on session-safety workaround: rotate session_id when possible. Root cause and permanent fix: Reverted lease behavior change from commit abc123 that left leases non-expiring on RPC failure. Deployed patch v2.18.1 that restores lease fallback TTL and adds a non-blocking rehydrate path (async warmup) so callers are not blocked. Added alerting for sticky_lease_count > 0.2% and a runbook to forcibly evict leases if alert fires. Follow-ups: create a test harness to simulate RPC error paths on lease refresh and add unit tests for lease expiry, update changelog and deployment notes. Customer-facing follow-up: support will send an incident summary and timeline to ClearHealth and schedule a 1:1 with their SRE in the next 48 hours.

Issue summary:
Customer (Clearance Bank) is onboarding Redwood audit exports into their SOC SIEM. They require a replayable activity ledger (chronological order) where each exported event is cryptographically signed (per-event signature or detached signature bundle) so the customer can verify non-repudiation and chain-of-custody when ingesting into their SIEM.

Impact:
- SOC ingestion cannot be finalized without per-event verification; blocking their compliance sign-off and STP production onboarding.
- Potential audit risk for financial transactions if events cannot be proven unchanged.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted audit export (prod-us-east) -> customer SIEM via SFTP or webhook (customer prefers webhook over TLS).
- Customer uses Splunk HF + indexed RT ingestion, expects NDJSON lines with header metadata.

Customer asks for:
1) Specification for per-event signature format (prefer Ed25519 detached signatures) and canonical JSON fields to sign.
2) A sample signed NDJSON export for a 24-hour window (timezone-normalized UTC) with resume tokens.
3) SIEM adapter mapping guidance (Splunk HEC field mapping example).
4) Runbook entries for resume/replay and gap detection (how to detect and request missing ranges).

Steps to reproduce / reproduce notes:
- Customer has not yet attempted ingestion because they require signature spec first. Support reproduced current audit export format and verified there is no per-event signature header today.

Logs / Evidence collected:
- Audit export job logs: export-job-2026-03-09T03:12Z (attached to ticket).
- Delivery logs show successful webhook handshakes but no signature header.

Requested deliverables (customer):
- A short deliverable pack: specification doc, one signed sample NDJSON (24h), a Splunk HEC example mapping, and a short runbook for detection+replay.

2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Liam Patel): Acknowledged. Opening P1 intake. Looping in SRE and Security for guidance on signature format.
2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Maya Chen): Assigned. Requested customer's SIEM ingestion specifics (HEC vs webhook file drop), and whether they require embedded signature field or detached .sig files per batch.
2026-03-10 11:30 - Customer (Security Ops, Clearance Bank): They prefer Ed25519 detached signatures per event and HEC ingestion. They want each NDJSON line to include event_id, event_ts (UTC), and resume_token. Prefer 2048-bit or better verification curve (they asked about Ed25519 specifically).
2026-03-11 08:45 - Security (Anya Morales): Recommended Ed25519 for per-event detached signatures. Noted HSM-backed signing key material management in Redwood Private — asked if customer needs attestation of key handling (Y/N).
2026-03-11 14:22 - Engineering (Jia Huang): Found an existing PR (audit-proxy#182) that implements detached-signature .sig per event for the batch exporter. Needs review for production hardening (resume token inclusion, canonical JSON ordering).
2026-03-12 09:00 - Support (Maya Chen): Preparing sample 24h signed NDJSON using staging key; will label as sample-only, not production-signed (customer notified). Target to upload sample to SFTP test bucket and provide Splunk HEC mapping snippet by 2026-03-13.
2026-03-12 11:10 - Customer: Confirmed sample staging OK, asked that signed sample include an example of replay gap detection workflow (simple script or curl commands to request missing sequence).
Checked audit-service: current export pipeline attaches export metadata but does not compute per-event detached signatures. Export pipeline is modular; signing hook exists in audit-proxy but is gated behind feature flag 'event_detached_signature'.
Hypothesis: Enabling the feature flag and populating canonical_signing_path should produce .sig attachments per event. Need to ensure canonical JSON fingerprint is deterministic across languages (use RFC8785 JSON Canonicalization?).
Observed: resume_token is present in top-level export batch metadata but not emitted per NDJSON line currently — engineer needs to add resume_token field to each event output for customer's replay validation.
SRE note: HSM-backed key can be used in Redwood Private. For hosted customers we can provide a signing key managed by Redwood but need customer consent to trust. Suggested interim: provide sample signed file using ephemeral staging key and separate production roadmap if they require HSM attestation.
Related code: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-proxy/tree/feat/event-signatures (PR referenced above). Engineer suggests adding a verification test with deterministic canonicalization and cross-language verifier (node/python).
Risk: If canonicalization differs, verification will fail. Need to choose and document canonicalization library and include sample verifiers for Splunk ingestion pipeline (python script included in sample pack).
Timeline estimate: produce sample and mapping guidance within 3 business days; for production-grade signed export with HSM attestation and permanent key provisioning estimate 3-4 sprints pending prioritization.
Workaround provided: sample 24h NDJSON signed with staging Ed25519 key uploaded to customer SFTP test bucket (link provided in comment). Runbook for replay detection and a small python verifier included in the sample pack.
Planned fix: Enable 'event_detached_signature' feature flag for customer's export pipeline and extend exporter to include resume_token per event. Roadmap item to add HSM attestation and formal key provisioning for enterprise customers. Target prod rollout contingent on security review and PR hardening (see github.com/redwood-inference/audit-proxy/pull/182).
Deliver sample signed NDJSON (staging) and Splunk HEC mapping by 2026-03-13.
Coordinate Security to confirm HSM attestation needs; if yes, schedule key provisioning call with customer and Solutions Engineer.
Open engineering rollout ticket to enable feature flag for customer exports and add per-event resume_token emission (linked INT-1321).
Add deterministic canonicalization tests and cross-language verifiers to CI for audit-proxy PR.
Once prod-ready, schedule a dry-run ingestion window with customer and capture acceptance sign-off for compliance evidence.

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Customer (Tensorlytics) reports a sudden ~20–30% drop in throughput (tokens/sec) for their Dedicated pool in eu-west.
- Impact appears isolated to eu-west; us-east Dedicated pool for the same workload unchanged.
- Redwood perf-canary also flagged a tokens/sec regression in eu-west for at least one overlapping model.

Customer impact
- Customer-facing symptoms: longer time-to-first-token (mild) and materially slower generation throughput (primary complaint).
- Customer observed: same prompt + parameters, same concurrency, but higher wall-clock completion times starting ~2026-01-18 08:10 UTC.
- Business impact: degraded SLOs for their production workload; they asked whether a rollback is possible.

Environment
- Deployment mode: Dedicated
- Region: eu-west
- Hardware: H100 pool (80GB) (per fleet inventory)
- Models: llama-3.1-70b-instruct (primary), mixtral-8x7b-instruct (secondary)
- Runtime: redwood-runtime v0.41.x (exact build tag confirmed below)

Initial customer report (from Support intake)
- Timestamp of onset: ~2026-01-18 08:10 UTC
- Comparison: eu-west Dedicated slower vs eu-west historical baseline; us-east Dedicated stable
- Workload: chat completions, streaming enabled, max_tokens 512–1024, typical prompt lengths 1.5k–4k tokens, concurrency ~12–20

What we looked at (triage checklist)
1) Confirm scope (region-only vs global)
2) Check perf-canary signals for eu-west + same model/hardware
3) Separate queueing/scheduler vs runtime execution (prefill/decode) vs infrastructure
4) Correlate against recent changes: runtime release, kernel change, scheduler config, fleet/image/driver changes, power caps

Timeline / investigation notes

2026-01-18 08:32 UTC - Comment (Rafael Mendes, Support)
- Acknowledged customer report and opened Sev2 incident track.
- Asked customer for a representative request_id(s) and their own before/after timestamps.
- Routed to #eng-sre and #eng-runtime with note: “eu-west only, tokens/sec down; possible fleet change.”

2026-01-18 09:05 UTC - Comment (Aisha Bello, SRE)
- Confirmed perf-canary warning in eu-west on llama-3.1-70b-instruct: tokens/sec down ~24% vs baseline, p95 latency slightly elevated but not the primary regression.
- Canary breakdown: runtime decode time increased; queueing time not materially changed. Batch size distribution roughly stable.
- Noted canary started flagging within ~20–30 mins of customer-reported onset.

2026-01-18 09:22 UTC - Comment (Noah Patel, Serving Runtime TL)
- Quick check: no runtime release rolled out to eu-west in the last 24h beyond standard stagger; runtime build tag observed in telemetry matches us-east.
- Kernel selection tags (from runtime telemetry) unchanged for the model (same kernel id family) — makes a pure kernel regression less likely.
- Requested Infra/Fleet to check eu-west node image / driver / power management changes.

2026-01-18 09:41 UTC - Comment (Vanessa Ortiz, Fleet)
- Found eu-west Dedicated H100 pool had an accelerated node image rollout starting 2026-01-18 07:55 UTC (image “gpu-node-euw-2026.01.18a”).
- Rollout reason: security patch + minor NVIDIA driver update.
- Rollout reached ~60% of eu-west dedicated nodes by 08:25 UTC.
- Hypothesis: new driver defaulted to a lower power limit / application clocks not being set by our init script.

2026-01-18 10:10 UTC - Comment (Logan Wright, Telemetry)
- Confirmed canary vs customer metrics align when filtering on eu-west + H100 SKU + node_image label.
- Observed tokens/sec on nodes with new image is ~0.74x compared to old image for same model/version.
- No corresponding increase in queueing time, suggesting per-GPU execution throughput regression.

2026-01-18 10:26 UTC - Comment (Vanessa Ortiz, Fleet)
- Verified via node bootstrap logs: nvidia-smi shows power cap not being applied on new image; running at a lower default limit.
- Noted a packaging change: init script path changed; our “set-clocks” unit did not run.
- Proposed mitigation: halt rollout and roll back eu-west dedicated pool to previous image; then hotfix image.

2026-01-18 10:38 UTC - Comment (Sean Gallagher, SRE)
- Approved rollback given customer impact + canary corroboration.
- Asked for safe-change plan: staggered rollback to avoid capacity shock.

2026-01-18 11:05 UTC - Comment (Vanessa Ortiz, Fleet)
- Action taken: paused rollout at 63% and began rollback to “gpu-node-euw-2026.01.12c” with max surge constraints.
- Expected time to recover: 60–90 mins.

2026-01-18 12:14 UTC - Comment (Rafael Mendes, Support)
- Updated customer: identified region-local infra change; rollback in progress; ETA ~1–2 hours for full recovery.
- Provided workaround for immediate relief: lower concurrency by ~15% to reduce tail effects while throughput stabilizes.

2026-01-18 13:02 UTC - Comment (Aisha Bello, SRE)
- Metrics: tokens/sec recovered gradually as rollback progressed.
- Perf-canary warning cleared after rollback reached ~85% (alert auto-resolved based on anti-flap window).
- p95 latency returned close to baseline; tokens/sec within 3–5% of baseline.

2026-01-18 14:20 UTC - Comment (Customer via Support summary)
- Customer confirms throughput is “back to normal” for their eu-west Dedicated deployment.
- Requested post-incident write-up and assurance about change controls.

Root cause
- Eu-west Dedicated H100 pool node image rollout (gpu-node-euw-2026.01.18a) changed the location/behavior of GPU clock/power-limit bootstrap. The unit responsible for applying application clocks/power cap did not execute.
- As a result, GPUs ran at lower effective power limit/clock settings, reducing decode throughput and overall tokens/sec.
- The issue was isolated to eu-west because the accelerated image rollout was region-scoped; other regions did not receive the image at the time.

Detection
- Customer ticket triggered initial response.
- Perf-canary independently detected tokens/sec regression for the same model/region and helped isolate the issue via node_image/hardware dimension correlation.

Resolution
- Paused eu-west rollout and rolled back the Dedicated GPU fleet to the previous node image.
- Confirmed recovery via:
  - tokens/sec back within baseline tolerance
  - perf-canary warning resolved
  - no sustained increase in queueing time or error rates

Follow-ups / action items
- Fleet: publish hotfix node image restoring clock/power-limit bootstrap; add explicit boot-time validation (fail health check if clocks not applied).
- Runtime/Telemetry: ensure perf-canary alert payload includes node_image/build tags in the “top contributors” section for faster infra attribution.
- SRE: add a pre-rollout canary gate for eu-west fleet image changes using perf-canary tokens/sec signal on top dedicated models.
- Support/CS: provide customer-facing summary and confirm change-management improvements.

Customer comms
- Customer received interim updates during rollback and a final confirmation after recovery.
- Support to send brief RCA summary + preventive steps (no customer data involved; synthetic canary detected regression).

Internal links referenced during incident (for context)
- Slack: #incidents thread for INC-2026-0118-EUW-THROUGHPUT (internal)
- Runbook used: runbook-perf-regression-canary-alert
- Dashboards: perf-canary per-model tokens/sec (eu-west) and fleet rollout tracking (eu-west H100 dedicated)

Resolution date
- Service restored: 2026-01-18
- Ticket marked Resolved after customer confirmation and follow-up plan logged: 2026-01-22
payload.summary: Tokens/sec drop in eu-west Dedicated pool (isolated to region; perf-canary signal correlates with fleet image rollout)

comments: 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Aisha Patel: Customer reported p99 spikes starting after a config tweak on 2026-03-09. Provided initial graphs and asked for SRE investigation. Assigned to Marco.

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightMetrics reported intermittent increases in p95/p99 latency and occasional 504 timeouts for chat-generation routes during steady low-to-moderate QPS. Impact: customer-facing latency regressions causing user-facing timeouts and one support SLA breach. Environment: Hosted production cluster serving enterprise customer in us-east on dedicated capacity. Initial observation window: 2026-03-09 22:00 -> 2026-03-10 06:00 UTC.
User-facing slowdowns and periodic 504s on chat endpoints for BrightMetrics (enterprise). Affects ~3% of requests in observed window with p99 > 2.5s and intermittent 504s. Business impact: disruption to live analytics demos and automated alerting from customer side.
1) Use BrightMetrics account on prod-us-east with model vicuna-13b-v1.3 and conversation-style payloads (short prompts, average 60 tokens).
2) Send steady low QPS (1-3 rps) traffic from a few persistent connections to mimic customer pattern (many long-lived streams).
3) Observe p95/p99 latency over 1-2 hours; note intermittent spikes and occasional 504s correlated to batcher flush periods.
4) Collect trace ids from affected requests and compare batcher flush timestamps and KV-prefetch logs.
Sample trace snippets: trace=tr-0a1b2c3d flush_delay_ms=480 linger_timer_ms=1200 kv_prefetch_start=11:23:45.112 kv_prefetch_done=11:23:45.933 worker_wait=820ms -> 504. Error samples attached in S3: s3://redwood-support/sup-23501/traces/ (internal). Also see router logs showing request routed to fallback model variant at 11:23:46.33.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - BrightMetrics (Customer): Sent timeline of their demo runs; observed timeouts clustered around 11:20-11:40 UTC. Mentioned they did not change client behaviour.
2026-03-12 - Eng (Runtime): Reproduced locally by toggling batcher idlemode and enabling artificial 200-400ms prefetch delay. Observed p99 spikes and 504s. Created PR with conservative change to idle-merge backoff. Marked as candidate hotfix.
Hypothesis: The continuous-batcher's idle-merge heuristic increases coalescing linger in low-QPS persistent connections. Combined with eager KV-prefetch, this can create head-of-line waiting where the batch waits for prefetch completion on one request before flushing others.
Evidence: Trace tr-0a1b2c3d shows linger_timer jumped from nominal 50ms to 1200ms during observed spike; corresponding kv_prefetch took ~820ms when worker experienced brief GC pause. Batcher metrics show coincident increase in queued_requests and a dramatic drop in flush_rate for 10s windows.
Repro: Local reproduction achieved by simulating 2 persistent connections with 1rps each and injecting 200-500ms delay in KV-prefetch path. Without idle-merge disabled, p99 replicates. With idle-merge disabled or prefetch made non-blocking, latency stabilizes.
Related artifacts: Log slices in s3 and Grafana dashboard panels (batcher/linger, kv-prefetch latency, worker-gc). Slack thread: #support thread ts 16432. Related internal ticket INT-412 scheduled to track runtime refactor.
Risk assessment: Hotfix (disable idle-merge) reduces batching efficiency and may slightly increase token-level cost but has low roll risk. Permanent fix requires kernel-level change to make KV-prefetch non-blocking / speculative or to ensure batch flush doesn't wait on single-request prefetch.
Next steps: 1) Roll targeted disable across customer's pod group (done). 2) Prepare runtime patch to backoff idle-merge when prefetch is outstanding (PR opened). 3) Add unit/regression tests and synthetic workload in perf lab. 4) Postmortem and follow-up INT ticket to track feature work.
Mitigation applied: idle-merge heuristic disabled for BrightMetrics pod group on 2026-03-13 14:12 UTC. Observed p99 drop from ~2.8s -> 0.45s and 504 count reduced to 0. Customer confirmed immediate improvement. Permanent fix: runtime PR created to make KV-prefetch non-blocking and to add a conservative cap to idle-merge (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8341). Rollout plan: staged deploy to dedicated clusters with monitoring alarms enabled; target complete by 2026-03-20. Follow-up: INT-412 assigned for refactor and perf validation.
2026-03-13 - Eng: PR 8341 includes unit tests and a synthetic workload reproducer. Perf impact estimated +1.8% unit token cost in worst case for low-QPS patterns; plan to optimize further.
2026-03-14 - Customer success: Scheduled check-in with BrightMetrics for 2026-03-18 to validate longer-term behaviour and cost implications.
Follow-up action: Create KB article describing workaround (disable idle-merge) and guidance for customers with many long-lived low-QPS connections.
payload.summary: Intermittent p95/p99 tail spikes and 504s traced to idle-merge + KV-prefetch interaction in continuous batcher

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightTranslate reports intermittent latency spikes (auth handshake + TLS) and unexpected cross-region egress when their web app refreshes long-lived tokens. Impact: sporadic P95/P99 latency increases for request batches that follow SDK token refresh events, only for tenants using region pinning.

Impact:
- Increased tail latency (~400-800ms extra on top of baseline p95) observed for ~0.8% of requests tied to token refresh windows.
- Affected customer SLAs for dedicated plan (BrightTranslate).

Environment:
- prod-us-east edge; customer tenant is pinned to eu-west for data residency but originates client requests from us-east.
- Client using Browser JS SDK v1.4.3 with automatic token refresh enabled.

Observed behavior:
- When SDK performs refresh (silent refresh flow that exchanges short-lived refresh token), subsequent calls within 10–30s intermittently show X-Redwood-Residency header absent or changed, leading to control-plane routing to nearest-edge (us-east) rather than pinned eu-west edge. This triggers TLS rehandshake and auth token exchange, adding latency.

Expected behavior:
- Token refresh should preserve residency stamp/pin on subsequent requests or control plane should ensure residency affinity for the token namespace until TTL expiry. No transient cross-region egress should occur during refresh.
1) Configure tenant with strict residency pin to eu-west via Console (tenant: brighttranslate-202).
2) Run Browser SDK v1.4.3 in us-east network, enable automatic token refresh with refresh interval ~55 minutes (short-lived tokens).
3) Force token refresh by invalidating token on auth server and observe next requests from same tab within 0-60s window.
4) Observe headers and egress path in request traces (trace ids attached in logs).
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z TRACE id=8a7f-... path=/v1/chat model=redwood-chat-1 X-Redwood-Residency=eu-west -> routed to eu-edge-12
2026-03-10T09:12:05Z INFO sdk: refreshing token (client-js v1.4.3)
2026-03-10T09:12:06Z TRACE id=8a7f-... path=/v1/chat model=redwood-chat-1 X-Redwood-Residency= (missing) -> routed to us-edge-3 (egress hop + TLS)
2026-03-10T09:12:06Z WARN auth: auth-exchange latency=210ms status=200
2026-03-10T09:12:07Z PERF id=8a7f p95_latency=620ms (baseline p95=130ms)
Initial hypothesis: SDK refresh flow opens a parallel connection to auth endpoint that omits or rewrites residency headers which control-plane uses for egress selection.
SRE verified traces from edge (us-east) and saw token namespace mapping flip for the short-lived token immediately after refresh; control-plane routing decision logs show 'residency-stamp' absent causing fallback to nearest-edge policy.
We observed that the Browser SDK preconnect behavior (preflight) occasionally rebinds to a different CDN edge and does not attach X-Redwood-Residency on the new socket, allowing edge-proxy to treat the request as non-pinned.
Control-plane currently treats requests without residency stamp as eligible for nearest-edge routing; there is a small propagation window (~15s) where newly minted tokens are not fully associated with tenant-residency in the token namespace cache.
Reproduced in staging with synthetic client script that calls refresh, then fires 25 parallel requests; ~12% of trials show at least one request routed to nearest edge during the 0-25s window after refresh.
Tentative root causes: (1) SDK refresh path does not consistently copy residency context header to subsequent requests, (2) control-plane token->residency cache update is eventually consistent and has a short window where residency-affinity lookup returns empty, (3) CDN/edge preconnect behavior can create new connections that lose runtime-added headers.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Aisha): Thanks for opening this — we're actively investigating. Can you confirm SDK version and whether you use service-worker prefetching?
2026-03-10 11:40 - Customer (BrightTranslate, Elena): Using Browser SDK v1.4.3 with service-worker enabled; we see latency spikes after users stay on page for >50min (token TTL).
2026-03-11 09:20 - SRE (Marco): We've reproduced in staging and confirmed missing residency header during refresh. Control-plane team looped in (cc @routing-team).
2026-03-12 14:00 - Support (Aisha): Temporary mitigation uploaded: disable SDK preconnect in config (sdkConfig.preconnect=false) and enable header-preserve shim on client side. Suggested workaround instructions attached.
Workaround provided to customer: disable SDK preconnect and add a client-side shim that reattaches X-Redwood-Residency after refresh. Engineering action items: 1) patch SDK v1.4.4 to preserve residency header and avoid connection reuse that drops runtime headers; 2) control-plane change to treat token namespace updates as atomic for residency-affinity lookups (reduce window to <=2s); 3) gateway edge-proxy change to accept residency stamp from token-claim when present. Planned rollout: SDK patch + gateway fix in canary 2026-03-18, global rollout 2026-03-24. Follow-ups: create small integration test exercising token refresh + residency affinity (confluence task created).
ENG-1267: SDK: ensure residency header carried across token refresh paths (assigned to mobile/web-sdk).
ENG-1299: Control-plane: make token->residency cache write atomic and instrument propagation latency (assigned to routing-team).
OPS-402: Edge-proxy: allow residency stamp derived from token claims when explicit header missing (assigned to gateway).
DOCS-88: Update SDK release notes and troubleshooting guide for residency refresh behavior.
payload.summary: Client SDK token refresh causes residency header flip and transient cross-region egress + auth latency

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reported repeated silent streaming sessions where the server stopped emitting chunks after initial token output. Clients retried the request and platform returned duplicate completions for the same prompt, causing a billing spike and customer-visible duplicate messages.
Impact: Intermittent loss of streaming payloads for BlueHarbor's high-throughput telematics pipeline, duplicate completions seen in ~22% of affected sessions, billing surge estimated +14% for the customer during the incident window. Several downstream systems de-duplicated incorrectly, resulting in operational confusion.
Environment: Production (us-east), customer on enterprise plan with pin to redwood/gpt-3.8x-large, traffic via dedicated API key and routed through streaming-proxy pools with autoscaling enabled.
Timeline (high level): 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC - First customer alert to Support; 11:12 UTC - Triage and page to SRE; 11:20 UTC - Initial mitigation: temporarily disabled streaming proxy keepalive optimization; 11:45 UTC - Traffic routed to fallback pool (non-optimized kernel); 13:10 UTC - Duplicate completions observed to drop to <1%; 14:00 UTC - Customer confirmed service stability; 15:30 UTC - Incident declared resolved.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Create long-running streaming session with prefix size >2k tokens and KV cache reuse; 2) Simulate client network hiccup (socket close/reopen) after initial chunk; 3) Observe server behavior: either silence until client retries, or immediate replay of completion token stream leading to duplicate outputs; 4) Reproduce reliably when streaming-proxy had keepalive optimization enabled and serving-runtime kernel A selected.
Investigation notes: Early logs pointed to stream session state marked CLOSED on proxy but serving runtime still had active generation job; subsequent retry requests were not matched against previous job IDs due to an edge-case in session reconciliation. Trace IDs: trace-uh12-03, trace-uh12-04. Packet capture from proxy showed TCP close followed by SYN new session within 250ms. Kernel A (attention-optimized) was selected for low-latency customers; observed race in KV cache handoff under socket reconnect. Billing showed duplicate invoiceable completion events because generator job emitted finalization event twice when session reconciliation returned mismatched session token.
Root cause: A race condition in streaming-proxy session reconciliation plus an optimistic finalization path in serving-runtime kernel A. When the proxy fast-reclaimed session state on socket close while the generator was still finishing, a subsequent retry created a new session that triggered the generator to emit completion events again. The billing system counted both finalization events as independent completed responses.
Resolution and roll-forward: 1) Emergency mitigation: disabled keepalive-based fast-reclaim in streaming-proxy and added 500ms grace period for session reclaim (rolled at 11:20 UTC). 2) Rolled traffic to fallback kernel B that uses conservative finalization (11:45 UTC). 3) Hotfix PR merged to ensure generator finalization is idempotent (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1298) and to include session reconciliation token validation. 4) Billing adjuster script run to dedupe duplicate completion events for BlueHarbor and any other affected keys and credit invoices (completed 2026-03-12).
Post-incident actions: - Engineering will land additional unit tests around session reconnection and finalization idempotency (owner: Priya Nair). - Add a monitoring alert for anomalous completion duplication rate >0.5% per API key (owner: SRE). - Update runbook to include immediate rollback knob for streaming-proxy keepalive optimizations. - Conduct a targeted audit of other optimizer kernels for similar finalization behavior (owner: Runtime team).
Customer communications: Support sent initial status updates at 11:18/12:05/13:00 UTC. Customer requested detailed RCA and billing correction; follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-14 16:00 UTC. Billing credit issued and reflected in customer's portal on 2026-03-12.
Notes: No PII was involved. No evidence of malicious intent or targeted attack. Related internal ticket INT-412 tracking longer-term kernel rework.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:28 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer updated: they are seeing improved behavior but would like formal RCA and invoice correction. Confirmed they will wait for post-incident report.
2026-03-12 09:40 - Finance (Liam O'Connor): Billing dedupe script executed for affected invoice range. Credit issued for estimated duplicate completions; customer notified and credit applied.
2026-03-13 09:00 - Action items: Priya to add unit tests; SRE to add alert; Support to deliver final RCA to BlueHarbor and record CSM ticket for check-in post-credit.
Mitigation and hotfix implemented. Billing credits issued and customer confirmed service stability. Long-term kernel rework tracked in INT-412.

Add completion-duplication alert and dashboard - owner: SRE - due 2026-03-21
Update streaming runbook with rollback knob - owner: Support Ops - due 2026-03-18

payload.description:
Issue summary:
FinEdge reported intermittent spikes in end-to-end latency for long-poll streaming sessions from their EU customers. Client-side timestamps and server traces show some streaming connections are routed to us-east-1 (US) despite the token and SDK residency header indicating eu-west-1.

Impact:
- A subset (~4-7%) of streaming sessions initiated from EU produce p95/p99 latency spikes (handshake + initial token fetch) from ~80ms to ~850ms, and some sessions experience dropped streaming frames.
- Affects FinEdge production traffic (enterprise private tenancy) and increases cost and SLA risk.

Environment:
- Customer private deployment using Redwood Private with control-plane in eu-west-1 and edge proxies in front of regional serving clusters.
- Mobile SDK v1.4.1 (iOS/Android) with streaming enabled.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure mobile client with a residency-scoped API token (residency: eu-west-1) and enable streaming long-poll in SDK.
2) From an EU client network, start 1k short streaming sessions over 10 minutes.
3) Observe connection establishment traces in edge-proxy logs and control-plane routing decisions.

Observed behavior:
- Most sessions route correctly to eu-west-1, but ~4-7% route to us-east-1.
- When routed to us-east-1 we see TLS ALPN negotiation falling back and an extra SNI lookup, causing handshake delays and occasional 502s from the CDN.
- SDK telemetry shows a header value named X-Residency-Stamp sometimes serialized as an empty string or URL-encoded with a trailing space when the app prefetches endpoints.

Expected behavior:
- All requests with residency tokens and headers for eu-west-1 should be routed to eu-west-1.

Relevant logs/snippets:
- Edge-proxy (eu-west-1) trace: "route_decision: fallback -> us-east-1 (control-plane: stamp-empty)"
- SDK telemetry example: "X-Residency-Stamp: \"eu-west-1\"" and "X-Residency-Stamp: \"\"" (from same app build).

Customer-provided artifacts:
- Packet captures, SDK telemetry bundle, and sample timestamps attached to the ticket (uploaded to secure bucket).
Initial hypothesis: mobile SDK prefetch / connection warm-up occasionally strips or corrupts the residency header leading to control-plane treating the request as unpinned and applying fallback routing.

What we checked:
- Control-plane routing logs show requests with empty residency stamp are routed to nearest capacity pool (us-east in some tests due to edge-proxy topology).
- Edge-proxy config had a rate-limited path for warm-up connections which bypassed strict-residency enforcement for healthcheck-like sessions.
- Reproduced locally by running mobile SDK instrumentation with background prefetch enabled: when the prefetch thread raced with token refresh, header string builder produced a trailing space that URL encoding removed, resulting in empty header at proxy.
- CDN (third-party) will select a different edge node based on SNI and ALPN; extra handshake path shows ALPN negotiation to legacy profile when header missing, adding ~600ms.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Updated control-plane to treat empty X-Residency-Stamp as "treat-as-pinned" for the affected tenant for 48 hours (hotfix toggle).
- Instructed FinEdge to disable SDK prefetch in their next client hotfix as a short-term workaround.

Next steps and open items:
- Patch mobile SDK (PR referenced) to sanitize header construction and make residency header atomic with token refresh. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2184)
- Deploy edge-proxy config change to enforce strict residency for long-poll/streaming handshake paths globally after validation.
- Add unit and fuzz tests in SDK to catch trailing-space/encoding issues.
- Add telemetry in control-plane to count empty-residency-stamp events per tenant and alert at 0.5% threshold.
- Follow-up postmortem and customer communication draft.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Alejandro Ruiz): Started control-plane trace for FinEdge token IDs. Observed ~5% of requests with empty residency stamp. Investigating SDK behavior next.
2026-03-10 11:40 - Mobile SDK (Nina Patel): Reproduced header serialization race in local instrumentation when prefetch and token refresh run concurrently. Preparing PR for fix and tests. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2184
2026-03-11 02:20 - Support (Maya Chen): Applied temporary toggle to treat empty residency stamp as pinned for FinEdge. Customer reported immediate reduction in p95/p99; monitoring ongoing.
2026-03-12 15:50 - Security (Rashid Khan): Confirmed no token leakage in traces; header trimming change is low risk but requires release notes.
Work in progress: temporary control-plane toggle applied for affected tenant; mobile SDK patch merged to main and scheduled for v1.4.2 release. Permanent resolution plan: rollout SDK v1.4.2 to customers, deploy edge-proxy strict-residency enforcement, and add monitoring/alerting for empty X-Residency-Stamp events. Postmortem and customer-facing root-cause explanation to be published after rollout.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports elevated tail latency and periodic gRPC streaming resets on their private deployment. Behavior coincides with branch office traffic bursts.

Impact: Intermittent 5-10% of streaming requests incur 1-2s additional latency or experience a short gRPC reconnect; KV cache entries are evicted, causing regeneration of large prefix caches and increased token cost. Affects real-time scoring pipelines and causes visible degradation for end-users.

Environment: Private deployment (control plane in us-east-1), VPC peering to customer branch office via Transit Gateway; branch uses vendor-managed edge router (BR-Edge-01) with IPv4-only WAN to MPLS overlay. Redwood-serving nodes in private VPC, kernel 5.10, runtime v2.18.2.

Observed start time: 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC. Pattern: spikes correlated with branch office backup windows (large UDP/ICMP bursts).

Steps to reproduce: 1) From branch network generate ICMP timestamp request bursts (observed in customer's packet captures). 2) Concurrently run streaming chat sessions against pinned model rw-instruct-7b. 3) Observe intermittent TLS renegotiation and gRPC keepalive drops from serving nodes in metrics and increased cache-miss rate.

Expected: No influence of ICMP control-plane traffic on application-layer TLS/gRPC sessions.

Actual: Periodic short-lived gRPC resets and KV-cache eviction on serving nodes leading to tail latency spikes and higher token re-generation.

Notes: Customer has already validated no CPU/memory pressure on nodes and no application-level errors. Issue only reproducible when branch-originated ICMP timestamp traffic is present.
Selected excerpts from customer pcap and server logs:
- br-edge-01.pcap: repeated ICMP type 13 (timestamp request) bursts from branch subnet -> internet egress IP at 10:21:03Z.
- serving-node-12 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log: 2026-03-09T21:00:04Z grpc: keepalive timeout, closing stream id=0x1f4c. kvcache: prefix eviction policy triggered for shard s-7b-03 (cache_size dropped from 1.9GB to 128MB).
- control-plane auth logs: multiple short TLS session resumption failures from same client source IP range around same timestamps.
- tcpdump on customer NAT: see TTL and ICMP timestamp replies with altered time fields and unexpected ICMP responses during bursts.

Attached: customer_pcap_excerpt_20260309.pcap (customer-provided), runtime_tail_20260309.log
Initial hypothesis: branch router is performing ICMP timestamp rewrite/normalization that interacts with middlebox timing heuristics in the customer's MPLS provider, triggering out-of-order packets and occasional RSTs on TLS flows. Alternative hypothesis: underlying NAT pool or conntrack entries are being stressed by the burst and causing ephemeral port reassignments that invalidate long-lived keepalive flows.

What we checked: 1) Verified serving-node kernel conntrack counts - no global exhaustion but short-lived spikes in TIME_WAIT counts aligned with incident. 2) Packet captures from serving nodes show occasional ACK reordering and duplicated ACKs. 3) TLS metrics show a pattern of short-lived session resumption failures (not full handshake failures). 4) KV-cache eviction correlates to detected stream reconnects where prefix state was not reused.

Intermediate conclusion: Evidence supports a network-induced reordering and short-lived session misbind rather than application bug. The ICMP timestamp bursts are likely symptomatic of branch backup and coincide with observed behavior.

Workaround attempted by customer: - Temporarily rate-limiting ICMP at branch egress removed the symptom. - Increasing keepalive frequency to 30s reduced impact but increased overhead.

Next steps: 1) Collect deeper synchronized pcaps from branch egress and a serving node across one reproducible window. 2) Engage customer networking team to inspect BR-Edge-01 for ICMP normalization feature or timestamp rewriting. 3) Try deploying conntrack tweaks (conntrack tcp-timeout adjustments) on customer NAT as a controlled mitigation. 4) Add additional telemetry on serving nodes to capture per-connection packet reordering counters.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:05 - Customer (NimbusOps Network Ops): Confirmed BR-Edge-01 is a vendor appliance running default ICMP handling with timestamp reply normalization enabled. They will try toggling timestamp normalization in a maintenance window. They also provided a bigger pcap covering backup window.
Mitigation path identified: disabling ICMP timestamp normalization on customer branch router removed the symptom during test window. Short-term recommended mitigations: rate-limit ICMP/time-critical control-plane bursts at branch egress and increase keepalive probing interval to 30s if needed. Long-term: customer to apply router firmware/config to stop timestamp rewrite or move backup traffic to off-peak windows; SRE to add per-connection reordering telemetry and a guard rule to flag correlated ICMP bursts that may impact streaming. Follow-up: monitor for 7 days post-change; if regressions persist, open a detailed packet-level RCA with customer's network vendor.
payload.summary: ICMP timestamp rewrite by branch router causing intermittent gRPC keepalive failures and KV-cache evictions on private deploy
