payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after initiating a canary rollback for route `finatlas-payments/checkout`, their tenants remained pinned to the legacy variant instead of migrating to the target promoted model. The route had been mirrored to a prewarm pool and a staged rollback was triggered when health probes saw degraded latency on the new variant.

Impact:
- Several high-volume tenants at FinAtlas remained served by the older 13b model for ~42 minutes after rollback was started.
- Observed increase in per-token cost and inconsistent outputs vs expected promoted model.
- Customer reported degraded user experience on payment routing and raised a support escalation.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool) in us-east.
- Canary policy: 10% -> 0% rollback initiated after probe spike.
- Prewarm mirror enabled for the canary slice.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Create staged canary promotion for `redwood/open-rlhf-v2-13b-32bit` on route `finatlas-payments/checkout` with prewarm mirror enabled.
2. Allow traffic to reach 10% for 12 minutes, then trigger health-driven rollback to legacy `redwood/open-rlhf-v2-13b-quantized`.
3. Observe routing state in console and confirm tenant `finatlas-prod-03` continues to receive legacy responses despite control-plane showing commit to promoted model.

Observed behavior:
- Control plane commit shows rollback succeeded and canary weight set to 0% at 2024-11-15T14:02:12Z.
- Edge routing logs show tenant session lease still targets legacy variant; requests contain header X-Session-Lease: shadow-lease-0x9f3.
- Session affinity cache on edge still maps tenant cookie -> legacy model for ~42 minutes after rollback.

Expected behavior:
- After a successful rollback commit, tenant traffic should be routed according to the new snapshot; sticky sessions should be reconciled and leases that were created for mirrored prewarm sessions should be cleared or honored by the new snapshot.

Logs / evidence provided:
- Customer traces: https://traces.redwood.ai/finatlas/trace/0a1b2c3d
- Edge logs excerpt (sanitized): https://logs.redwood.ai/edge/finatlas/2024-11-15/edge-tail.log
- Console snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/snapshots/finatlas/2024-11-15T14:03:00Z

Additional notes:
2024-11-15 17:01 - SRE Team (thread #support): Initial hypothesis: prewarm mirror creates a shadow lease entry that is marked as transient in the prewarm cohort, but our rollback snapshot merge logic currently ignores transient leases, leaving the edge cache pointing at an old variant.
Link to slack: https://slack.redwood.ai/support/pinned-lease-investigation
Hypotheses considered:
1) Prewarm mirror creates shadow leases in orchestrator metadata; rollback snapshot merge ignores those transient leases and does not produce explicit delete operations, leaving edge caches with stale mapping.
2) Edge cookie namespace rewrite during prewarm flow set a cookie path that extended TTL beyond expected, preventing automatic eviction.
3) Orchestrator-to-edge propagation lag combined with queueing at the route-coalescer allowed legacy mapping to persist.
What we observed:
- Audit trail shows lease objects with 'type: shadow' persisted through snapshot replace without tombstone records.
- Edge logs show repeatedly honored X-Session-Lease header until explicit route flush.
- TTLs on the cookie were extended by the prewarm mirror flow due to an interaction with the cookie domain normalization in edge-proxy v2.4.2.
Telemetry/links:
- Orchestrator audit: https://audit.redwood.ai/2024-11-15/snapshots
- Edge cache metrics dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/edge-cache/edge-ttl-breakdown
Short-term mitigation attempted:
- Forced route flush + session cookie invalidation for the affected tenant (applied by Product Ops).
- Suggested customer-side short-term workaround: rotate tenant cookie namespace to break affinity if immediate flush not possible.
Workaround applied: Product Ops performed immediate route flush and invalidated edge session cookies for affected tenants, which restored correct routing within 6 minutes for those tenants.
Permanent fix: Merged PR #2987 to orchestrator to record tombstones for shadow-session leases and to emit explicit lease-removal ops during snapshot replace. Additionally updating edge-proxy logic to respect 'shadow' lease TTL and to fallback when snapshot indicates removal.
Rollout plan: PR merged to main on 2024-11-18. Staged deploy to staging 2024-11-19, canary deploy to prod-us-east 2024-11-21 with monitoring playbook engaged.
Follow-ups:
- Add a unit test for snapshot replace behavior and lease tombstone emission.
- Update Canary Runbook to include a step to clear shadow leases on rollback when prewarm mirror is enabled.
- Notify affected customers and include mitigation recap in post-incident note.
Related artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2987
- Runbook update draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SUPPORT/Canary+Rollback+Runbook#updates
payload.summary: Orchestrator shadow-session lease blocks tenant migration to promoted model during canary rollback, leaving pinned legacy variant

payload.description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:10 UTC, Acme Payments reported intermittent large increases in TTFB (time-to-first-byte) for streaming completions >60s. The pattern is correlated with clients that upload request bodies slowly (chunked transfer) while also sending periodic trace/authorization header updates. Impact: Customer-facing inference calls return with long stalls before streaming begins; some requests trigger ALB/edge connection resets and 504s. Environment: prod-us-east-1, traffic through our public API Gateway -> edge proxy layer -> internal ALB -> serving runtime. Observed behavior: When the client uploads body slowly (multi-second pauses between chunks) and repeatedly sends header updates, the edge proxy's HPACK table grows and proxy buffering increases, triggering idle-send-timeouts or partial flush behavior. Expected behavior: Streaming should begin when the server has the initial request payload and upstream should not stall due to header accumulation or slow chunked uploads. Additional notes: This looks related to previous header-growth/idle-timeout tickets but differs because root trigger is slow-client upload combined with periodic header rotation (trace IDs/authorization refresh) that causes HPACK and proxy state churn.
1) Use a client that sends a chunked POST to /v1/chat/stream with a ~1.5MB prompt encoded in many small chunks (200-500B) with 200-500ms pauses between chunks.
2) Configure the client to rotate a custom 'x-trace' header every 5s while upload is in progress to simulate streaming telemetry/refreshing tokens.
3) Observe the edge proxy connection and ALB during the upload and the downstream serving runtime's TTFB for the completion stream.
4) Compare with a single non-chunked upload of the same payload (should start streaming immediately).
2026-03-10T08:12:17Z EDGE-PROXY conn=ip-10-0-1-23:52312 slow-read: paused 450ms, hpack_size=49, headers-buffered=12
2026-03-10T08:12:18Z ALB upstream reset: idle-send-timeout after 30s (client paused) request_id=abc123
2026-03-10T08:12:20Z SERVING runtime: request queued for model=llama-2-13b kv_warm=false latency_waiting_for_client_body=2100ms
2026-03-10T08:12:45Z EDGE-PROXY hpack-evict triggered: table_size_before=63 table_size_after=10 trace_id=trace-08c

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 Support (to customer): Recommended temporary workaround: disable header rotation during upload, or send the prompt as a single upload (non-chunked) when possible. Customer testing confirmed immediate improvement.
Initial hypothesis: Large header growth causes the proxy to delay flushes and then ALB considers connection idle leading to resets.
Packet captures show client pauses of 200-500ms between content chunks; edge proxy continues to accept but defers streaming to upstream until client body completeness flag is set.
HPACK growth observed because header rotation sends slightly different header values frequently (x-trace, x-client-info), causing table churn and increased memory used by header tables.
ALB/edge idle-send-timeout is 30s; combined slow upload + multiple small back-and-forths increases end-to-end time before initial server response and can cross that timeout window for some requests.
Temporarily lowering HPACK table size and enabling earlier flush path in canary has reduced reproductions from 8/10 to 1/10 in initial runs.
Potential long-term fixes: 1) treat chunked request body reads as enough to begin upstream streaming once a minimal prefix is received; 2) add heuristics to ignore frequent small header changes during an active body upload; 3) tune ALB/edge idle timeouts per route.
Workaround applied and validated: canary proxies in us-east-1 rolled with reduced HPACK table size and lowered proxy buffering threshold (rolled 2026-03-12). Customer asked to avoid rotating auth/trace headers during uploads; they implemented this and reported improvement. Next steps: engineering to evaluate upstream change to start streaming on partial body availability (RFC), and product discussion on adjusting default idle-send-timeouts for streaming endpoints. Postmortem and permanent fix planned; keeping ticket open until runtime change or config-managed mitigation is deployed globally.
1) Engineering to draft RFC for partial-body streaming behavior (owner: Mara Lee) - target 2026-03-19
2) Edge team to run extended canary for 48h and collect TTFB metrics across clusters (owner: Diego Martinez) - target 2026-03-14
3) Customer success to coordinate with Acme Payments on deployment windows for global rollout (owner: Elena Kim) - target 2026-03-16
payload.summary: Edge proxy connection stall from slow chunked uploads and header growth causing delayed TTFB for long completions

payload.description:
Issue summary
Banyan Search reports that their configured fallback model is not being used during overload events. Instead, requests fail with 503 and Redwood overload error codes.

Customer expectation
When primary model (rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct) is overloaded, Redwood should route to configured fallback (rw-llama-3.1-8b-instruct) per their tenant policy.

Impact
- Customer sees elevated failed requests during traffic spikes rather than degraded (lower quality) responses.
- Affects production search assistant experience and increases client retry pressure.

Environment
- Hosted API
- Region: us-east
- Route: /v1/chat/completions
- Streaming: mostly enabled

Customer configuration (as described by customer)
- Primary: rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Fallback: rw-llama-3.1-8b-instruct
- Trigger condition: overload (customer referenced 'circuit breaker open')

What the customer is seeing (excerpt)
- HTTP 503
- Error payload (representative):
  code: OVERLOADED
  message: "Service temporarily overloaded. Please retry."
  correlation_id: rwcorr_01JEMNQZJ5J9P2G6E3R9K8V6M2
  retry_after: (present for some responses; missing for some per SUP-2860)

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Identify Banyan tenant_id and active routing policy.
2) Induce overload condition (or replay from perf-canary) where gateway admission control sheds requests.
3) Confirm whether routing attempts fallback model when overload is detected.

Initial hypothesis
Fallback routing is only attempted when overload is detected at routing/runtime stages. When overload occurs at the gateway admission layer (breaker open / shed), the request is rejected before routing executes, so no fallback can occur. Additional suspicion: loop-prevention logic may be suppressing fallback when the request already contains an attempted-model chain header.

Requested outcome
- Confirm whether fallback is expected to work under gateway-level shedding.
- If not currently supported, provide clear customer guidance and (if safe) enable fallback-on-gateway-overload for this tenant as an exception/feature flag.
- Ensure Retry-After is consistently present on overload errors.

Additional notes:
(1) Most failures happen pre-routing (gateway admission sheds) => fallback not possible.
(2) In the subset that reaches routing, a header bookkeeping issue causes loop-prevention to incorrectly block fallback.
Proposed fix: clear attempted_models when the failure is classified as 'admission_shed' vs 'model_attempted'. We can hotfix routing to only append attempted_models after a backend attempt is made.
- Ship routing hotfix for attempted_models bookkeeping so loop-prevention doesn’t suppress valid fallback (owner: routing team).
- For Banyan: offer immediate mitigation via tenant policy update: prefer us-west secondary region for fallback (if acceptable) or temporarily raise dedicated priority class for fallback model pool during their peak window.
- Provide customer-facing clarification: fallback is best-effort; early admission shedding returns explicit OVERLOADED with Retry-After and correlation_id.
- Ensure Retry-After consistency is tracked via SUP-2860/PR-18472 rollout.
- Confirmed most errors were gateway admission shedding, which currently does not route to fallback.
- We fixed a bug that could suppress fallback when routing was reached.
- Recommended client respect Retry-After + exponential backoff with jitter.
- Offered optional tenant-scoped enablement for 'fallback on breaker open' once available; for now, we can explore a scheduled capacity adjustment / alternate region policy if they want.
Customer acknowledged and asked us to monitor next peak window.
Resolved with routing hotfix: loop-prevention/attempted_models bookkeeping bug prevented fallback from triggering in some overload scenarios. After deployment, fallback works when overload is detected at routing/runtime stages. Gateway admission shedding remains a terminal response by design (no fallback attempted) to prevent overload cascades; customer was informed and given mitigation guidance (Retry-After/backoff, optional policy/capacity adjustments).
payload.summary: Fallback model not triggering during overload (customer receives 503 OVERLOADED instead of routed fallback)

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports persistent 429 (soft throttling) for a subset of requests immediately after upgrading their plan from dedicated -> enterprise. Console shows quota/top-up completed and tenant credits updated, but production traffic sees continued 429s for ~40 minutes. Impact: search indexing jobs and real-time chat flows intermittently fail for a subset (~12%) of workers, increasing latency and retries. Environment: prod us-east-1, mixed websocket and HTTP/2 clients.

Observed behavior:
- Customer upgraded plan at 2026-03-10T12:05:00Z via billing API.
- Console quota reflected new limits at 12:06:30Z.
- Error spike begins 12:08Z: rate-limit 429s with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset: ~12:08:30Z on some edge-nodes, while origin shows non-exhausted token counts.
- Spike subsided ~12:48Z after interventions (see resolution).

Why this is different from prior tickets: quota refresh is visible in control plane but refill/refill-window alignment across edge nodes appears delayed, causing a ‘soft’ 429 pattern (not global exhaustion). Customer-facing symptoms look like sustained throttling even though tenant credit balance is sufficient.
1) Have an active tenant on dedicated plan with sustained background workers (~300 concurrent requests).
2) Trigger a billing tier change (upgrade) using the billing API during a high-concurrency window, record the time.
3) Observe console shows quota/top-up success immediately.
4) Send steady traffic through a subset of edge nodes (simulate ~200 short-lived websocket sessions and 100 HTTP/2 multiplexed calls).
5) Watch for edge-level 429s while origin rate limiter reports available tokens.
[edge-12] 2026-03-10T12:08:12Z - 429 - X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000 - X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 - X-RateLimit-Reset: 12:08:30Z
[origin-scheduler] 2026-03-10T12:08:15Z - tenant_balance: 250000 tokens - refill_epoch: 2468 - last_refill_update: 2026-03-10T12:06:30Z
sample-client: curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
=> HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
   Retry-After: 8
   X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
   X-RateLimit-Sync-Id: edge-12/rsync-20260310-1206

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:30 - Customer (DocuSearch): Provided request ids: rq_az3, rq_b7f, rq_z12 and confirmed upgrade completed at 2026-03-10T12:05:00Z. Noted that only a subset of worker machines see the 429s.
2026-03-11 09:10 - Product (Ava Lin): Noted that this surfaced a race between billing commit and edge broadcast; adding a follow-up to ensure atomic broadcast semantics during top-up operations.
Edge nodes maintain a local token-window and rely on control-plane broadcasts to reset refill_epoch after billing changes. When the billing service wrote the new balance, the broadcast to edge sub-clusters sometimes lagged behind due to an intermittent NATS partition (~30s).
Edge logs showed consistent local refill_epoch values that did not match the origin's refill_epoch for ~20-40s, causing local remaining counters to report 0 despite global balance being updated.
Hypothesis confirmed by reproducer in staging: paused broadcast for 45s while applying top-up produced identical soft-429 pattern on subset of nodes.
Root cause: lack of idempotent, versioned broadcast with acknowledgement from edges. Control-plane assumed eventual consistency; under high-concurrency window this surface caused customer impact.
Risk: Transient but customer-visible throttling during billing operations or manual quota adjustments if the broadcast path experiences partitioning.
Applied emergency hotfix: force-sync endpoint added to edge agent that accepts a refill_epoch and force-recomputes local token windows; invoked for the single tenant on affected edge subset at 2026-03-10T12:48Z.
Rolled a small control-plane change (PR github.com/redwood/inference/PR/4318) to publish top-up as a versioned message and require an ACK from edge sub-clusters; retried broadcasts until ACKs received. Deployed to canary 2026-03-11 02:00Z and to prod 2026-03-11 03:30Z.
Validated success: no recurrence after broadcast path reinforced; edges now report matching refill_epoch within <5s in normal conditions.
1) For immediate relief, support can run edge force-sync for affected tenant (internal runbook: Confluence -> Rate Limiter -> Force Sync).
2) Recommend scheduling billing-tier changes during low-concurrency windows to minimize blast radius until broadcast ACKs roll out to all regions.
3) As a short-term client-side mitigation, throttle client concurrency (max parallel requests) during upgrade window or implement exponential backoff on 429s with jitter.
1) Engineering to add end-to-end monitoring for broadcast ACK latency and create alert when >5s for >1% of edge nodes (assigned: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-18).
2) Product to update billing upgrade playbook to recommend background refill sync and show a progress indicator in Console (assigned: Ava Lin, ETA: 2026-03-25).
3) Dev to harden message publish retries and mark top-up events as strongly-consistent for enterprise tier (PR merged: github.com/redwood/inference/PR/4318).
4) Support to prepare KB article for customers explaining safe upgrade patterns and how to request immediate edge-sync (target publish: 2026-03-20).
payload.summary: Unexpected soft throttling after billing-tier upgrade; quota shows refreshed but 429s persist

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (VectorQ AI, dedicated tenant) reports repeated midday throughput drops over the last 48h on their reserved pool in us-west-2. Symptoms: p99 latency spike to 3-6s for short-text streaming requests, sudden queue length increase on tenant route, and autoscaler failing to add capacity for ~6-8 minute windows. Heartbeat flapping from tenant slots and short-lived slot reservations observed in metrics.

Impact:
- Customer reports user-facing latency spikes and occasional request failures (502/524) during peaks.
- Affects ~30% of their production routes (small-streams, high qps) reducing effective throughput by ~40% during events.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) assigned to VectorQ AI
- Region: us-west-2 primary, fallback to us-east-1
- Models: redwood-open-7b (main), rw-compat-small-chat for low-cost routes
- Serving runtime v2.6.1, scheduler v1.9.3, autoscaler v3.0.0-beta

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant sends a burst of many short-stream requests from many client IPs (common for mobile fanout).
2) Scheduler creates many ephemeral reservations / heartbeats for small streams; heartbeats show jitter (intermittent delays of 200-800ms).
3) Slot allocation becomes fragmented: many slots marked live but underutilized and with short-lived KV caches.
4) Autoscaler moving-average window interprets noisy signal as sustained warm tail -> chooses conservative scale policy but cannot consolidate fragmented slots.
5) New incoming requests queue and are routed to fallback lower-capacity nodes or throttled, causing p99 latency and occasional 502/524s.

Observed logs/metrics (relevant extracts):
- Scheduler heartbeat latency: median 35ms, 95th 420ms, 99th 760ms during event windows.
- Slot churn metric (slots/sec for tenant): baseline 0.2, spike to 4.6 during bursts.
- Autoscaler decision log: at 2026-03-13T16:18Z: "no-scale (fragmented), score=0.42, trend=unstable" then at 16:26Z: "deferred-add -> no-op".
- GPU utilization: pool avg 62% but many GPUs show <10% per-slot utilization due to many small isolated batches.
- Queue length: route qlen from 0->85 in <90s.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated tenant traffic with customer-side client releases pushing many concurrent short streams (mobile fanout pattern).
- Detailed trace shows high rate of short-lived connections; prefetcher on client side sets concurrency=16 leading to many tiny streams.
- There is measurable scheduler heartbeat jitter between sidecar and scheduler during these windows; network path introduces 100-800ms variance for many ephemeral connections.
- Autoscaler currently uses a 5-minute moving average with conservative thresholds; fragmentation causes it to undercount effective headroom and delay provisioning.
- No evidence of underlying GPU hardware faults. NVLink/PCIe metrics normal outside short bursts.

Hypothesis:
Primary: Heartbeat jitter + high fanout of short streams produces slot fragmentation (many small reservations with cold KV caches). The autoscaler misclassifies the signal as non-actionable because the per-GPU aggregate utilization masks per-slot underutilization and fragmentation. Combined effect -> transient effective GPU shortage and queuing. Secondary: client prefetch/concurrency settings exacerbate the problem.

Mitigation / temporary workarounds applied:
- Support recommended customer reduce client prefetch concurrency from 16 -> 4 for short-stream routes. Customer applied change at 2026-03-13T18:10Z; immediate reduction in slot churn and queue growth observed.
- Applied temporary increase to autoscaler sensitivity for the tenant's pool (lowered add threshold) at 2026-03-13T18:35Z which allowed a one-time add of 2 GPUs and cleared queues.
- Enabled short-lived slot coalescing (experimental switch) for the tenant to aggregate small streams on fewer GPUs for 2 hours as a pilot.

Root cause candidate fixes (engineering):
- Scheduler: implement heartbeat coalescing and tolerance window to avoid marking many ephemeral slots live when bursts are short-lived.
- Autoscaler: add fragmentation-aware metric (slot_churn adjusted) instead of raw aggregate GPU utilization; use per-slot utilization percentiles when evaluating adds.
- Serving runtime: improve small-batch consolidation and KV cache warmup prioritization for tiny streams.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering owner (Ravi Shah) to open runtime/scheduler PRs to add heartbeat coalescing and fragmentation signals (ETA: 7 days).
- Product/SRE to create an autoscaler tweak experiment for dedicated pools to detect high churn patterns and scale faster (ETA: 3 days for experiment config).
- Customer success to coordinate with VectorQ to roll back concurrency settings in a controlled way and monitor for regressions.
- Follow-up runbook addition: detect high slot_churn + low per-slot-utilization -> run mitigation (coalesce, temporarily relax autoscale thresholds).

Resolution notes (temporary):
- Customer reverted client prefetch to 4 and enabled coalescing pilot; throughput stabilized and p99 dropped to acceptable range within 10-15 minutes.
- Engineering changes are required to prevent recurrence under similar fanout patterns.

References/log links:
- Scheduler heartbeat heatmap: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/heartbeats/tenant-553780
- Autoscaler decision trace: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/0b8f3c3a-autoscale-20260313
- Customer support slack: https://slack.redwood.ai/support/p12345

2026-03-13 17:02 - VectorQ (customer): We're seeing sudden latency spikes in production around 16:15-16:30 PST; events seem to resolve after several minutes. This is impacting our chat feature.
2026-03-13 17:18 - Support (Ava Martinez): Requested traces, route names, and confirmed pool id. Asked customer to reduce prefetch concurrency as a quick test.
2026-03-13 18:12 - VectorQ (customer): Reduced prefetch from 16->4 per recommendation. Noticed immediate improvement on next burst window.
2026-03-13 18:36 - SRE (Ravi Shah): Temporarily lowered autoscaler add threshold for tenant pool and enabled experimental coalescing switch. Queues cleared after 3 minutes.
2026-03-14 09:10 - Engineering (Ravi Shah): Initial profiling indicates per-slot util percentiles are the best signal for fragmentation; opened internal design doc and will propose API changes.
2026-03-14 12:05 - Support (Ava Martinez): Scheduled follow-up with customer for 2026-03-16 to validate longer-term stability and coordinate on SDK best-practice guidance.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer ingests large CSVs through an orchestrator service that rotates short-lived API tokens per worker. During token rotation windows (hundreds of tokens created in <2s), they observe a 10–30% wave of opaque 429s affecting portions of the batch run.

Impact:
- Several bulk ingest jobs fail mid-run with 429s and exponential backoff, increasing total completion time by ~3x.
- Console quota counters show tenant credits available; customer believes requests are being double-counted or misattributed.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool, prod-us-east, VectorMaps tenant id: VM-2384
- Ingest orchestrator version: 2026.03.01
- Workers rotate short-lived keys issued by their orchestrator (TTL 60s) at high fanout during CSV split stage.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Submit large CSV ingest via VectorMaps orchestrator (200 files split into 2k parallel workers).
2) Worker process requests a new short-lived token on start; rotation occurs across ~200 workers in a 1.5s window.
3) Workers immediately begin embedding requests (small batches ~4k tokens each) to embedding-multibatch-v1.
4) After ~30s, intermittent 429s appear for some workers; retry storms amplify failures.

Observed behavior:
- A subset of requests returns HTTP 429 with minimal headers (opaque), console shows tenant quota ~80% available at time of wave.
- Some requests include X-RateLimit-* headers with remaining=0 while console counters indicate otherwise.
- Error pattern correlates strongly with token-rotation windows.

Expected behavior:
- Rotating short-lived keys should not cause tenant-level quota exhaustion or opaque 429s when tenant quota is available.

Sample logs/headers captured from customer (redacted):
- Request timestamp: 2026-03-12T22:10:18.764Z
- Authorization: Bearer sk-temp-xxxxxxxx
- X-RateLimit-Limit: 600000
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
- X-RateLimit-Reset: 2026-03-12T22:11:00Z
- Response: 429 Too Many Requests
- Trace header: x-rw-trace: rw-trace-7b2a3

Additional notes:
- Customer can reproduce reliably by forcing workers to request tokens in a tight window.
- They believe an edge-proxy or ingress component is fragmenting the token accounting when many ephemeral tokens map to the same pooled IPs.
- Customer requests: 1) explanation of accounting path, 2) short-term mitigation to complete in-progress jobs, 3) long-term prevention guidance.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 02:18 - Customer (VectorMaps - infra@vectormaps.com): Provided sanitized request log bundle and their orchestrator start script. Confirmed they rotate ~180 tokens across 200 workers within 1.4s.
2026-03-14 09:30 - Support (Miguel Torres): Shared short-term mitigation steps with customer (see resolution_notes). Coordinating with infra to prototype per-token affinity and to adjust refill smoothing parameters for dedicated pools.
2026-03-14 11:05 - Customer (VectorMaps): Applied suggested temporary mitigation and saw immediate drop in 429 rate from ~18% to ~2% on next run. Requests follow-up on recommended config changes and whether dedicated pool can get per-ephemeral-key accounting.
2026-03-14 14:22 - Product (R. Patel): Logged follow-up internal feature request to evaluate per-ephemeral-key lease tracking for high-fanout ingestion patterns. Will treat as low-latency accounting opt-in for dedicated customers.
2026-03-14 15:10 - Support (Miguel Torres): Marking ticket In Progress while long-term design work is scheduled. Customer job remaining; agreed to keep ticket open for additional assistance.
Checked tenant quota metrics on console: no simultaneous tenant-level exhaustion at time of waves; tenant credits >70% throughout.
Edge-proxy traces show multiple ephemeral token handshakes collapsed onto a small NAT pool (10 IPs) causing per-connection refill to be applied unevenly.
Rate-limiter logs: per-token counters incremented, but smoothing/refill logic also applies a per-connection window to reduce burst impact; per-connection window reached zero during rotation fanout.
Hypothesis: per-connection smoothing + NAT reuse + short TTL on keys creates transient window misalignment leading to opaque 429s despite tenant credits. This is distinct from double-counting; it's temporary connection-level exhaustion.
Reproduced in lab by spinning 150 ephemeral tokens behind a single proxy IP with current smoothing params; observed similar 429 waves and sawtooth refill behavior.
Short-term mitigation applied (customer): stagger token rotation across worker group using jittered start (recommended jitter 50-500ms) and increase client-side backoff to mitigate retry storm.
Immediate config change suggested by SRE: increase per-connection refill granularity for the dedicated pool to reduce per-connection window depletion during high-fanout rotations.
Customer confirmation: after applying jittered rotation and tiered backoff, 429s dropped from ~18% to ~2% and job completion time recovered to expected range.
Long-term follow-ups: product to evaluate opt-in per-ephemeral-key accounting and per-pool NAT sizing guidance; infra to add NAT pool telemetry to console for dedicated customers so they can see IP reuse/fanout.
Action items:
- PROD-INFR-452: Add NAT pool reuse metric to dedicated pool dashboards (owner: A. Gomez, ETA: 2026-04-05)
- ENG-OPT-119: Evaluate per-ephemeral-key accounting path and cost/latency tradeoffs (owner: R. Patel, ETA: 2026-05-15)
- Support runbook update: add recommended jitter/backoff snippet for high-fanout ingest jobs (owner: Support Docs, ETA: 2026-03-20)
Ticket status: monitoring until next customer run; keep open for follow-ups and to validate infra dashboard changes.
payload.summary: Opaque 429 wave when rotating pool of short-lived client tokens during CSV ingest

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a planned canary promote (weight shift 20%->100%) for BrightLedger's dedicated deployment in eu-west, a subset (~1.4%) of in-flight sessions were observed to silently reroute to an older model variant. Impact: Affected requests returned lower-quality completions (reduced coherence) causing BrightLedger to report production regressions for end users. Environment: prod:eu-west, dedicated cluster rdw-ded-eu-07, canary promote initiated via Console rollout API.

Observed behavior: Around 2026-03-12T16:05:00Z — immediately after the final promote step — routing logs show a correlated spike in session-rebind events where session affinity tokens issued during the promote window were evaluated as expired by the edge-router. Those sessions were matched against fallback rules and sent to a compatible older variant (quantized v1) instead of the promoted primary. No 5xx errors were returned; traffic appeared healthy but outputs degraded for affected requests.

Why this ticket: Customer escalated at 16:45Z after customer QA detected regression in generated summaries. They requested incident triage, root cause, and mitigation/rollback if needed.

1) Have a long-lived session pool with timestamp-based affinity tokens (TTL ~300s). 2) Start traffic against blue variant (open-7b-quantized-v1). 3) Initiate canary promote to green (open-7b-v1) using Console rollout API (weight 20->100 over 3 minutes). 4) Observe edge-router logs and session-rebind telemetry during final weight ramp. 5) Check per-session model routing decisions and compare affinity token timestamps vs server-side clock.

Issue summary: Nimbus Labs reported intermittent 401 Unauthorized errors for scheduled batch jobs and short-lived admin API calls after we rolled their private deployment changes last week. Impact: A subset of service-to-service token exchanges fail validation causing retries and job backlogs for their nightly worker fleet. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) in us-west, private control plane. Authentication flow affected: SAML->OIDC bridge + internal service-account token-swap that issues access tokens with 'azp' (authorized party) set but 'aud' (audience) omitted or set to a short list; our authz layer validates 'aud' and rejects tokens where expected audience is missing.

High level: Customers see intermittent 401s with message 'token audience mismatch' when worker instances try to call model-serving endpoints. Errors started shortly after Nimbus applied an upstream identity provider change (IdP started returning azp only for certain service assertions).
1) Trigger the scheduled batch worker that performs service account token-swap via the customer's IdP through the bridge proxy
2) Observe token issued by token-swap endpoint (inspect id_token/access_token claims), note presence of 'azp' claim and either missing or unexpected 'aud' claim
3) Call the protected admin/model endpoint with the swapped token; endpoint returns 401 with 'aud mismatch' error in logs
4) Repeat during high concurrency window to reproduce intermittent failure (rate/parallelism appears to correlate).

2026-03-10T02:14:24Z authz: token validation failed: required_audience="redwood-inference-api" actual_audience=null (azp=idp-client-7) -> 401
2026-03-11T03:05:11Z serving-runtime: incoming request from svc_worker_42 rejected 401 token_aud_mismatch (x-request-id=abc-123-def)
2026-03-12T08:22:44Z identity-proxy: intermittent 502 from upstream idp during assertion fetch (retry 2)
Support triaged and confirmed 401 pattern with Nimbus engineering via Zoom session 2026-03-10.
Confirmed a correlation between high-concurrency token-swap activity and increased 401s (reproducible in customer's load test harness).
Captured example tokens (redacted) where 'azp' is present but 'aud' is either missing or set to an array with a single element that does not match our expected 'redwood-inference-api' audience.
Hypothesis 1: IdP/bridge started emitting tokens where 'aud' is omitted and relying on 'azp' for audience semantics; our authz validator is strict and only checks 'aud'.
Hypothesis 2: Under concurrency, token-swap service occasionally returns a legacy token format due to a race in token-builder code path (local IdP proxy cache stale).
Collected telemetry: authz rejects spike corresponds to periods where the idp-proxy returned tokens with atypical claim sets.
Edge case: Some long-lived admin API calls succeed because they use cached tokens with correct aud; short-lived swapped tokens fail.
Added temporary log hooks to identity-proxy and authz to log claim sets for failed validations (sanitized).

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 16:30 - Eng on-call (Ivan Petrov): Confirmed token-swap sometimes returns tokens from fallback code path without aud when upstream responded with 202+retry; submitted PR to identity-proxy to normalize aud claim. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/198
Identity-proxy token-swap edge case: under certain upstream responses the token builder emitted access tokens lacking the 'aud' claim, while downstream authz strictly validated 'aud' only. An IdP change increased frequency of that code path, making failures intermittent under load.
Temporary workaround applied by Nimbus Ops: include static 'aud' in IdP assertions. We deployed an identity-proxy hotfix in the private control plane that synthesizes the expected 'aud' when absent (maps from azp).
Hotfix deployed to customer's private control plane (identity-proxy v1.8.3-hotfix). The patch normalizes token outputs: if 'aud' is missing, set aud to configured service audience derived from azp mapping. Post-deploy monitoring for 24 hours shows error rates back to baseline. Customer confirmed scheduled workers resumed normally.
1) Merge PR #198 into main and add unit + integration tests for aud/azp normalization (INT-2054).
2) Update Runbook: 'Token Exchange - aud/azp validation' with mitigation steps and verification commands.
3) Add metric and alert: authz.token_aud_mismatch_rate per-customer and per-region to Console (owner: SRE).
4) Documentation: add guidance for private customers on IdP audience configuration and expected claim sets.
5) Schedule a 1:1 with Nimbus to review long-term plan for token semantics; offer optional managed mapping configuration in Private Console.
Customers using private deployments who perform token-swaps should ensure their IdP includes aud matching the expected service audience. We will relax authz validator to accept aud derived from azp only after careful testing and opt-in for strict customers.

comments: 2026-03-10T09:15:00Z Asha Raman: Customer reports sudden chunk 429s after enabling host rewrite. Confirmed customer is on Private deployment; escalated to SRE for rate-accounting check.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer StreamlineMaps on a Private deployment using an on-prem reverse proxy began receiving 429 throttles during a multipart file upload job that previously succeeded. The uploads are large (50–150MB per object) and the client uses parallel chunked PUTs with automatic retry. The customer reports the 429s started immediately after they enabled a proxy feature that rewrites the Host header to the internal service name for routing.

Impact:
- Production ingest pipeline experiencing intermittent failures for ~10% of objects during hourly backfills (affects downstream geodata freshness).
- Customer sees 429s with Retry-After headers; console shows available burst credits in the Private control plane.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) in us-west region.
- Ingress: on-prem HA reverse proxy (envoy v1.25) rewriting Host header to internal-service.local for route affinity.
- Backfill worker fleet: 20 concurrent workers per host, HTTP/2 connection reuse enabled.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Enable Host header rewrite on their ingress so requests present internal-service.local as Host to the control plane.
2) Start the multipart uploader with 20 parallel chunk uploads per file, 500ms backoff retries on 5xx/429.
3) Observe a subset of chunk requests receive 429 responses; console credits do not reflect immediate exhaustion.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include throttle headers X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Window: route:short-window.
- Control plane metrics show token accounting against a route ID that does not match the customer's intended public route but matches the internal-service.local route assigned by the proxy.
- Retried chunks amplify the apparent per-route consumption, causing other tenants (on same private control plane) to see transient increases in their route-level counts.

Expected behavior:
- Host header rewrite should not change the tenant/route accounting; rate-limiter should use authenticated API key+path fingerprinting rather than Host header alone.

Attachments / Logs:
- Customer provided upstream proxy config snippet (sanitized).
- Excerpt of request/response pair (headers only) showing rewritten Host and throttle headers (attached to ticket).
- Control plane metric snapshot (token accounting per route) at time of incident (attached).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:40 UTC - SRE (Liam O'Neal): Observed that route fingerprinting used by our rate-limiter includes Host header when request arrives via edge proxy. Running traffic replay locally against a staging rate-limiter to reproduce.
2026-03-11 07:22 UTC - Customer (StreamlineMaps - J. Park): Added that disabling host rewrite immediately stops 429s. We can toggle, but need a permanent fix because internal routing requires rewrite.
2026-03-11 15:05 UTC - SRE (Liam O'Neal): Applied temporary mitigation on customer's private control plane: added a request normalization rule that preserves original public host in the X-Forwarded-Host header and uses that for route-fingerprint. Early results: 2 hours of backfill with no 429s reported.
2026-03-12 10:03 UTC - Support (Asha Raman): Notified customer of mitigation and requested permission for a software patch rollout to change rate-limiter fingerprint priority to authenticated-key > path > X-Forwarded-Host > Host. Customer requested immediate patch rollout window 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.
2026-03-12 14:12 UTC - Engineering (Marta Singh): Reviewing patch; finding a potential edge-case around HTTP/2 stream coalescing when X-Forwarded-Host is missing. Adding unit test to ensure we fallback to API key when header absent.
Token accounting analysis: Several thousand chunk requests were attributed to route id 'internal-service.local' due to header rewrite. When requests reused persistent HTTP/2 streams, route attribution persisted across multiplexed streams and inflated the single-route counter.
Hypothesis: Rate-limiter currently builds route fingerprint from (Host, request-path, hashed-api-key) with Host taking precedence when present. Host rewrite changed which route was considered hot, causing misattribution.
Reproduction: Staging proxy replay with Host rewrite reproduced 429 pattern. Disabling Host rewrite or adding X-Forwarded-Host to preserved public host prevented misattribution.
Telemetry: No change in overall tenant quota usage shown in billing; discrepancy between per-route counters and tenant-level counters indicates counting at wrong aggregation key.
Risk assessment: High for private deployments with ingress rewrite features; moderate for hosted customers behind certain edge proxies that perform similar header rewrites.
Mitigation applied: temporary request normalization rule configured on the customer's private control plane to trust X-Forwarded-Host when present and to prefer API key for fingerprinting. Engineering patch to adjust fingerprint precedence created (PR: https://github.com/redwood/ingress-proxy/pull/3284). Planned rollout: patch to private control plane images and a soft rollout on 2026-03-13 during low-traffic window. Follow-up: add defensive unit/integration tests for HTTP/2 multiplexed stream attribution and a runbook entry under Support for customers who use host-header rewrites.
2026-03-13 - Deploy patch to private control plane for this customer in scheduled window; monitor per-route counters for 24 hours.
Add integration test to CI that simulates host header rewrite + HTTP/2 multiplexing to prevent regressions.
Update public support KB: guidance on configuring on-prem ingress when using host rewrite and recommended headers (X-Forwarded-Host) to preserve route accounting.
Consider a long-term enhancement: change our rate-limiter to derive route fingerprint primarily from authenticated API key and request path, ignoring Host except as a last-resort tie-breaker.
payload.summary: Proxy host-header rewrite causing route quota misattribution and unexpected 429s during multipart upload workflow

comments: 2026-03-12T16:03:00Z Maya Rodriguez: Customer reported reconnect spikes after weekend deployment. Provided initial tcpdump and streaming client logs. Marked as P1 due to production impact.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a private VPC deployment intermittently observe gRPC stream resets and frequent reconnects when sending long-lived streaming inference requests. Impact: streaming clients experience token duplication, reconnect churn, and increased tail latency, causing transient user-facing failures during payments reconciliation jobs.

Impact:
- Multiple customers reported reconnect storms during peak batch inference windows (FinNova observed ~8% request failures, clients retried and duplicated outputs).
- Tail latency increases from 120ms median to >1.5s p95 for streaming responses.

Environment:
- Deployment: Private (customer-managed VPC peering + egress through corporate firewall)
- Region: us-east-1 (customer-routed egress)
- Redwood runtime: serving-runtime v2026.02.10
- OBS: TLS stays up; application-level gRPC shows RST and transient EOFs.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer runs a long-lived streaming generation job (streaming chat with >1024 token context) against a pinned redwood-7b-v2 model on their private deployment.
2) Load generator runs 100 parallel streams per node for ~30 minutes.
3) Observe intermittent request resets and reconnects in client logs; server sees TCP-level retransmits and occasional out-of-order segments.

Observed behavior:
- gRPC status CANCELLED / UNAVAILABLE on clients with reconnects multiple times per minute.
- Kernel/tcpdump on serving node shows TCP timestamp fields stripped or zeroed on some packets once flow exits through corporate firewall.
- When timestamps are stripped, TCP duplicate-detection heuristics mis-evaluate sequence numbers under reordering, leading to spurious retransmits and head-of-line blocking.

Expected behavior:
- No mid-path modification of TCP options (timestamps) for established flows; stable long-lived gRPC streams with graceful keep-alives.

Logs/Traces:
- Attached extract (sanitized) from serving node tcpdump: repeated TCP options length mismatch and TSval=0 in packets after 2026-03-12T15:21:10Z.
- Stackdriver/Datadog spans: multiple grpc:stream closed events correlated with increased retransmit counters on node NIC.

Temporary workaround:
- Customer routed egress around corporate firewall for a subset of serving nodes (temporary egress NAT through a managed firewall) and saw immediate reduction in reconnects.
- Short-term mitigation: reduce concurrent streams per node and enable smaller keepalive intervals to force faster recovery while we investigate.

Next steps:
- Coordinate with customer networking to capture full pcap across egress path and corporate firewall appliance.
- Reproduce in controlled staging with a middlebox that strips TCP timestamps.
- Evaluate runtime-level mitigation (disabling reliance on RFC1323 TS for duplicate detection in our user-space TCP stack or tuning kernel parameters) and a longer-term recommendation for corporate firewall config (preserve TCP options).

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 18:20 - CS Engineer (Vikram S.): Confirmed symptoms align with packet option mutation. Asked customer for firewall model and egress path diagram.
2026-03-13 09:12 - Customer (FinNova netops): We see an inline 'optimization' feature on our NGFW that advertises performance improvements; logs show option rewriting during peak throughput.
2026-03-13 13:46 - Assignee (Ethan Park): Reproduced in lab by inserting a policy that strips TCP timestamps on our staging firewall; observed identical stream churn. Starting work on mitigation plan.
2026-03-14 08:05 - SRE (Nadia K.): Kernel tcp_retrans_out and tcp_reordering counters spike when timestamps zeroed. Suggest testing net.ipv4.tcp_smart_metrics tuning and disabling timestamp-based heuristics for affected nodes as experiment.
2026-03-14 12:30 - Customer (FinNova netops): We'll schedule a firewall rule change in a canary set tomorrow morning to preserve TCP options and confirm impact.
Lab reproduction: enforced TCP timestamp stripping on staging NGFW -> confirmed gRPC reconnects and p95 latency regression.
Kernel traces: tcp_input_timewait and tcp_fastretrans triggered when TSval==0 and segment reordering present.
Hypothesis: corporate firewall has an inline optimization that normalizes TCP options under high throughput leading to malformed or zeroed TS option values.
Risk assessment: high for long-lived streaming workloads; short RPCs less affected. Private deployments relying on customer-managed middleboxes are exposed.
Potential mitigations: (1) recommend firewall patch/config to preserve TCP options, (2) runtime: reduce dependence on TS-based heuristics and increase tolerance for reordering, (3) route critical egress via managed egress that preserves options.
Pending - customer will canary firewall config change to preserve TCP options. Engineering to validate post-change and evaluate kernel/runtime tuning as fallback. Follow-up: if customer cannot change appliance, propose managed egress or document runtime knob and risk.
payload.summary: TCP timestamp stripping by corporate firewall causes intermittent gRPC reconnects and degraded streaming in private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a canary rollout for redwood-open-7b-v2 for customer TradeFlow.ai, requests that should have been routed to the canary pinned variant were intermittently routed to the quantized fallback (redwood-open-7b-v2-quant). This resulted in higher end-to-end latency spikes (200-800ms additional per request) and in several cases token truncation / inconsistent streaming behavior for long prompts.

Impact:
- Affects ~12% of TradeFlow.ai traffic on dedicated pool in us-east during the canary window.
- Visible user-facing errors: incomplete responses and streaming disconnects for long requests.
- Business impact: degraded demo reliability for TradeFlow.ai (enterprise customer on dedicated).

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: df-dedicated-us-east-4
- Router version: router@2026.03.08
- Serving runtime: serving-runtime@v2.8.1
- Canary config: 5% traffic, model pinning rule active for model redwood-open-7b-v2

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Trigger a long streaming generation (~1,200 tokens) pinned to redwood-open-7b-v2 via API with canary header X-Redwood-Canary=yes
2. Observe response intermittently stalls or returns truncated content after ~512 tokens, then reconnects and resumes as a different model variant
3. Check runtime logs for serving instance selection and fallback routing decision

Observed behavior:
- Router decision logs show a mismatch: requests matching canary selector were evaluated as eligible for fallback path due to a stale capability check on node labels (capabilities: quantized=true).
- Serving instances that received traffic were running quantized variant which enforces a 512-token limit under current config, causing truncation.
- Traffic percentage to canary remains ~5% but effective canary correctness dropped to ~3% due to reroutes.

Expected behavior:
- Canary-pinned requests should always prefer the pinned variant when available; fallback to quantized variant should only occur on explicit health/capacity failure, not on label capability mismatch.

Logs / Observables (snippets):
- router decision: "request_id=af3b2e, route=canary, evaluated_labels=[quantized=true, gpu=rtx6000], chosen_node=node-17, fallback_trigger=label_mismatch"
- serving runtime: "model_loaded=redwood-open-7b-v2-quant, token_limit=512"
- console traces: spike in tail latency between 2026-03-12T13:10Z and 2026-03-12T13:50Z correlated to canary window

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support toggled canary to 2% and added a hard exclude for quantized-capable nodes in the canary routing policy for TradeFlow.ai (workaround id: wk-2026-03-12-01). This restored correct routing to pinned variant but reduced canary throughput.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Router label evaluation change (deployed 2026-03-08) introduced stricter capability checks that erroneously mark canary nodes as incompatible when quantized capability is present.
- Hypothesis 2: Model pinning precedence logic had a regression where fallback rules can override pinning during selection.
- Initial reproducer run on staging with identical router build reproduced the label_mismatch path.
- Related PRs identified that touched selection priority: github.com/redwood-inference/router/pulls/611

Next steps / Actions:
- (ENG) Create a minimal unit test for routing precedence and backport fix to 2026.03.08 branch. (Owner: @mchen)
- (SRE) Audit node labels in dedicated pools for stale capability flags; remove quantized=true where not applicable. (Owner: @a.park)

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 "waves" observed shortly after our dedicated GPU pool autoscaler added capacity (scale-up). Pattern: a few minutes after scale-up the customer sees repeated 429s across many short-lived webhook callbacks/orchestrated workers. 429s subside after ~7–12 minutes.

Impact:
- AtlasMaps (dedicated) experienced degraded ingestion throughput for mapping telemetry; spike affected ~20% of requests for a 10-minute window and caused backfills to queue.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (prod-us-west), autoscaled from 8->12 GPUs at 2026-03-10T14:22Z.
- Traffic: multiplexed signed-callbacks + ephemeral worker processes that create short-lived API keys.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Kick off orchestrated ingestion with 80 concurrent short-lived worker processes (each worker performs many small webhook callbacks via signed URL).
2) Trigger a manual pool scale-up (or wait for autoscaler).
3) Observe increased rate of 429s for the next ~5–15 minutes, then recovery.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses from rate-limiter service. Throttle headers inconsistent (X-RateLimit-Remaining shows small remaining count then jumps).
- Console shows tenant quota temporarily near 0 then replenishes.

Expected behavior:
- Scale-up should reduce contention and avoid tenant-level 429s for legitimate fanout workloads.

Attachments / Logs:
- Customer provided request id samples: req_az9f2, req_bv4k1, req_cx1m9 (timestamps 2026-03-10T14:25Z - 14:31Z).
- Grafana snapshot (customer): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/atlasmaps-scaleup-spike

Notes: This looks similar to tenant-token-bucket drift but happens aligned with worker handoff during autoscaler activity. Customer is requesting guidance and a mitigation while we investigate root cause.
SRE initial triage 2026-03-10: correlated time window with autoscaler event; autoscaler initiated host replacement on two nodes leading to short connection churn.
Hypothesis A: healthcheck/probe traffic or ephemeral worker registration counted against tenant burst budget causing transient depletion during handoff.
Hypothesis B: new hosts introduced slightly different rate-window offset, causing token refill epoch misalignment and sawtooth-like refill behavior for short-lived keys.
Ran quick checks: rate-limiter logs show simultaneous token debit events from multiple ephemeral keys at handoff time; many of these map to signed-callback origin IPs.
Related metric: tenant_token_window_drift_us spiked from ~30us baseline to 12ms during the event window.
Cross-reference: Slack thread #support-atlasmaps (https://slack.redwood.ai/#support/archives/C03XYZ) contains customer traces.
Support (Maya): Acknowledged and requested customer sample ids and exact scale-up timestamp; asked for short-term workaround request.
Customer (AtlasMaps): Provided the three request ids and confirmed they can reproduce by triggering an ingestion job + scale-up. Asked for an immediate mitigation as backfill is blocked.
SRE (Ethan): Noted temporary mitigation available: exclude our internal healthcheck probes from tenant burst accounting and increase customer's burst pool delta for the next autoscaler window.
Engineering (Priya - rate-limiter): Looking at token-slicing and refill alignment code; flagged possible double-counting on signed URL callback handshake path. Will instrument extra logs for next hour.

Issue summary:
Customer reports a sequence of 429 throttles that began immediately after their monthly billing plan auto-upgrade and a scheduled bulk-embedding job window (02:00-03:00 UTC). FluxData runs a parallelized importer of ~12k small documents per minute across 50 workers using a dedicated pool. Impact: ingestion stopped for ~18 minutes, downstream index rebuild stalled, customer SLA hit.

Impact:
- Customer ingestion pipeline observed spike from ~200 TPS to ~1.2k TPS during warmup window; platform returned 429s and Client saw backoff.
- Visible revenue impact (ingest delayed), support escalation from customer success.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (enterprise-dedicated-42) in prod-us-east serving embeddings and reranking models.
- API clients use long-lived API key with multiplexed HTTP/2 connections and ephemeral signed URLs for chunk upload callbacks.

Observed behavior:
- Throttles began ~2026-03-10 02:09:14 UTC; 429s peaked at 02:16 and subsided ~02:27 after manual rate-smoothing toggle by oncall.
- Console shows tenant token-bucket reduced by ~40% compared to pre-upgrade baseline even after billing change completed at 01:58.

Expected behavior:
- Plan upgrade should refresh quotas immediately or follow documented grace period; scheduled bulk windows should not cause opaque double-accounting between route-level preflight and tenant-level refill.
-- sample API gateway excerpt (redacted):
2026-03-10T02:09:14Z INFO request_id=rid-7a4f path=/v1/embeddings model=open-embedding-xl-v1 api_key=*** status=429 reason=quota_exhausted tenant_bucket_remaining=0 route_bucket_remaining=3 conn_id=conn-83
2026-03-10T02:12:03Z WARN autoscaler warmup triggered pool=enterprise-dedicated-42 expected_capacity=10 current_capacity=6
2026-03-10T02:16:21Z INFO rate-limiter reconcile event=rebalance from=legacy-refill to=plan-refill tenant_bucket_before=1200 tenant_bucket_after=720 note="proportional-rebalance-after-plan-change"
2026-03-10T02:27:50Z INFO support action toggle rate_smoothing=off actor=oncall-ops@redwood internal_note="manual smoothing rollback"
1) Customer performs plan upgrade at 01:58 UTC for org FluxData and has scheduled bulk-embed job window at 02:00 UTC.
2) Start 50 parallel workers that open persistent HTTP/2 connections and push embedding requests at ~12k/min aggregate.
3) Observe tenant and route token-buckets, monitor 429 counts and refill logs in rate-limiter service.
4) Toggle rate-smoothing flag and observe logic path that applies proportional rebalance between legacy refill and new plan refill.
2026-03-10 03:05 - CS (Marina Rodriguez): Customer reports ingestion backlog of ~200k documents, requests ETA and whether tokens will be credited back.
2026-03-10 03:18 - Oncall (Liam Chen): Investigating; initial hypothesis is rebalance algorithm reduced effective tokens during the refill boundary. Temporarily toggled smoothing to mitigate, will follow up with logs.
2026-03-10 04:01 - SRE (Darren O'Neil): Confirmed rate-limiter emitted 'proportional-rebalance' events for this tenant. Need to correlate with billing webhook latency for plan changes (billing-service#pr-210).
2026-03-11 09:12 - Product (Rina Patel): Added to triage board; recommend a short-term console-visible warning on plan-upgrade windows for dedicated customers.
Hypotheses:
- Billing webhook processing latency caused the rate-limiter to run a proportional rebalance using stale baseline token counts, leading to under-allocation.
- Preflight/checks for multipart uploads are counted at route-level and then again at tenant-level due to recent ingress proxy affinity change.
- Scheduled autoscaler warmup consumed burst credits earlier than expected while pool scaled from 6 -> 10 nodes.

What we ran:
- Correlated billing webhook timestamps with rate-limiter events; billing completed at 01:58 but billing-notify delivered at 02:03 (5m delay).
- Replayed token accounting for the tenant for the 10-minute window using historical refill logs; saw double-debit of preflight tokens for signed-url callbacks.
- Simulated bulk importer with identical concurrency against a staging cluster with and without 'rate_smoothing' flag; smoothing off prevented the sudden drop but increased bursts.

Preliminary root cause:
- Edge case combination of billing webhook delivery latency + proportional rebalance code path that assumes immediate webhook arrival. This caused a conservative recalculation that temporarily lowered the tenant bucket mid-warmup. Secondary contributor: preflight callbacks being counted twice due to proxy header rewrite introduced in edge-proxy deploy (edge-proxy PR #337).
Mitigations applied:
- Oncall disabled proportional rate smoothing for tenant (manual toggle) which restored normal refill behavior; ingestion resumed.
- Reissued 100% of the timestamps-affected tokens to FluxData as a goodwill adjustment.
Short-term action items:
- Patch to rate-limiter to ignore proportional rebalance if billing-notify timestamp is >2m stale (hotfix merged: github PR 489).
- Rollback edge-proxy header rewrite that double-counted preflight callbacks (PR 337 reverted).
- Add console banner to warn during plan-upgrade windows and document guidance for scheduling bulk jobs.
Follow-ups / long-term:
- Engineering story to add idempotent billing-change handshake (linked: INT-3307) and more robust token-reconciliation runbook.
- SRE to add synthetic test that simulates plan-upgrade during autoscaler warmup.

Status: Hotfix deployed to prod-us-east 2026-03-11 22:40 UTC; customer confirmed recovery and backlog drain started immediately. Ticket remains open while we monitor for residual regressions and implement full reconciliation story.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Mediscope enabled "strict" residency pinning for their private VPC deployment (eu-west) on 2026-03-09 to meet data residency audit. After the change they see ~1-2% of requests routed to US edges, causing p95 spikes and additional egress cost. Customer is concerned this violates residency guarantees.

Impact:
- Intermittent cross-region egress to us-central for eu-west workloads (customer-visible logs and Sentry traces).
- P95 latency increases from ~200ms -> 650-1,200ms for affected requests.
- Regulatory risk for health data.

Environment:
- Private deployment with VPC peering and customer-managed DNS / corporate proxy.
- Region: eu-west (primary).
- Control plane residency mode: strict-pin (TTL 60s).

Steps to reproduce (customer reported):
1) Customer issues requests from internal app behind corporate proxy that performs DNS prerender + HTTP/2 connection pooling.
2) Occasionally the proxy reuses an existing connection that was originally established to a different edge (us-central) before the strict-pin was applied.
3) The reused connection omits the token-scoped residency header (X-RW-Residency) on the forwarded request due to header filtering on reuse.
4) Control plane treats the request as unpinned and routes to default global edge (us-central) leading to cross-region egress.

Relevant logs / snippets provided by customer:
- client-side trace: 2026-03-11T14:12:02Z request_id=abc123 url=/v1/generate proxy_conn_id=conn-44 reused=true header_count=12
- edge access log (us-central): 2026-03-11T14:12:02Z src=proxy-ip:45112 dst=edge-us-1 rw-token=masked residency=none route=default
- control-plane audit: 2026-03-11T14:12:03Z token=tok-xxxx resolved_residency=eu-west but incoming_metadata.residency_header_missing=true

Customer-provided hypothesis:
They believe their proxy's connection reuse is stripping or not forwarding the residency header on subsequent requests, creating a race against the control-plane pin-refresh window.

Attachments provided:
- tcpdump of proxy behavior (sensitive)
- aggregated access logs showing matching timestamps
- screenshot of console pin status for tenant

Investigation so far:
- Reproduced similar behavior in staging by simulating a proxy that reuses connections established before a pin update; when the X-RW-Residency header is absent we observe routing to default global edge.
- Confirmed control plane fallback behavior: if token-scoped residency header is not present, routing uses token metadata + runtime pin; when a request arrives without header during a pin-refresh window, the request may be sent to another region until the pin is re-established on the session.
- Looked at proxy logs: some client-side proxies reuse long-lived HTTP/2 connections even after DNS changes; if header set is applied only on the initial request, subsequent requests may omit optional headers.
- Noted the pin TTL customer uses (60s) is low; combined with connection reuse it increases probability of mismatch.

Hypotheses:
1) Header omission on reused connections is the proximate cause.
2) Short pin TTL + control plane pin refresh race increases odds of seeing unpinned requests.
3) Customer's DNS prerender/cache behavior can cause connections to open to non-local edges before pin flips, creating existing connection pool to wrong edge.
- Ask SRE networking to validate whether control plane can honor token-scoped residency by inspecting token at TLS layer for reused upstream connections (risk/feasibility).
- Recommend customer increase pin TTL temporarily to 3600s while they remediate proxy behavior.
- Provide customer with a recommended proxy configuration snippet to preserve residency headers across reused connections and to disable cross-region prerendering.
- Add instrumentation to console to surface number of requests lacking residency header per token per region for easier debugging.
- If reproducible, propose a control-plane guard to drop requests without residency header for customers with private strict-pin (opt-in) to avoid accidental egress.
2026-03-10: Maya Chen -> Mediscope (initial ticket) - Asked for logs, sample request IDs, and confirmation of proxy vendor/version.
2026-03-11: Customer uploaded tcpdump and confirmed corporate proxy is 'EdgeProxy v2.4' with HTTP/2 pooling enabled.
2026-03-12: Diego Ramos -> Customer - Shared staging repro steps and suggested increasing pin TTL to 3600s as a short-term mitigation.
2026-03-12: Customer applied TTL change and reported 90% reduction in observed US-egress events during monitoring window (24h).

Additional notes:
SRE-Team (2026-03-12): Control plane currently trusts residency header when present, but does not enforce drop for missing header during strict-pin in private deployments. Filing INT follow-up to evaluate safety of stricter enforcement.
Security (2026-03-13): Need to confirm any proposed control-plane enforcement change will not cause request loss for legitimate edge cases. Recommend feature gated opt-in for now.
Workaround implemented: advised customer to increase pin TTL to 3600s and deploy proxy config change to preserve X-RW-Residency header across connection reuse. Customer reported significant reduction in cross-region egress within 24h.
Longer-term action items: SRE to evaluate opt-in enforcement of residency-header presence for private strict-pin customers (INT ticket opened). Add console telemetry for missing residency headers per token.
Status: customer mitigation accepted; engineering follow-up in progress.

Issue summary: Customer (NimbleDocs) received a finalized monthly invoice that included a ~ $12 charge labeled 'healthcheck-ping' with token count 0. This occurred after a promotional credit was applied earlier in the cycle. Impact: Customer flagged unexpected charge and is asking for explanation and refund if charge is erroneous. Environment: Dedicated tenant on us-east, monthly billing cycle ending 2026-03-01. Steps to reproduce (as reported): 1) Scheduled internal monitoring service issues periodic HTTP healthcheck pings to Redwood endpoint using a service key tagged 'monitoring'. 2) During billing cycle, a promo credit coupon was applied to the org on 2026-02-20 that zeroed out several lines. 3) Finalized invoice (2026-03-01) contains an extra line: 'healthcheck-ping' quantity 0, unit price $0.003, amount $11.97, invoice total nonzero despite visible promo credit lines. Expected behavior: Healthcheck or zero-token lines should either be suppressed from final invoice or correctly zeroed by promo-credit logic. Actual behavior: Line shows zero tokens but a nonzero charge; promo-credit appears to be applied after a rounding/aggregation step causing a residual amount. Logs/evidence: Customer attached PDF of invoice and example API key tags. Internal logs: postback receipts show healthchecks were ingested as 'probe' traffic on 2026-02-27 03:12-03:18 UTC, but token counter shows 0 tokens for those requests. Billing reconciler shows event hashes for those postbacks with nonempty rate_id and unit_price. Timeline: 2026-03-02 customer ticket opened. 2026-03-03 CS acknowledged, asked for invoice PDF and API key. 2026-03-04 SRE started investigation. 2026-03-10 reconciler engineer reproduced aggregation edge case locally.

Additional notes:
2026-03-03 Customer (NimbleDocs - contact: Jose Alvarez): Attached invoice PDF (INV-2026-03-NIMBLE) and monitoring key id: mk_live_7f2a. Customer says monitoring pings are low priority and expects them to be suppressed for billing.
Hypothesis 1: Probe/healthcheck postbacks were tagged but not filtered from billing because token_count == 0 logic did not mark them as zero-charge in reconciler.
Hypothesis 2: Promo credit application occurs after line-level aggregation and rounding; small residuals can survive if a zero-token line was treated as quantity 1 at aggregation time.
Evidence: Local run of reconciler on archived bucket reproduced nonzero dollar amount when simulating probe postbacks with unit_price set in catalog. Reconciler logs (reconciler-2026-02-28.log) show 'tokens=0, rate_applied=true, quantity=1'.
Scope: We scanned 125 tenants in us-east with '_monitor' or 'health' tags and found 9 tenants with similar artifacts in the same cycle. NimbleDocs is the first to surface complaint.
Temporary mitigation: Add a reconciler rule to ignore any postback with tokens==0 AND tag in [monitor, healthcheck, probe] until code fix lands. This rule has been applied to production reconciler config on 2026-03-12.
Code change: PR github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/1428 updates billing aggregator to: (a) treat zero-token lines as zero-quantity, (b) apply promo credits at line-level where possible to avoid residual rounding, (c) add unit tests covering floating-point edge cases.
Provisional credit: Applied immediate credit memo of $11.97 to NimbleDocs (credit memo CM-2026-03-NIMBLE) pending reprocessed invoice; customer has accepted provisional credit.
Fix deployed: Merged PR 1428 and deployed reconciler change to staging on 2026-03-12 and to prod on 2026-03-13. Change ensures tokens==0 lines are dropped before aggregation and promo-credit rebalancing is performed at line-level.
Follow-up: Reprocess March billing window for affected tenants in us-east to remove similar residual charges; estimated rerun completion by 2026-03-17.
Runbook update: Added guidance to billing runbook 'Ignore zero-token probe lines' and created an alert for any invoice line with quantity==0 and amount>0.
Customer communication: Sent summary and credit confirmation to Jose Alvarez on 2026-03-13. Scheduled a short postmortem update on 2026-03-18 if rerun yields additional adjustments.
