Customer report (via CSM): Usage Insights page intermittently times out when selecting a 30-day time range. Reported during beta usage review; customer is using the route/model breakdown table for internal chargeback and prefers monthly (30d) views.

Issue summary
- When selecting Time range = Last 30 days on Console -> Usage -> Cost Insights -> Route/Model Breakdown, the page shows a spinner for ~20–30s then errors.
- Error shown in UI: "Something went wrong" / "Request timed out".
- Browser console shows 504 from insights query endpoint.

Impact
- Customer cannot use Insights for monthly reporting; they fall back to ad-hoc invoice exports, which do not provide route-level attribution.
- This blocks planned weekly/monthly reporting workflows and created concern about whether beta is production-ready for finance usage.

Environment
- Workspace: heliochat-prod
- Deployment mode: Hosted API
- Region: us-east
- Time range: Last 30 days
- Filters: Project = "production"; Route filter empty (All); Model filter empty (All)

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Enable Usage Insights beta for any medium/high-volume workspace.
2) Console -> Usage -> Cost Insights.
3) Select Last 30 days.
4) Leave Route/Model filters as All.
5) Observe request timing out (commonly at gateway timeout).

Expected
- Page loads within SLO (interactive query) or degrades gracefully (partial results banner / prompt to narrow range / offer export).

Actual
- Console query request returns 504; user must retry or narrow to 7d/14d.

Notes / artifacts
- Example request id (from customer HAR): req_01JMX8Z7K6QY8P2G9T1V
- Insights endpoint: GET /console/api/usage-insights/v1/breakdown?group_by=route,model&range=30d
- Gateway error: 504 upstream timeout at ~20s
- Support asked customer for an approximate volume band; Heliochat reports "~40–60M tokens/day" across multiple routes, frequent streaming.

Requested outcome
- Make 30d queries reliable (no timeouts) or provide a productized fallback: guidance/guardrails + export path for long ranges.

Owner / routing
- Initial triage by Support; routed to Console Backend + Telemetry Analytics for query optimization and/or server-side limits.

Additional notes:
(1) add server-side max row cap for interactive breakdown queries (top 500 groups by cost) + deterministic "Other" bucket;
(2) ensure time filter always hits partitioned aggregated table (no raw fallback for 30d);
(3) adjust query timeout and caching for 30d but keep SLO.
Tracking via ENG-3821 and PR for query optimization.
Resolved by optimizing warehouse query path for 30d interactive breakdowns (avoid raw-event fallback; improve partition pruning; add caching; cap interactive result rows with "Other" bucket). Added guidance in console (30d performance note + suggestion to filter/narrow range and use Export for full detail). Deployed to prod under beta feature flag; customer confirmed no further timeouts.
1) Continue monitoring 30d query latency + 504 rate for high-volume workspaces; alert if p95 exceeds SLO.
2) Follow up on route normalization completeness to reduce group cardinality and improve monthly queries (esp. OpenAI-compat paths).
3) Ensure docs/tooltips clarify top-N + "Other" semantics vs exports for full fidelity.
4) Consider raising async export prominence for 30d+ workflows (finance use cases).

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 03:14 UTC BrightAI reported intermittent 502/504 errors and corrupted model shard downloads from Redwood Private deployment. Symptoms include failed range-downloads (partial files with checksum mismatch), control-plane heartbeats showing DNS timeouts, and flakey artifact fetches that correlate with brief spikes in end-customer packet loss.

Impact: Customer's private deployment in us-east-1 experiences failed model pulls when autoscaling serving nodes trigger shard fetches. Application-level errors observed in customer's tracing: S3 presigned range 206 responses replaced by 200 HTML error pages or truncated content, causing model load retries and increased latency. The issue affects production traffic for BrightAI (~40 nodes) and causes cascading rollouts to fail.

Environment: BrightAI private deployment (VPC peered into Redwood control plane via VPCE). VPCE endpoint policy present. Customer uses a managed MPLS circuit to their on-prem datacenter which peers into the same transit provider as their egress path.

Observed start: 2026-03-10 03:14 UTC
Observed pattern: Intermittent, correlated with short BGP/LDP flaps reported by the carrier; lasts 10-30s and resolves.

From BrightAI environment, trigger parallel model artifact range requests (multipart range GETs) to presigned S3 URLs via VPCE while generating sustained outbound traffic through MPLS path
Monitor TCP connection state and DNS responses to api.redwood-inference.internal (control plane hostname) during the window
Reproduce traffic surge that triggers autoscaling on serving nodes to force concurrent shard downloads
2026-03-10T03:14:12Z control-plane: fetch_artifact presigned_url=*** status=206 size=245760 shard_id=12
2026-03-10T03:14:13Z edge-proxy: range-request-received range=bytes=0-65535 returned=200 content-type=text/html size=4096
2026-03-10T03:14:13Z customer-tcpdump: DNS response for api.redwood-inference.internal -> 10.20.30.5 (internal edge) via MPLS next-hop (unexpected)
2026-03-10T03:14:14Z control-plane: auth handshake delayed tls_resume_retry count=3

Additional notes:
BrightAI Tier1 (customer): Uploaded tcpdump and traceroute; pointed to intermittent route changes to our VPCE prefix originating at the carrier (MPLS).
BrightAI Network Lead: Opened a carrier TAC case; carrier confirmed brief LDP session resets during maintenance window and NAT appliance performed DNS rewrite to a maintenance cache node.
TCP dump analysis shows that during the event DNS A queries for api.redwood-inference.internal returned a private address (10.20.30.5) for ~12-27s windows; subsequent TLS handshake to that address failed ALPN and returned HTTP/1.1 200 error HTML for range requests.
Traceroute and mpls labels indicate that traffic shifted to a maintenance LSP where an edge cache appliance (carrier-managed) was present. That appliance rewrote DNS answers to point to a maintenance front-end that does not honor S3 presigned range semantics, causing 200 responses with HTML bodies instead of 206 partial content.
Control-plane logs show retry storms as artifact checksum validation failed and retries exhausted, increasing tail latency and triggering additional model reload attempts.
No Redwood control-plane configuration change correlated to the time window. VPCE endpoint policy and prefix lists remained unchanged. The carrier's maintenance was the only external factor.
We reproduced a similar failure in lab by simulating a DNS response rewrite to an alternate IP that serves non-S3 content; artifacts truncated and checksums failed identically.
Short-term mitigation applied (2026-03-11 01:40 UTC): instructed BrightAI to add static route to their VPC route table pointing VPCE resolver IPs to a preferred IGW path that bypasses MPLS egress for control-plane resolution. This avoided the carrier rewrite and stopped the corrupted downloads.
Applied a temporary VPCE endpoint policy suggestion: require host header validation and strict TLS SNI checks on control-plane hostnames to reject rewritten responses from non-Redwood front-ends.
Carrier root cause: planned MPLS LDP maintenance triggered a failover to a maintenance LSP where a cache appliance returned rewritten DNS responses pointing to maintenance hosts. Carrier to update maintenance playbook to avoid DNS rewrites for customer VPCE prefixes. BrightAI to obtain maintenance exclusion from carrier for our VPCE CIDRs.
Long-term action items: (1) Add detection to Redwood control-plane for mismatched content-types on presigned range responses and fail fast with clearer error to customers; (2) Add guidance in Private Deploy runbook to pin VPCE resolver IPs or use secondary egress path for artifact fetches; (3) Coordinate with carriers to include VPCE CIDRs in maintenance exclusion lists.
Status: customer workaround validated, carrier escalated. Follow-up planned with BrightAI and carrier for closure.
payload.summary: Intermittent MPLS LDP route rewrite causes VPCE DNS redirect -> control plane misrouted artifact fetches and corrupted range downloads

Issue summary:
Customer LexiDocs reports sporadic long-tail latency (spikes to several seconds) on inference requests using 'structured_output: json_stream' mode. The problem appears only when the model emits many small interleaved chunks (client flush behavior + model tokenization) and when payloads contain occasional non-ASCII control bytes.

Impact:
- ~4% of streaming requests for this customer show end-to-end latency spikes (tails up to 3-6s) despite normally meeting 100-200ms per-token latency.
- Affects production traffic in us-east region. Customer reports timeouts in their downstream workers and increased error rates.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod-us-east)
- Customer on Dedicated pool (reserved capacity)
- SDK: lexical-stream-js v2.3.1, server side runtime: redwood-serving v1.2.0-quant

Observed behavior:
- Long latency occurs late in the stream often on the final JSON closing characters or just after small bursts of punctuation tokens.
- Server logs show repeated "decoder backpressure" and "partial token flush" traces around the same request IDs.
- In some cases, the client receives a small final chunk that only contains a control byte; server waits ~2s before delivering the chunk to the socket.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming JSON mode should not introduce multi-second tail latency for small interleaved chunks; the runtime should batch and forward tokens promptly while preserving valid JSON output.
Use SDK lexical-stream-js v2.3.1 with structured_output=json_stream and set flush_every_token=true (this pattern mirrors LexiDocs client).
Send a prompt that yields nested structured output with many short tokens (lists of short objects, punctuation-heavy).
Observe latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) and watch for 2-6s tail outliers in prod-us-east.
2026-03-12T14:22:09Z [req:abc123] decoder: tokenized chunk size=1, queue_len=42, backpressure=true
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z [req:abc123] transport: delayed_write: waiting_for_buffer (2007ms)
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z [req:abc123] runtime: partial-kv-flush, reason=interleaved-control-byte
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z [req:abc123] error_rate: downstream_timeout_incremented customer_response_time_ms=3821
Initial hypothesis: small per-token flushes from client + model's tokenization produce many tiny socket writes, causing the runtime's per-request decoder to enter a backpressure loop and wait to coalesce to preserve JSON token boundaries.
Confirmed via tcpdump and internal trace: many TLV-sized writes < 64B arriving; the serving runtime applies a conservative flush threshold in json_stream mode to avoid emitting malformed JSON when tokens include control bytes — this threshold currently causes ~1.5-2s coalescing in edge cases.
We reproduced locally by simulating LexiDocs flush pattern and observed identical latency tail when the runtime's json_coalesce_ms parameter was set to the production default (1500ms). Lowering to 50ms in a dev build removed the 2s tails but increased short-lived malformed-JSON risk in tests with control bytes.
There is also an interaction with our UTF-8 sanitization path: when a control / non-UTF8 byte is observed, decoder stalls for additional validation (adds ~200-400ms per event).
Aisha Patel (Support) [2026-03-12]: Customer noticed a spike after they upgraded lexical-stream-js to v2.3.1. They can reproduce internally with a small script. Requested an explanation and workaround.
Marco Nguyen (SRE) [2026-03-12]: I can reproduce with the customer's flush_every_token pattern. Attaching tcpdump and internal trace. Triage -> high priority. Escalating to runtime team.
Elena Rossi (Runtime Eng) [2026-03-13]: Found config json_coalesce_ms=1500ms in serving-runtime prod profile. This was added to reduce JSON-splitting bugs but is too aggressive for dedicated low-latency pools. Proposing a quick mitigation to reduce default to 200ms for dedicated pools and add a per-route override.
LexiDocs (Customer) [2026-03-13]: Can we get a documented workaround while you patch? Our downstream workers expect sub-1s completion.
Short-term mitigation: add per-customer runtime override to set json_coalesce_ms=100ms for LexiDocs dedicated pool. Patch and deploy to prod-us-east (canary then roll).
Immediate customer workaround: set flush_every_token=false in lexical-stream-js or buffer client-side until a small threshold (>=64B) before flushing. Recommend disabling aggressive per-token flushes temporarily.
Medium-term: runtime change to perform safe coalescing while still streaming — allow emitting structurally-safe partial JSON fragments (e.g., emit commas/closing braces with escape handling) to avoid long stalls caused by control-byte detection.
Add test harness: create a fuzz test that simulates interleaved small-chunk flushes and random control bytes to prevent regressions.
Ongoing - temporary per-customer override applied to LexiDocs pool (json_coalesce_ms lowered to 100ms) on 2026-03-13 canary. Customer workaround documented. Runtime engineering to land safer streaming coalescing approach in PR#5207 (under review). Postmortem and permanent fix scheduled after deploy and 72h observation window.
Owner: Elena Rossi (Runtime) - implement safe coalescing logic and add unit + integration tests. Target: 2026-03-20
SRE: monitor p99 streaming tail for LexiDocs and other dedicated pools for 7 days after deploy
DX: update docs with guidance for SDK flush settings and a new 'json_stream_tuning' guide
payload.summary: Intermittent long-tail latency in JSON (structured) mode caused by small interleaved streaming chunks and tokenizer backpressure

Issue summary:
Customer Lumenly Inc. reports unexpected adjustment lines on their month-to-date invoice after a rate-tier change was deployed. Several provisional credits applied earlier in the cycle flipped to negative adjustments during nightly reconciliation. Impact: customer-facing revenue lines showed a net negative on their provisional invoice and triggered an autopay hold alert.

Impact:
- 3 invoice lines reversed for Lumenly (account ID hidden for PII) totaling ~USD 27,450 provisional variance.
- Autopay hold generated; customer requested immediate explanation and provisional waiver.

Environment and context:
- Rate-tier update deployed (pricing-service v2.14.0) at 2026-03-09T23:58:00Z.
- Edge proxy fleet in us-east had a rolling restart 2026-03-09T23:56–00:30 UTC.
- Postback-reconciler replays occurred during nightly reprocessing window 2026-03-10 02:00–03:00 UTC.

Why it's surprising: billing system is expected to consistently classify postbacks by the timestamp on the usage payload to apply the correct rate tier; here some postbacks were classified with pre-change tiers while others used post-change tiers, producing offsetting credits and negative adjustments.
1) Deploy a rate-tier update to pricing-service (v2.14.0) with deploy window overlapping edge-proxy restart.
2) Send a batch of postbacks from an edge instance that still has stale pricing-cache (simulate by freezing pricing-cache refresh for 60s).
3) Allow postbacks to land in async postback queue and then trigger reconciler reprocessing for the same time window.
4) Observe that reconciler produces both pre-update and post-update attributions for the same usage timestamps, leading to provisional credit + reversal lines on invoice preview.
2026-03-09T23:57:45Z edge-proxy-12 INFO outgoing postback id=pb_9f2c header:pricing-version=2026-03-09T23:55:00Z
2026-03-09T23:59:02Z edge-proxy-03 INFO outgoing postback id=pb_9f2d header:pricing-version=2026-03-10T00:00:00Z
2026-03-10T02:12:08Z reconciler WARN detected duplicate-window for customer=lumenly postback_group=pg_441
2026-03-10T02:12:12Z reconciler INFO reprocessed postbacks count=183 classification=post-change
2026-03-10T02:12:15Z billing-engine ERROR invoice-delta generation produced negative_adjustment_line id=adj_774
Support (Asha): Acknowledged with customer at 2026-03-10 04:05 UTC. Customer is requesting provisional waiver until root cause identified.
Customer (Lumenly - Maya R.): We saw the negative line on the preview and autopay was put on hold. Please advise whether this will be reversed; our AR team needs confirmation.
SRE (Diego): Reproducing locally with a cached pricing snapshot. Edge pods that restarted early sent postbacks with an old pricing-version header. Pinpointed two edge nodes with delayed cache invalidation.
Eng (Priya K.): Pricing-service change included a schema-compatible tier cutover; reconciler should have used usage.timestamp but used pricing-version header for classification in the presence of duplicates. Raising INT ticket for reconciler logic hardening.
Support (Asha): Coordinating provisional credit and customer communication. Finance contact CC'd for manual hold/waiver processing.
Timeline constructed from deploy logs and reconciler traces. Root contributors identified: (1) pricing cache expiry race on edge proxies during rolling restart, (2) postback-reconciler logic preference for an incoming pricing-version header when deduplication window is active, and (3) asynchronous reprocessing that applied a newer pricing tier to a subset of postbacks leading to offsetting credit and charge lines. Sample repro created with a 45s pricing-cache freeze reproduces negative adjustment pattern locally. Related internal issue created INT-4421 to change reconciler to deterministically use usage.timestamp -> pricing cutover lookup and ignore pricing-version header for replays.
Short-term: finance applied a provisional waiver for the USD 27,450 net variance for Lumenly (waiver ID FW-2026-03-11-LUM). Support communicated waiver to customer and removed autopay hold pending cleanup (customer notified 2026-03-11 10:20 UTC).

Mid-term: engineering deployed reconciler patch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/pricing/pull/2147) to prefer authoritative timestamp-based lookup for replay windows and added a sanity-check to detect mixed-classification in a single reconciliation batch; patch rolled out 2026-03-11T18:40:00Z.

Long-term: SRE will add a post-deploy edge-cache reconciliation step in the deploy playbook to avoid stale pricing-header forwarding during pricing changes. Also scheduling a billing postmortem and a customer-facing summary to be posted to Confluence.

Follow-ups: INT-4421 (reconciler code hardening), ENG-PR-2147 (merged), FIN-ops processed waiver. Customer billing statement will be reconciled in the next billing cycle and finance confirmed no further action required.

comments: 2026-03-10T09:48:00Z Marta Diaz: Acknowledged. We've opened an incident and are investigating. Can you share a sample request id that failed?

Issue summary: During the 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC traffic spike for HyperRetail's dedicated pool, a routing decision caused a subset of requests to be routed to a low-memory variant (sparse-mem-replica) that was not sufficiently warmed. Impact: ~10-15% of requests for the customer returned 504/timeouts or experienced multi-second token wait times for ~20 minutes. This affected storefront search latency and caused customer alerts.

Impact: Customer-reported elevated error rate and slow inference for critical search endpoints during peak traffic. No customer data leakage observed.

Environment: Dedicated pool for HyperRetail in prod-us-east. Autoscaling events were in-flight; new replicas launching. The routing policy includes a capacity-aware fallback that prefers low-cost variants under contention.

Expected behavior: Under capacity pressure the platform should route to warmed fallback variants or gracefully queue with backpressure, not shift a significant fraction of live traffic to replicas that require prolonged KV cache warmup.

Observed behavior: A traffic shift (tilt) routed ~12% of requests to a low-memory replica type which had cold or partially-cold KV caches, causing long per-request warmup stalls and 504s.

Steps already taken: throttled customer burst, temporarily disabled the low-memory fallback for the HyperRetail pool, coordinated with SRE to increase target warm replicas.

Provision a dedicated pool with mixed-capacity variants (high-memory and low-memory replicas)
Simulate a sudden traffic surge that triggers autoscaler and fallback routing (5000 req/min for 5 minutes)
Observe routing decisions in router logs: look for >10% traffic to sparse-mem replicas that recently transitioned from initializing
Inspect serving-runtime traces for KV cache misses and long warmup durations
Requests were diverted to sparse-mem replicas that returned intermittent 504s and showed long wait times due to synchronous KV warmup operations. Latency plots show a step increase in tail latency aligned with the autoscaler add events.
Platform should maintain traffic on warmed replicas, or use a staged ramp/fan-out to new replicas that pre-warm KV caches without taking live traffic until warm. Fallbacks should prefer replicas with warm KV cache or use queued warmup prior to routing production traffic.
Router decision logs indicate the capacity-aware fallback policy weights low-cost variants when available_capacity < threshold
Sparse-mem replicas were marked 'ready' by the scheduler once container started but before KV prefetch completed
Serving-runtime traces show synchronous KV prefetch running on first requests, blocking token generation for ~1.2-2.5s per affected request
Autoscaler events: 3 new sparse-mem replicas spun up between 09:12-09:18 UTC; router immediately included them in candidate pool
Hypothesis: readiness gating currently checks container liveness only; KV cache readiness is not gated leading to early routing
Related runbook: routing/fallback-policy.md suggests a warmup probe feature but it was not enabled for this customer's deployment

2026-03-10T09:13:01Z scheduler INFO replica sparse-mem-7b-32 initializing: container_up=true kv_prefetch_status=running
2026-03-10T09:13:05Z runtime WARN request_id=abc123 warm_kv_blocking=true duration=1287ms model=redwood-3B-q4_0
2026-03-10T09:14:22Z proxy ERROR 504 upstream_timeout replica=sparse-mem-7b-32 request_id=def456

Issue summary: After a customer-initiated org consolidation on 2026-03-09 (merging two sub-orgs into a single paid org), Brightline Freight reports that a block of retained hourly reserve credits (~48h worth) that previously appeared on the source subaccount vanished from the consolidated invoice and account balance. Impact: customer is short ~$4.2k of usable credits which they relied on for a scheduled batch embedding job. They requested urgent review before finance closes the billing cycle. Environment: production, us-east region, dedicated reserved capacity. Observed behavior: credits were visible in subaccount A (sub-acc-id: sub_7f9) through 2026-03-08; consolidation job completed on 2026-03-09; post-consolidation the consolidated org (org-id: org_bf-consol) shows reduced retained credit balance and the invoice for 2026-03-10 includes no rollover credit line. Expected behavior: credits should be transferred and reflected on consolidated org balance or appear as a prorated credit line on the first post-consolidation invoice. Steps to reproduce (customer flow): 1) Customer opened consolidation flow in Console -> Billing -> Organizations -> Merge subaccounts. 2) Selected sub_7f9 as source and merged into primary org_bf-consol. 3) Confirmed merge on 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC. 4) On 2026-03-10 customer ran a 6-hour batch embedding job and observed credit exhaustion earlier than expected. Logs/artifacts: attached usage-postbacks and postback delivery receipts (timestamped), consolidation audit record from console, and the 2026-03-10 invoice snapshot. Customer included billing export CSV and screen grab of pre-merge retained credits.

Additional notes:
Initial hypothesis: consolidation job executes a transfer of top-level balances then triggers postback processing; if there is an in-flight postback for the source subaccount, the postback may be applied to the old ledger id and lost during merge due to idempotency checks.
Observed that usage-postback processing has a window where ledger id mapping is cached; consolidation invalidates mapping. Postback pb_9832 was timestamped 2026-03-08T23:00:12Z and processed 2026-03-09T02:08:44Z—this is within the merge window (merge at 02:14 UTC). Processing time seems normal but missing ack from billing suggests a downstream write failed or was reconciled to old ledger and then dropped by consolidation cleanup.
Checked job traces: single node in usage-processor showed GC pause at 02:06 causing retry and delayed attempt. The processor retried and used stale ledger reference. Capture: trace link https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/trace/usage/trace-9832
Engineering note: potential race between org-merge workflow and postback processor's ledger resolution cache. Repro attempt: simulated consolidation in staging with scheduled postbacks and confirmed failure mode when consolidation occurs during a retry window.
Impact assessment: affects customers who run consolidation/merge flows while hourly reserve credits or recent postbacks are still in pipeline. Frequency estimated low (<0.5% of merges) but high impact for customers relying on retained credits.
Suggested mitigations: 1) short-term: provisionally apply credit while reconciliation runs (done). 2) mid-term: add strong handoff locking on merge for ledger id resolution or drain in-flight postbacks before committing merge. 3) long-term: make postback processing idempotent to new ledger ids by mapping legacy ledger writes to new parent ledger on detected merge events.
Related artifacts: usage-processor logs (s3://support-artifacts/usage/pb_9832.log), postback delivery receipt (pb_9832.delivery.json), consolidation audit record (audit_2026-03-09-02:14.json).
2026-03-14 - Temporary/Workaround: Applied provisional credit of $4,200 to Brightline Freight (visible in Console -> Billing -> Credits). Notified customer and Finance. This prevents immediate workflow disruption for scheduled jobs.
2026-03-14 - Root cause: Race condition between consolidation job and delayed postback processing where a retry used stale ledger mapping; resulting ledger write was dropped during consolidation cleanup. INT-4421 assigned to Accounting/Engineering for replay.
2026-03-16 - Permanent fix plan: Engineering to implement ledger-resolution locking for org-merge (PR referenced: github.com/redwood-inference/organizations/pull/1291) and add a reconciliation job that replays any postbacks targeting deprecated ledger ids into their consolidated parent. Expected rollout: canary 2026-03-22, full rollout 2026-04-01.
Follow-ups: Finance to issue formal credit memo on invoice 2026-03-10 and audit post-merge ledger migration logs. Support to reach back to customer with confirmation once reconciliation completes and the provisional credit converted to invoice adjustment. Ticket will remain open until INT-4421 is closed and invoice adjusted.

Issue summary:
Customers using streaming websocket sessions experience intermittent p99 inference timeouts (client sees connection-level timeout / aborted stream) when per-connection QPS is low but overall connection count is sustained.

Impact:
- Multiple NoteStream customers reported degraded UX: streaming responses occasionally stall for 7-10s then timeout at the client.
- Affects interactive use-cases (real-time transcription, chat) with many concurrent low-throughput connections.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east) on Dedicated pool dedicated-nylon-03.
- Models: redwood-mini-3b (primary), fallback to redwood-2b.
- Rolling upgrade to runtime v3.8.1 started 2026-03-08, customer observed regressions 2026-03-09 morning.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Establish ~1200 concurrent websocket streaming sessions to the hosted endpoint from many distinct client IPs.
2) Each connection issues a short request stream (1-3 tokens per second, bursty) with long-lived session semantics.
3) Observe p95/p99 latency for token responses and occasional stream disconnects/timeouts.

Observed behavior:
- p50 stable, p95 shows modest increase, p99 spikes to 6-12s intermittently.
- Affected sessions often show a long wait in server-side traces inside the batcher wait loop before execution.
- Some 499/499-like client aborts correlate with timeouts in streaming proxy logs.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous-batcher should dispatch small batches promptly for streaming sessions to maintain low tail latency even at low per-connection QPS.

Initial logs / evidence:
- Streaming proxy (proxy-7) logs: repeated entries of "connection-id=<id> downstream-timeout after 9s" at same time windows.
- Serving runtime trace: request queued in batch-window for 5.8s before dispatch.
- Metrics: continuous-batcher.batch_size distribution shifted lower; batch-window wait_time histogram shows heavy tail.
- No obvious GPU saturation; utilization ~40% on affected nodes.

Hypothesis:
- A change in the run-time v3.8.1 modified the batcher idle aggregation heuristic (aimed to reduce tiny-batch churn). Under sustained high connection count but low per-connection QPS, the heuristic increases the internal hold time for prefix coalescing which inadvertently amplifies tail latency for streaming sessions.

Temporary mitigation suggested to customer:
- Route streaming websocket traffic to a dedicated routing rule that pins to a lower-batching-enabled node pool (workaround applied for NoteStream on 2026-03-10).

Next steps planned:
- Engineering to reproduce at scale in staging with configured client emulator.
- Instrument additional traces in batcher to capture hold_time decision inputs.
- Evaluate reverting the heuristic change or exposing it as a tunable for Dedicated customers.
2026-03-10 - Support: Confirmed multiple incoming reports from NoteStream with identical pattern; created ticket and added to priority queue.
2026-03-10 - SRE: Captured flame graphs and queue histograms; no node-level CPU/mem/GPU pressure observed.
2026-03-11 - Eng (Liam Chen): Reproduced locally using 1.2k websocket clients; confirmed batcher hold_time increased under v3.8.1 compared to v3.7.4.
2026-03-11 - Eng: Narrowed root cause to a new adaptive_idle_alpha (introduced in runtime v3.8.1) that biases towards larger coalescing windows when observed inter-arrival variance is high across connections.
2026-03-11 - Eng: Crafted hotfix that exposes adaptive_idle_alpha as per-pool configuration and reduces default alpha for streaming-optimized pools.
2026-03-12 - QA: Ran a canary deployment of hotfix in us-east with NoteStream workload; p99 regressions no longer reproducible in 6-hour soak.
Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-10: Customer reports intermittent streaming timeouts around 09:20-10:45 EDT. Collected client-side logs and sample connection IDs. Marking P1 due to customer-impacting UX for interactive product.
SRE (Marcos Rivera) 2026-03-10: Uploaded batcher histograms and node metrics to support artifacts: /slack/archives/#support and linked Grafana panels. No saturation; suspect batching policy change in last runtime.
Engineer (Liam Chen) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with emulator. Observed that adaptive_idle_alpha increased hold windows under our test pattern. Will prepare patch to expose per-pool alpha and run canary.
Customer (NoteStream, Emma Zhou) 2026-03-11: Thanks — appreciate the quick diagnosis. We confirmed degraded UX during our morning traffic ramp. Happy to test canary routing as suggested.
Engineer (Liam Chen) 2026-03-12: Hotfix deployed to dedicated-nylon-03 as a canary: adaptive_idle_alpha lowered from 0.8 -> 0.35 for streaming pool. Observed p99 drop from ~9s to ~200ms in test harness. Rolling to remaining nodes now.
Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-12: Customer confirmed resolution in production: no further streaming timeouts during a 24h observation window. Closing ticket and scheduling follow-up to add opt-in streaming-optimized routing config to Dedicated docs.
Hotfix deployed: exposed and lowered adaptive_idle_alpha for streaming-optimized pools; routed NoteStream to streaming-optimized pool. Post-deploy canary showed p99 tail latency reduced to acceptable levels. Follow-up: document per-pool batching tunables and add an automated detection alert for streaming tail increases.
Add runbook step: how to pin streaming traffic to streaming-optimized pools
Expose adaptive_idle_alpha in Dedicated console UI as a tunable per pool
Create alert: continuous-batcher tail-latency delta > 2s for 5m
Backfill tests: integration test for many low-qps websocket clients during CI gating

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate external tool invocations when using function-calling across multiple SDKs. The customer issues a request from their TypeScript frontend that is proxied by a backend implemented in Python. Both sides attach an idempotency key, but when the backend retries on an internal 5xx, the function executor receives two invocations for the same logical request.
1) Customer sends chat completion with function-calling from TS client to backend API (TS -> Python proxy -> Redwood API)
2) TS client includes X-Idempotency-Key header and body.metadata.idempotency_key set to same value
3) Python backend attaches its own idempotency header based on incoming header and forwards request to Redwood using python-sdk call.function_call()
4) Simulate transient 502 from serving-runtime (we injected a kill to a replica) so backend performs exponential backoff retry
5) Observe two invocations executed by function-executor service within 2s window despite keys matching
Expected: single function invocation (at-most-once) observed for the idempotency key. Actual: duplicate invocations observed and customer sees duplicate side effects (two emails sent).
Initial hypothesis: idempotency keys from TS and Python layers were not normalized and were being interpreted as different keys by the API. Reproduction verified duplicates when backend retries after a transient 502. Traced headers across gateway and serving-runtime: both requests carried X-Idempotency-Key but python-sdk was also attaching a SDK-generated internal idempotency token in request body.metadata which the server prioritizes. The server dedup key resolution order currently prefers body.metadata.idempotency_key when present and falls back to X-Idempotency-Key; in this flow the first attempt had body.metadata absent and second (retry) had body.metadata populated by the python-sdk client wrapper. This caused server to treat them as distinct.
Additional findings: TypeScript client included idempotency in both header and body; Python client SDK auto-populates body.metadata when header is present unless explicit flag disabled. Race condition: transient error path where the forwarded first request did not include body.metadata (proxy stripped it), but retry path had SDK repopulate body.metadata resulting in two different dedup keys.
Impact: customer experienced duplicate side effects (two transactional emails). Occurred for ~0.2% of function-calling flows in their traffic pattern under transient upstream errors. Reproducible in staging with proxy that conditionally strips metadata.
[2026-03-10T14:02:07Z] api-gateway: received request id=abc123 header X-Idempotency-Key=snz-001
[2026-03-10T14:02:07Z] python-proxy: forwarded request to /v1/chat.func idempotency=snz-001 trace=trace-77
[2026-03-10T14:02:07Z] serving-runtime: returned 502 'upstream timeout' for req trace-77
[2026-03-10T14:02:08Z] python-proxy: retry attempt 1 for idempotency=snz-001
[2026-03-10T14:02:08Z] serving-runtime: accepted request trace-78 -> dispatched to function-executor invocation-id=fex-443
[2026-03-10T14:02:09Z] function-executor: executed tool send_email invocation-id=fex-443 status=success
[2026-03-10T14:02:09Z] function-executor: executed tool send_email invocation-id=fex-444 status=success (duplicate)
Notes: invocation-id differs even though idempotency header present.
Support - Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): Customer reported duplicate emails tied to a single user action. They pasted logs showing two function-executor invocations. Customer is on dedicated plan and requests urgency due to user impact.
SRE - Marco Nguyen (2026-03-10): Reproduced in staging. Confirmed two invocations and differing internal dedup keys. Noted the serving-runtime dedup priority ordering in code. Created a short reproduction script using ts-client -> python-proxy -> python-sdk.
SDK Eng - Priya Shah (2026-03-11): Observed python-sdk behavior: auto-populates body.metadata.idempotency_key if X-Idempotency-Key header present unless options.disable_metadata_injection=true. This was inconsistent with TS SDK which always attaches both. Opened PR to make metadata injection behaviour explicit and documented.
Backend Eng - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-11): Added a temporary server-side normalization in gateway: normalize dedup key by checking both header and body and preferring the earliest-seen non-empty value. Deployed to staging; duplicate no longer reproducible in controlled tests.
Customer - SparkNotez (2026-03-11): Confirmed that disabling backend retry eliminates duplicates, but they need retries for resiliency. Asked for recommended pattern for multi-hop architectures.
Support - Aisha Patel (2026-03-12): Advised customer on interim workaround (proxy must preserve header-to-body mapping or set python-sdk disable flag). Working on coordinated SDK + server fix.
Engineering - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-12): ETA for full fix: server-side dedup normalization + SDK patch to make metadata injection consistent across languages. Targeted rollout: canary 2026-03-18, full 2026-03-22.
Workaround provided to customer: (1) ensure proxy preserves original X-Idempotency-Key header and does not inject or remove body.metadata on the first attempt, or (2) set python-sdk option disable_metadata_injection=true to avoid body metadata being added only on retry. Temporary gateway normalization deployed to staging to reduce immediate duplicates. Engineering plan: add server normalization that canonicalizes dedup keys (prefer header if both present but accept either) and ship python-sdk patch to align behavior with TS SDK. Rollout schedule created; post-deploy monitoring dashboard added. Customer accepted workaround and will validate on staging before full rollout.
1) Merge and release python-sdk patch that documents and exposes metadata injection toggle (PR #1876). 2) Implement canonicalization in gateway to resolve mixed-key scenarios and add unit/integration tests. 3) Add a synthetic test in CI that simulates proxy stripping body.metadata to catch regressions. 4) Customer validation call scheduled 2026-03-13. 5) Monitor for duplicates for two weeks after full rollout.
If duplicates continue after fixes, track per-request trace across gateway + serving + executor to determine whether dedup keys were normalized; include exact header/body snapshots. Consider an API change that requires a single canonical idempotency header with SDK adapters performing mapping consistently.
payload.summary: Cross-language idempotency key mismatch causing duplicate remote tool invocations during function-calling retries

Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated partial tokens and duplicated early fragments when resuming SSE streams after a short disconnect. The pattern is consistent when requests route through their managed reverse proxy that enables HTTP/2 server-push (Apache/mod_http2).

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat UI shows duplicated early phrases and missing later tokens for ~10% of resumed streams.
- Users report 15% of resumed messages requiring manual refresh, affecting perceived reliability for the enterprise customer (billing tier: enterprise).

Environment:
- Customer runs web client in browser behind corporate reverse proxy (Apache 2.4 + mod_http2) + internal CDN.
- Redwood API requests route through our api-gateway -> edge-proxy -> serving-runtime in us-east.
- Model: redwood/gpt-3.5-small pinned.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open web chat session (long-running conversation, ~1k token context).
2) Trigger generation with streaming SSE response (streaming=true).
3) Simulate short network blip (~2s) that closes client TCP connection; client attempts immediate reconnect.
4) Observe resumed stream: initial fragments duplicated, later fragments missing or reordered.

Minimal repro (curl):
- Customer captured reproduction using http2-capable curl + netcat to simulate proxy push. Example (approx):
  curl --http2 -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true&model=redwood/gpt-3.5-small" 2>&1 | sed -n '1,200p'

Observed logs (customer):
- Edge logs show connection reset followed by two requests within 500ms reusing the same session affinity token.
- Proxy logs include: "H2-PUSH: stream 15 associated with stream 3" and several 200 OK but with "content-length: chunked" re-chunking.

Additional context:
- This customer only sees the problem when their proxy has H2 server-push enabled. They attempted disabling push and reported the symptom disappears.
- Others on standard load-balanced paths have not reproduced; however, we have similar-but-different tickets referencing fragmented chunks and proxy reordering (linked issues above).
2026-03-10 | Aisha Tan (Support): Customer opened case with chat transcript and edge/log snippets. Customer asserts issue began after proxy upgrade to mod_http2 1.15.
2026-03-10 | Marco Ruiz (SRE): Assigned for investigation. Requested packet capture and exact proxy config. Asked customer for TLS termination details and whether connection pooling was in use.
2026-03-11 | NeoDoc (Customer): Provided proxy config excerpt: 'H2Push on; H2PushPriorityPolicy interleave; SetEnv proxy-sendchunks on'. Also attached pcap showing server-push frames interleaved with reset. Customer confirms disabling H2Push removes the duplication.
2026-03-11 | Marco Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced locally using a test proxy with server-push enabled. Observed that our SSE framing boundary ("data: {json}\n\n") can be split across HTTP/2 DATA frames that are then associated with server-push streams; reassembly at the edge-proxy layer produced an off-by-one offset in event boundaries during rapid reconnects.
2026-03-12 | Eng (Serving Runtime): Noted possible root cause: when connection is reset and a subsequent request reuses the same HTTP/2 session, the proxy may deliver leftover pushed DATA frames tied to previous stream IDs before the new stream's end-event. This causes the client to see duplicated early fragments and missing terminal fragments because metadata end markers are misassociated.
2026-03-13 | Marco Ruiz (SRE): Proposed mitigation to treat server-push frames as ephemeral for SSE endpoints and drop any pushed frames that are not explicitly associated with an active stream ID in the runtime's reassembly logic. Filed internal follow-up INT-3420 to add stricter stream-id validation at the api-gateway layer.
Hypothesis 1: Proxy-level re-chunking + HTTP/2 server-push can shuffle DATA frames across stream boundaries during quick reconnects, producing event boundary misalignment in our SSE reassembler.
Hypothesis 2: Client reconnect semantics + reused session affinity token allow race where pushed fragments from prior stream arrive and are stitched into the resumed stream before the resumed stream's final end-event is observed.
Reproducer created: Local apache/mux proxy with H2Push on + curl --http2 -N. Able to produce partial-choice duplication in ~30% of trials when adding a forced connection reset between frames.
Edge observations: api-gateway currently relies on sequential assembly by stream connection and does not validate HTTP/2 PUSH_PROMISE lineage robustly for SSE endpoints. Flow currently treats DATA frames arriving on the session as belonging to the most recently active stream if stream ids overlap due to proxy mapping.
Workaround (customer): Disable HTTP/2 server-push on their reverse proxy (confirmed fix).

Short-term server-side mitigation: Implemented gating in api-gateway to reject or ignore HTTP/2 pushed DATA frames for SSE/streaming endpoints, and added conservative stream-id validation (edge patch deployed to us-east as a config toggle). Rolled out to 10% of edge hosts 2026-03-13 04:20UTC.

Long-term fix: Engineering to add deterministic stream lineage checks and stricter framing reassembly at api-gateway + update docs recommending disabling H2 server-push for streaming endpoints. Tracked in INT-3420 (add stream-id lineage validation) and ENG-5042 (update docs + SDK guidance).

Follow-ups: Monitor customer telemetry for 48 hours; pending customer confirmation (requested 2026-03-13). If telemetry remains clean, close ticket and document as KB article 'Proxy server-push interactions with SSE streaming'.
payload.summary: Stream offset skew after intermediary HTTP/2 server-push via reverse proxy causes partial-choice duplication

Issue summary:
LuminaHealth reports intermittent streaming disconnects and sporadic decoding errors after applying a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that enables aggressive KV-prefix prefetching and reduced-precision quantization. Customer observes that ~1.5% of requests within high-concurrency bursts produce truncated streams (client sees connection closed mid-token) and ~0.8% return malformed tokens (gibberish/unexpected UTF sequences).

Impact:
- Affects production traffic for LuminaHealth (dedicated pool) during peak hours (09:00-11:00 US-EST).
- Visible user-facing failures in chat flows and batch scoring jobs.
- Customer revenue impact: periodic failed submissions; they estimate ~120 failed chat sessions/day during peak.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-gpu-pool-12) in us-east-1, serving pinned model variants: llama-3-8b-4bit-quant and fallback azure-compatible-open-7b.
- Tenant optimizer profile changes rolled via console on 2026-03-08 21:12 UTC (optimizer flags: kv_prefetch=on, kv_prefetch_window=64, async_batching=on, quant_profile=aggressive-4bit, decode_safety_checks=off).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Send concurrent chat streams (20 parallel sessions) with average prompt length 350 tokens and streaming enabled.
2) Observe a subset of streams terminate mid-response (~1-2 per minute during peak) and occasional non-decodable characters in payload.

Observed logs / traces (customer-provided):
- Agent traces show streaming session closed with remote error: ECONNRESET after ~1.2s of token emission.
- Serving runtime logs around same timestamps show repeated small GC spikes and occasional kernel fallback on quantized matmul with warnings: "quantization-backoff: kernel-mismatch; using float fallback".
- Telemetry: token-rate spikes correlate with tail-latency increases and higher KV-cache eviction counts.

Investigation notes (Support/SRE):
- Hypothesis A: aggressive quant_profile decreases numerical stability in fused kernels causing kernel fallback and partial frame writes over streaming socket, producing truncated frames.
- Hypothesis B: KV-prefetch with large window + async batching increases memory pressure on the dedicated allocator; intermittent OOM/eviction leads to dropped stream frames.
- Hypothesis C: decode_safety_checks disabled allowed malformed tokens to be emitted when quantized decode encountered corner-case logits.
- Checked infra metrics: transient device memory spikes and allocator reclaim logs aligned with customer-reported windows. No full GPU OOMs, but allocator thrashing observed.
- Reviewed related PRs: optimizer-configs PR #217 contains a recent prefetch window change for tenant profiles that matches the timing.

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- Advised customer to set decode_safety_checks=on (temporary) — customer reported reduced malformed tokens but streaming disconnects continued.
- Applied a conservative runtime throttle for the tenant (reduced concurrency on routing) to reduce pressure — reduced disconnect frequency but not eliminated.

Requested outcome from customer: guidance and a safe, staged unwind plan for optimizer config to restore reliability without full service interruption, plus recommended post-unwind validation steps and a patch plan if needed.

Support/SRE recommended stepwise unwind plan (proposed):
1) Create config snapshot for current tenant profile (console export + optimizer-configs snapshot) — ensures fast rollback to the exact state if needed.
2) Immediately enable decode_safety_checks=true for the tenant (customer already applied; confirm persisted).
3) Reduce kv_prefetch_window from 64 to 16 for the tenant, keep kv_prefetch=on. Monitor allocator reclaim and streaming errors for 30 minutes.
4) If disconnects persist, toggle kv_prefetch=off for the tenant while maintaining aggressive quantization; monitor for 60 minutes.
5) If issues continue with kv_prefetch off, set quant_profile=conservative-8bit (non-aggressive) and keep kv_prefetch off; this should revert fused kernel pathways to stable float/8-bit kernels.
6) If stability regained at any step, progressively reintroduce lower prefetch window (8 -> 16) and test with synthetic load.
7) Post-recovery: run validation harness using 1k sample prompts and streaming checks, run token-decode detector (Conformance tests) and collect 48-hour telemetry to ensure no regressions.

Rollback safety notes:
- Snapshot export is critical prior to any change.
- Each step is additive and small; prefer temporary traffic-split (5% -> 25% -> 100%) to avoid large blast radius.
- Monitor decode error rates, streaming disconnects, allocator reclaim rate, and kernel-fallback logs as primary signals.

Next steps and owners:
- Support (Evelyn Ortiz): confirm snapshot availability and coordinate console changes with LuminaHealth.
- SRE (Marcus Chen): monitor allocator and provide quick toggle scripts to change kv_prefetch flags per-tenant without a restart.
- Customer CT (LuminaHealth engineer Priya Shah): run verification harness during each step and provide logs.

Attachments (provided):
- snippets of serving logs (timestamps redacted)
- optimizer profile JSON export from console

Requested timeline: customer requests resolution within 48 hours due to production impact.

2026-03-09 12:04 UTC - LuminaHealth / Priya Shah: We started seeing errors after the config update rolled on 2026-03-08. We can keep a maintenance window tonight if needed. Attaching a small sample of streaming frames that failed.
2026-03-09 14:30 UTC - Support / Evelyn Ortiz: Acknowledged. Requested snapshot export from customer and asked if they can enable decode_safety_checks immediately.
2026-03-09 15:01 UTC - LuminaHealth / Priya Shah: decode_safety_checks enabled; malformed tokens decreased but streaming disconnects persist. We've attached allocator metrics and kernel-fallback alerts.
2026-03-10 09:18 UTC - SRE / Marcus Chen: Observed allocator reclaim bursts around 09:05-09:15 US-EST and kernel fallback logs concurrent with the disconnects. Preparing per-tenant toggle script for kv_prefetch flags.
2026-03-10 11:40 UTC - Support / Evelyn Ortiz: Proposed stepwise unwind plan posted in ticket. Pending customer's approval for a staged traffic-split test this evening.
2026-03-11 08:55 UTC - LuminaHealth / Priya Shah: Approved. Will start with kv_prefetch_window=>16 tonight and run synthetic 20-parallel streaming tests. Will report back after 2 hours of test traffic.
Pending - awaiting results from staged unwind steps and telemetry confirmation.

Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC a subset of OnyxBank traffic routed through the realtime-router experienced a multipath retry amplification. Requests that normally fan out to 1-2 serving backends were duplicated across 6-10 backends due to stale routing metadata and an aggressive retry policy. Symptoms included elevated tail latency (p95 -> 18s), a surge of duplicate completions returned to the customer, streaming disconnects for long-running sessions, and a notable invoice delta reported by OnyxBank.

Impact:
- Customer-facing failures: intermittent streaming truncation and duplicate completions for 12% of OnyxBank requests between 14:12–15:25 UTC.
- Latency: sustained p95 increase from 400ms to 18s during peak amplification.
- Billing: OnyxBank reported a 3.7x unexpected token/billing delta for the affected window.
- Business: Enterprise SLA exposure and escalated executive contact.

Timeline (UTC):
- 14:08: OnyxBank reports increased errors to #support channel.
- 14:12: Alerts from routing service (error-rate, retries) trigger PagerDuty.
- 14:18: Triage confirms duplicate completions pattern; mitigation steps initiated.
- 14:25: Temporary rate-limiter rule applied to OnyxBank route; duplicate completions reduced by 60%.
- 14:42: Canary rollback of recent routing policy change (PR #2834) confirmed.
- 15:05: Autoscaler throttle engaged to protect global serving pools.
- 15:25: Normal routing behavior restored for OnyxBank.
- 15:40: Customer notified of resolution and temporary credit plan discussed.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Apply the exact routing policy merge from PR #2834 in a staging cluster with multiplexed fanout enabled.
2) Replay a burst of OnyxBank-like requests with high socket churn and intentionally delayed ack from 2nd-tier serving nodes.
3) Observe retry loop when routing metadata contains inconsistent 'preferred_backends' TTL across the router pool.

Logs / Metrics / Artifacts:
- Router logs: /var/log/realtime-router/2026-03-10/route-errors.log (sampled snippets pasted below).
- Trace: trace-id: 0a9f-onyx-14: link to trace in APM: https://apm.redwood.internal/traces/0a9f-onyx-14
- Dashboard: routing-retries/p95 and billing/token-usage dashboards (links attached in linked assets).

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis pointed to a misbehaving serving-host causing clients to retry. Sampling showed identical request IDs duplicated by the router itself.
- Root cause traced to a recent routing control-plane change that introduced a race: metadata TTL updates for 'preferred_backends' were applied asynchronously and a goroutine-level cache allowed stale values to persist for up to 45s under high churn.
- The router's retry policy default (max_retries=3 with aggressive backoff reset) combined with the stale metadata caused the same request to be sent repeatedly to multiple backends before successful ack.
- Billing exposure occurred because duplicate completions were accepted by OnyxBank's aggregator and counted as separate completions in token accounting.

Immediate fixes performed:
- Rolled back PR #2834 at 14:42 UTC (reverted control-plane behavior to synchronous metadata apply in the critical path).
- Applied an emergency soft-rate-limit for OnyxBank routes to cap concurrent fanout to 2 backends at 14:25 UTC.
- Disabled aggressive retry resets in router config (max_retries=1) for enterprise-tier routes at 14:30 UTC.
- Issued hotfix to router cache invalidation to reduce stale TTL window from 45s to 5s (deployed 14:56 UTC, promoted 15:12 UTC).

Workarounds for customer:
- Instructed OnyxBank to enable idempotency tokens on long-running conversational transactions to collapse duplicate completions on their side.
- Provided a temporary client-side retry guidance doc and recommended enabling server-sent deduplication heuristics.

Customer communication and escalation:
- OnyxBank CSM (Daniel Ortega) escalated to support at 14:10 UTC.
- Support provided rolling updates via #support channel and scheduled an executive-to-executive call at 16:00 UTC.
- Offered provisional invoice credit covering the affected 6-minute amplification window plus a 10% goodwill credit for SLA exposure.

Root cause (concise):
A race in the routing control-plane metadata propagation combined with an aggressive router retry policy resulted in request fanout amplification and duplicate completions which were counted by billing.

Resolution and verification steps:
- Control-plane rollback validated that router logs no longer show duplicate request IDs.
- Post-fix synthetic traffic and customer traffic show p95 latency returned to baseline and no duplication observed for 48 hours.
- Billing reconciliation indicates a 3.6x reduction of the anomalous tokens once deduplication and rate limits applied.

Follow-up actions (owner & due dates):
- (ENG-AP) Implement stronger metadata write-through guarantees in control-plane: owner Marco Ruiz, due 2026-04-02.
- (ENG-ROUTER) Add router-side request-id dedupe window and idempotency enforcement: owner Samira Patel, due 2026-03-24.
- (SRE) Add canary gating rule for routing policy merges with churn-level simulation: owner Kevin Osei, due 2026-03-31.
- (CS/Finance) Finalize billing credit and reconciliation with OnyxBank: owner Priya Kapoor, due 2026-03-17.
- (DOCS) Update customer-facing retry guidance and SDK examples: owner DevRel (Michael Liu), due 2026-03-20.

Post-incident retrospective notes:
- We lacked an automated pre-merge simulation that replays high-churn traffic patterns against routing config changes.
- The default router retry settings are too aggressive for enterprise routes that can trigger billing exposure.
- Need clearer cross-team ownership tags for control-plane changes that affect runtime invariants.

Lessons for on-call and support:
- For enterprise customers with billing sensitivity, prioritize soft-rate-limits and idempotency enforcement as the first mitigation path.
- Escalate to ENG lead within 20 minutes if duplicate request patterns are observed in router logs.

Resolution summary for customer-facing communication:
- Root cause identified and rolled back. Hotfix deployed to reduce stale routing metadata propagation and to cap retry-induced fanout.
- We will issue a billing credit for the affected window and follow up with a concrete prevention timeline.

Attached/linked artifacts:
- Router log excerpt (attached in ticket files).
- Trace and dashboard links (see related_confluence_pages).
- PR revert and hotfix commits: github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-router/commit/7a9b2c and /commit/9d4f1a

Status: Resolved.

Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring, highly regular 429 spikes that align with their webhook fanout windows after they applied a priority-split change last week. Errors surface as short (30–90s) waves of 429 responses across multiple backfill workers and interactive lanes, causing duplicate retries in their pipeline.

Impact:
- Incoming webhooks dropped intermittently (~10–15% of events during waves).
- Downstream consumer pipeline replays cause duplicated records and increased processing cost.
- Customer-facing dashboards show delayed processing and elevated retry rates.

Environment:
- Tenant: edgescale-prod-2 (enterprise, dedicated pool)
- Region: prod us-east (edge ingress -> origin rate-limiter -> serving-runtime)
- Recent change: priority-split flag toggled on 2026-03-08 to route webhooks into a higher-priority lane with a narrower refill window.

Observed behavior:
- 429 wave cadence ~every 10 minutes for ~45–70s.
- Throttle headers indicate token-bucket exhaustion on the tenant burst pool, not route-level limit.
- Console quota readout shows burst credits drained, refill lag visible in telemetry.

Desired outcome:
- Clear explanation of root cause and immediate mitigation steps.
- Configuration guidance so webhook traffic and background flushes do not contend for the same burst budget.

1) Using a test tenant with priority-split enabled, emit 10k small webhook POSTs over 30s from 50 parallel clients.
2) Observe ingress logs and rate-limiter metrics tied to the tenant burst pool.
3) Watch for refill-rate lag and 429 response headers (x-rate-limit-remaining, x-rate-limit-reset).
4) Toggle priority-split flag off and repeat load; observe reduced or eliminated 429 waves.
[2026-03-10T14:02:05Z] ingress: tenant=edgescale-prod-2 route=/webhook POST 200 token_remain=120
[2026-03-10T14:02:26Z] ingress: tenant=edgescale-prod-2 route=/webhook POST 429 token_remain=0 reason=burst_exhausted
[2026-03-10T14:03:12Z] ratelimiter: tenant=edgescale-prod-2 burst_pool=bp-14 refill_next=2026-03-10T14:03:45Z credits=0
[2026-03-10T14:03:40Z] serving: worker=ingest-02 retry=1 duplicate_detected=true

2026-03-10T14:15:00Z - Customer (EdgeScale): After the priority-split toggle we see these exact 429 pulses during our normal webhook batches. Rolling it back stops the pulses but we need the priority routing for low latency paths.
2026-03-10T15:00:12Z - Support (Lina Gomez): Thanks — collecting logs and linking telemetry. Can you confirm the approximate batch cadence and whether background flushers run at the same time windows?
2026-03-10T16:22:34Z - Customer (EdgeScale): Batch cadence is cron at :00 and :10 each 10 min. Background flushers run continuously but a heavy sweep runs at :00 align with the webhook window.
2026-03-11T09:01:50Z - Eng (Marco Ruiz): Initial hypothesis: priority-split created narrow, higher-priority window but left background sweeps accounted against the same tenant burst pool. That alignment causes synchronized refill starvation. Instrumented to capture per-route burst accounting next run.
2026-03-12T11:05:21Z - Support (Lina Gomez): Applied temporary mitigation: split background traffic into background-only burst pool and increased webhook lane burst window. Monitoring for next 6 windows.
Captured telemetry shows tenant burst credits drop to zero within ~18–25s of heavy webhook start when background sweep coincides.
Refill interval originally configured at 60s, priority-split created a faster token per-second consumption for the webhook route due to smaller slice sizes (token_slicing=4).
Token-slicing mismatch: edge proxy was slicing large multi-part requests into smaller accounted units at ingress, doubling token consumption compared to origin accounting expectations.
Confirmed route-level headers contained x-route-weight=1.5 while tenant-level weights remained unchanged, effectively increasing webhook burn rate against the shared pool.
No evidence of serving runtime CPU/GPU exhaustion; issue isolated to rate-limiter accounting and burst pool contention.
1) Deployed rate-limiter patch (PR #342) to ensure route-tagged background flush traffic is account-separated when priority-split flag is enabled.
2) Created separate burst pool for background sweeps (bp-bg-edgescale) and remapped background service role to that pool for edgescale-prod-2.
3) Increased webhook burst_window to 90s and adjusted token_slicing to align ingress/origin accounting (token_slicing=8).
4) Suggested customer-side client backoff pattern: 503/429 exponential jitter with max-backoff 120s; recommended linear slow-start for high-parallel fanouts.
5) Monitored 48 hours: 429 waves ceased during observed webhook windows; no duplicate replay incidents after mitigation.
For enterprise tenants with mixed realtime webhooks + background sweeps: 1) Split burst pools by traffic class (realtime vs background). 2) Align token_slicing config across ingress proxies and origin to avoid double accounting. 3) Use wider burst_window for short, high-parallel webhook fanouts (60–120s) and set a minimum route-weight cap to prevent aggressive burn. See runbook linked.
1) Engineering to roll rate-limiter patch to staging across two more tenants and run load test by 2026-03-18.
2) Product to add console affordance to visualize per-burst-pool telemetry and route-to-pool mapping (ticket INT-904321).
3) Customer success to schedule a 1:1 with EdgeScale to walk through backoff recommendations and validate their orchestrator jitter settings.
4) Add an automated alert for 'burst pool refill lag > 30s' in the tenant SLO dashboard

Issue summary:
AtlasDocs (enterprise) reports intermittent duplicate results in rerank top-k and elevated tail latency after upgrading to Redwood SDK 1.4.0. Problem appears when customers stream embedding batches and call the /rerank endpoint concurrently.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: Users see duplicated candidates in top-5 and occasionally top-1, degrading UX for search/rank features.
- Performance: Tail latencies for rerank spike (99th percentile from ~120ms to ~2.3s) during affected windows.
- Scope: Reported on production in us-west region for AtlasDocs; similar but less frequent behavior observed in internal smoke tests.

Environment:
- Customer: AtlasDocs production (enterprise tenant) in us-west; heavy concurrent embedding ingestion plus rerank traffic.
- Redwood platform: hosted API (prod-us-west).
- SDK version: 1.4.0 (notable change: async L2-normalize flag enabled by default, batching/streaming rework).
- Models: redwood-embedder-v2 for on-the-fly embeddings; open-retriever-1.0 for reranker scoring.

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1) Use SDK 1.4.0 with async_normalize=true and stream embeddings for ~200 concurrent requests (payloads of 5–20 documents each).
2) Immediately call /rerank for batched queries that overlap in time with embedding streams.
3) Observe rerank responses and latency distribution; duplicate IDs appear in top-k and 99p latency increases.

Observed logs / metrics / examples:
- APIGW trace ids: apigw-20260313-0812-az1 (customer trace), apigw-20260313-0829-az1 (internal repro).
- Sample rerank response (sanitized): top_k: [doc_124, doc_124, doc_7, doc_9, doc_3] — duplicate doc_124 appears twice with nearly identical scores.
- Serving runtime logs: buffered-queue: flush_count spikes aligned with duplicates; kv-cache hit-rate normal.
- SDK telemetry (from AtlasDocs): async_normalize.latency_hist: median 20ms, 99p 1.9s during incidents.

Initial hypothesis:
- Async L2-normalize introduced in SDK 1.4.0 performs normalization in a worker pool and re-emits normalized vectors back to the ingest path. Under high concurrency, a race may cause the same embedding ID to be enqueued twice (or the normalization callback to re-insert a completed vector), leading to duplicated vector presence in the local batch sent to rerank.
- Cross-batch memory of normalized vectors (cache-tagging bug) could cause mixes between adjacent streaming batches, producing near-duplicate vectors that bump tail latency due to reranker de-dup checks.

Attachments:
- reproducible_script.sh (internal repro harness), truncated logs attached in ticket thread.

Desired outcome:
- Identify root cause and provide a patch/workaround to prevent duplicate embeddings from being sent to rerank and to remove the tail-latency regression.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-13 08:20 PST: Customer reports first occurrence via support email.
- 2026-03-13 09:05 PST: Support triage; asked for traces and SDK version.
- 2026-03-13 10:10 PST: Engineering reproduced locally with SDK 1.4.0 and async_normalize=true; duplication repro consistent when worker_pool_size >= 8.
- 2026-03-13 14:30 PST: Heap/trace analysis shows duplicate enqueue events for same embed_id within ~12–18ms window.
- Hypothesis validated: race in SDK normalization callback can requeue the same payload on rare timing; also discovered missing idempotency check in local batch aggregator prior to dispatch to rerank.
- Quick check: toggling async_normalize=false returns system to baseline (no duplicates, tail latency normal).
Workaround (customer-facing):
- Instructed AtlasDocs to downgrade to SDK 1.3.x or set async_normalize=false in SDK 1.4.0 configuration. This reduced duplicates and restored tail latency to prior levels.

Engineering fixes in progress:
- SDK PR #4123 introduced to add an idempotency guard in the normalization callback and to ensure normalized vectors are deduplicated in the local batch aggregator. (PR link in related_github_prs).
- Serving-runtime alert rule adjusted to detect repeating embed_ids within a 50ms window and drop duplicates temporarily while fix is rolled out.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge SDK fix and ship 1.4.1 (patch) to customers; notify enterprise customers.
2) Enable additional telemetry around embed_id lifecycle in the platform for 72-hour monitoring post-rollout.
3) Confluence postmortem + recommended SDK flags added to upgrade guidance.

2026-03-13 09:12 - Support (L. Nguyen): Reached out to AtlasDocs for traces and timestamps; asked them to hold traffic for 30m while we triage.
2026-03-13 10:22 - Eng (P. Raman): I reproduced locally with a small harness; duplication appears when worker_pool_size >= 8 and concurrent streams > 150. Adding idempotency check to aggregator shows immediate improvement.
2026-03-13 12:05 - Customer (AtlasDocs Ops): Applied async_normalize=false as requested; reported that user-facing duplicates stopped appearing within 10m. Will keep monitor for 24h and confirm.
2026-03-14 08:00 - Eng (J. Lee): SDK PR #4123 opened, adding tests for race scenarios and stress tests for normalization path.
2026-03-14 11:30 - PM (S. Alvarez): Coordinate release notes and customer communication; add to high-risk upgrade advisory until 1.4.1 is released.
payload.summary: Async normalization in SDK 1.4.0 causing cross-batch embedding mixing leading to duplicate top-k and tail latency for rerank

Issue summary:
Customer enabled a new optimizer profile (aggressive batching + prefix prefetch + q4 quant) for their Dedicated pool. Within 30 minutes they reported intermittent 500/502 responses and truncated generations (token loss) for a subset of routes. Impact: user-facing failures and increased tail latency for chat features.

Impact:
- ~2.5% request error rate spike for client routes 'messages.create' and 'chat.stream' (customer reporting production impact).
- Some generations stop mid-stream (token loss) requiring client retry.
- Customer is on Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pool (LumenHealth prod pool).

Environment:
- Dedicated GPUs (4x A10g) in us-east-1
- Runtime: r-inference-3.8.1
- Optimizer profile: "aggressive-multi-batch-prefetch-q4" (created 2026-03-10 09:04 UTC)
- Affected model variants: redwood/gptx-13b-q4_0 (primary), fallback redwood/gptx-13b-fp16

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Route 'messages.create' sends streaming request with prompt size ~1.2k tokens.
2) Request routed to dedicated pool with the optimizer profile enabled.
3) Within 300-800ms the client sees connection reset or a 502 returned by API gateway.
4) Some requests return truncated generations that end without EOS token.

Observed behavior:
- 500/502 responses with backend reason 'generator-exit: eviction' in runtime logs.
- Per-worker logs show frequent KV cache evictions and occasional OOM warnings at the quant kernel layer.
- Spike in per-worker lock contention (see scheduler traces).

Expected behavior:
- Stable responses with 95p latency within SLA and no truncated generations when under similar traffic profile.

Immediate customer ask:
- Provide a low-risk, minimal-impact rollback or mitigation plan to restore full availability quickly without full profile revert if possible.
1) Confirm tenant uses optimizer profile 'aggressive-multi-batch-prefetch-q4'.
2) Send a batch of streaming chat requests with long prefixes (1k+ tokens) at the customer's normal QPS.
3) Observe errors in API gateway and runtime logs showing 'generator-exit: eviction' and 'kv-evict'.
Timeline:
- 2026-03-10 09:04 UTC: Profile activated for LumenHealth.
- 09:35 UTC: Customer reports first errors.
- 09:40 UTC: Support validated increased 95/99p latency and error spikes from our dashboards.
Hypothesis:
- The combination of aggressive batching and prefix prefetch increased per-request KV memory pressure; q4 kernels have smaller headroom causing intermittent kernel failures and eviction-driven generator exits.
- Traffic-patterns with long prefixes exacerbate KV growth and make continuous batching group incompatible with current worker memory reservation.
Evidence:
- Worker logs: repeated 'kv_cache.evict' followed by 'generator-exit: eviction' (see log extracts).
- Traces show batch sizes clustering at 64 (config target 128) but with longer-than-expected KV retention window.
- One runtime note: a small number of quant kernels reported 'mixed-precision fallback' messages before OOM warnings.
Next steps executed by support:
- Scoped the impact to the LumenHealth tenant and created an emergency snapshot of optimizer state.
- Raised a priority ticket with SRE to watch node memory and throttling during mitigation steps.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:12 UTC - LumenHealth (Customer): We need to restore production by EOD. Prefer minimal changes that avoid full revert if safe.
2026-03-10 10:36 UTC - LumenHealth (Customer): Approved. Please proceed with stepwise approach and notify before each step.

Mitigation executed (temporary):

- Reduced serving batch target from 128 -> 48 for affected tenant routes via per-tenant override.
- Monitored for 2h; error rate fell below 0.3% and truncated-generation reports stopped.
Permanent recommended plan:
1) Build a conservative optimizer profile 'conservative-lumen-v1' that:
   - caps continuous batch target at 48,
   - reduces prefix prefetch window by 60%,
   - keeps q4 enabled only for short-prefix routes,
   - enforces per-worker memory headroom reservation flag.
2) Run a shadow test (10k requests/day) for 48 hours using routing split.
3) If metrics stable (95p latency and error rate within SLA), roll forward with gradual traffic split (25/50/100).
4) Add runtime guard: automatic 429-based slowdown if KV eviction rate exceeds threshold for 5 minutes.
5) Postmortem: capture workload prompt-length distribution and add to model evaluation dashboard.
Follow-ups scheduled:
- Change window with customer: 2026-03-17 02:00-03:00 UTC.

- Product to create 'conservative' optimizer profile template in Console.

- Add per-profile snapshot button and rollback-traffic button in Console (dx).

Quick commands used during mitigation:

payload.description:
Customer reported a sudden spike in end-to-end inference latency and increased request timeouts from their Dedicated deployment. Symptoms: 95th/99th token latency up ~3x, frequent 504/502 responses from the Redwood API, and application-side request queuing. Customer runs the Redwood JS SDK embedded in a serverless front-end with moderate concurrency (~200 rps).
1) Use customer's runtime reproducer: spawn 200 concurrent requests to /v1/chat with streaming enabled. 2) SDK version pinned to 2.1.2 with custom retry/backoff: maxRetries=6, baseBackoffMs=20, maxBackoffMs=150. 3) Observe connection counts on client host and error rates to Redwood endpoint. 4) Repeat under steady load for 15 minutes.
Customer app logs: repeated 'socket: reuse failed' and 'connection timed out' entries, a steady increase in TCP TIME_WAIT sockets, and app-level debug: 'retries exhausted -> returning 504'. On Redwood side: Gateway logs show a burst of HTTP 429/502 over a 90s window, followed by recovery. Sample gateway lines: '2026-03-05T14:12:21Z - svc-gateway - 502 - upstream read timeout', '2026-03-05T14:12:22Z - svc-gateway - 429 - rate limit - connection-pool-exhausted'.
- Initial hypothesis: serving-runtime regression. Benchmarks on our fleet showed nominal tail latency for same model under similar load.
- Digging into customer environment: observed ephemeral port exhaustion on their host; socket counts grew linearly.
- Reproducer confirmed: the customer's usage pattern combined streaming responses with not awaiting/closing the stream iterator in their wrapper, causing TCP sockets to remain in TIME_WAIT longer.
- SDK review: version 2.1.2 had a bug in the HTTP connection pool where aborted streaming responses did not return connections to the pool under certain error paths. This increases per-host connection usage.
- Retry/backoff policy amplified the effect: customer's config retried quickly (baseBackoffMs=20, no jitter) and maxRetries=6, generating retry bursts that saturated the limited pool and triggered upstream 429s and 502s.
- Correlation: spikes in retries aligned with increases in socket counts and gateway 429s.
- Reproduction confirmed with an instrumented client: forcing a single connection leak path plus aggressive retries reproduced the perceived slowdown within 2-3 minutes.
Support (Ayesha): Initial triage - escalated to Eng after customer provided tcpdump and SDK logs.
SRE (Marco Ruiz): Confirmed gateway 429s correspond to increased simultaneous connections from customer's IP; recommended customer throttle and restart app as immediate mitigation.
SDK Eng (Liam): Identified connection return path bug in 2.1.2; drafted patch to ensure aborted/consumed streaming responses always release connection to pool; added jitter to example retry policy in docs.
Customer (AtlasHealthAI - Devops): Applied temporary fix: restarted service and set concurrency cap to 50; saw immediate reduction in 5xxs and queue lengths.
Support (Ayesha): Verified latency returned to baseline after customer applied SDK patch and config change; marking resolved.
Root cause: combination of a client-side connection return bug in SDK v2.1.2 and an aggressive retry/backoff configuration on the customer's side which together caused connection pool exhaustion and retry storms.
Actions taken: 1) SDK team released patch v2.1.4 to properly return connections on aborted/streamed responses (PR #984). 2) Provided customer with recommended runtime config: maxConnectionsPerHost >= 20, enable keep-alive, set maxRetries <= 3, baseBackoffMs 100-200 with jitter, and avoid un-awaited streaming iterator patterns. 3) Customer restarted service and deployed SDK v2.1.4; monitoring showed 95th/99th latency and error rates returned to baseline within 20 minutes.
Follow-ups: SDK team to add unit/integration tests for streaming abort paths (INT-1120), and update quickstart docs with explicit retry/backoff examples.
