Issue summary:
Customers embedding Redwood dashboards into third-party portals see alert context (tracehook links and the contextual query snippet) truncated or missing when the dashboard snapshot uses a large time range (>90 days). The symptom is visible on both the embedded iframe and when exporting a scheduled snapshot PDF.

Impact:
- Fathom Health reports that scheduled alert notifications no longer contain the drilldown tracehook for high-severity alerts tied to nightly batch failures.
- Embedded dashboards show the alert card but the "Open in Redwood" link arrives with a truncated ?tracehook= token, resulting in 404/expired link when opened from email/slack.
- Affects enterprise customers who rely on long-range retrospectives and scheduled reports.

Environment:
- prod (us-east primary), also reproduced in eu-west for a separate org.
- Console release: v3.19.2 (web-frontend), alerting-service: v2.8.1, tracehook-proxy: v1.4.0.

Steps to reproduce:
1) In an enterprise org with many monthly rollups, create a dashboard with an alert rule that includes a tracehook (trace_id/link) and set the query time range to 6 months.
2) Embed the dashboard via the embed token (org-scoped) into an external app.
3) Trigger the alert (or run a scheduled snapshot) and inspect the alert payload in the notification (email / scheduled PDF / Slack webhook).
4) Click the drilldown link that should open the console with the tracehook parameter.

Observed result:
- The tracehook query parameter is truncated or ends mid-token. Console shows "Missing trace context" and the linked time window is incorrectly bounded. Exported PDF shows the alert card without the link.

Expected result:
- Full tracehook token preserved in embeds and scheduled exports regardless of the snapshot time range. Alert notification should provide a valid link back to console with context preserved.

Excerpt from tracehook-proxy logs (2026-03-12T07:58:11Z):
[WARN] request: /api/alert/payload id=abc123 size=4821 bytes - url-length=8123; token-trimmed=true
[ERROR] embed-signer: encode failed: truncation at 8192 bytes for org=org-987
Console front-end (v3.19.2) reported: RangeError: URI too long when constructing embed URL containing long snapshot query string

Support confirmed reproduction in a staging org. Initial hypothesis: embed signing and tokenization path uses a fixed URL buffer or backend field trimmed at 8KB during snapshot serialization. The scheduled exporter compresses the alert context but does not base64-encode long tracehook payloads, which leads to mid-token truncation when persisted to the snapshots table.
Checked DB: snapshots.metadata for Fathom Health shows 'alert_context' blob length 8192 and trailing '...' appended by serializer.
Relevant PR touching serializer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4329 merged 2026-02-28 (optimize snapshot size) — may have introduced aggressive truncation logic.
Temporary reproduction note: reducing dashboard range to 30 days preserves full token; artificially expanding event aggregation (high-cardinality tags) increases token size causing truncation.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 11:22 - SRE (Mark Thompson): Observed serializer hitting 8KB boundary on snapshot metadata column (MySQL/TinyBlob behavior). We'll try increasing column type and test compatibility with existing backfills.
Workaround provided: reduce snapshot time-window to <90 days or disable tracehook in scheduled alerts. Engineering to land encoding+schema-change fix: base64-encode alert context and migrate snapshot.metadata column to MEDIUMBLOB. Patch branch created: fix/snapshot-context-encoding (PR #4521). Planned rollout: stage patch 2026-03-18, prod rollout 2026-03-21 after migration backfill. Post-deploy: run reconciliation job to re-encode existing truncated snapshot contexts.
1) Eng to get PR #4521 reviewed and merged. 2) DB migration plan: alter table snapshots.metadata to MEDIUMBLOB (SRE to run during low-traffic window). 3) Backfill/reconcile truncated entries using graceful re-encoding job. 4) Notify customers when fixed and confirm embedded alert links are valid. 5) Add test to prevent regressions: assert tracehook preserved for time ranges up to 12 months.
2026-03-14: Notified Fathom Health of root cause and provided workaround. Provided tentative ETA for fix (2026-03-21) and offered engineering time for testing their embed pages during stage rollout.

Issue summary: Customer FinScale Analytics reports an unexpected invoice charge tied to a single finalized invoice (invoice_2026_02_28) — an invoice line appears to bill ~18,700 embedding tokens that FinScale reports did not originate from production traffic. Impact: Customer is seeing a finalized charge of €3,740.50 on 2026-02-28 and requests reversal/credit; this blocks their finance team from closing the books for the month. Environment: prod, eu-west, hybrid-hosted with Private fallback to FinScale's VPC.

Observed behavior: Postback aggregator shows a burst of backfilled postbacks spanning 2026-02-27 23:45 -> 2026-02-28 00:12 UTC. Many of the postbacks reference API keys tied to FinScale but have edge-proxy metadata headers referencing edge-proxy IDs that were retired in our scheduled decommission on 2026-02-26. The reconciler accepted the late arrivals and attached them to the finalized invoice window, causing net additional billed tokens.

Steps to reproduce / reproduce criteria:
1) Look up invoice invoice_2026_02_28 and identify invoice line id 77891.
2) Cross-reference postback table for tag org_id: finscale-org and timestamps 2026-02-27/28.
3) Filter postbacks where header X-Edge-Proxy-ID matches retired proxies list (decom_2026_02_26_*).
4) Confirm reconciliation created usage_event records with source=postback-reconciler and finalized_flag=true.

Relevant logs / evidence:
- Postback stream IDs: pb-7f4a9c3d..pb-7f4a9d12 (list exported to SRE).
- Reconciler job log: reconciler-run-2026-02-28T01:05Z (attached excerpted grep).
- Edge-proxy decommission PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/88 (executor retired proxies but left drain TTL at 72h in staging config).
- Customer timeline: FinScale support email sent 2026-03-11 09:17 CET with CSV of unexpected invoice lines.

Customer impact notes: Finance escalation; customer requests immediate provisional credit and a postmortem explaining why retired proxies generated replayed postbacks that were billed to production org. They indicate these were test probes from a third-party partner that were supposed to be filtered to staging.

Current status: In Progress — triaged by Billing and SRE. Preliminary hypothesis: decommissioned edge proxies were still emitting probe traffic due to a misconfigured drain TTL; postback-reconciler treated late-arriving postbacks as valid usage because they had production org_id and correct signature, and our postback deduplication window did not catch replays originating from retired proxies.
03/12 13:20 CET: Support ingested customer CSV and matched invoice line to reconciler_uids.
03/12 15:05 CET: SRE replayed reconciler logs; identified recon-run job that accepted postbacks with header X-Edge-Proxy-ID decom_2026_02_26_07 and timestamps within the billing window.
03/13 09:45 CET: Billing confirmed postback->usage_event->invoice_line chain; no duplicate detection triggered because message IDs differed due to proxy rewrite.
03/13 11:30 CET: Edge team verified drain TTL was set to 72h in the live deploy branch; decommission step should have used immediate drain for retired proxies but did not due to missing flag in the runbook (PR #88 altered behavior).
03/14 08:00 CET: Reconciler team attached hotfix to ignore postbacks from proxies with 'decom_' prefix and to require original-client-ip header for attribution when proxies are retired (PR pending).
A provisional credit has been issued to FinScale for the full disputed amount while we complete reconciliation (credit_id: CR-2026-03-14-FS). Temporary mitigation: Block all postbacks that present X-Edge-Proxy-ID matching retired list from being accepted into the reconciler; this is enabled for eu-west staging and will be rolled to prod after smoke tests.
Short-term: issue provisional credit and revert charged invoice line; deploy reconciler filter to drop postbacks from retired proxies and re-run reconciliation for invoices impacted (target 2026-03-15).
Long-term: update decommission runbook to set drain TTL=0 for retired proxies, add reconciler validation for proxy provenance, and add a reconciliation audit that flags large single-org inflows from retired proxies older than 12h. Postmortem and customer-facing RCA to be published under support:Postmortems within 10 business days.
Aisha Kapoor (Support) 2026-03-12 13:40: Added initial ticket after receiving customer's CSV. Asked Billing to freeze invoice adjustments until SRE confirms source.
BillingOps (Omar Ruiz) 2026-03-12 14:05: Reconciler chain identified — creating provisional credit hold; not issuing credit until SRE confirms replay source. Linking to SUP-733555 for similar postback phantom cases.
SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-13 10:12: Found drain TTL mismatch; filed hotfix to reconciler to ignore retired-proxy postbacks. Patch in PR: github.com/redwood-inference/postback-reconciler/pull/412. Will run reconciliation replay after merge.
FinScale (Elena M.) 2026-03-13 16:22: Thanks — we need an immediate provisional credit to avoid payment hold. Our finance lead is cc'd. Awaiting confirmation.
BillingOps (Omar Ruiz) 2026-03-14 09:30: Issued provisional credit CR-2026-03-14-FS for €3,740.50 and marked invoice as disputed in accounting system. Pending reconciler replay and final adjustment.
Provisional credit issued on 2026-03-14 and reconciler filter deployed to prod (eu-west) on 2026-03-14 11:10 UTC. Reconciliation replay scheduled and invoice correction planned for 2026-03-15. Final RCA to be posted once runbook and reconciler changes are merged and validated.
Deploy reconciler patch to drop retired-proxy postbacks — done (2026-03-14).
Replay reconciliation for date range 2026-02-27..2026-02-28 and regenerate invoice lines for finscale-org (scheduled 2026-03-15).
Update edge-proxy decommission runbook to set drain TTL=0 and add a pre-decom validation step (owner: Edge team; due 2026-03-19).
Publish customer-facing RCA and internal postmortem (owner: Support/SRE; due 2026-03-26).

Issue summary:
VeloxApps reports that when they multiplex multiple client shards into a single batched request (they multiplex client connections for throughput), some tool/function invocations are executed out of the expected order and occasionally re-run despite using an idempotency token per logical action. This manifests sporadically under load and after a scheduler rebalance.

Impact:
- Multiple customers of VeloxApps observe transactional side-effects (webhook posts, DB writes) happening in the wrong order or being processed twice, causing inconsistent application state.
- Occurs intermittently (~0.3% of requests) but affects high-value workflows; customer flagged as P1 due to business impact.

Environment details:
- Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated pool) in us-east.
- SDKs: python 1.4.2, go 0.9.8.
- Pattern: 8 client shards multiplexed via a custom gateway that merges requests into a batch with per-invocation idempotency_token and sequence_index metadata.
- Model: rw-open-7b-v1 with KV cache enabled and batching window set to 50ms.

Expected behavior:
- Each logical tool invocation should be executed at most once (idempotent) and, when sequence_index is provided, should preserve ordering across invocations from the same logical session.

Observed behavior:
- Some invocations are processed twice despite identical idempotency_token.
- Sequence ordering is violated: later sequence_index gets executed before an earlier one for a small subset of multiplexed batches.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Spin up dedicated pool stub in us-east and route 8 client shards through a local gateway that multiplexes.
2) Send a batch of 120 short inference requests that include: model call + tool invocation (webhook POST) with idempotency_token and sequence_index.
3) Simulate scheduler rebalance by draining one serving worker during the run.
4) Observe webhook endpoints for duplicate posts and compare sequence_index ordering.

Logs (snippets provided):
- Gateway merge log shows single batched request id: batch-20260310-09:22:14 with 120 records.
- Serving runtime trace: "worker-7 accepted batch-20260310-09:22:14" then "worker-3 recovered KV cache for shard 4 and re-enqueued 7 ops".
- Webhook logs: duplicate POST for invocation token idemp-9a1b, timestamps 09:22:14.814 and 09:22:14.923.

Attachments provided by customer: merging gateway logs, serving traces, webhook endpoint headers.
2026-03-10 - Triage by Support (Maya): Collected logs and verified customer's dedicated pool id. Reproduced single duplicate in internal load test using customer's gateway pattern but only after simulated worker drain.
2026-03-11 - Eng (Rafael): Hypothesis A: During rebalancing, some in-flight batched subrequests are resubmitted by the scheduler when KV cache miss occurs; idempotency tokens may not be propagated to the resubmitted execution path due to an edge case in the batch splitter.
Hypothesis B: Multiplexing layer sets sequence_index but uses per-shard ephemeral id namespace which collides after requeue leading to double-exec detection not matching.
    Action: Add deterministic logging for idempotency_token at batch boundary and instrument batch-split/merge code paths.
2026-03-12 - Eng instrumentation: Found that when a batch is split into two worker assignments (for parallelism), the batch splitter was not always forwarding the original idempotency_token through the worker-queued tasks when a split occurs post-KV-cache-lookup. This causes the re-enqueued task to have a blank token which bypasses idempotency dedupe downstream.
2026-03-12 - Additional note: Sequence ordering violation appears correlated with split+requeue: requeued tasks are appended to the end of the target worker's queue without preserving original sequence_index ordering when cross-worker reshuffle occurs.
2026-03-12 - Customer note: Their gateway uses a custom header X-Session-Seq; confirmed that it maps to sequence_index but the multiplexer translates it to an internal monotonic per-batch counter that can reset during rebalance.
2026-03-13 - Priority decision: Treat as Sev1 for VeloxApps (P1). Engineering to implement a short-term mitigation (ensure idempotency_token is copied on split) and a medium-term fix (stronger invariants in batch splitter to preserve sequence_index ordering across requeue).

2026-03-10 - VeloxApps (Arjun Patel): We're seeing intermittent duplicates and bad order after rolling out a gateway optimization; happy to provide traffic replay. Impacting payment webhook ordering.
2026-03-10 - Support (Maya Chen): Thanks Arjun — we've opened SUP-81234 and requested logs + reproduction steps. Assigned Rafael from runtime eng to investigate.
2026-03-11 - Eng (Rafael Ortega): Can you confirm whether the idempotency_token is present in batch-level logs for re-enqueued tasks? Also, any chance the customer's gateway rewrites headers during multiplexing?
2026-03-11 - VeloxApps (Arjun): Gateway preserves cookies/headers; we attach idempotency_token in the body metadata, not headers. We'll send a traffic dump.
2026-03-12 - Eng (Rafael): We instrumented the splitter and confirmed tokens are sometimes lost when splitting for parallel workers. Working on a hotfix to copy token metadata explicitly on split. Will test on staging with simulated rebalance.
2026-03-13 - Support (Maya Chen): Hotfix deployed to staging; please test and let us know if duplicates/order anomalies persist. We'll schedule a maintenance window to push to customer's dedicated pool if green.
2026-03-14 - Hotfix applied (serving runtime): Ensure idempotency_token and sequence_index are propagated on any batch split and when enqueuing requeued tasks. This prevents blank tokens from bypassing deduplication.
Rollout: Canary in staging -> limited rollout to 10% of production workers -> full rollout to dedicated pools after 24h verification.
Mitigation recommended to customer: Gatekeeper pattern — add server-side confirmation endpoint for side-effecting tools so a second identical POST is safely ignored until dedupe window expires. Also update gateway to include idempotency_token in top-level batch metadata (already recommended).
Follow-ups: Create a unit test for batch splitter invariants (idempotency_token and sequence ordering across requeue). Add a monitoring alert on duplicate tool invocations per-token > 0.05% over a 5m window. Owner: Rafael Ortega. Target completion: 2026-03-21.
payload.summary: Unexpected ordering and idempotency anomalies when sending multiplexed batched tool invocations across sharded clients

Issue summary:
ArborBank requests cryptographically verifiable proof that the ordered audit stream delivered to their SQS->S3 bridge preserves event order and exposes a per-event resume token that can be used for deterministic replay within a configurable TTL. They also require a field-level retention mapping and confirmation of legal-hold behavior when records are flagged for preservation.

Impact:
Customer cannot complete SOC2 audit and legal e-discovery readiness without the ordered delivery guarantees and demonstrable replayability. Blocking their compliance review and delaying contract close.

Environment:
Production account for ArborBank (enterprise tier). Handoff is using Redwood's SQS delivery adapter into customer's AWS account with S3 archival. Region: us-east primary, eu-west for DR.

Customer asks (requested deliverables):
- Hourly signed manifest with checkpoint token and SHA256 per-file checksums.
- Per-event resume token spec and sample token for verification.
- Attestation that replay within TTL yields identical events and preserves order.
- Field-retention matrix mapping Redwood audit fields -> customer SIEM fields + redaction markers.
- Confirmation of legal-hold override on TTL-based deletion.

Steps to reproduce / validate (from support playbook):
1) Request a recent 1-hour manifest from Redwood (signed).
2) Use resume token to request replay from checkpoint T0 and compare sequence IDs and checksums.
3) Trigger a legal-hold flag for an entity and verify retention extension in the manifest for affected events.

Logs / Observations:
- Bridge logs show regular checkpoints every 15 minutes (checkpoint ids present).
- SQS visibility timeout and redrive policy configured, but TTL for replay defaulted to 7 days in current tenant config.
- No current public spec for token HMAC verification published to customer.

Requested deadline: customer asks for initial package and attestation by 2026-03-11 to meet auditor preview.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:46 - SRE (Ana Ruiz): Confirmed bridge emits checkpoint IDs and sequence monotonically increasing. Default replay TTL is 7 days; configurable via tenant retention window. Collected logs: s3://redwood-architect/bridges/arborbank/2026-03-09/*.log
2026-03-12 15:22 - ArborBank (Samir Desai): Thank you — we will run the replay test and follow up with results by EOD 2026-03-12. Also requested timeline for permanent doc publication.
Support validated that checkpoints are produced every 15 minutes and include a monotonic sequence counter. SRE reproduced replay from checkpoint T0 and compared SHA256 of events; binary match confirmed for sampled window. Found that default tenant setting uses a 7-day replay TTL; customer requested 90-day legal-hold override. Discovered no automated legal-hold flag propagation to S3 lifecycle rules — currently enforced by retention manifest and scheduled retention job. Security provided draft HMAC verification snippet but recommended ed25519 manifest signatures for audit-grade evidence.
Workarounds and deliverables provided to customer on 2026-03-12: 1) Sample signed manifest (ed25519) with per-file SHA256 and checkpoint tokens. 2) Resume token spec + example token and verification snippet (HMAC-based) for immediate verification. 3) Draft field-retention matrix mapping Redwood fields to ArborBank SIEM columns and redaction annotations. 4) Legal-hold playbook steps to request retention extension (manual for now).
Follow-ups opened:
- Product ticket (INT-4119) to add tenant-configurable replay TTL and automatic legal-hold lifecycle enforcement (scheduled Q2 2026).
- Docs PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2897 adds interim token verification snippet.
- Confluence page updated with ordered handoff playbook and sample manifests.
Customer confirmed acceptance of the delivered artifacts and marked this as satisfied pending their internal audit verification. Recommend tracking product ticket to closure and publishing formal token-verification API docs as next steps.
Monitor customer replay test results (expected 2026-03-12)
Close ticket after confirmation from ArborBank that artifacts satisfy auditor
Coordinate with Product on INT-4119 for TTL and legal-hold automation
Publish token verification spec to public docs once PR review completes

payload.description:
Issue summary:
SeismicEdge reports frequent 429s on their dedicated pool when a subset of edge devices (IoT sensors) emit microbursts every 5–10 minutes. Each microburst consists of hundreds of short chat/embedding requests. The customer wants guidance on configuring a dual-window quota model (short burst window + long sustained window) and whether to separate traffic by route or device identity to avoid tenant-level exhaustion.

Impact:
- Intermittent 429s affecting ~12k devices during sync windows; retries amplify the burst.
- Customer-visible errors in device logs and elevated support tickets.
- Business impact: ingestion delays for analytics pipeline; priority SLA risk.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool, prod-us-west, dedicated tenant id: seismicedge-prod-12
- Ingest path: POST /v1/embeddings and /v1/chat/stream (short-lived websocket sessions)
- Model: redwood/open-compat-13b pinned for embedding fallback

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Devices scheduled to upload small payloads at t=00:00, but due to jitter many clients attempt at t=00:02–00:05.
2) Orchestrator fan-out launches 300 parallel workers per shard, each opening streaming sessions and embedding calls.
3) Tenant experiences token-window consumption and several requests receive 429s within the 10s window.

Observed behavior:
- 429s surface both on REST endpoints and websocket starts. Throttle headers show tenant token bucket drained (X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0).
- Console shows short spikes in per-tenant token consumption; burst credits consumed quickly then soft 429s for ~30–90s.

Expected behavior:
- Allow short microbursts without immediate tenant-wide exhaustion by carving a small burst pool while maintaining a sustained window for background flushes.

Attachments / sample logs:
- Customer provided a small sample of request timestamps and throttle headers (attached in ticket).
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/seismicedge-prod/tenant-rate-overview (customer-supplied link)

Customer asks:
- How to configure two-tier windows on Dedicated (short burst window + sustained refill) and whether to:
  a) separate ingest routes (e.g., /v1/ingest-edge) with an isolated burst pool, or
  b) rely on per-device keys and client-side jitter/backoff only.

Notes: Customer prefers configuration changes over code changes on devices if possible.
Summary of findings (SRE):
- Tenant-level rate controller shows a single refill window with burst credits enabled, but the burst pool size is insufficient for the observed fan-out pattern.
- Health-check probes and orchestrator retries contributed ~8% of token consumption during the spike.
- Websocket session starts count against the same token budget as short REST calls in current configuration.
- No evidence of double-counting in proxy logs; counts align with agent telemetry.

Metrics observed:
- Peak token consumption: 18k tokens/sec for ~40s during microburst windows.
- Burst pool consumed to 100% within 6s. Sustained bucket refills at configured rate of 2k tokens/min, insufficient for sustained throughput.

Telemetry links:
- Rate controller trace: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/abc123-rate-window
- Ingest orchestrator logs: s3://redwood-support/seismicedge/ingest-2026-03-12.log

Hypothesis:
- A small dedicated burst pool per ingest route combined with a longer sustained window and reduced websocket accounting for session starts should eliminate client-visible 429s without device changes.
Support (Aisha): Acknowledged receipt and escalated to SRE for dedicated-pool analysis. First response ETA within 24h.
Customer (SeismicEdge - Rajesh Iyer): Appreciate quick triage. We prefer server-side config if possible — can you recommend exact parameters we can apply?
SRE (Marco): Reproduced pattern in staging using customer request trace. Recommend creating a separate ingest route with isolated burst pool and reclassifying websocket session start as a lighter-weight token (session-start exemption). Will propose config below.
Support (Aisha): Shared proposed config and asked for permission to apply to a non-prod copy first. Waiting on SeismicEdge approval.
Customer (Rajesh): Approved non-prod test, would like logs and metrics after test run to validate.
# Suggested rate policy (illustrative)
{
  "routes": [
    {
      "path": "/v1/ingest-edge",
      "quota": {
        "burst_window_sec": "10",
        "burst_credits": "12000",
        "sustained_window_sec": "3600",
        "sustained_rate_per_sec": "2000"
      },
      "weight": "1"
    },
    {
      "path": "/v1/chat/stream",
      "quota": {
        "burst_window_sec": "8",
        "burst_credits": "4000",
        "sustained_window_sec": "600",
        "sustained_rate_per_sec": "400"
      },
      "weight": "2"
    }
  ],
  "session_accounting_overrides": {
    "websocket_start_cost_tokens": "2"
  }
}
1) Create an isolated route (/v1/ingest-edge) with a dedicated burst pool sized to absorb observed microbursts. 2) Increase burst_credits modestly (12k in the example) and keep sustained refill conservative. 3) Adjust websocket/session-start accounting to low fixed cost; treat long-running frames normally. 4) Enable short canary rollout for 2 hours and monitor tenants’ token consumption in grafana. 5) If healthcheck/retry traffic contributes significantly, apply source isolation for probes by IP or agent and exclude them from tenant quota counting.

We will schedule a non-prod change window and share metrics after the test.
Pending: Non-prod change applied on 2026-03-13 to /staging/ingest-edge. Early test results: burst pool absorbed the spike and 429s dropped by ~92% during the 30-minute test window. Next step is production canary for 2 hours, followed by full rollout if stable. Customer agreed to production canary on 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC.

Follow-ups assigned:
- INT task to add a console toggle for session-start accounting (INT-3309).
- Support to document recommended dual-window templates in playbook (confluence link added).
payload.summary: Dual-window rate config recommendation for IoT fleet causing tenant 429s

comments: 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Maya Chen: Customer reports ~120 users across 2 projects cannot perform project admin tasks after a recent Private control-plane update. Provided sample token and request traces.
2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Diego Alvarez: Triaging. Initial hypothesis: claim normalization/sanitizer change in 2026-03-05 edge release. Asked for raw IdP assertion and edge proxy logs.

2026-03-11T00:00:00Z Priya Kapoor: Reproduced locally by feeding sample claim through sanitizer function. Confirmed sanitizer regex removes 'project:<digits>:' segments. Marked as regression introduced by commit 7a3f2c (PR #1234).

Issue summary: On AtlasEdge's Private deployment (VPC), users with resource-scoped roles (e.g. project-level admin) are receiving 403s when invoking admin APIs against the project resource. Impact: Blocks customer admins from performing project-level operations (role binds, model rollout, and key creation) for ~120 users across two projects. Background: Customer uses a custom IdP that emits a namespaced role claim 'urn:atlas:roles' with values like 'urn:atlas:role:project:1234:admin' and 'urn:atlas:role:org:sysadmin'. During Private edge processing we run a claim sanitizer to remove unexpected characters/characters that might upset downstream RBAC evaluation. Actual behavior: Sanitizer strips the 'project:1234:' namespace segment, leaving 'admin' which is interpreted as org-level admin or mapped to a default role, causing the RBAC engine to not match resource-scoped bindings. Expected behavior: Sanitizer should preserve resource scoping segments (project:<id>) or provide a configurable allowlist; RBAC should be able to evaluate resource-scoped roles as emitted by the IdP.
1) Customer configures Private deployment with IdP that emits 'urn:atlas:roles' claim containing 'urn:atlas:role:project:1234:admin'.
2) User exchanges SAML/OIDC and obtains token to call Redwood Private admin API (e.g., POST /v1/projects/1234/roles).
3) Request reaches edge-identity-proxy which runs claim sanitizer and forwards token to control-plane authz.
4) Control-plane RBAC denies with 403 when evaluating resource-scoped binding.
2026-03-09T15:21:22Z identity-proxy INFO incoming token sub=atlas|u-9812 claims_before=["urn:atlas:role:project:1234:admin"]
2026-03-09T15:21:22Z identity-proxy DEBUG sanitizer output claims_after=["admin"] (removed segment project:1234)
2026-03-09T15:21:22Z authz-engine WARN evaluation result=deny reason='no matching resource-scoped binding' resource=project:1234 action=bind.roles user=atlas|u-9812
curl -i -X POST https://private.redwood.example/v1/projects/1234/roles
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"forbidden","message":"user lacks role for resource" }

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - AtlasEdge (Customer): Sent SAML assertion and example API request. Clarified that role namespace format is stable and used by other tools in their stack.
Sanitizer code path: edge-identity-proxy v2.11.0 introduced a normalization pass to strip non-alphanumeric segments; the regex /(?:":role:)([a-z]+):[0-9]+:/ was overly greedy and removed the 'project:1234:' segment entirely.
RBAC engine expects exact role identifiers to include resource scoping; mapping fallback logic treats single-term roles as organization-level roles, not matching project bindings.
Reproduction run: unit test added to auth-integration suite reproduces failure when input contains 'urn:atlas:role:project:1234:admin'.
Risk assessment: Medium-High — impacts admin workflows only (not end-user inference), but customer operations are blocked; private customers expect fast remediation.
Workaround verified: Customer can configure IdP to duplicate full namespaced role into a secondary claim which currently bypasses sanitizer (x-redwood-roles-preserve). This is acceptable short-term but not ideal.
Root cause commit: 7a3f2c (edge-identity-proxy) introduced greedy replace. See linked PR.
Related tickets: SUP-89321 (idp-proxy-path-prefix), SUP-71855 (scim rolecache) - similar auth plumbing changes in same release window.
Patch modifies sanitizer regex to whitelist namespaced segments like 'project:<id>' and adds a feature flag 'SANITIZER_PRESERVE_NAMESPACE' defaulting to true for Private deployments. Unit/integration tests added. Engineering to coordinate rollback if unforeseen regressions during canary. Customer will be notified about planned maintenance window for patch application on 2026-03-14.
payload.summary: Resource-scoped claim sanitizer strips namespace, blocking resource-scoped admin operations in Private

Issue summary:
Customer ScoutMetrics runs a nightly daily-sweep job that uploads ~10k small embedding requests in bursts every 7 minutes between 02:00-04:00 UTC. Over the last three nights they saw a repeating sawtooth pattern of 429 responses — throughput spikes then a periodic waveform of throttles for ~30s, recovers briefly, then spikes again. This is affecting their pipelines (15-25% of batches failed), causing downstream retries and significant time-to-completion regression.

Impact:
- Approx 15-25% of batch embedding requests during sweep windows return 429s.
- Customer reports downstream job run time increase from ~12m to ~45m.
- Visible errors in their job logs; customer unable to complete daily indexing reliably.

Environment:
- Tenant: ScoutMetrics (dedicated pool, committed capacity).
- Region: prod-us-east (pool id: pool-ussc-07 provided by customer).
- API path: POST /v1/embeddings (batch upload via multipart clients).
- Keys: rotating short-lived keys used by their workers.

Observed behavior / logs provided by customer:
- 2026-03-09 02:07:13 UTC - burst of 10k requests, API returns 80% 200, 20% 429 distributed in ~30s window.
- Graph provided by customer: sawtooth pattern of error-rate with ~7m periodicity (attached as customer_graph_20260309.png).
- Customer log snippets: "ERROR: 429 rate limit - token_bucket_exhausted for tenant=ScoutMetrics pool=pool-ussc-07"

Steps to reproduce (customer job):
1) Start 200 concurrent worker processes each uploading 50 small documents in parallel to /v1/embeddings.
2) Repeat this at 7 minute cadence for a 2-hour window.
3) Observe intermittent 429s clustered as waveform spikes rather than uniform throttling.

Request from customer:
- Confirm why sawtooth throttle waveform occurs despite dedicated pool commitment.
- Provide recommended config changes (burst window, token refill, multiplexing guidance) and short-term mitigations to avoid daily job failures.
- Request SRE help to review pool telemetry (token-bucket accounting, health-check increments) and verify no cross-tenant bleed or health-checks causing miscounting.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:40 - Support (Marco Silva): Asked customer to provide exact timestamps, sample request IDs, and to confirm if workers use HTTP/2 multiplexing or short-lived API keys. Customer responded: multiplexing=enabled, keys=rotating every 10 minutes.
2026-03-11 02:45 - SRE (Leila Gomez): Observed periodic token-bucket depletion correlated with periodic warmup/scale events on the dedicated pool. Opening INT-5512 for investigation of autoscaler interactions. Linked thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C045POOL/p1678452000
2026-03-12 08:22 - Customer (ScoutMetrics rep - Jenna Patel): Verified that disabling per-worker HTTP/2 multiplexing reduced failures in their next sweep by ~70%. Requests guidance for configuration that preserves throughput but avoids throttles.
Hypotheses:
- Token bucket accounting and refill interacts poorly with many short-lived multiplexed streams: multiplexed sessions may cause token consumption to appear burstier at the gateway, triggering rapid bucket depletion and a sawtooth recovery as refill kicks in.
- Autoscaler warmup/health-checks may briefly reduce usable capacity during scale events, amplifying transient throttle patterns in tight cadence jobs.
- Short-lived API key rotation every 10m may increase connection churn and transient per-key counters leading to uneven per-key accounting.
Telemetry reviewed:
- Pool metrics (pool-ussc-07): token_bucket_level graphs show sawtooth troughs synchronized with customer job cadence.
- Gateway logs: 429 reason strings show token_bucket_exhausted and occasionally health_check_increment.
- Autoscaler events: scale-up at 02:06 and 02:13 with 12-18s of instance churn visible in infra logs. Links: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/pool-ussc-07/token-buckets
Staging reproduction results:
- Full multiplexing enabled: reproduced waveform with 18% 429 rate.
- Multiplexing disabled (one connection per worker): waveform reduced, 4% 429 (mostly at peak saturations).
- Staggered worker-start with multiplexing enabled: waveform amplitude reduced significantly.
- Adjusted token refill smoothing on staging (simulated): smoother refill reduced peak 429s but increased tail latency slightly.
Actions taken:
- Requested SRE to whitelist short-term traffic exemption window for ScoutMetrics nightly sweep (pending approval via INT-5512).
- Requested autoscaler team to inspect warmup behavior for pool-ussc-07 (links to INT-5512).
- Drafted recommended client changes to customer: enable connection pooling at a worker-pool level instead of per-process multiplexing, add jitter to job start times, and increase per-request retry jitter/backoff to avoid synchronized retries.
2026-03-12 15:10 - Temporary mitigation: SRE applied temporary 15% burst allowance increase for pool-ussc-07 during 02:00-04:30 UTC sweep window. This reduced 429s to ~6% on next sweep (per customer report). See INT-5512 for audit trail.
Recommended long-term fixes provided to customer:
1) Client-side: change from per-process HTTP/2 multiplexing to a shared connection pool per worker-group, add randomized start jitter (0-90s) to sweep windows, and implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries.
2) Platform-side: modify token_bucket smoothing parameter for dedicated pools with high short-interval burst patterns; consider a dedicated burst credit for scheduled batch windows.
3) Ops: autoscaler warmup tuning for pool-ussc-07 to avoid transient capacity loss during recurring scale events.
Follow-ups / open work:
- INT-5512 assigned to autoscaler/SRE to root-cause warmup behavior and implement safe warmup adjustments (owner: Leila Gomez).
- Engineering ticket requested to evaluate gateway token accounting for multiplexed HTTP/2 sessions (linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/412).
- Customer agreed to deploy client changes and share next run logs; Support will monitor two sweep windows then close the ticket if errors remain below 5%.
Status: Monitoring (Support will close after two successful sweep windows with <5% 429s).
payload.summary: Sawtooth throttling pattern during customer daily batch sweep causing intermittent 429s

Issue summary: During a planned weighted canary cutover for redwood-v2-medium -> redwood-v2-quantized at ~2026-03-13T18:22Z, approximately 7% of Finato Bank's tenant cohort (cohort id c-88ff) that should have been routed to the canary variant was instead routed to the legacy variant pinned from a previous rollout. Impact: mixed-model responses, higher than expected token costs, and a small number of failing structured outputs for validation prompts. Severity: customer-visible degradation (inconsistent outputs) and billing spike.

Observed behaviour: traffic that matched the pin cohort showed two routing fingerprints in edge logs; a subset of requests carried a routing cookie keyed to legacy-variant-id=rv2-2025-11 while orchestration snapshots indicated the cohort should map to rv2-q1. The routing mesh appears to have merged cohort metadata during a snapshot reconcile operation which coalesced two nearby cohort keys into a single pin entry pointing at the older variant.

Expected behaviour: cohort pins created during the cutover should be isolated per rollout slice; no cross-cohort coalescence should occur.

Impact summary: - ~7% of customer sessions experienced mixed responses for ~45 minutes. - Token spend for the customer spiked by ~18% during the window (billing alert). - No requests returned 5xx, but semantic/regression failures observed on validation set used by Finato.

Quick links: - PagerDuty: PD-RED-2331 - Dashboard (cost & cohort routing): https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/rollouts/finato-cohort-424242 - Edge logs slice: https://logs.redwood.internal/q?id=cohort:c-88ff
1) Trigger a staged weighted cutover: increase canary weight for model redwood-v2-quantized from 0% to 20% over 5 min using the standard rollout controller
2) Observe orchestrator snapshot updates in /orchestrator/snapshots for the tenant route (route: finato/transactions)
3) Inspect edge routing cookies and routing-mesh lookup for cohort id c-88ff during each snapshot commit
4) Compare routing-mesh cohort table pre/post-commit to detect any coalesced entries
2026-03-13T18:22:12Z orchestrator INFO snapshot-commit id=ss-9901 merging 2 cohort-entries (keys: hash=0x7a3b,0x7a3c) -> resulting entry pinned_to=rv2-2025-11
2026-03-13T18:22:15Z edge WARN route-lookup tenant=finato cohort=c-88ff resolved_variant=rv2-2025-11 (expected rv2-q1)
Router trace: route_cohort_lookup(route=finato/transactions, cohort_key=0x7a3c) -> entry_index=442 -> variant=rv2-2025-11
Cost alert: billing-service spike event id=BS-8892 customer=Finato Bank delta=+18% tokens over baseline (window 18:20-19:05)
Sample request trace: curl -H 'X-Tenant: finato' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> request_id=acb-3389 -> routed_variant=rv2-2025-11 -> model_output deviates on known regression prompt
2026-03-13 18:30 - Support (Ava): Acknowledged. Opening for SRE and Rollouts. Notified customer that we are investigating and temporarily paused weight increases.
2026-03-13 18:38 - Customer (Finato - Priya R.): We are seeing inconsistent outputs on validation calls; please advise. We've put a hold on critical workflows.
2026-03-13 18:46 - SRE (Diego): Observed snapshot merge in orchestrator logs that merged adjacent cohort keys; capturing dump of cohort table and rolling back weight to previous stable state. Temporary mitigation applied: reverted canary weight to 3% and forced cohort remap.
2026-03-13 19:05 - Eng (R&D - Jonas P.): Hypothesis: hash-bucket collision in snapshot-merge optimizer when commit contains contiguous cohort boundaries. Adding debug flags to snapshot commit to preserve separate entries. Preparing small patch to prevent coalescence on identical prefix hashes.
2026-03-14 09:12 - Support (Ava): Customer accepted temporary rollback and confirmed reduced inconsistency. Scheduling follow-up to validate patch in staging with synthetic cohort adjacency tests.
2026-03-14 11:00 - Customer (Priya): Thank you. Please keep us updated on root cause and fix ETA.
Initial hypothesis: edge cookie rewrite or cookie domain rotation evicted pin for cohort leading to fallback. Evidence: NOT supported — cookies persisted for affected requests.
Found orchestrator snapshot-commit log lines showing 'merging 2 cohort-entries' at the same timestamp as customer errors. The merge routine is intended to collapse redundant adjacent entries but appears to have an off-by-one collision when cohorts share a high-byte hash prefix.
Replaying snapshot commit in staging reproduced coalescence when two cohorts had adjacent hash keys (0x7a3b and 0x7a3c) and target variants differed. The merge took the lower-index variant as authoritative (rv2-2025-11).
Edge routing mesh respects orchestrator cohort table; once orchestrator commit contained the coalesced entry, edge routing immediately began resolving to legacy variant for the merged key range.
No evidence of orchestrator leader election or snapshot rollback during window — single-leader commit path used. No related resource exhaustion observed on orchestrator nodes.
Temporary mitigation applied: force-snapshot-abort and staged revert of commit + manual cohort re-insert for c-88ff with explicit pin to rv2-q1; proceeded to lower canary weight and observe traffic.
Patch under review: change 'collapsibleEntry' logic to verify variant equality before merge; if variants differ, create explicit boundary entry. Unit tests and staging run scheduled.
Risk: identical issue could occur on other tenants with adjacent cohort keying. Running batch scan for contiguous cohort key pairs across active rollouts in prod to identify candidates (query created).
Follow-ups: add snapshot-commit audit field to retain original cohort mapping for 24h to allow fast rollback when coalescence occurs.
Workaround/mitigation: Reverted canary weight to previous stable level (3%) and manually reinserted explicit cohort pin for c-88ff pointing to rv2-q1. Patch: small change to orchestrator snapshot merge that prevents collapsing entries when target variants differ (PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4938). Post-deploy actions: run bulk adjacency scan, add integration test that simulates adjacent-cohort cutover, and add alerting on 'snapshot-commit merges' that touch >1 variant. Customer follow-up: Finato Bank validated that outputs returned to expected cohort behavior after manual remap; billing team issued credit for the excess token spend. Planned permanent fix scheduled for next release window (2026-03-17).
payload.summary: Pinned cohort unexpectedly coalesced onto legacy variant during weighted canary cutover, causing mixed outputs and cost spike

Issue summary:
Customer BrightMind Analytics reports a negative invoice line (-$1,124.35) on the finalized invoice for billing period 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28. The negative line appears tied to a multi-model batch job that used two models with negotiated per-model overrides plus a month-end promotional credit. The customer expected per-model negotiated rates to apply and a prorated promotional credit to reduce the invoice total; they did not expect a standalone negative line item on the finalized invoice.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: billing team at BrightMind sees an unexplained negative line and requested immediate clarification before autopay.
- Financial: final invoice total differs from console estimate by -$1,124.35. Customer has paused autopay pending explanation.

Environment:
- Production (us-east primary, eu-west fallback)
- Customer account: org-id: org_brightmind_94
- Job: nightly multi-model batch (batch id: bm-2026-02-26-373) that invoked both redwood/open-3b-quant and redwood/optim-7b across two regions for redundancy

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run same nightly multi-model batch with same model pins and routing policy (primary us-east, fallback eu-west).
2) Check Console -> Billing Estimate during/after run.
3) Wait until postback reconciler processes usage window and final invoice generation completes.

Attached logs/ids (from customer):
- Invoice id: INV-2026-02-94-BM
- Negative line id: INV-2026-02-94-BM-LN-07
- Usage postbacks: pb-89124, pb-89125, pb-89130 (staging->prod replay noted)
- Batch job id: bm-2026-02-26-373
- Slack thread: #support-brightmind (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C07BRIGHT/FF12345678)

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - SRE (Mina Ortega): Noted there was a postback replay from a decommissioned staging proxy (pb-89130) at 02:12 UTC on 2026-02-27. That replay may have been deduplicated at estimate-time but reconciled in final run, causing a corrective offset. Adding to investigation.
Hypothesis 1: Promotional org-level credit applied after reserved-rate reconciliation and smoothing produced a negative line to preserve per-line accounting semantics.
Hypothesis 2: Postback replay (pb-89130) from staging proxy was initially filtered in console estimates but applied during final invoice reconciler; reconciler applied negotiated per-model override to the original usage, then applied org-level promo credit separately, resulting in double-application for the same usage volume across two line items, netting a negative line.
Data pulled: invoice lines export, postback timeline (pb-89124..pb-89130), per-model rate override table for org_brightmind_94, promo-credit allocation log (promo-2026-feb-1).
Observed: per-model override correctly listed at time of estimate. Promo credit was queued for prorated application on 2026-02-28 23:59 UTC. Postback replay was ingested 2026-02-27 02:12 UTC which is before promo allocation time; however reconciler reordering during smoothing window applied credits after dedup step causing mis-ordered adjustments.
Preliminary conclusion: ordering bug in final reconciler where credit application happens after per-line reserved-rate reconciliation and dedup offset application. The implemention wrote a negative balancing line to keep total sums accurate when credits exceed a specific line's post-dedup delta, instead of redistributing proportionately across lines.
Risk: Other enterprise customers using per-model negotiated rates plus org-level promos and run multi-region multi-model batches at month-end may see similar negative lines or misattributed credits.
(Liam) Confirm exact reconciler code path that produces negative balancing lines and capture commit/PR that last modified ordering (target: 2026-03-13 EOD).
(SRE) Correlate pb-89130 ingestion event and reconciler run timestamps; validate whether dedup filter was applied during estimate vs final run (target: 2026-03-12 noon).
(Billing) Draft one-paragraph explainer for customer finance explaining negative line origin and confirm provisional credit policy (target: 2026-03-12 afternoon).
(Support) Offer provisional hold on autopay and an interim credit if we cannot produce resolution within 48 hours. Notify BrightMind contact: finance@brightmind.ai (contact: Julia Park).

payload.description:
Issue summary: After the US DST forward shift (2026-03-14 in some regions) several enterprise customers reported missing and spurious alert notifications from composite dashboard panels (multi-query alert rules).

Impact: Nimbus Payments reports missed fraud-alerting notifications during a 2-hour window; they saw both an absence of expected alerts and duplicate firing shortly after. Multiple orgs in us-east showed temporal mismatches between trace-linked spans and alert evaluation windows.

Environment: production, affected regions us-east primarily with some spillover in eu-west where org timezone settings are non-UTC. Reported after recent timezone-service v2.4 rollout.

Observed behavior: Composite alerts that combine multiple panel queries using relative variables (eg. ${dashboard.time.start}, ${org.timezone_shift}) evaluated against server-local time boundaries, but dashboard variable interpolation for panel display used the org-configured timezone. The mismatch causes the alert-eval engine to construct an evaluation window that is offset by one hour in DST transitions, which in turn mis-buckets metric rollups and misattributes trace anchors.

Quick notes: This is not a general ingestion or rollup lag — single-panel alerts evaluated correctly when pinned to UTC or when not using dashboard variables. The problem manifests when: composite alert rules reference interpolated dashboard variables AND the org timezone differs from server-local time during DST boundary crossing.
1) Create a dashboard with org timezone set to America/New_York
2) Add two panels: A) 1-min rate of error responses, B) 5-min p50 latency; each panel displays using ${dashboard.time.start} relative variables
3) Create a composite alert that triggers when A > 0.5 AND B > 300 using the dashboard variables for the evaluation window
4) Simulate traffic across the DST-forward boundary (advance system clock for a test node or run synthetic job spanning the boundary),
5) Observe alerting history: missing alert during the boundary hour then duplicate alerts once server-local eval aligns back
6) Compare single-panel alert with equivalent absolute window (no variables) — it evaluates correctly.

2026-03-12T15:07:13Z INFO dashboard: variable_interpolation: dashboard.time.start='-5m' substituted_as='2026-03-14T01:00:00'

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a sharp increase in p99 latency and intermittent request timeouts on repeat prompts (identical prompt used multiple times). Impact: multiple user-facing timeouts (504) and elevated p99 token latency for SynthHealth's dedicated pool impacting their QA automation runs. Environment: Dedicated cluster for SynthHealth in us-east running text-gen-7B. Timeline: problem started 2026-03-10 15:20 UTC after a scheduled shard rebalance window.

Observed behavior: Identical prompts that previously returned in <200ms are now hitting 2s+ p99 and occasionally timing out (504). Issue appears to affect only identical/hot prompt patterns (high reuse of same prefix). Non-repeated varied prompts unaffected.

Expected behavior: Prefix/KV cache should serve warm hot keys with sub-200ms token latency once warmed.

Customer QA pipelines experiencing 20-40% test failures due to 504s; synthesis jobs delayed; customer escalation to account team. Business impact: blocking critical integration tests for SynthHealth release candidate.
1) Use SynthHealth's dedicated endpoint with a repeated short prompt (e.g., 'Summarize patient note: ...' same text repeated).
2) Send burst of 50 identical requests concurrently.
3) Observe p99 token latency and failures in tracing for warmup phase.
4) Compare behavior vs varied prompts (no issue).
Excerpt from request traces (us-east cluster):
 - Trace 2026-03-10T15:22:03Z: serve_request -> kv_prefix_lookup -> miss -> fetch_shard(sha=0x9f4a) -> fetch_backoff -> 504 after 2.5s
 - Agent logs: kvcache: shard 12 warmup_in_progress=true, inflight_warmups=48, active_replica_count=1
 - Scheduler: rebalance completed 2026-03-10T15:10 UTC, moved shards 10-14 between nodes node-ef12 -> node-fa33
 - SRE metrics: kvcache_eviction_rate spiked +320% at 15:11 UTC

Initial findings:
- Correlation between the rebalance window and onset of errors.
- Hot keys (highly repeated prefixes) concentrated onto a single shard replica that was briefly under-replicated during rebalance, causing warmup thundering herd when many identical requests hit.
- kvcache warmup queuing appears limited by per-shard warmup concurrency default (max 16), but queuing plus synchronous cold fetches produced serialized KV reads and long tails.
- Observed LRU churn: eviction_rate high leading to repeated cold reads for same prefix across worker processes.
- Client-side: SynthHealth uses very high retry (3 immediate retries) which amplified load during warmup.

Hypothesis: rebalance left a shard with only one replica accepting traffic while background warmup tasks were still initializing; combined with high concurrency on identical prefixes produced serialized blocking cold reads, leading to p99 token latency and 504s.

- Scoped traffic: temporarily routed SynthHealth traffic to a fallback replica set with pre-warmed shards (2026-03-10T16:05 UTC).
- Increased kvcache warmup concurrency for affected shard as mitigation (2026-03-10T16:20 UTC) and disabled aggressive LRU during warmup phase.
- Asked customer to reduce client retry aggressiveness as interim workaround.
- Eng created draft PR to add per-shard adaptive warmup concurrency and a short 'grace' replication window during rebalance (PR linked).
Route affected customer to prewarmed fallback pool OR reduce client-side immediate retries; restarting affected serving nodes also restored normal behavior for small windows. Customers with dedicated pools: schedule rebalance during off-hours and pre-warm hot prefixes ahead of cutover.
In Progress - temporary mitigations applied reduced 504s to <1% for SynthHealth but p99 still elevated during heavy bursts. Engineering to deploy adaptive warmup and rebalance grace window in next patch. Post-deployment: monitor for 48 hours then close.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 16:30 - SynthHealth (customer): Reported reduction in errors after temporary routing, requested ETA for permanent fix; flagged as release blocker.
payload.summary: Prefix cache shard degradation on hot keys leading to repeat-prompt timeouts

Issue summary: After onboarding AtlasFin's private deployment to Redwood Private (VPC) and enabling OIDC SSO, users intermittently received 403 Forbidden when calling the Redwood API despite successful login through the IdP. Impact: ~12 users across two teams could not access model endpoints. Error observed in production, intermittent depending on which IdP assertion was returned. Environment: Private control plane (v1.11.0), identity-proxy v1.12.0 (private deployment bundle), AtlasFin IdP: Okta (custom claim mapping), region us-east-1. Observed behavior: Some authenticated requests fail RBAC checks because the subject used for role binding lookup differs from the subject in user directory/role mappings. Expected behavior: Identity claims used to match RBAC bindings should be normalized consistently so that authenticated users inherit their expected roles. Root cause hypothesis: A mismatch between IdP-provided email claim casing/alternate-email claim and existing RBAC bindings that contain case-sensitive email strings. Recent identity-proxy change (2026-02 release) introduced an email normalization step that lowercases and strips plus-addressing, but AtlasFin's SCIM-provisioned role bindings were created earlier and contain original-cased primaryEmail entries.
1) AtlasFin user authenticates via Okta (OIDC) using standard browser SSO flow.
2) Okta returns ID token with claims: email: "alice.senior@atlasfin.com", alternate_email: "Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com" and preferred_username: "asenior".
3) identity-proxy processes the token and applies email normalization (lowercase + strip +tag).
4) Redwood authorization layer looks up role bindings using the normalized email (alice.senior@atlasfin.com) but AtlasFin role bindings were provisioned with SCIM and store the original-cased PrimaryEmail (Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com).
5) Authorization lookup fails and request returns 403 despite successful authentication.
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z identity-proxy INFO received id_token for sub=okta|00u123...
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z identity-proxy DEBUG incoming_claims: {"email":"alice.senior@atlasfin.com", "alternate_email":"Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com"}
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z identity-proxy INFO normalized_email=alice.senior@atlasfin.com
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z auth-service WARN rbac_lookup no binding found for principal=alice.senior@atlasfin.com
2026-03-10T09:12:04Z api-gateway ERROR request_id=abc123 status=403 message=RBAC: no principal binding
03/10 11:00 - Support (Aisha): Confirmed failing user tokens and collected sample IdTokens and SCIM record for the user.
03/10 12:10 - Eng (Diego): Reproduced locally by replaying token; observed that role lookup key depends on identity-proxy normalized email when preferred_username absent.
03/10 14:30 - SRE: Checked private control plane release notes and found email normalization behavior changed in identity-proxy v1.12.0 (commit 7f8b2c).
03/10 16:00 - Hypothesis: Older SCIM-upserted role bindings use the original-cased PrimaryEmail; normalization lowercases and removes plus-tags, causing a mismatch. The presence of alternate_email claim increases the mismatch window because SCIM used 'PrimaryEmail' while IdP issued 'email' in a different case.
03/11 09:00 - Reproduction: Updated local rbac store to include both 'Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com' and 'alice.senior@atlasfin.com' and confirmed access is restored. This indicates the lookup key mismatch is the problem.
03/11 10:20 - Mitigation plan: 1) Patch identity-proxy to include canonicalization that preserves case when SCIM-provisioned role bindings are detected, 2) provide a migration tool to normalize the customer's role bindings in-place, 3) short-term workaround to add duplicate normalized entries via support script.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10T15:45 - AtlasFin (Customer): Provided confirmation that SCIM provisioning created PrimaryEmail with uppercase letters historically; they cannot re-provision roles immediately.
2026-03-11T09:45 - SRE (Maya Singh): Pulled control plane logs and confirmed identity-proxy normalized email; no evidence of downstream caching issues. Shared relevant log snippets above.
2026-03-12T08:20 - Support (Aisha): Applied short-term fix: ran support migration script to add normalized duplicates for affected role bindings. Customer confirms users regained access. Marking ticket resolved pending follow-up migration + config change in customer's private bundle.
Applied multi-step resolution: (1) Deployed identity-proxy compatibility patch (v1.12.1) to the customer's private control plane which adds an option to detect SCIM-provisioned role bindings and preserve original-case keys when performing RBAC lookups. (2) Ran an on-demand migration script to add normalized duplicate keys for existing role bindings (script run: tools/migrate/normalize-rolebindings-2026-03-11.sh). (3) Documented recommended long-term fix: AtlasFin to enable SCIM canonicalization (lowercase) or reprovision roles; Redwood to offer automated normalization in the next maintenance window. Post-fix verification: confirmed 12 affected users regained access and downstream automated jobs resumed successfully. Follow-up action: INT-4452 created to add an opt-in config flag to the Private bundle and to backfill affected customers during next quarterly update.
payload.summary: IdP email claim normalization mismatch causing RBAC 403s in AtlasFin private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports a sudden reallocation of usage (daily metering) across three internal projects on their consolidated invoice for 2026-03-08. Usage that historically billed to project-prod-usa has appeared as billed to project-data-poc and project-internal-tests, triggering an unexpected overage on the consolidated invoice and breaking cost-center accounting.

Observed behavior / Timeline:
- 2026-03-08 00:00 - 08:00 UTC: multiple large batch embedding jobs run from BrightCart's orchestration cluster.
- 2026-03-08 09:12 UTC: customer notices unexplained spike on Console usage page; support ticket opened.
- 2026-03-08 10:00 UTC: customer exported per-project usage CSV and found token counts redistributed between project IDs.
- 2026-03-08 14:30 UTC: engineering initial triage observed reorder of postbacks during a reconciliation job backfill executed 2026-03-08 01:40 UTC.

Impact:
- Overcharge of approximately $5,900 on consolidated invoice for billing day 2026-03-08.
- Internal chargeback mismatches for three Cost Centers at BrightCart (finance needs retroactive correction).
- Customer unable to reconcile budgets; requested provisional credit and root cause explanation for auditors.

Environment:
prod | us-east-1
Redwood components involved: metering-postback-reconciler, hourly-aggregator, billing-tag-mapper
Affected models: text-embed-512, text-qa-2b (in mixed-job batches)

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Schedule a mixed-model batch embed job from BrightCart orchestration using api key tied to project-prod-usa at 2026-03-08 00:10 UTC.
2) Trigger a metadata tag migration on the org that renames some api-key tags to new project prefixes during the same billing window.
3) Run a manual reconciler backfill job for legacy postbacks (the backfill was run 2026-03-08 01:40 UTC in this incident).
4) Observe hourly-aggregator outputs and consolidated invoice; token counts appear split across projects rather than attributed to original project-prod-usa.
5) Export Console per-project usage for 2026-03-08 and compare CSVs before and after backfill; differences reproduce the redistribution in our environment replica.
Initial findings:
- Postback ordering during the backfill appears to have re-applied a tag remapping table that was mid-migration. The billing-tag-mapper accepted both old and new prefixes during reconciliation, leading to split attribution for identical usage fingerprints.
- Logs from metering-postback-reconciler show duplicate acknowledgements for a subset of postbacks (IDs in logs around 2026-03-08T01:42Z).
- Hourly-aggregator committed intermediate windows with mixed project tags before the backfill completed, creating persistent downstream ledger entries.
- No invoice-line level rounding or currency conversion faults observed; root cause looks like tag reclassification race during backfill.

Hypothesis: a backfill + tag-migration race caused deterministic but inconsistent mapping for postbacks emitted in the same hourly window. The reconciler's idempotency key logic allowed re-attribution when encountering postbacks with updated tags instead of merging to the original attribution.

Preliminary mitigation applied 2026-03-10 15:20 UTC: disabled the legacy-backfill job queue for org-level tag operations and forced a consistency pass to re-merge hourly windows for 2026-03-08. Re-merge job shows candidate correction but requires finance approval before issuing provisional credits.

BrightCart requests: 1) provisional credit equal to the overcharged amount ($5,900) applied to their account while we complete re-merge; 2) a clear root-cause writeup for auditors including timeline and steps we will take to prevent recurrence; 3) confirmation of any action required on their side (no changes planned).
Workarounds:
- Customer should not run tag-migration backfills during hourly-billing windows until reconciler fix deploy.
- For immediate relief we've offered a provisional credit pending final re-merge and finance approval.

Next steps (owned by teams):
- Billing team to approve provisional credit (Finance ticket required).
- Metering team to deploy a reconciler patch that enforces idempotent attribution by locking original attribution key during backfills (PR referenced above).
- SRE to run full re-merge for 2026-03-08 and validate ledger parity with pre-backfill snapshots.
- Postmortem and runbook update to prevent backfill/tag-change concurrency in billing windows.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 provisional credit of $5,900 applied to BrightCart account as a temporary hold. Final ledger adjustment to post after SRE re-merge validates parity. Metering team PR merged to enforce attribution idempotency; runbook updated to block backfills during billing windows. Finance will publish final credit and adjusted invoice upon completion.
payload.summary: Unexpected redistribution of daily metering across projects causing overcharge on consolidated invoice

payload.description:
Issue summary:
NovaAnalytics reports that scheduled background workers began failing with 403s when calling Redwood Private admin APIs after their internal STS rotation. Impact: dozens of scheduled jobs failing across environments, customer unable to run nightly ingestion.

Impact:
- Customer production scheduled workers returning 403 on admin/model endpoints.
- Jobs retried, causing backlog and higher cost.
- Affects all workers that use service tokens issued by customer's STS.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (on-prem bundle v1.6.2) deployed in NovaAnalytics datacenter (prod-us-east).
- Identity stack: internal STS -> ingress-proxy -> redwood identity-proxy -> private control plane.
- Auth scheme: bearer token with JWT including custom "realm" claim used by customer's RBAC mapping.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Obtain service token from customer's STS for job-runner service account (token contains claim: "realm": "edge/analytics").
2) POST to /v1/admin/models with Authorization: Bearer <token>.
3) Observe 403 response.

Observed behavior:
- Redwood returns 403 with message: "access denied: no matching role bindings for principal".
- Identity-proxy logs show claim parsing step: logged claim value truncated to "edge", roles not resolved.
- Customer's STS started emitting realm values with forward-slash (/) as part of namespace after recent rotation. Previously used hyphens only.

Expected behavior:
- RBAC claim parser should accept arbitrary UTF-8 in realm claim and treat it atomically (not split on '/'), or at a minimum provide configurable claim delimiter rules.

Relevant logs (redacted):
- identity-proxy: "parsed_claims={\"sub\":\"svc-jobrunner\",\"realm\":\"edge\"}"
- auth-service: "role_bindings_lookup: principal=svc-jobrunner@edge -> bindings=[]"
- customer-proxy-ingress: "received original-claim: realm=edge/analytics"

Temporary workaround provided:
- Instructed customer to update token transformation rule on their ingress-proxy to URL-encode '/' in realm claims (produces realm=edge%2Fanalytics). This allows Redwood parser to treat it as single token.

Customer notes:
- Change was low-impact and applied successfully; jobs resumed within ~20 minutes after proxy change.

Work requested from Redwood:
- Patch to identity-proxy/runtime to avoid splitting on '/' and to accept raw claim strings for role lookup OR documentation on claim normalization behavior and recommended proxy transforms.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:05 NovaAnalytics (Customer): Provided sample JWT (redacted) and said new STS release added hierarchical realm claims like 'edge/analytics' for multi-tenant separation.
2026-03-13 09:00 NovaAnalytics (Customer): Confirming they are happy to wait for scheduled upgrade; noted workaround is acceptable for now. Thank you for fast support.
Hypothesis: claim parser in identity-proxy used a sanitizer that split claim values on certain punctuation (including '/'), treating left-most token as tenant namespace. Verified by adding token with 'edge/analytics' and observing normalized value 'edge'. Traced code to claims_normalizer.go where splitter regex included '/'. Local fix: relax splitter to only break on whitespace and control characters, preserve punctuation. Added tests for URL-encoded and raw slashes. INT-4421 created to track further canonicalization work and config flag for legacy behavior.
Root cause: identity-proxy claim normalization split on '/' and dropped namespace suffix causing RBAC lookup miss. Temporary workaround: URL-encode '/' in upstream STS/ingress tokens. Permanent fix: merged runtime PR to stop splitting on '/' and added config flag to enable legacy splitting if customers depend on it. Release plan: include fix in private bundle v1.6.4 with migration notes. Customer confirmed jobs resumed after workaround; will validate again post-upgrade. Full rollout notes: backport to 1.6.x branch, run integration tests against existing private deployments, provide config migration steps in confluence page.
Add claim-normalization behavior documentation to Private deployment guide
Backport fix to 1.6.x and schedule non-breaking release for private customers
Add e2e tests for non-alphanumeric claim values (slashes, dots, percent-encodings)
Expose claim parsing mode as toggle in private config for compatibility
payload.summary: Private: scheduled-worker service tokens receive 403 after STS realm claim contains slash

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a guaranteed-ordered, timezone-normalized NDJSON audit stream suitable for Sumo Logic HTTP source ingestion. Requirements: deterministic event UUIDs (so identical logical events produce identical ids across retries), per-event HMAC signature header with key-rotation guidance, and UTC canonicalization of timestamps. This is intended as evidence for an upcoming security audit and to support forensic replayability across their SIEM.

Impact:
- Greenline cannot complete their SIEM onboarding without a reproducible schema and an example ingest configuration.
- They require per-event HMAC verification for tamper-evidence and a signed sample dataset for audit submission.

Environment:
- Customer production account ingest (Greenline-prod) -> Redwood audit webhook -> Sumo Logic HTTP collector (us1.sumologic.com). Region: us-east-1.

Requested deliverables (customer-facing):
1) NDJSON field schema document (canonical field names, required/optional fields, types).
2) Deterministic event_id algorithm spec (namespace + monotonic counter + canonical timestamp) with pseudo-code.
3) Per-event HMAC header spec (header name, algorithm, canonical string-to-sign, example HMAC value, KMS rotation guidance).
4) Sumo Logic HTTP Source example config (headers, content-type, recommended batch sizes, retry semantics).
5) Small signed sample dataset (100 events) and a verification script the customer can run locally.
6) Minimal transformation examples (jq and a lightweight Node script) to map Redwood fields to Sumo-friendly fields.

Steps to reproduce / verification steps requested by customer:
1) Provide sample NDJSON file and collector config.
2) Instruct customer to POST sample to their Sumo HTTP source and verify arrival and order.
3) Run provided verification script to validate deterministic event_id collisions and HMAC signatures.
4) Confirm timestamps normalized to UTC and monotonic sequence where expected.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sumo Logic team confirms events arrive and are queryable with original event_id values preserved.
- Verification script returns PASS for HMAC and timestamp canonicalization.
- Documentation includes clear KMS rotation procedure and recommended retention for verification artifacts.

Logs / evidence provided by customer:
- Example of failed ingestion attempt (HTTP 400) with request/response payloads attached to initial message.
- Screenshot of Sumo showing partial parse failures (field extraction mismatches).

Notes on security posture requested:
- Customer explicitly requests HMAC using SHA-256 and wants guidance on rotating signing keys monthly with a signed key manifest.
- They want per-tenant envelope separation (tenant_id in both payload and envelope header).
2026-03-14: Initial triage by Mateo. Quick spike shows Redwood can emit canonical timestamps (ISO-8601 UTC). Deterministic id approach validated in prototype: event_id = sha256(namespace||'|'||pad(counter)||'|'||timestamp_iso8601) encoded as hex. HMAC proposal: use HMAC-SHA256 over canonical JSON string with header 'X-Redwood-HMAC'. Key management options: a) customer-managed KMS (recommended for enterprise) with monthly rotation manifest; b) Redwood-managed signing key with rotation window configurable. No backend changes required to basic schema export; we will produce sample transforms and verification tooling.

Open questions / blockers:
- Customer asks for per-event nonce in addition to deterministic id to prevent replay attacks; needs guidance about trade-offs between determinism and replay protection.
- Confirm whether customer will use Redwood-managed KMS or provide external KMS endpoint.

Work plan / next steps:
- Produce NDJSON schema and event_id/HMAC spec (owner: Mateo) by 2026-03-15.
- Generate 100-event sample and verification script (owner: Support Tools) by 2026-03-16.
- Provide Sumo example and transform snippets; schedule a 1-hour call to validate integration (calendar invite pending).
payload.summary: Timezone-normalized audit stream with deterministic event UUIDs and per-event HMAC for Sumo Logic ingest

Issue summary:
During a scheduled keystore rotation in prod us-east on 2026-03-13 15:40 UTC, we observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses from the API gateway. Investigation indicates multiple downstream serving runtime processes terminated with SIGABRT shortly after the keystore swap, causing elevated error rate and client request failures.

Impact:
- ~12% error rate increase across affected routes for ~18 minutes.
- Several enterprise customers (including AcmeCloud) reported failed streaming and generation requests.
- Automated retries caused additional load and exacerbated upstream failures.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (us-east-1)
- API Gateway version: apigw-v2.14.1
- Serving runtime: runtime-v1.86 (NVIDIA accel nodes)
- Keystore service: vault-rotator-v0.9

Observed behavior:
- Keystore rotation completed at 15:40 UTC. 15:41:10 UTC first SIGABRT observed in runtime-worker-12. Within 2 minutes 8 runtime workers crashed in rapid succession. API Gateway began returning 502/503s and 504s for in-flight requests.
- Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/streams. Non-streaming small-embed endpoints saw degradation but less severe.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Rolled back keystore to previous version (15:48 UTC) and paused automated rotations.
- Temporarily increased graceful restart window on serving runtime to avoid simultaneous process exit.
- Put affected customers on dedicated fallback routes to minimize impact while we investigate.
1) Trigger keystore rotation in prod-us-east using vault-rotator staged rollout (canary=false).
2) Observe serving runtime worker processes during rotation with process supervision logging enabled.
3) Note sudden SIGABRTs in runtimes with stack traces referencing libcrypto and keystore client handshake code.
4) API Gateway /v1/generate starts returning 502/503 within first 90s of rotation if multiple runtimes restart concurrently.
