payload.description:
Issue summary
- Customer (Vidorama) reports sustained throughput below their Dedicated committed floor in us-east.
- Symptoms observed over multiple hours (not a transient warmup dip).

Customer impact
- Production inference throughput ~25–35% below expected; customer reports request queueing and elevated end-user latency.
- Customer states they are operating within agreed model/version + context constraints and not exceeding their committed concurrency guidance.

Environment
- Deployment: ded-vidorama-ue1-17 (Dedicated)
- Region: us-east
- Route: /v1/chat/completions (streaming enabled)
- Model pinned: llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Workload shape (per customer): steady-state concurrency 24–40; input ~600–1,000 tokens; output ~150–300 tokens

Expected vs observed
- Expected: meet or exceed committed throughput floor (per Dedicated order form; customer quoting “committed tokens/sec”) during steady state after warmup.
- Observed: throughput plateauing around ~5.5k–6.2k tok/s (aggregate deployment output tokens/sec) for extended windows; intermittent dips to ~4.8k tok/s.

Time window (customer)
- First noticed: 2025-02-26 ~18:00 UTC
- Reported to Support: 2025-02-27 09:12 UTC

Initial triage notes
- Confirmed this is Dedicated deployment traffic (not Hosted) and model is pinned.
- No evidence of customer-side throttling (429s) in gateway logs for the timeframe.
- Preliminary SLO panel indicates elevated burn rate for throughput floor on this deployment.

Dashboards / evidence
- Dedicated Throughput SLO dashboard (internal): panel “Throughput vs Floor (deployment_id=ded-vidorama-ue1-17)” shows sustained under-floor windows.
- Saturation signals: GPU utilization high, queue depth elevated, batcher frequently at max batch tokens, increased prefill time.
- Fleet view showed deployment running with fewer healthy workers than expected for its reserved shape.

Hypothesis (most likely)
- Effective capacity reduction in the dedicated pool (one worker node out / GPU unavailable) causing sustained throughput drop.

Mitigation performed
- Infra migrated the deployment to a healthy reserved pool matching the contracted shape in us-east and restored expected worker count.
- Performed controlled runtime restart to clear degraded worker assignments and rebuild warm caches.
- Monitored for 60 minutes post-migration; throughput stabilized above floor.

Customer communication
- Acknowledged incident, provided ongoing updates during migration window, and requested customer validation after recovery.

Resolution
- Root cause: dedicated pool drift (degraded worker capacity) after an automatic node drain + failed replacement, leaving the deployment under-provisioned for ~14 hours.
- Recovery: moved deployment to spare capacity; replacement fix queued with Fleet.

Follow-ups
- Add/enable alerting on “provisioned worker count < expected for tier/shape” for Dedicated deployments.
- Review change management around node drains for Dedicated pools in us-east; ensure spare capacity availability or proactive customer notice.

Additional notes:
2025-02-27 09:33 UTC — Customer (Vidorama): Provided deployment_id=ded-vidorama-ue1-17. Streaming enabled. Concurrency ~30. Input ~800 tokens, output ~200 tokens. Slow since yesterday ~18:00 UTC. Provided request IDs: req_7d2a… / req_91bf… / req_3a0c…
2025-02-28 03:10 UTC — Customer (Vidorama): Confirmed throughput back to expected and backlog cleared. Streaming responsiveness improved. Thanks.
Customer screenshot: throughput graph showing plateau at ~5.5k tok/s (uploaded in ticket)
Internal snapshot: fleet worker health view for ded-vidorama-ue1-17 (6/8 healthy) (uploaded in ticket)

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent missing top-k results from the reranking endpoint for a subset of queries after a bulk embedding ingest. Impact: missing candidates and long tail latency (p95 for rerank requests increased from 120ms to 1.8s for affected calls).

Impact:
- Clipper Analytics (dedicated tenant) observed a 4% drop in returned candidate counts for /rerank and a correlated p95 latency spike in us-east between 2026-03-11T22:05 and 2026-03-12T03:30 UTC.
- User-visible symptom: search results show fewer items and occasional empty candidate sets for queries that previously returned results.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment in prod-us-east (private overlay).
- Embedding ingest pipeline writes embeddings to object store and then emits an "ingest-commit" marker via the ingest-proxy.
- Reranker uses approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) shards with async refresh when new commits are announced.

Steps to reproduce (from customer reproduction recipe):
1) Perform large embedding backfill (approx 1.2M vectors) into customer's namespace with the ingest tool (batch size 1024, async_commit=true).
2) Immediately run a set of production queries that previously returned stable top-10 candidates.
3) Observe returned candidate counts and latency via the client logs and Redwood Console traces.

Observed behavior:
- Some queries return fewer than expected candidates (0-7 instead of 10) and occasionally return an empty candidate set.
- Rerank p95 latency for affected queries jumps to ~1.8s while p50 remains ~120ms.
- Console traces show rerank service waiting on follower-refresh timeouts and then falling back to a smaller shard set.

Expected behavior:
- After ingest commit, reranker should include new vectors deterministically. Request latency should not spike for stable queries and candidate count should remain stable.

Relevant logs & traces:
- Ingest-proxy logs show commit announcements published at 2026-03-11T22:07:18Z and 2026-03-12T01:44:03Z.
- Reranker traces show a sequence: ANN_SHARD_REFRESH_WAIT -> ANN_PARTIAL_FALLBACK -> RESPOND_WITH_SMALLEST_SET.
- Proxy->reranker handoff occasionally includes a commit_offset that is 1 behind the actual object-store commit timestamp (see ingest-proxy trace id ip-2721-commit-0x7f9).

Attachments: customer-provided curl logs, Console p95 charts, sample query IDs and timestamps.
2026-03-12 09:12 - Support (Maya Patel): Initial triage completed with customer. Collected curl logs, sample query IDs, and timeline. Escalated to infra on-call.
2026-03-12 11:04 - Infra (Jared Collins): Reproduced locally with a small backfill using async_commit. Observed a commit-announce race where the reranker sometimes sees an announce for batch N before all segment metadata for N is available on the follower. Opened hypothesis H1.
2026-03-12 13:27 - Customer (Clipper Analytics SRE - Theo Ramos): Noted that manual refresh (POST /admin/ann/refresh) temporarily restores full results. Provided additional timestamps where empty sets occurred.
2026-03-13 08:55 - Engineering (Lina Chen): Investigating proxy code path. Found that transient gzip compression on the proxy side occasionally truncates the trailing metadata record when commit announcements are piggybacked with batch heartbeats. Working on a repro with compression toggled off.

Additional notes:
Hypothesis H1: Race between ingest commit announcement and final segment metadata write causes reranker to refresh using incomplete shard metadata -> missing vectors.
Hypothesis H2: Compression/truncation in proxy can chop off trailing commit_offset bytes when announcements are coalesced with heartbeats, leading to offset mismatch.
Evidence: Multiple traces show reranker received announce at T but subsequent segment metadata lookup returned 404 for ~120-350ms window. The ingest-proxy log for ip-2721 shows a mismatch between commit_id and object-store HEAD at the same time.
Staging repro: With N=50k vectors and async_commit enabled, disabling proxy gzip eliminated the repro for 10/10 runs. Re-enabling gzip reintroduced the issue in 3/10 runs.
Temporary mitigation: Added 200ms guarded wait in reranker (staging) before accepting announcements. This reduced empty-set rate from 4%->0.3% in duplicates of the customer's workload.
Potential root cause: ingest-proxy coalesces multiple control messages into a single payload to reduce network overhead. When the payload crosses a compression block boundary, the trailing control record (commit_offset) can be truncated on some proxy builds due to a buffer-edge bug introduced in proxy v2.14.6.
Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/789 (buffer-edge fix) currently in review. Monitoring results from a canary build show removal of truncation repros.
Impact tradeoff: Guarded wait adds a small delay for fresh-announce visibility (~200ms) but reduces customer-visible missing candidates. Need evaluation against latency SLOs for the dedicated plan.
In progress: Patch for ingest-proxy buffer handling merged into PR 789; canary deploy scheduled for 2026-03-15 in prod-us-east with feature flag off by default. Temporary reranker guard wait will be rolled back after ingest-proxy fix validated. Postmortem to include code-level test for compressed control-message coalescing and an automated canary that exercises async_commit flows.
Plan: 1) Deploy ingest-proxy fix as canary to 10% of customer's hosts. 2) Monitor Console metrics for empty candidate rate and rerank p95. 3) If stable after 24h, roll out to full cluster and remove temporary guarded wait in reranker. 4) Create regression test in CI that reproduces coalesced compressed control messages.
Follow-ups: update ingest-runbook to include a validation step after large backfills; inform customer SRE when full rollout scheduled.
payload.summary: Async embedding commit offset causing missing top-k candidates and rerank P95 spike

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that for streamed SSE chat responses, the final sentence or punctuation is frequently missing when a user on mobile toggles network quickly (cellular <-> wifi) or app background/foreground happens within ~500ms of stream end. This appears as an incomplete final clause rather than a silent tail; choice metadata (completion end event) may be present but trailing tokens are absent.

Impact:
- Skylark Analytics reports ~8% of streaming completions for a specific mobile-heavy route are truncated, affecting end-user readability and downstream parsing.
- Customer uses Dedicated capacity; multiple customers may be exposed but reported threshold is currently for Skylark's production route.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-nyc-3 (prod us-east), node pool running v2.18.1 of serving runtime.
- Edge: internal edge-proxy for region us-east, HTTP/2 between proxy and API gateway.
- Customer SDK: mobile client using websocket fallback to SSE with reconnect/resume enabled (sdk v1.4.0).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a streaming SSE completion to generate a 6-10 sentence paragraph.
2) Within 200-800ms of the stream finishing, flip network between wifi and cellular or send the app to background and bring it back quickly.
3) Observe the stream end: sometimes the server-sent "end" event fires but the returned text stops mid-sentence or last punctuation is missing.

Observed logs/snippets:
- request_id=rx-7a9c timestamp=2026-03-13T17:03:22.452Z "choice_end" meta_id=ch-44 present, final_tokens_count=0
- edge-proxy: conn=proxy-1829 reset-before-close, upstream status 200, bytes_sent mismatches content-length by 12

Customer-supplied trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/rx-7a9c (restricted access)

Immediate workaround suggested to customer:
- Increase client reconnect-delay to >=1500ms and prefer a short polling fallback for mobile to avoid post-close socket churn.
- For critical parsing, add a server-side finalization check (e.g., confirm completion token) and request a small non-content keepalive to ensure final chunk transmits.

Desired outcome:
- Root cause identified and a permanent fix deployed so rapid client-side socket churn does not suppress trailing tokens or sentence fragments.

Additional context:
- Related but not identical to previous SSE resume truncation tickets; here we see the server emits end metadata but the payload is incomplete. Hypothesis includes edge-proxy half-close handling, HTTP/2 trailing frame drop on quick connection swap, or serving-runtime flush race during KV-cache priming when a follow-up resume arrives.

2026-03-13 18:02 - Support (Ava Chen): Acknowledged, collected traces and initial logs from Skylark. Requested sample client runbook and SDK version. Asked for production request IDs. SLA P1 acknowledged.
2026-03-13 19:10 - SRE (Diego Morales): Reproduced locally with an emulated mobile churn script. Observed that edge-proxy reported a FIN during tail flush, upstream returned 200 but last 8-16 bytes were missing from stream body. Attaching local capture to the ticket. Hypothesis: proxy rebind triggers graceful shutdown before kernel buffer flush completes.
2026-03-13 20:05 - Eng (Priya Nair): Looking into serving-runtime flush logic (v2.18.1). Noted a possible race when final chunk is queued and connection state transitions to half-closed. Adding instrumentation to confirm whether write completion callback occurs before connection state change.
2026-03-14 09:24 - Support (Ava Chen): Provided customer workaround to increase reconnect delay; customer confirmed reduced frequency of truncation in canary test. Customer requests ETA for permanent fix.
2026-03-14 12:47 - Eng (Diego Morales): Preparing a small edge-proxy config change to delay connection teardown by 250ms after detecting in-flight SSE terminal frames. Will roll to staging for 24h canary. If stable, will plan prod rollout next maintenance window.
Findings to date:
- Reproducible with churn script toggling network state within 200-800ms of completion.
- Edge-proxy logs show connection reset events concurrent with the server finalization sequence.
- Serving runtime counters: 'sse_terminal_write_complete' sometimes not incremented for affected requests.
- No 5xx returned; server reports success.
- Suggests a teardown timing window where OS/kernel or proxy drains aren't fully flushed to the socket before connection is torn down.
Hypotheses:
1) Edge-proxy aggressively closes sockets on client reconnect, racing with server flush.
2) HTTP/2 stream lifecycle between proxy and gateway has a race that can drop trailing DATA frames when connection migrates.
3) Serving runtime doesn't block until TLS record fully transmitted in some fast-teardown paths.
Next steps:
- Deploy temporary edge-proxy tweak (delay teardown by 250ms) to staging and monitor tail-loss metric on streaming routes.
- Add verbose write-complete instrumentation in serving runtime on v2.18.2 branch to assert durability of final writes.
- Coordinate with SDK team to add client-side jittered reconnect by default for mobile SDKs to mitigate.
Workaround applied: recommended client reconnect delay increase and edge-proxy teardown delay canary. Engineering change in progress: instrumented flush confirmation and short proxy teardown delay. Will update when PRs land and staging canary completes.
payload.summary: SSE post-churn fragmentation: final sentence missing when client socket rotates quickly on mobile

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated duplicate POSTs to their external callback endpoint when the SDK performs retries after transient network failures. The duplicates correlate with SDK restarts and browser service-worker rehydration.

Impact: Customer is observing duplicated downstream side-effects (duplicate invoice generation) for a subset of streaming funcall flows. Affected tenant is on enterprise plan with private routing to their webhook. This is causing incorrect billing and manual reconciliation.

Environment: Production, us-east region. Customer uses both python backend workers (server-side) and a TS client (browser) that installs a service-worker proxy for offline/resume support. SDK versions: python-sdk@1.14.2, ts-sdk@2.3.0.

Observed timeframe: First reported 2026-03-09 18:40 UTC; recurring across multiple days.

Detailed description: The SDK emits a per-funcall idempotency confirmation token after the service acknowledges a tool/function call. The customer stores that confirmation locally to treat subsequent client replays as already-acknowledged. In their deployment the service-worker cache layer persisted confirmation tokens between client sessions, but did not expire or validate them against the server TTL. When a transient network blip caused the SDK to retry a portion of the request chain after a client restart, the client re-sent a stale confirmation header (previous run's token) while the server had purged the original confirmation entry (TTL expired). Server treated the header as a new confirmation and proceeded to re-emit the webhook to the customer's callback, resulting in duplicate callbacks.

Reproduction steps: See steps_to_reproduce for an exact sequence.

1) Use TS SDK in browser with service-worker proxy that persists idempotency confirmations to IndexedDB.
2) Start a long-running funcall session that triggers an external webhook (tool call) and observe the webhook delivery succeeds once.
3) Let the confirmation TTL on server side expire (short TTL for testing) or restart the client process to simulate a session rehydrate.
4) Simulate a transient network failure that causes the SDK to retry the request chain after rehydration (e.g., disconnect and reconnect the client tab).
5) Observe that the client re-sends the stale confirmation token from IndexedDB; server-side confirmation lookup misses due to TTL; server treats flow as new and re-invokes the external webhook.
6) Verify duplicate side-effect on the customer's webhook endpoint and review request IDs in webhook payloads.
Expected behavior: Server should treat stale client-side cached confirmations as replay and avoid duplicate external webhook delivery, or client should not re-send confirmations that server has purged.
Actual behavior: Duplicate external webhook invocation occurs when client re-sends stale confirmations that no longer match server-side state.
Customer supplied webhook logs and SDK debug logs. Example webhook POSTs show identical payload body but different x-rw-request-id headers: rw-req-20260309-abc123 and rw-req-20260309-abc123-retry. SDK trace shows 'confirmation-token: conf-7f9e' persisted in service-worker storage; server debug shows 'confirmation lookup: not found (expired)'.
Initial triage (Support): Confirmed duplicates map to same funcall flow and originate from client retries following client restart.
Reproduced in our staging with a minimal TS service-worker that persists confirmations to IndexedDB; reproduces within 2-3 retry cycles when server TTL is configured short.
Hypothesis 1: Client persists confirmation tokens across restarts without validating server TTL leading to stale token re-use.
Hypothesis 2: Server-side confirmation TTL/garbage-collection semantics are too aggressive and lack correlation checks when clients present old confirmations.
Logs: server audit shows 'confirmation-accepted' followed by webhook; later 'confirmation-missing' on retry path and webhook re-emitted. No duplicate-dedup index entry present because key expired.
SDK review: ts-sdk@2.3.0 stores confirmation tokens with no server TTL metadata; python-sdk persists to ephemeral memory only (not implicated).
Temporary mitigation validated: Instructing customer to purge service-worker confirmation store prevents duplicates immediately.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:30 UTC - Customer (Acme Health): We've purged service-worker cache and saw no duplicates in the last 8 hours. Would prefer a fix that doesn't require client-side surgery because multiple browser versions are in the wild.
2026-03-12 15:00 UTC - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Customer accepted temporary mitigation (manual purge) and asked for ETA on SDK patch. Assigned to SDK teams to prioritize.
Client-side persistence of idempotency confirmations (service-worker IndexedDB) without awareness of server-side TTL allowed stale tokens to be re-sent after server-side entries were garbage-collected. The server currently accepts confirmation tokens if syntactically valid; when the server had already purged an entry, it treated the presented token as a new confirmation, causing duplicate outbound webhooks.
Customer-side: purge confirmation cache in the service-worker (IndexedDB) and deploy updated client that avoids persisting confirmations longer than session. Server-side temporary mitigation: return 410 when confirmation token is not found and include 'Confirmation-Status: expired' header so SDK can proactively purge stale entries.
Partial mitigation pushed: server now returns 410 for expired confirmation tokens and adds 'Confirmation-Status: expired' header (rolled to canary in us-east on 2026-03-12). TS SDK owners requested to implement handling for 410 to purge local confirmation caches and to add a 'confirmation-ttl' field in future server responses. Customer performed manual purge and confirmed no new duplicates.
Follow-ups:
- SDK TS team to add TTL-aware confirmation storage and purge-on-410 behavior (owner: @lina-chen; PR target: 2026-03-20).
- Add server-side instrumentation to log attempted replays against expired confirmations (owner: Ethan Miller; task ticket INT-3421).
- Update Developer Docs and best-practice guide on client confirmation storage and TTLs (owner: Developer Experience).
payload.summary: Stale client-side confirmation cache causes duplicate external webhook invocations on retry

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a recent regression in perceived inference latency and intermittent request timeouts for streaming responses. The customer is on a Dedicated deployment and uses our official Go and Python SDKs behind an internal gateway. Impact: API calls that previously returned streaming tokens within ~120–200ms now see long tails up to 6–10s or outright 504/ETIMEDOUT for some requests.

Observed behavior:
- Increased end-to-end latency for streaming calls from a subset of customer hosts beginning 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC.
- Spikes of 429/502/504 correlated with client-side retries and connection churn.
- Host-level connection pools show active connections ~= configured max_connections_per_host, while requests queue on the client.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming responses begin delivering tokens within expected latency envelope; client retries/backoff should not serialize requests behind a small connection pool.

Environment:
- Customer: FluxHealth (dedicated)
- Region: us-east (customer Dedicated capacity pool)
- SDKs: go-sdk v1.6.3, python-sdk v2.0.1 (custom wrapper used in production)
- Gateway: Envoy sidecar with connection pooling to Redwood API

Steps to reproduce (customer repro):
1) From a customer host with default go-sdk config (max_connections_per_host=8, max_retries=6, backoff_initial_ms=50, backoff_multiplier=2, no jitter) start 100 concurrent streaming requests to redwood-open-7b-v2.
2) Observe client-side queueing and a subset of requests timing out after 10s.
3) Reduce max_connections_per_host to 4 and repeat — serialization worsens and tail latency increases.

Logs / traces (redacted):
- Client logs show sequences: "request queued (pool exhausted) -> retry immediate -> socket closed -> retry -> request queued" repeatedly.
- Edge gateway (Envoy) logs show connection churn to the API and many HTTP/1.1 connection resets.
- Serving runtime traces show some requests arriving in bursts but no host-side CPU/GPU saturation during observed windows.

Initial hypothesis:
- Customer SDK configuration (high retry count with aggressive backoff multiplier but NO jitter + small connection pool) is leading to synchronized retry attempts that serialize behind the small connection pool. This effectively causes head-of-line blocking and perceived inference timeouts even though the backend is healthy. Envoy TCP connection churn exacerbates the problem by reducing available idle connections.

Customer impact and business context:
- FluxHealth runs interactive clinical-assistant features; long tail latency and timeouts are causing user-facing failures and a degraded product experience. They are on a committed Dedicated plan and have SLA expectations for latency and availability.
2026-03-10 09:15 UTC - Support triage: verified customer stack and observed synthetic reproduction with customer's wrapper.
2026-03-10 11:40 UTC - SRE validated that dedicated pool GPUs show normal utilization and no infra-level throttling during the window.
2026-03-10 14:05 UTC - Reproduced locally by running 200 concurrent streaming requests with SDK config mirroring customer; observed client-side queues and serialized request delivery.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that SSE/WebSocket streaming sessions abruptly close or stop emitting tokens when a client attempts session-resume after a short reconnect window. The pattern appears when client simultaneously retries the last request while the server is processing the final token, leading to a race that leaves the stream in a silent state.

Impact: Multiple FinEdge production customers experience truncated live transcripts in active chats. Business impact: real-time analytics pipelines drop messages; non-critical but high frequency. Estimated ~6% of sessions for this customer over the last 24h.

Environment: prod - us-east; customer is on enterprise plan with session-resume enabled and token-based session IDs.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start a streaming chat (SSE) with long-answer prompt (>800 tokens).
2) Force a short reconnect (simulate flaky mobile/mobile-VPN).
3) Client issues session-resume request within 200-500ms while the original stream still emits final chunks.
4) Client opens a new SSE connection with same session_id and re-sends the last request payload (duplicate request id).
5) Streaming pauses and then connection closes without finalizing generation.

Observed behavior: Stream becomes silent for ~5-30s then connection closed with no final token; no 5xx returned, server logs show request processing complete but no final chunk delivered to resumed connection.

Expected behavior: Session-resume should either (a) gracefully attach to existing in-flight generation and continue emitting tokens to the new connection, or (b) reject resume if in-flight generation finished and deliver final tokens, ensuring at-most-once semantics.

Selected log snippets (redacted):
[2026-03-10T14:22:10.482Z] session-manager: resume-request received session_id=fe-7753 req_id=abc123 client_ip=198.51.100.45
[2026-03-10T14:22:10.489Z] serving-runtime: start-generation model=redwood-1.6b trace=tr-9934 seq_len=820
[2026-03-10T14:22:10.701Z] api-gateway: new-sse-conn session_id=fe-7753 conn_id=conn-981
[2026-03-10T14:22:10.705Z] serving-runtime: final-token-emitted trace=tr-9934 token_idx=819
[2026-03-10T14:22:10.706Z] session-manager: resume-attach attempted conn_id=conn-981 but in-flight mapping still points to conn-977
[2026-03-10T14:22:41.809Z] conn-981: idle-timeout closed (no further data forwarded)

Initial hypothesis: race between session-manager resume attach and serving-runtime finalization; duplicate request IDs cause session-manager to mark generation as completed without flushing buffered final chunks to the resumed connection. Observed that session-manager drops buffered outbound frames when a resume request with identical request_id arrives while the emitter is mid-flush.

Reproduced in internal staging by replaying customer traffic with a short resume window and duplicate request_id: 3/5 attempts reproduce the silent-close. Root-cause candidate: resume path assumes idempotent resumes by request_id but does not reconcile in-flight emitter state, leading to orphaned output frames.

Telemetry: trace tr-9934 shows serving-runtime finished emission but session-manager did not forward last chunk due to atomic swap of connection handle. No 5xx, so no automatic alert fired.

Short term workaround applied for FinEdge: disabled session-resume feature flag for their org (org-id=fe-org-22) to force new sessions on reconnects; customers informed. This reduced recurrence to 0% for the last 6 hours.

Operational mitigation: increased idle-forwarding window to 60s to allow finishing emission to original connection before a resume attach is permitted. Deployed via config rollout to us-east edge nodes.

Temporary mitigation in place (feature-flag off + idle-forwarding window extended). Engineering implemented a server-side dedup/attach patch to session-manager to treat duplicate request_id as idempotent and forward any buffered final chunks to the resumed connection. Patch submitted as PR #4532 and is currently in canary with 10% traffic in us-east. Full rollback plan prepared.

Follow-ups: add an automated test covering resume-while-emitting race; instrument a metric for 'resume-attach-dropped-frames' and add alert; update runbook.
1) Monitor canary for 24h and verify 'resume-attach-dropped-frames' metric at zero for FinEdge traces.
2) If stable, promote PR #4532 to 50% then 100% rollout.
3) Add unit/integration test and include case in nightly regression harness.
4) Postmortem write-up linked to Confluence runbook.

Issue summary:
Customer reports unexpected split of hourly warmup/ reserve credits across two cost-centers and an apparent double-deduction of warmup credits for a series of batch and streaming requests during a short maintenance window.

Impact:
- Customer saw two invoice lines for the same warmup window, attributed to different cost centers.
- Provisional buffer credit was consumed twice leading to a mid-cycle negative provisional balance notification.
- Affects dedicated fallback traffic between us-east and eu-west for BlueWave Analytics (enterprise account).

Environment:
- Production, dedicated pool ID: dp-33-east, fallback region: eu-west.
- Time window observed: 2026-03-10T02:01:00Z to 2026-03-10T02:14:00Z (short rolling maintenance).

Steps to reproduce (customer-facing):
1) Run a mixed batch embed job with scheduled warmup (hourly) tied to cost-center tag A.
2) Trigger a failover to fallback region (canary/fallback routing).
3) Observe invoice/provisional buffer entries in the billing console and final invoice line items.

Observed behavior:
- Two invoice/provisional line items created for the same warmup window, different cost-center tags.
- Metering records show duplicate warmup debit for a subset (~3.2k tokens) of requests.
- Console estimate did not show this duplication.

Expected behavior:
- Single warmup credit application per hourly window, attributed to the canonical cost-center tag.
- No duplicate debit on provisional buffers.

Logs / evidence provided by customer:
- Billing CSV extract attached (customer-attachment reference).
- Postback delivery timestamps and request IDs from their side (customer provided sample: bw-req-10921, bw-req-10922).
- Screenshot of billing console showing split lines and negative provisional balance alert.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 15:10 - Support (Maya): Notified customer we are prioritizing reconciliation and will apply provisional credit while engineering works on a fix. Customer requested estimate for credit restoration and root cause details.
2026-03-13 20:05 - Eng (Arjun): Deployed temporary metric: postback-seq-token per-request to detect ordering anomalies. Found ~0.9% of postbacks in that window arrived out-of-order across consumers after partition rebalance. Created PR to add strict sequence checks in aggregator (linked PR below).
Initial triage: correlated billing CSV to postback-aggregator consumer logs. Root cause hypothesis: during a Kafka rebalance triggered by short maintenance, the postback-aggregator started two partial accumulators with different tag normalization state. The billing service treats accumulators as independent if cost-center tag differs and writes separate invoice lines. Additionally, one accumulator's offset was replayed leading to a duplicate warmup debit. Evidence: consumer offsets show overlapping commits; aggregator logs show 'tag-normalization: cache-miss' followed by different normalized values within 30s for same request IDs.
Key findings:
- Rebalance window: 2026-03-10T02:03:12Z - 2026-03-10T02:05:06Z.
- Duplicate debit volume: ~3,200 tokens (~$0.012/token equivalent; manual calc done by Billing Eng).
- Deterministic ordering missing in aggregator; reliant on consumer ordering which is non-deterministic after rebalance.
- Console estimate pipeline uses consolidated accumulators and did not reflect transient duplicate intermediate writes.
Immediate mitigations taken:
- Issued provisional credit to restore customer's provisional balance.
- Enabled postback-seq-token logging to detect further anomalies.
- Scheduled backfill job to recompute and dedupe hourly accumulators for affected window.
Longer-term fix:
- PR #402 in billing-collector (adds sequence token and canonical tag snapshot to accumulator key) to be canary-deployed 2026-03-16.
- Add alert for 'accumulator-split-rate > 0.1%' to detect early.
Notes for CS: Customer is enterprise and flagged for SLA follow-up; recommend a postmortem and a goodwill credit of one month of reserved-hours buffer if postback replayer uncovers further discrepancies.
Workaround applied: provisional credit $1,250 issued on 2026-03-14 to neutralize negative provisional balance. Manual reconciliation scheduled via backfill replayer to dedupe hourly accumulators for 2026-03-10 window. Engineering PR to make aggregator ordering deterministic (sequence token) created and scheduled for canary 2026-03-16. Customer notified and SLA escalation opened; awaiting backfill results before final invoice crediting and closure.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent truncation of the final SSE payload (missing terminal 'end' event) when using the browser JS SDK with fetch() pipelining enabled via a CDN/edge rewrite. The stream appears to produce all choice fragments during generation but never emits the end/closed metadata; client sees final partial sentence and then connection idle until abort.

Impact: Affects several production users at ClipWrite Labs who use low-latency streaming for assisted writing. Appears intermittently (~1 in 350 streams during peak); causes user-visible truncated paragraphs and increased retries. Customer observed elevated error/retry rate and user complaints.

Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated account (ClipWrite), SDK js v1.6.2, edge proxy: internal-cdn-1 (TLS termination + rewriting), load balancer: alb-us-east. Affected model variants: redwood-alpha-rlhf-v2 (token length ~400).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Init streaming call via SDK using fetch-based transport with keepalive + streaming response enabled.
2) Route through internal edge (internal-cdn-1) with HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 downgrade at edge.
3) Trigger generation with long final token (punctuation-heavy).
4) Observe client receives choice fragments but no final end event; connection remains open until client timeout.

Observed logs / excerpts:
- Client Wireshark/TCP: FIN not seen immediately; long idle then browser-level abort.
- Edge logs (internal-cdn-1): 200 OK upstream, chunked transfer encoded; last chunk size noted as 0 but no 'end-of-stream' metadata forwarded to client connection.
- API side (sse-service): stream close event recorded and choice metadata included in internal trace id=trace-88a3, but downstream edge trace shows chunk drain without SSE 'event: end' forwarded.

Hypothesis: Edge/proxy performs an early connection flush or HTTP/2->1.1 translation path coalesces/chops SSE frame boundaries. When the SDK relies on fetch() streaming semantics and the edge rewrites headers or injects a small buffering layer, the terminal SSE 'event: end' metadata may be stripped, coalesced into a zero-length chunk, or emitted behind an immediate keepalive flush that the browser treats as stream end suppression. This race is more likely with pipelined fetch and small trailing metadata frames.

Temporary workaround (customer): Disable fetch pipelining / enable websocket transport in SDK or increase client-side idle timeout to allow the edge to flush trailing frames. Customer reports fewer truncations when switching to WS or when inserting a 5ms server-side flush delay before sending terminal metadata.

Impact on platform: Could cause unnecessary retries and poor UX for streaming-first customers. If root cause is edge rewrite behavior, other customers behind the same CDN path could be affected under bursty conditions.

Next steps / proposed plan:
- SRE: capture end-to-end traces for affected trace ids and correlate with edge flush timings (ACTION: Morgan).
- Edge team: audit HTTP/2->1.1 conversion pipeline for SSE boundary preservation and small-chunk coalescing (ACTION: Javier from edge infra).
- SDK: add an optional client-side heuristic to treat an immediate post-choice zero-length chunk or a heartbeat as potential terminal event and buffer for an extra 200ms before aborting (ACTION: DX team).
- Reproduce: Create a controlled reproduction harness that simulates the CDN rewrite and pipelined fetch path (ACTION: Support; target repro by 2026-03-07).

Resolution criteria: Confirmed repro and a mitigation (edge config or SDK fix) validated in staging; publish guidance and rollout fix.

2026-03-05 09:12 - Customer (ClipWrite) - Initial report: 'During high-concurrency bursts some of our streaming responses are missing the final paragraph even though partial content arrives. Switching to WS helped temporarily.'
2026-03-05 10:00 - Support (Aisha) - Triage: escalated to SRE and Edge teams; requested example request IDs and SDK logs. Assigned to Morgan for trace correlation.
2026-03-05 14:30 - SRE (Morgan) - Investigation: I pulled trace trace-88a3 and see API emitted end metadata at 2026-03-05T14:09:12.231Z. Edge logs show a zero-length chunk and then a keepalive flush at 14:09:12.235Z; downstream TCP shows idle until client abort. Suspect boundary coalescing at translation layer.
2026-03-06 08:20 - Edge Infra (Javier) - Note: Found a recent config tweak (nginx chunk buffer optimizations) applied 2026-02-28 on internal-cdn-1. Will rollback one setting in staging to test SSE behavior.
2026-03-07 11:05 - DX (Rina) - SDK note: Added experimental 'tolerantEnd' flag to JS SDK that waits 200ms for trailing metadata; customer confirmed reduced truncations in quick test. Will propose PR after evidence of edge root cause.
2026-03-08 16:40 - Support (Aisha) - Customer workaround communicated: recommend WS fallback or set 'tolerantEnd' client-side; coordinating with customer for staged rollback window.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurrent 429s and apparent quota drift when they run a steady set of long-lived websocket chat sessions in parallel with periodic bulk embedding uploads. The customer expects per-API-key accounting to remain stable regardless of connection pattern, but observed token/quota counters moving unexpectedly during bulk runs.

Impact:
- Several end-user chat sessions receiving transient 429s during nightly embedding backfills.
- Bulk ingestion jobs intermittently fail and require retries, increasing cost and delaying data availability.
- Customer concerned about accuracy of quota metering for billing reconciliation.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-east-1, tenant: dataripple-prod (dedicated).
- WebSocket clients maintain long-lived streaming connections (avg 45-90 minutes).
- Bulk ingestion uses parallel workers starting 120 concurrent short-lived HTTP sessions to the embeddings endpoint.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start 200 long-lived websocket streams using api key X (each stream sends ~5 tokens/s).
2) Kick off a bulk embedding job: 120 parallel short HTTP POSTs each sending batches of 512 texts.
3) Observe quota headers and success rates for ~10 minutes.
4) Note 429 spikes reported by websocket clients and bulk workers intermittently.

Expected behaviour:
- Token/quota accounting remains consistent at the api-key / tenant level and 429s are surfaced only when the agreed quota is exhausted. Long-lived streams should not cause per-connection double-counting when parallel short sessions open/close.

Observed behaviour:
- Customer sees quota depletion messages attributed to short HTTP sessions while websocket sessions also report 429s. Header X-RateLimit-Remaining sometimes shows large drops synchronized with bulk job start. After bulk job completes, counts stabilize but some websocket sessions remain rate-limited for a short window.

Initial hypothesis:
- Possible double-counting when HTTP/2 or multiplexed connections share underlying sockets (connection-level counters vs token-level counters).
- Quota service may be aggregating per-connection tokens into per-key windows with a short reconciliation delay, causing transient over-consumption to be reflected across active connections.
- Dedicated pool autoscaler or routing handoff at the proxy layer could increment ephemeral counters during worker churn.

Customer provided sample headers and timestamps:
- 2026-02-26T23:01:12Z websocket stream id ws-102: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 3482, status 200
- 2026-02-26T23:05:03Z bulk-worker-17 POST /v1/embeddings: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 289, status 429
- 2026-02-26T23:05:04Z websocket stream id ws-120: status 429, retry-after: 3
Logs show bulk workers making bursts of large payloads; gateway logs show short-lived upstream connections closed and reopened during the window. Gateway trace: trace_id=c1a4b2, route=embeddings, proxied_to=embed-node-7

- Reproduced locally in staging by running 50 long websockets + 30 parallel embedding POSTs; observed a small window where quota headers were decremented faster than expected.
- Captured gateway traces showing per-connection token accounting emitted on connect and on close; a race condition in the aggregator task increments both per-connection and per-request counters for the same tokens when connections tear down concurrently.
- Quota service processes reports from streaming-proxy every 10s; bulk ingestion path reports per-request immediately. During high churn, the aggregator double-applies a 'recently-closed' delta.
- No evidence of tenant-level bug in billing pipeline; this appears to be transient accounting in the in-memory quota cache in the quota-service shim.
- Related PR touching aggregator timing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3442 (open, awaiting review).

Additional notes:
Temporary mitigation: recommend customer create a dedicated API key for bulk ingestion (separate quota bucket) and stagger worker fanout using exponential ramp (5m). Engineering change: patch to quota-aggregator to debounce closed-connection deltas and add idempotency keys for per-connection reports (PR opened). Follow-up: monitor for 72h after deploy and confirm with customer that websocket 429s no longer correlate with bulk job start.
- Engineering to scope and land aggregator debounce patch (ETA 2026-03-10).
- Customer to test separate API key for bulk jobs and report results by 2026-03-06.
- SRE to add a Grafana panel showing short-window delta between per-connection and per-key counters to detect regressions.
- If workaround insufficient, schedule hotfix rollout to dedicated pool.
payload.summary: Per-connection vs API-key quota drift when mixing long-lived WebSocket sessions and short bulk ingestion

payload.description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 13:22 UTC we saw a sustained elevation of 5xx responses (~8–12% error rate) for requests from customer ZephyrAI to chat/streaming routes. Impact: customer reports slow or failing chat sessions and multiple aborted streaming sessions during a high-concurrency training-validation job. Environment: dedicated tenant for ZephyrAI in eu-west-1; heavy long-lived streaming usage + periodic small burst uploads.

Observed behavior: API-GW logs show an increasing queue of TLS handshakes / connection accepts (~10k backlog over 15m window), followed by a rapid rise in accept errors on the gateway and repeated upstream connection resets. Upstreams (serving-runtime) show fd exhaustion, increased ephemeral port reuse, and subsequent process OOMs in one runtime pod.

Customer impact: partial service outage for streaming endpoints for ZephyrAI (affects ~35% of sessions), elevated latency for generation endpoints, and several retries that amplified load.

Initial triage: API-GW experienced accept queue growth and then EMFILE/too-many-open-files on the gateway host. However, runtime pods reported fd saturation concurrently; runtime logs show many half-open TCP connections and repeated TLS renegotiation attempts from aborted streams. Hypothesis: a combination of aggressive keepalive/short client abort pattern + our keepalive reaper and accept window sizing caused rapid socket churn; gateway accepted connections faster than runtime could finish TLS + handshake pipeline, pushing fds into CLOSE_WAIT on runtimes and hitting per-process fd limits.

Evidence: - fd_count near 10240 on runtime before OOM. - apigw accept backlog grew in lockstep with customer ramp. - Kernel logs show >95% of sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on a subset of runtime nodes. - No recent kernel or runtime image changes in eu-west cluster; customer traffic pattern appears to have triggered pathological behavior.

Alternate theories considered and ruled out: - NVMe iowait (no), - Known kernel TLS regression (not present in kernel versions), - Misbehaving routing rule (no, traffic correctly routed).
1) Applied per-tenant rate cap on new streaming session creation for ZephyrAI (throttle to 400 concurrent new session opens/min).
2) Increased apigw accept window and slowed handshake concurrency by enabling handshake-adaptive-backoff feature for the ZephyrAI route.
3) Recycled two most impacted runtime pods to free fd table and clear CLOSE_WAIT sockets.

Customer-facing message: We applied temporary throttles and recycled affected runtimes; the customer saw reduced 5xx and improved session success within ~6 minutes.
Primary root cause: socket-churn amplification from long-lived streaming clients that frequently abort sessions combined with conservative per-process fd limits on serving-runtime pods. The gateway continued accepting handshakes at high rate causing runtime CLOSE_WAIT/fd saturation and subsequent process exits. Contributing factor: keepalive-reaper and handshake concurrency settings were tuned for typical load and did not handle a high abort-rate workload from a single dedicated tenant.
Resolved by: (a) permanent increase of per-runtime soft ulimit for fds to 65536 for eu-west dedicated cluster; (b) deployment of handshake-adaptive-backoff as default on streaming routes for dedicated tenants (config flag enabled 2026-03-14 03:00 UTC); (c) rolling restart of affected runtime nodes to pick up ulimit change and clear socket state; (d) added a tenant-level guardrail to limit concurrent new streaming session opens and introduced exponential backoff on aborted handshakes at the gateway.

Post-fix verification: error-rate for ZephyrAI returned to baseline (<0.5%) within 15 minutes after mitigations; runtime fd headroom remained stable under replays of customer load.
1) Ops: roll out ulimit increase to all dedicated eu-west runtime pools and validate across canary workload (owner: infra-team).
2) Runtime: add metric for CLOSE_WAIT ratio and alert when >25% for >5m (owner: serving-runtime).
3) Product/Docs: add guidance for customers with high-abort streaming patterns and recommended client keepalive/abort backoff (owner: DX).
4) Support: coordinate with ZephyrAI to schedule a load profile change to prevent future saturation; propose staged ramp plan.
5) Conduct a post-incident runbook update for handshake-adaptive-backoff (owner: SRE).

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 14:10 - ZephyrAI (Customer): Confirmed sessions restored for a subset; asking for ETA to full recovery because validation job is time-sensitive.
payload.summary: API-GW handshake backlog leading to upstream FD exhaustion and elevated 5xx for ZephyrAI

Issue summary:

During a sustained traffic ramp for a single dedicated tenant (NovaChat Inc.) we observed a correlated increase in 5xx responses originating at the API gateway and upstream runtime restarts. The signal appears tied to aggressive prefetch behavior on the serving runtime where prefetch lock contention leads to a backpressure cascade: queued requests block on prefetch locks, API gateway queue growth triggers hedged retries, and runtimes hit watchdog timeouts and restart.

Impact:
- ~18% elevated 5xx rate for the tenant across us-east over a 30 minute window (affecting production traffic).
- Streaming sessions experienced intermittent resets; short requests returned 502/503.
- Customer reports increased error rates and a temporary degradation of SLAs for some user flows.

Environment:
- Production (us-east), Dedicated pool assigned to NovaChat.
- Serving runtime version: 2026.02.11-rc3
- API gateway version: 2026.03.01

Observed behavior:
- Prefetch workers spike CPU and hold kvcache locks for longer than expected (seen in runtime metrics).
- API gateway accept queue depth climbs, then hedged retries increase outbound volume.
- Runtimes emit watchdog timeout and restart; following restarts, prefetched KV warms cause transient additional load and more contention.

Expected behavior:
- Prefetch should back off under contention, API gateway should apply backpressure without creating hedged retry amplification, and runtimes should avoid watchdog restarts by failing fast or shedding load.

1) Use dedicated tenant with prefetch enabled and kvcache sharding (matching NovaChat config).
2) Ramp concurrent short text generation requests to ~4x normal baseline with a mix of streaming and non-streaming calls.
3) Observe prefetch worker CPU, kvcache lock wait times, and API gateway accept queue depth in prod metrics dashboards.
4) Watch for hedged retry growth and runtime watchdog restarts once queueing exceeds configured thresholds.
2026-03-12T21:03:12Z api-gw us-east accept_queue=132 hedged_retries=18 status=502 tenant=novachat
2026-03-12T21:04:01Z runtime-03 watchdog_timeout pid=4213 prefetch_lock_wait_ms=1207 model=llama-3-7b
2026-03-12T21:04:03Z runtime-05 OOM_predicted=true prefetch_worker_cpu=92% kvcache_locked=true
2026-03-12T21:05:20Z api-gw us-east accept_queue=10 hedged_retries=3 status=200 tenant=novachat
Initial triage: alerting flagged a sudden spike in 5xx for tenant Novachat around 21:00 UTC. Pagerduty routed to SRE on-call.
Metric correlation: high prefetch_lock_wait_ms correlated tightly with API gateway accept_queue growth. CPU profile shows prefetch workers doing long synchronous IO during kvcache fetch on cold keys.
Hedged retry policy amplified load: gateway sent duplicate requests when upstream latency crossed hedged threshold, increasing concurrency into already-congested runtimes.
Hypothesis: a particular key distribution for the tenant leads to frequent cold-prefetch across a small set of KV shards causing lock hotspots. Under burst, backpressure loops into hedged retries and watchdog restarts.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-12: Customer reported 15-20% error increase starting ~20:58 UTC. Collecting logs and route-level metrics per runbook.
SRE (Marco Ruiz) - 2026-03-12: Confirmed accept_queue climb and multiple runtime watchdog restarts. Temporarily increased API gateway hedged-retry threshold for the tenant as a mitigation (reduced duplicate load).
Eng (Lena Cho) - 2026-03-13: Reproduced lock hotspot locally when replaying tenant request key pattern. Adding exponential backoff to prefetch lock acquisition as a candidate fix.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-13: Customer notified of temporary hedged-retry threshold increase and asked to pause heavy batch jobs. They agreed to throttle custom load for 1 hour.
SRE (Marco Ruiz) - 2026-03-14: Deployed runtime backoff patch to canary pool for affected dedicated hosts (PR linked). Monitoring for error rate reduction.
Workaround applied: increased hedged-retry threshold in API gateway for NovaChat and paused aggressive background uploads per customer request. This immediately reduced duplicate fanout and lowered 5xx rate.
Temporary mitigation: throttled prefetch concurrency for the tenant and enabled a short lock-acquisition backoff in the runtime (canary rollout).
Fix planned: implement exponential backoff with jitter for prefetch lock acquisition and add kvcache hot-key backpressure metric to triggering autopolicy to shed prefetch for hot shards. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821
Post-incident follow-up: add a dashboard and an automated runbook step to increase hedged-retry thresholds per-tenant when kvcache lock contention is detected. Schedule: engineer-led rollout next week and customer postmortem with NovaChat.
payload.summary: Backpressure cascade from prefetch lock contention causing elevated 5xx error rate for dedicated tenant

Issue summary:
Customer requests a repeatable playbook and sample export for forensic audit consumption. They need deterministic ordering, per-event masked UUID provenance, chained resume tokens, and a field-enrichment mapping to correlate application traces with Redwood audit events.

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete SOC evidence handoff to their SIEM vendor for a regulatory review window starting 2026-03-20.
- Forensic team requires verifiable ordering and per-tenant pseudonymization metadata for subpoenas.

Environment:
- Production organization: Luminary Finance (enterprise tenant)
- Region: us-east
- Expected export channel: HTTPS webhook (customer-managed collector) and S3 archive backfill

Requested deliverables:
1) A short playbook (steps + curl examples) to request an ordered, resumable NDJSON export with: UTC canonical timestamps, per-event masked_uuid (HMAC-SHA256 using tenant salt), contiguous resume-token chain, and per-batch signed manifest (SHA256).
2) Mapping CSV that maps Redwood audit fields to Luminary SIEM field names (include examples for session, request_id, model_version).
3) A small sample export (50 events) demonstrating ordering, pseudonymization, and resume tokens.
4) Runbook notes about retention, clock-skew handling, and recommended collector acknowledgement semantics.

Steps to reproduce / HOWTO for support engineers:
1) Re-run export job for tenant lum-fin-93 with start_time=2026-03-01T00:00:00Z and end_time=2026-03-01T00:10:00Z.
2) Use the `export/resumable` API with `ordering=event_time,uuid_provenance=masked` query flags.
3) Inspect the resulting NDJSON for `resume_token` and `prev_token_hash` fields to confirm chain.

Observed behavior:
- Initial export contains events with non-deterministic ordering when pulled concurrently by multiple workers.
- Current pseudonymization uses global salt, customer wants per-tenant salt and an auditable HMAC header.

Expected behavior:
- Deterministic, monotonically increasing ordering by canonical UTC event_time, deterministic tie-breaker using event sequence number.
- Each event includes `masked_uuid`, `masking_method` and `masking_provenance` fields.
- Batch manifest is signed and includes start/end offsets and manifest SHA256.

Logs / Example snippet from prod (redacted):
{"timestamp":"2026-03-01T00:00:02Z","event":"request_received","request_id":"r_***","tenant":"lum-fin-93","model":"redwood-instruct-2.1"}

Support note: customer has provided SIEM schema and a legal hold notice referencing 2026-03-20. We need to treat sample as high priority and include chainproof evidence for legal team.
2026-03-10: Initial triage by support - identified two causes: (a) concurrent export workers using local sort windows causing out-of-order when merged; (b) global salt used for UUID masking rather than tenant-scoped salt.
2026-03-11: SRE checked export scheduler logs - found export job E-87321 retried twice at 00:03 causing partial replays without resume token updates.
2026-03-12: Eng spike indicates we can enforce single-pass merge with deterministic tie-break and add per-tenant HMAC via existing KMS envelope. Low-risk patchable change in export service.
Hypothesis: Reordering occurs during parallel chunk merging; resume_token chain is present but prev_token_hash not always written on retry path.
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Opened request after customer escalated compliance calendar. Customer attached SIEM mapping CSV and legal_hold.pdf (redacted).
Customer (Ellen Rivera, Luminary) 2026-03-10: We need the sample and playbook by 2026-03-14 to give to our SOC team. Please include signed manifest - legal requires cryptographic proof of chain.
SRE (Diego Martinez) 2026-03-11: Observed export scheduler retries - posting tail of export.log to ticket. Suggest toggling single-thread merge for a test run to confirm ordering fix.
Eng (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-12: Will prepare a controlled re-export job with single-pass merge and tenant-salted HMAC. ETA to produce sample export: 2026-03-13 17:00 UTC.
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-13: Confirmed sample arrived and validated by customer; Luminary asked for a short README and curl examples for webhook ack semantics.
Provisioned a controlled re-export for lum-fin-93 with single-pass deterministic merge and per-tenant HMAC masking. Delivered: (1) 50-event NDJSON sample demonstrating monotonic UTC ordering and resume_token chain; (2) mapping CSV; (3) playbook with curl examples; (4) signed batch manifest (SHA256) and verification steps. Customer validated sample on 2026-03-13 and marked delivery accepted.

Follow-ups: create a small internal runbook to default to tenant-salted masking for enterprise exports and add an export retry path test to CI. Owner: Eng infra (Liam O'Connor).
Eng to open INT ticket to update export service default for enterprise tenants to tenant-salted masking (targeted sprint 2026-03-20).
SRE to add export retry path artifact tests in scheduler CI (owner: Diego Martinez).
Support to schedule a short handoff meeting with Luminary SOC to walk through verification steps (owner: Maya Patel).

Issue summary: Customer NimbusChat reported that after opting a subset of tenants into a scheduled canary, some sessions that were explicitly pinned to the new model variant were unexpectedly routed to the fallback (legacy) variant.
Impact: Several customer tenants experienced degraded quality and a small cost spike due to re-evaluation on the legacy variant. Scope appears limited to a subset of tenants on us-east who use the customer's SSO flow.
Environment: Production (dedicated pool) - us-east.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer enables canary opt-in via console for a tenant and pins that tenant to redwood-v1.3.
2) Tenant opens a session in their app (long-running streaming session).
3) After a short time (10-30s), requests for that session are observed hitting the legacy variant and receiving degraded responses.
Observed behavior:
- Pin metadata initially applied (control-plane snapshot shows pinned=redwood-v1.3)
- Edge logs show requests arriving without the tenant claim header intermittently
- Orchestrator reports "no pin found" and route falls back to legacy-variant
- No GPU preempt events or autoscaler activity coincide with the times.
Recent change/context: Customer recently enabled an A/B header rewrite rule at their edge proxy to remove trailing user attributes for GDPR compliance. That rule was deployed at the same time as the canary opt-in.
Temporary workaround: Customer disabled the header rewrite rule at their edge which immediately restored pinned routing.
Support notes: We believe an authz/header rewrite at the customer's edge is stripping or renaming the tenant-claim header used in our pin handshake, which prevents the orchestrator from binding the session to the pinned model.
payload.summary: Pin migration blocked by edge authz header rewrite during optional canary opt-in

Issue summary: Several LexiChat customers report 100–300ms higher p50/p95 latency and intermittent p99 timeouts on follow-up conversational turns that should be served from the KV/prefix cache. Impact: user-facing latency regressions during multi-turn dialogs, elevated token costs due to cold-path decoding, and occasional 504s for long conversations. Environment: prod clusters in us-east with dedicated capacity for LexiChat (dedicated pool ID: dc-lexi-03). Observed behavior: Two subsequent identical prompts replayed by the LexiChat SDK are treated as distinct cache keys; first request warms the cache and completes in expected latency, the replay gets a cold-path KV lookup and shows increased latency or timeout. Expected behavior: byte-identical conversational turns should map to the same prefix/KV cache keys and be served from cache, producing consistent low latency for repeats.
1) Use LexiChat sandbox to send a multi-turn conversation to redwood-open-7b in prod/us-east (pool dc-lexi-03).
2) At turn N, send prompt text 'Summarize the last response:' (exact same bytes) and observe latency ~45ms.
3) Immediately replay the same prompt text as a follow-up request (same conversation id) and observe latency jump to 250–400ms or a 504 timeout in some cases.
4) Capture request traces, raw prompt bytes, and KV keys emitted by the serving-runtime for both requests.
5) Reproduce more reliably by toggling SDK option normalize_unicode=true/false.
Initial hypothesis: cache eviction or shard rebalance. Cluster metrics show no recent rebalances and shard occupancy stable.
Trace inspection: first/second requests show different prefix_key values despite identical visible prompt text. Raw byte dumps differ only in Unicode normalization forms (first used NFKC, second NFC).
Reproducer: toggling the SDK's normalize_unicode flag changes behavior; enabling normalization on client eliminates divergence and both requests hit the same key.
Root cause theory: recent tokenizer update (PR #4321) introduced a change in how prompt bytes are normalized before key derivation — server-side normalization now uses a different Unicode normalization form than older SDKs. When client and server disagree, semantically identical prompts produce distinct keys and miss the prefix cache.
Impact window: started ~2026-03-10 08:00 UTC correlating with rollout of serving-runtime v2.14.2 which included tokenizer normalization changes.
Ask LexiChat to enable client-side unicode normalization (NFKC) as a temporary measure; this restores key parity with current server-side behavior and reduces p99 latency. Applied to customer in prod pool dc-lexi-03 at 2026-03-12T17:00Z.
1) Roll a patch to serving-runtime to accept both normalization forms when deriving cache keys (backcompat shim) and log normalization form mismatches for visibility. 2) Coordinate a follow-up SDK release to align client normalization with server canonicalization. 3) Add a unit/integration test asserting identical visible prompts map to same cache key across normalization variants. Target: hotfix rollout to prod us-east by 2026-03-15.
Maya Chen - 2026-03-12T16:05Z: Filed ticket after reproducer from LexiChat support engineer. Attached traces and hex dumps. Marked P1 due to customer impact and timeouts.
Rafael Ortiz - 2026-03-12T16:28Z: Investigating. Initial traces indicate divergent prefix_key values; forwarding to tokenizer/runtime team and linking PR #4321. Assigned to me for follow-up with eng.
Elena Park (Tokenization) - 2026-03-12T17:02Z: Confirmed tokenizer change in v2.14.2 swapped normalization to NFKC on the server. We'll prepare a backward-compatible keying shim.
Support - 2026-03-12T17:45Z: Applied client-side workaround with LexiChat; observed p95 drop from 320ms to 62ms. Customer confirmed UX improvement, asking for ETA on permanent fix.
Rafael Ortiz - 2026-03-13T09:14Z: Patch branch created (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/compare/fix/kvcache-normalization). Waiting on code review; will schedule hotfix rollout to us-east staging then prod.
Deploy kvcache normalization-backcompat shim to staging and run LexiChat regression suite.
Publish SDK guidance and release note about unicode normalization parity in client/server keying.
Add monitoring alert for sudden divergence in prefix_key entropy (spike in unique keys per identical prompt).
payload.summary: Identical replayed conversational turns treated as cache misses due to prompt normalization key divergence

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 504 / request timeouts for single generation requests when using very large max_tokens (typically >= 120k token window). Failures occur late in the generation (after ~70-95% of requested tokens produced). Suspected stall during KV-cache refill / eviction cycle in serving runtime when prefill and decode phases overlap under heavy batching.

Impact:
- Affects multiple request attempts from NimbusAI production workloads on Dedicated pools in us-east; blocking their long-transcript generation features.
- Symptoms: spike in 5xx (504 gateway timeouts) and client-observed disconnects; partial outputs received before termination.

Environment:
- Dedicated customer pool (dedicated), prod:us-east; models: gptx-16b-fp16 primarily.
- Requests routed through API gateway with default 60s client timeout in their code, but server-side timeouts observed beyond that.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) POST /v1/generate using model gptx-16b-fp16 on dedicated pool.
2) Set prompt ~40k tokens, max_tokens=120000, stream=false, temperature=0.2.
3) Send concurrently from 6 clients to simulate production load.
4) Observe intermittent 504 from API gateway after long-running generation (often after ~30-50k tokens produced).

Observed behavior:
- Request occasionally returns 504 with no finalizing token. Partial stream of tokens earlier in the response.
- Serving runtime logs show long stall in "kv_cache_refill" and spikes in kernel scheduling latency.

Expected behavior:
- Long-context generation should continue to completion (or return a graceful error with a helpful hint) rather than sudden 504 mid-generation.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- Trace IDs: trace-us-east-78a4a3b, trace-us-east-78a4a3c (attached to ticket).
- Client-side logs showing request timings and partial payloads (attached).

Notes: This differs from previously reported "streaming hang" tickets because the requests do return partial tokens before failing and failure appears correlated to internal KV cache operations when requests are near the model token-window boundary.
2026-03-12 12:05 - NimbusAI (customer): We're seeing ~5-10% of long-generation jobs fail with 504s. This started after we increased max_tokens for a transcript feature. Attaching traces and sample request IDs.
2026-03-12 12:20 - Support (Ava Chen): Acknowledged. Opening P1 incident and routing to SRE + Serving runtime team. Could you confirm whether you're using streaming or non-streaming requests and whether you can temporarily lower max_tokens as a mitigation?
2026-03-12 13:02 - SRE (Marco Reyes): Initial triage - found correlated spikes in 'kv_cache_refill_ms' metric and increased kernel execution stalls on host pool rp-dedicated-12. Traces show long blocking in 'prefill->decode' handoff. Reproduced locally with synthetic load using customer-like concurrency.
2026-03-12 15:40 - Eng (Priya Nair): Added deeper prints to the runtime; observed that when batch mixing includes both very long prefill and short requests, eviction/refill of KV shards triggers synchronous disk/host-memory copies for certain quantized kernels causing stalls. Patch proposed to make KV refill asynchronous and add backpressure on batches that exceed token-window thresholds.
2026-03-13 09:15 - Support (Ava Chen): Shared a temporary mitigation with customer: (1) Reduce max_tokens to <= 80k or (2) enable streaming=true to flush tokens incrementally, or (3) route large requests to a low-concurrency pool. Customer applying (2) streaming and (3) routing; reporting fewer failures but still seeing rare timeouts.
2026-03-14 11:30 - SRE (Marco Reyes): Deployed a canary patch to rp-dedicated-12 that makes KV refill async and limits batch coalescing of very long prefill requests. Early telemetry (12h) shows 85% reduction in kv_cache_refill_ms spikes and near-zero 504s for affected traces on canary hosts. Planning broader rollout after runbook and automated test coverage added.
2026-03-14 14:00 - NimbusAI (customer): Thanks—canary seems promising. We'll keep streaming=true for now and report if we see new regressions. Please share ETA for full rollout.
2026-03-14 14:45 - Eng (Priya Nair): ETA for full rollout across dedicated pools: 2026-03-18 pending one more stability run and a regression test in CI that simulates heavy long-prefill coalescing. Follow-up action: create an alert for kv_cache_refill_ms > 5s per host and add a dashboard panel to per-pool view.
SRE reproduced failure pattern with synthetic workload mixing long (>=40k token) prefills and short requests at concurrency >=6.
Profiling shows blocking memory copies during KV shard refill on quantized kernels; the refill path executed synchronously within the decode thread under certain batch interleavings.
Host rp-dedicated-12 showed memory pressure and increased scheduler latency correlated with the failures. Not all hosts reproduce; correlated to specific kernel selection and quantized model variant.
Comparing traces to SUP-4827 indicates similar long-context timing but different root cause (there was a streaming socket hang there; here it's internal KV refill stalls).
Canary patch deployed 2026-03-14: KV refill made asynchronous and batch coalescing limited for requests with prefill token count > 30k.
Telemetry after canary shows 85% reduction in refill latency spikes and 0/1200 504s on canary hosts for the sampled traffic window.
Temporary customer workarounds accepted: enable streaming=true, reduce max_tokens to <=80k, or route large jobs to low-concurrency pools.
Planned follow-ups: full rollout 2026-03-18 after stability run; add CI synthetic test to cover long-prefill + mixed-concurrency; add dashboard and alert for kv_cache_refill_ms; update long-context runbook with recommended request patterns and a recommended default batch-limit for large prefills.
Postmortem: pending after full rollout and 48h stable telemetry; owner: Priya Nair (Eng).
payload.summary: Intermittent generation requests with very large max_tokens time out near token-window boundary (KV-cache refill stall suspected)

Issue summary: Multiple customers (first reported by Inkware Studios on a Dedicated pool) observe occasional long TTFB spikes (10–45s) followed by connection close or 502/504. This occurs primarily for streaming completions where the runtime emits many very small chunked frames (1–4 bytes per chunk) and no Content-Length. Impact: customer facing API calls fail ~3–7% of requests during peaks, causing degraded UX for streaming LLM completions and some automatic retries that increase cost. Environment: Dedicated capacity in us-east-1 behind our edge proxy + ALB stack. Occurs across model variants that stream output. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a streaming completion request that produces many tiny tokens (e.g., deterministic tokenizer, low temperature, model configured to flush per token). 2) Send request from a client with good network connectivity to the customer's dedicated endpoint. 3) Observe TTFB in client and ALB/edge proxy logs. Actual behaviour: Edge proxy waits until an internal buffer threshold is hit (~16KB) before flushing to the ALB, causing long TTFB for low-throughput streams; ALB idle timeout (60s) sometimes closes the connection before any bytes reach the client. Expected behaviour: First token(s) should be forwarded to ALB immediately as chunked frames so TTFB remains low and streaming continues. Temporary workaround: Customer increased runtime flush frequency (manual batch-flush) and we bumped ALB idle timeout to 90s for the Dedicated pool as a mitigation.
1) Use a model run configured to stream output token-by-token (e.g., low temperature, token-level flush).
2) Issue a streaming completion request to the dedicated endpoint from a stable client in us-east-1.
3) Monitor client TTFB and edge-proxy access logs (see sample logs below).
4) Repeat at low token throughput (1–5 tokens/sec) to see coalescing behaviour.
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-13T15:03:12Z INFO - upstream response chunk (3 bytes) buffered; current_buffer=3B; threshold=16KB
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-13T15:03:27Z INFO - upstream buffer flushed to ALB after idle; flush_size=12B; elapsed=15s
[alb] 2026-03-13T15:03:55Z WARN - connection closed by target due to idle timeout; target_response_time=43s
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-13T15:03:12Z DEBUG - stream token emitted; size=2B; flush_requested=true
Initial triage: reproduced in staging with a synthetic low-throughput token stream. Client TTFB matched edge-proxy flush delays (tens of seconds).
Hypothesis: the edge proxy has response buffering/coalescing enabled for performance with small chunk suppression; it's waiting for a buffer threshold or idle window before forwarding to ALB. For very-low-throughput streaming workloads this behavior increases TTFB and risks hitting ALB idle timeouts.
Config review: proxy setting 'response_buffering' set to 'auto' which uses a 16KB coalescing threshold and a 15s idle flush. ALB set to default idle timeout of 60s. Dedicated pool had additional fronting proxies with legacy buffering rules.
Correlation: incidents spike when models emit many small tokens (deterministic outputs) and for customers on dedicated pools with extra proxy hop. No evidence of model runtime slowness; runtime is emitting quickly per logs.
Related issues: SUP-50122 (chunked requests causing timeouts) and SUP-91827 (stream silence due to header fragmentation) — similar class but different root cause (proxy coalescing rather than header bloat).
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-13: Customer reported ~5% failure rate on streaming completions over last 4 hours. Sent initial repro and asked for engineering triage.
Marco Valdez (SRE) 2026-03-13: Reproduced in staging. Edge proxy configuration causes coalescing. Raising to P1 due to customer impact. Temporarily increased ALB idle timeout for affected dedicated pool.
Rashmi Gupta (Serving) 2026-03-13: Serving runtime already emits flushes per token when configured. Suggest disabling proxy response coalescing for streaming endpoints or honouring chunk flush flag from runtime.
Marco Valdez (SRE) 2026-03-14: Applied edge-proxy config change in canary: response_buffering=disabled for /streaming/* route. Observed immediate TTFB improvement in canary (median drop from 18s to 120ms). Will roll to remaining hosts after smoke tests.
Inkware Support (Customer) 2026-03-14: Confirmed improvement on canary host. Requesting permanent fix and guidance for dedicated customers.
Canary rollout of edge-proxy change (response_buffering=disabled for streaming routes) shows TTFB median reduced to ~120ms for low-throughput streams. Follow-up actions: 1) Roll change to all dedicated pool edge proxies (scheduled 2026-03-14 22:00 UTC). 2) Add traffic-based proxy rule: disable response coalescing when downstream uses chunked transfer or when 'x-streaming' header present. 3) Update Dedicated onboarding docs to recommend runtime-level flush settings and recommended ALB timeouts for streaming workloads. 4) Create infra task to add monitoring alerts for coalescing-induced TTFB >5s in streaming routes (INT-41207).
payload.summary: Intermittent TTFB spikes and mid-request closes due to edge proxy coalescing small chunked responses

Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-09T14:20Z Parcelly reported a sudden p95/p99 regression for generation requests. Impact: ~15% of requests for their dedicated pool in us-east had tail latency spikes from ~180ms to 1.2s, causing client-side timeouts and retries. Environment: Dedicated pool (parcelly-dedicated-01) in us-east using redwood-large-v2. Observed behavior: A subset of inferences were routed via eu-central egress nodes, adding ~800-1,000ms RTT and increasing total token latency. Expected behavior: Requests should remain in-region (us-east) or route to nearest healthy egress without cross-region detours.
1) Use Parcelly API key against production endpoint in us-east. 2) Send 1k concurrent generation requests with typical 512-token prompts and streaming enabled. 3) Observe p50/p95/p99 in Redwood Console per-route latency. 4) Correlate request IDs flagged by customer with edge/egress path in access logs.
[2026-03-09T14:22:07Z] request_id=rq_9f8a ... route=us-east -> eu-central-egress node=eg-32 latency=980ms
[2026-03-09T14:22:07Z] request_id=rq_9f8b ... route=us-east node=us-east-egress latency=120ms
[2026-03-09T14:22:07Z] healthcheck: eu-central-egress status=degraded for cluster=egress-v2 (reason=transient-conn-fail)
[2026-03-09T14:23:12Z] smart-routing: fallbackTriggered=true policy=latencyBudget computedBest=us-east selected=eu-central (cachedPreference=eu-central due to stale affinity)
Initial hypothesis: a transient degradation in a subset of us-east egress nodes caused the routing controller to fall back to a cached preference that favored eu-central. Evidence: Grafana trace (https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd/egress-latency?from=2026-03-09T14:00Z&to=2026-03-09T15:00Z) shows simultaneous health check timeouts for eg-29/eg-31 in us-east. Routing logs show 'cachedPreference' entries created by the affinity cache that have TTL=10m and were not invalidated after node recovery. Network team also observed a short-lived spike in packet loss on the us-east public egress AS path at 2026-03-09T14:18Z (BGP flap reported by cloud provider). Temporary correlation between BGP event and routing cache invalidation race. Repro attempted in staging with canary: forcing healthchecks to flip quickly reproduces cachedPreference not being refreshed; when we add immediate cache invalidation on healthcheck success, cross-region fallback stops. Next steps: create patch to invalidate affinity cache on healthcheck success, increase egress pool headroom for dedicated pools, and schedule a controlled canary rollout. Related: see linked issue SUP-20645 for prior egress fallback occurrences.
