payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicated external webhook invocations for server-side function_call events after a client stream reconnect/resume. The original function call appears to complete on our runtime but the webhook gets invoked twice when the client retries the streaming session.

Impact:
- Customer (NimbusPayments) sees duplicate payment-create webhooks resulting in duplicated downstream jobs (idempotency not respected by downstream).
- Occurs intermittently during poor mobile network conditions when the browser/edge SDK reconnects mid-stream.
- Potential financial impact for customer: duplicate charge attempts and manual reconciliation.

Environment:
- Customer using TypeScript browser SDK v1.12.0 with streaming chat + function_call enabled.
- Dedicated deployment, prod us-east region, API fronted by CloudFront-like edge layer.
- Server runtime: serving-runtime v2.7.3, api-gateway v1.9.1.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Open streaming chat session from mobile web client and trigger a sequence that results in a function_call to the payment webhook (function name: create_payment).
2) Simulate a flaky network (toggle airplane mode) so the socket disconnects during the streaming/chunked response (server had already emitted a function_call and partial response).
3) Client reconnects and the SDK attempts to resume the stream with a fresh resume attempt; SDK sets an idempotency header (x-idempotency-key) on the resumed connection.
4) Observe two webhook POSTs for create_payment within seconds.

Expected behavior:
- Only a single create_payment webhook should be delivered for the original function_call. SDK retries/resume should not cause duplicate downstream side effects when an idempotency key is provided.

Actual behavior:
- Two POSTs reach customer's webhook endpoint. The first is the original in-flight delivery from the runtime. The second comes after the resumed connection and appears to be triggered by a resumed function_call state.

Observed logs (redacted):
- Runtime logs show request traces T-9a7e... and T-9a7e... (same trace) with function_call recorded once, but gateway access logs show two separate incoming streaming requests with different idempotency header values:
  - req1: x-idempotency-key: "8e4b24f6-7a9e-4c3d-9f2a-aaaaaaa..."
  - req2: x-idempotency-key: "8e4b24f6-7a9e-4c3d-9f2a-1"  (note numeric suffix)
- Edge logs (CloudFront) show header normalization/truncation events when header length > 48 chars; downstream origin receives rewritten header name/value for second request.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Advise customer to include a per-call confirmation token in the webhook payload (client-side generated) and to deduplicate on the webhook receiver while we investigate.
- As an immediate mitigation, asked customer to increase server-side idempotency window and to enable "webhook delivery dedupe" via a short-lived token if possible.

Root cause hypothesis so far:
- Edge proxy is rewriting or truncating the x-idempotency-key header on connection resume (some internal normalization rule at the CDN that appends/truncates long header values), causing our gateway to treat the resumed request as a distinct idempotent scope. The runtime reconciles function_call state but the gateway's idempotency lookup uses the altered key, so the resumed request triggers an additional webhook delivery.

Data points collected / logs attached:
- Access logs and header captures from edge for the two attempts (attached as support artifact).
- Server trace showing single function_call state but duplicate webhook deliveries downstream.
- Customer-provided webhook receiver logs showing two POST requests within 2s.

Proposed next steps / remediation:
1) Short term (0-24h): Document and push the recommended customer workaround (embed client-confirmation token in webhook payload and dedupe).
2) Fix the gateway to canonicalize idempotency keys from either header or streaming-metadata and accept alternate name forms (x-idempotency-key and x-idempotency). Backfill support for keys truncated by edge (map detected rewritten forms to canonical token using a best-effort normalization).
3) SDK change (TS/browser): On resume attempt, include idempotency token in both header and in the first JSON control frame body so origin sees the same token even if an edge alters headers. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/842 (WIP).
4) Long term: Add signed confirmation tokens on function_call completion so webhook consumers can validate original call provenance.

Notes:
- This issue is reproducible with a synthetic test using our edge staging where we simulate header truncation; reproduction script and test harness stored on the linked Confluence page.
- We should coordinate with CDN partner to remove header normalization rules for this header or increase header length allowance.

Engineering ran correlation of traces across gateway, runtime and webhook delivery. Found mismatch between idempotency header observed at edge vs origin. Confirmed SDK sets a UUID v4 token; edge truncated to 37 chars and appended a suffix in some cases. Reproduced in staging by injecting header-mod rewrite. Eng hypothesis: CDN rule intended to canonicalize headers containing control chars is accidentally mangling long IDs. Next step: file ticket with infra/CDN partner and push gateway fallback normalization. Temporary SDK/console guidance added.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 15:22 - Customer (Danielle R., NimbusPayments): Confirmed they received two POSTs; currently deduping at receiver. Asked if Redwood can provide permanent server-side fix because dedupe is operationally expensive for them.
1) Add client-generated confirmation token to webhook payload and dedupe on receiver. 2) If using a custom CDN, disable header normalization for x-idempotency-key or increase header length allowance. 3) Use the SDK patch (1.12.1) when released which writes idempotency token into control frame body as well as header.
- Complete SDK PR review and ship 1.12.1. - Deploy gateway normalization hotfix to prod-us-east. - Engage CDN partner to remove/adjust header rewrite rule. - Follow up with NimbusPayments by 2026-03-18 with rollout plan and expected ETA.
In Progress - mitigation applied. SDK patch and gateway normalization hotfix planned and in review.
payload.summary: Streaming resume duplicates function-call webhooks when idempotency header is rewritten by edge proxy

Customer reports that after switching their embedding model from open-embed-v2-512 -> open-embed-v3-384 in their Dedicated pool, reranker results for several search flows degraded: top-N ordering changed unpredictably and relevance dropped. Some rerank requests return quickly but with low-quality ordering; others show higher latency and occasional 500s. Customer switched models to save cost and saw immediate impact in production traffic.
1) In customer account (Acme Payments) with dedicated pool in eu-west, change embedding model to open-embed-v3-384 and leave reranker pinned to open-rerank-512. 2) Run batch of 1000 search+rerank calls against route /v1/rerank using stored corpus. 3) Compare top-5 ordering and relevance metrics to baseline (embeddings=512). 4) Observe increased mismatches and occasional 500 errors with traces pointing to reranker-service.
- Top-N ordering degraded for 12% of queries by manual eval sets.
- Some requests have 500 errors with stack traces referencing 'vector_dot_product: length mismatch'.
- Median tail latency for rerank increased from 110ms -> 420ms for affected route.
- Customer sees billing unchanged but perceived quality regression.
- Backwards-compatible behavior where swapping to a different embedding model should either be blocked if dimensionality incompatible with pinned reranker, or auto-converted/handled without quality regressions.
- No 500s due to vector length mismatches.
- Latency should not spike by >2x for same traffic pattern.
Initial triage: traces show the reranker operator assumes 512-d vectors and performs native dot-product kernel on GPU. When 384-d vectors arrive, there is an internal validation error in native kernel that surfaces as 500. We also observed a compatibility shim in Dedicated cluster that attempts to pad/truncate vectors on the CPU for 'compatibility' and that path is single-threaded causing latency spikes. Hypotheses: 1) Model metadata for open-embed-v3-384 didn't register dimensionality with routing layer so reranker was not alerted. 2) Compatibility conversion code path is causing both quality degradation (zero padding changes vector semantics) and latency due to CPU-bound conversions. 3) Some edge requests bypass the shim and hit GPU kernel causing length-mismatch 500s.

Issue summary: After a targeted canary that adjusted cookie domain and SameSite attributes for cross-subdomain routing, a subset of long-poll streaming sessions from BrightChat saw their model version pin removed and traffic routed to the fallback model. Impact: ~6% of BrightChat tenant requests in us-east (long-poll streaming) returned responses from fallback variant (rwi-7b-compat) for durations up to 18 minutes. Customer impact: degraded generation quality and intermittent streaming disconnects for live agents.

Environment: production (us-east), Dedicated cluster for BrightChat (tenant id bc-091). Canary change: edge-proxy cookie domain normalization in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4872 rolled to 10% (cohort) starting 2026-03-12 03:10 UTC.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a long-poll streaming chat session using BrightChat tenant credentials (session cookie set to api.brightchat.com).
2) Observe router affinity header (x-tenant-session) and cookie domain in request/response.
3) Trigger a model request that is pinned to rwi-13b-v1 via tenant pin.
4) Monitor routing decisions in router logs and session-manager for pin refresh events.

Observed behavior: When the canary cohort hit an upstream edge with cookie-domain rewrite set to ".redwood.ai" (intended for drain handling across subdomains), the session cookie returned to the client with a different domain scope. For long-poll clients that reuse the original host-bound cookie, the session-manager validated the cookie as mismatched and treated the session as unauthenticated for pin reconciliation, causing the pinned routing key to be dropped and the request to be evaluated for fallback path. This only affected streams where the client reused the old host-scoped cookie and did not immediately refresh session metadata.

Logs / Traces: Relevant samples in trace-id list: trace: us-east-20260312-8a9b, us-east-20260312-8a9c; edge-proxy logs show Set-Cookie: session=...; Domain=.redwood.ai at 03:17:02 UTC. Router logs show pin_eviction_reason=COOKIE_DOMAIN_MISMATCH and decision=FALLBACK at same timestamps.

Workaround: For affected tenants, toggle canary off for edge cookie rewrite or instruct client to force a session refresh (POST /v1/sessions/refresh). Both steps reduced impact immediately.

Customer comment: BrightChat reported visible quality regression on agent UI and requested immediate mitigation and postmortem.
03/12 03:22 UTC: SRE observed correlation between canary cohort and spike in routing->fallback events for tenant bc-091 (BrightChat).
03/12 03:30 UTC: Confirmed edge-proxy change (cookie domain rewrite) rolled as 10% canary; rollback flag not yet triggered.
03/12 04:05 UTC: Hypothesis A - cookie domain normalization changed cookie scope causing session-manager to treat session as orphaned and drop pin. Evidence: router logs show 'pin_eviction_reason=COOKIE_DOMAIN_MISMATCH'.
03/12 04:30 UTC: Hypothesis B - autoscaler prewarm caused new warm instances without updated session DB mapping and triggered fallback; low evidence, metrics for warm instance churn not significant.
03/12 05:10 UTC: Reproduced locally using BrightChat dev tenant: emulate host-scoped cookie then inject Set-Cookie Domain=.redwood.ai and assert session-manager invalidates pin. Reproducible in staging with long-poll client that does not refresh session metadata.
03/12 06:00 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied: disabled cookie domain rewrite for canary cohort and instructed BrightChat to refresh sessions. Observed pinned routing restored after ~2 minutes for refreshed sessions.
03/13 09:00 UTC: Added extra logging in session-manager for cookie-origin and pin-check path (PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4879).
03/14 01:15 UTC: Confirmed regression window affected ~6% of tenant traffic and lasted up to 18 minutes per affected session before client refresh or session TTL expiry caused natural recovery.
Asha Kapoor (Support) 2026-03-12 03:45 UTC: Acknowledged customer report and opened investigation. Notified SRE and eng-ops channels (#support and #incidents).
Jonah Reed (SRE) 2026-03-12 04:12 UTC: Initial triage - correlates with PR 4872 canary. Pin eviction logs found. Will attempt controlled rollback for the cohort and add session-manager guard.
BrightChat - Samantha Lee (Customer) 2026-03-12 04:35 UTC: Seeing degraded responses for some live agents. We'll apply client-side session refresh but need platform mitigation ASAP.
Jonah Reed (SRE) 2026-03-12 05:05 UTC: Rolled back cookie-domain rewrite for the canary cohort. Monitoring for pin restoration.
Mitigation performed: canary cookie-domain rewrite rolled back for us-east cohort; advised customer to refresh sessions. Added defensive guard in session-manager to accept equivalent cookie scopes for pinned sessions when domain normalization occurs and added tighter logging. Patch PR 4879 merged to staging. Postmortem scheduled and follow-up action items assigned: update canary checklist to include pin invariants, add automated pin-eviction alert, and add e2e test for long-poll session cookie changes.
Complete postmortem and publish to customer (BrightChat) by 2026-03-18.
Backfill e2e test for cookie domain rotation and pinned session behavior (owner: platform/qe).
Add automated alert rule on pin_eviction_reason=COOKIE_DOMAIN_MISMATCH in prod router metrics (owner: sre).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer ParcelFlow reports intermittent 504/timeout errors when sending chats with combined long prompt histories and very large max_tokens (requests asking for up to 16k generated tokens). Failures started 2026-03-11 and appear correlated with high context-length + large max_tokens requests.

Impact:
- Several production storefronts experienced dropped responses during peak traffic windows (estimated ~2% of requests in the customer's traffic mix).
- Customer observed increased latency preceding the timeout (responses stalled ~40-90s before 504).
- Affects live ordering flows for ParcelFlow (potential customer conversion impact).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted dedicated pool for ParcelFlow (dedicated tenant on us-west region).
- API surface: /v1/chat/completions via SDK + long_history param.
- Typical request: combined prompt ~140k tokens (conversation history truncated but still large) + max_tokens=16000.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Create chat payload with ~60 messages (system + user + assistant), compressed but expanded to ~120k tokens after tokenization.
2) Set model to gpt-redwood-13b and max_tokens to 16000.
3) Call /v1/chat/completions with streaming disabled.
4) Observe that request either times out (504) or gets a 502/503 from gateway after ~60s.

Observed logs / traces (selected):
- Gateway logs: correlation_id=cf2a9b1e - upstream 504 after 61s waiting for response.
- Serving runtime trace: request queued, worker assigned, per-token generation begins but stalls at token ~10240 with repeated kernel resubmission warnings.
- SRE telemetries: GPU memory spike and frequent KV cache growth events for that session id; queue length increased causing head-of-line blocking for subsequent requests.
- Customer SDK trace: client socket closed after 65s with ECONNRESET.

Customer-provided sample payload (sanitized):
- model: gpt-redwood-13b
- prompt tokenized_length: ~120000
- max_tokens: 16000

Additional notes: ParcelFlow is on a dedicated instance with autoscaling policies configured but burst capacity is limited to three additional machines.

Expected behavior:
- Long-context prompts should either be accepted and streamed progressively, or be rejected early with a clear 4xx indicating request is outside service limits. Timeouts should not occur silently for valid but expensive requests.

Timeline and initial hypotheses:
- 2026-03-11: Support received first report; recreated with smaller-scale payloads in staging.
- 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC: SRE observed serving runtime worker saturations when both context length and max_tokens are large.
- Hypothesis A: Combination of very large context + large max_tokens can exceed per-request compute budget causing generation to take > gateway timeout.
- Hypothesis B: Large KV cache growth triggers less efficient kernel path and increased per-step latency (we see kernel resubmission warnings in runtime logs).
- Hypothesis C: Batching policy and request queueing allow a single heavy request to block multiple workers leading to head-of-line queuing and cascading timeouts.

What we've tried so far:
- Reproduced a reduced variant in staging with prompt ~40k tokens + max_tokens 8k; reproduced increased per-token latency but not immediate 504.
- Increased gateway upstream timeout to 120s for the customer's dedicated pool as a temporary mitigation (rolled 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC).
- Instrumented serving runtime to emit per-request estimated remaining work and token-rate metrics for further diagnosis (telemetry added to trace id sampling).
- Temporarily enabled streaming for a subset of customer requests to verify progressive output avoids gateway timeouts (worked for streaming-enabled test).

Preliminary findings:
- Large requests are compute-bound and sometimes hit inefficient execution paths (observed in runtime logs).
- When queue length > 8 and a heavy request enters, latency for all queued requests increases non-linearly.
- Autoscaler did not provision extra capacity quickly enough for the customer's burst profile (policy tuned for average, not extreme one-off heavy jobs).

Next steps planned:
- SRE/Runtime to add early-cost estimation in router to reject or redirect extremely expensive requests (work item created).
- Engineering to add guardrail: reject requests with combined estimated_ops > threshold with 413/Request too large and helpful error message.
- Improve autoscaler burst response for dedicated pools (tune cooldown and scale-up aggressiveness).
- Longer-term: add a model-variant fallback that can accept the request with quantized/low-memory variant when available.

Additional notes:

payload.description:
Issue summary:
BlueHarbor (private deployment) reports that recently provisioned users show up in the console but their RBAC role bindings are not applied. This started after a scheduled SCIM sync with the customer's LDAP/AD instance when the identity team enabled unicode normalization on the LDAP side.

Impact:
- ~27 users (subset of warehouse ops) cannot access Admin Console and receive 403 when attempting role-protected routes.
- Affects production cluster in us-west, intermittent but repeatable for users whose LDAP CN contains composed accents (e.g., 'José' vs 'José').
- Customer-facing workflows blocked for 6 users requiring immediate escalation.

Environment:
- Private deployment (private control plane) in us-west-2
- Version: identity-provisioner v2.14.1, scim-sync job v1.3.0
- LDAP provider: BlueHarbor corporate AD (OpenLDAP fronting)
- RBAC config: group->role mapping via exact string match in tenant bindings

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Ensure LDAP has a user with a CN containing a composed unicode character (e.g., U+00E9 'é' as single codepoint).
2) Run SCIM upsert from identity-provisioner against Redwood SCIM endpoint (customer's scheduled job triggered at 03:00 UTC).
3) Observe that the user account appears in Redwood Console but assigned groups do not result in role bindings.
4) Re-run SCIM but normalize LDAP CN to decomposed form (e.g., 'e' + combining acute).
5) If normalization differs between LDAP and Redwood's stored group names, role binding lookup fails with no match.

Logs / Evidence:
- identity-provisioner logs (attached by customer) show SCIM PATCH success for group membership: "member": "uid=jose\u0301,ou=users,dc=blueharbor,dc=loc"
- Console audit shows created user display_name: "José" (U+00E9) but group lookup uses stored binding key "Jose\u0301" (U+0065 U+0301) -> mismatch
- RBAC code path compares raw strings with binary equality during binding resolution (see dump snippet attached).
- Customer ran "iconv -c" to canonicalize and confirmed roles apply when both sides use NFC.

Temporary workaround requested:
- Customer can re-run SCIM sync with normalization set to NFC on LDAP side; they did and reported immediate remediation for 20 users.
- Suggested workaround: Create a mapping rule in the customer's provisioning job to normalize group names to NFC before sending.

Customer request / ask:
- Permanent fix: Redwood should canonicalize SCIM group identifiers and display names using a consistent unicode normalization form (NFC) before performing RBAC lookups, or perform normalization-insensitive matching.
- Assessment of scope: Are there other RBAC pathways affected (service accounts, API token owners)?

Attachments included by customer:
- scim-sync.log (trimmed)
- identity-provisioner config snippet
- CSV list of affected usernames

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:48 - SRE (Anita Gomez): Checked private control-plane storage for tenant bh-001. Group names in tenant bindings are persisted in the form received at creation time (no normalization). We see both forms present for different users across sync windows.
2026-03-12 11:03 - Customer (BlueHarbor SRE - L. Martinez): Applied temporary NFC normalization on their side and confirmed 20/27 accounts restored. Awaiting permanent fix timeline.
Root cause hypothesis: identity-provisioner and RBAC resolver perform binary string equality for group->role bindings. The customer's LDAP emits decomposed unicode sequences for some entries while previously stored bindings (created months earlier) used composed sequences. This results in logical equivalence but binary inequality. Repro confirmed in lab. Risk surface: any tenant with non-ASCII group/display names.
Actions taken: reproduced, collected logs, confirmed workaround, prepared code change (normalize to NFC at canonicalization boundary).
Mitigation plan and next steps:
1) Short term: document workaround for customers (SCIM normalizer snippet) and customer applied it with success.
2) Medium term: merged PR to identity-provisioner to apply unicode NFC normalization on all incoming SCIM group and user identifiers (github.com/redwood-inference/identity-provisioner/pull/217).
3) Long term: update RBAC lookup to perform normalization-insensitive compare and add unit tests for NFC/NFD variants.
4) Release plan: coordinate with Private deployment ops (INT-4021) to roll identity-provisioner v2.15.0 to affected clusters during low-traffic window; target: 2026-03-18.
Post-deploy: run SCIM re-sync and verify role bindings reconcile; follow up with BlueHarbor to confirm full remediation and close ticket.
payload.summary: UTF-8 normalization mismatch from SCIM/LDAP provisioning causes orphaned RBAC bindings in private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexaHealth reports persistent elevated p50/p99 latency and a degradation in throughput on their dedicated GPU pool during weekday business hours. Symptoms correspond to GPUs remaining attached/occupied for long periods even after clients close streams.

Impact:
- LexaHealth production traffic experiences 30-60% throughput degradation for batched routes and repeated autoscale down-failures.
- Automated fallback to lower-tier model variants has been observed but does not restore throughput due to slot reservation.
- Customer SLAs degraded; they are an important health-care partner (sensitive workloads).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: lexah-health-dedicated-prod (us-west-2)
- Runtime version: 2026.02.11-rc3
- Autoscaler: predictive-v2 (configured min: 2, max: 24)
- Scheduler/allocator: allocator-1.9.4

Steps to reproduce (replicated internally):
1) Send a sequence of long-lived streaming calls (keep-alive with no data for 45s) from a synthetic client matching LexaHealth traffic patterns (n=150 streams over 10m).
2) Close TCP connection abruptly on client side for ~30% of connections.
3) Observe connection/slot state in allocator and GPU attachment list.

Observed behavior:
- Several GPU slots show "attached" but have no active inference threads and show stale KV cache leases.
- Autoscaler fails to shrink because allocator reports slots in-use; new allocations are delayed and queue grows.
- p50 increases by ~120ms, p99 by ~800ms; throughput (requests/minute) drops ~40% relative to baseline.
- Monitoring shows high ephemeral socket counts on serving runtime sidecar and open file descriptors not reclaimed.

Expected behavior:
- Closed/aborted client connections should free associated slot leases quickly (within 3s). Autoscaler should be able to scale down when unused capacity is available and not blocked by leaked reservations.

Relevant logs & traces:
- Sample serving sidecar stacktrace: "runtime/connection: reclaim loop stuck waiting on lease-release for 00:12:34" (attached in support artifact).
- Allocator metric: slot_reserved_count spikes and does not fall for 10+ minutes after clients close.
- Kernel-level socket states show many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on sidecar.

Initial customer report (excerpt):
"We see our RL training jobs starve the dedicated pool in the morning window. It looks like slots are being held even though inference calls finished — this started last Wed after a deploy. Can you help?" — LexaHealth SRE

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:50 — LexaHealth SRE: Confirmed reduced impact with mitigation but requested permanent fix. Provided additional connection traces and a sample of client SDK behavior (abrupt closes after heartbeat failure).
Heap/profile analysis shows sidecar not entering connection finalizer when client TCP FIN is missing; sockets linger in CLOSE_WAIT.
Allocator only accepts lease release events from sidecar — if sidecar finalizer does not run, allocator considers slot in-use.
Repeatable with synthetic client that mirrors LexaHealth SDK abrupt-close behavior; not limited to a specific model but amplified for large KV caches (long context models).
Temporary TTL reclamation improved availability but is a blunt instrument and risks premature eviction of genuinely warm slots.
Mitigation: Enabled aggressive lease TTL reclamation for affected pool (lexah-health-dedicated-prod-agg1) at 2026-03-10 13:30 — partial throughput recovery.
Fix in progress: PR to add explicit lease cleanup on sidecar connection finalizers and defensive GC for orphaned leases (allocator PR #8921).
Rollout plan: Canary deploy fix to 5% of lexah pool traffic on 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC; monitor slot_reserved_count, p99 latency, and socket CLOSE_WAIT metrics for 2 hours. If stable, ramp to 100% over 4 hours.
Follow-ups: Add automated test for abrupt-close scenarios in our integration harness; add monitor alert for slot_reserved_count > threshold to trigger auto-ttl escalation with a safe floor.
payload.summary: Connection leak keeping GPU slots reserved and triggering autoscale shortfall in dedicated pool

payload.description:
Issue summary: Stratosight is seeing recurring, short-lived collapses in throughput and p95 latency spikes (up to 6-10x baseline) for inference requests routed to their dedicated pool. Impact: customer applications experience 504s and aborted streaming responses for ~30-90s windows multiple times per hour, affecting user-facing search and summarization features. Environment: prod (us-west-2) dedicated pool reserved for Stratosight with mixed-instance nodes and custom autoscaler profile. Timeline: first reported 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC; multiple recurrences observed through 2026-03-10 afternoon and again on 2026-03-11.

Observations: metrics show p95 token latency jumping from ~220ms to >2s, 5xx count increases, and sustained queue growth on gateway. GPU dashboards indicate high SM utilization and rising GPU memory fragmentation during incidents while host CPU remains moderate. Autoscaler logs show several rapid scale-down events in the 5 minutes prior to degraded windows.

Expected behavior: steady throughput within SLA, graceful queueing without intermittent 504s. Workaround requested: immediate mitigation to keep customer service online while we investigate root cause.
1) Send sustained batched requests that target long context lengths (avg 1024 tokens) and bathtub shapes (bursty traffic) to customer's dedicated pool endpoint.
2) Mix model variants in traffic (open-llama-7b-v2 + redwood-mix-medium) and include a subset of high-beam and sampling calls to increase KV cache pressure.
3) Observe p95 latency and request queue depth in serving-console over 5-15 minute windows; reproduce under autoscaler set to min=2, max=6, scaleDownAggressiveness=high (customer config).
2026-03-10T09:10:22Z gateway: upstream queue depth for pool-stratosight increased to 420 (baseline 38)
2026-03-10T09:11:07Z autoscaler: scaled down node-group-a from 5 -> 3 due to short-term cpu drop (policy: aggressive)
2026-03-10T09:11:34Z serving-runtime: kernel stall detected on GPU gpu-0 (SM busy 98%, active warps stalled)
stack: merge-kernel-1 -> attention-fused -> kv-cache-commit
2026-03-10T09:12:00Z gateway: returned 504 to request id req-7f3b2 (timeout 30s)

Additional notes:
SRE Pager (2026-03-10 10:05): Temporarily pinned pool to 4 nodes and disabled aggressive scale-down for customer pool. Noted immediate partial improvement but residual latency spikes persisted during co-tenant high memory jobs.
Customer (Stratosight Ops) (2026-03-10 10:28): Confirmed reduced 504s after pin, but still seeing spikes tied to specific time windows (every ~20-40 minutes). Provided logs of in-app batch storms.
Hypothesis 1: Autoscaler misconfiguration allowed scale-down during transient load dips, producing insufficient GPU capacity when burst arrived. Evidence: autoscaler events precede incident windows and pool size shrank 1-2 nodes within 2-3 minutes.
Hypothesis 2: Noisy neighbor from co-tenant batch jobs pinned to same nodes causing GPU memory fragmentation and kernel stalls. Evidence: during incidents non-customer pods observed with large memory allocations and elevated cudaMalloc times.
Hypothesis 3: Scheduler lacked affinity rules for model memory class; heavy and light models co-located increasing eviction/GC cycles in serving-runtime. Reproduced by mixing open-llama-7b-v2 and redwood-mix-medium in same node set — p95 increases and SM stalls observed.
Profiling: nvprof traces show long kernel tail on fused attention kernel when fragmentation rises. GPU_util high but effective throughput low. Serving-runtime logs show repeated KV cache invalidations leading to re-computation overhead.
Temporary mitigations tried: pinned node count to fixed level, increased per-pool node isolation, and temporarily routed heavy-batch traffic to fallback smaller model. Pin reduced 504s but did not eliminate transient spikes during simultaneous co-tenant jobs.
Mitigation applied (2026-03-11 16:30): Autoscaler policy for customer pool modified to set min=4, max=8, scaleDownAggressiveness=low and add cooldown 300s. Nodes with heavy-memory pods drained from mixed pools and moved to dedicated slot-pools.
Routing change (2026-03-11 18:00): Implemented short-term routing rule to avoid co-scheduling open-llama-7b-v2 with redwood-mix-medium on same GPU nodes for Stratosight traffic.
Customer impact: Incident windows frequency dropped to near zero and p95 returned to within SLA for 48h post-mitigation. Customer confirmed production stability on 2026-03-12.
Long-term actions: scheduler will receive an enhancement to consider model memory class and sequence-length distribution when placing pods; autoscaler UX will include safeguards against aggressive scale-down on dedicated pools. Follow-up tickets created: INT-4127 (scheduler affinity), SUP-82701 (autoscaler UX for dedicated).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when they replay short conversational prompts in quick succession (5–10s intervals), observed tail latency for repeat requests increases ~2x after the first two requests. This appears specific to repeat prompts that should hit the prefix/KV cache.

Impact:
- PromptlyAI production customers are experiencing slower-than-expected responses on multi-turn quick-replay flows (chat previews and autosave previews).
- Error rate is not elevated (no 5xx at API layer) but p95/p99 latency degrade from ~180ms to ~380ms on affected replicas.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (dedicated pool) in us-east-1, tenant PromptlyAI (dedicated).
- Model: gptx-14b-instruct pinned to v2026-02-28.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Send short prompt sequence (seed prompt + 2 repeat prompts) with streaming enabled and short inter-request gap (6s).
2) Observe normal latency for first two requests.
3) On subsequent rapid repeats, latency increases and streaming buffers appear to flush slower, sometimes triggering client-side timeout at 10s.

Observed logs/metrics (customer and support):
- Replica-level trace shows cache miss/partial-hit patterns on prefix lookup followed by synchronous KV fetch (~50–120ms additional).
- Serving-runtime metrics show an increase in kv_cache_prefetch_stalls and kv_lookup_sync_reads on the affected nodes.
- No corresponding CPU/GPU pressure spikes; memory utilization normal.

Workaround provided so far:
- Temporarily routed PromptlyAI traffic to warm pool (warmed replicas) which reduced latency back to baseline.
- Customer can also increase inter-request gap to >20s to avoid stall triggering.

Initial hypothesis: a race in the prefix-KV prefetching path causes subsequent requests to wait for a background warmup task that previously was fast. Evidence: kv_cache_prefetch_stalls metric correlates tightly with p99 latency spikes.

What we checked:
- Dashboard (Grafana) panels for kv cache hit ratio, prefetch latency, and request routing (link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv/kv-prefetch?orgId=1).
- Replica logs for the timeframe: search for 'kv_prefetch_block' and 'cache_index_mismatch'. Found intermittent 'cache_index_mismatch' warnings on 3 replicas.
- Compared two model variants: v2026-02-28 (affected) and v2026-02-14 (older). Older variant did not show same prefetch_stalls.

Hypotheses under validation:
1) Index regeneration TTL mismatch causes prefetch to fall back to synchronous disk/KV store reads for entries that looked cached but require rehydration.
2) A scheduler change last week (scheduler PR 8001) adjusted background prefetch concurrency, exposing a contention window under rapid repeated short contexts.
3) Eviction policy change caused high-churn prefixes (short repeated prompts) to thrash across KV shards leading to extra network hop latency.

Next steps planned:
- Reproduce internally with PromptlyAI sample trace using a dedicated replay harness (SRE assigned).
- Add extra logging around kv index lifetime and prefetch task handoff.
- Roll back scheduler concurrency tweak on a small canary pool if reproduction succeeds.

Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10: Customer reported p95/p99 increase from 180ms -> ~380ms on replay flows. They provided request IDs and a small replay script. Asked for full trace and tenant routing info.
Customer (PromptlyAI - Rajiv Sinha) 2026-03-10: Provided request IDs and mentioned issue started after model pin v2026-02-28 rollout. Notified they cannot increase inter-request gap in their UX flow.
SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-11: Correlated kv_cache_prefetch_stalls with the timestamps. Observed 'cache_index_mismatch' warnings on 3 nodes. Spun up a warmed replica set and routed traffic -> latency normalized.
Engineering (Sofia Martinez) 2026-03-11: Noted scheduler PR 8001 changed prefetch worker pool size from 8 -> 4 to reduce background load. Suggest reverting on canary. Opened PR to add more robust index TTL checks.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12: Informed customer of temporary routing workaround and asked to approve canary rollback test during low traffic window. Customer approved.
SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-12: Canary rollback scheduled for 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. Will monitor kv_prefetch_stalls, p99 latency, and error budgets.
Workaround applied: traffic routed to warmed replica pool which restored baseline latency. Root cause under validation; likely regression in prefetch concurrency + index TTL handling. Canary rollback of scheduler concurrency change planned. Permanent fix will include TTL consistency checks and fallback cold-read batching to avoid synchronous stalls.
payload.summary: KV cache warmup stall causing increased latency for rapid repeated prompts

payload.description:
Issue summary: CortexLabs reported a sudden increase in tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors after an optimizer configuration change was applied to their dedicated pool. The change included a mixed-precision quantization profile, aggressive batching windows, and enabling KV cache prefetch for low-latency paths.

Impact: Customer-facing inference for chat and generate endpoints experienced p95 latency jumps and a small but persistent 5xx rate, impacting a single high-traffic tenant. Traffic volume is production, dedicated pool. Customer has asked for a safe rollback procedure and guidance on how to profile the regression without causing customer-visible downtime.

Environment: prod-us-east dedicated pool (CortexLabs-reserved), affected model variants: llama-2-70b pinned -> mixed-quant profile; some requests hit a fallback redwood-rlhf-13b variant during overflow.

Ask: 1) Confirm root cause (config misalignment vs hardware noise). 2) Provide a minimal-risk rollback plan to restore stable p95 while preserving safety of long-lived sessions. 3) Suggest profiling steps to avoid reintroducing regression when re-enabling optimizations.
1) Use CortexLabs tenant on prod-us-east with the current optimizer profile (mixed-quant + kv_prefetch enabled + aggressive batch policy).
2) Send a representative workload: bursty chat sessions with long context (avg 1800 tokens, tail 95th percentile episodes).
3) Observe p95 latency and any 5xx spikes in the first 10–30 minutes after traffic shift.
4) Compare to baseline with kv_prefetch disabled and quant profile set to fp16-only.
p95 increased from ~120ms baseline to ~780ms for some requests; sustained 5xx rate ~0.8% (up from 0.05%). GPU utilization dropped on several nodes while CPU and mem pressure on host rose. Requests occasionally timed out during prefix cache warm-up windows.
p95 should remain within SLO (<=200ms for this customer tier) and 5xx should stay <0.1% after configuration changes. Mixed-precision should reduce token cost without increasing tail latency for long-context sessions.
Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/cortexlabs/shot123 (p95 spike).
Edge logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:03Z ERROR serving-runtime: kv_prefetch miss, fallback path triggered.
Kernel selection logs: runtime/telemetry/2314 shows increased kernel fallback events at 14:11-14:18Z.
Slack thread: #support-cortexlabs (link in related_confluence_pages).
Checked recent config rollout: deploy timestamp 2026-03-10T13:45Z, config bundle ID config-8472 changed quant profile and batching windows.
Observed a config diff: kv_prefetch switched from adaptive->always-on for CortexLabs tenant; batch window lowered from 40ms->12ms to favor throughput.
Telemetry shows repeated kernel fallback to conservative kernels when sequence length > 1024 — correlates with long-context requests.
GPU memory usage lower than expected; host-side CPU and page-faults increased consistent with frequent KV cache evictions during prefetch windows.
Hypothesis: combined effect of always-on kv_prefetch + tighter batching triggers cache churn and kernel fallback decisions on long-context requests, producing tail latency spikes. Quant profile likely exacerbates kernel incompatibility on some requests leading to fallback/heavier CPU paths.
No evidence of hardware degradation across nodes; replicas serving non-Cortex tenants show normal p95, pointing to tenant-specific config change as primary vector.
Related telemetry and stack traces attached in GitHub PR 2314 and config commit 7a8b3f4 for operator reference.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged customer, opened ticket, asked for traffic window to run profiling. First response sent within SLA.
CortexLabs (Customer) 2026-03-10: Provided load traces and stated regression aligns with their morning traffic spike after the config change. Asked for non-disruptive rollback guidance.
Luis Ortega (SRE) 2026-03-10: Confirmed config bundle and started metric sweep. Suggested immediate traffic quarantine option (route a small fraction to a stable variant) to gather live traces.
Priya Kapoor (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-11: Requested gdb/kern logs for two affected replicas; noted kernel fallback pattern and suggested disabling kv_prefetch as a low-risk mitigation.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-11: Ran a staged experiment routing 15% of traffic to baseline profile; p95 for that shard remained stable. Customer approved stepwise rollback if mitigation fails.
Luis Ortega (SRE) 2026-03-12: Prepared rollback checklist and scheduled a controlled unwind with the customer for 2026-03-12T16:00Z UTC.
Workaround and rollback plan (agreed with customer):
1) Immediately enable traffic quarantine: route 20% of CortexLabs traffic to baseline profile (fp16 quant, kv_prefetch=adaptive) for 30 minutes and monitor p95/5xx.
2) If baseline bucket shows stable p95 and reduced errors, schedule progressive shift: 50% -> 80% -> 100% over 15-minute intervals.
3) Apply targeted config change on dedicated pool: revert kv_prefetch to adaptive and restore batching window to 40ms for tenant.
4) Revert quantization profile from mixed-quant to fp16-only for the tenant for the next 24 hours while engineering runs a safe repro and kernel compatibility test.
5) Drain and gracefully restart any replicas that reported kernel fallback before moving to full rollback completion.
6) Validate: confirm p95 <= 200ms and 5xx < 0.1% across 2 consecutive 30-minute windows in prod-us-east and eu-west.
7) Post-mortem actions: add canary checks for kernel fallback rates in optimizer rollout pipeline, improve preflight test to include long-context session simulation, and add a one-click escape hatch toggle for kv_prefetch at tenant granularity.

Follow-up: Assigned to Priya Kapoor for kernel compatibility investigation and to Luis Ortega for drafting a tenant-scoped rollback runbook. Customer accepted the staged rollback and reported improved p95 at 2026-03-12T17:20Z after stepwise reversion. Mark as awaiting closure after post-mortem published.
Priya Kapoor to reproduce kernel fallback locally with long-context harness (target completion 2026-03-15).
Luis Ortega to update the rollback runbook with tenant-level kv_prefetch toggle and canary thresholds (target completion 2026-03-14).
Support to notify customer when post-mortem and runbook are available and review any billing/usage impacts from rollback (target completion 2026-03-18).

comments: 2026-02-20T09:12:00Z Aisha Patel: Acknowledged with first response. Collected client logs and asked for a HAR and proxy vendor details. Escalated to SRE due to suspected proxy-related frame handling.
2026-02-20T11:03:00Z Acme Support Engineer: Provided HAR, Squid proxy logs, and a short repro script. Noted that disabling corporate proxy eliminates the issue.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers using the Redwood websocket streaming API behind a corporate proxy observe that, after short network blips (2-5s), the resumed stream sometimes reorders intermediate chunks and drops the final 'choice/end' marker. The resulting output either contains duplicated trailing whitespace tokens or never emits the final end event, causing client-side completion logic to stall.

Impact:
- Production traffic for Acme Payments chat assistant experiences ~0.8% incomplete responses during business hours in us-east.
- Client SDKs report hung streaming sessions that require manual reconnects.
- Affects dedicated customers behind middlebox proxies; not reproducible in simple NAT environments.

Environment:
- Platform: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool)
- Region: prod-us-east
- Client: Browser apps (React) behind corporate HTTP/WS proxy (Squid/NGINX as TLS-terminating reverse proxy)
- Model: gpt-embed-4k serving via streaming websocket endpoint v1/stream

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Start a streaming generation via the JS SDK from a browser inside the corporate network.
2) Force a short network interruption (e.g. disable Wi-Fi for ~3s) or simulate transient proxy hiccup.
3) Allow reconnection; the SDK attempts resume.
4) Observe that some intermediate chunks are reordered and final end event is either delayed indefinitely or never seen.

Observed behavior:
- Reconnected stream resumes with chunks that appear out-of-order compared to original sequence numbers logged on the server.
- Final choice/end event absent ~0.8% of attempts, or duplicates of trailing whitespace tokens emitted.
- Server logs show resume token accepted and a follow-up stream session created, but downstream WebSocket frames logged from the proxy show intermittent fragment coalescing.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should preserve original token ordering and always include final choice/end event once generation completes on the server-side.

Initial hypothesis:
- Corporate proxy or TLS-terminating reverse proxy is re-fragmenting or buffering websocket frames and delivering them out of sequence to the backend after a short disconnect.
- SDK resume handshake may be interpreted as a new session by the proxy, which merges buffered fragments from both the old and new TCP streams in a way that reorders payloads.

Attachments/logs:
- Customer supplied client-side debug logs (attached link in ticket)
- Server-side streaming session logs and sequence numbers (anonymized)
- Proxy logs showing TCP-level retransmits and frame coalescing timestamps

Customer impact statement:
Acme requires reliable chat completions for payment support flows; missing final tokens cause their UI to show an eternal "thinking" spinner and occasionally submit incomplete instructions to downstream systems.

Additional notes:
Repro environment: local NGINX with proxy_buffering on reproduces reorder when resume allowed. Switching to proxy_buffering off eliminated reorder in tests.
Server-side logs: resume token accepted, resume session created, sequence_number during original session up to 3487, new session accepted frames with sequence 3482-3490 but timestamps indicate overlap/duplication from proxy.
Network trace: pcap from patient customer shows proxy replays buffered websocket frames after TCP reconnect causing interleaving from old and new stream fragments.
SDK behavior: resume attempts to patch prior message index; when backend receives interleaved fragments with lower counters, it previously appended them rather than discarding which allowed reordering/duplicates.
Similar tickets: SUP-4721 and SUP-20347 indicate other proxy-related resume edge cases; however this case shows explicit re-injection of buffered frames rather than simple truncation.
Risk assessment: high for dedicated customers behind enterprise proxies; low for customers on straightforward NATs or cloud load balancers with websocket passthrough.
Mitigation options evaluated: 1) Client-side: force full reconnect on resume failure; 2) Server-side: enforce monotonic message counters and drop stale frames on resume; 3) Ops: guidance to proxy admins to disable buffering/tuning tcp_nodelay.
Chosen short-term mitigation: provide customer with client-side flag to disable resume and documentation for proxy tuning. Long-term fix: server-side monotonic counter enforcement (PR-4321).
2026-02-25 - Temporary workaround provided: SDK flag to disable resume and support note for proxy configuration changes. Customer applied workaround and reported significant reduction of incomplete streams.
2026-03-03 - Engineering PR merged (https://github.com/redwood/streaming/pull/4321) implementing per-message monotonic counters and server-side discard of stale frames on resume. Rolling upgrade scheduled for prod-us-east on 2026-03-10 during low traffic window.
Follow-ups: add a note in streaming runbook about proxy tuning and include resume-safe headers for customers who must keep buffering enabled.
payload.summary: Intermittent stream chunk reordering and lost final choice after short websocket disconnect behind corporate proxy

Issue summary: Since 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC LexaHealth reported sustained throughput degradation for their dedicated pool after migrating to a multiplexed streaming route (embed+generate in same request). Impact: end-to-end p95 response time for short streaming requests increased from ~120ms to 950ms and p99 spiked >3s; overall token throughput for the reserved pool dropped ~35% despite GPUs showing <60% compute utilization. Environment: Dedicated pool lexhealth-dedicated (prod-us-east), autoscale enabled with min=2 max=10.

Observed behavior: high scheduler churn (frequent GPU attach/detach for tenant slots), many short-lived microbatches (~40-200 tokens) from a single tenant, per-GPU NVLink bandwidth nearing saturation, and long queue lengths on the serving runtime causing stall/wait. Customer notes the problem began after enabling streaming multiplexing to reduce client-side latency.

Why this is a concern: the autoscaler reacts to apparent low utilization by scaling down, then shortly afterwards scales up as queues form (oscillation). Slot fragmentation occurs because short streams prevent stable batch packing, leading to many partially filled slots which increases kernel kernel-launch overhead and cross-GPU NVLink chatter.
1) Deploy a dedicated pool with autoscale (min=2, max=10) in us-east-1.
2) Send 800 concurrent streams that do embed+generate in a multiplexed route: each request sends 20-120 tokens, short-lived, constant arrival rate for 15 minutes.
3) Observe scheduler logs for repeated GPU attach/detach for the tenant, and runtime metrics: queue_length, batch_fill_ratio, NVLink_tx_bytes/sec.
4) Compare p50/p95/p99 and token throughput before/after enabling multiplexing.

Expected: modest improvement in latency and steady slot packing.
Observed: autoscaler cycles every ~90–180s, batch_fill_ratio drops to ~0.25, queue_length spikes, and overall throughput drops by ~30–40%.
Customer production traffic affected; conversational flows time out at higher rates. Seen as elevated error retries from client (retry storms), higher billing due to reattempts, and reduced effective throughput from reserved pool. Business impact: degraded user experience for LexaHealth triage workflow; customer flagged as high priority.
Excerpt (scheduler.log 2026-03-10T02:12:30Z):
  INFO attach_slot tenant=lexahealth slot_id=slot-7 gpu=gpu-a1
  INFO detach_slot tenant=lexahealth slot_id=slot-7 reason=idle_reap
  INFO attach_slot tenant=lexahealth slot_id=slot-12 gpu=gpu-b3
  WARN nvlink: tx_util=92% rx_util=89% gpu_pair=gpu-a1<->gpu-b3 time=2026-03-10T02:13:08Z
  WARN runtime: queue_wait_ms=1350 p99 batch_fill=0.2 tenant=lexahealth route=multiplex-embed-gen
  DEBUG autoscaler: decision=scale_down delta=-1 reason=low_compute_util tenant=lexahealth
  DEBUG autoscaler: decision=scale_up delta=+2 reason=queue_latency tenant=lexahealth

NVLink counters (metrics dashboard snapshot): nvlink_tx_bytes/s peaked at 12GiB/s (95th pct) on gpu pairs serving lexhealth. GPU util (SM) remained ~48% average.
Initial hypothesis: noisy short streams cause slot fragmentation and poor packing -> low per-GPU compute efficiency but high cross-GPU sync/communication leading to NVLink saturation. Secondary hypothesis: autoscaler thresholds tuned on compute utilization alone are insufficient for multiplexed streaming workloads and cause oscillation.

What we checked:
- Confirmed low SM utilization but high runtime queue_wait and low batch_fill_ratio.
- Verified NVLink transmit/receive spikes concurrently with queue spikes.
- Reviewed autoscaler logs: scale decisions alternate scale_down/scale_up every ~1–3 minutes.
- Looked for GPU OOMs or kernel errors: none.
- Compared tenant vs pool-wide metrics: issue localized to lexhealth tenant traffic pattern.

Temporary mitigations attempted during triage:
- Increased min capacity for lexhealth to 4 GPUs (reduced oscillation but did not fully restore throughput).
- Enabled prefix KV caching for repeated prompts (minor improvement).
- Applied short-term autoscaler cooldown increase from 60s to 180s (reduced frequency of churn).

Conclusions so far: pattern indicates packing inefficiency + cross-GPU bandwidth bottleneck; need changes in slot packing heuristics and autoscaler signals (consider queue_length or network TX as input).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 04:10 UTC - SRE Team (Liu Zhang): Confirmed NVLink spikes coincide with queue_wait; filing infra follow-up for NVLink rate limits and topology-aware scheduling.
2026-03-10 06:22 UTC - Customer (LexaHealth - product@lexahealth.com): We rolled back multiplexing in staging and saw immediate improvement. Can you advise recommended config for production?
Workaround in place: increased reserved min capacity to 4 and extended autoscaler cooldown to 180s for lexhealth pool; recommended LexaHealth reduce multiplexing concurrency and increase per-stream token batching where feasible. Engineering actions: 1) Implement topology-aware slot assignment to prefer intra-GPU packing for multiplexed short streams. 2) Add autoscaler signal from runtime queue_length and nvlink_tx_util to prevent scale-down while queues persist. 3) Add telemetry alert to detect low batch_fill_ratio for multiplexed routes.
Status: workaround deployed (2026-03-11); engineering changes scheduled.
- Runtime team to land PR for packing heuristic and topology-aware assignment (ETA 2026-03-20).
- Autoscaler team to add queue_length signal and extend cooldown strategy (ETA 2026-03-25).
- SRE to add NVLink saturation alert and dashboard for dedicated pools by 2026-03-18.
- Follow-up with LexaHealth on production config and recommended client-side batching patterns; schedule joint load test after PR rollout.
- Postmortem to be produced after fixes are validated and deployed.
Capture metrics: batch_fill_ratio, nvlink_tx_util, queue_length, autoscaler_decision_history for the window 2026-03-10T01:50 -> 2026-03-10T03:30. Document customer config change that triggered spike (multiplexed embed+generate enablement), mitigation timeline, and engineering rollouts. Include remediation playbook for similar short-stream-heavy tenants.
payload.summary: Multiplexed short streaming requests causing slot fragmentation, NVLink contention and autoscaler oscillation in Dedicated pool

Issue summary:
Customers in the US (notably AcmeRetail) reported elevated tail latency and repeated streaming disconnects for chat/generation endpoints between 2026-03-12T11:20Z and 2026-03-12T13:40Z. Symptoms included 2-3s baseline latency jumping to 800-1200ms additional RTT and sporadic 504 timeouts on long-running streaming responses.

Impact:
- Customer-facing API calls experienced higher p99 token latencies and occasional streaming timeouts.
- Affected both hosted (public API) and Dedicated traffic that relied on global smart-routing.
- Estimated ~6% of requests from us-east were routed cross-region to eu-west during the window, contributing to customer errors and SLA exposure.

Environment:
- prod|us-east primarily; some mirrored traffic from prod|eu-west.
- Models: rw-inference-7b-v1 and gpt-4o-instruct used in affected requests.

Relevant timestamps:
- First customer report received: 2026-03-12T11:27Z
- Engineering triage begun: 2026-03-12T11:35Z
- Mitigation (rollback of edge routing change): 2026-03-12T12:10Z
- Errors subsided to baseline: 2026-03-12T12:40Z

Primary hypothesis: A recent routing policy tweak to the Smart Router (edge) that introduced a new geo-fallback heuristic caused a fraction of us-east requests to be routed to eu-west endpoints during transient region-local capacity signals. Cross-region RTTs caused higher p95/p99 and some client-side streaming timeouts on long responses.

Steps-to-reproduce summary (see below for curl examples):
- From a client in us-east, send sustained streaming generation requests to the public API with no explicit region binding. Observe elevated latency or streaming disconnects while the router is in the fallback state.

Notes: customer provided request IDs and timestamps; support has full request traces attached in observability links below.
1) Use a us-east based client (or set X-Client-Region: us-east)
2) Send a streaming /v1/chat/completions request for ~800 tokens with model rw-inference-7b-v1
3) During the affected window some requests returned 504 or had >800ms additional latency.

Example curl (non-streaming reproduction):
curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Client-Region: us-east' -d '{"model":"rw-inference-7b-v1","input":"long context...","max_tokens":800}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Observation: when routed to eu-west the round-trip time increased by ~900ms compared to us-east routing, pushing some client-side read timeouts past thresholds.
Attached traces: trace IDs [trace-us-20260312-1102, trace-us-20260312-1126, trace-acme-98765].
Edge proxy logs show: 2026-03-12T11:22:13Z edge-router[pid=4221] WARN routing: fallback-heuristic invoked for cluster us-east-1 -> selected eu-west-1 (latency penalty logged).
API gateway metrics: 5xx spikes at 11:25-11:35Z aligning with routing decisions.
Observability links: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/trace-us-20260312-1102 , https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboard/latency/regional-routing-2026-03-12
Investigation summary:
- Scoped to smart-routing policy change deployed 2026-03-12T10:55Z (release ref rwd-routing@v2.14.0). The change introduced a fallback that preferred lower-cost regions when local capacity signals were noisy.
- Correlated BGP/peering checks showed no external network outage. Internal capacity signals (autoscaler) emitted transient 'cold capacity' marks for a subset of us-east pools between 11:20-11:28Z causing edge-router to apply fallback.
- The fallback decision logic did not weight RTT sufficiently for streaming-heavy paths; result: some long-running streaming sessions were abruptly proxied cross-region.
- Reproduced locally by toggling policy flag (route.fallback.preference=cost_over_latency) which caused 5-7% of simulated us-east requests to choose eu-west nodes.

Action items identified:
- Roll back the fallback preference change (done at 12:10Z).
- Add RTT penalty into fallback scoring and ensure streaming sessions prefer latency-minimizing routes. (PR created)
- Add a circuit-breaker to prevent routing changes mid-stream for active streaming sessions.
- Improve rollout sizing and canary metrics for Smart Router changes to capture p99 streaming latency regressions earlier.
Support (Aisha): 2026-03-12T11:27Z - Customer reports high latency and streaming disconnects for chat endpoints. Provided request IDs. Kicking to SRE.
SRE (Tomas): 2026-03-12T11:36Z - Observed edge-router fallback decisions matching reported timestamps. Rolling back routing preference now to stop cross-region fallbacks.
Engineering (Priya Kaur): 2026-03-12T11:58Z - Confirmed deploy rwd-routing@v2.14.0 introduced fallback preference change. Working on quick PR to include RTT weight and to add mid-stream protection.
Support (Aisha): 2026-03-12T12:12Z - Notified customer that we've rolled back the routing change and are monitoring. Asked customer to validate whether errors have subsided.
Customer (AcmeRetail - John Lee): 2026-03-12T12:27Z - Confirmed degradation resolved and traffic back to normal. Appreciate fast action.
SRE (Tomas): 2026-03-12T12:40Z - Metrics show p99/p999 back to baseline. Documenting post-incident follow-ups and creating engineering work items.
Temporary mitigation: Rolled back Smart Router fallback preference (rwd-routing@v2.14.0 -> previous flag state) at 2026-03-12T12:10Z which stopped cross-region routing.
Permanent fix planned: Update routing scoring to include RTT penalty for streaming endpoints, implement mid-stream routing circuit-breaker, and strengthen canary checks for routing changes. PRs: github.com/redwood/routing/pull/542 (RTT penalty), github.com/redwood/routing/pull/543 (streaming circuit-breaker).
Follow-ups: Schedule postmortem, update runbook, notify affected enterprise customers with RCA and timeline for deploy of permanent fix.
If customers need immediate protection: pin requests to a region using X-Client-Region header or customer region binding in customer console. For Dedicated customers, recommend pinning model_version and routing_policy to 'latency_preferred' until fix deploy.

Issue summary:
During an automated promote from canary -> stable for rwd-base-7b-v2 at 03/13/2026 02:40 UTC, the serving runtime returned a series of cascading fallbacks to older model variants for a portion of traffic. Root cause appears tied to prefix/KV cache warming behavior: newly promoted replicas were marked healthy and only accepted traffic before their KV cache prefixes were sufficiently populated, leading to high initial KV cache miss rates, elevated generation latencies, and a spike in internal 5xx errors from the serving runtime.

Impact:
- FoldHealth (dedicated customer) experienced ~30m of elevated median latency (token generation 2x normal) and a 6% increase in 5xx rates on their /v1/generate route.
- Some requests were routed to fallback model variants as the router enforced latency SLO-based failover, resulting in reduced output consistency for ~12% of sessions during the window.

Timeline (UTC):
- 02:40:30: Canary promoted to stable via rollout automation (weight adjustments + promote).
- 02:41:00 - 03:10:00: Observed latency and 5xx spike; auto-fallbacks detected in routing logs.
- 03:12:00: Support notified by FoldHealth; incident opened.
- 03:24:00: Temporary traffic pin to previous stable applied to reduce user impact.
- 03:48:00: Rollback of the promote completed; metrics normalized by 03:55:00.

Why this is unusual:
Promotes normally rely on a warmup phase where a subset of traffic warms caches before full weight transfer. In this case the promote automation marked nodes as promotable before warmup thresholds were met because health checks focused on CPU/gpu and not KV cache fill ratio. The router's latency-based fallback logic then diverted traffic away from warmed-but-slow instances, which cascaded into more load on already warmed instances and created instability until rollback.
1) Deploy rwd-base-7b-v2 variant with default promote automation in a dedicated pool.
2) Configure promote automation to mark replicas healthy on readiness probe passing (current setup checks GPU health and serving process only).
3) Simulate steady traffic at FoldHealth's 95th percentile for 5 minutes and trigger promote.
4) Observe KV cache miss rate, token generation latency, and router fallback events in the 0-30 min window after promote.

2026-03-13T02:41:13Z serving-runtime[peer=i-09ab]: kv_cache: miss_prefix_count=872 miss_rate=0.74

2026-03-13T02:43:02Z metrics: /v1/generate p50=210ms p95=1.1s 5xx_rate=0.063
2026-03-13T03:24:08Z support: applied pin to previous-stable variant for FoldHealth - reason=mitigate-fallbacks
Ravi Patel (Support) 2026-03-13T03:16:00: Customer reported broad degradation after promote; capturing logs and escalated to SRE.
Aisha Khan (SRE) 2026-03-13T03:20:00: Initial hypothesis: KV cache warmup incomplete -> high CPU/backpressure -> latency SLO tripped. Requested router and cache metrics.
FoldHealth SE (Jordan Lee) 2026-03-13T03:22:00: We saw model responses degrade and some sessions got older-model outputs. Would like rollback asap.
Sofia Martinez (On-call Eng) 2026-03-13T03:25:00: Applied temporary pin to previous-stable; continuing investigation into promote gating logic.
Aisha Khan (SRE) 2026-03-13T03:50:00: Promote rolled back. Monitoring shows metrics normalized; preparing post-incident actions.
Ravi Patel (Support) 2026-03-13T04:05:00: Customer notified of rollback and workaround. Offer for follow-up design review scheduled.
Hypothesis 1: Readiness probe gating is insufficient; it doesn't measure KV cache fill ratio or prefix warm hit-rate.
Hypothesis 2: Router fallback thresholds aggressiveness caused cascading failover when a subset of instances were cold.
Checked: node readiness timestamps, KV cache metrics, router decision traces, and promote automation logs (promote_controller.log).
Found: promote_controller marked 6/8 new replicas healthy within 20s of start because service process was listening; KV prefix fill averaged 12% on those nodes at that time.
Found: router has a latency-based failover that considers 200ms p95 threshold; when a few instances exceed threshold, traffic is shifted to older variants—this amplified load on older instances.
Captured PR attempt: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4821 (add kv_warmup_check to promote gating).
Runbook cross-check: rollout checklist currently recommends manual warmup for high-throughput dedicated customers; automation did not honor warmup flag for this pool.
Workaround applied: immediate pin to previous stable variant for FoldHealth followed by rollback of the promote. Root cause: promote automation considered instances healthy based on process-level readiness only and did not require a KV cache warmup threshold. Fixes deployed: 1) Emergency change to promote controller to include kv_prefix_fill_pct >= 70% as part of readiness gating for high-throughput pools (merged PR 4821). 2) Router fallback configuration softened for first 10 minutes after a promote so it prefers slow-but-warmed instances over immediate fallback to older variants (config change rolled out to prod-us-east at 2026-03-14 09:00 UTC). 3) Added a warmup-run in promote pipeline that issues synthetic warmup traffic to populate KV prefixes for promoted replicas before marking them fully promotable. 4) Post-incident: scheduled follow-up INT task to add observability dashboard for promote warmup metrics and update rollout runbook. Customer follow-up: Support team provided a post-incident summary and offered a synchronous review with FoldHealth engineers.

Issue summary: Several BrightCart customer sessions report that when an SSE stream reconnects after a short network blip, the connector resumes but the first 'choice' returned by the model is truncated (loss of leading tokens) and occasionally an extra metadata heartbeat line is injected before the first choice. Impact: Customers see partial sentences at start of resumed content, which causes downstream parsers to fail and UX to show gibberish. Affected traffic is limited to BrightCart's dedicated pool behind our edge-proxy and the vendor L7 connection-recycler. Environment: BrightCart dedicated cluster in prod us-east (dedicated GPU pool, autoscale enabled). Models served: gpt-redwood-1.3b (default route) and fallback to 3.7b for large requests.
Steps to reproduce (reported by BrightCart):
1) Open SSE stream for long generation (~>800 tokens) from a browser client behind their corporate proxy.
2) After ~40s, the connection drops (short TCP reset from client network). The client issues resume with last-offset N.
3) Load balancer (vendor connection-recycler) hands the TCP to a new upstream connection and sends previously buffered ACKs; resume arrives with offset N but with a small clock/skewed window and different TCP sequence mapping.
4) The server accepts resume and returns a first chunk that is missing 2-7 leading tokens compared to a non-resumed run.
5) Sometimes a keepalive/metadata line "event: hb\ndata: {\"seq\":X}\n\n" is delivered in front of the truncated choice and some clients treat that as part of the text.
Expected: Resume should deliver the continuation with no dropped tokens and no extra application-level metadata inserted in the payload before the resumed choice. Actual: Partial-first-choice and spurious heartbeat insertion.
Relevant logs (from BrightCart and edge-proxy):
- edge-proxy: "conn-recycler: handoff id=0x7a1b, client-offset=10123, resumed-offset=10123, upstream-session-id=..." followed by "resume-accept, assigned-session=rc-4521"
- serving-runtime: "resume-window-check: delta=8ms, window-allowed=5ms, resume-accepted (soft)" and later "stream-assemble: missing-prefix-bytes=5, assembled-length= ..., emitted-choice-id=1"
- client-side snippet: "...\n[data: {\"type\":\"hb\", \"seq\":125}]\n[data: {\"text\":\"s... story continued\"}]"
Workaround attempted by BrightCart: disabling their connection-recycler (so upstream connection reused) eliminated the truncation. Short-term mitigation: increase client-side resume offset tolerance to request a slightly earlier offset (N-8) when feasible.
2026-03-12 09:15 - Support (Ava): Initial triage with BrightCart. Customer provided edge-proxy logs and a HAR-style dump of SSE frames. They reproduced consistently when their connection-recycler is enabled.
2026-03-12 11:02 - SRE (Liam): Correlated serving-runtime logs; observed 'missing-prefix-bytes' in assembly path for resumed sessions. Hint: resume-window-check flagged a small timing delta but accepted the resume path as 'soft'.
2026-03-12 15:40 - Eng (Priya R): Noted similarity to previous partial-choice cases but different root cause: here the TCP handoff can reorder buffered control frames resulting in a shifted resume boundary. Added link to internal thread #inc-stream-resume.
2026-03-13 08:21 - Support (Ava): Customer confirms disabling connection-recycler resolves issue; asks for plan for a permanent fix because they can't disable the L7 component in their environment.
2026-03-13 14:10 - Eng (Liam): Draft fix: expand resume reassembly to include a configurable 'lookback window' and make resume acceptance strict only if sequence checks pass. Prototype in PR 548. Landing requires regression tests for multiplexing and resume idempotency.
2026-03-14 10:00 - SRE (Liam): Running canary on dedicated staging pool with PR branch; initial runs show no truncated first-choice across 200 resume trials behind a simulated connection-recycler.

Issue summary:
During a customer bulk-embedding upload window, we observed a sustained increase in 5xx responses on the embedding upload route and generation endpoints. The API Gateway reported a large number of first-byte timeouts (upstream handshake/first-byte) coincident with an embeddings shard rebalance initiated by the embeddings service. Customers reported failed bulk uploads and slow inference (time-to-first-token) for embedding-related calls.

Impact:
- NovaForms (enterprise) bulk upload jobs saw ~45% failures and degraded throughput for live embedding calls across their tenant in us-east-1.
- Elevated 5xx rate across embedding routes and downstream chat/merge endpoints that fan-out to embedding services.
- Customer-facing timeouts and billing discrepancy inquiries filed via support.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east-1 region.
- Affected services: embeddings-service (shard rebalance), serving-runtime, api-gateway, autoscaler.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a bulk embedding upload (100k vectors) against /v1/embeddings with parallelism similar to NovaForms.
2) Monitor api-gateway metrics for upstream_first_byte_timeouts and 5xx_rate.
3) Observe embeddings-service shard rebalance logs and increased eviction/compact operations.
4) Observe runtime OOM and longer KV cache warmup on some shards leading to client-side retries and apigw 502/504s.

Recent timeline (key events):
- 2026-03-12 13:05 UTC: NovaForms bulk-upload starts (customer-reported).
- 2026-03-12 13:12 UTC: embeddings-service begins shard rebalancing (reshard event triggered by autoscaler).
- 2026-03-12 13:14 UTC: api-gateway first-byte timeout metric spikes; concurrent 5xx rate rises to 12%.
- 2026-03-12 13:22 UTC: Serving runtime OOM retries on two shard hosts; consumer-facing retries amplify load.
- 2026-03-12 13:40 UTC: Support ticket opened by Priya Kapoor; SRE paged.

Initial hypothesis: shard rebalancing caused a temporary increase in cold-starts (KV cache miss, model warmup) that pushed the serving-runtime beyond memory thresholds leading to OOMs and slow first-byte responses.
Observed correlation: embeddings-service logs contain 'reshard: moving 12 segments' and several 'compact' and 'snapshot' operations at 13:12 UTC.
api-gateway traces show majority of 502/504s are 'upstream-first-byte-timeout' with long tail of retries from client SDKs that increased connection churn.
Heap profiles from two runtime hosts (host-emb-07, host-emb-09) show transient GPU memory fragmentation and repeated CUDA driver resets around the time of elevated errors.
Autoscaler activity: an aggressive scale-out policy triggered multiple ephemeral embedding workers; they competed for NVMe and caused iowait spikes on the shard nodes.
Customer note: NovaForms client used 128 concurrent connections with aggressive retry backoff disabled, contributing to thundering retries.
We confirmed that rate limiting headers were not honored by the customer's older SDK version leading to higher effective QPS than tenant SLA allowed.
Short term: temporarily paused NovaForms bulk upload on request of customer at 2026-03-12 14:05 UTC to arrest error amplification.
Short term: applied a soft rate cap at the ingress layer for the NovaForms tenant (tenant-level QPS cap) at 14:12 UTC.
Short term: temporarily disabled automatic shard rebalancing for embeddings-service for 10 minutes to allow warmed shards to stabilize (operator intervention).
Medium term: rolled a hotfix to autoscaler policy to add a conservative cool-down window during shard snapshotting (PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings/pull/221).
Customer-facing workaround: advised NovaForms to upgrade SDK to v2.7.1 which respects rate-limit headers and introduces jittered backoff.
SRE to run a focused load test mimicking NovaForms profile and validate rate caps prevent first-byte timeout spikes (owner: Ethan Brooks).
Eng (embeddings) to implement graceful resharding mode that throttles incoming bulk uploads until KV caches are warmed (owner: Maya Lin).
Product: consider exposing tenant-level bulk-upload guidance and automated preflight checks in Console.
CS: follow up with NovaForms on SDK upgrade and offer a short credit for failed run (owner: Priya Kapoor).

Additional notes:
SRE (Diego Martinez) (2026-03-12 14:30 UTC): Observed driver resets on host-emb-07/09; flagged autoscaler surge and NVMe iowait as likely amplifiers. Temporarily disabled autoscaler scale-up during snapshotting window.
Maya Lin (embeddings engineer) (2026-03-12 16:05 UTC): Put up PR for autoscaler cooldown and discussed a more conservative reshard handshake protocol. PR refs in related_github_prs.
NovaForms (Alice Wu) (2026-03-12 17:10 UTC): Confirmed paused job; will upgrade SDK and retry tomorrow with lower parallelism. Requests notes for best-practices for bulk uploads.
In Progress — temporary mitigations applied (tenant cap, paused job, autoscaler cooldown hotfix merged). Root-cause draft: aggressive resharding during heavy customer parallel bulk upload caused cold-cache warmups, autoscaler surge, and IO/GPU contention leading to upstream first-byte timeouts and elevated 5xx. Final RCA and permanent mitigations (graceful resharding, tenant preflight checks) in progress.
Finalize RCA and publish to Confluence (owner: Diego Martinez).
Add tenant preflight bulk-upload check to Console with recommended parallelism and SDK compatibility check (owner: Product).
Add telemetry alert to detect embedding shard snapshot windows + first-byte timeout correlation (owner: Observability).
Run simulated replay test to validate autoscaler cooldown under production-like NVMe loads (owner: SRE).
