payload.description:
Issue summary: After a canary rollout that introduced a tokenizer change (progressive subword merges) for redwood-small-v2-tokenizer-v1, several FinSight requests previously pinned to the customer's explicit model version were routed silently to the legacy model variant. Impact: customer observed subtle response inconsistencies and a billing spike due to reprocessing; no explicit error returned to client, requests succeeded but used fallback model. Environment: production us-east-1; Dedicated/Enterprise tenant for FinSight. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use FinSight tenant token bound to a pinned model version for redwood-small-v2. 2) Issue identical prompt batches through the SDK client while shifting canary weight from 5% to 25% for the tokenizer-enabled variant. 3) Observe per-request token counts and routing decisions in the request traces. Observed behavior: When the tokenizer change produced different tokenization for identical prompts (differences in prefix token count and EOS placement), the runtime’s pinned-version matching (which relies on a request signature computed from canonicalized token stream) failed to find a matching affinity entry and quietly fell back to a compatible variant. Because the fallback path had trace-level backpressure suppression, no 5xx or 429 surfaced; response latency increased ~60ms on average and some outputs changed subtly (e.g., newline tokenization differences). Expected behavior: Pinned sessions should honor explicit model pins regardless of tokenizer divergence; if pin cannot be honored, system should surface an explicit warning/error to tenant and not silently route without audit. Logs/traces: see trace IDs in investigation_notes below. Postmortem risk: silent fallbacks can bypass audit trail and misattribute billing and quality regressions to pinned version.
trace: us-east-1:trace-20260310-55a1c3 - request_id=ff12ab34 sample prompt 'Analyze quarterly revenue' - tokens: variant-A=28, variant-B=31 - affinity lookup failed (no pinned entry) - routed to fallback variant
Hypothesis 1: Tokenizer microservice returns non-deterministic canonicalization across variants; affinity key generation depends on exact token stream -> small changes break pin lookup.
Hypothesis 2: Orchestrator cache contains epochal entries keyed by tokenizer version; cache invalidation race during canary weight increase caused shard to present older tokenizer version metadata.
Reproducer: Deployed two tokenizer binary builds (stable and canary) to staging and ran 10k identical prompts through pinned session harness; observed 0.7% of requests dropped pin affinity when tokenizer mismatch present.
Related config: affinity-key = sha256(<tenant_id> + <model_version> + <tokenizer_version> + <first_16_tokens>) - tokenizer_version was not included in previous pin schema; changed behavior surfaced when tokenizer changed token counts across variants.
Temporary mitigation: patched proxy to include 'x-tokenizer-version' header from tokenizer-service in routing key to make affinity lookup tolerant (shim) and surfaced audit event when mismatch occurs.
Next steps: 1) Add tokenizer_version as required field in pin-generation schema and migrate active affinities (coord with orchestrator). 2) Build rollout presubmit test to detect tokenization deltas for pinned tenants. 3) Consider fallback policy: explicit error or enroll tenant into grace-mode when pin cannot be honored.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 11:15 - Support (Asha): Notified customer of investigation and applied temporary monitoring alert to flag routing decisions where pinned=true and routed_variant!=pinned_variant.
2026-03-12 13:00 - FinSight (Customer): Confirmed they saw the audit metadata on subsequent requests; still seeing a handful of mismatches — requested ETA on a permanent fix.
Workaround applied: shim to include tokenizer-version in routing metadata and audit mismatches (rolled 2026-03-12). Permanent fix in progress: update affinity schema to include tokenizer_version and run migration job to recompute pinned entries for active sessions; rollout plan pending CR approval. Customer asked for final ETA; target complete by 2026-03-19. Follow-up task INT-4412 created for migration orchestration.
payload.summary: tokenizer-rollout-mismatch-causes-silent-fallback-and-pinned-version-divergence

Issue summary:
Customer Qrious observed a sharp throughput collapse (p50 throughput ~60% of baseline, p99 token latency up to 3x) on their dedicated reserved pool in us-west-2 between 2026-03-12 09:15 and 11:50 UTC. The path to error shows autoscaler failing to provision additional GPU slots despite elevated queue depth. Primary symptoms point to an adjacent telemetry sidecar from a customer analytics adapter emitting large batched samples that coincided with a prefetch warmup, which overloaded NVLink/PCIe fabric on several nodes and caused blocked kernel IO and attach delays.

Impact:
- Customer-facing LLM requests experienced increased latencies and a 25-40% drop in successful throughput for 2+ hours.
- Failing live canary and A/B rollout for Qrious; product team escalated to support.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Deploy a reserved pool replication in a staging cluster configured to mirror customer's burst pattern (small long-lived streams + sidecar telemetry bursts every 30s).
2) Start load generator (short multi-turn chat streams at 8 rps per tenant) while enabling sidecar telemetry flood at 200MB/s sustained for 60s bursts.
3) Observe queue depth growth, delayed GPU attach logs and autoscaler failing to register capacity changes for 45-90s.

Observed logs/metrics (selected excerpts):
- serving-runtime: "attach_request=queued duration_ms=7450 reason=nvlink_io_wait"
- autoscaler: "telemetry-lag=120s; decision=hold; reason=missing-utilization-samples"
- kernel/dmesg (node-7): "nvlink: peer stall detected, retrying"
- metrics: p99_token_latency increased from 220ms -> 720ms, avg_gpu_util unchanged (~40%) but io_wait spike + NVLink error counters increased 20x.

Customer notes: Qrious runs a lightweight analytics sidecar that recently rolled a telemetry change (v2.3.4) increasing batch size and switching to persistent NVMe-backed buffers. They rolled this at 2026-03-12 08:50 UTC; problem onset closely follows.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Triage by Support (Sofia): Confirmed customer impact, raised P1. Collected relevant telemetry URLs and requested dedicated logs from node pool.
2026-03-12 11:00 - SRE (Ethan): Reproduced high attach latencies in staging when replaying telemetry burst. Observed autoscaler metrics lag — aggregator drop rate increased during burst leading to stale utilization windows.
2026-03-12 11:20 - SRE: kernel logs on three nodes show repeated NVLink stall warnings and a pattern of increased pci_io_wait which correlates with sidecar flush windows (every 30s).
2026-03-12 11:45 - Support: Notified customer with temporary mitigation steps (throttle sidecar, reduce batch size to 1MB, stagger flushes). Customer applied throttle and reported partial recovery within 6 minutes.
2026-03-12 12:10 - Eng: Performed manual scale-up (allocated two extra GPU slots) to relieve queue while autoscaler telemetry pipeline recovered. Throughput returned ~85% of baseline after scale-up + sidecar throttle.
2026-03-12 14:00 - Eng: Identified autoscaler dependency on single telemetry aggregator path; when aggregator's ingress backpressures, utilization samples drop below threshold and autoscaler holds instead of scaling.
2026-03-13 09:00 - Patch created: implement rate-limiter in sidecar ingestion path and add backpressure metrics to autoscaler decisions (PR linked).

Additional notes:
Temporary workaround: Customer throttled telemetry sidecar to <10MB/s burst and staggered flushes; Support performed manual scale-up to restore service while fixes deploy.
Short-term fix: Deployed rate-limiter and circuit-breaker on ingestion path for telemetry aggregator to prevent full buffer floods. PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4321
Medium-term actions: Improve autoscaler resilience by adding a secondary utilization signal from job-level queue lengths and per-gpu attach latency. Add tuning guide for customers running sidecars that emit high-volume telemetry.
Follow-ups: Postmortem to be authored; recommended customer change: revert telemetry v2.3.4 batch settings and apply staggered flush pattern.

Ethan Liu (SRE) 2026-03-12 11:05: Reproduced in staging. Autoscaler window missed data during ingestion backpressure; suspected NVLink events on nodes.
Priya Rao (Customer Success) 2026-03-12 11:50: Qrious applied sidecar throttle and reported partial recovery. They will hold telemetry config changes until follow-ups.
Dan Keller (Infra Eng) 2026-03-13 09:20: Rolling rate-limiter to telemetry aggregator in staging, will monitor for false positives on legitimate bursts.
Ethan Liu (SRE) 2026-03-14 08:35: Added NVLink error counters to dedicated pool dashboards; set alert threshold to 5 events/min.
Finalize postmortem and share with customer by 2026-03-18.
Ship autoscaler telemetry redundancy (secondary signal) and validate in load tests by 2026-04-01.
Create public-facing KB article with recommended sidecar telemetry best-practices for dedicated pools.
Coordinate with CS to review customer telemetry agent release (v2.3.4) compatibility checklist before future rollouts.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer's internal scheduler (cron-driven backfills) occasionally forwards work into the realtime orchestrator bridge which then issues a dense fanout of short-lived inference requests. During these bridge events FluxMetrics sees intermittent 429 responses from the Dedicated pool.

Impact:
- FluxMetrics reports 5-15% request failures as 429 during scheduled bridge jobs (15–20 minute windows).
- Affects user-facing realtime features intermittently as the scheduler backfill overlaps peak traffic.
- Customer uses a Dedicated pool with autoscaling; needs guidance to avoid 429s while keeping cost predictable.

Background / notable config:
- Dedicated pool: 4 x A100 nodes reserved, autoscaler enabled for burst to 6 nodes.
- Scheduler job creates 3000 short requests/sec for 90s bursts to warm caches, then stabilizes.
- Scheduler-originated requests currently use same API route/priority as interactive traffic.
- No special burst pool or request tagging is configured.

Customer asks:
1) Recommended configuration to prevent scheduler-bridge traffic from consuming interactive burst credits.
2) Best-practice rate-limit/refill window split for cron-originated warmups vs interactive lanes.
3) Any short-term mitigations to reduce 429s during nightly overlap windows.
1) On a dedicated tenant with mixed traffic, configure a scheduler to send 3k short requests/sec for 90s to the standard realtime route.
2) Observe rate-limit headers returned on gateway and any 429s in serving runtime logs.
3) During an overlapping steady-state interactive workload (~200 rps), repeat the scheduler burst and measure 429 rate.
4) Toggle scheduler to send same workload to a different route tagged as 'background' and compare results.
Support replicated high-level pattern in staging by running scheduled bursts and saw token accounting attribution to tenant-level burst budget rather than route-tagged budgets.
Rate-limiter logs show scheduler-originated requests use same route key and therefore same refill window as interactive traffic; no separate burst pool exists.
Autoscaler did spin up additional nodes but node arrival was delayed compared to burst duration; autoscale cold-start contributes to pressure.
Hypothesis: two contributing factors — 1) lack of route isolation for scheduler traffic; 2) burst window size too small to absorb short warmup waves.
Support (2026-03-10): Thanks for the report — we can confirm 429s correlate tightly with your scheduler warmup windows. We'll propose a configuration change and short-term mitigation.
Customer (FluxMetrics) (2026-03-10): Priority is to avoid visible 429s for end-users during morning bridge. We're open to separating route or tagging scheduler traffic.
SRE (Liam O'Neill) (2026-03-11): Proposed immediate mitigation: route isolation for scheduler-originated jobs + assign a dedicated low-cost burst pool with longer refill window (e.g., 300s). We'll provide step-by-step commands.
Support (2026-03-12): Attached sample config and rollout steps. We have a follow-up PR to add explicit scheduler-tagging to the ingest orchestrator (see linked PR).
Workaround applied: created a separate 'background-warmup' route in the customer's dedicated pool and configured rate-limiter to allocate an isolated burst bucket with a 300s refill window and a smaller sustained window for interactive traffic. Scheduler now calls the background route with an explicit header (X-Redwood-Traffic: background). Autoscaler recommended to pre-warm one node 60s before scheduled run.

Engineering follow-up: created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-orchestrator/pull/412 to add header tagging in scheduler; monitoring dashboard added to Confluence runbook.

Next steps: support to monitor nightly windows for 3 days and then consider making the route isolation permanent. Customer accepted workaround and will report back after 3-day observation window.
2026-03-11: Background route created and rate-limiter policy applied to isolate refill credits.
2026-03-11: Scheduler configuration updated to target background route header and test burst run executed — 429s dropped from ~8% to <0.5% during test window.
2026-03-12: Monitoring dashboards added to tenant console and Confluence runbook link shared with customer.
1) Add traffic-tagging to scheduler codebase (PR 412) — assigned to Eng team, ETA 2026-03-20.
2) Recommend config doc update for Dedicated tenants to include background route examples (Confluence page updated).
3) Observe production for 72 hours and reopen if >1% 429s during scheduled windows.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer using Redwood SDKs (Python and TypeScript) with a buffered-sender enabled on a private deployment observed duplicated external tool/function invocations after a short network blip.

Impact:
- External payment and audit webhooks were invoked twice for ~3% of requests during a 20-minute window.
- Customer Acme Health observed billing and downstream side-effects; they temporarily disabled automatic tool calls.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) in us-east behind customer edge proxy.
- SDKs: python-sdk v0.9.8 (buffered sender enabled), ts-sdk v1.2.1 (buffered sender equivalent).
- Serving runtime: dedicated pool (gpu-a100) running redwood-1.3.

1) Configure SDK buffered sender with batch_window=150ms and enable function/tool auto-invoke.
2) Simulate intermittent 200-500ms TCP drop between client and gateway (eg. iptables drop for 250ms).
3) Send a stream-generating request that triggers a single function/tool call mid-stream.
4) Allow the SDK to perform automatic retry and observe webhook/tool invocation count.

[2026-03-10T14:02:31Z] python-sdk buffered-sender flushed message id=abc123 seq=12
[2026-03-10T14:02:31Z] gateway received batch id=bat-77 processing
[2026-03-10T14:02:31Z] gateway ack delayed due to transient DB lock (120ms)
[2026-03-10T14:02:31Z] python-sdk retry timer expired, resend message id=abc123 seq=12 (client-side retry)
[2026-03-10T14:02:32Z] serving-runtime delivered tool-call request to webhook payment-service txn=tx-999
[2026-03-10T14:02:32Z] serving-runtime delivered tool-call request to webhook payment-service txn=tx-1000

- Initial reproduction with customer network emulation reproduced duplicate tool invocations when ack latency crossed buffered-sender flush window.
- SDKs maintain per-message local dedupe keys but the buffered sender batches multiple logical messages into one envelope; the client-side retry path will resend envelopes when no ack is received within batch_window + jitter.
- Gateway de-duplication is currently keyed on request-id header which is set per-envelope. When envelope boundaries shift due to buffering, identical logical function calls may be split across envelopes with different request-ids leading to server-side inability to dedupe.
- Observed additional factor: webhook confirmation token TTL set to 30s; duplicate calls created distinct downstream transaction IDs, complicating reconciliation.

Race between buffered-sender flush+client retry and server ack that is keyed per-envelope. Root cause likely combination of: 1) buffered sender batching semantics producing variable envelope boundaries, 2) client-side retry triggering a second envelope with a different request-id, and 3) server dedupe relying on envelope-level request-id instead of function-call content hash or idempotency token.

Workaround provided to customer: disable buffered-sender or increase batch_window to 1000ms and enable per-call idempotency token propagation (client-generated idempotency_key header) for tool/function calls.
Engineering actions planned: server-side dedupe enhancement to consider function-invocation idempotency token (accept client-provided func_id header) and SDK patch to ensure buffered-envelope retains per-call idempotency metadata when splitting or reconstructing envelopes.
Status: in-progress. Patch branches created: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime#pr/1824 and github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk#pr/579. Expected hotfix rollout to prod us-east by 2026-03-15 behind a canary.

Support (Jordan Patel) 2026-03-10: Customer reports double webhook invocations tied to SDK buffered sender. Provided initial mitigation: set AUTO_INVOKE=false and link to retry/idempotency docs.
Customer (Acme Health Eng - Priya Sharma) 2026-03-10: Confirmed mitigation reduced duplicates but not acceptable for throughput needs. They requested root cause analysis and safe fix.
SRE (Maya Torres) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with iptables delay and confirmed duplicates. Added gateway logs showing ack lag correlating with duplicates. Opened PR for server dedupe improvement.
SDK Eng (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-11: Noted buffered sender reconstructs envelopes on retry and currently drops per-call idempotency headers. Working on SDK patch to preserve per-call idempotency metadata across batching boundaries.
Support (Jordan Patel) 2026-03-12: Sent customer a recommended temporary config (batch_window=1000ms + client idempotency_key) and scheduled a canary test for 2026-03-14.
Customer (Priya Sharma) 2026-03-12: Agreed to canary and provided sample traffic pattern for validation.
payload.summary: Buffered-sender client retry window causes duplicate function/tool invocations when server ack delayed

Issue summary:
Customer Greenline Health reports a sudden drop in model quality (increased hallucinations and lower BLEU/ROUGE on validation prompts) and an associated 2.4x increase in avg token cost after a staged enablement of a mixed-precision (8-bit) quant profile together with aggressive prefix-KV prefetching on their dedicated pool. They asked for an immediate safe unwind plan that minimizes user-visible downtime and cost exposure.

Impact:
- Business impact: Several clinician-facing flows returned lower-quality summaries leading to customer complaints and possible clinical risk.
- Scope: ~12% of requests routed to the optimized pool show quality regression; bucketed by tenant_id: greenline-prod (single-tenant dedicated pool).
- Cost: token spend on pool doubled for the last 6 hours.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity: greenline-prod-dedicated-us-east-1
- Runtime version: rwinf-2.8.1
- Optimization flags: quant_profile=mixed-8bit-fast, kv_prefetch=true, async_batching=true, batch_target_tokens=4096
- Deployed at: 2026-03-05T02:10:00Z (automated staged rollout)

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send a standard set of validation prompts to model redwood/gpt-13b-8bit pinned on greenline-prod tenant.
2) Observe generation quality and token counts.
3) Compare against the prior snapshot (pre-change) - customer attached metric deltas.

Observed telemetry & logs:
- Trace IDs (examples): trace-8f4c, trace-b7d2 (included in attachments).
- Console metrics: 95th latency stable, but per-token compute utilization increased and cost-per-response doubled.
- Eval metrics: validation BLEU dropped 9 points on summary suite; hallucination rate increased from 2.1% to 6.8%.

Issue summary: Customer reports sporadic 429 responses even though aggregate request rate is within their committed throughput. Impact: Intermittent failures for two internal services (search indexing and live-catalog rerank) causing ~2–5% request failure spikes during mid-day. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east, tenant BrightSearch (dedicated contract). Steps to reproduce: 1) Use three API keys belonging to the same org and run multiplexed short-text generation (50–100 req/min per key) against /v1/generate with streaming disabled. 2) Observe 429s on one of the keys after several minutes even though overall token rate < reserved capacity. 3) Re-running with only a single key removes 429s. Logs/observations: Customer provided screenshots showing 429 responses tagged with quota_id: "org-7689-global" and sub_bucket: "key-03". They also shared a pcap showing consistent connection success, only rejected by server with 429 body referencing "per-key bucket exhausted".

Additional notes:
Initial hypothesis: per-key bucket configured incorrectly during rolling deploy leading to mismatched refill intervals for key shards.
Gateway evidence: 429 responses have header X-RateLimit-Reason: per_key_exhausted and quota_id field matches org bucket. Token consumption counts show key-03 counters incrementing faster relative to refill ticks.
SRE reproduction: Local replay with three keys reproduced 429 on key-03 when gateway version v2.9.1 was fronting quota-manager v1.7.0; alignment fixed when we forced single-version mapping (temporary workaround).
Telemetry note: observed small clock skew between quota-manager instances (up to 150ms) exacerbated by staggered refill windows. Combined with burst allowance, this caused one shard to run dry while others had tokens.
Risk assessment: Medium — affects only multiplexed multi-key setups in dedicated pools after last quota-manager deploy. No data loss, but service degradation for some keys.
Related PRs/threads: github.com/redwood/quota-manager PR #2041 (deploy) and internal slack thread #support-rate-limits archived link: slack://channel/support-rate-limits/2026-03-11
Mitigation applied: SRE rolled back quota-manager to v1.6.9 for the affected pool which restored aligned refill behavior and eliminated 429s for BrightSearch. For a durable fix, INT-4492 created to implement refill tick consensus and drift-correction logic; target hotfix release v1.7.1. Customer actions recommended: (1) split high-throughput workloads across distinct project-level buckets when using many concurrent keys, (2) enable per-key rate overrides in Console for critical keys, (3) monitor the new per-key metrics panel in Console once hotfix is deployed. Follow-up: schedule post-deploy verification with customer (assigned to Miguel) and update customer on INT-4492 progress.
payload.summary: Uneven per-key token buckets causing intermittent 429s across multiplexed API keys

Issue summary: Over the evening window (2026-03-13 21:10 - 21:45 UTC) we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses for streaming sessions originating in us-west. Error rates peaked at ~18% for streaming endpoints for tenant clipper-ai-dedicated. The apigw returned 502/503/504s and the serving-runtime logs showed repeated reconnects and a recurring worker restart loop ('hotloop'). Impact: multiple customer streaming sessions stalled or returned errors; clipper AI reports production incidents in their product and elevated latency for non-streaming tokengeneration calls that fan out to streaming subsystems.
Initial findings: metrics show HTTP/2 flow-control/window exhaustion on the API gateway connections serving streaming. Keepalive eviction events spike at the same time; connection churn increases scheduling pressure on the runtime prefetch/kvcache subsystem, causing lock contention and heartbeat timeouts. The runtime logic attempts reconnection on worker failures; with high churn this enters a hotloop where workers restart rapidly, triggering GPU watchdogs and NVML resets. Observed amplification pattern: small increase in new streaming sessions -> more keepalives -> window and slab fragmentation on proxy -> backpressure into runtime -> prefetch locks -> reconnects -> worker restarts -> 5xx wave. Hypotheses: 1) apigw's HTTP/2 window defaults are too small for high keepalive churn; 2) runtime reconnect backoff is insufficient under rapid failure; 3) kvcache prefetch lock fairness exacerbates contention for tenants with many parallel long-lived streams.
1) From a dedicated tenant in us-west, open > 100 concurrent streaming sessions with medium-length prompts (avg 1.5k tokens).
2) Maintain active long-poll (keepalive) for ~30s and then send small completion requests.
3) Observe streaming session failures and 502s from API gateway.
4) Repeatedly create new sessions to mimic tenant burst and connection churn.
Notes: This reproduces under our internal load generator; lower concurrency reduces failure percentage.
[2026-03-13T21:12:03Z] apigw: upstream 10.12.8.23 returned 502, conn_id=abc123, window=0
[2026-03-13T21:12:03Z] runtime-proxy: stream session reconnect requested: session=clipper-045, reason=keepalive-evict
[2026-03-13T21:12:04Z] runtime-worker[pid=4201]: restarting worker due to repeated handshake failure
[2026-03-13T21:12:05Z] nvml: GPU 0 reset invoked by runtime-watchdog
[2026-03-13T21:12:05Z] apigw: 503 backlog full, accept_queue=256->14
[2026-03-13T21:12:06Z] runtime: reconnect hotloop detected for worker group wg-7, restart_count=7 in 60s
[2026-03-13T21:12:10Z] scheduler: prefetch lock contention on kv-shard-11, waiters=8

Applied mitigations (2026-03-13 21:40 - 2026-03-14 03:00 UTC):
- Increased apigw HTTP/2 initial window size by 2x in canary pool and observed reduced immediate 502s.
- Pushed runtime backoff patch (adds exponential backoff + jitter) to affected runtime pool; reduced restart hotloop frequency.
- Enabled tenant ingress soft-rate limiter for clipper-ai-dedicated to cap concurrent streaming session creation at 90 for 30 minutes.
- Customer asked to throttle client reconnect attempts; they agreed to stagger reconnects for 60s during daytime.
Current status: error rate reduced to ~2% for the tenant; mitigation holding but monitoring continues.
1) Complete kvcache prefetch fairness fix and land to staging (owner: scheduler team).
2) Run apigw http2 window canary on 20% of traffic for 24 hours and monitor.
3) Implement tenant-level circuit breaker to avoid runtime hotloops during tenant bursts.
4) Produce RCA doc (owners: SRE + Runtime) with timeline and permanent fixes.
5) Customer follow-up and communicate timeline for permanent fix.
Mitigations applied reduced impact but incident remains open while permanent fixes are scheduled. No code rollback required. Planned follow-ups: kvcache fix and tenant circuit breaker. Customer notified and monitoring continues.

Next steps: increase apigw http2 window in canary pool, finalize runtime backoff change, and add tenant-level streaming ingress rate limiter as a short-term protection.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A Streamline Analytics tenant observed a silent downgrade of a subset of production requests to the compatibility variant during a hybrid canary prewarm window. The requests had previously been servicing the pinned model (redwood/chat-medium-v2) but after an orchestrator prewarm step some sessions were routed to the compat model without customer-visible errors.

Impact:
- Customer reports increased token-level cost (~+28%) and a change in response style/quality for ~2.3% of requests across their us-west dedicated pool between 2026-03-12T18:03 and 2026-03-12T18:17.
- No 5xx errors surfaced; responses were valid but lower-quality. Customer latency SLOs remained met.

Timeline (local times UTC):
- 18:01:12 Prewarm wave initiated for canary fraction (hybrid prewarm: edge+serving prewarm).
- 18:03:04 Edge health probe rebalanced several prewarm connections.
- 18:03:27 We see a burst of orchestrator commit timeouts for sticker leases.
- 18:04:00 First customer report to support via portal.
- 18:06:45 Support triaged and escalated to SRE.
- 18:12:30 Temporary explicit model_pin applied by Support to affected tenant.
- 18:17:00 Traffic normalized, issue subsided.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: dsp-usw-7 (NVIDIA A100), orchestrator v2.14.1, edge-proxy v1.9.
- Customer configured explicit model selection in route, but relies on platform sticky session behavior for long-lived sessions.

Steps to reproduce (investigative):
1) Start a controlled hybrid canary prewarm against a dedicated pool with the same tenant (use prewarm=hybrid flag).
2) Simulate a slow commit path by injecting 200-400ms latency on orchestrator commit RPCs.
3) Observe session sticker TTLs and orchestrator commit logs during the prewarm wave.

Observed behavior:
- Orchestrator logs show sticker-lease commit returned with "commit_timeout" for ~1.9% of handshakes.
- Edge routes those sessions to the compat-quant variant as a fallback path when the model_pin commit is not confirmed within the handshake window.
- No explicit pin-unset events were emitted; behavior appears as a silent downgrade rather than an explicit unpin.

Expected behavior:
- When a model_pin commit fails transiently during prewarm, requests should either retry the commit path or keep using the already-committed pin rather than steering to a lower-quality compat fallback without an explicit pin change.

Relevant logs / excerpts (sanitized):
- orchestrator[2026-03-12T18:03:27Z] commitSticker(tenant=streamline-42) -> timeout after 320ms, lease=sticker-0x7f3b
- edge[2026-03-12T18:03:31Z] routeDecision(tenant=streamline-42) -> fallbackRoute=compat-quant-v1 (reason=pin_commit_unconfirmed)
- serving[2026-03-12T18:04:10Z] modelSwitch(tenant=streamline-42) -> applied variant=compat-quant-v1 session=abcd1234

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support applied an explicit per-tenant model_pin via the admin API for streamline-42 at 18:12:30 which prevented further silent downgrades while engineering investigated.

Next steps and current mitigation:
- SRE/Eng to reproduce in staging with injected commit latency and confirm the commit-handshake code path.
- Patch orchestrator to extend sticker handshake TTL or allow edge to honor last-known committed pin until commit confirmation arrives.
- Add metric/alert for "pin_commit_unconfirmed" rate above 0.1% of handshakes for a tenant.
- Coordinate hotfix rollout (see related PR).
2026-03-12 18:05 - Support (Ava Martinez): Received report from customer via portal — they note stylistic shift in responses and cost spike. Captured session IDs and sample responses. Escalating to SRE. Slack: #support -> @oncall-sre
2026-03-12 18:07 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Observed orchestrator commit timeouts in us-west pool. Correlating with prewarm window. Adding investigation tag and pulling logs from dsp-usw-7.
2026-03-12 18:10 - Customer (Streamline Analytics, Elena Rossi): Appreciate the quick turn. We saw lower-quality outputs for ~10 minutes on a subset of users. We can keep explicit pin while you root cause.
2026-03-12 18:13 - Support (Ava Martinez): Applied explicit model_pin for tenant streamline-42 as stopgap. Confirmed zero further downgrades after pin set.
2026-03-13 09:22 - Eng (Priya Shah): Reproduced in staging by adding 300ms commit latency. Hypothesis: sticker TTL window too tight during hybrid prewarm handshake; edge treats unconfirmed commit as safe fallback. Drafting PR to lengthen TTL and ensure last-known pin is honored. See PR linked.
Hypothesis: The prewarm path creates a short-lived 'sticker' lease to claim a session for a model variant during orchestration. If the orchestrator's commit RPC exceeds the handshake window (due to transient latency or backpressure), the edge chooses a fallback variant (compat-quant-v1) for safety. Because the last-known pin remains in control-plane state but the handshake was unconfirmed, we observed a silent downgrade instead of a transient retry or hold.
Data points: commit_timeout spikes align with cluster autoscaler activity at 18:02 and an internal control-plane GC at 18:03. A small subset of sessions did not receive commit confirmation before edge route decision.
Reproducer steps validated the condition in staging. No evidence of data corruption or incorrect pin metadata; this is ordering/timeout race.
Related: orchestration timeouts increased by ~4x for a 60s window during the prewarm wave. Edge routeDecision code currently treats unconfirmed commit as 'safe' to fallback quickly to compat rather than defer.
Short-term: Applied customer-scoped explicit model_pin via admin API to hold sessions on the desired variant (already performed).
Medium-term fix (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/3456): Increase sticker commit handshake TTL from 300ms to 800ms during hybrid prewarm; add a reconciliation path where edge will honor last-known committed pin for up to 5s if commit confirmation delayed.
Rollout plan: merge to v2.14.2-stable -> staged canary on staging -> prod canary in us-west only -> full rollout across dedicated pools. Expected risk low; change is TTL/handshake handling.
Postmortem action items:
- Instrument metric: pin_commit_unconfirmed_rate (per-tenant, per-region).
- Alert: >0.1% unconfirmed handshakes for any tenant for >5m -> auto-escalate to SRE.
- Update prewarm runbook to include jittered backoff on commit RPCs and a note to not aggressively fallback within first 5s of handshake.
- Customer follow-up: share explanation and ETA for fix; offer one week of usage credit to offset cost delta (coordinating with CS and Finance).
payload.summary: Hybrid prewarm sticker expiry causes silent downgrade to compatibility variant for some tenant traffic

Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~13:50 UTC PlymHealth began reporting a widespread increase in latency and frequent streaming frame drops for batched 'session-resume' fanout requests. Impact: customer-facing chat features experienced truncated or delayed responses, and PlymHealth's SLA dashboard recorded >15% of requests exceeding the 1s p50 latency SLO during the window. Environment: production, us-east-1, heavy batched fanout path for session-resume, primarily traffic to redwood-13b-v2.

Timeline / Observed behavior: 1) 2026-03-10 13:48 UTC - first alert from internal latency dashboard (route: /v1/chat/stream) showing p95 jump from 600ms to 2.8s. 2) 13:50 UTC - PlymHealth support rep posts to #support and opens a high-priority ticket. 3) 13:55 UTC - increased 5xx rate (502/504) on streaming gateway correlating with large fanout batches from PlymHealth customer-id. 4) 14:05 UTC - mitigation attempted (rate-limit backoff configuration and temporary reduction of max_batch_size for the customer), partial improvement but intermittent frame drops continued. 5) 14:40 UTC - fallback routing to smaller model variant (redwood-7b-quant) enabled for a subset of sessions to reduce tail latency; customer escalated to enterprise success for credits and root-cause.

Steps to reproduce (internal): 1) Simulate batched session-resume requests with fanout_count >= 40 and sequence lengths > 512 tokens. 2) Observe queue depth on serving-runtime and streaming-gateway metrics (queue_length, kv_cache_miss_rate). 3) Reproduce elevated kernel-selection stalls under quantized execution path.

Immediate impact metrics: - P50 latency increased from 0.58s to 1.2s for affected route. - P95 latency spiked to ~2.8s. - Streaming frame incomplete ratio rose from 0.3% baseline to 6.4% during window. - Approximate customer error budget burn: 22% for the 1-hour window.

Current mitigation in place: - Temporary per-customer batching cap set to 8 for PlymHealth at the router layer. - Canary fallback to redwood-7b-quant for 30% of sessions (gradual). - Enabled additional streaming-gateway logging for PlymHealth session_ids and request_ids.

Customer ask: PlymHealth requests a timeline, root-cause analysis, and a credit for SLA exposure. They also asked for a durable configuration option to cap fanout per-tenant to avoid recurrence.

Desired next steps: 1) Confirm root cause (kernel/kernel-selection interactions under high fanout and long sequences, possible KV-cache eviction amplification). 2) Implement a short-term scheduler patch to prioritize session-resume small-batches and reduce preemption of streaming workers. 3) Post-incident: propose a tenant-level fanout guard and documented operational runbook. 4) Draft customer-facing postmortem and propose billing credit calculation.
2026-03-10 14:10 UTC - SRE (Rafael) hypothesis: long-sequence fanout pushes KV cache churn, causing repeated cold-cache misses and kernel-selection thrash on quantized path; leads to blocking on GPU worker and streaming timeouts.
Heap/metrics snapshot: worker_queue_depth correlated with p95 latency spikes; kernel selection latency in traces increased by 3.5x for affected requests.
Checked autoscaler events: no scale-up events coincident with first spike (autoscaler throttled due to cooldown settings) - potential capacity constraint during fanout window.
Routing logs show PlymHealth traffic had unusually large batch_size values (40-60) coming from an SDK integration they rolled out at 13:30 UTC.
Initial reproduction: lab test with synthetic fanout 48x + sequence 1024 tokens reproduced the p95 increase and streaming frame truncation in staging with the same quantized kernel config.
Related: PR #2441 contains earlier kernel-selection logic changes for quantized models; flagged for review as potential contributor.
No evidence of authentication or network-level errors; 5xx appears service-side (worker queue / memory pressure).

Additional notes:
Slack refs: #support-thread SUP-413579 (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01SUPPORT/p1640000000)
Workaround: enforced per-tenant max_batch_size at router and temporary fallback routing to smaller model for a subset of sessions reduced immediate SLA burn.
Short-term fix (merged to canary 2026-03-11): scheduler patch to yield on high kv-cache-miss-rate and prioritize streaming-critical worker slots (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2478).
Planned long-term actions: 1) tenant-level fanout limiter feature in router (spec + implementation owner: Lina Chen). 2) Revise autoscaler cooldown logic to allow emergency transient scale-up for streaming-critical routes. 3) Add a targeted regression test harness for fanout+long-sequence scenarios.
Customer remediation: proposing pro-rated SLA credit for the affected 1.5 hour window; awaiting finance approval and final calculation.
Follow-up items created: INT-? (internal task to track router limiter implementation) and a public postmortem page under OPS.
Complete RCA and publish customer-facing postmortem by 2026-03-17.
Finalize SLA credit calculation and communicate to PlymHealth by 2026-03-16.
Deliver tenant-level fanout limiter design doc and schedule implementation (owner: Lina Chen) by 2026-03-24.
Add synthetic test to CI for fanout 48x + 1k token sequences to prevent regressions.
Monitor PlymHealth traffic for 72 hours after full rollout of scheduler patch; report metrics daily to customer.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed immediate deduction of reserved capacity credits and a matching hosted-usage charge during a scheduled maintenance window. The customer runs periodic KV-cache prefetch/warmup jobs to prime models on dedicated pools. During our regional maintenance the warmup traffic appears to have been routed to hosted fallback shards and also counted against the dedicated reserved-hour bucket, resulting in double-billing and a negative provisional credit balance.

Impact:
- Customer reports ~28,000 token-equivalent deduction from reserved credits and a separate hosted usage line for the same window (~$420).
- Affects production inference for low-latency endpoints using kv-cache warmup scripts (not user-facing inference but counts toward billing).
- Customer is flagged for potential overage and has paused automated jobs until resolved.

Environment:
- Prod / us-east (primary), maintenance event in us-east-1 on 2026-03-12 02:00-03:30 UTC.
- Customer on Dedicated (reserved pool id dp-57a9).
- Endpoints affected: warmup-job route /internal/kv-warmup, pinned to model: redwood/gptx-4-qlora-8k.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Schedule KV-cache warmup job to fan out 3000 requests of 30 tokens each to pinned dedicated model during maintenance window.
2) Platform maintenance triggers fallback routing to hosted pool for a short period.
3) Customer sees immediate reserved-credit deduction and a hosted usage line for the same tokens.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate consumption recorded (reserved + hosted) for the warmup window.
- Billing UI shows reserved credits consumed at 2026-03-12T02:07 and hosted usage posted at 2026-03-12T02:08.
- Provisional invoice shows a negative credit hold and sent autopay alert.

Expected behavior:
- Warmup traffic routed to hosted fallback should be billed only to hosted usage (no reserved-credit deduction), or if reserved pool accepted traffic then fallback should not double-count. Reserved credits should reflect only actual served tokens on the dedicated pool.

Logs / evidence attached by customer:
- Warmup job logs with timestamps and request IDs (prefetch-logs.txt).
- Billing invoice snapshot and provisional line items (invoice-2026-03-12.pdf).
- Warmup request IDs sample: rq_3b7f9c, rq_3b7fdd, rq_3b80a1.

Initial investigation notes:
- Support: verified customer pool dp-57a9 shows an autoscale event and several rejected accept-connection errors coinciding with maintenance.
- Billing: provisional postback shows both a reserved-hour debit (internal tag reserved:dp-57a9) and a hosted postback for the same request ids. Timestamps are within 1 minute of each other.
- Routing: early hypothesis is a race where the routing controller forwarded attempts to the dedicated pool while the fallback proxy also accepted and forwarded the same requests to hosted shards during connection handoff. This could create two meter events: one attributed to reserved and one to hosted.

Immediate customer impact and mitigation taken:
- Support recommended customer pause warmup jobs until fix confirmed. Customer has paused jobs and requested expedited resolution.
- Finance flagged provisional invoice to prevent automated autopay for 48 hours pending reconciliation.

Next steps / action items:
- ENG (serving-runtime & routing) to confirm if there is a known race in routing handoff that emits duplicate metering events when fallback activates. Link to slack thread #incidents-routing-246810.
- Billing to correlate postback IDs and tag sources to produce a provisional credit if double-count confirmed.
- SRE to review autoscaler logs for dp-57a9 and proxy handoff timestamps (window 2026-03-12T02:00-02:10Z).
- Create a short mitigation to dedupe postbacks by request id across reserved/hosted at the reconciler layer if not already present.

Related references:
- Related incident: INC-20260312-01
- Possible linked internal ticket: INT-5102 (routing handoff investigation)
- Customer-facing doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-warmup-billing-notes

Resolution: In Progress (pending ENG confirmation and reconciler credit issuance).

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 - Support: Notified customer that we are investigating, finance has paused autopay for 48h. Requested sample request ids and warmup schedule for replay.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer started seeing intermittent 429 responses from the hosted API while maintaining long-lived multiplexed streaming connections. These 429s appeared without a corresponding spike in token or request volume reported by the customer's telemetry. Impact: Nimbus Media reported degraded live transcription quality for a small subset of sessions (approx 2–3% of active streams), causing missed words and reconnect loops in their player. Environment: prod (us-west primary, eu-west failover), Dedicated pool on reserved capacity. Steps to reproduce:
1) Open 20+ concurrent multiplexed streaming sockets from a single API key with persistent keep-alive.
2) Use a mix of synchronous (short poll) and streaming requests on the same tenant key.
3) Observe occasional 429s after ~30–90 minutes with no increase in per-token volume.

Observed headers / sample log lines:
- HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
- x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
- x-ratelimit-reset: 162
- edge-proxy: ep-14
- gateway-log snippet: "rate_limit:count=41;limit=40;key=acct:xyz-012;route=/v1/stream?session=abc"

Customer-provided snippet:
- "We see 429s only on streaming sessions that use a query param (session id). Non-streaming calls to the same route from the same key are fine."

Additional notes:
Slack cross-ref: #support thread link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234ABC/p1677654321000000
Timeline: After reproducing with a local load generator, SREs inspected rate-limiter keys stored in Redis. Found pairs of keys representing the same logical route: one with query params preserved and one with query params stripped. Counting logic in control-plane aggregates counts by the stripped form; edge-proxy was sometimes emitting counts under the unstripped form for streaming sockets. Root cause: mismatch in path normalization rules between edge (which preserved query param for routing logic) and control-plane rate-aggregator (which strips them). This produced an apparent overrun of a per-route limit because counters accumulated under two canonical keys for the same tenant+route pair. Additional contributing factor: long-lived streaming connections do periodic heartbeats counted as individual rate events; when those heartbeats are counted under the unstripped key while normal API calls are under the stripped key, the combined total can cross the threshold unexpectedly. Repro steps used by Eng: run 25 multiplexed streams with session query param, enable verbose edge logging, inspect redis keys with pattern acct:<tenant>:route:*. Evidence: redis keys list showed both "acct:tenant123:route:/v1/stream" and "acct:tenant123:route:/v1/stream?session=abc" with counts adding to the effective usage. Also saw control-plane logs where aggregation job only read the stripped keys, leaving edge-only keys to be evaluated against per-route thresholds separately.
Workaround: Ask customers to avoid embedding ephemeral session identifiers in query params for high-concurrency streaming sessions; prefer a header-based session id or route parameter that the platform normalizes. Engineering fix: edge-proxy patch (PR #4123) to normalize path keying to remove ephemeral query params before emitting rate-counts and to emit a 'normalized_route' header for downstream. Deployed hotfix to prod us-west on 2026-03-02 (edge-proxy v1.2.3-hotfix). Follow-ups: add a rate-limiter integration test for streaming sockets with query params, update runbook, and publish guidance in SDK docs about avoiding session ids in query parameters for long-lived sockets. Post-deployment: 429 rate for affected tenant dropped from ~2.5% of streams to <0.1% over 48h window. No rollback required.
Add unit+integration tests to edge-proxy and control-plane rate-aggregator for consistent normalization (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-03-30).
Update public SDK docs and quickstart to recommend header-based session identifiers for streaming (owner: Developer Experience, due: 2026-04-10).
Add metric alert for "rate_norm_mismatch" when edge emits counts under non-normalized keys (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-10).
payload.summary: Intermittent 429s for long-lived multiplexed streaming sessions due to edge path normalization mismatch

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that a subset of users lose admin/console access after SSO login to their Private deployment. The Identity Provider is sending a multi-value attribute named 'memberRoles' where values are joined by a '+' character (e.g. 'org:123+role:owner+team:infra'). After login the platform's RBAC engine receives spaces instead of '+' characters, which prevents proper role binding lookup and causes 403 on admin console routes while other non-privileged API calls succeed.

Impact:
- Several customer admins (approx 6 users) cannot access the admin console and get 403 on /console/* and /api/admin/* endpoints after SSO login.
- No data loss.
- Customer reports this is blocking an upcoming compliance audit (high business impact).

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployment on customer-managed VPC (on-prem gateway).
- Ingress: NGINX 1.19 reverse proxy in front of the private control plane (customer-managed).
- IdP: Okta (SAML 2.0) configured to emit 'memberRoles' SAML attribute with '+' separators.
- Platform version: private-control-plane v2.8.1

Steps to reproduce:
1) IdP emits SAML assertion with attribute memberRoles = 'org:123+role:owner+team:infra' for a user.
2) Request passes through customer's NGINX ingress which terminates TLS and forwards to private control plane (X-Forwarded headers).
3) User logs in via SSO; SAML assertion is accepted and user session created.
4) User attempts to access /console/ or /api/admin/ and receives 403 Forbidden.

Observed logs / traces:
- Auth service logs show normalized claim for memberRoles = 'org:123 role:owner team:infra' (spaces in place of '+').
- RBAC evaluation logs show failed role lookup key 'org:123 role:owner team:infra' not found; expected 'org:123+role:owner+team:infra'.
- No token verification errors; SAML signature verified successfully.
- NGINX access logs show SAML POST and successful 200 to control plane endpoint. No obvious 4xx/5xx at ingress.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: upstream form-decoding or header normalization (application/x-www-form-urlencoded) at the ingress or the control-plane proxy is converting '+' to ' ' (space) when attributes are treated as URL-encoded values. This is a known behavior when servers apply URL-decoding to form bodies or query strings.
- Verified by capturing the raw POST to the ACS endpoint (from IdP to ingress): the assertion XML contains attribute value with '+'. The same assertion received by the private control-plane process (after NGINX) contains spaces in decoded attribute value.
- Reproduced in internal staging by inserting a proxy that does URL-decoding of SAML attributes; RBAC resolution fails the same way.
- Workaround identified: Adjust IdP to use a different separator (comma) or URL-encode the '+' as '%2B' in the assertion values. Customer cannot change IdP config quickly due to SSO managed by central IT.
- NGINX config on customer's ingress includes 'underscores_in_headers on' and a custom request-body-filter; further, there's a configuration that rewrites plus signs for legacy reason. Customer provided their ingress conf showing a lua filter performing ngx.req.get_post_args() and re-serializing the body without preserving '+' characters.

Root cause (current best understanding):
- A custom ingress request-body handling plugin is performing form parsing which treats '+' as a space per application/x-www-form-urlencoded decoding rules and does not preserve the original XML assertion encoding. This causes downstream services (control-plane auth parser) to receive mutated attribute strings which fail RBAC key equality checks.

Temporary mitigation / workaround applied:
- Customer rolled back the custom lua POST-body filter and confirmed new log capture shows '+' preserved through to control plane. Affected admin users regained access after re-login.
- We advised re-provisioning sessions to force new authentication.

Resolution plan / next steps:
- Short term: Documented the recommended ingress behavior in Confluence and provided minimal example NGINX config that preserves SAML raw body (avoid req body parsing, use passthrough). Coordinates: Lina Chen to send patch examples and test plan.
- Medium term: Add a defensive normalization step in the control-plane SAML attribute ingestion logic to detect and preserve '+' characters in attribute values or accept alternate separators. Engineering backlog item created.
- Long term: Add an attribute-normalization toggle in private deployments to allow customer-specific decoding rules.

Customer impact resolution status:
- Workaround applied by customer; admin access restored after re-login. Customer requested follow-up to ensure this does not recur and a code-level fix in the product.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 14:30 Customer (DataNimbus SSO team - Aaron Patel): Provided NGINX config and noted custom lua body filter introduced last month for legacy telemetry. Can rollback if necessary but prefer a product-side mitigation.
Workaround: rollback ingress body filter applied by customer and re-authenticate users. Engineering to implement defensive normalization and add runbook guidance.
1) Create code change to preserve/normalize '+' in SAML attribute parsing (INT-4321). 2) Add ingress guidance to Private deployment docs and include example NGINX config. 3) Follow up with customer for verification after patch release.
This issue highlights that external infrastructure (customer-managed ingress) can mutate assertions in ways that break equality-based RBAC keys. Recommend adding detection at ingestion time for common url-decoding mutations.
payload.summary: Plus-sign ('+') in SSO attribute gets decoded to space by ingress, breaking RBAC role bindings in Private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent quality regressions during a staged canary: some requests are routed to the fallback/compat variant despite an explicit model pin. Symptoms occur only while the canary prewarm completes and last for ~5-15s per cohort.

Impact:
- SparkLoop Media (dedicated) observed ~2.3% of user requests shifted to the degraded variant during canary windows, causing mismatched outputs and a small but measurable increase in support complaints.
- Affects live traffic in us-west for their reserved capacity pool.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated - reserved GPU pool (prod, us-west).
- Canary rollout: staged slices (10% -> 30% -> 60%).
- Clients use long-lived HTTP/2 connections with keepalive; edge sidecar performs cookie path normalization.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant session contains pinned model cookie (rw-pin) and orchestrator should commit pin atomically during canary handshake so requests continue to their pinned model.

Observed behavior:
- During slice transitions some sessions fail to commit the pin; orchestrator logs show pin_commit rejected with missing cookie. Edge logs show cookie update delayed by a downstream cookie rewrite step. Requests fall back to compat variant until cookie sync completes.

1) Create a dedicated tenant with pinned model redwood/v1-7b-quant and start a staged canary release.
2) Open persistent HTTP/2 streams from a client simulator that reuses keepalive and performs reconnects every ~30s.
3) Trigger canary weight adjustment (10% -> 30%) and observe traffic for 60s around the weight change.
4) Monitor response model headers and orchestrator logs for pin_commit events.

2026-03-10T09:42:12.139Z edge-proxy[info] rewrite-cookie path=/;HttpOnly addr=10.3.44.2 delay=22ms
2026-03-10T09:42:12.139Z session-manager[debug] received-handshake tenant=SL-931 cookie_header=(empty)
2026-03-10T09:42:12.140Z serving-runtime[info] routed tenant=SL-931 -> fallback-compat variant=redwood/compat-3.4 reason=missing_pin
2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Aisha Kumar): Confirmed customer traces with timestamped headers showing pin present on client side but not visible to orchestrator at commit time.
2026-03-10 12:30 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Replayed traffic in staging with an h2 keepalive emitter and reproduced missing cookie on the canonical handshake when edge rewrite latency >15ms.
Hypothesis: cookie rewrite step in the edge sidecar can race with orchestrator commit during canary prewarm; if the orchestrator receives the handshake before the cookie rewrite is acknowledged, commit aborts and fallback path is selected.
Checked correlated metrics: edge-cookie-latency spike aligned with canary slice adjustments. No quota or auth errors observed.

Race between edge sidecar cookie-rewrite acknowledgment and orchestrator pin_commit window: orchestrator required cookie present at handshake time and aborted commit when cookie absent; edge rewrite latency occasionally delayed cookie visibility leading to transient fallback routing.
Applied a three-part mitigation: 1) short-term: orchestrator now accepts a delayed cookie up to 200ms post-handshake behind a feature flag for the affected region. 2) medium-term: edge sidecar rewrite path optimized to acknowledge cookie writes faster and emit tracing for cookie sync latency. 3) long-term: add explicit session-handshake/ack step in the canary protocol and telemetry to catch pin_commit timing mismatches. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-coordinator/pull/459 was merged and rolled out to us-west with staged baking. Customer verified initial fix; monitoring shows fallback-rate reduced to baseline.
Rollout plan: feature-flag enabled in us-west on 2026-03-12 08:30, monitor for 2 hours then expand if stable.
Post-deploy: added alert on pin_commit_failed rate >0.1% for dedicated tenants during canary windows.
Follow-up: update canary runbook and add cookie-sync latency section to the pinning-playbook confluence page.
Owner for follow-ups: Diego Martinez (SRE) and Lena Horvath (Product).
1) Instrument median cookie-write-to-orchestrator visibility latency and expose on Console per-tenant.
2) Add automated smoke test in preflight that simulates cookie rewrite latency and validates pin commits under h2 keepalive.
3) Revisit security review for accepting delayed cookie window; document audit implications.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed intermittent, high tail latency and occasional client-side request timeouts when using the API in structured-output / JSON mode. The spike happens near the end of responses where the model appears to finish tokens but the finalization/post-processing step (decoder+json postprocess) adds an extra 2–30s in some requests.

Impact:
- Affects Nimbly Health (dedicated tier) production traffic for certain prompt templates that request tight JSON arrays.
- Client timeouts seen in ~0.5% of requests during peak (requests that normally complete <800ms see 3–12s).
- Business impact: user-facing feature degradation in nightly batch workloads and rate-limited retries.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: ddc-prod-us-east-1-a (GPU: A100s, 1 shard pool)
- API: v1/generate with mode=structured_output and response_format=json
- Client: Nimbly internal service (Go), default HTTP timeout 10s

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) POST /v1/generate with structured_output schema and examples, prefer_full_json=true
2) Send prompts that produce nested arrays (3–8 items) with relatively short token outputs (~100 tokens)
3) Observe that ~1/200 requests finish text generation but hang on final bytes and exceed 2s–30s

Observed logs and artifacts:
- Request traces: span shows serving-runtime 'decode->postprocess' span stretched after last token emission.
- Sample request ids: req-us-east-1-1726, req-us-east-1-1740, req-us-east-1-1802
- S3 trace dump: final chunk was emitted by model but the decoder postprocessor waited on a flush future before returning.
- Customer provided cURL trace with timing headers showing a 9.2s delay after last token chunk.

Immediate customer workaround suggested:
- Disable prefer_full_json or switch to plain text mode (customer confirms this reduces tail episodes to ~0.01%).
- Increase client timeout to 30s for batch jobs until fix is in place.

Requested outcome:
- Root cause analysis and permanent fix so structured_output/json mode does not add long-tail post-processing latency.
- Backport/patch for Dedicated pools and guidance for on-prem/private deployments.

Additional notes:
2026-03-09 07:22 - Customer (Nimbly Health): We validated disabling prefer_full_json and saw immediate improvement. Would prefer patch rather than changing client logic long-term.
Instrumented spans show 'postprocess_validator' waiting on an I/O-bound future in ~0.7% of requests.
Root cause hypothesis: validator uses a synchronous escape/unicode normalization routine that interacts poorly with continuous decoder emission when stream buffers are small, causing an extra context switch and thread scheduling latency.
Reproducible when structured_output schema includes nested arrays and prefer_full_json=true and when final token contains closing brackets ']' or '}' sequences.
Related to recent commit runtime/decoder: optimize/json-finalizer (commit sha abc123) which changed flush ordering to attempt eager validation after final token emission — introduced a race under high concurrency.
Mitigation verified: switching validator to run on the runtime's worker pool (async) eliminated the blocking and reduced tail latency to baseline in stress tests.
Load test: 50k requests over 30m with schema-heavy prompts showed reduction from 0.5% long-tail to 0.02% after mitigation.
No evidence of GPU saturation or scheduler throttling; metric dashboards confirm CPU thread context-switch spikes during incidents.
Linked internal issue INT-402 contains lower-level thread dumps and perf traces.
Follow-up to check: ensure change safe for private customers with strict audit requirements (KMS/HSM contexts) — may require opt-in flag during rollout.
Follow-ups:
- Postmortem draft (confluence) and change to runtime tests to include structured_output schemas in CI.
- Backport to supporting releases for dedicated/private customers (release branches: release-2026-02 and release-2025-12).
- Customer success to follow up regarding client timeout changes and confirm SLA impact.
payload.summary: Decoder post-processing lag in JSON mode causing sporadic long-tail latency and client timeouts

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several Finlytics customers report inference sessions that begin streaming correctly but then terminate with a 504/connection reset after ~15-30s with no additional tokens.

Impact: Intermittent but high-severity for production traffic—~12% of long-running streaming completions are truncated, causing downstream UI failures and lost user transactions. Affects enterprise plan customers in us-east-1.

Environment: Production (us-east-1) behind customer's AWS ALB in front of our API Gateway. Customer is on enterprise plan with per-account X-Trace headers enabled and request-level session cookies.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a streaming completion request with a large system prompt + long user context (~4k tokens).
2) Ensure the session uses per-request trace header rotation (customer SDK inserts X-Fin-Trace with unique id per sub-request).
3) Observe tokens streaming for ~10–20s, then stream stops and client receives connection closed/504.

Observed behavior:
- Early portion of response arrives (TTFB normal), then no additional bytes for 15–35s before connection reset.
- Gateway logs show repeated header block growth on connection, and the edge proxy reports delayed flushes.
- Customer ALB idle_timeout was configured to 15s (non-default, customer-side).

Logs & evidence:
- Support collected request/response traces and pcap from a repro session (attached link in ticket).
- Grafana: stream_byte_rate shows a gap after initial burst; backend serving CPU and GPU utilization normal.
- Gateway debug: "proxy.buffered_bytes" increments during the idle gap; "hpack.dynamic_table_size_inuse" seen to increase across requests.

Temporary mitigation provided to customer:
- Advised Finlytics to set ALB idle_timeout to 60s as a short-term mitigation.
- Suggested SDK change to stop rotating X-Fin-Trace header on every chunk; instead attach only once per session.

Requested outcome: Permanent fix in Redwood gateway to avoid buffering stalls when header blocks grow, and a recommendation/best-practice guidance for enterprise customers around ALB timeouts and trace header behavior.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:40 - SRE (Liam): Hypothesis: repeated rotating trace cookies/headers are expanding HPACK dynamic table and causing edge proxy to buffer header blocks; combined with customer's low ALB idle timeout, streaming connection gets torn down while proxy is waiting to flush buffered data. Linking initial findings: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming/stream-byte-gaps?orgId=1
2026-03-10 14:30 - Eng (Priya Rao): Confirmed HPACK table growth reproduced. Observed proxy's flush scheduler defers flush when header block changes exceed threshold; this delay ~18s aligns with the customer's ALB timeout. Created draft PR to force immediate flush on first token after header mutation and to clamp dynamic table size for long-lived streams.
2026-03-11 07:20 - Support (Aisha): Customer applied suggested ALB timeout change to 60s as an interim step; reported reduced truncations during a 2h test window. They still prefer a platform-side fix.
2026-03-11 16:50 - Eng (Liam): Deployed config change to canary gateway nodes in us-east-1: forced flush on header rotation for streaming routes + small hpack clamp. Monitoring closely.
2026-03-12 09:05 - Support (Aisha): Customer verified in production for 24h; truncation rate dropped from ~12% to <0.5%. Customer satisfied; asked for follow-up runbook and SDK guidance to avoid header rotation.
Reproduction: Created a long streaming request with per-chunk header rotation to simulate Finlytics SDK behavior. Observed sequence: initial headers -> first chunk (flushed) -> subsequent chunks paused (proxy buffered) -> header mutation observed (new X-Fin-Trace) -> proxy deferred flush due to internal coalescing policy -> ALB idle timer (15s) expired -> ALB reset connection.
Root cause hypothesis validated: three contributing factors:
1) Customer-configured short ALB idle_timeout (15s) lowers tolerance for short pauses between bursts.
2) Customer SDK rotates a heavy header (X-Fin-Trace) per sub-request, causing HPACK dynamic table growth and larger header block encodings.
3) Gateway edge proxy has a write-coalescing policy that defers small flushes when header block changes are detected to optimize throughput; this delays downstream bytes long enough to hit the ALB TTL.
Data: hpack dynamic table size increased by ~30% over session; proxy.buffered_bytes peaked shortly before reset. No CPU/GPU saturation. No model-level errors.
Related artifacts: Grafana stream gap panel, edge-proxy debug log IDs: edge-logs-20260310-1018, pcap attached: fin-req-20260310-0941.pcap
Actions taken:
- Short-term: Recommended ALB idle_timeout increase to 60s to customer and flagged as accepted.
- Platform fix (deployed canary 2026-03-11): changed gateway streaming flush policy to ensure first non-header payload after a header mutation is flushed immediately (removes coalescing delay). Added a clamp on per-connection HPACK dynamic table growth for long-lived streaming connections to limit header-encoded bloat.
- SDK guidance: Created a best-practice note recommending attaching trace identifiers at session-level instead of per-chunk to avoid repeated header churn.
Verification:
- Canary metrics in us-east-1 show truncation rate reduced to <0.5% for Finlytics traffic after change. No adverse effects on throughput or latency for short completions.
Follow-ups (backlog):
- Implement a gateway config toggle to allow customer-side override of flush aggressiveness per route.
- Add a linting check in SDK templates to warn on per-chunk trace header rotation.
- Postmortem to be published in Confluence linking PR and testing results.
payload.summary: Mid-stream inference sessions abort after long header growth and proxy buffer flushes

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers report that request-level traces are intermittently absent from the Console request timeline for a subset of calls originating from HelixHealth's production workspace. At the same time, alert notifications tied to error-rate thresholds are arriving 8–12 minutes after the incident onset. Both symptoms started after HelixHealth updated their retention TTL for trace events from 30d to 7d via the Console UI on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- HelixHealth (enterprise) cannot correlate failed inference requests with trace spans for debugging.
- Delayed alerting increases mean time to detect for SLA-impacting errors.

Environment:
- Redwood Console (hosted) - prod region us-east.
- Affected workspace: helixhealth-prod (customer attached account).
- Model: gpt-redwood-14b-v2 pinned on latest-serving revision.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) In HelixHealth prod, issue inference calls that occasionally return 5xx or streaming disconnects.
2) Open Console > Requests > select a request ID seen by the customer.
3) Expect to see trace timeline with span breakdown; sometimes timeline is empty or shows only top-level request event.
4) Trigger an error spike (simulated by replay) and observe alert delivery time in Slack webhook and email. Notifications are delivered 8–12 minutes after the spike begins.

Observed behavior:
- ~30% of failed requests in a sampled period show no tracing spans in the UI.
- Alerting pipeline shows processing lag; queue depth increases at the time of spikes.

Expected behavior:
- All instrumented requests should surface spans and the full timeline in Console within seconds.
- Alerts should evaluate and deliver within configured evaluation window (default 1 minute) and notify stakeholders promptly.

Attachments/logs:
- Customer provided two request IDs and timestamps (attached in ticket).
- Support grabs from request logs and alerting metrics: link to support S3 bundle attached.

Note: Customer changed trace-retention TTL immediately prior to the incident; they believe the UI change may have triggered a backend compaction / reindex operation.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:05 - SRE (Anya Sokolov): Observed a background retention compaction job kick at 2026-03-09T23:42Z for tenant helixhealth-prod. Compaction ran across several storage shards in us-east; some shards reported transient resource contention (IO wait). Collecting alert pipeline metrics and queue lengths now.
2026-03-10 12:40 - Eng (Leo Martinez - tracing): Reproduced missing spans in a synthetic load against a canary workspace when we simulate retention TTL change followed by compaction. Hypothesis: index compaction temporarily disables span-extraction worker for affected shards leading to a short window where spans are persisted but not indexed to the query store, so Console queries return incomplete timelines. Working on a fix to make compaction non-blocking for indexing.
2026-03-10 14:20 - SRE (Anya Sokolov): Alerting pipeline backlog correlated with a downstream Kafka consumer rebalancing when compaction increased partition lag. Consumer lag peaked at ~1.2M messages and processing latency jumped causing evaluation delays. We're throttling compaction on remaining tenants as mitigation.
2026-03-12 16:02 - HelixHealth (Customer comment via email): Reported that earlier missing traces are now populating after reindex and new alerts triggered within expected windows. Asking for postmortem and suggestions to avoid future disruption when changing retention settings.
Initial correlation: TTL change triggered compaction job starting 2026-03-09T23:42Z on helixhealth-prod tenant.
Storage observation: compaction caused increased disk IO on several trace store shards (s-us-east-04, s-us-east-05). IO wait increased to 85% for 12 minutes.
Indexing behavior: compaction path originally paused span-indexer worker to avoid conflicting writes; this created a short period where spans were accepted but not indexed into the query search store.
Alert pipeline: Kafka consumer group 'alerts-evaluator-us-east' experienced rebalances tied to retention job causing message-processing latency to increase; evaluation windows missed and notifications delayed by ~8-12m.
Reproduction: Created canary workspace, changed TTL from 30d -> 7d and observed same sequence: compaction -> indexing pause -> missing spans in Console queries -> alert evaluation lag. Reproducible on staging with synthetic traffic.
Risk assessment: Non-zero risk for other enterprise tenants that perform bulk retention TTL updates during peak traffic windows. Impact limited to trace visibility and alert timeliness, not to core inference serving (tokens still processed).
Mitigation applied 2026-03-10: Paused retention compaction for remaining scheduled jobs for 3 hours; increased alerting consumer concurrency for helixhealth-prod to drain backlog.
Hotfix rolled 2026-03-12: compaction changed to asynchronous index-updates to avoid pausing span-indexer. Deployed to us-east with canary and monitored for 48h. Commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/commit/2f9b7c3f.
Reindex performed for helixhealth-prod to backfill missing span indexes; previously missing timelines now available. Provided reindex report to customer (attached).
Follow-ups assigned: INT-411 to add throttling for tenant-wide heavy retention ops; INT-412 to add runbook steps and a Console warning modal for retention changes during high-traffic windows.
Customer communication: Sent summary email and scheduled a 1:1 postmortem with HelixHealth for 2026-03-16. Customer confirmed improved behavior and requested clear UI guidance before changing retention TTLs.
Status: Monitoring — no new recurrences observed in us-east as of 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC. Marking customer ticket resolved when HelixHealth acknowledges PM and runbook items; support will keep ticket open until postmortem meeting completes.

comments: 2026-03-11T03:00:00Z Runtime Eng: Reproduced use-case on staging with edge probe enabled. Observed KV shard lock wait >20s and inability to evict pinned entries while streaming sessions held references. Patch candidate: add soft-timeout on pin references and incremental eviction.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Retail, enterprise) reported a sustained increase in 5xx errors for short streaming and small-embedding requests originating from the us-east edge. Errors began ~2026-03-11 01:40 UTC and persisted with intermittent recoveries. Impact: elevated error rate (10-20% for the tenant window), failed inference calls, and downstream retries that increased load.

Observed behavior:
- API Gateway returning 502/503 to the customer for short streaming sessions and small embedding batches.
- Upstream serving runtime processes OOM-kill or crash-loop shortly after edge bursts.
- KV cache metrics show long-lived shard locks and high resident set size on a subset of runtime pods.

Expected behavior:
- Short-lived keepalive/multiplexed probes should not pin KV cache shards or escalate memory, and API Gateway should return graceful 429 or backpressure rather than widespread 5xx.

Impact:
- Customer-facing failures for Acme Retail storefront features during peak sync windows. Potential revenue impact for feature gating and degraded user experience.

1) From an edge node in us-east, open ~400 concurrent short streaming connections (2-4 tokens per message) using keepalive multiplexing.
2) Interleave small embedding batch requests (size 8-16) every 10s from same IP range to simulate batch-sync behavior.
3) Observe API gateway responses and runtime pod memory/kv-lock metrics over a 5-10 minute window.
Sample logs (truncated):
[2026-03-11T01:41:12Z] apigw: conn=1972 from=54.174.x.x route=/v1/embeddings status=502 upstream=runtime-12
[2026-03-11T01:41:14Z] runtime-12: ERROR: kv_shard=45 lock_wait=23.9s resident_rss=12.5Gi OOM-kill triggered
[2026-03-11T01:41:15Z] apigw: upstream reset on runtime-12: connection closed
[2026-03-11T01:41:20Z] runtime-9: WARN: heavy-prefetch detected, pinned_keys=812 latency_ms=1200
[2026-03-11T01:42:05Z] orchestrator: restarted runtime-12 due to OOM; restart_count=3

Initial hypothesis: an edge multipath health/probe pattern combined with heavy connection multiplexing caused repeated small requests to target the same KV shards, leading to lock contention and progressive RSS growth. This produced OOMs on a small subset of serving runtime pods which upstream API Gateway then surfaced as 502/503.

What we measured:
- apigw 5xx rate for tenant window spiked from 0.3% baseline to 18% for 20m.
- Runtime pod set (runtime-9..runtime-14) showed cumulative RSS growth correlated with pinned KV entries; GC churn high but insufficient to release due to pinned references.
- Network traces show repeated CONNECT/PROBE sequences from an edge multipath probe feature that rebalanced requests across a small hot-shard set.

Hypotheses tested:
- Disabling multiplexed keepalive at edge reduced new pinned allocations (tested on canary edge) and incoming 5xx dropped to ~2.1% within 6m.
- Forcing KV shard rebalancing did not immediately free memory because pinned entries were held by in-flight streaming sessions.

Next investigative actions assigned to SRE/Runtime: heap dump analysis, kv-shard ownership timeline, and edge probe configuration audit.
2026-03-11 02:05 UTC - Support (Anika): Confirmed customer observed errors starting 01:40 UTC. Collected request IDs and tenant window. Escalating to SRE due to OOMs reported on runtime pods.
2026-03-11 02:20 UTC - SRE (Diego): Rolled a temporary routing change to avoid runtime-12; monitored memory. Noted that runtime-12 restart_count=3 and RSS hit > 12Gi before OOM. Continuing analysis.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 04:10 UTC - Support (Anika): Customer acknowledged mitigation (routing change) reduced immediate errors but requests still see degraded latency. Asking for ETA on fix and recommended customer-side retries/backoff.
2026-03-12 09:30 UTC - SRE (Diego): Applied edge config change to disable multipath probes for affected PoP (canary then broad). Observed drop in 5xx to ~1.8% across tenant within 10m. Preparing coordinated runtime patch rollout.
Mitigation applied:
- Edge operators disabled multipath probe feature for the us-east PoP (canary then full) to stop hot-shard targeting.
- Routing change removed traffic from runtime-12 and sibling pods showing OOM behavior.
- Temporary throttle guidance sent to Acme Retail to lower concurrent streaming sessions until runtime patch deploy.
Permanent fix planned: runtime team implemented a patch to make KV cache pins time-bounded and to add soft-eviction for long-held streaming references. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8021. Rollout plan: canary on staging -> canary in us-east pool -> global during low-traffic window (ETA 2026-03-15).
1) Runtime: merge soft-eviction patch and schedule canary deploy (owner: Lina) - target 2026-03-14
2) SRE: add alert for rising KV pin ratio and RSS growth on small subset of pods (owner: Diego) - target 2026-03-13
3) Edge: audit multipath probe configuration and add safeguard to avoid shard-affinity (owner: Marcus) - target 2026-03-16
4) Support/CS: send post-incident summary and recommended client retry/backoff guidance to Acme Retail (owner: Anika) - target 2026-03-13
payload.summary: Edge multipath probe causes 5xx surge and serving runtime OOMs via KV cache pinning
