payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a traffic spike for BrightCart's dedicated tenant we observed a sustained increase in 502 responses from the API Gateway that correlated with a wave of upstream runtime worker restarts. Errors appeared primarily on streaming endpoints and high-concurrency batch endpoints.

Impact:
- ~7% of API calls returned 502 over a 18-minute window (2026-03-12 10:42-11:00 UTC).
- Latency P95 increased from 120ms -> 2.4s for affected routes.
- Customer reported degraded product experience in checkout flows.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant: BrightCart (tenant id: bc-8421)
- Deployment: prod, region us-east (some spillover to us-west due to cross-region routing)
- Models in flight: redwood/approx-3B (pinned), fallback: open/llama-2-7b

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant traffic ramped from normally steady 120 RPS to ~900 RPS over ~90s (gradual replica fan-out).
2) API Gateway started applying load-shedding (configured max-queue-length=750, backoff policy=reject-immediate).
3) A subset of streaming sessions received connection resets; API Gateway returned 502 for those requests while upstream runtime workers experienced watchdog restarts (SIGABRT) shortly after.
4) Autoscaler attempted to spin up extra runtime workers but prefetch and KV-cache thrash kept per-worker memory high leading to additional restarts.

Observed logs / metrics (summary):
- apigw: "rejecting request: queue_length=752, policy=reject-immediate" (10:43:21 UTC)
- runtime watchdog: "worker-12 killed: evicted due to memory_pressure, uptime=00:00:45" (10:43:22 UTC)
- runtime: repeated OOM-like memory pressure despite free system memory; per-worker RSS spiking to 95% of container limit (10:43:23-10:45:00 UTC)
- tracing: requests that got 502 have upstream remote_close / connection_reset entries, not 4xx client input errors.

Hypothesis / root-cause (working):
The API Gateway's load-shedding threshold was tuned for short-lived HTTP requests and rejects connections aggressively once queue length exceeded configured limits. The serving runtime uses a different health signal and can restart workers (watchdog) when per-worker memory or prefetch stalls happen. During the tenant spike, gateway rejections caused a retry amplification from the customer's client SDKs and the runtime entered a feedback loop: increased connection churn -> KV cache invalidations/prefetch -> higher per-worker memory -> watchdog restarts -> more upstream failures returned as 502s by the gateway. Essentially, load-shed policy mismatch + retry amplification caused transient overload and worker restart storms.

Temporary mitigation applied (by SRE at 10:58 UTC):
- Increased API Gateway max-queue-length to 1100 to reduce immediate rejects for BrightCart tenant (target: lower retry amplification).
- Enabled graceful-fallback route for streaming to send traffic to fallback model (open/llama-2-7b) after 5s queue wait instead of immediate reject.
- Disabled aggressive prefetch for the tenant via runtime per-tenant config (reduced per-worker memory footprint).
- Kicked stale keepalive connections and adjusted keepalive timeout from 120s -> 30s to free ephemeral ports.

Current status / next steps:
- Incident mitigation reduced 502 rate to ~0.5% by 11:05 UTC; latency back to baseline by 11:15 UTC.
- Engineering to schedule a coordinated change: apigw and runtime must share a unified load-shed health header so gateway can make reject decisions based on real-time runtime pressure metrics (PRs linked).
- Follow-up: implement client-visible Retry-After headers and backoff guidance for SDKs to prevent amplification.
- Postmortem assigned and timeline to be created in Confluence (owner: Marco Rivera).

Resolution notes (proposed):
- Short term: keep apigw queue-length safety increase and per-tenant prefetch disabled for BrightCart for 72 hours and monitor.
- Medium term: land apigw runtime health API and add adaptive shedding that considers runtime memory pressure; add guardrails in SDKs around retry amplification (circuit-breaker on the client).

Attachments / links:
- Dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant/brightcart-502-spike
- Packet traces and thread dumps: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/SUP-462019/


Additional notes:
2026-03-12 12:05 UTC - BrightCart (Customer): Thanks — we saw improvements after the changes, but will provide SDK logs for retry patterns. Please keep us updated on permanent fix timeline.
2026-03-13 09:40 UTC - Product (Nina Zhao): Recommend we add a doc note to the Dedicated onboarding guide about tenant-specific load-shed tuning and SDK retry guidance. Adding as follow-up action.
payload.summary: Intermittent 502s during tenant spike due to load-shedding policy mismatch between API Gateway and runtime

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customers that save dashboard variables using a regex capture group (e.g. /service-(.*)/) observe that trace links generated by the dashboard truncate the 'span_anchor' query parameter. When users click the trace link, the trace service returns a 500 and the console shows 'Trace lookup failed: invalid anchor'.

Impact: Aurora Health reported multiple users unable to jump from dashboard panels to corresponding traces for ~18 panels across several org projects. This blocks debugging of production LLM latency spikes for the customer and prevents normal incident triage. Approx 8% of dashboard-to-trace clicks from the affected org returned 500s over the last 24h.

Environment: prod (us-east), console v3.12.4 edge, tracing-service v2.7.1, query-engine v5.3.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a saved dashboard variable with 'Regex (capture)' type and pattern: /svc-(.*)/
2) Use that variable in panel queries and enable trace links (panel -> Trace ID link).
3) Save dashboard and click the generated trace link for a panel row where variable resolved to 'svc-payments-123'.
4) Observe redirect to /traces?trace_id=...&span_anchor=svc-payments-123 but the span_anchor value appears truncated on the trace service side and a 500 is returned.

Expected behavior: Trace links should include the full expanded variable value for span_anchor and redirect to the trace viewer without error.

Actual behavior: span_anchor is truncated at first hyphen when variable was produced via regex capture (e.g. 'svc-payments-123' becomes 'svc'). Trace service raises a 500: "invalid anchor format".

Logs/observations: Frontend console shows URL encoded parameter span_anchor=svc%2Dpayments%2D123 but tracer-api logs show incoming span_anchor=svc. Backend query-engine appears to be doing an extra tokenization step when variable origin is flagged as 'regex-capture'. No errors appear in console logs when variable comes from a plain text variable.

Temporary workaround: 1) Edit dashboard variable to be 'Text list' instead of regex capture, or 2) modify regex to include entire string in a single capture group without hyphens (not practical for many customers). Support can advise Aurora Health to change variable type as a stopgap.

Customer impact and urgency: Enterprise customer, active incidents in their product team. Customer requested elevated support and requested a Hotfix or rollback.
2026-03-12 09:22 - Evan McClain (Support): Customer reported: 'After saving a regex variable our trace links break. Help!'. Initial triage indicates pattern with capture groups correlates with failing trace lookups.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 07:58 - Evan McClain (Support): Notified customer we will attempt hotfix deployment to staging today and provide ETA for production. Customer requested targeted deploy to their org only if possible.
2026-03-12 10:12 - Repro: Created dashboard variable /svc-(.*)/; panel link built as expected in frontend; service request to tracer-api shows span_anchor=svc.
Hypothesis: query-engine normalization is applying a split on '-' to all variables originating from regex captures for historical reasons (legacy tokenization for older dashboards).
2026-03-12 11:00 - Review of commits: Identify commit 3b9f7a2 (console: variable-normalize) introduced change in v3.12.3. That commit added tokenize_var_parts() and marked regex-capture origin for special handling.

Correlated to dashboard trace links where span_anchor lacked expected colon separator.

payload.description:
Customer reports a slow, progressive drop in dedicated-pool throughput starting ~2026-03-11 10:00 UTC. P50 throughput steady but p99 and overall throughput have trended down over 8-12 hours, despite no recorded GPU driver errors. Symptoms looked like a noisy-neighbor allocation issue but was reproducible only under the customer's traffic pattern. Attach: dashboard snapshots, allocator logs. Impact: customer observed ~30% lower completed inference requests/hour on reserved pool; some requests hit autoscaler fallbacks to shared capacity.
1) Customer runs sustained short-lived chat requests (median context 256 tokens, request duration 100-300ms) with a 5s keepalive between streams.
2) Traffic pattern has many clients opening long-lived HTTP/2 streams but not sending traffic continuously (idle connections with periodic pings).
3) Over several hours, dedicated pool p50 stable but total active GPU slot count drops and request queueing increases; autoscaler triggers fallback routing.
allocator: lease_granted gpu_slot=slot-3f2a owner=conn-192.168.10.5 ttl=3600s
sidecar-proxy: connection id=conn-192.168.10.5 state=IDLE last_active=2026-03-11T11:02:17Z keepalive=5s
runtime: kv_cache_alloc_count=4321 gpu_attach_success=99.9% gpu_attach_fail=0.1%
scheduler: active_slots=124 target_slots=160 idle_slots_reserved=32 pending_requests=48
Initial hypothesis: noisy tenant or heavy mini-bursts causing allocator to fragment slots. Dashboards did not show typical short streaming fanout spikes.
Observed: a subset of customer-side connections held GPU leases far longer than request duration. Leases show TTLs ~1h with no active inference traffic for many minutes, preventing reuse and reducing effective pool capacity.
Recreated pattern in staging by simulating many clients opening streams and retaining them idle with 5s TCP/TLS-level keepalives. Staging reproduced gradual drop in available active slots similar to prod.
Root cause: customer SDK (v1.x) behavior opened a persistent sidecar connection per logical user/session and performed aggressive keepalives that prevented the sidecar and allocator from detecting inactive leases. The serving runtime treats the connection as in-use while the sidecar held the slot, which effectively leaked slot capacity under high connection cardinality.
Contributing factor: allocator TTL/idle-detection thresholds were conservative to avoid evicting legitimately long-running sessions; this interacted poorly with the customer's pattern of many short requests with long-lived idle connections.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 MapWise Support (customer): We don't see errors on our side; SDK keeps a session per user and uses connection pings every 5s for NAT traversal. We can try a client change if recommended.
Workarounds:
- Short-term: instruct customer to upgrade SDK to >=2.1.3 (beta) which enables connection pooling and extends keepalive interval (recommended 30s) which prevented slot leaks in our repro.
- Platform-side: deployed canary allocator heuristic (feature flag: allocator.idle_preempt=true) in us-east dedicated cluster. Heuristic frees slots with no active RPCs for >120s even if connection remains open.
Permanent fix / follow-ups:
- Engineering to land PR to sidecar-proxy (PR #412) to surface protocol-level idle signals so allocator can detect true inactivity without relying on TTL only.
- Update dedicated-pool runbook: add 'idle-connection leak' section and a dashboard for idle_slot_ratio and per-tenant connection_cardinality.
- Outreach: coordinate with MapWise to fully roll out SDK change and validate production stability over 72h window.
Status: partial workaround in prod canary (us-east) and customer pilot successful. Remaining: full sidecar change and allocator tuning across regions.
payload.summary: Idle client connections holding GPU slots -> slot leasing leak and gradual throughput drain on Dedicated pool

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a 3x unexpected invoice increase for the billing period starting 2026-02-28. BrightMap's invoice shows duplicated line items labeled 'tool-invoke' and 'async-postback' for a 6-hour window on 2026-03-05. Impact: immediate billing overage and accounting reconciliation failure for finance team. Environment: BrightMap runs a Private deployment (VPC) in us-west-2 with a hosted fallback configured for egress outages. Observed behavior: during a transient egress outage (VPN tunnel flap) the private deployment routed traffic to hosted fallback; multiple postbacks from the tool-invoke worker queue were retried and recorded twice by the postback-reconciler, resulting in duplicate metering events that rolled into finalized invoice lines. Expected behavior: fallbacks should not cause duplicate metering; reconciler should deduplicate by postback fingerprint and idempotency token. BrightMap believes this is a billing-system bug and requests a provisional credit and details for audit.
1) Configure a Private deployment with hosted fallback enabled for egress failures.
2) Trigger a short VPN tunnel outage (~5-10 minutes) to force fallback routing for in-flight tool-invoke requests.
3) Ensure tool-invoke worker is configured to use async postbacks with retry=3 and no jitter to simulate burst retries.
4) Observe postback-reconciler logs and billing events for duplicate fingerprints and duplicated invoice lines.
2026-03-05T10:12:03Z postback-worker tool-invoke id=tvk-0001 attempt=1 routed=private
2026-03-05T10:12:07Z postback-worker tool-invoke id=tvk-0001 attempt=2 routed=hosted (fallback)
2026-03-05T10:12:07Z postback-reconciler ack received postback_id=pbk-9f3d status=processed billing_event=created token=fingerprint-abc123
2026-03-05T10:12:07Z postback-reconciler ack received postback_id=pbk-9f3e status=processed billing_event=created token=fingerprint-abc123
2026-03-05T10:12:09Z billing-processor emitted invoice_line id=inv-99101 description=tool-invoke count=1 amount=12.00
2026-03-05T10:12:10Z billing-processor emitted invoice_line id=inv-99102 description=tool-invoke count=1 amount=12.00

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 Customer (BrightMap, J. Alvarez): Appreciates quick triage; requests detailed postmortem and assurance this won't recur. Asks for timeline for credit and permanent fix.
Idempotency investigation: reconciler dedupe key currently uses (fingerprint, gateway-id, timestamp-window). When gateway-id differs (private vs hosted) dedupe fails even if fingerprint identical.
Root cause hypothesis: during fallback, postback retried from hosted path assigned a new postback_id and gateway-id, so reconciler treated as distinct event and emitted separate billing_event.
Reproducer: integration test created that forces postbacks with identical fingerprint but different gateway-id; billing_event duplication reproduced consistently.
Temporary mitigation considered: billboard a patch to reconciler to ignore gateway-id when fingerprint matches and timestamp delta < 1 minute for tool-invoke events; need sign-off from billing to avoid deduping legitimately distinct events.
Edge cases: system must not merge two unrelated events that happen to hash-collide fingerprint; add a secondary check using invocation_id and api_key when present.
Related code: postback-reconciler service and billing-processor pipeline. See PR attempt: https://github.com/redwood-inference/postback-reconciler/pull/842 (WIP)
Potential customer impact: invoice overcharge during short egress incidents where retries cross gateways; frequency low but high-dollar customers affected when tool-invokes are high-volume.
1) Issue provisional credit for duplicated invoice lines for BrightMap and notify finance (assigned: Marco Ruiz).
2) Merge reconciler patch to change dedupe key logic for tool-invoke events (owner: postback team).
3) Add integration test to prevent regressions for fallback scenarios (owner: QA).
4) Schedule postmortem with BrightMap and internal teams; publish runbook updates for private-hosted fallback accounting (owner: Support / SRE).
5) Monitor billing events for similar duplicates across enterprise customers for 72 hours after deploy.

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a staged weighted traffic shear for tenant clearpath-health, a subset of requests drifted from the intended version-anchor and were transparently routed to the fallback (degraded) variant without explicit error or an increase in 5xx counts. Behavior observed during a 20%->40% traffic shear window.

What happened: The serving mesh experienced repeated short-lived reassignments of the tenant's version-anchor (oscillation). When a request hit an orchestrator epoch where the anchor did not match the edge replica's local pin state, the routing decision fell back to the backup variant. Because the responses were valid, the customer application saw correct responses but with degraded latency and quality compared to the pinned model.

Why this is critical: ClearPath Health uses model pinning for deterministic clinical prompts; silent routing to a degraded variant can change output quality and violates expected model guarantees. The customer noticed increased subtle hallucinations and higher token latency for a subset of requests.

Approximately 4.7% of tenant requests during the shear window were served by the fallback variant. Customer reported quality regressions on clinical summarization workflows and increased per-request latency (~120ms median increase). No 5xx spike; business impact is data integrity risk for clinical customers.
2026-03-13 09:12 UTC - Staged traffic shear initiated (20% -> 40% weight) for rwft-7b-quant
2026-03-13 09:17 UTC - Customer Slack #support-msg: reports of lower-quality summaries and slight latency increase
2026-03-13 09:20 UTC - Observability alert: small latency bump in edge-proxy per-tenant histogram (us-east)
2026-03-13 09:24 UTC - Support triage began; initial hypothesis routing mismatch
2026-03-13 09:35 UTC - Temporary rollback of traffic shear to 0% to stop further divergence
2026-03-13 10:01 UTC - Engineering replicated in staging and confirmed version-anchor oscillation under synthetic shear
Prod control plane (managed) with dedicated GPU pool for customer. Edge proxies in us-east fronting orchestrator shards. Orchestrator version: v1.21.3; serving runtime: v3.6.2 (KV cache enabled); edge-proxy: v2.9.1. Canary config used: staged shear with prewarm replicas. Pin model: rwft-7b-quant@2026-03-10-abc123. Backup variant: rwft-7b-quant-compat@2026-02-28-compat.
1) Create tenant-scoped rollout in staging that mimics production staged shear (20->40% over 10 minutes)
2) Prewarm target replicas and ensure orchestrator and edge-proxy epoch counters are unsynchronized (simulate small clock skew by delaying edge heartbeat)
3) Issue high QPS tenant-scoped requests with pinned-version header set and observe per-request routing decisions via debug route header X-Redwood-Variant
4) Monitor for short-lived variant flips correlated to orchestrator epoch boundary events
Edge-proxy logs show routing decisions where X-Requested-Version header present but local pin_lookup returned stale anchor; orchestrator log lines indicate "epoch_consensus=failed" and epoch mismatch at 09:16:47 UTC. Per-tenant routing histograms show a transient shift of ~4-5% of requests to backup variant. KV cache hit-rate stayed stable. No 5xx in the period; token latency histogram shows a tail shift. Relevant log excerpts saved to S3: s3://redwood-support/logs/SUP-482410/epoch-mismatch-09-16.log
Hypothesis A: Orchestrator-Edge epoch handshake timing plus staged shear increases the chance of local pin state being sampled pre-commit, causing fallback routing when the orchestrator later commits a different anchor.
Hypothesis B: Prewarm mirror write path may not immediately reconcile local replica pin cache; combined with rapid weight change (shear) this surfaces oscillation.
Reproduced in staging when artificially delaying edge heartbeat by 200-500ms and running 150 qps of tenant-scoped traffic. Observed same transparent degrade pattern.
Checked related subsystems: TTLs for anchor cache are 12s; commit window is 2s; under shear the commit cadence increases — race observed between commit window and TTL refresh.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-13 09:30 - Notified customer and escalated to SRE; initial mitigation planned: pause staged shear and increase pin commit atomicy window.
Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-13 09:38 - Confirmed reproduction in staging; proposing short-term mitigation: hold anchor TTL at 30s for affected tenants during shear and add an epoch-stability check before allowing fallback routing.
Emma Li (Serving Runtime) 2026-03-13 10:05 - Noted that prewarm mirror path does an eventual write; will add fast-path reconcile for tenant-scoped pin writes. Will submit PR for review.
Customer (ClearPath Health) 2026-03-13 10:12 - Customer acked rollback and requested follow-up on guardrails to guarantee no silent fallback during clinical runs.
Rolled back staged shear and temporarily increased anchor TTL to 30s for ClearPath Health tenant. Added an observability rule to alert on any cryptic variant assignment without 5xx. Notified customer and applied hold on further rollouts until fix lands.
1) Orchestrator: introduce epoch-stability handshake — require 2 consecutive epoch-aligned heartbeats before allowing a variant change for pinned tenants.
2) Serving runtime: fast-path reconcile for prewarm mirror write to update local pin cache immediately on commit.
3) Console: add rollout guardrail that disallows staged shear >X%/minute for pinned tenants (configurable by customer tier).
4) Postmortem: runbook update and customer-facing summary to be produced within 3 business days.
In progress. Short-term rollback and TTL extension stopped further customer impact. Engineering PRs opened: github.com/redwood-inference/coordination/pull/1128 (epoch-stability) and github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2043 (fast-path reconcile). Target deploy calendar: canary 2026-03-16, global 2026-03-18 after verification in staging. Postmortem scheduled.
Customer requested enforceable guardrail to prevent silent fallback for tenants with clinical SLAs. CS and Solutions will offer options: automatic no-fallback mode for pinned tenants or stricter rollout rate limits.
payload.summary: version-anchor oscillation during staged traffic shear causes transparent degrade to backup variant

Issue summary:
Customer private deployment started failing to pull model artifacts and agent heartbeats intermittently. Failures coincide with DNS failures and ICMP packets being dropped by customer-managed firewall appliances.

Impact:
- Model downloads for new replica launches fail ~15-30% of the time, causing delayed rollouts and increased cold-start latency.
- Agent heartbeat gaps observed on private control plane (heartbeat gaps 10-60s).
- Affects production traffic for inference and autoscaling; customer reports client-facing errors "503 - model not loaded" during spikes.

Environment:
- Private deployment in BrightSignals' VPC (eu-west-1), Redwood Private control plane connecting over VPC peering and a set of firewall appliances in front of subnet where inference agents run.
- Agent version: 1.12.4; serving-runtime: 2.3.1; model registry: artifactstore.svc.internal (DNS CNAME into on-prem cache).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a new autoscale run by sending 500 concurrent short infer requests to a pinned model.
2) Observe agents spin up new replicas and attempt to pull model artifacts from artifactstore.svc.internal.
3) Capture packet traces and agent logs during replica start.

Observed behavior:
- Agent logs show repeated "DNS resolution failed" and "connection reset during TLS handshake" when attempting to reach artifactstore.svc.internal.
- Packet capture shows DNS A responses being sparsely returned (many queries receive no response) and ICMP fragmentation-needed messages suppressed.
- Firewall (customer-managed) appliance logs show stateful connection entries for UDP/53 timing out and TCP half-open states being torn down after ~12s.

Expected behavior:
- DNS responses should be forwarded reliably to agents and model artifacts pulled successfully within startup window.
- ICMP Path MTU messages should not be silently dropped, allowing correct TCP MSS negotiation for TLS handshakes.

Logs/artifacts attached:
- agent-startup.log excerpts (lines with DNS/TLS errors)
- tcpdump capture (udp port 53 & port 443)
- firewall config extract (anonymized) showing firewall session timeouts

Additional notes:
- Customer confirmed recent firewall policy change two days prior that enabled aggressive stateful inspection and dropped "invalid" UDP fragments.
- Similar symptom patterns previously observed in SUP-24107 (heartbeat loss) but root cause here appears tied to DNS/ICMP suppression rather than route propagation.

2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Asha): Ticket created after customer's support intake. Requested packet captures and firewall logs.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Customer (Ops@BrightSignals): Uploaded tcpdump and anonymized firewall config. Noted firewall firmware updated two days ago.
2026-03-10 12:30 - SRE (Jordan): Reproduced DNS query loss in packet captures; initial hypothesis: stateful firewall misclassifying fragmented DNS/UDP responses as invalid.
2026-03-11 08:45 - Customer (Ops@BrightSignals): Applied a temporary policy to increase UDP session timeout to 30s; observed reduction in model pull failures to ~5%.
2026-03-11 11:20 - Support (Asha): Asked customer to enable ICMP fragmentation-needed and allow path-mtu ICMP messages for the subnet. Customer scheduled change.
2026-03-12 07:50 - SRE (Jordan): Noted one replica still failed TLS handshake; related to MSS mismatch when PMTU messages were blocked earlier in trace.
2026-03-12 16:00 - Customer (Ops@BrightSignals): Confirmed long-term firewall rule being rolled back and will monitor for 48 hours.
2026-03-12 16:15 - Support (Asha): Marking scope as narrowed; will keep ticket open until 48-hour monitoring window completes and follow-ups are scheduled.
Hypothesis 1: Firewall stateful inspection is dropping fragmented UDP responses for DNS; cause: firmware change flagged truncated UDP packets as invalid.
Hypothesis 2: ICMP 'fragmentation needed' (Type 3, Code 4) messages are being blocked at perimeter causing PMTU negotiation failures -> TLS handshake MSS mismatch and connection resets.
Findings: Packet traces show DNS queries retransmitted multiple times before response; many DNS responses are larger than 512 bytes and are fragmented. Firewall logs show 'invalid fragment' entries correlated with timestamps.
Test: Customer increased UDP session timeout and allowed ICMP PMTU messages; model pulls improved immediately but not fully resolved until fragmentation handling adjusted on firewall.
Artifact store: no evidence of artifact corruption; failures localized to connection establishment phase (DNS + TLS).
Workaround applied (customer): Increased UDP session timeout and relaxed fragmentation inspection on firewall appliance. Immediate customer-reported reduction in failures from ~25% to ~3%.
Permanent fix: Customer will upgrade firewall firmware to vendor-supplied patch that fixes fragmentation handling and will explicitly allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 for the agent subnets. Change scheduled and tracked by customer change control.
Redwood action items: 1) Add guidance to Private Deploy runbook advising customers to allow PMTU ICMP messages and to properly handle fragmented DNS responses. 2) Create alert in Console for repeated DNS resolution retries during replica startup (to auto-warn on similar issues). 3) Cross-reference with SUP-24107 to update runbook.
Follow-up: Monitor for 48 hours post-change; customer to report SLA metric for model pull success. If residual issues, open deeper packet-level session-trace with vendor support.
payload.summary: Stateful customer firewall suppresses DNS/ICMP responses causing model artifact pull failures on Private deploy

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports Redwood Private operational logs are not arriving in Splunk via HEC export. Log forwarder shows repeated 401 responses from Splunk HEC.

Impact:
- Customer SOC team cannot ingest Redwood operational logs into SIEM.
- Redwood Support unable to rely on customer-side SIEM for incident triage.
- No direct inference downtime, but compliance monitoring blocked.

Customer constraints / notes:
- On-prem, air-gapped. No outbound internet. Splunk is internal.
- HEC endpoint is fronted by F5 VIP with TLS re-encryption.
- Customer requires TLS (no plain HTTP). They will not disable certificate verification globally; they can install internal CA bundle if needed.
- Customer prefers HEC /event (structured JSON) over /raw.

Observed errors:
- From log forwarder: HTTP 401 from https://splunk-vip.customer.local:8088/services/collector
- Splunk admin states token is valid and HEC is enabled.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Install Redwood Private 1.12.3 using Helm values enabling log export to Splunk HEC.
2) Deploy log collector (daemonset) and set sink to HEC.
3) Generate traffic to Redwood gateway/runtime.
4) Observe 401s in collector logs; no events in Splunk index.

Artifacts provided:
- Collector config snippet (redacted) and a sample curl test (failing with 401).

Collector config snippet as provided (redacted):
---
# values.yaml excerpt
privateObservability:
  logs:
    enabled: true
    exporter: splunk_hec
    splunk:
      endpoint: "https://splunk-vip.customer.local:8088/services/collector"
      tokenSecretRef: "splunk-hec-token"
      index: "redwood_ops"
      source: "redwood-private"
      sourcetype: "_json"
      tls:
        caBundleSecretRef: "customer-internal-ca"
---

Collector runtime log excerpt:
- "hec sink: request failed" status=401 path="/services/collector" message="Invalid token" retry=true

Initial hypothesis:
- Authorization header is malformed or missing the required "Splunk " prefix.
- Endpoint path mismatch: using /services/collector vs /services/collector/event (Splunk can behave differently depending on proxy/WAF rules).
- F5 is rewriting/stripping Authorization headers.
- Token created without index capability, or HEC is configured with token-level index restrictions.

Requested from customer:
- Confirmation of exact HEC endpoint allowed through VIP (event vs raw vs base).
- Whether F5/WAF policies strip Authorization header.
- Splunk HEC settings screenshot: enabled, port, token, allowed indexes.

Support priority rationale:
P2/Sev2 due to compliance monitoring block + repeated auth failures; no production outage.
2025-07-18 (Dev Patel - Support): Acknowledged. Asked customer for (1) exact HEC endpoint they expect (/event vs base), (2) whether VIP/WAF strips Authorization header, (3) token permissions (allowed indexes), and (4) curl test from inside the collector pod with full headers.
2025-07-18 (Customer - Northbridge Health Systems): We are using Splunk Enterprise HEC behind an F5 VIP. Token is created by Splunk admin and should write to index redwood_ops. We currently allow only /services/collector/event through VIP. Our curl was: curl -k https://splunk-vip.customer.local:8088/services/collector -H 'Authorization: <token>' -d '{"event":"test"}'. Returns 401.
2025-07-19 (Colin O'Donnell - Solutions/Logging): The curl example is missing the required 'Splunk ' prefix in the Authorization header. Should be 'Authorization: Splunk <token>'. Also endpoint should match /services/collector/event for JSON events. If VIP only allows /event, pointing collector at base path will fail (403/401 depending on policy). Request customer to retry curl with correct header and /event path.
2025-07-19 (Dev Patel - Support): Sent customer corrected curl command and asked them to confirm if F5 strips Authorization headers. Proposed to update Helm values to use endpoint .../services/collector/event.
2025-07-20 (Customer - Northbridge Health Systems): Retried curl from a jump host: curl -k 'https://splunk-vip.customer.local:8088/services/collector/event' -H 'Authorization: Splunk ****' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"event":"test"}'. This works (HTTP 200). When we update endpoint in values to /event we still see 401 from the collector though.
2025-07-20 (Colin O'Donnell - Solutions/Logging): If curl works but collector gets 401, likely the secret contains the token without expected formatting and our collector template is adding/omitting prefix incorrectly, OR the VIP is blocking the collector's source IPs while allowing the jump host (F5 iRule/WAF allowlist). Ask for collector pod IP/node subnet; ask Splunk admin to check HEC logs for 'invalid token' vs 'token disabled' vs 'source IP not allowed'. Also confirm the token secret value does not include whitespace/newlines.
2025-07-21 (Dev Patel - Support): Requested customer (1) to paste kubectl describe secret output (no token value) and confirm token stored as plain token only, (2) to run: kubectl exec -n redwood-observability <collector-pod> -- sh -c "apk add --no-cache curl || true; curl -sv 'https://splunk-vip.customer.local:8088/services/collector/event' -H 'Authorization: Splunk $(cat /var/run/secrets/.../token)' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"event\":\"collector-test\"}'". Also asked whether HEC has source IP restrictions enabled.
2025-07-21 (Customer - Northbridge Health Systems): Running curl inside the collector pod works when we inline the token. Splunk admin found that requests from the Kubernetes worker subnet were hitting a different HEC token config due to VIP pool selection (legacy token disabled). VIP was routing based on source subnet. After fixing VIP pool mapping, collector no longer gets 401. Logs are now arriving in index redwood_ops.
2025-07-22 (Colin O'Donnell - Solutions/Logging): Great. Recommendation: document that HEC behind VIP/WAF must pass Authorization header and route consistently across source subnets. Also recommend setting endpoint explicitly to /services/collector/event and ensuring token secret contains raw token (no 'Splunk ' prefix).
2025-07-23 (Dev Patel - Support): Marking Resolved. Added internal note to update Splunk HEC export doc with: correct endpoint, correct Authorization header format, VIP/WAF routing/allowlist pitfalls, and an in-pod curl verification step.
Root cause:
- Customer Splunk HEC was fronted by an F5 VIP that routed traffic from the Kubernetes worker subnet to a legacy backend configuration where the referenced HEC token was disabled, resulting in 401 responses.
- Additionally, initial customer curl tests used an incorrect Authorization header format (missing the required 'Splunk ' prefix) and used the base /services/collector path while the VIP only allowed /event.

Fix / workaround:
1) Update Splunk HEC endpoint in Redwood values to the explicit JSON event endpoint:
   https://<hec-host>:8088/services/collector/event
2) Ensure token is provided as the raw token string in the Kubernetes secret (do not include the 'Splunk ' prefix in the secret; the client sets the header).
3) If HEC is fronted by a VIP/WAF, confirm:
   - Authorization header is not stripped.
   - Backend routing is consistent across the K8s node subnets.
   - Any source-IP allowlists include the K8s worker node/pod egress subnets.
4) Validate from inside the collector pod with curl using the exact endpoint and header.

Result:
- After the customer corrected VIP routing/pool selection for the K8s worker subnet, the collector stopped receiving 401s and logs began ingesting into the intended Splunk index.

Follow-ups:
- Support to request docs update to include the VIP/WAF routing caveat + in-pod curl test step.
- Customer to keep Splunk token ownership with their Splunk admin team; Redwood does not store/rotate customer SIEM tokens.
Sanitized notes: do not request or store customer HEC token values in tickets. When troubleshooting 401s, prioritize: endpoint (/event vs base), Authorization header format, token secret whitespace/newline issues, and VIP/WAF behavior (header stripping, source IP allowlist, backend pool selection). Consider adding a preflight check in the Private installer to detect common Splunk HEC misconfigurations (endpoint suffix + connectivity test) if customer opts in to running a synthetic event.
payload.summary: Private install: Splunk HEC log export returns 401 Unauthorized (token header/endpoint mismatch)

comments: 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Priya Shah: Raised after customer reported duplicated payment intents in production. Provided sample traces and a minimal python repro that simulates a reconnect/backfill scenario.
2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Carlos Mendes: Assigned for initial triage. Requesting sidecar config and exact SDK versions. Asked customer to share edge router logs and any custom header rewrite rules.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer running a Dedicated deployment (MercatoPay) observes out-of-order and duplicate executions of a transactional webhook that is triggered by function/tool calls from the Redwood streaming API. The webhook is used to create payment intents and must be executed exactly-once.

Impact:
- Duplicate charge-intent creations in production (customer-visible financial impact).
- Sporadic ordering issues when backfilled retries are processed (downstream reconciliation required).
- Affects a small fraction (~0.7%) of requests during client reconnect/backfill windows.

Environment:
- Customer Tier: dedicated
- Deployment: Dedicated pool behind a sidecar proxy used for routing and header normalization
- Region: us-west-2 (customer-provided VPC peering)
- SDKs in use: python-sdk v0.13.2 and typescript-sdk v0.10.8
- Webhook consumer: internal payment service (idempotency implemented via X-Payment-Id header)

Steps to reproduce (customer provided reproducible case):
1) Use python-sdk streaming call with function/tool invocation that sends an idempotency header composed as: "order-<order_id>:<timestamp-ms>".
2) Simulate a transient network disconnect; client reconnect triggers backfill of in-flight messages within a debounce window enforced by the sidecar (sidecar merges bursts to avoid webhook storms).
3) Sidecar canonicalizes headers (dropping suffix after first colon) during canonicalization step, turning multiple distinct keys into "order-<order_id>".
4) Debounce merge groups multiple logical requests that now share the same canonical idempotency key. Sidecar forwards multiple tool calls in a single merged batch to the webhook, which receives multiple events with the same idempotency key but different original timestamps.
5) Webhook idempotency semantics at the payment service treat the merged requests as distinct if internal payloads differ, leading to duplicate creation attempts or out-of-order processing depending on payload ordering.

Expected behavior:
- Sidecar should preserve full idempotency key or avoid canonicalization that collapses distinct keys.
- Debounce/merge behavior should not cause distinct logical requests to share a canonical idempotency identifier.
- SDK guidance should discourage composite keys that rely on preserved separators if sidecar configuration may rewrite headers.

Actual behavior:
- Multiple logical requests that differ only by timestamp suffix are collapsed into the same canonical idempotency key and merged into a single outbound burst. This causes duplicate/out-of-order webhook side-effects for transactional workloads.

Logs / traces (submitted by customer):
- Trace IDs: trace-redwood-20260310-8f1a, trace-redwood-20260310-8f1b
- Sidecar debug snippets show header rewrite: "X-Idem: order-12345:1617902398123" -> "X-Idem: order-12345"
- Webhook logs show two sequential requests with same "X-Payment-Id" but differing payload timestamps and resulting duplicate payment-intent creation attempts.

Attachments:
- small repro script (python) provided by customer
- sanitized webhook logs


Additional notes:
2026-03-11 — Customer (MercatoPay): Shared sidecar config snippet — it has 'normalize_headers: true' and a custom rule to 'collapse-after-colon' to normalize tracing headers. Confirmed they added the colon-suffix timestamp pattern for deduping on their side.
2026-03-12 — SRE (Liam O'Connor): Noted that debounce windows can merge up to 500ms of backlog by design when 'debounce.enabled' is true; recommended reducing debounce window and toggling 'preserve_idempotency_headers' flag for transactional endpoints.
Initial hypothesis: header canonicalization + debounce merging is collapsing distinct idempotency keys. Confirmed by reproducing with supplied sidecar config. Reproduction steps produced identical behavior: header rewrite rule removes suffix after ':'; debounce merge groups requests that now share canonical key. Rate of incidents correlates with client reconnect patterns and the sidecar debounce setting. No indication of SDK bug in generation of keys — issue is environmental (sidecar config) and guidance/defense-in-depth missing in SDK/docs. Linked internal issue INT-330 for sidecar runbook update.
Short-term workaround provided to customer (applied 2026-03-12):
- Toggle sidecar flag: 'preserve_idempotency_headers: true' on the dedicated sidecar for the payment route.
- Reduce debounce window to 50ms for transactional routes.
- Update webhook consumer to also accept a secondary header 'X-Original-Idem' to validate original composite idempotency token until sidecar config stabilized.

Medium-term changes (in flight):
- sidecar-config PR#442: add option to opt-out of colon-based canonicalization and to preserve entire header value (merged to staging, scheduled for canary on 2026-03-15).
- python-sdk PR#977: add guidance and a helper function (sdk.helpers.generate_hashed_idempotency_key) that hashes composite keys client-side to avoid reliance on separators.
- Docs: add a support note and a console alert for dedicated customers when sidecar header normalization is enabled.

Follow-ups:
- ENG to run a small canary of sidecar-config change in a subset of dedicated clusters (INT-330).
- Customer agreed to apply the short-term workaround and will monitor for duplicates.
- CS to schedule a post-fix verification call on 2026-03-16.
payload.summary: Sidecar header canonicalization + retry debounce leads to out-of-order / duplicate transactional webhook executions

payload.description:
Customer reports a noticeable increase in HTTP 429 responses immediately after upgrading Redwood SDK (Python -> latest minor). Customer believes they are under their purchased quota and that prior to upgrade they did not see sustained throttling.

Issue Summary
- Symptom: Increased 429s ("Too Many Requests") with inconsistent/misleading rate limit headers across endpoints.
- Trigger: SDK upgrade + switching more traffic to streaming + increased concurrency.
- Suspected: Edge-case in quota enforcement / header classification (429 returned with headers that do not reflect actual enforcement window), plus SDK retry behavior amplifying bursts.

Impact
- Customer-facing impact: Elevated request failures; customer implemented aggressive retries, causing additional burst traffic and more 429s.
- Scope: Primarily hosted API traffic; reported across us-east and eu-west.
- Business impact: Customer escalated due to downstream search latency and perceived platform instability.

Customer Environment
- Tier: self_serve (high-usage hosted account)
- SDK: Redwood Python SDK (upgraded within last 24 hours). Customer also has a TS service calling embeddings.
- Workload pattern: mixture of chat completions (streaming) + embeddings batch jobs.
- Concurrency: increased by customer during rollout.

What we need from customer (requested)
- Approx time range (UTC) for the spike
- Request IDs for sample 429s (5-10)
- Endpoint breakdown (chat vs embeddings)
- SDK version + language, and whether retries/backoff are enabled

Observed / Provided Examples
- Sample response indicated 429 with headers suggesting remaining=0 while dashboard usage looked below hourly quota.
- Some 429s appear to be rate-limit (burst) while others appear to be quota enforcement, but both surface as 429 and sometimes share the same error message.

Initial Hypotheses
1) Quota enforcement edge-case incorrectly classifies (or caches) limit state, leading to 429s even when token/quota counters look below the contracted limit.
2) Rate-limit headers inconsistent across endpoints and/or under fallback routing, confusing customer-side logic that keys on headers.
3) SDK upgrade changed default retry semantics or timeouts, causing higher effective RPS bursts (especially with streaming reconnect patterns).

Immediate Mitigation Guidance (Support)
- Reduce concurrency temporarily (cap worker pool)
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries; do not retry immediately on 429
- If using streaming, avoid reconnect loops without a backoff; log request IDs per attempt
- Use server-provided Retry-After (if present) over custom fixed delays

Engineering Follow-up
- Linked ENG-4825 to address rate-limit/quota mismatch and header consistency; request confirmation on whether fallback can affect header calculation.
- Track for known-issues sprint article: workaround-429-quota-mismatch-and-rate-limit-headers (draft already in progress).

Additional notes:
2026-02-04 18:44 UTC — Customer (Aurora Search, via Support portal): Time range: 2026-02-04 15:00–18:30 UTC. SDK: redwood-sdk-python 1.9.x (upgraded from 1.8.x). We added retries (3 attempts) with fixed 200ms delay. Seeing 429s on /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings. Regions: mostly us-east, some eu-west failover. Providing request IDs in a separate message.
2026-02-07 16:40 UTC — Customer (Aurora Search): After adjusting backoff and reducing concurrency, 429 rate dropped ~70% but still seeing occasional bursts where headers look wrong. We can operate with this for now, but want confirmation whether headers are reliable.
2026-02-10 14:12 UTC — Platform (via Ethan Park): Fix in progress; we’re making RateLimit headers consistent and ensuring 429 classification matches enforcement source. Will roll out behind a flag, then ramp. Please point customer to KB draft once published.
Resolved with customer-side mitigation while Engineering fix proceeded.
Customer Mitigation (immediate)
- Reduced concurrency and removed fixed 200ms retry.
- Implemented exponential backoff with jitter for 429s and respected Retry-After when present.
- Temporarily stopped using RateLimit-Remaining as an adaptive concurrency signal due to header inconsistency risk.
Engineering Outcome (tracked separately)
- Linked ENG-4825: quota enforcement edge-case + rate-limit header consistency.
- Related code change: PR-19322 (header consistency + regression tests) merged and queued for rollout.
Docs / Known Issue
- Added/updated draft guidance in workaround-429-quota-mismatch-and-rate-limit-headers with clear 'When to escalate' criteria.
Next Steps
- Support to follow up post-rollout to confirm header behavior is consistent for customer and close the loop with final KB link.
payload.summary: Unexpected spike in 429s after upgrading SDK (quota mismatch vs rate-limit headers)

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightDocs reports that during a scheduled canary of redwood/gpt-rl-3b-v2, a subset (~12%) of requests from a VIP tenant were unexpectedly routed to the compatibility variant (redwood/gpt-rl-3b-compat) despite an explicit per-tenant model pin. The diversion coincided with a brief configuration change at the edge performed by BrightDocs' CDN vendor to add an 'X-Forwarded-Model' header for debugging. Impact: Inconsistent outputs for end-users, degraded quality for some sessions, and a short billing uplift for the compatibility variant.

Environment: Production (us-east-1) on Dedicated cluster assigned to BrightDocs (enterprise). Canary weight set to 10% with tenant-level pin to v2. Observed window: 2026-03-09T21:17:00Z — 2026-03-09T21:25:30Z.

Expected behavior: Tenant pin should be authoritative and prevent routing to the compat variant during canary. Actual behavior: Requests bearing X-Forwarded-Model header were preferentially assigned to compat variant, bypassing pin enforcement for a small cohort of edge-generated requests.
1) Configure a route with tenant-level pin to redwood/gpt-rl-3b-v2 and set canary weight 10%.
2) From a client simulating the BrightDocs tenant, send streams with keepalive and session tokens while adding header 'X-Forwarded-Model: gpt-rl-3b-compat'.
3) Monitor routing decisions in the orchestrator logs and edge request logs for that tenant key.
4) Observe that requests with the header are assigned to compat variant despite the pin.
2026-03-09T21:17:03Z ingress-edge-123 INFO received request tenant=brightdocs session=abcd123 headers='Host: api.redwood.ai; X-Forwarded-Model: gpt-rl-3b-compat; Cookie: tenant=brightdocs'
2026-03-09T21:17:03Z orchestrator-12 DEBUG resolve_route tenant=brightdocs pin=redwood/gpt-rl-3b-v2 edge_header_model=gpt-rl-3b-compat chosen_variant=redwood/gpt-rl-3b-compat reason='header_override'
2026-03-09T21:17:04Z serving-34 WARN fallback chosen=compat variant latency_improvement=12ms
Initial triage: Support confirmed customer-performed header insertion via CDN debugging change. Edge logs show header present for affected sessions. Orchestrator logs show a code path labeled 'header_override' used during routing decision.
Hypothesis A: Edge header is being treated as higher precedence than tenant pin during route resolution due to a legacy precedence table introduced in pre-2025 orchestrator refactor.
Hypothesis B: A short-lived feature flag (allow_edge_model_hint=true) was enabled in the affected edge shard for observability and wasn't gated by tenant pin checks.
Telemetry snapshot: 1.2k requests from tenant in window, ~140 (11.6%) were diverted to compat; those requests all carried X-Forwarded-Model. No other tenants exhibited the issue.
Reproducibility: Internal replay with same header reproduces diversion on staging with current orchestrator canary build. Removing header prevents diversion (pin respected).
Related code paths: router/handler.go lines with 'modelHint' precedence and orchestrator/routing_policy.go where pin enforcement should short-circuit header hints. PR candidate: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2384 addresses precedence check order.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:40 — Eng (Alejandra Ruiz): Created PR to change precedence so tenant_pin short-circuits any edge hints. Link: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2384
2026-03-11 16:05 — Customer (BrightDocs, Hana Lee): Confirmed they removed header injection and that end-user experience normalized; asked about long-term guardrails.
Workaround applied: Instructed BrightDocs to disable the CDN header injection (immediate). Support enabled per-tenant 'strict_pin' toggle for BrightDocs which forces pin enforcement regardless of incoming hints. Engineering fixed precedence bug in orchestrator where edge model hints could override tenant pin; patch merged (PR #2384) and hotfixed to prod during small maintenance window on 2026-03-12 02:00Z. Post-deploy telemetry shows zero further diversions for tenant. Billing uplift reconciled: credits issued for compat variant usage during incident window.
1) Add unit/integration tests to ensure tenant pin short-circuits any edge-level model_hint (owner: orchestrator team; due: 2026-03-20).
2) Add detection rule to console to alert if >0.5% of requests for a pinned tenant are served by non-pinned variants (owner: observability; due: 2026-03-18).
3) Update runbook and customer-facing docs to call out that edge-inserted 'X-Forwarded-Model' may be treated as a hint and that strict_pin exists for enterprise tenants (owner: Support/Docs; due: 2026-03-22).
4) Audit feature flags that expose allow_edge_model_hint and ensure default is false in prod (owner: FeatureFlags; due: 2026-03-15).
5) Send post-incident summary to #support and to BrightDocs CSM (owner: Maya Thompson; due: 2026-03-13).
payload.summary: Coordinated header override at edge bypasses tenant route pin and triggers fallback to compatibility variant

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a burst of 429 responses across their tenant after an automated API key rotation during a high-throughput streaming upload window. The pattern is reproducible when their client rotates keys and simultaneously spawns short-lived prefetch workers that fan out requests to multiple routes.

Impact:
- LexaHealth observed ~30% request failures (429) for 7–12 minutes after an automated key rotation during a nightly data push.
- Business impact: ingestion pipeline stalled; downstream throughput SLA missed.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Configure two API keys (K-A primary, K-B rotated-in) with equal privileges under same tenant.
2) Client spawns 40 short-lived prefetch workers that request streaming completions and embeddings concurrently (burst over ~10s).
3) Client triggers automated rotation: start sending requests with both K-A and K-B for an overlap period of ~30s.
4) Observe 429s returned to many workers within 1–2 minutes of rotation, continuing for several minutes.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses show rate-limiter reason in headers: X-RateLimit-Reason: concurrency_window_exhausted
- Token-bucket headers show remaining=0 for tenant-level bucket while per-key buckets occasionally show small positive values.
- Logs include many short-lived connection opens/terminates tied to rotated key handoff.

Expected behavior:
- Smooth handover with exponential backoff from clients should avoid tenant-level token exhaustion; short overlap should not trigger wide 429 storms.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- Upload link to request traces (redacted): s3://leixa-logs/rotation-2026-03-09/traces.tar.gz
- Curl examples and client pseudocode for rotation logic included in attachments.

Immediate ask:
- Guidance on mitigation steps to stop ongoing 429 bursts and recommended configuration changes for dedicated customers performing frequent key rotations.

03/10 11:05 — SRE: Rate-limiter metrics show tenant token-bucket depletion coincident with a spike in short-lived connections; per-key buckets were distributed but tenant global window exhausted.
03/11 14:20 — Eng hypothesis: Client-side overlap + prefetch worker fan-out created a concurrency-pattern that bypasses smooth ramp controls and bursts queued requests into serving runtime, draining tenant pool faster than refill rate.
03/11 16:00 — Observed that streaming sessions that start close to rotation emit many small, parallel prefetch requests (metadata, embeddings) which count toward concurrency window immediately; aborts create extra churn.
03/12 09:00 — Suggested mitigations drafted: reduce overlap during rotation, add client-side jitter/backoff, enable per-key gradual ramp (request throttling), and consider increasing tenant concurrency limits temporarily for the rotation window.
03/12 10:30 — Engineering flagged related internal task INT-4882 to evaluate adding a graceful-key-swap header and server-side short buffer to smooth handovers for dedicated customers.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightData Labs is seeing periodic 429s on low-latency SSE streams while a parallel bulk embedding job saturates tenant burst credits. Impact: Intermittent 429s on realtime webhooks and SSE consumers causing degraded product UX during nightly bulk imports. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east running mixed realtime (SSE, webhooks) and bulk embed pipelines under a single tenant config. Observed behaviour: long-lived SSE connections report X-RateLimit-Remaining drifting to zero shortly after a bulk job starts; console shows burst credits consumed rapidly. Customer requests prescriptive configuration to prevent bulk embed work from starving low-latency lanes and guidance for implementing split/priority pools in a dedicated tenant.
1) On a dedicated tenant, start a sustained SSE connection to /v1/streams with keepalive every 30s.
2) Kick off a high-throughput embedding job that sends 10k small embeds over 20 minutes from the same org key.
3) Observe X-RateLimit-* headers on SSE; monitor console per-route token consumption and tenant burst pool.
4) Note 429s on SSE clients once burst credits drop below threshold and backoff behaviour begins.
2026-03-09T23:01:12Z ingress[proxy-43]: clientKey=acct-772 id=... X-RateLimit-Remaining=12 X-RateLimit-Limit=100
2026-03-09T23:05:00Z rate-limiter[pools]: tenant=acct-772 burst_pool=default remaining=2 reason=embed-import-burst
2026-03-09T23:05:03Z sse-handler[stream-conn]: clientKey=acct-772 connection=keepalive interval=30s last_msg=2026-03-09T23:04:58Z 429 returned to client

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:40 - BrightData Labs (customer): Provided embedding job concurrency (50 workers), request sizes (avg 300 tokens) and SDK version; confirmed SSE keepalive at 30s and 2s jitter.
Root hypothesis: Single tenant using default burst pool allows bulk ingest to deplete shared credits; long-lived SSE keepalive heartbeats counted against same pool and appear 'starved'
Observed signed-url callback traffic from embed workers issuing many short POSTs to customer callback endpoint; these callbacks appear in ingress logs and are accounted as interactive tokens rather than background (increases apparent realtime usage)
Console traces: per-route breakdown shows /v1/embed (bulk route) and /v1/streams (realtime route) are both contributing to tenant burst pool; no priority-slicing configured for this tenant
Checked dedicated-pool config: autoscaler healthy, no GPU pressure; issue is quota accounting rather than compute shortage
High-level recommendation: 1) Create isolated burst pools: allocate a dedicated burst pool for realtime (SSE/webhooks) and a separate pool for background bulk ingest. 2) Use route-based priority classes: mark /v1/streams and webhook callback routes as 'low_cost, high-priority' with guaranteed baseline credits. 3) Configure signed-url/callbacks from embed workers to use a background route pattern (path prefix) so they map to the bulk burst pool. 4) Adjust refill intervals: shorter refill for realtime pool (to keep latency-sensitive flows warm) and longer refill for bulk pool with higher capacity. 5) Exempt healthchecks/keepalives from tenant-burst accounting where safe. 6) Add client-side retry jitter and recommended backoff to avoid synchronized retry waves.
{
  "route_pools": [
    {
      "match": "/v1/streams*",
      "pool": "realtime-burst",
      "priority": "high",
      "refill_interval_seconds": 10
    },
    {
      "match": "/v1/embed*",
      "pool": "bulk-burst",
      "priority": "low",
      "refill_interval_seconds": 120
    }
  ]
}
Partial mitigation provided: support gave step-by-step config suggestions and a safe rollout plan. Customer to implement route tagging and separate burst pools in staging; Support will monitor console metrics and re-open if 429s persist post-change.
Provided JSON config snippet for route -> pool mapping in support response (see below).
Action item: SRE/Platform will add a runbook entry to recommend default split-pool templates for dedicated tenants running mixed realtime+bulk workloads.
Follow-up: instrumented additional telemetry on signed-url callbacks to ensure they map to the intended pool.
Customer to apply route tags in staging per recommended_config and report token consumption after next bulk run
Support to validate console metrics (per-route tokens, burst pool remaining) for 48 hours after change
If issue persists, open escalation to RateLimiter team and run controlled repro under support supervision
Advised customer that final change requires coordination with tenant admin to avoid service interruption; provided best-practice doc links and example pool templates.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Parcelly reported persistent elevated p99 latency and reduced throughput on their dedicated reserved slice in us-west between 2026-03-10T08:00 and ongoing. Symptoms look like capacity starvation on their reserved GPU slice despite available cluster level free slots.

Impact:
- Parcelly experienced 30-60% drop in observed requests/s for batched generation routes.
- Elevated p50/p95/p99 across multi-sequence jobs; customer reported user-facing timeouts on batching-heavy endpoints.
- Affects single reserved slice (customer-dedicated) but other tenants unaffected at cluster level.

Environment:
- prod-us-west (us-west-2) reserved slice: slice-id rs-8473
- Customer tier: dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Models: redwood-gpt-open-7b (primary), fallback opt-6.7b-q8 for low-cost routes

Steps to reproduce / Observed sequence:
1) Parcelly reproduces with heavy burst of short streaming requests (median len 60 tokens) and periodic long validation jobs (2k tokens) around 08:00 UTC.
2) Platform autoscaler shows no immediate scale-up (slice remains at target node count).
3) Allocator logs show slots being held by long-running prefetch leases from another tenant cohort routed into same reservation due to a routing mapping change earlier in the day.
4) Requests queue on the reservation; scheduler attempts gang allocation but fails to pack incoming short streams efficiently; p99 rises.

Observed behavior:
- Slot utilization reported as ~95% but effective available GPU memory for Parcelly's tasks drops to ~30% because several slots are occupied by long-prefetch KV caches and lingering connection contexts from unrelated tenant A (noisy cohort).
- Metrics show a spike in prefetch lease acquisitions tied to routing key hash region 'mosaic-12' starting 08:02.
- Autoscaler telemetry indicates low signal (no new nodes provisioned) because cluster-level free slots exist but they are outside the reserved slice boundary.

Expected behavior:
- Reserved slice should honor tenant isolation: prefetch/long-lived background contexts from other tenants must not route into Parcelly's reserved slice. Autoscaler should detect local starvation and trigger refill policies or temporary cross-slice fallback when isolation is violated.

Logs / Dashboards / Links:
- Allocator trace: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/allocator/alloc-traces?var=slice=rs-8473&from=2026-03-10T07:50:00&to=2026-03-10T09:10:00
- Autoscaler dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/autoscaler/provisioning?from=2026-03-10T07:00:00&to=2026-03-10T12:00:00
- Customer provided sample request IDs: [req-00ab12, req-00ab34, req-00ab67]
2026-03-10 09:05 - Support (Anika Shah): Initial triage with Parcelly; confirmed throughput degradation and collected sample request IDs and stack traces. Opened ticket and escalated to infra on-call.
2026-03-10 09:30 - Oncall SRE (Liam O'Connor): Observed prefetch lease growth in rs-8473; noted unexpected routing entries that map 'mosaic-12' cohort into the reserved slice. Adding allocator and routing teams.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:00 - Support (Anika Shah): Notified Parcelly of mitigation plan and requested permission for brief controlled rollback window. Customer approved; assigned maint window 11:30-11:40 UTC.
2026-03-11 08:22 - SRE (Miguel Ortega): Added an interim guard in allocator to reject prefetch leases that originate outside slice owner namespaces. Preparing permanent fix and a regression test for routing map rollouts.
2026-03-12 14:10 - Support (Anika Shah): Parcelly confirmed stabilization over 24h, slight p99 variance during validation jobs but within SLA. Moving to in-progress for follow-up work and postmortem.
Hypothesis 1: Stale shard map after an internal routing rollout allowed cohort 'mosaic-12' prefetch traffic to be mistakenly considered local to rs-8473. Evidence: allocator traces show lease grants with origin tenant 'ta-991' but target slice rs-8473.
Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler did not trigger cross-slice refill because it only considers cluster-unreserved capacity, not per-slice lease fragmentation. Need a metric to surface per-slice effective free-memory rather than slot count.
Partial finding: The allocator grants leases based on soft affinity when slot packing heuristics consider locality; a missing ownership check in the prefetch path was introduced in allocator v2.8.1 (commit 9f2b3ea).
Impact quantification: Observed 45% reduction in Parcelly's batched RPS during the peak 08:02-08:40 window. Other tenants on cluster saw no degradation.
Mitigation performed: rolled back the shard map rollout that introduced incorrect routing. Immediate reclamation of misrouted prefetch leases freed effective capacity for the reserved slice and throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline.
Follow-up / Next steps:
- Deploy a patch to allocator (PR github.com/redwood-infra/allocator/pull/3982) adding strict owner checks for lease grants and a unit/regression test for shard map rollbacks. (Owner: Priya Patel)
- Add a per-slice free-memory metric and alert when effective free capacity < 20% despite slot count > 0 so autoscaler can trigger emergency refill or fallback policies. (Owner: Miguel Ortega)
- Run a postmortem and include the issue in the Reserved Slice Runbook with steps: detection query, immediate rollback procedure, and customer communication template.
- Customer follow-up: scheduled a post-incident review with Parcelly on 2026-03-15 to review root cause and compensating controls.
Status: Mitigation complete, patch in review, monitoring/alerts planned.
payload.summary: Misrouted prefetch traffic causing reserved-slice starvation in us-west reserved capacity

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasHealth AI reported a sustained elevated 5xx rate starting ~2026-03-12 09:20 UTC from their production tenant in eu-west. The spike coincided with a scheduled data ingestion job that issued a high-concurrency embedding upload (multipart) while the product also maintained several long-lived chat streaming sessions.

Impact:
- Multiple customer endpoints returned 502/503 to end-users for ~2.5 hours with intermittent recoveries.
- Increased latency (p50 -> 600ms, p95 -> 3.6s) and ~18% request failure rate for the customer's tenant during the window.
- Business impact: degraded UX for AtlasHealth's clinical assistants; ticket raised by their on-call.

Environment:
- prod / eu-west (customer-dedicated capacity pool)
- Dedicated capacity (customer has reserved pool with 4 GPUs)
- Runtime version: serving-runtime v2.4.1
- Edge proxy: realtime-proxy v1.7.2

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Start large parallel embedding uploads from customer ingestion pipeline (50 concurrent multipart posts).
2) Maintain 15 active long-lived chat streaming sessions in parallel.
3) Observe elevated 5xx in API responses and runtime pool restarts within ~15-30 minutes.

Observed logs / telemetry snippets:
- api-gateway logs: repeated upstream 502 with "upstream reset: too many open files" and "connection reset by peer" messages.
- serving-runtime stderr (from one runtime instance): "ERROR: accept() failed: EMFILE (Too many open files)" followed by "worker process killed: exit_code=137" messages.
- node exporter fd count (runtime host): rose from ~1200 -> 32k during the ingestion window.
- edge-proxy traces show incremental backlog on accept queue and subsequent conn-close propagation.

Investigation notes (chronological):
- 09:25 UTC: Support alerted by AtlasHealth monitoring and support channel #support-enterprise.
- 09:28 UTC: Pager duty page to runtime on-call. Initial hypothesis: keepalive/connection leak or ephemeral port exhaustion in dedicated pool.
- 09:40 UTC: SRE observed rapidly increasing FD usage on 3/4 runtime hosts in the pool. Kernel shows many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT and some half-closed streams.
- 09:55 UTC: Reproduced at lower scale in staging by running customer ingestion + streaming client; confirmed steep FD growth in the realtime-proxy process tied to websocket connections that weren't being cleaned up after client disconnects.
- 10:30 UTC: Traced one failing code path in realtime-proxy: when upstream prefetch interplay occurs during multipart embed cancellation, an error path failed to close a wrapped websocket handle (third-party webhook integration code path).
- 11:05 UTC: Restarted offending runtime processes and realtime-proxy on the affected hosts as a mitigation. FD counts returned to baseline and 5xx rate dropped substantially.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Warm restart of runtime processes on affected hosts at 11:05 UTC (rebound seen ~11:10 UTC).
- Increased per-process soft ulimit for open files on dedicated-hosts to 65536 to give buffer while patch is prepared.
- Applied emergency rate limit for AtlasHealth tenant ingestion pipeline to throttle parallel multipart uploads (coordination with customer) to avoid immediate re-trigger.
- Added an on-call Grafana alert for rapid fd-growth (threshold: >5000 FDs or >200% baseline in 5m) for dedicated pools.

Root cause hypothesis and confirmation steps:
- Hypothesis: A rare error path in realtime-proxy (invoked by a combination of multipart embed cancellations + open streaming websocket sessions) did not close file descriptors / socket wrappers, causing fd leak and EMFILE on runtime, leading to worker exits and upstream 502/503.
- Confirmed by reproducing locally in staging and capturing process-level FD tables showing leaked websocket fds tied to a specific webhook/third-party integration code path.

Permanent remediation plan (engineering):
1) Patch realtime-proxy to ensure proper closure of websocket wrappers on all error/cancel paths and add unit tests for the multipart+stream cancellation scenario (PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-proxy/pull/1823).
2) Add FD-leak watchdog in serving-runtime to kill and auto-replace a worker that exceeds configurable FD growth thresholds (short-term guard).
3) Harden ulimits and systemd service configs in dedicated deploy artifacts to have safer defaults and alerting.
4) Update customer onboarding docs to recommend back-pressure configuration for heavy concurrent embedding uploads when long-lived streams are present.
5) Postmortem and runbook updates (Confluence) and a post-incident review with AtlasHealth CS.

Next steps / open follow-ups:
- PR 1823 needs code review and roll to canary; assigned to infra eng (Kenji).
- Create INT ticket to add automated FD growth detection in internal monitoring (linked INT-4092).
- Schedule a joint session with AtlasHealth engineering to review backlog/retry patterns and adjust client retry/backoff.
- After patch rollout, run targeted soak test using AtlasHealth reproduction case to validate fix and restore full ingestion concurrency.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:42 UTC - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Observed FD growth on runtime hosts; tagging realtime-proxy & runtime teams. Reproduced minimal repro in staging.
2026-03-14 09:00 UTC - Customer (AtlasHealth on-call): Thank you for the quick mitigation. Asking about timeline for permanent fix so they can plan ingestion windows. CS to follow up with timeline.
Temporary mitigations successful: runtime and proxy restarts reduced 5xx; ulimit increased and tenant ingestion throttled. Permanent code fix PR created to close websocket handles on error paths; FD watchdog and improved alerting scheduled.
payload.summary: Sustained 5xx for AtlasHealth AI in eu-west after parallel embedding uploads + long-lived streams — upstream fd leak causing runtime worker exits
