payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a steady increase in p99 tail latency over a 6-hour window in their dedicated pool. Throughput (tokens/s) dropped ~18% while overall GPU utilization looked normal. Impact: Multiple user-facing endpoints (chat completion) experienced degraded p99 latency and intermittent streaming disconnects for ~5 hours. Environment: Dedicated pool (customer tenant on dedicated capacity) in prod-us-west running mixed short streaming and medium-length generation workloads.
1) Send high-frequency short streaming requests (avg tokens per request ~45) with 30 concurrent clients from the customer's fleet. 2) Also run background medium-size batched inference jobs (batch sizes 8-12) on same pool. 3) Observe p50/p95/p99 latency over 30-90 minutes; reproduce on customer's dedicated pool config (reservation: 4 GPUs, autoscale min=4 max=8).
- p99 latency increased from ~720ms to ~2.4s over 4 hours.
- Overall GPU util remained ~65-78% but per-process kernel queue depth spiked and then dropped cyclically.
- Serving runtime logs show repeated small-batch kernel launches and frequent KV cache evictions: "kv_cache_eviction_ratio=0.47".
- Scheduler traces show one tenant with a high fraction of small concurrent streams occupying slots: tenant_id=n-docs-42, concurrent_slots=63% of pool.
- Autoscaler did not scale up because aggregate queueing signals did not cross scale-up threshold (short requests kept queues shallow).
Initial hypothesis: unfair slot allocation / slot hoarding by many short-lived streaming requests from a single tenant caused increased serialization overhead and prevented efficient batch formation, leading to elevated p99 while GPU looked 'normal'. Investigation steps: pulled per-tenant slot allocation, kernel occupancy profiles, and batch size distribution from 2026-03-10 02:00-08:00 UTC. Found a heavy skew: one tenant generated 70% of request spikes that were <50 tokens and opened many concurrent streams, causing fragmentation of the GPU batch scheduler and frequent kv-cache churn. Also observed high memcpy overhead from many tiny batches. Checked autoscaler logs: scale decisions were based on queue depth thresholds; short bursts were under the threshold and so not triggering scale-up. Cross-checked with network metrics: no packet loss or TLS errors. Checked node-level telemetry: no thermal or hardware throttling.
1) Temporarily applied per-tenant concurrent-slot cap for NimbleDocs (limit set to 20 concurrent slots). 2) Applied short-term request coalescing at edge (grouped bursts within 150ms window) for that tenant. 3) Increased autoscaler sensitivity for the affected pool to consider request rate + small-batch fraction for scale decisions. Result: p99 dropped back to ~850ms within 35 minutes and throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline.
A combination of high-volume short streaming requests from a single tenant (slot hoarding) and autoscaler heuristics that ignored burstiness of tiny streams. The scheduler's batch formation algorithm favored fairness by slot counts which, under many tiny concurrent streams, caused excessive small-batch launches, KV cache evictions, and poor GPU kernel efficiency.
- Short term: kept per-tenant concurrent-slot cap in place and retained autoscaler sensitivity change for the pool during business hours for 72 hours. Enabled request coalescing buffer for the tenant.
- Medium term (deployed): merged scheduler patch that biases consolidation of tiny concurrent streams into 'micro-batches' when safe (PR: platform/pull/4218). Also added a new autoscaler signal (small_batch_ratio) and a tenant-level throttling knob in the console. Deployment rolled out to prod-us-west 2026-03-12 14:00 UTC across the dedicated cluster; monitored for 24h.
- Post-deploy: p99 returned to baseline and no further slot-hoarding events observed for NimbleDocs.
1) Engineering: iterate on batcher heuristics to reduce memcpy overhead for tiny batches (owner: Serving Runtime). 2) Product: add per-tenant concurrent slot limit UI and documentation (owner: Console). 3) Support: notify customers on best practices for mixed workloads and recommend request coalescing and rate-limiting patterns. 4) Run a stress test simulating mixed short/medium workloads to validate autoscaler signal changes (owner: SRE).
Workaround applied + scheduler and autoscaler changes deployed; monitoring indicates stable recovery.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 - Support (Miguel Santos): Confirmed per-tenant skew in slot usage; opened investigation with serving-runtime and scheduler teams. #support channel: #support-dedicated
2026-03-11 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Identified KV cache churn and high memcpy counts from tiny batches. Proposed short-term tenant cap and request coalescing. Linked PR created.
2026-03-12 - SRE (Aisha Khan): Increased autoscaler sensitivity for the pool and rolled out scheduler patch to one AZ for canary. Observed p99 improvement in canary within 40 minutes.
payload.summary: Unequal slot hoarding in dedicated pool causing gradual p99 latency surge

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that many SSE streams from the hosted API appear to terminate 'silently': the client receives the penultimate chunks and then the connection closes or reuses the underlying TCP connection without the expected final 'end' event or final JSON metadata. The visible symptom is truncated final tokens and missing choice/finish_reason metadata.

Impact:
- Multiple calls from NimbusAI show incomplete responses for medium-length completions (typically 800-2k tokens).
- Affects production traffic routed through our edge proxy in us-west-2.
- Customer experienced degraded UX in customer-facing chat flows (some messages appear cut off).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (production) behind edge proxy (Nginx-based layer) -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime (GPUs).
- Customer traffic class: dedicated pool (reserved capacity).
- Observed primarily on HTTP/1.1 keepalive connections with higher request concurrency.

Steps to reproduce (observed from customer and reproduced locally):
1) Client issues SSE generation call using chunked encoding over HTTP/1.1 (curl example provided).
2) Server emits streaming choices and final metadata chunk.
3) Under proxy connection reuse / half-close timing, the final metadata chunk is consolidated with a subsequent keepalive/newline heartbeat chunk and dropped by the proxy as an orphan fragment.
4) Client either sees connection close without end event or a truncated last choice.

Minimal repro curl (observed):
  curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \n    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-v1.2&max_tokens=1500"

Observed logs / snippets:
- Edge proxy access log (sample):
  2026-03-09T22:11:04.423Z 198.51.100.22 "POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1" 200 2345 "-" "curl/7.85.0" "keepalive=1; reuse=1"
- Serving runtime trace (span):
  span=stream:emit chunk_id=521 status=written flush=ok
  span=stream:emit chunk_id=522 status=written flush=pending
- Customer client log (truncated final payload):
  [22:11:04.439] RECEIVED: {"delta":"...final text partial","chunk_id":521}
  [22:11:04.452] CONNECTION CLOSED (no end event)

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis: Edge proxy is performing a half-close/connection reuse optimization and coalescing a tiny final chunk (final metadata or '\n' heartbeat) into a previously flushed packet; due to keepalive logic or an upstream timeout, this coalesced fragment is never forwarded as a proper SSE event boundary.
- Reproduced locally behind a simplified Nginx config with HTTP/1.1 keepalive and small proxy_send_timeout (50s) when traffic is bursty. Setting proxy_buffering off reduces the rate of failures.
- No evidence of serving-runtime failing to write the final chunk; runtime traces show write attempts and flush requests. Problem appears between serving-runtime socket write and the client-observed SSE framing.
- Works reliably when forcing HTTP/2 (h2) at the edge or when client uses a fresh TCP connection per request (no keepalive).

Temporary mitigations tried and results:
- Turned off proxy buffering (proxy_buffering off) on a test edge instance -> repro rate dropped from ~12% to ~1.5%.
- Increased proxy_send_timeout and proxy_read_timeout -> minor improvement but not eliminated.
- Instructed customer to enable HTTP/2 in their client path (not viable for all due to legacy stack).
- Implemented a server-side small trailing chunk hack in a lab build that emits an explicit SSE 'end-of-stream' sentinel as a separate write (flush) and observed reliable delivery in lab.

Next steps / proposed engineering actions:
1) Short-term: Recommend edge config change for affected customers: set proxy_buffering off for SSE endpoints and ensure proxy does not coalesce tiny final chunks (document in KB). Ops to roll a canary of this config to 2 edge nodes in us-west-2.
2) Medium-term (engineering): Add a server-side safety write: always emit a dedicated terminal SSE event (e.g., 'event: _terminal\ndata: {"_final":true}\n\n') as a separate flushable chunk to make end-of-stream robust to proxy coalescing. Add telemetry to count how often we needed the terminal write to be resent.
3) Long-term: Evaluate upgrading edge terminating layer to prefer HTTP/2 for streaming or hardening HTTP/1.1 chunk framing behavior (ensure transparent pass-through of tiny chunks and keepalive heartbeats).

Workarounds for customer:
- Enable HTTP/2 between client and edge if possible.
- Configure edge proxy to disable buffering for SSE endpoints (proxy_buffering off).
- Application-level: client can request a small post-stream validation token appended to payload ('append_status': true) which serving-runtime will put in the penultimate chunk to reduce reliance on a separate final chunk.

Acceptance criteria for fix:
- Repro rate for this vector drops to <0.1% for production traffic in us-west-2 across a 48h window after canary rollout.
- No increase in other streaming regressions (e.g., duplicate tokens).
- KB updated with configuration guidance and a postmortem-style incident note if customer impact is confirmed.

2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer reported chat messages ending abruptly; attached client logs and example request IDs: req-09c8a, req-09c8b. P1 requested due to user-facing UX impact.
2026-03-10 11:02 - Eng (Jorge Martinez): Started tracing through edge logs and runtime spans for the provided request IDs. Found matching span writes for final chunks. Opening INT-4132 to coordinate edge config checks.
2026-03-11 02:47 - SRE (Maya Patel): Deployed a test nginx config with proxy_buffering off on canary-edge-3. Early samples show repro rate falling to ~1.2% in test window. Added dashboard panel: 'sse_tail_loss_rate'.
2026-03-11 15:30 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer tried HTTP/2 path; they report stable deliveries for the previously failing message set. They cannot migrate all clients immediately. Recommended proxy_buffering change and provided KB steps.
2026-03-12 08:14 - Eng (Jorge Martinez): Built lab runtime that emits explicit terminal SSE event in its own flush. Verified consistent delivery behind nginx reproduction. Drafting code change and tests. Planning PR and will include telemetry to count terminal-emit fallbacks. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/872

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer ClearSight reports that calls to the /v1/rerank endpoint started experiencing long tail latency and queueing beginning 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC. The rerank results also show quality regressions (unexpected ordering) when the customer mixes vectors produced by two different embedding variants in the same request.

Impact: Intermittent timeouts from the customer's service (503/504), increased 95th/99th percentile latency for rerank API in us-west, and customer-facing throughput drops. Several high-volume requests queued, causing rate-limit-like behavior and triggering their dedicated capacity autoscale.

Environment: Dedicated tenant (ClearSight) on prod:us-west using a mix of embed-lite-v2 (512 dims, L2-normalized) and embed-highdim-2025 (1024 dims, raw float) produced by their pipeline. Rerank service is expected to accept homogeneous vectors but did not validate dims in upstream request layer.

Steps to reproduce:
- Construct two embedding arrays: one from embed-lite-v2 (shape N x 512, l2-normalized) and one from embed-highdim-2025 (shape N x 1024, raw).
- Send a single /v1/rerank request containing a candidate list where some candidates include 512-d vectors and others include 1024-d vectors (no explicit embedding_version header).
- Observe immediate enqueuing and a sharp latency increase for that request ID (~>5s p99), occasionally resulting in 503 or rerank returning lower-quality ordering.

Observed logs: Trace IDs: rnk-20260310-8a4f, rnk-20260310-8b11. Error snippets show the rerank evaluator logging "embedding dim mismatch - implicit upcast" and downstream trace showing fallback to CPU quant path. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rerank/us-west?panelId=7&from=2026-03-10T08:00:00Z&to=2026-03-10T09:00:00Z. Slack thread: #support (thread ts 1700003000.002200).
Generate 512-d L2-normalized embeddings (embed-lite-v2)
Generate 1024-d raw embeddings (embed-highdim-2025)
Combine both types in a single /v1/rerank request payload without embedding_version headers
Send to customer's dedicated endpoint in us-west and observe latency and ordering
2026-03-10T08:34:12Z rnk-20260310-8a4f rerank WARN embedding dim mismatch - implicit upcast
2026-03-10T08:34:13Z rnk-20260310-8a4f rerank INFO fallback to cpu-quant path, estimated token cost +1.9x
2026-03-10T08:34:14Z api-gateway 429 upstream queue depth exceeded for tenant clearsight

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 09:20 - Customer (ClearSight - S. Patel): Provided sample payloads and confirmed the two models above; they said their ingestion pipeline accidentally stitched outputs during a rollout and didn't set embedding_version headers.
2026-03-11 07:18 - Eng (L. Chen): Root cause identified: upstream request validator omitted embedding dimension validation when a mixed candidate list is present. Implicit handling attempted to upcast 512->1024 and call into CPU fallback for several heavy kernels, causing latency spike. Created PR #1287 to add strict validation + syntactic hinting for embedding_version header.
2026-03-11 14:30 - Support (A. Martinez): Communicated temporary workaround to customer: ensure homogeneous embedding dims per request or include embedding_version header; If mixing is unavoidable, pad 512-d vectors with zeros to match 1024 length as a short-term mitigation.
2026-03-12 10:00 - Customer (S. Patel): Confirmed issue resolved from their perspective; no further timeouts observed in last 24h and quality returned to expected ordering.
Checked Grafana: rerank queue depth spiked at 08:34 UTC, correlated with increase in cpu pathway calls (serving-runtime cpu_binder).
Heap/CPU profiles captured for one trace showed expensive memcpy and zero-padding steps executed under request lock while scoring ran on CPU vector kernels.
Hypothesis: absence of embedding_version header + mixing dims caused system to try compatibility conversion; conversion fallback path is not gated by timeout and increased latency drastically under concurrency.
Confirmed that prior safety check for vector length exists at model-serving layer but the rerank preprocessor path bypassed it during a historical refactor (see commit 6a2f8b3).
Related PR adding strict dims check and clear error messages: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-service/pull/1287
Related internal ticket: INT-4012 for adding e2e tests and SDK validation helpers.
Deployed a validator that rejects mixed-dimension embedding lists with an informative 400 response explaining expected dims and embedding_version header format. Back-ported a short-circuit to avoid implicit upcast/conversion on hot paths. Created SDK guidance and sample code for ClearSight and added an integration test asserting consistent dims. Customer confirmed resolution. Action items: (1) Add automatic recommend-converter utility for customers who need cross-model compatibility; (2) Add telemetry to count mixed-dim attempts and trigger early alerts; (3) Update runbook with exact error messages and workaround steps.
Create conversion utility RFC (owner: L. Chen)
Add mixed-dim detector alert to PagerDuty playbook (owner: Ravi Shah)
Ship SDK helper that fails fast with clear error for mixed dims (owner: Developer Experience)
Customer-facing note provided: 'We temporarily observed elevated rerank latencies when mixing embeddings from different model families. The service now returns a clear error for mixed-dimension requests and we provided migration steps. We apologize for the disruption and are working on an automated converter for mixed workloads.'
payload.summary: Cross-model embedding format incompatibility causing rerank queue buildup and degraded latency

payload.description:
Issue summary: Between 18:20-19:10 UTC on 2026-03-13 BlueSparrow reported sustained p99 latency and 30-40% drop in aggregate throughput on their Dedicated pool. Impact: user-facing latency spikes for production traffic (~10% error spike for tail-heavy routes) and customer reports of degraded batch throughput. Environment: prod dedicated pool (us-east-1), nodes are a mixed GPU fleet (A100 and A10x).

Observed behavior: autoscaler opened and closed slots rapidly; many short-lived inference streams (1-3s) were observed. The scheduler reported a high number of node reassigns and a backlog in the assignment queue. Heartbeat metrics show a cascade of stale-heartbeat tombstones followed by rapid reconnects from ~80 tenant streams.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Customer runs a high-frequency sample workload that opens many parallel short streams (webhooks -> streaming inference, avg lifespan 1-3s).
2) Backend sends repeated keepalive/heartbeat pings; some heartbeats were delayed due to transient GC in a sidecar.
3) Scheduler marks many slots as briefly unavailable, triggering autoscaler adjustments and momentary GPU assignment imbalance.

Relevant logs & metrics:
- Scheduler assignment log snippet: "assign_worker timeout 120ms -> mark_tombstone -> requeue" repeated.
- Autoscaler events: scale_down 18:25:14 -> scale_up 18:25:23 repeated x6 within 5m.
- GPU utilization: observed p50 68% -> p50 42% during oscillation; p99 latency for redwood-open-7b jumped 3x.
- KV-cache growth stable; not a memory pressure symptom.

Immediate impact: customer throughput fell from expected 9.2k tokens/s -> 5.8k tokens/s during peak window; some requests hit retry loops and observed 429s due to slot churn.
2026-03-13 18:35 - BlueSparrow (support contact Elena Ruiz): 'We started seeing 5-6s tail latencies and errors at 18:20 UTC. Only changed workload is higher parallel short streams this evening.'
2026-03-13 18:42 - Support (Maya Chen): 'Thanks — collecting logs and requesting pool diagnostics. Can you confirm if any rollout happened recently?'
2026-03-13 18:50 - SRE (Arjun Patel): 'Observed repeated assign_worker timeouts and tombstones in scheduler. Autoscaler flapped 6 times in 10 minutes. Kicking off deeper traces.'
2026-03-13 19:05 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): 'Prelim hypothesis: heartbeat jitter from sidecar GC or network flaps created many short-lived tombstones; scheduler treats them as slot failures triggering preemptive reassignment and autoscaler reactions.'
2026-03-13 19:35 - Support (Maya Chen): 'Customer applied a temporary client-side backoff (reduced parallel streams) and saw throughput return to baseline. Applying mitigation while we investigate permanent fix.'
Queried scheduler logs for 18:10-19:20 UTC: found 14k assign_worker events; 7.2k contained 'mark_tombstone'.
Correlated tombstone bursts with autoscaler events; pattern: tombstone burst -> immediate scale_down decision due to perceived slot loss -> traffic redistribution -> scale_up as capacity dips detected.
Network traces from node-subnet show intermittent 50-200ms RTT spikes correlated to sidecar GC windows on ~6 nodes. GC logs indicate full pause at 18:24 and 18:30 UTC for a maintenance agent on the node image.
Hypothesis 1: noisy short-lived streams + heartbeat jitter lead to scheduler misclassifying slots as unhealthy, causing cascading autoscale operations and temporary GPU assignment imbalance.
Hypothesis 2: autoscaler tuning thresholds are too sensitive to transient slot tombstones in the presence of high small-stream churn.
Mitigation applied (2026-03-13 19:20 UTC): advised BlueSparrow to apply client-side parallelism cap and short randomized jitter between stream starts. Customer confirmed throughput returned within 15 minutes.
Hotfix deployed (2026-03-14 02:10 UTC): raised scheduler tombstone debounce window from 200ms -> 800ms for Dedicated pools behind stable SLA to avoid immediate slot reassign on transient heartbeat misses. Change pushed via serving PR #2134.
Autoscaler tuning (2026-03-14): increased scale-down cooldown and required sustained slot loss for decision to avoid flap during short-lived churn. Monitoring dashboards updated to highlight tombstone-related autoscale triggers.
Postmortem follow-ups:
- Create a runbook entry for 'short-lived-stream churn' mitigation with recommended client limits and SDK backoff patterns.
- Add a confidence test to CI that simulates many short streams to validate tombstone debounce and autoscaler behavior.
- Schedule a capacity audit for mixed GPU fleets to ensure A100/A10x heterogeneity doesn't amplify assignment instability.
Status: mitigated and changes deployed to prod; monitoring for recurrence over next 72 hours.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 401 Unauthorized when Redwood control plane requests pre-signed model shards. Failures started after customer enabled a secondary corporate NAT appliance in front of their TGW and peering route policy changes.

Impact: Model downloads for HyperBank private deployment fail ~5-10% of range download attempts, causing failed warm starts and increased latency for customer inference. No full site outage but degraded success rate and increased retries in serving nodes.

Observed failure mode: Control plane authenticated requests to S3 presigned URLs return 401; serving nodes report gRPC connection resets and kv-cache invalidation (cache miss followed by successful refetch) correlated with NAT churn.

Environment: Private deployment (VPC peering to HyperBank transit), prod us-east-1, peered TGW -> corporate NAT appliance -> internet egress. Redwood serving nodes in private subnet, control-plane traffic routed via customer egress during certain peering paths.

Customer-provided sequence: After adding secondary NAT appliance the customer saw a spike in failed shard fetches; failures are transient and often recover without action.

Additional notes: Not an SDK or application-layer bug; signatures are valid when retried. Timing suggests a stateful middlebox rewriting source port mapping after SYN/ACK reorder which results in a short-lived connection path rewrite and session attribution mismatch at the origin (S3/CDN).
1) Use private deployment with peered TGW and add an upstream NAT appliance that performs symmetric NAT with connection re-mapping.
2) Trigger multiple concurrent model shard downloads (large model, >100 concurrent range requests).
3) Observe intermittent 401s on presigned object range fetches and gRPC stream resets on serving nodes.
4) Correlate timestamps with NAT appliance logs and conntrack counters showing late SYN/ACK path rewrite.
2026-03-12T22:41:12Z serving-node-7 ERROR s3_fetch.go:241 presigned GET 401 x-amzn-err: SignatureDoesNotMatch (attempt 1)
2026-03-12T22:41:12Z serving-node-7 WARN kv_cache.go:132 eviction triggered after conn reset
2026-03-12T22:41:12Z control-plane-proxy INFO tcpdump: client 10.20.3.45:53104 -> s3.amazonaws.com:443 SYN, server reply appears from 3rd-party NAT path with different src port on SYN/ACK
Customer NAT logs: 2026-03-12T22:41:12 NAT: conn_rewrite original(10.20.3.45:53104) -> rewrite(52.14.23.9:33105) after SYN/ACK reorder
Hypothesis: Multi-NAT ordering and asymmetric path causes source-port remapping mid-handshake leading to origin (CDN/S3) attributing request to different connection and failing signature validation occasionally.
Checked control-plane and serving-node TLS sessions: session resumption not primary factor; mismatch happens at TCP 3-way handshake level (observed SYN then SYN/ACK from alternate egress IP).
Conntrack metrics on serving subnet show high NAT TIME_WAIT reuse and ephemeral port collisions during peak burst downloads.
Reproduced at small scale by toggling a test NAT appliance simulating symmetric NAT+hairpin; observed same 401 pattern at synthetic S3 endpoint.
CDN logs show requests from different source IP/port within 200ms window for the same logical client session, triggering signature verification failures on a small fraction of requests.

Additional notes:
HyperBank Network (customer): We added a secondary NAT as part of egress hardening change window. We saw spikes exactly during our nightly prewarm job. We'll keep the old NAT active for rollback and provide detailed conntrack logs.
Asymmetric/mid-handshake NAT remapping introduced by a recently added corporate NAT appliance combined with peering route changes. The remap sometimes changed source port/IP between initial SYN and subsequent SYN/ACK path, causing CDN/S3 to see a different 5-tuple than the one used to sign presigned URLs; this produced sporadic SignatureDoesNotMatch/401s and triggered serving-node kv-cache invalidations when downloads failed.
Short-term mitigations applied: (1) Advised customer to temporarily route control-plane artifact fetches via Redwood-managed egress (bypass customer NAT) OR reduce parallel shard concurrency in prewarm jobs. (2) Customer rolled back the secondary NAT while we validated fixes. (3) Redwood SRE adjusted serving-node retry logic to back off and revalidate signatures on mismatch and added an extra verification step before kv-cache purge to avoid cascading evictions.
Long-term actions (follow-ups):
- INT action (INT-4410): Add detection for mid-handshake source-mapping changes in our edge TCP stack and surface alerts if observed.
- Network design doc update: Recommend explicit egress path for artifact fetches in private deployments (constrain to single NAT or use VPC endpoint).
- Engineer PR planned: runtime change to treat signature mismatch as transient and attempt a deterministic rebind before purge (tracked in github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2598).
INT-4410: Instrument conntrack anomaly metric and alert at 0.1% of artifact fetches failing with signature mismatch.
DOC-707: Update private-deploy network hardening guidance to include ephemeral port capacity recommendations and NAT ordering constraints.
SRE: Deploy runtime PR to soften kv-cache purge on single-range signature mismatch (target: 2026-03-21).
Customer action: Validate NAT appliance configuration for symmetric NAT behavior and enable ephemeral-port-randomization.
Mitigation applied; customer rolled back secondary NAT. Engineering changes scheduled; monitoring in place. Awaiting INT ticket completion and runtime PR merge.
payload.summary: Multi-NAT translation ordering causes SYN/ACK rewrite leading to gRPC KV-cache invalidation and intermittent 401s on artifact fetch

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Northpeak Search (Dedicated, burst NOT enabled) reported elevated p99 latency and intermittent request timeouts during a 35–45 min window on 2025-05-16.
- Correlation observed between Northpeak’s latency spike and a separate tenant’s burst activity against the shared us-east H100 burst pool.

Impact
- Customer-reported: p99 latency increased from ~2.2s baseline to 6–9s for chat completion requests; a subset of requests hit client timeout (30s) and were retried.
- Redwood telemetry: elevated tail latency (p95/p99) on Northpeak’s dedicated route, plus increased queueing time at router/scheduler boundary.
- Duration: ~14:05–14:47 UTC (approx; see investigation notes).

Customer expectations / concern
- Customer is explicitly not opted into burst and expects neighbor activity not to affect their SLOs.
- Asked whether Dedicated implies strict isolation and whether Redwood is prioritizing burst traffic over reserved baseline traffic.

Environment
- prod / us-east
- Hardware class: H100
- Northpeak Dedicated baseline capacity: 8x H100 (reserved)
- Burst pool: shared managed pool, us-east H100

Initial hypotheses
1) Smart routing fallback or capacity spillover incorrectly sending burst traffic into non-burst dedicated pools.
2) Shared upstream bottleneck (router CPU, rate limiter, admission controller latency, shared KV cache service, or network) causing head-of-line blocking.
3) Fleet safety cap not engaging quickly enough; burst pool saturation caused global contention in the serving runtime / scheduler on the same cluster.
4) Telemetry lag causing the admission controller to admit too many burst requests temporarily.

What we need to answer
- Confirm whether Northpeak traffic ever ran on burst GPUs (it should not) vs. whether the impact was an upstream shared component.
- Identify the guardrail that failed (or was missing) and put a mitigation in place before continuing beta burst testing in us-east.

Customer-visible request
- Provide written explanation of root cause, assurances on isolation, and what changes were made to prevent recurrence.

Attachments / references
- Slack: #incidents thread 1739649912 (beta burst test latency event)
- Dashboards: Burst Saturation (us-east/H100), Dedicated Tenant Latency (Northpeak), Router Queue Depth (us-east)
- Runbook: Burst pool overload mitigation
2025-05-16 14:18 UTC — Miguel Santos (Reporter)
Customer (Northpeak) escalation via CS: “Our p99 jumped to ~8s starting around 14:05 UTC. We do not have burst enabled. Did you move us onto shared capacity?” Customer provided request IDs and noted spike coincided with their internal batch job, but request rate is within normal envelope (+10%).

Asks: please confirm isolation, and whether an incident is in progress. Tagging SRE due to potential neighbor impact + beta burst testing today.
2025-05-16 14:23 UTC — Sean Gallagher (Assignee)
Acknowledged. Treating as Sev2 until confirmed. Pulling dedicated tenant latency dashboard + burst pool panels. Also pinging #incidents and #eng-sre.

Immediate checks:
- Any failover/fallback routing toggles?
- Any evidence Northpeak ran on burst pool nodes?
- Burst pool saturation and admission rate in us-east/H100.
2025-05-16 14:31 UTC — Allison Grant (Observability)
Dashboard notes:
- us-east/H100 burst pool utilization hits ~92–96% between 14:06–14:41 UTC.
- burst_admission_denied_total spikes after 14:20 UTC, but only after saturation was already high.
- Router queue depth increased ~3x during that window across multiple tenants (not only burst-enabled).
- Northpeak p99 latency tracks router queue depth more closely than GPU busy time.

Hypothesis: shared router/scheduler bottleneck rather than Northpeak running on burst GPUs.
2025-05-16 14:36 UTC — Mina Haddad (Smart Routing)
Routing check: Northpeak tenant policy still pins to dedicated pool, burst disabled. No policy change events. No evidence of fallback into burst pool either.

However, we do see increased “admission decision latency” in routing logs during that time. If routing calls admission controller synchronously for burst-enabled tenants, and that service is overloaded, it could increase latency for unrelated routing paths depending on how shared the threadpools are.
2025-05-16 14:44 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE Manager)
Suggest applying runbook step 1: reduce max burst ratio and/or enable global circuit breaker for us-east/H100 while we confirm blast radius.

Also: check if we are sharing the same ingress/Envoy cluster for both dedicated and burst traffic. If yes, we may be CPU-saturated on ingress which would explain cross-tenant impact.
2025-05-16 14:51 UTC — Sean Gallagher (Assignee)
Mitigation applied at 14:49 UTC:
- Reduced burst pool safety cap (us-east/H100) from 0.30 to 0.15 of regional headroom.
- Temporarily disabled burst allow-list for the one tenant driving sustained burst (per Product-approved beta controls).

Result: router queue depth trending down within ~3–5 minutes; Northpeak p99 started recovering by ~14:55 UTC. Continuing to monitor for 30 minutes before telling customer we’re stable.
2025-05-16 15:05 UTC — Miguel Santos (CS)
Updated customer: We are investigating a suspected interaction with ongoing burst beta activity in the region. Confirmed no intentional changes were made to Northpeak’s Dedicated configuration. Provided status: mitigation in place and metrics recovering. Customer asked for RCA within 48 hours.
2025-05-16 16:12 UTC — Ethan Park (Control Plane)
Checked audit events for Northpeak burst settings: no changes in last 14 days; burst_enabled=false; no admin overrides.

Admission controller metrics:
- P99 admission decision latency rose from ~12ms to ~180–250ms during 14:10–14:35 UTC.
- CPU throttling observed on admission controller pods.

This supports the theory that a shared dependency (admission controller) increased request processing time. Action item: make admission checks async/isolated per routing path, or ensure non-burst traffic doesn’t wait on burst admission control.
2025-05-17 09:02 UTC — Ravi Menon (Routing)
Deep dive:
- Dedicated traffic path SHOULD bypass burst admission entirely, but current routing implementation still performs a “capability fetch” call that hits the same policy evaluation service used by burst admission (shared client + shared circuit breaker).
- Under load, the shared client pool backs up and impacts non-burst tenants.

Fix direction:
1) Split routing clients: non-burst path must not depend on admission controller/policy engine latency.
2) Add strict timeouts + fail-open for non-burst capability fetch (do not block request).
3) SLO gate: if non-burst p95/p99 degrades, automatically hard-disable burst in region/hardware.

Tracking to ENG-4902 / PR-23988.
2025-05-18 13:40 UTC — Sean Gallagher (Assignee)
Status update:
- No evidence Northpeak requests ran on burst GPUs (confirmed by capacity attribution logs and per-node tenant tags).
- Root cause is shared routing dependency coupling: burst admission / policy evaluation latency bled into non-burst routing due to shared client pools and insufficient isolation.
- Mitigations still active: lowered us-east/H100 burst cap + tenant-level burst paused.

Requesting approval to re-enable burst only after PR-23988 SLO gating is deployed to prod us-east.
2025-05-19 18:22 UTC — Keiko Yamamoto (Autoscaling/Guardrails)
Added an additional guardrail on the burst pool autoscaler to avoid pushing admission controller and router into CPU contention:
- If router CPU > 75% for 5m OR admission decision p99 > 100ms for 5m, freeze burst scale-up and progressively tighten burst token bucket rate.

This is a short-term safety valve until routing decoupling lands.
2025-05-20 10:11 UTC — Miguel Santos (CS)
Customer-facing summary sent to Northpeak:
- Confirmed: Northpeak traffic remained on reserved dedicated capacity (no spillover onto shared burst pool).
- What happened: during a burst beta test in us-east/H100, the burst admission/policy evaluation path experienced elevated latency. A shared routing dependency caused increased queueing that affected some non-burst tenants’ tail latency.
- What we changed immediately: tightened burst caps and paused sustained burst activity in the region; latency returned to baseline.
- Preventing recurrence: shipping an SLO regression gate + additional isolation in routing; adding alerts that page SRE before non-burst SLOs degrade.

Customer satisfied with explanation; requested notification once burst is re-enabled in region so they can watch their own dashboards.
2025-05-20 10:27 UTC — Sean Gallagher (Assignee)
Closing as resolved.

Resolution criteria met:
- Northpeak p99 back to baseline for 72 hours.
- Guardrail tightened in us-east/H100.
- Engineering work tracked and prioritized (SLO gate + routing decoupling).

Follow-ups:
- Ensure SLO gate (PR-23988) is enabled for us-east before resuming beta bursts.
- Add explicit runbook step: verify non-burst routing path does not hit admission controller under load.
- Link this incident in burst beta retro notes.
Mitigated by tightening us-east/H100 burst safety caps and pausing sustained burst activity for the burst-enabled tenant. Investigation confirmed no spillover of non-burst Dedicated traffic onto burst GPUs; tail latency increase was caused by a shared routing dependency on the burst admission/policy evaluation path, leading to queueing under admission controller load. Preventative work tracked: routing decoupling, stricter timeouts/fail-open for non-burst paths, and SLO-based burst gating (auto-disable burst when non-burst latency regresses).
Deploy and enable SLO regression gate for burst in us-east/H100 (PR-23988) and verify rollback behavior.
Routing: split client pools / remove non-burst dependency on admission controller and policy evaluation latency (owner: Smart Routing).
Add alert on admission decision p99 and router CPU that pages before non-burst SLO impact (owner: SRE/Observability).
Update CS enablement: how to explain that Dedicated does not run on burst GPUs, and what ‘shared dependencies’ are (owner: CS + Docs).
payload.summary: Noisy-neighbor tail latency increase for non-burst Dedicated tenant during another tenant’s burst window (us-east / H100)

Issue summary:
GreenSpring Health uses our tenant-scoped webhook endpoint for real-time audit delivery. During a scheduled client certificate rotation on 2026-03-09 they reported a gap: ~18k audit events (approx. 3 hours) did not arrive at their collector. They need (1) a validated backfill of the missing events for tenant T-GREEN-12 with chronological ordering preserved, (2) cryptographic proof of the server-side signing/checkpoint used during the backfill window, and (3) a signed artifact demonstrating the client cert rotation timeline (previous cert thumbprint, rotation timestamp, and validation that no events were re-delivered outside the window).

Impact:
- Missing audit records for regulated ePHI ingestion pipeline (GreenSpring Health, HIPAA scope).
- Customer cannot complete urgent SOC2 evidence packet for their auditor until audit continuity is proven.

Environment:
- Tenant: T-GREEN-12
- Delivery method: webhook (POST to customer collector) with mutual TLS (client cert).
- Redwood endpoint: https://audit-delivery.prod-us-west.redwood.ai/tenant/T-GREEN-12/events
- Delivery window affected: 2026-03-09 02:10:00 -> 05:15:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Customer rotated client certs at their collector at 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC.
2) Between 02:10--05:15 UTC they observed TLS handshake failures and 502/504 responses in their collector logs.
3) They validated our webhook retries but note their collector returned early 421/ENCRYPT errors for the rotated cert for ~3 hours.
4) Post-rotation (after successful TLS handshake) delivery resumed but missing chronological records were not backfilled.

Relevant logs and sample curl for reproduction (customer provided):
- Collector error snippet: "tls: client certificate signed by unknown authority" followed by "http: proxy error: upstream response timeout"
- Sample curl they used to test mutual TLS: curl --cert client.pem --key client.key -X POST https://audit-delivery.prod-us-west.redwood.ai/tenant/T-GREEN-12/events -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"event\":\"test\"}'

Request from customer:
- Backfill the missing events for the specified window in an append-only, time-ordered payload.
- Produce a signed manifest for the backfill (SHA256-based manifest and server signing key/thumbprint used).
- Provide a short timeline that shows server-side delivery attempts and TLS handshake statuses mapped to UTC timestamps and request IDs.
- Supply the cryptographic evidence of the client-cert rotation acceptance (server logs showing previous cert thumbprint, rotation acceptance timestamp, and per-request CN/subject mapping where available).

Attachments: customer-provided collector logs (attached), example curl invocation, and SOC2 evidence checklist from their auditor.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:34 - SRE - Priya Nair: Infra trace shows our webhook worker made retries at exponential backoff starting 02:11:02 UTC. Client returned 421 for 18,320 deliveries; our retry policy expired after 6 attempts. Retention projection: events are present in tenant ring buffer and object archive. No evidence of intentional suppression on server side. Need approval to perform controlled backfill to customer endpoint and to generate signed manifest.
2026-03-10 13:05 - Support - Ava Chen: Noted customer compliance requirements; requested legal/ps to pre-approve signed artifact format. Escalated to security for signing key use case.
2026-03-11 08:47 - Security - Omar Patel: Approved use of ephemeral signing key from audit-keyring with documented nonce. Provided PRNG seed and KMS attestation link. Proceed with requested signed manifest once SRE provides backfill plan.
2026-03-12 09:03 - Customer (GreenSpring Health) - Jacob Ruiz: Confirmed S3 bucket endpoint is ready (s3://greenspring-uploads/redwood-backfill/) with bucket policy limiting to Redwood IPs. Requests signed manifest and per-request trace. Auditor wants chain-of-custody (who exported, who signed, timestamps).
Initial infra traces indicate the webhook worker attempted standard retries and queued failed deliveries to the tenant object archive. The object archive contains the full set of events; there is no evidence of write loss at the ingestion layer. The cause of the delivery gap correlates with the customer's client-cert rotation which triggered client-side TLS validation failures. Two open questions: (1) customer collector returned 421 and custom ENCRYPT errors — verify whether those are transient collector-side errors or a misconfiguration; (2) confirm whether our retry expiration (6 attempts / 45m) is compatible with customer rotation windows for enterprise tenants; recommend discussing a configurable extended retry policy for enterprise webhook contracts. Trace references: trace-ids [trace-87f3, trace-87f4] and queue segment S-TG12-20260309-02.
Planned resolution path: perform controlled backfill from object archive to customer-provided S3 bucket (non-live push) to avoid duplicate ingestion. Produce signed SHA256 manifest and KMS attestation bundle (audit-keyring) including operator ID and PR link. Provide CSV of per-request delivery attempts with timestamps and TLS handshake outcomes for the affected window. Action items: (1) SRE to run export job and upload artifact (owner: Diego Martinez) — scheduled 2026-03-12 16:00 UTC; (2) Security to sign manifest and provide KMS attestation link (owner: Omar Patel) — complete; (3) Support to prepare cover letter for auditor summarizing chain-of-custody and validation steps (owner: Ava Chen). Post-delivery: capture customer ack and close ticket. If customer prefers live re-delivery, escalate for duplicate suppression safeguards.

Issue summary:
Customer GreenCart AI reports a provisional invoice generated 2026-03-09 that includes a sustainability surcharge line and omits the reserved-capacity prorated credit they should receive for dedicated capacity fallback hours on 2026-03-07 23:00-2026-03-08 03:00 UTC.

Impact:
- Customer provisional balance shows a +$1,420 surcharge and no -$600 reserved credit for the fallback window.
- Customer is flagged for autopay failure threshold because the provisional balance exceeds their forecasted budget.

Environment:
- Production routed through dedicated pool us-west-2 with hosted fallback on eu-west-1 during GP-failover.
- Affected org: org_0x7e5c (GreenCart AI).

Steps to reproduce (customer workflow):
1) Trigger sustained load on dedicated pool using a mixed-embed+chat workload (customer test harness attached).
2) Client experienced transient scheduling delay; smart-routing triggered host fallback to eu-west-1 (hosted).
3) Billing postbacks show two events for the fallback window: one hosted fallback surcharge and one reserved-capacity usage line but postback reconciler shows missing reserve-credit application.

Observed logs and artifacts:
- Customer-provided invoice screenshot (invoice_2026-03-09.png).
- Postback messages from 2026-03-07 23:05 UTC onwards (attached).
- Console runbook link: https://confluence.redwoodinc/ops/billing-fallback-runbook

Requested outcome:
- Explain why sustainability surcharge applied for fallback window and why reserved-capacity prorated credit not present on provisional invoice.
- Apply provisional adjustment or issue waiver pending root cause.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:27 - Customer (Elena Martins, GreenCart): We confirmed the dedicated pool was healthy; fallback happened automatically. We need the provisional adjustment ASAP to avoid payment failure.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Finance (Marta Kovacs): Holding provisional waiver approval pending final reconcile. Requested detailed charge breakdown and guarantee of not repeating.
2026-03-10 11:00 - Reconciler trace (job id: rc-20260307-23): two postbacks for fallback window present, but reserve-credit application pipeline returned 204 for reserve tag lookup.
Correlation: routing metadata for fallback events was tagged as 'fallback_v2' after a canary alias rename that rolled out 2026-03-07 22:58 UTC (deploy: github.com/redwoodinc/routing-service@c7a1d9).
Hypothesis: reserve-credit matcher expects tags 'dedicated-fallback' or 'reserved-fallback' and does not match new 'fallback_v2' tag. Sustainability surcharge is applied by hosted-tariff logic and matched by region tag, so surcharge applied correctly to hosted fallback consumption.
Evidence: Reconciler logs show message: 'reserve-credit-matcher: no match for tag fallback_v2 -> skipping credit apply' (see /var/logs/billing/reconciler/rc-2026-03-07.log lines 412-427).
Impact scope: Preliminary scan shows ~12 orgs affected in same time window that had traffic routed through the canary edge. GreenCart AI reserved credit expected: $600 (4 hours * $150/hr reserve discount). Sustainability surcharge unexpectedly applied because hosted tariff includes environmental surcharge flag for eu-west-1 and was not suppressed during reserved-credit reconciliation.
Workaround/fix applied 2026-03-12: Reconciler hotfix deployed to add fallback_v2 to reserve-credit matcher allowed list (PR: github.com/redwoodinc/billing-reconciler/pull/321). Backfilled reconcile job reprocessed 2026-03-07 postbacks and applied reserved credits for affected orgs; provisional invoices updated for GreenCart AI and three other orgs.
Follow-up actions: Added unit test to prevent tag-regression, and a migration task to map legacy/new fallback tag aliases (ticket INT-4221). Finance issued provisional waiver for sustainability surcharge for GreenCart AI while backfill completed; waiver id WAIVER-2026-03-12-07 applied.
Customer communication: 2026-03-12 16:00 - Diego Ramos (Support) emailed Elena Martins with explanation, the provisional adjustment amount ($600 credit plus waived $1,420 surcharge), and confirmation that final invoice will reflect backfill. Customer requested a short postmortem; SRE/Eng to prepare by 2026-03-18.
payload.summary: Sustainability surcharge applied to dedicated fallback while reserved capacity credit missing on provisional invoice

Issue summary:
Customer observed truncated rich-attachment payloads after an SSE reconnect while behind a corporate WAF. The client-side parser reports an unclosed XML tag and the final footer block is missing.

Impact:
Several Acme Logistics end-users saw incomplete shipment reports (missing closing XML tag on <report> attachment), which caused downstream processing to reject the payload. Approximately 12% of streaming requests for this customer in us-east in the last 24h show similar symptoms.

Environment:
- Customer on Dedicated tier in prod-us-east behind a corporate WAF (third-party) and their NAT/proxy.
- Client: in-house web app using SSE polyfill, reconnect logic enabled.
- Model: redwood-v1-medium via streaming chat endpoint.

Observed behavior:
- Stream starts and emits most fragments correctly. After an edge failover or WAF idle-probe, the client reconnects and resumes. The server-side logs show a resume delta containing the tail fragment, but the final closing XML tag is absent in the stitched output. The UI shows truncated XML and missing footer block.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should reassemble all fragments so that XML attachments end with a valid closing tag and the footer is present.

Notes on uniqueness of the failure:
- Affected payloads are XML attachments embedded in the streamed deltas (large multi-chunk attachments). The truncation consistently affects the last 8-40 bytes (closing tag and trailing whitespace). This pattern differs from simple duplicate-prefix or missing-final-event issues observed previously: here the final bytes are removed, not reordered or duplicated.

1) Configure a client to stream a long XML attachment via SSE to the Redwood streaming endpoint behind a proxy/WAF that performs chunked transfer rewrite.
2) Simulate an idle-probe or small failover at the edge (close the socket on an upstream LB) to force a reconnect/resume from the client-side SSE polyfill.
3) Observe the reassembled attachment on the client; check for missing closing XML tag (e.g., missing '</report>').
4) Capture edge and server traces (see trace id pattern below) and compare the server-emitted final fragment to the client-observed tail.
5) Repeat with direct (no-WAF) path — issue does not reproduce when WAF/proxy is bypassed.
customer-provided: client console shows parser error: 'XMLParser: unexpected EOF at line 1, column 1432'
gateway logs: trace=trace-0ab12c34 stream_id=st-9f3d: last_sent_fragment='.../report>
'
edge-proxy: connection reset by upstream (idle-probe) at 2026-03-10T17:04:12Z
serving-runtime: resume-delta: final_chunk_base64='PD94bWwgdmVyc2lvb...' (base64 ends earlier than expected)
Initial triage (Support): reproduced with Acme test app behind their corporate WAF; bypassing WAF yields correct final tag.
Edge hypothesis: chunk-boundary rewrite or chunk coalescing at WAF is dropping trailing bytes when connection is handed off during idle probe. This differs from simple reordering bugs — bytes are missing at the end of the stream assembly.
Captured pcap at customer edge shows WAF rewriting chunked boundaries; last chunk size header omitted during an upstream RST+reconnect sequence.
Server traces show we emitted the final bytes before connection closure — server-side assembly looks correct (trace-0ab12c34). Problem appears in transport during reconnect and chunked-transfer reassembly by the WAF/edge.
Checked proxy headers: found evidence of 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' header rewrite and a suspicious zero-length chunk sequence in one failover case.
Related tickets: SUP-311223 and SUP-214159 reference similar resume edge cases behind proxies, but this one consistently removes the trailing closing tag rather than duplicating or misordering fragments.
Customer provided corp-WAF vendor logs; vendor notes 'chunk coalescing optimization' on for that appliance version. They are reproducing internally with a similar workload.
Support (Ava Patel) 2026-03-10: Opened with priority P1 after customer reported automated downstream failures. Attached customer logs and sample payloads.
SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-03-11: Collected server-side traces (trace-0ab12c34). Serving runtime shows final fragment emitted. Asking edge team to check proxy handoff traces and LB logs.
Edge eng (Lina Chen) 2026-03-11: Found LB handoff at 17:04:12Z that preceded an upstream RST. WAF appliance appears to rewrite chunk headers when connection is reset, resulting in a dropped terminal chunk. Engaging WAF vendor.
Customer (Acme, Thomas Reed) 2026-03-11: Verified that bypassing their WAF removes the symptom. They've provided a test harness and allowed a short maintenance window to test mitigations.
Support (Ava Patel) 2026-03-12: Applied temporary workaround: recommend customer disable WAF chunk coalescing or enable connection draining to avoid mid-chunk RST. Customer confirmed improved results during maintenance window.
Edge eng (Lina Chen) 2026-03-12: Proposing a server-side mitigation: emit a final explicit 'end-of-attachment' control event that is idempotent on resume. This will be discussed with product and runtime teams for risk/release planning.
Interaction between corporate WAF chunked-transfer rewrite/coalescing and edge connection handoffs: terminal chunk size header was lost during a mid-stream upstream reset, leading to dropped final bytes on client-side assembly.
Advise customer to disable WAF chunk coalescing / enable connection draining on their WAF or LB. If not possible, enable short client-side post-resume validation and request re-fetch of attachment via REST endpoint as fallback.
Temporary: customer disabled chunk coalescing and confirmed attachments now include closing tag. Long-term: engineering will evaluate emitting an explicit idempotent 'attachment-terminator' control delta on the streaming channel and add guard logic in the edge proxy to preserve zero-length final chunks. Follow-up EPIC to be created if approved.
1) Edge team to add safeguards in proxy to avoid omitting final zero-length chunk headers during handoffs (owner: Lina Chen).
2) Product/Runtime to review streaming protocol extension for explicit attachment terminator event (owner: Marcus Liu).
3) Coordinate with customer to validate fix in staging and then schedule a controlled deploy (timebox: 2 sprints).
4) Update Stream Resume Runbook (confluence) with WAF-related troubleshooting steps and the new diagnostic trace ids to collect.
payload.summary: SSE reconnect behind corporate WAF rewrites chunk boundaries and truncates closing XML tag for rich attachment, footer omitted

payload.description:
Customer reports that the Console > Optimize > Suggestions view shows an estimated savings that does not reconcile with their billing totals for the same time period.

Customer impact:
- Confusion / loss of trust in "estimated $/day" shown in Suggestions drawer.
- Customer is using this as input for internal finance review; needs a defensible reconciliation.

Customer statement (from ticket intake):
- "The Suggestions panel says caching will save ~$1,250/day for /v1/chat on Llama-3 70B. Our usage/billing only moved by ~$300/day after we enabled caching. Where is the rest of the savings?"

Environment:
- Org: Arkadia Finance (enterprise)
- Region: us-east
- Routes: /v1/chat (primary), /v1/embeddings (secondary)
- Models observed in screenshots: rw-llama-3-70b-instruct, rw-qwen2.5-72b-instruct
- Suggestions feature flag: enabled (beta)
- Customer claims caching was enabled on 2026-02-19 ~17:00 ET

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Navigate to Console > Optimize > Suggestions
2) Filter to Project "prod-core" and Route "/v1/chat"
3) Open top caching suggestion (stable ID visible in drawer)
4) Note "Estimated savings ($/day)" and "Assumptions"
5) Compare to Billing > Invoices / Usage export for same days

Evidence / attachments (customer-provided):
- Screenshot 1: Suggestions list filtered to /v1/chat showing $/day estimate and risk badge
- Screenshot 2: Suggestion details drawer showing estimate range and stale_as_of
- Screenshot 3: Billing export excerpt with daily totals

Internal attachments (added by Support):
- Screenshot A: Console Usage Analytics "Inference cost (compute)" view (last 7 days)
- Screenshot B: Cost attribution query results for route/model (GPU-sec + tokens)

Notes:
- This is a beta feature; estimates are not contractual and use telemetry-derived assumptions.
- Need to confirm whether mismatch is due to time window, invoice vs compute cost basis, credits/discounts, partial rollout, or estimator bug.
2026-02-21 10:14 (Dev Patel): Created ticket from CS escalation. Tagging Miguel for customer comms and Nadia Rahman for cost attribution sanity check. Customer is specifically comparing Suggestions $/day to invoiced daily totals.
2026-02-21 11:02 (Miguel Santos): Reached out to Arkadia (email) requesting: (a) exact timeframe they’re comparing, (b) whether batching/caching was enabled for all projects/routes or just one, (c) billing export columns they’re using (gross vs net, credits, committed use).
2026-02-21 13:37 (Nadia Rahman): Quick check: Suggestions estimator uses compute-cost basis from cost-attribution aggregates (GPU-sec + token pricing) and excludes invoice-only items (platform fees, support add-ons, taxes) and can diverge from net invoiced totals due to credits/commit discounts. Also note estimator window defaults to trailing 7d with up to 24h ingestion lag; billing export Arkadia sent appears to be daily invoice accrual in local timezone.
2026-02-22 09:18 (Miguel Santos): Customer replied: comparing Feb 20–21 UTC days, using billing export "total_cost" column (net of credits). They enabled caching only for /v1/chat in project "prod-core" (not other projects). They did a phased rollout at 50% traffic for ~12 hours.
2026-02-22 10:41 (Mei Lin): Estimator for caching suggestion assumes full enablement on the route+model scope shown in the drawer and uses a baseline computed from last 7 days of traffic for that scope. It does not automatically account for partial rollout percentage unless telemetry indicates it as a separate "variant" (not currently wired in v0). If Arkadia enabled caching at 50% for 12 hours, observed savings will be ~25% of the headline daily number for those 24h windows.
2026-02-22 12:06 (Felix Schneider): UI currently labels this as "Estimated savings" but does not prominently call out that savings assume full adoption for the shown scope. Drawer has it in "Assumptions" section; might be too easy to miss. Also, the Suggestions list is sortable by $/day and people treat it as realized savings.
2026-02-23 08:52 (Miguel Santos): Did reconciliation attempt:
- Matched window to trailing 7d used by suggestion (drawer shows stale_as_of = 2026-02-21 00:00 UTC)
- Compared to Console Usage Analytics > "Inference cost (compute)" for same scope (project=prod-core, route=/v1/chat, model=rw-llama-3-70b-instruct)
Result: estimate implies ~18–22% compute cost reduction at full adoption. Customer observed ~6–8% reduction on Feb 20–21 which is consistent with 50% rollout + first-day cache warm-up effect.
Main deltas vs billing export: billing is net of credits/commit; estimate is on compute-cost basis and excludes non-inference line items. Billing is per-day UTC; customer initially compared to local-time days.
2026-02-23 09:30 (Jonas Weber): Cache warm-up effect is real: first 6–12 hours can show lower hit uplift depending on prefix repetitiveness. Estimator assumes steady-state uplift using median of last 7d prefix reuse distribution; it can overstate day-1 savings. Suggest we advise customers to evaluate over at least 48–72 hours after enabling and to look at cache hit metrics + compute cost, not invoice totals.
2026-02-24 14:12 (Miguel Santos): Sent customer guidance:
1) Use Console Usage Analytics "Inference cost (compute)" not invoice total to compare with Suggestions.
2) Align time window to UTC and to stale_as_of period.
3) If using partial rollout, scale the estimate by rollout percentage and allow 24–72h for cache warm-up.
4) If they need invoice reconciliation, we can help map compute-cost delta to net invoice (credits/commit discounts will compress visible delta).
Customer acknowledged and asked for a one-pager they can share internally. Looping in Elliot Price for docs link + suggested wording.
2026-02-25 10:27 (Elliot Price): Pointed Miguel to internal draft docs section explaining compute-cost vs billing totals and rollout scaling. We should also add a short inline callout in drawer: "Assumes 100% of traffic" + "Compute-cost estimate (not invoice total)".
2026-02-26 16:45 (Miguel Santos): Customer confirmed the discrepancy was primarily due to (a) comparing net billing totals (credits/commit) vs compute-cost estimate, and (b) partial rollout + warm-up. They can proceed with internal review using compute-cost deltas. Marking resolved. Follow-up: file copy/UX tweak request to make assumptions more prominent.
Root cause classification: Not a billing bug; a reconciliation/expectation gap + missing clarity in UI.

Contributing factors:
- Suggestions $/day is based on compute-cost attribution aggregates (GPU-sec + token pricing) and does not equal net invoiced totals (credits/commit discounts, platform fees, taxes).
- Estimator assumes full adoption for the scope shown; does not incorporate rollout percentage for A/B/canary in v0.
- Cache warm-up can make first-day realized savings lower than steady-state estimate.
- Time window mismatch: suggestion uses trailing 7d baseline + stale_as_of; customer compared to two UTC days and initially used local time.

Recommendation to Support/CS:
- When customers compare to billing, redirect to Console Usage Analytics (compute-cost) for apples-to-apples.
- Ask for rollout percentage and whether change was applied across all routes/projects.
- Ensure they compare a 48–72h window post-enable to avoid warm-up noise.

Product follow-ups (non-blocking):
- Promote assumption text in UI (100% adoption, compute-cost basis, exclude discounts/credits).
- Consider adding an optional field in suggestion payload for "adoption_factor" or a UI control to scale savings by rollout percentage (future).
- Add docs section on reconciliation: compute-cost vs invoice total.
Provided reconciliation guidance and validated that observed savings aligns with estimate after accounting for (1) compute-cost vs net billing totals, (2) partial rollout percentage, (3) cache warm-up and baseline window alignment. No platform defect identified; follow-up request logged to improve UI copy around assumptions and to clarify savings are compute-cost estimates.
payload.summary: Optimization Suggestions: estimated savings does not match billing/usage totals (Arkadia Finance)

comments: 2024-11-05T14:30:00Z Runtime Eng: Hypothesis: new quant profile increases transient memory pressure with large multi-turn KV caches, causing evictions and a cascade of decode retries. Suggest shadow-rollback path: toggle tenant feature-flag to legacy optimizer profile-v7, disable kv-prefetch for tenant, lower adaptive max_batch to 64 while observing metrics for 30m.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported intermittent 5xx errors and high tail latency after we enabled a per-tenant adaptive optimizer profile (adaptive batching + prefix-KV caching + new 8-bit quant profile) during a staged migration. Impact: production traffic from BrightClinic experienced 10-15% request errors and elevated p99 latency between 11:30 and 13:00 UTC.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests returned 5xx for a subset of tenant requests (multi-turn chat flows).
- Elevated p99 latency from 480ms to 1.8s for affected endpoints.
- Customer revenue-impacting: clinical decision assistant queries timed out for end users.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dc-eu-east-1a (customer-dedicated-045) routed through us-east control plane for this migration.
- Serving runtime v2.6.3, optimizer-service v1.9.0 (feature flag: adaptive-per-tenant-v2).
- Config: per-tenant profile applied via optimizer API, enabled KV-prefetch: true, batching: adaptive (max_batch=128, latency_target_ms=40), quant_profile: profile-v8-qat.

Steps to reproduce (customer flow):
1) Tenant sends a multi-turn chat request with average prompt length ~850 tokens and generate length ~400 tokens.
2) Request routed to dedicated pool and enters adaptive batching path.
3) When batches hit hybrid slow path (mixture of long sequences and short), some workers reported OOM-evictions or high GC pauses in runtime, leading to connection resets and 5xx.

Observed behavior:
- Connection resets and 502/504 spikes in CloudLB and gateway logs.
- Worker logs show transient KV cache mismatch warnings (eviction race) and quant-decode retries.
- Autoscaler did not spin up new GPUs during the window due to burst capacity gating.

Expected behavior:
- Adaptive profile should smooth batching without causing OOM or decode failures and fallback safely to a lower-cost path without user-visible 5xx.

Logs/Attachments:
- Attached API request IDs: [rcpt-20241105-1123-az, rcpt-20241105-1127-qd] (in ticket comments).
- Link to metrics snapshot: https://rwd-console/metrics/brightclinic/2024-11-05/11-30-13-00

Customer request:
- Immediate guidance to safely revert per-tenant profile (shadow rollback) and a checklist for migration to prevent reoccurrence.

2024-11-05 12:05 - Support (Maya Chen): Acknowledged. Opening investigation and coordinating with SRE to capture worker logs and autoscaler trace. Asking customer to provide a couple of failing request IDs and whether they can route a small repro traffic to a staging pool.
2024-11-05 12:18 - Customer (BrightClinic - Priya Rao): Provided request IDs rcpt-20241105-1123-az and rcpt-20241105-1127-qd. We can divert a replay of 1% of traffic to staging if needed. Impacting urgent clinical flows — please expedite.
2024-11-05 13:02 - SRE (Daniel Park): Observed repeated 'kv-prefetch eviction race' messages and 'quant-decode retry' errors in worker logs for that tenant's worker set. Autoscaler policy blocked burst due to a configured budget cap. Opening hotfix plan with runtime team.

Additional notes:
2024-11-05 15:10 - Support (Maya Chen): Performed staged rollback for tenant: 1) applied legacy profile-v7 snapshot 2) set kv-prefetch=false for tenant 3) adjusted max_batch to 64. Monitoring now. Customer confirmed improvement in a small replay run.
2024-11-05 15:45 - Customer (Priya Rao): Replay confirmed — errors dropped to <1% and p99 latency returned to ~420ms. Thanks; want post-mortem and migration checklist.
2024-11-07 09:12 - Support (Maya Chen): Ticket being closed after providing post-rollback runbook and follow-up items. Recommending gated re-rollout with staged canary, memory headroom checks, and temporary per-tenant circuit breaker for quant profile changes.
Captured worker logs from dedicated pool and correlated with customer request IDs — saw 'kv-cache-evict-race' followed by quant-decoder fallback on same worker threads.
Heap and GPU memory profiles indicate spikes coinciding with long sequence requests, pushing memory over configured headroom when combined with new quant code-path allocations.
Autoscaler policy prevented quick burst due to per-tenant budget - this prolonged worker saturation window and increased error exposure.
Hypothesis: quant-profile-v8 introduces temporary additional decode buffers and metadata, incompatible with high KV cache residency for long-turn conversations; adaptive batching's max_batch=128 increased variance causing straggler pressure.
Regression check: no similar errors in other tenants using same profile but with shorter typical sequence lengths; suggests workload-specific interaction.
Action taken: executed per-tenant shadow rollback (legacy profile snapshot restore) and disabled kv-prefetch to reduce memory churn. Verified through replay and metrics that errors remediated.
Follow-up recommended: add preflight memory simulation for per-tenant optimizer changes, add per-tenant circuit breaker for quant/decode failure spikes, and improve autoscaler burst thresholds tied to optimizer transitions.
Performed safe per-tenant shadow rollback to legacy optimizer profile (profile-v7 snapshot). Steps executed: 1) locked tenant config to prevent auto-retries of migration job, 2) applied snapshot restore of profile-v7 via optimizer API, 3) disabled kv-prefetch on tenant, 4) lowered adaptive max_batch to 64, 5) monitored for 45 minutes and ran 1% traffic replay. Observed errors fall from ~12% to <1% and p99 latency returned to baseline.
Post-rollback follow-ups delivered to customer and internal teams:
- Runbook: 'per-tenant optimizer migration preflight' with memory headroom checklist and simulated replay (confluence link provided).
- Work item opened with runtime team to add graceful fallback in quant decode path and to reduce transient buffer allocations (see PR infra/optimizer-config#4212).
- Autoscaler policy change proposal to allow a limited burst for first 10 minutes after optimizer profile toggles.
Customer accepted rollback and requested staged re-rollout only after preflight checks. Ticket resolved and turned into operative guidance for future per-tenant migrations.
Create per-tenant optimizer preflight script and CI job (owner: Runtime Eng)
Implement quant-decode graceful-fallback to drop to lower-memory path before returning 5xx (owner: Runtime Eng)
Adjust autoscaler burst gating to allow temporary capacity for optimizer transitions (owner: SRE)
Document runbook and publish to customer-facing migration guide (owner: Developer DX)
payload.summary: Per-tenant adaptive migration to new quant/batching profile causing intermittent 5xxs — request for guided shadow rollback

2026-03-12T14:22:00Z Rahul: Reproduced locally with shard-merge simulator. Found a codepath in the merge writer that appends a 16-byte alignment buffer when a segment file size is odd; metadata header not updated. Drafted hotfix to trim padding and align header write. Opening PR for review.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent loss of reranker candidates and large p99 latency spikes after a daily shard maintenance window.

Impact: NimbusDocs sees ~7% of queries return fewer-than-expected top-k results and p99 tail latency for their /rerank endpoint increased from ~120ms to ~1.3s during a 30m window. This affects search relevance and user experience for their dedicated cluster.

Environment: prod dedicated cluster (us-east), dedicated capacity, embedding ingestion pipeline writes to shard groups S-14..S-18 during the maintenance merge job.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a manual shard-merge on a replica set containing 3 rotated segments (simulated via staging script).
2) Submit batch embedding+rerank flow used by NimbusDocs (256-dim embeddings, batch size 64).
3) Observe rerank responses and token-level metrics; compare before/after merge.

Observed behavior: Merged embedding payloads include extra zero-padding bytes appended to the end of the serialized vector. The reranker receives vectors with inconsistent effective dimension metadata and rejects or drops candidates in the ANN stage, while some requests fall back to CPU-based brute-force scanning causing p99 latency spike.

Expected behavior: Shard merge should produce compact, canonical embedding payloads with matching dimension headers. Reranker should receive consistent vectors and return deterministic top-k without fallback for this workload.

Initial customer-provided logs: Attached trace id t-20260312-9f3a (included in comments). Customer also provided a sample merged payload (hex) showing 16 trailing 0x00 bytes.

Temporary workaround: Disabled shard auto-merge for NimbusDocs' namespace until a fix is deployed. Recommended customer-side mitigation: pin to older shard snapshot or route rerank to fallback model alias.

Notes on urgency: Customer is in active production and relies on consistent rerank results for their SLAs. Priority set to P1 and Sev1 assigned.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:15 - NimbusDocs (customer): Provided trace id t-20260312-9f3a, attachment hex_dump_9f3a.bin and noted issue occurs immediately after nightly maintenance job. Reports reproduction rate ~30% of merges.
2026-03-13 08:30 - Support (Maya): Confirmed customer workaround (disable auto-merge) in place. Noted customer would like ETA for permanent fix and request for a backfilled re-run once fixed.
2026-03-14 12:05 - NimbusDocs: Confirmed observed improvement in sample batch and approved canary expansion. Asked for postmortem and regression test to avoid recurrence.
Binary serializer writes a padding alignment buffer for historical reasons (optimizing page writes) but merge path omitted header-length recalculation in ~20% of runs due to a race when merging odd-numbered segments.
The reranker validates expected_dim header against payload length; mismatch triggers ANN index to drop candidates rather than erroring loudly, which is causing silent top-k loss.
CPU fallback path is invoked when the ANN engine returns empty candidate set; this explains p99 spike observed concurrently with dropped candidates.
Canary mitigation implemented at proxy layer: detect length mismatch, trim trailing 0x00 bytes, and rewrite dimension header before forwarding. This is a short-term bandaid while embedding-service hotfix is reviewed.
Root cause traced to commit 3b7d9a2 (storage: add alignment buffer) which did not update merge_writer metadata handling for odd-segment merges.
Proposed permanent fix: patch merge_writer to recompute and write correct header after padding, add unit/integration test for odd-size merges, and add an observability metric for "padding_trimmed_count".
Mitigation: proxy-level trimming was deployed to canary (10%) on 2026-03-14 and expanded after positive signals. Permanent fix is implemented in PR #1428 (embedding-service) and currently in code review. Post-deploy plan: deploy fix to production, backfill affected shard merges for NimbusDocs during a maintenance window, run regression test suite for shard merges, and add monitoring alert for "merge_padding_detected". Customer accepted mitigation and requested a postmortem after deployment. Follow-up tasks: INT-33421 created to add integration tests and retention metrics.
payload.summary: Embedding shard merge introduced extraneous padding bytes; reranker dropping candidates and causing p99 latency spikes

comments: 2026-03-10T05:00:00Z Aisha Patel: Customer reported p95 spikes during autoscale. Collected traces, requested consent to switch residency_mode temporarily.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers (CatalystHealth) observed periodic increases in p95 token latency for EU-pinned requests (prod, eu-west). The spike correlates with cluster autoscale events (~04:15 UTC and ~11:30 UTC) when additional serving nodes come online. During these windows ~10-20% of requests that should remain in eu-west are observed egressing via us-west, adding ~80-250ms TLS/RTT overhead and causing p95 jumps.

Impact:
- Increased p95 latency to ~620-950ms for interactive chat endpoints for ~5-12 minute windows.
- Degraded UX for CatalystHealth's customers (enterprise SLA impacted).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod, eu-west region; customer pinned route policy: residency_mode=preferred (pin with TTL=10m).
- Affected model flavors: redwood-1.3-llama-compat (primary), open-llama-7b (fallback).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer issues large fan-out workload to eu-west pinned endpoint over 10 minutes to trigger autoscale.
2) Observe p95 via customer metrics and our Console -> Route Latency.
3) Correlate with control-plane scale events in the same time window.

Observed behavior:
- Traceroutes from serving runtime during incident show asymmetric hop: requests originate in eu-west but egress via NAT IPs mapped to us-west (see logs below).
- Control-plane routing logs show a 'route-refresh' coincident with node registration, during which route selection briefly allows cross-region fallback for a subset of sticky sessions.

Expected behavior:
- For residency_mode=preferred with active EU capacity available, traffic should remain within eu-west; fallback to other regions only when capacity or health checks fail. Route-refresh should not flip egress for pinned sessions during scale-in/scale-out windows.

Logs / metrics (excerpt):
- traceroute to 10.32.54.11 (serving node) -> final hop resolves to 34.203.x.x (us-west NAT) at 04:15:12 UTC
- control-plane event: scale_event id=se-98233 timestamp=2026-03-10T04:15:10Z action=node-register pool=eu-west nodes=+4
- routing decision log: route-select session=abcd1234 residency=preferred candidate_pool=[eu-west, us-west] selected=eu-west (control_plane:router) but egress_nat=us-west-nat-07 (network:egress)
- cloud flow logs: conn_count spike from eu-west LB to us-west NATs during event window

Preliminary investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: during node registration there is a short control-plane state reconciliation window where route pins and egress NAT assignment are evaluated asynchronously. Sticky session mapping (control-plane) remained pinned to eu-west but the path chosen by the network overlay selected a us-west egress for a subset of new connections created while the node came up.
- Repro steps executed on staging with scaled-down pool reproduced the asymmetric egress when we artificially delayed the control-plane's route-store update by ~3s.
- No evidence of customer misconfiguration; their route TTL/TTL-refresh is standard (10m).

Workaround applied:
- Support/CS temporarily advised CatalystHealth to set residency_mode=strict for the critical endpoints; that prevents cross-region egress at the cost of returning 429s during total EU capacity exhaustion. Customer accepted temporary change for the time being.

Next steps / planned fixes:
- Short term (SRE): implement a guard in control-plane:router to suppress non-deterministic egress reassignment for existing sticky sessions while node registration is in-progress (INT-7741). ETA: 48 hours for patch and targeted rollout to eu-west.
- Mid term (engineering): add egress-assignment atomic update (ensure NAT assignment is consistent with route pin atomically) and add an integration test covering autoscale + residency pins. PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2211
- Postmortem: schedule full incident review and update residency runbook with explicit autoscale handoff behavior.

Resolution / status:
- Workaround (strict residency) accepted and applied for affected routes at 2026-03-10T21:30:00Z. Engineering patch scheduled for rollout 2026-03-13. Monitoring alert created to detect asymmetric egress IPs and unpinned egress > 1% during scale windows.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:04 UTC - Support (to customer): Applied temporary residency_mode=strict on the flagged endpoints. Please verify UX. Customer reported improved p95 immediately.
2026-03-12 16:21 UTC - Engineering (PR/CI): PR 2211 merged into main after canary. Release scheduled; will coordinate with CS before global rollout.
Workaround (strict residency) applied and engineering patch merged. Monitoring rules added to detect asymmetric egress. Full postmortem scheduled after global rollout.
Assigned to SRE for rollout coordination. Follow-up: validate that strict_residency toggles do not introduce undue 429s for customer traffic profile; coordinate rate-limits with CatalysHealth engineering team.
