payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a class of SSE streaming responses where the final paragraph (closing paragraph) is never emitted. The stream begins normally and intermediate chunks arrive; however, after a short mid-stream proxy reconnect or HTTP/2 stream multiplexing event, the runtime sends a truncated terminal event and the final closing paragraph is missing. The payload appears valid up to the last emitted chunk; the terminal JSON/choice metadata arrives but the last textual paragraph is absent.

Impact:
- Customer chat sessions are missing the final paragraph in ~3-4% of long multi-paragraph responses for a specific traffic pattern.
- Affects user-visible content quality; customers reported degraded UX and downstream truncation handling.

Environment:
- Customer: NovaSearch Inc. (dedicated cluster)
- Region: us-east (edge -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime)
- Client pattern: HTTP/2 multiplexed connections behind a corporate layer-7 proxy that performs quick connection rebinds for stickiness.
- Model: redwood-13b-compat (pinned for dedicated environment)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided simplified):
1) Start a long prompt that produces 3+ paragraphs (approx 400-800 tokens).
2) Keep client connection open; exercise simultaneous parallel streams on same TCP connection.
3) Trigger a controlled proxy rebind (customer simulates with a quick stickiness change on their proxy).
4) Observe streaming SSE session: final closing paragraph missing ~30% of the time under their proxy conditions.

Expected behavior:
- Stream emits all tokens and final paragraph, plus terminal metadata event, consistently even when upstream proxy rebinds occur.

Observed behavior:
- Middle and penultimate chunks arrive intact. After a short proxy-side session flip, the server-side terminal metadata is emitted but the final paragraph content is absent. In some reproductions the client receives a terminal marker without the trailing whitespace/punctuation.

Attached logs (redacted):
- Correlated request IDs where issue observed: req-20260310-9a7b, req-20260310-9a9f, req-20260310-a0b1
- Edge proxy logs show quick 302->reset sequence and new session token during the stream window.
- Runtime trace shows normal tokenization and choice assembly up to final chunk, then a brief "session token mismatch" event 90-120ms before terminal event.

Notes:
- Customer confirms disabling multiplexing on the client side eliminates the symptom for them (workaround).
- Issue reproduces only when the traffic is routed through their enterprise proxy with the rebind behavior; not observed in our public test harness with identical prompts.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:02 - Customer (NovaSearch): Confirmed toggling client multiplexing to single stream reduces incidents to 0 in 500 tests. They can provide a capture of proxy behavior if needed.
2026-03-12 10:55 - Support (Maya Chen): Shared customer-impact mitigation steps and asked customer to test a targeted client-side retry that delays finalization by 200ms; customer agreed to test and will report results by EOD.
2026-03-12 15:30 - Customer (NovaSearch): Confirmed small delay workaround reduces occurrences but would prefer server-side fix. Requested ETA for a permanent fix.
Hypothesis 1: Edge/proxy rebind causes RST_STREAM semantics overlapping with final chunk write; edge marks stream complete and discards trailing chunk body.
Hypothesis 2: Multiplexed HTTP/2 stream mapping at our edge lacks ordering guarantees during in-flight session token swap; writes can be acknowledged out-of-band and lost.
Observed: In all failing traces terminal metadata arrives but content length is shorter than expected by 60-120 bytes (consistent with missing final paragraph).
PCAP from customer shows single TCP connection where two logical H2 streams flip affinity; server-side logs show last-chunk queued at t0, RST_STREAM at t0+30ms, terminal emitted at t0+70ms.
Reproducibility: Customer environment strong (30% under their proxy conditions), internal repro without their proxy is rare.
Action: requested deeper edge logs for wire-level ordering and increased tracing on h2 stream lifecycle.
Workaround: Customer can disable HTTP/2 multiplexing or add a ~200-300ms client-side delay before finalization to allow pending writes to flush; both mitigate the issue.
Root cause: race between edge connection rebind (proxy-side token flip) and our edge's stream finalization path that allowed terminal metadata to be forwarded before the last text chunk write was durably flushed to the connection mapping.
Permanent fix plan: edge team will implement an idempotent finalization handshake so that the serving runtime waits for a confirmed flush/ack from the edge mapping before emitting the terminal event to the customer. Runtime patch (PR #2431) adds aggressive flush and retry on final chunk and an additional sequence check on the edge.
Rollout notes: will deploy a canary to edge-nodes in us-east first; target deploy window 2026-03-18 02:00-04:00 UTC. Customer impact expected to be resolved post-canary.
Follow-ups: add e2e test that simulates proxy rebinds during chunk flush; update streaming runbook with guidance for client multiplexing and recommended backoff.
Customer prefers server-side fix; support to coordinate announcement and post-deploy verification.
Consider adding explicit header to indicate "final-chunk-flush" semantics for customers behind aggressive proxies as short-term opt-in flag.
Related to INT-1198 where an internal ticket captured an edge-connection-affinity race in a different context.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Velociti reported a customer-facing outage beginning 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC during an automated multi-region failover test. A subset of routed requests entered a deadlock state in the serving-runtime during fallback routing, leading to streaming stalls, duplicate completions, and elevated token billing for affected customers.

Impact:
- ~42% of Velociti traffic in us-east and eu-west experienced stalled streaming responses for 6–18s before client-side reconnects.
- Duplicate completions were observed in ~4% of affected sessions (identical or near-identical responses returned twice).
- Billing exposure estimated at ~$4.2k for the incident window.
- Customer escalated to enterprise on-call and requested immediate remediation and credits.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 02:09 UTC: Canary regional routing change applied (automatic fallback rule updated to prefer quantized variants).
- 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC: Velociti alert (in-app and sent to support) — elevated latencies and streaming stalls.
- 2026-03-10 02:18 UTC: Support triage; SRE paged.
- 2026-03-10 02:24 UTC: Mitigation: rolled back routing change and pinned Velociti traffic to previous model variant.
- 2026-03-10 02:35 UTC: Partial recovery; engineering investigation continues.
- 2026-03-10 05:10 UTC: Full traffic normal for Velociti; incident declared resolved.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Start concurrent multi-region failover simulation targeting fallback to quantized variants with per-tenant fanout >= 12.
2) Inject a routing priority update that triggers simultaneous multipath fanout.
3) Observe serving-runtime streams for stalls and duplicate completions when kernel-selection path flips mid-request.

Logs / Observations:
- Serving-runtime traces show requests stuck at `kv_cache::lock_or_wait` for 8–16s in 1k+ traces.
- Router logs indicate simultaneous re-routing attempts to multiple fallback pools for same session id (multipath fanout).
- Autoscaler metrics showed transient burst that exhausted local GPU pool capacity triggering fallback; concurrent fallback logic attempted routing to two regions in quick succession.
- Trace snippet: https://logs.redwood.com/velociti/2026-03-10/trace-7a12f (SRE-only).

Initial hypothesis:
- Race between multipath fallback routing + KV cache eviction led to lock contention in the runtime when kernel selection changed (quantized -> fp16) mid-stream.
- Router's dedup/affinity window did not sufficiently de-dupe near-simultaneous fallback replays for the same session.

Temporary mitigations applied during incident:
- Rolled back the failing routing rule and pinned Velociti to the pre-change model variant.
- Increased per-tenant concurrency cap for Velociti to avoid autoscaler-induced fallback.
- Disabled cross-region multipath fallback for the customer's tenant until a permanent fix.

Desired outcomes / next steps (post-incident):
- Engineering to develop a runtime fix to abort in-flight kernel flip attempts when KV cache is present (PR referenced below).
- Router changes to enforce stronger de-duplication and an expanded affinity window during failover events.
- Add smoke tests that simulate kernel flip + multipath fallback concurrently.
- Runbook updates: explicitly include steps to pin models and throttle per-tenant concurrency during region failovers.
- Customer-facing: issue apology, provide detailed postmortem, and apply billing credit for measured exposure.

Additional notes:
Hypothesis refinement: kernel switching path lacks checkpointing for in-flight KV references; when cache is reallocated on kernel swap the runtime waits on a lock that the router's replay logic can re-trigger.
Cross-reference: similar symptoms seen in SUP-99555 (GPU pool exhaustion + streaming hang) but root cause differs (here it's kernel flip race).

Root cause: race condition between router multipath fallback logic and runtime kernel flip path that resulted in lock contention on KV cache during in-flight responses. Fixes applied: (1) rolled back routing change and pinned traffic (mitigation), (2) merged runtime hotfix to abort kernel swap if active KV refs exist (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1289), (3) router PR to increase dedupe window and serialize fallback for same session (https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-router/pull/452). Customer credited $4,200 for exposure and given extended monitoring for 48 hours. Postmortem published to Confluence.

ENG-2: Router dedupe and affinity window change to be rolled out with feature flag (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-03-17).

Engineering to provide canary deployment plan before the call. Flagged for quarterly reliability review. Slack thread: #incidents (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/INC12345).

03/10/2026 — Update: Routing rollback applied; symptoms reduced.
03/11/2026 — Postmortem: Shared detailed root cause, mitigation steps, and billing credit. Customer accepted credit and requested additional safeguards during planned failovers.
Velociti (enterprise) experienced degraded streaming and duplicate completions across US/EU regions for ~3 hours during a scheduled failover; customer traffic returned to normal after rollback and pinning. Billing exposure estimated and credited. Customer is satisfied with remediation but requested guardrails for future failovers.
Include root-cause timeline with kernel flip trace IDs, quantify duplicate completion types (exact dup vs near-duplicate), and runbook gaps that allowed multipath fallback to be enabled during a canary. Recommend policy: disable cross-region multipath during any rolling routing experiments until dedupe improvements land.

Issue summary: During the scheduled autoscale warm-up window for Polaris AI's dedicated pool (prod | us-west) we observed repeated short-lived throughput collapses (p95 and p99) for long-context streaming workloads. Impact: Customer-facing latency regressions and request queueing leading to dropped streams and client retries. Estimated customer impact: 8-12% of requests for the affected tenant experienced >=3x p99 latency increase during the window on 2026-03-10.
1) Customer tenant Polaris AI sends sustained long-context streaming traffic to dedicated pool between 09:30-10:15 UTC. 2) Autoscaler triggers scale-up from 6->9 GPU slots (incremental warm-up). 3) Observe serving-runtime logs and scheduler metrics. 4) Observe request queue growth and repeated per-slot 'prefetch-throttle' warnings and 'slot-lock' jitter. Expected: Smooth capacity increase with stable per-slot throughput. Observed: transient slot starvations and interleaved prefetch backpressure causing serialization of short and long streams.
Excerpt from serving-runtime (2026-03-10T09:41:12Z): WARN prefetch_throttle: tenant=polaris, slot_id=3, inflight_kv_prefetch=12, threshold=8
ERROR slot_lock_timeout: tenant=polaris, slot_id=7, hold_ms=1203

Additional notes:
Cloud infra (2026-03-10T09:42:05Z): INFO gpu_attach: slot_provision=2 latency_ms=4032
2026-03-10 - Support (Ava): Customer reported repeated client-side stream resets during autoscale warm-up window; opened ticket and flagged as P1 due to customer SLA breach.
2026-03-10 - Oncall SRE (Liam): Correlated serving-runtime 'prefetch_throttle' warnings with autoscaler scale events. Initial hypothesis: prefetch/backpressure on KV cache plus slow GPU attach latency causing slot serialization.
2026-03-10 - Customer (Polaris AO): We see spikes in request latency and increased retries starting around 09:36 UTC. The pattern aligns with your reported scale-ups. Logs attached from client side.
2026-03-11 - Eng (Rohit Gupta): Replayed traffic in staging; reproduced slot_lock_timeout when attaching GPUs under heavy long-context streaming. Observed NVMe prefetch queue saturation and per-slot mutex hold spikes.
2026-03-12 - Support (Liam): Proposed customer workaround: schedule warmups during off-peak hours or switch to pinned-reserve while we test fix. Customer prefers patching platform first; request expedited rollout.
Hypothesis A: KV cache prefetching continues aggressively during scale-up; newly attached GPUs contend on NVMe, causing per-slot I/O stalls and mutex holds -> serialized batches and higher p99.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler attaches multiple GPUs in quick succession without staggering; provisioning latency (4s-6s) plus scheduler bank-backoff causes allocation delays that amplify queueing for surviving slots.
Staging repro: Synthetic long-stream flood reproduced slot_lock_timeout at ~80% sustained load when GPUs attached within <15s intervals.
Telemetry: per-slot prefetch queue length peaked at 12 (threshold 8). NVMe write latency increased from median 2ms -> 35ms during attach events.
Cross-tenant signals: No evidence of another noisy tenant in the same pool at the time; noisy-neighbor metrics negative. Root appears tied to attach-time behaviors and prefetch settings for new allocations.
Related: linked issue SUP-631210 documented similar attach-latency patterns but attributed to background checkpoint writer; here background writer not active for this pool.
Mitigation experiments: Disabling prefetch for new slots during warm-up eliminated slot_lock timeouts in staging; adding 30s attach-stagger reduced NVMe latency peaks.
Risk assessment: Disabling prefetch may increase cold-start token costs slightly but reduces customer-facing errors during scale events. Attach-stagger delays peak provisioning but smooths throughput.
Proposed short-term mitigation: platform patch to suspend aggressive KV-prefetch for newly attached GPUs for first 60s + autoscaler attach-stagger of 30s. Long-term: dynamic prefetch throttling based on NVMe latency and active inflight counts.
Workaround applied: autoscaler team deployed attach-stagger (30s) to dedicated pools and serving-runtime patch to suppress KV-prefetch for newly attached GPUs for 60s. Deployment rolled to prod us-west at 2026-03-12T03:20Z. Post-deploy monitoring shows p99 latency for Polaris AI returned to baseline within one autoscale window and no further slot_lock_timeouts observed. Follow-ups: (1) telemetry alert for prefetch queue depth to trigger autoscaler pacing, (2) engineering story to implement adaptive prefetch throttle tied to NVMe latency (tracked in ENG backlog), (3) customer notified and agreed to re-open if regressions continue. Ticket transitioned to "Waiting on Customer" for final confirmation before Close.
Create ENG story: adaptive-prefetch-throttle-based-on-nvme-latency (priority P2)
Add an autoscaler test-case for rapid attach and long-streams to CI stress suite
Notify account team and schedule a 1:1 with Polaris AI to review mitigation and timing for a permanent fix
Add a runbook entry: 'suspend-prefetch-during-warmup' and include mitigation checklist

Issue summary: BrightWrite reported a sustained spike of 5xx responses beginning ~08:45 local on 2026-03-12 for production traffic. Errors surface at the API gateway and are amplified by upstream runtime crashloops. Impact: multiple customer endpoints returned 502/503/504; customer-facing feature degraded for ~75% of requests during peak. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east, customer pinned to dedicated GPU pool. Timeline: 08:42 - first elevated latency ticks seen in metrics; 08:45 - customer reported 5xx rate >30% of requests; 08:50 - internal alert (error-rate) triggered; 09:10 - triage started. Customer reported increased request latency followed by steady 5xx floor.
1) Send production-like concurrent chat/embedding mix against customer's dedicated route (concurrency ~600).
2) Cold autoscaler warmup triggers (~08:30 pattern) followed by a wave of prefetched model loads.
3) Observe API gateway 429/502 spikes then persistent 5xx as runtimes hit GPU soft-locks.
4) Replaying same traffic on staging with identical load did not immediately reproduce until GPU driver probe introduced longer prefetch concurrency.
Notes: reproduction requires sustained mixed load and autoscaler warmup pattern (tenant-scale-up).
[2026-03-12T08:47:02Z] apigw: route=/v1/generate status=502 upstream_error='upstream reset' tenant=brightwrite
[2026-03-12T08:47:06Z] runtime: watchdog: nvml driver unresponsive, kernel signaled reset
[2026-03-12T08:47:09Z] runtime: pid=14321 exit_code=137 signal=9 reason='GPU driver soft-lock'
[2026-03-12T08:48:10Z] apigw: rate_limiter: token_bucket_drop tenant=brightwrite effective_rate=600r/s configured=500r/s
[2026-03-12T08:49:33Z] observability: trace_id=abc123 latency=1450ms alloc=2.1GB prefetch=1.2s

Initial hypothesis: ingress rate limiter misconfiguration caused hedged retries and amplified connection churn. Secondary observation: serving-runtime instances experienced NVML/dGPU soft-locks under concurrent prefetch; driver log shows repeated resets and short-lived cuda contexts. Correlation: spikes in apigw token drops align with runtime restarts (pearson r=0.78 across 1-minute bins). Traces show high prefetch latency before crash. Autoscaler warmup created a cascading prefetch pressure: many runtimes initiated model loads simultaneously, increasing GPU context pressure and triggering driver soft-locks on particular kernel builds. We validated by isolating one runtime and reproducing higher error rate only when prefetch concurrency > 24. Metrics links: https://metrics.redwood.com/d/teams/brightwrite/5xx-waves and https://dash.redwood.com/runtimes/14321/events.
Workaround applied (2026-03-12 10:05): temporarily increased per-tenant token bucket and enabled conservative prefetch cap for BrightWrite (cap lowered to 8 concurrent prefetches). Routed traffic to fallback model variant (open-instruct-medium) while runtimes were restarted. Immediate effect: 5xx rate dropped below 2% within 12 minutes. Long-term fixes: (1) runtime PR#1987 (driver watchdog resilience) scheduled for canary 2026-03-15; (2) api-gateway PR#421 adjusts token-bucket calculation to account for warmup bursts and prevents hedged-retry amplification; (3) autoscaler backoff tuning to stagger shard prefetch; operational action items created: INT-55120 (autoscaler stagger job) and INT-55121 (driver vendor engagement for kernel-level fix). Customer notified of workaround and will be offered a credits review for impacted windows.

Additional notes:

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightDocs is observing intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and token throttling across their dedicated reserved pool. Spikes occur during short bursts (1–5 minutes) after a period of low activity and correlate with a high rate of prefetch/eviction churn on the GPU nodes. Symptoms point to priority inversion where on-demand/burst allocations trigger kernel preemptions and eviction storms that delay warmup of pinned reserved workers, causing downstream queueing and token-level throttling at the API layer.

Impact:
- BrightDocs reports elevated p95/p99 for generate and streaming requests; customer-facing features degrade for end users.
- Observed increased 429s/timeouts for some high-concurrency routes routed to the dedicated pool.
- Customer is on a committed reserved pool; they expect predictable latency.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool in us-east, mixed GPU types (A10g + A100 lite).
- Autoscaler: predictive+threshold policy; burst capacity enabled.
- Workload mix: short chat-style requests (seq len < 512) and occasional long-context tests.

Why unique/important:
This is not a simple capacity shortage: nodes have spare GPU memory and utilization looks moderate, but eviction/reload churn at the driver/kernel level is causing transient throughput regression. The packet of behavior suggests scheduling/kernel preemption interactions with our eviction prefetch logic and the autoscaler's burst routing rules.
1) Simulate low baseline load on reserved pool for 10+ minutes (idle warm cache).
2) Fire a sustained burst of short concurrent requests (50–200 RPS) with mixed routes pinned to reserved pool; include on-demand burst traffic aimed at same region.
3) Observe p95/p99 latency spikes within 30–90s of burst start and increased eviction/prefetch log lines on affected nodes.
4) Reduce burst; note that latencies take ~2–6 minutes to return to baseline depending on kernel cache warmup and batching behaviour.
2026-02-20T13:17:42Z node-09 kernel: evict:kv_cache miss -> reload (size=1.2GB) duration=237ms
2026-02-20T13:17:43Z serving-runtime: prefetch evict sequence for tenant=brightdocs-01 removed 6 segments
2026-02-20T13:18:01Z scheduler: allocate burst slot on-demand -> placed on shared-pool-node-21 (preempted reserved-worker node-09)
2026-02-20T13:18:05Z api-gateway: route=generate tenant=brightdocs-01 p95=842ms p99=2120ms tokens=~450
Initial hypothesis: autoscaler burst routing will place on-demand bursts onto shared nodes and occasionally trigger kernel-level preemption of reserved workers. When reserved workers are preempted, their KV caches + eager-prefetch window are invalidated leading to a rebuild cost that inflates tail latencies. Observed correlation between preempt events and first request latency for the next 50–200 requests.

What we checked:
- Node-level GPU memory usage and process lists: no out-of-memory; memory free but frequent allocation/free patterns seen.
- Kernel driver logs: repeated page migration/eviction entries matching timestamps of spikes.
- Routing decisions: short window where policy allowed placement of on-demand tasks on same node due to aggressive burst allowance.
- Autoscaler logs: predictive policy mis-specified affinity thresholds caused burst placements to favor shared nodes rather than cold-start new reserved nodes.

Hypotheses to validate:
- Lowering on-node preemption frequency (stronger isolation) will reduce p99.
- Tuning prefetch eviction policy to be more conservative on reserved pool will reduce rebuild cost.
- Autoscaler policy change: prefer new node allocation for burst if reserved-workers would be preempted.

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Disabled burst-placement-to-shared for BrightDocs (immediate reduction in p99 within 3 minutes).
- Applied a conservative eviction window (increasing retention) for reserved pool; observed reduced KV reload counts.

Remaining unknowns:
- Exact kernel-level threshold where eviction cost dominates vs. capacity tradeoffs for cold-start vs. preemption.
- Potential impact on overall cluster utilization if we restrict burst placements.
Support (Asha Patel) 2026-02-20T14:05: Customer reported that enabling a smaller concurrent limit temporarily reduces errors but latency still spikes intermittently.
SRE (Miguel Torres) 2026-02-20T15:10: We reproduced a similar pattern in staging with a mixed A10/A100 pool; attaching kernel logs to the ticket. Preemption correlates with eviction churn.
Engineer (Riley Chen) 2026-02-21T09:34: Rolled a conservative eviction config to reserved-pools in staging (flag: reserve.eviction_window=extended). Need to monitor 24h results before prod change.
Customer (BrightDocs contact - Lina Gomez) 2026-02-21T12:00: Thank you — we saw improvement after you disabled burst-to-shared. Can you quantify the expected latency SLO restoration and any cost implications?
Workaround implemented: disabled burst placement to shared nodes for BrightDocs' reserved pool and applied a conservative eviction window for reserved workers. Short-term results: p95 reduced by ~38% and p99 by ~54% for observed bursts.

Planned permanent actions:
- Implement autoscaler rule change to prefer new node allocation over preempting reserved workers when predicted burst would cause >20% eviction churn. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423)
- Add telemetry to detect preemption-induced eviction storms and auto-disable burst placement for affected pools until warmup completes.
- Follow-up runbook and SLO communication to customer, including expected recovery times and operational tradeoffs.

Follow-ups/owner:
- Riley Chen to drive PR and rollout (ETA 2026-03-02).
- SRE Miguel Torres to add observability alert for eviction-churn -> preemption correlation (ETA 2026-02-28).

Issue summary:
Nimbus Health began seeing increased latency for the first chat response and occasional completion timeouts after we rolled runtime 1.6 and a new quantized model variant (rwd-v2-small-quant) to production in us-east-1. Impact: intermittent UX degradation for chat product (initial spinner > 5s, sporadic 504s at the client).

Impact:
- ~20% of user chat sessions experience initial response > 3s, 5% > 8s during peak window (13:00-14:00 UTC).
- Several customer requests resulted in HTTP 504 from edge after 60s (timeout path) — reported by customer and corroborated in our API gateway logs.

Environment:
- Runtime: 1.6.0 (rolled 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC)
- Model: rwd-v2-small-quant pinned by rollout policy for tiered routing
- Region: prod-us-east (primary cluster)
1) Customer issues chat completions against /v1/chat with model=rwd-v2-small-quant. 2) Start a fresh chat session with a 3-10 sentence prompt with 1k token budget. 3) Observe initial response latency and occasional timeout after ~60s. 4) Repeating the same request within a warmed session reduces latency. 5) Incidence higher for new sessions and when traffic shifts to a new router lane after model routing changes.
- API Gateway traces: repeated upstream 504s at 13:18:42Z for connection pool entry timeout.
- Serving runtime logs: container start time for affected pods shows up to 900ms cold-start time plus 200-400ms additional stall at first generate call.
- Scheduler metrics: queue_depth spikes at 95th percentile coincident with rollout batch windows.
- KV-cache metrics: miss_rate increased from 3% baseline to 41% in the affected window for rwd-v2-small-quant prefix keys.
- Kernel selection: audit logs show fallback to reference_attention for ~12% of initial requests due to mis-detected attention pattern in compiled kernel selector.
- No elevated GPU utilization or OOMs observed.
Initial hypotheses:
- (A) Prefix/KV cache invalidation on model swap causing first-request work to rebuild cache and stall first token. Evidence: high KV cache miss rate and faster latencies for warmed sessions.
- (B) Kernel selector fallback path triggered for certain batching shapes leading to slower reference implementation for first chunk. Evidence: kernel audit entries show reference_attention fallback for initial requests.
- (C) Routing/scheduler burst behavior or container prewarm policy not firing resulting in brief queueing at canary/beta lanes. Evidence: queue_depth spikes around rollout times and increased cold starts logged.

What we ran so far:
- Correlated API gateway traces with pod logs and discovered the 504s align with higher miss_rate for KV cache and a small population of containers reporting the reference kernel fallback.
- Reproduced locally by running rwd-v2-small-quant with an empty KV cache; observed ~600-1200ms extra latency on initial generate compared to warmed run.
- Temporary traffic steering: manually moved ~30% of Nimbus traffic to runtime 1.5 in us-east for mitigation; observed immediate drop in >3s initial responses for that cohort.
- Enabled additional prewarm for new pods in us-east cluster; saw reduced cold-start incidence but residual kernel fallback stalls remain.

Next steps:
- Engineering to patch kernel selector to avoid spurious fallback for quantized variant (PR linked).
- Add targeted prewarming of KV cache keys for pinned models during rollout windows.
- Tighten autoscaling and scheduler prewarm policy for canary lanes during rollouts.
- Notify Nimbus with recommended temporary pin to runtime=1.5 or add header X-RW-Warm: true to force warmed path in their integration as a workaround.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 16:20 UTC - Customer (Nimbus Health): Confirmed reduced errors after steering; asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether pinning to runtime 1.5 is safe.
Workaround implemented: steering customer traffic to runtime 1.5 reduced incidents. Recommended customer pin to runtime=1.5 or add X-RW-Warm header for immediate relief.
Permanent fix: runtime kernel selector patch merged (PR #2431) to correct quantized attention detection; scheduled canary rollout 2026-03-15 with KV cache warmup job during rollout windows.
Follow-up: create runbook for model rollout warmup (task INT-430) and add automated prewarm in the deployment pipeline. Customer notified and SRE to monitor next 48h post patch.
- Verify KV cache miss_rate returns to baseline after warmup job.
- Confirm 95th percentile initial response latency decrease for pinned customers.
- Update runbook and include a checklist for rolling quantized models.
- Postmortem to be created if patch does not fully resolve within 72 hours.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers using NimbleDocs dedicated pool observed recurring 10-30% throughput drops and p99 latency spikes that coincide with short (30s-3m) 'pulse' events every ~12 minutes. Impact: customer-facing inference calls see increased queuing and occasional 5xx throttles as allocator reports 'no free slot'.

Impact:
- Throughput drop: steady ~15% lower token/sec for routes pinned to dedicated pool during pulses.
- Increased p99 from 180ms -> 900ms for small-stream chat-like requests.
- Several requests returned 503/504 during worst pulses.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (NimbleDocs reserved), region: us-east (prod).
- Models affected: gpt-open-13b for generation routes; redwood-emb-1 for embeddings.

Steps to reproduce / observed pattern:
1) Normal traffic: mix of long and short streams, baseline autoscaler target=6 GPUs.
2) Every ~12 minutes we see a short burst (30s-3m) of ephemeral sidecar connections from the customer's analytics sidecar: high-rate logging/metrics flushes (gRPC) to our collector.
3) Sidecar burst produces many short TCP connections and a flurry of sidecar logs which increases sidecar CPU and causes sporadic socket churn.
4) Autoscaler telemetry aggregator drops some heartbeat samples (aggregation window misreads), causing predictive shrink to decide an underutilization window and return 1 GPU in the next allocation step.
5) Serving runtime receives fewer slots; prefetched KV-cache entries get evicted; background prefetchers hold short leases; the combination yields transient GPU memory pressure and slot unavailability that increases queuing and triggers fallbacks.

Logs / snapshots (sanitized):
- allocator: "WARN alloc: free_slots=2 -> 0; attach_attempts=24; reason=prefetch_lock"
- autoscaler: "INFO window=60s utilization=0.34 predicted_scale_down=true"
- sidecar: "ERROR flush: conn_short_lived=2987 rate=8k/s"

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced at reduced scale by replaying customer traffic with an additional synthetic log-flusher that mimics their analytics sidecar. The same ~12m pulse triggers autoscaler to downscale by 1 GPU within the prediction window.
- Prefetch / kv-cache growth: eviction traces show eviction storms immediately after the shrink decision; memory pressure correlates with the timing of the pulse.
- SRE hypothesis: autoscaler sampling window and sidecar-induced socket churn are causing the aggregate utilization estimate to bias low for the short window, triggering premature shrink.
- Secondary hypothesis: sidecar bursts are increasing host-side interrupt/IO wait leading to transient NVLink/PCIe latency increases, aggravating slot attach latency.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Temporarily disabled predictive shrink (force-min cap) for NimbleDocs pool at 2026-03-13T22:05Z. Early telemetry shows pulses no longer produce allocation shrink; throughput stabilized back to baseline.

Next steps / remediation plan:
1) Engineering (autoscaler) to introduce short-window anomaly damping so a single short drop does not trigger predictive shrink (PR in progress: autoscaler#842). ETA 48 hours for canary.
2) Sidecar team to add rate-limiter/backpressure on high-frequency flushes and hard caps on short-lived connections (PR sidecar#197). ETA 72 hours.
3) Add additional telemetry to autoscaler: sample-counts, socket-churn metric feed, and mark samples from sidecar-origin connections to avoid being included in utilization calculation.
4) Long term: autoscaler policy to weight sustained trends over minute-scale spikes; also explore reserving 1 slot (soft) during known maintenance windows.

Customer comms:
- Initial notification sent to NimbleDocs: 2026-03-13 22:15Z (support). Provided mitigation and requested their sidecar to throttle flush frequency.

Attachments / dashboards referenced:
- Grafana panel: /d/dedicated/throughput-vs-attach-latency
- Logs: /logs/prod/us-east/pool-nd-774002/ (sanitized)
payload.summary: Intermittent throughput collapse in dedicated pool tied to ephemeral sidecar log storm and autoscaler shrink

Issue summary: Customers report intermittent 403s for admin and batch requests after migrating a large set of delegated roles through an IdP assertion broker. Impact: Customer's scheduled inference batch jobs and a small subset of admin console operations are failing authorization checks (403) despite the identity header being present upstream. This happens only for tenants with very large role lists (hundreds of role bindings) that produce a long 'X-Delegated-Roles' header (base64-encoded JSON). Environment: Private on-prem installation behind Pinebrook's corporate WAF and edge appliance. Private control plane in customer VPC; Redwood's ingress is behind the customer's perimeter WAF. Timeline: Started 2026-03-09 after Pinebrook deployed a synced role export that consolidated service roles into a single assertion header.

Observed behavior: Requests arrive at Redwood but RBAC middleware logs parse errors and returns 403. When the encoded header size exceeds ~8KB, the customer's WAF splits/strips header fragments instead of forwarding intact, which results in truncated JSON after base64 decode and an authz parse failure.

1) Configure IdP trust broker to emit aggregated roles into a single 'X-Delegated-Roles' header as base64(JSON) with ~250 role entries.
2) Send an authenticated admin API request or a batch inference request through customer's WAF to private Redwood ingress.
3) Observe 403 response from Redwood authz middleware for some requests; other requests succeed when header size is below the threshold.
4) Capture request on customer edge and on Redwood ingress to compare header payloads (pre- and post-WAF).
2026-03-09T14:03:21Z authz: error parsing delegated roles header 'X-Delegated-Roles': unexpected end of JSON at byte 8190
2026-03-09T14:03:21Z http: request from 10.12.54.21 method=POST path=/v1/infer status=403 duration_ms=21 user=svc-batch-pb tenant=pinebrook
2026-03-09T14:03:22Z ingress-proxy: header 'X-Delegated-Roles' size=8204 (raw), forwarded-fragments=2 (waf-chunked)
Initial triage by Support found consistent correlation between header size and failures. Packet captures from customer show the WAF rewriting large headers into multiple header lines without proper reassembly. Base64 decode on the reassembled header fails because fragments are being dropped or clipped at 8KB boundaries. Reproduced locally by injecting an 8.5KB header through a reverse-proxy configured to chunk headers — reproduced authz parse error 'unexpected end of JSON'. Hypothesis: customer's WAF enforces an 8KB per-header limit and uses header chunking that our ingress does not reassemble. Alternative cause considered: our ingress trimming or internal buffer, but local tests with intact headers show success. We engaged SRE for ingress config review; no recent changes on Redwood ingress that would truncate headers. Customer has Palo Alto PA-7000 with default header-size limits and an HAProxy-based edge doing header folding.
2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Ravi Patel): Customer reported ~15% of scheduled batch jobs failing with 403 since 03/09 morning. They attached example request ids and packet captures. Added to triage.
2026-03-10 11:47 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Confirmed parse error string in our logs for the supplied request IDs. Reproduced local failure with artificially chunked header. No ingress-side recent deploys that would explain change.
2026-03-10 15:30 - Customer (Lara Kim, Pinebrook): We upgraded IdP exporter to include consolidated service roles yesterday. We can temporarily disable consolidation if that helps.
2026-03-11 08:05 - Support (Ava Thompson): Suggested two immediate workarounds: 1) reduce header size by splitting roles across two headers (X-Delegated-Roles-1/2) or 2) switch to token introspection endpoint so roles are fetched server-side. Pinebrook prefers an ingress/WAF fix.
2026-03-11 14:22 - Customer (Lara Kim): Palo Alto support confirmed header-size enforcement and recommended increasing 'application-header-max-size' on their appliance. They will schedule a config change during a maintenance window.
2026-03-12 09:55 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Implemented a defensive server-side reassembly attempt for chunked headers (edge-case handling) in staging to tolerate common WAF chunking patterns. Still planning additional tests before prod rollout.
2026-03-12 13:01 - Support (Ava Thompson): Updated ticket with temporary mitigation guidance and tracked related internal follow-up INT-45290 for ingress enhancement.

Workaround applied and change planned: Pinebrook will increase their WAF/application header size limit to allow unchunked 'X-Delegated-Roles' headers (maintenance window completed 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC). Support worked with SRE to deploy a defensive reassembly patch to intake service in staging to handle simple chunked headers; patch will be promoted to prod after validation (planned 2026-03-15). Final fix options: 1) recommend customers avoid extremely large single headers and instead use token introspection or split role assertions across multiple well-known headers; 2) ingress-level reassembly and improved parsing tolerant to header chunking patterns — tracked as INT-45290. Postmortem action items: update private-deploy runbook to include WAF header-size guidance, add a validation check during onboarding that flags very large delegation assertions, and add Confluence doc with recommended patterns. Ticket will be closed after prod patch deploy and customer confirms successful job runs.
payload.summary: Delegated roles header truncated by corporate WAF chunking causes RBAC parse failures in private on-prem deployment

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent TLS handshake failures from model-serving pods after migrating fronting NLB to 'preserve client IP' with PROXY protocol enabled. Impact: model artifact pulls and live streaming sessions fail with TLS errors causing request 5xxs and retries. Scope: affects a fraction (~10-15%) of serving pods behind the internal NLB; appears after the customer's recent network change to enable proxy-protocol on the NLB.
1) Customer enabled PROXY protocol v1 on internal NLB and preserved client IP option in NLB config
2) Deploy a model-serving pod behind the NLB that expects TLS from the client (no PROXY handling)
3) Initiate a model artifact fetch or start a streaming generation request via the private endpoint
4) Observe TLS handshake failures and 5xxs on a subset of requests; some connections succeed depending on pod placement and LB path.
serving-pod stderr: 'tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake'
NLB flow logs: 'target:10.10.12.58:443, client:203.0.113.45:52344, action: forward, proxy_protocol: enabled'
agent network capture (pod): 'TCP payload begins with 'PROXY TCP4 203.0.113.45 10.10.12.58 52344 443\r\n' followed by TLS ClientHello'
SDK error on client: 'rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed before full handshake'
2026-03-10 09:22 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Customer opened ticket after enabling 'preserve client IP' on internal NLB during an internal migration. They report 5-10% of model pulls fail with TLS handshake errors. Asked for recent load-balancer config and pod logs.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Customer (SafeSend network admin): Confirmed NLB was toggled to enable PROXY protocol v1; sent NLB config snippet and flow logs. Provided pod logs showing 'first record does not look like TLS handshake'.
2026-03-10 13:40 - Eng (Marco Chen): Reproduced locally by injecting PROXY v1 header in front of our serving binary; observed identical 'first record does not look like a TLS handshake' from Go tls library. Hypothesis: serving process isn't expecting PROXY headers and fails TLS parsing.
2026-03-11 08:12 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Suggested two immediate workarounds: A) disable PROXY protocol on the NLB, or B) enable PROXY protocol handling on the serving side via the sidecar/nginx that can consume proxy headers and pass TLS through to the application. Asked customer to test disabling PROXY protocol for a subset of targets.
2026-03-11 10:00 - Customer: Disabled PROXY protocol on the NLB for one target group. Error rate dropped to baseline within 15 minutes. Customer rolled back the NLB change across all target groups and reported service recovered.
Confirmed root cause: internal NLB configured to insert PROXY protocol headers. Our serving processes accept raw TLS on port 443 and do not inspect/strip PROXY headers, so the PROXY header bytes are interpreted as the start of the TLS record, causing the Go TLS stack to reject the handshake.
Repro steps validated: injecting PROXY v1 line before ClientHello triggers the same error locally.
We observed partial impact because the customer's deployment uses mixed target groups and some targets had the NLB change applied while others did not; this explains intermittent failure rate.
Immediate resolution: Customer disabled PROXY protocol on internal NLB and service recovered. Long-term options: 1) If customer needs to preserve client IP, configure the serving ingress to accept PROXY protocol (add a PROXY-aware TLS terminator such as HAProxy/nginx with 'proxy_protocol' enabled or update our edge sidecar to parse PROXY v1), or 2) use a TCP-level load balancer mode that preserves client IP without inserting PROXY headers where possible. Follow-up task created to document PROXY protocol behavior for Private deployments.
payload.summary: Internal NLB inserting PROXY protocol header breaks TLS handshake to serving instances in private deployment

Issue summary:
Customer (NordicHealth Analytics, enterprise) is preparing for an external compliance audit and requested a cryptographically verifiable, read-only snapshot of audit logs covering a specified date range (2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28). The snapshot must include:
  - An immutable manifest listing exported files, checksums (SHA-256), and object sizes
  - A timestamped HSM signature over the manifest (we can provide a Redwood HSM-signed attestation plus optional customer-provided ephemeral signing key)
  - A chain-of-custody audit trail showing who initiated the export, S3 object write timestamps, and KMS key versions used
  - Delivery method: SFTP with pre-shared upload location and accompanied by a signed manifest and verification instructions

Impact:
  - Customer audit window is fixed; evidence required by external auditor on 2026-03-20. Failure to deliver verifiable artifacts could delay their certification and impact contract renewal discussions.

Customer's specific ask:
  1) Produce a frozen snapshot export for 2026-02-01..2026-02-28 containing API audit events and auth/audit metadata (user ids, API keys masked except key ids, route, model_version, request/response hashes)
  2) Generate manifest.jsonl containing file list and SHA-256 checksums and sizes
  3) Sign manifest with Redwood HSM with RFC3161-style timestamping and provide signature bundle and verification steps
  4) Provide chain-of-custody log (who requested export, SRE operator, job run ids, S3 put object timestamps, KMS key versions)
  5) Deliver via customer-provided SFTP endpoint and provide MD5/SHA-256 verification instructions

Environment:
  - Tenant: nordichealth-prod
  - Region: us-east-1
  - Services: Redwood API (hosted), Audit export worker, KMS-backed envelope encryption, Object storage (S3), HSM signing service

Steps to produce snapshot (requested by customer):
  1. Authorize export request via console or support ticket (customer has completed SOC approval and provided an export approval token)
  2. Run export job scoped to date range and tenant
  3. Persist ndjson files to a locked S3 bucket with object lock enabled (governance mode)
  4. Generate manifest with SHA-256 checksums and sizes, then sign manifest using HSM with RFC3161 timestamping
  5. Push files to customer SFTP with integrity verification headers and provide signed manifest and verification steps

Logs / Evidence attached to ticket (links):
  - Audit job run id: export-20260310-8092 (internal job log available)
  - S3 bucket: redwood-exports-us-east-locked/nordichealth/2026-02-frozen (S3 console runbook link provided below)

Notes / Constraints / Risk:
  - Some audit events contain PII. Customer requested pseudonymization for user display names but retention of consistent hashed identifiers to allow auditor correlation. We must confirm allowed pseudonymization approach and record mapping process.
  - HSM signing requires approvals from Security SRE; the HSM signing process leaves an auditable key usage record but cannot reveal key material. Customer asked for signed attestation and logs of HSM key version used.
  - Object Lock governance requires account-level setup; export job will attempt to enable governance mode objects but we must confirm bucket configuration and cross-account delivery to SFTP (not direct cross-account S3 copy).

Deliverables the customer expects:
  - SFTP drop with ndjson logs, manifest.jsonl (SHA-256, sizes), manifest.sig (HSM signature in CMS format), rfc3161.timestamp.tsr file, and chain_of_custody.txt (human-readable runbook of who/when/what)
  - Verification steps document with example openssl commands to validate signature and checksums

Support action items recommended:
  - (Support) Validate customer SFTP thumbprint and perform a dry-run with a sanitized 24-hour sample export by 2026-03-12
  - (SRE) Coordinate HSM signing window and approve RFC3161 timestamping; provide key version and key usage logs by 2026-03-13
  - (Security) Approve pseudonymization approach and provide required attestations for auditors
  - (Delivery) Execute final frozen export and SFTP delivery by 2026-03-18 to meet auditor deadline

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 16:40 - SRE (Marco Diaz): Need Security sign-off for pseudonymization mapping. HSM signing window available 2026-03-13 02:00-05:00 UTC; will reserve and document key id (hsm-key-17).
2026-03-12 08:05 - Security (Aisha Khan): Pseudonymization approach approved: SHA-256(salt + userid) with salt stored in customer-scoped sealed artifact. Security requests auditor disclosure language to be added to manifest.
2026-03-12 14:50 - Customer (NordicHealth): Confirmed sample looks good; asking for chain_of_custody to include operator email and IP addresses. Requested explicit KMS key version in manifest.
Awaiting final export run and customer confirmation of delivered artifacts; HSM signature and chain-of-custody to be attached upon completion.

Issue summary: Customer reported intermittent tail-latency spikes after enabling a deferred optimizer profile that adjusts batching thresholds and KV prefetch heuristics. The rollout targeted a subset of tenants on Dedicated capacity and used the 'defer-eager' gating flag.

Impact: Multiple production tenants experienced 95/99th percentile latency increases (2-5x) on interactive chat endpoints. No increased 5xx rate observed, but user-facing latency violated P99 SLO for affected tenants. Customer is on Dedicated plan and requested immediate guidance for a safe rewind.

Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east, mixed-quant profiles enabled per-tenant. Deploy timestamp: 2026-03-10 22:15 UTC. Snapshot label available: pre-opt-2026-03-10.

Observed behavior: Tail latency spikes concentrated on sessions that use long-context generation and streaming. Initial hypothesis from customer: KV cache invalidation races combined with a lower batching threshold introduced by the optimizer. Router shows traffic split (10% canary -> 90% baseline) but spikes persisted past canary window.

Request: Support asked to validate safe rollback steps, confirm snapshot restore procedure for tenant-scoped optimizer profiles, and provide a checklist to avoid request loss during rewind.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Use tenant TID-00923 with model llama-3-13b-v1.2 pinned.
2) Send multi-turn chat sequences with prefix length ~2k tokens.
3) Observe P99 token-latency after enabling optimizer profile 'defer-eager-v3'.

Logs/metrics provided: Link to customer dashboard and traces (redwood://dash/tenant/TID-00923/trace/2026-03-11), example request IDs: req-7a4f2c, req-9b0d1e. Attached CSV of percentile samples (uploaded to ticket).

Additional notes:
Telemetry sampling: observed 3x increase in KV cache miss rate for affected tenant during canary traffic windows (samples from 2026-03-10 22:20 -> 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC).
Batching thresholds: optimizer set 'min_batch_size' lowered from 8 -> 3 for low-latency preference; led to higher small-batch overhead and more concurrent kernel invocations under mixed-tenant load.
KV invalidation: race observed when prefix-cache eviction policy ran concurrently with async prefetch; trace req-7a4f2c shows double fetch path causing 2x token latency for first streamed chunks.
Router: traffic gating was applied but the canary's failure domain overlapped with a GPU node group experiencing noisy-neighbor due to unrelated maintenance; increased variance amplified the optimizer effect.
Working resolution plan prepared; not yet executed. Recommended safe rewind steps provided to customer and engineering ops: 1) Pause optimizer flag 'defer-eager-v3' for affected tenant via tenant-config API (non-disruptive). 2) Trigger tenant-scoped snapshot restore to label 'pre-opt-2026-03-10' for optimizer profiles only (no model re-pull). 3) Increase telemetry sampling to 100% for 30 minutes post-rewind and monitor P95/P99. 4) If latency remains high, execute controlled node drain for canary GPU group to rule out noisy-neighbor. Additional follow-ups: implement automatic preflight that simulates KV miss amplification for future optimizer gates.
Create runbook entry for 'deferred-optimizer-safe-rewind' (owner: Marco Reyes)
Add preflight simulation to CI for optimizer changes (owner: Research/Applied ML)
Schedule post-incident review with ClearBridge Health (CS lead: Priya Patel)
Monitor affected tenant for 72 hours after rewind and report metrics to customer

Customer reports sudden 429 throttling across multiple webhook callback routes after onboarding a new service account used by their ingest pipeline. - Business impact: delayed index availability for dashboards; customer reported SLA breach threat for nightly reports.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod-us-west), Dedicated ingestion pool disabled for this tenant (using hosted tier).
- Integration uses a single service account with automated signed-url refresh cadence triggered by multiple worker processes (server-to-server).

Observed behaviour / Symptoms:
1) High rate of 429 responses returned to customer webhook callers; headers include x-rw-rate-limit and x-rw-retry-after but values differ between otherwise-identical requests.
2) Requests mapped to different route subpaths (e.g., /v1/callbacks/ingest/stepA and /v1/callbacks/ingest/stepB) all show token-bucket exhaustion despite tenant-level quota remaining.
3) Traces show a flurry of concurrent auth refresh exchanges (service account signed-url rotation) aligned with the start of the backfill.

Steps to reproduce (customer repro):
1) Create a service account and configure signed-url refresh endpoint in the SDK sample.
2) Spawn 150 short-lived worker processes that all refresh signed URLs and immediately POST callback events to multiple subpaths in parallel (50 workers per subpath).
3) Observe 429s on many POSTs within 1–3s of concurrent refreshes; headers show per-route bucket claims failing even when tenant tokens available.

Logs / snippets provided by customer:
- Ingress logs show many requests with header: Authorization: Bearer svc-acct-rot-x
- Rate limiter trace excerpt: "route=/v1/callbacks/ingest/stepA tokens_claimed=6 tokens_left_route_bucket=0 tenant_tokens_left=214"
- Example response header that confused caller: x-rw-rate-limit: 60/60 window; x-rw-remaining: 0; x-rw-tenant-remaining: 214

Temporary mitigation provided to customer:
- Asked customer to stagger signed-url refreshes using jitter in their SDK and to reduce concurrency in backfill to 20 workers per subpath. That reduced 429s to <1% but is not an acceptable long-term workaround for their scale.

Requested outcome from Support/Eng:
- Confirm root cause and patch ingestion of signed-url refresh/healthcheck paths so they do not increment route-specific buckets incorrectly.
- Provide guidance for recommended signing/refresh cadence and SDK changes to avoid fanout during large backfills.

Additional notes:
- Customer attached a pcap-like sample and timestamps. They are requesting a targeted config change or a short hotfix before the next scheduled backfill tonight.
Timeline:
- 2026-03-10 01:00 UTC: Ticket created by Support after initial customer message.
- 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC: SRE instrumented traces on api-gateway, enabled verbose rate-limiter logging for the tenant.
- 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC: Reproduced locally using customer's reproduction script (150 workers, parallel refresh).

Hypothesis (initial):
- Signed-url refresh requests from the service account were being attributed to the origin route instead of a dedicated auth route due to path normalization mismatch in the ingress-proxy. When multiple processes refresh simultaneously, the rate-limiter records rapid per-route token claims and temporarily exhausts route buckets even though tenant-level tokens remain.

Evidence gathered so far:
- Trace correlation shows that signed-url refresh and subsequent POSTs share the same ephemeral connection metadata and are being classed into the same route bucket.
- Ingress-proxy code path uses a route-hash derived from normalized path; the normalization strip routine drops a per-route suffix ("/ingest/stepA") for auth refresh calls when the signed URL includes a query token, so both refresh and POST map to the same canonical route key.
- Local repro matched customer symptom; enabling a warehousing config flag in ingress-proxy (route_tagging_v2=false -> true) restored separation but flag was experimental and has side-effects.

Risk assessment:
- Medium-high: affects hosted tenants using service accounts; potential for repeated incidents on scheduled bulk operations. Fix likely requires ingress-proxy change and a minor SDK recommendation (stagger/jitter).

Proposed short-term fix:
1) Reconfigure tenant's ingress routing to force signed-url refresh endpoint to use dedicated route label (manual override) — tested in staging and reduced per-route claims.
2) Add server-side debounce for auth refresh path: do not count auth-only refresh requests against per-route quotas for 60s after a refresh detected from the same svc-acct.

Proposed long-term fix:
- Patch ingress-proxy normalization so query-token carrying refresh endpoints preserve route suffix or use explicit route label for auth flows. Submit PR and rollout with canary.

Follow-ups required:
- Engineering to implement PR and coordinate canary in prod-us-west.
- SDK team to publish guidance and implement default jitter in the refresh helper.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 02:15 - Customer (S. Nguyen, Nimbus): Uploaded repro script and timestamped logs. Reported next backfill scheduled 2026-03-11 23:30 PDT.
Workaround/hotfix applied: manual route override for Nimbus (did not require tenant downtime). Customer advised to patch SDK to add jitter and to keep concurrent workers <= 25 per subpath for nightly backfills until full rollout.
Next steps assigned:
- Jordan Lee: complete PR review and schedule canary (target: 2026-03-15 canary in prod-us-west).
- SDK team (owner: Maya Chen): ship jitter default in next minor release and add doc section for signed-url refresh best practices.
- Support: follow up with Nimbus after canary and confirm metrics remain stable for two backfills.
Follow-up tags: hotfix-applied, engineering-needed, sdk-action

Root cause: ingress path normalization misattributed auth refreshes to route-specific buckets in prod-us-west. Hotfix (manual routing override) applied; engineering PR submitted to fix normalization and avoid future double-counting.
We appreciate the quick workaround. Please prioritize the ingress-proxy normalization fix — monthly backfills at scale are core to our product. We will accept staged downtime during a low-traffic window if necessary.

Issue summary: Customer scheduled CSV report that includes embedded dashboard tracehook parameters (used for drilldowns into traces) is producing CSV rows where the tracehook field is split into multiple columns when the tracehook parameter contains a comma. This causes downstream workflows and emailed CSVs to show truncated trace links, breaking alert context linking and investigator workflows. Problem was reported after a retention compaction run earlier this week.

Impact: For FinSight (Enterprise tenant), scheduled daily CSVs from dashboards that include tracehook-anchored filters are missing valid trace links in approx. 12% of rows for ranges spanning retention-prune windows. This prevents their on-call and audit teams from following alerts back to traces. No customer data exposure; primarily usability and observability loss.

Scope: Reproducible for scheduled exports only (ad-hoc UI/Download appears correct). Seems triggered when export pipeline pulls compacted index snapshots and passes tracehook through legacy CSV sanitizer that treats commas as separators even when field is quoted.
Customer config: scheduled CSV snapshot of dashboard with variable 'tracehook' configured as a URL param containing commas (example: 'traceId=abc,context=prod').
Set scheduled report to daily and run once crossing a retention compaction window (we reproduced in prod after retention job at 2026-03-09T03:00Z).
Observe scheduled emailed CSV and S3 object: the tracehook column is split into two columns; resulting link is broken and trace id is only partially present.
Ad-hoc: Export same dashboard manually from UI -> Download CSV immediately; compare: manual CSV quotes the tracehook field correctly and link resolves.
2026-03-09T03:01:12Z export-service.INFO scheduled-export job=SUP-404422 tenant=finsight key=report-892 path=/exports/rep-892.csv sanitizer=legacy-csv version=1.3.2 shard=compact-2026-03-09
2026-03-09T03:01:12Z export-service.WARN sanitizer: unquoted_field_detected field=tracehook value="traceId=abc,context=prod" action=split_applied
2026-03-09T03:01:12Z notify.INFO email=reports+finsight@customer.delivery report=rep-892 size=42KB rows=480 tracehook_splits=58
Initial hypothesis: CSV sanitizer regression in legacy path used by scheduled exports when reading compacted snapshots; ad-hoc path uses newer CSV writer that enforces quoting.
Reproduced in prod with a synthetic scheduled job for internal tenant with tracehook containing comma; confirmed split occurs only when export_service loads 'compact' snapshot index (retention-compacted shard).
Checked exporter code path: scheduled exports still route through export-service:legacy_writer when snapshot_type == 'compact' (recent change in retention job introduced snapshot metadata flag 'compact' on 2026-03-08).
Review of sanitizer: legacy_writer relies on CSV library v0.9 which is configured with delimiter=',' and escape/quoting is conditional based on 'is_wrapped' flag. Compact snapshots lost the 'is_wrapped' flag during compaction step, introduced by retention PR #483 (see linked PR).

Additional notes:
SRE-Team (note): Holding change until risk window; proposed hotfix: on export read path, if snapshot_type=='compact' and field contains comma, force-quote field before writing. Quick patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reports/pull/824
Customer (FinSight) via CS rep: 'We rely on scheduled CSVs for nightly triage — any ETA?'. Mariana responded: 'Working on a hotfix for scheduled exports; will ship toggle to force-quote for affected tenants within 24 hours.'
Workaround: Enabled per-tenant toggle to force-quote all fields on scheduled export pipeline for FinSight (feature_flag=force_quote_exports for tenant finsight). This prevented further broken CSVs while a code fix is reviewed.
Permanent fix: PR #824 modifies export-service legacy_writer to treat compact snapshots as having 'is_wrapped'=true at read-time and upgrades sanitized-csv to explicit quoting-in-all-cases mode. Deployed to canary on 2026-03-13 and rolled to prod on 2026-03-14 02:30Z.
Post-deploy validation: re-ran customer's scheduled report for 2026-03-14; CSV attached by CS to customer; tracehook column intact and links resolve. Monitoring: export-service.alerts.csv-field-splits rate dropped to 0 in last 24h.
Follow-ups: 1) Add unit/integration test covering comma-containing tracehook fields across snapshot types. 2) Update retention compaction job to preserve 'is_wrapped' marker or annotate resulting snapshot explicitly. 3) Add telemetry to scheduled export path to detect future sanitizer regressions. Assigned INT-2123 for follow-up engineering work.

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a high-throughput marketing push, Emerald Commerce observed a multi-region degradation in multiplexed streaming where long-lived multiplexed sessions entered a silent state for several seconds, then replayed/duplicated completions when the stream resumed. Impact: duplicate completions led to increased per-token billing (customer-visible invoice exposure) and inconsistent application behavior for checkout flows. Environment: production (us-east-1) using multiplexed streaming over HTTP/2 to redwood-open-13B-quant-v2 pinned model. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create multiplexed session with 200 concurrent client streams. 2) Send a range of short prompt batches with intermittent small payload delays. 3) Observe transient stream silence ~2-6s followed by repeated completion frames. Observed logs: streaming-reset followed by completion-replay traces, per-request UUIDs repeated in audit logs, and billing meter reporting tokens counted twice for affected request IDs.
2026-03-06 01:12 UTC - Emerald Commerce reported higher-than-normal invoice for peak window and intermittent checkout errors (SUP inbound).
2026-03-06 01:30 UTC - Support triaged as P0; engaged SRE and Billing. First response to customer acknowledged impact and requested traces.
2026-03-06 02:05 UTC - Initial hypothesis: client-side retries + server-side replay due to idle connection reattachment. SRE collected multiplex logs and proxy traces.
2026-03-06 03:10 UTC - Identified pattern: upstream streaming proxy emitted a keepalive gap; runtime suppressed a retransmit flag and later re-sent completion frames without marking as duplicate.
2026-03-06 04:00 UTC - Temporary mitigation deployed: server-side dedup filter on request UUID + short token credit hold to avoid immediate double-billing; customer notified.
2026-03-06 10:30 UTC - Billing team applied a manual credit for the affected window and confirmed invoice adjustment; customer received confirmation.
2026-03-07 09:00 UTC - Permanent fix merged: ensure idempotency flags are preserved across proxy reconnects and add defensive duplicate-suppression in billing pipeline (PRs linked).
2026-03-14 15:00 UTC - Post-incident follow-up meeting completed; action items assigned and timeline published to customer.
2026-03-14 16:00 UTC - Ticket moved to Resolved after verification with Emerald Commerce that retries ceased and billing credit accepted.
Logs show repeated completion frames with identical request_uuid headers for multiplex participants; timestamps indicate a gap of 2-6s before duplication.
Proxy (edge-nginx-mlproxy) emitted a keepalive probe failure that caused connection rebind. Session rebind logic lacked propagation of idempotency metadata to new stream context.
Serving runtime did not mark retransmitted completions as duplicates because the idempotency token field was stored in ephemeral memory tied to the previous stream context.
Billing pipeline ingested both completion events before duplicate detection fired; dedup window too short for the observed gap.
Customer-side logs show no explicit client retries; behaviour is server-side replay rather than client-initiated retransmit in majority of traces.
Reproduced locally with a scripted connection-clobber at the proxy layer; confirmed duplicate completions when idempotency metadata is lost.
Support (2026-03-06 01:35 UTC) - @Ivy Martinez: Acknowledged issue to Emerald Commerce and requested request_ids + sample traces. Escalating to SRE and Billing.
SRE (2026-03-06 02:12 UTC) - @Samir Patel: Collecting multiplex proxy and runtime traces. Initial hypothesis: proxy rebind is stripping x-redwood-idempotency header.
Billing (2026-03-06 03:25 UTC) - @Maya Chen: Holding on automated invoice runs for affected account while we investigate; will prepare refund plan if confirmed.
Engineer (2026-03-06 08:47 UTC) - @Diego Alvarez: Patch submitted to preserve idempotency header through rebind and extend billing dedup window to 10s. See PR #4281 and billing PR #219.
Emerald Commerce (2026-03-06 11:15 UTC) - @Priya Rao (customer): Thanks for quick mitigation. Please confirm when billing credit is applied and what prevents recurrence.
Support (2026-03-06 12:05 UTC) - @Ivy Martinez: Manual credit applied for peak window; engineering will provide permanent fix timeline and postmortem.
SRE (2026-03-14 14:20 UTC) - @Samir Patel: Follow-up: increased unit tests, added e2e multiplex reconnect scenario to CI, and scheduled canary rollout for the patch across us-east-1 on 2026-03-16.
Emerald Commerce (2026-03-14 15:05 UTC) - @Priya Rao (customer): Confirmed no further duplicates in our smoke tests. Accepting post-incident report and credit.
Short-term mitigation: deployed server-side dedup filter for request_uuid and temporarily held duplicate token charges pending review.
Billing action: issued manual credit for the affected invoice window and prevented auto-invoice reconciliation for that account until fixes were validated.
Permanent fix: patched proxy rebind logic to carry x-redwood-idempotency through stream reconnects and extended billing dedup window to 10s; patches merged to main (PRs linked).
Deployment plan: canary rollout in us-east-1 on 2026-03-16 followed by gradual rollout to other regions; monitoring dashboards added for duplicate completions and mux keepalive gaps.
Verification: Emerald Commerce validated the fix in their acceptance tests; SRE observed no duplicate completions in 72-hour post-rollout sample.
Status: Resolved. Customer received credit and post-incident report; follow-up tasks remain for cross-region hardening.
ENG-1012 - Add end-to-end CI scenario that simulates proxy connection rebind during multiplexed sessions (owner: @Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-03-28)
OPS-914 - Update billing dedup rules and add an alert if duplicate-token rate > 0.1% over 10min window (owner: @Maya Chen, due: 2026-03-21)
SEC-432 - Review idempotency header lifecycle and ensure headers cannot be lost during TLS renegotiation or proxy failover (owner: @Lena Ortiz, due: 2026-04-04)
CS-219 - Email template and SLA addendum to notify enterprise customers about potential dedup exposure and available credits; coordinate with legal (owner: @Ivy Martinez, due: 2026-03-20)
Postmortem doc: write and publish runbook and timeline to Confluence and notify #support and #incidents channels (owner: @Samir Patel, due: 2026-03-18)

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated partial outputs and a truncated final sentence when resuming long streaming responses after a midstream reconnect. Behavior appears correlated with client reconnects that land on a different edge proxy instance and where the reconnect window overlaps an in-flight batched token flush.

Impact:
- NexusHealth production users intermittently receive responses that end mid-sentence or repeat a short prefix chunk after reconnects.
- Affects latency-sensitive UI flows that rely on complete closing paragraphs (medical-summarization UI).
- Repro rate reported ~2-4% of reconnects under NexusHealth traffic patterns (bursty mid-sized messages).

Environment:
- prod | us-east-1, customer on enterprise Dedicated plan (reserved capacity pool).
- Client: in-house browser app behind corporate proxy that forces frequent socket churn on network changes.
- Models in use: redwood-v1-large, fallback gptj-16k for some requests.

Steps to reproduce (provided by NexusHealth and verified in lab):
1. Start a long streaming generation (expected 800-1,200 tokens).
2. Simulate client path-migration: send TCP FIN then reconnect with same session token within ~200-800ms.
3. Ensure reconnection routes to different edge-proxy instance (load-balancer shuffles).
4. Observe resumed stream: sometimes the tail ends mid-sentence; in other cases a small prefix (10-25 tokens) is duplicated and the final punctuation and metadata chunk are missing.

Observed behavior:
- When reconnect occurs during a flush window the serving-runtime emits two batches with the same sequence-id namespace but different "batch-prefix" metadata. The downstream reconstructor (edge proxy + SDK glue) sometimes applies the newer batch-prefix but replays older token frames, producing duplicate small prefixes and a missing terminal end-event. Logs show sequence id collisions (seq=10255) followed by an EOM marker never received by the client.

Expected behavior:
- On reconnect, either resume cleanly without duplication and produce a definitive terminal event, or fallback to a fresh response with a clear reset and no partial duplication.

Logs / attachments:
- Customer provided capture: `proxy-conn-2026-03-04-14:12:53.log` (partial).
- Server side snippet (redacted):
  [2026-03-04T14:12:43Z] stream.emit seq=10254 batch-prefix=alpha flush
  [2026-03-04T14:12:43Z] stream.emit seq=10255 batch-prefix=alpha flush
  [2026-03-04T14:12:44Z] reconnect token=*** session=abcd123
  [2026-03-04T14:12:45Z] stream.emit seq=10255 batch-prefix=beta flush
  [2026-03-04T14:12:45Z] eom expected seq=10255 but not acked to client

Customer notes:
- Repro with NexusHealth network conditions using Chrome 112 + corp proxy.
- Business impact: summaries missing final care instructions for a small subset of users; flagged by QA as unacceptable for production clinical workflows.

Additional notes:
2026-03-05 14:22 UTC - NexusHealth Engineer (customer): Confirmed repro in their staging mirror. Provided additional packet capture showing proxy-level retransmit during reconnect.
Repro harness: lb-shuffle + curl-like streaming client reproduces partial truncation when reconnect latency between 150-800ms and load-balancer forwards new connection to different edge instance.
Server traces show same seq number (10255) emitted twice with different batch-prefix meta (alpha -> beta). Consumer reconstructor assumes batch-prefix monotonicity and applies last observed prefix but replays token frames from the other prefix resulting in duplicate small prefix and missing EOM metadata.
Edge-proxy code path: connection handoff does not guarantee in-flight flush idempotency. No cross-proxy coordination to pin flush sequence acknowledgement to session resume.
Customer workaround: reduce client reconnects (increase socket keepalive) and disable aggressive corporate proxy connection resets when possible. Server-side temporary mitigation: edge-proxy change to prefer authoritative in-flight-owner lookup for session tokens (controls resume only to the original instance if flush not confirmed). This is in staging and reduces repro to <0.1% in soak.
Triage in progress. Short-term mitigation deployed to staging (edge-proxy authoritative-attach). Longer-term fix under design by Serving runtime team: make flush/batch-prefix assignment deterministic and attachable across proxy handoffs or enforce session pinning until flush confirms. Postmortem and code PR to follow (tracking PR: github.com/redwood-infer/serving-runtime/pull/7421).
payload.summary: Sequence-ID collision and batched-prefix flip on midstream reconnect causes truncated concluding sentence

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightDocs reports intermittent rerank endpoint slowdowns and worse top-k ordering after a scheduled rollout of a quantized embedding variant. Impact: Production rerank latency increased from ~60ms median to 300–700ms for a subset of multilingual requests, and top-k quality degraded (different top1 in ~4% of queries). Environment: prod:us-west (BrightDocs customer, enterprise tier) using redwood-embed-large-v2 for embed generation and rerank-mono-1.3 for reranking. Timeframe: regression began ~2026-02-19 23:40 UTC immediately following a background rollout of embed-quantized-v2. Observed behavior: - Increased tail latency and occasional 504 timeouts from reranker service. - Rerank output ordering changes for multilingual inputs (notably Japanese and German) compared to pre-rollout baseline. - Errors are correlated with larger batch sizes and higher tokenization variance. Expected behavior: Stable latency distributions and consistent rerank ordering compared to baseline model/quantization profile.
1) Use BrightDocs test tenant with multilingual prompt set (EN/JA/DE). 2) Send embedding requests to the hosted embeddings API pinned to embed-quantized-v2 (as rolled out). 3) Immediately call /rerank endpoint with embeddings returned. 4) Repeat with batch sizes 1, 8, 32 and observe latency and top-k. 5) Repeat same input pinned to redwood-embed-large-v2 (non-quant) and compare ordering and timing. Expected: non-quant path shows baseline latency and stable top-k; quantized path shows latency spikes and top-k deviations in failing cases.
support_packet: customer request ids [bd-req-1021, bd-req-1042, bd-req-1075] attached. Example trace: 2026-02-19T23:42:12Z INFO embeddings-service req=bd-req-1021 model=embed-quantized-v2 batch=16 took=0.15s size=512 -> returned dim=768
2026-02-19T23:42:12Z WARN reranker req=bd-req-1021 model=rerank-mono-1.3 batch=16 kv-merge delayed: kv_cache_mismatch=true route=quant-path latency=0.62s
2026-02-19T23:42:12Z ERROR api-gateway req=bd-req-1021 downstream=reranker status=504 upstream_timeout=true
Relevant SLI graphs: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/embeds/embed-rollout?from=2026-02-19T22:00Z&to=2026-02-20T02:00Z
Initial hypothesis: quantized embedding variant introduced a rotational/packing alignment change for the vector layout (byte/word ordering) that interacts with reranker's batched distance computation, causing KV merge path to reserialize and fall back to slow path. Evidence: - Correlation between rollout window and spike in KV-cache-mismatch logs. - Failing cases show embeddings with expected dimension 768 but with anomalous low-entropy in trailing 64 dims for some languages. - When reranker receives embeddings with minor orientation shift, internal SIMD kernels choose fallback numeric path with per-item deserialization, doubling latency. Tests run: 1) Replayed failing requests against non-quant embed service -> baseline latency and ordering restored. 2) Manually re-encoded quant vectors with an extra byte-order normalization step before rerank -> latency restored but quality still slightly off. 3) Injected small perturbation (sign flip) into a copy of embeddings and observed similar ordering changes, indicating sensitivity to orientation in multilingual subspaces. Additional logs: linked internal trace: trace-id 7f3b2a67 (SRE)
Mitigation: Rolled back embed-quantized-v2 rollout for BrightDocs and any tenants still on auto-bump; reverted to redwood-embed-large-v2 for affected customers at 2026-02-20 02:10 UTC which restored baseline latency and ordering. Hotfix: Added input-vector schema checksum and dimensionality/orientation assertion in embeddings-service to detect nonconformant serialization and reject or normalize before proxying to reranker (hotfix PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings-service/pull/1987). Permanent fix plan: 1) Add unit/regression tests that exercise multilingual tokenization variance against quantized transforms. 2) Update reranker to tolerate minor orientation differences by inserting a fast normalization kernel and fallback thresholds. 3) Add rollout gating metrics (KV-cache-mismatch rate, tail latency delta by language) to the deployment pipeline. Follow-ups created below.

Additional notes:
2026-02-20 02:05 - BrightDocs (Customer): Provided consent to rollback for immediate mitigation. Reported that business-critical searches were degraded intermittently.
ENG-FT: add embed schema checksum to non-prod and prod pipelines (owner: embeddings team)
ENG-RT: add fast normalization kernel to reranker and run benchmarks across languages (owner: reranker team)
OPS: add KV-cache-mismatch and per-language tail latency to rollout gating dashboard
DOCS: update rollout runbook to include language-aware smoke tests for quantized variants
payload.summary: Rotational embed shift after quantized rollout causing rerank latency spike and quality drift
