Issue summary: Several customers (notably LumenHealth) report that historical dashboard panels (time ranges > 30 days) intermittently show zeroed or stale metric counts and their trace links are missing. The problem is transient: panels become correct again after ~10-30 minutes without user action. Impact: dashboards with SLA and usage rollups show incorrect historical values; alerting based on those rollups can under- or over-fire. This affects customer trust in console analytics and can mask billing/usage anomalies. Environment: production us-east region. Affected customers reported on enterprise tier; observed across multiple orgs.
1) Open Console -> Dashboards -> choose a dashboard with weekly/monthly rollups (time range > 30 days). 2) Observe counts for a low-cardinality metric (e.g., route_success_rate, total_tokens) and trace-link anchors. 3) Rapidly change time window back and forth (e.g., 90d -> 30d -> 90d) and refresh. 4) Some panels will render with zeroed or very old counts and trace-link buttons show 'No traces' instead of opening the trace view. 5) Wait 10-30 minutes; panels recover without manual cache clear. Repro is intermittent (~1 in 10 attempts during retention compaction windows).
console-frontend: panel-render: query=rollup_v2 start=2025-12-01 end=2026-03-01 shard=warm-compact read_mode=primary; retention-indexer: compaction job id=cmp-2026-03-12-08 warmup=true; indexer-lag: lag=18m; kv-cache: miss-rate spike to 78%. Trace-hook service logs show O(200) missing anchors during query window. No 5xx in api-gateway. No token auth errors. Relevant links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/retention/indexer-run-03-12, https://kibana.redwood.internal/app/discover#/logs?q=cmp-2026-03-12-08
Initial hypothesis: retention compaction warmup job is causing a temporary partition state where rollup queries hit compacted partitions that are in 'read-repair' mode; dashboard renderer treats empty result as zero and trace-hook anchor resolution returns empty. Confirmed with SRE that a compaction job ran with warmup=true and indexer lag spiked ~18 minutes. Queries during warmup hit a mix of old and compacted store replicas; read-repair and backfill to hot replicas happen asynchronously. Observed that the console frontend does not fallback to hot-replica read-path when primary returns empty for rollups, so panels show stale/zeroed values. Trace-links are resolved by joining rollup keys to trace-anchor index which is being reindexed during compaction; when anchor index is temporarily empty, UI shows 'No traces'. Repro correlates strongly with compaction windows and indexer backfill events.
- Affects historical panels (>30d) across multiple enterprise orgs in us-east during retention compaction windows.
- Observed on ~4 orgs in last 72h, including LumenHealth and 2 other enterprise accounts.
- Alerts relying on those rollups may be suppressed or show incorrect counts for the duration of compaction warmup.
- No data loss: data is present after reindex/backfill; this is a read-path consistency/window problem.
Short term: ask customer to (a) avoid rapidly toggling large time windows during the scheduled compaction window, or (b) use a narrower time range (<=30d) which reads from hot partitions. Support can also force a panel refresh via console 'Force reload' (admin button) which triggers a hot-replica read. We have provided LumenHealth with instructions for forced refresh and notified them of the scheduled compaction window.
Race between retention compaction warmup and dashboard read-path: compaction marks partitions compacted while the indexer backfills the hot replica asynchronously. Dashboard queries hitting compacted-but-not-yet-backfilled partitions return empty rollups; UI treats empty as zero. Trace-anchor index reindex causes temporary absence of anchor joins. No write-side data loss.
1) Frontend: treat empty rollup responses as 'retry with hot-replica' instead of rendering zero. 2) API layer: add fallback read-path to hot replicas when compaction-warmup flag is set for the partition. 3) Indexer: reduce warmup aggressiveness and emit explicit 'warmup-in-progress' header that the API can use to select fallback. 4) Add an observability alert for 'rollup-empty-during-compaction' so SRE is alerted earlier. Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood/reindexer/pull/1189 (adds warmup header); https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/4712 (frontend retry).

Additional notes:

2026-03-13 Support (Priya): Updated customer with ETA for fix and added LumenHealth to early verification list.
In Progress: Hotfix PRs opened and staged. Short-term guidance provided to customer; monitoring for recurrence. Final resolution pending deployment of API fallback and frontend retry. Follow-up postmortem to be created after prod rollout.
Deploy reindexer warmup-header to prod behind feature flag
Update console to retry rollup reads from hot-replica when empty
Add observability alert for rollup-empty-during-compaction
Postmortem documenting mitigation and scheduling change to compaction windows

Issue summary: Customer reports that long-form streamed responses (SSE) from the hosted API consistently drop the final epilogue — typically the closing paragraph and 'source' metadata — when their client performs a short socket swap (mobile network change) behind our edge.
1) Customer opens SSE streaming chat to redwood-curated-7b in prod/us-west with X-Stream-Meta header set as two identical headers (client library adds duplicate header).
2) After ~18s of tokens, client triggers an IP/mobility handoff (WiFi -> cellular) causing a short TCP close/rebind and upstream proxy swap.
3) Client reconnects and requests resume; the session returns prior tokens but the final epilogue and trailing metadata never arrive (stream ends mid-sentence).
4) Repeatable in ~4/10 attempts when duplicate X-Stream-Meta headers present; not reproducible when header is a single consolidated value.
2026-03-10T14:03:22Z proxy-ingress[edge-03] INFO: incoming SSE start session_id=sn-9f2a X-Stream-Meta=[a,b]
2026-03-10T14:03:40Z serving-runtime[worker-12] WARN: client-socket-flip session=sn-9f2a reconnect detected, resume-request=true
2026-03-10T14:03:41Z proxy-ingress[edge-03] DEBUG: sanitized headers for session sn-9f2a; X-Stream-Meta consolidated="a"
2026-03-10T14:03:41Z serving-runtime[worker-12] ERROR: sse-stream-halfclose session=sn-9f2a tail-buffer-not-flushed; bytes-dropped=512
Customer (Sara @ NoteSpring): We're seeing the assistant cut off mid-paragraph after our users switch networks. It looks like the session resumes but the final section (citation block + closing paragraph) is missing ~40% of the time.
Support (Maya): Thanks — confirmed we can see traces for the sample request you provided. I've escalated to SRE for deeper ingestion/proxy checks and requested pcap and tcpdump from the customer.
SRE (Oliver): Observed edge sanitization logs where multi-valued X-Stream-Meta became single-valued during header normalization. Need packet captures and proxy config to validate whether the final event flush path was suppressed by header state change.
Customer: Attached pcap + curl reproducible steps. We can toggle the client to send a single header as a workaround for now.
Support: Temporary workaround noted; SRE to test hotfix in staging and confirm.
1) Telemetry: grafana link shows increased stream-halfclose count for NoteSpring sessions around 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/stream-health?var-customer=NoteSpring).
2) Hypothesis: Edge proxy header sanitizer collapses multi-header X-Stream-Meta values to the first value, which causes the serving runtime to treat the resumed connection as lacking the 'finalize' marker. The runtime then half-closes without flushing trailing buffer to client.
3) Evidence: proxy-ingress debug line 'X-Stream-Meta consolidated="a"' present in failure cases; tcpdump shows original request carried two identical X-Stream-Meta headers before ingress rewrite.
4) Related behavior: Not seen when client sends a single header or when using websocket fallback — implies issue is tied to header parsing path in ingress -> sse adapter.
5) Repro rate: ~40% on NoteSpring reproduction; higher when handoff occurs within 10–30s of stream close.
Workaround: Instructed NoteSpring to consolidate their client SDK to send a single X-Stream-Meta header (server will accept comma-separated values). Implemented customer-side change and verified missing epilogue no longer reproduces in their test harness. Fix: Rollout PR to ingress-proxy that preserves multiple X-Stream-Meta values (avoids collapsing to first value) merged to staging (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/compare/fix-multiheader-sanitize). Production rollout plan: canary 10% edge nodes 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC, monitor sse-halfclose metric for 2 hours, then full rollout. Follow-ups: add unit tests for header normalization, add metric alert for 'sse-tail-drop' and update runbook to include header-multi value check.
payload.summary: SSE stream epilogue dropped after ingress multi-header sanitization; final paragraphs missing

Issue summary:
Customer reports that over the weekend a retention compaction job merged old partitions that included several archived API keys. After the compaction, the console shows a sudden drop in usage attributed to the active API key and spikes attributed to an 'archived' api_key_id. Scheduled alerts that rely on route-level usage thresholds also fired incorrectly (false-positive) because the post-compaction attribution window considered the archived keys in the same rollup bucket.

Impact:
- MapleHealth reported a spurious billing alert and two high-priority on-call pages overnight.
- Scheduled alerts for usage thresholds fired for a route that had no active traffic.
- Trace links (tracehook context) attached to the alert were missing or pointed to the archived api_key, making debugging difficult.

Environment:
prod-us-east cluster; retention compaction run id rc-20260307-03; org id: org-7891; route id: route-33; affected API keys: api_abc_old_443 (archived), api_maple_primary_2 (active).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Run usage report for route-33 for 2026-03-06 to 2026-03-08 in console time range UTC.
2) Compare per-api-key attribution before and after rc-20260307-03 compaction job.
3) Observe scheduled alert history for route-33 that fired at 2026-03-07T04:12:00Z.

Observed behavior:
- Hourly rollups show a drop of ~95% for api_maple_primary_2 for 2026-03-07 03:00-04:00Z and a compensating spike attributed to api_abc_old_443 in the same hour.
- Alert evaluation history shows the alert condition evaluated on compacted rollup records and attached trace_anchor referencing api_abc_old_443 (archived) which has no live tracehooks.

Expected behavior:
- Compaction should preserve correct api-key attribution and not reassign recent active traffic to archived identifiers.
- Alerts should evaluate against rollups that maintain route-to-active-api-key mapping for the alert time window.

Customer logs/attachments:
- CSV export of pre/post compaction rollup diffs (attached by customer).
Download hourly-usage rollups for route-33 for 2026-03-06..2026-03-08 from console export
Re-run rc-20260307-03 compaction locally against a small dataset (dev cluster) following runbook
Compare attribution by api_key_id across pre/post compaction datasets
Inspect alert-eval history for scheduled alerts on route-33 in the same timeframe and check alert.attach.trace_anchor
Active api key usage dropped ~95% in the post-compaction hourly rollup
Archived api key shows compensating spike in same hour
Alert evaluation attached trace anchors pointing to archived api key which has no live traces
Attribution remains stable across compaction boundaries
Alerts attach tracehooks that map to active api keys and include trace context
No spurious billing or alert pages due to compaction metadata merges
Compaction job rc-20260307-03 logs show fallback to legacy-canonicalization when merge conflicts detected at bucket-level.
Legacy canonicalization index contains entries mapping api_maple_primary_2 -> api_abc_old_443 for historical reasons (API key rotate path).
Alert evaluator reads aggregated rollups by bucket timestamp; it does not re-run attribution reconciliation post-compaction which allows the misattributed records to trigger alerts.
Tracehook linkage requires api_key to be present in active key registry to resolve trace anchors; archived keys are not present resulting in missing trace context.
Reproduced locally: running compaction with legacy index on a small dataset produced identical misattribution pattern and caused test alert to fire.
Temporary mitigation: disabled scheduled compaction fallback to legacy canonicalization for in-flight jobs (flag rc.fallback_legacy=false). Rolled back rc-20260307-03 indices for 2026-03-07 by restoring pre-compact S3 snapshot for affected partitions and re-running a safe compaction job using schema v3 merge logic. PR github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2187 contains the permanent fix to skip legacy index merges for buckets with any records < 14 days old. Recommended follow-ups: (1) run backfill to reconcile attribution for 2026-02-22..2026-03-08 windows, (2) add unit test for canonicalization map fallback, (3) postmortem to explain why legacy index entries remained for org-7891. Customer notified 2026-03-13 and asked to validate reconciled usage; they confirmed reduced false alerts but requested completion of backfill and confirmation of billing adjustments.
Mitigation applied and pre-compaction rollups restored for the affected hour; customer reported alerts stopped firing incorrectly. Follow-up backfill scheduled and owner assigned to Eng (Priya Singh). Billing team notified to review possible credit for spurious alerts/pages.
Backfill attribution reconcile job scheduled: owner Priya Singh, ETA 2026-03-20
Add unit/integration tests for compaction canonicalization fallback: assigned to Eng team
Create Confluence postmortem and chore for auditing legacy canonicalization index entries
Billing team to evaluate credits for MapleHealth Analytics: ticket FIN-1289

2026-03-12 | Eng - Priya Singh: Found compaction job used schema v2 rollup-merger; a fallback path executed for partitions > 30 days that uses legacy attribution index. Placed a patch to skip legacy index for partitions with recent timestamps. Opening PR #2187.

Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC OpalMetrics reported persistent streaming disconnects and slow tail latencies for high-priority scoring calls. Initial symptoms looked like throttling and 5xx errors but investigation found systemic priority inversion in request routing followed by failover amplification to a quantized model variant. Impact: sustained SLO breaches for conversational streaming endpoints, duplicated completions for long-running batch requests, and a downstream invoice variance for OpalMetrics. This ticket captures timeline, triage notes, mitigation, and follow-up actions.
OpalMetrics production traffic (enterprise plan) experienced ~18% request error rate for streaming endpoints and 2.3x tail latency on p99 for 30 minutes. Customer reported missing events in downstream scoring pipelines and a projected billing overage due to duplicate requests. SLA window flagged — customer escalated to CS and assigned P0.
1) Send mixed-priority traffic: interleave streaming/high-priority scoring requests with large low-priority batch embeddings for the same tenant (simulate 1:3 ratio).
2) Observe request routing: per-worker queues saturate causing high-priority requests to be queued behind long-running low-priority tasks.
3) Trigger failover by simulating a small GPU pool pressure so autoscaler marks pool degraded; observe fallback policy routing to quantized variant and duplicate-invocation amplification.
2026-03-10T14:07:21Z router INFO tenant=opalmetrics req_id=8f2e... queued priority=high behind task_id=cb1a... duration_est=120s
2026-03-10T14:08:03Z runtime WARN model=redwood-7b-v2 req_id=cb1a... long_running=true queue_len=42
2026-03-10T14:09:12Z fallback ERROR routing policy triggered fallback_to=redwood-7b-quantized triggered_by=pool_pressure replica=gd-11
2026-03-10T14:09:18Z api-gateway ERROR duplicate-invocation req_id=8f2e... dup_count=2 reason=failover_resend
Initial hypothesis: throttling at ingress layer due to per-tenant token rate limit — disproved by rate-limit metrics (no wild spikes).
Heap of evidence pointed to per-worker FIFO queues and lack of preemption: long-running low-priority batch tasks were occupying workers and preventing high-priority streaming requests from being scheduled (priority inversion).
Failover policy design: when node pool reported degraded capacity, router triggered immediate failover to a compatible quantized variant but also retried requests without de-duplicating in-flight requests, causing duplicate completions and billing anomalies.
Observed autoscaler behavior: a rapid short-lived GPU availability drop (OOM on one replica during a heavy background maintenance job) caused scheduler to mark pool degraded; autoscaler later recovered within ~2m but failover amplification window had already started.

Additional notes:
OpalMetrics (Customer): 2026-03-10 15:45 UTC — Customer acceptance of temporary throttling workaround; requested written action plan for billing variance and mitigation to prevent recurrence.
Mitigation: 1) Emergency routing rule applied to prioritize high-priority streaming requests for tenant opalmetrics and to preempt long-running low-priority tasks. 2) Temporary quota increase provided to OpalMetrics while the pool stabilized. 3) Hotfix (PR#4821) deployed to serving-runtime to add idempotency guard for failover retries and to introduce a preemption-aware scheduling policy. Root cause: combined effect of per-worker FIFO queues (no preemption) and failover retry logic that resubmitted in-flight requests without deduplication when pool health flapped. Result: resolved duplicate invocations, tail latency restored to baseline, and streaming disconnects ceased.
1) Engineering to refactor router scheduling: implement priority-aware worker preemption and bounded preemption cost model (owner: SRE/serving-runtime; ETA: 2026-04-15).
2) Deploy improved health gating for failover: require idempotency token or explicit dedupe header before resending in-flight requests (owner: Serving Runtime; completed 2026-03-11).
3) Update runbook and add a new play for mixed-priority traffic tenants to proactively set preemption thresholds (owner: Support; ETA: 2026-03-18).
4) Issue a customer-facing invoice reconciliation and apply credit for duplicate-invocation billing exposure (owner: Finance/CS; ETA: 2026-03-16).
5) Create a detection alert for 'priority inversion' signature: sustained high queue depth + increased p99 for high-priority requests (owner: Observability; ETA: 2026-03-20).
payload.summary: OpalMetrics: request-priority inversion → failover cascade causing streaming SLO breaches and invoice variance

Issue summary:
Customer reports that after switching their embedding alias from redwood-embed-v1-base -> redwood-embed-v1-updated (performed via Console rollout), reranking results for several queries reversed order and overall rerank latency increased by ~120ms P50. This was observed across multiple documents and queries that previously had stable top-3 rankings.

Impact:
- NovaDocs' search UX shows degraded relevance (top result swapped in 12% of weekly query sampling) causing user complaints.
- Per-request latency for /rerank endpoint increased from ~80ms median to ~200ms median for affected routes.
- Occurred immediately after alias change; customer rolled back alias and saw partial improvement in relevance but latency remained elevated for ~10 minutes.

Environment:
- Customer: NovaDocs (enterprise account, dedicated plan in us-east-1)
- Affected endpoints: POST /v1/embeddings, POST /v1/rerank
- Time window: 2026-03-09 15:10 - 15:45 UTC

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer and validated by Support):
1) Use alias redwood-embed-v1-updated to create embeddings for sample set (500 docs).
2) Call /rerank with same query/document embeddings using customer's reranker flow (cosine similarity followed by softmax).
3) Observe rerank ordering compared to baseline using redwood-embed-v1-base.
4) Measure /rerank p50 latency for 1000 requests.

Expected behavior:
- Rerank ordering should be consistent or improve; latency should remain within historical baselines.

Actual behavior:
- Top-k ordering changed for a non-trivial fraction of queries (12% of sample).
- Embedding vector norms looked similar but component distributions shifted noticeably (visualized in customer-supplied histograms).
- Cache hit rate on reranker-side prefix cache dropped by ~70% during and after alias change.
- Median /rerank latency increased by ~120ms for ~20 minutes after alias rollout.

Customer-provided logs and artifacts:
- Sampled JSON payloads used for repro (attached to ticket).
- Histograms of embedding component distributions for 1000 samples (base vs updated).
- Request/response timing logs from client showing 15:12 UTC spike.

Additional notes:
- Customer confirmed manual rollback of alias at 15:18 UTC and still observed latency uplift until 15:28 UTC; relevance partially reverted but not fully via rollback alone.

2026-03-09 15:55 UTC - Support (Aisha K): Thanks for the detailed repro artifacts, @NovaDocs. We're triaging this as P1 given production impact. Assigning to embeddings team for immediate investigation. @BenM is taking point.
2026-03-09 16:10 UTC - Customer (Jordan L, NovaDocs): We can provide additional sample queries; happy to share a live session. The rollback seemed to help relevancy but there are lingering latency spikes in our telemetry.
2026-03-09 17:00 UTC - Eng (Ben Morales): Initial checks: no infra provisioning events in us-east-1. Noticed cache miss spike correlating with alias switch and a short window of increased batching latency in serving runtime logs. Captured logs and started deeper trace collection.
2026-03-10 09:20 UTC - Eng (Ben Morales): Reproduced locally with customer's dataset. Observed that the updated embed pipeline introduced a sentinel prefix handling change: padding sentinel token contributions were being aggregated into the dense mean reduction when sequences were truncated at chunk boundaries. Hypothesis: embedding vectors from updated model include non-zero contributions for prefix sentinel which the normalization step did not strip out, shifting component distribution and breaking cache key normalization. Working on a fix PR and will test back-compat behavior.
2026-03-11 14:05 UTC - Support (Aisha K): We notified customer of ongoing investigation and ETA for a hotfix. Customer accepted occasional degraded relevance during short maintenance window.
2026-03-12 02:12 UTC - Eng (Ben Morales): Hotfix deployed to embeddings-service in us-east-1 (rollback of sentinel aggregation + cache key normalization patch). Monitoring shows rerank ordering returned to baseline for sampled queries and cache hit-rate recovered to prior levels. Will keep watch for 48h and prepare postmortem.
2026-03-12 02:30 UTC - Customer (Jordan L, NovaDocs): Confirmed we see rerank order back to expected results in our test suite. Thanks for the fast turnaround. We will monitor production traffic and report any regressions.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Support (Aisha K): Moving to In Progress -> monitoring; creating linked internal follow-ups for regression test coverage and rollout safeguards.
Collected request traces across API gateway -> embeddings-service -> reranker; identified three correlated signals: (1) sudden cache miss surge on reranker-side prefix cache, (2) a short change in batching window observed in serving-runtime logs, (3) distributional drift in embedding vector components for sequences that hit chunk/truncation boundary.
Reproduced with customer's sample dataset using redwood-embed-v1-updated: the mean pooling reduction included sentinel/padding token hidden states when a chunk boundary occurred; those sentinel vectors had non-zero values due to a tokenizer/model change in updated release.
Cache key generation used a normalized embedding fingerprint that assumed embeddings were L2-normalized and had sentinel positions zeroed. Because updated embeddings included sentinel leakage, fingerprints changed and resulted in cache misses (cold downstream reranker runs increased latency).
Hypothesis validated by instrumenting the embedding pipeline to zero-out sentinel positions prior to reduction; when applied locally, both rerank ordering and cache hit rate returned to baseline in repro tests.
Also observed a small regression in serving-runtime batching behavior triggered by slightly different sequence length distribution from updated embeddings; we adjusted batching heuristics to avoid enlarging batch windows when prefix-sentinels are present.
Related logs and trace IDs: trace-ea9f7 (15:12 UTC), trace-ea9f8 (15:20 UTC). Saved snapshots to internal S3 for postmortem (link in Confluence page).
Hotfix deployed 2026-03-12 02:12 UTC to embeddings-service in us-east-1: (1) ensure sentinel/padding positions are zeroed prior to mean/pooled reduction, (2) normalize embeddings consistently before cache key computation, and (3) adjust batching heuristic to avoid widening windows on chunk-boundary cases. Verified by running customer's repro suite: rerank ordering returned to baseline and cache hit-rate recovered. Next steps: formal postmortem, add unit/e2e tests to prevent regression on model alias rollouts, add a console warning when alias changes introduce embedding-shape/normalization differences, and coordinate with model ops to include a compatibility check during model alias rollouts.
payload.summary: Unexpected rerank order changes and latency spike after embedding alias update (prefix padding aggregation bug)

Issue summary: After BrightLens upgraded their Redwood client SDK from v1.3.9 to v1.4.0, they observed a sudden wave of 429 responses across their tenant in us-east. Impact: Production ingestion pipelines and real-time chat features saw repeated 429s for ~18 minutes, causing partial data loss for a subset of background workers and elevated error rates for interactive sessions.

Observed behavior: Tenant-level token quotas were exhausted quickly with many short-lived keepalive/healthcheck requests counted against burst credits. The 429s present as opaque rejections (no explicit route-level exhaustion metadata) and coincide with spikes in connection churn from the customer's side after the client upgrade.

Expected behavior: The client upgrade should not materially increase keepalive frequency or cause double-counting. Background heartbeats and short-lived connection probes should be excluded from burst credit accounting when the customer's recommended keepalive exemption flag is active.

Customer note: Customer has flagged that only client SDKs were changed, no server-side config or deployment changes. They attached SDK logs and said backoff logic is standard, but observed retries escalate rapidly when 429s start.

Links:
- Support thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C_SUPPORT/p1646001234000

Additional notes:
- Customer-provided SDK logs: s3://support-uploads/brightlens/sdklogs/2026-03-10-keepalive.zip
1) Upgrade Redwood client SDK from v1.3.9 to v1.4.0 using pip/npm package
2) Start a fleet of lightweight background workers (50-100) configured with default keepalive/healthcheck=enabled
3) Observe connection churn during deploy (workers reconnecting while upgrade rolls out),
4) Monitor /v1/usage and tenant token buckets for burst depletion and 429 responses
Edge logs (snippet): 2026-03-10T02:07:12Z tenant=brightlens conn_id=abc123 KEEPALIVE start
Rate limiter trace: token_bucket_refill: window=60s refill=1000 consumed=1180 (spike)
Customer SDK sample: reconnect loop delayed backoff 200ms -> 400ms -> 800ms then parallel restart of 40 workers
2026-03-10 02:25 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer reports 18 minute spike starting 02:05 UTC, all interactive endpoints showed elevated 429. Requesting immediate guidance and whether this is expected after client upgrade.
2026-03-10 02:40 - SRE (Daniel Kim): Triage started. Initial rate-limiter graphs show tenant token depletion coincident with ~600 short-lived keepalive requests/min. Investigating whether keepalive subjects are being counted as standard requests rather than 'probe' category.
2026-03-10 03:05 - Eng (Rita Sanchez): Noted client SDK change log includes a socket reconnect batching optimization that may cause simultaneous reconnects when process restarts. Flagging a potential throttling amplification. Creating an instrumentation branch to correlate connection IDs.
2026-03-11 10:12 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer confirmed they temporarily rolled back to client v1.3.9 and the 429 waves stopped. They can reproduce on staging with v1.4.0 under a rolling deploy pattern.
Hypothesis 1: v1.4.0 introduced synchronous reconnect behavior on startup that causes keepalives to fire earlier and in aggregate, pushing tenant over burst window.
Hypothesis 2: Edge proxy now counts certain preflight/keepalive frames as full tokens due to header changes in the new SDK (SNI/host header difference).
Data: Correlated edge metrics (conn churn vs token consumption) show a 7x increase in connection open/close rate for the customer's tenant during rollout period.
Checked linked rate-limiter config: tenant has default burst pool with 60s window, no exempted probe pool configured for this tenant.
Workaround (short-term): Advise customer to roll back to v1.3.9 or apply staged rollout with randomized reconnect jitter. They rolled back and observed normal behavior within 4 minutes.
Mitigation (platform): Engineering to add a temporary rule to classify rapid keepalive/healthcheck patterns from this tenant as 'probe' for 24h to prevent burst depletion while SDK fix is delivered.
Permanent fix (follow-up): Client SDK team to patch v1.4.1 to add randomized reconnect jitter and avoid synchronous heartbeat emission. Edge team to validate header normalization so probe frames are not token-accounted when probe-exemption header is present.
Rollout plan: feature flag gp/keepalive-exempt for edge to be deployed canary to us-east by 2026-03-15. SDK patch expected CI->release by 2026-03-14.

payload.description:
Issue summary
Acme AI is seeing intermittent request hangs/timeouts on their Dedicated cluster when running multi-GPU tensor-parallel replicas (A100 80GB, TP=4). During the affected windows, we captured NCCL debug output indicating a suspected collective mismatch / out-of-order collective sequence across ranks. Symptoms align with “silent stall” scenarios: GPU utilization drops to near-idle on one or more ranks, in-flight requests stop making progress, and the API layer eventually returns timeouts.

Customer impact
- Streaming chat requests hang (no tokens emitted) and then time out.
- p99 latency spikes + elevated 504s from gateway for the affected route.
- Incident-level impact during peak hours; Acme AI has implemented a temporary concurrency cap but is still seeing sporadic stalls under burst.

Environment
- Deployment: Dedicated (customer VPC peering)
- Region: us-east
- Hardware: A100 80GB (4 GPUs per replica)
- Runtime version: 1.18.6-redwood (customer pinned), canary candidate 1.19.0-rc2 available
- Models: llama-70b-instruct (TP=4), mixtral-8x7b-instruct (TP=2)
- Workload pattern: mixed prompt lengths (2k–16k), streaming enabled, bursty concurrency (spikes), cancellations observed (client disconnects)

What we collected
1) NCCL debug logs (sanitized) from an affected replica (rank 0 and rank 3). These were captured during a canary debug window (see INT-2219). Notable lines below.
2) Runtime structured logs showing TP step progress halting on a collective boundary.
3) Request IDs and approximate timestamps to correlate with tracing.

NCCL debug excerpts (sanitized)
Timestamp window: 2025-02-20 18:31:02–18:33:10 UTC

Rank 0:
- "NCCL INFO Launch mode: Group"
- "NCCL INFO comm 0x7f2a... rank 0 nranks 4 cudaDev 0 busId 0000:2b:00.0"
- "NCCL INFO Ring 00 : 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 0"
- "NCCL INFO AllReduce: opCount 184467 count 2097152 datatype 7 op 0 root -1"
- "NCCL WARN [Service thread] Connection closed by peer"
- "NCCL INFO Abort COMPLETE"

Rank 3:
- "NCCL INFO comm 0x7f93... rank 3 nranks 4 cudaDev 3 busId 0000:b1:00.0"
- "NCCL INFO AllReduce: opCount 184466 count 2097152 datatype 7 op 0 root -1"
- "NCCL INFO AllGather: opCount 184467 count 524288 datatype 7"
- (No further progress; no matching AllGather on rank 0 at same opCount)

Interpretation (tentative)
- Rank 3 appears to advance to a different collective (AllGather) while rank 0 is still at AllReduce for the same opCount+1 boundary. This is consistent with a collective ordering divergence between ranks (could be stream/event ordering, conditional path in kernel code, cancellation/early-exit path, or scheduler starvation causing one rank to enter a different phase).
- The “Connection closed by peer” and abort is likely a downstream symptom once one rank times out/aborts; we need to determine the first divergence trigger.

Current hypothesis (needs Eng confirmation)
- Ordering/synchronization issue around NCCL collectives on separate CUDA streams when mixed prefill/decode interleaving occurs, potentially amplified by request cancellation and/or CUDA graph capture constraints.
- Alternate hypothesis: scheduler fairness/starvation causes one rank to delay a collective while others advance, leading to mismatch.

Asks / next steps

Additional notes:
- SRE (Rafael/Aisha): confirm alerting signals available for “heartbeat gaps per rank” and whether this was visible during incident windows.
Temporary mitigations (currently applied / recommended)
- Apply concurrency cap per replica (Acme currently set to 24; previously 48).
- Disable CUDA graph capture on TP routes (if enabled) for stability testing.
- Prefer Dedicated-first canary on runtime 1.19 with NCCL stream/event sync hardening + stall detectors once available.
References
- Slack incident thread: #incidents (1740165551-sev1-dedicated-timeouts-suspected-tp-hang)
- Slack runtime thread: #eng-runtime (1739812205-nccl-collective-ordering-suspected-mismatch)
- In-flight fixes: PR-21853 (stream/event sync hardening), PR-21841 (scheduler guardrail), PR-21912 (error surfacing), PR-21860 (watchdog/drain)
Attachments
- Redacted NCCL log bundle uploaded to support case (internal link): support-attachments/SUP-48377/nccl-debug-logs-2025-02-20.tgz
- Correlation sheet (request ids + timestamps): support-attachments/SUP-48377/request-correlation.csv

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers using SSE streaming to a Dedicated pool see cases where the finalization metadata (terminal headers) for a completed choice is either missing or duplicated after a reconnect. In affected sessions a reconnect that happens late (after the runtime emitted final token fragments but before client ACK/close) results in two partial final fragments and no consolidated terminal header (choice_final=true, reason=stop) attached to either fragment.

Impact:
- TileCloud reports truncated transcript in production chat flows (missing final metadata prevents client SDK from persisting final choice).
- Rare but high-impact: results in application-level timeouts and duplicate persisted messages.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (customer pool id: dc-06b2)
- Production (us-east-1)
- Ingests via edge API (api.redwood.example -> internal gateway -> runtime)

Observed behavior:
- Client receives two final token fragments that both appear to be tail fragments of the same choice. Neither fragment carries the terminal headers expected by the SDK (no "final_choice":true header, no final reason metadata).
- Session trace shows runtime wrote a session snapshot on disconnect and then accepted a resume that merged an older snapshot ID, producing duplicated partial fragments.

Expected behavior:
- After resume the stream should deliver a single final fragment annotated with terminal headers/metadata, or if duplicate fragments happen the runtime should attach terminal metadata to the final emitted fragment and suppress duplicates for client SDKs.

1) Start an SSE chat session against the dedicated pool with a long final token buffer (example prompt that produces a 500-700 token final choice).
2) Simulate a client-side reconnect by closing TCP (or letting a proxy do a half-close) right after the server emits most of the final tokens but before the app-layer final ACK/End marker is sent,
3) Re-establish the SSE connection with the same session id within ~3s. Observe the resumed stream events and metadata.
TraceID: trace-7f9b1c - runtime emitted fragments: fragment-12345 (final-part-1), fragment-12346 (final-part-2) - neither contains 'terminal: true' header.
Gateway log: resume request contained X-Session-Snapshot: snap-v3, runtime active snapshot: snap-v4 - runtime merged snap-v3 into active state and replayed tail fragments.
Edge proxy (haproxy) connection log: client closed connection at 2026-03-09T14:21:12.123Z, new connection resumed at 2026-03-09T14:21:14.371Z.
03/10 - Maya: Initial customer report and attached client-side dump and raw SSE transcript; reproduced in a staging Dedicated pool with a tooling harness.
03/11 - SRE (Arjun): Correlated runtime traces to gateway resume path. Found resume handler accepts older snapshot versions when incoming snapshot header is present and merges by replaying deltas. This merge path doesn't reconcile terminal metadata for choices emitted just before the disconnect.
03/11 - Eng (runtime): Confirmed logic in snapshot merge path (session_manager/merge_snapshots) will re-emit buffered fragments on resume. Terminal headers are only attached when fragment emission completes in the canonical snapshot, so replays can omit finalization metadata.
03/12 - Test: Reproduced deterministically by forcing an artificial 'emit then drop' window; reproducer saved as repro/stream-snapshot-replay.sh in internal artifacts.
When a reconnect supplies an older session snapshot id (e.g., due to proxy connection reuse or client sending stale snapshot header), the runtime merges the older snapshot into the current session and replays buffered tail fragments. The replay path re-emits token fragments but does not re-attach terminal metadata, causing clients to see duplicate partial finals and missing terminal headers.
TileCloud switched the client to use websocket fallback for the short-term and disabled proxy connection pooling between client and edge (set 'Connection: close') to avoid stale snapshot ids being forwarded. Both actions stopped new occurrences.
Eng has a branch that: (1) validates incoming snapshot id against the active session generation and refuses resume if the incoming snapshot is older than current by more than 1 generation (configurable), and (2) attaches terminal metadata during replay of any final fragments. Patch PR: runtime/pull/2197. Pending QA and rollout to Dedicated pools. Plan to roll to a canary pool on 2026-03-15.
1) Roll PR runtime/pull/2197 to canary Dedicated pool (owner: Arjun).
2) Add an e2e regression test for late-resume path to ensure terminal metadata is preserved,
3) Update docs and SDK to tolerate duplicate tail fragments if terminal header is present or to request full-resume semantics via an explicit flag,
4) Notify TileCloud prior to canary deploy and schedule a 1-hour maintenance window if needed.
2026-03-10 - tilecloud-support@tilecloud.com: 'We're seeing whole messages saved without final punctuation; appears the SDK never got the final event. Attaching raw SSE transcript.'

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - TileCloud (Customer): 'We have an internal L7 proxy that enables keepalive pooling. We'll try a quick test with pooling disabled and report back.'
payload.summary: Late reconnect snapshots cause mismatched terminal headers and duplicate final fragments on SSE

payload.description:
Issue summary: During streaming sessions for AtlasDocs (enterprise customer) we observed a pattern where the client receives an end delimiter event but the accompanying termination metadata (choices.status / finalized=true / request_id) is missing, and the final code block is truncated. Impact: customers see partially closed code fences and cannot parse final output, leading to failed post-processing and user-facing errors. This appears to happen after a socket handoff triggered by the load balancer when the upstream returns a GOAWAY.

Environment: production, requests routed through our main api-gateway in us-east to the serving-runtime pool (dedicated). Occurs across both SSE and websocket clients using the SDK and custom websockets behind corp proxies.

Expected: a single well-formed end event with termination metadata and final tokens, or a clear recoverable resume token.
Actual: client receives terminal delimiter ("[END]"/EOF event) but missing termination metadata; last code fence cut mid-line. Logs show session_id mismatch and a GOAWAY from the LB preceding the event.
1) Customer sends a long streaming generation request (approx 700-1200 tokens expected) to /v1/chat/stream with streaming=true and resume=true.
2) While model is generating, trigger a simulated lb handoff: curl to control-plane to rotate connection (internal simulate-handoff).
3) Observe client stream: an end delimiter is emitted, but final metadata block (JSON chunk with status/finalized/request_id) is absent, and the last markdown code fence is cut off.
4) Reproduces ~1 in 50 tries in our dedicated pool under bursty traffic; customer reports ~10% of long streams affected in their environment behind corporate proxy.

2026-03-10T14:12:04.008Z lb us-east conn=1245 GOAWAY: last_stream=1023; error_code=NO_ERROR; debug=handoff-trigger
2026-03-10T14:12:04.010Z serving-runtime instance=gpu-7 session_id=xyz-987: streaming_event: data="...```js\nfunction hello() { console.log('hi');\n// CUT"
2026-03-10T14:12:04.011Z serving-runtime instance=gpu-7 session_id=xyz-988: warning: resume_token_mismatch expected=xyz-987 got=xyz-988

Triage 2026-03-10 15:00: Initial reproducible pattern when LB issues GOAWAY mid-stream during high-concurrency bursts; issue correlates with session_id rotation in session-mapper.
Hypothesis: handoff race in session-mapper causes a new worker to flush an end delimiter before it has the finalization metadata from the origin worker's KV cache. The origin worker sends final tokens but the handoff path doesn't merge termination metadata atomically.
Telemetry: traced a sample request end-to-end. Upstream worker logged final_choice and termination_meta at 14:12:04.009Z, but handoff path emitted [END] at 14:12:04.015Z from a different worker lacking the meta. No 5xx from runtime; behavior is protocol/ordering-sensitive.
Customer environment note: AtlasDocs routes via corporate proxy that reuses connections and sends keepalives which increases LB churn frequency.
Reproduction in staging: reproduced by forcing goaway in lb-proxy with 1s delay on write; increases failure to ~1 in 10 in staging dedicated pool.
Ask customer to temporarily set streaming_resume_policy="no_handoff" in their client config (SDK flag) or fall back to non-streaming completion for critical long responses. We also recommended increasing the LB graceful-drain timeout to reduce mid-stream handoffs.
1) Ownership: serve-runtime + session-mapper owners to design atomic handoff for termination metadata (assigned).
2) Create scheduled canary with lb-handoff-disabled for small percentage of traffic for 48h to measure impact (INT-4321).
3) Patch: ensure end-event emission is gated on finalization metadata present OR add a terminal 'meta-only' event when handoff occurs.
4) Communicate mitigation to AtlasDocs CS contact and recommend SDK flag change while fix deploys.

Additional notes:
Work in progress: temporary SDK flag and LB timeout recommendation communicated. Patch design in review; ETA for canary: 2026-03-18.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 responses with no clear throttle headers during a nightly load window where realtime chat traffic (low-latency) is mixed with bulk background flush jobs. Throttles appear opaque (no 'X-RateLimit-Remaining' in some responses) and correlate with a scheduled priority-rebalance that runs in the dedicated pool.

Impact:
- StreamScale Labs reports elevated 429s for end-users for ~8-12 minutes during their 03:00-03:30 UTC maintenance slot.
- Affects user-facing chat latency and causes job retries for background flushers.
- Customer is on a dedicated pool with autoscale and reserved burst capacity.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-prod-us-east-04
- Region: us-east
- Workload: mixed realtime chat (priority=interactive) + bulk background flush (priority=background)
- Observed against models: redwood/open-ggml-7b, redwood/opt-6b

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1. Start a steady stream of low-concurrency realtime chat (10-20 RPS) pinned to interactive route.
2. Schedule a background flush job that issues ~200 parallel embedding/flush calls over 20s.
3. Trigger the nightly "priority-rebalance" (internal flag) or wait for scheduled window at 03:00 UTC.
4. Observe increased 429s across both routes; some 429 responses lack throttle headers (opaque).

Observed behavior:
- 429s spike for ~8-12 minutes overlapping the rebalance window.
- Console shows pool-level token buckets briefly reporting negative available credits then rebounded.
- Some responses miss X-RateLimit-* headers (client sees opaque 429).
- Support logs show many short-lived ephemeral sessions and signed-url refreshes also firing at the same time.

Expected behavior:
- Priority rebalance should be non-disruptive and preserve reserved burst for low-latency routes.
- All 429 responses should include standard throttle headers and clear quota accounting.

Relevant logs (excerpts):
- rate-limiter: INFO priority-rebalance started job_id=rb-20260312-03:00 pool=dp-prod-us-east-04
- rate-limiter: WARN bucket_update race detected route=background old_weight=0.2 new_weight=0.05 tokens_delta=-120
- ingress-proxy: ERROR request=abc123 upstream=rate-limiter status=429 throttle_header_missing=true
- scheduler: DEBUG flush-job flush_id=fj-934 start=2026-03-12T03:00:02Z parallel=192

Attachments:
- Customer uploaded client-side sample trace and HTTP dumps (attached to ticket).

Investigation summary:
- Correlation observed between the scheduled priority-rebalance job and the first onset of opaque 429s.
- Hypothesis 1: Non-atomic weight update path in rate-limiter allows brief double-accounting during weight migration, leading to transient negative bucket valuations that produce 429s without properly-attached headers.
- Hypothesis 2: Concurrent signed-url refreshes and background flush fanout increase ephemeral session count, amplifying the refill-smoothing window and exposing race boundaries.
- Hypothesis 3: Dedicated pool autoscaler activity (scale-down/scale-up jitter) around the same time can cause token bucket reconciliation lag.

Initial reproduction notes:
- We reproduced a smaller-scale effect in staging by triggering the same rebalance and a parallel flusher with 50 workers; saw short opaque 429s on background route and a metric spike in "bucket_rebalance_race" counter.

Next steps planned:
- SRE to disable non-critical scheduled priority-rebalance in dp-prod-us-east-04 for tomorrow's maintenance window as a mitigation.
- Engineering to add an atomic-swap path for route weight updates to eliminate double-accounting window.
- Add extra instrumentation to rate-limiter to attach fallback throttle headers on any 429s generated by internal reconciliation logic.
- Recommend customer temporarily stagger background flush windows and add a jitter to signed-url refresh schedule.


Additional notes:
2026-03-12 13:22 - StreamScale Labs (customer): Confirmed that staggering the background flush reduced 429s in a quick test but requests still saw occasional opaque 429s. Requested guidance for long-term config.
Metrics observed: bucket_rebalance_race increased by +320 during the window; token_bucket_balance temporarily went negative on two worker shards. Staging repro validated race condition at lower scale. No indication of mis-billing. No model-level throttles (model latency stable).
Short-term: Disable scheduled priority-rebalance for the affected dedicated pool; stagger background flush jobs (add jitter and lower parallelism); increase reserved burst credits for interactive route. Medium-term: Roll out atomic weight-swap fix and ensure throttle headers fallback path. Long-term: Add preflight simulation for rebalances that predicts endpoint refill impact.
ENG: implement atomic route-weight update (PR referenced). SRE: deploy additional logging and a circuit-breaker to pause rebalance if bucket_rebalance_race > 50 for 30s. CS: advise customer on stagger/jitter and provide config snippet. Ops: schedule change for next maintenance window.
Priority: customer is P1/Sv1 due to user-facing impact during their peak maintenance window. Keep updated_at synchronized with progress.

Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10T10:45Z NimbleDocs reported progressive throughput degradation on their dedicated pool (tenant: nimbledocs-dedicated-1). P50 remained stable but p95/p99 climbed and many short-stream requests observed timeouts and attach failures. Impact: customer reported increased latency and a 25% drop in successful requests across pinned routes for ~2 hours. Timeline: 10:42Z - first errors in customer traces; 10:45Z - automated alert: allocator-heartbeat-gap > 5s; 10:55Z - autoscaler performed a shrink (reclaimed GPUs); 11:05Z - customer reports repeated retries and elevated 5xxs. This ticket tracks investigation into a transient "heartbeat suppression" pattern originating from a sidecar process that appears to hold prefetch leases and starve the allocator's credit accounting, causing autoscaler reactions and GPU-credit exhaustion.
1) Use a dedicated tenant with small, frequent short-streams and prefetch enabled. 2) Simulate sidecar log flood (high stdout/stderr throughput) or introduce a synthetic sidecall that delays connection close by ~2-5s. 3) Observe allocator-heartbeat metrics and prefetch-lease count for the tenant. 4) Watch autoscaler decisions (scale down events) and GPU credit metrics. Expected: allocator keeps leases short; actual: prefetch leases linger and allocator reports heartbeat suppression leading to shrink decisions.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
FinTechWorks reports intermittent failures when Redwood private agents fetch large presigned model artifacts (50–200MB) from S3-backed storage. Failures manifest as: (a) partial file writes (artifact truncated by a few KB to several MB) followed by checksum mismatch on agent side, (b) transient 502/504 errors surfaced to the application during model pulls, and (c) sporadic long-lived gRPC stream resets after artifact fetch attempts succeed but streaming later fails.

Impact:
- Several worker nodes repeatedly fail model startup leading to reduced throughput and degraded SLAs for production features.
- Affected traffic localized to FinTechWorks EU private deployment and coincides with scheduled business-hours traffic spikes.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) peered to Redwood control plane via ExpressRoute/partner link.
- Agents run on customer-managed subnet with NAT egress through corporate edge appliance that performs HTTP/2 multiplexing and connection pooling to a corporate proxy.
- Customer reports corporate edge enforces TCP MSS clamp (MSS reduced to 1200) and an SD-WAN vendor applies per-flow HTTP/2 connection coalescing.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Trigger a model update that causes agents to download artifact with size ~120MB via presigned URL.
2) Observe agent download attempt in logs; occasionally download completes but saved file size < expected and checksum mismatch occurs.
3) Agent retries; sometimes subsequent attempt succeeds, sometimes fails with HTTP 502 from edge proxy.

Observed behavior / logs (excerpts):
- Agent log (successful partial + checksum): "GET https://s3.internal-presigned/... 200 OK, bytes_received=118,742,912 expected=120,056,345 checksum mismatch"
- Edge proxy log: "upstream response 502: connection reset after transfer completion, stream_id=23"
- tcpdump (customer): repeated TCP retransmits after TLS ServerHello; final segment size larger than path MTU and blackholed until retransmit with smaller MSS.

Preliminary hypothesis:
- Combination of an enforced MSS/TCP MSS clamp at the customer edge + HTTP/2 connection pooling across multiple upstream destinations appears to cause an MTU/multipart fragmentation blackhole for large TLS records. When the presigned download uses persistent HTTP/2 connection that gets pooled across flows, some TLS record fragmentation crosses the MSS boundary and is lost by a middlebox. The agent perceives truncated body and reports checksum mismatch; in some cases the proxy or upstream returns 502.

Why different from prior tickets:
- Existing support cases typically call out ALPN/SNI rewrites, header injection, or SNI stripping. This case is distinct because the customer has a combination of aggressive HTTP/2 pooling (coalescing unrelated host flows onto shared TCP/TLS sessions) and an SD-WAN MSS clamp producing fragmentation that selectively affects large presigned downloads, not general small control-plane calls.

Immediate customer workaround requested:
- Temporarily disable HTTP/2 pooling / connection coalescing on corporate edge for flows to Redwood S3 endpoints OR disable MSS clamp on path for agent subnets. Customer cannot change both quickly; asked for guidance which is lower-risk.
2026-03-10 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged ticket to customer, requested packet captures and edge proxy config dump. Asked for timestamped agent log and expected file size.
2026-03-11 - Customer (FinTechWorks - network ops): Uploaded tcpdump (pcap) and edge-proxy config snippet. Noted MSS clamp applied by SD-WAN controller to 1200 bytes and HTTP/2 pooled tunnels enabled. Reported issue frequency ~4% of downloads during peak window.
2026-03-12 - SRE (Luca): Reproduced locally by configuring a lab proxy to clamp MSS and enable HTTP/2 connection coalescing; observed truncated body on large downloads when server-side emitted large TLS record crossing MSS. Filed hypothesis in ticket and linked reproducer. Asked for temporary mitigation to disable pooling for Redwood endpoints.
2026-03-13 - Customer: Disabled HTTP/2 pooling for a 1-hour window (as requested) and reported immediate drop in failure rate to 0.2% during the test window. Confirmed MSS clamp still in place. Asked for permanent mitigation suggestions.
2026-03-14 - Support (Luca): Proposed two remediation paths: 1) request customer change to avoid pooling or lift MSS clamp; 2) on Redwood side, serve presigned downloads with smaller TLS record sizes (split writes) as a compatibility workaround. Opened INT-20488 to evaluate artifact-serving server-side chunking and checkout of HTTP/2 behaviour.
2026-03-14 - Customer: Prefers server-side mitigation while they schedule change control for SD-WAN. Asked for ETA on Redwood-side fix and possible performance impacts.
Reproducer: Created a lab proxy that enforces MSS=1200 and enables http2 coalescing (multiplexing unrelated Host headers on same connection). Ran presigned download from S3-compatible backend. Observed that when server issues TLS record >1200 (e.g., a 16KB TLS record), the middlebox drops fragments and TCP retransmit behavior results in truncated read in the application layer. When same download is performed over non-pooled connection or with MSS large enough, no truncation. Additional observations: TLS-level fragmentation makes behavior non-deterministic and dependent on server-side write sizes and connection reuse timing.

Heap of evidence: pcap, agent logs, edge-proxy config. Linked INT ticket created to evaluate server-side TLS write-size control and whether we can force smaller TLS record sizes for artifact responses or switch to chunked-range requests to avoid large contiguous TLS records.

Related artifacts: pcap stored in FinTechWorks-share (link redacted), reproducer script in internal sandbox repo (gh:infra/reproducers#1287).
Workaround implemented: Customer temporarily disabled http2 connection pooling for Redwood S3 endpoints; failures dropped to near-zero.
Planned fixes: INT-20488 opened to prototype server-side mitigation (split large artifact responses into smaller TLS writes / enable chunked-range transfers) with target PR in two sprints. Provided customer runbook steps for permanent network change: 1) exempt agent subnets from MSS clamp or 2) disable HTTP/2 pooling for flows to Redwood artifact domains, with suggested firewall rules and rationale.
Follow-ups: After INT-20488 reproducer completes, will schedule rollout of server-side compatibility mode behind a feature flag and notify FinTechWorks for canary. Ticket remains open until server-side mitigations are validated or customer confirms network change.
payload.summary: Intermittent presigned artifact truncation + 502s over ExpressRoute: HTTP/2 connection pooling + MTU clamp

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During the customer's afternoon peak (14:00-15:30 UTC) their dedicated pool experienced a near-immediate drop in throughput (p50/p95 tokens/sec down ~45%/60%) with a correlated increase in short-lived GPU attach/detach operations. The customer observed streaming connections completing successfully but overall throughput and tail latency degraded for batched routes.

Impact:
- CogniDocs (dedicated) sees sustained throughput loss across their primary routes for ~90 minutes during business hours.
- Affected production jobs: document-summarization and realtime-qa endpoints.
- Customer reports increased error budget and missed SLAs for a scheduled analytics job.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in prod/us-east-1.
- Autoscaler set to target 70% GPU-utilization threshold, aggressive shrink policy enabled (scale-down cooldown 60s).
- Serving runtime version: 2026.02.11
- Node images: rwinf-gpu-2026-02.

Steps to reproduce (observed by support/SRE):
1) Load increased at 14:05 UTC with many short streaming requests and periodic background agent health-checks from several tenants.
2) Monitoring shows burst of small IO operations from sidecar health-checks (40-80ms each) multiplexed over management channel.
3) Scheduler begins detaching GPUs from pods (ephemeral attach/detach spikes), autoscaler interprets transient IO noise as lower ready capacity and initiates scale-down/scale-up oscillation.
4) While scale activity completes, throughput for batched routes falls due to reduced available slots and increased scheduling jitter.
5) By 15:30 UTC system stabilizes as transient probes subside and autoscaler settles.

Observed metrics/logs:
- GPU attach/detach rate: baseline ~0.2/min -> spike to ~4/min during incident window (metrics link: https://kibana.redwood/cogni/attach-spike).
- Autoscaler decisions: 6 scale-downs and 5 scale-ups in 20m window (see timeline in dashboard).
- p95 token latency rose from 220ms -> 1.8s.
- Kernel traces show increased PCIe queue latency concurrent with attach events.
- Sidecar logs show repeated health-checks to control plane: "probe succeeded" followed by immediate reconnects.

Hypothesis:
The customer's environment had many tenants running periodic background health probes over the management channel. These probes produce small but frequent IO that overlaps with GPU attach/detach code paths. The autoscaler sensing logic (which considers ephemeral attach latency and slot availability) misinterpreted transient attach/detach as persistent capacity loss and oscillated. The oscillation reduced effective slot capacity and increased scheduling jitter, producing throughput collapse.

Temporary mitigation performed:
- Support toggled autoscaler scale-down aggressiveness for the affected pool (increased cooldown to 300s) which reduced oscillation and restored baseline throughput within ~10 minutes.
- Requested customer temporarily disable non-critical sidecar probes on tenant containers for the 2-hour window.

Longer-term remediation proposed:
1) Patch autoscaler sensor to ignore short-lived attach/detach spikes under certain IO-latency thresholds (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1453).
2) Introduce sliding-window smoothing to autoscaler signals and increase minimum stable window before scale decisions for dedicated pools with mixed short/long streams.
3) Add monitoring alert for attach/detach rate anomalies and a runbook to toggle scale-down policy.
4) Customer guidance: move non-critical health-checks to lower-frequency or a separate management channel to reduce contention with GPU attach paths.

Next steps / Owner:
- SRE (Liam Chen) to validate patch in staging and coordinate controlled rollout to prod dedicated pools (ETA: 2026-03-18).
- Support to work with CogniDocs to audit sidecar probe frequency and recommend configuration changes.
- Engineering to add telemetry dashboard and alert (owner: infra-telemetry team).

Resolution notes (provisional):
- Temporary autoscaler cooldown increase restored throughput; final resolution pending autoscaler patch rollout and customer probe reconfiguration.
2026-03-10 14:25 UTC - CogniDocs Support: We saw throughput drop right after a small surge of short streams. No 5xxs but overall token throughput halved. Asking if this is a model or infra issue.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:05 UTC - CogniDocs Support: After the cooldown change we see throughput return toward normal, p95 dropping back. Leaving probes disabled for now per request.
2026-03-11 09:12 UTC - Eng (infra-telemetry): Reviewing autoscaler decision logic; creating PR to add smoothing and an attach-rate guard. Reference PR created.
2026-03-12 17:05 UTC - CogniDocs Support: Requesting postmortem and runbook entry once fix is live.
Mitigated (temporary) - autoscaler cooldown increased; awaiting autoscaler sensor patch and customer probe reconfiguration for permanent fix.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers with dashboard alerts that rely on trace links (`trace_link` / `trace_id`) are receiving notifications with the trace link omitted when the alert evaluator rewrites their ad-hoc query during evaluation. The alert fires correctly (count/threshold is correct) but the notification card and the alert email contain no link back to the trace, preventing customers from drilling into traces from the alert.
1) Customer creates a dashboard widget that includes tracing hooks (trace_link reference) and saves an ad-hoc query.
2) Create an alert on that widget using a custom query that references an expression or alias (example uses a subquery/alias for grouping).
3) Wait for the alert to fire or force-evaluate it.
4) Observe the alert notification in Console and email: notifications do not include the 'View Trace' link or trace_id context.
5) In some cases, adding an explicit 'SELECT trace_link' to the saved query restores the link (workaround).
Customer (BrightCart, enterprise) - inability to quickly triage alerting incidents because alert notifications lack trace links. Leads to increased mean time to investigate (MTTI) and escalations to Support. Affects multiple customers running ad-hoc queries with aliases or optimizer-friendly patterns.
- Eval logs (query-engine): optimizer rewrite shows projection elimination: `SELECT ...` -> `SELECT ...` (trace_link removed) (see partial extract below).
- Application log excerpt (us-east alert-eval pool) 2026-03-09T21:42:11Z: evaluator=alerts id=246381-start rewrite=true removed_cols=[trace_link]
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0123ABC45/p1678470000000
- Customer-provided screenshot of alert email (redacted) attached in case file (internal link).

Additional notes:
Initial hypothesis: optimizer rewrite/projection elimination removes columns that are not referenced in the final aggregation expression. However, trace_link is expected to be a side-channel used by Console/alerting for drilldown. Recent change (PR #4582 merged 2026-02-28) made projection elimination too aggressive and did not consider side-channel consumers (alerts/console). Repro case: saved query uses 'group by user_alias' and alert performs post-eval enrichment for trace_link; optimizer removes trace_link because it thinks it's unused in numeric aggregation. Verified by instrumenting the rewrite path and reproducing in staging. Query-engine logs show 'removed_cols=[trace_link]'.
Temporary workaround provided to customer: add an explicit 'SELECT trace_link' in the alert query or enable 'disable_query_rewrite=true' in alert advanced settings.
Engineer fix: query-engine PR #4620 adds a preservation rule to keep 'trace_link' and any column tagged as 'console_side_channel' during rewrite when the query is being evaluated for alerts. Patch deployed to staging on 2026-03-11. Canary rollout planned for prod on 2026-03-15 with monitoring on alert-eval success and notification completeness.
Follow-ups: add regression test covering alert-driven query evaluation, update developer docs to document 'console_side_channel' tagging for future columns, update Confluence runbook 'alert-eval-query-rewrite' with workaround steps and timeline. Notify BrightCart CSM when prod canary completes.
1) Complete canary rollout 2026-03-15 and validate notifications contain trace links. 2) Add automated regression to CI to ensure future optimizer changes don't drop side-channel columns. 3) Update Console alert UI to surface a 'preserve trace links' toggle for customers. 4) Close ticket after customer confirmation and postmortem entry.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Noteable Analytics reported intermittent p99/p999 latency spikes and increased 504s when they replay identical conversational turns at high parallel fanout. Problem appears only on their dedicated pool in us-east-1 and corresponds to bursts of KV prefix-cache misses.

Impact:
- Customer seeing 5-15% of generation requests time out during replay-heavy workloads (their QA harness replays the same turn across 200 concurrent sessions).
- Visible increase in per-request token cost due to repeated full-context re-evaluation after cache misses.
- Business impact: page templates and chat replays failing during demos; escalated to CS.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (d3.large-gpu cluster) in us-east-1
- Serving runtime version: 2.8.1
- KV cache service: kv-prefetch v1.7 (internal build)
- Autoscaler version: autoscale-3.2

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1. Create 200 parallel websocket streams to /v1/chat/stream with the same conversation turn (same prefix) replayed across sessions.
2. Ensure session affinity is disabled on the client (they use ephemeral session ids).
3. Observe generation latency and count 504 responses over a 10-minute run.

Observed logs / metrics (samples):
- p99 generation latency jump from ~220ms -> ~1.9s during burst windows.
- 504 count: 0.8% baseline -> 6.3% during spike window.
- KVCACHE-prefetch miss rate: 2% -> 48% on affected shard set.
- Metric spike correlated with short-lived node churn events reported by autoscaler (node retire/replace events within the same minute).

Initial investigation notes:
- Support reproduced a scaled-down version in staging using the customer's harness; confirmed miss amplification when many parallel replays target the same prefix.
- Cache telemetry shows an amplification pattern where a single hot prefix causes N concurrent prefetch requests to the backing store when prefetch deduplication fails.
- Deduplication failure seems to align with requests that lost session-affinity and re-routed to a shard that had an in-flight invalidation token.
- Autoscaler churn made the effect worse: when a node is removed and shards migrate, the prefetch dedupe map briefly contains concurrent keys with different ephemeral shard tokens, allowing duplicate prefetches to proceed.

Hypothesis:
- The prefetch deduplication key includes a shard-instance token that changes on migration. Rapid parallel replays with ephemeral session ids + node churn produce differing dedupe keys for the same logical prefix, causing a "missstorm" where many backends simultaneously fetch the same prefix. This overwhelms the backing store and increases end-to-end latency, and some requests time out.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support suggested customer enable consistent session-affinity in their dedicated pool (customer accepted and tested). Results: immediate reduction in missstorm amplitude but did not fully eliminate spikes during autoscaler churn.
- Applied conservative rate-limiting on prefetch concurrency at the edge (config change rolled to affected nodes) to bound fanout from 200->16 concurrent prefetches. This reduced 504s to ~1.6% for the next test window.

Engineering actions / root cause fix plan:
- Patch prefetch dedupe: move dedupe key away from ephemeral shard-instance token to stable shard-id + prefix hash (PR linked). Patch backported to 2.8.x.
- Improve migration handshake: add short grace window where migrating shards forward in-flight prefetch dedupe records to target to avoid duplicate fetches.
- Add automated test that simulates node migration + high-fanout replay to prevent regressions.
- Rollout plan: canary patch to 10% of dedicated pools in us-east-1 -> monitor kv-prefetch miss rate and 504s for 48 hours -> full rollout.

Resolution notes (work in progress):
- Patch merged to main and cherry-picked to release-2.8 (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8942).
- Canary scheduled 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC for the affected cluster.
- Customer advised to keep session-affinity enabled until full rollout completes.

Follow-up items:
- Postmortem doc to be created after full verification (owner: Ethan Blake).
- Add observability metric: dedupe-duplicate-prefetch-count per shard.
- Update runbook for dedicated customers to recommend session-affinity for replay-heavy workloads.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:03 - Support (Maya Chen): Reproduced in staging with scaled harness. Observed high KVCACHE-prefetch miss amplification. Escalating to serving runtime team.
2026-03-10 14:28 - Eng (Ethan Blake): Noted correlation with autoscaler churn. Hypothesis: dedupe key entropy introduced by migration token. Creating PR to remove shard-instance token from dedupe key. Will run integration test. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8942
2026-03-11 02:05 - Support (Maya Chen): Applied edge prefetch concurrency limit on affected pool as temporary mitigation. Customer reported lower 504s in next window.
2026-03-12 18:40 - Eng (Ethan Blake): Patch merged and backported. Canary scheduled for 2026-03-13. Assigned postmortem and follow-ups. Customer notified and will keep session-affinity enabled until full rollout.
2026-03-12 19:00 - Customer (Noteable Analytics, Alex Rivera): Confirming canary window acceptable; appreciates temporary mitigation. Will report results after overnight runs.
Fix deployed to canary; mitigation applied (prefetch concurrency limit + customer session-affinity). Awaiting canary metrics and full rollout. Postmortem and runbook updates pending.
Enable session-affinity for the dedicated pool; limit client parallel replays to <50 concurrent streams; temporary prefetch concurrency cap applied by Support.
Monitor canary for 48 hours; if stable, promote patch to all dedicated pools in us-east-1 and then global. Complete postmortem and add dedupe metrics to dashboards.
payload.summary: Hot-turn prefetch fanout causes cache missstorm and intermittent request timeouts for replayed conversational turns

Issue summary: Customer reporting gradual increase in first-byte latency (TTFB) over the lifetime of long streaming sessions. Problem does not manifest as immediate 5xx, but responsiveness for subsequent tokens drifts from ~120ms to 1.2s after ~90s of continuous streaming.

Impact: Enterprise customer (NovaChat) reports degraded UX for multi-turn assistant sessions where responses slow down mid-completion. Affects production traffic in us-east region. Customer is on enterprise plan and has SLA expectations.

Environment: Production, us-east, traffic via HTTP/2 multiplexed connections through our API Gateway -> ALB -> serving runtime. Observed with both rwd-gpt-7b-v1 and open-gpt-3.5-like model endpoints.

Observed behavior: TTFB slowly increases during a single, long streaming request; streaming session remains open (no connection reset) but data arrives in sparser chunks. Not a hard timeout or 5xx, more of a degradation that correlates with header/meta growth and number of concurrent streams on the client connection.

Expected behavior: Stable TTFB across the duration of a streaming request (within SLO bounds), no gradual drift and consistent token delivery cadence.
1) Create a long-running streaming request against the /v1/chat/stream endpoint pinning rwd-gpt-7b-v1 with max_tokens=2048 and low-temperature sampling.
2) Use an HTTP/2 capable client that multiplexes multiple streams (e.g., curl with --http2 or a browser-based multiplexer) and include a rotating trace cookie every 10s to emulate instrumentation headers growing over time.
3) Observe TTFB for the first 30s, then continue streaming for 90-120s and record token arrival intervals.
4) Repeat with a single-stream connection (no multiplexing) as control and compare TTFB drift.
2026-03-10T14:22:11Z api-gateway WARN upstream_write_delay stream_id=9 write_wait_ms=1300 headers_size=2048
2026-03-10T14:22:12Z alb INFO connection_coalesce flush_deferred=true queued_bytes=8192
2026-03-10T14:23:45Z serving-runtime DEBUG kv_cache_warmup duration_ms=45 request_id=8f7a2c
sample_trace: https://observability.redwood/s/trace/8f7a2c-ttfb-drift (redacted)
Initial correlation: drift aligns with (a) HTTP/2 stream density on the client connection and (b) gradual metadata/header growth from instrumentation cookie rotation. We reproduced in staging by running a stress client that opens 4 multiplexed streams and injects ~300B of extra cookie data every 15s.

Observed that API Gateway begins to coalesce small writes and delay flushes as outbound buffer grows; ALB reports 'flush_deferred' and write_wait_ms in logs. Serving runtime's token generation time remains stable (per internal telemetry), pointing to a network/proxy buffering effect rather than model compute.

We validated with tcpdump on a repro node: server sends small chunks but proxy delays outbound frames until a coalesce threshold is hit, increasing inter-chunk latency. This matches customer symptoms (no resets, gradual sparsity).
Proxy-level write coalescing + HTTP/2 multiplexing + header/meta growth causes outbound flushes to be delayed, effectively increasing time between small data frames and producing TTFB drift. Likely influenced by proxy buffer watermarks and aggressive coalescing for small writes under high stream density. Another contributing factor: ALB idle/send timeouts and HTTP/2 flow-control interactions when multiple streams share a connection.
Short-term: Advise customer to (a) reduce instrumentation cookie rotation frequency so headers stop growing mid-request, or (b) use separate connections per long-running stream (disables multiplexing), or (c) reduce concurrent multiplexed streams per HTTP/2 connection.

We provided a sample cURL invocation that forces a new connection per request and asked customer to validate: curl --http2-prior-knowledge --no-keepalive ...
Triage ongoing. Engineering (SRE and Gateway) engaged to tune proxy flush thresholds and investigate ALB HTTP/2 flow-control interplay. No permanent fix deployed yet; customer notified of workarounds and initial mitigations. Follow-up PR created to add diagnostic metrics to gateway showing per-connection buffered_bytes and coalescing_delay.
payload.summary: Sustained TTFB drift on long-running HTTP/2 sessions caused by proxy flush delay and stream multiplexing

Issue summary:
HeliosAI is reporting repeated p99 latency spikes and request queuing in their dedicated GPU pool that coincide with a daily scheduled batch window (12:00-12:30 PDT). Symptoms look like ephemeral GPU oversubscription and batch slot thrashing rather than model regression.

Impact:
- Customer reports increased p99 generation latency from ~400ms to >3s during scheduled window.
- Failed requests (5xx) are low but queued latency causes timeouts for streaming clients.
- Business impact: degraded user experience for HeliosAI production customers during a predictable 30-minute window.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: helios-dedicated-pool-3 (5 x A100:80GB equivalent nodes)
- Region: us-west-2
- Models: gptx-24b-v2 (primary), embedx-1024 (background embedding jobs)

Timeline (customer-supplied):
- 2026-03-11 19:00 UTC: First report of tail latency during scheduled batch run.
- 2026-03-12 19:25 UTC: Customer escalated after repeated occurrences over two days.

Observed behavior:
- Sustained queue growth during 12:00-12:30 PDT each day.
- Autoscaler shows transient spike in pending pods/slots that are not immediately reconciled.
- GPU utilization reports show per-GPU average ~70% but per-tenant slot contention and bursty kernel launches.
- KV cache growth for gptx-24b-v2 correlates to an increase in memory pressure on a subset of nodes.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should provision capacity ahead of steady scheduled load or apply predictive headroom to avoid p99 spikes.
- No single tenant should cause transient oversubscription of GPU batching lanes in a dedicated pool.

Workaround attempted by customer:
- Staggered batch start times (reduced but did not eliminate spikes).
- Reduced concurrency per client which lowered p99 but increased overall run time for batch job.

Additional notes:
- This is not a global capacity shortage; other dedicated pools in us-west-2 are unaffected.
- Appears related to tenant-level workload pattern (short, high-concurrency embedding bursts mixed with long-generation sessions).
1) Customer schedules concurrent embedding job burst at 12:00 PDT targeting embedx-1024 with high concurrency.
2) At same time, several long-running streaming generation sessions to gptx-24b-v2 remain warm.
3) Observe autoscaler activity (pending slots, allocation latency) and request queue growth in dedicated pool helios-dedicated-pool-3.
4) Check p99 latency and GPU kernel launch patterns during window.
