Issue summary: PilotDocs reports that when their product embeds a Redwood dashboard panel (iframe) with the panel auto-refresh enabled, tracehook links generated by the widget intermittently redirect to the customer's org root (/org/<org-id>/console) instead of preserving the trace anchor parameters (trace_id, start_ts). Impact: opening a trace link from an embedded panel often results in a missing trace context or a 404; users see the console but without the expected trace or timeline.

Impact: Customer-facing debugging workflows are interrupted; PilotDocs engineers cannot jump from an alert or dashboard row to the specific trace (high frequency during their morning dashboards). Several teams reported inability to investigate incidents originating from PilotDocs' embedded dashboards which is blocking release.

Environment: Production (us-east) — PilotDocs uses an iframe embed with our standard embed token + auto-refresh interval of 30s. Occurs across Chrome and Safari. Affects only embedded views; native console links open correctly.

Observed since: 2026-03-09 09:00 UTC. Volume: PilotDocs reports ~12% of tracehook clicks from embeds failing; our internal analytics show a matching jump in 302/redirect responses for the embed-proxy service for their org.

Expected behavior: Tracehook links opened from embedded panels should forward to the console with the full trace anchor preserved, opening the trace view (console/trace/<trace_id>) and maintaining time bounds.

Actual behavior: Users are redirected to org root or to an auth landing page where trace parameters are stripped or not processed, requiring manual search.

Additional notes: PilotDocs upgraded to the embed SDK v2.1.1 last week; they also rotated an embed token on 2026-03-08 which may be correlated.
Customer embeds a Redwood dashboard panel in an iframe with auto-refresh enabled (interval 30s)
Open the embedded page in a fresh browser session (incognito reproducible)
Trigger a dashboard row drilldown that generates a tracehook link (click trace link icon)
Observe the navigation target: sometimes lands on /org/<org-id>/console (no trace loaded) or an auth prompt; expected: console/trace/<trace-id> with trace loaded
Repeat until failure manifests (in customer cases ~1 in 8 clicks)
2026-03-09T09:14:21Z embed-proxy[pid=2234] INFO forwarding request /embed/redirect?trace_id=abcd1234 -> 302 /org/abc123/console
2026-03-09T09:14:21Z console[pid=1102] WARN missing query params: trace_id not found for request /org/abc123/console
2026-03-09T09:14:22Z auth[pid=900] DEBUG token_lookup: embed_token=rotated-2026-03-08 (PilotDocs) matched, session cookie not present

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 — PilotDocs (Customer via CS): We see the issue on users in EMEA as well but much less frequent; happy to provide a short-screen recording of failing clicks and the embed configuration. We rotated tokens last Tuesday and upgraded SDK on Thursday.
2026-03-12 — Product (Nora Li): Noted a recent change in embed SDK v2.1.1 that changed redirect type; assigned to frontend team to review. Creating follow-up engineering ticket for SDK fix and server-side fallback.
Checked embed-proxy codepath: when we receive /embed/redirect with fragment-only anchor (#trace=...), current code issues a 302 to /org/<org>/console (fragment not forwarded by browsers on 302).
Reproduced locally by constructing redirect with fragment in Location header — confirmed browsers drop fragment on 302. 307 preserves fragment in some cases but not reliable across proxies.
PilotDocs embed SDK v2.1.1 constructs links with fragment instead of query param due to a change in SDK anchor construction (commit 9f3b2a1).
Temporary mitigation considered: rewrite embed-proxy to convert fragment into query parameter server-side and issue direct 200 with meta refresh or an HTML page that executes a client-side redirect preserving fragment.
Workaround provided to customer: change embed SDK to build trace links using query params (trace_id=<id>&start_ts=<ts>) instead of fragment, or disable auto-refresh until fix is released.
Short-term fix (in progress): update embed-proxy to return an HTML relay page (200) that does client-side window.location = targetWithHash so browser preserves fragment — patch in review (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4567).
Long-term fix: revert SDK behavior to construct trace links as query params OR update proxy to consistently translate fragments to query params and use 307/HTML relay as appropriate. Frontend and SDK teams assigned; target patch release 2026-03-18.
Follow-ups: Add an automated test in embed-sdk that verifies redirect semantics across common browsers; schedule runbook update describing embed token rotation impact and how to validate tracehooks post-rotation.

Issue summary:
Customer BrightRetail observed repeated streaming cancellations and request timeouts starting 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC. Affected requests show unusually long TLS handshake durations (~2.5-6s) prior to application-level token exchange, causing client SDKs to cancel after 3s. The problem appears correlated with egress routing shifts where a small percentage of connections are routed across regions rather than to the account's pinned local egress pool.

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints experiencing elevated p95/p99 latency for streaming API calls.
- Customer reports ~6% of requests for their production key are aborted by the client due to handshake/tcp timeout.
- Business impact: degraded chat experiences and user-visible timeouts for BrightRetail storefront search assistants.

Environment:
- Customer: BrightRetail Inc. (dedicated pool, us-west primary)
- Platform: hosted Redwood API (prod)
- Affected routes: /v1/streams/generate and /v1/chat/stream
- Time window: first observed 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC, ongoing as of update.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Issue occurs on first request after connection idle or session cache miss.
2) Client initiates streaming request to us-west endpoint; server logs show egress selection to us-east for ~6% of fresh connections.
3) TLS handshake duration recorded as 2500-6000ms in edge-proxy metrics.
4) Client SDK cancels at ~3000ms, generating client-side cancel and no downstream tokens returned.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Edge-proxy TLS handshake histogram: p50 ~45ms, p95 ~260ms, p99 ~3100ms during window.
- Routing logs: route decision for affected keys shows fallback to remote-pop due to transient affinity tag mismatch.
- Connection traces: new sessions include missing session-id header leading to allocation from warm pool in us-east.
- Error patterns: client-side cancel + server write timeout followed by a short-lived connection reset.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Session affinity tags occasionally not preserved by upstream gateway under burst conditions, causing a small fraction of fresh connections to be routed to a non-local egress pool (cross-region). Cold TLS handshakes on these remote pools are significantly slower due to lack of warm TLS session cache and additional network RTT.
- Hypothesis 2: Edge-proxy warm pool eviction policy combined with NAT SNAT rotation results in different downstream 5-tuple, invalidating L4 affinity for a subset of connections.
- Metrics correlating egress-affinity flips with p99 handshake spikes: confirmed timestamps match customer reports.
- Captured packet-level pcap (redacted) shows TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello delay of ~2.8s for affected sessions.
- No config change recorded in the control plane for BrightRetail during incident window.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Engineering toggled strictly-local-egress routing rule for BrightRetail on 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC which reduced affected requests from 6% to ~0.3% in the following 6 hours.
- Increased edge-proxy TLS session cache TTL for the customer's egress pool to retain sessions across brief warm-pool churn (safe, short-term change).

Workaround for customer:
- Advise SDKs to increase client-side stream timeout to 6s during ongoing mitigation window to avoid client cancels (BrightRetail accepted temporary change).
- Recommend keepalive to reduce cold-connection rate.

Next steps / action items:
1) SRE: instrument detailed affinity tag propagation at the L4 proxy to capture missing headers and identify where tag removal occurs (assigned INT-7112).
2) Infra: audit warm-pool eviction thresholds; consider pre-warming remote egress for high-tier dedicated customers.
3) Networking: review SNAT churn and NAT table rotation that could be affecting L4 affinity.
4) Product: evaluate permanent local-egress enforcement option for dedicated customers to prevent cross-region cold-handshake regressions.
5) Postmortem: capture timeline and metric deltas; propose long-term fix and rolling deploy schedule.

Resolution notes (temporary):
- Local-egress enforcement and TTL increase applied as mitigations. Monitoring shows p99 handshake times returned to baseline for the majority of traffic. Longer-term fixes pending investigation.

2026-03-10 01:02 UTC - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reported intermittent streaming cancels; attached SDK logs and sample request IDs. Escalating to SRE due to cross-region routing evidence.
2026-03-10 02:15 UTC - SRE (Ethan Morales): Confirmed handshake p99 spike in edge-proxy metrics for BrightRetail key. Suspect affinity misassignment; temporarily enabled local-egress enforcement for account to reduce impact.
2026-03-10 05:20 UTC - Customer (BrightRetail Ops - Jordan Patel): Thanks for the quick mitigation. We'll extend client timeouts as you suggested. Please keep us posted on root cause.
2026-03-11 09:40 UTC - Infra (Priya Narang): Investigating warm-pool eviction logs; seeing correlated churn around 22:30-23:00 UTC. Opening internal ticket INT-7112 to trace SNAT rotation and pool assignment.
2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - SRE (Ethan Morales): Applied TLS session cache TTL bump and validated reduced incidence. Next: full affinity propagation traces scheduled for 2026-03-13. Updating ticket with progress; marking as In Progress.
payload.summary: Unexpected egress affinity shift causing cold TLS handshakes and streaming cancels for BrightRetail

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported that scheduled batch workers started receiving 403 Authorization errors this morning (2026-03-09) after their LDAP team rolled out a config change. The change was to the LDAP subtree filter quoting/escaping behavior used by their directory (they switched to a stricter escaping mode to mitigate LDAP injection vectors).

Impact:
- Multiple scheduled consumers (batch ingestion and nightly embeding jobs) are failing to authenticate/authorize and remain in backoff.
- Customer reports 428 failed job attempts in the last 6 hours; business impact: delayed reports for end users and queued message backlog.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) on Redwood Private release 1.14.1
- Identity proxy (sidecar) version: 1.14.1 (customer-managed image)
- LDAP connector: configured to evaluate group membership via subtree filter (memberOf and nested groups)
- Affected services: scheduled-workers service account + service-token exchange flow

Steps to reproduce (as observed by customer):
1) Customer triggered a scheduled job from their queue (same code that ran ok prior to LDAP change).
2) Worker performs service account token exchange with Redwood private control plane.
3) Identity proxy issues LDAP query to check group membership using configured subtree filter.
4) LDAP returns matches, but the identity-proxy logs show a zero-length group attribute (after parsing).
5) RBAC evaluation returns no matched roles and the request is denied with 403.

Observed behavior:
- Identity-proxy log excerpt shows the LDAP filter being rewritten and special characters being escaped; the returned LDAP attribute (memberOf) appears present in raw LDAP payload but is dropped during attribute normalization.
- Access logs show 403 for scheduled-worker requests.
- Cache warmup attempts for group membership do not populate roles.

Expected behavior:
- Identity proxy should correctly parse LDAP responses even when the directory switches to stricter subtree filter escaping. Group attributes should be normalized consistently and mapped to RBAC role bindings.

Relevant logs/snippets (redacted):
- identity-proxy: "ldap_query=(&(objectClass=person)(memberOf=CN=Data-Processors,OU=workers,DC=corp,DC=fin))"
- identity-proxy debug: "raw_ldap_attrs=[\"memberOf:\\"CN=Data-Processors,OU=workers,DC=corp,DC=fin\\\"\"] -> normalized=[]"
- scheduled-workers: "authorization denied: no roles matched"

Notes: Customer confirms the only change at their end was toggling the LDAP subtree filter escaping flag on their AD proxy appliance. No changes to service tokens or RBAC mappings were made on Redwood side.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 14:22 - FinReports (Customer): Provided LDAP server-side trace and config diff (switched 'strict-escape' on for subtree matching). Confirmed bulk run fails for service account only; console login still works for human users.
2026-03-12 10:15 - Support (Maya Patel): Deployed hotfix image identity-proxy:1.14.2 to customer's private control plane candidate node. Asked customer to validate scheduled workers after restart.
2026-03-12 12:03 - FinReports (Customer): Confirmed scheduled workers resumed and authorization errors dropped to zero after restart. Customer will monitor overnight and report any regressions.
Summary of findings:
- The AD proxy change introduced additional backslash escaping around multi-valued DN attributes. The existing attribute normalization code in identity-proxy treated the backslashes as part of the attribute value and then applied csv-splitting which removed the element entirely (edge-case when commas are escaped inside quotes).
- Reproduced locally by running OpenLDAP test server with 'strict-escape' behavior; identity-proxy returned empty normalized group list triggering RBAC deny path.
- Root cause: brittle attribute unescape + CSV-splitting logic that did not account for escaped commas inside quoted DN strings.
Mitigation path considered:
1) Customer side: revert LDAP escaping change (not desirable long-term).
2) Immediate Redwood hotfix: make unescape routine tolerant of quoted DN and preserve escaped commas until full DN parse; release identity-proxy 1.14.2 with tests.
3) Long-term: add integration test covering AD variations and add telemetry to detect empty-role-cache events for scheduled workers.
Action taken:
- Implemented identity-proxy patch to handle quoted DN unescape and updated unit tests (PR #1428).
Workaround and fix deployed:
- Hotfix image identity-proxy:1.14.2 built and pushed to customer's private registry.
- Deployed to candidate then to primary node during low-traffic window (2026-03-12 09:30).
- Customer restarted scheduled-worker cluster; authorization errors ceased and jobs resumed processing.
Follow-up items:
- Ops: add integration test in CI to exercise AD quoted DN and escaped comma cases (ticket INT-2201).
- Engineering: add metric 'role_cache_empty_events' and an alert threshold for scheduled-workers (ticket INT-2202).
- Support: confirm overnight stability with customer and close after 24h without regressions.
Status: fix applied and customer validated post-deploy. Monitoring ongoing.
payload.summary: Scheduled batch workers 403 after customer LDAP change to subtree filter escaping in private deployment

Issue summary:
Customer (ChatWrite Inc., dedicated) reports reproducible loss of final paragraph and duplicated prefix tokens when their mobile web client goes to background (Wi‑Fi sleep) and then resumes. The SSE connection experiences a half‑close while the client OS suspends sockets; upon reconnect the resumed stream is missing the final epilogue and the beginning tokens are replayed/duplicated.

Impact:
- Several production users see truncated outputs (missing final sentence or closing paragraph) in ~0.8% of streaming responses from the redwood/gptx-16k-v1 model in us-east-1.
- Customer's chat UX shows repeated initial fragment plus truncated ending, causing poor UX and increased retries.
- Affects mobile web users on iOS/Android when devices suspend background network sockets.

Environment:
- Cluster: prod-us-east (api-gateway + managed serving-runtime pool, dedicated capacity for ChatWrite namespace)
- Model: redwood/gptx-16k-v1 pinned by customer
- Client: ChatWrite web app using Redwood JS SDK v0.9.3 (SSE mode).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a streaming chat completion on mobile web (iOS Safari / Android Chrome) using SSE endpoint with a ~1k token response.
2) Put the phone into background for ~15–30s (device enters low‑power Wi‑Fi state).
3) Bring the app back to foreground; client reconnects to SSE and attempts resume via existing conversation id/last_event_id.
4) Observe: beginning of the response is duplicated (replayed prefix) and the final paragraph / concluding sentence is missing.

Observed behavior:
- On resume the client receives the same prefix tokens it had before suspension, then the stream ends without an explicit end event.
- Server logs show an upstream half‑close/h1 204 from the LB at approximately the suspend time and no explicit 'end_choice' event emitted for affected responses.
- Resume attempt includes last_event_id but resume sequence numbers don't align with server's half‑closed state, leading to a silent termination rather than a reissue of the missing tail.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should either stitch missing suffix correctly or return a clear terminal event (end_of_stream/choice_end) so client can surface a deterministic error and/or request a retry.

Logs / artifacts attached (references):
- Customer trace id: cw-trace-20260313-8421 (provided)
- Sample server logs (trimmed): logs/prod/us-east/serving-runtime/2026-03-13/trace-cw-8421.log (S3 link in ticket).
- LB probe & connection events: lb-us-east-probes-2026-03-13.log (S3 link).
- Client network capture (customer): ChatWrite_capture_2026-03-13.pcap (attached).

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Increase client reconnection backoff and enable client-side deduplication based on incremental token sequence if using SDK v0.9.3 (we provided a small snippet).
- If possible, switch to websocket streaming (WS) which does a full rehandshake and avoids the LB half‑close race in most cases.

Investigation notes (SRE/Support):
- Reproduced internally using an emulator that simulates TCP socket close on background suspend. Observed the same pattern: LB (haproxy fronting) sends a half‑close health probe/idle reset, upstream serving runtime finishes streaming but never emits the final end event due to a race with socket closure handling.
- Hypothesis: When the client socket is suspended the LB/edge treats the connection as idle and tethers a probe that triggers a graceful half‑close on the fronting connection. The serving runtime, upon detecting the half‑close, winds down the in‑flight response path without emitting the final JSON terminal frame (end_choice). The resume path attempts to replay from a last_event_id anchored to the prior session; however the server's per‑session resume state has been purged or advanced so server responds with a short reissue that doesn't include the missing epilogue.
- Evidence: correlating timestamps between lb log (probe reset at 15:02:12), serving-runtime partial stream completion (15:02:12.123), and client reconnect (15:02:42) shows the missing end event window.
- Similar patterns seen in INT-4382 (internal LB idle timeout tests) and a small subset of customer reports.

Temporary mitigation implemented (SRE):
- Adjusted haproxy idle_probe window on a subset of fronting nodes for ChatWrite dedicated capacity to 45s (previously 15s) as a canary.
- Patch queued for serving-runtime (PR referenced) to ensure explicit end_of_choice emission even on upstream half‑close; will also persist a short resume buffer to allow correct stitching when clients reconnect within 60s.

Action plan / next steps:
1) Roll out haproxy probe window change to all nodes for ChatWrite namespace (SRE), target 2026-03-15 04:00 UTC. (owner: Daniel Kim)
2) Merge PR in serving-runtime that forces terminal event emission on half‑close and adds a 60s ephemeral resume buffer for recently closed sessions. Test plan: unit tests + canary in staging + canary in prod. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2187 (owner: eng/sam-chen). Target: 2026-03-18.
3) SDK: publish guidance and a small dedupe helper in SDK v0.9.4 that identifies duplicate prefixes based on incremental token sequence ids. (owner: DevX / Priya Rao). Target: 2026-03-16.
4) Post‑mortem decision: evaluate increasing default probe windows for mobile‑heavy customer lanes and implement streaming end markers in protocol docs. (owner: SRE/Product).

Resolution notes (planned):
- Short term: LB probe window increased for ChatWrite (partial canary active). Customer verified reduction in reproduce rate in test sessions.
- Medium term: runtime patch to emit terminal events + resume buffer (pending PR merge and canary).

Customer communication plan:
- Notified customer on 2026-03-13 of an SRE canary and workaround. Will follow up with an engineering postmortem after full rollout and testing.

Support (Aisha): Logged initial report and requested pcap + server traces from customer. Escalated to SRE due to suspected LB/server race.
Customer (ChatWrite Ops): Provided pcap and server trace id cw-trace-20260313-8421; reports issue seen in ~0.8% of streams during peak mobile usage.
SRE (Daniel): Reproduced locally with socket suspension emulator; temporarily increased haproxy probe window to 45s on canary nodes. Observed lower reproduce rate on canary.
Eng (Sam Chen): Opened PR to ensure terminal frame emission on half‑close and to buffer resume metadata for 60s. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2187
Support (Aisha): Shared SDK dedupe snippet with customer and recommended WS fallback for critical sessions. Customer will test and report back by 2026-03-15.
payload.summary: Mobile Wi‑Fi suspend causes SSE half‑close: final paragraph missing on resume, client sees duplicate prefix tokens

Issue summary:
SoraAnalytics reports intermittent 429s for interactive chat endpoints during their nightly background telemetry sweep (low-volume healthcheck + probe jobs). The probes are light (single small request every 10s per host) but when the telemetry sweep runs across hundreds of workers it appears to push the tenant over a short-window burst and interactive chat calls receive 429s.

Impact:
- ~15% of interactive requests from SoraAnalytics in prod-us-west returning 429s during their nightly sweep window (23:30–00:15 PST).
- Customer-facing application shows degraded UX (stalling and retries).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool, prod-us-west, tenant id: t-sora-019 (provided on secure channel).
- Traffic mix: 70% interactive chat, 20% small background probes, 10% bulk embeddings (off-peak).

Observed behavior:
1) Between 23:30 and 00:15 the console shows tenant token bucket near 100% and short bursts of 429s correlate with telemetry sweep start.
2) Console quota readout refreshes to new credits but 429s continue for ~2–3 minutes after refill.
3) Throttle headers in responses show X-RateLimit-Remaining near 0 and Retry-After sometimes 3–7 seconds.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Deploy 150 small probe workers scheduled to run a lightweight status ping every 10s (each ping ~20 tokens).
2) Start probes simultaneously (they run a coordinated sweep).
3) Trigger an interactive chat request to the same tenant during the sweep.
4) Observe 429 or increased latency and retry cycles.

Logs / traces:
- Provided trace ids in secure attachment: trace-prod-usw-20260301-01z (corresponding to 23:34 PST spike).
- Console shot shows token bucket drop and then CLI credit refresh at 23:36:10 but 429 spikes until 23:38:30.

Temporary mitigation requested:
- Guidance on configuration best-practices to keep background probes from eating interactive burst credits.
- If possible, short-term recommendation we can apply to tenant-level config in Dedicated to prevent immediate customer impact.

Notes about what customer already tried:
- Staggering probe start times to a 60s jitter reduced peak but did not eliminate 429s.
- They attempted to reduce probe frequency from 10s to 30s and saw lower 429s but still persistent.

Support (2026-03-01): Thanks for the detailed reproduction steps and traces — we've escalated to SRE for quota accounting review. Can you confirm how many distinct host IPs the probes originate from?
Customer (2026-03-01): Probes originate from ~120 ephemeral hosts (k8s job), NATed behind a small pool of 10 egress IPs. We also sent a HAR with throttle headers attached.
SRE (2026-03-02): Hypothesis: healthchecks/probes are being charged to the same tenant burst pool and the simultaneous start creates a microburst that exhausts the short-window refill. We'll look at refill timing and edge vs origin accounting.
Support (2026-03-02): Temporary action: Recommend enabling a split-burst pool (if available) for background jobs or configuring probe clients to add an explicit header to mark probe traffic for a lower-priority class. Customer asked how to do this on their side and whether Redwood can set a tenant-level exemption.
Customer (2026-03-03): Can you confirm whether enabling 'longpoll-exemption' or allocating an isolated burst lane for their probes will require a Dedicated config change or code change on their side?
03-02-2026: Downloaded trace-prod-usw-20260301-01z. Observed ~120 concurrent connections within 30s window, each ~20 tokens; aggregate consumed ~2400 tokens in <60s. Tenant short-window burst budget was set to 2000 tokens -> exhausted. Refill aligned to :00 and :30 seconds (window length 30s).
03-02-2026: Edge counting shows preflight and healthcheck pings counted on edge in addition to origin accounting due to proxy keepalive reuse; possible double-counting for HTTP/2 multiplexed connections. Need to verify per-connection vs per-request accounting in proxy config.
03-03-2026: Confirmed console shows credit refill but request queueing/backpressure results in delayed clearance; clients retry amplifies token consumption in the following window.
Hypothesis: Two contributing factors - (1) coordinated simultaneous probe start causing a true microburst that overwhelms short-window refill, (2) proxy/keepalive behavior causing additional token accounting (duplicate counts) for multiplexed probe hosts.

Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout that should have preserved model-version pinning for a subset of NorthBridge Media tenants, a synchronization mismatch between the rollout epoch recorded by the control-plane orchestrator and the edge-proxy cohort table led to intermittent traffic being split across two model variants. Impact: ~3-5% of the customer's requests received responses from an unintended variant, producing observable quality regressions in the customer's production evaluation set and a small number of API signature mismatches for structured outputs. This occurred during a low-traffic window but affected production user-facing inference for a small cohort.

Observed behavior: Some sessions that were expected to remain pinned to the older model variant were routed to the new canary variant for several minutes before failing back. The routing decision logs show inconsistent epoch IDs between the orchestrator snapshot and the edge in-memory cohort map. No GPU exhaustion or autoscaler events were observed.

Expected behavior: Cohort epoch values should be atomically advanced across the control plane and all edge instances so that pinned sessions retain affinity unless an intentional reassign/eviction occurs.

1) Initiate a staged canary rollout with cohort weighting (10% canary) and model version pinning enabled for tenant namespace NB-*/priority routes.
2) Allow the orchestrator to publish epoch=E+1 snapshot and confirm push succeeded to config service.
3) Trigger a controlled connection shuffle at the edge by restarting a subset of edge-proxies in us-east for routine maintenance.
4) Observe session routing for pinned tenants during the 2-10 minute window after edge restart; compare orchestrator epoch vs edge cohort epoch and inspect model variant assignments.
5) Reproduce by toggling the deploy with a small canary weight and repeating edge restart to surface the mismatch consistently.
Initial hypothesis: edge local cache TTL allowed a stale epoch to persist across an edge restart, causing temporary divergence in routing decisions.
Found that config push to CDN cache layer recorded success but edge instances pulling from CDN occasionally returned 304 with stale cache due to GC race in the CDN edge cache layer (region us-east).
Edge restart timing with in-flight session handoffs exposed a race between session-store lease renewal and cohort epoch reconcile path, allowing a short window where session affinity rules were evaluated against outdated epoch metadata.
No evidence of autoscaler or GPU preemption; serving-runtime metrics normal. Tokenization and output parsing errors correlate with model mismatch rather than model corruption.
Reproduced locally by simulating delayed snapshot propagation (delay ~6s) plus immediate edge restart; variant-splitting reproduced deterministically under those timings.

Issue summary:
Customer on private deployment reports that after SAML assertion exchange several API calls and console actions return 403 Forbidden for users who should have access. The IdP (Okta) emits a roles attribute with multiple values in a single comma-separated string. The on-prem SSO connector appears to treat the entire comma-separated value as a single role label, so RBAC role mapping fails and the user is unauthorized.

Impact:
- Multiple users in FinEdge cannot perform model deployments or view logs via the Redwood Console; API calls from their backend services are also returning 403 when using the SSO-backed session tokens.
- Business impact: blocked deployments and customer-visible service degradation for internal apps; customer classified as private (compliance-sensitive).

Environment:
- Redwood Private (v1.9.3) deployed in customer VPC (us-west-2) using customer-managed control plane.
- SSO provider: Okta (SAML 2.0).
- Connector: sso-connector v2.4.1 (deployed as part of private package).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) User authenticates via SAML to the console using Okta.
2) IdP assertion includes attribute `roles` with value: "admin,platform:deploy" (single attribute value containing comma).
3) User completes login and receives session; attempts to call /v1/models (or use console Deploy button) and receives 403.

Observed behavior:
- Connector logs show mapped_roles = ["admin,platform:deploy"] (single element).
- RBAC engine tries to match exact role labels and fails to find "platform:deploy" so denies access.
- No error in SAML handshake; issue arises only at role parsing stage.

Expected behavior:
- Connector should split multi-valued role attributes into multiple entries (CSV or multi-valued attributes) and map each to Redwood RBAC roles.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- In Okta, add an attribute transformation rule to emit two separate attributes (roles and roles_split) or make roles multi-valued instead of comma-separated; OR
- Create a console-level group mapping that maps the full comma string to a role (less desirable).

Investigation notes (internal):
- Initial triage: confirmed with customer SAML assertion. Verified that Okta was sending a single attribute with comma-delimited content (saml payload attached by customer to ticket).
- Connector behavior: sso-connector v2.4.1 reads attribute values and only treats repeated attributes as arrays; it does not parse delimiter-separated values.
- Recent change: a parsing refactor in sso-connector PR #395 (released in 2.4.0) removed implicit CSV splitting to avoid false positives; this resulted in stricter behavior in private deployments. Hosted Redwood previously applied a claim-normalizer layer which handled CSV. Private deployments rely solely on local connector behavior.
- Reproducible in staging: deployed sso-connector v2.4.1 in test private cluster and reproduced 403s using a crafted assertion.

Logs/highlights (sanitized):
- connector auth debug: "received attribute roles: \"admin,platform:deploy\""
- rbac match debug: "looking up role \"admin,platform:deploy\" -> not found"
- console audit: "user X attempted /deploy -> 403 -> missing role 'platform:deploy'"

Preliminary root cause hypothesis:
- Behavioral change from claim-normalizer removal combined with IdP emitting CSV in a single attribute leads to mismatch between expected multi-valued claims and actual attribute format.

Action items / next steps:
1) Short-term patch: add CSV-splitting logic back as a configurable toggle in sso-connector (PR in progress). Owner: Marco Delgado. ETA for patch: 2026-03-13.
2) Long-term: update private deployment docs and quickstart for Okta to include explicit guidance on multi-valued attributes vs. CSV and provide example transformation rules. Owner: Developer Experience.
3) Provide customer with a scripted Okta transformation or temporary group mapping steps. Owner: Support (Aisha).
4) Coordinate a minor private package release (v1.9.4) with patched connector and rollout notes. Owner: Release Engineering.

Customer communication summary:
- Informed customer of workaround (attribute transform) and that we are preparing a connector patch. Customer accepted workaround to unblock immediate operations and prefers a connector toggle in the next private release so they do not have to change IdP rules across many users.

Resolution notes (pending):
- Targeting backport of CSV splitting as opt-in flag; full resolution will be marked once package v1.9.4 is released and deployed to FinEdge environment.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 08:20 - Customer (FinEdge SRE): Thanks — would prefer connector toggle. Please advise ETA for private package release.

Issue summary: BrightCart reports a spike of 429s starting 2026-03-09 17:00 UTC during nightly bulk-embed flushes. The requests are bulk ingestion jobs that should be treated as background/low-priority, but the ingress appears to classify them as low-latency interactive traffic and they hit a tight per-route concurrency window. Impact: ~35% failed batch shards (429s) for the BrightCart dedicated pool for ~45 minutes; downstream retry loops amplified the pattern.

Observed at: prod (us-east) dedicated pool for BrightCart; many requests originate from a long-running ingest worker that issues multiplexed /v1/embeds/bulk calls with chunked payloads and a custom header X-BC-JobId.
Customer ingest pipeline experiencing partial failure (35% shard failures) for nightly index updates; retries caused delays and invoiceable errors. Not a full outage but customer SLA for bulk ingest throughput violated.
1) In BrightCart staging/dedicated mimic: spawn 200 concurrent workers performing multiplexed chunked POST to /v1/embeds/bulk with Content-Type: multipart/form-data and X-Client-Job: bulk-flush
2) Set per-worker short timeout/fast retry loop (1s backoff) to surface early 429s
3) Observe rate-limiter accounting: per-route token window for "interactive" lane drops to zero and returns 429
4) Compare requests when header X-Redwood-Traffic-Class: background is set -> no 429s; when header missing -> 429s reproduced
Requests for the same job are alternately accepted or rejected depending on a normalized route key lookup. In many cases the route used for accounting is the interactive path (/v1/chat/completions) because the gateway normalization step failed for multipart bulk embeds; this causes them to consume from a small low-latency concurrency bucket and return 429s.
Bulk-embed flushes should be classified automatically into the background/bulk quota pool based on path pattern or explicit X-Redwood-Traffic-Class header; they should not be counted against short-lived interactive concurrency windows and should tolerate higher burst without early 429s.
Initial hypothesis: rate-limiter atomic key computed from canonicalized route ID. Edge proxy change in v1.14.2 introduced a path-normalization regression: multipart requests with Content-Type multipart/form-data lost the request.path suffix during header rewrite, producing an empty route match and falling back to default route id -> mapped to 'interactive' lane. Evidence: request traces in zipkin show route_id: 'interactive-v1' for bulk embeds between 2026-03-09 17:01 and 17:45.

Telemetry: rate-limiter logs show a spike in per-route token-exhaustion events (window_exhausted) matching BrightCart tenant_id. Heap of retries from orchestrator increased queue depth by 3x.

Reproduction in staging: toggling header X-Redwood-Traffic-Class allowed bypass; canonicalizing request.path in proxy removed the regression locally and eliminated 429s.

Related: this intersects with priority-routing changes rolled out 2026-03-08 (edge proxy v1.14.2) – see PR #4321 and the rollout notes.

[2026-03-09T17:02:12Z] tenant=brightcart tid=tb-11 decision=reject status=429 reason=per_route_window_exhausted request_path=/v1/embeds/bulk content_type= multipart/form-data
[2026-03-09T17:02:12Z] gateway=edge-12 proxy=v1.14.2 path_normalized=FALSE computed_route='' fallback_route=interactive-v1
Support (Aisha): Customer first reported 2026-03-09 18:10 UTC. Provided sample request IDs and timeframe. Asked for logs and tenant/lb mappings.
SRE (Diego): Reproduced in staging; observed path normalization regression in edge proxy. Temporary mitigation: add X-Redwood-Traffic-Class=background in customer integration; follow-up patch to proxy in progress.
Customer (BrightCart - Rajesh Kumar): We pushed a hotfix to add the header but would prefer the platform to not require header workarounds. This nightly job is scheduled and we cannot change it in prod quickly.
Eng (Kim, gateway): Confirmed bug in v1.14.2: header rewrite step strips path suffix for multipart in a small set of connectors. PR opened to fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321
SRE (Diego): Rolling forward a proxy patch to the dedicated pool (canary) and enabling a temporary route-level exemption to enlarge interactive window for BrightCart till patch completes.
Workaround applied 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC: support added a route-level exemption for tenant 'brightcart' to increase interactive concurrency window and avoid early 429s. Customer also updated their integrated job to send X-Redwood-Traffic-Class=background for nightly flushes (non-disruptive).

Permanent fix: gateway PR #4321 merged (normalizes request.path for multipart rewrites) and deployed to staging. Scheduled rollout to production dedicated pools on 2026-03-13 with phased canary. After deployment, monitored ingest for two nightly cycles; 429s did not recur.

Post-deploy: removed temporary route exemption on 2026-03-14 after verification.
1) Backport canonicalization fix to earlier edge proxy branches (v1.13.x) used by older dedicated fleets
2) Add unit test to ensure multipart/form-data preserves path suffix during header rewrite
3) Add a diagnostic metric: route_normalization_failure_count per tenant
4) Update support runbook: if customer reports bulk-embed 429s, verify X-Redwood-Traffic-Class and route_id in trace

## Issue summary
Enterprise customer reports intermittent request timeouts on the Embeddings endpoint in **eu-west**. Symptoms present as client-side timeouts (30s) and occasional gateway 504s. Customer indicates impact to production document ingestion pipeline.

## Impact
- **Customer impact:** Elevated latency/timeouts for embeddings requests; ingestion workers backing up.
- **Scope (initial):** Customer-reported, suspected broader eu-west degradation.
- **Business impact:** Enterprise account; risk of SLA breach/credits request if sustained.

## Customer context
- Company: Vertex Legaltech (Enterprise)
- Workload: batch embeddings (typically 64–256 inputs/request)
- Notable constraint: ingestion pipeline is region-pinned to eu-west for data residency.

## Environment
- Tier: Enterprise (Hosted API)
- Region: eu-west
- Endpoint: /v1/embeddings
- SDK: customer states Python SDK 1.12.x (exact patch unknown)

## Timeline (UTC)
- 2026-02-11 10:12: Customer email via Support portal: "embeddings timing out in EU region"
- 10:18: SUP-1850 created, triage started
- 10:22: Requested required intake fields (request IDs, timestamps, model, payload sizes)
- 10:29: First response sent (ack + comms cadence)
- 10:41: Error/latency checks indicate elevated p95 in eu-west embeddings
- 10:47: Escalated to SRE per trigger (Sev1) + opened incident bridge
- 11:05: Mitigation applied: route a % of embeddings traffic to alternate eu-west pool; recommended customer-side timeout/retry settings
- 11:32: Metrics stabilize; customer confirms improved success rate
- 2026-02-12 09:10: Continued monitoring shows stable; incident closed

## Intake checklist (requested / collected)
Requested from customer (per Support intake checklist):
- Region (confirmed eu-west)
- Model (text-embedding-3-large; also saw bge-large-en-v1.5)
- SDK + runtime (Python SDK ~1.12.x; running in Kubernetes)
- Request IDs (received 3 IDs; see internal note in comments)
- Approx payload sizes (64–256 strings; some up to ~5–8k chars)
- Time window + timezone (provided UTC timestamps)

## Triage notes (Support)
- Customer reports client-side timeout at 30 seconds; also observes sporadic 504s.
- No auth errors; no 429s. Not consistent with quota/rate limiting.
- Suspect regional capacity saturation or upstream dependency (vectorization workers) latency.

## Escalation trigger (per new playbook draft)
Escalate to SRE immediately (P1/Sev1) when any of the following are true:
- Regional p95 latency on embeddings exceeds customer-observed timeouts (>30s) for >10 minutes, OR
- 5xx rate >1% for embeddings in a region for >5 minutes with at least 1 enterprise customer impact, OR
- Multiple customers report the same symptom in the same region.

## Customer comms plan (Enterprise cadence)
Per SLA policy draft for enterprise incidents:
- **Initial acknowledgement:** within 15 minutes (met at 10:29 UTC)
- **Updates:** every 60 minutes while investigating, or within 30 minutes of major changes (mitigation applied, root cause confirmed, resolution)
- **Status page:** only if confirmed broad customer impact beyond a single account and sustained degradation; coordinate with #incidents and comms alignment doc.

## Interim workaround guidance provided to customer
- Increase client timeout to 60s temporarily for embeddings requests.
- Enable retries with exponential backoff on network timeouts/504s (max 2 retries) and log request IDs.
- If ingestion can tolerate it, reduce batch size per request (e.g., 64 inputs) while issue persists.
- If customer can temporarily fail over, consider routing to us-east (customer declined due to residency).

## Resolution
SRE applied a mitigation in eu-west to reduce queuing delay for embeddings workers and adjusted routing to rebalance load across pools. Latency returned to normal and timeouts ceased.

## Follow-ups
- Confirm whether this incident should generate a short known-issue entry (if recurrence observed) vs handled as one-off.
- Ensure canonical embeddings health dashboard link is included in Support quick-view set (see ENG-4823).
- Add clearer customer-facing error classification for gateway timeouts on embeddings (if feasible) to reduce ambiguity (request ID + retryable hint).

Issue summary:
Customer deployed two optimizer changes in prod earlier today: a new quantization profile (profile id qp-2026-03-13-v3) and enabled kv_prefetch=true at the serving-group level. Within ~30 minutes they observed a sharp increase in P95 token latency from ~120ms to ~620ms and intermittent request timeouts for long streaming requests. The issue impacts multiple routes and is causing user-facing latency spikes for LexiHealth's triage assistant flows.

Impact:
- Increased P95 token latency across affected model variants.
- Streaming sessions hitting websocket disconnects after 10–20s in ~5% of requests.
- Business impact: slowdown of patient triage flows; customer marked as Priority-1.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: rwd-dedicated-lexi-01 (prod us-east)
- Serving groups: sg-lexi-triage-a, sg-lexi-triage-b
- Model variants: redwood-open-7b-quant-8bit (pinned), gptx-13b-qat (fallback)

Recent changes (per customer):
1) Applied quant profile: qp-2026-03-13-v3 via Console rollout at 2026-03-13T13:22:00Z.
2) Enabled kv_prefetch=true on both serving groups at 2026-03-13T13:47:00Z.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send long-context streaming prompt (~1.5k tokens) to route /v1/generate/triage with concurrency 8.
2) Observe slow first-token times in traces and increased P95 across the Service Route dashboard.

Observed behavior:
- P50 stable, P95 and P99 jumped significantly after changes.
- Kernel-level slowdowns seen in runtime metrics: token processing time per-step increased.
- KV prefetch metrics show spike in disk IO wait and prefetch read latencies.

Expected behavior:
- No material change in P95 after applying quant/kv adjustments; throughput should be preserved or improved.

Attachments:
- Snippets of service traces and perf histograms provided by customer (attached in ticket).
- Sample logs: "kernel: op_conv_slow_path: avg 3.2ms -> 8.9ms", "kv_prefetch: read_latency_ms p95 145 -> 980".

Immediate mitigation attempted by customer:
- Rolled forward traffic to fallback variant (gptx-13b-qat) with partial success but still high P95 on that variant.
- Reduced concurrency on client side to 4 which reduced error rate but not P95.

Customer request:
- Assistance with a safe sequence to toggle/undo the optimizer changes with minimal customer downtime and guidance on verification before and after each step.

Summary of findings:
1) Timeline correlation: quant profile rollout preceded KV prefetch enable. Both changes overlap with latency spike.
2) Kernel compatibility: qp-2026-03-13-v3 appears to select an experimental GEMM kernel for certain sequence lengths. That kernel has higher per-token latency at 2048+ context in this runtime build.
3) KV prefetch interaction: kv_prefetch=true causes aggressive upstream block prefetch which increases IO contention on node-local SSDs for this workload pattern (many long contexts, high KV hit rate).
4) Autoscaling and cgroup traces show GPU utilization remained below capacity; CPU and IO were saturated during spikes.
Hypothesis: The quant profile selection resulted in higher per-step CPU overhead for kernel marshalling on long sequences; combined with aggressive KV prefetch this pushed the host IO/CPU path into queuing, increasing token P95 and causing stream disconnects.
Evidence: correlated timestamps across Console rollout audit, runtime logs, and node metrics (attached links).
Suggested priority sequence (safe): see resolution field for step-by-step commands and verification checks.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 14:18 - LexiHealth (Customer): Provided Console audit links and sample perf histograms. Traffic routing: 60% sg-lexi-triage-a, 40% sg-lexi-triage-b. Confirmed both groups received same config changes.
2026-03-13 15:05 - SRE (Jamie Liu): Node disks healthy; io depth shows sustained queue depth spikes concurrent with high kv_prefetch reads. No underlying storage errors. Recommended disabling kv_prefetch on one serving group as controlled test.
2026-03-13 16:02 - LexiHealth (Customer): Approved immediate actions. Requested step-by-step commands and monitoring checks; asked for a 1-hour maintenance window starting 16:30 UTC.
Workaround / rollback checklist (executed as of 2026-03-13T17:10Z for sg-lexi-triage-a, sg-lexi-triage-b):
1) Controlled disable of kv_prefetch (canary then global):
   - Verify: monitor metric rwd.kv_prefetch.read_latency_ms p95 and serving-group p95 tokens. Expect drop within 1–5 minutes.
   - If canary OK, apply to sg-lexi-triage-a.
2) Revert quant profile via model registry rollback (do not restart pods yet):

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running SSE streams intermittently return interleaved paragraph fragments and sometimes omit final punctuation after a short auth token rotation. Impact: QuantaDocs observed 3-7% of streaming responses missing closing punctuation or containing sentences where paragraphs are mixed (two paragraphs merged with parts out of order). This leads to downstream parsing failures for their document ingestion pipeline. Environment: Production, us-east-1, Dedicated tenancy with token rotation frequency: 5 minutes for short-lived session tokens. Steps to reproduce (observed by customer): 1) Start an SSE chat session to /v1/streams with a standard system+user prompt that elicits a multi-paragraph long-form answer (~300-500 tokens). 2) Allow the session to be open for >3 minutes. 3) Trigger an auth refresh (customer-side or via normal rotate) or wait for automatic token refresh to happen. 4) Client reconnects/resumes using the session id/last-event-id; sometimes receives interleaved fragments from two worker backends. Expected: Resume should stitch fragments in order and preserve terminal punctuation. Actual: On ~3-7% of attempts, the resumed stream contains chunks that interleave paragraph fragments (e.g., the end of paragraph 1 followed by the beginning of paragraph 3, then the remainder of paragraph 2), and in ~1% the closing punctuation for the final paragraph is missing. Additional notes: Customer uses an HTTP reverse proxy before the client which preserves Last-Event-ID header. They rely on the server-provided resume token in SSE body. They experimented with longer token TTL and saw reduced frequency.
Open SSE stream to /v1/streams with a prompt returning multi-paragraph output (~400 tokens)
Keep the connection idle for >3 minutes so token rotation will occur on client or server side
Allow auth-flow to issue a new short-lived token, then perform reconnect/resume using Last-Event-ID or resume token
Observe assembled stream for out-of-order paragraph fragments and missing final punctuation
Initial support triage: reproduced at low rate on staging when forcing short token TTL to 10s and performing reconnect during mid-generation.
Hypothesis 1: resume routing race — resume request can be routed to a different worker which begins producing the next sequence before the previous worker finishes sending its tail; mismatch in sequence ordering in assembly logic causes interleaving.
Hypothesis 2: token rotation causes a transient double-connection window where both workers consider themselves authoritative for the session; last-event-id hints diverge between workers.
Observed evidence: logs show overlapping seq numbers and two workers (worker-08 and worker-12) with partial_choice_ids pc_43 and pc_44 both sending segments within milliseconds of each other. Assembly reported "mismatch" and sequence array indicates out-of-order arrival: [202,203,201].
Edge-proxy behavior: proxy preserves Last-Event-ID header, but when cookie/token rotates, client may open a new TCP connection that LB routes to a different backend; LB sticky session TTL observed to be 30s so not always sticky across rotates.
Reproducer: integration test created that simulates rotation mid-stream and triggers reconnect; failing rate ~5/1000 on local agent with two simulated workers; increasing inter-worker arbitration (locking) reduced failure rate to zero in the test harness.
Potential regressions: recent change in resume orchestration (PR #2387) touched worker handoff and reduce-lock path for resume speed — may have opened a microwindow where two workers can both believe they should serve the resumed stream.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:47 - QuantaDocs (Customer): Confirmed regression visible after small traffic spike. They validated that increasing token TTL to 10 minutes reduced incidence but is not acceptable for their security posture. Asked for ETA on fix and whether there is a recommended workaround beyond TTL increase.
Workaround: customer set reverse-proxy affinity for 30s and temporarily increased token TTL to 10 minutes (reduced failures to <0.1%). Permanent fix: serving-runtime patch #2399 (adds short resume lease + stricter sequence handshake) merged and scheduled for staged rollout. Follow-ups: 1) QA regression for resume fast-path to add synthetic test forcing mid-generation rotate; 2) Monitor canary metrics for interleaving events in us-east-1; 3) Update runbook with guidance for customers using short-lived auth tokens during long-lived SSE streams. Ticket remains open until canary completes and customer confirms resolution.
payload.summary: Streaming race after auth token refresh causes interleaved paragraphs and missing closing punctuation

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports increased 5xx/timeouts and a long right-tail on inference latency starting 2026-02-19 morning. Impact: production traffic for several critical endpoints experienced user-facing slowdowns and occasional request failures leading to downstream transaction retries. Hypothesis early: client-side connection pooling and retry/backoff interaction causing serial queueing and replays that amplify perceived platform latency.
Customer-facing slowdowns for Inkling Financial morning batch windows, intermittent user transaction failures. Perceived platform reliability hit; customer escalated to platform SLA team.
2026-02-19 08:00 UTC - first signs of tail latency in customer's telemetry; 2026-02-19 09:15 UTC - customer opens support; 2026-02-20 10:30 UTC - support confirmed patterns consistent with connection pool saturation; 2026-02-22 14:00 UTC - reproduced in staging with default SDK config; 2026-02-24 11:00 UTC - mitigation applied and monitoring updated.
1) Deploy client using redwood-js-sdk v1.4.3 with default settings (connectionPool.max=2, keepAlive=false, retryCount=6)
2) Fire 200 concurrent short requests that produce small token outputs (avg 30 tokens) at ~100 rps
3) Observe request queueing at the client layer and multiple repeated attempts for single user requests
4) Inspect client connection metrics: long wait_for_connection times and frequent TCP teardown/recreate
5) Compare to same test with connectionPool.max=16 and keepAlive=true to note reduced perceived latency and fewer retries
Reproduced the client's symptom in our staging environment by using the same SDK version and default config. Observed client-side serialized requests: connectionPool.max=2 caused N concurrent app threads to wait for connections leading to long client wait times and retries.
SDK v1.4.3 default changed in PR #987: increased retryCount and aggressive exponential backoff jitter introduced more replay attempts when connections were slow to obtain. This amplifies client queueing under short-request, high-concurrency workloads.
HTTP/2 multiplexer misconfiguration not primary; most reproductions used HTTP/1.1 and showed clear per-host connection limits causing serial queuing. When keepAlive=true and pool max increased, tail latency dropped by ~70%.
No server-side capacity shortage observed: serving runtime metrics show steady CPU/GPU utilization and low token-level processing time. Error budget correlated with request timeouts initiated by the client, not 5xx from backend.
Customer's dedicated setup used an internal LB that terminated keepalives aggressively (idle timeout 20s) which increased socket churn and made connectionPool ineffective unless enabled with keepAlive.
Slack thread: #support SUP-27402 with eng: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05SUP12345/p164f...
[ingress-proxy] 2026-02-19T08:05:12Z WARN client_wait_ms=1430 host=api.redwood.ai path=/v1/generate
[sdk] 2026-02-19T08:05:12Z DEBUG retrying request attempt=3 backoff_ms=1200 trace_id=abc123
[serving-runtime] 2026-02-19T08:05:13Z INFO model=llama-3-13b latency_ms=78 request_id=req-9f2a
[customer-app] 2026-02-19T08:05:15Z ERROR request_timeout user_txn=txn-449
Customer (Samir Rao): 'We started seeing a flurry of timeouts and then a steady stream of retries. Our UX shows spinning indicators for minutes.'
Support (Aisha Patel): 'Requesting SDK config and connection metrics. Can you confirm SDK version and whether keepalive is enabled on your LB?'
Customer (Samir Rao): 'Using redwood-js-sdk v1.4.3 via our node microservice. LB timeout is 20s, default SDK settings otherwise.'
SRE (Nina Torres): 'Observed client_wait_ms spikes in API ingress logs matching customer request windows. No backend saturation.'
SDK Eng (Marco Nguyen): 'We have a patch to change defaults and expose pool sizing guidance in README. Preparing patch PR 1012.'
Short-term mitigation applied 2026-02-24: advised customer to upgrade to redwood-js-sdk v1.4.4 (hotfix) that enables keepAlive by default and reduces retryCount to 3. Customer applied change and reported reduced tail latency within 30 minutes.
Recommended configuration for high-concurrency, short-response workloads: connectionPool.max >= concurrency / 8 (empirical), keepAlive=true, retryCount <= 3, baseBackoff<=200ms. Example: connectionPool.max=16, keepAlive=true, retryCount=2 for 200 client threads.
Longer-term fixes: SDK default change merged (PR 1012) to sensible defaults for production workloads and expanded SDK docs with a 'connection pool sizing' section and runbook linked in Confluence.
Added an alert to platform ingress: client_wait_ms P95 > 500ms -> create ticket and surface client-side queueing to support during triage.
Follow-up: schedule a proactive run with top dedicated customers to review SDK settings and LB keepalive timeouts.
Follow-up internal task created: INT-4218 to add end-to-end tests for connection churn and retry amplification scenarios.
Mitigated - customer applied SDK hotfix and config guidance; monitoring in place. Follow-up tasks assigned.
payload.summary: High tail latency and intermittent request timeouts from SDK clients caused by small connection pool + aggressive retry policy

payload.description:
Issue summary:
FinSight reports that internal service-to-service API calls using service account JWTs are intermittently receiving 403 responses from Redwood's private deployment. The tokens are valid and accepted by the IdP, but when routed through the customer's private ingress + idp-proxy, Redwood's authz layer is evaluating them as belonging to a different tenant.

Impact:
- Production job-workers (data enrichment pipeline) failing to call Redwood inference endpoints for multiple customers of FinSight; ~30% of calls hit 403s over the last 8 hours.
- Customer-facing processing delays and retries causing downstream SLA breaches.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer VPC) in us-east-1
- Ingress: customer-managed ALB -> edge-proxy (Redwood idp-proxy) -> private control plane
- Customer service tokens are short-lived JWTs minted by the customer's IdP (Okta) and include tenant-scoped claim "tid" in the namespaced claim key: "https://finsight.example.com/claims/tid"

Observed behaviour:
- Tokens accepted by the introspection endpoint; token introspection shows "tid" present. However, once request reaches authz policy evaluation, tenant resolution falls back to default_tenant and policy denies access.

Hypothesis:
- The private ingress or our claim-normalization middleware is stripping or rewriting namespaced claim keys (removing the URL prefix) resulting in a mismatch with tenant routing (we expect full namespaced claim name). If the claim key is altered (e.g., becomes "tid" instead of "https://finsight.example.com/claims/tid"), tenant lookup fails and request is treated as cross-tenant.

Why this is different from previous tickets:
- Many prior SSO issues were related to whitespace, case sensitivity, or trailing-dot hostnames. This appears to be an interpolation/sanitizer that removes characters from claim keys (slash or colon) when certain ingress header transformations are present on the customer's ALB.

1) Customer mints short-lived service account JWT with namespaced claim key 'https://finsight.example.com/claims/tid' and value 'tenant-1234'.
2) Send request to Redwood private inference endpoint via customer's ALB with header Authorization: Bearer <token>.
3) Observe 403 from authz; call token introspection endpoint to confirm token validity (returns active:true and shows claim key).
4) Re-run with the same token but bypassing the ALB (direct route to edge-proxy) — request succeeds.
5) Capture ingress request headers at edge-proxy when routed via ALB vs bypassed.

edge-proxy (via ALB) log snippet:
[2026-03-14T02:14:03Z] request_id=0a1b authz:received_claims={"tid":"tenant-1234", "sub":"svc-account-9"} tenant_resolution=default_tenant decision=DENY reason='tenant claim missing namespaced_key'

edge-proxy (direct) log snippet:
[2026-03-14T02:12:19Z] request_id=ff4c authz:received_claims={"https://finsight.example.com/claims/tid":"tenant-1234", "sub":"svc-account-9"} tenant_resolution=tenant-1234 decision=ALLOW

ALB header transformation trace (customer-provided): 'X-Forwarded-User-Claims' truncated slashes and replaced ':' with '_' in header serialization.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 19:22 - FinSight (Customer): Sent sanitized token and ALB config. Confirmed the ALB has a JSON header serialization rule that flattens namespaced keys for downstream compatibility.
- 2026-03-13 20:05: Local repro: created middleware that rewrites 'https://finsight.example.com/claims/tid' to 'tid' and tenant resolution failed.
- 2026-03-13 21:00: Confirmed that token introspection still returns original claim keys (IdP shows namespaced key) — transformation happens at ingress header serialization step on the ALB.
- 2026-03-13 22:15: Authz's claim-normalizer currently performs exact-key lookup for tenant claims and falls back to a blacklist-safe default tenant if not found. There's no canonicalization path for rewritten claim keys.
- 2026-03-14 00:40: Tested tolerant lookup that attempts both namespaced and suffix-key match (i.e., check full key then strip URL prefix and check again) — tenant resolution succeeds in repro.
- 2026-03-14 02:00: Security review: tolerant lookup could create ambiguity if two tenants choose colliding short claim names. Decided to scope change to 'private' deployments where customer-provided claim namespace is configured in tenant mapping.
Workaround applied and patch submitted:
- Short-term workaround: Instructed FinSight to disable ALB JSON key sanitization (passthrough namespaced claim keys). This immediately restored traffic (customer confirmed success after 20 minutes).
- Medium-term fix: Auth team implemented tolerant tenant-lookup in private deployments that consults tenant mapping for both full namespaced claim keys and the suffix-only key. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth/pull/319 (under review).
- Rollout plan: patch gated behind feature flag 'private.tolerant_claim_lookup' and will be deployed to staging for canary in prod next 24 hours. Monitoring: added metric 'auth.tolerant_lookup_matches' and alert if mismatch rate > 0.5% after rollout.
1) Auth Eng to complete security review and merge PR 319 (ETA 2026-03-15)
2) Deploy feature-flagged change to staging and run regression tests against known claim mangling patterns (owner: Priya Nair)
3) Update Private Deploy runbook to document ALB header serialization caveat and customer guidance (owner: Support)
4) Outreach to other private customers to check for similar ALB/edge configurations (CS team to create a short checklist)
5) Close ticket after 48h stable canary and customer confirmation
payload.summary: Tenant-claim namespace stripping causes service tokens to be treated as cross-tenant and return 403 in private prod

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that a live usage panel (Organization -> Usage -> Live) is intermittently undercounting unique tokens and sessions when their dashboard includes a join between ingestion_events and embeddings_routes. The discrepancy appears correlated with dashboards that use multiple LEFT JOINs and a sampling hint parameter.

Impact:
- Prodcraft Media sees a 15-30% lower token count in the live panel vs raw usage export for the same time window (last 60m).
- Alerts driven by the live usage panel (rate-based) are not firing because the panel shows lower volume.
- Customer is concerned about billing/usage visibility for embedding-heavy routes during peak campaigns.

Environment:
- Redwood Console (prod) - us-east-1
- Affected org: prodcraft-media (enterprise account)
- Dashboard: "Live Embedding Traffic" (custom)
- Query uses sampling hint `/*+SAMPLE(0.2)*/` and two LEFT JOINs (ingestion_events LEFT JOIN embeddings_routes LEFT JOIN api_keys)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open the customer-provided dashboard in prod (Live Embedding Traffic).
2. Set time range to "Last 60 minutes" and refresh.
3. Export raw usage for same org/time range via console export or /usage/export API.
4. Compare unique token/session counts and token sums; observe mismatch.

Expected behavior:
- Live panel should show counts consistent (within sampling tolerance) with raw export after accounting for sampling fraction.

Actual behavior:
- Live panel underreports unique tokens by ~20% compared to raw export. Discrepancy grows with number of joins and when sampling hint is present. When sampling hint is removed, counts align within expected variance.

Logs / Observations:
- Query plan from query-engine shows sampling applied before join in some plan variants, after join in others, depending on optimizer heuristics.
- Trace-id from customer dashboard query: trace:console-20260310-7a2b33. Linked trace shows two different physical plans executed over successive refreshes for same logical query.
- Internal telemetry: sampling_rewrite_count metric spikes correlated to dashboard refresh times.

Investigation notes (engineering):
- Hypothesis A: Query planner's join reordering + sampling pushdown rule is non-deterministic when histograms are stale, leading to sampling being applied at different points in the plan and changing cardinality.
- Hypothesis B: Console query caching layer sometimes serves a pre-aggregated sampled result from a previous query execution with a different join order; cache key didn't incorporate join-order-sensitive fingerprints.
- Reproduced in staging by running the same logical query repeatedly with identical parameters; observed two physical plans with different sampling placement and different result rows when sampling < 1.0.
- Related PR in query-engine aims to make sampling pushdown deterministic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/query-engine/pull/547

Workaround provided to customer:
1) Remove the explicit sampling hint from the dashboard query (temporary) to force full aggregation in live panel.
2) If sampling is required, add an explicit subquery that materializes the sampled set before joins (e.g., WITH sampled AS (SELECT * FROM ingestion_events /*+SAMPLE(0.2)*/ ) SELECT ... FROM sampled JOIN embeddings_routes ...). This yields consistent counts but increases query cost.

Next steps / Action items:
- ENG: Apply PR 547 (deterministic sampling pushdown) to staging and run A/B compare job against a set of customer queries. Owner: query-engine team (Sasha Iyer). ETA: 2026-03-16.
- SRE: Add dashboard-level cache key fingerprinting to include query plan fingerprint. Owner: infra team (Liam O'Connor). ETA: 2026-03-18.
- Support: Coordinate with Prodcraft Media and schedule a time window to validate post-fix. Contact: Maya Chen.

Resolution notes (pending):
- Temporary workaround accepted by customer (removing sampling hint). Engineering changes planned for deterministic sampling placement and cache key hardening.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:20 - Customer (Prodcraft Media - Jenna Ortiz): Thanks for the fast response. We'll remove the sampling hint for now. Can you confirm whether alerts relying on live panels will be re-evaluated after the fix?
payload.summary: Dashboard query join-order causes sampling inconsistency and undercount in live usage panel

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightScribe reported a sustained P99 throughput degradation for their dedicated pool during midday on 2026-03-12. Impact: degraded request throughput and elevated queuing leading to increased tail latency for inference requests. Root behaviour appears to be the autoscaler suppressing scale-ups due to misleading heartbeat-derived utilization signals from one or more silent tenants.

Impact details:
- Customer-facing: increased request backpressure, timeouts for a subset of long-lived streams, and ~25% drop in p50 throughput for routed model 'redwood/longform-16k'.
- Internal: autoscaler did not trigger expected burst additions for ~18 minutes despite GPU queue depth > 90% for several allocation groups.

Environment: Dedicated capacity, reserved pool id rp-47, us-east, auto-scale policy 'midday-burst' with predictive window enabled.

Observed by: BrightScribe Support and console alerting (route p99 queue depth alert).
1) Route sustained 1.5x baseline traffic of small- and long-form streams to a reserved pool with predictive autoscale enabled.
2) Start a silent/low-IO tenant process that maintains heartbeats but produces negligible packet I/O (simulated via sidecar shim that replies to health probes only).
3) Observe autoscaler decisions and GPU allocation logs over 15 minutes; check per-tenant heartbeat and allocation weighting logs.
4) Verify that predictive autoscaler avoids additional allocation despite queue depth rising above scale thresholds.
- Autoscaler logs (autoscaler-controllers): repeated decisions 'scale: suppressed: low_active_weight' with reason 'heartbeat_pulse_low_io'.
- GPU allocator logs (gpu-manager): 'tenant_affinity=sticky' and 'available_slots=0' while 'queue_depth' climbs to 94%.
- Serving-runtime traces: continuous short-lived slot holds from tenant T-132 and a burst of many small streams causing slot fragmentation.
- Customer console screenshot referenced in linked Confluence runbook.
- No driver crashes or 5xx at infra layer; errors are queued timeouts from application layer.
03/12 11:10 - Support (Aisha): Customer reported sudden degradation at 11:05 local. Attached console timeline and request IDs.
03/12 11:18 - SRE (Ben): Correlated alert to reserved pool rp-47. Noted autoscaler logs showing repeated suppression flags tied to heartbeat-derived active-weight metric.
03/12 11:25 - Eng (Diego Morales): Dumped allocation state; found tenant T-132 registering heartbeats at expected cadence but emitting near-zero I/O. This created 'active' but effectively idle occupant for slot-weighting calculations.
03/12 11:31 - Eng (Priya Patel): Confirmed predictive autoscaler uses last N heartbeat pulses to compute expected demand; silent heartbeat clients skew expected_utilization downwards because they appear as 'active' but consume zero CPU/GPU until real traffic arrives.
03/12 11:40 - Hypothesis: Silent-heartbeat tenants are reducing the autoscaler's inferred demand variance, causing suppression of burst allocations until queued demand crosses a higher threshold. This leads to transient throughput starvation for other tenants.
03/12 11:52 - Temporary mitigation attempted: Increase autoscale aggressiveness for rp-47 via manual override (force-add 2 slots). Immediate improvement in p50 throughput observed; queuing dropped to normal ranges.
03/12 12:05 - Confirmed reproduction in staging cluster by running a heartbeat-shim service that responds to health checks only. Autoscaler suppressed expected allocation until manual override.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:45 - Customer (BrightScribe, Sarah Lee): We deployed a new sidecar last night; will rollback and test. Please advise if we should restart connections.\nCustomer note: This impacts high-priority flows for our transcription pipeline.
Hotfix: Autoscaler change to ignore heartbeat-only tenants when outbound-packet-rate < 1 pkt/s for the last 30s (owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-03-14)
Customer guidance: Add snippet to SDK/sidecar to produce a minimal periodic probe packet when an active session is expected to generate traffic (owner: Support Docs, ETA: 2026-03-16)
Follow-up: Add metric 'heartbeat_io_confidence' to autoscaler telemetry and surface in Console (owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-03-21)
Postmortem: Draft and share with BrightScribe and internal incident channel (#incidents) (owner: Ben, ETA: 2026-03-15)
Backport: Apply fix to autoscaler stable branch and coordinate Dedicated safe deploy window (owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-03-18)
Test: Add chaos test in staging that simulates silent-heartbeat tenants and validates autoscaler doesn't suppress scale-ups incorrectly (owner: QA, ETA: 2026-03-20)
Temporary workaround: manual slot increase for rp-47 restored throughput. Root cause: autoscaler's active-weight calculation treated persistent but low-IO heartbeats as evidence of capacity being 'in-use', which suppressed predictive scale-ups. Permanent remediation path: implement heartbeat IO-confidence metric and threshold, update autoscaler to down-weight heartbeat-only tenants, add SDK guidance for emitting minimal outbound packets when sessions are live. Issue summary:
After toggling the new streaming-trace hook for a subset of traffic, NimbleAI reported that several console dashboards and alert evaluations started showing inconsistent metric attribution windows. Usage rollups, cohort attribution, and alerting rules appeared to evaluate against a mixed sample window (some requests included streaming traces and some did not), leading to alert flapping and incorrect 'requests per minute' baselines.

Impact:
- Customer-facing alerts for error-rate and latency thresholds fired repeatedly between 02:00 and 03:30 UTC on 2026-02-18.
- Dashboard charts for 'streaming vs non-streaming requests' show overlapping counts (sum > total).
- Automated SLA calculators for the customer reported skewed 95th latency values.

Environment:
- Prod console metrics pipeline (us-east).
- Affected tenant: NimbleAI Inc. (enterprise).
- Hook enabled via console feature flag: streaming-trace=beta on routing policy nimble-team-a.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Enable the streaming-trace hook for a small percentage (10%) of production traffic via the Console rollout.
2) Wait 5-10 minutes until traces begin arriving to the metrics pipeline.
3) Open the 'Usage overview' dashboard and the 'Errors by cohort' alert definition for the tenant.
4) Observe counts and alert evals for the 1m and 5m windows.

Observed behavior:
- Metric rollups for the tenant included both trace-tagged and untagged requests in different aggregation buckets. Some hourly rollups double-counted requests because streaming traces produced additional telemetry events that were ingested as separate usage events.
- Alerts that reference the dashboard metric with a 5m evaluation window flapped: metric value oscillated as the ingestion pipeline alternated between deduplicating and not deduplicating streaming events.

Expected behavior:
- Enabling streaming-trace should not change total request counts or cause duplicate ingestion. Streaming trace events should be correlated to the original request and excluded from pure usage rollups, or marked so aggregation de-dupes them consistently. Alerts should evaluate against stable, deduplicated counts regardless of trace hook state.

- Initial logs show that the tracer service started emitting 'streaming.frame' events with the same request_id but without the original 'request.start' tag in the usage topic.
- Metrics consumer (analytics-pipeline) has a time-window based dedup strategy keyed by request_id, but streaming.frame events use 'trace_id' as key in the new schema—mismatch causes dedup to miss during high ingestion bursts.
- Spike correlates with PR #4021 which added lightweight streaming tracing; instrumentation added a new event type but did not set 'request_id' for legacy compatibility.
- Tentative hypothesis: schema change in streaming traces broke dedup keys and created ephemeral duplicate events that impacted 1m/5m rollups leading to alert flapping.
- Reproducer run in staging confirms mixed-key ingestion causes sum(metric_total_requests) <-> sum(streaming_events) inconsistency when trace events are present.

- Temporary mitigation: disable streaming-trace hook for tenant nimble-team-a (console toggle) which stabilizes counts.
- As a short-term pipeline change, add a lightweight transform to copy trace_id -> request_id when missing for streaming.frame events (rolled to canary for us-east).
1) Back out schema change in PR #4021 that omitted request_id; add explicit backwards-compat mapping (ETA: 2026-02-21).
2) Deploy a pipeline mapping rule to map streaming.frame.trace_id to request_id for dedup (canary first, then global).
3) Add unit/integration tests to analytics-pipeline to assert no double-counting when trace types present.
4) Run a controlled enablement with 1% traffic and monitor dashboard/alert stability for 24h before full rollout.

(pending) awaiting PR patch and pipeline canary results. If canary passes, schedule rollback window 2026-02-22 02:00 UTC.

2026-02-20 16:00 - NimbleAI (Customer): Confirmed that disabling the hook stopped the alert emails. Asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether historical metrics will be repaired.
