Issue summary:
Customer BrightHealthAI reported intermittent but sustained inference slowdowns and request timeouts for live traffic hitting rw-llm-large-v1 in us-east. Initial symptom: spikes in p95/p99 latency and a rise in perceived client-side timeouts.

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints for BrightHealthAI experienced higher tail latency starting 2026-03-11 21:00 UTC, with cascading 5xx/timeout observations from their frontend.
- Customer reports degraded user experience and several aborted sessions. Estimated ~12% request failure for the last 12 hours for the tenant.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant on prod (us-east), running rw-llm-large-v1 pinned to model:v2026-02-28.
- Customer using internal SDK (v0.9.2) with default retry settings (immediate retry ramp, no jitter).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1. Send a burst of concurrent streaming generation requests (20-50/sec) from their service using SDK v0.9.2.
2. Observe initial 429 responses followed by client-side timeouts and long-tail latency.
3. When retry storms occur, end-to-end p95 jumps >3x and many requests fail with timeout on the client.

Observed behavior:
- Server-side metrics: rising queue length at the API gateway, increased connection churn, and elevated CPU on serving nodes.
- Rate-limiter observed a growth in 429 responses for the tenant; however, some 429 responses lacked a Retry-After header in the path used by the Dedicated control plane.
- Customer SDK treats non-2xx as a transient network error and immediately retries without respecting Retry-After; retries have no jitter which concentrates load.

Expected behavior:
- Clients should respect Retry-After or backoff headers and include randomized jitter; server should return clear Retry-After when imposing quota enforcement.

Initial logs and evidence:
- Observability dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/tenants/BrightHealthAI/latency (private link).
- Sample gateway logs: repeated identical request IDs from the same tenant IP over short intervals; p99 request duration rose from 420ms -> 1.9s during amplification window.
- Rate-limiter trace: tokens exhausted at 2026-03-11T21:03:15Z followed by an increase of 429s for the tenant. Some enforcement paths returned 429 without body headers due to a fallback path in dedicated control-plane code (seen in logs).

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - Support (Diego Alvarez): Acknowledged and requested full request/response capture and SDK version. Asked customer to reduce concurrency as a temporary mitigation.
2026-03-12 - BrightHealthAI (Sarah Lee): Confirmed they were on SDK v0.9.2 and will try lowering concurrency; reported immediate improvement but issue returned when traffic resumed.
2026-03-13 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Correlated tenant traffic pattern with 429 spike. Noted missing Retry-After on some enforcement responses from dedicated control plane; created internal task INT-987 to track fix.
2026-03-14 - Support (Diego Alvarez): Applied temporary per-tenant ingress circuit breaker to limit retry amplification. Instructed customer to upgrade SDK to v0.10.0-beta (patched backoff).
Root cause hypothesis: Combination of (1) dedicated-plane quota enforcement returning 429s inconsistently (some enforcement paths lacked Retry-After header) and (2) customer SDK treating 429 as retriable network error with no jitter. This produced a retry amplification loop increasing load and tail latency.
Metrics show a tight correlation between the start of repeated identical request IDs and a rapid increase in queue depth -> p99 latency -> downstream timeouts in the customer's frontend.
A small code path in the dedicated control plane falls back to a generic enforcement response which didn't include Retry-After; affected tenants only when specific quota buckets were hit (explains why not all customers were impacted).
SDK replay confirmed that immediate retries double/triple request rate within seconds and can overwhelm tenant pool even when absolute QPS is modest.
No evidence of model runtime bug; serving nodes remained healthy once ingress load was throttled.
Relevant logs: gateway trace IDs [gw:0a3f, gw:0b7c, gw:0d21] show 8-12 repeated attempts per initial request from same client within <5s.
Related tickets: SUP-84217 highlighted 429s misinterpreted by clients (useful context) but this case differs due to a missing Retry-After header path in dedicated control plane.
Short-term mitigation (2026-03-14): Applied tenant-level ingress circuit breaker to cap immediate retries for BrightHealthAI. This reduced p95/p99 within 20 minutes of activation.
Customer action: BrightHealthAI agreed to upgrade to SDK v0.10.0-beta which implements Retry-After handling and randomized exponential backoff. They deployed the change to canary services and reported reduced retry storms.
Medium-term fix (planned): Deploy forced Retry-After header from all quota enforcement paths in the dedicated control plane (INT-987). Add server-side per-tenant token bucket to smooth bursts and return clear headers. Target rollout: 2026-03-21 behind feature flag.
Long-term: Update SDK docs and default settings to encourage conservative retry behavior; add automated detection/alerting for retry amplification patterns per tenant in the console (post-incident task assigned to Observability team).
Follow-up tasks: INT-987 (dedicated control plane header bug), INT-1024 (observability alert for retry amplification), DEV-PR-456 (SDK backoff/jitter default).
Track INT-987 to completion and coordinate deployment with Dedicated infra team.
Confirm BrightHealthAI completes SDK upgrade across all their services and monitor for recurrence for 72 hours post-rollout.
Add a short KB article for customers on recommended retry strategies and SDK versions. (Docs owner: Developer Experience)
Postmortem: schedule 1-hour blameless postmortem with SRE, Dedicated infra, DevEx, and the customer for week of 2026-03-22.
Update ticket with final closure details once INT tasks are resolved and customer confirms stability.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 95th/99th tail latency spikes (up to +600ms) on text-generation routes after a recent optimizer rollout that applied combined batching caps and a new mixed quant profile. Impact: Production traffic for ParagraphAI (dedicated) experiences request timeouts and degraded UX during bursty traffic windows. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east-1 running serving-runtime v2.18 with autoscaler enabled and latest optimizer controller applied on 2026-03-12 22:18 UTC. Observed behavior: increased token-latency variance, occasional 504s for streaming clients, and elevated GPU mem churn on pool-03 nodes.
1) Target the customer route /v1/generate with typical payloads (avg 350 tokens) and parallelism of 20 connections from us-east test harness.
2) Apply mixed-quant profile + batch cap (batched_max=64, stream_threshold=32) as in their rollout config.
3) Ramp to a 2x baseline QPS over 5 minutes to simulate burst. Observe 95/99 latency and backend 5xx counters in logs and Grafana.
4) Note KV cache hit-rate drop and sporadic model-worker restarts in the same timeframe.
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/AB12/op-runtime-tail-latency?orgId=1&var-cluster=prod-us-east
Err logs (s3): s3://redwood-logs/prod-us-east/paragraphai/2026-03-13/optimizer-rollout/
Slack: #support thread https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05SUPPT/p16787654
Initial triage: latency increase correlates with rollout timestamp; canary pods showed no issues but dedicated pool experienced cross-tenant memory pressure.
Hypothesis A: mixed-quant profile increased per-token CPU/GEMM working set causing more frequent KV cache evictions under heavy batching, increasing cache-miss penalty.
Hypothesis B: batch cap misconfiguration allowed oversized batches to queue on a small subset of workers leading to tail amplification during bursts.
Observed: KV cache hit-rate fell from 98% to 72% at spike, and p99 tokenize time rose by ~420ms on pool-03. No disk OOMs, but worker restarts correlate with transient CUDA OOMs logged immediately prior to 504s.
We advised customer to pin traffic to the previous optimizer profile via route override (console -> route config -> use snapshot <snapshot-id>) and to temporarily reduce client concurrency from 20 -> 8. This reduced p99 by ~300ms immediately.
1) Validation: run dry-run validator script (see related_github_prs) against current config to detect mismatched quant/batch rules and invalid batch caps. 2) Toggle: use the /admin/v1/toggles endpoint to flip optimizer.enable_mixed_quant to false for the affected tenant on prod-us-east. 3) Staged revert: apply previous optimizer snapshot (snapshot-2026-03-11-2130) to one availability zone pool and monitor 10 minutes. 4) Full revert: if metrics stabilize, roll snapshot to remaining pools during low-traffic window; keep autoscaler conservative for 30 minutes. 5) Post-mortem: capture full traces, KV cache metrics, and create a follow-up INT ticket for root cause analysis.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: safe-toggle.sh <tenant> <action> (action: disable_mixed_quant | enable_mixed_quant)
set -euo pipefail
TENANT=$1
ACTION=$2
API=https://api.redwood.ai/admin/v1/toggles
if [ "$ACTION" = "disable_mixed_quant" ]; then
  curl -s -X POST $API -d "{"tenant":"$TENANT","toggle":"optimizer.enable_mixed_quant","value":false}" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMINTOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
elif [ "$ACTION" = "enable_mixed_quant" ]; then
  curl -s -X POST $API -d "{"tenant":"$TENANT","toggle":"optimizer.enable_mixed_quant","value":true}" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMINTOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
else
  echo "Unknown action" && exit 2
fi
# After toggle: run validator: python tools/opt_validator.py --tenant $TENANT --dry-run --cluster prod-us-east
Dry-run validator detects: one route with batch_cap 1024 (exceeds supported soft-limit for the pool), quant-profile mix flagged for redwood/open-7b-ql. Suggested action: reduce batch_cap to 128 and disable mixed quant for tenant until per-worker mem use is validated.
1) Engineering POC: Diego to run staged revert on pool-03 at 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC and monitor p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit-rate, and CUDA OOM events.
2) CS: Notify ParagraphAI of planned revert window and recommended client concurrency reduction during the maintenance window.
3) SRE: Keep autoscaler headroom +10% during revert to avoid noisy-neighbor impacts.
4) Follow-up INT ticket: capture heap profiles and quant kernel metrics for deep analysis (create INT-XXXX).

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 00:12 - ParagraphAI (Customer): Thanks — they can accept a 90m maintenance window between 02:00-03:30 UTC.
In progress — canary toggled and early metrics show improvement. Awaiting full cluster stabilization and post-mortem.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer (Acme Solutions) reported a gradual but persistent drop in forward throughput for several reserved routes in their dedicated EU-West pool beginning 2026-03-12 08:40 UTC. The customer observed increasing attach latency (p50 -> p95), intermittent GPU allocation failures for short-lived streams, and progressive p99 token latency degradation for gpt-open-3b and redwood-2-small routes.

Impact: Affected customer requests experienced up to 30% throughput reduction during midday traffic window; no 5xx spike observed but high attach/retry rates triggered application-level backpressure and client-side retries.

Environment: prod, eu-west-1, dedicated pool ID: pool-euw-09, tenant: acme-prod.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Simulate 300-500 short-lived streaming requests (3–30s) with random small contexts;
2) Route to dedicated pool-euw-09;
3) Observe attach latency increase and allocation failures after sustained ~5 minute burst;
4) Notice throughput plateau despite autoscaler votes for additional capacity.

Observed metrics & telemetry:
- GPU attach latency: median rose from ~120ms to ~600ms over 6 minutes; p99 attach spikes to 2.3s.
- Alloc_failures increased from ~0 to ~18/min.
- Autoscaler signals show many short-lived slot requests (interarrival ~200–800ms) causing slot fragmentation metrics to rise (slot_holes metric).
- KV-cache growth for redwood-2-small routes increased transiently (small contexts pinned repeatedly).
- Kernel utilization on GPUs remained high but not saturated (~70–85%) with many small batch sizes causing low token throughput per GPU hour.

Key logs: scheduler logs show repeated attach attempts with "LeaseDenied: slot_unavailable" and rapid open/close websocket traces. Rebalancer traces indicate frequent tiny allocations causing placement churn.

Hypothesis: A cohort of short-lived prefetch/streaming sessions from the customer produced a high churn of ephemeral connections that prevented the allocator from coalescing batches efficiently. The autoscaler observed transient increased attach rates but its smoothing/cooldown windows caused slow scale decisions, while the allocator's slot fragmentation logic returned many fractional slots (slot holes) leading to effective slot exhaustion for medium-sized batch requests.

Investigation notes:
- Cross-referenced Slack (#support, #incidents) thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C07ABC/2026-03-12-prefetch-burst.
- Checked scheduler and allocator dashboards: spike in ephemeral_conn_count and slot_fragmentation_60s.
- Reproducer: local test harness reproduced attach-rate-induced allocation failures when simulating 400 short streams with 10s average duration.
- Quick mitigation tested in staging: temporarily increase min_active_slots for tenant and enable soft-throttling on tiny short-lived streams reduced attach failure rate by ~80%.

Impacted customer communication: Customer reported increased request retries; support advised temporary traffic throttling and increased retry backoff while we investigated.

Temporary workaround:
1) Applied a tenant-level soft throttle to limit simultaneous new attaches to 120/s for acme-prod in pool-euw-09.
2) Bumped min_reserved_slots for customer to reduce fragmentation sensitivity.
3) Added short-term autoscaler override to reduce cooldown window for this pool.

These reduced attach failures and gradually restored throughput.

Next steps / follow-ups:
- Engineering to adjust allocator coalescing logic to be more resilient to high-rate short-lived streams (ENG-allocator-2026-03).
- Autoscaler policy change: include attach-failure rate and slot_fragmentation signals as inputs to faster emergency scale-ups (PR referenced below).
- Add a synthetic test in CI that simulates prefetch-cohort bursts to detect regression early.
- Postmortem and runbook update: document prefetch-cohort mitigation steps in Confluence page linked above.
- Schedule a capacity review with customer to discuss long-term options (burst reservations, rate-limiter client-side).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports intermittent 429 responses during their nightly catalog syncs that use multiplexed websocket sessions and very short-lived API keys (ephemeral tokens). The 429s arrive in waves across multiple clients with a ~30s stagger; some 429 responses include Retry-After headers, others do not.

Impact:
- BrightCart sync jobs fail to complete ~15% of the time during the nightly window (00:30-02:00 PST).
- Partial syncs lead to downstream inventory mismatch and customer-visible listing gaps.
- Engineering on-call requests clarity about whether this is configuration guidance or a bug in our accounting for ephemeral, multiplexed sessions.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (dc-brightcart-ops) on prod in us-west-2
- Client uses websocket multiplexing over HTTP/2 with ephemeral keys rotated every 45s
- Traffic mix: 80% bulk embeddings and 20% small chat/generation calls used for telemetry

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start 120 parallel websocket connections from 15 hosts using short-lived keys (rotate every 45s)
2) Each connection opens 8 multiplexed streams and issues periodic embed+generate calls at 10-20 qps per host
3) Observe 429 responses during the 00:30-02:00sync window; 429s arrive in groups with ~20-40s stagger

Observed behavior:
- 429s are not uniform; they come in sawtooth waves instead of a single capacity hit.
- Occasionally 429 responses lack Retry-After headers (client cannot back off deterministically).
- Console shows per-route burst pools allocated, but token-window metrics for the tenant show no single-shot drain.

Expected behavior:
- Throttling should be smooth and Retry-After consistently present for responses that are quota-driven.
- Dedicated pool should present predictable per-tenant accounting and clear headers for automated clients.

Logs / key headers (sanitized):
- Example 429 response with Retry-After: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Retry-After: 60
  X-RateLimit-Tenant: 12000/12000
- Example 429 response without Retry-After: HTTP/2 429
  X-RateLimit-Tenant: 11986/12000
- Ingress proxy metrics show transient connection churn and a spike in auth-token-validation RPS coincident with rotations.

Workarounds attempted by customer:
- Increased ephemeral token TTL to 180s — reduced frequency of waves but did not eliminate 429s.
- Lowered parallel connections to 60 — bulk sync completed but with slower overall job runtime.

Requested outcome:
- Guidance on configuration best-practices for ephemeral key rotation + websocket multiplexing on Dedicated pools.
- Investigation into why Retry-After header is missing on a subset of 429s and whether this indicates accounting race between edge and origin.
- If a server-side fix is required, a timeline for mitigation or recommended temporary configs for BrightCart.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 20:44 - BrightCart (Customer): Confirmed rotation 45s, 15 hosts, 8 streams each. Attached client logs and simplified repro script.
2026-03-13 11:03 - Engineering (Rate-limiter): Initial hypothesis: ephemeral-key fanout creates transient multi-counting in ingress when key swap occurs while connections are being migrated between proxies. This can cause partial denial without consistent Retry-After if the response is generated at edge vs origin. Suggested capture: sample of 429 without Retry-After and associated proxy trace.
2026-03-13 14:20 - Support (Ava Martinez): Sent guidance to customer to temporarily increase token TTL and add a jittered backoff on client side. Customer applied TTL=180s and saw partial improvement (fewer waves).
2026-03-14 09:50 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Deployed additional logging on ingress token accounting for next nightly window (logged X-token-hash when swap happens). Scheduled a canary fix to ensure Retry-After is set at edge for quota responses in PR github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/93.
Edge tracing shows token rotation events cause short-lived duplicate validation calls; duplicate calls may increment temporary counters before origin reconciliation completes.
Race window appears to be ~300-600ms during key swap; larger client fanout increases probability of staggered waves.
Inconsistent Retry-After likely due to 429 being returned by two different components: ingress (no header set in one codepath) vs origin (header set).
Priority to add header at ingress path and tighten atomicity of token-counter updates across proxies.
Related: SUP-412345 noted similar post-upgrade refill lag; lessons learned applied to trace selection.
Push edge-proxy PR that ensures Retry-After header is set for ingress-returned 429s (PR #93 staged).
Instrument token-swap counter with per-connection token-hash logs for a 72h window to validate reduction in duplicate validation calls.
Work with BrightCart to trial TTL=120s + client-side jittered backoff as short-term mitigation.
If mitigation insufficient, schedule dedicated-pool rate-window smoothing configuration change to reduce burst sensitivity (follow-up change request).
(pending) Canary PR merged to staging; awaiting 72h observation window on prod traces. Temporary mitigation recommended (TTL bump + client jitter). Will update ticket after observation window concludes.

Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated 429 throttles during nightly orchestrator sweeps despite ample burst credits. Investigating whether internal monitoring/heartbeat probes are being counted against the tenant burst pool.

Impact:
- Production ingest jobs intermittently receive 429s during scheduled monitoring/telemetry sweeps.
- Latency-sensitive streaming clients experience short-lived degradation at sweep times.
- Customer is on a dedicated pool and expects monitoring probes not to affect burst allowance for production requests.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-novafleet-01 in prod-us-east (us-east-1)
- Redwood API via private VPC control plane
- Orchestrator and sidecars are in the customer VPC; healthchecks originate from an internal service mesh and a central monitoring cluster.

Observed behavior:
- Short windows (30–90s) of elevated 429s coincident with three scheduled telemetry sweep jobs (00:15, 02:15, 04:15 UTC).
- Console shows burst credits available but route-level token window drops to zero during sweeps.
- Logs sample attached below show many small concurrent probe requests (GET /v1/healthcheck) interleaved with long-poll streams.

Expected behavior:
- Healthcheck/monitoring probe requests should be accounted separately from production burst budget or routed to an exempted route/pool so they do not cause 429s for production traffic.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) On NovaFleet staging, schedule orchestrator sweep that hits 1000 endpoints over 60s.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated, short-lived (~30-90s) p50/p95 throughput collapses on their dedicated pool that correlate with low-frequency IO bursts from a co-located tenant. Symptoms differ from typical noisy-tenant CPU/GPU hogging: we see GPU utilization remain moderate but NVMe I/O wait and PCIe latency spikes precede an autoscaler shrink event which then triggers slot fragmentation and a transient drop in effective throughput.

Impact:
- Nimbus Analytics experiences intermittent inference latency increases and throughput drops impacting a live feature flag rollout (10-20% request failures as retries hit timeout window).
- Windowed drops last under 2 minutes but occur multiple times per day during low-traffic windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id dp-3920 (customer-dedicated-usw2-3920)
- Region: us-west-2 (prod)
- Models: redwood-llama-14b-quantized (default route), fallback to open-encoder-7b
- Autoscaler config: min_replicas 2, max_replicas 10, scale_down_delay 90s, metric: p95_latency + slot_utilization composite

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Normal traffic sustained for several minutes.
2) Low-frequency background IO burst from another tenant (observed in NVMe write-amps and host-side iowait) for ~40-80s.
3) Serving-side kernel queues backlog, PCIe latency increases, individual request latencies spike and p95 crosses autoscale threshold.
4) Autoscaler interprets p95 spike as sustained demand and triggers rapid shrink due to conflicting slot_utilization signal (false low-utilization on some slots) leading to eviction/reshuffle.
5) After autoscale event, batchers and placement rewarm; throughput collapses until KV caches and prefetchers repopulate (~60-120s).

Observed behavior:
- p50 stable, p95/p99 spike then abrupt throughput drop.
- GPU util remains 45-65% but kernel queue lengths increase and host iowait rises to 12-25%.
- Autoscaler logs show alternating up/down decisions within a 3-minute window.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should avoid aggressive shrink when host IO/PCIe noise is detected; fall back to maintaining capacity until IO stabilizes.

Logs/metrics/attachments:
- SRE traces: link to Grafana panel (internal) - /d/Yx7Xk/tenant-io-usw2?panelId=9&from=1640&to=1660
- NVMe host metrics: transient write amp increases, SMART counters within normal range.
- Autoscaler events: recorded two shrink events during spike at 2026-03-09T02:14:22Z and 2026-03-09T02:15:51Z.
- Customer provided request IDs: [req-8f2c1a, req-8f2c9b, req-8f3a14] demonstrating timeouts.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- We advised enabling dedicated route pinning to a secondary pool (if configured) and increasing scale_down_delay to 5 minutes while we investigate. Customer applied pinning; immediate frequency of incidents reduced but not fully eliminated.

Investigation notes (SRE):
- Host-level IO bursts traced to another tenant performing periodic checkpoint compaction; IO pattern is low-frequency but high-burst, causing NVMe controller queue saturation and increasing PCIe latency to the serving hosts.
- Autoscaler uses combined signals (latency and slot_util). The shrink decision logic had a corner case: a single-slot low-utilization metric combined with transient latency caused a shrink when the latency signal should have been considered ephemeral.
- Placement rebalance/eviction path currently does not account for host iowait or NVMe backlog; evictions can exacerbate throughput collapse by invalidating warm caches.

Root cause hypothesis:
1) A co-located tenant's periodic compaction bursts cause host NVMe and PCIe latency spikes.
2) Autoscaler misinterprets composite signals and performs shrink during a noisy-IO window, causing slot fragmentation and cache coldstarts that lead to throughput collapse.

Next steps / action items:
- Short term (SRE): add a temporary rule to autoscaler to require latency spikes > T and sustained for 3 intervals before shrink; increase default scale_down_delay for affected dedicated pools to 300s. (Owner: Rahul)
- Short term (Support): finalize customer guidance on route pinning and recommend enabling IO QoS on host if customer has control. (Owner: Lena)
- Mid term (Infra): instrument autoscaler to consume host-level iowait and NVMe backlog metrics to avoid shrink during storage noise. (Owner: Platform/Infra team, PR referenced below)
- Follow-up: schedule cross-team postmortem and update runbook for noisy-IO patterns.

Resolution notes (ongoing):
- Temporary mitigations applied 2026-03-11; incident frequency reduced by ~70% for Nimbus. Mid-term infra work required to fully prevent recurrence.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:40 - Customer (Nimbus Analytics): Confirmed pinning to secondary pool reduced visible incidents but still seeing 1-2 drops/day. Asked for long-term fix and whether other customers on same hardware could be isolated.
Workaround applied (route pinning + increased scale_down_delay). Infra change planned to include host-level IO signals in autoscaler logic. Monitoring and postmortem scheduled.
Temporary mitigations reduced incident rate; final fix requires infra change to autoscaler. Cross-team follow up scheduled (postmortem) and runbook updated to include noisy-IO signature detection.
Pin routes to secondary pool and increased autoscaler scale_down_delay to 300s for pool dp-3920. Recommend host IO QoS if available to customer.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexiDocs reports that after a short network blip their web client reconnects to the SSE endpoint and the resumed stream is missing the last 2–3 list items in markdown output. The fragments before the gap are intact; the final bullet list is truncated and the JSON metadata end-marker appears, causing the client to treat the response as complete.

Impact:
- Customer-facing document generation flows produce incomplete bulleted lists (important for legal/contract generation).
- Intermittent: happens roughly 3–4x per 1000 streamed responses for this customer during peak hours.
- Customer is enterprise tier and reported because this affects results displayed directly to end users.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1) behind customer-managed proxy that does transparent TLS termination for client devices.
- Customer SDK: redwood-js 1.12.1 (browser), connecting via SSE.
- Affected models: redwood/open-instruct-3b and redwood-chat-medium-v2.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Send prompt that yields a multi-paragraph markdown output ending with a 4–6 item unordered list.
2) Induce a short network disruption (cellular switch or simulated 200–400ms stall) while the SSE stream is active.
3) Client reconnects and resumes using our SSE resume token; client implements exponential reconnect holdoff with a first backoff of 300ms.
4) Resumed response loads and final list only contains first 1–2 items; stream end marker is present.

Observed behavior:
- Server-sent resume contains a trailing heartbeat-only chunk immediately before finalization. When the client delays reconnect (holdoff), the edge-proxy coalesces that heartbeat with a small final token batch which results in a boundary where the client-side parser sees an empty choice or prematurely-closed metadata envelope. The JSON end-marker arrives but the last text fragments are missing in the assembled message.

Expected behavior:
- On resume, the complete generated content (including final list items) should be delivered and reassembled regardless of small client-side reconnect holdoffs. Heartbeats should not cause final token batches to be dropped or mis-ordered.

Logs / evidence provided by customer:
- Client-side event log (attached in original ticket) showing reconnect timeline and holdoff at ~310ms.
- SSE transcript from customer: last server chunk before blip includes "delta": "-" heartbeat-only marker, then finalization event.
- Sample server-side request-id: req-20260310-lexi-7f3b. Edge proxy trace shows a 350ms socket rebind and a coalesced write of two small buffers.

Investigation notes (initial):
- Support reproduced a narrow variant in staging by configuring the edge-proxy to coalesce small writes and reproducing the client reconnect holdoff pattern.
- Hypothesis: When the runtime flushes a zero-content heartbeat close to final token flush, the edge-proxy or intermediate TCP stack may coalesce frames; our SSE assembler sometimes drops a trailing minimal token buffer if it is delivered as an out-of-band Nagle/coalesced write when resume logic is invoked.
- Related behavior observed in logs: small-token write (<= 64 bytes) followed by keepalive then finalization; assembly path treats the small-token as ephemeral and discards it during resume state transition.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Recommend client update to redwood-js 1.12.3 which contains a client-side parser tolerance change (do not treat heartbeat-only fragments as terminal) and reduce initial reconnect backoff to 100ms.
- Suggested server-side mitigation: temporarily enable aggressive prefix-KV cache priming for LexiDocs routing (applied for their tenant for the next 48 hours).

Resolution plan / next steps:
1) Engineering to add a defensive fix in streaming-runtime to ensure heartbeat-only chunks are queued and flushed before finalization during resume transitions (backport candidate).
2) Add stricter test coverage for write coalescence scenarios (edge-proxy + Nagle) including unit tests and an integration scenario with simulated TCP coalescing.
3) Customer success follow-up to validate 1.12.3 client behavior and monitoring for next 72 hours.
4) If mitigations fail, plan a patch release to streaming-runtime + edge-proxy bake.

Estimated ETA: initial engineering triage complete by 2026-03-13; fix planned for 2026-03-20 if repro confirmed in canary.
payload.summary: Client reconnect holdoff causes missing trailing markdown list items on SSE resume

1) Use customer private deployment with identity-proxy configured to introspect tokens using OIDC introspection endpoint
2) Acquire a bearer token from their IdP (has admin:read admin:write scopes), call Redwood admin endpoint -> 403

identity-proxy [2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] DEBUG introspect: upstream status=200 content-type='text/plain; charset=utf-8' body='{"active":true,"scope":"admin:read admin:write"}'
identity-proxy [2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] WARN parse_introspection: unsupported content-type 'text/plain', falling back to safe-parse -> scopes_missing

03/10 16:00 GMT - Hypothesis: identity-proxy uses Content-Type to select parser; text/plain branch does not run JSON decode, leading to missing scope and RBAC denial.
03/11 09:30 GMT - Confirmed: curl -v against introspection returns header 'Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8' despite JSON body. Patch idea: relax parser to try JSON decode regardless of Content-Type header, with a safe timeout and size cap.
03/11 11:00 GMT - Repro script and unit tests added locally. Created debugging PR against identity-proxy. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1287

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightDocs reports intermittent high tail latency and occasional 504s starting after a traffic shift on 2026-03-09. Impact: Customer experiences increased p95/p99 generation latency for a core search summarization endpoint, impacting live users and batch jobs. Environment: Dedicated tenant in prod (us-east-1), route r-7a9c pinned to redwood-ggml-13B:v2026-02-28.

Observed behavior: During sustained ramp (approx 300->1200 qps over 10m) the platform began diverting ~18% of requests to a deprioritized CPU fallback variant and another ~12% to a newly-provisioned quantized variant that had not finished warmup. These routes showed serial warmups: each routed replica performed a multi-step KV and tensor cache population that blocked other warmups, producing queuing and per-request additional 400-1200ms. Customer metrics: p50 steady at ~120ms, p95 rose from 420ms to 1.8s, p99 spikes to 3.6s, and a 504 rate of ~0.7% for the 30m window.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady traffic at 300 qps for 20m to route r-7a9c. 2) Gradually ramp to 1200 qps over 10 minutes while monitoring Console -> Routes -> r-7a9c and Grafana panels 'serving_latency' and 'fallback_routing'. 3) Observe variant activation events in logs and look for 'activation_deferred' markers in routing-service traces.

Expected behavior: Newly-provisioned variants should warm in parallel up to configured concurrency gates or be shielded from receiving production traffic until KV cache is populated and model KV warmup completes. Fallback routing should prefer warm replicas with KV cache hot so as to avoid serial coldstart penalty.

Initial hypothesis: A recent change to the routing gating logic treats newly-created quantized variants as 'eligible' earlier than before when cluster capacity is constrained. This caused the scheduler to perform a 'best-effort' activation that returned a ready flag before KV warmup finished, allowing the routing layer to send traffic. Additionally, capacity gating deferred activation of a memory-optimized variant, moving traffic to a CPU fallback variant with higher per-request setup cost.

Relevant logs and dashboards: Console route: r-7a9c. Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/XyZ/serving-latency?var-route=r-7a9c. S3 logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-east/routing/2026-03-09/r-7a9c/*.log. Traces: https://jaeger.redwood.ai/trace/7f3b2... (see spans tagged routing-service/activation_deferred).
2026-03-09 14:22 - Support triage: Received alert from BrightDocs via support channel (#support) and verified increased tail latency in customer's telemetry. 2026-03-09 14:40 - On-call routed to Samir. Observed repeated log entries 'activation_deferred: reason=capacity_gate' correlated with time windows of autoscaler activity. 2026-03-09 15:05 - Replayed traffic pattern in staging and reproduced serial warmup behavior when route concurrency gate was set to 8 and autoscaler returned new replicas with 'ready=true' before KV warmup completion. 2026-03-10 09:12 - Engineering confirmed a change in routing-service PR 665 modified eligibility check to only require 'process_ready' rather than 'kv_warm_complete' under heavy autoscale conditions. 2026-03-11 11:30 - Experiment: temporarily increased gate to require 'kv_warm_complete' for eligible=true; tail latency returned to baseline in canary cluster.
Applied emergency config rollback on 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC to restore pre-PR-665 gating behavior (require kv_warm_complete before routing). Deployed a hotfix to routing-service (PR 723) to add a delayed-activation grace window: newly-created replicas are marked ineligible until KV warmup AND model-cache metrics pass thresholds or until a 30s shield expires. Monitored customer route for 48h; p95 fell back to ~400ms and 504s returned to <0.05%.
For impacted customers: pin route to a known-warm variant or temporarily increase 'min_warm_replicas' in Dedicated config. For BrightDocs we pinned to redwood-ggml-13B:v2026-02-14 and configured a 2x warm replica buffer while fix deployed.
1) Backfill automated test coverage for route eligibility that simulates KV warmup gating under autoscaler churn. 2) Add a dashboard alert for 'activation_deferred' spikes and a playbook link. 3) Consider adding per-tenant warm replica buffer controls for Dedicated customers. 4) Postmortem to be drafted and linked to this ticket. Owner: Samir. Target: postmortem draft by 2026-03-18.

2) Tab A starts an SSE chat stream (streaming chat completion with kv-cache priming).
3) Midway through generation, client triggers a reconnect (network hiccup / auth refresh).
4) Tab B starts a separate SSE stream using the same multiplexing session id pool.
5) Observe Tab A receives an immediate 'data: [DONE]' but the final "choice" JSON is truncated or contains duplicated fragments; Tab B sometimes receives a leading fragment from Tab A's final tokens.
6) Check server-side logs for session ids and kv-cache eviction/attach events for cross-correlation.
2026-03-10T18:22:44Z service=serving-runtime level=ERROR msg="stream finalize: kv-attach mismatch session=ms-4f2a trace=00-abc123..."
2026-03-10T18:22:44Z service=api-gateway level=INFO msg="sse disconnect: client=parcelly-frontend-3 conn_id=conn-77fbb keepalive=timedout"
2026-03-10T18:22:44Z service=kv-cache level=WARN msg="tombstone collision when reusing multiplex-slot id=slot-21 owner=ms-4f2a previous-owner=ms-9d8c"
2026-03-10T18:22:45Z service=serving-runtime level=INFO msg="emitting final-event: choice_partial=true session=ms-4f2a"

Additional notes:
Priya Nair (SRE) (2026-03-10): ACKed. Requested full server trace ids and the customer's multiplexing header values. Suspect multiplex slot reuse under race on reconnect.
Parcelly_Eng (2026-03-10): Provided client capture (EventSource timeline), observed final chunk trimmed and then appeared as leading fragment in new tab. Attached cURL/headers.
Olivia Park (Serving Runtime) (2026-03-11): Hypothesis: kv-cache tombstone TTL too low combined with race in session detachment leads to stale KV context being re-attached to a different logical session id. This can produce partial/duplicated choices when the earlier generator emits buffered tokens after tombstone.
Correlation: customer conn_id conn-77fbb correlates to internal trace 00-abc123... across API Gateway -> Runtime -> KV-Cache. Event timeline shows client reconnect at 2026-03-10T18:22:43Z, slot deallocation at 18:22:43.120Z, new allocation at 18:22:43.135Z (15ms overlap window).
Reproduction: We reproduced locally with a synthetic client that aggressively reconnects and reuses multiplexing slots. Observed partial 'choice' emission and kv-cache tombstone warnings. Reproducible when tombstone TTL set to 50ms and multiplex allocator uses LIFO free list.
Root cause hypothesis: Race between HTTP/LD connection teardown (client-side reconnect) and multiplex-slot free path. The allocator can hand the same multiplex id to a new session before the previous runtime has fully drained buffered tokens tied to that id's KV context. The KV tombstone flow then reattaches stale state to the new session, producing mixed fragments.
Risk surface: Affects multiplexed SSE and websocket streaming on dedicated pools under bursty reconnect patterns and behind proxies that cause short disconnects (Fastly TTLs, client-side auth refresh). Non-multiplexed paths not affected.
Telemetry: Added a temporary metric 'kv.tombstone_collision' and increased logging for slot lifecycle. Early counts show ~120 collisions/day in tenant Parcelly; global rate ~0.05% of streams on ded clusters.
Temporary mitigation tested: increase tombstone TTL to 200ms and add short grace window before reassigning freed slots. This reduces incidence locally (observed drop to ~0.1% repro) but increases slot pressure under heavy load.
Short-term workaround (applied to Parcelly's tenant on 2026-03-11): Enabled per-tenant conservative multiplexing by setting 'multiplex_reuse_grace_ms' = 250 and 'kv_tombstone_ttl_ms' = 300. Instructed customer to disable browser prefetching and reduce concurrent tab reconnect rate. Customer reported immediate UX improvement.
Medium-term fix (in progress): Serving-runtime change to decouple in-flight generator buffer ownership from multiplex slot id. Patch PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8145 introduces explicit session tokens attached to buffered frames and only allows slot reuse after session token eviction. Also adds stricter invariant checks and unit tests for rapid reconnect scenarios.
Rollout plan: PR merged to canary on 2026-03-12, monitoring dashboard created (kv.tombstone_collision, stream.final_truncated_rate). Full rollout to Dedicated fleets scheduled after 72h canary and load test validation.
payload.summary: Intermittent SSE half-closed stream with cross-session kv-cache leakage causing partial/duplicated choices

Issue summary:
Customer CloudCart reports intermittent routing to an older quantized model variant for a subset of users after we promoted a canary. The misrouting keeps sessions sticky to the legacy variant (gptx-3.2-quantized-legacy) despite traffic weights set to 0% for the legacy variant.

Impact:
- ~0.8% of requests from CloudCart's tenant for the last 6 hours returned outputs from the legacy quantized model (higher latency, different tokenization), causing content formatting regressions in production-facing features. No increased 5xxs, but quality regressions triggered user complaints.
- Customer on Enterprise/Dedicated tier; risk to SLA and possible rollback request.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (dedicated pool for CloudCart)
- Redwood routing v2.13, edge-proxy v1.8.3, serving-runtime v4.7
- Tenant header used for affinity: X-Tenant

Steps to reproduce (observed in production trace):
1) Send repeated conversations from affected tenant via customer edge (sample header below).
2) Observe sticky session mapping to legacy model over multiple requests, even after new variant is promoted and traffic weight set to 100%.

Observed request header (from ingress logs, redacted):
X-Tenant: cloudcart
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
User-Agent: CloudCart/2.4

Note: X-Tenant value above contains a trailing space ("cloudcart " ).

Observed behavior:
- Router affinity key normalization occurs upstream in edge-proxy. When the X-Tenant header includes trailing whitespace, the affinity digest generated at the edge differs from the digest used inside the routing service (routing service receives a trimmed header via internal proxy transformation). This mismatch allowed previously sticky sessions to remain bound to the older variant because the session lookup used the non-normalized digest.

Expected behavior:
- Header normalization should be consistent across all components (edge-proxy -> router -> serving), producing identical affinity keys and preventing stale variant sticky retention after a canary promotion.

Logs/traces/evidence:
- Ingress logs (edge-proxy) show requests with X-Tenant values with trailing whitespace for affected cohort (request ids: rq_7b2f, rq_7b3a, rq_7b5e).
- Router lookup logs show session lookup hash H1; edge-proxy shows hash H2 (H1 != H2).
- Serving logs for legacy model show incoming session binds referencing legacy variant id legacy-20260115.
- Link to incident trace: https://sentry.redwood.com/trace/trace-cc-20260219

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally by injecting trailing-space in X-Tenant; edge-proxy code path uses raw header to compute affinity digest, router receives header after an upstream nginx layer which trims whitespace. Root cause appears to be inconsistent normalization responsibilities split between edge-proxy and upstream layer during an earlier refactor (edge-proxy assumed no pre-normalization).
- Hypothesis: customer-side proxy sometimes appends newline/space to headers; we should be defensive.
- Verified that requests with exact same logical tenant but different whitespace map to separate affinity bins and therefore retain older model mapping.

Temporary workaround implemented:
- Applied a short-term edge-proxy config that trims whitespace for X-Tenant before digesting (edge-proxy config hotpatch deployed to prod us-east at 2026-02-19T17:10Z).
- Asked CloudCart to sanitize headers on their end; they confirmed a recent proxy version adds trailing spaces to some headers and will deploy a fix.

Resolution / Next steps:
- Rolled out permanent fix: updated edge-proxy to perform aggressive normalization (trim + collapse internal whitespace) for affinity headers. PRs merged: edge-proxy/pull/2041, router/pull/1219. Deployment schedule: staged rollout to us-east on 2026-02-22, followed by global rollout.
- Added router-side validation to log mismatched header digests to surface future occurrences and to trigger alerts when >0.1% discrepancy is observed.
- Plan to run a 48-hour audit of affinity mismatches across all dedicated pools and alert customers with high mismatch rates.

Follow-up/Action items:
- (SRE) Observe for 72 hours and confirm that legacy model traffic percentage for CloudCart falls to 0.0% (Diego)
- (DX) Update docs for header normalization expectations and recommend defensive client behavior (Maya)
- (Product) Consider exposing an API flag for tenant header normalization for Private deployments (PM meeting scheduled)

Comments / customer communication (excerpt):
- 2026-02-19 18:02 (Support - Maya): "We see a small cohort still hitting the legacy model. We've hotpatched edge to trim tenant headers and asked your proxy team to sanitize headers. We'll monitor and follow up."
- 2026-02-19 18:28 (CloudCart - support@cloudcart.com): "Thanks — our ops found the proxy bug (trailing-space) and will push a fix. Please let us know when the percentage falls below 0.1%."
- 2026-02-22 09:40 (SRE - Diego): "Staged rollout completed in us-east. Initial audit shows mismatch rate dropped from 0.8% -> 0.02%. Continuing monitoring."

Related artifacts:
- edge-proxy PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/2041
- router PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/1219
- Internal investigation notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Edge+Header+Normalization

Status update:
- Workaround applied and permanent fix deployed to us-east; monitoring shows expected improvement. Customer notified and satisfied with progress. Action items assigned for audit and docs update.
payload.summary: Trailing-space in tenant header causes session sticky to older model variant during canary promotion

Customer (NordBank ASA) requests a production-ready incremental SIEM export delivered in Avro container format with the following non-standard requirements: per-batch Ed25519 detached signatures, a machine-readable tenant_retention_map describing per-field retention/TTL and legal-hold flags, timezone-normalized deltas (UTC canonical plus local-bank timezone mapping for reconciliation), and a compliance evidence package (sample GLUE schema, checksum manifest, and answers to regulator questionnaire). The feed will be consumed by the bank's Splunk/ELK bridge and must be demonstrably replayable and verifiable for audit. Impact: customer cannot onboard until signed-manifest and retention semantics are validated by their security and legal teams. Request is time-sensitive due to upcoming regulator audit window.
1) Customer-provided sink: SFTP endpoint and initial auth keys.
2) Customer requests hourly deltas partitioned by tenant and day, Avro container per hour.
3) Each Avro file must be accompanied by a small JSON manifest (manifest_v1) with fields: batch_id, start_ts, end_ts, record_count, sha256_checksum, and detached ed25519_signature.
4) Customer will validate signature and checksum and run reconciliation against their local timezone representation.
5) Support/SRE to provide sample payloads and signature verification script for bank to test.
sample_manifest.json
{
  "batch_id": "nb-20260310-13-tenant42",
  "start_ts": "2026-03-10T13:00:00Z",
  "end_ts": "2026-03-10T13:59:59Z",
  "record_count": 842,
  "sha256_checksum": "3a7c1f1d9c...ef4b",
  "signature_algorithm": "ed25519-detached",
  "signature": "MEUCIQDf...QKBgQ=="
}

Note: above is illustrative; actual signature bytes will be base64 of ed25519 detached signature.
2026-03-10 - NordBank (security@ nordbank.no): We need a signed manifest for every hourly Avro chunk; our SIEM bridge will reject unsigned batches.
2026-03-10 - Support (Ava Chen): Acknowledged. Opening triage ticket and validating that ed25519 signing is supported by our signing-service. We will provide sample files and a verification script. ETA for initial sample: 48 hours.
2026-03-11 - Eng (Ravi Patel): Preliminary triage: platform signing-service currently issues RSA-PSS signatures via KMS-backed keys. Native ed25519 support is not live in managed signing-service. Two paths: (A) emit RSA-PSS manifest today (accepted by some customers) and include verification script; (B) implement ed25519 signing flow (requires HSM/KMS support + deployment) — estimate 2-3 weeks. Asking customer whether RSA-PSS is acceptable as interim.
2026-03-11 - NordBank (security@ nordbank.no): RSA-PSS is acceptable only if legal/ops can verify non-repudiation and key provenance; they prefer ed25519 but can accept RSA for POC if we supply chain evidence and timestamped manifests.
2026-03-12 - Support (Ava Chen): Uploaded POC Avro file + RSA-PSS signed manifest to private S3 share and provided verification script. Requested NordBank SFTP creds to test direct delivery and confirmation that retention_map format meets their compliance team's needs.
- Confirmed signing-service uses AWS KMS RSA keys (RSA-PSS) and cannot produce ed25519 without feature work.
- HSM/KMS vendors used by dedicated/private customers support ed25519 via customer-managed keys (on-prem or BYOK) — we can support ed25519 in Private deployments sooner.
- Workaround: issue detached RSA-PSS manifest and include X.509 chain + RFC3161 timestamp token to satisfy audit.
- Need to define tenant_retention_map schema (proposed fields: tenant_id, field_name, retention_days, pii_class, legal_hold boolean, deletion_action). Shared Confluence draft linked above.
Triage complete. Interim workaround provided: RSA-PSS signed manifests with RFC3161 timestamp tokens and full X.509 key provenance bundle uploaded to customer S3 share for POC. Engineering scope item created to add ed25519 signing support to signing-service (tracked separately). Next steps: 1) NordBank to provide SFTP host/key for end-to-end test; 2) Support to confirm retention_map JSON schema with customer's compliance lead; 3) If NordBank requires ed25519 for production, escalate to PM/Infra for prioritized KMS/HSM work.

Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-13 18:15 PDT we observed a repeating sawtooth pattern of elevated 5xx responses on a small set of routes serving VoltCommerce (dedicated tenant). Errors manifest as 502/503 from the API gateway with corresponding runtime exits on a subset of serving hosts. Impact: Several VoltCommerce production customers reporting increased failed requests for chat and embeddings over an ~2 hour window; throughput degraded and tail latency increased >3x. Environment: prod us-west-2, dedicated pool (tenant-voltcommerce-reserved). Immediate symptoms: API gateway 502 spikes aligned with keepalive connection churn; runtimes show GPU OOM events and watchdog restarts. Steps to reproduce (observed): repeated small-interval client reconnects + long-lived streaming sessions from VoltCommerce SDK reproduce an accept-queue surge in our staging harness and cause the same runtime OOM pattern.
1) With a dedicated tenant config, open ~600 concurrent streaming sessions from single IP using VoltCommerce SDK v2.1 with keepalive interval 15s
2) Send short prompts (~50 tokens) in bursts (10 reqs/sec per connection) for 5-10 minutes
3) Observe apigw accept queue growth, keepalive half-open sockets increase, and runtime prefetch cancellation events
4) After a delay, runtime initiates background NVMe snapshot (observed on affected hosts) which coincides with a GPU memory spike and subsequent cuda OOM / process kill
5) API gateway surfaces 502/503 for in-flight requests while runtime restarts
[2026-03-13T18:17:02Z] apigw accept_queue: depth=520 -> 1120 (spike)
[2026-03-13T18:17:07Z] runtime-serve[pid=4231]: prefetch: cancel(token_id=0x7f9) - latency=120ms
[2026-03-13T18:17:12Z] nvme-snapshot: started background compact on /dev/nvme0n1p3
[2026-03-13T18:17:12Z] runtime-serve[pid=4231]: cuda: out of memory when allocating 512MB (free=48MB) -> SIGABRT
[2026-03-13T18:17:13Z] systemd: runtime-serve.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=6/ABRT
[2026-03-13T18:17:14Z] apigw: returning 502 to client (upstream closed) route=/v1/chat/stream tenant=voltcommerce
Initial hypothesis: keepalive/reconnect storm causes apigw accept queue growth, causing many short-lived handoffs to runtimes and frequent prefetch cancellations. Prefetch cancellation + high socket churn increases memory pressure in serving runtime. On affected hosts we observed background nvme snapshot compaction starting concurrently with peak churn which appears to delay disk I/O and trigger higher pinned GPU memory (shard rehydration path). The combination pushes runtime GPU allocation past threshold and triggers cuda OOM. Evidence: host metrics (link below) show GPU memory climbing ~10% immediately after nvme compaction started; dmesg shows NVML logs and CUDA OOM. Mitigations attempted: temporary tenant rate cap (applied at 18:22) reduced accept queue depth and error rate; rolling restart of two affected runtime instances removed hosts stuck in crash loop. Current working theory: two correlated factors (excessive keepalive churn + coincident nvme background task) produce transient resource spike. Follow-ups: schedule nvme snapshot compaction outside peak hours for dedicated pools, add apigw early-shed for high keepalive churn, and add guardrail in serving runtime to fail fast on prefetch-heavy sequences to avoid OOM.
2026-03-13 18:30 - Support (Aisha Patel): Triage complete. Applied temporary rate cap for tenant 'voltcommerce' and notified customer. Added labels and paged SRE.
2026-03-13 18:42 - SRE (Miguel Santos): Collected host-level traces (perf, nvme stats, nvidia-smi logs) and attached to runtime PR for further debug. Observed nvme compaction overlapping with OOMs on 3 hosts: ip-10-1-5-12, ip-10-1-6-44, ip-10-1-6-55.
2026-03-13 19:05 - Eng (Priya Nair): Reproduced accept queue growth with test harness using VoltCommerce SDK. Confirmed prefetch cancellation increases pinned GPU memory in the model loader path. Raising a follow-up INT ticket for snapshot scheduling change.
2026-03-13 19:30 - Customer (VoltCommerce - Laura Chen): We saw elevated errors starting ~18:16 PDT; thank you for the quick rate cap. Please advise on ETA for full mitigation and whether we should adjust client-side keepalive behavior.

Additional notes:
1) Engineering to add defensive prefetch memory ceiling and fast-fail path in runtime (owner: @pri-serve) - target patch by 2026-03-18
2) Infra to change NVMe compaction/snapshot cron to avoid 17:00-20:00 PDT for dedicated pools (owner: @infra-schedulers) - schedule change by 2026-03-16

4) Create INT follow-up to add apigw early-shed rule for high keepalive churn (owner: SRE)
Mitigation in progress: tenant rate cap and rolling restarts reduced error rate. Engineering and Infra follow-ups scheduled. Will update when runtime patch and compaction schedule change are deployed.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer FitAssist reported a sudden weekend spike in billable token usage attributed to a burst window on their dedicated pool. They noticed the spike coincided with a scheduled batch job and an out-of-hours traffic surge. Customer believes some tokens were double-counted when requests were routed between mixed-priority queues (interactive + batch).

Impact:
- Unexpected ~$3.2k charge on invoice dated 2026-03-09 for weekend usage window (period 2026-03-07 to 2026-03-08).
- Customer currently on Dedicated plan with reserved capacity and burst-of-spot enabled. This is a material billing concern for finance and the customer’s procurement.

Timeline (provided by customer):
- 2026-03-07 22:10 UTC: scheduled nightly batch launches (batch queue).
- 2026-03-07 22:12 UTC: sudden increase in interactive traffic from QA run (interactive queue).
- 2026-03-07 22:12–22:45 UTC: spike in metering events and token counts recorded in billing export (attached by customer).
- 2026-03-09: customer received invoice with unexplained line item "Burst Capacity - emergency".

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run a small interactive workload from dev host while a larger batch job runs.
2) Observe per-request routing to mixed-priority queues with fallback to burst capacity when reserved pool nears saturation.
3) Export metering usage for the time window; customer sees repeated entries for same request IDs with different route tags.

Logs / Observations from customer (attached):
- CSV of usage events showing duplicated request_id values across two route tags: "interactive" and "batch-fallback".
- Sample API traces showing a single client request that retried and then completed; both attempts appear billed.

Expected behavior:
- Retries or fallbacks should be deduplicated for billing where they correspond to the same logical request within X seconds (configurable), or at least attributed to the original route without double-counting token consumption.

Additional context:
- Customer uses prefix caching for interactive requests and larger sequence lengths for batch jobs. They enabled burst-on-demand in their dedicated pool to absorb spikes. They prefer a billing adjustment for the weekend spike and guidance on configuration to avoid recurrence.

2026-03-10 | Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged receipt and opened SUP-36321. Asked customer for invoice number, CSV of usage export, and example request IDs. Noted SLA window. Status: Triage.
2026-03-10 | Customer (FitAssist - billing@fitassist.com): Provided invoice INV-2026-03-09-772 and CSV with 18 candidate request_ids. Customer requests credit for duplicate-billed tokens and a short RCA so they can explain to procurement.
2026-03-10 | Support (Luis Navarro): Escalated to infra/metering. Linked INT-4271 to surface recent changes to mixed-queue routing. Requested meter team to check deduplication and billing attribution logic; attached PRs for recent routing changes.
2026-03-11 | Infra (SRE - Mei Chen): Confirmed detection of concurrent routing state during 2026-03-07 22:12 UTC window. Notes: an autoscaler event caused temporary overlap where requests were proxied to both interactive frontends and the batch runner for a small subset; meter wrote two usage events for the same internal correlation id. Working hypothesis: correlation_id was not propagated in one fallback path, preventing dedupe at billing aggregation stage.
2026-03-11 | Billing (Rajiv Singh): Tally of candidate duplicates yields ~98k tokens duplicated equating to $3,230. Proposing a manual credits adjustment and improving the aggregator to dedupe on correlation_id + request_hash for 30s windows.
2026-03-12 | Support (Luis Navarro): Applied a one-time invoice credit of $3,230 and created ticket BILL-1126 for accounting to post credit memo against INV-2026-03-09-772. Confirmed credit applied and customer notified. Recommend follow-ups to infra and metering teams for code fix and improved tests.
2026-03-12 | Customer (FitAssist): Acknowledged receipt of credit and thanked the team. Requests notice when fix is deployed and asks for recommended config changes to avoid recurrence.
Summary of technical findings:
- Root cause: race window caused by autoscaler + mixed-queue router change in infra PR #884 where in-flight requests could be proxied through two code paths. The metering agent emitted two usage events for the same logical request because the fallback path did not preserve the original correlation_id header.
- Reproducer: synthetic test created that runs heavy batch traffic with intermittent interactive pings; confirmed duplicate events in local staging.
- Short-term mitigation: billing-side filter to dedupe events by correlation_id + truncated request_hash for 30s.
- Long-term fix: change in router to always copy correlation_id into fallback requests and add unit/integration tests (metering PR #210).

Action taken: Applied a one-time credit for $3,230. Accounting ticket BILL-1126 created to attach credit memo to the customer's invoice. Infra changes: merged hotfix to ensure correlation_id is copied into fallback routes (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/884) and metering aggregator updated to dedupe within 30s windows (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/210).
Preventative steps: add e2e test harness for mixed-queue routing, update runbooks to temporarily disable burst-on-demand for vulnerable pools during large scheduled batch jobs, and notify customers about recommended config (set burst-grace-period to 60s).
Follow-up: Monitor billing export for two weeks post-deploy; assigned INT-4271 for infra verification and BILL-1126 for finance closure. Customer confirmed refund/credit received on 2026-03-12. Ticket closed.
We identified a short race condition in the routing layer that caused some requests to be billed twice during an autoscaler event. We issued a credit for the duplicated usage and deployed fixes to prevent recurrence. If you see any further unexpected charges, please reply and we'll investigate immediately.

Issue summary: Customer reports that a provisional credit previously issued for hourly smoothing was reversed automatically during an overnight billing run, causing the account to show a negative invoice balance and triggering an automatic payment hold. Issue summary: At ~2026-03-10T12:05Z we began a canary/staged rollout of a model variant (redwood-compat-v1 -> gptx-3-large) for BrightHealth AI's dedicated pool in us-east. Within ~3 minutes we observed a sustained spike in 5xx responses from the API gateway and increased upstream serving-runtime failures. Impact: BrightHealth AI reports ~30% error rate on /v1/generate endpoints, failures for synchronous requests, and streaming disconnects for chat sessions. Severity is customer-impacting (production traffic).

Impact details:
- Error profile: 502 and 503 from gateway, 500 and OOM/crash traces from serving-runtime workers, intermittent 504s from the load-balancer.
- Time window: 2026-03-10T12:08Z -> ongoing (mitigations applied 12:25Z).
- Customer-visible: failed inference calls, delayed processing of user requests, some webhook retries failing.

Environment: Dedicated pool for BrightHealth AI, prod, region us-east. Autoscaler configured for GPU-backed nodes with burst capacity. Canary rollout used 10% traffic routing to new variant.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Triggered canary rollout at 12:05Z routing 10% of customer traffic to gptx-3-large.
2) At ~12:08Z api-gateway started returning elevated 502/503. Circuit-breaker metrics showed rapid open events.
3) Serving-runtime logs show repeated worker restarts and OOM-like traces aligned with the model variant requests.
4) Autoscaler attempted to spin up additional nodes but observed Pod crash loops and failed readiness probes leading to capacity flapping.
5) Gateway escalated throttling and fallback policies for some routes, increasing 429s briefly then reverting to 5xx.

Relevant logs and telemetry:
- Kibana link (serving-runtime): https://logs.redwood.internal/app/kibana#/discover?_a=(query:(match:(message:(query:'oom|segfault|worker restart|gptx-3-large'))))
- Grafana dashboard (api-gateway error rates): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/AGW/error-rates?var-region=us-east
- SLO alert: api-gateway-p50-latency spike 12:09Z (alert ID: AGW-4271).
- Sample runtime stderr: "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc' at inference_loop.cc:412" (attached in incident bundle).

Initial hypothesis: The new model variant has a higher peak memory working set under the request mix used by BrightHealth AI, causing GPU memory pressure and worker process crashes. This combined with aggressive autoscaler/backoff and circuit-breaker thresholds at the gateway produced cascading 5xx errors. Secondary hypothesis: a kernel/driver mismatch in the dedicated pool exacerbated memory fragmentation under the new quantization layout.

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- 12:18Z: Scaled the canary back to 0% for BrightHealth AI (rollback candidate prepared).
- 12:20Z: Increased serving-runtime replica restart backoff and disabled quick-retry loops to reduce thrash.
- 12:23Z: Temporarily raised gateway circuit-breaker thresholds for the customer route to allow in-flight traffic to drain.
- 12:25Z: Eng started a hotfix branch to limit model cache pre-allocation.

Current status and next steps:
- Eng (runtime) to reproduce crash locally with a BrightHealth-like request corpus (action: Marcus Green).
- SRE to validate node driver/kernel versions in the BrightHealth dedicated fleet and check for recent node reboots (action: Liu Chen).
- Support to coordinate with BrightHealth AI on observed request characteristics and to verify whether they can hold traffic for a planned rollback to previous model (action: Ava Patel).
- If reproducer confirms memory pressure, proceed with model config changes (reduce batch size, disable certain ops) and re-run canary with expanded telemetry.

Customer communication: Notified BrightHealth AI at 12:22Z that we saw elevated errors and are investigating; provided ETA for next update 12:45Z.

Attachments: incident bundle (runtime crash dumps), sampling of failing request IDs, flamegraphs for model step.

Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10 12:08 UTC we observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses from the hosted API for a set of dedicated customers. Impact: Customer-facing requests for BrightWrite (dedicated tenant) experienced timeouts and 502/503 responses; streaming sessions were abruptly reset, and embeds/bulk operations observed retries. Environment: production us-east, dedicated pool for BrightWrite. Initial hypothesis: API gateway token bucket exhaustion combined with upstream runtime entering a CPU-bound hot-loop while processing prefetch invalidations, leading to backpressure and retry amplification.
1) Send a mixed workload from a single tenant with concurrent small-chat streams (keepalive) + large embedding batch uploads at 400 req/s
2) Ensure model pinning to redwood/gptx-13b-instruct and prefetch enabled
3) Observe gateway metrics and runtime process CPU/RSS over a sustained burst (2-10 minutes)

Observed correlation between large embedding bulk uploads (300MB payloads) and token-bucket refill lag on apigw for the dedicated tenant.
Prefetch-cache sweep routine triggered simultaneous invalidations for the tenant's pinned model; several runtime workers entered a tight loop handling invalidation tombstones (heap churn + CPU spike).
API gateway responded to upstream slowness by tightening token bucket allocation which created a feedback loop: more clients retried, causing broader enqueue growth and runtime saturation.
No recent deploys to serving-runtime in the 24h preceding the incident; a config sweep to prefetch thresholds rolled out earlier at 08:00 UTC but looked low risk (rollout ID infra-roll/2026-03-10-08).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long multi-turn chat sessions over SSE multiplexed connections intermittently go silent for ~25-40s mid-generation and then the client receives a 504 or connection reset. This affects sessions that use connection multiplexing (multiple user conversations over a single persistent connection) and often occurs after an earlier token-at-a-time progress period.

Impact:
- Affected customer: Veridian Analytics (dedicated tier) sees production users' chat sessions aborting mid-response 3-12 times per hour for heavy sessions.
- User visible: long pauses mid-generation followed by connection error or truncated final token.
- Business impact: product feature degradation for ~200 active users during peak window; P1.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-10 09:12: first support report received from Veridian via in-app ticket
- 2026-03-10 09:20: Support reproduced on a staging multiplexed client and opened incident
- 2026-03-10 10:00: SRE collected tcpdump + proxy metrics; observed windowing/backpressure behavior on streaming-proxy
- 2026-03-10 11:30: temporary mitigation deployed (shorter keepalive, disabled conn reuse for warm workers)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open single persistent SSE connection from client that multiplexes three chat sessions over it.
2) Execute a long multi-turn prompt that triggers ~1200-1600 token generation with streaming enabled.
3) Observe intermittent long idle periods (~25-40s) after an initial burst of tokens, then a 504 or socket reset.

Observed behavior:
- Streaming starts, tokens stream for a short time, then an extended silence of 25-40s with no bytes sent.
- On client side we see the SSE connection still ESTABLISHED but no events. After ~30-40s the client either attempts reconnect and sees 504 from api-gateway or receives FIN from upstream.
- Proxy metrics show large send-window stalls and HTTP/2 stream-level flow-control spikes correlating with the silence.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous token-by-token streaming without long silent gaps; keepalive or application-level heartbeats should prevent silent disconnects.

Relevant logs / traces:
- streaming-proxy: repeated "http2: stream blocked by flow control" messages around 10:04:23 UTC (see attached probe logs).
- api-gateway: 504 backend timeout at 10:04:58 UTC for the affected SSE connection id 02f9e3c.
- serving-runtime: minor GC pauses reported, but not at scale to explain 30s stalls; p50 token latencies remain <200ms prior to the idle.
- tcpdump: retransmission bursts preceding the silent period with zero window updates for ~18s, then a sudden ACK and bulk of bytes.

Workaround applied by SRE:
- Increased keepalive ping frequency between streaming-proxy and backend from 60s -> 10s for Veridian's dedicated workers.
- Disabled HTTP/2 connection reuse for the stream path in the proxy for the customer's worker pool to prevent head-of-line connection stalls.
- Deployed configuration to only apply to the dedicated pool to limit blast radius.

Next steps / long-term:
- Deep-dive network-level trace with packet-level instrumentation across proxy -> worker -> runtime to identify root cause of flow-control stalling.
- Implement improved window-update handling in streaming-proxy and surface connection-backpressure metrics to console.
- Consider TLS session pinning or separate per-chat connections as a hard fix for multiplex scenarios until proxy flow-control rework ships.

Attachments: tcpdump excerpt, proxy metrics dashboard links, customer request ID list

Preliminary SRE analysis suggests HTTP/2 stream flow-control and proxy connection reuse are interacting poorly under sustained long-tail generations and multiplexing. Hypothesis: when one multiplexed stream experiences transient client backpressure, the proxy's reuse + http2 flow-control stops sending window updates for other streams on the same connection, causing those streams to stall until a window update or new connection is created. No evidence yet of runtime token-generation hang. Also observed occasional bursts of retransmits from the customer's VPN appliance correlated with stalls.
Actions taken: enabled aggressive keepalives, disabled conn reuse for affected pool, increased connection pool size for dedicated workers. Collected additional packet captures for deeper analysis.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): 'Attached tcpdump shows prolonged zero window on the proxy->backend TCP flow. Posting preliminary packet-level chart to incident board.'
Mitigation in place: keepalive shortened and HTTP/2 connection reuse disabled for affected dedicated pool. Monitoring shows reduced frequency but not zero. Working on proxy fix to improve stream-level window-update behavior. Customer notified and monitoring dashboard shared.
Short-term mitigation decreased customer-visible incidents by ~80% during initial 24h observation. Root cause likely interaction between multiplexed SSE usage and proxy HTTP/2 flow-control; code change to streaming-proxy planned (PR referenced above). Postmortem to be filed after final fix deploy.
payload.summary: Multiplexed SSE client experiences prolonged idle spike then silent disconnect during long multi-turn chat

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when their async Python client sends a streaming generation request that triggers an external tool/function call (via function-calling), a client-side retry (triggered by a client timeout/error) results in the external tool being invoked twice.

Impact: Duplicate downstream side-effects (webhook notifications and payment capture) at a paying enterprise customer. Reproducible in production for NarrativeHealth, ~3x/day, causing billing and safety concerns.

Environment: Redwood dedicated prod cluster (us-east), customer using SDK v0.9.12 (python), streaming=True, function_call enabled, custom tool adapter that executes an HTTP POST to customer finance endpoint.

Expected behavior: Retry should be idempotent for function/tool calls if caller provides idempotency key or if the SDK handles function-calling idempotency for streaming flows. The second attempt should not trigger duplicate external side-effects.

Actual behavior: When the initial streaming response fails mid-stream (client-side read timeout or connection reset) and the client retries the call, the platform executes the function/tool callback again. The SDK retry path currently re-sends the request without a stable idempotency token for the function call portion, resulting in duplicate external requests.

Steps to reproduce (minimal):
1) Use python async SDK v0.9.12 with streaming=True and an async wrapper that retries on TimeoutError after 2s.
2) Provide a function schema for a single endpoint that triggers an outbound POST (customer tool).
3) Start generation and simulate network flakiness by killing the streaming connection mid-response (e.g., drop TCP or raise asyncio.TimeoutError in client).
4) Client retry kicks in and re-sends request. Observe two POSTs received by the external tool.

Relevant logs and snippets (customer-provided):
```# simplified pseudo-code
async def call_model_with_retry(prompt):
    try:
        async for chunk in client.generate_stream(prompt, streaming=True, functions=[...]):
            process(chunk)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        # client retry
        await client.generate(prompt, streaming=False, functions=[...])
```
Received webhook POSTs at: 2026-03-11T15:04:12Z and 2026-03-11T15:04:15Z for the same prompt_id.

Customer has temporarily disabled streaming and uses non-streaming calls as a mitigation. They are requesting a permanent fix or recommended guidance for safe retries with streaming and function-calling.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - Customer (NarrativeHealth - infra@nh.example): Provided request_id=nh-prod-7f3b, sample payloads, and noted SDK usage pattern above. Confirmed duplicate POSTs are causing payment gateway reconciliations to fail.
2026-03-14 - Support: Shared workaround while we investigate: (1) Disable streaming for requests that trigger external side-effects; (2) Use SDK-provided idempotency_key parameter on function calls (if available) to ensure dedup on the tool side; (3) Set client-side retry to only retry non-committing operations. Customer applied (1) and saw duplicates stop.
2026-03-14 - Engineering (Diego): Drafted internal plan: (A) Short-term: add SDK helper ensure_function_call_idempotency() that injects a stable x-redwood-func-id header before the request is sent, including for streaming flows; (B) Long-term: modify runtime to register pending function calls earlier in the request lifecycle so retries can be reconciled. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/418 .
Reproduction: Local reproducer built by engineering. Failure mode reproduces when stream is interrupted between model token emission and function_call completion acknowledgement.
Root cause hypothesis: Race between streaming lifecycle and function-call idempotency registration. SDK currently waits for function_call completion to attach stable idempotency metadata to the request context; if the client aborts mid-stream, there is no recorded idempotency token and a retry generates a fresh call_id.
Serving logs: Observed two function_call_start events with different call_id for same client request hash. No server-side dedup key present in the earlier attempt.
SDK codepath: async streaming path splits generation and function-calling flow; retry wrapper re-enters top-level generate call and does not reuse previous function-call metadata unless the caller provided an idempotency_key.
Workaround provided to customer: disable streaming for endpoint that triggers external side-effects OR provide an explicit idempotency_key in the request's function call metadata. Customer accepted workaround and reverted to non-streaming for now.
Short-term fix: SDK patch to v0.9.13 will expose helper argument function_idempotency_key and will set a stable header (x-redwood-func-id) for streaming requests before the first chunk is sent. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/418 (under review).
Long-term action: runtime change to register pending function calls earlier so that retries can be reconciled independent of streaming completion. Tracked in INT-512.
Follow-ups: QA test covering streaming interruption + retry + function-calling added to pre-release test matrix. Notify NarrativeHealth when v0.9.13 is released; schedule a post-deploy verification window with customer for 48 hours.
