Issue summary
- Customer reports Redwood webhook delivery failures to their callback endpoint with SSL/TLS validation errors.
- Failures began after customer-side infrastructure changes (new load balancer / certificate rotation) per customer report.

Customer impact
- Webhook events (job completion + alert notifications) not being delivered consistently.
- Customer is missing downstream automation triggers; manual reconciliation required.

Customer environment
- Tier: Dedicated
- Region: us-east
- Callback URL (redacted): https://<customer-domain>/redwood/webhooks
- Customer notes: traffic terminates at a managed LB/CDN layer; origin is internal.

What we see (Redwood side)
- Redwood delivery attempts failing during TLS handshake / certificate validation.
- Error variants observed in delivery logs:
  - "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"
  - "x509: certificate is not valid for any names, but wanted to match <customer-domain>"
  - "remote error: tls: handshake failure" (intermittent)
- Retries continue per webhook retry policy; no indication of Redwood-side outage.

Request IDs / evidence
- Example delivery attempt IDs (internal): wh_deliv_7c2d9f1a, wh_deliv_7c2da41e
- Sample timestamps (UTC): 2026-02-13 16:42–17:10

Support-safe troubleshooting checklist (customer-facing)
1) Confirm the callback URL and hostname
   - Ensure the hostname in the webhook URL exactly matches the certificate CN/SAN (including subdomain).
   - If the endpoint recently changed (new LB / new subdomain), update the webhook configuration to match.

2) Verify the certificate is publicly trusted
   - Redwood webhook delivery validates certificates against standard public trust stores.
   - Self-signed certificates and private/internal CAs are not supported for webhook callbacks.
   - Cloud/CDN “origin certificates” that are not publicly trusted can cause "unknown authority" failures.

3) Ensure the server presents the full certificate chain (leaf + intermediate)
   - Common failure: server only returns the leaf cert and omits the intermediate.
   - Ask the customer to verify using:
     - openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername <host> -showcerts
   - Confirm the output includes the intermediate certificate(s) needed to build a chain to a trusted root.

4) Check TLS policy compatibility
   - Ensure TLS 1.2+ is enabled.
   - Avoid requiring mTLS (client certificates). Redwood webhooks do not present a client certificate.
   - Ensure SNI is enabled/handled correctly on the LB (server should select the cert for the requested hostname).

5) Confirm there is no redirect or HTTP-to-HTTPS loop
   - Redwood follows standard redirects conservatively; redirects to a different hostname can fail hostname validation.
   - Ensure the callback returns 2xx within the expected timeout window.

6) If using a CDN/WAF
   - Ensure the CDN/WAF is configured to accept requests from Redwood and is not downgrading or re-terminating TLS incorrectly.
   - If the CDN uses an origin cert, ensure the edge cert (public-facing) is what Redwood connects to.

What Support needs from the customer (if still failing)
- Output of: openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername <host> -showcerts (with any private keys removed)
- Confirmation of TLS versions enabled and whether mTLS is required
- Whether the endpoint is behind Cloudflare/Akamai/ALB/NLB (provider + mode)
- A timestamp window of failures and the current callback URL

Internal notes / escalation guidance
- If errors indicate chain/hostname issues, do not escalate to SRE until customer confirms a valid publicly trusted cert and complete chain.
- Escalate to Platform (Control Plane) if we suspect webhook configuration mismatch, redirect behavior, or if delivery attempt logs contradict customer reports.
- If multiple customers report similar TLS failures across regions within a short time window, move to #incidents and page SRE per escalation playbook.

Current ask
- Validate whether the customer’s endpoint is presenting a complete chain and a certificate valid for the configured hostname.
- Provide customer with the checklist above and request openssl output.

Provided initial guidance: check full chain + SAN/hostname match; requested openssl output.","2026-02-13 18:05Z — Owen Phillips (Support): Pulled internal delivery log snippets: majority are x509 unknown authority; a smaller subset shows hostname mismatch. Suggests either wrong endpoint/redirect or cert not matching host.","2026-02-14 09:18Z — Ethan Park (Platform): Confirmed Redwood webhook client uses standard public trust store; no custom CA bundles; does not support mTLS for outgoing webhooks. Redirects to different hostname will fail hostname validation. Repeat with range not overlapping compaction -> export contains all rows.
CSV file finishes at event timestamp 2026-03-09T02:14:58Z, later events in raw event store exist up to 02:29:58Z but are absent from export. Export job exits with success code and no error in UI.
Ad-hoc CSV export should include all events in the inclusive time range requested by the user, regardless of retention compaction schedule. Export job should operate against data snapshot consistent for the requested interval.

2026-03-09T02:15:13Z [export-worker] export job id=exp_7b3a9 started query end_time=2026-03-09T02:30:00Z
2026-03-09T02:15:14Z [retention-compactor] replacing raw_events shard=17 with rollup buckets up to 02:15:00Z

2026-03-09T02:17:02Z [query-service] raw query returned rows=1248 for same range

Query plan shows exporter route prefers optimized rollup table only when compaction marker exists. Possible root cause: compaction sets compaction_marker for shard before rollup write completes, causing exporter to route away from rollup data for timestamps >= marker. Engineering reproducer created and PR drafted to add a short-lived snapshot lock and to adjust exporter routing logic to consult compaction transaction boundaries.

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-05 03:10 UTC Acme Analytics observed a rapid increase in 429 responses across their bulk-ingest jobs. The errors correlate with scheduled ephemeral API key rotation and concurrent health-check sweeps from their orchestrator. Impact: ~40% of chunked uploads were rejected with 429s over a 45-minute window; ingestion lag increased and downstream retry waves amplified tenant token exhaustion. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved), prod-us-west, tenant id T-ACME-77. Customer reports they did not change upload concurrency during the window. They are blocked from completing nightly backfills.
1) Configure a bulk upload orchestrator with 200 parallel workers pointing at the dedicated pool route
2) Enable ephemeral key rotation every 5 minutes (short-lived credentials) and immediate re-registration of worker sessions
3) Ensure the orchestrator has health-check probes configured to ping the /ready endpoint every 10s across all workers
4) Trigger a large split upload (250GB split into ~5000 chunks) and observe rate-limiter metrics and 429 counts

2026-03-05T03:10:17Z tenant=T-ACME-77 worker=orchestrator-3 event=retry_backoff reason=429 next_try_in=120s

Additional notes:
Customer (Acme Support, 2026-03-05): Confirmed orchestrator rotates keys every 5 minutes and health checks are across all workers. Asked for configuration recommendations to avoid losing burst credits.
Timeline: 03:10:12 rotate_keys -> 03:10:13 immediate reconnects -> 03:10:15 token bucket drained -> 03:10:17 first retry wave
Metric correlation: tenant_token_bucket shows negative burst balance starting 03:10:15 for ~45 minutes. edge-proxy logs show simultaneous TCP reconnects from ~180 workers leading to duplicate preflight/accounting for short window.
Hypothesis A: Ephemeral key rotation triggers worker re-registration calls that are counted against tenant quota and are not deduped during short windows, amplifying short-lived fanout.
Hypothesis B: Health-check probes are treated as regular requests on the same route and consume burst credits; combined with rebind traffic they push the tenant over the refill threshold.
Reproduction: Dev ran a simulated rotation+probe burst in staging with 120 simulated workers and reproduced 429 spike when rotation + probes overlapped. Verified mitigation by either staggering rotation or routing health-checks to admin path that uses internal exemption pool.
Cross-reference: Related to SUP-712999 (control-plane mirror private vpc opaque 429s) for cases where control-plane traffic is counted against tenant; see runbook link below.
Short-term mitigation applied: increased tenant burst allowance on dedicated pool for 30 minutes and advised customer to pause bulk uploads for next rotation window. Immediate effect: 429s dropped to <2% of baseline.
Recommended permanent changes for customer:
- Stagger ephemeral key rotation across worker sets (e.g., rotate subsets every 5m so not all workers rebind simultaneously).
- Reconfigure health-checks to hit a separate admin-ready route (/internal/ready) that is mapped to an internal exemption pool or has a different burst budget.
- If using very short-lived credentials (<10m), increase rotation granularity or use session refresh that does not force new connection creation at the same time across workers.
Platform-side actions and follow-ups:
- Engineering to investigate deduplication window for re-registration calls during key rotation and consider an adaptive debounce to avoid immediate token accounting spikes. (ENG-issue link provided).
- Add documentation section for 'ephemeral key rotation patterns' and recommended probe routing; link drafted to Confluence runbook.
- Consider adding a configuration option in Dedicated Console: 'Exclude probe routes from tenant burst accounting' as a configurator for enterprise/dedicated customers.
Ticket state: Waiting on customer to apply staggered rotation and probe route changes; Support to monitor next rotation (2026-03-12 scheduled) and will close if no repeat.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer SparkMaps reports repeated 429 responses during their scheduled batch pulls that run every 5 minutes. The failures are concentrated in a 10–20 second window at the start of each scheduled job.

Impact: Intermittent 429s affecting approximately 15% of batched API calls for the customer's dedicated tenant for ~2 hours after deployment changes. No data loss reported but job retries cause elongated job completion and downstream latency spikes.

Environment: prod - us-east (dedicated pool, tenant ID redacted in ticket). Using redwood-1-small for embeddings/generation and open-7b-v2 for reranking.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Schedule 50 parallel workers to start at the same cron time (every 5 minutes).
2) Each worker opens a short-lived streaming session and issues a 1–3 token warmup call followed by concurrent batch calls.
3) Observe 429s during the first 10–20s of the window; error rate drops to normal after the first refill interval.

Expected behavior: Smooth token accounting across rolling windows; scheduled bursts should be absorbed by burst credits or smoothed by refill window.

Actual behavior: Short window of concentrated 429s on tenant APIs at the scheduled job start. Rate headers from requests show near-zero refill immediately after midnight-aligned refill boundary; tenant token bucket appears depleted earlier than expected.

Logs & evidence: Support attached request traces and rate headers from one affected window (see attachments). Kernel-level rate-limiter logs show a refill event at 00:00:00 that leaves a residual mismatch between per-route accounting and tenant aggregation. Latency traces show retries concentrated on the first 18s.

Customer ask: Guidance on configuration to avoid synchronized refill spikes; temporary mitigation to reduce immediate job failures while we investigate server-side accounting behavior.

Additional notes:
2026-03-05 10:10 - SparkMaps (customer): Confirmed they start 50 workers exactly at the cron time and can't easily jitter due to pipeline orchestration. Asked for quick mitigation to drop error rate below 1%.
Hypothesis A: Synchronized worker starts coincide with refill boundary and small smoothing window leads to refill accounting drift between per-route and tenant aggregators.
Hypothesis B: Short-lived streaming sessions are creating ephemeral tokens that are not reclaimed immediately on disconnect, causing momentary bucket exhaustion during bursts.
What we observed: Rate-limiter server logs show per-route counters decrementing before tenant-level aggregates reflect refill. Reproducible in a controlled test when starting 40+ parallel short sessions at the same timestamp.
Metrics: Token consumption spike measured at ~1200 tokens/sec for tenant during first 12s of window; burst credit was exhausted and tenant-level throttle applied. After smoothing window increase, peak dropped to ~950 tokens/sec and 429s reduced substantially.
Related config: Customer is on Dedicated pool with default smoothing window=500ms and burst-credit=2000. Their worker orchestration doesn't jitter start times.
Action taken: Short-term smoothing window increased to 2.5s for customer's tenant and server-side backfill to align route->tenant accounting. Added increased logging around disconnect reclaim events for streaming sessions.
Temporary mitigation: Extended refill smoothing window from 500ms -> 2.5s for tenant during high-frequency scheduled jobs. This reduced immediate 429 spike from ~15% -> ~3%.
Workaround for customer: Stagger job start times by 1–3s per worker if possible; add small jitter to cron and slow-start workers in orchestrator (example script provided in comment).
Long-term plan: Engineering to roll a patch that aligns per-route accounting with tenant-level refill events (PR referenced), and add a configurable per-tenant scheduled-job guardrail to auto-apply jitter or local burst credits for scheduled cron bursts.
Follow-ups: Update Runbook 'Rate Smoothing Runbook' with this pattern, add automated detection to Console that surfaces synchronized start spikes for dedicated tenants, and schedule postmortem with SRE + Platform on 2026-03-10.
Status: In Progress — monitoring metrics steady; awaiting engineering rollout of alignment patch (linked PR).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer Novalia Health reports unexpected 429s and apparent double-counting of token/quota when they send mixed realtime (low-latency chat) and batched embedding jobs through the same tenant key. Impact: Production import pipelines and user-facing chat both see elevated 429s during daily ingest windows; customers report degraded UX and missed healthcare ingestion SLAs. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod in us-east, mixed traffic pattern: ~120 concurrent short-lived chat sessions + periodic backfill batches (50 parallel uploads, 5k items each).

Observed behavior / Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer pins chat route to low-latency model variant and also uses same API key for scheduled batch embedding job that uploads in parallel.
2) During backfill windows (approx 02:00–03:00 UTC) they observe repeated 429s for chat requests that previously were fine.
3) The console shows quota consumption spikes aligned to batch windows, but throttle headers on some chat responses indicate route-level tokens remaining while tenant-level counts are exhausted.

Logs / Evidence:
- Example throttle headers from chat request: x-rate-limit-remaining: 18; x-tenant-remaining: 0
- Ingest job timeline (from customer): 02:12:34 batch upload start; 02:12:35 spike in tenant token usage + chat 429s begin.
- Edge proxy logs show multiple signed URL preflight checks and chunked uploads around the same time.

Customer asks:
- Are chat and batch traffic supposed to be isolated when using the same API key?
- Why do chat responses still show route-remaining > 0 but tenant-remaining exhausted?
- Recommended config changes or immediate workarounds to stop chat from being throttled during batch windows?
Initial triage (03/10–03/11):
- Confirmed customer is using a single API key for both chat (realtime) and batch embed pipelines. They have not configured separate routes or isolated burst pools.
- Console metrics show tenant-level token refill was exhausted during backfill. Route-level counters are separate but enforcement occurs at tenant aggregation layer for certain global pools.
- Hypothesis 1: Backfill uses signed URL callbacks and preflight probes that create many short-lived token allocations at the ingress layer; these are accounted at tenant-level and deplete shared burst credits.
- Hypothesis 2: Fallback routing behavior: when dedicated low-latency pool saturates, requests get routed to a lower-cost shared pool which uses tenant-level accounting differently (counts more tokens per request due to batching amortization), causing tenant counter to drop faster.
- Evidence: correlated metrics from rate-limiter show refill events consumed by 'signed-url' and 'batch-chunk' subcomponents during spike.
- Repro attempt in staging: Ran a simulated mixed workload and reproduced tenant exhaustion when both flows use same API key and tenant burst pool set to "shared". When isolating batch route to a separate route with its own burst pool, chat remained healthy.
- Related internal note: INT-45012 contains the tracing of tenant-aggregation flow and an early prototype fix to expose clearer throttle headers for per-route vs tenant exhaustion.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:40 - SRE (Lina Zhou): Confirmed signed-url preflight is accounted as separate inbound events and currently increments tenant-level 'io' budget. Patch PR suggested to dedupe preflight accounting in most cases. See PR in linked_github_prs.
Workaround and next steps (03/12):
- Short-term mitigation agreed: temporarily increase tenant burst pool by 2x for Novalia Health (applied by infra team) and advise customer to throttle batch concurrency to reduce preflight fanout. This removed chat 429s in the next observed window.
- Mid-term fix: land PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/832) to dedupe signed-url/preflight accounting and expose clearer per-route vs tenant throttle headers to avoid confusion. INT-45012 will track rollout and telemetry changes.
- Long-term recommendation to customer: provision separate API keys/routes for realtime vs batch traffic and enable route isolation with independent burst pools for production. Document pattern added to Confluence page.
Follow-ups (owner Miguel Santos):
- Monitor tenant for 48 hours post-burst increase and confirm no collateral throttle side-effects.

Issue summary: SentinelPay observed elevated 5xx errors, unexpected semantic drift in generation outputs, and an unexplained billing spike starting 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC. Impact: customer production checkout flows returned malformed/irrelevant prompts and experienced API errors for ~45 minutes. Environment: prod (us-east-1), enterprise Dedicated + routing through canary pool. Immediate customer impact: checkout failures for ~1.2% of requests and two SLO breaches. This ticket captures the incident, investigation, mitigation, and follow-up actions.
1) Route customer traffic to canary variant (rollout step 3). 2) Execute high-concurrency embed + generation flows (checkout flow with prefill + semantic ranking). 3) Observe intermittent 500 responses, increased tail latency, and embedding mismatches. Note: reproduces only when canary rollback script is triggered with 'purge-cache --pattern=\"prefix:customer-*\"' against the shared cache cluster.
Selected log excerpts (timestamps UTC):\n- 2026-03-10T02:13:07Z SERVING runtime: cache-miss for key=prefix:customer-4821:model-v1 -> backend fetch OK\n- 2026-03-10T02:13:12Z ROUTER warning: request routed to fallback model (semantic-embeddings-v2) due to model-mismatch\n- 2026-03-10T02:15:41Z RUNTIME error 502: kv-cache: inconsistent prefix checksum (expected a86f, got 0000)\n- 2026-03-10T02:16:00Z BILLING metric: token_count surge +47% for customer_id=sentinelpay org=org-7689\n- 2026-03-10T02:23:33Z HEALTH check: canary instance reported degraded KV state; rollback initiated\n- 2026-03-10T02:25:02Z SUPPORT note: noticed 'purge-cache' job invoked with glob matching more keys than intended (pattern: prefix:customer-*)
2026-03-10 02:11 UTC - Canary rollout step 3 completed for customer traffic\n2026-03-10 02:12 UTC - SentinelPay reports elevated errors to CSM via #support-priority\n2026-03-10 02:14 UTC - Automated monitoring alerts: increased 5xx rate and token usage\n2026-03-10 02:16 UTC - SRE detects KV prefix checksum mismatches; temporarily disables canary routing\n2026-03-10 02:18 UTC - Canary rollback script executed; 'purge-cache' invoked to clear corrupted prefixes\n2026-03-10 02:19 UTC - Cache purge used a wildcard pattern and removed customer-specific cached embeddings across shared cluster\n2026-03-10 02:20 UTC - Routing fallback activated; traffic served by larger model variants leading to billing spike\n2026-03-10 02:56 UTC - Full recovery: caches repopulated, 5xx rates back to baseline, billing anomaly mitigated\n2026-03-10 03:08 UTC - Customer notified; incident declared resolved pending postmortem
CSM (Rachel Kim) 2026-03-10T02:13: reported: 'We're seeing checkout rejects — customers cannot complete payment. Please investigate urgently.'
Support (Aisha Monroe) 2026-03-10T02:15: 'Acknowledged, escalating to SRE and Eng. Gathering traces and request IDs.'
SRE (Carlos Vega) 2026-03-10T02:17: 'Observed KV checksum mismatch on canary nodes. Suspected cache corruption triggered failover.'
Eng (Marta Lopez) 2026-03-10T02:21: 'Rollback script ran a cache purge using glob pattern; it removed shared prefixes accidentally. Initiating repopulation and limiting future purge scope.'
Customer (SentinelPay - Ops) 2026-03-10T02:40: 'Thanks for the quick response. We observed a 3x increase in token charges in the 15-minute window.'
Support (Aisha Monroe) 2026-03-10T03:12: 'Service is back to normal; we are preparing a post-incident report and follow-up call.'
Hypothesis: During canary rollback we invoked a cache purge job to remove corrupted prefixes. Due to a bug in the purge utility, the glob pattern matched customer-specific kv namespaces across the shared cluster, resulting in mass invalidation. This caused requests to miss cached embeddings/prefix KV, forcing runtime to recompute embeddings and route to larger model variants for safety, which increased per-token cost and briefly pushed some request paths into error states (timeouts + backend retries). We verified: (a) purge logs show pattern 'prefix:customer-*' executed across nodes; (b) KV checksums show reset to zeros for affected keys; (c) repopulation flow restored embeddings and removed checksum errors. Root cause: insufficient isolation of purge jobs in canary rollback script + missing dry-run guard + overly-permissive cache key naming convention. Secondary contributor: routing fallback had no per-customer throttle when cache population lagged, causing load on fallback models and billing surge.
Mitigation applied: 1) Immediately disabled purge job and re-enabled pinned cache-serving nodes for SentinelPay. 2) Throttled routing to fallback models for SentinelPay to cap token surge. 3) Triggered prioritized cache repopulation using customer snapshot to restore semantic embeddings. 4) Conducted controlled rollback with dry-run verification. Impact remediation completed by 2026-03-10T02:56 UTC. Customer notified and credits applied for abnormal billing. Engineering deployed a hotfix to purge utility to require explicit namespace flag and added a dry-run confirmation step.
Initial acknowledgement sent 2026-03-10T02:14 UTC. Interim update 2026-03-10T02:30 UTC: explaining cause and mitigation steps. Final resolution email 2026-03-10T03:20 UTC with apology, summary of actions, and confirmation of billing credit. Follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC to review long-term mitigations and SLA implications.
1) Require namespace-scoped purge flags and add protective dry-run by default (owner: eng/cache, due 2026-03-17). 2) Introduce per-customer fallback throttles and token caps (owner: serving-runtime, due 2026-04-01). 3) Rename cache key prefixes to include instance-scoped hash to avoid accidental cross-tenant purges (owner: infra, due 2026-03-31). 4) Run incident tabletop with CSM/SRE/Eng and SentinelPay on 2026-03-12. 5) Add automated canary pre-check that simulates cache purge in a shadow cluster before allowing rollback (owner: release-engineering, due 2026-04-07).
Ticket created INT-1212 to implement purge utility hardening. Billing team ticket SUP-60001 created to process credits for SentinelPay. Engineering PR referenced for hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2173. Confluence postmortem published and linked.
payload.summary: SentinelPay prod: cache invalidation during canary rollback caused semantic mismatches, spike in 5xx, and billing anomaly

Issue summary: After an IdP metadata refresh in the customer's private VPC deployment, scheduled batch inference workers are failing to swap to ephemeral service accounts used for long-running batched jobs. Impact: Horizon Analytics' nightly bulk inference jobs (scheduled via their internal scheduler) are stalling with 403 authz errors and getting retried; this is impacting SLAs for their nightly reports. Environment: Private deployment in us-east-1 (customer-managed control plane). Affected path: token exchange flow used by the scheduled worker process (service account JWT -> Redwood ephemeral service-account). Observed behavior: Token exchange completes, but the resulting assertion presented to the admin API lacks the cert_role claim required by RBAC policy, leading to a deny. Expected behavior: After token exchange, the assertion should include cert_role and tenant bindings so scheduled workers can impersonate ephemeral service accounts and run batch jobs.
1) Customer runs a scheduled batch job in their private deployment that triggers a service-account JWT swap against the admin token-swap endpoint.
2) Identity proxy performs token exchange with configured external IdP and returns ephemeral assertion to scheduler worker.
3) Worker attempts to call Redwood admin-impersonation endpoint with assertion; request receives 403 due to missing cert_role claim.
4) Re-running the job after restarting the identity-proxy sometimes restores claims (intermittent).
2026-03-12T02:14:03Z identity-proxy INFO received token-swap request from scheduler-worker-42
2026-03-12T02:14:03Z idp-client DEBUG fetched IdP assertion (size=1.2KB)
2026-03-12T02:14:03Z identity-proxy DEBUG mapped claims -> {sub: 'svc-worker-42', aud: 'redwood-admin', tenant: 'horizon', exp: 1678626003}
2026-03-12T02:14:03Z admin-api WARN authorization failed for request id 7f9c: missing required claim 'cert_role'
2026-03-12T02:14:03Z scheduler ERROR batch-job-20260312-37 failed: 403 Forbidden (missing cert_role)
Scheduled batch worker calls to admin-impersonation endpoint are rejected with 403 because the assertion returned from the IdP exchange path does not include cert_role. This started after an automated IdP metadata refresh (customer reports on 2026-03-11 23:50 local). The problem is intermittent: in some cases a restart of identity-proxy returns cert_role again for subsequent exchanges.
All token-exchange flows for scheduled workers should preserve/translate the cert_role claim (or an equivalent mapped attribute) so RBAC policies that rely on cert_role succeed and batch jobs can proceed without manual restarts.
• Customer confirmed they did not change RBAC policies or service account templates prior to the first failure.
• Identity-proxy request/response traces show the raw assertion from IdP does contain a 'roles' array but not the expected 'cert_role' key after metadata refresh.
• Hypothesis: recent IdP metadata rotation changed the attribute mapping (NameFormat or attribute alias). Our claim-mapper defaults to 'cert_role' and falls back to scanning 'roles' only when explicit mapping exists—this can cause the claim name to be omitted.
• Reproduced in staging by forcing IdP metadata swap and running same token-swap flow: confirmed that NameFormat differences result in mapper skipping claim population (issue present in identity-proxy v1.8.3).
• Related: SUP-421999 has a similar claim-ordering symptom; linking for context.
• Trace ID: trace-redwood-0a1b2c (customer-provided)
Temporary workaround implemented: In the customer's ingress/identity-proxy configuration we enabled 'claim_passthrough: true' to copy raw IdP attributes through to the assertion without strict mapping. This allowed scheduled jobs to proceed for now. Workaround requires a config reload and is not persisted across identity-proxy restarts unless they keep the flag set.
1) Patch identity-proxy claim-mapper to treat 'roles' array as equivalent to 'cert_role' when a mapped claim is not present (backport to stable v1.8.x).
2) Add integration test to cover NameFormat variations and attribute aliasing.
3) Coordinate with customer to validate patch in their private deployment during a maintenance window (provide patch and runbook).
4) Consider adding a telemetry alert when claim-mapper results in empty critical claims for admin-impersonation flows.
Support (2026-03-12) - Maya Chen: Customer reported nightly bulk jobs failing with 403 after IdP metadata refresh. Provided initial logs and confirmed private deployment.
Customer (2026-03-12) - Horizon SRE (Samir Kaur): We rotated IdP metadata as part of routine cert renewal at 2026-03-11T23:50. We saw the first failed job shortly after. We can keep claim_passthrough=true for now if that helps.
Support (2026-03-12) - Maya Chen: Enabled claim_passthrough=true in customer's identity-proxy config and restarted the process. Observed subsequent token-exchanges include raw 'roles' and jobs resumed. Marking as workaround.
SRE (2026-03-13) - Liam O'Connor: Reproduced issue in staging. Filed a PR to treat 'roles' as alias for 'cert_role' and added unit tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/452
Eng (2026-03-14) - Priya Rao: Will schedule backport to v1.8.x and coordinate with Release Ops. Patch includes an opt-out flag 'strict_claim_names' for customers who require strict mapping.
Customer (2026-03-14) - Samir Kaur: We're available for a 02:00 UTC maintenance window Friday to accept the patch and test.
In Progress - workaround applied (claim_passthrough=true). Engineering patch authored and awaiting backport/QA before deployment to customer's private control plane. Follow-up: schedule maintenance window with customer to apply v1.8.x backport.
payload.summary: authn-context missing 'cert_role' claim prevents scheduled batch worker service-account swap in private

Issue summary: A customer-reported embedded dashboard panel started returning an empty visualization after a retention backfill. Investigation shows the query optimizer injected a redundant noop filter clause into the SQL-like query plan which caused the platform-side join to short-circuit. The panel therefore had zero rows and tracehook link generation skipped because no trace anchor was present.

Impact: Multiple embedded dashboards for BrightHealth Analytics (enterprise) in us-east show blank panels and missing trace links in their product when selecting 7d ranges that cross the retention backfill boundary. This affects internal customers embedding our console in a product-facing status page.

Environment: production, us-east region, console query-engine v3.7.1, retention backfill from 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-09 was running during the window.

Observed at: 2026-03-09 22:40 UTC when customer reported via #support-enterprise Slack.

Expected behavior: Embedded panel returns series and trace link anchors should be present for rows with sampling-enabled traces.

Actual behavior: Panel renders as "No data"; raw query returns empty resultset. Console does not attach trace_hook headers/links.

Workaround: Customer can toggle time-range to exclude the backfill window or disable "optimizer_trim" flag in advanced panel settings (temporary UI toggle we've exposed server-side) to force the legacy query path.
1) Login to console as org with embedded dashboard (BrightHealth Analytics)
2) Open embedded panel A (Usage heatmap) with time range that includes 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-09
3) Observe panel shows "No data" while surrounding panels show data
4) In developer tools capture the backend query and the planner output from /api/query/run
5) Toggle advanced setting 'optimizer_trim' to off and re-run the panel; panel repopulates data and trace links return
2026-03-09T22:37:05Z QUERY planner: injected_filter: (1=1) /* noop */; plan node: Join(Side: left, rows: 0)
2026-03-09T22:37:05Z QUERY engine: short-circuit zero rows => skip tracehook attachment
Request ID: req_9b2f7a3a - panel: embedded-usage-heatmap - org: brighthealth-42
2026-03-10 09:20 UTC - Support: reproduced with customer's org and time range; captured planner output indicates an injected noop filter '1=1' that appears with a following join node that returns zero rows.
2026-03-10 12:05 UTC - SRE: retention backfill job running; observed compaction and tombstone sweep overlap during the same window. Hypothesis: optimizer path prunes partitions aggressively when backfill markers present, then adds noop guard to preserve semantics which interacts poorly with join ordering.
2026-03-11 15:40 UTC - Eng (Julian): replicated locally using the backfill fixture. Confirmed optimizer_trim flag toggles between legacy and optimized planner; optimized planner produced noop filter and empty result for a crafted query pattern.
Telemetry: metric console.query.empty_panels_by_org[brighthealth-42] spiked from 2 to 48 between 2026-03-09T22:00 and 2026-03-10T02:00 UTC
Stacktrace: N/A - behavior is planner output / logical transform rather than runtime exception

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:10 UTC - CS (BrightHealth): Asked whether billing impact or data loss occurred. Confirmed no data loss and only display/trace links affected.
Mitigation applied: exposed 'optimizer_trim' toggle as temporary control for affected orgs; BrightHealth set to 'off' and panels restored.
Fix in review: patch avoids injecting noop guard for queries where partition prune + join reorder can produce zero-cardinality build side. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8793
Rollout plan: hotfix scheduled to us-east 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC (canary -> regional), monitoring dashboard created for console.query.empty_panels_by_org metric and tracehook_attach_failures.
Follow-ups: Add unit tests covering backfill partition markers, update runbook to include quick toggle for optimizer when backfills are scheduled, and postmortem draft after rollout closure.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer QueryFlow reports periodic sawtooth-shaped spikes in p95/p99 latency leading to streaming request timeouts. Spikes appear as regular oscillations on dashboards rather than single outlier events.

Impact:
- Several QueryFlow endpoints experienced 5-10% request failures (stream timeouts) during peak windows since 2026-03-10.
- A small percentage of short-streams (<= 2s) hit p99 > 1.2s and then time out intermittently.

Environment:
- prod/us-east primary, also observed correlated signals in eu-west.
- Dedicated pool for QueryFlow with pinned model openlm/gpt-14b-v1.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer/simulated):
1) Send steady short-stream traffic at ~60 QPS per connection with a mix of 50/50 short/long sequences.
2) Include occasional tenant burst (5s window with 200 QPS).
3) Watch per-tenant batcher metrics and streaming timeouts.

Observed behavior:
- p95 and p99 latency graphs show sawtooth oscillation every ~45-90s across many serving shards.
- During the rising limb of the sawtooth p99, streaming connections are closed with 504/timeout after upstream KV fetch waits increase.
- KV cache hit-rate temporarily dips during the oscillation and then recovers.

Expected behavior:
- Stable p95/p99 with occasional spikes during large bursts, not rhythmic sawtooth oscillations causing timeouts.

Relevant logs / metrics we collected:
- Dashboards: /dashboards/latency/queryflow-pool (attached screenshots in ticket).
- Batch flush frequency and mean batch size: flush frequency shows periodic drops coincident with latency valleys.
- Serving logs: repeated "coalescer: delayed flush due to tenant-hysteresis" lines (cluster-wide).
- Connection logs: streaming keepalive shows small pause then reconnects around each timeout.

Initial investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: dynamic coalescer's per-tenant flush hysteresis interacts with autoscaling and KV-cache warmup such that flush timings align across shards producing constructive interference (sawtooth).
- Observed tenant-weight recalculation spikes that align with the oscillation period. Those recalculations briefly reduce per-tenant batch weight which reduces effective flush frequency causing accumulation and a later large flush that increases tail latency.
- KV-cache warming appears to lag the large flush, producing transient backend waits.

Workarounds identified so far:
- Temporary mitigation: set continuous-batcher.max_coalesce_hysteresis_ms=0 for QueryFlow's tenant (rolling config) which flattened the oscillation in a canary pool.
- Alternative: gate tenant-weight recalculation to longer cadence (30s->120s) which reduced synchronization across shards in a test.

Next steps / proposed remediation:
1) Engineering to reproduce in a dedicated load test (priority) — assigned to Ethan Patel.
2) Create an alert to detect synchronized flush events across shards and auto-adjust hysteresis per-tenant.
3) Patch proposal: coalescer PR to add randomized jitter to per-tenant flush timers and safe guard for KV-cache warmup windows (see linked PR).
4) Schedule a controlled rollout and monitor p99 across QueryFlow pool.

Reference material:
- Slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C04SUPPORT)
- Runbook excerpts: Continuous Batcher runbook page above.

Please see attached screenshots and flame graphs in the ticket attachments area for timeline alignment.

Additional notes:
Mitigation in progress: canary config change (max_coalesce_hysteresis_ms=0) flattened oscillation for customer pool; engineering patch to add jitter and KV-warmup guard landed in staging. Production rollout planned behind feature flag after final validation.
payload.summary: Sawtooth p95/p99 latency oscillations and intermittent streaming timeouts traced to dynamic coalescer behavior

comments: Tom Hernandez: I can reproduce locally with the customer's repro harness. The JS SDK's refresh task is not merging stream-level idempotency headers when constructing replay envelopes.
Aisha Kapoor: Sent temporary mitigation steps to customer and scheduled a dedicated tenant test tomorrow morning.
payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightDesk reports that long-lived streaming sessions occasionally produce duplicate side-effects (external webhook posts and database writes) after a client-side retry. The customer observed that a function/tool invocation is accepted by the server but no 'funcall ack' is delivered to the client; the client retries and the tool runs again, causing duplicate downstream effects. Impact: duplicate charges and duplicate webhook deliveries for a set of mid-length (30s-2min) streaming sessions. This impacts a handful of customers using the Dedicated offering, higher severity because of billing/data integrity risks.
Duplicate webhook posts and duplicate DB writes reported by customer; estimated 14 customer-visible duplicates in last 48h. Potentially affects other dedicated customers doing background token rotation and reconnects.
1) Use the JS SDK to open a streaming chat session that may trigger function/tool calls (sample code provided by customer).
2) Configure client with background credential refresh enabled (refresh interval ~15min) and short connection idle preemption on LB (simulate using dedicated environment).
3) During an inflight tool invocation, trigger a background token refresh so that the SDK swaps credentials mid-stream (observed when refresh completes while stream is active).
4) Simulate a transient network hiccup (TCP reset or HTTP/2 GOAWAY) causing the SDK to reconnect and replay in-flight messages using retry logic.
5) Observe on server side that the retried request does not include the original Idempotency header or per-tool confirmation token (header removed/replaced), so server treats as a new funcall and executes tool again.
Missing idempotency header after token rotation + reconnect; server accepted second funcall and executed tool. Customer did not receive funcall ack on initial execution path; ack was observed only for the second run. Net result: duplicated external webhook posts and duplicate DB writes.
Idempotency scope (per-tool idempotency key and confirmation tokens) should be retained across background token refresh and preserved on replayed requests so replays are deduplicated on the server side and funcall ack mapping remains consistent.
client-js: INFO background-refresh: starting refresh for scope user-123 (token expires 2026-03-12T16:20:00Z)
client-js: DEBUG stream: replaying 3 pending events on reconnect; headers: Authorization: <rotated>, Idempotency-Key: <missing>
api-gateway: WARN http2: connection migrated (GOAWAY) client_id=bd-77; received replay without idempotency-key
serving-runtime: INFO funcall: executing tool 'charge-invoice' request_id=abcd1234 idempotency_key=null
serving-runtime: INFO webhook: delivered 200 to https://hooks.brightdesk.com/charge (attempt 1)
serving-runtime: INFO funcall: executing tool 'charge-invoice' request_id=efgh5678 idempotency_key=generated-uuid-789; webhook delivered (attempt 2)
Initial hypothesis: background token rotation path in SDK replaces entire request header bag during replay instead of merging original idempotency metadata.
Reproduced locally with JS SDK v1.12.0 when refresh completes during active stream and LB issues GOAWAY; confirmed Idempotency header absent on replayed frames.
Python SDK v0.9.8 shows different behavior: refresh pauses during active streaming by default in current customer's config (not reproduced), indicates SDK behavioral divergence across languages.
Gateway logs show no header-truncation at LB; header missing at SDK outbound before hitting gateway (client-side removal).
Race window corresponds to: background refresh thread obtains new token -> SDK rotates Authorization header -> replay logic reuses new header bag and drops ephemeral idempotency metadata generated earlier on the stream.
Related: we found link to existing notes on stream resume idempotency in SUP-472999; some overlaps but different root cause (token rotation path)
2026-03-12 10:15 - BrightDesk (S. Miller): We saw duplicate charges yesterday evening for three invoices, all tied to streaming sessions. Attached request/response traces.
2026-03-12 14:02 - Support (A. Kapoor): Asked for SDK versions, sample code, and whether background credential refresh is enabled. Customer confirmed using managed token refresh (delegated key) and JS SDK v1.12.0.
2026-03-13 09:40 - BrightDesk: Provided pcap and SDK debug logs (attached). Also noted they use a custom edge sidecar which does short-lived LB preemption (GOAWAYs).
2026-03-14 11:05 - Support (T. Hernandez): Shared workaround to disable background refresh during active streams (manual refresh) and requested permission to run reproducer in dedicated tenant. Customer approved.

Additional notes:
SRE (03-13): Gateway did not drop headers; verified via packet capture. Focus on SDK header assembly on reconnect.
SDK Lead (03-14): Queueing a patch to preserve per-tool idempotency tokens during token rotation; PR linked below. Also adding an opt-in client flag to pause refresh during active streams.
1) Disable automatic background credential refresh on active-stream clients (set SDK config 'pauseRefreshDuringStreams': true) OR 2) Upgrade to patched SDK when available. For immediate mitigation, customer set refresh interval to 1h and used explicit refresh before starting long streams.
Patch submitted to sdk-js to merge original per-stream idempotency metadata when replaying after token rotation. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/8123. Patch preserves Idempotency-Key and per-tool confirmation tokens across refresh and replay. Plan: backport to 1.x line, release RC, validate in customer's dedicated tenant, and roll out to prod. Expected full rollout: 2026-03-19.
1) Complete PR review and backport to js-sdk 1.x (ETA 2026-03-15).
2) Run reproducer in BrightDesk dedicated tenant with patched build (test window 2026-03-16).
3) If successful, promote RC to canary for Dedicated pool (2026-03-17) and monitor for duplicates for 48h.
4) Publish SDK changelog and docs note about token-rotation caveat and recommended config to pause refresh for long-lived streams.
5) Add unit+integration test to prevent regression (CI gate).
payload.summary: Background credential refresh during active stream removes idempotency header -> missing funcall ack and duplicate side-effects on retry

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports an unexplained $37.15 line on their latest provisional invoice after an SLO-triggered fallback event. They say a small percentage of traffic that hit their dedicated pool was routed to hosted-backed variants and billed at hosted tariffs instead of being covered by reserved capacity credits. Impact: unexpected charge and incorrect credit attribution for March 9 maintenance window.

Environment: prod-us-east, Novametrics dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-evg-09), reserved hours active during period.

Timeline: 2026-03-09 22:31 UTC — Dedicated pool experienced transient latency spike; SLO policy auto-routed traffic to fallback model variants. 2026-03-09 22:31–22:45 UTC — ~2.4% of requests routed through hosted fallback. 2026-03-10 — Novametrics noticed extra line on provisional invoice and opened this ticket.

Steps to reproduce (customer-facing):
1) Trigger SLO threshold via synthetic load against dedicated pool.
2) Observe policy routing to hosted variant (fallback).
3) Check provisional invoice / hourly postbacks for the minute buckets matching failover window.

Observed behavior: A subset of requests routed to hosted fallback appear in billing as hosted-tariff line items and were not offset by the customer's reserved capacity credits. Billing records show the postbacks for those minute buckets as coming from the hosted-postback queue rather than the dedicated-postback namespace.

Expected behavior: Fallback routing should still record origin tags such that requests attributed to the customer's pool within the reserved time window are billed at reserved/dedicated rates or credited appropriately. Postback reconciliation should preserve org/pool tags even when routing changes target model variants.

Logs / supporting data: Customer provided example request IDs: req-20260309-223412-9f1a, req-20260309-223458-4b6c. Issue summary: After BrightCart enabled the 'priority-bandit' routing feature to weight background webhooks lower than interactive traffic, a subset of their low-priority webhook workers started receiving sustained 429 responses. Throttle response headers are inconsistent (sometimes report remaining=0, sometimes omit headers).

Impact: BrightCart reports degraded processing of background webhooks (order-fulfillment retry callbacks). Approx 18% of callbacks fail with 429s over 6 hours, causing retry storms and delayed downstream processing. This is customer-facing (dedicated pool) and causing backlog growth in their systems.

Environment: Dedicated pool for BrightCart (org ID: org-brightcart), production us-west region. Traffic pattern: 250 webhook workers across 4 hosts, each opening 8 persistent HTTP/2 connections and issuing short POSTs (~600B payload) at ~1qps per worker. Priority-bandit was enabled at 2026-03-09 22:15 PDT.

Observed: Persistent 429s for endpoints /v1/webhook/recv from the same API key; headers inconsistent: sometimes X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, sometimes no X-RateLimit-* headers; Retry-After values vary between numeric seconds and RFC1123 timestamps. Console shows route-level burst pool configured (burst_pool_id=bg-webhook-burst) but metrics show route weight w_bg=0.1 and tenant-level token refill unchanged.

Expected: Low-priority routes should get separated burst capacity and stable, documented throttle headers with Retry-After in seconds. 429s should be queued and smoothed rather than persistent across all workers.

Temporary workaround attempted by customer: reduced worker concurrency from 8 to 2 and added exponential backoff; this reduced immediate error rate but backlog remains.

Relevant links: Slack thread #support-brightcart (https://slack.redwood/support-brightcart/p12345), console dashboard: https://console.redwood/teams/org-brightcart/metrics?panel=rate-limiter
1) Enabled priority-bandit with configuration: {route: '/v1/webhook/recv', priority: low, burst_pool: 'bg-webhook-burst', weight: 0.1}
2) Start 200 short-lived workers each maintaining 4 HTTP/2 streams to gateway and sending 1req/s
3) Observe 429 responses within 5-20 minutes, throttle headers inconsistent across responses
4) Scale worker concurrency down and observe partial mitigation
Sample 429 response at 2026-03-10T02:34:12Z from 10.14.22.101:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1710159252
Retry-After: 10
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"throttle"}}

Sample 429 at 2026-03-10T02:37:03Z from 10.14.22.102:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 02:38:10 GMT
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded"}}

Gateway logs show repeated token_reassign events and burst_pool_exhausted for bg-webhook-burst starting 2026-03-09T22:20:00Z. Metric snapshot: route_bg-webhook-burst.tokens_in_use=98, pool_capacity=100, tenant_tokens_free fluctuating between 200-400.

- Hypothesis 1: Route-level burst pool accounting is double-counting requests when HTTP/2 multiplexing reassigns streams across connections, causing pool to appear exhausted while tokens exist at tenant-level.
- Hypothesis 2: Priority-bandit weight calculation produced an unintended route weight floor, causing the route to be starved after a refill epoch shift (we saw refill epoch shift at 2026-03-09T22:18:45Z).
- Hypothesis 3: A header normalization change in edge proxy removed X-RateLimit-* headers for some connection reuse patterns.
Actions taken so far:
- Pulled gateway traces for two affected hosts and correlated token assignment ids (TA-ids) -> found TA-ids being recycled across streams, logged to /var/log/rate-limiter/ta-recycle.log.
- Replayed representative traffic in staging against the same priority-bandit config; reproduced inconsistent headers when HTTP/2 connection affinity set to "pool" rather than "sticky".
- Opened quick rollback flag for priority-bandit (flag PR: github.com/redwood-inference/flags/pull/312) and staged a canary to 5% for 10 minutes.

Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-10: Created ticket after customer reported high 429 rate for background webhooks following priority-bandit enablement. Customer provided request/response samples and console screenshots.
SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-10: Picked up ticket. Initial hypothesis: burst pool accounting under HTTP/2 multiplexing. Requested gateway debug logs (collected, attached). Scheduled deeper trace correlation.
Customer (BrightCart - Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Confirming we rolled the feature at 22:15 and saw error spike within 5 minutes. We can accept a short canary rollback window. Critical: we need clear guidance on proper burst_pool sizing for webhook fleets.
SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-11: Reproduced header omission locally when connection affinity set to 'pool'. Opening bug for edge-proxy header normalization (INT-998802 opened). Canary rollback started at 2026-03-11T16:40Z to 5% of dedicated hosts.
Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-12: Customer reports reduced 429s after rollback canary but still sees occasional inconsistencies; escalating to platform team for permanent fix. Advised customer to temporarily set HTTP/2 streams to 'sticky' affinity and increase burst_pool capacity by +30%.
(ongoing) Mitigation: Canary rollback of priority-bandit reduced error-rate to baseline on canary hosts. Temporary recommendation given: set HTTP/2 affinity to sticky and increase bg-webhook-burst pool capacity by 30%.
Next steps: platform engineers to fix edge-proxy header normalization bug (INT-998802) and update burst accounting to be stream-aware. Plan: patch in 2-week sprint, validate with BrightCart test harness, then re-enable priority-bandit behind a staged rollout and observability gates. Customer follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-14.
Patch candidate: edge-proxy will stop stripping X-RateLimit headers when connection ID changes (PR referenced in related_github_prs). Rate-limiter change: add per-stream token lock to prevent TA-id reuse across multiplexed streams. Postmortem doc template: confluence.redwood.internal/display/INC/Bandit+Refill+Drift+Postmortem

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 429 throttles for requests routed to their Dedicated pool during high-concurrency periods. Impact: production traffic (ingest + function-calling streams) receives sporadic 429s causing user-facing latency spikes and failed batches. Pattern appears during morning US-East traffic ramp and after scheduled autoscaler warmups.

Observed behavior: Multiple simultaneous requests from the customer's workers show 429s even though the token usage shown in the console is below configured tenant quota. Customer suspects token double-counting.

Expected behavior: Tenant-level quota should account correctly for concurrent connections, and identical API key traffic should not be double-counted due to proxy connection reuse.

1) Customer runs ~200 parallel workers in us-east with a single API key against dedicated pool; many workers use HTTP/2 keepalive via a corporate edge proxy.
2) Start a mixed workload: short streaming starts (chat) and batch embedding jobs concurrently.
3) Wait for autoscaler warmup to finish and observe token refills + quota counters in Console.
4) Notice spikes of 429 responses from the API while console reports apparent spare quota for the tenant.
5) Toggling client-side HTTP/2 connection reuse to each worker opening its own connection reduces 429s in reproduction.
Selected trace examples: edge-proxy logs show the same API key appearing on multiple simultaneous HTTP/2 streams with different upstream connection IDs. Rate-limiter logs show per-connection increment events with no session dedupe key, causing the same logical API key consumption to be recorded twice. Example trace IDs: trace-20260310-az1-1122, trace-20260310-az1-1137. Console token accounting snapshot attached in customer upload (trimmed JSON).
Initial triage by Support: confirmed customer quota settings and that Dedicated pool had available capacity. Reproduced locally with a corp-proxy shim that multiplexes streams over pooled upstream connections. SRE ran a capture on edge-proxy: observed that our rate accounting was keyed by (upstream_connection_id, route) rather than by API key + route in the hot path for HTTP/2. When a proxy reuses upstream connections and multiplexes client logical sessions, each HTTP/2 stream produced per-connection counters that incremented the tenant bucket multiple times. This is amplified during autoscaler warmups because many short-lived streams start concurrently and health checks create transient connections that further skew counting. Hypothesis: edge-proxy was introduced with a perf change that switched to per-connection counters to avoid lock contention; this inadvertently produced duplicates when connection pooling sits in front of the proxy. Related to a 2025 change in edge-proxy metrics (#PR-512).
Ask customer to disable HTTP/2 connection pooling at the corp-proxy for their Redwood origin (force each worker to open a distinct upstream connection), or increase tenant burst credit temporarily. Support also provided a client-side recommendation: add a short randomized jitter to worker start times to avoid synchronized warmups. Both reduced observed 429s in customer testing.
Engineering change in progress: patch edge-proxy to include API-key session deduplication in the rate accounting hot path and fall back to a shared atomic counter keyed by (api_key, route, logical_session_id) when available. PR created to revert the per-connection-only counter optimization and add tests that simulate HTTP/2 connection pooling. Target deploy to staging on 2026-03-15 and rollout to us-east on 2026-03-17 behind a gradual canary. Once patch is deployed, ask customer to revert the temporary proxy config.

Post-deploy follow-ups: add a unit test for multiplexed upstreams, update runbook to document proxy-interaction symptoms, and add a console alert when per-connection vs per-api-key accounting diverge by >5% over a 5m window.
1) Add telemetry that exposes per-route accounting deltas to Console (SRE ticket). 2) Coordinate with Dedicated onboarding to flag customers using corp-proxies and recommend proxy settings. 3) Add a KB article explaining HTTP/2 connection pooling implications for rate-limiting.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:42 - Customer (Nimbus Analytics, engineer): Disabled HTTP/2 pooling as requested; 429s dropped to <0.2% in a 2-hour trial. Happy to keep temporary config if fix ETA is >5 days.
2026-03-12 08:38 - Eng (edge-proxy owner): Identified PR that introduced optimization. Drafted fix to aggregate counters before persistence. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/789

Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 02:15 and 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC Waveform AI experienced a sudden elevated 5xx rate (primarily 503) from the Redwood hosted API. Impact: customer streaming sessions failed with repeated 503s and client-side disconnects; several hundred requests failed per minute. Environment: dedicated tenant on prod us-west serving gptk-13b-quant. Initial triage suggested API gateway timeouts; deeper inspection shows upstream serving runtimes repeatedly crashing/restarting under a prefetch lock amplification scenario.
1) Simulate sustained streaming burst from single-tenant (Waveform AI) with ~120 concurrent streaming sessions sending small prompts (avg 30 tokens) and prefetched model variant enabled. 2) Observe runtime prefetch subsystem queuing and increased lock contention on kv-cache shard 7. 3) After ~90s of sustained burst, upstream runtimes begin failing healthchecks and restart, API gateway returns 503/502 to callers. 4) Increasing the burst concurrency reproduces the crashloop more rapidly. Note: behavior not reproduced on lighter workloads or with prefetch disabled.
2026-03-10T02:18:12Z runtime[shard=7] WARN prefetch: queue-length=312 lock-wait-ms=1243
2026-03-10T02:19:05Z apigw[edge] ERROR upstream_timeout: upstream=runtime-7 region=us-west status=503
2026-03-10T02:19:07Z runtime[pid=2451] ERROR watchdog: worker OOM? exit_code=137 kernel_message=Killed process 2451 (runtime)
- Customer reported sudden increase in error rate at 02:15 UTC; support confirmed spike in 503s correlated to Waveform AI tenant. - SRE pulled runtime logs and noticed high prefetch queue lengths and long lock wait times localized to kv-cache shard 7. - Memory metrics: GPU memory utilization remained stable; CPU and thread contention spiked. - Autoscaler logs show no scale-up events during the first 2 minutes of the burst due to conservative HPA thresholds. - Reproduced locally in staging by replaying customer traffic pattern; disabling prefetch prevented crashloop. - Hypothesis: prefetch subsystem acquires a shard-level lock during model prefetch; with many concurrent small streaming sessions the prefetch hot-path serializes work and starves runtime main threads, causing healthcheck failures and ultimately runtime restarts. - Related findings: a similar prefetch lock amplification was referenced in SUP-328765 but that incident involved different shard skew; here amplification is tenant-local and tied to streaming keepalive patterns.
2026-03-10 02:42 - Support (Priya): Acknowledge customer, asked for request IDs and whether they had pinned model variants. Customer confirmed model pinning and streaming-heavy workloads.
2026-03-10 03:05 - SRE (Ethan): Collected runtime core dumps and kv-cache shard metrics; opened a short Slack thread #support-prefetch (https://slack.redwood/threads/T12345) and posted initial observations.
2026-03-10 03:22 - Customer (Waveform AI, T. Alvarez): Provided sample request IDs and agreed to test a temporary mitigation (disable prefetch on tenant).
2026-03-10 03:40 - Support (Priya): Applied tenant-level config to disable prefetch; customer reported error rate dropping to baseline within ~2 minutes. Proceeding with mitigation rollout and root cause analysis.
2026-03-11 09:15 - Eng (Sophie Chen): Noted potential quick patch: reduce lock scope in prefetch codepath and add shard-aware backoff. Follow-up PR planned.
2026-03-12 11:00 - SRE (Ethan): Increased autoscaler sensitivity for dedicated tenants and scheduled a controlled rollout of kv-cache shard rebalancer to prevent shard skew under tenant bursts.
Workaround applied: tenant-level prefetch disabled for Waveform AI at 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC which immediately reduced 503s. Mitigations in flight: 1) Hotfix PR to narrow prefetch lock scope and add exponential backoff (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521). 2) Autoscaler policy adjusted to allow faster scale-up on tenant-specific streaming CPU-thread pressure. 3) Short-term operational change: monitor kv-cache shard hotness and trigger automated shard rebalancer when shard queue length > 200 for >60s. Follow-ups: full postmortem due 2026-03-17, test case added to chaos/stress suite covering tenant-local prefetch bursts, and customer follow-up call scheduled for 2026-03-13.
ENG-1: Merge prefetch lock-scope reduction + backoff PR and deploy to canary by 2026-03-14
SRE-2: Implement shard hotness alert and automated rebalancer rule by 2026-03-16
OPS-3: Adjust dedicated-tenant HPA thresholds to respond to streaming bursts during blackout windows by 2026-03-15
DX-4: Add a KB article for customers about prefetch behavior and recommended request patterns for streaming workloads

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Lumos Analytics reports duplicate tool/function executions when using our gRPC multiplexed batch endpoint from their Go-based orchestrator. They are sending multiple logical user requests multiplexed over a single persistent stream with per-action idempotency metadata. Under load and intermittent connection resets, a tool call that should be at-most-once is being executed twice across different logical requests (not repeated for the same request).

Impact:
- Customer sees duplicate side-effects (duplicate database writes / downstream webhooks).
- Occurs intermittently under bursty traffic; observed 2-3x duplicates over a 6 hour window.
- Customer is on Dedicated capacity and requires guidance and a mitigation path; business impact: billing disputes and data correctness risk.

Environment:
- Lumos: Dedicated cluster in us-west-2, Redwood SDK Go v1.9.2 used for client, Python and Node microservices receiving callbacks.
- Serving runtime: redwood-v1-large pinned.
- Network: behind a customer edge proxy (Envoy) with HTTP/2 gRPC multiplexing enabled.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Start multiplexed gRPC client stream and dispatch 8 logical requests concurrently, each containing one tool/function call with per-action idempotency metadata (action_id + client_nonce).
2) After ~100 requests, simulate a transient network hiccup by briefly closing the TCP connection at the edge; client reconnects and resumes the multiplexed stream using client library resume token.
3) Observe downstream: some logical requests that previously showed ACKs have duplicate webhook deliveries or duplicate DB inserts from the downstream service.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicates are not correlated to a single action_id collision; they appear across multiple distinct action_ids.
- Duplicates sometimes appear on a different logical request than the original (i.e., action A handled again but attributed to slot/replay of action B).
- Customer's client logs show the SDK reusing a per-stream idempotency header bag that appears to be shared across multiplexed substreams after reconnect.

Expected behavior:
- Per-action idempotency scope should be isolated to the logical request boundary even when multiplexing over a single gRPC stream and across reconnect/resume.
- Retries/replays from the client or server should only re-run tools when the action_id for that logical request indicates a missing confirmation.

Preliminary logs / pointers from customer (included):
- Client trace snippet: "stream_resume_token=abc; last_acked_action=148; sent_action=149; action_id=uuid-149; idempotency: action_id=uuid-149; per_stream_nonce=ns-1"
- Downstream webhook logs showing two POSTs 1.2s apart for different delivery ids but same payload.
- Edge proxy (Envoy) logs show an HTTP/2 GOAWAY and immediate reconnect from the same client IP within 400ms.

Ask:
1) Confirm whether the server runtime has any behavior that can merge or normalize per-action idempotency baggage when a multiplexed stream resumes.
2) Provide recommended client-side patterns for Lumos to avoid cross-request leakage (e.g., per-request idempotency keys vs per-stream tokens, explicit confirmation step patterns).
3) If a bug is suspected in the serving runtime, provide investigation steps and a timeline for mitigation and/or hotfix.

Notes: This is distinct from a simple idempotency key collision—customer asserts keys are unique and contain UUIDs. The unusual part is re-assignment/duplication across logical requests after stream resume.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 11:05 UTC - SRE (initial triage): Noted that ours should treat per-action idempotency keys as opaque and never coalesce them across substreams. Hypothesis: SDK resume code path may be restoring a per-stream header map incorrectly. Asked customer for SDK debug logs at TRACE level and the go-client resume token handling snippet.
2026-03-14 12:30 UTC - Support (Priya): Noted potential interference point: header rewrite sidecar may be normalizing idempotency header names (lowercasing/truncation) and the Go SDK uses header bag serialization that might be susceptible to splitting across HTTP/2 frames. Requested a reproducible test plan to toggle sidecar header rewrite and observe behavior.
2026-03-14 13:10 UTC - Eng (runtime team): Observed a recent change in the resume path where cached per-stream metadata is re-applied to new substreams on resume; filing an engineering investigation to validate header isolation guarantees under multiplexing. Referenced PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2213 for related resume logic updates.
payload.summary: GRPC multiplexed batch: unexpected cross-request idempotency scope leakage causing duplicate tool runs

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-11 02:15 UTC, NovaDocs reported intermittent request timeouts and elevated tail latency when calling the Redwood inference API. Preliminary captures show a sudden rise in TCP retransmits and out-of-order packets for flows between our edge egress proxies and the regional serving fleet. Impact: Customer experiencing 10-20% 5xx errors and frequent streaming disconnects during business hours; production traffic for several routes timed out after multiple retransmit attempts. Hypothesis: asymmetric egress path causing packet reordering and spurious retransmits leading to request stalls and streaming cancellation.
~12% of NovaDocs requests observed with >5s tail latency or cancelled streams between 2026-03-11 02:00-04:30 UTC. Affects enterprise contract SLAs; customer reported degraded UX for real-time summarization feature.
1) Use NovaDocs prod API key and send 1k streaming generate requests to /v1/generate over us-east endpoint
2) Observe a 10-20% increase in aborted streams and >5s p95 on the customer route
3) Run tcpdump on egress-proxy-a and egress-proxy-b and compare sequence/ack patterns for affected flows
4) Reproduce shows bursty retransmits and duplicate ACKs when traffic traverses peering IX with AS path change
2026-03-11T02:18:22Z EDGE-EGRESS-A: TCP 10.32.4.21:52014 -> 172.31.9.7:443 RTO retransmit seq 0x1a2b3c
2026-03-11T02:18:22Z SERVING-01: TLS read timed out after 3200ms for request id=cd9f5
2026-03-11T02:20:10Z K8S-POD: high kubeproxy conntrack drops observed: conntrack: table full warnings
Capture note: load-balanced flows split across two egress peers with different AS path lengths; reordering observed when path switches mid-flow
Observed correlation between BGP flaps on transit provider B and spike in retransmits for affected flows.
Net team verified no interface errors on egress proxies; packet captures show consistent out-of-order delivery and duplicate ACKs from downstream.
Serving runtime logs show requests stuck in read loop waiting for TLS payload; retries from client cause multiple inflight KV cache misses increasing tail latency.
Applied iptables rule to force symmetric egress via preferred peer on a cohort of flows and saw immediate drop in retransmits and p95 latency improvement for test traffic.
Possible contributing factor: conntrack table reaching high-watermark under sustained burst causing NAT state convergence delays.
Related telemetry: increased retransmit rate aligns with customer request bursts and small window of BGP route change at 02:17 UTC.
Linked to runbook: Network Path Troubleshooting; follow up with transit vendor for asymmetry mitigation and adjust conntrack sizing on egress proxies.
Pinned NovaDocs routes to egress-peer-1 via iptables MARK + policy routing for the customer prefix; this reduced retransmit rate and dropped error rate for pinned traffic to <1% during the test window.
1) SRE to request upstream transit vendor ticket for AS path stability and to review peer filtering (owner: NetOps, due 2026-03-13)
2) Increase conntrack table size on egress proxies and roll to canary (owner: Infra, due 2026-03-13)
3) Implement short-term request-level retry backoff in the api-gateway to avoid immediate client retransmit amplification (owner: API team, due 2026-03-14)
4) Re-run load test with NovaDocs key after changes and monitor retransmit / p95 metrics for 24h (owner: Support/SRE, due 2026-03-14)
5) Postmortem and customer RCA to be prepared after root cause confirmation (owner: Support, due 2026-03-17)
Ava Martinez (Support) 2026-03-11T03:00Z: Customer observed failure spikes during morning ingest window. Sent initial mitigations and requested packet captures.
Liam Chen (SRE) 2026-03-11T04:05Z: Applied policy routing to pin traffic to egress-peer-1 for customer prefix. Early signals show improvement; continuing monitoring.
Priya Singh (Network) 2026-03-11T05:20Z: Opened ticket with transit provider TP-99823 for AS path churn; vendor acknowledges temporary misconfiguration on peering fabric.
NovaDocs_SRE 2026-03-11T06:02Z: Thanks for the quick mitigation — latency improved for our critical flows. Please advise on permanent fix schedule.
Mitigation applied: customer traffic pinned to stable egress peer and conntrack sizing increased in prod canary. Transit vendor is addressing BGP asymmetry. API gateway retry backoff deployed as a safety net. Follow-up: complete vendor fix and finalize postmortem. Customer notified and monitoring shows errors back to <1%.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent long-tail streaming responses (~10-30s) and occasional request timeouts while making high-concurrency streaming calls to the Redwood hosted API. Impact: User-facing feature (real-time summaries) degrading intermittently during peak windows; perceived as model slowness/timeouts. Environment: Dedicated account in us-east using SDK v1.3.1 with default retry/backoff settings. Initial hypothesis: model or runtime degradation. Actual root cause (see investigation): server-side windowed rate/soft-429 enforcement combined with aggressive client retries caused request amplification and queueing that manifested as long streaming latencies.
1) Use SDK v1.3.1 default config. 2) Start 40 concurrent streaming requests with small prompt sizes (~50 tokens) at 100 RPS aggregated from a single host. 3) Observe latency distribution: many requests succeed <500ms but a subset shows 10-30s tails or 504s. 4) Repeat under lower concurrency (10 concurrent) and tails disappear. 5) Upgrade to SDK v1.4.2 with adaptive jitter and limiters -> tails disappear.
Customer-provided excerpt (sanitized):
- 2026-03-10T14:02:01Z request id=rc-01a status=202 stream_open
- 2026-03-10T14:02:01Z request id=rc-01b status=429 retry-after=10
- 2026-03-10T14:02:02Z sdk retry attempt=1 id=rc-01b backoff_ms=100
- 2026-03-10T14:02:03Z request id=rc-01c status=200

Server side traces (sample):
- quota-controller: windowed_count=512 window_limit=480 window_reset_in=8s
- queue_depth: transient spike to 18 requests
- serving-runtime: token-gen latency per active worker normal (~12ms), but head-of-line wait due to queueing

Timeline: 2026-03-10 customer reported at 14:05; initial triage assumed model regression. Support captured request traces and SDK metrics. Key observations: 1) 429 soft-enforcement was returned during brief bursts (server logs show windowed_count > window_limit). 2) SDK v1.3.1 retries without jitter and with aggressive concurrency produced immediate replays into the same enforcement window. 3) Queue depth on gateway spiked; serving runtime workers were healthy but waiting on queued requests. 4) Reproduced in lab by simulating customer traffic pattern, confirmed that enabling SDK adaptive jitter limiter prevented amplification. 5) Found quota-controller behavior: window resets in ~8s; lack of distributed leaky-bucket smoothing allowed burst bleed-through. Hypothesis validated by: 1) reproducer with SDK v1.3.1 produces long tails and 429s; 2) SDK patch (v1.4.2) with randomized exponential backoff removes tails; 3) short-term server-side mitigation (smoothing window enforcement by adding 250ms random delay on suspected burst origin) reduces queue spikes.

2026-03-10 15:02 - SRE (Marta Chen): Observed windowed_count overshoot on quota-controller for the customer's tenant in us-east. Queue depth ephemeral but correlated with customer traffic spike. Attaching trace: https://internal-trace.redwood/trace/9931
2026-03-10 16:10 - Eng (Diego Alvarez): Reproduced locally using load tool with 40 concurrent streams. SDK retries retriggered 429s and amplified the burst. Patch candidate for SDK backoff settings prepared. Filing PR to platform to smooth enforcement window for bursty single-host traffic.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Customer (NarrativeHealth, Sarah L): Confirmed that reducing concurrency from 40->8 removes tail latencies immediately. Also validated that adding random jitter to client-side retries improved behavior.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer upgraded to SDK v1.4.2 per instructions. No further incidents observed over 48h. Closing with recommended actions and guidance.
2026-03-12 10:20 - Customer (Sarah L): Thanks — the real-time summaries are stable. We'll roll the SDK change to all services in their pipeline this week.
Root cause: interplay between windowed server-side soft-429 enforcement and aggressive client-side retry/concurrency behavior caused request amplification and head-of-line queueing that presented as long-tail streaming latencies and occasional timeouts. Fixes: 1) Customer guidance: upgrade SDK to v1.4.2 (includes randomized exponential backoff and client-side concurrency limiter) and reduce single-host concurrency for bursty workloads. 2) Server changes: merged quota-controller smoothing (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8321) to add small randomized admission delay to reduce synchronized replays; adjusted window thresholds for dedicated tenants to reduce overshoot. 3) Monitoring: added a dashboard alert for tenant-level queue_depth spikes and 429-rate anomalies and a runbook entry (Confluence link). Workaround applied: temporary smoothing rule in us-east until config rollout completed. Outcome: customer-confirmed stability; issue closed.
SDK: ship v1.4.2 and update quickstart examples to recommend concurrency defaults for streaming (max 10 per host)
Platform: quota-controller smoothing merged and rolled to us-east; schedule global rollout
Docs: update troubleshooting guide to surface 429 vs model-slowness patterns and recommended client settings
Monitoring: alert for tenant queue_depth > 10 and 429_rate > 3% sustained for 60s
