Issue summary: During a staged rollout of redwood-7b-v3 -> redwood-7b-v3-quant, session tokens issued immediately prior to the control plane's token rotation lost affinity. A small cohort of BrightPathHealth production requests were routed to fallback model variants, causing degraded quality and increased token spend.

Impact: ~0.8% of requests for the customer in us-east saw model fallback to quantized variant for up to 90s per session. Customers reported increased hallucination rates and a spike in per-request token cost. BrightPathHealth flagged as P1 due to clinical workflow impact.

Environment: Production (dedicated pool) in us-east region. Dedicated capacity, tenant-specific routing with session-pin enabled. Rollout policy: weighted progressive promote (10% -> 30% -> 60%). Control plane performed scheduled token rotation at 2026-03-12T14:03:00Z during the 10% -> 30% weight window.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a session (client receives session token T_old).
2) Trigger a weighted promote (promote 7b-v3 to 7b-v3-quant).
3) Control plane executes token rotation for routing keys (T_new issued).
4) In-flight requests using T_old temporarily lose lookup in the affinity store and are routed to fallback path.

Observed behavior: Affinity lookup for session tokens issued before the rotation returned a cache miss for ~60-120s, after which affinity reconciled. During the miss window, the routing layer selected the cheaper compatible model variant (quant) rather than honoring the pinned version. Logs show affinity misses coincident with control plane rotation events and prefix cache invalidations.

Expected behavior: Token rotation should be transparent to in-flight sessions. Existing tokens should map to the pinned version until session TTL or explicit unpin. No routing fallback should occur for pinned sessions.

Preliminary logs/traces (snippets):
- routing-service[2026-03-12T14:03:01Z] WARN affinity_lookup.go:142 missing affinity for token="T_old_abc123" route_id=brightpath-health-prod
- router[2026-03-12T14:03:02Z] INFO fallback_decision.go:87 selected_variant=redwood-7b-v3-quant reason=affinity_miss
- gateway[2026-03-12T14:03:05Z] ERROR proxy.go:212 upstream_call=failed status=200->quality_drop

Root cause hypothesis: Token rotation updated the control-plane token->affinity mapping and triggered a short-lived eviction cascade in the distributed affinity cache (Redis cluster + local in-process shards). Local shards remained stale until background reconcilers repopulated entries. During that window, routing falls back to variant selection logic which prefers capacity-compatible models. Two contributing factors identified: (1) the token rotation procedure cleared TTLs on the affinity namespace before repopulation, and (2) the routing fallback logic treats affinity miss as equivalent to "no pin" rather than transient cache miss.

Mitigation / Workaround applied:
- Immediately toggled token rotation to deferred mode for the active rollout (control plane) to stop further rotation operations.
- Temporary change deployed to routing-service to treat affinity misses during a known rotation window as "hold current route" for 120s (hotfix).
- Notified BrightPathHealth SREs and opened a dedicated Slack channel #support-brightpathhealth to coordinate.

Current status: Hotfix (routing-service) deployed to prod-us-east at 2026-03-12T15:10:00Z which reduces observed fallback to ~0.05% of requests. Control plane patch to perform rotation-safe handoff is under review.

Next steps / action items:
- [Eng] Convert token rotation flow to multi-phase commit: pre-warm affinity keys in new namespace and atomically flip pointer (owner: Rohan Patel, PR in review).
- [SRE] Add monitoring alert for affinity-miss spike during rotations (owner: Elena Kovacs).
- [Product] Schedule coordinated maintenance windows for rotations with affected dedicated customers (owner: Priya Nambiar).
- [CS] Follow up with BrightPathHealth with post-incident summary and SLA credit proposal (owner: Maya Chen).

Follow-up: We plan a full postmortem if customer impact persists beyond the SLA window. Temporary rollback of rotation is in-flight until the two-phase rotation is validated in staging.
2026-03-12T14:27:00Z - Rohan Patel: Acknowledged. Spinning up a debug trace on routing-service in us-east and pausing further control-plane rotations for dedicated tenants until we confirm behavior.
2026-03-12T14:45:12Z - Elena Kovacs (SRE): Confirmed affinity eviction pattern across 3 local shards. Possible race during namespace rename. Captured redis INFO and keyspace events.
2026-03-12T15:12:33Z - Rohan Patel: Hotfix pushed that treats affinity miss as transient if rotation flag is set (feature-flagged). Deploying to prod-us-east now. Monitoring for quality regressions.
2026-03-12T16:05:00Z - BrightPathHealth (customer): Noted much improved behavior after hotfix. Requesting timeline for permanent fix and assurance this won't recur during scheduled maintenance.
2026-03-13T09:22:10Z - Priya Nambiar (Product): Coordinating with account team to propose a maintenance window next week. Drafting customer comms and SLA credit offer.
2026-03-14T10:00:01Z - Rohan Patel: Control-plane PR submitted for two-phase rotation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1145. Added runbook steps and integration tests.

Customer reports sudden spike in 503s after applying a routing policy change for their Dedicated deployment.

Issue summary
- NimbusCRM updated routing policy (via Console) to prefer eu-west for a subset of traffic and pinned a model variant for an internal “assistant-v2” route.
- Immediately after change, they observed elevated 503s on /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses for that route.

Impact
- ~18–25% request failure rate (503) for route: assistant-v2 between 09:12–09:44 PT.
- Other routes remained stable.
- End users experienced degraded chat feature (intermittent failures, retries required).

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: nmb-ded-07
- Regions involved: us-east (primary), eu-west (new preference)

Customer-provided details
- Start time: 2025-02-18 09:12 PT
- Example request IDs (from customer logs):
  - req_01HQC2K3Z9X4R9P5YJ8V8Y8A1N
  - req_01HQC2M0B8P3JH2Y3A4M7ZQ2TT
- Symptom: 503 with body “upstream unavailable” (customer SDK surfaced as ServiceUnavailable)

What changed (per customer)
- Updated routing policy:
  - Increased weight to eu-west for assistant-v2
  - Disabled fallback routing (to avoid “unexpected model variants”)
  - Pinned model: redwood-llama-3.1-70b-instruct (customer label)

Support ask
1) Identify why this routing policy change results in 503s.
2) Provide guidance/guardrails to prevent recurrence.
3) Request: safer visibility into “what config changed” during incidents (customer noted that during incident response they couldn’t quickly confirm which flags/weights had actually propagated, and Redwood responders also had to manually hunt diffs).
2025-02-18 09:20 PT — Owen Phillips (Support)
Acknowledged. Pulling request IDs + checking Dedicated health for nmb-ded-07. Initial look shows increased 503s isolated to assistant-v2 route. Escalating to on-call (SRE + Platform Routing).
2025-02-18 09:24 PT — Dev Patel (Support Escalation)
Engaged #eng-oncall and #incidents with incident stub INC-2025-02-18-rcfg-503. Asking customer for exact policy JSON / screenshot of Console change + confirmation if change was saved once or multiple times.

Customer: Can you confirm whether you toggled fallback OFF and also pinned a model variant in the same change?
2025-02-18 09:28 PT — NimbusCRM (Customer)
Confirmed: single change. Fallback turned off + pinned model in assistant-v2 + set eu-west weight to 60% (us-east 40%). No other changes.
2025-02-18 09:33 PT — Mina Haddad (Routing)
Quick hypothesis: model pin is not available in eu-west for this dedicated pool OR capacity guard is rejecting due to admission control when fallback is disabled. If fallback enabled, requests might have been routed back to us-east where model is healthy.

Need to verify: model availability by region for this tenant + recent routing policy propagation status.
2025-02-18 09:36 PT — Logan Wright (Telemetry)
Metrics: eu-west admission_rejects spiked at same timestamp; queue depth elevated; GPU util normal in us-east. 503s correlate strongly with eu-west traffic shift. Looks like hard 503 from router when no eligible backends (fallback disabled).

Added temporary dashboard link in #incidents (tenant filter + route filter).
2025-02-18 09:38 PT — Ethan Park (Control Plane)
Checked config store history: routing policy write at 09:11:54 PT. The model pin was set to a variant that is currently only provisioned in us-east for this dedicated cluster; eu-west pool has older image and does not have that model artifact.

Because fallback was disabled, router had no alternate eligible target in eu-west and returned 503. We should improve validation: when a policy pins model X with region weights, validate model X is eligible in all weighted regions OR force fallback-on / warn.

Action now: customer can either (a) re-enable fallback or (b) set eu-west weight to 0 until model artifact is staged in eu-west.
2025-02-18 09:41 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Proposed mitigation sent to customer: set eu-west weight to 0 OR re-enable fallback. Customer prefers eu-west off for now (they explicitly disabled fallback for compliance review).

Also requesting Release Eng to confirm whether this model artifact can be staged in eu-west for nmb-ded-07 and ETA.
2025-02-18 09:44 PT — NimbusCRM (Customer)
We set eu-west weight to 0 (back to us-east 100%). 503s have dropped back to baseline. Thanks.

Request: can Redwood add a preflight check in Console so we don’t ship a policy that can cause 503s? Also during the incident it was hard to verify “what exactly changed” — we want a safe diff view (no secrets) we can reference during incident calls.
2025-02-18 09:52 PT — Connor O'Brien (Release Engineering)
We can stage the pinned model artifact to eu-west for this dedicated pool but need a maintenance window due to image update. Earliest window: 2025-02-20 01:00–02:00 PT. If customer wants earlier, we can do a hot stage but higher risk.

For now, region weight should remain 0 to avoid recurrence.
2025-02-18 10:05 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Noting a recurring pain point: responders had to manually reconstruct the routing policy diff + propagation state. This aligns with incident-bot v2 goals (config diff card with redaction + propagation hints). Linking internal threads and asking Platform to prioritize safe diff endpoints + audit.

Reference similar incident thread: #incidents 1740345510-sev1-503s-after-config-push (context gaps).
2025-02-19 11:18 PT — Dev Patel (Support)
Customer confirmed stable since mitigation. Scheduled staging window communicated.

Next steps on our side:
- Platform: add policy validation (model availability vs region weights, fallback off warnings).
- Tooling: provide customer-safe config diff visibility (during incidents + after change) with audit logging.

Marking as Resolved; keeping open follow-ups in internal tracking.
Root cause: customer routing policy pinned a model variant not provisioned/eligible in eu-west for their Dedicated pool while shifting 60% traffic to eu-west and disabling fallback routing. Router had no eligible targets in eu-west and returned 503.

Mitigation: customer set eu-west routing weight back to 0% (us-east 100%). Error rate returned to baseline within minutes.

Planned follow-up:
- Stage pinned model artifact to eu-west for nmb-ded-07 (scheduled maintenance window).
- Add guardrails/validation in routing policy editor: block or warn on region/model eligibility mismatches, especially when fallback is disabled.
- Improve incident-time visibility with a customer/tenant-safe config diff view (redacted) + propagation status and audit logging; align with incident-bot v2 work.
Notes for SRE/Platform:
- This is a prime example for incident-bot v2 config-diff + routing context: on-call needed immediate visibility of routing weights, pinned model, fallback toggle, and whether the change propagated to all regions.
- Customer explicitly wants a safe diff they can reference during incident bridges (redacted; no secrets). Ensure any future implementation includes allowlist fields, secret detection, and audited access.
- Consider adding an automated preflight check for (tenant, route, model pin, region weights) -> eligible backends. If not, Console should block save or require explicit override.

Artifacts:
- Slack: #incidents incident stub INC-2025-02-18-rcfg-503
- Similar pattern referenced in #incidents thread 1740345510-sev1-503s-after-config-push
- Confluence: Recent deploys + config diff debugging runbook

Customer comms:
- Customer wants compliance-friendly behavior (fallback disabled by policy), so we should treat “fallback off” as a high-risk config and require stronger validation + warnings.
payload.summary: Elevated 503s after customer routing policy change (fallback disabled + region pin mismatch) — request safer config diff visibility during incidents

2026-03-11T09:12:00Z Miguel Ortega: Replicated locally with synthetic client that performs a TLS write-half-close during a streaming response behind an h2->h1 downgrade. Found race where trailer/envelope serialization is queued after stream write but connection shutdown path flushes earlier, causing attachment not to be sent.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-form streaming responses which include attachments (base64 image footer + content-checksum metadata) occasionally arrive with the final attachment missing and with duplicated system messages interleaved near the end. The failure is correlated with an abrupt TLS half-close on the client path and a subsequent HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 downgrade at the edge.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: Final attachment (image footer and checksum) omitted from streaming response ~1-2% of long streams; downstream consumer rejects the response due to missing checksum.
- Workloads: Dedicated pool in us-west serving QuillDocs workspace.

Environment / context:
- Dedicated tenant, prod-us-west, edge-proxy chain includes corporate WAF -> CDN -> API gateway -> serving-runtime.
- Streaming method: SSE (fallback to long-lived HTTP/1.1 where upgrade fails) and WebSocket in an alternate path.
- Observed when model generates large multi-part payloads (attachments embedded as base64 and trailing metadata envelope).
1) Authenticate with QuillDocs dedicated API keys in us-west region.
2) Submit a long generation (approx 6-10k tokens) that includes an instruction to attach an image and a trailing checksum metadata envelope.
3) Simulate intermittent TLS half-close from client side (e.g., client closes TLS write channel) or force edge to downgrade to h1 by inserting a malformed ALPN on a path.
4) Observe SSE stream: in problematic runs the stream emits duplicated system messages and then terminates without the final attachment/checksum block.
Customer-provided truncated SSE transcript attached to ticket (redacted): https://files.quilldocs.net/tmp/sse-trace-03-10.log
Edge access logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:07Z - client ip 54.204.x.x - TLS half-close observed - ALPN fallback to http/1.1
API gateway trace (trace id: 7c1d9e): worker reported connection reset during flush; serving-runtime returned 200 with missing trailer meta
Serving runtime logs: session 0x7f4a - streaming flush aborted after window update race; KV cache preserved; trailing envelope not serialized
2026-03-10 14:25 - quill-support@quilldocs.com: Customer: We've seen this 3 times in the last 24h, always for longer documents with images. Consumer pipeline fails validation because checksum is missing. Attached a client-side PCAP and SSE log.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:37 - SRE triage (Elena Park): Observed ALPN negotiation fallback on several traces. Edge reported upstream GOAWAY after TLS session renegotiate. Marking as P1 due to customer validation failures. Assigning to runtime on-call.
Observation 1: Failure frequency correlates with multi-hop path changes (CDN + WAF path) and TLS renegotiation attempts.
Observation 2: Serving runtime emits final JSON choice and marks stream complete, but the trailing attachment envelope is owned by a separate serializer that races with connection close.
Hypothesis: Connection-level half-close leads HTTP/2 stack to issue a stream reset vs a graceful end; the runtime's trailer writer has no retry when kernel-level flush fails on abrupt TLS closure.
Reproduction: Synthetic test using a proxy that intentionally performs TLS write-half-close during final trailer write reproduces missing trailer 9/10 runs if an ALPN fallback to h1 is forced; only 0/10 runs fail on pure h2 path.
Temporary mitigation attempted: pin route to h2-only upstream (via edge rule) for a subset of customer traffic — eliminated missing attachments in A/B tranche.
Related: see linked incident SUP-214159 (stream final segment omission during proxy rewrite) and SUP-420420 (edge-probe split fragment leading to orphaned tail).
Workaround: Edge rule created to prefer HTTP/2 ALPN on QuillDocs tenant in prod-us-west (effective 2026-03-11T17:00Z). Mitigated customer-visible failures for the impacted production pool.
Fix in progress: Runtime change to make trailer/attachment serialization synchronous with final token flush when connection close is observed; added retry/flush path on TLS write errors. Engine PR drafted: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1452 (WIP).
Follow-up actions:
- Create API gateway health-check to detect ALPN fallback spikes and surface as alert (operational task).
- Add unit/integration tests for TLS half-close + trailer flush race.
- Postmortem draft (linked confluence) to review long-term design: ensure trailing envelopes are part of main response path or persisted to ephemeral KV to retry on reconnect.
- Customer follow-up: schedule check-in with QuillDocs success manager once PR is deployed to staging and validated.
payload.summary: TLS half-close + HTTP/2 downgrade during streaming causes final attachment checksum to be dropped and interleaved system messages

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NorthStar Bank, enterprise) requests a configurable on-demand forensic export pipeline that can: produce delta snapshots with monotonic watermark tokens, sign daily manifests with an RFC3161-style timestamping expectation, deliver to customer-managed SFTP that uses OIDC-based role assertions (no long-lived credentials), and provide an automated verification report that proves cross-region temporal consistency (us-east vs eu-west) for the export window.

Impact:
Customer requires this for periodic legal discovery and regulatory audits. They want proof that no events were dropped or re-ordered across regions during the export window and need artifacts suitable for chain-of-custody. Delay impacts legal compliance timelines and their incident response capabilities.

Environment:
Production audit stream (tenant: northstar-prod) spanning us-east and eu-west. SIEM target: Elastic ECS 1.13 index mapping; retention policy on their side is 7 years.

Requested deliverables / acceptance criteria:
- On-demand snapshot API that accepts a time-range and returns a signed manifest + resume token (opaque) for the delta.
- Manifest format documentation (fields, canonical canonicalization, signature algorithm). Customer expects SHA-256 digests and Ed25519 signature.
- RFC3161-style timestamping (or equivalent anchored timestamp) for daily manifests.
- SFTP delivery option that supports OIDC role assertion (customer will supply IdP metadata and allowed audience). No storage of long-lived credentials on Redwood.
- A verification report that includes: per-shard checksums, monotonic watermark tokens, event ordering checks, and cross-region reconciliation summary.
- A small verification harness (python script) and example Elastic ingest mapping snippet (ECS 1.13) for NorthStar's SIEM ingestion.

Example log snippet (customer-provided):
{"timestamp":"2026-03-10T14:02:03.123Z","tenant":"northstar-prod","event_id":"evt-9f3a","action":"model.generate","route":"/api/generate","user_id":"u-3421","bytes":1420}

Access notes:
NorthStar will provide a temporary test SFTP endpoint and OIDC client/role metadata for the POC. They do not want any PII returned in the verification report samples; pseudonymized IDs are acceptable.

Other constraints / non-goals:
- Customer explicitly asked that exported payloads are not re-ingested back into Redwood.
- They prefer per-tenant pseudonymization for exported user identifiers (salted HMAC).

Steps requested by customer for POC:
1) Provide a spec for the manifest and signature scheme.
2) Demo an on-demand delta export for a 24-hour window to the test SFTP using OIDC role assertion.
3) Deliver verification report and python harness that validates the manifest and checks cross-region temporal alignment.

Notes:
Customer emphasized legal auditability and chain-of-custody. They asked about retention of manifests on Redwood side for 90 days and about exposing export operation logs in the Console.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 15:05 - NorthStar Bank (Customer): Confirmed RFC3161-style timestamping is acceptable; they prefer Ed25519 for manifest signatures. Provided test SFTP endpoint hostname and IdP metadata pointer (privately shared).
2026-03-14 12:30 - SRE (Liam): Performed a quick inventory: existing export pipeline supports daily manifests with SHA-256 and RSA signatures. Ed25519 path requires a small infra change (lib update + sign endpoint). Delta-token resume semantics exist but not exposed via public API. Triage: add tasks for manifest docs, temporary POC endpoint, and OIDC SFTP connector test.
Confirmed current exporter supports deterministic JSON canonicalization and SHA-256 digests for payloads (RFC8785 style canonicalization needs verification).
Ed25519 signing currently not supported in production signing service; prototype exists in staging. Estimate ~3-4 engineer-days to enable in prod with KMS-backed key material or HSM proxy.
Delta resume token: service emits monotonic sequence numbers per-tenant per-shard. Need to expose an opaque resume token in the on-demand API and document its verification semantics.
Cross-region reconciliation: will build a reconciliation job that compares per-shard checksums and watermark tokens across regions for the requested window. Potential challenge: clock skew between regions; propose using manifest timestamps plus event-level timestamps and watermark ordering to compute consistency.
OIDC SFTP: SRE to evaluate existing sftp-exporter connector which currently supports user/password and mTLS. OIDC role-assertion flow will require an adapter to exchange token for short-lived sftp credentials or use ssh-cert issuance via customer's IdP.
Pending - POC plan drafted; waiting on NorthStar to provide temporary test SFTP credentials (OIDC metadata exchange) and to confirm whether they want Redwood-signed manifests only or cross-signed artifacts with their key.
1) Prepare manifest format draft and circulate to customer by 2026-03-16.
2) Stand up a POC Ed25519 signing path in a canary namespace and run two test exports to the provided test SFTP by 2026-03-18.
3) Deliver python verification harness and ECS mapping snippet for their SIEM by 2026-03-20.
4) Follow-up security review to decide HSM vs KMS for manifest signing keys.
payload.summary: On-demand forensic log bridge with delta-watermarking, OIDC escrow and cross-region temporal consistency verification

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports SSE sessions truncate final paragraph and lose trailing metadata when the client experiences a multipath network handoff (e.g., WiFi -> cellular) during an in-flight stream. Impact: several API calls from Nimbus Health observing truncated clinical notes at the end of streams, causing downstream data loss and retransmission. Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated enterprise tenant. Observed behavior: when the TCP path migrates and the edge layer rebinds the session, heartbeat frames are occasionally delivered out-of-order relative to payload fragments; the SDK resumes but the final 'end' marker and trailing metadata are missing or delayed past client timeout. Expected behavior: heartbeat frames should be ordering-neutral for stream framing; resume should replay missing payloads or ensure terminal events are reliably delivered after a handoff. Customer impact: moderate — several generation completions dropped (missing 1-2 sentences) affecting clinical note integrity.
1) Use the customer's SDK to open an SSE streaming request against redwood-chat-13b in us-east with verbose keepalive (200ms).
2) Start a long completion (~800 tokens) that will stream for >10s, include trailing JSON metadata in the final chunk,
3) Mid-stream, trigger network path migration on client (simulate WiFi->cellular using multipath proxy or local NAT path change).
4) Observe client reconnect/resume behavior and whether final 'end' event and metadata arrive or are truncated.
5) Repeat behind an enterprise transparent proxy / TLS-inspecting middlebox to reproduce edge-proxy interaction.
2026-03-10T15:42:11Z edge-proxy[conn-0x7f]: keepalive received (seq=1245)
2026-03-10T15:42:11Z edge-proxy[conn-0x7f]: payload chunk seq=1246 (partial), metadata header missing end-marker
2026-03-10T15:42:12Z serving-runtime[pod-a]: resume request from tenant Nimbus Health; client-id rotated -> replay window invoked
2026-03-10T15:42:12Z serving-runtime[pod-a]: heartbeat frame processed after payload chunk -> delivered out-of-order to SSE multiplexer
2026-03-10T15:42:15Z client-sdk: user timeout waiting for end marker -> client closed connection; last-fragment-not-final
Initial hypothesis: edge-proxy reorder of micro-frames during connection handoff can push heartbeat envelopes ahead of terminal payload fragments, confusing client SDK resume logic.
Observed a ~20-300ms window where the resume handshake accepts a new transport and edge-proxy flushes a heartbeat frame before queued payload fragments are drained from the old path.
Client SDK cancels on missing terminal marker after configurable 3s wait; in some cases the terminal JSON metadata arrives after client-side close, causing apparent truncation.
Correlation across traces shows affected calls cluster around NAT rebind/multipath events and when TLS session tickets are re-used by intermediate proxies.
Reproducible in lab when forcing path migration; adding 50ms artificial delay in edge-proxy drain makes behavior deterministic.

Issue summary: Customer (Novum HealthTech) observed that several user sessions that were pinned to their dedicated model version gpt-large-v1 started receiving responses from the canary variant intermittently during a peak traffic window. Impact: ~8% of requests from pinned sessions returned canary outputs between 2026-03-10T14:02 and 2026-03-10T14:45 UTC, causing subtle semantic differences in model output for live users. Pinned sessions should not be demoted under normal operation.

Environment: prod-us-east (dedicated capacity pool: novum-pool-3).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a session with version pin header X-Model-Pin: gpt-large-v1 for a tenant on novum-pool-3.
2) Simulate sustained burst of requests from many tenants to trigger edge rate-shedding (we used a controlled load test matching observed QPS).
3) Observe routing decisions in trace and request logs (trace IDs included below) where session affinity token is present but route resolves to canary variant.

Expected behavior: Requests with an active pin should route to the pinned model variant until pin expires or is explicitly changed.
Observed behavior: During the rate-shedding window our edge layer deprioritized pinned routes and allowed canary routes to be selected to satisfy SLOs; pinned sessions saw intermittent responses from canary variant.

Relevant logs/traces (sample):
- trace: us-east:trace-20260310-14:12:35: t=trace-8af3cf (session token: s-9c2b). Route decision: edge-proxy rate-shed priority=low -> routing-layer selected fallback route canary/gpt-large-v1-canary.
- request id: req-4f7a2f9b: pin header present, backend assigned: canary node id cn-42.

Notes: Customer reported via support channel #support-novum and provided 6 sample request IDs. We reproduced locally using controlled traffic and confirmed similar route inversion under the same rate-shedding config.
1) Pin session to gpt-large-v1 via X-Model-Pin header.
2) Generate a synthetic QPS spike across multiple tenants to trigger edge rate shedding policies.
3) Observe routing decisions in trace logs for pinned sessions.
4) Verify that the backend returned canary variant responses intermittently.
Selected sample traces: trace-8af3cf (see description), trace-8af3d1, trace-8af3e2. Edge proxy logs show 'rate-shed: true' with policy id rs-edge-priority-2. Routing-layer debug shows 'pin-resolve: ok' then 'deprioritize-pin: true' decision event. Serving runtime logs show request handed to canary pool node cn-42 with model tag gpt-large-v1-canary.
2026-03-10 14:20 UTC - Initial reproducible case validated by SRE: controlled load caused edge rate-shed to activate and routing decisions to deprioritize pinned flows.
Hypothesis A: Edge rate-shedding policy incorrectly treats pinned routes as low-priority under global contention due to missing pin-priority override in policy evaluation.
Hypothesis B: A short-circuit in routing-layer evaluation reorders candidate list after pin check when edge-proxy attaches a 'shed' tag, leading to selection of canary nodes with higher free capacity.
Checked config: edge rate-shedding rules (rs-edge-priority-*) did not include explicit 'pin:true' clause prior to 2026-03-10; default behavior was to evaluate available capacity only.
SRE ran a test toggling pin-priority flag in staging which preserved pinned routing under simulated edge load; suggests config deficiency rather than runtime bug.
Related PR 6b9f4d3 updated routing-layer to accept 'shed' tags and reorder candidate list for best-effort SLO compliance; change did not include safeguard for pinned sessions.
Cross-referenced SUP-31147 for earlier pinning anomalies during rollouts; different trigger but similar symptom of pin overshadowing.
We collected additional telemetry: ~92% of pinned requests stayed pinned, ~8% diverted during peak short window; average diversion duration per session was 1-3 minutes.
Engineering determined root cause: policy config omission — rate-shedding prioritized global SLOs without honoring explicit pin flags.
Customer (Novum) initial: 'We started seeing odd responses in prod around 14:05 UTC. Several ongoing user flows returned an older canary output. This is breaking a small fraction of user workflows.'
Support (Maya): 'Thanks — we're investigating. Can you share request IDs and whether pin header was present?' (attached 6 IDs).
SRE (Ethan): 'Reproduced with controlled load. Edge policy rs-edge-priority-2 active. Pin header checked but deprioritized by shed tag. Engaging routing team.'
Routing eng (Sofia Nguyen): 'Found that recent reorder logic added to favor low-latency nodes when 'shed' tag is present. That logic didn't exempt pinned sessions; proposing a config hotfix to treat pinned:true as highest priority.'
Customer acceptance: 'Workaround acceptable if we get a mitigation and root cause. Please advise ETA.'
Support update (Maya): 'We have a hotfix planned to land within the hour to add a pin-exempt clause to the edge evaluation. We'll follow up once change is deployed and confirm telemetry.'
SRE follow-up: 'Hotfix deployed 2026-03-10T15:05 UTC. Post-deploy checks show diversion rate dropped to 0.2% in subsequent 60 minutes; customer confirmed no further user complaints.'
Root cause: Edge rate-shedding policy omitted an explicit 'pin' exemption; combined with routing-layer reordering for shed-tagged nodes, pinned sessions could be demoted. Mitigation: 1) Hotfix (config change) applied to edge policy to set 'pin:exempt' in evaluation clause (deployed 2026-03-10T15:05 UTC). 2) Routing-layer patch (PR#1587) added defensive check to prevent candidate reordering for sessions with active pin tokens. Post-deploy verification: diversion <0.5% and customer confirmed. Follow-ups: schedule a test matrix to cover rate-shedding + pin combinations, add automated regression test to CI for pin-exempt behavior, and update runbook.
Hotfix deployed to prod-us-east at 2026-03-10T15:05 UTC (edge config rs-edge-priority-2 updated).
Routing-layer change merged PR#1587 and rolled out in canary + prod on 2026-03-11.
Customer notification sent 2026-03-12 with incident summary and follow-up plan.

Update Runbook: include step to verify pin-exempt flag when modifying rate-shedding rules (owner: SRE).

Issue summary: Customer (ClipSync Media) reported a recurring spike in P90/P99 latency between 18:00-20:00 UTC over several days. Symptoms included ~30-40s queueing, elevated p95/p99 from ~180ms to 2.4s, and intermittent 504 responses for short requests. Impact: production traffic degradation for 3 customer-facing endpoints; increased error rates triggered PagerDuty. Environment: dedicated reservation (4xA10G per reservation) in us-west-2, model pinned to redwood/gpt-3-small-q4. Timeline: first observed 2026-03-08 evening, escalated 2026-03-10. Customer reported correlation with their evening batch traffic window.
1) Send sustained low-latency inference requests at 100 qps to the customer's reserved pool during 18:00-20:00 UTC window.
2) Simultaneously schedule an internal large-batch offline job that schedules long sequences/batched inference (simulated noisy neighbor).
3) Observe queue length, GPU mem usage, and p95/p99 token latencies.
4) Note autoscaler behavior when pool utilization crosses 70% (expected scale-up) and watch for cooldown delays.
Expected: steady latency ~ <250ms. Observed: long tail latency and intermittent 504s when noisy batch starts.
[2026-03-10T18:07:12Z] serving-runtime WARN evict_kv_cache: eviction triggered, evicted 14 prefixes (pool=A-clip-01)
[2026-03-10T18:07:13Z] kernel ERROR cuMemAlloc: out of memory, fallback to host staging (alloc size=3.1GiB)
[2026-03-10T18:07:15Z] scheduler INFO queue_length=84 scheduled=2 running=6
[2026-03-10T18:07:15Z] api-gateway ERROR upstream_response_timeout status=504 path=/v1/generate request_id=xyz-123
[2026-03-10T18:09:02Z] autoscaler INFO scale_event: desired=6 current=4 reason=cpu_mem_pressure cooldown_remaining=40s
[2026-03-10T18:09:45Z] serving-runtime WARN kernel_preempt: preemption_count=3 high_latency=true
[2026-03-10T18:10:05Z] telemetry METRICS p95=2400ms p99=5880ms gpu_util=97% gpu_mem_used=98%
- Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor batch jobs triggered GPU memory pressure leading to KV cache evictions and host staging for allocations, causing long tail token latencies and timeouts.
- Telemetry confirms repeated spikes in GPU memory usage to ~98% coincident with customer's reported window.
- Autoscaler logs show a scale-up decision at 18:09 but cooldown prevented immediate scaling due to a conservative cooldown policy from previous config.
- Confirmed internal background job (batch-analytics-job id=ba-2026-03-08) was scheduled in same cluster and used large micro-batches that preempted kernels.
- Kernel-level messages indicate cuMemAlloc fallback; this correlates with >30s latency windows and occasional 504s from api-gateway.
- Repro tested in staging by launching synthetic noisy neighbor with similar GPU batch characteristics; reproduced tail latencies and evictions.
- Considered model-level change (reduce batch size), autoscale policy modification, and tenant isolation via scheduling affinities.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 19:28 - María Gutierrez (Customer Success): Customer confirmed error rate dropped after throttling their nightly batch. They still saw elevated p95 for ~10 minutes after. Customer asks for long-term fix to avoid manual throttling.
2026-03-12 11:07 - Customer (ClipSync Ops): Thanks for fast response. Requesting recommendation doc to avoid future collisions between scheduled analytics and inference traffic.
Immediate actions: 1) Throttled internal noisy neighbor batch job and applied node affinity to move analytics jobs off ClipSync reserved nodes. 2) Deployed autoscaler emergency path: reduced cooldown for emergency scale-ups when gpu_mem_pressure > 90%. 3) Increased eviction logging and alerting for KV cache evictions. 4) Short-term recommendation to customer: pin to smaller model variant during their batch window or schedule batches to off-peak.
Permanent/next steps: - Engineering to land autoscaler PR to safely allow faster emergency scaling for reserved pools (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/193). - Runtime team to add kernel preemption backoff and better host-staging mitigation. - Runbook update: document how to detect noisy neighbor and how to temporarily throttle internal batch jobs. Ticket closed after customer validation on 2026-03-11.
Add autoscaler 'emergency_scale' policy and tests
Add metric-driven scheduler isolation for dedicated pools
Improve KV cache eviction metrics and alerts
Customer-facing best-practices doc for scheduling large batches
We acknowledged impact same day, provided immediate mitigation (throttling and affinity), and deployed autoscaler override. Customer validated fix within 24 hours and agreed to follow-up guidance on scheduling and model pinning.

Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 08:23 UTC Arkwood Retail observed a sudden increase in duplicate completions, transient streaming resets, and a correlated billing surge. Customer reported widespread user-facing timeouts in their chat feature and duplicate messages appearing in production.
Multiple Arkwood endpoints (chat assist and order-intent classifiers) experienced duplicated completions and intermittent stream truncation for ~42 minutes. Estimated billable duplicate tokens: ~1.2M tokens. Severity impacted Arkwood's afternoon traffic window (high revenue period).
Dedicated GPU pool (dedicated-arkwood-us-east), control plane region us-east-1, routing policy: tiered-fallback (dedicated -> hosted-lowcost). Autoscaler configured with burst pools enabled.
Routing controller oscillated between dedicated and hosted variants on a per-request basis for a subset of customer traffic. The serving-runtime accepted duplicate inflight work (lack of idempotency enforcement across route changes). Retries + replays combined with streaming reconnects produced duplicate outputs and extra token billing.
1) Support placed Arkwood traffic into a temporary static route pinned to dedicated-arkwood-us-east (bypassed tiered-fallback) at 08:29 UTC. 2) Rate-limited automated client retries at the edge for Arkwood (6-second backoff). 3) Eng disabled burst pooling for the dedicated pool to stabilize autoscaler behavior.

2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - Full rollout complete. Monitoring shows normal completion rate; billing anomaly captured for reconciliation.

Hypothesis A: Autoscaler health-check window too aggressive; small transient GC/latency spikes marked nodes unhealthy and triggered routing fallback.
Hypothesis B: Routing controller lacked debounce; immediate fallback to hosted variant created per-request route flips which allowed duplicate dispatch.
Finding: Correlated node-level OOM-kernel reclaim spikes on two gpus in dedicated-arkwood-us-east pool; health-check threshold (3s) considered nodes unhealthy and removed them briefly; routing controller reacted within 500ms and started routing to hosted variant. When nodes recovered, routing flipped back.
Root cause: aggressive autoscaler health-check + routing controller rapid fallback led to per-request route oscillation. Fixes applied: (1) increased health-check stabilization window from 3s to 12s for dedicated pools, (2) routing controller route-change debounce of 5s added to avoid per-request flips, (3) serving-runtime patched to enforce request-level idempotency keys for in-flight deduplication across route changes.
Temporary: pin Arkwood to dedicated pool while hotfix developed and rolled out.
Hotfix rollout: canary 10% at 09:27 UTC -> full roll at 09:40 UTC. Monitored for 30m; metrics stable.

Issue summary:
Customer (FinLedger) reports intermittent user-facing streaming breaks for long-lived chat sessions in their private deployment. Breaks correlate with gRPC errors and immediate reconnect attempts from the SDK.

Impact:
- Several production chat sessions dropped every ~3 minutes for users in us-east-1.
- Affects real-time streaming responses and some control-plane heartbeats; customers see partial responses followed by reconnect.
- Customer SLA: private deployment with 24/7 support (enterprise).

Environment:
- Private deployment behind customer-managed Palo Alto NGFW (on-prem firewall + transit GW).
- Redwood control plane + model-serving endpoints over peered subnets (10.10.0.0/16).
- Observed in prod | us-east-1 only.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start long-running streaming chat session via Redwood SDK to vicuna-13b-stream pinned model.
2) Let session remain idle (no token generation) for ~180 seconds after last activity.
3) Next client send triggers a quick failure: gRPC UNAVAILABLE or TCP connection reset and immediate reconnect.

Observed behavior:
- TCP RSTs from peer seen in packet captures between client subnet and control-plane (RST originates from intermediate firewall IP).
- Session breaks consistently around ~180 seconds of idle time.

Expected behavior:
- Long-lived streaming sessions should survive idle periods; client should send keepalives or runtime should support session keepalives so firewall state is preserved.

Logs & diagnostic artifacts provided by customer:
- tcpdump from a client host showing: "src=10.20.12.58 dst=10.10.1.14 RST" at t=00:02:59 after session start.
- Firewall session log export (redacted): shows session aged-out at 180s with action=reset, policy=inspection-idle-probe.
- SDK debug logs: last successful frame at t=00:02:50; error at t=00:02:59: "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed".
- No evidence of server-side OOM or restart in serving runtime metrics for that pod.

Initial investigation notes (Support):
- Verified RSTs originate outside Redwood control-plane (intermediate firewall IP recorded in pcap).
- Control-plane and model-serving side show persistent sockets until RST; no server-initiated close recorded.
- Customer's Palo Alto configuration includes a custom TCP idle timeout of 180s for inspected sessions and an "idle-probe" action that injects a TCP RST for sessions it considers dead.

Hypothesis:
- Customer-managed firewall aggressively resets stateful connections after 180s idle (inspection/idle-probe). Our serving runtime keeps gRPC streams open without frequent application-level keepalives, so connections appear idle to the NGFW and are reset.

Workarounds attempted and results:
- Customer enabled SDK-level application heartbeats: sending a small application-level ping every 60s avoids the reset for several sessions. (Mitigates but not ideal.)
- SRE requested customer to create firewall exception for control-plane/model-serving subnets; customer plans to test a bypass rule during maintenance window.

Recommended mitigations / next steps:
- Short-term: advise customer to enable SDK application heartbeats or reduce firewall idle time. Documented as immediate workaround.
- Short-medium term: add TCP keepalive configuration in the private-deploy agent/runtime (configurable keepalive interval and probe count) so OS-level probes preserve state across middleboxes. See linked PR for initial runtime change.
- Long-term: update private deployment runbook to recommend recommended NGFW policies (allowlist control-plane ranges or extend idle timeout) and provide explicit guidance for inspection bypass for streaming endpoints.

Follow-ups / owner:
- Eng (networking) to review PR #1876 that plumbs conservative TCP keepalive defaults for private deploys (assignee: Diego Morales).
- Customer success to coordinate firewall exception test with FinLedger network team (owner: Priya Shah).

Resolution notes (in-progress):
- Customer implemented SDK heartbeats as a temporary mitigation and reported reduced incidents.
- Diego Morales opened INT-4382 to track runtime keepalive rollout and QA.
- Support to schedule confluence runbook update after runtime change lands.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 10:08 - FinLedger NetOps (customer): Confirmed Palo Alto policy 'session-idle-timeout' set to 180s for application-inspection profile. Will test bypass rule in staging tonight.
2026-03-14 03:20 - FinLedger NetOps (customer): After bypassing inspection for control-plane CIDR, streaming sessions no longer reset in the test environment. Will roll to prod later today.
payload.summary: Corporate firewall idle-probe policy terminates long-lived gRPC/control-plane sessions causing streaming interruptions in private deployment

Issue summary:
Customer reports a missing reserve (hourly buffer) credit on the finalized invoice for the billing window 2026-03-07 00:00 to 2026-03-07 01:00 UTC. The reserve credit was expected to offset a transient burst while their Dedicated fallback routed traffic to Hosted for ~15 minutes. Instead the invoice shows the burst usage billed with no reserve credit and an interim negative line item later that appears unrelated.

Impact:
- NovaCommerce incurred an unexpected charge of ~$1,200 on a finalized invoice for a one-hour window.
- Customer billing reconciliation flagged the missing reserve credit; finance has paused autopay pending resolution.

Environment:
- Production (us-east)
- Customer uses Dedicated capacity with Hosted fallback enabled
- Affected model variants: rw-open-7b-quant (dedicated), rw-embed-2.1 (hosted)

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) 2026-03-07T00:12 UTC - Dedicated pool reported transient saturation and triggered fallback routing policy to Hosted for ~15m.
2) During fallback, several large batch embed jobs (NovaCommerce batch job id: batch-8721) retried on client side producing duplicate postbacks to billing service within the retry window.
3) Postbacks from the Hosted backend for the window arrived out-of-order to the reconciler due to a reroute of hourly-metering tags (ref: routing-change 2026-03-07T00:10).
4) Reconciler applied an hourly tag for the fallback and queued credits; due to out-of-order arrival the reserve credit allocation job skipped the affected hourly bucket and later applied a negative adjustment to a different window.
5) Invoice finalized before the reconciler corrected the allocation, leaving the charge present on the invoice and a subsequent negative line that does not map cleanly to the expected reserve credit.

Expected behavior:
- Reserve (hourly buffer) credits should be applied to the exact hourly bucket where fallback consumption occurred, even if postbacks arrive out of order.
- Finalized invoices should reflect the corrected credit or show a clear provisional credit line for reconciliation.

Actual behavior:
- Reserve credit was not applied to the affected hour; invoice shows billed amount and a later negative adjustment that does not offset the invoice due to memoing to a different finalized billline.

Logs / artifacts attached:
- Reconciler logs (filtered) snippet: "reconciler:skip-allocation: bucket=2026-03-07T00:00 reason=tag-mismatch incoming_tag=hosted-fallback-hourly routed_tag=dedicated-hourly"
- Billing postback traces: trace ids: pb-20260307-00455, pb-20260307-00523
- Customer batch job id: batch-8721 (NovaCommerce internal id)

Investigation notes (initial):
- Correlated reconciler logs with postback traces and routing audit: there was a configuration push (scheduler/routing) at 2026-03-07T00:09 that changed the hourly-tag mapping for fallback windows.
- The reconciler assumes monotonic postback ordering for hourly allocation when tags change within the window; out-of-order delivery causes the allocation job to drop the tag-matching step and move on, leaving credits unallocated.
- Hypothesis: a combination of client retries (duplicate postbacks) + tag change + finalization timing created a race where the credit allocator skipped the bucket.
- Early workaround applied: manual allocation of reserve credit to the affected hourly bucket and generated a corrective invoice adjustment (provisional credit issued while finance reviews).

Next steps:
- SRE/Payments to add a guard in the reconciler to hold finalization on impacted hour when tag mappings change within a 10m window or when duplicate postbacks are detected.
- Engineering to backfill missing allocations for affected customers and reconcile invoices for finalized windows within the month.
- Communicate to NovaCommerce the workaround and ETA for a corrective invoice.

Support - Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): Opened ticket after customer escalated to CS manager. Collected invoice pdf and customer batch job id. Requested billing traces and reconciler logs from Payments team.
Payments - Oliver Grant (2026-03-10): Retrieved postback traces and initial reconciler logs. Noted out-of-order postbacks and a scheduling change at 2026-03-07T00:09. Marking high priority due to finalized invoice and autopay hold.
Engineering - Marcus Chen (2026-03-11): Confirmed reconciler behavior: tag mapping changes within an hour can lead to allocation skips when combined with duplicate postbacks. Drafting a short-term reconciler patch to re-try allocation when a late postback matches an unallocated bucket.
Customer - Jane Miller (NovaCommerce) (2026-03-11): Customer accepts temporary manual credit but requests assurance final invoice will be corrected and that autopay will not be charged while investigation continues.

Issue summary:
Customer (NimbleHealth, dedicated) reports intermittent high time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for inference requests originating from APAC (ap-southeast-1). Symptoms appear as 500–1200ms additional TTFB on many requests; overall completion latency not always elevated because responses stream after initial delay.

Impact:
- Production traffic for NimbleHealth sees increased p50/p95 TTFB and degraded UX for chat product.
- Affects critical inference endpoints pinned to dedicated pool.
- No API-level 5xx surge observed, but increased client perceived latency causing support complaints.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (customer-owned pool) in ap-southeast-1 region, nodes backed by multizone GPU hosts.
- API nodes fronted by global edge routing and smart-routing policies that can route to us-west-2 fallback when local capacity is constrained.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send authenticated chat generation request pinned to NimbleHealth dedicated model rw-instruct-7b-v2 from a client in Singapore.
2) Observe TTFB via curl -w '%{time_starttransfer}
'.
3) Repeat 1000 requests over 10m window; elevated TTFB observed on ~12–18% of requests.

Observed signals and logs:
- Grafana trace gaps show initial connection and TLS handshake times normal; delay occurs after routing decision and before first token generation (time between router->serving-runtime connection and first token).
- Edge logs show a subset of requests were routed to us-west-2 despite origin being ap-southeast-1.
- BGP peering/aggr metrics show transient asymmetric egress on one of the ap-southeast-1 egress routers during the incident window.
- No quota/429s; no scale-up events triggered for dedicated pool during window.

03/10 09:12 - Initial triage by Support (Maya): customer-provided traces and curl timings indicate TTFB spikes.
03/10 10:05 - Eng oncall (Luis) pulled edge routing logs; saw ~15% sessions routed to us-west-2 via fallback policy.
03/10 11:30 - Network team ran BGP/peering checks: found flapping on ap-southeast-1 egress-router-2 causing some sessions to take a longer as-path to upstream peer.
03/10 12:20 - Hypothesis: transient egress path asymmetry caused the smart-routing decision to prefer fallback region for a subset of requests, adding inter-region latency. Corroborated by flow logs showing routing hops crossing to us-west-2.
03/11 02:45 - Verified dedicated pool capacity normal; no autoscale anomalies.
03/11 08:10 - Replayed traffic from a synthetic agent in SG and observed occasional reroutes when egress-router-2 reported high prepkt-loss.
03/12 14:00 - Network vendor applied control-plane fix for egress-router-2; flapping cleared.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 15:10 - Customer (NimbleHealth - Alex Rivera): Acknowledged reduction in spikes; requested confirmation that no config change required on their side and asked for postmortem when incident closed.
Mitigation applied: constrained smart-routing policy for NimbleHealth to prefer ap-southeast-1 egress until network flapping fully resolved (temporary routing override). Network vendor fixed BGP peer causing egress-router-2 flapping.
Root cause: transient instability on a regional egress router (ap-southeast-1) caused asymmetric/longer egress paths; smart-routing fallback logic routed a minority of sessions to us-west-2 which added ~600–1200ms TTFB.
Workaround: Applied customer-scoped routing bias to prefer local egress and avoid fallback for short windows; advised customer to retry transient failures with backoff.

1) Keep temporary routing override in place for 48h of stable telemetry.

4) Re-evaluate smart-routing fallback thresholds to avoid cross-region routing for short-lived egress instabilities.

Issue summary:
Customer's private deploy is failing to download model artifact bundles intermittently. Failures cluster during periods of high parallel artifact fetches and show TLS/mTLS authentication errors from our control plane to the artifact host.

Impact:
- FinSigna production inference jobs intermittently fail to load new model bundles; customers see 5-10% increased model-load latency and a small fraction of requests fail with 401/403 during rollout windows.
- Affects private (VPC) deployment only; hosted customers not impacted.

Environment:
- Private deployment in customer VPC, prod-us-east (us-east-1).
- Egress path forced through corporate inline TLS-inspecting proxy that performs certificate rewriting/inspection.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Trigger parallel model rollout that causes 8 concurrent artifact fetches per serving node.
2) Observe artifact fetch logs (control-plane/artifact-fetcher) and TLS negotiation.
3) Failures observed ~30-60s after start of parallel downloads.

Observed behavior:
- Control-plane logs show TLS handshake succeeded but mTLS verification fails at application layer: "client certificate chain incomplete" or "unexpected certificate subject" depending on request.
- Artifact host returns 401 or 403 for the failed fetches.
- Packet captures show the CLIENTHELLO -> PROXY -> UPSTREAM sequence; proxy advertises ALPN and performs active inspection.

Expected behavior:
- mTLS handshake should preserve the full client certificate chain and proof-of-possession so upstream accepts requests.

Initial hypothesis:
- The customer's inline proxy is performing TLS interception but truncating part of the client certificate chain or not forwarding the client cert in the upstream mTLS session when connections are multiplexed/HTTP/2 is used. The failure rate increases with concurrency, suggesting a race or connection-reuse edge case in the proxy code.
2026-03-01 tcpdump summary from customer: multiple concurrent TLS sessions appear, but upstream server reports 'certificate verify failed: incomplete chain' in app logs.
Checked artifact-fetcher logs: repeated entries 'upstream mTLS verify failed: presenting incomplete client cert chain' correlated with high parallelism windows.
Replicated in lab by deploying SecureGate inline (vendor-supplied VM image) and routing egress through it; when client reuses muxed HTTP/2 stream, proxy establishes upstream TLS separately and fails to attach full client cert chain in 1 of 8 parallel streams.
OpenSSL s_client test: when proxy in-path, s_client -status -alpn h2 -cert client.pem -key client.key -> upstream returns 'verify return code: 21 (unable to verify the first certificate)' intermittently depending on timing.
Wireshark TLS record inspection shows proxy sending an upstream ClientCertASN1 but missing the intermediate cert in the chain; the downstream (from client to proxy) contains full chain.
Hypothesis: proxy's mTLS passthrough code incorrectly reuses a cached upstream connection which was established without client cert state, then attempts to inject client cert at application layer but loses intermediate CA. Race occurs under high concurrency when proxy opens fresh upstream connections asynchronously.
Related internal reference: INT-8472 (egress-proxy connection-reuse investigation).

Additional notes:
2026-03-01 FinSigna (Customer): Attached tcpdump from node showing SYN, TLS CLIENTHELLO and a subsequent application-level 401 from artifact host. Customer notes proxy vendor: SecureGate 4.2.1 inline appliance.
2026-03-03 FinSigna: Confirmed workaround (disable HTTP/2 multiplexing on egress) reduces failure rate to near zero for their rollout tests.
2026-03-04 Engineering (egress-proxy): Created a small test PR to force fresh upstream connections per client cert; waiting review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/egress-proxy/pull/238
Workaround applied: Customer disabled HTTP/2 connection multiplexing on their egress proxy policy and configured the egress appliance to open dedicated upstream connections per downstream mTLS session. This reduced failures to <0.3% during rollouts.
Permanent fix plan: Engineering to land egress-proxy PR that avoids reusing upstream TLS sessions for connections that require client-certificate propagation and to add a code path ensuring full client certificate chain is forwarded when interception mode is enabled. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/egress-proxy/pull/238 (under review).
Follow-ups:
- Coordinate with customer to test staged rollout of proxy fix next week in a controlled window.
- Add monitoring alert for 'artifact-fetch mTLS verification failure rate' and a knowledge-base article describing recommended egress proxy configs for mTLS-preserving inspection appliances.
Status: Engineering patch pending review; in-contact with SecureGate support to get appliance firmware that properly preserves client certificate chain in interception mode.
payload.summary: Intercepting egress proxy truncates client cert chain during mTLS to artifact host causing intermittent artifact fetch auth failures

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses at the API gateway beginning ~2026-03-10 09:40 UTC for an affected dedicated tenant (BrightForms Inc.). Errors correlate with a large number of client-side stream cancellations/aborts (long-polling webhook flows).

Impact:
- ~12% 5xx error rate on tenant's streaming route over a 35m window, impacting live inference features for BrightForms (multiple customers report failures).
- Latency tail increased (p95→p99) and token throughput reduced for the tenant's dedicated pool.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC: Traffic spike starts from BrightForms long-poll clients (sustained connection churn and frequent client-initiated ABORTs).
- 09:40 UTC: API gateway begins returning 502/503s for streaming routes.
- 09:45 UTC: Alert fired (5xx rate > threshold).
- 09:50–10:10 UTC: Support engaged, routed to SRE and runtime team.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east dedicated pool for BrightForms.
- Serving runtime: release 1.18.2 (event-loop + blocking threadpool for model IO).
- API gateway: envoy proxy mesh with HTTP/2 streaming.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Client establishes long-lived HTTP/2 streaming session and issues prompt.
2) Client rapidly sends aborts/finishes (CANCEL frames) in tight loops (multiple concurrent sockets per client).
3) Runtime receives cancellations and schedules cleanup tasks that perform KV-cache unlocks, GIL-adjacent teardown, and metrics flushes on a shared blocking threadpool.
4) Threadpool becomes saturated; new request handoff to blocking workers is queued and stalls the runtime event loop, causing request timeouts and upstream 5xx to API gateway.

Observed behavior:
- High number of CANCEL frames recorded per second for the tenant.
- Worker thread pool depth near capacity; queue length grows.
- Runtime logs show extended cleanup task durations (10–20s) under the abort pattern.
- API gateway surfaces 502/503 to callers when upstream runtimes are slow or unresponsive.

Expected behavior:
- Graceful and fast cancellation handling without blocking the main request path; cancellations should be processed with bounded CPU and not occupy blocking threads for long periods.

Additional notes:
- This looks distinct from prior NVMe/gpu OOM/customer-prefetch issues; root cause appears tied to cancellation handling and cleanup semantics under high abort frequency.

[2026-03-10T09:41:12Z] envoy: upstream reset before response (client: 10.240.3.18, path: /v1/stream)
[2026-03-10T09:41:13Z] runtime[tid=1402]: received CANCEL frame for session=bf-usr-224, scheduling cleanup on blocking-pool (task id=67341)
[2026-03-10T09:41:14Z] blocking-pool: task 67341 started (kv-unlock, metric-flush); estimated duration 14.3s
[2026-03-10T09:41:26Z] runtime[warning]: blocking-pool queue length=98, active=32, max=32
[2026-03-10T09:42:00Z] api-gateway: returning 502 upstream_timeout for tenant=brightforms route=/v1/stream
Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-10 09:48 UTC: Customer reports intermittent failures on live preview — errors start coinciding with a client rollout at 09:30. Asking for traffic window and sample client user-agent headers.
Customer (BrightForms) 2026-03-10 09:51 UTC: Sending logs and client patterns — new mobile SDK pushes a reconnect loop that cancels previous requests aggressively. Will provide SDK version and repro rate.
SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-03-10 10:01 UTC: Observed threadpool saturation for tenant. Hypothesis: cancellation handler performs heavy synchronous work on blocking threadpool. Recommending immediate mitigation: enable temporary rate-limit on concurrent streaming sessions for tenant and increase threadpool size to relieve backlog.
Runtime Eng (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10 10:12 UTC: Confirmed cleanup tasks include disk-backed metric flush and KV unlock which are blocking. Propose patch to offload metric flush to async queue and convert KV unlock to lock-free path. Will open a PR for safe rollout.
SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC: Mitigation applied: tenant concurrent streaming cap reduced to 60 connections; threadpool temporary scaled +50%. 5xx rate reduced to baseline within 20 minutes.
Correlation observed between client abort rate and blocking-pool queue length (Pearson r=0.82 over 30m window).
Heap and GPU stats show no memory fragmentation or driver resets; NVIDIA metrics within normal bounds for pool. Not a GPU OOM issue.
Tracing shows synchronous calls in cancellation path that touch disk (metric flush) and lock global kv-shard. These operations previously assumed low-frequency cancel events.
Prioritized repro harness created using a simulated SDK abort loop (100 clients, each issuing cancel 2–5s after request start). Reproduces blocking-pool queueing and upstream 502s within ~3 minutes.
Lock profiling indicates kv-shard lock hold time spikes to 12–18ms in the cancel path, multiplied by cancel rate causing pile-up.
Applied per-tenant concurrent streaming cap (60) and increased blocking threadpool capacity temporarily. Recommended customer to roll back mobile SDK aggressive reconnect until runtime patch is deployed.
Short-term: merge PR to make metric flush asynchronous and relax KV lock scope (github.com/redwood/realtime-runtime/pull/412). Patch scheduled for canary 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC. Long-term: implement cancellable cleanup tokenization to bound work per cancellation and add server-side abort-rate circuit that sheds excessive aborting clients.
Canary rollout started 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC; monitored tenant had 5xx drop from 12% → 1.8% within 10 minutes. No regressions observed in other tenants during canary. Full rollout planned 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC after 4h successful canary.
ENG-1692: implement cancellation backpressure circuit (owner: Maya Chen)
OPS-881: add exporter metric for cancel-frame-rate per-tenant and alert on sustained >100 cancel/s (owner: Diego Morales)
DOCS-43: guidance for customers on safe reconnect/abort patterns in mobile SDK (owner: Developer Experience)
SEC-22: review that async metric flush does not expose PII in transit (owner: Security)
SRE-504: evaluate default threadpool sizing heuristic for dedicated pools under high abort-rate workloads

payload.description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart reports repeated 429 throttles when performing parallel multipart dataset uploads to a dedicated ingest endpoint. The uploads are chunked into ~5MB parts and the customer runs 12 parallel workers. Throttles appear after 90-120 seconds into the job despite aggregate token rates remaining under their committed capacity.

Impact:
- Customer upload jobs fail with intermittent 429s, slowing onboarding of a large dataset (~4TB).
- Higher than expected invoiceable errors and engineering time spent retrying uploads.
- Risk of backoff-induced cascading retries hitting other tenants on the dedicated pool.

Environment:
- BrightCart dedicated pool in us-east-1
- Node pool tagged: dedicated-brightcart-1
- API path: POST /v1/uploads/multipart/start and chunked PUT to /v1/uploads/multipart/part
- Customer SDK: redwood-uploader v1.8.3 (Python)

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1. Start 12 parallel workers initiating multipart uploads for 4GB files split into 5MB parts.
2. Each worker streams parts sequentially with no inter-part delay.
3. After ~100s, some workers begin receiving 429 responses on part PUTs.
4. Exponential backoff triggers retries; retries also receive 429s or 504 occasionally.

Observed logs / evidence provided:
- Customer provided sample request/response headers with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset showing small windows.
- Gateway trace: multiple connections from same API key hitting different edge hosts; health probe logs show burst of small requests preceding the 429 onset.
- Ingest-worker logs: spike in concurrent open connections to backend serving runtime at time of throttle.
- Billing logs show token usage below their committed monthly rate at time of incidents.

Initial hypothesis:
- There is a mismatch between per-connection accounting (per-connection token bucket) and per-api-key token usage for chunked uploads, causing the gateway to attribute bursts to connection windows rather than aggregate tenant quota.
- Health-check or small metadata requests could be incrementing short-window counters and nudging the token bucket to exhaustion for the connection window used by the upload workers.
- HTTP/2 connection multiplexing across workers might produce per-connection accounting drift vs per-worker expectations.

Investigation notes:
- Support reproduced a reduced-case locally with uploader v1.8.3 by running 6 parallel workers and saw 429s on part PUTs after sustained parallelism; reproduced only when using HTTP/2 multiplexing.
- Packet captures show many small HEAD/OPTIONS probes from edge to origin (likely from cloud load-balancer health checks) interleaved with part PUTs.
- Rate-limiter logs (edge) show per-connection token windows being consumed faster than per-key smoothing would indicate.
- A quick experiment disabling connection-level short-window accounting on a staging route removed the early 429s but opened a risk of local spike amplification; this was tested briefly under low-traffic conditions.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Reduce parallel worker concurrency to 6 and add 100ms jitter between part PUTs per worker.
- Use chunk sizes of 8-10MB to reduce number of separate PUT requests.
- Optionally route uploads through a single long-lived HTTP/1.1 connection to avoid HTTP/2 per-stream accounting anomalies.

Next steps (internal):
- SRE: correlate rate-limiter per-connection vs per-key accounting across dedicated-brightcart-1 for the incident window (logs: /prod/edge/rate-limiter/2026/03/01).
- Infra: check load-balancer health probe frequency and origin probe routing for the pool; adjust probe header behavior if probes increment short-window counters.
- Eng (rate-limiter): evaluate move to smoothing tokens across connection windows for multipart endpoints or provide an explicit per-route exemption for chunked-upload semantics.
- Product: discuss a recommended upload pattern doc for dedicated customers (single connection vs parallel workers guidance).

Acceptance criteria for resolution:
- BrightCart is no longer receiving 429s under the original parallel job pattern (with agreed limits), or a documented config + SDK change is published.
- No regression in protection against abusive spikes for shared dedicated pools.

Resolution notes: (to be filled on close)

Additional notes:
2026-03-03 11:02 - Support (Aisha): Provided customer workaround (reduce concurrency, increase chunk size). Customer acknowledged and will test reduced concurrency today. Asked for ETA on permanent fix.
payload.summary: Assess throttle accounting mismatch during parallel chunked uploads

Issue summary: Customer BrightCourt AI reports that a promotional buffer (USD 2,500 trial credit) was exhausted during a Dedicated->Private migration window. They believe the credits were consumed by automated ephemeral 'healthcheck' invocations from a CI runner that had been re-bound to their org during migration cutover. Impact: Customer now shows a provisional negative balance on their invoice and is blocked from completing the final migration billing reconciliation. Environment: Dedicated cluster (dedicated-gpu-pool-7) transitioning to Private deployment (private-vpc-12) between 2026-03-05 23:45 and 2026-03-06 01:20 UTC. Steps to reproduce / observed sequence: 1) Customer initiated migration; infra automation re-registered some ephemeral CI keys under customer org to validate private endpoint. 2) At cutover a burst of 10k short-lived requests (healthcheck/tool-invoke) hit the hosted fallback and were recorded by the postback-processor. 3) Metering records show these as tool-invoke and warmup tokens attributed to the org's primary cost center. 4) Promotional buffer credits appear to be applied (and then reversed) in short order leaving a net negative provisional balance. Logs / evidence: - Customer provided org-usage-export CSV rows (attached) showing ~10,120 short requests between 2026-03-06T00:00:05Z and 2026-03-06T00:04:20Z. - Postback ID samples: pb_8a3f2c, pb_8a4031, pb_8a40d5 (timestamps included). - Console estimate before finalization: $0 due to buffer. Finalized provisional balance: -$1,374.45. Request: Please audit attribution for the burst, confirm whether ephemeral keys should have consumed the promo buffer, and provide a provisional credit or reversal while we investigate. Customer has asked for a timeline for reversal before final invoice is issued.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Support (Miguel Torres): Acknowledged receipt. Escalating to Metering and Billing for urgent audit. Assigned to SRE on-call for the migration window pinning.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
CypressLedger reported multiple customer sessions receiving out-of-order chunks in streaming completions and, in some cases, responses from other concurrent sessions being interleaved into their stream. This affected business-critical flows (transaction confirmation messages) and triggered a billing spike due to duplicate token accounting.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: intermittent out-of-order or mixed completions for ~2 hours impacting ~120 active sessions for CypressLedger (private deployment).
- Platform: temporary surge in billed tokens for the customer (~+18% above baseline during the incident window).
- Business: customer escalated to account team; potential compliance risk for ordered transaction confirmations.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) managed by Redwood control plane, dedicated serving pool for CypressLedger with autoscaling enabled.
- Regions: primary us-east cluster (serving), cross-region failover to eu-west observed but no failover executed.

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1) Customer uses the streaming completions endpoint with multiplexed user sessions over HTTP/2 keep-alive connections and session affinity enabled.
2) Issue reliably reproduced by concurrently opening ~50 client sessions and sending short prompts that produce 3–6 chunked responses per session.
3) Under concurrent load + autoscale event, some streams produced chunks interleaved from other sessions or reordered sequence IDs.

Observed logs/snippets:
- streaming-proxy logs showed reused connection IDs with concurrent stream IDs: "conn=0x7f43 stream=42 -> session_id=usr-99" then "conn=0x7f43 stream=42 -> session_id=usr-14" within same keep-alive window.
- serving-runtime traces show KV cache eviction events correlated with scale-out events: "kv-prefix-evict key=usr-14 seq=0-23" immediately before an inbound request resumed with stale prefix mapping.
- billing tallyer emitted duplicate token increments for some request IDs during period 14:12–16:30 UTC.

Customer communication template used:
- Initial acknowledgement within 15m: "We are investigating an elevated rate of streaming ordering anomalies affecting some private deployments; your account team will follow up with a targeted timeline and mitigations."
- Follow-up: request for root cause and remediation plan; offered immediate mitigation steps and a provisional billing adjustment while we investigate.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:22 - Eng-PR#7621 (Automated): Merged fix that serializes prefix mapping updates during worker handoff and adds a unit test for stream demux concurrency.
2026-03-11 12:10 - Support (Sofia Alvarez): Shared post-incident summary and offered a billing adjustment of 18% token-credit for the incident window pending finance approval.
2026-03-12 10:00 - Customer (CypressLedger - Naomi Ito): Confirmed mitigation observed and accepted the proposed credit; requested long-term safeguards and a canary schedule for the fix. Asked for updated runbook.
Timeline and root cause summary:
- 14:05 UTC: First customer reports of interleaved streaming chunks.
- 14:10–14:30 UTC: Repro harness confirms issue under high concurrency + scale-out.
- Root cause: race condition between streaming-proxy connection reuse and serving-runtime's KV prefix remapping during worker handoff. When the autoscaler started a new worker and the connection was reassigned, an active HTTP/2 multiplexed stream could be incorrectly demultiplexed to a different session ID because the prefix->kv handle update was not atomic with respect to stream demux table updates. This resulted in chunks being pulled from the wrong KV shard or sequence, producing out-of-order/interleaved responses.
- Secondary effect: duplicate token accounting in billing tallyer for requests where demux/reset events triggered re-processing of portions of a response stream.
- Contributing factors: private pools with aggressive autoscaler policies, HTTP/2 keep-alive reuse optimization that prioritized connection reuse over strict session isolation, and missing transactional semantics around prefix mapping in the runtime.
- Evidence: correlated timestamps across streaming-proxy, serving-runtime, and billing-tallyer logs; repro on staging with identical autoscale parameters.
Immediate mitigations:
1) Disabled HTTP/2 connection reuse for CypressLedger pool (prevents stream remapping across sessions).
2) Pinned autoscaler to avoid rapid worker turnover while we deployed fixes.
3) Temporarily routed traffic to a single stable kernel selection and disabled in-flight kernel swaps for the affected pool.
Permanent fixes deployed:
1) PR #7621: add atomic prefix mapping updates and serialization around stream demux changes.
2) Added an integration test that simulates concurrent stream demux and autoscaler worker handoff.
3) Billing tallyer dedup logic hardened to ignore replayed chunk accounting events when a stream reset is observed.
- Fix merged and canaried to internal staging on 2026-03-11; monitored for 24h with no reproductions.
- Full rollout to affected clusters completed 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC.
- Billing credit: provisional 18% token credit issued pending finance sign-off; customer notified.
- Compliance: traces retained 90 days and shared under NDA.
ENG-1452: Add end-to-end ephemeral session isolation test for HTTP/2 multiplexing scenarios (owner: Maya Chen, due: 2026-03-20)
SRE-781: Update autoscaler default policy for private pools to include a minimum drain/handshake delay of 120s (owner: Ravi Patel, due: 2026-03-18)
DOC-99: Update streaming runbook to include immediate mitigation steps for ordering anomalies and customer communication templates (owner: Sofia Alvarez, due: 2026-03-16)
OPS-410: Add billing tallyer dedup acceptance tests and audit export for customer credit windows (owner: Priya Rao, due: 2026-03-22)
SEC-57: Review compliance evidence handling for interleaved-response incidents and update retention/access controls (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-03-25)
We issued a formal incident summary to CypressLedger on 2026-03-11 with technical root cause, mitigation steps taken, a proposed 18% token credit for the affected window, and a timeline for the permanent fixes. Customer acknowledged and requested canary schedule; they will remain on a monitored routing profile during the canary rollout.
