payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports SSE streaming sessions that briefly stall during a CDN idle-probe window and then reconnect. After reconnect, the client sees a duplicated short token sequence followed by the final choice missing the last grapheme (cut mid-codepoint).

Impact:
- A subset of streaming responses (approx 3-4% for this customer during peak) show a short duplicate token sequence immediately before the final chunk, and the final output sometimes ends with an incomplete grapheme/byte (rendered as replacement char in some clients).
- Affects user-visible messages in ByteForge's chat integration; user experience degraded. No full crashes but increased support tickets.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east-1) behind CloudFront + internal streaming proxy + nginx h2 edge in customer's infra. Customer on self-serve account using Redwood hosted API.

Observed behavior:
- Client connects via SSE. After ~15-45s of idle, CloudFront issues an idle probe and the connection briefly enters a probe/half-close. The client receives a short duplicate sequence (e.g., "...ing. ing.") then final choice truncated (last Unicode grapheme missing).

Expected behavior:
- Streaming should either resume with exactly the remaining tokens (no duplication) or the server should send a clean terminal event with full Unicode boundary preserved. No partial grapheme or duplicated tokens should be observable to the client.

Note: customer provided packet capture and Application logs; see attached log excerpts below for timestamps and example event payloads.
1) Use a client that connects to /v1/stream with SSE and long-lived idle (~30s) between tokens.
2) Route traffic through CloudFront (default keepalive/idle-probe behavior).
3) Issue a generation with a relatively long final sentence (ensures streaming tail).
4) Wait for CloudFront idle probe or artificially lower keepalive to trigger probe, observe reconnect sequence and final tokens delivered to client.
5) Repeat 50-200 times to reproduce at low probability; customer saw ~3% occurrence under their traffic pattern.
2026-03-09T18:22:11.342Z - SSE event: data: {"choice":"...continu"}

2026-03-09T18:22:12.117Z - CloudFront: connection idle probe sent, upstream half-close detected
2026-03-09T18:22:12.118Z - proxy: observed FIN_WAIT -> new socket attempt; resuming session token=abc123
2026-03-09T18:22:12.120Z - SSE event: data: {"choice":"uation. u"}

2026-03-09T18:22:12.121Z - SSE event: data: {"choice":"ation."}

Client-side rendered output: "...continuation. uation." (duplicate sequence)

Later client render: final character replaced with U+FFFD (incomplete UTF-8 sequence)

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - Customer (ByteForge): Provided sample request IDs: r-20260309-1872, r-20260309-1899 and confirmed CloudFront default idle timeout (60s) but they have additional nginx-h2 edge with keepalive 20s.
Hypothesis 1: CloudFront idle probe causes upstream half-close; our streaming-proxy tries to reattach session and retransmit in-flight buffer leading to duplicate short sequence.
Hypothesis 2: The proxy/chunking path is splitting on raw bytes without ensuring UTF-8 grapheme boundaries; when retransmit collides with a split boundary, client displays replacement char (U+FFFD).
Evidence: pcap shows FIN/ACK from CloudFront then immediate new connection; server-side logs show re-queued chunk with same sequence id. Reproducer in staging shows duplication probability increases when keepalive shorter (20s).
Telemetry: token-level trace shows last two mini-chunks re-emitted with same sequence id in duplicated cases (trace r-20260309-1872).
Mitigations tested: a) Server-side dedupe on sequence-id prevented visible duplicate but left partial UTF-8 artifact in one run. b) Buffering to align on UTF-8 codepoint boundaries eliminated replacement char but introduced ~6-12ms tail latency in staging.
Workaround applied: Enabled UTF-8-safe chunk alignment in streaming-proxy for ByteForge account (feature-flagged) and added a short dedupe window (idempotency of last-in-flight chunk) to suppress immediate duplicate emission. Customer opted for UTF-8-safe alignment + dedupe. Post-change telemetry (24h) shows duplication reduced to <0.1% and no replacement-char events observed.
Planned permanent fix: 1) upstream: make chunking component UTF-8 grapheme-aware by default to avoid splitting multi-byte codepoints; 2) add idempotent resume handshake to prevent retransmit of already acknowledged chunk sequence; 3) update streaming runbook to include CDN keepalive guidance and a diagnostic flag to surface half-close events.
Follow-ups: Create INT task to roll UTF-8-safe chunking to all customers behind a gradual rollout (INT-3301). Add a dashboard alert for half-close retransmit rate exceeding 0.5% per customer.
1) Enable account-scoped feature flag: 'utf8-aligned-chunking' (internal flag name: ff/utf8_chunk_align).
2) Enable request-scoped dedupe window: temporarily ignore retransmit of a sequence id within 250ms of original emission.
3) Recommend customer to set CloudFront idle timeout >= 120s or align nginx keepalive > CloudFront probe interval while we roll fix.
payload.summary: Partial final choice & duplicate tokens observed after CDN idle probe during streaming reconnect

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer enabled two optimization changes in their Dedicated cluster: 1) kv_prefetch=true (prefix/KV warm-up across shards) and 2) quant_profile=aggressive_int4. They also increased preferred_batch_size to 256 in the route config. After deploy, NovaDocs observed intermittent token corruption (garbled tokens mid-stream), elevated P95/P99 token latency and a small number of 5xx stream terminations for long-context prompts (>= 8k).

Impact:
- Production inference degraded for ~3% of requests to the affected route; affects user-facing document generation workflows.
- Elevated tail latency (P95 up from 120ms to 470ms) and sporadic 5xx stream drop.
- Business impact: some time-sensitive document renders missing tokens; customer requested guidance and an emergency safe rollback.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster (customer-managed reservation) in us-west-2
- Model: redwood/llama-2-70b-rwkv-compat, seq_len typical 8192 for large prompts
- Route config: preferred_batch_size: 256, kv_prefetch: true, quant_profile: aggressive_int4
- Observability: Redwood Console + Kibana; customer forwarded example request IDs

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Send multi-turn prompt with ~6k tokens and pinned system prompt.
2) Stream generation with default chunk_size; after ~200 tokens, stream returns garbled tokens or sudden 5xx.
3) Reproduce probability increases with concurrent load ~80 RPS.

Relevant logs/snippets provided by customer:
- Kibana trace: trace_id=trc-88d3; shows KV cache read time spikes at cache-miss bursts and CPU-bound worker queueing.
- Runtime error sample: "kv_cache_fetch: shard 3 timeout after 120ms" followed by "tokenize: unexpected codepoint sequence"
- Console metrics: request_inflight rose 40% and batching latency increased during peak.

Investigation notes (support/SRE):
- Hypothesis 1: aggressive int4 quant profile reduces numeric headroom and with KV prefetch introduces alignment constraints causing subtle decoding differences under heavy batch packing.
- Hypothesis 2: kv_prefetch pre-warms cross-shard KV which increases instantaneous memory pressure and evictions leading to cache-miss storms and queueing at the serving-runtime layer.
- Hypothesis 3: very large preferred_batch_size combined with quantized kernels pushed some operators into slower fallback code paths under long-sequence workloads.

Actions taken so far:
- Collected heap/disk metrics and GPU memory timelines for the timeframe provided. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3872 for a minor telemetry enhancement we applied to the customer's dedicated control plane to surface per-shard prefetch latencies.
- Scoped the issue to routes with kv_prefetch=true + preferred_batch_size >= 200 + quant_profile=aggressive_int4. Routes without this combination have not shown corruption.
- Applied a temporary traffic-split to route 10% of production to a variant with quant_profile=balanced_int8 to measure delta in a small canary. Canary showed no token corruption and P95 returned to ~140ms.

Immediate recommended safe rollback (step-by-step):
1) Set route-level preferred_batch_size to 64 (non-disruptive): API call example: PATCH /routes/{id} {"preferred_batch_size": 64}. Wait 5–10 minutes and monitor P95/P99.
2) If corruption persists, disable kv_prefetch: PATCH /routes/{id} {"kv_prefetch": false}. This is safe and reversible; it will increase cold-start token latency slightly but eliminates prefetch-induced memory pressure.
3) If corruption still observed, revert quant profile to a conservative profile: PATCH /models/{model_id}/config {"quant_profile": "balanced_int8"}. NOTE: quant_profile change may require warmup; perform for a canary first.
4) If immediate rollback required and above steps not feasible, perform a route pin to a known-good model variant: POST /routes/{id}/pin {"model_version": "rev-2026-02-18-stable"}.

Validation checklist after rollback (what to monitor):
- Token correctness on previously affected request IDs (customer-provided samples).
- P95 and P99 token latency trends return to baseline within 30 minutes.
- No new 5xx stream terminations in logs for the route for 2h.
- GPU memory/disk swap metrics stable; no sustained cache-miss storms.

Workarounds (if customer cannot change config immediately):
- Decrease concurrent inflight requests via client-side rate limiting (e.g., limit to 50 RPS for the route).
- Reduce requested sequence length or split long prompts into shorter passes where possible.

Follow-up items and engineering recommendations:
- Engineering will add a guard in the optimizer that disallows pairing kv_prefetch=true with preferred_batch_size >= 200 for aggressive_int4 quant profiles without an explicit opt-in flag.
- Add a runtime check that logs and surfaces "kv_prefetch contention" and recommendations when memory pressure spikes are detected. See linked PR for telemetry.
- Consider adding an automatic canary gate that refuses to rollout aggressive quant profiles to dedicated clusters with long-seq heavy workloads.

Resolution notes (partial):
- We recommended the customer reduce preferred_batch_size to 64 and disable kv_prefetch in a controlled window. Customer applied step 1 and is monitoring. Canary to balanced_int8 was scheduled.
- No customer-facing patch deployed by Redwood yet; must coordinate for quant_profile change.

Requests from customer:
- Clear, minimal rollback steps and expected customer-visible impact (provided above).
- Confirmation that disabling kv_prefetch is safe for dedicated and reversible. (Confirmed by SRE: reversible and safe.)

Next steps:
- Support to wait for customer's confirmation after they apply step 1 (preferred_batch_size reduction).
- If customer wants Redwood to perform the kv_prefetch toggle and quant_profile canary, schedule a maintenance window and coordinate with their on-call.

Attachments: request IDs and log snippets provided by customer (attached to ticket).

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 11:45 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Collected telemetry and confirmed correlation between kv_prefetch + preferred_batch_size >=200 + aggressive_int4. Recommended staged rollback plan; asked customer to reduce batch size as first step.
2026-03-13 13:02 - Customer (NovaDocs On-call, Maria Alvarez): Applied batch size change to 64. Monitoring now. Asked whether disabling kv_prefetch will impact throughput expectations.
2026-03-14 08:30 - Support (Aisha Khan): Follow-up to ensure canary to balanced_int8 is scheduled. Created linked engineering ticket for optimizer guard (INT-4129).
payload.summary: KV-prefetch + aggressive quant profile causing intermittent token errors and elevated tail latency; guidance for safe unwind

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated throughput drops and transient 5xxs from their dedicated pool during midday usage window. Behavior started 2026-03-10 ~13:05 UTC and recurred in short waves.

Impact: DataSilo Analytics observed increased P50/P95/P99 latencies for generation routes and a spike in inference failures (5xx/ALLOC_TIMEOUT) for ~10-30 minute bursts. Traffic is primarily short streaming requests (~50-200 tokens) which correlate with the incidents. Customer is on a dedicated pool with reserved capacity and reports this is impacting production job SLAs.

Environment: prod us-east-1, dedicated pool ID ds-4a7c, model gpt-large-v1 pinned. Autoscaler configured with min_replicas=2, target_utilization=0.7.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Send concurrent short streaming requests (mix of 10-50 concurrent clients, 1-2 requests/sec each) to the pinned route for ~10 minutes.
2) Observe intermittent 5xxs and rising p99 latency; GPU attach failures in client logs.

Observed logs/metrics:
- allocator.attach_latency.p50/p95 spikes at same time window (dashboard link in comments).
- autoscaler shows no new replica launches during first 2 waves; subsequent waves triggered scale-up but after >90s.
- node exporter shows bursty PCIe and NVLink io wait on a subset of nodes (node-3x and node-7y).
- Serving runtime logs show ALLOC_TIMEOUT and PREFETCH_LOCK warnings.

Initial hypothesis: A 'shadow surge' of many short streams causes fragmentation in allocator slot assignments (slow-leak of slots), prefetch/kv-cache churn, and transient attach timeouts. The autoscaler did not prevent transient shortages because scale-in policy allowed aggressive shrink during off-peak and burst detection latency prevented timely scale-up. No single hardware failure identified; pattern resembles noisy-tenant interference with allocator slow-paths.

Immediate impact mitigation requested: customer asked for rapid action to stop 5xxs and reduce latency spikes. They prefer a short-lived mitigation rather than rolling traffic to another region.

Requested next steps:
- SRE: temporarily increase min_replicas for ds-4a7c pool and pin allocation affinity to reduce slot fragmentation.
- Support: enable debug-level allocator logs for the pool for 2 hours and collect attach/evict traces.
- Eng: evaluate prefetch lease behavior and scale-in thresholds for short-stream workloads.

Attachments: customer logs (uploaded), support traces, dashboard timeseries links (see comments).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:35 UTC - Customer (DataSilo): Confirmed bursts are repeatable on their workload pattern and provided sample client logs showing ALLOC_TIMEOUT errors.
2026-03-10 15:10 UTC - Customer: Accepted temporary isolation; requested monitoring and no service restarts during peak window.
Allocator trace: spike in slot rebinds and a small number of stuck leases (~1-3 per node) that recovered after 60-120s.
Autoscaler: scale-in had pruned pool to 2 replicas ~30 minutes before midday surge; decider delay + provisioning latency meant first scale-up attempt was late relative to surge onset.
Node metrics: node-3x and node-7y show PCIe latency and brief NVLink thrash correlated to attach latency peaks; could be co-tenant IO bursts.
Serving runtime: PREFETCH_LOCK logs precede ALLOC_TIMEOUT by ~6-12s in most traces — suggests prefetch eviction/locking interplay with allocator slow-paths.
Customer-side: client traces show many short-lived connections (stream open -> complete in <2s) which encourages slot churn and small-batch inefficiencies.
Short-term mitigation applied 2026-03-10: increased pool min_replicas to 4 during peak window, applied temporary affinity to isolate noisy burst streams to a separate pool, enabled debug allocator logs and collected traces. Impact: immediate reduction in 5xxs and ~40% p99 improvement.
Long-term actions: follow-up engineering ticket to add burst-detection delay to scale-in, adjust prefetch lease eviction policy for short-stream workloads, and improve allocator slot compaction to avoid slow-leak. Postmortem meeting scheduled 2026-03-17.
Status: Customer satisfied with immediate mitigation; changes to runtime scheduled under ENG prioritization.

Issue summary:
Customer reported a pattern of elevated tail latency and some 503 responses for long-running streaming completions. The symptoms show requests accepted by the API gateway but no bytes forwarded to the backend for up to 25s, then a late flush occurs and either a 503 or full completion is returned with a large TTFB. This started after a routing change deployed 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC affecting the dedicated pool for us-west.

Impact:
- Intermittent but reproducible for a subset of customer traffic (ClipperHealth dedicated pool).
- Observed for streaming completions > 8k tokens and for requests that include large client-side trace headers (~>12KB).
- Customer reports user-facing timeouts and degraded UX during peak hours; estimated ~3% of streamed requests in the last 24h.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted: Dedicated capacity for ClippeHealth (us-west).
- APIGW version: apigw-2.6.1 (deployed 2026-03-11).
- Realtime proxy: realtime-proxy-1.3.4.

Observed behavior:
1) Client completes request upload (chunked) and waits for a streaming response.
2) APIGW accepts request, downstream connection to proxy shows no upstream write for 12–25s.
3) APIGW then issues a flush/coalesce write that sends a large header blob; backend interprets as end-of-headers and responds with 503 or occasionally completes but with large TTFB.

Expected behavior:
- APIGW should stream request body to backend as chunks arrive, and not buffer header/metadata beyond configured thresholds. No mid-stream idle should be introduced for healthy streaming completions.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Use ClippeHealth account on dedicated pool in us-west.
2) Send a streaming completion with ~10k token expected output and include x-trace-cookie with several hops (~>12KB header).
3) Observe TTFB and watch APIGW->proxy traces for delayed writes.

Quick logs / traces:
- apigw access (tail): 
  2026-03-12T08:21:44Z GET /v1/stream 200 "chunked" ua=curl/7.85 ttfb_ms=24512
  2026-03-12T08:24:12Z GET /v1/stream 503 "upstream-reset" ua=python-requests/2.31 ttfb_ms=16672
- proxy logs (subset): 
  2026-03-12T08:21:44Z conn=78945 receive-chunk size=512
  2026-03-12T08:21:44Z conn=78945 upstream-write DELAYED by 18000ms (coalescing)
  2026-03-12T08:21:61Z conn=78945 upstream-write flush total-size=12812

Notes: headersize from sample request = 13140 bytes. APIGW configured idle_send_timeout=15s and max_header_size=16KB. The repro indicates buffering triggered around 12–18s, then a large coalesced write was performed.

Initiate a streamed completion from a client with a large trace header (~>12KB) against the ClippeHealth dedicated pool in us-west.
Ensure request body is sent chunked over several seconds to simulate slow client upload.
Observe APIGW and proxy connection traces; look for delayed upstream-write events and coalesced flushes at ~12-25s.
Compare TTFB and response codes for streamed vs non-streamed requests.

proxy: 2026-03-12T08:21:44Z conn=78945 upstream-write DELAYED 18000ms reason=coalesce-policy

Issue summary:
During the customer tenant's steady-state traffic window (03/12 07:15–08:45 UTC) we observed an abrupt rise in 5xx rates originating at the API gateway layer for BeaconHealth Analytics (dedicated tenant). Error rate climbed from baseline ~0.2% to a peak of 6.3% for their routes and correlated with elevated CPU utilization on several serving-runtime pods pinned to the tenant.

Impact:
- Multiple customer API routes returned 5xx (predominantly 502/503) for ~90 minutes, affecting live clinical scoring and chat features.
- Observed increased tail latency and client-visible stream disconnects.
- Customer reported degraded SLA and raised a high-priority support case.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant: BeaconHealth Analytics, prod-us-east, routing through edge-proxy cluster ep-us-1
- API Gateway version: apigw-3.7.1
- Edge proxy: envoy-1.26-custom
- Serving runtime image: redwood-runtime:2026-03-05-prod

Observed symptoms / logs:
- Edge accept-queue length increased prior to error wave: accept_queue_depth ep-us-1 peaked at 11k connections.
- Large number of long-lived keepalive connections from a small set of client IPs (slow-client pattern) holding multipath HTTP/2 streams in half-open state.
- Runtime pods serving the tenant logged frequent "worker-saturated" and "kv-cache-rate-limit-ejection" messages followed by "watchdog-reset" on high CPU.
- API gateway returned 502/503 to callers when upstream runtime stopped responding to new requests.
- Netstat/metrics show high socket count with many connections in CLOSE_WAIT / HALF_OPEN for the tenant's routed IPs.

Hypothesis:
- A small subset of clients are performing connection-holding/keepalive behavior (similar to slowloris), preventing the edge from reusing sockets efficiently and causing accept-queue growth. This in turn amplifies head-of-line blocking and creates load on specific runtime workers (KV cache hot-sharding + continuous batching starvation), pushing CPU to saturation and triggering watchdog restarts leading to 5xx responses.

1) Route a burst of long-lived HTTP/2 keepalive connections from ~200 clients that hold idle streams while occasionally sending small requests.
2) Maintain these connections over several minutes while the normal traffic mix continues.
3) Observe accept queue growth at edge-proxy and elevated runtime CPU for tenant-scoped workers.
4) Confirm increase in 502/503 responses and streaming session disconnects for routes mapped to the tenant.
Initial triage performed by SRE shows concentrated socket-hold behavior from a small set of customer IPs. Edge metrics indicate accept-queue became the bottleneck before runtime CPU throttling. We reproduced a FIFO starvation pattern in a local simulation by holding HTTP/2 streams open while issuing infrequent requests; this caused per-worker batch queues to back up and CPU utilization to rise due to retry/spin loops.

We correlated the tenant's request logs with the IP ranges in the customer's environment; BeaconHealth confirmed a third-party data-collector update rolled out earlier that morning which altered clients to keep connections open for longer to reduce TLS handshakes. This change inadvertently increased connection concurrency.

Temporary mitigations trialed:
- Enabled per-tenant connection rate-limiter on the edge for a subset of routes (reduced connection growth by ~60%).
- Adjusted accept queue high-water mark alerting and increased ephemeral worker pool by +2 for the tenant's shard.
Both actions reduced immediate 5xx rate but did not fully eliminate intermittent watchdog resets on the runtime.

2026-03-12T07:22:38Z apigw[ep-us-1] accept_queue_depth=11234 tenant=beaconhealth route=/v1/chat status=queue_grew
2026-03-12T07:27:17Z edge-proxy envoy WARNING: many half_open streams from 34.85.102.11/32
2026-03-12T07:31:02Z runtime[beacon-rt-3] ERROR: worker-saturated cpu=98% pid=2427 msg=watchdog-reset
2026-03-12T07:31:05Z runtime[beacon-rt-3] WARN: kv-cache-rate-limit-ejection shard=12 pending=812

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 08:15 - SRE (Jordan Mills): Captured live tcpdump; saw many streams with only keepalive frames for >120s. Suspect client-side change. Also bumped ephemeral workers by 2 on beacon shard; initial 10min window shows error rate drop to 2.1%.
2026-03-12 09:05 - Customer (BeaconHealth - DevOps, Maria Lopez): We pushed an update at 06:50 UTC to the telemetry agent — rolling it back now and will confirm if connections drop. Appreciate the rapid response.
Workaround applied: Coordinated with BeaconHealth to roll back the telemetry agent change; enabled per-tenant connection rate-limiting temporarily and increased ephemeral worker count for the affected shard. Result: 5xx rates dropped from 6.3% peak to ~0.25% baseline within 20 minutes.

Permanent actions planned:
- Implement edge idle-stream timeout and per-route max idle streams (Engineering ticket INT-3321).
- Add heuristic detection for keepalive-dominant clients with automated rate-limiting and alerts (SRE runbook update linked).
- Add tenant-level dashboarding for connection-age distribution to surface similar regressions earlier.

Follow-up owner: Riley Chen. Target for mitigation rollout: 2026-04-02. Postmortem scheduled in Confluence and will be attached when complete.
Tenant experienced degraded availability across chat and scoring endpoints for approximately 90 minutes. Root cause traced to a client-side change that increased long-lived keepalive connections; amplification at edge caused runtime worker saturation and watchdog resets yielding 5xx responses. Immediate remediation reduced customer impact; permanent mitigations planned.
1) Engineering to scope and implement edge idle-stream timeout (INT-3321).
2) SRE to add automated detection and alerting on rising connection-age percentiles per tenant.
3) Customer success to confirm BeaconHealth will adopt staggered rollouts for agent updates and add limits on client keepalive behavior.
4) Postmortem writeup and runbook updates to be created by 2026-03-20.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexiSearch reports that a set of dashboard panels which rely on a saved ad-hoc query grouping by client_id (high cardinality) began returning empty series after a nightly rollup/compaction job ran on 2026-03-10. Related alert rules that evaluate the same underlying rollup show `no_data` and did not fire, causing missed paging to the customer’s on-call.

Impact:
- Several dashboard time series show 0 points for windows where raw events exist (verified by raw_events query).
- Two alerting rules targeting those rollups evaluated to `no_data` during the retention job window and therefore did not trigger.
- Customer-facing dashboards used in LexiSearch SLO monitoring were impacted for ~90 minutes.

Environment:
- prod | us-east (primary tenant cluster: tenant-lexi-prod)
- High-cardinality metric: request.latency_ms grouped by client_id

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Open LexiSearch > Dashboards > "Per-client latency" panel.
2) Panel uses saved query: `select p50(latency_ms) by client_id where env='prod'` with time range last 1h.
3) Switch to time slice overlapping 2026-03-10 02:00-03:30 UTC (rollup window).
4) Observe empty series and panel shows "No data for range" despite raw events existing.

Expected:
- Dashboard should display per-client series from the most recent rollup or fall back to raw data if rollup is unavailable.
- Alerts should evaluate against fallback or at least show `insufficient_data` instead of `no_data` when raw events exist.

Actual:
- Rollup materialization produced no series for keys with >100k unique client_id during compaction TTL prune.
- Alert evaluation returned `no_data` and suppressed notification.

Attach logs/snippets provided by customer:
- Raw events query (sample): `select count() from raw_events where tenant='lexi' and env='prod' and ts > '2026-03-10T02:00:00Z'` returned 27,432 rows.
- Rollup lookup log excerpt (redacted): `WARN rollup/compactor.go:243: dropped partition due to ttl and high-cardinality threshold (partition_key=tenant-lexi-prod, series_count=127842)`

Workaround requested by customer:
- Immediate ability to trigger manual backfill for the affected rollup and a way to re-evaluate alerts against raw_events while backfill runs.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:05 - Customer (LexiSearch Ops): Provided dashboard JSON export, alert rule IDs (AR-7123, AR-7124), and sample raw_events query results. Noted they recreated the panel using a non-grouped series and saw data — suggests rollup-specific loss.
2026-03-11 07:48 - SRE (ops-oncall): Manually triggered a rollup backfill for tenant-lexi-prod for the 02:00-04:00 UTC window. Backfill is running; ETA ~2h. Notified customer of temporary mitigation.
2026-03-12 16:30 - Customer (LexiSearch): Confirmed dashboards gradually repopulated as backfill completed, but requested permanent fix to prevent future silent pruning and alert evaluation gaps. Asked for timeline and permanent mitigation plan.
SRE reproduced condition by creating >100k distinct client_id series in a test tenant; compactor TTL job prunes high-cardinality partitions when combined with retention TTL to avoid unbounded index growth.
Compactor code path `rollup/compactor.go` currently treats certain tenant-scoped rollups as best-effort and may drop partitions if series_count > configured threshold (default 100k).
Alert evaluator queries the materialized rollup table directly and does not fallback to raw_events when rollup returns empty; evaluation semantics result in `no_data` instead of `insufficient_data` or a fallback query.
Observed an existing feature-flag `preserve_high_cardinality_rollups` that is disabled for non-system tenants due to historical ingestion cost concerns.
Mitigation completed: manual backfill executed (see related_github_prs) and customer dashboards repopulated. Temporary alert re-evaluation workaround: change alert rule query to union rollup and raw_events (docs snippet provided).
Planned fixes: (1) Lower compaction aggressiveness for enterprise tenants behind explicit opt-in; implement a safety marker to prevent silent drop of rollup partitions. (2) Change alert evaluator to fall back to raw_events when rollup returns no data or to return `insufficient_data` so pager rules behave correctly. (3) Add monitoring around compaction drop counts to detect regressions.
Owners: SRE (Evan Liu) for compactor change; Alerts service (Priya Desai) for evaluator change. ETA for non-urgent config change: 2 sprints. ETA for alert evaluator fallback: 1 sprint.
INT-4021 - Audit compactor thresholds and introduce tenant opt-in flag
INT-4078 - Add compaction drop metric + dashboard and PagerDuty runbook
INT-4099 - Modify alert evaluator to implement fallback semantics or explicit `insufficient_data` mapping
payload.summary: Dashboard rollup missing high-cardinality series after retention eviction

Issue summary:
Customer (CartographAI, dedicated) began seeing sustained elevated 5xx responses from Redwood API beginning 2026-03-10 08:15 UTC after they enabled model-pinning to redwood-gptx-13b-quant-v2 for high-consistency routing. Errors observed across streaming and non-streaming endpoints.

Impact:
- ~18% error-rate elevated 5xx for the customer's tenant over a 45-minute window (api-gateway 502/503/504).
- Streaming sessions experienced frequent disconnects; customers reported partial responses and retries.
- Latency for successful requests increased 3x during peak.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool for CartographAI in prod-us-east; autoscaler configured with burst headroom of 2 nodes.
- Model pinned to redwood-gptx-13b-quant-v2; pinning took effect at 2026-03-10T08:12:30Z.

Steps to reproduce (from customer repro script):
1) Pin model on tenant config to redwood-gptx-13b-quant-v2 and route 90% of traffic to streaming endpoint.
2) Run steady small-batch (1-2 tokens per step) streaming traffic at ~150 rps for 20 minutes.
3) Observe increasing 5xx rate; runtime pod restarts visible in tenant pool.

Observed logs (examples):
- apigw: "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers\n (errno=104)" correlating with 502 spikes.
- runtime stderr: repeated lines of "kv_cache_eviction: thrashing detected, evicting prefixes" followed by "kernel_fallback: switching to slower execution path" and then "fatal: runtime OOM, killed by oom-killer".
- node exporter: GPU memory fragmentation high, sudden jumps in host OOM events.

Preliminary findings:
- Timeline shows pinning caused hot-spotting onto a subset of GPU nodes that had older kernel patches and a smaller prefetch queue configuration.
- Small, high-concurrency streaming requests cause frequent KV cache churn; cache evictions cascade into increased prefetch activity and repeated kernel fallback on a fraction of runtime pods.
- Kernel fallback path is significantly slower and increases per-request memory pressure; combined with aggressive prefetch, some runtimes hit OOM and restart. Restarts cause downstream upstream disconnects -> apigw 502/503/504 and elevated customer error rates.

Temporary mitigations applied (by infra on 2026-03-10):
- Rolled back the tenant-specific model pin to allow smart routing (completed 08:35 UTC) — immediate error-rate improvement to ~2% within 6 minutes.
- Increased prefetch queue window from 8 -> 16 for the affected runtime nodes to reduce churn (08:42 UTC) as a hotfix.
- Temporarily increased dedicated pool headroom by +2 GPU nodes (08:50 UTC) to reduce hot-spotting pressure.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering: build a runtime patch to limit prefetch concurrency per-tenant when KV cache thrash detected (priority).
- Apply kernel patch to affected node image and roll once canary validated (linked PR).
- Product/Support: add a tenant-level soft-circuit-breaker for high error/oom signals to divert traffic to fallback model variant automatically.
- Ops: add an automated alarm for "prefetch_thrash_rate" and a dashboard panel correlating kv_evictions -> kernel_fallback -> OOM restarts.

Links and artifacts:
- Customer support logs: s3://redwood-support/cartographai/2026-03-10/prefetch-thrash.tar.gz
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant-prefetch/CartographAI-prefetch-overview
- Slack thread: #support-cartographai (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/CS-1234)
- Related PR (runtime throttling prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 08:35 - Ops (Automated): Rolled back tenant model pin for CartographAI. Customer reports partial recovery; monitoring continuing.
Root cause hypothesis: tenant model-pinning concentrated traffic onto nodes with older kernel/fallback characteristics; small-batch streaming pattern created high prefix churn in the KV cache triggering prefetch amplification and kernel fallback which increased memory pressure -> OOMs -> pod restarts -> apigw 5xx amplification. Confirmed by correlated timestamps across apigw traces, runtime eviction logs, and node oom events.
Evidence:
- Exact match between pin activation (08:12:30Z) and initial rise in kv_eviction metrics.
- Runtime process core dumps show allocation spike pattern consistent with repeated fallback execution path.
- Reverting pin returned traffic to balanced routing and reduced thrash immediately.
Mitigation applied: rolled back customer model pin and increased prefetch queue; long-term fix planned (runtime prefetch throttling + kernel image roll). Postmortem and ETA to be published after Eng validation.
payload.summary: Elevated 5xx rate after customer enabled model-pinning; prefetch/KV-cache thrash causing upstream runtime restarts

Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 08:40 UTC, Verbio (dedicated pool in eu-west) reported sudden degradation in sustained throughput for short, low-token batched inference requests. The customer sees increased p50/p95 latency and a steady fall in token-per-second across their reserved capacity. Impact: customer-facing feature degraded with higher error rates and timeouts, affecting revenue-critical flows. Timeline: 08:40 UTC - customer alert; 08:45 UTC - Support triage; 09:05 UTC - SRE engaged; 09:30 UTC - initial mitigation applied (traffic shaping). Environment: Dedicated reserved capacity (dedicated pool id: dp-eu-142), prod, eu-west. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send many small requests (avg 8-32 tokens) across 100 concurrent connections to the customer's reserved endpoint. 2) Observe steady drop in throughput within 5-15 minutes and rising attach errors. 3) Check serving runtime and scheduler logs for "GPU_ATTACH_TIMEOUT" and batcher slot allocation errors. Observed behavior: - Persistent "GPU_ATTACH_TIMEOUT" and "slot_alloc_failed: resource busy" in worker logs. - Autoscaler did not provision new GPUs for ~7 minutes during the surge. - NVML warnings and occasional "Device is busy" kernel messages in node logs. - Prefix/KV cache hit rates unchanged, suggesting request pattern (many small, short-lived sessions) is causing slot churn rather than cache misses. Expected behavior: small-request bursts should be absorbed by existing batchers or result in quick autoscale add of capacity with minimal attach failures. Attachments: links to dashboards and sample logs cited in investigation_notes and comments.
Checked autoscaler logs: predictive window did not trigger scale because average queue length metric remained below threshold despite high attach error rate — queue length metric is averaged over 1m and misses short burst signature.
Worker logs sample (node nv1-eu-23): 'ERROR serving_runtime: GPU_ATTACH_TIMEOUT: failed to attach container to GPU after 120s; slot_alloc_failed: resource busy', repeated ~180 times between 08:38-09:12 UTC.
DB of pool allocations shows slot fragmentation: 62% of GPUs had >80% small-slot occupancy (many 1-request slots) leading to inability to coalesce.
Kernel logs: intermittent 'nvmlDeviceGetComputeRunningProcesses' latency spikes when attach attempts coincide; suggests NVML endpoint saturation under small-stream fanout.
KV cache footprint stable — rules out cache eviction. Batcher logs show many ephemeral batch windows (window < 30ms) which prevents effective batching and results in many tiny GRPC streams.
Hypothesis A: Noisy-tenant effect — other tenants on same dedicated HW (misconfigured or under wrong affinity) are producing many short streams causing slot churn and NVML contention.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler thresholds tuned for sustained queue growth; short, high-frequency attach-floods bypass trigger causing delayed scale and attach backpressure.
Cross-referenced SUP-631210 (tenant-preemptive-eviction) and SUP-742998 (pcie-saturation) for similar symptoms; differences: this incident shows attach-time NVML saturation rather than PCIe throughput saturation.
Collected packet captures from node nv1-eu-23 and attached to ticket. Dashboard slices: 'dp-eu-142 attach_errors', 'nvml_latency_telemetry', 'batcher_window_histogram' linked in confluence runbook.
Temporary mitigation validated: traffic shaping reduced attach churn and reduced attach_error rate by ~60% in 15 minutes. Customer still below normal throughput.
Engineering has prepared a scheduler patch to: a) add short-burst detection and immediate auto-scale override; b) add attach-request rate-limiter per-node to smooth NVML calls. Patch referenced in PR 879.
Follow-up: Add metric 'attach_error_rate' to alerting and reduce autoscaler averaging window from 1m to 10s for dedicated pools marked 'sensitivity: high'.
2026-03-13 08:50 UTC — Support (Aisha): Customer reporting degraded throughput and intermittent 503s. Asked for request sample and client SDK version.
2026-03-13 09:10 UTC — SRE (Marcus): Observed repeated GPU_ATTACH_TIMEOUT across three nodes in dp-eu-142. Opening investigation. Slack thread: #support-dedicated-eu (link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C09DDED)
2026-03-13 09:35 UTC — Support (Aisha): Applied temporary traffic shaping on customer route to cap concurrency at 40 to reduce attach churn. Customer reported immediate partial improvement.
2026-03-13 11:20 UTC — Engineering (Leila Gomez): Identified a scheduler race where many short-lived sessions trigger reattachment logic; filing infra PR to add hysteresis (see PR 879).
2026-03-13 12:45 UTC — Customer (Verbio AI, Tom R.): Confirmed that after shaping we see fewer 503s but throughput is still ~30% below normal during peak. Asked for root cause and ETA for fix.
Workaround: Applied per-route concurrency cap (40) and temporary tenant shaping which stabilized attach error rate and partially restored throughput. Long-term fix: merged PR 879 to add burst-detection autoscale override and node-level attach-rate limiting; rollout scheduled to eu-west canary 2026-03-15. Postmortem action items: 1) update autoscaler config for dedicated pools (reduce averaging window for attach-sensitive pools). 2) Add attach_error_rate to console dashboards and alerting. 3) Run dedicated stress test simulating many small ephemeral streams to validate mitigations. Related follow-ups assigned: INT-4022 (scheduler instrumentation) and SUP-742998 (monitor pcie/nvml saturation).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden increase in tail latency and 504s during routine batch inference. Symptoms point to client-side request serialization rather than serving-runtime slowdown. Impact: customer production pipelines observe ~95th-99th percentile latency spikes and intermittent timeouts for multi-request pipelines.
1) Install redwood-sdk-java v1.3.1 (customer-reported).
2) Configure SDK with connectionPool.max=2 and default retry/backoff jitter enabled (default customer config).
3) Start 50 concurrent client worker threads issuing streaming chat completions to the same tenant and model; each request keeps an open streaming connection for ~4s.
4) Observe that requests appear to serialize at the SDK level: only a few requests are active to the gateway while others are queued in user-space, producing long queue waits and some 504s after client-side timeout.
[2026-03-10T08:14:21Z] INFO client-sdk ConnectionPool.acquire waited=421ms in queue (max=2, in_use=2)
[2026-03-10T08:14:21Z] WARN client-sdk RetryManager retrying request id=abcd-1234 attempt=3 backoff=1500ms jitter=+500ms
[2026-03-10T08:14:22Z] ERROR api-gateway 504 upstream_timeout tenant=acme-dataworks request_id=abcd-1234 elapsed_ms=5100
Initial hypothesis: serving-runtime tail regression. Investigated and ruled out by comparing per-node p99 CPU/GPU and token throughput — no corresponding spike on the cluster for this tenant.
Reproduction in staging with load generator showed identical symptom when SDK connectionPool.max <= 2 and retry/backoff configuration active: queued requests accumulate in SDK before hitting API gateway (head-of-line blocking).
Root cause: SDK's pipeline implementation serializes streaming handshakes while a single socket holder is performing a retry/backoff; internal semaphore is held for longer than necessary while jitter/backoff timers run, preventing other concurrent requests from acquiring sockets. This effectively reduces concurrency below the configured max and causes user-space queuing and client timeouts.
Observed metrics supporting this: client_connection_wait_seconds.percentile(99)=0.48s, sdk_outbound_queue_length > 40, api_gateway_active_connections remained steady at expected levels (no gateway saturation).
Short term (immediate) - Instruct customer to increase SDK connectionPool.max to >= 10 and reduce per-request client timeout to allow longer upstream windows.
If changing pool size is not possible: disable client jitter or set retry.max_attempts=1 to avoid long in-process backoffs that hold semaphores.
Redirect some traffic to a separate tenant/model shard to spread concurrent streaming connections across more gateway workers.
Support has applied a temporary rate-limiter rule on the tenant to keep active concurrent streams per second within safe bounds while patch is prepared.
Engineering has created a patch to release for redwood-sdk-java v1.4.2 which changes the pipeline locking so backoff timers do not hold the socket acquisition semaphore and adds a non-blocking connection attempt path.
Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/324 (merged)
Planned release: v1.4.2 staged rollout beginning 2026-03-13 with Canary to 5% of enterprise customers, full rollout 2026-03-15 pending telemetry.
Post-release, customer should revert temporary SDK config changes (connectionPool.max can be lowered back to original documented defaults) and remove tenant rate-limiter rule.
Evan Park (Support) [2026-03-10T09:02Z]: Reached out to Acme Dataworks for concurrent request logs and confirmed they were using v1.3.1 with default pool settings.
Lina Patel (SRE) [2026-03-10T11:16Z]: Reproduced locally in staging using the customer's load profile. SDK queueing observed before gateway — filing internal reproduction notes and starting deep-dive on SDK semaphore logic.
Jordan Brooks (Acme Dataworks) [2026-03-10T12:05Z]: Confirmed increasing pool size to 10 temporarily removed most timeouts; grateful for workaround. Will coordinate SDK upgrade with our infra team.
Diego Alvarez (Eng) [2026-03-11T07:44Z]: Patch implemented to decouple backoff timers from socket acquisition. Preparing release notes and canary plan.
1) Engineering: Release SDK v1.4.2 and monitor connection_wait_percentile and sdk_outbound_queue metrics for 48h post-rollout.
2) Developer Experience: Update SDK docs to recommend default connectionPool.max=10 for streaming-heavy workloads and document retry/backoff interactions.
3) Observability: Add alert when client_connection_wait_seconds.p99 > 300ms and when sdk_outbound_queue_length > 20 for any tenant.
4) Support: Contact affected customers with mitigation steps and coordinate upgrade windows.
5) Product: Consider adding server-side soft-queueing to smooth short surges to avoid client-side semaphore contention in future releases.
payload.summary: SDK head-of-line blocking in pipelined client causes serialized requests, high tail latency and timeouts for enterprise tenant

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A Clarion Health tenant observed repeated fallbacks to the older model variant during a controlled canary shift. The customer had explicitly pinned sessions to rw-open-13b-v2 for regulatory consistency, but a subset of long-running sessions began receiving rw-open-7b-quant responses.

Impact:
- ~18% of requests for the tenant in us-east-1 were served by the legacy model over a 45-minute window (confirmed by token/log sampling).
- Some responses had degraded length/formatting; Clarion flagged this as a potential regression for clinical note generation.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (Clarion reserved capacity) in us-east-1
- Customer pinned model via tenant routing metadata header: X-Tenant-Model-Version: rw-open-13b-v2
- Deployment was performing a canary weight shift from 5% to 20% at the time

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Start a long-running streaming session with pinned_version header set to rw-open-13b-v2.
2) Continue with multi-part streaming prompts over ~20 minutes.
3) Trigger a canary weight bump (internal rollout).
4) Observe occasional responses produced by rw-open-7b-quant and session affinity logs showing routing to fallback variant.

Observed behavior:
- Edge logs show header normalization path rewriting X-Tenant-Model-Version to x-tenant-model-version (lowercased) for some streaming frames.
- Routing mesh relies on exact-match binding token produced by the control-plane handshake; when header key case changes mid-session, the binding token calculated at the ingress no longer matches the control-plane pin state and the request is routed via fallback logic.
- No 5xx errors; requests succeeded but hit wrong variant.

Expected behavior:
- Header case normalization at the proxy should be transparent to model-binding logic (control-plane should use header values case-insensitively or preserve the original header token across handshake).

Business impact:
- Customer paused an internal rollout until guaranteed pin stability.
- Regulatory/process concern: model drift for generated clinical text could require audit and rollback for affected outputs.

Attachments & logs:
- Sample request/response IDs: req-ccf4a6e1, req-ccf4b90a, req-ccf4d2b0
- Edge trace: https://observability.redwood/trace/ccf4a6e1
- Routing decision timeline: https://dashboards.redwood/d/tenant-routing/clarion-135791
- Slack thread: #support-clarion-health (ts: 2026-03-10T18:05:00Z)

Additional notes:
Edge proxy change (PR 998) introduced header canonicalization to prevent a separate routing bug; work runs per-chunk and can mutate header keys mid-stream.
Control-plane binding uses the raw header key name as part of the session affinity token; token generation assumed header key stability.
Sampling of logs shows mismatches correlate with streaming sessions longer than ~15 minutes and with chunk sizes that split header metadata across multiple frames.
No evidence of traffic loss or 5xx; only routing decision divergence leading to fallback to compatible variant.
Staging patch (PR 1428) that makes control-plane header matching case-insensitive removed the mismatch in simulated runs.
Potential edge cases: other middleware that mutates header payloads (trailing whitespace, quoting) could produce similar token mismatches; need to harden token derivation.
Workaround applied: staged case-insensitive matching in routing mesh (PR 1428) rolled to a canary group to prevent further pin divergence. Hotfix plan: revert canonicalization behavior in edge-proxy that mutates header keys mid-stream (edge-proxy PR 1001), and implement robust canonical token derivation in control-plane (PR 1430). Follow-ups: add regression test that simulates chunked streaming headers and an audit log entry for any header normalization events. Customer requested confirmation and a postmortem; SRE will run a 72-hour observation window before closing.
payload.summary: Header normalization at edge causes model-version-binding drift and unexpected fallback routing for tenant

comments: 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Maya Chen: We've tried setting idempotency_key on the function call metadata but when we batch/aggregate our queue items the key gets normalized by our own batching layer; we suspect the SDK is also normalizing per-HTTP-request. We need guidance on how to guarantee once semantics across retries.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer integration uses the Python SDK to orchestrate long-running orchestration jobs via a local background TaskQueue. Each job emits multiple function/tool calls (external webhooks and internal microservice actions). They are seeing duplicate downstream effects when the client experiences transient network timeouts and the SDK retries.

Impact:
- Duplicate invoices and duplicate downstream webhook posts for ~30% of jobs when a client worker restarts under load.
- Customer-facing correctness issue; blocking a few pilot customers on Dedicated capacity.

Environment:
- Nova Analytics Dedicated cluster in us-west-2; SDK version: 1.9.2 (python).
- Using a local task queue that batches logical operations and uses a per-tool semaphore (concurrency limit) to avoid overloading downstream services.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start long-running orchestration that schedules 5 function calls A->B->C in sequence.
2) Worker batches two calls and sends them as two near-simultaneous requests to Redwood.
3) Network hiccup: a TCP RST on call #2 around 1s after send.
4) SDK retry middleware retries the failed request with default idempotency scope.
5) Downstream webhook receives duplicate POSTs (same business effect) despite the original having succeeded on the server.

Expected behavior:
- SDK retries should not cause duplicate side effects if the original request was already accepted and executed. Per-action idempotency guidance should be possible for batched/multiplexed clients.

Actual behavior:
- Observed duplicates when the client-level retry happens and the client-generated idempotency key collides or is not preserved across batched/replayed messages.

Attachments / logs (sanitized):
- Client trace IDs: trace-20260310-9a2c, trace-20260310-9a2d
- Server response (first attempt): 202 Accepted, func_call_id=fc_0a1b2c ts=2026-03-10T17:01:21Z
- Client retry attempt: no server ack received -> retry -> server processes second request and returns 200 OK func_call_id=fc_0a1b2c (duplicate effect)

Customer asks:
1) Is there a supported way in the Python SDK to attach a stable per-action idempotency token that survives batching/queueing and retry hooks?
2) Can SDK-level retry hooks be used to consult a local durable store to prevent duplicate sends? Any recommended patterns?
3) Will a per-tool semaphore (client-side) guarantee ordering and single-execution semantics, or are there caveats for multiplexed/batched clients?

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 - Support (Arjun Patel): Thanks for the detailed traces. We're triaging — asking eng to validate server-side dedupe assumptions. Can you paste a sanitized sample of the request headers (idempotency header, content-length, and any client-generated nonce)?
2026-03-11 - Customer (Maya Chen): Sent headers via secure upload (included trace ids above). Notable header: X-Redwood-Idempotency: ephemeral-20260310-abc123 (generated per-HTTP-send by our batcher).
2026-03-11 - Support (Arjun Patel): Confirmed we found two server-side accept events with same func_call_id but two different request hashes. Eng to follow up with recommended SDK pattern.
2026-03-11 - Eng (SRE): Server dedupe operates on idempotency token + model + route. If the token is changed by client-side batching normalization the server will treat retried HTTP requests as new requests. Batching layers that rewrap payloads can drop original per-action idempotency metadata.
2026-03-11 - SDK Eng: Python SDK 1.9.2 provides a retry hook (Client.retry_callback) but it currently exposes only the HTTP request object and does not automatically rehydrate a per-action idempotency key if your batcher rewrites the payload. The SDK does not persist idempotency state by default.
Hypothesis: Customer's batcher generates ephemeral X-Redwood-Idempotency per HTTP send instead of per-logical action. When the worker restarts, the persisted mapping between logical action ID and idempotency token is lost, so retry attempts produce a new token leading to duplicate execution.
Evidence: server logs show two distinct incoming idempotency header values for the same business operation correlated by customer-provided func_call_id in body.
Workaround and recommended patterns provided to customer. Key guidance: 1) Generate and persist a stable per-logical-action idempotency_key in the orchestrator (durable KV or DB) before you enqueue/batch. Use that token as X-Redwood-Idempotency on every HTTP attempt for that logical action. 2) When batching multiple actions into a single HTTP request, ensure the SDK payload contains per-action idempotency keys in the function call metadata ("idempotency_key"). The SDK will forward those through to the server dedupe layer. 3) Use the SDK retry_hook (Client.retry_callback) to consult a durable dedupe store: before retrying, check whether the server already returned an ack for that logical action (fc_*) and skip retry if ack present. 4) Per-tool semaphores help limit concurrent execution but DO NOT replace persisted idempotency keys — semaphores are in-memory and lose state on worker restart. 5) If ordering is critical, prefer explicit sequence numbers and server-side transactional confirm endpoint (call -> server returns provisional token -> client calls confirm endpoint after durable local commit) to ensure exactly-once ordering.
Action items delivered to customer:
- Example code snippet (Python) with patterns: generate idempotency_key, persist to SQLite/Redis, attach to func call metadata, implement retry_callback that consults Redis and short-circuits resends.
- Link to internal SDK PR adding a small helper in next SDK release to persist idempotency mapping for background taskqueues (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/512).
- Recommend configuration change on Dedicated: enable per-action dedupe TTL=7d for heavy batch workloads (ops can flip this flag per-customer).
1) Before enqueue: for each logical action create stable_id = sha256(run_id + action_index + customer_id) and write mapping stable_id -> idempotency_key to Redis (ttl 30d).
2) When emitting widget func calls, set metadata['idempotency_key'] = persisted idempotency_key and set HTTP header X-Redwood-Idempotency to the same value.
3) Implement SDK retry_callback that does: if redis.exists(stable_id) and server_ack_exists(stable_id): return SKIP_RETRY else allow retry.
4) As an interim mitigation, reduce client retry attempts and increase initial timeout to avoid double-submit windows while you instrumentation corrects idempotency mapping.
Pending - customer to validate workaround in staging and confirm. Engineering scheduled a small SDK helper in the 1.10.0 release to make persisting idempotency mappings easier. Ops will review enabling per-action dedupe TTL change for this customer once they validate in staging.
- Track customer validation result by 2026-03-18.
- If duplicate effects persist after pattern adoption, open a targeted Dedicated config change (enable per-action dedupe TTL extension) and capture full request/response bodies for eng replay.
- Consider adding SDK built-in durable idempotency store option in roadmap (timeline Q2 2026).
payload.summary: Clarification on Python SDK retry hooks and per-tool semaphore ordering to avoid duplicated function invocations

payload.description:
Issue summary: SecuraHealth reports sudden P99 throughput degradation on their dedicated pool that correlates with a spike in short-duration inference streams (avg 50-200ms). Impact: customer-facing endpoints see p99 latency increase and effective throughput drop of ~18% for batched routes. Environment: Dedicated pool (prod-us-west), pinned to redwood-7b-v2, default batching profile, autoscaler configured with min=2 max=12. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run a mix of long streams (multi-second requests) and high-frequency short streams (50-200ms). 2) Observe batch slots and kernel queues via /internal/metrics for the pool. 3) Notice accumulation at kernel queue tail and serialized batch execution. Observed behavior: short-lived requests create many tiny batches that serialize on slots leading to kernel queue tail latency; this prevents larger multi-token requests from filling batches efficiently, causing throughput collapse at P99. Expected behavior: small short-lived requests should be buffered into micro-batches without starving larger batched workloads; autoscaler should smooth minor spikes without slot serialization. Workaround in place: customer temporarily routed short-lived endpoints to a separate dedicated route with lower batching (reduced concurrency) to isolate impact.
Deploy small scale reproduction using redwood-7b-v2 in a dedicated pool with min=2, max=12 GPUs
Generate a steady stream of long requests (1-2s) at 10 qps and concurrent bursty short requests (50-200ms) at 40 qps for 10 minutes
Collect metrics: serving.kernel_queue_length, serving.slot_utilization, batching.latency_per_batch, scheduler.enqueue_time
Observe batch sizes and kernel queue tail latency during bursts
[2026-03-10T14:02:13Z] pool-42 kernel_queue_tail=48ms slot_wait=12ms batch_size=1 model=redwood-7b-v2
[2026-03-10T14:02:14Z] pool-42 kernel_queue_tail=92ms slot_wait=9ms batch_size=1 model=redwood-7b-v2
[2026-03-10T14:02:20Z] autoscaler event=scale_up to=6 reason=queue_depth spike
Initial triage: pattern matches slot serialization rather than GPU exhaustion — GPU util steady at 64-72% while p99 increases
Hypothesis 1: micro-bursts create many single-request batches which tie up slot locks (KV cache and kernel mutex) leading to head-of-line blocking for larger batches
Hypothesis 2: scheduler backpressure thresholding currently prioritizes fairness evenly but doesn't account for high variance short-tail workloads — causing frequent context switches and kernel rebind penalties
Metric evidence: batch_size distribution shifted from median=16 to median=3 during incident window; kernel_rebinds metric increased by 4x
Related signals: increased PCIe peer-to-peer stall traces in trace logs when tiny batches executed in rapid succession
Reference runbook: linked Confluence page on Dedicated pool slot modeling for mitigation steps
Route isolation: moved short-lived endpoints to a separate dedicated route — immediate reduction in P99 for main route (restored by ~15%)
Batching tweaks: increased micro-batching window from 6ms to 12ms reduced single-batch counts by ~35% but added 5-8ms median latency
Autoscaler tuning: increased min_reachable_slots to reduce slot churn; prevented immediate oscillation but did not remove serialization entirely
High-frequency short-lived inference streams produce many single-request micro-batches that hold slot/kernel resources briefly but frequently, causing kernel queue tail latency and head-of-line blocking for larger batches. Scheduler fairness policy and micro-batching window were not adaptive to high variance request duration, enabling noisy short streams to serialize slot use.
Short term (next 72 hours): recommend customers isolate high-variance short endpoints into separate routes and apply temporary micro-batching window increase (12ms) — update runbook and notify SecuraHealth
Medium term (2-3 weeks): implement adaptive micro-batching window that expands under detected high-variance tails and a lightweight per-route backpressure token so short streams cannot immediately occupy slot mutexes
Long term (1-2 months): scheduler change to prefer batch assembly prioritization for multi-token requests when queued alongside short single-token requests, and add kernel rebind suppression when consecutive tiny batches detected
In Progress — temporary workaround validated (route isolation) and medium-term adaptive micro-batcher scheduled. Customer agreed to route isolation and is monitoring. Engineering assigned to implement adaptive batching and scheduler prioritization changes.
Schedule incident review with SecuraHealth and SRE on 2026-03-18
Add automated anomaly detection alert for sudden shift in batch_size distribution
Update runbooks and create a KB article for customers on best practices when mixing high-variance short and long inference workloads

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 16:28 - SecuraHealth (Support): Provided load script and tokenized sample; pointed to two endpoints that show the issue consistently.
2026-03-12 11:45 - Support: Suggested temporary route-level isolation worked around impact; customer requested permanent mitigation guidance.
payload.summary: Bursting short-lived inference streams causing slot serialization and p99 throughput drift in Dedicated pool

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers on Private (VPC) report opaque 429 responses for long-lived SSE streams during our nightly background flush/housekeeping window. The customer observed this recurring between 03:00-03:30 PDT after migrating their dedicated pool to the new VPC egress path.

Impact:
- Several real-time dashboards (SSE) saw spike of 500+ 429s over a 20m window, impacting DataBeam users' streaming sessions.
- Background flush jobs (bulk small requests) complete successfully, but concurrent SSE clients are intermittently rejected with 429 until the egress NAT state stabilizes.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) on dedicated GPU pool
- Region: prod-us-west
- Customer tier: private
- Components: sidecar egress, NAT gateway, cluster sidecar health probes, rate-limiter, serving runtime

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1. Cron background flush starts (many short-lived HTTP/1.1 POSTs from workers to /v1/embeddings) at 03:00 PDT.
2. Workers create many ephemeral outbound TCP connections; connections close quickly on completion.
3. Concurrently, several SSE streams (long-lived) from same customer remain active.
4. Within 10-15 minutes, SSE clients receive 429s; console shows "rate limit exceeded" headers but token accounting in console still shows available quota.

Observed behavior:
- 429s report on SSE responses with X-RateLimit-Remaining headers inconsistent with console readout.
- Edge logs show many ephemeral source ports reusing NAT mapping; origin sees many connections from same egress IP but different source ports.
- Sidecar metrics show high short-lived connection churn and ephemeral-port exhaustion warnings in nginx sidecar logs.

Expected behavior:
- Background flush traffic should not cause long-lived SSE streams to receive 429s (quota separation & smoothing should prevent this).

Relevant logs / snippets:
- nginx-sidecar: "[warn] worker 2: ephemeral port highwater 6143/65535"
- rate-limiter: "token-accounting: route=sse tenant=T-DBA short_requests=1200 long_requests=24"
- edge: "nat: conn_reuse=0 ephemeral_port_runout=true"

Notes on customer config:
- Customer uses a managed NAT gateway with 1 elastic IP for egress.
- They recently switched sidecar egress to route via a new NAT path as part of VPC migration.
- Background flush workers are configured as a cron and perform hundreds of concurrent short connections per minute.

Why this is unique / hypothesis:
- We believe the root cause is not classic token-bucket accounting but operational port exhaustion and proxy affinity changes that cause connection churn to appear as many distinct short sessions at the edge. The rate-limiter interprets the sudden influx of short requests (from the same tenant but new source ports) as increased concurrency for quota windows, triggering 429s for coexisting SSE streams.

Immediate customer-facing workaround suggested:
- Stagger background flush jobs to reduce concurrent short-lived connections (splay cron schedule).
- Move background flush workers through a different egress IP / NAT pool if available.
- Temporarily raise burst pool for the tenant via console (if enterprise controls allow).

Longer-term actions proposed (see investigation_notes):

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:05 - Customer (DataBeam): Applied splay and reported reduced 429s in the next maintenance window; still saw a small set of rejections for a few users.
Confirmed correlation between cron start times and 429 spike windows using request traces from 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-12.
Reproduced with synthetic worker that opened 1200 short connections over 5 minutes from a single egress IP; rate-limiter transiently increased concurrency buckets and then produced rejections for long-poll routes.
Hypothesis: NAT ephemeral port exhaustion + lack of per-ingress-path quota separation causes short-lived connection fanout to be attributed in the tenant's concurrency accounting, affecting SSE routes.
Sidecar nginx config currently reuses source ports but NAT path is configured with single elastic IP; need to evaluate whether connection reuse at the sidecar level can be improved or whether NAT pool size must be increased.
Console currently visible metrics do not include NAT ephemeral port utilization; this made root-cause harder to identify.
Action: Recommend customer splay background jobs (done) and add alternate NAT IP for background workers (customer action).
Action: SRE to add ephemeral-port saturation alert to prod sidecars and to expose a NAT-utilization dashboard for private deployments (ticket INT-4421 created).
Action: Engineering to update rate-limiter to prefer route-based quota segregation so long-lived SSE routes are exempt from short-request burst accounting (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/902).
Action: Product to evaluate console UX for showing egress NAT metrics and a recommended splay template for customers on private VPCs.
Workarounds applied: customer staggered background flush and provisioned an additional NAT egress IP, which eliminated the bulk of 429s for subsequent windows. Engineering will deploy a rate-limiter patch in the next sprint to better separate short-lived request bursts from long-lived SSE concurrency accounting. Monitoring and an alert for ephemeral-port saturation will be added to Private runbooks. Follow-up: verify patch in canary and schedule a postmortem runbook entry.
Create a runbook entry for Private customers describing NAT sizing and splay best practices.
Add an automated recommendation banner in Console when Private deployment exhibits >50% ephemeral port utilization during any 30m window.
Track rollout of rate-limiter route segregation change and validate with DataBeam in staging.
payload.summary: Intermittent 429s on SSE streams during nightly background flush after VPC egress NAT port exhaustion

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent severe reranking quality degradation (top-k collapse) accompanied by backend latency spikes. Impact: NovaSearch search relevance drops to near-zero on affected requests; several production queries return duplicate scores / truncated results and client-facing timeouts. Environment: Production (us-east-1) on Dedicated cluster (reserved GPUs), traffic proxying through api-gateway to embeddings ingest pipeline with async enrich/shims enabled. Timeline: 2026-03-09 customer first reported sporadic relevance regressions; support triaged and opened this ticket 2026-03-10 after reproducing on a small traffic window. Observed: Errors are not uniform — only ~0.6% of embed->rerank flows show the failure pattern, but those have outsized customer impact because they hit high-traffic endpoints. Failures coincide with short latency spikes from reranker pods (p95 -> 2.5s) and 5xxs in the rerank service. Hypothesis: asynchrony in the ingest shim leads to a mixture of float32 and uint8/quantized payloads arriving at reranker; a silent casting/padding bug in the serving-runtime quant path interprets smaller-length vectors as zero-padded high-similarity vectors, collapsing top-k diversity and triggering a CPU fallback causing latency. This ticket centralizes investigation, mitigation, and a follow-up plan.
1) Send two batched embedding requests from client UUIDs A and B within 10ms of each other using async-upload shim (the customer's pattern).
2) For latent repro, alternate precision: one request as float32 array, next request as uint8 packed bytes (customer uses mixed client SDKs).
3) Route both to embeddings-ingest with async enrichment enabled; observe metrics on reranker p95 and top-k diversity for the same query template.
4) Reproduce reliably by adding deliberate 5-15ms jitter on ingest worker to emulate async sharding behaviour.
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] reranker-0 pod: WARNING: topk output contains 8 identical scores; returned_ids=[123,124,125,126]
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] serving-runtime: INFO: received embedding payload metadata{"dtype":"uint8","length":1536} (note: upstream declared float32 for other batch)
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] serving-runtime: ERROR: kv-cache missstorm + quant_cast path triggered cpu_fallback (trace_id=tr-9b3f). stack=RuntimeError: quant_cast: unexpected shape after decode
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] api-gateway: 502 from reranker-service (backend_timeout) latency=2540ms trace=tr-9b3f
2026-03-10 - Reproduced locally against staging by replaying customer's trace; confirmed mixed-dtype payloads in single batch can be produced by customer's async shim.
Checked embedding-schema validator in the ingest path: it tolerates dtype mismatch but does not cast or normalize when async metadata shim is present (intended), which allowed mixed encodings to proceed downstream.
Instrumented serving-runtime to log incoming dtype/length per sample; observed runs where uint8-packed embeddings were decoded but length field mismatch produced zero-padding at the end of vector causing high cosine matches (simulated identical vectors).
Observed that when quant_cast path takes these malformed lengths, it triggers a slow CPU fallback in ~50ms of cases, increasing reranker processing time and causing p95 spikes.
Hypothesis validated: combination of async ingest reorder + missing per-sample schema enforcement + len/dtype mismatch -> both quality (top-k collapse) and latency (cpu fallback) issues.
Priority fix identified: enforce strict schema validation and per-sample casting at ingest boundary (fast-fail malformed payloads) and add defensive padding-trim logic in serving-runtime quant decoder.
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Customer provided three example request traces and a reproduction harness; escalated to SRE/Engineering due to production impact.
SRE (Dion Ramirez) 2026-03-11: Spin up isolated traffic mirror for NovaSearch pattern; confirmed rerank p95 jumps when mirror enabled. Adding temporary traffic-sampling toggle to prevent full customer impact.
Eng (Ethan Clarke) 2026-03-11: Drafted quick mitigation: 1) disable async-shim feature flag for NovaSearch in edge config 2) patch ingest validator to reject mixed-dtype batches. Preparing PR for serving-runtime defensive trim. (PR referenced below)
Customer (Alex Liu, NovaSearch) 2026-03-11: Confirmed workaround when support toggled async-shim off; relevance returned to baseline for the mirrored traffic. Please advise on timeline for permanent fix and SDK changes.
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-12: Noted that disabling async-shim reduced error rate to ~0.03% (from ~0.6%) and p95 latencies are back within SLO. Proceeding to coordinate fix rollout with Eng and Customer Success.
Mitigation applied: feature-flagged async-shim disabled for NovaSearch (edge config) 2026-03-11 which materially reduced incidents. Engineering patch deployed to staging 2026-03-12: serving-runtime PR #2786 adds defensive padding-trim and strict per-sample dtype-length checks in quant decode path; ingest-validator updated to cast or reject mixed-dtype batches depending on customer config. Production rollout plan: canary rollout to 10% traffic 2026-03-14, full rollout 2026-03-16 after 48h monitoring. Follow-ups: 1) add SDK-level embedding-schema validation and unit tests (owner: SDK team) 2) include a regression test in nightly e2e ingestion->rerank pipeline (owner: QA) 3) Docs: update embed schema runbook and customer guidance for async ingestion patterns (owner: Solutions). Linked internal INT-4302 created to track postmortem and permanent monitoring alerts.

Issue summary: Customer reports a missing hourly buffer credit (warmup/free buffer) for a Dedicated account after a weekend run spanning the DST hour boundary. Impact: Boxwell observed ~5-7% higher invoice line for dedicated hours for 2024-11-03 23:00–2024-11-04 02:00 US/Eastern. They expect buffer credits to offset microburst warmups; credits are absent for the hour containing the DST fallback.
1) Customer ran scheduled micro-batch warmup jobs on dedicated pool (tagged 'prod:boxwell') spanning 2024-11-03 23:30 - 2024-11-04 01:30 US/Eastern.
2) Postback system attributes hourly buffer credits based on 'hourly-window' tags and smoothing flags.
3) System evaluated smoothing policy with 'granular_rate_smoothing' feature flag enabled; credits generated for neighboring hours but not the DST fallback hour.
4) Customer compared Console estimate (shows buffer applied) vs finalized provisional invoice (shows no buffer line for that hour).
Expected: Hourly buffer credit applied for all covered hours; Actual: Missing credit for DST fallback hour (clock moved back one hour).
postback_id=pb_0a9f2b; timestamp=2024-11-04T01:00:12Z; window=start=2024-11-04T01:00Z end=2024-11-04T02:00Z; smoothing=granular_rate_smoothing=true; matched_buffer=false; reason='window-length-mismatch'
2024-11-12 09:14 - Support: Confirmed customer cohort uses Dedicated reserved pool and consistent tagging. Console estimate showed buffer; provisional invoice lacked it.
2024-11-12 11:02 - Billing eng (Daniel P): Replayed postbacks for the hour and saw postbacks processed but buffer allocator flagged window-length-mismatch when 'granular_rate_smoothing' was on.
2024-11-12 14:40 - Metering service logs show event counts consistent across windows; the allocator uses epoch-based hour boundaries which did not normalize the repeated hour during DST fallback.
Hypothesis: The granular smoothing allocator's window normalization assumes monotonic hourly windows and rejects duplicated clock hours, causing credits to be suppressed for the repeated hour.
Risk: Affects accounts with scheduled jobs spanning DST fallbacks and any region with manual clock adjustments or similar repeated-hour artifacts. Could under-apply buffer credits and increase customer invoices by a small percentage for affected windows.
Mitigation considered: patch metering window normalization to canonical UTC hour buckets before smoothing evaluation; backfill allocator to re-evaluate affected postbacks for 24h window; issue a provisional credit if validated.
Related: INT-40122 flagged a similar allocator assumption during scheduled maintenance; PR referenced for discussion is meter fix PR #3312.
