Issue summary: Customers reported increased end-to-end inference latency and occasional 504 timeouts for requests that trigger tool/function calls. Impact is concentrated on a small subset of routes that use validation-enforced toolcall schemas.

Impact: LyraHealth (dedicated) observed median tail latency for chat/tool routes increase from ~280ms to ~1.2s on 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC. Several user requests hit 15s client timeouts and surfaced as 504s in customer logs.

Environment: Production (us-west-2), dedicated cluster for LyraHealth, release rollout 1.2.8 applied 2026-03-09.

Initial hypothesis: Synchronous schema validation on the function-proxy path introduced an extra RPC round-trip to the validation service, serialized with the KV cache sequence, causing blocking behavior and tail amplification under concurrency.

Notes: This ticket consolidates customer reports, telemetry links, and engineering investigation notes. For internal follow-up see linked PR and backlog items.
1) POST /v1/chat/completions with tool_call enabled and a schema-heavy tool definition (LyraHealth: /tools/diagnose-patient)
2) Send a burst of concurrent requests (20 RPS) with median input length ~150 tokens
3) Observe per-request trace where toolcall enters function-proxy -> schema-validator -> function-proxy (extra hop)
4) Observe end-to-end latency and occasional client-side socket timeouts when concurrency increases beyond 10 RPS
Tool/function calls show an additional synchronous validation RPC that increases p95/p99 latency and causes intermittent request timeouts (client 15s timeout seen). Traces show function-proxy waiting on schema-validator response before resuming request processing.
Schema validation should be fast-path (in-process or async) and should not add a blocking network round-trip on the hot code path. End-to-end latency should remain within established SLOs for dedicated customers (p95 < 500ms).
2026-03-10T09:12:03Z ERROR proxy: requestId=abc123 route=/chat tool=diagnose-patient wait_for_validator=120ms total_handler=1140ms client=LyraHealth
2026-03-10T09:12:05Z WARN router: requestId=def456 upstream_timeout=15000ms returned=504

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:00 UTC - CS: Received LyraHealth SLA breach notification; customer provided sample trace and request body.
2026-03-10 11:30 UTC - SRE: Correlated spike with the 1.2.8 rollout which included a change to how the schema-validator is invoked (moved from in-process to a dedicated microservice).
2026-03-10 13:00 UTC - Eng: Traces show validation RPC adds 80-160ms per call; under high concurrency validation calls appear to queue at the validator, adding tail latency (we observed threadpool exhaustion in validator pod).
Hypothesis: validator migration to a networked service without adequate pooling caused head-of-line blocking for toolcall flows that synchronously wait for validation before generating model tokens.
Applied for LyraHealth (2026-03-10 14:05 UTC): Feature-flagged route to bypass synchronous remote schema validation and fall back to best-effort local validation for known-good tool schemas.
Customer advised to increase client timeout to 30s as interim safety net for high-concurrency bursts.
Autoscaler rules temporarily increased for validator pods to relieve queuing while a long-term fix is prepared.
Mitigation applied: disabled remote blocking validation for affected LyraHealth tool routes and scaled validator service. Root cause appears to be the 1.2.8 migration of schema-validator to a remote service without sufficient pooling/async patterns. Engineering to implement async validation and local fast-path; follow-up PR opened.

payload.description:
Issue summary: After private deployment onboarding, the customer's model-serving nodes fail to download model artifacts from the S3 bucket during startup. Impact: model pulls time out, endpoints fail health checks, customers observe 503s at control-plane level and the dedicated nodes remain UNREADY. Environment: Private deploy in customer's VPC (us-west-2) using AWS Gateway VPC Endpoint for S3 with a restrictive endpoint policy. Steps to reproduce:
1) Deploy a private agent with model pinning to redwood/open-embed-7b.
2) Agent attempts to fetch s3://finsight-models/prod/open-embed-7b/weights.tar.gz.
3) Agent logs show AccessDenied when calling GetObject; serving runtime retries and eventually fails liveness probe.
Logs / errors:
- From agent: "ERROR: s3.GetObject AccessDenied: Access Denied
 status code: 403, request id: 3A1A..."
- Control plane: "Model pull failed after 4 retries (403)"
- Customer reports that curl against S3 via VPC endpoint fails unless run from bastion as role user.
Additional context: Customer uses a VPC Endpoint Policy that intends to restrict access to a narrow set of prefixes but uses a deny statement that inadvertently blocks GetObject for the agent role. The private deployment uses instance profile role 'redwood-agent-role' that assumes an STS session; evaluation of the endpoint policy with STS session principal may differ from the console test.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:27 - FinSight (Customer) - James Huang: Provided endpoint policy JSON and the role ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-agent-role. Noted that policy was intended to only allow s3:GetObject on prefix 'finsight-models/prod/*'. Attached policy snippet.
2026-03-11 08:12 - SRE - Lara Gómez: Reproduced in our staging by applying a similarly restrictive endpoint policy to a test VPC endpoint. Observed the same 403 from the SDK when requests are signed with temporary STS credentials. Noted the endpoint policy included a Condition that compared aws:PrincipalAccount but the STS session came from a different account due to cross-account role chaining. Suggested temporary workaround: allow the role ARN or allow the specific aws:SourceArn for the signed requests.
2026-03-11 16:40 - FinSight (Customer) - James Huang: Implemented temporary Allow for the role and reports that agents successfully pulled artifacts and endpoints became Ready. Asked for long-term guidance to avoid broad Allow statements.
Checked agent logs: repeated 403 from S3 GetObject. SDK error shows x-amz-request-id consistent with endpoint path, confirming request reached VPC endpoint.
Applied customer's endpoint policy in staging; reproduced AccessDenied for temporary STS-signed requests. Console IAM policy simulator passed for the role but endpoint policy evaluated separately causing deny.
Confirmed that customer's policy used Deny statements scoped to aws:PrincipalOrgID and aws:PrincipalAccount which excluded the transient principal used by our agent (cross-account role/session).
Observed that S3 gateway endpoint policy evaluation occurs after signature verification but enforces principal and condition matches; cross-account STS tokens can produce different aws:Principal attributes causing policy mismatch.
Checked related control-plane logs: model pull job retried 4 times then aborted; no further errors from serving runtime once artifact fetched.
Looked at similar past tickets (SUP-33210, SUP-61234) — difference: those were DNS/TLS; this is endpoint policy logic and cross-account principal evaluation.
Root cause: overly restrictive VPC endpoint policy denied s3:GetObject for agent's STS session principal (cross-account/role chaining). Resolution: Customer added an explicit Allow for arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-agent-role in the endpoint policy and removed broad Deny conditions that blocked STS principals. After policy change agents successfully fetched artifacts and endpoints recovered. Remediation steps provided below.
Short-term workaround: Add an explicit Allow statement for the agent role ARN (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-agent-role) to the VPC endpoint policy so model pulls are permitted.
Recommended long-term policy: Use a least-privilege allow list that matches the exact role ARNs or aws:SourceIp/SourceVpc conditions instead of broad Deny on aws:PrincipalAccount/org. Example template provided in the related confluence page.
If using cross-account roles or STS chaining, ensure endpoint policy conditions accommodate sts:AssumedRole principals; prefer allowing the role ARN or using aws:SourceVpc/aws:SourceVpce where appropriate.
Onboarding checklist update: include a validation step to run a signed GetObject via the VPC endpoint using agent credentials (we provide a validation script) before cutting traffic to private agents.
Follow-up: INT-4121 created to add an automated policy-checker to the private-deploy onboarding flow to detect endpoint policies that will block STS-signed requests.
payload.summary: VPC endpoint policy preventing S3 model artifact fetches for private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10T01:12Z Lumenary reported users observing incoherent resumptions during multi-turn streaming sessions. When a mobile client reconnected (normal network flaps), resumed completions merged with new token streams producing garbled text and occasional hallucinated metadata. Impact: customer-facing clinical triage assistant returned malformed results affecting ~7% of sessions during the morning peak window (01:00-03:00 UTC). Environment: production, us-east, enterprise account with reserved dedicated pool and session-affinity configured. This ticket tracks the Major Incident, escalations with the customer, the immediate mitigations, and post-incident follow-up items.
1) Start a long-running chat (context > 1024 tokens) against redwood-v2-13b via streaming API with session-affinity enabled.
2) Induce a network interruption from a client (simulate cellular handoff) and reconnect within 3-8 seconds.
3) Observe resumed stream: tokens from prior prefix are replayed and interleaved with newly generated tokens leading to partial sentence fragments and mismatched entity references.
4) Check serving logs for overlapping KV write timestamps and socket reconnect events correlated to the same session_id.
2026-03-10T01:15:12Z SESS[abc123] reconnect socket_close=timeout client_ip=35.227.x.x
2026-03-10T01:15:12Z KV-WRITE session_id=abc123 prefix_len=118 ts=1700009712.345 write_id=0x7ff
2026-03-10T01:15:12Z STREAM-RESUME session_id=abc123 resume_offset=118 observed_replay=true
2026-03-10T01:15:12Z SERVE token_emit="Patient has a history" then token_emit="-complete: 0xBAD" merged
2026-03-10 01:12 UTC - Lumenary support engineer escalates via support@redwood. High volume of malformed resumptions observed.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 01:45 UTC - Metric spike: apparent KV write rate for session-affinity namespace increased 4x; tail-latency 95p rose from 80ms to 420ms.
2026-03-10 02:10 UTC - Engineering patch: disabled optimistic KV write parallelism for session restore on the dedicated pool; enabled conservative session lock for in-flight resumption.
2026-03-10 02:25 UTC - Mitigation validated with Lumenary on test traffic; malformed resumes dropped from ~7% to <0.1%.
2026-03-10 03:00 UTC - Issue declared resolved for production traffic; follow-up items created for root cause analysis and longer-term fix.
Support (Amira): Customer reported incoherent merged tokens across resumed sessions. They provided sample session IDs and example transcripts. Customer is highly sensitive — clinical assistant. Escalated to P0.
SRE (Jonas): Observed overlapping KV writes and reconnects for same session_id. Reproducer created in staging. Temporary mitigation: disable optimistic write-ahead for session restore and apply short session lock. Rolling to dedicated pool now.
Customer (Lumenary): Thank you for rapid response. Can you confirm there will be no data loss? Our compliance team is on standby.
Eng (Maya Chen): Patch PR opened to ensure single-writer guarantees on session restore path and to add sequence-number checks for KV-store merges. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2411
SRE (Jonas): Hotfix rolled at 02:10 UTC. Observability dashboards show normalized resume success rate. Scheduling RCA and postmortem owners.
Hypothesis 1: Socket-level reconnects were being handled by different serving nodes before KV prefix write was durable, leading to inconsistent prefix state on resume.
Hypothesis 2: Under bursty reconnect patterns the KV-store write-ahead buffer allowed two writers to commit overlapping prefix ranges; merge logic assumed idempotency which is false for partial token boundaries.
Findings: Trace correlation of socket reconnect and KV write events shows <200ms window where two processes accepted writes for the same session_id with adjacent sequence offsets. The merge routine did not enforce sequence continuity checks, producing token interleaving.
Observed contributing factor: recent kernel selection tweak (auto-batch aggressiveness) increased parallelism for prefix writes on quantized models leading to slightly higher concurrency on the critical path.
Telemetry: Affected sessions concentrated on customers using mobile clients behind NAT with frequent ephemeral IP changes; the dedicated pool routing and session-affinity TTL allowed reconnects to land on different workers.
Hotfix deployed: disabled optimistic KV parallel writes for session restore, enabled conservative session-level locks for resumptions, and added sequence continuity validation in merge logic. Post-deploy monitoring confirmed reduction of malformed resumes to <0.1% of sessions. Customer notified and mitigation validated.
Hotfix rolled to dedicated pool for Lumenary at 2026-03-10T02:10Z.
Linked PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2411 - adds single-writer guard and sequence checks.
Rollback plan existed: re-enable optimistic writes if latency/regression observed; roll forward used after 30-minute stability window.
No data loss detected; all affected sessions were read-only resumes and no persisted customer data deleted.
Owner: Maya Chen (Eng) - Implement durable session affinity improvements: tie session_id to routing token and extend affinity TTL for mobile clients. Due: 2026-03-24.
Owner: Jonas Klein (SRE) - Add sequence-continuity assertions to streaming integration tests and create a chaos test that simulates rapid reconnects. Due: 2026-03-20.
Owner: Support (Amira) - Coordinate a customer post-incident review call with Lumenary and share timeline and mitigation details. Done: scheduled 2026-03-12.
Owner: Observability (R&D) - Add a resume-failure alert (>=1% malformed resumes in 15m window) and dashboard panel for resume success rate per customer. Due: 2026-03-18.
Owner: Security/Compliance - Provide Lumenary an evidence bundle confirming no PHI exposure or deletion. Due: 2026-03-14.

payload.description:
Customer reported a sudden increase in end-to-end latency for chat completions after a model version rollout on rw-llama-70b-instruct. Regression correlated strongly with Redwood’s staged rollout from v3.1 to v3.2 in us-east.

Issue summary
- Symptom: p95 and p99 latency increased (customer observed and Redwood dashboards confirmed). Throughput stable; error rate unchanged.
- Trigger: model version rollout (v3.1 -> v3.2) started ~2025-11-18 16:05 UTC in us-east.
- Impact: degraded UX (timeouts on customer side at 12s client timeout); no material increase in 5xx.
- Scope: us-east primarily; eu-west unaffected (rollout not started there at the time).

Customer impact
- Asteria Search production workload (chat) saw p95 increase from ~1.9s to ~3.3s for comparable prompt sizes; p99 exceeded 8s.
- Customer mitigated temporarily by reducing max_output_tokens from 512 to 256 and increasing client timeout.

Environment / request profile
- Endpoint: /v1/chat.completions (streaming=false)
- Model: rw-llama-70b-instruct
- Parameters: temperature=0.2; max_output_tokens=512; typical prompt length 1.2k–1.8k tokens.
- Region: us-east

What we checked (high-level)
- API gateway: no saturation, no elevated queue time.
- Router: no fallback spikes, stable routing policy; capacity healthy.
- Serving runtime: per-token decode time roughly flat; prefill time increased.

Timeline (UTC)
- 2025-11-18 16:05: rollout begins (canary 5% traffic -> v3.2)
- 2025-11-18 16:22: perf-canary alerts: rw-llama-70b-instruct p95 latency +55% vs baseline
- 2025-11-18 16:40: customer report via Support; internal incident opened: INC-2025-11-18-042
- 2025-11-18 17:10: rollback decision for us-east (pin back to v3.1)
- 2025-11-18 17:28: rollback completed; latency returns to baseline within ~10 minutes
- 2025-11-19 01:15: root cause narrowed to runtime build flag/regression affecting prefill kernel selection for this model artifact
- 2025-11-19 03:40: hotfix PR opened to revert the change; v3.2.1 candidate built
- 2025-11-19 18:20: v3.2.1 canary in us-east passes; rollout resumes with guardrails

Canary + signals
- perf-canary scenario: ChatCompletion, 1500 prompt tokens, 256 output tokens
- Alert: p95 latency regression >30% (threshold) for 2 consecutive windows
- Supporting metric: runtime_prefill_ms increased; runtime_decode_ms stable; gpu_utilization stable

Investigation notes
- Correlation was tight with rollout gates (step function at the same timestamp).
- No evidence of capacity shortage (no queuing, no elevated batch sizes, no OOM spikes).
- Router fallback_reason distribution unchanged (no health/capacity/policy changes).
- Suspected model artifact change interacted with a runtime optimization toggle, selecting a slower prefill path for certain sequence-length distributions.

Mitigation / workaround
- Immediate: rollback model version in us-east to v3.1 (customer impact reduced quickly).
- Customer-side workaround: reduce max_output_tokens and increase timeout (not ideal; provided as temporary guidance).

Resolution
- Serving Runtime shipped v3.2.1 hotfix (reverting prefill kernel selection change) and re-ran canary.
- Rollout resumed with additional canary checks (prefill_ms guardrail) and slower ramp.

Taxonomy notes (for Reliability Program)
- Proposed incident_type: Latency regression
- Proposed subtype: Rollout regression (model version rollout / release-induced)
- Primary owner: Serving Runtime
- Secondary/consulted: Platform Control Plane / Smart Routing (for rollout controls + pin/rollback), SRE (incident process)
- Rationale: customer-facing latency regression caused by a model version release and runtime behavior; mitigation required rollback/hotfix rather than capacity actions.

Next steps / follow-ups
- Add explicit canary gate for runtime_prefill_ms deltas by model family.
- Add an incident-bot suggestion heuristic: if perf-canary regression aligns with model rollout start time, suggest subtype = rollout_regression.
- Document customer comms template for rollbacks vs long-running mitigations.

Customer communication
- Shared summary: identified regression introduced in latest model version in us-east; rolled back; preparing hotfix; will notify before re-rollout.
- Avoided over-specific root cause language pending full postmortem.

References
- Slack: #incidents (INC-2025-11-18-042), #support escalation thread
- Dashboard: Ops > Model performance > rw-llama-70b-instruct (us-east)
- PRs: redwood#28392 (hotfix), perf-canary#499 (additional guardrail test)
payload.summary: Latency regression after model version rollout (rw-llama-70b-instruct v3.1 -> v3.2) impacting Chat completions

2026-03-13T10:30:00Z Marco Ruiz: PR merged for runtime to accept idempotency header from trailers for replays (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421). Drafting advisory to SDKs to add best-practice checks.
payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent duplicated function/tool invocations when using long-lived gRPC streams through our edge stack. Duplicates occur after transient connection loss and reconnect. Initial triage shows idempotency header (X-Idempotency-Key / x-redwood-idempotency) is present from client, but server processing path only sometimes observes it on replays.

Impact: SlateMaps sees duplicate downstream webhooks and doubled billing for about ~0.6% of streamed tool calls during heavy workload. Customer is on Dedicated capacity and uses our Go SDK in production. They have also reproduced locally with TS/Python clients.

Observed behavior: When the client sends per-message idempotency metadata for funcalls on a streamed session, an intermediate Envoy filter (custom header rewrite configured for legacy analytics) occasionally moves headers into HTTP/2/3 trailers (end_stream event). On reconnect + replay, the serving-runtime's replay path only checks initial request metadata for idempotency tokens — it does not look for trailer metadata, so some replays are treated as new requests and trigger duplicate tool invocations.
(Go) Start a streaming session with the Go SDK (grpc-go v1.56.0) against the customer's edge: set per-funcall metadata header 'x-redwood-idempotency' with unique UUID per tool invocation.
Simulate an edge-level transient connection drop (e.g., curl -X POST to our /simulate-failure endpoint or kill TCP connection on client), then let client reconnect and replay pending frames.
Observe server logs: sometimes the incoming request metadata on replay does not include 'x-redwood-idempotency' in initial headers, but it is present in HTTP/2 trailers (seen in pcap / envoy logs).
Repro with TS and Python SDKs by adding per-request idempotency metadata in the streamed message envelope rather than initial metadata; same duplicates observed when edge moves header to trailers.
client (Go) send: metadata: :authority=stream.redwood.example, x-redwood-idempotency=0f7b2c1a-... , content-type=application/grpc+json
envoy (edge) trace: on StreamEnd header rewrite: move x-redwood-idempotency from header->trailer (filter: legacy-analytics-v1)
server (runtime) replay path: INFO replaying request id=abc123 initial-metadata={} (no x-redwood-idempotency)
server (runtime) exec: calling tool webhook idempotency-key=UNKNOWN -> POST /hooks/run (duplicate)

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 08:45 - SlateMaps (Customer): Confirmed repro with TS client in staging; duplicates stopped when they set idempotency key in initial-stream-metadata instead of per-message header. Asked for recommended SDK guidance and whether server can accept trailers permanently.
2026-03-13 11:05 - Support: Notifying customer of canary rollout schedule and recommended client mitigation (set idempotency at initial call metadata).
Hypothesis 1: Edge filter rewrites analytic headers and moves them into trailers at end_stream; runtime only inspects initial metadata on replay. Evidence: envoy logs show header->trailer rewrite event coincident with duplicates.
Hypothesis 2: Some SDKs set per-message headers vs initial call metadata depending on helper utility patterns (Go/TS wrappers have historically allowed either). Customer code uses helper that attaches metadata per message. Repro across languages confirms this is client-agnostic; root cause is missing trailer handling in replay path.
Test: Added runtime fallback to inspect HTT P/2 trailers on replay. In staging this eliminated the dupes for the captured repro cases. Edge-case: trailers are only available on stream end; ensure fallback doesn't break streaming partial acks.
Telemetry: Instrumented counts for 'replay_without_initial_idempotency' and 'replay_with_trailer_idempotency' to measure incidence. Current rate ~0.6% in prod for this customer traffic shape.
Risk assessment: Accepting idempotency tokens from trailers is safe for replay (tokens are client-supplied). Need to ensure we normalize header casing and length; avoid accepting tokens from untrusted proxy modifications without auth checks.
Mitigation steps: (1) Runtime patch merged to accept idempotency token from HTTP/2/3 trailers on replay path (PR #8421). (2) SDK guidance published: prefer setting per-call idempotency in initial stream metadata rather than per-message header; Go/TS/Python SDKs will include helper validation in next minor release to detect 'per-message header' usage and warn. (3) Customer advised to upgrade to runtime build with patch and to deploy SDK minor when available; temporary workaround: set idempotency token in initial metadata on connect.
Rollout notes: Canary deployed to staging 2026-03-12, canary to subset of us-east Dedicated on 2026-03-13 09:00, full prod rollout scheduled 2026-03-14 pending telemetry.
Follow-ups: (a) Add unit tests for trailer-handling in replay path. (b) Create an Envoy rule/guidance to avoid moving idempotency headers to trailers; coordinate with edge infra. (c) Add metrics alert if trailer-based idempotency hits >0.2% on customer traffic.
payload.summary: gRPC streaming: per-request idempotency header ends up in HTTP trailers and is dropped on reconnect causing duplicate tool/function invocations

payload.description:
Issue summary:
HelixHealth reported degraded response correctness and occasional 5xx errors for long-running interactive sessions (multi-turn clinical assistant). The issue appeared after we rolled out a tenant-scoped quantization profile plus an aggressive prefix/KV prefetch policy two days earlier.

Impact:
- Several long sessions (~30+ user turns) saw token-level output drift (repeated partial answers, incoherent context recall) and a small number of 5xx spikes (~0.5% of requests for that tenant).
- Customer flagged high business impact because sessions are clinician-facing; they requested an emergency restore to prior stable behavior.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant cluster (HelixHealth) in prod - us-west-2
- Model variant: gptr-7b-quant-v2 (8-bit quant profile), optimizer flags: async-batching=true, kv-prefetch=enabled, prefix-cache-ttl=600s

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a new multi-turn session with context size ~2500 tokens (system + patient history).
2) Alternate short user prompts and long assistant responses to exercise KV cache growth.
3) Observe: after ~20-30 turns, outputs begin to repeat content, hallucinate prior-turn specifics, or the request returns 5xx error.

Observed behavior:
- Output entropy decreases mid-session; repeated fragments show up across turns.
- Internal logs show mismatch between KV cache sizes on CPU vs. GPU path and occasional quant-dequant alignment warnings.

Expected behavior:
- Stable contextual continuity across long sessions with low error rate and no token-level regressions compared to pre-change baseline.

Logs / Artifacts:
- Attached request IDs: rh-req-20260310-45a1c, rh-req-20260310-7f3b2, rh-req-20260311-11c89 (provided to SRE).
- Traces: link to tenant trace set in Datadog (link redacted in ticket).
- Runtime warnings in logs: "quant-dequant-alignment-mismatch" and "kv-prefetch-evict-race" timestamps range 2026-03-10T03:12Z - 2026-03-11T06:40Z.

Customer request:
- Immediate assistance to restore parity with previous behavior (pre-quant profile change). They asked for a safe rollback approach that minimizes session loss and does not cause large capacity churn.

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Prefer in-place configuration change or traffic split to previous non-quant model variant rather than full cluster tear-down.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 - HelixHealth (Customer): Confirmed that traffic can be shifted for affected sessions but they prefer zero-downtime for ongoing clinician sessions. Asked for guidance on session handoff.
Correlation found between PR 2987 (tenant-scoped quant rollout) and increase in 'quant-dequant-alignment-mismatch' warnings in tenant logs.
KV prefetch code path had an eviction race for long KV chains when quant kernels truncated internal buffer offsets (root cause: index arithmetic difference between quant kernel and fp16 path under continuous batching).
SRE reproduced on a dedicated dev cluster by simulating 30+ turn sessions and enabling same optimizer flags; drift reproduced reliably in >90% simulated sessions.
Memory footprint for quant kernel decreased slightly which exposed edge-case where prefix-cache eviction TTL overlap removed older KV entries required for coherent decoding.
No evidence of model weights corruption; root cause is deterministic mismatch in KV indexing and prefetch eviction timing between quant and non-quant execution paths.
Risk assessment: immediate rollback to fp16 variant carries low risk and minimal capacity overhead for HelixHealth (they run on Dedicated pool with spare headroom).
1) Per customer's request and safety assessment, we performed a controlled traffic migration: created gptr-7b-fp16 variant and staged 90/10 for 30 minutes, then promoted to 100% fallback.
2) Verified with live sampling that token drift and 5xx spikes stopped. Monitored for 24 hours; no recurrence observed.
3) Restored tenant optimizer snapshot to 'pre-PR-2987' config for HelixHealth to prevent automated re-application of quant profile. Snapshot id: snap-helix-20260309-01.
4) Documented runbook steps for safe toggles: how to create variant, staged traffic split commands, warmup window (15-30 minutes), and verification queries. Added guidance to avoid aggressive kv-prefetch changes without a long-session simulator test-case.
5) Follow-ups assigned: Engineering (Gabe Morris) to add alignment checks in CI for quant vs fp16 KV indexing; Product to add a gating flag that requires long-session regression tests for tenant-scoped optimizer changes.
6) Customer-facing note: HelixHealth requested notification when quant profile is reintroduced; Support to coordinate a pilot with warmup shadow traffic only after upstream fixes.
7) Ticket closed after 48-hour stable observation and customer sign-off.
payload.summary: HelixHealth: help restoring stable inference after quantized model + prefix-cache divergence during long interactive sessions

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightAssist reported intermittent mixed-model outputs despite having an explicit tenant model pin configured. Impact: a subset (~4%) of requests during the canary window returned responses generated by a compat/legacy variant instead of the pinned model, causing degraded answer quality and downstream QA alerts. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod(us-east), pinned via tenant config to redwood-7b-v1.
1) Tenant has explicit pin: tenant_config.pin_model = 'redwood-7b-v1'
2) Trigger canary rollout for redwood-7b-v1 -> redwood-7b-v2 in same region with 10% weight
3) Simulate load spike with concurrent prefix-heavy streams (50 RPS sustained for 10m)
4) Observe router logs and serving runtime traces for requests that should honor tenant pin
edge-proxy trace: req=1a7c3f7e tenant=brightassist route=chat model_hint=redwood-7b-v1 fallback_reason=throttle_preemptor selected_model=redwood-1.5b-v2
orchestrator log snippet: 2026-03-11T15:42:08Z WARN fallback-controller: preemptive-throttle triggered for slice 10; suppressed explicit_pin=true for cohort 'tenant-42' to preserve SLOs
serving-runtime: request_id=1a7c3f7e latency=1200ms kvcache_hits=0 selected_variant=compat-v1 (fallback path)
2026-03-11 16:05 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer reported unexpected answer changes at ~15:40 UTC during canary. Provided request IDs and example outputs. They see mixed outputs for some user sessions despite explicit pin.
2026-03-11 16:22 - SRE (Liam Chen): Reproduced similar trace in prod; fallback-controller emitted preemptive-throttle event and set decision to allow degraded variant for a short window. Investigating why explicit pin was not honored.
2026-03-11 17:04 - Eng (Priya Sundar): Hypothesis: fallback-controller has a higher priority rule for latency mitigation that can preempt per-tenant pins when aggregate slot pressure exceeds a threshold. Need to confirm the rule evaluation order and recent config changes.
2026-03-11 19:30 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer accepted temporary mitigation (rollback canary and set strict capacity cap). Asking for ETA on fix and whether billing will be adjusted for impacted requests.
2026-03-12 09:18 - Eng (Liam Chen): Identified change in controller ordering deployed 2026-03-10 (PR #872) that introduced 'preemptive-throttle' as a higher-priority branch. Preparing a rollback of that behavioral change for emergency patch.
2026-03-14 11:10 - Eng (Liam Chen): Hotfix deployed to route-controller that enforces tenant pin precedence over preemptive fallback except under Sev0 global overload. Monitoring telemetry; customer confirmed no mixed-model responses in last 6 hours. Drafting follow-up change to add metrics and a toggle.
2026-03-14 11:45 - Customer (BrightAssist - T. Moreno): Confirmed improved behavior and restored quality. Asked for postmortem and timeline for full fix.
Initial triage: Not an auth or cookie issue. All affected requests had valid pin metadata attached at the ingress layer.
Correlated events: A canary rollout in the same region created a transient slot pressure pattern; fallback-controller responded by enabling preemptive-throttle to maintain P95 latency SLOs across tenants.
Root cause hypothesis: Route-controller policy evaluation order was changed in PR #872; preemptive-throttle branch was assigned a precedence above explicit tenant pin checks, allowing it to override pins during short overload windows.
Telemetry: During the incident window (15:38 - 15:51 UTC) fallback-controller logged 1,340 preemptive events; of those ~52 had explicit_pin=true and were forced to compat-variant selection.
Partial repro: Replayed the same traffic profile against staging with the new policy and reproduced pin suppression consistently when queue depth > 800 and prewarm cache miss ratio > 60%.
Edge-case note: Requests that were streaming with prefix > 1024 tokens disproportionately hit the fallback path due to increased per-token cost estimation and conservative slot accounting in the throttle algorithm.
Immediate mitigation (2026-03-11 20:10 UTC): Rolled back policy precedence change from PR #872 in the route-controller and toggled off preemptive-throttle for non-global overload conditions. Customer canary rolled back at their request to stop quality variance.

Additional notes:
Follow-ups / action items:
- ENG-8471: Add telemetry and dashboards for 'pin-suppressed-by-fallback' events (owner: Priya Sundar).
- OPS-5490: Add a canary guard that isolates pinned-tenants from preemptive-throttle decisions unless explicitly opted-in (owner: Liam Chen).
- CS to offer credit: recommend finance review for impacted token billing with BrightAssist (owner: Maya Patel).
- Postmortem: Schedule postmortem and publish to Confluence with timeline and corrective steps (owner: SRE lead).
Customer status: BrightAssist confirmed behavior stable as of 2026-03-14 11:30 UTC; team requested formal postmortem and follow-up on billing impact.

Issue summary: Customer reports that when a user in their org saves a dashboard filter and shares it with a team, tracehook links attached to panels are becoming visible in other projects that should not have access. Impact: Potential exposure of trace links and context across projects within the same org and occasionally to members of partner tenant projects after a recent saved-filter sharing change. Environment: prod us-west and eu-west, console v2.14.2, tracehook service tag v2026-03-10.

Observed behavior:
- Saved filter created in Project A with a tracehook attached appears in Project B when that filter is shared with team "DataInfra".
- Clicking the dashboard panel in Project B opens trace links that resolve to traces from Project A.

Expected behavior: Shared saved filters should preserve project-scoped tracehook tokens and not surface links to traces outside the viewer's project scope.
1) In org 'datawave', create Project A and Project B with two separate dashboards.
2) In Project A create a dashboard panel and attach a tracehook (project-scoped) via the panel's saved filter.
3) Save the filter and use the 'share' action to share it with team 'DataInfra' (team includes members of Project B).
4) Log in as a member of Project B, open the shared saved filter and apply to a dashboard panel in Project B.
5) Click the panel's trace link -> observe trace details from Project A visible in Project B UI.
6) Verify access via API: call /api/trace/{traceid} from a Project B API key and receive 200 + full trace payload for Project A trace (should be 403).

2026-03-12T18:02:12Z tracehook: attach hook created id=th-9f3a project=ProjectA scope=project
2026-03-12T18:03:05Z auth: token-verify result=ok user=bob@datawave project=ProjectB roles=[viewer]
2026-03-12T18:03:06Z trace-service: resolve-hook request=th-9f3a caller_project=ProjectB -> returned: 200 trace_link=https://trace.redwood/.../trace-0a1b

Additional notes:
Customer (Jane Liu, DataWave): "We only share filters with our infra team, not other projects. This looks like a regression after last week's console update. Please advise mitigation steps."
Repro confirmed in staging: saved filter share flow calls sharing-service which previously returned project-scoped hook metadata; new UI patch stores only hook id and a global token, causing service to resolve hook using caller project context rather than original project scope.
Auth logs show trace-service accepts API lookup requests based on token presence but does not validate original hook owner project after the UI change introduced a 'global' token mode.
Related PR identified that touched saved-filter serialization: PR #4302 (console) added optimism for shared-filters and inadvertently dropped project_id from hook envelope.
No evidence of external tenant cross-org leak; exposure limited to members within the same Redwood org who had access to shared filters.
1) Disable saved-filter sharing at org level for affected orgs (console: Organization Settings -> Sharing -> disable).
2) Rotate tracehook tokens for sensitive projects per runbook.
3) Temporary ACL applied: trace-service set to enforce project-owner check for all incoming hook resolution requests (rate-limited emergency guard).
In progress - hotfix branch created to restore project_id into saved-filter hook envelope and to enforce project validation in trace-service. Patch planned for 2026-03-14 canary deploy to us-west with feature-flag disabled-by-default. Will roll forward upon verification.
Regression introduced in console v2.14.2 where saved-filter sharing serialization dropped project scoping for attached tracehooks; trace-service did not have a defensive validation for hook owner project when resolving hook ids issued via shared filters.
1) Deploy hotfix to us-west canary and verify with DataWave staging repro (owner: Samir).
2) Add integration test that asserts saved-filter share payloads retain hook owner project id (owner: QE).
3) Enhance trace-service to require project-owner header when resolving a tracehook and return 403 if mismatch (owner: Platform).
4) Communicate to impacted customers with mitigation steps and token rotation guidance (owner: CS).
5) Postmortem + update runbook for saved-filter sharing (owner: Support Ops).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 throttles observed in their dedicated pool when their background telemetry heartbeats (scheduled every 30s) coincide with signed-url delivery callbacks from an upload pipeline. The traffic pattern is: thousands of short callback requests plus periodic heartbeat probes.

Impact:
- DriftScale sees elevated 429 response rates for application endpoints that are otherwise low-volume (their interactive chat endpoints start returning 429s for a few minutes).
- Customer is on a dedicated pool and expects telemetry/health to not exhaust tenant burst credits.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (dedicated-55) serving customer org driftscale-prod in us-west.
- Edge proxy: FastNat-v2 (customer uses proxy pool with multiplexing).
- Traffic mix: signed-url callback POSTs (~100-300ms), telemetry heartbeats (lightweight GETs every 30s), occasional large embed backfills.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start embed backfill (bulk uploader) scoped to a single dataset.
2) Enable uploader signed-url callback fanout to callback endpoint (X concurrent short POSTs).
3) Enable telemetry agent with 30s heartbeats across 200 instances.
4) Observe 429s on chat endpoints and callback endpoints during the overlap window.

Observed headers/logs (customer pasted snippets):
- X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
- X-RateLimit-Reset: 24
- X-Edge-Proxy: fastnat-v2
- sample error: {
  "status":429, "message":"tenant token bucket exhausted"
}

Expected behavior:
- Telemetry and signed-url callbacks should not consume the same burst credits that are critical for interactive chat paths, or customer should be able to configure separate burst pools / lower-weight accounting.

Actual behavior:
- The platform currently counts callback and heartbeat requests against tenant burst/refill windows causing short-lived tenant-level exhaustion.

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Any immediate config change or routing suggestion to avoid downtime for chat endpoints when callbacks/telemetry run.

Initial triage: reproduced soft-429 pattern in staging by simulating 250 heartbeat clients + 500 short POST callbacks at once.
Observed that callbacks and telemetry are counted under the same route weight class; priority weights not separated for signed-url callbacks in the customer's route map.
Edge proxy (fastnat) multiplexing causes many signed-url POSTs to be accounted as distinct logical sessions which accelerates token depletion in the tenant token bucket.
Rate-limiter logs (ingress): 2026-03-12T15:12:22Z - tenant=driftscale-prod - bucket_used=1198/1200 - refill_next=24s
Checked dedicated pool autoscaler and burst pool config: dedicated-55 has default burst pool allocation; no isolated pool configured for low-priority paths.
Hypothesis: health/telemetry probes and signed-url callbacks are using default 'standard' priority; should be moved to a separate low-priority burst pool or isolated API key to prevent tenant-level exhaustion.

Additional notes:
DriftScale (Customer): Is there a config we can flip today to route telemetry to a separate quota so our chat endpoints don't get impacted? We can't afford more downtime during business hours.
Workaround implemented: issued a scoped API key for telemetry/callbacks and updated customer's callback config to use it. Scoped key is mapped to a low-priority burst pool (separate bucket) and reduced weighting for short POSTs. Post-change telemetry: X-RateLimit-Remaining remained >1000 for tenant interactive routes during a simulated overlap.
Follow-ups:
- Engineering to add a new admin console option to create 'isolated burst lanes' by route pattern (runbook created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/rate-limiter-burst-pools).
- Add validation to signed-url generator to allow optional api_key override for callbacks.
Product: prioritize admin UI control for 'burst lanes' in the rate-limiter roadmap (spec by 2026-03-19).
Engineering: implement route-level burst pool bindings (RFC filed) and unit tests for multipath accounting (owner: @mtorres).
Support: create KB article outlining 'separate-key-for-callbacks' pattern and step-by-step cutover guidance.
Runbook: add a checklist for dedicated customers to configure low-priority pools for telemetry and signed-url callback traffic.
payload.summary: Configure isolated burst lanes for signed-url callbacks and telemetry to avoid tenant-level 429s

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a midday traffic shift on 2026-03-10 the ClearSight dedicated capacity pool (prod/us-west) experienced a sharp p99 latency increase and a sustained throughput fall (~40%) for ~90 minutes. Surface symptoms pointed to slow GPU attach and long batch serialization times.

Impact:
- Customer ClearSight (dedicated) reported increased inference timeouts and elevated error rates for RW-infer-13B and RW-infer-7B routes.
- Estimated request drop / retry rate increased by ~18% for the tenant window.
- Business impact: degraded user-facing features for ClearSight (reporting dashboards), impacting SLAs.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: prod/us-west, reserved capacity (8 GPUs)
- Affected models: rw-infer-13b, rw-infer-7b
- Redwood platform components: serving-runtime v2.8.1, autoscaler v1.4.0, prefetch-aggregator v0.9.2

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Run steady small-stream workload against ClearSight pinned model routes (peak window ~11:45-13:30 UTC).
2) Observe that new connections stall at "attaching GPU slot" for 200-600ms longer than baseline; batches serialize more often (single-request batches spike).
3) Datadog dashboards show prefetch-aggregator queue length growth and a sharp increase in kv-cache eviction rate.

Relevant logs / metrics (excerpts):
- scheduler logs: "attach_latency_ms p50=12 p90=48 p99=410"
- prefetch-aggregator: "queue_size=172 -> 1.6k in 12m; backpressure=true; upstream_time_ms=380"
- gpu allocator: "attach_retry=3; attach_error=OOM? false; attach_backoff_ms=500"
- serving-runtime traces: repeated tiny batches, KV cache miss rate +42%

Initial investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: A tenant (ClearSight) sent many small long-lived streams that increased prefetch-aggregator aggregation latency and caused starvation of pooled batchers.
- Hypothesis 2: Prefetch aggregator aggregated metadata across tenants causing head-of-line blocking when one tenant's streams stalled (noisy neighbor pattern).
- Hypothesis 3: Autoscaler telemetry read aggregated attach latencies and interpreted the signal as transient, avoiding scale-up.

What we checked so far:
- Correlated Datadog traces with allocator metrics; found sustained increase in prefetch-aggregator processing latency coincident with kv-cache evictions.
- Inspected prefetch-aggregator host list: one host reported periodic GC pauses (container-level OOM-kill events seen in host metrics) at the same time as queue growth.
- Looked at tenant request profiles: ClearSight had a high fraction of tiny, high-concurrency short streams during the window.

Mitigation taken (temporary):
- Isolated ClearSight traffic onto a dedicated subpool within the reserved cluster (manual routing) at 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC. This removed cross-tenant aggregation and restored baseline throughput within ~7 minutes.
- Restarted two prefetch-aggregator replicas and applied a temporary per-tenant queue cap (config flag) to limit head-of-line blocking.

Current status and next steps:
- Root cause inspection ongoing. Priority is to: (A) reproduce in staging with a synthetic mix of many small streams + induced host GC pauses, (B) instrument prefetch-aggregator to expose per-tenant processing time and queue metrics, and (C) evaluate autoscaler sensitivity to attach-latency signals so it scales appropriately instead of ignoring transient but sustained backpressure.
- Proposed short-term fix: enforce per-tenant queue limits in prefetch-aggregator and add a backpressure signal for autoscaler to consider aggregated prefetch queue depth.
- Longer-term follow-up: improve tenant isolation in scheduling and consider preferring per-tenant batching windows to prevent cross-tenant head-of-line effects.

Attachments / links:
- Datadog graph: https://app.datadog.com/graph/abcd-prefetch-queue

payload.description:
Issue summary: ParcelFlow reports that SSE streams occasionally finish without the final paragraph — the streamer closes without the terminal "event: end" chunk. Impact: customers see truncated outputs for long streaming responses (~4-12s generation) ~1-2% of sessions during weekday peak. Environment: prod, routed via CDN (FastEdge) -> Redwood edge-proxy (http2 upstream to runtime) -> serving-runtime. Observed behavior: final JSON chunk with choice 'finish_reason' is missing; client receives connection close without terminal delimiter. Expected behavior: final chunk and terminal event should be delivered before stream close.
1) Use ParcelFlow dedicated account in us-east to start an SSE generation with redwood-7B-instruct, prompt ~200 tokens expected finalization at 6-10s
2) Route traffic through customer CDN (FastEdge) configured with http2 fronting Redwood edge in us-east
3) Observe stream with client that logs SSE frames and final 'event: end' marker
4) Intermittent: connection closes from upstream during finalization and last chunk never arrives
edge-proxy (us-east) 2026-03-09T18:22:41Z INFO upstream: initiating graceful shutdown (GOAWAY) for conn conn=0x7f3a
serving-runtime 2026-03-09T18:22:42Z DEBUG stream=svc-1294 tail-chunk queued to conn but client connection already half-closed
edge-proxy 2026-03-09T18:22:42Z WARN sse: dropping tail fragment due to write error: write tcp 10.2.4.8:443->10.4.1.22:52314: use of closed network connection
client-side trace (ParcelFlow) 2026-03-09T18:22:43Z INFO SSE: connection closed, last-received-event=choice: 0, no 'end' marker

Additional notes:
Hypothesis: HTTP/2 GOAWAY from upstream CDN causes edge-proxy to transition connection state; if the edge-proxy does not flush pending SSE frames before closing underlying TCP, the last frame is lost.
Confirmed by reproducer: synthetic script that sends a 3-chunk SSE stream, then triggers upstream GOAWAY immediately after final chunk is queued -> final chunk missing at client.
Edge-proxy codepath uses non-blocking writes; when GOAWAY observed it initiated connection close callback that cancels outstanding write completion in some code paths.
Serving-runtime observed no internal generation error; generation completed and final tokens were produced and queued to downstream.
Related to prior ticket SUP-981024 (terminal output lost after short TLS stall) but root cause here is HTTP/2 graceful shutdown ordering rather than TLS stall.
Affected surface area: SSE over HTTP/2 and websockets proxied via edge-proxy when upstream initiates GOAWAY/stream reset close during tail-write.
Workaround (customer-facing): Configure CDN to increase the GOAWAY drain timeout on upstream connections (FastEdge setting: upstream_grace_period to 5s) OR enable retry-on-close in client to re-request with 'last_event_id' semantics (ParcelFlow implemented quick client-retry for truncated responses).
Fix deployed: edge-proxy hotfix delays final TCP close until write buffer drain completion and treats GOAWAY as 'drain and close' instead of immediate close. Hotfix rolled to us-east edge nodes 2026-03-12 14:45 UTC.
Follow-ups: add unit/integration test for SSE flush on upstream GOAWAY, add dashboard alert for upper-percentile truncated_stream_rate, and update streaming runbook with 'http2-goaway' troubleshooting steps. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/4312
Status: monitoring — initial metric shows truncated stream rate dropped from 0.8% to 0.03% in canary. Awaiting 48h observation window before closure.
payload.summary: SSE final frame dropped after upstream HTTP/2 graceful shutdown behind CDN

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 524 gateway timeouts and stalled model shard downloads from serving nodes in eu-west after we provisioned their private deployment. Impact: Serving requests intermittently hang for 20-90s and return 524 or gRPC CANCELLED before succeeding on retry. Affects user-facing inference and batch artifact fetches. Environment: Private deployment over transit VPC (customer-managed peering) with split-horizon DNS; control plane endpoints are resolved via customer's internal resolver for serving nodes and via public resolver for control-plane health checks. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger a large model request that requires shard downloads (e.g., 200MB ranges). 2) Observe gRPC stream establishment and subsequent 20-90s stalls followed by 524 or CANCELLED. 3) Repeat; behavior is intermittent and correlates with SRV record changes in customer DNS. Observed behavior: gRPC channels are repeatedly anchored to a single AZ's serving nodes that are intermittently degraded; DNS SRV responses from customer resolver reorder priority and weight between responses (split-horizon + low TTL). Expected behavior: SRV responses should present stable ordering/weights or our client should round-robin across healthy endpoints; gRPC should failover more quickly. Relevant logs: "stream_id=0x1a3c connect_to=svc-azb.eu-west-1.redwood.svc:443 delay=27.8s err=GRPC_CANCELLED"; DNS trace: ";; ANSWER SECTION: _redwood._tcp.redwood.svc 30 IN SRV 10 50 443 svc-aza...\n;; ANSWER SECTION: _redwood._tcp.redwood.svc 30 IN SRV 5 100 443 svc-azb..." Additional context: Customer runs an internal DNS layer that performs health-aware SRV rewriting and has a short TTL (30s). Their resolver sometimes returns the same SRV set with different priority/weight ordering across sequential queries which appears to interact with our client-side SRV selection and gRPC channel pinning logic.
2026-03-10 09:15 - Support (Lina Park): Ticket opened after customer post in #support-private-deploy. Customer provided pcap and dnsdig outputs. Marking P1 due to production impact.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Customer (Jules Rivera, AcmeAI): We're seeing repeated stalls specifically when requests fan out to multiple shards. Stalls go away after 30-60s and retries succeed. We've rolled back a recent DNS health-probe change but issue persists.
2026-03-10 11:25 - Support (Samir Gupta): Requested DNS dig + tcpdump around SRV resolution and first TLS ClientHello. Asked for agent logs from serving-node side (kv-cache and healthcheck events).
2026-03-10 14:40 - Customer (Jules Rivera): Uploaded tcpdump and DNS trace (attached to ticket). Noticed SRV answers flip ordering between identical queries; TTL is 30s. Also our firewall occasionally delays SYN+ACKs to one AZ for ~20s.
2026-03-11 08:12 - Eng (Diego Martínez): Hypothesis: client SRV parse + gRPC connectivity code pins to first endpoint in SRV set. If SRV ordering is unstable, subsequent queries can point to a node still marked active locally but unhealthy upstream, creating sticky failure. Asked SRE to check ALB target-health and AZ-specific egress performance.
2026-03-11 12:36 - SRE (Anya Kovalenko): ALB/targets show spiky 5xxs in eu-west-1-b at the times customer reported. No underlying instance crashes, but egress firewall queueing observed on customer side in the same windows.
2026-03-12 09:05 - Support (Samir Gupta): Temporary mitigation suggested: increase client-side SRV shuffle + reduce pin lifetime; customer applied a config to shuffle SRV records before selection and widened probe window on their DNS. Observing fewer incidents since 03/11 20:00 UTC.
2026-03-12 17:00 - Customer (Jules Rivera): After shuffling SRV results on our resolver, incidents dropped dramatically. We'll keep monitoring and ask us to coordinate if issues reappear.
Initial triage combined customer-provided packet captures, DNS traces, and server-side metrics. Evidence: 1) DNS traces show SRV sets with identical targets but varying priority/weight between sequential queries. 2) gRPC client logs indicate channels are established to the first backend in the SRV set and kept alive across requests (channel pinning). 3) Serving node metrics show elevated request queue times in eu-west-1-b during incidents. 4) Customer firewall logs show sporadic egress queueing and SYN delays impacting one AZ. Conclusion: root cause is a combination of customer-side split-horizon DNS reordering (low TTL + health-aware rewriting) and a client-side SRV selection implementation that prefers ordered SRV entries and pins channels, which amplifies transient AZ-level network degradations into sustained request stalls.
Short-term mitigation: Instructed customer to enable SRV shuffle on their internal resolver (applied 2026-03-11 20:10 UTC) and to increase SRV TTL to 60s. We released a server-side client config change to randomize SRV selection and reduce channel pin lifetime (infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4021) as a mitigant for private deployments behind split-horizon resolvers. Long-term: Engineering will land a robust SRV failover strategy in the client library that: 1) randomizes (or respects weight) SRV selection if TTL < 60s, 2) refreshes pinned endpoints after a short backoff on repeated errors, and 3) surfaces per-AZ health in tracing for faster detection. Follow-ups: INT task to add SRV-ordering test cases (INT-2041), update Private Deployment runbook with DNS guidance, and schedule a postmortem with the customer in 1 week.
payload.summary: Split-horizon SRV priority/weight oscillation pins gRPC streams to an unhealthy AZ causing intermittent 524s and model shard download stalls

Issue summary:
Customer Kestrel Health reports that a contractual rate override (enterprise addendum ID: KH-2025-A) is not being applied when their private deployment falls back to hosted in eu-west. They were charged at standard hosted per-token rates for ~3 hours on 2026-03-09 during a private->hosted fallback window.

Impact:
- Unexpected invoice line of ~€18,564 for fallback-hosted usage on the March invoice.
- Affects revenue recognition and customer expectations (enterprise contract explicitly specifies a lowered hosted fallback rate for private customers).
- Customer-facing SLA and CSM escalation opened; finance has paused autopay pending resolution.

Environment:
- Customer: Kestrel Health (private deployment, enterprise tier)
- Private control plane: vpc-kestrel-eu (managed by Redwood Private)
- Fallback path: private -> hosted (eu-west) automatic routing when private pool under capacity pressure
- Time window: 2026-03-09 02:12:00 to 2026-03-09 05:29:00 UTC
- Affected model: redwood-open-7b-v2 (pinned in customer config)

Steps to reproduce / observed workflow:
1) Simulated load test ran by customer at 02:10 UTC; private pool reached 98% GPU utilization.
2) Smart routing triggered fallback policy to hosted (eu-west) as expected.
3) Requests successfully executed on hosted; however billing records attribute usage to standard hosted tariff without KH-2025-A override.
4) Customer observed invoice charge for hosted usage and raised ticket via CSM.

Logs / evidence attached:
- Routing audit (s3://billing-audit/eu-west/2026-03-09/routing-20260309-02-05.log) [link redacted for support]
- Billing postbacks showing per-token rate applied (billing-id: bill-eu-20260309-459)
- Contract snippet uploaded to ticket (KH-2025-A clause 4.2 fallback-rate = 0.0045 EUR/token)
- Console screenshot: per-route cost breakdown for the fallback window

Initial hypothesis (Support):
- Rate override lookup was not applied for fallback-attributed postbacks because of an ordering issue in the rate-lookup service: the private-rate check happens in the routing phase but billing postback is evaluated against hosted-tariff by default when origin=hosted.
- Another possibility: the customer’s enterprise metadata tag (contract_id: KH-2025-A) was not present on hosted-side postbacks due to a header stripping in proxying.

Work done so far (investigation notes):
- Support retrieved routing audit and confirmed requests did hit hosted endpoints (confirmed).
- Billing team inspected the postback and found contract_id missing on ~72% of the postbacks during the window; remaining 28% included contract_id but still had standard tariff (inconsistent behavior).
- Routing engineers reproduced a local scenario using the private->hosted shim; observed that X-Redwood-Contract header is forwarded from private router, but our hosted ingress removes unknown headers as part of the proxy hardening rule set.
- Eng confirmed a recent proxy hardening change (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/214) added header whitelist; contract metadata must be present in the request body for billing to pick it up.

Proposed next steps / mitigation plan:
1) Immediate: apply provisional credit for the disputed hosted-line amount (finance approval requested) so customer invoice can be corrected while root-cause is fixed. (Assigned to Billing: Carlos Mendes)
2) Short term (hotfix): update hosted billing postback processor to fall back to routing tags (routing-audit correlation) when contract_id header absent. (Assigned to Billing + Routing)
3) Medium term: change proxy hardening whitelist to include X-Redwood-Contract and ensure the private->hosted shim preserves contract metadata. (Security and Routing teams)
4) Postmortem: document in Confluence and update runbook to validate contract metadata during deployment and fallback testing.

Customer requested outcome:
- Refund/credit of the €18,564 charged during the fallback window, or an invoice re-issue reflecting the contractual fallback rate.
- Written assurance and a timeline for permanent fix.

Resolution notes (to be completed):
- 2026-03-12: Provisional credit created for the disputed amount and applied as a negative line on the March invoice (waiver id: WAIVE-2026-1147).
- Hotfix PR created for billing postback processor (https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/332).
- Security whitelist change scheduled for 2026-03-15.
- Customer notified and CSM coordinated next steps.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:12 - Finance (J. Nguyen): Provisional credit authorized. Waiver id WAIVE-2026-1147 applied. Please confirm when invoice re-issue is needed.
Provisional credit applied; hotfix PR created for billing postback fallback; proxy whitelist scheduled to restore contract header forwarding. Invoice reissue pending final verification. Postmortem to follow after security change is in production.
Waiver WAIVE-2026-1147 created for €18,564. Recommend reissue of corrected invoice once billing postbacks reprocessed for the window. Customer requested autopay remain paused until reissue.

2026-03-12 14:10 - Support Aisha Patel to customer: A provisional credit has been applied to the March invoice. We will follow up with a permanent fix timeline and a postmortem once changes are deployed.

Issue summary:
Customer (KumoHealth) has configured region pinning to ap-southeast-1 for all hosted API calls. During a capacity spike on 2026-03-10 they observed increased tail latency and traces that show compute nodes in us-east-1 serving several requests. Customer is asking: did their request payloads leave APAC? What parts of request/metadata cross regions? What are supported mitigations (strict residency, fail-if-cross-region, dedicated capacity)?

Impact:
- Enterprise customer in regulated healthcare use case concerned about data sovereignty and audit controls.
- Observed latency spike impacting UI flows (patients and clinicians).

Environment:
- Hosted API (redwood public), prod - ap-southeast-1 region pin set via customer config.
- Customer account ID: KUMO-001 (internal ref).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send generation request with region=ap-southeast-1 pinned via SDK header X-Redwood-Region: ap-southeast-1.
2) Repeat during peak load window (2026-03-10 17:30-18:15 SGT).
3) Observe response latency increase and service trace indicating serving_region: us-east-1 for subset of requests.

Observed behavior:
- ~8% of requests in the window were served by us-east-1 compute.
- Token-level latency for those requests increased ~2.6s compared to fully ap-southeast-1 flows.
- Customer concerned that PII may have crossed regions.

Expected behavior:
- With region pin set, customer expects all inference compute to remain in ap-southeast-1 or a clear failure when capacity unavailable.

Attachments and IDs:
- Sample request IDs: req_20260310_1a2b3c, req_20260310_1a2b3d, req_20260310_1a2b3f
- Trace links (internal): https://observability.prod/redwood/traces/req_20260310_1a2b3c
- Screenshot of SDK header config attached in ticket.
2026-03-10 11:05 - KumoHealth (Sara Lim): We saw ~8% of requests served from us-east-1; need confirmation that customer data did not leave APAC. This is blocking compliance signoff.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 16:05 - Product (Lina Gomez): Flagging this to product for visibility — we should clarify residency semantics in docs and consider a customer-visible strict_residency option.
2026-03-11 - pulled router decision logs for req_20260310_1a2b3c and req_20260310_1a2b3d. Decision path: API gateway -> control-plane policy evaluation -> model-pool lookup -> assign compute node (us-east-1).
Capacity snapshot 2026-03-10 17:35 SGT shows ap-southeast-1 free slots at 12% below the configured soft-threshold for automatic fallback prevention. During this brief window, routing policy allowed cross-region fallback to preserve availability (configurable per-customer default: allow_fallback=true).
Audit log review: request metadata (headers, request_id, trace_id) were propagated to control-plane components in our global control plane. Payload bodies are encrypted in transit. No evidence of logging of plaintext customer payloads in control-plane logs. Compute nodes in us-east-1 received the encrypted payload and performed inference there.
Network traces (tcpdump) from compute nodes show connections served entirely within provider backbone; because compute was in us-east-1, egress did not flow back to ap-southeast-1 compute. Therefore compute did process the request in us-east-1 for the affected traces.
Customer uses healthcare PII workload — this is a policy violation for their residency requirements when compute crosses regions.

Issue summary:
Customer reports that during a rolling canary in us-east, long-lived streaming sessions for specific tenants suddenly switched from the tenant-requested model (explicit model_version header) to a canary variant. The switch happened without any client-side reconnect and while the stream was mid-response. This appears correlated with a background pin-refresh operation initiated by the tenant SDK at the same time the control-plane applied a reconciliation update.

Impact:
- Several production customers experienced inconsistent outputs for in-flight streams (approx 30 affected sessions over a 20m window).
- Outputs from the canary variant produced tokenization/format deltas, causing 3 downstream user-facing failures (alerts from customer evals).
- Customer Covalent Analytics (dedicated tier) reports degraded ML QA scores and asked for urgent mitigation.

Environment:
- prod, us-east primary (edge), eu-west had a smaller blast radius via cross-region routing fallback
- Affected tenant on Dedicated capacity pool (reserved), interacting with a staged canary weight shift for redwood/v1-chat-13b -> redwood/quant-4bit-7b variant

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Start a long-lived streaming session (server-side streaming) with header: "model_version: redwood/v1-chat-13b@2024-10-31" and tenant pin metadata in X-Redwood-Tenant-Pin
2) Trigger a tenant token refresh (SDK auto refresh) from client, which calls control-plane pin-refresh endpoint for lease renewal (~client-side refresh every 15m; here it occurred mid-stream)
3) Simultaneously the orchestrator applied a canary snapshot update and a reconciliation loop merged a prewarm snapshot into the control-plane routing table
4) During the next prefix/KV reconciliation window, edge dropped model_version affinity and routed mid-stream traffic to the canary lane

Observed behavior:
- Edge logs show a Control-Plane:PATCH routing update at 2024-11-05T17:03:12Z followed by an edge decision to remap requests from model_id redwood/v1-chat-13b to redwood/quant-4bit-7b at 17:03:14Z for the affected session ids.
- The HTTP/2 stream remained open (no reconnect from customer) and server continued generating; model switch appears to have been applied in-path by sidecar routing decisions.

Relevant logs (snippets):
- edge-proxy (us-east-1) 2024-11-05T17:03:12.217Z INFO "received controlplane routing patch" request_id=xyz-331
- front-proxy decision 2024-11-05T17:03:14.009Z WARN "session-routing: replacing pinned variant for session" session_id=abc-902 tenant_id=cov-17 old_variant=redwood/v1-chat-13b new_variant=redwood/quant-4bit-7b reason=controlplane-merge
- sidecar sanitizer 2024-11-05T17:03:14.011Z DEBUG "header mutate: tenant pin refresh token detected, applying ttl extension"
- serving-runtime 2024-11-05T17:03:14.120Z INFO "accepted request on model redwood/quant-4bit-7b" request_id=req-771

Notes on reproduction attempts:
- With a synthetic streaming workload (10 parallel long-lived streams) we could reproduce the mid-stream switch ~60% of runs when timing the SDK refresh to coincide with a control-plane canary apply.
- Reproduces more reliably when prefix/KV cache warmup is in-progress (suggests race between cache application and pin affinity checks).

Additional notes:
Investigative timeline: 11/05 reproduce -> captured edge+sidecar+control-plane traces; 11/06 isolated race between control-plane snapshot merge and sidecar TTL mutation; 11/06 runtime team proposed short-term guard to prefer explicit model_version header; 11/07 mitigation deployed to us-east. Hypothesis: sidecar TTL extension logic inadvertently replaced session-affinity token used by edge for routing during reconciliation. Other contributing factor: prefix/KV warmup during canary prewarm causes transient path where control-plane computed routing is temporarily preferred.
Hotfix deployed (control-plane PR #1842 reverted the merge ordering change and added an explicit 'preserve-explicit-model' flag during routing table apply; sidecar patch prevents TTL extension from overwriting affinity token mid-stream). Workaround offered to customer: (A) add explicit X-Redwood-Strict-Pin: true header to enforce immutable pin for session lifetime, (B) stagger SDK refresh windows or disable auto pin-refresh during critical streams. Customer accepted workaround and requested strict pin config (scheduled as follow-up).
Create Confluence postmortem and link to this ticket
Add e2e test coverage for long-lived streams + pin-refresh during canary apply
Implement alerting for midstream model switches (>1/min threshold)
Add tenant-level config flag for strict pin preservation (product + security review needed)
payload.summary: Tenant-initiated pin-refresh race overwrote explicit model selection mid-stream

Issue summary: Customer reports sporadic 504 gateway responses from /rerank and apparent non-deterministic changes in rerank ordering for the same query set. Impact: Production search UX degraded for a subset of SynthWorks customers with timeouts and inconsistent top-k. Root cause hypothesis is a format negotiation mismatch between client SDK and our ingest router leading to partial binary payloads being routed to a JSON-only consumer and to fallback CPU decoding that increases rerank latency and causes request queueing/backpressure.

Observed behavior: (1) Rerank endpoint returns 504 for ~0.8% of requests during peak, (2) When responses succeed after retries, top-5 ordering occasionally differs between retries, (3) Embeddings ingestion logs show a spike in proto-decode errors for some shard ranges coincident with increased CPU on reranker replicas.

Expected behavior: All embedding uploads should be accepted (binary or JSON) according to version negotiation; rerank should remain within latency SLO and return stable ordering for identical inputs.

Impact notes: Affects SynthWorks production clusters on dedicated capacity; visible to end users searching application knowledge base. Customer has ~1200 daily rerank calls; tail increase is driving user complaints.
1) Use SynthWorks SDK v1.2.0 to upload embedding payloads with header 'Embedding-Version: 2026-02' and Content-Type: application/octet-stream
2) Immediately issue a /rerank call referencing the recently uploaded ids (same session) against reranker-v2 pinned model
3) Repeat at ~120 qps from a single client to simulate burst and watch for 504s and order instability
4) Alternate uploads using SDK v1.4.1 (JSON payload, application/json) to demonstrate mixed-client behavior
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z ingest-router[ingest-3] WARN proto_decode: failed to decode message for shard=eu-451, err=Unexpected EOF
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z reranker[rk-7] ERROR request: slowpath cpu-decode fallback, decode_time_ms=172, total_latency_ms=904
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z api-gateway[gateway-2] WARN proxy: upstream returned 504, path=/rerank, rt_ms=901
2026-03-10T14:02:12Z ingest-router[ingest-3] INFO accept-negotiation: client_accepts=[application/octet-stream], server_candidates=[application/json, application/protobuf]; selected=fallback-cpu-decode
Support (Priya): Customer reports tail latency and occasional 504s starting 2026-03-10 13:55 PST. They attached a capture of embedded payload headers. Asked for request ids and sample ids.
Customer (SynthWorks, Sean Park): Provided trace ids 9f7a2c4 and 9f7a3e1 and confirmed multiple client versions in fleet. Says rolling upgrade to SDK v1.4.1 is planned but would take 48 hours.
SRE (Ethan): Correlated trace ids to ingest-router logs. Noticed proto-decode error pattern and CPU fallback spikes on reranker instances. Hypothesis: Mixed payload encodings (binary vs json) are being routed to consumers that only accept one format; fallback decode path expensive and causes tail-timeouts.
Eng (Maya Li): Asked for minimal repro and suggested quick router tweak to accept both content-types and forward a format-hint header to downstream consumers. Opened PR 1425 to add flexible decoder and added instrumentation.
Support (Priya): Shared temporary mitigation steps with customer: increase rerank client timeout to 2s and enable client retries with idempotent backoff. Customer acknowledged and applied the change; saw drop in 504 rate to 0.1%.
SRE (Ethan): Monitoring shows queue length decreased after client retries; still seeing occasional decode failures for older SDKs. Plan is to deploy patch to ingest-router and a graceful decoder to serving runtime in staging tomorrow.
- Trace 9f7a2c4: embedding payload arrived with Content-Type application/octet-stream and header Embedding-Version: 2026-02; ingest-router forwarded to shard that had JSON-only consumer due to recent rollout mismatch.
- Binary payloads are currently supported, but a recent consumer rollout removed protobuf decoder to optimize for JSON; router lacked content-negotiation enforcement leading to misroutes.
- CPU-decode fallback path in reranker is single-threaded and expensive: observed 120ms median decode vs 6ms for native consumer path under load.
- When fallback spikes, request queue builds and API gateway times out after 900ms (configured).
- Reproduced locally by running mixed-client simulator; adding 10% binary payloads at 150 qps reproduces 504 tail and top-k non-determinism.
- Related to older issue SUP-91455 where embed schema negotiation was flaky across rollout windows.
Workaround applied: Customer increased client timeout and enabled retries, reducing immediate 504s. Engineering action: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings-service/pull/1425 merges a tolerant decoder and router content-negotiation fix. Planned deploy to staging 2026-03-13, canary to prod 2026-03-14 with rate-limited rollout. Post-deploy tasks: rollback plan, run mixed-client soak test, and notify customer when canary reaches 50% of traffic. Follow-up: coordinate SDK deprecation notice for v1.2.0 and add server-side instrumentation to reject clearly incompatible payloads rather than fallback.
