payload.description:
Issue summary: Several ParcelFlow services using a dedicated GPU pool in us-west experienced repeated P99 latency spikes and transient 429/attach-failures starting 2026-03-13 11:20 UTC. The autoscaler initiated multiple rapid scale-ups and subsequent scale-downs (thrash) which led to perceived GPU shortages for customer routes and elevated token costs.

Impact: Customer Production traffic saw p50->p99 latency widening from 120ms -> 2.4s on batched routes; a small percentage (~3%) of requests returned 429s during attach failures. Throughput for the dedicated pool dropped ~30% during the thrash window. Customer reported increased error rates and degraded user experience.

Environment: Dedicated pool d-ed-usw-7 (prod-us-west / us-west-2). Affected routes are batched-generation endpoints pinned to gpt-j-6b and local-rewrite-v2. Autoscaler policy: predictive+reactive hybrid with cooldown 90s, max GPUs 24.

Timeline (observed):
- 11:18 UTC: background snapshot job from tenant TF-88 begins heavy NVMe upload to long-term storage (sidecar storage-proxy).
- 11:20 UTC: storage-proxy IO tail latency increases (NVMe write lat spikes to 400-800ms).
- 11:22 UTC: allocator observes attach latency increase and begins speculative adds; autoscaler scales up 6 GPUs over 4 minutes.
- 11:27 UTC: p99 latency spikes to 2.4s, several attach attempts time out; autoscaler cooldown expires and aggressively scales down when observed queue drains, releasing GPUs.
- 11:30-11:45 UTC: repeating cycle of attach latency -> scale up -> transient drain -> scale down (thrash) ~4 cycles.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) In a dedicated pool, launch a background job that uploads many small checkpoint files through storage-proxy to external NVMe-backed archive while maintaining steady small-batch inference load (1-2 rps per stream).
2) Observe storage-proxy IO tail latencies and allocator attach times.
3) Watch autoscaler decision graph and GPU attach/release events.

Logs and metrics (key links):
- Throughput dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/throughput?pool=d-ed-usw-7
- Autoscaler event log: https://console.redwood.ai/logs/autoscaler?run=2026-03-13
- Storage-proxy NVMe latency graph: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/storage?host=sp-usw-13
- Kernel/driver alerts: linked in investigation notes below.

Observed behaviour:
- High tail IO latency in storage-proxy correlated 1:1 with attach latency spikes.
- Allocator considered GPUs "attached" slower (nvme stall increased attach handshake).
- Autoscaler interpreted rising attach latency and queued requests as capacity pressure, chose to add GPUs; after short drain, it interpreted low utilization and removed GPUs.
- Resulting oscillation produced short periods where there were not enough warmed GPUs (cold starts) and short periods of overprovisioning while background IO recovered.

Customer-facing note prepared: "We have identified an autoscaler feedback loop tied to high storage IO tail latencies from a background checkpointing process. We're investigating mitigations and a short-term workaround to reduce impact."
Initial hypothesis: noisy-neighbor (background checkpoint uploader) caused NVMe write tail which increased storage-proxy latencies. The allocator's attach handshakes rely on low IO latency; prolonged attach times bubbled into autoscaler signals. Autoscaler tuning (short cooldown, aggressive reactive policy) amplified the oscillation.
Actions taken so far:
- Identified offending tenant job using sidecar audit logs (tenant TF-88).
- Temporarily limited TF-88 sidecar upload concurrency via emergency config on sp-usw-13 (reduced tail latencies).
- Increased autoscaler cooldown from 90s -> 180s as a temporary mitigation for d-ed-usw-7.
- Added alloc attach timeout increase to tolerate transient IO blips (short-term).
Next steps:
- Schedule follow-up to evaluate persistent autoscaler policy changes (rate-limits, hysteresis) and improve attach handshake resiliency.
- Work with infra to add QoS to storage-proxy NVMe path to protect inference attach operations from checkpoint upload tail latencies.
- Postmortem to capture long-term mitigations and customer communication plan.

Additional notes:
Workarounds applied: capped background upload concurrency for offending tenant and increased autoscaler cooldown; attach timeout slightly raised. These reduced oscillation frequency and recovered throughput to ~95% of baseline. Long-term fixes pending: storage-proxy NVMe QoS, autoscaler hysteresis tuning, and attach handshake backoff improvements. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-18.
1) Infra to prototype NVMe QoS on sp-usw-13 and partner hosts (owner: Dmitri Ivanov). 2) Autoscaler team to run controlled experiments on hysteresis and cooldown windows (owner: Marco Rivera). 3) CS to coordinate customer timeline and confirm expected behavior (owner: Lena Chen).

2) Observe autoscaler downscaling decisions in dedicated-nyc-a around the same time window
3) Check routing logs: a subset of Nimbus sessions hit rate limit and are routed to fallback smaller-quantized variants

KV-cache growth: observed transient spike in kv-cache entries for the noisy tenant which increased attachment time for subsequent batches (see kv-cache log snippet above).
Scheduler behavior: allocator logs show frequent small-lease grabs from the same tenant which starved larger batchers (allocator lease churn).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers (example: NimbusAI) report unexplained 429 responses during high-volume GraphQL batch ingestion. The Redwood Console shows tenant quota not exhausted and token-level breakdown indicates remaining tokens, but edge returns 429 with no retry-after header in some flows. This appears tied to our new ingress multiplexer (http2 aggregation + sidecar) and the 'annotated-accounting' feature rolled for the dedicated pool last week.

Impact:
- Customer-facing errors for production ingest jobs (binders/QA pipelines) causing partial failure of daily imports.
- Repro rate ~5-10% of batched GraphQL requests during spike windows; when it occurs, many concurrent workers observe repeated 429s and then backoff cascades.

Why this ticket:
Customer requested explanation and immediate mitigation. They are on a dedicated pool and ask for either a hotfix or recommended config to avoid further disruption.
1) Configure a multiplexing GraphQL uploader to send batches of 10–50 operations over a single HTTP/2 connection with header X-Client-Group: <tenant-id>.
2) Ensure the dedicated pool has 'annotated-accounting' enabled (this was enabled on 2026-03-08).
3) Start 200 parallel worker processes each sending batches at 25 rps per worker for 5 minutes.
4) Observe some requests returning 429 from edge (HTTP/2 stream error) while console token counters remain >0 for the tenant.

Example curl (simplified):
curl -v --http2 -H \"Authorization: Bearer <api_key>\" -H \"X-Client-Group: nimbus-prod\" -d @batch.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/graphql
Edge proxy logs (truncated):
2026-03-10T09:12:34.112Z E ingress-mux: stream_split id=0x9f2a client=nimbus-prod parts=4 accounting_mode=annotated
2026-03-10T09:12:34.113Z W rate-limiter: tenant=nimbus-prod token_count=42 refill_window=60s decision=REJECT reason=quota-exhausted (per-route accounting)
2026-03-10T09:12:34.114Z I origin: forward request id=0x9f2a-part0 upstream 200
2026-03-10T09:12:34.115Z I origin: forward request id=0x9f2a-part1 upstream 200
2026-03-10T09:12:34.116Z W ingress-mux: counted-as-multiple id=0x9f2a parts_counted=4

Console metrics snapshot (same minute):
tenant=nimbus-prod total_tokens=1000 tokens_used=958 tokens_remaining=42
per-route tokens (showing origin counts): route=/v1/graphql tokens_used=210
per-connection counts (aggregator view): aggregated_tokens=210

Customer-visible response snippet:
HTTP/2 429
:status: 429
content-type: application/json
{"error":"Too many requests"}

Additional notes:
Reproduced in staging with a dedicated pool mirror and annotated-accounting toggled ON.
- When annotated-accounting=off: no 429s at same load.
- When annotated-accounting=on: intermittent 429s appear and per-part increments are visible in proxy traces.
Token accounting mismatch: edge-level meter increments per internal part; origin-level logs show successful forwards for all parts. The console shows remaining tokens because the aggregator's aggregated counter is updated asynchronously and sometimes lags behind. The rate-limiter (edge) enforces strict token windows and rejects before the aggregated counter reconcile completes.
Root cause (short): ingress-mux iterates parts produced by the batch and calls rate_limiter.claim() for each part without deduping by original_request_id when annotated-accounting enabled. This causes tenant-level token exhaustion during high-concurrency batched uploads.
Related signals: CPU of ingress sidecar spiked 30% during repro; refill-window logs show token_count oscillation (sawtooth) consistent with multiple small claims in same refill period.
Mitigation applied (2026-03-11 03:20 UTC): Turned off annotated-accounting for NimbusAI dedicated pool via control-plane flag rollback (hotfix), which immediately stopped new 429s. Instructed customer to resume jobs; they reported success within 10 minutes.
Root fix merged (2026-03-12): PR https://github.com/redwood/ingress/pull/1987 modifies ingress-mux to attach original_request_id and perform a per-request dedupe before calling rate_limiter.claim(). Also added a unit test for batched requests and an integration test in the rate-limiter suite. PR https://github.com/redwood/rate-limiter/pull/543 adds a short-lived in-memory dedupe cache keyed by original_request_id for the refill window.
Follow-ups:
- INT-2104: Add monitoring alert for 'per-part accounting > aggregated tokens by > 10%' and autopilot to disable annotated-accounting if threshold exceeded.
- Confluence runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ingress-aggregation-accounting-runbook
- Customer billing: Confirm no overage billing for reimbursed rejected requests (CS handling).
Customer communication: Sent incident summary and workaround on 2026-03-11 04:10 UTC. Customer accepted workaround and requested permanent fix timeline; fix deployed to prod 2026-03-12 and verified 2026-03-13.

payload.description:
Customer (Vidorama) reports inconsistent throughput numbers for their Dedicated deployment when using streaming responses.

Issue summary
- Vidorama is comparing:
  1) Redwood Console throughput panel (tokens/sec) for their Dedicated deployment, and
  2) Their internal measurement based on streamed tokens (client-side) + Redwood usage export.
- They see Redwood Console tokens/sec ~1.8–2.1x higher than their client-side computed throughput for the same time windows.
- Discrepancy appears only for streaming (non-streaming requests match within ~5–10%).

Impact
- Customer confusion + concern about Dedicated throughput SLO reporting accuracy.
- Potential false positives/negatives in SLO compliance if the canonical throughput metric is inflated for streaming.

Customer-provided details
- Workload: chat completions, streaming enabled (server-sent events).
- Typical request: prompt 1–2k tokens, completion 150–400 tokens, 20–60 concurrent streams.
- Sampling window: 5-min rolling, comparing against their Prometheus counters.

Redwood initial checks (Support)
- Confirmed customer is hitting the correct deployment_id and region (us-east).
- Confirmed they are not mixing model variants in the comparison window (pinned to llama-3.1-70b-instruct; occasional mixtral bursts were excluded by customer).
- Confirmed they are not counting input tokens in their client throughput metric (they only count generated tokens).

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Run load test against a Dedicated deployment with streaming enabled.
2) Compare:
   - streaming token counter used by throughput dashboard (server-side), vs
   - sum(completion_tokens) from request final usage events (server-side) and/or reconstructed deltas.
3) Observe that for streaming requests, the dashboard-aligned metric increases faster than final usage totals.

Investigation notes (SRE/Obs)
- Hypothesis A: double-counting streamed completion tokens (both per-chunk deltas and final usage event contribute to the same counter).
- Hypothesis B: retries/resumes on stream reconnects cause duplicated deltas.
- Hypothesis C: mixed attribution labels (route vs deployment) cause aggregation overlap.

Findings
- We can reproduce consistent ~2x inflation when streaming is enabled and client consumes the full stream.
- Root cause identified in telemetry emission path:
  - For streaming responses, we emit per-chunk token deltas (used for near-real-time throughput).
  - At stream termination, a final usage event is emitted.
  - In the current pipeline, the dashboard throughput counter was incremented by BOTH the per-chunk deltas and the final usage event for the same request.
- This does NOT affect billing totals (billing uses finalized usage only). It affects the real-time throughput metric used in dashboards and SLO evaluation.

Workaround (until fix rollout)
- For customer reporting, use finalized completion token metrics (request end) for streaming workloads:
  - completion_tokens_total (finalized) / wall time
- Avoid using real-time streaming throughput panel for contractual/SLO comparisons until patched.

Next actions
- Engineering to patch streaming accounting to ensure final usage does not also increment the streaming delta counter (or to separate metrics cleanly).
- Backfill: no backfill planned; we will annotate the dashboard for the affected time range and document the known issue.
- Customer comms: provide written explanation that billing is unaffected; commit to patch timeline and a short validation report post-deploy.

Additional notes:
Resolved by patching streaming token accounting to prevent double-counting (per-chunk deltas + final usage). Deployed to prod/us-east on 2025-03-01 and validated against load tests and customer confirmation. Billing was not impacted. Ticket closed after customer confirmed metrics alignment.
payload.summary: Streaming throughput metric mismatch (customer dashboard vs Redwood export) — suspected token accounting double-count in streaming

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Northbridge Analytics reported increased p95 latency and intermittent 5xx in eu-west immediately after a cache-related optimization config change that was intended to apply to us-east only.
- Initial review indicates the apply operation was mis-scoped: cache toggle was applied to the EU region for the same tenant/model scope.

Impact
- Customer impact: elevated p95/p99 latency (EU traffic) and sporadic 5xx during peak load.
- Duration: ~46 minutes from first alert to rollback completion.
- Blast radius: single tenant (Northbridge Analytics) but affected an unintended region (eu-west).

Environment
- Product: Redwood Dedicated
- Tenant: northbridge-prod
- Model: llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Regions configured: us-east (primary), eu-west (secondary)

Observed behavior
- EU region started returning higher latencies and occasional 5xx shortly after config apply.
- Request traces show cache state mismatch across EU workers (cache enabled with incompatible cache key prefix settings).

Expected behavior
- Region-scoped apply should only modify the explicitly selected region.
- Console summary should accurately reflect blast radius and region targets.

Timeline (UTC)
- 2026-01-08 16:12: Customer reports EU latency regression; Support opens SUP-18503.
- 16:17: SRE confirms elevated p95 in eu-west; notes recent Optimization Config apply event.
- 16:24: Control plane audit trail indicates apply operation targeted us-east, but EU workers fetched new version.
- 16:36: Rollback executed to previous known-good config version.
- 16:58: EU p95 returns to baseline; errors normalize.

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) In Console, select tenant northbridge-prod and model llama-3.1-70b-instruct.
2) Choose region us-east only.
3) Apply optimization config with cache.enable=true and cache.key_prefix updated.
4) Observe that eu-west workers may also fetch the config version if the control plane scope filter is evaluated as (tenant, model) only under certain paths.

Customer-provided notes
- “We did not touch eu-west. Our change request was for US only to validate performance impact.”
- Customer attached request IDs around the onset window (redacted below).

Logs / signals (redacted)
- Gate dashboards: Rollout Health Dashboard shows eu-west p95 jump from ~480ms to ~930ms, 5xx from 0.2% to 1.6%.
- Example request IDs (EU): req_01HTJ9K0… req_01HTJ9K5…
- Runtime logs (EU worker): "opt_cfg_version changed" followed by "cache prefix mismatch" warnings.

Investigation notes
- Hypothesis A: Console applied to wrong region due to UI selection bug.
- Hypothesis B: Control plane apply pipeline wrote scope correctly, but runtime config fetch path ignored region filter under a cache warm path.
- Early findings:
  - Audit event payload indicates target_region=us-east.
  - Runtime in eu-west fetched the new version (same version ID) within ~90 seconds of apply.
  - Console blast radius summary showed “us-east only” (so the display and the operator intent were aligned).

Mitigation
- Immediate: rolled back to prior config version for tenant/model scope and forced refresh of runtime config cache for eu-west workers.
- Short-term: pause further optimization config changes for this tenant until scoping is corrected.

Preliminary root cause
- Mis-scoped propagation path: region scoping was not consistently enforced between apply orchestration and worker fetch/caching.
- Specifically, the runtime config resolver appears to treat "tenant+model" as cache key in one code path; region is not included, allowing eu-west workers to pick up the newest version for that tenant/model.

Follow-up / action items
1) Engineering (Control Plane): ensure region is part of the authoritative scope for version resolution and propagation.
2) Runtime: include region in resolver cache key and add assertion logging when regionless resolution occurs.
3) Console: add server-side confirmation check that the computed blast radius matches the request payload before apply.
4) Observability: annotate charts with config_version + intended_regions and alert when config_version changes in a region not listed in intended_regions.
5) Process: for Dedicated multi-region tenants, require canary-by-region (start with a single region) until safe apply gating is GA.

Notes
- This incident directly aligns with the “Safe apply + rollback mechanism” workstream; mis-scoping is a key risk this project is meant to eliminate.

Additional notes:
Rolled back Optimization Config to prior known-good version and refreshed runtime config cache for eu-west workers. Implemented control-plane guardrail to enforce region in active-version resolution and added diagnostics. Runtime resolver cache-key fix scheduled for release train to prevent regionless propagation.
Customer asked for an explanation they can share internally: “A region-scoping bug caused the EU region to pick up a config version intended for US; rollback restored prior behavior.” Provide audit event excerpts (redacted) if requested. Track prevention work in ENG-4824; consider adding explicit canary-by-region requirement for dedicated multi-region tenants until safe apply gating is GA.
payload.summary: Incorrect cache setting applied to unintended region (EU) during optimization config change intended for US only

Issue summary:
Customers (notably LuminaDocs) reported periodic 502/503 responses from the API during short-lived bursts of high concurrency (10s of requests per second sustained for ~30-90s). Errors are not continuous but spike coincident with traffic surges. Impact: request failures for production traffic, degraded app UX for end users.

Observed behavior:
- 502 and 503 responses returned by api-gateway with upstream error messages referencing broken pipe / connection reset in gateway logs.
- Serving-runtime instances show transient process restarts for a subset of pods during the largest bursts.
- No recent customer-side config changes reported.

Scope: Multiple LuminaDocs routes and a few other enterprise customers in us-east during their scheduled traffic bursts. Not observed in staging.

Initial hypothesis: Connection pooling / keepalive exhaustion at api-gateway or transient runtime OOMs causing process restarts and upstream 502s. Another possibility: ephemeral networking flaps between gateway and serving runtime under bursted load, resulting in upstream reset.

1. Send concurrent generation requests to a redwood-v2-small endpoint at 60 concurrent streams for 60 seconds
2. Observe gateway response codes and serving-runtime pod logs
3. Repeat with progressively lower concurrency to find threshold where 502s cease
Gateway excerpts (us-east):
[03-11T14:03:22Z] api-gateway: upstream response error: connection reset by peer (code 502)
[03-11T14:03:24Z] gateway: upstream closed connection prematurely while reading response
Serving-runtime excerpts:
[03-11T14:03:23Z] runtime-worker: process pid=2345 terminated unexpectedly (signal 9)
[03-11T14:03:23Z] runtime: kv-cache cleanup starting; active sessions dropped: 12
Resource metrics (cluster-autoscaler): CPU spike to 85% on affected nodes, short-lived pod restart count +3 during incident window
[2026-03-11 14:12] Customer (LuminaDocs) - Sarah J: We're seeing this during our indexing job bursts. Request IDs: rID-6a9f, rID-7b2e. Affecting ~8% of requests during the 30-90s windows.
[2026-03-11 14:18] Support - Aisha P: Acknowledged, opening incident. Asking for request IDs and timestamps; adding SRE on call.
[2026-03-11 14:25] SRE - Riley C: Correlating logs and metrics. Noted gateway upstream resets timed with runtime process deaths. Collecting full debug logs and heap profiles from affected runtime pods.
[2026-03-11 15:10] SRE - Riley C: Temporary mitigation applied: rate limit soft-cap for LuminaDocs routes at gateway during bursts; increased idle connection pool size between gateway and runtime. Monitoring for reduction in 502s.
[2026-03-11 18:02] Customer - Sarah J: After the temporary soft-cap we saw error rate drop from ~8% to ~1.2% during a subsequent scheduled burst. Thanks for the quick action.
[2026-03-12 09:20] Support - Aisha P: Marking investigation continuing; planning longer-term fix with runtime team.
[2026-03-12 11:40] Runtime Dev - Lucas M: Reproduced locally with stress harness. Found race in connection teardown handling when process is signalled; patch in review: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123
1) Correlation between gateway upstream 'connection reset' and runtime worker process exits suggests upstream provider side instability rather than pure gateway bug.
2) Heap and thread dumps from affected runtime processes show burst-related memory spike in tokenization path; not sustained OOM but memory pressure triggers kernel OOM-killer on some hosts under constrained node memory settings.
3) Load-balancer health checks did not show node-level failures; pod restarts were single-process only, pointing to in-process crash rather than node failure.
4) Gateway connection pool defaults were insufficient for the burst concurrency pattern (short lived fan-out), leading to connection churn and higher probability of encountering a closing connection.
5) Autoscaler reacted but with delay; node provisioning lag allowed pressure windows where multiple runtime processes experienced reduced available memory.
6) Repro harness: stress-generator run at 70-80 concurrent streams reproduces 502s within 25-40s on similar instance sizes used by LuminaDocs.
Workaround and long-term fixes applied:
- Immediate mitigations (rolled within 1 hour): gateway soft-cap for affected routes, increased idle connection pool and keepalive settings between api-gateway and serving-runtime, temporary bump of pod memory requests for affected node pool. Result: error rate dropped from ~8% to ~1% for subsequent bursts.
- Short-term patch (deployed to canary): updated runtime connection teardown to handle mid-flight resets gracefully (PR #4123).
- Medium-term actions: autoscaler tuning to be more aggressive for sudden fan-out patterns, increase default pod memory on heavy-tokenization models, and add a new alert for rapid spike in upstream connection resets.
- Follow-up: postmortem scheduled; customer will be notified of permanent fix timeline and tested before removing soft-cap.

Schedule postmortem and RCA (owner: Riley C)
Promote runtime PR #4123 to prod after canary validation (owner: Lucas M)
Adjust default gateway connection pool and keepalive config and document for runbook (owner: Networking team)
Tune autoscaler thresholds for short, high-concurrency spikes (owner: Infra)
Run workload replay with LuminaDocs sample traffic to verify stability (owner: Solutions Eng)
Inform LuminaDocs of timeline for permanent fix and arrange follow-up call (owner: CS)
Create alert: >3 upstream connection resets per minute for a given route (owner: Observability)
Review node sizing for tokenization-heavy models (owner: Runtime/Provisioning)

Issue summary: Customer reports repeated streaming chat sessions (SSE) that begin normally but freeze mid-generation after ~30-120s. The client observes no final event and connection remains open; eventually client-side times out. This appears correlated with bursts of 502/504 responses from an edge proxy in front of Redwood’s API and aggressive automatic retries by that proxy.

Impact: Several paid customers on Dedicated capacity experienced degraded UX for long multi-turn chats. Affected customers reported multiple sessions where partial output is delivered then stalls; some sessions recovered after forcing a client reconnect, others required server-side fix. No data exfiltration suspected.

Why this ticket: Customer asked for root cause, mitigation, and permanent fix. Ticket captures investigation and resolution plan.
Partial streaming output for long chats, client-visible stalls, increased support load. Customer reported ~12 impacted sessions across two accounts in the last 48h.
prod | dedicated | us-east (edge-proxy-3) and eu-west (edge-proxy-7)
1) Use a dedicated customer account with reserved capacity and open a long multi-turn SSE chat (>1k tokens).
2) Trigger a response that takes >30s to stream (complex prompt + external tool calls simulated),
3) During streaming, cause transient edge-proxy resource pressure (simulate burst of concurrent requests or apply artificial 502s),
4) Observe that SSE stream delivers some chunks then pauses indefinitely; client stays connected and no final event is emitted.
2026-03-09T14:22:11Z request_id=abc123 worker_id=w-42 proxy=edge-proxy-3 502 upstream_reset

2026-03-09T14:22:11Z request_id=abc123 retried by proxy (X-Retry: 1) -> new connection request_id=abc123-1, server accepted but stream eventually unblocks on worker but client sees no final chunk
2026-03-09T14:22:35Z serving-runtime: kv-cache-lock wait 240ms prior to emit chunk seq=12
2026-03-09T14:22:58Z connection remaining open, no further chunks; client-side heartbeat OK until client timeout at 2026-03-09T14:24:10Z
Initial hypothesis: serving runtime kernel swap or kv-cache eviction causing mid-stream stall. Logs show short cache waits but not long enough to explain full freeze.
Observed correlation: edge-proxy returned 502 for the original upstream connection then attempted an automatic retry. Proxy attaches X-Retry header and opens a new downstream connection with same request semantics.
Race condition found: server-side streaming handler expects a single long-lived connection per request_id. When a proxy retry opens a second connection carrying same idempotency markers, the server forks a second handler for the same logical stream but continues to keep the first stream in a semi-finalized state. Streaming chunks are interleaved; client receives first handler's output then stalls because jittered backpressure and connection pinning hold remaining tokens in the other handler.
Edge-proxy setup: retries for non-idempotent POSTs were enabled for a short window after recent config change to mitigate transient network errors. This is unsafe for streaming endpoints.
Reproducible locally by turning on proxy retry policy against the streaming endpoint; disabling retry restores correct behavior.
Support (Aisha Romero) 2026-03-10: Customer reported multiple sessions freezing mid-stream. Attached client logs and sample request ids. Escalating to SRE.
SRE (Liam Chen) 2026-03-10: Running live capture on edge-proxy-3; saw intermittent 502s followed by proxy-level retries for streaming POSTs. Hypothesis: proxy retries are causing duplicate upstream streams.
Customer (Elena, SynthDesk) 2026-03-11: We see similar behaviour in eu-west. Workaround of forcing client reconnect temporarily helps but hurts UX.
SRE (Liam Chen) 2026-03-11: Applied emergency config rollback on edge-proxy to disable automatic retries for POST /v1/stream endpoints. Monitoring for 6h.
Support (Aisha Romero) 2026-03-12: Customer confirmed significant reduction in incidents after rollback. Requesting a permanent fix and PR for config hardening.
Engineering (Diego Patel) 2026-03-12: Prepared PR to make serving-runtime reject duplicate retry connections for streaming sessions and to use explicit retry token negotiation when safe (https PR linked).
Mitigation applied: disabled automatic retries for POST streaming endpoints at edge proxy and rolled out server-side guard to reject duplicate in-flight retry connections for the same request id. Permanent fix planned: proxy config hardening + serving-runtime PR to unify idempotency negotiation.
Rollback completed 2026-03-11 22:40Z. Serving-runtime change merged to trunk and will be rolled to prod in next canary window (2026-03-14). Customer SynthDesk verified decreased incident frequency and accepted interim mitigation. Follow-up: add automated test simulating proxy retries against streaming endpoints and update runbook.
1) Deploy serving-runtime PR to canary and monitor streaming metrics (rollout 2026-03-14).
2) Add proxy rule to explicitly never retry streaming POSTs and add a unit test for config (owner: edge-proxy team).
3) Update incident runbook and add a detection alert for X-Retry headers appearing on active live streams.
4) Customer outreach: schedule postmortem call with SynthDesk to review timeline and corrective actions.

comments: 2026-03-10T12:05:00Z Marco Reyes: Thanks for the packet capture — confirmed TC=1 and TCP connect resets from your firewall. 2026-03-11T11:02:00Z Marco Reyes: We can provide a temporary toggle on the control plane to relax DNSSEC enforcement for artifact pulls for this deployment. payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent failures retrieving model artifacts and package metadata from S3/CDN from their Private deployment. Error pattern indicates DNS resolution failures for large responses when DNSSEC is enabled and DNS responses are truncated (TC=1). The customer's egress path blocks TCP/53, so DNS cannot fall back to TCP for large/truncated responses. Impact: model pulls fail intermittently, causing cold-start errors and deployment rollbacks in the serving runtime.

Observed behavior: runtime logs show repeated RESOLVE_FAILED errors for asset.hosting.cdn and subsequent model-pull retries that eventually time out. Local dig shows DNS responses with EDNS0 and DO flag set, length > 512 bytes and TC=1. Attempts to open TCP/53 for fallback are blocked by corporate firewall.

Expected behavior: either DNS responses over UDP fit within path MTU (EDNS0 supported) or DNS TCP fallback is allowed so DNSSEC-signed responses can be retrieved and validated. The serving runtime should be able to fetch artifacts reliably without manual intervention from the customer network team.
1) Deploy Private package in customer VPC with default resolver pointing to corporate DNS forwarder.
2) Ensure corporate firewall blocks outbound TCP port 53 and blocks fragmented UDP packets larger than 512 bytes.
3) Enable DNSSEC signing on the authoritative CDN zone used for model artifacts (or use an existing DNSSEC-signed zone).
4) Trigger a model pull for a new model version that references multiple CNAMEs and RRSIG records (this causes large DNS responses).
5) Observe runtime failing to resolve hostnames and model pull eventually timing out with repeated retries.
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T11:22:03Z model-puller: resolve('asset.hosting.cdn') -> timeout after 5s (attempt 1)
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T11:22:08Z model-puller: resolve('asset.hosting.cdn') -> RESOLVE_FAILED: truncated UDP response, tcp fallback attempted
[net-debug] tcpdump: captured UDP DNS response length 1382, flags: DO, TC=1, EDNS0 present
[net-debug] dig +dnssec asset.hosting.cdn @10.10.10.5 -> status: FORMERR; TC=1; attempted TCP connection to 10.10.10.5:53 -> connection refused
[dns-cache] 2026-03-10T11:22:20Z resolver: validation failed: DNSSEC validation could not be completed due to missing response over TCP-53
Customer-provided packet captures show large DNS responses being truncated (TC=1). The corp NGFW drops fragmented UDP payloads and denies outbound TCP 53 per egress policy.
Redwood runtime attempts TCP fallback on truncated UDP responses. Because TCP/53 is blocked, the resolver never receives the full DNSSEC-signed RRset and validation fails. This manifests as repeated model pull retries and eventual fetch timeouts.
SRE replicated in lab by configuring a forwarder to respond with EDNS0 large responses and then blocking TCP/53 on the outbound interface; observed identical failures and runtime error traces.
Related PR https://github.com/redwood/inference-runtime/pull/876 contains telemetry improvements to surface DNS truncation and fallback metrics in console. Linking for visibility.

Additional notes:
As a mitigation we can also temporarily disable strict DNSSEC validation in the private control plane (not recommended long-term).
2026-03-11 09:30 - BrightNova NetOps (customer): We have a corporate policy that blocks TCP/53 egress from host subnets. We'll discuss allowing TCP/53 from only the cluster's resolver IPs. Meanwhile can Redwood disable DNSSEC validation?
2026-03-12 15:40 - SRE (Eve Chen): Lab validation: enabling TCP/53 egress from resolver host eliminated RESOLVE_FAILED. Also validated that configuring forwarder to always do TCP to upstream resolvers (and return A/AAAA answers over UDP within 512 bytes) also succeeds.
Investigating long-term safeguards and customer guidance. Current recommended fix: allow outbound TCP/53 from the customer's DNS forwarder or enable EDNS0/fragmentation pass-through on the NGFW. We provided a temporary control-plane toggle to relax DNSSEC enforcement for artifact fetches for this deployment while customer evaluates firewall change. Scheduled follow-up to audit audit logging and update runbook.
1) Permit outbound TCP/53 from the resolver host(s) to public DNS or Redwood endpoints; OR 2) Configure your DNS forwarder to fetch records over TCP from upstream and synthesize small UDP replies to clients; OR 3) (temporary) Request Redwood to enable DNSSEC-validation-relax toggle on your private control plane until firewall rule change is implemented.
SRE to add console telemetry to flag repeated DNS truncation incidents per deployment (linked PR).
Customer to open change request with NetOps to allow TCP/53 from resolver IPs or adjust NGFW fragmentation rules.
Support to schedule a 1:1 walkthrough with BrightNova NetOps and SRE to verify post-change behavior and remove the temporary DNSSEC relaxation toggle.
Create KB article describing DNSSEC / EDNS0 failure modes and recommended firewall rules for Private deployments.
payload.summary: DNSSEC / EDNS0 truncation with TCP-53 egress blocked causing intermittent model-artifact fetch failures

Issue summary: Customer on a Dedicated pool is seeing intermittent p99 latency spikes and dropped throughput during sustained low-QPS workloads. Impact: Customer reports 20-35% throughput reduction across pinned routes during two daily windows. Environment: prod us-east-1 dedicated pool assigned to DocuSense (reserved capacity).
1) Route steady low QPS traffic with long-lived streaming sessions (keepalives every 60s) to the dedicated pool. 2) Maintain a handful (10-30) of long-lived sessions with occasional 1-2 token heartbeats. 3) Observe attach times and allocator HBM reservations during the window. Expected: stable attach and autoscale behavior; Observed: prolonged attach, P99 spikes, autoscaler failing to add slots in time.
Relevant traces pulled from grafana: grafana.redwood/internal/dashboards/attach-latency?from=2026-03-09T08:00Z&to=2026-03-10T20:00Z; example error: "slot attach wait > 12s" repeated; allocator logs show repeated HBM reservation entries and delayed lease returns. Metric snapshot: attach_time.p99 spike to 9.8s, pool_alloc_free_slots down by 30% during event windows.
Initial triage (2026-03-10): Observed correlation between long-lived sessions and HBM reserved memory not released promptly after session idle periods. Hypothesis A: long-lived sessions are holding small persistent KV caches and HBM reservations that block slot reuse leading to effective capacity shrink. payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (AcmeAI, dedicated) reports intermittent stream terminations during long completions. Sessions frequently end with client-side 499 or server-side 504/502 after ~65–120s. This started after the customer rolled a telemetry agent that attaches rotating X-Baggage headers every 10s and issues repeated small chunked POST uploads from their SDK.

Impact:
- Customer sees ~8–12% of long streaming responses fail after ~1–2 minutes.
- Affects production inference for mid-long completions (context lengths >2k).
- User-facing: truncated outputs, retries, and higher token cost.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted endpoint: prod us-east-1, api-gateway -> ALB -> edge-proxy -> serving pool.
- Customer using dedicated capacity pool behind private routing.
- Observed on models: open/ggml-transformer-xl-13b and redwood/llm-internal-compat.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a streaming generate request with a long prompt (approx 2k tokens context).
2) From the client, send the request body in many small chunked writes (client flush every 20–60ms).
3) Every 8–12s the client rotates a large instrumentation header (X-Inst-Baggage ~1.2kB each, cumulative on path due to proxy sticky connection).
4) Wait for streaming completion; intermittently fail between 65–120s with client 499 or server 504.

Observed behaviour / logs (excerpts):
- Edge proxy logs (us-east-edge-22) show repeated Nagle/coalescing behavior and large header frame growth; many connections show "deferred_flush=true" and "idle_write_timeout=65s" annotations.
- ALB access logs: several requests show status_code=504, target_status_code=-1, elapsed_time ~72.45s.
- Customer SDK trace: socket hangup after long silence then immediate reconnect.
- Serving runtime shows no obvious backend OOM; KV-cache warmup completed for affected sessions.

Initial hypothesis:
- The edge proxy (sidecar) is coalescing small client writes into larger buffers and deferring flushes to optimize TCP throughput. When header baggage rotates, the proxy's per-connection header table grows or triggers additional internal buffering which increases time-to-first-byte (TTFB) on warm streams. This interacts with ALB/edge idle-send timeouts and results in mid-stream resets once an idle threshold is hit.
- Alternatively, ALB/NGINX connection-level write stalls due to header/table growth (HTTP/2 HPACK pressure) cause the upstream to consider the connection idle and close it.

Investigation performed so far:
- Reproduced a failure in staging using a synthetic client that mimics small-chunk writes + header rotation; saw similar 504 after ~68s.
- Capture of tcpdump and http2 frames at edge-proxy showed long periods of no outgoing bytes from proxy toward ALB despite incoming client chunks being accepted.
- Increased ALB timeouts in a test harness prevented the 504, confirming timeout sensitivity.
- Temporary mitigation via customer SDK: batching client writes into larger chunks eliminated the failure in repro.

Workarounds suggested to customer:
- Short-term: batch client-side flushes to reduce coalescing artifacts (send at least 2–4KB per write).
- Reduce frequency/size of rotating instrumentation headers; send them as a single stable header if possible.
- If on dedicated, request routing to a different edge pool (we rotated the pool for one session and saw improvement).

Next steps / action items:
- SRE to review edge-proxy flush heuristics and evaluate disabling deferred flush for streaming endpoints. (Assignee: Jared Collins)
- Infra to add a short-lived ALB timeout increase test across a sample of affected customers and monitor for regressions. (Assignee: Ops)

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 Support (Maya): Applied temporary routing to alternate edge pool for customer. They reported immediate reduction in failures from ~10% to ~1% for an hour.
2026-03-14 Customer (AcmeAI - Todd Rivera): We've applied client batching and reduced header churn; will monitor for 48 hours and report back. Thank you for the quick rotation to alternate pool.
Repro in staging confirms timing window ~65–75s before ALB emits 504 when proxy defers writes.
HPACK table growth and repeated header rotations increase internal proxy memory accounting and appear to delay actual wire writes to ALB.
No evidence of backend model OOM or serving-runtime CPU starvation during repro.
Increasing ALB idle timeout alleviates but does not address root cause; will need proxy change to guarantee streaming liveness.
SRE to coordinate with infra/network to test edge-proxy config toggle on canary set first.
In progress: temporary mitigation is client batching and header stabilization. Pending edge-proxy config change and canary rollout. Follow-up: add streaming endpoint tag to bypass deferred flush optimization; monitor for throughput regressions post-rollout.
ENG-Infra: implement edge-proxy toggle to disable deferred flush for streaming endpoints (owner: Jared Collins)
SRE: run 48h canary with 5% of nodes toggled, measure TTFB and overall throughput (owner: Linh Tran)
DX: update SDK guidance about batching and header size for streaming clients (owner: Priya Menon)
payload.summary: Edge proxy defers flush during repeated small client-chunks and rotated metadata; long streaming completions drop with 499/504

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightWrite (enterprise) reports progressive slowdown of SSE streaming responses during long-chat sessions originating from their web client behind a corporate load balancer. After ~20–60s of normal token stream, chunk cadence degrades (increasing inter-chunk latency) and ultimately the stream stops sending data for 10–30s before the connection is closed by the client. This is not an immediate 5xx; it looks like a gradual drift in throughput leading to a silent stall and client timeout.

Impact: Multiple active sessions from BrightWrite saw interrupted chat generation in prod us-east. Reported as user-visible partial replies and increased perceived latency. Customer has traffic routed through an internal LB that reuses upstream connections (connection reuse/keepalive). Estimated 12 sessions per minute affected during peak.

Environment: prod us-east; Redwood hosted API (api.redwood.ai) -> internal edge proxy -> ALB (customer) -> customer web clients (multiplexed SSE tabs). Affected models: redwood-llama-13b-v2 and fallback quantized 7b variant.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Use BrightWrite web client with SSE streaming enabled and long system+user prompt (> 2500 tokens).
2) Ensure client sessions are multiplexed (multiple tabs) and routed through their corporate LB that does connection reuse.
3) Observe normal streaming for ~20–60s, then token emission rate drops progressively and eventually the stream goes silent.
4) Client times out and reconnects, sometimes resuming with a new session but losing prior in-flight context.

Observed behavior:
- Inter-chunk delay grows from ~50–200ms to multiple seconds before stream silence.
- No immediate 5xx from Redwood; upstream edges show continuous TCP keepalive but little application-level bytes.
- Customer-side LB logs show backend connection persistent with occasional zero-byte writes; LB reports 'http downstream keepalive reused' around same timestamps.
- When customer repro from outside their LB (direct to Redwood edge), issue is much less frequent.

Expected behavior: steady token cadence until generation completes or server closes normally.

Attachments/logs:
- Customer-provided client-side trace (x-request-id: rw-req-8b3f-20260310)
- Edge request logs: https://logs.redwood.company/edge/rw-req-8b3f-20260310
- Sample server-side token-delay histogram (attached as snippet in comments)

Notes: This differs from a plain mid-token abort or instant disconnect; the failure profile looks like gradual resource throttling or buffer coalescing somewhere in the request path.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 16:02 BrightWrite (Elena Park): Confirmed enabling 'proxy_preserve_chunked' reduced incidents in canary environment. Will schedule a config change to prod later today. Asked if Redwood can implement server-side mitigation for clients where changing LB is not possible.
Reproduce notes: Local repro succeeded only when client path included a proxy that reuses keepalive connections and aggregates small writes (mimic customer LB behavior). Direct connections rarely reproduce.
Metrics observed:
- Token_emit_latency: median increased from 60ms -> 1.8s during incidents.
- Edge pod kernel retransmit spike correlated with stream silence windows.
- No increase in runtime OOMs or worker crashes. Scheduler evictions were not elevated.
Hypotheses considered:
- Serving runtime backpressure gating due to KV cache locks: disproved (no KV lock logs).
- Worker GC spike causing pause: disproved (GC traces normal).
- Proxy/LB socket buffer coalescing (likely): supported by customer config change result.
- HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 or ALPN negotiation mismatch causing intermittent buffering: under investigation; customer uses HTTP/1.1 for SSE.
Temporary mitigation validated: Customer setting 'preserve_chunked: true' on LB reduced frequency from ~15% sessions to <1% in canary. This strongly implicates proxy-level aggregation.
Next steps:
- INT-44122: Implement server-side keepalive NOPs for streaming SSE when small-token pattern detected. Target: canary patch 2026-03-18.
- Add runtime heuristic to detect downstream proxy aggregation and switch to larger chunk writes.
- SRE to add alert for token_emit_latency 95th percentile crossing 800ms for SSE endpoints.
Partial workaround provided to customer: change LB setting to preserve chunked responses (confirmed canary improvement). Server-side mitigations planned: (1) runtime patch to emit periodic small NOP SSE events every 8s when token cadence drops; (2) heuristic to coalesce token writes into larger app-level writes when downstream proxy reuse is detected. INT-44122 created to track runtime work. Customer agreed to defer full rollout until after their maintenance window.
Customer instructed to enable chunked-preserve mode on LB or adjust keepalive reuse timeout. Alternative: client can reconnect with resume token after 10s silence (client-side).
INT-44122 - runtime change to emit periodic SSE NOPs (target canary 2026-03-18)
SRE: add token_emit_latency alert for SSE endpoints (threshold p95 800ms)
Postmortem if incidents reoccur at scale - link pending

Issue summary: When a customer opens the Console dashboard "Redwood API - Usage by client_id' and expands the timeframe beyond 14 days (e.g., 30d or 90d), multiple dimension series (client_id / route) disappear from the stacked breakdown. Impact: GreenPath AI reports that their monthly billing and SLA dashboards undercount unique clients by ~18% when using 30d range. Environment: prod (us-east), observed across multiple orgs but reproduced with GreenPath account. Steps to reproduce: 1) Open Console > Dashboards > 'Redwood API - Usage by client_id'. 2) Select time range 7d: all client_id series present. 3) Switch to 30d: top client series remain, medium/low-volume client_id series vanish. 4) Inspect raw events export for same timespan -> events present for vanished client_ids. Expected: Dimension breakdown should show series for all client_ids with nonzero activity (subject to sampling threshold). Actual: Several client_id series are missing from the visualization for ranges >14d despite raw events showing activity. Observations / logs: - Dashboard query id: q-ff72c3a - Raw event export (CSV) attached by customer shows ~120 distinct client_ids for 30d window. Console breakdown shows ~45 series. - Query profiler shows fallback to rollup index (rollup_v2) for ranges >14d. - Timeseries-store compaction run logs around 2026-03-09 show rollup job 'rollup_v2:topk' executed with top_k=50. - Slack thread: #support-greenpath link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C07SUPPORT/p1652xxxx - Customer impact: Monthly reporting and billing alerts are undercounted, causing finance/CS tickets.

Please triage to analytics/runtime team; customer needs a short-term workaround and long-term fix.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 CS (Ethan Li): Communicated interim workaround to GreenPath: use raw events export for full cardinality and switch dashboard timeframe to <=14d for accurate per-client breakdown until fix is deployed.
2026-03-13 Product (Anika Bose): Requested product decision on default top_k for rollups and whether 'other' should be expanded-by-default or collapsed.
Hypothesis 1: Rollup aggregator uses a top_k selection during compaction that discards low-volume dimension values, and the console UI does not render the 'other' bucket for breakdown charts. Evidence: rollup logs show top_k=50; raw export shows >120 distinct keys.
Hypothesis 2: Query router switches to rollup index for any range >14d; mismatch between rollup binning/aggregation window and UI's chart points causes missing intermediate series when series fall below per-bucket threshold.
Repro steps executed in staging: replayed 45m of production-like traffic -> reproduced missing series for 30d view. Adjusting rollup top_k to 200 restored series in staging.
Telemetry: Add a gauge to dashboard queries to emit whether result came from 'raw' or 'rollup' index and the rollup top_k value used. This will speed triage for future reports.
SRE note: Compaction re-run for affected orgs resolved majority of cases; global hotfix needed to prevent recurrence as compaction job resets to default top_k during upgrades.
Workaround: SRE re-ran rollup compaction with top_k=200 for GreenPath's orgs and invalidated dashboard caches; CS shared raw-export workflow for full cardinality checks. Long-term fix: (1) Increase default rollup top_k to 200 and make it configurable per-org, (2) change Console breakdown charts to render an 'other' bucket instead of dropping series, and (3) add telemetry flag for rollup vs raw source. GH PR #4721 implements UI change and telemetry; rollup default change requires infra deploy + migration steps. Planned timeline: hotfix UI rollout (canary on 2026-03-15); infra change planned for 2026-03-22 after migration runbook. Follow-up task: INT-430 (rollup migration runbook) created.

Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 10:40 UTC we have received multiple reports from EU customers (notably Inkwell Analytics) of high tail latency and request timeouts for text-generation and streaming responses. Impact: A subset of requests from eu-west were being routed to us-east (round-trip +120ms) causing queueing in serving runtime and SDK-level timeouts for streaming sessions. Environment: prod (eu-west); affected customers primarily enterprise tier. Timeline: 10:35 - spike begins; 10:40 - first customer report; 10:52 - alerting hit p1 threshold; 11:05 - mitigation pinned region routing; 11:20 - partial recovery for pinned routes; 12:00 - continued investigation. Observed behavior: large fraction of streaming sessions fail with: SDK error: "read timeout after 120s" and gateway 504s when backend token generation exceeded 110s. Cross-region latency correlated with a peering degradation reported by cloud provider in eu-west peering fabric. This ticket captures support engagement, investigation notes, and mitigation steps.
1) From an eu-west client, send a streaming chat request to /v1/chat/stream with rw-chat-3.0 and typical prompt (~800 tokens).
2) Observe SDK stream open then long silence; client eventually receives timeout at 120s or sees partial tokens then disconnect.
3) Check request routing headers X-Region-Routed-To and X-Routing-Policy in logs; observed value: us-east for affected requests.
4) Correlate with smart-router decisions in routing logs and with api-gateway connection traces to confirm cross-region proxied connections.
2026-03-12T10:42:11Z gateway[req-9a3d]: routed request region=eu-west -> target=us-east (route_policy=latency_fallback) ttl=30s
2026-03-12T10:42:13Z smart-router[decision]: evaluated peers: eu-edge-12 healthy=false last_check=00:20:07; selected us-edge-3 score=0.72
2026-03-12T10:44:55Z runtime[serve-42]: token-gen start id=req-9a3d latency_probe=0.0
2026-03-12T10:46:37Z runtime[serve-42]: token-gen long-tail: rpc to us-east backend RTT=128ms queue-wait=88s -> 504 threshold exceeded
2026-03-12T11:02:10Z sdk-client[inkwell]: stream disconnected with error: read timeout after 120s
Initial hypothesis: smart-router fallback to us-east due to transient eu-west peering health check failures (cloud provider reported BGP flaps).
Checked smart-router health checks: multiple eu-west edge peers marked unhealthy simultaneously; health-check interval set to 15s, but TTL for peer negative caching was 30s leading to over-eager failover.
Observed mismatch: routing rollout (PR #187) changed the fallback scoring weights last week and reduced locality bias; combination of health-check flaps and lower locality weight caused bulk reroute.
Metric correlation: spike in cross-region egress and RPC SLO violations coincident with peering event logged by provider (see provider status page).
Reproducibility: can reproduce by forcing eu-edge peers to 'unhealthy' in staging smart-router and observing routing to us-east and increased RTTs; confirms routing decision path.
2026-03-12 10:50 UTC - Inkwell support: "We're seeing many streaming sessions drop and SDK timeouts, impacting customer demos. Can you confirm region is eu?"
2026-03-12 11:10 UTC - Inkwell support: "Partial recovery observed after 11:05 but still seeing increased latency for some requests. Please advise on mitigation and ETA for root cause fix."
At 11:05 UTC ops pinned routing policy for enterprise customers in eu-west to prefer in-region endpoints and increased health-check sensitivity to avoid blackholing on brief flaps. Added temporary rate-limit exemptions for affected customer to reduce retry storms.
Temporary: pinned eu-west routes for enterprise customers and rolled back upstream routing weight change (PR #187) that reduced locality bias. Permanent: schedule change to health-check negative caching TTL and add continuous test that simulates peering flaps to validate routing behavior. Follow-up task created to harden smart-router scoring algorithm (INT-412).
Customers recovered to baseline by 11:25 UTC after pinning. Post-incident, we will deploy: 1) revert routing weight change in production (done 2026-03-12 11:45 UTC), 2) lower negative-cache TTL to 5s for edge peer health, 3) add canary that simulates transient peer failure. Owner: Maya Patel / Networking team.
Schedule code rollback verification for routing PR #187 in staging (owner: infra-team).
Create automated integration test for peering flaps in CI (owner: SRE).
Contact cloud provider to request postmortem for the eu-west peering anomaly and retain their timeline (owner: Partnerships).
Communicate summary and RCA draft to Inkwell and impacted customers (owner: CS - Nora Vega).

Issue summary:
Solara Financial needs an on-demand, ordered SIEM export for a regulatory evidence package covering a 48-hour window. They require cryptographically verifiable per-event offsets, a resume token to continue incomplete transfers, and a redaction-log CSV that maps event IDs to applied redaction rules.

Impact:
Customer cannot produce legally defensible evidence for a compliance request. Requested window contains ~12M events across two regions (us-east, eu-west). Customer reports missing sequence continuity in delivered archives and asks for proof-of-delivery for each transfer.

Customer request / desired deliverables:
- Hourly ordered export archives (gzip+parquet) with monotonically increasing sequence offsets and per-file SHA256 manifest.
- A signed per-tenant delivery manifest (ed25519) that includes resume_token, earliest_offset, latest_offset, and file-level checksums.
- Redaction log CSV with event_id, redaction_rule_id, redaction_explanation, and timestamp applied.
- Short-term replayable bundle for 2026-03-09 00:00 to 2026-03-11 00:00 (UTC) delivered to their S3 bucket under their KMS key.

Environment / context:
- Customer uses dedicated plan (enterprise).
- Exports configured via Console -> Integrations -> SIEM Bridge (ordered mode).
- Delivery target: solara-prod-reports (customer-managed S3) in us-east; fallback mirror in eu-west.
- KMS: customer key alias/solara-prod-key (cross-account key policy).

Steps to reproduce / verify (for internal use):
1) Trigger on-demand export for the target window via Console export UI or /exports API.
2) Observe job orchestration logs and manifest generator pipeline in Logs -> export-run-%Y%m%d.
3) Validate produced manifest JSON contains resume_token and file checksums and that per-file offsets are contiguous.
4) Attempt S3 put to customer bucket; verify PutObject permissions and encryption headers.

Logs / attachments provided by customer:
- s3-error-403-put.txt (from their S3 audit showing AccessDenied for eu-west mirror).
- sample_manifest_partial.json (manifest generated with two missing file entries).
- redaction_sample.csv (partial mapping uploaded by customer).

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 08:33 - Security (Harpreet Kaur): Reviewed signed manifest format; require insertion of redaction-log digest into manifest before finalizing for legal audit. Marked follow-up in infra PR.
Initial hypothesis: orchestration generator retries are being cut short by 30s task-level timeout for cross-region reconciliation (seen in export-run logs), leading to incomplete file lists. Secondary factor: cross-account KMS key policy in eu-west prevents PutObject with SSE-KMS by our service principal, resulting in 403s and missing mirror files. Evidence: export-run-20260311.log shows generator loop exit at 00:23:51 UTC with 'timeout: reconcile-segments'; sample_manifest_partial.json missing entries for hourly files 03:00-04:00 eu-west. payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated request timeouts and 5xx failures when sending deep priming + large max_tokens (token budgets >= 150k). Unlike typical KV-eviction stalls, failures are concentrated at the finalization phase: final chunk generation either times out (504) or the connection is closed with upstream 503. Impact: Several production pipelines at GlyphAnalytics (dedicated pool) have had daily failures during long-document summarization jobs, causing missed SLA windows and requeue storms.

Environment: prod: us-east, dedicated capacity pool 'glyph-dedicated-1', request pattern: multi-part streaming (chunk_size 4096) with max_tokens set to 120000-200000, average input context ~75k tokens.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Upload a 70k token priming document via our chunked priming API.
2. Issue a generation request with max_tokens=150000 and stream=true.
3. Observe normal token emission for ~95% of the run.
4. During finalizer step (last 5-10% of tokens) request stalls then either returns 504 or the connection resets with upstream 503.

Observed behavior: repeated finalizer-phase timeouts; stack traces in runtime logs show worker stuck waiting on finalizer queue priority and a later preemption of the streaming task. Expected behavior: finalizer completes within configured finalizer_timeout and stream remains connected for entire emission.

Initial logs (redacted):
- serving-runtime WARN [2026-03-10T18:12:43Z] finalizer: queue_wait=38.4s priority=low -> promoted=false
- scheduler ERROR [2026-03-10T18:12:57Z] worker-23: upstream 503 connection reset during finalize
- proxy INFO [2026-03-10T18:13:01Z] streaming-conn-451: client EOF after 1.3s of inactivity

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support increased finalizer concurrency on glyph-dedicated-1 (small Bump) and set finalizer_timeout to 120s; customer reports fewer failures but still sees intermittent resets on the largest budgets.
- Advised customer to split jobs into smaller max_tokens windows as a workaround.

Investigation notes (Eng):
- Hypothesis A: priority inversion between streaming emission tasks (high I/O) and finalizer tasks (CPU/serialization) allows high-priority streaming to be preempted by unrelated batch work; when finalizer wakes it finds streaming connection closed.
- Hypothesis B: KV cache flush/serialization at very large sequence lengths causes blocking I/O from storage layer while scheduler holds token-emitter slots, resulting in apparent finalizer stall.
- Collected traces show scheduler context switches around finalizer wakes and a correlation between long GC/serialization events and connection resets.
- Trace link: https://sentry.internal.redwood.ai/issue/9876 (redacted)

Next steps:
1) Run targeted repro on dedicated repro cluster with identical capacity and input sizes (owner: eng-repro team).
2) Add telemetry to finalizer queue for priority/promotions and measure time-in-queue per request.
3) Try a patch to temporarily bias finalizer tasks to higher real-time priority in the scheduler and validate if failure rate drops.
4) If confirmed, schedule a controlled rollout of priority-fix with feature flag and monitor.

Customer impact and follow-up:
- Customer is on a dedicated contract; CS has escalated to enterprise support. They require a postmortem and a timeline for a permanent fix.
- Proposed interim SLA concession: credit for failed jobs during investigation window (customer agreed to credits pending resolution).
Priya Raman (Support) [2026-03-10]: Opened after customer reported recurring 504s on long summarization runs. Assigned to Eng triage.
Elena Novak (SRE) [2026-03-10]: Increased finalizer concurrency and extended finalizer_timeout to 120s for glyph-dedicated-1 as a stop-gap. Customer confirmed partial improvement but still seeing failures on >150k budgets.
Dan Park (Serving Eng) [2026-03-11]: Reproduced partial stall in repro cluster; observed priority inversion where finalizer tasks stayed in low-priority queue for ~30s while emitter threads yielded. Collecting more scheduler traces. Linked PR for instrumentation: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4387.
GlyphAnalytics (Customer) [2026-03-11]: Provided sample job and agreed to try splitting into two sequential runs as temporary workaround. Asked for ETA on permanent fix and postmortem.
Elena Novak (SRE) [2026-03-12]: Proposed steps to bias scheduler for finalizers behind feature flag; testing under load tomorrow. Noted dependency on storage team for KV serialization metrics.
payload.summary: Priority inversion causing finalization timeouts and request failures on very large token budgets

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that several admin users in their private VPC are seeing 403s when calling the admin routes of the Redwood control plane. Authentication succeeds (SAML assertion is accepted) but the request is treated as unauthenticated for RBAC and falls back to minimal privileges.

Impact:
- ~12 users in Nimbus Health's admin group unable to access control plane admin endpoints (create/modify deployments, view audit logs).
- Production control plane operations for Nimbus are impaired; customer has manual escalation to platform team.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) in prod/us-west.
- Identity Provider: Shibboleth (SAML 2.0).
- Redwood private control plane version: 2025.11.3 (auth-proxy 1.4.2, rbac-syncer 2.0.1).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1. Log in via SSO as a user in the Nimbus-admin role (example: alice@nimbushealth.org).
2. Call GET /admin/deployments with valid session cookie.
3. Observe 403 and RBAC audit entry showing subject='user:anonymous' or role_bindings=[] .

Observed logs / traces (redacted):
- SAML assertion extracted attributes: eduPersonScopedAffiliation=["member@staff.nimbushealth.org", "employee%40nimbushealth.org@realm"]
- auth-proxy debug: "parsed_affiliations=[\"member\", \"employee%40nimbushealth.org\"]"
- rbac-syncer: "no role bindings found for subject 'employee' (missing domain)"
- application audit: "authorization denied; subject resolved to user:anonymous"

Initial hypothesis:
- The IdP is sending eduPersonScopedAffiliation values that contain an encoded '@' and/or an explicit scoped domain (e.g., user@tenant). Our parser in auth-proxy appears to split on '@' and take the left-hand side only, dropping the tenant portion. Nimbus's role bindings are scoped to the full scoped-affiliation (domain included), so dropping the domain causes a mismatch and no roles are assigned.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- SAML assertion (redacted) attached to ticket (file: saml_assertion_alice_2026-03-09.xml).
- Timeline of affected users (csv).

Immediate customer workaround requested:
- Allowlist affected user certificates for a temporary bypass OR add explicit RBAC user mapping for the truncated username. Customer prefers server-side fix in Redwood to avoid manual mappings for multiple users.

Requested next steps from Support:
- Confirm whether the parser behavior is intended.
- If bug, propose patch for auth-proxy that preserves scoped portion of eduPersonScopedAffiliation when mapping to role bindings OR make mapping configurable.
- Provide short-term mitigation steps customers can apply in private control plane to restore admin access.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:05 - SRE (Liam Park): Verified that adding a temporary role-binding for the truncated subject name restores access. Warned that this is not scalable. Recommending a change to preserve full scoped value or make a mapping table configurable in rbac-syncer.
Reproduced locally with auth-proxy 1.4.2 using the provided SAML assertion. Parser used regex /([^@]+)@.*/ and returned only the first capture group. This causes 'employee%40nimbushealth.org@realm' -> 'employee%40nimbushealth.org' then an additional decode step yields 'employee@nimbushealth.org' but subsequent domain-splitting step removes '@nimbushealth.org', leaving 'employee'.
Unit test added: tests/saml_affiliation_parsing_test.rb reproduces the exact failing assertions. Failure triggered when encoded '@' is present inside local part.
rbac-syncer fetches role_bindings by exact-match on subject id (scoped value). Because parser strips scope, lookup fails and fallback to anonymous occurs.
Checked changelog: normalization changes landed in auth-proxy release 1.4.0 (2025-10) that adjusted decoding order. Regression likely introduced during reorder.
Create explicit role_bindings for the truncated usernames in customer's private control plane (rbac table) until patch is applied.
Alternatively, configure the identity provider to emit a separate attribute (e.g., edupersonPrincipalName) that maps cleanly to username without encoding; Redwood can be updated to read that attribute if customer prefers.
Support can provide a script to bulk-create role-bindings from the provided CSV of affected users.
PR review and CI green: merge fix for auth-proxy to preserve full scoped affiliations (refer to PR #487).
Build and release patched private control plane package (target: 2026-03-16).
Coordinate maintenance window with Nimbus Health for upgrade; provide rollback instructions.
After release, verify affected users can access admin endpoints and confirm role bindings are resolved automatically.
Post-incident: update SSO troubleshooting runbook and add a note about eduPersonScopedAffiliation parsing quirks.
payload.summary: IdP eduPersonScopedAffiliation parser truncates scoped values, resulting in missing RBAC bindings for private VPC users

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers observe occasional requests from BrightMaps, pinned to eu-west, routing out via us-east for a small window when their 'sticky pin' TTL expires. Impact: transient p95 latency spikes (~650-900ms) and unexpected cross-region egress charges.

Impact:
- BrightMaps reported increased latency for interactive chat during peak times, affecting UX and SLOs for EU traffic.
- They see additional egress billing lines attributable to US region in invoices for the same time windows.

Environment:
- Customer workspace: brightmaps-prod
- API usage: hosted Redwood API (production) calling model redwood/gptj-6b-v2 pinned to eu-west with pin_ttl=3600s and strict_residency=false

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Create a pinned session to eu-west with pin_ttl set to 3600s.
2) Send sustained low-rate traffic for ~1 hour.
3) Observe around the TTL expiration boundary some requests route to us-east for 10-30s before returning to eu-west.
4) Note latency and check invoice for egress during those windows.

Observed logs/traces (examples provided by customer):
- trace: trace-eu-0a7b3 (2026-03-09T14:12:58Z) p95 820ms route: eu-west -> us-east -> eu-west
- trace: trace-eu-0a7b9 (2026-03-09T15:12:59Z) p95 680ms route: eu-west -> us-east

Customer ask:
- Why did traffic leave eu-west at the TTL boundary?
- Is this expected behavior for pin expiry?
- Can we avoid cross-region egress and the associated cost/latency when a pin expires?

Notes: customer is enterprise and requests both an explanation and a mitigation that doesn't require major architectural changes on their side.
Pin model to eu-west with pin_ttl=3600s and strict_residency=false
Run low-rate sustained traffic for >1 hour
Watch for TTL boundary (every 3600s) and capture traces and headers
Inspect routing decisions and billing egress for the observed timestamps
Initial triage (support): confirmed customer's traces show a short window where requests were routed to us-east. Hypothesis: when a sticky pin expires, smart-routing evaluates capacity and may pick a fallback region; because strict_residency=false, fallback policy allows cross-region selection to satisfy latency/capacity SLOs.

Engineering triage 2026-03-11 (Marco): reviewed router logs and route decision traces. Found that at TTL boundary the edge cache entry for the pin sometimes lags flush by ~5-20s on a small subset of edge nodes. During that lag, the routing decision treats the request as "unpinned" and applies region preference scoring; if us-east had slightly better immediate capacity score, the router issued a temporary route to us-east. Once the pin re-synchronizes (cache rebuild from control plane), subsequent requests return to eu-west.

We also found the control-plane TTL and edge cache TTL were not perfectly aligned for a few customers due to staggered configuration propagation introduced in a recent rollout (PR 4523). The billing records show cross-region egress for the matched timestamps.

Logs/IDs reviewed:
- router-node-7 logs (2026-03-09T14:12:58Z) request-id=rq-0a7b3 matched trace-eu-0a7b3
- control-plane publish event publish-id=pub-1189 for pin update at 2026-03-09T14:12:55Z

Severity assessment: customer-visible latency spike and unexpected egress cost = customer impact. Marking Sev1 and P1.
BrightMaps (Customer): We see a 10-30s window where p95 jumps and our invoice shows US egress. Can you explain?

Additional notes:
BrightMaps: We need a workaround we can apply quickly. Long TTL isn't ideal for our use case because we want some churn.
Marco: Short-term workaround: set strict_residency=true on the pin to forbid fallback to other regions. Alternatively, increase pin_ttl slightly (e.g., +30s) to avoid hitting edge-control boundary during churn windows. We're working on a server-side fix to align TTLs and add routing guard checks.
In progress: temporary workarounds shared with customer (strict_residency=true or extend pin_ttl by buffer). Engineering change planned: ensure control-plane publish completes before edge cache eviction by adding a pre-eviction guard and a metric to surface pin-expiry misalignments. Target PR created: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4523. Planned rollout: canary 2026-03-15, full rollout 2026-03-18 if canary shows no regressions. Billing team will review impacted invoices after fix. Customer offered monitoring dashboard for pin-expiry anomalies.
Assigned to Marco Hernandez for engineering fix. Action items:
- [ENG] Add pre-eviction check in edge cache (PR 4523)
- [ENG] Add metric and alert for pin-expiry misalignment
- [SUPPORT] Offer customer immediate flag strict_residency toggle and advise on pin_ttl buffer
- [BILLING] Correlate and, if validated, credit the egress for windows impacted by this bug (pending internal review)
- [DOCS] Update routing FAQ to document pin expiry behavior and recommended best practices
payload.summary: Sticky pin expiry triggers short cross-region egress with p95 latency spike and billing question

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer Nimbus Payments reports intermittent multi-second p95/p99 spikes and occasional request timeouts for streaming completions originating from their us-east tenant when routed to ap-southeast-1 model pools. Impacts mostly streaming responses (chunked / event-stream) where token emission pauses for 2–8s before resuming or times out after 30s.

Impact:
- Several customer production requests saw elevated tail latency affecting payment UI flows.
- Observed increased number of aborted streams and retry traffic from client SDK.
- Customer reported revenue-impacting failures for a small subset of flows.

Environment:
- Customer: Nimbus Payments (dedicated tenant on Redwood Dedicated).
- Affected model pools: ap-southeast-1 serving for redwood-compat-7b and open-llm-chat-13b.
- Traffic path: requests originated from us-east control plane -> egress transit VPC -> ap-southeast-1 serving nodes.

Steps to reproduce (customer-facing):
1) Run high-concurrency streaming completion workload pinned to ap-southeast-1 model pool from a us-east based client.
2) Enable chunked streaming and observe token arrival patterns (p50/p95/p99) via client SDK logs.
3) Notice intermittent multi-second pauses between chunks and occasional SDK-level timeouts.

Observed metrics & logs (excerpt):
- Grafana (obs/streaming) p99 latency spike aligned with egress connection churn (see dashboard link).
- Edge proxy logs: repeated FIN/ACK followed by quick reconnects on same client IP at specific windows.
- Conntrack counters on transit NAT nodes showed port churn and ephemeral port exhaustion warnings around incidents.
- TLS handshake durations spiked by ~300–800ms during events and TCP retransmit counters rose.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Increased SNAT / ephemeral port allocation on the transit NAT pool for Nimbus tenant (2026-03-12 02:15 UTC).
- Created egress-affinity exception: pinned Nimbus's egress to a smaller subset of stable egress IPs to reduce path-bounce while we investigate.
- Added healthcheck and alert on conntrack utilization for tenant-specific NAT pools.

Next steps / planned fixes:
- Short term: monitor for recurrence and add automated scaling for NAT pools in the transit VPC.
- Medium term: update BGP/eBPF route affinity to avoid asymmetric egress pathing for tenant-bound flows.
- Long term: introduce per-tenant egress autoscaling and refine TCP keepalive/idle timeouts used by edge-proxy to tolerate transient path changes better.

Attachments / links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/streams/nimbus-p99
- Kibana logs: https://kibana.redwood/logs?query=SUP-91234
- Slack thread: #support-nimbus (https://slack.redwood/archives/C12345)

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:03 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Observed conntrack warnings on transit NAT; started reproducer to exercise high-concurrency streaming from us-east to ap-southeast.
2026-03-12 02:20 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Applied temporary SNAT pool increase and egress pinning for Nimbus. Customer reports immediate reduction in observed stalls in canary tests.
2026-03-12 05:47 - Customer (Nimbus Ops): Confirmed reduced failures and fewer timeouts in production, but asked for a durable fix and why this started suddenly.
2026-03-13 15:33 - Support (Aisha Patel): Notified customer of mitigation and next steps; scheduled follow-up for 2026-03-16 to confirm stability after route policy changes.
Findings summary: repeated short-lived egress path flips for the tenant were observed at the transit VPC, resulting in new SNAT mappings and TCP connection churn. The combination of per-tenant SNAT pools sized for normal load plus an increase in concurrent streaming connections exhausted ephemeral ports during traffic bursts. When a source port was remapped, downstream servers saw a new 4-tuple and closed prior TLS/TCP connections; clients attempted quick reconnects triggering retransmits and delayed first-token emission. Edge proxy connection reuse semantics amplified the effect, as streaming chunks were tied to a single long-lived TCP connection which, when reset, incurred handshake delays and chunk queuing at the SDK layer.
Root cause hypothesis: insufficient NAT port capacity combined with egress path asymmetry in transit VPC routing rules.
Evidence: conntrack logs, TLS handshake histograms, Grafana graphs aligned to the incident windows, and reduced failure rates after increasing SNAT pool and egress pinning.
Temporary mitigation completed 2026-03-12: SNAT pool size increased and egress affinity enforced for Nimbus Payments; immediate reduction in p99 streaming stalls observed. Ongoing work: network team to deploy BGP policy update to stabilize egress pathing and an autoscaler for tenant NAT pools (PR linked). After stabilization period, will roll out improved keepalive/idle tuning on edge-proxy to reduce sensitivity to short path flips.
Follow-up action: post-mortem draft and runbook changes to add conntrack alerts and per-tenant NAT autoscaling. Customer update scheduled 2026-03-16.
payload.summary: Intermittent streaming slowdowns for Nimbus Payments due to SNAT path bounce between us-east and ap-southeast

Customer (HealthMetrics EU) is concerned that requests from their prod:eu-west tenant briefly routed to us-central during a dedicated pool autoscale event. They want confirmation that no customer data leaves the EU and an explanation of configuration options to prevent cross-region failover.

3) A subset of requests (~0.6%) routed to us-central fallback pool for immediate serving.
