Customer reports duplicate side-effects and apparent out-of-order execution of downstream tool calls when using streaming function-calls with client-side concurrency + backpressure. Behavior reproduced against Dedicated pool in us-west-2. Customer uses long confirmation/ack window on webhook side (up to 10s) and concurrent request batching on their orchestrator which retries stalled streams. Several tool calls that should be idempotent are executed twice and, on retries, sometimes appear applied in a different order than the original intent.
1) Client opens streaming chat session using Python SDK v0.9.2 with function_call enabled.
2) Orchestrator issues two parallel prompts that both trigger function A then function B in fast succession (concurrent streams multiplexed).
3) Customer webhook acknowledges function execution with an ack token but intentionally delays final confirmation up to 8-10s (to simulate heavy backend processing).
4) When ack not received within ack-window, client retries the streaming session / reconnects and the SDK / server retries function calls per default retry policy.
5) Observe downstream system shows function A executed twice for request 1, and in one of the retries function B runs before function A for request 2 (ordering flipped).
Duplicate executions of server-invoked functions (webhook receives the same tool call twice) and occasional reordering of function calls across retries under concurrent multiplexing. Customer sees side-effects like duplicate DB inserts and inventory adjustments applied out-of-order.
At-most-once or at-least-once semantics documented per SDK for streaming function calls depending on idempotency keys, but ordering across independent concurrent streams should be preserved per-request and retries should not reorder within a single logical request. Duplicate tool calls should be avoidable when idempotency keys are provided and respected by server-side retry logic.
2026-03-09T14:12:03Z INFO stream/start session=abc123 origin=py-sdk v=0.9.2
2026-03-09T14:12:05Z WARN webhook/ack-delay request=abc123 tool=funcA ack_window_exceeded=7.8s
2026-03-09T14:12:06Z INFO stream/retry policy=transient-reconnect session=abc123 attempt=1
2026-03-09T14:12:06Z INFO tool/invoke tool=funcA request=abc123 idempotency_key= (missing)
2026-03-09T14:12:07Z INFO tool/invoke tool=funcA request=abc123 idempotency_key= (missing) -- duplicate
2026-03-09T14:12:08Z INFO tool/invoke tool=funcB request=def456 request_latency=120ms
2026-03-09T14:12:08Z INFO tool/invoke tool=funcA request=def456 -- observed ordering mismatch (A after B)
Relevant slack: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C_SUPPORT/p1678471200000 -- #support-dedicated

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 — Customer (Neptune SRE, Jorge Ramos): Provided sample bundle (s3://neptune-prod/bugs/ack-window-bundle.zip) and timeline. Noted they intentionally delay final webhook confirm to simulate long-running downstream work.
2026-03-12 — Support (Markus Chen): Added temporary mitigation guidance for customer and recommended SDK upgrade path and server config change.
Checked server traces: reconnection path emits 'resend_pending_calls' for sessions with unacked tool calls.
Replay shows no normalized idempotency key was attached to per-tool invocation for multiplexed concurrent calls; server retry uses session-level token only and cannot deduplicate across reconnections.
Observed race between resend and in-flight 'delivery confirmation' path resulting in second invoke where first invoke later completes — leads to duplicates but also to crossover ordering when mixes of retried and original calls interleave.
SDKs differ: TS SDK (1.3.0) automatically attaches per-call nonce when function_call invoked in single-threaded path; Python/Go SDKs rely on user to pass idempotency_key or higher-level session flag.
No evidence of bug in customer's webhook. Root cause looks to be missing per-invocation idempotency coupling to server-side dedupe and race during reconnect under concurrent streams.
Mitigation provided: (1) Customer temporarily increased webhook confirmation aggressiveness to emit idempotency_key per tool invocation (or echoed session+sequence) and suppressed client-side reconnect retries for 15s to allow confirmation path to complete; (2) Support recommended upgrading Python SDK to 0.10.x which includes automatic per-call nonce generation when function_call is used concurrently, and applying server-side patch that normalizes idempotency headers on reconnection (PR #1428). Follow-ups: runtime team to backport dedupe logic to dedicated pools (ENG-1428), SDK team to document idempotency patterns in README and add guardrails for sessions with long ack windows.

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:10 UTC VectorHealth reported sustained 5-10% request failures and large latency tails from their dedicated tenant in us-west-2. Impact: customer production inference pipelines experienced elevated P99 latency (2-5x baseline) and sporadic request routing to lower-cost fallback model variants, causing reduced output quality. Environment: Redwood Dedicated cluster gdc-usw2-12 serving VectorHealth reserved pool (8xA100 nodes) with autoscaler enabled and burst capacity off. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady 10 RPS traffic mix of 1k token prompts to gptx-7b pinned model. 2) Observe queue length and scheduler logs over 30 minutes. 3) Correlate with node GPU utilisation and host-level telemetry. Observed behavior: - Autoscaler did not add nodes despite queue growth, instead scheduler started preemptively re-routing requests to lower-cost quantized model variants (fallback chain). - Several nodes reported transient GPU allocation failures and out-of-memory reclaim events; these nodes also showed higher-than-expected kernel eviction counts. - Request admission controller applied aggressive queue thinning (rejecting or re-routing ~12% of requests) to maintain latency SLO. Expected behavior: Autoscaler should spin up burst capacity or notify ops before fallback routing; GPU allocation errors should be isolated to misbehaving pods or noisy tenants rather than causing cluster-wide admission control changes. Logs/metrics attached below and in linked dashboards.
1) Use VectorHealth test harness to replay steady 10 RPS of 1k-token prompts against tenant pool
2) Monitor /metrics/queue_length and autoscaler decisions for 30 minutes
3) Pull kernel-level GPU logs (nvidia-smi nvlink, dmesg) on nodes reporting allocation failures
4) Verify fallback routing events in request-trace logs in the console

Initial hypothesis: noisy tenant on same pool causing higher memory pressure and kernel preemptions -> cascade into allocation failures.
Checked node metrics: nodes n02 and n03 have elevated GPU memory fragmentation and higher kernel eviction counts compared to baseline.
Autoscaler logs show 'policy_min_uptime' prevented immediate scale-up; cluster was configured with conservative burst settings for this dedicated pool.
Correlated with customer traffic: VectorHealth workload includes occasional long-sequence prompts (1k tokens) that increase KV cache pressure and reduce effective batch density.
Observed that fallback routing logic treats repeated allocation errors as cluster-level capacity signals and triggers lower-accuracy model variants rather than per-tenant isolation.
Checked cloud provider capacity: no region-wide GPU shortage events reported; problem localized to the tenant pool due to bin-packing of noisy pods.
[2026-03-10 09:01] Support (Aisha): Thanks for the report — we've started triage and pulled the last 6 hours of metrics. Can you confirm if any long-running jobs were added to the pool around 07:50 UTC?
[2026-03-10 09:12] Customer (VectorHealth - James Lee): No scheduled jobs were changed. We did run an A/B eval ramp at 07:45 that increased prompt length, but it was targeted to their staging cluster; nothing should have hit production.

[2026-03-10 11:00] Support (Aisha): After the mitigation, VectorHealth reports P99 latency returned to baseline and fallback routing stopped. We're monitoring for recurrence over 24h.
[2026-03-12 14:10] Eng (Miguel): Root cause analysis complete — noisy tenant's long-sequence evals created fragmented GPU memory; autoscaler policy prevented rapid burst. Patch submitted to autoscaler to relax burst gating when allocation errors exceed threshold (PR #210).
[2026-03-12 14:20] Customer (James Lee): Thanks — glad to see a plan. Please share any long-term recommendations for pool sizing and isolation.
Mitigation: 1) Immediate: tainted and evacuated misbehaving nodes, added +2 emergency nodes to VectorHealth reserved pool, restarted serving pods for clean GPU allocation. 2) Short-term fix: adjusted autoscaler policy to allow emergency burst on repeated allocation errors and added a threshold to trigger per-tenant isolation rather than global fallback routing. 3) Long-term: engineering to add GPU memory fragmentation metrics to autoscaler signals and introduce tenant-aware bin-packing. Follow-ups: create an alert for 'allocation_error_rate > 5% over 5m', update Dedicated capacity runbook to include noisy-tenant isolation steps, and schedule capacity review with VectorHealth in two weeks.

Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running streaming conversations (SSE and websocket) abruptly stop forwarding chunks to the client after ~18-25 seconds into a high-token generation. The model process continues to generate tokens (server-side progress and token counters continue), but the downstream transport layer stops emitting event/chunk frames and the client eventually times out.

Impact: Multiple production customers using persistent chat sessions experience mid-conversation silences resulting in failed user interactions and increased client-side retries. NeuroWrite Labs reported 6 user sessions impacted over a 2-hour window; business-critical workflows affected.

Environment: prod us-east, Redwood hosted inference, dynamic autoscaling enabled with burst capacity.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start SSE chat session against /v1/chat/stream with model redwood/open-llama-7b and a prompt that elicits a 1200+ token response.
2) Simulate background burst load to push worker pool utilization from ~45% to ~72% within 10s (we used a synthetic load generator).
3) Observe stream until token generation passes ~600 tokens and watch for silence after ~18-25s.

Observed behavior:
- Server logs show generator continuing: token_count increments and final token emitted internally.
- No SSE chunk frames sent to client after silence point.
- Connection remains ESTABLISHED for ~60-90s before client disconnects on timeout.
- Correlated autoscaler event: rebalancer triggered worker pool reshuffle at ~t+20s.

Expected behavior: continuous chunked SSE/WebSocket forwarding from generation until EOS event.

Temporary workaround applied by Support during incident: pinned the customer's requests to a dedicated worker pool (route override) and disabled dynamic rebalancer for their dedicated capacity; customer reports streaming resumed normal behavior.

Relevant logs/snippets:
- serving-runtime: "DynamicBatchRouter: initiating reassignment for request=abc123 to pool=b-pool-7 at t=2026-03-14T14:12:05Z"
- stream-proxy: "TransportSession: chunk-forwarder lost mapping for request=abc123, dropping next 1..n frames"
- scheduler: "Rebalancer: moved 24 tasks to b-pool-7 due to utilization spike"

Observed metrics:
- spike in worker-churn_count coincident with chunk silence
- p50 token latency normal, p95/p99 token latency increased during churn
- no 5xx returned to client (connection remained open)

Hypothesis: dynamic_batch_router triggers a worker-pool reassignment while a request is inflight. The streaming proxy's request->session mapping is not atomically preserved across the handoff, causing chunks produced post-handoff to be written to a worker-local forward queue that is no longer attached to the original transport session. The generator continues; the proxy drops forwarded frames until the session is reconciled or the client reconnects.

Next steps:
1) Engineering to reproduce in staging with deterministic rebalancer trigger and capture packet-level traces.
2) Implement guard in stream-proxy to pin sessions for the life of a streaming request (or to queue forwarders across reassignment).
3) Add observability: per-request session-mapping audit events and alert on dropped-forwarded-frame counts.
4) Evaluate rebalancer thresholds to avoid handoff for long-lived streaming requests.
5) Expand canary to ensure no regression with autoscaler disabled.

Priority: P1 / Sev1 due to enterprise customer impact.

Staging reproduction: deterministic rebalancer trigger reproduced silence when reassigning inflight streaming requests.
Hypothesis holds: the forwarder queue is local to worker and not reattached to new session mapping during reassignment.
Workaround: pinned customer's edge route to dedicated pool and disabled dynamic rebalancer for that pool (applied 2026-03-14 15:00). This prevented further silences for the customer.
Planned fix: implement stream-proxy handoff shim to preserve forward queues during DynamicBatchRouter reassignments (design in PR, target ship 2026-03-22).
Monitoring: added temporary Grafana dashboard panel for 'dropped-forwarded-frames' and alert when >5 drops/min across clusters.
Follow-up: schedule postmortem and update runbook with steps to pin routes and roll back rebalancer changes for affected customers.

Issue summary:

During a peak traffic window on 2026-03-09 17:22 UTC, Cinder Labs began seeing partial/stale streaming responses, token reordering for long chat sessions (>4096 tokens), and a surge in client retries that amplified upstream throughput. This led to increased 5xx rates from serving nodes, transient throttles from the API gateway, and an unexpected billing delta for the customer.

Impact:
- Multiple customer endpoints experienced truncated streams and out-of-order token sequences (~1200 user sessions affected).
- Observed 5xx rate peaked at 6.3% for the customer’s traffic window.
- Billing spike estimated at +42% for the affected 2-hour window due to retry amplification.
- Customer escalated to enterprise support and requested immediate mitigation, crediting and a post-incident review.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1) serving cl-13b-v1-quant behind api-gateway v2.13.
- Dedicated routing policy: enterprise-reserved-us-east.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. Create a multi-turn chat session pinned to cl-13b-v1-quant with >4096 token context and stream responses.
2. Induce a partial runtime eviction (simulate KV cache evictions / kernel reselect) while continuing to stream.
3. Observe token gaps and client-side automatic retries causing multiple inflight requests for the same session.

Observed behavior:
- When a serving shard dropped the KV prefix during a background compaction, subsequent token continuation resumed from an earlier cache state and produced overlapping token sequences.
- Client SDKs retried idempotently but without session-affinity checks, creating duplicate in-flight completions.
- API gateway detected elevated error rates and began conservative throttling; some requests received 429s while others returned 5xx from the runtime.

Initial mitigation and timeline:
- 17:28 UTC: Support opened escalation and notified SRE and Serving Runtime teams.
- 17:35 UTC: Temporary routing policy change to route Cinder Labs traffic to a healthy pre-warmed pool (bypassed recently-updated autoscaler rules).
- 17:42 UTC: Disabled aggressive client-side retry guidance sent to Cinder Labs; asked temporary SDK toggle to backoff.
- 18:10 UTC: Rolling kernel-selection rollback (PR linked) deployed for us-east pool which stopped KV prefix evictions during active streaming.
- 19:00 UTC: Error rates returned to baseline; streaming behavior normalized.

Timeline and findings:
- 2026-03-09 17:22 UTC: first elevated 5xx and streaming truncations for Cinder Labs observed (api-gateway metrics + their telemetry).
- Root cause hypothesis: interaction between a recent kernel-selection tweak (PR 4821) and aggressive KV compaction led to transient state loss for long-lived sessions.
- Evidence: heap/kvcache flush logs on serving nodes show compaction events coincident with affected session IDs.
- Replay of workload on staging reproduced token reordering when compaction was force-triggered during active streaming.
- Throttle amplification: client SDK retry logic started new requests that did not enforce session-affinity, creating fanout and repeated token generation for the same logical conversation.
- Billing delta analysis: aggregated request counts for Cinder Labs during the window were 2.4x baseline; cost-weighted tokens increased proportionally.
- Contrib factors: recent autoscaler tuning reduced pre-warmed buffer by 20% in us-east pool, increasing likelihood that compaction/eviction occurred under pressure.

Support (Maya Chen) — 2026-03-09 17:30 UTC: Customer reported truncated streams and repeated partial messages. Opened incident and paged SRE.
SRE (Arjun Patel) — 2026-03-09 17:38 UTC: Identified KV compaction entries correlated with session IDs. Temporarily rerouted traffic to healthy pool.
Customer (Elena Ruiz, Cinder Labs) — 2026-03-09 17:45 UTC: Confirmed temporary improvement after reroute; requested timeline and credit for billing spike.
Eng (Tomasz Novak) — 2026-03-09 18:05 UTC: Rolled back kernel-selection change (PR 4821) in us-east as mitigation; monitoring for regressions.
Billing (Priya Shah) — 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Preliminary credit calculation prepared; recommended 50% credit for the affected window pending final audit.
Support (Maya Chen) — 2026-03-11 11:02 UTC: Sent post-incident summary and next steps to Cinder Labs; scheduled follow-up review on 2026-03-12.
Customer (Elena Ruiz) — 2026-03-11 15:40 UTC: Appreciated rapid response; requested concrete SDK guidance to avoid amplification in future.
Root cause: interaction between a kernel-selection optimization and KV compaction behavior on serving nodes caused transient session state loss for long chat contexts, leading to token reordering. Secondary amplification: client SDK retries without enforced session-affinity produced duplicate inflight completions and a billing spike.

Fixes applied:
- Rolled back kernel-selection tweak in us-east (PR 4821) and deployed a guarded kernel rollout that disables compaction during active streams.
- Temporary routing to pre-warmed pool restored stability during the rollout.
- Issued a targeted billing credit to Cinder Labs (50% of the two-hour delta) and submitted final audit for adjustment.

Status: Mitigation deployed, monitoring in place, customer credited; incident closed after validation period.
Implement server-side session-affinity enforcement for streaming continuations (owner: Eng/Serving Runtime) — ETA 2026-04-07
Add a compaction-safe flag to the runtime that prevents KV prefix eviction during active streams (owner: Eng/Serving Runtime) — ETA 2026-03-25
Enhance SDKs to surface and opt-in to conservative retry modes for enterprise tiers (owner: DevX/SDK) — ETA 2026-04-01
Create billing audit dashboard to detect anomalous retry amplification per customer (owner: Finance/Platform) — ETA 2026-03-20
Run tabletop with top enterprise customers to validate failover behaviors and communication playbooks (owner: Support/GTM) — ETA 2026-04-15

Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-01 05:40 UTC EdgeLens reported a sustained elevation in 5xx responses on their dedicated embedding route under a large batching upload (embedding funnel). Impact: customer ingestion pipeline saw ~18% failed batches, downstream consumers falling behind; several upstream runtime workers restarted during the same window. Environment: dedicated tenant on prod|us-east using rw-embed-4k-v2 with batching enabled and priority routing to dedicated embedding worker pools. Steps to reproduce: 1) Submit concurrent embedding upload stream of mixed sizes (1k-4k tokens) from multiple clients to EdgeLens tenant. 2) Observe accept-queue growth on api-gateway and increased latency on embed route. 3) Watch runtime controller logs for preempt/evict events and NVML warnings. Observed behavior: api-gateway accept queue grows, connection backpressure causes hedged retries and 429/5xx amplification. Serving runtime reports KV cache lock contention and then OOM-like watchdog restarts on a subset of embedding workers. Logs/metrics (selected): - api-gateway: accept_queue_depth peaking at ~900 (normal <200), conn_accept_rate drop by 40% - runtime: kvcache_lock_waits spiking to 1200/s, worker_watchdog_restarts x6 - scheduler: preempt_eviction_count increased by 3x - customer: ingestion job failed rate ~18% during window Relevant traces/dashboards: embed-ingest-latency, accept-queue-health, runtime-watchdog. Customer notes: "We push large batched uploads every 6 hours; this first triggered during our midnight ingest window when we increased batch size."
2026-03-01 06:12 - Support (Ava): Logged initial report from EdgeLens; collected headers, sample request IDs (rids: rid_8e7b, rid_8e9c) and top-line metrics and routed to SRE.
2026-03-01 07:05 - SRE (Liam): Confirmed accept_queue_depth abnormal on prod|us-east for tenant; observed hedged retry amplification from api-gateway configs. Temporarily increased accept queue capacity on ingress to mitigate immediate failures.
2026-03-02 09:22 - Customer (EdgeLens, Jordan): Noted partial reduction after temporary mitigation but still see intermittent batch failures and occasional runtime restarts tied to large embeddings. Asked for permanent fix and rollback-safe mitigation.

Additional notes:
2026-03-03 14:00 - Support (Ava): Scheduled maintenance window for controlled rollout of ingress admission change and conservative kvcache backoff to avoid runtime restarts; customer notified and approved.
2026-03-03 16:10 - SRE (Liam): Ongoing monitoring post-rollout shows accept_queue_depth drop to <250 and kvcache_lock_waits reduced by ~70%. Still tracking small tail of restarts potentially due to fragmented GPU memory from older processes.
Hypothesis 1: Mixed-size embedding funnel causes priority misclassification at ingress resulting in large batches occupying accept queue and forcing hedged retries that cascade into 5xx amplification.
Hypothesis 2: KVCACHE lock contention during large-embedding prefetch increases worker latencies and triggers watchdog restarts under transient memory pressure.
Evidence: correlating trace IDs show hedged retry spikes aligned with accept_queue_depth peaks. NVML logs show transient allocation failures on two workers before restart.
Dashboards used: embed-ingest-latency (panel 2), accept-queue-health, runtime-watchdog (panels 4-6). Slack thread: #support-prod (link: slack.com/archives/C0123456/p1623456789000).
Temp mitigation applied: increased ingress accept queue cap, lowered hedged-retry aggressiveness on embed route, and disabled optimistic prefetch for rw-embed-4k-v2 for the customer tenant.
Next steps: instrument per-request token cost header to ingress for better admission control; refactor kvcache lock to finer-grained sharding; schedule follow-up load test with EdgeLens dataset.
Workaround: temporary ingress accept-queue cap increase and hedged-retry tuning deployed (rolled back after controlled test window). This reduced immediate 5xx failures and prevented further runtime restarts during peak ingest.
Permanent plan: implement per-tenant admission control that applies cost-based throttling for large embedding uploads and add per-request token estimate header pipeline. Also plan kvcache lock sharding and memory-fragmentation mitigation in serving-runtime milestone M34.
Rollout notes: change to ingress admission control will be rolled out gradually across regions with canary tests; target complete in two weeks pending QA. Customer notified and agrees to staged rollout.
Follow-up actions: assign ENG-PLAT-1425 for kvcache refactor; schedule joint load test with EdgeLens in staging (owner: Solutions Eng, estimated date 2026-03-10).

Issue summary:
Customer FinOptima reports intermittent 200–800ms additional tail latency on requests from eu-west that should be served by their dedicated eu pool. They observe spikes approximately 1–3 times per 1k requests and see traces indicating a short-lived cross-region egress to us-east for some requests despite region affinity.

Impact:
- Sporadic increased tail latency (affects user-facing search/assist features).
- No obvious 5xxs; throughput unaffected.
- Customer worried about data egress policy compliance and cost implications of cross-region routing.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated reserved capacity
- Primary region: eu-west (eu-west-1)
1) Send a steady stream of generation requests pinned to model redwood/open-llama-7b against customer's dedicated eu endpoint (500 rps, typical prompt length ~120 tokens).
2) Monitor per-request region tag in trace and routing logs for a 24h window.
3) Correlate latency spikes to any route changes or capacity events in the serving logs.
Small subset (~0.1%-0.3%) of requests were routed out of eu-west to us-east briefly and returned results; traces show an extra ~200-800ms attributable to cross-region network hop and additional TLS handshakes. No model fallback to smaller-quantized variants observed in the traces.
All requests from customer's eu-resident endpoint should be served from the dedicated eu-west pool (no cross-region egress) unless explicit failover or capacity policy is triggered.
Trace snippet: trace_id=abcd1234: route_decision=geo_affinity->eu-west; transient_routing_override=us-east; tcp_rtt_delta=120ms; tls_handshake=85ms
API logs: 200 responses; no upstream 5xx; service.agent=dedicated-eu-v2
Customer provided sample traces and timestamps (2026-03-09 14:02:10Z to 14:30:00Z).
Checked routing policy config for customer: geo_affinity=preferred, allow_cross_region_failover=true, failover_threshold=85th_percentile_latency>500ms
Dedicated pool metrics show a short spike in kernel queue wait on eu-west GPU node group at 2026-03-09 14:15Z coincident with reported spikes.
No autoscaler events that fully drained pool; there was a transient pod OOM on node eu-w-3 which triggered a short-lived request re-route to shared capacity in us-east.
Billing meter shows negligible cross-region bytes but customer accounting concerns remain.
Customer (FinOptima) - 2026-03-10: We're seeing occasional latency spikes and some internal compliance flags for cross-border calls. Can you confirm whether 'preferred' geo-affinity can be made strict to fully prevent any egress out of region?
Support (Asha Mehta) - 2026-03-10: Thanks for the report — I've escalated to infra and collected traces. Asking SRE to check for transient node-level issues in eu-west and to confirm routing behavior logic.
SRE (Evan Park) - 2026-03-11: Preliminary find: a single dedicated worker experienced an OOM and requests in-flight were diverted to fallback routing which currently prefers lowest-latency available capacity (which can be cross-region). Investigating whether we can short-circuit to strict-local policy for customer pools with 'no-egress' compliance needs.
Support (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-11: Workaround proposed to customer: enable 'strict_local_failover=false' -> (note: docs call this geo_affinity.mode with options preferred|strict) — set to strict to prevent cross-region fallback; recommend applying alongside autoscaler tuning to avoid OOM-driven diversions. Guidance sent with steps to apply via Console and API.
Customer (FinOptima) - 2026-03-11: We need a documented SLA for 'no-egress' behavior and confirmation that enabling strict mode won't increase request failures during local capacity pressure. Also want recommended autoscaler settings for steady 500rps workload.
SRE (Evan Park) - 2026-03-12: Follow-up: enabling strict geo-affinity will prevent cross-region reroutes but may surface 429/503 during local capacity exhaustion; recommended pattern: (1) strict geo-affinity with (2) increased reserved capacity or configured burst pools in-region and (3) reduce pod memory headroom to avoid OOMs, plus pre-warming. Drafted infra-runbook changes for 'strict-local' customers.
Pending - workaround documented and delivered to customer. Action items: (1) advise customer to switch geo_affinity.mode to strict if they accept risk of local failures, (2) SRE to publish runbook updates and autoscaler tuning recommendations, (3) infra to add a safety metric to detect node OOM patterns and trigger preemptive routing alerts.
1) Support to confirm with customer whether they want strict geo-affinity applied (ticket owner: Priya Nair).
2) SRE to convert runbook notes into a Confluence page and link the PR (owner: Evan Park).
3) Infra to propose an autoscaler memory headroom baseline for dedicated pools (owner: Platform Eng lead).

comments: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z Aisha Kumar: Acknowledged issue and requested customer debug logs and example trace. Asked for SDK versions and edge proxy vendor. (waiting on customer)
2026-03-03T00:00:00Z Miguel Torres: Reproduced locally with our proxy shim. Created PR to add normalization on resume path. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2487
payload.description:
Issue summary: The customer reports duplicate invocations of an external webhook (their downstream job queue) when a long-running tool execution is retried after a client-side backoff and the client moves to a new TCP/HTTP2 connection (connection migration). Impact: Duplicate side effects (duplicate downstream jobs) observed in production intermittently for a subset (~2%) of requests that hit long-running function calls. Scope: Customer uses Dedicated pool, runs high-concurrency multiplexed streams from the TypeScript SDK behind an edge proxy that performs connection pooling and occasional mid-session connection handover.
Customer sends multiplexed streaming request via TS SDK v1.14 with a tool invocation that triggers a webhook to their job queue (external HTTP POST).
Introduce simulated latency on the webhook (5+ seconds) to force the client SDK to hit internal retry/backoff logic while still holding the stream open.
Simulate client connection migration by closing the HTTP/2 stream mid-backoff and allowing the client to re-establish a new stream within the same logical session.
Observe duplicate webhook posts in customer job queue logs for ~1-3% of runs under these conditions.
Customer webhook logs show two POSTs with same payload spaced ~6s apart: 2026-02-28T18:14:22Z and 2026-02-28T18:14:28Z
Redwood request traces (trace-id: rbw-7b-20260228-xx) show original stream session with ack nonce 'n=v4-9f3a' and resumed stream reporting ack nonce 'n=v4-9f3a�' (trailing null), likely normalization issue in proxy
Edge proxy (provider X) logs: header rewrite on connection handover, truncated idempotency token to first 16 chars in some frames
Initial hypothesis: idempotency/confirmation token normalization mismatch between original stream and resumed stream after connection migration; downstream confirmation check failed leading to a second execution.
Reproduced locally with TS SDK + mocked edge proxy that rewrites headers on connection migration. When the token is truncated or has a non-printable suffix, server-side idempotency map treats resumed acknowledgement as distinct, so tool run is re-issued.
Python SDK does not show same behaviour in customer tests because their Python clients use single-request blocking pattern (no multiplex) and do not trigger connection migration in same way.
Observed additional factor: some proxies insert zero bytes (�) or split long header values across pseudo-frames; our header canonicalization path currently trims trailing control chars but only on initial request path, not on resumed connection path.

Additional notes:
2026-03-02 - Customer (DataBright SRE - Priya Menon): Provided traces, SDK versions: ts-sdk@1.14.0, py-sdk@1.12.2, proxy: EdgeX v3.2. Customer confirms duplicates are ~2% and correlated with proxy handovers.
2026-03-04 - SRE (Liam O'Neill): Added temporary mitigation in dedicated fleet: enable strict header passthrough on customer edge route to avoid proxy truncation. Monitoring for duplicate webhook counts.
Root cause: token normalization inconsistency between initial connection handling and stream-resume code path. When an idempotency/confirmation token is mutated (truncated, padded with control characters, or split), the resumed session supplies a different canonical token and server treats resumed invocation as a new request.
Contributing factors: multiplexed TS SDK using connection migration semantics, certain edge proxies that rewrite or split headers, and lack of resume-path normalization in the serving runtime.
Hotfix rollout: Applied runtime change to canonicalize idempotency tokens on resume and initial request paths. Deployed to Dedicated customer pool in us-east 2026-03-05 03:00 UTC.
Customer mitigation: Advised DataBright to enable 'preserve-headers' mode on their EdgeX routes and increase webhook idempotency resilience (idempotency key in payload as fallback) until hotfix rollout is verified.
Post-deploy monitoring: Duplicate webhook rate dropped from ~2% to <0.02% in 48h window; no new regressions observed.
Follow-up actions: Add unit tests for header-splitting/resume path normalization, update SDK docs with guidance on best-effort idempotency keys in payload for proxy-prone networks, track a follow-up internal task INT-3410 for improved diagnostics on header anomalies.

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports burst-driven p99 latency spikes (10–30s) on Dedicated capacity in us-east during mixed-length chat traffic. Median latency stable, but tail degrades sharply during bursts and high request churn.

Customer impact
- Production user-facing chat product experiences timeouts + retries when bursts happen (customer sees elevated 5xx from their upstream due to timeouts).
- Customer SLO target: p99 < 2.5s for streaming-first response; currently p99 intermittently 12–28s during bursts.

Customer environment
- Customer: Northwind Analytics
- Tier: Dedicated
- Region: us-east
- Workload: chat completions, mixed prompt lengths (short prompts + occasional long context ~8k tokens), sustained decode with bursty arrival
- Runtime: runtime-1.21.x (customer pool) at time of initial report
- Client behavior: retries after 12s; concurrency spikes at top-of-hour batch jobs

Symptoms observed (initial)
- Tail latency spikes correlate with GPU memory pressure events, allocator stalls, and opportunistic KV evictions.
- No evidence of network/TLS issues; primarily runtime scheduling/allocator behavior.

Reproduction hints provided by customer
- Burst traffic: 4–6x baseline QPS for 2–4 minutes, repeated 1–3 times/hour
- Mixed sequence lengths: ~70% short, ~25% medium, ~5% long contexts

Diagnostics requested
1) Request IDs + timestamps for worst spikes
2) Response headers (x-redwood-request-id / model / region)
3) Any client-side timeouts / retry counts

Internal investigation notes
- Suspected KV arena fragmentation due to long-lived allocations + churn.
- Next steps: enable fragmentation/compaction metrics, capture allocator snapshots, and evaluate canary runtime-1.22 compaction feature behind flag.

Links / escalations
- Slack escalation: sources/slack/support/1768159022.json
- Runtime discussion: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1767311205.json, sources/slack/eng-runtime/1767394021.json
- Canary incident thread (later): sources/slack/incidents/1767735109.json
- Oncall procedures draft: sources/slack/eng-oncall/1767660044.json

Relevant logs (excerpt)
- 2026-01-29T19:42:11Z request_id=rwreq_01HTZ0R6GQ9P7J9Q8A model=rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct phase=decode msg="decode step stalled waiting for kv page" stall_ms=1640 kv_free_pages=12 kv_frag_ratio=0.61
- 2026-01-29T19:42:13Z request_id=rwreq_01HTZ0R6GQ9P7J9Q8A msg="kv eviction triggered" reason="alloc_fail" evicted_sequences=3 tier="dedicated" pinned_skipped=1
- 2026-01-29T19:42:18Z request_id=rwreq_01HTZ0R6GQ9P7J9Q8A msg="oom_avoided_shedding" shed_requests=2 pool=northwind-us-east-03

Dashboards (internal)
- Dedicated pool latency: Grafana > Dedicated / Pool / Request latency (p50/p95/p99) (northwind-us-east-03)
- GPU memory + allocator: Grafana > Serving runtime / KV cache health (fragmentation, free pages, evictions)
- Traces: Tracing > request exemplars filtered by request_id(s) from customer

Hypothesis
- KV cache allocator fragmentation rises during bursts; compaction/eviction currently happens at poor times, causing decode stalls and p99 spikes. Feature work in progress (runtime-1.22) expected to reduce fragmentation via budgeted compaction + tier-aware eviction.

2026-01-29 20:03 (Paula Mendes - Support): Created ticket from customer escalation. Customer reports p99 spikes up to 28s during burst windows; baseline p99 ~1.8s. Asked for 10 request IDs and approximate timestamps + confirmation of client timeouts.
2026-01-29 20:26 (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Looking at northwind-us-east-03. Confirm tail spikes align with GPU memory pressure + allocator churn. Not seeing gateway 5xx first; latency originates in runtime. Recommend enabling new kv fragmentation counters if available in their current runtime build; otherwise need a canary upgrade.
2026-01-29 21:10 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Pulled logs around 19:40–19:50Z. Seeing repeated "decode stalled waiting for kv page" and "alloc_fail" bursts. Flagging Runtime team. Linking #support thread sources/slack/support/1768159022.json.
2026-01-29 22:04 (Omar El-Sayed - KV cache TL): This looks consistent with fragmentation + poor-timing evictions. We have fragmentation metrics landing (PR-19342) and budgeted compaction in runtime-1.22 behind flag. Propose: 1) get metrics in their pool; 2) run canary on a subset of traffic; 3) keep kill-switch ready.
2026-01-30 09:18 (Allison Grant - Observability): If we can roll the metrics build, please ensure we wire: kv_frag_ratio, kv_bytes_moved_total, kv_compaction_time_ms, kv_evictions_total, and decode_stall_ms. Standard naming in Confluence page linked in ticket.
2026-01-30 13:37 (Paula Mendes - Support): Customer provided sample request IDs + confirmed top-of-hour batch causes 5–6x burst. They see client timeouts at 12s; retries amplify traffic. Customer asked if there is a near-term mitigation besides increasing capacity.
2026-01-30 14:05 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Short-term mitigation: raise prefill/decode concurrency caps slightly to reduce queueing, but may worsen memory pressure. Prefer to avoid. Suggest temporary traffic smoothing (customer-side) + we proceed with runtime canary w/ metrics and compaction flag off first.
2026-01-31 10:22 (Connor O’Brien - Release): We can cut a dedicated-pool canary build of runtime-1.22.0-rc2 for northwind-us-east-03. Default compaction flag OFF; metrics ON. Target: 5% traffic via router policy. ETA 2–3 hours after approval.
2026-01-31 12:11 (Sean Gallagher - SRE): Approval granted with guardrails: rollback if p99 worsens >20% for 10 min OR if kv_bytes_moved spikes correlate with decode stalls. See incident playbook thread sources/slack/eng-oncall/1767660044.json.
2026-01-31 16:02 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Canary deployed (5% traffic) runtime-1.22.0-rc2 with metrics enabled, compaction OFF. Observing kv_frag_ratio rising to ~0.58 during bursts (baseline ~0.25). Evictions also spike (alloc_fail). Confirms fragmentation hypothesis.
2026-02-01 09:44 (Omar El-Sayed - KV cache TL): Next step: enable compaction flag with conservative budget (bytes/time) on canary only. Recommendation: compaction_budget_ms_per_tick=0.3ms, max_bytes_moved_per_s=256MB, trigger_frag_ratio=0.45. Ensure kill-switch config propagation is verified first (PR-19422).
2026-02-01 11:20 (Benji Okafor - Rollout/Flags): Kill-switch propagation validated in us-east (config commit -> runtime acknowledged in ~35s). Safe-disable semantics: stops scheduling new compaction steps; in-flight relocation completes per-step then halts. (See platform thread sources/slack/eng-platform/1768080411.json.)
2026-02-01 13:08 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Enabled compaction on canary (5%). Immediate effect: kv_frag_ratio peaks lower (~0.42) and returns to baseline faster post-burst. p99 improved during 14:00Z burst window (canary cohort p99 3.1s vs control 11.6s). No throughput drop detected at p50. Logging exemplar traces added (PR-19405) for correlation.
2026-02-02 08:57 (Paula Mendes - Support): Updated customer: we identified root cause as allocator fragmentation under bursty mixed-length traffic; we have mitigation in canary that is improving p99 materially. Customer agrees to keep current capacity and retest after we expand canary.
2026-02-03 17:31 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Hit an edge case during higher churn test (cancelled requests) causing transient allocator leak suspicion. Runtime patched via PR-19440. We paused canary expansion pending patch; compaction remained ON for 5% cohort with no customer-visible incident.
2026-02-04 12:26 (Connor O’Brien - Release): runtime-1.22.1 hotfix with cancellation fix is ready for dedicated canary. Plan: upgrade canary nodes, keep compaction ON w/ conservative budgets, expand to 25% if stable for 24h.
2026-02-05 15:18 (Sean Gallagher - SRE): After 24h on 25%: p99 improved ~55–70% during bursts; no OOM/forced shedding. Eviction rate down; decode stalls reduced. Proceeding to 100% within Northwind pool with rollback window open. Alert tuning notes tracked separately in sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/kv-compaction-alert-tuning-notes.json.
2026-02-06 10:42 (Rafael Mendes - SRE Oncall): Rolled to 100% of northwind-us-east-03. Observed top-of-hour burst: p99 2.7s (prev 12–28s). kv_frag_ratio stays <0.45 with compaction. No capacity changes needed.
2026-02-07 09:10 (Paula Mendes - Support): Customer confirms p99 stable across three burst windows; remaining issue is occasional client-side timeout at 12s on rare long-context requests (expected). Customer requested a summary + plan for making this default for Dedicated tiers.
2026-02-08 14:30 (Omar El-Sayed - KV cache TL): Summarized internally: compaction + tier-aware eviction will roll out broadly in runtime-1.22 with staged guardrails. This ticket can be resolved; follow-ups tracked in SUP-28472 for canary regression handling and INT-11904 for dashboard defaults.
Root cause confirmed as KV cache allocator fragmentation under bursty mixed-length workloads causing allocation stalls + poorly-timed evictions, leading to decode stalls and p99 spikes. Mitigation deployed by upgrading Northwind’s dedicated pool to runtime-1.22.1 (canary -> 100%) with fragmentation metrics enabled and budgeted KV compaction turned on (conservative budget/thresholds) plus cancellation edge-case fix. Post-rollout: burst p99 reduced from 12–28s to ~2.7–3.5s; forced shedding/OOM-avoid events eliminated during observed bursts.
Keep compaction enabled for Northwind dedicated pool; maintain kill-switch readiness during first 2 weeks post-rollout.
Share customer-facing summary + guidance on client timeout expectations for rare long-context outliers (PM-611 link tracked outside Jira).
Ensure dashboards include kv_frag_ratio, kv_bytes_moved_total, kv_evictions_total, and decode_stall_ms panels by default (tracked in INT-11904).
Continue staged rollout of runtime-1.22 compaction defaults across other dedicated pools; watch for regressions (SUP-28472).
payload.summary: Burst p99 latency spikes on Dedicated chat traffic (suspected KV cache fragmentation / allocator churn)

comments: Billing: Determined the invoice generator aggregated two separate feeds: reserved commit prorata from the reserved-commit service and a separate usage feed from the metering pipeline. Finance applied a temporary hold and advised Support to find root cause.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports they were charged both their Reserved Dedicated monthly commit and per-token metering for the same burst window on 2025-01-15 UTC. The invoice line items show a Reserved Capacity prorated charge plus an extra per-token usage line that aligns exactly with a 2-hour burst during peak traffic. Customer believes this is double-billing because their SLA/contract (enterprise reserved pool) should absorb the tokens while their pool scaled out into a hosted burst mode.

Impact:
- Immediate invoice discrepancy of ~$5,400 for the billing period Jan 1 - Jan 15.
- Customer-facing finance team has paused payments pending resolution.
- Application remained functional; no correctness or data exposure issues reported.

Environment:
- Customer account: nimbleretail-prod (org id: 99821)
- Deployment mode: Dedicated (monthly commit) with autoscaling to HostedBurst when capacity exhausted
- Region: us-east
- Affected service components: dedicated-allocator, scheduler, metering, billing pipeline

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Run sustained ingest + chat traffic from 2025-01-15T10:00:00Z -> 2025-01-15T12:00:00Z triggering autoscale and burst into hosted nodes.
2) Observe dashboard: dedicated pool reported full, scheduler routed 37% of requests to hosted-burst fallback during window.
3) After invoice processed, see per-token metering line that corresponds to the same token count during that 2-hour window.

Logs & evidence attached by customer:
- Billing invoice PDF (attached as nimble-invoice-20250115.pdf)
- Sampling of request IDs and timestamps (attached sample_request_ids.csv)
- Console screenshot showing pool scale events and fallback counts (attached scale-events.png)

Investigation notes (support):
- Initial triage (Support): Confirmed invoice contains both prorated reserved commit line and a per-token usage line matching the burst timeframe. Ticket escalated to Billing and SRE for metering trace.

Additional notes:
- SRE/Serving (Jonah): Preliminary hypothesis: requests routed to hosted-burst were still tagged with the original dedicated pool id by the scheduler during fallbacks; metering pipeline uses routing metadata to decide whether to bill against reserve vs on-demand. If fallback requests carry both tags or incorrect tag, they can be double-counted.
- Observed spike in bridging logs at 2025-01-15T10:05Z where fallback worker A retried and emitted two events: one increment for dedicated counter and one for on-demand counter. Suspect duplicate event emission from the router retry path.
Current status:
- SRE reproduced a narrow-case replay in staging showing duplicate metering increments for routed-fallback retries. Repro steps attached in staging-repro.md.
- Billing has issued a provisional credit for the disputed amount and marked invoice as under review. Finance requests a final explanation before reversing or retaining the credit.
- Engineering has a tentative fix in review to dedupe metering events in the router when fallback routing occurs (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2821).
Customer request:
- Formal explanation of what happened and assurance credits will be applied back to the account once root cause is fixed.
- Confirmation that future fallback events will not be double-billed.
- Timestamped audit log showing which tokens were billed to reserved vs on-demand for the disputed window.
Next steps:
- Engineering to finalize and roll out event-dedup patch to staging, run targeted canary for 24h, then promote to prod. (Owner: Jonah)
- Billing to confirm credit issuance and hold until final review complete. (Owner: Maria Chen - Billing)
- Provide customer an export of audit tokens and final postmortem within 5 business days.
Attachments: nimble-invoice-20250115.pdf, scale-events.png, sample_request_ids.csv, staging-repro.md
2025-01-18T13:15Z - Ariana Patel (Support): Logged ticket after initial call with NimbleRetail finance. Customer expects urgent review; escalated to P1.
2025-01-18T15:02Z - Maria Chen (Billing): Confirmed duplicate line items present. Applied provisional credit of $5,400 and placed invoice under review. Requested metering traces for 2025-01-15 10:00-12:00 UTC.
2025-01-19T09:40Z - Jonah Reyes (SRE): Reproduced duplicate increment behavior in staging with same router retry pattern. Opened PR to dedupe increment events. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2821.
2025-01-20T11:05Z - Liam O'Neill (Engineer): Added additional logging to the router for tag propagation; posting tentative fix to staging for canary.
2025-01-21T17:30Z - Ariana Patel (Support): Sent customer an interim update: provisional credit applied, engineering investigating root cause and will provide audit export once confirmed.
2025-01-22T10:12Z - Maria Chen (Billing): Finance requests final sign-off from SRE before releasing/keeping credit. Pending engineering postmortem.
Provisional credit applied by Billing; engineering patch in review to prevent duplicate metering increments during fallback retries. Final resolution pending postmortem and verification after prod canary.
If patch verifies in prod canary, Billing to keep provisional credit and mark invoice adjusted. If additional overcharges are found for other customers, run one-off audit and issue credits as needed. Follow-up owner: Maria Chen (Billing) and Jonah Reyes (SRE).
Run prod canary of dedupe patch for 48h and monitor billing counters
Provide NimbleRetail audit CSV showing per-request billing attribution
Add automated alert if router emits >1 metering increment per request in any 10m window

comments: 2026-03-12T04:15:00Z Runtime Eng: Confirmed attach RPC errors appear to surface from device-plugin during high IO wait. Requested device-plugin traces and kube events. Recommends temporary throttle of snapshotter and raising attach timeout to avoid shrink loop.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Background snapshotting/backup job in the dedicated cluster for DataFlowAI is producing short, high-throughput inflight I/O bursts. During these bursts GPUs briefly become unavailable for inference attach operations which triggers the autoscaler to shrink and then rapidly re-expand. Net effect: repeated attach failures, transient allocation gaps, and user-visible P99 latency spikes and 503s for the customer's reserved pool.

Impact:
- Customer: DataFlowAI (dedicated) is seeing p99 generation latency jump from ~120ms to >3s intermittently, plus a 1-2% spike in 503 errors during windows.
- Business: Dedicated SLA exposure for this tenant; potential churn risk if sustained.

Timeline (local timestamps UTC):
- 2026-03-12 03:18: first alert from customer (support ticket).
- 2026-03-12 03:22: Support reproduced elevated p99 in prod-us-west-2 and escalated to SRE.
- 2026-03-12 03:40: SRE observed short (~5-20s) NVMe/io wait spikes on nodes hosting the dedicated pool; correlated with snapshotter throughput peaks.
- 2026-03-12 04:05: Autoscaler recorded rapid shrink (release of GPU slots) followed by re-attach attempts; several attach RPCs timed out.
- 2026-03-12 08:00: Temporary mitigation applied (throttle background snapshot bandwidth for tenant namespace).

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated cluster: prod-us-west-2 reserved pool id: dp-84a9
- Infra: A100 nodes with NVMe-backed local scratch and periodic background snapshotter that flushes to S3
- Customer routes: dedicated reserved model routes pinned to rwkv-14b-quant and gptx-4b variants

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Run production traffic (typical mix of short chat streams + generation).
2) Background snapshotter initiates shard checkpoint flush; observed sustained NVMe write IOPS surge for 5-20s.
3) During the burst, serving runtime reports elevated io_wait%, attach latency increases; autoscaler interprets reduced attach success and triggers shrink.
4) When burst subsides, kube/gpu attach succeeds and autoscaler grows back, causing brief rebalancing and more attach traffic.

Observables & logs:
- Metrics: node.io.wait p95 spikes to 3800ms; gpu_attach_latency p99 increases to >2s; reserved_pool_alloc_failures increased by 8x during windows.
- Kube logs: repeated errors similar to "device plugin: failed to allocate device: timeout attaching GPU" stamped during bursts.
- Snapshotter logs (node agent): "flushing checkpoint shard=237 size=2.1GB duration=18s throughput=120MB/s"
- Autoscaler events: "pool dp-84a9: scaleDown triggered due to attach failures (reason: attach-timeout)"

Investigation notes so far:
- Correlation between snapshotter bandwidth and attach failures is consistent across three independent nodes.
- Noise is tenant-local: other dedicated pools on same cluster did not show same severity; investigation shows DataFlowAI's checkpoint cadence is synchronized across many small shards (many >1GB writes concurrently).
- Hypothesis: high concurrent local NVMe writes cause elevated IO wait and block device hotpaths used by GPU driver or device-plugin, which increases attach RPC latency and causes ephemeral allocation shortfalls.
- Another contributing factor: autoscaler currently uses attach success rate as an input signal and has a conservative cooldown (10m) and rapid shrink policy which amplifies the oscillation when attach telemetry is noisy.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Throttled snapshotter bandwidth for customer namespace to 20MB/s per shard (temporary).
- Blacklisted the snapshotter process from sharing the same NVMe stripes as the GPU device plugin on affected nodes via IO niceness and cgroup IO weight adjustments.
- Raised autoscaler attach-timeout from 5s to 12s for dp-84a9 (short-term) to reduce false-positive shrink decisions.

Proposed long-term actions:
- Run a quota on concurrent snapshot flushes per tenant (service-side control) and stagger checkpoint windows.
- Add a device-plugin health metric that excludes transient local io_wait spikes from immediate autoscaler shrink decisions (introduce smoothing window).
- Consider moving heavy snapshot flushing off local scratch to buffered streaming to S3 to avoid NVMe saturation.
- Update runbook: when you see bursty io + attach-timeouts, first throttle snapshotter and extend attach timeout before moving tenant.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can DataFlowAI adjust checkpoint cadence/config on their side? (Support asked customer for their snapshot schedule and retention settings).
- Should autoscaler be tuned cluster-wide or per-pool? Proposed: per-pool attach-timeout thresholds tied to observed baseline.
- Need SRE to review device-plugin trace to check whether GPU driver threads are blocked during NVMe saturation (assigned to Marco).

SLA notes:
- First response met within 30m. Customer-facing mitigation (throttling) applied within ~5 hours of first report. Engineering action item created for follow-up and permanent mitigations.
2026-03-12 03:25 - Support (Priya Patel): Customer reports intermittent elevated p99 and occasional 503s on their dedicated pool dp-84a9. They provided sample request IDs and times. Asked for immediate triage.

Issue summary: BrightCompose reports repeated mid-window throughput collapses for their dedicated pool. Impact: customer p99 latency increased from 80ms to 2.3s and overall throughput dropped ~42% for 5-15 minute windows several times across the last 48h. Environment: prod dedicated pool in us-west serving gpt-x-2.7b-quant pinned model. Observed behavior: sudden rise in queued requests, many 429 and transient 5xx failures from internal allocator, and frequent short-lived GPU attach failures. Expected behavior: steady throughput within SLA for pinned capacity. This ticket captures support triage, initial hypotheses, telemetry extracts, and mitigation plan.
1) Route steady traffic mimic for BrightCompose workload profile (mix of short chatlets and medium completions) to their dedicated pool in us-west.
2) During simulated midday peak, introduce a bursty background tenant that opens many short-lived multiplexed streams at 30ms interarrival for 5 minutes.
3) Observe autoscaler decisions, allocator attach logs, and per-GPU slot occupancy over the window.
4) Verify p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, and any 5xx/429 spikes from the serving runtime.

2026-03-13T12:05 Lina R. (Allocator): Observed affinity churn for GPU 2-4; prefetched KV cache footprint increased transiently causing eviction pressure and slot fragmentation. Hypothesis: bursty short streams cause slot fragmentation and autoscaler mis-evaluates scale-in/out due to noisy telemetry.
Telemetry: correlated spikes in 'attach_failure_rate' and 'slot_eviction_count' with short-stream fanout events; burst windows show KV-cache working set suddenly expands by ~28% triggering eviction waves.
Autoscaler behavior: evaluation function is sampling latency/queue metrics with a 30s window and has recently had parameter change to shorten smoothing window -> more sensitive to transient spikes, leading to oscillatory decisioning.
Allocator findings: slot fragmentation is high during incidents; many slots are held by ephemeral short-lived connections, preventing efficient batch packing and causing attach contention on remaining GPUs.
Hypothesis: noisy short-stream tenant (not BrightCompose) induces transient KV-cache growth + heartbeat bursts which cause evictions and allocator attach churn. Autoscaler then refrains from scaling due to the short sampling window and low aggregate 'score', leaving pinned pool understaffed to absorb the sudden tail.
Cross-checks: compared with SUP-712909 pattern (warmup lag) but distinct due to higher eviction counts and attach failure signature; linked for context.
Short-term workaround (applied 2026-03-13 14:00 UTC): enabled per-tenant attach backoff smoothing for BrightCompose pool and increased attach_retry window to reduce attach churn. Also applied temporary throttle on ephemeral-tenant connection creation in us-west reserved hosts.

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a soft-promote canary for NebulaAI (dedicated pool) we observed a transient loss of model pin enforcement that resulted in a small fraction of requests being served by a transparent/degraded variant and subsequently lingering after the promote window.
Impact: ~0.7% of NebulaAI requests in us-east were served by the fallback variant for ~15 minutes, resulting in a measurable quality delta for customer QA tests and a spike in token cost for degraded quantized fallback.
Environment: production, dedicated (NebulaAI), us-east region, orchestrator v2.4.1, serving-runtime 1.9.3.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Start soft-promote (10% -> 40%) for redwood-3b-v2; 2) Initiate scheduled prewarm on dedicated pool; 3) Trigger tenant header rotation + edge-proxy reconnect; 4) Observe routing matrix entries and pin map during epoch boundary; expected: pinned sessions maintain variant, actual: some sessions flip to fallback and remain.
Logs/observables: Orchestrator epoch logs (trace ids: 9876a, 9876b) show commit window overlap; edge-proxy reconnects at same timestamps as prewarm handshake (see attached traces). Console shows cohort affinity decay events between 12:03:45 and 12:18:12 UTC.
Workaround: Manual pin refresh for affected tenant via console (force rebind) restored correct routing. Temporary mitigation: pause promote, drain edge-proxy connections, resume with extended commit window.
Notes: Customer reported via #support-nebula thread; billing/quality impact reported to CSM.
Support (Maya Chen 2026-03-10): Customer ticket opened after they ran nightly QA and noticed degraded outputs. Provided initial ask and logs. SLA first response met.
Eng (Diego Ramirez 2026-03-11): Reproduced locally with a staging replay. Hypothesis: routing matrix apply step not honoring active pin set when an epoch boundary coincides with prewarm merge.
SRE (Anika Bose 2026-03-11): Observed edge-proxy reconnects causing partial route diff; prewarm mirror leaves shadow entries that are not properly garbage-collected until next full snapshot.
Support (Maya Chen 2026-03-11): Confirmed manual pin-refresh via console fixed customer session routing. Customer applied fix and confirmed reduction in quality delta.
Eng (Diego Ramirez 2026-03-12): Added a test-case for commit-window overlap in integration harness (PR linked). Working on a patch to make routing apply idempotent wrt pin sets.
Hypothesis 1: Orchestrator commit window pick-up merges shadow mirror entries with stale affinity flags causing session-level routing to evaluate to fallback despite pin present.
Hypothesis 2: Edge-proxy reconnect produced duplicated session cookies with differing cohort fingerprints; routing matrix picks newest fingerprint which lacked pin metadata.
Mitigation verification: Manual rebind invalidates duplicate cookie and forces tenant routing to re-evaluate, which restored pinned variant.
Repro scope: Observed only on dedicated pools with prewarm-mirror enabled and orchestrator version <=2.4.1; not reproduced on hosted API in our tests.
In progress: patch proposed to make routing matrix apply idempotent relative to active pin sets. Short-term: recommend extending commit window and pausing prewarm mirrors for dedicated customers during soft-promotes. Follow-up action: backport patch to 2.4.x and run coordinated rollout; customer notified and scheduled maintenance window.
Patch PR created and under review. Post-deploy verification plan includes telemetry checks for cohort-affinity-evictions and a canary test with NebulaAI in us-east.

payload.description:
Issue summary: KelpGuard reported large numbers of connection resets and truncated streaming responses during a scheduled canary for a custom routing policy. Impact: customer-facing calls returned repeated short-lived connections and ~25% duplicate reconnects leading to degraded transcript completeness for policy inference. Environment: production, us-west-2, customer pinned to dedicated routing policy and enterprise plan.

Observed impact window: 2026-03-11 02:40-03:15 UTC. Customer reported escalations to Redwood Support and SRE due to elevated error rates and user-visible truncations.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Send continuous streaming requests with routing header X-RW-Routing: kelpguard-canary to us-west endpoint.
2) Observe that initial socket connects then resets after 1-3s.
3) Subsequent retries frequently hit a different backend that drops the KV cache leading to partial transcripts.

Logs: Gateway logs show 502/GRPC_CANCELLED on stream tear, routing service logs show affinity token mismatch, serving-runtime reports cache-miss spikes and rapid VM handoffs.

Timeline: 02:42 UTC support acknowledged, 02:50 SRE triaged, 02:55 Canary was paused. Hypothesis: new sticky-routing change deployed in canary routing service introduced a race between affinity assignment and backend selection under bursty connect patterns. Evidence: correlation between routing-service commit deploy at 02:33 and error spike at 02:40; rejected affinity tokens seen in routing trace logs; serving-runtime metric 'kv_cache_invalidation_rate' increased by 12x. Reproduced in isolated canary by replaying 200 RPS with short-lived client connections. Noise from autoscaler: rapid pod churn in dedicated pool contributed to lost affinity mappings.

Cross-references: linked SRE slack thread #incidents and PRs above. Engineering noted two recent commits that changed cookie expiry and fallback ordering in router.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 02:50 - SRE Triage (Jamal Ortiz): Observed GRPC_CANCELLED spikes and affinity rejections in router logs; initiating immediate rollback of canary routing change.
2026-03-11 03:10 - KelpGuard (Customer): Confirmed reduced reconnects and improved transcript completion; requested root-cause and permanent fix timeline.
2026-03-12 14:05 - Product (Anika Patel): Agreed on safety gates for future sticky-routing changes and stricter canary load patterns; requested post-incident action items.
Immediate mitigation: rolled back the routing-service canary (02:56 UTC) which returned affinity behavior to stable. Temporary customer workaround: switched KelpGuard to the conservative routing policy and increased connection hold time to reduce short-lived reconnect patterns. Permanent fix: patch in PR github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/5879 addresses race by ensuring atomic affinity write-read barrier and introducing a short grace TTL for affinity tokens on backend handoff. Patch also adds a canary load pattern guard to avoid rapid connect bursts during canary windows. Deployed to staging 2026-03-12 and scheduled production rollout 2026-03-18 behind a throttled canary ramp.
Race condition in new sticky-routing implementation combined with rapid pod churn from aggressive autoscaler policy. Affinity tokens could be accepted by the assignment path before route lookup caches had replicated the mapping, causing subsequent requests to land on backends that did not have the expected KV prefix and leading to stream resets and truncated outputs.
Add canary load pattern guard: prevent >50 RPS short-lived connect bursts during routing canaries
Introduce atomic write-read barrier for affinity assignments (PR 5879) and add unit+integration tests
Tune autoscaler stabilization window for dedicated pools to reduce rapid pod churn during canaries
Create runbook entry for Support to toggle conservative routing policy during high-risk canaries
Schedule 1:1 with KelpGuard engineering to review change control and acceptance criteria (target week of 2026-03-16)

Sentry event IDs: sentry.io/organizations/redwood/issues/85733/

payload.description:
Customer reports that when a mobile user (Android, Chrome) transitions between Wi-Fi networks or the device enters a deep-sleep power-save state, the streamed response frequently arrives without the final paragraph and closing metadata. The visible stream contains all earlier paragraphs plus a keepalive/heartbeat chunk, then the connection is re-established but the final paragraph is missing. This differs from typical partial-token cases: the finalization marker ("event: end") is not observed in logs for affected sessions.
1) Use ClarionDocs integration to call chat-completion streaming endpoint with a 2-3 paragraph prompt that returns a multi-paragraph finalization.
2) On Android (Chrome), start on office Wi-Fi, then trigger a switch to cellular or force the device into background (simulated via Developer Options -> Dont keep activities / or use Nexus 6 emulator with network toggles).
3) Observe SSE/ws stream in client SDK (v1.8.3) — note heartbeat chunks and then an immediate re-open. Final paragraph is not present; client sees stream end without closing metadata.
4) Replaying the same request from a desktop client or keeping the connection stable does not reproduce the missing-final-paragraph behavior.
5) Attach full HAR and SDK debug output captured from the mobile client session.
6) Confirm server-side logs for the request id (included in logs_snippets) show no "finalize" event delivered to the connection that was torn down.
When the client experiences transient network handoff or sleep, the server should either deliver the finalization marker before connection teardown or allow the resumed session to request the missing tail (idempotent resume) so the final paragraph is re-emitted.
Affected sessions show a keepalive/heartbeat chunk then an abrupt disconnect; after reconnect, client receives full stream up to but excluding final paragraph and the closing metadata event. There is no explicit server-side error; connection logs show a graceful close from upstream LB in some cases.

2026-03-10T15:12:09.004Z DEBUG conn_id=az-01-7ff heartbeat=sent seq=118
2026-03-10T15:12:09.212Z WARN conn_pool=frontline lb_hint=idle_teardown conn_id=az-01-7ff upstream_close=keepalive_timeout
2026-03-10T15:12:09.246Z INFO request=cli-83f72 stream_finalizer=not_emitted conn_id=az-01-7ff
2026-03-10T15:12:11.612Z INFO conn_reopen conn_id=bz-09-a10 request=cli-83f72 resume_token=seq118
2026-03-10T15:12:11.613Z INFO reattach_attempt request=cli-83f72 resumed_seq=118 client_received_until=118
2026-03-10T15:12:11.614Z INFO response_sent_up_to seq=118 (no finalize)
2026-03-10T15:12:11.615Z DEBUG sdk-client: last_event=\"data\":\"...\" client-log: \"stream closed without end event\"

Additional notes:
- Reproduced on Android emulator when toggling cellular/Wi-Fi; not reproduced on desktop.
- Grafana trace for request cli-83f72: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/stream-traces?orgId=1&var-request=cli-83f72 shows LB idle_teardown at 2.3s after last payload write.
- Correlated with frontend LB config: idle timeout 2s for h2->h1 translation path. This explains upstream_close=keepalive_timeout entries.
- Serving runtime currently relies on in-memory 'end-event' emission during final token write; if upstream connection closes before the write is ACKed, we do not persist the end-event to the resume store.
- Hypothesis: Connection handoff combined with coalesced keepalives leads to server not observing final write completion; LB issues a graceful close which our pipeline treats as normal close and skips persisting finalize state.
Mitigation applied (2026-03-11): Increase LB idle timeout for streaming h2->h1 path from 2s to 10s for customer-dedicated pool. This reduced occurrences in ClarionDocs traffic from ~8% to ~1.2% in a 24h window.
Code fix (in review): Persist finalize marker to resume-store before acknowledging final token write to connection; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2245 (adds durable end-event write).
Customer workaround: Enable client-side resume logic in SDK v1.8.3 by providing last_received_seq as resume param. ClarionDocs adopted this in their mobile SDK to request missing tail on reconnect.
Status: Partial fix deployed to customer pool + runtime PR in review. Closing pending confirmation of patch and infra rollback plan for LB timeouts if needed.
1) Merge PR #2245 and release runtime v1.12.0 that durably persists end-event (owner: Ethan Monroe, ETA 2026-03-17).
2) Create infra ticket INT-82012 to audit LB idle timeout across streaming paths and set sane defaults for mobile-heavy pools (owner: Mateo Ruiz).
3) Update Streaming Handoff Runbook to include step: if keepalive coalescing observed, temporarily raise LB idle timeout and enable resume-store debugging (owner: On-call SRE).
4) Recommend SDK change: make resume-by-seq automatic for v1.9+ and document in breaking-changes (owner: Developer Experience).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer sees incomplete streamed payloads from SSE endpoint when their clients perform path migration (HTTP/3) or resume TLS 0-RTT. The last token of a JSON array (the closing "]") is missing, and a small metadata line ("::meta:session") is duplicated in the final frames. Impact: downstream parsers throw JSON parse errors and the customer application truncates saved transcripts. Occurs intermittently (3-8% of sessions) under higher concurrency and during client network transitions.

Impact: Blocks AcmeForms production ingestion pipeline (batch-facing form summarization). Customer reports ~17% failed jobs when they have concurrent SSE sessions per host. They are on Dedicated capacity and require a P1 response.

Environment: Dedicated serving pool (cluster-id: ded-west-11), customer VPC peered to us-west-2, clients are using a mobile browser SDK with HTTP/3 enabled and 0-RTT TLS enabled. Observed when mobile device switches between Wi‑Fi and cellular or when NAT mapping changes.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start SSE session to /v1/stream with model=open/llama-13b, accept: text/event-stream.
2) Send a prompt that results in a streamed JSON array response (large list, 900-1200 tokens).
3) While stream is active, trigger a client network handover (Wi‑Fi -> LTE) or enable QUIC path migration in the client lib.
4) Allow client to resume; observe final event(s) delivered.

Observed behavior:
- Stream ends without the trailing "]" token.
- A small metadata event line similar to "event: meta\n:data: {\"session\":\"abc123\"}\n\n" appears twice near the end.
- Parsers error on incomplete JSON array.

Expected behavior:
- Complete JSON payload with closing array token and a single metadata event.

Customer logs / sample: (sanitized)
- request_id: rwd-20260313-9a5b
- trace: trace-77da
- last received SSE frames (line-delimited):
  data: ["choice1", "choice2", "choice3", ... "choiceN"
  event: meta
  data: {"session":"abc123"}
  event: meta
  data: {"session":"abc123"}

  (connection closed)

- Note: the closing bracket "]" never arrives.

Client-side: reported client SDK v1.8.4 with QUIC path migration enabled and TLS early-data (0-RTT). Server-side: dedicated pool running runtime v2.11.3 behind the API gateway with HTTP/3 and keepalive enabled.

Attachments: customer pcap (redacted), stacktrace of parser failure, chunk log for request rwd-20260313-9a5b.
- Reproduced internally with simulated path migration using a QUIC emulator and 0-RTT replays; saw same symptom at low frequency when connection handover happened mid-stream.
- Correlation with worker log timestamps shows resume request arriving on a different worker (worker-id changed) and the resume handshake finishing while the tail buffer on the original worker still had pending buffered frames.
- Hypothesis A: resume/handshake idempotency token reused by client leads gateway to route resumed connection to new worker, old worker flushes remaining chunk set but our resume aggregator drops the final closing token because it believes resume has been completed earlier.
- Hypothesis B: early-data (0-RTT) replay at the gateway causes duplicate metadata emission path (metadata event is emitted both from pre-handshake buffer and post-handshake requeued frames).
