payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer sees duplicate external tool/function invocations when clients retry requests during short retry windows. The duplicates only appear for multi-call chat interactions that include function/tool calling (webhook to downstream job system). Root cause suspected to be cross-SDK idempotency token normalization differences combined with a tight retry window and batching behaviors.

Impact: Several dozen duplicate downstream jobs were launched over a 48-hour window for a single workflow. Customer reports increased cost and a handful of duplicated side effects (emails, DB writes) requiring manual dedup. This impacts production traffic for NovusHealth's onboarding pipeline and is blocking confidence in enabling automatic retries.

Environment details: Production Redwood hosted API, region us-east-1. Customer uses three SDKs in orchestrator: Python 1.7.3 (requests-based), TypeScript 0.9.8 (fetch-based), and Go 0.6.2 (net/http). They run a multiplexer that batches small chat messages to improve throughput; server-side us-east serving fleet running redwood-serving v2026.02.3.

Observed behavior: When a transient 502 occurs in the API gateway, client SDKs retry (backoff) inside a 3s retry window. In several cases we observe two retries being accepted by the server as distinct requests (not deduped) even though the customer attached an idempotency token. Post-facto analysis shows the idempotency token value received by the backend differs between attempts in subtle ways (timestamp formatting and microsecond truncation). Some retries are routed to a different shard which has an older cached canonicalization rule.

Expected behavior: Retries with the same idempotency token should be deduplicated at server-side so that external function/tool/webhook calls are not executed more than once. SDKs should present a canonical idempotency header consistently across languages.

Attachments: sample headers and truncated logs are below in the logs field.

Customer asks: 1) immediate mitigation steps to stop duplicate downstream jobs; 2) guidance for SDKs and orchestration patterns to avoid duplicates; 3) whether we can make server-side idempotency tolerant to token formatting differences.
Create a chat session with two function calls in a single message batch (function A then function B).
Attach client-side generated idempotency token: iso8601 timestamp + nonce (e.g. 2026-03-08T15:02:17.123456Z|nonce123).
Configure policy: client retries on 5xx with binary exponential backoff, max window 3s, max retries 2.
Simulate transient 502 on first request to trigger client retry.
Observe backend logs and downstream webhook logs for duplicated invocations of A and/or B.
--- Request attempt 1 (from python): Idempotency-Token: 2026-03-08T15:02:17.123456Z|nonce123
--- Request attempt 2 (from python retry): Idempotency-Token: 2026-03-08T15:02:17.123456Z|nonce123
--- Request attempt 1 (from go): Idempotency-Token: 2026-03-08T15:02:17.123Z|nonce123 (go truncated microseconds)
--- Request attempt 1 (from ts): Idempotency-Token: 2026-03-08T15:02:17.123456+00:00|nonce123 (ts includes explicit timezone offset)
--- Server saw tokens normalized to different canonical strings on different shards: '2026-03-08T15:02:17.123456Z|nonce123' vs '2026-03-08T15:02:17.123Z|nonce123' vs '2026-03-08T15:02:17.123456+00:00|nonce123'
--- Downstream webhook invoked twice for function 'create_user_profile', request IDs: job-7791 and job-7792

Additional notes:
2026-03-08 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Acknowledged. Setting priority P2. Asking for SDK versions and whether the customer sets idempotency header manually or uses SDK auto-generation.
2026-03-09 - NovusHealth (CS contact - Javier Ruiz): We use SDK auto-generate in Python and TS; Go is a thin wrapper around the HTTP client with a small helper that formats timestamp via time.Format(time.RFC3339Nano) but then we locally trim trailing zeros for compactness. We did not think trimming would affect deduping.
2026-03-09 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed we can reproduce a mismatch locally by sending tokens with different timezone encodings and microsecond precision. Added a temporary server-side tolerance rule for this tenant to map tokens by parsed (timestamp, nonce) pair (accepted for 72 hours).
2026-03-10 - SRE (Anika Patel): Investigating shard config; observed a stale token-canonicalization lib on two older serving nodes. Raising an infra patch to standardize canonicalization across the fleet.
2026-03-11 - SDK PM (Ravi Singh): Proposing a patch across SDKs to normalize idempotency header generation to RFC3339Nano with forced 'Z' timezone and preserved microseconds; also adding tests and docs.
2026-03-12 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Customer accepted temporary tenant-level mitigation. Will schedule SDK updates and server-side normalization rollout. Marking ticket In Progress.
Hypothesis 1: Clients produce semantically identical tokens but different string encodings; server-side shard-local canonicalization mismatch leads to treating them as distinct keys.
Hypothesis 2: Batching and multiplexing cause different attempts for the same logical request to be routed to different API gateway nodes which consult different token caches with different canonicalization behavior.
Findings: Reproduced locally using python/ts/go clients with deliberate token encoding differences. Found two serving nodes with redwood-serving v2026.01.7 missing the canonicalization patch. Once patched, deduping worked consistently in lab.
Risk: Until fleet-wide patch is deployed, customers using mixed-language orchestrators are at higher risk of duplicates under transient gateway errors.
Short-term mitigation (applied): Tenant-level request interceptor added that parses Idempotency-Token into (timestamp, nonce) and maps variants to a canonical token to dedupe for 72 hours. Customer confirmed duplicate jobs stopped after intervention.
Medium-term: Roll out redwood-serving patch v2026.03.15 that enforces server-side canonicalization of idempotency tokens by parsing timestamps and normalizing timezone+microseconds before keying. Will deploy to canary then fleet by 2026-03-15.
Long-term: SDK changes across Python/TS/Go to auto-generate tokens using a shared canonical format: RFC3339Nano with 'Z' suffix and fixed 6-digit microsecond field (pad/truncate to 6 digits). Add interop tests to SDK CI and include a migration note in the Idempotency section of the docs.
Docs/workflow guidance: Recommend customers include a stable nonce component (uuid4) and avoid ad-hoc string trimming. Add example helper functions for Python/TS/Go in docs page 'Idempotency tokens: best practices'
Follow-ups: Create INT ticket to track serving fleet rollout (INT-90123). Create GH PR for SDKs linked in related_github_prs. Postmortem to include cost impact analysis and recommendations for default tenant safety guardrails.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbleDocs reported a sharp degradation in perceived inference latency for a subset of endpoints starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Customer traffic is routed through Redwood hosted API (prod, us-east). The customer is on Dedicated tier with pinned model gptx-3.8-rlhf.

Impact:
- ~30% of requests from the customer's tenant observed >2s added tail latency and ~7% client-side timeouts reported from their monitoring.
- No platform-wide outage; increase concentrated to NimbleDocs' tenant and coincidentally a small group of other customers using the same SDK version.

Environment / context:
- Redwood hosted API (prod, us-east), dedicated capacity pool for customer.
- Customer using redwood-sdk-java v1.4.2 (default HTTP client config).
- Model variants: gptx-3.8-rlhf (primary), gptx-3.8-quant (fallback).
- SDK default connection pool configured with maxConnections=1 per host in this version for legacy compatibility; retry_policy: retry_on_5xx=true, retry_attempts=5, backoff=exponential(base_ms=400) with no jitter by default.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Send steady stream of chat-completion requests at ~12 qps with concurrent client threads (20 threads) and streaming response enabled.
2) Observe that after ~30s of load, p95 latency climbs and a number of client requests time out (client-side 30s timeout).
3) Restarting client processes temporarily restores normal latencies until load ramps again.

Observed behaviour:
- Server ingestion and per-request processing times remain within normal bounds (per-host token throughput steady).
- Connection metrics show many client connections short-lived; server logs show serialized request arrival bursts from the same client IPs.
- Client-side traces show requests being retried serially due to single-connection pool exhaustion and aggressive retry attempts, amplifying end-to-end latency.

Expected behaviour:
- Client SDK should use connection pooling and non-blocking retries to avoid serialized retries that add to end-to-end latency.

Attached / referenced evidence:
- Customer-provided flamegraphs and trace IDs (redacted) and sample request IDs: RID: 20260309-UE7-8832
- Internal logs indicating connection churn and HTTP 502->retry patterns in front-end load balancer.
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/nimbledocs-tenant?from=2026-03-09T21:50:00Z

Support (2026-03-10 04:05 UTC): Opened ticket after NimbleDocs raised alert. Initial triage indicates client-side retry behavior may be amplifying latency. Assigned to SRE + SDK owners.
SRE (Marius Chen) (2026-03-10 05:20 UTC): Correlated tenant's source IP with connection metrics. Observed max_connections_in_use frequently hitting 1 and average request queue length on client side growing. No server-side CPU/GPU saturation observed.
SDK (Leah Ortiz) (2026-03-10 08:45 UTC): Reproduced locally with redwood-sdk-java v1.4.2 using 20 concurrent threads; observed sequentialized retries when pool size=1. Behavior fixed when pool size increased to 8 and retry_attempts reduced to 2 with jitter enabled.
Customer (NimbleDocs - Martin Delaney) (2026-03-10 12:10 UTC): Confirmed temporary mitigation by toggling client config (increased pool size and lower retries), tail latency returned to baseline for the next 3 hours during testing. Asked for recommended long-term fix and whether Redwood will adjust defaults.
Support (2026-03-11 09:00 UTC): Escalated to SDK maintainers to ship a patch and to DX/docs to update quickstart guidance for concurrent workloads and streaming use-cases. Logged follow-up actions below.
2026-03-10 05:00 UTC - SRE: No GPU or node-level degradation in dedicated pool. Serving runtime per-request tokens processed within SLO. Indicates client-side serialization upstream.
2026-03-10 06:15 UTC - Network: Frontend ELB logs show bursts of re-issued requests (retries) from same client IP; request inter-arrival times indicate back-to-back retries rather than independent concurrent requests.
2026-03-10 07:30 UTC - SDK repro: With v1.4.2 defaults, a transient 502 causes up to 5 retry attempts; because pool=maxConnections=1, retries wait on the single connection leading to queuing at client and high client-observed latency.
Change of server health check frequency increased transient 502s by a small margin during rolling maintenance earlier that evening, which triggered retry cascade for affected tenants.
2026-03-10 08:40 UTC - Mitigation test: Adjusting SDK to maxConnections=8, retry_attempts=2, exponential backoff base_ms=200 with jitter reduces client-side queueing. Add async request path avoids blocking UI threads for customers using sync clients.
2026-03-11 03:20 UTC - Root cause hypothesis: A confluence of (1) SDK default pool set to 1 in v1.4.2 for legacy compat, (2) default high retry_attempts with no jitter, and (3) a short-lived increase in 502s from a frontend rolling update. These combined to create a retry cascade that serialized traffic per-client and produced perceived platform slowness for the tenant.
2026-03-11 07:00 UTC - Risk assessment: Any other tenants using the same SDK defaults are at risk under transient errors; customers using async clients or newer SDK versions not affected.
Mitigation and fix deployed:
1) Immediate customer workaround: Advised NimbleDocs to update local SDK config: set maxConnections=8, retry_attempts=2, enable jitter (add +/- 20%), and switch to async client where possible. Customer applied changes and confirmed latency returned to baseline.
2) Short-term platform mitigation: SRE adjusted frontend retry gating to be more conservative during rolling updates and added a temporary alert for unusual client-side retry spikes tied to tenant IDs.
3) SDK patch: SDK team published hotfix redwood-sdk-java v1.4.3 (PR #482) which changes default maxConnections to 8 for modern clients, reduces default retry_attempts to 2, and enables jitter in exponential backoff. Patch includes a migration note in CHANGELOG.
4) Long-term actions (planned):
   - Update Quickstart docs and streaming recipes to call out pool sizing and retry settings for high-concurrency streaming workloads.
   - Add a runbook entry to detect and respond to client-side retry cascades, including automated dashboards and an alert on per-tenant retry amplification.
   - Create a telemetry bucket to surface SDK versions associated with high retry amplification and notify Customer Success for outreach.

Ticket status: Leaving this ticket open while customer validates production stability for 72 hours and SDK release propagation is monitored. Follow-ups assigned to SDK and SRE teams (see linked PR and runbook).
payload.summary: Persistent client-side retry cascade + single-connection pooling from tenant SDKs causing perceived inference slowdowns

Issue summary: During a staged canary merge for KeplerDocs' dedicated cluster, ~12% of tenant requests started receiving responses from an unexpected legacy variant and then fell back to degraded variants, causing elevated latency and quality regressions. Impact: KeplerDocs reported a production-quality regression for a small subset of sessions and multiple application-level timeouts. Customer observed ~3–5% of requests returning legacy variant outputs over a 20-minute window. Root cause hypothesis: metadata hash collision between two concurrent canary slices produced non-deterministic cohort assignment for the tenant's session pin key, resulting in split pin state across orchestrator shards and subsequent fallback when one variant experienced transient prewarm eviction.
1) Configure a weighted canary with 5% slices for variant A (rw-open-13b-v1) and variant B (rw-open-6b-alpha) in prod/us-east on a dedicated capacity pool.
2) Use the customer’s tenant API key and replay a steady request stream (200 qps) with the session cookie header 'rw-session' set to a reproducible cohort id (example: cohort-88c3b5).
3) Run the control-plane canary merge operation that performs metadata snapshot + hash-based cohort split (internal runbook step: /confluence/canary-merge-v2) while simultaneously toggling a background prewarm optimization on the orchestrator.
4) Observe routing decisions in the edge-proxy and orchestrator: look for pin assignment differences between edge shards (edge-proxy logs) and control-plane (routing snapshot digest mismatches).
5) Verify intermittent fallback by inspecting model headers in responses and the serving-runtime logs for fallback triggers and eviction notices.
Approximately 3–5% of requests for the tenant were routed to the legacy variant; these sessions intermittently switched between pinned variants mid-session. The edge-proxy log shows 'pin_assignment: cohort-88c3b5 -> variant=rw-open-6b-alpha' for some shards and 'pin_assignment: cohort-88c3b5 -> variant=rw-open-13b-v1' for others. When one variant received a prewarm eviction, the split cohort triggered fallback logic and elevated latency as requests retried against alternative models.
Cohort pin computation should be deterministic across control-plane and edges: a given session key should map to a single variant during a canary slice period unless a deliberate remap/rollout is applied. Fallbacks should only occur when a variant actually fails, not because of mismatched pin state.
edge-proxy[edge-24]: pin_calc(h=0x7f12a9) cohort=88c3b5 -> rw-open-13b-v1
edge-proxy[edge-19]: pin_calc(h=0x0f7a1c) cohort=88c3b5 -> rw-open-6b-alpha
orchestrator[orch-03]: snapshot-merge: metadata_hash=0x7f12a9 vs expected=0x7f12a9; shard_consensus=split
control-plane[cp-02]: debug: metadata-hash-collision detected during merge; conflicting keys: [tenant=kepler-42 cohort=88c3b5]
serving-runtime[gpu-11]: prewarm: eviction due to OOM soft threshold; trigger fallback for cohort=88c3b5
2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Customer alert reported unexpected model outputs. 2026-03-10 09:17 UTC: Support acknowledged and opened ticket. 2026-03-10 09:35 UTC: SRE attached edge-proxy routing logs. 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC: Control-plane trace revealed metadata hash mismatch noted during canary merge. 2026-03-10 10:40 UTC: Mitigation (temporarily paused merging operation) applied. 2026-03-12 14:10 UTC: Engineering reproducer validated hash collision on a controlled staging run.
Hypothesis: The control-plane used a truncated 32-bit metadata CRC to compute cohort buckets during a high-concurrency canary merge which led to collisions for certain cohort keys.
Reproducer: Simulated the canary merge path with random metadata ordering; collision observed when two distinct metadata blocks hashed to same 32-bit digest and different orchestrator shards accepted different snapshots before reconciliation.
Edge evidence: edge-proxy logs show deterministic but differing hash inputs across shards due to non-idempotent map iteration order in snapshot generation when the 'prewarm' flag toggled concurrently.
Telemetry: routing-cohort-mismatch metric increased from 0.01% baseline to 3.8% during merge window on customer cluster.
Short-term mitigation validated: pause merge, force a consistent snapshot order (sort keys), and re-run merge — pins remained stable in validation window.
Immediate: paused the canary merge and rolled back the merge commit. For customers experiencing split-pinning we recommended restarting the tenant session cookies (temporary cookie rotation) to force a fresh deterministic mapping. Engineering applied a hotfix to abort merges upon detection of shard-level cohort mapping divergence.
Use of a truncated 32-bit metadata digest combined with non-deterministic snapshot key ordering in the control-plane's canary merge path led to hash collisions and inconsistent cohort-to-variant assignments across orchestrator shards. When a variant experienced prewarm eviction, the split cohort produced unexpected fallback behavior.
Engineering implemented three changes: 1) switch metadata digest to 128-bit (xxh3_128) for bucket computation, 2) enforce deterministic snapshot ordering (sorted map keys) during merge, and 3) add a merge-time validation step that aborts if shard consensus for cohort mapping is not unanimous. Hotfix deployed to prod/dedicated on 2026-03-12 06:00 UTC; monitored for 24 hours with no recurrence on the customer cluster.
Workaround applied and hotfix deployed. Customer confirmed no further legacy-variant responses after fix and cookie rotation. Incident remains open until 2026-03-15 for post-deploy monitoring and to complete a short postmortem. Follow-ups: add end-to-end test for metadata digest, update runbook /confluence/canary-merge-v2 with new validation step, and communicate to customers with dedicated clusters about recommended cookie rotation during merges.
2026-03-10 09:20 - KeplerDocs (Raj Patel): 'We see a small percentage of documents being returned in the old style. This is breaking our downstream QA checks. Can you confirm if pins can flip mid-session?'
2026-03-10 09:28 - Support (Aisha Khatri): 'Thanks Raj — we've escalated to SRE and are collecting routing logs. Can you provide a request example and the session cookie value for a few affected traces?'
2026-03-10 09:42 - SRE (Liam Chen): 'Observed inconsistent cohort mapping across edge-proxy shards. Attaching logs. Paused canary merge to stop further split commits.'

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 14:20 - Engineering (Liam Chen): 'Patched merge to include 128-bit metadata digest and added a guard to abort commit on conflicting cohort mappings. Test run on staging produced stable pin assignments for 10k simulated cohorts.'

payload.description:
Issue summary:
An aggressive optimizer profile (experimental profile 'aggr-prefetch-v3') was enabled for BrightHealth AI tenant in Dedicated capacity. Within minutes we observed P95/P99 tail latency spikes and intermittent 5xx responses for long-sequence streaming requests.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency increased: 95th latency rose from ~120ms to ~2.7s for token streaming paths.
- Spike in 5xx errors (503/504) and a few OOMs on one GPU node in their Dedicated pool.
- Production traffic was degraded for ~18 minutes before mitigations.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool: dhp-dedicated-us-east-4 (A100s), tenant BrightHealth AI.
- Model: redwood-v2-7b pinned at version 2026-02-18.
- Optimizer profile applied: aggr-prefetch-v3 (changes: prefix KV prefetch enabled + target_batch_size from auto->256 + delayed flush window).

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Apply optimizer profile 'aggr-prefetch-v3' via console -> tenant overrides.
2) Send long-sequence streaming requests (~2048 tokens) with concurrent clients at 30 RPS.
3) Observe serving/runtime metrics for request queue length and KV cache hit/miss.

Observed behavior:
- Sustained queue growth on a subset of shards.
- KV cache evictions climbed rapidly; prefetch thrash and increased host<->GPU PCIe traffic.
- Autoscaler did not immediately pick up the pressure due to burst policy thresholds.

Expected behavior:
- Optimizer profile should improve tail latency for typical workloads and not cause sustained queue growth or OOMs.

Logs & metrics:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant-brighthealth/tenant-serving-overview?from=2026-03-10T14:00:00Z&to=2026-03-10T15:00:00Z
- Error logs sample: request_id=rcq_9f7a, 2026-03-10T14:07:12Z, "kv_cache_eviction_rate=0.86, queue_len=72, gpu_mem_free=1.2GB"
- Node OOM events: kube://dhp-node-17 (oom_kill)

Customer impact note:
Customer reported a critical degradation affecting a staging-to-prod migration gate for a marketing launch. They requested immediate rollback help and confirmation of a safe rollback path that avoids cold-start regressions.
Support (2026-03-10 14:12 UTC) - Asha Patel: Acknowledged. Opening incident, prioritizing P1. I requested immediate snapshot of optimizer config and tenant traffic split. Asked SRE for node health and autoscaler logs.
SRE (2026-03-10 14:18 UTC) - Jamie Liu: Observed increased PCIe and host memory churn on node dhp-node-17; several pods showing high iowait. Autoscaler didn't scale because average CPU across pool remained below threshold; queue growth happened on per-shard basis.
Customer (2026-03-10 14:22 UTC) - BrightHealth Oncall: We rolled the change back from our side but see residual 5xx on some requests. Need confirmation the profile is fully disabled per-tenant and whether traffic was routed to fallback model variants.
Support (2026-03-10 14:28 UTC) - Marco Ruiz: Confirmed profile unset at tenant override layer. Initiating controlled per-tenant snapshot restore and staged traffic isolation to remove prefetch hooks. Also applied temporary rate-limit to tenant token throughput to prevent immediate re-thrashing.
SRE (2026-03-10 14:40 UTC) - Jamie Liu: Performed a hot-snapshot restore of the last stable optimizer snapshot (2026-03-09T02:12Z) for BrightHealth tenant on 3 affected shards. Evictions fell and queue length returned to normal within 9 minutes.
Customer (2026-03-10 15:05 UTC) - BrightHealth Oncall: Confirmed latency recovered and 5xx reduced to baseline. Thanks. Requesting a short post-incident summary and recommended safe profile rollout checklist.
Support (2026-03-11 09:10 UTC) - Marco Ruiz: Created this ticket to capture the mitigation steps, findings, and recommended preflight checks. Added follow-up tasks for engineering to harden circuit-breakers.
Hypothesis: Aggressive prefetch + larger target batch size caused pathological cache churn for long-tail sequence distribution used by this tenant.
Telemetry shows per-shard queue growth rather than cluster-wide CPU pressure—indicates scheduler/placement sensitivity to sequence-length skew.
Autoscaler logic thresholds are average-based and lacked per-shard burst response—contributed to 10-15 minute reaction lag.
No evidence of code regressions in model runtime; related PR (runtime#4821) was experimental flags-only and toggles look correct.
KV cache metrics show increased eviction_rate from 0.05 -> 0.86 during incident window.
One node hit OOM; root cause was combined host memory pressure from prefetch buffers and larger batch kernel memory reservation.
Fallback routing did not trigger because the fallback policy only matches when node health is 'unhealthy' not on per-shard queue thresholds.
Confirmed tenant override and immediately unset optimizer profile 'aggr-prefetch-v3'.
Applied temporary tenant-level token throughput throttle (reduce to 60% of baseline) to avoid immediate re-thrash during recovery window.
Hot restored optimizer snapshot (2026-03-09T02:12Z) to 3 affected shards to rehydrate stable KV profile and kernel settings.
Isolated routing: drained new connections from 2 noisy shards and rebalanced traffic across spare capacity nodes.
Filed internal engineering ticket to add per-shard queue-based autoscaler trigger (see linked issue SUP-82401).
Step 1: Disable tenant optimizer override from Console -> Tenant -> Optimizer Overrides.
Step 2: If 5xx persists, apply immediate tenant token throttle: support API POST /admin/tenant/throttle {tenant_id, pct=60}.
Step 3: Hot-restore last-known-good optimizer snapshot using admin CLI: redwood admin snapshot restore --tenant <id> --snapshot 2026-03-09T02:12Z
Step 4: If node OOM observed, cordon and drain the affected node and restart pods after verifying kernel memory release.
Rolled back tenant optimizer override, restored last stable optimizer snapshot to affected shards, applied temporary throughput throttling, and rebalanced traffic. Latency and error rates returned to baseline. Engineering to implement per-shard autoscaler triggers and a per-tenant optimizer gating rule before reintroducing aggressive profiles.
ENG-1258: Implement per-shard queue-length autoscaler trigger and test under synthetic long-sequence workload.
ENG-1259: Add optimizer profile gating checks in Console UI and disallow 'aggr-prefetch-v3' globally until safety validation completes.
DOCS-77: Publish a 'Safe Rollout' checklist for optimizer profiles (including prefetched memory budget estimation and per-tenant shadow runs).
SRE-404: Update incident runbook to include hot-snapshot restore steps and tenant throttle API examples.
2026-03-10 14:14 UTC: Acknowledged incident and escalated to SRE. Requested temporary mitigation permission.
2026-03-10 14:30 UTC: Informed customer we were unsetting the optimizer override and applying a short throttle while we restore snapshots.
2026-03-10 15:08 UTC: Notified customer that metrics returned to baseline and recommended waiting 24h before reintroducing changes and to run the preflight checklist.
Run tenant-specific synthetic workload that matches 95th/99th sequence length distribution for 30 minutes.
Estimate KV cache memory impact via 'optimizer-sim --profile aggr-prefetch-v3 --tenant <id>' and confirm < 40% of host spare memory.
Enable profile in shadow mode for 1% traffic for 6 hours and monitor eviction_rate and queue_len per shard.
Ensure autoscaler per-shard triggers are enabled or manual escalation plan is in place.

Issue summary:
Customer CumulusMart reported intermittent streaming responses that showed interleaved fragments and partial duplicate transcripts for multi-part chat completions. Symptoms began 2026-03-10 01:20 UTC and recurred on subsequent traffic spikes. Impact: several customer-facing sessions returned mixed transcripts (segments from two separate handler instances), resulting in corrupted messages and increased token billing for duplicate partial outputs.

Impact:
- Affected ~12% of CumulusMart's streamed completions during the incident window (peak 01:20–03:50 UTC).
- Some sessions exhibited fragment interleaving (parts from two different responses merged out-of-order).
- Elevated token usage contributed to a billing delta (temporary credit issued — see Resolution).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: cumulus-dedicated-us-east (reserved capacity).
- Models used: redwood-8k-v1 primary, redwood-quant-4bit-v1 as fallback.
- Traffic routed through api-gateway cluster rgw-3 and routing control-plane region us-east-ctrl.

Steps to reproduce (observed in customer traffic):
1) Start a multi-turn streaming chat against their pinned model (redwood-8k-v1).
2) During a reservoir spike (>180 rps), routing control-plane health-checks flagged a subset of model hosts as degraded and initiated fallback to redwood-quant-4bit-v1.
3) Requests for long-context sessions got partially served by host A (old KV state) then re-routed mid-stream to host B (different KV prefix), producing interleaved chunks and duplicate partial completions.

Observed behavior / logs:
- api-gateway logs show rapid route flips for a subset of session IDs: route-change events within single request lifetime. (logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-east/rgw-3/2026-03-10/stream-flip-*.gz)
- Serving runtime traces show mismatched KV-cache-version headers (kv-v: 17 vs kv-v: 18) across stream fragments for the same session id.
- Control plane health-checks returned transient 503s to router with increased flapping between 01:18–01:36 UTC.
- Linked incident on status page INC-20260310-03 (routing failover automation triggered).

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Support enabled sticky routing for affected customer (sticky until session end) at 01:40 UTC to prevent mid-stream handoff.
- Disabled cross-variant automatic fallback for sessions with active KV cache > 1k tokens.
- Opened emergency SRE rotation and paused a pending routing rollout.

Customer impact and communication:
- Customer sent urgent escalation via account channel at 01:30 UTC. Support acknowledged at 01:34 UTC and provided mitigation timeline.
- Customer-facing SLO degradation: brief stream corruption and billing exposure. Credits offered and accepted (details in Resolution).

Next actions (follow-up):
- Short-term: add KV-cache-version propagation to routing handshake to avoid cross-variant mismatches.
- Medium-term: add atomic route handoff that drains active KV namespaces before switching host for sticky sessions.
- Postmortem: full RCA and retro, update runbook for routing rollout safety checks.

Additional notes:
01:18–01:36 UTC: routing control-plane health-checks reported transient increased latency for backend host group A; automation triggered fallback to quant variant for some requests.
Trace evidence: stream fragments for session s-8a7f2 show kv-v header 17 then 18 within ~2s window; fragments merged by client produced interleaving.
Hypothesis: control-plane triggered fallback mid-request while downstream runtime had active KV state tied to original host; fallback host served partial completion without cache priming, so fragments had different context.
Reproduction attempt in staging: simulated host flapping with synthetic traffic produced deterministic interleaving when route-change occurred before 'kv-cache primed' event completed on new host.
Telemetry: affected request IDs clustered to a subset of router instances (rgw-3b/rgw-3c) behind a recent BGP overlay change that increased control-plane latency under burst load.
Root cause: routing control-plane health-check flapping combined with non-atomic route handoffs allowed mid-request re-routing to hosts with different KV cache versions, causing fragment interleaving and duplicate partial outputs.
Fixes applied:
- Immediate: enabled per-session sticky routing and disabled cross-variant fallback for long-context sessions during the incident window.
- Patch: added kv-cache-version propagation in routing metadata and a 500ms drain/priming window before finalizing route switch (PR merged).
- Operational: paused the in-progress routing rollout linked to the BGP overlay change; added canary safety checks to prevent mid-request flips.
- Customer remediation: issued a partial billing credit for the affected window and scheduled a technical deep-dive; customer accepted credit on 2026-03-12.
Follow-ups assigned:
- ENG: implement atomic route handoff and KV version gating (owner: Marco Ruiz, ETA: 2026-03-25).
- SRE: add routing health-check smoothing and per-router telemetry alerting (owner: Anya Patel, ETA: 2026-03-18).
- Support: coordinate postmortem and customer-facing RCA document (owner: Sofia Morales, ETA: 2026-03-17).
payload.summary: CumulusMart — intermittent streaming fragment interleaving due to routing oscillation (post-incident escalation)

Issue summary:
Customers using our reranking endpoint in front of the dedicated embedding cache observed sudden latency spikes (tail p99 > 2s) and elevated 5xx from the rerank path starting 2026-03-10 ~09:00 UTC. Impact: production traffic from ClipStream Media (dedicated pool) experienced timeouts and degraded ranking quality due to a high rate of cache misses and subsequent synchronous recompute.

Impact:
- Elevated p95/p99 for /v1/rerank (p99 from 450ms -> 2.3s for affected traffic).
- Increased token costs due to repeated embedding recomputations.
- Intermittent 503/504 responses for some requests behind the rerank route.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: clipstream-dedicated-3
- Region: us-east-1 (prod)
- Embedding model: embedder-lite-384-v2 pinned by customer
- Cache: sharded KV LRU cache fronting embedding service

Steps to reproduce (observed behavior):
1) Customer sends bursty rerank traffic with mixed TTL metadata headers (client includes embed-metadata:ts header).
2) Cache lookup attempted; cache key composed of (model, namespace, embed-metadata:ts).
3) When client clock skewed or header microseconds varied, cache keys didn't match leading to miss and synchronous recompute against embedder process.
4) Under burst, many concurrent recomputes saturated embedding workers causing queueing and retry/backpressure into rerank path.

Logs / Observations:
- KV-cache logs show surge of cache-miss events + unique key cardinality spiking at 09:03 UTC.
- Embed service CPU/GPU utilization at 95% across a subset of hosts.
- Rerank service traces show increased downstream latency waiting on embed RPCs.
- Customer reported that after a client-side release paused (09:20 UTC), the anomaly subsided.

Initial hypothesis:
- Cache key includes a client-provided timestamp header for debugging; clients sometimes send sub-second varying values resulting in effectively unbounded key variants and causing a cache missstorm.

Requested by customer:
- Immediate mitigation to reduce repeated recompute and restore p99 latency to SLA targets.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:15 - ClipStream Ops (customer): Confirmed a client-side SDK version deployed yesterday that started sending microsecond timestamps in embed-metadata header. Rolling back to previous release reduced churn temporarily.
Confirmed high-cardinality keys were the proximate cause via kv-cache histogram and unique_key_count metric (x1000 baseline -> spike).
Trace spans indicate rerank requests spend 80-90% of tail wait time on embed derivation when cache miss rate is elevated.
Customer SDK 1.3.7 introduced embed-metadata:ts with sub-second precision; earlier versions omitted the header.
Hotfix gate implemented to normalize timestamp header to second granularity for clipstream namespace; immediate reduction in unique cache keys observed.
Root cause: cache key derivation included unnormalized client-supplied metadata that should not contribute to key space.
Mitigation applied: transient normalization gate in kv-cache to strip sub-second precision from embed-metadata:ts for the affected namespace and a short-term whitelist to ignore non-keyable headers. Customer rolled back offending SDK release and confirmed latency improvement. Next steps: implement platform-wide key-derivation hardening (INT-4120) to ignore volatile client headers, add cardinality alerts, and update developer docs/SDK to discourage sending microsecond timestamps. Follow-up: schedule postmortem and add permanent fix PR (github.com/redwood/kv-cache/pull/1284).
payload.summary: Embedding metadata timestamp drift causing cache-miss storms and rerank latency spikes

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a tenant concurrency ramp for ClearSight Analytics (dedicated tenant) we observed a sustained elevation of 5xx responses originating at the API gateway with upstream runtime crashes and connection exhaustion. Symptoms began ~2026-03-13 09:42 UTC and persisted intermittently through 2026-03-13 15:00 UTC.

Impact:
- ClearSight reported ~18% of requests returning 502/503/504 during a high-concurrency ramp (affects production traffic in us-east-1).
- Latency for successful requests increased 2-3x for affected routes.
- Customer experienced disrupted embeddings and chat features for ~5 hours.

Timeline (high level):
- 09:38 UTC: ClearSight starts a concurrency-based load test for new feature (reported by customer).
- 09:42 UTC: First spike of 502s seen on api-gateway; Support page shows elevated error rate.
- 09:55 UTC: SRE triage noted upstream runtime OOMs and high ephemeral connection counts.
- 10:20 UTC: Engineering rollback of recent routing policy experiment (commit c3a8b2) initiated as mitigation.
- 11:05 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied: reduce prefetch parallelism to 1 and increase autoscaler headroom.
- 13:30 UTC: Error rate reduced but not fully resolved; further investigation ongoing.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Using a dedicated tenant with routing policy that includes variant-weighted matrix (mix of quantized and full-precision variants), start a concurrency ramp to 800 qps sustained for 10 minutes.
2) Ensure token-prefetch is enabled with default prefetch parallelism 4.
3) Observe gateway responses and runtime pod metrics (CPU, memory, connection counts) - see logs below.

Observed logs (excerpts):
- api-gateway: 2026-03-13T09:43:12Z ERROR route=embed/v1 tenant=clearsight upstream_status=502 "upstream reset before headers"
- runtime: 2026-03-13T09:44:01Z WARN eviction: kvcache lock contention=high tokens_prefetch_active=18
- runtime: 2026-03-13T09:44:17Z ERROR gpu0: OOM (alloc failed) pid=7421 free_mb=136 tearing_down=true
- proxy: 2026-03-13T09:45:03Z ERROR connection_pool: exhausted for tenant clearsight active=1024 max=1024

Initial hypotheses:
- New routing matrix weights (experiment c3a8b2) caused a subset of embedding/chat routes to be considered "incompatible" by the routing layer, which triggered synchronous fallback to heavier runtime variants instead of lightweight quantized variants. This increased per-request GPU memory and latency.
- Prefetch token manager leaked per-connection prefetch slots under high concurrency; prefetch counters remained inflated after request termination, causing effective connection+prefetch pool exhaustion and triggering upstream timeouts and runtime OOMs.
- Interaction between routing fallback and increased memory footprint produced a positive feedback loop: heavier variants increased prefetch concurrency which increased memory pressure and connection contention, causing more fallbacks and eventual runtime restarts.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Rolled back routing experiment c3a8b2 (10:20 UTC).
- Reduced token-prefetch parallelism from 4->1 for affected tenant route (10:30 UTC).
- Increased autoscaler min-replicas for serving-runtime pool for tenant to allow faster buffer during ramp (10:45 UTC).

Next steps (RCA):
- Reproduce in staging with the exact ClearSight traffic pattern and routing weights.
- Add telemetry for token-prefetch counters per-connection and ensure counters are atomically decremented on all error paths.
- Add routing-layer guardrail to avoid synchronous fallback to heavy variants if prefetch pool or runtime memory is above threshold.
- Postmortem and communication to ClearSight including crediting practice and follow-up timeline.

2026-03-13 09:58 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer reports 18% of requests failing with 502s during a load test. Asked for request IDs and timeframe; customer provided request sample and timestamps.
2026-03-13 10:05 - SRE (Marcus Lee): Observed runtime OOMs and connection_pool exhausted on runtime-proxy_3. Correlates with token-prefetch_active spikes. Starting mitigation planning.
2026-03-13 10:18 - Eng (Priya Desai): Noted recent routing policy commit c3a8b2 that modified variant compatibility flags. Proposing rollback as immediate mitigation.
2026-03-13 10:21 - SRE (Marcus Lee): Rollback of c3a8b2 completed; monitoring for error rate drop.
2026-03-13 10:33 - Ops (Evan Kim): Prefetch parallelism reduced to 1 for tenant route. Observed connection_pool pressure easing within 10 minutes.
2026-03-13 11:12 - Customer (ClearSight Admin): Confirmed partial recovery but noticed longer tail latencies on some heavy requests. Asked about root cause and ETA for full recovery.
2026-03-13 13:45 - Eng (Priya Desai): Captured flame graphs and memory traces showing increased resident set size for heavy variants. Preparing repro in staging with recorded traffic.
2026-03-14 09:02 - SRE (Marcus Lee): Added temporary alert for token-prefetch counter drift and opened follow-up task INT-471112 to harden decrement paths.
2026-03-14 12:30 - Support (Aisha Patel): Notified ClearSight that mitigations reduced error rate; pending RCA and long-term fixes. Scheduled postmortem meeting 2026-03-16.
Routing matrix analysis: policy c3a8b2 introduced a compatibility matrix change that incorrectly marked quantized variants as unsuitable for embedding-only route when prompt length < 128 tokens. Result: requests routed to full-precision variants more often under certain weight combinations.
Prefetch manager: race in connection close path - decrement of prefetch slot moved behind async cleanup; under high QPS the cleanup task was dropped when executor saturated, leaving slots counted but not in use.
Autoscaler interaction: short autoscaler cooldown meant nodes terminated quickly after brief pressure spikes; combined with slower cold-start of heavy variants, this increased likelihood of runtime OOM and restarts.
Correlation: peaks in token-prefetch_active align with the highest percent of fallback routes to heavy variants. Connection_pool exhaustion precedes runtime OOMs by ~30-90s in traces.
Mitigations in place: routing policy rollback and prefetch parallelism cap reduced produced immediate reduction in 5xx. Autoscaler min-replicas increased to avoid immediate scale-to-zero. Long-term fixes: fix prefetch decrement race (PR linked), add routing guardrail by memory/headroom threshold, and improve autoscaler warmup behaviour. Customer credited for downtime in follow-up. RCA meeting scheduled.
INT-471112: Hardening prefetch decrement paths and add unit/integration tests (owner: runtime team)
PLT-2026: Add routing guardrail feature to avoid heavy-variant fallback if memory or prefetch pools are saturated (owner: routing team)
OPS-8910: Adjust autoscaler warmup/cooldown heuristics for dedicated tenants with mixed-variant matrices (owner: infra)
PM-533: Communication + credits for ClearSight and update SLA incident page (owner: CS)
payload.summary: Cascading 5xx from routing-matrix mismatch and token-prefetch leak during tenant concurrency ramp

Issue summary: Customer NovaBI reports intermittent corruption of model shard range downloads from Redwood artifact storage in their private deployment. Corruption manifests as either checksum mismatch on concatenated ranges or truncated shard files leading to model load errors. Impact: Serving nodes drop to degraded capacity for affected model; endpoints return 5xx or stall during large-generation requests. Users see increased latency and token errors.

Observed behaviour: Failure occurs only in private deployment behind customer-managed egress ACL and corporate proxy appliance. Failures correlate with heavy concurrent range downloads and long-lived HTTP/2 multiplexed connections. Network traces show missing FIN/ACK frames from server->client path leading to connection pool reuse with stale TLS session context, which then causes range requests to be served on a re-used TCP stream with partial TLS state mismatch and corrupted byte ranges.

Expected behaviour: Normal HTTP/2 connection pool reuse should only occur when connections are cleanly closed; FIN/ACK suppression at the egress should not result in TLS session reuse that corrupts presigned range downloads.

Customer impact: Production model serve regressions for multiple product teams at NovaBI; estimated 12% of large shard downloads affected during peak ingestion windows.

1) Deploy private Redwood control plane with NovaBI egress ACL + corporate proxy enabled
2) Trigger parallel model shard range downloads by starting 24 concurrent model containers requesting 4-8 range slices each
3) Observe artifact fetch logs on serving nodes and client-side checksum validation failures
4) Capture packet trace at customer egress appliance and on serving node to compare TCP FIN/ACK visibility
5) Correlate timestamps with Redwood artifact service access logs to identify partial byte ranges returned
serving-node/artifact-fetcher INFO 2026-03-12T08:12:33Z: presigned-fetch range 0-1048575 started (req id: req-6b9d)
serving-node/artifact-fetcher WARN 2026-03-12T08:12:34Z: range 1/4 checksum mismatch after concatenation, expected sha256:aa3f.. got: aa2c.. (req id: req-6b9d)
envoy-proxy WARN 2026-03-12T08:12:35Z: http2 stream reset by remote, no RST frame seen from upstream
tcpdump: 08:12:34.123 IP 10.2.1.8.443 > 172.31.10.5.51094: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12567 ack 9876 win 64240 (payload),  -- FIN/ACK from server expected at 08:12:36 but not observed on egress side
artifact-storage access-log 2026-03-12T08:12:34Z: GET /models/gptx-large-v1/shard-12?range=0-1048575 206 Partial Content 200ms req-6b9d
2026-03-12: Initial triage by support: pattern matches FIN suppression or stateful firewall dropping FINs on post-connection tail packets
Packet captures show the server sent a FIN but the customer egress capture does not show the FIN leaving the customer appliance consistently
Envoy histograms show elevated http2 stream reset counts during peak concurrent downloads
Hypothesis: Egress ACL or inline proxy performs TCP stream rewriting or connection pooling that suppresses FIN to keep connections alive, causing upstream server to think connection closed while downstream client reuses connection with stale TLS record state
Reproduction attempt in Redwood staging without customer egress appliance failed — indicates issue is customer-e2e network dependent
SRE note: gRPC keepalive settings are standard; serving runtime relies on clean TCP close before reusing connection for next TLS session to the same destination when presigned URL reusage occurs
Asha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12: Received initial report from NovaBI engineering. Requested packet captures at both customer egress and serving node. Asked customer to run tcpdump for 5 minutes during a heavy ingest window.
NovaBI-Eng (customer) 2026-03-12: Uploaded captures and flow logs to secure bucket. Observed that their NGFW shows 'connection persist' rules with 'no-fin' enabled for HTTP/2 to reduce churn.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-13: Confirmed missing FIN in customer egress capture. Temporarily asked customer to disable 'no-fin' behavior on NGFW or create an exception for artifact storage IPs. Provided test ACL to allow FIN/ACK propagation.
NovaBI-Eng 2026-03-13: Temporarily adjusted NGFW rule as requested; reported immediate drop in corrupted downloads during afternoon window. Will schedule a wider rollback test tomorrow morning when load is higher.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-14: Proposed long-term mitigation: instrument serving runtime to detect reused connection with unexpected TLS sequence and force fresh connection handshake for presigned range requests. Logged feature ticket INT-45012 for implementation and added tests to artifact-fetcher to validate correct FIN handling semantics.
Asha Patel (Support) 2026-03-14: Notified customer that temporary mitigation is in place and that Redwood SRE will track implementation of permanent fix. SLA updated to P1 follow-up cadence.
Temporary mitigation applied: NovaBI disabled NGFW 'no-fin/connection persist' rule for artifact storage endpoints and corruption rate dropped to baseline. Long-term fix: serving runtime will be updated to detect stale connection TLS state and proactively perform connection reset before reusing streams for presigned range concatenation (tracking INT-45012). Follow-up: customer to roll out controlled test tomorrow; SRE to validate with synthetic large-range workload and update runbook.
1) Customer to run high-concurrency regression test with NGFW exception active and upload capture for validation (owner: NovaBI, due: 2026-03-15)
2) SRE to implement connection-state check and safe-reset for artifact-fetcher (owner: Liam O'Connor, ticket INT-45012)
3) Add anomaly alert to Console for increased http2 reset ratio and checksum failures on presigned downloads (owner: Platform Observability)
4) Update private-deploy runbook with NGFW configuration guidance and include a troubleshooting checklist for FIN/ACK suppression scenarios (owner: Docs)
payload.summary: HTTP/2 connection pool reuse blocked by egress ACL causing FIN/ACK drop and TLS session reuse leading to corrupted range downloads in private deployment

Issue summary:
Customer upgraded org credit limit + billing tier (enterprise plan migration) at ~2026-03-09T23:00Z. Console shows new quota immediately, but customer observed a wave of 429 responses for short-lived streaming and bulk-embed jobs for ~8–12 minutes after upgrade.

Impact:
- SlateDocs reported ~15% of requests returning 429 during a 10-minute window affecting critical ingestion jobs (bulk embeddings + live chat).
- Customer reported degraded UX and 3 failed ingestion batches requiring manual retries.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (api and billing)
- Region: us-east-1
- Customer account: slate-12345
- Workloads: mixed low-latency streaming + periodic bulk embedding jobs

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Perform org credit/top-up via console (billing tier upgrade).
2) Immediately start parallel bulk-embed workers (100 concurrent sessions) and 50 concurrent short-lived streaming sessions.
3) Observe 429 rate and throttle headers on some calls for next 5–15 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Console shows quota refreshed at 2026-03-09T23:00Z but rate-limiter logs indicate refill tokens were not applied uniformly to edge nodes for ~8 minutes.
- Throttle response headers (x-rw-rate-limit) show pre-upgrade limits consistent with the lower tier returned for some sessions.

Expected behavior:
- New quota should be available immediately across all serving nodes within the SLA window (<= 60s).

Frequency:
- Reproducible when heavy parallel traffic coincides with a billing/credit update. Occurred once during this customer's upgrade; support has observed similar patterns internally during large org increases but not this exact symptom.

Attempts to mitigate performed so far:
- Customer staggered worker starts (reduced concurrent workers) which reduced 429 frequency.
- Support performed a manual quota refresh for the tenant; partial improvement observed.

Attachments:
- Raw request + response examples supplied by customer (attached logs)
- Support trace IDs: trace-rw-8421, trace-rw-8422

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:05 - Customer (SlateDocs - Henry Lowe): Sent logs and a short repro script showing 50 concurrent streams + 120 embed workers. Noted that console UI updated instantaneously.
Checked billing service events: invoice and credit update accepted at 2026-03-09T23:00Z; billing write recorded to primary DB.
Rate-limiter ingestion pipeline shows a backlog for quota-refresh events at edge-fanout stage; some fanout worker retries were queued due to transient S3 metadata latency.
Edge nodes running keepalive-proxy version 2.7.1 held cached token windows that were not invalidated until TTL expiry (~9m) — caused partial stale-per-route limits.
Throttle header traces show mixed limit windows: some responses include pre-upgrade window (100r/s) while others reflect new window (1000r/s).
Hypothesis: billing->pubsub fanout occasionally stalls when org-level updates collide with high telemetry load; causes window mismatch across edge nodes until TTL refresh.
Searched for related incidents: similar pattern noted in SUP-412900 (keepalive affinity) but root cause here tied to refill event delivery path, not sticky sessions.
Impact scope estimated: affects only sessions that start within the propagation gap; established long-lived sessions pick up new tokens after reconnection or TTL expiry.
Recommended immediate steps to customer: 1) Stagger startup of bulk workers with randomized 30–90s jitter. 2) Temporarily raise per-tenant burst allowance via support console (we applied a +2x burst credit to slate-12345). 3) For streaming clients, prefer reconnect after upgrade to pick up refreshed windows.
1) SRE to patch fanout retry logic to avoid S3 metadata stalls (track as INT follow-up). 2) Product to evaluate reducing TTL on per-route token caches during tenant-level quota changes. 3) Add monitoring alert for refill-propagation-lag > 30s. 4) Follow up with customer once hotfix scheduled.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sudden rise in end-to-end inference latency and frequent client-side timeouts starting 2026-03-12 14:10 UTC. Symptoms observed across multiple endpoints (chat/generate) and manifest as long tails (p95-p99) and occasional 504s at the customer HTTP client. Impact: customer-facing product degradation for Nimbus Analytics (enterprise), multiple teams affected.

Impact:
- Elevated p95/p99 request durations (observed from 200–300ms baseline to 1.5–6s)
- Client-side HTTP timeouts and retries visible in customer logs
- Some calls successfully fall back to older model variants but throughput is reduced

Environment:
- Customer using SDK v2.7.1 with default client config, server side: hosted API (prod, us-east) running serving-runtime 1.14.x.
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline with periodic bursts from batch jobs and human queries.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Use SDK v2.7.1, default client options, simple generate request against gpt-4o-mini-instruct.
2) Run 50 concurrent threads each issuing a streaming generate with short prompts (10–30 tokens).
3) Observe serialized behavior: only a few active TCP sockets to our API from the host, queueing delays in application, and retries backoff in sequence.

Observed behavior:
- Application-level request queuing in customer stack (requests waiting on connection acquisition)
- Repeated exponential backoff retries serialized on the single/limited socket pool, producing perceived high latency and timeouts
- SRE traces show small number of long-lived idle sockets in TIME_WAIT and many requests waiting for connection lease from SDK pool

Expected behavior:
- SDK should maintain sufficient connection concurrency to handle bursts (or expose clear limits) and concurrent retries should not serialize behind a single connection acquisition path.

Attachments/logs:
- Customer attached HTTP client stack traces and timestamps (available in ticket).
- Support pulled API gateway trace ids: trace_ids: [trace_us_8761, trace_us_8763].
- Netstat sample from customer host showing high TIME_WAIT and low ESTABLISHED counts.

Notes:
- Customer initially escalated after seeing repeated 504s at 14:20 UTC and higher than expected token costs due to repeated retries.
2026-03-12 15:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged. Asked customer for SDK config and netstat output. Requested whether they set maxConnections or keepAlive options.
2026-03-12 15:22 - Customer (Nimbus SRE - Dan Cho): Provided SDK config: default client, maxConnections unset, keepAlive enabled. Attached netstat and trace snippets. Noted problem started after a spike in batch queries.
2026-03-12 16:00 - Support (Aisha Patel): Reproduced locally with SDK v2.7.1 using a small repro harness. Observed connection leasing delays and serialized retries when backoff is active. Escalating to SRE/SDK team.
2026-03-12 18:10 - SRE (Miguel Torres): Identified that SDK v2.7.1 has a per-host connection pool default of 6 and no upper bound on retry queue length; combined with our gateway's short accept windows this led to burst saturation and head-of-line waiting. Opened issue with SDK team; added label 'sdk-config'.
2026-03-13 09:30 - SDK Eng (Priya Menon): Confirmed bug in v2.7.1 where connection leasing is single-thread serialized under contention in the Node/Python clients. PR to add non-blocking acquisition and queue limits in flight. See PR #482.
2026-03-14 11:45 - Support (Miguel Torres): Proposed interim customer workaround and requested customer to apply config changes. Awaiting confirmation of customer applying changes.
Timeline:
- 2026-03-12 14:10 UTC: First customer reports.
- 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC: Support reproduced locally.
- 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC: SRE analysis shows connection pool exhaustion and long wait times for acquisition.

Key findings:
- SDK v2.7.1 default per-host connection pool size: 6.
- Under bursty workloads with concurrent streaming requests, the client queue grows; in v2.7.1 acquisition is serialized by a single lock, causing head-of-line blocking.
- Retries use exponential backoff and are enqueued on top of the same connection-acquisition path; when the pool is exhausted, retries and new requests wait, producing apparent latency even if server responds quickly for subsequent requests.
- Gateway traces show short-lived accept windows during spikes; small pool + serialized acquisition produced a bottleneck at the client side, not server.
- Observed system-level signs: high socket in TIME_WAIT, increased queued sockets in accept backlog, and customer process showing many threads waiting on 'acquireConnection'.

Diagnostics performed:
- Reproduced with synthetic load: 50 concurrent streaming requests -> p95 jump from 250ms to 2.8s.
- Captured tcpdump and ss output.
- Tested adjusting SDK to maxConnections=32 and enabling per-host queue_limit=50: client-side queueing reduced and observed p95 dropped to ~300ms.
- Verified that server-side latency remained stable during repro, confirming client-side bottleneck.

Hypothesis:
- Primary cause: client SDK connection pool defaults and blocking acquisition + retries serialized into the same queue. Secondary contributing factors: customer's OS socket limits and bursty traffic pattern.

Next steps:
- Immediate: provide customer a config/workaround to increase pool and cap retry queue.
- Short term: release SDK patch to make acquisition non-blocking and add a retry-queue cap. PR #482 associated.
- Medium term: update docs/quickstart with recommended client defaults for bursty workloads and add telemetry in SDK to surface connection queue metrics.
Workaround (applied by customer 2026-03-13):
- Upgrade client to SDK v2.7.2-beta or apply runtime config: maxConnections=32, connectionKeepAlive=true, retry.backoff.initial=100ms, retry.backoff.max=400ms, retry.queue_limit=20.
- Recommended OS tune: increase ephemeral port range and reduce TIME_WAIT by enabling TCP reuse where safe.

Permanent fix (planned/released):
- SDK patch released v2.8.0 (2026-03-14): non-blocking connection acquisition, default per-host pool increased to 12, and a configurable retry queue limit defaulting to 20. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482.
- Support/Docs: Added a page with recommended SDK connection settings for bursty workloads and a troubleshooting checklist: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/4321/Socket+and+Retry+Runbook.

Follow-ups:
- (Action) CS to contact customer to confirm stability and close ticket after 48h of stable metrics. Assigned to Aisha Patel.
- (Action) SDK team to add metrics for 'connection_queue_length' and 'connection_acquire_latency' in next minor release. Assigned to Priya Menon.

Customer impact: reduced to acceptable levels after workaround; customer confirmed improved p95 and ceased to observe 504s after applying config change.

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Zenlytics (enterprise) cannot create/update routing policies in the Redwood control plane. UI and API requests fail with 500 errors.

Customer impact
- Customer is blocked from: (a) updating routing policy weights, (b) pinning model version for a new rollout, (c) adding a new fallback region.
- Live inference traffic continues to serve, but customer cannot make policy changes and is stuck on last-known-good policy config.
- Customer indicates an urgent business need to shift traffic due to performance issues on a model variant; inability to change policy is time-sensitive.

Timeline (UTC)
- 2026-01-29 16:05: Customer reports in shared Slack + opens support ticket.
- 16:12: Support reproduces via API; escalated to SRE + Platform Control Plane.
- 16:25: Incident channel created; initial mitigation/workaround attempted.
- 17:10: Root cause narrowed to control plane config write path (DB transaction + audit log write) under specific payload size/shape.
- 18:05: Hotfix deployed to us-east control plane API.
- 18:18: Customer confirms ability to update policy via API; Console still intermittently fails due to retry logic.
- 19:10: Console retry/backoff change rolled out; errors resolved.

How to reproduce
1) PUT /v1/routing/policies/{policy_id} with policy payload >= ~200KB (customer has many routes + per-route conditions).
2) Observe HTTP 500 and no policy update.

Observed errors
- API response:
  - HTTP 500
  - body: {"error":"internal_error","message":"failed to persist policy config"}
  - response headers include x-request-id (examples below)

Customer-provided request IDs (x-request-id)
- 01JH2K6Q7S2W9N7D2K6D9M0FQK
- 01JH2K7A2F0S8Y3K1C1C5WQ8TX

Support reproduction notes
- Repro confirmed from Redwood side using customer-scoped token (impersonation) in us-east.
- Console (ops + customer) surfaced generic error toast; Network tab shows 500 from /console-api/routing/policy.

Initial triage / hypotheses
- Auth/RBAC rejected writes? (ruled out: requests pass authz and fail in persistence step)
- Control plane DB contention / transaction timeout? (partially true)
- Audit log write path failure causing overall transaction rollback? (confirmed)

Investigation notes (engineering)
- Primary oncall: Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park) with SRE support (Rafael Mendes).
- Findings:
  - A recent change increased audit log payload size by including full pre/post config diffs for routing policies.
  - For large policy payloads, the audit log row exceeded a DB row/TOAST threshold and triggered a slow write; combined with a strict transaction timeout caused rollback.
  - Control plane API returned a generic 500 without a structured error code, which slowed down triage.

Mitigation / workaround provided to customer
- Temporary workaround offered at 16:40 UTC: split policy update into smaller incremental PATCH operations (per-route) to reduce payload size.
- Customer attempted; reduced but did not eliminate failures (still hit the audit log path for some operations).

Fix implemented
- Hotfix (18:05 UTC):
  - Changed audit logging to store a summarized diff (hash + top-level fields) for routing policy writes; full payload stored in object store asynchronously when needed.
  - Increased transaction timeout specifically for the policy write path with bounded retry on serialization failures.

Customer confirmation
- 18:18 UTC: Customer confirms policy updates succeed via API.
- 19:22 UTC: Customer confirms Console UI updates succeed; no further 500s observed.
Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping (for Reliability Program)
- Proposed classification (v1 taxonomy): Control plane outage > Config write/CRUD failures.
- Primary owner: Platform Control Plane.
- Secondary/consulted: SRE (incident process + comms), Smart Routing (validation layer), Observability (dashboards/alerts for error rate).
- Note: This ticket is being used as a concrete example in the ownership mapping table to keep "control plane config writes" distinct from "routing/fallback misbehavior" and "auth/RBAC failures".

- Add structured error code for config write failures (e.g., CONTROL_PLANE_CONFIG_WRITE_FAILED vs INTERNAL_ERROR) and emit as metric label (low-cardinality).
- Add an alert for elevated 5xx on control-plane write endpoints, segmented by endpoint group (read vs write).
- Document known limit guidance: recommend policy size limits + how to structure complex routing policies.
Customer communications
- Rachel Kim provided customer-facing update cadence (every 30 min) in shared Slack; avoided attributing specific DB internals, focused on mitigation and restoration timeline.
Attachments / links
- Incident channel: #incidents (internal) referencing INC-2026-01-29-CP-CONFIG-WRITES
- Shared customer channel: #zenlytics-redwood (internal reference)
Next update
- Close ticket after 48h monitoring window and confirm no recurring write failures; keep one-week watch alert for elevated write failures on policy endpoints.
Resolved via control plane hotfix to reduce audit-log write payload and add bounded retries; Console retry/backoff improved and request-id surfaced. Customer confirmed ability to update routing policies via API and Console; no recurrence observed during 48h monitoring.

Issue summary:
Acme AI reports noticeable response differences ("quality drop" + more incorrect answers on internal spot checks) after enabling an opt-in Quantization Profile on one production route.

Customer impact:
- Customer states accuracy/response quality degraded on the affected route.
- No increase in 5xx observed by customer; primary concern is semantic correctness.
- Customer is a design partner for Quantization Profile Library beta; expects safe rollback and guidance.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated
- Region: us-east
- Route: acme/chat-prod (customer label)
- Model: llama3-70b-instruct@x1
- Quantization setting changed from default (baseline precision) to an INT8 profile (exact id requested below).

Customer report (from CS email recap):
- "After enabling the quant profile toggle on our /chat route, we saw answers become less consistent and sometimes miss key constraints. Rolling back to default seemed to restore baseline behavior. Can you confirm if a known issue exists and what evals we should run?"

Requested from customer (pending at time of filing):
- 5–10 request_ids before and after change
- Exact quant_profile_ref / quant_profile_id selected in Console
- Whether they also changed any route parameters (temperature/top_p/max_output_tokens/system prompt)

Support goals:
1) Confirm whether requests were actually served with the quantized profile (vs fallback/disabled).
2) Determine if this is a known regression for the selected profile/model variant.
3) Provide an immediate rollback path and a recommended A/B eval approach for re-enablement.
Triage checklist (Support):
- Confirm change history in Console for route-level quantization settings.
- Pull runtime traces for provided request_ids; verify log annotation quant_profile_id and resolution outcome (applied/fallback/disabled).
- Check dashboards: per-route fallback_rate, enabled_rate, p95 latency deltas, error rate deltas.

Initial findings (2025-03-07):
- Customer provided request_ids (shared via email; redacted here). Runtime traces show quant_profile_id present and resolution outcome = applied.
- Observability: No material change in 5xx. Small p95 decode latency improvement (~4–6%) consistent with INT8 profile.
- However, internal quick-check using customer-provided prompts showed measurable degradation on constraint-following prompts (qualitative).

Escalation (Applied ML / Evals):
- Loop in Arjun Desai + Jonas Weber to confirm whether the specific profile version had a known borderline regression on Redwood prompt sets.
- Cross-check against quantization regression thresholds policy for this model family.

Root cause (confirmed 2025-03-08):
- The enabled profile version for llama3-70b-instruct@x1 (INT8) had a known/ongoing quality regression on a subset of instruction-following + long-context prompts.
- Profile should have been blocked for publication/use on @x1 until recalibration; the allowlist/constraints were not updated quickly enough for this model variant.

Notes:
- This is not an incompatibility fallback issue; requests were deterministically applying the profile.
- Customer rollback restored baseline behavior, supporting a profile-specific quality regression rather than prompt/config drift.

References:
- Slack: #incidents thread about beta quality alert firing (see sources/slack/incidents/1741684000.json)
- Known fix/workaround tracked via hotfix PR to disable the profile for @x1 variant.
Resolution summary:
1) Immediate mitigation for Acme AI: advised disabling quantization on the affected route (set quantization_profile_ref = default) and to keep it off until a new profile version is published.
2) Platform mitigation: Applied hotfix to disable the problematic profile for llama3-70b-instruct@x1 in the allowed profiles list/constraints.

Customer-facing rollback guidance (provided):
- Console: Route → Settings → Quantization Profiles → set to "Default (baseline precision)" → Save.
- API/config: set route quantization_profile_ref to "default" (or null) and redeploy.
- Verification: pick a request_id after rollback; confirm quant_profile_id is absent and resolution outcome = disabled in traces.

Evals guidance (provided to customer):
- Use route-level A/B eval playbook to compare baseline vs profile-enabled on a representative prompt set.
- Suggested minimum: 200–500 prompts sampled from their production distribution; report win/loss/tie and task-family breakdown.
- Gate re-enablement on passing the Confluence regression thresholds policy.

Engineering actions taken:
- PR merged to disable profile on model variant @x1 due to quality regression and prevent future enablement until republished.

Current status:
- Customer confirmed (via CS) that disabling the profile restored expected behavior.
- Awaiting publication of a recalibrated profile version for this model variant before re-trying enablement.

payload.description:
Issue summary: During the 07:15–08:30 PST traffic surge on 2026-03-05 SolarisML experienced streaming stalls (clients saw partial frames and then long polling until a 5xx) and sustained GPU pool exhaustion. Impact: SolarisML's live inference features degraded, high tail latency (>10s) and intermittent 5xx errors for ~75% of requests to their dedicated pool; customer SLAs were at risk and the account escalated to our Enterprise team.

Timeline (high-level):
- 07:12: First alerts from internal SLOs showing spike in example_latency_p95 for SolarisML dedicated pool.
- 07:15: Customer reported multiple streaming connections paused and reconnects (they opened support chat).
- 07:20: Automated scaling failed to add capacity; GPU pool healthy pods remained at 0/desired for new allocations.
- 07:35: Engineering emergency page opened, routing temporarily shifted SolarisML traffic to a cold quantized fallback.
- 07:50: Fallback introduced significant quality regressions; CS paused the fallback and requested rollback.
- 08:10: Hotfix deployed to increase min_replicas for SolarisML pool and disable aggressive scale-down; connections began to recover.
- 09:05: Customer confirmed recovery and we closed the incident.

Steps to reproduce (internal reproduction notes):
1. Replay SolarisML morning workload (burst of long streaming sessions with high token churn and KV cache warmups).
2. Reduce autoscaler min_replicas and trigger scale-down by simulating low baseline.
3. Re-introduce the burst; observe queue saturation and long scheduling latencies.
4. Verify streaming stalls correlate with scheduling delays and sessions held in the pending queue for >12s.

Logs / Observations:
- Serving runtime logs consistently show "pending_queue_wait_ms > 12000" prior to 5xx spike.
- Node-level GPU metrics showed memory fragmentation and processes stuck in 'alloc' state while kernel preemption occurred.
- Autoscaler metrics revealed an erroneous scale-down snapshot at 06:58 that lowered min_replicas to 1 for SolarisML pool.
- Routing logs show an automated fallback rule that matched a policy "fallback-to-quantized" and sent 22% of traffic to redwood-quant-14b between 07:35–07:50.

Investigation notes / hypotheses considered:
- Hypothesis A: Autoscaler bug allowed min_replicas to be lowered during maintenance snapshot. Evidence: scale-down event at 06:58 with annotation "snapshot-applied". Root cause trace points to an edge case in snapshot merging logic when a ready-check timeout coincided with a rolling update.
- Hypothesis B: Long-lived sessions with large KV caches prevented graceful eviction, causing node-level scheduling delays and memory fragmentation. Evidence: heap and KV cache metrics for SolarisML sessions were 3x typical and sessions persisted across scale-down.
- Hypothesis C: Fallback routing policy lacked an upper-bound cap on traffic percentage for canary, exposing customer to quality regression. Evidence: fallback ramped to 22% without automated rollback on quality delta.

Resolution / Fix deployed:
- Emergency config change: increased min_replicas for SolarisML dedicated pool from 1 -> 4 and temporarily disabled scale-down; immediate effect reduced pending queue times and restored streaming.
- Hotfix PR: autoscaler now ignores maintenance snapshots if a rolling update is active (PR #4987). Deployed 07:58.
- Routing policy change: added hard cap of 10% traffic for quantized fallback canaries and a metric-based automatic rollback if quality_delta > 0.02.

Customer communication and escalation:
- CS rep Maya Chen maintained an open line with SolarisML PM; we provided twice-daily status updates in the first 48 hours and a final incident summary.
- SolarisML flagged this as "high severity - potential churn" and requested follow-up on safeguards to avoid future morning-window regressions.

Post-incident follow-up items (actionable list):
- ACTION-1: Fix autoscaler snapshot merge edge case and add unit tests (owner: Marco Rivera, due: 2026-03-12).
- ACTION-2: Implement session-aware scale-down that waits for KV cache drains or enforces graceful eviction (owner: Naoki Sato, due: 2026-03-19).
- ACTION-3: Add traffic cap + automatic quality rollback to all fallback rules (owner: Priya Patel, due: 2026-03-16).
- ACTION-4: Create a dedicated runbook for dedicated-pool morning-window surges and onboard SolarisML to scheduled pre-warm (owner: CS-Team, due: 2026-03-22).
- ACTION-5: Audit and set per-customer min_replicas defaults for top-100 paying accounts (owner: Finance/PM, due: 2026-04-01).

Postmortem link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/solarisml-2026-03-incident

Notes on risk and recurrence: Our mitigations reduce chance of immediate recurrence but further engineering (session-aware scale-down and additional autoscaler tests) required to avoid similar combined failure modes.

Additional notes:
2026-03-05 07:30 — On-call SRE (Evelyn Park): Observed pending_queue_wait_ms spikes; initiating emergency page and checking autoscaler events.
Capacity restored by increasing min_replicas and applying autoscaler hotfix; routing policy tightened to cap canary traffic. Planned engineering work to prevent recurrence assigned to owners. Customer confirmed recovery and accepted follow-up plan.

They are on Dedicated capacity. This ticket captures a conservative, testable fallback that preserves cache state where possible and gives an emergency path back to stable behavior without full workload interruption.
Customer-facing production latency regression (95p token latency >400ms), intermittent streaming disconnects, elevated GPU utilization on a subset of workers, and increased error budget burn for SLA targets.
1) Customer runs high-concurrency inference workload (80 concurrent connections) hitting /v1/chat/stream with model llama-2-7b-q4_keras-compat.
2) Deploy quant profile 'q4-mixed-prefetch-v2' + batching config: target_batch_tokens=1024, max_latency_ms=60.
3) Observe steady-state then see 95th latency climb from ~70ms to >400ms and occasional 502s from worker restarts.

Run synthetic load: replay a mix of 500 short streaming requests + 50 long generation requests pinned to same pool
Monitor autoscaler and GPU allocation during burst window

Workaround deployed: customer isolated to temporary reserved pool and autoscaler policy tuned to increase min_replicas and stabilization window. Root causes are (1) high-frequency short streams from customer's background job causing slot serialization and cache churn; (2) autoscaler stabilization too aggressive leading to oscillation and allocation fragmentation. Next steps: schedule follow-up with Finova to throttle and jitter background job, patch scheduler to implement small-stream aggregation and per-tenant short-stream smoothing (plan PR underway: github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/7123), and add runtime metric alarms for short-stream churn.
