Issue summary
- Customer reports p99 latency regression for long-context summarization workloads immediately after we enabled Runtime 1.21 canary on their Dedicated pool. Regression appears only for long-context requests (>= ~16k prompt tokens) and only on NVIDIA L40S.

Impact
- Customer-visible tail latency increase on long-context routes.
- Reported baseline (Runtime 1.20 / selector v1): p99 ~4.8–5.4s @ ~20k prompt tokens, 256–512 decode tokens.
- After canary (Runtime 1.21 / selector v2 enabled): p99 ~8.9–10.6s for same workload; p50/p90 mostly unchanged.
- No correctness issues reported. Error rate stable.

Customer context
- Northwind Analytics uses Redwood Dedicated for long-context summarization (document ingestion + map-reduce style prompts). Workload is bursty but within reserved throughput.

Environment
- Dedicated pool: nw-analytics-ded-01
- Region: us-east
- GPU SKU: NVIDIA L40S (SM89)
- Driver/CUDA: 550.54.14 / CUDA 12.4
- Runtime: 1.21.0-canary.3
- Feature: Kernel auto-selection v2 enabled via canary gate for Llama family

Steps to reproduce (as reported)
1) Send chat.completions with large prompts (~16k–32k tokens) and max_output_tokens 256–512.
2) Observe p99 latency increase vs previous runtime.
3) Short prompts (<4k) appear unaffected.

Observed signals
- Regressions correlate with selector choosing a different prefill kernel under v2 for the LONG seq bucket on L40S.
- Telemetry shows increased time in prefill stage; decode stage stable.

Example request IDs (customer-provided)
- req_7f2d5c8f2d8a4e1e (2026-02-20 18:12:44Z)
- req_3c19a0d91fb44b26 (2026-02-20 18:17:09Z)

Initial hypothesis
- Mis-selection in v2 for long-context prefill on L40S (SKU mapping + seq-bucket thresholds) causing fallback to a kernel variant with worse long-context characteristics on SM89.

Logs/snippets (redacted)
- Selection trace (sampled):
  - model_family=llama
  - seq_bucket=LONG
  - gpu_sku=l40s_sm89
  - chosen_prefill_kernel=fa3_fused_prefill_sm89 (candidate_score=0.71)
  - fallback_prefill_kernel=fa2_triton_prefill_sm89
  - chosen_decode_kernel=fa2_decode_sm89
- Perf counters summary (internal): prefill_ms +62% at 20k prompt; decode_ms within +/-3%.

Requested outcome
- Immediate mitigation (restore previous tail latency) and a safe path to re-enable v2 once fixed/guarded.
2026-02-20 18:33Z — Markus Klein (Reporter)
Customer escalation via email + Slack connect: p99 long-context lat doubled after today’s canary. Asking for quick rollback guidance; they have an exec demo on 2/22.

Customer notes:
- Only on L40S pool
- Only long prompts
- They can tolerate slightly worse average latency but not p99 spikes.
2026-02-20 18:52Z — Omar El-Sayed (Assignee)
Acknowledged. Pulling selector telemetry for nw-analytics-ded-01. Initial glance: selection distribution changed for llama LONG bucket on sm89; prefill kernel differs from 1.20.

Actions:
- Requested 10 representative request IDs + timestamps.
- Asked SRE (Sean) to confirm no cluster-level saturation/noisy neighbor signals.
2026-02-20 19:15Z — Sean Gallagher
Checked pool health: GPU utilization and queueing normal; no node-level throttling. Error rate stable. Regression isolated to request execution time, not scheduling.

Dashboards:
- latency.p99 long_context route jumped right after canary rollout marker.
- No increase in retry/timeout.
2026-02-20 19:44Z — Omar El-Sayed
Captured selection traces (sampling 1%). Correlation is strong:
- LONG bucket on L40S is picking `fa3_fused_prefill_sm89` ~78% of time; baseline v1 effectively picked `fa2_triton_prefill_sm89`.
- The fa3 variant looks fine on H100/A100 but is underperforming on L40S for long prefill.

Next step: apply runbook mitigation: disable v2 for (model=llama-3.1-70b-instruct, region=us-east, pool=nw-analytics-ded-01) OR pin prefill kernel for LONG bucket.
2026-02-20 20:02Z — Benji Okafor
Control-plane supports per-model deny for v2 with hot reload. I can push a rule scoped to that pool + model family. Confirm desired scope:
- Deny v2 for llama family on L40S in us-east for this dedicated pool only (least blast radius).
- Alternatively, add kernel deny for fa3_fused_prefill_sm89 when seq_bucket=LONG.

Recommend starting with v2 disable for llama + L40S until we confirm fix.
2026-02-20 20:20Z — Omar El-Sayed
Proceed with: v2 disabled for llama-3.1-70b-instruct + llama-3.1-8b-instruct on pool nw-analytics-ded-01 (us-east). Also pin prefill kernel to fa2_triton_prefill_sm89 for LONG bucket as a belt-and-suspenders if supported.

Linking runbook section: kernel-selection-v2-override-and-rollback-runbook (Disable by model/pool).
2026-02-20 20:41Z — Benji Okafor
Mitigation applied:
- Feature gate update propagated (hot reload complete in ~90s).
- Confirmed selector_v2_enabled=false for targeted models on nw-analytics-ded-01.

Added temporary deny entry:
- match: gpu_sku=l40s_sm89 AND seq_bucket=LONG
- action: disallow prefill kernel fa3_fused_prefill_sm89

Monitoring p99 now.
2026-02-20 21:10Z — Markus Klein
Customer confirms improvement within ~10 minutes. New measurements:
- p99 back to ~5.3–5.8s @ 18–22k prompts
- No new errors
They’re asking for RCA + when they can safely re-enable v2.
2026-02-21 09:05Z — Yuki Sato
Root cause likely threshold bug in LONG bucket classification for mixed workloads + overly aggressive scoring weight for fa3 on SM89. We saw similar anomaly in earlier thread.

We have a fix in progress to adjust long-context prefill decision rule and add SKU-specific penalty (L40S) for fa3 until validated.
- Target PR: pr-28522-fix-regression-in-long-context-prefill-kernel-choice

Also recommend keeping deny in place for driver 550.54.14 until we complete validation (possible interaction with CUDA 12.4).
2026-02-22 16:30Z — Omar El-Sayed
Posted interim RCA summary to customer (via Markus):
- Regression introduced by selector v2 prefill kernel choice on L40S for long prompts
- Decode unaffected; no correctness impact
- Mitigation applied (v2 disabled + kernel deny)

Asked customer if they can provide a sanitized prompt-length histogram; will help confirm seq-bucket boundaries.
2026-02-24 11:12Z — Omar El-Sayed
Validated fix behavior in internal perf suite for L40S long-context scenarios. Plan:
- Keep customer-specific deny in place through 1.21 GA.
- Re-enable v2 only after patch release (1.21.1) and a canary on their pool with explicit rollback window.

Customer agreed to schedule test next week.
Mitigated by disabling Kernel auto-selection v2 for affected Llama models on the customer’s Dedicated L40S pool (nw-analytics-ded-01, us-east) and adding a temporary kernel deny rule preventing selection of fa3_fused_prefill_sm89 for LONG seq bucket on L40S. Customer confirmed p99 latency returned to pre-canary baseline. No errors/correctness regressions observed.
Ship/land pr-28522 and include in Runtime 1.21.1 patch notes; ensure L40S long-context benchmarks are green before recommending re-enable.
Coordinate a controlled re-enable canary for Northwind (30–60 min window) with dashboards + explicit rollback trigger (p99 regression >10% for LONG bucket).
Audit selector v2 scoring defaults for SM89 and update known-issues list to call out L40S long-context prefill kernel sensitivity until validated.

Issue summary: Between 09:20 and 10:05 PDT on 2026-03-13 several customers observed intermittent 502 responses on multiplexed streaming endpoints. The errors coincided with a mid-morning tenant burst from a few heavy tenants on Dedicated pools. Impact: streaming sessions saw partial responses followed by 502s; reconnect loops caused visible degradation for ScribeAI (dedicated tenant) and a small set of other tenants. Not a global outage but high error-rate window for affected tenants.

Observed behavior: API gateway returned 502s with upstream read timeout/connection reset. Upstream runtime pods reported short-lived OOM restarts and voluntary eviction of ephemeral worker threads. Autoscaler logs show a rapid shed of ephemeral workers while persistent workers remained. Traffic pattern: long-lived multiplexed HTTP/2 streams with periodic large token bursts (embedding + generation mix).

1) Use multiplexed streaming client to open 100 concurrent HTTP/2 streams to a single tenant in prod us-west 2)
2) Send alternating large embedding batches (~1k tokens) and generation requests (seq len 1k) from multiple logical clients 3)
3) Observe increased API gateway 502s and upstream runtime restarts when concurrency crosses ~80 streams
apigw: 2026-03-13T09:34:12Z - 502 upstream read timeout - upstream=10.20.14.22:8080 request_id=abcd-1234
runtime: 2026-03-13T09:34:13Z - watchdog: ephemeral_worker_evicted id=0x7f4ca mem_pressure=0.78 restarts=3
autoscaler: 2026-03-13T09:34:14Z - scale_down(ephemeral) target=12->4 reason=memory_pressure heur=burst_shed
Initial hypothesis: apigw timeouts due to slow down at runtime when many long-stream sessions hold KV cache leading to backpressure.
Found correlation between ephemeral worker eviction events and peak 502 rate (cross-correlation r=0.82).
Heap/allocator traces show repeated small allocations from streaming multiplex code path causing increased GC pauses on ephemeral workers, triggering autoscaler memory heuristics.
Difference vs past incidents: persistent workers continued serving, but multiplexed streams rely on ephemeral workers for parsing/IO; eviction caused half-open sockets and apigw considered upstream unhealthy leading to immediate 502s.
Traffic replay from staging reproduced socket half-open pattern when ephemeral worker pool dropped below concurrency threshold.
1) Immediate: increased ephemeral worker target from 4 -> 16 for affected Dedicated pools (manual override) to absorb burst
2) Short-term: raised apigw upstream read timeout from 10s -> 20s for multiplexed route to reduce premature 502s (temporary config),
3) Customer guidance: advised ScribeAI to enable request-level retry with jitter and to spread large embedding batches across time windows
Root cause: aggressive ephemeral-worker shedding during memory-pressure detection combined with long-lived multiplexed streams holding socket resources produced half-open upstream connections; apigw treated these as unhealthy upstreams and returned 502s. Fixes: reverted the aggressive shed heuristic in autoscaler and added a minimum ephemeral_worker floor for multiplexed-route pools (runtime change merged). Deployed autoscaler patch (PR #2874) 2026-03-13 23:15 UTC and adjusted prod configs; observed error rates fall to baseline within one hour after scale changes. Postmortem and follow-ups created.
1) Add unit/regression tests for multiplexed stream behavior under ephemeral-worker eviction
2) Tweak memory heuristic to consider stream-depth and socket-hold-time before shedding ephemeral workers
3) Add dashboard alert for ephemeral_worker_evicted spikes tied to apigw 502s
4) Update customer-facing runbook for tenants using multiplexed streaming (recommend batching windows and retry guidance)
Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-13T10:12: We opened this after ScribeAI reported 20% streaming failures. Initial triage points to apigw 502s; escalation to SRE.
SRE (Hiro Tanaka) 2026-03-13T10:45: Correlated autoscaler logs showing ephemeral worker scale_down events at 09:33-09:36. Trying manual scale_up now.
SRE (Luis Ortega) 2026-03-13T11:05: Manual override increased ephemeral pool to 16 for tenant pool; monitoring error-rate. Seen drop from 18% -> 3% within 12 minutes.
Customer (ScribeAI - Marissa G) 2026-03-13T11:30: Confirmed reduced failures; appreciating update and mitigation steps. Asked for root cause details and ETA for permanent fix.
Eng (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-13T16:00: Patch to autoscaler heuristic submitted as github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2874. Request review from infra lead.
Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-14T09:00: Rollout complete. Sent ScribeAI follow-up with runbook and recommended retries. Marking ticket resolved but leaving follow-ups in backlog.

Issue summary:
Customers using long-lived streaming sessions observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses from the hosted API gateway starting ~2026-03-12 09:40 UTC. The pattern correlates with large numbers of clients that implement aggressive heartbeat/keepalive behavior (sub-30s) and intermittent TCP socket drift on edge proxies. Impact:
- LumenAI reporting 18% request error rate for streaming endpoints during the window, timed out sessions and partial responses.
- Platform-wide spike of 502/504 and some runtime OOMs in the serving fleet due to reconnect storms and connection churn.
Environment:
- Production (us-east-1), hosted API gateway fronting runtime pool (pools-03), nginx-based edge proxies + sidecar connection pool, runtime version runtime-v2.9.1.
Steps to reproduce (observed in lab with load generator):
1) Start 10k concurrent streaming clients using the LumenAI SDK configured to send JSON heartbeats every 20s.
2) Each client maintains an open HTTP/2 streaming session and occasionally sends small user messages interleaved with keepalives.
3) Introduce small packet loss / latency on proxy layer to simulate transient network jitter.
4) Observe connection resets from edge and a flurry of reconnect attempts within seconds.
Observed behavior:
- API gateway returns 502/504 for new streams as upstream runtime pool becomes partially unreachable.
- Serving runtime pods see a spike in open fds and ephemeral socket allocations, followed by OOM kills on a subset of pods.
- Edge proxy logs show `RST_STREAM` paired with `HTTP/2 PING` and long socket TIME_WAIT churn.
Expected behavior:
- Heartbeat jitter should be absorbed by connection backpressure and not cause bulk reconnect storms or upstream OOMs.
Logs / metrics pointers:
- CloudMetric: apigw.5xx.rate spike at 2026-03-12T09:40Z (dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.com/d/apigw/5xx-wave).
- Edge proxy logs (sample): "http2.RST_STREAM id=0x3fa err=2 remote=10.1.2.33" repeated.
- Runtime pod logs: "failed to accept connection: accept: too many open files" and kernel dmesg showing socket exhaustion on some nodes.

2026-03-12 10:02 - Support (Samir Patel): Initial triage with LumenAI. They confirmed they recently rolled a client SDK change that reduces heartbeat interval to 20s to keep UI ‘responsive’.
2026-03-12 11:15 - SRE (Elena Novak): Correlated apigw 5xx spike with increased TCP TIME_WAIT and high connection churn on edge proxies. Created alert rule apigw.conn-churn to track.
2026-03-12 13:40 - Support (Samir Patel): Customer applied temporary mitigation to revert SDK heartbeat to 60s; saw immediate improvement in error rate for their traffic but platform-wide noise persisted.
2026-03-13 09:30 - Runtime eng (Diego Morales): Observed file-descriptor leak in connection pool code path when stream client reconnects rapidly. Reproduced locally under synthetic reconnect storm.
2026-03-13 16:50 - PM (Aisha Kaur): Prioritizing a runtime patch to close sockets more eagerly and add backpressure at the proxy. Planning canary tomorrow.
Hypothesis 1: Aggressive client heartbeat combined with transient packet loss leads to duplicate keepalive semantics and outbound reconnect storms that exhaust FD limits on runtime nodes.
Hypothesis 2: Proxy->runtime socket handling has a small race where closed streams are not always releasing file descriptors until GC, amplifying during reconnect storms.
Metric checks: apigw.conn_attempts and apigw.conn_failures both spiked ~6x at 09:40Z. Runtime pods p63/p95 memory and open_fds increased before OOM. Node kernel shows large TIME_WAIT bucket growth.
Reproduction: In lab, reducing heartbeat to 20s + inducing 100ms packet loss caused 30% of synthetic streams to reconnect within 10s window, matching production error signature.
Temporary mitigation validated: Reverting client-side heartbeat to >=60s reduced reconnection rate by ~85% for that tenant; applying APIGW rate-limiter on new streaming session creation also damped the spike but needs cautious rollout to avoid breaking legitimate bursty UX.
Mitigation applied 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC: Enabled connection creation rate limiting on API gateway for streaming endpoints (soft limit: 200 new streams/sec per tenant) — rolled to us-east pool only. Immediate reduction in 5xx observed.
Hotfix deployed 2026-03-14 02:30 UTC to runtime (runtime-v2.9.2-hotfix): fixes a FD leak in the connection pool cleanup path and forces earlier socket close handshake when the peer resets. Canary monitored for 6 hours (no regressions).
Customer workaround: LumenAI reverted their SDK heartbeat to 60s and is publishing an SDK patch to implement exponential backoff on reconnects.
Follow-ups: 1) Full rollout of rate-limiter to other regions after load testing. 2) Backfill integration test that simulates noisy-heartbeat clients. 3) Update streaming keepalive guidance in docs. 4) Perf/QA to validate FD headroom on runtime nodes. Assigned to Diego Morales for runtime follow-up and to Nikhil Rao for APIGW policy rollout.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that after a network appliance upgrade in their edge stack, users in the private deployment started receiving 403s from Redwood Inference when invoking the admin APIs. Impact: Admin and service accounts for several tenants could not perform operations (role listing, service account impersonation). This blocks customer ops and scheduled model rollouts. Environment: Private deployment (VPC) for AceroHealth, prod/us-west, Redwood identity-proxy v2.3.1, customer-managed HAProxy 2.6.4 that sits in front of the identity proxy. Observed behavior: Requests arriving at identity-proxy contain an X-Forwarded-User header, but the value appears base64-like (e.g., "QWNlcm9cXFVzZXJcXDE=") instead of expected email/principal string. Authentication succeeds (JWT validated) but tenant resolution/subject canonicalization fails when mapping header to tenant-scoped principal, causing RBAC to drop all role bindings and return 403. Steps to reproduce: 1) Using a customer edge box with upgraded HAProxy, make a request to admin list roles endpoint with a valid OIDC token. 2) Observe 403. 3) Capture request at identity-proxy; header shows encoded principal. Logs / relevant headers: - Received header: X-Forwarded-User: QWNlcm9cXFVzZXJcXDE= - Expected header: X-Forwarded-User: alice.user@acerohealth.com - Example request id: rwd-req-20260310-7a3f - Identity-proxy log snippet (redacted): "tenant resolution failed: canonicalize_subject returned empty after header parse" Expected behavior: identity-proxy should map the incoming principal to a tenant and apply RBAC bindings; requests should not be blocked by a header encoding transformation introduced by the customer's edge appliance. Notes: Customer claims this started immediately after HAProxy upgrade and a config push from their network team. They do not intend to change upstream identity header behavior without a controlled rollout.
Hypothesis: network appliance config is intentionally encoding principal header. Confirmed by customer's HAProxy config and captured header values. Reproduced behavior in an internal testbed with HAProxy configured to base64-encode headers. Root cause: identity-proxy strictly validates header format and uses simple string canonicalization that rejects non-UTF8 or non-email-looking values, resulting in tenant lookup failing and RBAC falling back to deny. Risk assessment: automatically decoding customer-supplied headers can be risky (maliciously crafted values). Implemented temporary conservative decode that only runs when header matches strict base64 regex and decoded value matches tenant principal pattern (email-like). Logged this as INT-4421 for permanent fix: add explicit header-shaping policy and a tenant-trust flag for private deployments.
Workaround applied: deployed hotfix identity-proxy build that decodes base64-encoded X-Forwarded-User when and only when decoded value matches tenant principal pattern. Customer validated hotfix in canary and then applied to fleet. Permanent remediation: engineering to implement an opt-in header-normalization policy in identity-proxy and update private deployment docs with guidance: (1) do not transform identity headers upstream; (2) if transformation is required, coordinate with Redwood support to enable safe decoding or use signed headers. Follow-ups: INT-4421 (engineer work item), update Confluence runbook, add test coverage for encoded-header handling. Customer action: revert HAProxy base64 header encoding in next maintenance window.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 14:05 - AceroHealth (Customer): Provided HAProxy snippet: 'http-request set-header X-Forwarded-User %[base64(req.hdr(X-Forwarded-User))]' — says change was introduced to workaround logging corruption. Attached pcap showing encoded header passed through.
2026-03-12 17:49 - AceroHealth (Customer): Hotfix validated in canary and then rolled to fleet. Admin APIs functional again. No reports of additional 403s. Customer will revert HAProxy encoding after coordination with their logging team.
1) Add UI warning in Console when private deployments detect non-canonical identity headers. 2) Create k8s readiness probe for identity-proxy that flags header-normalization mismatches. 3) Add a short KB article for customers describing safe header transformations.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed a spike in end-to-end latency and an increase in auth retries immediately after a scheduled control-plane maintenance window that included a tenant residency pin swap.

Impact:
- Multiple requests from Acme Analytics (dedicated tenant) reported p95 increase from ~120ms to ~900ms and p99 bursts up to 3.2s for text-gen endpoints.
- Batch embedding jobs (off-peak) saw 4–6x token-cost increase due to repeated retries and multi-hop egress.
- Customer reported transient 401 and 502 errors correlated with the time window. No data loss reported.

Environment:
- Tenant: Acme Analytics (dedicated GPU pool)
- Primary residency: eu-west
- Control-plane maintenance window: 2026-03-10 03:00–03:20 UTC
- SDK: redwood-js v3.2.0
- Observed from multiple client regions (eu and APAC) via customer logs.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send steady stream of small generation requests at ~50 rps pinned to eu-west using tenant token.
2) Trigger pin-swap via control-plane (as performed in maintenance window).
3) Observe auth retries and occasional routing to us-east edges and degraded latency.

Logs / evidence snippets:
- edge-proxy: "2026-03-10T03:02:08Z ERROR auth: token refresh failed: 401 unauthorized (upstream=control-plane-2)"
- serving-runtime: "2026-03-10T03:02:09Z WARN route: selected-edge us-east-1 for tenant tid-ACME due to pin-ttl-expiry"
- customer telemetry: p95 120ms -> 900ms between 03:01–03:04 UTC; p99 spikes at 3.2s.

Observed patterns:
- Short-lived increase in control-plane write churn (pin updates) during maintenance.
- Edge nodes attempted token refresh and occasionally routed to secondary region edges while re-establishing residency.
- Auth retries were mostly 401s and followed by 1–3 retry attempts from SDK leading to higher e2e latency and duplicate upstream load.

Notes on customer impact and urgency:
Customer is on dedicated capacity and uses low-latency inference for real-time analytics dashboards. The incident caused visible UI lag and triggered on-call for their SREs. They requested a full RCA and mitigation steps to avoid recurrence.
2026-03-10 - 03:25 - Samira Patel (Support): Acknowledged and asked customer for request IDs and token TTLs. Requested sample SDK logs and timestamps. Escalated to SRE and control-plane on-call.
2026-03-10 - 04:10 - Diego Morales (SRE): Initial triage: observed pin update loop from control-plane services during maintenance window. Correlated with edges in us-east temporarily accepting requests for tid-ACME. Asked infra to pull edge TLS and auth logs for the 03:00-03:10 window.
2026-03-10 - 06:30 - Customer (Acme Analytics): Provided request IDs, SDK debug logs, and noticed same behavior from two different VPCs. Attached p95/p99 charts from their telemetry.
2026-03-11 - 09:00 - Diego Morales (SRE): Found ~18 control-plane writes for the tenant over a 90s window (expected 1 write). Hypothesis: control-plane maintenance task retried pin writes due to transient DB timeouts, which caused pin-ttl churn and edge affinity refreshes.
2026-03-12 - 11:45 - Product Ops: Noted that maintenance run involved a config deploy that bumped the pin-touch interval. Rolling back that config fixed the immediate churn in a canary cluster. Running a controlled replay to validate fix.
2026-03-12 - 14:30 - Samira Patel (Support): Shared temporary mitigation with customer: enable strict-residency-mode for tenant or schedule maintenance off their peak window. Customer applied strict-residency and reported p95 returned to baseline within 8 minutes.

Issue summary:
Customer (Aurelia Health, enterprise/dedicated) reports a sustained increase in prelude latency (time between request acceptance and first token emission) for short chat completions starting immediately after our runtime snapshot + model adapter update on 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC. Some requests escalate to 504 gateway timeouts when the first-token delay exceeds the proxy timeout.

Impact:
- Increased TTFB for ~70% of short-prompt chat sessions during peak for the customer's dedicated pools in us-east-1.
- ~2% of requests hit 504s during the peak window, causing customer app errors and increased support load.
- Affects production traffic only; staging unaffected.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (cust-dedicated-az1-us-east)
- Runtime snapshot: runtime-snapshot-2026-03-09-a
- Model adapter update: chat-adapter-v2.7 deployed to dedicated pools as part of the snapshot
- Region: us-east-1

Steps to reproduce (observed by Support):
1) Create a short chat prompt (~12 tokens) and request streaming completion via /v1/chat/complete on the customer's API key.
2) Observe request acceptance but delay in streaming start (30–1200 ms increase baseline) before first token emitted.
3) Repeated runs show high variance; longer prompts less impacted.

Observed behavior:
- Median TTFB increased from ~85ms to ~360ms for short prompts. Tail (95th) increased from ~220ms to ~1.4s.
- Some streams never start and result in 504 at the edge.
- No model-quality regressions observed in outputs.

Expected behavior:
- Short prompts should see first token within <150ms median on dedicated pools per SLA.
- Streaming should begin reliably without hitting the proxy timeout.

- Edge logs: edge-proxy/2026-03-09T03:12:45Z TRACE request-id=abc123 status=accepted backend=runtime-42
- Runtime logs (snippet):
  [2026-03-09T03:12:45.120Z] runtime-42 INFO accept request req=abc123 kernel=auto select_path=compat
  [2026-03-09T03:12:45.450Z] runtime-42 WARN kv-cache:prefix-miss key=conv-79 eviction=evict-oldest
  [2026-03-09T03:12:46.250Z] runtime-42 ERROR stream-start-delay req=abc123 elapsed_ms=1130 stage=kv-load

Hypothesis B: Scheduler affinity change (PR 112) delayed hot-slot assignment for short jobs causing queueing and head-of-line blocking at the runtime acceptor layer.

Additional observation: kv-cache eviction occurred more frequently after snapshot; eviction appears correlated with adapter v2.7 prefix hashing change.
Temporary mitigation validated by routing customer traffic to previous snapshot; suggests regression introduced in snapshot rather than customer config.
Mitigation applied: customer traffic routed back to previous runtime snapshot and observed latency returned to baseline. Engineering teams are coordinating a targeted rollback or patch to runtime-snapshot-2026-03-09-a that disables the new kernel-selection heuristics and restores previous kv-cache prefix behavior for dedicated pools. Permanent fix ETA TBD; follow-up ticket will be created for full postmortem and rollout plan.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer FinLedger reports intermittent shard validation failures when downloading model artifacts via presigned range GETs from a Private deployment behind their corporate ALB. The presigned GETs return 200 OK, but the assembled shard checksums do not match what the serving node expects, causing runtime checksum-fail aborts and degraded KV-cache warmup.

Impact:
- Serving nodes fail to load model shard(s) intermittently, causing increased cold-start latency and occasional fallbacks to smaller model variants.
- A subset (~2-3%) of shard downloads during nightly batch pulls result in checksum mismatch and abort, impacting capacity and customer SLAs.

Environment:
- Private deployment in customer VPC with a customer-managed application load balancer (ALB) in front of their corporate egress proxy.
- Redwood control plane and presigned URLs hosted in us-east-1.
- Affected nodes attempt concurrent multi-range downloads for shards (client issues 2-range requests per object).
1) Configure Private deployment with presigned S3-compatible URLs for shard range downloads.
2) From a host behind customer's ALB + egress proxy, issue parallel GETs with two Range units in the same request (e.g., Range: bytes=0-524287,524288-1048575).
3) Observe 200 responses but computed SHA256 checksum differs from expected on ~1-3% of attempts.
4) Reproduced reliably when traffic is routed through the customer's ALB; not reproducible from other networks.
Serving node logs: shard-fetch failed checksum: expected=ab12... got=9f3c... (partial content mismatch)
S3 access logs: 200 OK returned for presigned GET id=xyz-123, bytes served in two ranges
Customer tcpdump: outbound GET shows single Range header that appears normalized (units merged/reordered) by ALB before egress proxy.
Edge logs: occasional duplicate content-length values observed on 200 responses from upstream egress proxy.
Initial hypothesis: range-splitting or range-ordering mutation in transit leads to server returning merged byte ranges that client-side assembler misattributes to requested offsets.
Support downloaded pcap from customer — verified original client request contained two properly-formatted range units separated by a comma. Upstream observed request (captured after ALB) shows a single Range header value where units are coalesced and ordering is changed; in some cases spacing/semicolon normalization removed a crucial separator the object store relies on for multipart range processing.
Replayed requests directly to S3 origin from RW support network show correct behavior; replay from customer's ALB reproduces checksum drift.
SRE inspected ALB configuration and found a custom listener rule and a vendor-managed rewrite module (third-party WAF appliance) in front of the egress proxy; that appliance advertises header normalization and canonicalization features.
Correlation: failures cluster to specific ALB instance pool that routes through the third-party WAF/accelerator. Instances bypassing the accelerator show no failures.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 07:45 - FinLedger (Customer): Confirmed they recently enabled a vendor-managed WAF/accelerator rule-set (header canonicalization) last week. They can toggle it off for testing.
2026-03-12 15:20 - Support (Aisha Patel): Communicated temporary workarounds to customer and scheduled follow-up call with vendor and customer network ops. Recommended permanent fix approaches.
Workaround applied: Customer disabled the vendor header-canonicalization feature on the ALB/accelerator for egress to Redwood presigned endpoints. After disabling, shard downloads returned correct checksums and serving node load failures stopped.
Planned permanent remediation: 1) Customer to keep canonicalization disabled for calls to Redwood presigned endpoints and create an allowlist for presigned-hostnames. 2) Support guide updated with recommendation to avoid multi-range presigned GETs through header-normalizing middleboxes — added to runbook. 3) Engineering to add detection and more descriptive logs for checksum mismatches that include observed Range header text for easier triage (tracking PR: gh-rlw/infra#4321).
Follow-ups: Customer network team to engage vendor to patch header normalization behavior to preserve comma separation and ordering for Range headers. Redwood will add a console warning/tip for Private deployments behind ALBs that use vendor accelerators.
1) Customer to confirm vendor engineering ticket and ETA for fix.
2) RW SRE to land log-improvement PR to capture upstream Range header observed text in artifact-fetch traces.
3) Update Private deployment checklist and docs to call out header-normalizing middlebox risk.
payload.summary: ALB coalescing of multiple Range units in outbound requests causes sharded artifact checksum mismatch

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightRoute AI reported that after an attempted canary + shadow-mirroring rollout (promote -> shadow traffic -> abort), a subset of tenant requests continued to be routed to the legacy pinned version despite the canary being rolled back.

Impact:
- ~8% of requests from BrightRoute's production tenant were served by the legacy variant for ~30 minutes after the abort.
- Observed mixed outputs and intermittent tokenization deltas leading to downstream application errors and a brief billing discrepancy.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool for BrightRoute in us-west-2.
- Orchestrator version: v1.12.7.
- Edge-proxy: v3.4.2.
- Serving runtime: release-2025-11.

Steps to reproduce (customer report + internal repro):
1) Customer requested a canary rollout of redwood-v2-compat-7B with shadow-mirroring enabled for 10% traffic.
2) Prewarm and shadow started successfully; traffic mirrored to community-llama-70b-q4 for profiling.
3) At 10:23 UTC, customer aborted the rollout due to quality regression. Abort sequence initiated via console (rollout abort).
4) Control-plane reported abort complete at 10:24 UTC, but edge-mesh continued to serve legacy variant for ~30 minutes for a cohort of session tokens.
5) Repro by replaying session tokens from request logs shows consistent legacy variant routing for those tokens until a manual cache flush at 10:55 UTC.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Orchestrator logs show a successful abort and snapshot commit: "snapshot_commit: rollback -> epoch 8421".
- Edge-proxy logs show repeated 200 responses but with header X-Model-Version: redwood-v1-locked (legacy) for token cohort.
- Routing-mesh trace for a sampled request: "route-lookup -> route-cache hit -> affinity-token resolved to cohort-A -> model-binding: legacy" despite control-plane snapshot pointing to non-legacy binding.
- KV cache metrics show mismatched TTLs between edge cache and orchestrator snapshot: edge TTL remained at 12h, orchestrator snapshot epoch had a TTL of 30s for ephemeral binds.

Initial hypothesis:
- Shadow-mirror abort triggered a fast commit on the control plane, but the edge routing-mesh retained a stale affinity cache entry for a cohort of session tokens because prewarm shadowing wrote a long-lived binding in the edge cache. The longer TTL prevented expected unpin/unbind flows, causing implicit legacy routing.
- Possible race between cache-invalidation messages and the orchestrator's epoch bump, where the edge accepted the shadow prewarm write (with an undocumented TTL override) and ignored the subsequent rollback invalidate due to backpressure on the invalidation queue.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Support triggered a targeted cache invalidation for BrightRoute tenant cohort via edge admin API at 10:55 UTC which restored expected routing.
- We notified customer and opened this ticket for root-cause and broader mitigation.

Next steps:
- Engineering to verify invalidation queue metrics and whether backpressure led to dropped invalidation messages.
- Add telemetry to detect cohort-level routing divergence within 5 minutes of rollout abort.
- Short-term: tighten prewarm shadow write TTLs to 1 minute for dedicated-rollouts to avoid long-lived bindings.
- Postmortem to propose control-plane -> edge invalidation acknowledgements for committed rollbacks.

Notes:
- Customer reported a small billing spike due to additional served tokens while legacy variant was active; finance notified for adjustment pending final RCA.
- See linked GH PRs for an in-progress change to edge invalidation handling.

Additional notes:
2025-11-19 - Product (Ava Martinez): Request to add a rollout post-check to verify no cohort-level bindings remain after abort; will coordinate with engineering for telemetry dimension specs.
2025-11-20 - Engineering (PR note): gh:inference/orchestrator#4321 opened to ensure rollback sends explicit invalidation messages and retries on queue backpressure. Edge change gh:edge/proxy#508 will cap prewarm TTL and surface backpressure metrics.
2025-11-20 - Support (Sofia Chen): Customer update drafted; offering credit for extra tokens pending RCA. Asked finance to hold invoice adjustment until engineering confirms fix timeline.
Mitigation: targeted cache invalidation done; short-term fix to cap prewarm TTL deployed to staging. Long-term fix (invalidation ACKs + retries) in PR review. Pending full RCA and postmortem.
Deploy edge TTL cap to prod for dedicated prewarm flows
Add invalidation ack telemetry and alerting
Conduct postmortem and update rollout runbook
Finance: reconcile billing delta with BrightRoute

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer enabled two optimizer changes in production for /v1/generate: speculative-batching (enabled at 1s wait threshold) and a new aggressive mixed-precision quant profile (quant-profile: aggressive-e2e). Immediately after the change AcmeCorp observed spiking p99 latency and several timed-out streams.

Impact: Intermittent client timeouts and elevated p99 (~4-6x baseline) for a high-volume tenant lane. Customer reports user-facing errors in a throttled portion of traffic and requests an assisted, low-risk pathway to revert or safe-drain the optimizer changes without extended downtime.

Environment: prod us-east, Dedicated tenant lane for AcmeCorp (enterprise reserved pool), model variants rw-open-3b and rw-compat-1.0, traffic mix: chat streaming + small non-streaming inference.

Desired outcome: step-by-step escape-hatch that minimizes traffic disruption and provides a controlled rollback of speculative-batching and quant-profile with validation gates, plus recommended telemetry to monitor during unwind.

1) Tenant config: speculative-batching: enabled (1s); prefix_cache: enabled (default); quant_profile: aggressive-e2e applied to both variants.
2) Send steady-state streaming chat traffic at ~240 rps for 60 minutes.
3) Observe 95p/99p latency and increased stream disconnects.
4) Check serving-runtime logs for eviction and kernel fallback warnings.

Customer supplied timeline logs and spans: s3://acmecorp-prod-artifacts/2026-03-10/trace-tenant-76142.tar.gz; sample request ids: req-20260310-7a3f, req-20260310-7b1e. Relevant console graphs: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenant/AcmeCorp/latency?p=24h. Error snippets include:
- 'kv_cache_eviction: true, eviction_reason=kv_capacity'
- 'kernel_fallback: float32-path triggered for layer 4 due to quant mismatch'

Initial SRE triage: correlated p99 spikes with high speculative-batching coalescing windows that increased sequence length variance and triggered unexpected KV cache churn. Aggressive quant profile produced intermittent kernel incompatibility for rw-compat-1.0, falling back to slower float32 kernels.
Hypotheses: 1) Speculative batching increased inter-request packing causing larger effective sequences and cache pressure; 2) Aggressive quant interacts with certain kernels, causing rare slow-path execution; 3) Combined effect pushes some RPCs past streaming timeouts.
Telemetry consulted: request-level latency heatmaps, per-shard kernel version logs, KV cache hit/evict counters, and batching histogram via tracing endpoint.
Next steps proposed: capture per-tenant kernel-fallback rate (metric: runtime.kernel_fallback.count by tenant), enable per-tenant batching cap, and stage quant-profile downgrade on a small traffic slice.

Applied per-tenant batching cap: max_batch_size=64 and speculative-batching: wait_threshold lowered to 250ms for AcmeCorp lane (toggled via tenant optimizer overrides). Early metrics show p99 reduction from 1.8s to ~1.1s in the first 45 minutes. Still monitoring.
1) Start with non-disruptive throttles: set speculative-batching wait_threshold=250ms and max_batch_size=64 for AcmeCorp lane (apply via tenant override).
2) Monitor kernel_fallback.count and kv_cache_eviction.rate for 20 minutes.
3) If metrics improve, stage quant-profile downgrade to conservative-e2e for rw-compat-1.0 on 5% traffic (traffic-split via routing config).
4) Validate end-to-end: latency dashboard, streaming success rate, and customer sampling.
5) If step 3 passes at 5% for 30 minutes, ramp to 25% then 100% in 15-minute steps.
6) If any step regresses, perform immediate rollback to previous step and open an incident for deeper kernel/quant interaction analysis.
7) Post-mortem: collect flamegraphs and kernel-call traces, and schedule optimizer regression test for this workload pattern.
In Progress - temporary batching cap applied which reduced p99 by ~40% in initial window. Quant-profile downgrade staged at 5% traffic during maintenance window; awaiting 30-minute validation. No full revert performed yet. Final resolution pending validation; will document final steps and follow-up actions once complete.
- SRE to collect detailed kernel fallback traces and attach to ticket. - PM to triage aggressive-e2e quant profile for rw-compat-1.0 and add regression tests. - CS to confirm client-level retry/backoff guidance with AcmeCorp engineering.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:45 - AcmeCorp SRE (J. Patel): We can take a 30-minute rolling maintenance window starting 09:30 UTC if it lowers risk. We prefer stepwise traffic gates rather than abrupt config flips.
J. Patel - AcmeCorp (2026-03-11 09:37): Seeing reduced timeouts in user infra; appreciate live assist. Please proceed with quant downgrade staging.
V. Singh - Runtime SRE (2026-03-11 10:00): Kernel-fallback logs attached to internal artifact store: s3://redwood-internal/triage/SUP-76142/kernel_fallback_20260311.tar.gz. Noted increased L4 fallback rate coincident with large coalesced batches.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer uses the Python async iterator SDK to send batched requests that include multiple attachments (binary blobs) per request. They gzip each batch on the client side. When the server returns a transient 202+retryable ack (internal queue enqueue), the SDK retries and we observe duplicate tool/function executions downstream (duplicate webhook calls and duplicate DB side effects).

Impact:
- Multiple duplicate downstream webhook posts and side effects for a small subset (~0.6%) of batched requests during transient enqueue failures.
- Customer reports data duplication and billing noise for high-volume ingestion job.
- Affects dedicated customers using client-side gzip + async iterator batching pattern.

Environment:
- Customer: SwellHealth (dedicated cluster)
- SDK: sdk-python v1.14.2 (async iterator example)
- Runtime: dedicated serving pool in prod-us-east
- Proxy: edge-sidecar with gzip passthrough enabled
- Observed on models: redwood-gpt-3.5-large (primary), also reproduced on llama-2-13b in test runs

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Use async for chunk in client.stream_batches(...): send batch that contains 3 attachments (binary ECG, JSON metadata, PDF) compressed with gzip at client before sending.
2. Server returns 202 Accepted with body {"enqueue": "ok", "trace": "..."} but internal queue intermittently times out when attempting to ack.
3. SDK interprets 202 as transient and retries the entire batch (full gzip binary) after applying backoff.
4. Downstream worker consumes both messages from queue (original and retried) and triggers the same tool/function twice (webhook POST + DB write).

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate webhook POSTs with identical payloads and same content checksum but different request IDs.
- No idempotency key present in the batched/gzipped envelope because the client included per-item IDs inside the compressed payload, not in the request headers or envelope-level idempotency metadata.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should either be deduplicated server-side by an envelope-level idempotency key or the SDK should ensure a stable idempotency token is attached to the request header even when payloads are gzipped by client.

Logs and traces (redacted):
- API gateway logs show repeated POSTs for the same client session id within a 2s window: request_id=req-17a3, req-17a4
- Serving runtime trace: enqueue attempt 1 -> internal queue timeout (timeout after 550ms) -> SDK retry -> enqueue attempt 2 -> queue ok -> downstream worker processed message id ws-993 -> processed again id ws-994
- Edge proxy logs show content-encoding: gzip on both requests; content-length identical.

Customer-provided code snippet (sanitized):
async for batch in batch_generator():
    compressed = gzip.compress(serialize(batch))
    await client.stream_send(compressed, headers={"Content-Encoding": "gzip"})

Workaround attempted by customer:
- Client-side dedupe table (in-memory) keyed by per-item UUIDs inside payload. Reduced duplicates but did not eliminate them because some retry windows cross process restarts.

Notes:
- This pattern differs from single-request idempotency since the idempotency data is buried inside a compressed envelope and not visible to middle proxies or the enqueueer.
- There are existing tickets about idempotency header truncation and token rotation, but this is specifically about envelope-level idempotency and client-side gzip in the async iterator pattern.

Issue summary:
- LumenAI observed repeated ~10–30 minute windows of throughput collapse in their dedicated pool starting 2026-03-10 11:15 UTC. During windows, p50 stays stable but p95/p99 and tail token latency increase sharply and request attach success rate falls.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat endpoints returned slower responses and occasional 500s due to allocation timeouts; customer reported partial outages affecting ~20% of requests for the dedicated pool. Revenue-impacting for peak window.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: lumenai-prod-dedicated-1 (us-east-1)
- Serving runtime v4.3.2, allocator v2.8, autoscaler v1.6

Steps to reproduce / observed pattern:
1) Traffic steady 400 rps for short prompts.
2) At hh:15 and hh:45 local cluster prefetch sweep starts (background job to prewarm KV caches).
3) Prefetch causes short-lived burst of IO and CPU on sidecars -> several GPU attachments delayed by 200-800ms.
4) Autoscaler sees attach latency above threshold and triggers backoff/scale-down decisions for ~1–2 min.
5) Result: queued requests, slot starvation for the tenant, throughput falls and p99 spikes.

Observed metrics/logs (samples):
- allocator.attach_latency.p99 = 920ms (baseline 120ms)
- autoscaler.scale_decisions.rate increased by 3x during window
- sidecar.io_utilization spiked to 85% on affected hosts
- kernel logs show repeated NVMe io wait with device /dev/nvme1n1 busy

Temporary workarounds attempted by Support/Customer:
- Customer switched route to a warmed fallback model variant (reduced QPS to primary) — reduced visible impact.
- Support manually disabled hourly prefetch cron on 2 staging hosts to confirm correlation; throughput stabilized on those hosts.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: aggressive prefetch sweep (global daemon) is saturating sidecar CPU/network and NVMe IO, delaying GPU attach handshakes. This creates a noisy-neighbor effect: background maintenance from many tenants coincides and overwhelms allocator signals.
- Allocator/AWS-level logs show attach retries and timeouts at the same timestamps as the prefetch sweep.
- Autoscaler logic currently treats attach latency spikes as capacity pressure and tends to back off instead of temporarily increasing headroom.
- Related to previously seen patterns in SUP-271400 (ephemeral-allocator-latency-from-sparse-tenant-spinups) but differs because root cause is background cache sweeps rather than tenant burst traffic.

Next diagnostic actions planned:
- Disable prefetch sweeps for LumenAI dedicated cluster for 24h window (safe rollback plan in place).
- Run an instrumented prefetch job with reduced concurrency to measure sidecar CPU/IO impact.
- Add finer-grained autoscaler rule: ignore transient attach spikes shorter than 90s for dedicated pools or increase conservative headroom during prefetch windows.
- Correlate with NVMe telemetry and sidecar GC logs to confirm IO saturation.

Customer communication plan:
- Notified LumenAI CSM and on-call SRE; provided workaround steps and ETA for next update.
- Committed to a follow-up within 24h with findings and mitigation timeline.
- 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC: On-call SRE captured attach traces and NVMe iostat during event.
- 2026-03-10 12:30 UTC: Disabled prefetch cron on two warm hosts; those hosts returned to normal p99 within 3 minutes.
- Evidence: sidecar CPU+io bandwidth is the common factor across impacted hosts. Prefetch batch sizes in v1.1 of daemon are large and parallelized; appears to be safe for shared pools but not tuned for dedicated tenant sidecars pinned to small host sets.
- Autoscaler decision logs: multiple scale-down votes triggered by ephemeral attach latency metrics; scale-down window is 60s which is too short for short sweeps.
- No GPU driver crashes or kernel panics observed; attach delays are I/O/sidecar-induced rather than GPU-side failures.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 14:05 - LumenAI Engineer (Customer): Thanks, disabling prefetch on our side reduced errors; still seeing some p99 blips.
2026-03-12 08:55 - Product (PD): Need proposal for autoscaler change to avoid reactive scale-down on sub-2min attach spikes for dedicated routes; assigning to autoscaler squad.
Workaround: Disabled global prefetch sweeps for LumenAI dedicated cluster and rolled out a reduced-concurrency prefetch job (concurrency=2, batch-size=64). Post-change: allocator.attach_latency.p99 dropped to 140ms and autoscaler backoff events ceased.
Planned permanent fixes: (1) Autoscaler cooldown tuning for dedicated pools (PR merged target v1.7), (2) Add prefetcher tenant-awareness to throttle background jobs on small dedicated pools, (3) Run HV test to ensure no regressions.
Follow-up actions logged to Confluence runbook and linked engineering tickets for long-term change.
payload.summary: Midday warmup-prefetch sweeps causing transient GPU attach lag, autoscaler backoff and throughput collapse for dedicated tenant

Issue summary:
Customer reported intermittent 429 throttles observed during scheduled orchestrated worker waves immediately following a tenant merge (two subaccounts merged into NebulaSearch parent org).

Impact:
- Multiple production ingestion jobs returning 429s for ~7-15s bursts, 3-5 times per hour for the last 36 hours.
- Affects downstream ranking pipeline; spikes correlate with orchestrated worker restarts (cron-based parallelizers).

Environment:
- prod-us-east, tenant: nebulasearch-prod, dedicated: no (hosted), models: gptx-13b for text gen and embed-lite-v1 for embeddings.
- Merge occurred 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC (internal tenant consolidation script).

Observed behavior:
- Soft 429s with X-RateLimit-Reason: "window-smoothing-conflict" in headers (internal marker).
- Around the merge time the tenant-level refill window appears to have been switched from 60s smoothing to 300s smoothing, but some route-level token buckets still used the old per-route burst window leading to uneven accounting and short tenant-wide exhausts.

Expected behavior:
- After tenant merge, quota accounting should converge to the configured tenant-level smoothing policy without producing transient 429s for steady workers.
1) Tenant-merge: consolidate subaccount A and B into parent tenant C (use internal merge tool).
2) Start 50 orchestrated worker processes that each open a short-lived streaming session followed by a burst of concurrent embedding uploads.
3) Observe per-worker success followed by short 429 bursts on ~10% of sessions within first 5 minutes.
4) Inspect rate-limit headers and quota metrics for tenant and routes in console.

[2026-03-10T00:12:06Z] rate-limiter: tenant_token_bucket deplete_estimate=0 refill_window=300s route_token_bucket burst_remaining=0
[2026-03-10T00:12:06Z] ingest-orchestrator: worker-17 retrying after 120ms backoff
[2026-03-10T00:12:20Z] rate-limiter: tenant bucket refill partial=50 tokens

- Confirmed merge ran using consolidation tool v2.1 which flipped default tenant smoothing to 300s window (feature flag: tenant_smoothing_v2).
- Metrics show tenant-level token accounting reports periodic undercounting for ~10s after merge events.
- Route-level buckets for legacy routes retained 60s burst window; the cross-layer refill algorithm double-applies smoothing resulting in tenant tokens being counted then consumed by route refill logic.
- Hypothesis: During merge we left transient in-memory token snapshots for each route that were re-applied on top of the new tenant smoothing, causing short tenant-level exhaustion.

4) Rolling restart of rate-limiter pods to clear in-memory snapshots (coordinated with SRE).

- Add post-merge validation to consolidation tool to ensure route and tenant windows are reconciled before enabling traffic.
- SRE to schedule a controlled rollout of a fix and monitor NebulaSearch metrics for 24 hours post patch.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that chat completions show a pronounced delay before the first token is emitted after our runtime hotpatch and a model repin that went out 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC. The problem appears as ~1.5-4s extra TTFB on initial responses for small prompt payloads.

Impact:
- Affects Noteable Analytics (dedicated deployment).
- ~25% of chat sessions show elevated TTFB; some requests also time out after backend retries.
- User-facing: slow UI response, occasional socket disconnects when frontend gives up after 10s.

Environment:
- prod:us-east (customer-dedicated cluster noteable-prod-us-east)
1) Using Noteable Analytics workspace, start a new chat session with a short prompt (~12 tokens).
2) Trigger generation via the standard /v1/chat/completions endpoint pinned to rw-chat-medium-v1.
3) Observe that the client receives no tokens for 1.5-4s before streaming begins.
4) Repeat across multiple sessions and note percent impacted.

Observed behavior:
- Elevated TTFB (1.5-4s) on first token emission.
- Backend traces show requests queued at the serving-runtime input queue for 200-800ms and an additional ~1.2-3s spent in pre-compile/compat checks for certain kernels.

Expected behavior:
- Typical TTFB for same workloads is <500ms with small variance.

Relevant logs and traces:
- Trace IDs (sample): 34b7f2c1, 98a2c11e, d1a8b7f3.
- SLO dashboard: spike in first-token latency starting 2026-03-09 02:10 UTC and matching the hotpatch rollout window.
- Serving runtime logs: intermittent messages: "compat-layer: verifying kernel variant" followed by "alloc: delayed on device sync" for affected requests.

Temporary workaround:
- We validated that pinning the customer's route to the previous runtime bundle (runtime-2026-03-02) removes the extra TTFB.
- Routing to the dedicated fallback pool also mitigates the issue but reduces throughput capacity.

Notes:
- Customer is sensitive to latency; they have dashboards and are asking for an update within our SLA window.
Summary of preliminary findings:
- Timeline: hotpatch runtime bundle runtime-2026-03-09 was rolled out across regions 02:00-02:30 UTC 2026-03-09. At 02:10 UTC we see first-token latency increase correlated with that window.
- Kernel selection gating: New runtime adds an ABI compatibility check that performs a lightweight compile/verification step for some quantized kernels. For models rw-large-v2-onnx-quant we observed a full verification path that adds ~1-2s.
- Queueing behavior: The scheduler has a new affinity microtuning that attempts to consolidate KV-caches; this increases input queue wait when nodes are cold for a specific kernel variant (~200-800ms measured).
- Cache miss amplification: When model repin to rw-chat-medium-v1 occurs concurrently with runtime hotpatch, KV cache entries are evicted and subsequent requests pay an added compilation/verify penalty.
- Error surface: No increased 5xx rates observed in metrics, but client-level timeouts increase due to extra latency.
- Repro on staging: Reproduced by toggling the compatibility check flag and repinning model; deterministic on specific quantized variants.

Hypotheses:
1) The newly-introduced compatibility verification step in runtime-2026-03-09 causes per-request serial preflight work for certain quantized kernels, driving the 1-3s extra TTFB.
2) Affinity microtuning + on-the-fly model repin amplifies queueing and prevents warm kernel reuse, increasing overall tail.
- Short-term: keep customer's route pinned to runtime-2026-03-02 (validated). Continue routing to fallback pool while we patch.
- Medium-term: land a hotfix to skip full verification for previously-seen kernel signatures (change id: PR #2145) and deploy to a canary subset.
- Long-term: add a fast-path cache for kernel-compatibility checks and enhance rollout gating to avoid concurrent repins during hotpatch windows.
- Action owners: Marco Chen (runtime) to own hotfix; Priya Singh (scheduler) to evaluate affinity rollback; Aisha Patel (support) to coordinate with customer.
- ETA for patch: targeting 2026-03-16 canary; broader rollout after validation.

Workarounds in place: customer route pinned to previous runtime and temporary fallback cluster configured. Full resolution pending hotfix rollout (PR #2145). No permanent code rollback performed. Will update when canary metrics confirm improvement.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers using our multipart/streaming embedding ingestion path intermittently observe rerank result inversion (top-k order flips) and occasional 504s from the reranker. Problem appears after a protobuf/streaming encoder change rolled out in the embeddings-service last week.

Impact:
- A dozen customers on dedicated clusters report degraded search quality (relevant docs ranked lower) and spikes of 504s for batched rerank requests.
- DataSleuth Inc. reports 7% drop in A/B click-through on search within two hours of ingestion batch job.

Environment:
- prod us-east-1, dedicated pools, embed-lite-v2 used for ingestion, search-reranker-1 used for reranking.
- Upload method: multipart/streaming HTTP to /v1/embeddings:stream with chunked protobuf messages.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Client uploads a corpus using multipart streaming (boundary-based protobuf frames) where final chunk may be sub-full-size (common for last file).
2) Embeddings-service acknowledges and writes vectors to storage; reranker triggered on write.
3) Rerank endpoint returns reordered results compared to baseline (same corpus uploaded via single-request path).
4) Occasionally the rerank request times out (504) when fallback to CPU-based scoring is triggered.

Observed logs/snippets:
- embeddings-service: "WARN encoder: last_frame_size 0 -> trimming trailing zeros" (multiple occurrences)
- storage-writer: "INFO wrote_vector dims=768 id=ds-12345 size_bytes=3072"
- reranker: "ERROR scoring: kv-cache-mismatch detected, falling back to cpu-scorer (latency spike)"
- nginx: "upstream prematurely closed connection" for some requests

Notes: The baseline (single-request) ingestion produces stable top-k. The issue is intermittent and correlated with uploads that use chunked streaming or multipart uploads where the last chunk is < full-frame-size.

Initial hypothesis: encoder change introduced aggressive trailing-zero trimming on streaming frames; when the last chunk becomes shorter than expected we appear to pad/truncate to the wrong dimension during storage write, causing slight L2 distance differences that flip close ties in top-k. Evidence: encoder log warnings and increased rate of 'kv-cache-mismatch' messages in reranker logs.

What we've checked so far:
- Replayed affected uploads locally with the current encoder: reproduced top-k inversion for small final-chunk sizes.
- Compared storage vector byte size for same doc uploaded via single vs multipart: observed off-by-n bytes in some records.
- Verified that the dimensionality metadata in storage is correct (768), but trailing bytes contain garbage/zeros in problematic records.
- Confirmed reranker falls back to CPU-scorer when cache signature doesn't match (explains 504s/latency spikes).

Hypotheses:
1) Streaming encoder trims trailing zeros incorrectly and does not mark a frame boundary, causing write of truncated vector.
2) Protobuf framing change altered how last-frame lengths are interpreted (end-of-stream marker missed).
3) Storage write path has a compatibility shim that assumes fixed-chunk framing and pads differently.

Next steps planned:
- Reproduce with small test harness across embed-lite-v2 with multiple last-chunk sizes (0..frame_size-1).
- Add extra validations on write: reject vectors whose raw byte-length != dims * dtype_size. Temporary reject will force client retry path and avoid serving bad vectors.
- Roll a canary fix in embeddings-service to stop trimming trailing zeros until framing logic is validated (PR prepared).
- Add an alert to detect sudden jump in 'kv-cache-mismatch' and 'truncated-vector' warnings.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:34 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Correlated nginx upstream closed logs with same time window. Noticed encoder WARNs in embeddings-service logs for the customer's cluster.
2026-03-11 08:47 - Customer (DataSleuth SRE, Priya Rao): We can reproduce by splitting files into many small parts; we need a mitigation ASAP — affecting search results for production users.
Workaround: Advise customers to switch to single-request uploads or ensure chunking aligns with frame_size. Temporary canary guard added to reject vectors with mismatched byte-length, preventing bad vectors from being written.
Fix in progress: PR to embeddings-service (https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings/pull/212) pins protobuf framing behavior and disables trailing-zero trimming until a robust framing validation is implemented. Expect full rollout after automated tests and a staged canary (target: 2026-03-15).
Follow-ups:
- Add unit tests for streaming encoder corner cases.
- Add provenance flag on vectors written from streaming ingestion for future audits.
- Postmortem and runbook update to include multipart ingestion checks.

3) Monitor: console -> routes -> redwood-api/v1/generate -> 95p/99p latency spikes correlated with increased batch construction time and elevated GPU busy-waits

Observed: increases in batch formation time when request arrival bursts are > expected inter-arrival time. KV hit rate dropped ~12% during spikes (suspected misaligned prefix caching keys).
Router traces show several requests delayed in batching layer for 40-80ms while waiting for batch completion before GPU dispatch - amplifies under N:1 request patterns (long-running contexts).

1) Capture current optimizer profile snapshot for tenant (console export + s3 archive): command provided to customer for audit.
2) 'Soft-pause' per-tenant optimizations by disabling batching.max_wait_ms and kv_prefetch only for that tenant (no global rollout). This should be toggled via the tenant gating API to avoid node restarts.
3) Apply a 10% traffic split rule: route 90% to current profile, 10% to 'stable' profile (smaller batch size, kv_prefetch=false, quant_profile=latency-safe). Observe 5/15/95/99p for 30 minutes.
4) If metrics improve for the 10% bucket, increase split gradually (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with monitoring checks at each step. If any regression observed, revert split to previous ratio.
5) When back at 100% stable profile, run a controlled A/B test to reintroduce individual optimizations (first kv_prefetch as a toggle, then quant_profile change), verifying KV hit rate and tail latency after each step.
6) Provide customer-facing commands and a console checklist for performing the toggles without support intervention.
7) Post-mitigation: collect traces and schedule a design follow-up to refine batching heuristics (e.g., adaptive batch size based on observed inter-arrival distribution).
Soft-pause (disabling kv_prefetch and adjusting batching wait) is low risk: per-tenant flag toggles are applied at request-router layer, no pod restarts required.
Traffic-splitting increases complexity for a short window; must ensure idempotent routing rules and avoid sticky sessions that bypass split.
Quant profile rollback might change token-level costs slightly (higher compute cost) — inform billing/sales if long duration.
If KV cache keys are misaligned, toggling kv_prefetch could temporarily drop hit rate until cache warms; include warming phase in playbook.

Additional notes:
Elena Gomez (SRE) (2026-03-12): Executed 10% traffic split at 02:20 UTC. 10% bucket (stable profile) 95p dropped from 1.25s -> 360ms. 90% bucket still saw spikes. Recommended progressive ramp after 30m steady-state.
Customer Rep - Tom Rivera (BrightHealth) (2026-03-12): Approved 10% test; requests that we avoid full quant profile rollback due to latency-sensitive models for some endpoints.
Implemented soft-pause for batching.max_wait_ms and disabled kv_prefetch for BrightHealth tenant via tenant-gating API; applied progressive traffic-split to stable profile, validated improved 95p/99p latency, and retained stable profile after customer sign-off. Quant profile change was deferred and will be re-evaluated with extended A/B testing. Archived optimizer snapshot to S3 and updated customer's runbook with step-by-step commands and confirmation checks.
1) Engineering: Add a console 'soft-pause' one-click toggle and safe-restore wizard for per-tenant optimizer profiles (owner: runtime team, due: 2026-04-06).
2) Product: Review default batching heuristics and consider a conservative tenant guardrail for newly onboarded profiles (owner: product, due: 2026-04-15).
3) Support: Publish KB article 'How to safely split traffic and soft-pause tenant optimizer settings' and attach to BrightHealth account (owner: support docs, due: 2026-03-20).
4) SRE: Implement automated metric checks to detect KV hit-rate drops >= 10% concurrent with tail-latency regressions (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-28).

Issue summary:
Customer reports a $1,250 postpaid charge invoiced to their production org after a canary rollout. The customer uses a dedicated account with separate staging API keys which they expect to be covered by an internal sandbox allowance. BrightCart says the usage shows against their production org (parent) rather than the staging subaccount and that charges appeared overnight (billing date 2026-03-13).

Impact:
- Customer received an unexpected invoice charge of $1,250 for what they claim was low-traffic staging tests.
- Billing alerts triggered for the production org, causing PagerDuty alerts and SLA noise.
- Customer paused all deployments until attribution is resolved.

Environment:
- Dedicated account on us-east-1.
- Canary rollout performed from staging key associated with org: brightcart-staging (subaccount id: sb-87623).
- Production org: brightcart-prod (org id: org-11911).

Steps to reproduce / Observed sequence:
1) 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC: customer initiated canary rollout from staging key (sb-87623) to test redwood-rlhf-1.2b with a small percentage of traffic.
2) 2026-03-12 22:05–23:30 UTC: steady stream of canary requests (hundreds) with long-context generation.
3) 2026-03-13 03:05 UTC: internal metering batch job ran and aggregated per-hour usage for both orgs and persisted to billing table.
4) 2026-03-13 04:20 UTC: billing job attributed aggregated tokens from sb-87623 to parent org org-11911 and generated a charge.
5) 2026-03-13 08:30 UTC: BrightCart received invoice notification and opened support ticket.

Expected behavior:
- Usage originating from staging API key (sb-87623) should be billed to the staging subaccount and reflect sandbox allowances.

Actual behavior:
- Metering pipeline appears to have collapsed subaccount attribution, assigning tokens to the parent production org, generating an unexpected charge.

Logs / Evidence provided by customer:
- Customer attached a CSV of API request IDs and timestamps (redacted) showing requests tied to sb-87623.
- Billing invoice (PDF) showing $1,250 charge to brightcart-prod for 2026-03-13.

Customer notes:
- They temporarily disabled canary after seeing invoices.
- They request a reversal/credit for the charge and confirmation of fix.

2026-03-13 09:05 - Customer (Avery Chen): We ran a 2% canary on staging only. We have explicit sandbox credits on sb-87623. This invoice is unexpected — please investigate.
2026-03-13 09:12 - Support (Nina Walker): Thanks for the report. I've triaged this to billing and metering teams; assigning to Marcus Lee for investigation. We'll gather logs and confirm attribution. SLA P1 acknowledged.
2026-03-13 11:40 - Support (Marcus Lee): Initial findings: the metering pipeline emitted a cleanup job at 03:05 UTC that collapsed subaccount tags when batch-joining caches. Reproducing locally now against the nightly metering snapshot. Linked INT-4421 for deeper ingestion issues.
2026-03-13 14:05 - Eng (SRE Team): Hypothesis: a recent change in the batch-join (PR #981) introduced a null propagation when staging_key metadata is missing, defaulting to parent_org. We see unit tests covering per-request attribution but not the late-aggregation path.
2026-03-13 16:20 - Support (Marcus Lee): Temporary mitigation applied: disable the nightly aggregation job for affected billing window to prevent further mis-attribute writes. No new charges will be generated for 2026-03-13 window while we reconcile.

Investigation summary: Reproduced failure in staging using metering nightly snapshot. Root cause traced to merge in PR #981 (metering service) where late-aggregation join omitted 'subaccount_id' for requests that used staging API keys with a nonstandard metadata header. The late-aggregation path (runs in worker 'billing-aggregator-v2') falls back to 'owner_org' if subaccount_id is null. A regression test gap allowed this. Evidence: query logs (billing-db) show tokens originally tagged with sb-87623, but final billing_row entries show org-11911. Observed similar null propagation for two other subaccounts but only BrightCart crossed billing threshold. Related artifacts: slack thread #billing-ops (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C07BILL/12345), GH PR 981, billing DB query ids qb-7741, qb-7742.
Resolution summary: 1) Immediate: disabled nightly aggregation job for the affected window and re-ran reconciliation script with corrected join logic to preserve subaccount_id. 2) Billing: issued a $1,250 credit memo to brightcart-prod and offered immediate refund; customer selected credit memo (will appear on next invoice). 3) Engineering: merged hotfix (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/987) to ensure subaccount_id is never overwritten with null in late-aggregation; added regression tests covering staging key flow. 4) Follow-up actions: postmortem scheduled, add monitoring alert on sudden parent-org charge spikes, add canary for metering aggregation.
Notes for CS ops: Credit memo number CM-2026-317 applied to org-11911; billing asked to notify customer once credit posts. Engineering estimate for hotfix to reach prod: 6 hours (completed 2026-03-14 04:30 UTC). Postmortem (internal) due 2026-03-21.

Issue summary:

During a customer-triggered traffic surge last night, tenant sessions for NimbusHealth experienced repeated model-version pin oscillations after the autoscaler performed quota-driven preemptive GPU rebalancing. Traffic for affected sessions alternated between the pinned variant (gptx-7b-v1) and a degraded fallback (gptx-7b-v1-quant) causing mixed outputs and a visible quality regression for the customer.

Impact:
- ~18% of requests from the tenant in us-east-1 returned responses from the quantized fallback variant during a 22-minute window.
- Several long-lived streaming sessions were truncated (stream closed mid-response) and retried, leading to increased token counts and billing anomalies.
- Customer-facing SLA alerts for latency and output quality were triggered.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant pin should hold for the session cohort during autoscaler preemptive operations unless an explicit orchestrator demotion occurs.
- Fallback routing should only be taken during node failure or explicit health probe evictions, not as a side-effect of quota preemption.

1) Provision a dedicated pool with quota policy set to aggressive_preempt (customer-simulated).
2) Start 30 long-lived streaming sessions pinned to gptx-7b-v1 for a single tenant in us-east-1.
3) Trigger a quota-driven autoscale event by increasing unrelated tenant traffic to exhaust GPU headroom, causing preemptive rebalancing.
4) Observe routing decisions in request traces and model variant field in responses over the next 30 minutes.
2026-03-10T02:14:21Z orchestrator: epoch_jump detected during preemptive_rebalance job=preempt-7901 tenant_id=nimbus-42 session_cohort=cohort-7
2026-03-10T02:14:22Z autoscaler: scheduled_preempt: gpu_node=node-34 -> dest_pool=standby (reason=quota_headroom_low)
2026-03-10T02:14:22Z edge-proxy: session-handshake-delay=118ms pin_token=abc123 cohort_marker=cohort-7
2026-03-10T02:14:22Z serving-runtime: kv_cache-mismatch: expected_variant=gptx-7b-v1 actual_variant=gptx-7b-v1-quant (fallback_taken)
2026-03-10T02:30:45Z streaming: stream_closed mid-response: reason=orchestrator_rebind attempt=1
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10: Customer reported quality regressions and elevated token usage during their nightly load test. Attached traces show version field flipping between variants within session lifetimes. Escalating to SRE and Serving team.
SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-10: Reproduced on a staging replica of the customer's pool using aggressive_preempt. Observed orchestrator epoch jump correlated with autoscaler preemptive job. Hypothesis: preempt triggers a fast rebind path that does not wait for pin consensus, allowing the edge to reassign to standby variant under certain timing windows.
Serving (Priya Nair) 2026-03-11: Found evidence of kv-cache TTL mismatches across serving instances. When preempt rebinds sessions to a new host, the new host's cache lacks the pinned metadata and request routing falls back to compatibility variant. Opening a PR to add pin->cache warmup handshake and stronger pin persistence during preempt operations. Related PR: GH-Redwood/serving#2679.
Customer (NimbusHealth - Alex Reed) 2026-03-11: Impact verified on our side — model outputs changed mid-session on critical test flows. We saw increased token counts when retries happened. Appreciate ETA and temporary mitigations.
SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-12: Implemented temporary mitigation: inhibit preemptive rebind for cohorts with active streaming sessions older than 60s while we validate the pin-warmup fix. This reduced oscillation in canary runs. Working with Serving team for permanent fix.
Hypothesis 1: Orchestrator performs epoch advancement and issues rebinds before edge/serving cache synchronization completes. Leads to missing pin metadata on new serving hosts.
Hypothesis 2: Aggressive preempt policy bypasses normal graceful drain path and invokes a fast-path that does not honor pin handshake. Evidence: logs show preemptive_rebalance vs graceful_drain timestamps overlapping with session activity.
Telemetry: Trace sampling shows 27% of route decisions during the window were handled by nodes with last_cache_sync > 30s, correlates with fallback events.
Reproducible: Yes, staging repro by running aggressive_preempt with long-lived streams. Failure mode appears timing-sensitive — adding artificial 50ms delay to rebind reduced incidence in tests.
Related artifacts: Dashboards: /dashboards/tenant-routing/us-east-1, Traces: /traces/tenant/nimbus-42/2026-03-10, PR: GH-Redwood/serving#2679 (pin-warmup), Runbook snippet: CONFLUENCE-RT/pin-fallback-handling.
Temporary mitigation applied: preempt inhibit for active streaming cohorts >60s and added extra cache-sync confirmation in the preempt workflow. Serving team merged pin-warmup handshake (GH-Redwood/serving#2679) to staging; rolling canary to production scheduled 2026-03-13 with a monitored gradual ramp. Post-deploy monitoring thresholds: <=1% fallback rate for pinned cohorts and no stream truncations. Follow-ups: add telemetry metric for pin_consensus_latency and update orchestration runbook with explicit preempt safety gates.
1) Roll out GH-Redwood/serving#2679 to canary pools on 2026-03-13 and monitor fallback_rate and stream_close_rate closely.
2) Instrument pin_consensus_latency metric and add alert when >200ms for any cohort in prod.
3) Update orchestration runbook to disallow preemptive rebinds for cohorts with active streaming sessions unless emergency flag set.
4) Postmortem doc planned and will be linked here after completion.
payload.summary: Tenant pin oscillation after quota-driven preemptive autoscale causes mixed-model routing
