Issue summary: After an IdP-side change, some OIDC id_tokens issued to AcroHealth's native clients no longer include the 'azp' (authorized party) claim. The private deployment token-exchange path expects either 'azp' or a client_id-present assertion; absence causes the token-exchange step to fail validation and results in 401/403 for long-lived service flows.

Impact: Intermittent 401/403 for batch ingestion workers and CI/CD pipelines using the token-exchange endpoint. Affects non-interactive service clients only (no interactive console sessions reported). Customer reports ~20% of job runs failing since 2026-03-11 08:00 UTC.

Environment: Private deployment (VPC), prod, us-east region. Auth-proxy v2026.02.18, token-exchange microservice v1.9.2. Customer uses a tenant-bound OIDC client (native/mobile) with a downstream confidential service that performs token exchange + role assertion.

Steps to reproduce:
  1) Use AcroHealth's native client to obtain id_token via standard OIDC flow.
  2) Call /internal/token-exchange with id_token, requesting service-client access.
  3) Observe exchange failure when id_token payload lacks 'azp'.

Observed behavior: token-exchange returns 400 validation error or 401 depending on code path. Downstream call receives 403 with X-Auth-Trace: token-exchange:missing-azp. Log snippets attached in comments.

Expected behavior: Token-exchange should accept id_tokens that are valid per issuer and use the aud/client_id claim to determine authorized party when 'azp' is not present, or fall back to tenant configuration.

Repro rate: ~20% of batch runs; 100% for id_tokens from the IdP variant that omitted azp.

Notes: This appears after IdP configuration change that toggled issuing 'azp' only for brokered clients. AcroHealth's native app now receives id_tokens without azp for a subset of users. Our validation path was recently tightened in auth-proxy PR#882 and enforces presence of azp for non-confidential flows, which breaks this IdP behavior.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:05 - Support (Amina): Thanks Maya — we've opened SUP-741820 and are triaging. Can you attach a redacted id_token for a failing flow and a successful one? Also confirm tenant and client IDs.
  Customer attached two tokens (redacted) and tenant id: acre-1973.
2026-03-12 13:40 - Eng (Diego): Reproduced locally with supplied id_token. Token payload missing 'azp' causes the auth-proxy validation to follow the 'confidential-only' branch and reject exchange. This is a regression introduced by auth-proxy PR 882 which made azp mandatory for non-interactive flows.
  PoC patch: fallback to aud[0] when azp missing and aud length == 1.
2026-03-13 08:15 - Support (Amina): Applied temporary config on customer's private VPC to relax azp enforcement (runtime flag) and asked customer to re-run jobs.
  Customer confirmed reduction in failures to 0% for the overnight window.

2026-03-14 15:05 - Customer (Maya): Thanks — confirmed jobs green for two full cycles. Requesting timeline for permanent fix and whether rollback is required if we re-enable strict azp enforcement later.
Summary: Auth-proxy validation was tightened in PR#882 to require azp for non-interactive token-exchange. AcroHealth's IdP started issuing id_tokens without azp for a subset of clients (brokered/native vs brokered/confidential behavior). The missing azp caused our service to treat the token as malformed for token-exchange, leading to 401/403.
Evidence: Repro with customer's redacted tokens; logs show 'token-exchange:missing-azp' and stack frames in token-exchange validator. No signature or exp/nbf issues. Canary telemetry shows 0.0x increased failures pre-patch.
Root cause: Regression in auth-proxy validation logic that did not implement a safe fallback to aud when azp is absent. IdP behavior change exposed this regression.
Risk assessment: Low to medium. Fix is a conservative fallback to aud when azp is absent and aud is unambiguous (single audience). We added telemetry to avoid silent acceptance in ambiguous cases.
Mitigation applied: runtime flag toggled to relax azp enforcement in customer's private cluster (temporary). Customer reports full recovery.
Planned permanent fix: merge PR#890 to auth-proxy which implements aud->azp fallback and adds an opt-in safety check for multi-aud tokens. Security review requested; target deploy to private-prod us-east on 2026-03-16 after +24h canary.
Rollback plan: If any security or impersonation regression is observed, revert runtime flag and apply stricter config with a customer-specific exception while we iterate.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring 429 responses across mixed batch-embedding ingestion and low-latency chat streams. Pattern appears after a scheduled clock skew correction in the customer environment (they run cluster time sync every night). The 429s start ~30s after the time correction and persist for several minutes in bursts.

Impact:
- Customer ingestion pipeline (bulk embeddings) sees ~10% of requests rejected with 429s for 3-8 minutes during the window.
- Interactive chat to support agents experiences sporadic short-lived 429s causing degraded UX.

Environment:
- NovaHealth production (enterprise plan) in us-west region
- Traffic mix: background batched embedding workers (50 qps bursts) + interactive websocket streams (20 concurrent)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Ensure server nodes run ntp-sync job (simulate a 5s forward time jump).
2) Start a bulk-embed job with 100 concurrent short requests and a few persistent websocket chat sessions.
3) Observe 429s appearing roughly 20-40 seconds after the clock adjustment.

Observed behavior:
- 429s include X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and Retry-After headers of small values (3-10s), but retries still result in 429s until the spike clears.
- Console shows token buckets refilling less predictably; tenant-level counters appear to be out of sync briefly.

Expected behavior:
- Rate limiter should be robust to small clock adjustments; refill math shouldn't cause a token deficit across mixed connection types.

Attachments:
- Customer logs (session IDs provided) and a pcap of one websocket session uploaded to the ticket.

Additional notes:
2026-02-20 - NovaHealth (customer): Provided offsets: two nodes jumped +4s and +6s respectively. Uploaded request traces and sample bulk job id 'embed-20260220-81a'.
2026-02-21 - Support (Sana Patel): Requested a temporary mitigation: recommend staggering the customer's ntp job or configuring a short exponential backoff on retries while we investigate.
Pulled rate-limiter metrics for tenant NovaHealth between 02:00-02:10 UTC on 2026-02-20. Observed sawtooth drops in token count coinciding with ntp sync at 02:03:12 UTC.
Token refill is implemented with an epoch-aligned refill tick (1s granularity). A forward clock jump causes the refill loop to compute a larger-than-expected delta and then cap it, but internal accounting path for websocket-anchored sessions uses last-seen-timestamp which briefly lags, leading to double-debiting of pending requests.
Found one race: pre-counting logic for multipart bulk uploads increments an in-flight counter, then the refill path subtracts tokens based on elapsed time. If elapsed time jumps forward, accounting runs a fast-path that resets refill timers but doesn't reconcile the in-flight counter until after the request processing completes — leading to momentary negative effective quota.
Reproduced locally by forcing process clock jump in an integration harness. Confirmed 429s appear for mixed websocket + REST burst traffic when refill tick and websocket last-seen timestamps diverge.
Related systems: edge-proxy keeps per-connection state; if connections experience different system times (e.g., different hosts in a pooled IP set), aggregated tenant accounting can be skewed.
Metrics examined: tenant_token_balance, refill_tick_latency, per-route_inflight_count. Refill_tick_latency spiked during time jump.
Mitigation provided (2026-02-21): Recommended short-term customer workarounds: 1) Stagger NTP sync across hosts so not all nodes jump simultaneously; 2) Enable client-side jittered retry/backoff for bulk workers (recommended policy: initial_retry=250ms, backoff=1.5x, max=8s); 3) Temporarily isolate high-throughput batch worker keys into their own route to avoid competing with low-latency websockets.
Engineering fix (tracked): Implement a reconciliation pass in the rate-limiter to clamp negative effective balances when a forward clock jump is detected and to reconcile per-connection last-seen timestamps with tenant-level refill timestamps on the next refill tick. Patch proposed in PR #2241 and integration tests added to cover clock shifts.
Rollout notes: Patch will be staged to canary on 2026-02-24, monitored for refill_tick_latency regressions. If stable, promote to us-west prod by 2026-02-26 during a low-traffic window.
Postmortem follow-up: Add runbook guidance about scheduled time-syncs for enterprise customers and a console warning when refill_latency exceeds 500ms.
Confirm with NovaHealth after canary that 429s no longer correlate with nightly ntp job.
Add e2e scenario to customer onboarding docs explaining how to test for quota stability during node time resyncs.
Evaluate long-term: consider shifting refill to monotonic-clock based deltas to avoid wall-clock anomalies.

Issue summary:
Customers using the batch rerank endpoint observe misordered top-k results and periodic 429 rate-limit responses when reranking large batches (>128). The root cause appears tied to an embedding payload schema transpose that changes how the KV-cache key is computed for multi-item batches, causing stale cache hits and an internal throttling cascade.

Impact:
- LexiSearch (enterprise) reported production impact: rerank quality degradation (top-5 order flips) for ~12% of queries after a deploy on 2026-03-07 and intermittent 429s during peak traffic windows (09:00-11:00 UTC).
- Affects all customers using embedder-v2-512 in batch rerank mode; higher batch sizes increase probability.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod) us-east-1
- API: POST /v1/rerank/batch
- Embedding model: embedder-v2-512 (512-dim float32)
- Reranker: reranker-lite-1.3 pinned by customer

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Create a batch of 150 candidate documents and a single query, request embeddings with header X-Embed-Version: 2 and pass to POST /v1/rerank/batch with batch_size=150.
2) Observe rerank top-5 ordering differs vs. local baseline computed with same embeddings.
3) At higher concurrent load (10 qps), API begins returning 429s for rerank requests.

Observed behavior:
- Top-k order inconsistent: many documents receive an out-of-order boost (positions shift by +3 to +10).
- 429 responses from rerank endpoint showing "cache-key-mismatch" in logs and upstream 429s cascading from internal rate limiter.
- Traces show KV-cache get operations returning payloads with an unexpected tensor layout (transpose of last two axes) and cache hit ratio spikes coincident with quality shifts.

Expected behavior:
- Rerank should preserve deterministic ordering given identical embeddings and reranker weights. 429s should only occur when per-tenant quotas are exceeded; cache hits should not cause order changes.

Logs / Traces (excerpts):
- rerank-service ERROR 2026-03-07T10:12:02Z request_id=abc123 "cached-embed-layout=transposed; expected=standard"
- kv-cache INFO 2026-03-07T10:12:02Z key=tenant-lexi:embed:sha256:fd3a... hit=true layout=NHW->NWH
- api-gateway WARN 2026-03-07T10:12:03Z throttle=triggered reason="internal-backpressure"

Attachments provided by customer:
- raw request/response payloads (sanitized)
- local embedding dump used for baseline comparisons

Notes:
- Customer says issue started immediately after a platform rollout that included an embeddings-service change (PR referenced below).
- LexiSearch currently pinned to reranker-lite-1.3 and cannot accept quality variance.


Additional notes:
2026-03-08 11:40 - LexiSearch (support contact - Maria Gomez): Uploaded sanitized batch payloads and local rerank baseline. Confirmed issue replicates with our workload when batch_size > 128.
Hypothesis 1: Serialization change in embedder-v2-512 quant path permutes axes for certain batch sizes, producing a different memory layout encoding and thus different similarity scores when decoded in rerank pipeline.
Hypothesis 2: Cache key was computed without stable-layout fingerprint, so transposed payloads produce identical keys after lossy quantization for some batches causing stale hits with wrong layout metadata.
Reproduction: Local micro-bench used same embedding binary and reranker; created batches of size 150 and observed permuted embedding vectors when using new quant path. Reverting to previous serialization produced matching local vs platform results.
Metrics observed: after deploy, cache hit ratio increased by ~18% but quality (NDCG@5) decreased by ~12% for affected tenants. 429 rate increased due to internal backpressure from cache-miss storms after stale hits were invalidated.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings-service/pull/1898 (serialization refactor).
Related runbook snippets: see Confluence page 'Embedding Schema Standards' about stable on-disk layout and cache fingerprinting.
Workaround applied: tenant-specific cache-bypass toggle enabled for LexiSearch which eliminated the immediate 429 cascade. Engineering reverted the problematic serialization change and landed a canary rollback in us-east-1 on 2026-03-12; global rollback scheduled and cache flush planned 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.

Follow-ups (open):
- INT-452: add unit + integration tests for serialization invariants and add a layout fingerprint to cache key computation (assigned to Priya Nair).
- INT-453: improve observability: emit embedding-layout header in cache traces (assigned to Diego Morales).
- Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-16.

Status: In Progress — customer mitigation in place; global rollback pending and final validation after cache flush required before closing ticket.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports non-deterministic reranking results and occasional 504 timeouts when submitting batched embed+rerank requests from their dedicated cluster. Behavior started after they enabled 'auto-batch' on their SDK client and upgraded to open-embedder-v2-768 earlier this week.

Impact:
- DocuSearch Labs: search relevance fluctuates between requests (top results reorder unpredictably).
- Intermittent 504s observed on rerank endpoint (~1-2% of requests during peak).
- User-facing SLA degradation; customer flagged as P1.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment in us-east, serving runtime 1.18.2, batching-service 0.9.7.
- Client: docusearch-sdk v2.3.1 with auto-batch enabled.
- Model combo: embeddings (open-embedder-v2-768) followed by server-side reranker (reranker-tiny-v1) pipeline.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From customer's traffic pattern: issue appears when many concurrent sessions call /v1/embeddings in multi-item batches (sizes 8-32) followed by immediate /v1/rerank calls using the returned vectors.
2) Reproduce locally using sample harness (provided below) by enabling interleaved multi-tenant batching and replaying their header patterns.
3) Observe rerank score variance across repeated identical traces and sporadic 504s from reranker instances.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Rerank scores for identical inputs vary across calls (score deltas up to 0.12 in top-k).
- Request traces show embedding batches being interleaved incorrectly: request A's embeddings appear to be partially inserted into request B's batch metadata when forwarded to reranker.
- Reranker service sometimes returns long queue times and ultimately 504s for affected requests.

Initial hypothesis:
- Batching-service interleaves per-request vector buffers under high concurrency due to a race in buffer offset calculation after the SDK switched to a 'coalesced' prefix optimization.
- Partial corruption of per-request metadata leads to downstream reranker mixing vectors between requests, causing quality drift and timeouts when validation fails and the request is retried.

Requested customer action:
- Temporarily disable client-side auto-batch and set batch_size=1 to mitigate while we investigate.
- Provide a small redacted trace (request IDs) for two consecutive failing flows (we requested 3 trace IDs).
Checked batching-service logs for request IDs provided by customer; found overlapping memory offsets for concurrent batch assemblies at 15:14:32-15:16:18 UTC.
Heap and buffer metrics show increased live buffer reuse under high-concurrency; GC cycles correlated with timing of observed interleaving.
Added additional logging to record batch assembly start/end and per-request checksum — reproduces locally under synthetic load.
Hypothesis validated: off-by-one in the coalesced prefix length calculation causes offset drift when small padding occurs; race condition under multi-threaded assembler.
trace_id=docu-20260312-01514 req=embed batch_id=ba-7789 offset_start=0 offset_end=6144
trace_id=docu-20260312-01515 req=embed batch_id=ba-7790 offset_start=6000 offset_end=12144  <-- overlap detected
reranker-instance-7: queue_wait_ms=1823 process_ms=47 status=504 trace_id=docu-20260312-01515
stack sample (batching-service): batch_forward() at assembler.cpp:278, assemble_coalesced_prefix() at assembler.cpp:189
Workaround (customer action): Disable client auto-batch or set batch_size=1. Customer confirmed stabilization after this change.
Planned fix: PR 2243 implements atomic buffer allocation and an optional per-batch checksum validation; will be rolled out to canary on 2026-03-14 and to prod (dedicated) after successful canary gating.
Follow-ups: Add a regression unit test for coalesced prefix scenarios and integration test with multi-tenant interleaved load. Add an alert for 'batch_overlap_detected' metric.

2026-03-12 17:30 - DocuSearch Labs (Customer) - Elena Morozova: We rolled batch_size down to 1 and saw immediate stabilization; quality now consistent. Can you confirm what changed and when a permanent fix will be available?

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicated external tool/webhook invocations when their orchestration client retries after transient network errors. The pattern occurs intermittently during high sustained traffic and correlates with HTTP/2 connection migration on the edge proxy.

Impact:
- Multiple duplicate tool executions observed (pay-per-execution downstream cost).
- Customer-facing task orchestration experiences duplicate side-effects (duplicate invoices, double-posted messages).
- Affects multiple SDK languages (Python and TypeScript) in their mixed orchestration stack.

Environment:
- Customer running Redwood Dedicated in prod us-west with reserved capacity.
- SDKs: python-sdk v1.4.2, ts-sdk v2.0.1.
- Edge proxy: internal sidecar (we host) performing auth/token translation and HTTP/2 connection pooling.

Steps to reproduce (as provided):
1) Start orchestration: client opens long-running streaming session to our streaming endpoints from both Python and TS workers.
2) Client triggers model function calling that invokes downstream tool webhooks (POST to customer backend).
3) Simulate transient network interruption (brief TCP reset / container restart on client's side).
4) SDKs reconnect; requests get routed via a different HTTP/2 connection and are multiplexed through the edge sidecar.
5) Observe duplicate webhook/tool calls for the same logical operation ID within ~10s window.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should be deduplicated by idempotency key scope (per-request). A reconnection should not cause a second tool invocation if the original request may have been accepted by the serving runtime.

Actual behavior:
- Edge sidecar rewrites the idempotency header (X-Redwood-Idempotency) from the request header into an auth token blob in the request body for certain connection migration paths. When the header is rewritten into the body, our request routing treats it as missing for connection-scoped dedupe, and the retry is processed as a fresh request, causing duplicate tool invocations.

Logs / Observables:
- Customer-provided snippet from Python worker (timestamps redacted):
  - Sent: POST /v1/streams (X-Redwood-Idempotency: sess-abc-123)
- Edge proxy log: conn_migrate: 0x7f12 -> 0x8a9b, header_promoted_to_body=true, idempotency_header_removed=true
- Serving-runtime trace: request_id=rr-90012, idempotency_key=(none) -> processed as new
- Downstream webhook receipts show two POSTs for the same operation_id within 4s
- Reproduced in internal staging by toggling connection pooling behavior on edge-proxy; when header promotion is enabled the serving runtime no longer sees X-Redwood-Idempotency.
- Python SDK and TS SDK set idempotency header correctly; the mutation occurs inside our sidecar before forwarding.
- Root cause appears to be an optimization in the edge-proxy that compresses headers into an auth blob for long-lived multiplexed h2 streams; it was intended to reduce header overhead but unintentionally changes idempotency scope detection.
- Race window: when a retry originates over a different h2 stream that the proxy promotes header->body, the server's dedupe table misses the original key because lookup expects header-scoped key.
- Cross-language note: Some SDK variants include the idempotency token in both header and initial metadata frame; others only send header. Behavior is exacerbated in mixed-language setups where one client sends header-only and the other sends header+meta.

Temporary mitigation attempted:
- Asked customer to enable client-side explicit ack confirmation flow (returning a tool_confirmation token in response) — reduced duplicates but requires app changes.
- Disabled header promotion on the edge-proxy for a subset of flows; duplication stopped for those tests.

Open questions:
- Should idempotency be canonicalized to accept keys from both header and body?
- Do we need to change SDKs to include idempotency token in both header and initial metadata frame for streaming?
Customer reports ~0.6% of tool invocations duplicated during peak; financially material for downstream paid webhooks. Business logic duplicates (double-charges) require customer remediation and manual refunds.
Support (Aisha): Initial triage - customer reports duplicate webhooks; asked for recent request IDs, timestamps, and SDK versions.
Customer (Spellbound AI): Provided request IDs rr-90012 and rr-90046 plus edge-proxy logs and a small repro script that toggles connection pooling.
Eng (Marco): Reproduced locally by enabling header_promote flag on edge simulator; confirmed serving-runtime sees no idempotency header after rewrite.
Support (Aisha): Noted workaround to disable header promotion at edge; customer confirmed reduced duplicates in canary traffic (10k requests).
Eng (Marco): Created PR to change server dedupe to also read canonical idempotency keys from the auth blob (linked in related_github_prs).
Customer (Spellbound AI): Requests guidance for long-term fix and asks whether SDK updates are required on their side.
Workaround applied: disabled header promotion for streaming endpoints in us-west for this customer. Permanent fix plan: update serving-runtime to extract idempotency keys from both headers and promoted auth blobs, and update edge-proxy to avoid in-place header removal for dedupe-sensitive headers.

Rollout notes:
- Hotfix: patched edge-proxy config for affected pool (completed 2026-03-11 04:12 UTC).
- Medium-term: server change in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/412 to accept idempotency token from auth blob; will be canaried in staging, then deployed to prod in controlled rollout (expected 2026-03-18).

Follow-up items:
- Update SDK docs recommending inclusion of idempotency token in both header and initial metadata for streaming use-cases.
- Add automated test in CI to ensure edge-proxy header promotion does not strip dedupe headers.
- Postmortem capturing root cause and contributor mitigations scheduled once rollout completes.
payload.summary: Edge sidecar rewrites idempotency header into auth body during h2 connection migration, causing duplicate tool calls across SDKs

Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a mid-week deploy they started seeing re-ranked results that diverge from expected relevance and a 95th percentile latency spike on rerank calls. The problem appears correlated with bulk ingestion jobs that compute embeddings and subsequent rerank requests. Impact:
- Relevance drift: top-5 results reordered for ~8% of queries compared to baseline, causing product UX regression for Cordelia Health dashboards.
- Latency: rerank p95 increased from ~180ms to ~1.6s during ingestion windows.
Environment:
- Dedicated tenant: cordelia-prod (dedicated pool, us-east).
- Reranker service pinned to reranker-bert-qa:v2026-03-04.
- Embedding jobs using embedder-sim-v2 via our embeddings API.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Run batch ingestion of ~12k documents using embeddings endpoint with client SDK default settings (no explicit normalization).
2) Immediately issue rerank requests against the freshly indexed items.
3) Observe rerank ordering vs baseline and measure p95 latency on rerank endpoint.
Logs / sample traces:
- Trace IDs: trace-20260310-8f1a, trace-20260310-8f2b.
- Rerank service logs show frequent fallback to variant "reranker-bert-qa-cpu-quant" for ~22% of requests during ingestion window.
- Example latency sample: 2026-03-10T14:23:12Z rerank request id=abc123 p95=1610ms, model_variant=cpu-quant, queue_wait=1200ms.
Trigger large embedding bulk ingest (~10-15k docs) using client SDK default settings
Immediately run standard rerank queries against the new index
Compare top-K ordering with a known-good baseline and capture rerank p95
Rerank service log excerpt:
[2026-03-10T14:23:11Z] INFO rerank-handler request=abc123 routing=pool-dedicated decision=fallthrough_to_cpu_variant reason=capacity_threshold queue_wait_ms=1187
[2026-03-10T14:23:12Z] WARN reranker-bert-qa-cpu-quant score_distribution_shift=0.23 topk_mismatch=0.08
Embedding ingestion job:
[2026-03-10T14:20:05Z] INFO embed-job batch=ingest-987 compute_ms_per_doc=17 normalization_flag=off
Initial hypothesis: embedding vectors generated during bulk ingest were not L2-normalized; downstream reranker index expects normalized vectors -> score scaling leads to reordered topk.
Observed that ~22% of rerank requests were routed to a CPU-quantized variant because the GPU pool hit autoscale/burst thresholds during ingest; CPU variant uses a slightly different input preprocessing pipeline which lacks server-side normalization (introduced in earlier opt-in change).
Correlated client SDK usage: Cordelia's ingestion pipeline used an older SDK (v0.9.2) which omitted the new 'normalize' parameter default introduced in v1.1.0.
Confirmed through sample vectors: mean L2 norm for vectors produced in ingest window = 3.8 (unnormalized) vs baseline = 1.0 (normalized). Cosine-based scores diverge when magnitude varies; retrieval index search combined raw dot-product scoring then normalized by precomputed lengths in some paths but not all, causing inconsistency.

Additional notes:
SRE (Marta Rivera): Noted autoscale events in prod-us-east at 14:18-14:30; several pods terminated/restarted due to memory pressure during ingest.
Support (Asha Patel): Temporary mitigation suggested: re-run embedding step with explicit 'normalize=true' or pin rerank route to GPU pool until ingestion completes.
Workaround applied and permanent fix outlined:
Short term: Advised Cordelia to re-ingest affected batches using SDK v1.1.0 with explicit normalize=true. Support added a routing override for their tenant to prioritize GPU variants while they reprocessed data. This immediately resolved p95 latency back to ~210ms and restored top-k ordering to expected baseline.
Long term: Deployed hotfix to rerank service to perform server-side L2 normalization for incoming vectors when model variants differ in preprocessing (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/3210). Updated autoscaling policy to add headroom during large ingests.
Follow-ups: 1) Add telemetry metric for embedding L2 norm distribution per ingest job. 2) Update SDK and docs to highlight 'normalize' flag and bump default in next release. 3) Postmortem to be published and linked from support ticket.
Status: Resolved and verified with customer on 2026-03-12.

Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a scheduled HSM wrapping-key rotation in their private deployment, SAML SSO logins begin failing with 403 Authorization errors when the platform attempts to decrypt encrypted SAML assertions. The failures started immediately after rotation and affect both web console access and token-exchange flows for service accounts.

Impact:
- A subset (~8%) of PaperTrail Analytics' users receive 403s on SSO login attempts.
- Automated jobs using token-exchange via the private admin API fail to authenticate, causing downstream job failures and data ingestion delays.
- Customer is on a Private deployment with customer-managed HSM; they report an urgent business impact.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) deployed in prod-us-west (us-west-2).
- IDP: On-prem ADFS (SAML 2.0), assertions encrypted using AES-GCM with RSA-OAEP key transport.
- Customer HSM: Thales Luna (v11), wrapping-key rotation completed on 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC.
- Identity service version: 4.8.1-rc2 on private control plane.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Trigger SSO login to Redwood Console via PaperTrail SAML IdP.
2) Platform receives encrypted assertion and attempts to decrypt via HSM unwrap + local decryption flow.
3) Identity service returns 403 Authorization for affected user.

Observed behavior:
- Logs show decryption failures at the unwrap step: "failed to unwrap key: invalid padding" for some assertions and "unsupported content encryption" for others.
- Only assertions encrypted with AES-GCM are failing; AES-CBC assertions succeed.
- Failures correlate tightly with timestamps immediately after the HSM wrapping-key rotation.
- Customer's HSM audit logs show successful unwrap operations for server-side keys, but the key ID used by the platform sometimes points to the pre-rotation wrapping-key in our config cache.

Expected behavior:
- After wrapping-key rotation, the platform should either use the new wrapping-key for unwrap operations or fall back gracefully to a compatible unwrap method for legacy assertions. No 403s should be surfaced to end users.

Logs / snippets (redacted):
- identity-service[auth]: ERROR [2026-03-10T02:23:11Z] decrypt_assertion: unwrap failed: RSA_OAEP_decrypt: invalid padding
- identity-service[kms]: WARN  [2026-03-10T02:23:12Z] hsm-unwrapper: key-cache-miss: fetching current wrapping-key id=wk-20260228
- hsm-audit: SUCCESS [2026-03-10T02:23:12Z] UnwrapOperation user=redwood-identity opId=unw-7b2e

Mitigation / Workaround attempted by customer:
- Customer rolled back the HSM wrapping-key to previous key; failures temporarily subsided for a minority of users, but then reappeared intermittently.
- Customer toggled assertion encryption algorithm to AES-CBC (temporary), which reduced failures but is not acceptable long-term.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Key cache staleness in private control plane leads to attempts to unwrap with the wrong key id after rotation. Evidence: platform logs show key-cache-miss and immediate use of stale id.
- Hypothesis 2: Our AES-GCM decryption path in identity-service has a regression when fed an unwrapped content-encryption-key (CEK) that was wrapped under RSA-OAEP with newer key metadata (OAEP params mismatch).
- Collected traces from identity-service and HSM: unwrap success reported by HSM, but decrypt fails with "unsupported content encryption" for AES-GCM vectors — suggests CEK bytes or metadata mutated during round-trip or incorrect CEK length expectation.
- Correlated with PR (see related_github_prs) that updated HSM client library to v2.14. The update includes an internal change to ASN.1 parsing of OAEP padding info.

Action items taken so far:
- Support added request-scoped debug logging for identity-service unwrap/decrypt flows and pushed to the customer's private control plane (build 4.8.1-rc2+dbg).
- Eng (Samir) requested HSM vendor support ticket for full unwrap trace and raw CEK bytes (redacted) — ticket #HSM-PT-221.
- Temporarily disabled the new HSM client lib (v2.14) and rolled back to v2.12 on a test node: AES-GCM decrypts succeeded for previously failing assertions in test.

Next steps / Proposed fix:
1) Validate the ASN.1/OAEP parsing change in v2.14 is the root cause by running end-to-end decrypts with test vectors using both client lib versions.
2) If confirmed, either revert the HSM client lib or patch it to preserve OAEP param behavior for RSA-OAEP wrapping in our code path.
3) Add defensive logic to identity-service: if unwrap succeeds but CEK decrypt fails with AES-GCM, attempt a compatibility code-path (safe fallback) and emit an operator alert rather than immediate 403 to user.
4) Improve wrapping-key rotation hooks to invalidate key metadata cache across control plane nodes atomically to avoid short windows of stale key-id lookups.

Resolution notes (partial):
- Temporary mitigation: rolled back HSM client to v2.12 in customer staging; successful.
- Long-term: engineering to prepare patch for v2.14 compatibility and key-cache invalidation improvement. Plan target: patch release 4.8.2 by 2026-03-19.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:10 UTC - PaperTrail SRE (customer): We performed a rollback of the wrapping-key; saw partial recovery but inconsistent. HSM vendor opened ticket HSM-PT-221 and confirms unwrap logs match our calls.
Temporary mitigation applied: rolled HSM client to v2.12 in staging and prepared patch for control plane. Full patch to be included in 4.8.2. Added key-cache invalidation enhancements to rollout plan. Customer scheduled maintenance for patch application 2026-03-18.
payload.summary: Encrypted SAML assertion decryption fails after HSM wrapping-key rotation causing 403s for private customers

Issue summary:
Customer BrightSearch reports that scheduled alert notifications no longer include links that open the associated trace context from the Console. Instead the alert payload displays a placeholder and the trace link on the dashboard is broken.

Impact:
- Several scheduled alerts fired on 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-10 without trace links; SRE/eng on-call could not quickly jump to traces to investigate regressions.
- Customer says this blocked two incident investigations and increased MTTR.

Environment:
prod-us-east, BrightSearch org id: 987654321, customer on Dedicated plan with route pinning.

Steps to reproduce (observed locally with a BrightSearch test org):
1) Create a saved query panel that includes the tracehook header in response metadata (x-redwood-trace: <trace-id>).
2) Create a scheduled alert using that panel with an evaluation window of 5m and alert action set to send Console notification.
3) Wait for scheduled evaluation (or trigger manually via /alerts/eval endpoint using org header).
4) Inspect alert payload in Console -> Alerts and the link target on the dashboard.

Observed behavior:
- Alert payload shows "trace_link": "<missing>" and clicking "View trace" results in a 404 from the trace service.
- Query logs show join on organization column "org_id" returned empty for rows created after the metadata migration.

Expected behavior:
- Alert payload contains a working deep-link to the trace view for the matched event.
- Dashboard drilldown opens trace context in a new tab.

Notes:
- Customer confirmed they ran the org attribute rename tool last week as part of a metadata cleanup (internal migration from org_id -> org_uuid). They used the runbook but did not run the alert reindex step because it was optional per the runbook.
- This issue appears to affect scheduled alert evaluations and scheduled report exports; ad-hoc realtime queries from Explore still surface traces correctly.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:20 - BrightSearch (Customer - Priya Menon): We can provide a list of affected alert IDs and confirm that manual ad-hoc alerts still show traces. We prefer a hotfix because these are critical incident alerts.
2026-03-12 09:10 - QA (Lena Novak): Added regression test to CI to validate scheduled-alert trace linking during org attribute migration scenarios.
Timeline: After customer's org attribute rename (org_id -> org_uuid) some downstream services continued to reference org_id. We inspected alert-eval templates and saw a hard-coded WHERE x.org_id = :org_id. The saved panel stores tracehook headers referencing trace ids, but the alert-eval subquery that joins traces uses the old column and therefore returned no rows for events written with org_uuid. Reproduced locally by toggling the org mapping flag. A staging PR existed but had not been promoted to prod. We evaluated risk of immediate template change and decided to deploy a translation shim and run a reindex of alert bindings as the least disruptive mitigation.
Mitigation applied: emergency translation middleware added to alert-eval service to map org_uuid -> org_id for the duration of migration. Backfill reindexed 1,824 alert bindings for BrightSearch and two other orgs that ran the migration early. Patch PR (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2890) contains permanent fix: update SQL templates to use canonical org_uuid and include a migration verifier check during deploy. Customer notified; confirmed working for scheduled alerts after 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC. Follow-ups: INT-4021 tracks adding a migration checklist step to reindex alerts and a post-migration verification job. QA added a regression test to CI.
Missed trace links in scheduled alert notifications for BrightSearch's production org; two incident investigations delayed (MTTR increased). Only scheduled alert flows affected; ad-hoc Explore queries unaffected.
INT-4021: Permanent fix and deploy to prod
Add reindex step to org migration runbook
Add CI regression test for scheduled-alert->trace linking
Notify customers with recent org metadata changes about reindex requirement
payload.summary: Scheduled alerts lose trace context links after org attribute migration

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer EduScale reports intermittent mixed responses from two model variants after they pinned sessions to gpt-small-1.1 for a gradual canary. The problem started after an automated health-probe spike from an autoscaler event; session-level anchors appeared to oscillate between primary and fallback variants.

Impact:
- Affected ~12% of requests from the customer’s production tenant in us-west for approximately 18 minutes.
- Some chat sessions received tokens generated by the fallback variant (quantized) while the tenant believed sessions were pinned to the non-quantized model.
- Customer reports visible quality regressions for short-lived conversational flows.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod (us-west)
- Tenant: eduscale-prod-1 (dedicated pool)
- Routing policy: tenant-pinned -> canary-weighted (10%) -> fallback path to gpt-small-1.1-quant when capacity constrained

Steps to reproduce (observed locally by ops):
1) Trigger a short synthetic traffic spike (200 rps sustained for 30s) against tenant route with a pinned session cookie.
2) Simulate an autoscaler health-probe spike that induced controller probe retries around the same time.
3) Observe edge-proxy logs showing repeated pin reevaluation for the same session token and alternating route decisions.

Observed behavior:
- Pin handshake succeeded initially, then repeated health probes caused coordinator to mark a subset of nodes as degraded.
- Edge-proxy retry logic re-evaluated pins and sometimes selected the fallback (quantized) variant for new requests within the same session ID.
- No 5xx errors surfaced; responses completed but from unexpected variant.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant-level pin should remain anchored until explicit unpin or TTL expiry. Health-probe jitter should not cause mid-session variant switches.

Attachments:
- Edge logs (truncated) and coordinator metrics attached to ticket (log IDs: edg-logs-1132, coord-metrics-1132).
2026-03-13 09:18 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer opened with message: 'We see sudden quality drops in prod, some sessions sent responses from a different model even though we pinned to the stable variant. Happening intermittently around 09:00 PST.'
2026-03-13 09:24 - SRE (Marco Rivera): Acknowledged. I'm pulling coordinator and edge-proxy traces for the tenant and will validate pin TTLs and decision logs. Marking as P1/Sev1 since it's customer-visible in prod.
2026-03-13 10:02 - SRE (Marco Rivera): Initial findings: coordinator issued a transient degraded mark for two GPUs due to flapping health checks during autoscaler probe. Edge-proxy retry path contains a fast fallback path that re-queries model routing when coordinator returns partial health. Attaching snippets: coordinator decision IDs show alternating 'ANCHOR_OK' and then 'ANCHOR_STALE' for same session token.
2026-03-13 11:10 - Support (Aisha Patel) -> Customer: Please confirm whether you observed any client-side session token rotation during the window (we suspect not based on logs).
2026-03-13 11:35 - Customer (EduScale Support Rep - Daniel Kim): We did not rotate session tokens. We see the same session_id values. Impacted customers reported a notable difference when QA grader compared outputs.
2026-03-14 08:05 - Engineering (Priya Nair): Confirmed a race between health-probe debounce and the pin-lease refresh path. The debounce allowed coordinator to emit a degraded state for short windows; the pin reconciliation logic treated that as a candidate to re-resolve routing, which then picked fallback variants under our current prioritization rules.
2026-03-14 12:30 - SRE (Marco Rivera): Implemented temporary mitigation: extended pin-lease grace window (edge-side) for the tenant to 60s and disabled aggressive edge re-resolve for degraded->healthy transitions. Observing reduction in oscillations in monitoring. Awaiting customer validation.
Hypothesis: health-probe jitter + coordinator debounce window triggers re-evaluation of pinned sessions leading to edge fallback selection.
Logs show coordinator flagged two GPUs as degraded at 08:58:03 UTC, recovered at 08:58:26 UTC. During this 23s window > 200 requests tied to pinned sessions hit routing re-resolve path.
Edge-proxy's re-resolve path currently treats 'stale anchor' as eligible for fallback selection; this logic is by-design for availability but interacts poorly with tenant-level explicit pins.
Related config: pin-lease-ttl=300s, pin-grace-window-edge=10s (default). Increasing to 60s reduces occurrences in canary testbed.
No evidence of client token rotation or cookie corruption. CDN layer had no errors; all responses were 200 from either variant.
Potential race with autoscaler probe schedule aligning with canary traffic bursts; creating follow-up runbook step to avoid probe alignment with high canary weight windows.
Workaround applied: edge pin-grace-window temporarily increased to 60s for eduscale-prod-1 and aggressive re-resolve on degrade->healthy transitions disabled for 2 hours. Monitoring shows oscillation count dropped by ~88% after mitigation.

Permanent fix plan (tracking):
- Change routing reconciler so explicit tenant pins take precedence over short-lived degraded flags (< 30s) unless pin-ttl expired (PR in progress: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7890).
- Add coordinator metric and alert for 'pin-reconcile-retries' and expose to Console for tenant owners.
- Update canary runbook to include staggered health-probe windows during tenant-pinned gradual rollouts.

Follow-ups assigned to Engineering (Priya Nair) and SRE (Marco Rivera). ETA for code change and canary: 2026-03-20. Customer notified and asked to re-open if further regressions are observed.
ENG-TRACK: update routing reconciler to prefer explicit pins over transient degraded flags (< 30s) - assignee: Priya Nair - ETA: 2026-03-20
SRE-TRACK: create coordinator alert 'pin-reconcile-retries' and dashboard tile in Console - assignee: Marco Rivera - ETA: 2026-03-18
DOCS-TRACK: add runbook step to avoid autoscaler probe alignment during gradual canary rollouts - assignee: DevEx (Sam Cho) - ETA: 2026-03-22

Issue summary:
Customer (Northbridge Financial) is onboarding Redwood audit feed into Google Chronicle. They require cryptographically signed delivery receipts for each batch, strict per-tenant ordering guarantees with a resume token, and a sample field mapping tailored to Chronicle's schema (including explicit timezone normalization rules). Customer also requests an SFTP fallback for manifest delivery and proof of non-repudiation for legal retention.

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete SIEM ingestion and mapping validation.
- Potential delay to security/incident response integrations.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted audit export, production tenant: northbridge-001, expected throughput ~300-800 events/sec during business hours, events include API calls, auth events, and model invocation metadata.

Request:
1) Provide a sample batch (JSONL) with per-record and per-batch headers showing canonicalized timestamp (UTC ISO8601), tenant_id, event_uuid, sequence_number, and optional resume_token.
2) Demonstrate ed25519-signed per-batch manifest and HMAC-SHA256 per-record envelope example.
3) Provide mapping table to Chronicle fields and an example ingestion snippet.
4) Confirm ordering guarantees and behavior under retry/duplicate deliveries.
5) Outline SFTP fallback manifest rotation and verification procedure.
1) Customer configured Redwood audit export to deliver to Chronicle pull endpoint.
2) Customer attempted to validate incoming batches; discovered no signature header and inconsistent timezone presentation.
3) Customer attempted partial replays and found out-of-order sequence numbers when retries occurred.
4) Customer opened this ticket requesting signed-manifest and sequence/resume semantics clarity.
Customer provided sample failed batch (attached in ticket): batch_20260309_14.jsonl (showed local timezone offsets, missing 'signature' header, and duplicate event_uuid entries after retry).
Redwood delivery logs: delivery_id=del-9a7f3b, attempts=3, last_status=200 from Chronicle with no signature-ack.
S3 manifest generator logs: manifest-gen v1.3.2 emitted 'unsigned' flag for the batch due to missing KEK binding for tenant northbridge-001.
2026-03-10 09:15 - Support triage: validated attachments and confirmed missing signature header in delivered batches.
2026-03-10 11:02 - Eng (SRE) checked manifest-generator: found fallback path that emits unsigned manifests when tenant KMS key not bound. Hypothesis: tenant key binding not completed for northbridge-001.
2026-03-10 14:30 - Security reviewed proposed ed25519 signing approach; approved if key rotation and attestation are logged to audit chain.
2026-03-11 08:20 - Determined out-of-order sequence occurs when a failed upload is retried and batch-level sequence_number is regenerated. Need deterministic resume_token per upload attempt to allow Chronicle to dedupe/restore ordering.
2026-03-11 10:05 - Created GH PR to add deterministic resume_token (sha256 of tenant+batch_timestamp+nonce) and switch manifest-gen to sign with tenant-specific ed25519 key when KMS binding present (PR #4982).
2026-03-12 09:00 - Performed internal test delivering signed manifest to Chronicle dev account; Chronicle accepted and returned signature-ack header; ordering preserved when resume_token included.
Aisha Khan (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer request attached, asked for immediate sample and mapping. SLA P1 first response due 2026-03-11.
Marco Villanueva (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged, raised to infra and security for sign-off. Asking customer for tenant KMS thumbprint and preferred signature scheme (ed25519 or rsa-pss).
Customer (Northbridge SecOps) 2026-03-10: Prefer ed25519 and need evidence for legal retention (chain-of-custody). Provided KMS thumbprint: kmsthumb-northbridge-42.
SRE (Rina Patel) 2026-03-11: Found missing KMS binding for tenant; manual binding scheduled. Will run end-to-end test once binding is present. Suggested interim workaround: enable S3 manifest HMAC with shared secret to satisfy Chronicle while ed25519 is enabled.
Security (Jon Becker) 2026-03-11: Approved ed25519 with per-batch key rotation policy documented. Require Confluence note and audit log of rotation events.
Marco Villanueva 2026-03-12: Delivered sample payloads and mapping file in ticket attachments (sample_batch.jsonl, chronicle_mapping_v1.csv). Deployed PR #4982 to staging and ran verification against Chronicle dev account. Customer scheduled validation call for 2026-03-15.
Customer 2026-03-12: Received samples and confirmed they match Chronicle dev ingestion script. Asked for SFTP manifest example and a resume_token spec for their compliance team.
Provided artifacts: (1) sample JSONL batch with canonical UTC timestamps and per-record sequence_number and event_uuid, (2) chronicle_mapping_v1.csv mapping, (3) signed per-batch manifest using tenant ed25519 key (details and verification steps documented), (4) SFTP fallback manifest spec with rotation and verification commands, and (5) added deterministic resume_token generation (sha256 tenant+batch_ts+nonce) to manifest generator (PR #4982).

Workaround before KMS binding: enabled HMAC-SHA256 per-record envelope using tenant shared secret; Chronicle accepted HMAC verification.

Follow-ups: SUP-880500 created to track automated KMS binding checklist and post-onboarding audit sign-off. Scheduled validation call on 2026-03-15 with customer. Ticket will be closed after successful production validation and confirmation of receipts from Chronicle.

Issue summary: Customer reported duplicate streaming chunks, truncated responses, and intermittently missing final tokens for long-running streaming completions during a cross-region failover. Impact: HorizonCraft storefront chat features returned duplicated content to end users and occasionally truncated completions; customer reported lost state for 12% of streamed requests during a two-hour window. Environment: Production (dedicated capacity) servicing HorizonCraft account across us-west primary with eu-west failover. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a long-running streaming completion (>8s) pinned to redwood-2.0-large with session affinity; 2) Simulate a region failover by draining us-west pool (or trigger router failover); 3) Observe duplicate chunks and truncated finalization on client side. Observed logs and errors: streaming-proxy connection resets, sequence_id mismatches in serving-runtime logs, and repeated replay-receive events in the router trace. Customer impact: business-critical chat flows degraded for HorizonCraft's European user segment and Pager escalation issued. Workaround: temporary pinning of HorizonCraft to single region (eu-west) and application-level deduplication on client side were applied as mitigations.
Initial triage (Support): collected request IDs / sample client traces and escalated to SRE. SRE findings: 1) replay logic in streaming-proxy attempted to resume streams by re-sending buffered chunks when router returned transient 502/503 during region failover; 2) when the fallback routed to a quantized model variant (redwood-2.0-quant) the KV cache prefix and sequence counters were incompatible, causing partial replays and truncated final tokens; 3) controller routing completed a two-region failover at ~2026-03-08T09:22Z aligning with a canary rollback in dedicated autoscaler (recent deploy at 2026-03-08T08:50Z). Correlated telemetry: spike in stream_replay_count and stream_duplicate_chunks, tail-latency increase for streaming tokens, and inventory mismatch on per-session cursor metrics. Evidence: traces linked in incident channel #inc-horizoncraft, dashboard panels: streaming-proxy/errors, router/replay-rate (see Confluence links). Hypothesis: a recent change in streaming-proxy to persist ephemeral stream cursors across short disconnects combined with controller's cross-region sticky routing produced amplified replays when model variant compatibility differed. Also noted a missing guard in serving-runtime for quantized-model prefix mismatch.
Hotfix: rolled a targeted patch to streaming-proxy to reset ephemeral stream cursor on region/fallback boundary and to apply idempotent replay guards (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proxy/pull/87). Additional fix added a serving-runtime guard to detect model-variant prefix incompatibility and abort graceful resume, falling back to full cold-restart of the session (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321). Rollout plan: hotfix deployed to us-west canary at 2026-03-08T11:05Z; monitored synthetic streaming workload for 30m; progressive rollout to remaining us-west nodes completed by 2026-03-08T11:55Z; eu-west rollout completed by 2026-03-08T12:45Z. Validation: post-deploy telemetry showed stream_replay_count back to baseline and duplicate chunk rate dropped to <0.1% of pre-incident traffic. Customer communication: support notified HorizonCraft of root cause and mitigation at 2026-03-08T13:00Z; offered a billing credit for the impacted window and a post-incident follow-up meeting. Follow-up actions: 1) update streaming runbook with explicit failover cursor reset steps; 2) add unit & integration tests for model-variant prefix mismatch; 3) create alerting that triggers when stream_duplicate_chunks > 0.5% for >10m; 4) schedule a dedicated post-incident review with HorizonCraft customer engineering (confluence postmortem created).

Additional notes:
2026-03-08 12:50 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Notified HorizonCraft that hotfix fully deployed and we are monitoring; offered billing credit and scheduled follow-up call for 2026-03-10.
2026-03-12 13:20 - Customer (HorizonCraft - Elena Morales): Thanks for the quick response and clear remediation. Accept the credit offer; would like the runbook changes documented before next scheduled maintenance.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent streaming sessions that cut off mid-paragraph and never emit the final 'done' control event. Symptoms only occur for traffic routed through their site-to-site IPSec VPN egress path; direct traffic to hosted API not impacted. Impact: several end users see truncated responses or repeated reconnects during multi-kilobyte responses.

Impact:
- Multiple customers at Acme Payments encountering truncated assistant replies during large completions (long-form summaries).
- Client SDKs report 'connection reset' or 'incomplete final chunk' and do not receive closing metadata, leading to retries or stale UI state.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployed into customer VPC (version 2026.02.3).
- Egress through customer-controlled IPSec VPN appliance (vendor: SecuGate 3000).
- Observed with redwood-chat-v1, sequence length ~2k tokens.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Initiate streaming completion from client in customer network over Private endpoint.
2) Server streams multiple SSE chunks (heartbeats + tokens) over TLS.
3) After ~12–20s, connection resets; client receives partial JSON array without closing 'event: done' line.
4) Reconnect attempts sometimes replay prefix tokens or get duplicate small chunks.

Observed behavior:
- Reproducible with packet capture on customer egress: frequent ICMP "Fragmentation needed" (type 3, code 4) logged during long TLS records.
- Kernel logs on gateway show 'IP fragment failed - protocol TCP' and moderate retransmits.
- Sidecar / gateway logs show abrupt connection close from network layer; no application-level error from runtime.

Expected behavior:
- Streams complete with terminal metadata and 'done' event emitted. Client SDKs should receive consistent finalization.

Immediate customer-provided logs (attached):
- pcap snippet (pcap_20260310_acme_stream.pcap) showing TLS records > MSS and subsequent ICMP PMTUD messages.
- sidecar syslog excerpt with repeated 'tcp_retransmission' events.

Temporary workaround suggested in first response:
- Recommend temporary lowering of MTU on customer egress interface to 1400 and/or enable MSS clamping on VPN appliance. Customer applied MTU 1400 and saw immediate reduction in disconnect rate for a subset of sessions.
Start private streaming session from inside customer VPC using redwood-chat-v1
Produce a long-form completion (~1500-3000 tokens) to exercise large TLS records
Observe pcap and sidecar logs for ICMP "Fragmentation needed" and retransmits
Note whether final 'done' event is missing in client stream
pcap_20260310_acme_stream.pcap (customer attachment)
sidecar_syslog_excerpt.txt: repeated tcp_retransmission and ip_fragment failures
runtime_metrics_snapshot_20260310.json: spikes in retransmits and connection resets

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 16:22 — Networking (Elena Rossi): Asked customer to temporarily set MTU=1400 on their egress and enable MSS clamping on the VPN. Customer applied MTU change and reported lower failure rate for long streams — suggests MTU issue.
2026-03-11 08:40 — Support (Maya Chen): Customer confirmed large completions still occasionally truncate during peak traffic but rate dropped from ~1/30 sessions to ~1/300.
2026-03-12 12:30 — Customer (Acme NetOps): Agreed to enable MSS clamping on their SecuGate appliance and to test for 48 hours. Will report back; requested a root-cause writeup and permanent remediation steps.
Packet-level evidence: TLS records for long token batches exceed 1500 bytes; IP path returns ICMP Type 3 Code 4 pointing to next-hop MTU < packet size.
IPSec tunnels often encapsulate packets causing effective MTU shrinkage; if PMTUD is blocked (ICMP filtered) the sender continues sending large packets leading to fragmentation or drops.
Runtime logs show abrupt TCP FIN/RESET originating from kernel when fragmentation fails; application never observes EOF marker for streaming session.
Repro attempt from non-VPN egress (developer workstation) does not reproduce — isolates to customer egress path.
Customer appliance (SecuGate) configuration lacks MSS clamping and had ICMP filtered in egress ACLs.
Short-term: Customer enabled MSS clamping on the IPSec VPN and reduced MTU on gateway interfaces (to 1400). Observed immediate drop in truncated stream incidents.
Medium-term: Recommend adding explicit PMTUD probing and guidance to Private deployment onboarding docs; update runbook with 'if behind VPN, enable MSS clamping or lower MTU' checklist.
Long-term product action: INT-9012 created to add an automated PMTUD check during Private bootstrap that simulates long TLS records and alerts when path MTU < required threshold. Target release: 2026-04 minor.
Customer follow-up: Acme NetOps to monitor for 72 hours and confirm full resolution; Support to keep ticket open until 2026-03-15 or until customer closes.
Notes for SDK teams: consider buffering policy to emit smaller TLS application records when connecting through Private endpoints if path MTU unknown.

Issue summary
Northstar HR reported elevated tail latency on their Dedicated endpoint during a model canary rollout. The customer observed p95 and p99 latency increases and intermittent client timeouts during peak traffic. The rollout did not automatically pause/rollback, requiring manual intervention by on-call.

Customer impact
- Customer-facing latency degradation for chat completions.
- Intermittent client-side timeouts (HTTP 499s observed from the gateway; no increase in 5xx at the platform edge initially).
- The customer explicitly requested an automated safety rail: SLO-based auto-rollback (or auto-pause) for canary/A-B rollouts.

Environment
- Dedicated deployment
- Regions: us-east (primary), eu-west (secondary)
- Route: /v1/chat/completions (tenant: northstar-hr)
- Rollout type: canary traffic shift (10% -> 25% planned)

Timeline (all times PT)
- 2026-02-17 09:42: Rollout step increased candidate traffic from 10% to 25% in us-east.
- 09:49: First internal alert observed on rollout dashboard: p99 latency +38% vs baseline (us-east) for candidate.
- 09:52: Customer email to TAM (Liam) + support@ noting “timeouts + slow responses”.
- 09:57: #incidents thread opened; SRE begins triage.
- 10:05: Rollout manually paused at 25% in us-east; traffic held.
- 10:11: Manual rollback executed to baseline model version; traffic shifted back to 100% baseline.
- 10:18: Latency returns to normal ranges; customer confirms improvement.

What happened / initial findings
- Regression appears isolated to candidate model build/config in us-east under real traffic mix.
- Affected metrics were primarily tail latency (p99) with some p95 increase; error-rate SLO did not breach, and the existing monitor was not rollout-scoped (could not attribute to candidate vs baseline quickly).
- We did not have auto-mitigation wired: rollout controller did not evaluate burn-rate windows against rollout-scoped SLOs, so no automatic pause/rollback occurred.

Customer request
Please provide:
1) Auto-pause/auto-rollback when latency or error-rate SLOs breach during a rollout.
2) Ability to configure thresholds and windows per route/model/region/tier.
3) Audit trail explaining why a rollback happened (metrics snapshot + policy used).

Links
- Slack incident thread: sources/slack/incidents/1770705405.json
- Additional on-call notes on monitor staleness/rollout scoping: sources/slack/eng-sre/1770246692.json
- Internal postmortem/notes: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/2026-02-17-rollout-latency-regression-auto-rollback-gaps.json

Requested next steps (support-facing)
- Provide customer with a clear explanation of current rollout safety behavior and near-term mitigation.
- Share that SLO-driven auto-rollback is in-flight (project: Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration) and offer to include Northstar HR in early access once available.

Workaround (current)
- Keep candidate traffic capped at <=10% for this model family in us-east until regression root cause is addressed.
- Require manual monitoring + explicit SRE sign-off for step increases during business hours.

Resolution (support ticket)
Manual rollback performed; performance stabilized. Follow-up actions tracked in Eng/PM systems for SLO-scoped monitors and auto-rollback integration.

Additional notes:
Manual rollback to baseline model version in us-east; rollout paused. Latency recovered within ~7 minutes. Customer informed; follow-up tracked for SLO-scoped monitors + auto-rollback integration and auditability.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-05 07:40 UTC, FikaHealth reported repeated streaming inference sessions that stalled mid-response and ultimately timed out. Impact: Customer-facing chat experiences experienced partial or full message loss and 30s+ tail latencies for ~40% of streaming requests from APAC clients to their Dedicated capacity. Environment: Dedicated pool in ap-southeast-1 routing through our managed NAT + transit provider peering to us-west-2 where backend model replicas live. Steps to reproduce: 1) From an APAC client network behind FikaHealth NAT, open streaming chat request to model redwood-chat-1 pinned on their dedicated pool. 2) Send a prompt that produces first streamed chunk > 1400 bytes (typical multi-paragraph reply). 3) Observe that the client receives some initial bytes then stalls for >10s before TCP retransmits lead to connection reset and request timeout. Observed symptoms: - High counts of TCP retransmits and duplicate ACKs in tcpdump at our ingress proxy. - Server-side logs show streaming generator continued producing tokens but send() blocked on socket write (backpressure). - No 5xx from model runtime; health checks stayed green. - Increase in p99/p999 latency and client-observed timeouts (sockets closed after client-side 30s). Logs/snippets: "tcp_retransmits=12; dup_acks=7; write_block_duration_ms=12040"; client traceID=fh-12345-20260305. Investigation notes: - Initial hypotheses tested: serving runtime backpressure, model CPU/GPU saturation, proxy memory leak. Metrics and traces ruled these out: GPUs < 60% util, steady request queue depth. - Packet captures from ingress (ap-southeast-1) showed IP fragments with "fragment offset" set but remote side not ACKing full segments; ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages absent. - Transit provider reported a maintenance window coinciding with the start time where a new firewall/VPN appliance was inserted with MTU set to 1400 but no MSS clamping. - PMTU discovery appears to have failed because ICMP type 3/code 4 responses were dropped by an intermediate NAT/firewall, producing a PMTU blackhole for TCP flows that attempted to send large segments. - Because our streaming implementation sends chunks near ethernet MTU (large single writes), socket writes produce large packets which then get dropped or fragmented but never reassembled due to missing PMTU signals. - A smaller reproduction: forcing chunk size <= 1200 bytes avoided stalls consistently. Temporary mitigations applied: - Immediately rolled out a streaming chunk size cap to 1200 bytes for the dedicated pool serving FikaHealth (config change deployed 2026-03-05 11:05 UTC). - Enabled application-level TCP keepalive tune and reduced socket write timeout to fail-fast for stuck streams. - Opened ticket with transit provider to restore MTU to 1500 or enable MSS clamping on the egress VPN appliance. Root cause: A new transit firewall/VPN appliance with an MTU of 1400 was added during maintenance and did not advertise PMTU or perform MSS clamping. This led to a PMTU blackhole for large TCP segments used by our streaming implementation, causing retransmits, socket stalls, and client-observed timeouts. Post-incident actions: - Provider reconfigured appliance to support PMTU/ICMP or to apply MSS clamping on 2026-03-06 02:20 UTC. - We merged a code change to bound streaming chunk sizes by default and added a feature flag to tune per-customer chunking (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/3372). - Added synthetic PMTU/streaming healthcheck to our SRE probes for dedicated pools in cross-region topologies. - Added runbook steps for networking team to check PMTU if streaming stalls are reported.
Mitigation and resolution implemented: transit provider enabled MSS clamping and restored PMTU signalling; we deployed a conservative default streaming chunk cap (1200 bytes) for the affected dedicated pool and released a per-customer config knob. Customer confirmed reduction to near-zero streaming stalls after 2026-03-06 03:00 UTC. Follow-ups: implement PMTU monitoring and automated fallbacks, add explicit MSS clamp detection alerts, include chunk-size test in onboarding for dedicated customers. Ticket closed after verification with customer and post-incident runbook created.

Additional notes:
2026-03-05 10:00 - SRE (Marta Lopez): GPU/serving checks clean. No queued tasks, runtime writes blocked on socket in stack traces. Matches PMTU blackhole behavior.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several customers (first reported by Sentinel Health) observe that when a streaming session falls back from WebSocket to long-poll (or HTTP chunked longpoll) during a short network disruption, the final sentence(s) of the model response and trailing inline emoji/images are missing in the client UI. Impact: production customers see truncated responses, usually losing punctuation, the last clause, and trailing emoji or markdown image URLs. This affects user-visible correctness and downstream processing. Environment: production, us-east endpoints, connections typically go through a corporate edge proxy that performs WS downgrade for flaky mobile/corp networks. Repro frequency: intermittent but reproducible in lab under proxy-induced ws->longpoll handoff. Correlation ids from customer traces: trace=tr-7b2a1c0, session=ssn-91a2b, example request_id=req-4f8c31.
1) Use the JS client-sdk v1.2.5 configured to allow fallback (default) behind the enterprise edge proxy that strips WebSocket upgrades on flakey connections
2) Start a streaming generation (chat) with a long output that ends with a short clause followed by emoji and a markdown image URL
3) Induce a transient drop at the proxy layer to force the SDK into the long-poll fallback path (tooling attached below),
4) Observe client UI: response completes but the final sentence finalizer punctuation and trailing emoji/image URL are missing; server logs still show end-of-stream marker delivered before connection close
5) Reproduce with curl longpoll: hit /v1/stream with chunked response, then interrupt and re-establish via GET - the reassembled body sometimes omits the final chunk under the same proxy conditions
Initial hypothesis: terminal 'end' marker delivered but client reassembly on long-poll path drops the last small chunk when an adjacent heartbeat-only chunk arrives during conversion
Captured pcap and server-side chunk boundaries: the server emits terminal chunk with sequence=56 (small payload 12 bytes) immediately followed by a keepalive chunk; in proxy conversion the small terminal chunk is coalesced into the previous chunk and then truncated by the proxy's chunk rewriter
JS SDK v1.2.5 reassembly logic: accepts chunked frames and treats heartbeat-only frames ("hb") as no-op; however when downgrade occurs the SDK's fallback handler switches to polling code which merges frames using a regex that expects terminal JSON delimiting. The regex fails for very small terminal tokens and drops trailing punctuation/emojis during string concatenation
Server side: serving-runtime logs show the full payload was produced and end-of-stream marker posted before connection teardown (see logs). No evidence of model generating incomplete text. No errors in kernel selection or serving runtime.
Edge proxy: corp proxy (vendor X) configured with aggressive chunk coalescing/trim for HTTP/1.1; vendor-simulations reproduce the drop behavior when 'trim-empty-chunks' and 'coalesce-adjacent' flags are enabled
2026-02-27T16:12:43Z req=req-4f8c31 stream_event=delta data="...and that should do it"
2026-02-27T16:12:43Z req=req-4f8c31 stream_event=heartbeat data="hb"
2026-02-27T16:12:44Z req=req-4f8c31 connection=ws->longpoll handoff=true proxysignal=upgrade-stripped
2026-02-27T16:12:44Z req=req-4f8c31 stream_event=end data="[END]"
2026-02-27T16:12:44Z req=req-4f8c31 client_receive=chunked [partial body without trailing emoji]

Additional notes:
Customer (Sentinel Health - Ops): We see this on some users behind corporate mobile proxies. Workaround applied: set SDK option streamingMode=wsOnly — reduces incidence but not acceptable long-term for corp clients.
Workaround: advised customer to set client option streamingMode="wsOnly" to avoid fallback until SDK patch is released. Permanent fix: client-sdk v1.2.8 (patch) updates polling reassembly to use a length-prefixed buffer and sequence number sanity checks; edge-proxy guidance added to recommend disabling coalesce/trim flags for longpoll conversions. Patch PR merged and released to npm as v1.2.8. Follow-ups: add e2e tests simulating proxy downgrade, add metric streaming.incomplete_terminal_count and alerting, and coordinate with infra to flag regions with aggressive proxy rewriting.
payload.summary: Fallback multi-protocol fragmentation drops terminal sentence and trailing emoji when WS->longpoll fails over

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers are observing client-side read deadline exceeded errors (HTTP 504 / streaming disconnects) when sending priming prompts > 120k tokens together with max_tokens >= 65k. The failures started appearing after a throughput/priority tweak rolled 2026-03-08 and are intermittent but reproducible.

Impact:
- Multiple enterprise customers experience partial or full generation failures for long-context workflows (chat history + docs priming).
- Requests frequently stream initial tokens then hang for an extended period before client times out.
- Affects mission-critical health workflows at LexaHealth (delays in clinical note drafting).

Environment:
- Production (us-east) backend; traffic hits hosted API via edge proxy, routed to dedicated serving pools for enterprise tenants.
- Observed against redwood-v2-xl and v1-compat quantized variants.

Observed behavior:
- Successful first N tokens (often 800-2000 tokens), then long stall (30-80s) followed by client read-deadline and connection termination.
- Server-side traces show finalizer queue piling and per-request worker preemption in some cases.
- No immediate 5xx returned by runtime; client only sees a streaming disconnect or 504 after read deadline.

Expected behavior:
- Stream continues at steady rate until model generation completes or fails quickly with a deterministic error.

Notes:
- Customer reports reduction of failures when max_tokens reduced to <= 4k or when request split across multiple calls.

1) Use LexaHealth test tenant request with a priming document ~120k tokens + user prompt (~300 tokens).
2) Set max_tokens to 65,536 and streaming=true.
3) Send request to api.redwood.ai/v1/generate using SDK (node/python) with default client read timeout (60s).
4) Observe initial streaming chunks then a hang; client logs a read deadline exceeded after ~65-75s.
5) Repeat with max_tokens=4096 and observe successful completion within normal latency.

edge-proxy: tcp proxy forwarded; initial chunks delivered.
serving-runtime[2026-03-10T15:12:03Z]: request id r-8b3c: prefix tokens streamed (1-1200) then stalled; finalizer_queue_length=42; worker_preempt=true; kv_cache_evictions=3; kernel_swap_count=1.
finalizer: backlog spike from 5->120 between 15:12:02 and 15:12:08.
client (LexaHealth): socket read timeout at 15:13:08, error: 'read deadline exceeded'.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - LexaHealth (Customer): Confirmed that lowering max_tokens to 4k dramatically reduces failures; provided sample payload and reproduction script.
2026-03-12 - Eng (runtime): Reproduced locally with synthetic priming; observed kv-cache eviction thrash plus long GC-ish pauses around kernel handoff. Suspect combination of prefix size + large output budget causing synchronous finalization steps to queue.
2026-03-13 - SRE: Temporary mitigation applied: throttle long-context requests to lower-priority lane and force streaming heartbeat packets every 15s to keep client sockets alive. Customer notified; monitoring for regressions.
2026-03-13 - Eng: Working on a longer-term fix: batching/finalizer change to prioritize active streaming connections and introduce per-request soft time-slicing to avoid long blocking on kernel swaps.
Hypotheses: 1) Finalizer queue priority inversion: large output-budget requests block GPU worker finalization path while smaller requests are starved. 2) KV cache eviction churn on huge prefixes causes synchronous I/O and kernel handoffs, introducing long pauses. 3) Edge proxy/client heartbeat mismatch: client times out before streaming heartbeats are emitted during backpressure.
Evidence: finalizer_queue_length spikes and worker_preempt flag correlated to customer failures; reproducer reproduces latency spike when kernel_swap_count>0 and kv_cache_evictions>0.
Next steps: gather perf traces for finalizer loop; add instrumentation to record per-request kernel handoff duration; run controlled canary with throttled finalizer concurrency.
Mitigation applied (2026-03-13):
- Short-term: throttle enterprise long-context requests to a dedicated lane with guaranteed background progress; enable synthetic streaming heartbeats for in-flight long requests to prevent client read timeouts.
- Customer-facing workaround: split priming into smaller priming chunks (<= 32k tokens) or reduce max_tokens to <= 8k when possible.
- Medium-term: engineering will land changes to finalizer scheduling to prioritize active streaming sockets and implement incremental KV load/stream-friendly kernel handoffs (tracked in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/548).
Follow-up actions: add runbook step to detect finalizer backlog and auto-promote synthetic heartbeats; add metric alert (finalizer_queue_length>50 for >30s) and create playbook for traffic re-route.
Status: mitigation implemented and monitoring; permanent fix in development (target rollout 2026-03-27).
