Issue summary:
Customer (VectorMaps Inc.) observed a sustained p99 throughput regression on their dedicated reserved pool starting 2026-03-10 14:30 UTC. The degradation aligns with an autoscaler shrink followed by a tapered recovery window where short-lived high-concurrency streams repeatedly acquired and held GPU slots during warmup, preventing normal batched routes from filling and causing long tail queuing. Impact:
- Customer reported 3x increase in request latency p95->p99 and 40-60% drop in throughput for batched text-generation routes.
- Affects production traffic for multiple routes; some traffic fell back to hosted fallback model variants causing higher cost and inconsistent outputs.
Environment:
- Dedicated pool: reserved-capacity-vecmaps-usw (8x A10g equiv GPUs)
- Region: us-west
- Time window: 2026-03-10 14:30 UTC onwards
- Routes: /v1/generate-batched, /v1/stream-chat (batched backends), customer uses pinned model opt-13b for priority routes

1) Send a mix of long-lived batched generation requests and a burst of short 1-2 token short-stream connections at high concurrency (50-100 concurrent short streams).
2) Ensure autoscaler min_replicas at low baseline (2 GPUs) and cooldown window set to default 300s so autoscaler aggressively shrinks after observed drop in average load.
3) During the autoscaler recovery window, observe GPU attach logs and batcher fill rates for batched routes.
4) Measure p95/p99 for batched route and correlated slot allocation timelines from allocator telemetry.
2026-03-10T14:29:52Z allocator: shrink_to=2 triggered by 60s low load metric
2026-03-10T14:30:15Z serving-runtime: attach_request id=txn-8f1d short_stream=true duration=0.8s hold_slots=1
2026-03-10T14:30:16Z prefetcher: lease_acquired id=pref-342 type=short_warmup lease_ttl=120s
2026-03-10T14:31:03Z batcher: insufficient_fill route=/v1/generate-batched observed_fill=30% target=80%
2026-03-10T14:31:05Z autoscaler: recovery_in_progress cooldown_remaining=230s
2026-03-10T14:31:45Z allocator: slot_wait_queue length=42 p99_wait=1.8s
2026-03-10T14:32:10Z serving-runtime: eviction_attempt id=txn-ff2a cause=slot_blocked_by_prefetch
2026-03-10T14:33:00Z metrics: route=/v1/generate-batched p95=320ms p99=2.4s throughput=45req/s baseline=120req/s

Additional notes:
Customer (VectorMaps Eng - Jamie): We started a new feature at 14:25 that spins many short model-check requests. Rolling that back reduced error rate briefly but p99 stayed elevated until autoscaler spun back up.
01 - Correlation: Autoscaler shrink at 14:29 reduced active GPUs. Immediately following, short warmup streams (mean duration 0.7s) repeatedly acquired prefetch leases (TTL 120s) and occupied slot objects, preventing batched requests from filling target batch sizes.
02 - Batcher telemetry shows sustained low fill-rate (30-40%) for batched routes while short streams maintained steady attach churn; combined with fewer GPUs caused throughput to fall ~55%.
03 - Allocator traces show slot objects moved to 'pinned' state tied to prefetch lease; lease release did not occur promptly on short stream completion when autoscaler was in recovery (race between prefetcher and allocator release path).
04 - Hypothesis: Prefetch lease release path depends on heartbeat from warmup sidecar; during autoscaler recovery sidecar restart sequence introduced a window where leases weren't reclaimed promptly. Also TTL expiry was long enough to allow multiple short streams to hold onto slots sequentially.
05 - Secondary factor: default autoscaler cooldown prevented new GPUs from being added until recovery window elapsed (300s), so even when workload ramped the platform was slow to re-provision capacity.
06 - No signs of driver-level GPU errors; this appears scheduling/allocator-level resource contention rather than hardware faults.
07 - Related tickets: SUP-712909 (deferred-warmup-causing-spotty-gpu-assignments), SUP-371400 (allocator-heartbeat-skew) - useful traces and prior mitigation notes.
Workaround applied (customer consented):
- Increased pool min_replicas from 2 -> 4 for reserved-capacity-vecmaps-usw to reduce chance of slot starvation during recovery window.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive prefetching for short-stream route (/v1/stream-chat) for the customer via routing override.
- Customer rolled back the short-model-check feature burst.
Post-mitigation observations: latency/p99 recovered to baseline within ~6 minutes of changes and autoscaler stabilized.
Next steps (tracking):
- Engineering task created to add lease-release-on-shortstream-termination and to reduce default prefetch TTL for short streams (PR referenced below).
- Consider autoscaler cooldown tuning: expose per-pool cooldown or quick-provision path when significant queueing is detected.

Issue summary:
Customers see a truncated final output and missing attachment URL when the client performs an SSE stream that upgrades to WebSocket mid-response. The last few tokens (often the attachment link or final punctuation) are dropped and the stream terminates without the terminal metadata envelope.

Impact:
- KiteNote (enterprise) reports 12% of long-running generation requests lost last-line attachments during heavy traffic windows.
- Affects production traffic in us-west; some artifacts seen in us-east during cross-region failover.

Environment:
prod - us-west, api gateway behind ALB -> edge proxy cluster -> serving-runtime pool. Customer using SDK-js v1.2.4 with automatic SSE-to-WS upgrade enabled.

Expected behavior:
When a client upgrades an open SSE stream to a WebSocket (preferred for bi-directional control), the server should deliver remaining buffered tokens and the final metadata envelope ("event: done" + attachments list) exactly once.

Actual behavior:
During an upgrade window the stream sometimes closes with a partial final chunk; the JSON/metadata envelope for attachments is missing or arrives but with empty attachments array. The socket on the client shows a 101 upgrade then a FIN shortly after with no more data.

Attachments/Logs referenced below.

1) Start a long-generation SSE request using SDK-js v1.2.4 with streaming upgradable set to true.
2) After ~8-12 seconds of token stream, trigger client to proactively upgrade the connection to WebSocket (client does upgrade handshake).
3) Observe server behavior under moderate load (50-100 concurrent streams) and a behind-ALB probe cycling every 30s.
4) Look at final tokens & attachment metadata on client; compare to server logs for that request id.

Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 12:07 and 12:35 UTC, a customer (DataMuse - dedicated pool) observed a sharp drop in sustained throughput and elevated p99 latency on batched generation routes. Impact: multiple short-lived requests from many clients produced a sidecar connection storm which led to transient GPU slot reservations ('slot latch') and prefetch starvation for batched streams; customer reported 40-60% reduction in tokens/sec for 20 minutes. Environment: production reserved pool in us-east; Dedicated capacity cluster: rp-us-east-07; Serving runtime v2.8.1, sidecar-proxy v1.5.3, scheduler v0.9.4.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer traffic pattern: thousands of very short streams (median duration ~150ms) originating from a fanout of ~200 client endpoints hitting the same model route.
2) Sidecar proxies opened and closed connections rapidly; many connections reset mid-handshake.
3) Scheduler observed many transient slot allocations marked in-use while sidecar tracked heartbeat state; prefetch jobs queued but did not complete due to slot latch timing out.
4) Autoscaler did not trigger immediate scale-up (thresholds tuned to sustained queue depth) -> reserved pool maintained same slot count and p99 drift persisted.

Logs / snippets (sanitized):
- serving-runtime: "[12:12:17Z] slot-reserve: id=slot-78f, state=HELD_BY_SIDECAR, lease=30s"
- sidecar-proxy: "[12:12:18Z] conn: accept fd=210 remote=10.3.99.42:54321 state=ESTABLISHED -> RESET"
- scheduler: "[12:12:19Z] prefetch: id=pref-412 queued (dep: slot-78f) waiting for attach"
- k8s events: repeated CrashLoopBackOff on sidecar-reporter (metric handshake spikes)

Observed metrics: sudden spike in short-lived connections (+1200/min), slot_hold_count rose from baseline 4 -> 24, prefetch_queue_growth to 600, effective batch size dropped 3x, p99 latency increased from 180ms -> 1.4s for the route.
2026-03-10 12:27 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer submitted case with screenshots of Console p99 spike and sample logs. Marked P1 due to dedicated pool impact.
2026-03-10 12:45 UTC - SRE (Mateo): Initial triage — confirmed sidecar connection churn correlated with slot_hold_count rise. Hypothesis: sidecar connection resets left slots in a transient HELD_BY_SIDECAR state until lease expiry, preventing prefetch attach and reducing batching efficiency.
2026-03-10 13:05 UTC - Customer (DataMuse): Confirmed they had recently deployed a client change that multiplexes many tiny requests rather than batching. Willing to roll back if necessary.
2026-03-10 13:22 UTC - SRE (Mateo): Applied mitigation #1: reduced sidecar connection timeout and increased socket backlog to reduce reset storms. Observed partial recovery in throughput (tokens/sec +25%).
2026-03-10 13:48 UTC - SRE (Mateo): Applied mitigation #2: temporarily lowered autoscaler grow threshold for this reserved pool (allow faster reacts to queue spikes). Throughput returned to baseline by 12:55-13:00 UTC.
2026-03-12 09:15 UTC - Engineering (Priya): Patch merged to sidecar to coalesce rapid connects into a short windowed-attach operation (PR #412). Backport scheduled to v1.5.x.
2026-03-12 09:30 UTC - Customer (DataMuse): Confirmed good recovery and accepted compensating configuration changes; requested post-incident notes and preventive recommendations.
Hypothesis A: Sidecar rapid connect/disconnects were leaving ephemeral markers that scheduler treated as active holds; lease expiry (30s) is long relative to connection churn leading to effective slot underutilization.
Hypothesis B: Prefetch tasks are serialized to a single attach step which collides when many short streams compete; backlog prevents new batches from forming and autoscaler thresholds are tuned for sustained load, not sub-minute microbursts.
Telemetry review: correlation between conn-churn and slot_hold_count is strong (Pearson r=0.78 over 5m window). No GPU OOMs or driver errors detected. NVLink and PCIe metrics normal.
Repro notes: We were able to reproduce a smaller version of the problem in staging by generating 800 short-lived connects/minute and observed a drop in effective batch size and prefetch queue growth.
Mitigations applied in prod: (1) Reduced sidecar session timeout from 30s -> 8s and increased listen backlog to absorb bursts; (2) Temporarily lowered autoscaler grow threshold and reduced cooldown to allow faster slot allocation; (3) Rolling restart of sidecar-reporter instances to clear reset spike and remove stale holds. A code patch to coalesce attach operations in the sidecar was merged (PR #412) and backported to 1.5.x. The customer reverted the client change that caused extreme multiplexing while we deployed fixes.
Deploy sidecar v1.5.4 (contains attach-coalescing) to all reserved pools by 2026-03-18.
Add metric and alert: slot_hold_ratio > 0.15 for 2m -> Pager and create dashboard per reserved pool.
Update autoscaler tuning doc to include microburst window sensitivity and recommended temporary knobs for reserved pools with many small streams.
Add a runbook step: when slot_hold_count rises with conn-churn, perform targeted sidecar restart and consider lowering lease timeout; include safe thresholds and rollback.
Customer guidance: Recommend client-side batching or a short client-side queue to reduce connect churn; include sample SDK config snippet in CS reply.
Incident closed after validations on 2026-03-12. Root cause is a combination of client-side short-stream fanout plus sidecar behavior that left transient slot holds; autoscaler sensitivity compounded duration. Fixes included configuration mitigations and a sidecar attach coalescing patch.

Issue summary:
Customer NoteStream reports that long-running SSE generation sessions occasionally complete but the final 'choice' record (terminal chunk + metadata) is missing after a brief CDN edge circuit-breaker-triggered reconnect. The stream delivers partial text, sometimes duplicates a short prefix on resume, and never sends the terminal metadata event that includes the request_id and final token offsets.

Impact:
- Intermittent loss of final sentence/terminal metadata for a subset (~0.4%) of user sessions during peak load behind FastEdge CDN.
- Customer-side UX reports 'incomplete document' and retries result in duplicate prefixes.

Environment:
- Production (prod-us-west) behind FastEdge CDN and our api-gateway v2.3.0.
- Customer using streaming SSE client with short-lived OAuth token rotation (10s refresh window).
- Observed against model gptj-13b-v1 and redwood-llm-3.1.

1) Configure short-lived auth token rotation on client (rotate every 8-12 seconds).
2) Send a long-stream SSE generation request (prompt length ~800 tokens, expected output ~1200 tokens) through FastEdge edge with circuit-breaker configured to RST on backend latency > 8s.,
3) Induce transient backend latency (simulate 150ms CPU stall or connection freeze) so edge circuit-breaker opens and triggers reconnect path,
4) Observe that the client receives partial streamed chunks, then on reconnect sees a duplicated 8-20 token prefix and then stream ends without a terminal metadata event (no 'done' marker or final offsets).
Partial streaming payload arrives; on a small percentage of reconnects the client sees a short duplicated prefix, then stream terminates with no terminal metadata event (missing request_id and final_token_offset). Downstream SDK treats stream as incomplete and surfaces 'incomplete finalization' to app.
On transient reconnection the stream should either fully resume and deliver the terminal metadata (single coherent final choice) or fail with a clear terminal error. No silent truncation or missing metadata should occur.
2026-03-10T14:23:17Z api-gateway request_id=rn-4b7e6 trace_id=tx-88a3 stream=open upstream=host-12 path=/v1/generate status=200 latency=7.9s
2026-03-10T14:23:26Z edge-proxy trace_id=tx-88a3 circuit_breaker=open backend=host-12 action=rst reason=latency_spike
2026-03-10T14:23:26Z api-gateway request_id=rn-4b7e6 trace_id=tx-88a3 stream=resume token_ver=rot-20260310-14:23:25 client_token_id=note-auth-xx
2026-03-10T14:23:27Z serving-runtime request_id=rn-4b7e6 choice_stream_chunk sequence=... partial_text="...and conclude with a recommendation to...",
2026-03-10T14:23:27Z serving-runtime request_id=rn-4b7e6 final_meta=missing error=none
Initial triage by Level 1: reproduced with FastEdge in staging when circuit-breaker threshold set low and client token rotates in the reconnect window.
Hypothesis A: auth token rotation on reconnect leads api-gateway to treat resumed connection as a different session and server-side streaming state is garbage-collected before terminal metadata is emitted.
Hypothesis B: edge circuit-breaker issues an upstream RST and our resume path emits a duplicate small prefix because prefix caching + resume offset recalculation drift by N tokens under race conditions.
Trace analysis: trace tx-88a3 shows resume path invoked with a different token_ver header; serving-runtime logs show final metadata field absent rather than an explicit error, suggesting finalization hook may have been skipped.
Kibana dashboard: https://kibana.internal.redwood/streaming?trace=tx-88a3 (customer link redacted).
Relevant config: api-gateway session-ttl=5s, resume-grace=2s, token-rotation-window=10s, edge circuit-breaker latency-threshold=8s.
Reproduced in our internal staging cluster when rotating token at 9s and circuit-breaker threshold at 6s -> ~15% reproduction rate in synthetic runs (higher than prod).
Customer workaround: increase client token lifetime to avoid rotation during expected long-running streams, or disable aggressive CDN circuit-breaker for streaming endpoints.
Support workaround: enable 'streaming-grace' feature flag on customer's api-gateway which increases resume-grace to 30s (mitigates GC race).
Fix planned: engineering to adjust resume flow to accept stateless token rotation by mapping new token to previous session id when resume headers include prior_request_id; add idempotent finalization that emits terminal metadata even if resume token differs.
Short-term patch: extend resume-grace default from 2s -> 10s and make finalization commit occur before session TTL expiry. Rollout planned to prod-us-west on 2026-03-16 under canary.
Post-fix verification: synthetic test harness will run 10k long-stream sessions with intentional circuit-breaker RST and token rotation to verify <0.01% truncation rate.
ENG: PR for resume-tolerant-auth mapping and idempotent-finalizer (infra/edge-proxy#5248) assigned to Liam; target review by 2026-03-13.
SRE: monitor stream-terminal-missing metric and set alert threshold >0.05% over 1h to PagerDuty. Agent: Priya Sinha.
CS: advise NoteStream to temporarily lengthen token TTL or route streaming traffic to bypass FastEdge for mission-critical customers until patch ships.
DOCS: update runbook with recommended token TTL and circuit-breaker settings for streaming endpoints (owner: Product Ops).

Additional notes:
2026-03-11T12:30Z NoteStream-Support: Thanks — we applied the temporary token-lifetime increase and reports of incomplete streams dropped to near zero. We've paused our CDN aggressive failover rule as well.

Issue summary: BrightPost reported a sudden increase in 5xx errors and tail latency after enabling a tenant-scoped quantization profile and concurrent KV-prefetch tuning. The customer is on Dedicated capacity and observed sustained elevated error rates starting 2026-03-13 02:20 UTC. They need assisted, low-risk unwind steps and a live traffic policy to avoid a full-service interruption.
Customer-facing production endpoints returning 5xx at ~3-7% and 95p latency increase from 220ms to 1.2s for long sessions. Affects critical healthcare flows and triggers enterprise SLA alarm. No data loss reported. Several API keys show correlated error spikes.
1) Tenant-level opt-profile activation (quantization=q4_0, kv_prefetch=enabled, batch_target=dynamic)
2) Sustained ~80% concurrency for 30+ minutes
3) Observe eviction churn in KV cache and rising decoder OOM/5xx in logs
4) Repeat with canary traffic split to reproduce behavior in a smaller cohort
[2026-03-13T02:21:05Z] serving-runtime ERROR decoder: kv_eviction=high tenant=brightpost session=xyz status=500

Initial hypothesis: aggressive quantization profile reduced memory per-tensor but changed allocation patterns; combined with enabled KV-prefetch this increased transient allocation pressure leading to frequent KV eviction and decoder fallback paths that are not optimized for q4-prefixed weights. payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLedger reports intermittent long-tail token delivery delays from Redwood API during high-concurrency batch scoring. Responses from the service appear normal in traces (sub-200ms server processing) but customer-observed end-to-end latency spikes to multiple seconds on a subset of requests.

Impact:
- Several BrightLedger production endpoints (dedicated pool) seeing 5-10% of user requests delayed by 2-8s during peak windows.
- Customer experienced increased user-facing timeouts and retry storms within their app.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity, prod us-east region
- BrightLedger uses redwood-js-sdk v1.6.2 with default client configuration in a horizontally scaled Node.js service.
- Typical concurrency: 60-120 parallel inference requests per instance (small requests, many concurrent).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start 100 parallel small-batch (1-4 prompts) scoring requests using redwood-js-sdk default client config.
2) Observe that most requests return in ~200ms, but ~5-10% experience 2-8s latency.
3) Enabling verbose SDK debug logs shows requests queued in SDK prior to network send.

Observed behavior:
- Server traces show request handled in ~120-220ms.
- SDK logs show enqueue/wait events with exponential backoff attempts and long per-request wait times before TCP send.
- No 5xx from Redwood, few 429s noted earlier in week (likely related to the same config).

Expected behavior:
- Requests either be sent immediately or retried quickly; not accumulate multi-second client-side queuing when server responds fast.

Logs/snippets (customer):
[2026-03-09T14:12:03.153Z] SDK DEBUG enqueue request id=cb4f3
[2026-03-09T14:12:03.157Z] HTTP SEND request id=cb4f3 -> /v1/generate (no backoff)
[2026-03-09T14:12:05.672Z] SDK DEBUG retry backoff enter request id=cb4f7 delay=5000ms attempt=2
[2026-03-09T14:12:07.007Z] HTTP RESPONSE request id=cb4f3 status=200 time=145ms
[2026-03-09T14:12:09.009Z] SDK DEBUG dequeue request id=cb4f7 (waited=7387ms)

Notes: logs indicate request cb4f7 did not hit network for ~7s despite overall low server latency for other requests.

Attachments: customer provided SDK debug traces and a short Flamegraph showing Node event-loop idle time while requests awaited SDK queue slot.

Recommended immediate workaround for customer:
- Increase SDK connection pool and concurrent send slots from default (v1.6.2 defaults to poolSize=8) to poolSize=40 for their concurrency pattern.
- Reduce client max_backoff_ms from 60000 to 5000 to avoid multi-second queuing during transient throttling.
- Instrument SDK debug metrics to emit queue_length and avg_wait_ms per instance.

Follow-ups required:
- Engineering review to adjust SDK defaults or add heuristic warnings when init detects high concurrency vs. small pool size.
- Add an observability metric in platform to detect high client-side queuing reported by SDK telemetry.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 - BrightLedger (Customer): Provided reproduction harness and logs. Confirmed they run 60-120 concurrent scoring requests per instance. Asked for best-practice config.
2026-03-11 - Engineering (Investigator): Reproduced locally with redwood-js-sdk v1.6.2. Default poolSize=8 leads to queued requests under 100 concurrent clients. After increasing poolSize to 40 and capping max_backoff_ms to 5s, tails drop to <1%.
2026-03-12 - BrightLedger (Customer): Applied recommended workaround (poolSize=40, max_backoff_ms=5000). Confirmed 95th/99th percentile improved and user-facing timeouts resolved. Asked about permanent fix and SDK release timeline.
Timeline and findings:
- 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Customer reported issue.
- Reproduced in our lab using the customer's harness. With default SDK settings (poolSize=8, exponential backoff max=60s), concurrent requests above pool size cause the SDK to serialize outgoing HTTP sends behind a fixed-size socket pool.
- When transient 429s occur (observed earlier), the SDK's retry/backoff logic delays re-sends and holds queued requests for the backoff duration. Because queue slots are limited, new requests pile up in the SDK queue rather than being sent or failing fast. That creates the illusion of server slowness even when the server processes other requests quickly.
- Root cause: combination of (a) conservative default poolSize in SDK for Node.js, (b) large max_backoff_ms and no circuit-breaker for queued requests, and (c) customer workload pattern (many small, high-concurrency requests).
- Corroborating evidence: network traces show lack of outbound SYN until much later for delayed requests; server logs show corresponding requests handled quickly.
Resolution and action items:
- Immediate: Advised BrightLedger to update SDK config to poolSize=40 and set max_backoff_ms=5000. Customer applied change and confirmed mitigation on 2026-03-12.
- Short-term dev fix: INT-4129 created to implement SDK client-side safeguards: emit warnings at init when estimated concurrency > poolSize * 2, add a hard cap on per-request queue wait (fail-fast after configurable threshold), and shorten default max_backoff_ms to 10s for v1.7.0.
- Long-term: PR github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3481 adds telemetry hooks for client-side queue length to the Console and runbook updates. Also update our docs with recommended pool sizing guidelines for high-concurrency dedicated deployments.
- Postmortem notes: not a server regression; misalignment between SDK defaults and certain dedicated customer workloads. Update alerts to detect client-side queueing signals so we can proactively advise customers.
INT-4129: implement SDK warnings and fail-fast queue cap
Backport SDK patch to v1.6.x branch and release v1.6.3
Docs: add 'Sizing the client connection pool' guide under SDK best practices
Add client-queue-length metric to Redwood Console dashboard and alert when >100ms avg wait for >5min
payload.summary: SDK connection-starvation + aggressive retry backoff misconfiguration causing apparent inference token delivery delays

Issue summary: Since ~2026-03-09 21:00 UTC, a subset of requests from Mailboxly (dedicated account) to hosted endpoints are experiencing increased p95/p99 latencies and occasional streaming timeouts. The error pattern shows long-tail token emission stalls followed by request timeouts (client sees HTTP 504/stream disconnect).

Impact: Affects ~5% of Mailboxly production inference traffic routed through the us-west POP; degraded user experience for chat features, increased client-side retries, and duplicated billing events observed. No complete region outage.

Environment: prod; us-west POP (edge cluster usw-pop-17). Dedicated pool: dp-usw-mailboxly. Models in use: redwood-7b-v2 and community-llm-13b pinned in the customer's rollout.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Send chat-streaming request via customer API key to the redwood streaming endpoint from an IP traceable to Mailboxly's CIDR. 2) Observe response stream; after 10-60s tokens may pause, then connection drops or client receives 504. 3) Repeating with same client from different region (us-east) does not reproduce.

Observed behavior: p50 stable, p95 and p99 increased by 3-9x for affected traces; frequent streaming stall pattern where KV cache hits continue but no outbound tokens emitted; server side shows active inference threads stuck in "waiting-for-egress-ack" state.

Expected behavior: steady token emission with p95 within SLA (200-600ms per-client-turn depending on model) and no streaming disconnects for sustained sessions.

Initial logs & hashes: Request trace IDs evidence in customer logs: trace-20260309-usw-0001..0007. Edge proxy (usw-pop-17) logs show repeated 502->200->timeout sequences for same upstream host IPs. No model OOMs reported in serving runtime.

Additional notes: Customer first raised via support chat; elevated to P1 due to production impact and billing anomalies from client retries.
Issue is intermittent; reproduce reliably by sending sustained streaming session (>30s) from Mailboxly's IPs routed through us-west.
Run curl against streaming endpoint with chunked transfer to simulate typing pattern and observe stall after multiple tokens.
Compare runs from us-east and us-west to confirm regional skew.

serving-runtime/dp-usw-mailboxly/instance-3/kernel.log: no OOMs; threads show KV cache active; thread stack shows wait at net_send() in proxy client library
2026-03-09 22:05 - Support (Aisha): Logged case after customer reported repeated streaming stalls; assigned to SRE for initial triage.
2026-03-09 23:40 - SRE (Jin): Confirmed increased latency spikes on us-west POP; beginning packet captures at edge and upstream egress gateway.
2026-03-10 01:15 - Customer (Mailboxly): Provided pcap and example trace IDs; notes issue correlates with peak 20:30-22:00 PDT traffic.
2026-03-10 08:30 - Networking (Carlos Mendes): Observed intermittent BGP path change events to the POP resulting in asymmetric return path for a subset of client IPs.
2026-03-11 11:20 - SRE (Jin): Deployed temporary routing rule to force affinity to healthy egress node; observed reduction in stalled streams for affected requests.
2026-03-12 09:02 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed degradation reduced but still seeing occasional stalls; holding P1 pending permanent mitigation.
Hypothesis 1: Edge-to-egress asymmetric routing causing the upstream ACKs to be dropped or delayed; server's streaming library waits on ACK from proxy before sending next chunk -> long stalls.
Hypothesis 2: Healthcheck flapping on one NLB target group in us-west causing intermittent traffic to be sent to a degraded instance that partially accepts requests (200) but fails to keep TCP keepalive, leading to downstream stalls.
Finding: BGP churn timestamps line up with increased counts of retransmit and out-of-order packets in packet captures (pcap id pc-usw-03).
Temporary mitigation: Applied a static egress affinity policy for Mailboxly traffic (route via egress-set-2) and enabled more aggressive TCP keepalive on edge proxies. Result: p95 improved from 3.2s to 740ms for a sample window.
Observed side-effect: Some client IPs that previously routed to a closer POP were forced to a different egress, increasing TTFB for warm sessions; tradeoff accepted to restore stream continuity.
Workaround: Persistent route affinity applied for Mailboxly to egress-set-2 and aggressive keepalive settings on the edge proxies rolled out to usw-pop-17. Permanent fix: Networking to collaborate with infra to tune NLB healthcheck origin consistency and deploy control-plane change to stabilize BGP communities on the us-west edges.

Rollout notes: Change deployed to usw-pop-17 on 2026-03-11 14:00 UTC with verification window 48h. Post-mitigation metrics show p95 reduction and streaming disconnect count reduced by ~86% for Mailboxly.

Follow-ups: (1) Networking to add synthetic egress health probes that mimic streaming traffic patterns (owner: Carlos Mendes, due 2026-03-19). (2) SRE to add alert for "waiting-for-egress-ack" thread states (owner: Jin Park, due 2026-03-15). (3) Reach out to Mailboxly CS to review retry/backoff behavior to reduce duplicate billing (owner: Aisha Patel, due 2026-03-13).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
BrightForms is reporting intermittent throughput collapse for their dedicated pool in us-east starting 2026-03-10 11:40 UTC. Symptoms align with a regional GPU supply squeeze where many GPUs appear allocated but traffic shows a high proportion of very short inference streams with persistent TCP/TLS keepalive.

Impact:
- Customer-facing routes (real-time chat) p95/p99 latency sharply increased; observed request queues and autoscaler unable to reclaim GPUs quickly.
- Other tenants in the same reserved cluster experienced degraded throughput and increased fallbacks to lower-cap models.
- Business impact: customer reported degraded UX for production traffic across multiple endpoints.

Timeline & quick facts:
- 2026-03-10 11:38 UTC: BrightForms first observed degraded latency and opened a support channel.
- 2026-03-10 11:45 UTC: Support identified elevated "active_slot_count" with many connections showing <50ms compute but socket persisted >60s.
- 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC: Autoscaler attempted to add GPUs but allocation failed due to shortfall in the region (ephemeral shortage reported by infra).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Client opens long-lived streaming connection with frequent keepalive pings but sends only occasional short inference calls (1-5 tokens).
2) Serving runtime pins a GPU slot for the connection to maintain KV/cache affinity.
3) Connection remains open for minutes; batcher cannot efficiently combine tiny requests into useful batches.
4) When many clients behave similarly, GPU slot utilization becomes fragmented: many slots show low compute duty but remain reserved.

Observed metrics/logs (snippets):
- allocator metrics: "active_slots: 182 / 200", "avg_slot_utilization: 0.12"
- serving logs (sample): "INFO 2026-03-10T11:46:21Z connection_id=xyz keepalive=62s last_compute=0.043s pinned_gpu=gpu-17"
- autoscaler: "scale_attempt=1 -> fail: insufficient_available_gpus(region=us-east)"
- kernel-level: no OOMs; NVLink utilization low; PCIe spikes correlate with background snapshotter in other cluster shards.

Hypothesis:
- Not classic noisy tenant heavy compute: instead small-streams + long connections are causing slot linger (affinity retention) which fragments capacity and prevents autoscaler from recovering effective throughput.
- Combined with a short-term regional provisioning lag and a background snapshotter IO wave (seen in other shards), this amplified the impact.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Support signaled customer to reduce client keepalive to 15s where possible and to batch short requests client-side (temporary).
- On our side SRE applied a short-lived aggressive reclaim heuristic on the cluster (60s idle compute -> allow slot relinquish). This recovered ~30 GPUs back to the pool but needs careful rollback testing.

Next steps (planned):
- Short window: monitor reclaimed capacity metrics (assigned to SRE, see comments).
- Medium: add a scheduler feature flag to allow opportunistic slot preemption for connections with low compute density after a configurable grace period.
- Long: instrument per-connection compute duty cycle and expose it to console for customers to diagnose keepalive-heavy clients.

Requested from customer:
- Example client connection logs (tcp dumps / client-side timestamps) and sample session IDs to correlate.
- Whether they can apply client-side batching or reduce keepalive interval as a workaround.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:42 - BrightForms (Customer): Provided three session traces and confirmed they can try lowering keepalive to 20s within a maintenance window.
2026-03-12 08:30 - SRE (Investigation): Hypothesis updated: background snapshotter IO correlated with allocator sluggishness; need to coordinate with infra to reduce concurrent snapshot windows. Created follow-up INT ticket for snapshotter cadence adjustment.
Checked allocator logs: fragmentation metric increased from 0.08 -> 0.37 between 11:30-11:50 UTC.
KV-cache pin counts are normal; this is not because of long context usage but connection lifetime.
Autoscaler attempted to spin up 10 GPUs but region reported supply shortfall; coordination with infra needed to confirm temporary capacity dip in us-east.
Reclaim heuristic had side effects: observed a ~1.5% error-rate bump for short-lived clients during the reclaim; recommend canary before broad rollout.
Proposed config: idle_compute_threshold=60s; min_preemption_interval=300s; expose flag as allocator.oom_preempt=false by default for now.
payload.summary: Long-lived keepalive connections from small-stream clients holding GPU slots causing regional capacity squeeze

Issue summary: Beacon Health reports that scheduled cohort alerts tied to a monthly window (30–90 day ranges) stopped triggering after a retention compaction job ran on 2026-03-09. Impact: multiple missed SLO alerts and missing tracehook links in alert digests. Environment: prod (us-east) console and scheduled export pipeline. Urgency: customer has enterprise SLOs tied to these alerts — requires investigation and mitigation.
Customer scheduled cohort query: org=beacon, cohort=monthly_active_users, window=30d-90d
Confirm scheduled alert config in Console > Scheduled Alerts > Beacon Health > monthly_cohort_alert
Wait for scheduled run at 03:00 UTC (daily digest), observe alert did not fire and exported digest has empty tracehook links
Run ad-hoc cohort query from Console for same time range (30–90d) — query returns data and trace links are present when executed manually
Customer-provided digest: digest-2026-03-10-03:00.json (attached) — alert section empty and tracehook fields null
Console scheduler logs: scheduler/us-east/compact-run-2026-03-09.log shows retention compaction completed at 2026-03-09T02:18:43Z
Alerting service logs: alert-eval/us-east/2026-03-10T03:01:12Z WARN 'no series matched after rollup'
Grafana panel: scheduled-job-latency spike during compaction window (link provided by customer)
Initial triage: compaction and rollup jobs run during the customer's scheduled window. Hypothesis: compaction moved high-cardinality route identifiers into archive tier before scheduled alert eval which uses the rollup index, causing sample-filtering to drop cohort series.
Checked scheduler ordering: retention compaction finished at 02:18Z, next scheduled alert eval queued at 03:00Z — sufficient gap, but backfill/reshard job triggered at 02:55Z per logs and may have altered partition ownership.
Queried backend index: found that route_id namespace for org=beacon was compacted and assigned to cold partition with different indexing keys (prefix-truncation applied). This changes tracehook token join key used by scheduled digest export.
Reproduced in staging: ran compaction + scheduled alert run on a copy of Beacon's data; scheduled alert did not match series when rollup index had compaction-truncated keys. Manual ad-hoc query used raw event store and succeeded.
Customer (Elena @ Beacon): We missed three outbound SLO alerts yesterday morning. Can you confirm whether data was deleted or just inaccessible to scheduled alerts?
Support (Maya): Thanks Elena — investigating. Can you attach the scheduled digest you received? Also sharing scheduler and alert logs with engineering. #support
SRE (Luca): Observed retention compaction at 2026-03-09T02:18Z. Noted a reshard job at 02:55Z that likely changed partition mapping. Pushing to eng to validate index-key invariants.
Eng (Arjun): Reproduced locally in staging. Root cause appears to be prefix-truncation applied during compaction which is not compatible with the scheduled-alert join logic that expects full route_id keys. Preparing patch to fallback to raw-key join when scheduled-eval detects compacted-rollup state. See PR linked.
Customer (Elena): Appreciate the quick follow-up. Need ETA for workaround; our compliance team expects notification for missed alerts.
Workaround applied (2026-03-12T09:40Z): scheduled-alert-worker updated to detect 'compacted-rollup' flag and use raw-event fallback join for the next 48 hours for orgs with high-cardinality cohorts. This restored alerts for Beacon on subsequent runs.
Code fix merged to staging: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2294 introduces defensive join behavior and additional telemetry when rollup key normalization is present.
Customer notified: Support sent customer-facing summary and offered a one-time audit of other scheduled alerts that overlap with compaction windows.
Engineering to harden rollup-key compatibility: add migration/compatibility shim to production rollouts (owner: Arjun, due 2026-03-20)
SRE to schedule compaction/reshard windows to avoid peak scheduled-alert times for enterprise customers in us-east (owner: Luca, actioned 2026-03-13)
Product to document recommended guardrails for customers with long-range cohort queries and plan a UX note in scheduling page (owner: Priya, due 2026-03-25)
Support to follow up with Beacon Health on remediation summary and offer 1:1 review (owner: Maya, follow-up 2026-03-14)

payload.description:
Customer: HelioLogic (Dedicated)

Issue summary
- During a planned Dedicated pool expansion in us-east (A100), newly provisioned nodes were successfully allocated and joined the Kubernetes cluster but remained in readiness state "Validating" for >45 minutes, preventing them from joining the serving pool.
- Fleet readiness showed repeated post-provision validation failures/timeouts for the NCCL smoke test step and (in a smaller subset) perf canary step.

Impact
- Capacity shortfall during expansion window; temporary drop in available throughput on the customer’s Dedicated pool.
- No full outage, but elevated queueing/latency as autoscaling could not add the new nodes.

Customer-reported symptoms
- "Pool scale-up initiated but new nodes never become Ready; console shows Validating for an hour+".
- Noted increased p95 latency and occasional request timeouts during peak.

Environment
- prod / us-east
- Dedicated pool: helio-logic-dedicated-a100 (internal pool id: dp-7c1f)
- Image channel at time of failures: candidate (gpu-worker-2025.10.10-candidate)

Timeline (UTC)
- 2025-10-11 16:22: Customer opened ticket reporting expansion delay.
- 2025-10-11 16:34: Support acknowledged; SRE looped in (#incidents, #eng-infra).
- 2025-10-11 17:10: Initial triage: nodes stuck in "Validating" with repeated postflight NCCL failures/timeouts.
- 2025-10-12 00:40: Workaround applied: reimage affected nodes to stable channel + re-run validations.
- 2025-10-13: Engineering root-caused validation agent timeout behavior + flaky NCCL invocation.
- 2025-10-16: Fix merged (PR-18481) and rolled to us-east validation agent.
- 2025-10-18: Ticket resolved after successful expansion retry; no further stuck nodes observed.

Triage notes / Investigation
- Fleet readiness service showed nodes progressing through:
  Allocated -> Provisioning -> JoinedCluster -> Validating
  then repeatedly failing: postflight.nccl_smoketest

- Observed failure modes:
  1) NCCL smoke test: timeout / hang leading to repeated retries without a clear terminal failure reason.
  2) A small subset: perf canary failed due to missing warmup and network jitter (single-digit occurrences; not the majority).

- Dashboards used:
  - Provision-to-ready dashboard: "Step breakdown" for us-east + A100 (Validating step tail latency spike)
  - Failure heatmap by step: postflight.nccl_smoketest dominated failures

- Per-runbook guidance:
  Followed Confluence runbook "Provision-to-ready failures triage" sections:
  - "Validating stuck > 20m"
  - "NCCL smoke test failures"
  - "Safe remediation order: drain -> quarantine (if needed) -> reimage"

Log excerpts (sanitized)
- Validation agent (node-validation-agent) logs:
  2025-10-11T16:58:12Z INFO  step=postflight.nccl_smoketest attempt=1 timeout_s=300 cmd="/opt/redwood/bin/nccl-smoke --allreduce --min-bytes=256M --max-bytes=1G"
  2025-10-11T17:03:13Z WARN  step=postflight.nccl_smoketest result=timeout elapsed_s=301 exit_code=124
  2025-10-11T17:03:13Z INFO  step=postflight.nccl_smoketest attempt=2 backoff_s=5
  2025-10-11T17:08:20Z WARN  step=postflight.nccl_smoketest result=timeout elapsed_s=305 exit_code=124
  2025-10-11T17:08:20Z ERROR step=postflight.nccl_smoketest message="timeout; retrying" node=ip-10-44-18-203

- Fleet readiness state summary (API):
  state=Validating
  last_failed_step=postflight.nccl_smoketest
  failure_reason=VALIDATION_TIMEOUT
  artifacts=s3://redwood-internal-readiness/us-east/dp-7c1f/<node-id>/postflight.nccl_smoketest.log

- Perf canary (subset):
  2025-10-11T18:11:09Z ERROR step=postflight.perf_canary message="p95 > threshold" observed_p95_ms=410 threshold_ms=300 model=llama-3.1-70b

Workaround applied (customer-impact mitigation)
- For nodes stuck in Validating > 20 minutes:
  1) Drain node from k8s (if scheduled)
  2) Reimage to stable image channel: gpu-worker-2025.10.12-stable
  3) Re-run provisioning validations (orchestrator retry)
  4) Only then allow node to join serving pool

- Result:
  Reimaged nodes passed validation and became Ready within ~18 minutes (P95) after reimage.

Root cause
- Validation agent behavior under NCCL test hang/timeout was insufficiently defensive:
  - timeouts were applied, but retries could re-enter the same condition with minimal backoff
  - failure reporting was not consistently persisted, making nodes appear "Validating" rather than failing fast to Quarantined/terminal state

Fix
- Engineering shipped updated validation agent timeouts/retry behavior and improved log bundling and terminal failure signaling:
  - GitHub: PR-18481 ("harden validation agent timeouts and retries")
  - Also leveraged ongoing work to record validation artifacts and failure reasons centrally (PR-18429)

Resolution
- After rolling PR-18481 to us-east and pinning the pool image channel back to stable for expansion, the next expansion attempt completed successfully.
- No new nodes remained stuck in Validating beyond the expected window; NCCL smoke test failure rate returned to baseline.

Customer communication (external)
- We confirmed this was an internal provisioning validation issue impacting scale-up time, not an application-side configuration problem.
- We recommended (and executed on our side) a reimage of affected nodes and a stable image channel pin for the remainder of the expansion.

Follow-ups / Action items
- (Eng) Tune NCCL smoke test parameters for us-east A100 to reduce flakes and avoid long hangs (captured in Linear backlog; referenced in #eng-infra).
- (SRE) Alerting: ensure "Validating stuck" pages only when it correlates with capacity impact; otherwise ticket-only during rollout.
- (Infra) Staged rollout guardrails: keep candidate image channel off for customer expansions unless explicitly approved.

Comments (highlights)
- 2025-10-11 (Support -> SRE): "Seeing 12/20 new nodes stuck in Validating; last_failed_step is NCCL. Any known issue with candidate image?"
- 2025-10-12 (Infra): "Proceeding with reimage to stable; will quarantine repeat offenders after 2 attempts per runbook."
- 2025-10-16 (Eng): "PR-18481 merged; rollout to us-east validation agent tonight, then retry expansion."
- 2025-10-18 (Support): "Customer confirmed expansion completed; closing ticket."

payload.description:
Customer reports that requests from the RAG+Agent Quickstart template fail only when routed through their corporate proxy. Proxy rejects "unknown" request headers; as a result the HTTP request never reaches Redwood (no request-id, no gateway logs).

Issue summary
- When using the Quickstart template defaults (telemetry tagging enabled), requests include one or more template-origin telemetry headers.
- Northbridge’s corporate proxy rejects requests containing unapproved custom headers, returning HTTP 400/431 before the request leaves their network.
- Removing the custom header(s) makes requests succeed immediately.

Impact
- Blocks template evaluation behind corporate network controls.
- Customer perception: Redwood API is down/unreliable (but failures occur upstream of Redwood).
- Limits our ability to use header-based adoption telemetry in enterprise environments.

Environment
- Customer network: corporate proxy with strict header allowlist (exact vendor not disclosed)
- Client: Python quickstart template (internal beta branch per customer)
- Redwood: Hosted API, prod, us-east

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Run template behind corporate proxy (HTTPS interception disabled; standard outbound proxy).
2) Execute template endpoint that triggers LLM call.
3) Observe proxy error: request rejected due to custom header.
4) Manually remove telemetry header(s) and retry.
5) Request succeeds.

Expected
- Template should work behind common enterprise proxies with default configuration.
- Telemetry tagging should not break baseline API calls.

Actual
- Proxy rejects request when template telemetry headers are present. Request never reaches Redwood gateway.

Evidence / logs (sanitized)
- Customer proxy response (reported):
  - Status: 431 Request Header Fields Too Large (sometimes 400 Bad Request)
  - Error text: "Request rejected: header not allowed" / "Unknown header: X-Redwood-Template" (wording varies)
- Redwood side:
  - No corresponding gateway request logs for the timestamp window.
  - No request-id returned.

Investigation notes
- Correlated with internal Slack incident-adjacent thread about telemetry headers causing 4xx in some proxies (see #incidents reference shared by Support).
- This is not a Redwood API failure; it’s a compatibility issue with our telemetry mechanism.
- Header approach is convenient for downstream filtering but fragile with strict proxy/header policies.

Workaround (provided to customer)
- Disable template telemetry headers and rely on standard SDK headers only.
- Template-level change: make telemetry opt-in instead of opt-out.

Decision / resolution
- Decision (DevEx + PM + Gateway): make template-origin telemetry tagging opt-in.
  - Default templates will NOT send template telemetry headers unless explicitly enabled.
  - For customers who want to participate, provide a clear env var toggle and docs section (privacy + compatibility note).
- Gateway will continue to allow/validate a small set of telemetry headers (for opt-in users), but templates should not emit them by default.

Customer-facing guidance (final)
- Set template telemetry to disabled (default in upcoming template release). For current version, remove/disable the header injection.
- If customer later wants telemetry tagging for internal KPIs, coordinate with network/security to allowlist the header(s) or use a non-header mechanism (future enhancement).

Follow-ups
- DevEx: Update Python + TypeScript templates to make telemetry tagging opt-in and document proxy compatibility note.
- Docs: Add troubleshooting entry: "Corporate proxy rejects unknown headers" with fix steps.
- Telemetry/PM: Confirm KPIs still measurable for self-serve users; enterprise adoption metrics may be undercounted by design.

---
Comments / timeline

2025-03-06 09:18 (Priya Shah, Support)
Customer reports 400/431 from corporate proxy when running RAG template. Removing template telemetry header makes it work. Asking Eng whether we can avoid non-standard headers by default.

2025-03-06 10:02 (Owen Phillips, Support)
Confirmed no gateway logs for customer timestamps. Likely request never reaches Redwood. Requested sanitized proxy error message and the exact header name(s) being flagged.

2025-03-06 11:11 (Northbridge Financial)
Proxy blocks unknown headers. The header flagged is "X-Redwood-Template" (exact case may differ). When removed, calls succeed.

2025-03-06 12:30 (Brian Murphy, Eng - API Ergonomics)
If proxy blocks unknown headers, this will keep happening. We can whitelist on our gateway but can’t force customer proxy behavior. Recommendation: make templates not send these headers by default; keep as opt-in.

2025-03-07 09:05 (Monica Patel, DevEx)
Agree. Templates should be production-minded by default; telemetry must not be a footgun. We’ll change default to off and add an env var toggle.

2025-03-07 14:22 (Priya Shah, Support)
Shared workaround with customer: remove template telemetry header injection; continue with standard SDK. Customer unblocked.

2025-03-10 16:40 (Brian Murphy, Eng)
Noted related gateway work to validate/pass a small allowlist of telemetry headers for opt-in usage. Also aligning with DevEx on naming and keeping cardinality low.

2025-03-11 10:15 (Priya Shah, Support)
Closing as resolved: customer has workaround, and product decision made to ship opt-in telemetry in templates + docs update. Tracking template change in DevEx queue and will reference in release notes.

Resolution
- Workaround provided and verified by customer.
- Product decision: telemetry headers from templates will be opt-in going forward to avoid corporate proxy incompatibilities.

Support closure notes
- If customer wants adoption telemetry tagging later, advise them to allowlist the exact header(s) with their proxy/security team, or wait for future non-header tagging approach if shipped.
- If they still see 4xx with headers removed, reopen with request-id + timestamp + region so we can check gateway/serving logs.

Issue summary:
Customer BrightDoc reported repeated requests unexpectedly losing model pin affinity during a staged canary with mirror enabled; pinned sessions were stuck in a stalled state and traffic was routed to the canary mirror variant which later triggered a fallback to a degraded variant, producing mixed outputs and a billing spike.

Impact:
- Multiple BrightDoc tenants experienced mixed model outputs for ~90 minutes.
- Extra compute billed (mirror + fallback) estimated.
- Observed increase in user-facing latency for pinned sessions.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod-us-east)
- Customer tier: enterprise (BrightDoc Health)
- Affected model: redwood-alpha-v2 pinned by tenant route
- Canary configuration: mirror=true, canary_weight=5%, prewarm=true

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Create route with explicit pin to redwood-alpha-v2.
2) Enable canary mirror to new variant redwood-alpha-v2-canary.
3) Send burst of long-lived streaming sessions with custom X-Tenant-Affinity header containing tenant-specific token (>128 chars).
4) Observe that some sessions report pinned version in logs but requests are serviced by mirror then fallback.

Observed behavior:
- Edge logs show X-Tenant-Affinity header being truncated by the edge-proxy (header length limit).
- Orchestrator treats truncated affinity as a new session; mirror path commits a transient pin on the canary shard.
- When mirror health dipped, routing fallback logic rerouted those same requests to a degraded compatibility variant rather than original pinned model.
- Customer saw mixed outputs and a 2x token billing for affected sessions.

Expected behavior:
- Affinity header should be preserved end-to-end or trimmed deterministically such that orchestrator rehydrates existing pin.
- Mirror traffic should not be able to create a persistent pin for tenant sessions unless explicit promote is triggered.

Logs / telemetry pointers:
- Edge proxy traces: edge-proxy-traces/2026-03-10/brightdoc/trace-9987 (header length=128 -> truncated at 96)
- Router telemetry: router.events/tenant=brightdoc/pin-change/2026-03-10
- Serving runtime metrics: serving/runtime/pin-commits: spike coincident with mirror window 03:12-04:45 UTC

Initial hypothesis:
- Edge header normalization has a silent length-cut behavior for unknown headers, causing tenant affinity tokens to be altered.
- Mirror commit path currently accepts pin commitments from mirrored requests if the mirror shares identity metadata, creating a transient but sticky pin in the canary shard.

Immediate workaround given to customer:
- Disable canary mirror for the pinned route OR shorten tenant affinity tokens below the edge header truncation threshold.
- Temporary rate cap for long-lived streams applied on customer route to limit billing impact.

Requested outcome:
- Root-cause fix preventing mirror from committing tenant pins unless promote flag is explicit.
- Edge proxy change to preserve or consistently hash/namespace affinity headers.
- Postmortem and billing remediation for BrightDoc.


Additional notes:
2026-03-10 07:20 UTC - Eng (Liang): Edge-proxy config shows default header size 96 bytes for unknown headers; not applied to standard cookie headers.
2026-03-10 08:05 UTC - Routing team: Mirror commit flow accepts pin-commit events without requiring 'promote' flag when request provenance==mirror; this was an optimization gone wrong.
2026-03-10 07:05 Tomás Rivera (Routing): Found mirror commit path accepts pin commits from mirror traffic. Proposed change: require explicit 'pin_source'==controlplane OR require promote flag for mirror-origin commits.
Disable canary mirror on the affected route OR shorten X-Tenant-Affinity tokens. Temporary rate cap applied to limit billing exposure.
Two contributing faults: 1) Edge-proxy header normalization silently truncating non-standard long affinity header values, changing the identity token. 2) Mirror commit flow allowed mirror-origin requests to create persistent pin entries without an explicit promote signal.
Partial fix deployed: edge-proxy config adjusted to preserve X-Tenant-Affinity up to 256 bytes and routing service patched to ignore pin-commit events originating from mirror traffic unless promote flag present.
Hotfixes: 1) edge-proxy: increased header limit + explicit whitelist for X-Tenant-Affinity. 2) router: added origin check and promote requirement for pin commits (PRs referenced). We plan a follow-up to add automated tests and a canary-blocklist for pin-commits from mirror paths.
Add regression tests for header preservation across edge-proxy variants (owner: Edge)
Add unit/integration tests to prevent mirror-origin pin commits (owner: Routing)
Billing reconciliation: calculate overcharged tokens and issue credit to BrightDoc (owner: Finance/CS)
Postmortem and runbook update: explicitly document pin commit policy for mirror/traffic-mirroring workflows (owner: Platform)

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Prospecta Health reported large numbers of truncated streaming responses and a spike in 5xx errors for requests routed to eu-west beginning 2026-02-26 12:45 UTC. Customers observed partial completions (stream closed mid-token) and increased client disconnects that affected chat and real-time note-generation features.

Impact:
- Affected ~120k requests over a 45-minute window for Prospecta Health (enterprise plan).
- Visible truncated completions for both text generation and function-calling flows.
- Increased retries from customer side led to elevated token counts and billing concerns.

Environment:
- Production (eu-west) serving nodes behind streaming-proxy cluster v2.11.
- Traffic routed to redwood-2.7b-v1 and open-llama-3b model variants.

Timeline (abridged):
- 12:45 UTC: First alert from synthetic monitors (stream-sanity-check) showing partial streams.
- 12:48 UTC: Prospecta Support slack #prospecta-support escalated to Redwood #support with examples.
- 12:50 UTC: SRE acknowledged and opened INC-2026-02-26-03.
- 13:10 UTC: Mitigation: temporarily route Prospecta traffic to warm fallback pool (higher latency but reliable).
- 13:24 UTC: Deploy of streaming-proxy hotfix (rollback of a kernel-selection optimization).
- 13:36 UTC: Observed complete recovery; monitoring returned to baseline by 13:55 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (customer report):
1) Initiate a streaming completion with prompt size ~1.2k tokens using redwood-2.7b-v1 pinned version.
2) Observe intermittent stream termination after ~30-60 tokens on eu-west hosts.
3) Repeating on dedicated capacity did not reproduce; issue was specific to shared eu-west pools.

Observed logs and traces (high level):
- streaming-proxy logs: repeated 'client_keepalive_timeout' and 'stream_flush_incomplete' entries correlated with kernel-selection events.
- serving-runtime traces: high rate of aborted KV-cache reconciliation when requests were migrated across worker threads during late-stage kernel swap.
- API gateway: 502/524 surge for streaming endpoints, 200s for single-request non-stream flows unchanged.

Current status: Resolved. Root-cause fix deployed and validated. Customer notified and billing anomaly under review.

Additional notes:
Initial hypothesis: networking flaps between proxy and worker causing half-closed TCP leading to truncated streams — refuted by stable tcp-level metrics.
Telemetry review: spikes in 'kernel_swap' events coinciding with stream termination events and 'stream_flush_incomplete' errors logged by streaming-proxy (eu-west).
Reproduced in staging with traffic generator when kernel-selection optimization was enabled and worker thread migration occurred under load.
Root cause: a timing window during late-stage kernel selection where the streaming-proxy issued a flush while serving-runtime was migrating KV cache ownership; this could trigger partial chunk flushes and close stream before full completion. The optimization changed ordering of cache handoff and flush acknowledgement.
Evidence: correlated traces from trace-id 2026-02-26-1198 showing flush ack missing for final chunk, and subsequent proxy decision to close connection. Heatmap of events available in Grafana panel 'streaming/flush-latency/eu-west'.
Risk assessment: high for shared pools with high interleaved load and models with longer finalization sequences (e.g., redwood-2.7b-v1). Lower risk on dedicated pools, consistent with customer observations.
Immediate mitigation: route Prospecta Health traffic to the warm fallback pool for eu-west to prevent truncated streams (done 12:50 UTC).
Code fix: removed unsafe reordering in streaming-proxy related to kernel-selection flush timing and added an acknowledgement handshake (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/982).
Rollback/Deploy: rolled back optimization on streaming-proxy v2.11 and deployed patched v2.11.1 at 13:24 UTC; canary passed and cluster promoted at 13:32 UTC.
Monitoring: introduced new alert 'streaming.flush_ack_missing' and Grafana dashboard panel for flush/ack latency by region and model. Added 48h canary watch and 7-day trend retention for flush metrics.
Customer communication: initial incident notification within 30 minutes, full postmortem delivered 2026-02-28. Offered one-time billing credit and assistance in reducing client retry amplification.
ACTION-1: Add unit/integration test that simulates kernel-selection handoff + streaming flush. Owner: Luca Romano. Due: 2026-03-12.
ACTION-2: Update SDK docs with recommended retry/backoff for streaming clients to avoid amplification. Owner: Maya Singh (DX). Due: 2026-03-10.
ACTION-3: Run targeted audit of recent kernel-selection optimizations for similar reordering risks. Owner: Runtime Team. Due: 2026-03-19.
ACTION-4: Confirm billing adjustment for Prospecta with Finance and record credit issuance. Owner: Clara Nguyen (CS) + Rajiv Patel (Finance). Due: 2026-03-07.
ACTION-5: Schedule customer review call (Prospecta technical + account exec) to walk through fix and preventative measures. Owner: Aisha Patel. Due: 2026-03-09.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several customer requests from ScribeHealth during production traffic windows observed long-tail delays (10s-60s) or client-level timeouts. Customer reports intermittent failures while other requests succeed.

Impact: A subset (~0.5-1%) of requests for this customer see token-generation stalls that surface to the client as streaming pauses or total request timeouts. Affects critical clinical summarization flows; customer reported user-facing errors and elevated error rates in their dashboards.

Timeline (local):
- 2026-03-10T09:12Z: First alert from ScribeHealth via support chat (#support).
- 2026-03-10T09:20Z: Support triaged to SRE, initial sample traces requested.
- 2026-03-10T09:35Z: Observed bursts of 429s and elevated queue depths in rate-limiter metrics concurrent with customer retry spikes.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Send high-concurrency streaming requests using SDK v1.12 with default retry/backoff.
2) Observe occasional stream stalls after initial tokens and increased 302/timeout events on client side during 2x-3x traffic bursts.

Observed behavior:
- Server returns soft-429 enforcement in short windows (rate-limiter queueing) rather than hard rejection for some requests; these are exposed as delayed token emission.
- Customer SDK retries are synchronized (no jitter) causing fanout that deepens the queue and increases per-request latency in the window.
- Traces show request accepted by gateway, then waits in rate-limiter queue (approx 200ms-4s) then forwarded; a minority experience multi-second queueing (10s+).

Initial hypothesis: Short soft-throttle windows (burst enforcement with in-memory queueing) combined with client SDKs that retry quickly and in lockstep cause amplification. The amplification pushes requests into longer queue positions producing long-tail latency perceived as timeouts.
Checked api-gateway logs (prod/us-east-1) for sample request IDs; spike window matches customer reported times: 2026-03-10T09:30:00Z-09:38:00Z
Rate-limiter dashboard: token_drain_time and queue_depth metrics show brief spikes; 95th->99.9th percentile drift during window
Serving-runtime traces show most model backends healthy; no model OOMs or kernel errors found
Collected SDK telemetry from ScribeHealth: SDK v1.12 default retry policy retries immediately with linear backoff; no jitter set
Correlation: customer concurrency increased by ~2.8x when their autoscaling launched a batch worker; synchronized startup likely caused initial burst
Sample request IDs: req_20260310_us-3749a, req_20260310_us-3753f, req_20260310_us-3771d (attached logs)
Confirmed similar pattern in internal synthetic load test when running many identical clients without jitter
Link to traces: https://observability.redwood.internal/traces?query=incident=INC-2026-03-10-07

Additional notes:
Short-duration soft 429 enforcement windows combined with synchronized client retries (no jitter) amplified incoming burst, causing elevated queueing and long-tail latency for a small percentage of requests.
Immediate workaround provided to customer: enable randomized exponential backoff (SDK v1.12 config) and throttle client concurrency during peak bursts. Applied temporary quota bump for ScribeHealth to reduce immediate queuing.
Planned fix: rollout server-side soft-throttle debounce and reduce max queue hold time for burst windows; add metrics and alerting to detect synchronized retry patterns. Patch PR: github.com/redwood/inference-runtime/pull/4482.
Postmortem actions: update SDK quickstart to recommend jitter, add a runbook entry on retry-amplification, and create an automated detector for synchronized retries tied to customer-level alerts.
ENG: Deploy soft-throttle debounce across prod by 2026-03-18
DX: Update SDK docs and quickstart to highlight jittered backoff patterns
SRE: Create alert rule for per-customer retry amplification (threshold based on synchronized retry rate)
CS: Schedule a technical review with ScribeHealth to validate production behaviour after fixes
Keep ticket open until server-side debounce is fully rolled out and ScribeHealth confirms stable traffic with no reoccurrences.

Issue summary:
Customer SignalGrid reports a $12,300 unexpected charge on the monthly invoice dated 2026-02-28. The customer says most of their devices were offline for maintenance between 2026-02-20 and 2026-02-22; when devices came back online they uploaded queued inference results which appear to have been metered as new realtime requests instead of being deduplicated or attributed to the original batch window.

Impact:
- Immediate billing dispute: excess charge of ~$12.3k.
- Customer concerned about double-counting and incorrect attribution across regions.

Environment:
- Dedicated account on prod in us-west with burst routing to eu-west.
- Company uses SDK v1.8 with offline buffer and postback endpoint /v1/usage/postback.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Simulate device offline for 48 hours (devices buffer inference results locally).
2) Bring device online; SDK posts queued events to /v1/usage/postback in rapid succession.
3) Observe that metering records each postback as new realtime requests with full token counts (no dedupe).

Customer-provided logs & attachments:
- s3://sg-support-uploads/signalgrid/2026-02/postbacks/manifest.csv
- Screenshot of invoice line items (attached in ticket)
- Example postback HTTP payloads (postback_examples.txt)

Additional notes:
2026-03-01 Customer (SignalGrid - Tara Long): Provided invoice PDF and S3 manifest. Notes that the events show 'queued=true' in the SDK payload but billing still charged full real-time token price. Asked for provisional credit while investigating.
2026-03-04 Customer (SignalGrid - Tara): Confirmed acceptance of provisional credit and requested a short writeup of the fix to share with their finance team.
Metering pipeline analysis (metersrv) shows a spike of 1.45M token events between 2026-02-21 03:00Z and 2026-02-22 08:00Z attributable to org sg-9882. Many events lacked the 'queue-id' header that our dedupe worker expects.
Ingress logs: multiple retries from same device IP with distinct device_event_id values generated by SDK when buffer was flushed; SDK documented behaviour creates a new event_id on each retry causing dedupe miss.
Cross-region attribution: rapid postback fanout routed to eu-west when us-west pool was saturated, which multiplied visibility in billing aggregates due to cross-region multiply-counting in an older aggregator batch job (agg-v2).
Billing aggregation job (agg-v2) had a bug where it did not honor 'queued' flag and applied realtime pricing for all ingestion events when source was 'postback'. A hotfix was deployed to agg-v2 to respect the queued flag and apply batch pricing rules.
Related PRs: metersrv/pull/4123 adds queue-id header processing for dedupe; agg-v2/pull/877 adds queued flag handling; ingestion/pull/221 fixes retry event-id regeneration in SDK v1.8.
Risk assessment: Fix is low-risk, affects only postback processing path. Requires SDK patch release and a short migration notice to customers using offline buffering.
2026-03-03: Provisional credit of $12,300 applied to SignalGrid account (visible in billing UI).
2026-03-04: metersrv hotfix merged (PR #4123) and deployed to prod: dedupe now checks for queue-id and aligns postback retries.

Follow-up actions: Publish guidance for offline buffering SDK best-practices; create a migration notice for SDK v1.8 -> v1.8.1 to avoid event_id regeneration; add telemetry to billing alerts to detect similar postback spikes and auto-flag high-latency queues. Owner: Billing Eng (Ethan). Due: 2026-04-01.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer LuminaDocs reports a large increase in tail latency and occasional timeouts when using the API's JSON_OUTPUT mode to generate large structured documents (40-200KB). The failures started after the customer moved from a simple text template to the new structured schema validation and streaming-json post-processor.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests for one key API route are hitting >5s tail latency, and ~1.8% are returning 504s.
- Customer-facing feature (document generation pipeline) slowed; customers reported degraded UX and timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment for LuminaDocs in prod us-east.
- Request pattern: streaming responses with JSON_OUTPUT, large arrays nested under "pages" and per-item metadata.
- Model variants observed: redwood-open-7b-v2 and community-13b-q4_k with automatic fallback enabled.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) POST /v1/generate with mode=JSON_OUTPUT and schema v2 (embedded validator).
2) Provide prompt that yields ~150-350 tokens per array item and 20-50 items.
3) Enable streaming and client expects newline-delimited chunks that assemble into final JSON object.

Observed behavior:
- Normal throughput for first N-1 chunks, then a pronounced CPU spike on json-decoder workers for the final tokens.
- Streaming connection remains open but no bytes transmitted for ~2-6s before final chunk; sometimes results in HTTP 504.
- Logs show repeated "schema-enforcer: backpressure" traces and decoder retries on final tokenization step.

Expected behavior:
- Smooth streaming with small finalization delay for closing JSON. No long-tail spikes or timeouts.

Preliminary hypothesis:
1) The structured JSON post-processor (schema-enforcer + strict validator) runs a synchronous validation pass that becomes O(n^2) with many nested items, causing final token decode to block and oversubscribe event loop.
2) The streaming assembler waits for the validator to fully parse the buffered chunks before emitting final bytes; when validation stalls, network flush is delayed.
3) Fallback routing may trigger additional model warmups mid-stream (rare) which exacerbates the spike.

Relevant logs and artifacts:
- Customer-provided request ID examples: req_us-1234-20260309a, req_us-1234-20260311b
- Metrics snapshots: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/latency?range=2026-03-09..2026-03-11&customer=LuminaDocs
- Heap/CPU flamegraphs attached by the customer (S3 link): s3://lumina-artifacts/json-decode-spike-20260311.tar.gz

Notes on customer urgency:
- LuminaDocs is a dedicated customer with high-volume daily runs. They requested an update within 48 hours and asked for a mitigation to reduce timeouts.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:15 - Eng on-call (Anika R.) : Confirmed synchronous validator runs during end-of-stream finalize(). Observed lock on decoder's parse mutex for ~2.2s before final bytes flush. Opened internal ticket INT-341 for potential async validator work.
2026-03-11 08:05 - SRE (Tomas): Collected pprof; stack traces show heavy GC and repeated attempt to allocate large transient objects inside schema-enforcer. Memory churn correlates with number of array items.
2026-03-12 10:00 - Performance team: Kernel selection not implicated (same behavior across GPU/CPU-backed instances). Root cause appears computational complexity in streaming validation/assembly step.
Short-term mitigations active for LuminaDocs: 1) Disable strict server-side schema validation for large responses (flag: json_validators.strict=false) — customer accepted for now. 2) If strict validation is required, recommend client-side validation: request raw TEXT stream + client performs schema check. 3) Route heavy requests to a model variant with lower per-token overhead (community-13b-q4_k showed similar but slightly better behaviour).
Mitigation applied 2026-03-11: disabled strict validator for the affected customer route and increased request timeout to 12s for a rolling 24h window. Monitoring configured to alert if >1% servers hit >3s finalization delay. Engineering next steps: implement async validation pipeline that validates chunks incrementally and emit final bytes without blocking event loop; target PR and benchmark by 2026-03-20. Linked internal task INT-341 created to track implementation details.
2026-03-11 15:20 - LuminaDocs (Kevin M.): Noted improvement after we disabled strict validation. Small number of outputs still appear with slow tail (~1/1000). Customer requests permanent fix timeline.
2026-03-12 09:10 - Anika R. (Eng on-call): Added INT-341 and initial design notes. Async incremental validator sketch posted to PR thread: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3189

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a recent scheduled reindex, the rerank endpoint returns non-deterministic top-K results for identical queries, and they observe long-tail latency spikes (95th/99th percentile) on rerank calls. This first appeared after a bulk reindex job completed on 2026-03-08.

Impact:
- Affects production search quality for LexSearch customers (some queries return different top results on subsequent identical requests).
- Intermittent latency spikes up to 2–3x baseline on rerank endpoint, causing timeouts in downstream application flow.
- Behavior persists even when requests are pinned to the same model and replica.

Environment / Context:
- Customer uses Dedicated capacity in us-east-1 with pinned embedding model embed-large-v2 and rerank model rerank-small-v1.
- Bulk reindex job executed against their namespace (ns: lex-articles) using our indexer service; reindex used the offline batch-worker fleet with version tag indexer-2026-03-07.
- Embeddings were generated as part of the reindex; embedding payloads show expected dimension (1536) and types (float32), but similarity scores vary between requests.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Send identical search query payloads (same prompt, same rerank params) to rerank endpoint 3x spaced 10s apart.
2) Observe top-K list differs between calls ~30% of the time for certain queries.
3) Observe 95th/99th percentile latency increase correlated with mismatched top-K sets.

Observed logs/snippets (customer provided):
- Rerank request IDs: rr-20260308-abc123, rr-20260308-def456
- Timestamps show occasional GPU fallback to CPU path (serving-runtime: fallback=cpu, reason=\"kv-cache-miss-random\")
- Indexer logs during reindex: \"seed: unset; using system RNG\" and later \"completed batch 42/421\"

Customer workaround in place:
- Customer rolled back to previous index snapshot (pre-reindex) which removed nondeterminism for several hours. When re-running the reindex with the same job parameters, issue reappears randomly.

Desired outcome:
- Deterministic rerank results for identical inputs when underlying index and models are unchanged.
- Eliminate long-tail latency spikes and reduce CPU fallbacks tied to this issue.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 - Customer (LexSearch Technical Lead): Provided reindex job manifest and two sample request IDs. Confirmed that reindex was started at 2026-03-08T03:12:00Z and completed at 2026-03-08T07:45:00Z.
2026-03-11 - Customer: Requested ETA for permanent remediation and confirmation that future reindexes will not introduce nondeterminism.
Hypothesis 1: Indexer run omitted deterministic seed and inadvertently used a model image that executed stochastic ops (training-mode or non-deterministic kernels), producing micro-variance across embeddings leading to different top-K ordering for borderline candidates.
Hypothesis 2: KV cache keying uses a checksum of embedding bytes; small embedding variance causes cache misses triggering CPU fallback path for certain rerank requests, adding long-tail latency.
Evidence: Local reproduction showed top-K flips when reindex run omitted --seed and when model checkpoint was instantiated without eval flag. Profiling of rerank path shows increased CPU fallback rate correlated with cache-miss logs.
Telemetry: Increased 95th/99th latency for rerank endpoint correlated to reindex completion window in customer namespace. No global region-wide spike observed.
Action: Added temporary guarding to indexer orchestration to require explicit --seed and --model-mode=eval; added logging of seed and model flags to job metadata.
Root cause: Offline reindex job ran multiple batch-worker variants; one variant invoked the embedding model in a non-deterministic mode (training-like ops) and indexer orchestration omitted a fixed RNG seed.
