payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long-form streaming responses never reach a terminal state in their web client when connecting from within their corporate network. The SDK shows partial output and then remains in a streaming state — no 'done' or stream-complete callback is fired.

Impact: Customer's in-product chat feature appears to hang for ~30% of sessions originating from ClearSight Analytics' office subnets. Affects enterprise production users; vendor escalated to enterprise SLA.

Environment: Hosted Redwood API (prod) serving gpt-redwood-v1 to customer via web SDK. Customer traffic flows through a corporate TLS inspection device (commercial TLS proxy) in front of a transparent gateway. Reproduced from a machine on the same network and traced through the customer's proxy logs.

Steps to reproduce:
1) In Chrome desktop, load web client that uses redwood-js-sdk streaming chat.
2) Initiate a streaming generate call (large response, ~1200 tokens).
3) Observe tokens arriving for ~1–2s then client stops firing 'delta' events and never fires 'done' callback.
4) Using local curl to /v1/streams endpoint from inside network shows final JSON payload on wire but client remains open.

Observed behavior: Server-side access logs and packet captures show the final JSON end-of-stream frame is sent. However, the client's framing logic does not detect stream termination. Captured bytes include an unexpected 0x00 (null) byte appended to the final WebSocket/SSE frame in the customer's network path.

Expected behavior: Final frame should be delivered without stray control bytes; client should emit terminal event and close the logical stream.

Initial logs & attachments: Attached excerpts of tcpdump from customer (anonymized), server access logs (request ids), and SDK-side debug logs. Packet capture shows final chunk ends with '}\n' but with an extra 0x00 trailing byte after the newline.

Temporary workaround given: Instructed customer to bypass TLS inspection for Redwood endpoints (policy exception) which immediately resolves the symptom. Also provided a short-lived SDK patch they could deploy to their web client to ignore trailing null bytes until server fix rolled out.

Additional notes:
2026-02-18 14:40 - Customer (ClearSight NetOps): Provided TLS appliance logs: vendor TLSGuard v6.4.1; appliance shows it performed a re-wrap and added a low-level binary padding for segmentation alignment. They deny application-level modification.
Hypothesis 1: Serving runtime omitted closing delimiter — rejected after packet captures show server bytes include closing marker.
Hypothesis 2: Downstream TLS device injects alignment padding (null bytes) after final TLS record. Confirmed by customer's TLS appliance logs and recreated with local injector.
Reproduction: Built a local test harness that wraps outgoing SSE frames and appends 0x00. JS SDK behavior: parser waits for explicit newline+EOF but treats trailing 0x00 as non-terminator, leaving stream open. Node and browser SDKs differ slightly in trimming behavior.
Logs: r-98a3f2 trace shows final SSE event payload, Content-Length and chunking consistent. Edge logs prior to fix show identical payload; pcap shows extra null before TCP FIN from customer's proxy.
Root cause: Transparent TLS inspection device (TLSGuard v6.4.1) in customer's network path appended a single null (0x00) byte to the final application-level frame during re-encryption/segmentation. The JS SDK's stream parser treated that byte as stray binary data and did not consider the stream terminated. Fixes: 1) Serving-runtime updated to normalize and strip trailing control bytes from outgoing streaming frames (PR #1398). 2) JS SDK patched to treat trailing 0x00 as ignorable and to emit stream terminal event if valid end payload has been received (PR #412). 3) Customer guidance: request TLS inspector vendor to disable post-rewrite binary padding for known streaming endpoints or add an allowlist. Outcome: Customer upgraded SDK and confirmed no recurrence after runtime and SDK patches were deployed to us-east edge nodes. Follow-ups: add synthetic tests for trailing control bytes in CI, and add an item to runbook "stream-trailing-bytes".
Add CI test that injects stray 0x00/0xFF bytes to end-of-stream cases to prevent regressions
Coordinate with Trust & Safety to add known TLS appliance interference patterns to troubleshooting guide
Reach out to ClearSight NetOps in 30 days to confirm long-term stability and vendor remediation
payload.summary: Streaming session never finalizes for customer behind enterprise TLS inspector (trailing null byte injected)

Issue summary: Customer (Lyra Health, Dedicated) reports increased proportion of requests routed to degraded fallback variant during a scheduled canary mirror update. Impact: ~6% of tenant traffic observed returning responses from the degraded variant without explicit pin loss; customer reports increased latency and reduced quality. Symptoms surfaced after a mirror prewarm operation coinciding with a canary weight shift.
Customer-critical: affects production traffic for multiple endpoints. Observed increased 5xx fallback rates and 30-150ms higher p95 latency for affected tenants.
1) Configure a weighted canary rollout with traffic mirror prewarm enabled for model redwood-v2-small.
2) Start a dedicated capacity prewarm on pool DED-US-EAST-3 while pushing a small canary weight (5%).
3) Trigger tenant traffic with consistent session-affinity tokens and long-lived streaming sessions.
4) Observe cohort pin mapping and fallback routing in edge-proxy logs; note occasional silent diversion to degraded variant without explicit unpin event.
edge-proxy[2026-03-12T15:21:42Z] tenant=lyra-001 route=api.chat model=redwood-v2-small routed_to=variant-degraded reason=fallback_path_no_unpin
cohort-reconciler[2026-03-12T15:21:42Z] reconcile_id=abc123 prewarm_mirror=true cohort=pin-cohort-42 status=commit_delayed
orchestrator[2026-03-12T15:21:43Z] pool=DED-US-EAST-3 prewarm_attach=mirror session_affinity=kept cache_kv_mismatch=true
serving-runtime[2026-03-12T15:21:45Z] kvcache_hit=false warmup_inflight=2 fallback_trigger=rate_limit_smoothing
Initial triage: Mirroring/prewarm and cohort commit overlapped. We see a commit_delayed on cohort-reconciler when mirror attach completed; edge-proxy saw requests with cohort cookie but orchestrator had partial snapshot, causing routing decision to consult fallback path rather than honor pin.
Hypothesis 1: Prewarm mirror attach merges a shadow snapshot that does not include latest pin binding; if cohort commit is delayed, edge uses legacy mapping plus fallback policy (degraded variant).
Hypothesis 2: KV-cache mismatch (cohort-level KV) leads serving-runtime to mark session as stale and route to degraded fallback even though pin exists at control-plane—timing window where control-plane and edge disagree.
Observed: Approximately 4-7% of requests from Lyra tenants in the affected pool hit degraded variant for 2-5 minutes after mirror attach events. No explicit unpin was recorded in audit logs.
Metrics: spike in fallback_rate metric (fallback_rate.tenant.lyra-001) from 0.3% -> 6.2% at 2026-03-12T15:21Z; cohort_commit_latency spiked to 18s for the prewarm cycle.
Related signals: increased prewarm_attach_latency, orchestrator-snapshot-merge errors (transient), edge cache TTL expiration aligned with spike.
Race condition between mirror prewarm snapshot merge and cohort pin commit. Edge proxy resolves routing before cohort commit completes; due to KV-cache state mismatch the request is routed to a fallback/degraded variant despite control-plane pin still pending commit.
1) Force cohort reconcile for affected tenant (api: POST /internal/cohort/reconcile?tenant=lyra-001) to reapply pin snapshot. 2) Temporarily disable prewarm-mirror for scheduled canary windows for this customer's pool. 3) For affected requests, customer can set explicit model override in route header (x-redwood-model: redwood-v2-small) until fix is deployed.
Short term: Add guard in orchestrator to delay mirror snapshot activation until cohort commit ack received (rollback window 30s).
Medium term: Instrument additional consistency checks in edge-proxy to prefer committed pin mapping over fallback when commit_timestamp within 60s of mirror event.
Long term: Remove the shared shadow-snapshot path between mirror and commit; switch to atomic snapshot swap for pin metadata.
Owner: orchestrator team; PR being prepared to add commit ack gate.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 16:20 - Engineering (serving-runtime): Found kvcache validation returns stale when prewarm attaches shadow index; investigating adding validation on attach path.
2026-03-12 17:05 - Product (RP): Agreed to disable mirror prewarm by default for dedicated pools for next 48 hours for safety; coordinated with CS to inform customers.
Hotfix gate deployed to delay mirror activation until cohort commit ack for canary prewarm flows. Immediate workaround applied (cohort reconcile) for Lyra Health. Engineering roadmap item opened to implement atomic snapshot swap for pin metadata. Customer notified and monitoring continues for 24h before closure.
1) Engineering to complete atomic snapshot change - target sprint 2026-03-27.
2) Update Canary prewarm runbook with risk checklist and gating rules.
3) Notify Dedicated customers with prewarm enabled about temporary behavioral change and opt-in to mirror prewarm after fix.
4) Add automated alert when cohort_commit_latency > 10s during prewarm cycles.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports that several alert notifications did not fire for a high-severity error alert that is anchored to trace links. The anchor matching step in alert evaluation fails when trace link IDs contain unescaped characters (examples: pipe '|' or raw slashes) or are double-encoded in the trace link parameter.

Impact:
- Missed P1 alerts for BrightCart for ~2.5 hours on 2026-03-09 in us-east.
- Customers relying on trace-anchored alerts (click-to-trace) see no alert and cannot link to the trace from the notification.
- Affects any alert using trace_anchor() in the console when anchor contains characters like '|' or a pre-encoded '%2F'.

Environment:
- Prod: us-east region, console v3.12.1 evaluation engine, anchor-normalizer service v1.8.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create an alert with a condition that auto-links to a trace using trace_anchor(trace_id) in the notification template.
2) Trigger a trace with an ID that contains a pipe character (generated by internal tracing library): e.g., trace_id = "abc|def". The console stores/links traces as trace_id URL param encoded: trace_id=abc%7Cdef.
3) Observe alert eval logs and notification output.
4) Re-run with a trace id containing a literal slash or a pre-encoded slash (%2F) in the URL param.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Alert eval logs show: "anchor_lookup: returned 0 rows for key 'abc%7Cdef'" while trace index contains row for key 'abc|def'.
- Anchor-normalizer service logs include: "WARN: unexpected-percent-encoding: '%25' found in anchor-string'" when double-encoded values are passed.
- Notifications were not emitted; traces are visible in console but not linked from alerts.

Investigation notes:
- Root cause hypothesis: mismatch between how trace anchors are stored/indexed (raw/unescaped) and how alert-eval pipeline queries them (URL-encoded or double-encoded). The anchor-normalizer attempts to canonicalize, but does not handle a mixture of raw pipes and pre-encoded sequences (e.g., incoming trace URLs from BrightCart's proxy are sometimes encoded twice).
- Reproduced locally with a test trace that contains '|' -> confirmed alert eval fails to match when the alert engine receives the encoded string.
- Quick grep through service code shows alert-eval constructs lookup keys using request.query.trace_id without a final decode pass. Unit tests for anchor_normalizer cover simple encodings but not double-encoded or pipe-containing IDs.
- Related behavior referenced in SUP-42188 (sessionized-usage-splitting) and SUP-246381 (alert-links-drop-on-ad-hoc-query-rewrite) but root cause differs: this is an encoding normalization mismatch in alert path.

Next steps / proposed fix:
- Short term (workaround): add a deterministic decode/normalize step in alert-eval plumbing that attempts 1x decode and fallback 2x decode before lookup. Document and release as a hotfix to console v3.12.2.
- Medium term: add unit/integration tests covering pipe and double-encoded anchors and add canonicalization logic to anchor-normalizer service.
- Longer term: add a telemetry metric for anchor lookup miss-rate and an alert when miss-rate > 0.5% for 15m.

Support provided a temporary workaround: BrightCart updated their webhook to send raw trace IDs (no double-encoding) and support created a per-organization alert template that strips percent-encoding before calling trace_anchor(). For customers that cannot change webhook behavior, we deployed a hotfix (console edge) that attempts a second decode before lookup. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4321
SRE reproduction steps, logs, and test cases created. Local repro confirmed that alert-eval fails when lookup key is encoded (abc%7Cdef) while index contains abc|def. Anchor-normalizer currently applies single url-decode; needs fallback to handle double-encoded strings and to treat '|' as a valid stored key. Traces ingestion code historically retained raw id; newer proxies perform encoding which led to mismatch.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 BrightCart (Customer) via email: We can temporarily change our webhook payload if that speeds up resolution. Please advise recommended format.
payload.summary: Alert evaluation suppressed when trace-anchor URLs contain unescaped characters (pipe, slash)

Issue summary:
Customer AuroraPay reports that during a scheduled canary rollout (weight 10% -> 25%), they observed a subset of long-lived sessions get silently rebound to an earlier pinned model after an edge prewarm event. This produced mixed output quality for affected sessions and triggered our fallback paths for about 2% of requests from the customer region.
Approximately 2% of AuroraPay's production requests during the window returned responses from a legacy pinned variant (redwood-xl-v1) instead of the intended canary variant (rw-instruct-3b-quant). Customers reported degraded prompt alignment for multi-turn invoices processing. No PII exposure. Revenue impact limited but SLA risk (latency and correctness).
2026-03-12T22:17Z - AuroraPay alerts via support channel about mixed model outputs.
2026-03-12T22:22Z - Support opens ticket and escalates to SRE.
2026-03-12T22:30Z - SRE observes spike of edge prewarm activity in us-west and concurrent orchestrator epoch sync.
2026-03-12T22:45Z - Initial mitigation: temporarily hold canary weight increase and enable stricter pin-cohort checks.
2026-03-12T23:50Z - Partial rollback for affected cohort performed while investigation continues.
1) Configure a tenant with a pinned model variant (pin policy: tenant-level sticky pin).
2) Start a canary rollout for a compatible variant with weight increments.
3) Trigger rapid prewarming on edge (simulated by burst of prewarm probes across 4 edge nodes).
4) Simultaneously induce orchestrator epoch sync by pushing a snapshot (fast commit).
5) Observe session affinity rebind logs and compare model hash served to client session tokens.
Sessions that have an active pin should remain bound to their pinned variant unless an explicit unpin or TTL expiry occurs. Prewarm and orchestrator sync events should not force rebinds for active sessions.
A narrow cohort of long-lived sessions (session age > 10 minutes, streaming connections with keepalive) had their session affinity re-evaluated during the orchestrator epoch merge triggered at the same time as edge prewarm probes. The re-evaluation path incorrectly accepted a stale routing snapshot from an edge node that had not applied the tenant's latest pin-safety metadata, resulting in a rebind to the legacy variant. Fallback logic then attempted to correct output quality, causing additional routing churn.
Representative log snippets (timestamps truncated):
- edge-proxy/us-west-2: prewarm-probe id=pmn-42 latency=18ms snapshot-version=1704
- orchestrator: epoch-merge start id=eph-991 snapshot=1704
- affinity-manager: session=tn-21014 token=tok-xx aff-check=stale -> allow_rebind=true source=edge-us-west-2
- serving-runtime: request id=req-448 model=redwood-xl-v1 hash=0x7a8b
- customer: request id=req-448 responded variant=redwood-xl-v1 expected=rw-instruct-3b-quant
Correlation: edge node 3 reported snapshot 1704 while control-plane considered 1706 as canonical. Affinity-manager accepted the lower snapshot during a short race window.
Hypothesis: race between orchestrator snapshot commit and edge prewarm delivered inconsistent snapshot versions to affinity-manager. Affinity-manager's safety check has a compare that treats missing pin-safety labels as permissive under high prewarm load (optimizing for faster ramp), which allowed rebinds.
Evidence:
- Snapshot versions diverged for ~90 seconds; edge nodes reported older snapshot.
- Affinity-manager code path 'shallow_check' was exercised (trace found via trace-id=tr-99284).
- Customers with long-lived streaming sessions more likely to hit the code path due to periodic affinity re-eval.
Reproducible in staging with orchestrator latency artificially increased and simultaneous prewarm bursts.
Next steps: repro in dedicated staging, add additional logging around pin-safety labels, and review shallow_check permissiveness under race conditions.
Affinity re-evaluation logic accepted stale edge snapshots during an orchestrator epoch merge. The permissive 'shallow_check' code path lacked a strict snapshot-version gating when pin-safety metadata was missing on the edge node, allowing rebinds for active sessions under prewarm load.
Mitigations applied:
- Immediate: reverted the canary weight increase and forced edge snapshot refresh for us-west. Rolled back affected cohort to previous stable routing to eliminate mixed outputs.
- Short-term hotfix: added snapshot-version gating to affinity-manager shallow_check (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/6210) to require edge snapshot >= control-plane snapshot for pin-sensitive re-evals.
- Verification: ran staging reproduction tests with concurrent prewarm and epoch sync; no rebinds observed across 10k simulated sessions.
- Rollout plan: staged rollout of hotfix to us-west with canary weight frozen for 2 maintenance windows, monitor pin-affinity metrics and error rates.
Follow-ups: augment canary runbook to avoid aggressive prewarm bursts during orchestrator commits; add monitoring alert when snapshot version skew > 1 for >30s.
1) Code: enforce snapshot-version checks in affinity-manager and add unit tests for re-eval race.
2) Runbook: update Canary Routing Runbook to include prewarm coordination with orchestrator commits.
3) Monitoring: create Grafana alert for edge/control-plane snapshot skew > 1 for 30s.
4) Customer follow-up: provide AuroraPay a brief timeline and confirm no further impact; offer optional extended logging for next 48h.
5) Cross-team: schedule a 1-hour retro with Orchestrator, Edge, and Affinity teams.
Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-12T22:24: Logged initial customer description and captured sample request IDs. Notified SRE on #support-escalations.

SRE (Miguel Ortega) 2026-03-12T22:35: Observed snapshot mismatch between control-plane and edge nodes. Applied temporary hold on canary weight increase and requested edge nodes to refresh snapshot immediately.

Customer (AuroraPay - Emma Li) 2026-03-12T22:40: Shared two request IDs with inconsistent outputs and confirmed that sessions were long-lived streaming clients. Customer requests mitigation ASAP; noted that rollback restored expected outputs for affected session IDs.

Eng (Ravi Sharma) 2026-03-13T03:10: Found code path in affinity-manager where missing 'pin-safety' header causes permissive rebind during heavy prewarm. Pushed hotfix branch for additional snapshot version gating. PR referenced below.

SRE (Miguel Ortega) 2026-03-13T08:05: Deployed hotfix to staging and ran controlled prewarm/orchestrator sync test. No rebinds observed in staging. Planning controlled rollout to prod after verification window.

Issue summary:
Customer QueryWell reported a rapid increase in 5xx responses starting 2026-03-12 10:20 UTC for production traffic routed to their dedicated pool. Symptoms include API gateway 502/503 spikes coincident with long-lived streaming connections from a handful of client IPs. Upstream runtimes entered crashloop/eviction cycles and GPU memory fragmentation grew steadily during the window.

Impact:
- QueryWell observed ~18% of requests returning 5xx over a 40-minute period, primarily streaming endpoints.
- Latency increased for non-streaming requests by ~30%.
- Incident impacted a single dedicated pool (customer-dedicated) — no cross-customer outage reported.

Environment:
- prod/us-east (customer dedicated capacity)
- Affected runtimes: r10-r16 in dedicated pool qwe-us-east-02
- Models in use: redwood-alpha-13b-q4 (inference with KV cache and streaming enabled)

Steps to reproduce (as observed):
1) Customer opens many long-lived streaming sessions (keepalive) from ~8 client hosts.
2) Several sessions are not cleanly closed (client-side abrupt disconnects), leaving half-open streams.
3) API gateway accept queue depth climbs; accept-queue backlog growth is visible on edge metrics.
4) Serving runtime experiences elevated socket backlog and increases memory fragmentation; GPU allocator hits fragmentation threshold causing occasional out-of-memory reclamation and process restart.
5) Upstream restarts cause immediate 502/503 responses until new workers spin up and prefetch completes.

Observed logs / metrics snippets:
- apigw.accept_queue_depth spike to 962 at 2026-03-12T10:26Z
- edge.stream_sessions.active (customer-dedicated) increased from 120 -> 840 in 12 minutes
- runtime.gpu.fragmentation_pct rising from 12% -> 68% before evictions
- runtime.process.exit_reason: OOM_RECLAIM at 2026-03-12T10:33Z
- apigw.5xx_rate customer-dedicated: baseline 0.2% -> 18%

Attachments: collected tcpdump (partial), apigw and runtime graphs, sample logs from runtime r13, client connection list exported by edge service.
10:28 UTC - Support acknowledged customer signal and opened incident; triage to SRE and Runtime oncall.
10:35 UTC - Observed tight correlation between long-lived streams and accept-queue growth; single customer IP range responsible for ~65% of long-lived sessions.
10:45 UTC - Runtime oncall identified repeated gpu allocator OOM_RECLAIM cycles; worker restarts coincident with apigw 502 spikes.
11:00 UTC - Hypothesis: incomplete client shutdowns + aggressive keepalive behavior caused accept-queue starvation which increased per-worker socket state and prevented normal KV cache warmup, gradually fragmenting GPU memory and triggering OOM reclamation.
11:12 UTC - Validated via heapmaps and nvml counters: fragmentation increased in affected runtimes, unaffected runtimes in same zone stayed stable.
11:25 UTC - Applied temporary ingress mitigation: limited concurrent streaming sessions per-customer-IP and increased apigw accept queue threshold; observed immediate reduction in new half-open streams.
12:00 UTC - After mitigation, runtime restarts frequency dropped and 5xx rate declined to ~1.8% within 35 minutes.
Next steps: implement longer-term circuit (backpressure + client throttling), add detection alert for per-customer long-lived stream explosion, and coordinate with QueryWell to patch client behavior.

Ava Chen (Support) 2026-03-12 10:30 UTC: Initial customer report attached tcpdump and said errors started after a traffic ramp of streaming sessions.
Samir Rao (SRE) 2026-03-12 10:38 UTC: Looking at apigw metrics now; accept_queue_depth is spiking. Routing to runtime oncall @Raj.
Raj Patel (Runtime oncall) 2026-03-12 10:46 UTC: Found repeated OOM_RECLAIM in r13 and r14; collecting nvml and allocator traces. Suspect fragmentation from many small persistent tensors in streaming session lifecycle.
Customer (QueryWell) 2026-03-12 11:05 UTC: Their SDK opened persistent streams to support interactive dashboarding; confirmed a recent client-side SDK update that changed reconnect semantics.
Raj Patel 2026-03-12 11:28 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied (ingress concurrent-stream cap and accept-queue tuning). Seeing 5xx rate trending down.
Ava Chen 2026-03-12 12:05 UTC: Shared mitigation steps and timeline with customer; they will revert the SDK change and re-test. Will monitor for 24 hours.
Support note 2026-03-13 09:00 UTC: Follow-up requested to implement alerting for long-lived stream spikes and a runtime patch to compact small allocator fragments more aggressively on restart.
Workaround applied: per-IP concurrent streaming cap and accept-queue threshold increase reduced the new half-open streams; customer rolled back the SDK change that left sessions half-open. Runtime restarts declined and 5xx rate dropped to near-baseline in ~35 minutes.

Planned permanent fix: (1) introduce an automated per-tenant streaming explosion detection and ingress backpressure rule; (2) runtime change to defragment allocator proactively during low-traffic windows and add a safety eviction path before OOM_RECLAIM; (3) update runbook with client SDK guidance.

Follow-ups assigned: Raj to author runtime PR for allocator defrag (ETA 2 weeks), SRE to add alert and playbook (ETA 3 days), Support to coordinate with QueryWell on client SDK best-practices (ETA 1 day).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (MonetaBank) reports repeated duplicate audit events in their SIEM ingestion (Splunk) for a subset of webhook-delivered activity ledgers over a 48h window. The customer requires a signed evidence bundle enumerating delivered batches, per-batch checksums, resume tokens, and retention metadata to support a regulatory case and reconcile their retention policy enforcement.

Impact:
- Duplicate events seen in Splunk causing false positives in SOC alerts and inflated storage costs.
- Customer's compliance team has raised an escalation with legal; they require cryptographically verifiable delivery records for a specific 36-hour window (2026-03-09 16:00 UTC to 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC).
- P1 due to enterprise SLA and potential regulatory audit.

Timeline & Observed Behavior:
1) 2026-03-09 16:10 UTC - MonetaBank support reports an increase in duplicate event counts for tenant moneta-prod-1 (reported via #support-moneta slack).
2) Customer provided Splunk ingest statistics showing repeated event_id hashes and a rising dedup metric at index time.
3) On our side, webhooks to their HEC endpoint show successful 200 responses from the customer gateway with occasional 5xx responses upstream during the window.
4) Resumption tokens for some batches are identical across two deliveries and batch manifests show overlapping sequence ranges.

Steps to reproduce (support-side):
1) Retrieve delivery logs for tenant moneta-prod-1 for 2026-03-09 15:50 - 2026-03-10 05:00 UTC.
2) Filter audit-export events by delivery_id and sequence_range; identify any overlapping ranges or duplicate resume_token values.
3) Correlate our delivery manifest with the customer's HEC ack timestamps.

Attachments customer provided:
- Splunk index count CSV (split by hour)
- Sample of duplicated events (3 examples)
- HEC ingest timestamps and indexer GUIDs

Expected behavior:
- Each audit batch delivered once; resume tokens unique per batch; manifests contain non-overlapping sequence ranges.

Customer asks:
- Signed evidence bundle (per-batch manifest, sha256 checksums, resume tokens, RFC3161 timestamps) for the window specified.
- Short-term mitigation suggestion to prevent further duplicates (ingest-side dedupe guidance + temporary backoff settings).

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 08:10 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer confirmed they are seeing fewer duplicates after we suggested enabling Splunk dedup at index_time as a temporary measure. They still need the signed bundle for the window.
Collected delivery manifests for moneta-prod-1 for the full window; found 7 batches where sequence ranges overlapped by one or two messages.
Scheduler logs show two code paths that can trigger a retry: 'latency_requeue' and 'delivery_error_retry'. In 5 of 7 overlapping batches the requeue was triggered by 'latency_requeue' and the in-memory marker that prevents duplicate activation was not persisted due to a transient memcache timeout.
Resume_token generation uses (tenant,shard,epoch,seq_range)-based hashing. In the race we observed, the second delivery reused the same derived resume_token because seq_range calculation used end-exclusive semantics; off-by-one in the rounding produced identical tokens for the overlapping runs.
Customer HEC acks were 200 for both deliveries in 4 cases; in 3 cases the customer's gateway returned 502 for the first attempt and 200 for the retry, which explains why customer index shows duplicates when both deliveries were ultimately accepted by their downstream indexer.
No evidence of malicious replays or third-party resend. All deliveries originated from our scheduler with identical client_cert subjects (pinned).
Immediate workaround provided: advise customer to enable index-time deduplication in Splunk for event_id and to apply a 5-minute sliding window dedupe to suppress transient duplicate spikes.
Short-term mitigation implemented by infra: patched scheduler to persist 'delivery-activation' markers to redis before enqueuing a retry; deployed 2026-03-13 02:18 UTC (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2147). This prevents the race that created overlapping active manifests.
Long-term fix: updated resume_token derivation to include monotonic delivery UUID and made seq_range semantics end-inclusive consistently. Rollout plan: canary in us-east for 48h then global. Related PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2150.
Evidence bundle contents delivered to customer: per-batch manifest (JSON), sha256 checksums, RFC3161-signed timestamp bundle (via HSM), delivery traces (truncated), and a signed manifest index. Uploaded to secure S3 presigned URL: https://s3.redwood-internal/moneta/evidence/SUP-583214-bundle-20260314.tar.gz (link delivered via customer-only channel).
Follow-ups: create a support runbook for 'watermark-drift' incidents, add synthetic test to verify resume_token uniqueness under retry, and schedule postmortem with SRE/CS/Customer on 2026-03-18.
Status: evidence delivered and customer acknowledged receipt. Work items remain open for the long-term rollout and runbook (tracked in INT-4421 and INT-4488).

Issue summary:
At ~2026-03-10 13:20 UTC HydraNet (enterprise customer, heavy EOD ingest) observed a sudden throughput collapse on our hosted endpoint with a concurrent surge in 5xx responses and streaming connection churn. Customer-facing symptom: stalled streaming responses and partial transcripts, causing downstream ingestion failures for HydraNet's reconciliation pipeline.

Impact:
- Duration: ~13:20 UTC to 15:05 UTC (services gradually recovered after mitigation).
- Affected keys: HydraNet production account only (single-customer outage).
- Observable metrics: request success rate dropped to 64% at the peak; median token latency increased from 60ms to 450ms; streaming disconnects increased by 8x.
- Business impact: HydraNet reported delayed reconciliation jobs and customer SLAs missed for two internal teams.

Detection timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 13:18 UTC: Automatic SLO alert — sustained tail latency increase for prod us-east serving runtime.
- 13:20 UTC: HydraNet support message escalated to #support and #incidents.
- 13:28 UTC: On-call SRE triage — observed GPU pool evictions and autoscaler churn.
- 13:35 UTC: Streaming subsystem began reporting protocol-level disconnects correlated with high write latencies to KV cache.
- 14:05 UTC: Engineering confirmed a recently deployed kernel-selection optimization (serving-runtime PR 7421) had started rolling at 13:10 UTC and coincided with increased memory pressure on certain model variants.
- 14:25 UTC: Temporary routing change applied for HydraNet to reserved spillover capacity; errors and disconnects dropped noticeably.
- 15:05 UTC: Rollback of kernel-selection rollout and autoscaler headroom increase completed; service metrics returned to baseline.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Simulate HydraNet workload pattern: long prompt prefixes with many concurrent streams (~180 concurrent long-poll streams) and high token emission.
2) Push the kernel-selection optimization and observe memory/KV pressure under sustained concurrent prefix reuse.
3) Monitor autoscaler reaction and GPU pool eviction rates.

Logs & artifacts:
- Obs dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/serving/hydranet-20260310
- Kernel rollout PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/7421
- Autoscaler changelog PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/198
- Sample log snippets captured in S3: s3://redwood-incidents/2026/223456/log-snippets.txt

Investigation notes (summary):
- Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor / GPU exhaustion. Partially true: a combination of GPU pool saturation and unexpectedly long pod startup times caused by a change in kernel selection that increased per-process memory footprint for redwood/gpt-13b-v2-quantized.
- Autoscaler behavior: configured headroom was insufficient for the rapid EOD concurrency spike. The autoscaler attempted scale-up but pod startup latency (7–12s) combined with queueing resulted in amplified 5xx rates and connection timeouts.
- KV cache interaction: greater memory pressure led to higher eviction rates in the KV store for streaming sessions, which manifested as mid-stream disconnects and resume failures.
- Root cause (contributing factors):
  * Rollout of kernel-selection heuristics (PR 7421) increased resident memory for a subset of quantized model variants.
  * Autoscaler headroom and scale-up thresholds were too conservative for HydraNet's bursty EOD profile.
  * Lack of a dedicated canary window for kernel-selection across high-concurrency enterprise customers.

Workaround & mitigation applied during incident:
- Immediate actions: routed HydraNet traffic to reserved spillover capacity and temporarily increased per-customer concurrency caps. Rolled back kernel-selection optimization for affected variants. Increased autoscaler target headroom for the us-east GPU pool.
- Customer communication: CS provided live updates every 30 minutes and offered a temporary service credit pending post-incident review.

Resolution:
- Rollback of kernel-selection rollout completed at 15:05 UTC; traffic normalized after autoscaler scaled to the increased headroom.
- Confirmed by synthetic checks and HydraNet validation tests at 15:22 UTC. Full incident declared mitigated and later marked resolved after verification.

Post-incident action items (owners assigned):
- Engineering: add a canary gating policy for kernel-selection rollouts that includes a synthetic high-concurrency workload (owner: Marco Ruiz, due 2026-03-21).
- Autoscaler: revise default headroom for enterprise customers and introduce per-customer cap overrides (owner: Priya Desai, due 2026-03-18).
- Observability: add a composite alert for concurrent increases in pod startup latency + KV eviction rate to detect similar regressions earlier (owner: Liam O'Connor, due 2026-03-16).
- SRE/On-call runbook: update hydra/hotpath playbook with explicit spillover routing steps and contact matrix (owner: SRE team, due 2026-03-19).
- CS & Account: finalize customer credit and post-incident customer-facing summary (owner: Emily Zhao, due 2026-03-12 — completed).

Follow-ups:
- Engineering will open a targeted performance optimization PR for the quantized variant to reduce resident memory (tracking PR planned: serving-runtime/pull/7510).
- Schedule a joint postmortem review with HydraNet on 2026-03-17.

Notes:
- Incident was single-customer impacting but exposed a rollout risk that could affect other enterprise customers under similar concurrency patterns. Action items prioritize safety of rollouts and autoscaler policy updates.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:32 UTC — On-call SRE (Liam O'Connor): Noted spike in pod evictions and high memory RSS on a subset of gpt-13b-quant pods. Opening investigation. Routing change being prepared.
2026-03-10 13:58 UTC — Engineering (Marco Ruiz): Identified kernel-selection rollout 7421 as a strong correlation. Rolling back for affected variants now. Will coordinate with autoscaler team.
2026-03-10 14:27 UTC — Support (Aisha Patel): Routing HydraNet to reserved spillover capacity. Customer reporting reduced disconnects. Offering service credit; collecting exact impacted job IDs.
2026-03-10 15:10 UTC — Engineering (Marco Ruiz): Rollback complete and autoscaler headroom increased. Monitoring for recovery. Noted follow-up items and scheduling postmortem.
2026-03-11 09:02 UTC — CS (Emily Zhao): Sent preliminary post-incident summary and service credit confirmation to HydraNet. Customer requested deeper timeline and root-cause writeup; scheduled 2026-03-17 review.
2026-03-12 12:45 UTC — SRE (Priya Desai): Autoscaler headroom change staged for permanent config; PR linked. Will run canaries next week.
Rollback of kernel-selection rollout; increased autoscaler headroom; traffic routed to reserved spillover capacity. Post-incident action items created and scheduled.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightDocs reports intermittent 403s when nodes in their private deployment attempt to download model shard byte ranges via presigned S3 URLs. Failures correlate with nightly warm-up batches that fetch large sharded artifacts in parallel. Some downloads succeed; others return 403 and result in corrupted/partial shard files and checksum mismatches at validation time.

Impact:
- Several serving nodes failed warm-up during scheduled batch rollout; roughly 4-7% of range GETs in a job returned 403 leading to shard validation errors and degraded capacity while retries/backoff ran.
- Customer reports elevated tail latency and increased retry traffic (and cost) while this is ongoing.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peered to customer transit gateway) running serving-runtime 1.9.2
- Artifact storage: S3 presigned URLs generated by Redwood control plane (signed V4), default range fetching implementation in artifact fetcher.
- Affected hosts are behind customer corporate forward proxy / HTTP appliance in us-east-1 region.

1) From a host behind the customer's corporate forward proxy, run a range GET against a presigned URL generated by the control plane.
2) Include Range: bytes=0-4194303 header for a ~4MB shard chunk.
3) Observe HTTP response code and headers.
4) Repeat high-parallelism download job (e.g., 32 concurrent range requests) and note failure rate.

Reproducible: Intermittent (higher when parallelism > 16 and when downloads pass through corporate proxy appliance).
Some range GETs return 403 Forbidden. S3 response headers (when present) include x-amz-request-id and x-amz-id-2. Logs show 'SignatureDoesNotMatch' in S3 response body for the failed requests. Successfully completed GETs return 206 Partial Content as expected.
All range GETs using valid presigned URLs should return 206 Partial Content and produce intact shard bytes that pass checksum validation.
[2026-03-11T01:23:12Z] GET /presigned-url-id Range: bytes=0-4194303 -> 206, duration=120ms
[2026-03-11T01:23:12Z] GET /presigned-url-id Range: bytes=4194304-8388607 -> 403, duration=79ms, s3-error=SignatureDoesNotMatch, x-amz-request-id=89A1B2C3D4E5
[edge-proxy] removed headers: x-amz-content-sha256
[serving-node] validation: checksum mismatch for shard chunk 2 (expected abcdef, got abcd12)

2026-03-11 09:10 UTC - Support (Liam O'Connor): Acknowledged. Opening investigation with SRE and asking customer for packet capture across proxy during a failed download.
2026-03-11 11:05 UTC - Customer (BrightDocs Network Ops): Confirmed appliance vendor rule 'sanitize-signed-headers' active; reported that x-amz-content-sha256 is on the sanitized list by default for legacy signing. We're running a Blue Coat-like HTTP forward proxy (vendor redacted).
2026-03-11 15:48 UTC - SRE (Maya Patel): Correlated failing request traces to requests where x-amz-content-sha256 header was removed before reaching the S3 V4 verification step. Non-stripped requests show valid signature checks and 206. Posting packet capture in attachments.
2026-03-12 07:22 UTC - Support (Liam O'Connor): Temporary workaround suggestion sent to customer: allow x-amz-content-sha256 through the proxy or configure the proxy to preserve AWS-signed headers for endpoints in the Redwood artifact domain. Also documented 'UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD' option as a short-term mitigation for presigned URLs used for range fetches.
2026-03-12 12:00 UTC - Customer (BrightDocs Network Ops): Applied rule exception for redwood-artifacts.example.com in proxy; retested large warm-up job: failure rate dropped to 0.6% from ~5%.
Packet capture shows forward proxy rewriting/removing 'x-amz-content-sha256' header on some TLS-terminating inspection flows when requests are proxied via HTTP CONNECT + HTTP/2 upgrade path.
S3 V4 signature for range GET includes a payload hash in the canonical request when a streaming signature is used; if the header is removed, S3 rejects the request with SignatureDoesNotMatch even though the URL itself is presigned (the signature covers headers).
> Hypothesis: Proxy policy 'strip-signed-headers' removes a subset of headers for requests that match 'application/octet-stream' or for tunneled HTTP/2 sessions that the proxy normalizes. This behavior is enabled by default for older appliance config profiles.
Fetch telemetry shows higher failure rates during peak parallel downloads; likely because some requests take a different proxy path (load-balanced across inspection nodes) that still applies the sanitization rule.
Control plane currently generates standard V4 presigned URLs (payload hashed) and does not set 'UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD' by default for ranged downloads.

Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 03:10–03:45 UTC, MerchantEdge experienced elevated 5xx rates and repeated streaming disconnects. Customers reported truncated responses and repeated retry-triggered fallback requests that amplified load. The initial symptom was a rising tail latency on streaming sessions, then a cascade of 502/504 and a client-observed fallback loop.
2026-03-10 03:08 UTC: MerchantEdge support contact via #support-merchantedge.
2026-03-10 03:12 UTC: SRE triage declared incident and began traffic routing to secondary region.
2026-03-10 03:20 UTC: Observed increased error rate on streaming-proxy and smart-routing logs indicating session-state mismatch.
2026-03-10 03:27 UTC: Canary rollback of kernel-selection PR and temporary disablement of enhanced KV-cache routing applied for affected hosts.
2026-03-10 03:36 UTC: Error rate returned to baseline; streaming sessions stabilized.
2026-03-10 04:00 UTC: Declared major incident mitigated.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC: Post-incident review and follow-up actions documented.
1) Create a long-running streaming session with stateful tool-calls and a sequence of >512 token prefixes.
2) Route requests through smart-routing policy 'latency-prefer' with prefix-KV caching enabled.
3) Trigger concurrent reconnections from the client (simulated network jitter).
4) Observe eventual 502s from streaming-proxy when session token IDs misalign and fallback routing issues cause duplicate inflight requests.
Excerpt from streaming-proxy logs (prod-us-east):
[2026-03-10T03:18:11Z] WARN session-mismatch session_id=ab12... expected_seq=112 current_seq=95
[2026-03-10T03:18:12Z] ERROR router fallback-loop request_id=ff23... target=quantized-host-07 502 Bad Gateway
[2026-03-10T03:18:13Z] ERROR serving-runtime kvcache-miss inconsistent-kv-length model=redwood-instruct-v1.2
Related dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/metrics/INC-91234-streaming-errors
Hypotheses tested: 1) Kernel-selection PR introduced a perf path that changed sequence-number assignment for quantized kernels under certain batch sizes. 2) Smart-routing's prefix-aware KV-cache returned an out-of-sync KV snapshot when sessions reattached to a different host. Evidence: repeated 'session-mismatch' WARNs and 'inconsistent-kv-length' errors in serving-runtime logs. Confirmed by correlating request IDs across proxy and runtime logs and replaying with client jitter in staging. Linked instrumentation traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/INC-91234. Root cause narrowed to race between session-resume handler and KV-cache population code when a session migrated between hosts during enhanced kernel path selection.
Race condition in session-resume + KV-cache population interacting with an in-flight kernel-selection change. Under transient client reconnects, sessions could resume with stale sequence metadata, causing serving-runtime to reject requests (5xx) and triggering fallback routing that multiplied inflight attempts.
Immediate mitigation: rolled back kernel-selection change on canary and then full cluster (2026-03-10 03:27–03:33 UTC); disabled prefix-aware KV-cache routing temporarily for affected host pool; blocked smart-routing policy 'latency-prefer' from selecting quantized-hosts during customer sessions. Long-term fix: apply synchronization to session-resume handler, add validation and retry on KV-cache mismatch, and add unit/integration tests for session migration + jitter. Deployed hotfix branch serving-runtime@pr-2193-fix on 2026-03-11 and scheduled full rollout during low-traffic window 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC.
INT-4021: Implement synchronization primitives in session-resume code-path and add integration tests (owner: Marco Ruiz, ETA: 2026-03-14)
Create customer-facing postmortem and share with MerchantEdge; include timeline, root cause, and credits (owner: Elena Gomez, ETA: 2026-03-13)
Add dashboard alert for 'inconsistent-kv-length' errors and session-mismatch WARNs (owner: Observability team, ETA: 2026-03-16)
Run a tabletop with SRE/Applied ML/Platform teams to validate rollback playbook and smart-routing safety checks (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2026-03-20)
Review billing impact and issue pro-rated credit per SLA; coordinate with Finance (owner: CS-Billing, ETA: 2026-03-13)

Marco Ruiz (SRE) — 2026-03-10 03:15 UTC: Initial hypothesis: kernel-selection rollout + overly aggressive KV-cache routing created sequence-ID drift under jitter. Rolling back kernel-selection on a small canary cluster now.
Priya Menon (Applied ML) — 2026-03-10 03:22 UTC: Observed mismatched KV-cache lengths for quantized model instances; suspect race between cache population and session resumption code-paths.
MerchantEdge (Customer) — 2026-03-10 03:30 UTC: Thanks — we see responses stabilizing. Please advise on permanent fix and account credit for downtime.

Issue summary: Multiple ClarityAI requests uploading large embedding batches (~120k tokens total, chunked) started seeing 5xx responses (502/503) from the Redwood API gateway in prod-us-west. Errors began as a spike and turned into sustained elevated error rate for ~30 minutes. Impact: Affected customer experienced failed embedding imports (bulk job failures) and SDK retries. Observed impact confined to ClarityAI tenant in us-west; other tenants unaffected.

Environment: prod (us-west), dedicated tenant cluster for ClarityAI, serving-runtime 2026-02-28 build, proxy revision 2026-03-10.

Steps to reproduce (internal reproducible recipe):
1) Use ClarityAI bulk-upload pattern: multipart POST /v1/embeddings/upload with 2500 items, 32MB total payload.
2) Parallelize with 8 concurrent streams from one client IP.
3) Run for 1 minute.

Observed behavior: Gateway returns 502 or 503 intermittently across retries; logs show upstream runtime disconnects and ephemeral-proxy accept-queue growth to >95% of configured queue length. NVMe latencies on the embed-shard nodes increased (P99 ~ 240ms) around same time. Serving runtime emitted watcher log 'evicting worker due to response timeout' repeatedly.

Logs / excerpts: (sanitized)
- apigw: "2026-03-13T14:17:24Z ERROR route=upload tenant=clarityai upstream=disconnect code=502 msg=upstream closed connection"
- proxy: "accept_queue_length=198/200; ephemerals_in_use=48; conn_drops=6"
- runtime: "watchdog: response_timeout pid=2334 model=clarity-embed-large-v2"
- nvme: "iowait_p99_ms=240; io_depth=32; queue_stalls=12"

Hypothesis: Large embedding upload pattern causes burst of many small-fanout requests to the embedding shard. Ephemeral proxy accept-queue fills, causing connection drops to upstream runtimes which are also experiencing elevated NVMe iowait due to concurrent checkpoint/GC or background compaction. The combined effect triggers API Gateway retries and a retry-amplification loop resulting in sustained 5xx.

Immediate mitigation applied: Applied tenant-level temporary concurrency cap (reduced parallel streams to 2) and outbound hedged-retry tuning for the upload route; cleared accept-queue by rotating a small set of ephemerals (rolling restart of ephemeral proxies handling the tenant). Customer notified with temporary workaround.

Open questions:
- What triggered NVMe latency spike at 14:15? Background compaction was scheduled at 14:10 on shard nodes (check scheduler).
- Why did accept-queue not shed earlier (load-shedding config)?
- Do serving-runtime timeouts need to be extended for large multipart embedding uploads?
2026-03-13 14:05 UTC - First customer report via support form; 14:12 UTC - Alerts: ingestion error rate spike on tenant ClarityAI; 14:18 UTC - SRE observed elevated 502/503 across us-west edge; 14:33 UTC - Reproduced locally with large multipart embedding upload; 15:10 UTC - Temporary rate-limit applied for tenant; 15:45 UTC - Team investigating proxy accept-queue and nvme latency correlation
14:20 UTC - SRE: accept-queue metric shows sustained >90% and conn_drop spikes correlated with embedding upload throughput.
14:25 UTC - Infra: nvme compaction job started at 14:10 on embed-shard-3; iowait P99 rose to 240ms by 14:14.
14:30 UTC - Eng: runtime logs indicate repeated worker eviction due to response timeouts; kernel fallback not observed.
14:40 UTC - Tested reducing client parallelism from 8->2: errors drop to baseline and queues drain within 20s.
14:55 UTC - Applied temporary route-level backpressure: ingress concurrent limit for /v1/embeddings/upload lowered to 4 for all tenants on us-west to reduce blast radius.
15:05 UTC - Confirmed no other tenants impacted; load spike isolated to ClarityAI; but accept-queue aging logic did not trigger fast-enough shedding on these ephemeral proxies.
Tenant concurrency cap applied for ClarityAI (immediate).
Route-level ingress limit lowered to 4 on us-west for /v1/embeddings/upload (temporary safety).
Emergency throttle/abort of background NVMe compaction on embed-shard-3 (reduced iowait).
Rolled ephemeral proxy restart to flush accept-queue and clear stuck connections.
Customer advised to retry bulk upload with fewer concurrent streams; provided best-practice doc link.
ENG: PR to tune proxy shedding to trigger earlier (target threshold 75%) and add exponential backoff in accept-queue drain behavior. (owner: Diego)
ENG: Evaluate increasing runtime response_timeout for bulk embed uploads by +50% and add route annotation to override default for upload endpoints. (owner: Model Serving)
INFRA: Add NVMe maintenance blackout for embed-shards during known high-throughput customer windows and improve compaction scheduling logic. (owner: Priya)
CS: Coordinate with ClarityAI to reschedule large imports until fixes roll out; capture their preferred maintenance windows. (owner: Aisha)
SRE: Add a composite alert that correlates accept-queue, nvme iowait, and upstream disconnects to catch this pattern earlier. (owner: Maya)

Customer impact mitigated at 15:00 UTC via concurrency cap and proxy rotation.
No data loss observed; most failed uploads were retried successfully after mitigation.
Follow-up action required: schedule runtime timeout change and proxy shedding PR; target rollout in maintenance window next week.
Documented temporary workaround in support KB: 'Bulk embedding upload best practices' and linked to customer email thread.
2026-03-13T14:13Z - <Aisha Khan> Customer ClarityAI reports bulk embedding job failures; attached sample request and timestamps; escalating to SRE.
2026-03-13T14:19Z - <Diego Morales> Observed 502s from gateway and upstream resets. Pulling accept-queue and nvme metrics. Tagging infra.
2026-03-13T14:28Z - <Priya Kapoor (SRE)> NVMe compaction found on embed-shard-3. Starting emergency compaction abort and throttle. Recommending temporary tenant concurrency cap.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a dedicated instance report streaming sessions that produce interleaved prefix tokens from previous sessions and then stall without an end marker after our scheduled auth heartbeat/token rotation. The session does not emit the expected terminal event and client SDKs show a hung stream.

Impact:
- A subset (~3%) of long-running streaming requests from ClariTech are missing terminal closure and final few sentences, causing truncated responses in production.
- Affects dedicated customers behind our managed streaming-proxy in us-east-1.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted dedicated (customer tenant: clari-dev-dedicated)
2026-03-10 15:12 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reports repeated occurrences after maintenance window that rotated auth heartbeats. They pasted client SDK logs and a short HAR. Asked for immediate escalation.
2026-03-10 15:26 - SRE (Arjun Patel): Reproduced a stalled session in staging using the customer's reproducer. Observed stream prefix tokens from prior session arriving interleaved with new output, then no 'end' event. Captured tcpdump and upstream logs. Linking traces: https://observability.redwood/trace/8a7f2b
2026-03-10 16:02 - Eng (Priya Nair): Hypothesis: when auth heartbeat rotates, upstream proxy rebinds and a multiplexing ID collision allows a late packet from an old worker to be stitched into an active session. Looking into proxy multiplex handshake code and session id allocation.
2026-03-11 09:14 - Customer (ClariTech - Alex Rivera): We see it on both desktop and mobile clients, but more common under intermittent mobile network switches. Providing sample request IDs: rq_7f3a2, rq_7f3a3.
2026-03-11 11:30 - SRE (Arjun Patel): Rolled a temporary mitigant: set keepalive timeout lower on streaming-proxy for the tenant and forced close on token rotation to avoid silent rebinds. Customer confirms reduced frequency of the issue in nightly tests.
2026-03-12 08:05 - Eng (Priya Nair): Created PR to add stronger session tombstone on auth rotation and to add jitter to session ids to avoid immediate reuse: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2287. Rolling to canary now.
Reproducer steps (internal):
1) Start long-running SSE session that streams ~10-20s token bursts.
2) Trigger auth heartbeat rotation for tenant (simulate rotation in staging).
3) Induce proxy connection rebind (tcpkill simulating path migrate).
4) Observe interleaved tokens from previous session and missing terminal event.
Findings:
- tcpdump shows late packets with old multiplex header arriving and being accepted by the active socket after rotation.
- Upstream worker logs include 'primed_kv_cache mismatch' warnings for the affected request ids.
- Session id allocation in streaming-proxy currently reuses a counter without tombstone delay which can collide during rapid rotation.
- Client SDK reconnect logic attempts resume; resume flow assumes non-overlapping session ids which is violated.
Hypothesis:
Auth heartbeat rotation triggers a short window where proxy rebinds a socket to a different upstream worker; because session ids are reused quickly, a late packet from the previous worker is treated as part of the newly resumed stream. That interleaves old prefixes with new output and blocks finalization when the end-marker is dropped by the stitch path.
Evidence links:
- Trace: https://observability.redwood/trace/8a7f2b
- Proxy logs snippet: [WARNING] primed_kv_cache mismatch tenant=clari-dev-dedicated request=rq_7f3a2
- tcpdump (attached to ticket): tcpdump_rq_7f3a2.pcap

Mitigations applied (2026-03-11):
- Config change: streaming-proxy now forces Connection: close and tombstones session ids for 60s on auth heartbeat rotation for affected tenants.
- Client-side recommendation: update SDK to v1.4.2 which treats resume collisions as a hard resume (drops and reconnects).
Permanent fix (in progress):
- PR #2287 adds randomized session id suffix and explicit session tombstone window; also adds additional guard in stitcher to reject prefetched tokens that don't match current kv_cache priming fingerprint. Canaried to 5% on 2026-03-12 and rolling to 50% 2026-03-12 afternoon.
- Post-deploy test plan: run synthetic churn tests (auth rotate while simulating mobile handover) and validate end-event emission for 1000 sessions.
Follow-up actions:
- SRE to monitor tenant error-rate and stream finalization rate for 72 hours.
- Create KB article for dedicated customers describing how auth rotation interacts with streaming and recommended SDK pinning.
- Engineering to schedule deeper review of multiplexing protocol and add integration test in CI for auth-rotation + resume behavior.
payload.summary: Stalled interleaved stream after auth heartbeat rotation causing missing finalization

payload.description:
Issue summary:
BrightLoop reported significantly elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completion requests starting ~2026-03-11 22:10 UTC after their account was routed to the new runtime (runtime-1.9.0) and an upstream compiler swap (jit-compiler v3.4). Impact: ~10-25x increase in median TTFB for short chat prompts, customer-facing timeouts on interactive product flows and increased error rates in client telemetry.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: end-user chat flows in BrightLoop web app (session flow) saw interactive timeouts (client 10s) in ~12% of sessions for a subset of routes.
- Business: brightloop has dedicated capacity; this affects a paid account on reserved capacity (throughput SLA).

Timeline / Observed events:
- 2026-03-11 21:50 UTC: internal rollout of runtime-1.9.0 + compiler swap began for a subset of dedicated pools.
- 2026-03-11 22:06 UTC: BrightLoop's requests first show sharp TTFB increase in our tracing (span: first-token-delivery).
- 2026-03-11 22:30 UTC: BrightLoop opened support channel (#support-brightloop) and reported degraded UX.
- 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC: Support created this ticket and escalated to SRE.

Environment:
- Customer: BrightLoop (dedicated GPU pool: pool-ded-07-usw)
- Platform: runtime-1.9.0 with jit-compiler v3.4, scheduler v2.6, quant profile default-q4_0
- Regions affected: us-west (pool-ded-07-usw)

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer and SRE):
1) Client opens chat session and sends a short prompt (~12 tokens of user text).
2) Redwood API accepts request and routes to model instance in pool-ded-07-usw.
3) Request is accepted but first token is delayed: TTFB recorded between 800ms and 5.2s (median from historical ~90ms to current ~1.8s for same prompt).
4) Longer prompts (>200 tokens) show normal per-token throughput after initial delay.

Logs / telemetry snippets:
- Trace sample (span timings): api-gateway 12ms -> router 8ms -> container-sched 120ms -> runtime-init 1.3s -> first-token 1.45s.
- Exported metrics: first_token_latency.p50 increased from 95ms to 1850ms for pool-ded-07-usw between 2026-03-11 21:30 and 22:10 UTC.
- No OOMs or GPU errors in syslogs. No 5xx surge; 200 responses with delayed first tokens.

Initial hypothesis from SRE/serving team:
- The compiler swap introduced a coldpath where KV cache priming or attention-kernel selection adds synchronous work during initial decode for short inputs.
- Scheduler changes in v2.6 interact with runtime initialization, adding an extra synchronous slo that delays first-token emission for requests that miss the hot-cache.

Investigation notes:
- We reproduced elevated TTFB in staging by deploying runtime-1.9.0 + jit-compiler v3.4 to a dedicated test pool and replaying BrightLoop's traffic (same prompt set).
- When we revert to compiler v3.3 with runtime-1.9.0, TTFB drops back to expected medians (~80-120ms), indicating compiler-change is a strong signal.
- Per-container CPU profiles show a synchronous compile step on first request for a given model shard which is bounded but takes ~700-1200ms. This appears to be triggered even with existing compiled artifacts in some cases (path mismatch in artifact registry).
- Router logs show an increased percentage of requests routed to warm-but-not-primed containers (narrow windows where priming was ongoing).

Workaround / Mitigation applied:
- 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC: Rolled back compiler to v3.3 for pool-ded-07-usw as an immediate mitigation for BrightLoop. Metrics returned to baseline within ~30 minutes.
- Recommended customer-side: increase client first-token timeout to 15s while we complete rollout fixes (temporary).

Next steps / action items:
- (SRE) Add a pre-warm/priming job in rollout pipeline that ensures artifact registry path alignment and triggers priming compile tasks before traffic shift. Owner: Evan Liu, ETA: 2026-03-15.
- (Runtime) Fix artifact path handling in jit-compiler v3.4 to avoid redundant synchronous compile on warm containers. Owner: Marcos Rivera, PR created.
- (Scheduler) Investigate scheduling decision that surfaces containers still in priming state; add routing safety check. Owner: Priya Nair.
- (Support) Notify BrightLoop of rollback and next update window; track UX regressions. Owner: Aisha Patel.

Customer impact / follow-up:
- BrightLoop acknowledged rollback resolved immediate UX issues and requested a postmortem and preventive checklist prior to further runtime/compiler upgrades on dedicated pools.

Resolution (current):
- Temporary rollback to compiler v3.3 applied for affected pool; monitoring confirms TTFB returned to baseline. Full fix pending compiler patch and rollout priming job.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 09:00 - Customer (BrightLoop - Dev lead, Jordan Kim): Confirmed UX restored. Requested postmortem and assurance that future upgrades include pre-warm steps.
Rollback to compiler v3.3 applied; awaiting compiler patch and rollout priming job before closing. Postmortem requested by customer.
Merge compiler path-fix PR and schedule canary with pre-warm job
Implement scheduler routing check to avoid priming containers
Prepare postmortem and customer-facing summary for BrightLoop

Issue summary
Vectorgrid reports that audit events exported to Splunk HEC contain inconsistent field names and shapes depending on event type. Their SIEM correlation rules expect stable fields for actor, target, tenant, request/correlation IDs, and event taxonomy. Current inconsistency is blocking their rollout of detection rules and creating noise in dashboards.

Impact
- SIEM parsing rules break for a subset of events.
- Detection queries cannot reliably join events by actor/tenant/request.
- Customer perceives audit logging as incomplete/unreliable for compliance monitoring.

Customer expectation
- All exported events conform to the canonical v1 schema with consistent top-level fields.
- Exporter should tag schema_version and normalize legacy/variant producers into v1 shape.

Environment
- Dedicated deployment (Vectorgrid)
- Export target: Splunk HEC
- Region: us-east

Examples (customer-provided)
1) RBAC event (control plane) includes expected v1 fields:
{"event_type":"rbac.role.updated","schema_version":"1.0","event_id":"01HS...","occurred_at":"2026-01-24T18:02:11Z","tenant_id":"tnt_9f...","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"usr_4b...","actor_email":"admin@vectorgrid.com","source_ip":"203.0.113.10","request_id":"req_8c...","target_type":"role","target_id":"role_2a...","result":"success"}

2) API key event uses different names / missing fields:

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when Redwood packages audit events into our JSONL SIEM export wrapper (daily and ad-hoc slices), tenant-scoped context (tenant_id, session_id, request_context.*) is occasionally missing or collapsed into a generic envelope. Impact: NordicsBank cannot reconcile per-tenant activity in their SIEM, failing a regulatory playback test for transaction traceability (affects compliance proof). Observed behavior: - Batches with >200 events occasionally show a single top-level 'tenant_context' object rather than per-event context. - Missing session_id on downstream Splunk/Hec ingestion. Expected behavior: Each event line in JSONL should contain full per-event metadata (tenant_id, request_id, session_id, user_agent, region) and the wrapper must not deduplicate or hoist tenant fields across lines. Environment: prod export pipeline (s3 batch exporter), customer configured signed S3 delivery + Splunk HEC consuming via a Redpiper connector. Time window: problem observed intermittently between 2026-03-07 and 2026-03-09 during a high-volume replay test.
1) Customer requests on-demand JSONL export for tenant T-98234 covering 2026-03-07 00:00 to 2026-03-07 06:00.
2) Redwood export job packages events into line-delimited JSON (wrapper version v2.3.0).
3) Job writes compressed .jsonl.gz to customer's S3 bucket; Splunk connector pulls and ingests.
4) Customer runs their reconciliation that expects per-line tenant/session keys.
5) They observe intermittent lines where tenant fields are either absent or a single envelope object appears at top of file.
Repro notes: Issue rate increased with bursts where >200 events per batch were generated; smaller batches do not show the problem consistently.
Sample snippet from exported file (anonymized):
-- file: export-2026-03-07-02.jsonl.gz (decompressed) --
{"event_id":"e-1","timestamp":"2026-03-07T02:01:02Z","payload":{"action":"prompt"}}
{"tenant_context":{"tenant_id":"T-98234","session_id":"s-xxxxx"}}
{"event_id":"e-2","timestamp":"2026-03-07T02:01:05Z","payload":{"action":"response"}}
Note: expected each event line to include tenant_context; instead an envelope line appears between event lines in some batches. Attached raw export and compressed sample in ticket attachments (customer provided with permission).
Initial hypotheses: (A) JSONL wrapper v2.3.0 attempted an optimization to deduplicate identical tenant_context across consecutive events and mistakenly hoisted the object as a separate line; (B) Streaming serializer had a buffer flush boundary that emitted context object when a size threshold was reached; (C) Post-processing compressor/concat stage introduced line breaks that separated context from events. Actions taken: - Pulled export artifacts from the customer's S3 bucket for the time windows; reproduced the envelope pattern locally. - Cross-checked wrapper code in repo; found recent change in platform PR #939 that added a cross-batch 'context pool' to reduce payload size. - Triggered a local export using the same dataset and wrapper v2.3.0; observed same envelope when batch size >128KB. - Rolled test with wrapper v2.2.7 (previous stable) and did not reproduce. Observed correlation with batch size and with events where per-event metadata fields compressed to identical JSON, triggering dedup step. Telemetry/dashboards referenced: export-job-traces (trace ids: trace-7f3a, trace-7f8b), serializer-flush-metrics. Hypothesis now leans to (A) dedupe/hoist optimization bug in v2.3.0. Next steps: revert dedupe logic or gate behind stable flag for enterprise customers; create regression test for JSONL invariants.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:22 - NordicBank ASA (Customer): Connector is Splunk HEC via our managed Redpiper; no additional preprocessor. We also attached the connector logs.
2026-03-11 16:00 - SRE Pager (internal): Noted spike in serializer flushes on export workers correlating with high concurrency; investigating memory/buffer interaction.
Workaround: For immediate compliance playback, Support created an on-demand export using wrapper v2.2.7 which preserved per-event context. We delivered that export to the customer's secure S3 staging and confirmed their reconciliation passed. Permanent fix plan: revert/patch dedupe/hoist optimization in wrapper v2.3.0 and release v2.3.1 with a regression test covering JSONL per-line invariants. Owner: Diego Alvarez (Support) + Lina Park (Platform eng). Expected rollout: hotfix release 2026-03-13, followed by a 72-hour canary and global flip. Customer follow-up: provided timeline and offered pro-bono assistance for audit playback. Ticket will be closed after patch release and one successful customer-confirmed replay.

payload.description:
Issue summary: LexiChat reports increased 95th-percentile tail latency and sporadic streaming disconnects after enabling a new quantization profile and aggressive batching + KV prefetch on their Dedicated pool. They want a tested, low-risk policy to degrade features (quant profile, batching, KV prefetch) in production without full rollback to prior model version. Impact: Customer-facing chat experiences intermittent timeouts and elevated token costs due to retries. Request: concrete step-by-step safe-degradation policy and one-line CLI/API commands for toggles, plus verification checklist and recommended monitoring thresholds.
1) Customer enabled rw-13b-quant-v2 quant profile (q8_0) via model config on Dedicated pool
2) Set max_batch_size=2048 and enabled kv_prefetch=true in optimizer config
3) Observed increased request latencies and occasional streaming broken pipes under steady load (~120 rps)
4) Reproduce under prod-like traffic using loadgen: mean seq_len=512, 30% streaming responses
2026-03-13T10:12:43Z WARN serving-runtime: kv-prefetch eviction miss spike (rate 18.6%)
2026-03-13T10:13:01Z ERROR gateway: downstream stream disconnected code=ABORTED trace=abc123
2026-03-13T10:14:20Z WARN scheduler: batch-assembly-delay exceeded target (p95 420ms)
Support triage: symptoms align with aggressive batch sizes + quant profile edge-case kernel path that increases assembly latency for long sequences.
SRE checked Dedicated pool GPU utilization: per-GPU occupancy ~88% with spikes to 96% concurrently with latency spikes.
KV-prefetch shows higher miss ratio after enabling new quant profile — hypothesis: memory layout change increased kv cache fragmentation leading to extra CPU work.
No code regressions found in serving-runtime in last 72h; related PR touched kernel selection heuristics (see PR #4123) — flagged for engineering review.
Immediate risk: full rollback to previous model version will reduce throughput predictability and requires a pinned version change in customer configs; customer prefers staged degradations instead of full revert.
Apply staged feature degradations in order of lowest customer-visible regression to highest. Recommended immediate safe sequence: 1) reduce max_batch_size to 512, 2) disable kv_prefetch, 3) apply quant profile reduced aggressiveness (q8_1 -> q8_2 or switch to q16 fallback), 4) if still unstable, fallback route to gpt-4o-mini-compat for a subset of traffic via routing policy. Each step should be applied as a canary to 5-10% traffic with 10 minute observation windows.
Step A - Canary reduce batch: API PATCH /v1/configs/{pool} set optimizer.max_batch_size=512; verify p95 latency and batch assembly delay for 10 minutes
Step B - Toggle kv_prefetch: API PATCH /v1/configs/{pool} set optimizer.kv_prefetch=false; watch kv miss rate, CPU steal, and stream disconnect metrics for 15 minutes
Step C - De-escalate quant profile: API PATCH /v1/models/{model}/profile set profile=q8_2 or set profile_fallback_to=q16; confirm model correctness tests against golden prompts
Step D - Route fallback: Create routing rule to send 10% traffic to gpt-4o-mini-compat via Console -> Routing -> Add Rule; monitor error budget and token cost delta
Step E - If regressions persist after Steps A-D, perform model version revert: PATCH /v1/models/{customer_model}/pin set version={previous-stable}; coordinate a 5-minute maintenance window and notify customer

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 11:02 - LexiChat (customer): Provided config and confirmed no other infra changes. Traffic window attached as s3://lexichat-logs/prod/2026-03-13/
Create engineering ticket to add 'safe-mode' kernel selector that avoids q8 aggressive path for sequences >1024 (link to PR in related_github_prs)
Add a boolean flag in Console to perform single-click safe-degrade for Dedicated pools (batch_size reduction + kv toggle + route fallback)
Schedule a 1:1 with LexiChat success manager to review post-mortem and recommended default optimizer profiles for their workload
Update Degradation runbook in Confluence with exact API commands and monitoring thresholds used in this incident

payload.description:
Customer reports intermittent 403s for users whose admin role was removed in the IdP. The deprovisioning event is visible in the customer's SCIM logs, but Redwood's role cache retains the admin binding for ~30-90s causing a short window of authorization flip (allowed -> denied) depending on which token/session path is used. This is causing automated job failures and confusion during immediate post-deprovision operations.
1) In customer's IdP (SCIM provisioning), remove 'platform-admin' role from a user via PATCH request (delta) rather than full replace.
2) IdP sends SCIM PATCH to Redwood SCIM endpoint with Content-Type: application/scim+json; charset=UTF-8
3) Observe SCIM PATCH accepted (201/204) in customer's provisioning logs and in Redwood intake logs
4) Immediately attempt admin API call with an existing session token or perform console action: some requests succeed, some return 403 within the first ~90s post-deprovision.
5) After ~2 minutes, all requests consistently return 403 as expected.
<redwood-ingest> 2026-03-12T15:08:12.342Z POST /scim/v2/Users/84a1 PATCH Content-Type: application/scim+json; charset=UTF-8 204
<authz> 2026-03-12T15:08:12.458Z role-provisioner: delta applied user_id=84a1 removed_roles=[platform-admin]
<cache> 2026-03-12T15:08:12.462Z role-cache: scheduled invalidation key=user:84a1 ttl=300s
<authz> 2026-03-12T15:08:12.470Z token-lookup: token_id=tok_01 evaluated cached_roles=[platform-admin,read-only] decision=ALLOW
<api> 2026-03-12T15:08:12.475Z request_id=req_9fc call=admin.create-invite user=84a1 result=403 code=forbidden msg=User lacks platform-admin
Initial hypothesis: role-cache invalidation job not triggered for SCIM PATCH requests that carry 'charset' in Content-Type header. Our SCIM intake codec compares exact Content-Type values when selecting delta parser path.
Reproduced in internal staging by sending PATCH with 'application/scim+json; charset=UTF-8' — observed the SCIM delta handler fell back to generic ingest pipeline that writes a 'provision_event' but does not call cacheInvalidator.notifyUserChange().
Observed two different authorization evaluation paths: live session requests sometimes short-circuit to token-bound cached roles (fast-path) and do not re-check provisioner state until token refresh; API calls that trigger a synchronous re-eval hit the updated state sooner. This explains the interleaving of ALLOW then DENY behavior.
Customer SCIM logs show IdP (ForgeOnPrem) switched library version in last week to include charset in Content-Type for PATCH requests. No changes in payload body.
2026-03-12 - Support: Ava Chen: Thanks for the report and logs. We're starting an investigation focused on SCIM intake Content-Type handling and role-cache invalidation. We've escalated to infra.
2026-03-12 - Eng (Marco Ruiz): Reproduced locally with curl sending Content-Type: application/scim+json; charset=UTF-8. We see the delta parser not selected due to strict header match. Working on a patch to normalize Content-Type parsing and trigger immediate cache invalidation for affected user entries.
2026-03-13 - Support: Communicated workaround to customer: request IdP team to send full-replace (PUT) for role removals, or temporarily add 2-minute drain window to critical jobs. Customer accepted workaround.
2026-03-14 - Eng: Created PR to make Content-Type matching tolerant and add idempotent cacheInvalidator.notifyUserChange() on delta path. Running internal tests and will roll to canary tomorrow.
Rolling patch deployed to canary (scim-intake v2.3.8) which normalizes Content-Type header matching (ignores charset and parameter order) and ensures delta PATCH flows call cacheInvalidator.notifyUserChange(user_id). After canary validation, the fix will be rolled to prod. Workaround previously provided: have IdP send PUT or wait 2 minutes before relying on deprovisioned privileges.
payload.summary: SCIM PATCH Content-Type discrepancy causes role cache divergence and intermittent 403s for recently deprovisioned admins
