payload.description:
Issue summary:
Polarflare observed a class of streaming requests that never emit the finalization marker ("[EOS]" token) when clients close mid-stream and immediately reconnect. This left server-side sessions in a half-finalized state: connections showed as closed, but token accounting and billing counters continued to count tokens for up to 30 minutes until garbage collection kicked in.

Impact:
- Multiple Polarflare production customers saw inflated token usage in billing reports for the window 2026-03-09 02:00-04:30 UTC.
- Several long-lived streaming sessions from Polarflare agents remained tracked in the serving runtime metrics (inflight_streams > expected).
- Customer escalated to Redwood Support via their enterprise SLA channel and asked for immediate mitigation and invoice remediation.

Environment:
- Production; us-east-1, dedicated pool (pool-id: pf-us-east-3) owned by Polarflare account pf-4821.
- Affected variants: redwood-rlhf-v1 pinned to v2026-02-26-rc and a fallback to llama-extended-13b in some regions.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Open streaming generation with client that does not wait for final event (client issues early TCP FIN/RST after partial tokens).
2) Immediately re-open a new streaming session for same conversation ID.
3) Observe server keeps old session counters until GC timeout, and billing shows both sessions' tokens counted.

Observed behavior:
- Serving runtime maintained an internal "finalizer_pending" state for sessions where the finalization RPC was interrupted.
- Token accounting service incremented counters on chunk receipt but relied on finalizer acknowledgements to decrement transient reservation. When finalizer never arrived, the reservation was not cleared timely.
- Metrics: inflight_streams for pf-us-east-3 spiked to 182 (baseline 14), token_reservations_pending peaked at 41k tokens.

Expected behavior:
- If client disconnects before finalization, server should mark session aborted, clear reservation immediately, and emit an explicit abort event to billing and tracing.

Workarounds applied during incident:
- Temporarily applied a safety TTL in the routing layer to force-close streams that had not emitted finalization after 30s of idle (rolled to pf-us-east-3 at 2026-03-09T03:12:00Z).
- Enabled emergency token-crediting rule in billing to stop counting pending reservations for Polarflare while investigation in progress.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-09 02:06: Customer reported spike in usage; Support opened SUP-934562.
- 2026-03-09 02:28: Initial triage: identified unusual inflight_streams and token_reservations metrics.
- 2026-03-09 03:10: Engineering hypothesis: finalizer ack path not robust to ECONNRESET; rollback/GC needed.
- 2026-03-09 03:12: Safety TTL enforced via routing rules.
- 2026-03-09 04:05: Patch PR created (serving-runtime#2821) that detects mid-stream connection aborts and clears finalizer reservations immediately.
- 2026-03-09 04:50: Patch canary rolled to 10% and observed reservation drop to baseline.
- 2026-03-09 06:00: Patch rolled to 100% for pf-us-east-3.
- 2026-03-09 09:20: Billing team issued provisional credits and paused auto-invoicing for the window.
- 2026-03-12 14:00: Follow-up review completed; post-incident actions assigned.

Customer communication summary:
- Updated customer at 02:45 with acknowledgement and high-touch escalation.
- Shared temporary mitigations at 03:30 and confirmed preliminary rollback of overcount at 05:20.
- Issued provisional credit and committed to formal invoice adjustment pending audit at 2026-03-12.

Additional notes:
2026-03-09 03:30 - Support (Aisha): Notified Polarflare of temporary TTL mitigation; requested customer to hold on bulk replays until fix deployed.
Key findings and tests:
- Reproduction: created a toy client that sends a TCP RST immediately after receiving partial tokens; server state machine left session in finalizer_pending.
- Root cause: finalizer ack path relied on normal HTTP/2 stream lifecycle callbacks; on abrupt ECONNRESET the callback path did not trigger finalizer cleanup. This is a combination of a serving-runtime race and a missing defensive cleanup in token-accounting.
- Logs (sample):
  [2026-03-09T02:07:21Z] pool=pf-us-east-3 stream_id=0x7a3 finalizer_state=WAITING tokens_reserved=120
  [2026-03-09T02:07:21Z] net: connection reset by peer (RST) stream_id=0x7a3
  [2026-03-09T02:07:21Z] finalizer_check: no ack callback triggered for stream_id=0x7a3
- Metric references: Grafana panels 'pf-us-east-3 / inflight_streams' and 'token_reservations_pending' show correlated spike; internal alert 'STREAM-LEAK-3m' fired at 02:12.
- Mitigation verification: added instrumentation to emit 'finalizer_forced_clears' metric; saw 4.1k forced clears across pf-us-east-3 after TTL enforcement.
Engineering deployed hotfix (serving-runtime PR #2821) that: (1) makes finalizer cleanup resilient to abrupt connection closes by moving cleanup to the lower-level socket close handler; (2) adds a 30s safety TTL in routing as an additional guard; (3) introduces a gated metric (finalizer_forced_clears) and an alert to detect regressions. Billing halted counting of pending reservations for Polarflare during the incident window and issued provisional credit. Customer notified and a joint RCA call scheduled.
Rollout notes: patch canaried at 10% at 2026-03-09T04:50 and rolled to 100% for pf-us-east-3 at 2026-03-09T06:00. No regressions observed in 48h post-rollout.

2026-03-20 - Complete billing audit and issue final invoice adjustment (owner: Priya Menon) - status: in progress
2026-03-18 - Expand finalizer_forced_clears alert to cover all dedicated pools (owner: Marcelo Rivera) - status: todo
2026-03-22 - Add explicit abort event to tracing docs and update SDKs to document recommended client shutdown behavior (owner: Developer Relations - Kayla Thompson) - status: todo
2026-04-01 - Retrospective in SRE/Serving team; include test harness for abrupt-redisconnect scenarios (owner: Jenna Liu) - status: todo

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a consistent P99 latency increase (~350-450ms) for requests pinned to eu-west when their traffic appears to traverse a US egress/edge before returning to EU serving instances. They are using Dedicated capacity with a strict region pin (project-level pin to eu-west). Customer wants: (1) explanation of why traffic might take a multi-hop path across regions despite pinning, (2) confirmation about whether any data leaves the EU region (egress for processing vs egress for routing), and (3) guidance or configuration to ensure single-region egress for residency guarantees.

Impact:
- Customer-facing inference latency increase on P99 for EU users (from typical 140ms -> 500-600ms for some requests).
- User experience degradation for real-time inference endpoints used in production for trading insights.
- No reported data leak; main concern is latency and confirming residency guarantees for compliance.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool (dedicated-23), capacity reserved in eu-west.
- API endpoint: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
- Customer region pin: project config pin_region = "eu-west" (strict).
- Time window observed: 2026-03-12 09:00 -> 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC
- Example request-id headers: x-request-id: fc9a1b2d-e7a5-4f2f-9a6e-1f2b3c4d5e6f

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Pin a project to eu-west in the Dedicated console.
2) Send 1000 small-generation requests (~40 tokens) from a client in eu-west.
3) Observe P50/P95/P99 on customer side and compare to Redwood Console per-token latency.
4) Filter requests where x-request-id matches observed high-p99 (example IDs included below).

Observed behavior:
- For ~3-5% of requests, traces show an outbound hop to an edge in us-east before the request reaches eu-west serving instance. This corresponds to a spike in P99.
- Redwood Console shows model served from eu-west instance, but traces include an extra network leg (edge -> core -> back to eu).
- No 5xx errors, request succeeds.

Expected behavior:
- All traffic for a project pinned to eu-west should be routed and processed within eu-west without cross-region egress for inference path. 

Logs and traces (redacted):
- Example trace snippet (customer-provided):
  - request-id: fc9a1b2d-e7a5-4f2f-9a6e-1f2b3c4d5e6f
  - client -> edge-eu-west-01 (20ms) -> api-gateway-us-east-03 (210ms) -> serving-eu-03 (45ms) -> response path 230ms -> total 505ms
- Console route logs (sample): "route decision: sticky-affinity-expired -> fallback-edge: us-east-03 -> selected: eu-west-serving-03"

Additional notes from customer:
- They recently toggled stickiness TTL from 24h to 15m as an attempt to improve load distribution across dedicated pool.
- They are concerned whether any sensitive data is leaving eu region (privacy/compliance).
2026-03-13 11:02 - Support (Asha Mehta): Thanks for the detailed repro and trace. We're triaging with infra. Can you confirm whether the requests with multi-hop show any different model-version or host tags?
2026-03-13 13:45 - Customer (S. Petrov, FinCloud): Confirmed model_version: gptx-3.8-16k@v12 for all traces. Host tags for all 'served' segments are eu-west. The odd leg is always an api-gateway located in us-east.
2026-03-13 16:20 - Support (Asha Mehta): Noted. Looping in Diego (networking) and runtime to check routing heuristics and sticky-affinity TTL handling.
2026-03-14 09:05 - Infra (Diego Alvarez): Initial finding: smart-routing fallback policy can select an edge in any region when sticky-affinity TTL is expired/violated and the local edge doesn't have a fresh cached route to the serving pod. The selected edge is used to orchestrate the request and may add a cross-region hop before the serving runtime is reached. Investigating whether this path causes egress of request payload beyond EU for processing, or only for control-plane routing.
2026-03-14 11:08 - Security (Mira O'Connor): From a compliance perspective, control-plane routing metadata does not contain customer prompt content. We need to confirm whether any KV cache or prefix tokens are being forwarded during control ops.
Preliminary hypothesis: Changing stickiness TTL to 15m exposed cases where the edge node that initially handled a client (and had a warm cached prefix/KV route) expired and another client connection hit a different edge that lacked the route. The smart-routing fallback currently may select the closest available control edge, which can be cross-region. That edge then coordinates with the eu-west serving pod resulting in a visible extra leg in traces. Need to validate whether this control-edge performs any token-level proxying vs only routing control/handshake.

What we've checked so far:
- Console logs show serving kept in eu-west and model served there (no model shard in us-east).
- No 5xx or auth failures.
- Network team captured packet counts and did not find full request bodies in control-plane traffic samples (redacted).

Open questions for engineering:
- Is the routing decision for fallback-edge strictly control-plane (no customer payload), or can it forward partial request payloads (e.g., prefix cache warmup)?
- Can we add a per-project enforcement flag to avoid selecting non-EU control edges when project pin is strict?
1) Networking to run a packet-level capture (redacted) for a set of 50 reproduced requests to confirm payload vs metadata content. 2) Runtime team to audit smart-routing codepath for fallback selection and document whether any customer tokens are proxied across the control edge. 3) If confirmed control-plane-only, update customer with mitigation (increase stickiness TTL or enable local-edge-residency-preference). 4) If payload crosses regions, propose quick mitigation: prefer 'strict-egress' option for dedicated projects or add explicit egress-region affinity flag. 5) Create follow-up INT ticket to consider adding enforcement in routing logic and update runbook.
Please produce 10 request-ids (x-request-id) that show the multi-hop behavior and confirm whether you have any IP allowlists or client-side proxy settings that might cause requests to originate from non-EU egress. Also, revert stickiness TTL to 24h for a 2-hour test window if feasible so we can validate whether the incidence rate drops.
Temporary: Recommend restoring stickiness TTL to previous 24h or enabling the 'prefer-local-edge' project flag (if you have it) to reduce cross-region fallback decisions. This should reduce the multi-hop occurrences while we validate routing behavior.
payload.summary: Multi-hop egress observed when pinning to EU — increased P99 latency; clarification on residency policy and routing heuristics

payload.description:
Issue summary:
NimbleChat reports that alerting rules configured on console dashboards are not firing for a subset of low-volume usage metrics between 2026-03-09 02:00 and 2026-03-11 07:30 UTC. The metrics still appear in raw event logs but are absent from the aggregated rollup tables used by alert evaluation.

Impact:
- Customer-facing alerts (rate and error-rate thresholds) did not trigger for 2 of NimbleChat's critical routes, causing delayed on-call awareness.
- Affects enterprise customers using retention compaction settings that enable partition pruning.

Environment:
- Production, us-east region (us-east-1).
- Console alerting evaluation uses hourly rollups + partitioned aggregation.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Query console metric rollup table for customer_id:nimblechat and route X between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-11.
2) Compare against raw event stream query for same timeframe (request_id present).
3) Re-run alert evaluation job for the rule id shown in comments.

Observed behavior:
- Rollup query returns zero rows for several hour partitions where raw events exist (confirmed by sample request IDs).
- Alert evaluation job treats missing partitions as zeros and does not fire.

Expected behavior:
- Rollup tables should contain aggregated counts for partitions where raw events exist, or alerting should fallback to raw-event evaluation when rollups are pruned.

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Manual re-processing of the compacted partitions restored aggregates for the missing hours; customer asked for notification if pruning logic will cause future gaps.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 16:20 - NimbleChat (Customer): Thanks for the fast responses — can you confirm which hours were reprocessed? We need an ETA on permanent fix or mitigation to avoid reprocessing every week.
2026-03-13 11:55 - Product (Aisha Patel): Adding request to Console roadmap to add alerting fallback to raw-event scans if rollups missing. Draft spec in Confluence linked in related_confluence_pages.
2026-03-13 12:30 - NimbleChat (Customer): Confirmed they received alert notifications after reprocessing. Asked for postmortem and whether an SLA credit applies for missed alerting window.
Hypothesis: retention-worker's partition pruning step runs a low-volume eviction heuristic which prunes partitions older than the configured retention threshold if aggregate expected cardinality below threshold. In this case a race occurred: raw events were written to object-store, but the rollup backfill job (which reads object-store and writes hourly rollups) had not completed prior to the pruning sweep. We confirmed timestamps where object-store contains events (grep on request_id) but rollup table had no rows.
Queries run:
- raw events: SELECT * FROM raw_events WHERE request_id IN ('rq_1001','rq_1002','rq_1003','rq_1004'); -> returned 4 rows with timestamps in affected hours.
- rollup check: SELECT hour, sum(count) FROM metric_rollups WHERE customer_id='nimblechat' AND hour BETWEEN '2026-03-09' AND '2026-03-11' -> missing rows for specific hours.
Reproduction steps for eng: ran retention_worker in dry-run mode against staging with mocked backlog; confirmed pruning decision when backfill lag > 30m.
Root cause: pruning algorithm uses backfill lag estimate but does not treat hours with active alert evaluation windows as protected. Edge case occurs for low-volume customers where backfill can be delayed by transient compute scheduling.
Work completed (2026-03-13):
1) Immediate: reprocessed the missing partitions for NimbleChat to restore rollup aggregates and retriggered alert evaluations. Customer notified and confirmed receipt of alerts.
2) Short-term code fix: merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8123 which adds a safeguard to retention-worker to skip pruning partitions that are within alert-eval lookback windows when backfill lag exceeds threshold. Deployed to staging for validation.
3) Medium-term: engineering to implement an alerting fallback to raw-event evaluation when rollups are missing and to add a monitoring alert for pruning-induced gaps (INT-4022).
4) Postmortem planned: include timeline, SLA credit assessment, and runbook changes. Postmortem doc will be attached to this ticket when complete.
Follow-ups assigned:
- INT-4022: Update retention-worker heuristics and add unit tests (assignee: Riley Chen).
- Add console telemetry to surface 'pruned-but-unbackfilled' partition counts in daily health dashboard (assignee: Product/Telemetry).
Customer-facing note: Provided NimbleChat with reprocessing summary and mitigation timeline. Offered to schedule a technical review of retention configuration.
payload.summary: Console alert evaluations skip low-volume metric partitions after background partition pruning

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightCart reports repeated duplicate external tool/webhook invocations when using function-calls that return multipart attachments. Impact: Duplicate downstream side effects (order webhook processed twice) causing billing and data integrity problems for the customer. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east, customer routes traffic through corporate gateway that performs header and multipart boundary normalization.

Observed behavior: When BrightCart sends a function-calling request that results in a multipart (multipart/mixed) tool output attachment, their corporate proxy rewrites the MIME boundary token. Redwood's idempotency normalization logic includes a canonicalization step that includes boundary tokens for multipart bodies, so the idempotency key calculated on the server differs from the hash the client expects after proxy rewrite. This causes the platform to treat retried requests as new and re-execute tool calls, leading to duplicate webhook calls.

Expected behavior: Retries or network-level rewrites should not cause repeated tool invocations; idempotency should survive innocuous proxy rewrites or we should detect boundary-only differences and still deduplicate.
1) Customer issues a function-call via Redwood SDK (examples provided in both Python and TS) that triggers an external tool which returns a multipart attachment (Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=----redwood-abc123).
2) Traffic passes through a corporate gateway that normalizes/re-writes MIME boundaries (e.g., boundary=----corp-xyz789) and may adjust Content-Type header whitespace/quoting.
3) Client SDK performs a retry (exponential backoff) on a 5xx or streaming disconnect; the SDK includes an idempotency header based on client-side canonicalization that uses the original boundary token.
4) Server receives a request where the body boundary token differs from the client's canonicalized token and computes a different idempotency key, causing the request to be treated as new and re-invoking the tool/webhook.
2026-03-10T18:22:41Z - request_id=rcv-9f2a - Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=----corp-xyz789
2026-03-10T18:22:42Z - idempotency_check: client-key=sha256:abcd1234, server-key=sha256:ef56ef56 - mismatch -> re-execute tool
2026-03-10T18:22:42Z - tool_execution: webhook POST to https://hooks.brightcart.com/orders -> 200
2026-03-10T18:22:43Z - retry triggered by SDK on client; new request_id=rcv-9f2b - server computes server-key=sha256:11223344 -> treated as new -> second webhook POST to https://hooks.brightcart.com/orders -> 200
Initial triage: Reproduced on a Dedicated customer environment with corporate proxy that rewrites multipart boundary tokens.
Hypothesis: idempotency normalization currently includes exact multipart boundary token in canonicalization hash. Gateway rewrites cause mismatches even though payload semantic equivalence remains.
Checked SDK implementations: Python SDK canonicalizes body bytes including boundary token; TS SDK does the same. No current tolerant normalization for multipart boundaries.
Server side: serving-runtime compares idempotency signatures derived from the received bytes; there is a server-side normalization pass but it preserves boundary string for integrity checks.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - BrightCart support contact (Elena Martell): Impact is moderate but causing duplicate order notifications to downstream systems; asked for immediate mitigation and timeline.
Idempotency canonicalization algorithm uses the raw multipart boundary token as part of the signature. Corporate gateway rewrites boundary tokens during transit, producing different byte-level payloads for logically equivalent content. This causes retries to be recognized as new requests and re-trigger tool invocations.
1) Short-term: Advise BrightCart to disable client-side retries for function-call requests that trigger multipart attachments until a fix is deployed, or configure their gateway to preserve multipart boundary tokens.
2) As an alternative, suggest switching tool behavior to be inherently idempotent (e.g., use event dedup keys at webhook receiver) to tolerate duplicates.
In progress - engineering proposal accepted to implement tolerant multipart-normalization in idempotency calculation. Plan: canonicalize multipart boundaries to a stable placeholder token before computing server-side idempotency signature, and update SDKs to apply the same normalization. Will include a rollout that preserves existing signatures for a grace period (dual-hash check) to avoid immediate breakage of existing idempotency tokens.
payload.summary: Multipart response boundary rewritten by corporate proxy -> idempotency header normalization mismatch -> duplicate tool/function invocations

Customers on the private deployment report sudden 403s for administrative API calls that rely on conditional RBAC rules evaluated against JWT custom claims. Errors started after an ingress edge upgrade in us-east. This ticket tracks the investigation and remediation for Arcana Health (private tenant).
Multiple service accounts in the customer's private VPC receiving 403 on admin GraphQL routes; blocks operation automation and scheduled model rollouts. Estimated ~20% of ARC tenants impacted in us-east cluster during outage window.
1) Use service account token with custom claim 'tenant.env' set to 'arcana:prod' 2) Send POST to /admin/graphql route through customer's private ingress 3) Observe 403 with 'rbac:condition-eval-false' in response headers
Requests that previously passed RBAC now fail with 403. Request logs show the claim header present but conditional expression in RBAC evaluated to false.
Conditional expressions that reference JWT claim keys should evaluate using the original claim key names/values provided by the IdP exchange and preserved through the ingress path.

- 2026-03-10: Support reproduced issue with customer's token; confirmed mismatch in claim key casing during header propagation.
- Observed that the upgraded ingress (edge-proxy v3.7.0) started normalizing header names by capitalizing dotted claim keys (e.g., tenant.env -> tenant.Env) when serializing into X-JWT-CLAIMS header.
- RBAC engine uses case-sensitive JSON path lookups for condition evaluation; mismatch causes expression to short-circuit.

1) Roll back edge-proxy to v3.6.8 for affected us-east nodes (completed in canary, scheduled cluster rollback).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when a long SSE streaming session is resumed after an auth-token refresh the final payload (attachment URL + trailer metadata) is never received by their client. Instead the stream includes two near-identical heartbeat frames in quick succession and then connection silence. This appears to correlate with an auth refresh being processed concurrently with our SSE resume logic on the same session.

Impact:
- Key customer flows that deliver generated attachments (PDF links/embeds) are missing the attachment URL; end-user sees partial text but no downloadable link.
- Affects ~10% of resumed streams for this customer during their peak window.
- Customer is on a Dedicated plan with strict SLAs; business impact reported as "users cannot download generated statements".

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (dedicated tenant) in us-east-1
- Production traffic, customer uses long-running chat + attachment feature that streams interim text and final attachment URL as the last event
- Model: redwood-v1.3-large

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long streaming generation that ends with an attachment (customer artifact) returned as the last event.
2) Force an auth token rotation on the client (their middleware refreshes at the same time).
3) Allow connection to briefly drop (e.g., client network swap) and rely on SSE resume behavior.
4) Observe that the stream yields two rapid heartbeat events followed by silence; final attachment event is missing.

Observed behavior:
- Two heartbeat-like events (small keepalive JSON envelopes) are observed arriving back-to-back during resume.
- The trailing attachment metadata event ("attachment_url": "https://...") never makes it to the client.
- Server logs show the resume completed and the serving-worker emitted the attachment event, but downstream API gateway logs show the final event was dropped or replaced by an extra keepalive.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should replay buffered/generated tail events exactly once and deliver the final attachment metadata as the terminal event; heartbeats should not duplicate and should not suppress trailing payloads.

Workaround (customer):
- Customer temporarily added extra polling for the attachment endpoint (after a 2s delay) to surface missing attachments; workable but increases cost and latency.

Logs / snippets (redacted):
- Gateway trace (proxy): resume-id=abc123: forwarded event: heartbeat {"ts": 167.., "type": "hb"}
- Gateway trace: forwarded event: heartbeat {"ts": 167..+10ms, "type": "hb"}
- Serving-runtime: emitted terminal_event {"type":"attachment", "url":"https://files.finledger/..."}
- API gateway: downstream socket closed after second heartbeat; final event aborted with ECONNRESET

Notes: customer supplied pcap and SDK logs; see attached artifacts in ticket thread.

Additional notes:
2026-03-01 12:05 - Customer (FinLedger - S. Romero): Uploaded pcap + SDK logs. Notes that outage occurs when they rotate an OAuth token and network briefly switches from corp VPN to home network.
2026-03-03 08:58 - Support (Aisha Patel): Provided customer workaround (client polling) and ETA for patch: 2026-03-05 for config mitigation; full fix in 2026-03-10 release. Customer accepted workaround temporarily.
Initial hypothesis: concurrent auth refresh triggers session rebind at API gateway, race with resume flush causes gateway to interpret trailing event as a stale control frame.
Reproduction steps executed in staging: triggered client-side token rotation during resume; reproduced missing terminal event ~6/10 attempts under load.
Root cause narrowed: gateway treats the late small frame as an out-of-order keepalive and performs conn reset when it arrives while TLS session rebind in progress (0rtt-like behavior). Serving-runtime correctly emitted event; loss happens at gateway+conn layer.
Related change: resume backpressure adjustments in PR #4987 lowered the buffer window; combined with token rebind timings this increases probability of dropping trailing frames.
Temporary mitigation: increase resume buffer window at gateway to tolerate quick control-frame bursts and avoid conn tear-down on near-simultaneous keepalive frames.
Mitigation applied (2026-03-04): gateway config bump to 150ms resume flush tolerance for affected dedicated cluster in us-east-1. Monitoring for regression.
Customer confirmed on 2026-03-04 that missing attachments dropped to 0/200 reproductions; accepted as interim fix.
Root fix scheduled: runtime + gateway coordination to sequence auth-refresh hooks before resume flush and to tag resume frames with a session-stable marker. Target date: 2026-03-10.
Postmortem action items: (1) add an integration test that simulates auth-rotation during resume; (2) add gateway metric for 'resume-silence-after-heartbeat' and an alert; (3) update docs runbook to recommend client backoff when rotating tokens during active streams.
Close plan: resolve ticket once full fix deployed and 3 days of no regression in customer telemetry; customer to be offered credits for operational impact (pending billing review).
payload.summary: Concurrent auth refresh during SSE resume causes duplicated heartrate frames and omission of attachment URL in tail

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-lived gRPC streaming sessions (chat/generation routes) on their Private deployment reliably drop after ~30 minutes. Sessions terminate with application-level errors (gRPC INTERNAL / UNAVAILABLE) even though pod health and CPU/memory are normal.

Impact:
Multiple production customers behind the same egress appliance (FinLedger) experience intermittent stream failures that interrupt in-progress conversations and chunked streaming responses. Severity is high because sessions are stateful and user-facing.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployment in customer's VPC (FinLedger)
- Prod, us-east-1 region
- Corporate outbound proxy (BlueBox Inspect 3.2) doing TLS interception and outbound filtering
- Serving nodes use BoringSSL-based runtime (Redwood serving-runtime v2.13.1)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long-lived gRPC streaming session via the customer's app (server-side streaming generation).
2) Stream is stable for ~30 minutes.
3) At ~30 minute mark, stream abruptly terminates with error on client: "rpc error: code = Internal desc = stream terminated" or similar.
4) Server logs around the time show TLS handshake/alert messages and connection close.

Observed logs / captures provided by customer: (snippets)
- serving-runtime: "ERROR tls_handshake: unexpected message during handshake, closing connection"
- kernel net logs: repeated FIN from client side following TLS alert
- tcpdump on egress: a TLS ClientHello labeled as "renegotiation" from the corporate proxy at t+00:30:12

Expected behaviour:
Long-lived streams should remain open barring explicit client/server close or network loss. TLS interception should not cause application-level connection termination.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Configure application-level keepalives to close and re-open streams before 25 minutes as a mitigation (client change).
- Configure egress device to operate in TLS passthrough mode for Redwood endpoints (recommended) to avoid interception.

Permanent remediation (under investigation):
- Customer to change egress proxy policy to disable TLS renegotiation or not perform active rekeying on in-flight connections.
- Engineering to add clearer failure type detection and automatic retry with backoff at the streaming layer; follow-up PR opened.

Attachments/References:
- PCAP supplied by customer (s3 link in customer ticket)
- Slack thread: #support-private-deploy (link: slack://channel?team=redwood&id=C12345)
- Serving runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4587

Timeline and findings:
2026-03-12 09:15 UTC - Customer opened ticket after multiple incidents of mid-conversation drops.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Support reproduced issue in customer's staging mirror using their BlueBox appliance configuration. Connection stable until ~30m then dropped.
2026-03-12 13:30 UTC - Packet capture review: outbound egress device issues a TLS renegotiation ClientHello mid-connection. Serving node responds with fatal alert (handshake_failure) and tear-down.
2026-03-13 08:00 UTC - Confirmed runtime uses BoringSSL where renegotiation is disabled by default for security reasons; library returns fatal/NO_RENEGOTIATION alert when peer requests renegotiation.
2026-03-13 12:45 UTC - Reproduced with mitmproxy configured for on-the-fly rekeying; behavior matches customer capture.

Hypothesis:
- The corporate egress proxy attempts to rekey or perform an inspection-triggered renegotiation mid-stream. BoringSSL in serving-runtime rejects renegotiation (security-disabled), causing the server to abort the connection, which surfaces as gRPC INTERNAL/UNAVAILABLE.

Actions taken so far:
- Shared pcap and log excerpts with customer network team.
- Recommended immediate mitigations (passthrough, client keepalive change).
- Opened internal PR to make streaming layer detect fatal TLS alert with clearer error and perform automatic re-open/retry (non-destructive) for idempotent endpoints. PR link in related_github_prs.
- Raised postmortem follow-up to evaluate adding a runtime knob to accept TLS renegotiation only when explicitly configured (security review required).

Next steps:
- Coordinate with FinLedger network team to disable renegotiation for Redwood endpoints; customer has scheduled a maintenance window 2026-03-15.
- Engineering to land enhanced retry behavior for streaming endpoints (PR under review, target 2026-03-20).
- Draft runbook entry for Support and SRE that covers detecting TLS renegotiation events and applying the passthrough workaround.


Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:12 Customer (FinLedger): Uploaded PCAP and BlueBox config. Noted that their proxy performs rekeying policies for long sessions.
2026-03-13 14:02 Eng (SRE): Confirmed serving-runtime uses BoringSSL and rejects renegotiation. Suggested customer disable rekeying or use passthrough for endpoints.
2026-03-13 16:30 Support: Sent mitigation guide to customer (keepalive change + passthrough example). Customer accepted temporary keepalive change and scheduled passthrough test.
2026-03-14 09:10 FinLedger network: Will test passthrough during maintenance window 2026-03-15 02:00-03:00 UTC and report results.
Workaround and customer mitigation applied; awaiting customer passthrough test. Engineering PR created to improve streaming retry and error diagnostics. Permanent fix depends on security decision re: renegotiation support.
payload.summary: Long-lived gRPC streams disconnect after ~30m when customer egress proxy initiates TLS renegotiation

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a rolling kernel swap for a quantized variant of redwood-llama-3-13b, KV cache entries were misrouted to an incompatible deserialization path. This caused a small percentage of completions to include tokens copied from unrelated customer requests. One BlackFjord request contained sensitive financial identifiers and partial SSN-like strings that were reflected back in another completion.

Impact:
- Customer: BlackFjord Capital (enterprise) experienced exposure of PII in 12 completions across a 27 minute window on 2026-03-10.
- Functional: Streaming completions truncated or interleaved with unrelated prompt fragments for ~0.05% of requests served by the affected pool.
- Business: Customer escalated to legal/security and paused traffic to the affected model for regulatory-sensitive workloads.

Environment:
- prod/us-east, dedicated pool serving enterprise tenants on redwood-llama-3-13b quant variants.
- Kernel swap triggered by automated rollout: kernel-selection service v3.12.1 -> v3.12.2.

Steps to reproduce (investigation method):
1) Synthetic load replay of customer traffic with preserved prompt fingerprints.
2) Force kernel-selection to swap to quant-int8 path while concurrent prefix lookups hit hot shards.
3) Observe mixed deserialization in KV lookup path; some entries decoded with legacy layout and appended into generation buffer.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Serving logs show KV lookup hits with mismatched schema tags: "kv:tag=0x6d" vs expected "0x72" around 2026-03-10T14:07:xxZ.
- Traces (trace IDs provided to customer) show a short window where kernel handshake allowed an incompatible kernel to be scheduled onto active workers.
- Grafana: token interleaving rate spike correlates with kernel-change posterior 14:05-14:32 UTC.
- Audit: No public S3 uploads contain PII; exposure limited to runtime memory and transient completions.

Mitigation performed during incident:
- Immediate rollback of kernel-selection to v3.12.1 across impacted pools (14:12 UTC).
- Invalidate and purge prefix/KV caches for affected GPU pool (14:14 UTC).
- Forced drain of in-flight connections on affected nodes and restarted serving processes (14:20-14:30 UTC).
- Rotated service-side signing keys for cache metadata to prevent reuse (14:45 UTC).
- Notified BlackFjord Security with full timeline and example traces; activated joint call and retained evidence package.

Resolution / customer-facing actions:
- Confirmed removal of affected entries and applied additional scrub to remove reproduced PII from logs and observability exports.
- Provided raw evidence and forensics export to BlackFjord under NDA; coordinated with their legal team.
- Issued a two-week credit for affected capacity and waived associated request charges during the incident window.
- Opened a cross-team remediation epic to prevent recurrence and improve test coverage.

Post-incident investigation summary (high level):
Root cause hypothesis: A non-atomic kernel swap path allowed a short interval where workers ran kernel binary A for compute but continued to use cache serialization schema from kernel binary B. Combined with a recent change to quantized serialization layout in v3.12.2, this produced misdecoded prefix entries that were appended to unrelated generation contexts.
Contributing factors:
- Lack of an end-to-end integration test for rolling kernel swaps with live cache schema variations.
- No guardrail to block schedule of newer kernel on nodes with cached legacy-encoded entries.

Next steps / action items:
- (ENG-1) Implement atomic kernel + cache-schema version gating; prevent non-backwards-compatible kernel from scheduling until cache invalidation completes.
- (ENG-2) Add end-to-end gating test in CI that simulates rolling kernel swaps with active prefix cache.
- (SRE-1) Create a dedicated alert for schema-mismatch tags in KV path; threshold tie to immediate rollout rollback.
- (DX-1) Update runbook and customer-facing incident template for any PII exposure with clear remediation checklist.
- (CS-1) Follow up with BlackFjord weekly until the remediation audit is accepted by their security team.

Attachments / evidence references: traces: trace-91a2f3, trace-91a2f4; grafana dashboard screenshot links were provided to customer on 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 16:45 UTC — BlackFjord Security (external comment via support@blackfjord.com): Appreciate the rapid response. Requesting formal statement that no persisted storage contains PII and that further mitigations will be tracked.

payload.description:
Issue summary: FlowCart (dedicated customer) reports a sharp throughput collapse and prolonged p99 latency spikes across their reserved pool during their peak ingestion window (09:10-09:40 ET) on 2026-03-13. The pattern is repeatable each weekday morning. Impact: sustained failed requests, client timeouts, and downstream backpressure in FlowCart pipelines. Note: this is not an infrastructure-wide outage; affected hosts are concentrated in us-east serving the customer's reserved capacity but cross-tenant interference observed on a subset of GPUs.

High level hypothesis: a burst of many short-lived inference streams from a single tenant is causing persistent slot fragmentation and aggressive KV cache eviction. That, in turn, correlates with brief but recurrent PCIe latency spikes (observed as device IO wait and GPU DMA stalls) which amplify the scheduling delays and cause the autoscaler to overshoot during warmup windows, worsening p99 latency.

Customer visible symptoms: elevated p95/p99 across text generation endpoints, intermittent 5xx stream disconnects, and increased retry traffic.
1) Use dedicated FlowCart pool in prod-us-east with tenant pinned model rwd-3b-quantized
2) Generate an artificial workload that opens 500 short streams per minute (each stream sends 1-3 short prompts, then closes) over a 10-minute window
3) Observe scheduler slot allocation, KV cache churn, and GPU IO wait metrics; watch p50/p95/p99 on token generation and overall throughput
4) Compare to a control run with fewer long-lived streams (50 streams with 50 tokens each) — issue does not reproduce under that workload shape
2026-03-13T09:12:07Z host-312: serving-runtime: batch_worker: GPU DMA stall detected (device_io_wait=420ms)

2026-03-13T09:12:08Z host-312: scheduler: slot_fragmentation=0.78, small_stream_ratio=0.64, pending_queue=312

2026-03-13T09:12:09Z autoscaler: scale_up triggered: +8 slots; observed allocation lag 74s; multiple preemptions logged

2026-03-13T09:13:01Z network: nvlink/pci_util: pcie_latency_spike_ms=360, correlated with increased retry rate from tenant

Initial triage by support: verified customer pool is in dedicated mode and pinned to us-east hosts. Noted strong correlation between short-stream bursts and p99 spikes; reproduced with local load generator.
SRE ran perf captures on two affected hosts: found repeated small-batch dispatches with high DMA latency and elevated gpu_io_wait during burst windows. NVLink/PCIe metrics show short-lived latency bursts (~200-500ms) aligned with KV-cache eviction bursts.
Heap/KV-cache analysis: aggressive eviction rate observed; cache hot set thrashing when many unique prefixes are requested across short streams. This increased CPU-GPU synchronization overhead (small kernel launches) and more PCIe transfers per token.
Autoscaler behavior: reactive policy scaled up based on queue length but allocation lag and subsequent slot fragmenting caused more small-stream dispatches which further worsened contention — feedback loop identified.
No evidence of hardware faults on GPUs (no ECC errors). Affected hosts show normal temps and power; root cause appears workload-pattern-induced IO amplification rather than host failure.
Workload shape: sudden multi-tenant short-stream swarm causing high small-batch dispatch frequency, persistent KV cache thrashing, and amplified PCIe/NVLink DMA latency spikes. The autoscaler’s reactive ramp-up and the scheduler's current slot granularity allowed a feedback loop that created sustained contention on a subset of GPUs.
Short-term mitigation: applied per-tenant concurrency cap at the pool ingress for FlowCart at 2026-03-13T11:20, which immediately reduced p99 and stabilized throughput. Rolled out an autoscaler policy tweak to add a conservative warmup buffer for dedicated pools during known peak windows.

Long-term fix: merged scheduler change to coalesce many short streams into consolidated micro-batches and to limit concurrent small-streams per GPU (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/4123). Also added a PCIe latency alarm to the pool health dashboard and a runbook entry for noisy-tenant isolation. Patch deployed to canary hosts 2026-03-14 and slated full rollout after validation.
1) Validate scheduler micro-batching at load across 3 canary clusters (owner: Raj Patel, due: 2026-03-20)
2) Add PCIe/NVLink 1m/5m latency charts to Redwood Console for dedicated pools (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-17)
3) Update autoscaler default warmup policy for dedicated pools with high short-stream ratios (owner: Autoscale squad, due: 2026-03-21)
4) Create support playbook snippet to throttle or cordon noisy tenants without a full eviction (owner: Support SRE, due: 2026-03-16)
5) Follow up with FlowCart on workload shaping recommendations and offer help creating a backoff client (owner: Customer Success, due: 2026-03-18)
payload.summary: Throughput collapse and p99 latency spikes during morning short-stream swarm; evidence of PCIe latency bursts and noisy tenant KV-cache churn

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate outbound webhook POSTs to their payment orchestration endpoint when the customer's API key is rotated while long-running model requests are in flight. Observed behaviour: single user action results in 2-3 identical webhook deliveries. Impact: financial reconciliation mismatches and duplicate idempotent operations at the customer's downstream service. Occurs in their private VPC deployment after we issued a temporary key rotation to remediate a suspected key leak.

Context: FinEdge runs Redwood Private in their VPC. They use the Python SDK (v1.8.4) with automatic API key refresh enabled. Many of their requests trigger function/tool calls that in turn call their webhook. Key rotation happened at 2026-03-12T17:40:02Z via our KMS rotation API. The customer reports duplicates starting at ~17:40:05Z.

Customer-facing: duplicate idempotent downstream operations (refunds/receipts) observed; billing and reconciliation noise. Affects a single enterprise customer in prod, multiple users. Operational urgency high due to potential financial impact.
1) Deploy a private Redwood container with the customer's config (private connector, webhook endpoint).
2) Use Python SDK v1.8.4 with auto-refresh enabled and a long-running generation (30s+) that triggers a function_call -> webhook.
3) At ~mid-request, invoke an API key rotation via the control plane (simulate by replacing key in KMS and propagating new key).
4) Observe webhook endpoint receiving duplicate POSTs within 2–5s of each other.
5) Re-run without rotation — duplicates do not occur.

Notes: reproduction easiest with concurrent requests to cause overlapping key refresh logic across threads/processes.
Customer-provided logs (sanitized):
- 2026-03-12T17:39:58Z request-id=req-9b1 payload-id=evt-412 function_call=charge_post
- 2026-03-12T17:40:03Z api-key-rotation=begin key-id=k-20260312-01
- 2026-03-12T17:40:05Z webhook-post status=200 idempotency-key=charge_abc123 attempt=1
- 2026-03-12T17:40:05Z webhook-post status=200 idempotency-key=charge_abc123 attempt=2
- SDK debug: token_refresh triggered at 2026-03-12T17:40:04Z; retry loop executed for in-flight request
Server-side traces:  request req-9b1 shows two delivery attempts after auth header rehydration.

Initial hypothesis: when the API key is rotated mid-request, SDK refresh logic triggers a new auth token generation and our client-side retry replays the function_call to the webhook without preserving a server-assigned delivery token, causing the downstream endpoint to accept multiple deliveries.
What we checked: 1) Server request logs show the same webhook payload hash and identical idempotency-key header on both deliveries. 2) SDK v1.8.4 uses a per-request ephemeral nonce and falls back to client-side retry if auth fails; the retry path lacks canonical de-dup token. 3) Private control plane rotation path signals updated key to runtime; however, there is a short window where worker processes refresh and reissue requests.
Preliminary reproduction on staging: reproduced with local env using SDK mod that forces mid-request key swap. Observed duplicated webhook POSTs when the client retried after a 401/403 during rotation.

Ask customer to disable automatic API key rotation during peak processing windows, or apply the following: ensure SDK is pinned to a version (>=1.8.6) that includes the client-side change (see PR 1423) which preserves a server-provided delivery-id on retries. As immediate mitigation, enable webhook-side idempotency by validating idempotency-key header and rejecting duplicates for 60s window.
Engineering plan: 1) Update SDK retry path to attach a stable delivery_id (issued by the runtime when the function_call is first dispatched) to any subsequent retry attempts so downstream webhooks can deduplicate reliably. 2) Add server-side behavior: on key rotation, mark in-flight requests with a stable request token and surface it to SDK via runtime headers. 3) Release SDK patch (v1.8.6) and runtime patch in coordinated rollout to Private customers. 4) Publish runbook and add an automated test that simulates mid-request key rotation.
Target: runtime patch and SDK release within 2 sprints (by 2026-03-28).
Support (Emily Chen) 2026-03-12: Logged initial report from customer; collected sanitized request traces and webhook logs. Escalating to eng due to financial impact.
Eng (Jonah Miller) 2026-03-13: Reproduced in staging with a small harness. Confirmed duplicate POSTs tied to client retry after auth refresh. Adding label 'needs-runtime-change'.
Customer (FinEdge SI) 2026-03-13: We implemented immediate webhook idempotency check; duplicates stopped causing double charges but reconciliation team still wants root cause addressed. Willing to schedule maintenance window for a coordinated patch rollout.
Security (Priya Singh) 2026-03-13: Confirmed key rotation proceeded per policy; no evidence of leak. Rotation triggered by automated policy. Noted that rotation frequency could be reduced for private installs if requested.
In Progress: SDK PR prepared (1423) adding delivery_id preservation on retries. Runtime change required; patch branch open and under review. Customer applied webhook-side dedupe as temporary mitigation; no further duplicates after applying dedupe. Plan a coordinated release with FinEdge on 2026-03-20. Will update ticket when runtime patch is staged.
- Add automated test covering mid-request key rotation and retry dedup semantics.
- Document recommended webhook idempotency header semantics in customer onboarding guide.
- Add a flag in private control plane to schedule rotation outside of high-load windows.
- Coordinate SDK/runtime release notes and migration guide.
If customer requests immediate rollback of rotation: advise against rollback; instead, recommend webhook-side dedupe and SDK pin. If they insist on rollback, schedule maintenance and prepare coordinated runbook.
Key logs to gather if reproducing: runtime trace for request-id, SDK debug with token timestamps, KMS key-change timestamp.
payload.summary: Post-rotation retry causes duplicate outgoing webhook calls after API key rotation (Python SDK, private deployment)

comments: 2026-03-10T15:12:00Z Aisha Patel: 'Customer reports ~5% failure rate for long responses after recent config change to enable q4 fallback for cost savings. Customer impact high since sessions are customer-facing.'

2026-03-11T09:35:00Z Diego Ramos: 'I can reproduce locally by toggling fallback; attaching a script and logs to the ticket. Looks like kernel load blocks event loop for ~300-500ms repeatedly then a later preempt kills the worker.'

2026-03-11T12:10:00Z Priya Singh: 'Temporarily bumped autoscaler preemption timeout from 30s to 90s for FinBank dedicated pool; incidents stopped in canary. Need a permanent fix in serving-runtime to stream heartbeat before termination.'

2026-03-11T16:00:00Z Liam O'Connor: 'Opened PR to add graceful drain/flush on worker shutdown and to make quantized kernel loads async: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1872. Scheduling canary deploy tomorrow.'
payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple streaming chat sessions for FinBank using SSE/WebSocket stop emitting tokens mid-generation for responses longer than ~3s, then the connection is reset with a TCP RST or 502 returned to the client. Impact: Customer-facing chat experiences drop messages and the FinBank mobile app shows repeated 'generation failed' errors for ~5% of long responses. Environment: prod, us-east, enterprise tenancy on dedicated pool with autoscaling and model fallback enabled. Observed behavior: 1) Request starts and initial tokens stream normally. 2) After a latency spike (token emission pause ~4-7s) the server stops sending further chunks. 3) Within 10-20s the connection is closed abruptly. Expected behavior: continuous token streaming until generation completes or graceful error with structured error message and retryable code.
1) Using FinBank enterprise API key, start a streaming chat request with system prompt and a long assistant completion target (>300 tokens).
2) Force model fallback by simultaneously issuing a heavier non-streaming job to saturate the fp16 pool (we reproduced by running a 50-token batch on redwood-open-13b-fp16).
3) Observe token output for the streaming session; when worker fallback to quantized variant occurs we saw stalls and eventual connection reset.
4) Repeat under prod us-east with autoscaler min_capacity set to 2 and max_burst enabled to see consistent repro.
Request trace: trace_id=trc_20260310_5f7a2 - initial chunks at 2026-03-10T14:12:03Z then no emit after 14:12:07Z until RST at 14:12:25Z.
Serving runtime stderr: 'kv_cache_eviction: worker_preempted during in-flight request', repeated at 14:12:08Z.
API gateway: upstream keepalive closed by peer after 17s idle - see logs s3://redwood-ops/logs/finbank/2026-03-10/streaming/trace_trc_20260310_5f7a2.log
2026-03-10 15:00 - Support: Confirmed reproducible under load using FinBank's tenant key. Initial hypothesis: autoscaler or scheduler preempting quantized worker leading to abrupt KV cache loss and no graceful handoff.
2026-03-11 09:20 - Infra: Observed spike in tail latencies coinciding with model fallback events; the runtime issued 'worker_preempt' due to CPU watchdog triggered by a GC/compaction loop when quantized kernels loaded.
2026-03-11 11:45 - Eng: Found missing keepalive refresh for SSE sessions when a worker migrates requests to fallback instances; API gateway keeps connection open but upstream TCP reset occurs if backend process exits without flushing stream.
2026-03-11 14:30 - Repro attempt: Disabled fallback (pin to fp16) reduced incidents to <0.1% in short-run test, suggesting fallback path is correlated with failures.
Current hypothesis: Combination of (1) quantized model fallback path that loads kernels synchronously causing a short JVM/native pause, (2) autoscaler preemption policy that kills idle workers aggressively, and (3) missing SSE keepalive/flush on worker termination -> results in mid-generation silence and abrupt close.

Additional notes:
Workaround applied: increased autoscaler preemption timeout for FinBank dedicated pool and disabled automatic q4 fallback for their tenancy; implemented keepalive/flush in API gateway to reduce abrupt closes. Fix PR opened to serving-runtime to perform asynchronous kernel load and graceful worker drain (PR 1872). Plan: canary deploy patched runtime 2026-03-13, monitor for 72h, then roll to prod if stable.
payload.summary: Streaming session stalls mid-generation then abrupt connection close after model fallback to quantized variant

Issue summary:
BrightPath Analytics received their monthly invoice (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-31) with an unexpected negative line item named 'rate_adjustment_orphan' (-$1,198.45). The charge is labeled as an 'adjustment' but appears to have no matching postback or reconciliation record.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: BrightPath is refusing autopay until the invoice is corrected.
- Financial: Negative line causes final invoice to show a provisional credit; impacts revenue reporting and may be interpreted as duplicated credit.
- Operational: Customer is enterprise tier with Dedicated capacity; urgent to avoid SLA breach and churn.

Environment:
- Prod billing pipeline (postback-reconciler v2.4.1) processing region us-east-1.
- Customer uses dedicated capacity with tenant tag tenant: brightpath-prod.

Observed behavior:
- Invoice 2026-03 produced an extra negative line 'rate_adjustment_orphan' (-$1,198.45).
- No associated postback id, no matched usage window in hourly-accumulator.
- Billing UI displays source 'auto-recon', but the recon job logs do not contain a matching reconciliation run.

Expected behavior:
- Adjustments should always link to a reconciliation event or manual credit memo with author and rationale.

Additional context:
- Customer reports they did not request credits and have not disputed prior invoices.
- BrightPath provided the invoice PDF and CSV export (attached by customer in portal).
1) Query invoice lines for invoice ID INV-2026-03-BR-0042 via billing-api /v1/invoices/{id}/lines
2) Cross-reference postback-reconciler logs for timeframe 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-02T04:00:00Z
3) Query hourly-accumulator for tenant brightpath-prod for same windows for any retroactive adjustments
4) Inspect billing UI audit trail for 'auto-recon' job invocation and linked reconciliation id
Sample reconciler log snippet (2026-03-02T01:14:23Z): [INFO] auto-recon started run=run_20260302_01 tenant=brightpath-prod
[WARN] postback not found for candidate adjustment id=adj_7f8a3 - skipping link
[INFO] auto-recon completed run=run_20260302_01 adjustments_applied=1
Billing API query (2026-03-02T01:15:01Z) returned line: {"line_id":"line_98312","description":"rate_adjustment_orphan","amount":-1198.45,"source":"auto-recon","linked_postback":null}
03-12 10:22 - Support triaged; confirmed invoice PDF and negative line present.
03-12 11:05 - Billing team queried postback table (postbacks_2026_03): no postback with id adj_7f8a3 or equivalent found.
03-12 13:40 - Noted auto-recon run reported adjustments_applied=1; reconciler log includes a WARN 'postback not found' for adj_7f8a3. Hypothesis: reconciler applied adjustment record with missing linkage when postback lookup failed but fallback path created adjustment without provenance.
03-13 09:12 - Looked at deploy history: postback-reconciler v2.4.1 was rolled 2026-03-02 00:50 with config change 'allow-orphan-adjustments=true' toggled in feature flags for a hotfix. That flag may be responsible.
03-13 14:00 - Cross-checked git history: PR #5421 introduced allow-orphan-adjustments to avoid blocking large reconciles; intent was to create provisional adjustment records tagged provisional=true and with owner 'system-recon'. The created records should include original_run_id and candidate_postback_id; current record has null fields.
Temporary workaround: Applied manual credit memo CM-2026-03-BP-01 for $1,198.45 to negate the orphaned adjustment and reissued invoice draft. Finance applied a hold release to allow autopay once customer confirms.
Planned fix: Revert feature-flag 'allow-orphan-adjustments' for reconciler in us-east, add stricter validation to avoid creating adjustments with null provenance, and run a targeted rescan for reconciler runs 2026-03-02 to identify other orphaned adjustments.
Owner: Billing engineering (assignee: Ravi Patel). ETA for patch and rescan: 2026-03-17.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 15:05 - Finance (Marta Klein): Applied provisional credit memo CM-2026-03-BP-01. Notified customer and placed invoice hold until customer confirmation.
2026-03-14 08:45 - Customer (Elena Morris, BrightPath): Thanks — we see the provisional credit on the portal. Please confirm the underlying cause and when fix will be deployed; need written confirmation for our internal auditors.
payload.summary: Orphaned rate adjustment applied to tenant invoice causing negative line and provisional credit request

payload.description:
Issue summary
AcmeAssist (Dedicated tier) is asking for clearer cost reporting for their Dedicated deployment. They want a breakdown that looks like: blended $/1M output tokens with drilldowns by model, model version/quantization profile (if applicable), and region. Their current view (monthly invoice + high-level usage exports) doesn’t help them attribute cost changes to model mix, output length, caching/batching efficiency, or region.

Customer impact
- Customer is trying to justify Dedicated expansion internally and needs a defensible breakdown of unit costs for QBR/finance review.
- Without a breakdown, they are attributing cost spikes to “platform inefficiency” and are asking for manual ad-hoc reports.
- Risk: renewal friction and increased support load from repeated billing/cost questions.

Customer request (what they asked for)
1) Dedicated cost metric aligned to tokens: blended $/1M output tokens for a selected time range.
2) Drilldowns: model (and version), region, and (if possible) endpoint/route.
3) A way to export monthly and QTD summaries (CSV is fine).
4) Clarification on definitions: how idle capacity is treated, and how shared overhead is allocated.

Current state / constraints (internal)
- We have internal work underway for an Internal “Unit Economics” dashboard with finance-aligned definitions and drilldowns (model/region/tier).
- That dashboard is currently internal-only (RBAC restricted) and includes cost attribution logic not yet packaged for customer-facing delivery.
- Dedicated invoicing today is primarily contract/commit + capacity utilization reporting; token-level unit economics is not exposed as a product feature.
- Known data gaps in the past: streaming output token metering parity and some dimension normalization; improved recently but still treated as internal metrics until Finance signoff gates are met.

Notes on feasibility / future externalization
- This request is a strong signal for a future external feature: customer-facing cost visibility (especially for Dedicated + Private where customers need more detailed reporting).
- Product note (Marissa): v1 internal dashboard is meant to be the “source of truth” and should be stabilized first (reconciliation + SLOs). After v1 is stable, we can consider a curated external report/export that reuses the same metric definitions but hides sensitive internal allocation details.
- Finance note: any customer-facing unit cost number needs to be explicitly labeled (blended vs marginal) and have a stable rate card version for the reporting period; otherwise customers will compare month-over-month changes driven by internal rate-card updates.

Proposed immediate path (what Support/CS can offer now)
- Provide a one-time curated report to AcmeAssist for the requested time range, using internal aggregates where available, with clear caveats:
  - metric is “blended” (includes idle allocation per current internal methodology)
  - rate card version/date used
  - regions included and any missing-dimension coverage
- Offer a repeatable monthly export for the next 1–2 cycles as a Customer Success deliverable (manual / semi-manual), while we validate readiness for externalization.

Open questions to confirm with customer
- Do they want blended (all-in) or marginal (active GPU time only) costs for Dedicated?
- Do they want costs normalized by output tokens only, or input+output tokens?
- Time boundary expectations: calendar month in their timezone vs UTC.

Acceptance criteria for closing this support ticket
- Customer receives a clear answer on what Redwood can provide now vs later.
- Customer gets an initial report (or a committed plan with dates) and agrees to the interim approach.
- A product follow-up is recorded (internal) to evaluate external-facing reporting, but this Jira issue remains a support artifact (not a project plan).

Additional notes:
2025-02-21 15:18 PT — Customer (AcmeAssist): Thanks. We prefer blended (all-in) for internal planning. UTC month boundaries are fine. Need a QTD view and last full month, with model breakdown and us-east vs eu-west split. CSV export works.
2025-03-01 14:22 PT — Customer (AcmeAssist): Received, this is what we needed. The blended vs invoice note is helpful. Please plan to send this monthly; we’ll revisit if/when it becomes available in Console.
Provided customer with a curated CSV export (Jan full month + Feb QTD) showing blended $/1M output tokens with model and region breakdown, plus methodology caveats (blended/all-in, idle included, rate card version pinned, not a billing statement). Customer confirmed this meets immediate need; ongoing monthly exports to be handled via CSM as an interim measure. Product to evaluate future externalization separately.
CSM: schedule recurring monthly export for next 2 reporting cycles (owner: Allison Grant coordinating with CS).
Product: capture as input for potential customer-facing cost reporting once internal Unit Economics dashboard reaches stability gates (reconciliation + SLOs + RBAC).
Finance: maintain guidance on customer-safe wording and required disclaimers for any unit cost number shared externally.
payload.summary: Dedicated customer request: clearer cost reporting ($/1M output tokens) by model/region for Dedicated capacity

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (starting with Narra Health, dedicated tenant) observed a sustained elevation in server error rate (5xx) beginning 2026-03-10 06:15 UTC. Impact: ~3-5% of API requests returning 5xx for short-form and streaming calls; customer reports timeouts and degraded user experience. Timeline: - 06:15 UTC: first uptick in 5xx floor observed on edge dashboards. - 06:30 UTC: alerts triggered for elevated error_rate and downstream runtime restarts. - 07:05 UTC: customer reported increased failure rate to support. - 08:00 UTC: initial mitigations (traffic throttle) applied for the tenant. Environment: production (us-east-1) dedicated capacity.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
- Send mixed traffic with a 60/40 split streaming:non-streaming at ~120rps for tenant with priority tags (high/normal).
- Ensure prefetch enabled and aggressive priority rebalancer active in the routing config.
- Observe gradual increase in apigw 5xx and downstream runtime thread errors within 10-20 minutes.

Observed symptoms & logs (excerpt):
- Edge error-rate jump: baseline ~0.3% -> 4.2% within 40 minutes.
- Apigw logs: "upstream reset" and "502 returned after retries" correlated with connection queue growth.
- Runtime logs: repeated "worker-thread panic: evict-on-priority-squeeze" and "prefetch-lock timeout" before watchdog restarts.
- Autoscaler: frequent backfill and scale-down cycles visible during the window.

Impact: Customer-facing failed requests, elevated latency tail, increased retries and cost for customer. This is customer-impacting for Narra Health (dedicated).
Generate tenant traffic with mixed streaming and short text generation at sustained 100-150 rps
Enable prefetch and priority rebalancer on tenant routing policy
Observe apigw and runtime error rates over 30-60 minutes
Initial correlation: spikes align with priority rebalancer window adjustments and frequent shard handoffs
Hypothesis 1: Rebalancer is oscillating under mixed-priority load causing connection thrash and prefetch-lock contention
Hypothesis 2: Prefetch lock contention increases runtime latency causing upstream timeouts and apigw retries -> amplified 5xx floor
Observed runtime thread panics reference an internal eviction path (see runtime log snippets in linked PR)
Edge 5xx rate: baseline 0.3% -> peak 4.2%
Runtime restart count: +18 restarts in 1h for affected shard pool
Conn queue length on apigw: 40 -> 800 during peak window
Median latency: 120ms -> 380ms; P99: 1.2s -> 4.6s
Temporarily throttle tenant ingress (applied) to 40 rps - reduced error-rate to ~0.9%
Disabled aggressive priority rebalancer for the tenant routing policy (rolled back to stable weights)
Pinned tenant to fallback model variant with lower prefetch aggressiveness
Instrument rebalancer decision metrics (operator + weight oscillation) for canary shard pool
Add local prefetch lock metrics and expose timeouts to tracing
Deploy hotfix to rebalancer: add minimum hold-time to prevent oscillation (canary in staging)
Coordinate with SRE to stabilize autoscaler hysteresis to avoid backfill churn
Priya Desai (Support) 2026-03-10 07:12: Logged initial customer report & created ticket. Notified SRE on #support.
SRE (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-10 08:05: Observed runtime panics; suspect eviction path + prefetch lock. Starting a full shard-level trace.
Luca Moretti (Eng) 2026-03-10 09:45: Applied temporary tenant throttle and disabled aggressive rebalancer. Error-rate dropped but not back to baseline.
Narra Health (Customer) 2026-03-10 10:02: Confirmed user-facing retries reduced after throttle. Awaiting permanent fix.
Aisha Khan (SRE) 2026-03-11 14:20: Added tracing for rebalancer metrics; reproduced oscillation in staging with synthetic load.
Luca Moretti (Eng) 2026-03-12 11:30: Preparing a small rebalancer hold-time patch for canary rollout; will coordinate outage window.
In progress - mitigations applied (throttle + rebalancer disabled) reduced impact. Target: deploy rebalancer hold-time patch to canary by 2026-03-13 and monitor for regression. Postmortem to be created after incident closure.
payload.summary: Priority rebalancer feedback loop raising 5xx baseline for dedicated tenant

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer requests a live forwarding pipeline from Redwood audit events to their Graylog cluster (HEC-compatible endpoint). They require on-the-fly field-level pseudonymization for PII (email, phone, user_id) before leaving Redwood, plus a daily signed archival bundle (zip) containing the raw events for the day with per-file SHA256 checksums and a manifest signed by the customer-facing KMS key.

Impact: Finovo ingests audit events into their SIEM for realtime fraud detection and compliance monitoring. Without this pipeline they will miss alerts; the request is blocking their SOC attestation timeline. Estimated daily event volume: ~120k events (~2.3GB compressed).

Environment: Prod (us-east). Customer uses Dedicated capacity and has VPC peering with us-east-private. They have an enterprise contract and require HSM-backed signing for the archive manifest.

Requirements (customer-provided):
- Real-time forwarding to Graylog over HTTPS (HEC-like).
- Support for tenant-scoped field pseudonymization: email -> HMAC-SHA256(email, tenant_key) truncated to 24 chars, phone -> token prefix + last 4 digits, user_id -> stable opaque token.
- Option to include original field in daily signed archive only (not sent to SIEM).
- Daily ZIP archive stored in customer-designated S3 bucket (or delivered via SFTP) with: per-file SHA256 checksums, a manifest.json, and an RSA-SHA256 signature using customer's public key or Redwood HSM attestation report.
- Delivery confirmation webhook to customer when archive is available and verified.
- Audit events must maintain original event timestamps and event IDs for correlation.

Desired artifacts from support:
1) A short runbook for configuring the forwarding endpoint in Console (steps, required IAM role for S3/SFTP, how to enable pseudonymization rules).
2) A sample mapping/template of fields delivered to Graylog HEC (including tokenized field names).
3) Proof-of-integrity options and example manifest schema.
4) Timeline and rollout plan for enabling live forwarding and signed archive for tenant.

Steps to reproduce / customer setup actions we need to validate:
1) Provide target Graylog HEC endpoint URL + TLS client cert (if mutual TLS required) or API key.
2) Indicate which fields must be pseudonymized and whether originals should be kept for archive only.
3) Provide S3 bucket ARN (or SFTP endpoint) and KMS key ID for envelope encryption of archives.
4) Provide public key for manifest signature verification (or request Redwood-signed attestation).

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 - Security (by email, pasted): For HSM signing we require an audit exception and legal OK; recommend customer-managed key for signature verification, or provide Redwood attestation (x.509) as separate artifact.
Verified dedicated pool in us-east has headroom for expected throughput. Current exporter implementation supports header-level tokenization but not field-level HMAC pseudonymization; will need a small code change in siem-connectors repo.

Issue summary:
DataWeave Labs is migrating an offline embedding import pipeline into a mixed cluster that already serves low-latency chat traffic. They want guidance on configuring separate burst/budget pools so large bulk embed jobs do not cause 429s or deprioritize chat.

Impact:
During evening bulk imports the customer reported an increase in 429s for short chat sessions (P95 latency-sensitive flows). Business impact: degraded UX for paying end users; embeddings import can be deferred but needs throughput guarantees overnight.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated) in us-east
- Ingress via customer API keys, routed through shared gateway
- Model set: redwood-embed-6.1 for embeddings; open-llama-7b for chat

Steps to reproduce (customer-reported):
1) Start 40 parallel workers performing chunked embedding uploads (multipart) with small chunks (~128KB) over 3 hours.
2) Concurrently send low-qps interactive chat requests (~20 qps short-lived sessions).
3) Observe increased 429s on chat route after ~15 minutes; embedding jobs continue but with slower throughput.

Observed behavior:
- Chat route shows 5-10% 429s during high embedding activity; token headers show tenant-level window exhausted.
- Support console shows shared token bucket usage spike, no per-route separation configured.
- Customer sees no route-level quota in console (only tenant-level).

Expected behavior:
- Customer expects dedicated configuration that isolates a small sustained allocation for chat with a separate burst credit pool for embeddings or at least a weighted priority so chat maintains low-latency SLO.

Attached logs/headers (redacted):
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 (for tenant window)
- X-Route-Quota: not present
- Sampling traces: chat requests hit gateway queueing and then 429s while background embedding requests are long-running and consume refill credits.

Customer asks:
1) Is there a recommended pattern to carve out a steady low-latency allocation for chat while allowing overnight bulk embedding bursts?
2) What configuration changes are safe on a dedicated pool (without service interruption) to avoid chat 429s?
3) Any recommended monitoring/console settings to detect this earlier?
2026-03-10 | Sofia Patel (customer): We can delay the embed jobs but need at least 10k embeddings/hour overnight while keeping under 1% chat 429s. Embedding workers are orchestration-managed and can't be trivially rate-limited without slowing downstream pipelines.
2026-03-10 | Liam O'Connor (Support): Thanks — forwarding to infra to validate tenant bucket and route config. Can you share request samples and the API keys used for both flows (we only need metadata, not raw data)?
2026-03-11 | Infra-SRE (system): We verified the dedicated pool is using only tenant-level quota. No per-route isolation is enabled. Observed refill smoothing window set to 60s. Proposed options: (A) carve a route-level steady allocation for chat with higher priority, (B) create a secondary route for embeddings with separate token bucket and lower priority, (C) configure conservative burst cap on embeddings route and enable pre-warm scheduling during off-peak.
2026-03-11 | Liam O'Connor (Support): Provided configuration recipe and console steps to create a route-level quota. Asked customer to schedule a 30-min maintenance window to apply non-disruptive route binding for a test route.
2026-03-12 | DataWeave Eng (customer): Tried the test binding for chat route and observed P99 latency stabilized but still saw occasional 429s when embed workers spawn new multipart uploads. We captured additional traces and shared them in the ticket.
Tenant-level token bucket is physical source of exhaustion; no per-route buckets exist on this dedicated allocation.
Embedding workers use many short-lived connections which accelerate token consumption due to per-connection preflight counting.
Refill smoothing 60s means sudden parallel worker fanout can overwhelm short-window burst credits; reducing smoothing or increasing base steady allocation helps.
Gateway logs show embeddings route had no priority weight; chat route lacked route-specific quota or a guaranteed minimum share.
We reproduced a similar pattern in staging by spinning up 30 parallel multipart clients and observed tenant window exhaustion within 10 minutes.
Possible mitigations ranked: 1) route-level guaranteed share + lower-weight embeddings; 2) separate token bucket for embeddings route; 3) client-side sharding with rate-limiter; 4) scheduled pre-warm bursts with explicit burst reservation.
In progress — applied a non-disruptive route binding in prod that creates a guaranteed 12% steady allocation for chat (route-level quota) and a lower priority for embedding route. Recommended follow-ups: (1) customer to throttle embed workers to <= 30 concurrent chunk uploads per worker; (2) enable console alert on tenant-token-remaining < 20% for early detection; (3) consider creating a dedicated 'bulk-embed' route with its own bucket for large imports. If chat 429s persist after 48h we will open a Sev1 and schedule an infra change to add a secondary burst pool.
Customer action: throttle embedding worker concurrency and introduce jittered backoff on multipart retries.
Support action: monitor tenant and route quota dashboards for 48 hours and capture traces when 429s occur.
Infra action: draft RFC for secondary burst pools on dedicated customers to be reviewed by 2026-03-20.
Product action: add UI affordance to visualize per-route steady allocations and burst credits (tracked in product-board entry).
