payload.description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC we observed sustained elevated 5xx from the API gateway fronting dedicated tenant FableAI (us-east). Traffic patterns show many short-lived requests followed by aggressive client retries from a single tenant key. The gateway returned a mixture of 502/503/504 and several upstream runtime processes were observed to enter eviction/restart cycles, exacerbating the error rate.

Impact: Customer reports production customer-facing errors; embedding and chat endpoints returning 5xx for ~10% of requests during the peak window. FableAI business impact: degraded user sessions, automated job failures, and support escalations.

Environment: prod; dedicated capacity region us-east; tenant pinned to gpt-medium-v1 variant; Dedicated pool with reserved GPUs.

Observed behavior: Rapid retry loops from client (~50 retries within 30s per failed request), amplified by hedged retry policy at the gateway. Many retries created head-of-line congestion in accept queues and saturated ephemeral connection slots. Upstream serving-runtime processes hit resource pressure (fd exhaustion and elevated CPU threads) and triggered graceful eviction followed by prewarm which increased latency/first-byte-timeouts and more retries.

Expected behavior: Gateway should apply per-tenant retry damping, hedged retries should back off under sustained failures, and serving-runtime should avoid eviction cascade under bursty retransmits.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Simulate high volume of small requests (payloads <1KB) at sustained 200 RPS from a single API key with deterministic client-side retry policy (exponential backoff with short max delay). 2) Configure gateway hedged retry enabled. 3) Observe accept queue growth, 5xx rate at apigw, and runtime worker evictions.

Logs / metrics:
- apigw logs: repeated 429/502/503 for tenant fableai-tenant-01 with client-id X-Api-Key: fa-prod-01; timestamps 2026-03-10T02:17:xxZ to 02:45:xxZ.
- runtime logs: repeated SIGTERM to worker PID 1123 -> restart -> prewarm -> SIGTERM; nvml/gpu logs show high context-switches and elevated memory fragmentation.
- Observability graphs: accept-queue-depth for us-east apigw surged from 30 -> 420; ephemeral-fd-usage trending to 98% on proxies. Latency P95 rose from 120ms -> 2.4s.

Customer report: FableAI support engineer supplied a client-side timeout/retry config that matches the pattern (max_retries=10, initial_backoff=100ms, max_backoff=500ms). They reported sudden degradation at 02:15 UTC coincident with a release on their side (no certificate changes).
2026-03-10T02:15Z - Alerts from observability: apigw 5xx rate tripled for us-east
2026-03-10T02:18Z - Initial triage by support: identified tenant-scoped traffic spike and aggressive retry pattern
2026-03-10T02:25Z - SRE paged; mitigation steps recommended: tenant temporary rate-limit and disable hedged-retry for tenant route
2026-03-10T02:33Z - Temporary tenant rate-limit applied (20 RPS), hedged retries disabled on route; partial error rate reduction observed
2026-03-10T02:50Z - Runtime team noticed repeated worker evictions correlated with connection churn
2026-03-10T03:15Z - Customer applied client-side temporary backoff increase; errors dropped to baseline by 03:35Z

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 02:27 - SRE Ops (Ravi Patel): Observed accept-queue saturation and fd exhaustion on proxy nodes. Suggest temporary tenant RPS cap and toggle hedged-retry for tenant routes.
2026-03-10 03:20 - FableAI (customer): Confirmed applied client patch to increase max backoff to 5s and to jitter. Observed reduced error surface. Thank you for the quick assistance.
Accept-queue and ephemeral fd metrics are the strongest signal: when accept-queue > 250 the gateway begins returning 502/504 at a high rate.
Client behavior: deterministic retry pattern without jitter leads to synchronized retransmits amplifying short-lived failures.
Hedged retries at apigw multiply concurrent upstream work — combined with client retries this created >3x the usual inflight requests per connection slot for tenant.
Runtime responded to backlog by sequentially terminating idle workers to reclaim memory; however termination timing overlapped with prewarm causing transient capacity loss.
We reproduced locally with a traffic generator: enabling hedged-retry + aggressive client retries triggers accept-queue climb and repeated runtime SIGTERM within 5-7 minutes.
No evidence of GPU driver crash or hardware fault; resource pressure pattern points to connection storm and scheduling pressure.
Related historical incidents: SUP-421420 (apigw conn thrash during mixed embed/chat burst) shows similar accept-queue thresholds — consider reuse of that runbook.
Telemetry: adding tenant-scoped connection counters and per-route retry amplifiers would help auto-detect and throttle harmful patterns earlier.
Applied tenant-level RPS cap (temporary) to break retry loop
Disabled hedged retries on the route for the tenant to avoid duplicate upstream load
Suggested customer increase client backoff and add jitter (we provided recommended config: initial_backoff=250ms, max_backoff=5000ms, jitter=full)
Worked with customer to deploy a quick client-side patch; observed error rate reduction within 15 minutes of patch rollout
Primary: Synchronized client retries combined with gateway hedged-retry produced a thundering herd that saturated accept queues and ephemeral connection slots, leading to upstream timeouts and runtime eviction cycles.
Contributing: Hedged retry defaults are aggressive for high-concurrency small-payload patterns; serving-runtime eviction policy is sensitive to short bursts of connection churn and may benefit from longer grace before termination.
Short term: update gateway route config to apply automatic per-tenant retry damping when accept-queue exceeds threshold (owner: apigw team).
Short term: add observability alert for tenant-level retry amplification ratio > 2.5 (owner: observability).
Medium term: runtime team to adjust eviction grace period and prewarm logic to avoid capacity loss during churn (owner: runtime).
Medium term: recommend change to hedged-retry default to include adaptive backoff under sustained errors (owner: apigw).

Issue summary:
Customers observed a rapid elevation in 5xx responses (mostly 502/503) on the chat/generate endpoint between 08:12-08:28 UTC. The initial spike correlated with an ingress node rolling restart. Client SDKs retried aggressively and the amplified inflight connections overloaded upstream runtimes, which triggered runtime watchdog restarts and a transient GPU eviction pattern. Impact: several high-traffic tenants on Dedicated saw 30-60s failures and elevated tail latency.

Impact:
- NimbusDocs (dedicated tenant) experienced request failures for ~16 minutes, affecting production availability for their chat feature.
- Platform-level elevated 5xx floor and increased runtime restarts across 6 pods in us-east.

Environment:
- prod cluster in us-east-1; dedicated GPU pool (A100-style).
- Affected service: api-gateway -> ingress proxy -> serving-runtime (runtime v1.9.2).
2026-03-13 08:12 UTC - First customer report from NimbusDocs via support@; symptoms: 502s on /v1/generate and streams dropping
2026-03-13 08:13 UTC - Support triage: created ticket, notified SRE via #infra-support. Assigned Diego.
2026-03-13 08:14 UTC - Observed ingress rolling restart in us-east (k8s node upgrade). Connection drain started.

2026-03-13 08:18 UTC - Serving runtime processes (6 pods) reported watchdog_kill and subsequent restarts, GPU driver nvml resets on two hosts.
2026-03-13 08:28 UTC - Retry storm subsided after ingress finishes rolling and ingress config tweaked to increase graceful drain to 30s.
2026-03-13 08:40 UTC - Support pushed customer-facing update, SRE continues post-incident analysis.
Hypothesis 1: Short drain timeout on ingress combined with aggressive client-side retries caused a connection pile-up at api-gateway, amplifying load and causing runtime watchdogs to trigger restarts.
Hypothesis 2: Runtime memory fragmentation increased due to concurrent long-lived streaming sessions while GPU driver resets occurred on hosts, leading to GNMT OOM path and crashes.
Metric checks: confirmed 5xx rate correlated with accept_queue depth and SDK retry count. Serving-runtime CPU and memory CPC increased prior to restarts.
Correlation: two GPU hosts reported nvml resets within 30s of ingress restarts; those hosts hosted affected runtime pods.
08:20 UTC - SRE increased ingress graceful drain from 10s -> 30s for rolling restarts to reduce connection churn.
08:22 UTC - Temporarily tightened api-gateway per-tenant concurrent connection soft limits for NimbusDocs to avoid wider fanout.
08:25 UTC - Set client-side suggestion: Support sent recommended retry headers (Retry-After) and a customer note advising to reduce SDK retry aggressiveness until platform config stabilized.
08:35 UTC - Identified two GPU hosts with nvml resets and cordoned them; migrated pods off of the hosts and restarted the runtime pods cleanly.
08:47 UTC - SRE deployed a throttling rule at the ingress to backpressure retries originating from the common SDK user-agent while preserving in-flight streams.
Mitigation: Increased ingress drain timeout and applied temporary throttle on aggressive SDK retry user-agents. Replaced two affected GPU hosts and restarted runtimes; 5xx rates returned to baseline by 08:46 UTC. Root cause: replay amplification from client retry patterns interacting with short ingress drain window, which amplified transient accept-queue pressure and pushed serving-runtimes past watchdog thresholds. Permanent fix plan: adjust default SDK retry policy in docs, add server-side short-window backpressure and a gracebackoff layer in api-gateway, and improve GPU host watchdog heuristics to prefer graceful eviction over immediate kill when nvml reset detected.

2) Client SDK team: Propose and release updated SDK with exponential backoff baseline and jitter (owner: Priya Shah).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a network interruption and client resume, tool invocations from the TS SDK are executed in a different order than the original request sequence when using session-scoped idempotency tokens. This causes downstream side-effects (writes to customer DB) to apply out of order and occasionally duplicate.

Impact:
- Affected: Acme Finance production traffic in us-east-1 (enterprise account).
- Symptom: Incorrect ordering and occasional duplicate side-effects from external tool/webhook endpoints.
- Business impact: Data consistency issues for payment reconciliation flows; customer paused some traffic.

Environment:
- Redwood platform: prod (us-east-1)
- SDK: redwood-ts-sdk v2.4.1 (patched client is not yet deployed)
- Mode: streaming/resume flow using per-session idempotency (session_token passed at connection start)
- Customer infra: websocket client -> edge proxy -> API gateway -> serving-runtime

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Start a streaming session with session-scoped idempotency token (session_id=abc123).
2) Emit a sequence of tool calls A -> B -> C in that order (each tool call is a separate tool invocation event).
3) Simulate a transient network partition causing the client to reconnect and resume the session.
4) After resume, observed tool execution order at webhook sinks is B -> A -> C for ~5% of resumes; duplicates in ~0.5% of cases.

Observed behavior:
- The serving runtime accepts resumed requests and attempts retransmit/reconciliation of in-flight tool messages.
- Replayed messages sometimes interleave with newly processed worker queue items leading to reordering.
- Idempotency dedup appears to be keyed by (session_token, tool_nonce) but tool_nonce normalization differs between edge and worker after resume, causing failed dedup and duplicate invocations.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should preserve original logical ordering of tool invocations for a session and deduplicate retried tool calls.

Logs / traces / evidence:
- Customer-provided webhook logs: https://acme-logs.s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-replay-2026-03-11.log (redacted)
- Platform traces (sample): https://grafana.redwood/prod/traces/session-abc123?from=2026-03-11T14:00Z
- Edge request IDs: req_e7a2f3, req_e7a2f4, req_e7a2f9 (attached in customer log)

Initial hypothesis:
- Regression introduced in streaming resume path in serving-runtime that alters nonce canonicalization when requests are proxied by API gateway with HTTP/2 header reserialization.
- TS SDK resume logic may be re-sending tool messages with slightly different metadata (header case, truncated nonce) causing dedup mismatch.

Immediate workaround applied by customer:
- Customer temporarily disabled automatic resume and falls back to immediate session restart (loses short-term context but avoids reorder).
- Support recommended: pin SDK to last known-good v2.3.x for a short window while we investigate.

Next steps (investigation):
- Engineering to reproduce in internal staging using edge proxy + HTTP/2 path and SDK v2.4.1. (Ethan assigned)
- Compare nonce canonicalization between edge and worker (check header normalization code path).
- Add additional request tracing to mark original sequence numbers and enforce ordering in resume reconciliation layer.
- Quick mitigation: strengthen dedup key to include normalized nonce and original sequence counter if present.

Notes / cross-references:
- Slack thread: #support (thread ts 1700002000)
- Related ticket for idempotency normalization: SUP-271828 (linked)
- PR with preliminary instrumentation: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821

2026-03-12 | ACME Support (J. Alvarez): Initial report: noticed out-of-order tool executions and occasional duplicates after reconnects. Provided webhook logs and sequence hashes. We're paused on the streaming client until you confirm it's safe.
2026-03-12 | Support (Maya Chen): Acknowledged. Escalating to Eng. Requested full webhook timestamps and SDK version. Advised temporary disable of resume and pin SDK to v2.3.x. SLA P1 acknowledged.
2026-03-12 | Eng (Ethan Lopez): Investigating. I can reproduce a reordering locally when proxy reserializes :authority header over HTTP/2. Suspect nonce normalization mismatch between edge and worker. Adding instrumentation to resume path. Reference PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
2026-03-13 | Eng (Priya Shah): Found that header key-case normalization on the worker drops hyphenation for tool_nonce header in one code path, causing a different dedup key post-resume. Working on hotfix to normalize headers and include sequence counter in dedup key. Running tests against reproducer harness.
2026-03-13 | Support (Maya Chen): Shared recommended customer rollback steps and asked Acme to confirm whether they can deploy pin (v2.3.x). Customer indicated they will test pin this afternoon and report results.
2026-03-13 | ACME Support (J. Alvarez): Confirmed: pinned to v2.3.9 — saw no ordering incidents in 3 hours of traffic. Will keep monitoring. Thank you.
2026-03-13 | Eng (Ethan Lopez): Plan: ship hotfix 2.4.1-hotfix1 to normalize nonce and include seq counter in dedup key. After hotfix, we'll run a canary in us-east-1 and then rollout. Also creating follow-up internal task to add an automated resume-ordering regression test. Linked INT task INT-9812 created.
2026-03-13 | Support (Maya Chen): Marking ticket In Progress; will update when hotfix is deployed and customer confirms full recovery.

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 11:42 UTC Crestview Finance observed a class of streaming requests that returned no chunks for >30s ("streaming silence"), causing client-side retries and aggressive route-level retries which amplified load and produced duplicate completions. Impact: ~45% of real-time payments validation streams for Crestview failed to produce streaming tokens within SLO; visible user-facing delays and two downstream reconciliation timeouts. The event produced an unexpected billing delta for the customer window (estimated +14% token billing) and elevated error rates across the us-east serving pool.

Observed behavior: Certain streaming sessions initiated and returned an initial HTTP 200, then emitted zero data frames for an extended period. The client retried at the SDK level after 25s and triggered new sessions; server-side session affinity and prefix cache interactions created duplicate completions once one stream resumed. This produced both silent timeouts and duplicated outputs.

Expected behavior: Streams should begin emitting token frames within 3s for the workload distribution seen; retries should not generate duplicate completions when session resume and prefix/KV cache are still active.

Impact summary: Customer-visible latency and failed transactions; reconciliations delayed; financial risk due to timeouts; billing exposure. Customer opened an escalation with CS at 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC and requested immediate mitigation and a plan for credits and prevention.

Timeline (short): 2026-03-10 11:42 UTC — alert: streaming error rate spike for Crestview. 11:47 UTC — first CS acknowledged and created incident. 12:00 UTC — SRE enabled conservative route circuit-breaker and reduced per-route retry budget. 12:20 UTC — partial mitigation observed; silence occurrences reduced but retries continued causing billing surge. 15:10 UTC — fix deployed to streaming-proxy to enforce safe session-resume semantics and drop duplicate resume attempts. 18:00 UTC — system stabilized; customer notified.

Hypothesis 1: Interaction between session-resume logic in streaming-proxy and partial KV cache warmup for quantized variants created a window where streams were acknowledged but emitted no token frames. Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler and retry logic amplified load (aftershock) because retries created short-lived sessions that forced extra kernel selection, increasing tail latency. Evidence: correlation between no-chunk warnings and requests routed to recently scaled-up quantized shards. Kernel mismatch traces show expensive cold-paths for a subset of requests. Reproduced in staging by toggling prefix caching and forcing delayed resume.

Mitigations tried: 1) Reduced per-route retry budget (12:00 UTC) — immediate reduction in new session creation. 2) Circuit-breaker on route to avoid routing to recently scaled nodes (12:05 UTC). 3) Streaming-proxy patch to block duplicate resume attempts while KV warmup in-flight (15:10 UTC) — definitive reduction in duplicate completions.

Follow-up confirmations: After patch, no-chunk warnings dropped to baseline; billing delta projection revised downward after reprocessing logs.

Short-term fix: deployed streaming-proxy patch to enforce single-resume-per-session until KV/prefix warmup completes; tightened route-level retry budgets; added a safeguard in autoscaler to delay routing to newly provisioned quantized nodes for 30s. Customer communicated with a summary and offered a billing credit to cover the delta (+14% window) pending audit.

Long-term actions: 1) Runtime: add explicit per-session warmup handshake to avoid ack-without-chunk states. 2) Autoscaler: implement graduated routing cooldown for new nodes. 3) SDK: expose retry suppression flag when client detects long-tail silence. 4) Create a targeted regression test in the CI harness that simulates delayed-resume scenarios and measures duplicate-output risk. 5) Update runbooks: incident detection alert for no-chunk patterns and an automated mitigation playbook.

Status: patches merged (PRs referenced above), runbook updated, customer bill credit processing initiated, and a follow-up review scheduled for 2026-03-18 to validate long-term mitigations in canary.
1) Use Crestview request pattern: medium-length prompts (avg 800 tokens) with streaming=true and prefix caching enabled. 2) Send 8 concurrent sessions from same client session id and artificially delay network ingress to the second session for 25-30s. 3) Observe initial HTTP 200 with no chunk frames followed by client SDK retry and duplicate completion generation once prefix cache resumes. Note: requires production-like KV cache and session affinity to reproduce reliably.
Selected excerpts: [streaming-proxy] 2026-03-10T11:42:02Z WARN session[svc-1234] emitted no-chunk for 28000ms; candidate-resume=true; prefix-eviction=false. [serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T11:43:30Z INFO request[req-9f2] kernel-selection=quantized-evm variant=candidate returned NO_DATA until KV warmup. [autoscaler] 2026-03-10T11:50:12Z INFO pool us-east scale-up triggered by retry-fanout. [billing] 2026-03-10T12:05:01Z ALERT token-accounts delta +14% over 1h window for customer crestview-finance. Full logs attached in internal archive (link in related_confluence_pages).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customers using the us-west dedicated inference pool experienced a sudden degradation in throughput and a spike in streaming disconnects and 504/524 timeouts. Impact: Multiple NovaChat endpoints reported increases in tail latency (p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.4s) and a 4-6% 5xx rate for generation requests between 2026-03-10 03:25 UTC and ongoing. Several streaming sessions dropped mid-response causing client-side errors and retries. Environment: prod dedicated pool in us-west (pool-id: dp-usw-61), serving-runtime v2.8.2, autoscaler v1.3. Investigation timeline and steps to reproduce: 1) At 03:20 UTC alerts fired on high GPU util and elevated request queues for dp-usw-61. 2) Support observed progressive queueing on the pool's work-queue: pending_batches metric rose from near-zero to 400+. 3) Attempts to reproduce by hitting NovaChat's pinned model showed delayed first-token times and streaming disconnects consistent with production symptoms. 4) Logs and metrics examined: GPU SM power draw and memory bandwidth saturation correlated with queue spikes; node-level telemetry showed elevated PCIe retries on three nodes. Observed behavior: - Sustained high GPU utilization on a subset of nodes with frequent power/clock throttling events. - Autoscaler did not scale up quickly enough; observed scale-up latency ~6 minutes vs target 90s. - Some nodes reported elevated PCIe errors which coincide with large throughput flows from an unexpected training-like job. Expected behavior: - Inference pool should serve low-latency requests with autoscaler responding within configured SLOs and strict isolation preventing heavy compute jobs from impacting inference nodes. Logs and relevant links: - Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated/dp-usw-61?from=now-3h - Kibana traces: https://logs.redwood.ai/app/kibana#/discover/req-logs?query=dp-usw-61 - Slack thread: #support (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02SUPPORT/p165) - Node logs: /var/log/pool/dp-usw-61/node-12-gpu0.log (attached snippets in ticket) Initial hypothesis: A customer workload (identified later as a mis-labeled batch job belonging to internal data-ops or a third-party partner) was scheduled on inference-capable nodes in the dedicated pool, saturating PCIe and memory bandwidth, causing noisy-neighbor effects. The autoscaler metric was configured to use CPU-based thresholds and did not account for GPU memory-bandwidth saturation, resulting in delayed scaling. Investigation notes: - Identified three nodes (node-10, node-11, node-12) with repeated GPU thermal throttling messages and high PCIe error counters. - SSH access to node-12 showed an unexpected long-running process (container id: c5a1b9) launching a distributed data-prep workload that appeared to use the GPU extensively. - Node labels show a mis-applied admission rule that allowed batch jobs to land on dp-usw pools after a recent scheduler config change (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/commit/7f9a2a4). - Autoscaler config for dp-usw-61 used target_utilization: 0.65 on CPU, min_replicas: 1, max_replicas: 8; there is no separate GPU-bandwidth metric. - Queues backed up causing head-of-line blocking for streaming requests leading to disconnects. Immediate mitigation taken: - Isolated and cordoned node-10/11/12 for investigation to stop new tasks being scheduled. - Killed the mis-scheduled container c5a1b9 and restarted the node GPU drivers. - Manually scaled the pool to add 3 extra inference nodes from a warm spare pool; moved NovaChat traffic to the new nodes (partial failover). - Applied temporary admission rule to prevent non-inference jobs from being scheduled onto inference pools. Current status: In Progress. Remediation and next steps: - Short term: enforce strict nodeSelector and taints/tolerations in scheduler to block batch workloads from inference pools; update admission controller to reject jobs without "inference:true" label. - Medium term: update autoscaler to consider GPU-specific signals (memory bandwidth, PCIe retries, GPU SM utilization), and reduce scale-up cooldown to 90s for dedicated inference pools. - Long term: implement quota limits for per-customer persistent processes on dedicated pools and add automated detection of PCIe/memory-bandwidth saturation with alerting. - Post-incident: run root cause review and update runbooks; notify NovaChat CS with timeline and compensation options. Owner: SRE + Scheduler team. Follow-ups: linked INT-9942 (scheduler config rollback), infra PR to add GPU-bandwidth metric https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6321, and a planned postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-15. Customer-facing note: Support has told NovaChat we are investigating and provided a temporary traffic-migration workaround. Resolution: ongoing; full RCA pending.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 03:46 UTC - SRE (Marco Liu): Identified nodes with repeated thermal throttles and high PCIe error counters; cordoned nodes and killing suspected noisy containers. Notifying Scheduler team for admission rule check.
2026-03-10 05:05 UTC - Support (Elena Park): Migrated NovaChat traffic to warm spare nodes; customer reports reduced errors but still elevated p95 on large-context requests.
2026-03-11 09:20 UTC - SRE (Marco Liu): Opened infra PR to add GPU bandwidth metric to autoscaler (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6321). Planning postmortem on 2026-03-15.
2026-03-12 16:02 UTC - CS (Rohit S.): Sent customer incident update with mitigation steps and ETA for RCA; customer requested log bundle and timing for postmortem.
Telemetry indicates contention at the PCIe and GPU memory bandwidth layer rather than pure SM compute utilization. Head-of-line queueing on the pool's batcher caused significant delays for small low-latency streaming requests. Autoscaler not configured to react to this failure mode. Scheduler change allowed a noisy batch job into the pool. Root cause appears to be a combination of scheduler misconfiguration + autoscaler blind spot + a misbehaving scheduled job.
2026-03-10: Nodes cordoned and noisy container terminated; manual scale-out completed; customer traffic partially migrated.
2026-03-11: Scheduler admission rollback applied; temporary admission rule enforced to block non-inference containers.
2026-03-12: Infra PR for GPU-bandwidth metric opened; postmortem scheduled.

payload.description:
Issue summary: ParcelFlow is observing a sustained p50/p95 throughput drop in their dedicated GPU pool beginning ~2026-03-10 08:30 UTC. Traffic rate to the route is unchanged; however overall batch attach success rate and effective GPU credits available for the pool have gradually declined leading to queuing and p50 increase. Impact: customer-facing QPS reduced ~35% at 10:00 UTC and p95 latency increased by ~2.5x. This is customer-visible for their streaming and short inference routes. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved cluster) in us-west-2 backing ParcelFlow's tenant; models listed above. Steps to reproduce: 1) Import ParcelFlow test harness with long-lived keepalives (SDK v1.8.2) 2) Ramp to pre-failure normal QPS 3) Observe connection count per tenant and per-allocator socket, then watch allocator/gpu-credit metrics over 1–3 hours. Observed logs & metrics:
- slow but persistent growth in "allocated_socket_count" for the tenant (graphs linked)
- GPU-credit balance metric declines ~0.6 credits/min until autoscaler cannot attach new slots fast enough
- many long-lived connections reported in telemetry (timeouts not present; connections remain ESTABLISHED)
- allocator logs show frequent 'slot reserved but not used' events and repeated small attach attempts (see Sentry link). Initial hypothesis: a change in the customer's SDK usage pattern (long keepalive + infrequent request bursts) is consuming socket slots and preventing the allocator from reclaiming GPU credits, causing autoscaler to see low free capacity and delay scale actions. Consequence is noisy-neighbor-like starvation for short-burst routes and degraded batch packing efficiency.
2026-03-10 09:05 - Support (Leah Chen): Opened ticket with customer-provided telemetry and Grafana links. Requested a short-term mitigation: reduce keepalive TTL or enable connection pooling on client side.
2026-03-10 09:42 - ParcelFlow (Sara Holt): Confirmed they rolled back a new SDK configuration deployed yesterday that increased connection reuse. Rolled back at 09:30; seeing marginal improvement but throughput still not recovered to baseline.
2026-03-10 11:00 - SRE (Ravi Patel): Investigating allocator and autoscaler logs. Noted repeated reservation events where a socket remains reserved for >5m without issuing an inference. Added probe to log attach/release sequence for the tenant.
2026-03-11 02:20 - Engineering (Marcus Rivera): Observed allocator token-bucket depletion pattern when many connections hold reservations concurrently. Proposed quick fix to allow aggressive reclamation for sockets idle >60s in dedicated pools if tenant is in dedicated tier.
2026-03-11 14:07 - Support (Leah Chen): Customer applied client-side mitigation (keepalive reduction from 15m to 45s) per our guidance. Noted immediate drop in long-lived connection count and gradual recovery of GPU-credit metric. Customer still sees residual p95 latency spikes during afternoon bursts; tracking.
2026-03-12 08:15 - Engineering (Ravi Patel): Deployed hotfix (PR linked) to allocator: reclaim idle reservations after 60s for dedicated pools and emit metric allocator.reclaims.force. Monitoring for regressions; no negative signals in e2e smoke tests.
2026-03-12 11:38 - ParcelFlow (Sara Holt): Post-hotfix: baseline throughput restored to ~95% of pre-incident. Noted one small spike during a scheduled batch job; asked about longer-term safeguards.
2026-03-12 12:05 - SRE (Ravi Patel): Marking as In Progress; recommended follow-up actions: runbook update, autoscaler tuning for mixed keepalive patterns, and SDK guidance to customers.
Telemetry review showed a slow, linear draining of gpu-credit for the dedicated pool over ~4 hours prior to alerting. Drain correlated tightly with rising count of ESTABLISHED sockets from ParcelFlow's tenant.
Allocator logs: identified ~8k 'reservation_held' events in the window where reservation duration > 120s. Many reservations were never consumed for >30s following creation (pattern consistent with long-lived keepalives waiting for next request).
Autoscaler behavior: autoscaler waits for free credit threshold to fall below X before scaling. With steady reservation hold, perceived available capacity stayed low and scaling decisions were suppressed, delaying attach of new GPUs.
Workaround applied and platform hotfix deployed. Short-term: customer reduced client keepalive TTL (from 15m to 45s) and enabled connection pooling which immediately dropped idle reservation counts. Platform: hotfix merged (allocator PR) to forcibly reclaim idle reservations in dedicated pools after 60s and emit allocator.reclaims.force metric. Autoscaler has a follow-up tweak scheduled to be conservative when reclaim metrics spike. Customer confirmed throughput restored to ~95% of baseline; continued monitoring for 72 hours. Follow-ups: update keepalive guidance in SDK docs, add runbook entry for noisy keepalive symptoms, and schedule an autoscaler policy review (ENG-OPS sprint).
Combination of a customer-side change in SDK connection behavior (long-lived keepalives with bursty usage) and conservative allocator/autoscaler heuristics that allowed reservations to be held without reclamation. This produced a capacity illusion (low free credits) and delayed autoscaler actions, causing degraded effective throughput in the dedicated pool.
Document: Add a short troubleshooting section to the dedicated-pool runbook describing keepalive-induced GPU-credit drain and the immediate remediation steps.
SDK: Add guidance and a recommended default keepalive TTL for dedicated customers in the SDK README and changelog.
Autoscaler: Evaluate policy change to factor allocator.reclaims.force into scale decisions; run a canary for 2 weeks.
Customer: Follow up with ParcelFlow in 72 hours for final closure and offer postmortem summary.
Monitoring: Create an alert on allocator.reclaims.force > 50/min for a dedicated pool to flag noisy-keepalive patterns early.

Issue summary:
Customers on NovaRetail (Dedicated pool) report streaming chat sessions that enter a long silent period mid-generation. Client receives keepalive events (SSE 'ping' frames or websocket pings) and the connection remains open, but no new tokens are emitted for 12–60s. Impact:
- Multiple customers using dedicated capacity experience incomplete messages for long, multi-turn assistant responses (2–6% of long responses; higher under burst load).
- User-visible failures in chat flows (truncated guidance, missing code blocks).
- Reproducible for NovaRetail traffic during scheduled traffic spikes and observed on a handful of other dedicated tenants.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (dedicated-gpu-pool-7) in us-east region.
- Serving runtime version: 2026.02.28-rt.
- Edge proxy: envoy 1.27 with keepalive settings left at defaults.
- Autoscaler and preemption enabled (burst/overcommit allowed).

Steps to reproduce (best-effort):
1. Customer sends a long-form assistant prompt that triggers generation + streaming via SSE (chunked event-stream) or websocket. Request has expected token count ~1200 and window contains multiple function calls and long context.
2. Send concurrent background traffic to same dedicated pool to increase scheduling churn (simulate other tenants bursting).
3. Observe client-side keepalives continuing but no token stream for a prolonged period (12–60s).
4. When connection resumes, client sometimes sees a short duplicate segment and then final chunk absent.

Observed vs Expected:
- Observed: silent period mid-generation, duplicate token replay on resume, final tokens missing.
- Expected: steady token emission until final [DONE], no duplicate replays, reconnection resumes cleanly or fails gracefully with explicit error.

Logs / traces / snippets:
- Edge logs show continuous 200/0 responses and keepalive pings from client. No 5xx from edge at time of stall.
- Serving runtime logs around worker swap show: "worker preempted for eviction: host-oom?" followed by "kv-cache checkpoint start" and "reassign session queue id=...".
- Trace sample (redacted): timeline shows generator process paused at token 842, then worker evicted, new worker picked up request ID but reports missing tail-kv; a short backfill of tokens 820-828 emitted then stop.
- No explicit OOM error in kernel logs; but dmesg entries show sporadic CUDA evictions on same host at similar times.

Repro frequency: ~2–6% of long-generation requests during bursts; lower outside burst windows.

Customer notes (NovaRetail):
- Started after last patch to autoscaler (2026-02-26) that enabled faster eviction of idle workers in dedicated pools.
- They can reproduce by sending multiple long-chat requests in parallel (50–80 RTTs).

Investigation notes (summary):
- Hypothesis 1: aggressive worker preemption / eviction race leaves in-flight sessions in an inconsistent state where the new worker attempts partial backfill from KV-cache but misses final tail tokens due to checkpoint boundary.
- Hypothesis 2: edge-proxy connection reuse + HTTP/2 stream id recycling introduces subtle replay/duplication when sessions are reassigned mid-stream.
- Evidence: serving runtime logs show "kv-cache checkpoint start" immediately prior to pause and CUDA eviction traces overlap with observed time windows. Edge logs show stream-id reassign events for some request IDs.
- Mitigations tried: temporarily disabling burst evictions on the pool reduced incidence to near-zero in a controlled repro test.
- Related previous ticket: SUP-246811 (intermittent-stream-kill-during-priority-eviction) — similar symptom but not identical replay behavior.

Next steps (planned):
1. SRE: instrument dedicated autoscaler to record preemption reason (OOM vs policy) and add a per-request eviction hook tagged to request-id (ETA 2026-03-11).
2. Engineering: add guard in serving-runtime so worker preemption triggers graceful handoff that stalls accept but emits explicit stream-error to client if handoff cannot guarantee tail delivery (investigate idempotent token trimming). PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/5123 (WIP).
3. Edge: audit HTTP/2 stream id reuse and add a safety mapping between connection session-id and backend request-id to prevent replay on reassignment (small config change tested in staging).
4. Short-term workaround: advise NovaRetail to temporarily disable aggressive burst evictions for dedicated pool or increase min-retain-time to 30s.
5. Capture more live traces during next customer spike (runbook attached).

Workaround provided to customer:
- Support recommended: set dedicated pool flag min_retention_seconds=30 and disable preemption for critical queue. Customer applied change on 2026-03-09 and reported reduced occurrence.

Resolution: In progress — mitigation validated in staging and short-term customer workaround applied; engineering work to implement graceful handoff in serving-runtime is underway.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 08:30 NovaRetail (Customer): Confirmed temporary config change to min_retention_seconds=30 reduced truncations during peak. Asking for permanent fix timeline.
2026-03-12 11:02 Engineering (Alex Soto): Opened PR https://github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/5123 to gate worker preemption and emit explicit stream-failure when tail cannot be guaranteed. Requesting review from runtime owners.
2026-03-12 17:30 Support (Elena Park): Notified NovaRetail of progress and shared temporary mitigation. Customer satisfied with workaround pending permanent fix; keeping ticket open until patch merges and is validated in prod.
Detailed timeline: token stream paused at T+22s from request start. Worker eviction event initiated at T+22.3s with reason 'policy-preempt' for node host-7. New worker picked at T+24.1s, attempted KV backfill and emitted duplicate tokens 814-822, then stopped. No [DONE] emitted. Autoscaler logs show eviction triggered by burst policy; disabling burst evictions in staging reproduced mitigation. Edge logs show stream id reassignment for session at same timestamp. Action: prioritize graceful-handoff patch in runtime and edge stream-id mapping fix.
Set dedicated pool min_retention_seconds=30 and disable aggressive burst preemption for critical tenant queues. If immediate, move high-priority traffic to separate non-preemptible pool.
In Progress - short-term workaround applied successfully for NovaRetail. Engineering patch (graceful handoff) in PR and under review. Target for staged rollout: 2026-03-22.
payload.summary: Partial stream completion and duplicate token replay after worker preemption on Dedicated capacity

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed intermittent p95/p99 spikes specifically on short streaming requests (1-5 tokens per request) during a traffic shift window. Spikes manifested as long tail latencies (2-6s) and occasional 504s for the affected tenant.

Impact:
- ClippeHealth production: elevated p99 for streaming endpoints; several user-facing timeouts and degraded UX for chat snippets.
- Estimated affected request volume ~0.6% of total traffic but concentrated on high-value tenant routes.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east serving fleet (dedicated shard for enterprise customers).
- Serving runtime version: v2026.02.18-rc3.
- Coalescer config: continuous-batcher enabled, max_batch_ms=15, max_batch_tokens=4096, tenant_weighting=true.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Run baseline steady-state mix: 60% long sequences (>=512 tokens) + 40% short streaming requests. Latency normal.
2) Shift workload quickly to 85% short streaming (spike of chat snippet traffic) over ~30s.
3) Observe continuous-batcher behavior: short requests are held pending coalescer while long sequences occupy slots; when long sequences begin to finish, a burst of short streams flush with increased queuing latency.

Observed metrics & logs (snippets):
- SLO graphs: https://graphs.redwood.com/clippers/streams/p99-2026-03-01.png
- Sample proxy logs:
  [2026-03-01T14:22:07.123Z] tenant=clipper req_id=abc123 enqueue_time=14:22:07.123 coalescer_hold_ms=2100 flush_size=12
  [2026-03-01T14:22:07.124Z] tenant=clipper req_id=def456 downstream_start=14:22:09.234 downstream_latency_ms=3200 status=504
- Runtime trace: evidence of stream request staying in coalescer queue while GPU compute pipeline occupied by a few long batches.

Initial hypothesis:
- Continuous coalescer prioritization and tenant-weighted merging creates a hidden queue that allows short streams to accumulate behind long-sequence batches during sudden workload composition changes. When the coalescer flushes, the burst causes head-of-line delays visible as p99 spikes and occasional timeouts for streaming sessions.

Requested customer impact details:
- Customer provided a list of failed request IDs and approximate timestamps; support attached and correlated with cluster logs.

Workarounds attempted by Support before internal escalation:
- Temporary per-tenant rate-limit reduction for the short-stream route (reduced QPS by 20%).
- Applied a per-tenant config change to lower coalescer max_hold_ms to 5ms on a single shard as an experiment (reduced tail during trial but had broader throughput implications).

Next steps asked of SRE/Eng:
- Reproduce in staging with synthetic workload that transitions from long->short sequences rapidly.
- Add telemetry to coalescer to emit per-tenant queue depth and hold durations.
- Consider tenant-level safety valve: when short-stream fraction spikes, prefer immediate flush for streaming routes.

2026-03-01 15:02 - Support (Aisha): Customer reports repeated p99 spikes after traffic shift event at 14:20 UTC. Attached request ids + timelines. Marking P1 due to enterprise customer impact.
2026-03-01 16:10 - SRE (Marco): Confirmed cluster wide short-stream p99 increase overlapping timestamps. Root cause not yet identified. Kicked off staging replay job to reproduce with workload generator.
2026-03-01 18:34 - Eng (Priya Rao): Observed coalescer traces showing >2s hold for short streams while long sequence batches are draining. Hypothesis: coalescer chooses to wait to achieve economy-of-scale across tenants which backfires on short streaming sessions.
2026-03-02 09:12 - Support (Aisha): Customer applied temporary client-side retry/backoff; still saw degraded UX. Recommended keep connection open and wait for platform fix.
Staging replay reproduced: synthetic mix with sudden short-heavy spike produced identical p99 tails when tenant_weighting enabled.
Disabling tenant_weighting in staging eliminated tail but increased per-token cost for long-sequence traffic (unacceptable default change).
Telemetry gap: coalescer did not previously emit per-tenant hold times; added lightweight span to trace hold_ms and flush_reason.
Patch candidate: introduce flush-priority for streaming routes and a per-tenant short-stream-fraction threshold to force immediate flush when exceeded.
Tested hotfix on a single prod shard at 2026-03-02 02:30 UTC: adjusted coalescer to prefer streaming flushes under threshold; p99 improved from ~3000ms to ~420ms for affected tenant with minimal impact on long-sequence throughput.
Follow-up: add dashboard for continuous-batcher hold-time per tenant + alert when short-stream fraction >60% and avg hold_ms > 250ms.
Applied targeted hotfix (runtime PR #5894) to coalescer: streaming routes gain flush-priority when per-tenant short-stream fraction exceeds configurable threshold. Hotfix rolled to affected shard and then fleet. Customer confirmed p99 decreased to acceptable levels and timeouts stopped.

Post-incident actions:
- Backfilled telemetry to track per-tenant hold durations and flush reasons.
- Dedicated follow-up task: implement dynamic tenant safety valve and documentation of config knobs for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Engineering ticket created to evaluate long-term coalescer redesign to avoid head-of-line effects: INT-43102.

2026-03-02 04:20 - Eng (Marco): Hotfix rolled to remaining production shards; monitoring shows stable p99 for the tenant.
2026-03-03 10:00 - Customer (ClipperHealth - S. Gomez): Verified fix in production; UX returned to normal. Thank you for quick turnaround.
2026-03-03 12:05 - Support (Aisha): Closing ticket after confirmation from customer and post-deploy metrics review.
payload.summary: Hidden stream-queueing in continuous coalescer causing burst p99s for short streaming requests

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer on Private deployment reports repeated corrupted model shard downloads during automated prefetch and on-demand model pulls. Corruption manifests as checksum/CRC mismatch when the Serving node attempts to assemble multiple HTTP range responses into the final shard file.

Impact:
- Several inference nodes for VaultX service tier went into degraded state: model load failed and requests returned 5xx for ~20% of inference attempts for affected models.
- Customer reports production incidents with transactional features degraded for ~30 minutes during initial reports.

Environment:
- Private control plane deployed into VaultX VPC via Redwood Private package.
- Serving nodes in private subnet with corporate egress via a transparent L7 WAF/proxy appliance (on-prem).
- Artifact store: presigned S3 URLs (us-east-1) served via CDN (CloudFront) and signed by Redwood control plane.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1. Deploy a workload that triggers model prefetch for large model (llama-3-70b).
2. Observe artifact fetcher performing parallel ranged GETs to presigned URL for shard parts.
3. Randomly 1 out of 4 runs fails final CRC during range merge.

Observed behavior:
- Serving logs show: "range-merge failed: checksum mismatch (expected xxxxx, got yyyyy)"
- Network capture from customer egress shows HTTP/1.1 206 responses that sometimes contain Transfer-Encoding: chunked and no Content-Length header; payloads appear inflated compared to origin object length.
- WAF appliance is performing on-the-fly decompression (gunzip) of content flagged as compressed, then re-chunking into transfer-encoding while leaving Content-Range headers unchanged.
- The artifact-fetcher assumes raw byte offsets from Content-Range and stitches byte ranges; after WAF rewrite the offsets no longer align causing byte duplication or gaps.

Expected behavior:
- Ranged GETs should return raw byte slices that match the origin object's offsets. Intermediate proxies should not perform transparent decompression or alter payload length/encoding for presigned range requests.

Logs / evidence attached:
- Excerpts from serving node: "artifact_fetcher.go:278: range-merge failed: expected sha256=3a7bd..., got sha256=2f1e4..."
- Customer pcap excerpts showing Content-Encoding: gzip on origin 206, and WAF-modified response missing Content-Encoding but using chunked frames.
- CRC diff sample and original object length metadata.

Additional context:
- Customer reports WAF team recently enabled "smart-compression-optimization" policy that auto-decompresses responses for certain MIME types to perform inline scanning.
- This is unique to presigned range downloads because the WAF does not preserve range alignment when inflating gzip streams and re-chunks for upstream clients.

Immediate impact mitigation suggested to customer (support):
- Bypass the transparent WAF for redwood-artifact (S3/CloudFront) egress domains via IP ACL or explicit proxy bypass for presigned URL hosts.
- Alternatively, configure WAF to disable response decompression/inspection for Content-Range responses and for our artifact hostnames.

Customer-requested outcome:
- Permanent guidance or best-practice config for private deployments to avoid transparent decompression breaking ranged artifact downloads.
- If possible, a change in Redwood artifact fetcher to detect chunked/inflated responses and retry with a single full GET (fall back) before failing model load.
Captured end-to-end: origin 206 with Content-Encoding: gzip and Content-Range: bytes 0-524287/20971520; WAF returns 206 without Content-Encoding and Transfer-Encoding: chunked but still advertises Content-Range for original offsets.
WAF does decompression to run AV/inspection rules; it does not reconstruct range slices correctly after inflation because gzip streams cannot be arbitrarily sliced without recompression coordination.
Artifact-fetcher code assumes Content-Range byte offsets correspond to returned payload length and stitches byte slices using on-disk offsets — this assumption breaks if middlebox alters payload size without updating headers.
Tested mitigation: adding 'Cache-Control: no-transform' in client request prevented decompression on the test WAF appliance in ~60% of policy variants; some older appliances ignore it. Full bypass was reliable.
Risk analysis: implementing automatic fallback to single GET for large shards would increase bandwidth and latency; need to gate behind heuristics (e.g., N failed range merges, or chunked reply detected).
Next action: open INT change request for artifact-fetcher (INT-99021) to add detection and conservative retry behavior; publish KB for private deployments advising WAF bypass or 'no-transform' policy for artifact hosts.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 13:22 - Customer (VaultX-Networks): We pushed WAF policy change yesterday; saw first failures this morning. Attaching pcap and WAF policy name: vp-http-inspect-2026. We can schedule a maintenance window to test bypass.
2026-03-13 23:15 - Customer (VaultX-Networks): After bypassing WAF for artifact domains, model pulls succeeded and checksum errors disappeared. Happy to keep bypass in place but would like a long-term fix recommendation.
Mitigation validated by customer: bypassing on-prem WAF for artifact hosts resolves checksum mismatches. Engineering to implement conservative fallback (detect chunked/inflated responses and retry with full GET) under INT-99021. Support published KB with immediate config steps (configure WAF to honor Cache-Control: no-transform or add artifact hosts to bypass list). Pending engineering change for long-term remediation.
payload.summary: Transparent proxy inflating compressed responses mid-stream causes range-assembly CRC mismatch and corrupted model shard downloads

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Narrativa Labs reports intermittent streaming stalls and 504/502 proxy errors when rendering long completion streams (often >45s). Failures began after a gradual traffic increase on 2026-03-09 and coincide with spikes in request header sizes for a subset of calls that include long X-Customer-Metadata headers.

Impact:
- ~8% of generation requests for Narrative's prod workspace are failing or terminating early during 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-10 peak windows.
- Customer experiences truncated outputs or EOF in the middle of long responses; affects end-user flows (article generation) and causes retries that increase cost.
- No data plane model correctness regressions; issue appears infrastructural (timeouts/clipping).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (api.redwood.ai), edge LB: aws-alb + nginx edge-proxy layer, region: us-east-1 (primary).
- Customer is enterprise tier with high concurrent streaming usage and custom metadata headers.
- Affected model: redwood-2-large pinned by customer.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Call /v1/chat/completions with streaming enabled, include a large X-Customer-Metadata header (~8KB) and session cookie.
2) Send prompts that produce long running token streams (avg 40-90s).
3) Observe stream stalls or connection close from server after ~30-60s; sometimes client sees 502 or 504.

Observations & logs:
- Edge access logs (ALB + edge-proxy) show many upstream reset/timeout statuses around 30s. Example request ids: rID-20260310-7f8a3, rID-20260310-8b2c1.
- Nginx edge error log snippets: "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream" for requests with large headers.
- ALB metrics show increased 504 counts during the window; backend (serving) healthy target responses remain high for non-streaming quick requests.
- tcpdump from one suspect host captured FIN from proxy side while backend still transmitting data.
- No recent serving runtime changes in production for redwood-2-large since 2026-03-05 (see PRs).

Hypothesis:
1) Edge keepalive/idle timeout or proxy_buffer_size on the nginx layer is closing connections when header parsing or initial upstream handshake takes longer (large headers + TLS handshake overhead) and/or when continuous streaming keeps the request open without emitting headers within proxy idle window.
2) Header size or proxy_buffer limits are causing header clipping which trips a 502 on the ALB/nginx path for requests that include long auth/metadata headers.
3) Customer retried requests due to client-side timeouts causing thundering herd and temporary LB saturation, exacerbating latency/regression.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced a similar failure in staging by sending an 8KB X-Customer-Metadata header and streaming a long completion; staging nginx returned "upstream prematurely closed connection" after ~35s.
- Increasing proxy_read_timeout and proxy_send_timeout on a staging edge replica to 120s removed immediate disconnects in the reproduce run.
- Increasing proxy_buffer_size to handle larger headers prevented header-related 502s in staging.
- ALB idle timeout was at default 60s and nginx keepalive timed at 30s in edge config. Mix of these settings can create premature closes during long-lived streaming sessions.

Workarounds applied (temporary):
- Elevated edge proxy timeouts (proxy_read_timeout, proxy_send_timeout) on a limited canary fleet in us-east-1 to 120s at 2026-03-10 22:45 UTC.
- Increased proxy_buffer_size on canary edge to accept up to 12KB headers.
- Notified Narrative to reduce header payloads as short-term mitigation and to enable client-side keep-alive/read-heartbeat where possible.

Next steps / action items:
- Validate canary results for 24 hours; if stable, roll change to all us-east edge nodes. Owner: Ethan Brooks. ETA: 2026-03-13.
- Add automated alert that correlates large header usage with increased 5xx/stream-abort rates. Owner: Infra Monitoring. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- Audit edge nginx configs for proxy_buffer and timeout defaults and update runbook with recommended settings for enterprise customers with long-lived streams. Owner: SRE Docs. ETA: 2026-03-18.
- Evaluate whether ALB idle timeout should be increased or if we should move to a TCP-level proxy for long streaming paths to avoid HTTP header re-processing. Owner: Network Eng. ETA: 2026-03-20.

Resolution notes (temporary):
- Canary adjustments removed the reproduction case for the specific header size/test vectors. Final resolution pending global rollout and monitoring validation.

2026-03-10 20:10 UTC - support@narrativa: 'We're seeing ~8-10% of long article generation jobs fail mid-stream. Headers include user-profile blobs; these started after enabling richer metadata. Can you investigate?'

Additional notes:
Temporary mitigation applied: increased proxy_read/send timeouts and buffer size on edge canary; awaiting staged rollout and monitoring. Permanent mitigation to be defined after audit of edge timeouts and ALB config.
payload.summary: Intermittent streaming stalls and 504s for long completions; edge keepalive and header clipping suspected

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running WebSocket streaming calls intermittently return a truncated final event (missing closing JSON metadata) and duplicated intermediate chunks after the client crosses a network path that triggers their CDN/edge to re-establish connections.

Impact:
- Production traffic for BrightFlow's realtime summarization pipeline shows ~1.2% of streams ending without finalization; customer must request a re-run.
- Blocks BrightFlow from rolling to GA; customer escalated to enterprise support.

Environment:
- Client: BrightFlow web-app using SDK-js v2.2.0 with subprotocol "redwood-stream-v2"
- Edge: customer routed through FastEdge CDN -> our edge-proxy (h2 terminated) -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime
- Occurs in prod (us-west primary) and sporadically in eu-central during cross-region failover

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a long streaming generation (~1k tokens).
2) Induce network path change (client sim: switch wifi -> cellular or simulate CDN warm-up that causes HTTP/2 connection migration).
3) Client reconnects using the same session token; SDK attempts upgrade/hand-off.
4) Stream sometimes emits duplicated midstream tokens and the final "end" event is truncated (missing closing metadata JSON).

Observed behaviour:
- Sequence numbers out of order in received frames (e.g., chunk 102 appears after 115).
- Final frame arrives with incomplete JSON (truncated trailing "]" and metadata fields).
- Logs from our edge-proxy show an injected "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" header on the proxied upgrade path, followed by odd chunk-size boundaries logged during the same timeframe.

Expected behaviour:
- Upgraded WebSocket stream should preserve ordering and deliver a finalization event with full metadata consistently after reconnect/hand-off.

Logs & artifacts attached in ticket: trace ids (edge / gw): EDGE-202602-04A, GW-202602-04B, client-sample HAR and SDK debug capture.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Client-side: enable SDK retry-on-incomplete-final (workaround flag) and short-circuit to non-streaming fallback for long-running sessions until fix deployed.
- Customer applied the workaround and saw reduction in visible failures but still requests a platform-side fix.

Additional notes:
2026-02-15 16:20 UTC — BrightFlow (Customer): We applied SDK flag and saw failures drop from 1.2% to ~0.2%. Appreciate ETA on platform patch; critical for our GA next week.
Checked upstream: FastEdge sometimes downgrades h2 connection to h1 on warm-up. Our h1 adapter previously added Transfer-Encoding: chunked for streamed responses; this interferes with WebSocket frame passthrough during upgrade handoffs.
Reproducer: internal harness that toggles protocol version and simulates keepalive/handshake yielded deterministic reordering when TE header present.
Captured binary frame deltas: mismatch occurs where chunk size delimiter bytes are interpreted as part of next websocket frame payload on client-side parser implementations that expect contiguous frames.
Correlated customer SDK logs: when duplicate midstream tokens appear the SDK shows a short gap (~80ms) followed by a replayed buffer; suggests partial reassembly after chunk boundary is handled incorrectly.
Related previous ticket: SUP-314159 (socket-handoff-incomplete-terminal-json-batch) — similar symptom but root cause there was LB connection reuse; here root cause is explicit TE injection on upgrade path.
Mitigation validated: disabling TE injection + ensuring upgrade requests bypass streaming-chunking logic prevents corruption in all simulated handoff cases.
Root cause: edge-proxy http/1 adapter was adding Transfer-Encoding: chunked for proxied responses and in a small race this corrupted websocket upgrade passthrough during path migration, resulting in interleaved chunk delimiters being interpreted as part of the websocket payload by certain clients.
Fix deployed: edge-proxy PR #987 removed TE injection for 'Upgrade: websocket' proxied requests and added explicit passthrough mode for h2->h1 handoff. Canary rolled at 2026-02-16 06:00 UTC, full prod roll-out completed in us-west 2026-02-16 13:25 UTC. eu-central scheduled 2026-02-17 03:00 UTC.
Customer action: BrightFlow reverted SDK workaround flag and confirmed streams finalize correctly in us-west after canary/prod rollout. They observed failures drop to 0.05% (within noise).
Follow-ups created: INT-33091: add e2e handoff tests for websocket upgrade scenarios (http/2->http/1/CDN), INT-33102: update runbook and add alert for TE header seen on Upgrade requests, DOC-1222: release note for SDK mentioning edge-proxy fix and recommended SDK version 2.3.1.
Closure: Recommend leaving ticket open for 72h of customer-observed stability after eu-central rollout, then mark Resolved.
payload.summary: WebSocket H2->H1 upgrade via edge proxy inserts chunked framing and causes midstream event reordering and truncated final event

Issue summary: At ~2026-03-12 10:18 PDT customers started observing elevated 5xx responses on several chat and embedding endpoints. Impact: multiple enterprise tenants (notably Finlytics Analytics) experienced request failures and increased tail latency; visible error rate rose from ~0.2% baseline to ~8% over a 15 minute window, with streaming sessions dropping. Environment: prod-us-west (us-west-2), mixed workload: long chat sessions + bulk embedding uploads. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run mixed workload: concurrent long-chat sessions (seq len > 4k) with an embedding bulk upload (100k vectors) from same tenant. 2) Observe apigw request queue growth and progressive 502/503 responses. Logs / metrics: api-gateway accept_queue_depth spiked to 18k, apigw 5xx rate climbed to 8%, runtime process restarts recorded (SIGABRT) with nvml-driver resets on a subset of dedicated runtimes. Prefetch-service reported KV-prefetch lock contention and eviction churn (kvcache.evictions/sec up 350%).

Additional notes:
Correlated apigw accept queue growth with bulk-embedding uploads from the same tenant; accept_queue_depth telemetry tracks with kvcache.evictions/sec spikes.
Runtime logs show repeated 'KVPrefetchLockTimeout' warnings concurrent with high eviction rates; after a threshold the runtime main thread blocked on IO and watchdog triggered restart.
NVML driver logs show resets on 3/12 morning but those align with runtime restarts rather than preceding them; hypothesis is restart is protective rather than root cause.
Traffic replay from supplied Finlytics payload reproduced accept queue growth in staging when combined with synthetic long-chat sessions; confirmed race between prefetch worker and accept/handoff path.
We observed degraded keepalive reuse (socket churn) from apigw when accept queue exceeds 5k, amplifying connection reset/retry behavior and causing hedged retries to spin up additional load on runtimes.
Linked incident SUP-661234 showed a similar pattern but was primarily NVME iowait; this event appears distinct in that kvcache lock contention is the immediate amplifier.
Short term mitigation (applied 2026-03-12 12:12): 1) Per-tenant throttling for Finlytics on bulk-embedding route. 2) Route heavy embedding uploads to a dedicated warm pool to avoid cross-traffic amplification. 3) Raised apigw accept-queue soft limit and enabled faster admission control to shed load earlier.
Permanent fixes planned: 1) Patch runtime to add non-blocking prefetch fallback and reduce aggressive kvcache eviction policy when accept-queue signals backpressure. 2) Add tenant-level early-shed admission at api-gateway for heavy batch routes. 3) Improve observability: surface kvcache.lock-time and accept-queue correlations in Console dashboards and add automated detector alerting. 4) Backfill tests in load harness to include mixed workloads (long chat + bulk embeds).
Follow-ups: Create task for Runtime team to implement fallback (INT-3307-runtime-prefetch-fallback). Schedule postmortem and customer debrief with Finlytics (target 2026-03-18).

Issue summary:
Customers using the browser SDK report that when the client falls back from SSE to a WebRTC datachannel (fast reconnect after a flaky mobile network), the server-side SSE stream appears to deliver all prefix tokens but the final epilogue (closing sentence/metadata block) never arrives. The client sees a successful reconnect and partial completion, but the last paragraph and the "choice: done" metadata are missing.

Impact:
- Affects BrightNote Labs (enterprise) production traffic in eu-west; intermittent (~2-3% of streaming sessions during mobile network handoffs)
- User-visible: trailing sentence or final JSON metadata block omitted, causing client to wait indefinitely for end marker or to treat the response as truncated

Environment:
- Browser SDK v1.12.2 (Chrome & Safari mobile)
- Server side: Hosted API behind streaming-proxy (edge-router -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime)
- Model: redwood-v2-large, long-form summarization workloads (avg 1.2k tokens)
- Observed primarily during WebRTC fallback path (client chooses WebRTC datachannel when long polling/SSE flake)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. On mobile (cellular) with intermittent connectivity, start a streaming SSE generation request via SDK with streaming:true.
2. Induce a short disconnect (toggle airplane mode or force network path migration).
3. Client falls back to creating a WebRTC datachannel and attempts to resume the session using our resume token protocol.
4. Server accepts resume and replays buffered prefix tokens. Client receives content up to the last few tokens, but never receives the final epilogue JSON (closing choice/metadata).

Observed logs / snippets (redacted):
- edge-router: INFO 2026-03-09T14:21:12Z session=bn-89ac resume accepted path=webrtc-fallback
- api-gateway: DEBUG 2026-03-09T14:21:12Z req=0x7f2ff reattach-session token=*** resume_offset=129876
- serving-runtime: WARN 2026-03-09T14:21:12Z session bn-89ac partial_flush final_chunk_written=true kv_flush_deferred=true
- serving-runtime: INFO 2026-03-09T14:21:12Z choice_stream_end_emitted=false
- client SDK console: warn: "stream resumed but no terminating metadata after 12s"

Notes:
- This appears different from simple chunk duplication or splitting. The prefix is reassembled correctly and tokens look consistent; only the terminal metadata and final punctuation are missing.
- Customers sometimes report the client eventually drops the session after a user-visible spinner timeout (5-15s).

Desired outcome:
- Ensure that when a resume occurs over WebRTC fallback, the server emits the terminal epilogue (final JSON event or end marker) reliably, or the SDK should surface a deterministic end-of-stream event after a bounded wait to avoid UX hang.

Additional notes:
Hypothesis: race between final flush of the serving runtime and the datachannel handshake completion leads to terminal event being dropped when we switch transport mid-stream.
Hypothesis: race between final flush of the serving runtime and the datachannel handshake completion leads to terminal event being dropped when we switch transport mid-stream.
Action: adding instrumentation to emit the terminal marker in cleanup path as a mitigation.
2026-03-11 11:03 - Eng (runtime-team): Confirmed race between commit-to-sink and transport switchover. Proposed two changes: 1) ensure final epilogue is persisted to the session ledger before acknowledging resume; 2) SDK change to surface a fallback end-of-stream timer to avoid indefinite waits. Preparing PR for server-side fix and a companion SDK patch.
2026-03-12 16:45 - BrightNote Labs (Customer): Initial canary feedback: sessions observed for 24h show >90% reduction in missing epilogues; a few edge cases remain during rapid twin-handoffs. Requested ETA for full fix and SDK release.
Initial reproduce using Chrome mobile emulation with network toggles showed consistent loss of terminal metadata when client switches to WebRTC datachannel mid-stream.
Edge-router logs indicate normal resume handshake; api-gateway accepts session reattach; serving-runtime shows final_chunk_written=true but choice_stream_end_emitted=false in some runs.
Hypothesis: final epilogue emission races with a cleanup path that can be triggered by transport change. If flush-to-transport fails mid-commit, cleanup may mark stream completed without sending metadata.
Secondary hypothesis: datachannel MTU/fragmentation combined with proxy reassembly under HTTP/2 priority changes can drop the control frame containing end-marker when switching transport layers.
Staging mitigation: emit synthetic terminal metadata on cleanup when transport swap is detected; reduces occurrences in canary tests. Longer-term fix requires persisting final epilogue into session ledger before resume ack.
Related: see linked PRs for instrumentation added to serving-runtime (logs for choice_stream_end_emitted) and proxy handshake traceability.
Workaround deployed to staging (2026-03-12): server cleanup path emits a synthetic terminal metadata event when it detects a transport switch during finalization. Canary with BrightNote shows >90% reduction in missing epilogues.
Planned permanent fix: ensure final epilogue is durably persisted to session ledger and only ACK resume after ledger write (server-side), plus SDK change to include deterministic end-of-stream timer (client-side). Target for full rollout: 2026-03-19 after code review and QA.
Follow-ups:
- ENG-TO-DO: Implement ledger persist-and-ack (PR opened: github.com/redwood/serve/pull/4123).
- SDK-TO-DO: Add end-of-stream fallback timer and expose explicit "resumed_but_no_end" event to app developers (PR planned).
- OPS-TO-DO: Monitor eu-west streaming error rate post-rollout and update runbook with WebRTC-fallback checks.
Ticket will be updated when permanent fix is scheduled and after full rollout verification.

Issue summary: During morning traffic ramp (approx 08:45-09:20 PDT) RetailerX observed a sharp increase in 5xx and duplicate completions for chat and batch completion requests. Customer reported application-level retries and duplicate downstream events causing order duplication alerts and billing anomalies.

Impact: Approximately 18% of RetailerX production requests (targeting rw-instruct-13b-quantized) experienced long tail latencies >10s or 5xx errors. Several streaming sessions were cut and reconnected, producing duplicated completions reported by the customer. RetailerX escalated to enterprise support due to real customer orders being affected.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 08:42 PDT: RetailerX first alerts via support channel and sent sample request ids.
- 2026-03-10 08:44 PDT: Automated alert from latency SLOs (api-gateway) fires; paging SRE.
- 2026-03-10 08:47 PDT: Initial mitigation applied: enforce per-customer circuit breaker at router to limit concurrent inflight requests.
- 2026-03-10 08:55 PDT: Observed reduced 5xx rate but duplicate completions continued for a subset of requests.
- 2026-03-10 09:10 PDT: Root cause hypothesis formed; temporary scheduler tweak deployed to break request fanout.
- 2026-03-10 09:20 PDT: Traffic normalized and customer confirmed reduction in duplicates.
- 2026-03-11: Post-incident follow-up investigation and permanent patch rollout completed.

Steps to reproduce (investigation reproducer):
1) Send high-concurrency batched calls that trigger cross-shard fanout to rw-instruct-13b-quantized with prefix cache enabled.
2) Inject a short scheduler stall condition (simulated CPU spike on scheduler worker) and observe request queue growth.
3) If router-side retry/backoff windows are misaligned with scheduler drain, queued requests are retried and can be delivered twice when the stall clears.

Logs & evidence provided: request ids (sample): rdx-20260310-8a7e, rdx-20260310-8a9f, rdx-20260310-90b4. Grafana charts: latency_p99 by customer, router_retry_rate, scheduler_queue_depth. Link to live playbacks and HAR artifacts included in Confluence postmortem.

Customer impact summary for RetailerX: duplicate downstream events (order webhook fired twice), elevated token consumption (billing exposure ~+12% for the window), and short-lived UI errors. RetailerX requested a credit assessment for the affected window; finance/CSR looped in.

Mitigation taken during incident: temporary per-customer inflight limit at router, reduced default router retry attempts from 3 -> 1 for affected customer, and an emergency scheduler configuration toggle to prefer draining oldest requests first. These reduced amplification within 15 minutes and restored normal behavior after further tuning.

Permanent fixes implemented: scheduler patch to avoid request coalescing deadlocks under high queue pressure; router/backoff alignment so retries use exponential jitter tied to scheduler drain state; added failing-metric alarms for duplicate completion rate and per-customer inflight token accounting.

Follow-up ask from customer: formal post-incident write-up, confirmation of billing credit, and recommended best practices for their integration (per-tenant concurrency limits, client-side idempotency keys).
Support (Marisol): Received initial flagged request ids and screenshots of duplicate webhooks. Engaged SRE escalation at 08:44 PDT.
SRE (Liam): Confirmed router retry spike and scheduler queue growth; applied temporary inflight limit and lowered retries for RetailerX. Noted that draining order resolved duplicates for most sessions.
RetailerX (Ben Collins): Thanks — we still saw two order events for two customers after the change at ~09:00 PDT. Can you confirm if those will be credits?
SRE (Liam): Investigating root cause; adding postmortem and draft credit amount for finance. ETA for permanent fix: 48 hours. Will follow up with runbook improvements.
CS (Priya Singh): Escalated billing request to finance with preliminary exposure estimate +12% tokens during 08:30-09:30 PDT. Finance assigned to ticket FIN-2384.
Customer (Ben): RetailerX confirms that after the rollback at 09:20 PDT duplicates stopped. Awaiting postmortem and credit confirmation.
Initial hypothesis: autoscaler-induced scheduler jitter causing request starvation on a small subset of scheduler workers.
Observed scheduler_queue_depth spike correlated with a new scheduler release (rollout completed 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC) that changed coalescing semantics for batched requests.
Router retry policy did not observe scheduler backpressure signals; retries were retried aggressively and then reconciled when the scheduler cleared, producing duplicate completions in client-visible streams.
Reproducer created in staging by simulating scheduler stall and high fanout; confirmed duplicate completions when router retries were aggressive and prefix cache rehydration occurred.
No evidence of data corruption or model state issues; duplicates are delivery-level only.
Rolled back coalescing change in scheduler (patch ID: platform@release-2026.03.11:7f2a1bd).
Deployed router change to respect scheduler drain signals for retry/backoff alignment and added exponential jitter tied to drain state.
Added per-customer inflight caps (configurable) and defaulted RetailerX to a conservative cap for 72 hours post-incident.
Created new alerting: duplicate_completion_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m and per-customer token surge detection.
Finance and CS agreed on a provisional credit: 12% of tokens billed for 2026-03-10 08:30-09:30 PDT pending final audit (ticket FIN-2384).
Postmortem published and shared with RetailerX: https://confluence.redwood.ai/postmortems/SUP-824568-retailerx.

SRE-118: Expand per-customer observability dashboards to include inflight_count and duplicate_completion_rate (owner: Aisha Khan, due: 2026-03-16)
