Issue summary:
Customer LexiDocs reports their long-form streaming chat sessions (SSE) frequently stop emitting further tokens ~30–90s into a multi-minute generation. Client remains connected; no explicit SSE close. This started after 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC deploy of an edge proxy rewrite rule.

Impact:
- Several customers on Dedicated experienced mid-generation stalls affecting production chat features.
- Writes as 'hang' (no new data) requiring user refresh; some users reported multiple attempts to re-request leading to duplicate assistant messages.
- Incident causes downstream timeouts in LexiDocs processing logic; revenue-impacting for high-concurrency workflows during business hours.

Environment:
- Redwood prod, us-east region (edge cluster east-1).
- Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream (SSE) and websocket multiplexing.
- Traffic passes through our new streaming-rewrite proxy that performs HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation and header normalizations for tenant gateways.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided & internal):
1) Create a long prompt that triggers multi-minute generation (e.g., 6k token instruction + large completion target).
2) Start streaming SSE request via curl or browser client.
3) Observe initial token stream for ~20–90s then stream stops sending new data despite model still generating on worker (worker logs show active token production).
4) Client connection remains open; no "event: close" or final bracket is sent.
5) Replaying same request against a bypassed route (skipping streaming-rewrite proxy) completes normally.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- Edge proxy (haproxy-like) shows repeated small writes merged into a bigger TCP segment; upstream chunk boundary markers ("\n\n" SSE delimiter) missing after a particular rewrite path. Example tail: "data: {\"delta\":\"token\"}\r\ndata: {\"delta\":\"token\"}\r\n" then abrupt pause.
- Serving runtime worker logs (timestamps aligned) show generated token batches continuing for another 45s after client-side silence.
- tcpdump on edge indicates a mid-stream rewrite that collapses two chunked frames into one without re-inserting SSE event separators, causing client-side SSE parser to wait for delimiter.
- No 5xx seen; connection not closed by proxy.

Additional context:
- Change rolled out 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC to streaming-rewrite proxy intended to compress headers and reduce TLS handshakes.
- Not every long stream affected; appears correlated with sequences that produce many very small chunk writes (highly tokenized output).
- Customer attempted simple workaround: enable shorter max-token-per-chunk at client side; reduced frequency of stalls but not eliminated.

2026-03-10 09:12 Support - Aisha: Logged initial report, asked customer for sample curl + reproducible prompt; requested request IDs and approximate timestamps. SLA P1 acknowledged.
2026-03-10 09:38 Customer - LexiDocs (J. Ramirez): Provided request IDs (req-az3k, req-az3l) and a reproduction prompt; noted that bypassing tenant gateway removes issue.
2026-03-10 11:04 Eng - Diego: Started correlation of proxy logs with worker logs. Noted consistent pattern of chunk boundary loss in rewrite service for affected requests.
2026-03-11 02:46 Eng - Priya Shah: Deployed debug build of streaming-rewrite with additional socket-level write tracing to a canary subset of edge nodes. Observed a specific rewrite code path that coalesces small writes and drops SSE separator insertion under backpressure.
2026-03-12 14:12 Support - Aisha: Communicated interim mitigation to customer: toggle tenant bypass for streaming routes (temporary), ETA for permanent fix provided. Customer enabled bypass and confirmed improved stability.
2026-03-12 18:05 Eng - Diego: Preparing PR to ensure rewrite preserves chunk boundaries and forces flush after each SSE event. Target deploy 2026-03-13 morning UTC.
Hypothesis 1: Proxy byte coalescing removed SSE event delimiters (\n\n) causing client parsers to wait indefinitely for delimiter - supported by tcpdump traces.
Hypothesis 2: HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation routine incorrectly translated 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' boundaries when header compression triggered during rewrite - reproduced locally under high token emission rates.
Instrumented edge rewrite to log raw socket writes and SSE event emission times. Found write batching calls merging two separate event writes into one write without the middle delimiter when backlog > 16KB.
Serving runtime indicates no worker evictions or OOMs during affected sessions; KV cache and model workers continued producing tokens (rules out model-side stall).
Reproduced the failure in staging with same rewrite code and a scripted client that emits many tiny token writes; bypassing rewrite removes the failure.
Mitigation (short-term): Enabled tenant streaming bypass flag for LexiDocs and other impacted dedicated customers. This routes SSE directly to serving edge without rewrite layer. Customer confirmed immediate improvement.
Fix (long-term): PR merged (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4211) which: a) disables write coalescing for SSE endpoints, b) enforces explicit SSE delimiter preservation during HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation, c) adds unit tests simulating high-frequency tiny writes.
Deployment plan: Roll out to 5% of edge nodes on 2026-03-13 08:00 UTC, monitor streaming success rate and token delivery latency, then progressive rollout to 100% if metrics stable.
Follow-ups: Add synthetic end-to-end long-stream canary tests to CI (task INT-3882), update runbook with steps to toggle tenant bypass and identify proxy rewrite regressions, and notify customers via status page about 'streaming stability improvement' on 2026-03-14.
Postmortem action items: 1) Add precise SOCK_WRITE tracing for streaming-rewrite, 2) Add alerts for 'stream silence while worker active' pattern, 3) Backport fix to older edge clusters still running legacy rewrite.

Issue summary:
When customers apply multiple tag filters to a 'Top-N timeseries' widget (e.g., service.name and deployment.env), the widget occasionally renders duplicate series for the same logical entity (same service+deployment combination). Duplicates appear as separate lines with identical labels but different internal series IDs and slightly different point counts.

Impact:
- Inkling Health reports visual confusion and incorrect rollups in a customer-facing SLO dashboard.
- Affects decisioning workflows that rely on the top-n ranking (incorrect top-N selection).
- Reproducible on prod in eu-west and observed by at least two other enterprise customers via support chat.

Environment:
- Console (web) in prod: eu-west
- Dashboard widget: Top-N Timeseries (aggregation: sum over 1m, group by tag.key)
- Query backend: console-query-service v2.11.3 behind CDN
- Cache layer: in-memory per-tenant response cache (service-cache v3.0)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Open customer SLO dashboard in eu-west tenant.
2) Add two tag filters: service.name = "ingest-worker" and deployment.env = "canary".
3) Set time window to last 6 hours and refresh.
4) Observe Top-N widget: duplicate lines appear for the same service, with identical labels but separate series counts.
5) Remove one filter and reapply it -> sometimes duplicates disappear; results vary between hard refresh vs. soft refresh.

Observed logs / traces / query ids:
- Example query id: qid=20260302-8b7a1 (console-query-service)
- Raw query returned two aggregation buckets with the same composite key after server-side normalization: "ingest-worker|canary" and "ingest-worker|canary#alias-2"
- Trace snippet (span ids): span=svc-query-23a, cache-hit=true, cache-key=tenant-345:topn:ingest-worker|canary
- Browser console: widget-mapper warns: "duplicate-series-detected" for widget_id=wdg-79

Additional notes:
- Customer reports that exporting the same widget to CSV yields a single logical row per entity (server-side CSV export did correct dedupe), suggesting the duplication is introduced at the widget rendering or client-side series mapping stage, but query payload does include both buckets in some cases.
- Occurs more frequently when tenant-level cache entries are near eviction and when small timing offsets happen between cache refresh and name-aliasing updates.

Expected behaviour:
- Top-N timeseries widget should deduplicate on the logical grouping key (service.name + deployment.env) after server-side normalization prior to rendering.

Workaround (customer-facing):
- Temporary: Toggle one of the tag filters off and on OR perform a hard browser refresh; in some cases this forces the widget to request a fresh query and returns a single series.
- For pipeline users: Use the CSV export for authoritative values until fix is deployed.

Additional notes:
Initial hypothesis: client-side mapper bug — later adjusted after backend logs showed both buckets present in response.
Reproduction in staging required manipulating cache TTL and triggering name-alias normalization concurrently to hit the race window.
Root cause: non-idempotent alias rewrite in query-service normalization path leading to both aliased and unaliased aggregation buckets being included in responses when cache was partially updated.
Frontend should also defensively dedupe identical logical groupings to avoid visual anomalies in the event of future backend transient states.
Related regression: introduced in platform change 2.11.0 that modified aliasing behaviour — add to changelog and postmortem.
Fix deployed: made aliasing normalization idempotent at the query-service layer (v2.11.4) and added defensive dedupe in console-web widget mapper (v1.42.2). Verified with Inkling Health in eu-west; duplicates no longer appear. Follow-ups: add automated regression test that simulates concurrent alias and cache update, and add an alert to the console observability dashboard for 'duplicate-series-detected' events. Owner: Marco Liu (SRE) and Priya Shah (Frontend).
2026-03-05 - Hotfix rollout completed to eu-west, canary monitored for 24 hours with no recurrence.
2026-03-06 - Added unit tests for idempotent normalization and end-to-end test covering widget dedupe.
2026-03-08 - Backfilled postmortem note to Confluence and scheduled follow-up ticket for analytics alert: INT-4120.

Issue summary:
Customers on private deployment behind a Transit Gateway peered to a VPCE report intermittent control-plane failures where agent nodes cannot fetch model artifacts from S3 presigned URLs. Failures manifest as TLS negotiation timeouts or immediate connection close after ALPN negotiation. Impact: model pulls fail intermittently during autoscaling and rolling upgrades causing request failures and degraded latency for affected tenants.

Impact:
- Several serving nodes failed to pull model shards during scale-out windows for AtlasDocs (private deployment).
- Customers observed increased 5xx during the window and degraded throughput until manual node restart.

Initial environment details:
- Private deployment using TGW in customer account with AWS VPCE Interface for control-plane egress to Redwood S3 endpoints.
- Customer applies a third-party firewall appliance in the TGW attachment which performs ALPN-inspecting proxying and does HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation for some flows.
- Agents running our private-agent v2.9.1.
- Affected region: us-east-1.

1. Customer triggers scale-out by increasing model replicas (synthetic load).
2. New agent attempts to fetch model artifact via presigned S3 URL over TLS to storage.redwood.ai (via VPCE).
3. Traffic is routed through TGW attachment where firewall/proxy may inspect and rewrite ALPN.
4. Connection stalls during TLS handshake/ALPN selection or immediately resets after ALPN exchange.
5. Agent retries and eventually succeeds or hits timeout, leaving node partially provisioned.
Sample agent error lines (redacted):
- 2026-02-25T21:12:03Z agent[node-27] fetch_artifact: tls handshake failed: ALPN negotiation returned unexpected protocol (got 'http/1.1' expected 'h2')
- 2026-02-25T21:12:03Z agent[node-27] fetch_artifact: connection closed by peer during TLS handshake
- 2026-02-25T21:12:10Z agent[node-27] fetch_artifact: retrying (attempt 2)
- CloudTrail/VPC Flow: connections from node-27 to vpce-0abc: dst_port=443 tcp_flags=SYN
- Firewall logs (customer): ALPN rewrite applied, translated h2 -> http/1.1 for specific host patterns

- Hypothesis: third-party firewall attached to TGW performs ALPN rewriting/translation that breaks end-to-end HTTP/2 (h2) expectation from our control plane and S3 presigned host, causing TLS to fall back or be torn down.
- Reproduced with customer by capturing tcpdump at agent and comparing TLS ClientHello/ServerHello. ClientHello requests ALPN=['h2','http/1.1']; ServerHello from the upstream endpoint sometimes replies 'http/1.1' (rewritten) leading our agent's TLS stack to consider the connection incompatible for HTTP/2 artifact streaming, and subsequent application-level logic aborts.
- Packet traces show occasional SYN/ACK and then RST after ALPN selection indicating middlebox actively resetting flows it deems incompatible.
- Related to TGW path: when we forced an alternate egress via a NAT Gateway in a customer test subnet (bypassing the firewall appliance), artifact pulls succeeded consistently.
- Linked Slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/support) thread ID: C02QZ9X5L describing initial report.
- PR to add more diagnostic verbosity on agent TLS negotiation merged: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4382.

Additional notes:
AtlasDocs Infra (customer): 2026-02-25 22:10 UTC - Confirmed we have a proxy policy that downgrades h2 to http/1.1 for large-object downloads due to appliance bugs. Can we accept http/1.1 for artifact fetches?
Workaround provided: customer created a small egress path that bypasses the ALPN-rewriting appliance for agent control-plane egress to storage.redwood.ai (validated successful artifact fetch). Recommended cloud-side mitigations: configure firewall to preserve ALPN or whitelist storage.redwood.ai for pass-through TLS.
Permanent fix plan: engineering to release agent v2.9.2 with relaxed ALPN handling for presigned artifact flows and improved diagnostic logging (PR merged to trunk). SRE to publish runbook steps for customers with TGW/firewall appliances describing required ALPN passthrough policy and test checklist.
Follow-ups:
- Ship agent v2.9.2 (target 2026-03-02).
- Add automated healthcheck in private-agent to detect ALPN rewrite and emit clear alert to console and support.
- CS to schedule check with AtlasDocs to remove bypass after deployment of v2.9.2 and confirm normal behavior.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customers report intermittent authentication failures and increased handshake latency on long-lived gRPC streams. Failures correlate with TLS 1.3 session resumption attempts when traffic traverses the customer's corporate egress proxy which performs TLS interception.

Impact: Control-plane and serving-node connections using TLS 1.3 resumption fail ~2-5% of resumed handshakes, causing short-lived auth retries, increased token churn, and occasional 503s for streaming requests. Affects a single Private deployment for FinEdge Analytics (production, us-east-1).

Environment: Private deployment behind customer's egress stack. Egress proxy (company-managed) performs TLS termination and re-encryption; proxy advertises ALPN and supports TLS1.3 through re-encryption. Redwood control-plane and serving nodes are on current stable (r23.4).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Deploy private agents in us-east-1 and route outbound through corporate egress proxy.
2) Repeatedly open/close long-lived streaming gRPC connections to the control-plane with client configured to allow TLS 1.3 resumption (PSK).
3) Observe occasional resumed handshake failures and full-handshake fallback.

Observed behavior:
- Failed resumed handshake shows server rejecting the PSK with "unknown_psk" style result (observed in server TLS logs) after the resumed ClientHello is proxied.
- Full handshake fallback succeeds but adds 120–450ms latency per connection.
- Failure rate increases when the egress proxy scales (more re-encryption nodes).

Logs / Evidence provided:
- TLS server logs: "resumption: ticket invalidated/psk_does_not_match_client" on failing attempts.
- tcpdump from agent-facing node shows Proxy rewriting ClientHello and removing the "pre_shared_key" extension in the proxied ClientHello.
- Probe traces show a 2.8x increase in handshake latency during failure windows.
- Customer provided proxy vendor: SecureGate v5.6 with TLS interception module.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: The egress proxy performs TLS termination and re-encryption, and in the process it strips PSK-related extensions or fails to correctly map PSK tickets across its re-encryption backend, causing the origin server to receive a ClientHello without the expected PSK binder values.
- Hypothesis 2: Proxy horizontal scaling means resumed ticket encryption keys are not synchronized across proxy nodes, so a proxied resumed ClientHello may arrive at server wrapped by a proxy node that cannot present the original PSK state.
- Reproduced in our lab by placing a TLS-intercepting proxy that does not preserve the pre_shared_key extension; same failure mode observed.

Workaround / Mitigation:
- Short term: Disable TLS 1.3 PSK resumption on agents/control-plane for the affected deployment (fall back to full handshakes). This avoids the resumed-handshake failure at the cost of higher latency. Customer accepted temporary rollback to force full handshakes via agent config flag: "tls.disable_resumption = true".
- Recommended customer action: Configure egress proxy to preserve PSK extensions and binders across re-encryption or configure a passthrough rule for control-plane/serving endpoints to avoid interception.

Next steps / Action items:
- (Support) Documented workaround and requested change from customer support to egress team.
- (Eng) Investigate server-side tolerance: evaluate clearer logging and more descriptive TLS debug messages when PSK binders mismatch.
- (Security) Review whether PSK resumption across intercepted TLS flows introduces security expectations mismatch and update Private deployment guidance.

References: customer tcpdumps, proxy vendor doc, internal lab reproduction notes.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:40 - SRE Team (via slack #private-deploy-support): Noted similar symptom in an unrelated environment where a transparent proxy load-balanced across nodes lacked ticket-key sync. Suggested verifying proxy cluster key sync and passthrough rules.
Customer will coordinate with their proxy vendor to enable PSK preservation or create passthrough for control-plane endpoints. Eng to add clearer logs for PSK binding mismatch (ENG-3421).
payload.summary: TLS 1.3 session resumption fails intermittently after corporate egress proxy strips PSK extensions in Private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLane reports scheduled ingestion workers (background jobs) intermittently failing with 403s when hitting Redwood Private admin endpoints used to fetch model routing metadata. Failures began after they rolled a mapping change in their IdP that prefixed service principals with the tenant shortname (e.g. tenantA:svc-ingest).

Impact:
- Multiple scheduled worker processes (approx 12 workers across two hosts) cannot perform admin fetches; data ingestion backfill stopped.
- Customer business impact: delayed data pipelines and missed SLAs for nightly ingestion.
- Occurs only for the private deployment (VPC-connected) and only when workers originate from on-prem NATed IPs via their VPN gateway.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (v1.8.3) deployed in customer VPC us-west-2.
- Identity provider: Okta (custom SAML assertion + SCIM sync).
- Affected hosts: 10.0.34.0/24 (NATed to customer public IP 35.189.72.44).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Provision a service principal in IdP named tenantA:svc-ingest with role claim service_roles=["tenantA:ingestor","tenantA:readonly"].
2) SCIM sync runs and creates a service account object in Redwood with display name 'tenantA:svc-ingest'.
3) Scheduled worker authenticates via SSO service-account flow and receives SAML assertion with prefixed claims.
4) Worker attempts admin endpoint GET /v1/internal/model-routing and receives 403.

Observed logs / evidence:
- Gateway logs show 403 with message: "rbac: role lookup failed for principal 'svc-ingest'" (no tenant prefix).
- Identity proxy audit shows assertion transformed: original claim 'service_roles' => ["tenantA:ingestor","tenantA:readonly"] but downstream RBAC lookup strips prefix when request arrives from 35.189.72.44.
- SCIM audit confirms account created with name containing colon.
- Customer reproducer attached (steps + sample SAML assertion).

Initial hypothesis:
- Ingress path used by on-prem NATed IPs triggers header normalization in the edge/ingress (proxy) which strips or splits the claim value at ':' resulting in principal name mismatch during role binding resolution.
- Alternate hypothesis: SCIM provisioning created a resource with colon-encoded name and downstream claim canonicalizer treats colon as namespace separator only when IP is flagged as private-origin by the ingress.

Workarounds tried by customer before opening ticket:
- Re-provisioning the service account without the tenant prefix (svc-ingest) — works, but requires a breaking rename and rekeying across their fleet.
- Forcing workers to egress via a cloud NAT (different public IP) — also shows successful auth, pointing to IP-based path differences.

Requested outcome:
- Identify why prefixed claims are split/stripped on requests originating from customer NAT.
- Recommend minimal remediation (edge configuration, claim canonicalization, or SCIM mapping) so customer can retain tenant-prefixed service principals without renaming fleet-wide.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 08:45 - BrightLane (Customer): We can confirm both reproducer and workaround (re-provision without prefix) works. Prefer solution that preserves prefixed principal names.
03/12: Confirmed 403 pattern tied to principal canonicalization mismatch; RBAC engine expects principal names with tenant prefix but lookup attempted with stripped name.
03/12: Verified SCIM created account with full prefixed displayName; RBAC role bindings exist for 'tenantA:ingestor'.
03/13: Replication on internal staging fails when traffic egresses via cloud NAT; succeeds without ingress transform — indicates ingress path transforms are causal.
03/14: Identified legacy-proxy transform in edge-config where header values containing ':' are split into multiple headers for downstream processing. This transform is keyed by source IP lists (partner ranges).
03/14: Risk assessment: allowlisting customer's NAT IPs removes transform but may expand attack surface if misused. Patch attempts to narrowly target header names used for SAML claims and only for authenticated, signed assertions.
03/14: Security review requested on PR #2145; need to ensure no other header namespaces would be bypassed unintentionally.
Next: stage PR to canary, run integration test with BrightLane's assertion, and confirm scheduled workers recover without renaming.
Workaround and in-progress fix: temporary mitigation accepted by customer — allowlist their NAT public IP in edge config to bypass legacy colon-splitting transform. Engineering opened PR (edge-config/pull/2145) to stop splitting ':' for SAML claim headers and to only apply rule for non-authenticated paths. QA scheduled and canary deployment planned. Post-deploy follow-up: customer to confirm scheduled workers resume normal operations for 48 hours. Follow-up tasks: create permanent ingress rule exception documented in runbook, add integration test for colon-containing claim values, and consider SCIM normalization guidance in admin docs.
Temporary allowlist applied 2026-03-14 18:20 by Jordan Lee; customer reported recovery of 10/12 workers within 15 minutes.
Edge PR pending security sign-off; expected deployment to canary 2026-03-16.
Follow-up ticket to add automated test and runbook created INT-4208.
payload.summary: Prefixed claim namespace split during private SSO mapping causes scheduled workers to lose service-role bindings

Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12 11:45 UTC DocSearch reported that their reranking endpoint returned dramatically fewer candidates and streaming rerank requests stalled. Impact: 90% candidate suppression for multi-document rerank flows and ~30s tail stalls on streaming connections. Environment: dedicated tenant on prod (us-east), pinned to redwood-embed-v3-fp16. Symptoms appeared immediately following a scheduled proxy sidecar upgrade.
DocSearch search UX degraded — rerank returned empty or single-candidate responses for ~majority of requests. Several customer API clients experienced streaming connections that never completed and timed out. Business impact: customer-reported feature outage affecting search relevance for active users.
1) Use customer tenant credentials to call /v1/rerank with embedding vectors produced by redwood-embed-v3-fp16
2) Observe returned candidate list length and streaming behavior (server-sent events / chunked responses),
3) Re-run while toggling proxy compression flag (gzip vs none) or hitting a proxy version prior to 2026-03-12 to compare results
4) Capture raw request/response bodies from the proxy access logs for analysis
2026-03-12T11:46:03Z proxy-01 INFO forwarded request id=abc123 content-encoding=gzip payload-size=12460
2026-03-12T11:46:04Z embed-service WARN decode-failed id=abc123 heuristics=byte-alignment-mismatch
2026-03-12T11:46:05Z reranker ERROR empty-candidates id=abc123 returned=0
2026-03-12T11:46:07Z streaming WARN client-conn id=abc123 stalled-for=31s
Correlation: spike in rerank empty-set events aligned to proxy sidecar rollout at 2026-03-12 11:40 UTC (deploy tag proxy-v2.14.0).
Hypothesis A: proxy compression/encoding layer mutated binary embedding payload on-the-wire (zero-padding or truncation) — resulting in 'orientation flip' signatures in embed decoding heuristics.
Hypothesis B: new compression library toggled a short-circuit that changed chunk framing for streams, causing the embed deserializer to interpret payload as little-endian vs expected big-endian for some message frames.
Evidence: raw proxy-forwarded bodies show repeated 0x00 paddings and occasional 0xFF sequences near embedding vectors; decode error rate on embed-service rose from 0.03% to 12% in the 5 minutes after deploy.
Repro attempt: hitting an older proxy instance (proxy-v2.13.4) reproduced expected candidate counts; running with compression disabled restored normal behavior for the failing tenant.
Temporary mitigation: blocked rollout to remaining hosts and placed failing proxy daemonset on rollback schedule.

Additional notes:
Jordan Li - infra-proxy (2026-03-12): Confirmed compression library (libzstd 1.5.8 -> 1.5.9) bump in proxy-v2.14.0 — we added a streaming chunk aggregator change; rolling back now.
SRE Oncall (2026-03-12): Rolled proxy to v2.13.4 on us-east-k8s pool; customer reports immediate improvement in candidate counts; monitoring for 30m.
DocSearch Support (2026-03-12): Verified that search UX returned to expected behavior after rollback; requested root cause and permanent fix.
DocSearch Support (2026-03-14): Customer accepted workaround; asked for timeline for full redeploy with fix and postmortem.
A proxy-side compression/stream framing change introduced during the proxy-v2.14.0 rollout altered binary framing for some large embedding payloads. The embed-service decoder relied on stable framing/endianness and detected malformed frames, which led the reranker to drop candidates or return empty results; streaming chunk boundaries also caused stalls.
Immediate: rolled proxy rollout back to v2.13.4 for affected us-east pools, which restored correct behavior. Permanent: merged a patch to proxy that encodes embed payloads as base64 when compression is enabled to guarantee safe transport of binary vectors across chunked streams. Added unit and e2e tests that simulate large vector frames and integrated a canary deployment for 24h before full rollout.
For customers on dedicated instances, we temporarily disabled proxy-side compression on their tenant pool. Alternatively, customers could toggle to an older proxy route by setting X-Proxy-Route header to 'legacy' until the fixed version is deployed.
1) Postmortem doc: Author and publish root-cause analysis and timeline (owner: Maya Chen) — target 2026-03-16.
2) Monitoring: add a decoding-error dashboard and alert when embed decode error rate >0.5% over 5m (owner: Observability team).
3) Release: schedule full rollout of proxy-v2.14.0+fix to us-east on 2026-03-16 with phased canary and automated rollback (owner: infra-proxy).
4) Customer communication: Send RCA and remediation timeline to DocSearch and schedule a postmortem call (owner: CS Manager).
5) Tests: add fuzz tests for streaming chunk boundaries in CI for embed transport (owner: QA).
payload.summary: Embedding payload corrupted by proxy compression upgrade causing large candidate loss and streaming stalls

payload.description:
Several internal engineers reported being abruptly logged out of the Redwood Console and CLI while performing admin impersonation (sudo-style flow) after a staged Okta configuration change was rolled. The issue manifested as immediate 401s from the auth-proxy and failed token exchanges for active CLI sessions; browser sessions were intermittently preserved for the same users. This ticket captures investigation, mitigation, and postmortem actions.
Approximately 12 active developer/admin sessions across multiple teams were invalidated over a 3-hour window. CI jobs that relied on long-lived CLI tokens failed (3 pipelines). Internal support pages and a couple of emergency access requests were opened. No customer-facing traffic was affected, but internal deployment cadence was disrupted during the incident window.
1) Login to Console via Okta SSO (device-trust enabled) and start an admin impersonation session (sudo -> assume-role via console 'Act as' feature).
2) Open a long-running terminal that authenticates via redwood-cli using the same Okta-backed session (token exchange + short TTL refresh enabled).
3) Trigger an Okta session cookie rotation (internal change rolled via feature flag); observe CLI token exchange attempts after rotation.
4) Expected: CLI should transparently refresh or reauthorize without breaking active shell. Observed: immediate 401 from auth-proxy and CLI prompts for re-login; console session sometimes persisted depending on browser cookie timing.
2026-03-12T15:03:12Z auth-proxy ERROR token-exchange: refresh failed: invalid_grant (okta-session-rotated)
2026-03-12T15:03:13Z cli-proxy WARN session: user=jenna.s incoming-cookie-fingerprint mismatch (prev=0x8a3b, now=0xc1f9)
2026-03-12T15:04:02Z console INFO impersonation-start: user=devops-admin target=bob.k session_id=svc-imp-7741
2026-03-12T15:04:05Z auth-proxy DEBUG session-validate: okta-session-id=00u1... expired-at=2026-03-12T15:04:00Z

Additional notes:
Hypothesis A: Okta session rotation feature (cookie fingerprint rotation) invalidates internal session fingerprint used by auth-proxy, causing immediate token-exchange failures for CLI flows that depend on prior handshake.
Hypothesis B: Admin impersonation flow attaches additional short-lived claims that are not re-bound after Okta re-issuance, leading to RBAC lookup failure during token refresh.
Observed: Browser console sessions often persisted because front-end uses silent SSO with prompt=none and obtains new id_token; redwood-cli does a server-side token exchange and relies on a fingerprint that was rotated, producing invalid_grant.
Telemetry: Spike in 401s from auth-proxy at 15:02-15:10 UTC correlated with Okta tenant feature flag rollout. Affected users had CLI tokens minted within 30 minutes prior to rotation.
Reproduction validated in staging by toggling Okta rotation flag and initiating admin-impersonation CLI flow; reproduced reliably.
Immediate mitigation (15:30 UTC): Rolled back Okta cookie-rotation feature flag for the affected tenant to stop further invalidations.
CLI patch (17:50 UTC): Release redwood-cli v0.12.7 with improved retry: on 401 with reason 'invalid_grant' attempt in-band interactive reauth or fallback to web-based SSO flow before failing hard. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cli/pull/809
Validation: After rollout, no new token-exchange failures observed in 24-hour monitoring window and CI pipelines recovered once developers reauthenticated.
Asha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12 15:08: Report opened after three engineers reported lost CLI sessions while console remained active. Collecting affected users and time windows.
Priya Menon (SRE) 2026-03-12 15:15: Found correlation with Okta tenant flag roll; auth-proxy rejects token-exchange with invalid_grant. Spinning up staging repro now.
Ben Liu (Identity Eng) 2026-03-12 15:40: Confirmed fingerprint rotation path in Okta was toggled by rollout job. We're going to pause the rollout and prepare a tolerant auth-proxy patch.
Liam O'Connor (Eng, assignee) 2026-03-12 16:25: Rolled back tenant flag. Patch merged to auth-proxy to accept previous fingerprint for a 5-minute grace window. Monitoring.
Jenna S. (Reporter) 2026-03-12 17:30: Verified CLI reauth flow works and was able to resume long-running job after update. Marking as resolved pending postmortem.
Liam O'Connor (Eng) 2026-03-14 09:12: Postmortem draft added to Confluence; follow-ups: (1) add dashboard alarm for sudden spike in token-exchange invalid_grant (2) update runbook to coordinate Okta tenant rollouts with auth-proxy versioning (3) schedule an audit of short-lived session flows.

Issue summary: Customer requests a recurring SIEM export that includes per-event entity reconciliation metadata (mapping internal tenant/user IDs to customer-supplied pseudonyms), a GPG-signed snapshot manifest for each daily export, and a short attestation statement for legal review.

Impact: Nordica Payments requires this data package to satisfy an EU regulatory audit window. Failure to provide a deterministically comparable snapshotable export will delay their certification and could impact production go-live timelines.

Environment: Production (eu-west-1), tenant-scoped exports for multiple subaccounts under Nordica Payments AB.

Steps to reproduce / current approach:
1) Customer has configured a tenant-specific webhook to receive audit events (webhook-based delivery).
2) They asked for a dry-run: export of a 24-hour window (2026-03-01 00:00:00 -> 2026-03-02 00:00:00) as NDJSON with an additional reconciliation.csv that maps event.entity_id -> pseudonym_id.
3) They expect a manifest.json.gpg containing SHA256 checksums for each file, and a signature using our GPG key for non-repudiation.

Expected behavior: A reproducible export containing: archived ndjson (events), reconciliation CSV, checksum manifest, GPG signature, and a one-paragraph attestation stating export time range, export generation method, and operator who triggered it.

Actual behavior observed: Support previously generated ad-hoc exports but without reconciliation mapping in the customer-specified format and without a signed manifest. Customer also wants per-event monotonic sequence numbers preserved across retries to enable deterministic replay.

Logs / attachments: customer-provided mapping schema (reconciliation_schema_v2.csv), sample webhook delivery logs (redacted), and their legal checklist (Nordica_Audit_Checklist.pdf). Attached by customer in ticket thread.

Request: Please provide a plan and ETA for: (A) producing the requested dry-run export (single 24-hr window) with reconciliation CSV and GPG-signed manifest; (B) adding a recurring scheduled export option (daily rolls, 30-day retention bundle) that preserves per-event sequence numbers and includes per-file checksums; and (C) documenting the attestation wording we will produce for legal teams.

Customer: Acme AI

Issue summary
- Acme AI reports February invoice tokens are higher than their Usage API export totals for the same billing period.
- They are summing Usage API daily exports by model and region and comparing to the invoice line items.

Impact
- Potential overcharge claim / invoice dispute.
- Risk: RevRec confidence + customer trust.

Billing period / artifacts
- Invoice: INV-2026-02-ACME (Feb 2026 usage)
- Customer comparison window: 2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC through 2026-01-31 23:59:59 UTC (per invoice)
- Customer export method: /v1/usage?start_date=2026-01-01&end_date=2026-01-31 (aggregated by day)

Observed discrepancy (initial)
- Invoice total billed tokens: 9,842,110
- Usage API export total tokens: 9,521,774
- Delta: +320,336 tokens on invoice (+3.36%)
- Delta concentrated in streaming chat completions on rw-llama-70b-instruct (us-east) between 2026-01-18 and 2026-01-24.

Hypotheses
1) Duplicate billing ledger writes on server-side retry/fallback for streaming requests (same customer request counted twice).
2) Usage API export is de-duping by request_id while billing ledger is not (or uses different idempotency key).
3) Late-arriving events / backfills included in invoice but missing from Usage API due to export freshness window.
4) Token counting mismatch between OpenAI-compatible endpoints vs native endpoints (less likely for this specific window).

Investigation notes (what we checked)

Issue summary:
Customer BrightMap reports intermittent 429s on their dedicated pool when their service simultaneously maintains long-lived Server-Sent Events (SSE) sessions and high-volume webhook callback flows. The errors appear as 429 responses from the API edge with throttle headers.

Impact:
- Several production customers are seeing degraded ingestion for a subset of requests (webhook callbacks) while long-lived SSE client sessions are active.
- BrightMap reports ~6-12% callback failure rate during midday traffic spikes; business impact includes delayed analytics and missed alerts.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-012) in eu-west region.
- Prod traffic; mixture of interactive SSE streams (chat UX) + webhook-based batching callbacks to the ingestion endpoint.
- Model traffic: inference (mistral-7b) and embedding generation (emb-encoder-v2).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open 150 concurrent SSE connections using the customer client with keepalive ping every 35s.
2) Start a webhook callback fanout at ~300 requests/min to the /v1/callback endpoint from multiple worker hosts behind a NATed proxy.
3) Observe ~5-10% of webhook requests returning 429 over a 15-minute window; SSE connections remain healthy but some SSE starts are delayed.

Observed behavior:
- Edge returns 429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset in ~20-30s.
- Throttle scope appears to correlate with API key and IP NAT pool reuse.
- BrightMap notes spikes correlate with Kubernetes sidecar health-checks and occasional bulk webhook retries.

Expected behavior:
- Webhook callbacks should be isolated from long-lived SSE sessions where customer has configured route separation and priority classes.

Temporary mitigation requested by customer:
- Guidance on configuration to prevent webhook callback fanout from consuming burst tokens while SSE sessions are active.
- Recommendation on TTL/keepalive tuning and proxy connection pooling to limit token double-counting.
03/10 09:45 Support triage: initial hypothesis - burst accounting mixing long-lived sockets and short webhook requests triggers shared token exhaustion at edge layer.
03/10 11:00 Collected customer traces and X-RateLimit headers; observed repeated near-zero Remaining values across distinct routes but same API key.
03/10 13:20 SRE reproduced locally using a mixed load harness: long-lived SSE clients + short POSTs through pooled NATed proxies; reproduced ~7% 429s within 10 minutes.
03/11 08:10 Hypothesis refined: NAT pool IP reuse causes token bucket attribution to group, health-check pings counted against same key, and sticky route-weighting causes webhook path to inherit lower priority weight.
03/11 12:00 Ran targeted experiment: disabled keepalive probes from a subset of pods and saw webhook 429 rate drop by ~60% for the duration of the test.
03/12 09:30 Edge proxy team instrumented per-connection accounting logs and found websocket/SSE long-lived connections were still contributing to burst-window consumption under current burst-pool config.
Next steps: propose config changes (route isolation + dedicated burst pool for long-lived sessions) and schedule a limited rollback window for BrightMap to try configuration patch.
Also assess whether backfill of burst credits following TTL rollover is delayed due to refill epoch alignment with eu-west time drift.

Support (Aisha) 2026-03-10 10:02: Thanks for reporting. We have started a triage and will collect header traces. Can you provide example X-RateLimit headers and approximate times?
-- Customer attached traces at 09:30-09:50 UTC.
Customer (BrightMap - Lukas) 2026-03-10 11:15: Attached logs and a short runbook to reproduce. We see most 429s against /v1/callback; SSE connections are on /v1/stream. We have keepalives every 35s.

Recommending route isolation and dedicated burst pool for SSE-heavy clients. Scheduling config change for 2026-03-13 22:00 UTC with a 1-hour rollback window.
Customer (Lukas) 2026-03-11 15:10: Thanks — please share exact config changes and any SDK guidance. We need minimal disruption during our business hours (08:00-18:00 CET).
Mitigation in progress: Support recommended enabling per-route priority isolation and requesting a dedicated short-burst pool for webhook callbacks. Planned change window 2026-03-13 22:00 UTC. Permanent fix: edge proxy to treat long-lived SSE keepalive pings as exempt from burst accounting if keepalive interval > 30s and connection marked interactive; engineering ticket INT-33021 tracks implementation. Follow-up: monitor for 48 hours after rollout and collect rate-limit heatmap.
Apply route isolation flags for BrightMap in staging and run mixed-load test (SRE) - target 2026-03-12.
Deploy short-burst dedicated pool for callback route in prod during scheduled window 2026-03-13 22:00 UTC.
Edge engineering to implement keepalive-exemption rule (INT-33021) with PR linked above.
Post-rollout: gather heatmap and customer confirmation; escalate to Sev0 if 429s persist beyond 1 hour after change.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer LumenDocs reported unstable reranking quality and intermittent 502s from our rerank endpoint during a nightly ingestion job. The rerank step receives a mix of embeddings generated by two pipelines (an older FP32 pipeline and a newer ONNX quantized pipeline).

Impact: Several scoring requests returned 502s for batches that included mixed-dimension vectors; other requests returned valid responses but with unexpectedly low cosine similarity scores causing irrelevant top-k results. Customer reported production regression in search relevance and elevated error rate on their dedicated capacity cluster.

Observed at: 2026-03-10 02:14 - first error spike; sustained increased error rate during customer's nightly run (02:00–04:00 UTC).

Why this matters: The reranker assumes homogeneous vector dimensions and normalization semantics. Mixing quantized ONNX outputs (1536 dims, asymmetric quantization and different post-normalization) with FP32 outputs (1024 dims, L2-normalized) produced shape mismatches and incorrect dot-product math when batch-scored on the GPU path, causing runtime exceptions and silent score distortions when shapes were coerced.
1) Customer reproducer: run embed pipeline A (text-embed-1024-fp32-v1) for half the corpus and pipeline B (text-embed-1536-quant8-onnx-v2) for the other half.
2) Submit batched rerank request with interleaved candidate vectors from both pipelines.
3) Observe 502s in ~18% of batches and non-deterministic low similarity scores in successful batches.
4) Local repro by support: used customer sample bundle + mix script attached (see confluence) to produce identical stack traces and score anomalies.
Example stack trace (serving-runtime):
RuntimeError: matmul(): size mismatch, m1: [128,1536], m2: [1024,1024] at serving_runtime/ops/attention.cpp:412
Request id: req_8f7b2a3c
Reranker error context: batch_index=27, candidate_count=128, model=rerank-score-lite-v1
Gateway: 502 Bad Gateway returned by reranker service; upstream error: 1.7s timeout triggered after worker exit.
Customer reproduction log sample attached to ticket (log bundle id: lumendocs-20260310-02).
Initial hypothesis: dimension mismatch only. Deep dive found two correlated root causes: (1) Customer SDK rollout accidentally toggled a new ONNX quantized exporter for part of their pipeline, producing 1536-d vectors; (2) Our reranker accepts mixed-dimension payloads and attempts to pad/truncate silently in one codepath, which produced incorrect numerical results when quantized vectors were padded.

Key findings:
- The embeddings-service accepted both vectors without schema validation (no dim enforcement) when submitted via multipart batch.
- The GPU scoring path asserts equal dims; when that assert was bypassed in a fallback path, we tried a CPU pad-and-score path that produced incorrect normalization semantics.
- Quantized ONNX vectors arrived scaled differently (post-quantization scale factors not reversed) causing cosine scores to shrink even when shapes matched.

Evidence & links:
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/lumen/embedding-errors?from=now-3h&to=now
- Reproducer PR with sample mixed-payload: github.com/lumendocs/repro/commit/24a7c1
- Serving logs referenced above.
Hotfix: added strict embedding-dimension validation at the embeddings-service boundary to reject mixed-dimension batches with 400 and descriptive error. Fixed serving-runtime to fail fast (400) instead of causing 502s when shapes differ. Deployed PRs: embeddings-service#889, serving-runtime#2154. Customer temporarily rolled back ONNX export to FP32 pipeline while fix deployed.

Follow-ups:
- Create alert rule for sudden increase in 'embedding-dimension-mismatch' telemetry (SRE task).
- Update SDK docs to call out dimensions and provide migration checklist (Docs task).
- Outreach: CS to schedule postmortem call with LumenDocs and offer 30 days of waived overage credits for disrupted nightly jobs.
1) Add schema enforcement unit tests and CI gate for embeddings-service PR pipeline.
2) Product to publish embedding migration guide and prepare a compatibility page for quantized exporters.
3) Support to add knowledge base article with recommended remediation steps and SDK upgrade notes.
Ensure quantization exporter includes explicit metadata (vector_dimension, scale_factors, normalization) in embedding payload. Prefer rejecting unknown exporter metadata rather than silently accepting. Consider a migration mode that converts quantized vectors server-side only if safe and opt-in.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 04:20 — LumenDocs (Customer): Provided sample bundle (lumendocs-20260310-02) and noted they only recently enabled 'onnx-export-v2' in their internal pipeline. Asked for blocking priority due to search regression.
payload.summary: Mixed ONNX-quantized and FP32 embeddings in rerank payload causing inconsistent scores and 502 errors

Issue summary:
A Brightline Health tenant observed a sudden increase in 5xx errors from the API gateway for streaming and short request workloads. Error rate spike began ~2026-03-12 03:07 UTC and affected ~12% of the customer's requests for ~40 minutes. Support escalation requested due to degraded user-facing experience in production.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: end users experienced failed streams and short-text generation failures (5xx).
- Scope: single private deployment (Brightline Health VPC) in us-west-2, multiple routes across streaming and standard generation.
- Business: client escalation with account team; potential SLA credit if unresolved.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway returned a mix of 502/503/504 to client SDKs.
- Upstream runtime processes for the tenant showed repeated restarts and a short crash loop during the window.
- Error pattern correlated with a very high rate of TLS session resumption attempts (session-ticket and session-id churn) from a small fleet of customer IPs.

Required action: triage with SRE to identify whether root cause is networking (conn churn), runtime memory pressure, or recent runtime/kernel changes.

1) Send sustained short streaming requests (1-3 token responses, keepalive disabled) from a small number (~20) of concurrent clients, with clients rapidly reconnecting and requesting TLS session resumption instead of full handshakes.
2) Observe edge logs for session-cache misses and connection churn.
3) Watch private runtime logs for elevated prefetch activity and abrupt worker restarts.

Notes: reproduction requires session-resume behavior; normal long-lived keepalives do not trigger the same amplification.
[2026-03-12T03:07:12Z] apigw-usw2-01: http2: stream reset by peer (RST_STREAM) - tenant=brightline
[2026-03-12T03:07:13Z] runtime-tenant-172: Unhandled signal: SIGABRT (runtime-worker) - pid=8421 - reason=GPU memory alloc failed while loading shard
[2026-03-12T03:08:01Z] apigw-usw2-01: 502 Upstream connection closed prematurely - lat_p50=120ms lat_p99=2.1s
[2026-03-12T03:10:40Z] autoscaler: detected burst, attempted scale +2 workers but scale failed with insufficient capacity in private pool

Initial telemetry: session-resume attempts from 3 customer edge IPs spiked by ~8x at 03:07 UTC; connection churn increased accept_rate and short-lived TCP connections on the private gateway. Gateways retried failed backends which amplified load onto runtime prefetch code path. Around same time (03:06 UTC) we rolled a runtime kernel optimization (PR #993) in the us-west-2 private cluster that increased temporary GPU memory usage under heavy prefetch. Hypothesis: combination of resumption storm + increased transient memory footprint triggered GPU allocation failures -> worker exits -> gateway retries -> retry amplification -> elevated 5xx.

Supporting evidence:
- Correlation between session-resume spike and first worker exit timestamp.
- Kernel optimization increases temporary allocation shown in metrics (gpu_mem_temp_alloc 18% -> 62% under churn).
- No other tenants on the same host showed identical patterns (tenant-specific request pattern + model pinning).

Mitigations attempted during window:
- Rate-limited session accept on gateway for tenant (applied 03:12 UTC) -> error rate dropped by 70% within 6 minutes.
- Scaled private pool (attempted) but capacity constrained in that private cluster.
- Rolled back PR #993 from the private cluster for the tenant pool at 03:20 UTC -> runtime worker restarts stabilized.

Workaround applied: temporarily disable session-resume acceptance for Brightline Health at the gateway and rolled back the recently deployed kernel optimization in the tenant's private pool. This removed the immediate 5xx spike and stabilized runtime workers.

Permanent follow-ups:
- Postmortem to validate root cause and sequence (owners: SRE Marco Li, Runtime Eng Priya Desai) due by 2026-03-19.
- Add a guardrail to the gateway to detect session-resume floods and apply early throttling per-tenant. (Owner: network team).
- Add a canary memory-pressure check to the kernel selection path so runtime kernel changes that increase transient memory usage require a canary with prefetch-heavy workload. (Owner: runtime team).
- Update Private deployment runbook with steps to force-evict/isolated fallback routing for misbehaving tenant sessions.

Customer communication: account team notified; Brightline confirmed they accepted temporary throttle while we implement long-term fixes.
payload.summary: Session-resume surge from tenant causing upstream restarts and elevated 5xx across private deployment

Issue summary: A customer reports that a saved exploration (ad-hoc dashboard) changes its group_by ordering when the user toggles the dashboard 'Compact View' control. The ordering change results in trace links (trace anchors) embedded in rows to point to the wrong query cursor / trace context. Impact: Customers lose the ability to reliably click from a dashboard row to the corresponding trace; exports may have mismatched anchors. Occurs intermittently when the exploration contains multi-column group_by and nested aggregations.
1) Login to Console as user with org scoped API key (FinOptima test-org).
2) Open saved exploration 'revenue_stream_distributions_v2' (publicly shared in the org).
3) Ensure the view is set to Expanded (default) and sort is by group_by[0] then group_by[1].
4) Click the 'Compact View' toggle in the top-right of the panel to switch to compact mode.
5) Observe that the visible sort order reverts to a different group_by sequence and row-level 'View Trace' links open trace pages that do not match the row's timestamp or request_id.
6) Toggle back to Expanded view to confirm the order persists incorrectly and trace anchors continue to resolve to different traces.
Frontend console (client): Uncaught TypeError at dashboard-view: undefined comparator for group_by sequence (stack trace attached).
API: GET /v1/dashboard/exploration/{id}?view=compact returned 200 but payload.rewrite_group_order=true
Query service: query-cursor mismatch observed in logs: cursor_id=abc123 resolved to request_id=fx-92 while row metadata request_id=fx-17
Trace service link generation: anchor_hash computed from serialized group_by array (order-dependent) - hash mismatch when UI reorders fields.
03/13 14:22 UTC - Reproduced in staging with FinOptima dataset. Compact View uses a different client-side serialization that normalizes group_by into a sorted map. This transforms the order used to compute trace anchor tokens.
Hypothesis: compact view normalization breaks stable ordering assumption relied on by trace-anchor generation (anchor computed client-side using group_by order).
03/13 16:05 UTC - Confirmed server-side does not re-order group_by on save; problem arises during client render path and when making the ad-hoc export request for anchors.
Potential root cause: compact view component imports a utility (normalizeColumns) that returns keys in alphabetical order; previously anchor code expected insertion order.
Support (Maya): Notified customer and requested temp workaround - avoid toggling Compact View and use 'Export CSV' if they need stable anchors (customer accepted workaround).
Customer (FinOptima - product ops): We see this on multiple saved explorations and it impacts our incident troubleshooting flow. Happy to provide session replay or org-level access for debugging.
SRE (Liam): Reproduced in staging, created minimal test case. Adding @frontend-team for fix. Linking to frontend PR once ready.

Additional notes:
Workaround: Customer advised not to toggle Compact View; use Export CSV for stable anchors or open individual row details. Permanent fix: Frontend PR merged to compute anchor hashes from server-provided canonical_group_by ordering (or fallback to saved ordering when canonical absent). Patch rolled to staging 2026-03-14 and scheduled for prod release 2026-03-16 with a small feature-flag. Follow-up: Add unit tests for serialization order and add end-to-end test covering Compact View toggles.

Issue summary: NimbusAI reported intermittent increases in end-to-end p95 latency for requests from EU clients beginning 2026-03-09. Root cause suspicion: client requests occasionally route to a US-edge due to TLS SNI selection at the edge proxy, resulting in cross-region egress and added TLS handshake time.

Impact: Customer-facing inference experiences 200-800ms p95 spikes for streaming and non-streaming calls; affects SLA-bound workflows for enterprise customer (billing + availability concerns). Not a total outage—requests succeed but latency is elevated and inconsistent.

Environment: prod | eu-west; tenant scoped (NimbusAI account). Observed across multiple model routes (rw-instruction-7b, open-instruct-3b).

Observed behavior: Traffic from EU clients intermittently terminates at an edge node whose TLS SNI selection maps to us-east egress path. Datadog traces show additional 1–2 TLS handshakes and an extra network hop.

Expected behavior: Control-plane residency pin and edge selection should produce stable eu-west egress for pinned tenants with deterministic SNI mapping.

Initial customer-reported symptoms: "We see sudden latency spikes near p95 on the last two days—most calls are fine but every few minutes a request takes an extra 600ms and traces show a US hop."
1) Use tenant API key for NimbusAI (prod) from a eu-west client IP range
2) Send sustained streaming requests at ~5 QPS over 10 minutes to rw-instruction-7b endpoint
3) Observe p95 latency in client telemetry and collect X-Edge-Trace headers when spike occurs
4) Correlate with Datadog trace IDs and edge-proxy access logs (referenced below)
Datadog trace example: https://app.datadoghq.com/trace/trace_id=5f3a... (redacted) - shows extra TLS handshake and 120ms+ RTT to us-east edge
Edge proxy access logs: sni=tenant-nimbus.example.com selected_edge=us-east-1a x_forwarded_for=... timestamp=2026-03-09T14:22:31Z
Residency service timeline: control-plane pin refresh for tenant occurred at 2026-03-09T14:21:58Z (possible race window)
Auth token binding logs: token-scoped residency header present in 94% of requests, missing in 6% correlating with spikes
2026-03-10 09:40 - Support initial triage: confirmed customer p95 spikes correlate with occasional egress to us-east edges.
Hypothesis A: edge-proxy SNI selection falling back to generic SNI mapping when token-scoped residency header absent or trimmed by client (browser preconnect behavior).
Hypothesis B: control-plane residency metadata propagation lag during pin refresh (control-plane reported a 4s propagation delay to some edge caches).
Repro attempt: Forced removal of token-scoped residency header from test requests reproduced egress hop in local lab, indicating header presence is a strong factor.
Trace/metric artifacts: p95 latency increases align with a spike in TLS handshake duration and DNS re-resolve events on edge (see dd metric: edge.tls.handshake.duration.p95).
Cross-check with SUP-210999: similar egress detours reported during control-plane syncs; may be related to same propagation window.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:48 - NimbusAI Support Rep (Customer): 'We confirmed that adding a short header override on our side (X-Residence: eu-west) removed spikes during the afternoon test window. We need a long-term fix.'
Applied short-term workaround (edge proxy preference change to favor token-scoped residency earlier in request lifecycle). Customer reports ~90% reduction in p95 spikes. Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC, TileWave Labs has reported intermittent p95/p99 latency waves (streaming responses timing out or stalling) on their dedicated deployment. The pattern is periodic: 10-20 minute low-latency periods followed by sudden 2-8 minute windows of elevated tail latency for short streaming requests. Impact: Customer-facing features time out for end users (~3% of requests during peaks), causing degraded UX and ticketed escalations. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1 serving redwood/gptx-13b-8bit with continuous-batcher enabled and prefetch threshold tuned to 32 tokens. Observed start: 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC. Current status: In Progress — SRE and runtime eng investigating.
1) Send a sustained stream of short generation requests (1-20 tokens) to TileWave's dedicated endpoint in prod-us-east at ~25 QPS from multiple client IPs. 2) Ensure continuous-batcher mode is enabled with prefetch_threshold=32 and idle_linger_ms=12. 3) Observe p95/p99 latency over a 30 minute window; the issue typically reproduces after 8-12 minutes of traffic fluctuations. Note: reproduction is non-deterministic and appears correlated with small bursts from multiple tenants in the same pool.
- p50 stable ~80ms, p95 spikes from ~180ms to 850ms, p99 spikes up to 2200ms. - Increase in streaming reconnects and 504s during peaks (customer reports timeouts). - batcher_coalesce_delay metric shows periodic jumps from 6ms to 180ms correlating with latency waves.
Prefetch threshold interacts with tenant-aware reweighting and an idle-linger hysteresis in the continuous batcher; when a tenant's burst pattern crosses the prefetch threshold boundary the batcher flips between aggressive prefetching and conservative flush behavior, creating resonant accumulation and delayed flushes (head-of-line effects). This produces periodic micro-batch backlog and long-tail latency for short streaming requests.

2026-03-12 05:10 UTC — SRE collected Datadog flamegraphs; saw sampler threads paused when batcher_coalesce_delay jumps.

2026-03-14 11:00 UTC — Identified a race where prefetch counter and idle_linger_ms update path do not acquire same locks leading to transient misread of effective threshold under load.
Next steps — preparing a targeted patch to synchronize threshold updates and add smoothing to tenant weight changes; plan to deploy canary to a subset of dedicated pools.
Mitigation in progress. Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 03:20 UTC StreamlineAI sees high p95/p99 latency and streaming timeouts for inference requests originating in APAC and routed to eu-west. Symptoms point to an intermediate transparent proxy that is serializing HTTP/2 streams and introducing head-of-line delays; streaming responses are returned in full chunks rather than interleaved tokens, causing user-observed stalls and occasional 504s at the application layer. Impact: customer-facing production service degradation, active customer requests timing out or experiencing multi-second tail latency, increased error rates in their monitoring. Environment: production, apac-east region for client egress, destination region eu-west hosting model endpoints.

Expected behavior: streaming responses should arrive token-by-token (low TTFB, steady token stream). Observed behavior: initial handshake fine, then long pauses between token batches; tcpdump/traces show additional hop and increased TLS handshake + connect times.
1) From an APAC client sim (or from apac-east runbook host) send a streaming /v1/generate request pinned to eu-west using account token for StreamlineAI.
2) Observe the stream: instead of token-by-token frames, tokens arrive in large batches separated by multi-second gaps; p99 token latency > 5s.
3) Capture packet trace (tcpdump -w) and run H2 frame inspect; note single connection with serialized DATA frames and delayed ACKs.
4) Run traceroute and tcptraceroute to eu-west model endpoint and compare AS path to previous baseline; note extra hop through peer AS reported below.
edge-proxy: connect_time_ms spike from median 18ms -> 420ms for flows to eu-west (03:20 UTC)
serving-runtime: stream_chunk_dispatch delayed: queue_depth on egress-socket increased to 128 (03:21-03:40 UTC)
tcpdump: TLS handshake 1.2 resumed, but full handshake round trips increased by +3 (SYN->ACK->TLS) during spike window
app-logs: client-side 504 after 30s on 12% of streaming sessions (customer telemetry)
03:30 UTC - Support initial triage: confirmed customer-reported symptoms and requested packet captures and traceroutes.
03:45 UTC - SRE found AS path for several affected flows now transits through peer AS 64521 which is not in our baseline (baseline was direct transit).
04:10 UTC - Observed intermediate device rewriting TLS session parameters causing session-resume fallbacks and additional RTTs; proxy appears to be a transparent TCP/SSL proxy at upstream peering.
04:40 UTC - Proxy does not preserve HTTP/2 stream multiplexing; it queues/subdivides frames resulting in coarse-grained delivery (token batching) which explains serialized streaming behavior.
05:00 UTC - Workaround validated: forcing route to a different peering (edge-egress-policy override) restored streaming-token granularity and reduced p99 latency to baseline for customers tested.
Hypothesis: recent BGP/peering announcement at provider edge caused path shift through third-party transparent proxy/inspection appliance in APAC transit. That device does not support HTTP/2 streaming properly and is intentionally buffering/aggregating frames for inspection.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 12:00 - Customer (StreamlineAI): Confirmed degraded behavior affected live traffic between 03:20-05:15 UTC; accepted workaround while provider investigates. Asked for postmortem and long-term mitigation.
Workaround: applied edge-egress override to prefer alternate peering for affected account (temporary). Root cause: provider-side peering change routed traffic through a transparent inspection proxy that buffers HTTP/2 frames causing streaming serialization. Next steps: Network to negotiate peer fix or avoid peer via permanent routing policy; Product to add detection for serialized streaming anomalies. Customer notified and monitoring continues.

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports that Console → Usage Insights → Route/Model breakdown total for Feb 1–Feb 5 does not match the invoice usage total for the same period.
- Console shows: $18,742.61
- Invoice usage total shows: $19,008.14
- Delta: $265.53 (~1.40%)

Impact
- Finance team cannot use Usage Insights exports for internal chargeback/QBR because totals don’t reconcile with billing.
- Customer is on beta allowlist for Usage Insights and is using CSV export.

Customer expectation
- Totals should match invoice within small tolerance (customer asked for “exact” match, OK with documented rounding rules).

Environment
- Workspace: heliochat-prod
- Deployment mode: Hosted API
- Region: us-east
- Routes observed: /v1/chat/completions (majority), /v1/embeddings
- Models observed: llama-3.1-70b, llama-3.1-8b (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) In Console → Usage → Usage Insights
2) Time range: 2026-02-01 00:00 UTC → 2026-02-05 23:59 UTC
3) Group by Route + Model
4) Export CSV
5) Compare total_cost_usd sum to invoice line items for same workspace/time range

Notes
- Customer says the delta is not constant across days; some days match within ~$20, others are off by ~$80.
- Customer’s finance team is using UTC for invoice reconciliation.

Requested outcome
- Identify root cause and fix reconciliation for Usage Insights totals vs Billing totals.
- Provide customer-facing explanation and workaround until fix is deployed.
2026-02-06 09:18 (Dev Patel - Support)
Acknowledged. Looping in Cost Attribution + Console Backend. We’ll validate whether this is (a) rounding/timing boundary (b) credits/discount application (c) missing/late metering events or (d) double-counting retries/fallbacks.

Created internal tracking in ENG-3817 (reconciliation) and flagged as P1 due to finance workflow impact.
2026-02-06 10:02 (Markus Klein - Solutions Engineering)
From HelioChat: they’re reconciling against invoice usage subtotal excluding taxes/credits. They are not expecting committed-use discounts to be reflected in the Insights beta (they just want pre-discount usage to match invoice usage lines). They specifically called out /v1/chat/completions showing higher cost in invoice than in Console.
2026-02-06 11:11 (Nadia Rahman - Cost Attribution)
Initial hypothesis: Insights dataset uses request_start_time bucketed by hour; billing uses request_end_time (or ingestion time) for period boundaries. For multi-minute streaming sessions around midnight UTC, period assignment can differ. This would show up as day-to-day mismatch but should net out over longer ranges.

Action: pull sample of mismatched request_ids near boundary and confirm event_time semantics used by insights aggregation job.
2026-02-06 13:40 (Chloe Martin - Console Backend)
Checked query-service: breakdown endpoint sums cost_usd_attributed from analytics aggregate. That aggregate currently stores cost rounded to 4 decimals at hourly partition then re-summed. Billing line items store unrounded cost at request granularity and round at final invoice rendering.

If high volume, rounding-at-partition can create ~0.5–1.5% drift depending on distribution. Need to change to store integer microdollars (or store unrounded decimal) and round only at presentation.
2026-02-07 08:25 (Cole Summers - Billing)
Confirmed invoice usage subtotal is derived from metering event field billable_cost_microusd summed at request granularity, then rounded to cents at invoice generation. No discounts/credits in the number the customer quoted.

Also note: invoice includes retry attempts that were actually executed (each attempt generates a metering event). It does not include gateway-level “logical request retries” that never reached runtime.
2026-02-07 10:03 (Nadia Rahman - Cost Attribution)
Found two contributing factors:
1) Rounding drift: insights aggregate stores cost_usd as FLOAT with rounding at 4 decimals during rollup. Summing across many groups creates systematic undercount relative to micro-USD integer used for billing.
2) Late events: for us-east, ~0.2% of metering events arrive >2 hours late (mostly streaming disconnect + retry). Insights job for the current beta range was materializing hourly partitions with a 90-minute watermark; invoice uses full set (no watermark at generation time).

Net effect aligns with observed undercount in Insights vs invoice (~1.4%).
2026-02-07 10:41 (Dev Patel - Support)
Update drafted for customer:
- We identified a known beta limitation: rounding + late-arriving events can cause Usage Insights to undercount vs invoice for recent ranges.
- We’re implementing a fix to use integer micro-USD at aggregation and extending late-event handling.

Asked Eng for ETA and any recommended workaround for finance until fix ships.
2026-02-08 14:12 (Thomas Baird - Telemetry)
Proposed fix:
- Change aggregate schema to store cost_microusd (INT64) and tokens_in/out (INT64).
- Recompute last 14 days nightly (incremental backfill) until watermark extended and late events handled.
- Increase watermark from 90 minutes → 6 hours for beta, plus add a “data freshness / may be incomplete” banner.

Perf impact: minimal if we keep partitions hourly and only backfill recent partitions.

This aligns with ENG-3812/3817 work; we can land behind feature flag for Insights.
2026-02-10 09:30 (Chloe Martin - Console Backend)
Implemented server-side change to prefer cost_microusd when available and only round in API response. Added freshness metadata + banner support (ties into pr-23170).

Nadia/Cole: please confirm the reconciliation tolerance we should communicate during beta (e.g., <=0.1% once backfill completes).
2026-02-11 16:05 (Cole Summers - Billing)
After patch on staging with backfilled partitions, reconciliation vs billing export is within 0.03% for sample workspaces. Remaining delta is explainable by period boundary semantics for long-running streams, but that nets out if customer uses invoice period boundaries (UTC) and pulls completed partitions.

Recommendation: customer should avoid comparing “last 24 hours” until watermark/backfill finishes; for prior days it should reconcile.
2026-02-12 10:22 (Dev Patel - Support)
Sent customer update:
- Root cause confirmed: (1) rounding at aggregation time, (2) late-arriving metering events in streaming/retry scenarios.
- Fix scheduled and rolling out to prod behind beta flag; we’ll backfill recent days.
- Interim workaround: for reconciliation, use ranges ending at least 6 hours prior to “now” (reduces late-event impact) and prefer invoice’s UTC boundaries.

Customer asked for confirmation that exports will match invoice after fix and whether there will be an audit note in release notes.
2026-02-13 15:18 (Nadia Rahman - Cost Attribution)
Prod rollout complete for Insights allowlisted accounts in us-east. Backfill job completed for 2026-02-01 → 2026-02-12.

Re-ran HelioChat numbers:
- Console total now: $19,007.96
- Invoice usage total: $19,008.14
- Delta: $0.18 (0.001%)

This is within cent-level rounding variance.

Follow-up: we should document “freshness window” and show last_updated_at in UI (already in pr-23170).
2026-02-14 09:05 (Dev Patel - Support)
Confirmed with customer that totals now reconcile within rounding tolerance; customer validated on their side for the same range.

Resolution
- Adjusted insights aggregation to store and sum cost in micro-USD (integer) and only round at presentation/export.
- Extended late-event handling (watermark) and added freshness indicators to reduce comparisons against incomplete partitions.

Closing ticket. Linked to ongoing reconciliation hardening work in ENG-3817.
Fixed in beta rollout: cost aggregation now uses integer micro-USD (billing-consistent) + improved late-event handling and freshness indicators. Backfilled recent partitions; HelioChat totals reconcile within rounding tolerance.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
BrightWrite reported sudden p50/p99 throughput drop and elevated tail latency on their dedicated fleet during a 25-minute window. Traffic profile showed a sharp rise in many short-lived connections (ephemeral fanout) from a new internal worker pool. The autoscaler classified the ephemeral fanout as sustained coldstart activity, delayed scale-up decisions, and the scheduler routed more short streams to a subset of GPUs which saturated NVLink and increased kernel queuing.

Impact:
- Customer observed 4x p99 generation latency and 60% drop in sustained throughput for reserved pool routes.
- Affected customers had degraded UX for chat sessions and some 5xx retries.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: BrightWrite-reserved-01
- Region: us-west-2 primary (failover to us-east-1 unaffected)
- Runtime: redwood-serving v2.14.1
- Autoscaler: predictive policy v1.3.4

Observed metrics and timeline:
- 2026-03-10T13:02 UTC: fanout spike begins (many short connections, median duration 2.3s)
- 13:05–13:25: NVLink utilization on GPU set A rose from 18% to 92%
- 13:06: scheduler attach latency increased; kernel queue length grew, kernel-queue-wait p95 spiked
- 13:10: autoscaler misclassified load pattern and did not provision extra GPUs until 13:20
- 13:27: throughput recovered after manual intervention and temporary routing change
1. Recreate many short-lived parallel streams targetting the dedicated route (e.g., 3000 connections/min with median request length 200 tokens and keepalive 2-5s).
2. Ensure traffic targets the same small set of model variants and the same GPU stripe to mimic affinity.
3. Observe NVLink utilization, kernel queue length, and autoscaler decisions for 15–30 minutes.
4. Verify autoscaler classification metric (pod_attach_duration, connection_duration_histogram) and predictive window outputs.
[2026-03-10T13:06:12Z] gpu-A1 nvlink_util=0.72 kernel_queue=48 attach_latency=120ms
[2026-03-10T13:09:05Z] autoscaler: predicted_sustained=false window_score=0.18 decision=hold
[2026-03-10T13:12:30Z] scheduler: allocated=0 pending_attach=14 route=brightwrite-chat
Support (Aisha): Logged by BrightWrite CS at 2026-03-10 13:30 UTC — reported sharp latency increase on dedicated route BrightWrite-reserved-01.
SRE (Luca): Triage started. Captured GPU telemetry and traced NVLink saturation pattern. Suspect short-lived fanout causing affinity concentration.
Eng (Marina): Noticed autoscaler predictive model treats many short-lived connections as noise; thresholding logic kept it from reacting.
Support (Aisha): Customer confirms they deployed a new worker pool around 12:58 UTC sending rapid short streams.
SRE (Luca): Temporarily rerouted a percentage of traffic to neighbor pool and manually increased GPU allocation at 13:20; throughput normalized by 13:27.
Telemetry shows disproportionate attach events concentrated on 4 GPUs within the reserved stripe leading to NVLink hot spots.
Autoscaler decision logs show sliding-window score remained below reactive threshold due to median connection duration below configured min_duration parameter (default 5s).
Kernel queue metrics align with sustained NVLink saturation — the runtime serializes certain collective ops when NVLink is congested, exacerbating p99 latency.
We observed affinity decay: many short-lived streams reuse same socket pins causing scheduler to prefer GPUs with existing cached KV entries, worsening imbalance.
Cross-check with observability: no driver crashes or OOMs; errors were timeouts and increased 5xx retries from client library.
Immediate workaround: manually increased reserved GPU count for BrightWrite-reserved-01 and applied traffic-split rule to spread new connections across 3 additional stripes at 13:18 UTC.
Customer workaround recommended: throttle aggregator so new worker pool staggers connection bursts or increase keepalive to exceed autoscaler min_duration.
Root cause: autoscaler classification threshold too conservative for workloads with many short sessions; combined with scheduler affinity heuristics this produced NVLink hot spots and kernel queueing.
Long-term fixes: (1) adjust autoscaler to include high-connection-rate signals (attach_rate) in predictive model; (2) scheduler to consider NVLink usage when assigning new short-lived streams; (3) introduce short-session mitigation route that uses round-robin GPU selection; (4) add automated mitigation playbook in runbook.
Follow-ups: related GH PR to change autoscaler scoring (github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/4821), scheduler NVLink-aware allocator spike (github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/1289), and a Confluence postmortem link added.
Playbook updated to include attach_rate check for predictive autoscaler.
Customer requested weekly updates until fixes land; assigned to Solutions Eng for customer communication.
payload.summary: Dedicated pool throughput drop: autoscaler misclassification of ephemeral fanout leads to NVLink saturation and elevated p99
