Issue summary:
Medlytics reported recurring long-tail inference latencies and streaming timeouts each weekday between 08:10 and 09:00 local time. Customer perceived the model as 'hanging' or timing out for single-request generations. Initial triage showed elevated queueing and a large number of near-simultaneous reconnects from the customer's ingestion pipeline.

Impact:
- Several customer endpoints experienced 5-15% error rates (stream disconnects / 499s from customer SDK) during the window.
- Business impact: delayed processing of urgent clinical notes leading to batch reprocessing and customer downtime for parts of the morning ingest.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool assigned to Medlytics, prod/us-east-1, autoscaling enabled with burst capacity.
- Customer is on an event-driven ingestion system that issues many short streaming requests (avg 1.8s) at scale during morning startup.

Expected behavior:
- Short streaming requests should complete with median latency < 450ms and failure rate < 0.1% during normal load.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent long-tail latency spikes (p99 > 4s), increased streaming disconnects, and a high volume of repeated connect attempts from the client during the window.

1) Configure a dedicated customer pool with similar concurrency limits to Medlytics (dedicated GPUs, default burst policy).
2) Simulate morning ingest: send 6k short streaming generation requests over 3 minutes (average ~33rps burst).
3) Use a client that retries immediately on perceived timeout (simple exponential backoff with short initial delay and no jitter).
4) Observe serving-runtime queue depth, batcher saturation, and any 429/soft-quota signals.

Notes: reproducer attached in linked PR and support runbook.
Sample relevant logs (redacted):
- api-gateway: 2026-03-10T08:12:05Z [WARN] conn 0x7f3a drop: stream closed by client after 2500ms
- serving-runtime: 2026-03-10T08:12:06Z [INFO] pool=medlytics deduped-batches=18 active-batches=5 queued-requests=387 kernel-select=avx2
- scheduler: 2026-03-10T08:12:06Z [WARN] soft-quota-hit customer=medlytics window=60s tokens-left=0 next-unblock=2026-03-10T08:12:39Z
- sdk (customer): 2026-03-10T08:12:07Z [INFO] retry_attempt=3 event=client-timeout observed=408

Initial hypothesis: model regression or kernel stall.
Findings:
- No model-side regressions found (commit history & perf tests clean).
- Autoscaling behaved as expected, GPUs not saturated by compute, but request queue length spiked during the burst.
- The dedicated pool enforces a soft per-customer burst window to protect noisy neighbors. When the burst tokens were exhausted, requests entered a queue and received a soft-429 signal; customer SDK interpreted early streaming disconnects/timeouts as failures and retried quickly.
- Rapid retries increased instantaneous concurrency and caused batcher saturation and head-of-line blocking: longer tails for small requests that share batch windows.
- Observed correlation: peaks in SDK retry rate precede the longest queue depths by ~8-12s.
- Reproducible with local load generator when client retry policy lacked jitter and did not respect 429/Retry-After.

Relevant cross-references: Slack #support thread (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/G12345/p1674000), related incident SUP-331878 (soft-quota window behavior), and PR to add queue metrics (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2184).
Short-term mitigations applied (2026-03-10 12:30Z):
- Increased soft-burst tokens for Medlytics dedicated pool for morning window by 25% for 48h.
- Updated rate-window logging to emit detailed per-customer queue depth every 10s (helped verify mitigation).
- Escalated to SDK team: requested immediate guidance to customer to change client retry policy to honor 429/Retry-After and add jitter.

Medium-term fixes deployed (2026-03-11 to 2026-03-12):
- Serving-runtime: adjusted batcher scheduling to prioritize short, low-token-length requests during small-request bursts (deploy: serving-runtime v1.23.1).
- Scheduler: tuned soft-quota window algorithm to smooth token replenishment when repeated short requests are detected in a narrow time window (deploy: scheduler v0.9.7).
- SDK: released advisory and patch (redwood-sdk v1.4.2) with recommended retry templates and a client-side circuit breaker sample.

Customer communication:
- Notified Medlytics on 2026-03-11 with the changes and recommended client changes. Customer confirmed reduced error rates during subsequent windows (post-change p99 latency fell from ~4.2s to ~0.7s; stream disconnects down to 0.3%).

Follow-ups:
- Engineering to monitor next two weeks of morning ingest windows and consider permanent quota plan change if traffic pattern persists.
- Create a new runbook entry about coordinated quota + client retry patterns.

Additional notes:
Aisha Kapoor - SRE (2026-03-10T10:34:00Z): Confirmed soft-quota events in scheduler logs. Attaching logs and correlating with api-gateway disconnects. Hypothesis: token-bucket exhaustion + client retries.
SDK Team (2026-03-11T08:15:00Z): Published advisory with recommended retry config and ETA for patch. SDK patch includes jitter and honors 429 Retry-After. PR linked in ticket.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a small group of dedicated pools (NovaQ Analytics tenant) observed repeated p99 throughput regressions between 11:20-12:05 UTC on 2026-03-12. The pattern is a rapid series of short-lived inference sessions (median duration ~700ms) that chain through an internal multiplexer layer, causing a daisy-chain of allocator attach requests and transient slot hold times.

Impact:
- Intermittent p99 latency spikes and 10-30% throughput drop for the tenant's batched routes.
- Autoscales did not react quickly enough; allocator reported temporary slot exhaustion and denied new attaches.
- Some requests returned 5xx attach-timeout errors and a small percentage of early 429s from the tenant-level backpressure mechanism.

Environment:
- deployment: prod (us-west)
- pool: dedicated-usw2-03 (GPU type: A10x2 mixed inventory)
- model: redwood-open-7b-v1 pinned by customer

Steps to reproduce (observed in production):
1) The tenant issues high-rate short sessions from many small clients (fanout ~120 concurrent short streams).
2) Each session opens a connection and triggers allocator attach to a GPU slot; attach lifecycle includes sidecar-handshake + kv-prefetch + kv-cache-lock checks.
3) Rapid churn results in many attach operations queued in allocator, while sidecar log-flush tasks cause increased NVMe IO latency.
4) Autoscaler uses a 60s smoothing window and did not trigger fast enough; allocator hit transient slot depletion and started rejecting attaches.

Observed logs & metrics snippets:
- allocator.attach_time.p95 spike from 80ms -> 1.2s at peak
- gpu_slot_utilization dropped due to held-but-not-serving slots (ambiguous: 30% slots in 'attach' state)
- nvme_iowait increased by 3-4x on host snapshots coincident with sidecar flushes
- autoscaler.scale_decision lagged by ~45s due to metric smoothing

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Customer-side rate-limit applied to reduce small-session fanout to <60 concurrent short sessions (immediate improvement).
- Support lowered internal tenant priority to allow background housekeeping to proceed and freed several stuck attaches.

Notes: this ticket focuses on dedicated capacity behavior with noisy short-session fanout + sidecar IO coupling that produces oscillatory GPU shortfall. Full RCA pending.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 12:35 UTC - NovaQ Engineering (customer): Confirmed temporary customer-side throttling reduced error rate. They are running many short-lived client streams from mobile agents.
Hypotheses:
- Primary: Short-session daisy-chain creates high attach-per-second rate; allocator serializes work for slot consistency resulting in spikes of 'attach' state that appear as held slots.
- Secondary: Sidecar log flush/housekeeping spike increases host IO latency, extending attach time and amplifying slot hold duration.
- Tertiary: Autoscaler smoothing prevents fast scale-up. Together these produce oscillatory shortfalls.
Evidence collected:
- Allocator traces show surge of attach RPCs queued; median queue length increased from 3 -> 48 during incidents.
- Host iostat/NVMe samples align with sidecar flush cron at :20 and :50 each minute.
- Autoscaler decisions deferred due to 60s window; when smoothing reduced, scale-up happens within 10-15s.
Immediate actions in flight:
- PR #4482 (runtime): add optimistic attach path allowing concurrent metadata read for short sessions (in code review).
- PR #119 (autoscaler): introduce short-session detection profile with lower smoothing for pools tagged 'burst-short-sessions'.
- Sidecar tweak: change log-flush stagger and backoff to avoid synchronized host-level flush at fixed minute marks.
Monitoring & validation plan:
- Add allocator.attach_queue_length alert (>20 sustained for 30s).
- Temporarily monitor NVMe iowait per-host and correlate with attach_time.
In progress - temporary mitigations reduced customer impact: tenant admission cap and customer-side throttling. Implemented autoscaler smoothing override for pool (reduced to 10s) which cut scale-up latency from ~60s to ~12s; this reduced p99 spikes. Runtime PR to improve attach concurrency merged to staging and scheduled for canary on weeknight.
Follow-ups (action items):
- Merge and roll out runtime optimistic attach path across dedicated pools (ENG-2543).
- Add pool tag and autoscaler profile to detect short-session fanouts automatically (ENG-2561).
- Update dedicated runbook: add guidance for admission caps and temporary smoothing overrides.
- Coordinate with customer to adopt client-side connection pooling to reduce fanout.
Will update ticket when canary looks healthy in production and final postmortem is published on confluence.
payload.summary: Short-lived session daisy-chain causes oscillatory GPU shortfall and p99 throughput regression

Issue summary: Since weekend deploy (canary v2026-03-08) StellarApps started seeing repeated p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional 504s on generation endpoints. Impact: Several customer endpoints saw aggregated p99 jump from ~120ms to 1.8-2.2s for short periods (5-10 minutes) resulting in user-facing timeouts and retries. Environment: Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-32), prod us-east primary; steady QPS 6-10 rps per model but observed during traffic drops (2-3 rps) behavior worsens. Suspected area: continuous-batching behavior when connections go idle then re-awaken, causing many connections to fall into a single coalescing window and creating large head-of-line batches that exceed latency SLOs.
1) On dedicated pool customer-dedicated-32, deploy a load generator that ramps QPS from 8 rps to 2 rps over 2 minutes and holds for 10 minutes.
2) Observe per-connection session re-use (keepalive) and watch continuous-batcher metrics in /metrics (batch_size, batch_wait_ms, queue_depth).

Issue summary:
Starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC FluentDocs reported repeated waves of 503/502 responses for a subset of tenant traffic. Errors correlate with short spikes of ephemeral TCP connections from the tenant (~1-2s lifespan) at ~1.2k req/s sustained for ~30s. API gateway logs show large numbers of connections in CLOSE_WAIT and many request contexts timed out with upstream response 503.

Impact:
- Customer SLA impact: multiple failed calls for streaming and non-streaming generation; estimated 8% request failure rate during each wave.
- Affected workloads: both streaming chat and batch generation; latency for successful requests increased by ~300-600ms.

Environment:
- Tenant: FluentDocs (dedicated pool)
- Region: prod-us-west (us-west-2)
- Models: gpt-medium-v1, gpt-large-v1
- Serving runtime version: v2.14.0-rc3
- Gateway version: apigw 1.9.2

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant bursts ephemeral connections (short lived) from many client hosts.
2) API gateway connection pools hit high churn; many sockets rotated and short-lived TLS sessions.
3) Requests are routed to serving runtime; KV-prefetch and batching subsystems see cache thrash.
4) Some runtime workers hit kernel fallback paths (quantized kernel selection) and then exit with SIGABRT or OOM_kill under concurrent GC/alloc pressure.
5) Upstream exits produce 502/503 to client; gateway retries amplify if backend restart is slow.

Observed behavior:
- Gateway logs: repeated 502/503 with upstream "connection reset" and "no healthy upstream" messages.
- Runtime logs: repeated stack traces referencing 'kernel_select::fallback', 'kv_cache_miss_spike', 'prefetch_throttle::panic', and '/usr/bin/runtime: killed by SIGABRT'.
- Metrics: sudden spike in runtime process restarts (+150%), increase in apigw 502/503 rate from 0.2% to 8% for the tenant window.

Expected behavior:
- API gateway should shed load gracefully and route to warm fallbacks without causing widespread runtime crashloops.
- Runtime should avoid selecting unstable kernel fallback under high short-lived concurrency and instead throttle or queue.

Logs & traces (snippets):
- apigw: "conn_churn: pool_open=1200 pool_close=1187; handler_timeout=300ms; upstream_error=502; upstream_msg=connection reset by peer"
- runtime: "[2026-03-10T09:12:31Z] ERROR kernel_select: fallback triggered for model=gpt-large-v1; cpu_kernels_unavailable=2; nvlib_version=2.3.1"
- runtime: "/usr/bin/runtime[pid:23412]: abort() at kernel_runner.cc:412; reason=alloc_failure"

Mitigation applied:
- Support placed tenant on a temporary rate limiter (burst window 400 req/s) and enabled gateway keepalive-extension to favor reuse of TLS sessions.
- Scaled up dedicated serving pool by 6 instances (hot-add) to reduce per-worker load.
- Eng routed traffic to older stable runtime (v2.13.4) for the tenant as an emergency rollback.

Current hypothesis:
1) Short-lived connection surge causes apigw keepalive pool churn and SNI/TLS renegotiation amplification which increases per-request CPU and memory overhead.
2) Runtime kernel selector under v2.14.0-rc3 attempts fallback kernels under resource pressure which are less tested and can OOM or abort under high concurrency.
3) Combined effect leads to noisy neighbor overload inside the dedicated pool and runtime crashloops producing 502/503 amplification.

Next steps (investigation/engineering):
- SRE to capture end-to-end pcap for next burst window and correlate TLS session lifetimes with apigw process metrics.
- Runtime team to add guardrails in kernel selector: avoid fallback when process memory >75% and instead return 429 / queue.
- Product to consider permanent keepalive/burst controls for dedicated customers to limit connection churn.

Workaround/Resolution (temporary):
- Tenant remains on rate-limiter for ephemeral connections and routed to stable runtime. No full fix yet.

Notes:
- Related to but distinct from SUP-51234 (apigw saturation) and SUP-68410 (autoscaler warmup 503s); this ticket centers on kernel fallback crashloops induced by connection churn.

[2026-03-10 10:02 UTC] Aisha Patel (Support): Created ticket after customer reported failure window. Attached initial logs from apigw and brief metric screenshots. Escalated to SRE.
[2026-03-10 11:45 UTC] Diego Kim (SRE): Observed huge spike in TCP open/close rates. Confirmed apigw connection churn. Increased gateway keepalive pool and applied temporary tenant qps cap. Requested runtime logs from Eng.
[2026-03-10 12:30 UTC] Marcelo Ruiz (Runtime Eng): Found repeated aborts in kernel selector on v2.14.0-rc3 when concurrent alloc > 64GB. Rolling the tenant to v2.13.4 reduced restarts immediately. Opening PR to add memory-threshold guard.
[2026-03-11 09:20 UTC] Customer (FluentDocs): Confirmed errors dropped after rollback and rate limiting. They've requested timeline for permanent fix and whether dedicated pool can get kernel selector patch.
[2026-03-12 08:15 UTC] Marcelo Ruiz (Runtime Eng): PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321. Plan: backport guard to stable branch and prepare hotfix release v2.14.0-hotfix1. ETA for hotfix in staging 2026-03-14.
[2026-03-12 14:40 UTC] Aisha Patel (Support): Updated customer that hotfix is in progress and that we will schedule a maintenance window for dedicated pool patching. Keeping ticket In Progress.
workaround: tenant rate-limited and rolled back to v2.13.4; hotfix PR submitted; pending scheduled patch rollout
This ticket should be monitored during the next tenant-burst window. Consider adding synthetic test for short-lived connection surges in CI for dedicated pools.

Issue summary: Customer reports that after enabling a region pin for their dedicated capacity (pin_region=us-east), ~1-2% of requests are observed routing to eu-west and returning with a 60-120ms higher p50. This started after a traffic shift last week. Impact: user-facing inference latency spikes for a subset of requests; intermittent degradation for real-time product features.
Intermittent +60-120ms p50 for ~1-2% of inference requests. Affects time-sensitive features and violates internal latency targets for FinLedger workflows.
1) Customer app makes streaming chat completions to Redwood endpoint pinned to us-east (pin_region=us-east). 2) Observe per-request region header in response metadata. 3) Compare p50/p95 from customer telemetry and Redwood tracing for same request IDs. 4) Repeat during higher load to increase probability of fallthrough.
Some requests (sampled) show response_metadata.region = eu-west and corresponding latency delta. Requests include 'x-rw-request-id' headers and appear to have been handled by fallback routing logic.
When pin_region is set to an explicit region and customer has Dedicated capacity in that region, all requests should remain in the pinned region unless an explicit outage/fallback policy triggers, and fallbacks should be documented and deterministic.
Example request-id: rw-req-20260311-4823. Timestamp: 2026-03-11T14:22:07Z. Customer trace shows 96ms total, Redwood trace shows 174ms and 'route_decision': 'fallback-eu-west' in internal routing log. Another request rw-req-20260312-0192 shows similar pattern.
Attached: routing-decision.log (excerpt), request-trace-20260311.txt. Routing log lines: [2026-03-11T14:22:07Z] rw-req-4823 route_decision=FALLBACK target_region=eu-west reason=pool_capacity_low pinned_region=us-east; [2026-03-11T14:22:08Z] rw-req-0192 route_decision=FALLBACK target_region=eu-west reason=allocator_threshold_exceeded pinned_region=us-east.
Initial hypothesis: fallback policy is allowed for dedicated customers when local pool capacity falls below allocator_threshold. We confirmed via routing logs that the decision path labels these as FALLBACK and target eu-west. Checked Dedicated capacity metrics in the last 24h: short spikes in queue_length on us-east GPU pool during customer peak. Batching and placement attempts were observed to spill over. No errors or 5xx returned. Observed correlation between queue pressure events and fallthrough samples.
Customer provided timeseries and sample request IDs. Support reproduced trace correlation with our routing logs. SRE asked for full allocator metrics and pool sizes. Product asked whether 'pin_region' semantics should be 'strict' vs 'best-effort' for Dedicated customers; current behavior is best-effort with documented fallbacks but customer expected strict locality.
1) Increase reserved capacity for FinLedger's Dedicated pool in us-east to reduce spillover. 2) Temporarily set fallback_policy=no_fallback in customer's routing config to enforce strict locality (tradeoff: higher chance of 429s under load). 3) Tune allocator_threshold to be more conservative for this customer's pools.
Short-term: Customer agreed to increase reserved capacity by 20% and set fallback_policy=no_fallback for the critical route. After change, sampling over 24h shows fallthrough events dropped to 0. Long-term: Product will add explicit 'strict_pin' flag for Dedicated customers to make behavior deterministic and surface consequences in Console and API docs. SRE created INT-3419 to track allocator tuning and autoscaling policy improvements.
2026-03-11 15:02 - FinLedger (customer): We're seeing a small fraction of requests go to eu-west despite pin_region=us-east. This is causing brief UI hitches. Can you explain why?

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 17:05 - FinLedger: No manual changes. Traffic increased ~20% due to a marketing campaign.
2026-03-12 11:45 - Product (Lina Patel): We should clarify region pinning semantics in documentation and consider exposing a strict_pin option for Dedicated tiers. Logged product follow-up.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer FinSight reports intermittent p50->p99 latency jitter in eu-west after enabling strict data residency with automatic failover. Impact: Some user-facing API calls to the Redwood API show spikes from ~120ms median to >1.6s p99 for short windows (1-3 minutes) every 15-30 minutes. Environment: prod (eu-west), Dedicated/enterprise customer with residency toggle enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer routes traffic through eu-west with strict residency toggle on. 2) Run a steady load of short chat/generate requests (100rps) pinned to rw-13b-v1. 3) Observe p50/p95/p99 on Redwood Console and customer's app telemetry; spikes align with failover window events recorded in routing logs. Customer provided timestamps and sample request IDs and traces. Logs: Customer supplied trace ids: trace-eu-0001, trace-eu-0007, trace-eu-0012. Notes: Issue appears correlated with short-duration cross-region egress to us-west fallback pool and an associated rate limit on that fallback pool that manifests as queueing delays, not outright 5xx. No model-level errors observed. Temporary workaround suggested: disable strict residency failover or increase reserved capacity in eu-west while we investigate.

Additional notes:
2026-03-02 - Customer (FinSight, support rep Maya Chen): Confirmed disabling strict failover removed the spikes. Happy to run tests with controlled failover if needed.
2026-03-02 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Noted related alert noise from fallback pool rate-limit thresholds. Recommended adding a circuit-breaker to prevent short cross-region bursts when fallback pool latency or queue depth exceeds threshold.
Checked routing decision logs for the provided timestamps: 11:12-11:14 and 11:43-11:44 UTC show 3-4% of requests routed to fallback-us-west despite eu-west capacity reporting as 'healthy' with transient 'soft-saturations'.
Examined serving-runtime metrics: no model OOMs or infra restarts in eu-west during windows. CPU/GPU utilization showed micro-bursts but averaged below threshold. Us-west fallback pool showed protracted send queue depth with normal GPU utilization but elevated networking egress queueing.
Trace analysis: traces routed to us-west show increased time in 'egress-routing' step and 'send-queue' before token generation, contributing ~700-1200ms extra latency on p99 samples.
Routing policy configuration audit (INT-420): discovered fallback policy for residency toggles had 'global-any' fallback priority and a short 15s session sticky TTL, causing session rotation into fallback after capacity rebalancing. This, combined with an aggressive routing TTL refresh, allowed oscillation.
Hypothesis: combination of (1) fallback policy 'global-any', (2) short sticky-session TTL, and (3) fallback pool transient rate-limits leads to small, periodic cross-region diversions that amplify to p99 jitter for affected requests.
Risk assessment: high for customer P1 enterprise; widespread change must be coordinated. Short-term mitigations available.
Related metrics dashboards: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/routing/fallback-pools and https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/serving/send-queue-depth
Short-term mitigation (applied 2026-03-02): changed residency fallback selection from 'global-any' to 'continent-preferred' for requests originating in eu-west for FinSight. Increased sticky-session TTL from 15s -> 120s for residency-aware sessions. Result: observed elimination of p99 spikes during a 4-hour observation window.
Medium-term fix (planned): implement fallback circuit-breaker that blocks cross-region fallback when fallback pool queue depth or observed latency exceeds defined thresholds. Update routing policy defaults for residency strict mode to prefer same-continent fallback only.
Follow-ups created: INT-420 (routing config audit), INT-428 (fallback circuit-breaker implementation), SUP-99512 (customer follow-up verification after circuit-breaker rollout).
Customer communication: Informed FinSight of short-term mitigation and timeline for medium-term fixes. Provided recommended temporary action: increase reserved eu-west capacity if they expect higher peak loads until medium-term fix ships.
Monitoring: Added temporary alert with tags to detect any reappearance of cross-region routing for FinSight's project and to watch p95/p99 latency delta across regions for 72 hours.
Post-incident: schedule a 1:1 postmortem with Routing and SRE teams; update residency runbook with new fallback config guidance.
Status: In Progress - medium-term fixes scheduled in the upcoming sprint; short-term mitigation validated in prod for customer.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Nordholm Payments enabled Hosted data residency (region pinning) to EU-only in the Console on 2025-02-21 ~09:40 PT. Immediately after enabling, production traffic began failing with deterministic residency enforcement errors.

Impact:
- ~35–60% of requests blocked for ~2 hours (spiky; correlated with model selection).
- Customer reports "sudden 409s" and inability to complete their POC transaction flows.
- Primary pain: unclear which configuration change is required (region endpoint vs allowed region set vs model availability).

Customer expectation:
- All inference and related processing stays within EU.
- If capacity is constrained, they prefer an explicit error over cross-region failover.

What we saw (customer-provided):
- HTTP status: 409
- Error code: RESIDENCY_POLICY_BLOCKED

Additional notes:
- request_id examples: req_01HPZ7C2K7M1Z1TQ2H0Y2K3A9B, req_01HPZ7D4P8VZ6KJH9R3Q9S1W0X
Environment details:
- Hosted API
- Customer is calling via their backend service in AWS eu-central-1, but using default Redwood base URL (no explicit region in endpoint config) for part of their traffic.
- They use chat + embeddings endpoints.
Steps to reproduce (as described by customer):
1) Enable region pinning: allowed_regions = ["eu-west-1"], primary_region = "eu-west-1".
2) Send /v1/chat/completions using model redwood/llama3-70b-instruct.
3) Observe 409 policy blocks.
Initial hypothesis:
- Enforcement working as designed; requests are being evaluated for residency and blocked because routing selects a non-allowed region due to either (a) model availability, (b) client targeting a US endpoint/region implicitly, or (c) prior fallback policy now blocked.
Support questions to answer:
- Are they accidentally calling a US region endpoint / default endpoint?
- Is the requested model available in eu-west-1 for Hosted?
- Is an API key override policy set differently than org/project policy?
- Are embeddings routed differently / on a separate project?
Investigation notes (Redwood):
- Control plane check: org policy set to EU-only with allowed_regions [eu-west-1]; no cross-region fallback allowed.
- Routing traces: attempted region selection us-east-1 for llama3-70b-instruct (EU capacity/model availability constraint).
- Some embeddings requests were missing the intended project header and landed on a different project (still under same org policy, so enforcement still applies).
Customer ask:
They want to keep EU-only and need a concrete remediation checklist (client changes + what to change in allowed regions/model choice) to unblock traffic today.
2025-02-21 10:41 PT - Customer (via Avery): They are using default SDK config (no region override). Failing mostly on model redwood/llama3-70b-instruct. Embeddings failures are intermittent. They expected the platform to "just stay in EU" and pick equivalent infra there.
Also: update SDK/base URL to explicitly use EU region endpoint once configured to avoid confusion during troubleshooting.
1) In Console > Residency: add allowed region eu-central-1 (EU) if available; keep cross-region fallback disabled.
2) Update client to target EU base URL (or set region config) to reduce accidental cross-region attempts.
3) Change model to EU-supported SKU for Hosted (70B not EU-hosted yet).
4) Re-test with request_id capture and confirm 2xx.
Sending to Avery for customer comms.
Resolved with configuration + workload changes: customer switched to EU-available Hosted model(s) and updated client to target EU region explicitly. Confirmed residency enforcement behavior is correct; blocks were due to requested model/route requiring us-east-1, which is disallowed by EU-only policy.
After enabling EU-only residency policy (allowed_regions = [eu-west-1]), the customer continued sending requests for a model (llama3-70b-instruct) that is not currently available in Hosted eu-west-1. Smart routing attempted to select us-east-1 as the compatible/available region; API gateway enforcement deterministically blocked the request with RESIDENCY_POLICY_BLOCKED (HTTP 409). A smaller set of blocks were also caused by transient EU saturation where spill/failover would have gone cross-region (now correctly blocked).
Add/expand Console copy to highlight that region pinning may block requests when a selected model is not available in the allowed region set; recommend region-compatible models.
Product/Eng follow-up: enhance error detail to include a stable sub-code (e.g., RESIDENCY_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE) per ADR-022 guidance to reduce support load.
SE to track Nordholm’s need for 70B-in-EU as a Dedicated EU opportunity; route to Naomi Feldman / enterprise team.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
FinWave has requested the March compliance bundle exported as line-delimited JSON (JSONL) for ingestion into their SIEM. They reported that event timestamps are arriving with mixed timezones (some events stamped in UTC, others in local zone), and field names do not match their mapping (e.g. 'actor_id' vs 'user.id', 'service' vs 'source_service'). They require a normalized field map, stable event IDs for de-duplication, and a rotation-friendly SFTP key policy included in the delivery manifest.

Impact:
- Customer cannot ingest events reliably into their SIEM due to mismatched field names and timezone drift, causing gaps in audit coverage for the quarter.
- Compliance deadline: quarterly audit ingest completes 2026-03-31.

Environment:
- Hosted Redwood API (prod, us-east)
- Export pipeline: audit-exporter -> S3 (s3://redwood-audit-exports/finwave/2026Q1/) -> scheduled SFTP push to FinWave endpoint

Steps to reproduce / gather evidence requested:
1) Request a JSONL export for tenant finwave-prod with date range 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31 using the console export job.
2) Inspect the delivered file at s3://redwood-audit-exports/finwave/2026Q1/exports-2026-03-12.jsonl and sample the first 100 lines.
3) Check the delivery manifest and the signed key fingerprints in the SFTP handshake logs.

Observed behavior:
- Mixed timestamp formats found: ISO-8601 with timezone offsets and naive timestamps without offset. Example lines attached in 'logs'.
- Field normalization mismatch: customer expects nested user.id and event.source.service but we currently export flat keys in several variants.
- The manifest provided references key id 'rot-2025' but customer rotated keys in Feb 2026; SFTP connection shows accepted key but FinWave's ingest flagged signature mismatch.

Expected behavior:
- JSONL with consistent UTC timestamps (ISO-8601 Z) and a guaranteed 'event_id' UUID per event for de-duplication.
- A standard mapping layer applied at export time to match FinWave's SIEM field schema and an accompanying mapping file in the bundle.
- Delivery manifest containing current key fingerprints and a rotation policy note.

Attachments: export sample, delivery_manifest.json (from S3), SFTP handshake excerpt (redacted), customer mapping template.
1) From Console > Audits > Exports, create export for tenant finwave-prod for date range 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31.
2) Wait for scheduled delivery to s3://redwood-audit-exports/finwave/2026Q1/ and fetch exports-2026-03-12.jsonl.
3) Use jq or a JSONL parser to sample first 100 events and inspect 'timestamp', 'actor*', 'service*' fields.
4) Compare manifest fingerprints against SFTP server logs in /var/log/sftp/ on delivery host (internal).
Sample problematic JSONL lines (redacted PII):
1) {"event_id":"", "timestamp":"2026-03-12T14:02:33", "actor_id":"u-934", "service":"ingest", ... }
2) {"event_id":"d3f8e8a2-...", "timestamp":"2026-03-12T18:02:33+04:00", "user":{"id":"u-934"}, "source_service":"ingest", ... }
3) Manifest excerpt: {"bundle_id":"finwave-2026q1", "key_id":"rot-2025", "fingerprint":"SHA256:abc..."}
SFTP server log (delivery host): Accepted public key: SHA256:xyz... for user finwave-drop; connection closed unexpectedly by remote side after signature check failed.
Initial triage by Support on 2026-03-10: confirmed exported file contains mixed timestamp formats and inconsistent keys. Cross-checked exporter codepath in audit-exporter v1.12.3; mapping layer introduced as opt-in (flag 'normalize_fields') in PR #2148 but default was off for legacy customers. Linked PRs indicate mapping changes were merged behind a feature flag.

Hypotheses:
- Export job for finwave-prod was created without normalize_fields=true, resulting in raw fields.
- Timestamp normalization step runs in the manifest post-processing lambda but failed for some events due to null timezone metadata pulled from older logs.
- SFTP key rotation mismatch due to manifest referencing prior key id; deployment of rotation update to exporter service on 2026-02-15 may not have updated the manifest generator template.

Checks performed:
- Verified job config: console shows 'legacy_export' = true for this tenant.
- Searched logs: exporter lambda logs show 34 warnings 'tz-unknown' between 2026-01-01 and 2026-03-12.
- Confirmed PR #2199 adjusted manifest generator, but deployment to prod was rolled back on 2026-02-20 for an unrelated regression.

Next steps recommended:
1) Re-run export with 'normalize_fields=true' and 'force_utc=true' for finwave-prod and verify sample.
2) Regenerate delivery manifest after confirming current SFTP key fingerprints with FinWave.
3) Provide FinWave a short mapping file (CSV/JSON) and a one-time script to remap existing JSONL if they prefer in-place transformation.
4) Schedule a brief joint call with FinWave SRE to validate key fingerprints and sftp handshake behavior.
On request, Support built a temporary transformation script (Python) to normalize 2026Q1 JSONL into FinWave's schema and uploaded it to s3://redwood-audit-exports/finwave/2026Q1/normalized-exports-2026-03-12.jsonl. Script includes: convert timestamps to UTC (Z), map actor_id->user.id, service->source.service, and inject deterministic event_id (UUID v5 using event payload hash). Delivered to customer as stopgap while production fix is scheduled.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - FinWave SRE (customer): Confirmed they rotated keys on 2026-02-03 and provided fingerprint SHA256:xyz...; they saw signature mismatch for one of the deliveries (we provided handshake logs). Asked for an immediate normalized bundle for ingest—deadline 2026-03-14 for internal audit team.
2026-03-13 - Infra (internal): Validated SFTP host accepted current fingerprint SHA256:xyz...; identified manifest generator still referencing rot-2025 due to stale config in template-renderer service. Patch to template-renderer drafted in github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2215.
2026-03-13 - Support (Aisha): Notified customer of progress and shared temporary normalized bundle. Requested confirmation that their SIEM ingests the normalized file successfully; awaiting confirmation.
Pending - temporary normalized bundle delivered. Engineering to deploy template-renderer patch (PR #2215) and enable normalize_fields for finwave-prod, then re-run export. Final resolution will include updated manifest and documented rotation policy notes for FinWave.
If PR #2215 is deployed successfully, schedule re-export and confirm with FinWave SRE. Post-deployment tasks: update support runbook with checklist to verify manifest key_id/fingerprint prior to scheduled SFTP pushes and add automatic timezone fallback to exporter lambda.
Configuration and deployment drift: normalization feature behind a feature flag and manifest template out-of-sync with key rotation records after a partial rollback in Feb 2026.
Deploy PR #2215 to prod and run canary export for finwave-prod
Enable normalize_fields=true and force_utc=true for tenant finwave-prod
Add a pre-delivery manifest validation job that cross-checks key fingerprints with customer-supplied values
Document SFTP key rotation checklist in Support runbook and send quarterly reminder to enterprise customers

Issue summary:
BrightMed reports that after enabling an aggressive combined optimizer profile (async batching + kv-prefetch + mixed quant profile) for a subset of tenants on Dedicated capacity, a subset of their production traffic experienced elevated 95/99p latency and intermittent 5xxs. The customer wants guidance and an orchestrated safe rollback for the tenant to avoid global impact while reverting optimization flags.

Impact:
- Production request 95p latency increased from ~120ms to ~480ms for user-facing inference routes for ~10% of tokens.

- Customer traffic routed through regional gateway -> dedicated GPU pool.

Steps to reproduce (observed in prod live traffic):

- Sustained tail latency spike and transient memory pressure observed on several worker pods.
- Autoscaler attempted additional workers but allocation was delayed due to GPU availability constraints in dedicated pool.
- Rolling revert of optimizer flags at tenant scope was attempted manually but some routing rules applied globally, causing partial revert and inconsistent behavior.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant-scoped rollback should atomically demote optimizer flags for only BrightMed traffic, preserving other tenants and not requiring global pool changes.

- Scoped traffic split to route BrightMed traffic to a warm standby variant with conservative optimizer profile. This reduced 95p latency to ~160ms but increased cost.

- A short playbook runbook for the customer success engineer to perform an emergency rollback if automated rollback fails.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports long-running streaming completions disconnecting mid-stream during request flows that trigger KV-cache warmup. Impact: multiple merchant endpoints experience intermittent 5xx/stream resets leading to failed payments and degraded UX. Observed pattern ties failures to requests that include rotating trace headers (X-Trace-Id/X-B3) and large set-cookie/tracing metadata generated by the customer's SDK.

Environment: Dedicated capacity, prod/us-east, routes pinned to gpt-open-13b-v1. Problem began after a rollout of improved tracing middleware in the customer's SDK (they started rotating trace headers per-chunk) and coincided with higher percentage of cold KV-cache misses at the serving layer.

1) Send a streaming generate request against the Redwood hosted endpoint with an initial request producing long KV-cache warmup (cold model + cold KV cache).
2) Have the client rotate/replace tracing headers mid-stream (simulate SDK that sets new X-Trace-Id every 10s).
3) Observe the streamed chunks; after header rotation the connection is terminated with 502/stream-reset and the client sees incomplete completion.
4) Repeat with warmed KV cache and rotating headers disabled — issue does not reproduce reliably.
Streaming TCP connection reset by ALB/APIGW after header rotation; client receives truncated completion. ALB logs show Backend connection closed with error, idle-timeout metric spikes and 'Request length beyond configured max header size' is NOT consistently present. Upstream serving instances log 'client disconnected during send' and partial token emission.

Streaming remains stable for duration of completion regardless of header updates sent by client during the same logical session (we should tolerate header changes or negotiate without terminating connection).
ALB access logs: multiple entries with target_status_code '-' and target_processing_time ~30s prior to disconnect. APIGW proxy logs show sequence: initial HTTP/2 stream open, data frames, then a HEADERS frame with new trace headers, then ALB closes target connection. SRE packet capture indicates HTTP/2 header re-encoding triggered APIGW to re-chunk the upstream request and the ALB idle timer restarted.
Related snippets:
- alb-20260310-verbose.log: target:172.31.11.22 - - [10/Mar/2026:14:22:10 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" - - - - "-"
- serving-runtime-prod-13b-0 stdout: "kv-cache: miss, starting prefix load; chunk 1 emitted; write error: broken pipe"
Initial hypothesis: header re-encoding on the API gateway when receiving mid-stream HEADERS frames causes the gateway to buffer and reset the downstream connection rather than stream-through. Correlated factors: (a) KV-cache warmup increases time-to-first-byte for downstream responses, (b) client-side header rotation introduces extra HEADERS frames mid-stream, and (c) ALB idle timeout is at default 60s which interacts poorly when proxy restarts timers on header re-encoding.

What we checked:
- Replayed traffic with header rotation disabled — reproduces less than 5% of the time.
- Increased ALB idle timeout to 120s on a test target group — reproduces less and connections survive longer.
- Packet captures show client continues to send frames but ALB tears down the target connection after a header frame.
- Verified headers do not exceed max header size limit.

Working hypothesis: APIGW treats mid-stream header frames as a change that triggers buffer flush/rewrite path that restarts idle timers and sometimes causes premature target disconnect while the serving runtime is blocking on KV warmup. This is different from simple proxy buffering issues seen previously and explains why failures cluster when cold cache and header rotation coincide.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:50 - Customer (Acme Payments): Applied SDK change to stop rotating trace headers; error rate dropped to ~0.8% but customer cannot deploy globally without trace rotation. Asking for platform-side solution.
API gateway's handling of mid-stream HTTP/2 HEADERS frames interacts poorly with ALB idle timeout and serving runtime KV-cache warmup, causing target connections to be torn down during long prefix loads when clients rotate tracing headers mid-stream.
Workaround applied: increased ALB idle timeout to 120s for affected customer target groups and asked customer to temporarily stop rotating trace headers. We also added a mitigation flag in APIGW to avoid re-encoding headers mid-stream for long-lived streaming requests.
Permanent fix: runtime+gateway engineering will implement a change to tolerate mid-stream header updates by treating them as metadata-only (no upstream re-encode), and add a heuristic to detect in-progress KV-cache warmups and extend idle timers. Planned rollout: canary next week, full rollout in 2 weeks.
Follow-ups: add console alerting for 'streaming header-change disconnects', update public runbook, and review default ALB idle timeout recommendation in our docs.
payload.summary: Streaming sessions terminate after header rotation during KV-cache warmup in prod

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 18:45 UTC BrightDocs reported persistent ~5-8% 5xx rate on mixed-embedding and chat routes for their tenant. Errors manifest as 502/503 from api-gateway and upstream runtime connection errors. Impact: production traffic for BrightDocs degraded, intermittent user-facing failures for document ingestion and chat features. Environment: prod-us-east, enterprise tenant (BrightDocs), traffic mix: 60% small chat requests, 40% batched embedding uploads (small/medium).

Observed behavior: When BrightDocs client increases concurrent connections and aggressively reconnects after failed requests, api-gateway 5xx floor rises and remains elevated for ~10-30 minutes before gradually recovering. During elevated period: runtime worker logs show repeated small process OOMs, kvcache eviction storms, and frequent shard reloads (cold-shard events). Apigw logs show 'upstream reset' or 'no healthy upstream' followed by 502/503 responses.

Steps to reproduce (partial/operational):
1) Simulate mixed traffic: parallel 250 concurrent chat calls (short prompts) + parallel upload of 10k small embedding batches (size ~128 vectors) across 120s window.
2) Client aggressively retries on 5xx with short backoff (<200ms) and re-opens new connections per retry.
3) Observe accept-queue growth at apigw, followed by connection churn to runtime and small OOM/restart events in runtime logs.

Relevant logs/metrics:
- APIGW traces: link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ingress/apigw-traces?orgId=1&var-tenant=brightdocs (request ids: req-20260313T1848-0a1b, req-20260313T1851-4f2c)
- Runtime logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-east/runtime/2026-03-13/worker-23.log (OOMs and shard reload stack traces)
- KVcache metrics: kvcache.evictions/sec spike coincident with OOMs: 1200 -> 8500
- Host metrics: container RSS climb briefly before OOM, then restart and rapid reconnects

Initial customer note: "We started seeing errors after our nightly batch ramped up retries. UX shows failed uploads and chat messages not returning. Happened twice in the last 24 hours."
2026-03-13 19:05 - Support (Ava Chen): Acknowledged. Collected tenant and trace IDs and escalated to SRE. Asked customer to pause aggressive retries if possible while we investigate.
2026-03-13 19:18 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Observed accept queue growth at APIGW and connection churn to runtime. Several runtime workers reported small OOMs; kvcache evictions very high. Adding backpressure at edge could help immediate mitigation.
2026-03-13 19:31 - Support (Ava Chen): Informed customer to temporarily throttle client retries and increase retry backoff to 1s. Customer applied change and reported partial reduction in errors after 6 minutes.
2026-03-13 19:55 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Deployed temporary ingress rate-limiter rule for tenant brightdocs to cap concurrent connections (cap=120) and enabled soft-priority-shedding on their route. Monitoring for stabilization.
2026-03-13 20:12 - Customer (BrightDocs SRE - Lina Park): Confirmed error rate dropped to ~0.8% after throttling. Concerned about future bursts due to our ingestion pattern — requesting long-term fix.
2026-03-14 09:02 - Engineering (Samir Patel): Noted related PR implementing kvcache eviction smoothing and improved shard reload backoff: PR #4123. Planning canary to reduce hot reloads induced by transient connection storms.
Hypothesis 1: Aggressive client reconnect pattern produced connection oscillation that amplified ingress accept-queue and produced short-lived hot fanout to runtime workers, causing kvcache growth and GC pressure -> small OOMs and restart loop.
Hypothesis 2: KV cache eviction policy interacts poorly with mixed embeddings and chat request shapes: embedding warmups allocate larger kv entries triggering eviction storms under connection churn.
Evidence: High kvcache.evictions/sec correlates with OOM timestamps in runtime logs. Worker restarts align with apigw accept-queue peaks. No clear kernel or driver faults in node-level logs.
Temporary mitigations tried: asked customer to soften retry policy; applied tenant-level ingress soft cap (concurrent conn cap=120); enabled priority-shedding on embed-heavy route. Observed >5x reduction in kvcache eviction spikes and drop in 5xx rate from ~6% to ~0.9%.
Repro steps validated in staging: Simulated client with short retry backoff reproduces accept-queue oscillation and leads to kvcache evictions and worker OOMs in under 3m.
Root cause (working): Interaction between tenant traffic pattern (high short-lived retries + bursty embedding uploads), current kvcache eviction policy and shard-reload backoff leads to GC/eviction thrash and transient worker instability under load.
Mitigation applied (2026-03-13 19:55): Tenant-level throttle and soft-priority-shed decreased error floor. Customer applied client-side retry backoff per guidance.
Engineering fix (in progress): PR github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123 implements kvcache eviction smoothing, increases shard-reload backoff, and makes small-OOM handling graceful to avoid restart loops. Canary scheduled on 2026-03-15 in us-east staging lanes.
Operational follow-ups: 1) Add tenant-specific prewarm suggestions to Console for customers doing mixed embed+chat workloads. 2) Create automated alert for kvcache.evictions/sec > 1000 sustained for 1m. 3) Update runbook with guidance to apply soft ingress caps per-tenant and to ask clients to increase retry backoff to >=500ms for short-lived requests.
Customer communication: Sent status update and mitigation steps to BrightDocs on 2026-03-13 20:30. Will provide postmortem after engineering change is validated. Customer is satisfied with workaround but requests timeline for permanent fix.
Closure criteria: After canary validation and 24h of stable metrics (<0.5% 5xx floor) for BrightDocs tenant in us-east, mark Resolved and schedule postmortem.

Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicated external webhook invocations triggered by function-calls after an HTTP/2 RST_STREAM event. The customer uses TS SDK in their front-end to stream tokens and a Go worker to confirm tool executions. They observed the same function being executed twice (two downstream webhook POSTs) for a single user action.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream actions (webhook POST) causing double billing and incorrect user-facing state (duplicate emails/orders).
- Reproducible for specific sessions when underlying connection experiences a stream reset under proxy.

Environment details provided by customer:
- Frontend: ts-sdk v2.3.1, node 18, using streaming chat + function-calling.
- Worker: go-sdk v0.9.2 performing remote webhook POSTs upon function call confirmation.
- Backend: python ingestion service (python-sdk v1.14.0) that sometimes replays events after reconnect.
- Edge: Customer runs traffic through an HTTP/2 terminating proxy (Fastly-like CDN) that multiplexes requests and enforces header length limits (reportedly 16 bytes on a particular header).

Customer-observed symptoms:
- Two webhook deliveries within 2-5s for a single user prompt.
- SDK logs show: first stream reset (RST_STREAM) then immediate retry, second stream contains a different trace id but same session id.
- The idempotency header the customer adds (X-Idempotency-Key) appears truncated in upstream request logs.

Request from customer: explanation of root cause, recommended mitigations, and SDK config changes to avoid duplicates.
1) Use TS SDK streaming chat with a function described in the model manifest.
2) Ensure requests pass through an HTTP/2 multiplexing proxy that truncates headers >16 bytes.
3) Send a prompt that triggers the function-calling path and force a stream reset (simulate RST_STREAM).
4) Observe worker logs: two POSTs to the external webhook for the same logical function invocation.

Notes: The customer supplied a minimal reproduction where toggling the proxy header length limit to >64 bytes stops the duplication.
[frontend] ts-sdk v2.3.1 streaming: send chunk (id=abc123, idempotency=X-Id-9a2f3c4d5e6f7g8)
[edge-proxy] received headers: x-idempotency-key=9a2f3c4d
[frontend] connection RST_STREAM (code=2)
[frontend] retry: re-open stream, send chunk (id=abc123, idempotency=X-Id-9a2f3c4d5e6f7g8)
[go-worker] function-confirmation received: invocation_id=abc123, idempotency_hdr=9a2f3c4d -> POST /webhook -> 200
[go-worker] duplicate confirmation: invocation_id=abc123-2, idempotency_hdr=9a2f3c4d -> POST /webhook -> 200

Customer supplied raw proxy capture showing header trimmed to first 8 chars. The SDK-level idempotency key appears consistent on the client side but changes after proxying.
Initial triage (Support):
- Reproduced with internal proxy that enforces 16-byte header max; when header truncated, server-side dedup logic cannot correlate the two attempts.
- Observed that front-end TS SDK stores an 'session' idempotency token when streaming, which is reused across stream reconnections for convenience. This pattern works when the idempotency key is preserved end-to-end, but fails when intermediary proxies mutate/truncate headers.

Hypothesis: A combination of factors causes duplicates:
- SDK session-scoped idempotency (reusing the same key across retries and multiplexed streams).
- HTTP/2 proxy header truncation/normalization causing dedup mismatch between initial and retried requests.
- RST_STREAM triggers immediate client retry with same session key, but downstream received header differs (truncated) so server treats retry as new invocation.

SDK audit:
- python-sdk v1.14.0: uses per-request idempotency if user sets explicit header; session-scoped behavior exists behind streaming convenience APIs.
- ts-sdk v2.3.1: streaming convenience path reuses session token and does not regenerate per-request UUID on reconnect.
- go-sdk v0.9.2: confirm worker uses whatever idempotency header it sees from the request to dedupe outbound webhooks (no additional server-side sequencer).

Edge findings:
- Proxy reported header length limit and lower-case normalization. Proxy also reuses underlying connection and may coalesce headers in edge cases.

Action taken so far:
- Asked customer for packet capture and request traces (provided).
- Reproduced locally with simple Fastly-like proxy and confirmed duplication scenario.
- Opened internal engineering task to adjust SDK behavior for streaming reconnects (see linked INT-34567).
[2026-03-12 10:14 - Support (Aisha Khan)]: Thanks for the reproduction and captures — we're investigating. Could you confirm which header name you set? (X-Idempotency-Key or Idempotency-Key?)

[2026-03-12 10:26 - Customer (Merriweather SRE)]: We set X-Idempotency-Key initially. Proxy logs show header trimmed to 8 bytes. We can reproduce consistently when traffic goes through our staging CDN.

[2026-03-12 12:03 - Support (Ben Park)]: We reproduced this with a local proxy that truncates headers. Short-term workaround: set a short idempotency token (<=8 bytes) to match proxy behavior or configure proxy to preserve full header. Long-term: we'll propose SDK change to prefer per-request UUIDs on reconnects for streaming.

[2026-03-13 09:05 - Engineering (Maya Lopez)]: Confirmed: ts-sdk streaming path will be updated to rotate the per-request idempotency token on reconnects. Also adding a normalized header name mapping (accept X-Idempotency-Key and Idempotency-Key) and code to warn when header appears truncated. Patch PRs opened: sdk-ts#201, sdk-python#482, sdk-go#153.
Workaround and mitigation:
1) Customer temporary workarounds tried:
   - Configure proxy to pass through the full idempotency header (preferred).
   - Set a custom short idempotency token that fits the proxy limit (not ideal; potential increased collision risk across global traffic).
   - Disable streaming convenience session-scoped idempotency and instead generate a fresh UUID per request on the client side.

2) Platform/SDK fixes planned:
   - TS SDK: rotate per-request idempotency token on stream reconnects and emit a warning when a configured idempotency header exceeds 32 bytes. (PR sdk-ts#201)
   - Python/Go SDKs: add header normalization and server-side dedupe helpers in guidance docs. (PRs linked above)
   - Support runbook will include proxy guidance to avoid truncation/normalization issues for idempotency headers.

Follow-ups:
- INT-34567 created: apply SDK changes, add e2e test that simulates header truncation + RST_STREAM.
- Support to coordinate with customer for staged rollout and confirm resolution in their staging CDN.

Status: Engineering patching in progress, customer applied proxy config change in staging and reports no duplicates after the change. Will close when SDK patch is released and customer confirms in prod.
- Engineering to complete SDK PRs and add e2e tests (INT-34567).
- Support to validate fix with customer once SDK patch available; request customer to test in staging by re-enabling CDN policy.
- Update public docs with idempotency header best-practices for HTTP/2 proxies.
- Consider server-side defensive behavior: treat truncated matches as probable retries and prefer safe at-most-once semantics for function confirmations if configured.
This ticket highlights an operational class of issues where network intermediaries mutate headers expected by dedup logic. Recommend adding a short section to our docs about header preservation and header-length considerations for customers using HTTP/2 multiplexing proxies.
payload.summary: Duplicates observed for function-calls after HTTP/2 stream reset due to proxy header truncation and session-scoped idempotency

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated client-side timeouts and stalled streaming when sending prompts with an ultra-long prefix (~120k tokens) together with a large max_tokens (>=60k). The generation appears to start (initial tokens returned) then stalls for an extended period (~60–120s) before the client receives either a socket close or an HTTP 504. This is reproducible in prod for the customer on dedicated capacity.

Impact:
- Customer's batch jobs for document summarization fail ~40% of runs when using extended prefix + high max_tokens.
- End-users see partial outputs or timeouts; jobs must be retried, increasing cost.

Environment:
- Customer: PolarisAI (dedicated account)
- Region: us-west primary, some runs in us-east also affected
- Models: rwd-adapter-gpt-extended-7B (primary), rwd-adapter-gptx-13B (fallback)
- Platform: Dedicated pool (c5-gpu-4), API via production gateway, streaming enabled

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Construct a prompt with a ~120k-token prefix (multiple concatenated documents).
2) Call /v1/generate with streaming=true and max_tokens=60000.
3) Observe initial portion of tokens stream, then stall; client times out after 90s or receives 504.

Observed behavior:
- Initial generation and stream begin normally for first ~2000 tokens.
- Throughput drops sharply; the worker process shows high CPU on host but low GPU util in some samples.
- KV-cache growth is large (observed footprint ~2.4x compared to expected).
- Request either ends with an HTTP 504 from our edge or a client-side socket timeout depending on retry window.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming should continue at approximately steady token/s rate (subject to model size) until max_tokens reached or generation completes.
- System should fail fast with a descriptive 5xx if a serving constraint is hit rather than silent stalls.

Logs / Traces collected:
- Edge logs: connection held open; upstream returned 504 after 95s for request id rwd-usw-8f3a
- Serving runtime traces: request assigned to worker host gpu-12; kernel execution latency spikes after ~2k tokens, with repeated GC events in process logs.
- KV-cache metrics: memory spike correlating with stall time; cache eviction not keeping up.
- SRE sampling: strace on worker showed repeated futex/wait events consistent with queue backpressure.

Investigation notes / hypotheses so far:
- Hypothesis A: Continuous-batching + very large KV cache leads to runaway per-request memory/serialization overhead; runtime stalls while moving/compacting KV cache.
- Hypothesis B: A path in the streaming controller triggers repeated small wakeups under heavy prefix size (inefficient signaling), delaying downstream flushes to the client.
- Hypothesis C: For some model variants, quantization/attention kernel selection yields pathological perf when sequence length + new generation length exceed internal thresholds, causing CPU fallback paths.
- We observed that when the same request is routed to a lower-batched, dedicated single-worker instance (not autoscaled), the stall is less frequent but still present, suggesting both runtime and routing factors.

Workarounds attempted / recommended to customer:
- Reduce max_tokens to <= 20k or split generation into chunked suffix generations. Customer reports this reduces failures but increases orchestration complexity.
- Temporarily pin routing to a low-batch policy (support-set to route through dedicated single-worker gateway). This reduced incidence in ~70% of test runs.
- Increase client-side socket timeout to 180s as a stopgap (not ideal for UX).

Next steps / action items:
- SRE: capture a full CPU/GPU trace on next reproduced run and enable detailed heap profiling for the worker process (assigned: Maya Chen).
- Runtime team: add instrumentation around KV cache copy/compact/eviction path to measure time spent per request; create a microbenchmark for very long prefix + generation (assigned: Julian Park).
- Routing team: evaluate whether batching window heuristics can be bypassed for requests with explicit large max_tokens flag to avoid batching-induced stalls (assigned: Anika Rao).
- Product: update guidance for customers on recommended max_tokens + prefix sizing and add explicit error if request exceeds safe combined token heuristic (assigned: Priya Narayanan).

Customer communication:
- Customer notified 2026-03-12 (initial report) and informed of workaround options same day.
- We told the customer we expect a preliminary root-cause hypothesis by 2026-03-16 and will follow up with timeline for fixes.

Resolution criteria:
- Repro rate with baseline workload falls below 1% for similar prefix+max_tokens after fixes and/or a clear client-visible error is returned when request exceeds safe limits.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 12:05 - Customer (PolarisAI): Acknowledged and will run reproducibility tests during the scheduled window.
payload.summary: Generation stall leading to client-side timeout for ultra-long prefix + large max_tokens

payload.description:
Issue summary:
- Customer (QuillSync) reports periodic dedicated-pool throughput drop during their midday quiet windows (low traffic), recurring over 3 days. Affected routes are pinned to dedicated pool in us-west-2.
Impact:
- P50/P95 throughput decreased by ~30% for 2-6 minute windows; increased request queueing and observed fallback to shared tier for a subset of requests. Customer-facing latency spikes and elevated 429/504 retries.
Environment:
- prod:us-west-2, dedicated pool: quillsync-prod-pool-1, models: redwood/open-13b and redwood/opt-6.7b, customer_tier: dedicated.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Traffic profile: send steady low-rate traffic mimicking QuillSync background sync (10-15 concurrent short streams).
2) Wait for scheduled telemetry window (~midday, customer local timezone).
3) Observe allocator/gpu attach logs and autoscaler events for pool quillsync-prod-pool-1.
Observed behavior:
- Short windows of GPU availability thinness (slots reduce), autoscaler does not immediately scale up, queueing increases, routing starts falling back or throttling routes.
- Sidecar metrics show large short-lived burst of connections/metrics flushes coincident with drop windows.
Expected behavior:
- Dedicated pool should maintain steady attach capacity for pinned routes through quiet windows; autoscaler should respond within configured cooldowns to legitimate load shifts.
Initial pointers and logs:
- Customer-provided request traces: trace IDs attached in comments.
- SRE dashboard snapshot: p50 throughput chart and allocator-attach-count for quillsync-prod-pool-1 during 2026-03-11 to 2026-03-13.
- Sidecar metrics: telemetry-flush-rate spiked for multiple tenants at the same timestamps.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 11:05 - Support (Ethan Park): Acknowledged. Asked for pool name, model pins, and asked SRE to pull allocator logs and sidecar flush metrics for us-west-2. First-response SLA noted.
2026-03-13 13:40 - SRE (Lina Gomez): Pulled allocator and attach logs. Noted rapid ephemeral increase in sidecar emit events (metrics flush) at the same timestamps. Allocator reported short attach failures and temporary slot release. Sharing logs: /logs/quill/attach-2026-03-11-13.tar.gz (internal).
2026-03-13 15:20 - Support (Ethan Park): Asked customer to temporarily stagger their background syncs as a mitigation while we continue investigation. Customer tried and reported partial mitigation but not full elimination.
2026-03-14 09:02 - SRE (Lina Gomez): Observed that the autoscaler backoff combined with ephemeral sidecar CPU spikes caused attach latency to exceed autoscale thresholds, preventing timely scale-up. Hypothesis added to investigation notes.
2026-03-14 12:45 - Engineering (Raj Patel): Looking at sidecar commit history; flagged recent telemetry-batching change two weeks ago that increased synchronous flushes on low-traffic tenants. Opening PR to decouple flush scheduling from request thread. Refer PR in related_github_prs.
Hypothesis 1: Sidecar synchronous metric/connection flush spikes briefly consume CPU on node sidecars, delaying allocator attach handshakes and causing temporary slot releases in dedicated pool.
Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler cooldown/backoff logic treats attach latency as noise and delays scaling decisions; combined with brief attach failures this allows a cascade to queueing and fallbacks.
Telemetry checked: allocator-attach-latency, slot-count, sidecar-cpu, sidecar-metrics-flush-rate, autoscaler-evaluation-latency. Correlated sidecar-flush spikes with attach-latency spikes at 13:02-13:06 UTC across 3 days.
Trace sampling: captured three request traces where attach returned transient 504 while GPU slot showed released then reattached within 20s. Traces: trace-20260311-13a, trace-20260312-13b, trace-20260313-13c (internal IDs).
Reproduce attempts: Internal load test injecting synthetic metrics flush bursts on a small dedicated pool reproduced attach lag and p50 throughput drop within 90s.
Short-term mitigation applied (2026-03-14 14:35): temporarily adjusted autoscaler.cooldown_ms to 30000 for quillsync-prod-pool-1 and reduced sidecar.metrics_batch_max to 100 for the tenant’s sidecars. Customer reported immediate improvement in throughput valley duration reduced from 3-6m to <60s.
Root cause (provisional): recent telemetry batching change caused synchronous flush spikes on low-throughput tenants; these spikes increase sidecar CPU and block attach handshakes, which combined with conservative autoscaler thresholds produced temporary GPU thinness.
Permanent fix plan: engineering PR to decouple metric flushing from request-processing threads and add jittered flush windows for low-traffic tenants. Also update autoscaler to detect transient attach failures versus sustained load and avoid entering backoff for short-lived attach latency. PRs and rollout plan tracked in related_github_prs. Targeted rollout to staging then canary in us-west-2 over 2 weeks.
Follow-ups: 1) Post-deploy follow-up ticket to validate canary behavior and p99/p50 throughput during previous quiet windows. 2) Update Sidecar Runbook with recommended defaults for metrics batching for dedicated pools. 3) Offer customer a dedicated monitor dashboard and weekly check-in during rollout.
Status: Engineering work in progress; customer notified and mitigation remains in place.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer FinStrata reports intermittent increases in p95 latency for requests originating in eu-west after they flipped a regional-locality toggle on their tenant (dedicated). Symptoms began ~2026-03-04 09:00 UTC and are reproducible across multiple sessions.

Impact: Customer observes sustained p95 increase from ~120ms to ~440ms for text-generation calls. End-users in EU see degraded interactivity for document summarization workflows. No 5xx errors reported.

Environment: prod (eu-west tenant, dedicated pool). Model traffic primarily gpt-redwood-1-xl and gpt-redwood-1-large.

Observed behavior: Traces show a subset (~12%) of requests that should stay in eu-west are routed via an APAC edge for the initial TLS/TCP handshake, then proxied back to eu-west serving runtime. This adds ~250–350ms extra latency (DNS+TLS+cross-region RTT). Connection-level logs show repeated TLS renegotiation timestamps aligning with residency-lock refresh window.

Expected behavior: Regional-locality flip should keep traffic within eu-west; if routing fallback occurs it should prefer eu-west fallback pool. No cross-region hairpinning expected for steady-state traffic.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer enabled regional-locality=true for tenant FIN-ACCT-09 at 2026-03-04T08:55 UTC.
2) Run 200 concurrent short-generation requests (seq len 64) from eu-west test clients.
3) Observe p50/p95 on Console and trace sampling.

Logs / snippets (sanitized):
- EDGE-2026-03-04T09:03:14Z connection accepted from 3.76.12.55 (eu-west) -> proxy-ep-01 (apac)
- PROXY-2026-03-04T09:03:15Z upstream connect to eu-west-serving-03 TLS handshake start
- TRACE-ID ab12cd: initial edge hop apac->eu-west added 312ms RTT

Initial hypothesis: Control-plane residency propagation race + DNS rebind caused a small window where token-affinity map pointed to APAC edge despite tenant locality being EU. Another contributor may be TLS session reuse disabled at edge during the lock flip, triggering full handshake via wrong egress.

Immediate mitigation attempted: Support requested customer to toggle regional-locality back off; traffic returned to normal within ~7 minutes. We also rolled a targeted edge route cache flush for tenant token on eu-west edges.

Investigation plan:
- Validate control-plane event timeline and token-affinity entries at the time of the flip.
- Correlate edge DNS cache TTLs and healthcheck timestamps for eu-west vs apac edges.
- Check scheduler/placement logs for any recent GPU rebalances that might have flipped preferred fallback priority.
- Reproduce in staging with a staged residency flip while capturing full tcpdump on edge and serving nodes.

Customer request: A formal explanation of why a portion of traffic briefly egressed to APAC and confirmation that enabling regional-locality will not cause repeat cross-region hairpins. They also asked for longer-term guardrail (control-plane sequencing / token lockatomicity) and request a postmortem if production regression.

Additional notes:

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 03:15 UTC BrightCart (enterprise customer) reported elevated p95/p99 inference latencies and a rise in 504s originating from APAC clients. Symptoms show TLS handshakes complete successfully but application-level responses stall; many requests become queued and either time out or incur 20–60s tails. This ticket captures triage, investigation notes, and mitigation actions.
Customer-facing inference features for BrightCart in APAC experienced p99 latency increases from ~800ms to 18–45s and ~12% request timeouts for streaming/generation endpoints. Multiple SLAs are at risk; several customers reported user-visible errors during a marketing campaign peak window.
1) Use BrightCart account token scoped to apac-southeast-1. 2) Send concurrent streaming generate requests (batch of 50 clients, ~5 RPS each) with sequence length ~1024. 3) Observe initial TLS handshake and then long queue times in downstream proxy for many requests; p99 latency spikes and some streams report 'stream cancelled' client-side. 4) Reproduce is intermittent and more likely under sustained concurrent load.
Collected artifacts: envoy downstream_cluster metrics (queue_time_histogram spikes 20000–45000ms), egress-proxy logs with repeated upstream connect attempts, per-request trace IDs (list attached in Confluence). TLS logs show handshake completes at t0, first application bytes not seen until t0+seconds. No obvious 5xx during handshake stage. Kernel-level tcp retransmits low; path appears healthy until post-handshake proxying.
- Timeline: Spike first visible 2026-03-10 02:58 UTC; BrightCart reported at 03:15 UTC. - SRE checked POP health: local APAC POPs healthy; packet-level metrics show ARP/BGP stable. - Traces show requests complete TLS but then hand off to upstream cluster 'egress-global-us-east' instead of local 'egress-apac-southeast'. - Routing-service recently rolled out weight-based egress rewrite (2026-03-09 23:40 UTC) to support account-level egress preferences; rollout included a config that rewrites SNI/account tag for accounts flagged with 'global-egress' during a migration. - Egress-proxy v2.4.1 introduced a change in upstream selection: if local cluster reports >x active streams it rewrites to fallback cluster and queues requests waiting for connection; combined with prefix rewrite this triggered cross-region handoff. - Hypothesis: the new routing rewrite + egress-proxy fallback logic caused a subset of BrightCart traffic to be proxied cross-region (APAC -> us-east) after TLS handshake, introducing network RTT + downstream queueing and KV-cache cold misses in serving runtime, leading to long tails and timeouts.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 03:35 - SRE (A. Patel): 'Confirmed traces show post-handshake hop to us-east egress cluster for ~17% of BrightCart requests. Local egress capacity looks nominal; investigating routing rewrite config.'
2026-03-10 04:05 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): 'Found recent routing-service config change that tags BrightCart for global-egress during migration. Rolling back tag for BrightCart as an immediate mitigation. Will work with egress-proxy team on retry/fallback semantics.'
2026-03-10 04:40 - Support (Maya Chen): 'Customer observed latency drop after rollback; p99 returned to ~900ms for monitored endpoints. Customer still seeing occasional 5s tails; continuing to monitor.'
2026-03-10 10:12 - Eng (S. Gupta): 'PR created to patch egress-proxy fallback behavior to avoid cross-region handoff post-handshake: https://github.com/redwood-inference/egress-proxy/pull/345. Also adding a routing-service guard to prefer local POP when RTT delta < 30ms.'

Patch PR#345 applied to egress-proxy to change fallback behavior and avoid post-handshake cluster rewrite; hotfix deployment scheduled to 2026-03-11 05:00 UTC canary, 06:00 UTC full roll. Follow-ups: add a canary gate to routing-service rollouts, add alerting on post-handshake cluster switch rate, document playbook in Confluence and notify impacted customers. 1) Deploy egress-proxy hotfix and monitor. 2) Add routing-service guard and unit tests to prevent account tag misassignment during rollouts. 3) Add metric and alert: 'post_handshake_cluster_switch_rate' > 0.5% triggers auto-triage. 4) Coordinate with BrightCart CS for follow-up review and SLA credit if SLA breached. 5) Draft final incident report and distribute to GTM and Eng leadership.
