payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated occurrences where server-sent event (SSE) streams terminate with the final JSON payload missing and preceding fragments concatenated on a single event. The client receives a final TCP RST from an upstream proxy, which in some cases appears to cause two last fragments to be merged and the expected end-marker ('data: [DONE]' or 'event: end') not delivered to the client.

Impact: User-facing partial outputs (last sentence/JSON object dropped or merged), downstream parsing failures in Acme Health's ingestion pipeline, several production jobs failing to mark documents complete. Affects ~3% of long-running streaming requests from the customer in us-east during high load windows.

Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool for Acme Health, using gpt-redwood-1-large, requests are SSE over HTTP/1.1 routed through our edge fleet behind a third-party transparent proxy (customer's infra fronting Redwood in their VPC).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided + internal repro):
1) Customer sends streaming SSE request with prompt that produces a long multi-paragraph response.
2) Reproduction easiest when the stream remains idle for >20s between tokens (simulating slow token emission).
3) If an upstream probe or NAT refresh causes abrupt TCP RST on the connection, the client sometimes receives the two trailing fragments concatenated into a single SSE 'data:' event and no explicit end event.
4) Local repro: curl --no-buffer to our SSE endpoint via an HAProxy instance configured with aggressive idle-timeout and probe.

Observed behavior: Partial/garbled JSON at stream end (two JSON fragments joined at boundary), parser errors in customer app, and no separate end-marker event. In some cases the client reconnects and requests resume but resume token cannot be applied correctly because the tail fragment lacks clear boundary markers.

Attachments: customer request IDs, sample SSE capture (redacted), edge access logs, haproxy config snippet provided by customer.
Timeline: Support triaged on 2026-03-10 after customer report. SRE collected edge and service logs for the window. Key findings:
- Edge TCP logs show the connection terminated with RST originating from the customer's upstream proxy within 50-200ms of last token emission in the failing sessions.
- Serving-runtime emitted two small chunks (chunk A and chunk B) within 30ms; the edge HTTP layer attempted to flush them as two SSE events.
- Packet capture at the edge shows the final two packets were delivered to the edge but the upstream RST caused the edge's downstream buffering layer to coalesce the two writes into a single downstream write that lacked an intermediate SSE delimiter (we observed missing additional '\n' between data frames).
- The SSE framing parser on the client side expects either a closing 'event: end'/'data: [DONE]' or a newline-separated set of 'data:' frames. When frames were concatenated without the separator, the client parsed as a single malformed JSON.

Hypothesis: Rapid upstream TCP resets combined with the edge's write-coalescing optimization and the edge-proxy's transparent TCP handling can drop delimiting newlines between buffered write segments, resulting in concatenated payloads and absent explicit end-marker delivery. The serving runtime itself completed generation and emitted the end marker; it did not see an error. The truncation/concatenation happens between the edge flush and network egress.

Tests performed:
- Reproduced locally using HAProxy idle-timeout 20s and curl; observed identical concatenation.
- Disabled write-coalescing on a staging edge node; concatenation rate dropped to 0/200 attempts.
- Instrumented edge to log write boundaries; logs correlate coalesced writes with upstream RST events and overloaded epoll wakeups.
Support (Ana Martinez) - 2026-03-10: Opened after customer provided sample traces and example SSE fraction. Asked for exact request IDs and whether the customer saw any intermediary proxy or LB in their path.
Customer (Acme Health - DevOps) - 2026-03-10: Confirmed they run an HAProxy 2.4 instance with aggressive keepalive/health probe. Happy to reproduce with a test route. Reported failure rate ~3% for long streams during peak hours.
SRE (Marcus Lee) - 2026-03-11: Collected edge pcaps and confirmed RST timestamps. Added temporary log hooks to record write boundary metadata on edge nodes serving Acme. Hypothesis: edge coalescing + RST = lost delimiter.
Action: Disable Nagle/write-coalescing on selected edge nodes for Acme traffic as a mitigation; monitoring started.
Engineer (Priya Singh) - 2026-03-12: Verified serving-runtime always writes an end marker in the application layer. Created PR to ensure end marker is emitted as a separate flushable segment (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/6792). Also proposed an edge-layer sanitizer to insert a final '\n
' if missing on connection close.
Support (Ana Martinez) - 2026-03-12: Informed customer of temporary mitigation and asked them to relax HAProxy idle timeout to 90s as a quick fix. Customer agreed to test in their staging environment and will report results tomorrow.
Temporary mitigation: Disabled write-coalescing (SO_SNDBUF/Nagle adjustments) on three edge nodes routing Acme traffic and asked customer to increase HAProxy idle timeout to >=90s. After mitigation we observed reduction of incidents to 0.2% in the following 24h window.
Permanent fix plan:

Additional notes:
- Mid-term: Add an edge-layer sanitizer that ensures delimiter sanity on connection close (insert missing '\n
' between write segments when RST/FIN observed) and instrument coalescing thresholds.
- Long-term: Update runbooks and add an internal test harness that simulates upstream RSTs to validate SSE behavior end-to-end.
Follow-ups: Create INT ticket for edge fleet config rollout (INT-20444) and add a Confluence runbook entry for customers with aggressive upstream proxies explaining recommended proxy settings for streaming workloads.
Status: mitigation applied and customer monitoring. Engineering change in progress.
payload.summary: SSE mid-stream concatenated fragments and missing end-marker after upstream proxy abrupt RST

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Delta Bank, enterprise) requests a high-fidelity, near-real-time Kafka export of per-tenant inference request/response pairs (RPC-like call pairs) to integrate with their QRadar SIEM and internal billing reconciliation. Export must include per-call token counts and cost attribution, reversible pseudonymization for PII, a signed batch manifest (HMAC/ED25519) per exported partition with resume tokens, and a legal-hold carve-out mechanism to prevent deletion of specific customer user IDs on demand from their compliance team.

Impact:
- Delta Bank needs this for regulator evidence and billing reconciliation across multiple regions. Without this export they cannot accept Redwood as a vendor for regulated production workloads.

Request details / acceptance criteria:
1) Incremental Kafka topic per-customer (or partitioned with tenant ID header) with ordered events and resume token checkpointing.
2) Event payload must contain: timestamp (UTC), request_id, tenant_id (pseudonymized reversible ID), model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_cost_cents, latency_ms, trace_id, parent_trace_id (if present).
3) Reversible pseudonymization: vendor-managed KMS-encrypted mapping files (per-tenant key-encryption), or HSM-attested envelope so Delta can request decryption under legal process.
4) Signed per-batch manifest including range of offsets, time window, HMAC (customer-specific key) and server-side ED25519 signature.
5) Legal-hold carve-outs: API for Delta compliance to flag user identifiers for preservation; flagged records retained immutably and excluded from retention-based deletion workflows.
6) Delivery guarantees: at-least-once ordered per-partition, retention of manifests for 7 years (regulator request), and daily reconciliation report with checksums.
7) Sample SIEM mapping for QRadar (CEF or JSON mapping) and example consumer code.
8) SLA: initial PoC within 5 business days, full rollout scheduling after PoC signoff.

Issue summary: After HealthNow applied the mixed-quant profile (mix-v2) with an aggressive KV prefetch policy and higher batching window, production request P50/P95 latency increased by ~3-6x. Impact: user-facing slowdowns for real-time document summarization flows; elevated error budgets for dedicated capacity pool. Environment: dedicated cluster in us-east, serving model gpt-like-13b-quant-mix-v2. Steps to reproduce: 1) Deploy optimizer profile 'mix-v2' + kv_prefetch: aggressive on tenant HealthNow; 2) Send typical 0.9s median prompt workload with streaming enabled; 3) Observe endpoint latency metrics and per-token time. Observed behavior: sudden increase in tail latency and increased variance on streaming chunk emission. CPU on CPU-side orchestrator spiked briefly; GPU utilization appears lower than baseline. Expected behavior: batching and prefetch should reduce per-token latency/cost without increasing tails. Investigation summary: Initial hypothesis is that KV prefetch combined with mixed quant causes memory thrashing on GPU and increased host-side scheduling delays due to longer prep time for larger batches. We see elevated host-side serialize/deser times in traces and repeated small fallback to full-precision kernel for certain attention sizes. HealthNow reports no model code change other than optimizer profile toggle. Temporary workaround applied: Disabled kv_prefetch for tenant; reverted batching window to baseline (25ms) which reduced P95 back to near baseline. Work needed: define safe, staged rollback that preserves throughput while minimizing cost and quality regressions; identify precise kernel/attention sizes triggering fallback. Attachments: dashboard links and sample trace IDs are in comments.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 12:30 - SRE (Priya Menon): Looked at node metrics in us-east cluster. GPU memory fragmentation visible on a subset of pods running mixed-quant kernels. Observed OOM-kernel fallbacks logged in runtime: 'kernel_fallback=attention_full_precision' in /var/log/serving/runtime.log. Suspect mismatch between quant kernel selector and current attention length distribution.
2026-03-13 14:02 - Eng (Luca Bianchi): Reproduced locally with a traffic replay. When kv_prefetch is enabled aggressively plus batch_window >= 80ms, the runtime groups longer-context requests into mixed batches causing kernel selector to choose a safer (but slower) path. Proposed staged rollback: 1) disable kv_prefetch globally for tenant, 2) force batch_window to baseline, 3) pin model to pre-change variant for 48h while gathering perf traces.
2026-03-13 15:10 - Customer (HealthNow - infra@healthnow.com): Confirmed that disabling kv_prefetch and reducing batch window restored acceptable P95 within 10 minutes. Asked for a documented rollback checklist because they run hourly config syncs and want an automated safe-off ramp.
2026-03-14 08:21 - Support (Miguel Torres): Drafted rollback checklist below and requested SRE safety review. Also flagged potential follow-up: kernel selector telemetry missing for a small number of hosts; we need a bug ticket to add more granular kernel decision logs (INT-XXXX).
Workaround: kv_prefetch disabled and batch_window restored to 25ms for HealthNow tenant. Next steps: 1) Execute staged rollback playbook: A) snapshot current optimizer settings, B) disable kv_prefetch, C) set batch_window to baseline, D) pin model to gpt-like-13b:v2026-03-10, E) monitor on P95, P99 and error rate for 2 hours; 2) SRE to collect per-host kernel selector traces for the affected pods and upload to artifact storage; 3) Engineering to reproduce failure case in CI with mixed-quant + prefetch + larger batch windows and open a bug for kernel selector fallback (linked INT ticket will be created). Customer notified and accepted temporary mitigation. Follow-up: schedule a guided tuning session with HealthNow next week to test incremental optimizer flags with slower ramp and observability hooks.
Runbook reference: confluence runbook 'optimizer-rollback-guidance' section 'staged-offramps'
Priority is to reduce customer impact; cost regressions are secondary for initial rollback
Recommend adding automated guardrail that prevents enabling aggressive kv_prefetch when batch_window > 50ms for mixed-quant profiles

Issue summary: Customer reports that during a zero-downtime promote for model gptx-2.1-32k, a subset of requests were routed twice (edge -> primary shard AND edge -> fallback shard) resulting in duplicate responses and elevated tail latency. The incident appears tied to a pin reconciliation race where the in-memory tenant pin state was being updated concurrently with canary health probes flipping a host from unhealthy->healthy rapidly due to flapping.

Impact: Affects a single dedicated tenant (ClearFrame Media) during peak traffic windows. Symptoms: duplicated responses for some requests, spikes of 5xx and increased 95/99 latency, and a handful of customer-side application errors due to idempotency violations. Estimated impacted requests: ~0.6% of inbound for the tenant during a 12:00-12:12 UTC window.

Why we care: duplicates and unexpected fallbacks break guaranteed semantics for customers who rely on version pinning for A/B and rollout consistency. This is customer-facing P1 incident for a dedicated customer on a revenue contract.
1) Configure tenant-level version pin to model v2 (gptx-2.1-32k) and enable weighted canary set with health checks enabled.
2) Initiate a promote operation that adjusts weights from 100% v1 -> 100% v2 using gradual weight shifts (canary increments).
3) Simultaneously introduce synthetic probe flapping on a canary host (toggle health probe pass/fail every 2s).
4) Send high-concurrency requests that expect a pinned model response and observe routing paths and response duplication.
2024-10-22T12:01:03Z EDGE router: received request tenant=clearframe session=abc123 route=pin(v2) -> routing-reconciler lookup
2024-10-22T12:01:03Z RECONCILER: pin_lookup returned v2 primary=shard-42 fallback=shard-9 (cache hit ttl=1s)
2024-10-22T12:01:03Z EDGE: forwarded to shard-42 (conn id 785)
2024-10-22T12:01:04Z HEALTH: probe shard-42 failed (latency spike) mark=unhealthy
2024-10-22T12:01:05Z RECONCILER: cache eviction for tenant clearframe triggered; reconciling pins
2024-10-22T12:01:05Z EDGE: fallback routing engaged -> forwarded to shard-9 (conn id 792)
2024-10-22T12:01:05Z RESPONSE: two responses produced for session=abc123 (200 from shard-42, 200 from shard-9) -> duplicate observed by customer
Relevant traces: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/trace-8f72e
Error samples: 5xx rate increased from 0.2% -> 3.4% during window
Initial hypothesis: race between cache eviction + reconcilier refresh and health probe state change allowed router to concurrently forward the same request to both primary and fallback paths.
Confirmed via trace: two distinct forwards for same request id, forwarded within 200ms of each other. Edge router did not detect dedupe because session affinity token mutated during reconciliation.
Reconciler logs show an aggressive TTL (1s) on pin state update for this tenant due to a prior emergency tweak; this reduced the window for atomic swaps and exposed race.
Health probe flapping amplified the effect: host transiently toggled unhealthy then healthy, causing route recalculation mid-request.
No evidence of model-serving backend duplication; both shards returned legitimate 200s. The problem is at routing/edge-level concurrency semantics.
Diego Alvarez (Support) 2024-10-22: Customer opened ticket; attached request IDs and sample payloads. Customer notes: 'We saw duplicate messages and our idempotency keys failed.'
Maya Chen (SRE) 2024-10-22: Captured traces and linked to observability. Initial mitigation: bumped pin cache TTL to 30s for tenant clearframe to reduce reconciliation churn.
Jorge Martinez (Edge) 2024-10-23: Edge change deployed (hotfix) to serialize per-session routing decisions when a pin update is in-flight. Rolling to us-east. Monitoring shows dup rate falling to baseline.
Customer (ClearFrame) 2024-10-23: Confirmed duplicates stopped after mitigation, asks for root cause and timeline for full fix.
Maya Chen (SRE) 2024-10-24: Flagging follow-ups for product: adjust default pin cache TTLs and improve reconciler atomicity. Will schedule postmortem.
Partial mitigation applied: temporarily increased tenant pin cache TTL to 30s and rolled out edge hotfix to serialize routing decisions during pin-reconcile events. This reduced duplicate responses to near-zero for the tenant. Full fix planned: change reconciler to apply pin state updates using compare-and-swap with a short grace window to drain in-flight requests, and make health-probe flapping detection more conservative (remove <2s toggles as valid state changes).
Actions completed:
- Hotfix deployed to edge-router (PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-router/pull/2045)
- Pin cache TTL increased for affected tenant
- Customer confirmed fix
Follow-ups:
- Engineering: implement reconciler CAS and grace-window (owner: @maya) due 2024-11-05
- Product: review default pin TTL settings and add safe-guard for dedicated-tier (owner: @liam)
- SRE: add alert for >0.5% duplicate-response rate per-tenant (owner: @jorge)
Postmortem: scheduled 2024-10-30 in #incidents and Confluence notes page created.

Issue summary:
FinSight reports that their production SSE sessions intermittently terminate with the final stream metadata ("end_of_stream": true) present, but the final payload is empty (no tokens, blank text). This occurs after the customer's client performs a network rebind (corporate laptop switching from VPN to corp Wi‑Fi) and the connection flows through an enterprise HTTP rewriter/proxy that rewrites chunk boundaries.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: final paragraph(s) missing in 3–7% of long-running interactive sessions (>4 minutes).
- Business: FinSight uses streamed answers in a trading-monitoring UI; missing last lines cause manual refreshes and user complaints.

Environment:
- Production, us-east-1 fronted by customer-managed enterprise proxy that rewrites chunk framing and removes certain keepalive headers.
- Customer uses token refresh at 50 minutes; issue observed for streams lasting >4 minutes and commonly around their token-refresh boundary.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a multi-paragraph prompt that triggers ~60–100 token streaming response and keep the page open.
2) Trigger a network path change on client (VPN -> corp Wi‑Fi) during streaming or perform an auth token refresh midstream.
3) The client reconnects; the SSE session resumes and server emits final metadata.
4) The UI shows the final metadata (end_of_stream flag) but no trailing tokens/closing text (blank tail).

Observed behavior / customer logs:
- Client sees an event: {event: "meta", data: {"end_of_stream": true, "request_id": "req-FA2c1"}} followed by a final empty data chunk (data: "" or data: "\n").
- Server request logs show a final Write of 0 bytes for the request_id on the serving runtime side around the same timestamp.
- Edge proxy logs show a sequence of chunk rewrite operations where an HTTP chunk boundary was merged with a keepalive probe.

Relevant headers (edge logs snippet):
- original-client: FinSight-WebUI/2.3
- x-rw-request-id: req-FA2c1
- connection: keep-alive
- rw-proxy-rewrite: chunk-boundary-merge

Customer-supplied timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-11T15:21:12Z prompt submitted (req-FA2c1)
- 2026-03-11T15:21:15Z first tokens stream
- 2026-03-11T15:25:02Z client does VPN->Wi‑Fi rebind; client reconnects and resumes
- 2026-03-11T15:25:02.120Z server emits meta {end_of_stream: true} for req-FA2c1
- 2026-03-11T15:25:02.121Z server Write(0 bytes) logged for req-FA2c1

Notes:
- Repro rate at the customer site ~5/100 during their busy window. Internal testing using our public endpoint with a synthetic rewriter has not reproduced the exact blank-tail — we usually see duplication or truncated token sequences.
- Customer uses HTTP/2 fronting to the proxy; the proxy converts to HTTP/1.1 for our edge. Suspect chunk boundary transformation during protocol downgrade combined with an empty final write being treated as terminal metadata.

Attachments: customer provided proxy logs, client capture (har), sample request_id: req-FA2c1

Additional notes:
Edge trace: multiple h2->h1 conversions observed; proxy labeled chunk-boundary-merge in 60% of repro traces.
Runtime behavior: Terminal metadata emitted consistently at end-of-stream. Immediately after metadata, runtime calls Write(0) in the stream flush path for certain buffer states.
Hypothesis A: Proxy merges keepalive probe with final chunk and signals content-length 0 on the last write; downstream client receives end_of_stream metadata but actual payload bytes consumed by proxy rewrite.
Hypothesis B: Runtime flush path treats 0-byte write as no-op and does not send closing token sequence when buffer flagged as partially drained by edge.
Local repro notes: Using our test rewriter (simulates chunk merge) we reproduced a 'blank tail' when the rewriter performed an in-place coalescence of a keepalive probe and the final chunk boundary while the runtime's write buffer was in transition. Reproducer script saved to internal artifact store.
Telemetry: ~2 other enterprise customers with similar proxy setups show low-rate occurrences in token-level telemetry; not widespread for standard public routing.
Mitigations tested: forcing a non-zero terminal write (padding) from runtime prevents blank-tail but can add stray whitespace to outputs; not acceptable as long-term fix.
Workaround provided: customer to bypass enterprise rewrite for streaming endpoints or disable chunk-boundary-merge during validation window. Engineering fix: edge-proxy PR (github.com/redwood-inference/proxy@pr/612) adds detection of merge patterns and preserves final payload boundaries; runtime PR to handle zero-length final writes gracefully (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime@pr/1987) prepared. Planned rollout: staging 2026-03-16, prod 2026-03-18 after integration tests. Follow-up: post-deploy validation with FinSight for 72 hours.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send steady 200 RPS at production input distribution with average tokens/request ~120 during warm hours.
2) Ramp to 650 RPS over 3 minutes.
3) Observe route decisions and per-variant queue lengths via Console trace and /debug routing API.

Observed behavior & logs:
- Router decision traces show sampler selecting fallback variant 'io-quantized-13b' at ramp start. Trace excerpt: "fallback_decision: estimator_confidence=0.18, selected_variant=io-quantized-13b, variant_state=RUNNING".
- Replica logs show repeated cold-KV misses and long disk I/O waits: "kv_cache_miss=1.00, kv_populate_latency_ms=980".
- Autoscaler logs: "scale_event: triggered=false, capacity_headroom=-14%"; no immediate scale-up because provisioner considered existing replicas healthy.
- p99 and 504 spike correlates with multiple replicas concurrently executing first-populate of KV shards (serial population overlapping across replicas).
- Console trace links: https://console.redwood/internal/traces/dh-5473/2026-03-10/09:45 (redacted)

Initial hypothesis:
- Router's capacity estimator underweighted KV warmup cost for the quantized IO-bound variant, treating it as 'fast' due to low steady CPU usage in normal tests. During rapid ramp, multiple requests routed to the variant while its KV cache populated, causing high per-request I/O latency and queueing. Because the fallback variant carries a smaller memory footprint, the router preferred it despite cold KV state.

Investigation steps taken:
- Pulled per-replica KV warmup metrics across the fleet (kv_cache_fill_rate, kv_populate_latency_ms).
- Cross-checked recent commit that changed variant metadata scoring weights (GH PR: #8432) — found a change that reduced 'expected_kv_warmup_penalty' weight to 0.1 from 0.6 in routing heuristics.
- Replayed traffic in staging: reproduced p99 increase when routing decisions include io-quantized variant with empty KV. When we forced 'kv_warmed=true' in routing metadata, latency remained stable.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Applied a routing policy override for MacroHealth to disable io-quantized-13b fallback for the service (policy change id: policy-2026-03-11-07). This immediately reduced p99 to baseline and eliminated 504s during ramp tests.
- Notified customer and updated status.

Next steps & proposed fix:
1) Revert or adjust the recent routing weight change that de-emphasized KV warmup penalty (related PR #8432) — engineering ticket INT-1019 opened.
2) Add a pre-check in router to avoid routing new traffic to variants with kv_cache_fill_ratio < 0.6 during traffic ramps.
3) Improve autoscaler trigger sensitivity to concurrent KV warmup events to perform faster ramp-up of warm replicas.
4) Add unit + integration tests that simulate ramp traffic with cold KV replicas to prevent regression.

Resolution notes:
- Workaround holds for MacroHealth; long-term fix targeted for next maintenance window (2026-03-15). Associated internal rollout plan created in INT-1019.

Attachments/References:
- Routing debug dumps (sensitive) uploaded to secure ticket storage.
- GH PR #8432: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/8432
- Console traces and cluster metrics (links shortened)

Additional notes:
Samira Gomez (SRE) (2026-03-11): Confirmed concurrent KV population on 4/6 replicas triggered I/O waits; autoscaler delayed due to health gating. Gathering artifact logs.
Engineering (2026-03-11): Found PR #8432 reduced kv warmup penalty; reverting locally reduced routing to fallback and eliminated p99 spike in staging.
Workaround applied: disabled fallback to io-quantized-13b for affected customer; long-term fix planned to adjust routing heuristics and autoscaler sensitivity. Targeted deployment window 2026-03-15.
Follow-up: add e2e ramp tests to CI that include KV warmup scenarios, and update runbook to include detection of concurrent kv-populate thrashing.
payload.summary: Episodic fallback to IO-bound variant creating concurrent cold-cache thrashing and 504s

Issue summary:
BrightRoute AI reported an unexpected invoice line on their 2026-02 monthly invoice. The line shows a non-zero amount but the 'quantity' column is zero for metric 'cache-warmup:prefix-001' (EUR invoice).

Impact:
- Customer believes they were billed for cache warmups without recorded quantity, causing confusion and potential dispute with their finance team.
- Affects trust in cross-region multi-currency billing; customer is enterprise and requests a prompt resolution.

Environment:
- Production billing run for BrightRoute AI (org id: brightroute-001), billing region eu-west, invoice id INV-2026-02-BR001 (EUR).

Timeline:
- 2026-03-09 09:12 UTC: Customer emailed billing support with screenshot of invoice line showing amount €12.73 and quantity 0.
- 2026-03-10 08:45 UTC: Ticket created by support (Aisha).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Customer runs scheduled batch that triggers prefix cache warmups at low volume (~0.03 token-equivalent per event) across many short-lived jobs.
2. Usage postbacks are aggregated by hourly reconciler and converted to invoice lines in EUR.
3. Pricing re-rate for EUR was applied during end-of-month consolidation (new exchange rates applied).
4. Finalized invoice shows cache-warmup line with amount but quantity column rounded to 0.

Expected behavior:
- Small fractional usage should be aggregated and represented with non-zero quantity (rounded appropriately) or merged into a catch-all line; invoice quantity should never be zero if an amount is present.

Actual behavior:
- Reconciler produced a line with amount > 0 and quantity = 0 (see attachment INV-2026-02-BR001-snip.png).

Attachments:
- INV-2026-02-BR001-snip.png (screenshot provided by customer)
Initial hypothesis: rounding/precision error during multi-currency conversion combined with a postback dedup/merge bug.

What we pulled:
- Billing ledger entries (ledger export 2026-03-01T02Z) show a cost allocation record for metric cache-warmup:prefix-001 with cost_eur = 12.73 and raw_token_units = 0.00038.
- Hourly reconciler step 'normalize_and_bucket' currently records 'display_quantity' by rounding raw_token_units to 2 decimal places for invoice CSV generation. That produced 0.00 -> written as 0 in CSV while cost was computed upstream from higher-precision micro-units after FX.
- PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/usage-reconciler/pull/342 touched the EUR rounding logic; suspected edge-case introduced where quantity rounding happens after cost calculation instead of before, allowing cost > 0 with quantity 0.
- Reconciler logs (reconciler-eu-2026-03-01.log) include entries: "WARN: tiny usage preserved in cost bucket but display_quantity=0 -> invoice_line_id=IL-98765".

Interim conclusion: billing pipeline allowed cost to be computed at micro-unit precision, applied FX conversion, and then rounded display_quantity to 2 decimals. The UI/CSV generator does not reconcile display_quantity back to cost, leading to invoice lines with cost and zero quantity.

Workarounds considered:
- Manual credit for the specific invoice line (Finance can issue a credit memo).
- Patch reconciler to coerce display_quantity to a minimum of 0.01 when cost > 0 (avoids zero quantity lines).
- Longer-term: change flow to compute display_quantity from billed cost / unit_price after FX rounding, or aggregate micro-usage into a hidden fractional bucket that consolidates into >=0.01 quantity lines.
1) Run micro-burst cache-warmup jobs that generate raw_token_units < 0.005 per hour in eu-west.
2) Ensure pricing re-rate with FX applied during invoice consolidation (EUR).
3) Run hourly reconciler and produce invoice CSV.
4) Observe invoice CSV contains lines with amount > 0 and quantity = 0 for cache-warmup metric.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 10:12 UTC - Customer (BrightRoute AI): Appreciates quick response — please confirm when credit is visible and whether this will reoccur after pricing changes.
Workaround: Finance to issue a credit memo for €12.73 against INV-2026-02-BR001 (actioned 2026-03-12).
Engineering fix: Reconciler PR #342 merged to trunk; change computes display_quantity from billed_amount / unit_price after FX rounding and enforces minimum display quantity of 0.01 when billed_amount > 0.
Planned rollout: canary in eu-west completed 2026-03-13; full rollout scheduled 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC.
Follow-up: run a re-check job to scan invoices from 2026-02 consolidation window and flag similar zero-quantity lines for manual credits if found.
Status: Pending final rollout and post-rollout verification.
Create automated check in billing validation that rejects invoice CSV rows with amount > 0 and quantity = 0 (ticket created in billing backlog).
Backfill scan for Feb 2026 invoices for small fractional cache-warmup lines (owner: Mateo Li).
Add unit/integration tests covering FX + rounding edge-cases (owner: usage-reconciler team).
Communicate RCA and preventive measures to BrightRoute AI via CS email thread once rollout is verified.

payload.description:
Issue summary: After configuring IdP-initiated SSO for Nimbus Health's Private deployment, periodic IdP single-logout (SLO) probes from their vendor (AuthWave) are observed to cause the Redwood ingress to rewrite the session cookie domain by truncating tenant namespace suffixes. Impact: End-users and service accounts intermittently hit 401/reauth loops across the Redwood admin and ingest APIs. Expected: SLO probes should not alter or truncate session cookie domain/path; logout events should be processed without breaking other sessions. Environment details: Private control plane deployed into customer's VPC using edge-proxy v2.1.7, ingress-proxy v3.4.0, auth-bridge v1.9. Deployed certs: internal mTLS + customer-managed IdP metadata via SAML. Observed window: recurring since 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC, roughly every 6–8 hours when IdP health probes run.
1) Set up IdP-initiated SSO with AuthWave SAML metadata in a Private deployment (tenant-scoped).
2) Enable periodic IdP SLO/health probe from AuthWave (probe includes SLO endpoint + cookie-less GET).
3) Observe ingress logs when probe performs a request that triggers session cookie handling (AuthWave probe sends Host header without tenant suffix).
4) Attempt normal user API calls or console operations immediately after the probe; note 401 and redirect-to-login behavior.
2026-03-09T02:05:12Z ingress-proxy[router] INFO cookie_rewrite: original_cookie_domain=customer-tenant.nimbus.internal.local
2026-03-09T02:05:12Z ingress-proxy[router] WARN cookie_rewrite: computed_domain=customer-tenant.nimbus.internal (truncated suffix)
2026-03-09T02:05:12Z auth-bridge[session] ERROR session_validate: missing_tenant_namespace; session rejected, returning 401
2026-03-09T02:07:40Z control-plane[audit] INFO auth_flow: idp_slo_received idp_request_id=aw-probe-5514
Initial correlation shows 1:1 mapping between AuthWave probe timestamps and increased 401s across the tenant's sessions.
Cookie rewrite logic located in ingress-proxy/router/session_cookie.go; function CreateEffectiveCookieDomain(host) uses naive last-two-label heuristic that fails for internal multi-label domains and tenant prefixes.
AuthWave probe omits tenant prefix in Host header for health check optimization; this triggers fallback path that strips trailing label (eg. .local) producing non-matching cookie domain.
Reproduction steps executed in internal staging with a synthetic AuthWave probe confirmed cookie domain change and session invalidation when probe executed.
Patch candidate: change heuristic to prefer longest-match against tenant registry; skip truncation when Host header label-count < expected or when request path contains /slo endpoint.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 08:20 - Customer (Nimbus Health): Confirmed that when our IdP probe uses tenant-less host header the admin console fails for all web sessions. We can temporarily disable the IdP probe but need a durable fix.
Workaround: Nimbus Health disabled IdP SLO/health probes to stop immediate 401s. We validated a staging hotfix that conservatively bypasses cookie-domain truncation when Host header lacks tenant prefix; patch PR #4832 created for ingress-proxy. Plan: schedule controlled rollout to customer Private control plane during maintenance window 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC. Post-deploy follow-up: add unit tests for multi-label internal domains and update SSO runbook to recommend IdP probes include tenant-scoped Host or use probe path that doesn't hit session-handling endpoints. Owner for rollout: Ravi Patel.
payload.summary: IdP-initiated SLO probe truncates session cookie domain causing re-auth loops and 401s in private VPC

payload.description:
Issue summary: Glacier Analytics reports intermittent ~2-6s spikes in first-token latency for short-lived user requests from their web app. Spikes began after they upgraded to SDK v1.4.0 and changed client-side idle-connection eviction to aggressively close idle sockets (idle_evict_ms set to 1000). Impact: user-facing timeouts and increased visible retry counts, occasional 504s. Environment: Dedicated tenant in us-east region, traffic pattern is many short requests (avg token length small, high qps bursts).
1) Use SDK v1.4.0 configured with connectionPool: {maxIdle: 2, idleEvictMs: 1000, maxSockets: 8}
2) Simulate bursty short requests (50-200ms request intervals) with a pool of ephemeral front-end workers.
3) Observe first-request/first-token latency distribution and retry counts over 10 minutes.
4) Reproduce with SDK v1.3.8 (previous) using default idleEvictMs=60000 to compare.
- Frequent first-token latency spikes: 1200ms - 6000ms
- Client-side logs show connection teardown and reestablish sequences immediately preceding spikes.
- Server-side access logs show a corresponding SYN/FIN patterns and short-lived TLS handshakes.
- Customer sees >15% of requests trigger SDK retries within burst windows, leading to apparent timeouts in the UI.
- Warm pooled connections reused with first-token latency ~80-150ms for these short requests.
- Low retry counts and no visible timeouts for typical burst traffic patterns.
[2026-03-10T14:12:04Z] client-sdk-js connection=conn-7 state=evicted idle_ms=1100
[2026-03-10T14:12:04Z] client-sdk-js attempt=1 new_socket=true tls_handshake=120ms
[2026-03-10T14:12:04Z] request=abc123 first_token_latency=2300ms retries=1 status=200
[2026-03-10T14:12:04Z] server ingress connection=conn-7 accept_time=14:12:04.102 TLS=completed
[2026-03-10T14:12:04Z] server trace: model=redwood-3b-v1 schedule_wait=18ms batch_wait=2ms compute=102ms
[2026-03-10T14:12:04Z] support note: client reported 504 after 2 attempts

- Repro locally with customer SDK config and our load generator: when idleEvictMs set to 1s, pool frequently drains between bursts and reconnects incur TLS + TCP overhead.
- Observed head-of-line effect: front-end worker tasks block waiting for a new connection to complete handshake while other in-flight requests queue behind application-level locks in SDK.
- SDK v1.4.0 introduced an aggressive idle evict implementation and a synchronous socket creation path for missing connections; combined with small maxIdle this amplifies cold-start penalty.
- Server-side metrics do not show serving-runtime slowness; CPU and GPU utilization normal. Network RTTs stable. Root cause points at client-side pool misconfiguration + SDK behavior change.
- Linked to customer-side thread model: ephemeral workers create spike of concurrent dial attempts leading to transient connection storms and a small fraction of requests experiencing serialized waits (per-thread lock contention in SDK client).
Aggressive idle eviction + low maxIdle causes frequent cold connection creation. SDK's synchronous connection creation path and a global mutex in the pool code serializes dial path, producing perceived high tail latency and retries. Not a serving-runtime regression.
Client SDK configuration (idle_evict_ms=1000, maxIdle=2) combined with a synchronous dial path introduced in SDK v1.4.0 caused pooled sockets to be frequently torn down and re-created under bursty short-request workloads. Re-creation serialized inside the SDK led to head-of-line blocking and elevated first-token latency, triggering retries/timeouts at the application layer.
- Immediate: revert to SDK v1.3.8 or set idleEvictMs >= 30000 and maxIdle >= 8 on customer side to keep sockets warm during bursts.
- Short-term: bump keepalive settings and enable SDK async dial flag (sdkOptions.asyncDial=true) to avoid synchronous blocking while connections are established.
- We recommended increasing read timeout client-side to avoid premature 504s while they test config changes.
In progress (customer applied recommended config change on 2026-03-11: idleEvictMs=45000, maxIdle=8). Observed immediate reduction in first-token spikes in our telemetry: 95th pct latency dropped from ~2.6s to ~160ms across sampled bursts. We opened SDK issue to make async dial default and to remove global lock in pool (PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/612). Patch to SDK landed in v1.4.2 and scheduled for canary release internal 2026-03-14.
- Engineering: prioritize SDK pool fix (remove global mutex, default async dial) and ship in next minor (done in PR #612).
- Docs: add guidance for bursty/short-request workloads on connection pool tuning and defaults.
- SRE: add alert that correlates high client-side dial rates with elevated first-token latency for dedicated tenants.
- Customer success: check back with Glacier Analytics after canary rollout and mark ticket Resolved when 48 hours of stable telemetry confirmed.
2026-03-10 15:02 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer reports spikes after upgrading to SDK v1.4.0 and changing pool eviction. Asked for SDK config dump and sample logs.
2026-03-10 16:10 - Customer (Glacier Analytics - ops@glacier.com): Provided config and logs. Noted spikes only during peak bursts; no change in payload sizes.
2026-03-10 18:45 - SRE (Miguel Santos): Reproduced locally with load generator. Confirming warm-pool behavior fixes issue. Hypothesis: aggressive eviction + sync dial causes serialization.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Support (Aisha Patel): Sent recommended immediate config changes and temporary downgrade path. Scheduled 30-minute call to assist with rollout.
2026-03-11 12:37 - Customer (Glacier Analytics): Rolled out recommended settings. Preliminary metrics look better; still watching.
2026-03-12 08:20 - Eng (Lina Zhao): Submitted PR to make asyncDial default and to remove pool global lock; linked PR #612 for review.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Updated SLA and will follow up after SDK canary is live.
payload.summary: Intermittent cold-start latency spikes after aggressive idle-connection eviction in customer SDK leading to timeouts and retries

Issue summary:
Customer BrightAssist reports a sudden and sustained increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completion requests after they pin a specific model version and after the platform runtime rollout on 2026-03-11. Impact is restricted to their prod us-east workloads and started ~2026-03-12 09:40 UTC.

Impact:
- Chat TTFB increased from ~120ms median to 700-1,200ms for initial tokens.
- End-user experience: noticeably slower streaming starts; some requests time out at client SDK layer after 10s (rare).
- No increased 5xx error rate observed, but elevated latencies causing SLA concerns for enterprise contract.

Environment:
- Customer is on enterprise Dedicated/Dual-mode (private control plane, hosted runtime).
- Customer had pinned model: redwood-open-1.4-quantized@2026-03-10.
- Platform runtime rolled out to us-east on 2026-03-11: runtime-agent 2.14 -> 2.16 (canary->region).

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer and validated by Support):
1) Send new chat completion request to pinned model endpoint using streaming=true.
2) Observe initial HTTP chunk and TTFB measured at client side (SDK).
3) Repeat with warm session (existing conversation) vs new session.

Observed behavior:
- New sessions show high TTFB (median ~800ms, p95 ~1.15s).
- Warm sessions (after previous calls) show normal TTFB (~140ms).
- Larger prompts (context >1k tokens) exacerbate delay slightly.
- Logs show normal token generation throughput once streaming starts.

Logs excerpt and metrics (selected):
- Serving runtime traces: request_enter -> model_load_hit=true -> kernel_dispatch_time increased for first token on quantized path.
- Per-route latency: initial-byte latency increased 6x while tail-of-stream latency unchanged.
- No obvious memory pressure or GPU OOM events in node metrics.

Additional notes:
- Customer uses dedicated pool with pinned model; we observed the same TTFB pattern when we duplicated request traffic in a test namespace that also upgraded to runtime 2.16.

1) POST /v1/chat/completions to customer endpoint with streaming=true using pinned model. 2) Measure time from request send -> first chunk. 3) Compare cold session vs warm session. 4) Reproduce on an instance still on runtime 2.14 to confirm delta.
[2026-03-12T09:42:11Z] request_id=abc123 serving-runtime: model_lookup hit=true; kv_cache_lookup miss; kernel_select start; kernel_select took 420ms; first_token_emit at 850ms; subsequent tokens at 25ms/token.
[2026-03-12T09:42:12Z] node-metrics: gpu_util=45% mem_ok=true; no OOM; batch_size=1;

Initial hypothesis: kernel selection or quantized model path introduced a slow JIT/initialization path in runtime 2.16 that only affects first-token emission for cold contexts (e.g., KV cache miss or first forward pass after model pin).
Actions taken so far:
- Replayed customer traffic against a runtime-2.14 instance: no TTFB spike observed.
- Captured debug-level kernel dispatch traces and enabled extra timing for quantized operator init.
- Created INT ticket for runtime engineering to look at kernel dispatch fallbacks (INT-829).
- Temporarily routed BrightAssist traffic to a 2.14 pool as a mitigation for their SLA while engineering investigates.

A change in kernel selection logic in runtime 2.16 causes an extra CPU-bound initialization on the first execution of certain quantized kernels, adding ~400-600ms before the first token is emitted. Warm paths hit cached kernels and are unaffected.
Under investigation by runtime team. Preliminary root cause: regression in kernel dispatch when model is quantized and pinned; fallback to a compatibility kernel path triggers per-request initialization on cold contexts. See related PR investigation.
Mitigation applied: routed customer's requests to runtime 2.14 pool for us-east and created a temporary routing rule. Long-term fix: runtime patch to avoid per-request kernel init on quantized path (PR referenced below). Engineering ETA for patch and staged rollout: 2026-03-16.
Follow-ups: validate with synthetic cold-start tests across quantized models and add unit test to prevent regression.
2026-03-12T10:05Z — Support (Aisha Khan): Opened ticket after BrightAssist CS reported TTFB regressions. Customer provided sample request IDs and SDK timing. Escalating to runtime eng. Adding monitoring dashboards link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ttfb/braightassist-namespace
2026-03-12T11:20Z — Runtime Eng (Sofia Martinez): Reproduced locally against runtime-2.16. Observed 430ms spent in kernel_select for quantized path on first invocation. Creating INT-829 to track fix. Will try immediate config toggle to prefer cached kernels.
2026-03-12T14:00Z — Support (Aisha Khan): Applied emergency routing change to send BrightAssist traffic to runtime-2.14 pool in us-east. Customer confirmed immediate improvement in TTFB. Notified customer of temporary mitigation and next steps.
2026-03-13T09:45Z — Customer (BrightAssist, Maya Patel): Thank you — saw TTFB return to expected levels after reroute. Would like timeline for permanent fix and regression tests before we re-upgrade pooled runtimes.
2026-03-14T12:10Z — Runtime Eng (Sofia Martinez): Patch PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3456 opened to cache quantized kernel dispatch objects and avoid per-request initializers. Running CI; plan for canary in us-east 2026-03-15.
2026-03-14T15:25Z — Support (Liam O'Connor): Noted customer ask for regression test. Adding test case to QA plan and will coordinate canary window with BrightAssist for minimal disruption.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightDesk reports that long SSE streams which contain markdown with image embeds intermittently resume with the final closing bracket of a code block or image markdown truncated (e.g. '![screenshot](https://.../img.png' with missing ')'). The result is a half-formed markdown block and the image URL is not recognized by their renderer. The problem appears only after a short pause in the connection (~3-7s) followed by an automatic resume. Impact:
- End users see broken markdown or missing images for a small percentage (~1.2%) of long streaming responses.
- Customer has a production job that relies on rendered transcripts; this causes visual corruption and downstream parsing failures.
Environment:
- prod (us-east) behind customer's corporate edge proxy and ALB.
- Requests via browser-based SDK and server-to-server SDK.
Steps to reproduce (best-effort):
1) Use BrightDesk test workload (large narratives + base64 image references) against redwood-open-7b-v2.
2) Simulate a 3-7s network pause (client backgrounding or proxy backoff), then allow socket to resume.
3) Observe resumed SSE stream in browser: trailing markdown closing token or final ')' of image URL missing; sometimes final '
```' removed.
Logs / artifacts provided by customer:
- Customer-provided HAR and tcpdump snippets attached to the ticket (see comments).
- Sample truncated stream payload (sanitized) included in comments.
Additional notes:
- Customer reports increase after they rotated their corporate proxy to introduce HTTP/2 connection coalescing ~2 weeks ago.
- Affects both SSE and long-lived WebSocket-to-SSE fallback sessions.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 - BrightDesk (Customer): Uploaded sanitized tcpdump and HAR. Customer notes issue spikes when their ALB drains connections for short periods. They've observed truncated final ')' on image markdown in ~1.2% of resumed sessions.
2026-03-11 - Eng (runtime): Added trace log of SSE framing and noticed final '\n' delimiter not flushed in some codepaths when session resumes during edge backpressure. Pushing instrumented build to staging for additional repros.
2026-03-11 - BrightDesk (Customer): Verified that sending a short keepalive every 2s reduces occurrence. They cannot disable ALB settings due to internal policy.
2026-03-12 - Eng (runtime): Confirmed PR created to ensure final-frame flush and to add resilience to partial-chunk reassembly under HTTP/2 window adjustments. PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4951
Instrumented staging to reproduce: introduced artificial 4s stall in upstream read path; observed identical truncated trailing tokens in 9/100 runs.
Hypothesis: edge-proxy HTTP/2 flow control + ALB idle-probe creates a pause where the runtime's chunk-assembler returns early and final flush of the terminal delimiter is lost during socket rebind.
Correlated traces: client-seq 1023 shows last bytes not ACKed before pause; resumed TCP shows new stream id and payload missing last 10-14 bytes. No 5xx returned by runtime.
SDK behaviour: older SDKs do reliant optimistic buffering which assumes the server will always send terminal delimiter; adding a client sentinel reduces failed renders.
Related historical tickets: some overlap with SUP-314271 (resume delta issues) but this case includes image-URL-specific missing ')', likely due to being at chunk boundary during pause.
Risk: medium — data loss limited to final bytes of streams on resume scenarios, not entire conversations. However customer's parsing pipeline is sensitive to exact markdown closure.
Short-term workaround (customer action): upgrade to patched SDK v2.3.1 which emits explicit resume sentinel and performs local reassembly checks; route critical jobs over private link to avoid ALB-induced pauses.
Immediate mitigation (platform): increased server-side final-frame flush retries in staging and added a verification that final delimiter was sent before connection handoff (hotfix branch: github.com/redwood/repo/commit/9a7b2f1).

Issue summary:
Customer reports failing model artifact downloads for large model pulls using presigned S3 URLs from their Private deployment. Errors show TLS certificate name mismatch when the platform attempts to fetch artifacts during model load.

Impact:
- Model pulls fail intermittently, causing pod restart loops and degraded inference capacity for the customer's private deployment in us-east-1.
- Affects production traffic for a single customer (FinSolve Analytics).

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peering to Redwood control plane).
- prod/us-east-1.
- Model: gptx-13b-v2 (~4.2GB artifact).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a model rollout that requires a fresh artifact pull (scale up or new node join).
2) Observe model-puller logs in the private deployment agent.
3) Some requests show TLS handshake failures when fetching the presigned URL returned by Redwood Control Plane.

Observed logs (excerpts):
- model-puller: "GET https://finsolve-models.s3.amazonaws.com/artifacts/....?X-Amz-Signature=..."  --> TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed: hostname '10.10.20.45' does not match 'finsolve-models.s3.amazonaws.com'
- curl --location --verbose against presigned URL from within customer VPC shows: "* Connected to 10.10.20.45 (10.10.20.45) port 443 (#0)" then "* TLS: hostname mismatch (certificate is for internal-cache.company.corp)"

Notes from customer: their on-prem DNS resolver and corporate proxy return an internal IP for the s3 hostname (split-horizon) and forward traffic to an internal HTTPS cache/proxy for inspection and deduplication. The proxy uses an internal cert not matching the S3 hostname.

Timeline and diagnostics performed:
- 2026-02-28 09:10 UTC: Support replicated failing model pulls in a staging mirror using customer's forwarded DNS rules.
- Ran dig +short finsolve-models.s3.amazonaws.com against the customer's forwarder -> returned 10.10.20.45 (internal cache IP).
- tcpdump from model-puller container showed SYN->SYN/ACK with 10.10.20.45 then TLS ClientHello; server sent a cert with CN=internal-cache.company.corp and SANs not including the S3 hostname.
- curl -v to presigned URL inside customer VPC reproduced: certificate hostname mismatch and the TLS subject contained internal proxy name.
- Verified presigned URL host was the regional S3 hostname as expected; cert returned by upstream connection did not match.
- Control-plane logs confirm presigned URL generation was correct; Redwood side S3 endpoints unaffected.

Hypothesis:
- Customer split-horizon DNS returns an internal IP for S3 hostnames, routing presigned S3 requests to an internal HTTPS inspection/cache appliance that terminates TLS with its own cert, causing hostname mismatch and client-side verification to fail.

Evidence to support hypothesis:
- Packet captures show internal IP and proxy cert CN.
- Curl and openssl s_client show cert CN mismatch when run from inside customer network; same presigned URL fetched successfully from an external network.
- No signs of S3 or Redwood control plane issuing partial redirects or rewriting hostnames.

2026-02-28 - Customer (Rajesh Kumar): We've observed this intermittently across several nodes. Some nodes succeed, others fail. The proxy team insists they only touch hostnames in a permit list.
2026-02-28 - Support (Nina Patel): Thanks Rajesh — we've captured a pcap and certificate fingerprint. Can you confirm whether your proxy injects a substitute certificate for *.s3.amazonaws.com? Also please share whether you have DNS split-horizon rules for *.s3.amazonaws.com.
2026-02-28 - Customer (Rajesh Kumar): Confirmed: internal resolver returns 10.10.20.45 for bucket hostnames and our proxy performs TLS termination. It's intended for cache/dedupe. We'll escalate to network team to add an exception if recommended.
2026-02-28 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Reproduced in lab with customer's DNS. Verified host mismatch. Short-term workaround: set model-puller no_proxy to include *.s3.amazonaws.com OR add an ACL on proxy to passthrough S3 requests without TLS termination. Permanent: update DNS or use AWS VPC Endpoint (VPCE) for S3 access.
2026-03-01 - Customer (Rajesh Kumar): We added a proxy bypass for S3 hosts and model pulls succeed. We'll coordinate with proxy team to add an explicit passthrough ACL for S3 hosts and update split-horizon rules.
2026-03-01 - Support (Nina Patel): Marking resolved based on customer's confirmation and suggested follow-ups. Created INT-204 to add a runbook note for private deploy customers about split-horizon and presigned URL verification.
2026-03-01 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Noted: recommend adding both documentation and a healthcheck in the agent that validates presigned URL TLS termination path during start-up and surfaces clear error text suggesting 'no_proxy / VPCE / DNS exception' to reduce time-to-fix for customers.
Workaround applied by customer: added proxy bypass for bucket hostnames and configured model-puller 'no_proxy' to prevent proxy interception of presigned S3 requests. Result: model downloads resumed and nodes stabilized.

Root cause: Customer split-horizon DNS + corporate HTTPS caching appliance was terminating TLS for S3 hostnames, presenting an internal certificate that did not include the S3 hostname. Because presigned URLs are single-use and host-specific, the client's TLS verification failed.

Permanent remediation recommendations provided to customer:
1) Add an explicit passthrough rule on the proxy for S3 regional hostnames used by Redwood (do not terminate TLS for pre-signed artifact fetches).
2) Update split-horizon DNS so S3 hostnames resolve to AWS IPs or configure the model-puller/service to use a VPC Endpoint (VPCE) for S3 to keep traffic inside AWS without proxy interception.
3) Add a startup healthcheck in the agent to validate presigned URL TLS chain and produce actionable error messages (INT-204 created to track runbook change).

Follow-ups:
- INT-204: Add runbook note and agent healthcheck ticket for engineering.
- Customer will update proxy ACLs and confirm.
payload.summary: Presigned-artifact TLS name mismatch caused by split-horizon DNS rewriting S3 host to internal proxy

Issue summary: Customer BrightHealth AI reported a sudden increase in 95th/99th percentile tail latency for inference requests after applying a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that enabled aggressive batching, prefix KV prefetch, and a mixed 4-bit quantization profile. Impact: Intermittent API timeouts (up to 30s) affecting live features for 10% of requests, SLO breaches for the customer's dedicated pool. Environment: Dedicated tenant cluster in us-west-2; production traffic; tenant ID bhai-03. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use tenant API key bhai-03 in prod us-west-2. 2) Send typical 1-2k concurrent short-chat requests (avg seq len 120 tokens) over 2–5 minutes. 3) Observe increasing 95p/99p latency and occasional 504s. Observed behavior: Gradual buildup of host-level GPU memory pressure during steady traffic, periodic long-running server-side stalls that correlate with aggressive batch formation and KV prefetch spikes. Expected behavior: Stable p95/p99 for same workload after optimizer change with small improvements in median latency. Logs/metrics: - Serving runtime trace: intermittent block on batch-assembly loop (trace id included in comment) - Console metrics: burst in batch size to >2.5x configured target, KV prefetch cache hit ratio drops to 0.6 briefly - Example request ids: req_bhai_20260312_01..05 - No obvious OOMs in node-level logs; GC spikes on host reported. Initial hypothesis: Combination of larger-than-expected batching window + KV prefetch thrash causing temporary memory overhead and kernel scheduling stalls on GPU, accentuated by mixed 4-bit quant path. Temporary mitigations already applied: - Switched tenant traffic to conservative optimizer profile (via console rollback toggle) which reduced incidents but customer reports stateful sessions lost for some in-flight requests. - Applied traffic-split to route 10% to old profile for safety. Customer asks for: 1) a reproducible preflight checklist to validate optimizer profiles before tenant-wide promotion, 2) a safe, tenant-scoped hotpatch rollback procedure that preserves in-flight session continuity where possible, and 3) suggestions for configuration guardrails to prevent recurrence. Recommended action (short term): 1) Run the "safety-sentinel" preflight on a shadow workload: use the customer's representative prompt set (attached) against a staging pool configured to mimic dedicated pool (same GPU instance types & quant kernels). 2) Execute the following hotpatch rollback steps (tenant-scoped, staged):   a) Pause new session-creation at load-balancer for bhai-03 for 30s window.   b) Set optimizer profile to conservative snapshot (profile id: conservative-2026-02) via tenant-scoped API — this toggles batching window to 20ms, disables KV prefetch, and uses baseline 8-bit quant fallback.   c) Gradually re-open session creation and split traffic 80/20 (new/old) for 10 minutes, monitor p95/p99, batch-size distribution, KV hit ratio, GPU utilization.   d) If metrics stabilize, shift to 50/50 for 5 minutes then 100% over 15 minutes.   e) If any regression occurs, immediately reapply traffic-split back to 90% conservative and open an incident. 3) Provide a one-line hotpatch CLI command and a console playbook snippet for the customer's SRE (included in comments). Recommended action (long term): 1) Introduce a tenant-level optimizer preflight job that runs shadowed traffic for 10–15 minutes and validates thresholds for p95/p99, cache hit ratio, and batch size variance before allowing promotion. 2) Add a guardrail rule in the console that prevents promoting mixed-4bit profiles to dedicated pool without a preflight sign-off. 3) Capture optimizer profile snapshots automatically to enable atomic revert per-tenant. Post-action verifications: 1) Monitor 1h after full rollback for p99 stability and error rates. 2) Run a regression eval on the attached prompt set to ensure output quality isn't materially degraded by fallback quant profile. Follow-ups/future work: - Engineering to investigate kernel scheduling interaction with mixed-4bit execution path (link to PR). - Product to consider UI change for safer profile promotion. Attachments: representative prompt set (prompts_v1.json), sample traces (trace_ids list in comments).

Additional notes:
1) Coordinate with INT-339 owners for kernel scheduling investigation and backpressure feature. 2) Product to scope console guardrail UI change with PM. 3) Confirm 1h stability post rollback with customer and close ticket; deliver postmortem doc.

Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate downstream tool (webhook) executions when their long-running streaming session experiences an auth credential refresh. The idempotency/confirmation header added by the Python SDK is being rewritten/truncated during a mid-stream credential rotation at the API gateway which causes the server to treat the resumed chunk as a new request, re-invoking the tool webhook.

Context: QueryFlow uses the Redwood streaming chat endpoint with function/tool calling. Their Python client streams tokens and the server calls out to a customer-managed Go webhook to execute side effects. When the customer's token refreshes mid-stream (their environment rotates delegated credentials), we see duplicate webhook invocations in their logs.

Customer reports repeated duplicate side-effects (duplicate invoice sends and duplicate database writes) for ~2% of long-running streaming sessions. Business impact: end-user confusion and extra downstream processing, customer unable to safely rely on at-most-once semantics for streaming tool calls. Affects production workloads on dedicated capacity in us-east.
1. Create a long-lived streaming chat session using Python SDK and enable function/tool calling to a test Go webhook that logs invocations.
2. Start a multi-chunk generation (simulate >30s stream) that triggers a funcall during streaming (e.g., user asks to submit a batch job).
3. While stream is active, force a credential refresh on the client side (rotate ephemeral token or simulate delegated credential expiry + refresh mid-stream).
4. Allow the SDK to reconnect/resume the stream. Observe the webhook logs for duplicate invocations correlated with the same conversation id but different request IDs.
5. Collect API gateway request traces and headers for the chunk before and after refresh.
2026-03-13T15:12:08Z req=abc123 chunk=15 headers: Idempotency-Confirm=confirm:v1:eyJrIjoiYmFzZV9zaWcifQ==
2026-03-13T15:12:37Z req=abc123 auth=rotated chunk=16 headers: Idempotency-Confirm=confirm:v1:eyJrIjoiYmFzZV9zaWci
2026-03-13T15:12:37Z webhook invocation id=wh-001 conversation=conv-77 trigger=func_execute payload_id=pl-77
2026-03-13T15:12:38Z webhook invocation id=wh-002 conversation=conv-77 trigger=func_execute payload_id=pl-77
Initial triage: header value appears truncated/byte-altered after the gateway processes the token refresh. The base64 suffix changed length and server-side dedupe key no longer matched previous in-flight confirmation record.
Observed the API gateway performing header reconstitution when client presented a rotated auth token; header name preserved but value modified (line-wrapping/truncation in internal proxy).
Python SDK attaches idempotency confirmation as an HTTP header on the streaming chunks. If header is rewritten, server treats resumed chunk as new and re-issues tool call.
Customer's Go webhook is idempotent-by-body but relies on the Redwood confirmation header to avoid executing twice; without consistent header, dedupe fails.
Reproduced in our staging with a simulated credential rotation through the same proxy chain; confirmed header length and line-splitting behaviour under certain chunk-size boundaries (proxy config: max-header-size=8192, chunk-rewrite enabled).
Correlation IDs: api-trace:trace-20260313-abc123. Relevant gateway config: edge-proxy v2.18 with http2->http1 translation enabled on the dedicated stack for QueryFlow.
Short-term: ask customer to include a per-call idempotency token in the function call payload (body) instead of relying solely on headers. Alternatively, disable mid-stream auth rotation on their delegated token (increase TTL) while long streams are active. We can also ask them to patch webhook to dedupe using body payload_id.
In progress: engineering to patch two places — (1) edge proxy config to preserve header values across auth refreshes and avoid any line-wrapping/truncation; (2) server-side fallback to accept idempotency confirmation that arrives in the body if header is missing (opt-in via 'idempotency_fallback' flag). Patch PR created against edge-proxy and streaming-service. Temporary mitigation guidance provided to customer (see comments).
2026-03-13 16:05 - Support (Ava Thompson): Collected initial reproducer from customer, requested gateway logs and webhook request IDs. Customer confirmed duplicates happened ~3 times in last 24h. Asked them to run test harness with increased token TTL.
2026-03-13 18:22 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Reproduced locally with dedicated stack config. Found header line-splitting at 8k boundary when token refresh happens concurrently with chunk flush. Filed infra bug and started edge-proxy change. Assigned to Diego for patching.
2026-03-14 09:12 - Engineering (Priya Nair): Created PR to add body-based idempotency fallback. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-service/pull/3290. Needs review from security (to ensure fallback doesn't open replay attacks).
2026-03-14 11:30 - Support (Ava Thompson): Provided customer workaround steps: (1) add 'client_idempotency_key' to funcall payload; (2) increase ephemeral token TTL during long sessions; (3) update webhook dedupe by payload_id. Customer confirmed they can apply (1) immediately.
2026-03-14 14:00 - Security (Liam O'Connor): Raised concern about accepting idempotency in body without HMAC. Suggested adding signed idempotency tokens in future patch.
payload.summary: multipart stream: mid-stream credential rotation rewrites idempotency header and causes duplicate tool executions (Python client + Go webhook)

payload.description:
Customer reports their Hosted canary rollout auto-paused at the 25% step immediately after a short latency spike, despite overall application health appearing normal. They want to understand why it paused, whether this indicates a canary regression, and how to tune/avoid false positives during beta.

Issue summary
- What: Rollout transitioned to AUTO_PAUSED with reason "p95 latency regression > threshold".
- When: 2025-03-27 ~18:10–18:25 UTC during step 25%.
- Where: prod/us-east, route: /v1/chat/completions (Northstar customer route alias: support-agent-prod).
- Impact: Rollout progression blocked; customer held at 25% canary traffic for ~45 minutes until manual action. No hard outage, but rollout confidence reduced.

Customer-reported symptoms
- Console showed: "Rollout paused automatically due to SLO breach".
- Customer observed: brief latency increase across their app; no material increase in 5xx; canary model did not appear uniquely affected.

Expected behavior
- Auto-pause/rollback should trigger when canary cohort is reliably worse than baseline beyond configured thresholds, not when both baseline and canary are affected by a transient regional issue.

Actual behavior
- Auto-pause triggered on a short p95 spike; cohort comparison logic flagged canary regression even though baseline p95 also spiked in the same window.

Initial hypothesis
- Threshold sensitivity + evaluation window too short at 25% traffic created a false positive under transient regional latency. Also possible that the comparison job sampled unevenly across cohorts during the spike.

Notes
- This ticket is part of Hosted canary rollouts beta feedback. Customer asked for recommended settings (min soak time / evaluation window / sample size) and whether thresholds are configurable per route.

Additional notes:
2025-03-27 18:49 UTC — Customer (Northstar Support AI): Rollout ID rlt_7Qm2... Route: support-agent-prod. Step schedule was 1% (30m) → 5% (30m) → 25% (60m). Auto-paused ~10 min after entering 25%. We didn’t see error rate changes; did see increased latency for all requests for a bit. Can you confirm if canary is actually worse? We want to finish rollout today if safe.
Action: recommending customer resume rollout after us-east incident cleared, with temporarily relaxed stop condition or longer evaluation window for the 25% step.
2025-03-27 19:26 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support) to Customer: Root cause appears to be a brief us-east platform latency event impacting BOTH baseline and canary. The auto-pause was triggered by our default rule (p95 regression >20% over 5m) during a step transition (low/uneven samples). We do not currently see evidence the canary model is uniquely worse.
Recommendation: Resume rollout once p95 stabilizes (we’re seeing it back to normal now). For this rollout, either (a) temporarily disable p95-based auto-pause for the next step, or (b) widen lookback to 15m and increase threshold to 35% for the remainder of today. We can help apply settings in Console.
2025-03-27 19:44 UTC — Customer (Northstar Support AI): Thanks. We resumed at 25% and it has been stable for ~20m. Please share recommended defaults for next rollouts; we want guardrails but fewer false pauses.
Also: This aligns with internal SRE guidance page on Hosted rollout SLO metrics/alerts (linked).
Determined auto-pause was a false positive triggered by default p95 latency regression rule during a transient us-east latency incident affecting both cohorts, combined with a short evaluation window and low/uneven sample sizes immediately after a step change. Customer resumed rollout after the event cleared and completed rollout successfully.
Customer-facing outcome
- Provided explanation with timestamps + cohort dashboard interpretation.
- Recommended threshold tuning (longer lookback, higher regression threshold temporarily, minimum sample-size gating) for subsequent rollouts.
Internal outcome
- Captured beta feedback to adjust recommended wizard defaults and to add safeguards (sample size + grace period after step transitions) to reduce false pauses.
Product/Eng: Update rollout wizard recommended preset for latency stop conditions (lookback >=10m; guidance when <50% traffic).
SRE/Telemetry: Add minimum sample-size gating for p95 regression evaluation and a grace period after step changes (beta hardening).
Support: Add this scenario to canned responses / troubleshooting for "rollout paused unexpectedly" with links to cohort dashboards and the runbook.
payload.summary: Hosted canary rollout auto-paused unexpectedly after brief p95 latency spike (beta customer)

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 04:40 UTC Acme AI reported an increase in 5xx errors (502/503) and aborted streaming sessions coincident with scheduled maintenance windows where tenant preemption was active. Impact: multiple customer streaming sessions were disconnected and synchronous API calls returned intermittent 502/503 for ~15-25 minutes at two separate times. Root cause is hypothesized to be interaction between graceful preemption (node retirement) and the ingress prioritizer which caused uneven queue polarization and large head-of-line delays on lower-priority tenant queues, amplifying apigw timeouts and triggering runtime abrupt terminations under CPU pressure.
Initial hypothesis: preemption race causes backlog on the ingress prioritizer.
Evidence: 1) queue_polarization metric spikes exactly at node drain start time; 2) runtime processes show rapid SIGTERM + high CPU and elevated GC/ephemeral thread counts; 3) apigw logs show upstream 502s with proxied latency >10s.
Repro steps validated in staging with scaled-down topology; reproduces when autoscaler scale-in aggressiveness is set to >20% of pool and when prewarm headroom is <2 spare workers per shard.
Temporary mitigation implemented (2026-03-10 05:12 UTC): increased prewarm headroom for affected shard from 1->3 and slowed scale-in throttle for 30m which reduced 5xx to baseline.
Longer-term: engineering action items below.
1) Deploy two tenant traffic generators: one high-priority and one low-priority tenant (simulate Acme traffic pattern: many short chat streams + small embedding bursts).
2) Trigger graceful preemption on a subset of runtime nodes (simulate node drain via autoscaler scale-in).
3) Observe ingress-prioritizer logs and API gateway metrics while allowing connections to be handoff across runtimes.
4) Watch for queue length imbalance, streaming heartbeat timeouts, and upward 502/503 rates on the low-priority tenant.
Notes: reproduces reliably when preemption window < 60s and when headroom for new worker spin-up is limited.
[2026-03-10T04:40:12Z] apigw: recv from tenant=acme-stream id=abc123 latency=12000ms -> proxied upstream 502
[2026-03-10T04:40:14Z] ingress-prioritizer: queue_polarization: high=120, low=980 (threshold=750)
[2026-03-10T04:40:15Z] runtime(we-07): SIGTERM while draining active connections=42 cpu=94% rss=11.6G
[2026-03-10T04:46:03Z] apigw: streaming heartbeat timeout tenant=acme-stream id=def456
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/company/d/err/5xx-overview?orgId=1&from=2026-03-10T04:30:00Z&to=2026-03-10T05:00:00Z
Support Slack: https://slack.redwood/support/plato-incidents/archives/C02ABCDEF
Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-10: Received initial customer report; forwarded logs and graphs to SRE. Escalating to P1 due to streaming session drops.
Arjun Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Confirmed correlation with scheduled node drains. Creating temporary autoscaler config change to increase prewarm headroom; will monitor for 30m.
SRE-Oncall (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Temp mitigation reduced error-rate; still seeing isolated 502s on long-lived streams. Posting runbook link and will attach heap/gc traces if crash persists.
Customer (Acme AI) - 2026-03-10: Noted degraded UX during morning ET hours; asked for ETA on root cause and prevention.
Arjun Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Root-cause analysis in progress. Begin development ticket in runtime to make draining gentler (PR referenced below).
Mitigation applied: autoscaler prewarm headroom temporarily increased and scale-in throttled for high-priority shards. Rolling patch planned to adjust prioritizer fairness and runtime drain timeout. Customer notified and monitoring is stable at baseline. Follow-up engineering work scheduled.
1) Hotfix (config): increase prewarm headroom to 3 and delay aggressive scale-in for 10m windows during maintenance. Implemented 2026-03-10 05:12 UTC.
2) Code fix: runtime PR #1284 adds graceful-drain backoff to avoid SIGTERM until in-flight streams drop below threshold; ingress-prioritizer PR will add smoothing to queue weight adjustments to avoid extreme polarization. Targeted rollout to prod on 2026-03-18 behind canary.
3) Postmortem action: update maintenance runbook to ensure preemption window >= 90s or to schedule tenant-aware drains for dedicated customers.
Customer follow-up: CS emailed remediation summary and timeline; customer requested confirmation once patch is in canary.
