Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden increase in tail latency and intermittent 5xx responses after enabling a tenant-scoped optimizer feature-flag that changed batching and KV-prefetch behavior for quantized models. The flag was rolled out to a small percentage of traffic and then increased to 30% before the anomalies were noticed.

Impact:
- ~15% of requests from the customer's production traffic saw P95 latency jump from ~220ms to ~1.2s and P99 to ~3s.
- A subset of requests returned 502/504 when the serving process returned an internal error while loading quantized kernels.
- Customer reports increased error rate affecting business-critical inference pipelines.

Environment:
- Customer: Acme Analytics (dedicated, us-east cluster)
- Model: redwood/gpt-small-quant8 pinned at v2026-02-26
- Platform: Dedicated pool ID dp-acme-02, runtime version 3.4.1

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant scoped feature-flag enablement applied at 2026-03-12T09:10:00Z to toggle "optimizer_combined_mode" on for 10% traffic.
2) Traffic increased to 30% at 2026-03-12T09:40:00Z.
3) By 09:55, SLO alerts fired for latency and error rate.
4) Attempts to increase batch_size and enable kv-prefetch for quant8 were applied via config change in console.

Observed logs / links:
- Grafana request P95 dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/reqs/acme-p95
- Error traces (sample): request-id=acme-20260312-0917-3b4e, stack shows "kernel_selection_error: unsupported kernel for quant8 path"
- SRE alert runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Latency+Incident+Runbook

Immediate customer request:
They want clear, low-risk steps to revert the optimizer flag and related config changes, including any stateful caches or long-lived worker state that must be cleaned to avoid a repeat when the flag is re-enabled later.

Desired outcome:
- Restore baseline latency and error rates for affected tenant within the SLA window.
- Provide a reproducible, documented unwind procedure the customer can run with minimal service disruption.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Support: Confirmed timing of flag rollout with customer; flag was tenant-scoped and controlled through console toggles.
2026-03-12 10:28 - SRE: Observed increased kernel selection failures in serving logs for quant8 models on nodes gpux-03 and gpux-07 in dp-acme-02.
2026-03-12 11:00 - Eng (runtime): Kernel registry returned fallback path but fallback attempted an unsupported fused-attention kernel which causes an exception under current quant path.
Hypothesis: The combination of aggressive batching + kv-prefetch for quantized execution surfaces an untested kernel selection edge-case. The feature-flag enabled a different batching heuristic that increased sequence concurrency and triggered the incompatible kernel path.
Temporary mitigation already attempted: Partial traffic rollback to 10% reduced errors but latency remained elevated; full disable not yet performed at time of report.
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-12T10:15Z: Logged at customer request. Escalating to SRE and runtime engineering. Customer supplied request-id samples and console audit of flag changes.
SRE (Miguel) 2026-03-12T10:30Z: Looking into serving logs and node-level failures; tagging gpux-03/gpux-07. Will validate which processes still have the old kernel cache loaded.
Runtime Eng (Lena Cho) 2026-03-12T11:05Z: Confirmed kernel-selection exception stack. Recommending an ordered unwind: 1) disable tenant flag, 2) drain affected workers, 3) clear per-worker kernel cache (kv-store), 4) restart workers to ensure fresh kernel registry loads. Need SRE to coordinate drain and restarts for Dedicated pool.
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-12T11:30Z: Shared proposed unwind steps with customer and requested maintenance window for restarts. Customer gave permission for a rolling drain impacting up to 5% of their capacity at a time.
SRE (Miguel) 2026-03-12T12:10Z: Executed staged disable of feature-flag for tenant at 2026-03-12T12:12Z. Beginning rolling drain of dp-acme-02 workers. Monitoring metrics for improvement.
Customer (Tom Rivera - Acme) 2026-03-12T12:25Z: Confirmed they can tolerate the planned rolling drain. Asked for checklist to re-enable flag once fixed.
Resolution steps executed on 2026-03-12:
1) Disabled tenant-scoped feature-flag 'optimizer_combined_mode' via console (2026-03-12T12:12Z).
2) Performed rolling drain of dp-acme-02 worker set (max 2 workers at a time), cleared per-worker kernel cache (/var/lib/redwood/kernel_cache) and restarted runtime processes on each drained node.
3) Verified that kernel-selection exceptions ceased and P95/P99 returned to baseline within two rolling cycles.
4) Kept traffic at 5% for 30 minutes and then restored normal routing.

Follow-up actions and recommendations provided to customer:
- Do not re-enable combined optimizer mode until runtime patch is deployed (PR linked).
- If re-enabling is needed, do so behind a stricter canary (1% traffic), disable aggressive kv-prefetch, and monitor kernel-selection metrics closely.
- For tenant ops, include explicit worker drain + kernel cache clear in the rollback checklist to avoid stale kernel state.

Open follow-ups (owner):
- Runtime Eng to backport kernel-selection guard to 3.4.x (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1876) - owner: Lena Cho - ETA 2026-03-19.
- SRE to produce a short runbook snippet for dedicated pools showing how to safely clear kernel cache and drain workers - owner: Miguel Santos - ETA 2026-03-16.

Issue summary:
Customer reports that when their app loses a streaming websocket connection mid-response, their webhook-backed tool executes twice after the SDK retries the request. They use function-calling with a downstream webhook that performs a state change (creating invoices). Customer requests concise, language-specific patterns for preventing duplicate side effects while preserving streamed responses and automatic SDK retries.

Impact:
- Duplicate invoices created in customer production for ~0.1% of requests during brief network blips.
- Customer is enterprise tier and has compliance constraints around exactly-once semantics for financial operations.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod, us-east)
- SDKs: Python 0.9.8, TypeScript 1.3.2, Go 0.6.1
- Model: redwood/fast-chat-v1 pinned v2026-02-28
- Integration: webhook endpoint performing POST /invoices

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open streaming chat completion with function calling enabled and provide a tool URL as the function target.
2) During streaming, drop the client websocket for ~3s (simulate flaky network) so SDK reconnects and replays the request.
3) Observe webhook receiving two POSTs for the same logical operation; second POST runs because webhook has no idempotency key check.

Observed behavior:
- SDK retries the request automatically after connection recovery and the server re-delivers the function invocation payload.
- Downstream webhook treats each delivery as a new request and performs state update.

Expected behavior (for customer):
- Patterns and recommended changes so that duplicate delivery does not cause duplicate state changes while preserving the streaming UX and no manual disabling of SDK retries.

Temporary workaround recommended by Support:
- Add an idempotency key header on the webhook side based on conversation/message id, and persist it upstream to deduplicate.
- Disable immediate side-effect in webhook and accept a separate confirmation callback from the invoice service (two-phase commit).

Customer asks for:
- Concrete code snippets for Python/TS/Go SDKs showing headers or wrapper logic to ensure exactly-once for webhooks triggered by function-calling in streaming flows.
- Notes on when SDK will decide to retry a streamed request vs when it will fail-fast.

Initial hypothesis: SDK streaming reconnect path replays the user request (including function call) when it cannot confirm final ack from the server. SRE verified server delivered the function payload once but the client-side reconnection resulted in duplicate delivery path. Trace shows server accepted first delivery but due to client reconnect the same logical request was reissued; webhook endpoint performed a blind create. We reproduced locally by interrupting TCP and observed identical behavior. No server-side bug found so far; this is expected given current at-least-once delivery semantics for streaming reconnection. Engineering input requested on options to reduce customer blast radius and provide clearer SDK guidance.

Notes from logs: persistent connection id conn-4a1c, sequence numbers indicate replay of request envelope 42. No 5xx errors reported by serving runtime.

Recommended patterns to propose to customer: 1) Idempotency keys: include a stable operation_id in function call payload (conversation_id + message_id) and set as Idempotency-Key header to webhook; server returns 202 if already processed. 2) Two-phase approach: tool responds with a provisional response and asks customer to confirm via separate non-streamed API before committing. 3) Use 'operation_status' resource: webhook writes a record with operation_id and status PENDING then an async worker commits, deduping on operation_id. 4) SDK suggestion: expose an option to attach a user-provided idempotency_key to function-call envelopes in upcoming minor release.

Language-specific snippets to draft for customer:
- Python: middleware that computes idempotency_key = f"{conversation_id}:{message_id}" and sets header before sending to webhook; persist outcome in DB with unique index.
- TypeScript: use fetch wrapper that retries idempotent HTTP methods only if response status indicates in-progress and attach Idempotency-Key header.
- Go: accept idempotency header in handler, use database upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) to guarantee single commit.

Review feasibility of adding explicit idempotency_key field to function-calling envelope in SDKs
Consider making SDKs log when replay/retry occurs in streaming flows with a clear marker for customers
Assess whether server can return a replay-safe acknowledgment earlier in the stream to prevent client replay

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 11:21 - Customer (ScaleVision): Example webhook currently relies solely on request body to decide uniqueness; adding idempotency header is quick but we'd like canonical SDK guidance to avoid future issues.

payload.description:
Customer reports 504 Gateway Timeout when issuing a single-turn generation with an extremely long prompt (large context + large max_tokens) using streaming: connection closes before final chunks are emitted. Customer is on a Dedicated cluster in us-east. They reported this started after a spike in similar requests last week and is reproducible for one specific job id. The request uses the /v1/generate endpoint with streaming=true and max_tokens=150000. Impact: Podscribe's nightly ingestion job fails intermittently, causing downstream indexing delays and backfills.
1) Use customer API key on prod-us-east cluster. 2) POST to /v1/generate with model=redwood-open-6B-quant, streaming=true, max_tokens=150000, and a ~180k-token priming prompt (concatenated customer documents). 3) Keep TCP connection open and allow streaming chunks. 4) Observe 504 or connection reset after ~115-125s; occasional partial chunks delivered then finalizer error. Example curl provided to customer during triage: curl -i -N -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-open-6B-quant","stream":true,"max_tokens":150000,"prompt":"<very long priming text>"}'
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout or connection reset by peer. When a partial stream is returned, the final bytes are delayed then cut off. On successful-but-slow runs the finalizer queue length climbs and worker handoff latency spikes, then the connection is closed without finalization. No increased 5xx rate for other customers in the same cluster during most occurrences.
Streamed chunks continue until generation completes and finalizer emits final chunk; no client-visible 504 for requests that fit within resource quotas for Dedicated customers. If system must reject, return a clear 429 with a recommended fallback model/shorter max_tokens guidance.
Relevant logs for request_id=req_0a1b2c3d4e:
[2026-03-12T03:18:57Z] api-gateway: accept request req_0a1b2c3d4e client_ip=54.210.12.34
[2026-03-12T03:19:00Z] scheduler: queued job job_99877 priority=normal queue_pos=17
[2026-03-12T03:19:12Z] scheduler: dispatch job job_99877 -> worker pool dedicated-eu? (chosen us-east)
[2026-03-12T03:19:48Z] serving-runtime: pool-alloc-delay=36s kernel-swap=true req=req_0a1b2c3d4e model=redwood-open-6B-quant sequence_len_est=180000
[2026-03-12T03:20:30Z] kv-cache: hit_ratio=0.18 resident=22% attempting-evict=true evict_rate=78%
[2026-03-12T03:20:50Z] finalizer: queue_length=12 headroom_tokens=0 backlog_ms=13450
[2026-03-12T03:21:57Z] finalizer: emit_chunk seq=last error=deadline_exceeded connection_closed=client_reset
[2026-03-12T03:21:57Z] api-gateway: 504 Gateway Timeout req=req_0a1b2c3d4e
Additional metrics: grafana panel: https://metrics.redwood.com/d/abc123/cluster-finalizer?var=cluster=prod-us-east
Initial hypothesis: finalizer queueing + pool allocation delay caused by resource headroom exhaustion under spike of hyperlength jobs. Data points: sustained high kv-cache eviction and large pool-alloc-delay for this job; finalizer queue length correlates with 504 events in the cluster. Further checking: autoscaler logs show burst_capacity_remaining=0 at time of request; node-provisioning latency of ~28s causing delay in new worker attach. No immediate OOMs on worker; CPU on router pods spiked but not saturated. We saw several concurrent jobs with similar token budgets from the same customer window (backfill). The serving runtime stalls around kernel-swap for very long sequences — older kernel path selection causes higher mem copies leading to slower throughput; this cluster is using an older runtime image (runtime v2.14) not yet updated to the optimized kernel selection introduced in v2.18.
Combination of (a) cluster exhausted burst headroom due to multiple hyperlength jobs from the same customer, (b) scheduler allocation delay + autoscaler cooldown preventing timely worker provisioning, and (c) older serving runtime kernel path that increases CPU-bound handoff latency for very long-sequence workloads, which created a finalizer backlog and ultimately triggered gateway-level 504s.
1) Temporarily scoped rate-limit: applied per-customer concurrency cap for Podscribe to 2 concurrent hyperlength jobs to prevent further backlog. 2) Manually increased cluster burst_capacity for prod-us-east and forced a scale-up (nodes added, new workers attached). 3) Enabled fallback policy on the customer's routes to route to redwood-open-6B-quant-smaller (token-window-limited) when headroom < 5%. 4) Restarted a subset of router pods to clear TCP stale connections. These actions reduced immediate 504s and allowed most queued jobs to finish within 90s after scale-up.
Recommend customers split monolithic priming into smaller chunks and use incremental generation + rerank instead of single hyperlength generation. For now we advised Podscribe to reduce max_tokens to <= 50k or switch to a dedicated private deployment with reserved capacity for their nightly backfills. Support provided a script to chunk prompts and stitch outputs client-side.
1) Backport kernel-selection and memory-copy optimizations from runtime v2.18 to v2.14 and roll to affected Dedicated clusters. 2) Improve autoscaler heuristics to detect hyperlength job spikes and pre-warm workers when queue length and estimated sequence length exceed thresholds. 3) Add explicit API-level guardrail: return 429 with explanatory body when estimated token+context cost exceeds dynamic headroom threshold rather than letting requests queue to finalizer. 4) Update docs + quickstart with best practices for large priming workloads. Timeline: hotfix (kernel backport) targeted within 2 weeks; autoscaler heuristics in 6 weeks.
Work in progress. Immediate mitigation reduced customer impact and suggested workaround accepted by customer. Engineering is tracking kernel backport PR and autoscaler changes. Customer asked to keep ticket open until backport is deployed to their dedicated cluster and they validate nightly success for one week.

2026-03-12 07:30 UTC - SRE (Liam Chen): Scaled cluster manually and observed worker attach completed at 2026-03-12T07:47Z; finalizer queue drained. Created temporary per-customer concurrency cap. Investigating autoscaler cooldown behavior.
2026-03-13 12:15 UTC - Eng (Priya Nair): Found that runtime v2.18 kernel selection reduces memcopy for long sequences by ~35% in benchmarks. Opening backport PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2145

1) Merge and deploy backport PR to prod-us-east dedicated clusters for Podscribe (owner: Priya). 2) Implement autoscaler heuristic change and test on staging with synthetic hyperlength workload (owner: SRE team). 3) Keep ticket open; validate one week of successful nightly backfills from Podscribe; schedule a check-in on 2026-03-21.

Issue summary: BrightCart reports repeated 429 responses for production API keys across a dedicated pool beginning 2026-03-09 22:15 UTC. Impact: customer-facing inference endpoints return 429s for short bursts causing failed user requests and follow-up retries. Environment: Dedicated capacity (BrightCart dedicated pool) in us-east-1. Key observation: total token/requests quota for the tenant appeared to be depleted at times when customer traffic was low. Suspected cause: internal health-checks or probes consuming quota unexpectedly.
1) Deploy app using BrightCart's production API key against Redwood hosted endpoint in us-east-1.
2) Wait for scheduled health-check window between 22:00-23:00 UTC (customer's LB warmup).
3) Observe numerous short requests from the same API key without proper session pinning.
4) Observe 429 responses returned by Redwood within 5-10 minute windows and quota counters decreasing in Console usage pane.

Edge proxy logs: multiple 40-60ms small requests from 52.14.23.0/24 labeled 'health-check' using same API key.
2026-03-10 09:12 Support (Aisha): Customer noticed intermittent 429s starting 2026-03-09 22:15 UTC. Provided token usage screenshot and sample request IDs. Asked for rate-limit counters and recent quota activity.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:30 Customer (BrightCart - Omar): We run an autoscaling LB with health-checks every 10s during warmups. We did not expect those probes to count against API quota. Please advise.
2026-03-11 08:48 Support (Aisha): Reproduced in staging by running 8s interval health checks against staging key; observed equivalent quota drawdown. Raised INT ticket to engineering for policy review.
Initial anomaly: quota counters dropped by ~12k tokens within 10 minutes while customer reported low application traffic. Correlated timestamps with our edge-proxy and dedicated-pool LB logs; found ~600 small probe requests per minute from customer's load balancer IP range. These probes used the customer's production API key (automatically set in their LB config). Confirmed that current quota accounting is per-request and does not exclude perceived health-checks. Risk: if customers configure LB health-checks with production keys or short intervals, they may unknowingly consume quota and hit 429s.
Advise customer to: 1) rotate the prod API key and create a separate low-privilege key or internal-only key for health checks; 2) temporarily increase dedicated quota commit with account manager if needed; 3) adjust LB probe interval to >=30s until a permanent policy is in place.
Temporary mitigation applied: gateway will treat requests carrying header 'X-Health-Check: 1' from known customer LB IP ranges as out-of-band for quota accounting for BrightCart's dedicated pool. This was rolled out only to the BrightCart routing rule to avoid cross-tenant risk. Engineering to implement a configurable health-check exemption whitelist in the rate-limiter for dedicated pools. Customer informed and accepted workaround. No further 429s observed in the monitored window after mitigation.
1) Engineering: implement controlled health-check exemption feature in rate-limiter (INT-9821).
2) Product: document recommended health-check key patterns and guidance in Dev Center runbook.
3) Support: notify other dedicated tenants via customer bulletin about best practices for LB health checks and API keys.
4) Security: review whitelist risk and approve RBAC for health-check keys.
5) Billing: verify usage adjustments and issue credit if any overage occurred during the incident window.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports streaming SSE endpoint returns HTTP 200 but final JSON array is truncated (missing closing bracket) when an upstream connection rebind/redirect happens during worker draining. Impact: AtlasHealth's chat UI displays a partial JSON body and the client never receives the terminal end-event; users must refresh to get a retry. Observed behavior: 1) Server responds 200 immediately and then stream ends with EOF before closing the JSON array. 2) Edge logs show an upstream 302 redirect from A/B redirector during the final token window. 3) Resume attempts from client result in a resumed stream that duplicates earlier segments or returns an empty array depending on timing.
1) Start a long-running SSE generation session in prod-us-east against redwood-v1-medium with typical prompt length (>= 600 tokens).
2) Trigger a canary redirect at the edge (simulate A/B redirector returning 302 for the session cookie) while the model is streaming its final paragraph (within last 2-5s).
3) Observe client receives HTTP 200, a partial JSON array (missing trailing "]"), then EOF without terminal end-event.
4) Attempt a resume: client reconnects with resume_token; server either duplicates prefix segments or returns an empty array and final marker is missing.
[edge-03] 2026-03-10T14:12:21.902Z GET /sse?session=abc123 200 - upstream=10.4.12.9:8080 - referer=https://atlashealth.app
[edge-03] 2026-03-10T14:12:22.150Z upstream response: 302 redirect -> /ab-test/variant-b (set-cookie: ab=variant-b; Path=/)
[svc-gen-07] 2026-03-10T14:12:22.210Z streaming chunk: ["Patient shows improved vitals...","Recommend follow-up in 2 weeks..."] (partial)
[svc-gen-07] 2026-03-10T14:12:22.298Z connection: half-close detected, EOF without closing bracket
[edge-03] 2026-03-10T14:12:22.301Z tcp FIN from upstream during drain window
2026-03-10 15:01 - Support (Maya Thompson): Notified customer and requested HAR/HTTP trace. Asked for reproduction steps and browser/SDK version.
2026-03-10 16:22 - Customer (AtlasHealth - Jake R.): Provided browser network trace and confirmed this started after they enabled a phased redirect experiment on their CDN.
2026-03-11 09:08 - Eng (Riley Chen): Reproduced locally with a scripted redirect; captured identical truncated JSON array and missing terminal end-event. Assigned to Edge team to inspect redirect/in-flight drain interactions.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 16:10 - Support (Aisha Patel): Advised AtlasHealth temporary workaround: disable canary redirect for streaming routes or enable websocket fallback in their integration.
Hypothesis A: Edge 302 during in-flight stream causes upstream worker to start drain sequence; worker sends FIN before internal flush ensures final marker is emitted. This yields HTTP 200 with incomplete body.
Hypothesis B: The redirect sets a cookie which changes session affinity; resume_token mapping uses sticky session id that is reused for another recent session leading to offset collision and duplication on resume.
Observed: Upstream generator service does write final choice but connection close occurs between chunking and chunk flush to socket (timing window ~80-140ms).
Trace: tcpdump shows FIN after last write but before kernel send buffers drained; edge returns 200 because headers already sent.
Short term workaround provided to customer: disable the A/B redirect for SSE endpoints or switch to websocket mode to avoid HTTP redirect semantics; also suggested client-side retry logic that treats incomplete JSON as transient and re-requests completion.
Mitigation being developed: Edge patch to transform in-flight 302 into a grace-aware redirect for streaming paths: if a streaming response is in progress, delay redirect until final-marker flush or instead inject a 307 upgrade hint to preserve connection until generator confirms terminal event.
Server-side patch: generator will ensure an explicit "END_EVENT" sentinel is emitted and flushed with a blocking write prior to initiating graceful drain. Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/899
Follow-up actions: 1) Edge team to land canary for ab-router patch (PR referenced above). 2) Add monitoring for truncated JSON arrays on streaming endpoints and alert at >0.1% rate. 3) Update SSE resume logic to validate resume_token epoch and refuse non-monotonic offsets (prevents duplication).
Status: Mitigations in review (edge patch + generator flush). Customer workaround in place; monitoring and alerts planned.
Mitigations in review; customer has temporary workaround (disable redirect or use websocket fallback). Edge + serving-runtime patches pending review and canary.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (LexiSearch) reported a sudden evening rise in 5xx responses while performing a large, multi-file embeddings upload (mixed small/large payloads). Errors were observed primarily as 502/503 from the API gateway with downstream runtime exits and GPU OOMs.

Impact:
- Customer saw ~30% of embedding requests fail (5xx) for a 20-minute window starting ~2026-03-12 19:42 PDT.
- Multiple runtime workers restarted; transient GPU memory fragmentation observed by SRE.
- Customer reported degraded UX and retry storms from their client SDK.

Environment:
- Dedicated account (LexiSearch); prod cluster in us-west region; dedicated GPU pool (g4dn-like nodes) running serving-runtime v2.8.1.
- Keystore rotation was scheduled earlier that evening (automated periodic rotation).

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Bulk upload 2500 small-to-medium embedding items via multipart upload over a 1 minute window.
2) Observe initial handshakes spike as uploads begin; client retries on 5xx.
3) After ~2-3 minutes, API gateway surfaces 502/503, and streaming/async upload endpoints fail.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway returns 502/503; some 504s on long-polling operations.
- Runtime processes log OOM and SIGABRT around the same timeframe.
- System metrics: TLS handshake queue depth at edge-proxy increased x6 above baseline; keystore read latencies spiked from 5ms -> 120ms. Hedged retry count doubled for affected tenant.

Expected behavior:
- Bulk uploads should be rate-limited/queued with graceful backpressure and no runtime crashes. Keystore rotations should not meaningfully increase handshake latencies.

Relevant logs (snippets):
- api-gw: "WARN handshake_delay keystore_read=118ms tenant=lexisearch request_id..."
- proxy: "accept_queue_depth=732 baseline=120"
- runtime: "GPU OOM at step 15432, mem_avail=0.1GB, fragmentation=high"

Immediate customer impact: High — embeddings ingestion pipeline degraded and client SDKs retried aggressively, amplifying load.
Timeline and findings:
- 2026-03-12 19:45 PDT: Customer reports failures. Support triaged and opened this ticket.
- 19:48 PDT: SRE pulled edge-proxy and keystore metrics; observed periodic keystore rotation at 19:40 that coincided with handshake latency spike.
- 19:52 PDT: Runtime team correlated worker restarts with increased effective concurrency from hedged retries; CPU threads blocked waiting on TLS handshake I/O.
- Hypotheses tested:
  * H1: Billing/tenant misconfiguration causing burst not honored -> ruled out (tenant limits honored).
  * H2: Keystore rotation causing synchronous blocking I/O on accept path -> supported by spike in keystore_read latency and increased handshake queue.
  * H3: Mixed-size multipart embedding batch caused memory oversubscription on runtimes -> partially supported by runtime memory fragmentation metrics.
- Root cause (convergence): Synchronous keystore reads during rotation caused elevated TLS handshake latencies at the edge-proxy, which increased connection setup time. Customer SDK hedged retry behavior (retry on early 5xx) produced sudden concurrent retries that amplified traffic to the API gateway and downstream serving runtimes. The combined effect led to runtime processes exceeding memory thresholds (OOM) due to an unfavorable mix of embedding sizes and KV cache pressure, producing the observed 5xx wave.
- Corroborating evidence: Keystore rotation logs + TLS handshake histograms + increased hedged_retry counts from ingress tracing.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support instructed LexiSearch to throttle client SDK concurrency and enable client-side exponential backoff (within 10 minutes).
- SRE applied a short-lived ingress rate cap on the tenant route (20% reduction) to let runtimes recover.
- Rolled keystore rotation forward to complete and disabled synchronous blocking reads in the edge-proxy path (toggle applied via feature-flag: keystore_async_reads=true).

Follow-up actions (postmortem items):
- Engineering to implement asynchronous keystore reads for edge handshake path (PR referenced below).
- Runtime to harden memory accounting for mixed-size embed batches (prefer fixed buffer pooling).
- Developer docs: advise customers on SDK hedged retry configuration and recommended client-side backoff for bulk-embedding uploads.

2026-03-12 19:50 - Support (Leah Kim): Logged initial alert from customer. Collected request_ids and asked for sample payloads and client SDK version.
2026-03-12 19:58 - SRE (Omar Sanchez): Observed keystore rotation started at 19:40. Keystore read latency spike aligns with handshake queue growth. Increasing ingress accept queue and TLS backlog. Gathering pprof from edge-proxy.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 20:25 - Support (Ava Martinez): Requested LexiSearch to apply client-side throttling config (concurrency -> 8, backoff base 200ms). They implemented and reported partial recovery within ~4 minutes.
2026-03-12 21:05 - SRE (Rohan Gupta): Applied temporary ingress rate cap for tenant route and toggled keystore_async_reads feature-flag. Handshake latencies returned to baseline; no further runtime OOMs for the tenant. Monitoring continues.
2026-03-13 09:00 - PM (Evan Liu): Postmortem scheduled; assigned engineering action items. Customer success will follow up regarding SDK best-practices.
Root cause: synchronous keystore reads during scheduled rotation caused TLS handshake slowdowns which, combined with customer-side hedged retry behavior and a dense mixed-size embedding workload, amplified ingress leading to runtime memory OOMs and 5xx errors.
Fix applied:
- Temporary: ingress rate cap and client-side throttle mitigations to stabilize customer traffic.
- Permanent: merged PR to make keystore reads asynchronous on the edge-proxy (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321). Runtime change to improve buffer pooling for embedding uploads scheduled for v2.9.0.
Customer communication:
- Informed LexiSearch of root cause and mitigations on 2026-03-13. Provided recommended SDK settings and a runbook for bulk uploads.
Follow-ups (owner and ETA):
- ENG-Edge (Rohan Gupta): Ensure keystore_async_reads rolled into canary and GA by 2026-03-20.
- ENG-Runtime (Nina Patel): Buffer pooling improvements for embeddings targeted for 2026-03-28 release.
- Docs (Leah Kim): Publish SDK hedged-retry guidance and bulk-upload best practices by 2026-03-18.
Shared a short incident summary with the customer on 2026-03-13 and recommended immediate SDK throttling.
Check other tenants' keystore rotation timing for correlated spikes; evaluate making keystore rotation staggered across edge fleet to avoid global handshake waves. Add invocation-based circuit-breaker for hedged retries at the gateway level to prevent amplification.
payload.summary: Evening 5xx elevation: bulk-embedding upload exposed handshake-throttle + hedged-retry amplification causing runtime OOMs

payload.description:
Issue summary: A Beacon Health Tech admin reported that scheduled dashboard exports (CSV and PDF) produced last week contain annotations that were created by API keys which the customer had already revoked.

Observed behavior: Saved annotations and their metadata (creator identifier and route) created with revoked API keys are still present in scheduled export files generated after the revocation. Annotations are visible in the exported artifacts but not visible in the customer console UI for the same time range and dashboard.

Expected behavior: Exports should only include annotations that are currently visible to the org (i.e., annotations created by active users or active API keys or annotations that have not been soft-deleted/expired) and must respect API key revocations and annotation retention policies.
Customer reports potential exposure of historical annotation metadata tied to revoked credentials. This is a privacy/security concern for enterprise customers and may contravene their internal compliance rules. A single customer impacted so far, scheduled exports produced nightly for 10+ dashboards. No evidence of leaked PII in annotations yet but metadata (api_key_id, creator) is present.
1) Create API key (api-key-xyz) and use it to POST annotations on dashboard A via console exporthook for time range T-1d.
2) Revoke API key via Console > Settings > API keys (immediately mark revoked).
3) Wait for next scheduled export run for dashboard A (nightly job).
4) Download the generated CSV/PDF and inspect annotations section; revoked api-key-created annotations appear in the export although they are not visible when viewing the dashboard in the UI.
5) Compare annotations list via API /annotations endpoint (filtered by active=true) and exported file — mismatch observed.
export-service logs (2026-03-04T23:00:05Z): INFO scheduled-export job started for org=beacon-health id=exp-20260304-2300
export-service join query preview: SELECT a.id, a.creator_id, a.api_key_id, a.visible FROM annotations a LEFT JOIN api_keys k ON a.api_key_id = k.id WHERE a.dashboard_id = 'dash-789' AND a.ts BETWEEN ...
note: in preview query results, rows with k.state = 'revoked' still returned because annotations table stores api_key_id and export pipeline does not re-evaluate key state; TTL cleanup job is scheduled weekly (ttl-annotations-cleanup).

Additional notes:
2026-03-07 11:05 - Security (Dana Cohen): Recommended conservative mitigation: mask api_key_id column in exports until fix deployed and run backfill to regenerate exports for affected orgs. Customer prefers removal rather than masking.
1) Root cause hypothesis: Export pipeline relies on a materialized view (annotations_mv) for performance. The MV retains annotation rows referencing api_key_id values even after keys are revoked because revocation state is in api_keys table and MV is not refreshed on key update. Scheduled export job queries annotations_mv without joining to api_keys table to check current state. Thus revoked-key annotations are exported until ttl-cleanup refresh removes them.
2) Secondary issue: scheduled-export job uses snapshot timestamp semantics (snapshot_ts = job_start - 5m) which allowed a race where recent revocations were not visible to the snapshot read window, compounding the MV staleness.
3) Frequency: Confirmed with export logs — affected runs from 2026-03-03 to 2026-03-05 (until temporary patch applied in staging).
4) Security assessment: annotations do not include PII in supplied examples, but api_key identifiers and creator_uuid are present and considered sensitive for customers with strict credential handling policies.
Temporary mitigation: Added export query predicate to join with api_keys and only include annotations where api_keys.state = 'active' OR annotations.api_key_id IS NULL. This was deployed to staging and validated against Beacon's sample.
Planned permanent fix: 1) Update export-service to always join live api_keys table and avoid relying solely on annotations_mv for security-sensitive fields. 2) Reduce annotations_mv refresh window for orgs with scheduled exports to near-real-time or implement change-propagation for api_key state updates. 3) Run a one-off backfill job to regenerate exports for orgs with scheduled-export runs during revocation window (2026-03-02 -> 2026-03-05).

Issue summary:
NimbleFinance reported that after a scheduled control-plane failover (eu-west primary -> eu-west-failover) their tenant administrators lost admin privileges in the private deployment. Affected users could authenticate but RBAC group memberships were not applied, causing 403s on admin routes and failing scheduled ingestion jobs that use delegated admin tokens.

Impact:
- Tenant admin UI shows 'Insufficient permissions' for multiple users (5 admins affected).
- Daily scheduled ingestion jobs failed (5/5) over the failover window.
- Customer-facing apps with webhook provisioning experienced delayed processing (~3 hours).

Environment:
- Private control plane running v2025.11.3 on customer-managed VMs behind an on-prem edge proxy.
- LDAP: Microsoft AD (on-prem), single forest, referral chasing enabled.
- Failover executed using documented failover playbook at 2026-03-10T02:12:00Z.

Perform control-plane failover per runbook (primary -> standby) in eu-west on a deployment that uses LDAP with referral-chasing enabled.
Trigger a full resync of group bindings (Config > Auth > Sync Groups) or allow automatic post-failover sync.
Attempt to perform an admin-only action (tenant settings, user impersonation) as an admin user whose account is bound by an LDAP group with a DN containing a '#' character in the bind DN upstream metadata.
Observe 403 responses on admin API and missing group entries in /admin/tenants/{id}/bindings.
Check LDAP connector logs and control-plane auth logs for parsing errors.
2026-03-10T02:14:12Z auth-svc ERROR: group-sync failed for tenant 'nimblefinance' - ldap bind DN parse error: unexpected token '#' in DN 'CN=Sync Service#01,OU=Service Accounts,DC=nimble,DC=local'
2026-03-10T02:14:13Z ldap-connector WARN: referral-chase starting for base 'DC=partners,DC=corp'
2026-03-10T02:14:13Z ldap-connector ERROR: startTLS: bind failed: invalid DN format
2026-03-10T02:15:40Z control-plane INFO: user 'alice.n@nimblefinance' authenticated (id=10042) but effective groups=[] - expected groups=['tenant-admin']
Sample API trace: POST /admin/impersonate 403 {
  'request_id': 'req-9b2f7',
  'user': 'alice.n@nimblefinance',
  'reason': 'missing required role'
}
Support (Ava Patel) 2026-03-10T03:05:12Z: Received initial report from NimbleFinance via support@. Customer says failover completed and then tenant admins lost admin privileges. Asked for LDAP connector and auth logs; requested last successful sync timestamp.
Customer (NimbleFinance - Jose Mendez) 2026-03-10T03:22:01Z: Provided LDAP config snippet and indicated the service account DN has a '#' character because their onboarding script appends an environment tag (e.g., 'Sync Service#01'). They confirmed the DN works from their AD tools.
SRE (Ravi Sharma) 2026-03-10T04:45:30Z: Reproduced bind DN parse error in staging when LDAP connector hits an unescaped '#'. When referral chasing is enabled the connector re-encodes/refollows referrals and triggers a path where DN parsing uses our internal DN tokenizer which treats '#' as a comment/start-of-escaped-value. Filing with infra to hotfix parser tolerant behavior.
Support (Ava Patel) 2026-03-11T09:12:14Z: Applied short-term workaround for customer: modified their LDAP connector configuration to disable referral chasing and restarted connector; initiated manual full group resync; admins regained permissions within ~8 minutes. Customer confirmed scheduled jobs retried successfully.
Engineering (Samantha Liu) 2026-03-12T14:28:02Z: Root cause confirmed: LDAP DN tokenizer in private-deploy runtime incorrectly treats unescaped '#' as a DN comment per RFC2253 edge-case when referral-chasing codepath uses alternative parsing library. Patch PR prepared to normalize/escape '#' in bind DN and to accept both escaped and unescaped forms when reading upstream metadata.
Hypothesis 1: Edge proxy rewrites DN or header, inserting unescaped characters -> verified false: packet captures show DN header intact across proxy.
Hypothesis 2: Referral chasing causes alternate codepath in LDAP connector that uses a third-party DN parser with stricter grammar -> reproduced locally and confirmed. Third-party parser rejects '#' unless escaped as '\#'.
Correlation: Tenants using referral-chasing + service account DNs with '#' impacted; tenants without '#' or with escaped '#' were not impacted.
Logs show successful authentication but group membership empty (groups=[]). That indicates bind succeeded for authentication path but group enumeration (separate bind) failed in the connector's referral-return path.
Tested workaround: disable referral-chasing -> group sync proceeds (slower) because connector fetches local partitions only but succeeds because DN parsing codepath doesn't run.
LDAP connector's referral-chase codepath uses a stricter DN parser that rejects unescaped '#' in bind DNs. During failover a connector restart triggered a resync using referral-chasing, exposing the parser mismatch and dropping group resolution leading to lost RBAC bindings.
Short-term: Disabled referral-chasing in the customer's LDAP connector config and performed manual full group resync; verified tenancy admin privileges restored and scheduled jobs retried successfully.
Long-term: Engineering has merged a patch that normalizes/accepts '#' in bind DNs and updates the referral-chase parser. Patch will be included in v2026.04.1 for private deployments. Recommended customer follow-up: re-enable referral-chasing after patch rollout and run a scheduled group sync.
Rollout notes: Patch requires connector restart; rolling upgrade plan provided to customer to avoid prolonged window. Scheduled patch window proposed: 2026-03-20 02:00-03:00 UTC.
ENG: Monitor post-patch customer telemetry for 72 hours after enabling referral-chasing (owner: Samantha Liu)
SUPPORT: Confirm customer's IAM runbook includes escaping recommendations for generated service account DNs (owner: Ava Patel)
SRE: Add a health check to detect DN-parse failures during group-sync and alert early (owner: Ravi Sharma)

Issue summary:

Customers on a Dedicated VPC (AtlasDocs Inc) started reporting intermittent 502/503 responses from Redwood's API gateway beginning 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC. The error rate was concentrated on routes bound to the customer's dedicated pool and coincided with elevated CPU on a subset of serving runtimes in the us-west-2 footprint. Impact: production requests failing (5xx) and degraded tail latency for chat/embedding endpoints.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests returned 502/503 across the customer's dedicated route for a 3 hour window (peak).
- Several long-lived streaming sessions were reset.
- Customer reported degraded service quality and rising error alerts.

Environment:
- Dedicated VPC deployment for AtlasDocs Inc (dedicated GPU pool).
- Region: us-west-2.
- Routes: /v1/chat and /v1/embeddings pinned to dedicated pool.

Observed start: 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC (first customer alert).
1) Send sustained concurrent requests to pinned dedicated route (chat/embeddings) from within customer's region.
2) Observe increased 502/503 responses after sustained DNS lookup failures (simulated by blocking resolver response).
3) Observe runtime CPU climbing and API gateway backlog.

Notes: reproducing requires VPC networking conditions matching customer's resolver latency. Test harness used: internal load-generator -> dedicated pool route with 100 rps sustained for 5+ minutes.
- APIGW logs: repeated upstream connect_timeout and upstream response timeout entries (502/503). Sample: "upstream connect error: connection timed out".
- Runtime metrics: kernel scheduler latency + CPU sys time spike on runtime hosts (threads stuck in getaddrinfo/backoff).
- DNS resolver metrics: resolver RTT spiked from 10ms -> 600ms and occasional NXDOMAIN-like timeouts.
- Connection queue length on runtime proxy increased by factor 8.
- SLO telemetry: 95th latency rose from 180ms -> 1.4s during window.
- Packet captures: repeated DNS retransmissions between runtime hosts and customer-managed resolver IPs.
- Relevant logs: /var/log/redwood/runtime/*.log attached to internal investigation (pointer: slack #support thread thread-146789).
Initial hypothesis: upstream runtime crashes or GPU overload. After correlating metrics, evidence pointed to network/DNS resolver latency inside customer's VPC: runtimes were blocking on name resolution for remote dependencies (internal service discovery + keystore lookups) causing thread starvation and higher syscall CPU.

Steps investigators took:
- Correlated APIGW error graphs with DNS RTT dashboard (internal dns-observability). Peaks align within 30s.
- Pulled stack traces from a runtime host during a spike: threads stuck in getaddrinfo and repeated libc resolver retries.
- Confirmed resolver IPs were the customer's VPC resolvers (not our managed cloud resolver).
- Validated that when resolver RTT>250ms, runtime proxy reported accept queue saturation and started returning upstream 502s.
- Checked autoscaler: no GPU OOMs or driver resets. GPU and memory usage were nominal.

Hypothesis refined: customer-side DNS degradation introduced high blocking latency in the serving runtime process causing connection backlog -> APIGW 5xx wave.

Temporary mitigations tested:
- Increased runtime resolver timeout and enabled a local stub caching resolver on runtime hosts in a canary to reduce blocking impact (reduced error rate in canary).
- Adjusted APIGW hedged retry policy to reduce immediate retries to the same upstream during detected resolver latency windows.
Workaround and ongoing work:
1) Short-term workaround: deployed local stub-caching resolver on all dedicated runtime hosts serving AtlasDocs traffic (completed 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC). This reduced blocking on getaddrinfo and eliminated the transient 5xx wave for the customer.
2) Customer reverted DNS appliance firmware (2026-03-11 03:15 UTC) which resolved the root cause of high resolver RTT.
3) Medium-term action: add defensive local resolver stub + circuit-breaker for blocking name resolution in runtime (PR created).
4) Postmortem planned: Confluence page linked below.

Status: customer service restored. Rolling change to add local resolver by default to dedicated runtimes in progress (owner: Diego Ramos).

Additional notes:
AtlasDocs (Customer): Confirmed they performed a firmware update on the DNS appliance overnight. They're investigating and will revert if needed.
Diego Ramos: Deployed local stub resolver on two canary runtime hosts in us-west-2 and observed error rate drop from 12% -> 0.8% for pinned route during 30m load test. Will coordinate broader mitigation plan with infra team.
payload.summary: Dedicated VPC DNS resolver latency causing API-GW 5xx and runtime CPU spike

Hypothesis: short-lived connection churn + new worker warmups cause repeated GPU memory map faults and UVM thrashing under the current kernel scheduling; increases host CPU/GPU scheduler contention and causes runtime grpc failures.

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-01 19:20 UTC LexiAI reported a persistent elevated 5xx error rate (~3-6% vs normal <0.3%) for short-text generation endpoints. Errors appeared as 502/503 from the API gateway and downstream runtime grpc failures. Impact: Customer production traffic experienced degraded success rate and increased tail latency; user retries amplified load. Environment: prod | us-east; Dedicated tenant on shared runtime pool; models: redwood-3b-v1 (primary), open-llama-13b (fallback). Steps to reproduce: 1) Send sustained concurrent short-gen requests (50-80 RPS) to /v1/generate with keepalive enabled. 2) Observe gateway 5xx error rate rising in 15-30m window during high connection churn and at ~10m intervals when ingress keepalive rotation occurs. Observed metrics & logs: - API gateway 502/503 spikes align with 10m keepalive rotation TTL at the fronting proxy. - Runtime pod logs show repeated 'uvm_page_fault' and 'gpu-driver-reset' traces at the same timestamps. - Kernel dmesg on host showed GPU UVM pagefault queues bloating followed by driver recovery. - Autoscaler briefly scaled up, then some new workers failed readiness due to kvcache lock acquisition timeouts. Initial customer-facing mitigation applied: support recommended temporarily increasing ingress keepalive from 600s -> 3600s and reducing connection churn. This lowered immediate error-floor.

Additional notes:
Metric correlation: 502/503 spikes align to 10m fronting proxy keepalive rotation (TTL=600s) and cluster worker churn windows.
Host-level evidence: kernel dmesg shows UVM page fault queue growth and 'NVIDIA UVM: kill process' style driver recoveries in narrow windows coincident with keepalive rotation.
Runtime traces: grpc errors during kvcache lock waits (>= 250ms) and 'prefetch cancelled' messages for tenants undergoing fanout.
Autoscaler behavior: Scale-up happened but new pods failed readiness due to extended kvcache init time, amplifying connection pressure on existing pods.
Hypothesis: Combination of ingress connection churn + parallel worker warmups causes repeated UVM pagefault storms; kernel/driver then issues GPU resets, running pods lose in-flight requests producing 502/503 and runtime exits.
Deployed a two-part fix: (1) immediate mitigation - increased ingress keepalive and enabled socket reuse to reduce connection churn; (2) permanent runtime fix - staggered GPU warmup + kvcache acquisition backoff and a defensive UVM-fault threshold to trigger lightweight model-variant fallback. Both changes rolled to prod 2026-03-03. Customer reports error-rate back to baseline. Follow-up: SRE to monitor UVM fault metrics for 72h, Runtime Eng to add additional low-level metrics and a long-term plan to tune kernel UVM parameters or provide tenancy isolation guidance.
SRE: Monitor uvmpagefault_rate and kvcache_wait_ms for 72 hours; escalate if 5xx > 0.5% for tenant.
Runtime Eng: Implement additional diagnostic counters for UVM mappings and publish guidance for dedicated workloads in runbook.
Product: Communicate to LexiAI summary and recommended tenant configuration (connection reuse, pinned capacity) to avoid recurrence.
Infra: Evaluate kernel parameter tuning and NVIDIA driver recommendations (defer to infra schedule).

payload.description:
Customer reports repeated duplicate function/tool executions when their orchestrator (TypeScript SDK) issues a function call and the downstream webhook (Go service) confirms execution. The duplicate runs occur after automatic retries — confirmations appear to be dropped/mismatched at the Redwood platform because the confirmation payload's fingerprint does not match the idempotency key generated by the original request.
Acme Health is observing duplicated patient-record enrichment jobs (side effects are non-idempotent) in production. Approx 1.7% of inbound function calls for their busiest route have executed twice in the last 24 hours, creating billing and data integrity issues. Customer has paused a subset of traffic and requests priority help.
1) Use ts-sdk v1.12.3 to create a streamed chat that issues a function call with a nested JSON payload (objects with 3+ levels and map-like keys).
2) The TS orchestrator computes an idempotency fingerprint and sends the request to Redwood via POST /v1/chat/completions with header 'Idempotency-Key: <fingerprint>'.
3) Redwood dispatches funcall to customer webhook (Go service using go-sdk v0.9.7) and the Go service executes the side-effect, then POSTs the confirmation back to /v1/callbacks with a JSON body that includes the original function response payload and a confirmation field.
4) Observe on retry (either client retry or Redwood retry due to 200->504 transitional path) that the confirmation is not associated with the original Idempotency-Key and Redwood executes the function a second time.
5) Repro is intermittent but increases when payloads include empty arrays and when the webhook's Go runtime serializes the confirmation using encoding/json with default settings.
6) Customer attached minimal repro harness under an anonymized token and logs in their support bundle.

[2026-03-11T02:14:03Z] INFO dispatch func_call id=fc_4b9a header Idempotency-Key=hash:0x7b3df
[2026-03-11T02:14:04Z] INFO webhook POST /callbacks status=200 body={"result":{"name":"enrich","payload":{"meta":{},"items":[]}},"confirmed_for":"hash:0x7b3df"}
[2026-03-11T02:14:05Z] WARN idempotency confirmation mismatch id=fc_4b9a expected=hash:0x7b3df received=hash:0x1a9c0
[2026-03-11T02:14:05Z] INFO retrying func_call id=fc_4b9a attempt=2

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 10:00 Customer (Acme Health): Confirmed they recently upgraded to go-sdk v0.9.7 and added a middleware that reserializes webhook confirmation using a standard encoder (no key sorting). Asked for mitigation while Redwood teams investigate.
Root-cause hypothesis: mismatch between how the TS SDK canonicalizes nested JSON prior to hashing (it sorts object keys deterministically) and how customer webhook reserializes confirmation payload (Go encoding/json does not guarantee key order). The platform associates confirmations by computing a fingerprint from confirmation body; when ordering differs the computed fingerprint differs and matches fail.
Reproducer: local harness using randomized map insertion order in Go reproduced mismatch ~15/100 runs for deep-nested maps with empty arrays and nulls.
Alternate hypothesis ruled out: network truncation and header splitting were checked and not present in the sample traces.
Related SDK versions observed in traces: ts-sdk v1.12.3 (sortKeys=true), go-sdk v0.9.7 (default encoder), python-sdk v1.3.0 not implicated in initial report but later used by a subset of customer jobs.
Impact severity analysis: Because confirmations are dropped/mismatched the platform retries which causes second execution downstream. This is high-impact for non-idempotent side effects.
Temporary mitigation succeeded when customer echoed Idempotency-Key in confirmation body rather than recomputing fingerprint locally.
Platform-side quick fix: server now computes an additional confirmation lookup using raw header Idempotency-Key if present before falling back to fingerprint-of-body match. Patch deployed to prod us-east (canary) 2026-03-12 05:00 UTC; monitoring shows reduction in duplicate execs in canary zone.
Long-term fix: make canonicalization deterministic across SDKs and publish go-sdk patch to compute identical fingerprint (sort-map-keys prior to hashing) and add opt-in compatibility flags.
Test matrix: must include nested maps, arrays, nulls, and omitempty behavior across Go/TS/Python and across multiple Go encoder settings.
Linked documentation action: document recommended confirmation contract (either echo Idempotency-Key header or use deterministic canonicalization) in function-calling guides.
Customer applied a short-term middleware to include the original 'Idempotency-Key' string inside the confirmation payload as 'confirmed_for'. Recommended other customers who see this issue either echo the header in the confirmation or use a deterministic serializer in their webhook.
1) Push go-sdk v0.9.8 with deterministic canonicalizer used for computing idempotency fingerprint (target 2026-03-15).
2) Add server-side best-effort matching by raw header (deployed to canary already), roll to all regions after 48h of monitoring.
3) Update function-calling docs with explicit confirmation schema and sample middleware for Go/TS/Python.
4) Notify customer when go-sdk patch is published and offer hands-on validation for their production webhook.
5) Postmortem runbook item: add integration test to CI covering cross-SDK fingerprint compatibility.
payload.summary: JSON key ordering canonicalization mismatch across SDKs causing funcall duplicates

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer Edify.ai reports that when their browser-based client (web SDK) encounters a rapid shrink of the TCP send window (simulated on flaky mobile networks) concurrent with an opaque auth cookie rotation, the final clause of the generated stream is not returned. The server emits a half-close (FIN) path but the client-side backpressure and connection rebind cause the terminal chunk (closing punctuation + metadata) to be lost.

Impact:
- Intermittent loss of last sentence or trailing clause in streamed responses for a subset of long outputs (~>1k tokens).
- Affects a small percentage of dedicated-customer sessions in us-east under bursty mobile-proxied traffic.
- Customer-visible: generated text ends mid-sentence and no error/partial completion metadata is delivered.

Environment and context:
- Customer using dedicated capacity with reserved GPUs in us-east-1.
- SDK: redwood-js v2.8.1 (browser), WebSocket fallback to SSE for older browsers.
- Observed against model gpt-open-14b-quant pinned in customer config.
- Recent infra rollout 2026-03-10 included auth cookie rotation and an updated connection rebind path on the edge.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer + reproduced in lab):
1) Start a long generation request via web SDK with streaming enabled (expect >800 tokens).
2) While stream is in-flight, run a client-side network shaping tool to rapidly reduce the TCP send window / simulate aggressive client backpressure and momentary socket buffer exhaustion.
3) Simultaneously trigger an auth cookie refresh (server-induced rotation) so the client must rebind/reauth mid-stream.
4) Client performs reconnect; server logs indicate a half-close on the old worker and a new session begins.
5) Observe that the final clause and the terminal metadata (choice.finish_reason / end_event) are missing from the client's assembled output.

Observed behavior:
- Server worker logs show generation progressed to completion and had emitted the final tokens, but the last chunk does not arrive at the client.
- No explicit 5xx or error is surfaced to the client; connection transitions look like normal reconnect behavior.

Expected behavior:
- Client should receive terminal chunk (final sentence and metadata) even if a rebind occurs; reconnect/resume semantics should ensure tail delivery or explicit error.

Customer reproduction artifacts attached: example SDK trace, browser HAR, and sample prompt (stored in customer ticket).
Initial findings:
- Edge and worker logs correlated with customer timestamp show the generator reached EOS and emitted a terminal chunk that included finish metadata. The worker then entered half-closed state when the client send window shrank and client performed auth refresh.
- TCP traces from the customer indicate an immediate FIN from client side or abrupt socket close during backpressure; the edge retransmit path attempted to flush remaining data but connection was torn down before HTTP stream finalization.
- The new session established with rotated auth token proceeded to a fresh stream rather than resuming/pulling tail data.
- Reproduced locally with network shaping; reproduction rate ~6/50 runs when timing of window shrink + cookie rotation aligns.

Hypothesis:
- Interaction of three factors causes loss: (1) client-side aggressive send-window shrink triggers early socket close or half-close; (2) edge auth rotation forces a new session binding without a resume token handshake; (3) server's half-close handling currently relies on TCP orderly shutdown to deliver the final SSE/WS chunk into the socket buffer — when the socket is torn down mid-drain final bytes are dropped without generating an explicit post-close fetch or placing final chunk in durable resume store.

What we've checked:
- Verified worker emitted final payload and wrote to local socket buffer.
- Confirmed connection teardown originated from client side in customer traces.
- Confirmed no application-level error emitted to customer; stack treats this as a normal disconnect.

Telemetry and logs referenced:
- Edge request id: REQ-us-east-20260312-9a4f (attached)
- Worker id: WKR-1123 (attached)
- Example log lines:
  [2026-03-12T15:22:03.123Z] WKR-1123 STREAM OUT token_index=1249 "...and finally, to ensure idempotency."
  [2026-03-12T15:22:03.129Z] WKR-1123 WRITE_FLUSH bytes=32768 status=OK
  [2026-03-12T15:22:03.131Z] EDGE-9812 TCP_RST from=203.0.113.47 port=52344
  [2026-03-12T15:22:03.132Z] WKR-1123 STREAM END detected half-close=true

Next steps underway:
- Instrumentation change in runtime to track final-chunk durability: if a final chunk has been generated, persist minimal terminal envelope to resume store prior to returning 200 to edge (hotfix candidate).
- Edge policy change to hold rotated-auth rebind for a small grace window if a worker reports half-close pending final flush.
2026-03-12 | Support (Ava Chen): Customer reported missing trailing clause on multiple sessions. Provided request ids and HAR. Asked for immediate mitigation steps and SLA acknowledgement.
2026-03-12 | SRE (Diego Martínez): Confirmed we can reproduce in lab with network shaping. Probable race between socket teardown and flush. Escalating to runtime team. Assigned to Diego.
2026-03-13 | Runtime eng (Priya Kapoor): Reviewed worker code-paths; identified that final-chunk flush is best-effort and not guaranteed if socket receives RST. Suggested short-term edge grace window and longer-term durability for terminal envelope.
2026-03-14 | Support (Ava Chen): Notified customer of ongoing work and suggested client-side workaround: delay cookie rotation until stream completion where possible or use non-rotating ephemeral token for long streams. Customer testing these workarounds.
2026-03-14 | SRE (Diego Martínez): Lab hotfix branch created: runtime persists minimal final-envelope to resume-store on EOS (PR linked). Edge team evaluating grace-window behavior.
In Progress - mitigation deployed to staging and under review in prod canary. Short-term mitigations: (1) Customer advised to postpone mid-stream auth rotations where feasible; (2) Edge policy change to defer rebind by up to 500ms when worker reports half-close pending final flush (canary). Long-term: persist terminal envelope at worker and add resume-on-reconnect semantics to retrieve final chunk if a reconnect occurs within grace window.
ACTION-1: Runtime team to land PR to persist minimal final envelope on EOS (target: 2026-03-20).
ACTION-2: Edge team to implement 500ms grace window for auth rebind when half-close is reported (target: 2026-03-18).
ACTION-3: Update SDK docs with best-practice guidance for long streams and auth rotation (owner: DX team, target: 2026-03-25).
ACTION-4: Postmortem / RCA to be created after resolution with reproducer and quantification of affected sessions (owner: Support, target: 2026-03-27).

Issue summary:
VectorMetrics reported recurring p95/p99 latency spikes in production that occur in 3–7 minute windows roughly every 15 minutes. Spikes correlate with increased queue depth in the continuous batcher leading to delayed flushes and bursty GPU utilization.

Impact:
- Customer-facing inference latency p99 increases from ~180ms to 1.6–2.4s during each spike window.
- Errors: elevated 504s observed during two windows on 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-11 (customer: dedicated pool).
- Business impact: degraded UX for interactive product; customer reports reduced engagement during windows.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated cluster: pool-id vm-dedicated-us-east-7
- Region: us-east-1
- Models: open/redwood-vicuna-7b for short-chat flows; quantized/redwood-gptq-3b for embeddings fallbacks

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Run a steady multi-connection short-stream workload: 80 concurrent connections from a single tenant, steady 12 qps aggregate, prompt length 8–24 tokens, average response length 30–60 tokens.
2) Observe continuous-batcher queue depth metric and batch flush latency via /metrics/batcher.* and per-tenant trace.
3) Wait 10–20 minutes to capture oscillation window.

Observed metrics & logs:
- batcher.queue_depth (tenant vm-dedicated-us-east-7) shows sawtooth growth from 0→~320 over 3–5 minutes, then abrupt drain.
- batcher.flush_latency_p95 spikes to 900–1,800ms in the same windows.
- serving-runtime.gpu_utilization shows burst to 95% during drains and idle at ~25% between bursts.
- API gateway shows increased request queueing and occasional 504s: logs show upstream timeout after 30s in two traces.
- No corresponding OOMs, no GPU driver errors.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Increased continuous-batcher.flush_threshold to 200 for the affected pool (rolled 2026-03-12 03:40 UTC) which reduced spike magnitude by ~40% and eliminated 504s for a follow-up 6-hour window.

Notes:
- Behavior appears to be a feedback loop: higher queue depth delays flush; delayed flushes cause longer per-batch processing which increases queueing, exacerbating delay until a large batch drains and GPU is saturated.
- This is distinct from idle-linger growth; it looks like scheduler/backpressure settings plus tenant-level request burst patterns are creating resonance.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 08:25 VectorMetrics (Customer): Noticed improvement after mitigation but still seeing small p99 blips. Asking for ETA on permanent fix and whether changes affect latency for larger requests.
Collected tenant-level traces for affected requests (trace IDs attached in support system).
Profiling shows batch processing time grows nonlinearly once batch size > 128 for the quantized model due to KV cache backend contention.
Scheduler logs show adaptive backpressure was toggling between 'aggressive' and 'conservative' modes every few minutes, matching oscillation cadence.
Found correlation between a background job (tenant-side periodic health pings) and the initial queue growth; these pings are bursty and align with spike start times.
Related PRs touch flush heuristics: serving-runtime PR #3421 and batcher PR #128 — both referenced for potential fixes.
(SRE) Keep mitigation in place and extend monitoring window to 72 hours to validate stability.
(Batching Eng) Run controlled repro using tenant workload simulator with periodic small bursts and measure queue-depth thresholds (owner: Maria Chen, ETA 2026-03-17).
(Batching Eng) Prototype soft queue cap per-tenant that triggers earlier partial flushes when KV contention is detected (owner: Maria Chen, ETA prototype 2026-03-20).
(Platform) Add tenant-level metric export for burst-pattern detection to alert before oscillations (owner: Platform Observability, ETA 2026-03-24).
(Support) Coordinate with VectorMetrics about controlled window for testing and notify about possible small regression for long-sequence cold-starts.
Mitigation: flush_threshold increased to 200 for the affected dedicated pool which reduced spike amplitude and eliminated timeouts in the short-term. Permanent fix pending: implement soft per-tenant queue cap and adjust adaptive backpressure to avoid mode flapping. Customer notified and monitoring extended.
Increase continuous-batcher.flush_threshold or reduce per-tenant concurrency; schedule tenant-side burst smoothing. Workaround applied for this customer.
Postmortem to be created if spikes recur after mitigation window expires (owner: Ethan Walker).
If prototype soft-cap reduces p99 in test, schedule rollout in canary and then to all dedicated pools with rollback plan.

Issue summary: Customer requests a compact, chronologically ordered audit export (CSV/NDJSON) that is SQL-ready with a detailed column crosswalk mapping Redwood audit fields to common relational columns. They also request a SOC2-oriented evidence checklist showing how the export satisfies logging retention, ordering, tamper-evidence, and per-tenant pseudonymization requirements.

Impact: Customer (Aurelia Payments) needs the dataset for an imminent SOC2 audit in two weeks. Without a curated sample and a field-to-column mapping, their auditors cannot validate retention and event provenance. This is time-sensitive for contract renewal.

Environment: production account (customer-managed VPC). Region: eu-west. Export target: S3 presigned bundle.

Requested deliverables: 1) One compact CSV sample (max 10k rows) covering a 24-hour window across March 1, 2026, UTC, 2) SQL-ready column crosswalk (CSV header -> SQL column types and sample SELECT statements), 3) SOC2 evidence checklist (which fields prove retention, ordering, non-repudiation, HMAC manifest), 4) Playbook notes for timezone normalization and resume tokens for auditors to replay events.

Customer-provided context: They require deterministic ordering (UTC timeline), per-row HMAC or checksum, pseudonymized user IDs (reversible by escrow) and a mapping that shows which fields contain PII and how redaction/pseudonymization was applied.
1) Support console -> Exports -> New Export -> Select 'Audit: compact sample' template.
2) Select time range 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-01T23:59:59Z, set region eu-west, output format CSV with headers.
3) Choose 'pseudonymize' = reversible (HSM-backed) and 'include_hmac_manifest' = true.
4) Request via API: POST /v1/admin/exports with body {"template":"compact-audit-sample", "params":{"start":...}} and await S3 presigned URL.

Expected: single CSV file in S3 named aurelia-sample-20260301.csv plus aurelia-sample-20260301.manifest.json (manifest contains HMACs and resume token). Rows ordered by event_timestamp_utc ascending and timezone normalized to UTC.

Observed: Support generated a sample but observed timestamps in some rows use local timezone offsets (CEST) for events around 2026-03-01T01:00:00+01:00 which causes ordering anomalies. Manifest HMAC present.

Export job id: export-6f9b2c (generated 2026-03-12T18:02:13Z). S3 object: s3://redwood-aurelia-exports/prod/eu-west/export-6f9b2c/aurelia-sample-20260301.csv. Manifest: s3://.../aurelia-sample-20260301.manifest.json.
Sample row excerpt (CSV): "event_id,event_timestamp,event_type,tenant_id,user_id,payload"
"e-9f3a,2026-03-01T02:15:00+01:00,model.request,t-443,uid-XXXX,{...}"
Hash verification: manifest.hmacs[e-9f3a] = OK. Ordering check: row 18 timestamp 2026-03-01T00:58:00Z appears after row 19 timestamp 2026-03-01T01:05:00+01:00 when interpreted naively (string sort).
1) Reproduced export in support tenant and observed mixed timestamp representations (some events stored with timezone offsets preserved; others normalized to Z). Root cause hypothesis: ingestion-time metadata included original event timezone and our export pipeline conditionally preserved offsets when source_event.tz present. 2) Manifest generation uses canonical UTC conversion for HMAC inputs, so HMACs are consistent even when CSV shows offsets. 3) Ordering anomalies stem from consumers doing lexicographic sort on the textual timestamp instead of parsing ISO offset. 4) Immediate workaround: regenerate export with explicit parameter `normalize_timestamps_to_utc=true`. This was tested and produced uniformly Z-suffixed timestamps. 5) Engineering follow-up: add schema-version header and explicit `timestamp_normalization` flag to export API to prevent implicit behavior.
Support (Marco Lopez) 2026-03-12: "We ran the export and confirmed manifest HMACs verify. Ordering anomalies due to mixed timestamp formats — recommending UTC normalization flag."

Customer (Elena Martinez, Aurelia) 2026-03-13: "Thanks — can you also include a SQL snippet that shows how an auditor can deduplicate by event_id and reconstitute ordering using the resume_token?"

Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-13: "Planned: attach SQL-ready crosswalk and two sample queries (one for ordering/dedup, one for PII mapping). ETA for attachments: 2026-03-14 EOD. Engineering ticket to standardize export header created (INT-33099)."
Workaround delivered: regenerated an export with `normalize_timestamps_to_utc=true` and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-aurelia-exports/prod/eu-west/export-6f9b2c/normalized/aurelia-sample-20260301.csv and corresponding manifest. Provided SQL-ready crosswalk (attached as CSV) and sample queries: 1) ORDER BY event_timestamp_utc, 2) dedupe using ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY event_id ORDER BY event_timestamp_utc DESC). Provided SOC2 evidence checklist mapping: retention_policy->retention.metadata, ordering->manifest.resume_token, non-repudiation->manifest.hmacs, pseudonymization->pseudonymization.key_id & rotation statements.

Follow-ups: Engineering task INT-33099 to add export header `x-export-schema-version: 2026-03-14-v1` and API param `timestamp_normalization` (assigned to infra team). Security requested HSM attestation documents — escalated to Security Ops (SEC-1018).

Case status: Deliverables provided to customer; awaiting auditor confirmation. Keep ticket open until auditor signs off or until 2026-03-18, at which point we'll follow up.
