payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-lived streaming requests (SSE) intermittently finish with the final choice/token missing after an intermediate network path change. The behaviour appears when the customer traffic traverses a CDN/edge layer that performs multipath replay/failover.

Impact:
- Partial responses: finalizing token or end-of-stream marker is not delivered to the client ~3-6% of long-running streams for this customer.
- Customer application observes 'incomplete final sentence' and sometimes shows a retry UI.
- Affects production traffic for Streamline Health (enterprise dedicated capacity).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (customer using enterprise dedicated capacity behind customer-configured CDN), production, us-east region.
- Model: redwood-vicuna-13b non-quantized.

Steps to reproduce (observed with customer):
1) Initiate streaming generation (SSE) for ~30-90s responses via customer's edge (their CDN + internal multipath proxy).
2) Induce intermittent path failover on the edge (simulated by customer: bring down one POP or have CDN re-route).
3) Client receives stream chunks but final terminal event ("[DONE]"-style event) is not delivered; last few tokens are missing or truncated.

Observed behaviour:
- The runtime logs show the server emitted final token(s) and an EOS control frame, but on the customer-side the SSE stream ends without the terminal event.
- In several traces the proxy replays buffered data from a different backend path; sequence ordering is different and the reassembly logic on the client de-duplicates or drops fragments believed to be duplicates.
- Reconnection attempts from the client either resume and duplicate earlier tokens, or start a fresh stream with missing completion.

Expected behaviour:
- Final token(s) and terminal event should be delivered in-order to the client regardless of transient edge path failover. Replays must not cause drop of the terminal chunk.

Logs / evidence attached:
- Customer-provided TCP captures and CDN event logs (timestamped).
- Server trace (trace_id: trace-20260310-8772) showing emit of final EOS frame at 2026-03-10T15:21:13Z.
- Edge logs showing path switch at 2026-03-10T15:21:13.120Z and a subsequent buffered chunk replay.
- Example client SSE capture (provided by customer) missing terminal event.

Workaround attempted by customer:
- Enabling sticky sessions on their CDN reduced frequency of occurrence to <0.5% but did not eliminate the issue.
- Switching to direct connectivity (bypassing CDN) shows stable streams.

Notes:
- Customer is on an enterprise SLA and requests a root cause and remediation plan.

Initial triage by Support: correlated server-side trace with customer edge logs; server emitted EOS but client did not receive it. SRE hypothesis: multipath replay can inject out-of-order fragments or replay buffered partial writes that confuse client reassembly and cause client-side dedupe logic to drop the final frame.

SRE findings (2026-03-11):
- Several flows show identical chunk payloads replayed with different TCP sequence ranges when the edge switched origin. The runtime sends final EOS as a small control frame immediately after last token; if replayed payload omits the EOS or arrives before/after due to reordering, the client-side SSE parser can consider stream terminated without terminal marker.
- Observed HTTP/2 + ALPN interactions on customer's proxy that coalesced writes and changed chunk boundary alignment.

Engineering analysis (2026-03-12):
- Runtime currently relies on connection-level ordering guarantees; there is no per-choice monotonic sequence id in streaming payloads to allow safe reassembly across path changes.
- Client implementations tested drop fragments that appear as duplicates if they share identical payload and are flagged with earlier offsets; this interacts poorly with multipath replay semantics.

Temporary mitigation applied (2026-03-13):
- Advised customer to enforce session affinity / sticky sessions at CDN level (confirmed reduction).
- Support applied temporary CDN rule to avoid multipath replay for a subset of affected prefixes during highest traffic windows.

Longer-term fix proposed:
- Add lightweight per-stream monotonic sequence identifiers in streaming frames (runtime change) so client-side reassembly can deterministically order and accept final frame even after replay.
- Add defensive behavior in SDKs to accept an EOS event if it follows within N ms of last seen token even when payload similarity suggests duplication.
2026-03-10: Customer (Streamline Health) - 'We've got ~4% of long streams in production ending mid-sentence. Our UX shows 'incomplete summary' and we traced it to missing final SSE event. Attached captures.'
2026-03-10: Support (Maya Chen) - 'Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE for trace correlation. Please provide a server-side trace_id if possible.'
2026-03-11: SRE (Aisha Patel) - 'Correlated with trace_id trace-20260310-8772. Server emitted EOS. Edge shows POP switch ~120ms after last token. Suspect multipath replay at CDN.'
2026-03-12: Engineering (Ethan Rivera) - 'Confirmed lack of per-frame sequencing makes reassembly brittle across path changes. Working on a runtime patch and SDK defense.'
2026-03-13: Support (Maya Chen) - 'Temporary mitigation: sticky sessions applied at customer CDN; observed frequency drop to <0.5%. Will coordinate rollout of runtime patch.'
2026-03-14: Engineering (Ethan Rivera) - 'Created PR to add lightweight sequence_id metadata to streaming frames and updated server to flush EOS as a separate guaranteed control frame. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1098. Targeting canary in staging 2026-03-20.'
Mitigation and next steps:
- Short-term: Customer retained sticky sessions and CDN rule to avoid multipath replay for affected prefixes; this reduced occurrence to negligible for their traffic.
- Medium-term: Runtime patch adds per-frame sequence_id and explicit EOS control confirmation to avoid final-frame loss during edge path changes (PR #1098).
- SDKs: add acceptance window for EOS following last token to handle small reordering windows.
- Postmortem: scheduled after deployment and 72-hour observation window; update customer with remediation timeline and provide postmortem link.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4321: Implement per-stream sequence_id and adjust control frame handling (linked internal ticket).
- QA: Add integration test simulating multipath replay and path switch with chunk reordering.
- Customer follow-up: Confirmed with Streamline Health on 2026-03-14 that workaround is acceptable until runtime patch is rolled out.
2026-03-13 email to customer: 'We've applied a temporary CDN rule and confirmed a large reduction in incomplete streams. We're prioritizing a runtime patch to make streaming robust to edge replays; ETA for canary is 2026-03-20.'
payload.summary: Multipath proxy replay causes final-stream chunk reassembly to fail

payload.description:
Issue summary: After a customer-installed custom authorization policy was deployed to their private control plane, calls to admin endpoints (e.g., /v1/admin/models, /v1/admin/keys) started receiving 403 Forbidden for users who previously had admin access. The problem is intermittent and seems to correlate with requests routed through a new ingress rule that rewrites headers.

Impact: Admin tooling and automation (customer CI that rotates keys and updates model pinning) failed for parts of the fleet. Customer reports ~15% of admin requests are 403; non-admin user APIs are unaffected. This blocks rotation automation and SRE maintenance windows.

Environment: Beacon Analytics private deployment, prod in us-east, private control plane, identity-proxy v1.14.2, custom authz-policy v2 uploaded by customer via Console.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Authenticate as org-admin user via customer IdP (OIDC) and obtain bearer token.
2) Call GET /v1/admin/models with Authorization: Bearer <token> via their load balancer (route A or route B).
3) Observe 403 for some requests; retrying the same call occasionally succeeds.
4) Requests routed through an alternate ingress (route C) succeed consistently.

Logs / evidence:
- Sample 403 response (truncated): {
  "status": 403,
  "message": "forbidden: insufficient roles"
}
- Identity-proxy logs show: "policy_evaluate: matched policy 'deny_legacy_admin' precedence=50" for 403 requests.
- Successful request entries show "policy_evaluate: no deny rule matched; allowed by default".
- Ingress access logs correlate failing requests to LB backend instance id b-7f3a that applies an X-Route header.

Customer notes: They installed a packaged policy intended to block legacy maintenance endpoints in staging but the same policy was inadvertently applied in prod. The policy uses header matching and a precedence field; order of evaluation appears to cause the deny rule to capture legitimate admin requests when the ingress rewrites a header used in the rule.

Requested outcome: Help identify why policy is matching admin requests, provide a short-term mitigation (policy change or routing tweak) and guidance on longer-term safe policy rollout practices.
03/10 - Support triage: Confirmed 403s only for admin endpoints; not a token expiry or IdP claim issue per initial token inspection.
03/10 - Identity team: Pulled policy bundle the customer uploaded; found 'deny_legacy_admin' with header match condition 'X-Api-Route =~ /legacy/'. Policy precedence=50 (higher numbers evaluated earlier).
03/11 - Ingress team: Verified that LB route A rewrites path and sets X-Api-Route="legacy-admin" for internal routing. Route C does not set this header. This explains why some requests match deny rule only when routed through A.
03/11 - Reproduced: Deployed a local policy with same match and saw deterministic denies when X-Api-Route header present. When header removed, policy not matched and request allowed.
03/12 - Hypothesis: Policy precedence ordering in identity-proxy evaluates deny_legacy_admin before tenant-scoped allow rules; because deny matches on header only, it short-circuits allow by higher-precedence deny rule. Also possible misconfiguration: customer intended the policy to run in staging only but scope metadata contained 'prod' by mistake.
03/12 - Temporary mitigation tested: Added an explicit allow rule for tenant-admins with higher precedence (70) in a test bundle; admin requests succeed even when header present. This suggests precedence change will mitigate.
03/12 - Risk assessment: Patching precedence in customer-managed policy is lower-risk than changing LB header rewrite; however customer prefers a guidance-first approach and an option to rollback policy via Console.

Additional notes:
Mitigation applied: In customer's staging replica we added a tenant-scoped 'allow_admins' policy with precedence=70 which overrides the deny rule. Customer agreed to a phased remediation: 1) Rollback the uploaded deny_legacy_admin policy in prod via Console (actioned by customer ops). 2) Add an explicit tenant-admin allow rule in the policy bundle with precedence > deny if customer intends to keep deny rule. 3) Long-term: add a Console validation step to warn when policies include header-based matches that overlap with LB rewrites and provide a safe rollout toggle.
Follow-ups: Engineering to prepare a small identity-proxy update that adds a policy-preview tool (INT ticket) and a Confluence runbook for customers documenting safe policy scope and precedence examples. Customer reports immediate restoration of admin automation after rollback. Marking as monitoring; will close once customer confirms stable for 48 hours.
Customer to rollback deny_legacy_admin policy in prod (in progress by Beacon Ops).
Support to validate admin endpoints for 48 hours post-rollback and monitor 403 rate (Support will check daily dashboards).
Identity Eng to open INT ticket for policy-preview feature and add Console rollout warning (INT-512).
Create a short runbook for customers: recommended precedence ranges, recommended header naming to avoid collisions with LB rewrites, and a rollback checklist.
If customer wants to keep deny rule: recommend explicit tenant-admin allow with precedence > deny and update sample policy templates.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer LumenDocs reports an increase in transient 5xx errors and request timeouts after a tenant-targeted optimizer profile rollout (mixed-precision quant + aggressive KV prefetch + higher batching). Impact: ~2% of requests for the tenant are returning 5xx (predominantly 524/timeout-from-backend and some 500s), observed spikes in tail latency and occasional memory pressure on serving pods. Environment: Dedicated pool (tenant LUMEN-88), prod us-east, pinned model redwood-xl-13b-v2-int8 rolled 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC with optimizer profile "hybrid-prefetch-q4-aggr"

Steps to reproduce:
1) Route LumenDocs test token through prod us-east endpoint with tenant header X-Tenant: LUMEN-88
2) Send mixed-length chat requests (some >1k tokens) and synthetic high-concurrency bursts (30rps sustained)
3) Observe increased 5xx rates, KV cache evictions, and OOM/kernel warnings in pod logs

Observed behavior: Intermittent 5xx and increased tail latency (95/99th), high KV cache miss churn, sporadic worker restarts on nodes serving the tenant pool. Expected behavior: Stable success rate and tail latency within SLO after optimizer rollout. Logs/metrics: Attached links to customer request IDs, Grafana panels show uptick in pod memory RSS, KV eviction rate, and request queue length behind the runtime. No code change to model was made by customer. Attachments: gzipped sample request logs, tenant rollout config JSON, Grafana screenshot links.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:20 - SRE Oncall (Priya Singh): Noted correlated node-level oom_killer events at ~02:30 UTC on node ip-10-0-23-9. Suggested checking kernel dmesg and cgroups mem_high events. Recommended lowering tenant batch size or disabling KV prefetch as quick mitigations.
2026-03-10 13:40 - Engineering (Diego Morales): Observed that the quant profile applies a memory-heavy fused-kernel path that increases per-worker RSS at higher sequence lengths. Suggested surgical unwind approach: disable KV prefetch first (lowest impact), drop async batching window second, and only then revert quant profile to lower-precision fallback if instability persists.
Telemetry: Correlation between KV prefetch enablement and increase in memory RSS per worker for sequences > 1024 tokens.
Hypothesis: Combined memory footprint of prefetched KV + fused int8 kernel buffers causes transient memory pressure leading to worker restarts in tight concurrency bursts.
Checked artifacts: node dmesg, pod kubelet events, runtime heap profiles (heapster traces), batch size histograms, kv cache hit/miss timeseries.
Attempted non-invasive repro in staging with same optimizer profile reproduced increased RSS, confirming hypothesis.
Risk assessment: Immediate full revert of quant profile triggers throughput drop and potential cost increase; best to progressively unwind features with minimal customer impact.
Disable tenant KV prefetch flag (applied 2026-03-11 12:00 UTC) — immediate reduction in KV eviction churn and tail latency.
Temporarily lower tenant max_batch_size from 32 to 16 via tenant config page to limit per-worker memory pressure.
If instability persists, fall back to the model's conservative quant profile (redwood-xl-13b-v2-int8 -> redwood-xl-13b-v2-q4-conservative) during a defined maintenance window.
Use traffic-split to route 20% of production to conservative profile first for validation before full rollback.
Applied staged surgical unwind: 1) Disabled KV prefetch for tenant LUMEN-88 (non-disruptive) on 2026-03-11 12:00 UTC. 2) Lowered tenant max_batch_size to 16 as a protective throttle. Observed immediate drop in 5xx and 99th latency within 45 minutes. Customer confirmed improvement on 2026-03-12. No rollback of quant profile performed to avoid performance regression; instead we recommended a controlled re-test with instrumented sampling and a temporary cap on sequence length. Follow-ups scheduled: roadmap item to add a tenant-level 'safemode' toggle that atomically disables KV prefetch + async batching and an integration test to catch combined memory-heavy optimizer profiles.
ENG-ops: Implement tenant safemode toggle that disables prefetched KV + async batching in one atomic switch — owner: Diego Morales, ETA: 2026-04-05.
SRE: Add memory pressure alerter tuned to combined RSS + KV eviction rate for dedicated pools — owner: Priya Singh, ETA: 2026-03-20.
Support: Update runbook with snapshotless surgical unwind checklist and safe traffic-split instructions — owner: Raj Patel, ETA: 2026-03-18.
Customer: Plan controlled re-test with conservative quant profile and capped sequence length — owner: LumenDocs engineering, target week of 2026-03-22.
Product: Consider adding explicit optimizer compatibility matrix to Console to warn when a quant profile + prefetch + high-batch combination is likely to exceed memory envelope — owner: Anna Liu, ETA: Q2 2026.
Documentation: Publish short KB article for customers describing staged unwind steps and the 'safemode' workarounds — owner: DevRel, ETA: 2026-03-25.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (MapleCloud, Dedicated) reports an increase in mixed-model responses for a pinned route after an orchestrator leader election during a staged canary. The route had been explicitly pinned to redwood-open-v2-13b for a customer cohort; several requests returned the degraded variant (redwood-quant-13b) without an explicit fallback logged in the tenant's debug traces.

Impact:
- Customer experiencing ~8% of requests returning outputs from a different model variant for ~45 minutes.
- Affects production traffic for a high-volume endpoint (billing-sensitive).
- Customer reported quality regressions and alerted their SRE + our support.

Environment:
- prod, us-west-2 region, dedicated capacity pool (dc-aws-usw2-03).
- Route: /v1/generate pin: "tenant:maplecloud:route:billing-invoice-summarize" pinned_version: redwood-open-v2-13b

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Traffic against pinned route with sustained canary weight changes (10%->40%->10%) as part of their deployment window.
2) Orchestrator leader swap happened during the 40% window (they observed a control-plane blip and a brief leader re-election).
3) After leader swap, some users' sessions returned outputs with tokenization/format changes consistent with redwood-quant-13b.

Observed logs and evidence:
- Edge traces (MapleCloud tenant debug) show initial request carrying pin cookie and header X-RD-Pin: redwood-open-v2-13b but downstream routed to serving instance labeled redwood-quant-13b-POOL.
- Orchestrator logs show a snapshot commit and a leader promotion at 2026-03-12T14:21:03Z.
- Control-plane snapshot IDs: before swap snap-20260312-1409, after swap snap-20260312-1421.
- No explicit fallback event recorded in tenant-level fallback log; edge proxy logs show a small number of 502 retries contemporaneous with leader swap.
- Customer provided deterministic example request IDs: req-Maple-87921 and req-Maple-87942.

Immediate customer ask:
- Why did pinned requests route to a different variant without a fallback reason?
- Are tokens billed correctly when variants mismatch?
- Request for mitigation to prevent recurrence during leader elections.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 15:10 - Customer (MapleCloud SRE): Provided edge traces and pointed to orchestrator metric spike at 2026-03-12T14:20:50Z.
2026-03-12 16:20 - Eng (runtime): Noted edge retry 502s triggered a scaled-down fast-path that bypasses the full pin reconciliation check under specific retry-code paths.
Hypothesis: During orchestrator leader swap we observe a three-way timing window: (1) new snapshot published, (2) edge shards refresh routing metadata, (3) serving pool instances reconcile pin leases. If an edge shard receives a retry-triggered fast-path (502->retry) during this window it may route using cached fallback rules instead of the freshly committed snapshot, causing silent routing to a compatible quantized variant. Supporting evidence: 1) Repro in staging where leader election + induced 502s produced the same silent variant mix; 2) trace alignment between leader_promotion events and first misrouted request. Additional possible contributor: pin-lease refresh TTL was 5s; leader swap introduced an extra 2-3s delay in reconciling TTLs across shards.
Short-term mitigation applied 2026-03-12T17:10Z: increased pin-lease grace window from 2s to 8s and disabled retry fast-path routing that bypasses full pin reconciliation for the next 48 hours in us-west-2. Customer confirmed reduction in misrouted responses to <0.1% in subsequent hour.
Planned long-term fix:
- Orchestrator: make snapshot publication atomic with pin-coherence handshake (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2784) to prevent any edge shard from seeing a partial commit.
- Edge: ensure retry paths re-run pin validation after transient 5xxs before selecting fallback variant.
- Add a canary test that injects leader-election during staged weight adjustments and validates zero silent-fallbacks for pinned routes.
Rollout notes:

- Coordinate with Customer Success to update MapleCloud on permanent fix schedule and billing reconciliation if needed.
- Create a short runbook for SRE to follow if similar incidents occur during orchestrator maintenance windows.

2) Extend edge retry validation - target 2026-03-15.

Issue summary: Customer's private deployment behind a branch-office NAT appliance is experiencing intermittent timeouts during control-plane mTLS handshake and OCSP stapling verification, and occasional model shard validation failures (range GET SHA mismatch).
Impact: Customers report increased 5xx/timeout errors for model pulls and transient inference failures for a small percentage (~0.7%) of requests during nightly batch loads. Production latency impact for affected requests: 2-10s additional retries; some requests fail end-to-end.
Environment: Private deployment using VPCE to access Redwood control plane and S3 presigned artifact storage. Branch office egress appliance with TCP Segmentation Offload (TSO) enabled and on-path WAN optimizer.
Steps to reproduce:
  1) From branch office host behind NAT appliance, trigger model prefetch for rwd-open-13b-quant (range GETs).
  2) Observe OCSP stapling and mTLS handshake with control-plane endpoints via VPCE.
  3) During high-concurrency batch fetch (parallel shard downloads x32), ~1% of shards fail with truncated range content or TLS handshake timeouts.
Logs / Observed symptoms:
  - client: "TLS handshake timeout after 7s (tcp_retransmits=3)"
  - control-plane: "mTLS: OCSP response verify failed: short_read"
  - artifact service: "range GET returned content-length 0 for shard 00012 (expected 3.2MB)"
  - branch NAT logs: "TSO segmented packet exceed MSS, dropping segment"
 Additional context: Failures correlate with times when the branch egress appliance offloads segmentation and rewrites TCP options (SACK/ECN) and when VPCE path traverses a WAN optimizer performing MSS clamping.
Customer impact window: first observed 2026-03-12 23:40 UTC, intermittent since then, peaked during nightly batch on 2026-03-14 02:00-04:00 UTC.
03/14 03:05 UTC - Initial triage by Support: verified customer network path uses VPCE with on-path egress NAT appliance and WAN optimizer. Reproduced partial shard failures when batch-concurrency >= 16.
03/14 03:22 UTC - Gathered packet captures from customer (pcap provided): observed IP fragmentation/overlapping TCP sequence ranges and MSS mismatch between host and egress appliance. Egress appliance shows TSO on but reports MSS clamp to 1200 bytes on the uplink.
03/14 03:40 UTC - Correlation found with OCSP stapling failures: control-plane logs show TLS record layer truncation after stall; OCSP responder returns truncated payload when upstream connection resets. Hypothesis: TSO + MSS clamping causes middlebox to send improperly segmented TLS records leading to TLS/Ocsp parser read errors.
03/14 04:10 UTC - Eng (network infra) ran a controlled test: disable TSO on branch host VM and rerun batch prefetch. Result: no shard truncation observed across 10k range GETs; mTLS handshakes succeeded consistently.
    Hypothesis strengthened: TSO combined with asymmetric MSS rewrite is causing out-of-spec segment sizes resulting in TLS record reassembly failures on the VPCE-terminating proxy or OCSP path.
03/14 04:45 UTC - Checked related infra: VPCE endpoint service (internal NLB) is not modifying TCP options; observed failure happens before VPCE ingress (on egress path). Logged correlation with our existing ticket SUP-712987 (ocsp staple break during proxy injection).
03/14 05:20 UTC - Customer provided firewall config: 'accelerate_tcp true', 'tso on', and explicit MSS clamping rule to 1200. Suggested temporary disable of TSO and to remove MSS clamp for test.
03/14 06:00 UTC - Customer applied temporary change: disabled TSO on hosts and bypassed WAN optimizer for VPCE IP range. Monitoring: error rate for shard downloads dropped to baseline (<0.05%).
2026-03-14 03:10 - Support (Aisha Patel): Initial intake. Collected pcap, shard hashes, and customer topology diagram. Escalated to Network Infra.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 04:20 - Customer (BrightPath Health, NetOps - Jordan Lee): Applied test to disable TSO on a single host and re-ran fetch job. Attaching logs - observed immediate improvement. Asking if this aligns with Redwood recommendations.
2026-03-14 05:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Confirmed improvement. Recommended temporary mitigation: disable TSO on hosts that access VPCE or add explicit bypass rule for VPCE destination CIDRs on WAN optimizer. Documented steps and asked NetOps to schedule permanent fix.
2026-03-14 07:10 - Customer (Jordan Lee): Scheduling maintenance window to remove MSS clamp and to upgrade WAN optimizer firmware. Marking current change as successful; will report if recurs after full rollout.
Mitigation: Customer disabled TSO on branch hosts and added VPCE CIDR bypass on their WAN optimizer which eliminated the shard truncation and mTLS/OCSP errors in observed tests. Root cause: interaction between TCP Segmentation Offload (host-side) and an on-path MSS clamping WAN optimizer that produced out-of-spec TCP segments leading to TLS record truncation and OCSP read failures.
Permanent fix/action items:
  - Recommend customer: disable TSO/GRO for hosts that fetch model artifacts via VPCE OR ensure WAN optimizer does not MSS-clamp below path MTU.
  - Redwood: add a KB article and console alert guidance for private deployments warning about TSO/GRO + MSS clamping interactions with VPCE endpoints.
  - Infra: add automated telemetry to detect increased TLS record fragmentation / short_read OCSP errors and surface to support dashboard.
Follow-up: Customer to confirm after WAN optimizer firmware upgrade and removal of MSS clamp. Support will keep ticket open until customer confirms 72-hour healthy window.
Support to keep ticket open for 72-hour validation window after customer's WAN optimizer firmware upgrade (owner: Aisha Patel).
Create KB: 'VPCE connectivity and TCP offload interactions' (owner: Marco Diaz, due 2026-03-21).
Infra to implement TLS-fragmentation telemetry alert (owner: SRE team, ticket INF-4821).
Customer to confirm permanent rollout of MSS clamp removal and report any regression (owner: Jordan Lee).

payload.description:
Issue summary:

Customers started reporting increasing 5xx rates for streaming and short polling endpoints over the last 3 hours. Errors are primarily 502/504 from the API gateway and intermittent runtime panics on a subset of Dedicated pods.

Impact:
- BrightAssist (dedicated tenant) observed ~8% error rate on streaming requests between 13:00-15:30 UTC.
- Other tenants in us-east show slight uptick (0.5–1%).
- Some long-lived sessions abruptly reset, causing client reconnect storms and billing anomalies.

Environment:
- prod/us-east, Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-02
- API Gateway v2.1.7, Edge-proxy v3.4.0, Serving-runtime v2.8.1 (gptx-13b pinned)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Start ~300 parallel streaming sessions to /v1/stream with keepalive enabled and 60s heartbeat.
2. Simulate a long tail where a fraction (~20%) hold open idle streams for >90s.
3. Observe increasing ephemeral socket use on apigw and a backlog in accept queue.

Observed metrics / logs (high level):
- apigw.conn_count (ephemeral): +210% over baseline
- apigw.accept_queue_drops: spike from 0 to 480/min
- edge-proxy.keepalive_pool_exhausted: true on several hosts
- runtime.watchdog_restarts: 6 events correlated to the timeframe

Attachments / Links:
- Grafana dash (streaming/conn): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/us-east-streaming-overview
- Slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0123ABC)
Timeline:
- 13:02 UTC: BrightAssist reported first errors (via support chat).
- 13:10 UTC: SRE saw accept_queue_drops on apigw nodes apigw-us-east-[3,4,5].
- 13:22 UTC: Edge-proxy logs show steady increase in keepalive connections that are not progressing to runtime (idle streams).
- 13:45 UTC: A subset of runtime pods logged 'kv-cache-lock-timeout' and then a watchdog restart.

Hypotheses tested so far:
- H1 (proxy conn leak): edge-proxy failing to recycle idle streaming connections — partially supported by socket age histogram (many >120s).
- H2 (client retry amplification): clients reconnect immediately on reset causing thundering reconnects — supported by request spike after NACKs.
- H3 (runtime memory fragmentation): investigated but heap / GPU memory graphs show normal utilization prior to panics; panics align with connection pressure rather than pure OOM.

Key findings:
- Keepalive pool limit of 1024 per host was exceeded on 3 apigw hosts; new connections were dropped at accept() leading to 502/504 returned upstream.
- Stale long-polling sessions were not being closed by the proxy after the configured idle timeout due to a regression introduced in edge-proxy v3.4.0 (related PR in investigation).
- Connection churn triggered a cascade: accept queue drops -> client retries -> runtime prefetch and KV-cache contention -> a few runtime watchdog restarts on pods handling high-priority tenant requests.

Next steps:
- Short-term mitigation: increase apigw keepalive pool and bump accept queue size; enforce immediate proxy-side hard idle timeout for streaming sessions.
- Medium-term: revert faulty edge-proxy behavior via hotfix (PR ready for review) and add stricter telemetry around socket age.
- Postmortem: schedule after stabilization with BrightAssist and SRE.
Applied at 13:25-14:30 UTC:
- Increased apigw keepalive_pool size from 1024 -> 2048 on impacted hosts.
- Raised accept queue (listen backlog) from 128 -> 512 temporarily.
- Enabled emergency proxy hard-idle-timeout for streaming sessions to 90s (overrides tenant setting).
- Rotated a subset of apigw nodes out-of-service for cleanup.

Outcome: error-rate dropped from ~8% -> ~1.2% for BrightAssist within 35 minutes. Runtime restarts subsided.
Hotfix PR #1423 merged 2026-03-14 15:20 UTC to revert the reaper regression. Full rollout completed to prod by 2026-03-14 15:50 UTC.

Follow-ups assigned:
- INT-4401 (SRE): Add alert for keepalive_pool_utilization > 80% with automated mitigation runbook.
- INT-4420 (Eng): Add unit/integration tests to prevent regression in session reaper logic.
- Support: Notify BrightAssist of root cause and credits applied.

Ticket will remain open until postmortem is completed and follow-ups are closed.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 13:18 — SRE (Diego Ramos): Noted accept_queue_drops on apigw-us-east-03/04/05. Adding hosts to rotation drain and increasing accept queue temporarily.
2026-03-14 13:55 — BrightAssist (Customer): Confirmed they see reduced errors after SRE applied accept_queue changes, but intermittent resets still occur.
2026-03-14 14:40 — SRE (Claire Nguyen): Observed decline in apigw.accept_queue_drops and fewer runtime watchdog restarts after proxy hard timeout applied to prod hosts (gradual rollout).
payload.summary: Incremental 5xx growth from sticky long-poll streaming sessions and keepalive exhaustion

payload.description:
Customer BrightChat reports that after a planned canary weight adjustment at 2026-03-10T15:20Z, a subset of live chat sessions began receiving completions from a different model variant despite having been previously pinned. The customer observed content quality regressions and inconsistent conversation history in a small cohort (~0.9% of sessions).
1) Start long-running chat session against tenant endpoint using SDK v1.12 with session affinity header set (X-Session-Affinity).
2) Simulate sustained traffic for ~10 minutes to warm caches and KV prefixes.
3) Trigger canary weight shift: increase canary from 2% to 25% via console rollout controller (time: 2026-03-10T15:20Z).
4) Observe session responses for 30 minutes after weight change and check model version reported in response metadata.
5) Confirm that affected sessions return model variant redwood/gpt-3.5-large-v1-canary while they were previously pinned to redwood/gpt-3.5-large-v1-stable.
Pinned sessions intermittently lose version affinity immediately after the canary weight change and receive responses from the canary variant. This occurs without explicit unpinning in the control plane and affects only some SDK versions and edge nodes.
Pinned sessions should maintain version affinity for their active lifetime or until an explicit unpin/promotion occurs. A global canary weight change should not rebind already-pinned sessions to the canary variant.

edge-proxy/us-east-1 - 2026-03-10T15:20:04Z - session-id=abc123 - outgoing route=tenant-42->canary - reason=route-table-update-applied
canary-coordinator - 2026-03-10T15:20:03Z - applied weight change tenant=tenant-42 old=2 new=25 - propagation=async
routing-cache - 2026-03-10T15:20:05Z - cache-ttl=2s - evicted key=tenant-42-session-affinity-abc123
serving-runtime - 2026-03-10T15:20:05Z - dispatch to model=redwood/gpt-3.5-large-v1-canary - runtime-node=node-17
2026-03-10 - 15:35 - support@redwood - Hi BrightChat, we've acknowledged the report and started tracing edge logs. Can you confirm SDK version and whether you use sticky cookies or header affinity?
2026-03-10 - 15:42 - BrightChat-SRE - Confirm SDK v1.12. We set X-Session-Affinity header. Issue reproduces on roughly 1 in 100 sessions. Attached sample request IDs.
2026-03-10 - 16:10 - Daniel Morales - Initial hypothesis: race between routing cache eviction and async canary propagation. Assigning to infra for edge-proxy tracing.
2026-03-11 - 09:22 - infra@redwood - Found that edge-proxy versions <1.7 do not write affinity into persistent route cache on weight-change events; instead they rely on short TTLs. Upgrading edge nodes to 1.8 recommended as workaround.
2026-03-11 - 12:30 - BrightChat - After edge-proxy nodes were rolled to 1.8 in staging, we saw no reproductions. Can you advise production mitigation?
Correlation: all affected sessions used SDK v1.12 and were served by a subset of edge nodes running edge-proxy 1.6/1.7.
Root cause hypothesis: canary-coordinator applies weight change async to route table; edge-proxy evicts short-lived route cache entries on weight-change and rewrites route without persisting session-affinity => subsequent requests routed to new variant.
Additional factor: certain SDK builds omit the explicit affinity cookie fallback, relying on header-only affinity which is lost when proxy rewrites requests.
Reproducible in internal test: reproduce with controlled weight change and mixed edge-proxy version fleet; failure occurs within <10 seconds post-change and affects ~0.7-1.2% of sessions in our test run.
Risk: ongoing rollouts that change weight quickly may impact long-lived session consistency for tenants using older SDKs or edge-proxy versions.
Related: linked to prior ticket SUP-8234 which described stale route-cache during gradual rollout but this incident is distinct due to async propagation timing and affinity write behavior.
Temporary mitigation: rolled edge-proxy fleet in us-east-1 to version 1.8 which persists session-affinity keys across route-table refreshes and increased route-cache write-through to reduce TTL evictions. Recommended customer-side workaround: upgrade SDK to >=1.13 which sets a persistent affinity cookie, or include explicit tenant-affinity header on every request.
1) Infra: backport affinity-persistence patch to edge-proxy v1.7 (PR repo/edge-proxy#981) and schedule global rollout (owner: Daniel Morales).
2) Platform: change canary-coordinator to use synchronous affinity-preserving update path for weight changes when TTL-sensitive tenants are detected (owner: Priya Ramesh).
3) DX/Docs: update rollout runbook to add steps for 'affinity-safe' canary increases and a troubleshooting checklist for pinned session divergence (owner: Lauren Park).
4) Customer outreach: Send BrightChat an incident summary and recommend SDK upgrade and confirm mitigation (owner: CS Manager - Monica Lee).
payload.summary: Unequal routing after canary weight shift causes mixed model outputs for ongoing sessions

payload.description:
Issue summary:
North Harbor Bank has requested an on-demand export of the transactional_activity audit ledger for a legal review. They require a segmented NDJSON export that includes: per-tenant resume tokens per segment, canonical UTC anchoring for all timestamps, and a field-name translation lexicon (customer -> bank field names) so downstream forensic tools map correctly. Export must preserve ordering within tenant sequences and include a small manifest with segment checksums for reproducibility.

Impact:
- Customer cannot produce a legally-scoped playback for a compliance request without this export.
- High priority due to pending regulatory deadline in customer legal team.

Environment:
- Production activity ledger (prod - us-east).
- Primary ingestion path: webhook -> kafka -> ledger service -> archival exporter.

Steps to reproduce / request template used by customer:
1) Customer sent request via the Console "On-demand audit export" modal requesting: stream=transactional_activity, date_range=2025-10-01..2025-10-15, tenant_scope=tenant_9853, output_format=ndjson_segmented, include_resume_tokens=true, timestamp_mode=utc_canonical, include_field_lexicon=true, delivery=presigned_s3.
2) Support confirmed receipt and escalated to export ops.

Observed data / logs:
- Initial validation run (2025-11-03 14:05 UTC) showed ~0.4% of tenant events had sequence gaps.
- Ledger exporter logs: exporter/segment_writer WARN shard-lag detected on shard-7 between 2025-10-08T02:10:05Z and 2025-10-08T02:12:30Z.
- Kafka consumer offsets showed transient rebalances during the requested window.
- No authentication errors; S3 presigned write succeeded in dry-run.

Requested deliverable (customer acceptance):
- One or more NDJSON files partitioned by tenant sequence ranges (max 1M events / segment).
- A manifest.json (small) listing segments, per-segment SHA256 checksum, inclusive timestamp range, and a resume_token representing a stable offset for that tenant range.
- A CSV field-translation lexicon mapping Redwood field names -> North Harbor canonical field names.
- All timestamps in UTC ISO8601 with explicit tz (e.g. 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z).
- Delivery via presigned S3 URL with 7-day validity and a signed delivery receipt.

Acceptance criteria:
- Customer can replay the segments in-order without gaps using the resume tokens and manifest.
- Field mappings applied by customer result in no loss of critical attributes used by their compliance tooling.
- CRC/SHA checksums match on both sides.

Investigation notes (internal):
- Hypothesis A: kafka rebalances led to duplicate offset commits causing perceived sequence gaps for tenant_9853 only (tenant has high event density).
- Hypothesis B: temporary exporter shard-lag caused exporter to flush partial segments and then resume with new segment IDs, leaving apparent gaps until remapped by resume token logic.
- Action taken: replayed offset window to a staging export to verify segment continuity (INT-3321). Staging export produced contiguous segments but with different resume tokens than production run.
- Mitigation: we can stitch contiguous segments together in the exported manifest and provide synthetic resume tokens that map to per-segment start offsets for customer playback. Need SRE sign-off for token mutation approach.

Risks / compliance notes:
- Resume tokens are considered sensitive because they implicitly reveal offset state; shared tokens must be treated as limited-scope and delivered via secure presigned S3.
- Legalhold: customer requested preservation flags to avoid deletion; follow-up required with retention team.

Next steps / work items:
- [Support] Confirm final date window and whether additional tenant IDs included (Samantha - 2025-11-03).
- [SRE] Produce a curated NDJSON export from a controlled replay with stitched manifest (Marco - target 2025-11-06).
- [Export Ops] Generate CSV field lexicon based on customer-supplied mapping file and our schema (Nora - target 2025-11-06).
- [Security] Approve presigned S3 parameters and delivery receipt format (Ajay - target 2025-11-05).

Deliverables timeline: tentative - curated export available 2025-11-06 for customer review.

Additional notes:
2025-11-03 - Customer (North Harbor Legal - Maria Chen): Confirmed tenant_9853 only. Requested retention hold for exported slices and asked for checkable integrity proof for court submission.
If SRE cannot produce native resume tokens that are stable, implement translation layer that maps exporter offsets -> synthetic stable tokens and include mapping in manifest. Ensure mapping is cryptographically anchored (HMAC) and documented in manifest schema.

Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 14:10 UTC we observed a slow, stepwise rise in 5xx errors for a Dedicated customer (NimbleDocs) using pinned model rw-large-v1.1. Errors manifested as 502/504 from API Gateway with upstream runtime process restarts. Impact: customer-facing failures for batch embedding and streaming chat sessions, elevated error rate ~12% during peak.

Environment: prod (us-west-2), Dedicated GPU pool (pinned tenant), runtime version: rtx-serve-2.7.3, gpu-driver package: nvidia-530.11.

Observed behaviour: Initial symptoms were intermittent higher latency and sporadic 502s. Over ~30 minutes failures increased and stabilized at an elevated rate. Multiple runtime instances in the dedicated pool reported NVML reset events and kernel retries, followed by prefetch cancellations and hedged retry amplification at the API Gateway.

Issue summary:
Customer reports that their SIEM (Splunk-heavy forwarding) shows out-of-order event sequences and timestamp drift when receiving batched audit webhooks from Redwood. This is affecting reconciliation for regulatory reporting and causing events to appear in the wrong sequence for root-cause timelines.

Impact:
- Ingestion and alert correlation for certain high-severity user events are misordered for ~2-3 minute windows each hour.
- Customer compliance team cannot reliably map actions to transaction IDs for audit reports.
- Business impact: temporary delay in regulatory reconciliation workflows and manual effort to re-order events.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted audit webhook to customer's SIEM forwarder (customer-managed collector)
- Prod account: stratus-prod-42, region us-east-1, delivery via HTTPS webhook, batching enabled (batch_size=25, max_wait_ms=1500)
- Customer SIEM: Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) behind a load balancer

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Enable webhook deliveries with batching on for a tenant and generate 1k user actions in ~5 minutes.
2) Observe the HEC raw events index and sequence numbers for events referencing the same session_id or transaction_id.
3) Correlate Redwood event timestamps against SIEM ingestion timestamps and sequence fields.

Observed behavior:
- Events occasionally arrive at the SIEM with timestamps that are earlier than prior events for the same session (clock skew or serialization out-of-order).
- Batches contain mixed timestamps and the last event of the batch sometimes has an earlier timestamp than the first event at the receiver side.
- Customer sees gaps in their sequence numbers in Splunk (e.g., event_seq: 120, 123, 121).

Expected behavior:
- Events emitted by Redwood should preserve chronological ordering for events generated within the same source session and maintain monotonically increasing timestamps in delivery order (modulo minor network reordering that does not change sequence semantics).

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- 2 example HEC raw payload captures (hec_capture_20260309_01.json, hec_capture_20260309_02.json)
- Sample of reconstructed event timeline and CSV of event_ids with timestamps (timeline_20260309.csv)
- Support trace id: trace-7a9b3e11

2026-03-10 | Aisha Bryant (Support): Received initial ticket from Stratus Bank support contact (S. Patel). Customer provided HEC captures and a CSV with perceived ordering issues. Asked for delivery headers and batch payload examples. SLA acknowledged.
2026-03-10 | Marco Ruiz (On-call SRE): Reproduced a similar pattern in a staging harness when batching and small max_wait_ms are combined with per-request concurrency limits. Asked engineering to check batch serialization and timestamp generation path. Linked INT-1142 for internal kernel investigation.
2026-03-11 | Engineering (Elena Park): Found that webhook batch serializer uses event.emitted_at from the event store, but there is a microsecond rounding step in the batching loop that can re-order events when multiple events share identical emitted_at values. Proposed patch to preserve original in-batch order and include a sequence counter per-event in the batch envelope for receiver-side ordering. Created PR github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-service/pull/879.
2026-03-11 | Support (Aisha Bryant): Shared interim mitigation with customer: increase max_wait_ms to 5000 to let batches accumulate in stable order, and enable per-event sequence header 'X-Redwood-Seq' (can be turned on via support flag) so customer's parser can re-order on ingest. Customer accepted temporary workaround and will test change overnight.
2026-03-12 | Customer (S. Patel, Stratus Bank): After increasing max_wait_ms to 5s, observed a significant reduction in ordering anomalies. Requested timeline for permanent fix and an audit statement describing root cause and remediation steps for regulators.
Summary of findings:
- Root cause traced to batching code path in ingest-service where events pulled from the event store are sorted by emitted_at only, and if emitted_at is identical or rounded during transfer, the stable ordering is not guaranteed due to use of a parallelized serialization worker pool.
- Edge condition surfaced when bursty client traffic generates many events with identical millisecond timestamps; parallel workers serialized payloads in non-deterministic order.
- Network/TLS retries and LI (load-balancer) multiplexing exacerbated perceived re-ordering at receiver but were not primary cause.

Hypothesis tested:
- Reproduced in staging harness by generating events with same emitted_at and enabling two serialization workers; confirmed non-deterministic ordering.

Short-term mitigation implemented:
- Support flag to enable X-Redwood-Seq header containing monotonic per-tenant sequence number (applies to webhook deliveries) for customers requiring ordering guarantees.
- Recommended customer change: raise max_wait_ms to 5s for batching to reduce inter-worker contention.

Planned permanent remediation:
- Ensure ingest-service preserves stored in-order index when creating batch envelopes (use explicit index rather than sort by emitted_at).
- Add integration test that generates identical timestamps and asserts delivery order preservation.
- Release timeline: patch targeted for 2026-03-18; will coordinate rolling deploy with smoke tests and notify impacted customers.
Workaround and fix plan:
- Workaround provided and validated by customer: increased max_wait_ms and enabled sequencing header via support flag. Customer observed improvement and accepted workaround for interim.
- Engineering patch (PR #879) merged to preserve in-store order when building batches and to attach per-event 'sequence_in_batch' field to payload. Patch scheduled for canary on 2026-03-16 and global rollout 2026-03-18 pending smoke tests.
- Post-deploy actions: update docs on webhook ordering guarantees, publish short advisory for customers using SIEM ingestion, and add a new check in Redwood Console alerting when batch_size/max_wait_ms combinations are likely to cause ordering anomalies.

Follow-ups:
- Support to send an audit-style statement describing root cause and remediation to Stratus Bank compliance contact by 2026-03-13.
- Create a low-friction toggle in Console to enable X-Redwood-Seq for customers until the fix is live.
- Close ticket when rollout completes and customer confirms no further anomalies for a 48-hour validation window.

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Customer (Acme AI, Dedicated) reports intermittent hangs on multi-GPU tensor-parallel replicas (A100 80GB, TP=4) that present as streaming requests timing out. When the hang occurs, affected replicas stop making forward progress; queued requests back up; downstream app sees elevated p99 and repeated client-side timeouts.

Impact
- Customer-facing: streaming responses stall mid-generation; client disconnects at ~60–180s depending on their gateway timeout.
- Platform: p99 latency spikes, retry storms, autoscaling churn (adds capacity but stuck replicas remain in rotation unless drained).
- Incident classification: Sev1 (enterprise Dedicated), started 2025-02-17.

Customer symptoms (from Acme)
- “Some requests never finish. They stream a few tokens and then hang until our 120s timeout.”
- Happens more during peak traffic and mixed workload (short prompts + long prompts, concurrent streams).

Environment
- Dedicated deployment: Acme AI (us-east), A100 80GB.
- Replica topology: TP=4, 1 replica = 4 GPUs.
- Runtime: 1.18.x (pinned) with CUDA graphs enabled.
- Traffic pattern: bursty concurrency, mixed prefill/decode, long contexts (~8k–16k) present during peak.

What we’ve observed (initial triage)
- Symptoms match known “TP silent stall” signatures: GPU utilization drops on one rank; other ranks appear blocked; no hard NCCL error surfaces to API.
- Request traces show decode iteration stops advancing; stream remains open; eventually customer gateway times out.
- At least 2 occurrences correlate with high prefill load on the same replica prior to stall.

Reproduction status
- Not yet deterministic in customer environment. Runtime team has a similar repro in progress using mixed prompt lengths + streaming decode.

Logs / signals (snippets)
- Customer-provided (sanitized) streaming timeout logs:
  - 2025-02-17T19:44:12Z request_id=rw_01HR… model=llama3-70b tp=4 stream=true status=client_timeout duration_ms=120000 tokens_out=214
- Redwood replica logs (sanitized, from us-east dedicated cluster):
  - [rank=2] WARN tp_step stalled: last_progress_ms=93210 in_flight_collectives=all_reduce:7 all_gather:3 scheduler_q_depth=128 stall_hint=collective_wait
  - [rank=0] INFO decode_loop: waiting on barrier event=tp_sync_42 stream=decode
- NCCL debug (after enabling extra logging window):
  - NCCL WARN Async operation in progress, stream=comm, opCount=1193 (no subsequent completion)

Immediate mitigations recommended (customer + SRE)
- Drain/replace suspect replicas when heartbeat gap/timeout spike detected.
- Reduce max concurrency per replica (cap inflight streams) and cap max batch tokens.
- Temporarily disable CUDA graphs for TP replicas (reduces performance, improves debuggability; recommended during incident).
- Enable safer scheduling guardrail flag (prefill/decode fairness) if available in pinned runtime.

Links
- Incident Slack: #incidents thread 1740165551-sev1-dedicated-timeouts-suspected-tp-hang
- Eng runtime threads: 1739812205-nccl-collective-ordering-suspected-mismatch; 1739973309-watchdog-default-timeout-values
- Internal runbook: Confluence “runtime-tp-hang-mitigation”

Ask / next steps
- Need runtime engineering to confirm likely root cause category (scheduler starvation vs NCCL ordering vs cancel path) and provide near-term fix/flag recommendation compatible with Acme’s pinned version.
- Need SRE to add temporary alerting on TP heartbeat gaps for Acme’s Dedicated cluster and automate drain on stall detection where safe.

Account context
- Acme AI is in active expansion; this is blocking a production rollout unless we can reduce timeouts to near-zero at peak. Customer requested ETA for fix and recommended settings for peak traffic.
2025-02-17 19:58 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support) — Created ticket from Sev1 intake. Customer reports intermittent streaming hangs; attached sanitized request IDs + timestamps. Paging SRE + runtime on-call via #incidents.
2025-02-17 20:07 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE) — Acknowledged. Seeing elevated request_timeout_rate on Acme dedicated route starting ~19:40 UTC. Manually drained 2 replicas with anomalous GPU util drop. Short-term improvement observed. Tracking in incident thread #incidents/1740165551.
2025-02-17 20:19 UTC — Liam O'Rourke (TAM/Support) — Sent customer interim mitigation: cap concurrency to 24 streams/replica (from 48), reduce max_batch_tokens by 25%, and disable cuda_graphs on TP replicas for now. Asked for 3 stuck request IDs + client timestamps for correlation.
2025-02-17 20:44 UTC — Noah Patel (Eng, Runtime TL) — This matches known TP stall signatures under mixed prefill/decode. Likely collective ordering/scheduler starvation interaction (collectives blocked behind prefill-heavy work). We’re working ENG-4821 initiative; near-term: try scheduler fairness guardrail flag + reduce prefill batch aggressiveness. We’ll share exact flag names once confirmed for 1.18.x.
2025-02-18 00:12 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE) — Added temporary dashboard panels for Acme: per-replica request timeout correlation + GPU util by rank. Alert draft: tp_heartbeat_gap_seconds > 30 for 2m (notify, not page) during mitigation window.
2025-02-18 16:05 UTC — Rachel Kim (CS Lead) — Customer says mitigation reduced frequency but not eliminated; still saw 2 hangs during peak. They can accept reduced throughput temporarily but need a real fix/ETA. Requested weekly updates and canary plan details.
2025-02-19 09:31 UTC — Hiro Tanaka (Eng, Kernels) — Recommend enabling extra NCCL debug logging for a short canary window (need helpdesk to flip safely). Opening INT-2219 to coordinate logging + rollback.
2025-02-20 13:22 UTC — Tomáš Novák (SRE) — Updated internal runbook with explicit drain steps + what logs to capture (NCCL opCount, per-rank heartbeat). Shared link in incident channel and pinned to oncall notes.
2025-02-21 18:47 UTC — Liam O'Rourke (TAM/Support) — Customer provided additional data: hangs correlate with long-context prompts (12k–16k) plus concurrent short requests. Notably occurs when a client cancels mid-stream (browser disconnect). Forwarded to runtime team; may match cancellation-path deadlock bug.
2025-02-24 10:03 UTC — Sofia Ivanova (Eng, Scheduling) — We have a candidate fix: prevent collective starvation by enforcing ordering/fairness between prefill-heavy batches and decode steps. Targeting runtime 1.19; can provide backportable flag to reduce risk for pinned customers (lower perf).
2025-02-26 17:28 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE) — Enabled automated drain on sustained TP heartbeat gaps for Acme dedicated cluster (guarded, rate-limited). This is a mitigation only; should reduce hang duration impact from ~120s to <60s in most cases.
2025-02-28 08:40 UTC — Liam O'Rourke (TAM/Support) — Shared rollout plan with customer: Dedicated-first canary for runtime 1.19 TP stability fixes, starting with non-critical route, then expanding. Customer agreed to provide a 2-hour peak window for observation. Linked Fireflies deep-dive notes in CRM (internal).
2025-03-03 19:05 UTC — Marissa Cole (Product) — Go/no-go approved for 1.19 canary for TP stability package (watchdog + scheduling + NCCL sync hardening, feature-flagged). Dedicated sequencing: Acme first (opt-in), then broader dedicated fleet.
2025-03-03 21:12 UTC — Liam O'Rourke (TAM/Support) — Customer confirmed mitigations + auto-drain reduced user-visible impact; proceeding with 1.19 canary next. Leaving ticket in Resolved with workaround; will reopen if canary shows regression or continued hangs > agreed threshold.
Resolved via mitigations and operational controls while fixes are prepared for runtime 1.19: (1) reduced concurrency and batch aggressiveness, (2) temporarily disabled CUDA graphs on TP replicas, (3) enabled additional NCCL debug logging during a short window, and (4) added SRE automation to drain replicas on TP heartbeat gaps. Permanent fixes tracked in ENG-4821 initiative and related PRs (scheduler fairness/collective ordering, NCCL stream/event sync hardening, TP watchdog + safe abort/drain, improved error surfacing). Customer aligned on a Dedicated-first canary rollout plan for runtime 1.19.

Issue summary: Customer reports periodic increases in p95 latency (~400-900ms above baseline) for API requests immediately following a region pin toggle via Console or API token-scoped change. Impact: Production inference latency spikes cause observable timeouts in their synchronous request paths and increased user-facing errors. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod us-east with strict data residency to eu-west for a subset of tokens. Observed behavior appears tied to token-scoped pin updates and subsequent edge selection for a short window (30s-3m).
1) Customer toggles region pin for tenant via POST /v1/tenants/{id}/pin (pin to eu-west). 2) Immediately send a burst of 100 concurrent completion requests using token scoped to that tenant (seq length ~512). 3) Observe p50/p95/p99 before and after toggle. 4) Repeat toggle back to us-east and send another burst. 5) Capture edge request IDs and tracer headers for any slow requests.
Sample logs (redacted):
- 2026-03-10T15:02:11Z EDGE-req-id=edg_7a3bf2 token=tenant-abc action=pin_update scope=eu-west controlplane_tx=txn_9921
- 2026-03-10T15:02:12Z PROXY-req-id=prx_11ac slow= true upstream_edge=eu-west selected_backend=eu-west-kernel-3 node_latency_ms=720
- 2026-03-10T15:02:13Z PROXY-req-id=prx_11ad selected_backend=us-east-fallback node_latency_ms=850 auth_scope=tenant-abc note='fallback after pin'
- Traces attached: trace-url: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/edg_7a3bf2 (customer provided)
Initial hypothesis: Control-plane propagation of the pin change is asynchronous; some requests route to newly preferred eu-west edge while in-flight control-plane or DNS state still points to us-east leading to mixed egress and handshake overhead. Secondary hypothesis: Token-scoped SNI or CDN cache not fully warmed for the new edge, causing TLS session warm-up and increased handshake times. Evidence: We see mixed selected_backend values within the 30s window after pin update. Auth logs show the token scope update at controlplane_tx=txn_9921 followed by a handful of requests routed to us-east for the same token. DNS TTL observed 20s on certain internal edges, and some client IPs hit a different POP due to geo-dns rounding. Related control-plane PR (see related_github_prs) introduced an optimization that batches pin writes; this may introduce a short propagation lag. Next steps: capture more tracer spans across multiple tenants, reproduce with synthetic load from different client IPs, instrument SNI selection path, and verify CDN and edge TLS session reuse metrics.

Additional notes:
Eng (Control Plane): Batching changes introduced to reduce DB writes were deployed recently; investigating whether commit visibility to edge proxies is delayed under bursty writes.
Customer (FinCloud): We prefer an explanation and a short-term workaround; we can schedule pin changes during low-traffic windows but need assurance the p95 won't spike for customers in production.
Workarounds provided: (1) apply pin toggles during maintenance windows and allow 90s for propagation, (2) pre-warm the target edge with a lightweight health/keepalive request to establish TLS sessions, (3) if possible, use console rollout canary instead of immediate toggle to reduce mixed routing. Engineering actions: control-plane team will adjust batching timer to commit pin writes sooner under dedicated tenant mode and add a short synchronous push to edge proxies for token-scope changes. SRE to monitor p95 over next 48 hours. Follow-up ticket created to track code change: INT-2026-controlplane-pin-flush (internal).

Issue summary: Customer reported an unexpected 'scaling-surcharge' charge on their finalized invoice for 2026-03-01 00:00-01:00 UTC. The charge corresponds to ~3 reserved GPU-hours that Veridian expected to be covered by their dedicated reservation. Impact: Customer sees a $1,250 line item labeled 'scaling-surcharge' and provisional negative balance that blocks autopay. Environment: Dedicated pool (veridian-prod-pool), prod/us-east-1, hourly billing window. Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Customer's dedicated pool autoscaled from 8->12 GPUs at 2026-03-01T00:07 during a scheduled warmup.
2) A set of asynchronous warmup jobs (internal tag: warmup-job, tenant tag: veridian-tenant) were executed and completed between 00:08-00:14.
3) Postback stream delivered usage records; postback ordering shows warmup postbacks arrived after hourly boundary reconciliation.
4) Finalized invoice shows scaling-surcharge line for 3 GPU-hours billed at on-demand uplift instead of consuming reserved hours. Expected behavior: Warmup tasks from dedicated pool should consume reserved capacity and be billed at the dedicated reserved rate, not the scaling/on-demand surcharge. Actual behavior: Three warmup hours attributed to on-demand/scale-surcharge due to rate-ladder recalculation at hour boundary after out-of-order postbacks. Logs/attachments: customer provided invoice PDF, warmup job IDs, and postback timestamps (attached).

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 11:25 - SRE (Ana Ruiz): Pulled postback ordering from kafka partition 12. Observed 3 warmup postbacks with produced_at 00:12:02 but consumed/acked 00:01:10 due to retry window; ordering index suggests they were reconciled after hourly aggregator ran. Possible race between hour-finalize job and late postbacks.
2026-03-13 13:08 - Billing eng (Marco Silva): Rate-ladder recalculation at 00:00 uses committed reservations snapshot. If late postbacks are applied after finalization, they should be backfilled into reserved bucket. Investigating aggregator idempotency and late-postback handling path.
2026-03-14 08:41 - Customer (Veridian Billing Ops - Jenna S.): Customer requests temporary credit for the $1,250 while engineering investigates; also wants confirmation that future warmup runs won't be billed at on-demand rates.
Hypothesis: Late postbacks and out-of-order delivery caused the hourly finalizer to mark the 3 warmup-hours as overflow/on-demand. Two contributing factors spotted: (1) autoscale-created warmup jobs are tagged 'warmup-job' and routed to async runner which posts back to a different partition causing replay ordering; (2) hourly aggregator (hourly-reconciler v2) finalizes rate-ladder then applies late-postbacks as separate 'overflow' items instead of reassigning into reserved bucket. Evidence: kafka offsets and aggregator logs show late_postback_handler invoked with 'overflow' flag at 00:05 and invoice generator accepted overflow lines. Repro: Simulated warmup jobs in staging with delayed postback show same surcharge behavior when postback arrives after aggregator finalization. Preliminary fix: Mark late postbacks with tenant reservation_id and trigger aggregator re-evaluation for the affected hour before finalization or apply retroactive backfill. Follow-up work: Introduce dedupe/backfill path in hourly-reconciler and ensure warmup jobs postback to main partition to avoid reorder. Related internal PR: INT-1289 references aggregator backfill prototype.
1) Refund or provisional credit for the $1,250 scaling-surcharge charged to Veridian for 2026-03-01 hour.
2) Code fix or compensating process to backfill late postbacks into reserved buckets so future warmup tasks are not billed at on-demand rates.
3) Confirmation note to customer and a short runbook describing warmup tagging best practices.
Pending - provisional credit requested from Billing team. Engineering to provide patch ETA.

Issue summary:

Customer (Nimbus Health) reports intermittent 403s for their scheduled export workers that run in the private VPC deployment. The failures started after an identity provider rotation on 2025-02-10 and affect long-running scheduled batch jobs that use SAML->session assertions created by the customer IdP.

Impact:
- Several nightly export jobs fail ~10-20% of runs across 3 tenants; when they fail the worker reports 403 from Redwood admin API token-swap endpoint.
- Customer visibility: export backfill delays; operational impact to downstream analytics pipeline.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) in eu-west region behind customer edge proxy.
- IdP: Customer-hosted SAML IdP (Shibboleth) with per-tenant metadata and rotating signing keys.
- Affected components: identity-proxy token-exchange path, session assertion ingestion, scheduled-worker token refresh flow.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) IdP rotates signing keys (metadata updated) and publishes new SAML assertions for service account login.
2) Scheduled worker obtains SAML assertion and posts to Redwood identity-proxy /assertion endpoint to exchange for session tokens.
3) Approximately 1 in 8 exchanges return 403 (unauthorized) with body: "authorization failed: assertion validation error: authnInstant mismatch".

Observed logs (customer and Redwood):
- identity-proxy logs (excerpt):
  "2025-02-11T02:14:12Z WARN assertion-validate tenant=nh-prod svc=scheduled-worker err=\"authnInstant parse error: invalid timezone offset\""
- token-swap endpoint returns 403 with structured error code AUTHN_INSTANT_PARSE_FAIL.
- No 5xx from upstream, no network errors reported.

Workaround reported by customer:
- Re-running the job after 30-60s succeeds in most cases.
- Temporary mitigation: customer disabled clock-skew strict validation on their IdP (not ideal).

Desired outcome:
- Determine root cause and provide a fix or recommended remediation for the customer's private deployment.
- Provide a non-invasive mitigation that does not require disabling IdP validation or manual retries for every job.
2025-02-11 09:12 - Support (Avery Chen): Acknowledged. Gathering logs and escalated to SRE. SLA P1 acknowledged. Working with customer to capture a full SAML assertion sample (redacted).
2025-02-11 11:03 - Customer (Helena Ortiz, Nimbus Health): We captured three failing assertions and attached them to the secure file share. Failures mostly occur in exporters scheduled between 02:00-03:30 UTC. No other services reported issues.
2025-02-11 13:22 - SRE (Marcus Patel): Initial triage: parity check between identity-proxy SAML parser and upstream library (python-saml) shows we reject timezone offsets with colon vs no-colon variants in offset part (e.g., +01:00 vs +0100) depending on incoming assertion format. We requested the actual Assertion XML from customer to confirm.
2025-02-12 08:45 - SRE (Marcus Patel): Confirmed failing assertions contain authnInstant="2025-02-11T02:12:34+01:00" while our parser path normalizes tz to +0100. Edge case occurs when IdP sends fractional seconds or the colon in offset is present; parser rejects when fractional seconds are present with colon. Working on a reproduction test harness.
2025-02-12 14:05 - Support (Avery Chen): Customer applied a short-term retry backoff in their scheduled worker and reports success rate improved to 98%. Requested permission to enable a permissive parsing fallback in identity-proxy for their private deployment as a hotfix.
2025-02-13 09:02 - Engineering (Sofia Rivera): Agreed to a targeted fallback. Will ship an opt-in config to the customer's control plane that enables relaxed SAML datetime parsing. Preparing patch and integration test to ensure strict mode remains default.
2025-02-13 12:30 - Customer (Helena Ortiz): Approved opt-in hotfix for relaxed parsing while upstream IdP team adjusts assertion generation. Please provide rollback steps.
2025-02-13 16:40 - SRE (Marcus Patel): Hotfix deployed to customer's private control plane: identity-proxy config flag 'saml_datetime_permissive=true'. Monitoring for 24h. Rollback: toggle flag to false and restart identity-proxy; documented in deployment notes.
1) Collected three failing Assertion XML payloads from customer; samples show authnInstant variants: with and without fractional seconds, with timezone offsets both in +HH:MM and +HHMM formats.
2) Reproduced parsing failure in unit test where authnInstant contained fractional seconds plus colon-based offset: our parser's regex expects either fractional seconds OR coloned offset, not both (legacy regex bug introduced in 2023 datetime refactor).
3) Hypothesis: IdP rotation triggered a minor change in assertion formatting (new IdP version returned timestamps with fractional seconds and coloned offsets). Because assertions are otherwise valid and signed, failures appear intermittent depending on which IdP node served the assertion (mix of old/new formatting during rotation).
4) Confirmed that strict validation path returns AUTHN_INSTANT_PARSE_FAIL before signature validation, therefore re-signing assertions won't help if parser rejects format.
Test harness: identity-proxy unit tests created with sample assertions; local runs show 1 failure pattern identical to customer.
5) Compatibility options explored: update regex to accept both formats, or add a permissive parsing path that normalizes datetime into RFC3339 canonical form before downstream validation. Chosen approach: permissive normalization with feature flag to avoid global behavior change.
6) Related risk: permissive parsing could mask malformed assertions. Mitigation: keep permissive mode opt-in per-customer; add additional assertion syntactic checks and log-level increase for discreet monitoring.
Hotfix: deployed opt-in identity-proxy configuration 'saml_datetime_permissive=true' to Nimbus Health private control plane on 2025-02-13 16:40 UTC. The permissive path normalizes authnInstant variants (handles fractional seconds and both +HH:MM and +HHMM offsets) and falls back to strict parsing for malformed values. Post-deployment monitoring (24h) shows failure rate dropped from ~12% to <1% for scheduled exporters.

Follow-ups:
- Engineering will submit upstream patch to identity-proxy master to include normalized parsing + unit tests (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/412). Target merge after security review.
- Ops: Provide a runbook entry for toggling 'saml_datetime_permissive' and guidance for customers during IdP rotations.
- Product/Security: Evaluate if permissive mode requires explicit customer acknowledgement as a documented compatibility tradeoff.

Status: Pending PR merge and post-24h monitoring completion. Customer accepted hotfix and will coordinate IdP patch rollout to remove the need for permissive mode.
- Ensure unit tests cover authnInstant formats with fractional seconds and both offset styles.
- Add telemetry metric AUTHN_INSTANT_PARSE_FALLBACK_COUNT per tenant to detect other customers who may benefit or be at risk.
- Draft customer-facing KB article describing the issue, safe workarounds, and steps to harden IdP assertion formatting.

Issue summary: Customer Findly reports that after a recent model rollout and automatic embedding-quantization optimization, search rerank orders for a subset of queries have inverted (previously top-3 items fall to bottom and vice versa).

Impact: Affecting several product search flows for Findly's production workspace on Dedicated capacity in us-east-1. Visible to ~2% of queries (but high business impact since these queries are high-conversion).

Environment: Dedicated cluster (pool-id d-101), embeddings served by rwd-embed-quant8-v2 variant in prod:us-east. Reranker service uses cosine similarity over 1024-d vectors; downstream ranking uses softmax on scores.

Expected behavior: Embeddings computed after rollout should be backward-compatible in ordering for high-similarity pairs; rank stability metric should not regress beyond thresholds.

Actual behavior: For certain queries, result order is inverted despite only small L2 differences. The shift appears correlated with embeddings produced by the quantized variant (rwd-embed-quant8-v2), while the full-precision model (rwd-embed-large-v2) shows expected ordering.

Additional context: Findly attached sample query IDs and old vs new embedding vectors (hashed). Customer observed change immediately after we enabled an aggressive precision-trimming optimization on the Dedicated pool intended to reduce memory and bandwidth.

1) Use Findly prod workspace on d-101 (us-east) with model rwd-embed-quant8-v2.
2) Run the provided canonical query set (attached in comments).
3) Generate embeddings via /v1/embeddings and run rerank endpoint (POST /v1/rerank) using cosine similarity on returned vectors.
4) Compare top-5 orders against same queries generated with rwd-embed-large-v2 on a non-quantized pool.
Initial hypothesis: precision truncation from int8 quantization is amplifying small angular differences, changing cosine orderings for near-tie vectors.
Reproduced locally by forcing quantize(embedding) and comparing pairwise cosine deltas between fp32->int8->fp32 upcast paths; observed sign flips in ~0.9% of pairs where true cosine difference < 1e-3.
Observed that our on-the-fly upcast used nearest-neighbor dequantization without the original scale/bias metadata in some Dedicated deployments — leading to inconsistent reconstruction of float vectors.
Caching interplay: prefix/KV cache was returning pre-quantized vectors for some requests while other requests invoked fresh computation with a different scale; mismatch surfaced in cross-batch reranking.
No evidence of NaNs or 5xx; scores are valid floats but ordering changed due to subtle numeric artifacts.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:22 - Support (Maya): Notified Findly we are investigating; provided temporary mitigation: pin workspace to rwd-embed-large-v2 and disabled auto-quant for their pool.
Workaround applied: Customer workspace pinned to rwd-embed-large-v2 and auto-quant disabled for their Dedicated pool. Hotfix deployed to embeddings-service to persist and transmit quantization scale/bias alongside int8 payloads. Validation added so cache entries without metadata are invalidated.
Planned permanent fix: Update quantization pipeline to use per-channel scales and deterministic rounding, add end-to-end unit tests for order-preservation on near-tie sets, and add telemetry to track rerank inversion rate per workspace.
Customer communication: Findly notified 2026-03-11 about workaround; follow-up scheduled for 2026-03-13 to coordinate re-testing and safe re-enable of optimized path.
INT-3412 - Add unit/regression tests for pairwise ordering preservation after quantization (assigned ML Infra).
INT-3420 - Add telemetry/dashboard for 'rerank inversion rate' per workspace and per model variant (assigned Observability).
INT-3431 - Review Dedicated pool upgrade checklist to ensure quantization metadata compatibility before opt-in (assigned Release Eng).
SUP-20412 - Post-mortem with customer-facing summary and timeline (assigned Support)
