payload.description:
Issue summary: During a morning traffic spike on 2026-03-05 ApolloHealth reported that their clinical-summary assistant returned inconsistent patient summaries for the same conversation session. Some completions omitted recently provided context and in one case combined content from unrelated sessions. This produced incorrect triage suggestions and violated ApolloHealth's SLA (95th percentile latency and correctness guarantee).

Reported impact: incorrect patient summaries in production, multiple customer-facing misclassifications, and an SLA credit request.

Initial customer-reported symptoms: session X returned an earlier cached summary while session Y returned newly appended clinical notes; both queries used same session_id and conversation_id in client logs.
Affecting 1.8% of ApolloHealth requests between 07:22–08:05 UTC in us-east-1. Observed incorrect completions for ~24 unique patient sessions; 3 customers escalated to Apollo's security/compliance team. SLA 95th-percentile latency breached and functional correctness violations reported.
1) Use ApolloHealth account credentials and simulate conversation with session_id=ap-h-<seed>.
2) Send a sequence of messages that append a new clinical note and ask for an updated summary.
3) Trigger a parallel request to the same session_id routed to a different replica (force by changing origin IP to simulate multi-edge routing).
4) Observe that one replica returns summary without appended note while the other includes it; occasionally responses mix fragments from unrelated sessions.
Key logs: session-coordinator: WARN session-affinity-mismatch for session_id=ap-h-9e3 (07:26:13). serving-runtime: ERROR kv-cache-denormalization detected for model=redwood-chat-7B (07:26:14). autoscaler: info added replica r-az2-14 (07:25:59); routing: debug routed request to r-az2-14 (07:26:12). Stack traces show fast restart of replica r-az2-14 and cache warmup. Full log excerpts saved to S3: s3://redwood-support/apollohealth/SUP-981234/logs-20260305.tgz
First responder (Support) validated client logs and asked for sample request IDs to correlate: client provided reqs 78a1, 78a4, 78b0.
SRE replicated traffic in staging with same autoscaler behavior and reproduced mismatch when autoscaler spawned a new replica while in-flight requests were being forwarded.
Hypothesis A: new replica handled a request before KV-prefetch completed leading to missing prefix context. Hypothesis B: session-affinity header was intermittently dropped by edge router causing two different replicas to handle sequential messages.
Correlation found between autoscaler replica addition and session-affinity expiration TTL of 60s — requests that hit newly added replica saw stale/no KV cache state for the session.
Telemetry: 98% of mismatches occurred within 30s of a replica lifecycle event (start/stop); tails aligned with autoscaler events in us-east-1 AZs.
Root cause: race between autoscaler and session-affinity/cache-warmup. New replicas accepted traffic prior to completing KV prefix population for live sessions. The routing layer allowed session-affinity to fall back to best-effort routing after affinity TTL expired; combined with fast replica joins this produced cross-session KV cache reads that manifested as missing context or interleaved fragments. Secondary factor: default affinity TTL (60s) and cache warmup latency (~5–12s) were not coordinated.
Short-term: applied emergency rollback to autoscaler scaling policy for ApolloHealth's dedicated pools (disabled reactive scale-ups for 10 minutes) and increased session-affinity TTL to 300s for the customer's routing policy, preventing mid-session reroutes. We also implemented a gate in serving-runtime: replica will reject requests for known session_ids until KV prefix warmup completes (feature flag ff/kv-warmup-gate enabled for ApolloHealth).

Long-term: engineering PR to modify autoscaler and routing handshake to ensure replica readiness signal is only returned after KV cache warmup and session-affinity handoff confirmed. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/15432 (merged 2026-03-11).

Customer communication: support sent an incident summary and remediation timeline on 2026-03-06; SLA credit offer and compliance evidence delivered on 2026-03-10.
ENG-1: Instrument warmup-ready metric and add healthcheck gating to routing (owner: @ethan-brooks, ETA: 2026-03-18).
ENG-2: Lower default affinity TTL configurable per-customer and document tradeoffs (owner: @maria-gonzales, ETA: 2026-03-22).
OPS-1: Add automated canary for replica-join warmup behavior and alert when in-flight requests routed to non-warm replicas (owner: @sre-oncall, ETA: 2026-03-15).
CS-1: Follow up with ApolloHealth compliance to confirm acceptance of evidence package and closure of their audit request (owner: @maya-chen, ETA: 2026-03-12).
DOC-1: Update runbook for session-affinity incidents and include steps for temporary policy adjustments (owner: @docs-team, ETA: 2026-03-19).
payload.summary: ApolloHealth: conversation state inconsistency across replicas causing incorrect patient summaries and SLA breach - follow-up

payload.description:
Issue summary:
At ~2026-03-12 10:40 UTC DataSage (dedicated pool) reported sudden p50/p99 throughput collapse for batched routes. No standard autoscaler events or capacity shortages were shown in high-level dashboards. Investigation found a background snapshotter process holding ephemeral GPU reservations (not visible in normal slot metrics) and producing heartbeat jitter that the autoscaler sensor interpreted as a large increase in small-streams, triggering conservative shrink decisions and preventing new attachments.

Impact:
- Customer: DataSage Analytics (dedicated) experienced ~60% drop in sustained throughput across pinned batched routes for ~45 minutes.
- Business: SLA blips for the customer during peak processing window.

Timeline (brief):
- 10:38 UTC: Monitoring alert p99 throughput up > 2x for DataSage reserved pool.
- 10:40 UTC: Customer opened support channel and ticket (this issue).
- 10:45 UTC: Support triaged to SRE; initial telemetry collected.
- 10:55 UTC: SRE observed slot attach backlog and autoscaler downscale triggers.
- 11:10 UTC: Identified snapshotter snapshots running concurrently on GPUs; manual restart of snapshotter replica started at 11:18 UTC.
- 11:25 UTC: Throughput recovered to baseline by 11:30 UTC; ticket escalated to eng for fix.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: ds-data-prod-usw1
- Region: us-west
- Runtime image: rw-infer-2026-02-26
- Autoscaler sensor window configuration: 30s sample / 3-min smoothing

Steps to reproduce (repro is non-trivial; approximated):
1) Provision a dedicated pool with a background snapshotter configured to write incremental checkpoints every ~2 minutes.
2) Generate a mix of long-batched requests and many small short streams from a synthetic tenant.
3) Trigger concurrent snapshot compaction (simulate snapshotter scanning incremental checkpoints).
4) Observe slot attach latencies, autoscaler downscale events and throughput drop.

Observed logs & metrics excerpts:
- serving-runtime logs: "attach_delay_ms=1250 slot_reserve_attempts=3" repeated across hosts.
- snapshotter logs: "Compacting checkpoint shard: gpu0 shard_id=17 reserved_fd=1" (multiple hosts)
- autoscaler telemetry: downscale_decision{window=180s} -> aggressive_shrink due to perceived small-stream fraction rising from 0.12 -> 0.47 in 2 minutes.
- NVMe/IO metrics: short I/O latency spikes (p99 IO latency increased 3x during compaction windows).

Business/Customer notes:
Customer observed backlog of queued requests in their application and reported higher retry rates. DataSage is mid-enterprise and depends on predictable reserved throughput during daily processing windows.
2026-03-12 10:42 - Support (Aisha): Logged initial ticket after customer report; requested pool and route IDs. Asked for immediate telemetry and SRE triage.
2026-03-12 10:51 - SRE (Marco): Observed attach backlog and autoscaler downscale traces. Collecting diag bundles from ds-data-prod-usw1 hosts. Punting to infra-engineer for snapshotter correlation.
2026-03-12 11:06 - Infra (Lina Gomez): Snapshotter compaction jobs found running on 6/8 GPUs in pool; compaction holds temporary file descriptors and pins GPU memory briefly. Scheduled manual restart of snapshotter replica to confirm impact.
2026-03-12 11:20 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed throughput recovery; continuing monitoring. Will provide postmortem and timeline to customer.
2026-03-13 09:10 - Eng (Marco): Root cause fix merged to infra branch to add backpressure limiter and change compaction window. PR linked. Planning canary deploy to staging today.
Hypothesis 1: Snapshotter compaction holds ephemeral GPU reservations + generates IO bursts leading to attach latencies and autoscaler mis-reading small-stream fraction.
Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler sensor window too narrow combined with IO-induced attach jitter caused aggressive shrink decisions instead of transient stabilization.
Evidence: Correlated timestamps between snapshotter compaction log entries and autoscaler downscale events across 6 hosts. IO p99 spikes coincident with attach_delay_ms spikes. No driver or hardware errors present.
Repro attempt: Local repro with injected IO compaction on small test pool reproduced autoscaler reacting within the configured window; increasing autoscaler smoothing prevents premature shrink.
Short-term mitigation tested: Restart snapshotter replica -> immediate drop in attach delays and autoscaler stabilized; validated by customer during recovery window.
Root cause: Snapshotter compaction jobs on tenant-dedicated hosts were performing concurrent checkpoint compactions that temporarily pinned GPU resources via ephemeral reservations and produced short NVMe IO pressure. The autoscaler’s small-stream fraction sensor and smoothing window interpreted attach jitter as a shift toward many short streams and made conservative downscale decisions, preventing new attachments and reducing throughput.

Fixes implemented:
- Infra PR #4578: add compaction backpressure limiter to snapshotter (limits concurrent compactions per host) and make compaction IO more rate-limited.
- Autoscaler config change: increase smoothing window from 3m to 5m for dedicated pools and add a guard to ignore single-window spikes when attach_delay_ms > 800ms but without slot-free events.
- Monitoring: New alert created for "snapshotter_compaction_rate" and "attach_delay_ms" correlation; dashboard panel added to dedicated pool runbook.

Rollout & follow-up:
- PR merged 2026-03-12; staged canary deployed to staging cluster 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC; no regressions observed.
- Production rollout scheduled in two phases: low-traffic pools then full rollout (completed 2026-03-13 08:00 UTC).
- Postmortem: schedule follow-up with DataSage to review SLAs and offer 10% credit for the impacted window.
- Owner for permanence: Marco Lin (infra) to track post-deploy metrics for 7 days and close monitoring with CS.
payload.summary: Silent snapshotter process reserving GPU slots and causing autoscaler sensor misclassification leading to dedicated throughput collapse

Requesting runtime logs and PR that introduced opt-profile change. Asked customer to toggle tenant-level profile to baseline as a temporary rollback.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer NovaHealth reported that after a targeted optimizer-profile migration for a small set of tenants, a subset of streaming responses were truncated mid-stream and some requests returned 499 client disconnects. This began immediately after a staged opt-config push that enabled a mixed-quant + aggressive KV-prefetch profile for their workload.

Impact:
- Several NovaHealth integration endpoints experienced truncated streaming sessions for ~12% of requests to their /chat/stream route.
- Tail latency increased from 180ms to 1.2s for affected tenants.
- No token-level quality regressions reported, but user-facing sessions were interrupted.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated cluster (dedicated pool for NovaHealth) in prod us-west-2.
- Model: redwood-lm-3b-v2 pinned.
- Opt-profile applied via central config-service (staged rollout: tenant gating, 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 90m).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Use NovaHealth tenant API key and send streaming chat requests with frequent short prompts (~30 tokens).
2) Observe that ~1 in 8 streams terminates early with client-side disconnect and server-side 499.
3) Reverting opt-profile at tenant level appears to restore prior behavior.

Logs / Observations:
- Serving-runtime logs show intermittent KV cache eviction spikes and a correlated increase in upstream send buffer full events.
- Traces show a subset of requests hit a mix of kernel paths (quantized + prefetch) and experienced unexpected loopback on the per-request router creating a fast-path abort.
- No underlying GPU OOMs.

Customer request:
- Assistance to safely snapshot current opt-config state, perform an atomic restore to pre-change profile for affected tenants, and guidance on per-tenant gating best practices to avoid rollout blast radius.

Workaround attempted by customer:
- Manual removal of tenant opt override restored normal behavior. Customer requests a reproducible, supported procedure they can follow in future and confirmation we will investigate root cause.

Additional notes:
2026-03-05 11:45 - SRE (Maya Chen): Observed same 499 signatures in load balancer logs correlated with short-duration spikes of write stalls on the RPC channel. No host-level network issues. Captured a flamegraph from runtime during spike window.
2026-03-06 08:22 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Found a race in kernel selection when a request toggles between cached KV-path and quantized path mid-request. Filed infra PR to add guard (see related_github_prs). Recommended atomic opt-config snapshot/restore procedure.
Timeline and findings:
- 2026-03-05: Initial reports and sample IDs collected.
- 2026-03-05: SRE captured LB and runtime metrics; observed 499s and write stalls.
- 2026-03-06: Eng reproduced a race locally when opt-profile toggles mid-request; root cause: kernel selection path lacked an in-flight request guard when prefix-KV cache eviction and quantized kernel selection coincided.
- Hypothesis: The staged rollout exposed a rare state where a request saw a config delta mid-eviction, causing the runtime to switch execution paths and drop the streaming write without retry.
- Evidence: runtime trace and flamegraph; matching request IDs across serving-runtime and LB.
- Mitigating action: snapshot current config and perform atomic tenant-level restore.
- Additional observation: higher incidence for short prompts due to tighter batching windows and increased sensitivity to KV cache behavior.
Next steps recommended by Eng team:
1) Merge guard fix in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/412 (adds in-flight request pin during kernel selection).
2) Publish a snapshot/restore runbook for ops and customers with explicit atomicity checks.
3) Update rollout policy: increase initial gating checks, add canary with end-to-end streaming smoke tests, and extend observation window before wider rollout.
4) Create monitoring alert for sudden increase in 499 streaming disconnects and KV eviction rate.
Actions performed to resolve:
- Captured a consistent snapshot of NovaHealth opt-config (snap-20260307-nh) before any changes.
- Executed an atomic restore to the pre-migration baseline profile for all NovaHealth tenant IDs during a scheduled low-traffic window (2026-03-07 02:00-02:20 UTC).
- Verified streaming endpoints for customer (end-to-end synthetic smoke tests).
- Monitored tail latency, KV eviction rates, and 499/stream-disconnect counts for 72h post-restore; metrics returned to baseline.
- Eng pushed hotfix PR to add in-flight request guard and a subtle config-change mutex; PR linked above.
Follow-ups and recommendations given to customer:
- Use tenant-level snapshot before any opt-profile changes: run config-service snapshot command and capture the snapshot id.
- For staged rollouts, start with a small canary of 1% tenant traffic and run an automated streaming smoke test for 30m before expanding.
- Avoid combining quantization changes and aggressive KV-prefetch in the same initial canary; separate those changes across independent rollout waves.
- If you need an emergency restore: provide snapshot id and tenant IDs to support and we will execute an atomic restore. Provided documented steps and a one-time assisted runbook to the customer.
- Engineering will schedule the hotfix to roll through Dedicated clusters this week; we will follow up when the fix is in canary and when fully rolled out.
Atomic snapshot/restore checklist (summary):
- Verify snapshot id integrity (sha256) and timestamp.
- Put tenant(s) into maintenance mode to quiesce new long-running streams.
- Execute restore via config-service with --atomic flag.
- Confirm via synthetic streaming smoke test and edge LB logs that 499s have stopped.
- If still present, escalate to runtime oncall and collect traces and per-request kernel selection logs.
- After restore, re-enable staged rollout with separate waves for quantization and KV-prefetch.
payload.summary: Atomic optimizer-config snapshot/restore and per-tenant gating assistance after mixed-opt changes caused stream truncation

payload.description:
Issue summary: Midday we observed a gradual throughput degradation and p99 latency growth for a NimbleTranslate dedicated pool. Traffic pattern unchanged; the autoscaler started oscillating (add/remove cycles) and many short batched requests were deferred for several seconds before execution.
Impact: Customer requests hit p99 latencies of 8–12s and observed occasional 5xx spikes; downstream SLA alerts triggered.
Environment: Dedicated capacity (pool-id: pool-nimble-az1), region us-east, GPU type: A100-40GB with NVLink, serving-runtime v2.8.3, autoscaler v1.4.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Replay NimbleTranslate midday traffic pattern via load-test (small short streams + bursts). 2) Watch allocator attach rates + NVLink error metrics. 3) Observe autoscaler decisions and slot attach/detach events.
Observed behavior: - At ~12:05 UTC we saw short intermittent NVLink/PCIe completion delays (what we label as "sputter") lasting 100–400ms at 1–2 minute cadence. - These delays caused the internal batcher to push several small batches into deferred state; deferred queue length grew from 0 to ~200 in 7 minutes. - Autoscaler interpreted elevated queue length as capacity shortage and tried to add nodes; new nodes attached but their initial attach throughput was low because the same IO sputter persisted, leading to quick scale-downs. - End result: autoscaler oscillation (add -> remove -> add) for ~20 minutes and a net throughput reduction.
Relevant metrics/logs: - nvlink_err_count spiked in short bursts (see graph link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/xyz/nvlink-errors). - pci_io_completion_ms 95th jumped from 12ms -> 380ms intermittently. - Allocator logs show repeated attach timeouts followed by retries: "attach_slot(timeout) -> retry". - Autoscaler decisions: add-node at 12:08, remove-node at 12:11, add-node at 12:13 (see autoscaler audit: https://logs.redwood/auto/2026-03-10/12).
Hypotheses considered: 1) Noisy tenant saturating NVLink lanes (some tenant performing heavy allreduce-like IO). 2) Hardware-level PCIe switch hiccups causing transient completion latency. 3) Driver-level regression in CUDA/NVML that surfaces under mixed short-stream workloads.
Quick checks performed: - Correlated tenant IDs with NVLink spikes; found tenant tx-778 (internal analytics) had a burst of small heavy-IO jobs coincident with incidents. - SRE run 'nvlink-reset' on one host: transient improvement observed for ~15m. - Driver rolling window: no recent driver upgrades in that zone in past 48h. - Kernel dmesg on one affected host shows occasional 'PCIe completion timeout' warnings at time of spikes.
Current working theory: combination of a noisy tenant causing periodic NVLink fanout plus a hardware PCIe completion sensitivity causing IO completion tail. This combination magnifies deferred-batching behavior and misleads autoscaler heuristics.
Investigation owners: Diego (SRE), Lina Chen (infra).
Immediate mitigations (in-progress): 1) Triage noisy tenant: asked customer and platform to throttle/limit tx-778 analytics batch window; SRE applied soft throttling on that tenant for 30m. 2) Temporarily widen autoscaler hysteresis: bump scale-up cool-down to 3m and scale-down window to 8m for pool-nimble-az1 to avoid rapid churn. 3) Isolate affected hosts: schedule workloads away from hosts that show persistent PCIe warnings.
Follow-ups: - Replace suspect PCIe switch hardware on two hosts (ticketed with infra vendor). - Add NVLink/pci IO tail alerts and enrich autoscaler heuristics to ignore short transient IO spikes under X seconds.
Owner: Diego Ramos. ETA for vendor replacement: 2026-03-16.

2026-03-10 12:25 - Support (Aisha): Customer reported p99 rising and some requests failing; escalated to SRE. Slack thread: #support-pool-nimble.

Issue summary:
During a peak ingest window on 2026-03-10 08:45–09:20 PST, Falkon Systems reported that semantic search results returned incorrect document ids for a subset of recently ingested vectors. Simultaneously, audit logs for ingestion latency and billing counters were missing for a 22-minute interval which prevented Falkon from reconciling billed usage.

Impact:
- Customer-facing search returned stale or mismatched results for ~3.2% of queries routed to the dense-index-service in us-west-2.
- Falkon reported a billing delta (observed vs expected) of ~12% for the ingestion window due to missing audit log events.
- Customer escalated to enterprise support; legal/finance looped in for potential credits.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (customer-managed VPC peering) in us-west-2 using embedding-encoder-v2 -> dense-index-service (quantized).
- Autoscale pool scaled up at 08:40 but indexer pod restarts were observed between 08:46 and 08:53.

Steps to reproduce (investigation checklist rather than deterministic repro):
1) Ingest high-throughput batch (approx 18k vectors/min) with mixed small and large payloads.
2) Observe indexer task restarts in the dense-index kube pool.
3) Run sample search for recently ingested document ids and compare to precomputed vector->id map.
4) Check audit-log stream for missing log sequence numbers in the 08:45–09:07 window.

Logs / telemetry pointers:
- Observability trace: https://observability.redwood.internal/traces/2026-03-10/idx-mismatch-08-47
- Grafana panel: embeddings-indexer pod restarts: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/embeddings/indexer-pod-restarts?from=2026-03-10T08:30:00Z&to=2026-03-10T09:30:00Z
- Billing delta dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/billing/deltas/falkon/2026-03-10

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Switched Falkon to a pinned read-route that bypasses the in-flight indexer shard (read-only replication) while we replayed the missing events into the index.
- Issued temporary billing credit to cover immediately visible delta pending reconciliation.

Customer impact and communication:
- Customer was updated on-call and received an interim timeline within 30 minutes. Finance requested formal reconciliation and credits; CS opened this ticket to coordinate post-incident follow-up and evidence delivery.
2026-03-10T09:05Z - Lydia Park (Customer Success): Customer on the line; reporting returned results pointing to wrong doc ids. They can reproduce against queries hitting us-west. Asked for immediate mitigation and credit hold. Escalating to SRE.
2026-03-10T09:12Z - Priya Nair (SRE): Observed 3 indexer pod restarts starting 08:46. Restarted due to OOM eviction on node gpu-12. Raising hypothesis: burst ingest + large batch led to memory pressure on indexer causing partial write batches to be lost before durable ack to audit log stream.
2026-03-10T09:30Z - Evan Chen (Engineer, Index Service): Found gaps in RSM (replicated state machine) commit log for shard-7 between 08:46:23 and 08:58:41. Some commit entries were retained in local ephemeral storage but not flushed to the audit-log producer before the process restart.
2026-03-10T10:10Z - Raul Mendez (Falkon DevOps): Confirmed behavior from our side: ~11% of recent ingest batch ids not present when we ran verification against our sidecar map. Appreciate the temp read-route fix. Need formal reconciliation file and proof of replay before we close billing request.
2026-03-11T14:22Z - Marco Ortega (Assignee): Replay completed and verified. Attached reconciliation CSV to customer Slack and Confluence. Initiated billing adjustment flow. Planning a postmortem and longer-term fix (persistent commit flush before ack).
2026-03-12T16:00Z - Aisha Kumari (Support): Customer accepted reconciliation and billing credit. Customer asked for a timeline for persistent fix and a test plan for future peak ingest scenarios. Added to post-incident action items.
Timeline and findings:
- 08:40: autoscaler increased indexer pool to handle surge; several indexer pods scheduled onto new GPU node types.
- 08:46: node gpu-12 experienced transient memory pressure; kernel OOM killed indexer process leading to abrupt restart.
- 08:46–08:59: RSM commit log had unflushed entries that were not propagated to the audit-log Kafka topic due to in-memory batching.
- 08:59–09:10: indexer recovered, but some vector->id mappings were written to ephemeral local store only; replication missed the durable ack.
Root cause hypothesis:
- Combination of aggressive in-memory batching in the dense-index-service and a recent change that increased batch size for latency optimization caused larger transient memory usage. When a pod was OOM-killed, in-memory batch in producer was lost before flush to audit log, creating both search inconsistency and missing billing events.
Contributing factors:
- Autoscaler packed pods onto a smaller set of nodes during the burst (bin-packing behavior).
- No enforced pre-ack flush semantics for commit batches on indexer restart.
Evidence:
- Commit log gaps in index shard-7 trace.
- Missing sequence ranges in audit-log topic for 08:46–09:07.
- Pod OOM event records on node gpu-12.
- Replayed entries successfully restored search parity and reduced billing delta to <0.2%.
Immediate remediation:
1) Executed controlled replay of missing commit ranges into indexer from durable write-ahead log stored in object storage.
2) Temporarily pinned Falkon read-route to read-only replica while replay completed.
3) Issued pro-rated billing credit covering the measured delta; finance notified and reconciliation file delivered.
Permanent fixes applied (short-term):
- Rolled out indexer v2.1.3 which reduces in-memory batch size under memory pressure and forces flush on SIGTERM.
- Autoscaler safety adjustment to avoid bin-packing sensitive pods onto a single node by setting podAntiAffinity hints in dense-index-service deploy.
- Added alert rule for audit-log sequence gaps and a check for commit-flush duration > 2s.
Follow-up verification:
- Post-deploy canary with synthetic high-throughput ingest (20k vectors/min) passed for 3 consecutive 30-minute windows with no commit gaps.
Customer communication:
- Shared reconciliation CSV, replay proof, and audit-log segment references. Finance accepted credit; customer closed the escalation after verification.
Create a durable flush-on-commit test and add to CI for indexer (owner: Evan Chen) - due 2026-03-20
Adjust autoscaler bin-packing policy for indexer class pods (owner: Priya Nair) - due 2026-03-18
Run a cross-team runbook review session with SRE, Indexing, and Billing to validate audit-log handoff semantics (owner: Marco Ortega) - due 2026-03-25
Provide Falkon with a monthly report for two months showing post-fix ingest parity and billing reconciliations (owner: Lydia Park) - deliver by 2026-04-10
Add an observability dashboard to surface audit-log sequence continuity per-customer and per-shard (owner: Observability Team) - due 2026-03-22

Issue summary: Between 2024-11-02 15:05 and 2024-11-02 15:40 UTC StratosCargo began seeing intermittent streaming truncation and missing transcript segments from their private VPC deployment. Impact: ~18% of streaming completions returned truncated transcripts (client received EOT prematurely) and ~6% of requests resulted in silent streaming resets. Customer reports production user-facing failures and requested immediate remediation and SLA credit. Environment: Private deployment (vpc-connect) hosted in us-central, running private control plane v2.3.1 and inference nodes on GPU pool 'private-usc-phi'. Immediate ask: identify root cause, mitigate to restore streaming reliability to >99.9%, and agree next steps for rollback/patch and customer SLA remedy.
1) Customer long-running chat session with streaming enabled and model redwood-llm-13b-quantized-v1 pinned.
2) Send multi-turn prompts with frequent resets of client-side TLS session (simulated NAT timeouts).
3) Observe intermittent early stream termination and missing transcript ranges.
4) Reproduce more reliably by triggering TLS renegotiation at burst rates (NAT rebind + client reconnects).
[15:05:17 UTC] node-07 TLS renegotiation initiated from 10.12.5.22
[15:05:17 UTC] node-07 stream session id=acb-7f terminated (early-eof) code=STREAM_RESET reason=peer-magic
[15:05:18 UTC] gateway auth proxy reconnection count=12 for customer StratosCargo
[15:05:19 UTC] serving-runtime: kv-cache miss for prefix session=acb-7f
[15:05:21 UTC] node-07 TLS handshake completed (new session)
[15:05:22 UTC] stream resumption succeeded but transcript gap detected tokens missing: [1021-1044]
[15:05:25 UTC] node-07 cpu spike 78% while performing TLS renegotiation
[15:06:10 UTC] rate limiter logged bursts on private-usc-phi pool (burst-window exceeded)
[15:10:04 UTC] SRE: observed correlated increase in 5xx for streaming endpoints (endpoint/stream)

Hypotheses: 1) Client-side aggressive TLS renegotiation + private NAT behaviour causing session churn and premature stream resets. 2) TLS renegotiation path triggers a short-lived state where serving-runtime drops active stream checkpoint leading to transcript gaps. 3) Rate limiter/autoscaler reaction created a brief resource pressure window on node-07, exacerbating resets. Findings: - Reproduced spike by simulating TLS session churn; early-eof correlates with active TLS renegotiation window (~200-400ms). - Kernel selection / quantized model execution continues but session affinity mapping to streaming multiplexer briefly returned 502-like resets. - Node-level metrics show CPU and epoll wake spikes coincident with handshake bursts. - No evidence of data corruption on disk or model weights. Related artifacts: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/stratos-tls-storm, packet captures uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/stratos/tls-storm-pcaps/
Maya Patel (Support) 2024-11-02T15:18Z: Acknowledged with customer and opened incident. Notified SRE and Private Deploy team. Customer reports user-visible truncation, requested ETA for mitigation.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2024-11-02T15:25Z: Initial triage: saw TLS renegotiation bursts on node-07. Spinning up node-09 as hot spare and enabling conservative reconnect backoff for customer route. Requesting traffic mirroring to test cluster.
Aisha Khan (Private Deploy Eng) 2024-11-02T15:40Z: Found that our TLS stack allowed renegotiation to skip stream resume handshake in the multiplexer when handshake overlapped with chunk flush. Applying short-term patch to hold stream state until handshake completion. Will deploy to canary group now.
StratosCargo (Customer) 2024-11-02T16:00Z: Thank you for quick response—we saw improvement after you enabled backoff. Please confirm what caused this and what the compensation will be for impacted customers.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2024-11-03T09:12Z: Canary patch confirmed in canary (node-09/10), dropped truncated streams below 0.3%. Scheduling full rollout 2024-11-03T10:00Z with monitoring and rollback on failure. Preparing customer-facing incident summary and SLA credit calculation.
Maya Patel (Support) 2024-11-04T11:48Z: Incident resolved with full rollout complete. Preparing formal post-incident follow-up and credit offer.
Mitigation steps: 1) Applied a hotfix to the private TLS multiplexer to defer stream state teardown until TLS renegotiation completes and stream chunks are flushed. 2) Enabled conservative reconnect/backoff policy for StratosCargo route to reduce NAT-triggered handshake storms. 3) Added temporary node headroom (scaled private-usc-phi pool + spun up node-09) during remediation window. Rollout notes: patch rolled to canary at 2024-11-02T15:50Z, observed drop in truncated streams from 18%->0.3% in canary, full rollout completed 2024-11-03T10:20Z. Post-incident customer action: Support offered SLA credit and scheduled 2024-11-06 deep-dive call. Root cause: overlap between client-initiated TLS renegotiation and the streaming multiplexer teardown path exposed a race that caused early EOFs and missing transcript fragments under high renegotiation rates. Engineering fix: patch to multiplexer to await handshake completion and explicit chunk-flush acknowledgement before session teardown. Monitoring and prevention: added alerting for TLS renegotiation rate >10/s per node, introduced canary traffic test that simulates NAT rebind scenarios, and updated the private-deploy runbook.
Deploy multiplexer race-condition unit tests into CI to cover TLS renegotiation overlap
Add synthetic canary that simulates NAT rebind/TLS renegotiation to PR gate and canary pipelines
Update private-deploy runbook with explicit TLS renegotiation troubleshooting steps
Create customer communication template for private TLS incidents and SLA credit process
Schedule cross-team retro (SRE, Private Deploy, Networking) for 2024-11-08

Issue summary:
Customer AtlasHealth (dedicated pool) reported a sharp rise in 5xx responses impacting both chat streaming and embedding upload endpoints. Error rate rose from baseline ~0.4% to ~12% over an 18-minute window starting 2026-03-14T09:12:00Z. Impacted tenants saw streaming disconnects and ~50% of large embedding uploads failing with 502/503/504 variants.

Impact:
- Customer reported degraded UX for interactive chat and failed background embedding jobs.
- Estimated 30% of requests for this tenant returned 5xx during the peak.
- No invoice/billing discrepancies reported.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool: cluster-dedicated-usw-06 (prod-us-west)
- Ingress: api-gateway (v2.7.1) fronting tenant routes
- Serving runtime: redwood-runtime 1.13.0 (nvml 520.61)
- Observed on model variants: openchat-v2-large (fp16) and embed-small-quant (int8)

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer runs interactive sessions (long-lived streaming) while concurrently uploading large embedding batches (multipart uploads, 10k vectors).
2) After ~10 minutes of sustained mixed load, api-gateway accept-queue length grows and hedged retries increase.
3) Serving runtimes start to exhibit GPU driver NVML resets on a subset of workers, followed by runtime worker restarts and KV cache thrashing.
4) Requests routed to affected hosts return 502/503/504. Canary route weights shifted (see investigation) causing traffic to concentrate on warm-but-fragmented instances.

Observed logs / metrics snippets:
- api-gateway: accept_queue_length: 0 -> 420 in 12m; open_fds trending up; 5xx_rate: 0.4% -> 11.7%
- runtime kube events: "nvml: GPU driver reset" on nodes gw-rt-07, gw-rt-09 at 2026-03-14T09:25:42Z
- runtime logs: repeated OOM watcher restarts followed by watchdog kill: "runtime: fatal: nvml reset observed, initiating restart"
- kvcache: eviction_rate spike 6x, cold-prefetch latency 220ms -> 1.9s

Initial hypothesis:
- Mixed workload (long-lived streaming + large embedding multipart uploads) caused connection and kernel pressure at the API gateway and runtime layer.
- Canary/route-weight rebalancing (recent automated shift) amplified concentration of heavy requests on hosts with fragmented GPU memory, triggering NVML resets and subsequent runtime restarts.
- KV cache lock contention during simultaneous prefetches aggravated tail latency and increased hedged retries, amplifying load in a feedback loop.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Support manually paused customer's bulk embedding uploads at 09:32Z (customer cooperated).
- Traffic temporarily shifted off nodes gw-rt-07 and gw-rt-09 via healthcheck weight adjustment at 09:36Z.
- Autoscaler set to immediate scale-up + drain policy to avoid colocating new heavy jobs on warm instances.

Status / next steps:
- Eng SRE oncall (Miguel) currently reproducing failure mode in a scaled staging cluster with a synthetic mix of long-lived streams + large embedding batch uploads.
- Short-term: continue to keep heavy embedding upload policy rate-limited for AtlasHealth.
- Mid-term: evaluate guardrails: per-tenant concurrent-streams cap OR simultaneous-embed-upload threshold; introduce slower prewarm/rehab routing after NVML-resets to avoid immediate traffic reattachment.
- Long-term: investigate kernel fallback behavior and kvcache lock avoidance; consider runtime patch to reduce aggressive prefetch during observed high-conn scenarios.

Customer-facing note:
- Customer informed 09:40Z about active mitigation and recommended to resubmit failed embedding jobs after 2 hours or use smaller batch sizes. Support will follow up with a post-incident summary when investigation completes.
2026-03-14T09:18Z - Support (Aisha): Triage started after AtlasHealth reported streaming disconnects and embedding failures. Gathering initial metrics and requested upload job IDs.
2026-03-14T09:26Z - SRE (Miguel): Observed NVML resets on two runtime hosts; increasing accept-queue at apigw. Paused customer embedding uploads and started draining affected hosts.
2026-03-14T09:34Z - Support (Aisha): Confirmed customer paused uploads. Customer reports improved streaming stability but intermittent failures persist for short-lived requests.
2026-03-14T09:45Z - SRE (Miguel): KVCACHE eviction/lock contention visible; running a synthetic repro in staging; suspect hedged-retry amplification. Creating linked issue for autoscaler/route gating work.
2026-03-14T10:10Z - Product (Leah Bhandari): Noted recent route-weight sweep that coincided with onset. Requesting logs from traffic-manager to correlate weight change timestamps.
2026-03-14T11:05Z - SRE (Miguel): Staging repro triggered NVML reset when embedding multipart size >= 8k vectors concurrently with 250 active streams. Captured kernel traces and NVML logs; attaching to related PR.
2026-03-14T12:00Z - Support (Aisha): Notified customer of temporary rate-limits and next update ETA 2026-03-14T16:00Z.
Healthcheck weights: traffic manager applied automated weight change at 2026-03-14T09:11:32Z — correlates to customer traffic ramp.
Node gw-rt-07 shows GPU memory fragmentation pattern consistent with long lived cache + embedding allocations; NVML resets correlate with fragmentation windows.
Hedged retries doubled during tail-latency spikes, increasing load on worker set by ~28% in peak window.
No immediate evidence of hardware fault — suspect fragmentation + driver stress; vendor driver team engaged if repro confirms deterministic NVML reset.
Potential quick fix: avoid immediate route reattachment to instances that recently reported NVML resets; route-manager should add a cooldown label.
Follow-up created: INT-210203 to track autoscaler/drain policy tuning (internal).
Mitigations applied (paused customer's heavy uploads; drained affected hosts; temporary rate limits). Root cause investigation ongoing. No permanent fix yet; working on route-manager cooldown and prefetch/backpressure improvements.
Collect full trace bundles from affected runtimes and apigw between 09:00-10:00Z
Complete staging repro and confirm NVML reset trigger conditions
Define and ship short-term rate-limits/guardrails for dedicated pools (per-tenant concurrency caps)
Create follow-up engineering tickets for kvcache lock improvements and route-manager cooldown behavior

Issue summary:
Customer NovaMind received a one-off surplus invoice line for a high-volume embedding job dated 2026-03-09. The line shows ~1.8M embedding tokens charged as ‘probe:edge-metrics’ at hosted rates. Customer states they only ran a 150k-token batch job.

Impact:
- Customer reports an unexpected $4,350 charge on finalized invoice for org ID org-novamind-77.
- Customer is enterprise tier with monthly billing and is asking for provisional credit and root cause.

Environment:
- Production (us-east). Keys: key-****-prod bound to org-novamind-77.
- Billing pipeline: postback-receiver -> hourly-accumulator -> invoice-generator.

Steps to reproduce / observations:
1) Customer ran batch embedding on 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC (150k tokens).
2) Billing shows additional postbacks at 2026-03-09 02:18–02:26 UTC labeled probe:edge-metrics from retired probe edge proxies.
3) Postback consumer accepted the probe entries and attributed them to the customer org prefix due to a missing namespace tag after the probe fleet decommission.
4) Offline reconciler merged these into the hourly accumulator; invoice pipeline picked them up in finalized invoice dated 2026-03-10.

Logs / evidence:
- Postback receiver logs (prod-us-east) 2026-03-09T02:18Z: incoming POST id=pb-9f7e probe=true namespace=null org_prefix=org-novamind-77
- Accumulator trace: commit batch_id=accum-20260309-02 shard=5 included 1.8M token_count flagged as probe-origin
- Invoice line: invoice-20260310: line_item id=line-889 probe:edge-metrics qty=1800000 rate_id=hosted-embed

Customer requested outcome:
- Immediate provisional credit for the surplus line and removal from final invoice while investigation proceeds.
- Root cause and mitigation plan to prevent recurrence.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:45 - Customer (NovaMind - Tomas Li): Provided batch job logs and API key id. Confirms they did not trigger probe traffic. Asks for ETA on refund.
2026-03-11 08:30 - SRE (Marta Nguyen): Found decommissioned probe fleet had a scheduled replay job that failed to set namespace headers after the decommission change. Linked to deploy 2026-03-09T01:50 UTC.
Hypothesis 1: legacy probe replay process replayed buffered events without namespace metadata, causing attribution to the first-matching org_prefix (customer's key).
Hypothesis 2: postback-receiver lacked a post-decommission filter for probe origin, allowing probe=true messages to be routed into billing path.
Confirmed: probe fleet deploy 2026-03-09T01:50 removed namespace header in 2 of 3 replay workers due to config drift (diff: 2026-03-09T01:49 deploy config).
Metric: ~1.82M probe tokens observed across 9 postbacks from IP range 34.203.x.x between 02:18–02:26 UTC. Attribution algorithm picked org-novamind-77 because org_prefix header present and namespace header null.
Risk: If accumulator accepts probe traffic again, multiple customers could see one-off charges during future replays.
Immediate actions (2026-03-11): Billing placed provisional credit for $4,350 on NovaMind account and marked invoice as disputed to prevent autopay. Customer notified.
Fix applied (2026-03-12): Postback-receiver updated to reject any postback with probe=true unless probe-namespace header present. Hotfix rolled to prod-us-east (deploy id hun-20260312-7).
Follow-up (2026-03-12): INT-3321 created to add end-to-end replay test and add schema validation at replay producers to ensure namespace header is always set.
Final reconciliation (pending): Re-run invoice generator to remove the probe line from NovaMind's finalized invoice and issue a credit memo if necessary. Billing to confirm once batch job completes.

Issue summary:
During the DST (daylight savings time) rollover on 2026-03-09 -> 2026-03-10, Medivault Health observed a one-hour shift in daily metrics buckets displayed in the Redwood Console. Hourly charts on several dashboards show data points shifted by +1 hour for the first 6 hours after the DST change.

Impact:
- Multiple production dashboards used by Medivault engineering and ops show misleading hourly usage and latency numbers for 2026-03-10 UTC-5.
- Alert evaluations that use hourly rollups triggered false positives for a short window (several alerts evaluated above threshold).
- Customer reported downstream confusion for billing reconciliation for the affected day.

Environment:
- customer_tier: enterprise
- region: us-east-1
- Console version: web-2026-03-08-build.5
- Aggregation cluster: metrics-agg-prod-3

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Open Redwood Console > Dashboards > Medivault Production Overview (hourly timeseries, 24h window)
2. Set timezone to America/New_York in user preferences
3. Inspect the hourly series for 2026-03-10 (date of DST forward shift)
4. Observe that bucket timestamps and labels are offset by +1 hour for buckets between 02:00 and 08:00 local time

Observed behavior:
- The ingestion pipeline appears to have produced hour-aligned buckets, but the console rollup/labeling layer applied a local-time shift incorrectly at DST boundary, causing displayed bins to be associated with the wrong hour.
- Alert evaluations that use 'last complete hour' windows evaluated against misaligned buckets and produced several noise alerts.

Expected behavior:
- Hourly buckets and dashboard labels should reflect correct local time alignment across DST transitions; alerts should evaluate on correctly aligned buckets.

Temporary workaround:
- Support advised customer to switch dashboard timezone to UTC to view correct alignment for the affected date, and to silence specific alert rules for the 03-10 window until fix is applied.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: time conversion code in console's rollup layer used fixed-offset logic instead of timezone-aware DST rules when mapping ingestion timestamps to display buckets.
- Checked ingestion logs in metrics-agg-prod-3: raw event timestamps are correct and consistent (UTC-based).
- Checked job metrics for the hourly rollup workers: two rollup workers (w-12 and w-13) reported a short period of retrying due to a transient clock-sync warning on 2026-03-10T07:00:12Z; retries did not drop data.
- Reviewed recent PRs: redwood/metrics-ingest#1423 included a refactor to rollup indexing, and redwood/console#2098 updated timezone display code last week. Both PRs touched DST-sensitive code paths.
- Reproduced locally by simulating America/New_York TZ with forward DST transition: console label function returned 'bucket_label = bucket_start + offset' using offset derived from server timezone instead of user's timezone.

Next steps / action items:
- Roll back the timezone-labeling change from redwood/console#2098 in a canary release and validate dashboards for Medivault (assigned to Console team, ETA: 2026-03-12).
- Patch the labeling logic to use tz-aware libraries (moment-timezone -> tz-helpers) and add unit tests covering DST transitions (assigned to metrics UI owner).
- Run targeted re-evaluation for alert rules that fired during the window and prepare a corrected incident summary for Medivault.
- Postmortem and a short blameless runbook update for DST handling in rollups (link to Confluence page to be added).

Customer note: Medivault flagged billing reconciliation as blocker for close; they requested confirmation that raw usage counts were not lost and only display/alerting was affected.
2026-03-10 | Aisha Kapoor (Support): Ticket opened after customer report at 09:12 EDT. Customer provided dashboard screenshot and CSV export of hourly counts showing the apparent +1h shift.
2026-03-10 | Evan Morales (SRE): Acknowledged. Kickoff investigation. Confirmed raw timestamps in ingestion show no gap or duplication. Focusing on console rollup/label path and recent UI PRs.
2026-03-11 | Simone Li (Console Eng): Found that redwood/console#2098 changed label computation to use serverOffset in one branch. Preparing revert PR and unit test that simulates DST forward/back transitions.
2026-03-11 | Evan Morales (SRE): Applied temporary alert suppression for affected rules for Medivault; notified customer of workaround (switch dashboard to UTC) and ETA for patch.
2026-03-12 | Aisha Kapoor (Support): Customer confirmed they can view correct numbers in UTC and have paused billing reconciliation until we confirm full root cause and fix rollout plan. Customer asks for postmortem when available.
2026-03-12 | Simone Li (Console Eng): Revert PR landed to canary (redwood/console#2104). Canaries in us-east-1 are being monitored; will promote to prod after 12h of green metrics. Next update by 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC.

Issue summary:
Customer Finlytics reports that long-running SSE streams occasionally end with an "orphaned" final line (partial sentence or dangling punctuation) after the user’s browser returns from background/suspended state and the client performs a reconnect. The stream shows an end marker from the server, but the last application-visible line is malformed or missing final punctuation; in some cases the client receives an extra heartbeat-only event after the final payload.
Affects a small subset (~0.5%) of streaming requests for Finlytics' enterprise account. Observed in production US-West region. Disrupts downstream parsing in their ingestion pipeline (customers see missing trailing clause or malformed JSON snippets when using structured outputs). Customer has flagged this as P1 due to production data loss for analytical pipelines.
Prod traffic through edge-proxy group ep-west-2. Finlytics connects from various corp NATs; many affected clients are on Chrome Desktop (v112-v116) and are using the JS SDK with background tab suspend/resume patterns.
1) Start a long SSE stream that emits multi-paragraph output (structured JSON lines or prose).
2) In browser, switch tab or put machine to sleep to trigger background suspension for ~30s-90s.
3) Restore tab / network and allow client SDK to attempt reconnect/resume.
4) Observe final line: sometimes truncated punctuation, isolated trailing newline, or a heartbeat event after terminal output.
5) Reproduce rate ~1 in 200 attempts in customer environment; higher if proxy buffering/backoff present.
- Client-side capture from Finlytics attached in the ticket (sse_capture_975311.zip).
- Edge proxy logs show a short 502 around reconnect windows for some sessions; backend serving runtime logs show normal end-of-stream and close on same request id.
- Example server event sequence: payload(chunk N), payload(final), end-event, keepalive
- Example client sequence when broken: payload(chunk N), payload(final) (incomplete), end-event, keepalive, orphaned-heartbeat
- Correlation id examples: cor-id=aa7f5e4b, aa7f5e4c.

Hypothesis: under background-suspend + NAT refresh there is a small race where the edge-proxy flushes buffered TCP segments later than the runtime expects, causing the client reconnect path to replay resume logic but miss a terminal chunk boundary. Two parallel factors observed: (1) edge-proxy idle connection reset during suspend, (2) client SDK treats the first reconnect as a new session and merges a keepalive that lands after end-event, producing a parser-visible trailing token.
What we've ruled out: model encoder truncation, server-side model tokenization errors, and generic rate-limiter throttles.
Reproducibility: internal lab simulation with Chrome headless + proxy replay reproduced truncated final chunk when we injected 50-200ms delayed FIN/ACK from proxy after resume.
Preliminary fix candidate: ensure server emits a distinct terminal marker event with a monotonically increasing stream-seq header and make client SDK prefer terminal-marker continuity check before merging heartbeat events. Also evaluate adjusting edge-proxy tcp_kill/grace timeout to reduce late-segment flushes.
Customer can enable non-resumable stream behavior (client reconnect creates new conversation) for critical jobs, or add a post-assembly checksum on the last line to detect partial outputs. We provided Finlytics a small client-side filter to drop a final keepalive that arrives after end-event as a short-term mitigation.
1) Engineering to add additional diagnostic logging in api-gateway for FIN/ACK/close timing and stream-seq headers (ETA 2026-03-13).
2) Edge team to test lowering proxy idle flush delay for ep-west-2 (ETA 2026-03-14).
3) SDK team to prototype terminal-marker continuity check and release patch v1.4.3 (ETA 2026-03-20).
4) If prototype confirms, schedule a canary rollout for affected fleet and coordinate with Finlytics for verification.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:30 - Edge team (note): Observed several sessions where proxy performed an idle connection reset during the suspend window. We are running an experiment to extend TCP FIN grace by 200ms in ep-west-2.
2026-03-11 13:50 - Runtime team (note): Reproduced issue in lab by injecting delayed FIN/ACK after stream end; terminal marker was delivered but a late keepalive collided with parser state in the SDK. Drafted SDK continuity check.
payload.summary: Intermittent SSE flush delay causes orphaned final line after client background reconnect

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports WebSocket-based chat sessions enter a silent state approximately 20-45s into long-generation responses. The server continues to report the worker as alive for a short time, but no bytes are observed at the client; the TCP connection eventually half-closes and the client must reconnect.

Impact: Affects NoteDock Labs (dedicated) for interactive editor feature; ~12% of long-chat sessions (>800 tokens) in us-east-1 experienced a stall in the 48-hour window. Users see a frozen spinner and must refresh or reconnect. No token loss is consistently reproducible but session continuity is disrupted.

Environment: prod, dedicated pool (dp-nd-01) in us-east-1. Traffic routed through ALB -> websocket-proxy fleet -> gateway -> serving-runtime workers. Customers are using WebSocket with incremental event frames (application/json). Many client connections are behind corporate NATs with TCP keepalive enabled.

Observed behavior: mid-generation silence (no SSE/WebSocket frames) for 20-45s, then client receives FIN from upstream or TCP resets after long idle. Server logs sometimes show worker preempt/eviction for the request's worker due to a short-lived eviction event (node maintenance/autoscaler). We see a pattern where the proxy keeps the socket open while the worker has been reassigned; the proxy's half-open behavior results in no application-level error until TCP times out.

Expected behavior: When a worker handling an active streaming request is preempted/evicted, the platform should either: a) graceful failover the stream to a fallback worker with resume support, or b) promptly signal an application-level error over the WebSocket so client can reconnect and resume. Users should not see long silent intervals without an error or reconnect suggestion.
1) Use a dedicated account in us-east-1 (NoteDock Labs test tenant).
2) Open a WebSocket chat session that triggers a long generation (>800 tokens).
3) While generation is in-flight, trigger a worker preempt by forcing a short restart (internal test: drain one serving node) or cause autoscaler to reassign (simulate load spike).
4) Observe client for silent period and eventual FIN/RESET without an application-level error message.
[2026-02-28T14:23:41Z] websocket-proxy-12: conn_id=abc123 last_frame=2026-02-28T14:23:41Z forwarded_to=gateway-7
[2026-02-28T14:23:53Z] gateway-7: request_id=rd-98765 dispatched_to=worker-54 (redwood-3b-v1) kv_cache_miss=true
[2026-02-28T14:24:12Z] scheduler: node-54 marked_for_preempt due_to=maintenance_window; eviction_start=2026-02-28T14:24:12Z
[2026-02-28T14:24:13Z] worker-54: active_stream_id=stream-77 keepalive_seen=true evict_grace=5s
[2026-02-28T14:24:14Z] websocket-proxy-12: conn_id=abc123 no_bytes_forwarded_since=2026-02-28T14:24:14Z
[2026-02-28T14:25:00Z] websocket-proxy-12: conn_id=abc123 TCP_FIN from upstream=true client_seen_idle=46s
[2026-02-28T14:25:02Z] gateway-7: error=worker_connection_reset request_id=rd-98765
SRE confirmed worker eviction window coincides with silent period. Proxy keeps TCP session in established state while gateway detects worker disconnect but does not immediately return a WebSocket-level CLOSE frame. Packet captures show no RST from worker until the eviction completes; however, proxy's TCP persist settings and ALB idle timeout are allowing a long half-open interval. Reproducible in internal test cluster when we simulate scheduled preemptions and set the same tcp_keepalive and ALB idle-timeout values as customer's environment.
1) Worker preempt leads to an internal handoff where gateway transitions connection; proxy and ALB TCP timeouts are longer than application-level detection, producing silent window.
2) Under high token generation, KV cache misses increase latency and extend time-to-detect worker loss, pushing the silent window past client-side keepalive intervals, so the client only sees a socket-level timeout later.
3) Proxy's current behavior does not emit a WebSocket CLOSE or error frame on upstream worker disconnect during streaming; instead it waits on TCP semantics (causing user-visible stall).
2026-02-28 15:02 - Support (Avery Chen): Customer reports ~12% session stalls; provided timeline, sample request ids and client pcap. Asked SRE to triage.
2026-02-28 16:10 - SRE (Mateo Ruiz): Reproduced in staging by scheduling a node preempt. Observed same silent period. Attaching pcap and scheduler logs to ticket. Potential quick mitigation: reduce proxy TCP idle timeout to align with autoscaler/eviction grace period.
2026-03-01 09:18 - Eng (Samira Khan): Ran targeted experiment: lowered websocket-proxy keepalive to 8s and ALB idle to 30s on a canary; silent window reduced but some sessions still get short pauses. Need graceful application-level close on upstream disconnect.
2026-03-01 14:40 - Customer (NoteDock SRE, Rajesh Kumar): Confirmed test canary reduced user-impact to ~3% but still see occasional stalls on long responses. Asking for an SLA-friendly fix or recommended client-side reconnection logic to minimize UX disruption.
2026-03-02 11:05 - Eng (Samira Khan): Opened runtime PR to detect worker disconnects during streaming and emit WebSocket CLOSE with error code. PR linked. Planning A/B deploy to dedicated pool next week.
2026-03-02 12:30 - Support (Avery Chen): Notified customer about canary and upcoming fix timeline; provided temporary client workaround (exponential reconnect + resume token).
1) Deploy PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 to canary in dedicated pool and run 72h soak with NoteDock traffic replication.
2) Adjust websocket-proxy TCP keepalive and ALB idle timeout defaults for dedicated pools to reduce half-open window (rollback plan in runbook).
3) Add an application-level close/error emission in gateway when worker disconnects mid-stream (server-side fix).
4) Provide customer with client SDK patch notes and recommended reconnection/resume strategy as interim workaround.
5) Postmortem and follow-up: evaluate whether autoscaler eviction cadence or KV-cache warmup profiles can be tuned to reduce mid-gen evictions.
Triage ongoing; temporary mitigation (proxy keepalive/ALB adjustments) reduced impact in canary. Server-side fix PR created; schedule and verification in progress. Customer notified and given client-side reconnect guidance.

Issue summary: BrightRoutes reported a missing invoice line for 2026-01-20 12:00-15:00 UTC in their finalized invoice. They observed a ~45% drop in recorded token usage for the midday window compared to expected traffic. Impact: Under-billing observed on a finalized invoice; customer requests provisional credit while we investigate root cause. Timeline: 2026-01-20 12:10 UTC customer opened chat to billing; 2026-01-20 13:00 support ticket opened; 2026-01-20 18:00 customer uploaded sample request IDs. Environment: prod (eu-west), BrightRoutes on Dedicated pool BR-DED-004. Relevant notes: Traffic pattern unchanged on customer side; requests show successful 200 responses in application logs. Suspected area: metering-service aggregation after kv-cache TTL invalidation at 12:00 UTC caused intermittent microbatch drops and loss of token counts in hourly accumulator. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run a controlled microbatch stream using BrightRoutes API key in prod eu-west during a scheduled kv-cache TTL boundary. 2) Verify ingested events reach metering-service and are forwarded to billing-processor. 3) Observe hourly accumulator delta vs raw token log. 2026-01-21 09:34 - SRE (Liu Chen): Found repeated 'microbatch-commit timeout' at 2026-01-20T12:00:05Z aligning with kv-cache TTL eviction. Forwarding trace to metering engineers.
Hypothesis A: TTL boundary on kv-cache triggered a short window where aggregated microbatches were not committed to the hourly accumulator due to a race in the metering-service 'flush_on_evict' path.
Hypothesis B: Ingest-proxy backpressure resulted in silent drop of non-critical telemetry events that metering-service uses to correlate request fragments; application responses were still proxied, so customer app saw no errors.
Logs (summary): metering-service logs show 'flush_on_evict: commit-failed: context deadline exceeded' at 12:00:05Z repeated ~8 times. Billing-processor accepted the downstream postbacks for surrounding minutes but missing batch for 12:00-12:05 UTC. Ingest-proxy trace shows elevated latency but no 5xx.
Reproduction attempts: Replayed batch with identical size in staging with TTL boundary present and observed a ~30-50% reduction in hourly accumulator delta because the local accumulator refused late commits during eviction. Root cause narrowed to a race condition introduced by kv-cache eviction handler in version v1.8.2 of metering-service.
Scope: So far only confirmed for dedicated pools where kv-cache TTL is set to 3600s and eviction coincides with microbatch flushing. Likely affects other dedicated customers on eu-west with similar TTL schedules.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/4123 contains a proposed fix to make flush_on_evict idempotent and resilient to commit timeouts.
Workaround (applied): Issued provisional credit of 325.50 USD to BrightRoutes invoice on 2026-01-22 and flagged account with 'billing-review' until postmortem complete.
Fix (planned): Patch metering-service v1.8.3 to make 'flush_on_evict' retriable and to persist microbatch to durable queue before eviction. PR #4123 opened; target canary deploy in eu-west 2026-01-25.
Follow-ups: 1) Run targeted audit for other dedicated customers with kv-cache TTL alignment during the last 30 days. 2) Add telemetry alert for 'microbatch-commit failures' to trigger automated replay to billing-processor. 3) Confluence postmortem to be published after root cause verification.

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightCart is seeing intermittent model artifact fetch failures from serving nodes in their private deployment. Failures manifest as TLS certificate name mismatch (x509: certificate is valid for storage.internal.corp, not artifacts.s3-external.net) when nodes attempt to download shard objects. This happens ~0.3-0.8% of shard fetches, spikes during nightly warmups.

Impact: Inference requests occasionally return 502/5xx or experience longer tail latency while retries happen. Customer reports degraded end-user batch jobs during peak.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peering to our control plane) with egress routed through the customer's branch-office proxy/NGFW. Serving nodes are dual-stack (IPv4+IPv6) and use system default Happy Eyeballs behavior.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger model rollout that causes serving nodes to fetch shard objects concurrently (large model or batch warmup).
2) Observe artifact fetch logs and TLS errors on a subset of nodes.
3) Failures correlate with a resolver returning AAAA records and the kernel selecting IPv6 egress first.

Logs / observations:
- serving-node.log: "GET https://artifacts.s3-external.net/model-12345/shard-0: x509: certificate is valid for storage.internal.corp, not artifacts.s3-external.net"
- tcpdump on node during failure shows TLS ClientHello SNI = "artifacts.s3-external.net" but proxy/NGFW upstream opens TLS to storage.internal.corp endpoint (IPv6 path) and responds with a different certificate.
- DNS responses during failure include AAAA then A; Happy Eyeballs chooses IPv6 path leading to branch proxy path.

Suspected cause: Branch-office egress path for IPv6 is hairpinned through an intermediate corporate proxy that performs SNI rewriting (or routes to an internal storage translator) only for IPv6-preferring flows. IPv4 egress takes a different ISP path that preserves SNI. Happy Eyeballs/dual-stack behavior causes a fraction of connections to use IPv6 and encounter proxy SNI rewrite, producing hostname mismatch.

Temporary workaround: Request customer to either (a) prefer IPv4 on serving nodes (gai.conf / sysctl tweak) or (b) add an exception in the branch proxy to preserve SNI for artifacts.s3-external.net/storage endpoints. We provided exact gai.conf line to prefer IPv4.

Requested next steps:
- Collect pcap and proxy logs from customer for a failing window.
- Confirm proxy rule that rewrites SNI or routes IPv6 traffic differently.
- Consider adding an artifact fetch fallback that retries with IPv4 on TLS hostname mismatch to avoid transient failures.
- 2026-03-12 09:10 Support triage: Identified x509 certname mismatch errors in serving logs; customer confirmed private egress via branch proxy.
- 2026-03-12 11:45 SRE captured tcpdump showing ClientHello->proxy->upstream change only on AAAA path.
- 2026-03-13 14:20 Eng hypothesis: proxy rewrites destination or uses different backend for IPv6 egress (NAT64 or internal cache) leading to certificate for internal hostname.
- Gathered artifacts: pcap (redacted), serving logs, DNS query/response samples, proxy ACL snippet from customer (sensitive - stored in secure ticket file).
1) Customer applied temporary gai.conf preference to prefer IPv4 on serving nodes (precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100). 2) Customer created an exception in branch proxy to stop SNI rewrite for artifacts.s3-external.net. Both reduced failure rate to <0.01% during tests.
Temporary mitigation applied: customer prefers IPv4 on nodes; proxy exception configured. Root cause: asymmetric egress behavior where IPv6 flows were routed through a proxy path that replaced or proxied TLS to an internal storage hostname, causing x509 name mismatch. Permanent recommendation: customer to update proxy to preserve SNI for public artifact hostnames or ensure consistent egress routing for IPv6 and IPv4. We will add a robustness change to the artifact fetcher to attempt IPv4 fallback on TLS hostname mismatch (tracked in INT-8893).
Workarounds implemented by customer reduced errors to noise level. Engineering task created (INT-8893) to add lightweight IPv4 fallback when artifact fetch fails with certname mismatch. Support to follow up in 2 weeks to confirm stability.
2026-03-12 08:57 - BrightCart (customer): 'We see intermittent shard fetch TLS errors causing batch jobs to fail. Attaching serving logs and a sample of failing request IDs.'

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:05 - BrightCart: 'Yes, egress goes via our branch-office proxy and IPv6 is enabled for subnets. We'll capture tcpdump during the next warmup window.'
2026-03-13 13:30 - BrightCart: 'We added a temporary proxy rule to preserve SNI for artifacts host and applied gai.conf to prefer IPv4. Will report back after nightly warmup.'

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightForms reports that SSE-based chat streams stop producing tokens mid-response (~after 200-600 tokens) but the HTTP connection remains open. The client sees no final event and ultimately times out after ~30s of silence. This is observed only on their Dedicated pool in us-west-2 and primarily with redwood-neo-13B-quant; some occurrences with redwood-14B-v1 were reported after model fallback.

Impact:
- Multiple end users see partial/paused responses in production web chat widgets.
- Reported across three customer sessions in the last 24 hours; affects important SLAs for BrightForms (enterprise contract).
- Workaround (client reconnect) recovers response but may produce duplicated content or truncated context.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) for BrightForms Inc. in us-west-2
- Serving runtime version: v1.18.3
- Autoscaler: v0.9.1 (scale-down idle threshold 120s)
- Workers: NVIDIA A100s, driver 535.xx, CUDA 12.2
- Networking: customer VPC peering + internal NAT gateway

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1. Start long chat generation with ~2k token context and streaming enabled (SSE).
2. Request a response expected to be ~700-1200 tokens.
3. Observe tokens streaming for ~200-600 tokens, then stream silence while connection remains ESTABLISHED.
4. After ~30s silence client times out and reconnects, which resumes by starting a new generation (duplicate/truncated).

Observed logs / traces (excerpts):
- Worker stdout around stall: "[2026-03-10T15:22:31Z] kernel: triggering memory_compaction phase=post-kv-checkpoint seq=42"
- Serving runtime trace: "sse: flush-sentinel sent; downstream ack not received; stall_detected=1"
- Scheduler: "eviction_candidate: false; compaction_in_progress:true; reserved_tokens: 0.2"
- No 5xx returned to client; connection stays 200 OK. TCP shows steady bytes but no SSE payloads.

Initial hypothesis:
- A per-worker GPU memory compaction/defragmentation path (recently introduced to reduce OOMs during dynamic batch spikes) is blocking the token flush loop for multi-second windows, which for SSE looks like a silent stall to clients. The compaction code executes while a generation is in-flight causing the kernel to rebind memory and temporarily block attention kernels.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced internally on a dedicated test pool by forcing compaction during an in-flight generation: same silent pause observed at compaction boundary.
- Tracepoints added to serving-runtime show token-emission paused during "gpu_compaction:begin" -> "gpu_compaction:end" (median pause ~4.8s, 95th ~12s).
- Autoscaler logs show no worker preemption during stalls; worker remains assigned.
- No TLS termination or proxy events correlating with the pause (TLS keepalives continue).
- Kernel JIT path triggered when switching to quantized fused-attention kernel; compaction sometimes coincides with kernel selection logic.

Mitigation performed so far:
- Temporarily disabled proactive compaction on dedicated pools for BrightForms (flags pushed to fleet: compaction.enabled=false for their pool) which reduced incidents to zero in the 6h observation window.
- Added a short client-facing warning in console for BrightForms engineers and recommended reconnect/backoff pattern as emergency fallback.

Next steps / action items:
1) Engineering (serving-runtime) to modify compaction so it yields to active token-emission loop (owner: Miguel Torres). Target: non-blocking compaction variant or scheduling compaction only when worker is idle. ETA: 2026-03-16.
2) Add server-side SSE stall detector metric and alert (observability) to catch pauses >2s during streaming (owner: Observability team). ETA: 2026-03-13.
3) Run a canary of the non-blocking compaction patch in staging with long-chat test harness for 48h (owner: QA/Eng). ETA: 2026-03-15.
4) Post-deploy: gradually re-enable compaction with throttling and monitor token-emission latencies (owner: Product/Infra).

Follow-ups requested from customer:
- Provide any client-side logs showing the exact time of stall (UTC) to match with server trace IDs.
- Confirm if they can tolerate temporary compaction disablement long-term or prefer a patch.

Resolution: ongoing. Temporary workaround applied (compaction disabled for their dedicated pool).

Additional notes:
Temporary change: proactive GPU memory compaction disabled for BrightForms dedicated pool to avoid mid-stream stalls. Engineering is building a non-blocking compaction implementation to re-enable safely. Customers should see normal streaming behavior while we validate the fix.
This issue surfaced after compaction change landed in v1.18.0. The compaction code path interacts poorly with the fused-attention kernel JIT path. Need careful validation of kernel-switch race. payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long SSE streams containing a final rich attachment (base64-embedded image) are truncated on reconnect. After a midstream Azure WAF idle probe, the resumed stream returns a small heartbeat-only trailer and the expected base64 image chunk never arrives.

Impact: FinSolutions sees corrupted/wrapped chat transcripts where the final image URL or base64 block is missing. This breaks downstream UX and automated document ingestion. Affects a handful of production requests (estimated ~0.3% of long streaming sessions) in us-east. Customer is enterprise, high priority.

Environment: prod us-east, hosted Redwood API, model pinned to redwood-open-13B-v1, requests originate via customer VPC-to-Redwood edge through Azure WAF/ALB chain.

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Start a long chat request that ends with an instruction to attach an image as base64 and a short concluding paragraph. The full server stream normally emits text tokens then an "attachment" choice containing the base64 payload.
2) Midway through token emission perform a simulated Azure WAF idle probe (customer does this regularly from their edge).
3) Client reconnects/resumes SSE using the session resume token.

Observed behavior: After resume the client receives:
- resumption ACK, a few text tokens repeating a short prefix, then a single keepalive/heartbeat line ("event: heartbeat" + tiny payload), and then connection close. The large base64 attachment is not delivered. The server logs show the final choice was generated and committed but downstream connection to the WAF/edge was closed before the attachment chunk was flushed to the client.

Expected behavior: On resume the remaining tokens including the final attachment should be delivered intact, or a clear error/rollback should be returned. Heartbeat-only trailers should not suppress pending payload frames.

Notes: This appears distinct from earlier "fragment duplication" cases — here the issue is loss of a large trailing chunk (attachment) combined with a synthetic keepalive from the edge. Customer indicates their edge probe pattern differs from standard health checks; the probe performs a lightweight HEAD/GET that can cause the connection to briefly half-close and trigger downstream buffering behaviors.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 09:45 - Eng (runtime-team): Hypothesis: edge probe triggers early TCP FIN or HTTP2 RST that causes write buffers to be coalesced into a heartbeat frame during resume path. Large base64 chunk (>>16KB) may be queued in runtime streaming buffer and not flushed during resume because of incorrect keepalive/flush ordering in the SSE reconstructor.
Traces: request_id 7f9d3c (customer example) shows model generation finished; final chunk appended to outgoing stream buffer at 14:01:32.389Z.
Edge event: Azure WAF inserted a synthetic probe and subsequently returned 200 to the probe; logs show a half-close from the WAF side at 14:01:33.041Z which aligns with missing attachment delivery window.
Runtime behavior: sendQueue.flush() called but heartbeat emission path runs concurrently; race condition observed where small heartbeat frame is written after sendQueue flush flags cleared, but large chunk remained in overflow buffer guarded by 'resumeLocked' flag and was skipped on resume.
Staging repro: toggling the probe to occur after final flush avoids the loss. Repro rate in staging ~70% when probe placed between final token emission and stream termination; implies timing-sensitive race.
Potential root cause: ordering/race in resume path between flush/commit of large payload frames and keepalive/heartbeat generation when an upstream/edge emits an out-of-band connection probe causing half-close semantics.
Relevant code area: streaming reconstructor and sse-session manager (v2.7.1). Candidate fix ensures flushLargeFrames() is awaited before emitting heartbeat or returning resume READY to client.
Finish internal PR review and run extended streaming regression suite against stagers with simulated edge probes.
Create a short-term mitigation for customer: feature-flag to disable midstream keepalive emission for resumed sessions or maintain a forced flush-on-resume behavior.
Canary deploy fix to prod us-east in a low-traffic window, monitor token delivery and SLOs for streaming.
Coordinate with customer FinSolutions to temporarily suppress edge probes or whitelist streaming endpoints while canary runs.
Postmortem/Follow-up: add synthetic probe test cases to CI and update runbook for WAF/edge interactions.
Customer workaround: avoid injecting idle probes during active long streams; increase edge probe interval for identified endpoints. Temporary support flag provided to customer to enable forced flush-on-resume while fix is rolled out.
This ticket differs from standard fragmented-chunk issues because the missing payload is a large base64 attachment combined with an external edge probe. Add E2E tests that simulate probe-caused half-close semantics (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2).
payload.summary: SSE resume drops final rich attachment (base64 image) and emits heartbeat-only trailer after edge WAF probe
