payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (FjordAI production fleet) report that for long-running SSE responses (>60s) the final termination metadata object ("type": "done") is not delivered after a short reconnect flap from mobile clients. The body of the stream contains the full generated text, but the trailing metadata that signals completion and contains final token offsets and provenance is missing.

Impact: Downstream consumers treat the stream as still-open or as having incomplete provenance. Customer logs show repeated duplicate replays of the last 1–2 token chunks when client retries, or else the client hangs waiting for the terminal event. This causes stalled UI state for end-users and increases token accounting disagreement between client and server. A subset of events also show duplicated terminal metadata arriving much later (20–40s) after reconnect, which causes duplicate-finalization processing.

Environment: Customer on Dedicated cluster in prod/us-east, clients are mobile apps behind flaky corporate mobile proxies (Android, RN 0.71), connections observed to have short TCP-level resets and intermittent 502s from their proxy. Affected models: redwood-3.2-chat (primary), fallback to open-llama-7b observed in some sessions.
1) Use the customer mobile app configured to stream chat responses via SSE to streaming proxy in front of Redwood API.
2) Initiate a long generation (expected >60s) with streaming enabled and metadata/batch_tokens enabled.
3) Simulate intermittent mobile proxy behavior: a short TCP reset or HTTP/1.1 half-close for ~1-3s then immediate reconnect.
4) Observe the client output: last token chunks may replay or the stream may never receive the final metadata event ("done").
Final metadata event ("done" envelope containing offsets and provenance) is often missing immediately after a reconnect. Clients either hang or reconcile by replaying last token chunks. In ~15% of reproductions the final metadata arrives delayed and duplicated, leading to double finalization in client logic.
After a brief reconnect, streaming resume should deliver any missing terminal metadata exactly once, and clients should be able to reassemble a contiguous completed response without duplicate terminal events.
2026-03-09T21:14:02Z [proxy-1] upstream reset id=abc123 tcp_reset from 10.11.12.13
2026-03-09T21:14:03Z [streaming-proxy] resumed session sid=svc-789, replayed buffer size=512 bytes
2026-03-09T21:14:05Z [serving-runtime] response id=resp-456 tokens_streamed=1180 final_meta_emitted=false
2026-03-09T21:14:28Z [api-gateway] client reconnect from 198.51.100.22 session-claim returned stale-offset=1180
Hypothesis 1: The proxy resume path replays buffered token chunks but drops the small terminal metadata frame because the resume heuristic treats it as control-only and de-duplicates frames based on sequence numbers which reset across reconnect. Hypothesis 2: Client SDK fast-reconnect code suppresses processing of terminal metadata when it detects duplicated chunk IDs, causing it to ignore a legitimate terminal event arriving after session renegotiation.

What we checked:
- Reviewed streaming-proxy resume logic: it merges buffered chunks then attempts to re-emit terminal events only if last-seen-offset != terminal-offset. There is a race around updating last-seen-offset when replaying and when the final metadata is queued by serving-runtime.
- Instrumented serving-runtime to log when final_meta is enqueued; logs show final_meta_enqueued but api-gateway trace shows final_meta not forwarded before connection swap.
- Reproduced with local proxy script that performs half-close: reproduction consistent with customer reports.

Partial finding: When the upstream final metadata is queued within a ~500–1200ms window during connection tear-down/hand-off, the proxy's resume merge path discards that frame because it appears as an out-of-order control frame (sequence number lower than replay head). This leads to a missing immediate terminal event. In some cases the terminal event is delivered later as a duplicate when the client performs a second reconnect and the serving runtime re-emits the metadata as part of client-side backfill.
Advise customer to enable short-lived client-side timeout to force a re-request of the most recent message on missing terminal metadata, and to enable SDK flag 'allow-late-finalization' which tolerates delayed terminal events. Provided client patch for RN that replays session token claim after reconnect (v0.7.9) to reduce race. Also advised reducing proxy idle-timeout to avoid mid-frame resets.
Engineering (streaming-proxy and serving-runtime owners) to implement: 1) Make terminal metadata emission idempotent and attach explicit stream-seq numbers not tied to ephemeral buffer head; 2) Update proxy resume merge to prioritize forwarding terminal metadata even if sequence appears out-of-order within a small window; 3) Add server-side test coverage for reconnect races and a canary rollout to dedicated clusters. Target: patch landed to staging by 2026-03-18, prod rollout week of 2026-03-25 behind feature flag.

Short-term mitigation: Add additional logging and a metric 'terminal_meta_dropped' to detect regressions and notify SRE alerts if rate > 0.5% of streams for a tenant.
In Progress - patch in review (PR linked). Customer notified and given workaround. Tracking follow-ups and SRE alerting pending.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:30 - SRE (Lin Zhao): Added correlation IDs and increased proxy logging. Saw terminal_meta_dropped metric spike for tenant fjordai-prod. Investigating rate and pattern.
2026-03-12 19:05 - Product (Maya Chen): Confirmed priority and scheduled cross-team sync for 2026-03-15 to plan rollout and tenant communication.
payload.summary: Reactive reconnect flap suppresses final termination metadata in multipart SSE responses

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a staged canary drain in us-west-2, multiple tenant streaming sessions were observed to lose their pinned model affinity and begin routing to the legacy variant. Impact: Customer RelayDocs (enterprise) reported degraded outputs and a sudden usage/billing spike for affected sessions. Problem appears correlated with an edge ingress header rewrite that trims tenant routing hints when requests are merged from the ingress retry queue.

Environment: prod cluster in us-west-2, canary slice id=canary-2026-03-10-02, edge-proxy version v3.6.1, api-gateway v2.12.

Steps to reproduce (observed flow):
1) Start long-lived streaming session pinned to redwood-open-7b-v1.
2) Trigger a canary drain (graceful prewarm drain) on a small subset of edge nodes.
3) Some requests hit an overloaded ingress node which defers and enqueues the request into the ingress retry/merge queue.
4) When ingress merges queued retries, the edge-proxy applies a header normalization (ingress-rewrite) that strips the last-of-key hint header: "x-tenant-route-hint" if it detects a long header chain.
5) Merged request reaches orchestrator without the tenant hint. Orchestrator cannot reconcile the existing session pin and falls back to routing heuristics, which send traffic to the legacy variant.

Expected behavior: Merge/retry logic should preserve session pin identity metadata (x-tenant-route-hint / x-session-pin) and merged requests should be routed to the pinned model variant.

Observed behavior: Clients experienced mixed outputs mid-stream (part of the stream from pinned model, subsequent frames from legacy variant). Telemetry shows the pin TTL remained active in the control plane but edge routing decided to route to fallback due to missing hint. Some sessions never re-established the pin resulting in continuous degraded routing until a new session was created.

Logs/evidence:
- Edge-proxy logs (edge-23) showing ingress-merge events at 2026-03-10T14:22:07Z with header_sanitizer:TRIM applied.
- Orchestrator trace for tenant relaydocs-17 showing route-decision: fallback_variant when x-tenant-route-hint=null.
- Serving runtime telemetry shows active pin lease for session s-8b9f but no incoming affinity token from edge for 7 minutes.
- Customer-provided recorded stream with timestamps mapping to variant switch at 2026-03-10T14:22:09Z.

Support (Aisha): Initial report received from RelayDocs. Customer saw mixed generation outputs and unexpected cost increase during their heavy ingestion job. Raised to engineering and flagged as P1.
SRE (Luca): Reproduced on prod canary slice. Observed header trimming in ingress-merge path; will collect full edge-proxy logs and packet captures. Note: ingress-rewrite config recently hardened to remove duplicate headers (PR 2413).
Customer (RelayDocs): We observed 18 sessions impacted across multiple tenants, stream continuity broken. We have a post-hoc transcript if needed. Please prioritize — this affects production inference quality.
SRE (Luca): Temporary mitigation: disable ingress-merge header sanitization for canary slice via feature-flag ff/ingress-preserve-hint (rolled back at 2026-03-11T03:00Z). Early telemetry shows pinned routing resumed for new requests, but already-orphaned streams require reconnection.
Eng (Maya R.): Hypothesis: header sanitizer treats long header chains as suspicious and drops the last-of-key occurrence. Merged retry requests collapse headers and accidentally remove x-session-pin. Need codepath review in edge-proxy merge handler.
Support (Aisha): RelayDocs requested a timeline and whether they will be credited for the unexpected cost. Ticket owner to coordinate with billing.
Timeline: 2026-03-10 14:20 UTC canary drain started. 14:22 ingress-merge queue flushed with header_sanitizer active. 14:22:09 first variant switch observed. Root cause likely regression in edge-proxy header merge logic introduced in PR 2413 (duplicate header removal) that did not preserve pinned-session header ordering. Evidence: packet capture shows x-session-pin present on initial request; absent on merged retry subset. Control plane retained pin leases — so this is purely edge-side metadata loss. Additional contributing factor: queue-merge uses last-of-key semantics when combining headers; session pinging uses the last header occurrence to indicate active pin (implementation detail).
Actions taken so far: disabled sanitizer flag for canary slice, collected edge logs, captured orchestrator decision traces, reproduced locally with simulated merge queue.
Next steps: patch edge-proxy merge logic to canonicalize headers without dropping last-of-key for x-session-pin / x-tenant-route-hint, add unit tests for merge behavior, and add a safety check in orchestrator to consult control-plane pin leases if hint missing for active stream.
Planned fix: revert aggressive duplicate-header prune for specific routing hint headers and add a defensive lookup in orchestrator to cross-check control-plane pin for active session ids. Patch branch: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/tree/fix/preserve-session-pin-merge. Target hotfix rollout to canary on 2026-03-13 and full rollout 2026-03-15 after verification.
Workarounds: 1) Customer reconnects streaming sessions to re-establish pins. 2) We temporarily disabled ff/ingress-preserve-hint on affected canary slice to preserve previous behavior.
Follow-ups: Billing review for unexpected token usage (assigned to Finance, ticket FIN-8842), add integration test for ingress-merge header preservation (assigned to QA), add monitoring alert when session pin TTL exists in control-plane but edge trace shows repeated route-decisions to fallback for same session (assigned to Observability).
payload.summary: Proxy ingress header rewrite + queued retry merge orphaned session pin during canary drain

payload.description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-11 07:12 UTC Montclair Health experienced a region-wide streaming blackout for production requests routed to us-east. Long-lived streaming connections dropped silently and the request router triggered fallback rules that redirected traffic to smaller quantized variants, amplifying tail latency and producing duplicate/incoherent completions for a subset of requests. Customer began escalating at 07:30 UTC citing truncated clinical transcripts and inconsistent patient summary outputs.

Impact:
- Affected ~18% of Montclair Health's traffic for 31 minutes (07:12–07:43 UTC).
- 5xx spike to 12% across streaming endpoints; synchronous completion endpoints saw a 4x latency increase for long-context calls.
- Several calls fell back to open-7b-v1 and open-13b-v2-quant; customers reported hallucinated medication entries in 2% of returned transcripts.
- Billing exposure: duplicate completions and replayed fragments led to estimated 6k token overcount for Montclair's account during the window.

Environment:
- prod-us-east cluster behind streaming-proxy v2.1.1 and api-gateway v3.8.
- Autoscaler configured with headroom policy: min_inflight_headroom=0.18, burst_enabled=true.

Steps to reproduce (investigative):
1) Simulate a high-fanout streaming workload with persistent 30s prefix followed by large completion (seq_len 2048) using Montclair's production prompt set.
2) Inject intermittent TCP resets at proxy layer (simulated network jitter) and observe router behavior when connections fail mid-KV-stream.
3) Observe fallback decision path: router reassigns to quantized variant when latency > 2.2s or 429s exceed threshold.

Logs / observed traces (snippets):
- streaming-proxy: "2026-03-11T07:12:05Z WARN conn=xyz reset-by-peer; pending-frames=3"
- router: "fallback: reason=connection_reset; target=open-13b-v2-quant; trace_id=abc123"
- serving-runtime: "2026-03-11T07:12:27Z ERROR tokenization_mismatch: prompt_chunk=8; kv_miss=1"
- billing: "2026-03-11T07:43:05Z NOTICE duplicate-completion-detected count=187 estimated_tokens=6120 account=montclair-health"

Timeline: 07:12 UTC first proxy resets observed; 07:15 UTC SRE alerted via #support; 07:20 UTC customer CS rep engaged; 07:30 UTC customer began escalating to CSM and APAC ops. Root cause hypothesis: connection pooling at streaming-proxy failed to gracefully drain when upstream transient TCP resets occurred, triggering abrupt connection closures and leaving inflight streams in indeterminate state. Router logic interpreted closed connections as instance failure and executed fallback amplification across multiple routers because of stale affinity cache. Secondary factor: autoscaler headroom was tightly tuned for cost, which reduced available capacity for rapid fallback handling leading to queuing and duplicate retried attempts.

Key evidence: proxy logs show a 1.9s median reconnect loop for affected frontends; affinity cache TTL was set to 15s and had a stale entry spike during the incident. No disk or GPU OOMs found on serving nodes.

Temporary mitigations performed during incident: rolled back streaming-proxy to v2.0.8 in the affected availability zone (07:34 UTC) which restored graceful connection teardown; increased router affinity cache clear frequency; temporarily increased autoscaler headroom to 0.35 to reduce immediate failovers.

Fixes applied:
- Reverted streaming-proxy to 2.0.8 in us-east and queued a canary for 2.1.2 with an additional connection-drain patch (PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proxy/pull/428).
- Updated router fallback policy to require two consecutive connection failures before mass fallback (config change rolled at 08:10 UTC).
- Raised autoscaler min_inflight_headroom to 0.35 and adjusted burst window to 60s.
- Issued a billing credit to Montclair Health for token overcount (credit amount: $1,320) and opened an invoice reconciliation ticket with finance (linked).

Follow-up action items (owners and due dates):
- Eng/SRE to implement connection-drain observability metrics and alert (Owner: Marcus Li, due 2026-03-18).
- Runtime team to add deterministic replay-detection to prevent duplicate token counting during abrupt disconnects (Owner: Priya Rao, due 2026-04-01).
- Support to update post-incident customer-facing summary and confirm acceptance of billing credit (Owner: Aisha Patel, due 2026-03-14).
- Product to revisit autoscaler default headroom recommendation for streaming customers and publish guidance (Owner: Lina Martinez, due 2026-03-25).

Customer update sent 2026-03-13: apologized for impact, summarized actions and credit offered, scheduled technical review with Montclair engineering team for 2026-03-16. Customer acknowledged and requested a follow-up on waveform logs and a copy of the new router config. CSM accepted and follow-up meeting scheduled.
2026-03-11T07:18Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial report from Montclair - multiple truncated transcripts and empty stream closes. Captured sample request IDs and escalated to SRE via #support. SLA first response met.
2026-03-11T07:25Z - Marcus Li (SRE): Noted surge of 'reset-by-peer' in streaming-proxy logs. Hypothesis: proxy drain regression in 2.1.1. Kicking off revert to 2.0.8 in affected AZ now.
2026-03-11T07:40Z - Priya Rao (Runtime): Confirmed fallback amplification due to router affinity TTL spike; quantized variants handled significantly more fanout than expected. Opening PR to require double-failure before fallback. See PR #428.
2026-03-11T08:05Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer accepted temporary workaround but requested billing reconciliation and postmortem. Created finance ticket FIN-1120 for credit processing.
2026-03-12T10:14Z - Lina Martinez (Product): Will include recommended headroom defaults for streaming customers in next week's release notes. Drafted guidance and shared with SRE for review.
2026-03-13T15:30Z - Marcus Li (SRE): Incident declared resolved after monitoring window passed. Closing major incident but keeping follow-ups tracked in this ticket.
2026-03-13T16:00Z - Montclair Health (Customer): 'Thanks for the rapid response. We'll review router logs in the 3/16 call. Please include test vectors for our eng team.'

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customers see intermittent stalls and 0-byte ranges when Redwood agent (private deployment via TGW peering) downloads model shard artifacts using HTTP range requests. Impact: model pulls time out or produce corrupted shards causing model load failures and request 5xx at application layer. Behavior is intermittent and correlates with high ephemeral port churn on the customer's NAT/GW.

Observed impact: - Model download failures cause instance restart loops and failed inferences for a subset of hosts. - Customer-facing error rate spike: ~3-6% of artifact GETs in a 1-hour window.

Initial hypothesis: TCP connections for range GETs are being observed as reused/collided due to ephemeral source port reuse across TGW/NAT translation after the customer's flow-aggregation/port-reuse policy. The remote S3 endpoint sees duplicate 4-tuple tuples, and packets from different flows are being delivered to the wrong socket or dropped by an inline stateful device, causing partial/zero-length range responses.
1) Deploy Redwood Private agent behind customer TGW with NAT gateway enabled and aggressive ephemeral-port reuse configured on corp firewall.
2) Trigger a model pull for redwood-v1.3 (large shard >1GB) so the agent issues HTTP range requests in parallel.
3) Observe agent logs for repeated Range: bytes=... responses that are 0 bytes or have unexpected Content-Range headers.
4) Simultaneously capture flow logs on TGW/NAT and packet captures on agent host to correlate source port reuse events.
2026-03-12T09:14:22Z agent: fetching shard part 12 range=1258291200-1677721599 -> HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content Content-Range: bytes 1258291200-1677721599/1677721600 (size mismatch)
2026-03-12T09:14:22Z agent: got 0 bytes for expected 419430400 bytes, retrying (attempt 1)
2026-03-12T09:14:24Z kernel: conntrack: NAT translation reused for src=10.0.4.23:40123 dst=52.216.12.34:443 (reused with existing tuple)
2026-03-12T09:14:25Z s3: response with Content-Range header but content-length 0 returned by edge.
03/12 10:00 - Support collected agent logs, TGW flow logs, and asked customer to capture tcpdump on a single problematic host.
03/12 13:45 - Packet capture shows two different internal hosts using the same source port to the same S3 IP within < 200ms after customer's NAT port recycling window; server returned 206 for one 4-tuple but packets were delivered to socket belonging to the other flow.
03/13 09:30 - Reproduced in staging by configuring iptables SNAT with aggressive port reuse using ephemeral-port-range <50000 and reuse settings; range requests interleaved and produced occasional zero-length responses.
03/13 11:20 - Hypothesis refined: stateful middlebox (customer NGFW or NAT) is performing source-port reuse or asymmetric state mapping across TGW attachments, leading to cross-flow packet delivery or early TCP teardown observed as 0-length body on range responses.
03/14 08:15 - Eng attempted a mitigation: enable connection pinning on the agent's S3 downloader (force single connection per host for concurrent range requests); reduced failure rate to <0.2% locally but not acceptable long-term for throughput.
Marisol Gomez (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reported intermittent model load failures after a rolling restart. Asking for network captures and TGW flow logs.
Acme NetOps (customer) 2026-03-12: Provided TGW flow logs and noted they run a custom NAT appliance that aggressively recycles ephemeral ports to conserve session table.
Ethan Cole (SRE) 2026-03-13: Reproduced locally with iptables SNAT config. Suspect port reuse collision. Posting preliminary packet captures to #support and linking pcap in Confluence.
Priya Shah (Networking Eng) 2026-03-14: Suggested two workarounds: 1) relax NAT ephemeral-port reuse on customer NAT/GW; 2) enable agent-level conservative connection strategy (single pinned connection per remote host for range streams) until customer fixes NAT behavior.
Acme NetOps 2026-03-14: Will test relaxing ephemeral port reuse and provide results by EOD.
Stateful NAT/firewall on customer side was configured to aggressively reuse ephemeral source ports across TGW attachments, causing 4-tuple collisions and mis-delivery of TCP segments for concurrent S3 range requests. This manifested as 0-byte or partial range responses at the agent.
Short-term workaround implemented: agent patch deployed to prod agents for Acme that pins range-download streams to a single connection per host to avoid parallel 4-tuple reuse. Customer agreed to update NAT/GW configuration to increase ephemeral port range and disable aggressive reuse. Long-term: recommend adding agent-side detection of repeated range response size mismatches and automatic backoff to single-connection streaming, and document NAT recommendations in Private deploy runbook.
2026-03-12 initial report -> 03-13 repro in staging -> 03-14 agent workaround deployed + customer to change NAT settings. Monitoring shows error rate dropped from ~4% to <0.3% after mitigations.

Issue summary: Customer reports an unexpected deduction and missing hourly-buffer credits on their finalized invoice for 2026-03-09. They saw a ~$12.5k charge labelled 'hourly-buffer-eviction' which they believe should have been covered by their reserved/dedicated buffer for that hour.

Impact: Financial; customer-facing invoice shows a one-off negative credit and provisional balance increased. Customer reports this blocks autopay review for accounting and may delay month-end reconciliation.

Environment: prod, dedicated tenant for NovusDocs in us-east-1. Tokens processed via hybrid batch/stream queue between 2026-03-09T01:00 and 2026-03-09T02:00 UTC.

Steps to reproduce reported by customer: 1) Run multi-model batch job (mixed embed + chat) across two worker pools with tagged warmups and hourly snapshot enabled. 2) During job, a scheduled maintenance caused a transient mux swap (staging->prod) for some postback tags. 3) After job completion, invoice finalized and shows eviction deduction.

Observed logs/snippets:
- postback-reconciler INFO 2026-03-09T01:12:03Z postback accepted tenant=novusdocs tag=hourly-snapshot instance=prod-05 postback_id=pb_8a7f
- postback-reconciler WARN 2026-03-09T01:12:13Z tag-resolve collision detected tag=hourly-snapshot namespace=default->staging

payload.description:
Issue summary: FinSight needs an on-demand SIEM export that includes (1) a per-event retention flag indicating whether an event is eligible for customer-initiated deletion, (2) a cryptographically signed attestation that a requested deletion window was applied to the exported slice, and (3) HMACed resume tokens so their downstream receiver can perform gap-resilient ingest.

Impact: Customer cannot complete legal hold verification with their internal compliance team without both the per-record retention metadata and a verifiable deletion attestation. This is blocking their SOC2 evidence package for Q2 readiness.

Environment: Redwood production, tenant=fin_sight_prod, region=us-east-1, SIEM bridge configured to push to customer's S3/Hec endpoint.

Steps to reproduce / request details:
1) Customer requests an on-demand export for tenant fin_sight_prod for time window 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z -> 2026-02-28T23:59:59Z.
2) Export must include a field audit.retention_flag with values {retain, deletable, pending-review}.
3) Export bundle must contain a signed deletion_attestation.json manifest (RFC3161-style timestamp + SHA256 manifest of deleted record ids / hashed identifiers).
4) Each CompressedDelta file should include a resume_token header HMACed with customer's shared secret.
5) Customer requests a sample package (first 1M events) and a full runback plan for weekly incremental exports thereafter.

Expected behavior: Redwood produces an export package with the described fields, a signed manifest proving which records were removed due to a tenant-scoped deletion request, and HMACed tokens so the customer's SIEM can verify continuity.

Actual / current behavior: Customer has successfully received standard SIEM deltas but they lack per-record retention metadata and there is no signed deletion attestation format currently available in our default export. They also requested HMACed resume tokens which are not in the standard header today.

Attachments: sample_export_request.json (attached by customer), screenshot of customer's compliance checklist, link to customer's ingestion spec (provided below).

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - Legal (Sara Donovan): Suggested attestation should include: (a) RFC3161-compatible timestamp, (b) canonical list of hashed identifiers (SHA256 with tenant salt) for records removed, (c) signature using our HSM key. Asked for retention policy doc from customer to verify mapping to 'pending-review'.
Findings: internal audit pipeline contains event.metadata.retention_state and event.id (uuid). We currently compute ledger checkpoints with SHA256 of raw event bytes, but we don't produce a canonical hashed list of removed IDs. HSM team confirmed we can sign arbitrary blobs with tenant-signing-key alias 'signing/exports' with owner approval. Engineering risks: exposing retention_state might reveal sensitive teardown signals; must map internal states to customer-friendly flags and redact any PII fields.
Hypothesis: We can satisfy request by (1) adding a per-export transformer that emits audit.retention_flag and canonical_identifier (sha256(event.id + tenant_salt)), (2) include deletion_attestation.json containing RFC3161 timestamp, canonical list hash, and HSM signature, (3) add X-Resume-Token-HMAC header to delta objects.
Work items created: INT-991 (schema-and-transform), INT-1002 (hsm-signing-workflow), INT-1003 (siem-bridge-header-and-s3-manifest).
Workaround supplied: On 2026-03-13 we provided a manually-generated sample package (1,000 events) that includes event.retention_flag and a provisional deletion_attestation signed with a staging key. Customer validated format.
Next steps / targeted fix: Engineering will implement automated deletion_attestation generation and HMACed resume tokens. ETA for production-ready export and HSM-signed manifest: 2026-03-22 (subject to keys approval). Please confirm whether customer requires ed25519 or can accept RSA-PSS signing; legal prefers ed25519 if feasible.
Open follow-ups: obtain customer's HMAC key exchange method (KMS-wrapped or shared secret), confirm acceptable signature algorithm, and schedule a validation run for a 1M event slice in a non-production sandbox before full export.
payload.summary: SIEM export - per-record retention flags, deletion attestation, and HMAC resume tokens

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that after switching their embedding producer to a low-precision path (int8 quantized embeddings) the /rerank endpoint returns near-identical top-k scores (score saturation) across distinct queries and p99 latency increases from ~120ms to >2s. Impact: Queries that previously returned meaningful re-rank order are now effectively random or identical in order; downstream UX shows repeated top result and customers are throttling traffic. Environment: Dedicated account in prod (ClariSearch Labs); embeddings produced by customer integration with embeddings endpoint specifying precision=int8. Steps to reproduce:
1) POST /v1/embeddings with model=text-embed-large-v2 and body {"input": [..], "precision": "int8", "namespace": "cs-search-2026"}
2) POST /v1/rerank with same namespace and top_k=10 using reranker-compact-v1
3) Observe rerank scores are clustered near 1.0 and top-k ordering is unstable between identical queries.
Expected behavior: Rerank should accept embeddings in supported formats or convert/dequantize appropriately and return discriminative scores.
Observed behavior: Score saturation (many scores ~0.98-1.0), repeated identical ordering across different queries, and intermittent p99 latency spikes focused on rerank service.
Relevant logs/snippets:
- Embeddings call returns header: "embedding-format: int8;scale=0.0078125"
- Rerank request shows no precision header forwarded in service logs; path triggers fallback conversion in CPU path with repeated memcopies.
- Grafana: reranker.p99_latency_us spiked from 120000 to 2500000 around 2026-02-19T15:10:00Z.
- Kibana trace: trace_id=tr-8f3a2f -> time spent in reranker.dequantize: ~1.4s per request.
Attachments: customer-supplied sample request IDs: EMB-cc-20260219-9734, RER-cc-20260219-9735.
Customer impact level: High (search relevance broken; business users reporting regressions)

Additional notes:
2026-02-20 10:05 - ClariSearch Support Engineer (customer): Provided sample IDs EMB-cc-20260219-9734 and RER-cc-20260219-9735. Confirmed they toggled embedding precision to 'int8' last night only for A/B tests.
2026-02-21 08:45 - SRE Pager (automated): Linked Grafana alert ran; incident page created INC-20260221-04.
2026-02-23 09:10 - ClariSearch Support Engineer (customer): Confirmed immediate improvement for A/B traffic using new canary; scores are now discriminative. Still seeing occasional latency blips for large batch sizes (~>1024 embeddings).
Reproduction: Diego reproduced with a small script that generated int8 quantized vectors (scale 0.0078125). The reranker service previously relied on caller-conveyed float32 embeddings or an explicit 'float32' header. When presented with an 'embedding-format: int8;scale=...' header the header was dropped during namespace routing in api-gateway due to an older proxy rule. Result: reranker interpreted payload as Base64-encoded float32, then triggered an error path that attempted to convert via CPU fallback. Findings: 1) Missing header propagation between embeddings-service -> metadata-store -> reranker. 2) No GPU fast-path for int8->float32 dequantize in reranker; conversion was memory-bound on CPU and took ~1.2-1.6s per request for medium batches. 3) Normalization/scaling mismatch: dequantize used an incorrect scale when header absent leading to near-equal vectors after L2-normalize which produced score saturation. Tests performed: A) Reproduced locally with explicit header injection and observed normal behavior. B) Forced header drop and observed saturation and latency spike. C) Implemented unit test that fails on missing header propagation and added integration test for precision variants. Observability: Added temporary telemetry to count requests where embedding-format header is absent but payload length matches int8 pattern. Current hypothesis confirmed: header drop + incorrect fallback dequantize cause both quality and latency regression.
Short-term mitigation: deployed canary patch to reranker to accept int8 payloads by reading scale from payload metadata and apply correct dequantization fast-path when possible. Also updated API-gateway rule to propagate 'embedding-format' and 'embedding-scale' headers through namespace routing. Provided customer workaround: set precision=float32 or enable 'compat_mixed_precision' flag in their client to force on-the-fly dequantize at production embedding time.
Long-term fix & follow-ups (backlog): 1) Add GPU-accelerated dequantize kernel to reranker for dedicated/private clusters (PR #428 merged). 2) Add end-to-end test for precision header propagation and scoring stability. 3) Add alert that fires when >1% of rerank requests have missing precision header for a namespace. 4) Documentation update: explicitly call out supported embedding serialization formats and interaction with reranker.
Customer communication: Informed ClariSearch that hotfix rolled to canary and then to full fleet; they validated improved ranking and reduced p99 latencies. Next steps: schedule a short postmortem with Eng + SRE + Support and deliver a follow-up note to the customer with recommended client settings.
payload.summary: Misaligned precision between embeddings producer and reranker causing score saturation and p99 latency spikes

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long chat completions which include fenced code blocks sometimes return without the closing triple-backticks (```), and the client SDK (js v3.2.0) stops parsing the stream and never emits the final 'done' event. This occurs after transient socket handoffs seen in the customer's edge path.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat UIs occasionally render unclosed code blocks and hang in a streaming state.
- Affects NovaHealth internal tools (HIPAA-scoped) using our Private deployment in us-east-1.
- Repro rate ~1-2% for eligible long responses; customer sees it multiple times per hour in production.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) in us-east-1.
- Client: NovaHealth web app using Redwood JS SDK v3.2.0 with websocket transport fallback enabled.
- Edge path: customer->enterprise WAF->CDN (FastEdge) with TLS early-data/0-RTT enabled->Redwood edge proxy->serving cluster.
- Request pattern: chat-completion streams with function-calls and metadata envelope events interleaved with token chunks.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Use web app with JS SDK v3.2.0, start a chat completion that produces a multi-paragraph response containing a fenced code block near the end.
2) Induce a short network path change (customer used a curl-based test that sends a RST from the CDN simulating connection handoff).
3) Observe that the stream resumes but the SDK never sees the closing fence and does not emit finalization events.

Observed behavior:
- Final token fragments appear in edge logs, but the client only receives partial suffix tokens and a metadata envelope arrives out-of-order (metadata finalizer arrives before the last token payload).
- Client SDK parser treats metadata finalizer as terminal before receiving remaining byte fragments and ignores subsequent payload frames.
- Server-side traces show the serving runtime emitted the closing tokens and end-event; however the edge-proxy log contains a coalesced keepalive + final-metadata frame that is re-ordered during socket handoff.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming frames (tokens) and metadata envelopes are delivered in original emission order. Finalizing metadata should not be treated as terminal unless all tokens are delivered and end-event has been passed.

Attachments:
- Customer-provided capture: client-side websocket capture (redacted) attached to ticket (link provided via secure upload).
- Edge logs (scrubbed) and serving traces from our trace collector.

Notes:
- Customer has production SLA and requires a mitigation while we investigate.

2026-03-12 09:24 UTC — Support (Aisha): Acknowledged. Reproduced once in our staging environment with a synthetic path-change using FastEdge's RST probe. Escalating to SRE.
2026-03-12 12:37 UTC — SRE (Diego): Collected edge-proxy pcap and request-id trace. Observed coalesced frames immediately after a connection handoff. Attaching pcap to INT-2143.
2026-03-13 08:03 UTC — SRE (Diego): Hypothesis: FastEdge TLS early-data retry triggers a half-close then socket rebind; edge-proxy's outbound socket queue reorders small keepalive/metadata frames with last token fragments. Will instrument reordering counters.
2026-03-13 15:12 UTC — Eng (Ravi Patel): Noted client SDK v3.2.0 treats a metadata-final event as terminal if it sees the 'final' flag. Suggest change to parser to buffer until end-event token seen or a timeout. Opened PR github.com/redwood/replay-fix/pull/442.
2026-03-14 02:41 UTC — Support (Aisha): Customer requested a short-term workaround they can apply without code changes on production private network. Suggested configuration toggles below.
Edge-proxy (v1.17.3) shows 37 instances of small-frame-coalescing within 5 minutes for this request-id range.
PCAP indicates a SACKed RST from FastEdge followed by 0-RTT retry; TCP-level re-ordering of 2-3 small frames was observed.
Serving runtime emitted finalization event at 2026-03-12T09:15:21.382Z and tokens up to offset 1024; edge-proxy logged metadata-final at 2026-03-12T09:15:21.385Z and token payload arrives at 2026-03-12T09:15:21.388Z (re-ordered).
Client SDK behavior: in v3.2.0 parser sees metadata-final with final=true and transitions to terminal state immediately; subsequent payload frames are dropped by parser.
Reproduction in internal lab: reproducible when edge-proxy coalesces keepalive/metadata frame and a socket handoff is performed within 50ms window.
Workaround trial: disable websocket multiplexing or disable CDN early-data: both reduced repro rate to <0.1% in customer tests.
Frame reordering at the edge during socket handoff combined with an overly-eager client parser that treats metadata-final as termination prior to receiving remaining payload frames.
Customer action: 1) Instruct their CDN to disable TLS early-data (0-RTT) for the edge path to prevent the rebind probe; or 2) Set JS SDK option 'streamingFallback: false' to prefer a single websocket connection without multiplexed handoffs. Both reduced occurrence in tests.
Temporary mitigations suggested to customer. Engineering PR (github.com/redwood/replay-fix/pull/442) landed a parser change to buffer metadata-final events until an explicit end-event or a short buffer timeout. Edge-proxy PR (github.com/redwood/edge-proxy/pull/998) adds a small reordering guard for coalesced small frames during handoff. Will schedule coordinated canary with Private customers.
1) Backport parser buffer logic to SDK v3.2.x branch (customer uses v3.2.0): planned.
2) Deploy edge-proxy reorder guard to canary pool in us-east-1 (edge team).
3) Coordinate with customer to disable FastEdge 0-RTT for a 48-hour window to validate reduction prior to full rollout.
4) Monitor for stream-finalization errors and client 'hung' sessions via Console alerting (new metric: stream.finalization_mismatch).
Partial: Workarounds recommended and parsing PR merged to main. Edge-proxy fix merged to staging. Awaiting coordinated customer canary and telemetry for full close.
Schedule joint test window with NovaHealth to run canary (edge-proxy + SDK patch) — owner: Diego
Backport and release SDK v3.2.1 with buffering change — owner: Developer Experience
Create Console alert and dashboard for stream.finalization_mismatch — owner: Observability team
Add runbook entry under /confluence/runbooks/edge-handoff-troubleshooting describing mitigation steps for private deployments
payload.summary: Metadata envelope reorder during socket handoff causes client to drop closing code-fence and final tokens

payload.description:
Customer reports repeated 429s during large multipart import where our rate limiter shows bursts from a single API key. Console credit counters appear higher (less consumed) than runtime rate limiter, creating confusion about quota depletion. Issue started after the customer migrated their upload workers behind a retry-proxy that appends a tracing query param to callbacks.
Multiple background ingestion pipelines at Streamline Analytics are failing to complete nightly backfills. Visible symptom: steady stream of 429s for upload-callback POSTs originating from the customer's worker fleet; end-users see backfill job failures and missed SLAs.
1) Configure a dedicated tenant with multipart storage callbacks enabled.
2) Deploy an upload worker behind a proxy that performs retries and appends a unique query parameter (?trace_id=...) on replay.
3) Start parallel multipart uploads that trigger signed-url-callbacks to Redwood callback endpoint.
4) Force intermittent failures on the callback path so the proxy retries, replaying the callback with unique query strings.
5) Observe increased 429s on the tenant and a mismatch between Console 'remaining credits' and runtime rate-limit denied requests.
2026-03-10T02:13:40Z gateway rate-limiter DENY tenant=streamline key=sk_live_XXX path=/v1/uploads/callback status=429 reason=token-exhausted
2026-03-10T02:13:41Z gateway rate-limiter DENY tenant=streamline key=sk_live_XXX path=/v1/uploads/callback?trace_id=abc123 status=429 reason=token-exhausted
2026-03-10T02:13:42Z billing aggregator ingest credit-usage tenant=streamline delta=+1200 tokens (deduped)
Console shows remaining_credits: 12,345 while rate-limiter logs indicate sustained denials. Cobrowsing screenshot uploaded to ticket.
Initial hypothesis: gateway token-bucket is keyed on full request URI (including query string) causing retries with new query params to be treated as distinct windows and double-counting. Billing aggregation pipeline deduplicates callbacks by callback-id in body, hence console shows fewer unique consumptions. Verified via sampling: 1 physical upload produced 3 distinct rate-limiter entries (different query strings) but a single billing record. Confirmed request header differences: proxy adds X-Retry-Index and appends ?trace_id on retry. Related metrics: rate_limit.window_usage spiked to 300% of expected during proxy retry waves. Cross-referenced with dedicated-pool autoscaler metrics: no GPU saturation; this is allocation of request tokens at ingress.
Support (Asha): Customer provided a replayable curl example and pcap. Asked to confirm whether gateway normalizes query params for rate accounting.
SRE (Liam): Reproduced locally with a small proxy that appends ?r=UUID; observed identical behavior. Created a minimal test that shows rate-limiter keying by full request path. Adding as linked issue for gateway change.
Support (Asha): Noted console and billing team treat callbacks as idempotent using callback_id in the body, which explains the visible credit mismatch. Customer is worried about opaque 429s and lack of correlation in Console.
Eng (Riley Chen): Proposed short-term mitigation: recommend disabling query-param append on proxy retries or add 'X-Original-Callback-Id' header from uploader so gateway can dedupe for rate accounting. Filed gateway PR to normalize callback path for rate-limiter (see related PR).
Customer (S. Rivera): Confirmed they can change proxy behavior but prefer a platform-side fix for long-run since multiple clients use proxy.

Additional notes:
Gateway rate-limiter keyed on full request URI including transient query params introduced by retry proxies; billing pipeline deduplicates by callback_id leading to apparent mismatch between Console credits and rate-limiter denials.
Short-term workaround: customer disabled query-param splaying on retry-proxy and enabled X-Original-Callback-Id header; retries now preserve callback_id in header and 429s stopped. Long-term fix: gateway change to normalize signed-url callback paths for rate accounting (strip known tracing query params and prefer callback-id header if present). Patch merged: github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1492. Console note: added a tooltip explaining deduplication logic for callbacks and billing display.
Patch rolled out to dedicated-pool edge in us-east-1 on 2026-03-12 with canary at 5% then 100% after 30m. Post-deploy monitoring: rate-limiter DENY events for tenant dropped by 98% during a replay test. Customer confirmed nightly backfills completed on 2026-03-12 run.
1) Add docs entry in runbook for 'signed-url callback best practices' and recommended headers.
2) Console: surface dedupe vs raw runtime discrepancy in billing pane.
3) Add e2e test that simulates retry-proxy query param splay to prevent regressions.
4) Consider making query-param normalization configurable per-tenant for private deployments.
payload.summary: Multiplexed signed-url retry loop counted as separate requests causing opaque 429s and console credit mismatch

payload.description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12 20:15 UTC we observed a sustained uptick in 5xx errors (predominantly 503 and 502) for a Dedicated customer (BrightWrite Inc.) in us-east. Errors correlate with a heavy number of long-lived streaming sessions that use hedged prefetch requests. Impact: API calls to generation/chat endpoints intermittently return 502/503; streaming sessions abruptly close; customers report degraded latency and dropped responses. Initial hypothesis: runtime threadpool exhaustion / blocking IO in prefetch path leading to upstream failures at the API gateway.
Multiple BrightWrite production routes degraded. Estimated 12% of requests for the customer returned 5xx during peak window (~20:15–21:10 UTC). Customer reported feature-affecting outages for end-users (chat sessions drop). Financial impact potentially high for the customer; they are on a Dedicated plan with SLA.
2026-03-12 20:12 UTC - First alert from synthetic checks.
2026-03-12 20:15 UTC - Customer (BrightWrite) opened support channel reporting dropped streams.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 20:30 UTC - Support engaged SRE and Runtime on-call.
2026-03-12 21:05 UTC - Temporary mitigation (disable hedged prefetch for customer) applied; error rate dropped to baseline by 21:10 UTC.
2026-03-13 10:00 UTC - Follow-up patch PR created to harden streaming prefetch path.
1) Configure high concurrent streaming sessions to the same tenant (BrightWrite test harness used 1k concurrent streams).
2) Enable hedged prefetch for small prompts so runtime issues speculative prefetch calls.
3) Observe runtime threadpool usage and accept queue depth on api-gateway.
4) Reproduce elevated 503/502 when threadpool threads block on socket reads in prefetch path.
- api-gateway metrics: accept_queue_depth spiked to 8k, 502/503 rate climbed to 11%.
- serving-runtime logs (us-east-rt-12): repetitive stack traces showing runtime worker threads blocked on synchronous socket read in prefetch handler.
- pstack / thread dumps attached: threadpool showing ~600 blocked threads waiting on io.
- perf profile: high syscall time for epoll_wait / recv.
- customer-provided trace ids: trace-20260312-BW-4512, trace-20260312-BW-4683.
Initial triage: API gateway reported healthy upstreams but queuing increased; downstream returning 502/503 when upstreams became unresponsive.
Runtime team examined thread dumps and found large count of runtime worker threads in 'blocking socket read' state tied to prefetch/hedge requests. These long-lived streams held threads for extended durations leading to starvation for active generation work.
Hypothesis: hedged prefetch implementation used a synchronous/blocking read path that is safe at low concurrency but causes threadpool fragmentation at scale (combined with a tenant burst pattern).
Perf experiment: disabling hedged prefetch for the tenant immediately lowered blocked thread counts and accept queue depth; error rate returned to baseline (confirms causal link).
Further note: the Dedicated fleet for this customer had slightly smaller runtime threadpool sizing (customer-specified to limit cost), increasing sensitivity to this pattern.
Logs point to socket-level timeouts being extended by client-side keepalives; long tail of idle-but-open prefetch connections prevented reuse of threads.
Related historical tickets flagged a similar resource-pressure pattern but for a different prefetch variant (see SUP-472901).
2026-03-12 21:05 UTC - Applied emergency mitigation: disabled hedged prefetch for BrightWrite tenant via feature-flag (console toggle).
2026-03-12 21:10 UTC - Increased runtime threadpool soft limit for affected Dedicated nodes to provide immediate headroom.
2026-03-12 22:00 UTC - Adjusted api-gateway accept queue and keepalive timeouts to reduce backlog sensitivity.
2026-03-13 09:30 UTC - Runtime patch developed to convert prefetch handler to non-blocking async reads and add per-stream idle timeout; PR opened.
2026-03-13 10:15 UTC - Customer notified of mitigations and planned patch; support scheduled canary rollout.
2026-03-13 14:00 UTC - Canary rollout on staging and one production shard; monitoring shows no regression at low to medium load.
2026-03-13 17:00 UTC - Plan to roll out to rest of Dedicated nodes with monitoring and rollback window.
Mitigation and remediation in progress. Short-term mitigation (disable hedged prefetch + threadpool soft-limit bump) reduced error rate to baseline. Medium-term fix: runtime PR to implement non-blocking prefetch reads + per-stream idle timeout; targeted for production rollout 2026-03-15 after extended canary. Issue summary: MiraHealth reported repeated customer-facing ’inference hangs’ between 08:30–09:20 EDT on 2026-03-10. Symptom reported by customer: long tail requests (30–120s) and apparent timeouts; instruments in their UI show many requests failing and then retrying.

Impact: Production inference for MiraHealth (dedicated pool) experienced degraded p95/p99 latency for text generation endpoints; multiple customer application threads reported blocking waiting for responses and user-facing errors. Impacted ~30% of requests for that tenant during the incident window; major impact for their morning batch job.

Environment: Dedicated tenant in prod-us-east using pinned model redwood-13b-instruct. SDK observed: mira-sdk-js v1.4.2 integrated with custom retry wrapper.

Observed behavior: Redwood backend returned intermittent 429 responses with short-lived quota signals. The customer SDK wrapper retries aggressively (no exponential backoff) which caused a burst of repeated requests in short windows. This amplified load on the tenant's dedicated serving pool and produced longer queues inside the gateway, which in turn increased latency and produced additional 5xx/timeout symptoms at the client.

1) Configure a dedicated tenant with modest concurrent limit and soft quota thresholds (mirrors MiraHealth setup).
2) Run an early-morning batch of 500 concurrent inference requests (mix of streaming and non-streaming) at a token rate similar to customer workload, using mira-sdk-js v1.4.2 + custom retry wrapper that retries immediately on non-2xx.
3) Observe gateway returning intermittent 429s and the client immediately retrying with no backoff, causing request bursts and queueing at gateway and backend.
4) Check metrics: increased gateway request concurrency, queue length in serving-runtime, rising p95/p99 token latency and backend retry rates.
Initial triage by Support: confirmed incident window and mapped to tenant-specific soft quota throttle signals; customer reported client-side retries correlate with spike times.
Checked console dashboards: per-tenant rate-limiter counters show repeated short 429 bursts rather than sustained limit crossings; concurrency inside dedicated pool spiked following each customer retry wave.
Hypothesis A: SDK custom retry wrapper ignores Retry-After header and retries immediately, causing self-amplifying traffic bursts that exceed short-term burst quota and create queueing.
Hypothesis B: Gateway returned 429 without Retry-After consistently for some paths (streaming vs non-streaming) which left client implementations with no guidance and different retry logic.
Telemetry: request traces (link: https://console.redwood.ai/traces?tenant=mirahealth&from=2026-03-10T08:30&to=2026-03-10T09:00) show retry chains of depth 3–6 within 2s windows.
Reproduction: Team reproduced locally using load harness and mira-sdk-js wrapper; immediate-retry pattern recreated the gateway queueing and p99 latency increases.
Root cause candidate: Combination of conservative soft-quota enforcement on the dedicated pool + client retry behavior that does not honor backoff/Retry-After headers.
Amplification loop: tenant-level soft quota produced intermittent 429s. Client-side immediate retries (no exponential backoff / ignored Retry-After) converted transient quota signals into sustained request bursts, overloading gateway queues and increasing p99 latency for the tenant.
Short-term workaround provided to MiraHealth: 1) patch client to implement exponential backoff with jitter and respect Retry-After header (we provided code snippet), 2) temporarily increase the tenant burst window and soft-quota threshold for the dedicated pool to absorb morning batch load, 3) enable per-route explicit 'Retry-After' header emission from gateway.

Operational fix rolled out: engineering adjusted gateway behavior to include Retry-After for soft-quota 429 responses and increased default Retry-After value for streaming endpoints. Also opened PR to add server-side mitigations that limit immediate retries per connection and to emit clearer quota headers (PRs listed above).

Follow-ups: 1) Update SDKs with safe-retry defaults (mira-sdk-js patch PR #412), 2) run post-fix load test for dedicated tenants with similar concurrency patterns, 3) create runbook entry for customers on best retry practices.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:10 - MiraHealth (Customer): Confirmed they will patch client to add exponential backoff; asked for recommended backoff parameters for morning batch.

Issue summary:
Customer reports that a recent client upgrade (MediumCorp Data Platform v2.5) resulted in rerank responses whose top-k ordering flips intermittently and which sometimes stream blank/partial responses then time out. The customer uses our dedicated deployment in us-east and runs their own batching layer in front of the embeddings API.

Impact:
- Observed order instability in production queries affecting relevance-sensitive features (search and recommendations).
- Occasional streaming timeouts on rerank endpoint with 504s after token stream stalls for ~8-12s.
- Customer business impact: A/B tests show CTR drop ~6% on search page for affected cohort.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (customer subnet) in prod:us-east, fallbacks to eu-west for cross-region traffic.
- Client: MediumCorp Data Platform v2.5 (uses client-sdk v3.2 with batched embedding calls and explicit L2-normalization client-side).
- Server models: rwd-embed-1-small (embeddings), rwd-rerank-2 (reranker).

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Construct a 50-query batch at 200 qps via their batching layer to /v1/embeddings with normalize=true on the client.
2) Send the resulting vector batch to /v1/rerank with per-item metadata and expect top-5 ordered scores.
3) Observe that in ~5-10% of batches, rerank returns an ordering where items with identical content flip positions between requests; streaming path returns partial tokens then stalls to timeout.

Observed logs / artifacts provided by customer:
- Example payloads (sanitized) showing embedding vectors of length 384 and some vectors containing trailing zeros for ~30% of items in certain batches.
- Client debug shows it calls client-sdk.normalizeBatch(vectors) before sending; server side logs show Accept-Encoding: chunked and several "stream-write timeout" events around the rerank worker PID.
- Sample timestamps: 2026-03-11T15:23:01.123Z batch-id=mc-9912 - rerank stream stall after token 12 of 45.

Initial hypothesis:
- Mismatch between client-side normalization and server-side expectation (server expects unit-normalized embedding when computing cosine similarity inside reranker). Batched client normalization + internal batch-padding/truncation could produce slightly different floating point distributions, and occasional trailing-zero padding from the customer's batching layer is being interpreted as valid vector data. That leads to near-duplicate vectors with changed magnitudes, which both perturbs ranking and occasionally triggers the streaming path to fall back/mis-handle KV cache offsets, causing stream stalls.

Requested from customer:
- Full raw batch (pre-normalization) and post-normalization vectors for three failing batches.
- Network captures around the chunked stream difference.
- Confirmation of exact client-sdk version and any custom patch to normalization routine.

Priority/SLAs:
- P1 / Sev1 due to direct revenue impact (CTR and search regressions). First response SLA met. Working with customer success on daily syncs.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 13:45 - MediumCorp (Customer): Uploaded three failing batches (mc-9912, mc-9940, mc-10012). Noted they do call normalizeBatch and that they recently upgraded client-sdk.
2026-03-14 09:12 - SRE (Helena Zhou): Observed a correlation between chunk size and stream stall windows. When batch encoding crosses 16KB boundary, rerank streaming writes sometimes block under high contention. Investigating connection buffer thresholds.
2026-03-14 12:05 - MediumCorp: Confirmed that after temporary hotfix their failing batches now receive a 400 with detail indicating 'trailing_zero_padding_detected' and are working on fixing client-side batching. Customer requests permanent fix to co-exist with client-side normalization differences.
2026-03-14 12:45 - Product (Sofia Martinez): Requesting design doc for server-side resilient normalization and clear API contract (server expects unit vectors unless header 'raw-embeddings: true' set).
1) Reproducer built using the customer's client-sdk v3.2 + a small shim that pads batches to multiples of 8 causing trailing zeros. Confirmed rank flips when padded zeros are present and when server does not re-normalize. 2) Rerank code historically assumed incoming vectors are normalized; defensive checks were minimal to avoid extra CPU. 3) Streaming stall reproduced when chunked response hit internal write buffer limit while a goroutine performing KV lookup experienced GC pauses; combination caused stream writer to block and client to time out. 4) Metric spike: rerank.invalid_vector_detected=128 in 24h window for customer pool. 5) No sign of model weight corruption or quantization mismatch (scores scaled normally).
Short term: server hotfix to validate vectors and return explicit 400 with 'trailing_zero_padding_detected' and a remediation message. Medium term: implement server-side optional renormalization flow when header 'x-allow-renorm: true' is provided; add best-effort trimming of all-zero suffix bytes in embedding payloads and log telemetry. Long term: update public API docs and client-sdk to avoid silent normalization semantics mismatch, add pre-flight validation endpoint /v1/embeddings/validate. Also add integration test to CI that simulates batched padding patterns.
In progress - temporary validation hotfix deployed to MediumCorp's dedicated pool on 2026-03-14 11:30. Customer confirmed hotfix surfaced explicit 400s and they are rolling a client patch to stop appending padding zeros. Engineering to deliver medium-term renormalization option and docs updates. No full RCA posted yet; follow-up postmortem scheduled after deploy of medium-term fix.
- Track metric 'rerank.invalid_vector_detected' for customer pool for 7 days.
- Schedule API contract clarification in next sprint; owner: Sofia Martinez.
- SRE to review streaming write buffer defaults and GC tuning for dedicated pools.
- Communicate to SDK teams to add explicit warnings when normalize=true is used with batched padding.
payload.summary: Batched normalization discrepancy causing rerank order flip and streaming timeouts

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasAI received invoice #INV-2026-0310 with a charge for a private VPC egress connector that was retired mid-billing-cycle (connector id: vpc-conn-78-retired). AtlasAI requested a prorated credit for the portion of the cycle after retirement.

Impact:
- AtlasAI was charged €1,240.00 for VPC egress hours spanning 2026-02-25 to 2026-03-01 even though the connector was removed on 2026-02-27.
- No prorated credit line appears on the invoice; the customer reports their payment auto‑charged and requests correction before month-end accounting.

Environment:
- Customer private deployment (VPC) with Private control plane and on-prem connector routing through eu-west-1.
- Billing backend: postback-reconciler v3.7.1; invoicing service v2.12.

Steps to reproduce / observed flow:
1) Customer retired the connector via Console on 2026-02-27 09:12 CET (console activity id: act-20260227-901).
2) Post-rotation traffic was routed to hosted fallback for 02/27–03/01 because a cached mapping still referenced the retired connector id.
3) Metering postbacks for the retired connector arrived with tag connector_id=vpc-conn-78-retired on 2026-02-27 09:14–23:59 and 2026-02-28–03-01 from fallback nodes; reconciler accepted them and attributed to AtlasAI private-eject tariff.
4) Invoice generated on 2026-03-10 included the full daily egress lines for 02/27–03/01 with no prorate or credit.

Expected behavior:
- Connector retirement should trigger (a) immediate update to the postback mapping table and (b) postbacks coming from fallback nodes referencing retired IDs should be reclassified to hosted-fallback tariff and to a provisional billing code that is excluded from final private-eject lines, or else generate a prorated credit.

Actual behavior:
- Postback reconciler accepted retired connector-tagged postbacks as private-eject and created invoice lines without prorate. No automatic credit job was triggered.

Logs / evidence attached in ticket body:
- Console activity id: act-20260227-901 (customer supplied).
- Sample reconciler acceptance events: reconciler.log lines with trace ids rcz-89a1, rcz-89a2 (2026-02-27 09:14–09:18 CET).
- Invoice excerpt: INV-2026-0310 lines 12–14 (private-vpc egress charges).
- Slack thread: #support -> thread t: slack.com/archives/C0123456/p167762 (customer message included).

Immediate customer ask:
- Apply a manual prorated credit for the amount charged after 2026-02-27 09:12 CET and update the finalized invoice or issue a one-time credit memo. Customer requires confirmation before 2026-03-16 for their internal close.

Investigation notes (support):
- Billing ops ran a dry reconcile and found reconciler mapping table still had a live mapping entry for vpc-conn-78 until 2026-02-27 09:20 due to delayed cache invalidation (cache flush job failed and retried).
- Postback payloads from fallback proxies included connector_id but also older tag format connector.name; reconciler v3.7.1 prefers connector.name when present and fell back to connector_id in a path that does not trigger retirement rules.
- Related PR created to add a retired-connector guard in reconciler: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/4123 (merged, awaiting rollout).
- Potential root cause: cache invalidation race plus a reconciler matching priority regression introduced in v3.7.0 that allowed retired connector_id matches to persist.

Proposed next steps:
- Short-term: issue manual credit memo equal to prorated egress amount for 2026-02-27 09:12 CET -> 2026-03-01 end-of-day and notify customer. (Billing ops assigned to do this).
- Mid-term: deploy reconciler patch that rejects postbacks for retired connector_ids or classifies them under provisional-hosted tariff, and add an alert for cache-flush failures. (Engineering).
- Postmortem: document the cache invalidation behavior and update Console retirement flow to force synchronous reconciler mapping update for private connectors.

Status: engineering patch merged to main; staging deploy scheduled 2026-03-14; manual credit prepared and pending finance approval.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 08:10 - Finance (automated): Manual credit memo draft created for €762.00 (prorated portion). Pending manager approval (finance ticket FIN-2026-1187).
Manual credit memo drafted for €762.00 and linked to FIN-2026-1187. Reconciler fix merged (PR #4123) to prevent retired-connector acceptance; staging deploy scheduled 2026-03-14. Follow-up action: after staging verification, run backfill to identify any other retired-connector postbacks in the last 30 days and issue credits where appropriate. Customer will receive confirmation and updated invoice once finance finalizes the memo.

Issue summary: Between ~18:03 and 18:22 UTC on 2026-03-13 we observed an abrupt elevation in 5xx responses for a subset of dedicated customers in us-east-1. Errors were concentrated on streaming and short-payload chat routes. Impact: BrightChat Labs reported a 25% failure rate for in-flight requests during the window; customer-facing sessions observed stream resets and 502/503 responses. Initial hypothesis: coincident SSL session ticket rotation on several load-balancers triggered connection churn that amplified hedged retries and runtime preemption leading to upstream throttling and transient 5xxs.
2026-03-13 17:58 UTC - Keystore rotation job scheduled for region us-east-1 (automated daily rotation).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer (ScribeLabs) reports large p99/p95 latency increases and an overall throughput collapse for requests routed to their dedicated GPU pool starting 2026-03-10 07:30 UTC. Impact: production traffic for several customer routes degraded to <10% expected throughput for ~40 minutes, causing user-facing timeouts. Environment: prod dedicated pool in eu-west serving mixed chat and classification workloads on pinned model redwood-chat-3b-v2. Observed symptoms include repeated GPU allocation failures, batch queue pileups, and autoscaler failing to scale up fast enough.

High-level hypothesis: a staggered prefetch sweep from multiple internal tenants created transient NVMe I/O pressure and prefetched large KV caches which forced the allocator to serialize GPU attachments; combined with the autoscaler's cooldown heuristics this produced a window where new allocations were throttled, leading to noisy-neighbor-like starvation in the dedicated pool.
ScribeLabs experienced a 40-minute production degradation during peak onboarding period affecting new user sign-ups and demos. No data loss, only increased error and timeout rates. Customer requested an RCA and timeline for permanent mitigation.
1) Route sustained short-chat streams (~200-300ms per request) plus intermittent long-context classification jobs to a dedicated pool pinned to redwood-chat-3b-v2.
2) Trigger a prefetch/config-sweep across multiple tenants in the same pool by deploying a policy change (simulated via internal tooling).
3) Observe allocator logs and GPU attach timings and measure per-tenant batch queue depth and p99 latency over a 30-60 minute window.
4) Confirm autoscaler does not immediately add capacity due to backoff/cooldown.

Expected behavior: smooth autoscale ramp and bounded p99 latency. Observed: bursty attach failures and throughput collapse until a manual override/increase is applied.
[2026-03-10T07:32:05Z] allocator: attach_request start tenant=scribelabs session=xyz\n[2026-03-10T07:32:06Z] allocator: attach_request blocked nvme-io=high prefetch_jobs=18\n[2026-03-10T07:33:10Z] serving-runtime: batch_queue_depth=124 p99=4.1s p50=210ms\n[2026-03-10T07:34:02Z] autoscaler: scale_decision=NOOP cooldown_remaining=270s reason=\"recent_scale_down\"\n[2026-03-10T07:34:30Z] gpu-driver: gpu_attach_timeout pid=4312 elapsed=30000ms\n[2026-03-10T07:35:50Z] allocator: attach_success tenant=scribelabs attach_latency=4.3s\n[2026-03-10T07:40:12Z] monitoring: pool_throughput_drop=87%\nLogs archived to: s3://redwood-support-logs/SUP-248621/2026-03-10/
07:33 UTC: replicated slot-attach latencies correlate with elevated NVMe IO wait on nodes in eu-west cluster N-12.
07:38 UTC: prefetcher telemetry shows overlapping cache population jobs from 5 tenants; two tenants launched large context prefetches within a 2-minute window.
07:40 UTC: autoscaler logs indicate cooldown prevented immediate scale-up; cooldown policy requisition did not consider nvme-io as a trigger metric.
07:45 UTC: manual scaling (add 2 gpus) brought throughput back to baseline in ~5 minutes, indicating capacity rather than model failure.
Hypothesis: combination of storage I/O saturation and conservative autoscaler cooldown created a transient allocation bottleneck; tenant prefetch waves acted as noisy neighbor events despite dedicated pool tenancy due to shared node-level IO subsystems.
Telemetry sliced by tenant shows ScribeLabs' requests were getting queued behind a small number of prefetch-heavy sessions from internal test tenants.
Potential mitigations: introduce nvme_io pressure metric into autoscaler triggers; stagger prefetch jobs; implement per-node I/O fairness (limit concurrent large prefetches).
Customer comment (2026-03-10 08:05 UTC) - Helena @ ScribeLabs: "We saw user sessions timeout and a spike in errors across two routes. Appreciate any ETA, this is impacting onboarding demos."
Support (2026-03-10 08:18 UTC) - Aisha: "Acknowledged, we're investigating. Can you confirm if any large batch jobs started around 07:20-07:40 UTC on your side?"
Customer (2026-03-10 08:22 UTC) - Helena: "No large jobs on our side; most traffic was short chat. We did roll a small model-pin change earlier but that shouldn't trigger heavy prefetch."
SRE (2026-03-10 09:02 UTC) - Miguel: "Found concurrent prefetch sweeps from internal QA tenants; starting manual scale and isolating those sessions. Pushing patch to autoscaler logic to consider nvme_io."
Support (2026-03-10 10:10 UTC) - Aisha: "Manual mitigation complete, we've added temporary capacity to ScribeLabs' pool and paused QA prefetch jobs. Monitoring for stability."
Workaround applied: manually added 2 GPUs to ScribeLabs' dedicated pool and paused overlapping prefetch jobs from internal tenants, which restored throughput. Root cause: node-level NVMe I/O saturation from concurrent prefetch sweeps combined with autoscaler cooldown prevented timely scale-up and serialized GPU attachments. Permanent fixes planned: (1) autoscaler change to include nvme_io and queue_depth as up-scaling triggers, (2) a prefetch-scheduling gate to stagger large cache population jobs across nodes, (3) implement per-node I/O throttles for prefetcher to avoid blocking attach paths. Follow-ups: scheduled postmortem with SRE and Runtime teams (CON-2026-03-PM-72) and a customer-facing RCA by 2026-03-15.
PR to autoscaler: add nvme_io and batch_queue_depth thresholds for aggressive up-scaling (owner: autoscaler team) - target merge 2026-03-12
Implement prefetch gate in prefetcher service to avoid simultaneous large cache jobs on same node (owner: runtime team) - ETA 2026-03-18
Create runbook entry for dedicated pools to detect nvme_io-pressure and manual scale runbook (owner: support) - ETA 2026-03-13

Issue summary: Customer VelaCommerce reports intermittent 403s when Redwood serving nodes attempt to fetch large model shard ranges (presigned S3 URLs) from within their private deployment (VPCE). Failures are selective: small artifact fetches succeed, full-object GETs succeed from some subnets, but parallel ranged requests for large shards return AccessDenied (403) from the presigned host.

Impact: Production inference jobs for VelaCommerce intermittently fail to initialize large models. Customers see ~2-6% of shard range requests returning 403 which causes retry storms and increased token/compute cost. Affects only the private deployment in us-east-1.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) using VPCE to access S3-backed artifact store. Serving nodes run our 2026.02 runtime. Problem reproduces from two branch office subnets behind the customer's recursive DNS appliances; not reproducible from VelaCommerce's bastion that uses cloud DNS directly.
1) From a node in the affected branch office subnet, curl a presigned shard GET (with Range header) -> observe 403 from S3-like endpoint
2) Re-run curl with the fully-qualified host name suffixed by a trailing dot (e.g., 'bucket.s3.amazonaws.com.') -> request succeeds
3) Re-run curl from same node but force resolver to 8.8.8.8 -> request succeeds
4) From a different customer subnet (same VPC) where DNS is resolved by corporate forwarding bypass -> requests succeed normally
403 AccessDenied for ranged GETs to presigned hostname only when resolved via the customer's branch recursive DNS/resolver appliance. S3 logs show the request reached a different backend hostname (internal ALB) and AccessDenied reason: 'Signature does not match' along with an altered Host header in some traces.
Presigned shard range GETs should succeed from any customer subnet that can reach the artifact endpoint via the VPCE; DNS resolution should return the canonical S3 host used to generate the presigned URL, and host header should match the signed hostname.
Serving node logs (excerpt): GET /shard?id=... Range: bytes=0-10485759 -> 403 AccessDenied (request-id: 5D1A9X)
S3-like endpoint audit: request-id 5D1A9X -> Host header received: 'bucket.s3.amazonaws.com.corp.local' -> Auth failed: Signature mismatch
tcpdump from branch node: DNS A lookup for 'bucket.s3.amazonaws.com' returns 52.216.xx.xx; subsequent DNS resolve with search suffix appended returns 10.1.2.7 (internal) via split-horizon resolver
Initial triage: reproduced from customer's branch subnets. Bypassing the corporate DNS (using 8.8.8.8 or adding trailing dot to the FQDN) returns the original public S3 hostname and fixes fetches.

Hypothesis: Customer's recursive resolver applies search-suffix aggregation incorrectly for single-label or multi-label FQDNs due to ndots and search order config. When the presigned host is queried without trailing dot, the resolver appends the corporate search suffix and returns a CNAME/A pointing into the customer's internal realm (10.*) or to a private ALB backed by their VPCE. Because presigned URLs are host-bound (signature includes hostname), routing to the internal backend produces signature mismatch and 403.

We observed that only ranged requests (multipart/range GETs) were failing in larger volumes; preliminary theory is that parallel ranged GETs cause different underlying connections to be routed to different backends due to split-horizon last-mile NAT or egress load-balancer rules, which amplifies the problem (some parts hit the correct endpoint, others hit the internal rewrite), causing partial shard failures and validation errors in the runtime.
Resolver search-suffix + ndots misconfiguration at branch DNS appliances rewrites FQDNs into split-horizon internal names. VPCE still NATs/forwards traffic, but host header mismatch results in S3 returning 403. Parallel range requests increase exposure because some connections resolve to the wrong IP. Not a Redwood presigned URL bug but a network/DNS configuration issue at customer side that interacts badly with VPCE split-horizon and presigned host binding.
Short-term mitigations provided to customer: 1) Re-generate presigned URLs with a trailing dot in hostname (e.g., 'bucket.s3.amazonaws.com.') — most resolvers treat the dot as absolute and will not append search suffix. 2) Configure branch DNS appliances to set 'ndots' higher (>=5) or remove the search suffix for the VPC domain. 3) Add an explicit hosts entry on the affected nodes mapping the presigned host to the expected public S3 IPs (temporary, not recommended at scale). 4) Route artifact fetches from branch nodes through a bastion/proxy that uses cloud DNS (short term).
Customer applied workaround #4 (proxy through bastion) during business hours; artifact fetch success rate returned to ~99.8%. We've scheduled a follow-up with customer's network team to update resolver configs.
1) SRE to verify whether VPCE policy/logs show requests routed to internal ALB when DNS includes search suffix. (Assigned: Tomás)
2) Recommend long-term: customer to exclude presigned S3 host patterns from search-suffix application or update branch resolver firmware.
3) Engineering to add a short note in the Private deployment onboarding docs about presigned-hostname and ndots/search-suffix caveat. (Assigned: Docs/DevEx)
4) Track/close once customer confirms resolver change in a staging branch and we observe no presigned 403s for 48 hours.
Pending customer DNS configuration change. No platform code change required at this time. If customer cannot change resolver behavior, we will discuss SDK-level fallback patterns (append trailing dot when generating presigned URLs) as a compatibility option, documented and opt-in only.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:10 - Tomás Alvarez (SRE): Reproduced from customer branch via VPN. Confirmed DNS search-suffix appended; bypassing resolver fixes fetch. Filed hypothesis and requested VPCE flow logs.
2026-03-12 14:42 - VelaCommerce Network Team (customer): Confirmed branch resolver appliances are on default ndots=1 and corporate search suffix 'corp.local' is applied. Will trial changing ndots on one branch tomorrow.
2026-03-13 08:05 - Tomás Alvarez (SRE): VPCE access logs show mixed backend IPs for the same presigned hostname when queries come from branch subnets. Correlates with our hypothesis. Recommended customer apply exclusion rule for S3 hostnames in their resolver policy.
payload.summary: Branch DNS search/suffix truncation causes presigned hostnames to be rewritten, resulting in selective shard 403s
