payload.description:
Issue summary: Customers using dedicated capacity reported SSE/chat streams silently pausing mid-generation for ~25-40s then resuming. Impact: Interactive chat UX times out or appears frozen for users; some clients hit SDK timeouts and close the socket, resulting in truncated replies. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) in us-east; affects a subset of workers on machines with >48GB GPU memory running quantized models. First reported by BrightGuide Analytics during peak usage window. Observed behavior: Server keeps producing keep-alive events but no token chunks are emitted for the pause window. When generation resumes, multiple tokens are emitted in a burst to catch up.
1) Provision dedicated instance with gpt-redi-6B-quantized-v2 pinned in us-east
2) Start an SSE chat stream with long-generation prompt (expected >600 tokens) and response_continuation enabled
3) Simulate sustained load (50 concurrent chats) to force normal batching and occasional KV checkpointing
4) Observe that ~10-15% of streams experience a silent pause ~25-40s into generation; server keep-alives continue but data tokens stop
5) Remove/disable the scheduled memory compaction task on the worker and repeat — pause frequency drops to ~0%
[2026-03-12T15:07:42Z] worker-71 INFO start-generation request_id=ch_zz12
[2026-03-12T15:07:55Z] worker-71 DEBUG kv-checkpoint begin checkpoint_id=ckpt-187
[2026-03-12T15:08:04Z] worker-71 WARN memory-compactor triggered: active_allocations=0.92 total_free=3.1GB
[2026-03-12T15:08:04Z] worker-71 DEBUG cuda-defrag blocking on stream 3 for 26080ms
[2026-03-12T15:08:04Z] http-sse connection keepalive sent to client_id=bg-conn-9
[2026-03-12T15:08:30Z] worker-71 INFO cuda-defrag completed; generation resumed; tokens_emitted=+320
SRE initial triage correlated stalls with the on-host memory compaction/defragmentation routine that runs as part of periodic KV checkpointing and a background 'memory-compactor' service. NVML traces show a spike in pci mem operations and a blocking CUDA stream wait for ~25-40s at the same timestamps as customer reports. pprof of the runtime during an incident shows the generation coroutine is blocked waiting on a GPU defrag mutex while the SSE connection remains open and keepalive frames continue. Pattern reproduced reliably on dedicated workers with >40GB allocations and when a background snapshot/compaction coincides with long in-flight generations. The compaction is synchronous and uses a single-threaded CUDA stream which starves generation kernels. We confirmed disabling the compaction on a single host removed the pauses. No changes to the customer SDK or networking path were found. Related PR introduces an async compaction path: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1426

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 09:03 - BrightGuide Support (Customer): We can reproduce on our end; disabling the 'auto-continue' option reduces impact but is not acceptable. Please advise ETA for fix.
Workaround: Disabled synchronous memory compaction on impacted dedicated pools and adjusted KV checkpoint timing to off-peak windows (00:00-03:00 UTC) to avoid coinciding with customer peak. Patch: Merged non-blocking compaction PR implementing GPU-friendly defrag on a separate CUDA stream (PR 1426). Planned rollout: staggered canary to 10% of dedicated hosts on 2026-03-20, full rollout targeted 2026-03-21 after monitoring. Follow-ups: add alert for >5s CUDA stream blocking, add dashboard tile for compaction events, and update runbook to include immediate mitigation steps. Customer notified and opted into canary.
payload.summary: SSE streaming silent pause (~25-40s) during GPU memory compaction on Dedicated worker causing mid-generation stall

payload.description:
Issue summary
Customer reports a regression in Hosted Chat streaming latency (TTFT and p95) when their traffic mix shifts toward long-context prompts. Symptoms match head-of-line blocking in mixed prompt-length workloads (long prefill dominating batch selection), causing short chat requests to wait behind long-prefill work.

Impact
- User-visible TTFT regression for short prompts during periods of long-context load.
- Increased p95 for end-to-end latency on streaming chat.
- Customer has a latency SLO for interactive chat; current behavior is impacting production rollouts.

Customer context
- Company: Northpeak AI (enterprise)
- Workload: chat assistant with periodic long-context retrieval (8k–32k context) mixed with short conversational turns.
- Client uses streaming responses and measures TTFT as time until first token chunk.

Environment
- Hosted API, prod, region: us-east
- Models reported: redwood/llama-3-70b-instruct (primary), redwood/qwen2.5-72b-instruct (fallback)
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (stream=true)

Observed behavior (customer-reported)

Additional notes:
- During long-context bursts: TTFT p95 rises to ~2.5–3.8s; end-to-end p95 rises disproportionately
- Customer notes this correlates strongly with an increase in long-context requests; overall QPS stays roughly constant.
Internal observations (initial)
- Our us-east pool shows increased prefill time-in-queue coincident with long-context traffic spikes.
- Tail amplification appears driven by queueing/scheduler effects rather than a single-model regression.
Reproduction steps (customer)
1) Start N=40 concurrent streaming chat sessions (short prompts, 50–150 input tokens).
2) Add a background load of N=8 concurrent long-context sessions (8k–16k input tokens; same model).
3) Keep max_output_tokens constant (e.g., 256–512) across both classes.
4) Observe TTFT distribution for short prompts.
Reproduction steps (Redwood suggested harness)
- Use benchmark-lab “mixed” scenario with 80/20 short/long mix and long spike (see benchmark-lab PR-903 scenarios).
- Compare baseline scheduler vs short/long-aware two-queue scheduler prototype.
Grafana / dashboards (internal)
- Hosted API latency overview (us-east): https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/hosted-api-latency/overview?var-region=us-east
- Streaming TTFT percentiles: https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/hosted-api-streaming/ttft?var-region=us-east
- Runtime queueing + batch metrics: https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/runtime-batching/queue-and-batch?var-region=us-east
- (If enabled) Scheduler class metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/scheduler-class/metrics?var-region=us-east
Initial hypotheses
- Mixed prompt-length workload causing head-of-line blocking: long prefill batches dominate GPU iteration selection, delaying short prompt prefill/first token.
- Continuous batching heuristics overweighting backlog tokens, effectively biasing toward long requests under bursty long-context traffic.
- Potential kernel selection instability when mixing sequence lengths (less likely primary driver for TTFT, but noted in earlier prototype work).
Requested customer artifacts
- Request IDs for 10–20 slow TTFT examples during a long-context burst
- Their long-context prompt length distribution (approx buckets are fine)
- Confirmation of any client-side retry/timeouts (to rule out reconnect effects)
Recommendation / next steps (internal)
- Validate with mixed-workload scheduler prototype behind feature flag in staging, then limited us-east canary per SRE guardrails.
- Ensure per-class scheduler metrics are enabled for the canary pool (queue depth/time-in-queue by class, starvation counters).
- If confirmed, provide customer a mitigation path:
  - Short-term: route long-context traffic to a separate pool/model variant if available (Dedicated-like isolation behavior in Hosted is limited, but we can apply internal routing policy for their org as a stopgap).
  - Medium-term: enable the short/long scheduling policy once canary passes and metrics are stable.
Owner notes
- Tracking under mixed-workload scheduler initiative; aligns with runtime prototype work currently staged for canary validation.
2025-12-02 (Rafael Mendes - Support): Created from customer escalation. Customer reports TTFT p95 jumping from <1s to ~3s when they run long-context evals in parallel. They provided a chart screenshot; requesting request IDs + timestamps. Looping in runtime + SRE.
2025-12-02 (Aisha Bello - SRE): Confirmed us-east had a TTFT p95 increase during the same window. No broad 5xx increase. Suspect queueing/scheduler effects. Please provide 10–20 request IDs and we can correlate to runtime traces.
2025-12-03 (Julian Moore - Serving Runtime): Looking at traces: prefill queue time spikes during long-context traffic. This matches the mixed-workload head-of-line blocking we’ve been prototyping a fix for (short/long class-based scheduling). We should test the two-queue policy in staging and compare TTFT p95 for short class.
2025-12-03 (Customer - Northpeak AI via Support): We can reproduce reliably with 40 short sessions + 8 long sessions. Long prompts are typically 10k–14k input tokens; shorts are ~80 tokens. We can send request IDs for 15 slow TTFT samples (attached in email thread).
2025-12-04 (Sean Gallagher - SRE sponsor): If we enable the scheduler prototype in a canary pool, must follow hosted-api tail latency guardrails. Please ensure rollback trigger is set (TTFT p95 +30% sustained 10m, or error budget burn increase). Also confirm starvation prevention is active for long class.
2025-12-05 (Julian Moore - Serving Runtime): Action items: (1) run mixed 80/20 and long-spike scenarios in perf-canary for runtime-1.18 candidate; (2) confirm new per-class metrics are present; (3) propose initial knobs (classification threshold, token budgets, aging) for us-east canary. Will update ticket with benchmark deltas before requesting canary approval.
Pending. Next checkpoint: staged benchmark results + SRE sign-off to run limited us-east canary with short/long scheduler prototype enabled for Northpeak AI traffic (or a representative pool).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer ScribeAI reports sudden increase in end-to-end request latency (p95/p99) for short chat completions after a recent rollout of a validation change in the function-proxy. Impact: Customer-facing streaming sessions experience long tails and periodic 10s request timeouts. This has escalated to degraded UX for interactive flows.

Observed behavior: During short prompts (<= 64 tokens) we observe p99 latency rising from ~220ms to ~2.1s and occasional 10s timeouts. Traces show an extra synchronous RPC from function-proxy to the schema-validator service during the tool/function call orchestration. The RPC performs a schema/contract validation and an indirect K/V metadata lookup which adds blocking I/O on the request path.

Expected behavior: Schema validation should be async or performed off the hot path (prefetch/validate-on-register) so that per-request latency remains bounded. The function-proxy should not synchronously wait on an external cache miss that triggers DNS and K/V backend calls for every invocation.

Immediate impact: Affected sessions are timing out at the client (10s) and failing fast for interactive users. Customer reports a 12% drop in completed calls and is at risk of pausing dedicated traffic if not remediated.

Temporary workaround: Rolled back function-proxy change on the customer-dedicated cluster to the previous tag which removed the synchronous validation hop. Engineering mitigation applied at 2026-03-13T18:40Z. Longer-term mitigations in progress.
1) Send short streaming chat request to Redwood API with tool invocation metadata enabled
2) Observe trace in X-Ray/Tracing showing synchronous function-proxy -> schema-validator RPC prior to serving-runtime invocation
3) Reproduce p99 spike and intermittent 10s timeout on dedicated customer cluster under light concurrent load (5-20 rps)
4) Toggle schema validation feature flag in function-proxy to confirm regression appearance/disappearance
[2026-03-13T17:12:08Z] function-proxy request_id=abc123 event='validation_rpc_start' target=schema-validator node=fp-03
[2026-03-13T17:12:09Z] schema-validator request_id=abc123 event='cache_miss' lookup_key=tool:contract:uuid latency=532ms
[2026-03-13T17:12:19Z] api-gateway request_id=abc123 event='client_timeout' code=504 message='upstream request timed out after 10s'
[2026-03-13T17:12:19Z] serving-runtime request_id=abc123 event='request_cancelled' reason='upstream canceled by API gateway'
Initial hypothesis: recent merge to function-proxy introduced blocking validation path for tool calls; appears in release notes 2026-03-12 (PR #4892).
Trace analysis: majority of tail latency correlates with schema-validator RPCs that surface a K/V metadata lookup causing an extra 300-800ms per request on hits and 400-1200ms on cache misses.
Network evidence: several RPCs show repeated DNS lookup delays (~200ms) when schema-validator falls back to external metadata service; suggests missing local cache or cold cache behavior in dedicated clusters.
Customer impact: Dedicated cluster had lower warming of validation cache due to isolated traffic patterns; host-level cold-starts exaggerated the effect.
Mitigation applied: Rolled back function-proxy change on ScribeAI's dedicated cluster. After rollback observed p99 fall back to baseline within two minutes.
Next steps: implement async validation path, add local LRU cache in function-proxy, introduce circuit-breaker and metric to detect sync validation hot-paths.

Additional notes:
SRE Channel #support (2026-03-13T17:45Z): Noted related incident INT-4112 — rolling restart of schema-validator in us-east coincided with increased DNS latencies. Investigating resolver config.
Engineering (2026-03-13T18:42Z): Rollback applied for ScribeAI; monitoring metrics. Need follow-up EPIC to make validation non-blocking across all clusters.
Partial mitigation: function-proxy rollback applied to customer-dedicated cluster which restored baseline latency. Root cause: synchronous schema validation path that triggers K/V backend and DNS lookups on the hot request path. Follow-up tasks created for non-blocking validation, local caching, and circuit-breaker (linked INT-4220).
Create EPIC: async-tool-validation-architecture
Add local LRU cache to function-proxy (PR #4925)
Add dashboard heatmap for validation RPC latencies
Improve resolver config and warmup on dedicated clusters
payload.summary: Synchronous schema ping from function proxy adds blocking validation hop — p99 end-to-end latency spikes and 10s timeouts for dedicated customer

Issue summary:
Customer (Arcadia Healthtech, enterprise) is onboarding to a high-assurance audit ingestion flow for legal evidence. They require delivered audit batches over mTLS with per-batch signed manifests, an HMAC header scheme for per-event integrity, idempotency tokens for replay protection, and a reversible pseudonymization example using a customer-managed KMS wrapping key.

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete onboarding to their SIEM/legal-evidence pipeline until we provide a sample package and definitive headers/semantics.
- Regulatory deadline: Arcadia needs evidence bundles for an upcoming readiness audit (deadline in 2 weeks).

Environment:
- Production audit export for Arcadia tenant (multi-tenant export pipeline, audit-stream-v2).
- Region: us-east primary, eu-west secondary for cross-border retention.

Request details (what customer needs):
1) A sample signed-manifest JSON schema for batch deliveries: fields, anchored digest algorithm (prefer SHA256), canonicalization rules, per-event offsets, gzip payload checksums, and overall bundle signature format (detached signature acceptable).
2) HMAC header spec to validate individual events when delivered over webhook: header names, canonical string to sign, key rotation guidance, and an example verification snippet.
3) mTLS client-auth configuration: client cert CN conventions, recommended rotation cadence (customer requests monthly), OCSP / CRL guidance, and sample nginx/HAProxy config used by Redwood for webhook endpoints.
4) Replay protection and idempotency semantics: mandatory idempotency-id header semantics, sequence number validation in manifest, and recommended backoff/retry policy for 429/503 responses.
5) Reversible pseudonymization sample: a small NDJSON sample (3 records) showing PII fields tokenized with a reversible tokenization approach using customer-wrapped DEK (AES-GCM) where Redwood wraps DEK with the customer KMS; include mapping metadata and a recommended key-rotation policy.
6) Example signed bundle (gzipped ndjson + manifest + detached signature) as a downloadable artifact and clear instructions for verification.

Deliverables requested by customer:
- Signed-manifest schema and a worked example (JSON).
- HMAC signing/verification spec and code snippet (python or go).
- mTLS config cookbook and cert rotation checklist.
- Three-row reversible-pseudonymized NDJSON sample and the wrapping/unwrap flow documentation.
- Endpoint URL(s) to validate a test push and expected HTTP response codes for acceptance.

2) Customer attempted a test push with an unsigned manifest on 2026-03-11 and received 400 (manifest schema invalid).
3) Customer asked for sample package to validate on their ingest pipeline.

- TLS handshake log excerpt (client side): "alert 40: handshake_failure"
- Server response to unsigned-manifest push: HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request - "manifest.schema: missing bundle_digest"

Compliance constraints called out by customer:
- Audit bundles must be reproducible and verifiable by an external auditor; detached signatures preferred to avoid storing private keys on either side.
- Pseudonymization must be reversible by Arcadia on-demand; Redwood must demonstrate the wrap/unwrap steps without storing the plaintext DEK.

Issue summary:
Customer Lumina Analytics reports a finalized invoice (period ending 2026-02-28) that contains a one-off surcharge line for 128 dedicated GPU-hours (~xlarge) that they did not consume. They are on a reserved dedicated pool and only report normal steady usage.

Impact:

- Reservation ID: resv-88f4aac
- Invoice ID: INV-2026-02-28-LUM-003

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Customer performed a capacity downscale (reduction of target vGPU count) on 2026-02-27 via Console.
2) On 2026-02-27 23:45 UTC, autoscaler rebalanced reservations; scheduler assigned orphaned GPU hours to a decommissioned allocation ID that still had an active billing tag.

- Downscale should reduce billed reserved hours for the customer; no orphaned hours should be billed to their cost center.

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 responses during sustained parallel short requests (50-200ms requests) even though average tokens/sec is well below tenant quota. They suspect a 'burst window' or delta-rate policy interaction that punishes short-lived concurrency spikes.

Impact:
- Affects DocuFlow's background indexing workers and webhooks; ~10% of calls are 429-ing intermittently during peak sync windows.
- Customer-facing failures (failed webhook retries) and delayed indexing jobs. No billing anomalies reported.

Environment:
- Prod us-east, self-serve account
- API: /v1/generate (non-streaming)
- Model: redwood-v1-large pinned to v1.3

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Launch 40 short-lived workers (each sends 15 concurrent requests in bursts for 30s)
2) Observe steady average throughput ~300 requests/minute but many 429s in bursts
3) Backoff and retry results in sustained job delays; sometimes 429s appear even when individual request rate per API key looks low in customer's telemetry.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include error_code: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and message: "quota burst window exceeded" in a subset of responses.
- 429s correlate with many short-lived connections (HTTP/1.1) and rapid opener/closer patterns.

Expected behavior:
- Customer expects short bursts to be smoothed by token-bucket burst allowance so long as long-term sustained rate is under tenant limits.

Logs and snippets (customer-provided):
- Request timestamps show clusters of 200-500ms gaps, ~300-600 calls within 1-min windows.
- Example 429 response header excerpt: X-RateLimit-Policy: delta=60s;burst=120;window=30s

Temporary workaround tried by customer:
- Introduced jitter between worker starts (random 0-500ms) reduced 429 rate but did not eliminate them.
- Reduced per-worker concurrency to 5 and improved success rate.

Ask / Questions from customer:
1) Explain semantics of 'burst' vs 'window' vs 'delta' in our rate-limit headers and how short TCP connection lifecycles affect counting.
2) Is there a per-API-key concurrency window or is it strictly token-bucket over time?
3) Are there any per-route heuristics (e.g., small payloads) that cause more aggressive throttling?
4) Recommended configuration for heavy short-request workloads (webhooks / indexing) to avoid 429s while staying within tenant quota.

Investigation notes (initial):
- Reproduced a similar pattern in staging with synthetic workers that mimic connection churn. Observed that our rate-limiter counts 'request attempts' and aligns them to fixed 1s windows for certain heuristics; the burst allowance is distributed per window and can be exhausted quickly by many short-lived connections.
- There's a delta policy intended to prevent 'token carpet-bombing' where many tiny requests bypass smoothing; this appears to trigger here.

Next steps proposed:
- Engineering confirm exact semantics of delta= / burst= / window= headers (SRE/Rate-limiter owner).
- Provide customer guidance: recommended client-side pacing patterns, exponential backoff presets, and per-key concurrency recommendation.
- Investigate offering a per-tenant temporary burst increase or smoother token decay for DocuFlow while they stage a refactor.

Notes on severity: this is causing user-visible retries but not a full outage. Customer requests clearer docs and a specific mitigation plan.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 14:02 - Support Manager Lena Kim: Drafting customer-facing guidance and temporary mitigation options (increase per-key concurrency limits in Dedicated or advise pacing). Will include recommended client backoff settings and jitter patterns.
Staging run produced metrics: burst allowance exhausted within ~7s when 200 short requests align. Token-bucket refill is conservative for self_serve tenants. Rate-limiter owner notes a known tradeoff between strict delta enforcement and fairness. Possible quick wins: 1) advise client jitter and lower per-worker concurrency, 2) one-off tenant burst increase, 3) longer-lived HTTP/2 connections to reduce churn counting. Engineering to confirm feasibility of smoother decay policy and per-tenant overrides.
SRE to validate potential change to refill algorithm (INT-54321)
CS to offer temporary elevated burst allowance pending SRE approval
Docs team to publish a short KB article: 'Designing clients for short-request workloads'
payload.summary: Clarify burst-window vs sustained-rate delta policy causing intermittent 429s for many short parallel requests

payload.description:
Issue summary:
- Customer (CleverAI Labs, dedicated) reported a sustained p50 throughput degradation across their reserved pool (pool-id: reserved-pool-42) during evening commit window. The pattern coincided with many long-lived prefetch/keepalive streams from a small set of customer processes.

Impact:
- P50 increased by ~30% and p95 by ~12% for the customer's batched routes between 18:00-22:30 UTC on 2026-03-13. Latency increases caused timeouts for a small percentage of critical inference requests and triggered failover to a cheaper model variant. No data loss reported.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity: reserved-pool-42 (prod-us-east)
- Models: redwood-compat-v1 and gptj-7b variants
- Autoscaler: predictive window enabled; composite metrics include slot-utilization and heartbeat-rates

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer ramps a mixture of short inference streams and long-lived prefetching streams (persisting >10m).
2) Observe slot occupancy in pool (multiple slots appear held by the long-lived streams even when idle).
3) Autoscaler does not provision in time because heartbeat sampling shows steady but low active throughput, misclassifying idle-prefetchers as active.
4) Incoming burst from short streams experience queueing and p50 increases.

Logs / metrics attached:
- sample scheduler logs:
  [2026-03-13T18:05:12Z] scheduler: slot-assign reserved-pool-42 tenant=cleverai process=proc-12 assigned gpu=gpua-3
  [2026-03-13T18:05:13Z] sidecar-prefetch: keepalive start stream_id=sf-82 duration_est=3600 tenant=cleverai
  [2026-03-13T18:20:02Z] autoscaler: window_eval(pool=reserved-pool-42) observed_slot_util=0.78 predicted_need=0.0
- metric snapshots: p50_routes: baseline 120ms -> 156ms (peak), gpu_utilization averaged 73% but NVLINK-io waits increased; slot_held_count for tenant cleverai jumped from 3 -> 28 in 30m

Additional context:
- This pattern is not a single noisy tenant hog (tenant concurrency is modest) but many staggered long-lived prefetch streams from a handful of processes that never fully release slots.

[2026-03-13 18:45] Anika Patel (Support): Customer filed initial report. Provided request IDs and example timestamps. Escalated to SRE because this impacts reserved throughput and appears capacity-related.
[2026-03-13 19:12] Marcus Liu (SRE): Observed slot_held_count spike. Early hypothesis: sidecar prefetch logic opens persistent streams and doesn't release slot back to pool on idle due to mismatch in idle_timeout config. Reproduced a similar pattern in staging with synthetic prefetchers.
[2026-03-13 20:03] Priya Rao (Runtime Eng): Looked at autoscaler telemetry; predictive model suppressed scale-up because historical duty cycle looked steady. Telemetry gap: we did not account for long-lived streams that hold slots with near-zero CPU but non-zero heartbeat cadence. Filed PR to adjust heartbeats weight (see related PR).
[2026-03-13 21:15] Customer (CleverAI Labs - devops@cleverai.com): We recently deployed a new prefetch worker releasing after 60s, but rolled back to a different replica that keeps it alive. We'll attempt to throttle on our side but need coordination if a runtime change is recommended.
[2026-03-14 09:30] Marcus Liu (SRE): Applied temporary tenant-level throttle (rate-limit long-lived streams) for cleverai tenant; observed p50 drop back toward baseline within 12 minutes. Planning controlled runtime-side mitigation today.
[2026-03-14 12:00] Anika Patel (Support): Customer confirmed improvement; monitoring and will report if regressions return.
Hypothesis 1: Sidecar prefetches hold GPU slot lease while idle. Idle slot detection currently uses CPU-based heuristics which don't trigger for prefetchers that perform infrequent KV cache requests.
Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler's predictive component underweights slot-hold time and over-relies on task-throughput signals; scale-up suppressed during steady prefetch load.
Finding: Slot_held_count correlated strongly with number of active prefetch streams (r=0.86). NVLink IO wait and PCIe latency increased during the spike, indicating contention beyond simple compute load.
Repro: Created staging harness that opened 40 staggered prefetch streams across 5 processes; reproduced p50 sag and autoscaler non-action.
Workaround (applied 2026-03-14 09:25 UTC): Tenant-level throttle limiting concurrent prefetch streams to 6 for CleverAI Labs. This reduced slot_held_count and restored p50 toward baseline.
Short-term fix (deployed 2026-03-14 14:00 UTC): Autoscaler patch merged to incorporate 'slot_held_time' as a weighted signal in predictive model (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/4321). Deployed to canary nodes in prod-us-east.
Runtime change (rolling 2026-03-15): Add explicit idle-release path in sidecar-prefetch when stream bandwidth < 0.5 req/min for > 90s; will gate behind feature flag for dedicated pools.
Follow-ups: 1) Add metric alert for slot_held_count growth per-tenant (SLO guardrail). 2) Runbook update to include prefetch throttling guidance for customers. 3) Post-incident review scheduled with customer and runtime team to define best practices for prefetch design.
Status: Mitigations in prod canary and tenant throttle active; monitoring for regression.
payload.summary: Staggered long-lived prefetch streams causing sustained slot hogging and p50 throughput sag in dedicated pool

Issue Summary
Northpeak Search reached out with questions about the new “Dedicated Burst Usage” line item on their June invoice draft. They believe the burst charges for 2025-06-15 to 2025-06-18 are ~1.6–1.9x higher than expected based on their internal job schedule.

Customer Context
- Customer: Northpeak Search
- Product: Dedicated (Burst enabled)
- Region / hardware: us-east (H100 pool)
- Workload: periodic indexing jobs that intentionally burst for ~30–90 minutes, plus steady baseline serving.

Impact
Billing trust / customer confidence issue. No production outage, but customer requested we pause invoice approval until reconciliation is complete.

What the customer observed
- Invoice draft shows:
  - Dedicated Baseline (as expected)
  - Dedicated Burst Usage (higher than expected)
- Customer believes they ran 3 burst windows; our charges look closer to 5–6 windows.

Initial Hypotheses
1) Retries are being counted as additional burst usage (idempotency / double-counting bug).
2) Console “Burst Usage” view is lagging or using a different aggregation window than billing export.
3) Burst “cooldown / denial” behavior caused extra retries that increased token/GPU-sec usage (but should still be accurately metered).

Requested from customer (to reconcile)
- Approximate timestamps of indexing job bursts (start/end) and request IDs if available.
- Confirmation whether client is retrying on 429 / overload or admission-denied responses, and what retry policy/backoff is configured.

Internal Reconciliation Plan
1) Compare billing export (daily burst usage CSV) vs. Console usage charts for same tenant/time range.
2) Query metering pipeline for tenant_id + request_id aggregation; look for duplicate request_id entries.
3) Cross-check gateway logs for elevated retries and response codes during windows in question.
4) If discrepancy confirmed, coordinate credit/rebill with Finance (Rishi/Laura) and provide a customer-readable explanation.

Current Status
Confirmed discrepancy due to retry-path double-counting for burst metering under specific client retry behavior (see investigation notes). Fix merged and scheduled for backfill + billing adjustment.

Next Steps
- Apply metering fix (already merged) + run backfill job for affected dates.
- Provide reconciled burst usage report to customer with timestamps and methodology.
- Finance to issue invoice adjustment/credit memo as needed.

Owner(s)
- Support / CS: Miguel Santos
- Billing hooks: Cole Summers
- Metering pipeline: Nadia Rahman
- Finance: Rishi Malhotra (analysis), Laura Bennett (approval)

Attachments / Links
- PR: pr-24108-fix-billing-double-counting-on-burst-retries
- Burst usage report export job: pr-24091-add-burst-usage-report-export
- Packaging / metering definition: Dedicated burst option packaging doc
2025-06-19 (Miguel Santos): Customer flagged burst usage line item as higher than expected. They requested reconciliation before approving invoice. Looping in Cole (billing hooks) + Nadia (metering) + Rishi (FP&A).
2025-06-19 (Customer - Northpeak Search): We ran three indexing jobs that should have burst for about ~1 hour each. The invoice draft suggests almost double. Can you confirm what’s included in burst usage and whether retries can inflate it?
2025-06-19 (Cole Summers): Acknowledged. We meter burst usage as incremental usage above baseline capacity allocation (GPU-seconds and token accounting rolled up daily). Retries should not double-count if request IDs are consistent, but we’ll validate in the pipeline. Can you share your retry settings and whether you retry on 429/admission-denied?
2025-06-20 (Miguel Santos): Customer confirms client retries on 429 with exponential backoff; they also had a transient spike in 429s during one of the windows. They can’t easily provide request IDs but provided burst window timestamps: 06/15 ~09:10–10:05 PT, 06/17 ~08:55–09:40 PT, 06/18 ~09:05–10:00 PT.
2025-06-20 (Nadia Rahman): Checked metering aggregation for tenant. Seeing duplicated entries with same upstream correlation key but different internal attempt IDs. Looks consistent with double-counting on retry path when idempotency key not propagated to metering event. Escalating to Cole + Vikram for confirm in gateway->metering event payload.
2025-06-21 (Cole Summers): Confirmed bug: burst metering event increments on each retry attempt when idempotency_key is missing/empty, and the downstream de-dupe is keyed only on (tenant_id, request_id). In some retry cases, request_id changes per attempt (gateway regeneration). Fix in progress: use idempotency_key when present; otherwise derive a stable hash from upstream trace/correlation IDs with safeguards.
2025-06-21 (Rishi Malhotra): From finance side: OK to hold invoice finalization for Northpeak pending a reconciliation report + adjustment. Please provide estimated delta and a customer-facing explanation for approval.
2025-06-22 (Cole Summers): Fix merged: pr-24108-fix-billing-double-counting-on-burst-retries. Includes: (1) idempotency key propagation requirement from gateway, (2) de-dupe improvements, (3) reconciliation check that flags duplicate-attempt spikes. Next: run backfill for 06/15–06/18 and generate corrected usage report export.
2025-06-23 (Miguel Santos): Updated customer that we found a metering bug related to retry attempts and we’re running a backfill to correct the burst usage line item. ETA 24–48 hours for final reconciled numbers and invoice adjustment.
2025-06-24 (Nadia Rahman): Backfill completed for affected dates. Corrected burst usage reduced by 41% for 06/15 and 18% for 06/18; 06/17 unchanged. Exported corrected report to billing bucket and validated against Console usage (now consistent within normal aggregation variance).
2025-06-25 (Laura Bennett): Approved issuing a credit/adjustment for the delta and proceeding with corrected invoice. Please document in the ticket and attach the reconciled report summary for audit trail.
2025-06-26 (Miguel Santos): Sent customer reconciled burst usage summary (daily totals + explanation). Customer confirmed it matches their expectations and approved moving forward. Closing ticket as Resolved.
Root cause was double-counting burst metering on retry attempts when a stable idempotency key was not used; request_id changed per attempt and downstream de-dupe did not catch duplicates. Fix merged (pr-24108), backfill run for affected dates, and Finance approved invoice adjustment/credit for the corrected delta. Provided reconciled burst usage report to customer and clarified retry guidance to avoid unnecessary 429-triggered retries.
Follow-up actions: (1) Add automated detection alert for sudden duplicate-attempt ratio in burst metering events; (2) Update customer docs to recommend idempotency keys and retry-on-denial guidance; (3) Ensure Console and billing exports share the same aggregation window definitions; (4) Post a short note to #support with the symptom pattern and how to spot it quickly in dashboards.

Issue summary:
Customer reports that during long-running streaming sessions, when the client-side SDK rotates a per-request id value mid-stream (they implemented a per-request nonce rotation to try to avoid stale-ack replays), downstream tool invocations are executed twice. The duplicates are visible in AtlasChat's backend logs and cause side effects (duplicate emails/jobs).

Impact:
- Multiple customers experienced duplicate third-party webhook calls and duplicate job enqueues leading to billing spikes and user-visible duplicate actions.
- Reported against a handful of high-throughput chat sessions for AtlasChat (Dedicated cluster, us-east region).
- Severity: customer is blocking rollback of a new feature until duplication root cause is understood.

Environment:
- Customer: AtlasChat Inc. (dedicated)
- SDKs in use: python 1.4.1 (async streaming), go 0.9.x client used in parallel workers
- Deployment: Dedicated pool rtx-a100 (us-east), API gateway w/managed edge proxy in front
- Models: gptj-redwood-13b (primary), open-compat-3.7 (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Start an async streaming session using Python SDK with per-request nonce header X-Req-Id that the customer rotates every ~30s.
2) Server generates a tool call (webhook POST to their system) triggered by a function_call in the streaming transcript.
3) Mid-stream, the client rotates X-Req-Id and continues the stream without reconnecting.
4) Server appears to treat the later frames as a new request and replays the tool invocation, resulting in two webhook posts for a single logical tool call.

Expected behavior:
- Rotating a per-request client nonce mid-stream should not cause duplicated tool invocations. The server should use an idempotency scope tied to the session or to a stable tool-call identifier emitted earlier in the stream.

Actual behavior:
- A second downstream tool invocation is executed after the header rotation point. The second invocation has a different request id in logs but the same function_call payload.

Relevant logs (anonymized excerpts from customer):
- at 2026-03-10T16:22:31Z Serving: func_call id=fc_1 request_id=req-abc123 X-Req-Id=nonce-793
- at 2026-03-10T16:22:59Z Edge: header X-Req-Id rewritten -> nonce-793-rotated
- at 2026-03-10T16:23:01Z Serving: func_call id=fc_1 request_id=req-def456 X-Req-Id=nonce-793-rotated
- atlas backend: webhook POST /enqueue job_id=job-998 duplicate_of=job-997

Additional notes from customer:
- They call out they are using a per-request-id rotation as a mitigation for a separate session-staleness problem and did not expect that to change idempotency semantics.
- When they pin X-Req-Id for the life of the streaming session duplicates disappear.
Initial triage (2026-03-11):
- Replicated with internal harness using Python SDK v1.4.1: rotating header mid-stream triggers a second tool invocation.
- Hypothesis: idempotency scope is currently derived from a combination of (session_token, X-Req-Id) in the API gateway layer. When X-Req-Id changes, the gateway normalizes headers and the request is routed to a different backend connection resulting in re-evaluation and re-emission of the pending function_call.
- Edge proxy (managed) rewrite observed: long nonces that included a colon were truncated; some LB rules added suffix "-rotated" to preserve uniqueness. This causes the edge to emit a distinct header value to downstream which then increments the request fingerprint.
- Serving runtime: function_call dedup currently keyed by (session_id, request_fingerprint). request_fingerprint built from headers + frame counter. Rotating the header changes fingerprint -> treated as new invocation.
- Also confirmed that if the SDK instead sends a stable per-session id in the additional header X-Session-Id and rotates X-Req-Id, server still deduplicates by X-Session-Id if present. This suggests acceptability of a per-session stable id fallback.

Supporting artifacts:
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C_SUPPORT/p1620xxxxx (internal)
- Related PR with kernel change (investigation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/874
- Repro harness: https://git.company.internal/atlaschat/repro-stream-rotate
Workaround provided 2026-03-12:
- Instructed AtlasChat to set X-Session-Id (stable for session) in addition to their rotating X-Req-Id. This prevents duplication immediately.
- Customer implemented the workaround and confirmed no further duplicates in their next 24h run.

Planned fixes and rollout:
- Edge config: infra will disable the header suffix rewrite for X-Req-Id on dedicated pools (scheduled 2026-03-14 maintenance window).
- SDK change: patch queued to add convenience option `session_id` for streaming clients and to document that per-request id rotation can change idempotency unless a stable session id is supplied. Target SDK release: python 1.4.2 (2026-03-18), go 0.9.3 (2026-03-18).
- Server change: design doc for server-assigned tool_call_id submitted and under review (PR link in related_github_prs). Implementation planned Q2 2026.

Follow-ups:
- Add telemetry to detect header-value changes mid-stream and emit counts to SLO dashboard.
- Update public docs with recommended patterns for streaming idempotency.
payload.summary: Duplicate downstream tool executions when SDK rotates per-request id mid-stream

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports inconsistent rerank results and spikes in p95 latency when calling the embeddings endpoint followed by rerank, observed only on dedicated tenancy in us-east and intermittently in eu-west. Impact: Search results reorderings and tail latency spikes causing visible UX regressions for AsteriaHealth users. Environment: Dedicated tenancy, heavy concurrent mix of 1-32 item embed batches; requests originate from two client SDK versions (1.4.0 and 1.5.2) using multi-part embedding upload.

Observed:
- Intermittent rerank top-k order changes (non-deterministic) across otherwise identical payloads.
- Rerank p95 increases from ~200ms to 1.6s during bursts.
- Traces show repeated retransmits and occasional fallback to CPU quant path during affected windows.

Expected: Deterministic top-k ordering for identical inputs and stable p95 latency under normal load.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use AsteriaHealth test keys against embeddings endpoint in us-east with mixed-size batches (client SDK 1.5.2).
2) Send 400 concurrent requests with multipart payloads containing metadata header X-Client-Embed-Order set to "client" or omitted randomly.
3) Immediately call rerank endpoint with the returned embedding IDs.
4) Observe ordering variance across repeated runs and p95 latency on rerank.

Relevant logs/traces:
- Example trace ids: trace-us-20260310-5f2a, trace-eu-20260311-9c7b.
- Proxy logs (us-east): "[envoy] rewrite header X-Embed-Order=proxy-inserted for request id=5f2a"
- Embeddings service batching log: "batcher: observed chunk_order mismatch, invoking ordering-heuristic v2"
- Reranker warning: "candidate_alignment: mismatch_count=3, falling back to relaxed-match-mode"

Immediate impact: Customer-facing search relevance regressions and increased cost due to CPU fallbacks.

2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reported non-deterministic rerank ordering after embedding uploads. Asked for request ids and sample payloads. AsteriaHealth provided two trace ids and sample multipart payloads.
2026-03-10 11:03 - SRE (Arjun Patel): Noted spike in p95 for us-east cluster around 09:05. Found a canary Envoy config that rewrites X-Embed-Order header during multipart parsing. Investigating correlation.
2026-03-10 14:22 - Eng (Luis Ortega): I can reproduce locally (using provided sample) when proxy injects header. Batcher's ordering heuristic reorders chunks if header present to 'proxy-inserted' which can flip normalization path selection. Assigned to embeddings-service to harden validation and to proxy team for rollback.
2026-03-11 08:37 - Proxy owner (Sofia Müller): Canary rule was introduced in PR #4789 to standardize client headers for legacy clients, but the rule unintentionally sets X-Embed-Order on chunked uploads. Rolling back now in eu-west and us-east canaries.
2026-03-12 10:01 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer confirmed improvement after rollback in us-east; will monitor eu-west behavior. Providing postmortem link and ETA for embedding-service patch to ensure idempotent ordering at service boundary.
2026-03-12 15:30 - Customer (AsteriaHealth - R. Kline): Thanks — behavior looks stable in our integration tests. Please follow up with permanent fix timeline and any required client-side changes.
Envoy header rewrite introduced on 2026-03-09 in canary (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/4789). Rule unconditionally added X-Embed-Order when content-type is multipart/form-data.
Embeddings service batcher relies on explicit client-provided ordering header to decide whether to preserve client chunk order or to normalize by arrival timestamp. When header is injected by proxy, heuristic selected 'preserve' path which mismatched the actual client chunk sequence for some SDK versions.
Mismatch caused occasional use of quantization CPU fallback path: heuristic toggled normalization that changed embedding dtype/shape assumptions, triggering a conversion path with higher latency and slight vector orientation perturbation leading to rerank top-k variance.
Affected traffic mostly on dedicated hosts during burst windows where proxy canary was active (us-east full rollout partial; eu-west partial). Regression window aligns with proxy rule deployment times and customer reports.
SRE rollback of the Envoy rule reduced incidents in us-east; eu-west rollback in progress. Embeddings-service PR to ignore injected X-Embed-Order and validate sequence checksums prepared (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings-service/pull/233).
Temporary: Rolled back the Envoy header-rewrite rule from canaries in us-east and eu-west (2026-03-11). Confirmed AsteriaHealth's rerank ordering and p95 latency returned to baseline in our integration tests.
Permanent: Merged a fix in embeddings-service to validate chunk sequence checksums and ignore non-signed/injected X-Embed-Order headers (PR #233). Added a proxy integration test to prevent header injection for chunked embed uploads.
Customer communication: Notified AsteriaHealth of rollback and planned fix; provided link to follow-up postmortem and ETA for patch (ETA: 2026-03-15 for full rollout).
Follow-ups: Add canary gating for header-rewrite rules, add unit/integration tests for multipart header handling, update runbook to check for header rewrites during latency regressions.
payload.summary: Embedding header ordering heuristic causing rerank variance and intermittent p95 latency in multi-region bursts

comments: 2026-03-08T15:05:00Z Maya Patel: Thanks for the reproduction bundle — we can reproduce this when we force WS->SSE in staging. Assigning to SRE for deeper analysis.

2026-03-09T09:41:00Z Liam O'Connor: Edge rewrite identified. Proxy is rewriting the Upgrade header and coalescing small body chunks. Repro script attached to ticket. Investigating runtime envelope semantics.

2026-03-10T10:34:00Z Liam O'Connor: Pushed a staging hotfix (serving-runtime PR #3682) that emits a duplicate final-terminal event and preserves resume token as body JSON (not header). Issue summary:
Customer observed truncated outputs when a WebSocket session degraded to SSE behind their corporate firewall. The last paragraph is missing and footnote markers (e.g. [1]) become detached from their references; in some cases the final fenced code block is not closed.

Impact:
- Several Notewise users report lost final paragraphs or missing closing code fences for long streaming generations.
- Affects a small percentage (~0.6%) of streams for this customer; repeats reliably under firewall-induced ws->sse fallback.
- Customer uses Dedicated tier in us-east; high priority because it corrupts generated content for educational materials.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (us-east), customer traffic through corporate edge appliance that strips some upgrade headers.
- Client: Notewise web app using SDK v1.8.2 with automatic websocket->SSE fallback enabled.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Initiate a streaming chat request over WebSocket to redwood endpoint with a long multi-paragraph prompt containing markdown footnotes and a final fenced code block.
2) Simulate their corporate appliance by dropping/rewriting the WebSocket Upgrade header mid-session (their appliance forces downgrade to SSE fallback).
3) Client reconnects using SSE resume semantics. The stream resumes but the final paragraph is missing; footnote references appear earlier and the closing ``` is not emitted.

Logs / traces collected:
- Edge proxy logs show an in-flight 101->200 handshake rewrite at 2026-03-08T14:22:10Z for connection id c3f2a.
- Gateway access logs show SSE fallback triggered and a final control envelope (control: pause) sent by the runtime at 2026-03-08T14:22:11Z. The proxy log shows header X-Stream-Control removed during proxy rewrite.
- Serving runtime trace (trace id trc-9a7b) includes graceful pause event and resume token generation; however resume token seen by client differs by one byte.

Expected behavior:
- When WS->SSE fallback occurs and a runtime-inserted control envelope (pause/end markers or resume metadata) is present, the proxy must preserve the envelope contents or the runtime must attach idempotent terminal markers that survive header/body rewrites. The client should receive closing tokens delimiting the final JSON/markdown output.

Observed behavior:
- Proxy removed/re-wrote the in-band control header and also coalesced the last 1-2 SSE chunks into a single HTTP response chunk; downstream client parsing treated the closing marker as already processed and discarded the trailing textual tokens (final paragraph, closing code fence).

Attachments:
- Minimal reproduction bundle provided by customer (request payload + client logs) attached to ticket.
- Edge/gateway logs and serving trace links included above.

Request from customer:
- Root cause analysis and durable fix so that WS->SSE fallback does not corrupt terminal chunks or detach footnote references.

03/08 - Initial triage by Support (Maya): reproduced locally by simulating header rewrite; observed similar truncation in staging when ALB rewrites upgrade headers.
03/09 - SRE (Liam): correlated edge rewrite with missing X-Stream-Control header; runtime emits 'control:pause' and 'control:resume' envelopes as small SSE meta-chunks. Proxy HTTP/1.1 coalescing combined meta-chunk with final text chunk causing parser to drop delimiting token.
03/09 - Hypothesis: proxy header/body rewrite + chunk coalescing removes idempotency of terminal envelope; resume token off-by-one indicates token trimming on proxy when converting WS frames to SSE events.
03/10 - Added instrumentation to runtime to emit an extra JSON-terminal event with explicit 'terminal_id' field that is double-checked on resume; short-term mitigation patch prepared in serving-runtime PR.
Logs: edge:c3f2a (raw) and trace:trc-9a7b uploaded to incident artifact store (links in related_confluence_pages).

Additional notes:
2026-03-09 13:12 - Customer (Notewise contact - Priya Rao): This is blocking a batch of grading exports today. Any ETA on a hotfix?
Workaround and fix:
1) Short-term mitigation: runtime emit duplicate terminal JSON event (idempotent) in body so that proxies coalescing chunks still carry terminal marker. Deployed to staging (PR referenced) and validated by customer.
2) Long-term fix: update gateway/or edge-proxy docs and runtime to avoid relying on upgrade-only headers for in-band control; switch control frames to a small JSON terminal event appended to stream body that survives WS->SSE translation.
3) Add automated test that simulates header rewrite + chunk coalescing across the gateway and validates terminal integrity across fallbacks.
Rollout notes:
- Staging validation passed 03/10 (Notewise confirmed).
- Target prod rollout: 2026-03-12 (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 12 hours).
- Post-rollout follow-up: monitor "streaming.terminal-mismatch" metric and customer error reports for 72 hours.
Create automated integration test for WS->SSE fallback with proxy rewrite (owner: serving-runtime)
Add metric and alert for terminal-mismatch rate above 0.1% (owner: monitoring)
Document recommended SDK config to prefer body-based resume tokens when operating behind known header-rewriting appliances (owner: SDK team)

Issue summary: During a staged canary cutover for FluxHealth's dedicated tenant, a subset of routed requests started returning responses from the shadow/legacy variant despite the tenant being explicitly model-pinned to redwood-xl-2.7B. Impact: Production traffic experienced mixed-model outputs for ~6% of sessions in us-east, resulting in degraded model quality for customer-facing features and repeated client-side retries. Environment: Dedicated cluster for FluxHealth spanning prod-us-east and prod-eu-west, canary weight applied to 20% of traffic in us-east. Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:02 UTC - canary rollout initiated from Console; 09:07 UTC - first anomalies reported by FluxHealth; 09:10 UTC - increased 5xxs and mixed responses observed; 09:24 UTC - initial triage by Support and SRE. Observed behavior: Requests that included explicit tenant pin metadata still routed to legacy shadow variant intermittently. Edge logs indicate fallback decisions were taken using an older route metadata snapshot that did not include the updated fallback_map and roll-forward policy. This appears correlated with the region-specific metadata propagation window during the canary slice update.
1) On a dedicated tenant with an active model pin (redwood-xl-2.7B), initiate a staged canary slice update that patches route metadata in the control plane (fallback_map change + new canary weight).
2) Simulate traffic from us-east with 20% sampling for the canary cohort and keep session affinity across multiple requests.
3) Observe routing decisions at the edge and check if any requests are routed to the legacy shadow variant despite pin header present.
4) Correlate timestamps with control-plane metadata snapshots and edge-cache TTLs to reproduce the desync window.
2026-03-10T09:07:12Z edge-proxy[ingress] INFO tenant=fluxhealth req_id=abc123 route_select=shadow_fallback reason=metadata_snapshot_mismatch snapshot_id=2026-03-09T23:50:10Z
2026-03-10T09:07:13Z orchestrator WARN tenant=fluxhealth apply_patch=canary-slice-45 status=partial success=true missing_keys=[fallback_map]
2026-03-10T09:09:01Z serving-runtime ERROR tenant=fluxhealth model_mismatch=expected(redwood-xl-2.7B) actual(legacy-shadow-1.3) latency=312ms
Support triaged with SRE and confirmed deviation affects a small cohort in us-east where canary weight was applied.
Edge inspection shows edge cache used a snapshot timestamp older than the control-plane commit for the fallback_map key; metadata push succeeded in control-plane but TTL-based invalidation on edge didn't fire immediately.
Hypothesis 1: Control-plane metadata patch applied in phased manner (region-first), but edge cache invalidation was scoped incorrectly and left a stale fallback map in place for some shards.
Hypothesis 2: Patch ordering: canary weight update committed before fallback_map update in control-plane, creating a temporary state where routing logic falls back to legacy priority list.
Action taken: Forced a metadata sync to the edge for tenant fluxhealth at 09:31 UTC and flushed route metadata caches for affected shards.
Metric check: After cache flush, legacy-variant routing dropped to <0.1% within 3 minutes; client retries returned to expected model outputs.
Mitigation applied: manual metadata re-sync + shard cache flush for FluxHealth at 2026-03-10T09:31Z. Follow-up fix: control-plane patch ordering guard introduced in PR #4221 to ensure fallback_map is committed atomically with rollout weights; edge-proxy PR #1987 adds a robust metadata-change webhook to trigger immediate shard invalidation. Customer notified and monitoring remains active. Postmortem requested and scheduled (link above).

Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external API calls (webhook POSTs) when using Python SDK streaming + function-calling. Behavior occurs after a network interruption causes the client to reconnect and resume a partially delivered streaming response. The resumed session appears to replay the function invocation without the original idempotency token reaching the downstream webhook, resulting in side-effect duplication (duplicate invoices / duplicate task creation).

Impact:
- Customer (SlateCRM Inc.) is observing duplicate third-party webhook side-effects impacting billing and downstream task systems.
- Occurs intermittently on long-running streaming interactions where the client reconnects to resume.
- Business impact: customer flagged as P1 due to operational impact on billing pipeline.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (customer-owned VPC) in us-east region.
- SDK: python-sdk v1.8.7 pinned by the integration.
- Server: streaming-proxy v2.12.
- Webhook consumer is a third-party billing service that relies on a header idempotency-key to dedupe requests.

Desired outcome:
- Prevent duplicated external side-effects on stream resume by ensuring idempotency metadata persists across reconnect/resume flows, or provide a recommended workaround pattern for safe function execution from streaming clients.
1) Create a Python streaming session using python-sdk v1.8.7 and enable function-calling for external webhook invocation.
2) Trigger a function call that results in a webhook POST (payload includes business operation such as invoice.create).
3) During the streaming response, interrupt network (simulate client disconnect) after the function-call frame but before final stream close.
4) Reconnect and resume the stream using the SDK's resume logic.
5) Observe two webhook POSTs at the billing partner: one from the original attempt and a second on resume.

Notes: Customer can reproduce ~30% of the time using a flaky network emulator. Reproduction is faster with larger function payloads and longer stream durations.
[2026-03-09T15:12:03Z] client: stream-disconnect: websocket EOF
[2026-03-09T15:12:06Z] client: reconnect attempt: resume_token=abc123
[2026-03-09T15:12:07Z] proxy: resume accepted, session_id=sess-77
[2026-03-09T15:12:07Z] function-exec: invoked external webhook idempotency-key: <MISSING>
[2026-03-09T15:12:07Z] billing-partner: POST /invoices 200 id=inv_554
[2026-03-09T15:12:07Z] billing-partner: POST /invoices 200 id=inv_555 (duplicate)
Initial support triage: confirmed duplicate webhook receipts from customer's partner logs and corresponding stream resume events in streaming-proxy traces.
Hypothesis: idempotency metadata (header or per-call token) is not being attached to resume frames; resume path reconstructs a function invocation without original metadata, so webhook receives a new request without dedupe key.
Trace inspection: server-side function-call frame created at t=15:11:59 included idempotency-key header in initial POST. On resume, proxy generated a new POST lacking the header—logs show '<MISSING>' where original key should be.
SDK behavior: python-sdk v1.8.7 persists resume_token but does NOT explicitly persist per-function idempotency header across reconnects for streaming sessions (confirmed by SDK team).
Repro rate correlates with network disconnect timing: if the upstream already received and ACKed the function-call, resume should not re-fire; but current resume logic sometimes replays the frame when ACK was lost to client.
Related internal note: streaming-proxy resume flow deserializes pending frames and re-emits them; it relies on frame metadata provided by client during resume. If client omits per-call headers during resume, downstream receives incomplete requests.
Support (Aisha Kapoor) [2026-03-10]: Acknowledged ticket, requested partner logs and full SDK client logs. Asked if customer can reproduce with an isolated webhook stub to confirm duplicate payloads are coming from Redwood path.
Customer (Simon Lee, SlateCRM) [2026-03-10]: Provided partner logs showing duplicate invoice ids and attached client trace from python-sdk. Reproduction steps and flaky network simulator config included.
Eng (Ethan Park) [2026-03-11]: Reproduced locally using network emulator, confirmed resume path can replay function-call without original idempotency header. Filed SDK change to persist per-call idempotency in resume frames (see PR link).
Support (Aisha Kapoor) [2026-03-11]: Provided temporary mitigation guidance to customer: (1) add an application-level idempotency token in the function payload (body) that their webhook consumer can dedupe on, (2) enable server-side confirmation callback pattern if possible, (3) upgrade to upcoming SDK patch when available.
Customer (Simon Lee) [2026-03-12]: Implemented application-level token dedupe and observed no further duplicates in 48h smoke tests. Requested recommendation for permanent fix and timeline.
Eng (Ethan Park) [2026-03-12]: Proposed two fixes: (A) SDK change to persist per-call idempotency headers in resume frames and ensure streaming-proxy replays those headers (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/987), (B) server-side safety: streaming-proxy could reject replay of frames already ACKed by the downstream if it's able to detect progress via ack markers. Plan: land SDK patch first for faster rollout.
Workaround implemented by customer: application-level idempotency token in function payload dedupes at billing partner — successful in smoke tests.
Short-term fix: SDK patch in python-sdk v1.8.8 will persist function-call idempotency header across resume flows (PR #987). Patch scheduled for staged rollout to dedicated customers on 2026-03-18.
Long-term backlog item: enhance streaming-proxy to include explicit ack markers for function-call frames so resume cannot replay already-acknowledged side-effects. Logged as INT-4320 for infra team.
Customer notified of planned SDK rollout and long-term server-side work. Recommend customer to keep application-level dedupe until patch rolled out.
payload.summary: Partial-stream resume replay leads to duplicate external webhook side-effects for Python function-calls

Issue summary:
Customers report SSE streams that appear to terminate silently after a short network path migration (e.g., mobile -> wifi) and, on reconnect, the resumed session contains interleaved partial JSON fragments instead of a clean continuation. Impact: customers see truncated final sentences or corrupted JSON payloads, causing downstream parsers to fail.

Impact:
- Korvo Media (dedicated) observed ~18% of streaming requests during a 3 hour window dropped final paragraph or returned invalid JSON after reconnect.
- Product features that expect structured JSON choices fail to render the final block.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated, customer pool rdx-ded-02 (us-east)
- API: /v1/stream (SSE) with auth token scoped to Korvo account
- Client: Korvo mobile app v2.4.1 using native SSE client with keepalive and automatic reconnect
- Observed during cellular->wifi handoffs and when edge proxy path migration occurs

Steps to reproduce (observed / customer steps):
1) Start SSE streaming request against gpt-redwood-rlf-2.7b with long output (>= 600 tokens).
2) While stream is active, trigger network path change (disable cellular, enable WiFi) or simulate path migration via network emulator that changes source IP.
3) Client reconnects using same session token and attempts resume.
4) Client receives a tail of the previous stream (heartbeat or partial chunk) and the resumed stream includes fragments like '{"choices": [{"text": "...in conclusion"}]}' (truncated) followed by a new fragment from resumed response, producing interleaved JSON tokens.

Logs / Observables:
- Proxy logs (edge-proxy-us-east-3) show a GOAWAY / path-migrate entry followed by a 101 upgrade for a new connection within 200-400ms.
- Serving runtime trace (trace_id=tr-20260310-9982) shows request rung up on worker-7 then a reconnect pinned to worker-12 after path migration. KV cache priming occurs on worker-12 but a stale end-marker from worker-7 is delivered before resume chunks.
- Client-side stacktrace (Korvo) shows JSON decode error: "Unexpected end of JSON input" at resume boundary.

Relevant links:
- Slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05SUPPORT/thread-2026-03-10)
- Incident note (internal): INC-2026-03-10-07
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821

Start a long SSE stream (>600 tokens) to /v1/stream using the customer's dedicated pool
Trigger a client network path migration (cellular -> wifi) while stream is active
Allow the client to reconnect and resume using the same session token
Observe the resumed stream for interleaved partial JSON fragments and final sentence loss

serving-runtime: trace_id=tr-20260310-9982 worker=worker-7 HANDOFF->worker-12 cache_primed=false
client (Korvo mobile): JSONDecodeError at resume boundary: Unexpected end of JSON input
Asha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports 18% failure rate for long streams during mobile handoffs. Attached client logs and example payloads.
Ravi Kapoor (SRE) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally using tc/netem path migration; observed that worker handoff sometimes emits a trailing partial chunk flagged as 'end' before KV cache priming completes on new worker.
Eleni Morris (Serving Eng) 2026-03-11: Hypothesis: resume protocol does not strictly enforce 'end' marker origin; if a stale 'end' is delivered from previous worker and followed by resume chunks, client-side parsers see interleaved JSON. Adding to backlog to add origin tagging to end markers.
Korvo Support Contact (Martin Li) 2026-03-11: We can throttle reconnects for now but need a more reliable fix; this affects our live-captions feature.
03/11: Reproduced with netem delaying 300-500ms between connections; race window appears when handoff time < 600ms.
03/11: Worker handoff path: controller issues a 'handoff' message to new worker and old worker sends final chunks then exits. Final chunk may be buffered by edge proxy and delivered after new worker's resume stream begins.
03/11: KV cache priming on target worker takes ~80-120ms for long context; resume transparent when priming completes before any buffered tail is flushed.
03/12: Edge proxy (envoy) configuration shows connection_coalescing enabled and keepalive probes are set to 10s; observed earlier GOAWAYs during path migration which flush buffered writes.
03/12: Added verbose trace to serving runtime to tag end-markers with origin-worker-id; observed cases where origin id differs between end fragment and subsequent resume chunks.
Workaround (customer-facing): Instructed Korvo to implement a client-side parser tolerant to partial fragments at resume boundaries (ignore trailing incomplete object until a valid end marker is observed). Not ideal but reduces crashes.
Temporary mitigation (platform): Disabled connection_coalescing on edge-proxy-us-east-3 for Korvo's pool to reduce buffered tail delivery. This reduced error rate to ~3% in the next 6h window.
Planned fix: Engineering to implement origin-tagging of terminal markers and require an explicit resume ACK from client before resuming stream content on new worker. PR #4821 adds end-marker worker-id tagging and a short jittered hold-window to ensure cache priming. ETA: 2026-03-20 for internal rollout to dedicated pools.
Follow-ups: Add automated test covering netem path migration scenario and update runbook with 'disable coalescing' mitigation steps. Notify accounts team when fix is deployed to schedule verification with Korvo.

Issue summary: When a user with org-level impersonation (via API key swap) drills down from a dashboard tile into a trace, the returned trace link opens the trace viewer but the trace anchor and tracehook context do not match the original event. Impact: Users see wrong trace context (different span/time) for ~10-15% of drilldowns from saved dashboards across Cartograph Labs org. This breaks incident workflows and increases mean time to debug. Environment: prod (us-east), affected org on enterprise plan using API-key impersonation for automated report generation. Observed since 2026-03-09 after the org started daily scheduled snapshot exports under a new service account. Reproducibility: Intermittent but ~1 in 10 drilldowns reproduce when the dashboard was generated while impersonating a service account that has an API-key rotation policy enabled.
1) Log into Console as org-admin (Cartograph Labs) and enable impersonation via API-key swap for a service account.
2) Trigger a scheduled dashboard snapshot generation while impersonating the service account (snapshot includes a drilldown-enabled tile with tracehook parameter).
3) From the dashboard, click the drilldown link for a row that contains a tracehook anchor parameter.
4) Observe the trace viewer opens but the linked span/time does not match the original tile's timestamp or span id.
5) Repeat for several rows; failure occurs intermittently and correlates with times when the snapshot was produced immediately after an API-key rotation event.
Example tracehook param seen in dashboard link: tracehook=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...; when opened the trace viewer shows anchor_id=span-0x7f9c instead of expected span-0x1a3b. Console service logs around 2026-03-09T04:12:21Z show: [console-service] INFO drilldown-link-gen user=svc-reporting org=cartograph-labs impersonation=enabled original_token_id=ak-rot-20260309 new_token_id=ak-rot-20260309-2 signed_anchor=sha256:abc123; later when resolving tracehook: [trace-resolver] WARN signature-mismatch expected=sha256:abc123 got=sha256:def456; fallback-resolve produced anchor span-0x7f9c.
Initial triage by Support (Aisha): confirmed reproduction with customer while reproducing scheduled snapshot flow.
SRE (Mateo) pulled console-service logs and trace-resolver logs; correlation shows mismatch between signed anchor digest and resolver input when impersonation header present.
Hypothesis: API-key impersonation flow performs an internal token re-signing/rewriting for downstream URLs. When snapshots are generated during or immediately after a key rotation, the link's tracehook token may be re-signed with the wrong org/service account context, leading the resolver to compute a different digest and resolve to the wrong trace anchor.
Verified repro locally by simulating a key rotation during snapshot generation; reproduced anchor mismatch consistently when rotation event occurred within the 30s window.
Checked related components: console link generator (v1.22.0) uses canonicalize(org, user, original_anchor) before signing; impersonation middleware rewrites org header during swap which overwrites canonicalization input incorrectly.
Related PR found that changed signing behavior for impersonation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1824 — this PR added a shortcut that inadvertently used live impersonated-org for re-sign instead of preserving original context.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported increased debugging time; attaching example dashboard and snapshot URL. Asked for reproduction steps and logs.
Mateo Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-11: Confirmed logs show signature mismatch; I can reproduce locally by toggling api-key rotation. Escalating to Console backend owners. Adding related PR that likely introduced regressive behavior.
Jin Park (Console Engineer) 2026-03-12: Reviewed PR 1824; agree this looks like a regression where impersonation path alters canonicalization inputs. Preparing a patch to capture original org/user for signing when generating persisted links. Will run integration test with snapshot generation under rotation.
Cartograph Labs (Customer) 2026-03-12: Thanks for quick triage — business impact is moderate; scheduled executive on-call will use workaround. Please advise ETA for fix and whether we need to re-generate past snapshots.
Mateo Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-13: Hotfix deployed to staging (console v1.23.1-preview). Integration test passed for rotation window. Planning canary to prod tomorrow morning UTC. Will follow up with migration plan for existing snapshots.
Mitigation: Temporary workaround provided to customer — disable automatic API-key rotation for service account used to generate scheduled snapshots and re-generate snapshots after rotation window passes. Fix: Console backend patched to preserve original signing context when generating drilldown links under impersonation. Patch landed in console v1.23.2 and deployed with a gradual canary rollout to prod (started 2026-03-14). Post-deploy migration: background job to re-sign persisted snapshot links for affected orgs queued (job id: JOB-2026-03-14-77). Follow-ups: add unit/integration tests for impersonation+rotation window, add dashboard SLI to detect tracehook signature mismatches, update runbook at linked Confluence page. Customer notified and offered assisted snapshot refresh; waiting on confirmation for migration window.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when sending batched generation requests that include very large context prefixes (200k+ tokens) and high max_tokens (40k+), about 5-15% of requests in the batch terminate with an HTTP 503 or the streaming connection aborts mid-generation. Failures typically happen between 35s-75s after request start and often occur on the finalization step (flush/final chunk).

Impact:
- NovusHealth feeds multi-document patient histories as a single prompt; intermittent generation aborts result in missing critical notes in downstream processing.
- Customer reports increased retry churn and billing variance for partial responses.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity; prod - us-east.
- Requests are client-batched (client sends 8 concurrent requests in a single connection) with keep-alive and streaming responses enabled.
- Observed across two model families (gpt4o-redwood-70b and llama-2-70b-bleeding).

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Build prompt by concatenating ~250k tokens from clinical notes.
2) Call /v1/generate with max_tokens=45000, stream=true.
3) Use client-side batching: 6-10 requests in parallel on the same connection.
4) Observe that some requests return 503 or stream terminates with "upstream reset" while others complete.

Logs (examples):
- gateway: "upstream returned 503: handler timeout after 58.206s for request SUP-88219-customer-call"
- runtime: "evicting KV cache entry due to memory pressure, evicted 3 segments for model gpt4o-redwood-70b, request_id=abc123"
- scheduler: "batch overcommit: requested_budget=52000, allocated=48000 -> delaying finalization"

Additional notes:
- Customer attached request IDs and timestamps to the ticket and allowed SRE access to trace logs.
- Customer states reducing max_tokens to ~10k reduces error rate to <1% but is not acceptable for their workflow.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 09:12 - NovusHealth (Customer): Provided additional payloads and confirmed that temporarily reducing client concurrency is an acceptable short-term mitigation while a patch is developed. Thankful for timeline estimate.
Hypothesis: recent batching heuristic (PR 3421) overestimates safe packing when prefixes are very large. This leads to batch overcommit where combined per-batch token budgets exceed node memory/KV cache thresholds -> triggers eviction during generation finalization -> some streaming connections abort with 503 or upstream reset.
Evidence: reproducer runs with heuristic ON show 10-15% failures; with heuristic OFF failures drop to <1%. Kernel traces show finalizer waiting on KV segments that were concurrently evicted and reloaded, creating stalls and timeouts.
Scheduler logs show 'batch overcommit' entries matching timestamps of customer failures. evict metrics spike during incidents. No evidence of network flakiness at gateway level beyond the 503s issued by upstream runner.
Risk assessment: issue primarily affects large-prefix + high max_tokens + client-side batching. Dedicated customers using smaller max_tokens or single-request patterns unaffected. However, regression was introduced in last 2 weeks and could impact other enterprise customers using large contexts.
Related tickets: SUP-84127 (kv eviction on large prefix), SUP-29541 (context tail latency) — similar symptoms but different root causes identified in earlier triage.
- Ask customer to reduce client-side concurrency (recommended 1-2 concurrent requests) or reduce max_tokens to <= 10k until soft fix deployed.
