Issue summary:
Customer DataHarbor reports periodic waves of 429 throttles across multiple endpoints during daytime ingest windows. They see server-side rate-limit rejections for a sustained 30–90 minute window even though aggregate token usage reported in their console remains under their committed burst and sustained quotas.

Impact:
- Multiple background jobs and webhooks failing with 429s (non-idempotent retries cause downstream duplicates).
- Customer reports increased error rates in their SLA dashboards and two supportable customer incidents.
- Revenue-impacting: delayed batch commits and retry storms.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant on prod-us-east, dedicated GPU pool.
- Jobs originate from a delegated service account (service-account-managed by DataHarbor) that rotates short-lived credentials every ~2 minutes.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Deploy connector that rotates delegated SA keys and launches 8 parallel upload workers.
2) Each worker uses temporary credentials to start streaming SSE connections + periodic background flush jobs.
3) Observe console & client errors: 429s appear within 3–5 minutes and persist in waves.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses have X-RateLimit-Reason header: "burst_credit_exhausted" or sometimes missing header (opaque 429).
- Console token usage graphs show transient micro-spikes but not sustained over-billing matching the 429 duration.
- Logs show repeated token bucket refill attempts correlated with many short-lived sessions tied to the delegated SA refresh.

Expected behavior:
- Short-lived credential rotations should not cause tenant burst credits to be depleted repeatedly; system should amortize transient reconnects and keep background probes/healthchecks excluded where configured for dedicated tenants.

Initial diagnostics attached by customer:
- Sample logs (redacted) showing auth refresh timestamps and 429 timestamps.
- Wireshark snippet showing quick TCP teardown/connect cycles.
- Console screenshots of token bucket and per-route counters.

Immediate ask from customer:
1) Explanation for why burst credits are consumed faster than console suggests.
2) Temporary mitigation to stop ongoing 429s while we investigate root cause.
3) Permanent recommendation for their delegated-credential rotation pattern.
2026-03-13 10:14 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE for rate-limiter tracing. Asked customer for redacted auth logs and snapshot of console offsets.
2026-03-13 11:03 - SRE (Miguel): Pulled rate-limiter traces for tenant. Seeing high token-accounting churn aligned with short session lifetimes. Starting hypothesis: per-connection preflight & health probes being counted as separate requests due to signed URL / header mismatch during reconnect.
2026-03-13 12:22 - Customer (DataHarbor — Sam Li): We can pause rotation for test; will stand up a test run with 30-minute rotation window in 30 minutes and report back.
2026-03-13 13:05 - SRE (Miguel): Traced an event where ephemeral session tokens are created and not properly deduped at ingress, leading to double-accounting in edge token counters for ~20% of reconnects. Creating follow-up internal ticket INT-485 to validate edge dedupe behavior.
2026-03-14 09:41 - Support (Aisha): Applying temporary mitigation: suggested client change to reuse a single long-lived connection per worker and increase credential TTL to 10 minutes while we push edge fix patch. Customer confirmed immediate error-rate drop in test setup.
2026-03-14 11:02 - SRE (Miguel): We have a patch candidate that deduplicates preflight accounting on reconnect at ingress-proxy; scheduled for canary deploy to us-east edge next 2 hours. Will monitor for reappearance of waves.
Hypothesis 1: Edge ingress treats each auth handshake + preflight as a fresh request for burst accounting when ephemeral keys rotate rapidly; double-counting occurs during an edge LRU session mapping miss.
Hypothesis 2: Client creates ephemeral signed callbacks that trigger immediate short-lived webhooks; these callbacks are counted against token buckets separately from main requests (no consumer tag), so bursts not visible on tenant aggregate charts which only sum route-level counters.
Trace findings: Numerous meter entries with identical client_ip and ~1–2s offsets; suggests reconnect fanout from orchestrator. Correlation with delegated SA rotation events confirmed in customer logs.
Workaround validated: Reusing connection per worker and increasing credential TTL prevented rapid reconnect churn and stopped repeated burst-credit depletion in the test run.
Next steps: Roll canary ingress patch to dedupe preflight accounting and add server-side heuristic to suppress counting of health-check probes for dedicated tenants. Also update docs to recommend credential TTL > 3 minutes when using multiple parallel workers.
Linked internal action: INT-485 created to instrument ingress session-id mapping and add unit tests for reconnect dedupe.
Mitigation in progress: customer applied temporary client-side change (reuse connection + increase TTL) — immediate improvement observed. Ingress dedupe patch scheduled for canary in us-east; post-canary rollout will be communicated. Post-incident runbook to include recommended TTL and orchestration patterns for delegated creds.
Canary deploy dedupe patch to us-east edge and monitor rate-limit events for tenant for 48 hours
Add a refill-accounting dashboard for dedicated tenants that includes per-connection dedupe rate and preflight counts
Document recommended rotation cadence and example code for connection reuse in SDKs (suggest TTL >= 5 minutes for 8+ worker fanout)
Close linked internal ticket INT-485 after tests and rollouts

Issue summary:
Customer LexaHealth reports sudden p99 and throughput regressions in their dedicated GPU pool around 2026-03-10 13:10 UTC. Impact is intermittent but recurring across three 10-minute windows during peak. Affected routes are low-latency chat endpoints pinned to redwood-7B-quantized.

Impact:
- LexaHealth observed 30-45% drop in overall throughput and p99 increasing from ~600ms to 2.3s for short chat streams.
- Consumer-facing degradation for a small set of users; no data exfiltration or error 5xx increase noted.
- Customer is on Dedicated tier and expects capacity SLA.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: reserved-pool-lexa-01 (us-west)
- Serving runtime version: v2.16.1
- Autoscaler policy: predictive-burst-v2 (min=2 GPUs, max=8 GPUs)
- Kernel profile: cuda-optimized-llama-kernels-2025.11

Steps to reproduce / Observed behavior:
1) Traffic pattern: many short chat streams (~100-300 tokens), occasional long context requests.
2) Coincident with throughput drop we observe many short-lived worker subprocesses spawned by the inference-sidecar (child process model loaders for small-batch prefetch) which then linger "zombie-like" holding GPUs for 100-300ms before release.
3) Autoscaler reports normal slot counts but GPU allocation telemetry shows fractional unusable time slices (high nvlink wait and serialize counts).
4) KV-prefetch lease sizes for the customer grew without matching release events; prefetch lease count increased steadily during incident windows.

Logs and metrics (highlights):
- telemetry:slot_utilization: p50=0.62, p95=0.78 during normal, dropped to p50=0.42 during incident windows.
- serving-runtime logs: repeated lines: "spawned child_infer_worker pid=14277 lease_id=lk-89fa hold_ms=182"
- nvlink_wait_ms increased by 3-6x in the same windows.
- autoscaler: no scale-up triggered (pool still below max) but per-GPU effective utilization spiked leaving small unusable gaps.
- kube events: no node restarts or driver crashes.

Initial hypothesis:
- A regression in the prefetch worker lifecycle (introduced in v2.16.1) where background subprocesses start a short prefetch and do not properly release the GPU/lease before exit, causing brief but frequent GPU hold that fragments availability.
- Noisy child-processes from a customer-side helper causing serializing NVLink small transfers.

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- Support instructed LexaHealth to toggle route to a compat model variant (redwood-7B-compat) which showed temporary normalization of p99 (back to ~700ms) — indicates problem correlated with model kernel path.
- SRE provisionally configured a temporary autoscaler aggressor threshold to prefer additional warm GPUs earlier (reduced impact but costlier).
- Killed orphaned sidecar child processes on a subset of GPUs (manual), which restored a pool to baseline for that host.

Next steps / Action items:
- Engineering to reproduce locally with v2.16.1 and the customer's traffic profile (assigned to eng:kernel-team).
- Add enhanced tracing to prefetch worker lifecycle in serving-runtime (PR link above).
- Create a hotfix to ensure prefetch lease is released on unexpected child exit. Target: v2.16.2-canary.
- Postmortem and runbook updates to include detection of fractional GPU hold via nvlink_wait_ms and child process counters.

Requested from customer:
- Share a 2-hour trace of production traffic during the next window (they agreed to DO NOT SHARE PII).
- Allow a canary deployment against 1 GPU node in their dedicated pool night window.

2026-03-10 15:30 - SRE (Jonah McKenna): Observed repeated child_infer_worker spawn patterns; created a short script to list lingering pids and lease ids. No driver/kernel errors. Posting telemetry sample to #support: https://slack.redwood/support/archives/C03ABCD2/p1623456789000100

2026-03-13 03:40 - SRE (Jonah McKenna): Deployed interim autoscaler tweak to Lexa pool to favor prewarm up to 4 GPUs on high burst signals; reduction in p99 but cost spike; monitoring continues.

Workaround applied: temporary autoscaler policy updated and manual reap of orphaned prefetch child processes. Engineering patch in PR will enforce lease cleanup on child exit and add tracing. Canary scheduled. No billing remediation requested yet.

Monitor nvlink_wait_ms and child_infer_worker hold_ms metrics for 48 hours after canary
If canary stabilizes, roll v2.16.2 to the rest of Lexa pool with 10% canary -> 50% -> 100% rollout

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer VertexHealth experienced sudden throughput collapse on their dedicated pool during midday traffic spike with many short chat fanouts. Traffic profile: high fanout of short streams (avg tokens/stream ~40) with a metadata-heavy prefetch pattern.

Impact:
- Customer observed p99 token latency spike from ~120ms to ~2.4s across routed model variants.
- Requests began receiving allocator attach delays (attach_time spikes) and a subset of short streams failed with 504s on the client side.
- Customer reported visible increased costs due to retries and fallback to hosted tier.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id d-pool-vertex-03 (prod-us-west)
- Models: redwood/gpt-13b-v2-quant pinned for customer routes; fallback to 7b quant during capacity fallbacks
- Infra: nvidia-A100 heterogeneous mix; allocator version: v2.8.1; prefetcher: v1.4.0

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Run high fanout load: 60k short streams over 10 minutes with average concurrency ~120 per tenant shard.
2) Enable prefix prefetch with aggressive TTL refresh (~30s) and small kv-cache budget per stream.
3) Observe attach_time and p99 token latency across the pool.

Observed logs / snippets:
- allocator: "attach_delay=1123ms attach_retry=3 slot_wait=87ms reason=allocator-throttle"
- prefetcher: "prefetch_lock_acquired stream_id=xxxx duration=1450ms kv_growth=+40MB"
- runtime kernel: "nvlink_io_wait=high pci_stall=intermittent kernel_queue_depth=low"

Notes: this is not the usual long-lived-ephemeral-snapshotter pattern; noise appears tied to many concurrent short sessions and aggressive prefetch TTLs that are causing transient kv-cache growth and prefetch locks which in turn starve allocator attach bandwidth for new attaches.
2026-03-10 08:42 - Support (Priya): Customer opened after noticing p99 jump at 08:30 UTC. Provided load profile and sample request IDs.
2026-03-10 09:05 - Oncall SRE (Ethan): Replicated a small-scale fanout locally; saw attach_time jitter under synthetic prefetch activity. Escalating to infra team. Linking related allocator PRs.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 02:34 - Support (Priya): Customer confirmed increased client retries and some timeouts. Requested ETA for mitigation; asked for a short-term workaround.
2026-03-11 09:12 - SRE (Ethan): Rolled patch to allocator to increase ephemeral attach concurrency and added soft backpressure on prefetcher TTL refresh for this pool. Monitoring effects.
Hypothesis: aggressive per-stream prefetch TTLs + high fanout produce rapid kv-cache growth and frequent lock acquisition. Prefetcher holds locks while performing NVMe reads/writes to populate KV pagefiles; at peak concurrency this generates IO bursts causing node-level PCIe/NVMe backpressure. Backpressure delays runtime kernel io and allocator attach flows, causing attach_time spikes and effective GPU scarcity.
Telemetry checked:
- allocator attach histogram (pool d-pool-vertex-03): saw 90th->99th percentile jump coincident with prefetcher lock durations >800ms.
- node io wait: elevated during incident window (iostat, blktrace attached in confluence).
- kernel_queue_depth: low while io_wait high -> suggests compute waiting on IO.
Reproduced locally by: synthetic short-stream fanout + enabling prefetch TTL=30s; reproduced attach spikes and nvlink_io_wait.
Temporary mitigations tried:
- Reduced prefetch TTL to 120s across pool (soft config) — decreased lock churn but did not fully eliminate p99 spikes.
- Increased allocator concurrent attaches by +25% (hotfix) — improved attach tail once prefetch flush reduced.
Short-term workaround (applied 2026-03-11):
- Rolled soft-config to VertexHealth pool: prefetch TTL increased to 120s and aggressive refresh disabled.
- Applied allocator hotfix to increase attach concurrency and to throttle prefetcher when node IO exceeds threshold.
Observed result: p99 improved from ~2.4s -> ~350ms; customer retries and timeouts reduced by ~92%.
Long-term action items (tracking):
- Infra: add NVMe IO reservation / QoS for dedicated pools to prevent tenant prefetch IO from impacting attach path (owner: Maya Rodriguez, ETA 2026-04-01).
- Runtime: implement non-blocking prefetch locks or lock-free KV staging to avoid long critical sections (owner: Alejandro Cruz, RFC due 2026-03-20).
- Allocator: enhance attach prioritization to favor short streams under high-fanout scenarios (owner: Ethan Bernstein, PR in review).
- Product: add documentation & console toggle for per-pool prefetch aggressiveness; recommended defaults for dedicated customers with high short-stream fanout.
Follow-up: schedule a post-incident review with VertexHealth and cross-team stakeholders; planned for 2026-03-18.
Transient node-level IO backpressure caused by aggressive per-stream prefetch behavior under high short-stream fanout. Prefetch locks and NVMe activity created IO stalls that delayed allocator attach and runtime IO, producing an apparent GPU scarcity (attach_time spikes) and throughput degradation.
Partial mitigation applied; monitoring continues. Permanent fixes are in roadmap and owners assigned.
2026-03-11 14:05 - Support (Priya) sent interim mitigation steps and advised customer to keep prefetch conservative for short-stream workloads. 2026-03-12 10:00 - Follow-up note: acknowledging partial recovery and sharing roadmap items. Customer asked for notification when NVMe QoS is available.
payload.summary: Unexpected GPU scarcity during high fanout; prefetch locks and allocator throttling

Issue summary:
DataScribe reported a sudden drop in dedicated pool throughput in us-west-2 starting 2026-03-10 14:10 UTC. Customer traffic experienced elevated p50/p95/p99 for batched routes; many short requests were queued and not scheduled to GPUs.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency p99 increased from ~220ms to >2.8s for batched generation routes.
- Throughput dropped ~40% for the reserved pool attached to DataScribe's dedicated capacity.
- Automatic fallback to lower-tier variants triggered repeatedly, causing billing and quality regressions.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: ds-prod-reserved-17 (us-west-2)
- Serving runtime: 2026.02.21-release
- Autoscaler: adaptive-v3
- Affected models: redwood-v1-13b (pinned), redwood-v2-7b (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Run high concurrency burst of many short chatlet streams (avg 120 tokens, 50ms client think-time) pinned to ds-prod-reserved-17.
2) Observe steady-state: throughput falls after ~20 minutes of sustained small-stream traffic; p99 climbs.

Observed behavior:
- Long-lived TCP connection handles and scheduler slots remained reserved even when requests idle between tokens.
- Scheduler shows high "connection_reservoir_in_use" metric approaching pool capacity; batchers unable to form optimal batches because slots appear held by idle connections.
- Autoscaler did not provision additional GPUs due to perceived capacity fullness; eviction signals low.

Expected behavior:
- Idle connections should yield reservoir slots after short idle window so batchers can reassign slots to active requests.

Relevant logs and dashboards:
- Loki query: {job=\"serving-scheduler\",pool=\"ds-prod-reserved-17\"} |~ \"reservoir\"
- Grafana dashboard: /d/pool/ds-prod-reserved-17/throughput-latency
- Trace sample: trace.redwood.ai/trace/8a3f2e7b

Summary of findings:
- Reproduced in staging using a synthetic small-stream flood test (script attached to ticket).
- Scheduler maintains a per-connection reservoir counter; we observed a regression in connection idle timeout policy after release 2026.02.21 where ephemeral streams keep reservoir entries for up to 5 minutes instead of configured 15s.
- Root causes identified: (1) change in connection pool handshake path that delayed idle detection; (2) a bug in reservoir bookkeeping where multi-part streams created duplicate reservations that were not folded on reconnect.
- Evidence: metric 'scheduler.connection_reservoir_occupied' moves to 95% while 'gpu_attach_success' remains nominally green. Autoscaler sees pool as saturated because reservoir occupancy is used as a gating signal.
- Correlation with customer traffic pattern: DataScribe uses many long-lived interactive streams with intermittent typing pauses (~30-90s), which previously yielded slots quickly; regression now keeps them reserved causing slot starvation for batched short requests.

2026-03-10 15:05 - Support (Ava Chen): Acknowledged customer, collected initial traces and asked for traffic sample. Escalated to SRE with high priority.
2026-03-10 15:28 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Started reproducer against staging. Observed reservoir holding behavior. Added temporary alert on scheduler.connection_reservoir_occupied > 80%.
2026-03-10 16:10 - Eng (Priya Kapoor): Confirmed recent handshake change in runtime PR #4821 could affect idle detection; requested runtime logs for connection state transitions.
2026-03-10 18:02 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer accepted a short maintenance window to apply a configuration rollback to restore 15s idle timeout on their pool.
2026-03-11 02:14 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Rolled back the timeout config for ds-prod-reserved-17 as an emergency mitigation — reservoir occupancy fell from 96% to 28% and p99 returned to ~240ms. Noted this is a temporary mitigation.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Eng (Marcela Ruiz): Proposed code fix to fold duplicate reservations and added an integration test for multi-part streams. Patch target: autoscaler v3 + scheduler bookkeeping. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1299.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Support (Ava Chen): Customer report: latency stabilized after mitigation; however they saw a single recurrence during a midnight burst — investigating follow-up automation to prevent regressions.
2026-03-12 14:40 - Eng (Diego Martinez): Hotfix deployed to scheduler that ensures X milliseconds idle threshold is respected and merges duplicate reservoir entries on reconnect. Monitoring shows stable reservoir occupancy across pools.
Mitigation and fix:
- Emergency mitigation: rolled back the idle timeout config for the affected dedicated pool (ds-prod-reserved-17) from 5m -> 15s which immediately freed reservoir slots and restored batching behavior.
- Code fix: merged hotfix to scheduler that (a) enforces idle detection on connection state transitions and (b) merges duplicate reservations for multi-part streams. Patch landed in runtime and autoscaler PRs and shipped to prod on 2026-03-12 14:30 UTC.
- Customer outcome: DataScribe throughput returned to baseline; p99 dropped to pre-incident levels.

Regression introduced in release 2026.02.21 that increased connection idle retention and a separate bug where multi-part streams duplicated reservoir reservations. Together they caused effective slot hoarding in dedicated pools which looked like GPU shortage to the autoscaler, triggering reduced batch formation and throughput collapse.
ENG: Add integration tests for reservoir folding and multi-part-stream lifecycle (owner: Marcela Ruiz).
SRE: Add a safeguard in autoscaler to ignore reservoir occupancy spikes from >50% transient duplicate reservations for 2 minutes before making scaling decisions.
DX: Update runbook for dedicated pools to include connection-reservoir occupancy as a primary triage metric.
Support: Contact DataScribe with RCA and offer a post-incident call (owner: Ava Chen).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Holden Analytics is observing a steady decline in effective throughput for their dedicated pool over a 6-hour window. P50 latency remains acceptable but p99 and queue length spike intermittently. Customer reports that requests either queue for >3s or receive 503 during these periods. Impact affects several high-traffic endpoints using gptx-large-v1.

Impact:
- Customer production jobs (document extraction & chat) seeing ~30-50% drop in completed requests per minute for the pool.
- Increased tail latency (p99 > 4s) and intermittent 503/504s.
- Business impact: customer-facing SLAs degraded for automated workflows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: holden-dedicated-us-east-1 (reserved GPUs, heterogeneous mix: A100+T4 fallback)
- Region: us-east-1
- Time window: 2026-03-10 02:20 - ongoing

1) Send steady stream of medium-length streaming requests (~300-500 tokens) from multiple clients with concurrent streams (20-40).
2) Enable streaming + function-calling on gptx-large-v1.
3) Observe autoscaler behavior during sustained 15-30 minute elevated concurrency windows.
4) Monitor serving-runtime / scheduler metrics and slot allocation logs.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should scale predictably and scheduler should allocate slots without serialization. p99 should stay within SLOs.

Actual behavior:
- Autoscaler attempts to add capacity but allocation requests fail or are delayed. Serving nodes show small CPU/GPU utilization spikes and repeated batcher sidecar logs indicating "pinned_stream_id" retention. Scheduler reports slot fragmentation and repeated short-lived batch creation.

Relevant excerpts from logs/metrics:
- [2026-03-10T02:43:21Z] scheduler: allocate_gpu(pool=holden-dedicated) -> insufficient_free_slots (fragmentation=0.62)
- [2026-03-10T02:43:27Z] sidecar-batcher[gid=17]: pinned_stream_id=stream-3a9b locked_for=920ms
- [2026-03-10T02:44:10Z] runtime: kv-cache-growth tenant=holden key_count=1.4M mem_used=78%
- [2026-03-10T02:44:30Z] autoscaler: scale_request(+2gpus) -> pending allocation, offer_timeout=90s
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/holden-dedicated?orgId=1 (p99 spike series)

Initial triage by Support (Maya) and SRE (Ravi):
- Observed pattern: many short streaming sessions create micro-batches that pin a GPU slot while waiting for downstream function calls. These micro-batches do not pack efficiently into larger batches, causing slot fragmentation.
- KV cache for tenant increased substantially — likely due to many unique conversation keys and long contexts; this increases per-slot memory pressure and makes packability worse.
- Autoscaler issued scale requests but cloud/gpu allocator returned delayed offers because of global fragmentation and a concurrent maintenance window in the region.
- Sidecar-batcher version 1.9.2 has a known heuristic that retains stream affinity for 1s by default; under heavy micro-bursting this became >1s pinned due to downstream latencies.
- No kernel errors or OOMs observed on the GPUs, but slot serialization (short-lived exclusive locks) increased request queuing time.

Correlated evidence:
- Linked SUP-631210 showed similar small-stream fanout symptoms last quarter but had different root cause (eviction preemption).
- Heap and KV cache growth trace: https://logs.redwood.internal/queries?q=tenant:holden+kv_cache+grow

Applied temporary mitigations at 2026-03-10T04:10Z:
- Deployed temporary routing policy: route Holden's highest-throughput routes to a lower-concurrency model variant (gptx-mid-v2) for 30 minutes.
- Restarted sidecar-batcher on 2 affected nodes to clear pinned streams.
- Increased autoscaler aggressiveness flag (scale_cooldown reduced) and requested +2 spare GPUs from cloud (hot-add).
- Customer-side ask: reduce concurrency per client to <=15 concurrent streams until follow-ups are deployed.

Effect: these reduced p99 spikes by ~40% and dropped immediate 503s.

Temporary fix applied (routing + sidecar restarts + scale request). Root-cause hypothesis: interaction of long-tail micro-streaming, sidecar affinity heuristic, and KV-cache growth produced slot fragmentation preventing efficient packing; autoscaler allocation delayed by regional offer constraints.

Planned permanent actions (Engineering):
- Scheduler: implement "micro-batch coalescing" heuristic to defragment slot allocation (ENG-ASA-1720).
- Sidecar-batcher: reduce default affinity window and add adaptive release on downstream stalls (PR linked above).
- Autoscaler: surfaced allocation diagnostics to detect region-level offer starvation earlier and to auto-failover to compatible fallback pools.
- Customer follow-up: create a dedicated tenant-level KV cache caps advisory and add best-practice for streaming concurrency limits in onboarding docs.

Follow-up tickets: INT-46011 (scheduler coalescing work), INT-46012 (sidecar affinity tuning).
payload.summary: Dedicated tenant experiencing steady throughput loss due to background-batcher slot pinning and long-tail micro-batches

- API gateway cluster: apigw-us-east-02 (HTTP/2 enabled)
- Proxy: streaming-proxy-v2 (env=prod)
- Models: rw-v1-chat-8k pinned v2026-03-01

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer establishes long-lived streaming sessions with aggressive client keepalive: client interval 1s, timeout 3s.
2) High concurrency warmup (tenant concurrency climbed from 120 -> 420 over 6 minutes).
3) API gateway begins returning 503/502 for some streaming sessions; upstream serving-runtime logs show connection resets and watcher restarts.

Observed behavior / logs snippet:
- apigw metrics: http2.reset_count spiked +320 in 6m; accept_queue dropped to 40% capacity.
- streaming-proxy logs: repeated "RST_STREAM: PROTOCOL_ERROR (HTTP2_SETTINGS_TIMEOUT)" and "peer closed stream: ENHANCED_CONNECTIVITY_RESET".
- serving-runtime: N lines indicating "watchdog: runtime restart due to OOM (gpu mem fragmented)" and several core dumps during watchdog resets.

Expected behavior:
- Keepalive negotiation should not cause protocol resets. Our proxies and gateways should handle aggressive keepalive from clients without amplifying to upstream restarts.

Initial hypothesis:
1) Aggressive per-connection keepalive combined with HTTP/2 SETTINGS timing differences between apigw and streaming-proxy caused repeated settings re-negotiation and RST_STREAMs.
2) RSTs produced cascaded aborts that left GPU KV cache state inconsistent, leading to increased memory fragmentation and occasional serving-runtime OOMs.
3) Autoscaler / HPA warmup created a short-lived surge in ephemeral workers that amplified accept-queue pressure and threadpool oversubscription on the proxy.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support instructed customer to increase client keepalive interval to 10s (immediate reduction in resets reported).
- Deployed short-lived throttle patch at apigw to cap per-tenant concurrent handshake rate (rollout to apigw-us-east-02 completed 2026-03-13 22:14 UTC).
- SRE triggered a rolling restart of streaming-proxy-v2 instances to clear fragmented socket state (completed by 22:28 UTC).

Current status and impact assessment:
- Error rate reduced to ~0.6% after mitigations; still above baseline.
- Serving-runtime crashes have stopped after proxy restarts but KV cache evictions increased; monitoring collection ongoing.

Next steps / Proposed fixes:
- Engineering to add defensive backoff for HTTP/2 SETTINGS ack/timeouts in streaming-proxy to avoid RST storms (ENG-PR queued).
- Add per-connection keepalive advisory and enforceable soft limits for dedicated tenants in apigw config.
- Follow-up: run memory fragmentation and KV cache durability loadtest with aggressive connection churn to validate fixes.

References:
- Slack: #support-nimbushealth thread https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C045NIMBUS/p1678901234567
- Metrics dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/apigw/streaming-health?orgId=1&var-tenant=nimbushealth

Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden increase in 403s for API requests that require tenant-scoped role bindings after we rolled an edge/ingress modifier update in their private VPC. The requests include an 'x-tenant-roles' header which contains multiple comma-separated role values. After the upgrade, the serving runtime shows the request as authenticated but with no roles attached, leading to authorization rejections.

Impact:
- Multiple Novum Health users across teams are blocked from calling admin-scoped endpoints.
- Affects production traffic in us-east for this private deployment.
- Potentially broad: the customer uses multi-value headers to represent role sets, which is common in our private RBAC integrations.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed ingress) behind Redwood identity proxy
- Cluster: prod-us-east
- Agent/edge version rolled: ingress-modifier v3.7.1 -> v3.8.0 (rolled on 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC)
- Auth components: identity-proxy v2.4.3, rbac-service v1.12.0

1) On a private deployment using multi-value role headers (x-tenant-roles: role-a,role-b,role-c) send a request to an admin API route with a valid access token.
2) Confirm request succeeds pre-upgrade (roles observed in request context).
3) Deploy ingress-modifier v3.8.0 which includes header normalization changes.
4) Re-send request and observe response: 403 and rbac logs show an empty role list for the request.

Relevant snippets from rbact-service and ingress logs:
- rbac-service: INFO authorization denied user=svc:novum-user tenant=novum-prod roles=[] resource=/v1/admin/config decision=deny
- ingress-modifier: DEBUG incoming-header x-tenant-roles='role-a, role-b, role-c' normalized-header x-tenant-roles='role-a'
- identity-proxy: INFO token validated subject=svc:novum-user

Initial hypothesis: header normalization logic in ingress-modifier is folding multi-value headers and keeping only the first token when header length or internal list normalization triggers.
What we checked so far:
- Replayed a production request via a test proxy and observed header mutation at the edge during normalization stage. The original header arriving at ingress was 'role-a, role-b, role-c' but downstream the header value seen by the auth service was 'role-a'.
- Verified identity-proxy and rbac-service logs show authentication succeeded; role parsing happened downstream and shows truncated value.
- Compared old and new ingress-modifier code paths: v3.8.0 introduced a header-sanitizer that splits on commas but then applies an aggressive dedupe and trimming routine which accidentally drops values containing internal whitespace when running under the 'single-valued' compatibility flag.
- Reproduced in staging by toggling the compatibility flag and observing roles restored when flag is disabled.
- Determined this only impacts multi-value headers that have spaces after commas (common from some IDPs) and when the proxy is configured to coalesce headers into a single header entry.

2026-03-10 15:40 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Customer called in reporting regressions for admin API. Attached example requests and response traces. Escalating due to P1 impact.
2026-03-10 16:10 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Captured ingress-modifier version and started a staged repro in our sandbox. Observed header value mutated between edge and auth-service.
2026-03-10 18:25 - Engineering (Li Chen): Confirmed code change in v3.8.0 header sanitizer; added unit test that fails for 'role-a, role-b'. Preparing hotfix branch. Linked PR https://github.com/redwood/ingress-proxy/pull/412
2026-03-11 09:02 - Customer (Novum Health, Emma Ross): Noted outage window for admin workflows yesterday evening. Provided sample traces and timestamped pcap. Asked for ETA on fix.
2026-03-11 12:30 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Notified customer we have a confirmed root cause and a proposed mitigation (rollback or toggle compatibility flag). Providing temporary mitigation steps.
2026-03-12 02:14 - Engineering (Diego Martinez): Deployed hotfix (ingress-modifier v3.8.1) to canary; hotfix preserves whitespace-trimmed values and properly emits multi-value header entries. Running canary tests now.
Mitigation implemented: Engineering released ingress-modifier v3.8.1 which adjusts the header-sanitizer to: 1) split on commas, 2) trim whitespace from each token, 3) preserve all tokens when configured to coalesce headers, and 4) add a feature-flag to enable strict single-value compatibility only when explicitly requested.
Rollout notes:
- Hotfix rolled to customer's us-east private ingress at 2026-03-12 02:40 UTC.
- Post-deploy tests: sample requests from Novum Health now show roles=['role-a','role-b','role-c'] at rbac-service and admin endpoints return 200.
Follow-up actions:
- Engineering to add e2e test in ingress-proxy suite for multi-value role headers with several common IDP whitespace patterns.
- Support to coordinate with Novum Health to monitor for 72 hours, confirm no more 403 regressions.
- Create a KB article documenting the header compatibility flag and recommended IDP normalization practices.
payload.summary: Ingress modifier truncates multi-value tenant-role header during edge upgrade, resulting in missing role bindings and 403s

Issue summary: Customer reports a $5–6 discrepancy between the cost estimate displayed in the Redwood Console for a 24h window and the finalized invoice line for the same window. The customer indicates the traffic was dominated by cache hits (we returned cached completions for repeated prompts).

Impact: SummitRetail is an enterprise customer running high-volume product search augmentation. The variance affects their month-end reconciliation and they have paused autopay pending clarification. Potential customer churn risk if unresolved.

Environment: Production (us-west region), traffic primarily to redwood-open-13b via hosted API with caching enabled at the gateway layer.

Observed numbers: Console estimate (2026-03-08 UTC): $3,421.58. Final invoice line (2026-03-08): $3,426.12. Delta: $4.54 (0.13%). Customer provided a CSV of sample requests showing cache_hit=true for ~72% of requests.
1) Use SummitRetail org key to send 10k repeated prompts that should trigger prefix cache hits.
2) Observe Console estimated spend under Billing -> Cost Explorer for the 24h window.
3) Wait for hourly reconciler to produce the finalized invoice lines (or run billing dry-run for the same window).
4) Compare per-request token rounding and per-invoice line rounding.

Expected: Console estimate and final invoice line should match within rounding error tolerance (<= $1 for this workload).
Actual: Finalized invoice is larger by $4–6 for the window in question.
customer-provided-sample-requests.csv attached in ticket (10 rows sample). Relevant billing reconciler logs: billing/reconciler/us-west/2026-03-08.log lines 1241-1253 show per-request token_charge rounding to 2 decimal places before aggregation. Gateway logs: gateway-usw-01 cache_hit=true header present for 72% of requests.

Snippets:
[reconciler] 2026-03-08T03:12:11Z request_id=abc123 token_units=0.333333 billed_units=0.33
[reconciler] 2026-03-08T03:12:12Z request_id=def456 token_units=0.666667 billed_units=0.67
[gateway] 2026-03-08T03:12:11Z request_id=abc123 cache_hit=true cache_key=sku-lookup-7

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:12 - SummitRetail (Customer): Thanks for the update. We need to understand whether the difference will be corrected on our current invoice or if a credit will be issued. Autopay is on hold until resolved.
Hypothesis: The reconciler's per-request rounding to two decimal places causes rounding-up bias on many small cached responses. Console estimator aggregates raw token fractions across the window and only rounds at currency formatting, producing a slightly lower estimate. Evidence: DB aggregate vs sum(per-request-rounded) shows +$4.54 delta for the window.
Tech details: billing service uses 'per_request_rounding=2' by default for performance reasons. Cache-hit responses produce token fractions <1 which are sensitive to per-request rounding. Tax conversion (USD->EUR) not a factor here (customer in USD).
Next steps: 1) Run aggregator in aggregate-first mode for exact window. 2) Produce provisional credit if recalculated invoice is lower. 3) Implement short-term config toggle to use aggregate-first for orgs flagged as enterprise. 4) Longer-term: change default reconciler behavior to aggregate raw token fractions and round once at final stage to reduce bias.
Workaround applied: BillingENG ran a manual recalculation for SummitRetail's 2026-03-08 window using aggregate-first mode. Recalculated invoice delta: -$4.54 matching Console estimate. A provisional credit of $4.54 was queued and will appear on the next billing cycle. Patch PR created to make aggregate-first mode toggleable; rollout scheduled to prod during low traffic window.
Customer-facing note sent: explanation of rounding and confirmation of credit. Finance notified to apply credit and to confirm autopay resumption is safe.
2026-03-12 17:00 - Aisha Patel to SummitRetail: We investigated and found the difference was caused by per-request rounding on many small cached responses. We have recalculated the window using aggregate-first rounding and queued a $4.54 credit to your account (ref CR-2026-0312-571829). Autopay can be re-enabled at your discretion. We are rolling out a fix to avoid this class of discrepancy in future invoices and will follow up once the feature-flag rollout is complete.

Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in streaming completion failures and long TTFB spikes starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Symptoms are mid-stream stalls followed by 504 Gateway Timeouts from the ALB after ~60s. Problem appears intermittent but reproducible under sustained parallel sessions from the customer's dedicated capacity pool.

Impact:
- Multiple user-facing SDK sessions see incomplete streaming responses (sse/chunked) where the client receives initial bytes then stalls and eventually times out.
- Customer reports a 10-15% increase in failed completions and several production incidents triggered.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (customer-vpc) in us-east-1.
- Inference path: client -> ALB (external) -> API gateway (nginx/proxy) -> serving runtime (GPU pool).
- Client: NeuroFlow mobile SDK + server-side ingest, uses custom instrumentation headers (X-NF-Span) and applies small-chunk flushes every 100-200ms for reduced latency.

Observed behavior / Evidence:
- ALB logs show connections reaching connection_limit and many 504 responses with target response time ~60s.
- Proxy/nginx access logs show lots of connections in CLOSE_WAIT and frequent FIN_WAIT from backend.
- Packet captures from a dedicated test node show many half-closed TCP sessions where the ALB reuses sockets to different backend hosts, and some write()s on sockets returning EPIPE when backend closed.
- Application-side traces show repeated injection of X-NF-Span headers (the SDK is appending span ids on retries) which causes per-request header size to grow across a single long-lived connection when keepalive is reused.
- Serving runtime logs show KV-cache warmup periods coinciding with spike windows; when warmup occurs, per-request streaming is more fragile.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start 200 parallel streaming sessions using NeuroFlow SDK against dedicated endpoint in us-east-1.
2) Each client sends chunked request and flushes small chunks every 100-200ms.
3) Simulate a small client-side retry loop that appends a new X-NF-Span header value on each retry (this mirrors customer instrumentation behavior).
4) Observe initial bytes then mid-stream stalls and eventual 504s on a subset of sessions.

Logs / snippets:
- ALB sample: 2026-03-09T22:07:14Z 504 target/10.0.3.12:443 60000 60023 "GET /v1/streams/..."
- nginx: "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream" (repeated)
- tcpdump: many retransmits and RSTs within connection pools during peak load windows

Hypothesis:
- Repeated header appends (X-NF-Span) combined with HTTP keepalive socket reuse causes the ALB/nginx to see increased header frame sizes and intermittent buffering behavior. Frequent small flushes from clients keep connections busy and prevent timely socket teardown, leading to connection pool saturation at the ALB and proxy. When backend tasks (KV-cache warmup) increase tail latency, ALB marks targets slow and triggers 504s.

Initial mitigation attempted by support:
- Throttled customer's parallel sessions from 200 -> 80 and observed immediate reduction in 504s.
- Advised customer to stop appending instrumentation headers on retries (temporary SDK patch) which eliminated header-growth in test runs.

Next steps (proposed):
- SRE: review ALB connection limit and reuse behavior for this dedicated pool; consider increasing connection pool or reducing keepalive timeout for the pool to avoid sticky growth.
- Infra: add instrumentation for per-connection cumulative header length to detect header-growth in long-lived keepalive sockets.
- Eng (SDK/DevEx): provide guidance to customers to avoid mutating request headers across retries on the same logical session; surface this in best-practices doc and the SDK.
- Product: evaluate whether we should implement server-side header truncation or reject requests that exceed safe header budgets with clearer 4xx errors.

Workaround for customer:
- Patch SDK to not append X-NF-Span across retries and reduce parallelism to <=100 while we investigate.
- Enable an intermediate proxy config that forces shorter keepalive for this pool (reduces probability of header accumulation).

Status and timeline:
- 2026-03-10 04:30 UTC: Incident triaged and assigned to SRE/infra.
- 2026-03-10 08:00 UTC: Temporary customer throttling reduced error rate.
- 2026-03-12 14:10 UTC: SRE confirmed connection pool exhaustion pattern and reproducible header-growth during long-lived connections. Further infra changes scheduled (see linked PR).
Start 200 parallel streaming sessions against dedicated endpoint
Use SDK that flushes small chunks every 100-200ms
Have client retry logic append a new X-NF-Span header on each retry
Monitor ALB and nginx logs for 504s and connection_limit events
ALB: 2026-03-09T22:07:14Z 504 target/10.0.3.12:443 60000 60023 GET /v1/streams/
nginx: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
tcpdump: repeated RSTs and retransmits during peak windows
Cumulative header growth from repeated instrumentation + frequent small-chunk flushes keeps keepalive sockets active and causes ALB/proxy connection pool saturation; when backend latency increases (KV warmup) the combination pushes targets over ALB thresholds resulting in 504s.
Throttle parallel sessions to <=100 and deploy SDK patch to stop appending instrumentation headers on retries; set pool keepalive shorter as short-term mitigation.

2026-03-10 07:45 - SRE (Ethan Park): Reproduced locally with load harness; confirmed many CLOSE_WAIT sockets and ALB connection_limit logs.
2026-03-10 09:10 - Customer (NeuroFlow - J. Patel): Applied recommended throttling and saw error rate drop ~80%. Will hold on further changes until we hear back on infra plan.
2026-03-11 16:30 - Infra (Lina Rodriguez): Opened PR to add per-connection header-length metric and to lower keepalive for the affected pool (PR linked).
2026-03-12 13:55 - SRE (Ethan Park): Confirmed reproducible header-growth when keepalive reused; scheduled change to increase ALB capacity and to add connection metrics in staging first.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer Queryly reports production-quality and latency regressions after a recent client SDK change that projects embeddings with PCA before upload.

Impact:
- Rerank responses are returning fewer relevant items (top-k quality drop) for ~8% of requests.
- Tail latency for rerank API increased from p95 240ms -> p95 820ms and p99 spikes to 6s for affected traffic.
- Some requests hit CPU fallback paths and Faiss shard imbalance is observed.

Environment:
- Queryly dedicated environment running in us-east on Redwood Dedicated (v2026-02-15).
- Client-side SDK version: queryly/sdk-js@v2.4.1 (added optional PCA projection flag).
- Server expects 1024-d fp16 embeddings ingest, reranker index built on 1024-d vectors.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send batch of documents through Queryly's client with PCA projection enabled (1024->256) and tags: provenance=client-proj.
2) Call /v1/rerank with those query embeddings and request top_k=10.
3) Observe response count, scores distribution, and timing metrics.

Observed behavior:
- Requests that include client-projected embeddings return fewer hits or degenerate score distributions (many ties, many near-zero similarities).
- Rerank service logs show increased shard load on a subset of FAISS workers and repeated CPU fallbacks: "fallback_to_cpu=true, kv_cache_miss=true, shard_load=high"
- Ingest pipeline does not currently validate dimensionality header strictly and accepts 256-d vectors, storing them in a 1024-d index with zero-padding which changes distance distribution.

Expected behavior:
- Either the platform should reject mismatched-dimensional embeddings with a clear error OR automatically detect projection and route to a compatible index/compatibility path. Reranker scoring should remain stable and tail latency should not increase due to shard imbalance.

Logs & traces (excerpts):
- reranker-2026-03-10T15:42:11Z [warn] shard=faiss-17 load=0.92 fallback_to_cpu=true process_time_ms=4820 topk_returned=4
- ingest-2026-03-10T15:41:58Z [info] Accepting embedding payload: dims=256 header:client-proj=true request_id=qly-req-9b2a

Hypothesis:
1) Client-side PCA reduces effective dimensionality and alters vector norm distribution; zero-padding into the 1024-d index causes many vectors to lie near the origin in high dimensions, collapsing similarity signals and causing the ANN search to return fewer good candidates.
2) The cluster rebalances shards to satisfy the anomalous nearest-neighbor distributions, which leads to higher load on specific FAISS workers and triggers CPU fallbacks for scoring and KV-cache misses, causing the observed tail latency.

Immediate customer impact and request:
- Queryly has a small percent of traffic flagged by feature flag rollout; they want a hotfix to avoid quality regressions while they revert the client change. They also ask for guidance on safe embedding pre-processing.

Requested action:
- Block client-projected embeddings from being accepted into the production rerank index (short-term) OR auto-route projected embeddings to a separate compatibility index.
- Provide a short runbook for customers about embedding pre-processing compatibility and how to detect projection mismatch from server side metrics.

2026-03-10 16:05 - Support: Received initial report from Queryly (A. Morgan). Captured request ids and asked for sample payloads and SDK config. Assigned to Marco Diaz.
2026-03-10 17:12 - Customer: Uploaded sample payloads and confirmed SDK flag pcaProjection=true. Not rolling back yet due to staged rollout. Provided sample request qly-req-9b2a.
2026-03-11 09:20 - Eng (Marco Diaz): Reproduced locally with provided samples. Confirmed server accepted 256-d vectors into 1024-d index without rejection. Observed Faiss shard hot-spots and CPU scoring fallback triggering. Attaching trace ids in GH PR.
2026-03-11 13:45 - Eng (Marco Diaz): Proposed mitigation - reject embeddings where dims != index_dims with HTTP 422 and descriptive error. Quick patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4892
2026-03-12 08:30 - Support: Notified Queryly of temporary mitigation (feature flag to reject mismatched dims in prod) and provided guidance to roll back PCA on their SDK while we deploy the fix.
2026-03-12 12:15 - Customer: Rolling back PCA flag for 90% of traffic; requests immediate monitoring during canary.
Checked ingest pipeline schema validation; embedding dimension header is optional and currently not enforced for back-compatibility. This allowed client-projected vectors to be accepted.
Benchmarked ANN recall for zero-padded 256->1024 embeddings vs native 1024-d: recall@10 dropped from 0.87 to 0.34 in local reproduction.

Long-term: Add server-side detection and an adaptive compatibility index route. Merge PR #4892 and deploy validation patch to prod (eng)
Create a public support doc on embedding pre-processing recommendations (docs)

Schedule follow-up call with Queryly for 2026-03-14 to validate recovery and discuss dedicated compatibility index (CS)
Postmortem to be created if similar incidents exceed threshold in next 30 days (SRE)

Proxima Bank is requesting a temporary increase to their burst allowance on the enterprise-protected chat route (/v1/chat/completions) in eu-west. They report predictable short spikes at market open (08:55–09:10 local) where they see elevated 429s despite overall sustained RPS being within their contracted baseline.

Customer request
- Increase burst capacity (token bucket burst) for /v1/chat/completions in eu-west.
- Keep sustained rate unchanged (they are not asking for a permanent throughput increase).
- They want the change to apply only to their tenant + route group (no broader tier default changes).

Impact observed (customer)
- During spikes, client sees 429 responses with reason=quota_exceeded and occasionally reason=overload_admission when the region is under pressure.
- Primary business impact is delayed responses for end-user chat assistant at market open; they can tolerate some throttling but want fewer hard 429s during the first 10–15 minutes.

Environment
- Hosted API (enterprise tier)
- Region: eu-west
- Route: /v1/chat/completions
- Model: rw-chat-large (pinned)
- Client uses streaming; retries are currently immediate (no jitter) per their current implementation.

Qualification notes (Support/CS)
- Customer is enterprise with explicit latency/availability SLO expectations.
- Pattern appears bursty and time-bounded; sustained usage is stable.
- Customer can implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter, but wants Redwood-side burst adjustment as primary mitigation.

Risk assessment (internal)
- Increasing burst allowance can shift pressure onto shared enterprise GPU pools during localized demand spikes.
- Must avoid degrading other protected enterprise tenants on the same route group.
- Exception must be scoped (tenant + route + region), time-boxed, and monitored.
- Must keep decision auditable and reversible (feature-flag/config driven; clear rollback criteria).

Requested outcome

Attachments/References

Issue summary:
Customers using the console's trace-to-dashboard links intermittently see 'Trace not found' when opening spans from dashboard panels. The problem is concentrated for requests routed through our new edge proxy in front of the api-gateway.

Impact:
- NimbusAI reports 12% of dashboard trace-links failing for recent spikes, causing loss of triage context for SLO alerts.
- Affects live incident troubleshooting and alert jump-to-trace workflows in Console.

Environment:
- Production (us-east) behind edge-proxy v1.4.2 -> api-gateway v3.0.5 -> tracing-ingest cluster.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From Console, open a dashboard panel with a trace-linked timeseries (example org project + route).
2) Click an alert/trace link for a failed request within the panel.
3) In ~10-30% of tries, Console opens the trace page with 'Trace not found' even though the span exists in tracing ingest.

Observed logs / artifacts:
- Console link contains trace_id and span_id query params.
- Tracing ingest shows the span (verified by trace_id) but the Console backend receives a Trace-Context header with trace_id missing or truncated for failing cases.
- Edge-proxy access logs show the same request IDs for success and failure; difference is presence of 'traceparent' and 'tracestate' headers in upstream payloads.
- Reproduced by enabling debug capture on proxy: failing requests have trace headers removed when route uses header-normalization rule 'strip-internal'.

Initial hypothesis: header normalization rule on edge-proxy strips the W3C trace headers for requests routed from some client IP ranges.
What we did:
- Captured pcap and request samples for successful and failed link clicks.
- Verified that Console builds trace lookup requests using headers sent from browser -> proxy -> api-gateway. For failing cases, api-gateway receives no traceparent.
- Confirmed tracing ingest still has the span because the original service injected trace headers when calling the model serving runtime; headers present in service-to-ingest path.
- Reproduced locally by toggling 'strip-internal' header-normalization rule in proxy; when enabled, traceparent is removed for requests marked as 'health-check' or with missing user-agent; our dashboard link clicks sometimes matched that predicate when an A/B experiment inserted a synthetic UA.
Policy risk: header normalization was intended to remove vendor-internal headers but a mis-scoped predicate matched legitimate client requests.

2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Aisha Thompson): Customer reported spikes in 'Trace not found' for dashboard trace-links. Provided early capture and asked for production poke.
2026-03-10 11:48 - SRE (Miguel Hernandez): Reproduced locally with proxy rule. Created staging test to toggle header-normalization. Linked INT-4021 to track proxy rule change request.
2026-03-11 15:03 - Support (Sofia Patel): Notified NimbusAI of partial mitigation: we can temporarily disable header-normalization for the affected edge pool. They requested timeline and risk assessment.
2026-03-12 08:27 - SRE (Miguel Hernandez): Patch PR opened to narrow predicate and add explicit allowlist for traceparent/tracestate: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/912
Temporary mitigation: turned off 'strip-internal' normalization for us-east edge pool at 2026-03-11 18:20 UTC — immediate reduction in failures to <1%.
Permanent fix: PR 912 adjusts predicate logic and adds automated integration test to assert W3C trace headers are never removed for requests containing trace_id query params. Plan: roll to prod after canary on 2026-03-14.
Follow-ups: add dashboard-level healthcheck to surface trace-link missing-rate and create runbook step to check proxy header rules (assigned to networking team).
- Complete PR review and canary deploy (SRE)
- Add console metric alert for trace-link failure ratio > 2% (Observability)
- Document header-normalization rules and exceptions on Confluence (Networking + Support)
2026-03-11 19:05 - Support (Sofia Patel): Notified NimbusAI that we have applied a temporary mitigation and are rolling a scoped fix. They acknowledged and requested a short post-mortem once root cause is deployed.

Issue summary: Since 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC NordicFin (enterprise) reported elevated p95/p99 inference latency and intermittent streaming cancellations for chat endpoints. Impact: Customer observed client-side 504s and stalled streaming chunks; tail latency increased from baseline p99 ~800ms to >6s for some requests. Scope: Reported for customers with EU POP affinity but observed traces showing sudden handoffs to US POPs during request lifetime. Environment: prod eu-west. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use customer's API key and call /v1/chat with streaming=true from eu-west; 2) Issue a long multi-turn prompt (~600 tokens); 3) Observe first chunks arrive then long pause (3-10s) before resume or cancellation. Observed behavior: - Traces show initial connection to eu-west-edge-03, after 1-2 tokens traffic is forwarded to us-east-edge-01 (TTL ~20s) - TCP connection is reused at proxy layer without full reconnect leading to head-of-line blocking on the forwarding path - Kernel tcp retransmit counters spike on proxy host. Logs: "proxy=eu-west-edge-03 forward=us-east-edge-01 route_cache=stale pop_affinity_cache_age=128s conn_reuse=1". Metrics: - p50 unchanged, p95 up 300-900ms, p99 up to 6-8s for affected time windows - 504s correlated with abrupt route handover windows - Flow logs (vpc-flow) show small bursts of inter-region egress during incidents. Initial hypothesis: A stale POP-affinity cache in the regional proxy layer persisted past a routing failover; the proxy tries to preserve connections by reusing upstream sockets, forwarding to a remote POP resulting in extra RTT and occasional packet loss leading to stalls/timeouts. Investigation notes: - SRE captured tcpdump of a reproduced case and saw FIN/ACKs from upstream followed by retransmit backlog - Edge proxy config shows cache TTL misaligned with global route-change TTL (edge TTL = 120s, control-plane route TTL = 30s) - Early mitigation: rolled back cache TTL change on eu-west-edge fleet and enabled strict upstream reconfirmation for active streaming sessions (hotfix rolled at 2026-03-11 05:30 UTC). Current state: Hotfix reduced incidents but not fully resolved; working on a coordinated control-plane cache invalidation mechanism and test coverage for streaming handoff. Next steps: 1) Implement cache invalidation push (infra) and force refresh for all eu-west-edge (sprint P0) 2) Add E2E test that simulates route flapping during active streaming 3) Monitor for 72 hours and coordinate with NordicFin CS to validate. Runbooks/links: incident runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-03-10-27, grafana traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/latency-overview?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:40 - Product: Proposed cache-invalidation push via control-plane. Assigned infra ticket INT-4482 to deliver change.
2026-03-12 11:02 - Support (Aisha): Sent workaround details to customer; requested validation and monitoring confirmation.
Mitigation applied: temporary rollback of cache TTL and enabled upstream reconfirmation for active streams. Permanent fix: control-plane cache invalidation and improved test coverage scheduled. Customer monitoring in progress; no customer data exposure detected. Follow-up: infra to deliver forced cache invalidation (INT-4482) and add streaming handoff test (ENG-6345).

Issue summary:
On 2026-03-12 09:14 UTC Nexline Telecom observed repeated truncated streaming responses, duplicate completions, and a sharp increase in token usage that resulted in an invoice exposure. The customer reported timeouts and garbled partial-replies across two regions (us-east, eu-west).

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat flows truncated or duplicated messages for ~42 minutes.
- Token usage spiked by ~7.8x their baseline for the affected services, causing billing exposure and customer escalation.
- Some streaming connections reset mid-response; clients retried without idempotency keys, amplifying completions.

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Hosted + Dedicated fallback routing for Nexline enterprise pool.
- Regions: us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (production).
- Models: gptj-xxl-quantized-v2 (preferred on dedicated), gptj-xxl-legacy (hosted fallback).

Timeline (UTC):
- 09:13: first alerts: increased 5xx rate and streaming disconnects on dedicated pool.
- 09:14: Nexline traffic routed to hosted fallback policy due to autoscaler marking dedicated pool as underprovisioned.
- 09:15–09:40: numerous client retries observed; streaming resets and duplicate completions recorded in telemetry.
- 09:42: Support opened major incident; SRE rollback plan prepared.
- 09:48: Autoscaler policy reverted and routing fix deployed; streaming stability returned by 09:56.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. Create mixed-quantized and non-quantized model variants in a dedicated pool.
2. Simulate sustained burst of traffic that triggers autoscaler thresholds.
3. Induce transient kernel-selection latency on quantized variant (test harness commit linked below).
4. Observe fallback routing to hosted variant and repeated client retries without idempotency keys.

Observed logs / key signals:
- serving-runtime logs: repeated "No available node in pool -> triggering fallback" messages with 200ms timeouts.
- autoscaler metrics: temporary mis-evaluation of GPU availability due to quantized kernel probe timeouts (spike in probe latency to ~1.2s).
- routing traces: requests dropped idempotency headers during path rewrite to hosted endpoints.
- billing telemetry: per-tenant token counter jumped by 680% for affected endpoints.

Customer impact and communication:
- Nexline reported production customer-visible defects and opened an urgent escalation with their CTO.
- Support provided interim mitigation guidance and hourly updates until remediation.

Next steps captured in ticket: see post_incident_actions and resolution fields.

Initial hypothesis: autoscaler over-evaluated pool pressure due to probe latency on quantized kernels.
Found mismatch: routing rewrite strippped X-Idempotency-Key header when routing to hosted fallback (routing proxy v2.9.1).
Telemetry shows repeated retries from client SDKs without idempotency header, causing duplicate completions on the hosted variant.
Commit 3a7f9b2 in autoscaler introduced a probe timeout default change (from 100ms -> 500ms) that made quantized kernels appear unhealthy under short-lived jitter.
Root cause: combined effect of autoscaler probe timeout change + routing proxy rewrite bug + client SDKs retrying without idempotency keys.
Reproduction validated in staging by toggling probe timeout and simulating jitter; duplicate completion observed when header stripping present.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 14:20 UTC - Product (Amelia Park): 'Schedule follow-up with Nexline next week to review RFC for safer fallback semantics and stronger SLA for dedicated pools.'
Applied immediate mitigations: rolled back autoscaler probe timeout change, deployed routing patch to preserve idempotency headers, and updated client SDK guidance to set X-Idempotency-Key on retries. Issued provisional billing credit of $18,240 to Nexline Telecom. Created follow-up RFC for more conservative fallback thresholds and mandatory header forwarding. Incident declared resolved after stability returned and token ingestion normalized.
Add automated alert for 'probe latency > 300ms' correlated with fallback events.
Modify autoscaler default probe timeout back to 100ms and add gradual backoff logic for quantized kernel probes.
Harden routing proxy to never strip idempotency headers during endpoint rewrite; add unit tests.
Add an integration test simulating mixed quantization pools with burst traffic to detect amplification loops.
Perform billing reconciliation report and finalize customer credit; share result with Nexline and close finance loop.
Update runbook: include explicit checklist for fallback-related customer escalations and a communications template.

payload.description:
## Issue summary
Helix Health (Private) attempted an in-place upgrade of the Redwood Private control plane using the Private installer. Upgrade appears to hang during the "migrations" step. Installer UI/CLI reports "running migrations" continuously (>60 minutes) with no visible progress. Customer is blocked from completing the upgrade window.

## Impact
- Customer cannot complete planned upgrade during maintenance window.
- Risk: partial upgrade state / inconsistent schema versions.
- Customer is compliance-heavy; prefers minimal manual DB intervention.

## Customer environment
- Deployment mode: Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC cluster)
- Control plane: customer-managed
- Data store: customer-managed Postgres (managed service)
- Observability: limited access; Support relies on customer-provided logs + diagnostics bundle.

## What changed
- Customer initiated upgrade from previous installer release to latest available at time of ticket.
- Reported that preflight checks passed, then upgrade stalled at migrations.

## Initial triage notes
- Suspect: long-running migration waiting on lock / blocked by active connections
- Alternate: migration tool deadlock / insufficient privileges / connection pool exhaustion
- Need: installer logs + migration output + DB lock snapshot if available

## Requested from customer (safe artifacts)
Please provide the following (no customer data content required):
1) Installer logs bundle:
   - installer.log (or equivalent)
   - migration runner output (stdout/stderr)
   - timestamps for start of upgrade + when it appeared stuck
2) Cluster events around installer job/pod:
   - kubectl get pods -n redwood-private
   - kubectl describe pod <installer/migrations pod>
   - kubectl logs <installer/migrations pod> --since=2h
3) Control plane version details:
   - current version prior to upgrade
   - target version
   - installer version
4) Postgres connectivity + health (high-level):
   - confirmation Postgres reachable from cluster network
   - any recent DB maintenance

## Workaround / mitigation (validated guidance)
See KB: workaround-private-installer-upgrade-stuck-migrations

### Mitigation checklist (customer-safe)
A) Confirm migrations pod/job is still running and not crash-looping
- If crash-looping: capture logs and do NOT rerun repeatedly (can create noisy partial state)

B) Check for lock contention (if customer DBA can assist)
- Ask DBA to review active sessions + locks during the migration window
- If lock contention is confirmed, pause heavy workloads and retry within the window

C) Controlled retry
- Only after collecting logs and confirming no partial schema corruption
- Support/Platform to guide exact retry steps depending on installer version

## Rollback guidance (if upgrade cannot complete)
Rollback is allowed ONLY if we confirm no irreversible schema migrations have executed.
- Step 1: Collect diagnostics + logs first.
- Step 2: Stop the installer/migrations job to prevent further changes.
- Step 3: Revert control plane deployment manifests to the previous known-good release (customer’s prior pinned artifacts).
- Step 4: Validate control plane health checks + auth + API reachability.
- Step 5: Confirm DB schema version matches the pre-upgrade state.

Do not attempt manual schema downgrades without Platform approval.

## Escalation / ownership
- Primary Eng owner: Platform / Private Deployments (per escalation playbook)
- This ticket is linked to ENG-4828 (add diagnostics bundle + clearer errors for upgrade/migrations failures)

## Next actions
- Support: obtain artifacts above, maintain update cadence with customer during window
- Platform: review logs and advise whether safe rollback is possible
- Engineering follow-up: ensure diagnostics bundle is available + documented (ENG-4828)

Additional notes:
2026-02-06 17:05 UTC — Customer (Helix, via Support email): Provided installer version + target version; confirmed Postgres reachable and no maintenance today. They can pull pod logs and will share within 30 minutes. They asked if they should cancel/retry the installer now.
2026-02-06 18:02 UTC — Customer: Shared kubectl describe + logs snippet indicating migration step repeatedly printing "waiting for advisory lock" and no progress. No crash-looping observed.
2026-02-07 09:12 UTC — Customer: DBA reviewed and found one long-running session holding advisory lock from previous failed attempt. They terminated that session. Migrations progressed and upgrade completed successfully ~10 minutes later. Control plane health checks green.
Customer upgrade completed after terminating a stale DB advisory-lock holding session from a prior attempt. Control plane returned to healthy state. Published/updated workaround guidance and linked ENG-4828 to improve diagnostics and error clarity.
Ensure workaround-private-installer-upgrade-stuck-migrations includes the advisory-lock symptom and customer-safe lock-check guidance
Track ENG-4828: diagnostics bundle + clearer migration phase output
Add Support macro snippet: required artifacts for Private upgrade/migrations issues (installer logs, migration output, pod describe/logs, versions)

payload.description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC we observed a progressive increase in 5xx responses from API Gateway for a small set of requests from customer Acme Personalization. Impact: customer application experienced ~12-18% error rate (5xx) for short-lived chat and embedding mix requests resulting in failed personalization calls and user-visible failures. Environment: production; traffic originates from Acme's dedicated pool in us-east and also shows correlated spikes in eu-west. Observed behavior: API Gateway returns 502/503 intermittently. Traces show upstream runtime instances hitting short-lived crashloops and the autoscaler performing rapid warms/cools. Expected behavior: steady <0.1% 5xx for this tenant. Additional context: errors cluster during tight burst windows from the customer (small payloads, high QPS), and coincide with runtime worker restarts referencing NVML/GPU driver logs and runtime watchdogs.
1) From a client on customer account, send a burst of 40-60 small chat+embedding requests concurrently (payloads <1KB) to /v1/chat/stream
2) Repeat bursts every 30s for 10 minutes to emulate tenant spike profile
3) Observe API Gateway return 502/503 for 10-18% of requests and runtime pod restarts in the same timeframe
2026-03-10T08:31:14Z api-gateway WARN upstream-reset tenant=acme path=/v1/chat/stream status=502 request_id=aa1b2c
2026-03-10T08:31:15Z runtime ERROR watchdog-reset pid=3421 reason=gpu-watchdog-timeout nvml_status=UNINITIALIZED
2026-03-10T08:31:16Z runtime INFO graceful-shutdown start pid=3421 trace_id=aa1b2c
2026-03-10T08:31:20Z autoscaler INFO scale-up reason=burst tenant=acme target_replicas=6 current_replicas=2

Additional notes:
- Pattern: 5xx spikes align with tenant-scale bursts where autoscaler increases replicas quickly from 2->6 within ~30s.
- Runtime logs include 'gpu-watchdog-timeout' then immediate process exit; NVML reports 'UNINITIALIZED' in some restarts suggesting driver init contention under rapid spin-up.
- Kernel: startup race between model hot-swap/prefetch and GPU init path leads to partial state; when next request arrives, runtime panics and exits rather than gracefully failing request.
- Related signals: increased NVMe IO wait noted on nodes concurrently performing snapshotting; potential I/O contention extends GPU init time and amplifies race window.
- Reproduction: local harness reproduced with scripted burst and artificially slowed NVML init (strace sleep on /dev/nv0) resulted in identical crashloop pattern.
- Hypotheses ranked: 1) GPU init race with model swap (high confidence), 2) NVMe snapshot I/O causing init delays (medium), 3) API gateway mis-propagated retries amplifying error rate (low).
Mitigation applied and code fix in progress. Short-term: implemented per-tenant warmup rate limiting and a 10s startup grace that defers accepting traffic until runtime reports full GPU init and KV cache readiness. Mid-term: merged runtime PR to add deterministic GPU init handshake and serialized model prefetch during startup (PR link above). Long-term: autoscaler change to stagger replica startups and guard against simultaneous model hot-swap across replicas. Customer communicated and patch scheduled for rollout to production 2026-03-14 with follow-up monitoring for 72 hours.
- Create an autoscaler policy to jitter replica scale-ups for dedicated pools (owner: infra/autoscaler)
- Add a runtime readiness probe that checks GPU and KV cache readiness before marking pod healthy (owner: serving-runtime)
- Extend observability: per-tenant GPU-init-duration metric and dashboard (owner: observability)
- Run retrospective with customer to validate burst shaping options (owner: CSM)
- Validate NVMe snapshot scheduling to avoid heavy IO during warmup windows (owner: platform-storage)
Notified customer (Acme Personalization) of temporary mitigation 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC and planned full fix/rollout 2026-03-14. Asked customer to throttle their nightly job as an interim measure if possible.
Acme reported intermittent failures for personalization endpoints during their nightly burst window, impacting ~5% of end-users at peak. Mitigation reduced error rate to ~1% regionally; full fix expected to restore baseline <0.1%.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Starting ~03:10 UTC on 2026-03-13 BrightChat observed persistent 5xx errors from the Redwood API. Impact: customer-facing endpoints returned 502/503 in waves causing ~40% request failure rate for ~30 minutes and client-retries. Environment: production, us-east region, Dedicated capacity pool assigned to BrightChat. Observed behavior: repeating sawtooth pattern of failure spikes followed by partial recovery as worker pool recycled; runtime processes repeatedly crashed shortly after startup. Expected behavior: steady success rate and graceful backpressure without crashloops.
1) Send sustained burst of short text-generation requests (1000 QPS peak, average 200QPS sustained) to the tenant's pinned model. 2) Observe autoscaler pre-warm and create >30 ephemeral worker instances in a short window. 3) Note repeated runtime exits and API gateway 502/503 responses as pool churn occurs. 4) Reproduce requires tenant-specific prefetch enabled and pinned model version X.3.4.
2026-03-13T03:11:22Z runtime[worker-7]: ERROR: GPU memory allocation failed: cudaErrorOutOfMemory
2026-03-13T03:11:22Z runtime[worker-7]: INFO: aborting process due to unrecoverable allocator state
2026-03-13T03:11:23Z apigw[edge-12]: WARN upstream connection reset by peer to 10.12.45.67:5020 (worker-7)
2026-03-13T03:11:24Z apigw[edge-12]: ERROR 502 "Bad Gateway" for tenant=brightchat request_id=rc_8f3a
2026-03-13T03:12:05Z autoscaler: DEBUG created 18 ephemeral workers in 12s for pool=brightchat-prod-prewarm
2026-03-13T03:12:37Z runtime[worker-12]: ERROR watchdog: fast restart triggered (restart_count=6) -- runtime.v1.3.9 -> crashloop
2026-03-13T03:13:10Z apigw[edge-12]: INFO connection-pool exhausted, queue-length=384, retrying with backoff
03:15 UTC: Pager alert (5xx rate > 25%) fired; support triage initiated.
Checked gateway metrics: saw periodic spikes in upstream connection failures paired with large increases in open connections to runtime nodes.
Correlated with autoscaler metrics: aggressive prewarm policy created many ephemeral workers within a short cooldown window; pool size jumped from 12 -> 46 in ~30s.
Examined runtime logs: repeated OOMs in early allocation path; crashloops started immediately after new worker boot and persisted until workers recycled.
Hypothesis A: prewarm + pinned model version X.3.4 exposes memory fragmentation/regression in runtime allocator leading to OOM at cold-start batches.
Hypothesis B: gateway retry policy combined with connection pool limits amplified the effect, producing sawtooth 5xx waves as retries hit already-saturated upstreams.
Reproduced locally with smaller cluster by simulating short high-QPS bursts with prefetch enabled; observed similar restart patterns on runtime v1.3.9 build.
Checked recent deploys: a runtime kernel backport (PR #4827) was applied to some nodes in us-east two hours before incident; suspect binary mismatch across node groups.
Memory inspection on one host showed large KV-cache allocations consuming >70% GPU reservation immediately after worker startup when prefetch was enabled.
No evidence of noisy-neighbor GPU exhaustion at host level outside the failing worker process; problem appears per-process allocator behavior.
Temporary customer workaround validated: disabling tenant prefetch eliminated new-worker OOMs and stabilized 5xx rates within 8 minutes.
Root cause (converging): combination of an allocator regression in runtime v1.3.9 under cold-start + tenant prefetch enabled, amplified by autoscaler prewarm policy and gateway retry/amplification behavior.

Additional notes:
Mitigation: temporarily disabled tenant prefetch, adjusted autoscaler prewarm policy to add a 120s cooldown, and rolled back affected us-east runtime nodes from v1.3.9 -> v1.3.7 (rollback PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4835). Outcome: error rate returned to baseline (<1%) and worker churn stopped. Permanent fix: runtime allocator patch merged to main (github.com/redwood/runtime/commit/1a2b3c) and scheduled for v1.4.3; autoscaler prewarm defaults updated to conservative settings; gateway retry policy to be tuned to add per-tenant circuit-breaker to avoid amplification. Customer communication: BrightChat informed of mitigations and timeline; no SLA credit requested at this time. Follow-ups: postmortem with action items, add automated test for cold-start memory patterns, and telemetry to alert on prewarm-induced OOMs.
