payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403s when Redwood control plane attempts to download model shard presigned URLs during control-plane-initiated artifact fetches from S3. Failures are selective (only some shards fail), and occur only for the customer's private deployment behind a corporate DNS forwarder and egress proxy.

Impact:
- FinLedger sees ~10-20% of nightly shard fetches fail causing degraded cold-start time and occasional fallback to smaller model variants.
- Customer reports production inference errors during scale-up events.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) peered via TGW to corporate network
- Egress path: serving nodes -> VPC egress -> corporate DNS forwarder -> internet egress proxy -> AWS S3 (presigned URLs)
- Region: us-west-2, prod

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a model scale-up on customer's private cluster (simulate a cache-miss by restarting a serving node).
2) Control plane issues presigned GETs to S3 for model shard objects from serving nodes.
3) Observe that 1 in 5 shard GETs return 403 from S3 while others succeed.
4) Re-query resolved A/AAAA and CNAME for the presigned host from inside the forwarding resolver and compare to direct public resolution.

Observed behavior / Logs:
- curl -v "<presigned-url-for-shard>" shows TLS handshake succeeded but HTTP 403.
- tcpdump on serving node shows SNI sent on ClientHello as host=presigned-<hash>.s3.amazonaws.com but resolved IPs are a mix of public S3 IPs and a privately-aliased front-end owned by the customer's corp-proxy.
- dig @corp-forwarder for presigned host returns a CNAME chain: presigned-<hash>.s3.amazonaws.com -> s3-redirect.internal-corp.example.com -> <corp-egress-ip>. The intermediate CNAME is only present when queried via corp resolver; public resolvers return canonical s3 endpoints.
- ALPN offered by corp-egress terminator is h2 but the TLS stack on the egress terminator strips or rewrites SNI in-flight for the proxied connection to the upstream S3 endpoint which leads to AWS treating the Host header as mismatched from the presigned URL hostname in the signed request (403).

Initial hypothesis:
- Corporate DNS forwarder is injecting an internal CNAME (shadowing) to steer traffic through an HTTP/TLS egress terminator. The presigned URLs are sensitive to exact hostnames used during the TLS handshake and request signature validation; the egress terminator rewrites SNI or host headers which invalidates the presigned signature on some call paths, producing intermittent 403s. The mix of responses is due to resolver cache eviction / round-robin between internal-corp alias and direct IPs.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 14:45 UTC - Support: Noted correlation between TTLs of internal-corp CNAME and observed failure rate — when TTL expires, resolver falls back to public resolution and requests succeed.
2026-03-13 16:10 UTC - Support/SRE: Confirmed that some corp egress nodes rewrite SNI to canonicalize hostnames for TLS inspection. This breaks presigned URL validation.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-13 09:30 UTC: Looping in FinLedger network/security team. Asked for corp-forwarder config and appliance vendor logs. Provided packet captures and failing curl output.
FinLedger (Customer) 2026-03-13 10:05 UTC: We see proxy-side TLS inspection, but believed it only terminated on outbound web traffic; attaching proxy logs that show rewrite actions. We cannot change proxy behavior without risk approvals.
Marcus Chen (SRE) 2026-03-13 11:15 UTC: Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) pin control-plane artifact-relay to use our internal artifact-relay gateway (tunneled via Redwood control plane) or 2) configure the customer's egress to allow direct passthrough for s3.amazonaws.com hostnames to preserve original SNI/Host. Asked for timeline for corporate change.
FinLedger Network Team 2026-03-13 13:30 UTC: Can whitelist s3.amazonaws.com but their corporate policy prevents passthrough by default; need exception ticket and 48-hour change window.
Workaround applied: enabled control-plane artifact-relay for FinLedger so shard downloads are proxied via Redwood-managed egress (preserving presigned hostname and avoiding corp SNI rewrite). Customer confirmed shard fetch success rate returned to 100% after switch.
Permanent next steps: 1) Customer to submit change request to allow SNI passthrough for s3.amazonaws.com or to stop the proxy from rewriting SNI for presigned hostnames. 2) Engineering follow-up: add detection/alerting when presigned-hostname resolution returns CNAMEs to non-AWS domains and auto-failover to artifact-relay for private deployments.
Post-incident tasks: create runbook entry for "CNAME shadowing / SNI rewrite causing presigned URL 403s" and expose a diagnostic script to customers to detect CNAME shadowing.
Add runbook and alerting: detect CNAMEs that do not end in aws domain when resolving presigned hosts (ENG-PR-901)
Add UI note in Console for private deployments: warning when custom DNS resolves presigned hostnames to non-AWS CNAMEs (DOCS-412)
Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to provide template customer firewall/DNS exceptions for presigned artifact fetches
payload.summary: CNAME shadowing by corporate DNS forwarder causes SNI hostname mismatch and selective artifact 403s during shard fetch

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers (AcmeChat) reported a multi-minute window of elevated 502 responses from the Redwood API beginning 2026-03-13 10:12 PDT. The wave coincided with a customer-side traffic pattern that mixes a small number of long-lived streaming sessions and a large volume of short request bursts (chat completions and embeddings).

Impact:
- ~15% of requests returned 502s or immediate connection resets for the tenant during the peak window.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/completions
- Visible customer errors and retries; customer reported degraded UX and increased retry cost.

Environment:
- Host: prod/us-west-2 gateway cluster (apigw-v4) -> runtime pool (dedicated tenant pool: tenant-acmechat-03)
- Models: gpt-3.5-redwood-v1 (primary), fallback to open-llama-7b-quant observed in logs

Steps to reproduce (how customer recreated):
1) Start 8 long-lived streaming sessions that maintain an open SSE/HTTP2 connection for ~40s each.
2) Launch 300 short non-stream requests/sec to /v1/completions for 3 minutes.
3) Observe 502 rate rising around minute 2, with some streaming sessions being torn and short requests getting 502s.

Observed symptoms in initial reports:
- API Gateway returned 502s and TCP connection resets; no explicit runtime 5xx in some samples.
- Customer telemetry shows backlog of outstanding connections on their side (timeouts).

Requested by customer:
- Root cause analysis and temporary mitigation to reduce errors during bursts.

Initial triage notes:
- Correlated Redwood apigw metrics (connection_queue_length, accept_errors) showed rapid growth in listen backlog during the burst window.
- Proxy (apigw) connection accept queue hit configured so_backlog limit; OS-level SYN queue counters showed SYN_RECV spikes.
- Runtime (tenant-acmechat-03) logs show repeated 'prefetch worker stalled' traces during the same window and multiple runtime worker restarts with watchdog timeouts.
- Hypothesis: mixed long-lived streams are occupying proxy worker slots, causing accept/handshake queue pressure; short requests then push through, causing runtime prefetch threads to contend for GPU scheduling leading to watchdog restarts and upstream connection closures.
- Confirmed by sampling: when runtime restarted, apigw returned 502 for active in-flight short requests.

What we checked:
- apigw pod logs and netstat snapshots from 2026-03-13 10:11-10:16.
- Runtime heap and GPU utilization graphs (no near-100% GPU saturation, but scheduling latency spiked).
- KV cache miss rate increased during bursts (more cache churn).
- No TLS handshake errors, certs healthy.

Action items created during investigation:
- Quick mitigation: tighten per-tenant concurrent-connection soft limit and enable short-request prioritization on apigw.
- Runtime change: increase runtime watchdog threshold for prefetch throttles in the tenant pool and add slight backoff on prefetch worker retries.
- Infra change: increase apigw listen backlog and tune keepalive/epoll parameters for prod/us-west-2 cluster.

Mitigation applied 2026-03-13 11:05 PDT:
- Deployed apigw config bump: so_backlog increased from 128 -> 512; keepalive_timeout increased to reduce churn; enabled tenant short-request prioritization. (PR: runtime #4521)
- Rolled runtime patch to tenant pool: prefetch backoff + watchdog threshold increased from 1s -> 3s for prefetch stalls.
- Temporarily applied per-tenant soft concurrent connection limit of 300 connections to prevent single-tenant consumption of proxy workers.
Post-mitigation: error rate for AcmeChat dropped to <0.3% within 2 minutes; no further runtime restarts observed in follow-up 60m window.

2026-03-13 10:22 - Support (Maya Chen): Reproduced initial error pattern in staging by running customer's mixed load pattern. Opening SRE ping.
2026-03-13 10:35 - SRE (Diego Ramos): Observed accept_queue hits on apigw; collecting netstat + epoll dumps. Suspect backlog exhaustion, escalating to runtime team.
2026-03-13 10:50 - Runtime (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed prefetch worker stalls correlate with spikes in scheduling latency; drafting small watchdog/backoff change. I'll attach PR when ready.
2026-03-13 11:08 - Support (Aisha Patel): Applied apigw config change for AcmeChat tenant and enabled short-request prioritization. Customer reports immediate improvement.
2026-03-13 12:15 - Customer (AcmeChat - Jenna Torres): Thanks, errors are gone for now. Please advise long-term fix so we can avoid tuning our traffic pattern.
2026-03-14 09:00 - Engineering (Diego Ramos): Follow-up: rolling cluster-wide backlog and prefetch changes next week; will add automated soak test for mixed streaming+burst profiles.
Add a synthetic canary test that simulates long-lived streams + aggressive short bursts; run in perf lab weekly.
Implement smarter apigw prioritization policy that favors handshake/short RPCs over long-lived streaming connections when backlog pressure detected.
Consider exposing guidance to customers about preferring connection multiplexing or separating streaming vs short-request tenants for heavy mixed workloads.
Track a long-term runtime improvement: adaptive prefetch concurrency based on observed scheduling latency rather than fixed worker count.
payload.summary: Intermittent 502 wave tied to socket backlog and runtime prefetch throttle under mixed streaming+short-request burst

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer requests a reproducible, verifiable 'immutable audit ledger' export to support a 90-day SIEM backfill and ongoing delta deliveries. They require a plan showing how Redwood will: 1) produce an initial backfill bundle covering 2025-11-01 to present, 2) provide incremental delta exports (hourly) with deterministic ordering and checksums, 3) include pseudonymization for PII fields, and 4) deliver cryptographic proof (digest/hmac/x509-signed manifest) that the archive has not been tampered with.

Background: FinLedger is undergoing a regulatory audit and wants a vendor-provided backfill and a repeatable daily delta feed into their SIEM (Graylog). They need evidence for chain-of-custody and demonstrable immutability for ingestion into their compliance archive.

Requested deliverables: initial backfill (S3-compatible bundle or signed tarball), delta ingest endpoint or push schedule with manifest and checksums, field mapping document for SIEM ingestion (timestamp formats, tenant_id mapping, event_type normalization), PII redaction/pseudonymization description, and a short runbook for verification steps auditors will run.

payload.description:
Multiple docked Dell Precision 7770 workstations imaged via the standard SCCM/Autopilot pipeline boot into Windows correctly but container workloads that depend on the NVIDIA GPU fail to start. Investigation shows the nvidia-container-toolkit (and underlying NVIDIA driver) bundled by the imaging job does not match the firmware/driver expected when the WD22TB4 dock is attached at first boot, resulting in Docker + containerd errors and inability to launch CUDA-enabled containers.
1) Start with factory-fresh Dell Precision 7770 and WD22TB4 dock connected via TB4
2) PXE boot / SCCM task sequence + our standard imaging task (image v2026.03.01) applied
3) OOBE completes, company policies and drivers installed by driver-management role
4) User logs in, Docker + containerd auto-start; attempt to run a simple CUDA container (e.g., nvidia/cuda:11.8-base)
5) Observe container fails to start with NVML/nvidia-smi errors and container runtime messages about missing driver hooks
Mar 10 09:12:45 host1 dockerd[1234]: time="2026-03-10T09:12:45Z" level=error msg="Failed to start container: runtime error: driver hook not found"
Mar 10 09:12:45 host1 containerd[987]: level=error msg="nvidia-container-toolkit: failed to prepare device: NVML library not found"
Mar 10 09:12:46 host1 kernel: nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel
Mar 10 09:12:46 host1 kernel: nvidia 0000:01:00.0: firmware: failed to load nvidia/firmware.bin (-2)
Reproduced on 3 distinct devices that were docked during first-boot after imaging; undocked systems do not show the failure.
Driver-management recipe currently applies NVIDIA driver package v525.85 from driver-factory repo; however dock firmware query shows TB4 dock exposing a different PCI topology requiring a newer 531-series driver.
Hypothesis: imaging job bundles driver packages in a fixed order and when TB4 is present at first boot Windows Device Install chooses the wrong driver (older package) because the dock enumerates GPU differently. This mismatched driver prevents NVML-init causing nvidia-container-toolkit to fail.
Checked SCCM task sequence: 'apply-drivers' step is non-idempotent and does not re-run after dock enumeration changes — potential race between driver package application and dock attaching.
Temporary repro: force uninstall NVIDIA drivers and re-install 531.* and containers recover immediately (worked on two test units).
Support (Avery Chen) 2026-03-10: Customer-facing devs reported CI runners on docked laptops failing unit tests that use GPU. Created ticket after triage.
SRE (Marcus Patel) 2026-03-11: Confirmed logs; reproduced locally on eu-west lab with a docked 7770. Captured full driver store listing and attached to GH PR for driver-selection change.
Driver team (Lucia Fernandez) 2026-03-11: Asked for exact driver-store manifest and SCCM package GUIDs. Noted that 531-series package was published last week to driver-factory but imaging still picks up 525 due to package order in task sequence.
Imaging (Rohit Desai) 2026-03-12: Added a diagnostic step to re-enumerate PnP and re-run 'apply-drivers' post-firstboot for test run; will try with 10 machines in staging tomorrow.
Reporter (Avery Chen) 2026-03-12: Confirmed workaround (manual driver re-install) restored container workloads for two affected engineers; request for a systematic fix to avoid repeated manual steps.
Workaround: Manual uninstall of older NVIDIA driver and install of 531.* driver restores NVML and allows nvidia-container-toolkit to operate. Short-term mitigation: imaging team will add a post-OOBE driver re-enumeration + driver re-apply step for docked devices in the task sequence (testing in staging). Long-term: driver-management will update the driver-selection logic to prefer the dock-aware 531-series package when a TB4 dock is present and publish a patched ansible-imaging role. Tracking PRs: ansible-imaging/pull/312 (diagnostic step) and driver-factory/pull/89 (prefer 531). Follow-up required: schedule delayed rollout and update provisioning runbooks on Confluence.
payload.summary: Docked Dell Precision receives mismatched NVIDIA driver during imaging, breaking container runtime (nvidia-container-toolkit)

payload.description:
Issue summary:
After Okta session refresh triggered by our short-lived SSO cookie policy, admins attempting to unlock the Redwood Console get redirected into a conditional access evaluation loop and ultimately receive a generic 403 / Access Denied in the console UI.

Impact:
- ~8 administrators across multiple teams unable to access the Console for ~45 minutes during maintenance window.
- Unable to escalate or change role bindings while console access is blocked; delayed incident responses.

Environment:
- Affected environment: prod - us-east
- Identities: corporate Okta org (redwood.okta.com) using device-trust + conditional access policy set (MFA + network restrictions)
- Affected services: Console (web), Okta session refresh hook, Auth proxy (oauth2-proxy variant)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Admin with existing Console session sits idle until Okta short-lived cookie rotation (~30m) triggers session refresh.
2) Console redirects to Okta for re-auth; Okta evaluates conditional access policies that include device trust + recently-rotated endpoint tag.
3) Okta returns a redirect to our auth callback with a state token.
4) Our auth proxy attempts to exchange the state token but receives a 401 from Okta introspection due to a race where the device-trust assertion has not propagated to the session.
5) Proxy triggers another redirect to Okta; Okta starts a new evaluation and repeats step 4, creating a loop.

Observed logs / traces:
- auth-proxy (us-east-1, pod auth-proxy-62): repeated lines: "Failed token introspection: 401 - Device assertion pending" timestamped every 5s.
- Okta logs (audit link):  multiple auth evaluations for user a.patel@redwood.ai with status "MFA_REQUIRED" then "DENIED" then "CHALLENGE" in quick succession.
- Browser console: final error page shows HTTP 403 from console API: "Access Denied - missing session".

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Conditional Access policy coupled with very short cookie rotation creates transient state where device-trust assertion hasn't propagated between Okta's eval path and token introspection endpoints.
- Hypothesis 2: Our auth-proxy does not honor the Okta state token retry TTL and immediately attempts introspection leading to a predictable 401.
- Reproduced consistently in staging with identical Okta policy (see test user test.admin@redwood.ai).
- Correlated with a recent roll (2026-03-09) of the auth-proxy container which introduced a change in how query params are forwarded to Okta (PR referenced above).

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Increased the proxy's Okta introspection retry delay to 10s in runtime with a manual config override — reduced loop frequency but did not fully prevent denial on first refresh for some users.
- Temporarily relaxed the conditional access tag requirement for our admin group in Okta and confirmed normal re-login flow for test users (manual change reverted after validation).

Next steps / action items:
- [Assigned] Liam Chen: Revert the query-param forwarding change from PR 1147 and redeploy auth-proxy canary (ETA: 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC).
- [Assigned] Oncall IAM (Rhea Kapoor): Coordinate with Okta support to confirm that device-trust assertion propagation time is within expected bounds and request workaround flags if available (ETA: 2026-03-13 EOD).
- [Assigned] Aisha Patel: Create a short-term console-level guard to surface a clearer error message and a self-service unlock link for affected admins (ETA: 2026-03-14).

Resolution notes (provisional):
- Reverted auth-proxy change in canary; canary passed smoke tests and no loop observed for 30m in staging.
- Okta confirmed the propagation delay is normal during a high-fanout policy evaluation and suggested adding a 5-10s introspection backoff.

Follow-up / Postmortem items:
- Produce a short postmortem documenting root cause and timeline, include runbook additions to handle short-lived session rotations (owner: SRE).
- Consider extending Okta introspection backoff in default auth-proxy config (owner: platform infra).
- Add a monitoring alert for repeated auth-proxy 401 introspection failures to detect loops earlier.
payload.summary: Conditional Access policy loop prevents admin console unlock after Okta session refresh

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled bulk KMS rewrap for ephemeral runner credentials, a subset of runners entered a secret-cache livelock where vault-sync repeatedly refreshed secrets but the runner-provisioner refused to mark nodes healthy. This prevented the release cutover job from acquiring the required pool of labeled runners and blocked the production deploy window.

Impact:
- Release cutover delayed for two release pipelines (nightly + hotfix).
- ~18% of ephemeral runner fleet in us-west-2 and 12% in eu-central-1 continuously flapped between REGISTERED and UNHEALTHY, failing job assignment.
- Some long-running jobs were evicted and re-queued, creating billing churn.

Environment:
- prod account (redwood-prod) running 2026-03-10 KMS rewrap job initiated from operations-rotate-key pipeline.
- Runner image v2026.02.1, runner-provisioner v1.14.0, vault-sync v0.9.3.
- Autoscaler policy: conservative-surge with max-unavailable 10%.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Triggered bulk KMS rewrap for ephemeral runner service account keys across regions.
2) vault-sync pushed new wrapped secrets and incremented secret-version labels on k8s Secret objects.
3) Runner pods attempted to fetch new secret; cache layer (runner-provisioner cache) attempted a soft-refresh but observed nonce mismatch with authz-cache table.
4) Provisioner flagged pod as unhealthy and restarted the token renewal flow. vault-sync simultaneously rewrapped again due to perceived failure, renewing secret-version and causing the runner to see a new version mid-refresh.
5) Loop repeated until operator intervention.

Logs / Observations:
- Vault-sync logs (us-west-2): many 2026-03-10T22:14:xx entries "secret rewrap: success version=222->223" followed quickly by retries for same pod IDs.
- Runner-provisioner logs: repeated "cache nonce mismatch, dropping token refresh" followed by "marking runner UNHEALTHY: token-refresh-failed" for same container IDs.
- Authz-cache (redis) had transient high CPU and eviction spikes coincident with the rewrap window.
- Scheduler metrics showed job-assign latency spike to 4.1s (baseline 0.6s) and pending-job queue growth.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: concurrent rewraps + eventual consistency of authz-cache caused the provisioner to observe mixed secret-versions across components and treat that as compromise, triggering aggressive eviction.
- Vault-sync retry/backoff is too eager when secrets appear outdated; it will rewrap again for a pod perceived as failed, which escalates version churn.
- The provisioner cache validates both secret-version and nonce; if versions do not align within a short window, it refuses to accept the token and evicts. The short acceptance window is too tight for our multi-region rewrap choreography.
- Related: similar pattern to INT-30542 (runner deregistered during credentials rotation) but here it manifests as livelock due to compounded rewrap retries across components.

Temporary workaround implemented:
- Paused the rolling rewrap in eu-central-1 and set vault-sync to single-threaded mode for us-west-2.
- Increased provisioner token acceptance window (config toggle) from 5s to 45s as an emergency mitigation to allow reconciliation.
- Manually reconciled ~120 affected pods by forcing a single rewrap and restarting runner-provisioner for the affected node pool.

Resolution plan (short-term):
- Stabilize by rolling a hotfix to vault-sync to add optimistic backoff and a per-pod rewrap gate so we don't rewrap the same pod while a previous refresh is in-flight. Target: vault-sync v0.9.4.
- Roll hotfix to runner-provisioner to make cache-version acceptance window configurable and to add a one-time idempotency token check to tolerate brief version skew. Target: v1.14.1.
- Increase authz-cache resource requests and add Redis persistence tuning to avoid eviction during rotation windows.
- Re-run controlled rotation with feature flags enabling single-region stagger and observability hooks.

Follow-ups and postmortem items:
- Postmortem to be authored once stable with timeline, blame-free root cause, and remediation owner assignments.
- Add automated test that simulates concurrent rewrap + cache skew to CI test harness.
- Update the Release Cutover Checklist to include a secret-rotation readiness gate.
- Consider orchestration change: central coordinator that stages rewraps per runner label instead of region-wide parallel rewraps.

Additional notes:
Hotfixes planned: vault-sync v0.9.4 (optimistic backoff + per-pod gate) and runner-provisioner v1.14.1 (configurable acceptance window + idempotency token). Authz-cache tuned and more conservative rotation orchestration to be adopted. Postmortem owner: Mateo Alvarez. Estimated regression window closed after incremental rollouts.
Merge vault-sync PR with per-pod gate and backoff
Roll runner-provisioner config change and bake in staging
Re-run secret rotation with single-region stagger and SLOs monitored
Create postmortem and update runbooks
payload.summary: Runner secret-cache livelock during bulk key rewrap blocks release cutover

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Some internal developers are unable to obtain ephemeral CLI tokens for runbook/approval actions. Browser SSO (console) works normally, but CLI flows that rely on token exchange return 401 with a service log message 'missing authn_context'. This started after the identity-proxy v2.8.0 rollout on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- A subset of engineers (~6-10 reports so far) cannot run oncall runbooks via the CLI.
- Affects runbook approval / ephemeral token flows only (interactive browser SSO unaffected).
- Potentially blocks oncall operations for infra teams during incidents.

Environment:
- prod cluster us-east (identity-proxy fleet behind NGiNX ingress)
- identity-proxy v2.8.0 (rolled 2026-03-09 02:15 UTC)
- approval-service 1.14.2
- cli-runner v0.42 (token-exchange subflow)

Steps to reproduce (reported):
1. Run `rw runbook approve --id <PR>` from a developer machine behind corp-proxy.
2. CLI opens browser for Okta SSO; user completes MFA and returns to CLI.
3. CLI performs token exchange with /internal/token-exchange endpoint and receives HTTP 401.
4. CLI shows: "Token exchange failed: unauthorized (missing authn_context)"

Observed logs (excerpt):
- identity-proxy logs: "WARN token-exchange request missing header X-Authn-Context; rejecting"
- approval-service logs: "ERROR exchange failed: identity-proxy rejected request (401)"
- Okta logs: successful session creation and token issuance for browser flow (no errors)

Initial hypothesis:
- The proxy upgrade introduced a header whitelist that strips the X-Authn-Context / X-Forwarded-Authn header used by the CLI token-exchange path. Browser flow uses cookie + callback and does not require that header, which explains discrepancy.

Notes:
- Affected users are both Mac/Linux and are on corp VPN. Some remote staff using different egress paths not impacted (inconsistent).
- No billing/customer impact but internal ops risk.

Investigation checklist performed so far:
- Confirmed identity-proxy was rolled at the time reports started (deployment audit).
- Reproduced locally behind corp-proxy and captured headers via tcpdump: X-Authn-Context header is absent on requests forwarded from proxy.
- Compared working and failing requests: working (pre-upgrade) requests included X-Authn-Context: okta:amr:pwd; failing ones do not.
- Reviewed identity-proxy config (v2.8.0): added "trusted_headers" whitelist which by default drops unrecognized headers. See PR linked below.

Temporary workaround suggested:
- Use the web console for runbooks until fix is deployed.
- Developers can run the CLI with `RW_PROXY_BYPASS=1` to bypass corp-proxy and preserve headers for token exchange (not ideal for everyone).

Supporting links:
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234ABC/p1678520000000 (channel #support)
- Deploy PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1824
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/ephemeral-token-exchange-runbook

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:05 - Security (J. Alvarez): Confirmed adding back X-Authn-Context header is acceptable from a policy perspective for internal flows. Requested a small risk doc before deploy.
Timeline:
- 2026-03-09 02:15 UTC: identity-proxy v2.8.0 rollout.
- 2026-03-09–2026-03-10: ~6 internal reports.
- 2026-03-10: Reproduction and header capture; identified missing X-Authn-Context.
- 2026-03-10 11:00: PR created to re-add header to trusted list (PR 1831).
- 2026-03-11 04:00: Canary v2.8.1 deploy (identity-proxy with whitelist fix).
- 2026-03-11 08:00: Canary test passed; proceed to full rollout 2026-03-12 10:00.
Root cause:
- identity-proxy v2.8.0 introduced a whitelist for incoming headers and by default dropped non-standard internal headers (including X-Authn-Context). Token-exchange flow depends on that header to carry Okta authn context from the callback; its absence caused the exchange to be treated as unauthenticated and rejected.
Mitigations considered:
- Re-add X-Authn-Context to proxy trusted headers (implemented).
- Modify token-exchange flow to tolerate missing header if session cookie is present (longer-term change, tracked as follow-up).
Workaround:
- Temporary bypass environment variable documented for power users (RW_PROXY_BYPASS=1).
Fix applied:
- identity-proxy v2.8.1 deployed to prod on 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC; X-Authn-Context added to trusted headers.
Post-deploy verification:
- 12/12/2026 (typo?) verified 8 previously impacted users can now obtain ephemeral CLI tokens; no additional 401s reported in 24h window.
Follow-ups (action items):
- Dinesh to open engineering task to make token-exchange resilient when header missing (INT-995124).
- Update release checklist to include a header compatibility test for proxy upgrades.
- Add entry to knowledge base about RW_PROXY_BYPASS workaround and security considerations.
Observed inconsistency across egress paths—some corporate egress nodes had additional header rewrite rules. This made the bug appear intermittent. The fix standardizes trusted headers at the proxy level so rewrites do not silently drop auth context.
payload.summary: Ephemeral CLI token exchange failing (missing authn_context) after identity-proxy upgrade

Checked KMS policy bindings: laptop encrypted volume key is a customer-managed envelope key (CMK) in us-west-2 with grants to user's Okta service principal. No cross-region replication configured.

In progress — operational checklist drafted by Endpoint and IAM. Next steps: HR to confirm decision (retain vs return) by 2026-03-13; if retain, Endpoint to schedule remote wipe and KMS team to create apac CMK and perform key rotation. Legal/Finance will finalize customs/tax guidance.

payload.description:
Issue summary: An employee clicked a vendor onboarding form link (recruited-vendor.example.com) that initiated an OAuth consent flow. The external app requested limited API token scopes. Post-consent, an API-scoped token and a service account key named 'vendor_onboard_2026' were observed in the org via audit logs. Impact: potential unauthorized service-level access that was subsequently used by CI pipelines to run a privileged job and fetch secrets. Timeline and observed activity are below.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:05 - SecOps (Elena Ruiz): Preliminary log parse shows an OAuth app with client_id 'vendor-5123' granted by the user. App requested scopes: read:org, write:ci, create:service_keys. Found a service key creation event 3 minutes after grant.
2026-03-12 13:22 - SRE (Daniel Cho): The service key was used by runner 'ci-runner-9' at 03:12 UTC from IP 198.51.100.42 to pull a privileged job 'deploy-metrics'. We have paused that runner and blocked the IP in firewall rules.
User flow: Clicked link -> vendor page presented OAuth consent -> user accepted using SSO session. OAuth grant recorded at 2026-03-11T23:58:12Z.
Audit evidence: oauth.grant events show client_id vendor-5123, redirect_uri vendor callback URL vendor-5123.example.com/cb, scopes included 'create:service_keys'. service_keys.create event by actor user:ap.patel@redwood at 2026-03-11T24:01:05Z creating 'vendor_onboard_2026'.
Service key activity: key 'vendor_onboard_2026' used by ci-runner-9 to call /api/v1/ci/jobs with token presented in Authorization header. Job pulled secret store keys for deployment 'deploy-metrics'.
Network: outbound connections from CI runner to vendor endpoints observed following job. External IP 198.51.100.42 resolves to a hosting provider used by multiple vendor forms; reverse lookup inconclusive.
Hypotheses: (A) Malicious vendor form requested excessive scopes and created a service key to escalate access; (B) Vendor form was legitimate but compromised; (C) User consent was coerced by deceptive UI (consent phishing).
Risk assessment: High — service-level credential creation and CI usage gives attacker a lateral path to internal infra; priority high until keys rotated and further evidence is negative for exfiltration.
Data search: No S3 or database export events linked to this service key in the 24 hours following creation. CI job logs show read-only metrics fetch and a call to an internal telemetry endpoint; exfil not confirmed.
Detection gaps: Current OAuth app onboarding allows create:service_keys scope by default for vendor apps. No org-level denylist existed for apps requesting service key creation.
Related indicators: vendor client_id vendor-5123, service_key name vendor_onboard_2026, runner ci-runner-9, external IP 198.51.100.42, redirect domain vendor-5123.example.com.
Suggested evidence collection: full CI job logs, container snapshots for job run, VPC flow logs for runner, complete OAuth grant history for user and org.
Communication: Notified Legal and Incident Response. Drafted user-facing advisory advising not to reauthorize external apps until review completes.
Immediate mitigation actions taken 2026-03-12: revoked vendor-5123 tokens, disabled service key 'vendor_onboard_2026', paused ci-runner-9, blocked external IP 198.51.100.42 at perimeter, rotated CI credentials referenced in logs.
Policy changes implemented: added org-level rule to block OAuth apps requesting create:service_keys and implemented manual approval for any vendor app requesting elevated scopes.
Detection and monitoring: new alert created to flag OAuth grants that include service_key or admin-equivalent scopes; added logging retention for IAM events for 90 days.
Runbook tasks: update onboarding templates to remove one-click OAuth for non-SSO-approved vendors; add mandatory security review checkbox on onboarding form.
Status: Containment successful; keys revoked and runner paused. Incident remains open for forensic analysis and vendor validation. Expected update 2026-03-18 with forensic summary.
payload.summary: Unexpected OAuth app conceding API-scoped token and creating service key after vendor onboarding form

payload.description:
Background: BrightCart reported a small set of customer complaints where the model returned legacy payment token formats in 3 unique sessions over the past 48 hours. Initial triage indicates the routing and model versioning are correct, but the customer has supplied matching request IDs and a suspected KV-cache collision window that might have replayed a stale prefix for these sessions.

Impact: Business-facing (BrightCart enterprise). 3 affected user sessions; potential PII exposure of masked payment tokens (masked but format-leaking). Customer expects a remediation plan and a scoped transcript to perform a rectification for impacted end-users. No broad production outage.

Request: Approve timeboxed, read-only access to encrypted KV-key checksums + minimal session metadata (no raw user payloads) for the three specified request IDs to validate whether a stale prefix replay occurred. The data requested is the HMAC keyed checksum of KV-keys and the timestamp window they were active. This allows verification without transmitting plaintext user data.

Justification: The checksum approach preserves data minimization (we do not request plaintext payloads). Customer requires evidence to support their remediation and user notifications. Legal and Privacy have preliminarily confirmed this is a proportional request if proper safeguards are in place.

Data minimization plan: Only return checksums and metadata: kv_key_hmac, key_active_from, key_active_to, internal_node_id, request_id. Redaction: strip any IP, auth headers, and raw prompt/response content before any handoff. No long-term persistence allowed; snapshot will be deleted after verification and audit log entry.

Access controls: Two-person control required (SRE + Privacy reviewer). Access will be read-only via ephemeral audit account with KMS-wrapped session token. All activity logged in the audit trail. Access window requested: 2 hours. Storage retention: 72 hours encrypted, then automatic delete.

Timeline: Need approval by 2026-03-14 (EOD) to meet customer remediation timeline; extraction can be executed 2026-03-15 09:00-11:00 UTC.

Approvers requested: Security (Data Access Approver), Privacy Counsel, SRE oncall.

Deliverables: 1) CSV of checksums+metadata (HMAC only), 2) verification note stating whether checksum correlation indicates stale-prefix replay, 3) signed access audit entry.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 13:18 — Security (Marco Diaz): Noted. Can we confirm that the requested CSV will not include any PII or raw tokens? Also need to confirm KMS wrapping approach for the ephemeral session token.
2026-03-13 16:55 — Privacy (Dr. Helen Ko): Preliminary ok with checksum-only approach but require two-person control and proof of deletion after 72h. Please add the exact retention deletion command to the runbook entry and link the audit entry in the ticket when finished.
2026-03-14 09:12 — SRE (Liam O'Connor): I can provision the ephemeral account and run the extractor in a timeboxed window. Need final approval from Security and Privacy to proceed. Will post extraction hash and run summary back here.
2026-03-14 12:30 — Security (Marco Diaz): Approving conditional on two-person presence. Approver: Marco Diaz + Dr. Helen Ko. Please schedule extraction and update linked_confluence page with final commands.
Triage performed 2026-03-13 by SRE: located three sessions with request_ids: rc-20260311-8a7, rc-20260312-33f, rc-20260312-7d2. All routed to redwood-open-7b in us-east. No 5xx or throttling recorded around those timestamps.
Checked model rollout logs: client pinned to rwx-compat-13b v2026-03-01. No recent rollouts overlapping timeframe. Serving runtime trace shows brief KV eviction spike on node n-us-east-07 at 2026-03-12T02:11Z (GC window). Hypothesis: transient eviction caused lookup fallback to stale prefix on that node.
Risk assessment: Low probability of large-scale exposure, but high customer trust impact. Need cryptographic verification (HMAC checksums) to confirm if session KV keys matched stale entries.
Extraction plan drafted: run checksum extractor against node n-us-east-07 for specified keyspace and time window; produce HMAC values using audit-only HMAC key stored in KMS; don't emit plaintext keys or payloads.
Awaiting approvals from Security and Privacy. No extraction executed yet. Next step post-approval: schedule two-person extraction window and provide CSV output plus audit log reference.

SRE to schedule 2-hour extraction window and provision ephemeral KMS-wrapped token
Run extractor, upload CSV to secure confluence attachment, then delete snapshot and record deletion command and S3 lifecycle entry
Notify CSM (Emily Wu) and customer of findings with remediation recommendations

Supporting evidence: AP import logs, Concur export CSV (attached in ticket), suspense queue record ID SUSP-99877. Current status: Ticket created by Finance Ops. Issue summary: Request to build a conditional channel-claim automation that: (1) exposes a lightweight Slack 'Claim' button for ephemeral project channels, (2) when claimed creates a templated Confluence seed page and optionally provisions a scoped Jira project, and (3) applies a configurable TTL retention policy that auto-archives or marks channel for review when expiry reached.\n\nImpact: Currently teams manually claim ephemeral channels and create associated docs; channels either remain orphaned or get prematurely archived. This automation reduces orphaned channels, enforces retention guardrails, and ensures discoverability (seeded Confluence page). Helps compliance and on-call handoff for experiments.\n\nEnvironment: Production Slack workspace (redwood-prod), Confluence (prod), Jira (prod). Primary scope: public and private ephemeral channels created by self-service pod bootstrapping.\n\nRequest details:\n- Add a Slack workflow button (or message action) \"Claim channel\" that opens a small modal: owner, team, expected TTL (7/30/90 days), opt-in for Jira project creation.\n- On claim: create Confluence seed page from a template (metadata: channel-name, owner, claim-date, TTL), tag page with 'ephemeral-claimed', and post link to channel.\n- If Jira project requested: call existing provisioning webhook to create a lightweight project with restricted permissions and link project key in Confluence.\n- TTL enforcement: scheduled job evaluates claimed channels; for channels approaching TTL-7d send reminder DM to owner; at TTL expiry automatically archive channel or mark for retention-review (based on channel policy).\n- Audit: write claim, reminders, archive actions to central audit log (Confluence page comment + centralized log file + optional S3 export).\n\nAcceptance criteria, rollout plan, and runbook details below.

payload.description:
Issue summary: AtlasAI reports repeated midday drops in end-to-end throughput (p50 throughput falls ~40%, p99 latency spikes >5x) on their dedicated pool during a customer load window (approx 12:00–13:30 UTC). The failure mode includes failed GPU allocations for new requests, high queue depth, and a short-lived pattern of many tiny streams that appear to 'thrash' batch slots. Impact: production degradation for AtlasAI ML feature endpoints; customers see 5xx/timeout spikes and elevated token latency. Hypothesis: noisy tenant or short-lived ephemeral jobs creating slot churn combined with autoscaler cooldowns and insufficient burst headroom leading to temporary GPU shortages and preemption events.
1) Observe dedicated pool metrics for AtlasAI between 12:00 and 13:30 UTC on 2026-03-10.
2) Send a burst of 1000 short requests (approx 50–200 token responses each) across 30 concurrent clients to the customer's pinned route.
3) Watch scheduler slot allocation, GPU attach logs, and autoscaler events in the same window (k8s events + autoscaler audit).
4) Note that many streams are <300ms and cause rapid open/close of batch slots, increasing fragmented utilization.
5) Confirm that new requests either queue for >30s or return 503/504 while existing longer-lived streams complete.
6) Reproduce shows autoscaler did not open new nodes quickly due to a 10m cooldown and conservative scale-up policy.
2026-03-10T12:06:14Z scheduler: attach_gpu request failed: no available slot (pool=atlas-dedicated-42)
2026-03-10T12:06:16Z serving-runtime: batcher: enqueue request id=rx-29f size=120 tokens stream-duration=0.18s
2026-03-10T12:07:03Z autoscaler: scale_up_decision deferred: cooldown_remaining=7m10s min_replicas=2 target_replicas=6
2026-03-10T12:07:05Z node-exporter: gpu_util=92% mem_util=78% but free_slots=0 fragment_ratio=0.63
2026-03-10T12:10:22Z kubelet: pod preemption event: eviction of atlas-job-ephemeral-ptf-847 to free gpu resources
2026-03-10T12:10:24Z nvidia-driver: NVML_ERROR_ON_DETACH for gpu=3 code=43 (transient link error) — several retries succeeded after 12s
2026-03-10T12:11:00Z serving-runtime: response timeout -> upstream: 504 route=atlas-route-qa (p99 latency saw 5.6x increase)
Initial triage: confirmed spike window and correlated with a large number of short-lived streams from a single tenant (inbound request sampling showed 70% of streams <500ms).
Autoscaler behavior: scale-up cooldown of 10m and pod startup time ~3.5–4.5m meant new capacity did not arrive fast enough for the burst. Max_replicas for the pool was set to 8 — headroom was insufficient for the observed burst.

payload.description:
Issue summary: After a coordinated BIOS firmware flash for a batch of staging workstations, ~12% fail PXE boot with a timeout during initramfs/ramdisk validation. Impact: Staging provisioning pipeline stalls, blocks test environment imaging, and increases re-image retries. No data loss; devices fail to reach SCCM task sequence.
Environment: Staging PXE fleet, us-east TFTP/PXE servers, BIOS versions updated to 1.23.4 on Dell/HP images. Boot path: UEFI PXE -> iPXE -> download initramfs and kernel -> initramfs checksum and signature verification -> mount ramdisk -> continue.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Flash BIOS 1.23.4 on a freshly provisioned Dell Latitude 7440.
2) Boot to network PXE (UEFI). 3) Choose provisioning task sequence. 4) Observe PXE log on server and client serial console.
Observed behavior: Client downloads kernel and initramfs, then stalls ~45s waiting for ramdisk verification; TFTP retransmits and eventually client times out with PXE timeout and reboots. Some clients proceed successfully; failure rate ~12% across batch.
Logs: Attached dmesg snippets, iPXE debug trace, and PXE server tftpd logs (filenames in attachments). iPXE shows 'initrd verification failed: signature mismatch' on failing hosts but succeeding hosts show valid signature and continue.
Initial hypothesis: BIOS firmware change affects UEFI runtime or Secure Boot variables leading to corrupted retrieval of initramfs or altered memory alignment that triggers signature check discrepancies. Alternative: race in PXE server compressed payload delivery, tied to a new kernel/initramfs size exceeding negotiated window with older NIC firmware.
Impact owner: Imaging/Provisioning team. Escalation path: Support -> Infra SRE -> Firmware vendor escalation if needed.
Flash BIOS 1.23.4 on supported model
Boot UEFI PXE and select provisioning task sequence
Monitor iPXE client console and PXE server logs for initramfs verification step
02/18: Priya verified failure reproduction on 3/25 devices in staging. 02/19: Collected iPXE logs and kernel/initramfs SHA256 manifests. 02/20: Noted that failing hosts have identical initramfs SHA reported by server but client reports verification mismatch. 02/22: Eng hypothesis: firmware update changed UEFI variable ordering causing dpkg-signed initramfs verification library to use wrong key slot. 02/24: SRE reproduced with custom iPXE build that logs more verbose UEFI variables; observed difference in SecureBoot db ordering on failing hosts. 03/01: Created test image with stripped signature check; those hosts boot successfully (mitigates immediate provisioning). 03/05: Filed PR to add a more tolerant fallback (see related_github_prs); still under review. 03/09: Opened vendor support ticket with BIOS vendor referencing serial numbers and Secure Boot variable dumps. See Slack thread #imaging-pxe-T1245.

Additional notes:
Nadia Ruiz - SRE (02/24): Reproduced failure on emulated QEMU environment by swapping UEFI variable order; confirms firmware influence. Suggest testing a signed initramfs with alternate key ordering to validate.
Marcus Li - Firmware (03/02): Reached out to vendor; vendor requested SecureBoot variable exports and system event logs. Provided on 03/03.
Mitigation: Added a staging-only temporary bypass for initramfs signature enforcement for affected models and BIOS versions to unblock provisioning (IMAG-2026-033). Ongoing: Eng to complete PR for tolerant verification fallback and automated detection of broken SecureBoot variable ordering. Vendor engagement open for firmware fix. Full resolution pending firmware vendor patch or upstream initramfs verifier update. Post-mortem planned after vendor response; follow-up tasks assigned to Imaging and Firmware teams.
03/10: Temporary bypass held in staging; imaging throughput returned to baseline. PR for fallback verification remains under code review. Vendor acknowledged issue and requested additional traces; expected ETA for vendor patch ~4 weeks. Postmortem and rollout plan to be scheduled after vendor fix or upstream change is released.
Finalize PR to implement tolerant verification fallback and add unit tests
Create detection alert for downstream provisioning failures tied to BIOS version and model
Coordinate with vendor for firmware remediation and plan controlled production rollout
Document mitigation steps in Confluence runbook and notify SRE on-call rotations

payload.description:
Issue summary: After a bulk template import via the new UI, the canonicalization step for SLA/macros produced inconsistent keys. Multiple distinct templates collapsed to overlapping canonical keys, causing routing to match multiple escalation policies and the SLO reporting pipeline to double-count matches. Impact: internal routing automation misrouted approximately 18% of support traffic for a cohort of accounts during the nightly import window (03/05 02:00-03:00 UTC). Several internal pages in the SLO reporter show inflated counts and some alerting cohorts triggered incorrectly. Environment: production, us-east, bulk import UI v2.1.1, canonicalizer service version 1.8.2. Observed behavior: templates that previously produced unique macro keys are now producing identical canonical keys after the import. Expected behavior: canonicalization should deterministically normalize to unique keys per logical template; imports should preserve separation unless explicit duplicates exist. This ticket captures the investigation, temporary mitigations applied, and next steps to roll a permanent fix.
1) Navigate to Console > Templates > Bulk Import (v2 UI)
2) Upload a CSV with 1,200 SLA templates that include minor punctuation/whitespace variations (sample provided in attached), e.g. 'SLA: 24h - Billing', 'SLA 24h Billing', 'SLA:24h:Billing.'
3) Start import with 'canonicalize on' and default locale en-US
4) Observe job completes with success code but canonicalizer emitted warnings in logs
5) Query /internal/slo-reporter/match_counts for the imported cohort and compare pre-import vs post-import counts
2026-03-05T02:12:41Z canonicalizer WARN canonicalize_batch: found 42 collisions while deduplicating batch id=import-2026-03-05-0211
2026-03-05T02:12:41Z canonicalizer DEBUG sample_collision: ['SLA: 24h - Billing', 'SLA 24h Billing'] -> 'sla-24h-billing'
2026-03-05T02:12:41Z template-importer INFO import_complete: imported=1196 duplicates=0 canonicalized_groups=114 total_time_ms=18234
2026-03-05T02:43:02Z slo-reporter ERROR aggregation_pipeline: cohort=enterprise-us count_mismatch=+214 (expected 120, reported 334) trace_id=abc123
Initial hypothesis: canonicalizer's normalization rules were tightened in v1.8.2 to strip punctuation and adjacent stopwords, which increased collision surface for similar templates.
Reproduced locally with a reduced set (20 templates) and confirmed the same collisions when using en-US locale and default stopword list.
Telemetry shows canonicalizer emitted per-key hashes; collisions happened when whitespace/colon removal combined with aggressive stopword removal (e.g., 'the', 'and').
Impact analysis: collisions cause multiple routing macros to map to the same canonical id; router uses canonical id to select escalation policy, so multiple logical templates can be treated as a single policy leading to both misrouting and inflated metrics.
Related config: canonicalizer config uses 'stopword_set=v2' and 'collapse_digits=true' changed in PR 1528 (see related_github_prs).

Additional notes:
Mitigations applied: (a) Immediate - disabled canonicalize-by-default for bulk import UI in prod-us-east; (b) Short-term - re-canonicalization job run with conservative rules to restore separation for affected templates; (c) Mid-term - revert or patch canonicalizer stopword behavior and add a collision-score threshold before collapsing groups. Both the router and reporter were patched to include a guard that consults template metadata before treating a canonical id as authoritative. No customer-facing incidents were triggered; impact limited to internal routing and reporting metrics. Next steps include a full rollout plan and a test harness for large bulk imports.
1) Platform Eng to open a PR that reverts stopword_set=v2 or adds opt-in switch for aggressive canonicalization (owner: Alex Chen, ETA: 2026-03-12)
2) Add unit+integration tests for bulk imports with 10k+ templates to CI (owner: QA team, ETA: 2026-03-19)
3) Run a controlled import in staging with v1.8.3 (patched canonicalizer) and validate reporter counts and router behavior (owner: Ravi Patel, ETA: 2026-03-14)
4) Postmortem to be drafted and linked to this ticket; include SLO for bulk import detection and alerting (owner: Maya Alvarez, ETA: 2026-03-17)
5) Backfill corrected counts for affected cohorts in the SLO reporter and reconcile dashboards (owner: Analytics, ETA: 2026-03-15)
payload.summary: Batch canonicalization variance causes overlapping SLA macro matches after template import

Issue summary:
New hire laptop provisioning using the macOS 13.6 base image fails during automated MDM enrollment step for users who require hybrid SSO (Okta PIV + company SSO). Enrollment hangs on 'Waiting for user authentication' and the device never appears in Jamf inventory.

Impact:
- Blocks onboarding for 3 hires in the past 2 days.
- Manual image/enroll path works but requires ~30–45 minutes of tech time per device.
- Causes delays for engineering hires that need GPU-enabled workstations.

Environment:
- Office devices imaged at SJC imaging station (prod-us-west-office).
- macOS 13.6 base image built 2026-03-05.
- MDM: Jamf Pro 11.2.1.
- SSO: Okta with hybrid PIV flow + internal auth proxy.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot target Mac to NetBoot/auto-imaging via SJC imaging VLAN.
2) Apply base image 2026-03-05 and allow enrollment to trigger.
3) Observe endpoint stop at 'Waiting for user authentication' screen in Jamf enrollment log.
4) Device never registers in Jamf inventory (last seen status: pending enrollment).

Observed logs (excerpt):
- imaging-station.log: "mdm-enroll: start callback; handshake ok; waiting for oauth token"
- jamf-enroll.log: "ENROLLMENT_STATUS: pending_user_auth (timeout 600s)"
- okta-proxy.log: "incoming auth request: session created; SSO redirect issued; user never POSTed credentials"

Investigation notes so far:
- Rebuilt base image (2026-03-08) without changed drivers — same symptom.
- Manual enrollment via Jamf Pro console (generate enrollment URL and complete flow) does succeed for the same user on same hardware.
- Devices enrolled in staging imaging VLAN succeed with same image; difference seems tied to SJC office network's auth proxy flow.
- Packet capture on imaging VLAN shows outbound redirect to auth proxy but occasional TCP RST between imaging station and proxy at 10–20s into the flow.
- Hypothesis: corporate auth proxy (edge device in SJC) has an MTU/inspection rule that breaks the hybrid SSO flow during automated enrollment sequences.

Immediate workaround:
- Techs should use manual enrollment URL from Jamf Console when provisioning new hires at SJC until fix is applied (adds ~30–45m per device).

Next steps / action items:
- [Assigned] Networking to review auth proxy logs and firewall rules for imaging VLAN (Samuel).
- [Assigned] SSO/Identity to verify whether Okta sessions are being invalidated for automated flows (Riley Chen).
- [Assigned] Imaging/Endpoint team to provision a temporary imaging VLAN that bypasses the proxy for onboarding (Ava Nguyen).
- Collect full pcap and provide to Security for DPI inspection if permitted.
- Target remediation ETA: 2026-03-15 for either firewall rule change or proxy config update.


Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:20 - NetOps (channel #netops): Found that the edge proxy is trimming 'Authorization' headers for requests over the imaging VLAN; behavior started after rule push on 2026-03-06. Suggested test: temporarily allow passthrough for imaging VLAN and retest.
Use Jamf Console generate-enroll URL and complete manual enrollment for devices imaged at SJC when automated enrollment fails.
Partial: networking applied passthrough rule and automated enrollment works in testing. Pending formal firewall exception and post-change validation scheduled for 2026-03-14.
Ticket captures combination of imaging/network/identity; consider adding an automated synthetic test in CI to catch enrollment regressions during image rebuilds.

payload.description:
Issue summary
- During a live SE-led demo for Northstar Payments, the Redwood demo tenant began returning HTTP 429 responses mid-flow (streaming chat + tool call step). This caused the demo to stall and required switching to backup screenshots for the Console section.

Customer impact
- Live demo interruption (~6–8 minutes). Customer saw repeated 429s and intermittent retries.
- Risk: undermines reliability story and raises concern about quota predictability/noisy-neighbor.

When / where
- Date/time: 2025-11-12 ~19:10–19:25 UTC
- Environment: prod / us-east
- Tenant: Redwood internal demo org ("demo tenant")

Observed behavior
- Chat/completions requests started returning:
  - 429 Too Many Requests
  - Response headers included rate-limit remaining=0 (per-minute)
- Retries from demo app increased request volume, exacerbating throttling.

Expected behavior
- Demo tenant should be sized for at least 2 parallel demos, with headroom for retries/streaming and synthetic traffic seeding.

Steps to reproduce (as seen during call)
1) Start demo app scenario runner (streaming chat)
2) Execute tool-calling step (adds 1–2 additional calls)
3) Open Console in parallel (refreshes usage/cost panels)
4) Within ~2 minutes, observe 429s

Initial hypotheses
- Demo API key configured with self-serve default RPM/TPM limits.
- Synthetic traffic generator + live demo sharing same project/key.
- Parallel demos earlier in the hour consumed burst capacity; rate-limit window not reset.

Investigation notes
- Checked gateway logs for the demo org/project: throttles triggered on request-rate limit (RPM), not GPU capacity.
- No elevated 5xx in serving runtime; this was an API gateway quota/rate-limit enforcement event.
- Console page refreshes were not the root cause but contributed to request count and distracted during recovery.

Mitigation applied (during incident)
- Temporary quota uplift applied to demo org/project in us-east:
  - Increased RPM cap + burst allowance
  - Increased TPM cap to reduce retry amplification for streaming
- Confirmed new limits took effect within ~60 seconds; 429s stopped.

Root cause
- Demo tenant was provisioned with quota defaults intended for standard self-serve tenants, and our automation did not reliably apply the higher demo profile. Additionally, synthetic traffic seeding was configured to use the same project/key as live demos, consuming part of the minute-based request budget.

Resolution
- Short-term: raise demo tenant quotas and move synthetic traffic generator to a dedicated "seed" project/key to isolate from live demo activity.
- Long-term: update demo tenant provisioning automation defaults to always apply demo quota profile + create separate scoped keys (live-demo vs seed-traffic), and add a demo healthcheck gate that verifies quota/rate-limit settings before SEs start a call.

Customer-facing notes (what SE said)
- Framed as: "We hit our safety rate limit in the demo environment; production customers set limits appropriate to their workloads, and Dedicated capacity has separate controls. We’ll adjust the demo tenant so it never happens again."

Follow-ups / action items
- [DONE] Document immediate workaround in demo runbook: if 429s occur, switch to backup mode and run healthcheck.
- [DONE] Add healthcheck validation for quota/rate limits and surface clear pass/fail output (linked PR).
- [DONE] Provisioning automation: ensure demo profile quotas applied idempotently; prevent seed job from sharing live-demo key.
- [TODO] Add alerting on demo-tenant approaching RPM/TPM caps (warning threshold) routed to demo on-call alias.

Workarounds (SE playbook)
- Run demo tenant healthcheck endpoint; if quotas not applied, page #support and switch to backup screenshots.
- If throttling persists, pause synthetic traffic generator for the live window and retry after 60s rate-limit window reset.

Notes on data/security
- All traffic is synthetic/demo; no customer data involved.

References
- Slack: #support and #sales thread (internal) around live demo throttling
- Confluence: Demo capacity/quotas runbook + demo tenant reset runbook
- Related: SUP-4189 (Console dashboards empty; seed traffic generator separation work overlaps)

Additional notes:
Resolved by increasing demo tenant RPM/TPM quotas, isolating synthetic traffic to a dedicated seed project/key, and adding a demo healthcheck to validate quota/rate-limit settings before demos. Provisioning automation updated to apply demo quota profile idempotently; subsequent demos confirmed stable.
payload.summary: Demo tenant hitting 429 throttling during live customer demo (Northstar Payments)

Issue summary: Request to provision a reusable, auditable onboarding workflow for third-party vendors and contractors that combines timebound Slack guest channels, automated transcript capture to Confluence (evidence bridge), and a lightweight Jira approval microflow.

Impact: Currently vendor onboarding is ad-hoc: teams create guest channels and store notes in project spaces with inconsistent retention and no single evidence trail for audits. This increases risk during compliance reviews and makes forensic reconstruction of access/activity difficult.

Request: Build and deploy an opinionated template and automation that any pod can request via a Jira form. The automation should: 1) create a tenant-scoped Confluence space (audit namespace) populated with a vendor onboarding checklist; 2) provision a Slack guest channel with timebound membership (TTL) and a small guest bot that posts onboarding checklist items; 3) capture the full Slack transcript at deprovision time and attach it to the Confluence evidence page; 4) create a Jira approval task for Security and the Requesting Team with configurable SLAs; 5) emit structured metadata (owner, vendor name, access window, artifacts links) back to the original Jira issue.

Requirements and constraints: - Evidence artifacts must be immutable (Confluence page with view-only history) and linked to the Jira request. - Access TTL should be adjustable via the Jira form but default to 14 days. - Approvals flow must require Security sign-off for vendors with outbound network access. - All actions must be logged and traceable (who provisioned, timestamps). - Sensitive PII must not be stored in Confluence; automation must scrub any detected email/SSN patterns in transcripts before storing, and flag for manual review.

Proposed flow (high level): 1) Requester opens a templated Jira request with vendor metadata and requested duration. 2) Automation creates a Confluence evidence page from template and a Slack guest channel (private) via service account. 3) Automation creates a Jira subtask assigned to Security and notifies the on-call via #security-approvals. 4) Upon Security approval, automation adds guests (email invites) to Slack and posts onboarding checklist. 5) During access window, requesters can extend via the Jira issue; extensions spawn a brief approval. 6) At TTL expiry or manual close, automation exports Slack transcript, scrubs PII patterns, attaches the export to the Confluence evidence page, and archives the Slack channel. 7) Automation closes the Jira request with structured metadata and retention tags.

Acceptance criteria: - Template Jira request available to all pods in the Internal Tools category. - Automation successfully creates Confluence page and Slack channel in 95% of test runs. - Transcript capture to Confluence preserves message timestamps and poster handles and is scrubbed for PII. - Security approval step is enforced for high-risk vendors. - Logs include provisioning events and final artifact links.

Security considerations: - Use tenant-scoped service principals and least-privilege Slack bot token; rotate tokens regularly. - Confluence evidence pages should be created under a central audit space with restricted edit permissions. - Automation must surface any potential PII matches to Security for manual review.

Test plan: - QA team will provision three test vendor flows: low, medium, high risk. - Verify TTL enforcement, transcript capture, scrub behavior, and approval gating. - Pen test and access review for service account tokens.

Rollout plan: - Pilot with two non-sensitive pods for two weeks. - Iterate on scrub heuristics and timeouts. - After pilot, enable self-serve for all pods and publish runbook.

Owner team: Internal Tools - Admin Automation.

Estimated completion: 2026-03-24

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 - QA automation: Added tests for TTL enforcement and transcript attachment. Found edge-case where Slack export truncates long threads; plan to chunk export and re-run.
payload.summary: Provision auditable external-vendor onboarding workflow: Slack guest channels, Confluence evidence bridge, and timebound approvals

Issue summary: Request to create a managed gateway that provisions Slack channel templates (team, project, incident-runbook templates) and a cross-tenant channel-claim bot that automates Confluence space seeding and a matching Jira project.

ISSUE SUMMARY: Support requests temporary, minimized extract of inference traces for a regulated payment dispute. The export must contain only cryptographic hashes (SHA-256 hex) of request/response blobs plus minimal metadata (timestamp, model_id, route_id, obfuscated_client_id). No plaintext prompts, completions, KV cache contents, or raw customer identifiers may be included.

IMPACT: Legal and Payments teams need a verifiable hexdigest to correlate an external payment reference with an internal processing trace. Customer privacy and compliance require zero plaintext exposure.

ENVIRONMENT: prod - us-east (hosted + dedicated edge routing active during window).

REQUEST DETAILS:
- Provide a timebound (48 hour access window) export scoped to 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z..2026-03-01T06:00:00Z for the specified payment transaction IDs list (provided to Security out-of-band).
- Export format: CSV or newline-delimited JSON where each row contains: sha256_hex(request_blob), sha256_hex(response_blob), event_timestamp, model_id, route_id, obfuscated_client_id (one-way salted hash).
- Salt policy: per-customer ephemeral salt derived from KMS-protected secret; salts are never to be stored in plaintext; provide proof of rotation and KMS audit events.
- Delivery: KMS-wrapped file in ephemeral S3 bucket with 7-day auto-delete and restricted cross-account access; copy to Legal bucket only after two-person approval recorded in audit logs.

JUSTIFICATION: Finance is contesting a charge and needs non-reversible correlation evidence that does not expose PII. A hash-only extract satisfies evidence requirements while preserving customer privacy.

DATA MINIMIZATION & RISK MITIGATION:
- No full request/response or token-level data will be exported.
- Hash algorithm: SHA-256 with per-customer salt; include the hashing algorithm and salt derivation method in the audit record.
- Include an attestation manifest describing what was excluded and verification steps used.

ACCESS CONTROLS REQUESTED:
- Two-person control for unlocking KMS-wrapped salts (security + legal approvers).
- Timebound IAM role scoped to this export job only.
- Full audit trail (who, when, KMS decrypt logs, S3 access).

TIMELINE: Need approval within 72 hours if possible; export job estimated runtime ~15 minutes once query approved.

DELIVERABLES WANTED:
- Signed approval from Security and Legal recorded in this ticket.
- Link to ephemeral S3 object and KMS audit events when export completes.

Additional notes:
Identified relevant tables: inference_events (sharded), kv_cache_refs (separate store). Important to avoid kv_cache joins to prevent accidental materialization of prompt fragments.
Prototype approach: stream selected events through an AWS Lambda that normalizes JSON (stable key ordering) then computes SHA-256 for request and response blobs. Output schema will be minimal. Estimated cost negligible for 6 records, but design must scale for larger batches.
Security concerns: potential for hash correlation attacks if salt is weak; recommend per-customer KMS-derived salt with HMAC(key, customer_id) where key is KMS-wrapped and never exposed. Provide KMS audit logs as proof of operation.
Related infra change: small PR to add 'hashed_trace_export' job to infra repo (gh:infra/hashed-trace-export#342). Needs 2 reviewers from SRE and Security before merge.
Query risk assessment: confirmed that query plan will not read from raw S3 buckets containing plaintext; all reads will be from canonical event store with fields restricted to blobs for hashing only.
Security: review and approve KMS key policy and two-person unlock flow (Asha).
Legal: confirm final attestation language and accept hashed artifacts as evidence (Legal lead).
Engineering: land infra PR and run dry-run smoke test against staging with synthetic data (Liam).
On approval: run export, upload KMS-wrapped file to ephemeral S3, attach KMS audit logs to this ticket, record two-person signoff, and deliver to Legal.
pending - awaiting Security + Legal two-person approval. No export performed yet. Engineering prototype ready and gated on approval.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Users who submit a self-service access request for internal tools receive the approval email and click the ephemeral approval link, but their account is not fully provisioned and they remain without console roles or session tokens.

Impact:
Several internal teams (approx 8 engineers reported so far) cannot complete just-in-time provisioning after manager approval. Affected users see a successful approval screen but subsequent attempts to open the console return 403 or a blank onboarding flow. This is blocking day-of-oncall rotations for a small set of teams but is not widespread.

Environment:
prod-us-east; SCIM provisioning pipeline + Okta JIT integration + internal runbook provisioner. Device-trust enforced for affected org units.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Requestor submits access request via support portal and selects manager for approval.
2) Manager receives approval email and clicks ephemeral approval link.
3) Approval is recorded in approval service and approval webhook fires to provisioning pipeline.
4) Provisioning service attempts to read SCIM profile but fails to reconcile 'manager' attribute because the manager entry references the requester (circular reference).
5) Provisioner marks job SUCCESS on approval webhook but does not attach RBAC roles or emit session tokens.
6) User attempts console login and gets 403 / missing roles.

Observed logs / snippets:
- provisioner (INFO) "approval received: request_id=abc123, manager_id=U-207"
- scim-sync (WARN) "manager attribute unresolved: manager=U-207 -> targets requester U-207 (circular)"
- runbook-service (INFO) "provision job completed but role_attach_count=0"
- browser: 403 JSON {"message":"no roles assigned"}

Temporary workaround:
Support can manually trigger a role attachment for the user via the admin runbook ("AttachMissingRoles") or create a one-off SCIM patch that clears the manager attribute then re-run provisioning. Both are manual and risky for scale.

Requested outcome:
1) Prevent approval webhooks from marking provisioning as complete when role attachment fails.
2) Add detection for circular manager references in SCIM reconcile and escalate to a manual provisioning queue rather than completing silently.
3) Ensure a compensating automated retry path once manager attribute is resolved.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:22 SRE-Team (via #support): Observed a spike of provisioner 'role_attach_count=0' entries between 2026-03-09T22:00 and 2026-03-10T02:00 UTC correlated with a SCIM import job. Investigating import delta list.
Initial hypothesis: recent SCIM import transformation started populating manager attribute with external id that resolves back to the same SCIM entry, creating a circular manager->reportee mapping.
Reproduced in staging by seeding SCIM fixture where user.u_id == user.manager_u_id; provisioner checks manager and calls profile lookup which returns same uid leading to role attach path skipping.
Confirmed provisioner logic treats unresolved manager as non-fatal and continues, but downstream role-attachment code expects manager to be a distinct identity for device-trust flows and short-circuits when manager == requester.
Slack thread: #support -> https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0SUPPORT/p167857 (internal).
Observed related SCIM delta job: scim-import/2026-03-09-22:03 had a transform rule (mapping: manager = externalId lookup) introduced in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ident-sync/pull/412 which may be the regression.
Added staged validation to scim-sync that flags circular manager links and moves record to manual-review queue.
Triage in progress; fix gated on deploy of scim validation and provisioner fail-fast changes. Manual runbook available as interim.
If scim validation confirms circular manager refs, automated import should mark record for human review and not mark provision job complete. Once PR merged, will monitor for recurrence for 72h.
Code review and merge provisioner fail-fast PR in staging and run canary import against a limited delta set.
Add pre-import unit in ident-sync transforms to detect manager==self and reject/flag records.
Create an automated remediation job that clears manager on transient circularity and retries provisioning with audit log.
payload.summary: Self-service access approvals accepted but account provisioning stalls due to circular SCIM manager attribute

payload.description:
Issue summary:
HR has flagged inconsistent behavior when adding late hires to SCIM-managed groups during remote onboarding, and paired that with several late hardware handoffs where asset tagging/KMS key ownership didn't align with our normal workflow. This ticket tracks clarifying the SCIM sync semantics, documenting the expected group membership propagation window, and defining an explicit temporary-asset handoff policy for remote hires who receive equipment after initial account provisioning.

Impact:
- New hires (remote) occasionally arrive after initial account creation and are added manually to groups; sometimes they miss automatic group-provisioned SAML roles for 24+ hours.
- Asset ownership in the asset inventory sometimes records the hiring manager as owner instead of the employee for KMS-wrapped devices when assignment occurs post-provisioning, creating audit gaps.
- HR and IT teams are asking for a short, documented process to reduce repeated rework and avoid privileges being out-of-sync.

Goal:
1) Confirm actual SCIM propagation window and whether re-sync is triggered on manual console changes (vs SCIM push).
2) Propose a documented temporary-asset-handoff flow for remote hires who receive equipment after account creation, including required KMS transfer steps and ticketing preconditions.
3) Update runbooks and automation where feasible to reduce manual steps.

Desired deliverables:
- Short KB entry (for HR/IT) describing expected timeline and manual steps.
- Small automation playbook for reconciling group membership within 2 hours of manual addition.
- Decision on whether KMS key ownership change should be automated or a manual ticketed step.

Relevant constraints:
- Changes must preserve audit trail and not bypass HSM/KMS policies.
- Any automation needs security review before production roll-out.

1) Create onboarding account via HR system (SCIM provision) for new remote employee
2) Wait for scheduled SCIM sync (15m polling window), confirm group membership assigned
3) If equipment arrives late, IT manually updates asset inventory and tags device; observe KMS metadata differs from account owner
4) Manually add user to console groups; note delay for role-capabilities to appear in the user's session or need for forced re-login
2026-03-06: Spun up debug logs on SCIM connector. Observed successful SCIM push to identity provider; identity provider shows group change but downstream RBAC refresh appears tied to session TTL (~1h).
2026-03-08: Asset inventory export shows ~12% of late-assigned devices recorded with manager as owner; cross-reference with provisioning tickets shows manual asset assignment correlates with off-hour operations (outside 9-5 PT).
Hypothesis: RBAC role bindings are applied by the console via a cache that refreshes on session start or periodic job; manual group changes require reauth for immediate effect. Asset ownership drift appears linked to asset tagging process using manager email when employee account has 'not yet confirmed' status.
Aisha Patel (Reporter) - 2026-03-05: HR flagged three hires last month where roles were incomplete for first-day access. They want a clear checklist for late-supply scenarios.
Marco Chen (Assignee) - 2026-03-06: I'm running the SCIM connector logs and will validate whether changes are pushed immediately or batched. Tentatively planning a short automation that triggers a role refresh when a manual group change is detected.
Lina Roberts (Security) - 2026-03-07: Any automation that triggers role refresh or KMS key changes will need an approval path. We must log the actor who initiated KMS ownership transfer and ensure HSM audit events remain intact.
