payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple new-hire workstations failed Autopilot enrollment during provisioning. Devices repeatedly timed out at the network registration step and did not receive MDM enrollment. Impact: 9 new hires across two cohorts were delayed from completing onboarding (approx. 6–10 minute timeouts per device), increasing manual imaging work by IT ops. Environment: Production Autopilot provisioning in us-west region; affected both docked and undocked laptops attached to the same dock model. Observed on Dell Latitude 7440 and Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Gen5 that use the CalDigit TS4-equivalent A/B dock (vendor-supplied).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect laptop to vendor Thunderbolt dock and PXE/boot into Windows Autopilot OOBE.
2) Proceed with network connectivity and allow Autopilot to reach enrollment endpoint.
3) Observe enrollment hang during device registration/network handshake stage; event viewer shows repeated DHCP/Nic errors.

Logs and evidence:
- DHCP server logs show multiple requests using identical MAC address for different ports/hosts.
- Windows SetupDiag capture shows "Network adapter initialization failed" and retry loop.
- Netsh show interfaces on one affected laptop reported MAC 00:16:3E:XX:XX:XX matching another laptop in the same bay.
- Packet capture attached to linked Confluence doc (see page) with ARP duplication and DHCP ACKs being delivered to wrong host.

Initial mitigation applied:
- IT Ops instructed onboarding team to provision devices undocked on wired network to avoid dock-induced duplication. This allowed enrollment to complete for 7/9 devices.
- For the remaining 2 devices, USB-Ethernet adapters bypassed the dock NIC and succeeded.

Business impact and urgency: Blocking new hire onboarding and causing increased manual imaging time; prioritized P1 due to operational impact and reproducibility.
2026-03-10 09:40 - Initial triage by IT Ops: confirmed timing pattern, observed identical MAC addresses across two devices attached to same dock cluster.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Reproduced locally in lab: attaching two laptops to the same dock resulted in both reporting the same MAC on the host OS after hot-plug sequence.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:00 - Confirmed DHCP server logs show lease offers granted but ARP resolution conflicts caused retransmits and network stack retries in Windows OOBE.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Vendor engagement: CalDigit-esque vendor support escalated; vendor reproduced issue internally and identified firmware build 1.8.4 as shipping regression that introduced MAC cloning across Thunderbolt ports when using chain-docking firmware.
2026-03-11 12:15 - Workaround validated: disabling dock NIC using dock management utility or using undocked/wired provisioning prevents duplicate MAC behavior and allows Autopilot enrollment to proceed.
2026-03-11 16:40 - Risk assessment: If left unaddressed, bulk provisioning events in open-office labs will be impacted; also causes intermittent network connectivity and inventory inaccuracies in network management system.
2026-03-12 08:10 - Root cause: Faulty dock firmware (1.8.4) that incorrectly applied a static MAC template across multiple dock units when in daisy-chain mode.
Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Two new-hire cohorts hit this during morning provisioning. I moved most to undocked provisioning but wanted a ticket so we can identify the root cause and stop future churn.
Liam Chen (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Thanks Aisha — collecting DHCP and pcap dumps. Please keep any affected docks isolated for vendor repro. Assigning to Hardware Ops and Network to assist.
Network Team (Emily Rao) 2026-03-10: Confirmed duplicate MACs in DHCP logs. Switch ports show ARP flaps. Tagged as high priority on our end.
Hardware Vendor (CalDigit Support) 2026-03-11: Reproduced and identified firmware regression. Preparing hotfix (v1.8.5) for validation. ETA 48 hours for signed build and release notes.
Liam Chen 2026-03-12: Vendor patch validated in lab and signed build deployed to staging. Imaging workflow updated to avoid docking during initial Autopilot OOBE until fleet update completes. Closing incident with remediation steps below.
Aisha Patel 2026-03-12: Confirmed onboardings for the delayed hires completed after undocked provisioning and later device check-in post-dock firmware update. Thanks team.
Root cause: Faulty dock firmware (vendor build v1.8.4) that applied identical MAC addresses across multiple docks in daisy-chain mode, causing DHCP and ARP conflicts during Autopilot enrollment.
Fix applied: Vendor released firmware v1.8.5 that removes MAC cloning behavior and corrects port-specific MAC assignment. Firmware pushed to affected dock units in office via Dock Management Utility (DMT).
Workaround applied: For immediate onboarding events, provision devices undocked on wired NIC or use USB-Ethernet adapter until dock firmware is updated.
Config/Process changes: Added a pre-provision checklist step — "disconnect dock during Autopilot OOBE" — to IT onboarding runbook. Updated provisioning playbook in Confluence and created PR to provisioning repo to add a detection flag for duplicate MACs (see related PR).
Follow-ups: (1) Hardware Ops to perform mass firmware rollout to all office docks by 2026-03-18. (2) Inventory to tag affected dock serials and track post-upgrade stability (INT-41260). (3) Network to monitor DHCP/ARP error rate for two weeks post rollout (INT-41302).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple engineers reported laptops failing to remain suspended overnight. Machines appear to enter suspend but then immediately wake (10-30s) and stay on. This is impacting developer workstations and our overnight build agents on Framework Laptop 13 devices.

Observed scope: Reports started 2026-02-28; ~7 confirmed devices in Engineering and Infra teams. Problem is intermittent but reproducible on affected firmware revisions.

Business impact: Developer disruption, increased power usage for remote workers, flaky CI runners that rely on suspend for power management. Not customer-facing but affects SRE/dev productivity.
~7 developer machines + 2 runner hosts observed; increases power drain and causes processes that expect long suspend to fail. No data loss reported. Priority elevated due to CI runner disruption.
1) Boot Framework Laptop 13 with stock Redwood engineer image (ubuntu-22.04-custom) and firmware EC v1.1.3.
2) Leave machine idle for 5 minutes, then trigger system suspend (systemctl suspend) or close lid.
3) Observe that the machine wakes after ~10-30s and remains active. Reopening lid is not required for wake event.
4) Check ACPI events and journalctl logs for wake source.
Mar 01 08:12:45 workstation-019 kernel: PM: suspend entry (deep)
Mar 01 08:12:55 workstation-019 kernel: wakeup source: LID (EC) - event 0x23
Mar 01 08:12:55 workstation-019 systemd[1]: Started User Manager for UID 1001.
Mar 01 08:12:55 workstation-019 kernel: ACPI: Lid Switch (PECI) reported open -> closed (value 0x1)
Mar 01 08:12:56 workstation-019 kernel: PM: Device X triggered wakeup: gpio-ioexpander-ec:gpio13
Initial triage (2026-03-01): Reproduced locally on a test Framework 13 with EC firmware v1.1.3. Suspected EC/lid debounce logic introduced in recent firmware change.
Cross-check: Identical image on Lenovo X1 and Dell Precision reproduced no wake behavior, pointing to vendor EC firmware as common factor.
/proc/acpi/button/lid/LID/state showed rapid toggling in the short suspend window on affected machines; wakeup source consistently reports EC GPIO pin.
Tried kernel parameter 'acpi_osi=' and 'acpi_enforce_resources=lax' — no change. Disabling autosuspend for USB devices did not affect behavior.
Infra tried imaging latest nightly (ubuntu-24.04-beta) — still reproduced with EC v1.1.3. Suggests not an OS regression.
Contacted vendor (Framework) support and opened internal Slack thread #it-support; vendor acknowledged a known EC debounce regression in v1.1.3 and provided EC v1.1.5 candidate.
Vendor provided test EC firmware v1.1.5 addressing lid-debounce and pin state reporting. Applied to two test devices; neither exhibited spur wakes after multiple suspend cycles.
Risk assessment: Firmware update touches EC; packaged deployment to all engineers should be scheduled with consent and backup steps.
Applied vendor test EC firmware v1.1.5 to two affected laptops (Priya N). Performed 20 suspend/resume cycles overnight — no unexpected wakes.
Temporarily applied workaround for affected CI runners: set 'HandleLidSwitch=ignore' and mask systemd-logind suspend triggers to prevent flaky wake affecting jobs.
Notified Engineering via #it-support with detection script to list EC firmware versions (script attached in Slack).
Prepared step-by-step EC flash runbook and rollback instructions. Added check to asset DB to flag devices running v1.1.3.
Opened internal GitHub PR to include EC firmware v1.1.5 in our provisioning image build: https://github.com/redwood-inference/firmware-updates/pull/128
Root cause: EC firmware v1.1.3 on Framework Laptop 13 has a debounce/regression causing spurious lid open/close events during suspend, triggering wakeups. Fix: vendor-supplied EC firmware v1.1.5 corrects debounce behavior.

Resolution steps: Applied v1.1.5 to affected machines and rolled out a staged firmware update to remaining flagged devices (opt-in schedule for developers). Updated provisioning image to include v1.1.5. Workaround (HandleLidSwitch=ignore) used for CI runners until firmware applied. Ticket closed after 48 hours of stable verification on updated devices.

Additional notes:
2026-03-02 08:47 - Vendor (Framework Support): Confirmed issue on v1.1.3; provided v1.1.5 candidate. Asked for test results.
payload.summary: Intermittent wake-from-suspend on Framework Laptop 13 due to lid sensor firmware misreporting

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During routine depot repair of several Lenovo units (replacement of M.2 Wi-Fi module), devices enter a provisioning stall on first boot. The provisioning-agent never completes Intune enrollment and the corporate VPN profile fails to push. Devices remain in a limited state: local login works, but corporate policies/patching and VPN are missing, blocking sign-in to internal apps.

Impact:
- Affects small batch of recently repaired machines (3 reported so far) from depot team.
- Blocks end-user access to internal resources until manual remediation.
- Potentially increases repair turnaround time if left undetected.

Environment:
- Depot staging lab (imaging/provisioning flow).
- Windows 11 23H2 build; provisioning-agent v2.4.1; Intune Company Portal version 5.8.0; VPN client: Palo Alto GlobalProtect 6.1.3.
- Hardware: mostly Lenovo M.2 Wi-Fi Module replacements (Intel AX201 → Intel AX211 variants), some devices with vendor firmware mismatch.

Observed behaviour and symptoms:
- During post-repair OOBE/check-in, provisioning logs show repeated failures to apply VPN profile with HTTP 404 from Intune device configuration endpoint.
- local logs indicate NIC persistent naming changed (old NIC GUID persisted in registry, new NIC got a new GUID). Intune seems to look up device network adapter by ID cached earlier in provisioning script.
- If the device is booted without network (airplane mode), the provisioning-agent times out waiting for the expected adapter and aborts enrollment.

Initial theory:
- M.2 Wi-Fi replacement combined with firmware/driver differences is resulting in adapter GUID/instance ID changes. The depot imaging scripts (legacy step) reference the original NIC identity for tagging and early Intune bind operations. When that lookup fails, subsequent steps that push VPN/device policies skip or error.

Perform M.2 Wi-Fi module replacement on Lenovo device (swap AX201 → AX211)
Boot device into depot imaging OOBE and let provisioning-agent start automated enrollment
Observe provisioning-agent logs / Company Portal output: check for Intune enrollment success/failure
Check registry HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Network\{GUID} for old vs new adapter instance ids
Attempt manual Intune sync from Company Portal and check MDM diagnostic logs
Excerpt from provisioning-agent.log (2026-03-10 09:12:03):
[ERROR] lookupAdapterById: adapter 'PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_XXXX' not found for expected-id 'NIC-7a3f-2b1c'
[IntuneClient] ApplyDeviceConfiguration 404 Not Found (device-binding failed)
[INFO] provisioning-agent: fallback retry in 30s (attempt 3/3)

System event log: Network Adapter Instance ID changed from '{NIC-7a3f-2b1c}' to '{NIC-94bc-ef01}' after driver install'
Reproduced locally in depot lab with Lenovo X1 Carbon: replacing AX201 with AX211 reproduced provisioning failure consistently (3/3).
Driver/firmware mismatch observed: AX211 shipped with firmware v1.2.0; depot imaging image includes AX201 drivers which trigger adapter instance rename on driver install.
Provisioning pipeline contains an older helper script that binds VPN profile using hardcoded adapter instance id stored in device metadata during OEM depot tagging step (legacy behaviour).
Intune APIs returning 404 because device object in our device registry was created without the new adapter identifier; agent tries to POST to device-specific endpoint constructed using old id.
No indications of upstream Intune outage — isolated to devices with adapter GUID change.
Manual remediation: Windows admin can force Intune re-enrollment (Settings → Access work or school → Disconnect → Enroll) and run Company Portal sync. This restores policies and VPN profile.
Apply a short-lived PowerShell helper on depot: regenerate NIC mapping by running 'Get-NetAdapter | New-GuidRemapScript' and re-run provisioning-agent hooks.
If VPN is still missing, reinstall GlobalProtect after Intune policy sync (order matters).
Legacy depot tagging and provisioning helper scripts rely on a NIC instance identifier recorded at time of OEM tagging. Post-repair M.2 Wi-Fi swaps change the adapter instance id and the provisioning flow lacks a resilient lookup, causing Intune binding to fail.
Implemented a short-term depot-side fix: updated the imaging pre-provision script to detect adapter instance changes and use a network-agnostic lookup path (match by MAC OUI + driver signature) to bind the device record. Deployed new helper (provision-fix-v1) to depot-staging on 2026-03-12.

Operational remediation steps performed:
- Deployed updated script to depot staging images.
- Reprocessed the three affected devices with updated script — all three successfully completed Intune enrollment and received VPN profile.
- Created a follow-up task to upstream the change into baseline image and add unit tests to depot CI.

Patch baseline imaging image with provision-fix-v1 and include AX211 drivers to avoid instance renames post-driver install (Owner: Depot Eng, due 2026-03-19)
Add a post-repair verification step in depot runbook to run Intune sanity check (check Company Portal MDM status and VPN profile), update repo runbook (Owner: SRE-Endpoint)
Audit depot spare-part firmware versions and create gating rule to refuse module swaps if firmware mismatch detected (Owner: HW Ops)
Add telemetry for adapter-instance-change events to provisioning logs so detection is automated (Owner: Provisioning Team)
Create KB for field repair techs describing manual remediation steps and link to to Confluence page

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:12 — SRE Endpoint (Lucas Wong): Temporary guidance added to depot-runbook: run 'ds-regenerate-mdm' after swap and before imaging. This is a manual stopgap until we push an automated fix.
payload.summary: Provisioning stalls after M.2 Wi-Fi replacement: persistent NIC rename prevents Intune check-in and VPN profile application

payload.description:
Issue summary:
CLI users who authenticate with client certificates are able to establish a session after last week's Okta identity migration, but their effective RBAC scopes are truncated (missing several delegated groups). Affected users see 403s when calling the runbook and deploy APIs even though their principal is authenticated.

Impact:
- Several infra engineers cannot run elevated runbooks or deploy to staging/production from CLI.
- Blocker for oncall rota: runbook elevation and emergency deploys.

Environment:
- Production, us-west region.
- CLI auth path uses client-cert -> sso-proxy -> identity-mapper -> rbac-service.

Observed symptoms:
- Successful client-cert TLS handshake and SSO assertion exchange.
- RBAC tokens returned with missing delegated group claims (group list truncated to first 2 entries).
- Console web login for same users functions normally.

Discovery timeline:
- 2026-03-10 08:45 reporter alerted #support about failed runbook run.
- 2026-03-10 09:10 SRE confirmed certificate authentication step succeeded but authorization failed.
- 2026-03-11 engineers correlated with Okta identity migration performed 2026-03-09 23:00 which introduced new session issuer TTL and claim encoding.
- 2026-03-12 quick workaround deployed (client-cert rebind script) restored access for a subset of users.

1) Use pre-migration client cert/profile (or new cert) to run: rw-cli login --cert /path/to/cert.pem
2) Confirm rw-cli reports 'Authenticated as <user@example.com>'
3) Run a restricted command that requires delegated runbook access: rw-cli runbook execute --id emergency-db-rollback
4) Observe 403: 'insufficient_scope' despite authenticated principal
5) Inspect /var/log/sso-proxy/auth.log for the auth flow and identity-mapper logs for claim set.
Authenticated CLI sessions should receive the full set of delegated group claims and be authorized against runbook/deploy endpoints the same as console/web sessions.
Client-cert authentication completes but the downstream identity-mapper returns a truncated groups array (only first two groups), causing RBAC to deny elevated operations.
[2026-03-10T09:11:02Z] sso-proxy: tls: client certificate verified: subject=CN=eng-alice@example.com
[2026-03-10T09:11:02Z] sso-proxy: exchanged assertion with idp, assertion-issuer=okta, assertion-id=0a1b2c
[2026-03-10T09:11:03Z] identity-mapper: mapped principal alice@example.com, groups=[infra-oncall, infra-deploy] (expected 8 groups)
[2026-03-10T09:11:03Z] rbac-service: authorization denied for alice@example.com on runbook: missing required group infra-runbooks-admin -> 403 insufficient_scope
Aisha Kapoor (reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed first customer-facing unblock case; affected user had valid cert and previously working CLI flow.
Diego Morales (assignee) - 2026-03-10: Initial triage - authentication succeeds, looks like an identity claim population issue between identity-mapper and rbac-service. Pulling logs and checking Okta migration notes.
SRE-Team (channel #sre) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed Okta migration changed assertion 'groups' encoding from JSON array to comma-delimited string for assertions issued by the new pool. Identity-mapper had no handling for the new shape in CLI flow.
Identity (PR author) - 2026-03-12: Raised PR to identity-mapper to normalize group claim to array and added defensive parsing. Deployed to staging for validation.
Diego Morales - 2026-03-12: Deployed a hotfix to identity-mapper in prod: parse both array and comma-delimited strings. Partial restoration observed. Follow-up: audit tokens older than migration window for stale encoded sessions.
Oncall-Eng (alice@example.com) - 2026-03-12: Verified workaround (rw-cli cert-rebind) rebinds a new session and regained runbook access. Logged steps in the ticket.
Hypothesis: Okta migration changed claim serialization for group attributes in the assertion issuer pool used by CLI certificates (pool-id: okta-cli-pool-09).
Confirmed that web/OIDC flow uses a different assertion path that still returns group as an array, which explains why console users are unaffected.
Identity-mapper library v1.3.2 assumes groups claim is JSON array; v1.3.2 used by sso-proxy in CLI path did not attempt to coerce string -> array.
Telemetry: ~14 distinct engineers hit the failure between 2026-03-09 23:30 and 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC. Peak impact window aligns with migration cutover.
Risk: Some long-lived CLI sessions still have legacy assertion shape; token refresh path must be addressed to avoid recurrence.
Related config: Okta assertion mapping change documented in internal changelog: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/okta-migrations/2026-03-09
Workaround: instructed affected engineers to run 'rw-cli cert-rebind' which forces a fresh assertion exchange and results in normalized group claim. Hotfix: identity-mapper parsing change deployed to prod (2026-03-12) to accept both array and comma-delimited group claims. Full fix scheduled to add schema validation + unit tests in identity-mapper release v1.3.3.
1) Add assertion shape validation to identity-mapper and reject/alert on unexpected shapes (owner: Identity Team, due 2026-03-18).
2) Backfill short-lived session refresh to normalize claims for active CLI sessions (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-17).
3) Add automated e2e test for CLI cert flow that validates group claim mapping across Okta pools (owner: QA, due 2026-03-20).
4) Postmortem draft linking to Okta migration notes and mitigation steps (owner: Diego Morales, due 2026-03-19).
payload.summary: CLI certificate login fails with limited RBAC after Okta identity migration

payload.description:
Issue summary:
After the identity-proxy release v2.3.0, the session cookie used by the internal oncall runner CLI is being truncated to a shorter path (e.g. /api) which causes the runner to lose the web SSO session when attempting elevated commands.

Impact:
- On-call engineers cannot run elevated infra commands via the internal 'runner' CLI without being redirected to re-auth.
- Affects all environments in us-west where identity-proxy v2.3.0 is deployed.
- Interrupts incident response workflows; workarounds are non-obvious and increase time-to-resolution.

Environment:
- prod us-west cluster running identity-proxy v2.3.0 and oncall-runner 1.7.2
- Affected users are primarily SSO-authenticated employees on the enterprise org.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login to the web console as an SSO user (okta) and verify session is active.
2) On terminal, run: runner run --elevate --target=infra-node-01
3) CLI issues a request to /api/runner/elevate and receives a 302 redirect to /sso/authorize with query error=session_mismatch
4) Runner falls into reauth loop; no token is produced.

Observed logs / error messages:
- ingress-auth (identity-proxy) logs: "cookie path mismatch: expected='/' actual='/api'"
- runner CLI: "error: SSO session missing or invalid (status 302)"
- browser developer console: cookie set by identity-proxy has Path=/api and SameSite=Lax

Notes: This is not affecting basic web console sessions; only endpoints that rely on cookie path crossing between / and /api.
Initial hypothesis: recent cookie-path handling change in identity-proxy caused path to be set to request path instead of root.
Findings:
- Reproduced on staging by deploying identity-proxy v2.3.0; identical symptoms.
- identity-proxy change log shows commit that attempted to tighten cookie scope for API routes (commit 9b7c4f).
- Debugging identity-proxy session-store revealed a truncation in the cookie serializer when cookie metadata exceeded 128 bytes; path value fell back to request.Path which was '/api'.
- Okta SSO flow sends original redirect to /sso/callback which expects cookie with Path='/' to be attached to subsequent subrequests. With Path='/api' cookie is not presented for CLI elevation flows routed at /.
- Confirmed runner CLI works when identity-proxy downgraded to v2.2.9.
Evidence and links:
- identity-proxy logs: /var/log/identity-proxy/2026-02-28.log (lines with cookie-write events)
- Reproducer: staging cluster deployment rollout #2026-02-28-18:42
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/12890 (cookie scoping change)

Workarounds tested:
- runner login --web (opens browser flow and writes local token) — works for temporary access but not ideal for scripted runbooks.
- Manually setting REDWOOD_RUNNER_COOKIE_PATH=/ in identity-proxy env on a canary host — allowed normal flow for that host.

Additional notes:
SRE (J. Nguyen) (2026-03-01): Deployed identity-proxy v2.3.1 to a 10% canary with patched cookie serializer; canary shows cookies Path='/' and runner flows succeed.
Oncall (L. Martínez) (2026-03-01): Using runner login --web as short-term workaround. Requesting timeline for full rollout and session invalidation guidance.
Temporary workaround: instruct on-call to use 'runner login --web' or deploy identity-proxy to a local canary with REDWOOD_RUNNER_COOKIE_PATH=/ until patch is rolled out.
Permanent fix: revert the cookie-scoping change and update the serializer to avoid the 128-byte truncation; increase buffer and explicitly set Path='/' for SSO session cookies.
Action taken:
- PR #12912 merged to identity-proxy that fixes serializer and enforces Path='/' for SSO cookies.
- identity-proxy v2.3.1 rolled to prod canary 2026-03-01, full rollout completed 2026-03-02 03:10 UTC.
- Sessions: expired SSO cookies for affected hosts and forced a fresh login to ensure consistent cookie shape (communicated to staff via #oncall).
Follow-up / next steps:
- Postmortem to be drafted and linked to this ticket (owner: Marco Chen) due 2026-03-09.
- Add unit tests for cookie serializer and add integration test covering CLI elevation flows.
- Update runbook with guidance for cookie-path-related incidents and include a checklist for identity-proxy rollouts.
payload.summary: Internal runner SSO session cookie path truncated, blocks elevated CLI commands

payload.description:
Background
- We are shipping cross-language SDK parity updates (Python/TS/Go) for auth precedence, retries/backoff, timeout model, streaming disconnect semantics, and error taxonomy.
- Support is currently using a mix of older macros and ad-hoc questions, which is contributing to slower triage and inconsistent guidance.
- Related: INT-1182 (request_id not visible in SDK errors) is being addressed by SDK changes, but we still need the support workflow updated.

Request
Update Zendesk/Support macros and the internal troubleshooting runbook so that:
1) We ask for the correct minimum set of info (SDK + version, request_id, timeout/retry config, streaming vs non-streaming).
2) Guidance aligns with new standardized option names and defaults (retryable codes, Retry-After behavior, backoff/jitter, overall vs connect/read timeouts).
3) We include streaming-specific guidance (safe retry recommendations, idempotency, partial output expectations).
4) We do not request/collect secrets and we reinforce redaction requirements.

Scope
- Macros to update/add:
  A) "SDK retry/timeout - initial info request" (customer-facing)
  B) "SDK streaming disconnect troubleshooting" (customer-facing)
  C) "SDK 429 / rate limit guidance" (customer-facing)
  D) "Internal triage checklist - SDK failures" (internal note)

Proposed macro content (draft)

A) Customer macro: SDK retry/timeout initial info request
---
To help us diagnose this quickly, could you reply with:
1) Which SDK and version? (Python / TypeScript / Go, e.g. redwood==X.Y.Z)
2) Is this streaming or non-streaming? If streaming, which endpoint/method are you using?
3) A Redwood request_id from a failed attempt (from the error message, response headers, or logs).
4) The approximate timestamp (with timezone) and region where the request was sent.
5) Your configured timeouts and retries (if set):
   - overall timeout (ms or seconds)
   - connect/read timeouts (if your SDK exposes them)
   - max attempts / retry count
   - any custom retryable status codes
6) The HTTP status code(s) observed (e.g., 429/500/502/504) and whether you see a Retry-After header on 429.
7) Any proxy/VPN/corporate network details if applicable (streaming issues often correlate with proxy buffering/timeouts).

Please do NOT paste API keys or bearer tokens. If you share logs, please redact secrets.
---

B) Customer macro: Streaming disconnect troubleshooting
---
For streaming requests, a few extra details help:
1) Are you seeing a disconnect mid-stream (partial output) or no output at all?
2) Is the client behind a corporate proxy or gateway that may buffer/terminate long-lived connections?
3) What is the streaming read/overall timeout configured on the client?
4) If you retry streaming, are you using an idempotency key / request de-duplication strategy? (We generally recommend being conservative with retries for streaming to avoid duplicated side effects.)

If you can share a request_id from the stream attempt (or the last successful event before the disconnect), we can trace it end-to-end.
---

C) Customer macro: 429 / rate limit guidance
---
A 429 indicates you are being rate-limited.
- If the response includes Retry-After, the SDK should respect it by default (newer SDK versions).
- Recommended next steps:
  1) Share the request_id from the 429 response.
  2) Confirm SDK version and whether retries are enabled.
  3) If you run high concurrency, consider lowering parallelism or adding client-side jitter.

If you’re on Dedicated capacity and still seeing sustained 429s, we’ll check capacity/limits for your org.
---

D) Internal note: triage checklist
- Capture: customer tier, workload type (chat/completions/embeddings), streaming yes/no, region.
- Ask for request_id and confirm it’s from the failing attempt (not a successful one).
- Verify SDK version is on or after the parity releases (if not, recommend upgrade + link migration notes).
- Confirm configured timeouts (overall/connect/read). Watch for:
  - overall timeout too low for long prompts/streams
  - streaming read timeout not wired (older versions)
- Confirm retry configuration:
  - ensure no retries on 4xx other than 408/409/429 (per standard)
  - confirm Retry-After handling on 429
- If symptoms suggest retry storm: ask for retry_count / max_attempts, and coordinate with SRE.

Acceptance criteria
- Updated macros published in Zendesk (or equivalent) and linked from the Support runbook.
- Runbook page includes the standardized question set + links to:
  - SDK migration notes (auth/retry/timeout)
  - Retry/timeout standard
  - Auth resolution & secret handling guidance
- Support oncall acknowledges in #support that macros are updated and available.

References
- SDK parity initiative: ENG-5120
- Top support drivers: SUP-29410, SUP-29477, SUP-29505
- Request_id visibility: INT-1182

Issue summary: Several engineers and on-call have reported that when they use the console's 'Switch account' feature after authenticating via Okta SAML, they are immediately redirected back to the Okta login flow or see a 401 in the console even though Okta indicates an active session. This appears to be a session affinity / cookie routing problem that surfaces only when switching between org accounts (cross-account switch) or when requests are routed to different backends behind the auth-proxy.
Multiple internal teams (SRE, Platform, and Support) and on-call users are unable to switch accounts reliably in the console. Breakage affects productivity for engineers who operate across multiple customer accounts and prevents some on-call flows that require quick org switching. Estimated ~15-25% of cross-account switch attempts fail during the regression window.
1) Login to console via Okta SAML in Chrome (prod-us-west)
2) From the top-right, choose 'Switch account' -> select a different org (owned by the same user)
3) Observe console goes to Okta and then returns either to a blank console screen or shows '401 Unauthorized' in the network tab
4) Check cookies: auth-session cookie value differs before and after switch; RelayState is present but new session is created on different backend
5) Repeat in incognito or after clearing cookies -> behavior changes (sometimes works).
- auth-proxy logs (2026-03-10 09:12:43 UTC): 'saml: assertion accepted; session_id=abc123; backend=grpc-7'
- shortly after (09:12:44 UTC): 'request: /switch-account -> routed to grpc-3; cookie lookup failed; creating ephemeral session def=tmp-9'
- browser console: XHR /api/v1/auth/session -> 401 (invalid_session)
- haproxy logs show differing server selection for subsequent requests from same client IP during the switch operation
During a deploy (2026-03-09 23:00 UTC) the load-balancer sticky session settings were temporarily relaxed to allow rolling restarts. The console's account-switch flow relies on a transient in-memory session reference on the backend (short-lived state keyed to RelayState). If subsequent requests land on a different backend that doesn’t have that ephemeral state, SAML response handling fails and the user is sent back to Okta or receives a 401. Additionally, a SameSite cookie attribute change in a recent auth-proxy PR may make the browser drop the session cookie on the redirect to RelayState under certain conditions.
- Reproduced with engineer Chrome profile (prod-us-west) using devtools; confirmed that RelayState token was posted to different backend node than initial SAML initiate.
- Checked deploy history: auth-proxy rollout 2026-03-09 22:50–23:05 included lb config tweak for draining behavior (PR referenced above).
- Load balancer (HAProxy) metrics show short-term increase in backend selection churn during rollout window.
- Session-store is primarily in-memory with memcache fallback; ephemeral RelayState objects are not persisted to memcached (design choice to reduce latency).
- A/B test altering SameSite=None for auth-session cookie landed in auth-proxy PR #842 which affected Chrome behavior for cross-site POSTs used by RelayState.
- Reproduced failure pattern when auth-session cookie had SameSite=Lax. With SameSite=None the switch succeeds more reliably, but non-sticky routing still breaks when ephemeral RelayState is missing.
- Short-term: instruct affected engineers to open a new browser session (incognito) and perform the switch; this forces a fresh session that completes the flow.
- Admin workaround: disable cross-account quick-switch and perform full logout/login to move accounts.
- On-call note: If a 401 occurs during a critical incident, open console in incognito and perform full SSO to the desired org.
1) Persist RelayState tokens to memcached for 60s so any backend can handle the SAML response. 2) Revert the temporary LB sticky-session relaxation and ensure HAProxy maintain server affinity during auth flows. 3) Adjust auth-session cookie attributes to SameSite=None; secure; samesite flag behavior to be validated across browsers. 4) Add end-to-end integration test that simulates cross-account switch under non-sticky routing and validates RelayState resolution.
- Rolled back the LB drain setting to previous stable behavior at 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC (config rollback).
- Opened PR to persist RelayState to memcached (auth-proxy PR #842) — awaiting code review.
- Temporarily enabled a proxy-level sticky header (x-auth-stick) to force affinity for SAML POST flows (deployed to prod-us-west canary at 2026-03-13 18:30 UTC).
- Notified on-call and SRE via #support and #platform Slack channels with mitigation steps and link to this ticket.

The PR to persist RelayState to memcached (auth-proxy) is in review; once merged we'll schedule a controlled rollout and monitor. The definitive fix will be deployment of memcached-backed RelayState plus SameSite cookie adjustments. After rollout we will run the new e2e test and keep the sticky header as fallback for 72 hours.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During the 2026-03-10 release window we observed an increase in CI job failures that traced to incorrect routing of jobs to unavailable or wrong runners. The root cause appears to be corruption/staleness in the runner label index (the in-memory index used by the CI router to match job labels to runner capabilities).

Impact:
- ~12% of release pipeline jobs in us-east are routed to mismatched runners and fail pre-start health checks, resulting in manual requeues and delayed rollouts.
- Affected pipelines include multiple release branches and a few critical canary flows.

Environment:
- prod (us-east) CI cluster (k8s) running runner-service v3.7.1, ci-router v1.4.0, kvstore (etcd) v3.5

Observed behavior:
- Router returns a candidate runner list that lacks runners with the required label (e.g., "gpu:rtx-a100") or includes runners that have been decommissioned.
- Jobs enter "Pending" state, then fail with "RunnerCapabilityMismatch" or time out waiting for pod binding.
- Manual requeue usually schedules correctly after a short interval (30-90s).

Expected behavior:
- Router should consult fresh index and use up-to-date runner capabilities; decommissioned runners should never be selected.

Steps to reproduce (best-effort):
1) Deploy a synthetic job with label set that matches a small subset of runners (e.g., "pool:release-canary, gpu:rtx-a100").
2) Simultaneously simulate a runner heartbeat gap by temporarily blocking runner-service-to-kvstore writes for ~45s.
3) Observe router candidate selection via debug endpoint (/debug/route) and compare to kvstore state.

Investigation notes:
- Heap snapshots and trace logs show duplicate keys and out-of-order index entries in the in-memory label index within runner-service. Suspect a race during incremental index rebuild when rapid runner heartbeat churn occurs.
- kvstore (etcd) data is correct; corruption is limited to the runner-service process memory index.
- A recent change in ci-router v1.4.0 introduced a quick-sync path that can trigger concurrent label-index merges; timeline aligns with when errors first appeared.
- No signs of disk corruption or network packet loss between services.

Logs and links:
- Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ci/router-health?orgId=1&var-region=us-east
- Trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/7f3a9c0b
- Slack thread: #internal-ci (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0CI12345/p1615567800000)
- Related PR currently under review: github.com/redwood-inference/ci-router/pull/1427

Workaround:
- Restarting runner-service pods in a rolling fashion forces a full index rebuild from kvstore and restores correct routing (temporary).
- Applying a short cooldown on heartbeat fast-syncs reduces incidence but does not fix the underlying race.

Immediate mitigation applied (2026-03-11):
- Scoped rollout: temporarily pinned ci-router to v1.3.9 for prod us-east.
- Added a conservative backoff on heartbeat-triggered index merges in runner-service config to reduce simultaneous merges.

Next steps / remediation plan:
- Engineering to reproduce in staging with a high-churn runner simulator to exercise the merge path. (Owner: Miguel Ortega)
- Add a unit/integration test that simulates concurrent merge operations and ensures index invariants. (Owner: Backend QA)
- Implement an atomic swap update for the in-memory index instead of in-place merges to eliminate the race. Target PR by 2026-03-18.
- Postfix: monitor for recurrence for 72 hours after code rollout; keep the temporary pinned ci-router version until fix validated.

Resolution: (pending)

1) Create a synthetic CI job with a narrow runner label set.
2) Induce runner heartbeat flare by restarting half of the runner pods quickly.
3) Observe routing differences between /debug/route and kvstore entries.

Heap dumps show index entries with duplicate runner IDs under different label buckets. Concurrency window observed at index merge routine path mergeLabels(). Adding mutex reduced occurrence in local repro. Running more exhaustive fuzz tests in staging. Reference trace IDs included in logs_and_links.
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ci/router-health?orgId=1
Trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/7f3a9c0b
Slack: #internal-ci thread link
PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ci-router/pull/1427
Runbook candidate: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CI/Runner+Index+Runbook
Rolling restart of runner-service pods to force full index rebuild; pin ci-router to v1.3.9 in prod us-east; add temporary backoff on heartbeat-triggered merges.
Reproduce in staging with churn simulator; land atomic-swap index update; add regression tests; schedule coordinated rollout with SRE and release engineering.

Additional notes:

2026-03-11 13:22 - QA (Ravi Menon): Spun up staging churn simulator; able to reproduce index duplication ~30% of runs when merges overlap.

Issue summary:
Legal has requested a one-week access window to production inference logs to validate customer data handling claims for an upcoming compliance audit. Due to sensitivity, they require logs to be masked/obfuscated and access to be time-limited and fully audited.

Request details:
- Scope: Inference logs for customer 'Acme Health' (customer data referenced in application traces) from 2026-02-15 to 2026-03-08.
- Required fields: request_id, timestamp, route_id, model_version, input_prompt (masked), decoded tokens removed, output metadata, redaction_flags.
- Prohibitions: No raw PII or raw customer payloads; no unredacted training data identifiers.

Approvals required:
- Security approval (SRE/Infra): ensure masking pipeline and read-only access
- Compliance/Legal: confirm scope and retention
- Product/Data: confirm that requested fields suffice for audit

Audit expectations:
- Access recorded in central audit logs with KMS key ID
- Actions logged to Splunk/Datadog with user and session id
- Access TTL enforced via IAM token expiration

Legal requested masked prod logs dump (not full downloads) for evaluation. Preference for an S3 bucket with object-level SSE-KMS using key redwood-prod-logs-legal. Access must be via temporary IAM role assumed through Okta SAML and limited to group 'legal-audit'. Bucket objects should be pre-masked by the redwood masking lambda with documented mask algorithm.
1) Initial triage by Support (Aisha) to verify scope and escalation path.
2) Eng on-call (Marco) reviewed masking feasibility and confirmed masking lambda exists but needs schema adjustment for new redaction_flags.
3) Security (Priya Patel) requested proof-of-concept of masking on a synthetic sample.
4) Generated masked sample and uploaded to pre-prod private bucket for Legal to preview.
Hypotheses:
- Existing masking pipeline covers common PII but not embedded base64/blobs present in some customer payloads.
- If uncovered, need to extend regex sanitizer and add decoding step for base64 detection.
Findings:
- Sample run found 2% of payloads with nested base64 strings; current sanitizer flagged them but did not decode for inner PII.
- No evidence of model training data exposure.
Links:
- Slack: #support (thread: 2026-03-10 legal-log-access)
- Confluence draft runbook: /confluence/redwood/runbooks/log-masking-procedure
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repos/infrastructure/pull/489
Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-10: Raised by Legal during prep for client audit. Need to preserve minimal context for traceability while removing PII.
Oncall Eng (Marco Silva) 2026-03-11: Reviewed masking lambda. Can add base64 decode stage; estimate 1-2 engineering days to patch and validate in staging.

Issue summary: Several recently returned laptops from depot repair fail Windows Autopilot provisioning because the OS falls back to ACPI battery emulation. Impact: Affected units do not pass Intune compliance checks and remain in a provisioning 'Waiting on device' state; staging pool throughput reduced by ~18% while units are quarantined. Environment: Corporate depot-repaired Dell and HP devices, corp-imaging lab (staging-us-east), Autopilot + Intune + ConfigMgr hybrid enrollment. Steps to reproduce: 1) Apply depot firmware flash image to battery controller during repair (DEPOTFW v1.3.2). 2) Re-image using corp task sequence with latest image (Win11 22H2, corp baseline). 3) On first boot, device reports battery as ACPI 'Unknown' and Windows reports 'Battery information unavailable' in Device Manager. 4) Autopilot enrolment triggers but device stalls on 'Applying device settings' and fails compliance checks. Observed behavior: Battery reports manufacturer id mismatch and Windows falls back to ACPI battery driver; WMI battery classes return inconsistent charge/discharge data. Device does not reach 'Azure AD joined, Intune enrolled' state. Expected behavior: Battery firmware flash should be transparent; OS should report valid battery telemetry and allow Autopilot to complete. Logs/diagnostics collected: eventvwr System and Application logs, MDM enrollment traces, Intune device status snapshots, dump of WMI battery class output, depot repair manifest with battery FW version. One affected serial: SN-REDACTED-001. Relevant artifacts uploaded to internal SMB path and linked below.
Initial triage by support: reproduced failure on two lab units. Hypothesis: depot FW flasher writes incorrect EEDATA battery descriptor causing OS battery driver to choose ACPI fallback. Hardware team confirmed depot tool EXE used v1.3.2 which has new checksum behavior. Imaging team: task sequence does not reflash battery controller after re-imaging which leaves mismatch. SRE: Intune failure correlates with WMI battery class errors; compliance policy checks for battery presence/health which fails when telemetry blank. Temporary experiment: re-run depot flasher with legacy compatibility flag and re-image -> Autopilot completes. Evidence: mjr-battery-dump-2026-03-11.log, wmi-battery-output.txt attached in artifacts. Priority escalated due to impact on staging capacity.

Imaging task sequence will be updated to include battery-FW verification step. Follow-up action items assigned to Depot and Imaging teams; monitoring provisioning throughput for next 48 hours.

The instance replacement lag plus oscillation extended the incident duration.

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 01:40 UTC ClearLedger observed a sharp rise in 5xx responses (primarily 502/503) from the Redwood API. Errors correlated with sustained client concurrency from their dedicated tenant. Impact: ClearLedger experiences failed generation calls and truncated streaming responses; several customers reported degraded UX. Environment: Dedicated capacity in us-east serving gptx-13b-v1 (pinned). Symptoms: - API gateway returning 502/503 intermittently for requests routed to tenant pool. - Upstream runtime logs show repeated worker process restarts (~OOM or forced exit) followed by rapid reconnects. - Autoscaler reported frequent scale events for ephemeral pool and then rate-limited backoff. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run ClearLedger's traffic replay (provided) with ~350 concurrent streaming sessions pinned to gptx-13b-v1. 2) Observe increased tail latencies and then 502/503 error rate rising past 8% within 15 minutes. 3) Check runtime worker processes on affected nodes for restarts. Logs & metrics: - apigw: elevated 5xx rate beginning 2026-03-10T01:40Z; spike correlated to tenant burst (ingress qps +180%). - runtime: repeated worker PID churn, exit code 137 and watchdog restarts. - autoscaler: oscillation of ephemeral worker group between 2 -> 8 nodes then rapid drain. Immediate customer-facing impact: Calls failing, streaming sessions dropping, higher token costs due to retries. Workaround requested: Temporarily rate-limit the tenant to 200 concurrent sessions or change model pin to a smaller instance type. Follow-ups: SRE to validate root cause and recommend durable mitigation (autoscaler tuning, backoff safeguards, and worker watchdog parameters).
Initial hypothesis: Retry loop combined with prefetch/backpressure caused inflight queue saturation on scheduler layer, leading to kernel-level memory pressure and worker OOMs. Evidence: - Worker exit codes 137 in /var/log/runtime/worker.log. - dmesg entries indicate process killed by OOM killer on worker nodes that experienced high KV cache miss rates. - Autoscaler logs show reactive scaleouts followed by rapid drains (node reuse delay ~30s) leading to connection thrash. Secondary hypothesis: a recent runtime patch to do aggressive prefetching (PR 4221) increased resident set for certain prompt shapes, pushing close to GPU memory limits under high concurrency. Actions taken so far: - Scoped impacted tenant and applied a temporary ingress concurrency cap at the API layer (200). - Disabled prefetch for the tenant via routing override (will revert after fix validated). - Collected core dumps and GPU memory snapshots and uploaded to S3 (links in comments). - Eng on-call reproduced a smaller-scale replay and confirmed worker churn starts around 250 concurrent sessions. Next steps: - Runtime team to revert aggressive prefetch patch for the dedicated pool and run canary (priority). - Autoscaler to add minimal cooldown and stabilize drain behavior to avoid oscillation. - SRE to investigate if libcudart or driver versions on these nodes are correlated with higher-than-normal fragmentation. - Coordinate with ClearLedger to schedule a controlled traffic ramp test once mitigations are in place.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:30 UTC - Customer (ClearLedger contact - Anya R.): Thank you for the quick mitigation. We saw reduced failures after the throttle. We'll coordinate a controlled ramp next week. Please advise on expected maintenance window.
Workaround applied: ingress concurrency cap and prefetch disabled for tenant; runtime patch rollback PR created (PR 4221 revert + guardrails). Pending verification and coordinated canary with customer before closing.

Issue summary:
Customer requested a compliance-grade audit slice for a forensic review. The exported NDJSON shows a consistent ~7-10 second clock skew on event timestamps compared to Redwood auth logs and external SAML IdP assertions. In addition, a subset (~3%) of events from a set of service accounts created before 2025-11 appear to lack the expected saml.subject or saml.nameid mapping in the audit payload, preventing deterministic correlation with the customer's SIEM.

Impact:
- NorthBridge cannot reconstruct a tamper-proof timeline for a sample window required by their internal SOC and legal team.
- Forensic queries in Splunk/Qradar fail to join events by identity for ~3% of activity, blocking the evidence handoff.
- Customer has a regulatory request (legal hold) with a 48h delivery expectation for a preliminary artifact.

Environment:
- Redwood prod (us-east) audit-export pipeline (ndjson) -> S3 bucket -> customer HEC/Splunk pull.
- Affected tenant: northbridge-prod (enterprise, dedicated routing to us-east).
- Service accounts impacted largely created in 2025-08 to 2025-11 timeframe.

Steps to reproduce / How we pulled sample:
1) Customer requested slice: 2026-03-08 00:00:00Z to 2026-03-08 06:00:00Z for tenant northbridge-prod.
2) Support generated a signed NDJSON slice via internal exporter and delivered to staging S3.
3) Customer ingested slice into Splunk using their ingestion script and joined on event.headers.request_id and event.actor.identity.saml.nameid.
4) Customer reports 45/1,200 events in the slice had no saml.nameid field and timestamps in audit.events[*].ts are 7-10s earlier than corresponding auth logs.

Observed behavior:
- Timestamp drift: audit.events[*].ts vs auth service logs show systematic negative offset (~7-10s).
- Missing SAML subject mapping for older service accounts. The events still contain actor.service_account_id but lack saml.nameid and saml.issuer fields in audit payload.

Expected behavior:
- Audit events exported should preserve canonical timestamps aligned with auth logs (within 1s median), and saml fields should be populated for all events where a SAML assertion was present at auth time.

Logs / Artifacts attached by customer:
- sample_slice_2026-03-08.ndjson (customer-provided post-ingest)
- support_export_signed_manifest_620333.json

Attachments (internal):
- exporter-run-2026-03-08.log (internal exporter),
- svc-auth-2026-03-08.log (redacted auth logs),
- mapping-matrix-v0.9.csv (showing header-field-to-Splunk-field mapping).

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 13:40 - NorthBridge SOC (Elena Morris): We see the missing saml.nameid on events that came from service accounts named 'integration-*' and 'legacy-hook-*'. We cannot join on service_account_id for privacy reasons; saml.nameid is required for legal matching. Please advise workaround for immediate delivery.
2026-03-12 15:05 - Support (Maya Chen): Provided temporary mapping script to customer to join by actor.service_account_id for preliminary timeline while we resolve; warned on privacy implications. Customer accepted and will scope for legalized sharing.
2026-03-13 17:18 - SRE (Priya Nair): Staging canary passed for 24h with no skew on 10k events. Investigating why saml.nameid missing only for older service accounts — possible missing lookup from identity-store migration in 2025-11. Opened INT-4412 to restore sso-legacy-index reconciliation job.
2026-03-14 11:02 - NorthBridge SOC (Elena Morris): Customer confirms preliminary timeline generated using mapping script is acceptable as temporary evidence; requests signed statement that production slice will be regenerated after fix and re-delivered with integrity manifest.
Hypothesis A: Clock skew arises when exporter serializes batches before identity/context cache returns canonical auth_ts; fallback uses exporter host clock. Confirmed via exporter-run log timestamps surrounding entry ids 82213-82261.
Hypothesis B: Missing saml.nameid fields tied to identity-store migration (2025-11) where older service accounts were not fully backfilled with saml metadata. Identity lookup returned null; exporter omitted saml envelope instead of labeling as 'unknown'.
Tests run: reproducible test using synthetic traffic with instrumented delay in identity cache - reproduced 8s negative offset consistently in 25/1000 events; added guard to wait up to 250ms for auth context before falling back to host_time and to emit a warning flag in event.metadata.timestamp_source.

Issue summary:
Customer LuminOS observed repeated throughput degradation and p99 latency spikes in their dedicated GPU pool during a staged model rollout. The effect began ~2026-03-10 09:20 PDT and recurred during subsequent rollout windows. Impact: customer-facing API p99 increased from ~420ms to >3s and effective throughput fell ~40% for 5-10 minute windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (reserved) assigned to LuminOS, region us-west-2, mixed GPU type (A100+H100), pinned model redwood/longform-13b for rollout.

Observed behavior:
- Periodic (clustered) 5–12 minute intervals where p99 spikes and throughput drops.
- Spike windows correlated with a high rate of short-lived inference streams (<250ms) from a different tenant sharing the same pool.
- Autoscaler did not provision additional slots during the earliest minutes of the window; autoscale metrics showed allocation attempts but low successful GPU attachments.

Initial hypothesis:
- Short, high-frequency streams from another tenant were fragmenting batch slots and causing the scheduler to compact many small batches, increasing kernel overhead and creating slot starvation. The autoscaler telemetry appearing delayed/masked by heartbeat noise led to undersizing during the first minutes of each surge.

Steps to reproduce (attempted by Support/Eng):
1) Recreate a small-stream flood in a synthetic testbed attached to a dedicated pool with mixed short and long streams.
2) Start a rollout on a pinned model to simulate LuminOS traffic mix.
3) Observe scheduling logs, batch sizes, slot allocation, and autoscaler decisions (30m window).
Provision test dedicated pool in us-west-2 with mixed short (<250ms) and long (>2s) stream traffic pattern.
Simulate a burst of short lived streams at 200–400 rps from a shadow tenant for 8–12 minutes.
Run steady long-stream traffic (LuminOS-like) concurrently at 40–60 rps and start rolling model update.
Collect scheduler/batcher traces, autoscaler attach logs, and GPU slot allocation metrics for the window.

2026-03-10T09:21:04Z batcher: batch_created size=1 model=redwood/longform-13b latency_est=120ms
2026-03-10T09:21:05Z autoscaler: attach_attempt pool=dedicated-west reason=scale_up desired_slots=4
2026-03-10T09:21:09Z attach: attach_failed gpu_attach_err=NVML_TIMEOUT code=504
2026-03-10T09:21:10Z monitoring: p99=3120ms p50=480ms throughput_rps=36
2026-03-10T09:26:12Z scheduler: observed 700 short_stream_starts in 60s from tenant=shadow-9
2026-03-10T09:26:12Z runtime: kv_cache_size_growth=+12% over 5m; memory_pressure=71%
2026-03-10T09:27:01Z console_alert: dedicated_pool_throughput_drop pool_id=dp-west-128 drop_pct=43
2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Aisha): Logged with SRE + Customer. Collected traces and requested SRE to run targeted synthetic test; provided customer a temporary traffic-shaping workaround to reduce short stream concurrency.
2026-03-10 11:12 - SRE (Diego): Reproduced with local testbed. Observed slot fragmentation and delayed attach_failures tied to NVML timeout on mixed GPU nodes. Short streams occupied slot headers causing preemption of batched work.
2026-03-10 11:50 - SRE (Diego): Pushed a hotfix to scheduler to prefer coalescing small streams into ephemeral micro-batches and increased autoscaler polling frequency for affected pool. Monitoring will track p99/successful_attach for 24h.
2026-03-11 09:33 - Customer (LuminOS, S. Park): Confirmed that p99 spikes reduced at next rollout window. Noted one residual 2-minute spike; asked for root cause details and long-term mitigations.
Testbed reproduction: synthetic short-stream flood reproduced throughput fade and p99 spikes within 4–6 minutes.
Root cause chain:
  1) High rate of short-lived streams (shadow tenant) created many small batches and frequent context switches.
  2) Scheduler assigned slot headers for each short stream; this fragmented GPU slot scheduling and reduced batch efficiency.
  3) NVML attach timeouts on mixed GPU nodes (A100+H100) caused transient attach failures, reducing usable slot capacity.
  4) Autoscaler telemetry aggregation window (30s default) smoothed the early signal; autoscaler did not request needed slot capacity until after visible throughput drop.
Telemetry artifacts: autoscaler_emit_delay_ms spiked to 1200ms during event; attach_fail_rate rose to 7% vs baseline 0.2%.
Model sensitivity: redwood/longform-13b long-context KV cache growth amplified memory pressure during the windows, exacerbating attach failures on heterogeneous nodes.
Implemented a 2-stage mitigation: (1) short-term — applied traffic-shaping guidance to LuminOS (throttle concurrent short streams) and enabled the scheduler hotfix to micro-batch short streams; (2) medium-term — increased autoscaler polling frequency from 30s -> 8s for affected dedicated pools and added attach retry backoff jitter. Hotfix was rolled to us-west-2 at 2026-03-10T11:44Z. Post-change monitoring showed p99 returned to baseline (~420ms) and throughput recovered to >92% of steady-state within 6 minutes of each test window.
ENG-OPS: Create a scheduler improvement ticket to add explicit slot compaction heuristics for mixed short/long stream workloads (INT-6420).
INFRA: Validate NVML timeouts across heterogeneous GPU mixes and provide driver-level mitigation (upgrade plan for H100 nodes).
PRODUCT: Document 'short-stream guidance' for Dedicated customers and add auto-detect rule in Console to recommend traffic shaping when small-stream percentage >40%.
SRE: Reduce autoscaler default aggregation window for dedicated pools with mixed workloads and add synthetic short-stream canary to alert earlier.
LuminOS reported increased error-budget burn during rollout windows but no SLA breach; customer-facing endpoints experienced 5–10 minute degradation windows with p99 >3s.

Issue summary: After a recent auth-proxy rollout that normalized cookie prefixes, the Console 'Run as user' / impersonation flow intermittently returns 403 for support engineers and oncall. Impact: prevents support from performing oncall troubleshooting or using impersonation runbooks for customer investigations. Not a complete outage but significantly impairs oncall response.
Support engineers report 20-30% failure rate for impersonation attempts in us-west; delays in oncall escalations and a missed pager escalation window for one incident.
1) Open Redwood Electron Console (prod, us-west).
2) From support tools, select a target user and click 'Impersonate / Run as'.
3) Console attempts token exchange with auth-proxy and then calls service-ticket endpoint.
4) Observe immediate 403 response and console shows 'Impersonation denied: session mismatch'.
5) Repeating the flow in same session sometimes succeeds (racey), other times fails consistently until app restart.
6) Reproduction more reliable when user agent is Electron (desktop) and less frequent from browser.
403 returned from /internal/v1/impersonate with log 'cookie validation failed: multiple session cookies; prefix mismatch'. Electron session shows stale cookie present with __Host- and without- prefix variants.
Impersonation flow should succeed when user has valid session and support has privileges; cookie normalization should be transparent to downstream services.
2026-03-12T17:08:12Z auth-proxy[proxy-23] WARN cookie_validator: found duplicate session cookies: session, __Host-session; choosing longest path -> validation failed
2026-03-12T17:08:12Z console-service[runas] ERROR token_exchange: external 403 from auth-proxy (reason=CookiePrefixMismatch)
2026-03-12T17:09:55Z electron-client[desktop-71] DEBUG cookie-store: retained legacy 'session' cookie alongside new '__Host-session' after proxy set-cookie response
Initial triage (Support): replicated in prod us-west with Electron client; browser repros much less frequent.
SRE looked at recent auth-proxy change: PR #2345 added stricter '__Host-' prefix enforcement for cookies to tighten path/scoping.
Hypothesis: proxy now issues __Host-session but older Electron client keeps non-prefixed session cookie, causing validation to detect duplicate cookies and treat as potential session-splitting attack -> rejects request.
Observed that cookie path and domain differ slightly for legacy cookie (path=/; domain=.redwood.internal) vs __Host- cookie (path=/; no domain attr) — srv-side validator treats this as two active session cookies.
Temporary mitigation tested: proxy added a normalization header that instructs Electron client to delete legacy cookie on next response; immediate drop in 403s for users who received the normalization header.
Related deploys: auth-proxy rollout v2.1.8 (2026-03-11) referenced in Slack #deploys and linked PR.
Edge case: support-runbooks that use embedded webviews (electron) do not clear legacy cookie automatically; persists across app restarts for some users due to client-side cookie store bug.
Risk: rolling back proxy change reduces the enforcement benefit; client upgrade plus norm header preferred.
Support Triage - Priya S. (2026-03-12): Received multiple reports during oncall; raising to SRE for immediate investigation. Added logs and example request IDs.
SRE - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-12): Confirmed cookie prefix change on 2026-03-11. Hypothesis: duplicate cookies trigger validator rejection. Will try normalization header as low-risk mitigation.
Reporter - Maya Chen (2026-03-12): Verified workaround after Liam applied normalization header to proxy in us-west canary: impersonation attempts succeeded for 7/8 previously failing sessions.
Desktop Eng - Nora Patel (2026-03-13): Electron client has known cookie-store TTL issue; will push an update (PR referenced) to explicitly remove legacy 'session' cookie when encountering __Host- variant.
SRE - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-13): Patch deployed to production us-west: normalization header active for 1 hour; monitoring shows error rate for impersonation dropped from 26% to 3%.
Support Triage - Priya S. (2026-03-13): Marking as 'In Progress' while Desktop ENG completes client publish and we monitor long-tail failures. Notifying oncall and internal access docs.
Temporary proxy normalization header added to instruct clients to delete legacy 'session' cookie; effective immediately in us-west. Desktop client patch queued and will be rolled out in electron v3.4.1.
Partial mitigation applied (normalization header) and desktop client patch in flight. Plan: 1) ship electron client fix to explicitly remove legacy cookie (PR merged), 2) keep normalization header for 48h post-client rollout, 3) monitor impersonation success rate and then remove normalization header. Final resolution will include postmortem and runbook update.
Desktop ENG to merge and ship electron v3.4.1 with explicit legacy-cookie removal (ETA 2026-03-15).
SRE to leave normalization header enabled in us-west until client uptake >= 95% (monitoring dashboard link in confluence).
Support to update internal runbook 'Impersonation troubleshooting' with note about cookie-prefix migration and temporary remediation steps.
Conduct short postmortem after full rollout and create a preventative ticket to add cookie-compatibility tests to CI for proxy changes.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During automated Autopilot provisioning of newly imaged Dell Latitude fleet, devices attached to corporate Thunderbolt docks fail to bring the dock NIC up in OOBE. Autopilot times out and machines enter provisioning retry loop (OOBE restart). This started after we rolled BIOS package 1.7.3 on the deployment image branch (pushed 2026-03-09).

Impact:
- ~18 new hires' devices failed first-boot autopilot in us-west region (blocking satchel deliveries).
- Imaging throughput reduced; manual intervention required to complete onboarding for docked devices.

Environment:
- Windows 11 22H2 golden image (SCCM/Task Sequence), Autopilot profile provisioning, corp Thunderbolt docks (TB16 gen2), Dell BIOS 1.7.3, previous BIOS 1.6.8 was OK.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Apply SCCM task sequence with BIOS 1.7.3 to Latitude 7440 with TB16 dock attached.
2) Boot to Autopilot OOBE with ethernet via dock.
3) Observe OOBE network detection timeout and device restart (retries).

Observed behavior:
- Thunderbolt security mode changed from "No Security" to "User Authorization" after BIOS 1.7.3 update.
- Dock's NIC enumerates after user accepts thunderbolt device on-screen prompt; OOBE has already timed out by then.
- Event logs show network adapter not found during first-boot; Autopilot times out at ~8 minutes.

Expected behavior:
- Dock NIC should enumerate immediately during OOBE so Autopilot can complete without user interaction (same as prior BIOS 1.6.8).

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed reproducible on two lab units with TB16. Rollback to BIOS 1.6.8 restores previous behavior.
- BIOS release notes for 1.7.3 mention "Thunderbolt security enhancements" but do not call out default mode change.
- DellCommand Configure / WMI reports attribute: ThunderboltSecurityMode = 2 (User Authorization) on 1.7.3, previously 0 (No Security).
- SCCM BIOS package applied without extra vendor config; we expected BIOS vendor defaults to remain compatible with autopilot workflow.
- Network team confirmed Autopilot timeouts are normal when no NIC present during OOBE; typical workaround is user acceptance, but that is not possible during zero-touch onboarding.
- Reproduced in staging and prod images. Not related to cabling or switch config.

Temporary workaround applied:
- For incoming batches: temporarily gate BIOS 1.7.3 in SCCM and reimage affected units back to 1.6.8; this allowed Autopilot to complete without manual steps (applied to 18 devices so far).
- Developed a post-imaging SCCM step using DellCommand Configure (DCU) to set ThunderboltSecurityMode=0 prior to first boot. Applied to new task sequence in staging for immediate mitigation.

Root cause hypothesis:
- BIOS update 1.7.3 changes default Thunderbolt security to require user authorization; it prevents dock devices from being enumerated at pre-login stage, causing Autopilot OOBE to retry and fail.

Proposed remediation / long-term plan:
- Update golden image task sequence to include a DCU configuration step that forces Thunderbolt security to the legacy/no-security mode before first OOBE network check. (Short term, implemented as emergency change in staging.)
- Engage Dell support to request a BIOS option to preserve previous default or expose a persistent OEM setting we can configure silently during imaging. Opened SR 123456789.
- Add a preflight check in our imaging pipeline to detect BIOS-level security changes (scan DCU/BiosProvider attributes) and block image promotion if compatibility-impacting flags are changed.
- Communicate gating policy to site reliability and procurement: delay broad BIOS rollouts for new models until compatibility verification with Autopilot/docked scenarios is validated.

Resolution notes (work-in-progress):
- Workaround (DCU step) merged to staging TS (Task Sequence) 2026-03-11; initial run reimaged 6 units successfully.
- SCCM BIOS rollout paused for 1.7.3.
- Dell SR opened and vendor engineering has requested a BIOS dump; vendor estimate: 5 business days for root cause analysis.

Attachments / logs:
- Excerpt: System event log during OOBE: "NetworkAdapter: No adapters present at startup. Autopilot network detect timed out."
- DCU query output: ThunderboltSecurityMode=2 (on 1.7.3)
- Screenshot: OOBE thunderbolt pairing prompt (requires user acceptance).

Next steps:
- Continue reimaging remaining affected devices with rollback where necessary until DCU step validated across fleet.
- Track Dell SR and update when vendor provides remediation or a signed BIOS patch.
- Implement imaging pipeline preflight and update runbook for docking scenarios.

Additional notes:
SRE - L. Nguyen: Suggest updating Autopilot network timeout as a stop-gap? Concerned that increasing timeout masks other failures and will slow onboarding. Prefer BIOS-level fix.
Procurement - R. Ellis: Flagging for hardware intake: we may need to request BIOS QA signoff from vendor for future firmware shipments for docked fleet.
Devon Patel: Applied DCU change in staging TS. Reimaged 6 devices attached to docks; all 6 completed Autopilot without manual intervention. Preparing change request to deploy DCU step to prod TS.
Aisha Ramos: Customer-facing note: Internal onboarding ops informed — manual acceptance required only if device shipped prior to workaround. New shipments will be imaged with DCU step.
Workaround implemented: DCU configuration step to set ThunderboltSecurityMode=0 in task sequence and BIOS rollout paused. Vendor SR opened; long-term fix pending vendor response.
Reimage to BIOS 1.6.8 OR run DellCommand Configure step in SCCM task sequence to set ThunderboltSecurityMode=0 prior to first OOBE.
payload.summary: Dell BIOS update enabled Thunderbolt user-authorization, preventing dock NIC init and blocking Autopilot provisioning

Summary: Starting 2026-03-09 we observed a rise in missed P1 SLAs where tickets with explicit P1 conditions in the priority expression were evaluated as lower priority and routed to the 'standard' queue. Impact: Several P1 and escalated issues reached first-response SLA breaches over the last 36 hours. Root cause hypothesis: the expression evaluator used by the rule-compiler appears to treat OR with higher precedence than AND in some compiled execution paths, causing expressions like '(env == "prod" OR customer_tier == "enterprise") AND sla_hours <= 2' to be evaluated incorrectly as 'env == "prod" OR (customer_tier == "enterprise" AND sla_hours <= 2)'. This changes the boolean logic and drops intended P1s out of fast paths.
Create a rule in staging with priority expression: (env == 'prod' OR customer_tier == 'enterprise') AND sla_hours <= 2
Send a synthetic ticket matching env=prod, customer_tier='self_serve', sla_hours=1
Observe which queue the rule-engine assigns (expected: p1-fasttrack / actual: standard)
Repeat in pairing session with a debug build of the evaluator and enable expression tracing
2026-03-09T13:07:22Z support-tooling[router] DEBUG evaluate_expr: raw='(env == "prod" OR customer_tier == "enterprise") AND sla_hours <= 2' compiled_ops='OR,A,COMPARE,AND,COMPARE'
2026-03-09T13:07:23Z support-tooling[router] INFO route_decision: ticket_id=tid-98321 assigned_queue=standard matched_rule_id=rule-117
Stacktrace: n/a - logic bug in evaluator, no crash

Additional notes:
Confirmed reproduction in both Python-based interpreter and optimized AOT-compiled path. AOT path used a different precedence table (bug introduced in commit 7f2c8b1).
Unit test missing for mixed AND/OR expressions without explicit parentheses — adding coverage.
Hypothesis: parser emitted correct AST but codegen flattened binary ops and used left-to-right reduction without respecting canonical boolean precedence.
Experiment: forcing explicit parentheses in codegen fixed all failing cases in staging (see branch feature/expr-precedence-guard).
Workaround applied: added runtime parentheses guard in router interpreter (rolled to prod us-east at 2026-03-12T04:30Z) which restores correct evaluation order for affected rules. Long-term fix: merged PR #3124 that updates the compiler precedence table and adds unit tests + fuzz tests for expression combinations. Rollout plan: gradual deploy of compiler fix to canary, then prod after 24h of monitoring. Post-deploy verification checklist included in linked Confluence page.
2026-03-12: Guard deployed to prod/us-east — immediate reduction in misrouted P1s observed (0 incidents in 8h window).
2026-03-13: Compiler fix merged to main (PR 3124). Canary build in eu-west for additional validation.
Follow-up: add a telemetry alert for boolean-eval mismatches (new metric: expr_evaluation_discrepancy_count) and schedule a postmortem in #support blameless-rotation.
Owner for follow-ups: Arjun Patel (engineering) and Maya Chen (support ops)
payload.summary: Operator-precedence bug in priority expression evaluator causes incorrect queueing of P1s

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several ephemeral CI runners failed to finish job startup during the secrets rewrap event performed by Secrets Team (2026-03-10 01:13 UTC). The runner initContainer that fetches repo credentials from Vault exits with a 401/permission denied error and the pod moves to CrashLoopBackOff.
Impact: A subset (~8%) of ephemeral runners in prod-us-west failed to complete job bootstrapping for ~45 minutes, blocking CI jobs across multiple repos for internal teams. No user-facing product outages, but CI capacity degraded and release pipelines were delayed.
Environment: prod cluster (us-west), runner autoscaling group: ephemeral-runner-*-pool, Vault path: secret/ci/repos/*, Vault cluster: vault-prod-02.
Observed pattern: Failures correlated with a scheduled Vault rewrap (transit rekey) that rotated wrapping keys and reissued some service tokens. Affected pods show initContainer failing immediately when attempting to exchange the mounted token for Vault session credentials. A manual pod restart usually recovers the runner.

1) Trigger a Vault rewrap (or simulate token re-issue) while an ephemeral runner pod is in the init stage (initContainer running).
2) initContainer (vault-agent/credentials-fetcher) requests /v1/auth/token/renew or /v1/secret/data/ci/repos/foo with mounted token.
3) Vault returns 401 or error: "invalid token" for the mounted token for a short window.
4) initContainer exits non-zero; Kubernetes restarts the pod and it sometimes recovers after a fresh token is provisioned.

kubectl logs pod/ephemeral-runner-ht2k -c init-fetcher --previous:
2026-03-10T01:14:09Z client=init-fetcher level=info msg=attempting to read secret path=secret/ci/repos/repo-abc
2026-03-10T01:14:09Z client=init-fetcher level=error msg=vault read error status=401 body='{"errors":["invalid token"]}'
2026-03-10T01:14:09Z client=init-fetcher level=error msg=exiting code=2
---
vault-audit (excerpt):
time=2026-03-10T01:14:09 path=auth/token/lookup token_accessor=xxxx result=permission_denied

Initial hypothesis: race between Vault wrapping/rekey operation and the ephemeral projected service account token refresh path. The mounted token TTL and the vault-agent's token cache are misaligned: during rewrap a token accessor is briefly invalidated while Vault finishes key rotation, causing immediate 401 responses for clients using the old accessor. Secondary hypothesis: the initContainer code path does not implement retry on auth errors and treats 401 as fatal. Observed that kubelet projected tokens were rotated at the same minute (kubelet logs show service account token refresh). Correlation with Secrets Team's rewrap job (job id: secrets-rewrap-20260310) confirmed.
Partial findings: - No evidence of Vault ACL changes; ACL stable. - Restarting the pod often results in success (fresh token mount). - Some nodes saw more frequent failures suggesting timing window depends on node clock and kubelet token refresh timing.

1) Temporarily delay Vault rewraps for the ephemeral-runner node pool by 2 minutes of the planned window to allow in-flight pods to finish init.
2) For currently failing pods: kubectl rollout restart daemonset/ephemeral-runner and/or delete the CrashLoopBackOff pod to force fresh token mount.
3) For urgent CI capacity: scale up dedicated-runner pool to compensate while we stabilize.

In progress. Temporary mitigation (grace window + rolling restarts) reduced failures to near-zero. A code change to the initContainer to implement idempotent retries on Vault auth failures and to treat 401 as retryable during rotation window has been opened (PR referenced above).
1) Merge and rollout initContainer retry logic (PR 124) and bump image tag for ephemeral-runner. 2) Add automated 'rotation-safe' pause hook to the Secrets Team orchestration so rewraps can detect active initContainers via a small API on the runner agent. 3) Update runbook with steps for pausing rewraps and for forced restart of runner pods. 4) Postmortem to be drafted if residual impact >5% of runner capacity; deadline 2026-03-20.
