payload.description:
Issue summary:
Intermittent GPU OOMs in Northwind Analytics dedicated pool during high-churn chat traffic (many short-lived sessions + cancellations). OOMs occur despite dashboards showing non-zero free GPU memory prior to failure. Initial hypothesis: KV cache arena fragmentation causing allocation failures / forced request shedding.

Impact:
- Customer saw ~0.6% of chat requests fail with 5xx between 2026-01-26 21:10 UTC and 2026-01-27 02:40 UTC.
- Two pods restarted due to CUDA OOM; transient increased p99 latency (~+1.2s) while pool rebalanced.
- Customer escalated due to concern about stability during upcoming load test.

Customer-reported behavior:
- Failures clustered during bursty load (spikes to 3–4x baseline QPS) with frequent client cancellations (mobile app backgrounding).
- Largest prompts were not the trigger; failures correlated with churn.

Environment:
- Dedicated: nw-analytics-gpu-pool-03 (A100 80GB)
- Region: us-east
- Runtime: 1.21.3-redwood (customer pinned)
- Models: llama-3.1-70b-instruct (primary), qwen2.5-72b-instruct (A/B)

Steps to reproduce (from customer + internal replay):
1) Create ~1,200 concurrent chat sessions.
2) Mix request sizes (prompt tokens: 200–2,000; target decode: 64–512 tokens).
3) Cancel ~20–35% of requests during decode (client disconnect / explicit cancel).
4) Repeat in bursts (30s spike, 60–90s trough) for 20–30 minutes.

Observed errors (excerpt):
- "CUDA out of memory" from KV allocation path.
- Preceded by increasing allocation retries and occasional opportunistic evictions.

Requested from customer:
- Request IDs around OOM window
- Confirmation of cancellation rate and client retry behavior
- Whether any long-lived pinned sessions exist (none reported)

Notes:
This ticket is tracking customer impact and the mitigation applied in the dedicated pool while KV compaction/eviction improvements roll out more broadly.
Timeline + investigation notes:

2026-01-27 (00:18 UTC) - Detection
- Oncall (Rafael Mendes) paged for elevated 5xx + pod restarts in nw-analytics-gpu-pool-03.
- Node exporter + NVML showed sawtooth free memory; OOM occurred while ~6–10GB free was reported, suggesting fragmentation / inability to satisfy a large contiguous allocation.

Allocator/KV signals (new + existing):
- KV arena fragmentation estimate (internal debug snapshot) increased over time; free bytes were present but split across many small extents.
- Spike in "kv_alloc_retry" and "kv_page_reclaim" counters.
- Prefix cache hit rate steady; no clear correlation with OOM.

Hypothesis
- High churn (cancels) creates many short-lived KV segments.
- Long-lived sessions keep older allocations pinned.
- Free list degenerates into many small holes; allocation path increasingly scans/retries.
- Under burst, allocator fails to find contiguous pages for new decode segments and triggers CUDA OOM (or fails during internal arena growth/defrag path).

Reproduction
- Runtime team (Omar El-Sayed + Samir Qureshi) replayed traffic pattern using a synthetic churn harness in staging and reproduced a similar fragmentation pattern within ~25 minutes.

Related work
- Compaction/eviction project already in flight; metrics PR referenced for fragmentation counters.
- Kill-switch/config plumbing PR referenced for safe toggling in Dedicated.

Customer-specific considerations
- Dedicated pool has predictable traffic but spiky bursts; better to accept slightly higher background maintenance than hard OOM.
- Customer requested no model changes and minimal downtime.

Decision
- Apply mitigation via runtime flags in customer pool to reduce worst-case fragmentation behavior until compaction is GA:
  (a) Enable compaction in "budgeted" mode.
  (b) Lower fragmentation trigger threshold to start earlier.
  (c) Slightly increase safety headroom to avoid operating near the cliff.

Risk assessment
- Main risk: compaction work adding latency spikes if not budgeted; mitigated by strict budget and scheduler boundary enforcement.
- Rollback plan: flip kill-switch to disable compaction if p99 regresses >10% sustained for 10 minutes (per SRE guardrails).
Resolution / mitigation applied:

2026-01-27 (02:55 UTC)
- Applied dedicated-pool runtime config change (no model change) via control-plane rollout:
  - runtime.kv_compaction.enabled = true
  - runtime.kv_compaction.mode = incremental
  - runtime.kv_compaction.budget_ms_per_step = 0.25
  - runtime.kv_compaction.max_bytes_moved_per_step = 268435456 (256MiB)
  - runtime.kv_fragmentation.trigger_ratio = 0.18 (was 0.30)
  - runtime.kv_allocator.safety_headroom_mb = 2048 (was 1024)
  - runtime.kv_eviction.tier_aware = true (Dedicated: prefer evicting preemptible/prefix cache before active decode)

Observed outcome (next 24h):
- No further CUDA OOMs in nw-analytics-gpu-pool-03.
- p99 latency: neutral to slightly improved during bursts (estimated -4% to -7% in the affected windows).
- Compaction counters show steady low-volume moves; no single-step spikes exceeding budget.

Customer communication:
- Confirmed mitigation deployed and asked customer to re-run the same high-churn test; customer reported stability improvement and no failures over 45 minutes (per Support thread).

Follow-ups:
- Keep customer pinned on 1.21.3 but maintain pool-level flags until runtime 1.22 rollout is complete.
- Add this workload to perf canary / benchmark suite gating (linked to ENG-4828 externally; tracked internally by Runtime).

Close criteria:
- Ticket marked Resolved after 7 consecutive days with no OOMs and customer confirmation of successful retest.
- Will reopen if OOM recurs or if p99 regressions are observed from compaction settings.

Additional notes:
2026-01-27 01:05 UTC — Support (triage note, via #support): Northwind says ~30% cancel rate on mobile during decode; retries enabled with exponential backoff (max 3). No pinned sessions; they do have a long-lived system prompt prefix shared across sessions.
2026-01-28 16:10 UTC — Support: Customer reran the load test for 45 minutes, no 5xx observed. They request we keep this mitigation until the next runtime train and ask for guidance on what to monitor on their side.

Issue summary: During a scheduled run of the automated environment-permission-reconciliation job (reconcile-runner), multiple data-platform service accounts used by the data ingestion pipelines lost access to a subset of production resources in prod-us-east. The job applied an org-policy alignment change that removed a tag used upstream by the private-deploy onboarding flow, causing short-lived permission denials.

Why this ticket: capture investigation, temporary rollback actions, and next steps to prevent recurrence.
Data ingestion pipelines experienced transient failures (~35 minutes) across three nightly runs. No customer-facing API was affected, but internal analytics and downstream model retraining jobs were delayed. Estimated job-run backlog ~ 12 hours for affected pipelines. Two on-call pager escalations were triggered.
Prod account master/org structure: GCP org: redwood-prod (projects: prod-us-east-data, prod-us-east-llm). Reconcile-runner runs as a cross-account IAM service principal (aws-assumer:reconcile-runner, gcp-sa:reconcile-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com). Reconcile job implements org-policy normalization and tag-to-role syncs.
1) Trigger reconcile-runner with tag-normalize=true against prod-us-east dry-run=false. 2) Job evaluates projects under org and translates policy tags to ephemeral role bindings. 3) If tag key 'env:deployment' absent, job removes fallback binding 'data-platform-reader:fallback' and leaves only tag-scoped bindings. 4) Data-platform service accounts without the tag lose effective access.
- reconcile-runner logs (2026-03-12T01:12:03Z): applied binding removal on projects/prod-us-east-data: removed IAM binding data-platform-reader:fallback
- Stackdriver (prod-us-east-data) authz logs: repeated 403s from service-account data-platform-pipeline-sa@prod-us-east-data.iam.gserviceaccount.com starting 2026-03-12T01:15Z
- Pager duty notes: #oncall notified at 2026-03-12T01:23Z
- reconcile-runner metrics: job-duration 182s, affected-projects 3, failed-bindings 0
- Audit logs show subsequent reconcile rollback at 2026-03-12T01:50Z triggered by infra-ops alerting rule 'reconcile-unexpected-binding-changes'
- Hypothesis 1: A recent reconcile-runner change (PR 412) tightened role-scoping to prefer tag-scoped bindings and removed a default fallback. The change was merged last week and scheduled for daily runs.
- Hypothesis 2: Org-policy enforcement for tag presence was recently enabled for a subset of GCP folders; reconcile-runner removed bindings where tag was absent.
- Evidence: PR 412 includes code that drops fallback bindings when tag key missing (see PR diff). The audit trail shows the binding removal correlates with job start times.
- Quick repro in staging: ran reconcile-runner against staging-project with tag removed; observed identical binding removal behavior.
1) Rolled back reconcile-runner to previous stable image (tag v2026-03-05) at 2026-03-12T01:52Z. 2) Re-applied fallback IAM binding 'data-platform-reader:fallback' to prod projects affected. 3) Requeued stalled ingestion jobs; pipelines resumed by 2026-03-12T02:05Z. 4) Created an alert on 'binding-removal-without-tag' to stop future runs until patching done.
Change in reconcile-runner (PR 412) removed the 'safe-fallback' binding if tag absent. When combined with a recently enforced org-policy that strips the 'env:deployment' tag for some onboarding projects, the reconciliation job interpreted lack of tag as signal to remove fallback bindings, resulting in access loss.
Short term: pin reconcile-runner to v2026-03-05 for prod runs and keep alerting in place. Medium term: update reconcile-runner to preserve fallback bindings and add a dry-run gating for first-run in newly onboarded projects. Long term: implement pre-flight checks that detect tag absence and notify owners instead of removing bindings.
Owners: Marco Ruiz (infra) to land code fix; Aisha Khan to coordinate with Data Platform to validate bindings; Security (Leah Park) to review org-policy rollout plan.
Planned PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/reconcile-runner/pull/418 (preserve-fallback), PR 419 (preflight-checks).
Workaround and rollback applied; reconcile-runner pinned and fallback bindings re-applied. Code patch PR #418 opened to preserve fallback binding behavior and add explicit opt-in gating for tag normalization. Monitoring: additional alert added and a runbook updated. Incident not escalated to customers.
1) Postmortem write-up due 2026-03-20 (owner: Marco Ruiz). 2) Update runbook 'Env Reconcile Runbook' with preflight checklist and safe-rollback steps (owner: SRE). 3) Security to review org-policy rollout checklist and coordinate with onboarding team. 4) Add unit/integration tests in reconcile-runner to cover fallback binding cases.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several contractors reported immediate 403 / Access Denied when opening the Feature Flags console after receiving a temporary access approval. Impact: Contractors who were previously in ff-admin-like groups were removed by Okta due to an applied group expiry policy (Okta Lifecycle), causing RBAC lookups to deny access. This affects runbooks and time-sensitive release toggles.

Observed behavior: After approval flow completes, the user lands on the console sign-in but receives 403 and no RBAC roles are returned. Okta System Log shows a GroupMembership.deactivate event for the contractor groups around the same timestamp as the approval. SCIM provisioner logs show a subsequent "ignored" deprovision event attributable to an attribute mapping mismatch (expiredUntil != expirationDate).

Expected behavior: Temporary access approvals should result in users being in a valid group/role for the requested TTL and SCIM + RBAC should remain consistent for the life of that approval. Group expiry policy changes in Okta should not silently drop active temporary approvals without a re-provision attempt or alert.

Business impact: Blocks contractors from completing feature flag reviews and emergency toggles; could delay production fixes.
1) Provision contractor user and add to 'contractor-ff-admins' with Okta expiry set to 7 days
2) Trigger self-service temporary approval (internal feature-flags console) and complete SSO sign-in
3) Observe immediate 403 on console even though approval flow completed
4) Check Okta System Log for GroupMembership.deactivate and SCIM provisioner logs for a rejected deprovision mapping
Okta System Log: 2026-03-10T14:02:03Z GroupMembership.deactivate userId=00u9abcD reason=expiry policy
SCIM Provisioner: 2026-03-10T14:02:04Z WARN - incoming group change: user=evan.contributor@acme.com mapping mismatch: expiredUntil vs expirationDate -> action=ignored
RBAC Service: 2026-03-10T14:02:05Z INFO - lookup roles for userId=00u9abcD returned empty set (cache miss)
Evan Morales (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Customer-facing contractor reported 403 after approval completed; raising as P1 since it blocks releases.
Oncall (SRE) 2026-03-10: Initial triage - looks like Okta group expiry events are arriving during approval flow. Suspect lifecycle policy change push last night.
Priya Nair (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Assigned. Reproduced locally with test contractor account. Will instrument SCIM mapping and propose workaround.
Identity Eng (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-11: Confirmed Okta org has a new Group Expiry Rule applied to groups with name pattern 'contractor-*' rolled out 2026-03-09. SCIM mapping expects 'expirationDate' while Okta uses 'expiredUntil' TTL attribute in this rule.
2026-03-10 14:30 UTC - Reproduced with test account; auth flow completes but RBAC returns empty due to missing group membership row.
2026-03-10 15:10 UTC - Reviewed Okta System Logs: batch of GroupMembership.deactivate events coincide with approval timestamps. No explicit re-provision attempt observed.
2026-03-10 16:00 UTC - SCIM Provisioner (provisioner-3) code path ignores group change when attribute key != configured mapping; attribute key mismatch 'expiredUntil' vs 'expirationDate' prevents deactivation handling path from reconciling state.
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Session behavior: existing active sessions continue until cookie expiry; new logins fail because group membership already removed in Okta and not present in RBAC DB.
Hypothesis: Recent Okta Lifecycle rule introduced a TTL attribute key name incompatible with our SCIM mapping. SCIM treats deprovision events as 'ignored', leaving RBAC in inconsistent state (no re-add).
Workaround applied 2026-03-11: Identity Eng rolled back the Okta Group Expiry Rule for 'contractor-*' groups to prevent further deactivations. Manually reconciled 14 affected contractor accounts by re-provisioning group memberships and running the RBAC sync job.

Permanent fix: Update SCIM provisioner mapping to accept both 'expiredUntil' and 'expirationDate' attributes, and add an alert rule for sudden group membership delta (>5% change in 5 minutes) for monitored groups. Created follow-up INT task to ship the mapping change and tests.

Follow-ups: identity team to schedule a postmortem and update the approval flow to validate group membership post-Okta events before presenting final success to the user.

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled multi-region KMS key rotation that began 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC, ephemeral CI runners began failing to complete credential refreshes and artifact uploads. The scheduler accumulated queued release jobs (nightly/canary pipelines), causing the 03:00 and 04:30 release windows to be blocked.

Impact: Release pipelines in prod for multiple teams are queued and not progressing. No customer-facing API outage detected, but internal release cadence and automated canaries are blocked. Estimated blocked runs: ~120 jobs across two regions.

Environment: Production CI fleet using ephemeral runners with Vault-backed service account injection and artifacts written to object-store with KMS envelope encryption. Rotation involved rewrapping artifact-service encryption keys and rekeying Vault transit in both us-west-2 and eu-central-1.

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Start multi-region KMS key rewrap / rotate in eu-central and us-west.
2) Vault transit rewrap increases write latency to Vault replica clusters as rewrap jobs spike.
3) Runner token refresh requests to Vault timeout or receive 503/429 intermittently.
4) Artifact uploader microservice (artifact-uploader) receives rebind event for service account cred and returns 403 for upload PUTs while key propagation is incomplete.
5) CI runner agent waits for credential injection and stalls; job remains in RUNNING state but makes no forward progress, holding ephemeral runner slot.

Observed behavior is a mix of Vault throttling (writeback queue), artifact-service 403s, and long-lived runner sessions occupying ci capacity.
Selected excerpts from logs (sanitized):
[2026-03-10T02:12:08Z] vault-api-usw2: WARN request_id=ab12 time_ms=1200 backend=transit rewrap_queue_length=78
[2026-03-10T02:12:11Z] runner-ephemeral-92: ERROR token-refresh failed status=503 error=transit-write-timeout
[2026-03-10T02:13:02Z] artifact-uploader-euc: WARN upload object=build-987 status=403 reason=key-propagation-pending
[2026-03-10T02:18:20Z] scheduler: INFO pending_jobs=94 avg_wait=00:09:12

Full logs attached to internal S3 bundle: s3://redwood-internal-logs/INT-531807/2026-03-10.tar.gz
Initial hypothesis: Vault transit rewrap spike caused transient throttling which cascaded into runner credential refresh failures; artifact uploads then failed because object-store key metadata was not yet visible in the region, producing 403s.

What we validated:
- Vault metrics show 5–10x write latency during the window and queued rewraps on both primary and replica clusters.
- Runner token refresh attempts increased error rate from 0.2% to 18% during rotation window (metrics: ci.runner.token_refresh.errors).
- Artifact service returned 403 consistently for objects encrypted with the new wrapping key until propagation completed (~9 minutes in eu-central).

Partial finding: Runners block on token refresh for up to their refresh timeout (default 15m) before they fail the job; our ephemeral runner controller leaves the runner allocated while waiting for credential injection, which causes headroom exhaustion.

Counterfactuals ruled out: network partition between regions (no network loss), IAM policy revocations (policy unchanged), manifest misconfiguration (no recent deploy to runner agent).
Immediate mitigations applied on 2026-03-10 03:30 UTC:
- Manually paused the remaining scheduled rewrap batch in eu-central to allow propagation in us-west.
- Restarted artifact-uploader instances behind the us-west ALB to pick up new key metadata (hot-restart).
- Issued a manual Vault reissue for a subset of affected runners to unblock 28 highest-priority release jobs.
- Temporarily reduced runner token refresh timeout to 2m for new runner allocations to avoid long-lived blocked slots (to be reverted after follow-up).
Result: Released ~40% of queued jobs within 45 minutes; remaining jobs require runner recycle or credential reissue.
2026-03-10T03:05Z - Aisha Patel: Initial alert from release-ci #infra-nightly. Observed sudden spike in pending jobs and vault write latency. Opening ticket and paging SRE.
2026-03-10T03:22Z - Maya Singh (SRE): Confirmed vault rewrap queue and elevated latency in us-west. Artifact service shows key-propagation delays in eu-central. Hypothesis: simultaneous multi-region rotate overloaded propagation path.
2026-03-10T03:30Z - Diego Morales: Applied manual pause to eu-central rotation and restarted artifact-uploader in us-west. Kicking off manual token reissue for critical runner set.
2026-03-10T04:10Z - Samir Rao (Build Eng): Manual reissue cleared a subset but several jobs still stuck in RUNNING state and holding runner slots; requesting controller change to immediately recycle stalled runners after N seconds of no stdout.
2026-03-11T09:15Z - Diego Morales: Implemented temporary controller patch (hotfix) to recycle runner if token-refresh error persists > 90s. Patch rolled to prod canary; monitoring queue depth for next scheduled rotation.
2026-03-14T11:00Z - Maya Singh: Follow-up runbook edit proposed: add 'staggered multi-region rotate' and 'artifact key propagation verification' steps. Confluence PR: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/KMS+Multi-Region+Key+Roll+Runbook#comment-7
1) Implement staged rotation orchestration to enforce region-propagation confirmation before continuing to next region. 2) Add a pre-rotate probe that validates artifact-service key visibility across replicas. 3) Change ephemeral runner controller to set shorter wait-for-injection window and implement backoff+recycle behavior. 4) Create automation to pause subsequent rotation batches when vault queue length crosses threshold.
Owners: Diego (runner controller), Maya (SRE rotation), Samir (artifact service). Due: 2026-03-24.
In progress: temporary mitigations have unblocked majority of jobs. Engineering action items open to reduce blast radius on future multi-region rotates. Will close ticket once staged rotation automation and runner controller change are merged and runbook updated.
payload.summary: Runner credential refresh stalemate during multi-region key roll causing queued release jobs

comments: 2026-03-10T10:12:00Z Aisha: Logged ticket after customer provided traces. Customer says incident began after last kernel update. Assigned to infra SRE for triage.

2026-03-10T11:03:00Z Liam: I reproduced a stall in staging using rw-instruct-13b-quant with prompt 25k tokens + max_tokens=30k. Initial hypothesis: flushing/streaming buffer interaction with the new kernel path causes blocking when KV cache grows beyond ~30M entries.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer FathomAI Labs reports streaming responses hang and eventually timeout when sending requests that combine a very large prompt (40k-90k tokens) with high max_tokens (50k+). The requests either stop producing tokens mid-stream and client sees a socket/read timeout, or the API returns a 504 after ~120s. Customer reports this started after last week's runtime kernel update (deploy r3456).

Impact:
- Affected production traffic for the customer on rw-instruct-70b-v1 and rw-instruct-13b-quant.
- Several customer sessions stalled; feature in their product that relies on streaming completions became unusable.
- Business impact: regression blocked a rollout; customer has paused live experiments.

Environment:
- prod, us-east-1 region
- Customer using hosted Redwood API with token-based auth and streaming SSE endpoint (/v1/stream).
- Observed on both dedicated and hosted shared pools for this customer.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) POST to /v1/stream with prompt containing ~60k tokens (concatenated logs + context)
2) Set max_tokens=60000 and temperature=0.2
3) Expect streaming chunks within 1-3s; instead client receives initial tokens then streaming stalls after ~18-30s and eventually socket times out, or API returns 504.

Observed logs and telemetry snippets:
- Customer trace-id: trace-cust-7a2f
- Proxy logs show long-lived connections and intermittent chunked writes stop being produced. Example: "[stream_writer] connection 0x7f9a stalled at seq 128, last_chunk_ts=2026-03-09T21:14:03Z"
- Serving runtime logs (linked): datadog: https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=trace-cust-7a2f
- Kernel selector commit r3456 changed sequence-kernel heuristics (PR: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/987)

Notes to reproduce in staging (support):
- Reduced reproduction with smaller numbers: prompt 20k tokens + max_tokens 25k will reproduce stall consistently in isolated staging pool when using rw-instruct-13b-quant.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Cap max_tokens to <= 25k and split very large prompts into smaller windowed requests. This avoids the stall for now but affects latency and requires client-side engineering changes.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:45 - Engineering (runtime team): We see elevated GC and websocket write timeouts in the same window. Attaching profiling run: github.com/redwood/serving/issue/9152/profile-run-20260310. Noting that kernel r3456 modifies async token emission ordering under large sequence lengths.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Customer (FathomAI): Acknowledged workaround (capping tokens) but requests ETA for permanent fix as this blocks a new feature. Asking for SLA credit if resolution exceeds 72 hours.
2026-03-11 14:22 - Engineering: Bisect narrowed to change in commit 3456 -> file kernel/seq_optimizer.cpp around async_flush() changes. Hypothesis: when KV cache cross-threshold, async_flush waits for pending batch callbacks that are lost in some scheduling interleavings, leaving stream_writer pending indefinitely.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Product/Support: Notified customer of root cause hypothesis and proposed remediation plan: revert the specific async_flush change in a hotfix release to dedicated and hosted clusters; schedule patch for 2026-03-13.
- Reproduction was achieved in staging with smaller thresholds; rollback of kernel selector removed the hang.
- Traces show stream_writer stops emitting chunks despite model backend continuing token generation (model logs show continued step progress).
- Memory and GC spikes observed when KV cache grows above 28M entries for rw-instruct-70b-v1.
- Candidate root cause: scheduling/race introduced in async_flush path (commit r3456) that can leave front-end stream writer awaiting a callback that never fires under certain batching sizes.
- Next step: engineering to prepare hotfix reverting the async_flush behavior and add additional telemetry to detect stuck stream writers in future.
Pending (hotfix planned). Temporary workaround: cap max_tokens to 25k and split large prompts. Engineering to push hotfix revert of async_flush changes in r3456 on 2026-03-13 and monitor customer traffic. If hotfix is successful, schedule a follow-up ticket to add a synthetic test for large-KV streaming to prevent regressions.
Hotfix: revert async_flush change from r3456 and roll to us-east-1 pools (owner: runtime eng)
Add e2e regression test for streaming with large KV cache sizes and high max_tokens (owner: QA/runtime)
Instrument stream_writer with 'stuck' metric and alert at >15s without emission for active streams (owner: infra)
payload.summary: Streaming stalls and request timeouts for requests with very large input + high max_tokens

Background
- We’re approaching pilot/RC for Redwood Private signed offline bundles. Security requested we rotate CI secrets used by the signing stage to align with least-privilege + auditability requirements.
- This ticket covers rotation of CI tokens/service accounts used by the signing pipeline (NOT the long-term signing private key itself). The signing key remains in protected KMS/HSM custody per key ceremony.

Scope
1) Rotate CI credentials used to:
   - authenticate from CI runner to secrets backend (Vault/KMS broker)
   - access the signing service/operator endpoint (where applicable)
   - write signed artifacts + signature metadata to the internal artifact store
2) Update CI pipeline config to reference the new secrets.
3) Validate end-to-end: build offline bundle -> generate manifest -> sign -> publish -> installer verify in preflight.
4) Capture evidence (timestamps, job URLs, approver notes) needed for compliance/customer questionnaires.

Systems / impacted pipelines
- repo: release pipeline job “private-offline-bundle-sign” (Release Train)
- repos consuming outputs: redwood-private-installer (preflight verify), redwood-helm-charts (chart tarball checksums referenced by manifest)

Change window
- Preferred: 09:00–12:00 PT during business hours to keep Release Eng available.

Risks
- If CI loses access to signing step, Private release artifacts may be blocked.
- If wrong creds are rotated, pipeline may fall back to unsigned artifacts (must be prevented by gating; confirm fail-closed behavior).

Acceptance criteria
- Old CI credentials revoked/disabled.
- Signing stage succeeds in staging and produces:
  - bundle manifest
  - detached signature file
  - signing metadata (key id / trust root reference)
- Installer preflight verification passes using a staging bundle.
- Audit log contains entries showing:
  - secret rotation event (where available)
  - signing job execution with new identity
- Rollback plan documented (re-enable previous creds only with Security approval, time-boxed).

Owners / reviewers
- Assignee (CI): Sahana Iyer
- Secrets/KMS: Hanae Suzuki
- Release: Connor O’Brien
- Security review: Marcus Lin

Notes
- This rotation is part of ongoing hardening following the signing key ceremony; see evidence guide for required artifacts/screenshots.

2026-01-08 10:14 PT — Hanae Suzuki (Reporter)
Created to coordinate CI secret rotation ahead of next RC cut. Security request: rotate CI auth tokens used to fetch signing credentials + artifact publishing credentials. Signing private key remains in HSM/KMS, not rotated in this ticket.

Requested deliverables:
- New CI identity (service account) with least-privilege policies
- Disable old CI identity
- Evidence: job run IDs + change record

Looping in Sahana (CI) and Connor (Release).
2026-01-08 11:02 PT — Sahana Iyer (Assignee)
Plan proposal:
1) Create new CI service account: ri-ci-signing-v2 (scoped to signing pipeline only).
2) Bind least-privilege policies (read-only secret paths for signing session token + write-only artifact publish path).
3) Update CI variables for the release pipeline.
4) Run staging pipeline:
   - Build bundle
   - Sign manifest
   - Verify with installer preflight on a staging VM
5) Revoke ri-ci-signing-v1.

Open question: do we need a dual-run period (both creds valid) to avoid mid-flight failures? Suggest 24h overlap; ok to revoke after validation run completes.

Requesting approvals from Marcus + Connor for revoke timing.
2026-01-08 12:18 PT — Connor O’Brien
Approved 24h overlap. Please ensure release gating is still fail-closed if signing step cannot access secrets (no unsigned artifacts published). After rotation, run the RC validation job in staging (same as we’ll run for the release train).

Also: capture exact principal name used in the job output for audit evidence.
2026-01-09 09:37 PT — Hanae Suzuki
Created ri-ci-signing-v2 in secrets backend and generated new short-lived auth method config for CI (TTL 30m, renewable during job). Policy attached:
- read: secret/signing/session-token
- read: secret/signing/trust-store-public-keys (for metadata)
- write: artifacts/private/offline-bundles/staging/*
- deny: any other paths

Shared new credential reference with Sahana via approved channel (not in ticket).
2026-01-09 10:26 PT — Sahana Iyer
Updated staging pipeline configuration:
- rotated CI variable reference SIGNING_SECRETS_AUTH -> points to v2
- rotated ARTIFACT_PUBLISH_TOKEN -> v2 publisher token

Kicked off pipeline run: private-offline-bundle-sign (staging).
Validation checklist in progress:
[ ] signing step can fetch session token
[ ] manifest signature created
[ ] artifacts published
[ ] installer preflight verify passes

Will post job ID + installer output once complete.
2026-01-09 11:41 PT — Sahana Iyer
Staging pipeline completed successfully.
- Job: private-offline-bundle-sign / run #18427 (staging)
- Signing step identity in logs: ri-ci-signing-v2

Installer verification:
- redwood-private-installer preflight against bundle build-id: rpi-private-staging-2026.01.09.18427
- Result: PASS (signature valid, manifest hashes match)

Next step: schedule revocation of v1 after 24h overlap unless objections.
2026-01-10 08:05 PT — Marcus Lin
Security sign-off:
- Confirmed v2 scope aligns with least privilege.
- OK to revoke v1 after overlap. Ensure revocation evidence (change log entry or screenshot) is attached/recorded.
- Reminder: if any break-glass path exists in CI for unsigned publish, it must remain disabled for release branches.

No further concerns.
2026-01-10 10:12 PT — Sahana Iyer
Revocation executed:
- Disabled ri-ci-signing-v1 auth + artifact publisher token.
- Confirmed staging signing pipeline still works with v2 by re-running a short “sign-only” validation (run #18466).

Evidence captured:
- secrets backend change record: CHG-77219 (internal)
- job runs: #18427 and #18466

Proposing to resolve ticket after 1 business day of monitoring for unexpected CI failures.
2026-01-12 09:18 PT — Sahana Iyer
No CI regressions observed post-rotation; release train signing jobs succeeded in staging and dev.

Resolution:
- CI secrets rotated to ri-ci-signing-v2
- Old creds revoked
- End-to-end signing + installer verification validated

Follow-ups (not blocking):
- Add automated check in pipeline to print the principal name + key id to a standardized “evidence” section for faster audits.

Marking Resolved.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A PDF batch from vendor ThermaFlex Ltd. (received via AP email) contained three physical invoices stapled together. Our scanning pipeline ingested the file as a single invoice record, merged line items and totals, and created an invalid posting that failed three-way PO matching. The scheduled payrun (03/12) was blocked for this vendor as the system flagged an unresolvable mismatch and duplicate detection prevented manual splitting during the automated pre-check stage.

Impact:
- One vendor payment (ThermaFlex Ltd.) not processed in the 03/12 payrun (approx. $68,400 total across three invoices).
- AP team unable to clear the payrun because the ingestion-created invoice record fails GL allocation and PO reconciliation checks.
- Risk of late fees and vendor escalations if not resolved before next pay cycle.

Environment:
- Prod AP ingestion pipeline (ocr-batch-ingest v2.4.1)
- Scanner vendor: PaperFlow Services (scanned PDF file: TF_20260309_batch_A.pdf)
- Regions affected: us-east (primary AP region)

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Received email with TF_20260309_batch_A.pdf attached (3 invoices stapled).
2) PDF passed to ocr-batch-ingest which runs page-level OCR then document-level consolidation.
3) Consolidation logic merged the three invoices into one invoice record because no explicit page-break anchors were found.
4) Generated invoice record had combined amounts and three different invoice numbers concatenated in the invoice_number field (e.g., "INV-1001;;;INV-1002;;;INV-1003").
5) AP system attempted PO matching and GL mapping: failed because combined totals did not equal any single PO, and 'duplicate detection' flagged the record as suspicious.
6) Payrun pre-check aborted and held the vendor group.

Error artifacts / logs:
- ocr-batch-ingest logs (ingest_id: ingest-20260309-77e2) show repeated pattern: "WARN: page_anchor_not_found, consolidating pages into single doc"
- Ingest error code: INV_PARSE_422
- OCR confidences (per page): 0.88, 0.84, 0.67 — third page contains lower confidence & partial footer obscured by staple crease.
- AP UI record ID: APINV-20260309-553 (shows combined totals and concatenated invoice_number).

Investigation notes (initial):
- Finance triage (Leah): Verified physical PDF had three distinct invoice headers when viewed in Preview. Manual split resolves PO matching.
- OCR engineer (Oscar): Confirmed consolidation module falls back to document-level grouping when page anchors absent; current heuristics miss stapled multi-invoice batches where header margin is reduced.
- SRE: No platform-wide degradation; ingestion throughput normal.

Workarounds applied / temporary resolution:
- AP team manually created three invoice records in the AP UI using the original PDF pages as attachments and matched them to the correct POs. Manual payment release processed for one invoice immediately; remaining two are queued pending final approver signatures.
- For immediate payrun unblock: OS (Oscar) applied a temporary ingest rule to force page-level split for files from "thermaflex@invoices.com" for the March 9–12 window. This bypass is logged and will be reverted after confirmation.

Proposed permanent fixes / follow-ups:
1) Engineering task: Enhance ocr-batch-ingest to detect page-boundary invoice anchors and add a page-break classifier (ML-based or heuristic) to avoid consolidating physically grouped invoices. (Create follow-up INT ticket for the eng task).
2) Update AP pre-check UI to allow ops to flag an invoice record as "split candidate" and provide an inline tool to split into N records before payrun locking.
3) Add additional OCR rules to detect repeated "Invoice Number" headers per page and prefer page-scope parsing when multiple headers exist.
4) Run a targeted backfill for ThermaFlex and other vendors with a history of multi-invoice scans for the last 30 days to ensure no missed payments.

Attachments / Links:
- Original PDF: TF_20260309_batch_A.pdf (stored in finance-shared S3: s3://redwood-finance/inbound/TF_20260309_batch_A.pdf)
- Ingest trace: https://logs.redwood.local/ingest/ingest-20260309-77e2
- AP UI record: https://ap-console.redwood.local/invoices/APINV-20260309-553
- Slack thread: #finance-ap (thread ts: 1611499328.000400)

Next actions (owners / ETA):

Additional notes:
SLA / urgency justification:
- P1 due to direct blocking of scheduled vendor payment and potential financial penalties. Recommended targeted response within 24 hours and full remediation plan within 5 business days.
2026-03-10 11:05 - SRE (Marta Hughes): Confirmed no anomalies in platform infra. Temporary ingest rule deployed on ingest-nodes-us-east; attached node logs to ingest trace link. Recommend manual approval path in AP UI to avoid repeated bypasses.
payload.summary: Scanned vendor batch with multiple stapled invoices ingested as single invoice, posting fails and blocks payment run

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A Redwood engineer reported seeing multiple active privileged sessions from the same browser after clicking a shortened external link (peer recruitment message). The link redirected through two intermediate domains before landing on a page that initiated an SSO flow. Instead of a normal interactive consent, the SSO redirect sequence completed in a way that swapped a pre-existing OAuth refresh token and produced new API tokens usable by the attacker's agent.

Impact:
- 3 developer accounts temporarily had additional active sessions with elevated API privileges (access to private model rollout configs and a limited set of deployment APIs).
- No confirmed data exfiltration found so far; investigation ongoing.
- Potential lateral access risk to adjacent internal services if tokens were reused.

Detection:
- Detected via IAM session anomaly alerts (unfamiliar user_agent + repeated token exchange within 2s window) generated by Security Telemetry.
- User reported odd multi-session popup and later elevated activity in their session list.

Initial timeline (approx):
- 2026-03-10 08:47 UTC: user receives Slack DM with shortened URL (snip.ly/abc123).
- 2026-03-10 08:48 UTC: user clicks link; browser opens external redirect chain.
- 2026-03-10 08:48:12 UTC: SSO redirect initiates; user briefly sees consent dialog (may have been auto-closed by redirect).
- 2026-03-10 08:48:15 UTC: additional sessions appear for user and for two service accounts they recently accessed.

Why unique / hypothesis:
The redirect chain included a scripted auto-post back to the SSO callback URL with a forged state token that matched an existing browser state, which allowed the attacker-controlled page to complete the OAuth handshake without explicit user interaction. This appears to be a subtle token swap rather than classic credential harvesting. A secondary hypothesis is a malicious intermediary inserting an id_token exchange for a different client_id that maps to elevated scopes in our SSO configuration.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Revoked suspicious refresh tokens for affected accounts.
- Forced re-authentication for the SSO application used by developer tools.
- Blocked the shortlink domain at corporate web proxy and added domain to threat list.
- Isolated the three affected hosts for further forensic capture (memory + browser artifacts).

Next steps:
- Full Okta/IdP audit for token exchange patterns in the 08:40-09:00 UTC window.
- Review SSO client configs for overly permissive redirect URI handling and implicit flows.
- Add telemetry rule to flag rapid token exchange + redirect chain lengths >2.
- Work with Legal/PR if any customer-facing disclosure needed.
1) Simulate redirect chain: shortened URL -> attacker site -> attacker-postback -> IdP callback.
2) On a session with an active refresh token for the SSO app, perform a crafted POST to the OAuth callback with a forged code/state pair tied to attacker-controlled client metadata.
3) Observe server issuing new id_token/access_token and session creation for the victim account without explicit interactive consent.
Note: reproduction requires privileged access to IdP test environment; do not attempt in prod without SSO team coordination.
2026-03-10T08:48:15Z auth.token.exchange user=ajkumar@redwood.com client_id=dev-console ip=18.205.14.33 ua=Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT) session_id=abc12345 action=exchange status=200 duration_ms=58
2026-03-10T08:48:16Z iam.session.create user=ajkumar@redwood.com session_id=abc12345 actor=browser origin=external_redirect grant=scoped_deploy_api
2026-03-10T08:48:17Z telemetry.anomaly rule=rapid_token_swap score=92 users=[ajkumar@redwood.com] ips=[18.205.14.33]

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:15 - SRE (Daniel Reyes): Okta logs pulled (request id okta-20260310-651). Noted a repeated /oauth2/v1/token POST with identical ip and sub-second repeats. Confirmed no bulk revocation by IdP yet; coordinating with IdP SRE to escalate revocation and rotate client secrets if needed.
2026-03-10 11:40 - Reporter (Aisha Kumar): Provided screenshots of the popup and Slack DM thread. No password was entered. Happy to preserve devices for forensics; laptop currently quarantined as requested.
Checked CloudTrail for cross-account activity — no IAM AssumeRole artifacts beyond user sessions.
Confirmed the IdP returned tokens with scopes that include 'deploy:write' for a subset of sessions — likely due to client misbinding.
Reproduced redirect-chain behavior in sandbox IdP with controlled test client; observed that an attacker-controlled page can auto-submit a form with code/state to the IdP callback and complete the flow if the browser still holds a valid session cookie.
No evidence yet of long-lived exfiltration — telemetry shows no large download spikes from code repos or model artifacts tied to affected sessions.
Workaround and containment completed: revoked all suspect refresh tokens, blocked malicious shortlink and intermediary domains, quarantined affected endpoints, required reauth for sensitive SSO apps, and deployed a telemetry rule to detect rapid token-exchange bursts. Long-term fixes: enforce PKCE for applicable clients, tighten redirect URI matching rules, and add automated blocking of suspicious redirect chains. Security will coordinate with IdP vendor to rotate client secrets for internal apps and run a global token revocation sweep if further anomalies are found.
payload.summary: External shortened URL triggered silent SSO token swap; multiple privileged sessions observed

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During an automated ephemeral pool scale-up for BlueWave Health (enterprise tenant), we observed a sustained elevation of 5xx responses (~8-12% error rate on the tenant's routes) for ~45 minutes. Errors manifested as 502/503 from the API gateway and short-lived upstream runtime exits. This appears correlated with ephemeral proxy socket leakage combined with aggressive TLS session pruning on the tenant's route.

Impact:
- Customer reports failed inference requests and client-side retry loops producing repeated billing attempts.
- Estimate: ~1.2k failed requests per minute at peak, latency doubled for successful requests.
- Affected customer flows: chat streaming and bulk embedding uploads. Business impact: degraded SLAs and customer support escalations.

Environment:
- prod (us-east-1) cluster serving BlueWave Health (enterprise).
- Tenant pinned to a dedicated subset within shared ephemeral pool.
- Autoscaler triggered scale-up at 2026-03-10T02:11:00Z.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Simulate tenant load spike mirroring customer's embedding + chat mix (high concurrent short requests + occasional large embedding batches).
2) Trigger autoscaler scale-up of ephemeral worker group (same policy as production).
3) Observe keepalive socket pool growth and TLS session churn.
4) Notice API gateway responses 502/503 and runtime restarts from ephemeral proxies.

Observed logs / metrics (selected):
- apigw.error.rate (tenant route): baseline 0.3% -> peak 11% between 02:12-02:55 UTC.
- ephemeral-proxy.conn_count: sudden growth from 120 -> 2.1k within 90s during scale-up.
- ephemeral-proxy.fd_usage: approaching OS soft limit on several nodes (sample node: node-eph-17 fd_usg 93%).
- runtime.exit_count: +18 exits correlated with scale-up window. Kernel logs show repeated EMFILE on proxy process.
- sample request ids with 502: [req:b7f3c2a1, req:bf21d3a8, req:c2aa1b77]. Trace link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant/bluewave?from=1617310000000&to=1617315000000

Initial hypothesis:
- Rapid ephemeral worker scale-up increased concurrent accept/connect attempts and pushed proxy socket pools to OS limits. A subtle connection leak in the ephemeral proxy caused sockets to remain in CLOSE_WAIT; combined with TLS session pruning, this prevented efficient reuse and led to amplifyhed retries from clients. Hedged retry behavior on the API gateway amplified load and produced a retry loop producing more failed attempts.

Workaround applied so far:
- Temporarily disabled hedged retry for BlueWave tenant routes at 2026-03-10T03:05 UTC (reduced retry amplification).
- Increased ephemeral-proxy system fd soft limit from 4096 to 16384 on affected nodes as an emergency relief at 2026-03-10T03:12 UTC.
- Applied a short-term kernel-level keepalive tuning (tcp_fin_timeout lowered from 60->30s) to speed socket cleanup.

Next steps / action items:
- SRE: Deploy a fix to close connection handle path in ephemeral-proxy (assigned, investigating memory of fd table). Link: github.com/redwood-inference/ephemeral-proxy/issues/1221.
- Platform: Add rate-limiting guard during autoscaler-driven ramp-ups to keep accept-queue growth bounded.
- Engineering: Audit TLS session prune policy interplay with keepalive reuse and add integration test covering scale-up scenarios.
- CS/Support: Coordinate with BlueWave to blacklist aggressive client retry policies and confirm billing adjustments.

Notes:
- No evidence of GPU OOM; runtime exits point to proxy-level EMFILE and accept-queue exhaustion.
- Related incidents show similar symptoms but different root causes; this one is primarily connection-leak + scale-up interaction.

2026-03-10 03:20 Z - Marcus Chen (SRE): Scoped the problematic nodes and increased fd limits; disabled hedged retry for tenant as temporary mitigation.
2026-03-10 05:10 Z - Asha Rao (Support): Customer confirmed reduced error rate to ~0.8% after mitigations; still seeing occasional 502s during their large batch uploads.
2026-03-11 09:02 Z - Ingrid Müller (Platform Eng): Reproduced the leak locally by running scale-up harness; file descriptor table did not always release on connection close in ephemeral-proxy v2.3.4. Preparing PR.
2026-03-11 15:45 Z - Marcus Chen (SRE): Scheduled a staged rollout of ephemeral-proxy patch to canary nodes in us-east-1 tomorrow 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC. Added temporary autoscaler ramp throttle.
2026-03-12 02:30 Z - Asha Rao (Support): Notified BlueWave of planned maintenance window for patch rollout and confirmed monitoring cadence.
Canary reproducer shows fd leak occurs when connection teardown races with internal session prune task. The leak is in connection_release() path where some sockets skip close() on backpressure. Attach: reproducer script and kernel logs uploaded to artifact store.
Disabled hedged retries for tenant; raised fd limits and tuned tcp_fin_timeout; limited autoscaler ramp velocity for ephemeral workers.
(pending) Patch PR #8432 ready; awaiting canary verification. If canary passes, schedule full rollout with pre-warm ramp throttle. Postmortem planned once resolved.
payload.summary: Connection leakage during ephemeral scale-up causing throttled 5xx and client retry-loop amplification

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We need a short-lived, auditable broker role that lets SRE/Platform engineers assume cross-account access into customer-facing Dedicated and Private environments (AWS/GCP) for live debugging and incident response. The broker should centralize approval, rotate credentials automatically, and emit audit events to the central logging pipeline.

Background:
Recent incidents required manual cross-account key exchange and one-off service-account impersonation. That flow caused delays and missing audit context when engineers debugged GPU-backed inference stacks in customer staging and prod. We want a managed ephemeral path that enforces least privilege and automatic expiry.

Impact:
- Time-to-diagnose is increased for Sev1/Sev2 incidents affecting dedicated/private customers.
- Manual processes create orphaned access snapshots and inconsistent audit trails.

Request / Acceptance criteria:
- Provision a broker IAM role (AWS) and a service-account impersonation flow (GCP) that can be assumed via a short-lived session (max 1 hour).
- Central approval: integrate with internal approval workflow (Slack + Approvals API) and capture approver identity in audit logs.
- RBAC mapping: broker maps to scoped roles (e.g., readonly-serving, gpu-debug) rather than full admin.
- Automatic credential lifecycle: no long-lived keys; sessions are ephemeral and recorded.
- Logging: all assume/impersonation events logged to central Cloud Logging and forwarded to SIEM.
- Revocation: ability to immediately revoke active sessions and list active sessions per engineer.

Security constraints and notes:
- No direct customer secrets or keys are exposed in Slack.
- Use KMS/HSM-backed signing for temporary credentials issuance where supported.
- All changes must be reviewed by Security before prod enablement.

Expiry policy and audit retention:
- Default session TTL: 30 minutes; configurable up to 1 hour with justification.
- Audit records retained according to compliance policy (90 days hot, 1 year cold).

Owners and timeline:
- Owner: Diego Morales (Platform/SRE)
N/A (operational request). Example of current manual flow: 1) Engineer requests cross-account SA key via #priv-access, 2) Infra provides short-lived key in DM, 3) Engineer uses key to access customer VPC and run debug commands. This flow lacks centralized approval metadata and consistent logging.

Additional notes:
Reviewed existing INT-11456 (scoped debug role) for patterns to reuse resource naming and policies.
Checked current org trust relationships for aws:role assumption and gcp:iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permissions; some accounts require org-level changes.
Evaluated open-source brokers (HashiCorp Boundary, short-lived session helpers) — decided to implement a lightweight internal broker to keep tighter audit hooks.
Identified required change windows for accounts with strict Service Perimeter (GCP) — will coordinate with Cloud Platform team for rollout.
Mapping proposal: broker -> scoped role policies: readonly-serving, gpu-debug, network-trace. Each mapping will be a separate policy attached at request time.
WIP: terraform module created in branch infra/ephemeral-iam-broker; PR opened for review (see related_github_prs).
Next steps: 1) Security review (Priya), 2) Automation for Slack approval -> Approvals API webhook (Diego), 3) Integration test with staging accounts, 4) Runbook and oncall training, 5) Prod enablement behind feature-flag.
If approved, will schedule a small canary with SRE on 2026-03-24 to validate session expiry and revocation flows.
payload.summary: Provision ephemeral IAM broker role and cross-account access for runtime debugging across GCP/AWS

Requesting GitHub access required to update and review the public status page component registry (component ids/display names/ownership/rollout flags) as part of the “Status page transparency upgrades” initiative.

Background / why:
- We’re moving the component mapping + registry to a repo-backed source of truth per ADR-014.
- Ongoing work requires occasional edits to the registry + mapping rules (new components, ownership changes, hotfixes for misclassification).
- Current state: I can open PRs but cannot (a) merge after required reviews, and (b) update CODEOWNERS/team review requirements for the registry path. This is blocking taxonomy rollout and on-call readiness.

Access requested:
1) Add me (Christine Wong) to GitHub team with write access to the repo(s) that contain the registry + mapping config:
   - repo: observability-pack (registry schema + registry JSON)
   - repo: incident-bot (intake fields + enforcement)
   - repo: redwood (service-to-component mapping layer)
2) Add me to the reviewers/owners group for the registry directory so I can participate in required review flows (not bypass them).

Scope / guardrails:
- Least-privilege preferred: write access + PR merge rights constrained to these repos; no admin access needed.
- Maintain review requirements: changes to registry should continue to require SRE/Observability review (Rafael Mendes / Allison Grant or delegates).

People to include (if applicable):
- Christine Wong (requester; implementer)
- Ravi Menon (service-to-component mapping)
- Devon Price (incident-bot automation engineer)

Target date:
- Needed by EOW to unblock component taxonomy rollout work in ENG-4821/ENG-4830 and avoid last-minute manual edits during staged rollout.

Approval:

2025-11-11 09:18 (Christine Wong): Adding detail: the registry path is being validated via CI (schema checks). I’m not asking to bypass checks—just to be able to maintain the registry and participate in ownership/review changes as we stabilize rollout flags (dogfood vs public).
2025-11-11 10:02 (Owen Phillips): Acknowledged. To proceed I need: (1) exact GitHub org/team name to add you to (if already exists), or confirmation we should create a new team; (2) list of users requiring access. payload.description:
Multiple provisioning jobs for returned/repaired laptops are hanging during the post-image checkin stage. Investigation points to a udev rule left behind by a vendor USB management tool that triggers a blocking call in the provisioning agent when the device is present.
Blocking autopilot-style provisioning in staging for ~6% of depot-return devices. Slows depot throughput and prevents automatic re-enrollment; potential customer-impact if regression reaches prod.
Observed in staging-us-east image pipeline. Repro rate higher on devices that previously received vendor dongle firmware update (security tokens used in corporate field repair workflow). Affected devices boot to Windows PE then the provisioning agent runs and stalls at hardware enumeration step.
1) Take a repaired laptop that previously had vendor security dongle attached. 2) Flash latest vendor dongle firmware using vendor tool. 3) Wipe and image device via depot imaging pipeline. 4) Wait for provisioning agent to perform hardware checks — process stalls during udev/driver enumeration and provisioning does not progress.
Provisioning-agent log snippet:
[2026-03-08 09:12:03] provisioning-agent: start hardware-check
[2026-03-08 09:12:03] provisioning-agent: enumerate-blocking-drivers
[2026-03-08 09:12:03] udev: found rule 99-vendor-token.rules -> executing handler '/usr/local/bin/vendor-token-probe'
[2026-03-08 09:12:03] vendor-token-probe: waiting for HSM init (timeout suppressed)
... (no further progress)

- Reproduced locally with a test token: vendor probe script enters a blocking wait for token initialization when run by system user in provisioning context.
- The vendor's MSIX installer drops a udev rule in /etc/udev/rules.d/99-vendor-token.rules that invokes /usr/local/bin/vendor-token-probe on add events.
- In depot images the provisioning agent triggers a udev enumerate which fires the rule; vendor-token-probe expects interactive environment and hangs.
- Temporary workaround: remove the udev rule before running provisioning agent or override probe script to exit quickly if run as 'provisioning-agent' user.
- Root cause: vendor firmware flash tool bundles a hardware integration package that was not removed during field repair; our imaging sequence does not always scrub third-party udev entries when wiping user space artifacts on returned units.
1) Manual removal of /etc/udev/rules.d/99-vendor-token.rules allowed provisioning to complete. 2) Updated staging image to include udev rule cleanup hook; short-term patch applied to depot 'pre-imaging cleanup' script. 3) Created a feature flag in provisioning-agent to ignore udev-triggered handlers when running in automated depot context.
Run 'rm /etc/udev/rules.d/99-vendor-token.rules' in pre-imaging hook or boot to WinPE and use our depot cleanup script prior to starting provisioning agent.
1) Add a robust cleanup step to depot imaging that removes third-party udev rules and vendor probe binaries. 2) Update provisioning-agent to run udev enumeration under a filtered environment that does not trigger external handlers. 3) Open vendor support case to request an updated firmware package that does not drop a blocking probe script or to document safe uninstall steps.
Low risk for imaging pipeline if cleanup runs; provisioning-agent feature-flag change is reversible. Vendor engagement may take longer — we'll maintain cleanup script until vendor releases updated package.
- (Liam) finalize and land pre-imaging cleanup patch to staging by 2026-03-11. - (Priya) open vendor support ticket and attach logs by 2026-03-10. - (Eng Ops) schedule a canary where 5% of depot images run the cleanup hook for 48 hours. - (SRE) add alert to detect provisioning stalls >10m during hardware-check.
payload.summary: Provisioning hang caused by orphaned udev rule from USB dongle firmware update

comments: 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Aisha Raman: We're seeing recurring 429s exactly at 30s intervals during our ingest window. We only get partial success after retries. Can you help us avoid retries and reduce failed requests?

2026-03-12T00:00:00Z Packetwave: After increasing TTL to 120s and lowering concurrency to 90 we observed ~90% reduction in 429 waves during test run. Still want a permanent fix so we don't have to throttle ourselves.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Packetwave reports recurring 429 responses in their dedicated pool during a daily high-concurrency job that multiplexes short-lived SSE/websocket embed requests and low-latency chat calls. The 429s arrive in short, regular waves (1–3 minutes) rather than a single sustained throttle; patterns align with ephemeral-proxy handoffs and orchestrator rebalancing.

Impact:
- ~15% of their user-facing chat requests get 429s for brief intervals, causing degraded UX and automatic retry loops in their orchestrator.
- Background embed imports (bulk, short-lived connections) see partial failures that require retrying, increasing cost.

Observed behavior:
- 429s stamped with route=/v1/embeddings and X-Rate-Limit-Reason: window_refill_mismatch.
- Console shows token bucket refill pulses on the edge roughly every 30s but origin refill uses a 60s epoch for the same tenant when ephemeral-proxy IPs change.
- Failures correlate with Packetwave's upload workers that spin up many ephemeral HTTP/2 streams with short TTL keys.

Expected behavior:
- Short-lived connections and ephemeral keys should not induce repeated tenant-level 429 waves every refill epoch. Edge and origin should align refill windows or gracefully handle handoff without double-counting.

1) Use dedicated tenant with mixed traffic: many short-lived embed upload workers (concurrency 200), plus low-latency chat connections multiplexed via HTTP/2.
2) Rotate ephemeral keys frequently (TTL 45s) and reuse them across workers while keeping connection pooling at the edge.
3) Observe tenant-level token bucket consumption in console; watch for 429 bursts at 30s intervals while origin refill logs show 60s epochs.
[2026-03-10T18:02:30Z] edge-proxy: POST /v1/embeddings 429 tenant=pw-881 token=abcd... reason=window_refill_mismatch

[2026-03-10T18:02:31Z] origin-rate-limiter: tenant=pw-881 window_epoch=60s refill=10000 credits

[2026-03-10T18:02:31Z] edge-rate-limiter: tenant=pw-881 window_epoch=30s refill=5000 credits

Trace: connection=ephemeral-https-8743 -> proxied-ip=10.2.4.33 reused-for-4-sessions

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 — Support (Ethan Morales): Thanks, Aisha — we see matching 429 signatures. We're triaging rate-limiter logs and checking alignment between edge refill and origin refill windows. Please share your worker concurrency and ephemeral key TTLs (you included them above; we'll validate against telemetry).
2026-03-11 — SRE (Maya Singh): Initial hypothesis: edge-level token counting uses a shorter refill epoch when connection pool affinity is high (per-proxy IP window). When ephemeral keys move between proxies the origin's tenant accounting resyncs on a different epoch resulting in transient double-counting. Repro steps created; capturing pcap and sampling proxy affinity.
2026-03-11 — Support (Ethan Morales): Provided temporary mitigation to Packetwave: 1) Reduce worker concurrency to 80–100 during ingest window; 2) Increase ephemeral key TTL to 120s to reduce handoffs; 3) Requesting isolated burst pool for their embedding route while we patch. Packetwave will test and report by EOD.
Edge and origin rate-limiter code paths use separate window_epoch defaults; edge uses 30s for per-proxy affinity accounting, origin uses tenant-level 60s. This mismatch surfaces when ephemeral keys cause rapid proxy handoffs.
Observed duplicate credit deduction when a request is counted at edge (proxy A) and origin then re-evaluates the token consumption under a different epoch boundary after the handoff — net effect looks like faster depletion resulting in a 429 spike.
Recreated locally with k6-based harness that simulates 200 short-lived streams with TTL 45s; reproduces 429 waves matching customer pattern.
Hypothesis: two mitigation paths: align refill epochs (config change) or make origin-idempotent accounting that dedupes short-window double-counts keyed by request-id / ephemeral-token fingerprint.
Performance note: changing origin accounting to dedupe requires careful coordination and a migration plan; aligning epochs at edge to 60s may increase perceived burstiness for other tenants — consider tenant-scoped override for dedicated pools.
Workaround provided (reduce concurrency, increase ephemeral TTL, requested isolated burst pool). Engineering to schedule change: tenant-scoped refill-alignment flag for dedicated pools. Patch PR opened to add a per-tenant config; follow-up rollout planned after tests.
payload.summary: Staggered 429 waves caused by short-window refill mismatch during ephemeral-proxy handoff in hybrid embed/chat workload

payload.description:
Issue summary: During the 2026-03-12 nightly gated release, several CI jobs using the 'release-runner-us-east' service account failed to start. The pipeline stalled at 'Acquire runner' with 403/401-style authorization failures from the cloud IAM token exchange. Impact: Nightly release blocked for ~3.5 hours, manual rollback required for one canary. Environment: Production CI (self-hosted runners) in us-east region; release window 02:00-06:00 UTC. Affected components: ci-runner, auth, vault, gcp-iam. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger gated release pipeline targeting canary group. 2) Observe runner registration step hang and repeated auth errors in runner logs. 3) Attempt manual token refresh via ci-admin account fails with 'conditional access denied' response. Logs & observed errors: - Runner: "401: AccessDenied - ConditionalAccessPolicyRestrictsSignIn" - Token-service: "403 Forbidden: token exchange blocked by CA policy (require compliant device)" - Vault: "wrapped token unwrap succeeded" (no obvious Vault error) Notes: This appears related to a Conditional Access (CA) policy change that started enforcing device compliance for service principals earlier today. The release-runner service account uses short-lived OIDC tokens minted by the CI control plane; the policy may be evaluating the identity as a user session rather than a machine identity. No previous incidents observed for this runner pool.

Additional notes:
Hypothesis A: Conditional Access policy treats any token exchange originating from the CI control plane as interactive because the exchange path includes a user-agent header from the webhook proxy.
Hypothesis B: New SecOps rule was applied broadly to service principals; vault-wrapped tokens lack the expected claim ('client_type':'machine') used by the CA gating logic.
Observed: Vault unwrap and local token caching succeeded; failure occurs on cloud IAM token mint step returning CA deny.
Correlation: Policy change timestamp aligns with start of failures. No code deploys to CI control plane during window.
Temporary mitigation: IAM applied an exclusion that restored runner auth but is not acceptable long-term. Need documented JIT exclusion and automation guardrails.
Next steps: 1) Define durable signal in OIDC token (e.g., add 'auth_method':'pod_identity' or 'client_type':'service') and coordinate with SecOps to map condition. 2) Harden CI token exchange to use dedicated mTLS channel for machine identities. 3) Add synthetic checks to detect CA policy regression before release windows.
Temporary workaround applied: SecOps added a scoped Conditional Access exclusion for the 'release-runner-sp' service principal and the nightly pipeline was resumed. Root cause: SecOps rollout of a device_compliance requirement inadvertently matched the CI token exchange path because tokens lacked a machine signal. Permanent fix plan: 1) Implement token claim augmentation in the CI token-minting service to include 'client_type':'machine' and 'auth_method':'oidc:ci' (PRs opened: infra#2418, ci#1192). 2) Coordinate with SecOps to map a CA condition that evaluates the new claim instead of blanket device_compliance. 3) Add pre-release synthetic gating that validates runner registration under current CA rules (task assigned to Release Eng). Follow-ups: update runbooks and add an automated rollback if CA changes block runner auth. Target completion: 2026-03-24.
1) SecOps: Add Conditional Access exclusion for 'release-runner-sp' (scoped to CI token exchange endpoints) to restore pipeline. (Already applied)
2) Release Eng: Avoid scheduling high-risk gated nightlies until claim augmentation is deployed.
3) SRE: Monitor runner registration metrics and alert on CA-deny spikes with a 1-minute window.
payload.summary: Locked runner service account access due to Conditional Access policy during nightly gated release

Issue summary:
A vendor invoice for contractor services (INV-2026-0487) was submitted and validated against PO 45001-A. After validation, Procurement created a change order that introduced a new PO suffix (45001-B) to capture scope adjustments. The AP system attempted to auto-match the invoice to the original PO (45001-A) but then flagged a mismatch when the ledger posting required the updated PO suffix. This has caused the payment to be placed on hold pending manual PO reconciliation and GL code confirmation.

Impact:
- One outstanding vendor payment (~$82,400 USD) is blocked for the weekly payment run scheduled on 2026-03-12.
- Vendor has sent a reminder escalation to Accounts Payable.
- Risk of late fees and strained vendor relationship if not resolved before the next scheduled run.

Environment:
- AP system: Redwood AP v2.4 (hosted prod)
- Procurement system: Procurement Portal v1.9 (SaaS)
- Payment processor: FinPay (ACH/SEPA)

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence of events:
1) Vendor submitted invoice INV-2026-0487 referencing PO 45001-A on 2026-03-04.
2) Invoice matched to PO 45001-A and routed to approvals.
3) Procurement created change order CO-334 on 2026-03-06, which updated the formal PO suffix to 45001-B to reflect scope and budget reallocation. Change order note: "retro change for additional hours; amend PO suffix B".
4) AP attempted ledger posting on 2026-03-09; system matched line-level amounts to PO 45001-A initially, then failed final validation because the canonical PO suffix in procurement is 45001-B.
5) Payment entry placed on hold with reason code: PO_MISMATCH_SUFFIX.

Attachments/References:
- Invoice: INV-2026-0487.pdf (attached to ticket)
- Change order: CO-334.pdf (attached)
- Slack thread: #ap-escalations (link in comments)

Expected behavior:
- Invoice should either auto-resolve to the most recent PO revision/suffix when the change order is explicitly linked, or AP should surface a clear user action to reconcile the PO suffix during payment approval.

Desired immediate outcome:
- Clear reconciliation path so payment can be released in the 2026-03-12 payment run, with a documented audit trail linking the invoice, original PO, and change order.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:30 - Reproduced behavior in staging: when procurement API returns multiple PO revisions, AP comparator chooses the earliest active revision rather than the most recent. This is an edge case introduced by simultaneous invoice arrival and CO creation within a 72-hour window.
Logs: ap-matcher-prod.log lines 2458-2475 show match attempt for INV-2026-0487 -> candidate POs [45001-A (created 2026-02-10), 45001-B (created 2026-03-06)]. Comparator score tied on amount and vendor, timestamp tie-breaker selected earlier.
Error code surfaced: PO_MISMATCH_SUFFIX.

Cross-ref: see INT-246801 (stuck-approval-role-sync-failure) for previous cases where repayments were delayed due to mismatched metadata between Procurement and AP. Procurement has been notified to update the PO API to include a canonical 'current_revision' field.

This will allow release in the upcoming payment run. Procurement to confirm the canonical PO revision in the procurement API to prevent recurrence.
AP to perform manual reconciliation and attempt payment release (target: 2026-03-11 EOD).
Procurement to add 'current_revision' flag to PO API and update CO creation flow to optionally mark 'replace_previous_revision' for retroactive changes (ticket raised with Procurement engineering).
Platform/Eng to patch AP comparator to prefer the most recent active PO revision when multiple candidates are returned (PR reference above).
Finance to notify vendor of targeted payment date and record waiver if late fees applicable.

Issue summary: During the staged canary rollout for service 'inference-proxy' at 2026-03-12 18:05 UTC, the CI/CD pipeline failed when attempting to provision ephemeral GCP deployer certificates for new runners. Impact: Canary deployment halted in us-west and us-east, preventing automated promotion and blocking the release window. Environment: prod clusters in us-west / us-east; release triggered by release-engineering pipeline 'release/inference-proxy/v2.9.1'.
1) Trigger release/inference-proxy/v2.9.1 pipeline from release-engineering branch
2) Pipeline attempts ephemeral deployer cert issuance via infra-service account 'ci-deployer@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com'
3) Runner bootstrapping step 'bootstrap-deployer-creds' fails with certificate validation error and TLS handshake abort
4) Canary traffic not shifted, pipeline aborts due to failed smoke tests and healthchecks
[2026-03-12T18:05:11Z] bootstrap-deployer-creds: ERROR: failed to fetch ephemeral cert: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (issuer mismatch)
[2026-03-12T18:05:12Z] runner-init: WARN: falling back to cached kubeconfig (age=36h) - not allowed for ephemeral flows
Pipeline stage 'promote-canary' aborted: exit code 1
GCP IAM audit: token issue event 7e3b2c in us-west showing 'audience mismatch' for signed JWT
Canary rollout stalled in two regions. Manual promotion blocked. Estimated number of affected release windows: 1 (today). No customer-facing downtime, but release backlog now delayed and manual action required for every future ephemeral deploy until root cause fixed.
Support received alert from release-engineering at 18:12 UTC via #release-engineering channel.
Checked recent secret-rotation job run: 'ephemeral-deployer-cert-rotation' completed at 2026-03-12T17:58 UTC; rotation logs show issuer change from 'ci-issuer-v3' to 'ci-issuer-v4'.
Hypothesis: cert rotation produced new issuer value but some regional caches or long-lived runners still expect old issuer; token audience validation failing during ephemeral cert exchange.
18:20 UTC - ran 'gcloud iam service-accounts keys list' and compared thumbprints between us-west and us-east; observed different metadata timestamps but same key id.
18:27 UTC - inspected infra service 'ephemeral-issuer' deploy: found rollout of issuer v4 started at 17:58 UTC; rollout completed in control plane but edge caches (runner bootstrapper CDN) still serving v3 metadata in us-west - cache TTL misconfiguration discovered.
18:35 UTC - reproduced failure locally by forcing bootstrap flow to use issuer v3 while CA bundle contained v4 root -> x509 issuer mismatch matches production logs.
18:42 UTC - confirmed pipeline step uses library 'runner-bootstrapping'@commit a1b3f4d which validates token 'aud' against canonical issuer value embedded in the artifact. The artifact was built before rotation and still has old issuer baked in.
18:50 UTC - Slack thread #release-engineering linked to #infra-openssl: noted that rotation job replaced CA content in secret 'ephemeral-deployer-ca' but did not trigger rebuild of ephemeral runner bootstrap image.
Rolled back rotation audit marker to allow legacy issuer v3 to be accepted by the cert exchange (temporary safeguard) at 19:05 UTC.
Issued manual requeue of canary pipeline at 19:12 UTC using a patched bootstrap image (runner-bootstrapping@a1b3f4e) that accepts both v3 and v4 issuers.
Validated canary succeeded in us-east at 19:28 UTC and us-west at 19:33 UTC; smoke tests passed and promotion proceeded to scheduled canary traffic percentages.
Created short-term gating: rotation job now pauses automatic image rebuilds until CI verifies compatibility across regional caches.
Workaround applied: patched bootstrap image (runner-bootstrapping@a1b3f4e) and temporary accept-list for v3 issuer allowed immediate canary resumption.
Root cause: CA rotation completed but did not trigger coordinated artifact rebuilds and CDN/cache invalidation in the runner bootstrap path; a timing gap between rotation and artifact refresh caused issuer mismatch in bootstrapping flows.
Permanent fix: implement coordinated rotation orchestration - rotation job will now perform three steps atomically: (1) update CA and secret, (2) trigger artifact rebuild of runner-bootstrapping, (3) invalidate bootstrapper CDN caches and wait for global propagation. New orchestration playbook committed to infra repo. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2387.
Postmortem owner: Diego Martinez. Postmortem to be published by 2026-03-16 and tied to confluence page 'runner-ephemeral-rotation-postmortem'.
Follow-ups: schedule an emergency test of rotation orchestration in a staging multi-region cluster (task INT-19012 created).
