payload.description:
Issue summary: During QuantEdge's production window (09:30–12:00 UTC) on 2026-03-10 their dedicated reserved pool experienced sustained throughput degradation and rising p99 latency. Symptoms matched a capacity thinness (GPU attach failures, long queueing) rather than model-level slowdown. Impact: QuantEdge reported 40% increase in tail latency and a 30% drop in steady-state throughput for batched routes. Environment: prod-us-east-1 reserved capacity pool for customer QuantEdge (dedicated).

Observed behavior:
- Repeated short-duration GPU attach failures and allocation churn for the reserved pool between 09:32–10:20 UTC.
- Autoscaler observed transient high CPU and small I/O spikes from an analytics sidecar, classified several tenants' long-lived small-stream connections as low priority and demoted them, which then triggered reconnects and short bursts, creating a feedback loop.
- The loop caused the allocator to repeatedly steal slots and reassign, fragmenting batch formation and raising p99.

Steps to reproduce (internal reproduction):
1) Create 3 reserved-tenant workloads: heavy-batching client, long-lived keepalive low-token stream (analytics sidecar), and a medium-burst embedding job.
2) Emit irregular sidecar metric bursts (high small-IO) while keeping keepalives active.
3) Configure autoscaler with fast-demote threshold (as in QuantEdge's tenant template) and observe allocator slot churn under sustained 10–30s bursts.

Logs/alerts collected: allocation-trace.log lines 213-478 showing repeated slot reassigns; autoscaler decisions trace: demote events spiking at 09:33, 09:40, 09:51; monitoring graphs: reserved-pool-attach-fails.png and p99-latency-rise-quantedge-2026-03-10.png (attached in ticket).
Initial triage (Support): Confirmed symptoms were not model runtime errors (no OOMs, no kernel crashes). Telemetry showed bursty small-IO from a single tenant sidecar correlating with demotion events.

SRE deep-dive:
- Allocator timeline showed a repeated pattern: demote->reconnect->short-burst->prefetch->slot-fragmentation. The allocator's slot compaction lagged behind reconnects, leaving many partially filled batches.
- Autoscaler policy for 'fast-demote' (customer override) had a sensitivity that treated transient I/O/backpressure as sustained priority drop. The policy action path included an aggressive demotion that reduced tenant concurrency while failing to account for immediate reconnect behavior.
- We observed a delta in allocator heartbeats between the reserved control-plane and agents (~150–300ms) coincident with the reconnect window causing misplaced slot reclamation timing.

Hypothesis: A combination of (1) analytics sidecar emitting short-lived I/O spikes, (2) an aggressive customer-level autoscaler demote policy, and (3) heartbeat timing variance produced a feedback loop that demoted and reallocated GPUs quickly enough to fragment batching and starve steady routes.

Relevant artifacts:
- allocation-trace.log (lines referenced)
- autoscaler-audit.csv (demote decisions)
- heapster metrics: reserved_pool_slot_utilization (spike/valley pattern)
- flamegraph of allocator thread during 09:44 showing compaction stall
2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Ava Martinez): Customer reports sustained p99 increase after recent config change to 'fast-demote' in policy template. Provided request IDs and graphs. Asking for immediate mitigation.
2026-03-10 10:18 - SRE (Rafael Chen): Observed repetitive demote events correlated with sidecar bursts. Creating hypothesis and requested temp workaround: disable fast-demote for QuantEdge and increase autoscaler demote cooldown to 60s. Kicked off allocator heartbeat checks.
2026-03-10 10:40 - Customer (QuantEdge - Samir Patel): Confirmed disabling fast-demote reduced reconnects. Still seeing elevated p99 but improved throughput by ~12%. Asking for permanent fix.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Engineering (Priya Nair): Reproduced in staging, confirmed allocator compaction lag. Drafted PR to adjust demote sensitivity and add a short suppress window after demote to avoid immediate reconnect churn. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood/allocator/pull/2893
2026-03-11 09:12 - SRE (Rafael Chen): Rolled hotfix to production for reserved-pool autoscaler: increased demote cooldown to 90s and suppressed immediate demote-triggered reconnects. Monitoring closely.
Root cause: aggressive customer-level autoscaler demote policy interacting with noisy analytics sidecar and allocator heartbeat variance produced a demote/reconnect feedback loop that fragmented batching and reduced throughput.

Fix applied (2026-03-11):
- Hotfix 1: Increased demote cooldown to 90s for reserved pools and introduced a 30s 'post-demote suppress' that prevents immediate reconnect-triggered slot reclamation. Deployed via allocator hotfix (PR #2893).
- Hotfix 2: Temporary rollback of customer's 'fast-demote' override and recommended conservative demote thresholds.
- Hotfix 3: Tightened heartbeat jitter handling (reduced false-positive reclaim window) in scheduler agent.

Workarounds provided to customer:
- Disable fast-demote in tenant policy (applied by Support).
- Reduce sidecar keepalive frequency or batch telemetry uploads.
- If immediate relief needed, request a manual drain/restart of reserved pool to force compaction (performed 2026-03-10 12:30 UTC).

Follow-ups and action items:
- INT-1210: Add deterministic suppress window after demote in autoscaler (engineering backlog).
- INT-1211: Improve allocator compaction instrumentation and add alerting for repeated demote->reconnect cycles.
- Runbook update: Add QuantEdge case to 'Reserved Pool Demotion Runbook' with reproduction steps and mitigation checklist.

Customer impact: Post-fix metrics show p99 returned to baseline within 45 minutes of hotfix; steady throughput recovered to within 95% of pre-incident levels. Customer acknowledged resolution and accepted follow-up items.
This ticket required cross-team coordination: Support -> SRE -> Serving Runtime -> Allocator. The hotfix was low-risk configuration change plus a small allocator suppress window. Monitoring should remain for 72 hours.
Customer requested a postmortem summary be shared with their platform team; scheduled a 30-min call on 2026-03-13.
payload.summary: Priority-demotion loop causing reserved GPU scarcity and degraded batching for dedicated tenant

Issue summary: WaveDesk reports intermittent duplicate side effects (external webhooks executed twice) and occasionally missing funcall confirmations after client retries. This occurs only for long-running streaming sessions where the client issues both streaming tokens and explicit function/tool calls in the same session.

Impact: Customer sees duplicated downstream webhook posts (billing and order-processing systems) and a handful of lost confirmations that look like the server never acknowledged a funcall even though the call executed. Affects production traffic in us-east and spillover routed to eu-west via failover.

Observed behavior: When the client triggers a retry (network blip, http2 stream reset), some funcalls are executed on the server but the client-side SDK logs show a different confirmation mapping (older inflight id). In other cases, the SDK never releases its internal semaphore for in-flight funcalls, preventing subsequent requests from attaching the correct confirmation tokens and causing silent replays on reconnect.
1) Provision a Dedicated WaveDesk workload in us-east using rw-open-7b-v1 pinned model.
2) Use the Python SDK to open a streaming session and interleave streamed text chunks with funcall requests (call external tool via function calling).
3) Simulate a transient network reset (tcp reset or http2 stream reset) while a funcall is inflight. Repeat with Go SDK orchestration client calling the same backend concurrently.
4) Observe per-request logs and webhook endpoints for duplicate posts and check SDK client logs for "inflight semaphore" warnings (see logs below).
[python-sdk] 2026-03-10T18:22:41Z WARN retry_coordinator.py:178 - inflight_semaphore acquire timeout, inflight_count=7, max_inflight=8
[python-sdk] 2026-03-10T18:22:42Z INFO funcall_client.py:242 - sent funcall id=fc-7b2a0, awaiting confirmation token=<redacted>
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-10T18:22:43Z INFO proxy.go:512 - http2: stream reset by peer, streamID=42
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T18:22:44Z INFO router.go:304 - routed request id=req-88ab to model rw-open-7b-v1 node=n1-us-east
[python-sdk] 2026-03-10T18:22:45Z ERROR retry_coordinator.py:206 - confirmation mapping mismatch for funcall fc-7b2a0 -> observed confirmation fc-3c9f2
[wave-webhook] 2026-03-10T18:22:46Z POST /orders 200  (duplicate payload detected by order_id=ORD-20260310-991)
Initial repro confirmed with WaveDesk using a reproducible harness that performs stream+funcall interleaving and explicit http2 resets.
Python and Go SDK clients both exhibit the problem, but Go repro required multiplexing two goroutines that share the SDK retry coordinator in a particular pattern.
Heap of evidence points to client-side resource accounting: a semaphore/counter that tracks inflight funcalls is not always decremented on cancel/error paths introduced in the streaming backpressure refactor (SDK change in v2.8.0).
Server logs show the funcall executed and webhook posted; server emitted confirmation token A, but client later associated confirmation token B (stale mapping) leading to 'missing' confirmation for the original funcall.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Received initial ticket from WaveDesk, requested session IDs and webhook timestamps. Asked for SDK versions and orchestration pattern.
WaveDesk (customer) 2026-03-10: Provided session ids session-9c3a and session-1d77, noted duplicates happened ~18:22 UTC and ~18:45 UTC.
Liam Chen (SRE) 2026-03-11: Confirmed stream reset spikes in our edge-proxy around same timestamps; capturing tcp resets and HTTP/2 RST_STREAM events. Forwarding to SDK team for deeper dive.
Priya Rao (SDK eng) 2026-03-12: Able to reproduce locally against a test harness; suspect missing semaphore.release() in on_cancel path of retry_coordinator for interleaved streaming+funcall code path. Preparing small patch (PR linked).
A race between the streaming backpressure drain path and the funcall retry coordinator: when a stream reset or early cancel occurs while a funcall is inflight, the SDK falls into an error path that does not decrement the inflight semaphore and does not remove the temporary funcall->confirmation mapping. Subsequent requests reuse slot indices and the confirmation mapping becomes inconsistent, causing duplicate downstream side effects or apparent 'missing' confirmations.
1) For affected customers in production, advise immediate temporary mitigation: reduce concurrency (max_inflight) to 1 for streaming sessions that interleave funcalls, and increase retry delays to avoid overlapping inflight windows.
2) On the server/consumer side, make webhook receivers idempotent by checking order_id/correlation_id to avoid duplicate processing.
Investigation ongoing. SDK engineers prepared a candidate fix that ensures the inflight semaphore is always released on every error and cancel path, and improves mapping hygiene for confirmation tokens. Patch PR submitted for python SDK (see related_github_prs). QA scheduled for 2026-03-13. Will coordinate a 2.8.1 patch release if QA passes.
1) SDK eng to land the semaphore-fix PR for both python and go SDKs and add unit tests that simulate cancel/reset during inflight funcall (owner: Priya Rao).
2) QA to run end-to-end repro harness using WaveDesk session traces and confirm duplicates no longer happen (owner: TestEng).
3) If QA green, coordinate a patch release and notify WaveDesk of a planned rollout window (owner: ReleaseManager).
4) Postmortem draft to capture lessons about streaming+funcall interplay and add regression tests to the SDK suite (owner: Reliability).
payload.summary: Client-side semaphore leak causes silent retry replays and mismatched funcall confirmations across Python/Go SDKs

Issue summary:
Users on corporate Wi‑Fi who dock their Mac/Windows laptops to a USB‑C/Thunderbolt dock intermittently lose connectivity to internal services routed over WireGuard. Symptoms include repeated WireGuard re‑handshakes, long tail RPC latency to k8s API, and some TCP sessions resetting. The problem manifests primarily when the docked client is on the office Wi‑Fi SSID and the dock exposes an internal USB‑Ethernet adapter (Realtek/AX88xx and similar).

Impact:
- Multiple engineering users experienced transient loss of internal service connectivity while docked; impact noticed during code pushes, kubectl calls, and internal dashboards.
- Not a global outage but reproducible on affected hardware and reported by 6 users across 3 teams.

Observed behavior:
- WireGuard peer on client enters repeated handshake state (frequent Keepalive/Handshake attempts).
- Packet captures show large UDP/ESP (WireGuard) packets being fragmented and dropped at office gateway/NAT.
- When fragmentation happens, WireGuard falls back to re-sends and handshake churn increases, causing higher latency and connection resets for TCP over the VPN.

Expected behavior:
- WireGuard sessions remain stable when docked; no excessive handshake churn and no service-level impact.

Raw evidence & pointers:
- Slack thread: #internal-support thread "wg rehandshake while docked" (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CXXXXXX)
- Packet capture (pcap) excerpt saved to internal S3: s3://redwood-support/pcaps/INT-991337-dock-wg.pcap
- Local capture findings: multiple UDP/51820 packets > 1400 bytes flagged as fragmented in Wireshark; office NAT drops fragments that contain ESP payload (likely due to DF/mis-handling).

Initial hypothesis:
- USB‑Ethernet NIC offload features (GRO/TSO/LRO or checksum offload) on USB3 dock adapters produce large aggregated packets that exceed path MTU. Office gateway/NAT does not reassemble or it drops fragments with ESP/UDP when DF handling is inconsistent, leading to WireGuard retransmit/rehandshake.

Steps to reproduce (summary):
1) Use a laptop docked to a common corporate dock model (examples tested: CalDigit TS3 Plus with Realtek AX88179, Dell WD19TB with USB-Ethernet dongle).
2) Connect laptop to corporate Wi‑Fi (us-east office SSID) while docked (dock provides USB‑Ethernet interface).
3) Establish WireGuard connection to internal mesh (UDP 51820).
4) Run continuous ping to internal k8s API and tail a health endpoint with curl -v --keepalive 10; run tcpdump -w before/after.
5) Observe periodic handshake churn and packet fragmentation in capture.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Instructed affected users to apply local workaround: disable offloads on the USB‑ethernet interface and set MTU to 1420:
  - Linux/macOS: sudo ifconfig <iface> mtu 1420; sudo ethtool -K <iface> gro off gso off tso off

Additional notes:
- Workaround restores stable WireGuard sessions for affected clients.
Investigation notes:
- SRE reproduced on a test bench with the same dock + Realtek adapter. With offloads enabled, captured aggregated UDP frames were greater than 1500 and fragmented. Office edge showed NAT translations with the fragments being dropped; when offload and GSO disabled, UDP payloads remained under MTU and sessions stable.
- Verified that standalone laptops on Wi‑Fi without dock do not exhibit the issue.
- Confirmed behavior across macOS and Windows clients.
- Office edge device (vendor firewall) logs show "fragmented UDP - dropped" entries correlated to the timestamps.
- No evidence of malicious activity; root cause appears to be combination of (1) USB NIC driver offload aggregating packets, (2) office NAT/firewall not reassembling ESP fragments reliably.
Related artifacts & links:
- Related internal incident for similar fragmentation issues: INT-424246
- Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/IT/WireGuard+Dock+Fragmentation+KB
- GitHub issue opened against Realtek driver repo (vendor ticket #RTL-2026-311) and IT ticket to vendor for dock firmware.
Resolution & follow-up actions:
1) Short-term: Communicated and deployed a scoped MDM configuration (Windows/Intune & Jamf) that disables large send offload for recognized USB‑ethernet device IDs and sets MTU to 1420 for docked interfaces. This was rolled out to the known affected device pool (approx 50 seats).
2) Medium-term: IT to open formal support case with dock vendors (CalDigit, Dell) and Realtek for driver/firmware fix.
3) Long-term: Add an automated test in the corporate network validation suite to detect aggregated UDP/fragmentation behavior during docking transitions and flag firmware/driver combos that cause it.
4) KB published for manual troubleshooting steps: Confluence link above.
Status: Workaround deployed and affected users confirmed stable connectivity. Vendor engagement ongoing; tracking as a low‑frequency hardware/driver compatibility issue.
Dock laptop with CalDigit/Dell dock exposing USB-Ethernet adapter
Connect to corporate Wi-Fi while docked (us-east office SSID)
Start WireGuard to internal mesh (UDP 51820)
Run continuous tcpdump/tail on internal RPC endpoint and observe handshake churn and fragmented UDP packets
Office firewall logs: timestamps show 'fragmented UDP - dropped' correlated to client IPs
Client tcpdump: multiple UDP(51820) segments > 1400 bytes with IPv4 fragments
WireGuard log (client): repeated 'latest handshake' timestamps every ~10s during churn
Network Eng (Marta Ruiz) (2026-03-11): Confirmed office NAT behavior. Recommend workaround to disable GSO/TCP offloads and set MTU to 1420 until vendor fix is available.
SRE (Evan Cho) (2026-03-12): Added MDM config to push offload settings to identified dock device IDs; rollout started to 50 devices. Will monitor for regression.
payload.summary: USB-C dock NIC offload causes UDP/ESP fragmentation and WireGuard re-handshakes on corporate Wi‑Fi

Issue summary:
Data Science requests a repeatable, auditable pattern for short-lived experimental sandboxes across AWS and GCP. Current ad-hoc approach creates long-lived roles/service accounts with broad permissions and manual approval, which increases blast radius and audit friction.

Impact:
- Elevated risk of data exfiltration or unintentional access to prod resources if credentials are mis-scoped.
- Slow onboarding for experiments due to manual IAM provisioning.
- Audit evidence for external/compliance reviews is incomplete.

Background / request details:
- Provide a Terraform-backed module and runbook to create ephemeral sandbox environments with: permissions boundary (AWS) / IAM Conditions (GCP), tag-based scoping, KMS key restrictions (decrypt only for sandbox key), and prevention of key/service-account key creation.
- Support two modes: developer-initiated ephemeral role via STS assume-role (AWS) or Workload Identity Federation (GCP); and short-lived service accounts for batch jobs.
- Enforce that sandboxes cannot access production VPCs or prod tagged resources via SCP or org policy.
- Add automated audit logs (CloudTrail, GCP Audit Logs) + alerting for any cross-environment access attempts.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Terraform module published in infra repo with examples and documented variables.
2) IAM permissions boundary template (AWS) and IAM Condition examples (GCP) reviewed by Security.
3) A CI-validated PR that prevents service account key creation and enforces KMS key policy for sandbox keys.
4) Runbook for SRE/Support to onboard and revoke sandboxes with a one-click timeline.
5) Audit dashboard tile (Console) wireframe showing active sandboxes and last access events.

Requested timeline: "deliver initial module + runbook within 3 sprints; security review and rollout to dev accounts in sprint 4".
1) Developer requests sandbox and a long-lived role is created manually.
2) Role has ad-hoc policy granting s3:* and kms:Decrypt across multiple keys.
3) CloudTrail shows cross-account calls to a prod bucket in us-east-1 under the developer's role.
4) There is no tag-based deny SCP, and GCP audit logs show workload has wide IAM roles.
(These steps describe the unsafe manual flow to be prevented.)
Recent audit evidence: CloudTrail event ID: 2b3a-85f4-11e2-prod-access showing s3:GetObject by sandbox-role-1972 (2026-03-02T18:14:22Z). GCP audit log entry: projects/123456789012/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity eventId:7890 showing iam.serviceAccounts.keys.create on sandbox-service-account (2026-02-28T09:03:11Z). Attached links to raw logs in internal S3 and GCP log viewer provided in related_confluence_pages for reviewers.
- Confirmed two recent manual role grants in aws-dev account: permissions included blanket s3 and kms:Decrypt.
- Reviewed org SCPs: no deny on tag=prod in dev account; need new deny SCP or OU-level guardrail.
- Prototyped permissions boundary that limits kms:Decrypt to arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333:key/sandbox-*. Works in unit tests but needs policy review for cross-account use.
- On GCP side, IAM Conditions can constrain iam.roles to when resource.labels.environment=="sandbox"; prototyped condition expression and validated via gcloud simulator.
- Identified requirement: block iam.serviceAccounts.keys.create via org policy and enforce Workload Identity for pods needing GCP access.
- Potential blockers: terraform module must be able to attach permissions boundary to roles created by data-science infra; need infra repo maintainers sign-off.

Next investigative steps: confirm list of KMS keys used by data science; draft PR for SCP; coordinate with Platform Eng to add runbook steps to Console onboarding flow.
Asha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Filing this after two ad-hoc sandbox approvals last week. Prefer an automated path for JIT role issuance. Attachments: screenshot of prod bucket access and dev request thread.
Lena Kim (Assignee) 2026-03-11: Started prototyping module and permissions boundary. Will post an RFC to #infra-sandbox. Planning to coordinate with Security for policy language tomorrow.
DevSec (Security) 2026-03-12: Security okay with permissions boundary prototype but requests explicit deny for iam:CreateServiceAccountKey and a KMS key policy that excludes decryption of prod keys. We'll review PR once included in infra repo.
Marco Ruiz (Platform Eng) 2026-03-12: Flagging that the infra repo has a breaking change window next week; recommend merging the Terraform changes after the window. Also propose adding a Terraform plan CI gate that fails if any role without boundary is created.
WIP: Initial Terraform module and permissions boundary prototype completed and pushed to a feature branch (see related_github_prs). Pending Security review of final policy language and Platform Eng merge window. Follow-ups: build CI gate for role boundary enforcement, create Console onboarding step, schedule cutover to enforce deny SCP in dev OU. Expected full rollout after security sign-off and merge (target: end of sprint 4).
payload.summary: Establish conditional guardrails and ephemeral IAM flows for experimental data-science sandboxes

payload.description:
Owner requested: SRE/Infra to triage CI instability in the Private Observability Minimum Pack smoke-test pipeline.

Issue summary
- Our GitHub Actions job "private-observability-smoke" is intermittently failing on main for redwood-private-installer + redwood-helm-charts integration.
- Failures started after the smoke-test harness changes landed and we began validating dashboard provisioning + Prometheus scrape targets as part of the gate.

Impact
- Blocks merges/releases touching the Private observability minimum pack because CI gate is red.
- Consumes SRE/Eng time due to retries; reduces confidence in pack validation.

When/where
- Pipeline: CI (GitHub Actions), kind cluster, ephemeral.
- Job: "smoke-test-private-observability" (step: post-install validation).
- First observed: 2025-08-18 evening; escalated 2025-08-19.

Symptoms (from CI output)
1) Prometheus targets never reach healthy state within timeout
- Validation expects all Redwood ServiceMonitors to be "up" within 180s.
- Error:
  - "FAIL: expected Prometheus target job=redwood-serving-runtime to be up; got state=down, lastError=context deadline exceeded"

2) Grafana dashboards provisioned but API query returns empty folder on first attempt
- Error:
  - "FAIL: expected >= 3 dashboards in folder 'Redwood Private - Minimum Pack'; got 0"

Suspected regression area
- Prometheus Operator version drift in CI base image / chart dependency.
- ServiceMonitor label selector mismatch between helm chart defaults and kube-prometheus-stack in CI.
- Race: Grafana sidecar loads dashboards async; our check hits Grafana too early.

How to reproduce locally
- On a dev machine with docker/kind:
  1. ./scripts/ci/smoke/private_observability_smoke.sh
  2. Or: make smoke-test-private-observability
- Expected: install completes, Prometheus scrapes Redwood targets, Grafana folder contains Redwood dashboards.
- Actual: intermittent failure ~40-60% across retries.

Logs (snippets)
- From CI run 2025-08-19T10:42Z:
  - "[validate] waiting for prometheus targets..."
  - "GET http://prometheus-k8s.monitoring:9090/api/v1/targets"
  - "target=serviceMonitor/redwood-private/serving-runtime state=down lastError='server returned HTTP status 403 Forbidden'"
  - "NOTE: NetworkPolicy in namespace monitoring blocks ingress from prometheus-k8s -> redwood-private"

- From CI run 2025-08-19T15:08Z:
  - "[grafana] GET /api/search?folderIds=23"
  - "HTTP 200 []"
  - "[grafana] sidecar log: 'processing 7 dashboard files' (appears ~45s after our first query)"

Attachments / references
- Slack thread: #internal-support (linked from SRE triage channel) referencing #eng-infra discussion about prom operator + selectors.
- Customer-relevant context: SUP-49210 (missing dashboards) and SUP-49238 (noisy alerts) were both triggered by packaging changes; we want CI to catch real regressions, not flake.

Request
- Infra/SRE to identify root cause and propose a stable fix (chart pin, selector alignment, timeout/backoff strategy, or policy adjustment).
2025-08-19 09:17 (Sahana Iyer): Creating INT to get SRE eyes on this. We merged PR-18544 last week and since then the job is red ~50% of runs. I can reproduce locally only sometimes. Failure modes: (a) prometheus targets down, (b) grafana dashboards query returns empty (then succeeds if rerun).
2025-08-19 10:03 (Sean Gallagher): Picking up. First pass: looks like kube-prometheus-stack chart in CI is pulling a newer prometheus-operator than our local dev env. We also have a namespace NetworkPolicy in monitoring in the CI harness that might be too strict. I’m going to run the workflow with debug to confirm selectors + netpol.
2025-08-19 11:22 (Sean Gallagher): Confirmed one hard failure: Prometheus target error is actually 403 due to NetworkPolicy (prometheus in monitoring cannot scrape pods in redwood-private in some runs when policy controller applies before allow rules). This explains the "context deadline" symptom. Suggested fix: apply allow-scrape NP earlier or make it part of helm install ordering; also add explicit egress/ingress between namespaces for metrics ports.
2025-08-19 11:40 (Diego Santos): +1. We saw similar in a customer cluster when they tightened NPs (see Slack #incidents 1746729722). In CI, the policy controller timing probably makes it racy. We can relax CI netpol to reduce flake while keeping the real check in the installer preflight.
2025-08-19 13:05 (Rafael Mendes): On the Grafana side, I think it’s a race. Sidecar provisions dashboards async; our smoke check hits the API immediately after pods Ready. We should add backoff (e.g., wait up to 2–3m for folder population) and/or check sidecar logs for "processing" completion before asserting counts.
2025-08-19 16:18 (Sean Gallagher): Root causes:
1) NetworkPolicy ordering in CI harness: allow-scrape policy applied after default-deny in some runs => Prometheus scrape blocked => targets down.
2) Grafana dashboard provisioning check too eager (no retry/backoff) => transient 0 dashboards.

Proposed changes:
- Update smoke harness to apply allow-scrape NetworkPolicy before installing kube-prometheus-stack + Redwood charts.
- Add exponential backoff (max 180s) to Grafana dashboard count check.
- Pin kube-prometheus-stack chart version in CI to avoid operator selector behavior changes without review.

I’ll open a small PR in the harness repo / redwood PR to fix ordering + retries.
2025-08-20 09:12 (Sahana Iyer): Thanks. Please include in the PR notes that we still want failures when dashboards truly never appear (e.g., missing ConfigMaps), just not on first API call. Also please keep the Prometheus target check strict once netpol ordering is deterministic.
2025-08-20 14:37 (Sean Gallagher): Fix landed and validated in a branch run (5/5 green). Changes:
- Reordered CI script: create namespaces + netpol allow list first, then install monitoring stack, then install Redwood.
- Added retry loop for Grafana: wait until folder exists AND dashboard count >= expected, with logs printed on timeout.
- Pinned kube-prometheus-stack chart to 56.6.2 in CI.

Handing back to Sahana to re-run against main once merged.
2025-08-21 10:26 (Sahana Iyer): Re-ran main with the harness changes. 8 consecutive runs green. Marking resolved. Follow-up item for later: move pinning into documented CI dependency policy so we bump intentionally (and run a compatibility sweep).
2025-08-21 10:29 (Sean Gallagher): Closing. If we see further flakes, next suspects are Prometheus TSDB startup time on overloaded runners and image pull delays; current timeouts are still tight but should be acceptable with retries.
Resolved by fixing CI harness ordering and stability: applied allow-scrape NetworkPolicy before default-deny takes effect, added retry/backoff for Grafana dashboard provisioning validation, and pinned kube-prometheus-stack chart version to prevent operator drift. Verified with repeated green CI runs.
Document CI dependency pin policy and add a scheduled job to bump kube-prometheus-stack + run compatibility checks.
Add a dedicated smoke-test metric for 'dashboards provisioned' to avoid relying solely on Grafana search API timing.
Consider adding an installer preflight note warning that restrictive NetworkPolicies can block Prometheus scrapes across namespaces (link the day-2 runbook).
payload.summary: Private observability minimum pack: CI smoke tests failing (Prometheus scrape targets down / dashboards not detected)

Issue summary:
Users report that the internal Runbook Launcher (Electron desktop app) intermittently fails to complete SSO sign-in when the flow uses the embedded webview. The error presented is a generic 'Unable to authenticate' dialog and the app logs show an Okta SAML/OIDC response being rejected due to an authn_hint mismatch.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers on call cannot launch runbooks that require elevated access during their shift (affects PagerDuty on-call rotation).
- Blocks emergency runbook execution and increases Mean Time to Resolution for operational incidents.

Observed behavior:
- Webview navigates to Okta, user authenticates successfully, but on redirect back to the app the identity-proxy rejects the assertion with: 'authn_hint mismatch: expected electron_app, got electron-webview'.
- Affected sessions show a short-lived cookie created by a legacy proxy path (/auth/electron) while current proxy expects /auth/desktop.

Expected behavior:
- Electron app webview completes SSO and grants a session token consistent with other clients (browser, CLI).

Initial logs/snippets:
- identity-proxy: "WARN auth: assertion rejected - authn_hint mismatch (expected=desktop, received=webview) tx=0x9c71"
- electron app: "INFO sso: received redirect URI with state=..., code=...; token-exchange failed: 403"
- Okta debug logs (partial): "Redirect URI matched, but relayState contained legacy client_id 'runbook-launcher-legacy'"

Workaround so far:
- Short-term: instruct affected users to use the web console (browser) instead of the Electron app to run critical runbooks.
- Support has temporarily allowed a permissive mapping in the identity-proxy config for 24 hours for 'runbook-launcher-legacy' clients in us-east-1 while we investigate.
Install the internal Runbook Launcher Electron app (v2.4.1) on macOS or Linux.
Launch the app and click 'Sign in with SSO'.
Complete the Okta sign-in in the embedded webview.
Observe the webview redirect back to the app and note the error dialog 'Unable to authenticate'.
Check identity-proxy logs for authn_hint mismatch for that transaction ID.
[identity-proxy] 2026-03-10T15:22:04Z WARN auth: assertion rejected - authn_hint mismatch (expected=desktop, received=webview) tx=0x9c71
[electron-runbook] 2026-03-10T15:22:05Z ERROR sso: token-exchange failed status=403 body="Forbidden"
[okta-debug] 2026-03-10T15:21:58Z INFO authn: redirect_uri=https://app.internal/redwood/cb relayState=runbook-launcher-legacy"
Support (Aisha): Captured initial user reports from #support. Reproduced with macOS 13.4 and Electron v21. Reproduced reliably when webview uses the legacy client_id.
Oncall (Miguel): Scoped the issue to identity-proxy authn_hint validation. Temporarily allowed legacy client_id in identity-proxy mappings for us-east-1 to unblock users (24h).
SRE (Priya Kaur): Adding identity-proxy diagnostics to trace authn_hint and relayState. Suggest validating Electron upgrade path; previous desktop packaging moved from client_id 'runbook-launcher-legacy' to 'runbook-launcher-desktop' causing mismatch.

Additional notes:
Support (Aisha): Communicated browser workaround to affected on-call engineers and logged names for targeted follow-up.
Reproduction confirmed on macOS and Ubuntu when app config still references legacy client ID in embedded webview header.
Okta confirms the assertion contains a relayState parameter that the proxy expects to match a current client mapping. If it doesn't match, the proxy treats the assertion as potentially replayed or from a deprecated client and rejects it.
Telemetry shows ~0.4% of active desktop users still have the legacy client_id in their persisted app config (likely from v2.2.x).
Identity-proxy mapping implementation performs strict equality on authn_hint; suggests relaxing matching logic to accept known legacy aliases for a migration window.
Risk assessment: relaxing matching introduces minor spoofing risk if combined with open redirecters; mitigation is to restrict relaxation to signed client metadata and region-specific mapping (us-east-1 only initially).
Short-term mitigation: identity-proxy mapping relaxed for 'runbook-launcher-legacy' in us-east-1 for 24h to unblock oncall. Medium-term fix: PR #1824 updates identity-proxy to accept configured legacy aliases for a 30-day migration window and adds audit logging. Desktop app PR #341 will migrate stored client_id on first launch to canonical 'runbook-launcher-desktop'. Next steps: complete PR review, deploy identity-proxy change to staging, run focused e2e with instrumented logs, then promote to prod. Follow-up: email campaign targeted at 0.4% of users with legacy installs and add upgrade enforcement in v2.5.0.
Complete code review and merge PRs (#1824, #341).
Deploy identity-proxy change to staging and run regression test suite focused on SSO flows.
Monitor auth rejection rate in us-east-1 for 72 hours post-deploy; rollback plan ready if error rate increases >2x baseline.
Notify support and oncall channels once migration shim is live and schedule a follow-up to mark the issue Resolved.
payload.summary: Electron runbook launcher fails to authenticate: SSO authn_hint mismatch for embedded webview sessions

Issue summary: AtlasHealth (enterprise customer) submitted a DSAR escalation requesting removal of specific user PII from production logs between 2026-02-25 and 2026-03-02. Impact: Potential compliance breach if logs containing PII are not removed; customer is pausing ingestion of new data until confirmation is provided. Request: Evaluate feasibility of targeted log redact/scrub for the date range and provide legal-signed approval for the operation.

Some telemetry and request metadata contain user identifiers. Need a cross-team plan involving SRE, Security/Privacy, and Legal.
1) N/A - customer-provided request for retroactive deletion of log rows.
2) Context: query used to identify affected log lines: {service="api-gateway", customer="AtlasHealth", timestamp>="2026-02-25" and timestamp<="2026-03-02"}.

2026-02-27T14:12:03Z api-gateway INFO req_id=abc123 customer=AtlasHealth user_email=jane.doe@atlashealth.com prompt_id=pf_99...\n2026-02-28T09:04:17Z api-gateway INFO req_id=def456 customer=AtlasHealth user_email=redacted prompt_id=pf_101... (full logs redacted here for ticket)

2026-03-12T08:46:12Z audit: token=svc-transcriber id=abc123 path=/v1/streams status=200 ip=45.77.12.9 ua=TranscribeClient/1.0

1) Identify affected service token in audit log. 2) Observe token exchange pattern (oauth callback) and origin IPs. 3) Recreate request flow using a test token to validate endpoint access pattern (do not reuse production tokens).
Hypothesis A: A third-party transcription vendor's OAuth app was compromised, allowing silent consent flow and token exchange for a service account.
Hypothesis B: A developer reused a service account credential in an insecure environment; attackers scraped it via an exposed artifact. Less likely given IP/geolocation clustering.

Forensics: Exported full oauth server logs, CloudTrail-like audit entries, and the sequence of IPs for correlation with external threat intel.

Work in progress: immediate mitigations applied (keys rotated, client disabled). No confirmed data exfiltration to date; investigation remains open.
1) Complete forensic timeline and determine if tokens were ever exported. 2) Vendor engagement: request IOCs and review their client security. 3) Expand detection to catch similar client_id anomalies across prod regions. 4) Update runbook and schedule org-wide note about transient OAuth risks.

Issue summary: Security & Compliance team requests a time-limited export of production request/response logs to validate a customer data-handling exception.

Impact: Needed to complete a DPIA-style review and to respond to an incoming regulator probe for a customer using Redwood Private. No service changes required, but access is sensitive because logs may contain customer-provided prompts and potentially PII.

Background: Legal engaged Support to retrieve a sample set of full request/response pairs for May 2026 (production, us-east). The sample must include entries for one tenant (tenant_id: redwood-corp-237) across three peak days (2026-05-10 to 2026-05-12). The request originates from Compliance (Priya Mehta) with a formal evidence request.

Requested access and scope:
- Data scope: full HTTP access logs + application-level request/response payloads filtered by tenant_id redwood-corp-237.
- Time window: 2026-05-10 00:00 to 2026-05-12 23:59 UTC.
- Output format: gzipped JSONL with field-level metadata (timestamp, request_id, model, route, region).
- Redaction requirement: customer email addresses and session tokens should be redacted unless Legal indicates otherwise.
- Duration: One-time export; access artifacts retained via audit logs.

Approvals required: Security (Data Protection Officer), SRE for extraction plan, and Legal for redaction rules. Compliance has requested proof of redaction prior to wider distribution.

Proposed method: run a controlled extraction job on an isolated infra worker with read-only access to the log S3 prefix, write output to a pre-approved secure artifact bucket (s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/prod-exports/INT-4312/), and notify Compliance when ready. All actions will be executed by a short-lived role (assume-role) and recorded in CloudTrail and internal audit logging.

Acceptance criteria:
- Extraction completes with file checksum and file listing in ticket.
- Redaction verification performed and attested by Security.
- Artifact accessible only to: Priya Mehta (Compliance), Daniel Brooks (Legal), Marcus Li (SRE), and an internal reviewer from Security.

Notes: This is an internal-support request; no customer-facing ticket required unless the customer is to be notified by Legal.

Priya Mehta (Compliance) 2026-03-10: Submitted formal evidence request; we need minimally privileged export to support a regulator Q, ETA for final deliverable is 2026-03-18.
Marcus Li (SRE) 2026-03-11: Can perform extraction but need clarification on exact S3 prefixes and whether the application-level payloads are stored encrypted with customer-managed keys. Requesting a runbook approval and jumpbox account for execution.

Riley Thompson (Reporter) 2026-03-12: Redaction plan: automated regex heuristics for common PII (emails, credit card patterns) + manual spot-check of a 0.5% sample. Legal to advise on whether to include or redact client identifiers beyond email.
Daniel Brooks (Legal) 2026-03-13: Legal requests that client billing identifiers be redacted. Also, we need a chain-of-custody note in the ticket before delivering artifacts to external counsel.

Marcus Li (SRE) 2026-03-14: Extraction job scheduled for 2026-03-16 with STS assume-role and artifact bucket s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/prod-exports/INT-4312/. Will attach runbook and job logs to ticket when complete.

Hypotheses: payloads may include customer-sent identifiers in prompts; redaction necessary prior to sharing. SRE to confirm extraction performance impact (expected ~2 hours, 25GB output).

Follow-up task: create a short runbook for future similar requests (INT-XXXX) and consider an automated, auditable redaction pipeline.

Issue summary: After a policy publish window on 2026-03-01 ~09:10 UTC, the support-orchestrator ingestion path showed sustained lag (~10-25m) causing escalation_owner to flip between default on-call user and team-owned on escalate attempts. Impact: SLA calculations for routed tickets were delayed and the daily routing report showed gaps. Users reported incorrect owner assignment for a subset of internal tickets, leading to missed P1 handoffs. This ticket captures triage, investigation, fix, and follow-ups.
1) Create a new escalation policy via Policy UI that sets escalation_owner to a named team user.
2) Publish policy and observe the policy-engine change events emitted to the policy-topic.
3) Watch support-orchestrator consumer lag in the consumer group dashboard (kafka-consumer-offsets).
4) Trigger a test ticket that should pick up the new owner (simulate via support API).
Expected: owner is applied within 30s and SLA calc runs. Observed: owner either remains default or flips during retries and SLA calc delayed by up to 25m.
[2026-03-01T09:12:03Z] support-orchestrator[consumer]: WARN consumer lag: 13489 msgs behind
[2026-03-01T09:12:06Z] support-orchestrator[ingest]: ERROR failed to apply policy change: null value for escalation_owner at policy_id=pol-2048
[2026-03-01T09:12:07Z] support-orchestrator[ingest]: INFO scheduling retry backoff=30s attempt=1
[2026-03-01T09:23:12Z] support-orchestrator[metrics]: WARN sla-calc-delay=1200s tickets_pending=42
(see attached support-orchestrator.log excerpt in attachments)
Timeline: 09:10 publish -> 09:12 consumer lag spikes -> 09:15 first ERRORs for null escalation_owner -> 09:40 backlog processed intermittently -> 10:00 most policies reconciled. Hypothesis 1: recent policy-engine v2.3.7 allowed nullable escalation_owner on intermediate schema causing parser to emit nulls. Hypothesis 2: consumer backpressure + large GC pause in support-orchestrator pod slowed reprocessing and exponential backoff amplified delay. Verified: support-orchestrator pods showed a 2.3s stop-the-world GC at 09:11 with 40% CPU saturation; policy-engine PR 1123 introduced a change to policy schema (owner can be omitted) without downstream defensive handling. Repro: Applied a crafted policy missing owner field in staging and observed same null parse path and owner fallback behavior. Metrics: policy-ingest error rate peaked at 7.8% and sla-calc latency 20x baseline during the window.
Support (Tanya): Customer-facing symptom reported by internal ops at 09:25 UTC; escalated to SRE.
SRE (Luca): Identified consumer lag and GC spike in support-orchestrator. Pinning pods and pulling logs for span. Noted recent deployment of policy-engine v2.3.7 in prod at 08:58 UTC.
Eng (Mateo): Timesketch of PR 1123 shows optional owner field. Suggest immediate rollback and hotfix to handle null owners gracefully.
Support (Asha): Created this ticket and added nightly routing report snapshot for affected hours. Requested backfill of SLA metrics once fix is deployed.
SRE (Luca): Rolled back support-orchestrator to prior JVM tuning and cleared consumer group offsets for a controlled replay. Monitoring backlog drain now at 2026-03-04 02:14 UTC.
Eng (Mateo): Deployed hotfix v2.3.8 to policy-engine to enforce owner defaulting and validation at publish time. Patch set: PR 1129.
Support (Tanya): Verified owner assignment on sampled tickets; routing report reprocessed and reconciled. Marking as resolved pending follow-ups.
Short-term remediation: rolled back problematic consumer JVM flags, cleared and rebalanced consumer offsets, and applied hotfix to policy-engine (v2.3.8) that restores non-null escalation_owner default and rejects malformed policy publishes. Long-term: added a defensive parse layer in support-orchestrator to ignore null owner and emit a clear validation metric. Backfill: reprocessed the policy change stream for the impacted window and re-ran SLA calc job for tickets created between 2026-03-01T09:00 and 2026-03-01T11:00; results ingested into daily routing report.
Regression introduced in policy-engine v2.3.7 that made escalation_owner optional at publish time, combined with lack of defensive parsing in support-orchestrator and a concurrent JVM GC/CPU pressure that amplified consumer lag and retry backoff leading to owner flapping and delayed SLA calculations.
1) Add unit and integration tests that publish policies with missing owner to prevent regressions (owner required at policy publish).
2) Add a validation gate in the Policy UI that prevents publish when owner is missing for escalation policies.
3) Create a support-orchestrator health dashboard: consumer lag, owner-null-rate, sla-calc-latency.
4) Update runbook (confluence) with step-by-step for clearing consumer backlogs and safe replay.
5) Release post-mortem summary to #support and ops channels.
6) Schedule a changelog review for 2.3.x releases to catch schema drift with consumers.
payload.summary: Policy ingest lag in support-orchestrator leading to escalation-owner flapping and delayed SLA calculations

Issue summary: Request to build a gated, auditable self-serve path so engineers can request new project workspaces (Jira project + Confluence space + Slack channel) without manual ticket handoffs. Impact: Current process requires manual SD/IT triage and ad-hoc emails causing 2-5 day turnaround and inconsistent naming/permission patterns. Business rationale: Reduce lead time for new project launches, enforce naming conventions and least-privilege access, and capture automated audit records for compliance. Request: Design and implement a workflow accessible from a lightweight UI (Confluence macro or Slack command) that captures request metadata, runs policy checks, routes for approval (team lead + security for sensitive classifications), provisions resources via existing provisioning bots, and records the full lifecycle in a central audit Confluence page.
Desired fields captured: project name, short description, owning pod, privacy level (public/internal/strict), data classification tags, initial member list (github/okta groups), retention policy choice. Approval gates: auto-approve for 'public' and 'internal' with owner signoff; require Security review for 'strict' or if data_classification contains PHI/PCI. Provisioning steps: create Jira project from 'team-template' (default issue types and workflows), create Confluence seeded space using 'project-kickoff' template, create Slack channel with naming prefix pod-<pod>-<shortname>, attach onboarding checklist bot and set channel retention policy, create service account with scoped token for bots, and seed runbook under the Confluence space with links to the Jira project and channel. Audit: every provision event must write a line to 'Internal Provisioning Audit' Confluence page and emit an event to ops-telemetry channel (for future telemetry ingestion).
Operator steps (for automation implementer): 1) Add a new API endpoint to the provisioning gateway to accept structured requests (JSON). 2) Implement policy evaluation module (name compliance, classification checks, membership sanity). 3) Wire approval flows into Slack modal + Jira for audit (create a lightweight approval ticket). 4) Call existing slack-bot-provisioner to create channel and install onboarding automations. 5) Call confluence-seed job to create space and seed template with variables. 6) Call jira-template-provisioner to create project and apply permission scheme. 7) Emit audit entry and webhook to ops-telemetry. 8) Return provisioned object URLs to requester and create an ephemeral follow-up task for onboarding checklist.
1) Request UI validates required fields and rejects disallowed names. 2) Policy engine correctly flags 'strict' classifications and prevents auto-approve. 3) Approvals are routed to correct reviewers and decisions are logged. 4) Provisioner creates Jira project, Confluence space, Slack channel, and service account, all with correct naming/permission templates. 5) Audit entry is written and webhook emitted. 6) End-to-end test exists and is runnable by Platform Eng. 7) Documentation for requesters and runbook for operators added to Confluence.
Checked current provisioning bots and templates. Found gap: no single source-of-truth for naming rules (some pods use prefix vs suffix). Existing slack-bot-provisioner supports channel creation and apps install but lacks hooking into an approval workflow. Confluence template 'project-kickoff' exists and is suitable with minor variables. Jira permission schemes need minor adjustments to support pod-based admins.
Phase 1 (design): finalize request JSON schema, approval routing, and RBAC mapping (1 week). Phase 2 (build): extend provisioning-gateway API, add policy module, integrate approver routing to ops-approvals Jira project and Slack modals (2 sprints). Phase 3 (test): integration tests and smoke tests in staging with sample pods (1 sprint). Phase 4 (rollout): enable opt-in for a pilot pod and collect feedback, then enable org-wide with telemetry (2 weeks).
Pilot with two pods (Platform and Developer Experience) for 2 weeks. Monitor provisioning telemetry and support tickets for drift. Gradual ramp: enable new projects for 10% pods after pilot, then 50%, then org-wide. Provide rollback via a deprovision job that can be invoked if naming or permissions are incorrect.
1) Final sign-off on approval routing (ops-project vs ephemeral). 2) API access to team-directory service for owner resolution. 3) Minor Jira permission scheme change that requires Product Security sign-off.
1) Marco to open INT ticket to modify Jira permission scheme (blocked until security sign-off). 2) Aisha to share team-directory service token with platform-eng sandbox. 3) Security will publish checklist for 'strict' classification reviews. 4) Platform Eng to draft E2E integration tests and a staging runbook.

Issue summary:
An engineer was put on an approved medical leave (FMLA-equivalent) with temporary reduced access for 90 days. HR followed the deferred-revocation process that preserves emergency sudo for the manager and a limited set of service accounts. We need clarification and an operational plan for: (1) signaling emergency sudo revocation if HR later decides to enforce immediate revocation, (2) collecting the engineer's company laptop after 30 days if leave is extended beyond the original window, and (3) wiping encrypted disks remotely vs. in-person collection.

Impact:
- Potential risk if emergency sudo remains active longer than intended (affects privilege hygiene).
- Unclear collection window creates logistics risk for device recovery and asset accounting.
- Legal/HR constraints require we avoid premature account termination.

Environment:
- Internal offboarding/leave workflows; affected identity is in Okta and Azure AD; device is corporate MacBook (FileVault enabled) enrolled in Intune/MDM.
- Region: us-west (employee based in US).

Steps / requested action:
1) Confirm the signal mechanism for immediate emergency sudo revocation (who can trigger, what playbook/automation exists, expected propagation time).
2) Create a short plan for conditional device recovery at 30/60/90 days with owner contact steps, courier options, and remote wipe policy decision matrix tied to HR approvals.
3) Recommend a safe remote wipe/run-wipe fallback that preserves forensics if needed and complies with HR/legal constraints.
4) If automation is required (e.g., a webhook from HR system to IAM), list required scopes and an outline PR for engineering.

Attachments / references:
- HR leave approval case: HR-57321 (internal HR tracker link)
- Current offboarding playbook: https://confluence.redwood/HR/OffboardingPlaybook
- MDM device record: device-id-REDACTED

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - SRE oncall (Marco Li): Asked whether remote wipe should be single-step or two-step (lock then wipe) to preserve forensic image if required; recommended two-step with quarantine label in MDM.
Reviewed playbook: deferred-revoke section is ambiguous about 'emergency toggle' and references a Slack-only signal in #security with no audit webhook.
Checked Okta access history: engineer's emergency sudo was granted to manager via group 'emergency-sudo-rotating' created at onboarding. No automatic removal scheduled.
MDM (Intune) supports remote lock and full wipe APIs; enrollment indicates FileVault enabled which allows remote wipe without key escrow access. Forensics team advises image capture before wipe if HR/legal suspects wrongdoing.
Possible automation: HR could post to internal webhook that calls a small service to remove the manager from 'emergency-sudo-rotating' and trigger a device collection workflow. Scope will require Okta SCIM removal rights and MDM API token with device-read and wipe permissions.
(Draft) Agreed path: 1) Add an 'Emergency Revoke' checkbox in HR case UI that triggers an authenticated webhook to the 'offboard-orchestrator' service. That service will remove the manager from the emergency-sudo group in Okta (SCIM call) and post an audit entry to the security log. 2) Device recovery: default courier pickup scheduled at day 30 if leave extends; if courier not possible, team will attempt remote lock at day 30 and remote wipe at day 45 after forensic hold evaluation. 3) Engineering to create a small PR (offboard-orchestrator) implementing SCIM remove + MDM lock endpoint. 4) Legal/HR to sign off on the forensic hold timeline. Next steps: assign PR to infra team, draft HR UI change, and schedule a 30-minute alignment call with Security, HR, and MDM owners.

MDM team: confirm courier vs remote wipe capabilities and estimated costs - owner: Priya Shah
HR: update leave workflow to include 'Emergency Revoke' option and approve forensic hold timeline - owner: Jenna Morales

Schedule alignment call: target by 2026-03-18

payload.description:
Issue summary
- On-call operator cannot see the "Rollback" button in the Console for Optimization Config versions.
- This blocks rollback during gameday / incident response and is confusing because the operator is in the expected on-call group.

Impact
- Internal: on-call cannot execute one-click rollback via Console (must escalate to Platform team or use break-glass).
- Risk: delayed mitigation if a bad optimization config causes latency/5xx regression.

Who is affected
- Internal users in Okta/SSO group: sre-oncall (expected to have Optimization Change Operator privileges).

Observed behavior
- UI: No "Rollback" CTA shown on version detail page.
- API: direct call to rollback endpoint returns 403.

Expected behavior
- Members of the on-call operator group should have permission to rollback optimization configs within approved scopes.

Error details
- Console network call response:
  - POST /v1/optimization-configs/rollouts/{rollout_id}:rollback
  - HTTP 403
  - Body: {"error":"permission_denied","message":"missing permission: optimization_config.rollback"}

Notes
- This started after the RBAC policy bundle update earlier this week (Console safe-apply/rollback internal beta enablement).
1) Sign in to Console with an account in group "sre-oncall" (example: aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com).
2) Navigate: Console → Optimize → Optimization Configs → History.
3) Open any rollout/version detail page where rollback should be permitted.
4) Observe the Rollback button is not present.
5) (Optional) Attempt rollback via API using the same session token:
   - POST /v1/optimization-configs/rollouts/{rollout_id}:rollback
   - Result: 403 permission_denied (missing optimization_config.rollback).
Initial hypotheses
- UI feature flag off vs. permission gating.
- Role mapping (group → role) missing in prod.
- Policy bundle version drift between control plane and console backend.

Findings
- Feature flag for rollback UI is ON for internal beta (confirmed by Console team).
- AuthZ check in console-backend hides the CTA when user lacks permission optimization_config.rollback.
- RBAC evaluation for affected user resolves to role "optimization_config.viewer" only.
- Expected role: "optimization_change_operator" (or equivalent) should include:
  - optimization_config.apply
  - optimization_config.promote
  - optimization_config.rollback

Root cause
- Group-to-role mapping for "sre-oncall" in prod was missing the operator role assignment.
- Additionally, RBAC policy sync job in us-east showed stale policy bundle (cache not invalidated after last bundle publish), causing inconsistent results across pods.

Evidence
- AuthZ debug header from console-backend (captured by Dylan Brooks): effective_permissions did not include optimization_config.rollback.
- RBAC service logs (queried by Jordan Lee): policy_version remained at N-1 in us-east for ~6 hours.
Resolution (2026-01-24)
- Added/confirmed group-to-role binding in prod:
  - sre-oncall → optimization_change_operator
- Forced policy sync + cache invalidation:
  - Ran rbac-policy sync job in us-east
  - Restarted console-backend pods to clear in-memory authz cache
- Verified:
  - Rollback button visible for aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com
  - POST rollback endpoint returns 200 and emits audit event

Follow-ups
- Add an alert for RBAC policy_version drift > 15 minutes in prod.
- Add a short internal doc snippet to the rollback runbook: "If CTA missing, verify permission optimization_config.rollback via /whoami + authz debug".
- Opened an engineering bug for making the Console show a clearer "insufficient permissions" empty state instead of silently hiding the CTA.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer/internal report that several service account API keys showed elevated privilege usage within a 20-minute window after a handful of employees clicked an onboarding email containing an embedded PNG. Impact: potential API key compromise and unauthorized calls to internal admin endpoints.

Impact:
- Multiple service-account API keys issued to new hire onboarding automation made calls to admin/organization/keys and admin/billing endpoints (read-only and write attempts observed).
- No confirmed data exfil, but suspicious token refresh patterns and new ephemeral tokens were minted.
- Affected systems may include console UI, API gateway, and a small set of internal agent services.

Environment:
- prod-us-west primary, spikes also visible in prod-us-east (proxied traffic).
- New-hire onboarding automation service (onboard-agent-v2) and associated CI user tokens appear involved.

Steps to reproduce / How detected:
1) 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC Security automation alerted on anomalous admin API calls from IPs not previously seen for these service accounts.
2) On-call checked correlate logs in api-gateway and noticed a cluster of requests coming immediately after employees opened an onboarding welcome email.
3) Email contained an inline PNG (welcome_badge.png). Recovering the image payload from the mail archive showed an unusual payload size and a base64 blob in metadata.
4) Replaying the sequence in a sandbox (isolated environment) by rendering the PNG triggered an outbound HTTP callback to an external domain and a subsequent redirect to a shortlink.

Initial evidence / logs:
- api-gateway access logs (see excerpts in related_confluence_pages) show admin endpoints hit by tokens tied to service accounts onboard-agent-01..03 between 2026-03-10 09:10-09:30 UTC.
- Token issuance logs show refreshes at unusual intervals and refreshes originating from a user agent string matching the desktop email client.
- Mail logs indicate the outbound email was rendered by Marketing via SendGrid; the embedded PNG metadata contains a 4KB base64 chunk with non-image signature.

Hypothesis:
- The PNG contained a steganographic payload that triggered the email client (or a preview service) to make an HTTP request to an external callback, leaking an authentication artifact (session cookie or token exchange) which allowed the attacker to exchange for ephemeral API keys OR to trigger a server-side callback that used internal credentials during processing.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Revoked affected service account API keys and rotated credentials for onboard-agent-v2 at 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC.
- Invalidated active SSO sessions for users who opened the email (targeted invalidation) and forced global SSO reauth for the org at 2026-03-10 10:25 UTC.
- Blocked the external domain at perimeter and WAF rules updated to drop requests to the observed callback host.
- Disabled email rendering previews in the internal mail sandbox and removed the specific email from queued sends.

Next actions planned:
- Full token audit across org and reissue of any tokens created in that window.
- Deep analysis of the image metadata and reproduction of the stego payload in a controlled environment.
- Forensics on affected hosts and any services that performed callbacks while processing email assets.
- Engage Legal and CISO for possible disclosure and coordinate with Marketing for a send-source review.
- Update onboarding automation to require stricter validation of external assets and to run asset rendering in an isolated environment with no credential access.

Timeline summary and findings to date:
- 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Anomaly detection fired on admin endpoint rate and SSO refresh pattern; alert routed to #sec-ops.
- 09:18 UTC: Confirmed cluster of admin calls all signed with tokens issued within previous 30 minutes.
- 09:40 UTC: Mail team provided raw MIME for the onboarding welcome email; discovered embedded PNG has a 4096-byte base64 blob in tEXt chunk.
- 10:00 UTC: Sandbox rendering of PNG caused HTTP POST to hxxp://img-callback[.]host/collect and redirect to a shortlink. Outbound request included an Authorization header when run under the user's environment due to automatic credential forwarding from internal proxy.
- 10:05 UTC: Rotated keys and invalidated sessions.
- Forensic note: No evidence yet of lateral movement beyond admin API calls; storage buckets and customer data show no access outside normal read patterns.
- Risk: medium-high until full token audit completes.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:20 UTC - CISO (Priya Nair): Please coordinate with Legal; preserve all raw email artifacts and host network captures. Also prepare a short summary for execs if customer data is affected.
Mitigations applied: revoked affected API keys, forced targeted SSO reauth, blocked callback domain, suspended offending email batch. Token audit and forensics ongoing. Post-incident action items created: update onboarding asset handling, add stego detection to mail pipeline, and coordination with Marketing and Legal for follow-up.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We need a guided, interactive onboarding wizard for provisioning Slack channels (public/private), associated Jira project space stubs, and a templated Confluence page. The wizard should surface a permission matrix (who can join, who can post, archival schedule), pre-populated RBAC templates for common pod types, and automate service-account creation for channel apps/bots.

Impact:
Right now onboarding is manual and error-prone: channel creators often pick incorrect privacy settings, forget to add required compliance reviewers, or request overly broad permissions. This leads to follow-up tickets for access changes, intermittent security exposures, and a backlog in the internal-support queue. A self-service wizard reduces support load and shortens time-to-onboard for new pods.

Request / Acceptance criteria:
- Build a lightweight web-based wizard (hosted internally) reachable from the "New Channel" Confluence template and the Slack-provisioning bot.
- Step-driven UI: Purpose -> Visibility -> Membership policy -> App integrations -> Retention/archival policy -> Compliance reviewers -> Jira + Confluence stubs.
- Permission matrix must present recommended defaults per pod type and allow scoped overrides with justifications that record who approved.
- Provide 3 RBAC templates: Engineering Pod, Data Platform, External Partner. Templates map to Slack groups, Jira permissions scheme, and Confluence space permissions.
- Auto-create a dedicated service account and provision minimal bot scopes for each channel when integrations are selected; record keys in Vault.
- The wizard writes a structured record into Jira (INT-*) and optionally triggers a CLA/contract gating flow for external partner pods.
- All actions must produce audit log entries in Confluence page metadata and central audit log (security requirement).

Proposed flow / Steps to implement:
1) Design step flow and template matrix (Product + Support) — deliver mockups.
2) Prototype backend endpoints that call Slack Admin API, Jira project creation API, and Confluence REST API.
3) Integrate service-account creation with internal identity automation and secrets storage in Vault.
4) Implement approval step: For non-default broad permissions, wizard must require a named approver (group or user) and store approval as part of the Jira ticket.
5) Add an option to create a lightweight runbook stub (Confluence) with owner/slo/retention.
6) Create a small runbook and test plan for Support to use during rollout.

Risks / Privacy / Security notes:
- Creating automated service accounts increases attack surface; scopes must be principle-of-least-privilege and keys rotated on creation. Security to sign-off on scope list before implementation.
- External partner templates require additional gating to avoid data leakage — legal review required.

Dependencies:
- Slack Admin API permissions for provisioning (team-admin or org-integration role).
- Jira API token with project-creation rights or an internal provisioning service.
- Confluence template endpoints and a location for standardized templates.
- Vault secrets writer role for service-account keys.

Timeline suggestion:
- Week 1: finalize mockups & permission matrix with Security & Product.
- Week 2: backend prototype for Slack/Jira/Confluence calls; security review of service account scopes.
- Week 3: integrate approvals, vault storage, and audit logging.
- Week 4: internal pilot with two pods, iterate, then rollout.

Additional notes:
Reviewed last 30 support tickets tagged 'channel-provision' — average time-to-complete 3.8 days, ~48% required follow-up access changes.
Examined current automation repo: provisioning command only supports top-level creation; no integrated Confluence/Jira stubbing available.
Identified that Vault role for existing bot does not permit writing new service accounts without manual ops intervention — will need a short-lived elevated role or a provisioning lambda.
Security raised concern: some pods request full 'manage' permissions in Confluence; template needs to constrain to 'add' or 'edit' for specific groups only.
(In Progress) Next steps: Leo to deliver mockups and a prototype API contract by 2026-03-12. Security will provide an approved scope list and required audit logging keys. Support will prepare a pilot checklist and a rollback plan.
If approved, create two pilot channels: 'eng-runtime-pilot' and 'data-platform-pilot' and run the end-to-end flow including service-account creation and vault write.
payload.summary: Interactive channel onboarding wizard with permission matrix and RBAC templates

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Perform a full entitlement snapshot across primary AWS and GCP orgs and provision a Just-In-Time (JIT) "jump" role for on-call and security engineers to use during the upcoming privilege audit. The snapshot will capture IAM role bindings, service account key usage, and cross-account trust relationships at the organization and project level.

Background:
- Quarterly security audit requires an authoritative mapping of who can assume high-privilege roles across our cloud accounts.
- Previous audits revealed stale role bindings in a handful of projects and two service accounts with unexpected broad scopes.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
- After a scheduled Vault SSH certificate rotation at 02:00 UTC on 2026-03-12, several ephemeral CI runners in prod-us-west started failing to forward SSH agent connections. Nightly release pipeline jobs that perform artifact fetches and deploy steps hang waiting for SSH operations to complete.

Impact:
- Nightly release (release/nightly) jobs in prod-us-west are stuck in "Queued" or "Running" with steps blocked on SSH forward (artifact scp/git fetch).
- Two releases missed the overnight window; customer-facing deploys delayed ~3.5 hours.
- No token theft or data exfiltration observed; scope appears limited to runner agent forwarding and key usage.

Environment:
- prod-us-west (GKE-based runner pool: runner-pool-ephemeral-usw1)
- Vault: v1.12, transit mount for SSH-cert-signing; automation rotated host and user SSH certs for ephemeral-user
- Runner image: rwm/ci-runner:2026-02-28-canary

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a new ephemeral runner pod with agent forwarding enabled (GIT_SSH_COMMAND with SSH_AUTH_SOCK mounted).
2) Attempt git fetch from private repo using SSH key that relies on agent-forwarding to use a signed cert from Vault.
3) Observe command stalls with 'Agent has no identities' or long TCP connection without authentication.

Expected behavior:
- SSH agent remains available inside runner pod; forwarded sockets accept requests and return signed cert identities.
- Git fetchs and scp complete within normal latency.

Observed behavior:
- Agent appears present (SSH_AUTH_SOCK path exists) but returns no identities when queried (ssh-add -l returns "The agent has no identities").
- `ssh -vvv` shows Agent forwarding accepted but new cert requests to Vault fail with TLS handshake EOF or 403 depending on pod.

Initial hypothesis:
- Vault rotation changed the SSH CA cert or altered the SSH sign endpoint token scope; ephemeral agent sockets were not rekeyed and the agent-proxy sidecar is failing to authenticate to Vault with rotated client certs.
- Alternatively a file-permissions change on the mounted socket during pod restart is preventing the ssh-agent process from accessing the socket file.

Logs / evidence:
- Runner pod logs (excerpt):
  - 2026-03-12T02:07:12Z runner-init: mounted /ssh-agent/socket, uid=1000 gid=1000
  - 2026-03-12T02:07:15Z agent-proxy: request to /v1/ssh/sign returned 403 {"errors":["permission denied: token missing role"]}
  - 2026-03-12T02:09:35Z git-fetch: fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
- Vault audit entries: multiple sign requests returning 403 at 02:07-02:10 UTC correlated with rotation job id vault-rotate-ssh-2026-03-12.
- No core dumps; Docker / container logs attached to related PR for deeper trace.

Workarounds attempted:
- Manually restarted agent-proxy sidecar (temporary fix for ~15 minutes on a handful of pods).
- Reissued a short-lived token scoped to ssh/sign and injected into a pod; cert signing then succeeded, indicating an auth issue rather than SSH daemon bug.
- Reverted the Vault rotation for the ssh-sign role on one test namespace which restored signing for new pods, but not for already-running pods.

Next steps requested:
- Engineering to confirm whether rotation job changed token scopes or CA fingerprints used by agent-proxy.
- Run controlled rotation in staging to reproduce and capture full agent-proxy traces.
- Add a healthcheck in the runner bootstrap that verifies agent-proxy can sign a test payload post-rotation and fails fast if not.

Additional notes:
Agent-proxy authenticates to Vault using k8s service account token + role mapping. Rotation playbook updated role metadata which removed the 'impersonate:ephemeral/*' matcher in ACE.
Reproduced locally by deploying a runner pod with old SA token vs new role mapping; older tokens succeed until TTL expiry; new tokens fail immediately with 403.
File permission hypothesis weakened: several pods show correct socket permissions (srw-rw----) but still no identities. Points back to upstream auth rejection rather than file-level access.
Vault team confirmed the rotation job created a new signing key and replaced role bindings to tighten access for long-lived hosts; ephemeral runner pattern not included intentionally but missed in role mapper list.
Potential risk: continued rotation without fix will cause future transient blackouts when tokens refresh.
Mitigation applied: Vault rotation was partially rolled back for the 'ci-agent-ssh-signer' role mapping for ephemeral/* service accounts to restore signing capability for existing runner pools. Longer-term fixes: (1) Update vault-rotation playbook to include ephemeral runner role in role-to-SA mapping and add automated validation in the rotation job to run a smoke-sign against a canary runner-pod, (2) Add a bootstrap healthcheck in runner image to validate agent-proxy signing on startup and fail fast, (3) Add monitoring alert for 403 spikes on /v1/ssh/sign. Follow-up ticket created to harden rotation: INT-871578.
Patch vault-rotation playbook to include ephemeral runner SA mapping and smoke tests (owner: Vault team, due: 2026-03-18)
Add runner bootstrap agent-proxy sign healthcheck and fail-fast behavior (owner: CI infra, due: 2026-03-20)
Create alert for >5 403s/min on /v1/ssh/sign in prod-us-west (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-15)
Document emergency rollback steps for SSH role rotation in OPS runbook (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-17)
payload.summary: SSH agent forwarding broken for ephemeral runners after Vault SSH cert rotation, nightly release jobs hang

Issue summary: Multiple user accounts across two regions entered a brief lockout state and we observed a surge of failed token exchange attempts tied to a set of legacy service tokens that were scheduled for rotation. Impact: Intermittent login failures for ~12 engineers and two service accounts; alert storm to PagerDuty; potential phishing correlation under investigation. A subset of orphaned tokens (previously issued to decommissioned CI runners and not fully removed from the token store) started cycling, leading to repeated refresh attempts that generated account lockout conditions for user identities associated with those tokens. Concurrently, we saw an increase in suspicious external consent grant requests to an old AD app registered in the tenant. Hypothesis: A prior phishing incident exposed or orphaned refresh tokens; automated rotation job re-used the stale entries and amplified the auth failures.
