payload.description:
Issue summary
- Helio Health reports that S3 audit export appears to be missing events for a ~25–40 minute window on 2025-04-28 (approx 18:10–18:50 UTC). They observed a gap when querying S3 objects by ingestion time in their downstream pipeline.

Impact
- Customer perceived loss of audit evidence (compliance concern). No Redwood control-plane/service disruption reported. Primary risk is trust in export correctness and ability to reconstruct audit trail.

Customer context / destination
- Destination: Amazon S3 (cross-account), SSE-KMS enabled (customer-managed key)
- Delivery format: newline-delimited JSON batches written to date/hour partitions
- Customer ingestion: internal pipeline that expects near-real-time object creation, then forwards into their SIEM.

What the customer observed
- Gaps in their SIEM view when filtered by event timestamps.
- S3 bucket showed reduced object creation during the window.
- They did not see explicit DLQ notifications.

Initial hypothesis (support)
- Exporter backlog due to downstream throttling (S3 SlowDown / 503) causing lag and later backfill; events not dropped but delivered late.

Investigation notes (Redwood)
- Checked exporter metrics for tenant (us-east):
  - audit_exporter_export_lag_seconds increased sharply during window (peaked ~2,100s).
  - audit_exporter_adapter_errors_total{adapter="s3", error_code~"SlowDown|503"} spiked with exponential backoff.
  - Throughput recovered after downstream errors subsided; backlog drained over ~50 minutes.
- Checked exporter logs: repeated S3 PutObject failures with SlowDown responses; retries succeeded after backoff.
- Checked checkpoint progression: checkpoint did not advance while S3 errors present; resumed and advanced monotonically afterward.
- No evidence of event drops in exporter pipeline; no DLQ entries for the time window.

Root cause
- Downstream throttling from S3 (SlowDown/503 responses) triggered exporter backoff and temporary reduction in delivered batches.
- Customer pipeline interpreted the resulting delivery delay as missing data because it keys off S3 object creation time and uses a tight "arrival window".

Delivery semantics clarification (beta)
- Audit export is at-least-once with checkpointing. During downstream outages/throttling, delivery can lag and then backfill once destination is writable.
- Customers must deduplicate using event_id (stable) and should not assume near-real-time object creation during throttling.

Requested from customer
- Re-run their ingestion for the window using a broader time horizon (e.g., last 24h) and deduplicate by event_id.
- Confirm their pipeline does not discard late-arriving objects.

Workaround offered
- If they still see a gap after re-run, Redwood can assist with an operator replay (if any batches ended in DLQ) or targeted backfill within allowed backfill window.

Next steps
- Provide customer-facing guidance: recommended ingestion approach, dedup expectations, and how to monitor exporter lag/health.
- Ensure Helio Health has access to Export Status view in Console for lag/last success (RBAC permitting).
2025-04-29 09:12 UTC — Liam O'Rourke (Reporter, TAM)
Customer report from Helio Health (security ops) that they have a gap in audit events in their SIEM view and suspect S3 export dropped records. They cite a ~30 minute window yesterday where their S3 ingest saw no new objects. Requesting urgent confirmation whether Redwood dropped events or can backfill.
2025-04-29 09:26 UTC — Miguel Santos (Enterprise CSM)
Adding: customer is in beta cohort. They are concerned about audit evidence completeness for compliance. They are currently querying by object creation time; may be discarding late data in their pipeline. They asked whether we guarantee exactly-once (they assumed yes).
2025-04-29 09:41 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE, Assignee)
Looking at exporter dashboards for tenant in us-east. I see a lag spike around 18:10–19:00 UTC with increased s3 adapter errors. Pattern looks like S3 SlowDown + retries. Checkpoint did not advance during that window; it resumed afterward and caught up. No indication of drops so far.
2025-04-29 10:03 UTC — Colin O'Donnell (Solutions Engineer)
Can someone confirm customer bucket settings? Cross-account + SSE-KMS can be sensitive if KMS throttles. Also ask if they have lifecycle rules or prefix hot-spot issues. For now, we should align on semantics: at-least-once, dedup via event_id.
2025-04-29 10:18 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE)
Pulled exporter logs (sanitized). Repeated PutObject failures:
- error_code=SlowDown
- http_status=503
- retry_backoff_ms increasing
Retries eventually succeed. No DLQ writes during the reported window. This is consistent with delivery delay, not loss.
2025-04-29 10:33 UTC — Liam O'Rourke (TAM)
Relayed to customer: we see downstream throttling responses from S3, exporter applied backoff, and delivery lagged but resumed and backfilled. Asked them to re-run ingestion for the window and dedup on event_id. Customer asked for written explanation they can attach to internal incident ticket.
2025-04-29 11:05 UTC — Kevin Osei (Security Engineering)
Please be explicit: beta uses at-least-once; not exactly-once. Dedup is expected downstream using event_id. Also confirm they understand Redwood retention vs export responsibilities (Confluence policy page). Avoid implying we retain indefinitely; stick to documented backfill limits.
2025-04-29 12:02 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE)
Follow-up: export lag peaked ~35 min, then returned to baseline. Current health: last_success within 2 min, error rate normal. I recommend we ask customer to adjust their pipeline to accept late-arriving objects and not treat "no objects created" as data loss.
2025-04-30 08:17 UTC — Liam O'Rourke (TAM)
Customer re-ran ingestion over last 24h and confirmed the previously "missing" events appeared, but their pipeline had filtered them out as late. They will update their logic to use event timestamp and dedup by event_id. They requested a short set of best practices; I pointed them at our current beta guidance (delivery semantics + dedup).
2025-05-02 16:40 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE)
Closing notes: no evidence of data loss; behavior explained by S3 throttling and exporter backoff. Suggest adding a product/docs action item to emphasize that object creation time is not a reliable proxy for audit event time and that lag/backfill is expected during downstream throttling.
Resolved as "not missing" — exporter experienced downstream S3 throttling (SlowDown/503), causing temporary delivery lag and later backfill. Customer pipeline incorrectly discarded late-arriving objects; customer confirmed events were present after re-ingestion. Provided guidance: monitor exporter lag/health, widen ingest window, and deduplicate by event_id per at-least-once semantics. No DLQ replay required.
payload.summary: S3 audit export: customer reports "missing" audit events during downstream throttling; exporter lag/backfill semantics and dedup guidance

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple employees on the 5th floor report intermittent failures reaching internal services (e.g., internal registry, metrics, and auth services) while connected to the corporate SSID and the company VPN. Symptoms appear when a nearby personal mobile hotspot (identified by device MACs ending in :A3:B2) is active and clients are simultaneously connected to both Wi-Fi and the hotspot (phone tethering).

Impact: Affects ~8-12 users on floor 5 during peak periods. Causes service access errors (timeout, TCP RST) for internal infra services; developer workflows and monitoring alerts are impacted. No customer-facing outages.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-09 08:45: First user report in #it-support. Intermittent 502/timeout from internal registry.
- 2026-03-09 09:12 Initial log correlation shows VPN tunnels established but service replies not reaching client.
- 2026-03-10 10:00 Wireless controller logs show client is connected to corporate-SSID; ARP and DHCP entries show frequent default-gateway change for some clients.
- 2026-03-10 14:30 Wireshark capture from affected client shows SYN/ACKs from internal service returning to public hotspot IP (asymmetric path) and NAT hairpin failures.

Observed behavior: When personal hotspot is active, some clients choose the hotspot's upstream path for return traffic despite sending via VPN. Packet captures show outbound packets encapsulated by VPN to the datacenter, but the return path uses hotspot's public IP (likely because of source address selection or local policy), causing stateful firewall/NAT to drop or misroute replies. Symptoms include TCP connection reset, application-level timeouts, and occasional VPN rekey/teardown after repeated failures.
1) On a laptop joined to corporate SSID, start company VPN and confirm access to internal service (curl http://internal-registry:5000/ping).
2) On nearby phone, enable mobile hotspot and connect the same laptop to the hotspot simultaneously (test cases seen when laptop maintains both Wi-Fi and hotspot associations via different radios or USB tethering).
3) Re-run curl to internal service; observe intermittent failures and capture packets with tcpdump.
4) Compare traceroute and tcpdump to confirm asymmetric return path via hotspot external IP.
Hypotheses considered:
- Client OS/source address selection uses non-VPN interface for some return traffic (Windows metric or multipath behavior).
- NAC/Edge firewall stateful NAT expects symmetric path; hotspot introduces asymmetry.
- AP/controller roaming or client sticky rules causing local route preference swings.

Findings so far:
- Packet captures confirm return traffic leaving the datacenter to the hotspot public IP rather than the VPN source.
- DHCP lease events on affected clients show occasional default gateway re-evaluation when hotspot is active.
- Wireless controller shows no immediate configuration anomalies for corporate-SSID; guest/guest-vlan isolation appears intact.
- No config changes were rolled out in the timeframe, making a local client/network interaction the likely trigger.

Temporary mitigations tested:
- Instructed users to disable phone hotspot while on corporate SSID: immediate improvement.
- Applied a quick NAC rule to de-prioritize clients with active tethering flags (RADIUS vendor attribute) on floor 5 for 24h; reduced incident count by ~70%.
Aisha Kapoor (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Initial user reports collected from #it-support and direct Slack DMs. Attaching sample client IPs and timestamps.
Liam Chen (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Captured tcpdump from an affected laptop and uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-debug/INT-130218/client-capture-20260310.pcap). Observed SYN/ACKs returning to hotspot IP. Suspect asymmetric routing due to source address selection.
Network Eng (Priya Reddy) 2026-03-11: Confirmed controller logs show client retains corporate-SSID association while tethered in some USB-tether cases. Will review AP roaming/power settings and client metric policies.
SRE (Marcus Li) 2026-03-11: Raised PR to update firewall NAT timeouts and add heuristic allowing return traffic to hotspot IP for short windows (PR link in related_github_prs). This is a stopgap and not ideal.
Liam Chen 2026-03-12: Rolled temporary NAC rule to isolate tethered clients on floor-5 for 24 hours. Monitoring for recurrence. Planning long-term fix with wireless team.
Workaround applied: NAC rule deployed to reduce likelihood of asymmetric routing by isolating tethered clients on floor 5; users advised to disable personal hotspots while on corporate network. Long-term plan: wireless team to adjust AP power/steering and implement controller-level tethering detection and enforcement; network team to evaluate route preference and Windows metric tuning documentation. Follow-ups: schedule change in controller to enforce guest uplink isolation on APs serving floor 5 and roll firewall NAT/window improvements (tracked in related_github_prs).
1) Wireless team (Priya) to test AP power/roaming adjustments in staging (target: 2026-03-18).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403/Range mismatch errors when fetching large sharded model artifacts from Redwood control plane. Failures correlate with network path through customer's Transit Gateway (TGW) where IP-in-IP encapsulation and an inline WAN appliance perform MSS clamping. Impact: model pulls fail during model boot, causing degraded serving and elevated latency for customer-facing inference.
Model pull failures for ~20% of attempts during nightly scaling; serving nodes fall back to older cached weights, causing slower cold-start and a small percentage of inference errors.
Private deployment with TGW-attached branch sites using IP-in-IP (IPIP) encapsulation for site-to-site tunnels. Egress path traverses branch WAN appliance that applies MSS clamping to avoid PMTU blackhole on legacy MPLS links. Control plane and object storage endpoints reachable via VPCE gateway.
1) Provision a serving node in customer's private deploy in us-west-2 with model gpt-large-3b-sharded pinned to version v2026-02-28.
2) Trigger a cold start by scaling from 0 -> 3 replicas during nightly batch window (large shard downloads).
3) Observe artifact presigned range GETs failing intermittently with HTTP 206/416/403 or aborted HTTP/2 stream resets in curl/nghttp2 logs when path traverses branch TGW -> appliance -> internet egress.
4) Re-run with tcpdump on serving node and packet capture on branch appliance to correlate MTU, IPIP headers, and TCP segments.
5) Reproduce is time-correlated with branch appliance applying MSS clamp to 1200 bytes for tunneled flows.
6) Disabling IPIP (or bypassing the appliance) removes the failure consistently.
[serving-node] 2026-03-10T03:14:22Z GET /shards/part-12 Range: bytes=0-1048575 -> HTTP/2 stream error: PROTOCOL_ERROR (frame size mismatch)
[serving-node] 2026-03-10T03:14:23Z curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data
[appliance] 2026-03-10T03:14:21Z TCP: mss clamp applied: original 1460 -> 1200 for conn src=10.1.22.5 dst=54.239.12.10 (IPIP)
[pcap] seq 0x1a2b3c TCP payload sizes: 600, 600, 300 (after IPIP header) -> observed TLS record boundaries crossing frames leading to HTTP/2 HEADERS+DATA split and nghttp2 frame reassembly error
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Initial triage — customer reports shard validation failures on 0->3 scale-up. Asked for packet captures and appliance config screenshots.
Customer (DataSense SRE) 2026-03-10: Uploaded tcpdump and appliance syslogs to shared S3 (link in ticket). Note: this started after TGW attachment to new branch hub and enabling IPIP with legacy WAN appliance.
Marco Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-11: Observed consistent MSS clamp to 1200 bytes post-IPIP encapsulation resulting in TLS records spanning multiple TCP segments. Hypothesis: TLS record fragmentation + HTTP/2 frame splitting triggers nghttp2 frame length mismatch leading to stream resets and partial range reads, which artifact client treats as corruption and retries with invalid range -> 416/403.
Marco Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-11: Requested customer to temporarily disable MSS clamp on appliance or route traffic around the appliance. Customer agreed to test bypass during maintenance window.
Customer (DataSense SRE) 2026-03-12: Bypassed appliance for VPCE egress path during 02:00-03:30 UTC; artifact downloads completed without error for 2000+ pulls. Re-enabling appliance reproduced failures. Will coordinate WAN vendor to change clamp policy.
Marco Nguyen (SRE) 2026-03-12: Created infra PR to add additional guardrails: increase artifact client retry validation, and detect HTTP/2 frame reassembly errors to initiate TLS renegotiation fallback (gh PR #1289).
Reproduced locally using network emulation: adding 20 bytes of IPIP header + mss clamp to 1200 reproduces the nghttp2 frame error under HTTP/2 multiplexed shard fetches.
TLS stack (OpenSSL 3.1) preserves record boundaries but TCP segmentization from clamp causes a HEADERS frame split; nghttp2 treats illegal split as PROTOCOL_ERROR.
S3 presigned range behaviour: partial range retries with adjusted Range header contain offset mismatches when client received truncated payload leading to validation checksum mismatch -> server 403 on second attempt (presigned token replay semantics).
No evidence of model artifact corruption on S3 side; validation failures are client-side partial-read reassembly issues.
Related to path MTU/encapsulation interplay; existing docs mention PMTU but not interactions with MSS clamps on encapsulated flows.
Customer TGW route propagation timing and traffic steering to hub appliance exacerbated the window where this surface area affected scale-ups.
Workaround: Instructed customer to disable MSS clamping for VPCE-bound flows or to adjust clamp to MTU 1350 (accounting for IPIP overhead) until WAN vendor can patch. Implemented client-side mitigations: increased HTTP/2 reassembly tolerance and added explicit detection of truncated TLS records to trigger connection restart in PR gh.com/redwood/infra/pull/1289. Post-change verification: customer reported 0 failures during bypass window and subsequent test with adjusted clamp=1350 showed successful pulls for 5000 sequential shard downloads.
Confluence runbook update: add section on 'Encapsulation-aware MSS guidance' with recommended clamp values per encapsulation type.
Cloud infra task: add an early-detection metric for nghttp2 PROTOCOL_ERRORs during shard fetches and alert at >0.5% of shard pulls per minute.
Customer-facing docs: updated Private Deploy network checklist to call out TGW+IPIP interactions and VPCE egress validation steps.
Engineering: track gh issue #1290 to harden artifact client reassembly and add a test harness that injects small MTU and encapsulation headers.
payload.summary: TGW IP-in-IP encapsulation + MSS clamping causing TLS record fragmentation and HTTP/2 frame split, corrupting presigned shard downloads

Issue summary:
We need a narrowly-scoped, time-bound service principal/broker identity to enable the data-bridge CI workflow in the staging environment to run integration tests that read from a private AWS S3 bucket (analytics ingestion fixtures) and connect to a GCP Cloud SQL (Postgres) instance via the Cloud SQL Proxy.

Impact:
- CI integration tests for data-bridge are blocked; test coverage gated on these end-to-end runs.
- Affects several platform PRs queued behind green CI (approx 10 PRs).

Background:
- The data-bridge integration runner executes in our staging CI project (projects/redwood-staging-ci). The runner needs read-only access to s3://redwood-bridge-test-fixtures (AWS account: 123456789012) and Cloud SQL connect permission to staging-db (project: redwood-staging-db, region: us-central1).
- Current engineers have tested locally using personal credentials; org policy disallows using personal creds for CI.

Request (what we want provisioned):
1) An ephemeral GCP Service Account (SA) in projects/redwood-staging-ci named sa-data-bridge-ci@redwood-staging-ci. It should have only the roles/cloudsql.client role and iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator for the short-lived token path we use for proxying.
2) A short-lived AWS IAM Role in account 123456789012 named redwood-data-bridge-ci-role that the SA can assume via workload identity federation OR a temporary federated role accessible via STS for our cross-account CI runner. The role must be read-only for the specific S3 prefix redwood-bridge-test-fixtures/* and only allow GetObject, ListBucket.
3) The credentials MUST be limited to the staging CI runner service identity (k8s service account: staging/data-bridge-runner) via Workload Identity Federation mapping; no broad project-wide bindings.
4) Automatic revocation/expiration: tokens should expire within 6 hours and the role/session validity for cross-cloud assume should be limited to 1 hour. We request a maximum TTL policy enforced.

Access matrix (requested):
- GCP SA: roles/cloudsql.client (connect to staging-db), roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (restricted to token exchange for the specific K8s SA).
- AWS role: s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket for arn:aws:s3:::redwood-bridge-test-fixtures and arn:aws:s3:::redwood-bridge-test-fixtures/*; sts:AssumeRole allowed only for the OIDC principal mapped to the GCP SA/workload identity.

Security constraints and audit:
- Add both the GCP SA and AWS role to audit logs with a high retention flag for 90 days for these sessions.
- Add a Confluence runbook link (below) for rotating or revoking the mappings.
- Enable Cloud Audit Logs filter and CloudWatch logging for the assumed role events.

Steps we expect support to perform:
1) Provision the GCP SA with least-privilege roles and bind identity to the staging k8s SA via Workload Identity.
2) Create the cross-account AWS role with trust policy limited to the OIDC issuer + GCP SA subject and attach a restrictive inline policy for the S3 prefix.
3) Provide documented short example in our infra repo showing how CI exchanges SA token for AWS STS credentials and the minimal IAM policy required.
4) Add the created resources to the staging inventory (Terraform state or a managed alert) and populate a ticket comment with ARNs/email addresses.

Acceptance criteria:
- Data-bridge CI pipeline can run integration tests and access test fixtures without using personal credentials.
- Access is demonstrably scoped to the requested resources and sessions expire automatically.
- Audit logs show a successful assume/exchange during a CI run.

Rollback / cleanup plan:
- If anything is mis-scoped, revert by removing the trust binding and disabling the AWS role.
- We request a scheduled reminder to delete/confirm the need for the setup in 14 days (expiration/cleanup).

Additional notes:
CI runner can fetch S3 objects from the specified prefix without using personal creds
Cloud SQL connections succeed via Cloud SQL Proxy using the provisioned SA token
Sessions show assume/exchange events in audit logs
All credentials/tokens expire within the requested TTL windows

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several depot repair tickets from the last week report machines that fail imaging or drop into BitLocker recovery after a routine USB-C dock disconnect and hot-swap while NVMe is present. Impact: Machines returned to users with missing OS boot entries or BitLocker recovery prompts; blocks re-provisioning pipeline for affected units. Environment: Depot repair bench (staging-us-west), Windows 11 22H2 imaging profile, latest vendor NVMe drivers deployed via driverstore. Initial discovery: Repair tech unplugged a USB-C dock while NVMe drive remained active (hot-swap). After reconnect and power cycle, device shows additional orphaned EFI partitions or changed disk GUIDs so imaging fails to attach expected OS volumes.
1) Boot machine from WinPE recovery media with NVMe mounted and a USB-C dock connected (external USB hub present)
2) While OS image still assigned (WinPE session or Windows running in lab), unplug USB-C dock without performing safe removal for hub-attached devices
3) Reconnect dock and perform standard reboot to Windows PE imaging target
4) Run imaging task (image-builder v4.3) and notice imaging script cannot locate expected disk by signature; Diskpart lists unexpected extra EFI partition and missing OS partition
5) Attempt to continue results in BitLocker recovery or imaging abort with code 0x80070057 or 'no match for disk signature'.
2026-03-07 14:12:23 WinPE image-builder: ERROR ImageTask: failed to find disk with signature 0x3B2A1C4D - found disks: 0x9F1E2D3C, 0x3B2A1C4D (offline)
2026-03-07 14:12:26 diskpart: Disk ### Status Size Free Dyn Gpt
  Disk 0 Online 476 GB 0 B *
  Disk 1 Offline 512 GB 0 B *
2026-03-07 14:13:02 kernel: nvme0n1: controller reset due to sudden detach (dmesg capture from lab image log)
Hypothesis 1: USB-C dock hot-swap leaves NVMe controller in a transient state where the device returns with new GUIDs or exposes hidden recovery partition first.
Hypothesis 2: Vendor NVMe driver or firmware on certain SKUs does not gracefully handle bus detach/reattach under Windows PE, causing driverstore to register a duplicate device instance path.
Reproduced: Lab tech reproduced on Dell-Precision-5560 with dock model PD-2100 following steps above; observed orphaned EFI partition and disk signature mismatch.
Checked imaging logs and image-builder code: imaging looks up disk by signature GUID; when signature changes imaging treats disk as foreign and fails fast rather than performing fallback by model/size.
Driver/firmware correlation: Both affected units have NVMe firmware v1.2.3 and vendor-provided Windows driver 2.1.0 deployed. A Lenovo unit with newer firmware v1.3.0 did not reproduce the issue.
Temporary mitigation tested: Running 'diskpart -s cleanup-and-reassign.cmd' to clear orphan partitions and reapply expected GPT data let imaging succeed, but this is destructive and requires tech confirmation and data wipe — acceptable in depot but dangerous if done incorrectly.
Related past ticket: INT-31842 had an NVMe behavior after imaging referenced as similar symptom; cross-checked but root cause differs (that ticket was driverstore DKMS conflict in Ubuntu imaging).

Additional notes:
On depot bench, instruct techs to fully power down the machine before unplugging docks during repair workflows. Use provided depot cleanup script (disk-wipe-and-gpt-restore.ps1) to remove orphan partitions and rebuild GPT before imaging. Do not run cleanup on user-returned devices without explicit user data wipe authorization.
Patch adds a size+model match fallback when disk signature lookup fails, reducing false negatives in imaging. Firmware team engaged with NVMe vendor for a definitive firmware fix. Post-deploy we will run a 48-hour soak test in lab with dock hot-swap cycles. Follow-up ticket will track vendor firmware rollout to affected SKUs.
payload.summary: Orphaned NVMe partitions after USB-C dock hot-swap during depot repair causing imaging and BitLocker failures

Issue summary: Security audit discovered multiple CI service principals with overly broad roles (OrganizationOwner / Owner) in both AWS test accounts and GCP project sandboxes. This ticket is to consolidate those identities into a small, auditable set of service accounts with least-privilege roles and to remove any direct Owner/OrgOwner bindings from CI runner identities.

Impact: Potential for accidental or malicious privilege escalation from compromised CI runners; increases blast radius for config drift and deployment automation. No active exploit identified, but policy requires remediation before next quarterly audit.

Background: During the Feb 2026 internal IAM sweep (security-runbook v3), we flagged ~7 CI runner identities across two AWS accounts and three GCP projects that have owner-level permissions. These identities were created at different times by multiple teams and are referenced in a mix of GitHub Actions, CircleCI, and an internal self-hosted Runner Fleet. Ad-hoc fixes have been applied previously, but we need a coordinated consolidation and role-replacement plan that preserves CI workflows and secrets access.

Request: 1) Inventory every CI-related service principal/service account across the listed environments and map usages (pipelines, vault policies, KMS keys). 2) Create 2 standardized service accounts per cloud (ci-build, ci-deploy) with narrowly scoped roles and condition-based bindings. 3) Implement IAM bindings via IaC (Terraform modules) and revoke legacy Owner/OrgOwner bindings. 4) Update runbooks and rotate short-lived credentials/keys as part of cutover.

Constraints/Non-goals: This ticket does not include rearchitecting CI tooling (e.g., replacing CircleCI). We will avoid changes that require immediate changes to customer-facing deployments. Migration windows must be schedulable with team owners.

Acceptance criteria: - Inventory documented in linked Confluence page. - Terraform modules reviewed in a GitHub PR and merged. - No CI runner identity has Owner/OrgOwner after cutover. - CI pipelines validated in staging and smoke-tested in prod. - Post-change IAM scan shows reduction in owner-level principals by >=90%.
2026-03-02: Initial audit produced CSV of principals; 7 candidates identified (4 AWS IAM roles, 3 GCP service accounts).
2026-03-03: Confirmed two AWS roles are referenced by legacy CircleCI runners; owners are @infra-legacy and @data-eng.
2026-03-04: One GCP service account is used for KMS unwrap in a deploy pipeline; will require a key-binding migration or a short-lived key approach.
Hypothesis: Historical convenience overrides (Owner role) were used for speed. Least-privilege roles can be implemented by scoping to specific APIs (kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt, storage.objects.get) and resource-level RBAC.
Risk note: Removing Owner from the deploy identity without staging cutover will break scheduled releases; schedule a canary deploy window.
Run internal iam-scan v2 against AWS account: aws-test-1 and aws-test-2 (script: tools/iam_scan.sh) to list principals with AdministratorAccess or Owner policies.
Run gcloud asset search-all-iam-policies for projects: ci-sandbox-eu, ci-sandbox-us, ci-staging to surface serviceAccount bindings to roles/owner.
Correlate principals to CI pipeline config (repo .github/workflows, .circleci/config.yml) to find usages.
In progress: terraform module 'ci-service-accounts' created in infra-iam repo (PR referenced). Staged bindings applied to staging account on 2026-03-11; successful pipeline runs observed. Legacy Owner bindings scheduled to be revoked in a maintenance window 2026-03-15.
Follow-up: create automation to detect owner-level bindings weekly and alert #infra-iam with a one-click remediation runbook.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:20 - SRE Oncall (comment): Staged change applied to staging; two smoke jobs failed due to missing storage.objects.get permission. Adding storage reader role to ci-build service account and retesting.

payload.description:
Issue summary: After performing an in-place upgrade from Windows 11 21H2 -> 22H2 on several Lenovo devices, the SCCM client (ccmexec) fails to start due to WDAC enforcement. Devices repeatedly exit OOBE/provisioning and reapply imaging tasks, resulting in an enrollment/provisioning loop for end users.

Impact: ~24 developer laptops affected across two regions; users unable to complete provisioning or access corporate resources. Timed reboots and repeated autopilot/OOBE restarts observed. Triage escalated because this blocks new hires and several existing engineers.

Environment: Production autopilot-imaging profile; affected devices report as Lenovo models listed above; build image includes SCCM client v5.00.9088.1000 and WDAC policy bundle deployed via ConfigManager baseline.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start with device in OOBE and autopilot profile applied.
2) Apply latest image which performs an in-place 21H2 -> 22H2 upgrade.
3) During first-boot, ConfigManager baseline pushes WDAC policy and attempts to start the SCCM client service ccmexec.
4) Observe service start failure and automatic restart of OOBE/provisioning sequence.

Observed behavior: ccmexec fails to start with exit code 0xC0000409; Windows event logs indicate Device Guard/WDAC blocked the executable due to a hash mismatch. SCCM logs (CcmExec.log) contain repeated "Service start failed: Access denied" and "WDAC enforcement: prevented image execution" entries.

Expected behavior: WDAC policy should allow signed SCCM binaries (company-signed) and SCCM client should start normally so provisioning can complete.

Logs/snippets:
- EventLog (System): "Device Guard: Image execution prevented. Rule type: AllowList, Hash not recognized: C:\Windows\ccm\ccmexec.exe"
- CcmExec.log: "Failed to start ccmexec.exe, error 0xC0000409"
- WDAC audit logs show a policy hash mismatch against the manufacturer-supplied signed list.

Temporary workaround: Reimaging device with a fresh 22H2 offline image that includes the updated WDAC policy manifest resolves the loop. Manual acceptance (audit->permit) of the SCCM binary via local WDAC policy also allows ccmexec to start, but not scalable.

Business risk: High for onboarding cadence. If left unaddressed, new machines may require manual imaging intervention and SRE time for each onboarding.

Request: Investigate why WDAC policy deployed by ConfigManager rejects the company-signed SCCM binary after in-place upgrades. Determine whether the 22H2 upgrade changes file hashes (compression, signatures) or if policy manifests are not being refreshed. Provide a fix path and a short-term mitigation to prevent more devices from entering the loop.
2026-02-12: Initial triage - reproduced on two lab T14s. Confirmed ccmexec hash differs from manifest recorded in WDAC policy bundle.
2026-02-13: Compared ccmexec.exe from 21H2 base image vs post-upgrade; observed byte differences despite identical version metadata. Hypothesis: Windows upgrade re-signing/packaging changes binary hash.
2026-02-14: Pulled WDAC policy deployment logs from SCCM. Policy distribution completed, but policy manifest created during initial image build remains unchanged. Possible mismatch between manifest creation time and post-upgrade binary state.
2026-02-15: Confirmed that manual replacement of WDAC manifest with an 'AllowHash' entry for the post-upgrade ccmexec allows service start. This is not a long-term solution.
Next steps: Create reproducible test that captures binary delta during upgrade and verify whether ms-signed signature flag changes. Coordinate with Applied ML infra team for automated policy rebuild and with Build system to include post-upgrade manifest generation in image pipeline.

Additional notes:
2026-02-15 16:40 - Security (Evan Holt): We need to avoid wholesale 'Allow' rules. Prefer hashed allowlist entries generated from upgraded binaries. Requesting approval to publish new manifest to production after validation.
Workaround and short-term mitigation: publish an updated WDAC manifest containing post-upgrade hashes for SCCM binaries and roll out to autopilot image distribution. Long-term fix: update image build pipeline to generate WDAC manifests post-upgrade and add a validation step to detect hash drift. Follow-up action: Security to sign and approve the new manifest and SRE to automate manifest generation in CI. Pending tasks: security approval and controlled rollout (planned 2026-02-18).
payload.summary: WDAC blocks SCCM agent service start after Windows 11 22H2 in-place upgrade causing provisioning/enrollment loop

payload.description:
Users intermittently receive 403/authorization failures when trying to approve runbook requests in the internal Runbook Console. The UI prompts for reauthentication but Okta reports the user still has an active session. Behavioral pattern suggests two different session contexts are being observed by the runbook service (session swap) which results in the approval token being rejected.
Affects oncall engineers attempting to approve critical runbooks via the internal console and Electron runbook client. Approx 8-12 occurrences in the last 48 hours across US-East clusters; prevented at least three emergency mitigations from being executed within SLA windows.
1) Login to Runbook Console in Chrome (session A) via Okta SSO.
2) From the same machine, start Electron runbook client or CLI that initiates a separate SSO flow (session B) without fully clearing cookies/SSO state.
3) Trigger an approval flow in the Console (POST /api/v1/approvals).
4) Observe intermittent 403 with response body 'session-mismatch' or the UI asking to reauthenticate even though Okta shows active session.
Note: behavior is intermittent; reproduces more reliably when there is background automatic token refresh (Okta session refresh) occurring close to approval attempts.
2026-03-11T23:02:14Z auth-proxy[auth-78]: INFO user=lena.ortiz event=okta-session-refresh session_id=abcd1234 -> rotated to efgh5678 (source=refresh)
2026-03-11T23:02:14Z runbook-service[rb-21]: WARN approval=4423 user=lena.ortiz outcome=403 reason="session-owner-mismatch" expected_owner=abcd1234 observed_owner=efgh5678

2026-03-11T23:02:14Z console[ui-5]: ERROR approval-fallback user=lena.ortiz error="approval token validation failed: session mismatch" request_id=req_9a7b
Stacktrace excerpts show auth-proxy returned Set-Cookie with new session id while the session reference in the approval payload still referenced the old id.
Observed correlation between Okta session refresh events and approval failures (strong temporal clustering around refresh timestamps).
Auth-proxy rotates session id by issuing Set-Cookie during POST okta/refresh; runbook-service validates approval tokens against a session id stored client-side which can be stale when rotation happens mid-flow.
Hypothesis A: race during session rotation where UI obtains an approval token bound to old session id while auth-proxy issues new session id to the browser, causing token validation to fail server-side.
Hypothesis B: load-balancer affinity change causes the initial session-binding validation to hit a different auth-proxy instance that does not yet have the rotated session mapping.
Initial telemetry: 11 incidents between 2026-03-10 16:00 and 2026-03-12 08:00; 9 of 11 show identical runbook-service error string 'session-owner-mismatch'.
Repro steps created and confirmed locally by reproducing with parallel SSO flows (Console + Electron).
Related config: Okta refresh interval in our SSO policy was changed 2026-03-09 (internal change request ID IDP-2026-03-09), which increased frequency of background refresh by ~30%.

Issue summary:
A subset of internal users are unable to complete the Just-In-Time (JIT) temporary admin elevation flow for the Analytics Console. The identity proxy is returning 403 during the elevation callback. This appears correlated with IdP profiles that contain multiple 'primary' email aliases (legacy mail forwarding + new corporate alias).

Impact:
- ~8 engineers in the last 24 hours could not perform JIT elevation to run support queries in the Analytics Console.
- Blocking oncall investigation and timely incident responses for customer issues.
- Affects internal tooling only (no public API impact).

Environment:
- Prod identity-provider: Okta (organization profile namespace)
- Affected application: analytics-console (internal) behind identity-proxy v2.4.1
- Region: us-east cluster (token-issuer instance a1)

Steps to reproduce (observed with affected user accounts):
1) User clicks 'Request temporary admin' in Analytics Console.
2) Redirect to Okta app for approval flows.
3) Manager approves via Okta Approvals.
4) Callback to /auth/jit/callback returns 403 with body 'role_mapping_validation_failed' and missing role claim.
5) User remains un-elevated despite approval shown in Okta.

Observed behavior:
- Identity proxy logs show role-mapping step selecting an email principal that does not match the RBAC record because Okta profile contains two emails both flagged as 'primary' (legacy attribute set by previous migration). Role-mapper uses first-match logic and later normalizes to lowercase; the stored RBAC principal is uppercase alias. The combination leads to an unresolved principal lookup and 403.

Expected behavior:
- JIT flow should normalize aliases and reconcile duplicates so manager approval results in temporary elevation and audit log entries.

Logs & traces (excerpts):
- identity-proxy (a1) 2026-03-13T16:22:07Z ERROR role-mapper: principal_lookup_failed: principal="A.PATEL@EXAMPLE.COM" matched_candidates=["a.patel@example.com","a.patel+legacy@example.com"]
- auth-service 2026-03-13T16:22:08Z WARN elevation: elevation_callback status=403 reason="role_mapping_validation_failed" request_id=abc1234
- Okta system log (event 0oa1xj2a3): user.profile.emails=[{"value":"a.patel@example.com","primary":true},{"value":"a.patel+legacy@example.com","primary":true}]

Temporary workaround:
- Support can manually grant a short-lived role in RBAC for the canonical lowercase alias via admin UI. This has been used for 3 users while investigation proceeds.

Other notes:
- The IdP migration in 2025 left a small population of accounts with duplicate primary flags. We previously patched some flows but JIT path was not covered.
- There is an open plan to normalize Okta profiles (consolidate primary flag) but it requires coordination with HR onboarding sync.

Suggested next steps:
- Short-term: update role-mapper to perform deterministic normalization and try alternate candidate matching before failing.
- Mid-term: run bulk IdP profile audit and schedule cleanup for duplicates.
- Add test coverage for duplicate-primary-email cases in identity-proxy unit/integration tests.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 09:05 - DevOps Oncall: Staging build with normalization landed (identity-proxy v2.4.2-rc1). Running integration tests against synthetic Okta responses including duplicate primary emails.
Hotfix (identity-proxy v2.4.2) implemented normalization and fallback candidate matching. Deployed to prod us-east 2026-03-14T15:12Z. Verified 5 recent failed elevation attempts now succeed. Follow-up action: schedule IdP profile cleanup with HR sync team and add integration test for duplicate-primary email scenarios.
payload.summary: Duplicate primary email in IdP profile prevents temporary admin elevation for internal analytics console

Issue summary:
- Users with long or colliding identity attribute namespaces (department/service prefix + username) received a 403 during SSO completion to the bastion host.
Impact:
- ~18 engineers and several CI service accounts could not start interactive bastion sessions for ~3 hours in us-west.
- Blocked access to internal-only diagnostics and runbook execution for oncall.
Environment:
- prod, us-west; identity-proxy v2.13.1; bastion session parser 1.7.0.

1) Ensure user identity has a long attribute in Okta: departmentPrefix-userName (e.g., svc-data-analytics-longprefix-jdoe)
2) Initiate SSO login to bastion via console (electron app) or CLI plug-in
3) Observe that callback from identity-proxy returns 200 but the bastion session initialization returns 403 with 'principal namespace mismatch'

SSO flow completes at identity-proxy; callback shows user identity attributes present. Bastion rejects the session with 403 'namespace collision' logged by session-parser. The session object shows truncated 'identity_namespace' or a replaced value (e.g., 'svc-data-analytic' instead of full 'svc-data-analytics-longprefix-jdoe').
Identity attributes should be forwarded intact from identity-proxy to bastion session-parser and used for RBAC lookups. No truncation or overwriting should occur for identity namespace fields.
[identity-proxy] 2026-03-10T09:12:04Z INFO callback received for state=abc123 attrs={'identity_namespace':'svc-data-analytics-longprefix-jdoe','roles':['dev'] }
[bastion-session] 2026-03-10T09:12:04Z WARN session_parser: normalized namespace 'svc-data-analytic' length=20 -> collision_detected=true
[bastion-auth] 2026-03-10T09:12:04Z ERROR authorize: principal namespace mismatch for principal 'svc-data-analytic' -> 403

Initial hypothesis: Okta SCIM or attribute mapping truncated value during SCIM sync. Verified by pulling raw callback payloads from identity-proxy logs — full attribute present. Root cause reproduced in staging: session-parser module applies legacy normalization that strips trailing tokens after 20 chars to match old schema. This normalization predated the current naming convention which now frequently exceeds 20 chars.
- Confirmed no recent Okta mapping changes (checked audit logs).
- Triage with SRE and Identity team at 09:40; created hotfix branch on identity-proxy to bypass parser normalization where upstream attribute is already namespaced.
- Cross-checked GraphQL RBAC service: lookup succeeded when given the full namespace; failure happens only when session-parser produces truncated key.

Legacy session-parser normalization truncates identity_namespace to 20 characters to accommodate an older downstream index. Naming conventions expanded over time (service prefixes + descriptive team names), causing frequent collisions and RBAC mismatches. The identity-proxy was forwarding attributes correctly; the truncation was introduced in session-parser for historical compatibility and not updated with schema changes.
Applied hotfix: removed hard 20-char truncation in session-parser and added explicit validation so long namespaces are passed through. Deployed patch to us-west canary at 2026-03-10T10:30, full rollout completed by 2026-03-10T11:50. Backfilled the session store for affected sessions (recreated 18 sessions after user re-auth) and cleared stale entries. Added feature flag to revert if unexpected downstream issues arise.
Hotfix verified by two affected users and automated smoke tests. No downstream index regressions observed. PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/422. Follow-up tasks tracked in INT-314900 (runbook/schema work).
- ACTION-1: Add schema contract test between identity-proxy and bastion session-parser (owner: Priya) - due 2026-03-20
- ACTION-2: Update runbook 'Bastion SSO namespace collisions' with detection query and mitigation steps (owner: SRE) - due 2026-03-17
- ACTION-3: Add lint/CI check to fail builds that introduce hard truncation of identity fields (owner: Platform Eng) - due 2026-03-25

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:03 - Oncall (SRE Rotation): Monitored; no new 403s related to namespace collisions observed after rollout.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We need a tenant-aware Slack topic provisioning gateway (webhook/API) that enforces required metadata at creation time (tenant_id, owning_team, owner_email, data_classification, related_jira_project). The gateway should create a Jira project draft or link to an approval ticket, seed a Confluence space from a template, attach retention/archival metadata, and register the channel in the central provisioning index.

Impact:
Manual channel creation frequently results in missing owners, incorrect data classification, inconsistent channel naming, and no automated audit trail. This increases compliance and onboarding friction for cross-tenant teams and creates incidents when channels with regulated data are created without controls.

Request / Requirements:
- A provisioning gateway endpoint that teams (and self-serve UI) call to request new public/private Slack channels and topic spaces.
- Enforce required metadata: tenant_id, owner_email, owning_team, data_classification (Public/Internal/Restricted), retention_tier, and expiry_date (optional).
- Gate creation behind a Jira approval flow for enterprise/private tenants: creating a Jira approval ticket in project INT-ONBOARD (or configurable) with prefilled fields and SLA.
- On approval, automatically: create Slack channel with standardized name, assign channel owner(s), seed Confluence space from template 'Tenant Project Seed v2', attach retention policy, and add channel to central index (git-backed manifest).
- Integration with Okta group mapping and service account provisioning for bots.
- Emit audit events to existing telemetry pipeline (logs + datadog metric + retention index).
- Admin/UI: expose an admin page to view pending requests, metadata compliance failures, and audit history.

Background / Context:
- There are many prior tickets and requests about inconsistent channel metadata and missing owners (see linked_issues). Existing onboarding bots handle ephemeral research channels but lack tenant scoping and metadata enforcement. The provisioning manifest is currently manually edited in a repo which introduces drift.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) New requests can be submitted via an API or Slack shortcut that populates required metadata.
2) Requests missing required metadata are rejected with clear error messages and a link to docs.
3) Approved requests create Slack channel + Confluence seed + Jira project link + entry in provisioning index automatically.
4) Audit events for every step appear in the telemetry pipeline within 5 minutes.
5) Admin view shows pending approvals and metadata compliance metrics.
6) Security review signoff checklist satisfied (KMS keys for any service accounts, least-privilege Okta mappings).

Steps to reproduce (example flow):
1) Team calls POST /provisioning/v1/request with payload missing owner_email -> gateway returns 400 with guidance.
2) Team resubmits with owner_email and tenant_id -> gateway creates approval ticket INT-927463-APPROVAL in INT-ONBOARD and sends Slack DM to approver.
3) Approver clicks Approve -> provisioning runs and creates resources.

Notes on scope boundaries:
- This task covers the gateway, metadata validation, Jira approval wiring, Confluence seed orchestration, Slack channel creation, and telemetry emission.
- UI polish, non-critical UX improvements, and multi-tenant billing hooks are out of scope for the MVP.

Initial scan: existing provisioning-bot repo (github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning-bot) supports ephemeral channel templates but hardcodes tenant-less naming and lacks mandatory fields. There is an ad-hoc provisioning manifest in infra/provisioning/index.yaml that teams edit by PR. Talked to infra-owner (Aisha Martin) and product (Liam Rodriguez) on 2026-02-28. Risk: current service accounts do not have Okta group lookup permissions for tenant mapping; need to create a dedicated service account with read-only Okta directory access. Linked previous tickets: INT-246801 (tenant-gated onboarding), INT-613214 (jpt lifecycle sync) for reference.

Implementation proposal (MVP):
1) Build a small gateway service (serverless or lightweight k8s service) that validates payloads against a JSON schema and emits a pre-approval Jira ticket (project configurable).
2) Reuse provisioning-bot code for Slack channel creation but add standardized naming function and metadata label attachments (topic + pinned message with metadata).
3) Hook Confluence REST API to clone 'Tenant Project Seed v2' and set page permissions according to owning_team Okta group.
4) On approval event, run an orchestrator job that performs creation steps in a transactional way and emits audit events to the observability pipeline. Implement rollback on partial failure (e.g., delete created channel if Confluence seed fails).
5) Add an admin endpoint and a small React admin UI for reviewers to approve/reject and inspect metadata compliance.

Implementation notes: prefer service account approach and limited Okta permissions. Use existing infra CI for manifest PR creation and update to central index repo. Ensure feature flags for gradual rollout.

1) Gateway rejects requests missing tenant_id or owner_email with descriptive errors.
2) Approval tickets are auto-created in the configurable Jira project with required fields populated.
3) On approval, Slack channel, Confluence seed, and provisioning index entry are created within a single orchestration and audit events are emitted.
4) Admin UI surfaces pending approvals and metadata compliance metrics.
5) Security review is completed and documented in related_confluence_pages.
2026-03-01 | Priya Kapoor (Reporter): Creating this request after recurring issues with tenant channels missing owners. See examples in INT-246801. Goal is an automated, auditable path for enterprise/private tenants.
2026-03-02 | Aisha Martin (Infra): Quick note - provisioning index is currently a YAML file in infra/provisioning. We should avoid manual edits and instead update via a PR that the gateway generates. Also we need a dedicated service account for Okta lookups.
2026-03-03 | Maya Singh (Security): Security checklist items: ensure KMS keys for any service account secrets, rotate keys quarterly, ensure Confluence cloning respects page-level permissions. I'll volunteer for the security review during design phase.
2026-03-04 | Evan Chen (Assignee): Starting design spike. I'll prototype the validation schema and Slack naming function this week, then wire up Jira ticket creation for approvals. ETA for first prototype: 2026-03-12.
2026-03-05 | Liam Rodriguez (Product): Please ensure admin UX exposes reasons for metadata rejection and links to docs. Also capture metrics: avg time to approval, percent of requests with missing metadata.
2026-03-05 | Evan Chen: Noted. Adding telemetry goals to acceptance criteria.
TBD - design spike in progress. Will update ticket with PR links and rollout plan after prototype.
payload.summary: Tenant-aware Slack topic provisioning gateway with metadata enforcement

payload.description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-05 09:20 UTC multiple internal users reported 403 / "role not found" errors when accessing the Analytics Portal. Failures correlated with recent Okta group membership changes made by HR/IT provisioning. Impact: ~30 engineers intermittently unable to open dashboards or run queries for ~30-90 minutes. Not a full outage but blocked several oncall and reporting workflows.

Observed behavior: Users re-authenticating sometimes succeeded immediately; other times they needed support to trigger a manual RBAC cache invalidation. Errors surfaced as 403s from analytics-portal with response body: "RBAC: user has no roles for resource".

Environment details: Production (us-east). Identity pipeline: Okta -> event-stream (kafka) -> identity-events-consumer -> identity-service (applies changes) -> rbac-cache (in-memory cache in identity-service with 5m TTL) -> service-side authorization checks.

1) Make an Okta group membership change for a test user (add to analytics_readers).
2) Wait for the provisioning change to be emitted to the Okta event stream (Okta system->event webhook).
3) Observe identity-events-consumer processing lag in metrics (consumer lag > 0).
4) Immediately attempt to access Analytics Portal while consumer lag exists and rbac-cache TTL has not expired — expected: 403 despite user being in Okta group.
5) After either the event consumer catches up OR cache TTL expires (5m) and cache invalidation occurs, access is restored.
2026-03-05T09:22:11Z identity-events-consumer [WARN] partition 3 lag=1248 events; processing stalled
2026-03-05T09:23:03Z identity-service [ERROR] rbac-lookup user=apatel role_lookup=miss -> deny
2026-03-05T09:24:09Z analytics-portal [INFO] authz deny user=apatel reason=RBAC_CACHE_MISS ttl=240s
2026-03-05 09:30 UTC — Support (Marco Ruiz): Confirmed multiple 403 reports. Asked affected users to capture screenshots and exact timestamps. Asked oncall SRE to check consumer lag and identity-service logs.
2026-03-05 09:42 UTC — SRE Oncall (Diego Morales): Observed kafka consumer lag spike on topic okta.events.consumer-group (partition 2/3). Consumer CPU at 95% on identity-events-consumer-1; replicas were restarted during a deploy window 09:10-09:15 UTC. Possible backlog created by mid-deploy transient. Increased consumer parallelism from 2->4 to catch up; lag dropped to zero by 09:58.

Additional notes:
2026-03-05 12:10 UTC — Support (Marco Ruiz): Customers (internal) confirmed access restored. Documented mitigation steps and asked Identity Eng to propose a long-term fix.
Hypothesis: sequence of events — a deploy/restart window at 09:10 caused identity-events-consumer to fall behind; meanwhile HR bulk group changes were processed causing many membership events to be queued. Because identity-service relies on a TTL'd in-memory RBAC cache (5m), the processed events were not applied to cached entries until cache expired or explicit invalidation occurred -> transient denies. Root cause contributors: (1) small consumer parallelism and CPU saturation during deploy, (2) RBAC cache TTL too long for high-churn groups, (3) no immediate cache invalidation on event processing success. Metrics reviewed: consumer lag timeline, identity-service cache hit ratio, analytics-portal 403 spike. No database corruption or Okta webhook failures found.
Short-term mitigation: increased consumer parallelism to drain the backlog; provided support workaround to invalidate per-user RBAC cache via admin endpoint; manually cleared cache for affected users.
Long-term fix (deployed 2026-03-07): publish explicit cache-invalidation events after identity-events-consumer successfully applies membership changes; adjust auto-scaling for identity-events-consumer to react at lag > 500; reduce RBAC cache TTL for high-churn groups from 5m -> 60s and keep default 5m for low-churn groups. Added dashboards: consumer lag, cache-miss ratio per org, and a synthetic auth check for analytics-portal for critical service accounts.
Follow-ups: (1) Add documented runbook section (Confluence) for consumer-lag incidents and manual cache invalidation steps. (2) Evaluate persistent storage for role mappings to allow immediate lookups rather than in-memory TTL dependency.
payload.summary: Intermittent RBAC denial on Analytics Portal after Okta profile events; identity event consumer lag + cache TTL interaction

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A subset of automation/service accounts created via SCIM provisioning include a custom attribute 'authNamespace' with a colon (e.g. 'automation:ci'). When these accounts attempt delegated SSH key provisioning for the internal bastion service, the RBAC parser rejects the namespace and key provisioning fails with a 403 from the bastion API.

Impact:
- Automated jobs that require bastion access (deploy hooks, nightly model-eval runners) are failing to obtain ephemeral SSH keys.
- Affected workloads are on prod us-west only. Estimated blast radius: ~14 service accounts across two repos.

Environment:
- Okta SCIM -> internal provisioner -> RBAC parser -> bastion-service (ephemeral SSH key issuance).
- Region: prod us-west.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a SCIM user with custom attribute authNamespace set to 'automation:ci' (this mirrors our customer/automation pattern).
2) Trigger service-account delegated key request via the API (POST /bastion/delegate with subject set to the SCIM-provisioned id).
3) Observe bastion API response 403 and error_code RBAC_NAMESPACE_PARSE_FAILURE.

Observed behavior:
- Bastion API responds 403 with body: {"error":"RBAC_NAMESPACE_PARSE_FAILURE","detail":"invalid namespace token ':'"}.
- Provisioner logs show mapping: scim.user.attributes.authNamespace=automation:ci -> validation failed.

Expected behavior:
- Namespaces with a single colon (legacy encoding used by automation team) should be accepted or normalized to a supported format during SCIM ingestion so delegated key issuance can proceed.

Logs / evidence snippets:
- provisioner stderr (2026-03-12T07:15:23Z): "ERROR rbac_parser: parse_namespace 'automation:ci' -> invalid token ':' at pos 10 (trace_id=tr-8a7f6)"
- bastion-service access log: "POST /delegate 403 trace_id=tr-8a7f6 subject=scim-usr-112"
- Okta audit event: SCIM PATCH user scim-usr-112 attribute authNamespace='automation:ci' (2026-03-12T07:14:55Z).

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support added an on-the-fly normalization mapping in the provisioner to rewrite 'automation:ci' -> 'automation-ci' for the 14 affected accounts. This allowed immediate key issuance and unblocked nightly runs. Change applied via hotfix config toggle 'scim.normalize_colon_namespaces=true' (rollout tracked in #support-hotfix channel).

Next steps / proposed fix:
1) Update SCIM ingestion to run a stable normalization pass for legacy namespace tokens (PR opened in repo 'provisioner', see related_github_prs).
2) Add unit tests around RBAC namespace parsing for the colon case.
3) Add a temporary metric that counts incoming SCIM authNamespace values containing disallowed characters and alert if >5/min.
4) Consider communicating expected namespace patterns to automation teams and add translation rules to SCIM mapping docs.

Customer-facing impact: none (internal-only).
Initial hypothesis: RBAC grammar change in rbac-parser v2.1.0 rejects ':' characters that were previously tolerated.
What we checked:
- Deployed rbac-parser v2.1.0 on 2026-03-10 (deploy audit: infra/deploy/v2.1.0).
- Replayed SCIM events for scim-usr-112 in a staging replay and reproduced parse failure.
- Confirmed Okta is sending attribute verbatim; no transformation at the IdP.
- Scoped blast radius by querying provisioner DB: SELECT id FROM service_accounts WHERE authNamespace LIKE '%:%' -> 14 rows.
- Looked for related incidents: none in status-page history.

Hypothesis now: parser grammar tightened to disallow namespace delimiter ':'. Root cause likely a defensive change without back-compat mapping in SCIM ingestion.

Trace IDs and logs of interest: tr-8a7f6, tr-9c2b1 (hotfix applied), provisioner-log-2026-03-12-07.gz.

Action items assigned:
- @Marcus Rivera: finish PR to add normalization and unit tests (in progress).
- @Lina Chen: notify automation teams and prepare short doc describing accepted namespace patterns.
- @SRE oncall: add alert on metric scim_bad_namespace_count > 5 for 10m.

Additional notes:
SRE-Oncall (2026-03-13): Added alert rule scim_bad_namespace_count to staging and wired Slack notification to #sre-alerts.
Partial workaround applied: config toggle normalization enabled to immediately restore bastion key issuance for affected accounts. Long-term fix implemented in provisioner (PR opened) and awaiting code review and canary rollout.
Avoid changing Okta-side values until normalization PR lands to prevent provisioning churn. This ticket will track PR review and production canary rollout.
payload.summary: SCIM 'authNamespace' value containing ':' prevents delegated SSH bastion key provisioning for automation service accounts

payload.description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC we observed a large automated login attempt spike against the Redwood identity endpoints originating from a small set of IP subnets. Around the same time, a cluster of privileged invite tokens were created via the internal /admin/invite API. Impact: potential unauthorized creation of privileged invites and risk of lateral access. No confirmed end-user breaches yet; invites were invalidated as a precaution. Environment: prod (us-east-1).

High-level timeline: 2026-03-12 08:58 UTC - first credential-stuffing alerts from auth-rate-limit; 09:05 UTC - enrichment API calls to breached-password vendor spike; 09:10 UTC - spike in POST /admin/invite creating admin-level invites; 09:15 UTC - automated remediation started (invite invalidation, key rotation).

Why this is concerning: attack pattern suggests automated credential stuffing combined with use of our enrichment/verification pipeline which had a service integration able to escalate or create invites via a synchronous job. The enrichment calls appear to have been used as part of a scripted flow to verify account existence and then trigger invite creation from a service account.

Initial mitigation applied: blocked 10 suspicious IP ranges via WAF; rotated the service account credentials used by enrichment pipeline; invalidated all outstanding admin invites created between 09:00-09:20 UTC; enabled stricter rate limits on /admin endpoints pending permanent fix.

Requested priority: urgent security follow-up and forensic preservation of logs and artifacts.
Simulate high-volume login attempts against auth.v1/login with common username lists under rate-limit thresholds to reproduce detection alerts
Trigger enrichment flow by making enrichment API calls for enumerated emails and observe whether invite creation job is invoked when enrichment returns 'known' status
Attempt repeat POST /admin/invite calls from a service token with similar call pattern to verify server-side rate-limiting behavior
Auth logs: ~37k failed login attempts over 12 minutes from 18 IPs clustered in two ASNs (timestamps 2026-03-12T08:58:00Z - 2026-03-12T09:10:00Z)
Enrichment vendor API: 1.2k enrichment requests for 'breach-check' returned positive for ~420 accounts (calls share X-Request-ID header series)
API gateway logs: 23 POST /admin/invite calls from service account token svc-enrich-01 between 2026-03-12T09:09:40Z and 2026-03-12T09:11:05Z (userAgent bot/1.2)
Created invite tokens: 18 admin-level invites created; 5 subsequently accepted (internal test accounts) before invalidation; we believe acceptance attempts were automated and against staging-like accounts
Hypothesis 1: credential-stuffing enumeration identified valid accounts; attacker script called enrichment endpoint which returned 'known' and triggered downstream invite creation via a legacy synchronous job path
Hypothesis 2: service account svc-enrich-01 had overly broad privileges allowing it to call invite-creation as part of a data-enrichment workflow; attacker abuse of compromised CI/automation credentials cannot be ruled out
Evidence shows service token present in X-Forwarded-Auth header on invite calls; token rotation and audit confirms token was active at time of calls
SRE traced the invite-create code path and found an unthrottled async worker (invite-provisioner) that processed enrichment results and called the admin-invite API; this worker lacked request-level RBAC enforcement
No indications yet of lateral movement beyond invite creation; logs of subsequent invites show immediate invalidation at 09:16 UTC; however, forensic snapshots of Kafka topic 'enrichment-results' were saved for retention

Additional notes:
Temporary: rotated the svc-enrich-01 service token, invalidated all admin invites created in the window, blocked offending IP ranges at WAF, captured forensic logs. Permanent: applied RBAC checks to invite-provisioner (PR merged), added request-level authorization and rate-limits, scheduled an identity team audit to remove invite creation from enrichment worker and instead surface candidates to a human-approved queue. Follow-up tasks created for Product and SecOps to review enrichment privileges and vendor usage policy.
Complete SecOps postmortem and circulate to Exec and IR teams (owner: Priya Nair)
Product to design UX change to require human approval for any admin-level invites created by automated workflows (owner: Tom Reynolds)
Run account compromise sweep for any accounts with enrichment-positive flags in the 24h window (owner: SRE)
Add additional alerting rules to detect enrichment->invite call chains and throttle automatically (owner: SRE)
Engage vendor to rate-limit enrichment API responses per account and review contractual abuse detection (owner: VendorOps)
Prepare customer-facing note if any external account evidence emerges (owner: CS)
Close ticket after 7-day monitoring window with no recurrence
payload.summary: Spike of credential-stuffing attempts followed by enrichment-API-driven privileged-invite creations

payload.description:
Multiple engineers reported inability to authenticate to Okta-backed internal apps while connected to the USB-C dock at SF office. Symptoms: repeated SSO timeouts or hanging at 'Signing in...' in browser, intermittent 502/524 errors in internal services. Disconnecting the dock (relying on laptop Wi-Fi only) restores SSO and internal app connectivity immediately. Issue started 2026-03-09 after a recent batch of Dell TB4 docks were deployed to hot-desks. This ticket centralizes investigation and mitigation notes.
~14 employees across two floors affected intermittently. Productivity impact: cannot sign in to internal apps (Confluence, Jira, internal admin UIs). No customer-facing outage. Roll-based fix required for broader fleet if regression replicates.
1) Connect Windows 11 laptop to USB-C TB4 dock (ethernet out) while Wi-Fi remains connected to corp-wifi
2) Launch WireGuard-based corp VPN client (auto-start) or ensure it is active
3) Open browser and navigate to any Okta-protected internal application (e.g., https://internal.redwood.test)
4) Observe SSO hanging on 'Redirecting to Okta...' or receive a TLS timeout; unplug dock or disable Ethernet adapter -> SSO completes within 1–3s
5) Reconnect dock -> problem returns within seconds
When dock connected, initial TCP SYN/handshake to Okta completes but TLS handshake stalls and browser reports timeout. WireGuard client logs show repeated handshake timeouts. Packet capture from client shows SYNs originating from expected private IP but server responses (SYN-ACK) are received on a different interface or not at all; many RSTs and retransmits observed. DNS queries for internal hostnames sometimes resolve to public IPs while on the docked path due to suffix/order issues.
With dock connected and VPN up, SSO and internal apps should authenticate normally regardless of Wi-Fi/Ethernet order. Network stack should prefer corporate route for traffic destined to Okta/internal services and not produce asymmetric routing.
-- windows ipconfig /all (snippet) --
Ethernet adapter Ethernet (Dock):
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . : 10.8.0.58
   Default Gateway . . . . . . . : 10.8.0.1
Wireless LAN adapter Wi-Fi:
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . : 10.9.3.112
   Default Gateway . . . . . . . : 10.9.3.1
-- route print (snippet) --
IPv4 Route Table
 0.0.0.0          0.0.0.0          10.9.3.1     10.9.3.112    25
 0.0.0.0          0.0.0.0          10.8.0.1     10.8.0.58     35
-- wireguard client log --
2026-03-10 08:41:12 [INFO] wg0: initiating handshake
2026-03-10 08:41:22 [WARN] wg0: handshake timeout, retrying
2026-03-10 08:41:32 [WARN] wg0: handshake timeout, giving up
-- browser console / network --
Request: POST https://redwood-okta.example.com/oauth2/v1/token -> net::ERR_TIMED_OUT
TLS: ClientHello sent, no ServerHello received
-- tshark pcap summary --
Client (10.8.0.58) -> Okta (34.215.12.101) SYN seq=0 win=64240
Server -> Client SYN-ACK appears with destination 10.9.3.112 (Wi-Fi IP) instead of 10.8.0.58 -> client drops packet -> retransmits -> connection times out
-- dhcp/dns observed --
Some clients reported internal.example.local resolving to public egress IP when route chosen via dock interface; investigation points to DNS suffix and interface order causing wrong resolver to be used
2026-03-09 16:10 - Initial reports from #internal-support: SSO failures concentrated on users docked at SF hotdesks. Reporter test reproduces with dock A02.
Checked WireGuard server logs: no upstream errors; saw multiple handshake attempts from same client IPs but no established session when dock connected.
Captured packets at client and observed mismatched destination IPs for responses (asymmetric path). Hypothesis: dock provides a small NAT/bridge that creates a secondary default route; Windows interface metrics prefer Wi-Fi or dock unpredictably leading to source IP selection mismatch.
Test: disabled Wi-Fi, authenticated successfully via Ethernet while docked. Re-enabled Wi-Fi, problem returned. Setting Ethernet interface metric lower than Wi-Fi (manual) made problem disappear for test machine.
Reproduced on macOS laptop: when dock created additional virtual interface (bridge 192.168.50.0/24), DNS suffix order changed and curl to internal services went to public IP; adjusting service order fixed immediately.
Checked recent hardware provisioning: new Dell TB4 docks firmware v1.3.2 deployed 2026-03-07. Vendor release notes mention 'alternate interface mode' which can surface as a bridge device on host. Suspect firmware interacts poorly with OS metric assignment.
SRE ran controlled pcap in lab: when laptop source IP differs from interface used to receive server replies, TCP handshake fails because server replies are NATed out a different public IP; Okta drops incomplete TLS sessions.
Related to INT-33109 (dns-suffix-order) - cross-referenced for DNS suffix behavior but root cause is multi-homing and source IP mismatch.
Immediate mitigation (2026-03-10): Posted dispatcher KB in #internal-support instructing affected users to either unplug dock or disable 'Ethernet (Dock)' adapter until fix applied.
Temporary fleet mitigation (2026-03-11): Endpoint team rolled out Group Policy to set interface metric precedence on Windows: Ethernet (Dock) metric forced to 15, Wi-Fi metric 25 for corporate SSID. Rollout targeted SF office first (approx. 120 devices).
macOS mitigation (2026-03-11): Pushed login script via Jamf to set network service order to prefer Ethernet when dock present; script also removes bridge service created by docks where possible.
Coordinated with vendor (Dell) to request firmware build that changes bridge behavior and to confirm TB4 firmware backport is possible. Vendor acknowledged and opened case DELL-INC-88792.
Network team added a temporary WireGuard server-side rule to accept handshakes where payloads show mixed source IPs (rate-limited) to reduce false negatives while endpoint mitigations propagate.
Manual validation: 12 test users verified fix and reported restored SSO flows. No further regressions observed after GP/Jamf policies applied.
Follow-up ticket created to automate interface metric enforcement for all corporate images (INT-928004).
Mitigated by enforcing interface metric order on Windows via GPO and network service order script for macOS. Endpoint team to bake metric changes into golden images. Dell provided firmware work item; vendor will release patch v1.3.3 addressing bridge mode. Closing this incident as 'Resolved' after 48h with no recurrence in SF office. Permanent follow-ups: INT-928004 (image changes), work with vendor DELL-INC-88792 for firmware QA and wide deployment.

Additional notes:
Kai Müller (Network, 2026-03-11): Captured PCAP during repro; concluded asymmetric routing due to duplicate default gateways and inconsistent source IP selection on return path.
payload.summary: USB-C dock triggers asymmetric routing and Okta SSO timeouts when Wi-Fi + Ethernet active

Issue summary: Several employees reported being prompted to reauthorize SSO after opening a calendar invitation (.ics) that contained an HTML redirect. Steps to reproduce: 1) Receive calendar invite with embedded URL in DESCRIPTION. 2) Clicked link from macOS Mail or Google Calendar. 3) User redirected to SSO login/reauth flow. 4) Some sessions invalidated and new sessions created. Logs: See audit log entries linked below; suspicious redirect chain observed in proxy logs.
1) Open received .ics/caldav invite in default mail/calendar app. 2) Click embedded DESCRIPTION link. 3) Observe redirect to internal SSO endpoint and reauth prompt. 4) Check /session/create and /session/invalidate audit events in proxy logs.
Calendar invite contained an HTML redirect or URL shortener that caused browser to re-request SSO cookies; potential malicious actor tricked users into initiating auth flows leading to session reuse or token replay.
03-13 09:22 - Marcus: Pulled proxy logs for urls associated with suspicious invite tokens; found same IP 35.214.10.9 hitting /sso/callback for 6 distinct users within 90s.
03-13 11:10 - Security: No evidence of privilege escalation; tokens exchanged appear to be short-lived. Session creation events show new session IDs but originating IPs match user IPs.
