payload.description:
Request: Build an automated tenant-scoped onboarding gateway that provisions a Jira project, Confluence space (templated), and Slack channels (private + public variants) when a new business tenant/team is approved. The gateway must enforce conditional retention policies on Confluence and Slack (based on data classification), and kick off an approval chain that includes Legal and Security before spaces are created for tenants classified as 'sensitive'.

Background: Product Ops and Platform receive frequent manual requests to create project spaces for new tenant teams. Compliance requires retention baseline and Legal approval for any tenant handling regulated data. The current manual process is slow and error-prone (ticket escalations, missed retention settings). This automation should reduce support load and enforce guardrails consistently.
Manual provisioning requires 2-3 support staff hours per request and leads to inconsistent retention settings and missing approver evidence. Risk of non-compliance for regulated tenants and delayed onboarding affecting sales and CSM SLAs.
Onboarding requests come via a support form → manual triage by Platform-CS → engineer creates Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channels; manual retention settings are applied if requested. Legal/Security approvals are collected as email threads and attached to tickets.
Self-serve gateway: Product Ops or solutions engineers can submit a tenant onboarding request form that triggers an automated workflow. Workflow evaluates tenant data classification, routes approval requests to Legal/Security when required, and only after approvals provisions Jira/Confluence/Slack via service accounts with correct permission templates and retention tags. An audit trail (Confluence page and ticket activity) is created automatically.
1) User fills 'Tenant Onboard' form with tenant name, owner, classification, and required templates
2) Gateway evaluates classification and applies policy rules (sensitive → require Legal & Security approval)
3) Approval tasks are created and routed to on-call Legal/Security approvers; reminders if not responded in 48h
4) Upon approval, gateway provisions Jira project (with permissions groups), Confluence space from template (with retention tags), and Slack channels via provisioning bot
5) Gateway posts a summary to #platform-onboarding and attaches approval artifacts and links to a created Jira issue for traceability
A) Gateway can provision Jira/Confluence/Slack for a new tenant using service accounts with least privilege
B) For 'sensitive' classification, approvals from Legal and Security are required and enforced by the workflow (no provisioning without both approvals)
C) Retention settings are applied to Confluence spaces and Slack channels according to classification and are visible in audit logs
D) Created Jira issue contains links to approvals, Confluence space, and Slack channel; permissions and membership follow template
E) Monitoring: failures emit alerts to #platform-ops and create an incident ticket automatically
Checked existing automation: INT-997777 contains a provisioning gateway prototype that uses GitHub Actions to call service endpoints — could be reused but lacks approval routing
Confluence templates: templates exist under OPS templates but are not parameterized for retention tags. Need template variables for data_classification and retention_period
Slack provisioning: current bot supports channel creation and invites; retention settings require Enterprise Grid API calls (audit: confirm token scopes)
Permissions: Jira project template must create groups prefixed with tenant_<short>_admin/read and add OKTA group sync mapping; ensure SCIM/Group sync is part of design
Audit trail: store approval artifacts as attachments on the resulting Jira issue and a snapshot page in Confluence; retention of approval artifacts must be immutable for 3 years for regulated tenants
Design/requirements approved in triage; next steps: author RFC linked to this ticket, assign eng owner for implementation, and schedule Security/Legal integration session. MVP plan: implement provisioning for non-sensitive tenants first (no approvals), then add approval step for sensitive tenants.
Create RFC in Confluence and link back to this ticket
Assign eng owner and add to infra backlog
Security/Legal to provide approver rotation roster and SLAs
Use existing workflow-engine integration where possible. Reuse INT-997777's provisioning adapters but replace ad-hoc scripts with idempotent API calls. Ensure service account keys are stored in KMS and rotated per policy. Add metrics: time-to-provision, approval latency, failure rate.
payload.summary: Orchestrate tenant-gated onboarding binding: auto-create Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channels with conditional retention + Legal/Security approver chain

payload.description:
Issue summary: Users requesting Temporary Support Role via internal approval flow fail to receive the role when their Okta profile has a secondaryEmail element that is set to 'hidden'. The SCIM PATCH generated by our identity-provisioner is rejected by the internal RBAC API with a 422/validation error citing unexpected attribute format. Impact: multiple engineers could not elevate to the emergency support role during a Friday afternoon oncall rotation; manual provisioning was required.
On-call engineers unable to get short-lived support role via self-serve approval; delays ~15-45 minutes per user due to manual provisioning. Affected team: Support & SRE rotations. No customer-facing outage but elevated operational risk.
1) Ensure Okta user profile has secondaryEmail element present and marked with 'visibility': 'hidden' in the profile (this can happen via certain IdP imports).
2) As a user, trigger Temporary Support Role request from /internal/approvals -> request 'support:temporary-admin' and complete manager approval flow.
3) Observe the identity-provisioner logs: it sends a SCIM PATCH to /internal-identity/provision with payload that includes secondaryEmail in the patch body.
4) RBAC API responds with 422 ValidationError: 'attribute secondaryEmail: unrecognized format' and the provisioning job fails; the user does not receive role membership.
5) Manual workaround: SRE manually adds role via admin console; job then retries but subsequent automatic retries still fail.
Expected: Temporary role should be created without the SCIM PATCH failing for hidden secondaryEmail.
2026-03-12T15:23:41Z identity-provisioner INFO sending PATCH /v2/users/7234 - payload keys: [name, emails, groups, meta]
2026-03-12T15:23:41Z identity-provisioner DEBUG patch: { 'emails': [{'value':'a.patel@example.com','type':'work','primary':true}, {'value':'a.patel+alt@example.com','type':'secondary','visibility':'hidden'}] }
2026-03-12T15:23:41Z rbac-api ERROR 422 ValidationError: 'emails.secondary.visibility' unexpected value 'hidden' for attribute 'secondaryEmail' (requestId=5f8c-9b2d)
2026-03-12T15:40:02Z support-bot INFO manual role add: admin added support:temporary-admin to user a.patel@example.com (performed by samira.chen)
Relevant trace: https://sentry.redwood.internal/issue/ID-2026-provision-5f8c
Initial hypothesis: SCIM consumer (rbac-api) expects a different structure for secondary / hidden emails; our provisioner forwards Okta's attribute verbatim.
Checked Okta SCIM mapping: secondaryEmail lands in 'emails' array with an extra 'visibility' key when Okta profile field configured as 'internal' or migrated from legacy IdP.
Reproduced locally by creating a test Okta user with secondaryEmail visibility:hidden and submitting approval flow — got same 422 from rbac-api.
Reviewed rbac-api schema: it accepts emails[] with attributes value,type,primary; unknown keys cause strict schema rejection. Previously unseen 'visibility' field triggers schema validation failure.
Workaround validated: modify provisioner to strip unknown keys from emails[] before PATCH — immediate success for role creation in test env.
Root cause: Okta idP import introduced a non-standard metadata key 'visibility' on secondaryEmail which our strict RBAC API rejects. The identity-provisioner forwards full Okta payload without sanitization.
Probability of recurrence: high for users migrated from legacy IdP or for Okta workflows that set field visibility flags.
1) Support/SRE: manually add temporary role via Admin Console for impacted oncall users (runbook page linked).
2) If frequent, use CLI admin tool: `adminctl add-role --user a.patel@example.com --role support:temporary-admin` and confirm in /internal/roles.
3) Avoid mass automated retries; disable provisioning job for the single user and rely on manual until canary sanitizer deploy completes.
A) Complete canary deploy of identity-provisioner sanitizer to prod us-east (Samira) — scheduled 2026-03-14 10:00 UTC.
B) Monitor provisioning logs and oncall escalation queue for 2h post-deploy; revert if unexpected rejections increase.
C) Productize sanitizer: add explicit schema-normalizer in identity-provisioner to drop unknown SCIM keys or map known Okta 'visibility' to internal metadata if needed (follow-up PR).
D) Compliance to confirm that dropping 'visibility' has no audit implications; if it does, add a mapping to log original value in a non-user-visible audit field.
E) Update Confluence runbook to document this class of failure and manual mitigation steps.
TBD - awaiting canary deploy results. If canary successful, will mark Resolved and merge sanitizer PR to main with small migration note.
If sanitizer is insufficient, plan B is to add a permissive schema acceptance layer in rbac-api for emails[] to ignore unknown keys rather than strict 422 on unknown attributes.
Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-12T15:50:12: Filed ticket after manual workaround; attaching logs and approval trace.
Samira Chen (Assignee) 2026-03-12T16:05:33: Looking into provisioner; initial patched workaround ready on staging. Will coordinate hotfix if confirmed on prod.
Evan Morales (SRE) 2026-03-13T09:12:08: Confirmed two additional incidents during last rotation where manual intervention was required. Please include runbook entry for manual add and rollback guidance.
Samira Chen 2026-03-13T11:23:44: Pushed quick sanitizer to staging branch identity-provisioner@sha:7f2cbd -> strips 'visibility' and other unknown keys from emails array. Running approval flow tests now.
Samira Chen 2026-03-14T07:41:09: Staging tests passed. Preparing canary deploy to prod targeting identity-provisioner instances serving approvals in us-east. Scheduling 2026-03-14 10:00 UTC with rollback window 30m.
Legal/Compliance note: We must ensure we are not discarding a field that has compliance meaning; flagged compliance@redwood for review.
payload.summary: Temporary support role provisioning blocked when Okta secondaryEmail marked 'hidden' — SCIM PATCH rejected

Issue summary:
Customer BrightHome AI reports recurring spurious threshold alerts for 'unique_client_count > 500' on their usage dashboard. Alerts show up as hourly spikes at 02:00-03:00 UTC but the raw event stream and request logs do not show corresponding traffic.

Impact:
- False P1 alerts for an enterprise customer (BrightHome AI) leading to unnecessary paging.
- Dashboard hourly rollup panels show inconsistent numbers compared to raw event explorer for the same time windows.
- Potential trust erosion in Console metrics and alerting.

Environment:
- prod/us-west (BrightHome AI org id: bh-923)
- Affected console release: web-console v1.17.4
- Aggregation service: rolling-aggregator v2.3.1 (deployed 2026-03-03)

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer and Support):
1. Open Console -> Analytics -> Usage -> Hourly view for last 48 hours (organization BrightHome AI).
2. Inspect 'unique_client_count' series and alert history for the 'High unique clients' threshold alert (threshold 500).
3. Open raw events explorer for the same hour window and run a query counting distinct client_id for the hour.
4. Observe mismatch: hourly rollup shows ~600 at 02:00 UTC while raw explorer shows ~420.

Observed behavior:
- Hourly rollup snapshots occasionally reflect an older window (e.g., show numbers that appear to be a mix of two adjacent hours) leading to inflated values.
- Alert evaluation uses the rollup feed and triggers on the inflated value.

Expected behavior:
- Hourly rollups should reflect exactly the aggregated events for the hour window and match raw queries aggregated to the same timezone/window.

Logs / snippets (redacted):
- rolling-aggregator logs (2026-03-11T02:05:12Z): "BatchWorker[hourly]: finished batch id=hb-20260311-01 duration=8.4s processed=1,024, expected=1,020"
- rolling-aggregator logs (2026-03-11T02:59:58Z): "BatchWorker[hourly]: started batch id=hb-20260311-02 seq=17 backlog=0"
- console alert-engine (2026-03-11T03:02:03Z): "Evaluation result: metric=unique_client_count value=612 threshold=500 rule=bh-high-unique-clients eval_time=2026-03-11T03:00:00Z"

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support disabled the specific alert rule for BrightHome AI and created a one-hour mute window to stop paging while we investigate.
- On-call SRE triggered a manual rerun of hourly rollup for affected hours via admin tool (admin/rollups/recompute). Manual rerun produced numbers consistent with raw events, which suggests issue is with the scheduled rollup path.

Notes:
- This ticket focuses on console-facing symptoms; underlying cause may be in rolling-aggregator scheduling or in the handoff between trace-ingest and the aggregator's windowing logic.
- Customer is sensitive to repeats; they are currently on enterprise contract with strict paging expectations.
2026-03-10T11:08:24Z - Maya Thompson (Support): 'Opened with customer after they received three false alerts this morning. They attached screenshots and a CSV export comparing raw counts to hourly rollup values.'
2026-03-10T12:03:55Z - Diego Martinez (SRE): 'Acknowledged. I will investigate rolling-aggregator logs and confirm if job runs are overlapping or if window boundaries are off.'
2026-03-10T15:22:10Z - Diego Martinez (SRE): 'Found a cluster of aggregator logs where batch start times overlap by up to 40s under high ingest. Suspecting a race in lock acquisition in aggregator-v2.3.1. Spun up replication locally for repro.'
2026-03-11T02:45:01Z - Elena Park (Customer): 'We muted the alert but would like permanent fix. Our uptime is impacted by paging fatigue.'
2026-03-11T04:10:32Z - Diego Martinez (SRE): 'Applied manual recompute for hours 01:00-04:00 UTC for the org (admin job id: recompute-bh-923-20260311). Recomputed metrics align with raw events. Continuing root cause analysis.'
2026-03-12T09:30:15Z - Priya Singh (Eng): 'Reproduced on staging under synthetic burst. Aggregator lock TTL race causes a small percentage of batches to pick up overlapping event ranges; write path de-duplicates partially but can produce merged windows. Preparing a patch to extend lock TTL and add explicit window watermarking.'
Hypotheses considered:
1) Aggregator job overlap due to insufficient locking -> observed overlapping starts in logs.
2) Delayed ingestion leading to late-arriving events being attributed to earlier window -> raw event timestamps show steady arrival, less likely.
3) Alert-engine misreading timezone offset -> alert evals consistently use UTC; not likely.

Actions taken:
- Pulled aggregator logs (rolling-aggregator v2.3.1) for 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-11 and identified overlapping batch start timestamps.
- Ran staging repro with synthetic burst (100k events/min) and replicated the overlap; root cause narrows to lock acquisition TTL expiry under GC pauses.
- Manual recompute admin job fixed numbers for customer windows.
- Created engineering PR to add stronger coordination (use Redis-based leader election with renewals) and to add an 'aggregation-watermark' field to rollup outputs to make futuresafe comparisons.

Next steps:
- Merge aggregator coordination patch and deploy to canary ring (target 2026-03-14).
- Add a one-time migration job to recompute any hourly windows processed by overlapping batches in the last 7 days for affected orgs.
- Add an alert for 'aggregation overlap detected' metric to catch regressions earlier.
Workaround applied: alert muted and manual recompute run. Engineering patch in progress to fix lock coordination and add aggregation watermark. Canary deploy scheduled; follow-up recompute migration planned if canary confirms fix.
ENG: merge and deploy aggregator coordination patch to canary
SRE: run recompute-migration for last 7 days for affected orgs after canary pass
DX: notify BrightHome AI CSM of timeline and remediation plan

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple corporate MacBook units restored with Apple Configurator (AC2) after an internal firmware prerelease reflash are booting into recoveryOS with no network interfaces available. Devices never reach Setup Assistant and therefore fail DEP/MDM (Intune) enrollment.

Impact: Affected machines cannot be provided to users; onboarding blocked for 8 devices so far (carrier build and standard retail units). Blocking P1 for provisioning queue in US-West.

Environment: macOS 13.6.8 (pre-release firmware applied via AC2), Apple Configurator 2.20.0, corporate DEP (Automated Device Enrollment) + Intune profile push. USB-C Apple Configurator cable workflow from macOS host (Big Sur server host).

Observed behavior: After AC2 restore and firmware reflash, machine boots to a recoveryOS prompt showing Utilities, but ifconfig and networksetup show no active Ethernet or Wi‑Fi hardware. System Information shows PCIe controller present but with no driver; IORegistry entries for airport and en0 are absent. Device never contacts Apple DEP servers.

Expected behavior: Post-restore machines should reach Setup Assistant, enumerate network interfaces, and contact DEP for automated enrollment.

Initial hypothesis: Pre-release firmware image applied by AC2 changed SEP/bridge configuration causing I/O providers for Wi‑Fi/Thunderbolt to not instantiate in recoveryOS. Alternative: AC2 restore workflow using our provisioning host is accidentally applying an OEM factory image (with non-public kext signing) instead of the standard corporate image.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced on two machines (MBP-14,3 and MBA-10,1) using the same AC2 host image.
- When running 'system_profiler SPNetworkDataType' from recovery terminal, network section is empty.
- Checking /Volumes/Recovery/System/Library/Extensions on the mounted recovery image shows missing Apple80211 kext references.
- USB cable logs from host indicate a firmware reflashing step completed with exit 0, but config manifest shows firmware version suffix '-rc1' (we expected '-prod').
- Cross-checked with vendor firmware manifest: vendor accidentally signed an internal RC when tagging the release; AC2 picks image by manifest hash.

Temporary workaround: Pause AC2 restore workflows on the provisioning host; use device-to-device enrollment (user performs setup and enrolls manually) where acceptable. For urgent hires, use previously imaged stock units that were not reflashed.

Proposed fix: Update provisioning host manifest to pin to the confirmed production firmware hash; coordinate with firmware vendor to revoke RC image tag. Add a validation step to AC2 workflow to reject images with '-rc' in version string.

Next steps / action items:
- [Evan Ross] Hold AC2 workflow and tag host image as quarantined (completed 2026-03-12).
- [Aisha Patel] Open vendor escalation with firmware team and request rollback of RC artifact (ticket opened 2026-03-12).
- [OS Team] Add a preflight check to imaging script to validate kext presence in the recovery image.
- [IT Ops] Identify stock pool unaffected by AC2 reflashes for immediate deployments.

Resolution notes: Work in progress — vendor confirmed RC tag was published in error and will publish corrected manifest 2026-03-15. We will resume automated restores after host manifest is updated and preflight validation is added.
1) Connect Mac to provisioning Mac with Apple Configurator using corporate USB-C cable
2) Select Restore and apply firmware image chosen by provisioning host manifest
3) Wait for AC2 workflow to complete and device to reboot
4) Observe device booting into recoveryOS with no network interfaces and no Setup Assistant
5) From recovery terminal, run 'ifconfig' and 'system_profiler SPNetworkDataType' to confirm absence of network hardware
AC2_host: restore_step=firmware_apply exit_code=0 manifest_version=2026-03-11-rc1
Recovery terminal: ifconfig -> no en0 or bridge devices listed
system_profiler: SPNetworkDataType -> <empty>
Imaging host: AC2 log excerpt -> applied_firmware_hash=sha256:abcd1234ef... (tagged -rc1)

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 08:44 SRE oncall (Jorge Martinez): Added interim check in imaging script to block firmware versions containing '-rc' and alert. Deployed to staging hosts.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A small subset of internal users are receiving 403 when opening the Feature-Flag Console (console.redwood.internal). The requests authenticate successfully via Okta SSO, but the console denies RBAC role binding due to an unexpected group claim format.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers across a couple of teams cannot view or modify feature flags.
- Blocks on-call debugging and staged rollouts for two services (payments, telemetry).
- Not customer-facing but affects internal release velocity and incident response.

Observed behavior:
- User completes Okta SSO and is redirected to console, then immediately sees a 403 page with "insufficient permissions" message.
- Identity payload in logs shows groups claim present, but group strings do not match RBAC matcher.

Expected behavior:
- Okta groups map to internal RBAC roles and users with the matching groups have access to the Feature-Flag Console.

Notes: This ticket covers the support investigation; follow-up work (config rollouts) will be tracked separately.
1) Use an affected user account (example: aisha.k@redwood.test)
2) Navigate to https://console.redwood.internal/flags
3) Click Sign in with Okta and complete MFA
4) Observe redirect to 403 page instead of dashboard

Repro on-off: reproducible for affected users and their sessions; other users unaffected.
Auth proxy logs (excerpt):
- RequestId: rq-93a2f
- SSO assertion validated, issuer=accounts.okta.com/xx
- groups claim: ["eng-team_42", "release-managers-2026"]
- RBAC lookup: attempted match against roleBindings: ["eng-team-42", "release-managers"]
- Result: no exact match -> deny -> 403

Console debug log: roleBinding resolution failed: claim string mismatch (underscore vs hyphen).
Hypothesis: A recent Okta attribute transform rolled out a prefixed format for group names (underscore insertion) for certain synced groups. RBAC matcher expects hyphenated names; therefore roleBindings don't match.

What we checked:
- Okta SCIM sync jobs ran at 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC; group metadata changed for two groups (team id appended with underscore in 'displayName').
- No recent RBAC config changes on the console side in the last 30 days.
- Identity proxy (auth-proxy) normalizes group names only in one code path; discrepancy occurs when claims come from SAML vs OIDC, and the new transform applies only to SAML assertions.

Telemetry: Started seeing first 403 errors for feature-flag console at ~2026-03-09 03:20 UTC correlated with SCIM sync window.

Quick test: Rewrote a binding in dev to match underscore variant and login succeeded for the test user. This confirms mapping mismatch.

Potential root cause: Okta attribute transform for displayName added an underscore-delimited suffix for certain migrated groups. RBAC matching uses exact string equality instead of canonical normalization.

Related risk: If we apply a broad normalization change to RBAC, it could affect many bindings; need targeted fix.

Additional notes:
- Add temporary roleBindings matching the underscore-suffixed group names for the impacted roles.
- Alternatively, affected users can be added to a cross-team role (release-ops) that has flag access until fix is deployed.
In progress: temporary roleBindings approved and queued for deployment. Identity team scheduled Okta transform rollback for non-migrated tenants and provided list of affected groups. Dev work to normalize RBAC matching has been scoped and PR created. Final resolution will be recorded after prod rollout and verification.
payload.summary: Feature-Flag Console denies access after Okta group attribute format change (role scope mismatch)

Issue summary: Scheduled Jenkins pipelines triggered by the internal service account 'ci-bot@redwood' are failing intermittently. Jobs start, then immediately fail with 401 from the token refresh endpoint, causing downstream deploy steps to abort. Impact: Several release pipelines and nightly jobs are blocked for multiple teams.
Multiple teams unable to run Jenkins release and nightly pipelines. Automated canary promotions are failing; manual intervention required for builds created between 2026-03-10 01:15 UTC and ongoing.
1) Configure Jenkins job to use 'ci-bot@redwood' service account via Okta OAuth token exchange.
2) Trigger job via SCM webhook or scheduled timer.
3) Observe job obtain access token then fail on refresh call approximately 15 minutes after start with 401 unauthorized.
4) Reproduced on multiple Jenkins masters in us-west cluster and on a standalone curl against the token refresh endpoint using stored refresh_token.
5) Temporary workaround: generate a long-lived API key for the job and use that instead of OAuth refresh flow (manual change).
2026-03-10T01:17:12Z ERROR token-refresh-service 401 RefreshTokenInvalid: refresh token rejected for client_id=jenkins-internal
2026-03-10T01:17:13Z WARN jenkins.pipeline Step 'deploy' aborted due to auth failure (401)
Okta audit: 2026-03-10T01:16:58Z EVENT policy.evaluation Evaluated user ci-bot@redwood: matched policy 'Session Lifetime > 10m' applied to group 'all-Employees'
Initial hypothesis: Jenkins client misconfigured with wrong client_secret or token endpoint. Rejected after cross-checking client config and successful initial token issuance.
Correlated Okta audit logs showing policy evaluation exactly when refresh tokens were rejected. The policy 'Session Lifetime > 10m' was edited on 2026-03-09 and unintentionally included attribute selector matching service-account group due to a wildcard in rule scope.
Token refresh flow: access_token issued successfully, refresh fails when Okta policy returns 'invalid_session' for refresh_token because service account considered a human session with too-short lifetime.
Temporary mitigation by token service permit rule showed pipelines succeeded, confirming policy mismatch as root cause.
Related config: Jenkins OIDC client uses refresh_token rotation; rotation tokens are short-lived if session lifetime policy applies. Service accounts must be excluded from that policy.
Repro steps executed in staging using a cloned service account to test policy change impact before applying to production.
No evidence of credential compromise; this was a policy scoping error from Identity team's recent change.

Permanent fix: Identity team updated the Okta session lifetime policy to exclude OU 'service-accounts' and replaced the overly-broad group selector with explicit include/exclude rules. Token service and Jenkins clients were rolled to accept rotated refresh tokens under the corrected policy. Post-deploy verification: 10+ scheduled jobs executed between 2026-03-12 02:00-04:00 UTC successfully. Next steps: add automated policy unit tests, create a runbook for service-account policy changes, and schedule an audit of Okta policies to catch similar regressions.
Ava Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed jobs failing in the morning cycle. Reproducible on two different Jenkins masters. Captured token logs and Okta audit event IDs.
Diego Ramos (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Triage started. Obtained refresh_token artifacts and validated 401 responses. Escalating to Identity team for Okta policy review.
Maya Chen (Identity) 2026-03-11: Found that a recent session-lifetime policy change inadvertently targeted 'all-Employees' and included service accounts. Investigating an exclude-list for non-human accounts.
On-call Infra 2026-03-11: Applied temporary permit rule in token service to allow existing refresh tokens to be accepted for 24h while fix planned.
Diego Ramos 2026-03-12: Patch deployed to token service to ignore short-session policy for members of OU 'service-accounts'. Monitoring pipeline runs.
Release Engineer 2026-03-12: Verified nightly jobs completed successfully at 02:00 UTC without manual key swap. Recommend formal policy change and follow-up audit.

Issue summary: A recent change to the support macro templating engine unintentionally stripped the SLA routing tags that downstream routing rules rely on. Impact: automated escalation and SLA metering for internal queues is misattributed, causing false P0/P1 alerts to paging and corrupting the daily and monthly SLA reports for the support org. Environment: production support-tooling cluster (us-east) and the reporting pipeline ingesting alerting events.

Observed impact:
- On 2026-03-12 07:10 UTC, multiple internal pages were created for support queues that should have been routed to the Dedicated SRE rotation. Those pages were instead routed to the general #support-ops rota.
- Upstream analytics shows a ~42% drop in routed SLA-tagged events between 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC and 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC.
- The nightly SLA aggregation job produced a monthly report with missing SLA rows for four internal queues.

Steps to reproduce (attempted):
1) Create a support ticket via the internal UI using template 'DEDICATED-ESCALATE-v2' in prod/us-east.
2) Observe the generated ticket payload in the support-tooling queue (support-events topic).
3) Confirm whether the sla_tag and routing_policy fields are present in the payload.

Expected behavior: macro templates preserve required metadata fields (sla_tag, routing_policy, customer_tier) in generated payloads.
Actual behavior: sla_tag and routing_policy are empty strings in 100% of reproduced tickets when template rendering uses the new template engine version.

Immediate mitigation applied: we rolled back the template-engine to v1.17 at 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC which restored normal routing for newly created tickets. Historical events from 2026-03-11 21:00 UTC to 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC still require remediation in the reporting ingestion layer.

Business impact: internal paging fatigue due to duplicate/false pages, inaccurate SLA reporting for leadership, and potential missed escalations for Dedicated and Private customer queues. This is an internal-support incident but could affect SLA dashboards used by GTM and CSM teams.

Issue summary: We need to onboard a batch of 18 employees transferred from AcmeAI (acquisition close on 2026-03-01). The group will be split into two waves (12 then 6) over the next three weeks to avoid bottlenecks.

Impact: These are product and infra engineers that require access to internal repos, dedicated service accounts for migration work, VPN/VPC access, and temporary elevated privileges to perform a one-time migration of model checkpoints and namespace resources. Failure to stage access will block the migration work and delay integration milestones.

Requirements: 1) Create Okta users with SCIM sync and assign to two pre-created groups (acq-wave-1, acq-wave-2). 2) Provision company laptops for 12 immediate hires from the shared acquisition asset pool and ship to listed home addresses. 3) Issue temporary sudo and K8s cluster edit role for a 90-day window for 8 engineers (knowledge transfer), with monthly review reminders. 4) Migrate/transfer ownership of 3 service accounts and rotate KMS access keys after transfer. 5) Tag assets, record serials in Asset Management, and attach custodian notes.

Constraints: VPN onboarding requires new onboarding subnet approval from Networking (ticket NET-5463 referenced in comments). Summary: Several engineers reported being unable to complete SSO into Redwood Console from company-managed macOS devices. The SSO flow stalls at device-trust / platform authenticator step showing a generic 'Unable to verify device' message. Impact: blocked access to Console for ~14 employees in us-east; affects internal ops and oncall rotations.
1) On a company-managed macOS (Ventura+), open Console URL behind SSO
2) Primary Okta SSO redirect completes, prompted for device verification (Touch ID/Face ID dialog appears)
3) After approving on-device prompt, browser shows 'Device verification failed' and login does not complete
4) Attempting to use fallback OTP returns success but device trust remains unverified for future logins
User-facing: 'Device verification failed (invalid_assertion)'.
Browser console (Chrome): WebAuthn: "signature verification failed" from relying party check
Okta system log (event id okta-logs-20260312-07): 'webauthn.assertion.verify.failed - signature verification error'
Device MDM (munki/MDM) reports: 'webauthn-credential-present: true, last_seen: 2026-03-12T07:42:10Z'
Initial hypothesis: recent change in IdP signing keys or JWK cache TTL leading to signature verification mismatch.
Performed repro with test account: observed Okta returns assertion validation error while macOS returns successful user presence. This suggests validation failure on server side.
Checked Okta change log: automated key rotation completed at 2026-03-12T06:50Z (internal note: rotation job id 'rot-20260312-01').
Our device-trust service caches Okta JWKs for 24h; cache refresh job did not pick up new key due to a transient 502 from Okta's jwks endpoint during rotation window.
Private control plane (redwood-private-auth) was using cached JWK set containing old attestation key which no longer verifies assertions signed with the rotated key.
Re-enrolling device (clearing platform credential) produces a new credential signed with current key; newly enrolled credentials validate successfully.
Affected population appears to be devices that had last re-enrolled before 2026-03-12 06:50Z and have not re-authenticated since rotation.
Number of affected users: ~14 engineers (reported via #internal-support and survey)
Services impacted: Redwood Console admin flows, role escalations, oncall runbook access for affected users
Duration: began ~2026-03-12T07:00Z, continuing until workaround applied
Short term: Use alternate OTP MFA (email/SMS) or SSO fallback to finish login and then re-enroll device from Console > Security > Device Trust.
Support must trigger remote re-enrollment for users who cannot reach Console by creating a temporary session via SRE support token (documented in Confluence runbook 'device-trust-ops').
Manual fix on server: flush device-trust JWK cache to force fetch of rotated keys (performed as temporary mitigation).
1) Roll out immediate cache flush to all control plane replicas and verify JWK fetch success (done 2026-03-12T09:15Z on prod-us-east).
2) Add retry/backoff when fetching jwks to avoid permanent stale cache if endpoint returns transient 5xx.
3) Lower cache TTL from 24h to 5m for JWKs and implement a health check alert if jwks.fetch fails > 3 times in 10m.
4) Update post-rotation runbook to include coordinated cache flush across private/hosted control planes and MDM notifications for re-enrollment window.
5) Outreach: notify internal Slack #internal-support and affected employees with steps to re-enroll and temporary OTP fallback.
6) Follow-up ticket to audit other services that cache IdP jwks (linked issue INT-20671).
Temporary mitigation: Flushed JWK cache on all prod-us-east replicas (2026-03-12T09:15Z) and confirmed that subsequent assertions validate. Short-term communication sent to affected users with re-enrollment steps. Long-term fix: config and runbook changes scheduled (PR opened).
Aisha Patel (reporter) - 2026-03-12T07:18Z: Posted initial reports from Slack channel #internal-support. Included screenshots and user agent strings.
Tom Nguyen (assignee) - 2026-03-12T07:45Z: Confirmed reproducer and started capturing Okta and identity-service logs. Suspect JWK rotation race.
Lena Schmidt (IDP team) - 2026-03-12T08:30Z: Verified automated rotation ran and Okta jwks endpoint returned 502 for ~4 minutes around rotation. Working with infra to confirm endpoint stability.
Priya Menon (SRE) - 2026-03-12T09:20Z: Performed cache flush and validated successful login for repro device. Rolling to rest of replicas now.
Tom Nguyen - 2026-03-12T12:05Z: Following up with runbook PR and instrumentation changes; marking as In Progress.

payload.description:
Issue summary: After standard depot-imaging using the 2026.03 corporate image, a subset of laptops fail to establish our corporate certificate-based VPN (CertVPN) post-provisioning. Impact: Affected devices cannot access internal services; users report "no valid certificate" errors in the VPN client and helpdesk sees enrollment loops. Environment: Corporate imaging pipeline (SCCM/ConfigMgr task sequence), corp PKI (HashiCorp Vault-issued machine certs), Windows 11 22H2-based image, post-imaging Company MDM (Intune) enrollment.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Pick a device (Dell 7440 or Lenovo X1) out of depot stock.
2) Boot PXE and run depot image 2026.03 via SCCM TS.
3) Device completes imaging, reboots to OOBE, auto-enrolls in Intune.
4) Run corporate baseline scripts including network drivers and Cisco AnyConnect (CertVPN) config.
5) Attempt CertVPN connection.

Observed behavior: VPN client reports "Certificate not found / authentication failed". Device local cert store shows machine cert present, but VPN logs indicate certificate selection failed and the system network interface used for the initial machine cert request is not the expected physical NIC but a virtual NIC created by the docking/Thunderbolt controller. Expected behavior: Machine certificate selection succeeds and VPN establishes automatically after network is available.

Additional notes: Issue is intermittent (~6-8% of imaged units) and correlates with devices docked during depot imaging or with dual NICs present. Not seen when devices are imaged unattached to docks. No prior reports before the 2026.03 image rollout.
Attached excerpts:
- VPN client log (AnyConnect): "Cert selection failed: no matching cert on interface {vEthernet0}" timestamp 2026-03-13T10:22:14Z
- System event log: Schannel warnings during TLS handshake to authproxy: 0x8009030e
- Imaging task sequence log: network drivers applied: 2026-03-13T09:58:02Z (netwtw10 v22.60)
- Intune enrollment debug: TPM attestation succeeded; machine cert requested from PKI endpoint, cert issued but final step reported 'scope mismatch' in orchestration logs.
Initial triage by SRE: reproduced on a lab Dell docked to TB4 dock and on Lenovo with an external USB-C NIC. Observed interface list order differs: virtual adapter enumerated before physical Ethernet, which causes machine cert client to bind to wrong interface context during the certificate selection callback. Verified TLS handshake from wrong source IP. Checked SCCM TS: network driver installation order changed in 2026.03 image (new net driver package installs 'virtual switch' driver earlier). Intune MDM profile didn't include interface-scoped certificate selector. Ticket escalated to imaging and network driver owners.
Driver installation order in 2026.03 causes a virtual NIC (or dock vNIC) to enumerate before the physical adapter, which leads to cert enrollment and VPN client picking the wrong interface context, failing client-side policy that expects the cert on physical NIC IP. This only manifests when dock/hub creates virtual NICs or when multiple NICs present during the initial cert bind.
- Re-imaged a affected unit without dock attached: CertVPN worked. - Re-imaged with dock attached reproduces failure. - Swapped driver package order in a local task sequence (deferred virtual switch install to after Intune enrollment) — reproducer passes. - Collected kernel-mode net adapter enumeration timestamps. - Opened a support call with third-party VPN vendor (Cisco AnyConnect) to review cert selection logic.
Device/driver enumeration order change in the 2026.03 image caused virtual/dock-created adapters to appear before primary NIC during early boot/enrollment, leading to incorrect interface binding in our cert selection logic and the VPN client.
Temporary process for depot: ensure devices are imaged off-dock. For already provisioned devices, instruct users to disconnect docks/hubs, reboot, and re-run the 'Corporate Network Repair' script (Intune remediation package) which reinstalls network drivers in the fallback order and forces rebind of machine cert. Documented in runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IT/Imaging+Workarounds
Imaging team to reorder net driver packages in the next 2026.03.1 build (virtual switch drivers deferred). Rolling patch scheduled for 2026-03-16 to update SCCM task sequence. VPN vendor provided a client-side config knob to prefer interface by name; applied as emergency policy for impacted fleet via Intune until patched. Follow-up: update Intune device configuration to avoid interface-scoped cert assumptions.
Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-13: Initial ticket created after Service Desk reported 12 devices failing post-imaging this morning.
Miguel Santos (Assignee) 2026-03-13: Confirmed logs attached. Reproduced locally with docked Dell. Marking as P1 and escalating to Imaging + Network driver owners.
Imaging Engineer - Priya Rao 2026-03-13: Investigating change set - discovered net package reorder in 2026.03. Adding to 2026.03.1 fix.
Network Eng - Tomas Eriksson 2026-03-13: Verified interface enumeration timestamps; agrees with root cause. Will coordinate driver reorder test.
SRE - Chen Li 2026-03-14: Deployed Intune emergency remediation to pinned subset; verified VPN connects for previously failing unit after remediation.
- Imaging team to build 2026.03.1 with driver order fix and run validation matrix including docked scenarios (owner: Priya Rao) - Network team to add adapter-preference override in corp VPN policy as a config transient (owner: Tomas) - Update Intune device config to avoid interface-scoped cert selection (owner: Security/Endpoint) - Communicate depot imaging stop-gap: no docking during imaging until 2026-03-16 patch.
Run fleet query to enumerate devices imaged with 2026.03 and report failures (owner: SRE)
Add docking scenarios to CI imaging matrix
Audit other task sequence package ordering for similar enumeration risks
payload.summary: Network interface ordering change triggers certificate-based VPN failure after imaging

Issue summary:
Provision a standardized ephemeral sandbox environment for ML infra experiments that ties together: templated Jira project(s), Confluence blueprint, ephemeral Slack channels, and an approval/TTL Slack bot that enforces RBAC and automated cleanup.

Impact:
Currently each pod creates ad-hoc sandboxes with inconsistent RBAC, no TTL, and no audit trail. This leads to stale resources, elevated blast radius from experiment runs, and repeated manual Jira/Confluence provisioning requests to internal-support.

Request / Requirements:
- A Jira project template for ephemeral experiment workstreams with predefined issue types, labels, and a lifecycle transition (Request -> Active -> Expiring -> Archived).
- A Confluence space blueprint with a short-form experiment template (hypothesis, datasets, cost estimate, rollback plan) and automated page metadata for owner and TTL.
- A Slack automation (bot) that:
  * Handles requests via slash command (/sandbox-request) and initiates an approval workflow.
  * Provisions an ephemeral Slack channel name pattern (#exp-<team>-<id>), invites approved members, and annotates channel topic with TTL and experiment owner.
  * Enforces RBAC by syncing with a designated GitHub team or SCIM group for access control on Jira/Confluence pages.
  * Posts TTL reminders and triggers automated archive/cleanup jobs at TTL expiration.
- Audit logging hooks to a central Confluence page and to SRE logging (Datadog/ELK) for retention of actions (create/approve/archive).
- Admin UI or runbook for support to override TTL and perform emergency extension or teardown.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pod leads can self-serve creation via /sandbox-request and receive an approval response within 15 minutes in the happy path.
- Created sandbox includes a Jira project (templated), Confluence page (blueprint), and Slack channel with correct members, TTL metadata, and audit entry.
- TTL enforcement runs automatically and archives channels/pages/issues; support can extend TTL via documented workflow.
- RBAC maps to existing org groups and prevents cross-pod access unless explicitly granted.

Priority justification:
This reduces repeated manual requests to internal-support, lowers risk of stale credentials/data exposure from long-lived experiment sandboxes, and standardizes onboarding for ML experiments across pods.

Additional notes:
Checked existing ephemeral workspace automation (INT-88512) — overlapping goals but that ticket is focused on generic ephemeral workspaces. This request needs ML-specific templates and RBAC mapping.
Reviewed Slack API rate limits; approval workflow must batch requests to avoid throttling during mass onboarding events.
Verified Confluence blueprint creation via REST API is supported by our instance, but will need an app credential and page template JSON to be stored in platform-infra repo.
Datadog audit event schema: will include event.type = sandbox.create|sandbox.approve|sandbox.archive, correlate with jira.issue.key.
Potential blockers: SCIM sync delay for new members; need fallback where approval can be emailed to reviewers if SCIM not reflected within 10 minutes.
Until automation is available, support can provision sandbox manually using the manual provisioning runbook: create Jira project from template 'EPHEMERAL-EXPERIMENT', create Confluence page from Experiment Template, create Slack channel and add members. Documented in Confluence runbook linked above.
Slash command implemented and tested in staging
Jira project template and transition workflow created
Confluence blueprint deployed and webhook wired
Slack bot approval flow functional and rate-limited
Audit logs appear in Datadog on create/approve/archive
Support runbook published and tested
payload.summary: Provision ephemeral experiment sandboxes with RBAC, approval bot, and lifecycle automation for ML infra

Impact:
- Ongoing customer-reported increased end-to-end tail latency for customer workloads that span regions.
- Cannot complete root-cause analysis because the network team lacks read access to the peer account's flow logs and the GCP project that hosts the inter-region VPN.

Environment:
- Affected AWS account: aws-prod-main (us-east-1)
- Peer AWS account: aws-prod-shared (eu-west-1)
- Affected GCP project: redwood-prod-networking (europe-west1)

Requested access summary:
- A temporary, timebound role usable via AssumeRole from aws-prod-main into aws-prod-shared and a temporary service account key or workload identity binding for redwood-prod-networking.
- Permissions must be scoped to read-only network telemetry and storage buckets used for flow ingest. No compute modification privileges.

Duration and constraints:
- Requested window: 4 hours on 2026-03-11 09:00-13:00 UTC (one-time).

Environment: prod / us-east (hosted Redwood runtime).

Requested window: 2026-02-01 through 2026-02-18 (inclusive).

Requested fields: timestamp, request_id, customer_id (hashed), model_version, token_count, latency_ms, status_code, response_hash. payload.description:
Issue summary:
Ephemeral CI runners are failing to mount their encrypted home/workspace after the scheduled workspace-encryption key rollover completed on 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC. Affected jobs are predominantly release pipeline steps that rely on a persistent ephemeral workspace (artifact signing and packaging).

Impact:
- ~40% of release pipeline jobs in the last 2 hours failing on runner startup with a 500-like mount error.
- Two release candidates blocked; production deployments delayed.
- Failures are transient per-runner (newly provisioned runners after a manual remediation sometimes succeed).

Environment:
- Prod ephemeral-runner fleet in us-east-1.
- Runners configured to mount encrypted EBS volumes using the workspace-kms-key alias (recently rotated to new key id).
- KMS provider: HSM-backed KMS (customer-managed key in AWS) with automatic rewrap flow.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Start a release pipeline job that provisions an ephemeral runner pod.
2. Runner init script attempts to attach and mount encrypted workspace volume.
3. init fails with mount error referencing invalid/unencryptable volume header.
4. Runner enters RUNNER_ERROR state; orchestration attempts to reprovision which sometimes succeeds if provisioning hits a different host.

Observed behavior / logs (representative excerpts):
- system logs on runner host: "block device attach succeeded but crypto_setup failed: key not available"
- runner-agent logs: "workspace-mounter: mount exited 32 (ENOMSG) after cryptsetup open --type luks /dev/xvdh workspace: Command failed: exit code 32; cryptsetup: keyslot 0 is not authenticated"
- k8s events: Pod pull/launch OK, then CrashLoopBackOff on init container that does mount.

Expected behavior:
Runners should be able to use the rewrapped volumes with the new KMS key transparently; mounts should succeed without human intervention.

Hypothesis and preliminary findings:
- The key rollover triggered a rewrap operation for existing EBS volumes, but some volume metadata still references the old key-id in LUKS header keyslot metadata.
- Workers that were reprovisioned after the KMS policy fully propagated succeed because their instances request fresh rewrap at attach time and KMS returns the new wrapping.
- Some hypervisor hosts have cached a stale CMK ARN or IAM temporary role token that prevents rewrap/unseal on attach. This aligns with host-level syslog entries showing KMS access denied during rewrap attempts (403).
- We observed a small window where the key alias mapped to a new key-id but the cross-account role used by the runner attach flow had not been updated to include the new key's grant; subsequent attach attempts are allowed.

Mitigation applied so far:
- Manual remediation: restart of affected runner nodes forces a fresh attach flow; ~60% of reprovisioned runners recover after host restart.
- Temporarily paused non-critical release pipelines and notified release engineering.
- Escalated to infra team to validate KMS grants and IAM role propagation.

Immediate next steps / action items:
1. Infra to validate KMS key policy and ensure new key-id has same grants as old key (assigned to runner-attach-role and instance profile) by 2026-03-13 09:00 UTC.
2. SRE to roll a targeted restart of 15% of runner nodes per availability zone to clear cached credentials and test rewrap behavior.
3. Release Eng to coordinate with release owners to requeue blocked release jobs after a successful pilot restart.
4. Add an automated check in the rotation runbook to verify LUKS header keyslot compatibility and KMS grants before cutover.

Longer term follow-ups (post-incident):
- Update ephemeral-runner provisioning to explicitly call rewrap/unseal flow with the alias rather than relying on implicit attach semantics.
- Add observability: metric for "workspace-mount-failures-by-key-id" and dashboard alarm.
- Update rotation runbook to include a staged host cache invalidation and IAM grant propagation verification.

Resolution criteria:
- All affected release jobs can run to completion without manual host restarts.
- Root cause identified and runbook updated.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 05:37 UTC — Infra (channel #infra): Found KMS 'AccessDenied' audit entries tied to the runner-attach-role ARN between 03:02–03:20 UTC. It looks like grants weren't duplicated to the new key until 03:18 UTC. We'll add the grant now and follow up.
2026-03-12 06:04 UTC — SRE (channel #sre): Kicked a controlled restart of 5 runner hosts in us-east-1a. 4/5 recovered and mounted workspaces successfully; one host still shows cryptsetup keyslot auth failures. Collecting more logs.
2026-03-13 09:05 UTC — Infra: Confirmed key grants duplicated. Recommend scripted host cache invalidation + restart. Will coordinate with SRE for rollout today.

Issue summary: Customer reported a rapid increase in 5xx responses on streaming chat endpoints beginning 2026-03-13 10:05 UTC. The elevation coincided with a platform-wide keepalive and backpressure config sweep that rolled out a shorter keepalive deadline and more aggressive priority fallback thresholds. Impact: Multiple short-lived streaming sessions (~1-3s) observed reconnect loops that triggered apigw 502/503s and upstream runtime connection resets for the customer's tenant. Customer-visible symptoms: aborted streams, repeated client reconnects, and elevated error-rate metrics on their integration. Environment: prod-us-west, dedicated tenant for NimbleDocs with reserved capacity.
1) Initiate large number (~1000/min) of short streaming sessions to POST /v1/chat/stream with small payloads and immediate client disconnects
2) Observe apigw 502/503 counts and runtime connection resets in the same minute window
3) Reproduce after toggling keepalive window to 15s and enabling aggressive priority fallback policy
4) Verify increased retry attempts from client-side leading to accept-queue pressure
2026-03-13T10:07:12Z apigw[edge-12] WARN conn_reset upstream=runtime-8 status=502 tenant=nimbledocs request_id=abc123
2026-03-13T10:07:14Z runtime[rt-8] ERROR grpc: connection closed by peer during active-stream tenant=nimbledocs threadpool=exhausted
2026-03-13T10:07:14Z ingress-prioritizer[prio] INFO fallback invoked for tenant=nimbledocs due_to=keepalive_deadline short_sessions=high
2026-03-13T10:08:01Z apigw[edge-12] INFO accept_queue_length=412 -> throttle_actions=reject rate=5xx
2026-03-13T10:20 Support - Aisha Patel: Customer reported 5xx spike at ~10:05 UTC; initial hypothesis is the keepalive change + priority fallback causing accept-queue churn. Asked for tenant logs and sample request IDs.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13T11:02 Customer - NimbleDocs Support: Confirmed we saw repeated reconnects from our client SDK. We did not change our client code; spike started after Redwood announced config sweep.
2026-03-13T12:10 Engineering - Ethan Cole: Temporarily rolled back aggressive keepalive deadline in us-west to previous baseline (30s). Deployed an emergency increase to runtime gRPC threadpool min (x3). Monitoring shows 5xx rate trending down but still above baseline for some customers.
2026-03-13T13:45 Support - Aisha Patel: Notified customer of temporary rollback and asked for validation. Customer confirmed partial relief: streams succeed more often but intermittent blips remain during peak ingress bursts.
Metric correlation: Timing aligns precisely with keepalive/backpressure policy sweep (change-id cfg-2026-0313-keepalive).
Accept-queue snapshots show a sawtooth pattern where short sessions create accept spikes, triggering priority fallback which closes long-lived keepalives and forces re-establish; this created a retry storm on tenants with many ephemeral streams.
Runtime observation: gRPC worker threads drop below expected min briefly during churn, causing connection resets (observed in rt-8 and rt-12). Hypothesis: runtime threadpool resizing + aggressive keepalive caused transient scheduling holes and GRPC library hit a path that closed sockets with ECONNRESET.
Customer behavior: NimbleDocs client SDK aggressively retries immediate reconnects on stream abort (backoff disabled for short sessions), amplifying the issue.
Cross refs: Linked to infra PR that applied prioritizer config (github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/587).
Hotfix applied: 1) Reverted keepalive deadline to 30s for us-west and disabled the aggressive fallback threshold while root cause is validated. 2) Increased runtime gRPC worker pool minimum and added a short stabilization window during config sweeps to prevent immediate threadpool shrink. 3) Deployed tenant-level guardrails: detect short-session reconnect storms and apply soft rate-limits per tenant to avoid accept-queue amplification. Customer workaround: NimbleDocs enabled client-side exponential backoff which reduced immediate retries. Follow-ups: engineering to add a canary gating step for keepalive/backpressure changes, add automated acceptance test that simulates high short-session churn, and add an alert for rapid accept-queue oscillation. Ticket will remain open until post-mitigation metrics show sustained baseline for 48 hours.
ENG-PR: add canary gating and automated short-session churn test (owners: serving-runtime/ingress)
OPS-TASK: create dashboard and alert for accept-queue oscillation (owner: SRE)
DX: update rollout playbook to include stabilization window and threadpool tuning notes
CS: confirm with NimbleDocs after 48h that error rate is back to baseline and close ticket
payload.summary: Short-lived streaming sessions reconnect storm causing elevated 5xx rate after keepalive/backpressure policy sweep

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several macOS laptops on the SF office Wi‑Fi could not resolve or reach internal services (internal-auth, build-cache, service-discovery) starting 2026-03-01 08:10 PST. Failure surface was DNS resolution and mDNS/TDNS-like discovery for zero-trust agent bootstrap. Impact: ~12 users reported inability to start development tools and SSO logins failing intermittently. No server-side incidents reported. Initial triage pointed to DNS failures from client hosts only over Wi‑Fi; wired clients unaffected.
1) Connect a macOS laptop (12.6+) to Redwood_SF_Guest SSID (configured with client isolation enabled)
2) Attempt to reach internal-auth.redwood.local via browser or curl (expected resolution to internal DNS)
3) Observe NXDOMAIN or long timeouts for SRV/TXT/DoT probes from client resolver
4) Connect same laptop to Redwood_SF_Employee (no isolation) or wired network and repeat: resolution succeeds
Mar 01 08:14:22 client-resolver[6789]: dns-over-tls: handshake timeout connecting to 10.10.5.5:853
Mar 01 08:15:01 kernel: sandboxd[123]: network error: prevented outgoing TCP connection to 10.10.5.5:853 (AP client-isolation)
tcpdump (client, wlan0): TLS ClientHello to 10.10.5.5:853 then RST from AP, no SYN-ACK
syslog (ap-controller): client 02:45:8a:cc:bb:01 blocked: client-isolation outbound-to-client-policy
08:40 - Confirmed scope: only Wi‑Fi clients on SSID 'Redwood_SF_Guest' affected; wired and Employee SSID not impacted
08:52 - Reproduced with instrumentation: macOS resolver issues DoT probe to cluster DNS (10.10.5.5:853). AP responded with TCP reset when probe attempted to connect to 'server' IP in same VLAN but classified as 'peer-to-peer blocked' by guest policy
09:10 - AP config review: guest SSID had 'Client Isolation' and 'Block intra-VLAN TCP' enabled by default after recent firmware push (release 2026-02-27). Change log references 'tightened P2P policy' but did not call out DoT/TLS port exemptions
09:25 - Zero-trust agent (ZTA) behavior: agent attempts local DoT (systemd-resolved equivalent) to office DNS for split-horizon records; if DoT blocked, agent falls back to plaintext or mDNS heuristics but macOS resolver prevents fallback without user prompt, causing application failures
10:05 - Cross-check with AP vendor support: default client-isolation rule blocks TCP port 853 unless explicitly allowed via 'service exceptions' or ACL; firmware patch altered default rule behavior
10:40 - Temporary mitigation: updated AP SSID policy to allow TCP/853 and TCP/853 from clients to 10.10.5.0/24; immediately resolved DoT handshakes and restored service discovery

Additional notes:
2026-03-01 10:45 - Network (Priya Singh): Applied ACL exception to Redwood_SF_Guest SSID for TCP/853 to office DNS cluster. Verified successful DoT handshake and ZTA bootstrap for 5 test clients. Monitoring for side effects.
2026-03-01 12:20 - Security (Liam Chen): Quick risk check: allowing TCP/853 internally should be fine; ensure rule scoped to 10.10.5.0/24 and logged. Recommend add to runbook if vendor defaults change again.
Applied scoped ACL on Redwood_SF_Guest SSID to allow TCP port 853 to the office DNS subnet (10.10.5.0/24). Verified DoT handshakes and ZTA bootstrapping for affected macOS clients. Raised vendor TAC ticket; vendor acknowledged firmware change removed implicit DoT exemption and will release a follow-up. Added runbook step to test DoT and mDNS behavior post firmware upgrades. Incident resolved 2026-03-04.
payload.summary: Client DoT probe blocked by AP client-isolation, causing internal service discovery failures for macOS clients

Requester: SRE (Aisha Bello) on behalf of Runtime canary for TP stability fixes.

Context:
We are running a Dedicated-first canary for runtime v1.19 TP stability fixes. We need higher-fidelity NCCL/runtime diagnostics to differentiate:
- NCCL collective ordering mismatch vs
- stream/event synchronization stall vs
- scheduler starvation leading to ranks waiting indefinitely.

Ask:
Enable additional NCCL + runtime collective debug logging for a short, pre-approved canary window, scoped to canary replicas only.

Scope / Constraints (must-have):
1) Scope: Only Dedicated canary clusters (no Hosted global).

Additional notes:
   - Workload: 2 enterprise accounts participating in canary (names shared in private rollout doc; do not include in logs)
2) Time window: 24–48 hours max.
3) Volume control:
   - Sampling: enable only on 1 replica per cluster (or 5% of replicas, whichever is smaller)
   - Log rate limit / size cap enforced
4) Privacy/security:
   - No prompt/user content should be emitted.
   - No customer identifiers beyond internal opaque request_id/trace_id.
   - Retention: 7 days max for debug logs; stored in restricted index with on-call + runtime owners only.
5) Performance:
   - Avoid enabling extremely verbose NCCL settings platform-wide.
   - Prefer INFO/WARN rather than TRACE.
Requested settings (proposed defaults):
- NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
- NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=COLL,GRAPH,INIT (omit NET unless requested by kernels team)
- NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 (if supported / already on)
- Redwood runtime: enable structured "tp.collective" debug events (already added in runtime PRs; ensure they are routed to logs/traces for canary)
Deliverables / Acceptance Criteria:
- Confirmed deployment/config change enabling NCCL debug logs on canary replicas only.
- Confirmed logs are arriving in the restricted index and are queryable by request_id/trace_id.
- Documented rollback procedure and verified rollback works (disable flag + confirm log volume drops).
Rollback:
- Remove env vars / config from canary deployment (feature flag off) and restart affected canary replicas.
- Verify: NCCL debug lines stop within 5 minutes; log ingestion returns to baseline; no continued elevated CPU due to logging.
Approvals:
- SRE lead: Rafael Mendes
- Runtime TL: Noah Patel
References:
- Slack: #eng-sre thread "alerting plan tp stalls" and #eng-releases "runtime 1.19 canary plan"
- Support escalation: SUP-48377 (contains NCCL stall suspicion)

Issue summary:
Request to create a self-service Slack namespace (provisioning gateway) that allows pod leads to create partner and project channels with just-in-time RBAC, preflight data-classification checks, templated channel settings, and automated lifecycle hooks for archival and audit export.

Impact:
Current channel provisioning is manual and centralized. This causes delays for partner work, inconsistent channel metadata, and an accumulation of stale channels that complicate audits and increases noise. A self-serve gateway will speed onboarding, reduce manual admin load, and enforce guardrails.

Desired outcome:
- A lightweight provisioning service (Slack app + automation) accessible via a Jira / Confluence form and Slack command.
- RBAC is granted via short-lived ephemeral grants tied to Okta group approvals (JIT: max 7 days) with automatic revocation.
- Channel templates (private/public, retention, pinned resources, on-call rotas) selectable at creation.
- Lifecycle hooks: reminder at 30/90/180 days, optional archival workflow with archive reason + export to Confluence, and automatic archival for channels flagged as inactive for 240 days.
- Audit events emitted to central audit log (Confluence page and ingestion hook) and optional export to customer-compliant S3 bucket for partner channels.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Pod lead can create a channel via /provision-channel command or a Confluence form and receive JIT RBAC for collaborators.
2) Template selection applies channel topic, purpose, retention, and pinned resources.
3) Channel lifecycle events appear in audit log and produce a Confluence export summary on archival.
4) Automation includes an opt-out flow for channels that require extended retention and sets a manual approval path.

Steps to reproduce (how a pod lead would use it):
1) Run /provision-channel in #pilot-ops with parameters: template=partner-private, collaborators=@alice,@bob, retention=90d.
2) System creates private channel, applies topic/purpose, pins the onboarding doc, and posts a creation summary.
3) Okta approval flow triggers ephemeral membership grants for external collaborators for 7 days.
4) 30/90/180 day reminders posted; no response after 240 days triggers archival job and Confluence export.

Risks & constraints:
- Okta JIT integration work required with Security review for ephemeral guest access.
- Exporting partner data requires consent and potential S3 bucket tenancy for compliance.
- Need to avoid flooding #support with automation messages; rate-limit notifications.

Stakeholders:
- Requester: Product Partnerships (Aisha Patel)
- Security: Priya Singh (review RBAC / guest access)
- Platform/Infra: Connor Miller (assignee)
- Legal/Compliance: Marcos Diaz (export and retention policy)

Additional notes:
Initial spike completed 2026-03-11. Prototype Slack app can create channels and set topic/purpose. Okta team confirmed API for JIT group membership exists but requires scoped service account and approval from Security. Performance: creating channels via Slack API within rate limits is feasible; rate-limiting strategy: batch notifications and exponential backoff.
Open questions: whether to store audit exports in central S3 (Platform-managed) vs tenant-specific buckets for partner channels. Need Legal sign-off on retention lengths for partner PII.
Links:
- Slack prototype repo: github.com/redwood/provisioning-slack-app (PR TBD)
Prototype turned into feature branch. Security review scheduled. Will not enable JIT guest provisioning in prod until Security and Legal sign-off and scoped service account are in place. Aim to land MVP behind feature flag by end of Q2 2026.
payload.summary: Build self-serve Slack namespace with just-in-time RBAC, lifecycle hooks and automated archival

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Users in the San Francisco office intermittently lose connectivity to internal developer services (git, CI dashboards, kubernetes API) immediately after roaming between Wi-Fi APs. Connections appear to fail service discovery (git-server.example.internal, registry-svc.local) rather than DNS resolution for public sites. Impact: several engineering teams report failed git pushes, inability to list pods via kubectl, and flaky service-to-service name lookups when on corporate Wi-Fi and connected through the ZeroTrust agent VPN.

Impact:
- Affected ~15 engineers across multiple teams since 2026-03-10 09:00 PDT.
- Symptoms: "git push" stalls with SSH timeout or fails with "could not resolve hostname git-server.example.internal"; kubectl returns "No resources found" or times out when targeting in-cluster services by name.

Environment:
- Corporate Wi-Fi (APs managed by ACME Wireless controller) using VLAN-per-SSID and client isolation off.
- ZeroTrust agent (v2.8.1) performing split-tunnel + forced internal routes.
- VPN gateway cluster (us-west-1) handling ZeroTrust tunnels.
- Internal name resolution relies on LLMNR/mDNS for some legacy service discovery and conditional DNS forwarding for *.internal zones.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect Macbook (macOS 13.6) to corp-employee-5g SSID.
2) Authenticate via 802.1X (Okta SAML) and allow ZeroTrust agent to start.
3) Move ~20 meters to trigger roaming to an adjacent AP.
4) Attempt to resolve or use service names that are discovered via mDNS/LLMNR (e.g., git-server.example.internal, registry-svc.local).
5) Observe failed name resolution or service discovery; public DNS (google.com) remains reachable.

Observed behavior:
- After roaming, mDNS/LLMNR traffic is intermittently blocked; we see no mDNS announcements from the hosts on the same VLAN when captured on the AP.
- ZeroTrust logs show repeated link re-registration, but successful tunnel re-establishment.
- Wireless controller shows "multicast-snooping: enabled" on several APs and a recent firmware push on 2026-03-09.

Expected behavior:
- Roaming should preserve multicast discovery frames inside the office VLAN or ZeroTrust agent should fallback to DNS-based discovery. Service name resolution should remain stable across AP handoffs.

Initial hypothesis:
- A recent AP firmware (2026-03-09) introduced more aggressive multicast snooping/IGMP proxy behavior that suppresses mDNS/LLMNR broadcast flooding across uplinks during client roaming, causing discovery packets to be dropped between clients and edge service proxies. ZeroTrust agent split-tunnel routing expects the multicast traffic to be available locally and does not re-issue DNS queries to conditional forwards when discovery fails.

Relevant logs/metrics/links:
- Wireless controller event stream: https://acme-wireless.console/company/events?id=EVT-20260309-472
- ZeroTrust agent logs (anonymized) attached in comments.
- Packet capture (pcap) from AP before/after roam: stored on /mnt/support_pcaps/INT-856123/pcap_pair.zip
- Slack thread: #netops -> https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0NETOPS/p1640001234567

Connect to corp-employee-5g SSID and authenticate
Trigger AP roaming by walking between AP coverage zones
Attempt to resolve mDNS/LLMNR-hosted service names
Observe resolution failures while public internet remains reachable
PCAP analysis: client mDNS queries present; AP uplink suppresses multicast frames post-roam; IGMP reports not propagated.
Wireless controller config diff shows 'fast-snooping' flag introduced in 5.4.2 that reduces IGMP query forwarding during client handoffs.
Reproduced locally on a lab Macbook with 802.1X and ZeroTrust agent: enabling fast-snooping causes 60-90s discovery blackhole during roam.
Workaround validated: disable fast-snooping on APs or perform firmware rollback to 5.4.1; both restored expected behavior.
ZeroTrust agent could implement a fallback to conditional DNS forwarders when mDNS/LLMNR discovery fails but that requires product change and release coordination.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:45 - Support: Customer-impacting. Raising P1. Notifying affected teams via #eng-oncall.
Mitigation: rolled back AP firmware on affected units (6/8), disabled 'fast-snooping' where needed. Service discovery restored in monitored zones. Next steps: complete rollback to 5.4.1 across SF campus, open product ticket for ZeroTrust agent to add DNS fallback (INT-856124). Post-incident: recommend vendor firmware hold until multicast behavior validated in lab.
Complete firmware rollback on remaining APs in SF by 2026-03-14
Coordinate with Wireless vendor to revert default behavior in future builds
Work with ZeroTrust product team to scope DNS-fallback feature (INT-856124)
Add synthetic service-discovery checks to Redwood Console network health dashboards
payload.summary: Wi-Fi AP multicast snooping drops mDNS/LLMNR over ZeroTrust VPN causing internal service discovery failures

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several on-prem and remote employees intermittently lose connectivity to internal Kubernetes control-plane endpoints (k8s API) over the corporate VPN. Symptoms include HTTPS stalls (TLS connection hung after ClientHello/ServerHello), kubectl timeouts, and SSO failures when Okta redirects attempt to hit cluster endpoints.

Impact: Affects ~8% of remote users on IPv6-only mobile hotspots and some office users routed through a branch edge running CLAT/464XLAT for IPv6-only carrier links. Breaks developer workflows (kubectl, code pushes) and automated jobs that depend on k8s API. No evidence of a serving platform outage; problem correlates with path MTU size and IPv6-to-IPv4 translation path.

Environment: Production, corporate VPN (WireGuard-based branch/host tunnels), edge NAT64/464XLAT devices at two branch sites (boston-edge, seattle-edge). Affected clients: macOS 14 and Android hotspots. Control-plane endpoint IP: 10.20.5.12 (internal VPC).

Observed behavior: TLS handshakes appear to complete in some packet captures but subsequent HTTP traffic stalls. tracepath/traceroute6 show MTU clamping on the path when CLAT is present; larger packets (1480+) are dropped without ICMPv6 Packet Too Big messages being delivered to the client. The VPN uses UDP encapsulation and fragmentation is disabled on clients (df set).

Expected behavior: PMTU discovery should work across translated paths. Larger packets should either be fragmented/PMTU-adjusted or ICMPv6/PTB should be forwarded so endpoints can reduce MSS and avoid stalls.

1) Connect a macOS laptop to mobile carrier hotspot configured IPv6-only (carrier uses 464XLAT/CLAT on the CPE).
2) Establish WireGuard VPN to prod-us-east via corporate profile (UDP encapsulation).
3) Run 'kubectl get pods --all-namespaces' against internal k8s API (10.20.5.12) or curl https://10.20.5.12/api. Request may hang after TLS setup.
4) Run 'sudo tracepath -n 10.20.5.12' and 'tcpdump -i any icmp6 or icmp' on laptop and edge to observe PTB behavior.
5) Toggle client MTU to 1280 and re-run requests (observe workaround success).
pcap_excerpt: client->server TLS ClientHello (len 512), server->client ServerHello (len 256), subsequent TCP segments with MSS 1460 never ACKed in capture window.
tcpdump_edge_boston: outgoing IPv6 packets fragmented/clamped; no ICMPv6 PTB forwarded back to client (filtered by carrier NAT).
tracepath_output: pmtu 1280 detected between client and first-hop but path through CLAT to internal 10.20.5.12 requires lower MTU; intermediate hop dropped 1420 packets without PTB.
vpn_logs: wg-quick reports peer handshake OK; UDP session active; no peer disconnects.
system_logs: macOS kernel shows 'IPv6: packet too big' entries but application sockets never reduce MSS because PTB not delivered to user-space due to encapsulation/iptables rules.
Initial hypothesis: PMTUD failure due to IPv6-to-IPv4 translation (464XLAT) on carrier/edge resulting in PTB dropped by carrier NAT or not propagated back through WireGuard UDP encapsulation.
Verified reproducible with IPv6-only carrier hotspot and with branch edge using CLAT (seattle-edge). Non-IPv6 clients on standard NATed IPv4 home links do not see the issue.
Workaround: forcing client MTU to 1280 or enabling fragmentation (client-side) allows traffic to flow and kubectl resumes. This reduces throughput but restores connectivity.
Checked iptables/nft rules on branch edge: we have MASQUERADE rules but no explicit ICMPv6 handling; WireGuard endpoint does not decapsulate/rewrap ICMPv6 in a way that Docker/k8s control-plane notices.
Captured pcap on edge shows ICMPv6 PTB generated by internal path but carrier's NAT64 implementation strips or rate-limits PTB messages and they never reach the client; therefore PMTUD cannot complete.
Reproduced in lab using an IPv6-only test SIM and vendor provided CLAT appliance (replicates behavior).

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 13:42 - NetOps: Captured pcap on boston-edge; saw PTB generated by internal router but not delivered upstream to carrier. Suspect CLAT box rewriting ICMP or carrier filtering.
2026-03-13 15:06 - SRE: Noted that enabling 'df' clear on client allowed fragmentation by WireGuard and restored traffic; that's a temporary mitigation if client-side change possible.
2026-03-14 12:30 - Security: Reviewed workaround and confirmed no policy violation to temporarily enable fragmentation for affected support users.
End-to-end PMTUD failed because ICMPv6 'Packet Too Big' messages were lost/filtered across the CLAT/NAT64 translation boundary and not propagated through the UDP-encapsulated WireGuard tunnel back to the IPv6-only client. The result is a silent path MTU blackhole for larger TLS payloads.
Workarounds applied: pushed client MTU profile (1280) to affected MDM group and enabled WireGuard interface iptables rule to allow/forward ICMPv6/PTB translations for known branch edges. Ongoing: vendor engagement to fix CLAT appliance ICMP translation semantics and plan for permanent fix in infra to translate PTB across encapsulation. Rolling change in staging scheduled to add ICMP translation rule and small MTU enforcement on VPN egress.
Follow-ups: 1) Postmortem to document PMTUD checks in runbook. 2) Add automated synthetic tests for IPv6-only path MTU to internal CI. 3) Coordinate with carrier/vendor to ensure PTB propagation.
1) Implement WireGuard iptables/nft rule in staging to map ICMPv6 PTB <-> ICMPv4 PTB and test with lab CLAT appliance (owner: Diego, ETA: 2026-03-18).
2) Push temporary MTU 1280 profile to affected users via MDM (owner: IT Ops, ETA: 2026-03-15).
3) Open vendor escalation with CLAT/Carrier (owner: NetOps, ticket ref: VND-2211).
4) Add postmortem and update network runbook with checks for IPv6 PMTUD (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-22).
payload.summary: Intermittent path MTU blackhole with 464XLAT/CLAT causing VPN tunnel TLS stalls to internal k8s API
