Issue summary:
Automated SCIM provisioning did not reconcile a recent role transfer for an employee (SWE -> Platform) which resulted in: (1) local laptop SKU remaining assigned to the old team inventory bucket, (2) a transient duplicate service-account that overlapped permissions for a short window, and (3) the user's peripheral assignments (badge access, desk reservation) not migrating to the new office seating pool.

Impact:
- One engineer had elevated overlapping service-account keys for ~45 minutes (no evidence of misuse).
- Asset inventory shows a laptop and two monitors still under previous team asset tags causing reporting discrepancy for hardware auditors.
- Desk booking and badge access mismatch prevented the engineer from accessing the new team's office pod for one morning.

Context / Background:
- This follows a cross-team role change performed via HR (Workday) on 2026-03-09. SCIM sync jobs run hourly between Workday -> Identity Provider -> Redwood internal SCIM consumer.
- The new role triggers group membership changes (platform-team, infra-read, devbench-access).
- A concurrent, manual service-account rotation was initiated by the Security team for unrelated reasons at ~09:10 UTC on 2026-03-10.

Observed behavior:
- Workday shows new role and group assignment.
- IDP group membership updated correctly.
- Our SCIM consumer displayed the user still in the old inventory group for hardware allocation and did not remove the old service-account binding; instead it created an overlapping binding with a different naming suffix.

Expected behavior:
- SCIM consumer should: (a) atomically update group memberships, (b) migrate asset allocation records to new owning group, and (c) ensure any deprecated service-account bindings are removed or marked rotated, not duplicated.

Temporary mitigation requested:
- Patch the SCIM reconciliation to detect and remove duplicate service-account bindings for this user until a permanent fix is deployed.
- Manually reassign the laptop and monitors to the new team inventory and create an audit entry for the change.

Notes: this ticket combines access, inventory, and policy questions about acceptable remediation paths for duplicate bindings created during automated provisioning failures.
1) In Workday, change an employee's department from 'swe' to 'platform' and update group mapping that triggers SCIM group changes.
2) Ensure a concurrent service-account rotation or manual key operation occurs in the same hour window.
3) Observe SCIM consumer logs for reconciliation: look for non-atomic updates, duplicate service-account names with suffixes, and asset allocation not moving groups.
4) Check hardware-inventory DB for old_team_tag remaining associated with the user's device after the SCIM run completes.

2026-03-10T09:11:32Z scim-consumer WARN reconcile: detected existing service-account 'svc-jdoe-2023' and created 'svc-jdoe-2026-dup' instead of rotating
2026-03-10T09:12:05Z inventory-service ERROR migrate_asset: asset tag RWI-3421 still mapped to team 'swe' after expected migration
2026-03-10T09:45:00Z iam-service INFO rotation: manual rotation triggered for svc-jdoe-2023 by security@redwood.com
Marissa Clarke (Reporter) 2026-03-10T10:05: We saw this manifest during a routine HR sync. User is jdoe@redwood.com. Raising to infra and security for triage.
Eliot Ramos (Assignee) 2026-03-10T11:20: Confirmed duplicate service-account detected. Holding off immediate deletion until we validate key usage. I've started a manual inventory migration and noted the change in the audit log.
Nina Alvarez (Security) 2026-03-10T12:00: Security ran a quick check against key usage and found no API access from the duplicate account. Recommend marking duplicate as disabled and schedule a clean rotation. Need approval from Policy before deletion.
Harpreet Singh (Hardware Ops) 2026-03-10T13:30: Reassigned monitors and laptop to 'platform' asset group. Updated asset tags and attached audit images to this issue (links below).
Eliot Ramos 2026-03-11T08:40: I've implemented a short-lived reconciliation hook that detects suffix-pattern duplicates and pins them for manual review instead of creating them. This reduces risk but is a temporary measure.
Hypothesis: race condition between SCIM consumer and a separate IAM rotation job. The consumer expects idempotent set operations but the rotation job mutates service-account names causing consumer to treat rotated account as absent and create a new one.
Checked metrics on scim-consumer: reconciliation latency spikes at the same timestamp as the rotation job; see dashboard: https://confluence.redwood.internal/dashboards/scim-reconcile-latency
Inventory projection: our migration code relies on group->team mapping in cache; cache eviction during reconcile may cause non-updated migration path. Need to instrument cache hit/miss ratio.
Related config: scim-consumer version 2.6.1 has a known non-atomic patch; PRs to address were started in infra repo (see PR #1759).
Manual audit and reassignment completed for affected user. Duplicate service-account disabled and keys archived. Short-term reconciliation hook deployed to prevent auto-creation of suffix duplicates until robust fix lands.
Partial mitigation applied: hardware reassignments performed, duplicate SA disabled, short-term consumer hook deployed. Permanent fix requires making SCIM reconcile and IAM rotations mutually transactional or introducing a lock; engineering will prepare a change request. Pending Policy sign-off on automated duplicate deletion.
1) Engineering: implement transactional reconcile or lock around user service-account operations (owner: infra-team, ETA 2026-03-24).
2) Security: finalize deletion policy for duplicate service-accounts created by automated provisioning (owner: security-policy, ETA 2026-03-18).
3) Hardware Ops: run an audit sweep for last 30 days for assets with stale team tags and reconcile (owner: hardware-ops, ETA 2026-03-20).
4) HR/People Ops: add a short pause window note in the role-change workflow to reduce concurrent manual rotations (owner: hr-ops, ETA 2026-03-21).

Issue summary:
We need a federated 'ops-broker' pattern that enables SRE/Cloud-Ops to assume a narrowly-scoped cross-cloud identity for the purpose of decrypting storage objects and retrieving specific S3/GCS objects during incident investigations. The broker must be timebound (max 4h), fully audited, and require request approval via the internal ops access flow.

Impact:
- Debugging for two ongoing incidents (failed customer uploads) is blocked because on-call cannot decrypt KMS-wrapped objects across accounts.
- Affects Dedicated and Private customer troubleshooting where data is encrypted in customer-scoped buckets and keys.
- Potential SLA & escalation impact if access request flow remains manual/slow.

Background:
- Existing JIT approaches (temporary SA impersonation or long-lived cross-account roles) were flagged by Security as too broad or blocked by org policy.
- Previous tickets referenced similar needs but implemented either overly permissive AWS AssumeRole or manual key material export.

Request / Desired outcome:
- Provision a federated broker that allows an authenticated Redwood principal (ops-broker service account) to exchange a short-lived credential for either: 1) an AWS AssumeRole with scoped kms:Decrypt + s3:GetObject on specified resource ARNs, or 2) a GCP service account impersonation with cloudkms.cryptoKeys.decrypt + storage.objects.get for specified buckets.
- Enforce max session TTL of 4 hours and require reason/approval recorded in the access request tool.
- Audit: every access must log principal, target resource, approver, and full request/response trace in Cloud Audit Logs / CloudTrail and be forwarded to the central SIEM.
- Provide a runbook for on-call with exact steps and required request fields (customer ticket, incident id, approver).

Proposed permission set (example):
- AWS role trust: only ops-broker SAML/OIDC provider or service principal allowed to assume.
- AWS role policy: "kms:Decrypt" restricted to arn:aws:kms:us-east:123456789012:key/EXAMPLE-KEY and "s3:GetObject" restricted to arn:aws:s3:::relevant-customer-bucket/*
- GCP: service account IAM binding with roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on specific key resource and roles/storage.objectViewer on specific bucket.
- Tagging/session tags: include requester, ticket id, and expiry policy in session.

Security controls / constraints:
- Access requests must be approved by Security or designated approver (two-eyes for prod).
- No long-lived credentials permitted.
- Prevent credential forwarding: deny iam:PassRole for the assumed role unless explicitly required and logged.
- Terraform plan for infra changes must be reviewed by Security/Infra prior to apply.

Test plan / rollout:
- Implement broker and role definitions in staging (us-west) and validate both AWS and GCP flows with synthetic object decrypt and retrieval.
- Once validated, roll to prod (us-east) with a one-week monitoring window and an automatic revocation hook if anomalous usage detected.

Acceptance criteria:
- SRE can request and obtain access via the broker, decrypt a test object, and retrieve a targeted object in staging within 10 minutes of a ticket approval.
- Audit logs surface required fields in SIEM and link back to the originating support ticket.

Issue summary: Customer BrightCart reports that the Console 'Usage Ledger' tile for their org shows a negative offset (yesterday's usage dropping by ~18k token units) immediately after our nightly compaction/partition rewrite. This coincides with a customer-configured alert that suppresses when reported daily usage decreases by more than 10% - causing an important budget-alert to not fire.

Impact: Enterprise customer billing/usage dashboard data appears to shift retroactively, causing trust issues and missed alerts. Affected a single org in us-east-1 but likely affects any org whose hourly ingest was rewritten during the compaction window.

Environment: Hosted production, us-east-1. BrightCart org id: org_0b3f7. Affected console view: Console > Billing > Usage Ledger (daily rollup). Nightly compaction job: ingest-compact-v2 (runs 03:00-03:30 UTC).

Observed behavior: After compaction job completes, the console daily usage graph shows a sudden decrease for the previous day, sometimes going negative when combined with route-level corrections. The affected ledger rows in the raw export have 'delta' values that appear to be applied twice (one from live ingest, one from rewrite).

Expected behavior: Compaction should only backfill missing historical rows and not alter already-committed daily rollup totals displayed in Console. Alerts based on daily usage should only evaluate against final committed values without transient negative deltas.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Monitor an org with high cardinality API-key traffic through the compaction window (us-east nightly).
2) Export "Usage Ledger" CSV before compaction.
3) Let ingest-compact-v2 run.
4) Re-export Usage Ledger for the same date range and compare.

Temporary workaround: Disable auto-alert suppression threshold until fix is deployed or schedule critical alerts to use a 3-day rolling aggregate. For BrightCart we have temporarily disabled the "suppress on negative drop" rule and set a rolling 72h window.

Export Usage Ledger CSV for org before compaction (Console > Billing > Export)
Allow ingest-compact-v2 to run during maintenance window
Export Usage Ledger CSV after compaction
Compare per-route/per-key deltas and daily rollups - observe negative correction rows and double-applied adjustments

03-11 02:45 - Proposed change: compact-rewrite will check materialized_daily_rollup.version and apply only merged delta or mark tombstone; PR created to gate double-apply behavior.
03-11 11:30 - Data team ran a backfill script to reconcile Ledger for org_0b3f7 and three other sampled orgs; reconciled totals match pre-compaction exports after correction.

Customer (BrightCart) 2026-03-10 09:02: 'We saw our daily spend drop overnight and our budget alert didn't trigger. Can you confirm this was not a billing charge reversal?'

A race condition between ingest-compact-v2 rewrite job and the live-aggregator led to duplicate adjustment records being applied to the daily rollup materialized view. Compact rewrite used an upsert path that did not merge with an existing interim adjustment marker, causing a net negative delta when combined with live ingestion corrections.
Short term: run targeted reconciliation job for affected orgs to re-calc daily rollups from raw events (completed for BrightCart and sampled orgs).
Medium term (PR landed): change compact-rewrite to perform merge-on-key and update rollup.version atomically to avoid double-apply (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/2891).

Issue summary:
A recent IDP rollout changed the order of claims in the OIDC assertion (okta->auth proxy). Our RBAC evaluation code implicitly relied on claim ordering and only considered the first matching 'roles' claim, which in some assertions no longer contained conditional roles. This causes users who should receive a temporary escalation role (e.g., 'oncall:read') via a secondary claim to lose that role and receive reduced console permissions.

Impact:
- Several engineers reported 403s for internal dashboards and runbooks during normal workflows.
- Affected users lose conditional roles for the duration of their session; persistent sessions created before the change were unaffected.
- No data exfiltration risk identified; impact is availability/permissions only.

Environment:
- Production (us-east) using OKTA as the OIDC provider, auth-proxy v2.14.1, console v3.6.0 and identity-service v1.9.

Steps to reproduce:
1. IdP emits OIDC assertion with base 'roles' claim first and conditional 'roles' array in a later claim (observed after IDP rollout).
2. User authenticates via OIDC SSO through auth-proxy.
3. Identity-service performs RBAC evaluation and binds roles to session token.
4. Observe missing conditional roles in session token; attempts to access UI endpoints return 403.

Observed behavior:
- identity-service logs: "rbac-eval: matched roles claim index=0, roles=[\"user\"], conditional_roles not found; final_roles=[user]"
- UI returns 403 with 'insufficient_scope' when calling /console/runbooks for affected users.

Expected behavior:
- RBAC evaluation should aggregate roles from all role-bearing claims and evaluate conditional role rules irrespective of claim ordering.

Temporary workaround:
- Engineering SREs can trigger a session refresh by forcing a re-auth which causes auth-proxy to request the new assertion with claims normalized by the client-side transformation (manual step).
- Identity team applied a temporary patch on identity-service to fallback to scanning all claims for 'roles' arrays; this is not yet in stable rollout.

Investigation notes:
- Timeline: IDP change to token claim ordering rolled out 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC (internal change request #IDP-2026-03-09). Errors began 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC.
- Reproduced locally by constructing OIDC JWTs with roles in second/third claims; identity-service v1.9 reproduces missing roles when RBAC eval short-circuits on first match.
- Root cause hypothesis: legacy RBAC matcher used 'first-match' semantics to be fast; IDP update changed claim order which exposed this assumption.
- Affected surface: console and several internal APIs that rely on role-based gating; non-console tooling that uses alternate token parsing untouched.

Logs / snippets (sanitized):
- auth-proxy: 'received assertion for user=a.patel; claims_order=[sub,iss,aud,roles,roles_conditional]'

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:03 - SRE #oncall: Noted spike in 403s in /console endpoints for ~12 unique users; added temporary alert to track error rate.
Workaround applied: identity-service fallback patch deployed to prod-canary; next steps are a non-breaking fix to RBAC matcher and coordination with IDP to stabilize claim order or publish contract.
1) Merge identity PR that replaces first-match semantics with claim-key aggregation and add unit tests (PR 1428). 2) Plan controlled rollout across regions (canary -> 50% -> 100%). 3) Update SSO runbook and add a contract doc in Confluence documenting expected claim shapes. 4) Postmortem and follow-up action with IDP team to decide on long-term claim ordering contract.
payload.summary: OIDC assertion claim ordering causes conditional RBAC role drop for console sessions

Issue summary: Multiple pods need a reliable, project-scoped way to forward and transform Jira issue events (create, update, comment, transitions) to other internal Jira projects, Slack channels, and Confluence pages for coordinated incident escalations. Issue summary:
Customers using Kerberos/GSSAPI SSO in private deployment report intermittent 401/403 when calling the Redwood private admin API. The incoming GSSAPI negotiation succeeds at the HTTP layer but RBAC denies the request because the principal string does not match any role bindings.

Impact:
- Customer DataWave Health cannot perform admin operations via service accounts bridged by Kerberos (affects scheduled jobs and human ops).
- Intermittent: some requests succeed and others fail depending on which KDC host canonicalizes the principal.

Environment:
- Private control plane deployed in customer VPC (us-east-1).
- Identity flow: nginx ingress -> identity-proxy (GSSAPI/negotiation) -> internal token exchange -> RBAC enforcement.

Steps to reproduce:
1) kinit -k -t /etc/krb5.keytab host/web01@datwave.EXAMPLE.COM
2) curl --negotiate -u : https://private.redwood.internal/admin/keys -H "Accept: application/json"
3) Observe 401/403 in ~30% of attempts when KDC returns canonicalized principal with uppercased realm or altered case in SPN.

Expected behavior:
- GSSAPI-authenticated principal should be correctly normalized and matched against RBAC role bindings.

Actual behavior:
- Identity-proxy and RBAC compare the full principal string (primary/component@REALM) verbatim. KDC sometimes returns REALM in uppercase or the component with different case, causing string mismatch and denial.

Relevant logs (redacted):
- identity-proxy: "auth: gssapi OK principal=host/web01@DATWAVE.EXAMPLE.COM"
- rbac: "lookup: principal 'host/web01@datwave.example.com' not in role bindings -> DENY"
- access log: 403 POST /admin/keys  -> X-Auth-Principal: host/web01@DATWAVE.EXAMPLE.COM

Temporary workaround:
- Customer added a permissive role binding for wildcarded principal pattern 'host/web01@*' in their admin RBAC to allow operations while we investigate.

Request/ask:
- Need an SRE/identity owner to validate normalization behavior and propose a safe fix path (proxy-side normalization vs RBAC tolerant matching).
03/10: Initial triage by Support; reproduced with customer's test harness. Observed KDC canonicalization variability across KDC cluster.
03/10: Identity-proxy currently forwards the raw principal string from GSSAPI (no normalization). RBAC store uses exact-match keys created from SCIM/IDP provisioning which are lowercase in customer's setup.
03/11: Hypothesis: mismatch arises because customer's provisioning pipeline lowercases principals when creating role bindings, while KDC preserves original case or canonicalizes to uppercase realm (DATWAVE.EXAMPLE.COM).
03/11: Confirmed by enabling debug on identity-proxy: GSSAPI principal differs only by case from SCIM entry in RBAC. Example pair: 'host/web01@DATWAVE.EXAMPLE.COM' vs 'host/web01@datwave.example.com'.
03/11: Quick test: adding a case-insensitive match at RBAC allowed the requests to succeed; indicates root cause is string-comparison policy rather than cryptographic principal mismatch.
03/12: Proposed remediation: add canonicalization layer in identity-proxy to normalize principal to lowercase realm and component before token exchange. Also add unit tests, and a feature flag for rollout.
03/12: Risk assessment: low-risk change if behind feature flag; however must be careful for customers relying on mixed-case principals for legacy reasons. Add opt-in config per private deployment.
Related: INT-3321 contains previous notes on principal normalization for SAML/ODIC flows (reuse patterns).
Support (Aisha Kapoor) 2026-03-10: Customer reported intermittent 401/403 after Kerberos upgrade on their KDC farm. Sent request for krb5.conf and sample access logs.
SRE (Miguel Santos) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally using customer's keytab. Observed principal case differences. Will open PR to add normalization in identity-proxy behind feature flag.
Customer (DataWave SRE) 2026-03-11: Confirmed wildcard binding workaround works; would prefer a server-side normalization so we don't have to change provisioning.
Security (Priya Raman) 2026-03-12: Confirmed that normalization must be deterministic and logged for audit. Recommend recording original principal in audit events when normalized.
SRE (Miguel Santos) 2026-03-12: Draft PR available: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/784. Plan: feature-flag rollout to a single private customer cluster, monitor for unexpected allow lists.
Finalize PR to add principal normalization (lowercase realm + stable casefold) with feature flag and audit log of original principal.
Coordinate canary rollout with DataWave support window and monitor RBAC denials and audit trails.
Update Kerberos runbook and add a section on recommended KDC canonicalization settings and provisioning guidelines.
Add an automated test to the provisioning pipeline to detect case mismatches between SCIM-created bindings and KDC-returned principals.
payload.summary: Kerberos (GSSAPI) SPN casefolding causes RBAC principal mismatch in private deployment

Users complete Just-In-Time (JIT) elevation flow via Okta but the resulting session token lacks role claims required for console access; requests to per-route admin APIs return 403 immediately after elevation.
Issue summary:
- Several engineers reported being able to complete the Okta JIT MFA + approver flow, receive a console session, but then immediately get 403 on routes that require elevated roles.

Impact:
- Affected users can temporarily elevate but cannot perform elevated tasks (deploys, infra access) for the duration of the elevated window.
- First reported for 3 users in production US-WEST; could affect others using JIT in the same tenant.

Environment:
- Prod (us-west cluster)
- Okta tenant: redwood-production.okta.com
- Console version: 2.9.1
- JIT flow uses Okta inline hook to transform role claims and issue short-lived elevation grant via SSO token.

Steps to reproduce:
1) User without elevated roles clicks "Request elevation" in Console.
2) Okta prompts for MFA and notifies approver in #approvals slack channel.
3) Approver accepts via Slack approval link.
4) User receives a console session and redirect to /console/dashboard.
5) Immediately attempt action requiring elevated role (e.g., POST /api/v1/deploy or access /admin/audit).

Observed behavior:
- Console responds with HTTP 403 and body: "missing required role claim: admin:deploy".
- Session token in browser lacks the expected roles array (claims truncated).
- Okta system logs show the inline hook executed but returned a payload with roles joined as a single truncated string (length ~800 chars).

Expected behavior:
- Elevated session token should include full roles array (admin:deploy, admin:rollouts, etc.) and elevated actions should succeed.

Temporary workaround:
- Re-authenticating via Okta SSO (full sign-out and sign-in) returns a session with correct claims for some users.
- Manual grant of role via admin console fixes access until token expiry.

Attachments/links:
- Related Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0ABC1234/p1678480000000
- Okta system log excerpt: https://okta.redwood.com/logs/evt-98432

Issue summary:
We observed a set of ML-serving compute instances and associated service identities in prod that appear to hold broader cloud privileges than required for their runtime responsibilities. This ticket requests an automated scan, manual triage, and a phased remediation plan leveraging IAM Conditions and permission boundaries to reduce blast radius without disrupting ongoing inference traffic.

Impact:
- Elevated risk of lateral privilege escalation and data exposure for model artifacts and customer telemetry.
- Potential for accidental credential misuse during oncall/debugging workflows.
- Requires coordination with SRE and ML infra to avoid disruption to high-throughput inference endpoints.

Scope / target systems:
- AWS: prod account(s) hosting Dedicated GPU fleets in us-east-1 (instance profiles, ECS task roles, cross-account roles).
- GCP: prod projects running TPU/GPU pools and serving runtime (service accounts, workload identity bindings) in europe-west1 and us-east1.
- Focus on identities used by: inference-worker, kv-cache-daemon, model-loader, batch-compiler services.

Request / Acceptance criteria:
1) Run a targeted least-privilege scan (automated) across the listed service identities and produce a prioritized findings CSV with explicit APIs/actions allowed but unused in the last 90 days.
2) For the top 25 high-risk principals, create remediations that apply one of: permission boundary, IAM Condition, narrowed role replacement, or scoped cross-account role. Each remediation must include a rollback plan and a smoke-test checklist.
3) Implement JIT scoped roles for debugging (timebound STS sessions) and remove any long-lived human-assumed roles attached to compute.
4) Update the ML prod runbook and add an automated policy check in CI that fails on new role attachments exceeding the approved template.

Estimated workplan and timeline:
- Day 0-2: discovery and automated scan run.
- Day 3-5: triage high-confidence over-permissive bindings and draft remediation PRs.
- Day 6-10: staged rollout (canary on non-critical serving pool, monitor latency/5xxs for 48h).
- Follow-up: postmortem and schedule recurring quarterly audits.

N/A - investigative ticket. Repro steps: 1) Run the provided least-privilege scanner against AWS prod account using role 'infra-audit' and store findings to S3. 2) Export GCP Service Account IAM policy bindings via gcloud for target projects. 3) Correlate unused permissions against CloudTrail/Stackdriver last 90d activity. See scanner runbook linked in Confluence.
Automated scan executed 2026-03-11 with 'infra-audit' role. Initial findings: 42 principals with permissions larger than observed usage. Top risks: broad S3:* on model-artifacts buckets, kms:Encrypt with wildcard resources, compute.instances.setMetadata allowed for non-admin roles, iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on multiple batch workers. Correlation with CloudTrail shows low invocation of kms key management APIs from serving pods. Hypothesis: historic convenience permissions granted during an experimental workload were never tightened post-launch.
Triage flagged 7 roles that are safe to restrict immediately (non-customer facing batch compilers). 3 roles require canary due to being attached to live inference pools.

Additional notes:
Playbook items created: (1) 'audit-to-remediate' script in infra repo, (2) PR template that includes smoke-test checklist and rollback commands. Next action: create PRs for 5 highest-risk principals and request Security review.

Canary scheduled for critical 'model-loader' on 2026-03-14 with rollback plan. Final resolution will include CI gate and updated runbook; close ticket once canary completes and no regressions seen for 48h.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Automated garbage-collection (GC) run in support-tooling removed stale macro/template records referenced by routing rules in the prod us-east cluster. Result: incoming internal tickets were routed to the default queue instead of SLA-aware queues; several P1/P2 internal issues missed expected SLA handoffs for ~45 minutes.

Impact: Approximately 120 internal tickets created between 08:12 and 09:00 UTC were assigned to the generic intake queue, causing delayed triage and escalation. No customer-facing outages were reported, but internal SRE and Oncall workflows were disrupted.

Timeline (key events):
- 2026-03-01 07:58 UTC: Scheduled template GC job starts (support-tooling/sync-cleaner v2.14).
- 2026-03-01 08:10 UTC: Spike in intake queue size noticed by #support-alerts; SLA alerts fired for routing mismatches.
- 2026-03-01 08:20 UTC: Pager duty triggered for internal triage; Rafael engaged.
- 2026-03-01 08:40 UTC: Hotfix applied to disable GC job; template-store restore initiated from 07:50 snapshot.
- 2026-03-01 09:05 UTC: Routing rules re-evaluated and most tickets re-routed to correct queues; monitoring shows backfill progress.

Steps to reproduce (dev/staging):
1) Seed template-store with templates A,B,C and routing rules referencing macro IDs X,Y,Z.
2) Run sync-cleaner with simulate=true and then with simulate=false using the same retention cutoff used in prod.
3) Observe that cleanup removes templates with last_touched older than cutoff even if referenced by active routing rules (edge-case in check that should have looked up live references).

Observed logs/snippets:
- sync-cleaner.log: "INFO Removed 187 stale_templates in us-east; removed_macro_ids=[X, Y, Z]"
- routing-engine.log: "WARN referenced_macro_not_found macro=Z route_id=rt-4491 fallback=default-intake"
- intake-queue-metrics: SLA_miss_count +37 between 08:12-08:50

Initial hypothesis: A regression introduced in sync-cleaner v2.14 bypassed the live-reference lookup when the template-store was under high read load; the cleaner used an index snapshot which was slightly stale and did not reflect recently created routing references. The cleaner then removed templates still referenced by active routing configs. When routing-engine recalculated, it fell back to default intake.

Immediate mitigation performed: Disabled the scheduled sync-cleaner job in prod (07:58 schedule) and paused the GC cron. Restored the deleted template rows from a 10-minute-old snapshot (07:50) to minimize state drift. Re-ran a reference integrity check to mark templates as protected if referenced by routing rules.

Observed side-effects of mitigation: Brief duplicate templates appeared during restore; routing-engine threw transient conflicts for ~2 minutes while indexes rebuilt. All conflicts cleared after index refresh.

Next steps / follow-up work:
- Merge PR to add a strong referential check before deletion and to read routing references under a consistent read view (see related PRs).
- Add an additional safety throttle to the cleaner to limit deletes per minute in production.
- Create a scheduled integration test that exercises GC job against a snapshot of production routing configs.
- Postmortem to be drafted in Confluence and shared with platform and SRE.

Owner: Rafael O'Neill (support-tooling lead).
Correlation between GC start time and intake SLA alerts clear. Query of template_store_deletes shows spike at 07:58-08:02. Repro in staging using identical cleaner config reproduced deletion of referenced templates when we induced a read index snapshot lag by pausing index refresh for 30s. Root cause: cleaner used stale index query, not consistent read.
Actions taken: disabled GC job, restored snapshot, re-protected templates, requeued affected tickets to correct queues.
Potential long-term fix: Use database transactions or consistent timestamped reads; upgrade template-store API to return live references with strong consistency flag.
Work in progress: immediate rollback of GC job completed and templates restored. Short-term fix merged to add pre-delete referential guard and safety throttle (PR linked). Long-term fix tracked in INT-35002 to rework cleaner to use consistent reads and add canary runs. Once fixes land, schedule a controlled GC run in staging and a progressive rollout to prod with monitoring.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Support received multiple alerts from NovaHealth that after a canary steering adjustment earlier this week, a subset of user sessions previously pinned to their explicit model version were observed to 'elevate' to the canary variant. When the canary briefly failed health probes, those sessions immediately fell back to a degraded legacy variant, causing silent fallback behavior and degraded outputs for customer users.

Impact:
- Intermittent correctness regressions for ~0.4% of NovaHealth traffic during the steering window.
- Customer reports increased 5xx fallback responses and user-facing content degradation for a focused cohort (estimated 200–600 requests/hour).
- Billing spike risk from fallback cost differential and repeated retries.

Environment:
- Production (us-east) using Dedicated pool (enterprise contract).
- Canary steering rule applied at 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC targeting 10% of tenant cohorts.

Observed behavior:
- Traffic that previously honored explicit tenant model pin (redwood/v2-chat-8b) shows header-affinity tokens bound to the canary variant after steering change.
- When canary health transitions to degraded, those sessions are rerouted to a legacy variant (redwood/v1-chat-4b) rather than honoring the tenant pin or falling back to staged compatible variant as expected.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant-level explicit pins must remain authoritative; steering should only influence unpinned cohorts. If steering promotes a variant for unpinned cohorts, pinned sessions should not be re-pinned or promoted.
- On canary failure, fallback should choose compatible fallback variant per per-tenant policy and never cross-tenant-divert pinned sessions.

Steps to reproduce (internal repro):
1) Setup tenant config with explicit pin: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/NOVA/config -d '{"pin":"redwood/v2-chat-8b"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
2) Apply a canary steering rule that increases steering weight for header X-Steer: tenant-cohort -> canary redwood/v2-chat-8b-canary at 10%.
3) Send 1k requests across two client sessions: one with tenant pin header and one without. Observe routing decisions in traces.
4) Flip canary health to unhealthy via orchestrator health override and watch pinned session routing.

Relevant logs / traces (sanitized):
- Edge trace (2026-03-10T02:14:03Z): routing_decision: {tenant_id: "NOVA", session_id: "s-09f3", prior_pin: "redwood/v2-chat-8b", selected_variant: "redwood/v2-chat-8b-canary", reason: "canary-steering-match"}

Additional notes:
- Audit (2026-03-10T02:15:21Z): pin_change_detected: {session_id: "s-09f3", new_affinity: "variant_affinity_token:canary-epoch-42"}
Notes:
- Customer asserts they did not change tenant pin config.
- Controls show steering was toggled by Product at 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC for broad experiment.
2026-03-10 NovaHealth (Support Contact Laura Kim): Confirmed they did not change pin configuration. Provided sample request IDs and timestamps. Impacting dashboard linked in message.
Findings so far:
- Repro shows steering path sets a transient 'variant_affinity_token' that has higher precedence than tenant pin during routing decision. Edge prioritization logic treats affinity token promotion as an explicit bind. This is a regression introduced by orchestrator PR that aimed to reduce cold-starts by pre-binding warm canary KV caches.
- The promoted affinity token can survive into subsequent requests for the same session and is being honored even for tenants with explicit pins because precedence ordering checks only on token existence, not pin origin.
- Race condition: if promotion happens between the initial tenant pin check and final route selection, the affinity token wins.
Open hypotheses:
- A header normalization step in the ingress sidecar might be translating tenant pin headers into affinity tokens incorrectly in certain header combinations.
- Token TTL handling might be too long and not scoped to 'steering-only' sessions.
Relevant artifacts:
- Orchestrator commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/commit/4f8a2d
- Trace collection: s3://redwood-traces/prod/2026-03-10/NOVA/s-09f3.log (internal link)
Temporary mitigation applied (2026-03-12): disabled 'steering promotion' flag for NovaHealth cohort and reverted steering propagation in edge-config for that tenant. Observed immediate reduction in cross-variant fallbacks.
Next steps (short term):
- Backfill a guard in the edge routing priority: if tenant pin present, ignore steering-affinity promotions (target: hotfix by 2026-03-15).
- Add integration test covering steering + explicit pin precedence (target: 2026-03-18).
- Scan recent orchestrator PRs for similar 'promotion' logic and create follow-up PR to centralize precedence rules.
Longer term:
- Add telemetry to classify affinity tokens by origin (pin, steering, prewarm) so routing decisions can be audited.
- Adjust token TTL semantics and ensure steering promotions are ephemeral and isolated to unpinned cohorts.
Owner: Aiden Chen. Expected permanent fix rollout: 2026-03-22 (can be accelerated if tests pass).
We have applied a targeted mitigation for your account (NovaHealth) which removed the promotion behavior while we implement a safe precedence fix. We do not expect further user-facing regressions; our engineering team will notify when a permanent patch has been deployed.
payload.summary: Pin elevation observed during canary steering leads to cross-tenant fallbacks

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Users report they cannot unlock laptops or authenticate to internal web apps after a Kerberos policy push that rotated the realm mapping. Affected endpoints show repeated sssd/sshd and winbind errors and the local credential cache (ccache) file appears zero-length or corrupted after a reboot.

Impact:
- Several desktop engineers in us-west cannot SSO to internal dashboards and must use recovery codes.
- Some machines drop network mounts that rely on Kerberos tickets (NFS mounts failing).
- Blocks pair-programming and local test runs for ~20 users (approx 15% of devs in region).

Environment:
- Hybrid AzureAD-joined laptops managed by Redwood Intune + an on-prem AD/ADFS/Kerberos realm (krb5).
- Affected OSes: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (custom imaging), Windows 11 22H2 (corporate image).
- Provisioning agents: corp-provisioner v3.4.1 and endpoint-sidecar v1.9.

Steps to reproduce (from one repro machine):
1) Boot a hybrid-joined Ubuntu 22.04 workstation with existing cached tickets.
2) Apply the Kerberos realm mapping change via the central config push (ansible job kerberos-realm-rotate).
3) Reboot as prompted by the policy agent.
4) Attempt to unlock screen or run klist / kinit.

Observed behavior:
- On boot, systemd services sssd.service and winbind.service fail to start transiently with exit code 203 (unit configuration problem) and then later report STATUS=failed.
- /tmp/krb5cc_* files created but show 0 bytes. klist returns "klist: Credentials cache file '/tmp/krb5cc_1000' not a valid ccache file".
- On Windows, cached Kerberos tickets are evicted and ADFS SSO redirects to a login loop; Windows Event Viewer shows Schannel warnings and LSA kerberos errors referencing 0x8009030E.

Expected behavior:
- Policy push should rotate realm mappings without corrupting on-disk ccache files; services should gracefully restart and re-acquire tickets or prompt user for interactive re-auth to recover.

Logs and artifacts collected:
- /var/log/sssd/sssd_pam.log: "[sdap] Could not open ccache file: Invalid ccache"
- journalctl excerpt: "sssd[pid]: Could not initialize ccache: Bad file descriptor"
- /var/log/syslog contains the ansible job timestamp and agent restart markers.
- Attached: anonymized klist/kinit outputs and sample zero-byte ccache metadata (sha256 sums and inode info).

Immediate mitigation attempted by reporter:
- Manual removal of zero-byte ccache files and recreation with kinit succeeds for single-user session (interactive), but corruption recurs after next policy push or reboot.
- Workaround for now: disable automated kerberos-realm rotate job for us-west while we investigate (Ops rollback implemented 2026-03-12 22:15 PDT).

Additional notes:
- Change was rolled out to all regions; only us-west has user reports so far (suspect timing/ordering with provisioner).
- Ansible job uses a templated /etc/krb5.conf replacement and signals provisioner via SIGHUP.

Recommended next steps listed below in investigation notes.
Investigation timeline:
- 2026-03-12 20:30 PDT: Ticket created by Priya after multiple Slack reports (#internal-support).
- 2026-03-12 21:00 PDT: Confirmed repro on Ubuntu image; zero-byte ccache appears immediately after policy handler restarts sssd.
- 2026-03-12 22:15 PDT: Ops rolled back kerb-rotate job to stop additional machines being affected.
- 2026-03-13 09:40 PDT: Repro attempted on Windows 11 VM image; observed LSA failure patterns similar to on-prem bug KB12345.
- Hypothesis A: Provisioning agent restarts sssd/winbind before krb5 config is fully written to disk, leaving ccache creation in a bad state (race).
- Hypothesis B: New krb5.conf template changes default ccache format/permissions and an older agent version mishandles binary ccache -> creates empty file.
- Actions taken: captured strace of sssd startup (shows EIO when opening /tmp/krb5cc_1000 after SIGHUP), compared krb5.conf diffs, verified agent version on repro machine differs from fleet by one minor patch.
- Correlation: machines with endpoint-sidecar v1.9 (and provisioner v3.4.1) consistently repro; machines with sidecar v2.0-beta do not.
- A/B test: Pinned sidecar to 2.0-beta on two repro machines -> no corruption after policy push.

Temporary risk assessment: Recurrent corruption could lead to mass-login failures if rotation resumes; severity raised to Sev2 due to partial regional impact and user productivity loss.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 10:05 - L3-SRE (Elena Kaur): Ran diff on krb5.conf templates (old vs new). New template changes default CCACHE_TYPE to "FILE" and sets stricter umask; that might interact with older agent behavior. Recommending to test agent 2.0 on repro fleet.
2026-03-14 09:20 - Security (Noah Patel): Confirmed no credential material exfiltration observed in EDR logs; corruption appears local-disk only. Recommend full audit post-fix.
Workaround/temporary resolution:
- Kerberos rotate job rolled back for us-west to prevent further surface area.
- Users can manually recreate tickets with kinit after removing zero-byte ccache files; this is a stop-gap.
Planned permanent fix:
- Provisioner team to land two changes: (1) ensure krb5.conf write is atomic + fsync before signalling agent, (2) upgrade endpoint-sidecar on repro fleet to v2.0 which avoids the empty-file bug.
- GH PR #7832 (prov/signal-ordering) and GH PR #7835 (agent version pin) linked.
- Post-change canary scheduled 2026-03-15 02:00 PDT for 20 machines in us-west; monitoring dashboard panels created (dashboards/kerberos/INT-842468-canary).
Follow-ups:
- Run full audit of machines that received the original rotate change for potential ticket replay or stale mounts (assigned to Marco).
- Update Confluence runbook with steps to recover corrupted ccache files and add agent compatibility note.
Status: In Progress - awaiting provisioner PR merge and staged canary deployment.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a spike of 429 throttling errors across multiple endpoints after deploying new route patterns to isolate background flushers from interactive traffic. Impact: Persistent 429s for interactive requests during normal traffic (5-10% error rate for tenant), leading to user-visible failures in document preview and search. Environment: Dedicated pool, prod:us-east, tenant bound to dedicated pool. Observed behavior: Many requests show quota token consumption that appears to be applied twice per incoming request (route-level and route-variant match), exhausting route-specific burst credits quickly. Expected behavior: Each incoming request should decrement tenant quota exactly once; route isolation should prevent low-priority background flushers from affecting interactive route quotas.
1) Customer created two overlapping route patterns: /api/documents/* (interactive) and /api/documents/uploads/* (background flush).
2) Configured per-route quotas with a low burst allowance for the uploads route and a higher burst for interactive route.
3) Started background flush job that performs parallel multipart uploads to /api/documents/uploads/* while interactive traffic continues.
4) Observed elevated 429 responses for interactive requests after ~10 minutes; quota console shows rapid depletion on the interactive route despite volume fitting configured thresholds.
Sample request traces:
- 2026-03-12T14:05:21Z tenant=nimbledocs request_id=abc123 path=/api/documents/preview token_deducted=2 route_matches=[/api/documents/*, /api/documents/uploads/*] policy=per-route-burst status=429
- 2026-03-12T14:05:22Z tenant=nimbledocs request_id=abc124 path=/api/documents/uploads/part token_deducted=1 route_matches=[/api/documents/uploads/*] status=200
Rate-limiter debug (sample): new_token_count=-1 after deduction (expected >=0). Edge proxy logs show duplicate match entries for some requests when route regexes overlap. Full trace links: https://logs.redwood.internal/trace/abc123 (customer tenant scoped link provided).
Initial hypothesis: overlapping route regexes are causing the request to be counted against both route buckets when the routing layer emits multiple matches rather than choosing a single best-match.
Verified console: per-route quota counters incremented twice for a subset of interactive requests; ingress request inspection shows two matched routes recorded on the request metadata.
Reproduced in staging: created same pair of route patterns, ran synthetic parallel uploads and interactive calls — saw same double-accounting behavior when route ordering was not longest-prefix-first.
Root cause candidate: routing precedence change in recent edge-proxy release allowed multiple matches to be returned for instrumentation; the rate-limiter then applied quota deductions for each matched route without deduplicating by request ID and best-match selection.
Risk assessment: high for dedicated tenants relying on per-route isolation; may lead to persistent 429s and SLA violations during background flush windows.
Priya Shah (Support) - 2026-03-12: Logged by customer after spike observed during scheduled flush. Attached example trace and console snapshot. Requested triage for P1 impact.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Acknowledged and started reproduction in staging. Noted edge-proxy change two days ago. Will instrument internal rate-limiter to log match counts per request.
Eng (Routing) - 2026-03-13: Confirmed change in edge-proxy returns all matching routes when advanced_match flag is enabled. Rate-limiter assumed single match. Created INT-5521 to add defensive dedupe logic in rate-limiter and push validation to Console route editor.
NimbleDocs (Customer) - 2026-03-13: Provided topology and background flush schedule. Customer asks for immediate mitigation while engineering ships fix.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) - 2026-03-14: Temporary mitigation applied: disabled advanced_match flag for the customer's ingress host to restore longest-prefix single-match behavior. Monitoring shows 429s dropping to baseline. Preparing patch for dedupe logic.
Mitigation and permanent fix plan: 1) Immediate mitigation: rolled back advanced matching flag for tenant ingress (2026-03-14 03:20 UTC) — interactive 429s reduced to baseline within 10 minutes. 2) Engineering fix: added deduplication guard in rate-limiter to collapse multiple matched routes to a single best-match before quota deduction (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1983). 3) Console validation: added preflight validation in route editor to warn on overlapping patterns with different quotas and recommend explicit isolation. 4) Post-action: created follow-up internal task INT-5521 to add unit tests and rollout plan across dedicated pools. Customer confirmed functionality restored and will monitor during next scheduled flush. Follow-ups: document pattern in support KB and include example config to avoid overlap.
payload.summary: Overlapping route patterns causing double-counted quota and persistent 429 responses

Issue summary:
Request to build a reusable automation that creates a standard set of Slack channels, a Confluence space skeleton (with scoped templates), and an empty Jira project skeleton when a new product pod is launched. The goal is to accelerate pod onboarding and enforce consistent conventions across engineering, product, and support teams.

Background:
We currently onboard new product pods manually. That includes creating a Slack channel set (team, ops, incident, #help, #announcements), a Confluence space with a kickoff template and runbook templates, and a Jira project with standard issue types and workflows. This is error-prone and delays cross-functional alignment. Several recent pod launches (referenced in linked issues) requested the same artifacts.

Request details / acceptance criteria:
1) Automation endpoint (internal-only) or Confluence/Jira admin-driven wizard that when triggered will:
   - create Slack channels following naming conventions: podname-eng, podname-ops, podname-incident, podname-support, podname-announce
   - set channel purpose and pinned resources automatically (e.g., link to the Confluence kickoff page)
   - create a Confluence space with pre-populated pages: Kickoff, Architecture Overview, Runbooks, Postmortem template, Oncall Roster template
   - copy and apply page templates for Runbook and Postmortem in that space and set view/edit permissions for the pod's identity group
   - create a Jira project skeleton (key prefix suggestion, default board, issue types: Task, Bug, Incident, Spike) and apply the standard filters/boards used by product pods
   - create group IAM bindings: grant pod-admins group admin on the new Confluence space and assign default Jira roles (Developers, Viewers, Maintainers) mapped to Atlassian groups
2) The automation must log actions to a central audit Confluence page and produce a one-line summary back to the triggering Slack thread with links to created artifacts
3) Ability to run in a staging mode (dry-run) that returns diff of what would be created without mutating systems
4) Admin-only access control for launching the automation; invocation should require an approvals step for enterprise-tier pods (flagged by a label)
5) Conform to retention and audit policies (no modification of existing global templates, and the automation must annotate who triggered the creation)

Impact / Rationale:
- Reduces manual onboarding work by ~2-4 hrs per pod and reduces misconfiguration risk during handoff.
- Improves discoverability for new contributors and ensures runbooks exist at launch.

Dependencies / constraints:
- Slack admin API rate limits and channel naming constraints.
- Confluence space creation permissions (may require bot/service account with space-create rights).
- Jira project creation API: need a mapping for project keys to avoid collisions.
- Identity groups for pods must be pre-provisioned (or the automation should optionally create groups).

Acceptance tests / validation steps:
- Trigger automation with test pod "acme-search" in staging (dry-run) and verify output shows correct channels/spaces/projects.
- Trigger with real pod "acme-search" in prod and verify channels and pages are created and the audit log entry exists.
- Verify permissions: pod-admins group has edit on Confluence space, Developers role exists in Jira project.

Attachments / links:
- linked confluence templates above
- prior discussion: Slack thread #platform-automation (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01PLAT/; internal)

Expected timeline:
- Triage/requirements refinement: 1 week

Additional notes:
- Production rollout + docs: additional 1-2 weeks (including security review)
2026-03-12 - Security (Laura Kim): FYI — any service account that creates Confluence spaces will need an audit trail and must use our KMS-backed credentials. We'll schedule a short review when prototype exists.
Initial review: existing OPS onboarding doc covers required pages. No existing automation currently set up. Slack API token will need chat:write and channels:manage scopes; Confluence REST for space creation requires app with impersonation. Jira project creation requires a mapping table for keys. Estimated engineering effort: 2-3 sprints including security review.
payload.summary: Template + automation request: standard Slack channel group, Confluence space skeleton, and Jira project bootstrap for new product pods

Issue summary: Several support engineers report that Just-In-Time (JIT) elevation approval emails are being delivered to users but the approval service rejects the approval tokens when the user's Okta profile contains a plus-addressing variant (user+alias@example.com). Impact: Affected support and SRE staff cannot complete runbook elevation from approval links in email; manual escalation required for affected users. Scope: Intermittent — appears for ~3% of elevation request attempts over last 48h, concentrated on users who have email aliases with a plus sign in Okta and who are routed through our legacy approval link encoder.
1) In Okta, confirm a user has an email profile with a plus sign (e.g., alice+infra@company.com) and that the primary email is the plus-addressing variant.
2) From the internal console, request JIT elevation for that user to execute a runbook that requires approval.
3) System sends approval email with a click-through link to the user’s email address.
4) Click the approval link (desktop mail client -> browser).
5) Observe the approval service returns an error page: 'Approval token not recognized' and the console shows the elevation pending with no change in status.
Approval emails are delivered to the user (verified via mail headers and user confirmation).
Clicking the link opens console but approval service logs 'token validation failed: identity mismatch'.
Affected users must escalate to on-call to manually grant temporary elevation.
Approval link should validate the token and complete the elevation flow for any email alias that the user owns, including plus-addressing variants.
No manual intervention required if user clicks the email link within SLA window.
2026-03-13T09:14:22Z approval-service ERROR token_validation: uid mismatch (expected: alice@company.com, observed: alice+infra@company.com) request_id=req-6b2f1
2026-03-13T09:14:22Z console WARN elevation_flow: approval_link_clicked user=alice+infra@company.com ip=18.204.12.33
Email headers (delivered): To: alice+infra@company.com; Message-ID: <abc123@ses.company.internal>
Initial hypothesis: token payload includes a normalized email (stripped plus) but approval link encodes the raw email address, causing mismatch during validation.
Checked SCIM profile data: Okta primaryEmail is 'alice+infra@company.com'. Our identity-proxy normalizes some addresses (lowercase + strip tags) for older tenants but not consistently across all codepaths.
Replayed a failing approval event in staging with identical inputs: reproduced token_validation error when email normalization flag differs between approval-link-encoder and approval-verify service.
Related code paths: approval-email-generator (legacy) URL-encodes the raw email into 'user' param; approval-verify service compares against normalized identity from idp-claim (which strips plus-address tags for some orgs).
No changes to Okta or SES observed in the time window; spike correlates with a rollout two days ago that reintroduced legacy encoder behind a feature flag for a subset of requests.
Support (Marta Kline) 2026-03-13: Customer (internal user) confirms they received the email but link failed. Provided screenshots and mail headers.
Assignee (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-13: Reproduced in staging; filing as bug. Temporarily disabling legacy approval-link encoder for routing group 'migration-canary' to stop new failures.
SRE (Dylan Cho) 2026-03-13: Disabled the feature-flag for migration-canary at 2026-03-13T16:05Z; monitoring for regressions. No further failures for that cohort since the toggle.
Auth eng (Priya Nair) 2026-03-14: Found mismatch in email normalization libraries between approval-generator (uses simple stripTags util) and approval-verify (uses identity-proxy canonicalizeEmail). Preparing PR to centralize normalization to identity-proxy library.
Support (Marta Kline) 2026-03-14: Confirmed workaround for two affected engineers; both were granted manual elevation by on-call. Requesting release timeline for fix.
On-call can manually grant temporary elevation for affected users. Temporary mitigation already applied: roll back feature-flag to stop routing requests through legacy approval-link encoder for migration-canary cohort.
Fix in progress: centralize email canonicalization in identity-proxy and update approval-email-generator to use canonicalized address when generating/encoding approval tokens. Auth eng to submit PR (related_github_prs: AUTH-4573) and coordinate a canary deploy. Post-deploy, run a sweep of pending JIT approvals older than 24h to reissue links. Target deploy: 2026-03-18.
payload.summary: Plus-addressing email variants cause JIT elevation approval links to be unrecognized

Issue summary:
Request from Partner Compliance (Vendor: Veritas Analytics) for a limited extract of prod inference sessions to validate redaction behavior against their PII-detection tooling. They need a minimal sample (approx. 150 sessions) scoped to the partner's tenant IDs and timeframe.

Impact:
- Partner requires sample within 72 hours for audit window.
- High sensitivity due to potential customer PII in free-form prompts/responses; must enforce strict redaction and two-person control.

Environment:
- prod (us-east-1) serving runtime.
- Session slicing will read from secure eventstore and inference-telemetry index; no full database exports.

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
1) Provide up to 150 anonymized session records that meet the partner-provided filter (tenant IDs and 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-05).
2) Apply canonical redaction script (see linked confluence) to remove or pseudo-anonymize: email addresses, phone numbers, payment tokens, and any 16+ digit numeric sequences.
3) Hash user identifiers (salted HMAC), keep mapping only in ephemeral HSM-wrapped artifact owned by Security; mapping must be destroyed after verification.
4) Ensure stripped payloads contain only: request timestamp, anonymized user_id, model_version, token_count, and the redacted prompt/response.
5) Produce a verification checklist and a diff report showing pre/post redaction counts for common sensitive regexes.
6) Delivery via secure S3 bucket with KMS encryption and two-person ACL (Compliance + Security).

Issue summary:
Employee (BER-017) reports inability to reach internal services (git.redwood, console.redwood-inference) when on office Wi‑Fi and connected to corporate WireGuard VPN. Intermittent behavior: sometimes services work after reconnect but then fail again. Impact: blocked developer, SSO pages failing, critical deploy delayed.

Impact:
- Single developer impacted initially, potential for more if root cause is AP or DNS policy.
- Affects access to internal git and console (portals behind internal DNS).

Environment:
- Location: Berlin HQ (floor 3).
- Client: Windows 11 laptop (Dell XPS), VPN client: company WireGuard profile (wg0), Wi‑Fi: Meraki MR access points (SSID: Redwood-Staff).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Join SSID Redwood-Staff and authenticate via 802.1X (OK).
2) Establish WireGuard tunnel (wg-quick up redwood-wg).
3) Attempt to resolve internal hostnames (git.internal, console.internal).
4) Observe failures intermittently; traceroute shows packets leaving client to public DNS instead of corporate DNS.

Observed behavior / Logs:
- nslookup git.internal -> Server: 1.1.1.1
  Address: 1.1.1.1#53
  ** server can't find git.internal: NXDOMAIN
- ping console.internal -> Destination host unreachable (no route to 10.48.10.5)
- wg show: interface up, peers present, allowed-ips = 10.48.0.0/16, 10.0.0.0/8, but resolv.conf shows 1.1.1.1
- Browser developer reported DoH (DNS over HTTPS) enabled in Firefox which points to cloudflare-dns.com

Initial hypothesis:
- Split-tunnel policy should push corporate DNS (10.0.0.53) to the client but DoH in the browser and a cached system DNS configuration are causing name resolution to bypass the WireGuard-supplied resolver. Additionally, a recent firmware push to a subset of MR APs enabled client isolation/captive-portal fallback that intermittently breaks DHCP/DNS update during fast roaming.

1) Connect to Redwood-Staff SSID and authenticate 2) Start WireGuard profile redwood-wg 3) Try to resolve git.internal and open console.internal 4) Note DNS server and traceroute outputs
- Confirmed user was on MR-AP MR33, firmware 28.6.1; AP had recent config change (rollout-berlin-2026-03-02).
- Reproduced on second laptop: enabling DoH in Firefox caused internal names to fail even with wg0 present.
- Captive portal: observed DHCP lease refresh failed during AP fast-roam; client sometimes dropped system DNS to AP-supplied DNS until reconnect.
- WireGuard config contains PostUp scripts intended to update resolv.conf but was being overwritten by NetworkManager on Windows when DHCP events fired.
- No evidence of central WireGuard server rejecting DNS push; server-side logs show successful handshake and routes assigned.

Primary cause is a race between AP DHCP events (client roaming) and WireGuard's DNS push/update; DoH in-browser masks the system resolver changes leading client to query public resolvers. Secondary contributor: AP client isolation feature triggers captive portal behavior during the roam, briefly removing local DNS and routes.
Scoped incident to BER floor 3 and disabled recent AP change (client-isolation) on MR33 cluster as quick mitigation
Advised user to temporarily disable DoH in browser and flush DNS cache (ipconfig /flushdns)
Applied Windows local workaround: run wg-quick down/up + netsh interface ip set dns to force corporate DNS 10.0.0.53
SRE verified WireGuard server logs and confirmed allowed-ips and DNS push succeeded
Opened ticket with Meraki support referencing rollout-berlin-2026-03-02 for firmware behavior
Workaround provided: disable browser DoH and re-establish wg0; AP change rolled back for affected cluster. Root fix pending: update Windows WireGuard wrapper to force system resolver update post-tunnel-up and patch Meraki roaming config. Owners: Networking team (rollout fix) and SRE (VPN client update). Targeted change window scheduled for 2026-03-18.

Follow-up items:
- Deploy WireGuard client update (force resolv.conf update on tunnel up) - owner: SRE - ETA 2026-03-18
- Audit MR AP clusters for similar config drift - owner: NetEng - ETA 2026-03-20
- Add DoH detection and UX warning in internal onboarding docs - owner: IT Docs - ETA 2026-04-01

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - Jana Müller (NetEng): Rolled back MR33 client-isolation change for BER cluster at 11:30 CET. Asked Meraki to investigate roaming DHCP behavior.
2026-03-13 - IT Ops (note): Workaround communicated to BER floor via Slack #berlin-office. Monitoring for recurrence.
payload.summary: Berlin office: intermittent captive portal + WireGuard split-tunnel causing internal DNS failures

Issue summary: A developer reported an unexpected approval prompt from a GitHub Actions workflow after clicking a link in an external email. The link redirected to a third-party page that requested a GitHub OAuth reauthorization. The developer completed the flow using their corporate SSO (Okta), after which we observed an unusual spike in CI-triggered deploy jobs and new runner labels appearing in the org. Impact: Potential exfiltration or misuse of GITHUB_TOKEN-like secrets or third-party app tokens created during the OAuth flow. No confirmed data leakage yet, but CI pipelines ran on branches with privileged deploy steps. Environment: production GitHub org (redwood-inference), GitHub Actions runners (self-hosted and GH-hosted), corporate SSO via Okta, developer laptop (macOS, corporate-managed). Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - developer receives external email with link; 09:18 UTC - developer clicks link and completes OAuth reauth; 09:22 UTC - spike of CI workflows started across unrelated repos; 09:24 UTC - security alert triggered by anomalous runner label creation; 09:30 UTC - developer opens internal support and Security notified. Steps to reproduce (observed flow): 1) Malicious email contains link to staging.redwood-assets.com/gh-auth?redirect=... 2) Link redirects to github.com/login/oauth/authorize with a client_id matching a third-party app (app id matches a public vendor account) 3) OAuth consent screen shows organization-level scopes (workflow, repo) 4) Developer approves via Okta SSO 5) New personal access-like token or app installation leads to CI runs. Observed logs: - Audit log entries: oauth_authorization.created (client_id: 5f4a3b, scopes: repo, workflow) - Actions logs: multiple repository_dispatch and workflow_dispatch events initiated from IPs in EU region not associated with our CI pool - Runner registration events: new runner label "temp-uk-12" associated with self-hosted pool, token used from unknown host. Initial hypotheses: a malicious third-party OAuth app used a phishing redirect to request org-level workflow access and a service token was issued (or a token-equivalent app installation). Alternatively, the flow could have leveraged a consent phishing page that swapped client_id after redirect. Immediate risk: execution of privileged deploy workflows and access to secrets provided to Actions contexts. Recommended immediate mitigations executed: 1) Revoked all recent OAuth authorizations issued around 2026-03-10 09:00-10:00 UTC. 2) Rotated repository-level secrets used by deploy workflows (CI_DEPLOY_KEY, PROD_DB_DSN). 3) Disabled self-hosted runner registration and removed suspicious runners. 4) Temporarily set Actions permissions to read-only where possible and limited workflows with deploy permissions. Next steps (pending): run audit across org for other new OAuth apps, review Okta login events for the developer, collect dev laptop forensic snapshot, verify whether any secrets were exfiltrated from workflow logs or artifacts.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 09:52 UTC - Security (Naomi Park): We've revoked the OAuth grant for client_id 5f4a3b and disabled new self-hosted runner registration. Collecting Actions run logs for affected repos.
2026-03-10 10:15 UTC - Infra (Diego Ramirez): Removed runner 'temp-uk-12' from pool and blacklisted its registration token. Confirmed runner's host IP traces to a VPS provider in Poland.
Initial containment appears successful: OAuth grants revoked, secrets rotated, and suspicious runners removed. Still investigating whether the OAuth flow resulted in an app installation granting persistent access or a one-time token used to trigger workflows. Audit logs show org-level oauth_authorization with repo+workflow scopes; need to correlate token usage to run IDs. Okta logs show the developer's SSO session originated from their corp IP at 09:18 UTC. No outbound data transfer to unknown endpoints from GH-hosted runners found so far. Artefacts and workflow logs scan in progress (pattern scan for secrets).
In progress - mitigations applied (revoked OAuth grants, rotated secrets, removed runners, limited Actions permissions). Follow-up items: full org OAuth sweep, CI artifact review, user education email on consent phishing, update runbook to require security approval for org-level app consent. Will update when root cause confirmed or when containment completed.
Full org OAuth app inventory and sweep
Forensic image of developer laptop
Scan workflow artifacts for secrets
Update security runbook and phishing guidance
Notify Legal/Compliance if leakage confirmed

Issue summary: Several depot-return laptops that underwent battery replacement (battery swap and EC firmware reflash step) are failing to finish post-repair provisioning. Symptoms: machines drop into BitLocker key protector prompt or Windows enter recovery screen, Autopilot/AAD join does not complete, and our agent stalls on 'finalizing device identity'.

Observed pattern: EC (embedded controller) serial number on some repaired units is being re-assigned to a different chassis serial in the asset DB during repair staging. The asset DB reconciliation process then flags a serial collision which triggers our provisioning agent to clear TPM owner state as part of a safety flow. That leads to BitLocker key protector mismatch and a recovery loop on first boot.

Why this matters: Blocks reprovisioning throughput at depot (~25-30% reprovision failure rate for battery-repaired builds this week), delays laptop return-to-service, increases manual intervention, and risks exposure of untracked asset state changes.
Depot imaging stalls, ~20-30 machines affected this week in us-west depot. Manual recovery required for each unit. Increases repair lead time and costs. No customer-facing outage but internal SLA for RMA turnaround impacted.
1) Perform battery replacement and run depot staging image (includes EC firmware reflash tool v2.1.4)
2) Run asset-sync (depot tool) to update chassis/EC serials to central asset DB
3) Initiate Autopilot / Imaging task and reboot into Windows OOBE
4) Observe WMIC/sgfw outputs show EC serial differs from chassis serial in asset DB, asset-sync triggers a reconciliation path that marks duplicate=TRUE
5) Provisioning agent invokes TPM reset safety flow -> BitLocker protector mismatch -> Windows recovery screen
Excerpt of provisioning-agent log (timestamps normalized):
2026-03-09T09:11:23Z INFO starting asset-sync for host DELL-7440-AB12
2026-03-09T09:11:24Z WARN ec_serial 0x1A23F conflicts with asset-db chassis_serial 0x1A23F (owner: DEVICE-2982)
2026-03-09T09:11:24Z INFO reconciliation: flag_duplicate=true, invoking safety_reset_flow
2026-03-09T09:11:25Z INFO tpm_reset_requested by safety flow
2026-03-09T09:11:30Z ERROR bitlocker_unseal_failed keyprotector not found (status 0xE07)
2026-03-09T09:11:30Z ERROR provisioning halted - awaiting manual recovery

Initial hypothesis: EC firmware reflash tool v2.1.4 writes an EC serial field that is non-unique (race or defaulting) leading to collisions in asset-sync.
Verified: two repaired units show identical EC serial bytes after reflash; original chassis serial unchanged in system BIOS. EC serial duplication only appears after reflash step.
Asset DB reconciliation logic currently treats any EC serial collision as authoritative and triggers TPM safety reset. This was intended for rare tamper cases but is too aggressive in depot repair flows.
Checked recent PRs: imaging-scripts PR-87 modified EC reflash step and introduced fallback default in case of flash failure; this may mask failure and set default serial to 0x1A23F. Linked PRs for review.
Repro locally in depot lab with synthetic EC flash -> duplicates are reproducible ~80% when flash fails fast-path and fallback executes.
Risk: current automatic TPM reset flow can cause BitLocker key protector loss if machine had encryption enabled before repair (common for enterprise fleet).
Support (Daniel Kim) 2026-03-10: First reported by Depot Team when triage noticed two DELL units booting to recovery after battery swap. Attached logs and initial sample images.
SRE (Priya Menon) 2026-03-11: Confirmed duplication in lab. Repro steps documented. Pausing automatic TPM safety_reset in asset-sync to avoid further incidents (temporary mitigation deployed to us-west depot only).
Firmware Eng (Lena Ortiz) 2026-03-11: Investigating EC reflash tool. Found code path that writes fallback serial 0x1A23F on verification failures. Preparing PR to abort and surface explicit failure instead of writing fallback.
Policy (Aaron Lee) 2026-03-12: Noted that asset-sync reconciliation policy was intended to be conservative for tamper detection. Recommend adding depot-repair exception flag based on vendor repair token.
Depot Lead (Marta Silva) 2026-03-12: Requesting runbook entries for manual recovery and guidance for technicians when encountering this state.
Security (Oliver Grant) 2026-03-12: Concern about disabling TPM safety flows; acceptable as temporary mitigation only if logging/audit preserved.
Partial mitigation applied: asset-sync updated in us-west depot to treat 'depot_repair_token' annotated requests as low-confidence duplicates and skip automatic TPM reset. Firmware team opened PR to stop writing fallback EC serial in reflash tool (PR-412). Full rollout pending QA. Manual recovery runbook created and circulated to depot techs.
1) Merge firmware fix PR to abort flash instead of writing fallback serial (owner: Lena Ortiz, target: 2026-03-15)
2) Update asset-sync reconciliation to add repair-token-aware policy and add explicit audit events (owner: SRE, target: 2026-03-14)
3) QA of changed flows in staging depot (owner: Depot QA, target: 2026-03-16)
4) Backfill audit and run a cross-check job to detect any previously mis-assigned EC serials and remediate (owner: AssetDB team, target: 2026-03-18)
5) Follow-up postmortem and update depot runbook with recovery steps and detection heuristics (owner: Operations, target: 2026-03-20)

payload.description:
Issue summary:
After a recent upstream IdP configuration change, the SAML assertion's roles attribute is being emitted as a single space-separated string (e.g. "admin data_science") rather than the expected comma-separated list or repeated <Attribute> elements. Redwood's RBAC claim parser currently expects either an array or comma-separated values and does not split on spaces, so users with multiple roles fail to be assigned expected permissions and receive 403 when accessing the console or Model Observability dashboards.

Impact:
- A subset of users with multiple roles intermittently receive 403 during console actions that require role elevation (e.g., switching workspace, accessing dashboards).
- Affects both employee and contractor identities that came from the updated IdP connector.
- Blocking on-call workflows for analytics and on-call runbook access during engineer rotations.

Environment:
- Production (us-east)
- Affected apps: redwood-console (web), model-observability services behind the console SSO gateway

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use an Okta test account that has two roles assigned at the IdP level (e.g., admin and data_science).
2) Initiate SAML SSO to the Redwood console from Okta (IdP-initiated or SP-initiated SSO).
3) Observe the SAML assertion in the Auth service logs; confirm roles attribute serialized as a single space-separated string.
4) Attempt to perform an action that requires the second role (e.g., open Model Observability).
5) Observe 403 and no RBAC entries created for the second role in the session record.

Expected behavior:
- RBAC parser splits roles and binds both roles to the user session so permission checks succeed.

Actual behavior:
- Only the first token (before the first space) is picked up, or parsing fails entirely, resulting in missing permissions and 403 responses.

Workaround:
- Short-term: Create a temporary mapping in the Auth service claim-transformer to split roles on space for the affected user groups (manual fix).
- Longer-term: Coordinate with IdP team to restore comma-separated or repeated role attributes.
Create IdP user with two roles at Okta
Initiate SAML login to Redwood console
Capture SAML assertion in auth-service logs (trace=sampled)
Attempt to access Model Observability that requires second role
Observe 403 and check session.rbac entries
2026-03-10T14:12:02Z auth-service INFO incoming-saml assertion=... roles="admin data_science"
2026-03-10T14:12:02Z rbac ERROR parse-roles failed to split roles: unexpected-format
stack=org.redwood.auth.RBACParser:line 212
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z gateway WARN permission-check user=alice@redwood.com resource=/observability/overview result=403
Avery Chen (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Raised after support on-call noticed multiple 403 reports during the 08:00 rotation. Collected sample SAML assertion and attached logs.
Samir Patel (Assignee) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed SAML roles string shows space-separated tokens for 7/12 samples. Added temporary claim-transformer rule to dev auth cluster for verification; test users now get both roles when routed through dev gateway.
Nadia Ortiz (Identity Team) - 2026-03-11: We rolled a connector update in Okta last night for attribute serialization. Investigating whether the change was intentional; can revert if needed. We will provide a change log by EOD.
Samir Patel - 2026-03-12: Mitigation plan: deploy claim-transformer change to prod auth-service behind a feature flag and coordinate with Identity to freeze connector changes until we ship parser fix. Monitoring 1 hour post-deploy.
Auth team reproduced parsing error in local with sample assertion containing 'admin data_science'.
RBACParser currently splits roles on ',' and checks for repeated Attribute elements; does not sanitize spaces. We can add .split(/[ ,]+/) in parser and add unit tests.
Temporary claim-transformer rule implemented in dev by Samir: roles = roles.replace(' ', ',') for affected group 'engineering-legacy'. Verified with 6 users.
Identity team indicates connector change was to normalize attribute formatting for some external partners; rollback possible but may impact partner integrations.
Security review: change to parser is low-risk but needs unit tests and regression checks to avoid mis-parsing roles containing spaces as part of a single role (rare).
In progress - feature-flagged parser change prepared (auth-service PR #4291). Short-term claim-transformer mitigation applied to affected groups in prod. Coordinating with Identity to either revert connector change or produce a stable attribute format. Post-deploy monitoring and a rollback plan exist. Follow-up: add robust unit tests for multiple role serializations and update SSO runbook.
PR ready: github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/4291 (parser: split on commas OR whitespace, add tests)
Mitigation applied: claim-transformer rule id=ct-20260311 active for groups: engineering-legacy, contractors-analytics
Post-deploy checks: 200/200 auth sessions for a 30m sample showed correct role binding after mitigation in canary cluster

comments: Benicio Reyes: Assigned to Priya for design. Initial approach: implement a rotator that writes new token version to Vault and updates token-proxy, leaving previous version accepted for a configurable grace_seconds parameter. Need orchestration that optionally sends graceful restart signal to runners that support hot-reload.
