Two blockers: (1) some runner images don't support hot-reload and need restart orchestration; (2) Vault revocation API currently used by ops revokes immediately — need delayed-revoke or scheduled revoke.

Priya Singh: Working on a design doc and implementation plan. Will submit PR for token-proxy to support accepting previous token version and a CLI tool for scheduled revokes. Targeting rollout to prod-ci in two phases: token-proxy change + scheduled revoke orchestration (phase 1), runner restart orchestration (phase 2).
payload.description:
Issue summary: Our central CI service account tokens (used by self-hosted GitHub/GitLab runners and several release pipelines) are rotated manually by SRE. This creates short windows where scheduled or push-triggered jobs observe auth errors. Impact: intermittent CI failures during releases, flaky deploys and developer friction. Goal: design and implement an automated rotation flow that provides an overlapping grace period (dual-valid tokens) and a rollback path in case a rotation causes failures.
Multiple release pipelines across teams experience sporadic authentication errors (401/403) during manual token swaps. Recent incident increased mean time to merge for a hotfix by ~90 minutes and blocked one nightly build. Affects platform and product teams that rely on self-hosted runners and the release automation service account.
Tokens are stored in Vault (transit+kv v2). Runners pull short-lived credentials via the internal token-proxy service. Current rotate procedure: generate new token in Vault, update token-proxy, and then revoke old token immediately. Runners poll token-proxy on restart or job start; some long-lived runner processes cache token until restart.
1) Coordinate with SRE to trigger manual token rotation in Vault (generate new secret, write to path used by token-proxy)
2) Deploy token-proxy configuration change to point to new secret version
3) Trigger a concurrent release pipeline run on a self-hosted runner that has a cached token
4) Observe the job failing with 401/403 while the runner is still using the old token after it has been revoked
Jobs started by runners that still hold the old token fail with 401/403 until runners are recycled. Job logs show errors from token validation endpoint and 401 responses from the control-plane auth check.
Rotation should not cause running or newly-scheduled jobs to fail. We should have a transition window where both the old and new tokens are accepted until all runners have picked up the new token, or runners are gracefully instructed to rotate without aborting in-progress jobs.
Checked vault audit logs (vault-audit-2026-03-09): immediate revoke events at 2026-03-09T22:14:03Z correlated with first 401 spike
Token-proxy logs (token-proxy-prod-2026-03-09): config reload succeeded; no explicit dual-token handling present
Runner processes: several teams run long-lived runner containers that only refresh credentials on container restart — documented in runbooks but not consistently enforced
Hypothesis: immediate revokes combined with long-lived cached tokens cause timing windows where in-flight jobs see token invalidation
Quick test: applied a prototype dual-acceptance patch to token-proxy to accept previous token for 10 minutes — jobs that would have failed succeeded in test cluster
Related slack thread: #infra-ci (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02INFRA/p1623456789000000)
Related runbooks: Confluence - CI Token Rotation Runbook (https://confluence.internal/redwood/ci-token-rotation)
Implement a three-part safe-rotation flow: (A) token-proxy supports dual-accept for previous secret version for a configurable grace_seconds; (B) rotation orchestration script that: creates new token secret, updates token-proxy, schedules a revoke job in Vault after grace_seconds; (C) review and gradually deploy runner hot-reload/restart automation for long-lived runners so that they pick up new tokens without manual restarts.
Design and land token-proxy PR to accept previous secret version (owner: Priya)
Add scheduled revoke utility to ops-tooling to revoke vault secrets after grace window (owner: SRE)
Inventory long-lived runner pools and add restart hooks where feasible (owner: DevOps)
Update CI runbooks and add 'recommended grace window' defaults per region (owner: Documentation)
Run phased rollout in staging, then prod-ci with 15 minute default grace for cross-region pools (owner: Release Engineering)

Additional notes:
SRE Oncall (Liam O'Connor) (2026-03-11): Proposed changes to ops process: change manual revoke to schedule revoke job that runs after grace window. Also suggested adding a health-check endpoint for token-proxy to report last rotation time.
Devops (Marina Velasquez) (2026-03-12): Noted one edge-case for private clusters (on-prem runners) where network lag causes longer token propagation — recommend 15 minute default grace in cross-region pools.
In Progress - prototype validated in staging; production rollout scheduled. Resolution pending completion of token-proxy PR and scheduled revoke tooling. Follow-ups: create monitoring alert for post-rotation 5xx/401 spike and add a post-rotation checklist in runbook.
Avoid immediate revokes in manual process until tooling is in place. Prefer automated rotations that include observability and a rollback path. Planned next update: PR link and rollout schedule by 2026-03-15.
payload.summary: Automate rotation of CI service-account tokens with graceful overlap to prevent job failures

Issue summary:
- After the Okta claim sanitization rollout (2026-03-08), service-runner impersonation attempts intermittently receive 403 Forbidden from the internal console authorization layer.

Impact:
- On-call engineers are unable to assume affected user sessions to run elevated runbooks ~15-30% of attempts during peak hours.
- Affects internal incident response and automated remediation flows for a subset of service accounts that have legacy group attributes.

Environment:
- Prod, us-west-2. Observed across multiple clusters and proxies; not present in staging.

Observed behavior:
- Impersonation calls return 403 with "rbac:role-claim-mismatch" and an empty roles array in the authorization debug payload.

Expected behavior:
- Impersonation should succeed when requester has delegated runbook role and claim mapping is intact.

Business urgency:
- P1 (Sev1) - Blocks critical runbook execution during incidents. Needs mitigation and rollback plan if needed.

Hypothesis B: Non-ASCII removal mutates legacy group IDs that contained accented characters, causing exact-match RBAC lookups to fail.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent failures while pulling model shards and repeated gRPC stream chunk drops from serving nodes. Failures occur during large artifact downloads and during long-lived chat streaming; symptoms include repeated TLS renegotiation attempts, delayed handshake completion (200-800ms additional), and gRPC framing errors leading to 5xx retries.

Impact: Affects FinStrata internal private deployment (prod, us-east-1). Multiple model pulls and streaming sessions saw transient stalls for ~10-30s, increasing latency and causing client-side reconnects. Several retries caused elevated token cost and client errors for the customer.

Environment: Private deployment behind customer-managed edge (MPLS + SD-WAN), corporate firewall with deep-packet inspection (DPI), customer NAT appliance, TGW peering to Redwood control plane.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Trigger a large model pull for redwood/open-llama-13b-v2 via the agent on a private node behind the customer edge.
2) Stream a long-lived chat session (token window > 2048) to force multiple TCP segments and TLS records.
3) Observe occasional TLS handshake stalls, gRPC FRAME_ERROR in client logs, and partial artifact ranges failing with HTTP 499/502 on range downloads.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Client logs show repeated 'tls: short record' and 'tls: record reassembly failed' messages alongside gRPC errors: "received unexpected EOS" and "stream reset by peer".
- Serving node traces show token-generation continued but ACK gaps and retransmissions on TCP level.
- Packet captures (pcap link in comments) show segments being coalesced/large skbs leaving the host and the firewall sending truncated reassembled packets back, with TLS records split differently on egress vs. what the server expects.

Initial hypothesis: The combination of NIC offloads (GRO/GSO/TSO) on the private node and stateful DPI on the corporate edge is causing large aggregated TCP segments to be re-segmented incorrectly by the firewall, which results in TLS record boundary mismatches and reassembly errors at the Redwood side. This triggers gRPC frame parsing errors and stream resets.

Requested by customer: urgent mitigation and recommended permanent remediation; customer is on a private deployment and requires a network-compatible fix or guidance they can apply to their edge appliance.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:45 - FinStrata NW Team: Confirmed that SD-WAN appliance has 'transport offload' and DPI active. They ran tcpdump and uploaded pcap to S3 (s3://support-artifacts/SUP-673918/trace1.pcap).
2026-03-12 11:55 - SRE (internal): Reproduced locally by enabling GSO on a test node and inserting a proxy that performs DPI-like segmentation; observed identical 'tls: short record' errors. Confirmed firewall re-segmentation as root cause in lab.
Captured and analyzed pcap from customer (s3://support-artifacts/SUP-673918/trace1.pcap). Observed egress SKBs with aggregated segments sized > 16KB (typical for enabled GSO).
Firewall shows behavior consistent with DPI that inspects and attempts to re-segment TLS records; returned segments do not preserve original TLS record boundaries causing our TLS stack to see partial records and report 'short record' or 'unexpected EOF'.
Local repro: Enabled GSO on a lab node and placed an inline proxy that performs payload inspection and segmentation. Reproduced gRPC frame errors and TLS reassembly logs matching customer trace.
Experimented with disabling GSO/GRO on the agent (via ethtool -K enp1s0g gso off gro off tso off) — after disabling, TLS reassembly errors disappeared in lab and customer reported immediate relief when they applied same change on their hosts.
Tested alternative mitigations: TCP MSS clamp at SD-WAN edge to 1200-1400 bytes prevented large SKBs from being produced and also resolved reassembly errors; however this requires config change in customer WAN (may impact throughput).
Captured server-side logs: additional handshake latency spikes correlated with packet re-ordering and retransmits; no evidence of server-side CPU resource exhaustion during incidents.
Workaround implemented: Customer disabled NIC aggregation offloads (GSO/GRO/TSO) on private-agent hosts and applied TCP MSS clamp on SD-WAN for egress to Redwood model artifact endpoints; both actions eliminated TLS reassembly errors and gRPC frame drops.
Permanent remediation path: Customer has agreed to schedule firewall firmware update with their vendor to correct DPI re-segmentation behavior. Internally, we will add a Console alert to detect 'tls: short record' and elevated gRPC frame errors and include a KB article that documents network checks and mitigations (disable offloads, MSS clamp, vendor firmware guidance).
Rollout notes and follow-ups:
- Customer to confirm firmware patch date by 2026-03-20 and provide post-patch pcap for verification.
- INT-3245 created for Engineering to add enhanced TLS reassembly logging and an automated detection rule (assigned to runtime team).
- Support will remain in active monitoring for 72 hours post-customer firmware upgrade; set ticket to Waiting on Customer after they confirm patch scheduling.
Final status: mitigation validated in customer environment; awaiting vendor firmware update for permanent fix.
payload.summary: Intermittent TLS reassembly errors and gRPC chunk drops caused by customer edge offload + DPI on private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
After a vendor dock firmware rollout pushed via MDM overnight, multiple Linux workstations (encrypted home with LUKS) failed to complete resume or early boot unlock when attached to the dock. Systems are left at console without the home partition decrypted, preventing user login and halting provisioning/repair workflows.

Impact:
- Affected ~8 devices reported so far across two imaging waves; blocks users from logging in after suspend/resume or cold boot while docked.
- Prevents laptop re-provisioning and kiosk/desk setups that remain docked during imaging cycles.
- Working hours interruption for a small engineering cohort; potential larger rollout if vendor firmware continues.

Environment:
- Corporate laptops (Lenovo X1 Gen11, Dell Precision 5560) running corp-linux-image-2026.02 (systemd 251, cryptsetup 2.5), encrypted home on LUKS2 with systemd-cryptsetup hook in initramfs.
- Dock firmware v2.18.0 pushed via vendor MDM plugin on 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC.
- Region: prod-us-west MDM cohort rollout.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start from laptop fully powered off with disk encrypted.
2) Connect to vendor USB-C dock (firmware v2.18.0 installed).
3) Power on or resume from suspend.
4) System attempts early unlock of LUKS; systemd-cryptsetup fails to find the expected block device path because USB hub topology changed (device numbers shift).
5) Device falls to emergency shell / shows login prompt but home not decrypted; some devices then hit kernel oops during xHCI rebind on resume.

Relevant logs (excerpt):
- journalctl -b -1:
  Mar 09 08:21:12 hostname kernel: usb 1-1.3: new high-speed USB device number 7 using xhci_hcd
  Mar 09 08:21:12 hostname kernel: usb 1-1.3: USB disconnect, device number 6
  Mar 09 08:21:12 hostname systemd[1]: Starting Setup crypttab and LUKS encrypted volumes...
  Mar 09 08:21:13 hostname systemd-cryptsetup[312]: Failed to activate /dev/disk/by-uuid/XXXX-XXXX: device not found
  Mar 09 08:21:13 hostname systemd[1]: cryptsetup@home.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
  Mar 09 08:21:14 hostname kernel: ------------[ cut here ]------------
  Mar 09 08:21:14 hostname kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: Attempted to kill init!

Investigation notes:
- Support validated the correlation between vendor firmware rollout timestamp and first reports.
- Reproduced on a lab X1 running identical corp image when dock firmware v2.18.0 applied. Rolling back dock firmware to v2.16.7 restores expected USB topology and fixes LUKS unlock behavior.
- Hypothesis: firmware introduces a hub re-enumeration behavior during early resume such that expected /dev/disk/by-path or symlinked device nodes used by crypttab/keyscript are transiently unavailable when cryptsetup runs.
- Secondary hypothesis: some kernels see xhci_hcd rebind/race that can escalate to oops on older kernel versions; we saw a kernel panic on one reproduce with stock kernel-5.15-corp.
- Temporary fix validated: undock before suspend/resume or perform cold boot while undocked prevents the failure. Also, a small initramfs hook that probes for the LUKS UUID with a retry loop until timeout allowed successful unlock in lab repro.

Workaround and mitigation applied:
- Immediately paused vendor firmware rollout and flagged MDM cohort. (MDM ticket created with Vendor #VND-2026-17).
- Communication sent to docking fleet: instruct users and desk provisioning teams to undock devices before suspend/resume until fully resolved.
- Provided step-by-step restore: use vendor firmware tool to rollback to v2.16.7; validated with 3 affected devices.
- Pushed a test initramfs with a 10-second retry probe for LUKS UUID to a small subset of devices (imaging lab) as a temporary resilience measure.

Next steps / proposed remediation:
1) Work with vendor to get a firmware build addressing USB re-enumeration race (priority raised with vendor PM).
2) Prepare formal cryptsetup/initramfs change: include a robust wait-and-retry probe for UUIDs (backward-compatible), and land via images repo (MR referenced).
3) Add test case in our imaging CI: boot while docked and resume multiple times to catch regressions.
4) Expand rollback instructions and automation in MDM to auto-detect affected firmware versions and prevent rollout.

Resolution criteria:
- Vendor publishes firmware marked as safe in our test matrix OR our initramfs change prevents device node races consistently across affected kernels.
- Rollout can resume with no further user-impacting reports for 48 hours in the initial cohort.

2026-03-10 10:12 - Support (Aisha Patel): Initial reports from imaging team. Collected three devices and reproduced in lab. Paused vendor rollout and notified MDM.
2026-03-11 09:04 - Eng (Jared Kim): Root-causes look like USB re-enumeration. Confirmed rollback to v2.16.7 fixes. Drafting initramfs probe change for testing.
2026-03-11 14:30 - SRE (Marta Lopez): Observed one kernel panic during repro on kernel-5.15; filing kernel trace request to infra-kernel to capture oops.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 08:55 - Support (Aisha Patel): Deployed initramfs-probe to imaging lab cohort; 6/6 boots with dock attached succeeded. Still blocked for full rollout pending vendor fix and CI test addition.
Workaround deployed (initramfs retry probe) and vendor rollback recommended; awaiting vendor firmware fix and CI test coverage before marking resolved.
payload.summary: Dock firmware topology change prevents LUKS unlock on resume, blocking provisioning and user login

Issue summary:
Request to rotate the long-lived GCP service account keys used by the infra-team CI runners and to grant a narrowly scoped set of IAM permissions to the new service account. Goal is to follow least-privilege principles and satisfy upcoming SOC audit questions about key rotation cadence.

Impact:
- CI pipelines in prod-us-east intermittently fail when keys are changed without coordinated rollout.
- If rotation is not performed, audit will flag a finding for >90-day key lifetime.

Environment:
- Projects: redwood-prod, redwood-staging
- CI runners: infra-ci-runner-1 (prod-us-east), infra-ci-runner-2 (staging-eu-west)

Background and rationale:
- Current service account redwood-ci-sa has an old key created 2025-11-01. Security asked for rotation and evidence of least-privilege mapping.
- Previous rotation (INT-4127) covered cross-project role mappings but did not update CI runner keys.

Requested changes:
1) Create a new service account redwood-ci-sa-v2 in redwood-prod and redwood-staging projects.
2) Bind a minimal custom role (custom role: roles/redwood.ciRunner) with the following permissions:
   - resourcemanager.projects.get
   - storage.objects.get
   - storage.objects.list
   - compute.instances.get (read-only for instance metadata checks)
   - secretmanager.versions.access (only for the specific secret resource)
3) Rotate keys for infra-ci-runner instances by updating the workload identity or replacing long-lived keys depending on infra-team recommendation.
4) Set key expiry and a rotation schedule: 30-day TTL for the key material with documented automation for replacement.

Steps to reproduce / runbook:
- See Confluence runbook linked above. High-level flow: create SA -> create key / configure workload identity -> deploy to CI runner pool -> monitor pipeline success for 24 hours -> revoke old key.

Justification for access:
- The infra team needs read access to project metadata and storage artifacts to run build/test steps. Write permissions are intentionally omitted.

Requestor note:
- Tightly scoped access required for CI; request temporary elevated permissions for the rotation ops only. Expiry requested: 2026-04-10.

Additional notes:
Checked audit logs for redwood-ci-sa: last key usage pattern shows frequent GETs to storage objects between 02:00-05:00 UTC (nightly test runs). Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/query;query=resource.type%3D%22service_account%22
Validated no existing impersonation workflows depend on iam.serviceAccounts.actAs for redwood-ci-sa in staging (scoped check via gcloud iam roles describe).
Verified CI runner AMIs/containers: runners mount secret at /etc/ci/keys/redwood-ci.json (old pattern). Work planned to move to workload identity provider (WIF) to eliminate long-lived keys.
Risk assessment: If we rotate key without updating runners, pipelines will fail. Plan includes deploying new SA + workload identity in staging, running 48-hour verification, then rotating prod key during maintenance window.
Staging: new SA created and workload identity bound; pipelines validated for 24h with no failures. Old key removed from staging mounts. (See PR #1290)
Production: awaiting scheduled 2-hour maintenance window from Release Ops. Post-rollout tasks: revoke old key, record rotation in audit log, update runbook with observed rollback steps.
Follow-up: automate rotation using Cloud Scheduler + Cloud Functions to generate and upload short-lived keys OR migrate all runners to Workload Identity within 30 days. Security to re-evaluate after prod rollout.
payload.summary: GCP service account rotation + least-privilege role grant for infra-team CI runners

payload.description:
Issue summary: After the nightly template-indexer run (v2.9.1) we observed a cascade of detached macro-to-SLA bindings resulting in low-priority cases being routed to default queues instead of the intended escalation paths.

Impact: Approximately 12 routing templates across multiple teams lost their SLA weightings and macro associations. Customers on Dedicated and Private tiers reported longer initial response times for tickets created after the indexer window.

Observed behavior: Indexer job completes successfully in logs but the template binding table (template_bindings_v2) contains stale object IDs; the UI and routing-engine reconcile step mark templates as "orphaned". Automated rollbacks were attempted but the reconciliation task re-applied incorrect macro IDs from an older snapshot.

Expected behavior: Nightly indexer should update template lookup tables without changing macro IDs or SLA weightings. Reconciliation should preserve existing bindings when a clear owner mapping exists.
Customer-facing routing misassignments leading to delayed responses; estimated increase in median TTR (time-to-respond) by ~27% for affected templates during the window. No data loss; primarily operational/regression impact.
1. Trigger nightly template-indexer (simulated with indexer --dry-run omitted) using snapshot from 2026-02-28
2. Observe template_bindings_v2 before job: macros and sla_weights present for templates TPL-100..TPL-112
3. Run indexer v2.9.1 against the snapshot; check logs at /var/log/indexer/2026-03-01.log
4. After job: templates TPL-103, TPL-107, TPL-110 show macro_id=null in DB and UI flags them as Orphaned
5. Routing-engine then falls back to default queue causing misrouted tickets in support ingestion telemetry

2026-03-01 04:00 - Pulled indexer logs: indexer reported successful commit, but post-commit reconciliation logged UID mismatches for 14 entries.
2026-03-01 05:10 - Ran DB diff between pre/post snapshots; macro_id canonicalization step replaced newer GUIDs with legacy GUIDs present in fallback snapshot.
2026-03-02 09:20 - Correlation with deployment: indexer v2.9.1 included a heuristic to dedupe macro objects by name which incorrectly matched macros across namespaces.
2026-03-03 11:05 - Confirmed UI read path shows detached bindings; routing-engine metrics show increased default_queue hits for templates list.
2026-03-04 08:30 - Workaround: paused nightly indexer schedule and queued a manual rebind operation to restore correct macro IDs for affected templates. Manual rebind success rate: 12/12.
2026-03-05 14:00 - Added integration test to catch macro canonicalization regressions; test failing on master reproduces mapping swap.
Support (2026-03-01) - Asha Patel: Customer reports - multiple tickets routed to default queue. Started investigation; escalated to SRE. Linked slack thread #support-indexer.
SRE (2026-03-01) - Marco Ruiz: Initial findings: indexer commit completed but node reconciliation replaced macro GUIDs. Pulling indexer artifacts and DB snapshots for deeper diff.
Eng (2026-03-02) - Priya Desai: Root cause hypothesis: dedupe-by-name heuristic introduced in v2.9.1 incorrectly ignores namespace field; creating PR to add namespace back to comparison key. Refer PR: github.com/redwood-inference/indexer/pull/4510.
Support (2026-03-04) - Claire Nguyen: Workaround applied: paused scheduled indexer and executed manual rebind job ID RB-20260304-1; monitoring routing metrics. Customers notified with temporary expectations.
SRE (2026-03-05) - Marco Ruiz: Manual rebind validated in prod; no further orphans observed after rebind. Leaving ticket open while fix is rolled out and additional tests are merged.
Workaround: nightly indexer schedule paused (2026-03-04) and manual rebind executed to restore macro associations. Root cause identified as namespace-agnostic dedupe heuristic in indexer v2.9.1.

3) Canary: Deploy patched indexer to staging and run a full reindex against the 2026-03-01 snapshot. Monitor template_bindings_v2 diffs (owner: Marco Ruiz) - window 2026-03-07
4) Rollout: Gradual rollout to prod with indexer scheduler re-enabled only after validation (owner: Release Eng) - target 2026-03-09
5) Postmortem & runbook update: Document safe-index migration steps and add automatic pre/post diff validation (owner: Claire Nguyen) - due 2026-03-12

Issue summary:
Customer NoteWave Labs reports that during long-form SSE streams the final paragraphs frequently arrive with stripped trailing punctuation (periods and parentheses) and image markdown links (e.g., ![alt](https://...)) missing after an auth cookie rotation and fast reconnect. This results in corrupted markdown documents and broken image previews in their consumer app.

Impact:
- Several NoteWave production users receive incomplete markdown: sentences end abruptly without closing punctuation and the final image references are dropped.
- Breaks client-side markdown renderer resulting in UI glitches and broken card previews.
- Appears intermittently following auth cookie refresh during long SSE sessions behind the customer's CDN.

Environment:
- prod | us-east-1, customer requests served from our hosted Redwood API cluster on redwood-dedicated-01.
- Affected routes: /v1/streams/generate and chat streaming endpoints.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1. Start a long SSE stream request that outputs markdown with an embedded image near the end.
2. While the stream is active, NoteWave's edge rotates their SSO cookie (short TTL) triggering the client to re-auth and re-open the SSE connection.
3. Client performs an immediate reconnect; upstream CDN uses HTTP/1.1 keepalive and replays a 100-continue probe in front of the handshake.
4. After reconnect completes, the last paragraph is missing trailing punctuation (usually "." or ")") and the markdown image URL is omitted.

Expected behavior:
- Stream should resume or fall back without losing trailing characters or image references. Final tokens and markdown should stitch cleanly.

Observed behavior:
- The stream resumes but the final chunk is missing the terminal characters and the entire markdown image link token sequence. The rest of the output appears intact.

Immediate customer-provided logs (redacted):
- Client-side SSE events show final data chunk as: "...conclusion of thought\n\n![diagram]" (image URL missing)
- Server-side proxied access logs show a timed cookie refresh and a 100-continue preflight from the CDN within 120ms of the reconnect.
- No 5xx from runtime; serving runtime logs show an ACK for last-KV-cache priming followed by a short-lived socket replacement.

Attachments:
- customer_trace_2026-03-09.zip (contains client SSE sequence and server access logs)

Additional notes:
Summary of findings:
- Reproducible when a reconnect happens within 200ms of an auth cookie rotation and when an intermediate CDN sends a 100-continue or idle probe during handshake.
- The streaming runtime's chunk reassembly state machine expects a clearly delimited 'end-of-chunk' marker. During the handshake replay, a small buffered suffix (1-6 bytes) containing punctuation or the tail end of a markdown image token is being classified as 'prelude' and not appended to the prior choice.
- Edge-proxy logs show connection rebinds that reorder control bytes; our parser currently treats an immediate SYN/HTTP1 probe sequence as a boundary and flushes partial token buffers.
- Affected models are token-dense near stream ends (long-form markdown with links) which increases chance of tail bytes alignment.
- No evidence of model truncation or tokenization loss inside the runtime; this is an I/O/assembler issue.
Next steps proposed:
1) Add conservative reassembly window: when a reconnect occurs within X ms of the prior stream tail, retain the last 12 bytes of buffer and attempt to stitch if subsequent resume begins with an open markdown bracket or punctuation. (short-term patch)
2) Harden handshake handling in edge-proxy to avoid treating 100-continue as stream boundary. (medium-term)
3) Add end-to-end test scenario with injected 100-continue / CDN probes to catch regressions.
4) Coordinate with customer to test a canary patch that preserves trailing bytes in stitch path.
Workarounds and fixes in progress:
- Temporary customer workaround: increase SSO cookie TTL for long-run streams (reduces rotation events mid-stream). Customer applied and reported reduction in occurrences to near 0 during test window.
- Engineering hotfix (in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-runtime/pull/410) introduces a 12-byte stitch buffer on reconnect and adds heuristic to merge if next chunk starts with markdown markers or typical trailing punctuation.
- Edge-proxy change (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-gateway/pull/205) updates probe handling so 100-continue is not treated as an SSE boundary.
- Added a regression test to CI that simulates cookie rotation + 100-continue scenario.
Pending:
- Awaiting customer validation in their staging CDN by 2026-03-13. If validation passes, schedule hotfix roll to prod in a limited canary (5% of traffic) with observability flags enabled.
Fix in progress (stitch-buffer patch + proxy probe handling). Customer workaround applied and validated on staging. Pending customer sign-off for prod rollout.
Do not change tokenizer or model weights as this is an I/O boundary case.
Ensure canary includes both redwood-small-13b and open-llama-7b traffic to validate model-agnostic behavior.
payload.summary: SSE handshake stall after auth cookie rotation strips trailing punctuation and image URLs from streamed markdown

Issue summary: After depot repair (Wi-Fi module + SSD replacement) the Lenovo ThinkPad T15 fails to finish corporate provisioning. Intune enrollment stalls at 'Applying Wi-Fi profile' and the provisioning agent exits with a network profile conflict error. Impact: Blocked check-in for two devices returned from depot in the last 48 hours; users cannot complete provisioning and join corp network without manual intervention.
Two devices from depot repair failed provisioning and required helpdesk manual cleanup. Affects internal provisioning SLA for depot returns and delays deskside returns to users.
1) Receive device from depot after Wi-Fi module replacement
2) Run standard depot imaging (autoprov-image-v2) with corporate packages and join steps
3) Boot out-of-the-box and let provisioning agent run (provisioner v1.8)
4) Observe provisioning stall at 'Applying Wi-Fi profile' and agent exit status with "NetworkProfileApplyError: duplicate-profile-id"
2026-03-10T08:32:12Z provisioner[3421]: INFO: Starting network configuration
2026-03-10T08:32:15Z network-manager: ERROR: apply_profile: failed, code=409, message='duplicate-profile-id'
2026-03-10T08:32:15Z intune-client[778]: WARN: Enrollment paused: network profile application failed
netsh wlan show profiles
Profiles on interface Wi-Fi:
Group policy profiles (read only)  : 0
User profiles
-----------------
All User Profile     : Corp-WiFi
All User Profile     : Corp-WiFi-OLD
Helpdesk reproduced failure and captured netsh/profile output showing two profiles for 'Corp-WiFi'.
Depot imaging logs indicate that the post-image script that imports Wi-Fi XML profiles (scripts/wifi-import.sh) ran twice due to an edge-case restart when the WLAN driver enumerated after image completion.
Hypothesis: Replaced Wi-Fi module caused interface name/NetCfgInstanceId to change, triggering the wifi-import script to re-apply an already-present profile under a slightly different identifier resulting in duplicate profile metadata in the Windows WLAN store.
We also observed that if a docking station is attached during first boot the system enumerates an additional virtual interface, and the current depot script does not de-duplicate profiles by SSID, only by GUID, so duplicates were created.
No evidence of DHCP MAC duplication or network-level collision; issue isolated to local WLAN profile store and provisioning agent's strict validation.
Reproduced locally by intentionally interrupting imaging after driver install to force a re-run of wifi-import.sh; observed duplicate profile GUIDs and provisioning failure match.
Related artifact: staging depot image had older wifi-import logic that used netsh wlan add profile filename=... without checking for existing SSID - this was the immediate trigger.
2026-03-09 10:12 - Depot completed hardware swap and pushed device to imaging pool
2026-03-09 11:03 - Imaging completed; device returned to user.
2026-03-10 08:30 - User reported provisioning stalled; ticket opened.
2026-03-11 09:15 - Helpdesk reproduced failure on staging depot machine.
2026-03-12 14:40 - Eng confirmed root cause and deployed depot script change.
2026-03-13 10:30 - Workaround applied to affected devices and provisioning completed.
Workaround: Helpdesk removed duplicate Wi-Fi profiles and re-ran provisioner on affected devices: commands used: 'netsh wlan delete profile name="Corp-WiFi-OLD"' and 'provisioner --enroll'.
Permanent fix: Updated wifi-import.sh in depot image to be idempotent and to clear stale NetCfg registry keys prior to profile import. PR gh/pr/infra/1384 merged and new depot image built (autoprov-image-v2.1).
Follow-up: Added a depot smoke test that verifies Intune enrollment completes within 5 minutes of imaging; updated depot runbook (confluence/redwood/depots/runbooks/wlan-cleanup) with manual steps if failure occurs.
Rollout notes: Image v2.1 deployed to central depot on 2026-03-12; regional depots scheduled for staggered rollout over next 3 days.
Closure: Affected devices were re-provisioned and validated on 2026-03-13. No further incidents reported by end of day
Helpdesk (J. Sullivan) 2026-03-10: User tech reported provisioning stuck on Wi-Fi. Collected logs and moved device back to depot for inspection.
Depot Technician (M. Lee) 2026-03-11: Reimaged device and reproduced issue. Noted 'Corp-WiFi-OLD' lingering in profiles after imaging. Suspect script ran twice post-driver install.
Eng (Diego Martinez) 2026-03-11: Investigating. Will instrument wifi-import.sh to log invocation count and skip if SSID exists.
Eng (Diego Martinez) 2026-03-12: Confirmed repro on staging. Pushed branch gh/pr/infra/1384 to add idempotency and pre-clean step (netsh wlan delete profile name="Corp-WiFi-OLD" /all) plus registry NetCfgInstanceId clear for stale entries.
Helpdesk (Aisha Kaur) 2026-03-13: Applied manual cleanup to the two affected devices (netsh wlan delete profile name="Corp-WiFi-OLD" and re-run provisioner) - enrollment completed and devices joined domain.
Depot Lead (R. Patel) 2026-03-13: Deployed updated depot image with wifi-import idempotency. Added a post-image smoke test to validate Intune enrollment completes before marking as ready.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple engineers report 'permission denied' when attempting to SSH through the internal bastion that uses Okta group-derived RBAC. Impact: ~6 engineers blocked from accessing production debug hosts; scheduled deploy rollback delayed. Environment: prod / us-east.

Observed behavior: After user authenticates via Okta and attempts to assume the 'bastion-access' role through the SSH gateway, the gateway rejects the assume-role call with '403: role not found' and logs show the role mapping lookup returned empty groups for affected users. Affected users are members of the Okta group 'infra-bastion-access' which was created on 2026-03-11.

Expected behavior: New Okta group membership should be provisioned via SCIM within 5 minutes and subsequently mapped to RBAC policies so engineers can assume the bastion role.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Add user to Okta group infra-bastion-access (via Okta UI or API).
2) Attempt SSH to bastion (ssh -J user@bastion prod-host).
3) Observe assume-role failure in ssh-gateway logs and 403 returned to client.

Logs & evidence:
- ssh-gateway: /var/log/ssh-gateway/assume.log shows repeated 'role lookup empty for principal uid=...'.
- SCIM provisioning audit: event scim/2026-03-11/PR-789 shows group created and membership change recorded, but downstream webhook retries exist.
- Okta admin console screenshot attached in original ticket (link not embedded here).

Workarounds attempted:
- Manual RBAC grant (temporary) by infra-admin allowed two engineers immediate access.
- Re-triggered SCIM sync from Okta; sync job logs show HTTP 202 accepted but one downstream consumer returned 504.

Customer impact / business context: Production debug access required for an incident rollback; this is blocking on-call and reducing remediation velocity.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:25 - L1 Support (Sofia R.): Verified inability to assume role for 3 users. Confirmed Okta shows group membership for those users. Escalating to SRE/Identity.
2026-03-12 09:40 - SRE (Maya Lin): Observed SCIM consumer 'rbac-sync' returning 504 to provisioning webhook around 03/11 22:01 UTC. Investigating consumer pod restarts and network timeouts in us-east cluster.
2026-03-13 15:05 - Security (Anika Gomez): Requesting audit log export for membership changes between 2026-03-11 and 2026-03-13 for compliance evidence.
Initial hypothesis: SCIM webhook consumer (rbac-sync) experienced transient network egress failures causing membership deltas to not reach RBAC datastore.
Verified consumer pod restart events around 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC correlate with NAT gateway flaps recorded in VPC flow logs.
Found a long-running schema migration job on rbac-db holding a DDL lock from 2026-03-11 21:45 to 2026-03-12 02:10 which delayed applying membership deltas even after successful delivery.
Combination of transient network 504s + DB migration lock created a backlog and race where newly-created groups were visible in Okta but absent in RBAC mappings for the ssh-gateway.
Reproduction steps validated in staging by simulating Okta group creation while forcing consumer egress failure; observed same role-not-found behavior on ssh-gateway.
Mitigated: reconfigured rbac-sync consumer egress to stable subnet, restarted affected pods, completed migration during low-traffic window, and invalidated ssh-gateway caches. Applied temporary manual grants for immediate unblocking. Postmortem and hardening follow-ups scheduled.
Short-term fix: Manual RBAC entries for affected users (audit path recorded) and ssh-gateway cache invalidation to restore immediate access.
Root cause: Two contributing factors — transient VPC NAT gateway egress failures causing SCIM consumer 504s, and a long-running RBAC DB migration lock delaying membership application.
Permanent fixes: (1) Add retry/backoff and dead-letter handling for SCIM consumer webhooks; (2) Update infra runbook to avoid long-running schema migrations during provisioning events; (3) Add synthetic monitors for SCIM delivery latency and for role-mapping freshness to alert at 5 minutes of drift.
Follow-ups assigned: INT-918770 (config change for consumer egress), INT-918771 (add SCIM telemetry and alerts), INT-918772 (postmortem doc and compliance artifact delivery).
Compliance: Exported membership audit logs attached to this ticket and shared with Security; Security to confirm sufficiency for SOC evidence.
payload.summary: SCIM group provisioning delay prevents SSH bastion role propagation — engineers cannot assume bastion

Issue summary: Several internal engineers report they cannot log in to the feature-flagging console. Login attempts redirect back to Okta and then return a 400 from the auth proxy. Impact: Blocks ~12 engineers from toggling flags and viewing rollout state in prod-us-east. No external customers affected, but a high operational impact for releases planned today.

Observed behaviour: Users authenticate successfully at Okta; after Okta redirect the auth-proxy returns 400 and the console shows 'Login failed'. This began after IdP announced header size enforcement (removing oversized headers) earlier today.

Business impact: P1 – operational runway for a production release is degraded.
1) Open feature-flag console (https://flags.redwood.example) in chrome (incognito recommended).
2) Click 'Sign in with Okta'.
3) Complete Okta MFA flow and allow redirect back to console.
4) Observe auth-proxy returns 400 and console shows generic login failure.
auth-proxy: 400 Bad Request - invalid_request (header_too_large)
browser console: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400 (Bad Request)
2026-03-12T09:12:03Z auth-proxy us-east-1 pod-23: incoming request /auth/callback size 67512 bytes -> rejected: header_too_large
2026-03-12T09:12:03Z auth-proxy us-east-1 pod-23: x-forwarded-for: 10.1.2.3, cookie length: 67000
2026-03-12T09:12:05Z okta-webhook: user john.doe@example.com completed authentication, returned redirect to https://flags.redwood.example/auth/callback?state=...&code=...
2026-03-12T09:12:05Z feature-flag-console us-east-1 pod-4: received 400 from auth-proxy when handling callback
Initial hypothesis: IdP header truncation/enforcement removed or modified a long cookie/header leading to mismatch in auth-proxy parsing logic.
Reproduced in prod-us-east with synthetic user; request headers show a single cookie with long JSON blob used by legacy session glue (pre-prod consolidation).
Auth-proxy recently had nginx upgrade (2026-03-10) which enabled stricter header-size defaults; review of nginx.conf shows client_header_buffer_size and large_client_header_buffers set to default values.
Okta confirmed they rolled out a header-size enforcement change at ~2026-03-12T08:50Z for our tenant (reference OKTA-OPS ticket), which removed duplicate long Set-Cookie header introduced by a legacy tracking middleware.
Workaround discovered: clearing browser cookies for *.redwood.example allows successful login; shorter cookie payloads work.
Maya Thompson (reporter) 2026-03-12: Reported after trying to onboard a release toggling. Noticed several teammates with same symptoms.
Diego Ramirez (assignee) 2026-03-12: Acknowledged, running pod-level captures and nginx error logs. Suspect header size enforcement; starting mitigation plan.
SRE Team 2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation - increase large_client_header_buffers on auth-proxy to accept current cookie sizes, and add server-side normalization to strip legacy tracking cookie.
Security 2026-03-13: Flag - confirm removing/trimming cookies does not leak PII. Confirmed legacy tracking cookie contains no PII but must be redacted before downstream services see it.
Product Eng 2026-03-14: Requested ETA on permanent fix so we can resume scheduled flag flips for release tomorrow.
Mitigation applied: increased nginx large_client_header_buffers in auth-proxy deployment in prod-us-east and deployed a header-normalizer sidecar that strips legacy __rf_track cookie. Workaround for users: clear cookies for .redwood.example. Permanent follow-ups: remove legacy tracking middleware from upstream services (ENG-FF-921), add cookie-length monitoring alert, and coordinate with Okta to revert tenant header enforcement once cleanup is complete. Status: mitigation in place; monitoring for 24h.
payload.summary: Okta SSO fails for feature-flag console after IdP header size enforcement

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Request to build an automated provisioning flow that creates tenant-scoped Slack channel hierarchies (department/team prefixes + subchannel namespace), automatically seeds a corresponding Confluence index page per tenant, wires an approval webhook (Jira) for non-standard channel creates, and enforces retention/archive hooks based on data classification tags.

Why we need this: currently teams create ad-hoc channels and separate Confluence pages with inconsistent metadata. This causes discoverability and audit gaps for regulated projects and increases overhead for Security/Compliance to review retrospective requests. A single automation will standardize naming, policy enforcement, and lifecycle.

Impact: improves discoverability, reduces manual review load on Security by ~40% (estimate), enforces retention for sensitive workspaces, and provides tenants with an explicit claim/ownership flow.

Request details / acceptance criteria:
- A Slack provisioning API that accepts tenant_id, team_owner, data_classification tag (e.g., public/internal/confidential), channel_type template (project, incident, standup), and optionally retention_window.
- On create, provision channel with naming convention: <tenant-prefix>-<team>-<purpose> and set channel topic to include a link to the corresponding Confluence index.
- Automatically create a Confluence index page under /spaces/TENANT-<tenant_id>/Project Index with seeded metadata (owner, tags, lifecycle dates, linked channels).
- If data_classification is confidential or retention_window > 90 days, trigger Jira approval flow (Jira ticket auto-created, approvers list from tenant metadata). Channel remains in a pending state until approve/deny.
- On approve, webhook updates channel state and Confluence index; on deny the channel is archived and requester notified.
- Archival/retention hooks: after lifecycle end date, channel gets archived and Confluence index flagged for review; automatic snapshot exported to audit bucket (S3) for tenant-scoped retention period.
- Audit logs for every provision action emitted to central audit topic (audit-automation).
- Integration tests and runbook (Confluence) documenting the flow and escalation path.

Constraints and non-goals:
- This ticket is only to implement the automation and necessary infra hooks; UI/console changes are out of scope.
- On-prem/private tenant special network/SCIM integration is out of scope for phase 1 (we will add an adapter later).
- API creates channel and Confluence index with correct metadata.
- Jira approvals gate confidential/long-retention creates.
- Archival exports snapshots to tenant-specific S3 location encrypted with KMS.
- Audit logs emitted for every lifecycle event.
- Runbook published and validated by Ops and Security.
1) Review existing slack-provisioner library and identify extension points for tenant scoping and metadata.
2) Add Confluence SDK integration to create seed index pages and populate metadata.
3) Implement Jira approval webhook: create Jira ticket template and approver mapping.
4) Wire retention/archival task producer to audit-automation topic with S3 exporter.
5) Create integration tests in staging: happy path + approve + deny + retention expiry.
6) Draft runbook and Confluence page describing operations and escalation.
7) Security review for audit exports and retention handling.
8) Canary deploy to a single pilot tenant, collect metrics for 2 weeks, then roll out org-wide.
- Create tenant-scoped request via new API with data_classification=public: expect channel created and Confluence index present, no Jira ticket.
- Create with data_classification=confidential: expect Jira ticket created in 'Pending Approval', channel remains in 'pending' state until approved.
- Approve ticket: expect channel activated and audit log emitted.
- Deny ticket: expect channel archived, requester receives notification.
- Set small retention_window=7 days and validate archival job archives channel after lifecycle end and uploads snapshot to S3.
- Verify audit event payloads include tenant_id, requestor, timestamp, and action outcome.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:00 - Platform PM (Evan Brooks): Suggest adding telemetry: provision latency, approval lead time, and number of denied requests. Please add to worklist.
Slack API supports channel creation with topics and purpose fields; we can set topic to include Confluence link. No rate-limit concerns for pilot volume.
Confluence has an API for page creation, but we need to provision a dedicated service account for tenant-scoped spaces. Ops to request space template permissions.
Jira approval flow: reuse existing jira-workflow-bot, add approver group lookup from tenant metadata stored in internal 'tenant-registry' service.
Retention exports: audit-automation currently writes JSON payloads; implement S3 exporter to produce zipped mbox-like message bundle and hash-signed manifest.
Edge case: tenant with >5K channels. For these we should default to a single umbrella index and paginate child entries to avoid Confluence page bloom.
Risks: accidental mis-tagging could cause data to be exported with wrong retention; mitigate with a pre-approval validation and a manual review step for flagged changes.
TBD - Implementation and pilot pending. Security review must pass before production roll-out. Runbook and telemetry required prior to org-wide enablement.
payload.summary: Provision tenant-scoped Slack hierarchy + Confluence indexer with approval webhook and retention hooks

Issue summary: Developer requested delegated Admin access to feature-flag control path via internal Console. After a recent manager change (manager transfer in HR system), the approval workflow for the delegated access request did not progress and remains 'Pending approval' with no visible approver. 2026-03-12T09:14:25Z SCIM-SYNC INFO processed PATCH /Users/usr_94821 {manager: mgr_55012} status=200
2026-03-12T09:15:03Z NOTIF-WORKER WARN delivery-failed: no-recipient found for approverId=mgr_55012 requestId=req_77e5

4) Add end-to-end integration test that simulates SCIM manager transfer during a pending approval.

payload.description:
Issue summary: New Surface Pro 9 units provisioned through the corporate SCCM imaging pipeline arrive with screen rotation stuck in portrait and system reports no accelerometer device. Impact: Users cannot auto-rotate display or use orientation-aware apps. Repro rate: 6/12 devices in recent batch.
Initial reporter noticed after applying standard Windows 11 image with DriverCatalog v4. Steps and logs attached below.
Boot Surface Pro 9 from USB boot media running SCCM task sequence
Apply corporate Windows 11 22H2 image with default driver package 'Corp-Drivers-2026-02'
Complete autopilot/azuread join and install company apps
Reboot and check Device Manager > Sensors
Attempt to rotate screen using orientation setting and notify double-tap to trigger sensor
System event 03-01T10:22:44: SensorCollectionService failed to enumerate sensors: 0x57
DriverInstaller 03-01T10:23:10: 'IMU_HID' driver install returned SUCCESS but no sensor presence
ACPI 03-01T10:23:12: BIOS reported sensor table absent (ACPI: SNC0 not found)
SCCM task sequence log smsts.log shows driver package applied from DP01 without errors

Additional notes:
2026-03-03 14:05 - SRE (Riley Chen): Saw similar reports on #endpoint-ops. Suggested test: imaging with latest BIOS v1.0.16 and driver package Corp-Drivers-2026-03.
Hypothesis: Recent BIOS firmware (1.0.14) on Surface Pro 9 does not expose ACPI sensor table required for IMU enumeration; later BIOS 1.0.16 restores table.
Reproduced on lab unit by imaging with 2026-02 driver package and BIOS 1.0.14; accelerometer missing in Device Manager > Sensors.
Manual driver install sequence: pnputil /add-driver <imu.inf> /install — driver shows, but ACPI table missing causes device to disappear after reboot.
Tested imaging with BIOS 1.0.16 + Corp-Drivers-2026-03: IMU and Inclinometer persist across reboots. No kernel errors in event log.
Checked SCCM DP and driver package manifest; Corp-Drivers-2026-02 did not include vendor firmware shim that coordinates with BIOS 1.0.16. Recommended to pin BIOS version in provisioning pipeline and include firmware shim in driver package.
Applied workaround: created SCCM hotfix task sequence that applies BIOS 1.0.16 followed by Corp-Drivers-2026-03 driver package. Deployed to affected batch (6 devices) and verified sensor enumeration and rotation on all. Root cause: regression introduced by earlier BIOS that hid ACPI sensor table; fix requires BIOS update and updated driver package. Follow-up actions: 1) Update golden image to include BIOS 1.0.16 and Corp-Drivers-2026-03 (see INT-18390). 2) Add sensor enumeration check to provisioning validation automation. 3) Notify procurement to avoid shipping units with 1.0.14 BIOS. Postmortem to be added to Confluence.
payload.summary: Surface Pro 9 accelerometer not initializing after SCCM image; rotation locked

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple engineers report 403/Access Denied when opening the Feature Flag Console after a recent Okta SCIM change that normalized usernames to lowercase. Impact: ~12 internal users (engineering and product) cannot access the feature-flag console to review and toggle flags; blocking several onboardings and a small internal experiment rollout. Environment: production console behind SSO via Okta + SCIM-based provisioning. First seen 2026-03-10 08:15 UTC after SCIM change deployed 2026-03-10 07:45 UTC. Expected: users provisioned via SCIM (case-insensitive username match) should inherit RBAC roles and access console. Observed: RBAC lookup fails due to mismatch between stored console principal (TitleCase userPrincipalName) and new SCIM username (lowercase), leading the console to evaluate the user as "unknown" and return 403. No group membership changes reported in Okta.
1) Provision or update an Okta user record with a username change that only differs by case (e.g., Aisha.Kapoor@redwood.com -> aisha.kapoor@redwood.com)
2) Wait for SCIM sync window (or trigger manual sync)
3) Login to console via Okta SSO
4) Attempt to navigate to /console/feature-flags or open the feature flag UI
5) Observe 403 and 'Access Denied' modal.
Note: reproduces reliably when the console principal record still references the older-cased identity.
Initial triage by Support (Luis) confirmed error path in console auth logs pointing to RBAC lookup failure: 'principal lookup no-match: username="aisha.kapoor@redwood.com" expected="Aisha.Kapoor@redwood.com"'. SCIM provisioner logs (provisioner-02) show successful PATCH that normalized userPrincipalName to lower case at 2026-03-10T07:44:12Z. Console's RBAC cache retains the old principal key and does strict string equality when resolving identities. We confirmed at least 12 principals in the console DB with mixed-case stored usernames; SCIM syncs now produce lowercase. Hypothesis: SCIM normalizer change intended to enforce lowercase broke backward compatibility with console RBAC keying. No ACL/group changes were observed in Okta. Session tokens created before the change remain valid but new sessions are evaluated against new SCIM usernames and denied. Logs referenced: auth-console-prod.log lines 4782-4800 (attached), provisioner-02.log lines 213-218. Related PR that changed normalizer: provisioner PR #412.

Additional notes:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-12): one-off backfill script updated 12 affected console principal records to normalized lowercase username; users regained access. Longer-term fixes: (1) Console change to perform case-insensitive identity resolution and record a canonical username on first login (PR #589 pending review). (2) Update SCIM provisioner to publish canonical_username attribute and add a migration runbook. Follow-up items created: INT-64200 (RBAC canonical key migration plan), provisioner PR #412 closed and replaced with #421 to include canonical attribute. No customer-facing impact.
- Add automated reconciliation job to run daily for 30 days to catch mismatches. - Update RBAC layer to accept case-insensitive lookups and persist canonical_username. - Add integration test for SCIM normalization behavior. - Communicate change in internal release notes and IAM changelog. Assigned owners: Marcos (Console), Priya (IAM), Luis (Support).
Admin can run temporary backfill script (internal-only) to rewrite console principal keys to lowercase for specific users. Support executed this for the 12 affected users and validated access. Steps and script are documented in the linked runbook.
This ticket is internal; prioritize the RBAC canonical key fix ahead of the next SCIM deployment. Consider a short freeze on additional SCIM normalizer changes until migration path is in place.
payload.summary: Feature Flag Console access broken after SCIM username casing change causing RBAC lookup fail

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Users roaming between the corporate SSID and a partner-managed SSID (same ESSID in some locations) intermittently lose connectivity to internal HTTP and gRPC services. The WireGuard session remains in the 'established' state on the client and peer, but packets to specific internal subnets are not forwarded (blackholed) until a manual network toggle or agent restart.

Impact:
- Multiple engineers in the San Francisco office report frequent timeouts to internal services after roaming (laptop moves between APs or from corp-ssid to partner-ssid and back).
- Breaks deployments, CI jobs that depend on internal artifact store, and interactive dev/debug sessions.
- Affects macOS and some Linux laptops with the zero-trust agent installed; mobile devices less affected.

Environment:
- Zero-trust agent: zt-agent v1.8.3 (autoupdate enabled)
- WireGuard kernel module + userland wg-quick 0.0.202601
- macOS 13.5 and Ubuntu 22.04 clients observed
- Office APs: vendor-managed partner network with VLAN trunking; corporate APs run Aruba 8.x
- Internal services on 10.10.0.0/16 and 10.20.0.0/24 (routed via WG peer on 198.51.100.1)

Steps to reproduce (observed consistently for repro):
1) Connect laptop to corporate SSID (corp-ssid). Zero-trust agent establishes WireGuard tunnel to peer (wg0). Internal services accessible.
2) Walk to area overlapped by partner-managed SSID that shares the same ESSID string and roam onto a partner AP (client OS reports 'roamed').
3) Agent shows WG session still established. Services time out.
4) Run simple network tests (ping to internal-ip) — no response.
5) Toggling Wi-Fi off/on OR restarting zt-agent restores connectivity immediately.

Observed behavior and quick diagnostics:
- "wg show" on client shows handshake and latest handshake timestamps (no tunnel rekey required).
- "ip route" shows correct routes for internal subnets bound to wg0, but packets to 10.10.x.x accumulate in tx queue on wg0 and never get seen on the peer (tcpdump on client shows outgoing packets, tcpdump on peer shows none).
- ARP/ND cache on office switch shows MAC of client associated with previous AP/gateway for a short time after roam.
- Kernel route metric on macOS remains pointing at the older interface for a fraction of a second; during that window, the zero-trust agent does not rebind the socket to the new source interface until it receives an interface-change event (event sometimes missed when AP disassociation is 'soft' with fast BSS transition).
- DNS lookups sometimes succeed (cached), but when DNS TTL expires, queries fail because agent-level DNS proxy can't reach upstream due to same blackhole.

Logs snippets (sanitized):
- client zt-agent log: "[net] interface-change event dropped: race with roaming; deferred rebind"
- server wg peer log: "handshake OK from peer id=...; allowed IPs 10.10.0.0/16"
- kernel dmesg (client): "wireguard: wg0: tx-queue full for dst 198.51.100.1"

Investigation notes / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis 1: Partner AP's client isolation + ARP suppression causes switch to forward client traffic to wrong uplink for a short window; since WG packes originate from wg0 but link-layer mapping is stale, peer never sees packets.
- Hypothesis 2: Zero-trust agent relies on reliable OS interface-change events to rebind sockets; on fast/soft roam the event is dropped and socket keeps using stale binding until agent restart or Wi-Fi toggle.
- Hypothesis 3: Some APs rewrite source VLAN tagging on roam; client kernel keeps route bound to old egress and kernel-level source-based routing mismatch causes blackhole.

Tests performed so far:
- Reproduced with macOS using controlled roam (AP steering), capture shows client tx but peer sees none.
- Enabling agent debug logs increases event delivery frequency and reduces but does not eliminate races.
- Forcing wg persistent-keepalive to 15s did not change symptoms (handshake still present).
- Flushing ARP/ND on switch clears blackhole immediately in reproducible case.

Temporary workaround applied to affected users:
- Instructed users to toggle Wi-Fi off/on or restart zt-agent when they hit the issue.
- ITPOps temporarily deployed a DHCP option change on corporate APs to avoid VLAN rewrite on roam in a small test area where partner APs overlap.

Resolution plan / next steps:
1) Short-term (P0 mitigation): ship a zt-agent patch that aggressively rebinds sockets on any transient interface-change signal (w/ a 200ms debounce) and expose an end-user command to force rebind without full restart. Target: 2026-03-15 rollout to office Canary group.
2) Medium-term: add explicit ARP/ND probe after rebind to accelerate kernel path refresh and fall back to toggling the device if probe fails.
3) Network-side: coordinate with partner-managed AP team to disable AP-level ARP suppression for corporate VLANs in overlapping spaces; if not possible, ensure consistent VLAN tagging on roam.
4) Long-term: enhance agent to watch for tx-queue/backpressure signals and proactively rebind or force route refresh; add telemetry to detect dropped interface-change events.

Acceptance criteria for closure:
- Repro rate in Canary drops to 0% over 48h under identical roam tests.
- No more manual agent restarts required for affected users in pilot zones.
- Post-fix monitoring added to detect similar blackholes automatically.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 14:45 - NetEng (A. Kim): Saw ARP entry stickiness on the access switch in overlapping zone. Confirmed partner AP is doing aggressive client isolation.
payload.summary: Intermittent blackhole to internal services after roaming between corp and partner SSIDs; WireGuard session stays up

Issue summary: We need a delegated channel-claim workflow in Slack that allows pod leads to claim ownership of unclaimed channels, ties channel metadata to a Confluence project page, and enforces automated guards for external collaborators. Impact: Without this flow, stale channels remain unowned, external invites bypass review, and auditability is weak for compliance. Request: Implement a Slack provisioning flow + bot command /claim-channel that triggers a lightweight approval (pod lead or delegated approver), writes metadata to a Confluence template page, and applies channel-level restrictions for external guests until an approval is recorded. Background: Several pods requested a streamlined way to take ownership of legacy channels created by experiments. Security flagged a recurring gap where external guests were occasionally added to channels without a documented justification. The proposed flow reduces manual ticket churn and centralizes audit artifacts.
1) User runs /claim-channel in a channel. 2) Bot posts ephemeral form: proposed owner, purpose, retention window, external-collab needed (yes/no), linked Confluence doc title. 3) If external-collab=yes, bot requires a delegated approver to ACK; if no approver available, channel is marked 'quarantine' (restricted posting) and Ops notified. 4) On approval, bot sets channel topic with standardized metadata stub and creates a Confluence page from the 'Channel Owner' template with links and retention policy. 5) Channel ownership is recorded in the centralized Jira space for operations reference.
/claim-channel slash command deploys to prod and accepts owner, purpose, external-collab flag, and Confluence title
Bot posts approval request to designated approver group and enforces 48h TTL for approvals
Channels requiring external access are put into restricted mode until approval is completed
Successful creation or update of a Confluence page from the 'Channel Owner' template with a permal link
Record created in the internal Jira operations tracker with link back to Confluence and slack channel
Audit log entries emitted to the central audit export pipeline for every claim action
Provision Slack app scopes: commands, channels:write, users:read, chat:write:bot, admin.conversations:write (if available)
Add new approver group 'channel-claims-approvers' and seed with pod leads
Create Confluence template 'Channel Owner' in /spaces/OPS/Pages and grant bot account edit rights
Deploy Lambda (or internal function) to handle slash command and approvals; wire to existing audit export webhook
Run rollout in canary org unit (research-pods) for 48 hours, collect metrics on claims and quarantines
If metrics stable, schedule org-wide rollout and add to on-call rotations for support

Additional notes:

Audit export currently logs admin actions; claim events will need a new event type 'channel_claim' — add mapping in audit exporter.
Confluence API requires bot user with space-level edit permission; current service account has read-only in OPS space — request change submitted via INT-151002.
Potential gap: admin.conversations scope requires workspace admin approval; scheduled for security review meeting 2026-03-15.
PoC built and validated in staging (slash command, approval ping, Confluence page creation).

Next steps assigned: Marco to file admin scope change ticket with workspace admins; Aisha to coordinate canary schedule with research pod owners.

payload.description:
New hires and contractor accounts created via SCIM are not triggering the configured approver chain in the internal Access Request UI. The UI reports "No approvers configured" despite group->approver mapping present in RBAC rules. Affects onboarding for multiple teams; manual approvals required.
Blocking: new users cannot be auto-routed to their approvers. Multiple onboarding flows stalled across infra and analytics teams (estimated ~12 users in last 24h). Increases manual work for Identity team and delays project access.
1) Create user in Okta with onboarding profile (manager populated as LDAP DN) using SCIM provisioner.
2) Wait for SCIM sync to create user in Redwood identity service.
3) Open Access Request UI for any resource that relies on manager-approver workflow.
4) Observe UI message: 'No approvers configured' and request cannot be submitted to approver chain.
Access Request UI fails to resolve approver list when user.profile.manager contains an LDAP-style DN (e.g., 'cn=Jane Doe,ou=People,dc=example,dc=com'). The identity service lookup returns 0 approvers and logs show a failing attribute normalization step.
Manager attribute should be normalized to a canonical Okta user id/email during SCIM processing and mapped to the approver policy. Access Request UI should show approver(s) and route approval requests automatically.
Identity-service logs (2026-03-13T14:22:11Z): ERROR scim-provisioner: failed to map manager attribute 'cn=Jane Doe,ou=People,dc=example,dc=com' -> user lookup returned 0 results.
Approver-service logs (2026-03-13T14:22:12Z): WARN approver-resolver: empty candidate set for user id 'okta|null'
Okta System Log event: /api/v1/apps/SCIM/provision - 200 (user created) (link: https://okta.example/logs/ev/0oab12CD)
- Hypothesis 1: Recent SCIM mapping change introduced by PR #382 normalized 'manager' to raw LDAP DN instead of Okta user id.
- Hypothesis 2: Approver resolver service expects an email or Okta uid; receiving DN causes lookups to miss.
- Query run against identity DB shows 12 users created in last 24h where manager attribute contains 'cn=' pattern.
- Checked Git history: identity/scim/mappings.js modified in commit 'fc9a8b' (linked PR below).
- Reproduced locally by creating a SCIM stub with manager=DN; identity-service failed to resolve manager -> approver mapping.
- SRE confirms no infra failures (no 5xx spikes). This is mapping / normalization logic bug.
SCIM mapping change deployed 2026-03-12 replaced manager normalization rule. Instead of extracting Okta user id/email, the provisioner now stores the raw LDAP DN string. Approver resolver code does an exact match on email/uid and therefore finds zero approvers.
Identity team can manually create a 'canonical_manager' attribute on affected user records by using the admin console to point manager to the Okta user id. Manual approvals via admin path enabled: identity-admin -> Requests -> Approve. Onboarding team notified to perform manual routing until fix merges.
1) Revert mapping change and reintroduce manager normalization (extract okta:userId or email) - PR #388 to be merged.
2) Add a defensive fallback in approver-resolver: attempt DN->email lookup using LDAP adapter, log telemetry if fallback used.
3) Backfill: script to scan users created 2026-03-12..2026-03-14 with 'cn=' in manager and populate canonical_manager.
4) Add unit/integration tests for SCIM manager mappings and end-to-end approver resolution.
5) Post-deploy: monitor Access Request success rate and Okta event logs for manager mapping errors for 72 hours.
(pending) workaround in place (manual approvals) and PR #388 under review. Backfill script prepared and awaiting run approval. No permanent fix deployed yet.

- Add regression tests to CI (assigned: identity-eng).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers upgrading Redwood Private 2.8.0 -> 2.9.0 can enter an infinite rollback retry loop. UI shows "Rollback in progress" and never completes.

Impact:
- Upgrade/rollback does not converge; customer cluster remains in degraded state.
- Support load + customer trust risk.

Environment:
- Private installer 2.9.0
- Kubernetes (various), observed in us-east + eu-west

Suspected root cause:
Rollback cleanup hook exits before clearing rollback lock (ConfigMap `installer-rollback-lock`), causing controller to retry indefinitely.

Workaround (customer-safe):
1) Confirm namespace `redwood-private`
2) `kubectl -n redwood-private delete cm installer-rollback-lock`
3) `kubectl -n redwood-private rollout restart deploy/installer-controller`

Acceptance criteria / fix:
- Always best-effort clear lock
- Add TTL + loop detection to stop retries and surface actionable status
- Add metric + alert when rollback retries >3 in 10m

Comments:

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Support Portal approval attempts return 403 when the user's SSO assertion does not include a phoneNumber claim. The approval microservice validates an 'auth_level' decision which currently depends on the presence of a phoneNumber (SMS MFA) claim produced by Okta for some users. Impact:
- On-call and support engineers cannot approve access requests for a subset of employees (mostly those with MFA via Okta Push only).
- Affected flows: Support Portal -> approval-webhook -> approval-microservice -> RBAC grant.
Environment: production, us-east region.
Observed: Approver clicks Approve -> UI shows "Approval failed (403)" -> Support Portal logs show 403 from approval-microservice: "insufficient_auth - missing phone claim". Not all users are affected; those with Okta SMS enrollment produce the phoneNumber claim and succeed.
Expected: Approval should succeed for users who meet MFA policy (Okta Push or SMS), or at minimum the microservice should evaluate 'amr' (authentication methods) rather than relying on phoneNumber claim which is inconsistently emitted.
