Issue summary: Finance has reported a token billing discrepancy for Acme Analytics (enterprise customer). We need a timeboxed, access-controlled join between billing token events and a hashed-identifier slice of inference traces to confirm whether tokens billed map to customer sessions. Impact: potential under/overbilling affecting invoice for month M-1. Request: short-lived query that joins billing.transactions (token counts) to inference.request_traces using a salted SHA256 hashed customer_id (salted per-request to avoid exposing raw identifiers). Purpose is reconciliation only; no raw PII may leave the secure environment.

Requested by: Finance (Elena Ruiz). Business urgency: must resolve before next billing cut (2026-03-18).
1) Finance observed an unexpected +18% token delta vs expected from usage dashboard for account Acme Analytics for billing period 2026-02.
2) On dashboard: open Billing -> Account usage -> select Acme Analytics -> date range 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28.
3) Drilldown shows token_total != sum(per-route tokens) for the account.
4) Proposed repro: run a deterministic join between billing.transactions (token_count, billing_event_id, hashed_customer_id) and a redacted subset of inference.request_traces (request_id, hashed_customer_id, model_id, timestamp, token_count) for the same period.
Note: The hashed_customer_id field already exists in billing and can be derived in traces via salt from request metadata; we will not expose raw customer_id in exports.
[billing-service][2026-02-28T23:59:03Z] account=acme-analytics hashed_customer_id=3f2a... token_count=134872
[trace-service][2026-02-28T23:59:05Z] request_id=rtx-7a9b hashed_customer_id=3f2a... model=redwood-rlhf-v2 token_count=134872
(Example lines; full slice required for reconciliation.)
Maya Chen (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Finance submitted a formal ticket. Attaching signed data-handling attestation from Finance and Acme (doc link). Requesting SRE/Privacy approval for timeboxed join and export of aggregated reconciliation CSV (hashed_customer_id, billing_event_id, billing_tokens, trace_request_id, trace_tokens, model_id, timestamp).
Omar Singh (Assignee) - 2026-03-10: Acknowledge. We need Privacy sign-off and an access plan describing minimal fields, retention, and where the export will be stored. Marking for review by Privacy and Legal.
Priya Kapoor (Privacy) - 2026-03-11: Preliminary OK if: (1) salt used to hash IDs is managed by KMS and not exported, (2) CSV contains no raw identifiers or free-text prompts, (3) export stored in secure internal bucket with 7-day TTL, (4) access limited to named Finance members. Please provide query and ACLs.
Elena Ruiz (Finance) - 2026-03-11: Finance confirms only the three named users (Elena, Raj, and Tammy) need access. They accept 7-day TTL. We will not attempt re-identification.
SRE Team Lead (Jamal Ortiz) - 2026-03-12: Technical note: we can create a read-only, time-limited view in prod analytics that performs the join and writes to s3://redwood-temp/billing-recon/INT-772559/. We'll require an execution runbook and an automated deletion job. Requesting final Legal sign-off before execution.
Hypothesis: A routing fallback caused some requests to be served by a fallback model variant with different prompt-token accounting, creating a mismatch between billing aggregator and per-route counters. To validate: (a) verify hashed_customer_id join returns 1:1 mapping across billing events and traces; (b) compare token_count per matched pair; (c) surface any unmatched billing events. Data minimization: limit trace slice to date window 2026-02-01..2026-02-28, models listed, and only fields necessary for reconciliation. Salt rotation: use KMS key rk-prod-001; salt value not to be exported. Queries will be run from a bastion job with no interactive SSH and audited execution logs.
PENDING - awaiting Legal sign-off (requested 2026-03-12). Once Legal approves, SRE will run the join in a read-only view and produce a minimal aggregated CSV. After validation with Finance, SRE will verify deletion and publish an exec note to Confluence. If discrepancy confirmed, Finance will issue invoice adjustment and CS will notify Acme. No raw prompts or customer_id values will be exported. Full audit trail will be retained in audit-log index for 90 days.
Legal sign-off on export and attestation (owner: Legal)
Create time-limited prod read-only view and scheduled deletion (owner: SRE)
Prepare runbook for execution and logging (owner: SRE)
Run join and deliver reconciliation CSV to named Finance users (owner: SRE/Finance)
Confirm deletion and add exec note to confluence (owner: Omar Singh)

Issue summary: ParcelFlow reports that WebSocket streams for long chat responses consistently terminate after approximately 55–70 seconds into a response. This started after a rollout on 2026-03-10. Impact: Multiple users see truncated replies mid-generation causing failed UX and token re-requests. Affects a small subset of long-response use cases on the customer's dedicated GPU pool. Environment: prod-us-east, customer Dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-pool-74), requests use WebSocket transport with keepalive pings enabled by client. Observed behavior: Stream connection drops with TCP FIN from load balancer and client sees "connection closed" without an explicit 5xx. Expected behavior: Long-running generation streams should stay open until generation completes (several minutes for >2k-token outputs).
1) Use ParcelFlow account on dedicated pool ded-pool-74
2) Open WebSocket to /v1/chat/stream endpoint (w/ Authorization header)
3) Send a prompt that yields long multi-part response (>= 1500 tokens) using redwood-xlarge-7B with streaming enabled
4) Observe disconnect consistently at ~60 seconds into generation (repro rate ~85% for long outputs)
2026-03-12T14:02:11Z stream-start req_id=rc-9a3f5 client_ip=18.205.12.34
2026-03-12T14:03:13Z keepalive-ping recv from client; last-chunk-sent=00:00:59
2026-03-12T14:03:14Z nlb-idle-timeout-close target=streaming-proxy connection-closed-by=nlb
proxy-trace: downstream FIN observed -> upstream half-close not propagated; worker still generating
Initial hypothesis: NLB idle timeout (60s) closing the connection when traffic pattern has quiet periods between token flushes.
Checked proxy metrics: streaming-proxy shows correct keepalive forwarding for HTTP/1.1 chunk flushes but NLB reports idle-termination around 60s for these connections.
Observed that adaptive-batching-v2 introduced an extra internal buffer step that delays the first token flush for very long-context workloads, creating a quiet window longer than NLB timeout.
Ded-pool worker logs show generation continues after downstream FIN, but SDK/client sees closed socket causing retry logic and duplicate prompt submissions.
No 5xx from serving-runtime; kernel preemption spikes were low. GPU worker remained allocated and reported steady throughput.
Related: SUP-332110 notes a websocket fragmentation hang in a different customer environment; cross-referenced for proxy tracing patterns.
Mitigation deployed 2026-03-12 16:20Z: increased NLB idle timeout from 60s -> 300s for ded-pool-74 load balancer (config change: infra/prod/nlb/ded-pool-74.yml #PR 667)
Temporary rollback: disabled adaptive-batching-v2 for ParcelFlow routing rule (feature-flag: adaptive-batching-v2=off for customer id cf-4091)
Observed after mitigation: repro rate dropped to ~5% for same prompts. Customer confirmed major UX flows functional.
Follow-up actions: hardening task assigned to SRE/Runtime teams to ensure token-flush heartbeat is guaranteed within 30s (INT task created), and review default NLB timeout assumptions for dedicated pools. See linked PRs and runbook updates.
Status: mitigated; root cause analysis in progress and assigned to Eng (runtime + infra) for permanent fix.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12T15:05: Logged initial ticket after CS call with ParcelFlow; included sample request IDs and reproduction steps.
ParcelFlow (Emily Rivera) 2026-03-12T15:18: Customer confirms failures happen in production, provided example conversation id cf-4091-conv-77 and consent to prod traces.
SRE (Arjun Patel) 2026-03-12T15:45: Observed NLB idle timeout closes around 60s; pushing to increase idle timeout as short-term mitigation.
Runtime (Dina Kaur) 2026-03-12T16:05: Noted adaptive-batching-v2 introduces a buffer delay for long-context that can create >60s quiet windows between chunk flushes. Recommending disabling for this customer until fix.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12T16:30: Mitigation applied (NLB timeout increased); customer asked for monitoring window and confirmation when risk is acceptable.
ParcelFlow (Emily Rivera) 2026-03-12T17:02: Customer reports immediate improvement; a single manual repro succeeded end-to-end without disconnect.
SRE (Arjun Patel) 2026-03-12T18:00: Creating INT ticket for default NLB timeout audit and scheduling a joint runtime+infra RCA for 2026-03-15.
payload.summary: WebSocket stream terminates after ~60s during long multi-part responses on Dedicated pool

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We need to consolidate multiple team-level JetBrains subscriptions into a centrally managed pool of floating 'All Products Pack' licenses and create a short-term contractor seat pool. This will reduce duplicate spend, simplify renewals, and provide fast on/off boarding for contractors and short-term hires.

Background and request:
- Request procurement of 120 JetBrains All Products Pack floating seats managed by a central JetBrains License Server (self-hosted) or equivalent enterprise offering.
- Create a time-limited contractor pool of 20 seats reserved for the next 6 months. Contractors should be able to be assigned seats by IT within 2 hours of request.

3) 20 contractor seats reserved and a documented quick-request flow for IT to allocate/deallocate within 2 hours.

Estimated cost and billing:

Stakeholders:
- Requesting: SDK Team (Liaison: Priya Nair)

3) Legal to review licensing terms.

comments: 2026-02-28T02:18:00Z Support Intake: Initial ticket created after alerting on 12 failed cron runs. Notified #infra-ops and #platform-auth.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
- On 2026-02-28 ~01:10 UTC, multiple nightly model-evals cron jobs (model-eval-pipeline) failed to start; investigation shows the service account refresh token used by the scheduler returned invalid_grant.

Impact:
- Nightly evaluation and validation runs did not complete for ~6 hours (primary impact: model quality dashboards stale; secondary: delayed nightly cost reports).
- Approximately 12 scheduled jobs in prod us-east failed and retried until exhaustion.

Environment:
- Production cluster (k8s), us-east region.
- Scheduler: kubernetes CronJob invoking eval-runner service which requests a refreshed access token from identity-broker via Okta refresh token flow.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) CronJob triggers eval-runner pod.
2) Eval-runner calls identity-broker /oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token and service-account refresh token.
3) Identity-broker calls Okta token endpoint; Okta responds 400 invalid_grant and revokes refresh token.
4) Eval-runner fails and exits; scheduler marks job failed.

Observed behavior:
- Okta token endpoint returns HTTP 400 with body: {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"The refresh token is invalid or has been revoked"}.
- No prior token rotation event recorded in platform key-rotation logs.

Expected behavior:
- Service account refresh tokens used by scheduled jobs should remain valid for rotation window or be automatically rotated by our token broker without causing job failures.

Initial hypothesis:
- A recent Okta Conditional Access policy enforcement (device trust) was tightened and inadvertently targeted the OU or client used by service account tokens, triggering revocation of refresh tokens for non-interactive sessions.

Telemetry and logs (excerpt):
- identity-broker logs (2026-02-28T01:09:58Z): "refresh token exchange failed: invalid_grant, okta error: token revoked by policy"
- scheduler logs (job eval-20260228-01): "Failed to obtain access token, retry count 0, aborting"
- Okta audit (admin): policy change id=pol-2026-02-27-7 by admin.carol -> enforced device_trust=true for group '/Services/NonInteractive'

Additional notes:
2026-02-28 03:05 - Marco H.: Started triage. Confirmed identity-broker received 400 invalid_grant from Okta. Pulling Okta audit logs next.
2026-02-28 03:40 - Lina S. (SRE): Observed the same pattern on two other non-eval cronjobs (backup-prune, billing-usage). Possibly broad impact to non-interactive service accounts.
2026-02-28 04:05 - Marco H.: Found Okta admin change: policy pol-2026-02-27-7 enabled device_trust and applied to group '/Services/NonInteractive' at 2026-02-27T23:57Z. Reached out to Identity team to request rollback or exception.
2026-02-28 06:00 - Marco H.: Revert applied. Running a full retry of queued cron jobs. 10/12 jobs completed successfully after revert; 2 require manual rerun due to retry exhaustion—requeued.
2026-03-02 14:12 - Marco H.: Implemented emergency workaround doc and scheduled follow-up epic to migrate eval-runner to new token-broker flow. Assigned owners and timeline in linked Confluence.
2026-03-02 16:00 - Aisha P.: Customer-facing alert not required (internal-only). Closing impact window. Keeping ticket open until migration is complete.
Okta audit proves root cause: policy pol-2026-02-27-7 incorrectly matched '/Services/NonInteractive' and revoked refresh tokens for that group.

Issue summary: A recent internal access request for the 'runbooks-v2' tool is showing as APPROVED in the approval queue, but the provisioning pipeline did not create the corresponding RBAC role bindings or service tokens. Impact: impacted users cannot access runbooks-v2 dashboards or runbook actions; several oncall requests are blocked. This appears to affect only the new onboarding flow that uses the lifecycle-sync lambda rather than the legacy backfill.
3 engineers (including oncall) blocked from runbooks-v2; workflow escalations piling up; potential oncall delays
1) Submit access request for runbooks-v2 via internal access UI
2) Approve request through manager approval step (approver receives notification and clicks approve),
3) Observe approval status turns to APPROVED in queue,
4) Verify that no role binding appears in rbac-service and no service token is issued in vault-provisioner
5) Attempt to access runbooks-v2 -> receive 403 / entitlement missing
approval-queue: request_id=ac-20260310-77 status=APPROVED timestamp=2026-03-10T14:12:08Z
lifecycle-sync lambda: invocation for request_id=ac-20260310-77 ended with exit code 0 but no operations logged to rbac-service (logs show early return path)
rbac-service: no binding created for subject user: ava.chen@redwood.ai within window 2026-03-10T14:12Z - 2026-03-10T14:20Z
vault-provisioner: no token mint recorded for request_id=ac-20260310-77
Initial hypothesis: lifecycle-sync executed but hit a guard that prevented creating bindings for identities without 'account_namespace' claim. The new access UI omits account_namespace for cross-org roles.
Reproduced locally by submitting a request with blank account_namespace; lifecycle-sync returns early from precondition check (code path added in patch rprovisioner #441).
Guard introduced in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/441 to avoid creating bindings for deprecated role types; rollback candidate.
Observed that legacy backfill-based onboarding still creates bindings because it sets account_namespace explicitly. This explains partial impact.
SRE note: there is no obvious 5xx or timeout in lifecycle-sync — the function appears healthy and reports success; logic prevented work.
Workaround (applied 2026-03-11 09:40Z): Manually backfilled RBAC bindings for affected users via rbac-service admin endpoint and recorded in audit log.
Short-term fix (in progress): revert the precondition check added in PR 441 and deploy a patch that treats missing account_namespace as 'default' for runbooks-v2 onboarding. Patch branch: fix/onboarding-fallback-882.
Long-term follow-up: update access UI to include account_namespace field for all onboarding flows and add unit tests covering this precondition. Create a ticket to add an automated reconciliation job to surface approved-but-not-provisioned requests.
Postmortem owner: Raj Patel. Target postmortem completion: 2026-03-20.
Ava Chen (Reporter) [2026-03-10T15:02Z]: Users reported 403 when clicking into runbooks-v2 after approval. I can share a request id privately.

Raj Patel [2026-03-11T09:50Z]: Manual backfills complete for current affected users. Deploying revert PR to staging for verification.
Security (Liam Nguyen) [2026-03-11T10:30Z]: Manual backfill entries have been recorded in audit trail. Please ensure any revert doesn't reintroduce the deprecated role creation path without owner approval.

Impact: Multiple deploys and emergency escalations blocked for on-call and contractor teams. Expected: Requests transition to 'AwaitingApprover' and email/Slack approvals delivered. Observed: Requests stuck for >3 hours, approvers did not receive notifications.

Initial hypothesis: Access-approval-svc lost permission to read group membership after Okta client credentials rotated without updating the service secret in Vault. Alternatively, group renames changed keys used in the approval mapping table and caused a lookup failure.
1) Create a temporary admin access request from Console > User > 'Elevate access' for a contractor account
2) Observe request created with state 'PendingApproval' in /admin/access-requests

Daniel Cho (SRE) 2026-03-10: Investigating - saw 403s to Okta. Checking Vault client credential rotation and service token scopes.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Several macOS laptops (MacBook Pro 2021/2022 w/ Intel AX210 and Apple Silicon devices) observed intermittent loss of internal API connectivity while on corporate Wi‑Fi 6E SSID. WireGuard sessions are marked dead by gateway after missing keepalives. Problem correlates with AP channel-avoidance events and the AP marking the client as non-responsive to Router Advertisements (RAs).

Impact:
- Affects ~6–12 users in SF office (prod-us-west) intermittently since 2026-03-01 09:30 PDT.
- Internal services (console, internal metrics, git pushes) stall or return 502/524 from services behind the zero-trust gateway.
- No evidence of server-side overload; issue localizes to client <-> AP behavior.

Environment:
- SSID: Redwood-Corp-6E (802.11ax/6E, DFS enabled, channel-avoidance + ACS enabled)
- Clients: macOS 12.6.7 & macOS 13.4.1 (mix of Intel AX210 and Apple Silicon Wi‑Fi stacks)
- VPN: WireGuard-based zero-trust agent (keepalive default 15s)
- APs: Aruba CX series (firmware 10.8.3), automatic channel-avoidance/DFS response enabled

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Client on 6 GHz band joins SSID, normal traffic flows.
2) AP triggers channel-avoidance/DFS sweep (noise detected) and briefly moves radios or suppresses probe responses on specific clients.
3) During the window (~2–8s), client stops receiving Router Advertisements (IPv6) and some multicast neighbor ops; WireGuard keepalives are queued by client stack and not transmitted timely.
4) Gateway marks peer as dead after 3 missed keepalives; user loses internal connectivity until WireGuard restarts or user toggles network.

Observed logs (client side):
- syslog excerpts: "kernel: wlan0: disassociated by AP (reason 36)" followed by "kernel: ra_timer: no RA received for 8s, suppressing RA processing"
- zero-trust-agent log: "peer not reachable, last handshake 18s ago, scheduling rekey"
- AP event: "DFS Channel Avoidance: radar detected, client probe suppression engaged for 5s"

Investigation notes / hypothesis:
- Hypothesis 1: AP DFS/channel-avoidance implementation suppresses multicast/RAs for certain clients during avoidance windows. macOS Wi‑Fi stacks treat RA loss as network liveness degradation and deprioritize sending keepalives, leading to WireGuard timeouts.
- Hypothesis 2: Specific driver/firmware combo (Intel AX210 on macOS via Intel firmware shim) mis-handles probe suppression, buffering outgoing small UDP packets (keepalives) until radio re-enabled.
- Correlation: Events align with AP DFS timestamps in Aruba logs and client syslogs. Not reproducible on 2.4/5 GHz SSIDs or on wired ports.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Network team changed AP policy for affected AP cluster to "defer DFS channel-avoidance for user-critical SSID" (reduces avoidance aggressiveness).
- Support recommended affected users to temporarily switch to 5 GHz SSID or wired desk port.
- Increased WireGuard keepalive in agent config to 25s on a small test cohort (will reduce false-positive disconnects).

Impact mitigation status:
- After AP policy change and 5 GHz fallback, occurrence rate dropped by ~85% for affected users. Still reproducible in heavy DFS environments.

Resolution plan / next steps:
- Eng to produce a host-agent change to: 1) make keepalive adaptive when RA loss is detected (extend keepalive window during RA suppression windows) and 2) attempt fast re-transmit of keepalives at lower level when radio flaps are detected (PR linked below).
- Network team to schedule Aruba firmware upgrade (10.9.x) that contains improved DFS channel-avoidance behavior; test in canary APs.
- SRE to add metric/alert for RA loss events per client aggregated across APs.

See also linked artifacts and runbook for RA suppression troubleshooting.

Additional notes:
Interplay between AP DFS/channel-avoidance behavior and macOS client radio handling resulted in temporary suppression of multicast Router Advertisements and delayed transmission of WireGuard keepalives. The gateway then considered peers dead after missed handshakes.
Switch affected clients to 5 GHz SSID or wired network, or relax AP channel-avoidance policy for Redwood-Corp-6E. Increase WireGuard keepalive from 15s to 25s on affected hosts until agent patch is deployed.
Mitigation: AP policy relaxed for affected cluster and test cohort moved to 5 GHz; keepalive increased for test users. Full fix: agent PR to add adaptive keepalive behavior and AP firmware upgrade planned. Status: in progress.
1) Merge and roll out zero-trust-agent PR to canary (Diego). 2) Network to upgrade firmware on cluster 12 to Aruba 10.9.x and run 14-day telemetry (Rajiv). 3) SRE to add RA-loss metric and alert (Priya). 4) Re-evaluate ticket after canary results (target 2026-03-26).
payload.summary: Wi-Fi 6E client channel-avoidance causes RA suppression and VPN liveness failures on macOS

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Ephemeral debug/service operator role sessions originating from the access-broker in eu-west are intermittently missing full session tag payloads. When tags are truncated, org-level IAM condition policies deny KMS Encrypt and S3 PutObject for the ml-deploy-runner/ephemeral sa, causing private-deploy debug and bootstrap workflows to fail.

Impact:
- Several private/preprod debug jobs and a small percentage (~3%) of dedicated onboarding runs in eu-west are failing with AccessDenied for kms:Encrypt and s3:PutObject.
- Customers on dedicated/proxy debug paths unaffected externally, but internal debugging and scaling tests are impacted.
- Increase in SEV1 escalations from SRE when ephemeral runs fail during preflight checks.

Environment:
- Affected: prod accounts in eu-west region (eu-west-1), access-broker v1.9.3, auth-proxy v2.4.
- Observed during automated onboarding and manual JIT debug flows that assume cross-account STS roles from GCP WIF / AWS broker.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger ephemeral bootstrap via ops tooling: ./ops/bootstrap --env=eu-west --job=ephemeral-debug --service=ml-deploy-runner
2) Observe broker logs for STS AssumeRole call and returned SessionTags payload.
3) Reproduce via aws sts assume-role with generated session tags header (simulate long tag set).
4) Check KMS/S3 access with aws kms encrypt and aws s3 cp; failures correlate with truncated session tag string length > 256 chars.

Observed behavior / Logs:
- access-broker logs (trace id ab12f3): "session_tags length 256 -> truncated" recorded in v1.9.3.
- AWS CloudTrail shows AssumeRole success but RequestParameters.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName absent when tags truncated.
- KMS denies: "User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/ephemeral-debug-role/Sess is not authorized to perform: kms:Encrypt on resource" with condition failure on StringEquals tag:team.
- S3 PutObject denies with similar tag condition failures.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: tag serialization in the broker is not consistent across the GCP->AWS translation path; long metadata + multiple tag keys exceed allowed header lengths, causing silent truncation by the broker or by STS session encoding.
- Reproduced locally by constructing a tag payload > 260 bytes; AWS STS accepts call but resulting sessionContext truncates some keys.
- auth-proxy v2.4 introduced extra identity attributes (workspace_id, deploy_hash) which increased average tag payload size from ~120 bytes to ~320 bytes.
- Related historical tickets indicate similar symptoms but not identical: linked INT-100200 addressed tag normalization in a different broker service.

Workarounds tried:
- Short-term: added a temp condition exception for the ephemeral-debug-role resource in eu-west (resource-based allow) to unblock immediate bootstraps. Applied on 2026-03-11 at 03:20 UTC.
- Short-term alternate: trim optional tag keys at the caller side (ops shim) before calling assume-role; this reduces tracing fidelity.

Proposed resolution / next steps:
1) Priority bugfix: normalize tag serialization inside access-broker to deterministic compact encoding (key hashing + allowlist) and prevent truncation (owner: infra-team). Target: ship v1.9.4 to staging by 2026-03-15 and prod rollout 2026-03-18.
2) Add unit/integration tests that simulate long session tag payloads and assert no IAM condition denials.
3) Revert resource-based allow once v1.9.4 is live and verified.
4) Post-deploy: run a targeted soak in eu-west with 1k ephemeral bootstraps to validate.
5) Follow-up task: document tag size limits in cloud-access-runbook and update ops shim to enforce tag allowlist.

Risk and rollback plan:
- Rolling back v1.9.4 is low-risk (broker change only) but will require coordination with SRE to revert ephemeral allowlist.
- If issue persists after fix, escalate to security for potential policy adjustments.

Resolution notes (in progress):
- Temporary allowlist applied on 2026-03-11 to restore service.
- Patch PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4212 (access-broker: compact-tag-encoding).
- Deployment plan drafted and stuckpoint is adding integration test harness for STS session encoding.

2026-03-10 | Olivia Martinez | Initial report: alerted by oncall after two bootstrap failures in eu-west. Included logs and initial reproduction steps.
2026-03-11 | Marcus Chen | Confirmed correlation between tag payload size and denies. Applied temporary resource-based allow to reduce customer impact. Linked PR for compact encoding opened.
2026-03-11 | Priya Singh (SRE) | Requested that we add metrics for session tag sizes to broker logs and a dashboard to surface this for 24h post-deploy.
2026-03-12 | Marcus Chen | Added integration test plan and scheduled staging rollout for 2026-03-15. Noted need for runbook update after fix.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Users in the model-eval-runner group are receiving 403 when attempting to start evaluation jobs after last week's identity migration. Investigation shows SCIM profiles created/updated by the migration have 'accountVerified': false for affected users. RBAC policy for model-eval-runner explicitly requires verified accounts.

Impact:
- 8+ internal users (platform and research) cannot start model evaluation runs in prod us-west.
- Blocked telemetry and nightly evals; some scheduled CI jobs fail with 403 causing alert churn.
- Affects developer velocity for model-quality investigations.

Environment:
- prod (us-west) — Console and runner service behind internal SSO.
- Affected identities were created via bulk SCIM migration job 'scim-migration-2026-03-08'.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Try to open https://console.redwood.internal/model-evals and trigger a new evaluation run.
2) Request is authenticated via Okta SSO, then SCIM profile is queried for 'accountVerified'.
3) RBAC service denies grant due to accountVerified==false, resulting in 403.

Observed logs / evidence:
- authz proxy (authz-proxy-2a) logs 2026-03-12T09:42:11Z: "grant denied: accountVerified=false, required=true; principal=U12345"
- SCIM sync job logs show bulk_create with patch property 'accountVerified=false' for new identities (scim-migration-2026-03-08)
- Okta profile for user shows emailVerified=true but internal SCIM object has accountVerified=false (mismatch).
- Related incidents: INT-314159 (relaystate/ttl mismatch) referenced because that incident changed SCIM sync timing.

Hypothesis:
- Migration code path sets accountVerified conservatively to false when it cannot confirm verification timestamp from Okta attribute mapping. A recent Okta attribute name change (email_verified -> isEmailVerified) during the migration led to fallback value false for many users. RBAC policy was tightened in February to require accountVerified=true for any console/eval-runner grants.

Immediate customer-visible workaround:
- Manual override: run 'id-sync fix-verify U12345' to flip accountVerified to true for critical users (devops oncall has used this to restore a small set).
- Temporary RBAC mitigation: relax model-eval-runner policy to accept accountVerified==false for 72 hours (requires change control and risk approval).

Suggested next steps / owner:
- Identity team to audit scim-migration-2026-03-08 code path and patch attribute mapping (owner: Priya Nair).
- Patch applied to scim-sync to copy Okta's isEmailVerified -> accountVerified and rerun migration fixes for affected users.
- Run a dry-run script to list identities with accountVerified=false and cross-check against Okta emailVerified attribute.
- Consider short-term RBAC policy toggle and then revert after migration fix.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 Security (Elena Ruiz): Note — any RBAC relaxation must be approved by security. Recommend targeted manual fixes for named users rather than broad policy relax unless emergency declared. Open to rapid exception for 72 hours if change control approved.
Patch added to SCIM mapper to read both 'isEmailVerified' and 'email_verified' attributes from Okta. Backfill job executed 2026-03-15; post-run verification shows 72/74 previously-unverified accounts now true. Two accounts required manual email re-verification with owners. No RBAC policy changes were applied after security recommended manual fixes. Monitoring for 48h — no further 403s reported from model-eval-runner. payload.description:
Request Legal review/approval of updated internal pricing guidance language before Sales Enablement rollout and before we reuse wording in MSAs/order forms.

Background
Finance + Product + Eng are hardening billing meters (tokens/requests, cache-hit attribution, retries/idempotency behavior) and updating internal pricing/packaging guidance. We need Legal to confirm that internal/customer-facing language is accurate, consistent with our current contract positions, and does not create implied guarantees that we can’t operationalize.

Scope of Legal review
1) Usage definitions (Hosted API)
- Define “token” for billing purposes (prompt vs completion; billed_tokens vs raw tokens) and clarify that models/tokenizers vary.
- Clarify treatment of streaming responses (partial chunks, client disconnects) and what is billable when output was generated server-side.
- Clarify tool/function calling and structured output token attribution.
- Clarify retries/fallback behavior (server-side retries, fallback routing, idempotency) and how we prevent double-counting.
- Clarify caching behavior and cache-hit attribution (when cache reduces billed tokens and how it appears in usage exports).

2) Disputes, credits, and invoice adjustments
- Dispute window language (timeline; evidence required; how we handle late-arriving telemetry/backfills).
- Credits/refunds guardrails: when credits may be issued, approval path, and how credits apply to usage meters.
- Avoid committing to retroactive changes without Finance/Legal sign-off; ensure language preserves forward-fix preference.

3) Consistency checks
- Ensure wording is consistent across: Sales FAQ, Product pricing pages (internal), RevRec procedures, and clause library.
- Confirm any “audit log / usage export” promises align with the metering data retention & access controls policy.

Artifacts for review (links)
- Sales Enablement draft FAQ (Hosted API): sources/confluence/sales-enablement/pricing-guidance/hosted-api-pricing-faq-and-objection-handling.json
- Usage-based pricing legal terms playbook + clause library: sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/usage-based-pricing-legal-terms-playbook.json
- Free tier + overage policy language (internal): sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json
- Discounts & credits policy (internal): sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json
- Hosted API meter spec (reference for definitions): sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/billing-meter-spec-hosted-api-tokens-and-requests.json
- Metering data retention & access controls (reference): sources/confluence/policies-and-process/data-management/metering-data-retention-and-access-controls.json

What we need from Legal (acceptance criteria)
- Approval (or redlines) on the exact recommended customer-facing phrasing for:
  a) “billed tokens vs raw tokens” explanation
  b) retries/fallback + idempotency wording (avoid implying we never retry)
  c) caching / cache-hit attribution wording
  d) dispute window + credit issuance language
- Confirm whether any phrases should be marked “internal only” vs acceptable for customer-facing collateral.
- Identify any changes required to the clause library or contracting playbook to align with new guidance.

Timeline / urgency
Target to finalize language by 2026-02-26 to support end-of-month enablement and to avoid conflicting messaging during ongoing pricing experiments.

Notes / constraints
- Meter semantics are evolving under shadow-billing compare mode; avoid language that implies absolute immutability of meter internals. We can commit to stable definitions and transparent usage exports, but need to preserve ability to fix bugs.
- This ticket is for review/approval and wording guidance only; meter implementation work is tracked separately in Eng/Product systems.

Owner coordination
Primary contacts: Elliot Price (docs), Nikhil Sharma (Product), Emily Stone (RevRec), Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel), Michael Grant (GC, usage terms).

Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent mixing of model outputs (expected variant A but receiving partial outputs from variant B) for a subset of requests during their configured tenant 'snooze' window. The mixing appears transient and correlated with scheduled background metrics aggregation that runs at the same minute as the snooze window end.

Impact: Affected tenant seeing degraded output consistency for ~0.2% of requests during their nightly snooze window (00:00-00:10 UTC). Some responses include tokens or formatting from the older model variant which the tenant had explicitly pinned. Potential billing discrepancy suspected due to fallback to quantized variant at same time.

Environment: Production, us-east region, enterprise tenant with dedicated route and pin to open-llama-3b-v2.

1) Tenant has a pinned route to open-llama-3b-v2 with an active snooze window 00:00-00:10 UTC.
2) Send mixed synchronous chat+streaming requests spanning 23:59:50-00:00:30 UTC.
3) Observe that 1 in ~500 requests returns a response that contains truncation/format artifacts tied to open-llama-3b-v2-quant variant.
4) Re-run during non-snooze time and the issue does not reproduce.

Edge proxy trace: cookie-rewrite at 00:00:05 UTC (edge-proxy-12)
Orchestrator: prewarm-sweep started 00:00:04 UTC (orch-3), async metrics flush queued 00:00:04.1 UTC
Serving runtime: kvcache warm assign for model open-llama-3b-v2-quant on node gpu-9 at 00:00:05.8 UTC
Request traces (sample): request-id=nx-9f2a: pinned-model header present but cohort_token missing on a few requests; fallback route executed to quant variant; latency 92ms vs usual 48ms.
Billing logs: two requests recorded usage under quant variant SKUs at 00:00:05 UTC for tenant nimbledocs-acc-21.

Hypothesis 1: The 'snooze' window lifecycle handler performs an atomic state transition that momentarily clears cohort_token or tenant-affinity before the orchestrator completes prewarm allocation; this leads the edge to treat the request as unrouted and fall back to the fastest available compatible variant (quant).
Hypothesis 2: Async metrics aggregation triggers a small reconfiguration message to the orchestrator that races with the snooze end hook, causing temporary epoch/route metadata mismatch between control plane snapshot and edge cache.
Telemetry examined: control-plane snapshot versions show sequence gap between 00:00:03.9 and 00:00:05.2. Edge cookie rotation logs indicate TTL reset events at 00:00:04.9 for the tenant cookie namespace.
Reproduced in staging by co-locating metrics-aggregator cron at same second; reproduction rate ~0.18%.
Related code paths: route-snooze-handler, edge-affinity-reconcile, orchestrator-prewarm-sweep.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Support (Aisha): Customer reported mixed outputs during their scheduled snooze. Provided request ids and sample responses. Marked P1 due to enterprise SLA.
2026-03-11 09:45 - Eng (Jonah): Pulled traces and saw cookie TTL reset at snooze boundary. Raising orchestrator attention; tagging orch on Slack #support-orch.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 07:29 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirms issue continues at low rate overnight; provided a list of 28 request ids from 00:00-00:06 UTC across last 10 nights.
2026-03-13 14:02 - Eng (Jonah): Deployed hotfix: edge now rejects control-plane snapshot updates with non-monotonic seq numbers within 5s of snooze-end events. Observed no mixed responses in canary run last night (n=120k requests).
Mitigation applied: orchestrator prewarm cron jittered and edge snapshot apply hardened to avoid non-monotonic sequence updates within the snooze handoff window. Hotfix PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1892.
Customer workaround: move snooze window by +15s (temporary) or schedule metrics aggregation away from snooze boundary.
Current status: mitigation in prod canary for tenant cohort, monitoring for 72h. No full rollback required.
1) Postmortem runbook: add check to snooze-handler to block background snapshot applies for 10s after window end.
2) Engineering story to add a control-plane seq monotonicity gate and improved telemetry for cohort_token lifecycle (ETA 2 weeks).
3) Inform Billing ops to reconcile two quant-variant SKUs charged during impacted timestamps and issue credit if necessary (owner: Finance Ops).
4) Notify customer via CSM with summary and expected timeline.

payload.description:
Issue summary:

Mapora Analytics has reported sustained p95/p99 inference latency spikes and intermittent 504 timeouts starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC for traffic coming from their EU tenant. Traffic is consistently being routed through a US-east egress path for a subset of account tokens; requests routed via that path show a significant tail latency (p99 > 5s) and occasional streaming disconnects.

Impact:
- Customer reports degraded service in production for 3% of requests, spike concentrated on long-context chat sessions.
- SLO breaches for Mapora (dedicated) on latency and availability.
- Observed increase in downstream cost due to additional retries and cross-region egress.

Environment:
- Redwood prod (customer-dedicated capacity in eu-west).
- Affected routing span appears eu-west -> us-east egress.
- Observed on both rw-instruct-13b-quantized and openchat-7b serving pools.

Steps to reproduce (customer-facing):
1) Send streaming chat request with 4096-token context to endpoint using account token A (Mapora).
2) Observe p95/p99 response times; reproduces with 1/30 requests hitting >3s p95, and 1/500 hitting >5s or timing out.
3) When observed, check request headers for x-redwood-egress and x-pop-affinity.

Logs / Observations:
- x-redwood-egress header sometimes shows us-east-pop-12 despite eu-west routing policy.
- KV cache miss rate for affected requests is ~3x baseline for that account during spikes.
- Trace IDs show additional hop through cross-region egress proxy which adds ~120-180ms RT, but end-to-end tail suggests queueing/batching delays on remote pop.
- No recent deploys to serving runtime in eu-west cluster during window; control plane routing weight change occurred 2026-03-09 21:45 UTC (automated rebalancer job).
- Netflow/peering graphs show brief BGP path-change around the same time (external transit), but not sufficient to explain affinity flip frequency.

Investigation notes (internal):
- Hypothesis A: Account token routing metadata wrong — account-level tag (region_hint) not being honored for some in-flight sessions, causing cross-region routing and cold KV cache on remote pop.
- Hypothesis B: Rebalancer job introduced an intermediate weight change that triggered affinity re-evaluation for a subset of sessions, then some requests landed on a less warmed-up backend in us-east.
- Hypothesis C: External transit path-change caused occasional latency spikes that amplified KV-cache miss penalty (remote cache miss + cross-region RTT).

Diagnostic queries run:
- Queried routing logs for token A between 2026-03-09T21:30 and 2026-03-10T04:00 UTC — ~4.8% of requests were labeled with fallback_egress: true and routed to us-east.
- Correlated with cache hit metrics in us-east pop: affected TTLs showed lower prefix cache hits (~72% vs baseline 94%).

Temporary mitigation / workaround applied:
- Support recommended pinning Mapora account to strict eu-west affinity via account tag override (applied 2026-03-10 05:10 UTC). Post-override telemetry shows drop in cross-region routed requests to 0.3% and immediate improvement in p99 for the customer.
- Added short-term config to treat this account as high-stability for rebalancer (prevent auto-migration) while we investigate.

Resolution plan / next steps:
1) Engineering to review automated rebalancer runbook and roll back/adjust weight-change heuristics that may re-evaluate affinity for active sessions (owner: infra-routes).
2) Runtime team to instrument per-pop KV-cache warmup metrics and expose a heatmap to detect remote cold-starts on cross-region fallbacks (owner: serving-runtime).
3) SRE to correlate BGP/transit changes with routing-controller decisions to determine if external factors should suppress affinity flips (owner: network).
4) Postmortem to include customer impact and recommend change to default rebalancer aggressiveness for dedicated tenants.

Customer communication summary (to be posted):
- 2026-03-10 06:00 UTC: Acknowledged and applied account-level affinity override as temporary mitigation; asked customer to validate.
- 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Customer confirmed perceived latency improvements and fewer timeouts on their long-context tests.
- Will follow up with permanent fix timeline within 72h.

2026-03-10 04:15 - Support (Elena): Initial triage, reproduced elevated p99 with Mapora token in EU tenancy. Escalated to infra-routes.
2026-03-10 05:05 - Infra (Jonah): Found rebalancer weight-change at 2026-03-09 21:45 UTC for eu-west pool; flagged as candidate cause. Pin/override recommended.
2026-03-10 05:30 - SRE (Priya Singh): Correlated with transient BGP change; collecting netflow snapshots for the interval.
2026-03-10 06:10 - Support (Elena): Applied account-affinity override; asked customer to re-test. Customer reports improvement at 06:50 UTC.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 14:00 - Infra (Jonah): Assigned follow-up tasks to infra-routes and network. Owner: infra-routes. ETA for rebalancer change: 2026-03-18.
Temporary mitigation applied (account affinity override). Engineering plan in progress to harden rebalancer heuristics and improve cache warmup visibility. No code rollback required; config change successful.
Infra-routes to adjust rebalancer aggressiveness and produce rollout changelog
Serving-runtime to deploy kv-cache telemetry to prod and add alerting for sudden cache-miss bursts

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that alerts tied to saved dashboard widgets are not firing when the dashboard is embedded with URL filter parameters. The alerts appear to evaluate without error in the alerting UI (green checks) but no incident notifications are generated for the filtered context.

Impact:
- Multiple Lumina Health monitoring dashboards did not trigger escalation for a threshold breach between 2026-03-09 22:10 and 2026-03-10 01:45 UTC.
- Potential compliance exposure for an enterprise healthcare customer because they rely on dashboard-driven alerts for SLA and Ops workflows.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east)
- Customer embedding dashboards via iframe with URL params (e.g., ?region=midwest&team=careflow)
- Alerts configured on dashboard saved queries (alert_eval window 1m, severity critical)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Save a dashboard with a widget alert on metric A (threshold > 5).
2. Embed dashboard in a customer page and append URL filters: ?region=us-east&team=ops
3. Trigger metric A to exceed threshold for >1 minute in the filtered scope.
4. Observe alert evaluation history and notification channel delivery.

Observed behavior:
- Alert evaluation logs show the alert checked and returned a state change timestamp but no incident or notification appears in the delivery channel (PagerDuty, email).
- When opening dashboard directly (no URL filters) alerts behave normally and fire notifications.
- Applying the same filter from dashboard UI (not via URL) also results in proper notifications.

Expected behavior:
- Alerts tied to dashboard queries should honor the exact filter context supplied via URL parameters for embedded dashboards and produce notifications when conditions are met.

Logs / links / artifacts:
- Customer-provided trace: https://s3.redwood-inference/test-exports/lumina/alert-eval-2026-03-10.log
- Internal trace link: https://traces.redwood.example/trace/7f3a2b
- Slack: #support thread <https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C05ABC12345/p164>

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:32 - Engineering (SRE): Reproduced locally using embedded iframe with URL params. Observed alert evaluation engine receives global filter instead of URL-scoped filters for embedded requests.
2026-03-12 14:08 - Product (Maya Ortiz): Customer notified of in-progress fix and temporary mitigation. Coordinating release notes and postmortem scope.
Checked alerting-service logs for eval window: alert-eval worker processed job id 0a3f at 2026-03-09T22:11:05Z.
Found discrepancy: requests originating from embedding proxy contain X-Embed-Filters header; alerting-service uses a cache key that only considers saved_query_id and org_id, ignoring X-Embed-Filters leading to stale cache hits.
Replication steps executed on staging: embedding proxy -> console-service -> alerting-service. Confirmed header dropped at console-service when request was transformed for background evaluation.
Hypothesis: recent refactor (https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-service/commit/abc1234) removed propagation of embed filter context for background evals, resulting in alerting-service evaluating wrong filter set and de-duping notifications.
Observed that notification suppression occurs when an alert transitions back-and-forth within the same cache key period; because the evaluation used wrong filter, the system considered the state already seen and skipped notification deduping incorrectly.
Console-service background evaluation path dropped embedded URL filter context (X-Embed-Filters header) after a refactor, causing alert eval cache keys to be computed without the embed-scoped filters. This led to false de-duplication and suppressed notifications for embedded dashboards.
A patch was merged and deployed to prod that ensures console-service preserves embed filter headers for background alert evaluation and includes the embed filter fingerprint in the alerting-service cache key. The fix is in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-service/pull/4521 and deployed to us-east on 2026-03-12 03:10 UTC.
Workaround prior to patch: disable background evaluation for embedded dashboards (console toggle) or avoid URL-based embedding filters and use saved dashboard filters. We applied a temporary rule-level fallback that forces saved-query parameters while the patch rolled out.
1) Backfill tests: add unit/integration tests to ensure X-Embed-Filters propagation across console-service background eval path.
2) Metric: add alert-eval telemetry to count cache key mismatches by source (embed vs console UI) and create a dashboard tile for 90-day trend.
3) Customer follow-up: schedule 1:1 with Lumina Health CS to review impact and provide evidence of fix and audit logs.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Automated prefetch/cache-sweep job ran across a subset of shard groups starting ~2026-03-10T12:05Z which coincided with a sharp rise in 5xx responses at the API gateway and upstream runtime process crashes. The event produced a multi-tenant error wave affecting self-serve customers and transiently raising our 5xx rate by ~8x for ~30 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: increased 5xx for text generation and streaming endpoints across us-east and spillover into us-west. Several customers (Polylingo Inc. observed) reported degraded performance and timeouts.
- Platform: serving-runtime processes on 4 shard groups experienced rapid restarts and elevated OOM/page-fault counts during the sweep window. API gateway returned 502/503 at scale due to upstream unavailability.

Environment:
- prod - us-east primary; partial spill to us-west during fallback routing.
- Autoscaler observed rapid scale-down attempts before the wave.

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Prefetch/cache-sweep triggered by scheduled invalidation job (internal cron) at 2026-03-10T12:05Z across shard groups A,C,F.
2) Prefetch triggered high concurrency model loads and KV cache invalidations; runtime memory usage spiked and GC pressure increased.
3) Upstream runtimes began to OOM/restart; health-check flaps removed endpoints from the pool.
4) API gateway load redistributed, causing connection churn and 502/503 return for in-flight requests.
5) Autoscaler oscillation and prefetch retries amplified load, creating a retry storm.

Observed logs & metrics pointers:

Additional notes:
- Runtime shard crash trace: https://sentry.redwood.ai/issue/RT-78321
- Prefetch job history: internal-jobstore/prefetch/2026-03-10-12:05
Temporary impact mitigation in-flight:
- Disabled the scheduled full-sweep invalidation job at 2026-03-10T12:18Z (SRE action).
- Applied a soft concurrency cap to prefetch workers for affected shard groups at 2026-03-10T12:25Z.
- Scoped rolling restarts of runtimes for shards with persistent OOMs starting 12:30Z.
Requested from customer (Polylingo Inc.):
- Status updates and ETA for full service recovery. They reported 12 failed request traces and requested a root-cause follow-up.
Note: This ticket captures the operational incident and customer-facing support interactions. Follow-up work will be tracked in a separate postmortem/ops task once root cause confirmed.
2026-03-10T12:12Z - Support (Maya): Customer reported sudden increase in 5xx on generation endpoints. Kicked off SRE paging.
2026-03-10T12:17Z - SRE (Ethan): Observed prefetch sweep job running; runtimes A/C/F have repeating OOM traces. Pausing sweep recommended.
2026-03-10T12:19Z - Support (Maya) to Polylingo: We are investigating; temporary throttling applied and we will update within 15m.
2026-03-10T12:25Z - SRE (Ethan): Soft concurrency cap applied to prefetch workers; monitoring for error rate drop.
2026-03-10T12:40Z - SRE (Ethan): Gateway 5xx rate decreasing but still above baseline due to inflight retries; continuing targeted restarts.
2026-03-12T09:00Z - Engineering (Priya Singh): Added hypothesis - kvcache invalidation caused a sudden working set change that triggered suboptimal kernel paths and memory fragmentation. Investigating kernel selection logs.
2026-03-12T11:15Z - Product (Liam Chen): Requested clarification on whether this could recur during large-scale model onloads. Planning follow-up meeting.
2026-03-12T12:40Z - SRE (Ethan): Assigned follow-up owners for runbook updates and prefetch rate-limiter feature; see linked PRs.
Initial hypothesis: Prefetch + cache invalidation created concurrent eager model loads exceeding expected memory headroom for some shards.
Sentry traces show repeated 'cudaMalloc' failure patterns immediately before runtime restarts (RT-78321).
Autoscaler logs indicate scale-down/scale-up oscillation between 12:10Z-12:35Z that likely exacerbated connection churn.
Kernel-selection logs: some big-model loads fell back to non-optimized kernels for long sequences, increasing memory usage (see runtime/pull/3721).
We were not rate-limiting prefetch across tenants; a global sweep created simultaneous hotloads across multiple tenants.
Mitigation applied: scheduled sweep disabled and prefetch concurrency capped; targeted rolling restarts removed unhealthy runtimes; temporary global rate-limit for prefetch jobs enforced.
Next steps: implement tenant-aware prefetch throttling, add memory budget checks before eager model load, update cache-invalidation runbook to avoid full-shard simultaneous sweeps, and schedule a full postmortem (INC-20260310-001). Planned PRs for kernel logging and prefetch limiter: runtime/pull/3721, apigateway/pull/1189.
Quantify memory delta during sweep vs baseline per shard.
Run chaos test of prefetch sweeping with synthetic tenants to validate limiter behavior.
Add guard rails in autoscaler to avoid oscillation during high transient memory pressure.
payload.summary: Multi-tenant 5xx wave following automated prefetch + cache sweep

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer enabled an AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoint) to reach Redwood control plane from their VPC and on-prem network. After enabling the endpoint and a Route 53 private hosted zone, their application started failing TLS handshakes to api.redwood-inference.com.

Impact:
- All control-plane API requests from FinLedger's prod environment to api.redwood-inference.com in us-east-1 are failing TLS validation.
- Attempts to create new inference jobs and token refreshes are failing; customer reports degraded production traffic and automated retries do not recover.
- Error surfaces in app servers: "tls: certificate is not valid for requested name" and connection resets during TLS handshake.

Environment:
- Customer: FinLedger Inc (private tier)
- VPCs: vpc-0a1b2c3d (us-east-1) with interface endpoint vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a (com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com)
- Route 53: Private hosted zone created for redwood-inference.com in the customer's account
- Region: us-east-1
- Client stack: Go HTTP client + SNI enforced by client libs

Timeline / Observed behavior:
- 2026-03-09 10:12 UTC: Customer created interface endpoint for com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com and attached security groups.
- 2026-03-09 10:20 UTC: Customer created a private hosted zone redwood-inference.com with a CNAME record mapping api.redwood-inference.com -> vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com
- 2026-03-10 01:05 UTC: Customer apps started returning TLS validation errors; initial support ticket opened.

Steps to reproduce (customer environment):
1) From an app host inside their VPC: dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @10.0.0.2 (their resolver) -> returns "10.10.5.12" (private ENI IP of the interface endpoint).
2) curl -v --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:10.10.5.12 https://api.redwood-inference.com/health 2>&1 -> TLS handshake fails with certificate name mismatch.
3) openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -showcerts -> server cert CN/SAN contains "vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com", not api.redwood-inference.com.

Debug logs / evidence collected:
- dig output (customer resolver): "10.10.5.12" (matches interface endpoint ENI).
- openssl s_client shows server cert: subject CN=vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com; SANs do NOT include api.redwood-inference.com.
- tcpdump on host shows ClientHello SNI=api.redwood-inference.com and Server Certificate for vpce-... (mismatch).
- Support-side confirmation: public DNS resolves api.redwood-inference.com -> our public IPs; certificate served by our public LB includes api.redwood-inference.com in SAN.

Initial hypothesis:
- Customer created a private hosted zone or DNS override that maps api.redwood-inference.com to the VPCE interface IPs. The PrivateLink interface endpoint is terminating TLS with a certificate that lists the VPCE DNS name (vpce-...) as the certificate identity, not the public hostname. Because the clients request api.redwood-inference.com via SNI, TLS validation fails.
- This is a split-horizon DNS misconfiguration on the customer side, not a platform bug. The PrivateLink endpoint alias and the certificate presented by the endpoint are not compatible with the customer's DNS aliasing approach.

Workarounds and recommended remediation provided to customer so far:
- Immediate workaround (customer): add an explicit host override in /etc/hosts or container DNS to point api.redwood-inference.com to our public control-plane IPs so TLS certs match (not ideal for traffic routing). Example: curl --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:34.201.12.34 https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
- Preferred long-term remediation: remove the private hosted zone or CNAME mapping for api.redwood-inference.com. Instead, configure PrivateLink using an alias record that preserves the original hostname and ensure the endpoint is set up with a certificate that includes api.redwood-inference.com (requires coordination with infra; see runbook).
- Alternative: use SNI override on the client to accept the vpce-... certificate name (only if customer controls TLS validation behavior and accepts risk).

Next steps assigned:
- Support: Confirm whether the customer intended to route control-plane traffic over PrivateLink. If yes, coordinate with Infra/Platform to evaluate whether we can provision a PrivateLink-compatible cert chain or recommend a supported DNS pattern. (Assigned: Liam Ortega)
- Engineering/Infra: Review PrivateLink interface endpoint configuration and whether our endpoint can present a certificate containing api.redwood-inference.com for customer-managed endpoints or whether we must document this incompatibility. (Linked: INT-4389)
- Customer: Evaluate removing the private hosted zone and use Route 53 resolver rules to forward only specific suffixes to the endpoint, or accept the temporary /etc/hosts workaround.

Impact statement for internal stakeholders:
- Production outage for FinLedger's inference control-plane integration. Customer blocked on job creation and token refresh flows. Potential SLA breach if unresolved by sla_due_at.

Attachments / evidence files stored in ticket:
- tcpdump snippet (pcap) uploaded to ticket
- openssl output pasted into ticket notes
- dig outputs and private hosted zone screenshot provided by customer


Additional notes:
2026-03-10 03:40 UTC - FinLedger (Customer): Provided dig results showing api.redwood-inference.com -> 10.10.5.12 and screenshot of private hosted zone redwood-inference.com with CNAME to vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com.
2026-03-11 09:12 UTC - Infra (Engineering): Acknowledged INT-4389; noted PrivateLink interface endpoints are managed by customer account; we cannot change the endpoint certificate in customer account. Suggested doc updates to PrivateLink runbook to call out split-horizon DNS caveat.
2026-03-12 16:45 UTC - FinLedger (Customer): Confirmed temporary /etc/hosts workaround restored traffic for one of their app clusters. They will evaluate full DNS change this week and asked for recommended best practices documentation.
payload.summary: TLS handshake failures to control plane after enabling AWS PrivateLink due to split-horizon DNS aliasing

Issue summary:
Zero-touch (ZTP) depot provisioning jobs are timing out during the network phase for new arrivals. Devices enter 'Waiting for network' for >20 minutes and then fall back to manual imaging. This started after a switch OS upgrade on depot-spine-2 on 2026-03-08.

Impact:
- ~18% of incoming depot devices fail automated imaging in staging-us-west between 07:00-19:00 PST.
- Blocks throughput for technician bench (devtools) and increases manual imaging load.
- No reported impact on production fleet yet, staging-only so far.

Environment:
- Staging depot network (staging-us-west) behind spine-switches: depot-spine-1, depot-spine-2.
- PXE/HTTP netboot orchestrator: provisioning.redwood.internal:8080 (staging).
- DHCP servers: isc-dhcpd-v4 (for IPv4), infrax-dhcpd-v6 (for IPv6 PD).
- Switches running NXOS-like vendor OS; depot-spine-2 was upgraded 2026-03-08 to 10.4.x.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Rack a factory-fresh Dell Latitude 5440 on a staging bench port configured as access VLAN 100.
2) Power on with default BIOS settings (PXE enabled).
3) Observe EFI netboot sequence; device requests DHCP/PD.
4) Device state stalls at 'Waiting for network' in provisioning console (~15-25min) and eventually times out.

Observed behavior / Logs:
- provisioning-orch.log: "job 0x7a3f netboot-wait timeout waiting for vlan assignment"
- dhcpv6 server log (infrax-dhcpd-v6): "SOLICIT from DUID:00:01:00:... IA_NA/IA_PD assigned for client mac=44:38:39:xx:xx:xx prefix=fd20:...:0/64 via interface bond0.200"
- switch syslog (depot-spine-2): "dhcp-relay: forwarded DHCPv6 from port Ethernet3/1 to relay 10.11.12.9 (egress VLAN 200)"
- netboot bootloader: "no IPv4 lease received; waiting for IPv6 PD; VLAN lookup returned tag=200 (expected 100)"

Hypothesis:
- After the switch OS upgrade, DHCPv6 relay behavior changed: the relay path uses a different egress interface/VLAN when handling DHCPv6 PD than for DHCPv4. Our provisioning stack determines the intended VLAN via DHCPv4 Option 82 / observed egress interface; with DHCPv6 PD now being served from a different VLAN (200) the provisioning orchestrator marks the device as 'unknown VLAN' and drops the job.
- The ZTP flow currently prioritizes IPv6 PD events to attach a network tag. If the PD returns a different VLAN than the physical port config, the orchestrator treats it as a mismatch and fails the assignment.

Workaround currently in place:
- Tech bench instruction: disable IPv6 in bootloader temporarily (press OOB -> add "ipv6.disable=1" in netboot args) to force IPv4 DHCP flow; that bypasses the faulty DHCPv6 relay path and allows images to proceed. This is manual and slower but effective.
- We added a short-term ACL on depot-spine-2 to block DHCPv6 relay to infrax-dhcpd-v6 while we triage (reduces failures but interrupts legitimate IPv6 testing).

Investigation notes (timeline):
Confirmed regression correlates with depot-spine-2 OS upgrade (10.4.x) on 2026-03-08.
Reproduced consistently on bench ports attached to spine-2; bench ports attached to spine-1 behave normally.
Packet capture at spine-2 showed DHCPv6-relay egress interface uses SVI for VLAN 200 instead of 100; DHCPv4 relays still use VLAN 100.
Provisioning service code inspects DHCP events and currently trusts VLAN indicated by IPv6 PD egress; it lacks fallback to physical port mapping when PD VLAN differs.
Switch vendor confirmed a changed default in 10.4.x that picks relay egress based on route selection for IPv6 vs IPv4; previously both used the incoming SVI's VLAN.
Preliminary test: adding static policy to depot-spine-2 to force DHCPv6 relay egress via SVI 100 resolves the hang for test devices.
No evidence of MAC collisions or DHCP lease exhaustion; issue is deterministic with IPv6 PD path on spine-2 only.

infrax-dhcpd-v6: Mar 10 08:13:57 SOLICIT from DUID 00:01:00:... mac=44:38:39:aa:bb:cc IA_PD assigned prefix=fd20:abcd::/64 via bond0.200
depot-spine-2: Mar 8 22:00 dhcp-relay: forwarded DHCPv6 from Gi3/1 to relay 10.11.12.9 egress-vlan=200
netboot-efi: no IPv4 lease received; waiting for IPv6 PD; vlan lookup returned 200; expected 100

Additional notes:
Techs should disable IPv6 in netboot args (add ipv6.disable=1) for affected devices or temporarily block DHCPv6 relay from depot-spine-2 to infrax-dhcpd-v6. Both are manual and have trade-offs.
2026-03-13 02:00 UTC - Apply switch policy on depot-spine-2 to force DHCPv6 relay egress via SVI 100 (Priya).
Deploy provisioning PR #2153 to staging and run sanity on 50 devices (Ben).
If switch policy fixes immediately, revert ACL block and monitor for 48 hours (Jordan).
Postmortem doc & follow-up to review switch upgrade checklist (owner: Ops).
ongoing - temporary ACL applied; switch policy scheduled; code PR open to make provisioning resilient.

Issue summary:
Users on TPG-14 v2 devices report intermittent 'ghost' left-click events after the Windows 11 cumulative update (KB500xyz) installed via WU on 2026-03-09. Ghost clicks occur while typing or when the palm rests near the touchpad; frequency varies but reproducible on affected hardware.

Impact:
- Several engineers reported spurious clicks causing accidental text selection, misplaced cursor actions, and interrupted builds.
- Affects day-to-day productivity for ~8 known devices in US-West office and a few remote users with the same SKU.

Environment:
- OS: Windows 11 22H2 (post-update state 2026-03-09)
- Devices: TPG-14 v2 corporate images (Autopilot-provisioned)
- Management: Intune + Autopatch for cumulative updates
- Region: prod-us-west

Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot TPG-14 v2 with latest cumulative update installed.
2) Log into corporate profile (Intune policies applied).
3) Open VSCode or Chrome, type continuously and use touchpad to move cursor.
4) Occasionally observe a single left-click event without physical tap.

Observed logs / traces:
- Event Viewer (Windows Logs -> System) shows sporadic HIDCLASS warnings around the time of ghost clicks: "HID Input Driver reported unexpected input" (Event ID 1541).
- Device Manager shows HID-compliant touchpad driver version 3.2.1.45 (installed by Windows Update) whereas OEM driver previously was 2.9.0.12.
- ETW trace captured 2026-03-11 15:23 UTC shows an unsolicited input report from HID device 0x0A12 at the same timestamp as the user-observed ghost click.
- No blue screen or kernel dump captured; no consistent power state transitions.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced on two local TPG-14 v2 test units by installing the WU-provided driver (3.2.1.45). Reverted to OEM driver (2.9.0.12) and ghost clicks stopped during extended typing sessions.
- Checked Autopatch and Intune update rings: WU driver was pulled as part of the March cumulative on the Fast ring.
- Hypothesis: WU-provided HID driver introduces sensitivity change or misinterprets palm signals as discrete clicks under certain palm-rest electrical characteristics.
- Confirmed similar symptom referenced in vendor forum thread for a different OEM model after same WU package but not identical device.

Workaround applied:
- Rolled back driver to OEM 2.9.0.12 on 4 affected laptops and confirmed cessation of ghost clicks.
- Created an Intune temporary device configuration (script + Win32 app) to reinstall OEM driver and set a blocking policy for the WU driver version. Policy scheduled for cohort rollout tonight (2026-03-12 22:00 UTC) for all TPG-14 v2 devices.

Planned fix / next steps:
1) Push rollback package via Intune (Win32) for full fleet of TPG-14 v2 devices (deployment planned 2026-03-12).
2) Add a driver device configuration profile to block driver version 3.2.1.45 via Intune GPO equivalence until vendor releases a patch.
3) File upstream vendor SR with HID vendor and attach ETW traces + reproducer notes (ticket opened).
4) Update corporate imaging: bake OEM driver into the next image and modify Autopatch ring exclusions for the TPG-14 SKU until fix is released.
5) Monitor helpdesk queue for regressions for two weeks post-deployment and escalate if more devices surface.

Follow-ups / long-term:
- Vendor has indicated a potential fix timeline of ~2 weeks after triage.
- Engineering to consider a small telemetry datapoint to detect elevated input report rates near typing sessions (opt-in, privacy reviewed).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:40 - SRE (Kara Nguyen): Captured ETW trace and verified unsolicited HID input reports correlate to timestamps of user-reported ghost clicks.
2026-03-11 16:30 - Affected user (J. Morales): Confirmed workaround worked after receiving manual installer. Asking for fleet-wide remediation timeline.
Partial workaround deployed: OEM driver pushed to pilot cohort and full rollout scheduled. Root cause pending vendor driver fix. Follow-up: track vendor SR and update imaging to include OEM driver.

payload.description:
Issue summary: The ephemeral-service-account bootstrapper used by Private deployment onboarding is failing during automated provisioning. The controller attempts to create a short-lived GCP service account and then exchange credentials with our AWS assume-role chain. GCP returns a DENY on serviceAccount.create due to an organization-level deny constraint; simultaneously the AWS AssumeRole step requires a session tag 'env' which our token exchange flow is not supplying because the GCP SA creation never completes. Impact: new private deployments are stuck in 'initializing' and cannot attach dedicated GPU pools. A few recent onboards hit this (customer-facing but internal provisioning). Environment: prod-us-west private control plane and staging mirrors for verification.
Trigger private deployment onboarding via infra bootstrapper (service: private-deploy-runner, job: create-ephemeral-sa).
Bootstrapper calls GCP IAM API: projects/-/serviceAccounts:create with payload including displayName and labels.
On create success, bootstrapper uploads key and initiates AWS STS AssumeRole chain with session tags: expects 'env' tag.
Observe failure path when org deny constraint present or when GCP create returns PERMISSION_DENIED.
Result: bootstrapper retries then times out, leaving deployment in initializing state.
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z private-bootstrapper ERROR create-service-account: googleapi: Error 403: Request had insufficient authentication scopes., forbidden
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z private-bootstrapper WARN attempt=3 skipping assume-role: ephemeral SA not created
2026-03-10T14:12:20Z sts-exchange ERROR AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed: Missing required session tag: env
stacktrace snippets: bootstrapper.go:298 -> iam.go:112 -> cloudclients/gcp.go:77
03/10 15:00 - Confirmed error originates from organization Constraint 'constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountCreation' applied at folder level for project-parent-123 (applied via Terraform in infra-org).
03/10 16:20 - The bootstrapper is running with a delegating service account that has iam.serviceAccounts.create at project but org-level constraint overrides and denies creation. Reproducible in staging when the same policy is applied.
03/11 09:10 - AWS side: AssumeRole policy requires 'env' session tag by Condition: StringEquals: sts:TagKeys includes 'env' and Tag key-value must match caller's environment. Token exchange code path only populates tags on successful GCP SA + keyflow; since SA creation fails there are no tags.
03/11 10:00 - Hypothesis: two independent guardrails combined create a deadlock: GCP deny prevents SA creation, AWS assume-role enforces tags that are only set after SA creation.
Evelyn Park 2026-03-10: Raised after customer onboarding retries failed; attached bootstrapper logs. Requesting priority triage.
Diego Morales 2026-03-10: Investigating org constraints and bootstrapper flow. PoC: manually creating SA in project as org-admin succeeds only when constraint is relaxed.
SRE-Oncall 2026-03-11: Temporary mitigation: we can run a manual one-off create using a privileged operator account and then annotate deployment to skip bootstrapper, but this is manual and not scalable.
Security-Infra 2026-03-11: Org deny constraint was introduced to prevent uncontrolled SA creation after an audit. We need an approved automation exception flow rather than blanket relax.
Diego Morales 2026-03-12: Created PR to add a preflight check in bootstrapper to detect org constraints and surface clear actionable error. Also sketching an automation workflow to request just-in-time exception via existing JIT tooling. PRs listed in related_github_prs.
Evelyn Park 2026-03-12: Customer success informed about manual workaround and ETA for automated fix.
In progress: temporary manual workaround documented (operator SA creation + annotate deployment). Next steps: implement preflight check + JIT exception request flow in bootstrapper, and update org policy runbook. Security team to review exception design. Target: automated mitigation deployed to staging by 2026-03-18.
payload.summary: Ephemeral bootstrapper failing: GCP SA creation denied + AWS assume-role session tag mismatch blocks private deploy

Issue summary: After the March 11 macros service deployment (v2.7.0), several internal queues observed incorrect priority assignments. The priority enrichment matrix appears to overwrite explicit route priority fields when a channel macro template is applied.

Impact: Internal routing for support ops and oncall teams is misordering tickets; P1 tickets occasionally landing in lower-priority inboxes and missing SLA-driven escalation. This impacts internal SLAs and delays investigation for critical incidents.

Observed behavior: When a 'high-urgency' channel macro is attached to an incoming ticket, the enrichment pipeline applies matrix rules and sets priority to P3 in routing metadata, even though the route definition had priority=P1. The console view shows the route priority still as P1 but the routing decision uses the enriched value (P3).

Expected behavior: Enrichment should only add missing priority or append a suggested_priority field; it should not override explicit route.priority. Routing engine should prefer route config over enrichment unless a flag explicitly allows overwrite.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a synthetic ticket via internal webhook with route_id=ops-oncall and priority=P1. 2) Attach macro template channel: "high-urgency:notify-escalation". 3) Observe enrichment logs in macros-service: enrichment.applied -> priority=3. 4) Inspect routing decision in rule-evaluator: selected_queue uses priority=3. 5) Confirm ticket lands in ops-inbox (P3 queue).

Logs & artifacts: See macros-service logs (mar-11 21:10 UTC) at /var/log/macros/macros-2026-03-11.log and rule-evaluator trace id re-0a3b6f. Example log snippets included in investigation notes.

Immediate mitigation: Rollback macros-service to v2.6.4 or patch enrichment pipeline to set enrichment.suggested_priority instead of priority. Mitigation applied: temporary feature-flag enabled to skip priority enrichment for routes with explicit priority on 2026-03-12 03:45 UTC.
POST synthetic ticket to /internal/v1/tickets with route_id=ops-oncall and priority=P1
Attach macro template header X-Macro-Template: high-urgency:notify-escalation
Stream logs from macros-service and filter enrichment.applied events
Check rule-evaluator trace for selected_queue and resulting priority metadata
Enrichment pipeline sets priority=P3 when macro is applied
Routing engine uses enrichment.priority over route config
Console shows route priority=P1 but ticket delivered to lower-priority queue
Enrichment should not overwrite explicit route.priority
Routing should prefer configured route.priority unless overwrite is enabled
SLAs should trigger escalation based on configured priority
2026-03-11 21:12 UTC: Initial alert from #internal-support that two P1 tickets missed oncall alerting
SRE (M. Li) pulled re-0a3b6f trace; rule-evaluator shows priority metadata = 3 pre-route-selection

Hypothesis: New code path applies enrichment and writes to ticket.priority instead of ticket.suggested_priority, then rule-evaluator does not check 'is_source_explicit'

Evan Patel (Reporter) - 2026-03-12: Noticed pattern after deploy; opened ticket and flagged as P1. Added preliminary logs.
