payload.description:
Issue summary:
After the scheduled IdP certificate/nonce rotation on 2026-03-10 18:30 UTC, several terraform-runner workers started returning 401/invalid_grant during token exchange. This prevents CI jobs from provisioning or applying state in prod-us-west.
Multiple CI pipelines using terraform-runner are failing to authenticate; customer-facing services cannot deploy configuration changes. Roughly 8-12 runners affected, ~25% of job throughput reduced in prod-us-west during the window.
1) Trigger a terraform-runner job that performs state operations using service account token.
2) Observe runner logs during authentication handshake with sso-proxy.
3) Intermittent failures show 'nonce_mismatch' during token-exchange step.
Note: issue correlated with IdP rotation window and is not reproduced outside that window.
- Failures spike from 2026-03-10T18:31:00Z to 2026-03-10T18:48:00Z.
- Logs show new cookies from IdP with rotated nonce but some intermediate sso-proxy instances still validate against old nonce index.
- A subset of runners retried successfully after 90s; others required manual restart.
- No TLS errors observed; failures limited to token exchange path (500s/401s).
Race between IdP nonce roll-forward and the sso-proxy in-memory cache of valid nonces. Some sso-proxy replicas used stale nonce validators causing token-exchange to fail if request routed to those pods immediately after rotation.
- Support (Aisha) confirmed scope and collected logs, ticket opened.
- Oncall SRE (Carlos) checked sso-proxy deployment: rolling restart was in progress at rotation time due to unrelated config deploy.
- sso-proxy instances show two different accepted-nonce values across replicas when queried.
- Reviewed IdP rotation runbook; runbook expects sticky deployment ordering but that was not honored due to concurrent deploys.
- Reproduced locally by forcing nonce update while half of sso-proxy cluster uses old validators.
- Related issue INT-271001 shows previous oauth refresh edge cases during overlapping rotations.
auth-service: 2026-03-10T18:42:11Z ERROR token-exchange failed: nonce_mismatch
ssh-proxy: 2026-03-10T18:42:12Z WARN stale-cookie detected for runner-id: tr-09a3

Additional notes:
Restart affected terraform-runner pods (kubectl rollout restart) or temporarily scale down/up sso-proxy to force validator refresh. Runners that were restarted recovered and reauthenticated within ~30-90s.
Mitigation: sso-proxy patched to persist nonce history in Redis and to accept last N nonce indices for 2 minutes post-rotation. Runbook updated to pause unrelated sso-proxy deploys during IdP rotations. Patch deployed 2026-03-12 08:40 UTC to prod-us-west.
Follow-up: schedule a dry-run of rotation with SRE and Identity team. Postmortem draft created in Confluence.
sso-proxy v1.14.2: nonce-history persistence to redis; accept last 2 nonce indices for 120s; added readiness gating during IdP rotations.
1) Runbook update merged and published.
2) Coordinate rotation windows with SRE via scheduled maintenance calendar.
3) Add integration test to rotation test harness.
4) Notify Platform teams of new sso-proxy behavior.
Mitigated in prod; monitoring in place for two rotations to validate durability

Issue summary: Legal has received a civil subpoena requesting a narrow set of customer transcripts tied to a specific account for calendar year 2025. Legal requests a timeboxed credentialed access path so we can produce pseudonymized replay traces required for evidence.

Impact: Controlled internal access only. Data contains potentially sensitive PII in user prompts; exposure risk if full raw payloads are shared. Request must satisfy legal chain-of-custody and minimize re-identification risk.

Requestor: Legal (N. Chen), Case ID: SUBP-2026-014; Customer account hash: acct_0x9bfc (lawyer provided full account identifier internally).

Data needed: Selective replayable traces for matching session IDs between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31. Each trace should include timestamps, request/response token counts, model version, and redacted/pseudonymized request text where identifiers are replaced with consistent tokens (e.g., <PERSON_1>, <EMAIL_1>). The legal team specifically requests the request/response sequence in a format suitable for evidence review (CSV + gzipped JSONL) and a short provenance report describing how pseudonymization was performed.

Constraints:
- Access must be time-limited (48 hours) and audited.
- Deliverable must be stored encrypted and KMS-wrapped; only Legal and the named SRE/forensics analyst may decrypt.
- No uncontrolled copy to external accounts.
- We must include a checksum and notarized extraction log for chain-of-custody.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Windows clients moving between wired dock and Wi-Fi (fast LAN switching / NIC preemption) intermittently lose access to internal services (k8s cluster APIs, internal console) while external traffic continues to function. Affected clients show WireGuard interface re-binding to a different route metric after the NIC change, and split-tunnel routes bound to the old interface remain in kernel routing table for ~30–90s. This causes TCP connections to internal IPs to blackhole until routes are reconciled or the WG interface is restarted.

Impact:
- ~7% of office staff and hybrid workers in US region have reported transient failures to reach internal dashboards and services when docking/undocking or switching networks.
- Automated jobs (dev laptops running local test harnesses with port-forwarding to cluster) occasionally fail and require manual restart.

Environment:
- Platform: Corporate Windows 11 (22H2) with corporate Dock USB-C and 802.11ax Wi‑Fi.
- VPN: WireGuard-based Zero-Trust agent configured as split-tunnel (internal CIDR routes pushed locally).
- DNS: Internal suffixes are pushed via DHCP/WPAD; Windows sometimes retains old DNS suffix search order after NIC changes.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Connect laptop to Ethernet via dock (WireGuard establishes, routes for 10.0.0.0/8 installed with metric 50).
2) Undock or disable Ethernet (fast LAN switch), client moves traffic to Wi‑Fi; WireGuard interface remains up but kernel route metrics change (WG route moves to metric 300).
3) Split-tunnel routes referencing internal CIDRs remain attached to previous NIC route (metric 50) and are no longer reachable, causing internal TCP flows to hang.
4) After ~30–90s routes are reprogrammed or user restarts WireGuard agent and connectivity restores.

Observed logs and metrics:
- System event logs: network profile change events (NetworkListManager) at switch times.
- WireGuard agent logs: interface stays listed UP; agent reports same endpoint/peer state. No obvious tunnel re-establish.
- Routing table snapshot: duplicate internal route entries for same CIDR with different interface indices and metrics.
- Endpoint traces to internal k8s API show SYN retransmits; external https flows succeed.

Hypothesis:
1) Windows fast NIC preemption changes interface metrics before the agent updates split-tunnel routes, leaving stale per-interface routes in the table.
2) WireGuard agent does not react to the specific network-change event sequence on Windows and therefore does not reprogram routes atomically.
3) DNS suffix order persistence compounds the problem for name-based services, causing name lookup to prefer an unreachable resolver briefly.

Investigation notes to date:
- Reproduced on two different laptop models with corporate dock.
- Packet capture shows encapsulated WireGuard traffic continues but routing selects wrong next-hop for internal CIDR.
- Compared behavior with macOS laptops: mac handles reprogramming immediately and does not leave duplicate CIDR routes.
- SRE observed RETRIES spikes on api-gateway per-host when user population spikes during EV charging (docking area).

Temporary workaround:
- Educate affected users: Restarting the WireGuard client or toggling the adapter (disable/enable the WireGuard interface) restores connectivity immediately.
- Interim support script: run `wg-quick down && wg-quick up` or run the Windows agent's "rebind routes" helper. Deployed via Intune for a small pilot.

Proposed remediation steps:
- Short term: update Windows WireGuard agent to listen to NetworkListManager and call route reconciliation on NIC change events. Add an expo-backoff retry to reprogram split-tunnel routes.
- Medium term: change split-tunnel route program to prefer interface-independent routes (where supported) or use next-hop-based routes that survive interface swaps.
- Long term: add deterministic route reconciliation in agent startup and a small kernel monitor that prunes stale duplicate CIDR entries.

Next actions assigned:
- Marcus Chen: capture additional packet traces and produce minimal repro script (by 2026-03-13).
- Nora Patel: roll out support helper script via Intune to 20 pilot users (by 2026-03-12).

Issue summary: An on-call engineer reported sudden loss of SMS delivery for company number and then received unexpected password reset confirmations for multiple services. Initial triage indicates a likely SIM port / carrier takeover attempt that was used to attempt MFA bypass for Redwood SSO and an external SaaS account.

Impact: Potential account takeover attempt of one high-privilege engineer (on-call). No confirmed data exfiltration at time of ticket creation. Temporary access attempts observed to console and vendor portals. Could lead to lateral access if additional factors (device, tokens) were compromised.

Environment: prod | us-east (user's primary region). Affected identity provider: Okta SSO (company-managed), mobile carrier: external (redacted), device: iPhone 14 (personal with company MDM enrollment in progress).
On-call engineer temporarily unable to receive SMS MFA codes; attempted authentications to Redwood Console and PagerDuty during incident window. No successful invalid console sessions found after immediate containment, but one vendor SaaS account shows suspicious password-reset acceptance attempt. Customer-facing services unaffected.
1) User reports SMS delivery failure at 2026-03-13T22:11:00Z.
2) User receives SMS from carrier confirming number porting at 2026-03-13T22:15:00Z (user did NOT authorize).
3) Automated password-reset emails for third-party vendor arrive at 2026-03-13T22:22:00Z.
4) Unauthorized MFA challenges to Okta appear at 2026-03-13T22:25:00Z using SMS channel.
5) SOC triggered account disable and factor removal at 2026-03-13T22:30:00Z.
Auth logs: Okta sign-in attempts from IPs in different metro (city: unknown) at 2026-03-13T22:25Z. MFA method: SMS delivered to company number marked as delivered by carrier but user reported no device messages. Device registration: new device enrollment attempt recorded for user at 22:28Z but blocked by MDM policy. PagerDuty log: SMS fail and subsequent push delivery to device succeeded after MDM push at 22:32Z. Carrier confirmation email (forwarded by user) shows port request ticket number: CARRIER-876412.
Relevant log IDs: okta_auth_20260313_2252, mdm_enroll_20260313_2258, pd_inc_20260313_2255.
Hypothesis 1: SIM porting social-engineered via carrier support (caller posed as employee and provided spoofed account details).
Hypothesis 2: SIM swap coordinated with compromised secondary email to confirm port.
Observed: Carrier ticket indicates porting request originated from VOIP gateway number +1-800-XXX-XXXX. No successful console sessions from new device after containment. Correlation: recent spearphish voicemail to employee about 'benefits update' received 8 hours prior (see linked Slack thread).
Next steps: request carrier port reversal, collect CPNI trace, escalate to legal if carrier cooperation insufficient, rotate user service tokens, require hardware MFA for on-call role.
- Disabled user's SSO account at 2026-03-13T22:31Z.
- Removed SMS as a factor in Okta for the account and enforced push-only MFA and YubiKey requirement for on-call group.
- Blocklisted source IP ranges in WAF for temporary containment.
- Initiated incident call with SOC and Support at 22:40Z.
- Opened ticket with carrier (CARRIER-876412) requesting emergency reversal.
- Forced logout of all active sessions and rotated service api keys that the user had access to.
- Notified Legal and HR to prepare for disclosure if escalation needed.
Containment in place: user account disabled and SMS factor removed; hardware MFA enforced for on-call group. Carrier reversal pending. No confirmed exfiltration. Case remains open pending carrier trace and confirmation of no further unauthorized activity.
Follow-up: implement org-wide ban on SMS-only MFA for admin-tier roles and update on-call runbook to require hardware keys. Post-incident: SOC postmortem and PSIRT writeup planned.
Ava Martinez (reporter) - 2026-03-13T22:20Z: Received voicemail with 'benefits update' link earlier today; then SMS stopped working. Forwarded carrier email and screenshots.
Ravi Patel (assignee) - 2026-03-13T22:35Z: Disabled user and removed SMS MFA. Pushing YubiKey requirement for on-call now. Kicking off incident bridge.
SOC Lead (Jordan Kim) - 2026-03-13T22:50Z: SOC confirmed suspicious okta auth attempts; blocking IPs and revoking session cookies. Collecting carrier ticket details.
MDM Engineer (Lin Zhao) - 2026-03-14T08:12Z: Blocked new device enrollment; existing company-managed devices re-verified. No MDM policy breaches observed.
Legal (Priya Singh) - 2026-03-14T09:05Z: Preparing templates for regulatory notification if carrier confirms porting and proof of fraudulent consent.
1) Confirm carrier CPNI trace shows fraudulent authorization. 2) Roll out hardware-MFA requirement to all admin-tier groups by 2026-03-20. 3) Add SIM-swap detection signals to our identity pipeline (monitor for churn of SMS factor, sudden SMS delivery failures).

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled rotation of the API gateway's JWT signing key, in-flight CI/CD builds that had been running for >30m experienced authentication rejections and were force-evicted. Impact: Multiple long-running release and e2e pipelines across internal clusters failed mid-run with HTTP 401/403 on subsequent agent heartbeats and artifact uploads. Environment: internal CI fleet (self-hosted runners) in k8s clusters: ci-us-east-1-a, ci-eu-west-1-b. Rotation window: 2026-03-10 03:00-03:15 UTC.

Observed symptoms: runner websocket connections stayed open but CI jobs reported 'authorization failed' when trying to POST logs or renew session tokens; some runners retried and re-registered successfully, others aborted and left orphaned pods. No node restarts. No Vault rewrap coincident with event (Vault Ops confirms no rewrap during that window).

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Start a long-running job (>20m) on a self-hosted runner that periodically renews its session via /agent/refresh (JWT header).
2) Rotate gateway JWT signing key and replace JWKS endpoint served by the gateway without a dual-key grace period.
3) Observe the runner's next refresh attempt being rejected with 401 and build aborting.

Logs / errors (representative):
- runner-agent[pid]: POST /agent/refresh -> 401 Unauthorized {"error": "invalid signature"}
- ci-orchestrator: job 12345 -> Cancelled: authentication failure during artifact upload
- gateway-audit: key_id change event: old kid=gw-sig-v12 -> new kid=gw-sig-v13 (2026-03-10T03:05Z)

Workaround applied: Re-deployed gateway with dual-JWKS support (accept both old and new kid) and restarted CI ingress to allow older tokens for 10m grace period. Affected long-running jobs were retried from last checkpoint where possible.

Request: Post-rotation runbook and safer rotation procedure for gateways that sign agent-facing tokens; consider deploying a) key rollover support with overlap, b) token versioning/rotation TTL recommendations for runner SDK, and c) detection/alerting for mass 401 spikes tied to key rotations.
2026-03-10 - 03:22 UTC - Maya Patel: Triage started. Reproducer attempts queued against ci-us-east-1-a. Noticed 401s spike at 03:05 UTC correlating with gateway key_id change.
2026-03-10 - 04:10 UTC - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed gateway published new JWKS and removed old key immediately. Rolling back to accept both keys reduced failures. Patching gateway to support key overlap now.
2026-03-11 - 09:14 UTC - Release Eng (Priya Nair): Affected two release pipelines (release/2026-03-09-candidate and nightly-e2e). We saw mid-run cancellations; will rerun jobs that support checkpointing. Requesting a formal runbook to avoid recurrence.
2026-03-12 - 11:05 UTC - Auth Eng (Noah Kim): Draft PR added to infra repo to add dual-key acceptance and JWKS versioning. Also adding metrics to alert on >5% agent 401 rate within 5m after any key rotation event. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4890
Correlation matrix shows 401 spike exactly aligned with gateway key_id rotation event timestamp (03:05 UTC).
Runner SDK uses JWTs signed by gateway and refreshes every 60s; tokens have 10m TTL. During rotation we lacked a grace window in gateway, so tokens signed with old key were rejected immediately at first refresh after 03:05.
No Vault KMS rewraps or service account key changes detected in the same window; authentication failure localized to gateway signature verification.
Some runners retried with a fresh registration flow and obtained new tokens successfully; long-running jobs that did not trigger a full re-registration remained stuck because their vended token was still valid but rejected by signature check at refresh step.
Hypothesis: immediate key replacement without JWKS overlap caused stateless auth to break for any actor that held tokens signed by old key but attempted operations validated against the new JWKS.
We also observed an edge-case where proxies with aggressive caching of JWKS (internal CDN) continued serving stale keys for ~2m, causing a mixed verification environment.
Short-term: Reconfigured gateway to accept both old and new signing keys for a 15m overlap window during rotations. Deployed fix to CI ingress to clear JWKS CDN caches faster.
Medium-term: Merged PR implementing graceful key rollover and JWKS versioning (infra PR #4890). Added a deploy-time verification step that exercises agent refresh flow before finalizing key switch.
Long-term actions: Update runbook to require a minimum 10m overlap when rotating gateway signing keys, add monitoring alert that ties key rotation events to agent 401 rates, and update runner SDK to detect key-rotation-related 401 and automatically attempt re-registration flow with exponential backoff.
Follow-up: Schedule knowledge-transfer with Release Engineering to walk through runbook. Add a postmortem entry in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood-inference/internal/pm/postmortems/INT-99555
payload.summary: CI runners evicted from long-running builds after gateway JWT signing-key rotation

Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reported a sustained p95 latency increase and a rising number of 504 gateway errors across their dedicated GPU reservation during evening traffic (18:00–20:00 PDT). The spike began after a tenant mix change when a new high-concurrency tenant was onboarded into the same reservation. Initial hypothesis points to GPU affinity/misalignment combined with autoscaler target sizing that did not account for the new job mix.

Impact:
- Multiple BrightCart endpoints experienced p95 latency increase from ~120ms to 900–1,200ms and an elevated rate of 504s (~2% of requests) for ~90 minutes.
- Customer reports degraded user experience in production peak window; marketing campaign affected.

Timeline (local times):
- 2026-03-10 17:45 PDT: BrightCart opened a support chat reporting slow responses.
- 2026-03-10 17:58 PDT: Support created ticket SUP-274983.
- 2026-03-10 18:05 PDT: Observability shows p95 trending upward; spike correlated with new tenant traffic ingestion.
- 2026-03-10 18:20 PDT: Mitigation: routing fallback to smaller model variant for high-latency routes.
- 2026-03-10 18:45 PDT: Ops increased autoscale target for the reservation as an interim measure.

Environment:
- Dedicated reservation: resv-cc-84 (us-west-2)
- Node types: A100-sliced and V100-legacy mix
- Serving runtime: 3.14.1
- Autoscaler policy: conservative target (min:4, desired:6, max:12) with scale cooldown 300s

Steps to reproduce (observed reproducible pattern):
1) Run mixed traffic with a small number of long-sequence streaming requests concurrently with a burst of short-chat requests from a second tenant.
2) Observe GPU allocation and affinity mapping via /debug/affinity endpoint.
3) Watch queue length and per-GPU microbatching metrics.

Observed behavior:
- GPUs servicing the long-seq tenant saturated VRAM and started preempting KV caches, leading to increased microbatch latency and head-of-line blocking.
- Scheduler placed new short-chat pods onto already hot GPUs due to affinity scoring not penalizing per-sequence memory usage.
- Autoscaler did not scale quickly enough because observed throughput deltas were smoothed by the averaging window.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Shifted BrightCart heavier routes to fallback model variant (gptx-2.7b-16k-quant-lite) for low-latency paths.
- Increased desired autoscale target from 6 to 9 for resv-cc-84.
- Isolated the high-concurrency tenant onto a separate reservation as a stopgap.

Next steps planned:
- Short term: Tune affinity scoring to consider per-sequence VRAM footprint and adapt scheduler penalties.
- Short-to-mid term: Adjust autoscaler sensitivity (shorter smoothing window during peak hours) and lower cooldown for dedicated pools.
- Postmortem: Run capacity planning for mixed job mixes and update onboarding checklist for new tenants into reservations.
Start reservation resv-cc-84 with current autoscale policy (min 4 desired 6 max 12)
Inject two tenants: Tenant A long-sequence streaming requests (avg seq len 24k), Tenant B short-chat bursty traffic
Monitor /metrics and /debug/affinity; observe per-GPU queue length and KV cache miss rate
Watch autoscaler logs for scaling decisions and the smoothing window behavior
2026-03-10T18:03:21Z resv-cc-84 serving-runtime[pid:4210] INFO p95 latency increased to 920ms - active_queue=118 gpu0_vram=87% gpu1_vram=90%
2026-03-10T18:04:05Z scheduler WARNING assigned pod chat-req-22 to gpu1 (affinity_score=0.68) despite gpu1_vram>85%
2026-03-10T18:06:40Z autoscaler INFO smoothing_window average_throughput_delta=+3% decision=none

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:02 - BrightCart (Customer): Noted improved latency after mitigation but requested a permanent fix and capacity confirmation for upcoming campaign.
Affinity scoring: discovered it ignores per-request sequence length and KV-cache pressure; low penalty allowed colocating heavy long-seq and bursty short requests.
Autoscaler: configured with a 5-minute smoothing window and 300s cooldown; with mixed workloads the instantaneous need was masked and scaling lagged during the spike.
Serving runtime: KV cache thrashing observed on GPUs with >80% VRAM, causing serialization of microbatches and p95 degradation.
Hypothesis: Combination of scheduler affinity mismatch + autoscale smoothing window caused sustained tail latency, not a single GPU hardware fault.
Mitigations applied: isolated noisy tenant and increased desired autoscale target to 9; routed latency-sensitive endpoints to lighter model variant. Engineering tasks opened to: 1) update affinity scoring to include estimated KV VRAM per-request (PR linked), 2) reduce autoscaler smoothing window during peak hours and lower cooldown for dedicated reservations, 3) add automated onboarding checks to flag high-KV workloads before co-locating. Long-term: capacity planning and reservation placement policy update. Ticket remains In Progress until affinity change is deployed and observed over two peak cycles.
payload.summary: High p95 latency and 504s across reserved GPU reservation after tenant mix change — suspected GPU affinity and autoscaler sizing gap

payload.description:
Multiple employees reported intermittent loss of internal services and failed WireGuard handshakes when switching between personal hotspot and corporate Wi‑Fi. Symptoms include long pauses during ssh/kshell connect, stalled LLM inference calls from internal tooling, and zero traffic observed through the WireGuard peer despite tunnel remaining logically up.
Connect MacBook (macOS 13.x Intel + Thunderbolt dock) to cellular hotspot and start an active WireGuard session to corporate gateway.
Switch to corporate SSID (802.11ax enterprise) and roam between two nearby APs (manual roam trigger or walk between desks).
Observe WireGuard handshake stalls, KV-cache-backed inference RPCs drop or hang, and internal services report client IP mismatch.
Check client and firewall logs for UDP flow entries and DHCP lease events.
Client tcpdump excerpt: '14:23:02.123 IP 10.52.1.82.51820 > gw.example.net.51820: UDP, length 1200' followed by '14:23:02.456 IP 10.52.1.82.51820 > gw.example.net.51820: UDP, length 0 (encap)' then no replies for ~30s.
DHCP server log: 'DHCPDISCOVER from 84:2b:14:... rapid-renew, offering same IP 10.52.1.82', 'DHCPACK issued with lease-time 600s, renew requested immediately'
Branch firewall anti-spoof log: 'SPOOF-DROP: interface br0: src 10.52.1.82 seen on port AP3 then port AP7 within 3s' (rule 3104)
Zero-trust agent logs on client: 'network-change detected: ifindex 5->7, rebind failed: socket busy'
Hypothesis 1: AP power-save and aggressive client roaming cause very short DHCP renews / rapid rebindings; firewall anti-spoof rules consider the quick IP appearance on different APs as duplicate/malicious and drop UDP.
Hypothesis 2: Endpoint zero-trust agent doesn't gracefully rebind WireGuard socket on interface change when Thunderbolt dock interfaces reorder, causing in-transit UDP packets to be dropped by downstream NAT.
Packet captures show client continues to send large UDP packets without receiving responses; firewall logs show drops due to 'source-on-different-port' enforcement.
Replication: reproduced on macOS Intel and one Windows 11 laptop with vendor NIC driver 22.30; did not reproduce on Android hotspot clients.
On APs: disable aggressive client power-save / enable low-latency roaming mode for affected AP group.
On firewall: temporarily relax anti-spoof threshold to allow 5s grace period for same src IP on different AP ports (rule 3104 -> 3112 emulation).
On endpoints: instruct affected users to toggle Wi‑Fi off before switching networks to force clean rebind.
Endpoint team to push updated zero-trust agent that explicitly closes and recreates WireGuard socket on network-change event.
Network: Update AP group profile to 802.11k/minimize power-save timer, and schedule config change for branch floor A (ETA 2026-03-15).
Security: Patch firewall rule to add short grace window for DHCP-renew related IP movements (owner: Priya Shah).
Endpoint: Add network-change rebind logic to zero-trust agent PR (see related_github_prs) and QA across macOS/Windows.
SRE: Add dashboard panel highlighting 'WireGuard handshake failure rate' by AP and client MAC for 24h window.
Ava Chen (Reporter) 2026-03-10: 'Received three Slack reports in #it-support within an hour. All impacted users were near AP cluster A3-A7.'
Marco Ruiz (Assignee) 2026-03-11: 'Confirmed reproducible on my test MacBook with Thunderbolt dock attached. Captured pcap and firewall logs, uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-data/INT-991000/pcaps.tar.gz'
Priya Shah (Firewall) 2026-03-11: 'We can relax the anti-spoof rule for the AP VLAN for up to 10 minutes, but prefer a targeted 5s window. Will coordinate maintenance window.'
Endpoint Team 2026-03-12: 'We can land a rebind patch to the agent but need two days of QA; will provide an alpha build for affected users tomorrow.'
payload.summary: Office AP power-save / DHCP rapid-renew causes WireGuard handshake to stall and internal service blackholes

2026-03-10T17:12:00Z Marco Li: Confirmed reproduce in staging. Hash truncation (to 12 chars) is the culprit — two different env seeds hashed to same prefix. Temporarily patched pipeline to include CI_BUILD_ID; re-ran failing job and it succeeded. Need a permanent fix.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Automated environment bootstrap (infra/provisioner) fails when creating a service account because the generated account_id collides with an existing account_id in another project.

Impact:
- New private/development GCP environments fail to finish onboarding; terraform/apply aborts with 409 errors.
- Affects Dedicated/Private onboarding pipelines that rely on deterministic account naming.
- Blocks a small number of envs in eu-west and us-east while we investigate.

Environment:
- Component: infra/auto-provisioner (terraform wrapper + custom python helper)
- Affected projects: redwood-private-eu-west-003 (example), redwood-dedicated-eu-west-001 (example)
- Regions observed: eu-west, us-east
- When reproducing: staging and prod-like CI runners invoking provisioning workflow

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run the onboarding job for a new environment using the standard pipeline (provisioner v2.4.1).
2) Provisioner calls helper to compute service account account_id using deterministic hash(account_name + env_seed) truncated to 12 chars.
3) Terraform applies google_service_account resource and fails with a 409 response from IAM.

Observed behavior:
- Terraform error: "googleapi: Error 409: Service account with the given accountId already exists, alreadyExists"
- Provisioner log shows two different projects resolving to the same account_id (e.g. redwood-llm-provisioner-9f2b7c1a).
- IAM audit log shows creation attempt in target project followed by a duplicate creation attempt that resolves to existing SA in a different project id.

Expected behavior:
- Provisioner should generate unique account_ids across projects to avoid collisions; onboarding should succeed.

Logs/Artifacts:
- Provisioner log snippet (CI run 2026-03-10T14:22Z): "create service account redwood-llm-provisioner-9f2b7c1a -> 409 alreadyExists"
- gcloud IAM audit: principal: infra-provisioner@redwood-ci.iam.gserviceaccount.com attempted createServiceAccount; response: AlreadyExists
- Terraform plan shows new google_service_account resource with account_id = "redwood-llm-provisioner-9f2b7c1a"

Temporary workaround:
- Manually pick a unique suffix and re-run apply (team: infra-ops).
- Short term: modify pipeline to append CI_BUILD_ID to account_id for new envs to guarantee uniqueness (applied to two failing envs, success verified).

Notes on scope:
- This is not a GCP platform outage; it is a deterministic-naming collision inside our provisioning tool.
- Risk: If left, will continue to intermittently block environment bootstrap for new projects created with colliding seeds.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 14:47 - Security (Evan Ortiz): Confirmed no privilege escalation observed. Recommended adding an audit alert for 409 createServiceAccount events to SRE alerting channel.
Checked terraform apply logs and IAM admin audit logs in Cloud Logging to correlate project IDs to the 409 errors.
Reproduced locally: deterministic_hash('redwood-llm-provisioner','env-seed-abc') truncated to 12 returned same token as hash('redwood-llm-provisioner','env-seed-xyc') due to truncation and collision in algorithm (birthday paradox at truncated length).
GCP error message: 'AlreadyExists: Service account with the given accountId already exists.' The API returns the project_id that owns the existing account in the audit entry — used this to enumerate collisions.
Provisioner code path: provisioner/helpers/sa_namer.py uses sha256 -> hex -> first 12 chars. Collision rate estimated ~1e-6 per new env, but deterministic seeds increase likelihood between certain env names.
CI workaround applied: append CI_BUILD_ID or timestamp to account_id when invoked from CI; manual remediation applied to two blocked envs and verified success.
Security review: no cross-project binding automatically granted because of collision; create call fails, so no credential leakage.
Work in progress — root cause identified (hash truncation collision). Short-term mitigations applied (CI append fallback). Next steps: merge PR to change account_id algo to include project id + longer hash (24 chars), add pre-flight collision check against org-wide service account index, and add alerting for 409 createServiceAccount events. Targeted rollout: provisioner v2.5.0.
PRs: infra/pull/7345 modifies SA naming; provisioner/pull/502 adds collision tests and preflight check. Plan to deploy to staging 2026-03-18 and to prod 2026-03-22 after smoke tests.
payload.summary: Service account name-hash collision during automated provisioner blocks GCP env bootstrap

payload.description:
Issue summary: New hires and some service accounts are intermittently unable to finish SSO login to internal developer tools (console, runbook editor). Failures began after a recent Okta claim-normalization rollout. Impact: onboarding blocked for ~4 hires, intermittent 403s for automation jobs, delayed oncall provisioning. User-facing error is '403 Forbidden - missing role claim'.
1) Attempt SSO login to console with Okta user that has long group/entitlement attributes (multi-org membership).
2) Observe redirect back to console with 403 and claim-missing error in UI, or immediate 403 for API clients using the same token.
3) Reproduce more reliably by creating a test Okta user with >1500 char 'groups' attribute and initiating auth flow via identity-proxy.
Users with valid Okta groups should receive RBAC roles and be able to log in; service accounts should exchange tokens successfully.
Identity-proxy drops/truncates the SSO header containing normalized role/group claims when payload exceeds ~1200 bytes; downstream RBAC code receives truncated claim, fails role resolution, returns 403.
2026-03-10T09:14:22Z identity-proxy gw=proxy-5fdc: WARN claim-header truncated: original_len=1682 trimmed_len=482
2026-03-10T09:14:22Z console svc: ERROR role-resolution failed: missing 'entitlements' claim for user uid=u-3748
2026-03-10T09:16:03Z auth svc: INFO token-exchange success for svc-account-sso (short-claims)
Link to support thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0SUPPORT/p1646981123000700
Ava Martinez (reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed this during batch onboarding; several new hires hit the same error after Okta claim-normalization rollout yesterday. Attach test user examples.
On-call Identity (Ravi Kapoor) - 2026-03-10: Spun up reproducer with long groups attribute; identity-proxy logs show header truncation. Paging network infra to check edge-proxy header limits.
Network Infra (Liam O'Connor) - 2026-03-11: Edge proxy (ingress-nginx) has default header buffer size of 8k; proxy isn't truncating. Observed truncation inside identity-proxy service at request header assembly step.
SRE (Jin Park) - 2026-03-11: Hypothesis: claim-transform lambda now produces expanded JSON which is serialized into a single header; identity-proxy enforces a 1.2k per-header limit. Need short-term workaround to compress or split claims across headers.
Identity Eng (Ravi Kapoor) - 2026-03-12: Implemented temporary pruning of non-essential entitlements for users in 'self_serve' orgs; rollout to canary reduced 403s for repro users. Full fix in progress.
Confirmed: failures correlate to users/groups with large aggregated claims after claim-normalization change (rolled 2026-03-09).
Identity-proxy code (header_builder) uses single header 'x-rdwd-claims' and truncates payload to 1200 bytes with a WARN log. This is the truncation point causing RBAC mismatches.
Edge ingress nginx and cloud load balancer are passing headers intact; upstream logs show proxy-side trimming, not network drop.
Reproducer: Okta test user 'onboard-longgroups' with 42 group memberships -> x-rdwd-claims length 1682 -> truncated to 482 -> role resolution fails.
Temporary mitigation reduced exposure by stripping rarely-used entitlement keys for users in self_serve orgs; not acceptable as permanent fix for enterprise/private customers.
Potential root causes: (A) claim-normalization expanded arrays into verbose strings, (B) identity-proxy header size config intentionally conservative to avoid downstream system limits, (C) lack of split-header support in identity-proxy.
Mitigation applied (2026-03-12): claim-normalization trimmed to only include RBAC-relevant groups for users in 'self_serve' and 'dev' orgs; canary rollout to prod-us-west succeeded for repro cases.
Planned permanent fix: identity-proxy PR #5821 to implement header chunking (split x-rdwd-claims across x-rdwd-claims-1..N) and update console/service to reassemble claims. Target deploy: 2026-03-17.
Follow-up: update runbook 'SSO-Claim-Truncation' in Confluence and add exponential alerts when identity-proxy emits 'claim-header truncated' WARN logs.
Workaround for affected hires: manual RBAC grant by Support (temporary) until full rollout; documented steps in support response template.
INT ticket to track PR and rollout: INT-101045 (ensure to pick unique key after creation).
Add monitoring alert: identity-proxy.warn.claim_truncated -> PagerDuty if rate > 5/min over 5m.
Confluence: /internal/runbooks/sso-claim-size -> include guidance for Okta mapping and limits.
Postmortem item: evaluate claim-normalization expansion and add size regression tests to CI.
payload.summary: Identity proxy header truncation prevents new hire onboarding & tool login

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several employees in the SF office reported VPN disconnects when roaming between APs on the 5GHz mesh. Symptom correlates with APs configured in bridge mode with 4-address (4addr) enabled. Impact: intermittent IKEv2 (UDP 500/4500) NAT-T negotiation failures; users experience brief drops (~10-30s) and repeated rekey attempts. No mass outage, but reproducible for specific APs and clients.
Moderate internal impact: engineers lose VPN tunnel during building-level roaming and reconnects are slow. Affects productivity in-office but not remote workers. ~8 distinct reports in 48h.
Affected SSID: redwood-corp; AP models: Aruba IAP-535 (firmware 8.5.0.3) and OpenWRT bridge nodes in meeting rooms. VPN: IKEv2 strongSwan on client and rtr-edge firewall using NAT (AWS Transit Gateway + on-prem router). Environment: prod-us-west (SF office subnet 10.24.12.0/22).
1) Join redwood-corp SSID on macOS Big Sur/Monterey and Ubuntu 22.04 laptops. 2) Establish IKEv2 VPN tunnel to edge. 3) Walk between two APs served by a bridge-mode WAP that has 4addr enabled (AP1 -> AP2). 4) Observe VPN rekey/teardown in client logs and intermittent 4500/500 drops in packet captures.
strongSwan logs show repeated "NAT-T keepalive" and "no response to informational" then 'failed to establish CHILD_SA' messages. tcpdump on client shows UDP 4500 packets leaving with original client IP but replies arrive with bridged MAC/address mapping that conntrack considers mismatched. conntrack on router shows ephemeral NAT entries expiring when source MAC changes with 4addr bridging.
IKEv2 NAT-T should survive AP-to-AP roaming with no NAT state loss; UDP packets should be correctly NATed and tolerated across layer-2 handoffs.
03/10 09:20 - Triage: Collected client strongSwan logs and tcpdumps from affected user laptop.
03/10 11:40 - Observed that APs running bridge mode with 4addr send frames where the original client MAC is preserved but outer headers change; this led to the on-prem router seeing alternating source MACs during a short roam.
03/11 08:05 - Reproduced in lab by enabling 4addr on a test AP chain: immediate rekey failures observed when traffic traversed AP boundary with different bridge forwarding behavior.
03/11 10:22 - conntrack on rtr-edge shows NAT entries with src=10.24.12.45 translated->public:xxxxx; when client roamed, a second entry with same src but different layer2 arrived and conntrack timed out existing mapping causing UDP port mismatch.
03/12 14:30 - Hypothesis: 4addr causes the AP to forward frames encapsulating the L2 source in a way that interacts poorly with our NAT-T expectations; the edge NAT implementation treats the different L2 association as a new flow and clears existing translation, breaking IKEv2 keepalive continuity.
03/13 09:50 - Confirmed that disabling 4addr on AP2 eliminated the reproduction in lab; VPN stayed stable during roaming between AP1 and AP2.
03/13 15:10 - Noted that some AP firmware versions behave differently (Aruba 8.5.0.3 vs 8.4.x); Aruba's bridge proxy-arp mode maintains consistent L2 appearance.
03/14 08:00 - Eng network team suggests adding NAT tolerate option on strongSwan and increasing UDP timeout as a short-term mitigation while AP configs are remediated.
Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Users reported VPN drops walking from north wing -> meeting rooms. Attached client logs.
Nate Huang (SRE) 2026-03-11: Got tcpdumps. Looks like 4500 keepalive replies are not matching conntrack entries after roam. Flagging network team.
Priya Rao (Wireless Eng) 2026-03-11: We have two APs in bridge mode with 4addr enabled for the mesh. Can we try disabling 4addr on the second AP as a test?
Kiran Desai (Assignee) 2026-03-12: Disabled 4addr on AP2 in meeting room A and asked affected user to reproduce. User reports stable VPN. Planning rollback to all APs in that building.
Diego Morales (Edge Eng) 2026-03-13: Added conntrack logging for UDP 4500/500; observed conntrack DELETE events corresponding to roam timestamps. Working on rule to extend NAT timeout for UDP 4500 for internal subnets.
Kiran Desai 2026-03-14: Drafted config change: disable 4addr on Aruba APs in SF, and enable 'proxy-arp' mode. Will schedule change window 2026-03-16 02:00-03:00 PT.
Priya Rao 2026-03-14: Filing follow-up firmware ticket with vendor about proxy-arp vs 4addr behavior and recommending patch. Link in related_confluence_pages.
Disable 4addr on affected APs (set APs to proxy-arp/normal bridge), or move affected APs out of mesh bridging mode. Alternatively, increase conntrack timeout for UDP 4500 on rtr-edge to 120s and enable strongSwan nat-t keepalive. Workaround applied to building A on 2026-03-13.
1) Execute scheduled AP config rollout to disable 4addr in SF building (2026-03-16). 2) Patch edge conntrack to extend UDP 4500 timeout and deploy strongSwan nat-t tolerate options as precaution. 3) Open vendor firmware escalation to Aruba for 4addr handling across NAT-T. 4) Add alerting for repeated conntrack DELETE on UDP 4500 for corp subnets.
In Progress - mitigation applied on a per-AP basis; full rollout and vendor follow-up pending. No code changes to core services required at this time.
payload.summary: Wi-Fi 4-addr bridge mode on APs causes IKEv2 NAT-T negotiation failures and VPN disconnects during roaming

Issue summary:
Service broker (provisioner service) is failing to complete the AWS assume-role chain used to provision Dedicated GPU pools for new customer commits in prod-us-east. The failure began after a credential rotation and an infra config bump last week.

Impact:
- New Dedicated provisioning jobs fail immediately with a permission error, blocking customer onboarding (self-serve and sales-assisted).
- Existing Dedicated capacity remains healthy, but any automated scale-up or reprovisioning attempts for pending orders are failing.
- Estimated customer-facing impact: 4 onboarding tasks stuck, potential SLA breach if not resolved within 48h.

Environment:
- Service: provisioner-service (service broker) running on k8s in prod-us-east cluster rwi-prod-1
- AWS accounts involved: provisioning-controller account (central infra), dedicated-customer accounts (cross-account role target)
- Components: IAM role chaining: provisioner -> provisioning-controller assumeRole -> cross-account DedicatedRole

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a dedicated provisioning request via the console or API for a test tenant.
2) Provisioner service requests temporary credentials from provisioning-controller by assuming provisioner-controller-role.
3) Provisioning-controller attempts to assume the DedicatedRole in the customer's account to create EC2 resources.
4) Request fails with AccessDenied/NotAuthorized during the final AssumeRole attempt.

Observed logs (redacted):
- provisioner: 2026-03-05T03:22:11Z ERROR assumeChain failed: AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/DedicatedRole
- provisioning-controller: 2026-03-05T03:22:11Z WARN assume-role-response: {"error":"AccessDenied","message":"STS AssumeRole: external ID mismatch or missing sts:TagSession"}
- AWS CloudTrail (cross-account): 2026-03-05T03:22:11Z EventName: AssumeRole, ErrorCode: AccessDenied

Initial investigation notes / hypotheses:
- Recent credential rotation for the provisioning-controller service account updated the external ID value used by TF state; provisioning-controller may be trying to assume with stale ExternalId.
- Alternatively, a change in role trust policy for DedicatedRole started requiring sts:TagSession or a specific session tag that our chain doesn't include.
- Terraform PR #117 adjusted trust relationships in a sweep to tighten cross-account trust; it may have introduced a condition on aws:PrincipalTag or aws:RequestTag.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Rolled back the most recent infra-config change in staging and re-tested the assume chain there (staging succeeded).
- For prod, we reverted the provisioning-controller deployment to the previous image which still failed; this points to IAM/role policy vs runtime code.

Next steps proposed and action items:
- SRE to validate current ExternalId values across TF state, secrets manager, and provisioning-controller config (assigned: Miguel).
- Security to review DedicatedRole trust policy changes in PR #117 and confirm whether conditions require session tags (assigned: Priya Nandakumar).
- Infra automation to run a dry AssumeRole test from the provisioning-controller principal in prod and capture full CloudTrail event for the failed attempt (assigned: Ben Chu).
- If trust policy requires session tags, update provisioner/provisioning-controller to include the required tags and open a deployment PR with e2e test.
- Communicate a mitigation ETA to Customer Ops for affected onboarding tickets and escalate to Sales if ETA > 24h.

Notes on urgency:
- Classified as Sev1 due to customer onboarding blockage and potential SLA exposure. We should have a mitigation plan within 6-8 hours and a fix within 24-48 hours depending on policy rollbacks or code changes.
2026-03-05T04:05:00Z - Miguel Ortega: Confirmed CloudTrail shows AccessDenied on final AssumeRole. Pulling the trust policy for arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/DedicatedRole now.
2026-03-05T05:30:00Z - Priya Nandakumar (Security): I reviewed PR #117; there is a conditional that added StringEquals: {"aws:RequestTag/environment":"prod"} and required TagSession. If true, our assume calls need to tag the session or we need a service principal exception.
2026-03-05T07:10:00Z - Ben Chu: Ran an sts:AssumeRole simulation from provisioning-controller principal using aws CLI with current ExternalId; simulation returned AccessDenied with MissingRequiredTag: sts:TagSession not present.
2026-03-06T09:20:00Z - Aisha Patel: Notifying Customer Ops and Sales about potential onboarding delay; working on customer-level communication templates.
2026-03-07T11:45:00Z - Miguel Ortega: Reproduction script & troubleshooting runbook uploaded to /confluence link. Preparing a hotfix branch to include session tags in the assume flow.
2026-03-08T14:02:00Z - Priya Nandakumar (Security): Approving short-lived exception to relax TagSession requirement for the provisioning-controller principal while hotfix is validated. We'll log the exception and schedule a policy hardening review.

Mitigation: short-lived security exception applied to DedicatedRole trust policy to allow provisioning-controller principal to AssumeRole without sts:TagSession while a hotfix is deployed. Hotfix: provisioner/provisioning-controller updated to attach required session tags on AssumeRole calls (PR #842). Post-deploy, revert exception and run automated policy checks. Follow-up: schedule policy review to standardize session tagging across all assume chains and add unit tests to infra-config PR checklist.
Deploy hotfix branch with tagged AssumeRole calls and run e2e provisioning smoke tests
Revert temporary trust policy exception once hotfix verified
Add automated assume-role simulation to CI for infra-config PRs
Update the Service Broker runbook with new session-tagging steps and troubleshooting checklist
payload.summary: Service broker assume-role chain failing for Dedicated provisioning in prod-us-east

Issue summary: Customer requests a forensic-grade SIEM sample package for an ongoing audit. They require that exported events be temporally scrubbed (time-shift within a deterministic window), identifiers pseudonymized with HMAC keyed per-tenant, and an accompanying resume-token manifest so ingestion can be replayed by their SOC without raw PII.

Impact: Customer cannot complete regulator evidence submission until sample bundle is delivered in accepted format. This is blocking their audit sign-off and legal review.

Request details: deliver a compact NDJSON sample (<= 500k events) covering 24 hours of tenant activity, with:
- deterministic temporal scrubbing (shift timestamps by tenant-seed + manifest mapping)
- per-field reversible pseudonymization whitelist (user_id, session_id) using tenant HMAC (customer provided key material)
- keep original event ordering and provide resume-token checkpoints every 15 minutes
- manifest (signed) describing transformations, time-shift seed, algorithm versions, and KMS key IDs used
- delivery via pre-signed S3 link with object-lock for 7 days

Expected behavior: Redwood provides an evidence bundle that the customer's SOC can ingest into their Splunk/QRadar proof-of-playback harness with documented checksums and replay tokens.

Observed behavior: Customer reports previous export (SUP-701999) included raw user identifiers and lacked resume tokens; they flagged it during internal audit. This ticket requests an alternate delivery method that meets the regulator's evidence checklist.
1) Customer run a standard SIEM export job for tenant finsecure-prod for window 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z - 2026-02-01T23:59:59Z.
2) Request delivery using the 'compact-evidence' export profile.
3) Observe that downloaded file contains original user_id and timestamps and lacks resume-token manifest.
4) Customer submits to SOC and gets an error in ingestion indicating missing resume_token header.

Note: we reproduced locally in staging using the export tool and confirmed missing resume-token metadata in the manifest for the 'compact-evidence' profile prior to applying privacy transforms.
2026-03-09T16:22:11Z exporter[pid=4421] INFO starting export job: tenant=finsecure-prod profile=compact-evidence window=2026-02-01Z
2026-03-09T16:22:12Z exporter[pid=4421] DEBUG resolved checkpoint_count=96 resume_tokens_missing=true pseudonymization_step=skipped
2026-03-09T16:22:13Z s3client INFO put_object: bucket=evidence-uploads/key=finsecure/2026-02-01/compact-ndjson.gz status=200
2026-03-09T16:22:15Z signer WARN manifest-signature-mismatch: expected_alg=RS256 actual=none

Attached sample lines (redacted):
{"@ts":"2026-02-01T00:00:01Z","event":"model.infer.start","user_id":"alice@example.com","session_id":"sess-abc123","request_id":"r-1"}

2026-03-10 10:05 - Triage by Support (Aisha): validated customer audit checklist and confirmed required fields.
2026-03-10 11:30 - Eng (Daniel): reproduced in staging; found export path skipped pseudonymization when 'compact-evidence' profile used without explicit --privacy flag.
Hypothesis: legacy compact profile predates resume-token and privacy pipeline changes; exporter falls back to legacy manifest schema so signature and token fields are not emitted.
Ran local debug: set ENV EXPORT_PRIVACY=1 -> manifest includes resume_tokens and pseudonymization metadata. Behavior suggests configuration gating in server side feature flag 'export.legacy_compact_enabled'.
Checked related dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/siem-exports/export-errors?var-tenant=finsecure-prod shows a spike on 2026-02-01 where manifest-signature-mismatch and missing-resume-token events increase.
Customer provided an HSM-wrapped key identifier and confirmed they can accept HMAC-based pseudonyms using tenant HMAC-KID 'projects/finsecure/keys/hmac-01'.
Aisha Khan (Support) 2026-03-10: Thanks for the details. We'll prioritize a privacy-preserving delivery. Can you confirm whether FinSecure will provide a tenant HMAC key or require Redwood KMS to issue a wrapping key?
Rajiv Patel (FinSecure SOC) 2026-03-10: FinSecure will provide an HMAC key wrapped with their KMS; we will upload the wrapped key to the S3 staging area. Need manifest to list KMS key id and HMAC-algo SHA256-HMAC.
Daniel Wu (Eng) 2026-03-11: Reproduced. The compact profile bypasses privacy transforms when legacy flag is set. Proposing two workarounds: (A) Run 'evidence-export --privacy' which applies deterministic temporal-scrub and HMAC pseudonymization; (B) patch exporter to include manifest fields for legacy profiles. Which do you prefer?
Rajiv Patel (FinSecure SOC) 2026-03-11: Option A is acceptable if you can guarantee deterministic time-shift seed and provide a signed manifest. Please proceed with Option A and deliver a pre-signed S3 link. Also require object-lock for 7 days and MD5+SHA256 checksums.
Daniel Wu (Eng) 2026-03-12: Preparing export run in prod with privacy flag. Will upload to s3://evidence-deliveries/finsecure/2026-02-01/ and share manifest. ETA 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC.
In Progress - export job with privacy transforms queued. Planned remediation steps: (1) run one-time privacy export for requested window with --privacy and tenant-wrapped-HMAC provided by customer; (2) generate signed manifest (RS256) including time_shift_seed, pseudonymization: {algo: HMAC-SHA256, kid: projects/finsecure/keys/hmac-01}, resume_tokens every 15m; (3) object-lock S3 upload and provide pre-signed URL + checksums; (4) follow-up run to bake config change: remove legacy bypass or ensure compact profile requires explicit opt-in.

Follow-ups assigned: ENG-ops task to remove export.legacy_compact_enabled by 2026-03-25 (linked INT ticket), and create a console toggle for privacy exports. Customer to confirm receipt and verify ingestion by FinSecure SOC.
payload.summary: Request: privacy-preserving SIEM sample for forensic handoff with temporal scrubbing and resume-token manifest

Issue summary: Customers report higher-than-expected latency and intermittent client-side timeouts when sending repeated short prompts (followup turns) to pinned model endpoints. Impact: Degraded P99 latency for repeat prompts; several customer requests timed out and were retried by clients. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool for PromptlyAI. Observed on redwood-open-3B and redwood-llama-7B. Steps to reproduce:\n1) Create a short-turn conversation (single-turn prompt) and call the API repeatedly with identical prompt payloads at ~20 qps.\n2) Observe response latency distribution and streaming disconnects.\n3) Reproduce against the customer's pinned endpoint (dedicated) and generic hosted endpoint for same model.\nObserved behavior: P95/P99 latency for repeat prompts jumps from baseline ~120ms to 800ms-2s in bursts; some requests return 504 client-side after stream disconnect. Logs show a resync cycle for the prefix catalog and a burst of KV cache cold-path reads immediately after. Expected behavior: Repeat identical prompts should hit warm prefix/KV cache and return within baseline latency with streaming intact. Additional context: Customer only started seeing regression after the weekly catalog resync job deployed 2026-03-10. The customer is on a production SLA and reported business impact (in-app search degradation).
2026-03-11 09:32 - Support - Ava Martinez: Acknowledged customer report and collected initial logs and request IDs. Asked customer for affected endpoint and example request ID. Triage -> P1 due to SLA and user-facing timeouts.
2026-03-11 10:05 - Customer (PromptlyAI - Michael Chen): Provided sample request IDs: rQh7-20260311-01, rQh7-20260311-02. Noticed regression after maintenance window on 2026-03-10. Can confirm traffic pattern is repeated short prompts from our chat agent.
2026-03-11 13:20 - SRE - Priya Rao: Initial trace shows a batch of prefix-catalog resync events on cluster pool 7; nodes intermittently marked as "refreshing" and evicting index shards. Correlated with increased cold-path KV lookups. Attach dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/kv/resync?var-cluster=pool7
2026-03-12 08:50 - Eng - Liam O'Connor: Rolled a debug build to one replica with additional KV tracing enabled. Observed that resync job holds a global lock on prefix-catalog index for ~600ms, causing concurrent requests to fall back to slow backfill path and rehydrate KV entries one-by-one.
2026-03-12 16:10 - Support - Ava Martinez: Notified customer of findings and provided short-term workaround (route repeat-turn traffic to fallback model variant on other pool). Customer accepted workaround to mitigate user impact while we fix root cause.
Trace IDs: rQh7-20260311-01 (p99 latency 1.8s), rQh7-20260311-02 (stream disconnect at 1.2s).
Observability: 'kv.resync.duration' spikes coincident with 'serving.request.fallback.count' increases. Dashboard indicates resync job runs every 24h, the recent run duration increased from ~80ms to ~600ms after change in PR #2148.
Hypothesis: Recent change (PR #2148) to prefix-catalog resync introduces a global catalog lock while updating shard mappings; this causes in-memory index to be briefly unavailable and requests hit cold-path backfill (per-key KV lease acquisition) leading to serialized latency on hot keys for repeated prompts.
Repro run: Synthetic traffic test at 25 qps on dedicated pool reproduced p99 latency spike when resync triggered. Disabling the resync job on one staging pool removed spike immediately.
Related logs: kvcache-service stderr snippet (2026-03-11T09:28Z): 'WARN prefix_catalog: lock_acquire_time=612ms, shard_reindex=true, fallback_to_backfill=true'
Workaround applied: Traffic routing rule created in Console to send PromptlyAI repeat-turns to alternate pool (pool-3) for 48 hours to avoid resync window. Hotfix plan: revert the global-locking change from PR #2148 and reintroduce incremental shard update with per-shard locks. Engineering will ship patch (kvcache v1.4.7) and deploy to prod-us-east during a low-traffic window. Post-deploy validation: run synthetic 25 qps repeat prompt test and monitor kv.resync.duration and serving.request.fallback.count for 48h. Follow-ups: (1) Add telemetry alarm if resync duration >250ms, (2) Update runbook with safer resync strategy, (3) Coordinate with PromptlyAI on a scheduled maintenance window for final rollout. Target ETA for full fix: 2026-03-18.
payload.summary: Prefix catalog resync delay leads to repeated prompt latency and occasional client-side timeouts

Issue summary:
During a scheduled Vault rewrap and KMS key rotation in prod us-east, a subset of self-hosted CI runners failed to refresh their auth session within the re-auth grace window. Long-running Maven publish jobs (gradle/maven artifacts) observed 401/403 from the artifact registry and the CI controller marked runners as disconnected, leading to queued/pending deploys across several release pipelines.

Impact:
- ~120 CI jobs stalled across nightly release and customer-facing release branches for ~45 minutes.
- Artifact publish failures impacted two Canary releases (canary-frontend v1.12.7 and canary-runtime v3.4.0).
- No data loss; artifacts not published and must be requeued or republished.

Environment:
- prod us-east (k8s cluster: ci-runner-prod-01)
- Runner type: ephemeral self-hosted (ephemeral-runner-controller v2.8.1)
- Vault: transit rewrap triggered (vault-cluster-prod, transit rekey job)
- Artifact Registry: internal-nexus (https://nexus.internal.redwood)

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Trigger Transit rewrap / KMS rotation for Vault (same procedure as scheduled maintenance).
2) Observe ephemeral runners performing token refresh at next heartbeat window.
3) If runner's token-refresh overlaps with Vault rewrap and KMS latency spike, runner fails to exchange token and marks itself Unregistered for >30s.
4) Long-running build that tries to push artifacts during this window receives 401/403 and fails stage.

Observed logs / errors (representative):
- runner pod logs: "ERROR auth: token refresh failed: transit/rewrap: decryption failed"
- ephemeral-runner-controller: "WARN runner-heartbeat: missed-heartbeat: marking runner unavailable (grace window exceeded)"
- maven publish step: "Failed to deploy artifacts: Server returned HTTP response code: 401 for URL: https://nexus.internal.redwood/..."
- controller events: "PodNotReady -> JobRetryScheduled"

Initial investigation notes:
- Vault transit rewrap produced a short period (~20–60s) of elevated API latency in us-east. KMS key re-encryption added to the latency.
- Runner token refresh logic has a strict re-auth grace window of 30s before CI controller evicts. Many runners retried immediately with no jitter, causing thundering refresh retries against Vault.
- Artifact publish failures correlate 1:1 with runner eviction events (publish attempted from ephemeral runner that lost token mid-upload).
- There is no bug in Nexus; requests that include a valid fresh token succeed.

Temporary mitigations applied (timeline):
- 2026-03-09 02:18 UTC: CS and SRE paused non-critical nightly releases and set affected pipelines to manual re-run.
- 2026-03-09 02:28 UTC: Increased runner-controller grace window from 30s -> 120s (hotfix flag enabled) to reduce eviction during in-flight token refresh.
- 2026-03-09 02:35 UTC: Applied client-side retry/backoff to maven publisher step via pipeline wrapper script (retry 3x with exponential backoff).
- 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC: Requeued failed publish jobs; most completed successfully after re-run.

Root-cause hypothesis:
- Combination of KMS-backed Vault transit rewrap latency spike and aggressive runner re-auth eviction policy. Lack of jitter on token refresh amplified load on Vault causing some refreshes to fail temporarily.

Permanent remediation proposals:
1) Add randomized jitter and exponential backoff to runner token refresh to avoid thundering herd during Vault operations.
2) Make runner-controller re-auth grace configurable per deployment and set safer default (e.g., 90–120s) for prod.
3) Add limited buffering/stream-resume support for artifact uploads so mid-upload auth refresh does not force failure (longer-term engineering task).
4) Update Vault rewrap runbook to include a temporary throttle on agent refresh endpoints and coordinate with CI to drain long-running publish jobs before rewrap.

Follow-ups / Owners:
- Engineering: implement jitter + backoff on runner agent (owner: @marcus-patel) — linked ticket INT-942321.
- Platform: change default grace window and expose operator flag (owner: @sre-oncall) — linked ticket INT-942322.
- Release Engineering: add pre-rotation drain step for artifact pushes (owner: @olivia-chen) — linked ticket INT-942323.

Links and artifacts:
- Slack: #infra-ci thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0ICRI0/thread-xyz
- GitHub (temporary pipeline wrapper PR): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-config/pull/814
- Runbook draft for Vault rewrap: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=1284921

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 11:42 UTC - SRE Oncall: Confirmed no regression after hotfix rollback in canary. Scheduling config change via operator to make grace window configurable. See INT-942322.

Issue summary:
HR is evaluating a short-term consulting engagement with a recent alum who will work remotely for ~6 weeks. The ask: understand approved patterns for reactivating accounts, issuing short-lived credentials, rotating keys/secrets, and reassigning company hardware that the alum previously kept when they left.

Impact:
- Delay in engagement start if we cannot confirm an approved path for account/reactivation or hardware handback.
- Potential security risk if long-lived credentials or previously-returned hardware are reused without proper rotation and attestation.

Background / Context:
- Candidate: former SWE (left 2024-09), now engaged as 6-week paid consultant starting 2026-03-22 to help with inference runtime tuning.
- They retained a company-issued Lenovo laptop at departure under our standard loaner transfer agreement; currently in their possession overseas (EU).
- Their primary Redwood account was deactivated at offboarding and archived; there is an archived service-account access record and several SSH keys previously registered on GitHub and internal bastions.
- HR requests a minimal-friction reactivation path that preserves auditability and follows KMS/rotation rules. Security asks for assurance that no stale keys or lingering sessions remain.

Request / Questions (explicit):
1) Policy: Do we allow alumni to re-use previously-issued company laptops for short-term consulting if they were not formally returned? If yes, what attestation and device checks are required (OS image, disk wipe, firmware checks)?
2) Accounts: Is temporary reactivation of an employee account permitted, or should we create a short-lived contractor identity? Preferred TTL for credentials?
3) Keys & Secrets: What rotation cadence is required for SSH keys, GitHub deploy keys, and KMS-wrapped secrets before re-enabling access?
4) Cross-border considerations: Any policy for device handback or exception when the alum is overseas and cannot ship hardware back?
5) Audit / Paperwork: Templates / required sign-offs from Legal/Finance/HR for ‘alumni-as-consultant’ engagements (billing, NDA, incident liability) — links requested.

Proposed low-risk approach (for discussion):
- Create a dedicated contractor identity (SCIM-provisioned) with explicit TTL of 45 days and enforce MFA + SSO.
- Require device attestation: full disk wipe, verified OS image via our internal image signer, OS patch level and firmware recorded; hardware re-enrollment performed by Hardware Ops on return or by partner vendor for overseas case.
- Rotate all user SSH keys and remove archived deploy keys; issue ephemeral deploy keys for the scope needed, bound to a single repo and expiring at engagement end.
- Issue temporary KMS access via a time-limited role; log all decrypt operations and flag any access > 5 minutes latency for review.

Requested artifacts / links:
- HR: engagement letter / SOW draft (if available).
- Security: checklist for device attestation and image signer runbook.
- Legal: NDA/consulting addendum template.

Next steps requested from assignee:
- Confirm which of the above options are allowed under current policy and list required approvals.
- If policy gap exists, advise on an exception flow and required stakeholders for sign-off.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:47 - Security (Maya Chen): Initial thought — prefer contractor identity with TTL; do not reuse archived employee account. Need device attestation and proof of wipe. Will prepare checklist.
2026-03-11 11:30 - HR (Lina Park): HR would like a minimal process to avoid delaying start date. Can Security provide the checklist and sign-off matrix by EOD 2026-03-12? Also need Legal template link.
2026-03-12 15:08 - Legal (Priya Singh): We have an 'alumni-consulting addendum' draft—link added to related_confluence_pages. Will confirm liability language for hardware loss/damage.
Checked archived account metadata: user 'jdoe' deactivated 2024-09-15; last SSH key fingerprint appears in git-authorized-keys list and in bastion logs until deactivation date.
Confirmed no active sessions or API tokens remain associated with the archived account. Token ledger shows revoke events at offboard time.
Hardware asset tag shows 'loaned' status at departure; transfer paperwork has signature but no handback record. Asset tracker flagged for manual reconciliation.
Identified cross-reference INT-27133 for device handoff case studies and INT-20241 for return-to-work reprovisioning notes.

Issue summary: New international hire (engineering contractor) needs immediate access to VPC resources and a lab workstation. Conditional Access policy is blocking the SSO provisioning path; HR needs a temporary exception to complete onboarding.

Detailed: HR attempted to provision account via SCIM. SCIM returned a 409 due to an existing shadow account from previous contractor engagement; Azure AD conditional access requires MFA from corporate IPs and blocks legacy auth from outside office IPs. Device shipping timeline is constrained; contractor start date is next week.
Onboarding delayed for one contractor; potential delay to feature delivery and mentoring schedule. Access to reserved GPU lab is blocked.
1) HR submits SCIM create for user marisol.v-hire@example.com
2) SCIM API returns 409 "conflict: duplicate externalId".
3) Provisioning flow retries SAML assertion; conditional access returns 6: user blocked due to location/MFA policy.
4) Endpoint for device enrollment cannot complete due to blocked auth.
SCIM response excerpts and AAD sign-in logs attached in Confluence link; sample error id: 0xA2C4 (SCIM409-conflict); AAD sign-in risk policy code: CA-LOC-403
Checked SCIM: duplicate externalId linked to archived contractor account (last used 2024-09).
Azure AD sign-in logs show 'ConditionalAccessPolicy kt_office_only' triggered for sign-in from 203.0.113.45 (shipping vendor).
Device enrollment attempts fail because corp MDM challenge cannot be completed from vendor network.
Hypothesis: Shadow account prevents SCIM upsert; conditional access blocks token exchange for device enrollment.
Workaround implemented: security approved a 48-hour conditional-access exception for the specific onboarding IP range and user principal name; network allowlist created in firewall (VPN-staging-APAC).
IT manually created a temporary service account and linked it to the contractor's laptop serial number for initial device enrollment. Manual KMS key access granted with timebox.
HR deactivated shadow externalId and we initiated a SCIM merge plan to consolidate records; longer-term automation ticket raised.
Follow-ups: Update onboarding runbook to include a conditional-access exception request template; add a pre-onboard SCIM duplicate-check step; schedule a change to reduce manual exceptions.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
- Customer reports Console cost breakdown pages intermittently taking 20–60s to load or timing out.
- Root symptom appears to be elevated p95 latency on internal Cost Model API (estimate/breakdown endpoints), which Console backend calls on-demand.

Customer impact:
- Northbridge Security Labs (enterprise) cannot reliably load Console cost breakdown for the last 24h; internal finance review blocked.
- Console UI shows partial data or "Something went wrong" after ~30s.

Scope / suspected:
- Internal Cost Model API p95 latency spike and occasional 504s between Console backend and cost-model-service.
- Possible regression due to higher request volume and cache-miss heavy query patterns (high-cardinality breakdown dimensions).

Notes:
- This is not a customer calling the Cost Model API directly; it is Console calling internal endpoints on the hot path.
- Console is behind a feature flag for cost-model-backed breakdown; fallback is legacy aggregation if enabled.

Requested outcome:
- Immediate mitigation to restore Console responsiveness.
- Follow-up work: add server-side caching/memoization and enforce tighter request bounding for Console hot paths.
1) In prod Console, navigate to Usage → Cost breakdown.
2) Select: Time range = Last 24 hours; Group by = model + route + region (or other multi-dimension view).
3) Observe: UI spinner persists >20s; often times out.

Internal reproduction:
- Hit Console backend endpoint that requests cost-model breakdown for the same range; observe cost-model-service p95 > 8s and occasional gateway timeouts.
Console cost breakdown loads in <5s for Last 24 hours views; Cost Model API p95 within SLO.
Cost Model API p95 spikes to 8–15s (with tail up to ~30s) leading to Console timeouts/partial results; sporadic 504s.
Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-02-18 16:40: Support intake from CSM: Northbridge reports Console cost pages timing out.
- 2026-02-18 17:05: Console team confirms elevated latency calling cost-model-service; opens SUP-31905.
- 2026-02-18 17:20: SRE reviews Grafana dashboard (cost-model API). p95 latency jump coincides with increased request volume after enabling breakdown feature flag for additional orgs.
- 2026-02-18 17:40: Noted many requests with high-cardinality breakdown configs (multiple group_by dimensions) and large time windows returning large intermediate aggregates.
- 2026-02-18 18:05: Checked telemetry/analytics dependency health: ingestion lag within normal bounds; not the primary driver.
- 2026-02-18 18:15: Cost-model-service CPU saturation observed; GC pressure increased; request concurrency spikes.
- 2026-02-18 18:30: Identified Console backend retry behavior amplifying load during slow responses.

Hypotheses evaluated:
- Telemetry lag / backfill causing slow queries: ruled out (lag normal; queries still slow with fresh data).
- Schema negotiation issues causing retries: not primary (version distribution stable; errors not concentrated).
- Cardinality explosion from unbounded breakdown dimensions: likely contributor.
- Missing caching layer for identical repeated queries (Console refresh/polling): confirmed (cache hit rate near zero).

Slack coordination:
- Referenced #incidents thread about cost drift alert/telemetry lag earlier in the week; not directly related but informed mitigation approach.

Customer comms:
- Acknowledged incident, shared mitigation plan: temporarily reduce breakdown complexity and/or fall back to legacy aggregation while performance improvements roll out.
Mitigation applied (2026-02-18 19:05 UTC):
- Console: temporarily reduced feature-flag exposure for cost-model-backed breakdown for affected org(s) and enabled legacy fallback for high-latency scenarios.
- Cost-model-service: applied a temporary config to enforce stricter request bounds for breakdown requests coming from Console (max group_by dimensions and max time buckets) per API guidelines.
- Infra: increased service replicas and tightened timeouts to reduce queued tail latency; added circuit-breaker behavior in Console backend to avoid retry amplification.

Result:
- Cost-model-service p95 returned to ~2.1s; 504s stopped.
- Console load times improved to <6s for Northbridge on standard views; advanced high-cardinality view now shows a "refine filters" message rather than timing out.

Customer confirmation:
- 2026-02-19: Northbridge confirmed Console is usable again for finance review; requested ETA for permanent fix/caching improvements.
1) Implement server-side caching/memoization for common Console queries (time-window + org + breakdown config) with bounded TTL and cache-size guards.
2) Add explicit Console guidance and guardrails: default group_by set, maximum dimensions, and proactive UI validation.
3) Update Console backend client usage: backoff + jitter; reduce automatic retries on timeouts; introduce request coalescing.
4) Add alert for cache hit rate and high-cardinality request share; ensure dashboards include request-shape distribution.
5) Post-incident follow-up: document the temporary bounds change and ensure it is captured in cost-model API guidelines as a Console-specific profile.

Owners:
- SRE: Rafael Mendes (monitoring + rollout safety)
- Cost Model API: Ethan Park (caching + bounds)
- Console: Jada Williams / Felix Schneider (client behavior + UI guardrails)
2026-02-18 16:47 (Chloe Martin): Getting reports from Northbridge that cost breakdown pages are timing out. We see a spike in calls to cost-model-service when loading Usage/Cost pages. Can SRE help triage p95? Customer impact: finance review today.
2026-02-18 17:12 (Rafael Mendes): On it. Looking at cost-model API dashboard now. p95 is ~12s over last hour; error rate low but timeouts at gateway are rising. Will dig into request patterns and saturation.
2026-02-18 17:33 (Felix Schneider): Console backend logs show long tail from /internal/cost-model/v1/breakdown. We also retry on timeout (2x). Might be amplifying traffic. We can hotfix to reduce retries if needed.
2026-02-18 18:02 (Ethan Park): Seeing many breakdown requests with 3–4 group_by dimensions + fine-grained buckets. This is worst-case for aggregation. We don’t have caching yet; identical queries repeat on refresh and navigation.
2026-02-18 18:41 (Rafael Mendes): Proposed mitigation: (1) shrink feature-flag exposure for cost-model breakdown; (2) enforce stricter bounds for Console caller; (3) scale replicas. Chloe/Felix please confirm legacy fallback still acceptable for customer until caching ships.
2026-02-18 18:55 (Chloe Martin): Confirmed. We can route Northbridge to legacy breakdown (with a banner) as an interim. Proceed with bounds + scaling now.
2026-02-18 19:18 (Rafael Mendes): Mitigation deployed. p95 trending down to ~2–3s; no new 504s observed. Monitoring for 30 minutes before declaring stable.
2026-02-19 09:10 (Chloe Martin): Northbridge confirmed pages load again. They asked if we can avoid removing advanced group_by options long-term; told them we’re adding caching + performance work.
2026-02-20 14:05 (Rafael Mendes): Closing as mitigated and stable. Follow-ups tracked with platform team; recommend adding cache hit-rate panel and request-shape guardrail metrics to dashboards.
