Issue summary: HorizonAI (dedicated) reports elevated tail latency (p99) and intermittent streaming resets for real-time chat traffic originating from APAC. Initial signal started 2026-02-20 08:45 UTC.

Impact: Approx 12% of requests for HorizonAI experienced >1.5s token generation p99 during the window; several streaming connections were reset mid-response causing partial outputs. Customer reported user-visible timeouts in production and opened a support escalation.

Observed behavior: Requests that historically stayed in ap-southeast pop are being routed through eu-west for a subset of accounts, increasing handshake and TTFB. Traffic appears to lose account-level region affinity then fall back to remote egress, triggering added TLS handshakes and KV cold starts on remote model shards.

Immediate mitigation request: Customer asked for a short-term route pin to ap-southeast and confirmation of no customer data egress outside expected regions.
1) Use HorizonAI test account (account tag AHZ-310) in ap-southeast-1.
2) Send steady chat stream traffic with sequence lengths ~400 tokens against gpt-neox-20b.
3) Observe connection setup and route chosen via X-Redwood-Route header (internal header) and monitor backend pop selection.
4) Compare p50/p95/p99 over a 10-minute window and inspect any stream disconnects in client logs.
2026-02-20T08:46:12Z edge-proxy[proxy-12] WARN: selected-egress=eu-west-1; account-affinity=lost; sni=redwood-eu; tls-handshake=0.34s
2026-02-20T08:46:12Z serving-runtime[serve-07] ERROR: kv-cache-miss account=AHZ-310 route=eu-west-1 cold-warmup=true
Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency/horizonai-p99?from=2026-02-20T08:30:00Z&to=2026-02-20T09:00:00Z
Packet capture snippet (sensitive): sni mismatch observed when egress choice changed - stored in secure log store at /secure/logs/SUP-531224-pcap-1

Additional notes:
2026-02-20 11:10 - HorizonAI (Customer): Confirmed production impact on ~7% of sessions; asked for temporary region pin until fix is applied.
1) Timeline: affinity loss events correlate with periodic router cache GC job that runs every 6 hours. The GC had an off-by-one condition that considered dedicated-account tags stale under high-tag-count scenarios.
2) Root cause hypothesis: router cache eviction removed account->pop binding; subsequent request used global fallback scoring that favored eu-west due to transient weight bump from capacity reshuffle.
3) Additional effect: when egress flips, serving runtime sees KV prefix miss causing cold KV warmups adding ~150-400ms per request, amplifying p99.
4) Reproducible locally by simulating high tag churn and triggering the router GC; confirmed by integration test that previously passed and now fails intermittently.
5) Cross-checks: no billing or quota anomalies. Not an authentication issue. No model degradation found.
Workaround: Temporary routing policy added to pin HorizonAI account AHZ-310 to ap-southeast-1 while fix is validated. Customer notified and verified reduced p99.
Fix deployed: Router cache eviction logic patched (router v2.14.3) to respect dedicated-account sticky TTL and to use conservative eviction when tag-count > 1000. Edge-proxy SNI mapping clarified to prefer account-specific SNI for dedicated customers. Hotfix promoted to canary on 2026-02-23 and to prod on 2026-02-24 after 24h observation with monitoring thresholds green.
Follow-ups: 1) Add unit/integration test covering eviction scenario (owner: routing team). 2) Add dashboard alert for >3% cross-region egress for dedicated accounts (owner: SRE). 3) Run a canary burn-in for 48h for high-tag-count customers.
Alert created: GEO_AFFINITY_LOSS_DEDICATED - fires if >2% of requests for dedicated accounts go to remote egress for 10m
Grafana panel updated: HorizonAI account affinity heatmap added to /d/latency/horizonai-p99
Synthetic test: hourly synthetic stream pinned to ap-southeast for AHZ-310 to verify route stability

Issue summary:

Overnight we observed that several Dedicated-staging service accounts stopped being authorized to read artifacts from the shared-storage project and to list compute instances in the staging fleet. The common failure pattern is permission-denied errors for roles that should have been inherited via the folder-level IAM bindings applied at the team folder.

Impact:
- Affected internal CI/CD jobs and a subset of dedicated staging nodes failed health checks, causing degraded test rollouts.
- No customer-facing production impact identified so far, but this blocks our Dedicated onboarding flow for two upcoming demos.

Environment:
- Affected folder: projects/folders/teams-dedicated-staging (folder display name: "dedicated-staging-team")
- Affected projects: shared-storage-prod-staging, dedicated-staging-pool-eu, dedicated-staging-pool-us
- Time window: first errors observed 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) CI job attempts to access gs://shared-storage-prod-staging/artifacts; received 403 permissionDenied on storage.objects.list.
2) Health-check script running on dedicated-staging node calls `gcloud compute instances list --project dedicated-staging-pool-us` and receives permissionDenied.
3) Policy Troubleshooter for a failing service account returns "No binding found" for role roles/storage.objectViewer even though the role is present at folder level in Audit logs prior to 02:00 UTC.

Observed behavior:
- Folder-level bindings that previously granted roles to group:sre-dedicated@redwood.ai are missing for multiple bindings (storage.viewer, compute.viewer).
- Audit logs show a IAM policy change around 2026-03-10 01:58 UTC with actor serviceAccount:org-admin-bot@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com. The change was a removal of 3 bindings and an addition of a different set scoped to a single project.

Expected behavior:
- Folder-level IAM bindings should remain intact unless a deliberate retention or migration plan is executed. Changes to folder bindings should be approved via the org-iam-change pipeline.

Investigation performed so far:
- Pulled Cloud Audit Logs for `google.iam.admin.v1` and confirmed a single change event at 2026-03-10 01:58 UTC authored by org-admin-bot.
- Ran `gcloud resource-manager folders get-iam-policy` and confirmed the bindings are absent.
- Policy Troubleshooter confirms lack of effective permission on affected service accounts.
- Cross-checked terraform state in infra repo: no recent merges that would delete folder bindings; however a scheduled automation job `infra/auto-iam-migrator` had a dry-run earlier that morning according to CI history.
- Reached out to infra-automation oncall in #infra-automation Slack for context; thread indicates a failed migration attempt that retried with an unintended apply.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Manually re-applied the most-critical folder bindings (roles/storage.objectViewer, roles/compute.viewer for group:sre-dedicated@redwood.ai) to the folder at 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC. Verified that CI jobs recovered and health checks returned green.

Immediate risk and open questions:
- Need to verify whether any other folders/projects were affected by the same automation job.
- Confirm why the `auto-iam-migrator` retried with an apply and bypassed the usual approval gate.
- Assess whether service accounts that had ephemeral keys or binding-specific grants lost access permanently or if this was limited to inherited bindings only.

Proposed next steps:
1) Run a wide scan across org folders comparing current folder-level bindings to the snapshot from 2026-03-09 23:59 UTC (we have a policy-snapshot in gs://infra-iam-snapshots).
2) Rollback automation: revert last apply from `infra/auto-iam-migrator` or pause the automation until root cause is confirmed.
3) Add an emergency guard in the automator to require manual approval when a change affects more than N folders (N=1).
4) Coordinate with Security to determine if this event requires an internal postmortem.

Resolution notes (work in progress):
- Critical bindings re-applied, services recovered. Further remediation pending org-wide scan and automator rollback.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 05:20 UTC - Security (Liam O'Connor): Please treat as potential misconfiguration incident. Holding on public reporting until we have full scope. Recommend snapshot verification before further applies.
Audit log id: projects/redwood-org/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity: entries around 2026-03-10T01:58:00Z show SetIamPolicy called by serviceAccount:org-admin-bot@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com
Gcloud commands executed: gcloud projects get-iam-policy, gcloud resource-manager folders get-iam-policy, policyTroubleshooter testIamPermissions
Terraform state check: no merged PRs that removed folder binding; CI shows auto-runner with job id infra-auto-20260310-01 which failed then retried with apply
Partial - emergency bindings restored and affected services recovered. Full remediation pending: pause/rollback of infra automator and org-wide validation against snapshot. Postmortem scheduled.
Pause infra/auto-iam-migrator until code change merges and approval gate added
Create automated snapshot diff alert that mails #security and #infra when folder-level binding count changes > 2
Run verification job to compare gs://infra-iam-snapshots/2026-03-09-2359 against current state and produce a CSV of mismatches
Document and enforce a two-person approval for any automations that modify folder-level IAM bindings

Issue summary: The ML Platform team needs temporary debugger access in the preprod project (preprod-llm) to investigate a model caching regression. When we attempt to grant a short-lived group the necessary IAM role bindings, the org-level policy 'restrict-iam-bindings-to-managed-groups' blocks the change. Impact: engineers cannot impersonate the debugging service account or attach the preprod-llm-monitor role, delaying triage for an ongoing performance regression. Request: create a temporary managed group that is allowed by the org-policy allowlist (or add an explicit allowlist entry) and bind roles/iam.serviceAccountUser and roles/logging.viewer to service-account/llm-debug@preprod. Set an automatic expiry for 7 days. Background: Org policy was tightened last quarter to limit direct IAM bindings to GSuite-managed groups and SCIM-provisioned groups for auditability. The ML team cannot use the existing on-call groups because they require long-term membership and broader privileges.
1) Attempt in Console or gcloud to bind roles/iam.serviceAccountUser to group:llm-debuggers@external.redwood.test in project preprod-llm.
2) Console returns an error and prevents saving the policy.
3) gcloud error: gcloud iam policies set-iam-policy: PERMISSION_DENIED: Resource violates organization policy 'constraints/iam.allowedPolicyBindings'
Error detail (policy evaluation): ORG_POLICY_VIOLATION: binding 'roles/iam.serviceAccountUser' denied because principal 'group:llm-debuggers@external.redwood.test' is not in the allowed groups list for constraint 'constraints/iam.allowedPolicyBindings'.
Policy path: organizations/1234567890/policies/constraints/iam.allowedPolicyBindings
- Confirmed org policy exists at org level and lists only 'managed:' and 'scim:' group patterns.
- gcloud command used to inspect: gcloud org-policies describe constraints/iam.allowedPolicyBindings --organization=1234567890 and gcloud projects get-iam-policy preprod-llm.
- Tried adding a federated group (GSuite) but our dev GSuite provisioning for temporary groups requires admin console changes.
- Security reviewed and prefers a temporary managed group over adding individuals to a broad role.
- Options: 1) Provision a GSuite-managed group redwood-llm-debug-preprod, ask Identity team to add it to the org-policy allowlist (preferred). 2) Create a short-lived service-account proxy with narrowly scoped permissions and add individual engineers via impersonation (workaround). 3) Request an exception from OrgPolicy owners with justification and TTL.
- Recommended immediate path: create managed group + add to allowlist with a 7-day TTL. Request Identity + OrgPolicy owners to action.

Additional notes:
Pending - plan is to: 1) Identity to create GSuite-managed group redwood-llm-debug-preprod. 2) SecOps/OrgPolicy owners to add pattern 'group:redwood-llm-debug-preprod@redwood.com' to constraints/iam.allowedPolicyBindings allowlist with a TTL entry. 3) Infra to apply the IAM bindings: roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on sa:llm-debug@preprod and roles/logging.viewer on project preprod-llm. 4) Verify audit logs and remove allowlist + group after TTL expires. If org-policy cannot be changed quickly, fallback is to create a scoped proxy service-account with short-lived keyless impersonation and document audit steps.
- Created checklist for Identity -> OrgPolicy -> Infra steps.
- FYI to oncall channel #infra-identity.
- Need PR for infra automation to attach TTL metadata to the allowlist change for auditability (infra/ops#4821 referenced).
payload.summary: Request: Temporary managed group + role binding for LLM debug in preprod blocked by GCP org-policy

Issue summary:
Request from Legal for a narrow, timeboxed extract that maps anonymized response hashes back to ephemeral request identifiers to support an eDiscovery demand. The extract must not include raw customer payloads and must follow our redaction/aggregation controls.

Impact:
- Legal needs mapping for three subpoenas to validate response provenance.
- Customer data must remain protected; extraction must be minimized and reversible only within a secure enclave for the legal team.
- High urgency due to 7-day statutory response window.

Environment:
- Production inference traces in us-west and EU-CENTRAL for the affected customers.
- Data flows touch serving-runtime, tokenization, and the session KV cache.

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
- Provide a timeboxed artifact that contains: anonymized_response_hash -> ephemeral_request_id (internal id), timestamp, model_version, region. No full prompts, no full outputs.
- Apply deterministic salt per-legal-request stored in HSM, record KMS envelope IDs.
- Redaction verification: automated scan to ensure no PII patterns leaked; attach verification report.
- Data access window: 72 hours after approval to export; artifacts to be stored in secure S3 path with restricted ACLs and audit logging.

Steps to reproduce / gather:
1) Legal attached subpoenas (see comment) and specified scope.
2) Privacy asked for minimal mapping; SRE to produce sample for verification.
3) Need formal privacy sign-off and infra gating (temporary role-based access).

- SRE trace slice: s3://redwood-prod-traces/edr/2026-03-05/slice-11.jsonl
- Dashboard snapshot: https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboards/edr-384217

Approvals required:
- Privacy (Data Protection Officer)
- Security (temporary access and HSM use)
- Legal (requestor confirmation of scope)

Requested by: Legal - Samir Patel (internal counsel)
Urgency: statutory (7 days)

2026-03-10: SRE sampled a 1000-request slice and validated that response hashes can be generated deterministically using sha256 with a per-request salt; placed sample in secure staging bucket.
2026-03-11: Privacy reviewed sample, flagged two edge cases where low-entropy outputs could risk re-identification; recommended bucketization and suppression for outputs under token-length threshold.
2026-03-11: Security requested KMS envelope approach; will generate ephemeral key scoped to this request and log envelope ID in audit trail.
2026-03-12: Created runbook draft for the export process and RBAC steps; awaiting DPO signature. Runbook location attached in related_confluence_pages.
Hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: A deterministic hash + per-request salt is sufficient if outputs below N tokens are suppressed.
- Hypothesis B: Additional noise/aggregation may be required for small outputs to avoid re-identification.
Samir Patel (Legal) - 2026-03-10: Confirming subpoenas 2026-03-A/B/C. Scope: responses between 2025-11-01 and 2026-01-31 for two customer IDs. Request minimal mapping only.
Aisha Khan (Support) - 2026-03-10: Triage accepted. Noted required approvals and listed components. Assigning to Diego for SRE coordination.
Diego Martinez (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Collected sample slice and uploaded to staging. Link: s3://redwood-staging/edr-samples/384217/sample-1.jsonl. Privacy please review.
Marta Novak (Privacy) - 2026-03-11: Reviewed sample; two short-response cases flagged. Recommend suppression for outputs < 16 tokens and record suppression count in report.
Eli Chen (Security) - 2026-03-12: Approving KMS envelope flow. Will provision ephemeral key (kms-enc-384217) and restrict to group legal-ediscovery for 72h. Will run verification of audit logs post-export.
Samir Patel (Legal) - 2026-03-12: Legal approved suppression rule and KMS approach. Please include chain-of-custody statement in artifact manifest.
Finalize runbook and obtain DPO signature (Privacy).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several newly imaged devices fail to register display orientation when connected to the company TB4 dock that hosts an external GPU (eGPU). During Autopilot/OOBE provisioning the system reboots repeatedly and never completes device setup. Impact: Blocks onboarding for engineers using docked workstations in depot lab; ~5 devices repro'd so far; slows imaging throughput and blocks a small number of active hires. Environment: Depot imaging lab (depot-usw-01), Windows 11 22H2 corporate image with company kernel-mode signed graphics driver bundle, test TB4 docks with updated firmware v1.3.2 and eGPU enclosure running NVIDIA RTX A5000 via Thunderbolt 4. Observed behavior: After the first OOBE reboot, device enters a hardware re-enumeration loop. Event Viewer shows Display subsystem errors (EventID 4101) and kernel driver bind/unbind churn. Autopilot fails to finalize device state and service principal registration (AAD) times out due to repeated network interface re-enumeration. Expected behavior: Dock+eGPU should not interfere with Autopilot/OOBE device state; display orientation should register and devices should finish provisioning. Initial hypothesis: New TB4 dock firmware causes the GPU/NIC to briefly detach during driver initialization which races with provisioning hooks in the corporate image, causing a state machine deadlock. Alternatively, a driver signing mismatch in the bundle may trigger Kernel Mode Driver Framework (KMDF) rebinds when multiple GPUs present.
1) Image device with standard corporate WIM (win11_22h2_corp_v3.wim) and apply company driver bundle.
2) Connect TB4 dock with eGPU enclosure before first boot (power on dock + eGPU).
3) Boot device and proceed through Autopilot/OOBE until first automatic reboot.
4) Observe device rebooting 2-6 times and Autopilot never reaching 'Setup complete'.
5) Check Event Viewer > System and Application for Display/Driver events and verify network re-enumeration logs.
System Event: Kernel-PnP 419: Device "PCI\VEN_10DE&DEV_25F8" unexpectedly removed and reattached (timestamps: 2026-03-10T09:12:33Z, 2026-03-10T09:12:34Z)
Event Viewer: Display 4101: Display driver nvlddmkm stopped responding and was successfully recovered (driver version 31.0.15.0).
Autopilot log excerpt: RegistrationService: StateMachine transition 'Finalize' failed due to network adapter erratic availability (timeout 00:02:00).
Dock firmware serial: TB4-DOCK-01 fw=1.3.2, eGPU enclosure fw=2.0.7, thunderbolt controller reports link flaps in firmware console (see /var/log/tb4_console.log).
- Reproduced 5x in depot-lab on two hardware families.
- Swapping to legacy dock (no eGPU) allows provisioning to complete consistently.
- Captured Windows kernel ETW trace: shows repeated PnP remove/add for PCI device class during early driver load.
- Hotplug sequence differs vs. older dock firmware: eGPU root complex reports as 'surprise removed' for ~200-400ms before reattachment.
- Tested with vendor-supplied signed driver and in-box driver: both show same churn.
- Network interfaces attached to dock (USB-c NIC) also re-enumerate causing AAD token requests to time out.
- Hypothesis refined: dock firmware introduces a short device-reset that races with Autopilot network registration window; provisioning scripts don't tolerate transient NIC loss early in OOBE.

Additional notes:
Workaround: For depot lab imaging, detach TB4 dock (or disable eGPU) during Autopilot/OOBE and reattach after initial sign-in. This allows Autopilot to complete and avoids re-enumeration race.
Fix path: Vendor supplied TB4 firmware candidate v1.3.3rc eliminated the surprise-remove in lab repro; we requested an official vendor release and are coordinating a test plan. Engineering to add a short wait/retry for network/Azure registration during OOBE (autopilot retry), and update our imaging runbook to explicitly recommend 'dock disconnected' during first boot for eGPU-equipped docks until vendor firmware is rolled out.
Follow-ups: 1) Roll out vendor fw v1.3.3 after lab validation (owner: HW Vendor + Priya Nair). 2) Update Confluence runbook with temporary dock handling steps (owner: IT Ops). 3) Add automated post-provision validation step to imaging pipeline to detect NIC flaps (owner: Imaging Team).
payload.summary: Display orientation registration fails when docked to eGPU, causing provisioning loop

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A vendor (OptiRack Ltd) sent a single EUR invoice that references three separate POs across two cost centers. Our AP system consolidated the lines into one outgoing payment file. The receiving bank rejected the SWIFT payment citing missing beneficiary intermediary code (BEN code) and mismatched invoice/PO metadata. The vendor is unpaid and has escalated to procurement.

Impact:
- Supplier payment stalled for a quarterly hardware invoice (~€42,600).
- Potential supplier relationship risk; procurement escalation.
- Cash forecast reporting inaccurate for March payrun.

Environment:
- Production (accounts-payable pipeline)
- Region: eu-west
- Payment rail: SWIFT (SEPA cross-border)

Steps to reproduce / Observed behavior:
1) Vendor invoice INV-2026-0847 posted on 2026-03-11. Invoice contains lines for PO-7781, PO-7782, PO-8029.
2) AP automation grouped lines under a single payment instruction during scheduled payrun 2026-03-12.
3) Treasury submitted outgoing SWIFT; downstream bank returned a rejection with code: BEN-MISSING/MDATA-MISMATCH.
4) AP shows payment as REJECTED and vendor remains unpaid.

Attachments / Logs:
- AP system export: ap_export_INV-2026-0847.csv (attached to ticket)
- Bank rejection file: MT103_REJ_20260312.txt (attached)
- Vendor email thread: procurement_optirack_20260313.eml (attached)

Immediate ask:
- Require finance ops to split the original instruction into separate payruns aligned to each PO/cost center and re-submit with corrected remittance details.
- Confirm bank advice format corrected to include BEN code and PO metadata matching vendor expectations.

Desired outcome:
- Vendor paid within 48 hours of ticket creation.
- Short-term workaround: manual payments for the rejected amounts.
- Long-term: update payment validation to surface consolidated-PO edge cases before payrun submission.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 08:22 - Procurement (Jules Carter): Vendor confirmed IBAN correction; outstanding payment now cleared in reconciliation. Vendor appreciates the quick manual handling.
Findings:
- Root cause: AP consolidation flag 'consolidate_by_supplier' combined multiple PO lines into one remittance block. Our SWIFT/MT103 generation only preserves a single beneficiary reference when consolidation occurs, dropping BEN code and line-level PO annotations that this supplier's bank uses for routing.
- The bank's MT103 validation enforces a beneficiary intermediary for multi-cost-center invoices from this vendor; when missing, the payment is rejected downstream.
- Existing unit tests cover single-PO flows but not multi-PO consolidation for vendors that require repeated remittance elements.
Immediate mitigation implemented:
- Manual split payruns executed (two accepted, one required vendor IBAN update).
- AP process owner disabled automatic consolidation for vendors flagged as 'requires-line-remittance' until fix is deployed.
Recommendations for fix:
1) Update payrun generator to preserve line-level remittance fields and replicate beneficiary blocks when consolidating multiple POs for the same supplier, or skip consolidation for vendors with 'line remittance required' flag.
2) Add validation step pre-submission to detect dropped BEN/PO fields and surface a hard block for treasury.
3) Create a small regression test suite covering consolidated multi-PO -> MT103 mapping for sample vendors.
4) Add vendor metadata field in AP (requires-line-remittance) and a migration for historical vendors with previous rejections.
Workaround: Manual split payruns created and resubmitted. Vendor paid (two payments cleared, final payment cleared after vendor IBAN confirmation).
Permanent fix plan: Engineering ticket raised to modify MT103 generator and payrun validation; release target: 2026-04-01. Change will: prevent silent dropping of BEN/PO fields during consolidation and add a pre-submit validation step.
Follow-ups:
- Create a short runbook for AP/Treasury to handle future multi-PO bank rejections.
- Data task: flag vendors that previously experienced MT103 rejections so consolidation can be disabled.
- Linked engineering task assigned (see related_github_prs).
payload.summary: EUR multi-PO vendor invoice flagged after bank rejection; needs split payrun + corrected remittance

Issue summary:
Support is requested to provision timebound, least-privilege, cross-cloud read-only access for the Security Automation team to run an org-wide compliance/audit scan. The automation runs a set of read-only checks across AWS and GCP accounts (prod and staging) and requires the ability to enumerate IAM bindings, list S3/GCS buckets, and pull recent logs (CloudWatch / Cloud Logging) for the past 30 days.

Impact:
- Automation required by Compliance (internal) cannot complete until access is available; this blocks a scheduled control test for next week.
- Not providing timebound, auditable access increases risk around ad-hoc broad permissions.

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
- Provision an ephemeral AWS IAM role and a mapped GCP service account access pattern usable by the automation runner.
- Access must be strictly read-only across specified projects/accounts: prod and staging (see environment field).
- Access TTL: 8 hours per issuance, issued via STS / Workload Identity; no long-lived credentials.
- All assumes/issuances must be logged (CloudTrail + Cloud Logging) and a short summary posted to #security-ops.
- Terraform changes must be captured in infra repo PRs listed above and linked to this ticket.

Environment / scope:
- AWS org: core-prod, core-staging (us-east region primary)
- GCP org: redwood-prod, redwood-staging (eu-west project group)
- Systems: S3, CloudWatch (Log Insights), IAM, GCS, Cloud Logging, Resource Manager (projects)

Steps to reproduce / how automation will use access:
1) Security automation pod (k8s) will exchange its short-lived pod identity for the ephemeral access via STS/Workload Identity and run inventory scripts.
2) Scripts call list/describe APIs only; no write/modify operations.

Requested TTL and justifications:
- TTL 8 hours to allow full scan without re-authorization.
- Timebound issuance reduces blast radius and supports auditability.

Approval chain / business justification:
- Approved by: Security (Maya R.) and Compliance (Evan R.).
- Business reason: required quarterly control test and evidence collection for SOC2 readiness.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 08:30 - Security (Maya R.): Confirmed approval for 8h TTL and audit logging requirement. Security requests conditional on MFA-backed assume or token issuing from internal STS gateway.
Checked org SCPs and IAM conditions in AWS - existing org-level deny prevents broad s3:ListAllMyBuckets; will create resource-level allow for listed bucket ARNs.
GCP projects use centralized KMS and audit logs are routed to a logging-bucket; will ensure service account has logging.viewer and storage.objectViewer scoped roles only.
Validated that the automation runner can use workload identity federation to assume AWS role via OIDC proxy; implemented external ID pattern to prevent confused-deputy.
Confirmed CloudTrail and Cloud Logging retention is sufficient for 30-day evidence; added extra event logging for AssumeRole and key service calls for this TTL window.
Applied least-privilege principle: no iam:PutRolePolicy or iam:PassRole; restricted to sts:AssumeRole and read-only API sets.
In-progress rollout: Created AWS role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ephemeral-audit-readonly with a trust policy that allows sts:AssumeRole from the internal STS gateway (external-id in place). Created GCP service account redwood-ephemeral-audit@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com and mapped to a workload identity pool for the automation runner. Terraform PRs: infra/pull/2387 and terraform-cloud/pull/166 contain the exact policy bundles.
Testing notes: Applied to staging 2026-03-12, successful assume-role end-to-end and inventory run completed with only read operations. Logs were forwarded to the compliance logging bucket and an audit summary posted to #security-ops.
Follow-ups before closing:
- Roll the change to prod after one more smoke test (assigned to Diego).
- Add automated TTL issuance to the internal STS gateway (ticket INT-16010) and link back.
- Add an Ops-runbook snippet to Confluence: Cross-Cloud Ephemeral Access (pending PR).
Ticket will be updated when prod rollout is complete and PRs are merged.

A subset of developer laptops imaged with the standard Ubuntu 22.04 corporate image are failing to finish post-imaging provisioning: users report that their dotfiles (dotfiles repo sync via git+ssh) do not materialize, dev shells fail because configuration files are missing, and some user services that depend on files in the home directory fail to start.

Environment:
- Image: redwood-ubuntu-22.04-corp-2026-02 (autogenerated SCCM/MAAS image)
- Provisioning flow: first-boot cloud-init + custom postinst scripts -> enroll in MDM -> fscrypt/ecryptfs home unlock -> dotfiles sync (git) via /usr/local/bin/corp-sync
- Hardware: Dell XPS 13 (9310), Framework 13 dev units, and a few custom Ubuntu pre-rolled Lenovo units.
- Regions: staging-us-east for validation; repro also seen in prod-us-west.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Flash image and boot for first-time provisioning with a network-attached user account.
2. cloud-init runs; MDM enroll succeeds.
3. home-directory encryption unlock code (fscrypt) runs as part of postinst.
4. corp-sync kicks off via systemd user service to clone dotfiles.
5. corp-sync exits with permission denied errors when writing into ~/<dotfiles> and sometimes reports empty repository after clone.
6. Systemd user services that expect the dotfiles fail to start.

Logs / artifacts attached: (pasted extracts below and in attachments)
- /var/log/cloud-init-output.log: shows corp-sync execution starting at 2026-03-09T09:10:21Z
- /home/<user>/.cache/corp-sync/log: contains Git permission denied: "error: insufficient permission for adding an object to repository database"
- dmesg: occasionally shows kernel messages about FS metadata updates being retried after IO errors during early boot on NVMe.

Expected behavior:
- Postinst should ensure home directory is fully unlocked and owned by the target user before corp-sync runs. Dotfiles repo should clone successfully and services depending on them should start.

Actual behavior:
- Race condition where corp-sync sometimes runs before fscrypt fully rewraps/permits writes to the home directory, resulting in git failing with permission errors or creating files owned by root.

Workarounds tried:
- Manual chown and rerun of corp-sync -> fixes the machine
- Enqueue corp-sync to run on first interactive login via PAM (works but delays provisioning)

Attachments: cloud-init fragments, example corp-sync log snippets, sudo ls -la output showing root-owned .git directory in home.
Aisha Romero (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Initial ticket created after two new hires reported broken shells post-imaging. Collected logs and repro steps.
Ethan Cole (Assignee) - 2026-03-11: Started investigation. Observed root-owned .git directory in one repro. Hypothesis: postinst fscrypt unlock race with systemd user service startup order.
SRE (Maya Lin) - 2026-03-11: Saw repeated IO errors on NVMe during early boot in dmesg for one unit. Suggested delaying corp-sync until /home health check passes.
Ethan Cole - 2026-03-12: Confirmed reproducible on a Framework 13 dev unit by toggling timing; created a small systemd oneshot that waits for /home writeable check, which prevents the failure in manual tests.
Aisha Romero - 2026-03-12: Requesting this be added to the image pipeline ASAP; new hires are waiting. Asked for suggested short-term mitigation for on-call imaging team.
Ethan Cole - 2026-03-12: Proposed mitigation documented in resolution field. Will produce a PR to image repo by EOD and follow up with QA validation steps.
Timeline and technical findings:
- Reproduced locally by creating artificial delay in fscrypt re-key/unwrap path; corp-sync was triggered by a systemd user service that has DefaultDependencies=no and WantedBy=graphical.target to speed up provisioning.
- When corp-sync runs early, git creates repository objects owned by root (postinst runs as root but corp-sync called as systemd --user during user-session setup causes mixed ownership).
- dmesg intermittent IO errors correlate with NVMe firmware version 2.3.5 on one Dell unit; that unit shows delayed filesystem metadata commits which may exacerbate the timing window.
- fscrypt unlock happens in /etc/cryptsetup scripts during early mount; however, our image uses fscrypt with login-passphrase unlocking via PAM which completes slightly later for network accounts.
- The root cause is a startup ordering/timing race between home-directory writeability and the user-level dotfiles sync service.

Actions taken during triage:
- Reproduced failure with timed repro harness.
- Implemented temporary systemd oneshot (check-home-writeable.service) that verifies writing and reading a small test file as target user before enabling corp-sync. Manual testing showed reliability improvement from ~65% success to 100% in 20 trial boots.
Mitigation and next steps:
Short-term workaround (applied to staging image pipeline):
- Add check-home-writeable.service as a dependency for corp-sync.service; the oneshot will retry up to 10 times with a 2s backoff to wait for home writeability. This reduces the race window and allows provisioning to complete without manual chown.

Medium-term fixes planned:
- Update image pipeline to run corp-sync from a root-run postinst that chroots into the final home and performs the clone with sudo -u <user>, ensuring correct ownership regardless of systemd timing.
- Work with Firmware Team to identify NVMe firmware versions causing delayed metadata commits and block problematic versions from depot images.
- Add test coverage in CI that simulates delayed fs metadata commits and confirms corp-sync behavior.

Related artifacts/PRs:
- github.com/redwood-infra/image-repo/pull/987 (draft) - add check-home-writeable.service and test harness
- internal runbook created: confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Ubuntu+home+fs+race+provisioning

Status: workaround merged into staging image; PR for root-run clone being prepared. QA validation scheduled for 2026-03-16.
payload.summary: Encrypted home-directory permission race prevents dotfiles sync and breaks dev environment after Ubuntu imaging

Issue summary: During the scheduled Vault transit key rotation on 2026-03-12 at 03:00 UTC, the cluster admission controller started rejecting self-hosted runner pods that did not include the new required annotation (assembly.redwood.com/cred-rotation=2026-03-12). Impact: ~120 queued release jobs across two orgs failed to provision runners and remained in Pending state for ~45 minutes. Affected services: CI/CD canary and nightly release pipelines; customer-facing builds were delayed. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger a runner pod create without the annotation (kubectl apply -f runner-pod.yaml). 2) Observe admission controller deny event. 3) Check runner-manager logs for provisioning backoff. Observed behavior: admission controller returns 403 with message "missing required cred-rotation annotation" for pods created by runner-manager. Expected behavior: runner-manager should either be updated to attach the annotation or admission policy should permit existing pods during rotation. Relevant logs/dashboards: - Kibana: logs/dashboard link: https://kibana.redwood.local/app/logs#/discover?_a=(query:...) - PagerDuty incident: PD-78321 - Affected node pools: ci-workers-*-uswest (spot-backed), which experienced high churn during restart window.
Hypothesis: admission policy was tightened in infra PR 1289 but runner-manager was not synchronized with new annotation requirement before vault rewrap completed.
kubectl get events --field-selector reason=FailedAdmissionWebhook -n ci-prod -> many entries 'missing required cred-rotation annotation'
AdmissionWebhook configuration snapshot: kubectl get ValidatingWebhookConfiguration kube-policy -o yaml (see related_confluence_pages for snapshot).
Runner-manager image: registry.redwood/cirunner:1.14.2 (does not include annotation injection code path). Hotfix builds add metadata in pod template generation.
Observed token lifecycle: Vault rewrap short TTL (3600s) caused quick rotation; onboarding window for runner-manager update missed due to deployment rollout cadence.
CI queue depth: max 124 pending runner requests at 03:18 UTC; mean pod create latency increased 3x.
Manual mitigation steps tested: - disable admission enforcement; - deploy runner-manager 1.14.3 with annotation; - re-enable enforcement; all validated in canary us-west-1a before full enable.
Related traces: trace ids trace-prod-ccf9 and trace-prod-d1b8 correlate with runner-manager create requests.
Related existing tickets reviewed: INT-620743 (proxy tls rotation), INT-35720 (agent bootstrap token expiry)
Related infra PRs: github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/1289, github.com/redwood/runner-manager/pull/342

Additional notes:
Root cause: timing mismatch between cluster admission policy rollout (requiring assembly.redwood.com/cred-rotation annotation) and runner-manager rollout; Vault rewrap completed triggering enforcement earlier than runner-manager update. Fix applied: 1) Deployed runner-manager hotfix v1.14.3 to emit required annotation. 2) Temporarily disabled annotation enforcement during immediate recovery window, then re-enabled after validation. 3) Updated deployment pipeline to include annotation compatibility gate before admission policy changes are promoted. 4) Increased Vault rewrap notification to downstream services and added a 30-minute grace window for admission policy activation during credential rotations. Follow-ups: - Create automated pre-flight check in infra CI to validate that all runner-producing services include required annotations before merging admission policy PRs. - Update runbook: CONFLUENCE-Runbooks/Credential-Rotation to include a rollback playbook and communications checklist. - Schedule cross-team drill for secret rotations. Incident closed after backlog drained and normal provisioning observed for 24h.
payload.summary: Admission controller annotation enforcement causes runner pods to be rejected during credential rotation

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A customer reported a potential PII leak in generated outputs from an application using redwood/longform-v1. We need a narrowly scoped forensic sample extract from production inference logs to reproduce the issue and validate whether PII appeared in model outputs.

Justification:
- Reproduction required to determine root cause (model prompt leakage vs. prompt content).
- Small, time-boxed sample minimizes exposure.

Scope of data requested:
- Time window: 2026-03-11 00:00:00 to 2026-03-11 23:59:59 (UTC)
- Up to 200 inference records matching the customer tenant and the reported conversation hashes.
- Include fields: request_id, customer_tenant_id (hashed), request_prompt (redacted), response_text (original and redacted copy), model_version, routing_info, timestamp, and system metadata (instance id, region).
- Explicit exclusion: do NOT include raw user identifiers or customer-provided file blobs.

Redaction & security controls proposed:
- Hash customer_tenant_id with HMAC-SHA256 and store salt in KMS-scoped key; original id not stored in extract.
- Run automated PII DLP scanner on response_text and mask email addresses, phone numbers, and long (>=16) numeric sequences. Keep an unmasked copy in an encrypted S3 object encrypted with customer-specific KMS key accessible only to approvers for a maximum of 7 days.
- Write-only S3 path with ACL restricted to the approved list; enable S3 object lock and server-side encryption with KMS.
- Access audit: all downloads require an IAM session with MFA and are logged to the security audit trail.

Retention & disposal:
- Extract TTL: 7 calendar days from extraction completion; automated deletion triggered by lifecycle rule.
- Any derived artifacts (screenshots, local copies) must be ephemeral and deleted after use; users must attest to deletion in this ticket.

Approval needed from:
- Security (data handling and key access)
- Legal/Privacy (customer notice & contract review)
- Engineering (SRE or runtime owner to run job)

Impact if delayed:
- Slows customer response and may escalate to incident; potential regulatory exposure if PII is confirmed.

Requested owner and run plan:
- Owner: Ethan Park (SRE) to run extraction job with help from Infra tooling.
- Run plan: run a narrow query against tensorflow-prod-logs table, filter by customer tenant hash, limit 200 rows, pipe to DLP scanner, package results to secure S3 with metadata manifest and HMAC verification.

Acceptance criteria:
- Security and Legal sign-off documented in comments.
- Extract contains only scoped fields and passes DLP masking policy.
- TTL and audit controls in place and verified.

Additional notes:
Staging dry-run query (staging table names replaced): SELECT request_id, tenant_hash, response_text, model_version, timestamp FROM inference_logs_staging WHERE tenant_hash = '<tenant_hash>' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-03-11T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-11T23:59:59Z' LIMIT 200;
Initial staging sample: 12 candidate records where response_text contains potential PII-like patterns (emails/phone). None confirmed as customer-provided content yet.
Hypotheses: (1) customer prompt included pasted contact details => not a model leakage; (2) model exposed training data artifacts under specific prompt pattern => requires broader sample analysis. Forensic extract will help distinguish.
DLP config: run 'dlp-scan-v2' that masks emails using regex and flags high-entropy numeric sequences. Verify mask_count == 0 before allowing approvers to download unmasked artifact.
Extraction script location: github.com/redwood/infrastructure/forensics/scripts/extract_prod_samples.sh (PR pending: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/842)
S3 upload target (write-only): s3://redwood-secure/forensic/INT-32177/ (server-side-encryption: aws:kms, kms-key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/forensic-int-32177)
Approvers list: Maya Chen (reporter), Ethan Park (SRE), Priya Natarajan (Security), Jonah Ruiz (Legal).
2026-03-14: Security and Legal approved the extraction with conditions. SRE ran the extraction job and uploaded two objects: masked_results.json (masked) and encrypted_unmasked_results.enc (KMS-wrapped) to s3://redwood-secure/forensic/INT-32177/. Extraction produced 87 records; DLP scan flagged 5 records which were masked in masked_results.json. Access granted to approvers only via temporary IAM session. TTL configured to delete objects after 7 days (lifecycle rule). Customer notification template drafted by Legal and queued for sending; audit trail entry created in the security log. Follow-up action: add a pre-filter runbook to annotate suspicious prompts at ingestion and schedule a post-incident review to consider automated prompt redaction (owner: Product Security).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A subset of observability agents (metrics/traces collectors) running in the Dedicated fleet are failing to push telemetry because they cannot impersonate the GCP service account when routed via the AWS STS->GCP broker. This started after a recent org-policy/IAM cleanup that added attribute-based conditionals on serviceAccount impersonation roles.

Impact:
- Production metrics and traces missing for ~6 Dedicated customers in us-east and eu-west regions for ~36 hours.
- Alerts suppressed for affected tenant routes; engineering oncall escalations generated.
- No customer-facing requests reported yet, but internal SLAs for observability were violated.

Environment:
- prod | us-east, eu-west
- Dedicated fleet (redwood-dedicated-prod), STS identity broker between AWS account A and GCP org.
- Affected component: observability-agent container image: redwood/obs-agent:v2.1.4

1) From an affected dedicated node, run: gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=sa-observability@customer-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
2) Observe IAM denial: 'Request had insufficient authentication scopes' or 'Permission iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken denied'.
3) Trace path through STS broker: aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/redwood-sts-broker -> broker uses workload identity federation to exchange credentials for GCP impersonation.
4) Reproduce intermittently depending on which broker instance and GCP org policy evaluation path is used.
2026-03-10T02:12:14Z obs-agent[pid=4378]: ERROR: impersonation failed: iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken denied for sa-observability@customer-project.
    (requestor: sts-broker-arn:aws:sts::ACCOUNT:assumed-role/redwood-sts-broker/session)
2026-03-10T02:12:14Z broker[info]: federated token exchange success -> attempting gcloud impersonate -> IAM DENY response: 'Permission denied. Condition "resource.name.startsWith('projects/_/serviceAccounts/')" not satisfied'
2026-03-10T02:45:01Z gce-audit[warning]: orgPolicy: constraint 'iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains' enforced; conditional binding present on roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
Support (Rajesh Patel) 2026-03-10: Triage - observed spike in obs-agent 'impersonation failed' errors. Opening cross-team Slack #infra-iam and paging SRE.
SRE (Marta Alvarez) 2026-03-10: Initial hypothesis - recent org-level conditional binding added to service account token creator role; may be matching on resource.name vs resource.service. Asking Cloud Infra to export binding conditions.
Cloud Infra (Tobias Nguyen) 2026-03-11: Confirmed conditional exists on project-level role binding applied by terraform module 'iam/roles-v2'. Condition expression uses request.auth.aud and resource.name mismatch when using federation via STS broker. Working on repro and mitigation plan.
Support (Emily Chen) 2026-03-12: Working mitigation - temporarily relax conditional on dedicated broker principal in staging, then apply to prod after validation. Will coordinate a short maintenance window and notify customers if needed.
- Root cause: Org-level IAM conditional added to restrict iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to calls where resource.name matches 'projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/serviceAccounts/*' exactly. Workload identity broker exchanges credentials via federated principal path that results in a slightly different resource.name evaluation path, causing condition to fail.
- Reproduced locally by using the broker's federated token with alterted audience claim -> condition evaluation fails only for broker-issued tokens.
- Also observed a related org-policy enforcement that denies certain federated principals unless an attribute 'broker_id' is present in the condition. The broker did not add this attribute in its token exchange flow.
- Affected customers: dedicated tenants on redwood-dedicated-prod whose telemetry pipeline uses broker instance group a/b. Not all instances affected because some broker instances include additional claims.
Mitigation applied 2026-03-12 03:40 UTC: Temporarily updated terraform 'iam/roles-v2' module to add an exception for arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/redwood-sts-broker with a condition that matches the broker's token attributes.
Follow-up permanent fix: (1) Update STS broker to include 'broker_id' and stable audience claim during federation exchange; (2) Add unit/integration test to terraform module to validate conditional expressions against broker tokens; (3) Roll out a policy-change runbook for cross-cloud IAM condition updates.
Post-action: Verified metrics ingestion resumed for affected tenants within 15 minutes of mitigation. Created proposaland PRs for infra and broker changes.
payload.summary: Observability agent service-account impersonation denied due to cross-cloud IAM conditional mismatch

Issue summary:
Several engineers report failing to clone/pull private repos and being unable to open Grafana dashboards. Errors surface as SSH auth failures against the internal SSH proxy and 403s in the console. Problem started after an Okta device-trust client update rolled on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- Multiple developer workflows blocked (git clone/push).
- On-call engineers cannot access Grafana runbooks tied to incidents.
- Productivity impact across two teams (Infra and SDK).

Environment:
- prod-us-west (SSH gateway cluster sgw-prod-3)
- Okta device-trust release v2.8.1 deployed 2026-03-09

Observed errors:
- ssh: handshake failed: no acceptable authentication methods
- logs show proxy rejecting agent-signer assertion: "missing CA-forwarding-claim"
- Grafana requests 403 with SSO error: "assertion missing forwarding_subject"

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start local ssh-agent and add key using okta-ssh-sign (okta-signer v1.5.0).
2) Attempt git clone git@git.internal.redwood.ai:team/repo.git from a laptop with device-trust enrolled.
3) Observe immediate failure and check ssh-agent debug output.

Notes: This is not a full outage but blocks core developer flows. The condition appears intermittent across machines; some users on the same Okta policy are unaffected (likely dependent on agent version and agent-forwarding negotiation).

Run: GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -v' git clone git@git.internal.redwood.ai:team/repo.git

Issue summary:
HR is offboarding a long-term contractor (EU-based) who is relocating to LATAM and requests to ship company laptop internationally. There are multiple open policy questions: who pays VAT/customs, whether we permit encrypted SSDs shipped across borders, whether we should capture a forensic snapshot before wipe, and how to handle KMS/HSM keys and cloud service account ownership tied to the contractor.

Impact:
- Delay in deprovisioning cloud/service accounts if ownership transfer is unclear.
- Potential regulatory or tax exposure if hardware is sold/transferred across borders without proper VAT handling.
- Security risk if device is wiped without backup of corporate data and service account secrets.

Relevant context:
- Contractor tier: dedicated-like engagement (access to private repos and some service accounts).
- Device: company-owned MacBook Pro with corporate MDM, FileVault enabled, company-managed recovery keys stored in KMS.
- Cloud access: GCP service accounts, GitHub org admin access on a small set of repos, Okta SSO.
- Payroll status: final invoice being processed; contractor requests shipment of device to new personal address in LATAM.

Questions we need answered by policy owners:
1) Is shipping company laptop to a non-EU personal address permitted? If permitted, who covers shipping + VAT/customs?
2) Do we require a forensic snapshot (disk image + log export) before a device is wiped and returned? Under what conditions?
3) Should the FileVault recovery key be escrowed and then destroyed, or should we perform a hardware wipe before shipping?
4) What is the expected process/timeline for transferring ownership of service accounts and repo access vs immediate suspension?
5) Who must approve an exception (HR + Legal + Security + Payroll)?

Suggested short-term approach (HR proposal):
- Pause immediate suspension of GitHub and GCP ownership until a transfer plan is executed (48-72h window).
- IT to take encrypted forensic snapshot to secure S3 bucket for Legal/Security if there are suspected IP/contract obligations.
- If snapshot is taken, Security approves scoped retention of snapshot for 90 days; then purge unless Legal requests retention.
- We pay for standard return shipping when device is returned to a Redwood facility; if shipping overseas to personal address, request contractor covers costs unless Legal approves exception.
- KMS: rotate and revoke any keys the contractor exclusively holds and ensure recovery keys are captured in corporate vault prior to any wipe.

Desired outcome:
Clarify policy and approval chain so HR can finalize offboarding checklist and communicate to contractor without ad-hoc decisions.
1) HR to obtain written approval from Legal and Security for any deviation from standard return-to-US policy.
2) IT asset manager to create encrypted forensic snapshot (if requested) and store in restricted bucket.
3) Security to rotate/revoke KMS keys associated with contractor services after ownership transfer.
4) Access team to remove repo org admin roles only after transfer or documented handoff.
5) Payroll/Finance to confirm cost owner for shipping/VAT.
6) Final confirmation and closure in this ticket.
- IT confirmed filevault is enabled and corporate recovery key exists in the KMS vault.
- Security notes: previous similar case required a 72h window to transfer ownership for critical repos (see linked case INT-17430).
- Legal flagged potential VAT reporting obligations for hardware shipped out of EU to personal addresses; advised to avoid unless contractor covers VAT and provides customs paperwork.
- Payroll confirmed final invoice timeline overlaps with proposed 48-72h transfer window; recommends holding final payout until asset reconciliation is complete if company bears shipping cost.
Priya Nair (HR) [2026-03-10]: Opening ticket after contractor notified their relocation. Requesting clear vendor/legal guidance on cross-border hardware shipments and KMS handling.
Maya Chen (IT Asset) [2026-03-10]: We can create an encrypted forensic snapshot. We need Legal permission to retain for >30 days. Also: do we require contractor signature for chain-of-custody when shipping internationally?
Arjun Patel (Security) [2026-03-11]: Prefer to rotate any KMS keys the contractor had access to and require an internal handoff for service accounts. Forensic images only if there are IP concerns. Legal to advise on VAT/customs.
Sofia Duarte (Legal) [2026-03-11]: Shipping company assets abroad may trigger VAT/import paperwork and potential registration depending on country. Recommend contractor covers VAT and signs customs declaration; otherwise, return-to-US preferred. Legal to approve exceptions case-by-case.
Diego Ramos (Payroll) [2026-03-12]: If company pays for overseas shipping, Finance needs an approved cost center and vendor quote in writing. Suggest contractor pay and be reimbursed after asset confirmation if HR approves.
Maya Chen (IT Asset) [2026-03-12]: Proposed checklist attached in Confluence link. Suggest implementing a 72-hour transfer window for critical access before suspension.
Pending: awaiting Legal sign-off on VAT risk and approval path for exceptions. Security to prepare KMS rotation playbook for this scenario. HR to hold final payout until asset reconciliation is decided.
Legal to provide written approval or denial for outbound shipment by 2026-03-15.
Security to draft KMS rotation checklist for contractor-owned keys by 2026-03-14.
IT Asset to prepare encrypted snapshot runbook and cost estimate by 2026-03-13.
HR to communicate interim hold on final invoice payment to contractor and update offboarding email template.
If exception approved, Finance to capture shipping vendor quote and set cost center.
Close ticket after policy decision and completion of actions above.

Issue summary: WebSocket-based streaming responses for a long-form chat request intermittently stall and stop sending tokens after clients switch network connectivity (observed during 4G->5G handoff). Customer reports that the client-side socket remains open but no additional chunks arrive for ~20-90s, after which the connection either recovers or the server closes the socket with 502.

Impact: Multiple paying customers using LinguaChat's dedicated Redwood pool see degraded UX for long chats (5–20 minute responses). Symptoms started around 2026-03-12 22:10 UTC and correlate with increased tail latencies and a spike in worker preemptions. Affects ~3% of long-stream sessions for this customer during the incident window.

Environment: Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated GPU pool), production, us-east-1. Traffic routed through our edge websocket-proxy, then to per-tenant dedicated serving-runtime instances.

Observed behavior: Streaming halts mid-token sequence after client experiences cellular handoff. Server traces show in-flight request marked as "active" but no socket writes for 20–90s. Upstream worker remains healthy (CPU/GPU not saturated) and KV cache appears consistent. Edge logs show TLS session renegotiate events from the client IP at the time of stall.

Expected behavior: Streaming continues uninterrupted or fails-fast with a clear error and model fallback; tokens should not silently stop with socket left open.

Initial customer impact notes: LinguaChat reports multiple user sessions where the chat response stops for ~30s then resumes with a burst of tokens or the client shows an indefinite loading spinner. Customer escalated since it affects demo flows and user retention.

1) Use a mobile client connected to a 4G network and start a long-form chat request that triggers a multi-minute generation.
2) While the model is generating, trigger a cellular network handoff (4G -> 5G) or switch between mobile carriers (can be emulated via network conditioning tools).
3) Observe websocket traffic: client reports connection stays ESTABLISHED, but token frames cease for 20–90s (server-side), then either resume or the connection returns 502/connection-reset.
4) Capture server trace IDs and edge-proxy logs around the time of the handoff for analysis.

serving-runtime: trace=trc-20260312-1a2b3c, worker_id=d-pool-17b, kv_cache_hit=true, gpu_util=42%, last_token_emit=2026-03-12T22:13:46Z, in_flight_request=true
edge-proxy: trace=trc-20260312-5f6g7h, tls_session_resume=0, tls_renegotiate_count=1, client_user_agent=LinguaChat/4.7 (iOS)
2026-03-13 03:00 UTC - Initial triage (Aisha): Correlated customer reports with a small spike in websocket idle-write timeouts and with an increase in TLS renegotiation events from mobile IP ranges.
2026-03-13 05:20 UTC - SRE (Diego): Pulled edge-proxy traces for affected trace IDs; observed that the socket remained open and proxy did not send FIN. No obvious OOM or worker OOM events on serving runtime.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - Reproduced in staging: Simulated handoff with network emulator; saw keepalive packets reach proxy but a burst of retransmissions. When kernel TCP retransmit count exceeded threshold, proxy returned 0 bytes to worker and stalled for ~30s.
2026-03-13 11:00 UTC - Correlated with recent edge-proxy change: rolling deploy of proxy v2.17 introduced conservative write-coalescing when retransmit_count > 3 (PR 4123), which may amplify stalls for long-lived streaming sockets.
1) Short-term: Edge team to roll back proxy v2.17 write-coalescing change to previous behavior (v2.16) for affected dedicated pools (target: 1-hour hotfix).
2) Customer workaround: Reduce client-side keepalive interval to 10s to reduce perceived stall window and enable client reconnect logic that can resume stream using conversation_id (app-level workaround).
3) Fallback: Configure model fallback to small-batched non-streaming endpoint with fail-fast if the HTTP/WS layer reports network retransmit counts above threshold.
In progress: Edge proxy team preparing hotfix roll-back (v2.16) to remove aggressive write suppression on TCP retransmit events. Plan: roll back to v2.16 for LinguaChat's dedicated pool during low-traffic window, validate with customer test devices, monitor tail latency for 24h. Post-mortem and follow-up PR will add better heuristics for streaming sockets under mobile network conditions.
1) Edge team to schedule rollback in canary (by 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC) and run targeted tests with customer test devices.
2) SRE to instrument additional websocket metrics: retransmit_count, write_suspend_events, per-socket buffer_queued_bytes.
3) Product to assess long-term mitigations: streaming retry semantics, resumable token ranges, and client SDK helpers for mobile reconnection.
4) After stabilization, run a postmortem and notify customer with timeline and permanent fix plan.
Support (Aisha Kumar) 2026-03-13: Customer reports 8 sessions affected in the last 24h; provided sample trace IDs and HAR of websocket session. Asked for priority handling due to demo impact.
SRE (Diego Ramirez) 2026-03-13: Replicated stall in staging using network emulation. Opening follow-up with edge team to revert/coarsen new write-coalescing threshold as a hotfix.
Edge eng (Maya Chen) 2026-03-13: Found the proxy change that suppresses writes on retransmits. Will prepare a rollback/patch and run canary with LinguaChat's dedicated pool traffic if approved.
Customer (LinguaChat ops contact) 2026-03-13: Confirmed they'll schedule a maintenance window for a canary if we can guarantee minimal disruption. Provided their test device pool for validation.

Issue summary:
A Vault transit rewrap that coincided with a CI image refresh resulted in SSH agent socket files being created under a different path inside ephemeral runner containers. Runner init and job entrypoints assume a predictable SSH_AUTH_SOCK path; when the socket was created under /run/user/<uid>/ssh-XXXX the job processes could not locate the agent and all git-over-ssh operations failed.

Impact:
- ~120 nightly release pipeline runs in us-east failed between 2026-03-12 02:40 and 2026-03-12 03:25 UTC.
- Failures manifested as immediate git fetch/clone authorization errors, blocking canary artifact promotion and delaying three release jobs.

Environment:
- Prod CI (ephemeral runner fleet) in us-east region
- Runner base image: rdx/ci-runner:2026-03-10
- Vault: transit rewrap performed 2026-03-12 02:30 UTC

Expected behavior:
- Ephemeral runner init should locate active ssh-agent socket or start an agent and export SSH_AUTH_SOCK so job steps that perform SSH can authenticate.

Observed behavior:
- Job logs show errors: 'Could not open a connection to your authentication agent.' and 'ssh: connect to socket /tmp/ssh-XXXXX: No such file or directory'.

- Correlated Vault transit rewrap window with start of failures. Rewrap rotated secrets used by cloud-init that influence systemd user session behavior; side-effect: ssh-agent created by systemd user spawned under /run/user/<uid> instead of historical /tmp prefix.
- Runner image update on 2026-03-10 introduced a change in bootstrap ordering: ssh-agent is now started by 'systemd --user' early in the boot, while the old entrypoint created a socket in /tmp and exported SSH_AUTH_SOCK before job steps inherit env vars.
- Ephemeral runner bootstrap relies on a deterministic SSH_AUTH_SOCK path derived from a tmp prefix; when systemd user created the agent in a different namespace, the bind-mount step in the runner pod creation failed because it attempted to reference the old /tmp path on the host where no socket existed.
- Reproduced in staging by forcing ssh-agent to use /run/user path; confirmed that without a fallback we see immediate git-over-ssh failures in job container.
1) Patch runner-init to probe common agent locations (/tmp/ssh-*, /run/user/*/ssh-*) and, if found, export the discovered path into job environment before executing steps.
2) For existing pods, restart the ephemeral runner pods to pick up patched init; applied to canary pool (5% of runners) to validate.
3) For particularly urgent releases, use HTTPS git remotes as a temporary workaround (not ideal for deploy keys).
Hotfix: Commit rdx/ci-runner@patch-2026-03-13 modifies entrypoint to perform a socket discovery routine and fall back to starting a local ssh-agent if no socket is found. Deployed a canary rollout to 5% of ephemeral runners at 2026-03-13 09:10 UTC. Observed success: subsequent nightly jobs in canary used discovered /run/user sockets or started their own agent and completed git operations. Full rollout to prod runners completed 2026-03-14 03:30 UTC.

Follow-ups scheduled: update runbook for Vault rewrap procedures to include runner socket invariants, add a CI test that simulates agent socket relocation, and coordinate with infra team to avoid simultaneous image & Vault rewraps during midnight deploy window.
- ACTION-1: Add socket-discovery integration tests to runner image CI (owner: CI Eng, due: 2026-03-20)
- ACTION-2: Update Vault rotation runbook to notify CI/Runner teams and pause image rollouts if socket namespace behavior changes (owner: Security/Infra, due: 2026-03-18)
- ACTION-3: Instrument agent socket creation in runner metrics and alert if a socket path is created outside accepted prefixes (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-25)
- ACTION-4: Add a canary gating step to prevent Vault transit rewraps and runner image rollouts from overlapping (owner: Release Eng, due: 2026-03-22)
Ava Martinez (SRE) [2026-03-12T03:05Z]: Initial triage - failures spike right after Vault rewrap. Watching for pattern; escalating to CI Eng.
Priya Nair (CI Eng) [2026-03-12T04:10Z]: Confirmed reproduction in staging. Socket path differs; preparing patch to probe /run/user. Will canary ASAP.
Liam Chen (Release Eng) [2026-03-13T08:50Z]: Deployed canary patch to 5% of runners. Observed successful git clones in canary runs. Approving wider rollout pending monitoring results.
Ethan Clarke (reporter) [2026-03-14T02:50Z]: Full rollout completed. Marking as in progress until we close out postmortem actions and update runbooks.
payload.summary: ssh-agent socket relocation after vault rewrap causes ephemeral runner SSH auth failures

Issue summary: After approvers click 'Grant' on a JIT access request for the internal Support Runbook Portal, the request shows Approved but the requesting user is unable to access the portal and receives a 403 with an Okta error referencing device posture. Impact: Two on-call engineers were blocked from performing emergency runbook steps during a paging event; manual SRE escalation required. Environment: Production, us-west region, Runbook Portal (internal), Okta org with recently enabled device-posture Conditional Access policy. This ticket tracks diagnosis and a safe mitigation path.
1) Create a JIT access request for 'runbook-portal:edit' via the Support Portal approver flow.
2) Approver authenticates in Okta, reviews request, and clicks 'Grant'. Okta logs show approval completed.
3) Requesting user attempts to open https://runbooks.internal.redwood.com and is redirected to Okta then receives 403 with message 'Access denied: device posture not compliant'.
4) Repeating flow with a user who has device enrolled works as expected; approval grants immediate access.
2026-03-12T02:14:03Z - Approval event: okta.event: grant_approved, request_id=JIT-9876, approver=j.kim
2026-03-12T02:14:05Z - Auth redirect: /idp/authorize -> /idp/verify-device, status=403, error=device_posture_noncompliant
2026-03-12T02:15:12Z - Runbook portal returned 403 with header X-Auth-Reason: device_enrollment_required
Okta system log snippet: 'Device not enrolled; conditional access policy "Enforce managed device" blocked session.'
Initial hypothesis: JIT grant flow issues with token exchange step — approval completes but the session token lacks device claim required by Conditional Access.
Checked Okta system logs: approval event is recorded, but subsequent token exchange from support-portal to runbook-portal includes scope but omits device_posture claim for non-enrolled devices.
Reproduced locally with test user: when device is not enrolled, Okta prompts for device verification and then denies access despite approval; suggests policy evaluation happens after approval and blocks the session creation.
Observed difference: Managed/enrolled endpoints receive a different OIDC /userinfo response including 'device.enrolled: true', which is used by runbook-portal's authz layer. Non-enrolled flows do not get that claim and are rejected.
SRE can generate a short-lived bypass token via the support admin service (manual step documented in Confluence) and attach it to the user's session to allow runbook access during incident response. This is in place for affected requests until policy changes are deployed.
Coordinate with Identity team to: 1) Update the JIT grant token exchange to include a device_posture evaluation step and return a controlled bypass flag for approved requests issued to non-managed devices, OR 2) Adjust Conditional Access rule to allow JIT-approved sessions through a specific Okta client_id (support-admin) for the Runbook Portal. Prefer solution 1 for least privilege.
1) Identity to implement token-exchange change in staging and run a canary with a subset of oncall users. 2) Add observability to log device_posture evaluation events and approval correlation IDs. 3) Deploy to production behind a feature flag for two weeks, monitor access failure rate and incident page time-to-resolution.
Add clearer UX message in the Runbook Portal when device posture blocks access (linking to enrollment docs).
Create a short runbook for on-call SREs describing the manual bypass token procedure and how to request it from Identity team.
Audit other internal apps using JIT to ensure they don't assume device enrollment claims are present after approval.
Investigations show the Conditional Access policy evaluates device posture post-approval and the JIT token exchange did not include a special claim to let approved non-enrolled devices in. Identity has scoped a token-exchange change and a safe config tweak for the Okta policy. Temporary bypass procedure used successfully in two incidents. Pending code rollout and policy update.
payload.summary: Device-posture conditional access blocks JIT access grant to Support Runbook Portal after approval

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We need an automated self-service workflow to provision temporary cross-product 'Experiment Pod' environments for short-lived research projects (hackathons, model eval sprints, partner pilots). Each pod should create a Jira project, a Confluence space, and a Slack channel set using centralized templates and enforced guardrails (retention, membership controls, audit hooks).

Motivation / Impact:
- Current manual provisioning is slow (0.5–2 business days) and error-prone; teams create inconsistent spaces and slack conventions.
- Research teams frequently spin up many short-lived projects; lacking lifecycle automation leads to stale spaces and audit headaches.
- Need to reduce ops overhead while ensuring compliance (retention, DLP hooks, and access approvals).

Background / Context:
- Similar ephemeral automation exists for some pods but is fragmented.
- Security wants approved groups and audit events for all created artifacts.
- Product & Research teams want a single button self-service flow in the internal portal with optional manager approval for enterprise pods.
Desired features (high level):
1) Self-service form (internal portal) that captures: pod name, owning team, experiment lead, duration/TTL (1–90 days), access list or Okta group, and classification (public/internal/confidential).
2) Approval gate: instant for self_serve TTL <= 7 days and < 10 users; manager approval required otherwise.
3) Provisioning actions: create Jira project (kanban template, default workflows), Confluence space from sandbox template (pre-populated experiment checklist and retention metadata), and a Slack channel with naming convention and pinned onboarding message.
4) Lifecycle automation: automatic TTL enforcement with email notices at 7/3/1 day(s) before expiration, one-click extend, and automated archival/cleanup after expiry (with audit log).
5) Audit & telemetry: send creation/deletion/approval events to Datadog and write structured audit entries to the compliance Confluence page; capture service-account and webhook activity.
6) RBAC: integrate with Okta groups and centrally managed service accounts; created artifacts inherit group membership and use ephemeral service tokens.
7) Fail-safe: if any step fails, rollback created artifacts and notify requester + infra on-call with runbook link.
Internal portal form that provisions Jira/Confluence/Slack with one submit
Approval flow works per TTL rules and logs approvals
TTL lifecycle notifications and archive job run automatically
Audit events emitted to Datadog and appended to compliance Confluence space
Rollback works on partial failure (no orphaned spaces/channels)
Documentation and runbook published to Confluence and linked in the portal
Proposed implementation approach:
- UI: add a short flow in the internal provisioning portal (Frontend Team) that POSTs a request to platform-automation service.
- Orchestration: platform-automation will call terraform-managed modules (or internal provisioning lambdas) for each system in a transactional way; use a saga pattern with compensating actions.
- Slack: use the internal Slack app (bot) to create channels, set retention tags, and post onboarding messages.
- Confluence & Jira: use Atlassian REST APIs with a central service account; leverage a namespaced template repo for space/project skeletons.
- Auth: use Okta group lookups and SCIM to sync membership; create ephemeral service tokens stored in HashiCorp Vault.
- Observability: emit structured events (payload includes key, owner, template, TTL, approval_id) to the events stream (Kafka) and Datadog.
- Tests: e2e test harness that runs a dry-provision without creating real artifacts (mock APIs) plus integration tests in staging region.
- Rollback: implement compensating calls that delete created artifacts and record failure reason to central incident log.
1) Prototype in staging: small group of research engineers (2 weeks).
2) User feedback loop and iterate on form fields & templates (1 week).
3) Soft launch to consenting teams with quota limits (2 weeks).
4) Full launch with automated TTL enforcement and documented runbook (GA).
5) Post-launch: monitor for 30 days for failure patterns; add rate limits and quota controls if needed.
- Atlassian API rate limits may cause partial failures; need retry/backoff strategy.
- Incorrect TTL handling could lead to premature deletion or excess retention; require conservative defaults.
- RBAC misconfiguration could expose confidential spaces; require automated policy validation and pre-launch security review.
- Slack app permission model needs least-privilege check; legal/infosec signoff required for posting user invites.
- Automation creating many artifacts could increase cost/metadata clutter if not pruned properly.

Additional notes:
2026-03-03 - SRE Triage (Lena Huang): We can reuse the terraform modules from the ephemeral-sandbox project; will validate rate-limit considerations. Assigned to Marco Ruiz for implementation planning.
2026-03-05 - Security (Ravi Shah): Security sign-off request: need artifact classification enforcement and automated DLP checks on creation for confidential pods. Blocking until checklist items are satisfied.
payload.summary: Self-service 'Experiment Pod' automation for temporary research projects (Slack + Confluence + Jira)
