Issue summary:
HR asked for clarification on onboarding a contingent research contractor who will start remotely from two countries over the first 6 weeks. The contractor requires staggered seat/license activations (corporate laptop, cloud dev seat, and a Dedicated test account) and we need guidance on:
- policy for activating paid licenses only when the contractor permanently relocates to a covered region vs short-term travel;
- process for shipping company hardware cross-border (EU->UK->US) and required declarations;
- temporary service-account provisioning for VPN + ephemeral GPU access and the required KMS handling for device keys;
- recommended approach for rotating temporary credentials when the contractor has split-device custody (home and coworking space).

Impact:
- Onboarding is scheduled for 2026-03-22; uncertainty blocks IT procurement and hardware courier booking. Delay could push start by 1-2 weeks. There is low security exposure if handled correctly, but improper KMS handling or delayed credential rotation increases risk.

Context / environment:
- Contractor is engaged through a vendor (EU legal entity) and will be physically located in Ireland for weeks 1-3, then the UK for weeks 4-6, with occasional remote US overlap.
- They need a corporate laptop (encrypted), a Dedicated test account on a short-term reserved pool, and access to a shared S3 bucket with limited data.
- Legal requires evidence of device declaration for customs when shipping.

Steps to reproduce / replicate the ask:
1) HR submitted vendor contract and requested hardware shipment and cloud seats.
2) Procurement created PO and flagged that activation dates should be staggered against contract milestones.
3) IT needs to know whether to: (A) ship laptop immediately and activate cloud seats later, (B) hold ship until license/region alignment confirmed, or (C) ship but keep accounts disabled until verified.

Logs / attachments / references:
- Procurement PO: PO-43321 (attached in HR ticket).
- Previous guidance: Confluence pages listed above.

Requested outcome:
- Clear recommended process and short checklist HR/IT should follow for cross-border contingent hires with split-region schedules, including: shipping guidance, license activation triggers, KMS handling for device keys, and credential rotation cadence.
payload.summary: Staggered license activation and cross-border device staging for contingent worker (policy clarification)

comments: Console: dashboard panel fails to load; API returns 403 for incident taxonomy endpoints.
payload.description:
Issue summary
- CS team members cannot access the new Incident Taxonomy dashboards (volume by incident_type/owner, MTTR/SLA breach panels).
- Errors observed:
  - Grafana: "Access denied" / "You do not have permission to view this dashboard"

Additional notes:
Impact
- CS cannot answer customer questions during escalations ("what kind of incident is this?", "which team owns it?", "are we within remediation SLA?") without asking SRE/Eng to screenshot or paste data.
- Blocks rollout of the comms workflow described in the incident taxonomy program (CS is supposed to use incident_type + owner to pick templates and escalation steps).
- Affects at least 8 users in Customer Success/Support (reported by Rachel K. + Owen P.).
Who is affected
- Customer Success / Support (CS) viewers who should have read-only visibility into incident taxonomy dashboards and incident_type fields.
- Not requesting write permissions (no ability to edit incident types, owner mapping, or dashboard definitions).
Expected behavior
- CS can view (read-only):
  - Incident taxonomy dashboards (top types, owner breakdown, MTTR, SLA breach rate)
  - Incident details fields exposed via ops Console API: incident_type, subtype, resolved owner
- CS cannot edit:
  - incident_type on incidents
  - owner mapping config
  - alert routing or paging policies
Actual behavior
- CS users get denied at the dashboard folder level and at the underlying datasource query/API permission layer.
Steps to reproduce
1) Login as CS user (Okta group: "CS" / "Customer-Success")
2) Navigate to: Observability -> Dashboards -> "Incident Taxonomy" folder
3) Open "Incidents by Type / Owner (v1)" dashboard
4) Observe access denied
Initial notes / suspected cause
- Dashboard folder was created under an "ops" namespace; permissions look restricted to SRE/Eng on-call groups only.
- Even after adding dashboard viewer role, embedded Console panels still hit a 403 on incident taxonomy API endpoints (suggests dual-layer permissioning: Grafana folder + internal API scopes).
Requested outcome
- Grant CS read-only access to the incident taxonomy dashboards and the minimum required API scopes for the Console embed.
- Document the intended access model so future dashboard additions don’t repeat the issue.
References
- Slack: #support thread referencing this ticket (CS asking for access to incident taxonomy dashboards)
- Related initiatives: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping rollout
Acceptance criteria
- At least 2 CS users confirm they can open the taxonomy dashboards and view panels without 403/denied errors.
- No CS write/edit capabilities granted.
- Access model captured in a short note (Confluence or runbook) and shared with CS + SRE.

We also have a Console embed path that queries incident taxonomy endpoints; likely a separate permissions gate. Will coordinate with Allison (Obs standards) + Platform for scopes.
2026-01-21 (Allison Grant): Confirmed: folder permissions are too tight (only SRE and Eng-Oncall). For v1 we agreed CS can view incident_type/owner but not edit. Suggest adding Okta group "Customer-Success" as Viewer to the "Incident Taxonomy" folder only (not the entire ops folder). We should also ensure queries don’t expose any sensitive tenant identifiers.
2026-01-21 (Sergio Costa): Implemented Grafana folder split: moved taxonomy dashboards into a new folder "Incident Taxonomy (Read-only)" and granted Viewer access to groups: SRE, Eng-Oncall, Customer-Success. Left the rest of ops dashboards restricted. Need CS validation.
2026-01-21 (Dylan Brooks): Re: Console embed 403. The ops Console API endpoint for incident taxonomy is behind internal scope "ops:incidents.read". CS has "cs:incidents.read" only. Proposed: allow CS group to call ops endpoint but with filtered fields (no internal-only annotations). Alternatively expose a CS-safe endpoint. For speed, adding CS group to ops:incidents.read with field-level filtering seems safest.
2026-01-22 (Sergio Costa): Patched API permissions: CS can call incident taxonomy read endpoints; confirmed response excludes internal-only fields (incident commander notes, private links). payload.description:
Issue summary: Several engineers' just-in-time (JIT) ephemeral SSH key requests remain in 'Pending Manager Approval' even after their managers click approve in the approval UI. The approval records are not being picked up by the runbook/provisioner service.

Impact: Affected engineers cannot access internal bastion for runbook work and incident response. ~8 active requests discovered, broader population unknown. Business impact: interrupts oncall response for non-critical incidents and delays routine maintenance.

Observed behavior: The approval UI shows manager action completed (timestamped). Approval queue shows approval event for the request id, but runbook-provisioner does not transition the request to 'Approved' and does not issue an ephemeral key. Audit logs show the SCIM sync transforming the Okta 'manager' attribute into an email string (e.g., "alice@example.com") rather than Okta user id or canonical SCIM reference, causing the runbook-provisioner lookup to fail (it expects manager to be an Okta 'id' or SCIM reference).

Expected behavior: Approval events should link to manager principal by Okta id / SCIM id and drive the provisioning to 'Approved' and issue SSH key.
1) Submit a JIT SSH access request for a user whose Okta profile has manager set.
2) Have manager approve via approval UI.
3) Observe approval entry in audit log.
4) Check runbook-provisioner logs; provisioning does not proceed and request remains Pending.
5) Inspect SCIM payload forwarded to provisioner and note manager attribute contents.
- Approval audit entry present: approval_event{request_id: 'req-20260310-73', approver: 'alice@example.com', time: 2026-03-10T15:04:22Z}\n- Runbook-provisioner error: 'manager_lookup_failed: no user found for manager_ref: alice@example.com'\n- SCIM outbound payload (excerpt): {\"userName\": \"bob@redwood.ai\", \"manager\": \"alice@example.com\"}\n- Prior behavior (before 2026-03-09): manager field was a SCIM reference object like {\"value\": \"00u1abcd2e3F\", \"displayName\": \"Alice M\"}\n- Identity-sync service recent deploy: github.com/redwood/identity-sync/commit/4f9a2d (auto-flatten-manager-field)
- Identity team reproduced locally: SCIM adapter commit 4f9a2d introduced a transformation that flattens manager to manager.email when manager.profile is present. This was intended to simplify a previous NA-characters bug but regressed consumers that expect SCIM reference format.
- Runbook-provisioner performs a lookup by Okta user id / SCIM ref only; codepath does not accept email string as a stable foreign key.
- No existing fallback mapping: when manager is email we attempt an email->Okta lookup via Identity API which has higher latency and rate limits; in most failing cases the lookup returned 404 due to query normalization differences (dot vs plus addressing).
- Affected requests appear clustered for employees whose Okta manager attribute was modified in the last 7 days (bulk org import on 2026-03-08).
- Cross-reference: related incident INT-314271 (identity namespace collision) was unrelated but shows prior bulk import risk patterns.
1) Manual approval by Platform Oncall: Support engineers can manually set request state to 'Approved' in the provisioning DB (runbook-provisioner admin UI) for emergency access until fix deployed.
2) Identity team rolled back the SCIM adapter transform on staging and pushed a canary to a small subset of customers to verify behavior.
Note: manual DB state change is logged and requires follow-up audit entry.
Partial: Rolled back identity-sync change that flattened manager to email in staging; applied hotfix (revert commit 4f9a2d) to identity-sync in prod on 2026-03-12 02:10Z. After rollback, runbook-provisioner consumed SCIM reference objects and resumed provisioning for new approvals. For stuck requests where approval event used email form, runbook-provisioner now accepts a one-time fallback email lookup (added small patch) and advanced 6 of 8 pending requests to Approved. Remaining 2 required manual DB approvals due to plus-addressing mismatch.
Follow-up: identity team will add a contract test to prevent manager attribute shape regressions and add a migration script to normalize manager fields for pending requests.
- Identity: add SCIM contract test (PR planned) and schedule a data normalization job for manager attributes (owner: Marco Rivera, ETA 2026-03-18).
- Provisioner: add robust email fallback path with rate-limit backoff and deterministic normalization (owner: Priya Shah, ETA 2026-03-17).
- Support: run audit on all JIT requests created between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-12 to identify any remaining stuck items (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA 2026-03-14).
2026-03-10 16:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer reported 'Waiting on manager' but manager confirmed approval. Collected approval audit logs and SCIM payloads; attaching to ticket.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:42 - Support (Aisha Patel): Confirmed 6/8 stuck requests moved to Approved after fallback patch. Two remaining require manual intervention due to email aliasing. Documented manual DB approval steps in ticket.
2026-03-13 11:03 - Security (Lena Kim): Requested audit artifact for manual DB approvals. Support attached changelog and approver screenshots. SRE to preserve for compliance.
payload.summary: JIT ephemeral SSH key request stuck in 'Pending Manager Approval' after Okta SCIM 'manager' attribute returned as email string

payload.description:
Issue summary: We need an automated 'identity translation' pipeline that converts external/partner Okta guest groups into least-privilege artifacts across Jira, Confluence, and Slack.

Impact: Right now onboarding external guests requires manual mapping by Platform SRE and Workspace Admins which is slow (1-3 business days), error-prone, and causes over-permissioning (users sometimes get broader Jira or Confluence roles than needed). This is increasing support load and audit findings for temporary partner access.

Request: Build an automated system (service + automation jobs + approval gate) that: (1) consumes Okta guest group events, (2) maps each group to configured targets: Jira project role(s), Confluence space permission sets (page-level viewer where applicable), and a dedicated Slack guest channel membership, (3) enforces TTL on granted access with automated revocation, and (4) emits auditable events to our logging and compliance pipelines.

Requirements:
- Support one-to-many mappings (one Okta group -> multiple Jira project roles and Confluence spaces).
- Allow per-mapping approval gates exposed in Slack or Confluence (for example: a request appears in #guest-requests with Approve/Deny buttons that trigger the pipeline).
- Enforce TTL (default 7 days, configurable per mapping) and automated revocation.
- Record every grant/revoke event into CloudTrail-equivalent logs and Confluence audit page for quarterly review.
- Safe rollback: if mapping fails mid-operation, system must revert partial changes (remove created Jira role membership and Slack invites).
- Least-privilege defaults: mappings must default to viewer/commenter where possible; no admin-level roles from guests.
- RBAC for who can create mappings: only members of identity-admins group in Okta and Platform SRE role in Jira.

Acceptance criteria:
- Demo: Onboard an Okta test guest group and show automated creation of Jira role assignments + Confluence view-only access + Slack guest channel invite, all approved via Slack, with a TTL that auto-revokes after the window.
- Audit: All events visible in centralized logs and Confluence audit page with user, mapping id, timestamps.
- Tests: Unit and integration tests for mapping logic + a canary run in staging.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Slack invite API rate limits. Mitigation: queue invites and include exponential backoff and alerting.
- Risk: Partial failure across systems. Mitigation: implement two-phase commit style orchestration with compensating actions.

Timeline: 3 sprints (design + infra + rollout) with early staging prototype in sprint 2.

Mapping configuration should be stored as YAML in a git-backed repository (infra/guest-mappings) with a schema: mapping_id, okta_group_id, jira_project_keys, jira_roles, confluence_spaces, confluence_permission_level, slack_channel_template, ttl_days, approval_required, approvers_okta_group. The pipeline reads changes via PR merge and also accepts ephemeral request flows from Slack that create temp mappings with auto-generated mapping_id.
Every grant/revoke must emit JSON records to the security logging pipeline with fields: mapping_id, okta_group, targets (jira/confluence/slack), actor (system or approver), request_id, timestamp, ttl_expiry, outcome. Retain logs 540 days for partners. Export a summary row to Confluence audit page for quarterly compliance review.
Reviewed current manual checklist located in Confluence: steps include manual Okta group lookup, creating corresponding Jira role membership, adding Confluence space viewer, and inviting to Slack channel. The total average time is ~26 hours including approvals.
Checked existing automation patterns: INT-35677 contains partial channel provisioning logic; could be extracted. INT-71234 has RBAC templates for mappings; reuse suggested.
Slack API capabilities: guest invites are supported via SCIM for Enterprise Grid; we need to confirm whether our workspace permits programmatic guest channel invites or requires admin console flows.
Jira API: project role assignments require the projectAdmin or admin scope; using a service account with delegated rights is necessary. Must rotate service token quarterly.
Confluence: space-level permissions can be set via REST API; for page-level viewer, we may need to create a viewer group per mapping which increases group cardinality. Consider using space-level 'view' and restricting pages manually if needed.
1) Get security approval on TTL and approver rules (Maya). 2) Confirm Slack guest invite automation feasibility with Workspace Admins (Sergio). 3) Provision service account with minimal scopes (Jordan). 4) Prototype staging run with one internal test partner group and run canary. 5) Prepare audit export and Confluence audit page template.
Pending - initial prototype PR created. Awaiting Security sign-off and workspace admin confirmation for Slack SCIM invites. No production changes performed yet.
payload.summary: Automate translation of Okta guest groups into scoped Jira roles, Confluence viewer sets, and Slack guest channels

comments: 2026-03-10T09:14:00Z Maya Chen: Ticket created after customer outage alert. They noticed several serving nodes in their private pool never completed startup due to repeated artifact fetch failures.
payload.description:
Issue summary: On Acme Health's Private deployment (VPC + VPCE) some on-prem serving nodes intermittently fail to pull model shards and presigned S3 artifacts. Failure mode is DNS resolution returning NXDOMAIN for hostnames that should be resolvable via the customer's split-horizon DNS (search-suffix based discovery).

Impact: Several serving nodes fail to initialize, causing reduced capacity for customers' private pool. Affects model start-up and shard fetches; customer reports ~8% request retries and visible latency spikes on rolling restarts.

Environment: Private deployment behind VPCE in us-east-1. Customer uses internal DNS forwarder that advertises a search list (e.g., svc.acme.internal). Nodes run systemd-resolved with default search behavior. Control plane and artifact fetches traverse VPCE egress through a corporate DNS forwarder/proxy.

Steps to reproduce:
1) On a serving node in the customer's private deployment, run: dig +short model-artifact.s3-presigned
2) Compare resolution with and without the configured search suffix (e.g., model-artifact.s3-presigned.svc.acme.internal).
3) Trigger a model pull via control-plane (redeploy) and observe fetch failures in serving-node logs.

Observed logs/snippets:
- serving-node: "artifact fetch failed: lookup model-artifact.s3-presigned: no such host"
- systemd-resolved: "search domain discarded: total name length > limit" (intermittent)
- tcpdump on node: client sends DNS query for name with search suffix; response is NXDOMAIN when query goes to the customer's forwarder via UDP; when we force TCP query to the same forwarder, server returns the correct A record.

Initial hypothesis: The customer's DNS forwarder (or an intermediary DNS proxy) appears to be truncating or returning NXDOMAIN for long FQDNs produced by the node's search-suffix expansion. UDP responses are truncated/incorrect and TCP fallback is required, but TCP DNS (port 53) is intermittently blocked by the corporate egress appliance leading to resolution failures. systemd-resolved's local search list can produce expanded names longer than 63 octets which some forwarders mishandle, producing NXDOMAIN instead of forwarding correctly.

Notes: This is not an S3 signature or presigned URL validity problem; requests reach S3 when DNS is resolved. The problem is deterministic when search-suffix expansion is used and intermittent when clients resolve strictly-qualified hostnames.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:02 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Asked customer for tcpdump and systemd-resolved logs; requested output of 'resolvectl status' and 'cat /etc/resolv.conf' on an affected node.
2026-03-10 11:30 - Customer (Acme Health - S. Patel): Uploaded packet captures and noted that their corporate egress appliance filters TCP/53 intermittently during business hours; UDP is allowed but upstream forwarder occasionally truncates EDNS0 responses.
2026-03-11 08:45 - SRE (R. Alvarez): Reproduced NXDOMAIN when adding long search-suffix in lab using the customer's forwarder config. Observed correct RRs over TCP. Blocked TCP/53 by the egress appliance reproduces the failure pattern.
2026-03-12 16:05 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Suggested and validated a short-term workaround with customer: set REDWOOD_ARTIFACT_HOST_OVERRIDE to fully-qualified S3 hostnames (avoids search expansion), and added a VPCE private DNS entry for the presigned host in customer's Resolver endpoints.
2026-03-12 18:20 - Customer (S. Patel): Confirmed that nodes recovered after applying host override; rolling restart now shows successful shard downloads. Customer will contact network/security team to allow DNS over TCP to their forwarder or increase UDP EDNS0 buffer support.
Checked serving-node agent logs (artifact_fetcher). Error consistently 'no such host' concurrent with NXDOMAIN from forwarder over UDP.
Replayed queries from lab replicating customer's resolver chain: UDP path returned TC flag or NXDOMAIN for names > ~140 chars; TCP returned successful answers.
Validated systemd-resolved search expansion can generate FQDNs that exceed 63-character label limits, but total length within 255. Forwarder incorrectly treats long labels as invalid and responds NXDOMAIN instead of REFERRAL/TCP fallback.
Packet captures show corporate egress appliance sometimes drops TCP 53 sessions; pattern correlates with business-hour maintenance windows reported by customer firewall team.
Control-plane logs show repeated retry attempts; we had not previously forced fully-qualified hostnames for artifact resolution in private deployments — relying on client resolver behavior has this risk.
SRE reproduced issue in isolated lab by blocking TCP/53 and using a forwarder that returns truncated EDNS0 responses.
Workaround applied (short-term): Instructed customer to set REDWOOD_ARTIFACT_HOST_OVERRIDE on affected nodes to the canonical presigned S3 host (fully-qualified), bypassing search-suffix expansion. Confirmed artifact pulls succeed after change.
Workaround (alternative): Added alias/host entry in customer's VPCE private DNS zone pointing presigned host -> S3 endpoint; validated model shard downloads.
Engineering mitigation (internal): Opened INT-99827 to add stronger client-side fallback: always attempt resolution of the fully-qualified host (append trailing dot) for artifact fetches before relying on search-suffix expansion. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/2147 created and linked.
Customer action required: Allow DNS over TCP (port 53) to the internal forwarder or upgrade forwarder to honour EDNS0 and avoid truncation for legitimate long queries. Recommended security change request to allow TCP/53 in egress policy for resolver IPs.
Follow-up: Add automated detection to serving-node startup to log and surface 'search-suffix expansion NXDOMAIN' pattern and provide recommended fix hints in Console. Filed INT-99890 for the Console UX change.
Status: Customer confirmed recovery after workaround. Marking as In Progress until client-side fallback PR is merged and customer implements a permanent DNS fix.
payload.summary: DNS search-suffix truncation prevents artifact resolution for on-prem serving nodes

Issue summary: HR and IT have inconsistent procedures for granting short-lived network and GPU lab access to contractors and new hires. This ticket requests a standardized onboarding lifecycle artifact and an implementation plan for a short-lived SSO role ("onboard-temp") with automated deprovisioning, temporary VPN profiles, and a GPU-lab booking + entitlement workflow.

Impact: Delays in ramping new contributors; elevated risk from manually granted long-lived entitlements; several teams currently use ad-hoc processes leading to inconsistent audit trails and rework for Security/HR during monthly reviews.

Environment: Org-wide; SSO: Okta SAML; VPN: Palo Alto GlobalProtect; Workstation fleet: Jamf (macOS) / Intune (Windows); GPU lab: private rack with Kerberos-backed reservation system.

Steps to reproduce the pain points (observed):
1) Contractor request submitted to People Ops with Slack approval thread.
2) IT engineer manually creates Okta group, issues GlobalProtect profile, and manually records expiry in a spreadsheet.
3) GPU lab access granted by emailed note to lab-admins; access often extended manually with no ticket.
4) At offboarding, some entitlements linger because spreadsheet entries were not updated.

Requested outcomes / Acceptance criteria:
- A documented onboarding checklist (Confluence) that becomes the single source of truth for short-lived access flows.
- An Okta role (onboard-temp) mapped via SSO rules that grants a time-bound session and membership TTL of 30 days.
- Automated ticket generation in ITSM when a role is issued and a deprovision reminder 7 days before expiry.
- VPN profiles issued with per-user certs and TTL aligned to SSO role lifetime.
- GPU lab booking workflow integrated with access provisioning (temporary Kerberos principal or group) and automatic revocation at TTL.
- Audit logs surfaced to Security for monthly review; retention policy noted.

Proposed rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Draft Confluence checklist and approval matrix; small pilot with one hiring team.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement Okta role + TTL automation using existing SCIM hooks; update ITSM automation.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): Integrate GPU lab reservation system with provisioning hooks; run end-to-end pilot.
- Phase 4: Expand org-wide with training and publish runbook.

Approvals required: People Ops, Security (IAM), and SRE for VPN changes.

Estimated effort: 3-4 SRE weeks + 1 Security engineer + 0.5 People Ops coordinator.

Additional notes:
Checked historical churn: cross-referenced INT-11856 for sudo/time-limited GPU laptop workflows and INT-7810 for staggered offboarding; both show manual steps that created drift. Reviewed audit logs for last 90 days: found 12 entries where VPN certs remained active 10+ days after exit. Ticket includes sample log snippets and references to 'labscheduler-pr-42' and 'okta-onboard-ttl' branch in GitHub.
Phase gates listed in description. Immediate next steps: (1) Create Confluence draft and circulate to People Ops and Security by 2026-03-16. (2) Provision a test Okta role in the sandbox tenant and verify SCIM TTL enforcement by 2026-03-20. (3) Open a PR to GPU lab scheduler for webhook-driven provisioning (samir will own). Final signoff required from Security before org-wide rollout.
Create Confluence checklist (owner: Aisha)
Okta sandbox role + SCIM tests (owner: Jamal)
GPU lab webhook PR (owner: Samir)
Update ITSM ticket schema to include entitlement-type (owner: ITSM admin)

Issue summary: Scheduled diagnostics and live debugging from the SRE toolkit fail when attempting to impersonate the GCP ops-service-account and then assume the linked AWS cross-account role. The failure appears to be caused by an IAM Condition on the GCP side that blocks token exchange when a specific session tag is present.

Impact: SRE runbook executions that require cross-cloud debugging are blocked for multiple platform teams. This prevents live investigation of high-latency incidents in Dedicated clusters and delays incident response. Affects internal tooling and some on-call escalations.

Environment: prod | us-east (GCP), prod | us-east-1 (AWS). Affected clusters: redwood-dedicated-prod-us-east-01 and redwood-debug-proxy-prod.
1) From an SRE workstation with normal SSO session, run the ops-tooling script that calls gcloud iam service-accounts impersonate for projects/infra/ops-service-account
2) Attempt to exchange the impersonated credentials to assume-role in the AWS debug account via our broker (sts:AssumeRole with external ID)
3) Observe failure immediately with a 403 on the token-exchange and a subsequent AssumeRoleDenied error in the AWS broker logs.
GCP IAM debug: 'Token exchange denied: condition request.auth.claims.session_tag != "ops-debug"'
Broker log (aws-broker-prod): AssumeRoleDenied - sts:AssumeRole - role arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/redwood-debug-role - reason: invalid token
Ops-tooling stdout: 'Impersonation succeeded locally; token exchange failed: 403 Forbidden'.
Initial hypothesis: recent org-level IAM Condition introduced to restrict service-account impersonation when a session tag is present. Verified via gcloud iam policies that a conditional binding exists on infra/ops-service-account restricting iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken when request.auth.claims.session_tag == "ops-debug".
Checked SSO token payloads and found session_tag populated by the new session middleware we rolled out last week (INT-472999 referenced).
Reproduced with a synthetic service account token: tokens without session_tag exchange successfully; tokens with session_tag are rejected.
AWS side: broker expects a standard OAuth token; it rejects tokens that have non-standard claims. The broker logs show token validation failed rather than role trust policy rejecting the role; suggests upstream token was invalid when presented to STS proxy.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 15:45 - Security (Anika Bose): Approved emergency scoped workaround for 4 hours for SRE group only. Logged with change control CHG-2026-0313.
1) Implement IAM Condition whitelist for projects/infra/ops-service-account limited to serviceAccount:roles/sre-debug and audit binding (Security to approve).
2) Add integration test in auth-broker suite that validates token exchange with session_tag present.
3) Patch broker to log token origin and provide clearer error codes for token validation failures.
4) Schedule follow-up change window and notify oncall.
Owners: Marco (Auth Eng) for condition change, Priya (SRE) for broker tests and ops-tooling patch.

Issue summary: An internal ephemeral access bridge used by SRE to assume AWS diagnostic roles from GCP CI runners is failing with AccessDenied errors after the org moved to tag-enforcement for resource tagging. Impact: SRE cannot perform cross-cloud live debug of customer Dedicated clusters or run ephemeral cost-inspection jobs. Root cause appears to be a combination of an AWS Organizations SCP that denies AssumeRole when required tag keys are missing and a GCP IAM Condition on the service account that injects a tag attribute which does not match the AWS expectation.

This ticket tracks investigation and mitigation steps for restoring safe, auditable cross-cloud assume-role flows for ephemeral diagnostics.
SRE debugging and some automated maintenance jobs that rely on cross-cloud assume-role (GCP -> AWS) are blocked. Potential delayed incident response for dedicated customer clusters in us-west-2. No external customer-facing API errors observed yet, but operational risk elevated.
1) From a GCP CI runner with the diagnostic service account: gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=$KEY
2) Generate STS token and call AWS STS: aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ephemeral-diagnostic --role-session-name test --duration-seconds 900
3) Observe: An AccessDenied with message 'Caller does not have required tags' or 'Condition check failed'.
Command output and STS request/response captured in logs below.
[2026-03-10T09:12:03Z] AWS STS AssumeRole failed: AccessDenied: Request explicitly denied by policy.\n\tStatus Code: 403, Request ID: 0a1b2c3d4e\n[2026-03-10T09:12:03Z] aws-sdk-js: assumeRole error {\n  code: 'AccessDenied',\n  message: 'Caller does not have required tag: redwood:team',\n}\n[2026-03-10T09:12:04Z] GCP audit: iam.serviceAccounts.signJwt invoked by service-account@ci-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com\n[2026-03-10T09:12:04Z] Bridge logs: outbound STS request included tags: {"redwood:env":"ci"}, missing key redwood:team
03-10 09:20 — Confirmed failure reproduces from staging runner and prod runner using identical flow.
03-10 10:05 — Pulled AWS Organizations SCPs: new tag enforcement SCP added 2026-03-08 requiring redwood:team and redwood:owner on cross-account assume-role. SCP denies AssumeRole when tags absent or mismatched.
03-10 11:00 — Reviewed GCP-to-AWS bridge code: bridge populates tags based on GCP service account attributes. Current mapping only sets redwood:env and redwood:job-id, not redwood:team.
03-10 14:15 — Hypothesis: Org policy enforcement on AWS is stricter than the bridge mapping; missing tag causes deny. Also found a GCP IAM Condition on the diagnostic service account that explicitly allows impersonation only when attribute 'team' == 'infra', but that attribute is not propagated into AWS tags.
03-11 09:40 — Tested local patch to include static redwood:team tag in bridge token; temporary test succeeded (AssumeRole returned credentials).
03-11 13:05 — Need coordination: changing bridge to include tags requires security review and update to logging to ensure tag provenance is auditable.

2026-03-10 — Incident created by Aisha after on-call observed failed diagnostic run in #sre-support.
2026-03-10 10:30 — Notified Cloud Infra; triage meeting scheduled at 11:00.
2026-03-10 14:30 — Reproduced failure; confirmed SCP addition on 2026-03-08 as likely trigger.
2026-03-11 09:00 — Implemented temporary patch on a staging bridge instance to inject redwood:team for testing.
2026-03-11 11:00 — Patch validated; security requested design doc for permanent change.
2026-03-12 08:45 — This ticket updated with proposed remediation options and owners.

Mitigation applied: temporary bridge patch in staging to include required tags while security reviews permanent approach. Long term options: (A) enhance bridge mapping to derive 'redwood:team' from GCP service account attribute and add audit logging; (B) introduce intermediary tag-assertion Lambda in AWS with strict provenance checks; (C) update org SCP to allow specific service account ARNs to assume without tags for a transition window. Next step: decision required from Cloud Security + Infra.

payload.description:
Issue summary: A request to provision an ephemeral service account (ml-debug-sa) used by SRE/ML for live debugging is failing. The provisioning workflow touches both GCP (creating SA in customer-linked project) and AWS (creating a mapped cross-account role and tagging it for lifecycle).

Impact: Blocked access for SRE/ML engineers trying to reproduce a high-latency serving regression in staging. Affects scheduled incident debug windows and delays triage of related incidents. Two engineers reported inability to create the SA and obtain temporary credentials.

Environment: The request runs through the internal provisioning pipeline (service: access-broker) which orchestrates GCP SA creation under folder F-ML-ENG (staging project) and then triggers AWS role mapping in the analytics AWS account. Fail occurs in staging us-west1; similar guardrails exist in prod us-east1.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Submit ephemeral access request via /internal/access-broker with template ml-debug and ttl=4h.
2) Broker calls GCP IAM API: projects.serviceAccounts.create under folder F-ML-ENG.
3) After SA creation, broker tags metadata and calls AWS provisioning lambda to create cross-account role and attach trust policy.
4) End user attempts to assume role via sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.

Observed behavior:
- GCP API returns PERMISSION_DENIED: "Request contains a deny policy that prevents service account creation at this folder level".
- AWS provisioning step fails later with validation error: "Missing required tags: request-id, owner; SCP prevention of untagged role creation".
- Because GCP step fails early, the broker doesn't reach a consistent rollback path; orphan entries observed in internal request DB.

Expected behavior: Ephemeral SA and corresponding AWS role should be created atomically (or broker should cleanly rollback) when caller is allowed via temporary JIT exception path. Clear error surfaced to requestor with remediation steps.

Investigation notes:
- Checked folder-level policy on folder F-ML-ENG: an explicit GCP deny exists (deny: iam.serviceAccounts.create) applied by security to prevent arbitrary SA creation in sensitive folders. This deny was introduced 2026-02-20 to close a gap identified in audit.
- Provisioning broker normally obtains a short-lived elevated token via the JIT broker role and is added to an allowlist. The allowlist entry for service access-broker was missing the new deny-exception tag attribute.
- AWS side: org-level SCPs now enforce presence of lifecycle tags on new roles. The broker did not attach the required tags because tagging is performed after GCP SA creation; this creates a sequencing dependency.
- Logs: access-broker logs (link: https://logs.redwood.internal/access-broker/2026-03-10/INT-118276) attached show GCP error first, then AWS validation attempt in subsequent retries.
- Repro with a manual elevated token (impersonation by oncall) allowed role creation in AWS but not GCP because deny is enforced at folder-level and has higher precedence than allow rules.

Potential remediations considered:
- Short term workaround: Security to add a timebound exception to the folder deny for service account creation for calls coming from the provisioning broker service identity (serviceAccount:access-broker@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com) for the debug window. This requires a ticket to Security with justification.
- Medium term: Change broker sequencing to perform AWS role metadata/tags creation first (or create a placeholder tagged role) and then create GCP SA, with robust rollback if either step fails. Also add pre-flight policy checks so failures fail fast with clear user-facing reason.
- Long term: Update folder deny policy to include an allowlist mechanism keyed by service identity and signed request token, and update the broker to request and surface policy exemptions automatically when operator-approved.

Next steps (owner: Diego Morales):
- Reach out to Security to request a scoped, timebound exception for the oncall timeframe and include audit justification (ETA: 2026-03-12 14:00 PDT).
- Implement a broker pre-flight check to detect folder deny using Policy Troubleshooter API and return actionable error messages (ETA PR by 2026-03-18).
- Add tagging step earlier in AWS pipeline and unit/integration tests to validate atomicity (ETA PR by 2026-03-22).
Temporary workaround executed 2026-03-11: Security granted a 2-hour folder-level exception scoped to access-broker service identity for staging folder F-ML-ENG. SREs performed manual provisioning during the window. Action: request follow-up to make exception auditable and recorded in Confluence.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:43 - Security (Priya Singh): We put that deny in place 2026-02-20 after audit. We can issue a scoped timebound exception for access-broker if you provide exact service identity and justification. Request submitted via SEC-EXC-192.
2026-03-12 17:02 - Product (Maya Chen): Please ensure the user-visible error message is clear so that customers/internal users know when deny policy is the cause and how to request access.
Workaround: timebound folder exception granted and manual provisioning performed. Permanent remediation planned: broker pre-flight policy check and reordering of AWS tagging to ensure atomic provisioning and clear user errors.
OPEN-TASK-118277: broker pre-flight policy-check implementation
OPEN-TASK-118278: move aws-role-tagging before role activation and add rollback logic
OPEN-TASK-118279: update runbook and error messages for access-broker failures
payload.summary: Ephemeral ML debug service-account creation blocked by combined GCP folder deny + AWS SCP tag enforcement

payload.description:
Issue summary: An internal debugging utility (impersonation-proxy) that performs a two-step cross-cloud impersonation (assume AWS role -> exchange STS creds for GCP workload-identity access) is failing with authorization errors when running from staging and intermittently in prod. Impact: Engineers cannot access cross-cloud logs and diagnostics; some automated oncall playbooks that require audit reads are blocked. Environment: staging us-west and prod us-east. Error snippets:
- AWS side: 'AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole' returned intermittently for the ops-broker role.
- GCP side: 'Permission denied: iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy' and 'Request had insufficient authentication scopes' when the proxy attempts to impersonate target SA.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Run impersonation-proxy from a workspace with the ops-aws-bridge role in account: redwood-infra-ops-prod.
2) Proxy attempts sts:AssumeRole to arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ops-broker-role.
3) On success, it exchanges temporary AWS creds with our sts-exchange lambda to mint a short-lived GCP access token via workload identity pool.
4) The final step attempts gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy for target-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com and fails.

Observed behavior:
- Failure rate ~20% in prod, 100% in staging after maintenance window on 2026-03-09.
- Logs show both AWS AssumeRole errors and GCP IAM access errors; failures are correlated with recent org policy change and an automated permission-boundary rollout to some service accounts.

Initial hypothesis:
- A recently deployed permission boundary on ops-broker-role (AWS) blocks sts:TagSession or conditions used by the proxy causing intermittent AssumeRole failures.
- GCP failures stem from missing iam.serviceAccounts.actAs binding for the impersonation principal produced by the workload identity pool exchange, possibly because the GCP IAM binding was applied to a specific principal format that changed after the exchange implementation update.

Investigation notes:
- Checked Terraform diffs for the week of 2026-03-08: found PR #repo/infra/terraform/changesets/1248 that added a permission boundary to 'ops-broker-role' and tightened org-policy on 'iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains' for staging.
- CloudTrail (aws-us-east-1) shows AssumeRole API returning AccessDenied with condition 'PermissionBoundaryEvaluationFailed' for three distinct sessions.
- GCP audit logs (projects/redwood-prod) show 'permission_denied' for service account getIamPolicy when principal is 'principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/12345/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/wip-prod/providers/p-ops#c9a8f2e2', suggesting the exchange step changed the principal format from 'serviceAccount:...'.
- Correlation: proxies that use the old exchange lambda version (v2.1) succeed; proxies that pick up the newer lambda (v3.0) produce the new principal format and fail because no IAM binding exists for that principal.

Temporary workaround:
- Roll back the sts-exchange lambda to v2.1 in staging to restore previous principal format (applied as hotfix on 2026-03-10).
- For AWS errors, granted a narrowly scoped sts:AssumeRole policy exception to the ops-broker-role for sessions originating from the proxy identity (timebound, expires 2026-03-17).

Resolution plan (in progress):
- Short term: Update IAM bindings in GCP to accept both principal formats used by v2.1 and v3.0 of the exchange lambda; coordinate with security to whitelist workload identity pool principals for the impersonation proxy.
- Mid term: Reconcile permission boundary policies in AWS to allow sts:AssumeRole with the required session tags and documented conditions for the proxy. Submit a follow-up Terraform PR that includes explicit allow statements for the proxy session tags and documents the rationale.
- Long term: Add an integration test that exercises the full assume-role -> workload-identity exchange workflow during CI to prevent format regressions.

Follow-ups assigned:
- Marco Ruiz: Create Terraform PR to add dual-format IAM bindings in GCP and run canary in staging (due 2026-03-15).

Additional notes:
- SRE runbook update: Add a diagnostic section for PermissionBoundaryEvaluationFailed and workload-identity principal mismatches.
Partial: Hotfix rollback of exchange lambda (v2.1) in staging restored functionality. Narrow AWS sts:AssumeRole exception granted and dual-format GCP IAM binding PR opened. Awaiting security sign-off and a staged canary in prod. Full resolution pending policy reconciliation and CI integration test.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Provisioning helper script (setup_local_policies.sh) exits with non-zero when system locale uses legacy Unicode collation normalization (NFKD) or certain non-default LC_CTYPE/LC_COLLATE values. This stops the imaging task sequence mid-run and prevents Intune check-in/enrollment on a subset of repaired devices.

Impact:
- ~8 machines in the last two depot batches failed imaging and never completed Intune enrollment; users received a partially provisioned workstation (local accounts only, no corp certs).
- Blocks fast-redeploy for depot repair queue; increases turnaround time.

Environment:
- Affected devices repros on prod imaging pool in us-east.
- OS: Windows 11 22H2 corporate image (with latest platform patches as of 2026-03-01)
- Provisioning artifact: provisioning-scripts v2026.02.28 (bash + PowerShell wrapper)
- Managed via SCCM task sequence that runs setup_local_policies.sh late in the image.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot a test device (Dell Latitude 7440) into SCCM task sequence in the us-east imaging pool.
2) Set system locale environment to one of the affected collations (example repro used: LC_COLLATE="fi_FI@collation=NFKD" exported in cmd before running the script).
3) Allow task sequence to reach the provisioning-scripts step.
4) Observe that setup_local_policies.sh aborts with an encoding/collation exception and the task sequence halts.

Observed logs (excerpt):
- C:\Windows\Temp\provisioning\setup_local_policies.log:
  [2026-03-09 14:07:02] INFO: starting local policy setup
  [2026-03-09 14:07:03] ERROR: fatal: string normalization failed when writing registry key: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SOFTWARE\\Redwood\\Provision"
  [2026-03-09 14:07:03] ERROR: exit code 1
- SCCM smsts.log shows task sequence step 'Run Command Line' returning 1 and aborting sequence.

Hypothesis and root cause (initial):
- The helper script uses Python 3.9 subprocess invocation and writes UTF-8 strings to the Windows registry using a small C# helper compiled during the build. Under certain LC_COLLATE/LC_CTYPE values the runtime performs Unicode normalization (NFKD) on strings and strips combining characters; combined with our registry write helper's unsupported normalization mode this results in an exception thrown by the helper (System.ArgumentException: Invalid character in registry value).
- This only triggers when a depot-repair process re-applies device-specific locale settings prior to provisioning (we see this on repaired devices that retain OEM locale overrides).

Temporary workaround applied:
- Imaging team added a wrapper to forcibly set LANG and LC_COLLATE to en_US.UTF-8 before running the provisioning step in the task sequence. This is in place for the current depot batch and prevents the failure.

Next steps / planned fix:
- Engineering (Provisioning) to update provisioning-scripts to sanitize locale inputs and coerce strings to NFC normalization before passing to the registry helper. Also update the C# registry writer to accept NormalizationForm variants. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning-scripts/pull/412
- Imaging ops to roll the temporary LANG/LC_COLLATE wrapper into the standard task sequence until the patch is deployed.
- Confirm fleet-wide by running a small canary set of 20 repaired devices with the patch and removing wrapper after two successful batches.

Owner: Miguel Torres (Provisioning lead)
Estimated ETA for PR review & QA: 2026-03-16
Boot a device into SCCM task sequence in us-east imaging pool
Set system locale to a legacy collation variant (example: LC_COLLATE=\"fi_FI@collation=NFKD\") before provisioning step
Allow sequence to reach provisioning-scripts and observe failure
- 2026-03-10 09:20: initial report from depot engineer (see comment below).
- 2026-03-10 10:05: duplicated on Lenovo test device.
- Reproduced reliably by setting LC_COLLATE in PowerShell and running the provisioning script under an elevated cmd shell.
- Confirmed exception originates from Registry write helper when passed composed characters.
- Confirmed wrapper fix prevents failures for current imaging batches.

Additional notes:
Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning-scripts/pull/412
Set LANG and LC_COLLATE to en_US.UTF-8 (or remove OEM locale overrides) in SCCM task sequence before invoking provisioning scripts. Imaging Ops to keep wrapper until patch deployed.
Update provisioning-scripts to normalize strings to NFC before registry writes and harden the C# registry helper to accept multiple normalization forms. Add unit tests for legacy collation inputs. Roll patch through canary imaging pool and remove LANG wrapper after verification.
payload.summary: Provisioning script fails on systems with legacy locale collation (NFKD) causing device-enroll and imaging stall

Issue summary:
Customer (NeuroMed, enterprise) reports a spike in perceived inference timeouts starting 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC. Symptoms look like long tail responses or client-side timeouts, but request traces show repeated 429 responses from the API. The NeuroMed SDK is configured with high concurrency and an aggressive retry loop which appears to amplify quota-enforced 429 throttles into a client-visible outage.

Impact:
- Production traffic for NeuroMed's clinical notes summarization endpoint experienced degraded throughput and many user-facing failures for ~3 hours.
- Estimated 18k requests affected, intermittent errors caused background tasks to queue up and retry, increasing latency for other endpoints.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod) - us-east region
- Customer using Redwood JS SDK v1.8.2 with default retry strategy overridden to high concurrency (maxConcurrency=50) and short initial retry delay (50ms).
- Customer pinned to model redwood-alpha-3b; fallbacks to open-llama-7b configured.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by NeuroMed / reproduced internally):
1) Customer signature code: fire large batch of concurrent requests (50 concurrent generators) against /v1/generate for 10 minutes.
2) SDK receives 429s from API gateway and immediately retries with exponential backoff starting at 50ms and jitter disabled.
3) Retried requests re-enter the gateway and are counted against the same quota bucket, producing more 429s.
4) Observed: request latencies climb, many client-side timeouts after retries, and streaming connections drop.

Observed behavior:
- Short bursts of 429s at the edge, followed by a retry storm from the SDK producing an amplification loop.
- Traces show repeated 429s for the same original client request id and high retry counts per request.
- On the console, token-level cost looks normal, but per-route throughput drops because retries are queued.

Expected behavior:
- SDK should back off when 429 signals are returned and avoid immediate retriggering that counts toward quota.
- Platform should provide a clearer quota signal to SDKs so retries are coordinated (e.g., Retry-After, or a soft-throttle hint).

Logs / snippets:
- Example gateway log: "2026-03-09T18:07:12Z | req=abc123 | upstream=quota-service | status=429 | reason=quota_exceeded | remaining=0"
- SDK client log (NeuroMed): "sendRequest(id=xyz) -> 429; retrying after 50ms (attempt 1)" repeated 6x.
- Trace link (internal): https://internal.redwood.com/traces/2026-03-09/neuro/abc123

Temporary workaround requested by customer:
- Lower concurrency to 8 and enable exponential backoff with base 500ms and jitter. Customer reports immediate improvement when reduced.

Notes on customer impact and urgency:
- Customer is enterprise and running nightly jobs that missed processing windows; requires mitigation and guidance ASAP.

Configure Redwood JS SDK v1.8.2 with maxConcurrency=50 and retryDelayBase=50ms
Send sustained concurrent load (50 parallel requests) to /v1/generate for 10 minutes
Observe repeated 429 responses and client retries inflating request counts
03/10 - Initial triage: Support reproduced amplification locally using customer's SDK settings. Observed identical retry counts and 429 loops.
03/11 - Eng (serving-runtime) reviewed gateway logs; quota-service returns hard 429 with remaining=0 but no Retry-After header in existing implementation for this quota type.
03/11 - Hypothesis: Short retry base and disabled jitter -> retry amplification. SDK should honor 429 and backoff more aggressively or respect Retry-After header.
03/12 - Confirmed: reducing concurrency and increasing base backoff eliminates client-visible timeouts; service-side metrics show lower request churn to quota bucket.
2026-03-10 | Maya Chen (Support): Opened ticket with NeuroMed after they reported production failures. Attached logs and initial reproduction steps.
2026-03-11 | Rafael Ortega (SRE): Reproduced locally; filing follow-up with serving-runtime team to add Retry-After hints for quota responses.
2026-03-11 | Priya Nair (Serving Runtime): Noted that quota-service currently does not emit Retry-After for burst-soft-quota; will evaluate safe delay to recommend to SDKs.
2026-03-12 | NeuroMed (customer): Confirmed temporary workaround reduced failures; requests recommendation for SDK update and platform-side mitigation.
2026-03-13 | Rafael Ortega (SRE): Proposed short-term config change: emit Retry-After (ms) in quota 429s and add server-side token bucket smoothing for enterprise customers. Linked PR created.
SRE: Add Retry-After header for quota 429 responses for prod us-east (target: 03/15) - Rafael
SDK: Publish advisory and patch to default retry strategy (increase base delay, enable jitter) and release v1.8.3 - SDK team
Support: Send mitigation guide to NeuroMed with recommended SDK config and follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-14 - Maya
Eng: Evaluate smoothing algorithm to prevent immediate re-counting of retries against quota buckets (postmortem follow-up)
In progress. Short-term mitigation: customer applied reduced concurrency + longer backoff and saw improvement. SRE will emit Retry-After header and create smoothing for enterprise quota buckets. SDK team to publish recommended settings and patch release.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Several devices coming back from depot repair fail automated corporate certificate rotation during first post-repair checkin. Failure correlates with DHCPv6 temporary address collisions at the repair facility network; the provisioning agent attempts rotation but receives an identical IPv6 temporary address (TLA/ULA conflict) already mapped to a different device, causing the cert-rotation handshake to stall and the agent to retry into exponential backoff.

Impact:
- A subset (~6%) of repaired laptops are blocked from rotating machine certificates on first checkin, delaying MDM enrollment and blocking policy application.
- Affects devices reprovisioned from depot repair facility in us-east region.
- No user-facing data loss, but devices remain in partial-managed state for up to 24+ hours unless manually remediated.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east) depot repair VLAN (172.31.200.0/24) with IPv6 SLAAC + stateful DHCPv6 enabled on site router appliance.
- Devices: Dell Precision 5570 and Lenovo ThinkPad T14 generations returned for keyboard replacement.
- Provisioning stack: intune-agent v4.3.1 -> provisioning-agent v2.8.0 -> cert-rotation service (internal)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Device receives temporary IPv6 address via router's SLAAC/DHCPv6 on depot repair VLAN.
2) Device runs provisioning-agent first-boot flow and requests corp machine cert via cert-rotation endpoint.
3) Cert-rotation performs IP/hostname correlation checks; backend ledger shows a different device already holding a lease with same IPv6 temporary address (collision).
4) Agent stalls waiting for ephemeral confirmation, retries with backoff, and eventually reports failure to CS.

Observed behavior:
- provisioning-agent logs show repeated "ip_conflict_detected: temporary_ipv6 already in ledger" followed by exponential-retry and eventual "certificate rotation timed out".
- Affected devices get flagged as "partial-managed" in console and show missing machine certs.

Expected behavior:
- Cert rotation should tolerate transient temporary IPv6 collisions at depot networks by falling back to alternative identifier (MAC/serial) or forcing short randomized client ID for rotation handshake.
Confirmed increased collision events on depot VLAN via dhcpv6-snoop logs between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-09.
Ledger currently keys cert requests by IP+clientid; collisions occur when temporary IPv6 addresses are non-unique across NAT/proxy segments at repair facility.
Reproduced locally by spinning up two VMs on same depot VLAN emulator and forcing identical temporary IPv6 (SLAAC edge case); provisioning-agent blocked as seen in field.
Checked related tickets: INT-660321 (networkmanager duplicate route) and INT-272831 (kmod-signature); networking team aware of odd VLAN config at depot vendor.
No changes to provisioning-agent code between baseline good fleet and failing cohort; likely environmental IPv6 lease footprint at repair site.
Repair facility network is performing IPv6 address recycling or proxying in a way that causes identical temporary SLAAC/DHCPv6 addresses to appear for multiple devices. The cert-rotation service's strict IP-based correlation is not tolerant to transient collisions.
1) On inbound repair returns, instruct depot to isolate devices into per-device VLANs (short-term).
2) Manually trigger provisioning-agent restart with --force-clientid flag to use serial-based client id for cert rotation (run by support).
3) Added short-lived server-side mitigation: mark collision events as transient and accept rotation if serial/MAC matches within 30s window (hotfix toggled on 2026-03-12).
Mitigation applied: backend hotfix tolerates transient ip collisions for 30s window when serial or MAC correlates, and support documented a depot isolation playbook. Engineering roadmap item opened to make client rotate by default to serial-based handshake as a durable fix.
Ship provisioning-agent change to default to serial-based client id for rotation (Engineering) - PR #789
Coordinate with Depot vendor to reconfigure IPv6 handling and ensure per-device isolation (Ops)
Monitor production depot VLAN for 72h for recurrence and collect dhcpv6-snoop traces on each failure (SRE)

Additional notes:
SRE (Liam O'Connor) (2026-03-12): Deployed temporary backend toggle to accept serial match within 30s window as a mitigation; monitoring for false positives.
Depot Ops (Maya Ruiz) (2026-03-12): We will isolate repairs into ephemeral VLANs today and escalate if more failures seen.
payload.summary: DHCPv6 temporary lease collision prevents corp certificate auto-rotation on repaired laptops

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer applied a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that enabled aggressive async-batching, KV prefetch and an 8-bit quantization profile. After rollout, they report intermittent 95th percentile latency spikes (~200-400ms above baseline) and occasional streaming partial frames (client sees chunk gaps) for production traffic.

Impact:
- Affects NeonMed's dedicated cluster (single reserved pool) in us-east-1.
- Approximately 12% of requests observed above customer SLA target at 95p during peak.
- User-facing degradations for key interactive endpoint (chat/stream).

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated (reserved) pool, tenant NeonMed, 4x A100-equivalent instances
- Runtime version: serving-runtime v2.9.1
- Optimizer profile: tenant/optimizers/neonmed-aggressive-v2 (enabled 2026-03-09 14:20 UTC)
- Traffic pattern: bursty short-turn conversations (mean tokens 80, tail to 1024), streaming enabled

Steps to reproduce (customer reported):
1) Send multiple concurrent interactive streams (50 concurrent sessions) with mixed short and long contexts.
2) Observe occasional 95p latency spikes and streaming chunk gaps.
3) Reverting manually to the previous optimizer profile appears to reduce spikes but customer needs a safe rollback plan.

Logs & telemetry snippets provided by customer:
- Request traces: https://telemetry.redwood.ai/trace/NEON-20260309-88a
- Console screenshot (percentile graph): https://files.neonmed.com/latency-spike-0309.png

Notes on urgency: Customer is on a dedicated contract and requires resolution or a safe mitigation within 48hrs to meet SLAs for a live product demo on 2026-03-15.
Initial analysis (Marcos Silva):
- Correlation seen between optimizer rollout time and first spike window.
- KV prefetch appears to increase memory pressure for longer contexts, causing intermittent GC-like stalls in the runtime thread.
- Async-batching improved throughput but introduced queuing jitter under bursty short sessions.
- Streaming chunk gaps likely due to head-of-line delays when a long request sits in a batch.
- No 5xx spike; errors are primarily increased tail latency and some client perceived stream discontinuities.

Hypotheses tested:
- Disabled KV prefetch for a single backend pod in staging: 95p improved but throughput dropped slightly.
- Reduced max-batch-size from 64 to 32 in a canary: reduced 95p by ~120ms.

Next steps proposed:
1) Advise customer to enable traffic shadowing (split traffic 10% shadow -> new profile, 90% stable) while keeping the aggressive profile in shadow mode to collect telemetry without impacting users.
2) Prepare atomic snapshot of tenant optimizer settings and a fast revert script to restore previous profile per-tenant.
3) Provide stepwise tuning suggestions: lower async batch window, disable KV prefetch for streaming endpoints, and revert quantization to 16-bit fallback for long sequences.
4) Recommend using routing policy to pin streaming endpoints to a less aggressive profile until post-tuning verification.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 02:40 UTC - SRE Oncall (Elena Gomez): Observed increased memory working set on the tenant pool correlated with KV prefetch threads. Suggested candidate mitigation: disable prefetch per endpoint and lower async batch delay to 8ms for streaming routes.
2026-03-12 16:30 UTC - Support (Marcos Silva): We've prepared a safe snapshot and a revert script (attached PR). Proposed immediate actions: a) enable 10% shadowing to gather live samples; b) lower batch-size and async delay for streaming; c) standby to execute tenant snapshot revert if 95p does not improve after 2 hours.
2026-03-13 08:10 UTC - Customer (Priya Nair): Starting 10% shadow now. Will report after 90 minutes. We also approved a maintenance window on 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC if needed.
Mitigation in progress as of 2026-03-13:
- Applied conservative changes to streaming routes (async delay reduced, max-batch-size reduced to 32) which improved 95p by ~90-130ms in the canary.
- Enabled 10% shadowing to gather live behavior for the aggressive profile without impacting production.
- Prepared tenant optimizer snapshot and tested per-tenant revert script in staging (PR linked).
If metrics do not stabilize after full tuning steps, plan is to execute per-tenant snapshot revert to previous optimizer profile during the approved maintenance window (2026-03-14 02:00 UTC).
Follow-ups:
- SRE to add a sentinel: auto-detect 95p regression >100ms for 15min and trigger a support alert.
- Support to provide a compact runbook for customers to perform safe shadowing and atomic revert in the Console.
- Engineering to evaluate memory footprint of KV prefetch under long-context workloads and consider a bounded-prefetch mode.
payload.summary: Guidance for shadow-traffic migration + snapshot rollback after aggressive batch/quant profile change causing intermittent 95p latency increases

payload.description:
Several engineers in the SF office reported intermittent SSH resets and failures when connecting to internal build hosts (10.3.4.0/22) while connected to the corporate Wi‑Fi. Connections over wired ethernet to the same hosts are stable. Initial hypothesis: wireless aggregation/A-MPDU interaction with the branch NAT and our UDP hole-punching for VPN is leading to ephemeral port reuse and mid-session TCP/SSH resets.
Multiple engineering users in office unable to maintain stable SSH sessions to internal build/test infrastructure. CI jobs running from laptops occasionally drop during deploys. Affects productivity; no public customer impact detected.
1) Connect a laptop to corp‑wifi (SF office, 802.11ax APs). 2) Establish site-to-site VPN via corporate edge (WireGuard client from laptop). 3) SSH to an internal build host behind branch NAT (10.3.4.x). 4) Start an interactive session and run a long-running command (e.g., tail -f + large scp). 5) Observe intermittent SSH disconnects after ~300-1200s. Repeat with wired ethernet — issue does not reproduce.
SSH sessions drop with 'Connection reset by peer' or 'Broken pipe'. netstat on branch edge shows ephemeral port mappings being reclaimed and reused rapidly. AP telemetry shows high A-MPDU aggregation sizes and bursty TX patterns for affected clients. NAT table entries time out unusually quickly for UDP/VPN flows on the branch gateway during the bursts.
SSH sessions should remain stable over Wi‑Fi; NAT should preserve ephemeral mappings for the negotiated lifetime; wireless aggregation should not trigger premature NAT eviction.
branch-gateway/syslog: Mar 10 10:42:11 natd[1223]: evicting entry UDP 10.3.4.23:51734 -> 34.67.12.9:51820 (age 8s)
ap-telemetry: client 02:11:22:33:44:55 a-mpdu: avg 64k, bursts: 12 in 60s
laptop dmesg: wireguard: peer 34.67.12.9 handshake OK; keepalive every 25s
ssh client: Mar 10 10:49:21 packet_write_wait: Connection to 10.3.4.45 port 22: Broken pipe
- Reproduced with two different laptop models and two different APs in SF office.
- Packet captures show that when AP sends large aggregated frames, bursts of ACK-less UDP keepalives are delayed (driver coalescing), causing branch gateway to see no activity for VPN UDP mapping and prune it.
- NAT eviction policy on branch gateway uses inactivity thresholds of 10s for UDP by default; aggressive pruning combined with delayed keepalives leads to a race where ephemeral ports are reclaimed and later reassigned to new flows. When reassigned, inbound packets land on the wrong TCP tuple causing upstream TCP resets.
- Wired path shows no aggregation; keepalives are timely and NAT entries persist.
- Configuring laptop wireguard keepalive to 10s reduced occurrence but did not eliminate it under heavy aggregation bursts.
- No related recent code deploys in networking infra; change window: AP firmware update two weeks ago that enabled higher TX aggregation sizes on 802.11ax under heavy client load.
- Correlated increase in incidents with AP firmware rollouts (ticket AP-FW-2026-02-25).
1) Temporarily adjusted branch NAT UDP inactivity timeout from 10s -> 60s for SF office gateway (mitigated immediate flapping).
2) Contacted wireless team to throttle A-MPDU max aggregation per-client to default levels on affected APs (rolled back recent aggressive setting).
3) Recommended laptop-side workarounds: set WireGuard PersistentKeepalive to 15s and reduce driver TX coalescing (sysctl/net driver knobs) where feasible.
4) Scheduled follow-up: firmware vendor validation of aggregation vs keepalive interplay and vendor bug report ID: VENDOR-1823.
Maya Chen | 2026-03-10: Reported initial symptom — SSH resets while on corp‑wifi. Attached packet capture and screen recording of ssh disconnects.
Luca Romano | 2026-03-11: Started reproducibility testing. Reproduced on AP‑B1 and AP‑B2. Captured pcap on branch edge and AP. Noticed NAT evictions correlated with large A‑MPDU bursts.
SRE Oncall (Jonah Patel) | 2026-03-11: Increased NAT UDP timeout to 60s on sf-branch-gw as a short-term mitigation. Observed immediate drop in user reports.
Wireless Team (Aisha Raman) | 2026-03-12: Rolled back AP aggregation parameter 'tx_aggregation_max' from 256->64 on the affected radios. Monitoring for regressions.
Maya Chen | 2026-03-13: Confirmed SSH sessions stable for daily workflows after NAT timeout increase + AP rollback. Still collecting telemetry for full closure.
Mitigation applied: NAT UDP inactivity timeout increased and AP aggregation parameter rolled back. Short-term workaround documented for engineers (set persistent keepalive). Long-term fixes: vendor patch expected to address interaction; plan to add a NAT heuristic to avoid reclaiming recently used UDP mappings for flows identified as VPN tunnels.
- Track vendor bug VENDOR-1823 and schedule patch validation.
- Implement NAT heuristics in branch gateway to detect and protect VPN UDP mappings.
- Add monitoring alert for increased NAT eviction rates and correlate with AP aggregation telemetry.
- Update runbook: recommend WireGuard keepalives and client-side driver knobs for on-prem office Wi‑Fi.
payload.summary: Office Wi‑Fi client aggregation interacts with NAT timeouts causing ephemeral port reuse and SSH connection resets to internal hosts

payload.description:
Issue summary:
After SSD replacement and depot reimage, a small cohort (~6) of Dell Precision 5580 units fail Autopilot/Intune enrollment during the initial provisioning step. Devices boot, fetch image, and reach 'applying provisioning' but stall waiting for network-based SCEP and MDM enrollment. Enrollment ultimately times out and image is marked as failed.

Impact:
- Blocking provisioning for replacement/repair fleet arriving from depot (affects 6 machines reported so far).
- Delays RMA turnaround; customers waiting on devices.
- Manual remediation currently required (DHCP lease purge + reimage) which takes ~30 minutes per device.

Environment:
- Production provisioning image (autopilot + corp preprovisioned).
- Region: us-west-2 corporate DHCP on-prem site.
- Affected hardware: Dell Precision 5580 with NVMe SSD swapped during depot repair.

Steps to reproduce (observed flow):
1) Depot performs SSD replacement and runs depot reimage (corporate imaging flow).
2) Device boots into provisioning image; systemd-networkd brings up link.
3) DHCP client obtains lease, but provisioning agent later reports ‘network unreachable’ when connecting to SCEP and enrollment endpoints.
4) Enrollment retries until timeout; imaging marked as failed.

Observed behavior / key logs:
- journalctl excerpt from repro unit (truncated):
  Mar 08 10:12:31 precision5580 systemd-networkd[812]: eth0: Gained carrier
  Mar 08 10:12:31 precision5580 dhclient[940]: DHCPREQUEST on eth0 to 10.0.0.2 port 67
  Mar 08 10:12:31 precision5580 dhclient[940]: DHCPACK from 10.0.0.2
  Mar 08 10:13:03 provision-agent[1221]: ERROR connecting to scep.redwood.internal: connect ECONNREFUSED
  Mar 08 10:13:03 provision-agent[1221]: retrying (attempt 3/5)
  Mar 08 10:13:33 kernel: r8169 0000:03:00.0 eth0: MAC address changed from 3c:97:0e:aa:bb:cc to 3c:97:0e:dd:ee:ff
  Mar 08 10:13:33 systemd-networkd[812]: eth0: link lost
  Mar 08 10:13:34 systemd-networkd[812]: eth0: Gained carrier
  Mar 08 10:13:34 dhclient[940]: DHCPDISCOVER on eth0 to 255.255.255.255 port 67
  Mar 08 10:13:34 dhclient[940]: DHCPACK from 10.0.0.2 (lease offered for 86400 seconds)

- On DHCP server (ISC DHCP) logs there are duplicate lease entries for the old MAC and the new MAC from the same scope; server served a lease but client traffic observed on a different VLAN/gateway for a subset of packets (packet capture showed mismatched gateway).

Expected behavior:
- After depot repair and reimage, device should successfully request and maintain a DHCP lease, reach SCEP/MDM endpoints, and complete Autopilot enrollment without manual intervention.

Additional notes:
- Not all depot-rebuilt units are affected; pattern correlates to units that also had EC firmware updated at depot (suggests transient NIC firmware or EC interaction).
- Devices occasionally show a mid-boot MAC change (kernel log above) which triggers a second DHCP handshake; provisioning agent appears sensitive to transient link resets and can mark network 'unavailable' even after lease is re-established.

Additional notes:
2026-03-08 15:45 - SRE Team (via #support): DHCP server shows both old and new MACs leased in the same scope for 3 of the units. We purged stale leases for one device (asset TAG RWD-2051) and repro attempt progressed to SCEP successfully.
2026-03-11 17:03 - QA (L. Park): Deployed patched image to staging depot; 0/12 failures in reproduced runs (was 4/12 previously).
Hypothesis: EC firmware flash during depot repair transiently resets NIC or swaps MAC presented to kernel, creating a race where provisioning-agent believes network unavailable while DHCP server still holds stale binding. Evidence: kernel log shows MAC change mid-boot and DHCP server shows duplicate/stale leases. Reproduced by forcing a NIC reset mid-provision; provisioning-agent reliably failed unless DHCP lease was purged or provisioning image waited for stable TCP connect to SCEP. SRE confirmed DHCP behavior; purging lease allowed normal flow. Patch approach: ensure provisioning flow treats transient link drops as recoverable by explicitly releasing and renewing DHCP and validating TCP reachability to SCEP before marking network as 'ready'.
Temporary workaround: updated provisioning image (v2026-03-10-hotfix) with a pre-provision network-stabilizer script that: (1) on link state change runs dhclient -r && dhclient, (2) retries TCP connect to scep.redwood.internal up to 10 times with backoff, (3) delays provisioning-agent start until network check passes. Deployed to production depot image and applied to the 6 affected units (remote DHCP lease purge by SRE + reimage). Result: all 6 devices enrolled successfully.

Issue summary: A scheduled bulk import of support templates (escalation templates + conditional priority expressions) during the nightly maintenance window produced a set of templates with duplicated internal IDs and erroneous priority values. Impact: ~23% increase in P1 internal alerts between 02:10-02:30 UTC on 2026-03-09, multiple oncall pages triggered, and internal reporting shows doubled counts for a subset of routing buckets. Observed behavior: importer created templates with duplicated "template_id" values (UUID collisions) and parsed numeric priority expressions as strings which, after downstream normalization, resulted in extremely high numeric weights (default fallback applied). Expected behavior: each template should have a unique ID and priority expressions should be validated and normalized to the configured numeric range. Immediate mitigation: rolled importer back to snapshot v2026-03-08 and suspended scheduled batch imports until a fix is deployed. This ticket tracks the RCA, hotfix, and reporting reconciliation.
1) Run batch_importer v2.4.1 against templates CSV containing mixed locale numeric formats (e.g., '1,000' vs '1000') in parallel (shards=8). 2) Observe generated template IDs in support-templates table; note duplicates. 3) Trigger routing simulation; observe priority weights showing extreme values and routing to oncall. 4) Re-run with strict-parse flag to see validation errors. Note: reproduction requires parallelism and CSV with at least one conditional expression using comma as thousands separator.
- support-importer logs: import_worker[7] ERROR: "template insert conflict: duplicate key value" at 2026-03-09T02:12:43Z.\n- support-alerts-dashboard: P1-count spike +23% at 02:10-02:30 UTC.\n- DB slow queries: elevated locks on support-templates table during import window.\n- sample stack trace + link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/commit/4f2b9a2 (importer run id: batch-20260309-01)
Initial hypotheses: (A) UUID generator had a regression causing truncated UUIDs under high parallelism; (B) CSV parser locale handling turned thousand-separated numbers into strings; (C) downstream normalizer treated non-numeric priority as NaN and applied fallback max-weight (10000). Current findings: importer was updated in PR #8142 to a new UUID function that trimmed entropy for dedup stabilization but introduced collisions when shards > 4. Also, a CSV parsing library bump removed automatic numeric coercion for specific locale formats. Evidence: compare hashes in batch-20260309-01 vs snapshot v2026-03-08, and reproduced collision locally by running importer with shards=8. Correlation with reporting inflation: duplicate template IDs cause reporting pipeline to count templates twice; priority fallback amplified routing to oncall.
1) Reverted importer to snapshot v2026-03-08 (rollback deployed 2026-03-09T04:05Z). 2) Suspended nightly batch imports until validation gates added. 3) Manual dedupe on support-templates table performed: removed 128 duplicate rows and re-indexed primary key. 4) Oncall notified and false-positive alerts suppressed where possible.
- Backout problematic UUID change and restore high-entropy generator with proper collision checks (PR #8228). - Add strict numeric parsing and validation to CSV import pipeline; fail import on unparseable priority expressions. - Add preflight dry-run with duplicate-detection and shard-safety check. - Add unit/e2e tests that simulate shards > 4 and localized numeric formatting.
