payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple users in the London office observed that Chromebooks (ChromeOS 114/115) suddenly lose corporate IPsec VPN (IKEv2) after connecting to an AP that shared the same SSID but different BSSID and VLAN. Impact: Users report immediate loss of service to internal tooling, console, GitHub repos and inability to reach internal KMS endpoints. Several sessions triggered NAC re-auth and received a restrictive ACL until manual rejoin.

Impact: Around 6 users in the office affected during the 09:00-10:30 window. Productivity blocked for a subset of platform engineers. Not customer-facing but high internal availability impact.

Environment: Office Wi-Fi: "RedwoodCorp-Employee" SSID, mixed 2.4/5GHz, controller: Aruba 8400; NAC: ISE 3.2; VPN gateway: Palo Alto GlobalProtect/IKEv2 terminating to FW cluster; DHCP via Catalyst DHCP relay; ChromeOS versions 114.x/115.x.

Observed after-change window: a new AP on temporary PoE switch was deployed earlier that morning. AP was mis-provisioned to the same VLAN tag as the guest AP but advertised the corporate SSID via a different BSSID.

Expected behavior: Devices should either: 1) choose the corporate AP with matching corporate VLAN and maintain VPN; or 2) if moved to a different VLAN, the client should drop and the NAC should present clear remediation steps rather than applying a restrictive ACL that blocks VPN control traffic.
1) Bring a ChromeOS laptop to the London office on a Wi-Fi profile bound to 'RedwoodCorp-Employee'.
2) Ensure two APs are broadcasting the SSID: one correctly configured on VLAN 100 (corporate) and one misconfigured on VLAN 300 (guest) but advertising same SSID.
3) Force assoc to the misconfigured AP (move physically closer or power-cycle the AP).
4) Observe IP assignment, default gateway and whether IKEv2 negotiations continue.
5) Check NAC session in ISE for posture and applied ACL.
Immediately after associating to the misconfigured AP the Chromebook receives an IP from VLAN 300 (guest). IKE_SA rekey attempts fail: IKEv2 SA tears down with CHILD_SA negotiation errors, then ChromeOS initiates rekey which times out. NAC (ISE) detects mismatch and applies a restrictive ACL; device loses both internal and internet-bound access to corporate endpoints. Users cannot trigger a transparent reauth; manual disconnect/reconnect to the correct AP is required.

Network evidence: DHCP offered from wrong scope (10.30.0.0/24) rather than corporate (10.10.0.0/24). IKE logs show error 'NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN' followed by 'ISAKMP-SA not found' and rekey timeouts.
Client should either get corporate VLAN and keep VPN alive, or, if VLAN difference detected, NAC should redirect to onboarding/remediation page rather than apply a full block that prevents reauth. VPN gateway should fallback gracefully or clearly report misconfiguration so SRE/network team can detect earlier.
IKE logs (vpn-gw-02) 2026-03-10T09:12:14Z: 'peer 10.30.12.45:500 IKE_SA_INIT received', 2026-03-10T09:12:15Z: 'NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN', 2026-03-10T09:12:16Z: 'CHILD_SA negotiation failed' ; DHCP server dhcp-srv-lon.log excerpt: 'DISCOVER from 24:6E:96:AB:CD:EF; OFFER to 24:6E:96:AB:CD:EF via 10.30.0.12 scope 10.30.0.0/24'; ISE session trace: 'AuthZ decision: RESTRICTIVE_ACL applied due to VLAN-mismatch posture'. Full packet capture uploaded: https://s3.redwood-inference.internal/network/pcaps/INT-76321-chrome-ike-pcap.pcap
Network team instructed to power-cycle the misprovisioned AP and remove the SSID from the guest VLAN. Users were advised to toggle Wi-Fi off/on and re-select the corporate AP; manual reauth performed via ISE guest portal allowed restore. For immediate mitigation we disabled fast roaming 802.11r on nearby APs to reduce client flapping until patch deployed.
Hypothesis: SSID/BSSID collision + VLAN misassignment causing IP change mid-IKE life-cycle. ChromeOS expects continuous connectivity; sudden subnet/gateway change causes IKE SA validation to fail and client attempts rekey from new source IP, which the VPN gateway rejects. ISE treats the new IP as non-corporate and enforces restrictive ACL.

Evidence collected: DHCP leases, AP provisioning snapshot, ISE session traces, and pcap showing IKE_INIT from 10.30.x.x then NAT detection mismatch. No indication of DNS poisoning or intentional spoofing.

Next steps: Add an AP provisioning validation script to CI to prevent corporate SSID assignment on guest VLANs. Add a monitoring alert to detect corporate SSID broadcasting in guest VLANs (controller syslog). Investigate whether VPN gateway can tolerate source-IP change mid-session (suggested feature request to firewall vendor).
Workaround implemented: misconfig AP removed from rack, provisioning template fixed. Firmware patched to prevent mismatched VLAN assignment on SSID profiles. ISE policy updated to present an onboarding/reauth portal when VLAN mismatch posture detected instead of immediate restrictive ACL. Follow-up action: Create configuration validation check in Ansible templates and add a dashboard alert for corporate-SSID-on-noncorporate-VLAN events. Pending: vendor feature request to accept transient IP change for IKE rekey (ticket opened with firewall vendor).
2026-03-10 09:35 - Support (Aisha Malik): User reported laptop 'lost VPN and couldn't access console'. Collected ChromeOS system logs and DHCP lease details.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:02 - Security (Priya Desai): ISE shows posture change triggered by VLAN mismatch; recommended failing soft-landing to onboarding portal rather than ACL block. Opening follow-up policy ticket.
payload.summary: Chromebook associates to duplicate SSID BSSID -> IPsec VPN disconnect and NAC re-auth blocks traffic

payload.description:
Issue summary: Run a phased credential sweep and conditional asset retrieval for a batch of 18 international contractors whose offboarding windows span multiple countries. The sweep must coincide with sealed-storage handling for any removable media and follow the sealed-HDD escrow policy for contractors leaving in restricted regions.

Background: HR initiated end-dates for contractors in EMEA and APAC cohorts (group A & B) due to contract expirations. Recent audit flagged inconsistent asset receipts for previous batches and a missed KMS key rotation tied to contractor service accounts. Security requires: (1) verified identity confirmation before asset handback, (2) sealed-HDD chain-of-custody when applicable, (3) revocation of cloud console and VPN access only after evidence of asset return or documented exception.

Impact: If not executed carefully, risk of lingering privileged credentials, unreturned encrypted drives, and noncompliance with contractual data-handling clauses. Business impact: potential compliance tickets for legal and delayed contractor payroll clearance.

Scope: 18 contractors across UK, FR, SG, and AU regions; mix of laptop + removable HDDs (7 flagged removable drives). Affected systems: Okta, GSuite, AWS IAM roles, internal service accounts, company asset inventory.

Acceptance criteria: All contractor accounts either fully deprovisioned or placed into documented exception cases; KMS key access revoked from contractor principals; asset return recorded in inventory with photo evidence and sealed-HDD chain-of-custody documented in Confluence; open exceptions have SRE/Legal-approved mitigation and TTL assigned.

Runbook links: Sealed HDD procedure (Confluence), Asset receipt form (internal), HR offboard batch template (internal).
Initial reconnaissance: HR export received with contractor list and signed NDAs. Inventory cross-check showed 5 contractors previously marked 'returned' with no photo evidence. IAM audit shows two service accounts still granted read access to redwood-prod-s3 via an older role binding.

Hypotheses and actions taken:
- Hypothesis 1: Asset returns were recorded but photos not uploaded. Action: PS sent to site coordinators to request receipts.
- Hypothesis 2: Service accounts were not included in automated deprovision rule due to legacy naming. Action: Running inventory query and plan to add name patterns to deprov script.

Partial findings:
- KMS grants: contractor-batch-A had an explicit grant via role/contractor-data-reader; schedule to rotate associated key material at 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC.
- Networking: VPN sessions show no active connections for these contractors in last 7 days.

Dependencies: Legal sign-off for sealed-HDD cross-border shipping for FR -> UK returns. Slack thread created: #support-internal (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05ABC123).
1) Coordinate with HR to get missing photo evidence and signed handback forms. 2) Execute targeted deprovision script for legacy-named service accounts (test in staging). 3) Rotate KMS key and revoke contractor grants at scheduled window. 4) Arrange sealed-HDD pickup or escrow per region policy (Logistics vendor: SecureShip). 5) Update offboard automation to include legacy patterns and a 'pending asset' state. 6) Document exceptions and notify Finance for final payroll clearance.
Risk: Contractor requires laptop return but is remote with local customs restrictions (APAC). Mitigation: Use SecureShip certified pickup and create legal-approved exception if pickup infeasible.

Risk: KMS rotation causes transient service disruptions for systems that relied on contractor access keys. Mitigation: Verify no production job depends on contractor principals; run key rotation in low-traffic window and have rollback plan.

Risk: Delay in legal approval for cross-border sealed-HDD transport. Mitigation: Hold encrypted drives in regional escrow and revoke access until clearance obtained.
- 2026-03-12: Complete KMS rotation and revoke grants (Marco). - 2026-03-13: Confirm receipt photos for outstanding 5 contractors (HR liaison: Elena Morris). - 2026-03-14: Execute deprovision script in prod after 1h monitoring (SRE: Priya Desai). - 2026-03-15: Close exceptions or escalate to Legal/Finance.

Owner: Marco Ruiz
payload.summary: Phased credential sweep for international contractor cohort with conditional asset return and sealed-storage HDD policy

Issue summary: A €48,250 prepayment (bank reference RB-20260309-9987) was posted to vendor ledger for vendor 'Nordic Data Supplies' (VND-4472) but was not allocated to the open invoice INV-2026-0345. The AP system shows a prepayment/suspense GL code instead of an AP-credit that can be applied, resulting in an outstanding invoice on the supplier portal and a reconciliation mismatch for March bank close.

Impact: Blocks automatic 3-way match for PO-987245, prevents supplier from being marked settled, causes month-end unreconciled suspense of €48,250 (affects cash position reporting). Finance close window at risk if not resolved.

Environment: Production AP ledger (NetAcct v4.2) integrated with payments gateway (PayGrid); AP batch 2026-03-09-09:00 CET. Region: eu-west.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Payment file generated by Payments team for vendor VND-4472 on 2026-03-09.
2) Bank confirmed debit on 2026-03-09 09:12 CET (RB ref above).
3) NetAcct processed incoming payment feed and created prepayment record using GL 2995-suspense instead of GL 2100-AP-credit.
4) Matching engine did not auto-apply to INV-2026-0345 due to missing vendor application rule (expected behaviour: auto-apply when PO match found).

Logs / evidence: Bank statement excerpt (s3://redwood-finance/evidence/2026-03-09/RB-20260309-9987.pdf), AP processing log snippet (ap-processor-2026-03-09.log lines 412-428), NetAcct audit trail (audit-trail-VND-4472.csv). Slack thread: #fin-ap (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02FINAP123).

Immediate business workaround requested: reverse suspense entry, repost as AP credit and apply to INV-2026-0345; then re-run reconciliation for March close.

Recommended long-term action items: Add a mapping validation that rejects prepayment to suspense when vendor and invoice are both present in the batch; add alert for single prepayment >€10k to create manual review task; review PayGrid -> NetAcct mapping for remittance reference parsing.

Additional notes:
Initial hypothesis: remittance parsing edge-case — delimiter ';' vs expected '|' produced null invoice_id in mapping layer.
NetAcct created prepayment because incoming payment record had vendor ID but missing matched invoice_id field; fallback path uses GL 2995-suspense.
Payment gateway (PayGrid) sometimes formats remittance differently for vendors sending consolidated files; no prior alert existed for >€10k prepayments.
Confirmed that auto-apply engine requires both vendor_id and invoice_id to be present; adding guard to attempt fuzzy-match on remittance when invoice_id missing.
Related historical ticket INT-34121 documented a similar mapping mismatch for a different vendor in 2025 Q4; root cause was parser robustness.
Manual reversal and repost completed on 2026-03-12 (JR-2026-03-12-557). INV-2026-0345 marked settled and suspense GL cleared. Engineering deployed parser fix to staging (PR merged 2026-03-14) and scheduled production deploy for 2026-03-16 after smoke tests. Finance requested monitoring rule for prepayments >€10k and a follow-up audit to close any other lingering suspense entries. Owner for follow-up: Maya Rodriguez.
Prod deploy parser fix on 2026-03-16 - Engineering
Add alert for prepayments > 10000 EUR - Finance Ops
Quarterly sweep for suspense GL entries - Finance Ops

payload.description:
Issue summary: After depot repair and NIC firmware reflash, several workstations had Ethernet MAC address randomization enabled by default. This changed the device network identity and caused our VPN SCEP/certificate profile and device tagging to fail during provisioning.

Impact: New and repaired devices in depot that have mac randomization turned on are failing automated VPN profile deployment (cert provisioning) and subsequently blocking access to internal resources. Affected devices are stuck in provisioning flow until a manual remediation is performed. Approximately 18 devices reported in the last 72 hours across two depot batches; potential to scale with larger repair runs.

Environment: Production provisioning pipeline (intune/autopilot + internal VPN SCEP profile) in us-west and us-east. Affected images: internal-provision-2026-02, provisioning-agent v1.9.4, NIC firmware package fw-net-3.2.1 applied during depot.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Depot technician reimages device using internal-provision-2026-02 image and applies NIC firmware fw-net-3.2.1.
2) Device boots and Autopilot/Intune enrollment triggers provisioning-agent.
3) Provisioning-agent requests device identity and tries to deploy VPN SCEP profile keyed to persistent NIC MAC + asset tag.
4) NIC reports randomized MAC (locally administered) and the inventory service record does not match expected asset-tag->MAC mapping.
5) SCEP cert enrollment fails with status 403 in our MDM logs and VPN profile install is skipped.

Observed logs (excerpts):
- provisioning-agent.log: "[2026-03-10T08:14:22Z] identity-check failed: mac_mismatch (expected 3c:97:0e:aa:bb:cc, reported 02:12:34:56:78:9a)"
- mdm-audit.log: "2026-03-10T08:14:25Z SCEP request denied: device identity mismatch, reason=mac_mismatch"
- inventory-service: "asset 12345: last_seen_mac=02:12:34:56:78:9a, asset_tag=RW-12345, depot_repair=true"

Hypothesis: A NIC firmware reflash or default driver setting is enabling locally-administered MAC or randomization mode post-repair. Our provisioning flow assumes stable hardware MAC for device identity checks; when it changes, the inventory index lookup fails and SCEP policy denies cert issuance. There is also a gap where depot technicians do not run the post-flash identity normalization script.

Workaround: Manual remediation steps that have been successful: connect device to depot staging network, run `netcfg normalize-mac` script (internal tool) which forces factory MAC and updates inventory via `inventory-service update-mac`. Then re-trigger provisioning. This is manual and time-consuming.

Immediate next steps and owner:
- Endpoint team (Ravi M) to coordinate with Depot to add a post-flash check in the repair runbook and ensure `netcfg normalize-mac` is executed (owner: Ravi Malhotra).
- Infra/Inventory (Liam C) to add tolerant matching logic to inventory-service to accept persistent asset_tag mapping when MAC is locally-administered for 72 hours post-repair (owner: Liam Casey).
- Networking team to audit fw-net-3.2.1 release notes for MAC randomization behavior and liaise with vendor (owner: Priya Shah).
- Short-term: Add a provisioning-agent bypass flag for SCEP when `depot_repair=true` that launches a supervised manual approval workflow (owner: Security Ops).

Acceptance criteria for resolution:
- Depot runs include automatic normalized MAC step OR NIC firmware updated with settings to preserve factory MAC.
- Inventory-service has fallback matching for recently repaired assets and provisioning-agent can progress to VPN cert install without manual intervention.
- No Regressions: test plan in CI that simulates repaired device flow.

References:
- Slack: #it-depot (thread ts: 2026-03-10T09:00Z)
- Ticket: INT-246801 (related depot repair provisioning stall)

payload.description:
Issue summary: LexiHealth reports sudden, repeatable P99 token-level latency spikes and occasional 504s when sending near-identical prompts repeatedly (chat/regen patterns). Impact: customer-facing document summarization pipeline experiences degraded throughput and intermittent timeouts during peak traffic windows (approx 15-40% of requests in a burst window). Observed behaviour: sequences of near-identical prompts that previously hit in-memory prefix/KV cache are now producing cache misses, triggering cold KV reads to the backing store which serialize and amplify latency under concurrent repeat requests. Hypothesis: a recent cache key normalization change caused semantically identical prompts to map to different prefix keys, causing cache miss amplification on repeat patterns.
1) Use LexiHealth sample prompt set (provided in attachment) with 80% repeat-rate: send the same 6-8 token prefix followed by small completions.
2) Target 50 concurrent connections at 120 r/s for ~2 minutes.
3) Observe P50/P95/P99 for token generation and watch for 504s after ~30s.
4) Compare requests hitting cache-service (hits vs misses) and trace through request IDs collected from api-gateway logs.
Expected: high cache hit-rate for repeat-prefixes; Actual: burst of cache misses followed by P99 increases and rare 504 timeouts.
Example errors and traces:
- request_id=rx-20260310-9921 path=/v1/chat/generate status=504 downstream=serving-runtime msg='request timeout after 30s'
- serving-runtime: prefix_key="conv_v1::user123::a1b2c3_norm" cache_lookup=MISS backend_kv_latency_ms=1523
- cache-service metrics: prefix_miss_rate spike at 2026-03-10T14:12Z (from 4% -> 62%)
- sample trace: https://sentry.redwood.com/issue/INC-2026-00310 (private)
Relevant request IDs: rx-20260310-9921, rx-20260310-9925, rx-20260310-9958.
Timeline:
- 2026-03-08: rollout v2026-03-08.3 deployed normalization change to cache key generator (PR #4872). No immediate alerts.
- 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC: LexiHealth reports elevated latency. Support triaged and opened this ticket.
- 2026-03-10 15:10 UTC: SRE observed cache miss-rate spike correlated with repeat-prompts.
Key findings:
- The normalization change introduced a subtle variant mapping for high-frequency punctuation and whitespace patterns in user prompts; semantically identical user inputs now sometimes map to distinct prefix keys (example: trailing non-breaking space vs normal space).
- Cache shards showed hot-cold imbalance: one shard saw a 6x increase in backend KV reads.
- Backend KV pool exhausted under concurrency causing queues and serialization of KV reads which amplified latency and produced downstream request timeouts.
- Reproduced locally by applying the same normalization rules to prompt variants; confirmed miss-rate increase and p99 amplification.
Related signals and cross-references:
- related_github_prs: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/4872
- linked_issues: SUP-30012, INT-4567
- related_confluence_pages: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/KV+Cache+Design
Open hypotheses to validate:
- TTL desync between prefix cache metadata and backing store might exacerbate cold reads.
- Prefetch/backfill logic may not trigger for near-miss keys due to hash normalization mismatch.
Mitigations applied:
- 2026-03-10 17:45 UTC: Rolled back normalization patch (v2026-03-08.3 -> v2026-03-08.2) across us-east; immediate drop in miss-rate observed.
- Increased KV backend pool size by 30% temporarily to reduce queueing and tail latency.
- Added temporary circuit-breaker on heavy-prefix bursters to shed non-critical work.
Customer communication: LexiHealth notified of rollback and temporary mitigations; asked to validate workload during next window.
Status: Mitigated (rollback + KV pool increase). Permanent fix plan: 1) Rework normalization logic to be idempotent for common whitespace/punctuation variants and add unit tests covering edge cases; 2) Add deterministic prefix canonicalization and a graceful backfill path for near-miss keys; 3) Implement stronger shard rebalancing alerting and autoscale thresholds for KV backend; 4) Postmortem and doc update scheduled. Follow-up owner: INT ticket created (INT-4567) for permanent fix track. Estimated timeline: hotfix and tests by 2026-03-17, full rollout with monitoring by 2026-03-24.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:45 - Customer (LexiHealth, Support Contact: Daniel Cho): Confirmed improved performance during morning batch; requested ETA for permanent fix and test coverage.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several recently returned/repaired laptops (Dell Precision 5560 and Latitude 7440) fail to complete Azure AD / Intune registration after SSD/NVMe replacement. Machines boot to Windows but provisioning times out during MDM enrollment and AAD device attestation. Impact: Blocking users from being re-enrolled after depot repairs; affects onboarding and turnaround times for depot returns. Environment: Production fleet, post-depot-repair images using standard corporate Task Sequence (SCCM/WinPE) and the latest post-image drivers. Reproducible on devices that had third-party NVMe firmware applied during depot repair.
1) Replace NVMe SSD during depot repair; 2) Re-image device with standard corporate image (Win10/11 baseline) and drivers; 3) Boot and connect to corp network; 4) OOBE/Autopilot flow triggers AAD join and Intune MDM enrollment; 5) Enrollment times out or fails with TPM/attestation errors and device remains not-enrolled in Intune.
- Windows event log: DeviceEnrollmentManager timeout entries (DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider) timestamp 2026-03-05 09:12:23
- System log: Kernel reported ACPI CPPC reporting 0 performance states for CPU (Event ID custom telemetry) during early boot
- Imaging agent logs: nvme-identify returned firmware quirks flagged 'PSTATES_ZERO'
- Endpoint logs: TPM attestation retry count exceeded; 0x801c0001 timeouts
- Relevant sample device IDs: SN:DP5560-0123, SN:DL7440-0456

Initial triage (Support): Confirmed pattern only on devices that had NVMe replacements performed by third-party depot partner between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-04.
Hypothesis 1 (Hardware): Third-party NVMe firmware misreports NVMe identify fields leading Windows ACPI subsystem to mis-evaluate CPU P-state capability indirectly through OEM driver interaction.
Hypothesis 2 (OS/Driver): Our NVMe driver or power management shim sees a malformed identify and disables ACPI CPPC table parsing, causing scheduler to prefer deep low-power state; TPM attestation window is missed due to CPU being pinned to low performance.
Kernel debug: Reproduced with local lab unit. 'nvme id-ctrl' returned valid model but Capability bits cleared; a vendor-specific firmware quirk bit matches known vendor X pattern.
Cross-team signal: Hardware depot confirmed applying firmware bundle v3.2.1 from vendor X during staging; rollback to OEM firmware v2.9 resolved pstate reporting on a test unit.
Imaging script note: imaging-scripts currently do not validate NVMe controller identify flags post-replacement. Add validation step to detect vendor-quirk bit.
Related telemetry: Increase in post-repair intune enrollment failures from baseline 0.3% to 6.1% for affected models in us-west during window.
Temporary mitigation trial: Added a post-boot powerprofile change to High Performance as a workaround which allowed enrollment to complete in 3/3 lab re-tests.
Slack thread: #support-depot (link): https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12DEPOT/p1646342345000
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-05: Customer-facing depot reported multiple returns with re-enroll failures; creating ticket after initial triage.
Ravi Kapoor (SRE) 2026-03-05: Assigned. Requesting sample device and full imaging logs. Ordered one spare test device to reproduce locally.
Depot Lead - Jenna Ortiz 2026-03-06: Confirmed vendor X pushed firmware v3.2.1 during their staging process; we've paused further firmware updates and quarantined remaining spares.
Hardware Eng - Carlos Mendez 2026-03-06: Reproduced in lab. Firmware v3.2.1 sets NVME_CTRL_CAP quirk flag that our nvme shim doesn't handle. Filing firmware rollback request with vendor X.
Imaging Eng - Priya Nair 2026-03-07: Added temporary imaging script change to set Windows power plan to High Performance during first-boot to avoid attestation timeout; pushed PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-infra/imaging-scripts/pull/298
Ravi Kapoor (SRE) 2026-03-08: Confirmed workaround on 5 test units; enrollment completes. Planning hotfix rollout for depot and imaging pipeline. Will track via linked PR and confluence checklist.
Root cause: Third-party depot-applied NVMe firmware v3.2.1 sets a vendor quirk that results in NVMe identify capability bits cleared. Interaction between NVMe controller behavior and OEM power management caused CPU performance states to be effectively unavailable during early boot, leading to prolonged low-power scheduling and windowed TPM/AAD attestation timeouts. Fixes implemented: 1) Imaging hotfix: imaging-scripts PR #298 adds a post-image NVMe validation step and sets temporary High Performance power plan for first boot to ensure attestation window; 2) Depot action: halted vendor X firmware bundle, initiated rollback on quarantined units; 3) Hardware team engaged vendor for firmware patch. Follow-ups: Add CI check in depot SOP to verify NVMe identify fields after any firmware writes, update post-repair validation runbook on Confluence, and monitor enrollment failure metric for the next 7 days.
Deploy imaging-scripts hotfix to all depots (PR merged 2026-03-08).
Vendor firmware patch expected ETA 2026-03-12; verify and validate before redeploy.
Add NVMe identify validation to Post-Repair Validation Checklist on Confluence.
Monitor FD enroller failures metric (metric id: ENROLL_FAIL_RATE) daily for 7 days and report to support leadership.
Schedule a retro with depot partner to prevent future uncoordinated firmware bundles.
payload.summary: Post-repair NVMe reports zero P-states causing prolonged low-power CPU state and AAD/Intune registration failures

Support already attempted local redaction and sampling but requires Privacy engineers to run pattern checks and replay in a sandbox.

Access requested: Two obfuscated session snapshots (session IDs provided), each reduced to first 200 tokens, all user-provided free-text replaced with salted hash except token-like strings left for pattern analysis. No API keys, no full raw traces. Access window: 6 hours.

Duration and scope: 2026-03-14 09:00 UTC to 2026-03-14 15:00 UTC (6 hours). Data will be accessed only from Privacy VPC sandbox. No extracts allowed outside approved VPC.

Data minimization and audit controls: Only fields requested (session_id, timestamp, truncated_obfuscated_payload, model, region, route) will be provisioned. All access will be logged; KMS audit enabled; access recorded to internal audit log and linked to this ticket.

Approvals required: Security approval for obfuscation method and ephemeral KMS unwrap, Privacy lead sign-off for triage, and SRE notice for any sandbox replay.

Requester: Maya Chen (Support)

Notes: This is NOT a general log access request; it is scoped and timeboxed to reduce compliance surface area. If Privacy requests deeper slices, a new approval with legal signoff will be required.

2026-03-13 11:12 - Security (Omar Ruiz): Reviewed obfuscation method. Salted SHA256 ok if salt is ephemeral and not stored. Approve conditional on ephemeral salt rotation and no write-access to persistent stores from sandbox. Security will generate the IAM role and KMSEncrypt/Decrypt policy.

Snapshot exported to sandbox as truncated_obfuscated_payload and made available to Privacy triage. Access window enforced and all accesses logged. Request to enable timebound cross-tenant Slack guest access for an external payments partner on the Platform Payments pod. In addition to Slack guest provisioning we need a matching Jira project skeleton (kanban board, default issue types, labels) and a Confluence space with a read-only view for guests. - Without a standardized onboarding flow, manual provisioning is slowing down partner work and introduces inconsistent permissions.

Environment:
- Redwood prod workspace, global Slack workspace (org-wide guest model), Confluence Standard tier, Jira internal projects.

1) Create a timebound Slack guest template: channel list (#payments-integration, #payments-oncall-readonly), limited message/post permissions, 30-day auto-expire with optional 1x extension.

4) Enforce 90-day retention for Slack messages in the provisioned channels; confirm retention policy does not affect Confluence pages.

- Any automation needs to emit audit events to the central audit Confluence/Jira index.

Issue summary: After recent IdP metadata refresh, some internal users are able to complete Okta SSO but land in internal portals with no group-based roles. Impact: editors/devs/support reports '403' or reduced privileges in internal-runbook-portal and analytics-portal; blocks runbook access for oncall. Environment: prod-us-west, identity-proxy v2.8.3, auth-service v1.13. Steps to reproduce: 1) Initiate SSO from internal-runbook-portal login button. 2) Choose Okta enterprise IdP (primary). 3) Complete IdP auth; on redirect back to identity-proxy user lands in portal but roles missing. Observed behavior: SAML assertion arrives to identity-proxy with expected GroupClaims, but the identity-proxy logs show the idp_hint value trimmed and percent-decoded incorrectly; the downstream token issued to apps omits groups claim. Expected behavior: idp_hint preserved exactly, group claims forwarded and RBAC mapping applied. This ticket focuses on diagnosing why canonicalization of the idp_hint/EntityID during the proxy handoff strips trailing characters when it contains encoded '+' and double-encoded path segments.
1) Use Chrome (non-incognito). 2) Navigate to https://internal-runbook-portal.redwood.com/login and click 'Sign in with Okta'. 3) Authenticate as affected user (example: aj@redwood.com). 4) Observe redirect to identity-proxy and final page shows limited role (Viewer) instead of Editor. 5) Check identity-proxy logs at time of login for 'idp_hint' handling entry.
2024-11-12T09:12:03Z identity-proxy: Received SAMLResponse for user aj@redwood.com; idp_hint='https%3A%2F%2Fidp.example.com%2Fokta+org'
2024-11-12T09:12:03Z identity-proxy: Normalized idp_hint='https://idp.example.com/okta' (trimmed '+org')
2024-11-12T09:12:03Z auth-service: Issued OIDC token sub=aj@redwood.com scope=openid profile groups=[]
2024-11-12T09:12:04Z rbac: No mapped group found for user aj@redwood.com; default role Viewer applied

Timeline: - 2024-11-12 09:00 UTC: Reports start from support channel #internal-auth. - 09:05: triage by Support (Aisha Patel), escalated to identity team. - 09:40: Reproduced by engineering; logs show idp_hint percent-decoding path component containing '+' becomes space then trimmed by URL normalization middleware. Hypothesis: Our identity-proxy includes a URL canonicalizer that runs a library upgrade two weeks ago (go-urilib v1.4.0->v1.5.0) which now aggressively normalizes path tokens and removes characters it considers 'unsafe', inadvertently dropping +encoded suffixes that Okta uses to disambiguate tenant aliases. Corroborating evidence: affected users share IdP alias values containing a '+' (legacy migration from partner tenants). Non-affected IdPs without '+' succeed. Work done: - Pull logs for 50 recent SSO flows, 12/50 show idp_hint modifications. - Reproduced locally by crafting SAML responses with idp_hint containing '%2B' -> normalization trims. - Created minimal repro script and filed related PR to add a unit test in identity-proxy. Risks: All SSO flows with encoded '+' in EntityID might be impacted, which could affect cross-tenant impersonation and delegated admin flows.
Temporary routing: For affected tenants we configured identity-proxy to bypass the canonicalization middleware via a header-based toggle (applied to us-west only). This restores group claims for ~80% of repro cases. Documented mapping in runbook 'IdP+ canonicalization bypass'.
1) Prepare a targeted patch to identity-proxy that preserves percent-encoded '+' (%2B) in idp_hint and passes unit tests. 2) Submit PR with tests (linked above). 3) Deploy canary to staging and one us-west instance, monitor login success rate and group propagation. 4) Plan full rollout if canary stable; otherwise rollback to previous library version. 5) Longer-term: add end-to-end tests for IdP EntityID variants.
(Pending) Partial mitigation applied via bypass toggle on 2024-11-12 13:00 UTC. Full fix PR prepared and awaiting code review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1427. Post-merge steps include canary and rollback plan. No postmortem required unless issue scope expands to >1% of SSO traffic.
payload.summary: IdP hint canonicalization truncates group claims, dropping RBAC during SSO->proxy handoff

Issue summary: Multiple new corporate workstations fail Azure AD / Autopilot enrollment during automated provisioning. Devices complete imaging but show as 'Not Joined' in Intune and reach a local account OOBE state. Impact: Blocks batch onboarding for a new cohort of hires; prevents BitLocker key escrow and standard policy application. Scope observed on 12 devices across 2 imaging racks; appears correlated to devices booting on the 'provisioning' VLAN.

Observed behavior:
- Device applies OS image and reboots to OOBE.
- Windows shows 'Can't connect to your organization' or times out on the 'Sign in with work or school account' stage.
- Devices end up with a locally created admin account (autopilot fallback) and do not appear in AAD as Hybrid/AAD joined.

Initial hypothesis: Intune/Azure endpoints are being blocked or timed out during enrollment when devices are on the provisioning VLAN, causing autopilot service calls to fail and fallback to local provisioning flow.
1) Boot device in imaging rack connected to provisioning VLAN.
2) Start Windows Autopilot provisioning with latest corp image.
3) Observe network calls to Microsoft/Graph endpoints during OOBE enrollment stage.
4) After timeout, device falls back to local account creation.
5) Check Intune device list and Autopilot service logs for failed enrollments.
- Collected network packet capture from an affected rack (pcap saved to /shared/logs/pcaps/INT-87245_provisioning.pcap).
- Observed repeated TCP RSTs and SYN timeouts to graph.microsoft.com and login.microsoftonline.com from devices on provisioning VLAN only.
- Firewall and layer-3 ACLs for the provisioning VLAN were recently updated (change committed 2026-03-09) - commit ID referenced in infra PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/842.
- ACL rules shown to inadvertently block outbound 443 to a subset of Microsoft IP ranges (customer-requested hardening for lab segmentation).
- Devices on corporate workstation VLAN (non-provisioning) do not show the issue.
- Intune logs on the service side show failed enrollment attempts with timeout errors; local device logs (eventvwr) show MDM enrollment timeouts and AAD join error 0x801c0003.
- No evidence of incorrect image or driver failure; token acquisition reached a TLS handshake but then connection reset.
- SRE confirmed ACL change rolled out to provisioning VLAN switches at 2026-03-09 04:12 UTC.
Aisha Patel (Reporter) [2026-03-10]: Noted first reports from hiring ops: 6 devices failed this morning in rack B3. Raising to SRE as P1 because onboarding blocked.
Marco Alvarez (Assignee) [2026-03-10]: Investigating network captures. Reached out to SRE network on #infra-networking. Will attach pcap and look for dropped connections.
SRE-Network (SRE) [2026-03-11]: Confirmed ACL change on provisioning VLAN that restricts outbound IP ranges. We see denied packets to Microsoft Graph endpoints. Rolling back ACL on the provisioning VLAN will restore connectivity.
Marco Alvarez [2026-03-11]: Performed controlled rollback for rack B3 and re-ran provisioning on 3 test units — all 3 successfully enrolled and appeared in Intune. Marking as actionable fix; need full VLAN rollback and runbook update.
Security (InfoSec) [2026-03-12]: We understand ACL intended to reduce exposure in lab. Recommend adding explicit allow rules for Microsoft enrollment ranges and document exceptions. Will review change flow to require an impact assessment for provisioning VLAN changes.
Marco Alvarez [2026-03-13]: Coordinating full rollback with SRE. Also creating alert to detect enrollment timeouts during autopilot runs to catch regressions early.
Temporary fix: Rolled back the restrictive ACL on provisioning VLAN for all imaging racks (completed 2026-03-12). Verified by repro on 10 affected devices — successful Autopilot enrollment, BitLocker escrow and policy application.
Permanent remediation: Update infra-config repo to add explicit allow rules for Intune/Autopilot and Graph endpoints before re-applying segmentation rules (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/843). Update provisioning runbook to include network impact checklist and require automated enrollment smoke test post-change.
Post-incident actions:
- Runbook updated at https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/autopilot-provisioning-runbook (section "Network change checklist").
- Create monitoring alert to fire when >5 Autopilot enrollments fail within 30 minutes in any rack (ticket INT-87246 created to track alerting work).
INT-87246 - Implement autopilot enrollment failure alerting
Infra PR 843 - Add explicit allow list for enrollment endpoints and document exceptions
Schedule post-change review with InfoSec and SRE (owner: Marco Alvarez)
payload.summary: Autopilot enrollment failing during provisioning due to provisioning-VLAN ACL blocking Microsoft endpoints

Issue summary:
A regulatory body (foreign financial regulator) has requested a narrow sample of raw request/response payloads for one customer's high-severity allegation. Legal has requested a minimal, timeboxed access to production raw payloads and associated audit logs strictly scoped to the impacted customer and timeframe.

Impact:
- Request is time-sensitive (regulator deadline in 5 business days).
- Access must be provable/auditable and redacted to remove unrelated PII.
- Any extract must not expose other customers or broader telemetry.

Request details / scope:
- Provide a minimal set of inference request/response payloads for customer-customer_omega between 2026-02-12T00:00:00Z and 2026-02-12T23:59:59Z (UTC).
- Include associated API audit logs, auth headers metadata (key IDs only, not full keys), and routing metadata needed for timeline reconstruction.
- Exclude any unrelated customer payloads.
- Redaction: substitute or remove user-provided PII fields (emails, SSNs, account numbers) per the attached redaction spec (confluence link).

Environment:
- prod (us-east-1) serving-runtime and audit-logs.

Steps to reproduce / access path (requested):
1) Query audit index for customer_id: customer_omega and timestamp range.
2) Pull associated raw payload blobs stored in object store (internal path masked) and mount to ephemeral analysis workspace.
3) Run automated redaction script (approved pattern file) and produce final zip with manifest and hash.

Logs / links:
- Suspected incident timeline: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-0312-omega
- Redaction runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Legal+Evidence+Collection+Runbook

Approvals required before any extract:
1) Compliance sign-off (legal@redwood.ai).
2) Engineering owner (serving-runtime) approval for any trace mounting.
3) SRE on-call to supervise ephemeral workspace and network egress controls.

Proposed controls / safeguards (requested):
- Timebound access window: 48 hours of workspace availability; extract snapshot to be purged after 7 days.
- Least-privileged service account with short-lived tokens generated via Vault, auditable via KMS logs.
- Automated redaction pass mandatory before handing to regulator; manual verification by Compliance.
- Audit entries for every action (who/downloaded/hashed) to be attached to ticket.

Desired delivery ETA:
- Proof-of-slice (redaction script run on a 3-record sample) within 48 hours of approval.
- Full timeboxed extract delivered within 96 hours after approvals, subject to SRE windows.

Notes:
- Legal emphasized zero-tolerance for over-broad extracts.
- This is not a blanket data export; narrow-scope only.

Additional notes:
Compliance (Maya Patel) (2026-03-11): Confirmed redaction patterns; provided confluence doc and a signed legal subpoena copy. Compliance requires manual sign-off after automated redact pass and wants MD5+SHA256 hashes of artifacts.
SRE (Rajat Singh) (2026-03-12): Feasibility check: we can produce timeboxed mount with ephemeral role. Two blockers: (1) current object-store retention rules require an admin assist to snapshot older blobs, (2) need Vault role creation for the ephemeral service account. Est ETA for prep: 24–36 hours pending approvals.
Hypotheses considered: (a) requested data exists in object-store indexed by request_id -> success; (b) some payloads may have been truncated by prefix caching / batching optimization — will verify presence of full payloads. Initial audit query returned ~12 candidate requests in the timeframe. Need to confirm payload completeness and whether KV-cache-only responses exist (which would not have persisted full blobs).
1) Obtain Compliance & Legal sign-off (Maya). 2) Create ephemeral Vault role and short-lived token; SRE to snapshot required blobs into an isolated bucket. 3) Run approved redaction script in ephemeral workspace; Compliance to verify. 4) Produce final bundle with manifest + hashes and upload to secured evidence share. 5) Purge workspace and snapshot after confirmation. Estimated timeline after approvals: 48–72 hours.
All actions must be logged under the ticket ID INT-903957. SRE to attach KMS logs, Vault issuance logs, and object-store access logs. Redaction script version and commit: infra/tools/redact:v2.3 (PR attached).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During automated Dedicated capacity provisioning for customer-tenant 'acme-ml', the cross-cloud credential broker (GCP Workload Identity Federation -> AWS STS) succeeded but downstream KMS operations failed with AccessDenied. Impact: Dedicated provisioner could not finish creating reserved clusters for two customers, blocking onboarding and test traffic.

Impact:
- 2 Dedicated provisioning runs failed in us-east region (customer-facing).
- Provisioner left partial resources (EC2 instances created without required KMS-wrapped secrets).
- Oncall had to rollback an attempted retry causing extra cost.

Environment:
- Provisioner service: prod-us-east namespace
- Broker: gcp-wif-broker (uses service account svc-provisioner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com)
- AWS role: arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-dedicated-provisioner
- KMS key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222222:key/aa11-bb22-cc33

Expected behavior:
- Broker issues STS token with session tags (team, tenant, request_id); AWS assume-role propagates tags and KMS key policy allows Encrypt/Decrypt when aws:PrincipalTag/team == "platform" or tenant == "acme-ml".

Observed behavior:
- STS assume-role succeeded (AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity) but subsequent KMS Encrypt calls return AccessDenied: "User: arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/redwood-dedicated-provisioner/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Encrypt on resource ... because condition aws:PrincipalTag/tenant missing"

1) Use GCP service account svc-provisioner@redwood-prod to request OIDC token for workload identity federation.
2) Call AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity including >6 session tags (tenant, team, request_id, env, feature_flag, region, extra_tag) via provisioner codepath.
3) With returned creds, call KMS:Encrypt against customer key that has condition checking aws:PrincipalTag/tenant.
4) Observe AccessDenied in CloudTrail and provisioner failure.
CloudTrail: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity: Success - RequestedSessionTags: {tenant=acme-ml, team=platform, request_id=pr-9857, env=prod, feature_flag=dedicated, region=us-east-1, extra_tag=xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx}
CloudTrail: KMS Encrypt: AccessDenied - Error: User arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/redwood-dedicated-provisioner/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Encrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222222:key/aa11-bb22-cc33 due to failed condition: aws:PrincipalTag/tenant

GCP Broker logs (gcp-wif-broker): TokenSize=3792 bytes, TruncatedTagsCount=2, Warning: session tag payload exceeds AWS STS max size; dropped last 2 tags
Provisioner: Error: provisioning aborted after KMS failure; partial infra left (i-0abcd1234).
03-10 09:12 - Reproduced in staging by creating OIDC token with many session tags; observed identical KMS denial when tags were dropped.
03-10 11:00 - AWS STS enforces a max size for session tags and will silently drop tags if token payload exceeds limit; keys after a certain index were missing in assumed-role session (confirmed in CloudTrail).
03-11 14:30 - KMS key policy uses aws:PrincipalTag/tenant condition to scope access to tenant-specific keys. If 'tenant' tag missing, KMS denies even if caller is assumed-role principal.
03-12 08:05 - Provisioner recently added extra session tags (feature_flag and extra_tag) in PR 439 to carry trace metadata. This increased session tag payload size and pushed 'tenant' tag past the truncation boundary in some calls.
03-13 16:20 - Confirmed with AWS Support that when tag payload exceeds STS limit, AWS may drop a subset of tags without failing the AssumeRole; there is no server-side error in that case.
Hypothesis: Addition of non-essential tags caused session payload > limit for some requests, causing tenant tag to be dropped leading to KMS denial.
Ava Chen (reporter) 2026-03-10: First observed during dedicated provisioning for acme-ml; escalation requested.
Miguel Alvarez (assignee) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged - assigning to SRE + Auth to investigate token size and tag propagation.
SRE-Lead (comment) 2026-03-11: Confirmed CloudTrail shows missing PrincipalTag keys on assumed role. Captured full STS request/response for sample trace id pr-9857.
Auth-Engineer (comment) 2026-03-12: We reproduced in staging. Suspect session tag ordering in caller code matters; recommend moving tenant/tag keys up earlier and dropping non-essential tags.
Miguel Alvarez 2026-03-13: Coordinated with Provisioner owners to open PR to remove extra_tag and always emit tenant as first tag. Built hotfix branch for immediate rollout.
Provisioner-Owner 2026-03-14: Hotfix merged and deployed to prod canary; provisioning for acme-ml retried and completed successfully. Monitoring for two hours.
Root cause: Provisioner started sending additional non-essential session tags which increased the OIDC/session payload beyond AWS STS tagging size threshold. AWS truncated the tail of session tags; the tenant tag was sometimes dropped, causing KMS key policy conditions to fail and produce AccessDenied on kms:Encrypt.
Immediate mitigation: Reverted the non-essential tag (extra_tag) and reordered tags in the provisioner code so tenant and team are emitted first. Deployed hotfix to prod canary on 2026-03-14 08:40 UTC and rolled to full prod after 2-hour verification window.
Long-term remediation actions:
- PROV-214: Add validation in provisioner CI to ensure total session tag payload stays under AWS documented limits and fail PRs that exceed the threshold.
- AUTH-59: Add instrumentation to gcp-wif-broker to report dropped tags count as a metric and alert on >0 drops in prod.
- SEC-87: Update KMS key policies to include a fallback allow for the provisioner assumed-role (with tight conditions) to reduce single-point failure mode while other mitigations land.
- Runbook update: Confluence runbook updated with troubleshooting steps for session tag truncation and checklist to check CloudTrail for missing aws:PrincipalTag entries.
Status: Resolved for the immediate customer onboarding runs. Follow-up work assigned to Provisioner and Auth teams with tickets PROV-214, AUTH-59, SEC-87 linked.
payload.summary: GCP Workload Identity federation -> AWS assume-role: session-tag truncation causing KMS key policy denies during Dedicated provisioning

payload.description:
Request from CS + Sales Enablement: add a Dedicated-focused SLO surface in Redwood Console to reduce back-and-forth with SRE/Infra when customers ask "what tier am I on", "what throughput is guaranteed", and "are we meeting the guarantee".

Background / why:
- Dedicated customers are asking for throughput guarantees in writing and for ongoing visibility (esp. procurement/security-led accounts).
- Current state: tier + committed throughput floor is in internal systems (contracts/order forms / provisioning notes), but not discoverable by CS/Sales in Console; SLO compliance requires navigating internal dashboards and knowing the right deployment_id.
- This causes slow responses, inconsistent messaging, and escalations that could be avoided with self-serve internal visibility.

Requested Console capabilities (internal visibility first; customer-visible later):
1) Dedicated overview panel (per customer org):
   - Dedicated tier: Standard | Plus | Premium (or current taxonomy)
   - Region(s) / deployment(s) included in commitment
   - Committed throughput floor (canonical metric per SLO doc; show units explicitly)
   - Burst policy summary (e.g., "burst allowed" and whether metered)

2) Per deployment details (deployment view):
   - Model pinned (name + version) and context limit used for sizing (if available)
   - Current throughput vs floor (last 15m and last 1h)
   - "SLO status" for last 7 days and last 30 days (green/yellow/red) with a short explanation of measurement window and exclusions
   - Link-outs to internal dashboards (Grafana/Looker) filtered by deployment_id

3) Recent incidents / credits (if available):
   - Show last N SLO-impacting incidents for that deployment (date, duration, incident id/status page link if public)
   - If credits were issued due to throughput SLO miss, display "credit issued" + date (no $ amount required)

Users / permissions:
- CS, Support, Sales, Solutions: internal-only (behind role gate).
- Do NOT expose raw internal SLO evaluator details publicly at this stage.

Data sources (proposal):
- Tier + committed floor: control plane config / billing contract metadata (needs a single source-of-truth surfaced via API).
- Throughput + SLO status: SRE throughput SLO evaluator summaries (or timeseries + computed rollups).
- Incidents: internal incident log + mapping to deployment_id (may be v1 manual).

Out of scope (v1):
- Customer-facing public SLO portal.
- Full contract text rendering in Console.
- Automated credit computation; only surface "credit issued" if recorded.

Acceptance criteria:
- A CS/Sales user can open Console -> Customer org -> Dedicated tab and see tier + committed throughput floor without additional tooling.
- A CS user can open a deployment and see last 15m/1h throughput vs floor and a simple last-7d/30d SLO status badge.
- UI contains clear metric units + a tooltip referencing the canonical throughput SLO definition.
- Link to the internal dashboard is pre-filtered by deployment_id and region.
- Access is restricted to internal roles (or feature flag) and audited.

Operational notes:
- This request is directly tied to recurring confusion in support tickets about streaming token accounting and which throughput numbers are "official". Ensure UI references the canonical metric and uses the post-fix streaming accounting (see related PR).

Suggested owner(s):
- Console UX + Observability: Sergio Costa / Allison Grant
- SRE for SLO semantics: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Product Dedicated for tier fields: Lauren Bishop

Business priority:
- P2: Needed for upcoming Dedicated tier + throughput SLO rollout enablement; reduce escalations and improve response times to customer questions.

References:
- Design work in progress: DES-771 (Dedicated tier UI), DES-784 (Throughput SLO status widget)
- Enablement asks coming from Sales thread requesting clearer guidance on what can be promised around burst vs committed throughput.
2025-02-21 (Rachel Kim): We’re seeing repeated escalations where AEs/CS can’t answer “what’s my committed throughput floor” without pulling SRE into a dashboard deep link. This needs to be visible in Console for internal users before we expand the SLO language rollout.
2025-02-24 (Sergio Costa): Acknowledged. We can reuse panels from observability-pack PR-842 for the visualizations, but we still need an API to fetch tier + committed floor (source-of-truth). Can Product confirm where this lives today (control plane vs billing metadata)?
2025-02-24 (Lauren Bishop): Tier + committed floor is defined at order form and then mirrored into deployment config during provisioning. Current canonical field is in control plane deployment metadata. We need to confirm naming and ensure it’s populated for legacy Dedicated deployments.
2025-02-25 (Sean Gallagher): Please ensure the Console badge uses the SLO evaluator summary (not raw tokens/sec) so we respect exclusions and measurement windows. Also: streaming accounting was recently fixed; only rely on metrics post PR-19422 for any computed views.
2025-02-26 (Allison Grant): We can provide a minimal “SLO status” API that returns compliance over 7d/30d with a short reason string for most-common failure modes (capacity saturation vs customer throttling vs model mismatch). Recommend keeping it internal-only until we validate customer interpretation.
2025-02-28 (Isabelle Laurent): Sales Ops request: please include an obvious “export/share” link for internal quoting context (not customer-shareable) that includes tier, region, shape, committed floor, and last-7d status. Even a copy-to-clipboard text block would help.
2025-03-03 (Sergio Costa): Proposed v1 UI: Dedicated tab on org page + a compact widget on deployment page. Feature flag: console.dedicated_slo_internal_view. Need backend endpoint for tier fields + SLO summary; tracking in eng board separately.
2025-03-06 (Rachel Kim): Confirmed CS leadership is OK with v1 being internal-only. Main goal is faster, consistent answers during procurement/security calls. Please prioritize tooltip wording so it matches the customer-facing SLO language once finalized.
payload.summary: Request: Console view for Dedicated tier + committed throughput floor + recent throughput SLO status (CS/Sales visibility)

Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a client-side compression change, reranking responses for some requests return near-zero scores and occasional 502/503s when the embeddings endpoint is called with compressed payloads. This manifests as silent suppression of top-k results (customer observes empty top-5) and tail latency increases (~200-400ms) leading to downstream timeouts.

Impact:
- Several production queries from QuokkaHealth return empty or low-quality rerank lists intermittently (estimated 2-5% of traffic).
- Customer-facing feature (related-document recommendation) degrades and triggers automated rollback on their side.
- Observed during business hours in us-west region; Dedicated cluster for customer affected.

Observed behaviour:
- When client sends embeddings compressed with the new zstd-lite wrapper, server accepts the request but reranker scores are suppressed (most distances collapse to ~0.0001) or the request fails with 502/503 downstream from reranker. Uncompressed payloads behave normally.

1) Use QuokkaHealth client build that applies zstd-lite wrapper to the embedding payload (header 'X-Embed-Compression: zstd-lite').
2) POST embeddings to /v1/embeddings with content-type application/octet-stream and compressed binary body matching their schema.
3) Call /v1/rerank with ids referencing the uploaded compressed-embeddings or single-request rerank that sends compressed embed vector in-line.
4) Observe returned rerank scores and HTTP status. Repeat across a small batch (10-50 requests) to reproduce non-deterministic failure rate.
[2026-03-10T15:24:03Z] embeddings-service: received payload (hdr: X-Embed-Compression=zstd-lite) size=12KB
[2026-03-10T15:24:03Z] embeddings-service: decompressed -> length=6144 floats
[2026-03-10T15:24:03Z] reranker: scoring start req=abc123 model=redwood-embed-v2-768
[2026-03-10T15:24:03Z] reranker: numeric check - any(isnan)=false, norm=2.3e-5 -> abnormal low norm
[2026-03-10T15:24:03Z] reranker: scores all < 0.0005 -> returning empty_topk
[2026-03-10T15:24:03Z] proxy: upstream response 502 from reranker shard 5

Initial hypothesis: client-side compression wrapper alters byte alignment or dtype packing resulting in tiny-magnitude floats after decompression.
Reproduced in staging with Quokka sample payloads using zstd-lite wrapper; unwrapped zstd decompress yields expected norms.
Binary diff of decompressed payload shows extra 2-byte header inserted by zstd-lite that client library doesn't strip; our embed deserializer treats header bytes as leading float values -> results in small values and collapsed norms.
Reranker code currently does not validate float-range nor checksum header; small norms flow through scoring and produce low similarity values instead of raising error.
502/503 observed when a shard attempted fast-path vectorized normalization and threw FP exception during AVX2 path on misaligned input (observed in logs as 'SIMD_ALIGNMENT_ERROR').
Ask QuokkaHealth to disable zstd-lite wrapper and send raw zstd-compressed payloads (or base64-encoded vectors) while we deploy a compatibility fix. Temporary customer-side rollback already performed by Quokka. On our side, can set a request inspector to reject X-Embed-Compression=zstd-lite with 400 and an explanatory message.
1) Add header validation and magic-byte detection in embeddings-service to reject or auto-strip zstd-lite 2-byte wrapper. 2) Add defensive checks in reranker: verify vector norm > 1e-3 and checksum; if below threshold, return 422 with diagnostic rather than silent low scores. 3) Add unit tests with misaligned inputs and enable additional logging for first 1k affected requests.
serving-runtime: add 'embed-compression' detector and stripper (PR #4123 already created)
reranker: add norm-check + clear error code path (PR pending)
PR 4123 merged to main (serving-runtime) - strips zstd-lite header in decompressor on canary hosts
reranker PR opened draft, awaiting review (author: mpatel)
In Progress - initial decompressor change merged to canary hosts; monitoring for regressions. Reranker defensive checks targeted for 2026-03-14 deploy.
Monitor canary for 12 hours and sample request norms and top-k distributions (dashboard: /dashboards/embeddings/compression-compat).
Coordinate with QuokkaHealth to validate behavior on their next deploy (PM runbook step 3).
Complete reranker PR and schedule infra window to roll to dedicated cluster if tests pass.
Follow-up doc: add 'embed-compression' compatibility section to onboarding checklist.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:30 - SRE Team: Canary deployed change (serving-runtime PR 4123). Observed initial reduction in 502s but some low-norm requests still logged; likely requires reranker checks.
2026-03-12 15:48 - QuokkaHealth (Customer): Confirmed that after instructing their client team to revert zstd-lite, product returned to normal. They would like notification when permanent fix is in production.
payload.summary: Embedding compression compatibility failure causing silent score suppression and intermittent 5xxs

Issue summary:
HR intake created a new hire (FT-2026-03-09) using the standard onboarding template. Two automated workers then processed the request: the Onboarder job (HR -> PeopleOps) and the Provisioner job (platform-automation). They created overlapping artifacts:

- Two service accounts were auto-created in the platform namespace: platform-sa-maria.1 and platform-sa-maria.2. The duplication caused the CI job that binds team roles to fail intermittently.
- Desk allocation in the facilities system was assigned to two locations (SFO-Desk-122 and SFO-Desk-141) due to a stale mapping between HR template 'preferred_desk' value and facilities sync. Facilities then created a desk reservation for both ids.

Impact:
- Onboarding blocked: engineering onboarding checklist prevented finalizing access because the provisioning audit detected duplicate service accounts.
- CI flakes: new hire could not run initial onboarding pipelines for first-day tasks until manual cleanup.
- Facilities confusion: two desks reserved for same start date causing manager frustration.

Background:
We recently updated the HR onboarding template field names in PeopleOps to consolidate 'workspace_preference' and 'preferred_desk' into a single 'desk_choice' attribute to support hoteling. The platform Provisioner still reads the older 'preferred_desk' key. The Onboarder job was updated at 2026-03-01 but rollout to the automation fleet was staggered; some runners still process an older template.

Steps observed / reproduction notes:
1) HR creates hire record for Maria Lopez on 2026-03-09 using the new consolidated template.
2) Onboarder job (older runner) triggers and creates service account platform-sa-maria.1 and posts a facilities reservation for SFO-Desk-122.
3) Provisioner job (new runner) triggers later and reads the new field, creates platform-sa-maria.2 and posts SFO-Desk-141 reservation.
1) Create hire with mixed-field template (include both 'desk_choice' and simulate legacy 'preferred_desk'). 2) Trigger both old and new onboarding runners (or simulate race) 3) Observe duplicate service accounts created in IAM and two desk reservations in facilities.
Checked PeopleOps template change log: 'desk_choice' introduced 2026-02-28, migration flagged 'preferred_desk' deprecated but still readable.
Provisioner log (2026-03-09T10:14Z): processed payload with 'desk_choice': 'SFO-Desk-141' and created platform-sa-maria.2; no idempotency key present.
Onboarder runner (older image) log (2026-03-09T10:11Z): processed payload with 'preferred_desk': 'SFO-Desk-122' and created platform-sa-maria.1.
IAM audit shows both accounts created within 3 minutes of each other. No automated cleanup job ran because deletion guard requires source to be marked 'reconciled'.
Facilities API: two active reservations exist for same employee start date; facilities UI allowed duplicate reservations from different sync ids.
No existing linked issue about template migration rollout was raised to automation-ops prior to the incident.
Maya Chen (reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed hire couldn't finish onboarding; blocked on access. Please advise whether PeopleOps should revert template or if platform should tolerate both keys.
Evan Brooks (assignee) 2026-03-10: Assigned for triage. Reproduced locally by replaying payloads. Root cause appears to be lack of idempotency and field-name drift between runners. Will propose immediate mitigation.
Priya Kapoor (Infra) 2026-03-11: Suggest adding an idempotency_key tied to hire_id when creating service accounts. Also recommend Facilities add a uniqueness constraint for reservations with overlapping dates.
SRE team lead (Zach Turner) 2026-03-11: Note that provisioning runners are on a staged rollout; ops should pause newer runners until all are upgraded or run-time compatibility shim added.
Maya Chen 2026-03-12: HR would prefer not to revert PeopleOps changes if a compatibility shim can be deployed quickly. HR asks for a documented policy about who owns service-account creation moving forward.
Pending policy decision. Interim mitigation applied: 1) Rolled back new Provisioner runners for the 2 affected fleet shards to stop duplicate creations. 2) Runbook step added: manual reconciliation script to merge duplicate service accounts and cancel duplicate facilities reservations for the affected hires. 3) Added idempotency_key prototype to platform-sa creation endpoint; still needs PR review and rollout.
Create a formal policy doc: single owner for service-account lifecycle (PeopleOps vs Platform).
Enforce idempotency on service-account creation endpoints (deploy PR 812 to canary after review).
Add uniqueness constraint to Facilities reservation service for same-employee/start-date.
Run a one-week audit of onboarded hires to detect any other duplicates and reconcile.
Schedule a cross-team postmortem discussion: PeopleOps, Provisioner, Onboarder, Facilities, and SRE.
payload.summary: Onboarding template desync: duplicate service-account creation and conflicting desk assignment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Acme AI (Dedicated) reports intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes on chat completions during peak traffic windows. Spikes are large enough to cause upstream request timeouts in their app. Customer requests clearer, actionable saturation context for Dedicated pools (GPU/queue/KV cache pressure) and faster escalation guidance.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency spikes (p95 up to ~4–8s; p99 >10s reported by customer) for ~20–40 minute windows.
- Increased retry traffic observed from customer (amplifies load).
- No sustained elevated 5xx; primary symptom is latency + occasional streaming stalls.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment in prod, us-east
- Pool: acme-ai-dedicated-us-east-1
- Models: llama-3-70b-instruct, qwen2.5-72b-instruct
- Request pattern: high concurrency, mix of 1–4k prompt tokens, 200–800 output tokens; streaming enabled for most traffic

Customer report (from CS call / email excerpts):
- "Everything is fine most of the day, but when we hit our morning peak we get sudden latency cliffs for 20–30 minutes. We can’t tell if it’s GPU saturation, queueing, or a bad rollout."
- "We need to know what to look at during an incident: is it capacity, batching, or routing?"

Initial hypothesis:
Likely saturation/queueing in Dedicated scheduler (admission control/backpressure) and/or KV cache pressure causing effective throughput collapse under long-context + high concurrency.

Gaps:
We do not currently surface a consistent 'saturation context' bundle for Dedicated pools in support workflows. The on-call investigation required ad-hoc dashboard hunting and manual correlation. This ticket tracks both the immediate incident handling and the follow-up requirement to standardize saturation signals + incident-bot context cards for Dedicated incidents.

Additional notes:
Resolved.
What we did:
- Confirmed issue localized to Acme AI Dedicated pool in us-east.
- Observed scheduler queue depth/backpressure spikes correlating with reported latency cliffs; GPU util alone was not a reliable indicator.
- Applied temporary pool-level queue limit / guardrail to cap queueing delay and stabilize p95/p99 latency during peak.
Customer outcome:
- Customer reported immediate improvement and fewer upstream timeouts after guardrail change.
Follow-ups (tracked elsewhere):
- Standardize saturation signals for Dedicated pools (GPU util + queue depth + admission control/backpressure + KV cache pressure where available) and ensure there is a single support-friendly dashboard.
- Add/expand incident-bot v2 saturation context card to include Dedicated pool saturation snapshot + deep links (references: incident-bot diagnostics v2 design).
Notes:
- This ticket highlights the operational gap: support + on-call lacked a consistent, tenant-safe saturation context bundle. Investigation required ad-hoc correlation and manual dashboard navigation.
payload.summary: Dedicated: latency spikes during peak traffic; needs standardized saturation context (GPU/queue/KV) for faster triage

Issue summary:
Several corporate developer laptops started reporting fan RPM as 0 in telemetry and have experienced thermal throttling or unexpected shutdowns after the March 8th BIOS firmware push. Affected devices are primarily Lenovo ThinkPad fleet that received the v1.2.3 BIOS rollback/upgrade during nightly autopilot/intune maintenance window.

Impact:
- Multiple engineers reported sudden shutdowns while compiling or running local model-serving containers.
- Telemetry shows CPU package temps > 95C and fan RPM 0 prior to shutdown.
- A subset of devices are recoverable by power-cycling; others require manual reseating of fan cable or BIOS re-flash.

Environment:
- corp-laptop | us-west region endpoints registered in Intune
- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise 22H2 with latest cumulative updates
- Endpoint management: Intune + Autopilot + custom vendor BIOS automation job

1) Receive BIOS v1.2.3 via vendor auto-upgrade orchestrated through Intune.
2) Reboot as prompted to apply BIOS update.
3) Boot to Windows, run synthetic CPU load (e.g., Prime95 or compile job).
4) Observe fan telemetry via Company Telemetry Agent and Windows thermal events.

- Company Telemetry Agent: fan_rpm=0, cpu_package_temp=98C, thermal_event=critical at 2026-03-09T02:14:33Z
- Windows Event Log: Kernel-Power ID 41 at 2026-03-09T02:14:34Z
- Intune device action log: BIOS update completed for machine GUID abcd-1234 at 2026-03-09T01:58:10Z
- Vendor BIOS logs (where available): FW_UPDATE_OK, but fan controller init returned error code 0xA5 on devices 1002,1007

- First triage (03/09): Confirmed correlation between install window and spike in thermal incidents. Many affected devices show firmware v1.2.3.
- Hypothesis A: BIOS v1.2.3 has a regression in fan controller initialization causing the embedded controller (EC) to not spin fans under Windows ACPI calls.
- Hypothesis B: The vendor packaging script accidentally toggled an EC config bit during provisioning job causing fans to be disabled until manual EC reset.
- Collected devices into secure bench. On two devices reseating fan connector returned fan RPM to normal; on three devices re-flashing BIOS v1.2.1 (previous) restored expected behavior.
- Telemetry team confirmed gradients: pre-update fan RPMs normal; immediately post-update many report 0.
- Cross-referenced with vendor forum: single report from partner company with similar symptoms after same BIOS build.
- Escalated to vendor support (case# VEND-7782) and Eng for triage. Created blocked test matrix for imaging pipeline to exclude BIOS v1.2.3 until vendor confirms fix.

- Instruct impacted users to power cycle and avoid heavy CPU loads.
- For machines on-site: MCS bench will reseat fan connector and re-flash BIOS back to v1.2.1 where possible.
- Disable automatic BIOS rollout job in Intune for the vendor SKU until vendor patch is validated.
- Adjust monitoring alert thresholds to detect sudden rise in 'fan_rpm==0' counts and proactively quarantine devices from build pools.

- 2026-03-12: Vendor released BIOS v1.2.4 marked as hotfix addressing EC fan init regression (vendor case VEND-7782).
- Validation: Bench devices re-flashed to v1.2.4 show normal fan RPM under synthetic load; telemetry returns to baseline.
- Deployment plan: Staged rollout to remaining fleet with canary of 20 devices, monitoring for 48 hours, then roll to broader population.
- Follow-ups: Update runbook for BIOS vendor rollouts to include post-update fan sanity check, add pre-flight canary for firmware jobs, and add an automated rollback tag for updates that trigger >=3 thermal events within 1 hour.
payload.summary: Workstation experiencing thermal shutdowns and 0 RPM fan telemetry after BIOS firmware rollout

Issue summary: After a recent HR-driven department rename (Growth -> Go-To-Market) users in the renamed department are not receiving their console roles when their Okta profile is re-provisioned. Impact: 18 employees report 'No roles assigned' on the internal console and cannot access internal dashboards and feature flags. This blocks a small number of support and infra tasks for the GTM org. Environment: Production; SCIM provisioner v2.3.1; Okta org: redwood-prod.okta.com. Expected behavior: When Okta department attribute changes and SCIM reprovisions the user, RBAC role mappings should be applied to the console account automatically. Observed behavior: SCIM create/update completes but resulting user in console has no group memberships mapped; audit log shows mismatch between Okta attribute value and our expected normalization rules.
1) In Okta admin, change a user's 'department' attribute from 'Growth' to 'Go-To-Market'
2) Trigger SCIM provisioning push (Okta > SCIM > push) or wait for scheduled sync
3) Observe the user row in Console > Admin > Users; expected RBAC group membership is missing
4) Attempt login: user authenticates via SSO but Console shows 'No roles assigned' and denies access to protected routes
2026-03-10T08:14:23Z scim-provisioner INFO user_update user=marina.lopez@redwood.com dept=Go-To-Market mapped_dept=go-to-market
2026-03-10T08:14:24Z scim-provisioner WARN mapping_failed user=marina.lopez@redwood.com reason=normalization_mismatch expected='growth' actual='go-to-market'
Console audit: user_create/modify id=U-98432 status=ok roles_assigned=[]
Okta system log event: application.user_update timestamp=2026-03-10T08:14:22Z
Marina Lopez (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed this first thing after HR renamed the department. Several GTM hires are blocked from submitting deploy requests.
Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged; collected logs and asked for list of affected users. Escalating to Identity team.
Devon Patel (Assignee) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally. SCIM mapping layer lowercases and strips punctuation, our RBAC rules expect legacy short name 'growth' which doesn't match 'go-to-market' after normalization. Hypothesis: mapping table needs alias entries or a normalization rule change.
SRE (Tom Reynolds) 2026-03-11: Confirmed no errors in token exchange; this looks strictly mapping/transform related. Added temporary feature flag to bypass strict-match check for department->role mapping in provisioning service.
Identity (Priya Menon) 2026-03-12: Ran one-time backfill script to map legacy 'growth' alias to 'go-to-market' for affected users as temporary mitigation. Will follow up with PR to extend alias table.
SCIM provisioning logs show update events but role assignment pipeline returns empty group list when normalized department value != expected key
Normalization pipeline: lowercase -> remove punctuation -> collapse spaces. 'Go-To-Market' -> 'go-to-market' but RBAC rules use 'growth' (legacy) -> mismatch
Workaround applied: one-time backfill mapped 18 users to the correct role in Console DB; users regained access around 2026-03-12 09:20Z
Root cause: HR migration renamed dept without creating alias mapping in our identity normalization table; provisioning assumes canonical keys without consulting alias mapping service
Risk: Future renames will repeat unless we implement alias resolution or make role mapping resilient to normalized synonyms
TBD - temporary backfill applied to restore access. Engineering to land PR that adds alias mapping and a normalization-tolerant lookup in the SCIM provisioner (tracking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/482). Post-deploy runbook to add aliases for any HR-driven department rename. Planned rollout: patch to provisioner in next maintenance window, followed by audit to ensure no additional users are affected.
payload.summary: Okta attribute normalization mismatch prevents new console role provisioning after department rename
