Issue summary:
A scheduled secret rotation job failed during the weekly rotation window for two private-deploy customers (prod us-east) after a recent onboarding. Investigation shows the k8s operator's cross-cloud identity normalizer is mapping two distinct cloud service identities to the same internal service-account display name. This produced a name collision in our secret-store key naming and caused the rotation job to overwrite metadata unexpectedly, resulting in stale image-pull credentials on several GKE/eks nodes.

Impact:
- Two private deployments observed 503s and repeated image-pull failures for inference pods between 2026-03-09 01:12 UTC and 2026-03-10 04:50 UTC.
- Customer-facing inference endpoints degraded; autoscaling created new pods that could not start because the node-level image pull failed with permission errors.
- Secret rotation job reported success but new secrets were not applied to node service accounts.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) in prod us-east (customer tenant IDs masked).
- Kubernetes distributions affected: GKE (private cluster) and EKS nodes in customer-dedicated VPC peering.
- Components involved: k8s-operator v2.3.1, crosscloud-identity-normalizer v1.7.0, secret-rotation-runner v4.0.

Steps to reproduce (summary):
1) Create two distinct cloud identities in different cloud accounts with identical display names (e.g., "redwood-llm-worker-sa").
2) Run the onboarding sync that populates the identity index used by the normalizer.
3) Trigger the secret-rotation-runner for the tenant namespace.
4) Observe that the rotation job writes a single secret key corresponding to the normalized display name and clears previous per-account metadata.

Observed behavior:
- Rotation job logs show success but emitted secret resource points to the wrong cloud identity metadata (account ID mismatched).
- Kubernetes pods fail imagePull with errors referencing unauthorized: "Denied: iam.serviceAccount.get denied" and container runtime logs show pull failure for private registry because image-pull-secret metadata didn't map to the correct KMS-wrapped key.

Expected behavior:
- Normalizer must preserve unique identity namespace (account/project prefix) in secret key generation so different cloud accounts cannot collide on display-name alone.
- Secret rotation should update the correct account-bound image-pull secret and annotate nodes/pods accordingly so kubelet pulls succeed.

Relevant logs / excerpts:
- secret-rotation-runner: "INFO 2026-03-09T01:14:03Z rotation complete: tenant=redacted namespace=ns-abc key=sa-redwood-llm-worker-displayname"
- k8s-operator: "WARN 2026-03-09T01:14:04Z detected display-name collision: normalized_key=sa-redwood-llm-worker-displayname accounts=[acct-111, acct-222]"
- kubelet/containerd: "rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to pull and unpack image \"our-registry/redwood-inference:prod-20260308\": failed to resolve reference: denied: Permission denied (iam.serviceAccounts.get)"

Attachments:
- links to rotation job logs and anonymized kubelet logs were uploaded to the ticket thread and to the private S3 bucket (s3://redwood-support/anonymized/INT-902345/).
1) Onboard two cloud identities in different provider accounts but set identical display names. 2) Run identity sync. 3) Trigger secret-rotation-runner for tenant namespace. 4) Inspect secret-store keys and node annotations for account mismatch.
k8s-operator WARN: detected display-name collision: normalized_key=sa-redwood-llm-worker-displayname accounts=[acct-111, acct-222]
secret-rotation-runner INFO: rotation complete but metadata.account_id=acct-111 when kubelet expected acct-222
kubelet ERROR: failed to pull image: denied: iam.serviceAccounts.get
Initial hypothesis: crosscloud normalizer strips account/project prefix when generating stable keys; recent change in v1.7.0 introduced a regression that prefers display-name deduping across accounts.
What we did so far:
- Replayed onboarding sync in staging with two test accounts and confirmed collision reproduces.
- Confirmed secret-rotation-runner considers only 'normalized_key' when writing secrets and overwrites per-account metadata.
- Verified KMS ciphertexts differ per account; rotation job wrote the ciphertext for acct-111 into the key used by acct-222's pods.
- Temporary mitigation: rolled back crosscloud-identity-normalizer to v1.6.4 for affected clusters; this restored per-account key naming and allowed re-run of rotation which fixed image pull for one tenant.
Open questions:
- Need to confirm if any downstream caches (console token-level breakdowns, on-host secret caches) require invalidation after fix.
- Confirm whether Dedicated provisioning paths also used same normalizer; preliminary scan shows dedicated provisioner uses the same library in onboarding flow.

Next steps planned:
- Patch normalizer to include account/project prefix in generated secret keys (PR in progress).
- Run canary rollout of patched normalizer to one affected prod private-deploy cluster and re-run rotation.
- Create a test asserting collisions are flagged and rotation job fails safe (no overwrite) until manual reconciliation.
- Coordinate with Ops to invalidate node-level secret caches where necessary.
Aisha Patel (reporter) 2026-03-10: Added initial logs and two anonymized kubelet traces. Customer CS alerted us to repeated 503s; internal SLAs triggered immediate escalation.
Marco Rivera (assignee) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally in staging by creating two GCP service accounts with identical display names. Confirmed rotation writes single key. Rolling back normalizer to v1.6.4 in one cluster restored behavior. Will prepare patch to include account prefix in normalization.
SRE Team (channel #support) 2026-03-11: Applied rollback to two prod private clusters (tenant redacted). Nodes re-registered; some pods still failed until rotation rerun — coordinated with k8s-operator to trigger reapply. Noted that dedicated provisioning may be impacted; we scheduled a scan across dedicated queues.
Security (2026-03-12): Confirmed that no KMS keys were exposed; ciphertexts are distinct. We recommend auditing any automated cleanup that might have removed old secrets during overwrite window.
Marco Rivera 2026-03-13: Opened PR github.com/redwood/k8s-operator/pull/772 to change normalization behavior and added a unit test for collision detection. Will schedule canary for 2026-03-14.
CS (2026-03-13): Customer notified of partial mitigation and ETA for full fix and canary rollout. SLA workaround documented and shared.
Operations (2026-03-13): Flagged follow-up task to scan private-deploy clusters for other potential display-name duplicates and to patch onboarding sync to validate uniqueness constraints before accepting identities.
Mitigation applied: rolled back normalizer to v1.6.4 in affected clusters to stop overwrites and re-ran secret rotation for impacted tenants. Patch PR available (github.com/redwood/k8s-operator/pull/772) to include account/project prefix in normalized keys and to fail-fast on collisions. Awaiting canary rollout and verification. Post-deploy actions: run full scan of private-deploy tenant identities, add unit/integration tests to onboarding pipeline, and create rollback playbook for future rotation runs.
payload.summary: Service account display-name collision blocks automated secret-rotation and prevents node image pulls in private deploy

Issue summary: During the scheduled nightly Okta group membership sync (critical path for IAM grants) a delay between the IdP and our group-sync agent caused cached group membership to expire. The ephemeral release service-account (release-sa@redwood) lost Kubernetes RoleBindings that grant it permission to register and annotate ephemeral CI runners. Impact: several nightly release jobs failed to provision runners and ongoing canary rollouts stalled. User-facing impact limited to internal release cadence (no customer-facing downtime), but this blocked automated canary promotion and caused a manual release delay of ~90 minutes.

Observed: At 02:15 UTC the group-sync agent logged repeated 5xx responses from the Okta API and subsequently dropped group membership for the release-sa. The k8s-operator reconciler attempted to register runners but was rejected with "forbidden: user not bound to role" errors. The Okta primary certificate was rotated earlier in the night by IdP team; agent retried but backoff and local TTLs expired before membership was refreshed.

02:10 UTC - Release automation began provisioning 12 runners for canary. Initial requests succeeded.
02:12 UTC - Okta rotated cert; IdP responses intermittently returned 502/504 for ~12m. Group-sync logged 502s and incremented local miss counters.
02:18 UTC - Local cache TTL for group membership (configured 10m) expired; group-sync returned empty membership for release-sa and updated k8s RBAC records removing rolebindings.
02:21 UTC - k8s-operator attempted to create runner pods; API returned 403 'user not bound to role' from admission webhook. Pod creation failed and pipeline stalled.
02:30 UTC - Manually re-applied RoleBinding as emergency workaround to restore release-sa permissions; first pipelines resumed provisioning at ~02:45 UTC.
Hypothesis: brittle cache TTL + aggressive cache invalidation policy combined with Okta transient errors. Agent should be resilient to temporary IdP flakiness and avoid removing rolebindings until a confirmed membership change is observed across retries.
Logs: included snippets from group-sync agent, k8s-operator admission webhook, and runner-service error traces (archived to S3: s3://redwood-support/INT-863274/logs/)
Cross-reference: IdP rotation event logged by security-idp channel #idp-rotations-2026-03-10 at 02:11 UTC
Manually re-applied RoleBinding for release-sa and disabled automatic rolebinding prune in group-sync agent config (set prune=false) to allow pipelines to finish. This is a temporary safe-open setting until we deploy a fix. Manual rollout required for two affected clusters in us-east-1.
Partial mitigation applied 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC (manual RoleBinding re-apply + temporary prune disable). Engineering patch PR created to modify group-sync behavior: (1) increase membership confirmation window to 5 consecutive negative checks over 30m before pruning, (2) add exponential backoff and circuit breaker on IdP 5xx errors, (3) add automated retry that preserves current rolebindings during transient IdP failures. Patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/452. Planned rollout to prod 2026-03-13 04:00 UTC after smoke tests in staging. Postmortem owners: Marcus Nguyen (lead), Priya Shah (idp). Follow-ups: update runbook to include immediate step to re-apply RoleBinding and a new alert when group-sync experiences >5m continuous 5xx from IdP.
Ava Patel (Reporter) - 2026-03-10 03:05: 'Filed ticket after manual unblock. We should treat any IdP 5xx window as tolerated for rolebindings; removing privileges is too aggressive.'
Marcus Nguyen (Assignee) - 2026-03-10 04:12: 'Confirmed logs. Re-applied RoleBinding and set prune=false. I'll open patch PR to change confirmation window and backoff. Need IdP team to share rotation schedule.'
Priya Shah (IdP) - 2026-03-10 06:21: 'We rolled the cert at 02:11 UTC and saw a spike in 502s from the edge due to staged propagation in our CDN. We'll provide a post-rotation health-check hook next time.'
SRE Pager - 2026-03-10 07:00: 'Alert threshold created: group-sync >5m continuous 5xx -> P1. Adding runbook snippet for manual rebind.'
Marcus Nguyen - 2026-03-12 09:30: 'PR merged to staging, smoke test passed. Scheduling prod rollout 2026-03-13 04:00 UTC with pre/post checks. Closing manual prune override after rollout.'
payload.summary: Okta group-sync delay removes runner roleBindings for release service-account during nightly rollout

Purpose: correlate spikes in token consumption with network anomalies and routing fallbacks to determine whether invoiced usage map to legitimate inference activity.

Requirements: extract must be minimized to only the time window and fields needed, stored in an encrypted temporary bucket, and accessible to a limited set of approvers. Redaction rules must be applied prior to delivery: redact client IPs to /24, hash any customer-provided prompt text, and preserve request_id and model_id for correlation.

Time window: 2026-02-28T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-03T23:59:59Z.
Client IPs: truncate to /24. Prompts/payloads: replace with SHA256 of original + keep length metadata. PII fields: remove any headers matching 'x-customer-*' except x-customer-id (hash). Attach redaction script and verification checksum in S3 manifest.

Issue summary:
A delegated access request for console elevation is stuck in the approval workflow for multiple engineers after an Okta group merge. The approval UI shows 'Pending - waiting for approver' even though required approvers are listed and have approved. This prevents engineers from obtaining temporary elevated roles to access production dashboards and runbooks.

Impact:
- 6 engineers are blocked from elevating to a support role across multiple teams (SRE, Platform).
- On-call rotation had to manually escalate via Slack and temporary token sharing, increasing operational risk.
- No customer-facing outages, but internal response time for incidents increased.

Environment:
- Production (us-east)
- Affected service: approval-microservice v1.3.2, rbac-service v2.0.1, okta-scim-sync job (daily)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a delegated access request via Console -> Access -> Request Elevation (select 'support-engineer' role).
2) Add approvers from two different teams (team leads who are members of Okta groups).
3) Confirm approvals in the Console UI. Approver shows as confirmed but request remains Pending.

Observed behavior:
- UI shows approver checkboxes checked and timestamps on approver actions, but the request state is still 'Pending' and no role assignment is created in RBAC service.
- approval-microservice logs contain repeated errors of parent-role lookup failures: "parent role id lookup returned null for role_id=role-1243"
- Okta SCIM sync shows a recent group merge event at 2026-03-09 23:05 UTC (group A merged into group B).

Expected behavior:
- After required approvers approve, the request transitions to 'Approved' and rbac-service issues the temporary role assignment with TTL for the requester.

Relevant logs and links:
- approval-microservice error sample:
  2026-03-11T02:12:45Z ERROR approval: failed to compute approval cascade: null parent for role=role-1243 request_id=REQ-20260311-132
- Okta SCIM sync job trace: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/okta-sync/5678
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0ABCDEF1/p1678550400000500
- Related infra PR (applied partially): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4321

Temporary workaround:
- Support engineers with admin privileges performed a manual role assignment in rbac-service for affected users. This restores access but bypasses the normal approval audit trail.

Next steps planned:
1) Investigate why parent-role lookup returned null after Okta group merge. Hypothesis: role inheritance cache references an Okta group ID that was deleted during the merge and the approval-microservice does not handle a missing parent gracefully.
2) Re-run a scoped role-propagation job to rebuild role lineage cache for the merged groups.
3) Patch approval-microservice to treat missing parent references as soft-missing and surface a clearer error + auto-retry path.
4) Add monitoring/alerting on approval-failure rates and parent-lookup errors.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:02 - Security (Nina Roberts): Raised concern about manual role assignments bypassing audit trail. Requested a follow-up to capture approval metadata for manually-assigned cases.
2026-03-11: Hypothesis A - Okta group merge removed a group id referenced by role parent_id in RBAC DB. approval-microservice code assumes parent exists and throws, which prevents marking completed approvals.
2026-03-11: Hypothesis B - SCIM sync applied deletions in the wrong order during merge leading to transient dangling references (observed SCIM events: 'group.delete' followed by 'group.update').
2026-03-11: DB check - rbac.role_hierarchy shows role-1243.parent_id referencing okta-group-983 which is absent from okta_group mapping table. Evidence: SELECT * FROM okta_group WHERE id='okta-group-983' returned 0 rows.
2026-03-11: Reproduction - Replaying the merge event on staging with a copy of org metadata reproduced the parent lookup error. Approval microservice log trace identical.
In progress: Scoped role-propagation rebuild executed for the support role namespace which auto-cleared the majority of stuck requests. A code patch to approval-microservice has been created to handle missing parent references without failing the entire evaluation path (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/approval-microservice/pull/102). Follow-ups: add metric approval.parent_lookup_null, alert at threshold, and add an automated recovery job that re-evaluates stuck requests daily. Planning a postmortem after full rollout to cover changes to SCIM merge ordering and add a playbook for manual recovery.
2026-03-11: Rolled a temporary role-propagation job (job id rp-20260311-01) for affected namespace; transitioned 4/6 stuck requests to Approved.
2026-03-12: Deployed approval-microservice patch to prod canary (10% traffic) — no new parent_lookup_null errors observed in 24h window on canary nodes.
Follow-up action: Identity to add a pre-merge validation step in okta-scim-sync to ensure role mappings have graceful fallback values. Timeline: 2 weeks.

comments: Aisha Malik: Reported after 7 devices failed post-repair provisioning this morning. Captured Intune correlation IDs and inventory mismatches. Raised to SRE for network evidence.
Ethan Chen: Running controlled repro with 2 devices. Confirmed MAC flip when dock firmware v1.04 is applied. Temporarily pulled firmware bundle from depot staging. Placed hold with techops.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
When devices are re-docked after depot repair (battery replacement + firmware refresh on Thunderbolt dock), the dock-assigned Ethernet MAC changes to a locally administered OUI. The new MAC breaks certificate-based SSO binding (device certificate is bound to inventory MAC), which causes the device to fail the final stages of provisioning and land in a provisioning loop (Intune/SSO handshake fails, device marked non-compliant).

Impact:
- ~18 devices processed through depot in the last 48 hours are failing post-repair provisioning at the corporate NYC docking stations.
- Affected users cannot complete SSO login or access corporate resources until reprovisioning or manual MAC override.
- Potential audit/compliance risk if devices are marked non-compliant.

Environment:
- Prod docking racks at NYC office (us-east).
- Dock model: Dell TB18D with firmware v1.04 applied by depot technician.
- Host models: Dell Latitude 7430 (Windows 11 22H2 with corporate image).
- Provisioning flow: SCCM -> Intune autopilot staged -> cert enrollment via SCEP -> SSO cert binding to MAC in asset inventory.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Depot performs battery replacement + applies latest dock firmware from vendor package (v1.04).
2) Device returned, user docks at corporate station and boots.
3) Device starts provisioning; Intune enrollment initiated.
4) Certificate enrollment fails with mismatch; backend compares MAC in asset inventory vs MAC presented by NIC.
5) Device fails SSO binding and retries provisioning, eventually flagged non-compliant.

Observed logs & evidence:
- Intune enrollment logs: "CertificateBindingError: MAC_Mismatch" (correlation id: 0a3b-7c9f).
- Asset DB entry (pre-repair): mac=00:1A:4B:12:34:56, post-dock log on host: mac=02:5E:AC:77:11:22 (locally administered bit set).
- Windows event viewer: AAD SCEP enrollment error 0x80070005 at 10:12:23.
- USB/Thunderbolt vendor diag from depot: dock firmware v1.04 applied successfully; no errors in vendor tool.
- Packet capture from docking switch shows link up with new MAC; switch port learned 02:5E:AC:77:11:22.
Initial hypothesis: dock firmware change is enabling MAC randomization or overriding host NIC MAC with a locally administered address.
- Confirmed via walk-up test: re-dock a known device with previous MAC bound certificate; observed MAC flip once dock firmware is applied.
- Verified asset inventory still records host NIC MAC (pre-repair) which no longer matches observed MAC when dock is connected.
- Checked vendor release notes for TB18D v1.04: mentions 'improved NIC failover' but no explicit MAC randomization note.
- Tested with another dock (v1.02) — MAC preserved; with v1.04, MAC changes consistently.
- Cross-referenced with INT-41256 (duplicate-dock-mac-enum-loop) — similar symptoms but different root cause (driver binding vs firmware override).

Temporary workaround tried:
- Manual MAC override in OS using netsh/PowerShell on host restores expected MAC and allows cert binding to complete. Not scalable for depot-returned fleet.
- Replacing dock with older firmware unit (v1.02) allows provisioning to proceed.

Next steps:
- Coordinate with depot to halt automated TB18D firmware push for now.
- Engage vendor support (Dell) with packet captures, vendor diag output, and example device IDs.
- Add an automated verification step in depot checklist to validate persistent MAC post-repair.
- Create an Intune detection rule to flag locally administered MAC addresses during enrollment as a pre-emptive block.

Additional notes:
SRE - Priya Rao (2026-03-11): Collected switch CAM table, confirmed that MAC presented is locally administered (LSB of first octet = 1). We should treat this as firmware-induced override. Logged case with Dell ESCALATION ID: DELL-ESC-44321.
Depot - Marcus Li (2026-03-11): We pushed firmware as part of the 'dock refresh' workflow. Will stop the firmware step and quarantine affected docks for vendor return. Added a checkbox to the depot runbook to validate NIC MAC persistence.
Security - Lina Gomez (2026-03-12): Flagged as compliance risk. Recommend we block devices with locally administered MACs from auto-enrolling until resolved.
Workaround implemented: Depot halted automatic TB18D firmware pushes and replaced returned docks with known-good units (v1.02) for affected devices. Added temporary Intune enrollment detection to block locally administered MACs and route to manual remediation.
Permanent actions planned:
- Dell provided firmware reproducer and confirmed regression; vendor to issue hotfix or rollback guidance (ESCALATION DELL-ESC-44321).
- Update depot SOP to include 'verify host NIC MAC persistence' as a required step post-repair.
- Implement automation in the depot QA script to run netsh and compare MAC against asset DB before returning device.
- Create KB for helpdesk: steps for manual MAC override and when to escalate to hardware vendor.
Current status:
- Affected docks quarantined; 12 devices reprovisioned using replaced docks; user-facing impact reduced. Awaiting vendor firmware fix.
payload.summary: Thunderbolt dock firmware update resets Ethernet MAC causing SSO certificate bind failure and provisioning loop

Issue summary:
A traveler (E. Kaur) submitted an expense settlement for a €2,300 travel advance. The reimbursement processed shows a settled amount that differs by €17.40 after the payments system converted currencies and applied bank fees.

Impact:
- Employee has an outstanding balance that prevents closure of the travel advance.
- Finance cannot reconcile the ledger for Q1 until the variance is explained.

Environment:
- Expense platform: Redwood Expenses (prod)
- Payment rail: BankWire EU (partner bank)
- Region: eu-west

Initial evidence:
- Original advance issued: 2026-01-15, amount: EUR 2,300, PO/advance ID ADV-2026-8975
- Settlement submitted: 2026-02-20, itemized receipts in EUR and GBP (airport transfer paid in GBP).
- Payment recorded in ledger: EUR 2,282.60 (difference EUR 17.40).

Desired outcome:
- Identify source of EUR 17.40 variance (FX rounding, bank fee, reimbursement policy).
- Post corrective entry or issue supplemental payment to employee if required.

Notes on scope:
- This is internal support (no external customers). Ledger and AP integrity required for month-end close.
1) Locate advance ADV-2026-8975 in Redwood Expenses console
2) Open settlement submission dated 2026-02-20 and export receipts and line items
3) Review AP payment record and bank transaction for the corresponding payout date
4) Compare per-line conversions (GBP->EUR) and any applied fees recorded by the payment provider
5) Check GL posting for rounding or FX adjustment entries during settlement batch processing
Expense export CSV (attached to ticket) shows net reimbursable EUR 2,300 before per-diem adjustments
AP payment trace ID: PW-32918-BNK shows outbound amount EUR 2,282.60 and bank reference 'BKFEE 1.75 GBP'
Bank payout CSV row: 2026-02-24, beneficiary E. Kaur, amount 2,282.60 EUR, fees 15.20 EUR (converted)
2026-03-01 10:12 - Finance ops: Confirmed settlement includes a GBP transaction (airport transfer) that was converted by the payment provider. Provider returns their own FX conversion and fee column.
2026-03-01 14:05 - Payments team: Provider CSV shows two separate entries for same payout: gross EUR 2,300, fees 15.20 EUR, net EUR 2,284.80. AP ledger shows EUR 2,282.60; discrepancy of EUR 2.20 identified between provider net and ledger net.
Hypothesis A: Double rounding when converting GBP receipt and then reconverting to EUR for ledger posting.
Hypothesis B: Manual adjustment applied by AP clerk to correct previous small rounding, not documented in settlement notes.
    Hypothesis C: Interbank fee of ~EUR 2.20 applied by correspondent bank and not reflected in provider CSV.
2026-03-01 11:00 - Maya Chen (Finance) - Added exported receipts and provider CSV. Asked Payments team to validate provider FX math.
2026-03-01 15:20 - Alex Rivera (Payments) - I pulled the provider raw feed; they report net EUR 2,284.80. Will escalate to bank partner for correspondent fee breakdown.
2026-03-02 09:30 - Liam Patel (Assignee) - Reviewing GL posting scripts for batch 2026-02-24. Found a rounding helper that truncates to 2 decimal places at different steps. Possible source of EUR 2.20. Will run repro in staging with same inputs.
2026-03-02 17:45 - Priya Nair (AP) - Confirm no manual adjustments recorded on ADV-2026-8975. If bank partner confirms no extra fee, we may need to correct ledger entry and issue EUR 17.40 supplemental payment.
2026-03-03 08:10 - Alex Rivera (Payments) - Bank partner replied: correspondent fee of EUR 2.20 applied. Provider will supply signed fee breakdown by 2026-03-05.
Pending - awaiting bank partner signed fee breakdown. Next steps: once partner confirms correspondent fee EUR 2.20, Finance will post GL correction for EUR 2.20 and issue supplemental payment of EUR 15.20 to employee (to cover remaining variance). If provider CSV changes, coordinate reverse entry and adjust supplier reconciliation. Owner: Liam Patel.
Action 1: Payments to request formal fee breakdown from bank partner (owner: Alex Rivera, due 2026-03-05)
Action 2: Finance to prepare GL corrective journal and payroll top-up if needed (owner: Maya Chen, due 2026-03-07)

Purpose:
Request approval to extract a scoped, sampled set of production request/response pairs (redacted and KMS-wrapped) for an upcoming third-party compliance evidence check. This is NOT a full session export; it is a narrow slice targeted by time window and request fingerprinting patterns.

Scope:
- Time window: 2026-03-01 00:00:00 UTC — 2026-03-07 23:59:59 UTC (7 days)
- Targeted customers: internal test customers + two enterprise customers with signed NDAs (IDs to be provided to approvers separately via secure channel)
- Sample size: up to 250 unique request/response pairs, prioritized by observed error rate and variance in tokenization across affected models.

Data minimization and transformations:
- Remove user-identifying fields via the redaction script (field_map_v3).
- Replace any detected email/phone patterns with deterministic tokens.
- KMS-wrap each payload before extraction; extract only ciphertext blobs plus a minimal metadata CSV (hash-only identifiers, model,id-hash,timestamp).
- No raw keys or plaintext left on any intermediary host.

Controls and guardrails requested:
- Two-person control for the extraction run: operator (infra-runner) + approver (security lead) to sign the run command via vault-signed token.
- Extraction to occur in a segregated ephemeral pod in prod with no external network egress; files written to a short-lived S3 bucket encrypted with customer-managed key and lifecycle set to auto-delete after 7 days.
- Audit logging enabled (who/when/command) with links recorded in the ticket.

Deliverable:
- A KMS-wrapped tar.gz containing the sample blobs (ciphertext) and metadata CSV, plus a short README of the redaction transformations applied.
- A verification manifest and SHA256 of the archive.

Retention and follow-ups:
- Extracted artifacts to be retained for maximum 7 days in the secure bucket; then automatic delete.
- If compliance requests longer retention, a separate approval flow required.

Approval rationale:
- Third-party validator requires representative examples to confirm redaction rules and to validate retention controls. No other viable way to demonstrate production-redaction fidelity without a data slice.

Requested by: Compliance engineering (internal), ticketed per DPA operator checklist.

Requested approvers: Security Engineering lead, Privacy & Compliance owner, and Infra Oncall (for scheduling).
1) Approver sign-off in ticket comments (security + privacy).
2) Infra operator picks 7-day window and builds a fingerprint query (sha256 of request prefix) limited to sample size 250.
3) Run redaction script field_map_v3 against a stage-like replay on a snapshot; review sample of 10 in-person with approvers before prod run.
4) Execute extraction tool (prod-extract v2.1) with --kms-wrap --no-egress flags in ephemeral pod; operator and approver must present signed tokens.
5) Upload artifacts to kms-encrypted S3 path under s3://redwood-compliance-samples/INT-418273/ and attach SHA256 manifest to this ticket.

Issue summary: Several engineers in the SF branch reported intermittent timeouts when hitting internal K8s API services (team dashboards, CI runners) over corporate Wi‑Fi. Impact: Affected team members experienced 10–30s timeouts or 502/504 errors against internal services intermittently during the day. Scope: ~10–25% of clients on the branch mesh; not global.

Observed behavior: Client HTTP/gRPC calls to internal services would hang for ~15–25s then either succeed or return a 504. Simultaneously, packet captures from affected clients showed ARP requests for service VIPs with no ARP reply from the AP/edge for extended periods. When the same client switched to wired network or another site, issues disappeared.

Expected behavior: Mesh APs should proxy/forward ARP and not suppress legitimate ARP requests for internal VIPs. Service discovery and routing should remain stable during client roaming between mesh nodes.
1) Connect corporate laptop to branch mesh SSID (ssid: redwood-office).
2) Start continuous curl -v against internal k8s service VIP (https://svc-internal.redwood.local:8443).
3) Walk across open office to trigger mesh roaming between APs (or force disconnect via AP web UI).
4) Observe intermittent large request latencies (15-25s) or HTTP 502/504 failures.
WiFi AP syslog (excerpt): [Mar 05 09:13:12] AP-03 client-steer: suppress-arp for 10.18.3.45 -> 10.18.0.200; [Mar 05 09:13:13] AP-01 client-assoc: sta 02:12:ab:cd:ef:01 roam->AP-03; Edge firewall logs show NAT-translation hits but no ARP proxy reply during suppression windows.
10:22 - Triage: Collected pcap from affected client and APs (AP-01 and AP-03). Noted ARP requests for cluster VIP (10.18.0.200) with repeated retransmits; AP forwarded some ARP replies but often dropped them during 'suppression' windows.
11:05 - Hypothesis: Mesh controller feature 'ARP suppression / proxy' (enabled to reduce broadcast storms) is aggressively suppressing/proxying ARPs but has a bug where it suppresses ARPs while the client attachment state is still transitioning (roaming edge-case).
11:30 - Reproduced: Forced roaming between AP-01->AP-03 while running tcpdump on AP-03. Observed ARP suppression log entries coincident with client reassociation; these windows match user-visible timeouts to k8s services.
12:10 - Correlation: Only clients that relied on internal VIPs (k8s services) and had short-lived sticky sessions were impacted. DNS lookups succeeded; TCP handshakes stalled waiting for ARP resolution, hence HTTP timeouts rather than DNS failures.
13:00 - Check config: Mesh firmware 5.4.2 has 'arp_proxy_aggressive=true' set at site profile. Vendor release notes show a related bug fixed in 5.5.0 where proxy incorrectly drops ARP during roam.
13:45 - Communication: Opened fast-track with WiFi vendor TAC (case #TAC-2026-143) and linked AP syslogs and pcaps.
Maya Chen (reporter) [2026-03-05 10:00]: Users started reporting intermittent timeouts after morning standups. Filing ticket to collect traces.
SRE Oncall - Priya Patel [2026-03-05 11:40]: Collected tcpdumps, seeing repeated ARP requests from clients for 10.18.0.200 with no reply during the timeout window. Moving to investigate mesh AP behaviour.
WiFi Eng - Alex Nguyen [2026-03-05 12:30]: Confirmed 'arp_proxy_aggressive' set on site profile. Vendor notes suggest issue in 5.4.x series during fast roam. Recommending temporary disable of 'ARP suppression' as mitigation.
Diego Alvarez (assignee) [2026-03-05 13:20]: Will put change in place during 16:00 maintenance window. Will monitor for regressions and vendor response.
Vendor TAC [2026-03-05 15:10]: Acknowledged bug, provided hotfix image 5.4.2-hf1 that addresses suppression race during roam. Recommended either apply hotfix or disable feature as workaround.
Diego Alvarez [2026-03-05 16:30]: Rolled back 'arp_proxy_aggressive' to false on branch site profile during maintenance window. Applied vendor hotfix to AP-03 (root) for additional validation.
Root cause: Mesh controller's aggressive ARP suppression/proxy feature incorrectly suppressed ARP replies during fast client roaming windows, causing clients to fail to resolve cluster VIPs and producing 15-25s application timeouts.

Mitigation and fix deployed: 1) Disabled 'arp_proxy_aggressive' on branch site profile (immediate mitigation). 2) Applied vendor hotfix 5.4.2-hf1 to root AP and staged roll to satellite APs (completed 2026-03-06). 3) Adjusted AP roaming thresholds (lowered roam hysteresis) and increased ARP proxy fallback timers.

Verification: Post-change monitoring across 72 hours showed dropped error rates to baseline (internal service 5xxs returned to <0.5% at the site) and user reports ceased. PCAP samples show ARP replies delivered promptly during roam.

Follow-ups / Action items: [2026-03-09] - WiFi Eng to schedule full-site hotfix rollout and perform customer-style acceptance testing. [2026-03-09] - Update runbook for branch mesh profiles to include 'disable aggressive ARP proxy' as a temporary troubleshooting step for service discovery timeouts. [2026-03-12] - Postmortem page: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/INT-657890-mesh-arp-suppression-postmortem
payload.summary: Branch mesh AP ARP suppression + client-isolation causing intermittent internal service discovery timeouts

Issue summary:
Several users with legacy usernames (containing a dot + suffix, e.g. 'j.smith+team') intermittently receive a 403 when attempting to SSH through the company SSH gateway. The gateway validates Okta SSO assertions including a device_claim (device_id/device_fingerprint) injected by our Device Trust pipeline. The identity-proxy is truncating the device_claim under certain lengths, causing downstream service-side assertion mismatch and immediate 403 / impersonation failure.

Impact:
- A subset of internal employees cannot establish SSH sessions via the centralized SSH gateway (affects ~12 users reported in past 48h).
- Blocks oncall and incident runbook access for those users.
- No production workloads impacted beyond internal tooling access, but this is high-priority because it affects incident response.

Environment:
- production cluster behind identity-proxy v1.12.3 (us-west region)
- Okta Device Trust enforcement enabled for SSH gateway app

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use a test account with a legacy username pattern (e.g. j.smith+infra@example.com) that has device-trust enrolled.
2) Initiate SSH through the centralized ssh-gateway which redirects to Okta SSO device flow.
3) Complete device attestation and allow SSO redirect back to identity-proxy.
4) Observe gateway returns 403 and session is not established.

Observed logs / evidence:
- identity-proxy stderr (excerpt):
  [2026-03-12T08:23:12Z] WARN auth: incoming assertion device_claim length 520, truncating to 256
  [2026-03-12T08:23:12Z] ERROR ssh-gateway: user "j.smith+infra" assertion mismatch after device_claim rewrite -> 403
- Okta auth audit (correlated):
  2026-03-12T08:23:11Z  AUTH_SUCCESS user=j.smith+infra app=ssh-gateway claims_total=7 device_claim_len=520
- Browser/CLI symptom: immediate "Permission denied (publickey)" followed by gateway 403 in support logs.

Investigation notes:
- Triage by oncall identity-engineer (Diego M.) confirmed truncation happens in the identity-proxy component when claim length >256 bytes; this is new behavior after the 2026-03-10 hotfix to sanitize incoming headers (PR: https://github.com/redwood/identity-proxy/pull/405).
- Reproduced locally by forging SAML assertion with long device_claim; identity-proxy drops trailing bytes and emits a WARN. Downstream SSH gateway performs an exact-compare on the device_claim and denies when mismatch occurs.
- Hypothesis: previous token pipeline normalized username + device claim ordering; the new sanitizer trims header values at 256 bytes which wasn't an issue for non-legacy usernames. Legacy usernames produce longer combined claims due to appended '+' suffix and device metadata.
- Quick check shows no Okta-side truncation; Okta advertises device_claim up to ~1k bytes in our tenant.
- Session cookies for affected users show regenerated session IDs after the failed flow, suggesting identity-proxy rejects upstream assertion before session finalization.

Comments:
- "Diego Marquez (Identity): I've reproduced the truncation locally and confirmed the identity-proxy sanitizer enforces a 256-byte header cap. Working on a patch to allow 1k bytes for device_claim only. Will open PR for review." 2026-03-12T14:02Z
- "SRE oncall (Marta Chen): Confirmed two oncall users were impacted during incident window; provided per-user workarounds (clear cookies + use web-based ssh-console which uses alternate flow)." 2026-03-13T09:30Z
- "Support (Aisha): Collected 12 affected usernames, sample assertion payloads, and keyed linked incidents. Adding to ticket." 2026-03-13T11:45Z

Action items / tentative fix plan:
- Short term workaround: instruct affected users to clear identity-proxy cookies and use the web-console ssh fallback or use a temporary service account to escalate. Documented in the incident Slack thread #support-ssh.
- Code change: update identity-proxy sanitizer to allow device_claim header up to 1024 bytes and only apply relaxed cap to header name 'X-Device-Claim' to avoid wide-open header size increases. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/identity-proxy/pull/418 (draft).
- Add normalization step in auth pipeline to canonicalize legacy usernames (strip '+' suffixes for device-claim generation) to avoid oversized combined claim metadata.
- Add automated regression test to identity-proxy for device_claim sizes and for legacy username patterns.

Resolution / current status:
- Workaround shared with affected users.
- Draft fix PR created and assigned to Diego for tests and CI adjustments.
- Planned deploy to staging: 2026-03-15; canary to prod-us-west 2026-03-17 if tests pass.
- Follow-up: add monitoring alert when identity-proxy emits more than 5 "truncating" WARNs in 10m for device_claim in production.

Follow-up notes:
- Link to related incident postmortem will be added after production rollout.
- Consider long-term: reconcile device metadata format with Okta Device Trust team to prevent oversized claims and add server-side resilient comparison (hash compare instead of raw-compare).
2026-03-12T14:02Z - Diego Marquez: I've reproduced the truncation locally and confirmed the identity-proxy sanitizer enforces a 256-byte header cap. Working on a patch to allow 1k bytes for device_claim only.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During depot imaging in staging (us-east), machines with an attached USB-C dock or USB-to-Ethernet adapter sometimes stall at the network bring-up step. systemd-networkd and NetworkManager show repeated carrier state flaps; the provisioning-agent waits on network-online.target and the imaging step times out, leaving devices in a half-imaged state.

Impact:
- ~6% of Ubuntu 22.04 images in the last 48 hours failed to complete in depot-staging-us-east.
- Blocked devices require manual intervention (reboot/detach dock) which delays repairs.
- This affects internal provisioning throughput during high-volume depot windows.

Environment:
- Depot-staging racks in us-east with USB-C docks (Dell WD19) and several USB3-to-RJ45 adapters (AX88179).
- Ubuntu 22.04 base image, kernel 5.19.0-40, NetworkManager 1.46, systemd 253.
- Provisioning agent v1.18.2 running in the imaging container.

Steps to reproduce (intermittent):
1. Attach USB-C dock with onboard Ethernet or plug in USB3-Ethernet adapter.
2. Boot PXE image and start depot imaging job.
3. Provisioning agent waits for network-online.target; logs show repeated carrier on/off events from the USB NIC.
4. After 15-20 minutes the imaging job times out and the host is left at a partial state.

Observed logs and artifacts:
- Journal excerpts (nm and kernel):
  > kernel: usb 3-2: new high-speed USB device number 7 using xhci_hcd
  > kernel: r8152 3-2:1.0 eth0: v1.12.9 driver loaded
  > NetworkManager[1212]: <info>  [03-10 10:22:15] device (eth0): link connected
  > NetworkManager[1212]: <warn>  [03-10 10:22:17] device (eth0): link disconnected
  > systemd[1]: NetworkManager-dispatcher[2321]: Waiting for carrier...
- Provisioning agent log: "waiting for network-online.target: timed out after 900s"
- Kernel dmesg shows occasional USB resets for the adapter.

Hypothesis:
- The USB Ethernet adapter driver (r8152 / ax88179) combined with specific dock firmware is flapping carrier state when traffic/energy-saving interactions occur during PXE/bootstrap, causing NetworkManager to keep retrying and blocking systemd-network-online.
- Provisioning-agent is relying on network-online.target which is too strict for flaky USB NICs; we should either add a shorter fallback or use an alternate reachability probe (e.g., DHCP success/ping to provisioning server).

Initial troubleshooting steps taken:
- Confirmed replication in staging with same dock model and adapter. (Field tech: removed dock = imagening proceeds normally).
- Upgraded provisioning-agent in a test container to v1.18.3 with extra logging; no behavioral change.
- Temporarily adjusted systemd-networkd-wait-online timeout to 30s in a test image; imaging proceeds but we saw post-image network configuration failures in a small fraction of hosts.

Next steps / action items:
- [Assigned] Mateo to capture full packet traces and USB reset timestamps on a repro machine (ETA 2026-03-12).
- [Investigate] Try alternate DHCP client (dhclient) behavior vs NetworkManager to see if link state flaps still block provisioning.
- [Mitigation] Add a provisioning-agent flag to ignore network-online.target and instead wait for DHCP lease + TCP handshake to provisioning backend (short-term workaround).
- [Long-term] SRE/hardware to coordinate with depot vendor to test dock firmware; open support ticket with dock vendor if we can repro consistently.

Requested by: depot support shift lead for March maintenance window.
payload.summary: Provisioning hang: systemd-network waits indefinitely on usb-ethernet carrier flaps during depot image step

payload.description:
Issue summary:
HR received reports from Finance and IT that when an employee is placed on Immediate Termination (ITerm) in Workday, the seat/license in third-party SaaS (notably the design/legal tool vendor) remains billable for up to 14 days and the assigned corporate laptop sometimes remains tagged as 'active' in our asset management inventory. This ticket seeks clarification of the intended policy (grace windows) and the operational mechanics (which systems enforce the reclaim/return windows).

Impact:
- Potential short-term double-billing for SaaS seats when seats are quickly re-assigned.
- Delays in device recovery leading to inventory inaccuracies and security exposure for high-risk departures.
- Confusion between HR, IT, and Finance on expected timelines and required manual steps.

Environment:
- Identity sync: Okta -> SCIM -> downstream SaaS (prod)
- Asset tracking: FleetOps (prod) with inventory sync to ITSM
- HR system: Workday (prod)

Observed behavior / Steps to reproduce:
1) Create an employee termination in Workday with 'Immediate' flag at 09:00 UTC.
2) Workday emits termination event, HR webhook updates Okta.
3) Okta SCIM provisioning sends deactivation to SaaS vendor; we observe the user status change but vendor maintains seat as billable for a 14-day grace window (vendor policy).
4) FleetOps does not mark the laptop as 'awaiting pickup' until an asset-handback task is created manually by IT; automatic tagging is not triggered by the termination event.
5) Finance reports a new invoice line for an additional seat 3 days later after license reassign because the old seat was not reclaimed yet.

Logs / evidence:
- Okta SCIM audit (okta-audit-2026-03-09.log) shows deactivation event at 09:02 UTC and response 200 from vendor with response body: {"status":"deprovision-scheduled","grace_days":14}.
- FleetOps event stream shows no asset lifecycle change tied to the Workday termination event (fleetops-events-2026-03-09.ndjson).
- Finance ticket FIN-1189 referencing unexpected seat charge for week of 2026-03-02.

Question / Requested clarification:
- What are the company-wide defaults for SaaS license reclaim windows and how many days are considered 'standard' vs 'exception' requiring manual immediate reclaim?
- For Immediate Terminations, do we have an established exception/accelerated flow that forces vendor-side seat revocation and device pickup tagging?
- Which teams are expected to take manual actions vs which actions should be automated by identity/asset tooling?

Desired outcome:
- A concise policy statement HR/IT/Finance can rely on for immediate-term offboards, including: default reclaim window, criteria for accelerating reclaim, and the single authoritative runbook link for immediate offboards.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 13:15 — Jana Müller (Finance): Current invoices show an average of 2.3 days of overlap per reassign. Shortening reclaim window will materially affect monthly spend forecasts. Please include Finance in policy decisions.
Okta->SCIM behavior: The connector implementation uses PATCH to set 'active' to false. Vendor accepts this and sets an internal grace policy (14 days) rather than immediate seat relinquish.
FleetOps integration: Asset lifecycle changes are only triggered by ITSM ticket creation at present; there is no webhook or SCIM-driven asset tagging for device pickup. This is a gap for immediate offboards.
Workday mapping: 'Immediate' termination is mapped to Okta attribute 'terminationType=immediate' but that attribute is not propagated to downstream SCIM calls currently; therefore downstream vendors cannot differentiate Immediate vs standard terminations.
Hypothesis: If Okta emitted a 'terminationType' custom attribute or we used a 'hard-delete' SCIM call on certain vendors, seats could be reclaimed faster, but vendor policies and contracts may prohibit forced immediate deletion (data retention concerns).
Tentative operational plan agreed on 2026-03-12:
1) Policy clarification: Default reclaim window remains vendor-determined; for 'Immediate' terminations, HR + IT will follow an accelerated flow.
2) Automation tasks: Identity team to add terminationType flag propagation to SCIM (Ethan Park) and to implement a 'hard-delete' option gated behind a documented approval step.
3) Asset tagging: FleetOps to listen for Workday/Okta terminationType events and auto-tag devices as 'awaiting-security-pickup' (IT will still approve pickup).
4) Finance: will be looped into the vendor contract review to identify vendors that support immediate seat removal vs those with mandatory grace windows.
5) Runbook: Create a concise 'Immediate Offboard' runbook in Confluence with decision tree and contact channel (#it-offboarding).
Notes: Until automation is in place, manual vendor escalation is the workaround for high-risk departures. This ticket should remain open until the SCIM flag propagation PR (INT-821408) is merged and FleetOps webhook (INT-821409) is live.
payload.summary: Clarify provisional license reclaim window and equipment-return grace period for immediate offboarding

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed intermittent mixed model outputs after we started a weighted canary promote of llama-3b-v2-canary. Some sessions that had been pinned to the stable model returned responses from the canary variant or returned 502s mid-stream. This began approximately at 2026-02-21 03:10 UTC during the first traffic ramp to canary weight 10%.

Impact:
Multiple enterprise tenants (LotusAI) experienced corrupted or inconsistent responses for ongoing multi-turn sessions. No data leak observed; user-facing application errors and user complaints. Estimated affected sessions ~120 over 25 minutes.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment for LotusAI (dedicated pool dp-lotus-prod-us-east)
- Routing policy: weighted canary promote with session pin retention policy 'session-lock' enabled
- Canary model: llama-3b-v2-canary (quantized)
- Edge health probing enabled with short probe interval for host liveness

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a multi-turn session pinned to stable model (llama-3b-v2).
2) Trigger a simulated canary promote with 10% weight to llama-3b-v2-canary.
3) Rapidly flip edge host health (simulate probe failures) on subset of edge proxies during promote window.
4) Continue multi-turn requests; observe model hashes and stream disconnects.

Observed behavior:
- Session that had been pinned to stable model sometimes routed to canary after an edge host health probe caused a rebind at the edge layer.
- Some responses were mixed (prefix tokens from stable model, continuing tokens from canary) leading to incoherent outputs.
- A small number of requests returned 502 mid-stream with logs showing KV cache mismatch/detection in serving-runtime.

Expected behavior:
- Session pins should persist for the duration of the session unless customer explicitly unpins or session TTL expires. Edge health probes should not trigger migration of pinned sessions to canary variant. If host fallback is required, pinned sessions should prefer a compatible pinned variant or fall back to stable variant, not mix models.

Relevant logs/snippets:
- Edge proxy log at 2026-02-21T03:12:06Z: "probe:host_unhealthy host=ep-34 status=503; session_rebind candidate=route-redirect"
- Routing service trace 2026-02-21T03:12:07Z: "session_lock_check: found lock=stable@tenant:12345 ttl=2m but host_rebind=true; applying rebind policy=prefer_any"
- Serving runtime WARN 2026-02-21T03:12:09Z: "kv-cache-consistency: detected model-hash-mismatch incoming=hash-canary existing=hash-stable; terminating stream"
- Application error seen by customer: "Conversation turned nonsense at step 7"

Additional notes:
Reproduced issue in staging by triggering edge host flaps during a weighted canary promote using the same routing config as production.
Root cause hypothesis: when edge detects host unhealthy and triggers a session rebind, the routing service's rebind policy 'prefer_any' did not consult session lock metadata. Rebind path allowed assignment to an instance running canary model. The serving runtime then detected KV cache model-hash mismatch and terminated stream or produced mixed outputs when partial state was accepted.
Session tokens lacked an embedded model-hash or model-stability flag, so downstream allocator could not enforce 'pin-to-compatible' at rebind time.
Edge probe frequency combined with short session-lock TTL (~2m) made race window measurable during our promote window.
Policy interaction: routing fallback policy 'prefer_any' during edge-induced rebinds bypassed session-lock enforcement, allowing pinned sessions to be routed to non-compatible model variants. This caused KV cache mismatches and mixed outputs.
Mitigation applied: 1) edge probe aggressiveness reduced for affected dedicated pools; 2) temporary routing override 'prefer_compatible' applied for LotusAI tenant; 3) emergency patch to routing service to check session-lock metadata on rebind is merged (PR #918) and staged for internal canary. Full rollout after internal validation.

Issue summary:
Customer requests a compact, chronologically-ordered activity bundle tailored for their on-prem Splunk HEC ingest. Requirements include a deterministic resume token per-batch, explicit timezone normalization to UTC, per-event field provenance for PII-sensitive fields, and a redaction/pseudonymization mapping file that the customer can apply prior to ingestion. They also asked for a small diagnostic harness (scripts + sample data) that demonstrates how to rehydrate compressed delivery bundles and replay into their Splunk test HEC endpoint for verification.

Impact:
FinNova cannot complete SIEM onboarding validation for a production cutover until they can reproduce ingest behavior and validate PII redaction. This is blocking a planned compliance go-live in two weeks. Customer reports partial rejects in their test HEC where fields are dropped or show unexpected nulls.

Background and constraints:
- Customer is on our enterprise plan with private deployment networking to their on-prem Splunk cluster.
- They require evidence that delivered audit records are consistent, ordered, and that PII normalization is reversible by escrowed keys (for legal reasons).
- Preferred delivery: gzipped NDJSON with per-batch manifest, separate CSV mapping of fields->redaction profiles, and a short rehydration script (Python 3.10) that shows streaming upload to HEC.

Requested deliverables:
1) One-hour scoped diagnostic bundle: ~2,500 events spanning auth, inference.request, inference.response, and system.audit events, timezone-normalized to UTC and annotated with provenance metadata (field_origin, redact_profile_id).
2) CSV redaction mapping: column name, redact_profile_id, pseudonymization_method (hmac-sha256 with per-tenant salt OR reversible-escrow), sample before/after.
3) Small rehydration + ingest script (Python) and README that shows: how to decompress, validate manifest checksums, and post to Splunk HEC with idempotency headers.
4) Playbook excerpt for troubleshooting common mapping mismatches and a list of quick queries customers can run in Splunk to validate ordering and completeness.

Acceptance criteria:

Issue summary: Several engineers intermittently cannot access the internal Secret Manager console. After clicking 'Sign in with SSO' they are redirected to the Okta device-trust step; after approving device challenge the browser returns to the Secret Manager page but immediately redirects back to Okta and repeats the device approval prompt (login loop).

Impact: Affects a subset of users who have device-trust enforcement enabled (device-registered via MDM). Blocks access to secret rotation and emergency credential retrieval. Reported by 6 engineers across two teams; on-call and runbook access impacted.

Environment: Production, us-west region, internal console behind identity-proxy and okta-device-trust flow. Not observed in staging.

Steps to reproduce: listed below. Intermittent; not reliably reproducible for all affected users.

Expected behavior: After Okta device approval, users should be returned to Secret Manager with a valid session and RBAC claims.

Observed behavior: Post device approval, redirect loop back to Okta device challenge. When loop breaks, session often lands in a minimal unauthenticated page or immediate 403 from console API requiring re-login.
1) Navigate to https://internal-secretmgr.redwood.company
2) Click 'Sign in with SSO' -> Okta page loads
3) Okta prompts for device-trust challenge (push or biometrics),
4) Approve device challenge on MDM client,
5) Browser returns to secret manager but immediately redirects back to Okta device-trust prompt (loop)
auth-proxy: 2026-03-10T14:22:03Z INFO Received callback from Okta for user priya@redwood.com, state=xyz123
auth-proxy: 2026-03-10T14:22:03Z DEBUG Introspecting session cookie: missing 'device_binding' claim
okta-svc: 2026-03-10T14:22:04Z INFO Device challenge accepted for device id dv-9182 for user priya@redwood.com
console-api: 2026-03-10T14:22:04Z WARN Session create returned 403 RBAC: claim 'device_trust' not present
browser-console: Failed to exchange authorization code: 400 - "invalid_grant: code already redeemed" (observed in one trace)
Trace 1 (priay@redwood.com) shows Okta device challenge accepted at 14:22:04 but auth-proxy logged missing device claim at 14:22:03 due to ordering mismatch between callback and background claim fetch.
We observed 'invalid_grant: code already redeemed' in one trace meaning the authorization code was processed twice; second attempt returns 400 and leaves session half-initialized.
Sticky routing reduced recurrence in limited canary (2/6 users stopped looping), indicating a race between instances is likely contributor.
RBAC check on console-api strictly requires 'device_trust' claim; when claim is absent created session rejects with 403 leading client to re-initiate SSO, causing the loop.
No evidence of Okta misconfiguration; device challenge events are recorded as accepted consistently in Okta logs.

Additional notes:
Temporary mitigation: enabled sticky callback routing for identity-proxy and added extra logging around authorization-code handling. Long-term fix: PR to serialize callback handling per OAuth state token (identity-proxy PR 5182) and additional idempotency checks when redeeming auth codes. Requesting rollout to prod us-west during next maintenance window after code review. Follow-up action to add a targeted Canary in us-west for 24h monitoring.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During automated task-sequence imaging in APAC (ap-southeast-1), NetworkManager on fresh Windows PE handoff writes two overlapping default routes (0.0.0.0/0) to the primary interface. The duplicated routes have different metrics and intermittently cause the Azure AD join step to time out (AADSTS network error) or attempt to use an internal management VPN endpoint, failing domain registration and stalling the task sequence.

Impact:
- ~5-8% of devices in the last 48h fail AAD join during imaging and are left in the 'Autopilot not completed' state.
- Affected devices require manual intervention (local admin join + re-run of post-provision scripts) delaying depot turn-around.
- Mostly impacts APAC staging fleet and a small subset of production depot images.

Environment:
- Imaging orchestrator: SCCM task sequence handing off to WinPE -> OOBE scripts (internal imaging-playbooks v3.7).
- Network manager: Custom NM shim used in WinPE handoff (win-nm-wrapper v0.9.2).
- Observed on Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen11, Dell Latitude 7440.
- Regions: ap-southeast-1 staging and select prod depots.

Steps to reproduce (intermittent):
1) Boot device into SCCM task sequence using depot network VLAN (APAC depot).
2) WinPE hands off to windows setup, imaging-playbook triggers win-nm-wrapper to apply DHCP/route config.
3) Watch netstat / route print or use PowerShell Get-NetRoute after handoff.
4) Observe two default routes: one with metric 15 and one with metric 5, sometimes bound to same interface.
5) Continue imaging -> Azure AD Join step times out or reports network unreachable.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate default routes appear immediately after win-nm-wrapper runs; sometimes the lower-metric route points at a management VLAN gateway that should be unreachable from the depot VLAN.
- AAD join logs show network requests routed to the wrong gateway and either timing out or returning HTTP 502 from an internal proxy.
- Re-running networking script that deletes the duplicate route allows AAD join to succeed.

Expected behavior:
- Single default route to depot gateway (correct metric).
- AAD join uses depot network path to Microsoft endpoints.

Logs / Artifacts attached in ticket: list of sample Get-NetRoute outputs, win-nm-wrapper logs, SCCM task sequence trace snippets, sample AAD join traces (correlation IDs) and pcap from one repro.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: race between DHCP client registering routes and win-nm-wrapper adding explicit route entries leads to duplicate entries.
- win-nm-wrapper v0.9.2 introduced a change to add a default-route fallback with lower metric when DHCP lease is delayed (PR infra/imaging-playbooks#157). Suspect this path improperly fires even when DHCP later populates the route.
- Correlated failures with depot switches that have intermittent DHCP lease latency (~100-400ms) during peak provisioning windows.
- Reproduced locally by delaying DHCP response in a lab: when wrapper adds fallback route and DHCP later adds its route, system ends up with two default routes. Windows route selection uses metric so traffic can go to unintended gateway.

Temporary workaround:
- Add a cleanup step in task sequence immediately after win-nm-wrapper: run PowerShell to remove duplicate default routes, keeping the DHCP-provided one (script snippet available). Deployed to staging depots, reduced failures to ~0.5% in first 12h.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering to patch win-nm-wrapper to check for an existing default route and avoid adding fallback when DHCP is expected (owner: infra/imaging team).
- Long-term: update imaging-playbooks to wait for DHCP lease or implement an idempotent route reconcile step; add unit test for delayed DHCP scenarios.
- Ops: monitor APAC depot provisioning metrics and roll the cleanup script to remaining depots pending patch.

Resolution (work in progress):
- Temporary cleanup script deployed to 2 staging depots -- effective as a stopgap.
- Patch PR opened: infra/imaging-playbooks#157 (fix adds route-existence check and 2s wait for DHCP). Pending code review and canary.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:20 - SRE (Diego Morales): Noted DHCP server logs show occasional lease latency spikes correlated with provisioning peaks. Coordinating with network team to validate switch load and DHCP performance.
payload.summary: NetworkManager writes duplicate default routes during imaging causing AAD join timeout in ap-southeast

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A subset of macro/template bundles deployed during the March 10 release introduced cyclical references between templates (A -> B -> C -> A). The rule-compiler's dependency resolution step does not detect these cycles and enters a prolonged evaluation loop, causing a compiler worker to spin without progress.

Impact:
- Delayed rule compilation for new/updated routing templates across the us-east cluster.
- Autoroute updates queue up behind the hung compiler shard; customers on internal tooling workflows experienced delayed assignments for up to 18 minutes.
- Metrics: compiler task latency spike from median 1.2s to 320s on affected shard; alerting on compilation backlog triggered multiple P1 alerts.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east), rule-compiler fleet version: v2.14.1, templating-service: v1.9.0
- Affected node pool: compiler-shard-7 (k8s: us-east-compiler-7)
1) Push three templates with cross references: Tmpl-A references macro B, Tmpl-B references macro C, Tmpl-C references macro A (inline refs using {{ref:...}} syntax)
2) Trigger a bulk template publish via Console or API (bulk publish job id seen in logs)
3) Observe rule-compiler worker logs for dependency resolution stage and watch task remain at 'resolving_dependencies' for >5m
4) Check metrics: compilation_queue_depth for shard-7 climbs and cpu% spin remains high
Compiler should detect cyclical macro/template dependencies at parse/validation time and fail the publish with a clear error (validation error pointing to cycle). The compiler worker should not enter an infinite or prolonged loop and should handle the invalid template by marking it failed and returning control to the orchestrator.
Compiler enters a tight evaluation loop during dependency resolution; no cycle detection is raised. The publish API returns HTTP 200 for the bulk job even though individual templates are not compiled. Compilation backlog accumulates and autoroute updates are delayed until operator intervention (restart of compiler worker clears the stuck state).
2026-03-10T08:17:02Z compiler-shard-7 pod compiler-7-2fc8: INFO resolving dependencies for bulk-job: bj-4829
2026-03-10T08:17:45Z compiler-shard-7 pod compiler-7-2fc8: DEBUG resolving dependency chain: Tmpl-A -> Tmpl-B -> Tmpl-C -> Tmpl-A
2026-03-10T08:35:12Z compiler-shard-7 pod compiler-7-2fc8: WARN stuck in dependency-resolver loop for 1080s, iterations=4321
2026-03-10T08:36:00Z orchestrator: ERROR bulk publish bj-4829 incomplete: waiting on shard-7; API returned 200 (job accepted)
2026-03-10T08:40:01Z infra: ACTION restart pod compiler-7-2fc8 (cleared stuck worker); backlog drained by 2026-03-10T08:55:00Z
Initial triage (2026-03-10 09:00) by SRE: reproduced locally in a staging cluster using the same templating bundle — confirmed cyclical chain causes resolver to re-evaluate repeatedly without termination condition.
Static analyzer/validation step in templating-service (v1.9.0) does not include global graph cycle detection for cross-template macro refs that are created via runtime refs (inline vs import).
Compiler code path: dependency_resolver.walk() uses DFS but lacks a visited-set guard for templates referenced via dynamic macro indirection; this allows revisiting nodes via different ref paths, causing unbounded recursion/iteration.
Heap and CPU: worker did not OOM but CPU spiked; stack traces show repeated calls into dependency resolution rather than deep recursion (iterative loop detected).
Related to previous operator precedence bug (INT-128450) but root cause is different — that was evaluation order; this is missing cycle detection in the graph builder.
Affected shard (compiler-shard-7) has a single replica due to recent autoscaling config; when it becomes unhealthy the backlog cannot be redistributed because the job-assigner treats ongoing task as 'in-progress' with no failover policy for long-running dependency resolution.

Additional notes:
Mitigation applied (2026-03-10): immediate operator remediation — restart of compiler-shard-7 worker cleared the stuck state and drained backlog; rollback of the bulk publish job prevented further queued cycles.
Short-term fix (2026-03-12): merged validation change in templating-service to run a graph cycle detector at publish time. Tempting change also added a safety timeout in compiler dependency resolver (abort after 30s with error). PRs: templating/pull/384, compiler/pull/912.
Long-term actions: 1) Add failover for long-running compile tasks in job assigner so other replica can pick up tasks after threshold. 2) Add integration test harness that exercises templating corpus with synthetic cycles. 3) Update runbook to include 'restart compiler pod' step and how to detect cycle-induced hangs via metric 'dependency_resolver_iterations'. 4) Increase min replicas for compiler-shard pools handling bulk publishes to 2. Logged as follow-up INT-881444.
Status: patch deployed to prod us-east on 2026-03-12 02:30 UTC behind a feature flag; monitoring for 48hrs. No further compiler hangs observed in the window.
payload.summary: Rule compiler hangs when macro templates contain undetected cyclical dependencies

payload.description:
Issue summary: VisionaryChat reported a multi-minute window of elevated 502/503 responses for chat endpoints across us-west and us-east. The pattern is a sawtooth (rapid rise/fall) of 5xx rate coincident with tenant-initiated prefetch spin-ups. Impact: Several customer agents experienced degraded availability during high concurrency warm-ups; customer reported increased user-visible errors and retries. Environment: prod (us-west primary, traffic mirrored to us-east). Hypothesis: prefetcher + runtime hotpath lock ordering creates transient deadlock/long-hold on runtime request queue leading to proxy upstream 502/503s and queued conn backpressure on api-gateway.
1) On a dedicated tenant, send a steady low-rate of chat requests for 5 minutes. 2) Trigger a high-concurrency burst (20x baseline) that causes the tenant prefetcher to warm multiple model shards. 3) Observe api-gateway 5xx rate and runtime thread stacks for kvcache/prefetch lock holds. 4) Repeat with and without prefetch enabled to compare.
Relevant logs: apigw/2026-03-10T18:02:14Z 502 upstream reset; runtime/worker-12 2026-03-10T18:02:14Z blocking on prefetch::ShardLock for 8.3s; stackdump: serving::batch_queue -> prefetch::lock -> kv_store::writeback -> scheduler::try_alloc. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/987-prefetch/tenant-5xx-sawtooth and trace: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/0af4-prefetch-spinup. Extract: "runtime: blocking on ShardLock; concurrent_prefetch=12; accept_queue=120/128"
2026-03-10 17:58 UTC - Customer reported elevated errors. 2026-03-10 18:00 UTC - Support triaged and escalated to SRE. 18:05 UTC - SRE observed sawtooth 5xx aligned with tenant prefetch spikes. 18:15 UTC - Temporary mitigation: routed 30% traffic away from tenant, increased runtime pool by 2 nodes, disabled prefetch for tenant. 18:40 UTC - 5xx rates dropped to baseline. 2026-03-11 - Engineering reproduced locally, identified lock-order inversion in prefetch hotpath. 2026-03-12 - Hotfix PR opened and staged to canary; further rollout planned.
Initial hypothesis: GPU overload during shard warmup causing watchdog resets — not supported by NVML metrics (no driver resets).
Observed long-held mutexes in runtime worker stacks centered on prefetch::ShardLock and scheduler allocation path.
Correlation: api-gateway accept_queue fills during prefetch spikes; 502s originate when upstream runtime cannot accept new streams for >1s.
Reproduction: synthetic burst with prefetch enabled reproduces 5xx sawtooth; toggling prefetch disables the pattern.
Root cause draft: lock-order inversion between kvcache writeback path and scheduler allocation triggers long critical-section holds when concurrent prefetchers contend for shard metadata.
Customer impact: retries observable in VisionaryChat logs; increase in user-perceived failures by ~4% during window.
Related incidents: SUP-412345 (model-stage-swap 5xx spike) shows similar accept_queue dynamics but different root cause.
Mitigations tried: route-weight shift, temporary prefetch disable, runtime scale-up — all reduced surface but required code fix for long term.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer first reported at 17:58 UTC — they saw a ~6 minute window of errors, attached sample request IDs.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Confirmed sawtooth pattern on grafana; increased runtime pool and disabled prefetch for tenant as stopgap.
Priya Nair (Eng) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally; attaching perftrace and locking profiles. Suspect lock-order inversion in prefetcher + kv writeback.
Diego Alvarez 2026-03-11: After temporary disables, error-rate normalized. Planning hotfix to change lock ordering + add bounded prefetch concurrency per-tenant.
VisionaryChat (customer) 2026-03-11: Appreciated rapid mitigation; asked for root cause and ETA for permanent fix.
Short-term: disabled tenant prefetch and increased runtime pool which restored availability. Temporary route reweight reduced user impact. Long-term: merged hotfix that enforces consistent lock ordering and adds bounded prefetch concurrency per-tenant (PR 1824). Deployed to canary 2026-03-12 and to 50% of prod 2026-03-12; full rollout targeted 2026-03-13 after monitoring window. Follow-ups: add prefetch chaos test to CI, instrument per-shard lock hold histograms, update runbook with mitigation steps and customer communication template.
Automate prefetch stress scenario in system tests (owner: eng/prefetch).
Add histogram metric for shard lock hold time and alert if >500ms (owner: infra-metrics).
Update Redwood Console incident dashboard to show per-tenant prefetch concurrency and accept_queue depth (owner: console-team).
Customer follow-up: send detailed RCA and planned changes to VisionaryChat account team (owner: CS).
payload.summary: Tenant prefetch spin-up causing intermittent 5xx sawtooth and runtime hotpath lock contention

Issue summary:
Invoice INV-2026-349 from vendor 'NorthStar Logistics' was imported into the AP queue but failed to progress because the payment import step could not map the vendor's payment method code 'NSL-ACH-UK' to an internal payment channel. The invoice remained in state 'Awaiting Payment Method' and was excluded from the scheduled payment run.

Impact:
- 1 vendor invoice held (INV-2026-349) and part of a small batch of 7 invoices delayed for the Mar-11 payment run.
- Potential late fees if not cleared before vendor SLA (terms: Net30).
- Finance ops had to notify vendor and escalate to ERP/Admin.

Environment:
- prod (NetSuite integration via payments-mapper v2.1.4), region: us-east
- AP inbound via SFTP -> preprocessing lambda -> payments-mapper service -> ERP API

Steps to reproduce:
1) Drop sample invoice payload (INV-2026-349.json) to SFTP inbound processed for vendor NorthStar Logistics.
2) Observe preprocessing logs: /ops/sftp/imports/2026-03-10/INV-2026-349.log (PMAP-404 errors).
3) Check payments-mapper service logs: PMAP-404 (unmapped payment code).
4) Open ERP UI to pay invoice; manual mapping was not available in the UI at that time.

Expected behavior:
- Payment method code should map to an allowed payment channel (e.g., ACH_UK) and invoice should enter the scheduled payment run.

Actual behavior:
- Mapping failed because 'NSL-ACH-UK' was not present in payment_method_master and the regex-based mapper rejects hyphenated vendor codes.

- Payments-mapper log excerpt: s3://redwood-ops-logs/payments-mapper/2026-03-10/pm-3589.log
