payload.description:
Request: Create a standardized, auditable, timebound delegation pattern that allows our new analytics vendor to ingest telemetry and billing data into Snowflake/BigQuery using least-privilege roles across both AWS and GCP production accounts. This should be reproducible via Terraform modules, include automated teardown/rotation, and meet security audit requirements (CloudTrail + Cloud Audit Logs retention).
Onboarding the analytics vendor is blocked for product analytics and billing reconciliation. Without this pattern, teams will either over-provision long-lived credentials or delay the vendor integration, impacting visibility for the Growth and Finance teams.
Design and implement a cross-cloud access pattern that provides:
- GCP: a Workload Identity Federation mapping to a short-lived service identity for the vendor with a narrow IAM role limited to BigQuery datasets (read) and Cloud Storage prefixes (read). KMS decrypt access only for the dataset encryption key. Include IAM Conditions limiting access from specific OIDC issuer+subject claims and time window.
- AWS: an STS-assumable cross-account role with an external ID and permission boundary restricting S3 prefix read and limited KMS decrypt, plus CloudWatch Logs read. Prefer ephemeral credentials via AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity or AssumeRole with short TTL.
- Centralized audit: ensure all actions are captured in CloudTrail + GCP Audit Logs and routed to the security logging bucket/topic. Tag all created resources with onboarding:analytics-vendor and owner:analytics.
- Automation: Terraform modules and a small automation hook (GitHub Actions or CI job) to create the required resources, grant the vendor, and produce time-limited access tokens. Provide a runbook to revoke access immediately.
1) Analytics team created a GCP service account in a sandbox project and generated a JSON key (temporary) for PoC. 2) Attempted to use Workload Identity Federation but the vendor uses a custom OIDC flow that we haven't verified; mapping failed due to claim mismatch. 3) Security team recommended no long-lived keys. 4) Infra tried an AWS cross-account role with external ID but the vendor cannot rotate external ID frequently, causing operational friction.
- PoC keys exposed the problem: long-lived keys are not acceptable per security policy (no external key issuance without rotation).
- The vendor supports OIDC federation and JWT issuance but the 'sub' claim pattern differs from our typical doc; they include a vendor-specific prefix (e.g., vendor:ingest:org-123) which prevented the initial Workload Identity mapping.
- AWS role trust policy requires external ID; vendor prefers a web-identity approach. We need a consistent mapping design that supports both patterns or a short-lived bridging token service.
- Logging retention and access path currently not fully aligned: CloudTrail is enabled but vendor activities were logged in a non-central bucket in the PoC; we need centralized sink and a read-only viewer role for security and audit.
1) Build a Terraform module 'third_party_delegation' that provisions:
   - GCP: a Workload Identity Pool + Provider keyed to vendor OIDC issuer, a trimmed IAM role 'roles/bigquery.dataViewer' scoped to datasets via resource-level bindings, a storage objectViewer on specific GCS prefixes, and KMS CryptoKeyDecrypter limited to one key. Include IAM Conditions to restrict based on 'aud' and 'sub' patterns and a time-bound condition (notBefore/notAfter) for temporary access.
   - AWS: a cross-account role with a trust relationship that supports both AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity and AssumeRole (for vendors without OIDC). Include permission boundaries and a managed session policy generator that constrains allowed actions to s3:GetObject on a specific prefix, kms:Decrypt on one CMK ARN, and logs:DescribeLogGroups/logs:GetLogEvents. Configure role to require an external ID if using AssumeRole.
   - A small token broker Lambda (or Cloud Run) that can exchange vendor-issued JWTs for temporary, constrained STS/GCP tokens with TTL 1 hour. Broker performs claim validation and emits audit events to an ops topic.
2) Deliver runbooks, a PR template, and tests: terraform plan/apply CI checks, unit tests that assert IAM conditions and least-privilege. 3) Deploy audit sink aggregation and add alerting on unexpected resource access (e.g., KMS decrypt outside expected IP ranges).
- Terraform module 'third_party_delegation' in infra repo (module + example usage)
- Token broker implementation (pooled Cloud Run service) with OpenTelemetry traces
- Runbook: onboarding checklist (verification steps, required vendor claims, revocation steps)
- Security review checklist + planned PR for security approval
- Smoke tests that validate scoping and log ingestion
- Backout plan and immediate revocation script
Requested completion: 2026-03-31. Priority is P2 (business important but not P0). Suggest 2-week sprint with initial PoC of token broker + Terraform module in first week, security review and hardening in second week.
Maya Thompson (reporter) - 2026-03-12: Opening ticket. Growth needs vendor onboarding to complete Snowflake/BigQuery pipelines for product analytics. We're blocked until we can provide a secure delegation pattern.
Diego Alvarez (assignee) - 2026-03-13: I'll draft a Terraform module scaffold and a WIF proposal. Need vendor OIDC metadata (issuer + claim examples) and exact dataset/S3 prefix ARNs. Tagging Sec and Infra.
Lina Park (Security reviewer) - 2026-03-13: Security won't approve long-lived JSON keys or broad KMS decrypt. Require automated rotation and centralized logging. Please include Permission Boundaries on AWS and resource-level bindings on GCP.
Paul Nguyen (Infra) - 2026-03-14: Noted that legacy infra modules don't support IAM Conditions for GCP resource-level bindings; will add feature flags and tests. Need go/no-go on building token broker vs. asking vendor to change 'sub' format.
Maya Thompson - 2026-03-14: Vendor contact provided sample JWTs and OIDC metadata in the linked Confluence page. They've agreed to support web-identity flow if we can accept their 'sub' format in an allowlist.
TBD - awaiting infra PoC and security sign-off. Once PoC passes tests and security approves, schedule rollout to prod and run the vendor onboarding checklist.
- Validate that the token broker logs are forwarded to the security logging GCP project and AWS central logging account.
- Ensure Terraform module exposes variable for TTL and permission boundary ARNs.
- Create an automated job to revoke access at end of engagement and rotate any created short-lived keys if used for PoC.
payload.summary: Unified IAM scoped delegation for third-party analytics pipeline across AWS and GCP

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We need an automated flow to rotate ephemeral SSH deploy keys/certificates used by our self-hosted release runner pool. Current manual rotation is brittle and has caused at least two blocked releases in the last quarter.

Impact:
- Release pipelines intermittently fail with 'Permission denied (publickey)' during deploy stages.
- Engineers are manually intervening to re-provision keys on runners, adding 30-90 minutes of delay per blocked release.
- Upcoming major release scheduled 2026-03-18; this needs mitigation to avoid on-call escalations.

Environment:
- GitHub Actions self-hosted runners (pool: release-runner-prod) running on k8s nodes in us-east.
- SSH deploy keys and SSH certs are issued and stored in HashiCorp Vault (transit/ssh, kv/secret/release-keys).
- Runner bootstrap script retrieves key at start and writes to ~/.ssh/ for the runner user.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Run a release job that triggers deploy stage to production via SSH to deploy-hosts.
2) Job fails with 'Permission denied (publickey)'.
3) SRE/ReleaseEng logs into runner and sees that ~/.ssh/id_rsa is the rotated (new) key but deploy-hosts have only the previous public key.
4) Manual sync required: update authorized_keys on deploy-hosts or re-issue cert.

Logs / Observations:
- Agent output: "ssh: handshake failed: "ssh: unable to authenticate"" (see job logs).
- Vault audit shows the rotation operation executed, but there is a 2–5 minute window where some runners still present the old key due to cached bootstrap artifacts.
- Runner provisioning: bootstrap script runs only on container start; long-lived runners don't re-fetch keys automatically.

Initial investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: Manual key rotation flow (rotate key in Vault, update deploy-hosts, restart runners if necessary) is inconsistent because runners are long-lived and do not re-fetch secrets.
- Confirmed: Vault roles do not currently issue short-lived SSH certs; we rely on static keys stored in kv/ which are rotated manually.
- There is an existing infra PR ([infra#482]) that adds a 'secrets refresh' sidecar but it's not enabled for release-runner pool.

Proposed solution / next steps:
1) Implement ephemeral SSH cert workflow using Vault's SSH CA or dynamic SSH certificates: Vault mints short-lived certs per-runner for deploy access.
2) Update runner bootstrap to request a fresh cert at job start (or before deploy step) rather than on container start.
3) Add a lightweight secrets-refresh sidecar for long-lived runners to poll/renew certs with configurable TTL.
4) Add a CI job that performs a dry-run of rotation during non-peak hours and validates deploy-hosts accept the new cert (automated smoke test).
5) Add monitoring/alerting: percentage of deploy jobs failing with auth errors; alert if >1% over 1 hour.
6) Document runbook and rollback steps in Confluence; add a Release Eng checklist for the 2026-03-18 release.

Blockers / required approvals:
- Need Vault role change to allow issuing SSH certs from transit/ssh endpoint (security approval required).
- Need infra PR to be reviewed and enabled for release-runner-prod.

Owner / proposed assignees:
- Primary: Release Engineering (Marco Chen).
- SRE support: Priya Das.

Acceptance criteria:
- Release runners automatically obtain a short-lived SSH cert at deploy time without manual intervention.
- No deploy-stage 'Permission denied (publickey)' failures in the 7 days after rollout for any release-runner job.
- Rollback path documented and tested.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - Security (Chris Nguyen): Security OK in principle but need an approval ticket for granting the Vault role the 'ssh/sign' capability. Please add scope and audit plan. Recommended TTL <= 15m for certs used in CI deploys.
payload.summary: Automate ephemeral deploy-key rotation for self-hosted release runners

- Seen for at least one user in the main Redwood workspace; unclear if limited to enterprise-connected Slack workspaces.

2) Observe modal loads without taxonomy fields.
3) Submit incident; bot creates channel but no taxonomy set.

- Potential permission / Slack app installation scope mismatch causing blocks to be pruned.

- SRE to advise whether to temporarily relax enforcement for affected workspaces/users until hotfix is deployed.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Several recently depot-repaired laptops are hitting a consistent failure to load the Windows user profile after resuming from S3 (suspend). Machines appear to boot, login occurs at the credential prompt, but user profile services fail to mount and the session loops back to the sign-in screen.

Impact:
- Affected internal users cannot access their desktop after depot repair or battery replacement; productivity is blocked until a technician visits.
- Roughly ~8 confirmed devices across two models so far; potential wider exposure from recent OEM driver bundle updated in depot image.

Environment:
- Redeployed corporate image (CorpImage-2026-02-18) via SCCM task sequence at depot.
- OS: Windows 11 23H2, corp image with custom drivers.
- Regions: us-east and eu-west depots.

Steps to reproduce (observed reliably):
1) Depot tech performs battery replacement and reimaging with CorpImage-2026-02-18 via SCCM.
2) Device boots, device drivers and agent bundles install during OOBE.
3) Technician signs in to validate provisioning, then places machine to sleep (S3) for QA transport.
4) On resume, user signs in; profile load fails, explorer does not start, and sign-in returns to lock screen.

Observed behavior:
- Event Viewer: repeated errors from "User Profile Service" (Event ID 1530) with path access issues referencing C:\Users\<username> tmp symlinks.
- Windows logs show multiple crash dumps from a process named redwood-hid-daemon.exe around resume time.
- Device manager shows HID-compliant device with warning immediately after resume.

Expected behavior:
- Normal resume with user profile loading, explorer starting, and endpoint agents initializing.

Workaround in place:
- Remote assistance to create a new local admin profile and migrate data; not ideal.
- Temporary mitigation: instruct depot techs to avoid putting device to sleep during post-repair QA (hold on login and run a scripted sleep/resume test locally instead of S3) and to roll back to previous driver package for HID devices when possible.
Telemetry and early hypotheses:
- Repro on two different hardware models suggests common software component.
- redwood-hid-daemon.exe (our in-house HID sensor agent included in the corp image) shows an unhandled exception during resume sequence; stack traces point at descriptor parsing after EC/ACPI wake.
- Core dump (collected from one device) shows heap corruption pattern following a call to HidParseDescriptor() shipped by vendor-hidkit.dll included in driver package v1.4.3 (added to depot bundle 2026-02-10).
- Correlation: all affected devices were imaged after 2026-02-10, which matches when vendor-hidkit.dll v1.4.3 was added to the depot bundle.

Actions taken so far:
- Collected dumps from 3 devices and uploaded to SRE/Platform storage (link in comments).
- Re-imaged a test Dell Latitude 7440 with previous driver bundle (v1.4.1) — resume succeeds and profile loads as expected.
- Reproduced failure on an isolated lab machine using CorpImage-2026-02-18 and driver bundle v1.4.3.
- Eng assigned to reproduce in VM with kernel debug; initial test shows same crash sequence.

Hypothesis:
- Vendor HID library v1.4.3 contains an incompatible change that triggers heap corruption when redwood-hid-daemon parses certain descriptor sequences after S3 resume, causing the agent to crash and leave temporary profile symlinks in a bad state, resulting in User Profile Service errors.

Next steps:
- SRE/Platform to prepare an emergency rollback of vendor-hidkit.dll to v1.4.1 in depot image artifact (blocked by QA signoff).
- Dev (Marcus) to add defensive parsing and crash handling in redwood-hid-daemon; publish hotfix build for validation.
- Depot leads to pause issuance of CorpImage-2026-02-18 until rollback or hotfix is validated.
- Create follow-up change to add resume smoke test to depot QA checklist.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 16:22 - SRE (Noah Kim): Uploaded aggregated crash dumps to s3://redwood-attachments/INT-386420/dumps.tar.gz and added a Grafana panel showing spike in agent crashes post-2026-02-10. Link pasted into Confluence playbook.
Mitigation applied: Depot teams instructed to use driver bundle v1.4.1 for immediate repairs and to avoid sleep during post-repair QA. Hotfix for redwood-hid-daemon (with defensive parsing and crash handling) built and delivered to internal QA on 2026-03-14.
Planned permanent fix:
- Release hotfix agent v2.3.1 and update CorpImage with either the fixed agent or vendor driver rollback after validation.
- Add resume/suspend smoke test to depot SCCM task sequence and QA checklist to catch regressions.
- Open follow-up change request to vendor to investigate descriptor parsing differences between v1.4.1 and v1.4.3.
Follow-ups created:
- INT-386421 (Task): Update depot SCCM task sequence to include resume smoke test.
- INT-386422 (Bug): Vendor driver compatibility verification and coordination.
payload.summary: HID sensor daemon corruption prevents user profile load after resume on several laptop models

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FinlyBank Inc.) requests a near-real-time SIEM export to their Splunk HEC endpoint with the following requirements: per-tenant pseudonymization of user identifiers (deterministic, salted hash with per-tenant salt), field-level redaction for PII (SSN/email), a signed delivery manifest (PKCS7 preferred) for each hourly bundle, and an auditable key-rotation proof that shows evidence of KMS key changes over the retention period. They also report a discrepancy in daily event counts between Redwood's audit export and their Splunk index for 2026-02-20 to 2026-03-04, which they want reconciled as part of the evidence package.

Impact:
- Security/compliance team at FinlyBank cannot close their internal SOC2 evidence package without a signed manifest and rotation proof.
- They treat this as time-sensitive due to an upcoming audit window.

Customer ask (explicit):
1) Design and deliver a temporary signed-hourly S3 dump + manifest that includes: SHA256 checksums for each file, PKCS7 signed manifest, sample redacted payloads (3 examples), and a CSV reconciliation showing per-hour counts.
2) Provide KMS rotation history and attestable proofs (key version IDs, rotation timestamps, and signed audit entries) for the last 90 days.
3) Advice and timeline for a permanent Splunk HEC connector supporting per-tenant envelope encryption and HEC ingestion with backpressure/ack semantics.
4) Reconcile the event-count discrepancy for 2026-02-20 -> 2026-03-04 and supply a remediation plan.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod) exports to customer Splunk HEC endpoint via outbound TLS (customer-managed endpoint). Region: us-east.
- Customer uses enterprise tier with VPC peering and static egress IP allowlist.

Steps to validate (proposed):
1) Support prepares sample hourly S3 export for 2026-03-09 00:00-03:00 UTC with PKCS7 manifest and provides presigned URLs to customer.
2) Customer verifies manifest signature and per-file checksums; validates redaction on sample payloads.
3) Support provides KMS rotation log entries and signed attestations; customer verifies continuity of key lineage.

Observed vs Expected:
- Observed: Customer reports ~8-12% fewer events indexed in Splunk for certain hours; missing records appear correlated with peak ingest windows.
- Expected: The export should be lossless for audit events and any dropped events should be captured in a delivery failure log with retry metadata.

Attachments:
- Splunk HEC debug headers (provided by customer) and sample indexed events (redacted). Links included in comments.

Notes: This ticket will become part of the formal evidence bundle; please include clear steps and a signed manifest for archival.

Lina Chen (FinlyBank - Security) 2026-03-10: We're preparing our SOC2 folder and need a signed manifest + rotation proof before 2026-03-15. We can accept temporary S3 links for now; long-term HEC is preferred. Also attaching Splunk index screenshots and HEC ingestion logs. (link: https://files.finlybank.com/attachments/finly-splunk-evidence-2026-03-10.zip)
Marco Gutierrez (Support) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged — assigning to SRE for delivery pipeline check and to Security Eng for manifest/key proof. SLA noted for 2026-03-13. Will follow up with ETA for temporary S3 bundle by end of day 2026-03-11.
Devon Morales (SRE) 2026-03-11: Initial triage — audit-service delivery metrics show increased retry count between 2026-02-25 18:00 UTC and 2026-02-27 06:00 UTC for that customer's tenant due to transient 502 responses from the HEC endpoint. We are pulling retry logs and will generate reconciliation CSV for hourly sent vs acked. Suspect backpressure and connection resets at peak.
Marco Gutierrez (Support) 2026-03-12: Temporary S3 bundle uploaded: presigned urls emailed to Lina. Manifest signed with PKCS7 (signature key id: redwood-export-signing-v1). KMS rotation log excerpt attached in Confluence page. Long-term design/estimate posted to the HEC connector design doc for review.
Sven Johansson (Security Eng) 2026-03-12: Verified PKCS7 signature on manifest and validated SHA256 checksums for the sample files. KMS rotation proof included key version map and rotation timestamps. We recommend retention of signed manifests for 180 days for audit purposes.
Checked delivery logs for tenant finlybank-tenant-42: increased 5xx responses from customer HEC between 2026-02-25T18:10Z and 2026-02-26T02:45Z.
Retry subsystem queued ~18k events that were successfully retried after the endpoint recovered; however, some retries exceeded our max-backoff window and were written to 'failed-deliveries' S3 bucket — those correspond to missing events seen by customer.
Hypothesis: combination of aggressive client-side backoff + intermittent network resets on customer side led to transient drops; root cause needs coordinated network trace with customer infra team.
Verified that current export manifest generation includes SHA256 and UTC timestamps but not PKCS7 by default; implemented one-off PKCS7 signing using redwood-export-signing-v1 for temporary bundle.
KMS rotation proof: exported CloudKMS audit entries (signatures of rotation), matched key-version IDs to artifact signatures; will provide canonicalized CSV with rotation history.
Workaround delivered: Temporary signed S3 bundles provided (PKCS7 manifest, per-file SHA256 checksums, and three redacted sample payloads). Reconciliation CSV detailing hourly sent, acked, retried, and permanently failed counts for 2026-02-20 -> 2026-03-04 attached to Confluence. KMS rotation proof exported as signed CSV and uploaded to Confluence.

Permanent plan / next steps:
1) Build first-class Splunk HEC connector that supports per-tenant envelope encryption and deterministic salted hashing for identifiers; include explicit ack/backpressure handling and a persistent delivery ledger to avoid silent drops. Planned PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/siem-connectors/pull/198 (design is drafted).
2) Add PKCS7 manifest generation to the audit-service as an opt-in export mode; implement retention policy for manifests and signed archives (proposal: 180 days).
3) Implement improved retry semantics and alerting for tenant-level delivery failures, and add a dashboard in Console for per-tenant delivery success rate.
4) Coordinate a joint network trace session with FinlyBank infra for 2026-03-15 to validate connection stability under load.

Follow-ups: Marco to schedule an engineering design review (ETA 2026-03-18) and a security handoff meeting to sign off on per-tenant salt handling. Ticket will be updated with PR numbers and rollout dates.
Temporary deliverables accepted by customer on 2026-03-12. Customer confirmed PKCS7 manifest validated and reconciled counts matched provided reconciliation CSV for flagged hours. Next milestone: HEC connector design review 2026-03-18.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Orchestrator process that serializes routing/template binding state has begun emitting cohort identifiers with a transient prefix ("tmp_cohort:") which the nightly aggregation job does not normalize. This caused the weekly SLA/cohort report to undercount P1 SLAs and misattribute escalations to an empty cohort bucket.

Impact:
- Incorrect SLA cohort counts in weekly executive report for 2026-02-22 -> 2026-02-28 window.
- Automated routing tests flagged ~12% of incidents as "unmatched cohort" leading to noisy reroutes and temporary owner-flapping.
- Potential downstream billing/priority analytics skew for mid-market customers using cohort-based SLA routing.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (orchestrator v1.4.3, reporting-aggregator v2.1.0, template-compiler v0.9.8)
- Affected service: orchestrator serializer (hosted in k8s cluster cluster-orch-01) and reporting aggregation worker (batch-runner-07).

Observed behavior:
- Serialization output contains keys like "tmp_cohort:enterprise_42" instead of canonical "enterprise_42".
- Aggregator treats unknown prefix as new bucket and does not remap during aggregation window.
- Graphs on the SLA dashboard show sudden drop in counts for known cohorts and growth in "(unknown)" bucket.

Expected behavior:
- Serializer should emit canonical cohort identifiers consistently. Aggregator should either normalize known prefixes or drop malformed cohort keys and surface errors for remediation.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) On cluster-orch-01, run a dry-serialize using the current orchestrator binary against a recent routing snapshot: 
   kubectl exec -n infra orchestrator-0 -- /app/bin/orch --dry-serialize --snapshot-id=2026-02-27
2) Inspect the output payloads in /tmp/serialization-dump/*.json and grep for "tmp_cohort:" prefix.
3) Run local copy of reporting-aggregator v2.1.0 against the dump and observe separate buckets in the aggregation output.

Logs / evidence:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/SLAs/sla-cohort-overview?orgId=1&from=1646000000000&to=1646604800000
- Orchestrator logs (sample): "WARN serializer - emitted unknown cohort prefix=tmp_cohort enterprise_42" (link to log slice: https://logs.redwood.ai/orch/2026-03-01/serializer-logs.gz)
- Aggregator run metadata: batch-run-07 job id 2026-02-28-agg-71 shows "unclassified_cohorts=1354"

Business/operational notes:
This began to surface after a canary build of orchestrator was promoted to stable on 2026-02-26 (v1.4.3). The serializer binary includes a new temporary-cohort feature intended for in-progress migrations; it was supposed to set a compatibility flag but that flag was not respected when the binary ran in prod. The issue has exposure to enterprise-tier routing and weekly SLAs for multiple accounts.

2026-03-01 10:22 - Support triage (Aisha Patel): Triage complete, marking P1 due to SLA reporting impact. Assigning to platform oncall.
2026-03-01 11:05 - Oncall (Marco Alvarez): Reproduced dry-serialize locally, seeing tmp_cohort prefixes. Opening investigation; suspect serializer drift between v1.4.2 and v1.4.3. Correlating with recent canary promotion.
2026-03-01 13:40 - Reporting eng (Nina Cho): Confirmed aggregator is not normalizing unknown prefixes; current design expects canonical ids. PR to add normalization would be straightforward but we need fallback behavior for historical data.
2026-03-02 09:12 - Platform eng (Marco Alvarez): Ran quick fix: registered a transient normalization rule in routing-indexer to map tmp_cohort:* -> *. This reduces noise but does not correct already-aggregated weekly snapshots. Need backfill for the 2026-02-22 -> 2026-02-28 window.
2026-03-03 16:30 - Data eng (Rafiq Khan): Backfill job queued: backfill-cohort-normalize-20260228. ETA ~4 hours. Will re-run weekly report after backfill and flag caveats in the executive dashboard.
2026-03-04 08:50 - Security (Leah Brooks): Confirmed no PII was exposed in malformed keys; normal prefixes only. Noted that release process could use an extra gate when serializer flags are present.

Additional notes:
Hypothesis: backward-incompatible flag in serializer binary introduced a transient prefix for cohorts. Evidence: 1) deployment timeline matches spike in unclassified cohorts; 2) dry-serialize output contains "tmp_cohort:" prefix only from v1.4.3 nodes; 3) aggregator has no normalization path for that prefix. Queries run: SELECT count(*) FROM routing_snapshot WHERE cohort LIKE 'tmp_cohort:%' (result 1,354) and checked job metadata for batch-run-07; memory footprint unchanged. Root cause appears to be a config gating error in the orchestrator promote job where COMPAT_COHORT_FLAG was not set.

Technical findings:
- Orchestrator v1.4.3 binary changed serializer behavior when env var COHORT_MIGRATION_MODE=staged but the promote job did not set COHORT_MIGRATION_MODE=compat.
- Serializer emits a header X-Serializer-Compat; v1.4.3 omitted it in the production docker image build step due to a Dockerfile ARG mismatch.
- Aggregator assumed any unknown cohort string is a newly created cohort and increments unclassified counters instead of dropping or normalizing.

Short-term: Deploy serializer v1.4.4 with compatibility enforcement to prod-us-east (done 2026-03-05).
Short-term: Add transient normalization mapping tmp_cohort:* -> * in routing-indexer (applied 2026-03-02).
Mid-term: Backfill aggregator data for 2026-02-22 -> 2026-02-28 and regenerate executive weekly report (completed 2026-03-03).
Mid-term: Add unit/integration test in release pipeline to ensure X-Serializer-Compat header present for production images (work tracked in GH PR 477).
Long-term: Add guardrail in deploy pipeline to fail promotion if serializer flag mismatch detected; document migration gating in Confluence.
Partial remediation applied. Serializer rolled to v1.4.4 with compatibility enforcement and aggregator patched (v2.1.1) to ignore malformed prefix when seen in historical windows. Backfill job executed and weekly report re-generated; counts reconciled and exec dashboard updated with a note about the corrective action. Monitoring placed to watch unclassified_cohorts metric for 7 days. Follow-up ticket created to harden release gating (INT-789101).
payload.summary: Orchestrator state serializer drift causing SLA cohort aggregation mismatch in weekly reports

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer FinSpan reports intermittent gRPC streaming disconnects from model-serving pods in their private deployment. Failures manifest as TLS session resets during long-lived token streaming requests and occasional artifact fetch retries that surface as 502/handshake_failure in our logs.

Impact:
- ~15-25% increase in streaming error rate for FinSpan production traffic between 2026-03-10 08:00 and ongoing.
- Affects latency-sensitive inference endpoints and causes user-visible truncation of real-time responses.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) connected to Redwood private control plane via TGW.
- AWS Network Firewall (stateful) deployed in inspection path for egress to the internet and S3 VPCE.
- Serving nodes in subnets: private-a, private-b (us-east-1).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send long streaming inference request to the streaming endpoint (open stream, keep >30s).
2) Observe intermittent stream termination after a few dozen KB of data transmitted.
3) Repeating same test via a NAT path that bypasses the firewall appears to be stable.

Logs and artifacts:
- serving-runtime logs: "tls: received alert: handshake_failure" and "grpc: stream terminated unexpectedly (code: 14)"
- control-plane auth logs: several short-lived TLS sessions for the same client IP within <1s window.
- customer tcpdump (redacted) shows RST shortly after TLS 1.3 handshake completes for affected flows.
- pcap summary attached by customer indicates asymmetric modification of TCP options on return path (TSval/TSecr values zeroed for packets coming back through the firewall).

Customer impact level: production traffic degraded; customer requested high-priority investigation and mitigation.
2026-03-11 - FinSpan Support (Elena Gomez): Initial report — attached pcap and sample request IDs. Noted high error spike between 08:00-09:30 UTC, sees GRPC resets and S3 presigned 403s intermittently.
2026-03-11 - Support (Asha Patel): Acknowledged and escalated to SRE. Requested traceroute, tcpdump on node, and route table + firewall policy snapshot.
2026-03-12 - SRE (Diego Ramirez): Received node tcpdump and firewall policy. Observed TCP timestamp zeroing on packets egressing the firewall. Suggested bypass test to confirm hypothesis; customer started routing a test ENI via alternate NAT path.
2026-03-12 - Customer (FinSpan - NetEng, Priya Singh): After routing test traffic around the firewall the streaming instability disappeared within 5 minutes. Willing to apply temporary route change while we determine a long-term fix.
2026-03-13 - SRE (Diego Ramirez): Filed internal INT-4422 to capture change to our private-deploy runbook and detection telemetry. Drafted recommended firewall policy changes and workaround instructions.
2026-03-13 - Support (Asha Patel): Notified customer of recommended mitigations and next steps; keeping ticket open for follow-up validation post firewall policy change.
Packet-level analysis: client->server MSS, SNI and TLS ClientHello are intact on egress. Server->client return packets observed with TCP Timestamp option values reset to 0 by the firewall appliance. This is reproducible in captures when traffic traverses the firewall path.
Hypothesis: the firewall's TCP normalization feature is rewriting TCP timestamp options to enforce a stateful policy; this interacts poorly with the server's anti-replay heuristics or with TLS session resumption behavior, causing the server or the middlebox to terminate or reset the connection during/after the TLS handshake.
Reproduction: Rerouting egress traffic for the serving node to an alternate NAT gateway that does not traverse the Network Firewall eliminated the failure immediately. Reintroducing the firewall path reproduces the resets.
Correlated signals: spikes in short-lived TLS sessions and immediate RSTs line up with firewall policy changes the customer applied on 2026-03-10 07:45 UTC. No changes on Redwood side in the same window.
Configuration review: firewall policy uses stateful TCP normalization with 'rewrite timestamps' enabled. Customer confirmed this is the default hardening rule they applied recently.
Temporary test performed: added explicit route for redwood-controlplane.cust-> NAT bypass for serving subnets; streaming stabilized. Packet capture during bypass shows TSvals preserved and no immediate RSTs.
Potential false positives: we verified SNI, ALPN (h2) and TLS ciphers were unaffected and that the issue is specific to flows with long-lived gRPC streams and certain TCP option patterns.
Next diagnostic steps: request firewall vendor logs for packet normalization, obtain full firewall policy JSON, and run controlled test with tcpdump on both sides of the firewall to capture before/after packet bytes.
Owners: Diego (SRE) owns network tests and runbook update; Asha (Support) owns customer comms and scheduling policy changes with customer NetEng.
Workaround (applied by customer on 2026-03-12): added route to bypass AWS Network Firewall for egress to Redwood control plane endpoints and S3 artifact hosts. This reduced streaming error rate to baseline within 5 minutes.
Short-term remediation: customer to disable TCP timestamp rewriting (tcp-normalization) for the firewall inspection rule targeting serving subnets, or add an allow rule for our control plane and S3 hostnames so those flows are not normalized. Customer scheduled change window on 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC for permanent policy update.
Long-term actions: document firewall compatibility guidance in the Private Deploy Runbook (INT-4422) describing known problematic normalization features (TCP option rewriting, sequence number normalization) and recommended allow-lists for control plane and artifact fetch hosts.
Follow-up: Support to validate post-change captures and mark ticket Resolved once customer confirms no recurrence for 48h. If policy cannot be changed by customer, engage vendor (AWS Network Firewall support) for firmware/policy fix.
Lessons learned: add detection metric for sudden increases in short-lived TLS sessions and immediate TCP RSTs on private deploys, surfaced in Console alerts so we can surface this class of fault earlier.
Status: workaround in place; monitoring and customer validation pending.
payload.summary: Intermittent gRPC streaming disconnects: stateful network firewall rewriting TCP timestamps leads to TLS session resets

comments: Maya Thompson: Filed after two users hit recovery key prompt when returning from depot (ticket DEPOT_REPAIR_2231). Both units had NVMe replaced. Escrowed keys exist in AD but do not match local protector IDs.

Ethan Rivera: Performed manual flow: Initialize-Tpm, Clear-Tpm (handled with consent), then enable BitLocker with protectors; successful protector creation and AD escrow observed. Suggest adding explicit TPM init step in imaging.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple users report that laptops coming back from depot repair present a BitLocker recovery screen on the first boot after reimaging. The machine shows the OS as successfully applied in SCCM, but Disk Management reports the OS volume as 'Healthy (Active, Primary Partition)' while manage-bde reports no protector associated with the OS volume. Impact: Users are blocked from completing post-repair provisioning and require IT intervention to retrieve and reattach recovery keys. Scope: So far observed on two Dell Precision 5560 units and one HP EliteBook repaired during the same repair batch (DEPOT_REPAIR_2231).
1) Depot replaces NVMe, performs hardware repair, returns device to IT depot
2) Imaging team runs standard corporate image via SCCM/Task Sequence (corporate-image-2026Q1)
3) Machine boots to OOBE, completes AzureAD join and Intune enrollment
4) On first user login the system prompts for BitLocker recovery key instead of unlocking automatically
manage-bde -status output: OS volume: No Key Protectors Found
Event Viewer System: TPM error 809: 'The TPM reported an error while attempting to create a primary key' (2026-03-09 08:21:12)
SCCM Task Sequence logs: SMSTS.log shows 'Apply Operating System' succeeded; no BitLocker step errors
Intune Device Registration: MDMEnrollment logs show device ID match but BitLocker policy applied after enrollment
2026-03-10 - Initial triage by IT depot: Verified disk hardware and physical connection. NVMe verified healthy using vendor tool.
2026-03-10 - Imaging team re-ran the image on one affected device and reproduced the recovery prompt consistently after AzureAD join.
Hypothesis A: TPM ownership or TPM PCR values changed during repair (firmware wipe) so previously provisioned key protectors aren't valid for the new TPM state.
Hypothesis B: Imaging task sequence ordering applies BitLocker policy via Intune before TPM is initialized/owned, resulting in no protector created (race condition).
Checked AD: DeviceObject has escrowed BitLocker key in AD for the older device ID; keys present but protector IDs don't match manage-bde output.
2026-03-11 - Consulted with Security: Confirmed corporate BitLocker policy requires TPM+PIN for new devices; policy in Intune appears to be applied but local protector not recorded.
2026-03-12 - Reproduction attempt: Modified task sequence to explicitly run 'Initialize-Tpm -AllowClear' and then re-run BitLocker enable step; observed protector creation when run manually after TPM init.
Conclusion so far: Race between Intune/MDM policy enforcement and TPM initialization during post-image OOBE is the most likely root cause. Depot repair that resulted in TPM cleared exposes the timing bug.
Next steps: Update imaging task sequence to ensure TPM is initialized and TPM owner taken before BitLocker policy can be enforced; add telemetry to detect missing protectors post-enrollment and fail task sequence with a clear remediation step.

Additional notes:
Imaging Team - Priya Desai (2026-03-11): Reimaged one unit in lab, reproduced. Task sequence applies Windows Enrollment profile which triggers BitLocker policy from Intune immediately after MDM enrollment. Will try delaying policy enforcement step.
Security - Omar Khalid (2026-03-11): Confirmed corporate policy requires TPM+PIN. If TPM was cleared at repair, PCR values will differ and previously escrowed keys can't automatically unlock. We need to ensure a new protector is created and escrowed during enrollment.
SRE - Lina Park (2026-03-12): Filed PR to add a TPM init + protector-check step to imaging scripts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/imaging-scripts/pull/482
Customer note: No external customers impacted; internal devices only.
Workaround: IT desk can initialize TPM and run helper script to create BitLocker protector and escrow key into AD/Intune. Imaging change in progress: PR 482 adds an explicit TPM initialization and protector verification step; once merged we'll roll out updated task sequence to depot. Pending validation: Run the updated sequence on 5 devices in lab and then deploy to depot. Follow-up action: Add telemetry alert to detect 'No Key Protectors Found' after enrollment and auto-open an INT ticket for remediation.
payload.summary: Repaired workstation drops BitLocker protector and forces recovery prompt on first post-repair boot

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Support routing is repeatedly sending P1 customer tickets to the Tier-2 escalation queue after SLA window extensions. The problem appears related to priority hysteresis logic in the SLA engine: when SLA windows extend (e.g., extended first_response_due_at), downstream routing incorrectly re-evaluates priority and applies an upward escalation that should be idempotent.

Impact:
- Approximately 8-12% of P1 tickets created in the last 36 hours were re-routed to Tier-2 after a delayed SLA refresh.
- Increased load on Tier-2 on-call and delayed resolution for priority lanes that expect a single escalation hop.
- Observed duplicate notifications to on-call Slack channel (#oncall-tier2) and PagerDuty triggers in some cases.

Environment:
- Production (prod) in us-east-1 only observed so far.
- Affects support-tooling stack: SLA engine service (v2.4.1), routing-evaluator (v1.9.0), and the enrichment pipeline that applies macros/templates.

Steps to reproduce (observed flow):
1) Create a P1 customer ticket with customer_tier=dedicated and no initial assignment (SUP intake).
2) SLA engine computes initial priority and sets first_response_due_at.
3) Automated enrichment updates ticket metadata (adds escalation_hint) after 15m due to missing agent assignment.
4) SLA refresh job runs (periodic refresh triggered by kafka topic sla-refresh) and extends the SLA window because enrichment changed fields.
5) Routing-evaluator receives updated priority and applies escalation policy, routing ticket to Tier-2 even though the ticket already had a previous escalation record.

Observed logs / telemetry snippets:
- sla-engine logs: "refresh_sla: ticket=INT-76241 prev_priority=P1 new_priority=P1 reason=window-extended" (2026-03-05T14:22:03Z)
- routing-evaluator logs: "apply_escalation: ticket=INT-76241 target_queue=tier-2 force=true source=sla-refresh" (2026-03-05T14:22:04Z)
- enrichment pipeline: "macro_attach: ticket=INT-76241 added=escalation_hint=high_reassign" (2026-03-05T14:21:59Z)
- telemetry snapshot: reroute_count by hour shows spikes correlating with sla-refresh cron at hh:22.

Initial hypothesis:
- The SLA refresh path marks priority as changed when only the due timestamp changed. Downstream routing checks both priority and "changed_at" timestamp and treats any change as a candidate for forced escalation. There is missing idempotency guard for escalations tied only to timestamp shifts.

Impact analysis and risk:
- Medium-high operational risk: frequent noisy escalations could mask real Tier-2 incidents and increase MTTR.
- Low risk for data loss. Changes to evaluator logic must be safe-guarded with feature flag.

Proposed immediate mitigation:
- Add a temporary rule in routing-evaluator to ignore escalations where prev_priority == new_priority and the only delta is first_response_due_at within a tolerance window (e.g., 5 minutes). Deploy as a runtime config flag.
- Throttle automatic re-route actions to limit duplicate route events to 1 per ticket per 1h until permanent fix is deployed.

Permanent fix suggestions:
- Update SLA engine to emit a delta payload that explicitly lists what changed (priority, due_timestamp, severity) so routing can make deterministic decisions.
- Add idempotency token on escalation events persisted in routing DB to prevent duplicate actions.
- Add unit/integration tests for edge cases where only SLA timestamps change.

Required follow-ups:
- Run backfill to identify tickets impacted in last 48 hours and add manual rollback where Tier-2 assignment is incorrect.
- Postmortem draft if customer-impacting trends exceed threshold (10% of P1s misrouted).

Create P1 ticket with no assignment and dedicated tier
Trigger enrichment macro that adds escalation_hint after 10-20m
Wait for sla-refresh cron job to run and observe routing-evaluator behavior
Checked sla-refresh consumer offsets in Kafka: no lag observed; messages processed in sequence.
Replayed update for a test ticket in staging and reproduced reroute when only due_timestamp changed.
Event payload from sla-engine lacks a structured 'changed_fields' array; it only emits ticket diff as freeform text.
Emily Chen (Reporter) [2026-03-05]: Initial report filed after noticing multiple Tier-2 notifications during the 14:00 window. Added logs and telemetry charts.
Priya Nair (SRE) [2026-03-05]: I see the same pattern in PagerDuty alerts. Temporarily muting reroute notifications on #oncall-tier2 to reduce noise; will not resolve routing actions.
Raj Patel (Assignee) [2026-03-06]: Starting root-cause triage. Reproduced in staging. Creating feature-flagged patch to routing-evaluator to ignore timestamp-only diffs.
Ana Gomez (Platform Eng) [2026-03-08]: Submitted PR to routing-evaluator to add idempotency key storage: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-evaluator/pull/289. Needs QA and canary.
CS Lead - Marcus Lee [2026-03-09]: Please prepare a customer-impact brief if we see escalation rates continue; notify accounts with potential delays.
In progress: feature-flagged guard merged to routing-evaluator canary and rolled out to 10% of pods on 2026-03-09. Early telemetry shows 90% reduction in duplicate escalations for canary traffic. Next steps: full rollout after 48h canary and SLA-engine signature change to include structured changed_fields. Manual fixes for 17 affected tickets in the last 24h are in the backlog assigned to CS ops.
Enable routing-evaluator runtime config 'ignore_timestamp_only_sla_changes=true' and set reroute_throttle_per_ticket=1h. Manual reassignment for misrouted tickets via support console.
Partial mitigation applied; permanent fix planned (SLA engine contract change + idempotency).
Quantify total P1 misroutes in 72h window
Timeline of changes to sla-refresh consumer and enrichment macro rollout
Evaluate adding schema to SLA events (changed_fields) and updating routing contract
payload.summary: SLA priority hysteresis causing repeated misrouting to Tier-2 queue

Lena Morales: Assigned for remediation. Plan: verify proxy rollout state and confirm whether we need to rollback the conditional IAM or complete the proxy rollout.

Lena Morales: Completed hot rollout to 100% of infra-proxy-prod with v2026.03.05. Monitoring shows successful token-exchange rate increased from ~97% to ~99.99% in last 12 hours. Continuing observation window 24h.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We observed intermittent authorization failures when the prod inference service in the aws-main account attempts to assume the analytics-reader role in the gcp-analytics project via our federation bridge. Failures present as AccessDenied errors in the bridge logs and missing events in downstream analytics pipelines.

Impact:
- Analytics ingestion has sporadic gaps for ~3% of inference requests routed to analytics, causing skew in usage metrics and billing attribution.
- No user-facing outage, but metrics/reports used for billing and capacity planning are affected.

Environment:
- prod (aws-main account id: 111122223333) -> federation proxy -> gcp-analytics (project: redwood-analytics-prod)
- Bridge implemented via short-lived AWS STS -> GCP workload identity federation with a proxies service in k8s (cluster infra-proxy-prod).

Observed behavior:
- STS AssumeRole returns success, then proxy attempts to exchange credentials for GCP identity and receives HTTP 403 / IAM_PERMISSION_DENIED from IAM token exchange endpoint.
- CloudTrail shows successful AssumeRole calls from the proxy service but the token-exchange step to GCP fails in same minute windows.
- Errors appear concentrated in us-east-1, with a smaller spike in us-west1.

Expected behavior:
- Seamless role chaining with sub-second token exchange success and no authorization errors.

Steps to reproduce / replication steps:
1) Trigger a synthetic inference workload from prod that routes telemetry to analytics (use synthetic job id SNY-permcheck-2026).
2) Tail infra-proxy-prod logs in namespace infra-proxy-prod: kubectl logs -f deploy/proxy --since=10m.
3) Monitor CloudTrail AssumeRole logs for caller arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/proxy-role/* and check GCP token exchange endpoint logs (token-exchange.googleapis.com).
4) Observe 403 errors on token-exchange and correlate with STS success entries.

Logs / Evidence:
- infra-proxy-prod logs snippet (Mar 10 03:14 UTC): "ERROR token-exchange: failed to exchange aws-session for gcp-identity: status=403 detail=Permission denied: serviceAccountTokenCreator missing"
- CloudTrail (Mar 10 03:14 UTC): AssumeRole succeeded for principal: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/proxy-role
- GCP audit (redwood-analytics-prod): "MethodName=GenerateAccessToken Resource=serviceAccount:redwood-analytics-sa@redwood-analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com Response=PERMISSION_DENIED"

Additional notes:
- This pattern started around 2026-03-08 after the infra team rotated a subset of service account bindings and tightened a set of IAM conditions for serviceAccountTokenCreator on the analytics service account.
- The issue is intermittent; many exchanges succeed while others get PERMISSION_DENIED. Hypothesis: a policy condition tied to "request.time" or tag propagation may intermittently not be present on short-lived session credentials.
Initial hypotheses and checks performed:
- Hypothesis 1: Role chaining works but GCP service account binding condition rejects some sessions. Checked GCP IAM binding history and found a recent addition of a conditional binding requiring attribute 'aws:principalTag/env=prod'.
- Hypothesis 2: Tag propagation from AWS STS -> proxy -> GCP token exchange is missing for some requests because proxy does not forward session tags. Confirmed proxy code path only attaches tags when NewSession field set; synthetic tests showed missing tags in failing traces.
- Performed deterministic replay with synthetic session that included aws:sts:session-tag env=prod and saw token-exchange succeed 100% of the time.
- Correlated logs: failing traces consistently lacked session metadata header X-AWS-Session-Tags.
- Checked ks-config for infra-proxy-prod: older deployment revision (v2026.02.18) does not include the session-tag middleware; new revision (v2026.03.05) includes it but rollout partial (50%).
- Risk assessment: partial rollout plus conditional IAM bindings explains intermittent nature.
- Related infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4721 (adds session-tag passthrough).

Additional notes:
Infra Oncall (Rami Durand) (2026-03-11): Checked k8s rollout: infra-proxy-prod at revision v2026.03.05 at 50% healthy. Node selector mismatch caused half of pods to remain on older revision. Opening hotfix rollout.
Security (Priya Kaur) (2026-03-11): Conditional IAM binding was applied intentionally to reduce blast radius. We prefer fixing proxy to preserve security posture rather than reverting IAM change.
Partial remediation completed (2026-03-12):
- Deployed infra-proxy-prod v2026.03.05 to 100%, which includes session-tag passthrough middleware. This addresses the missing X-AWS-Session-Tags header that caused GCP conditional IAM bindings to reject some exchanges.
- No rollback of GCP conditional IAM performed; security team prefers this posture.
- Observed success rate for token exchanges improved to ~99.99%.
- Follow-ups:
  1) Run reconciliation backfill job for analytics (task assigned to analytics team, job id: ANL-FILL-2026-03-12).
  2) Add synthetic end-to-end regression to infra CI to validate session-tag passthrough on every proxy deploy (infra ticket INT-200101 created).
  3) Update runbook in Confluence with troubleshooting steps and common error signatures.
- Status: Monitoring (will close once backfill confirmed and 48h of stable telemetry observed).
Until proxy rollout completed, temporarily add an exception for the conditional IAM by allowing the token-exchange principal (proxy-role) an unconditional serviceAccountTokenCreator permission. This was considered but rejected by Security; prefer completing proxy rollout.
1) Verify analytics backfill completes and confirm metrics aligned (owner: Analytics Team).
2) Add synthetic regression to CI and gate proxy deployments on tag passthrough tests (owner: Infra).
3) Close ticket after 48h stable observation and successful backfill.
4) Postmortem to capture rollout process gap and add guardrail to k8s rollout automation to avoid partial revision stuck on node selectors.
Key observables: CloudTrail AssumeRole entries, infra-proxy logs for X-AWS-Session-Tags header presence, GCP IAM audit for GenerateAccessToken PERMISSION_DENIED.
Escalation path: #infra-support -> oncall -> secops if permission changes requested.
payload.summary: Validate cross-account role chaining and remediate permission gaps for prod->analytics IAM bridge

comments: Aisha Patel: Filing because teams keep asking for quicker experiment spin-up with predictable teardown. Security wants an auditable snapshot of who had access when.
Liam Chen: Adding initial acceptance criteria. Will investigate whether Confluence API supports clean export/import of page-level restrictions; if not, we will build a mapping layer.
Liam Chen: Marking pre-design complete. Next actions: spike Confluence restrictions export (ETA 2026-02-22) and prototype handshake emails/DMs. Linking related tickets.
payload.description:
Background: Rapid experiment teams frequently request cloned Confluence spaces spun up from a canonical template. Current manual cloning loses a reliable snapshot of page restrictions and group membership, and onboarding owners is manual. This increases audit overhead and causes surprises when access needs to be reverted after a project ends.

Request: Implement an automated, conditional Confluence space cloning flow that: 1) performs a template-based clone of a source space; 2) captures and stores an RBAC snapshot (groups, page restrictions, explicit user grants) for the cloned space; 3) triggers an ownership handshake workflow (invites nominated owner(s) to accept ownership within a configurable TTL, default 72 hours); 4) returns the space to a quarantine/archive state if ownership is not accepted; 5) optionally creates matching Jira project skeleton and Slack channel with linked lifecycle hooks.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- A self-serve UI or slash-command triggers a clone with parameters (source template, owners list, ttl, create-jira, create-slack).
- RBAC snapshot is stored as an auditable artifact (read-only) and accessible to security/audit teams.
- Owners receive an email and Slack DM with an accept/reassign link; acceptance flips a 'live' flag and sets retention rules.
- If ownership not accepted within TTL, space is set to "archived-quarantine" and requestor + infra notified.
- Audit log entries created for clone and ownership events; Confluence page-level restrictions are preserved in the cloned space.
- Optional Jira project and Slack channel created when toggle enabled; each gets lifecycle hooks tied to the Confluence space state.

Why this matters: Reduces manual steps, prevents lingering access after short experiments, and provides an auditable RBAC snapshot for compliance reviews.

Proposed timeline: 3 sprints (discovery + design; automation prototype + RBAC export; owner handshake + lifecycle integration + rollout).

Contacts: Aisha Patel (Product, requester), Liam Chen (Platform eng, primary assignee), Priya Rao (Security reviewer)
Self-serve clone action with parameters exposed in Console and via a slash-command
RBAC snapshot (groups, page restrictions, explicit grants) persisted and queryable by security/audit
Owner handshake invites sent (email + Slack) and accept/reassign recorded in audit log
TTL-based auto-archive/quarantine if no acceptance within configured window
Optional Jira and Slack resources created and linked; lifecycle sync to Confluence state
Trigger clone from Console using 'Clone with RBAC snapshot' option
Verify cloned space content matches template and page restrictions are present
Check audit artifact for RBAC snapshot containing groups and explicit grants
Confirm owner handshake message sent and acceptance flips space to live
Simulate TTL expiry and validate space moves to archived/quarantine state and notifications fire
If toggled, verify corresponding Jira skeleton and Slack channel exist and are linked
Risk: Automated cloning could inadvertently grant broader access if RBAC snapshot applied incorrectly. Mitigation: Implement a dry-run mode that logs intended grants without applying them; require security approval for initial rollout to top-level spaces; limit self-serve to templates in a vetted namespace.
Confluence API: space export supports content and attachments; page restrictions available via REST endpoints per page (will need iterative crawl)
Potential privacy gap: explicit user grants on pages could include external collaborators—ensure export flags external identities
Slack provisioning: can create channels via admin API but workspace bot needs 'channels:write' and 'users:read' scopes; approval required
Jira skeleton: use existing project templates API; must ensure project key naming avoids collisions

Additional notes:
Priya Rao (Security) (2026-02-12): Security: prefer RBAC snapshots stored in S3 with object versioning and limited KMS keys. Also require owner acceptance TTL not be shorter than 48h by default.
SRE (2026-02-14): Note: Slack channel creation requires workspace app scopes; will need a short security review of bot scopes and to coordinate with infra for app provisioning.
Initial rollout to 3 pilot teams (Model Evals, Growth Experiments, Integrations) gated by security sign-off. Monitor audit logs for 2 weeks; schedule rollback plan: disable self-serve and run manual cleanups.
Spike: Confluence page restriction export (owner: Liam Chen)
Implement RBAC artifact storage (owner: Platform infra)
Build owner handshake UX and email templates (owner: Product)
payload.summary: Enable conditional Confluence space cloning with ownership handshake and RBAC snapshot for ephemeral project spaces

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Windows 11 laptops intermittently lose connectivity to internal services after roaming between APs. The WireGuard interface remains up but the system installs a stale 0.0.0.0/0 route pointing at the local wifi gateway (metric low), effectively blackholing outbound traffic for processes bound to the wg interface. DNS queries either fail or go to the wrong resolver.

Impact:
- ~8 active users in the SF office reporting repeated failures during heavy roaming (moving between floors / boardroom).
- Symptoms: applications time out (internal dashboards, git pushes), developer shells lose connections, Slack remains connected but messages to internal services fail.

Environment:
- OS: Windows 11 22H2 (build 22631.x)
- Wireless chipset: Intel AX211 / AX201 (driver 22.50.1 reported on affected machines)
- VPN: WireGuard v0.7.6 (enterprise config via enterprise-agent)
- Zero-trust/agent: redwood-edge v2.1.0 (manages wg interface and DNS overrides)
- SSID: Redwood-Corp (802.11ax, controller-managed fast-roaming/FT enabled)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect to Redwood-Corp from a Windows 11 laptop with WireGuard active.
2) Walk between two nearby APs or trigger a roam using the vendor utility (force roam).
3) Observe that user retains WPA2/WPA3 session but some processes lose access to internal services.
4) Run 'wg show', 'route print', and 'nslookup internal-service'.

Observed behavior / logs (excerpt):
- route print shows 0.0.0.0 -> 192.168.10.1 metric 10 (preferred) coexisting with wg0 route 0.0.0.0 -> 10.10.0.1 metric 50; processes bound to wg0 still attempt outbound but packets never egress correctly.
- WireGuard peers show keepalives delayed; 'wg show' shows handshake timestamps stall for 30–120s.
- Windows System event: WLAN AutoConfig reported 'Roaming completed' then 'Driver queued packets during power save transition'.
- tcpdump on edge gateway shows missing keepalives during DTIM handover windows.

Initial hypothesis:
- Wireless driver power-management / DTIM handling during fast roaming causes packet queuing and delayed keepalives; WireGuard's endpoint detection thinks tunnel still healthy but routing table gets re-ordered when interface metrics are recalculated.
- Controller fast-roaming timers (FT) combined with Windows power profile and driver implementation create a race where the default route is re-inserted before wg interface routes stabilize.

Impact assessment:
- P1 due to multiple developers blocked during peak hours; intermittent but reproducible in SF office.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced on 2 lab machines with same Intel AX211 driver.
- Disabling 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' on the WLAN adapter immediately eliminated the symptom on test devices.
- Changing Windows Power Plan (Wireless Adapter Settings -> Power Saving Mode = Maximum Performance) also mitigated.
- On the controller side, reducing FT roam aggressiveness and increasing reassociation hold time reduced the frequency but did not fully eliminate.
- Packet captures show keepalives delayed by up to 90s during roam; WireGuard handshake resumes but application sockets experience default TCP timeouts.
- Intune profile was used to push temporary registry settings and wireless power plan to a pilot group (10 machines) with success.

Mitigation applied:
- Deployed Intune device configuration to pilot cohort (10 users in SF) to set Wireless Adapter power to Maximum Performance and to disable the 'allow device to sleep' option.
- Rolled controller config change to throttle FT handoffs to be less aggressive (increase reassociation timer to 500ms).
- Sent bug report to Intel with packet captures and driver logs; vendor acknowledged potential driver-side race and requested additional telemetry.

Next steps / plan:
- Expand Intune mitigation to all SF office laptops (scheduled phased rollout over 3 days).
- Validate Intel driver fix when available; test in lab (matrix: Windows builds x driver versions x WG config).
- Add a customer-side guard in redwood-edge agent: detect roaming handshake gap > 10s and force reassertion of wg route metrics (work queued as GH PR).
- Update wireless runbook with mitigation steps and add monitoring rule for 'wg handshake gap' on fleet.

Related artifacts and links:
- Packet captures: s3://redwood-captures/INT-864209/roam-pcap-0309.pcap (internal)
- Controller config change PR: https://git.internal.redwood.net/network/configs/pull/122

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 16:20 - Security (Rajiv Sinha): Confirmed Intune changes do not change firewall posture or keys. OK to proceed to wider rollout after test window.
Key findings: driver queues during DTIM handoff; WireGuard keepalives delayed; Windows route recalculation introduces lower-metric gateway route before wg routes reassert. Temporary device-level power profile fix works; network controller tuning reduces frequency. Next: agent-level guard and vendor driver fix. Refer to controller logs and wg handshake graphs in the packet capture directory.
Mitigations: Intune policy (wireless adapter power = Maximum Performance, disable 'allow device to sleep') deployed to pilot and now expanded to full SF office. Controller FT timers adjusted. Long-term: validate Intel driver fix and merge agent guard (GH PR linked). Will mark Resolved after successful validation of vendor driver across 2-week window.
Expand Intune rollout to SF office (scheduled 2026-03-15 to 2026-03-17)
Validate new Intel driver in test matrix and report results
Implement agent-level route reassert guard (PR linked)
payload.summary: Windows 11 roaming + adapter power-save causing WireGuard route ghosting and DNS failures on corporate Wi‑Fi

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Request from Audit team to provision a timeboxed (expiring) set of collaboration artifacts for external guest auditors: a Confluence space scoped to the audit, a Slack channel with restricted posting, and a scoped Jira project for evidence collection. The workspace must be gated by a security approval step (Slack-based approval bot or approver group) and automatically revoke guest access after the timebox expires.

Request:
- Automate creation of Confluence space, Slack channel (#audit-<id>-guest), and Jira project (AUDIT-<id>-guest) on request form submission.
- Trigger a security approval workflow: send approval request to #security-approvals and to the Security Approvers group in Slack; only after explicit approval should guest accounts be provisioned.
- Provision guest accounts with minimum privileges; map to a temporary group that auto-expires at T+30 days (configurable).
- Ensure audit logging for provisioning actions and create a Confluence page template (audit kickoff) pre-populated with requested metadata.

Impact:
- Improves compliance and reduces manual overhead for Audit/Legal when onboarding short-term external auditors.
- Reduces risk of lingering guest accounts.

Acceptance criteria:
1) On submitted request (Jira form or Confluence template), an automated job creates the Confluence space, Slack channel, and Jira project in a queued transaction and marks the request as "Pending Approval".
2) Security approvers receive an interactive approval message in Slack; approval triggers provisioning. Denial halts provisioning and notifies requester.
3) Guest accounts are assigned to a time-limited group that is removed from all artifacts automatically at expiry; a post-expiry email is sent to the requestor and security.
4) Provisioning events are written to audit log (Confluence/Atlassian audit logs + internal infra logs) with correlation ID.
5) A Confluence kickoff page is created from the template and includes links to the Jira project and Slack channel.

Proposed implementation:
- Reuse existing automation pipeline in platform-infra (Terraform module for space/channel/project creation) and extend with a new `guest_workspace` module that supports `approval_hook` and `expiry_days` properties.
- Implement Slack interactive message using existing bot (Bot service) to avoid adding new credentials. Approval events post back to the automation service via signed webhook.
- Add a scheduled cleanup job (daily) that scans for expired guest groups and performs revocation, then creates a Jira ticket for manual review if revocation fails.
- Store ephemeral group membership in Vault and record provisioning events in S3 audit bucket and Atlassian audit logs.

Security & compliance considerations:
- Guests must be flagged and have MFA enforced if possible. Work with IAM to ensure guests cannot access sensitive spaces outside the provisioned Confluence space.
- Approval flow must require at least one Security Approver and one Audit Owner.
- All artifacts and steps must be logged for SOC2 evidence.

Runbook & rollback:
- Runbook link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/908172/Guest+Provisioning+Runbook
- Rollback: on partial failure, automation should tear down any created artifacts and post a failure summary with correlation ID. Manual rollback steps documented in runbook.

Notes:

- Consider adding an investor/third-party NDA gating step in a follow-on ticket if needed.

HR and Security want a documented and auditable flow that lets new hires start work with minimal risk. This ticket asks for clarity on acceptable temporary identity/service-account patterns, MFA handover rules, and device-binding expectations.

Background:
- New hire (software engineer) based in APAC has start date before hardware arrival.
- Current options considered: 1) loaner company laptop shipped locally, 2) temporary shadow account with limited privileges, 3) contractor-style bridge account.
- Security wants MFA to be enforced, but hardware (company phone) will arrive later than start date.

Impact:

- Teams reported delays in ramp time and onboarding blockers for early-start hires.

Request:
- Confirm policy for (a) issuing timebound shadow accounts, (b) acceptable MFA alternatives until company device available, and (c) required steps to convert temporary identity to full employee account and revoke temporary creds.

- A concise policy bullet list and a recommended runbook for Support/IT to follow per-hire.

Security (J. Rosen) raised two constraints: (1) no shared credentials, (2) MFA must be enforced but can be TOTP app or FIDO2; hardware phone not strictly required if user has a personal device enrolled under a temporary policy.

Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 we observed a concentrated spike of short-lived LDAP binds originating from multiple internal service accounts immediately after several employees submitted an external survey form linked in a marketing email. These binds were to the LDAP bind DN used for CI/CD service accounts and had a pattern of rapid failed attempts followed by a small number of successful binds from geographically diverse IPs.

Impact:
- Potential compromise or credential reuse of service account credentials used by internal CI/CD and monitoring tools.
- Temporary increase in directory authentication failures affecting metric collection (10-20% higher error rate for 30 minutes).
- No confirmed data exfiltration as of last update; some dashboards showed partial gaps while retries were happening.

Environment:
- Production directory (OpenLDAP-managed by infra).
- Region: us-east-1.
- Affected authentication path: ldap-bind service account DNs used by CI runners and exporters.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-10 10:22: first anomalous failed binds detected by IDS (suspicious user agent and uncommon source IPs).
- 2026-03-10 10:24: spike increases; Security alert triggers automated rule and pages oncall.
- 2026-03-10 10:30: detection of ~8 successful binds from 3 distinct external ASN ranges for two service accounts.
- 2026-03-10 10:35: SRE rotates the LDAP bind credentials for impacted service accounts and cuts immediate access.
- 2026-03-10 11:05: Evidence of additional login attempts from previously unseen IPs stops after credential rotation.

Observed indicators:
- Bind pattern: repeated failed binds with short intervals (0.5-1s) followed by 1-2 successful binds per account.
- User agent strings: generic curl/wget patterns and a terse bot UA: "SurveyFetch/1.0" (likely from the external survey system).
- Source IPs clustered across 3 ASNs that host common marketing/survey vendors and some suspicious residential ranges.

Steps taken so far:
1) Oncall rotated LDAP bind credentials for 4 service accounts at 2026-03-10 10:35.
2) Temporarily blocked suspicious source IP ranges at edge WAF and firewall.
3) Scoped logs (auth, CI, proxy) for related successful binds and correlated with CI run IDs and deploy events.
4) Notified Product Security and Compliance; created this internal ticket for triage.
5) Disabled automatic survey-webhook ingestion to internal systems pending vendor validation.

Immediate hypothesis:
- Employees clicked an external marketing/survey link that triggered the third-party vendor to fetch assets or embedded resources using service account credentials (credential exposure via referer or webhook configuration), or attackers used harvested credentials to attempt automation-driven binds.

Evidence still needed:
- Full mapping between the external survey vendor fetch logs and the timestamps of successful binds.
- Proof whether credentials were exfiltrated (no confirmed downstream API calls with those credentials beyond the observed binds).
- Any suspicious process-level activity on CI runners around the times of successful binds.

Next recommended steps:
- Forensic image/collect logs from CI runner hosts that used the rotated service accounts (SRE).
- Vendor engagement: request survey vendor to produce access logs for 2026-03-10 09:50-11:00 UTC.
- Expand firewall blocks to ASN-level while preserving customer-facing vendor connectivity (Network).
- Rotate any other LDAP bind credentials that share patterns or were created in the same provisioning window.
- Run org-wide safe-scan for tokens embedded in public forms/webhooks (Security).

Communication notes:

- Customer-facing teams: none impacted directly; internal incident only.

10:29 UTC: Correlated CI job IDs show no deployment triggered at same time; binds did not coincide with a scheduled run

Issue summary: After depot SSD replacement and reimaging, affected devices fail to complete the provisioning pipeline. The provisioning agent stalls during the post-imaging user-profile phase when the system attempts to rotate btrfs snapshots via snapper. Impact: Depot staging queue throughput reduced; ~8% of devices hit the stall and require manual intervention (reimage or manual mount). Environment: Depot imaging pod (staging us-west), btrfs root filesystem with snapper-enabled snapshot rotation. Observed behavior: provisioning-agent logs show repeated 'Device busy' and 'failed to remove old snapshot' errors; root mount eventually remounts read-only on a subset of hardware after disk firmware update. Expected behavior: snapper rotates snapshots cleanly and provisioning completes without manual steps.
1) Replace SSD in depot lab device and apply firmware baseline (firmware v1.4.2).
2) Boot into PXE image and run standard depot imaging task sequence (depot-imaging-2026Q1).
3) Allow SCCM/Provisioning agent to run post-image tasks including snapper cleanup and user profile restore.
4) Observe provisioning-agent at 'post-image: user-profile mount' step; on affected devices the step hangs for >20 minutes and eventually fails with snapshot removal errors.
/var/log/provisioning-agent.log: 2026-03-10T09:12:03Z ERROR snapper: failed to remove snapshot 2026-03-10_09-10: Device or resource busy
kernel dmesg excerpt:  [  241.532112] BTRFS error (device sda1): unable to delete inode 123456: -16 (Device or resource busy)
system journal: provisioning-agent[2145]: Waiting for loop device /dev/loop0 to unmount; stuck on busy loop
Initial hypothesis: new SSD firmware changes block discard/TRIM sequences causing btrfs metadata transactions to hang during snapshot cleanup.
Cross-checked similar failures in prod imaging logs — no recent occurrences before firmware v1.4.2 rollout to depot hardware.
Reproduced locally in staging by flashing firmware v1.4.2 to a test Dell 7440: confirmed snapper cleanup intermittently fails when snapper tries to delete oldest snapshot while a background scrub/garbage-collect is running.
Temporary workaround applied at depot: disable automatic snapper rotation step in the provisioning task sequence for affected hardware class; this allows provisioning to continue but leaves snapshot backlog (follow-up required).
Raised a kernel/firmware hypothesis with Platform Eng: linked to btrfs handling of discard on qemu/nvme combo; asked Eng to triage kernel traces and fio workload reproduction.
Attached strace and block traces collected from failed host saved in /mnt/depot-artifacts/INT-434210/
Asha Menon (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed a cluster of staging devices stuck in provisioning today after SSD replacement. Creating ticket to track investigation and depot mitigations.
Depot Tech (Marcus Lee) 2026-03-10: When I hit the hang I manually killed snapper cleanup and mounted the fs; after remounting provisioning continued but user profile restore failed until reimage. Placing affected devices on hold in the queue.
Diego Ruiz (Assignee) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally; collecting bpftrace/blkparse traces. Disabling snapper rotation as short-term mitigation. Coordinating with platform-eng for kernel trace review.
Platform Eng (Sana Kapoor) 2026-03-12: Requested full kernel oops and blk traces; suspect interaction between firmware v1.4.2 and btrfs qgroup accounting during discard. Will prioritize a repro and patch candidate.
Depot Ops (J. O'Neill) 2026-03-12: Applied change to depot task sequence to skip snapper rotation for devices with firmware >=1.4.2. Tracking manual cleanup backlog as sprint work item.
Diego Ruiz 2026-03-12: Marking this ticket In Progress; follow-up PR and confluence runbook link below once triage complete.
Mitigation: Depot imaging task sequence updated to skip automatic snapper rotation for affected firmware class (v1.4.2+). Manual snapshot cleanup runbook created for depot techs. Engineering follow-up: platform-eng to reproduce and provide kernel patch or recommended firmware rollback. Post-fix tasks: revert task-sequence change, run a controlled firmware rollout, add an automated check to fail imaging early if snapper queue grows >50 snapshots.
