Ayesha Kapoor (Reporter) — 2026-03-10: Noticed spike in support pages around 21:00 UTC. Several engineers reported identical 403s when attempting to assume runbooks during an incident. Placing ticket to capture and track triage.
Diego Martinez (Assignee) — 2026-03-10: Triage started. Reproduced locally against staging by replaying auth-proxy cookies. Hypothesis: session cookie rotation + concurrent login can cause stale owner_id to be read from cookie cache. Collecting more traces.
Elena Park (SRE) — 2026-03-11: Added temporary logging on auth-proxy to dump session-token hashes (non-PII) and correlation id. Saw 4 traces where owner_id was swapped between two active sessions originating from same client IP but different devices.
Marco Chen (Identity eng) — 2026-03-12: Instrumented identity service to log token issuance events and nonce mapping. Found race in session-store snapshot write path when multiple SSO flows commit near-simultaneously for the same user via different devices. Working on a fix to make writes atomic.
Diego Martinez — 2026-03-13: Rolling out a hotfix to session-store which adds optimistic locking on session keys. Will monitor for 24 hours.
Reproduction: Lowered concurrency window in staging and reproduced owner_id mismatch by firing two near-simultaneous device-trust SSO flows for same username.
Root cause hypothesis: session-store (redis snapshot + local in-memory cache) allowed a stale snapshot to be applied during concurrent session creation, causing the new session to inherit the owner_id from the other session's transient state.
Correlated alerts: Spike in runbook-service 403s at the same timestamps as session-store write contention metrics on redis-master-2 (see perf graph).
Temporary mitigations tested: added 100ms linear backoff on session-store write retry eliminated reproductions in staging under the test harness.
Edge case: cross-region redirected OIDC callbacks appear to exacerbate probability due to increased callback latency; eu-west report likely a compounded factor.
If impersonation fails, wait ~60-120s and retry. For urgent escalations, use alternate support account (with manual verification) or SSH into a bastion with SRE-approved out-of-band escalation. On-call runbook includes steps to use the temporary-bypass CLI token (audit-logged).
Deploy optimistic-locking hotfix to session-store to prod us-east (Diego/Marco) — in progress
Monitor 403 rate for runbook-service and session-store write contention — SRE dashboard updated
Follow-up: review callback timeouts and add metrics for OIDC callback latency per region (Elena)
Postmortem and permanent fix: refactor session creation to single-source-of-truth commit path (identity eng roadmap)
payload.summary: Intermittent SSO session owner_id shadowing prevents runbook impersonation and CLI elevation

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer AsterHealth reports intermittent 401/403 when calling Redwood Private inference endpoints. Errors correlate with requests that traverse their on-prem HTTP proxy. Impact: Several production endpoints for routing inference requests are failing ~3-7% of traffic causing degraded user experience for API consumers. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed ingress), prod-us-east. Observed behavior: Token exchange attempts fail with 401 from identity-proxy; Redwood logs show Authorization header value truncated at first space. Expected behavior: Full Bearer token should be forwarded intact and validated by identity service.
1) Customer issues curl request through on-prem proxy: curl -x http://proxy:8080 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <LONG_TOKEN>' https://private-api.customer.redwood/v1/generate
2) Some requests return 401 with response body {"error":"invalid_token"}, other requests succeed (intermittent).
3) Direct curl to private endpoint (bypassing proxy) succeeds every time.
4) Packet capture at proxy shows header value split across two lines (folded) where a CRLF SP insertion occurs within token string.
ingress-proxy (2026-03-13T15:02:11Z) - received header: 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9 ...',
ingress-proxy (2026-03-13T15:02:11Z) - forwarded header: 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9\r\n  abcdef...'
identity-proxy (2026-03-13T15:02:11Z) - token parse failed: token contains unexpected whitespace -> returning 401
application logs show 401 and 403 spikes that align with proxy flow start times (see dashboard: /dashboards/ingress/401-spike-AsterHealth)
Checked Redwood ingress and identity-proxy traces; token is valid when received directly from customer app but appears truncated/contains whitespace when forwarded via on-prem proxy.
Packet capture from customer's proxy shows header folding (HTTP line folding) - a historical behavior where proxies insert CRLF+SP for long headers. This is deprecated in HTTP/1.1 and leads to the token containing a literal newline+space sequence which our token parser rejects.
Customer confirmed proxy is an older F5 BIG-IP configuration with 'allow-http-folding' behavior enabled in the intermediary iRules. Proxy vendor docs indicate toggles exist to disable header folding or to normalize headers.
Reproduced locally by configuring an nginx reverse proxy with 'proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization; more_clear_input_headers...' and forcing injection of CRLF SP - token parsing fails similarly.
Temporal correlation: incidents started after customer upgraded proxy firmware to a build that changed default header handling (03/10/2026).
Priya Shah (Support) 2026-03-13: Raised initial ticket after customer report. Collected traces and asked for pcap. Requested exact proxy model and firmware.
AsterHealth SRE (customer) 2026-03-13: Attached pcap and proxy config snippet. Confirmed recent firmware change on appliance. Asked if Redwood can tolerate folded headers.
Maya Chen (Eng) 2026-03-13: Ran local repro, confirmed token parser rejects whitespace. Opening internal issue to add clearer logging for folded headers. Assigned INT-448 for infra follow-up.
AsterHealth SRE 2026-03-14: Applied temporary workaround on proxy (disabled header folding) and reported immediate reduction to 0.2% failure rate.
On-prem proxy inserts HTTP header line folding (CRLF SP) into Authorization header for long values. Identity/token parser treats whitespace as invalid and returns 401. The customer's proxy firmware default changed behavior in a recent upgrade.
Workaround provided: Customer updated F5 iRule and disabled header folding behavior and validated end-to-end. Short-term: advised customer to upgrade proxy to vendor patch that preserves header single-line semantics or apply config flag to disable folding. Long-term: internal change: ingress now detects folded header sequences and emits a 400 with explicit 'folded-authorization' code and guidance to customer instead of returning generic 401; created PR github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/pull/612 to add debug logging and a clearer error message. Runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SITE/Proxy+compatibility+runbook. Follow-up task INT-448 created to consider tolerant header normalization with strict validation for downstream auth (pending security review).
Customer applied workaround at 2026-03-14 09:18 UTC; support observed immediate reduction in errors.
Added temporary alert on ingress for any Authorization header containing CRLF or leading whitespace; will be monitored for 72 hours.
Security reviewed proposal to do on-the-fly header unfolding: currently rejected for private deployments due to risk of accepting modified tokens. Team will instead provide explicit diagnostics and vendor guidance.
Scheduled follow-up with AsterHealth for 2026-03-18 to verify stability and discuss preventative controls.
1) Engineering to ship clearer ingress error message (PR #612) and ensure runbook contains vendor-specific guidance for F5/HAProxy/Nginx rules.
2) SRE to monitor alert for folded Authorization headers and escalate if frequency rises above 0.5%.
3) Customer success to confirm AsterHealth has scheduled proxy firmware update to latest vendor recommended build.
payload.summary: On-prem proxy header folding trims Authorization token, causing intermittent 401/403 in private deployment

comments: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z Priya Shah: Filed after three reports from depot last week; batch ID DPT-2026-03-10. Noticed asset tag matched an existing record but DiskSignature differed.

2026-03-02T00:00:00Z Mateo Alvarez: I pulled two affected devices into bench, captured disk signatures and partition GUIDs. See attached export in Bitbucket: repo/repairs/INT-892345/ (private). Initial hypothesis: NVMe vendor firmware write during reflow resets/reset UUID fields.

2026-03-03T00:00:00Z Imaging: Re-imaged an affected unit with the same image, device normalized and registered correctly. Suggests issue occurs only post-repair before depot image re-flash. Potential hardware/firmware ordering artifact.
2026-03-03T00:00:00Z Mateo Alvarez: Requested depot to run vendor NVMe secure-erase workflow rather than reflow; holding further repairs until we confirm.
payload.description:
Issue summary: After depot repair (NVMe replacement or reflow) some devices boot with the OS disk signature and partition GUIDs reordered. This triggers our assetdb/device fingerprinting logic to report a different Device ID back to Intune/Autopilot. Impact: devices appear as duplicate assets, Autopilot hostnames collide (hostname-1, hostname-1-1), and deployment policies targeted by device ID do not apply. Scope observed: ~7 devices from the same repair batch over the last two weeks. Not observed in fresh builds from imaging lab.
1) Receive repaired device from depot with NVMe replacement. 2) Power on and complete Windows OOBE. 3) Device auto-enrolls in Intune / Autopilot. 4) Check assetdb entry and compare Disk signature (via 'wmic diskdrive get serialnumber' and 'Get-PnpDevice' combined with disk GUIDs). 5) Observe duplicated Device ID and hostname collision in Autopilot console.
Event log snippets:
- System: Kernel-Boot: Boot device changed: "NVMe0n1" -> partition order: 1,3,2
- MDT/Task Sequence: TSManager: Applied image "CorpWin11-Image" (success)
- Intune MDM: Enrollment token accepted for deviceID: 9f2b-... but assetdb maps to existing asset with device tag 'DLT-7440-234'
- Autopilot: Duplicate hostname collision detected for serial: G7G12345
- Diskpart list: Disk 0 Online, Partition 1=EFI(100MB), Partition 2=MSR, Partition 3=Windows (C:)
(Observed ordering differs between repaired devices and lab reference image).

Additional notes:
2026-03-03 - SRE (Noah Kim): Checked assetdb ingestion pipeline. No recent changes; ingestion keys use TPM UUID + disk signature fallback. In affected samples TPM reports are present but disk signature mismatch triggers fallback path.
Hypotheses:
- NVMe controller/firmware during vendor replacement produces non-deterministic partition/disk GUIDs leading to mismatch with our device fingerprinting which partially uses disk signature as tie-breaker.
- Depot repair process may be cloning an older drive image and then performing a secure erase/partition step that inadvertently reorders partitions.
Commands/observations run:
- get-wmiobject -class Win32_DiskDrive | select SerialNumber,Model
- Get-Partition -DiskNumber 0 | select PartitionNumber,Guid
- compare TPMDeviceID vs DiskSignature across sample set (affected and control)
Findings:
- TPMDeviceID consistent across samples; disk signature different for affected devices.
- Re-imaging normalized disk signature to expected value.
- No kernel driver errors in System event log.
Next steps:
- Request depot to perform NVMe secure-erase + vendor FW update and re-run OOBE before shipping back.
- Add a one-time assetdb mapping override to merge duplicate entries when TPMDeviceID matches but disk signature differs to avoid hostname collision during Autopilot enrollment.
Workaround applied (temporary): Imaging team added a post-repair re-flash step at depot: run vendor secure-erase + FW revision to the drive, then re-image if the device shows disk signature mismatch. This prevents duplicate Device ID creation. Long-term: Engineering to update assetdb ingestion to prioritise TPMDeviceID and add a tolerant merge rule when TPM matches but disk signature mismatches. Depot ops notified and a quick-check script added to depot QC runbook. Follow-up ticket created to modify ingestion logic: INT-892900. Status: mitigation in place; awaiting full ingestion change PR and depot confirmation.
payload.summary: NVMe disk signature reorder after depot repair causes Intune/assetdb mismatch and Autopilot hostname collision

comments: 2026-03-12T00:00:00Z Platform Eng: Noted that signed-url refresh requests were routed via the same route as webhooks (route weight 100) and not assigned to a low-priority background pool. Proposed route-splitting and burst pool isolation.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightEdge Labs reports sudden waves of 429 responses from our public ingestion endpoint during a scheduled signed-url refresh job. The refresh is multiplexed across ~1500 workers; retries from their webhook orchestrator create cascading backoff storms.

Impact:
- ~15% of their webhooks failing with 429s for ~18 minutes starting 2026-03-10T02:08:00Z.
- Observable increase in concurrent token accounting and token-window exhaustion on the api-gateway layer.
- Customer reports degraded downstream processing and duplicate webhook deliveries after retries.

Environment:
- prod-us-west (primary), some traffic routed to eu-west via geo-failover.
- Customer on enterprise plan, using signed URL refresh service and hosted webhook callback ingestion.

Steps to reproduce (from customer's repro):
1) Start a multiplexed signed-url refresh job that issues refresh requests using ephemeral keys (approx 1500 parallel workers).
2) Simultaneously run a webhook callback batch that fans out to our ingestion endpoint (payload small, high QPS).
3) Observe 429s at the ingestion endpoint and increased retry loops from the customer's orchestrator.

Observed behavior:
- Rapid 429 surge correlated with signed-url refresh windows.
- Token refill traces show refill lag and transient negative token-balance on several edge nodes.
- Retry amplification observed due to short client backoff in customer's orchestrator.

Expected behavior:
- Signed-url refresh worker traffic should be accounted against ephemeral-key windows and not push tenant-wide windows into negative for interactive webhook callbacks.

Attached logs and traces:
- Edge token accounting snapshot: edge-token-accounting-2026-03-10-02-08.log (internal S3 link).
- Ingress gateway traces: trace-req-2026-03-10-02-09-12.txt.
- Customer provided orchestrator backoff config (attached).

Customer asks:
1) Why did signed-url refreshes contribute to tenant-wide token exhaustion?
2) Can we configure isolated burst pools or route separation for refresh jobs vs webhook paths?
3) Recommendations to avoid duplicate deliveries and retry storms while keeping refresh throughput.

2026-03-10 - Support (Alejandro Cortez): Acknowledged and requested customer's orchestrator backoff config and sample signed-url worker logs.
2026-03-10 - Customer (BrightEdge ops): Uploaded backoff config (initial_backoff_ms=200, max_backoff_ms=2000, retry_count=6) and confirmed ~1500 concurrent refresh workers.
2026-03-11 - SRE (Maya Singh): Observed refill lag on a subset of us-west edge nodes between 02:06-02:24Z. Opening INT-4422 to track edge token refill investigation.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 - Support (Maya Singh): Shared temporary mitigation steps with customer (see investigation_notes) and requested permission to schedule a canary to split refresh traffic to a background lane during maintenance window.
Edge refill lag: refill scheduler experienced a 12s GC pause on three edge nodes, delaying token window refills and causing temporary negative accounting.
Route configuration: webhook and signed-url refresh traffic share route '/v1/ingest/callback' with no priority differentiation; weight-based routing allows background traffic to compete with interactive traffic.
Token accounting: ephemeral-key fanout created many small windows; our current token-slicing aggregates at node-level which allowed bursts to deplete node-local buckets before global refill completed.
Client behavior: customer's orchestrator retries quickly (initial backoff 200ms), which amplified the perceived failure and led to synchronized retry waves.
Related internal ticket INT-4422 documents GC pause and edge node kernel patch rollout scheduled 2026-03-15.
Hypothesis: a combination of edge refill lag + shared route + aggressive client retries produced the observed 429 wave.
(Short term) Recommend customer increase client initial_backoff_ms to >=1000ms and enable retry jitter to de-synchronize retries.
(Short term) Apply route-split: move signed-url refreshes to '/v1/internal/signedurl-refresh' and mark as background priority so it draws from isolated burst pool. Support will coordinate with customer to update their refresh job target.
(Short term) Enable ephemeral-key smoothing: throttle refresh job concurrency to recommended 200 parallel workers while we assess background pool sizing.
(Mid term) Platform: roll INT-4422 edge GC patch and add node-level refill slower-path fallback to prevent negative accounting during GC windows.
(Mid term) Product: create a runbook to suggest 'signed-url refresh' as a candidate for background lanes; update docs with configuration examples for burst isolation and retry backoff best practices.
(Follow up) Schedule a joint postmortem with BrightEdge in 1 week to validate mitigations and confirm no invoice impact due to retries.
payload.summary: Burst 429s during multiplexed signed-url refresh leading to webhook retry storms

comments: 2026-03-10T09:34:00Z Asha Patel: Opening ticket after on-call noticed weekly SLA drop. Tagging routing and reporting owners. (cc @Diego)
2026-03-10T11:12:00Z Diego Morales: Reproduced locally against fixtures. Suspect merge strategy change in template-evaluator. Adding impacted templates list to the ticket.

2026-03-10T14:05:00Z Claire Nguyen: Confirmed ingestion shows missing sla_cohort field for affected tickets. Weekly report pipeline does not backfill when field absent. Temporary mitigation: marking those tickets against 'manual-cohort' is non-trivial.
2026-03-11T08:21:00Z Diego Morales: Created PR with unit test and candidate fix; draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7921. Running integration test in staging now.
2026-03-13T09:10:00Z Diego Morales: Hotfix rolled to prod (platform release 2026-03-13.1). Patch preserves recursive inheritance semantics. Monitoring metrics show initial recovery in proto-buckets.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
- Reproducible regression introduced by template-evaluator rewrite (flat-merge strategy) that drops inherited SLA tags from enriched tickets.

Impact:
- Weekly SLA attainment numbers for internal support queues are underreported by ~3-6 percentage points for the week of 2026-03-08.
- Escalation routing still works for most tickets, but reporting and SLA cohort attribution are wrong which affects capacity planning and on-call load estimations.

Scope/Environment:
- Affects templates that use macro inheritance (parent templates that define sla_cohort or priority tags).
- Observed in prod (us-east) reporting bucket; not seen in staging.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a parent template with "sla_cohort: infra-high" and a child template that does not declare sla_cohort.
2) Send a test ticket through the autoroute pipeline.
3) Inspect routed ticket metadata in the routing-engine logs and in the enrichment pipeline.
4) Compare the ticket meta emitted to reporting ingestion vs. expected meta (should contain sla_cohort).

Expected behavior:
- Child templates inherit sla_cohort from parents unless explicitly overridden. Reporting ingestion should receive the resolved sla_cohort tag.

Actual behavior:
- Resolved template object emitted by the evaluator shows sla_cohort missing for child-derived tickets (tag removed). Reporting ingestion then records ticket as "unattributed" for SLA cohort.

Observed evidence / logs:
- Routing engine enriched payload excerpt (2026-03-09 14:02:12 UTC): "template_resolved": {"id": "child-xx", "labels": ["billing"]} (expected sla_cohort key present).
- Reporting ingestion counts: internal-support.sla_attainment_weekly shows drop from 98.7% -> 94.3% for queue infra-ops.
- Related runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SUPPORT/Template+Inheritance+Runbook

Initial triage by CS tools: verified regression window aligns to 2026-03-07 when PR #7890 was deployed to prod.
Diego reproduced locally by running the new evaluator against stored template fixtures; flat-merge behavior removes nested 'metadata.sla_cohort' when child has empty metadata.
Hypothesis: evaluator's merge algorithm treats empty child metadata as explicit null and deletes inherited keys instead of preserving parent values.
Potential root cause: change from recursive-merge preserving keys to a shallow overwrite step when computing final template representation.

Mitigation applied: deployed hotfix that restores recursive-merge semantics in template-evaluator (release 2026-03-13.1).
Resolution notes: candidate fix in PR #7921 merged after CI and staging validation. No data loss to ticket content; only reporting attribution affected.
Post-deploy monitoring: sla_attainment_weekly for infra queues trending back to baseline over next two reporting cycles.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 16:46 - SRE (ops-runbook): Suggested hot rollback of template-evaluator deploy if staging tests fail. Noted potential churn to routing behavior during rollback window.
payload.summary: Template evaluator rewrite strips SLA cohort tags, causing weekly SLA attainment underreporting

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Northbridge Bank reports that their configured retention policy for request/response logs (TTL = 7 days) does not appear to be enforced in us-east. They are seeing request log entries older than 10 days still present in the Dedicated tenant.

Impact:
- Customer is in an active enterprise security review and needs evidence that retention controls are enforced.
- Operational impact: risk of non-compliance with customer policy until backlog is cleared.
- No serving/runtime impact reported; this is a data lifecycle / purge enforcement issue.

Customer statement (paraphrased):
"We set request log retention to 7 days last week. In us-east we can still query request logs from 10–12 days ago. Is TTL actually running?"

Environment:
- Product: Dedicated
- Region: prod us-east
- Data class: request/response logs (NOT audit logs)
- Customer policy: request_logs.ttl_days=7, prompts/completions storage disabled (per customer settings)

What we expected:
- Records older than 7 days should be deleted by scheduled purge jobs with observable progress (ttl_lag_seconds trending near 0–6h depending on job schedule).

What we observed:
- ttl_lag_seconds for request_logs in us-east increased to ~280k–420k seconds (~3.2–4.9 days), suggesting purge backlog.
- purge_failures for request_logs shows spikes during/after recent telemetry DB maintenance window.

Attachments / screenshots (customer-provided):
- Screenshot 1: Console query showing request log entries dated 2025-02-27 still present (captured 2025-03-11).
- Screenshot 2: Customer internal dashboard noting retention TTL 7d set on 2025-03-04.

Internal screenshots (linked in comments):
- Grafana: Retention Controls Verification / Request Logs (us-east) showing ttl_lag_seconds elevated and purge_rows_deleted dropping to near-zero during maintenance.

Triage checklist:
1) Confirm customer policy is set and evaluated correctly (policy service + cache).
2) Confirm request logs store TTL enforcement job is enabled in us-east.
3) Check purge job backlog and throttles (safety limits / DB pressure controls).
4) Validate no policy exceptions (legal hold / incident hold) are active for this tenant.
5) If backlog exists, run safe backfill purge and monitor lag until within SLO.

Notes:
- This ticket is distinct from audit log retention/export issues (see SUP-3917). This is specifically request/response log storage TTL enforcement.
2025-03-11 09:18 PT (Rachel Kim, CS): Opened on behalf of Northbridge Bank. They are blocked in security review; request is to confirm TTL is applied in us-east and provide a short evidence statement + remediation ETA if delayed.
2025-03-11 09:42 PT (Sean Gallagher, SRE): Acknowledged. Pulling retention verification dashboards for us-east. Will also check purge workers health and queue depth.
2025-03-11 10:05 PT (Sean Gallagher, SRE): Found elevated ttl_lag_seconds for request_logs in us-east only. eu-west is normal. purge_rows_deleted dropped sharply 2025-03-10 01:00–05:00 UTC (matches telemetry DB maintenance). purge_failures spiked with error: "context deadline exceeded" from deletion batches.
2025-03-11 10:22 PT (Logan Wright, Telemetry): Confirmed: maintenance window introduced slower deletes due to index rebuild + throttling; purge job framework saw repeated retries and automatically reduced batch size. Backlog accumulated; should recover but may take ~24–48h at current throttle.
2025-03-11 10:31 PT (Ethan Park, Control Plane): Checked retention policy service for tenant. Policy is set correctly (request_logs TTL=7d). No legal hold flags present. Policy evaluator cache updated 2025-03-04; no anomalies.
2025-03-11 11:02 PT (Sean Gallagher, SRE): Proposed mitigation: temporarily increase purge worker concurrency for request_logs in us-east with tighter per-query time limits + off-peak scheduling; also run an on-demand backfill purge up to 'now-7d' for the tenant partitions.
2025-03-11 11:20 PT (Allison Grant, SRE/Obs): +1 as long as we keep DB pressure guardrails. Please set max_rows_per_minute cap and alert on p95 delete latency. Use runbook: runbook-retention-purge-jobs -> 'Handling purge backlog after maintenance'.
2025-03-11 12:10 PT (Sean Gallagher, SRE): Executed controlled backfill purge (job id: purge_request_logs_us-east_2025-03-11T19:58Z). Set concurrency from 2 -> 6 for request_logs only, capped by QPS limiter. Monitoring: ttl_lag_seconds started trending down (from ~410k -> ~260k in first hour).
2025-03-11 13:44 PT (Rachel Kim, CS): Customer asking for: (a) why us-east only, (b) when their view will reflect TTL, (c) whether they can get an evidence snippet for auditors. Please provide a crisp explanation we can forward.
2025-03-11 14:05 PT (Sean Gallagher, SRE): Draft customer-facing summary: 'Retention policy is configured correctly; a temporary purge backlog occurred in us-east following a telemetry database maintenance window. Purge jobs are running and we increased capacity to catch up; expected to return to normal within ~24h. No data access exposure; this is lifecycle deletion timing.'
2025-03-12 08:12 PT (Sean Gallagher, SRE): Backlog reduced further overnight. ttl_lag_seconds now ~55k–80k seconds (~15–22h). purge_rows_deleted steady; purge_failures back to baseline. Expect to be within <6h lag by end of day.
2025-03-12 10:26 PT (Olga Petrov, GRC): For evidence: include (1) tenant retention config export timestamp, (2) screenshot/metric showing ttl_lag decreasing, (3) statement that legal hold not enabled. No need to share internal error logs.
2025-03-12 16:40 PT (Sean Gallagher, SRE): ttl_lag_seconds now ~12k seconds (~3.3h). Considered recovered. Leaving concurrency elevated until 2025-03-13 12:00 PT, then revert to standard. Added note to on-call handoff.
2025-03-13 09:05 PT (Rachel Kim, CS): Customer confirmed: they no longer see >7d request logs in us-east queries as of this morning. They requested a short written confirmation + time window of remediation.
2025-03-13 09:22 PT (Sean Gallagher, SRE): Reverted concurrency to standard; system stable. Provided final wording for customer: 'As of 2025-03-13, request log retention for TTL=7 days is actively enforced in us-east; backlog from 2025-03-10 maintenance has been cleared. Ongoing monitoring in place.'
2025-03-14 11:11 PT (Rachel Kim, CS): Closing the loop. Sent customer confirmation + retention config export and a redacted dashboard screenshot showing ttl_lag returning to normal. Marking resolved.
Root cause:
- Request logs TTL enforcement in prod us-east fell behind due to a telemetry database maintenance window (index rebuild + increased delete latency). Purge job framework throttled automatically after repeated timeouts, which reduced deletion throughput and allowed backlog to accumulate.

Fix / remediation:
- Verified retention policy configuration and evaluation were correct (no policy/legal hold exceptions).
- Ran a controlled on-demand backfill purge for request_logs up to (now - 7 days) and temporarily increased purge worker concurrency with DB-pressure guardrails.
- Monitored ttl_lag_seconds and purge_failures until lag returned to normal operating range (<6h).

Customer-facing outcome:
- As of 2025-03-13, request/response logs older than the configured 7-day TTL were no longer queryable for the tenant in us-east.

Follow-ups:
- SRE to add a post-maintenance checklist item to verify ttl_lag_seconds returns to baseline within 6h.
- Telemetry to review timeout thresholds for delete batches during known maintenance periods to reduce auto-throttle overreaction.

Workaround:
- If recurrence happens, Support can request an on-demand backfill purge with capped concurrency per runbook.
payload.summary: Retention policy TTL not being applied to request/response logs in prod us-east (purge lag > configured TTL)

comments: 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z Jenna Liu: Ticket created after two repros in staging. Attached smsts.log and event snippets.

2026-03-10T11:05:00Z Ravi Menon: I can repro locally on a Dell 7440. Confirmed VBS flagged as enabled in registry (HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\DeviceGuard). Collecting full kernel boot logs and bcdedit output.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
When devices are provisioned from the new SCCM/Intune hybrid task sequence (TS-2026-v2) VBS (Virtualization Based Security) and Credential Guard are being left enabled. End-users cannot complete Windows Hello (Facial/IR camera) enrollment after first sign-in. Enrollment UI reports a generic error and returns immediately.

Impact:
- New hires and reimages unable to enroll face unlock; slows time-to-productive for ~12% of provisioning runs in staging so far.
- Manual workaround required by IT to disable VBS or re-run provisioning which delays handover.

Environment:
- Imaging task sequence: TS-2026-v2 (SCCM -> Intune autopilot handoff)
- Affected OS: Windows 11 22H2 corporate image (customized with Defender ATP, VBS policy bundle)
- Regions: staging-us-east, small sample in prod-us-west reported by 2 users
- Affected models: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 10, Dell Latitude 7440

Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot device to SCCM PXE and run TS-2026-v2 provisioning sequence
2) Device is joined and Intune enrollment runs post-OOBE
3) Complete out-of-box experience and sign in with corp account
4) Attempt to set up Windows Hello Face (IR camera)

Observed behavior:
- Windows Hello enrollment fails immediately with an error (translated UI message: "Can't set up your camera right now")
- Event Viewer: Microsoft-Windows-User Device Registration / Operational shows Error 0x80090016 and TPM access denied messages.
- System logs show Device Guard / Credential Guard service active and VBS reported enabled (Platform Configuration Manager trace).

Expected behavior:
- Windows Hello enrollment should succeed for supported hardware without requiring VBS to be disabled during provisioning.

Temporary workaround:
- IT Support: Disable VBS/Credential Guard using the bcdedit toggle (bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off) and reboot; then re-run Hello enrollment. Alternatively reimage using legacy TS that does not enable VBS. Both are manual and disruptive.

Attachments:

Issue summary:
During a high-priority tenant ramp at ~2026-03-10T14:30 UTC customer observed elevated 5xx responses (502/503) and a subset of streaming sessions dropping with runtime processes reporting 'socket read timeout' and reduced accept queue depth. Impact: customer tenant experienced degraded throughput and increased latency across chat and embedding endpoints.

Impact:
- PapertrailAI reported ~18% of requests returned 502/503 over a 12-minute window.
- Long-lived streaming sessions dropped; reconnect attempts saw retry amplification.
- No billing discrepancy observed; throughput throttles triggered for the tenant.

Environment:
- Prod cluster in us-east: mix of dedicated and shared GPU nodes serving the tenant via a weighted route.
- Route config: tenant pinned to route-weight group beta-weighted-3 with fallback to general-pool.

Steps to reproduce (customer-reported):
1) Start high-concurrency test against /v1/chat/stream with 80 concurrent streams pinned to the tenant.
2) Simultaneously submit embedding bulk uploads to /v1/embeddings with small batches (~16 per request).
3) After ~8-10 minutes observe increased connection resets and 502/503 responses.

Observed logs (excerpt):
- runtime[worker-21] WARN socket read timeout (fd=1024) after 30000ms
- proxy[acceptor] DEBUG accept-queue-depth dropped from 1024 -> 128 in 90s
- runtime[monitor] ERROR ephemeral runtime heartbeat missed, initiating drain
- api-gateway WARN upstream returned 502: connection reset by peer

Notes: This pattern differs from usual GPU OOM or kernel fallback; traces point to an accept-queue drain along with a runtime-side slowdown (socket stalls) that amplified apigw backpressure and hedged retries.
Initial hypothesis: a surge in tenant-priority traffic triggered a priority rebalancer event that concurrently initiated transient connection draining on a subset of ephemeral proxies. That drain reduced accept queue depth on front-line proxies and forced excess hedged retries into a small number of runtimes causing socket stalls and TLS handshake backlog.

What we checked:
- Health checks: ephemeral worker heartbeats for affected node pool show repeated 1–2s delays starting at 2026-03-10T14:25 UTC.
- Kernel metrics: no immediate kernel fallback events or NVML resets; GPU memory not saturated.
- Network: intermediate proxies reported increases in SYN_RECV and reduced free file descriptors on the worker process.
- Routing: weighted-route shift occurred at 2026-03-10T14:20 UTC (auto-rebalance policy).

Partial findings:
- Accept queue collapse correlated with a concurrent config sweep that toggled priority windows for the tenant.
- Runtimes entered a slow syscall path (observed via strace sampling) when faced with >200 concurrent ephemeral TLS handshakes while the accept queue was depleted.

Logs & dashboards referenced:
- Grafana: /dashboards/d/accept-queue/accept-queue-us-east (spike at 14:25)
- Loki: cluster/us-east/runtime/error stream (query ref: #L-309481-14)
- Slack: #support thread T05B3K2 (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05B3K2/p167?)
- Disabled weighted-route sweep for PapertrailAI to prevent further rebalances.
- Applied temporary proxy accept-queue increase on us-east front-line proxies.
- Advised customer to reduce concurrent streaming sessions to <40 until fix is deployed.
- Enabled hedged-retry rate limiter on the route to prevent amplified fanout.
In progress — short-term mitigations applied stabilized error rate to <1% within 12 minutes. Medium-term fix planned: adjust rebalancer cooldown to avoid simultaneous drain on multiple proxies and harden runtime accept() path to pre-allocate file descriptors for TLS handshakes.

Follow-ups scheduled:
- SRE to deploy rebalancer cooldown patch to staging on 2026-03-13 (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/5021).
- Runtime team to land fd-prealloc change in canary: planned 2026-03-15.
- Postmortem to be authored in Confluence and shared with PapertrailAI by 2026-03-18.
Priya Rao (Support) — 2026-03-10T15:05Z: Acknowledged with PapertrailAI; requested request IDs and timestamps for failed calls. Asked for temporary throttling to reduce concurrent streaming sessions.
Marco Chen (SRE) — 2026-03-10T15:32Z: Observed accept-queue depth collapse on proxy-ephemeral-12. Kicked off live capture and increased proxy keepalive timeout. Correlates with weighted-route rebalancer activity.
Action: Disabled route sweep for affected tenant to stabilize.
Lina Ortega (Runtime Eng) — 2026-03-10T16:10Z: Found high syscall latency in accept() path when fd table approached 90% usage on runtime-worker processes. Proposed two mitigations: (1) increase ephemeral proxy accept queue and fd soft limits; (2) add backpressure at api-gateway for hedged retries.
Customer impact prioritized due to dedicated tier SLA. No data exfiltration suspected. Billing unaffected. Recommend adding an automated pre-check in route weighter to ensure accept-queue headroom before rebalancer operations.
payload.summary: Unresponsive runtime sockets and elevated 5xx during tenant priority surge

payload.description:
Issue summary
- The benchmark fleet runner service account cannot (a) create/run GPU benchmark jobs reliably and (b) export run artifacts (manifests, traces, JSON results) to the shared artifacts bucket.
- This started after the benchmark fleet moved to Workload Identity + a new namespace split for perf-canary vs ad-hoc runs.

Impact
- Blocks Q1 2026 perf baseline sweeps and perf-canary nightly runs from producing publishable artifacts.
- Engineers can sometimes run locally, but CI and scheduled runs fail, leading to missing data in dashboards and delayed regression triage.

Who is affected
- Serving Runtime benchmarking owners + SRE perf-canary pipeline.

Environment
- Benchmark fleet Kubernetes clusters: bench-us-east (primary), bench-eu-west (secondary)

Additional notes:
- Runner identity:
  - KSA: perf-runner (namespace: perf-canary)
  - KSA: benchmark-runner (namespace: benchmark-lab)
  - GSA (expected): bench-fleet-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- Artifact destinations:
  - GCS: gs://rw-benchmark-artifacts-us-east1/perf-suite/
  - GCS: gs://rw-benchmark-artifacts-eu-west1/perf-suite/
  - (optional) BigQuery dataset used by dashboard ingest: rw_perf_bench
Symptoms / errors
1) GPU jobs fail at image pull (intermittent but common)
- Pod events:
  - Failed to pull image "us-docker.pkg.dev/redwood-prod/benchmark-lab/runner:2026.01.14": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to authorize: failed to fetch anonymous token: unexpected status from GET request to https://us-docker.pkg.dev/v2/token: 403 Forbidden
  - ImagePullBackOff
2) Artifact export fails at the end of runs
- Export step logs:
  - gsutil cp results.json gs://rw-benchmark-artifacts-us-east1/perf-suite/INT-8821-test/...
  - AccessDeniedException: 403 bench-fleet-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com does not have storage.objects.create access to the Google Cloud Storage object.
3) Some runs create pods but fail to attach GPU resources in perf-canary namespace
- Kubernetes error surfaced by harness:
  - Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:perf-canary:perf-runner" cannot create resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "perf-canary"
Steps to reproduce
1) From CI (perf-canary) trigger the representative suite nightly job.
2) Observe failure at either:
  - Pod creation in perf-canary namespace (RBAC Forbidden), or
  - Image pull from Artifact Registry (403), or
  - Result upload to GCS bucket (403).
Investigation notes (internal)
- Confirmed failures on both us-east and eu-west benchmark clusters.
- K8s service accounts exist but are not consistently bound to the expected Google service account.
- RBAC in perf-canary namespace diverged from benchmark-lab after namespace split; benchmark-lab had RoleBinding granting create/list/watch pods/jobs, perf-canary did not.
- Artifact Registry access appears to require explicit reader permission on the repo; previously inherited via a broader project-level role that was removed during least-privilege cleanup.
- GCS bucket permissions were granted to the old GSA (bench-fleet@...), not the new bench-fleet-runner@... account.
Root cause
A) Kubernetes RBAC missing in perf-canary namespace
- The perf-canary namespace was created without the Role/RoleBinding that grants the runner KSA permissions to create Jobs/Pods and read Pod status/events.
B) Workload Identity binding incomplete for one KSA
- The KSA (perf-canary/perf-runner) was not annotated with iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account=bench-fleet-runner@... in one cluster, causing requests to use the node default identity (no access).
C) IAM regressions during least-privilege cleanup
- bench-fleet-runner@... lacked:
  - Artifact Registry read access to the benchmark-lab runner repository
  - GCS object create permissions on rw-benchmark-artifacts-* buckets
  - Logging writer permissions for structured benchmark logs
Resolution
1) Fixed K8s RBAC (both clusters)
- Added Role + RoleBinding in perf-canary namespace to allow the runner to:
  - create/get/list/watch pods
  - create/get/list/watch batch/jobs
  - get/list/watch pods/log and events
2) Fixed Workload Identity binding
- Annotated KSAs:
  - perf-canary/perf-runner
  - benchmark-lab/benchmark-runner
  with the intended GSA bench-fleet-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- Added iam.workloadIdentityUser binding to allow those KSAs to impersonate the GSA.
3) Restored required GCP IAM roles to bench-fleet-runner@...
- Artifact Registry:
  - Granted roles/artifactregistry.reader on repo: redwood-prod/benchmark-lab
- GCS buckets:
  - Granted roles/storage.objectAdmin on:
    - rw-benchmark-artifacts-us-east1 (restricted to perf-suite/* prefix via bucket policy where supported)
    - rw-benchmark-artifacts-eu-west1 (restricted similarly)
- Observability:
  - Granted roles/logging.logWriter (to ensure harness logs are not dropped)
- Dashboard ingest (optional path used by nightly):
  - Granted minimal BigQuery dataset write role to rw_perf_bench ingest service (not to the runner) and updated pipeline to use ingest SA instead of runner SA (reduces blast radius).
Verification
- Ran a smoke benchmark in perf-canary namespace on us-east:
  - Pod scheduled with GPU, image pulled successfully, job completed.
  - Artifact upload succeeded; results.json + manifest.json present under gs://rw-benchmark-artifacts-us-east1/perf-suite/smoke/2026-01-16/
- Re-ran on eu-west:
  - Same outcome; no 403s.
- Confirmed perf-canary nightly run unblocked (next scheduled run expected 2026-01-16 03:00 UTC).
Follow-ups / notes
- Please keep IAM changes in Terraform (single source of truth). Manual console grants were avoided; any emergency grants done during triage were removed after Terraform apply.
- Recommend adding a startup check in the harness to assert:
  - can create Job in target namespace
  - can read/write to artifact bucket
  - can pull runner image
  and fail fast with actionable error.
Requester notes
- Rina: needs this resolved before the next baseline sweep window reservation (Q1 2026 baseline plan).
payload.summary: Benchmark fleet service account missing IAM/RBAC permissions (GPU jobs + artifact export)

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 18:10 UTC we observed an unusual spike in password-reset events that were initiated by an internal webhook endpoint. The requests appear to have been triggered by submissions to an external marketing/vendor form (FormRelay) which forwards leads to our legacy support integration. The webhook calls lacked the expected HMAC signature header in many cases and targeted the internal endpoint responsible for generating password-reset emails.

Impact: Hundreds of password-reset emails were generated for accounts that did not explicitly request resets via the standard UI. No confirmed account takeover activity has been observed to date, but the volume of unsolicited reset emails could enable phishing or account confusion. This affects production only (us-east).

Primary endpoints observed: POST /internal/hooks/form-relay -> /internal/hooks/user-triggered-reset (internal)

Immediate action taken: Rate-limited the legacy webhook endpoint, disabled auto-forwarding from the FormRelay integration, rotated the webhook signing secret, and blocked the vendor IP range in the WAF pending vendor investigation.
Generated ~480 password-reset emails in a 2-hour window (us-east prod). No 5xx server errors; high customer confusion and support volume expected. Potential phishing exposure due to out-of-band resets.
2026-03-13 18:05 UTC - First anomalous reset event detected by alerts; 18:10 UTC - spike observed (approx +1200% above baseline); 18:22 UTC - oncall notified via #sec-triage; 18:35 UTC - endpoint rate limit applied; 19:10 UTC - FormRelay integration disabled; 20:00 UTC - webhook secret rotated; 2026-03-14 09:30 UTC - vendor call scheduled; 2026-03-14 14:15 UTC - follow-up investigation in progress.
1) Submit a lead via the external FormRelay marketing form with a target email address.
2) FormRelay posts to our legacy /internal/hooks/form-relay endpoint.
3) Legacy handler forwards to /internal/hooks/user-triggered-reset without HMAC header under certain payload shapes.
4) Internal system queues a reset email to the user.
Note: Attempt requires reproducing with the specific payload keys used by FormRelay (lead.email, lead.type=marketing, lead.flags.include_reset=true).
Truncated example logs (prod us-east):
- 2026-03-13T18:11:02Z POST /internal/hooks/form-relay 200 origin=52.23.110.17 userAgent=FormRelay/1.3 signature= -
- 2026-03-13T18:11:03Z POST /internal/hooks/user-triggered-reset 202 user=redacted@example.com requestId=abc123 queue=reset-emails
- 2026-03-13T18:12:45Z POST /internal/hooks/form-relay 200 origin=52.23.110.17 signature=sha256=deadbeef
- 2026-03-13T18:12:46Z POST /internal/hooks/user-triggered-reset 202 user=another@example.com requestId=def456 queue=reset-emails
Note: ~65% of form-relay->user-triggered-reset calls during the window had empty/missing 'X-Webhook-Signature' header.
2026-03-13 18:28 UTC - @oncall: Detected large uptick in reset emails; clustering to vendor IP 52.23.110.0/24. Applying rate limit and alerting security.
2026-03-13 18:40 UTC - @Rina Patel: Rotated legacy webhook secret and disabled forwarding from FormRelay. Notifying vendor ops for immediate validation.
2026-03-13 19:05 UTC - @Jordan Meyers: Added WAF block for vendor IP range and disabled auto-accept for legacy payloads (feature-flag off). Gathering list of affected user IDs for support outreach.
2026-03-14 09:37 UTC - @VendorContact (FormRelay): Confirmed they sent a retry loop for malformed payloads after a recent schema change; will provide a timeline and fix.
2026-03-14 11:12 UTC - @sec-eng: SIEM rule added to flag any un-signed webhook-to-reset chain. Recommend permanent deprecation of legacy forwarder within 2 weeks.
2026-03-14 13:05 UTC - @customer-support-lead: Drafted customer-facing message and UI banner to clarify unsolicited resets; preparing KB article.
2026-03-14 14:00 UTC - @Jordan Meyers: Next steps: finalize post-incident runbook, validate vendor patch, and schedule rotation of any remaining shared secrets.

Initial hypothesis: vendor-side schema change caused FormRelay to strip the signature when certain optional fields were present, creating unsigned requests that the legacy forwarder still accepted.
Evidence: 480+ reset events without X-Webhook-Signature; payloads contain lead.flags.include_reset=true which maps to legacy behavior.
Verified 3 unique requestIds mapping to 3 customer support tickets so far.
Privilege review: No reset tokens were auto-approved for machine logins; reset emails follow standard token generation process and expire per policy. No token reuse detected.
Mitigations tested: rate-limit, secret rotate, vendor IP block, feature-flag disable for legacy forwarding. All mitigations reduced event rate to baseline within ~25 minutes.
Follow-up: schedule deprecation of legacy forwarder, add strict signature enforcement at ingress, add payload schema validation, and require vendor onboarding checklist for future integrations.
Workaround implemented: disabled legacy forwarder and rotated signing secret; vendor (FormRelay) to deploy fix to retain signature and correct payload shape. Permanent fixes planned: enforce X-Webhook-Signature on all webhook endpoints, add explicit schema validation, and remove legacy auto-forward path. Support will send notification to users who received unsolicited resets with guidance. Postmortem and runbook updates in Confluence.
Create follow-up task to deprecate legacy forwarder - INT-82346
Runbook update: ensure checklist for vendor webhook onboarding
Support KB: article on unsolicited password resets and what to do

2026-02-06T10:09:00Z Mateusz Zielinski: Go error types have StatusCode and Body; RequestID is not plumbed. We’ll parse X-Request-Id header and add RequestID string to error. For mid-stream failures, we’ll return a typed error with RequestID if we had it at stream start.

2026-02-10T12:22:00Z Kaitlyn Nguyen: Quick note: gateway sometimes emits request_id as both header x-request-id and JSON field request_id depending on endpoint and compat layer. Platform PR in flight to standardize (redwood/pr-28426). SDKs should treat header as source of truth, and JSON field as fallback for older paths.

2026-02-14T09:55:00Z Ibrahim Khan: Update: Implementations landing across SDKs as part of parity. Streaming fixture will assert request_id present on disconnect error when stream was established successfully.

2026-02-18T15:08:00Z Owen Phillips: Verified in beta builds with a repro: 429 now surfaces request_id in error object in TS + Go; Python streaming disconnect now throws typed exception containing request_id captured from headers. This unblocks oncall log correlation. Marking resolved.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Support + Eng Oncall are regularly unable to correlate customer-reported SDK errors to server-side logs because request_id is not consistently included in SDK-raised exceptions.

Impact:
- Slower time-to-triage (often 20–40 min longer per escalation).
- Higher back-and-forth with customers ("can you reproduce with debug logs?"), especially for intermittent 429/5xx and streaming disconnects.
- Oncall cannot quickly pivot to platform logs without request_id; forces broad log searches by timestamp/customer which is noisy.

What we need:
- All SDKs (Python/TS/Go) should surface request_id on every error thrown/returned from the client, including:
  1) Non-streaming responses with JSON error bodies
  2) Streaming responses where the connection drops mid-stream
  3) Network failures where there is no HTTP response (should be explicit: request_id unavailable)
- request_id should be exposed in a standard field name (request_id) and included in toString()/message only in a safe way (no secrets).
- When available, include status_code and error_code as well.

Notes / examples observed:
- TS: Some errors include headers but do not reliably map x-request-id into the thrown error shape.
- Python: For streaming iterator exceptions, we often see a generic "Stream disconnected" without request_id even when gateway logs show one.
- Go: Some error types surface StatusCode but not RequestID.

Acceptance criteria (supportability):
- Support can ask for "request_id" as a standard question; customers can paste it from the thrown exception object or logs.
- request_id is present in SDK errors for all HTTP error responses (4xx/5xx) and best-effort for streaming errors.
- Conformance tests cover request_id propagation in: 429, 500, invalid auth (401), and streaming disconnect scenario.

References:
- Related support escalations: SUP-29410 (Python streaming timeouts) and SUP-29505 (streaming disconnects behind proxy)
- Slack context: #eng-oncall discussion on request_id capture (see thread 1768161022)

Hypothesis 2: Legacy CSV import in 2025 may have transformed branch codes due to locale formatting (leading zeros stripped) - but here values differ not just leading zeros.

Cross-checked vendor bank details with remittance PDF and vendor banking letter (received 2026-03-08): both state branch 0314 and IBAN ends with 5829, which matches our account last4, so account number is correct but our branch is wrong.

payload.description:
Issue summary: A developer requested temporary debug/admin access via our internal console 'FeatureRollouts'. The usual flow issues a short-lived debug token after Okta group membership is confirmed via the SCIM provisioner. Impact: affected user did not receive any token; console showed 'pending' state and token issuance job logged an error. The incident is blocking one engineer from performing an urgent rollback for a customer-facing rollout. Recent changes: a bulk group rename migration (okta-group-migration job) ran within the same minute as the token-issue job for this user. Hypothesis: SCIM events out of order or a transient failure in our group lookup caused the token-issuer to skip creation without a retry.
1) Perform group rename in Okta for an admin group (simulate migration job)
2) Trigger temporary debug token issuance from console for a user who was member of the renamed group
3) Observe the token-issuer logs: if the SCIM lookup returns 404 or 409, the issuer currently exits without creating token
4) Repeat with delays and the token is created as expected (timing-sensitive).
2026-03-10T14:02:12Z token-issuer INFO: start request user=aechen
2026-03-10T14:02:12Z scim-provisioner WARN: group-lookup status=404 group=rollout-admins-old-name request_id=abc123
2026-03-10T14:02:12Z token-issuer ERROR: missing-group-membership, aborting token creation user=aechen request_id=abc123
2026-03-10T14:02:12Z okta-api INFO: okta bulk rename job started job_id=migrate-20260310-1
(see full logs at) https://logs.redwood.internal/aechen/2026-03-10/token-abc123
Initial triage by SRE (Diego): reproduced locally by running the migration tool concurrently with token-issue worker. Observed a race where SCIM returned a transient 404 for group lookup immediately after rename and before membership sync finished. Token-issuer codepath treats non-200 from SCIM as 'not a member' and returns without retry. Previously assumed SCIM is strongly consistent; bulk rename introduced window of inconsistency. Added hypothesis: missing idempotent semantics for group lookup and no retry/backoff. Correlated Slack thread #infra-auth (https://slack.redwood/team/infra-auth/p12345) and related runbook. Linked PR added to add retries and idempotent check: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-provisioner/pull/1142
Manual workaround: Support can manually create the short-lived token via admin console 'Create Debug Token' flow for affected user while SCIM sync completes. Steps: 1) Verify user identity via SSO audit. 2) Use internal admin tool (requires SSO admin role) to issue token and record in incident. Temporary measure until automatic fix is deployed.
Planned fix: update token-issuer to tolerate transient SCIM 4xx/5xx by adding exponential retry (max 3 attempts) and an idempotent verification step that checks provisioning timestamp. Also add monitoring alert when token-issuer observes >1% transient SCIM failures. Patch PR created and under review (auth-provisioner#1142). Deployment plan: merge to canary, monitor token-issuance success rate in prod for 24h, then promote. Follow-up: add migration checklist to avoid bulk renames during high-priority rollouts.
Oncall: if user reports 'pending' state for token issuance, check SCIM sync status and open this ticket. Manual token issuance permitted for urgent rollbacks. Do not run bulk Okta rename jobs during active rollouts; coordinate with Platform team.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports unexpected duplicate downstream tool/function invocations when client aborts and retries streaming/function-calling requests. Behavior differs across SDKs: TS clients observe a single execution most of the time, Go sometimes sees duplicates, and Python sees duplicates more predictably. Customer is using a managed edge HTTP proxy (third-party) in front of Redwood API for routing.

Impact:
- Potential double side-effects in customer's downstream systems (webhooks, DB writes).
- Customer running on Dedicated plan; high business impact for some requests.

High level ask: explain root cause and provide immediate mitigations and clear SDK guidance (and docs) to avoid duplicate tool/function invocations on client-side retries and mid-stream aborts.
1) Use Python SDK to open a streaming function-call session to redwood-3b-v2 via customer's edge proxy (proxy with connection pooling).
2) Trigger a long-running function call (customer provided test harness that invokes external webhook).
3) Mid-stream, cancel the client connection (SIGINT/close socket) and immediately retry the same logical request with the same idempotency token (client code uses per-session nonce).
4) Observe: external webhook receives 2 POSTs in ~500-1500ms window. Repeat with TS and Go SDKs and compare behavior.
Customer-provided logs (trimmed):
- python-client: 'stream closed by client' then 'reconnect using idempotency: nonce=3f6a...
POST /v1/streams 200 OK'
- edge-proxy logs: 'connection reused, header-length-truncated: idempotency-token=3f6a...->3f6'
- webhook logs: two deliveries timestamped 2026-03-01T14:22:10.123Z and 2026-03-01T14:22:11.349Z
- go-client: 'request retried, idempotency token present' but sometimes '200 processed' twice.
- ts-client: mostly single delivery; occasional duplicate in older proxy instances.
Relevant traces: link: https://redwood.internal/traces/trace-abc123 (customer-supplied)
Initial hypothesis: header rewriting/truncation at edge-proxy + SDK connection-pool reuse causes mismatch between what the SDK thinks it sent as the idempotency token and what the service actually received. Specific observations:
- Edge proxy truncates headers above ~1KB when reusing persistent connections; the customer's per-session idempotency token included extra metadata (base64 + signed salt) pushing it over threshold. Truncation appears non-deterministic depending on connection reuse and chunking.
- Python SDK historically sets a per-stream idempotency nonce and then reuses the same http2 connection with the header in the initial request metadata. If the proxy rewrites the header during connection reuse, the server treats the retry as a new idempotency key and re-executes the function.
- TS SDK performs per-request header injection (on each retry it regenerates the header), reducing chance of mismatch; Go SDK behavior depends on http client usage and whether user code constructed a single client vs per-request.
- We reproduced a truncated header in lab by configuring our internal envoy to simulate customer's proxy behavior. When truncated, server writes indicate a different idempotency key (shortened).
- No evidence of server-side double-execute due to internal retries: server logs show two distinct keys arriving.

Next steps suggested:
- Recommend immediate customer mitigation + patch in SDKs to canonicalize idempotency header generation and fallback detection.
- Patch request queued for SDKs to ensure per-retry header regeneration or authoritative header re-transmit on reconnect.
- Edge guidance: recommend proxy config to not truncate headers and to preserve header casing and content length.

Additional notes:
2026-03-02 Customer (Streamline AI): Provided proxy debug logs and confirmed they run connection pooling with header size limit 1024 bytes. They also confirmed they observed duplicates only when using their custom auth metadata added into idempotency tokens (we asked for sample).
2026-03-03 Streamline AI: Will test reducing token size and report by EOD. Asked for short-term config snippet for disabling automatic retry in Python SDK.
WORKAROUND PROVIDED — In Progress to patch SDKs and docs.
Short-term workarounds provided to customer:
- Use compact, short idempotency keys (UUID v4) instead of large signed blobs.
- Configure edge proxy to increase header size limit and avoid truncation on connection reuse.
- Set SDK retry policy to disable automatic client-side retries for function-calling/streaming endpoints until SDK patch deployed.
Planned long-term fixes:
- SDKs (Python/Go/TS): implement per-retry idempotency header regeneration and add detection for truncated/changed idempotency token returned by server -> surface clear error to client instead of silently re-executing.
- Docs: add dedicated guidance for idempotency token size, proxy interoperability, and recommended header placement.
- Confluence runbook: add steps for SRE to debug edge-proxy header truncation.
Related PRs and patches:
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/985 (experimental, will add tests)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/462 (WIP)
- Docs draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SUPPORT/Idempotency+and+Edge+Proxies (draft)
payload.summary: Discrepant ack timing between SDKs and edge HTTP proxy causing confusing retry behavior for function/tool calls

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A background service flow that creates ephemeral CLI tokens for the internal 'runner' is being interrupted by an interactive Okta device-enrollment prompt. This prevents automated token issuance for many engineers and CI jobs that rely on the headless flow.

Impact:
- Internal CLI token creation fails or hangs for ~40 engineers and several scheduled CI jobs.
- Symptoms include '401 Unauthorized' or long-lived request stuck in 'Waiting for user interaction' state.
- On-call and runbook tooling that depends on these tokens cannot complete certain automation (deploy hooks, debug runbooks).

Environment:
- Prod identity proxy (us-east) fronting Okta conditional access.
- Affected clients: macOS laptop users and headless CI runners performing ephemeral-token requests via token-broker.

Steps to reproduce (representative):
1) Run: redwood-cli auth request-ephemeral --service runner from a machine without a pre-established device session.
2) Token broker redirects through identity-proxy to Okta for conditional access evaluation.
3) Okta responds requiring device enrollment; identity-proxy issues a 302 to interactive device-enrollment flow.
4) Headless flow cannot follow the interactive enrollment, request times out or returns 401/403.

Observed behavior:
- Request logs show a redirect to /enroll/device with X-Okta-Requirement: device_enrollment_required.
- identity-proxy logs: "interactive_flow_required=true, flow_type=device_enrollment".
- Token-broker logs: "token-request: blocked-by-interactive-enrollment".

Expected behavior:
- Service-account and runner-scoped ephemeral-token flows should bypass interactive device-enrollment (or receive a clear error code) so automation can either use an alternate path or fail fast.

Notes:
- This began after the March 2026 conditional access policy rollout that tightened device enrollment enforcement for new sessions.
- Not all users are affected; machines with an existing device-binding/session complete successfully.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:05 — SRE (Diego Morales): Captured identity-proxy trace ID ip-20260310-3345; confirmed redirect chain to Okta /enroll/device. Adding identity-proxy and okta teams.
Initial investigation traced the failure to the conditional access policy change rolled out on 2026-03-09. Okta began returning a device-enrollment requirement for sessions where the request lacked the device binding claim. The identity-proxy logic mishandles token-broker flows that are intended to be non-interactive: it maps absence of device info to 'interactive required' rather than to a specific error code indicating device-enrollment required. We reproduced the failure by invoking the ephemeral-token flow from a clean VM.
Key findings:
- Okta policy applies to any auth context missing enrollment, regardless of client type.
- Token-broker / client libraries previously relied on a 'flow=service' claim to opt-out; a client-side change (client-lib v2.4.1) dropped that claim for some runner invocations.
- identity-proxy did not whitelist the 'service' client_id for device-enrollment bypass and lacked explicit handling for service flows.
- Workaround implemented: Okta admins created a temporary policy exception for the token-broker service principal; identity-proxy feature toggle to treat 'X-Client-Flow: service' as non-interactive was enabled in prod.
Repro commands, logs, and trace IDs attached in linked PR and runbook page.
Mitigation steps (applied 2026-03-12):
1) Okta policy exception created for token-broker service principal to prevent device-enrollment enforcement on its sessions.
2) identity-proxy feature toggle deployed in prod to honor 'X-Client-Flow: service' header; token-broker updated to include header in requests.
3) Rolled back client-lib change in runner that caused 'flow=service' claim to be dropped (client-lib PR reverted).
Permanent fix and follow-up (planned):
- Update identity-proxy to explicitly enumerate non-interactive flows and return a deterministic error code when device enrollment is required for non-interactive flows, so callers can implement fallback logic (PR filed).
- Add unit/integration tests to prevent claim omission regressions.
- Create an audit report for all service principals and ensure they have correct conditional-access exemptions if appropriate.
- Add an alert in SLO dashboard to detect sudden increases in 'blocked-by-interactive-enrollment' incidents.
Status: workaround in prod allowed normal operations to resume. Engineering change for identity-proxy PR merged to staging and scheduled for canary next week. Okta policy change will be re-scoped to only target interactive user sessions once follow-ups are complete.
Create INT follow-up to track identity-proxy feature parity and tests (target: INT-424300)
Convene policy review with IAM/Okta team to scope conditional-access rules for non-interactive flows (owner: Priya Kapoor)
Add regression test to client-lib pipeline to catch claim drop in release gating
Publish runbook amendment to Confluence: how to respond to device-enrollment blocks for service accounts
payload.summary: Device-enrollment interactive prompt blocks automated background service token creation for CLI runner

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customers using long-form streaming chat report the SSE/WebSocket stream becoming silent mid-generation followed by a client 408 timeout. Impact: Several long-running conversations (10-60s) with EchoWrite on Dedicated pool show repeated mid-stream silence in ~2% of sessions, causing degraded UX and failed message deliveries. Environment: prod us-east, dedicated pool for EchoWrite, traffic via edge ALB -> edge-proxy -> serving-runtime. Observed since 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC after an edge-proxy config push.

Impact: User-visible interruptions for long responses, highest on multiplexed clients and clients using HTTP/2 connection reuse. No complete worker crashes or 5xx reported; downstream reconnections sometimes succeed and sometimes require client to re-issue the prompt.
1) Using EchoWrite test client configured to multiplex 6 logical SSE streams over a single HTTP/2 connection to api.redwood.com
2) Start a long-generation chat (system + ~3 user turns) that triggers ~40-80 tokens/sec output from model redwood-llama-13b-v2
3) Observe the SSE stream: generation starts normally, then at ~12-35s of generation the client sees no new events for 8-25s and eventually times out with HTTP 408 or client-level socket timeout
4) Repeat under different TCP keepalive/idle settings and observe higher failure rate when connection reuse is enabled on client (multiplex=true)
Active generation produces tokens for 10-30s, then the HTTP/2 stream associated with the client's logical SSE path stops sending frames while the underlying connection stays open. Server logs show the worker continuing generation and periodically flushing small chunks, but the client receives no frames until it times out or reconnects. Postmortem traces show mismatch between HTTP/2 stream ID in edge-proxy and stream frames arriving at the client after connection reuse events.
SSE/WebSocket multiplexed streams should deliver tokens continuously during generation. Connection reuse/multiplexing should not cause tokens to be dropped or routed to the wrong client stream. No 408s or client-visible silence should occur for healthy sessions within SLOs.
edge-proxy INFO 2026-03-09T22:03:12Z conn=abcd1234 stream_id=15 flush: sending 128 bytes to client
edge-proxy WARN 2026-03-09T22:03:25Z conn=abcd1234 stream_id=15 idle-ping-timeout=8s - no client ACKs observed
serving-runtime DEBUG 2026-03-09T22:03:25Z worker=wp-77 gen-token idx=128 flush_size=64 - write to outbound buffer
edge-proxy INFO 2026-03-09T22:03:30Z conn=abcd1234 stream_id=31 reusing connection for new client multiplex stream_id=31
edge-proxy ERROR 2026-03-09T22:03:37Z conn=abcd1234 stream_id=15 unexpected frame for stream_id=31 - dropped
tcpdump excerpt: IP client -> edge 10.1.2.3:52344 -> ALB 52.95.1.12:443; TLS packets show ALPN=h2; HTTP/2 frames: WINDOW_UPDATE for stream 15 at 22:03:16
http2 frame dump: HEADERS stream=15 status=200; DATA stream=15 seq=0..10 then silence; HEADERS stream=31 appearing for unrelated logical session at 22:03:30
Initial triage: high correlation with multiplexed HTTP/2 clients that reuse a single TLS connection and with a recent edge-proxy config change on 2026-03-09 (connection pooling tweaks).
Hypothesis: edge-proxy is incorrectly recycling HTTP/2 stream identifiers or mis-associating DATA frames to logical SSE sessions when connection reuse and aggressive stream-id reuse are enabled on the ALB/edge proxy layer.
Repro attempt: Re-running with single-stream (no multiplex) removes the failure in 10/10 runs. Re-enabling multiplexing with max concurrent streams=2 reproduces failure ~3/20 runs. Increasing client keepalive frequency reduces window where reuse occurs and lowers failure rate.
Tracebacks: no worker OOM or crash. Serving runtime indicates continued token generation and flushing; only edge-proxy logs show frame routing anomalies.
Related artifacts: PRs linked above include an experimental HTTP/2 stream pool change that may have introduced a race when streams are torn down while another logical stream is attached to the same connection.
Customer impact: EchoWrite customers on dedicated pool hit 2-3% session failures for long responses; rollback of edge-proxy change reduced failures to ~0.1% in canary subset.
Immediate workaround: disable HTTP/2 multiplexing for EchoWrite via per-customer edge config (set multiplexing=false) — applied at 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC; mitigated visible errors.
Short-term: revert the edge-proxy connection pool change in canary and schedule full rollback pending root-cause fix (PR revert applied 2026-03-10 12:30 UTC).
Medium-term: add per-stream sequence verification at edge-proxy to detect and reject misrouted frames and failfast the connection so clients can reconnect without silent stalls.
Long-term: harden HTTP/2 stream-id bookkeeping in edge-proxy and add regression tests for multiplexed SSE/WebSocket scenarios; consider a streaming SLO test in CI.
Rollback applied to edge-proxy configuration in prod us-east and per-customer multiplex disable for EchoWrite. Incident mitigated 2026-03-10 12:30 UTC. Root cause pending final fix in edge-proxy codebase (tracking PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/412).
2026-03-10T08:22Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer report received via support@echoWrite.com. Included client SDK logs and sample session IDs. Escalated to SRE.
2026-03-10T09:05Z - Marco Liu (SRE): Confirmed pattern on canary dedicated pool. Reproduced with EchoWrite test harness. Suspect edge-proxy HTTP/2 stream reuse race.
2026-03-10T09:20Z - Elena Gomez (Platform Eng): Rolling back connection-pool change in canary now. Adding additional http2 frame logging for deployed edge-proxy instances.
2026-03-10T12:35Z - Marco Liu (SRE): Rollback successful in us-east. Customer multiplexing disabled as a safety toggle. Monitoring for failures; no new customer 408s in last 30m.
2026-03-11T10:12Z - EchoWrite Support (Customer): Thank you — impact reduced. Requesting ETA for permanent fix and whether this will affect other dedicated customers.

payload.description:
Multiple engineers reported inability to reach internal Kubernetes API (kube-apiserver) from developer laptops when connected to Corporate VPN. Problem correlates with Windows machines running WSL2 and a DoH/DoT stub resolver (system or third-party), which create a Hyper-V vEthernet adapter and local UDP/TCP endpoints. Traffic to cluster control-plane IPs appears to be routed out the wrong interface causing TCP resets and TLS handshake failures.
Developers cannot kubectl to production-like clusters while on VPN; CI jobs run from local machines fail. Affects ~8 reported engineers across us-west office and remote contractors. Productivity loss estimated at 6-8 engineer-hours so far.
1) On Windows 11 machine with WSL2 enabled and DoH client running (either built-in Windows DoH or a user-level DoH client), connect to Redwood Corporate VPN (WireGuard).
2) Confirm new vEthernet (WSL) interface present in 'ipconfig /all'.
3) Attempt 'kubectl get pods' against internal cluster (cluster IPs routed via VPN).
4) Observe long timeouts or TLS handshake errors.
5) Disable WSL2 or stop DoH client and retest; connectivity is restored.
kubectl timeouts, TLS handshake errors 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority' in some captures, connection resets (RST) seen in tcpdump on client. Traceroute shows traffic goes out local vEthernet (Hyper-V) interface intermittently rather than the VPN interface.
All traffic destined for internal cluster CIDRs should be routed via VPN interface; DNS lookups should resolve internal service names to VPN-provided DNS servers or be bypassed as configured by split-tunnel policy.
Mar 10 09:12:21 client-tcpdump: SYN to 10.12.5.3 from 192.168.50.18 sent on vEthernet (WSL) - no SYN-ACK
Mar 10 09:12:21 vpn-daemon: route add 10.12.0.0/16 -> wg0
Windows Event: NetworkProfile change: vEthernet (WSL) registered with metric 25, interface index 14
kubectl: dial tcp 10.12.5.3:6443: connect: connection refused (after retries)
WireGuard status: interface up, AllowedIPs includes 10.12.0.0/16
Hypothesis: WSL2 creates a virtual interface with a more-preferred metric, Windows route selection prefers local vEthernet for specific destination address ranges when DoH client binds to 127.0.0.53 style addresses or exposes a local DNS proxy.
Reproduced on two machines: one with built-in Windows DNS-over-HTTPS (win11 feature) and one with third-party DoH client (cloudflared). Both show same symptom when WSL2 active.
Packet captures on client show SYN leaving on vEthernet and never reaching VPN peer; tcpdump on VPN gateway shows no inbound SYN from that client IP when failure occurs.
Workaround test: setting Interface Metric for vEthernet to a higher value (less preferred) restores correct routing to VPN interface and fixes kubectl connectivity.
Potential root cause: interaction between Windows DNS/DoH stub resolving and WSL2's NAT/virtual adapter triggering Windows to choose local adapter for certain IPv4 destinations. Split-tunnel or policy-based routes installed by VPN may not have strong enough precedence due to interface metrics.
Related config: some users have persistent static routes added by dev tools that overlap VPN CIDRs (need to check 'route print -4').
Temporary: On affected Windows machines run as admin:
  netsh interface ipv4 set interface "vEthernet (WSL)" metric=400
  or stop the DoH client/service (e.g., cloudflared) and restart VPN client.
Alternative: Add explicit persistent route that forces VPN interface for 10.12.0.0/16: route add 10.12.0.0 mask 255.255.0.0 <wg_gateway> metric 1 -p
Longer-term: Push a configuration update to the Corporate VPN client to set stronger policy routes (use 'route metric 1' and enforce via WireGuard pre/post-up scripts) and publish recommended interface-metric settings in onboarding docs.
Investigate adding a startup hook for Windows VPN provisioning that sets vEthernet interface metric to reduce precedence when WSL2 is present.
Lena Park (reporter) - 2026-03-10: Initial report from eng on-call. Provided client tcpdump and Windows 'route print' output. Symptoms started after Windows update and WSL2 kernel patch.
Diego Martinez (assignee) - 2026-03-10: Confirmed on my test VM. Reproduced with cloudflared and with system DoH. Prioritized because it blocks deployments.
SRE (Amit Rao) - 2026-03-11: Captured traffic at edge for affected client; no packets from client observed when failure occurs. Suggest check of interface metrics and persistent routes on Windows.
Platform Eng (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-11: Noted that WireGuard adds policy routes but Windows may honor interface metrics over route specificity in some cases; asked for 'netsh interface ipv4 show interfaces' output.
Diego Martinez - 2026-03-12: Applied temporary mitigation guidance to affected users (increase vEthernet metric or stop DoH client). Requesting a more permanent client-side policy or onboarding change.
Lena Park - 2026-03-12: Customers/devs confirmed workaround works; documenting steps for internal KB.
1) SRE to prototype WireGuard pre/post-up script to enforce route metrics and test in staging. 2) Defect: Add client policy to onboarding docs and VPN installer to set recommended metrics. 3) Follow up with Windows team to track any Windows DoH change that alters adapter selection behavior.
payload.summary: WSL2 DoH stub + Hyper-V vEthernet causes asymmetric routing and breaks access to internal k8s API over VPN
