Issue summary: Automated ephemeral service-account provisioning (JIT) used by the Dedicated provisioner is intermittently failing during STS/session creation. Impact: onboarding/provisioning flows for internal tooling and some Dedicated customer onboarding jobs are stuck; CI jobs that rely on ephemeral SA keys fail, causing rollout delays. Observed error is an IAM condition rejection referencing a time-window condition. This appears to affect only a subset of requests and correlates with transient clock skew and a recently tightened IAM condition on the 'provisioner-broker' service role.
1) Run the ephemeral provisioning job: tools/provisioner/jit-create --project=dedicated-prod --env=staging-proxy
2) Observe the broker attempt to assume the target service role via STS (gcp->aws federated path)
3) Provisioner logs show 403/ConditionNotMet returned by IAM when evaluating a condition expression containing request.time comparison
4) Re-run the same job: some attempts succeed, others fail (non-deterministic).
2026-03-10T15:22:41Z ERROR broker: sts-assume failed, error=ConditionNotMet: Condition (request.time < timestamp('2026-03-10T15:22:30Z')) not satisfied. request_id=abc123
2026-03-10T15:22:41Z DEBUG broker: token creation attempted with now=2026-03-10T15:22:41Z
Audit log (GCP): principalEmail=provisioner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com protoPayload.methodName=SetIamPolicy protoPayload.status.code=7 conditionEvaluation=false
Stacktrace: tools/provisioner/broker/assume.go:142
Initial hypothesis: tightened IAM condition was deployed in org-policy update on 2026-03-09 to restrict provisioner tokens to a narrow time-window; side effect: clock skew between hosted provisioner and auth validators causes ConditionNotMet. Evidence: failed requests show request.time outside the allowed timestamp range; successful requests have request.time within. We reproduced by artificially shifting the provisioner system clock forward/back and observed failures/successes. Correlated with a change in repo infra/iam/policies/2026-03-09 that added a hard-coded timestamp window for temporary SA issuance. Also found a handful of related 403s in cloud-audit logs with same condition id. Possible root causes: (A) overly strict hard-coded time window in IAM condition, (B) provisioner uses cert-based short-lived tokens with slight clock skew, (C) STS/GCP evaluation expects RFC3339 exactness and we supply a different granularity.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:34 - Security: Recommend follow-up to replace hard-coded timestamps with relative conditions (e.g., request.time < request.auth.token_issue_time + duration) where possible; also request NTP compliance checks on fleet nodes.
Mitigation applied: Reverted the change that introduced the hard-coded upper time bound in the IAM condition (infra/iam/policies rollback commit f7a1b). Immediate effect: provisioning success rate returned to baseline. Permanent fix: replace fixed timestamp conditions with duration-based conditions and add test coverage for condition evaluation under clock skew. Deployment notes: patch to policies implemented in canary org, then rolled to prod after 24h monitoring.
1) Add unit/integration tests that emulate clock skew against IAM conditions. 2) Enforce NTP/chrony checks in provisioner deployment jobs. 3) Replace static timestamp conditions with relative logic across all org-level IAM policies. 4) Create runbook entry for diagnosing ConditionNotMet during ephemeral SA creation.
payload.summary: Ephemeral service-account provisioning failing due to IAM condition time-window rejection

Issue summary: During a targeted canary push to ~10% of traffic for rwinf-redwood-2.1-xl, a cohort quarantine/revocation step executed by the orchestrator revoked cohort membership before cohort pin metadata was fully committed to the edge caches. Impact: Affected tenant (BeaconForms Inc) experienced silent fallback to legacy model variant (open-llama-30b-q4_0) for ~27 minutes. Requests returned mixed outputs without error codes; billing reflected calls to the legacy variant which impacted SLAs and evaluation continuity.

Expected: cohort quarantine/revocation should either wait until edge pin commits are durable or trigger an explicit rollback with visible 4xx/5xx signals so customers can detect fallback.

Observed behavior: No 5xx errors; user requests were accepted and processed by legacy variant. Route metadata at control-plane showed 'pin: rwinf-redwood-2.1-xl' but edge cookie and cohort membership expired earlier, producing token-to-route divergence.
Customer-facing generation quality regression and billing discrepancy for BeaconForms flows. Sessions tied to the tenant lost model affinity and some prompts returned significantly different output. Customer reported interrupted QA and a production regression alert. Estimated affected traffic: 2.3k requests, duration ~27 minutes.
1) Configure a staged canary roll for model rwinf-redwood-2.1-xl at 10% traffic for tenant beacon-forms (dedicated).
2) Schedule a quarantined cohort eviction in orchestrator with prewarm enabled.
3) Force a short orchestrator control-plane snapshot merge (simulate noisy coordinator) while edge cache TTLs are being rotated.
4) Observe tenant session tokens and edge cookie namespaces for mismatch and confirm requests being routed to legacy variant despite control-plane pin metadata.
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z orchestrator.INFO cohort_quarantine: initiating revoke for cohort_id=cohort-77
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z control-plane.DEBUG commit_window: snapshot_id=78 commit_start
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z edge-router.WARN cookie: namespace rotation detected, cookie_domain=beacon-forms.local ttl_old=120s ttl_new=30s
2026-03-10T14:12:06Z orchestrator.ERROR commit: cohort membership write incomplete: write_ack_timeout
2026-03-10T14:39:10Z control-plane.INFO reconcile: pin metadata reconciled to rwinf-redwood-2.1-xl for tenant beacon-forms (post-fix)
Example request trace: req=abcd1234 -> edge chose variant=open-llama-30b-q4_0, control-plane_pin=rwinf-redwood-2.1-xl
Support (Aisha): Customer opened with QA screenshots showing degraded outputs at 14:14 UTC. Asked SRE to escalate for potential pin mismatch.
SRE (Tomas): Initial look shows orchestrator revoked cohort before edge ack. Opening controller snapshot logs and asking for edge-router traces; tagging @platform-team.
Customer (BeaconForms): Provided examples and said billing shows calls counted to legacy variant. Requesting immediate mitigation and clarification on root cause.
SRE (Tomas): Applied mitigation at 14:42 UTC - forced explicit tenant pin flush and disabled automatic cohort revocation for that tenant. Confirmed routes back to intended model at 14:46 UTC. Noted potential race in commit window handling.
Support (Aisha): Notified customer of temporary mitigation and shared steps to reproduce for internal triage. Customer accepted temporary workaround and requested postmortem.
PM (Elaine Park): Marking follow up to capture rollout guardrails; asked to include canary prewarm invariants in release checklist.
Hypothesis 1: Quarantine flow triggers a cohort membership revocation before the commit window fully persists pins to the distributed edge caches; commit ack was lost due to a short write timeout (write_ack_timeout).
Hypothesis 2: Edge cookie namespace rotation TTL change (120s -> 30s) caused cookie-based affinity tokens to expire earlier than control-plane metadata, creating a window where control-plane believed tenant pinned but edge selected fallback routing.
Evidence: Orchestrator error logs show write_ack_timeout at 14:12:06Z. Edge router warnings show cookie TTL rotation at 14:12:04Z. Reconciliation occurred at 14:39:10Z after a control-plane snapshot merge. Traces show mismatched variant selection across components.
Attempted reproductions in staging: Reproduced mismatch when forcing snapshot merges and edge TTL shrink; could not reproduce when prewarm handshake is blocked until edge ack.
Mitigations performed: 1) Forced tenant-specific pin flush and explicit cache invalidation at edge to restore affinity (14:42-14:46 UTC). 2) Temporarily disabled automatic cohort revocation for the tenant pipeline to prevent recurrence during ongoing canary. 3) Rolled back the cookie namespace TTL change for production edge fleet while root cause analysis continued. Outcome: Traffic returned to rwinf-redwood-2.1-xl; customer confirmed recovery and asks for a postmortem and billing reconciliation.
T1: Add commit-window ack gating so orchestrator will not revoke cohort membership until edge-router acks persisted pin (owner: orchestrator-team, ETA: 2026-03-19).
T2: Implement telemetry alert for pin/edge-cookie divergence with automatic rollback (owner: edge-team, ETA: 2026-03-22).
T3: Postmortem documenting timeline, impact, and billing reconciliation plan (owner: SRE/Support, ETA: 2026-03-16).
T4: Backfill end-to-end integration test in staging to simulate fast cookie TTL rotation during canary commit (owner: qa, ETA: 2026-03-24).
Customer billed for model open-llama-30b-q4_0 for requests between 2026-03-10T14:12:00Z and 2026-03-10T14:39:10Z. Finance should prepare a credit for BeaconForms Inc for estimated 2.3k affected requests. Contact billing@redwood.ai with SUP-286714 reference.
Draft message prepared for customer: explanation of transient cohort revocation race, mitigation steps, and planned fixes; will share postmortem when complete.
payload.summary: Cohort quarantine revocation causes tenant model-pin mismatch and silent fallback

Issue summary:
Users who should receive temporary elevation via role inheritance (team -> project -> console-role) are not getting elevated roles after the scheduled Okta sync. This affects engineers attempting cross-project admin tasks using the Console elevation flow.

Impact:
- Multiple engineers reported Access Denied when attempting to open elevated admin pages across projects (error 403 with RBAC check failed).
- Blocking cross-project triage and incident response for several P0/P1 incidents this week.
- Affects approx. 12 users in the SRE and Platform teams; broader groups may be impacted but not yet reported.

Observed behavior:
- Okta group sync completes without errors per provisioner logs.
- Console authorization layer denies access due to missing "inherited_roles" entries in the internal RBAC cache for affected users.
- Manual role recompute (admin console -> Recalculate Roles) restores access for a user temporarily.

Expected behavior:
- After Okta sync completes, role inheritance should be recomputed or queued so users immediately gain derived roles (project-level roles and console elevation permissions) without manual intervention.

Context and recent changes:
- Rolled out RBAC service refactor on 2026-03-08 to optimize inheritance calculation for large orgs (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/commit/3a9f2b8).
- Okta provisioner upgrade (2026-03-09) changed the group-change webhook payload shape to include `changed_members` as an array of objects. RBAC recompute job expects `changed_members` as a flat list of strings. This mismatch likely skipped enqueueing recompute jobs for some user events.
1) Identify an engineer with team-level group membership that should inherit project-admin role via policy.
2) Trigger a synthetic Okta group-change event for that user (okta-provisioner/simulate-membership-change).
3) Observe provisioner logs: webhook accepted and processed (no errors), but the RBAC recompute queue does not receive a message for that user.
4) Attempt to perform a cross-project admin action in Console -> Access Control and observe 403 with 'rbac.authorization.inherited_missing' message in response header.
2026-03-11T09:12:03Z okta-provisioner INFO received webhook id=wh_1a2b payload_size=4
2026-03-11T09:12:03Z okta-provisioner DEBUG changed_members=[{"id":"U123","type":"USER"}]
2026-03-11T09:12:04Z rbac-service WARN recompute-handler skipped 0 events (payload shape mismatch)
2026-03-11T09:12:04Z console ERROR authorization 403 user=U123 reason=rbac.authorization.inherited_missing trace=tx-7e9f
03/11 11:00 - Support triaged: replicated with synthetic webhook; observed mismatch between provisioner payload and recompute handler schema.
03/11 13:30 - Reproducer: manually POSTed older payload shape -> recompute job enqueued and user gained inherited roles immediately.
03/12 08:45 - Reviewed PR 3a9f2b8 (rbac refactor): code assumes changed_members is list<string>. New provisioner sends list<object>.
03/12 10:10 - Hypothesis: type check in rbac-service swallowed the event without logging full payload for privacy; added debug hook to log sanitized payloads.
03/13 16:00 - Confirmed: handler returns early on payload element type mismatch. Fix is to accept object form and extract .id field, fallback to string when present.
Maya Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Initial report from SRE oncall: 'can't escalate to project admin after policy change'. Filed ticket and added Lina.
Lina Becker (Identity) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally using synthetic webhook. Attaching logs. Suspect schema mismatch introduced by okta-provisioner 2026-03-09 deploy.
Ethan Morales (SRE) 2026-03-11: Workaround: run 'rbacctl recompute --user U123' which granted the inherited role. Need an automated fix for bulk affected users.
Lina Becker 2026-03-12: Drafted small patch to rbac-service that normalizes changed_members entries. Running unit tests; will deploy canary to staging today.
Alex Chen (Oncall) 2026-03-13: Confirmed patch on staging; recompute queue now receives events. Requested deployment to prod with 10m canary before full rollout.
Maya Patel 2026-03-14: Notified affected teams and opened a short incident postmortem page. Collecting list of users impacted for retroactive recompute.
Manual recompute using 'rbacctl recompute --user <user-id>' or triggering admin console 'Recalculate Roles' on affected user. For bulk, run rbacctl --input users.csv --batch-recompute.
1) Merge and deploy rbac-service patch that accepts the object-shaped changed_members and extracts .id (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4821).
2) Deploy to prod behind a 10-minute canary in us-east, monitor recompute-queue metrics and console authorization 403 rates.
3) Run bulk recompute job for window 2026-03-08..2026-03-12 for users who had Okta group changes (job id: recompute-bulk-20260314).
4) Postmortem: write RCA, timeline, and add a contract test between okta-provisioner and rbac-service to prevent payload-breakage.

Issue summary:
Intermittent removal of RBAC roles for employees after scheduled Okta group synchronization. Affected users lose access to the internal Feature Flags console and other RBAC-protected endpoints and receive 403 responses. Problem appears after periodic full-group syncs and is sometimes resolved by re-login but recurs for a subset of identities.

Impact:
Multiple internal engineers (SRE and Product) blocked from feature flagging flows during deployment windows; impact is production and preventing emergency toggles. Approximately 12 unique users reported in first wave.

Environment:
Production (us-west) identity sync pipeline: Okta -> SCIM provisioner -> identity-service role-mapper -> console. Scheduled full-group sync runs nightly 03:00 UTC.

1) Wait for scheduled full Okta group sync (nightly or manual trigger)
2) Have a user who is member of multiple Okta groups with overlapping role mappings (e.g., engineering-team + deployers) log into Console
3) Observe that the identity-service issues a 200 for token exchange but the console returns 403 for RBAC-protected routes
4) Re-login/SSO often restores access intermittently; in some cases a manual forced SCIM resync recovers roles for a user
5) Users with single, simple group mappings are not affected in observed cases
Splunk: search index=auth sourcetype=scim_provisioner status=500 "group-attribute-mapper" | earliest=-6h | stats count by error_code
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/sys/okta-sync/dashboards/role-mapper-latency (spike at 2026-03-09T03:02:18Z)
Console error example: 2026-03-09T03:02:20Z - 403 - role "deployers" not found for principal sub=U12345
03/09 04:10 - Initial triage: observed correlation between nightly full sync start and first error reports (3 users).
03/09 05:00 - Replayed sync in staging and hit attribute-mapper 502s when group list length > 120; suspect batching bug.
03/09 07:20 - Identity-service logs show role claim normalization step dropped duplicate group names but did not merge aliases (alias groups with same display name across different org units).
Hypothesis: race between SCIM provisioner and role-mapper cache invalidation where group aliasing causes transient drop of role claim until the next sync or token refresh.
Observed partial failure pattern: SCIM returned HTTP 202 for some group updates while sync coordinator marked job successful; downstream role reconciler did not process partial updates correctly.
Related: linked issue INT-462199 describes a cookie stripping redirect loop that previously masked token refreshs — could explain why some users need a full browser restart to recover.
Temporary mitigation tested: manual SCIM resync + clearing identity-service group cache for affected principals restores access consistently.
PR opened to add stricter idempotency checks and backoff on scim-provisioner: github.com/redwood-inference/scim-provisioner/pull/197 (in review).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10T09:10 - SRE Lead (Jon Erickson): Requesting a hotfix to add defensive handling for partial SCIM responses and a stricter sync success criterion.
2026-03-10T14:40 - QA (Elena Gomez): Running expanded staging test with >200 group memberships per principal to validate batching edgecases.
Mitigation performed: manual SCIM resync and identity-service cache purge restored access for all reported users. Hotfix PRs opened: identity-service #482 (adds fail-on-partial-sync + immediate reconciliation), scim-provisioner #197 (idempotency and backoff). Scheduled emergency deploy of hotfix to production 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC with rollback plan. Follow-ups: add end-to-end sync tests, increase monitoring thresholds for partial syncs, document manual cache purge runbook.

Add a reconciliation step post-sync that verifies role claims across services - owner: Auth Eng
Implement alerting for partial-successful SCIM jobs with >1% failure rate - owner: SRE
Document manual cache purge and resync runbook in Confluence and link from identity-service runbook

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent control-plane authentication failures on their private deployment. Impact: serving nodes repeatedly fail to establish mTLS sessions to the control plane, resulting in model-sync stalls and occasional 401-like control-plane reauth loops. Environment: OmniRetail private deployment (prod-us-west) behind corporate egress proxy that filters DNS responses. Hypothesis: control-plane mTLS verifier performs a reverse DNS (PTR) lookup of the client IP for peername validation; the customer's egress proxy returns NXDOMAIN or synthesizes incorrect PTR responses for outbound PTR queries, causing peername mismatch and mTLS rejection.
1) Deploy private agent in a branch office behind an egress proxy that blocks or rewrites reverse DNS queries.
2) Start the agent so it attempts to open a persistent mTLS session to control-plane.example.redwood.ai.
3) Observe control-plane logs for peername verification checks and agent-side TLS handshake outcomes.
4) Repeat after configuring egress proxy to return NXDOMAIN for  in-addr.arpa PTR queries (common corporate resolver config).
- Agent fails repeated TLS handshakes with control plane; control-plane logs show: "client identity did not match PTR name (expected controlplane-client.<customer>.internal, got <no-ptr>)".
- Agent enters auth retry loop; heartbeats stop and model shard syncs stall.
- Issue resolves temporarily when egress proxy is bypassed or when PTR is present/accurate.
mTLS handshake should succeed even if reverse-DNS is missing; control-plane should fall back to certificate SAN/IP validation rather than hard-failing on absent PTR, or documentation should require PTR for private deployments that restrict reverse DNS queries.
[control-plane] 2026-03-10T14:03:12Z WARN peer_verifier.go:87 peername check failed: ptr_lookup(203.0.113.45) => NXDOMAIN
[control-plane] 2026-03-10T14:03:12Z INFO auth.go:204 rejecting client certificate: peername mismatch
[agent] 2026-03-10T14:03:13Z ERROR tls_handshake.go:56 handshake failed: remote error: handshake failure (peername mismatch)
[agent] 2026-03-10T14:03:18Z INFO retry.go:120 backoff=5s next_attempt=2026-03-10T14:03:23Z
Initial triage by CS reproduced with customer's proxy in their lab. We confirmed control-plane code path performs an optional PTR lookup to corroborate IP -> hostname mapping for audit-friendly peername checks. When PTR returns NXDOMAIN, current verifier treats that as an explicit mismatch.
- Packet capture from customer's egress shows outbound DNS PTR (UDP/53) to their forwarder; forwarder returns RCODE=3 (NXDOMAIN) without forwarding to upstream.
- Bypassing proxy or adding explicit PTR records (or allowing proxy to forward PTR) restores connectivity.
- We validated agent cert SAN/IPs are correct; certificate verification would succeed if verifier didn't require PTR.
- Linked to internal discussion: control-plane verifier behavior is stricter than documented for private deployments (see linked Confluence note).
Short-term workaround provided to customer: 1) Add a firewall rule to allow PTR queries to the customer's recursive resolver to be forwarded to upstream DNS where PTRs are published for agent IPs, or 2) Configure egress proxy to allow/whitelist PTR responses for Redwood control-plane destinations, or 3) Add internal DNS PTR records in the customer's resolver for agent public IPs. We provided a command snippet and a temporary route ACL example.
In progress: Engineering will implement a safer fallback in the peername verifier to accept a cert SAN/IP match when PTR lookup returns NXDOMAIN or times out (change in control-plane auth verifier). A PR (see related_github_prs) has been opened to add a configurable policy: 'peername_check_mode: strict|san_only|ptr_prefer'. For this customer we applied a temporary policy toggle to 'san_only' via their private control-plane config while the code change rolls out.
Follow-ups: update private deployment docs to call out PTR requirements and recommended egress proxy rules; add a diagnostics check to the agent installer to detect PTR blocking and warn during onboarding.

Issue summary: Users requesting Just-In-Time (JIT) elevation via the Runbook Portal approval flow intermittently do not receive granted roles. The approval appears successful in the approval queue but the identity proxy shows duplicate claim entries, and the downstream RBAC grant never applies.

Impact: Engineers attempting on-call runbook escalations (temporary elevation) are blocked from executing critical remediation steps. Occurred ~15 times in the last 24h across multiple teams; affects oncall readiness.

Initial hypothesis: Recent identity-proxy change to de-duplicate incoming Okta assertions introduced a race where duplicate approval webhooks create two nearly-identical claims; the JIT service treats the second claim as conflicting and aborts role application.

1) As a non-priv user, open Runbook Portal and request temporary elevation via JIT.
2) Approve request from the Approval Queue (team approver).
3) Observe approval queue displays granted state and webhook POSTs a claim to identity-proxy.
4) Identity-proxy logs show two claims within 200ms, claim-ids differ only by suffix.
5) User session does not gain elevated roles; RBAC checks still return 403.
6) Repeating sometimes succeeds if duplicate does not occur.
Single approval results in one claim propagated to identity-proxy and successful role grant to the user's session within <10s.
Approval shows success but duplicate claim entries appear; JIT service aborts role application and user remains unprivileged. Sometimes requires manual reapplication by SRE.
identity-proxy ERROR: duplicate assertion detected: claim-id=a1b2c3dy_1 (incoming), claim-id=a1b2c3dy_2 (incoming)
jita-service WARN: aborting grant because existing claim with same user and ttl present (trace=trace-08c3)
approval-queue INFO: webhook delivered status=200 id=web-33445
runbook-portal DEBUG: request_completed request_id=req-99123 status=approved
- Correlated timestamps between Approval Queue and identity-proxy show duplicates arriving within 100-300ms.
- Recent deployment on 2026-03-09 to identity-proxy added an idempotency check that rewrites claim IDs when deduplication hot path triggers; this appears to create near-duplicate IDs instead of normalizing to a single canonical ID.
- Replayed webhook payloads from staging: single delivery => OK, duplicated replayed payloads => jita-service moves to 'conflict' code path and aborts grant.
- No errors in Okta logs indicating duplicate approvals; duplicates appear to originate in the approval-queue webhook dispatcher which retries on a perceived transient 502 from identity-proxy (race between first delivery success ack and retry window).
- Hypothesis: identity-proxy sometimes responds with 502 before processing complete; approval-queue retries and produces second webhook with a slightly different claim ID.
- Temporary mitigation tested: increase webhook timeout and suppress retries for identical payloads; reduced duplicate events in a short test window.
payload.summary: Approval queue claim duplication prevents just-in-time access grant for runbook portal

payload.description:
Issue summary:
After a scheduled CA/intermediate certificate rotation on our RADIUS/802.1X stack, a number of recently provisioned laptops failed to establish the corporate VPN when connected to office Wi-Fi. 802.1X association completed and DHCP was assigned; however VPN negotiation (IKEv2) repeatedly failed with certificate validation errors.

Impact:
~22 employees in SF office unable to initiate VPN over Wi‑Fi between 2026-03-10 08:15 and 2026-03-10 11:30 local time. Devices on wired network or cellular could connect successfully. Affected users were mostly new joiners provisioned in the last 4 weeks. No production services were impacted.

Environment:
- RADIUS: FreeRADIUS cluster behind F5, certificates rotated via automation runbook (rotate-ca.sh) at 2026-03-10 07:50 PST.
- VPN gateway: strongSwan-based IKEv2 endpoints (redwood-vpn-1/2) in us-west.
- Endpoints: mix of macOS 13/14 and Windows 11 corporate images provisioned via MDM.
- Wi-Fi controllers: Aruba controllers with 802.1X profile pointing to RADIUS pool.

Expected behavior:
New cert rotation should be transparent to already-provisioned endpoints and new endpoints that have the updated CA trust via MDM.

Actual behavior:
Endpoints that were provisioned in the last 30 days fail IKE auth with messages indicating untrusted client certificate or chain mismatch. Older endpoints and wired-connected devices succeed.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Provision a new corporate laptop with MDM profile pushed but before scheduled CA trust update applied.
2) Connect to office Wi‑Fi and complete 802.1X authentication (observed to succeed).
3) Attempt to start VPN via built-in IKEv2 profile.
4) Observe VPN negotiation failure repeating immediately after IKE_SA_INIT / IKE_AUTH.

Logs / evidence:
- strongSwan log excerpt (vpn gateway): "charon: 12[CFG] certificate verification failed for 'CN=device-123,OU=endpoints' - reason: unknown_ca"
- FreeRADIUS auth log: user EAP TLS OK (802.1X stage), shows server cert chain served from rotated CA chain.

Additional notes:
- macOS Console (racoon/charon): "peer certificate chain does not chain to trusted root"
- Automation job rotate-ca.sh ran at 07:50 and updated RADIUS server certs, but MDM CA push job (mdm/push-ca) scheduled for 09:00 failed for some devices (see mdm job failure ids).
Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: rotation introduced a new intermediate CA not present in endpoint trust stores. Confirmed by inspecting cert chain from RADIUS and comparing to MDM CA bundle.
- Verified that RADIUS and VPN certs were using the new chain; freeRADIUS sends full chain but endpoints validate against their local trust store which lacked the new intermediate.
- Why only recent devices? New images are built to only trust the narrow CA bundle provided at provisioning; older devices had the broader historical CA store. MDM push job showed ~30% failure rate during the scheduled rollout due to an intermittent device-side MDM agent issue.
- Workaround discovered: connecting via wired Ethernet allowed SCEP client renewal to fetch and install the intermediate during provisioning flow. Cellular tethering also worked.
- Peer test: created a temporary VPN endpoint that accepted certificate chain anchored to the old CA and verified those affected devices could connect. Rolling back RADIUS to old chain restored connectivity for everyone immediately.
- Root cause: automated CA rotation executed before confirming MDM rollout completion; lack of staged canary and device-level validation in the runbook.
Actions taken during incident:
- 08:25 - Triage call in #internal-network, incident owner assigned to Diego Ramos.
- 08:40 - Identified correlation between rotate-ca job and first VPN failures.
- 08:55 - Rolled back RADIUS/VPN TLS chain to previous CA on all RADIUS nodes to restore connectivity (temporary roll-back).
- 09:10 - Created targeted MDM retry job for failed devices (mdm/push-ca retry) and manual intervention queue for machines that did not auto-apply the CA.
- 10:20 - Confirmed affected users could connect via Wi‑Fi after rollback.
- 11:00 - Re-executed rotation with staggered rollout and verification hooks; verified MDM push succeeded for sample cohort via device logs.
- 11:30 - Rotation completed with updated runbook controls and monitoring; incident declared resolved.
Comments:
- "Aisha Patel (reporter): Noticed multiple new joiners hitting this at 08:10; they were blocked on internal tools and support queue filled quickly. Pushed for rollback asap." (Slack #it-support)
- "Diego Ramos (assignee): Rolled back RADIUS cert chain at 08:55; will coordinate root cause and follow-up. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/981" (Slack #internal-network)
- "Jules Kim (Endpoint Eng): MDM agent had a known regression in 2.18.3 that caused CA pushes to hang on devices with fresh images. Filed INT-14801 to patch agent across fleet." (internal-support)
- "SRE note: Added an alert to detect simultaneous failures of VPN auth + 802.1X OK within 5m window to catch this faster." (Diego)
Related links and artifacts:
- Slack: #internal-network thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123456789/p1678579200000000
- Infra PR for rollback & staged rotation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/981
- Confluence runbook (updated): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/IT/pages/8021X+CA+Rotation+Runbook
- Linked issue: INT-14801 (MDM agent patch)
Resolution summary:
- Immediate: Rolled back RADIUS/VPN certificate chain to previous trusted CA at 08:55, restoring VPN for affected devices.
- Short-term: Re-ran CA rotation with staged rollout, targeted MDM retries, and manual remediation for devices that failed to apply the CA.
- Long-term: Runbook updated to include pre-rotation MDM verification step, canary subset, automated rollback on >5% auth failures, and a post-rotation health check that validates VPN establishment for recent-provisioned endpoints.
Follow-up / action items:
- INT-14801: rollout MDM agent 2.18.4 and re-run CA push for remaining devices. (Jules Kim)
- INT-14802: add automated canary validation to rotate-ca.sh to verify MDM trust distribution before switching RADIUS (Diego Ramos)
- Update internal runbook and postmortem doc in Confluence. (Aisha Patel)
Resolution:
- Status: Resolved on 2026-03-12 after completing staggered rotation and MDM fixes. Root cause: premature CA rotation without validating MDM propagation; contributing factor: MDM agent regression on new images.
payload.summary: New 802.1X CA rotation prevented recent endpoints from establishing corporate VPN over office Wi-Fi

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Users attempting to approve runbook actions in the Console intermittently receive a UI error ('Approval failed: session not found') and are dropped back to the login page. The failures began after a proxy canary rollout on 2026-03-08.

Impact:
- Internal engineers cannot complete runbook approvals in the Console (affects ~10% of approval attempts in us-east-1 during incident window).
- Blocks on-call workflows that rely on expedited approvals (pauses automated remediation).

Environment:
- Prod Console behind identity-proxy cluster (canary and stable pools active).
- Okta SSO for authentication; session cookies issued by identity-proxy (cookie domain: .redwood-internal.com, SameSite=Lax).

Observed behavior:
- Users appear authenticated (Console shows user badge) but approval endpoint responds 401/403 with message 'session mismatch' or 'csrf token invalid'.
- Affected sessions have duplicate session IDs observed on two different proxy replicas within a 10s window.
- Requests with duplicated session id show differing SameSite/secure attributes between replicas in proxy access logs.

Expected behavior:
- Single authoritative session cookie per user with consistent attributes across all proxy replicas; approval requests should validate session and CSRF token and succeed.

Steps to reproduce (consistently under load with canary active):
1) Sign in through Okta to Console in Chrome (us-east region).
2) Open two tabs and load runbook approval page in both.
3) Trigger canary proxy route to flip traffic to replica A then to replica B (test harness toggles).
4) Attempt approval action in tab where session was initially established.
5) Observe approval fails and user is redirected to login.

Relevant logs/traces (snippets):
- identity-proxy-A access.log: "GET /runbook/approve 200 - session_id=abcd1234; SameSite=Lax; Secure"
- identity-proxy-B access.log: "POST /api/approve 401 - session_id=abcd1234; SameSite=None; Secure"
- console-service error: "session validation failed: csrf-mismatch for session abcd1234"
- Okta assertions: user session OK, no token revocation events.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Canary rollout introduced configuration drift where one proxy replica is setting SameSite=None and another SameSite=Lax, causing CSRF token checks to fail when requests route between them.
- Hypothesis 2: Session stickiness is not enforced for POST approval endpoints; when traffic flips between replicas, a stale in-memory session index leads to duplication and validation failures.
- Replayed traffic against single replica reproduces success; replay across two different replicas reproduces failure.
- No Okta-side anomalies found; user sessions remain valid.
- Affected window lines up with deployment of identity-proxy change in PR github.com/redwood/identity-proxy/pull/482 which altered cookie-setting logic for cross-site support.

Temporary workaround:
- Roll back canary and route all traffic to stable proxy pool (mitigates within minutes).
- Soft workaround: instruct approvers to open approvals in a new private window after rollback to avoid stale cookie attributes.

Next steps / proposed fix:
1) Roll back partial change in identity-proxy PR and patch cookie-attribute normalization so all replicas set explicit SameSite and domain values.
2) Make session-index storage resilient across replicas (move from in-memory to shared Redis-backed index for approval endpoint).
3) Add e2e test that asserts consistent cookie attributes across proxy replicas and enforces request stickiness for mutating endpoints.
4) Run a controlled canary with synthetic approval traffic and observability checks before broad rollout.

Owner: Diego Ramos (SRE)


Additional notes:
Reproduction shows cross-replica cookie attribute drift is root cause; in-memory session index exacerbates issue for POST endpoints. Related to recent cookie normalization change in identity-proxy PR 482.
Rollback proxy canary to stable pool; ask approvers to refresh sessions in private window if they still see failures.
Merge hotfix PR enforcing explicit cookie attrs (SameSite and Domain) + migrate approval session index to Redis; add e2e canary checks; schedule postmortem if incident recurs.
Priority P1 because this blocks internal remediation. Coordination required between SRE and Auth Eng. Diego to own rollback/hotfix, Marta to own PR review and canary plan. Postmortem draft after stabilization.
payload.summary: Console proxy session duplication prevents runbook approval flow

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a staged rollout of a new routing macro bundle, we observed conflicting SLA weight assignments inherited by child routing profiles. Impact: A subset of internal support routes were deprioritized unexpectedly, resulting in delayed automated triage and increased manual reassignments (~12% increase in median time-to-first-action for affected queues over the rollout window).

Observed behavior: The macro bundle 'support/sla_v2' contains a top-level SLA weight of 10 with an override rule for 'priority:internal' to 8. When the bundle was applied, several downstream routing profiles (created via inheritance templates) ended up with weight=0 in the active routing table due to an incorrect merge that treated missing keys as explicit zeroes. Expected behavior: Inherited routing profiles should inherit numeric SLA weights from parents unless explicitly overridden; missing fields should not be treated as zero.

Why this matters: SLA weight drives our automated routing and prioritization in the support router. Incorrect zeroing caused lower-priority buckets to consume less capacity than expected and pushed tickets to manual queues. This rollout impacted internal SLAs tied to response SLAs for P1/P2 internal tickets, and temporarily broke some autoscaling decisions made by the sla-orchestrator.
1) Create a macro bundle 'support/sla_v2' with top-level 'sla.weight: 10' and an override 'match: {priority: internal} -> sla.weight: 8'
2) Create a child routing profile via inheritance that does not explicitly define 'sla.weight'
3) Deploy the macro bundle with the routing-engine preview and apply to staging routing table
4) Observe the active routing table entries for the child profile showing 'sla.weight: 0' and compare to expected '8 or 10',
5) Reproduce by applying to a small subset of prod namespaces (we did this for 'support-team-alpha') and watch triage throughput drop
Initial hypothesis: merge function treats undefined keys as default 0 for numeric fields. Verified by running unit tests for merge logic on schema v3.
Reproduction in staging: toggling 'treat_missing_as_none' flag in router preview produces correct behavior; when flag is false, missing numeric field becomes 0.
Root cause: a change in the routing-engine merge library (commit 9f7a2c) changed the default for NumberNode.merge() to coerce null->0 for backward compatibility with legacy routes. That change did not account for macro inheritance semantics.
Scope: 7 routing profiles in prod were affected during the rollout window; historical runs show this merge behavior is new as of 2026-02-28 deployments.
Risk: Applying a hotfix to the merge library can affect other systems that expected the coercion; need careful rollout and compatibility tests.

[2026-03-05T14:02:14Z] routing-engine: profile=alpha-internal; sla.weight=0; source=merge_step
[2026-03-05T14:05:01Z] sla-orchestrator: allocated-concurrency=2 -> expected=6; decision=deprioritize
[2026-03-05T15:12:44Z] support-ops-alert: increased-mtfa=12pct; bucket=internal-alpha
(see attached logs in internal S3: s3://redwood-support/logs/2026-03-05/INT-47321/merge-debug.log)

2026-03-07 Product (Omar Reyes): Noted this affects internal SLAs for feature rollout automation. Requested a short postmortem and add a guardrail in console UI to preview effective SLA weights before applying macro bundles.
Workaround applied: feature-flag 'merge_strict_nulls=true' enabled on canary routing-engine pods which prevented zeroing of missing SLA weights. Hotfix branch prepared and tests added. Full patch pending staged rollout; no full resolution until patch is in prod across all regions.
1) Merge and release fix/merge-null-coercion; run compatibility suite with legacy macro bundles (owner: Marco)
2) Add console preview guardrail that computes effective SLA weights for a bundle before apply (owner: Product/Console)
3) Create telemetry for merge events that log when numeric fields are coerced (owner: Observability)
4) Postmortem documenting timeline and a new playbook for macro rollbacks (owner: Support Ops)

Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~02:30 UTC PagerDuty alert (PD-SEC-1218) flagged an anomalous increase in API activity originating from service account svc-ingest-2024. Impact: elevated API call volume (~1800 calls/min for a short window) causing transient backpressure on ingest queues and several 5xx spikes in downstream consumers. No customer data exfiltration has been confirmed, but investigation is ongoing.

Observed evidence:
- Monitoring alert: Anomaly detector + custom rule 'service-account-rate-surge' fired.
- Access logs: client_user_agent strings include 'Mozilla/5.0 (Chrome) TabBoost/2.1.0' and 'TabBooster', not seen historically.
- Unusual referer/Origin headers pointing to 'chrome-extension://a1b2c3-tabboost'.
- Egress destinations include a handful of external IPs (listed below) with POST requests to suspicious domains.

Environment: prod-us-west (primary incidents observed from us-west-2 region). Affected principal: service account 'svc-ingest-2024' (IAM roles: ingest-runner).

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 02:27 UTC: first anomaly detector trigger.
- 2026-03-10 02:31 UTC: spike peaks, alert routed to on-call SRE.
- 2026-03-10 02:35 UTC: temporary rate-limit applied to svc-ingest-2024; token rotation started.
- 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC: observed agent strings correlate with recently-installed browser extension samples reported by developers.

Steps to reproduce (investigation sandbox):
1) Install TabBoost (dev-supplied extension build) in a dedicated sandboxed Chrome instance.
2) Perform standard login flow; invoke local dev console to capture network traffic.
3) Observe extension performing background requests to collect tokens from localStorage/sessionStorage and sending to external collector.

Logs/snippets: (sanitized)
- Access log line: 2026-03-10T02:30:58Z svc-ingest-2024 POST /v1/ingest 200 host=api.redwood.prod us-west-2 ua=\"Mozilla/5.0 (Chrome) TabBoost/2.1.0\" src_ip=18.203.12.45 dst_ip=54.210.11.7
- Egress sample: POST https://collect.example-malware.com/ingest - payload contains base64-encoded JSON with fields matching localStorage keys.

Initial hypothesis: A malicious or compromised browser extension installed on several developer/designer machines is exfiltrating service-account tokens that were present in local caches (developer tools / long-lived tokens persisted by earlier workflows), then using those tokens from external infrastructure to call Redwood APIs. The pattern is distinct from standard phishing link flows and points to client-side exfiltration via extension.

Immediate impact/risks: unauthorized API usage, potential lateral movement if tokens grant broader privileges, and transient service degradation.

Stakeholders: InfoSec, SRE (ingest), Endpoint team, IAM, Developer Experience (to remediate dev workflows).
Summary of investigative steps performed to date:
- Correlated alerts with CloudFront/ALB logs and internal proxy (envoy) traces.
- Cross-referenced with CrowdStrike telemetry for endpoints of responding engineers; found TabBoost extension installed on 7 machines.
- Reproduced token-exfil pattern in an isolated VM with network capture (pcap saved to secure storage). Extension background page was observed reading window.localStorage and session cookies, then POSTing data to a known-malicious domain.
- Identified external collector IPs: 185.230.101.12, 193.47.152.9, 104.248.78.33. Filed abuse reports and blocked at perimeter.
- Inspected service-account usage: calls were made from external IP ranges not associated with our VPCs; behavior stopped after initial mitigation (token rotation).

Evidence store and links: Slack thread #sec-alerts (link below), pcap uploaded to /secure-evidence/INT-90231/pcap-03010.pcap, CrowdStrike case CS-11497.

Open hypotheses:
- Extension is explicitly malicious and exfiltrates credentials.
- Extension is benign but a third-party dependency was compromised.
- Developer workflow allowed long-lived service-account tokens to be present in browser storage (misconfiguration).

Next investigative steps: endpoint forensic (EDR sweep), MDM/Intune/Workspace One enforcement to remove extension, audit developer onboarding scripts for token persistence, check other service accounts for similar patterns.
Mitigations applied immediately:
1) Rotated all keys and tokens for svc-ingest-2024 and created short-lived credential alternatives.
2) Applied emergency rate-limits and an enforcement rule at the API gateway to block requests with user-agent strings matching 'TabBoost' and associated referer patterns.
3) Blocked outbound traffic to the three external IPs at the edge firewall and filed abuse with host providers.
4) Pushed an MDM policy to mark the extension as blocked where possible and notified the Endpoint team to remove it from managed machines.
5) Forced session invalidation for developer portals and required re-authentication with MFA for sensitive roles.
6) Opened escalation to Legal/Privacy for possible data exposure review.

All actions are documented in the internal incident runbook. Temporary mitigations appear to have stopped the bulk of unauthorized calls; we are continuing forensic analysis before declaring full remediation.
Partial mitigation completed: service-account tokens rotated, gateway blocks in place, and extension removal underway. Endpoint team reports 6 of 7 affected machines cleaned; one machine is offline and pending follow-up. Org-wide developer guidance sent to remove any unapproved extensions and to audit local credential storage practices.

Status: Mitigations deployed and immediate risk reduced, but root-cause verification and a full postmortem required. Postmortem scheduled and assigned to InfoSec (owner: Priya Nair) with delivery ETA 2026-03-18.
payload.summary: Malicious browser extension correlated with sudden service-account API activity spikes

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a Private deployment (customer X onboarding), our terraform-runner fails when attempting to attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance profile. The AWS API returns AccessDenied with a note about a permission boundary. This appears after a recent org-wide permission-boundary propagation. Impact: Provisioning for one private customer environment is blocked; dedicated/nodepool creation for private deploys is failing and CI runs are stuck. Environment: prod account for private-deploy-us-east, terraform-runner job v2026.03.09, org permission-boundary recently updated (deploy-priv-boundary-v2).
Private deployment provisioning blocked for one onboarding customer; manual workarounds required for other pending customers. CI job queue for private deploys is growing and dedicated capacity allocation is delayed.
1) Kick off private deployment pipeline for customer X (pipeline: private-deploy/provision) using terraform-runner v2026.03.09
2) Terraform applies resources: create instance profile, create role, attempt aws_iam_role_policy_attachment and aws_iam_instance_profile_role attachment
3) aws API returns AccessDenied when attaching role to instance profile with error referencing permission boundary 'deploy-priv-boundary-v2'
4) Pipeline errors out and keeps the terraform workspace locked; further retries fail with same error
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name rw-priv-deploy-ec2-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonEC2RoleforSSM ERROR: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/terraform-runner-role/terraform is not authorized to perform: iam:AttachRolePolicy on resource: role rw-priv-deploy-ec2-role due to permission boundary: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/deploy-priv-boundary-v2
Terraform apply log snippet: Error: Error attaching IAM Role to Instance Profile: AccessDenied: Cannot call PutRolePolicy on role rw-priv-deploy-ec2-role: Permission boundary prevents operation
CloudTrail event id: 9a1b2c3d-logs: iam:PutRolePolicy denied by policy deploy-priv-boundary-v2 (principal: terraform-runner-sa)
Recent org change: PR #2754 merged 2026-03-08: 'enforce-deploy-boundary-v2' applied across prod accounts
Checked CloudTrail events for the failing request (event IDs above). The denied action is iam:AttachRolePolicy / iam:PassRole when called by terraform-runner assumed role.
Confirmed permission boundary 'deploy-priv-boundary-v2' was applied org-wide on 2026-03-08 (related PR). The boundary restricts allowed IAM actions and principals; its current statement blocks attaching managed policies unless the request includes a specific tag 'trusted-deployer=true'.
Observed terraform-runner assumes role 'terraform-runner-role' that does not include the required tag in the request context; AWS does not accept request context tags for iam:AttachRolePolicy in our current setup.
Hypothesis: The permission boundary was tightened to require either a specific resource tag or a caller principal condition. Terraform provider calls that do not set the tag fail. Older roles created before the boundary are unaffected, new role attachments fail.
Verified GCP side (for cross-cloud workflows) is unaffected; this is AWS-specific.
Checked linked internal ticket INT-951357 (similar boundary enforcement), but that ticket dealt with CI service account tagging; current issue is terraform-runner cannot surface the required tag when calling IAM APIs.
Temporary mitigation tested: manually create the EC2 role and instance profile using a human operator with elevated perms, then let terraform import the resources. This allows pipeline to continue but is manual and not scalable.
Manual creation of role & instance profile by ops (with elevated user that bypasses the boundary), then terraform import to unlock workspace. For queued pipelines, ops can create temporary roles to unblock. Documented in runbook 'priv-deploy/mitigations-2026-03'.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:20 - Security (Elena Novak): 'Permission boundary was intended to prevent cross-account delegation by nonapproved runners. We can add terraform-runner role ARN to an allowlist in boundary policy as an immediate fix. Long-term we want runners to surface request tags.'
1) Schedule emergency org-policy patch to include terraform-runner ARN in boundary allowlist (owner: Security). 2) Implement a change in terraform-runner to call STS:AssumeRole with SessionTags or set aws:RequestTag at call time (owner: infra, ETA 2 weeks). 3) Re-run blocked private deploy pipeline after emergency change and document full postmortem (owner: SRE).
pending - emergency allowlist patch planned. Manual workarounds in place to unblock individual customers. A long-term fix will modify terraform-runner to surface request tags or alter provisioning flow to use an allowed intermediary.
payload.summary: Terraform runner unable to attach IAM role to instance profile during private deployment (permission boundary enforcement)

Issue summary:
Request to build a reusable, auditable gateway (self-service) for provisioning short‑lived cross-organization collaboration artifacts: Slack shared channels (external workspace or guest), a dedicated Confluence space with a restricted template, and a tied Jira sandbox project for joint work. The gateway must include approval workflow, RBAC guardrails, automated retention/archival, and audit exports to S3.

Impact:
- Currently multiple pods create ad-hoc shared channels and external Confluence spaces using manual steps. This causes inconsistent permissions, missed offboarding, and manual audit effort for security/compliance.
- We need a standardized lifecycle to avoid stale external access and to centralize evidence for compliance requests.

Request details (what we want done):
1) A self‑service form (Confluence page or internal portal) that creates a Jira approval ticket and, after approval, triggers automation to:
   - Create a Slack shared channel (or a private channel + external guest invite depending on external tenant capabilities) following naming convention redwood-external-<vendor>-<purpose>-<YYYYMM>.
   - Create a Confluence space with the "External Collaboration" space template and permissions limited to specified users and the external address.
   - Spin up a scoped Jira project (temp-sandbox) with preloaded issue types, a canned workflow, and reduced visibility.
2) Approval flow: Must include security reviewer and requestor manager; approval should be required within 48 hours or auto-escalate to IT manager.
3) Retention & archival: Default TTL 90 days after last activity; automation to snapshot Confluence pages and export Slack channel history to S3 bucket (encrypted) before archival. Admin should be able to extend TTL with recorded justification.
4) Audit and evidence: All artifacts, approvals, and exports must be logged to an audit S3 path and have a Confluence record. Provide a discoverable report that security/compliance can query by vendor name or date range.
5) Permissions & least privilege: External guest accounts must have limited access; no ability to create new channels or add other guests. Jira project role mapping must restrict admin-level access to internal approvers only.
6) Service account: Create or reuse a service account with scoped keys; keys must rotate every 30 days and be stored in KMS.
7) Rollout plan: Pilot with Platform Solutions (2 squads) then enable across org.

Acceptance criteria:
- A working demo of the end‑to‑end flow (form -> approval -> artifacts created) in a staging tenant.
- Automated export job successfully writes Slack history and Confluence snapshot to S3 and a sample audit report is generated.
- RBAC policy applied to created artifacts matches the spec and documented runbook exists.
- PR with IaC and automation code merged and a runbook created in Confluence.

Notes / constraints:
- Must preserve PII minimization during export; security will supply filters.
- Avoid creating long-lived external service accounts.
- Work with Legal for terms if sharing data with external partners.

Additional notes:
2026-03-04 - Legal (comment): Please ensure the Confluence space template has the legal disclaimer and shared-space checklist checkbox. Legal will review samples during pilot.
Until automation is ready, Platform Solutions will follow manual checklist posted in Confluence: manual ticket + security email + ad-hoc channel creation. This will be tracked under label 'external-manual'.
payload.summary: Create self-service Cross‑Org Collaboration gateway: automated Slack shared channels + Confluence space + Jira sandbox with approval & retention

Issue summary:
The LLM health-check agent that runs periodic self-checks and registers service endpoints with the prod cloud-account registration-service is failing to obtain a short-lived STS session. The STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity call returns an AccessDenied error with a context that indicates an attribute-based delegation policy rejected the session because the SAML assertion did not include the org:env attribute.

Impact:
- Health-check agent unsuccessful in registering ~30% of dedicated node pools in us-west-2.
- Alerts on service-registration topic firing intermittently; some canary routing fallbacks triggered.
- Potential risk for automated failover/rolling restarts not being recorded in central inventory.

Environment:
- prod account: aws-prod-123456789012 (us-west-2)
- Component: dedicated-provisioner -> registration-service -> auth proxy -> STS assume-role path
- Agent version: 2026.02.15-rc3

Steps to reproduce:
1. Deploy health-check agent image 2026.02.15-rc3 to a new dedicated pool in us-west-2.
2. Observe registration logs (agent -> registration-service) for AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity call.
3. Check CloudTrail event for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity and IAM policy evaluation details.

Observed logs / errors:
- Agent logs: "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed: AccessDenied: The SAML assertion is missing required attribute 'org:env'"
- CloudTrail: "eventName": "AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity", "errorMessage": "Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity on resource arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/llm-registration-role"
- IAM policy simulator trace points to a DENY in org-wide delegation policy (org-policy-id: ORG-DELEG-2025) that enforces attribute whitelist for SAML/OIDC sessions.

Expected behavior:
- Agent should be able to complete a delegated STS session and register the pool. The registration-service should fall back to alternate short-lived credential flow only if delegation is not permitted by org policy.

Workaround attempted:
- Temp: Manual invocation of AssumeRole with a fully-populated SAML assertion from the ops identity provider allowed registration to proceed.
- Workaround for customers: run the agent with a pre-provisioned long-lived service principal (not acceptable for long-term).

Request / Next steps:
- Triage policy mismatch with Identity team to confirm whether org attribute 'org:env' should be required for these agent-initiated flows.
- If policy is intended, update the agent's OIDC/SAML assertion generation path (auth-proxy) to include org:env attribute for dedicated pools.
- Short-term: create an allowlist exception for the registration-service role for existing dedicated pools while patch is implemented.
2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Initial ticket created after oncall saw 12 failed registrations in last 15m (alerts: registration.failures.high). Reporter: Angela Park.
Checked CloudTrail events for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity - consistent AccessDenied with missing attribute in assertion. Confirmed by security-tooling trace.
Reviewed org delegation policy ORG-DELEG-2025: policy enforces Condition: StringEquals: saml:attributes/org:env to allowed list [prod, staging]. The agent assertion did not include this attribute (agent auth-proxy uses minimal claim set).
Auth-proxy (auth-proxy v1.4.2) code path: when running as daemon for fleet agents it serializes only 'sub' and 'aud' claims. OIDC bridge library change in 2026.01 removed attribute injection for backward-compatibility - likely regression.
Reproduced locally by forging an OIDC assertion without org:env and calling AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity -> AccessDenied. With org:env present the call succeeds.
Consequence: any agent instance bootstrapped via the current auth-proxy cannot register unless the IdP supplies org:env or auth-proxy is patched.
Linked to PR for auth-proxy fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/392 (work-in-progress).

Additional notes:
Priya Raman (identity team) (2026-03-10 11:30 UTC): We rolled out ORG-DELEG-2025 in Feb to enforce env tagging on SAML/OIDC. That should not break internal agent flows. Can you attach CloudTrail event id?
SRE Lead - Jordan Miles (2026-03-11 08:20 UTC): As a short-term mitigation, we can add an allowlist for role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/llm-registration-role scoped to instance-profile principal, but prefer an auth-proxy fix.
2026-03-12 15:30 UTC - Auth-proxy patch merged: inject org:env claim for agent registration flows. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/392
Temporary allowlist created for role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/llm-registration-role scoped to instance-profile principal on 2026-03-11 10:00 UTC (ops action id OPS-REG-001).
Canary deployment of patched auth-proxy to registration-service succeeded in staging (2026-03-12 12:10 UTC). Production rollout scheduled in maintenance window 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.
Follow-up: Identity team to audit other internal agent flows for missing attributes (task INT-883999 assigned).
Ticket to be closed after 48h of stable registration metrics in prod (post-rollout verification).
payload.summary: LLM health-check agent failing to register in prod AWS account due to STS delegation policy rejecting session

payload.description:
Issue summary: After a staged sidecar (edge-proxy) rollout on 2026-03-09, a subset of internal users intermittently lose group-based RBAC attributes when accessing the Redwood Console. Impact: Affected users see console UI in read-only mode or receive 403s for actions requiring role write privileges. This affects internal employees and on-call SREs in prod us-east and some cross-region requests routed via us-east.

Observed behavior: Identity proxy logs show 'missing_groups' and header truncation/parse errors. Re-authenticating sometimes restores full access for a short window.

Expected behavior: Okta-derived group claims (X-Okta-Groups header) must be consistently preserved and parsed by the identity proxy for correct RBAC role resolution.

Workaround: Rolling back sidecar to the previous image (edge-proxy:v1.24.7) on the affected node pool restores stable behavior for users routed through those nodes. Users can also trigger a manual sign-out/sign-in which occasionally recovers proper group mapping until the next request hit a problematic node.

1) Use a user account with >10 Okta groups (replicates longer header values).
2) From prod us-east, open Redwood Console and navigate to a write-protected page (feature flag admin or rollout).
3) Observe UI rendered in read-only mode or attempt an action and receive 403.
4) Check identity-proxy logs for the request id (X-Request-Id) and see 'header_truncation' or 'missing_groups' entries

Issue summary: During a user merge performed by the SCIM reconciliation job, two user identities were linked at the session layer. This produced duplicate active sessions where one session intermittently reflected the other user's RBAC claims. Impact: Affected internal staff observed seeing stale role claims (temporary elevation) or missing roles unpredictably when switching between tabs or services. No external customer data was accessible, but the behavior risks privilege confusion for oncall and SRE workflows.
~7 users intermittently affected; primarily support-console and runbook-runner access. Potential privacy/privilege risk; currently contained to prod us-west. No confirmed malicious activity.
1) Trigger a SCIM merge for accounts with shared external_id hashes (test clone of production data).
2) Observe session records in session-store for both identities immediately after merge (session_id reuse or linked parent_id present).
3) Login as merged user and open support-console; switch to runbook-runner in a new tab to surface claim desync.
4) Check identity-proxy request headers; some requests carry the merged user's session token but the RBAC claim payload belongs to the pre-merge identity.
5) Capture traces via X-Req-Id and correlate to scim-sync job run id.
Auth trace: req=abcd1234 owner=user-137 -> session parent_link=session-xyz (unexpected)
Session-store dump (redacted): session-xyz { user_id: user-137, linked_user_ids: [user-522], last_touch: 2026-03-10T14:02:11Z }
SCIM job run: scim-sync-2026-03-10-14:00 (merge batch=17)
Sample console audit entry: 2026-03-10T14:04:02Z user=user-137 action=impersonation_check result=ok (claims from user-522)
Initial hypothesis: SCIM merge job updated identity aliasing but did not atomically update session linkage metadata, leaving stale linked_user_ids in session-store.
Identity-proxy applies RBAC claims from cached session blob when request arrives; if session blob references linked_user_ids, proxy selects highest-privilege claim without verifying primary ownership.
Reproduced locally by replaying scim-sync merge with existing sessions present; observed session.parent_link set to the wrong canonical id when merge ordering was reversed.
Race condition suspected between scim-sync worker finalize step and session-store cleanup TTL (finalize writes alias table, session cleanup expects alias table first).
Run session invalidation for affected user IDs and force re-login: /admin/sessions/invalidate?user_ids=[user-137,user-522]. Also paused SCIM merge batch processing until hotfix deploy. Issued a temporary helm rollout that disables non-critical session-link merging in scim worker.
1) Patch scim-sync to perform atomic alias swap and emit a session-invalidate event for merged user IDs. 2) Add an identity-proxy verification step: cross-check session.primary_user == claim.user before applying RBAC claims; if mismatch trigger re-auth flow. 3) Add unit+integration tests to simulate merge concurrency.
1) PR created: github.com/redwood/auth-service/pull/4887 (hotfix) — awaiting review by 2026-03-13.
2) Schedule canary deploy to staging and us-west-small pool on 2026-03-14.
3) Run retro-check sweep to invalidate sessions for all merges in the last 48 hours.
4) Postmortem + runbook update after incident closure.

Additional notes:
in progress - hotfix PR opened and patch queued for canary. Pending verification in canary and runbook update.
SCIM Merge Runbook v2 (confluence link above) - will add a new section 'force-session-invalidate-after-merge'
Privileged access anomalies were transient and limited to internal tooling. Recommend privilege review for any users affected after re-provisioning. Notify security if any user reports unexpected data access.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We need company-wide enforcement of a lightweight metadata schema for new and existing Slack channels, plus a nightly export that creates an easy-to-browse directory (CSV + Confluence index page).

Impact:
- Currently many channels are created without clear owners, project codes, or data-classification tags which makes audits and onboarding slower.
- Security and compliance teams request a machine-readable channel directory for quarterly reviews.
- Platform teams want to filter channels by lifecycle (ephemeral vs permanent) for archival automation.

Request:
- Define minimal metadata fields: project_code, owner_handle(s), data_classification (public/internal/confidential), lifecycle (ephemeral/permanent), canonical_confluence_page.
- Implement enforcement on channel creation: when a new channel is created via self-serve flow, an automation should verify metadata is present. If missing, present a modal or message prompting the creator to provide required fields; for certain workspace types (e.g., broad public channels) require explicit owner and classification.
- Backfill existing channels: run a best-effort discovery job that populates metadata from channel descriptions and recent activity; surface channels that need manual review in a Confluence table.
- Nightly export: assemble an exportable CSV and update a Confluence index page with the directory (one line per channel with metadata). The export should include last_active, member_count, and a link to the canonical Confluence page if provided.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New-channel modal or verification triggers for >90% of new channel creations in the prod workspace.
2) Nightly CSV export stored in an internal S3 bucket and Confluence index page updated automatically.
3) Backfill job flags channels with missing owner or classification and creates a review ticket for channels with >100 members and no owner.
4) Security and Compliance can download the directory and filter by data_classification.

Notes on constraints:
- Slack admin APIs (SCIM and Conversations APIs) are available but rate-limited; the design must tolerate retries and exponential backoff.
- Some partner integrations create channels programmatically; we need a short whitelist for trusted bots to skip human prompts.
- Confluence has API quotas; batch updates are required to avoid rate limits.
Create a test channel in a sandbox workspace and confirm the modal prompts for metadata fields.
Create a channel via the approved webhook (whitelisted) and confirm it bypasses the modal but still includes metadata when provided.
Run the backfill job on a sample set of 200 channels and verify it annotates or flags channels as expected.
Verify nightly CSV appears in s3://redwood-ops-exports/channel-directory/YYYY-MM-DD.csv and Confluence index is updated.
Ask Security to filter exported CSV by data_classification and confirm results are correct.
Simulate Slack API rate limit errors and confirm the job retries with exponential backoff without losing entries.
Evaluated Slack admin APIs: Conversations.list + conversations.info + users.lookupByEmail are sufficient for metadata reads; SCIM needed for service account discovery.
Backfill heuristics: parse channel topic/description for 'owner:@handle' and project codes like 'PRJ-\d{3,6}'. Use last 30-day active user to guess owner when description absent.
Confluence update approach: generate a single HTML table page via the REST API on nightly run to avoid many small updates (reduces quota hits).
Whitelist criteria: integrations with service accounts that have existed >90 days and are in infra/tools org; will maintain a small allowlist in a config repo.

Additional notes:
In Progress - scaffolding complete. Modal prototype posted and initial backfill job run flagged ~1,420 channels for review. Next: finalize metadata schema with Security and DevTools, implement retry logic for Slack API rate limits, and wire nightly export to Confluence. ETA for MVP rollout to prod workspace: 2026-03-21.

Issue summary: Multiple customers (first reported by NimbusChat) observe that when an SSE session is interrupted by an edge proxy connection migration and then resumes, the final conditional 'end' control event that signals a clean terminal block is not delivered to the client. Impact: Final punctuation/closing JSON wrapper for streamed choices is missing or truncated, causing client parsers to treat the response as incomplete. Affected clients see partial final choices, missing closing metadata and inconsistent 'done' flags.

Environment: prod/us-east fronted by our edge-proxy fleet; customers on enterprise plan using our JS SDK with fetch-based SSE. Affected models: redwood-alpha-1 and gpt-open-7b observed in reproductions.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long SSE stream via the JS SDK (example attached) for a request that emits a conditional 'end' control event once model completes.
2) Trigger a controlled edge-proxy connection migration (simulated by tcpkill / forced circuit shuffle on repro host) during the last 5–10s of streaming.
3) Allow client to auto-reconnect and resume session using resume-token.
4) Observe that stream payload contains final text tokens but final 'end' control event and trailing metadata are missing or arrive as an empty line.

Observed behavior: Clients receive what looks like the last paragraph but no terminal control event; JSON wrappers may be unterminated (missing closing ']' or '}}'). Some SDKs treat this as stream timeout and throw parsing errors. No 5xx seen in logs; the runtime marks the session as Completed, but the edge-proxy logs show an early 101->200 handoff.

Expected behavior: Resume should preserve and forward the terminal 'end' control event and associated metadata so clients can deterministically close the stream.

Attachments: repro script, client traces, edge-proxy logs excerpt, sample SSE transcript (redacted), sample SDK stacktrace.
Aisha Karim (Support) - 2026-03-10: Opened ticket after NimbusChat sent multiple example transcripts showing missing terminal control event. Included repro steps and raw SSE transcript.
Jonah Park (Eng) - 2026-03-10: Assigned. Initial hypothesis: edge-proxy connection migration is normalizing or dropping a one-byte terminal marker during handoff. Will reproduce in staging with tcpkill and enable verbose edge-proxy debug logs.
NimbusChat (Customer) - 2026-03-10: Customer indicates this happens intermittently, ~3% of long streams, higher when mobile clients are on flaky networks. They can repro with our sample app by toggling airplane mode twice.
Samir Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Correlated incidents to an edge-proxy host rotation cluster at 2026-03-09T23:xxZ in us-east-1. Found sequences where proxied response flush was acknowledged but the control frame arrived in a subsequent TLS record that was dropped during rebind.
Jonah Park (Eng) - 2026-03-12: Added temporary mitigation to SDK to accept final newline-empty-line as implicit end and attempt JSON reassembly. This is a conservative workaround; customers must upgrade SDK to opt-in. Preparing runtime patch to include redundant end marker during resume window.
Reproduction: Created a long streaming request that emits final 'end' control event and reproduction succeeded locally when inducing connection migration using tc qdisc netem + tcpkill. Edge-proxy logs: observed sequence of events where TLS connection handoff returned 200 before last TLS record with control event arrived. Packet capture (pcap) shows last Application DATA record containing "\n[end]'" was retransmitted but ACKed only to previous connection; forwarded handover created a small window where last record was not consumed. Runtime behavior: serving-runtime set session state to COMPLETED when it sent terminal event; however, the edge-proxy's resume logic used idempotency mapping that filtered duplicate control frames during rebind, treating them as retransmits and dropping the trailing control marker. Hypotheses: 1) Edge-proxy idempotency filter incorrectly dedupes final control markers when resume-token timestamp delta < 1s. 2) SDK resume handshake does not include a trailing-offset/byte-check and relies solely on token; missing offset allows proxy to drop trailing bytes during handoff. Evidence: grep of edge-proxy logs found markers 'idemp:drop control-frame end token=<token>' at the time of incidents. Repro commands: curl --http2 -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?resume_token=abc ; tcpdump -w capture.pcap host <edge> and filter for TLS records containing [end]. Observed commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/commit/8f3b2d5 (added logging). Next steps: instrument edge-proxy to preserve last 2 control frames during connection migration, add resume offset to SDK handshake, and add runtime idempotency blacklist for 'end' markers during resume window.
Mitigation deployed: 2026-03-12 - Released edge-proxy logging and temporary config to preserve last 2 control frames during connection migration in the us-east canary. SDK patch 1.2.4 published to treat an empty final event as implicit end; provided NimbusChat with pre-release build. Long-term fix: engineering to ship edge-proxy change that disables dedupe for 'end' control events within a 2s resume window and update resume handshake to include byte-offset verification. Follow-up tasks: test rollout across eu-west and production runbook to validate resume integrity (INT- follow-up ticket created). Customer follow-up: NimbusChat asked for post-rollout verification; Support scheduled a joint test on 2026-03-15. Ticket status: In Progress until full prod rollout confirmed.
payload.summary: SSE resume hides conditional terminal 'end' event after edge proxy connection migration

Issue summary: After SSD replacements performed during the standard repair workflow, devices fail automated device certificate (SCEP) enrollment and do not complete Intune/Autopilot provisioning. Impact: Repaired devices require manual intervention (local admin action or offline cert enrollment) and cannot join Azure AD or apply compliance policies. Environment: repair bench network uses corporate proxy with PAC; affected image is Windows 11 22H2 corporate build applied after SSD swap.

Observed behavior: Enrollment stalls on 'Applying device configuration' or fails with SCEP errors in device logs. CA side shows incomplete SCEP challenge/response sequences for affected attempts.
Perform SSD replacement and restore corporate image via repair bench process
Boot device into OOBE/Autopilot and connect to repair bench network (uses PAC/HTTP proxy)
Allow Intune/Autopilot to progress; observe SCEP enrollment step
SCEP client logs show HTTP 407 or persistent timeouts; device does not receive machine certificate
Initial hypothesis: proxy returns HTTP 407 for SCEP POSTs because it requires authentication for the repair subnet; SCEP client cannot present machine credentials prior to obtaining a device cert.
Packet capture shows SCEP POST to https://ca.internal.example/SCEP met with immediate 407 from proxy. When proxy bypassed, SCEP completes normally.
Network team confirmed PAC file contains a legacy rule that routes the repair bench subnet through the proxy rather than DIRECT for the CA FQDN.
Endpoint team reproduced the failure by assigning a repair-bench IP to a test VM and saw identical SCEP 407s.
Workaround tested: update PAC to return DIRECT for CA host for repair subnet; devices then completed enrollment and received machine certs.
Impact estimate: repair bench reported ~8 of 10 devices affected during the morning shift; manual remediation takes ~10-15 minutes per device.
Intune shows devices assigned Autopilot profile but missing device certificate which blocks compliance/policy application and conditional access.
Sofia M. (Support) 2026-03-10: Device fails SCEP enrollment after SSD RMA; logs show HTTP 407. Requesting network team confirm proxy behavior.
Jordan Patel (Network) 2026-03-10: Confirmed proxy requires auth for outbound POSTs from repair subnet; PAC returns proxy for that range due to legacy rule. We'll update PAC to return DIRECT for CA host as an interim measure.
Ethan Chen (Endpoint Eng) 2026-03-11: Verified bypassing proxy fixes enrollment. Propose updating repair bench DHCP options to include WPAD override or static route. Also recommend implementing certificate pre-staging for repaired devices in Intune.
Elena Park (Repair Tech Lead) 2026-03-11: Repair techs reported ~8/10 devices impacted today; manual fix workflow is slowing throughput. Please prioritize PAC change.
Sofia M. 2026-03-11: PAC override applied by network at 09:45 PT; verified SCEP success on a sample of 20 devices. Monitoring for regressions.
Temporary workaround: Network updated PAC to return DIRECT for the CA FQDN from the repair bench subnet (rolled 2026-03-11 09:45 PT). After the change, re-provisioned devices successfully completed SCEP and received machine certificates. Long-term remediation: network to implement static route or proxy allowlist for CA servers from repair VLAN and Endpoint team to implement pre-staging of device certificates for RMA workflow via Intune automation.
Workaround applied in prod and validated - SCEP enrollment succeeded for the sampled devices.
Follow-up ticket INT-9281 created to automate pre-staging of device certs for RMA workflow.
Recommend adding SCEP endpoints to proxy allowlist and adding monitoring alert for spike in SCEP failures.
Update repair runbook to include proxy check and quick bypass steps prior to imaging.

INT-9282 - Network: add static route and proxy allowlist for CA servers from repair VLAN
