Issue summary: Several infra engineers need temporary cross-project access in both AWS and GCP to diagnose a networking/permission problem surfaced during a private cluster migration. Request: establish least-privilege, time-bound role mappings between the 'infra-ops' GCP project and the 'platform-prod' GCP project, and create an AWS IAM role assumption path from Redwood-staff accounts to the production account for specific SRE personas.

Impact: Engineers are blocked from collecting instance-level logs, describing certain VPC connectors, and running diagnostic jobs in the target projects. This is delaying a staged migration and causing elevated alerting noise as automated runbooks retry and fail.

Environment: Production (prod) across multi-cloud: GCP (europe-west1 primary), AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2).

Request details: 1) Define and apply GCP IAM custom role(s) that allow iam.serviceAccounts.get, compute.instances.get, compute.networks.list limited to resources in the target projects. 2) Configure IAM bindings so members in the 'redwood-infra-eng' Google Group can impersonate a service account in the target project using iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy/allow impersonation. 3) In AWS, create a cross-account role (AssumeRole) named RedwoodInfraDiagnosticRole in the production account with a trust policy for the Redwood-staff AWS account IDs (list provided privately) and scoped policies that allow ec2:DescribeInstances, logs:GetLogEvents, logs:DescribeLogGroups, and sts:AssumeRole chaining only to a short-lived diagnostics role. 4) All changes must be time-bound (72 hours) by default and logged to audit (Cloud Audit Logs/CloudTrail) with tags 'temp_access_migration'.

Acceptance criteria: - Infra engineers in the specified groups can perform listed diagnostics for up to 72 hours. - All actions are covered by audit logs with a retention label. - There is a documented rollback that revokes access at expiry or on-demand.

Notes: Customer-facing incidents are not involved; this is internal to migration workstreams.
Not an application bug. Repro steps for blocked behavior: 1) Attempt to list network connectors in target GCP project using gcloud compute networks list --project=platform-prod -> Permission denied. 2) Attempt to get logs from a production EC2 instance via aws logs get-log-events -> AccessDenied. 3) Attempt to impersonate target service account -> iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy returns 403. These steps can be reproduced by an engineer without elevated membership in the target projects.
GCP denied response samples:
- "Error: Permission 'compute.networks.list' denied on resource project 'platform-prod'" (2026-03-12T16:03:21Z).
AWS denied response sample:
- "An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the DescribeInstances operation: User is not authorized to perform: ec2:DescribeInstances" (2026-03-12T16:12:04Z).
2026-03-13: Triage by Priya. Confirmed issue is permissions surface, not networking. Verified group memberships for two engineers: membership shows in Google Groups but no IAM bindings in target project. Checked Cloud Audit Logs: no prior role binding events for 'redwood-infra-eng' group.

Hypotheses: 1) Role mappings were not propagated when the platform-prod project was created under a different org folder. 2) Pending org policy prevents cross-project service account impersonation. 3) In AWS, SCPs or account-level deny rules block AssumeRole from staff accounts.

Evidence gathered: - GCP Organization policies show 'restrictServiceAccountDelegation' enabled at org level (affects impersonation). - AWS SCP audit shows a Deny for 'sts:AssumeRole' from external principal for one prod account (account 987654321098).

Next steps: 1) SRE/Cloud Infra to propose exact custom role definitions. 2) Security to review org policy exception request for impersonation (if required). 3) Create ephemeral roles and apply tagging. Assigned to Marco to coordinate with Security and Cloud Infra.
Draft GCP custom role YAML and test in staging
Open security exception ticket for org policy change if needed
Create AWS cross-account AssumeRole with time-bound sessionDuration
Add audit tags and update runbook with revocation steps

AWS role created in a sandbox account for testing; production role blocked by SCP — security will coordinate with finance-owned account to authorize temporary trust. Final revocation automation will be implemented using an expiry Lambda that removes the binding at 72 hours and emits a Jira comment. No permanent privileges granted.

Also schedule a post-mortem to evaluate why initial project onboarding missed these role mappings.

Issue summary:
We need a new cross-pod incident bridge pattern that creates a threaded Slack channel (or private channel thread) for high-severity incidents, automatically persists a sanitized transcript to Confluence for post-incident review, and runs an opt-in AI summarizer to create a one-paragraph incident summary. The transcript must be time-bound (TTL) and auto-archived/expunged after 90 days unless retention is extended via an approval flow.

Impact:
- Improves follow-up and onboarding for postmortems by centralizing discussion threads and summaries.
- Reduces noise in primary #incidents channel by creating ephemeral threaded bridges.
- Must satisfy security/compliance requirement: transcripts must be scrubbed for PII before persistent storage and retention controlled with an approval workflow.

Request details / acceptance criteria:
1) Automation creates a locked thread or private channel per incident with standardized naming: incident-<ID>-<short-title>.
2) Bot pins incident runbook link and posts list of on-call participants.
3) At incident close the bot triggers: (a) optional AI summarizer (internal model endpoint) that produces a 3-sentence public summary, (b) scrubber that masks email addresses, API keys and other probable secrets, (c) publishes sanitized transcript to a Confluence page under OPS > Incident Archives.
4) Transcript pages get TTL metadata (90d default). A request button in Confluence allows owners to extend retention via an approval workflow routed to Security and Legal.
5) All automation actions must be auditable (Jira ticket created and linked, audit log entry for retention changes).
6) Provide toggle in admin console to enable/disable AI summarizer for specific pods.

Timeline: prefer pilot in two pods within 3 weeks, full rollout after compliance signoff.

Notes on safety: the AI summarizer must not expose raw PII; summarizer must run on private model endpoint (dedicated tier) and store only the sanitized output.

1) New incident thread creation verified in staging and prod; 2) Sanitizer detects and masks emails and API-like strings in a sample transcript; 3) Confluence page created with TTL metadata and a visible 'Request Retention Extension' action; 4) Jira ticket auto-created on finalization with links to thread and Confluence; 5) Admin toggle works and disables summarizer when off.
Trigger path to repro in staging:
1) Create test incident ticket INT-TEST-800 and mark severity as Sev2.
2) Use /incident-start in #incidents-staging channel and follow prompts.
3) Add a message containing an email and a fake API key.
4) Close incident and observe bot workflow: summarizer prompt, sanitizer output, Confluence page creation, TTL metadata, Jira ticket creation.
- Prototype options reviewed: reuse incident-bot (python) and add post-close hook to call sanitizer service.
- Sanitizer implementation: regex-first pass + danger-signal heuristic + optional manual review for flagged tokens.
- Access control: Confluence page creation must set space to OPS Incident Archives and apply a page property 'ttl: 90d'.
- Audit concerns: add structured metadata to created Jira ticket (labels + custom field incident-thread-url).
- Dependencies: Security approval for masking rules, Confluence admin permissions to create pages via automation, and an internal model endpoint for summarizer (request to infra needed).
1) Build a small service 'bridge-controller' that subscribes to incident lifecycle events. 2) On incident-start create slack private-thread via bot user, enforce naming convention. 3) On incident-close run sanitizer, then call private summarizer endpoint if summarizer toggle is enabled for the pod. 4) Create Confluence page via API with sanitized transcript and summary, set TTL metadata and ACLs. 5) Create final Jira ticket linking to artifacts. 6) Implement an approval workflow in Confluence using page comments + a webhook that triggers a Jira approval ticket routed to Security+Legal for retention extension. 7) Add admin console toggle and a flag in pod config.

Additional notes:

2026-03-14 - Legal (D. Nguyen): Need retention policy draft and escalation path for retention extension requests. Will review Confluence workflow mockup.

payload.description:
Issue summary: During a coordinated Vault KV bulk rotate (scheduled maintenance) several release pipelines stalled with long-running 'auth refresh' waits from the release agent sidecar proxy. Impact: multiple nightly and release pipelines (team-release/*) hung for 20-45 minutes, blocking 3 release windows and delaying Canary rollouts. Scope: ~12 runner pods across two node pools; only pods with the sidecar proxy enabled and with Vault rewrap enabled were impacted. Timeline: 2026-03-01 01:12 UTC - Vault rotate started; 01:19 UTC - first CI API timeout observed; 01:20-02:05 UTC - multiple builds stuck with no agent logs updating; 02:18 UTC - temporary mitigation applied (sidecar restart) and some jobs recovered. Expected behavior: sidecar should gracefully refresh tokens and retry with backoff without stalling the main agent or failing in-flight pipelines.
1) Trigger a Vault KV bulk rewrap/rotate in prod using the standard rotate job (performed at 01:12 UTC)
2) Ensure release-agent pods have sidecar proxy with VAULT_REWRAP=enabled and short-lived tokens (TTL ~5m)
3) Observe sidecar attempting auth refresh: sidecar logs show 401 -> rewrap -> transient decrypt failures -> blocking call to agent until restart
4) Confirm that restarting the sidecar unblocks the agent and job resumes without job-level retry logic kicking in
[release-agent-sidecar] 2026-03-01T01:18:57Z WARN auth: token refresh attempt failed: transit/decrypt: ciphertext not found
[release-agent-proxy] 2026-03-01T01:19:02Z ERROR backoff: refresh loop stuck waiting for 'key-unwrap' (attempt=7, sleeping=30s)
[agent] 2026-03-01T01:21:11Z INFO heartbeat: heartbeats stopped; last task_id=rel-20260301-378
[kubelet] 2026-03-01T02:05:14Z INFO pod/runner-xyz sidecar restarted by liveness-probe
Initial hypothesis: Vault rewrap affected transit keys causing sidecar decrypt to return 404/KeyNotFound for short-lived tokens
Observed: not all pods were impacted; pattern correlated with node pools that had recent OS patches (kubelet 1.28.2) and slightly delayed Vault agent rolling restart
Repro attempt in staging: reproduced by forcing rewrap + blocking KMS availability for 30s; sidecar entered a synchronous refresh path that blocked agent main thread
Found race: sidecar's auth refresh is implemented as a synchronous blocking call with exponential backoff up to 5m and no circuit-breaker; if transit decrypt returns 'ciphertext not found' repeatedly, it does not fallback to short-lived retry token generation path
Support (Aisha): Escalated to SRE at 01:40 UTC after multiple pipelines reported >10m stalls. Notified #release-ops and #sre on-call.
SRE (Diego): Confirmed sidecar logs show repeated transit/decrypt 404s coincident with Vault rotate window. Will try interleaved restarts to validate mitigation.
Eng (Priya Patel): Suggested a hotfix to change sidecar refresh to async with cancellable context so agent isn't blocked by decrypt loops. Will open PR for quick rollback and test in staging.
SRE (Diego): Applied temporary mitigation 02:12 UTC - rolling restart of affected sidecars; pipelines resumed. Collecting postmortem data and traces.
Mitigation applied: rolling restart of sidecar proxies unblocked agents and allowed pipelines to complete. Short-term code workaround merged (sidecar-proxy PR #122): switch auth refresh to asynchronous non-blocking path with bounded retry and fallback to token re-request endpoint. Follow-ups: 1) Release a patched sidecar-proxy image (v1.7.3) and orchestrate controlled rollout across all node pools; 2) Update secret-rotation runbook to include targetted sidecar rolling strategy and pre-check for KMS/transit availability; 3) Add health-check endpoint to detect 'stuck refresh' and trigger liveness restart earlier; 4) Postmortem to be authored and linked to incident record.
payload.summary: Release agent proxy token refresh fails during Vault bulk rotation causing CI jobs to hang

Issue summary: A consolidated invoice (Vendor: GlobalCloud Services) was uploaded to the AP pipeline on 2026-03-02. The PDF contains charge lines attributable to two Redwood legal entities (Redwood Inference, Inc. - US and Redwood Inference Ltd. - UK) but the supplier did not provide entity-level purchase order (PO) mapping or VAT breakdown. The invoice was flagged by tax-validation as 'ambiguous legal entity' and moved to a manual hold queue.

Impact: Payment for the invoice (approx. $142,300 USD / £84,600 GBP equivalent) is blocked for both legal entities. Vendor has emailed requesting confirmation of payment date. This affects month-end close for the UK entity and may induce late-payment fees. Finance needs a deterministic allocation before releases to avoid misposting to tax and GL accounts.

Background: Vendor regularly issues consolidated monthlies that include UK professional services (GBP) and US cloud credits (USD). Historically the vendor provided a split invoice, but this month they consolidated without indicating which line items belong to each registered entity. AP automation dropped the invoice into manual review due to missing VAT/GL attributes and mismatched supplier legal names on the header vs. line items.
1) Upload consolidated vendor PDF to AP intake (tested with staging AP connector)
2) AP OCR extracts header 'GlobalCloud Services' and line items but no explicit legal-entity tag
3) Tax validation rule 'entity-mapping-required-for-multi-currency' triggers and sets invoice.status = HOLD
4) Invoice routed to manual queue 'AP - Entity Allocation' and triggers notification to finance@redwood.com
AP pipeline log excerpt (2026-03-02T08:42:12Z): ERROR tax-validator:ENTITY_MAP_MISSING invoice_id=GC-2026-03-01-339 action=HOLD reason='multiple currencies, no entity allocation' user=ap-processor-2
AP OCR confidence: 0.78 for supplier name, VAT field empty. Payment scheduler prevented scheduling run 'weekly-payrun-03-05' for related vendor account. Email from vendor received 2026-03-03 14:10 (support@globalcloud.example) stating 'we consolidated per your request' but no split attached.
- Initial triage by AP (Mar 4): invoice contains 23 lines; 9 lines clearly GBP services, 14 lines appear to be USD cloud credits but no PO numbers for four GBP lines.
- Hypothesis 1: OCR omitted a small 'billing entity' footer on page 2; request a higher-quality original PDF from vendor (sent 2026-03-04).
- Hypothesis 2: Vendor intentionally consolidated invoices for efficiency but expects us to allocate by product code mapping; product codes don't map cleanly to legal entities in our GL.
- AP ran a heuristics allocation (based on currency and product code) that suggested 87% USD / 13% GBP allocation, but tax team rejected as insufficient evidence for VAT reporting.
- Tax requested supplier-signed allocation or invoice with entity-specific VAT numbers per UK HMRC guidance.
- Related past ticket INT-151234 indicates vendor has previously misunderstood our PO instructions; contact history attached.

Additional notes:
Pending: vendor to supply entity split with VAT numbers or separate invoices. Interim action: partial payment authorization approved up to 60% of USD-allocated amount to mitigate late fees; funds to be posted to tax-suspense GL 2109 and reversed when final allocation confirmed. Tax has documented required evidence in Confluence. Next steps: Vendor Ops to obtain signed allocation by 2026-03-16; AP to prepare manual payment once evidence is received.
1) Vendor Ops to escalate to GlobalCloud account manager for signed split invoice by 2026-03-16.
2) AP to prepare partial payment template and JV posting once vendor signs agreement.
3) Tax to confirm acceptable evidence format and update rule set to allow supplier-attested allocation for small consolidations.
4) Procurement to add updated PO instruction to future contracts to avoid consolidated ambiguous invoices.
payload.summary: Ambiguous legal-entity on consolidated vendor invoice causing tax allocation hold

Issue summary: Request to create a new Confluence space for 'Privileged Reviews' (security/privacy evidence and sign-offs) and an associated Slack channel gateway for approved external partners. The space should have a timebound auditor reviewer group, strict page-level permissions, and an automated daily snapshot retention that exports evidence to the legal vault. The Slack side should provision a read-only channel for partners via an approval workflow and a bot that enforces ephemeral membership (auto-removal after 30 days).

Impact: Several upcoming partner integrations require a secure, auditable collaboration surface where partners can view design docs and evidence without access to internal edit permissions. Current workaround is sharing documents manually which increases audit burden and risks stale permissions. This blocks partner onboarding timelines for two partner pilots starting next quarter.

Request details:
- Confluence: create space key PRVREV (title: Privileged Reviews).
  - Space permissions: only members of 'security-priv-reviewers' (timebound group), Legal-SLM, and space-admins can edit. Partner groups must be granted view-only on selected pages.
  - Create page templates: Evidence Checklist, Review Sign-off, Export Snapshot Job.
  - Configure automation: nightly snapshot that exports pages tagged "evidence" to a read-only export in the existing legal vault space; snapshots should include page history and attachments. Retention policy: retain 7 years.
- Jira: create a lightweight project or permission scheme mapping so reviewers can raise follow-up issues into INT project with minimal cross-perm friction.
- Slack: create a channel provisioning gateway that:
  - Creates a partner-specific channel e.g., #partner-acme-readonly (naming enforced).
  - Adds approved partner email domains via SCIM or invite flow, but members are added with a read-only role via the bot (no posting).
  - Enforce auto-removal of external members after 30 days unless renewed by the requester.
  - Audit logs forwarded to #security-audit and linked Confluence snapshots.

Desired automation/approval flow: Requesters fill a short form (Confluence page or Jira issue) that triggers an Ops bot to: validate requester, create space/page scaffolding, provision Slack channel, and kick off the nightly snapshot job. Admins should be able to revoke partner access centrally and see audit records.

Acceptance criteria:
- New Confluence space PRVREV exists with correct permission schema and templates.
- Nightly export automation is implemented and runs on staging for two nights with successful exports.
- Slack partner channel gateway can create a read-only partner channel and remove external members automatically after 30 days.
- Audit logs from both systems are visible in #security-audit and cross-linked on the Confluence snapshot pages.

Risks and considerations: must ensure export automation does not transmit PII outside approved vault. Coordinate with Security and Legal before enabling snapshots for real partner data. SCIM invites require approval from Identity team.

Additional notes:
Initial review: Confluence space skeleton can be created by site-admins; export automation likely built using existing Atlassian automation + AWS Lambda to move snapshots into the Legal Evidence Vault S3 with IAM role. Slack gateway can reuse the partner-channel bot (needs enhancement for read-only enforcement and 30-day TTL). Identity team needs to enable SCIM provisioning for partner domains; otherwise we will rely on bot-invites. Potential blockers: SCIM approval timeline, Legal sign-off on retention export destination.

Issue summary:
We need a self-service, auditable gateway that provisions a bundled project surface for new cross-pod initiatives: creates a Slack channel (with tiered permission roles), a Confluence runbook space pre-populated from a template, and a Jira service/project skeleton. The gateway should require an approval step (pod lead + security reviewer) and emit audit logs to our central logging pipeline.

Impact:
Currently onboarding is manual: pod leads request a channel, infra manually grants roles, and runbooks are copied ad-hoc. This causes delays (2-5 business days), inconsistent runbook content, missing audit trails, and occasional over-permissive Slack access which has compliance risks for some pods.

Request / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement an automated provisioning gateway accessible from an internal UI/Slack slash command that:
  - Creates a Slack channel with three predefined roles: owners (full), contributors (message/post), observers (read-only via restricted channel).
  - Instantiates a Confluence space from an approved runbook template with placeholders populated (pod name, owners, lifecycle dates).
  - Optionally creates a Jira service project skeleton with default issue types and labels.
  - Includes a two-step approval workflow: pod lead (auto-approve for designated pods) + security reviewer for pods marked as "sensitive".
  - Emits structured audit events to our Log Pipeline (ELK/Kafka) and writes an entry to an internal provisioning audit Confluence page.
- All created artifacts should include a TTL and automatic archival workflow (e.g., 6 months inactive -> auto-archive notification -> archive).
- RBAC rules should be translated into existing IAM groups and mapped to Slack SSO groups; no ad-hoc member invites.
- Provide an operator runbook and rollback steps; unit/integration tests for the automation.

Background / constraints:
- Security requires that any channel with >50 external collaborators or with the label "sensitive" must trigger a security review.
- Slack API rate limits mean we should batch channel creation calls and handle 429 backoffs gracefully.
- Confluence templating must preserve page-level metadata for future programmatic updates.

Proposed technical approach:
- Implement a GitHub Actions-backed provisioning service that validates requests, kicks off an approval workflow (OpsApprovalBot via Slack), and calls a Terraform module for Jira/Confluence provisioning plus a small service (internal-tools/provisioner) that uses the Slack SCIM API for group-sync and channel creation.
- Store templated metadata in a managed S3 bucket and render with safe placeholders.
- Emit events to Kafka topic provisioning-events and wire into existing audit dashboards.

Risks and guardrails:
- Ensure we do not bypass existing enterprise SSO/SCIM flows; all operations must run under a service account with scoped permissions.
- Rollback plan in case of partially provisioned resources (e.g., Slack created but Confluence failed) must remove the Slack channel and submit a cleanup ticket automatically.

Requested timeline:
- Proof-of-concept within 3 weeks, pilot with two pods in 6 weeks, full rollout Q2.

Attachments:
- Example template: Confluence Runbook v2 (linked in related_confluence_pages)
- Slack UX mockups attached in Slack thread #internal-tools-onboarding

Additional notes:
2026-02-14 - Security (Amira Sol): We'll need an automated checklist run during approval to flag any pod labeled 'regulated' and require an additional legal approval. Also request PII scanning for Confluence templates.
Checked existing channel provisioning flows: we have ad-hoc scripts in internal-tools that create channels but they don't manage TTL or Confluence templating.
Found prior attempt in INT-623214 to batch-create channels; aborted due to 429 handling issues. Reuse rate-limit logic from infra/batch-worker#132.
Confluence API preserves page metadata but current template store is spread across team spaces; consolidate to a single managed template bucket.
Identified required Terraform modules: jira-project, confluence-space. Need to add idempotent semantics (create-if-not-exists) to prevent duplication on retry.
2026-03-12 - Implementation summary: Provisioning gateway implemented as GH Action + provisioner service. Slack channel creation uses SCIM group-sync + Conversations.create, with exponential backoff for 429s. Confluence spaces are created from the managed template S3 bucket and populated with runbook placeholders.
Created operator runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Provisioning+Gateway+Runbook
Rollout: Piloted with 'data-platform' and 'evals' pods. No permission regressions observed. TTL/archival notifications sent at 5 months inactivity.
Follow-ups: (1) Automate legal approval hook for 'regulated' pods (INT-951002). (2) Add automated PII scan for new runbook pages (security ticket raised).
payload.summary: Automated onboarding gateway for cross-pod Slack channels + templated Confluence runbook deployment

Issue summary: Multiple engineers report that after the latest imaging/provisioning cycle, machines connected to corporate Thunderbolt docks fail to restore external displays and USB input devices after suspend/resume. Impact: productivity loss for docked users; machine appears functional but external monitors remain black and external keyboard/mouse unresponsive until dock power-cycle or full reboot. Scope: observed on ~6 users in SRE and Platform teams; reproducible on two model types in lab.
1) Provision a machine with the current corporate image (ubuntu-22.04 + endpoint-agent v1.8.0).
2) Connect to company-issued Thunderbolt 4 dock (Anker/CalDigit tested). Attach 2 external monitors (DP/HDMI) and USB keyboard + mouse via dock hub.
3) Confirm displays active and input devices responsive. Lock screen and suspend (sudo systemctl suspend) or close lid to trigger suspend.
4) Wake machine. Observe that internal display resumes but external displays remain black and USB input devices are unresponsive. Dock may show power/activity but no video enumerated.
5) Workaround: unplug and replug dock power or reboot the laptop; displays and keyboard/mouse return after cycle.
After resume, internal laptop display turns on but external monitors stay blank; xrandr shows connectors disconnected. lsusb does not list hub devices until dock power-cycle. dmesg contains thunderbolt and drm errors.
External displays and USB devices should re-enumerate on resume without requiring a reboot or dock power-cycle.
Mar 10 09:22:11 laptop kernel: thunderbolt 0000:00:14.0: hostbridge: resume failed, error -12
Mar 10 09:22:12 laptop kernel: drm: connector DP-1: lost link, disabling
Mar 10 09:22:13 laptop kernel: usb 1-4: device not accepting address 5, error -71
Mar 10 09:22:14 laptop systemd: Endpoint agent v1.8.0 started: /opt/redwood/endpoint-agent --daemon
- Reproduced in lab on Dell XPS 15 and ThinkPad X1 with corporate image 2026-03-09 build.
- Not present on older image (2026-02-24) that uses endpoint-agent v1.6.2 and kernel 5.19 -> suggests regression introduced between imaging builds or bundled kernel modules/firmware.
- Kernel version on failing image: 6.2.14-rt. Working image: 5.19.8. Suspect kernel/thunderbolt driver interaction or fw update on dock.
- Endpoint-agent binds to USB power-management rules; verified systemd sleep hooks run but no explicit module reload on resume.
- Quick test: running 'sudo modprobe -r thunderbolt && sudo modprobe thunderbolt' after resume re-enumerates devices without reboot.
- Searched upstream kernel changelogs: several thunderbolt/resume fixes in 6.x series; also known regressions with certain firmware versions on CalDigit TB4 docks.
- Checked corporate Dock firmware: some units running v1.02, others v1.04. v1.04 has reported fixes for Windows only; Linux behavior unclear.
Power-cycle dock or run 'sudo modprobe -r thunderbolt && sudo modprobe thunderbolt' after resume. As short-term fix, advise affected users to avoid suspend when docked or close lid with external display as internal-only session.
1) Coordinate with SRE to capture serial console + persistent journal on next occurrence and attach full dmesg output.
2) Spin up image with kernel 5.19 (previous working baseline) to confirm regression window and create controlled A/B test.
3) Test latest mainline kernel (6.5 rc) in lab to see if resume regression already fixed upstream.
4) File upstream bug with kernel thundebolt maintainers if reproduction steps confirmed; include dmesg and usb/dp logs.
5) Evaluate rolling back kernel in next imaging build or adding resume-trigger module reload hook in endpoint-agent as a mitigation (requires QA and release plan).
6) Communicate temporary mitigation and instructions to affected teams and update Confluence runbook.
Maya Chen (Reporter) 2026-03-10: First reported by SRE on 3/9 after reimage. Affected users: sally@redwood.com, jason@redwood.com; both used CalDigit TS4 docks.
Diego Alvarez (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in lab. Added logs. Hypothesis: kernel 6.2 regression or dock FW mismatch. Will validate A/B imaging tomorrow.
SRE-Team 2026-03-11: Captured full journal for one occurrence (attached link in Confluence). Observed repeated 'device not accepting address' USB errors post-resume.
Maya Chen 2026-03-11: Noted one user had success after manually toggling thunderbolt permissions in BIOS (setting security level from 'User' to 'No Security') — could be related to enumeration timing.
Diego Alvarez 2026-03-12: Proposed interim endpoint-agent change: add systemd-suspend post hook to reload thunderbolt and usbcore modules. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/endpoint-agent/pull/412. Will run QA on a small dogfood cohort if approved.
Diego Alvarez 2026-03-12: Todos: confirm dock FW versions across affected fleet and coordinate with Procurement for firmware update path if necessary.
Work in progress: mitigation PR open to reload thunderbolt module on resume; A/B validation against previous imaging baseline scheduled. No permanent fix deployed yet.
payload.summary: Thunderbolt dock: external displays and keyboard not restored after suspend/resume on provisioned Ubuntu workstations

Issue summary: Customer DocuFlow AI reports repeated 504 Gateway Timeouts and stalled finalization when sending requests with ~120k token prefix and max_tokens=40k. The generation starts (initial tokens stream), throughput slows dramatically after ~30s, and the finalization step frequently times out at the load-balancer with 504. Impact: Production workflows for document summarization pause and go into retry loops causing downstream backpressure and duplicate billing events reported by the customer. Environment: Dedicated cluster (cust-dedicated-03), pinned model redwood-v1-large, autoscaling enabled but observed not to react during incidents. Occurred intermittently starting 2026-03-09 18:40 UTC and reproducible with provided prompt.
1) Use customer API key for cust-dedicated-03 in us-east.
2) POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-v1-large, max_tokens=40000, temperature=0.0.
3) Provide a ~120k-token prefix (customer supplied anonymized excerpt) and enable streaming=true.
4) Observe initial tokens arrive for ~20-30s, then streaming stalls; final chunk never arrives and client receives 504 from LB after ~90s.
5) Reducing max_tokens to 5k or truncating prefix to <20k tokens removes the timeout and finishes normally.
edge-lb (prod-us-east) 2026-03-09T18:42:01Z: upstream timed out (110) while reading response header from upstream, client: 198.51.100.23
api-gateway 2026-03-09T18:42:00Z: request id=bb3e7f, route=/v1/generate, model=redwood-v1-large, total_tokens=160000
serving-runtime (node-gpu-07) 2026-03-09T18:42:22Z: WARN slow-step: kv-cache-evict loop detected, evicted 3 blocks in 4s
scheduler 2026-03-09T18:42:25Z: INFO batch formed: size=6, window_ms=200, payload_tokens=1.2e6
gpu-metrics node-gpu-07 2026-03-09T18:42:40Z: memory fragmentation high, free_gpu_mem=1.1GB, oom_recoveries=2
Initial hypothesis: KV cache eviction thrash with very large prefix causing repeated recomputation and slow finalization.
Observed scheduler batching windows spike when per-request token budgets are extremely high; current batcher groups many oversized requests causing serialization and extended tail latency.
Autoscaler did not add nodes because node memory usage did not cross the simple threshold due to fragmentation; new instances would still not accept the fragmented memory allocations quickly enough.
Edge LB 504s appear to be after the runtime stalls in finalizer step rather than immediate OOM; logs show repeated small evictions then long compute on repeatedly rebuilt KV state.
Reproduced in staging by sending synthetic 100k token prefix and max_tokens 30k: same pattern of initial throughput then stall and 504 from LB at default timeout.
Related slack thread: #support (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C07SUPP123/p1678478400000)
Related dashboards: request-latency / prod-us-east / cust-dedicated-03 (link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123)
Captured heap/profile from runtime: large number of small KV allocations; GC-like pauses observed in runtime logs during finalization step (link to tar: s3://redwood-logs/sup-473201/runtime-profiles.tar.gz)
Confirmed that using a quantized model variant reduced memory pressure but did not eliminate the finalization stall when max_tokens remained very large.
Potential root cause: combination of unbounded per-request token budgets + scheduler batch policy + KV cache eviction strategy + GPU memory fragmentation.

Additional notes:
Daniel Park (SRE) (2026-03-10): Started reproducing in staging; observed identical scheduler batch spikes and kv eviction logs. Captured runtime profile and heap. Assigned investigation.
Lina Zhao (Serving Runtime) (2026-03-11): Confirmed runtime pauses correlate with repeated KV rebuilds. Submitted short-term patch to avoid full rebuild on eviction (PR: #rwd/serving-runtime@f2d4c1).
SRE (2026-03-11): Deployed patch to staging; staging requests with max_tokens=30k now finish but still high tail latency at scale. Need change to batcher policy and LB timeout tuning for dedicated customers.
Customer (DocuFlow AI) (2026-03-11): Applying suggested temporary mitigations (truncate prefixes to <=40k tokens, lower max_tokens). Reported immediate improvement but would like platform fix.
Support lead (2026-03-12): Opening follow-up task to audit autoscaler memory fragmentation heuristics and to add guidance to doc/limits for dedicated customers.
Workaround applied: recommended customer to trim prefix and reduce max_tokens to <=5k for immediate relief; enabled prefix chunking suggestion in their account settings. Short-term fix deployed to staging (runtime patch to avoid full KV rebuild on eviction). Next steps: modify scheduler to cap per-request batching window for oversized token budgets and tune autoscaler to consider fragmentation metrics. Plan rollout: patch to staging validated, rolling to prod for dedicated clusters in us-east starting 2026-03-13 with Canary traffic. Postmortem to follow.
payload.summary: Throttled finalization and 504s when requesting very large output budgets with deep prompt prefix

Issue summary: Request to build a managed deprecation workflow for Slack channels used across the org. Goal is to standardize how channels are flagged for deletion/archival, ensure owners are notified, create a Jira task for audit and approval, and automatically update the canonical Confluence channel index when archival completes.

Impact: Currently channel archival is ad-hoc and manual which leads to stale channels, missing owners, and noisy notifications. This workflow will reduce clutter, surface ownership gaps, and produce an auditable trail.

Request: 1) Add a Slack-native way (slash command and channel topic tag) for channel owners to mark channels for deprecation with a configurable TTL (14/30/90 days). 2) When a channel is marked, create a templated Jira task in project internal-support assigned to the channel owner with metadata (channel id, workspace, last active, member count). 3) Send an automated Slack modal to the channel owner that lists actions and requires confirmation; if owner unresponsive for a configured window, escalate to team admin. 4) After archival completes, update the Confluence channel index page to reflect status and attach the Jira ticket link and runbook snapshot. 5) Provide a dry-run mode and an audits-only mode for the first 60 days.

Acceptance criteria: - Slash command /deprecate-channel <ttl> creates a Jira issue with correct metadata and posts a confirmation message in the channel. - Owners receive modal and can confirm/extend/transfer ownership. - Unconfirmed deprecation escalates to the configured admin after X days. - Confluence index page is updated by automation after archival with ticket link. - Audit logs in the automation service show webhook events, Jira creation, and Confluence update.

Desired timeline: design + runbook 2 weeks, implementation + testing 3 weeks, pilot in #internal-tooling for 30 days, rollout org-wide after pilot.
1) As a channel owner, run /deprecate-channel 30 in a test channel.
2) Expect immediate ephemeral confirmation message and Jira ticket created.
3) Open Jira ticket to verify template fields populated: channel_name, channel_id, owner, last_message_ts, member_count, suggested_archive_date.
4) Do not interact with modal; after escalation window verify admin gets notification.
5) When archival completed by bot, verify Confluence index row for channel shows status 'archived' and includes Jira ticket link.
Preliminary notes: We already have bots that can create Jira tickets (see INT-645210) and a Confluence API integration. Major gaps: ownership resolution logic (Slack profile vs. team-admin mapping), escalation policy, and secure service account scope to write to Confluence. Need to validate rate limits for bulk updates to Confluence index and ensure the Jira project has a template scheme for these deprecation issues.
Potential approaches: leverage existing slack-app (channel-management-bot) and extend with a new endpoint that uses conn-service account with limited scopes; store TTL state in infra-config (DynamoDB) and schedule periodic reconciliation via GitHub Actions/runner or internal scheduler service.
Open questions: 1) Who is 'team admin' mapping source? 2) What is the escalation window default? 3) Are there legal retention exceptions for certain channels (legal/privacy)?

Additional notes:
Dry-run mode: automation should log actions without mutating Jira/Confluence. Test steps: 1) enable dry-run via /deprecate-channel --dry-run. 2) Verify log entry includes payload sample and intended Jira payload. 3) Flatten to live mode and run on test channel. Edge-cases: channels without owners, private channels (needs explicit invite), channels with integrations (do not archive if active integrations unless owner confirms).
When a channel is marked for deprecation: 1) Bot captures channel metadata and creates INT-ticket auto-draft. 2) Send interactive modal to owner. 3) If confirmed-> schedule archival job at TTL expiry. 4) On archival-> post message to channel and update Confluence index row with link to ticket and archive timestamp. 5) If owner not found or flagged as 'legal-retain', mark ticket as 'needs manual review' and do not proceed.
API footprints required: Slack chat:write, views.open, channels:read (or conversations:read), conversations:write for archiving; Jira: createIssue; Confluence: updateContent. Service account must be scoped to only the internal-support Jira project and the Confluence space used for the index. Include idempotency keys when creating Jira tickets to avoid duplicates. Add feature flag and pilot whitelist for #internal-tooling and #platform-oncall.
Create Jira issue template schema and sample payload (Devon)
Request bot service account from infra with limited scopes (Devon)
Add compliance toggle for retention-exempt channels (Priya)
Prepare pilot communication and runbook for owners (Maya)
payload.summary: Design and provision Slack channel deprecation workflow with automated Jira ticket creation and Confluence index update

Issue summary: Data Platform needs a standardized onboarding workspace for new DataOps teams that includes a Jira project, Confluence space with templates, and Slack workflows to automate invites and checklist creation.
Impact: New teams onboarding are currently using ad-hoc spaces which causes duplicated effort, missing security controls, and inconsistent runbooks. This slows onboarding and increases risk for sensitive dataset access.
Request details:
- Create Jira project key DATOPS-ONB (company naming guidelines) with permission scheme scoped to Data Platform, Security, and Team leads. Roles: Admin, Developer, Viewer. Constrain Create/Transition of 'Access' issues to Admins only.
- Provision SSO group mappings in Jira: okta:group_dataops_engineers -> Developer, okta:group_dataops_leads -> Admin, okta:group_dataops_view -> Viewer.
- Create Confluence space 'DataOps Onboarding' with the attached skeleton pages: Welcome, Access Checklist, Runbooks, Compliance Evidence. Apply space permissions mirrored to Jira roles.
- Slack: create two channels #dataops-onboarding (private) and #dataops-guides (public read-only). Add a Slack Workflow (via Workflow Builder) that: 1) triggers on ticket creation in the Jira DATOPS-ONB project, 2) creates a private channel for the new team, 3) posts an onboarding checklist linking to Confluence pages, and 4) invites the SSO group okta:group_dataops_engineers.
- Jira automation rules: on issue created (template type = 'onboarding'): create sub-tasks from checklist template, add watchers: data-platform-oncall, assign to DataOps pod lead, and post a message to #dataops-onboarding with issue link.
- Webhooks: add a read-only webhook to GitHub org repo 'infrastructure/onboarding' for status updates.
Deadline: requested by 2026-03-20 to align with the next cohort.
Business justification: reduces time-to-first-delivery for teams by ~40%, enforces least-privilege, and centralizes audit trails.
Attachments: reference Confluence template draft (see related_confluence_pages).

Confirmed no existing DATOPS- prefix used in Jira (searched global projects).
Validated SSO group names with IAM; awaiting group IDs for automation invite API.
Checked Slack workspace app scope - existing Workflow Builder app has permission to create channels and invite users; will require owner approval for sending invites to SSO groups via SCIM.
Reviewed 'onboarding' issue type templates in Jira Cloud and will base sub-task checklist on existing 'team-setup' template.

Additional notes:
Pending - initial staging configs to be rolled out for validation. Automation owner: automation-team. Plan: complete staging by 2026-03-14, request sign-off, then production rollout.

Issue summary: External privacy assessment firm (PrivAudit LLC) has requested a scoped sample of production ingestion logs to verify PII minimization and retention profiles. Request includes a 48-hour contiguous segment of API gateway access logs plus associated audit metadata (no raw inference outputs).

Impact: Minimal service impact expected. High compliance risk if access is not authorized correctly or if sensitive customer data is exposed. Customer-facing incidents could result if accidental raw inference output is included.

Request details:
- Requestor: PrivAudit LLC (contract attached to Security ticket SEC-2026-037)
- Data requested: API gateway access logs and associated audit fields (timestamps, request IDs, route, headers summary hash, auth subject) for window 2026-02-10T00:00:00Z to 2026-02-11T00:00:00Z. Explicitly exclude request/response bodies and any unredacted inference outputs.
- Purpose: external verification of anonymization and retention workflows.
- Duration: Access window 72 hours from token issuance. Token must expire automatically and access must be read-only.
- Delivery mechanism proposed: timeboxed S3 presigned URL to a restricted bucket prefix with SSE-KMS encryption using dedicated audit KMS key and enforced ACLs.

Security/controls required:
- Minimization: supply only NDJSON lines with hashed header values (salted HMAC provided by Security) and removed bodies.
- Access control: temporary IAM role scoped to s3:GetObject for the specific prefixed objects; MFA not required for external auditor but access must require a signed presigned URL generated by Security on behalf of Compliance.
- Audit trail: all actions must be recorded in CloudTrail and our internal access-log index; create a monitoring alert for any list/bucket ACL changes.
- Redaction verification: Security to validate redaction script output prior to handing to external party.

Steps for reviewers:
1) Legal/Compliance: confirm contractual permission for third-party access and any DPA amendment needed.
2) Security: review redaction script, generate HMAC salt, approve KMS key usage and presigned URL approach.
3) SRE/Infra: prepare export job to produce NDJSON lines to s3://redwood-prod-audits/tmp/INT-90812/ and create IAM role + presigned URL.
4) Requestor: run validation checklist and confirm no bodies included.

Logs & evidence: Proposed export path will be s3://redwood-prod-audits/tmp/INT-90812/segment-20260210.ndjson.gz (GZIP, line-delimited). Manifest and SHA256 checksum will be provided.

Acceptance criteria:
- No unredacted inference outputs are present in objects.
- Access granted only for the specified path and time window.
- KMS and CloudTrail confirmed for the action.

Additional notes: This is a one-off, timeboxed external audit. Follow-up will include a purge confirmation and a short runbook update to document the steps used.

Additional notes:
2026-02-22 - Legal (Monica Ruiz): Confirmed contract permits this specific scope. Please ensure we have the signed SOC addendum on file. Legal requests redaction verification report prior to external delivery.
SRE checked existing retention hooks. Ingestion logs are sharded by day and can be filtered by request_time. Identified ~1.1M lines for the 24h window; expected compressed export size ~180MB gzip. Verified pipeline will exclude bodies by using the 'headers-only' export flag and applying the redaction script as a post-filter. Security will provide HMAC salt and the redaction checklist. No dependency on model-serving traces required.
Approved on 2026-02-23 after Security and Legal sign-off. Actions taken: 1) Security created KMS alias/redwood/audit-int-90812 and uploaded HMAC salt to Secrets Manager (rotation note: ephemeral salt for this audit only). 2) SRE generated NDJSON line file at s3://redwood-prod-audits/tmp/INT-90812/segment-20260210.ndjson.gz and provided SHA256 manifest. 3) IAM role 'audit-access-int-90812' created with s3:GetObject limited to the prefix. 4) Security generated a presigned URL valid 72 hours; delivered to PrivAudit via Compliance. 5) CloudTrail export entry created and cross-linked to this ticket.
Follow-ups: create INT-90813 to purge the S3 objects and retire the IAM role after access window closes; Compliance to obtain written confirmation of file destruction from PrivAudit and upload to Confluence.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A supplier invoice submitted through the vendor portal (Solstice Labs Ltd, INV-2026-0098) has a net_amount of 0.00 because it's a credit/adjustment that only carries a withholding tax amount. The payrun engine excluded the invoice from payment because of a zero net_amount rule. As a result, the supplier's credit memo was not netted or paid out and the month-end AP aging and reconciliation are incorrect.

Impact:
- Supplier Solstice Labs is showing unpaid balance and has open dispute with Finance.
- March month-end AP aging will not match supplier statements until this is resolved.
- Potential tax reporting issues if withholding amounts are not accounted for in the GL.

Environment:
- Production AP pipeline, vendor portal (ap.redwood.internal), payrun batch PB-20260310-77, GL instance accounting-ledger-prod.
- Invoice metadata: vendor_id SL-0043, invoice INV-2026-0098, vendor_currency USD, gross_withholding_amount 120.00, net_amount 0.00, tax_code WHT-30.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Upload a vendor credit/adjustment invoice in vendor portal with zero net (line adjustments = -120.00, withholding 120.00, net = 0.00).
2) Submit to AP queue and allow automatic invoice validation to complete.
3) Trigger scheduled payrun (PB-20260310-77) or run payrun validation step.
4) Observe payrun excludes invoice due to net_amount == 0 rule.

Observed behavior / Logs:

Issue summary:
Users who recently underwent Okta account merge (duplicate identities merged into single canonical account) are unable to complete self-service temporary elevation flows. The approval UI completes but the backend returns a 403 during the token exchange step. Impact: oncall and SRE asking for rapid manual elevation; several engineers blocked from emergency runbooks.

Impact:
- ~8 engineers across infra and platform teams were unable to obtain temporary elevated roles (SSH bastion, runbook edit).
- Self-service path fails; manual SRE intervention required to grant ephemeral role.
- Repro window: 2026-03-10 09:12 - 2026-03-10 12:40 UTC.

Environment:
- prod (us-east), approval-service v1.2.1, auth-proxy v2.0.0, Okta tenant redwood-prod.

Observed behavior:
- Approval UI shows success but the POST /api/v1/approve/exchange returns 403 with body: "approval_token invalid: subject_mismatch".
- Okta SAML/ID token appears valid for the session; however the approval token subject (NameID) differs from the current session subject after account merge.

Expected behavior:
- Temporary elevation should succeed if the user is now a canonical merged account that retains entitlement mappings. Approval exchange should accept subject aliasing from the account-merge path or reject upfront with clear remediation steps.
1) Have an Okta test subject 'alice+old@redwood.com' merged into 'alice@redwood.com' via SCIM/Okta account-merge flow.
2) Login to console via SSO (user sees session for 'alice@redwood.com').
3) Trigger self-service temporary elevation in Console -> Access Requests -> Request Elevation.
4) Complete approver flow; UI displays approval success and returns approval_token to client.
5) Client posts approval_token to /api/v1/approve/exchange and receives 403 with 'subject_mismatch' error.
6) Repeatable when approval token subject differs from current Okta NameID after account merge.
2026-03-10T09:13:21Z approval-service ERROR token-exchange: approval_token=abcDEF123 invalid: subject_mismatch (expected: okta|alice@redwood.com, got: okta|alice+old@redwood.com)
2026-03-10T09:13:22Z auth-proxy INFO session-validate: okta-subject=okta|alice@redwood.com session_id=sess-9f3a
2026-03-10T09:13:22Z console WARN elevation-client: received 403 from approval-service, showing generic failure to user
2026-03-10T10:02:04Z okta-webhook INFO scim-account-merge: merged oktaId=00u111 -> 00u999; preserved_old_names=['alice+old@redwood.com']
Initial hypothesis: approval-service rejects approval_token when NameID in token does not match current SSO NameID; account-merge workflow does not surface alias mapping to approval service.
Checked Okta merge logs (via /events) and found merge completed at 2026-03-10T09:12:58Z; SCIM propagation finished ~5s later.
Confirmed approval-token generation included pre-merge subject (alice+old@redwood.com) when user started flow in a session that straddled the merge timing.
Reproduced locally by simulating merge: generate approval_token for old-subject, then update session to canonical subject and attempt token exchange -> identical 403 subject_mismatch.
Auth team verified session cookies are anchored to current NameID; approval tokens contain a subject claim tied to the original SSO assertion used to request approval.
Risk: users who initiate approval flows during account-merge windows get orphaned tokens; rare but high-friction for oncall.
Sofia Martinez [2026-03-10T09:25Z]: Raised by PagerDuty alert from infra-oncall. Several folks filed manual elevation requests in #oncall. Blocking emergency runbook execution.
Evan Patel [2026-03-10T09:40Z]: Reproduced in staging by performing Okta account-merge. Confirmed subject mismatch on token exchange. Will own fix; creating a short plan.
Lina Zhou (Auth) [2026-03-10T10:15Z]: Okta can preserve aliases in SCIM metadata; authorization checks currently compare strict NameID. Suggest adding alias mapping layer in approval-service as quick mitigation.
Ben Carver (SRE) [2026-03-10T10:45Z]: Temporary workaround: SRE can issue manual elevated SSO session via admin console (bypass token-exchange) while fix is implemented. Documented steps in runbook and informed #oncall.
Evan Patel [2026-03-11T02:10Z]: Implemented hotfix branch that accepts approved alias mapping header produced by auth-proxy. Running canary in us-east-prod (5% traffic).
Sofia Martinez [2026-03-12T07:32Z]: Hotfix verified: affected users reported successful elevation post-rollout. Closing incident and adding follow-up tasks.
Hotfix released in approval-service v1.2.2 -> v1.2.3: service will accept approved alias mappings surfaced by auth-proxy for a short window during account-merge events, and logs token subject alias occurrences for monitoring. Deployed as canary (5%) then 100% in prod us-east on 2026-03-11 23:45 UTC. Runbook updated with full manual-elevation workaround and detection alert for duplicate-nameid events. Follow-ups: add telemetry to Okta merge webhook consumer and create a daily alert for subject-alias occurrences. Incident closed after confirmation from affected users.
payload.summary: Approval token reuse after Okta account-merge prevents temporary elevation for affected users

Issue summary:
During a scheduled KMS key rolling update on 2026-03-08, a subset of short-lived CI tokens used by self-hosted runners were rejected shortly after issuance. This caused intermittent job failures across multiple release pipelines (no global outage but high error rate for ~40 minutes).

Impact:
- ~18% of scheduled CI jobs in prod-us-east failed with 401/403 during the window.
- Several long-running release jobs were retried and timed out, delaying two releases by ~2 hours.
- No secrets were exposed; failures were authentication rejections.

Timeline (key events):
- 2026-03-08 02:05 UTC: KMS rotation started in us-east.
- 2026-03-08 02:12 UTC: First CI job failures observed (401 from auth-service).
- 2026-03-08 02:20 UTC: Pager alert to #support and on-call SRE.
- 2026-03-08 02:30 UTC: Investigation identified token verification failures against rotated key.
- 2026-03-08 02:54 UTC: Quick mitigation applied (auth-service hotfix to accept previous signing key for 15m).
- 2026-03-08 03:00 UTC: Runner restart/workaround rolled out and job success rate returned to baseline.

Environment:
- prod cluster: us-east-1
- Affected CI runner pool: r2-large (self-hosted fleet)
- Auth stack: auth-service v1.14.2, token provider service v0.9.7
- KMS: AWS-KMS key alias: alias/redwood-ci-keys (rotation schedule)

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1. Issue an OIDC short-lived token from token-provider immediately after KMS key rotation event.
2. Attempt job registration/heartbeat from a runner using the new token.
3. Observe token verification rejection in auth-service logs referencing missing signature key id.

Observed behavior:
- auth-service logs: "token verification failed: unknown key id: k-20260308-1"
- client (runner) logs: repeated registration attempts, then transient 401s, then eventual reconnect after token refresh or restart.

Expected behavior:
- Tokens issued shortly before or during KMS rotation should validate against either the active key or the previous key for a short grace window, avoiding mass evictions.

Relevant logs and dashboards:
- grafana: ci-runner/error-rate (spike 02:12-02:55 UTC)
- kibana: auth-service logs filter: "token verification failed"
- slack thread: #support (link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234567/p1678387200000)

Maya Patel (Reporter) - 2026-03-08 02:25 UTC: Noticed increase in 401s hitting multiple release pipelines. Creating incident. Attaching first log snippets.
Ethan Cole (Assignee/SRE) - 2026-03-08 02:33 UTC: Correlated with KMS rotation event from infra calendar. Pulling auth-service logs now.
Lena Ortiz (SRE) - 2026-03-08 02:38 UTC: auth-service shows rejection due to unknown key id. Token provider appears to issue tokens referencing the new key id immediately after rotation.
Arjun Mehta (Auth Eng) - 2026-03-08 02:45 UTC: Confirmed token signature verification only uses current key set; previous key shadowing not applied. Preparing emergency patch to accept previous key for short window.
Priya Singh (Release Eng) - 2026-03-08 02:56 UTC: Restarted a sample set of runners in r2-large pool; jobs resumed successfully. Will coordinate larger restart after hotfix is deployed.
Ethan Cole - 2026-03-08 03:05 UTC: Hotfix deployed to auth-service (PR #4823). Monitoring for recurrence. Filing postmortem and runbook updates.
Maya Patel - 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Added proposed postmortem notes and next steps. Assigned follow-ups to release engineering and infra.
Arjun Mehta - 2026-03-11 14:20 UTC: Follow-up PR to token-provider to pre-warm key cache and delay new-token issuance by 60s during rotation: PR #4990
Hypothesis: token-provider begins issuing tokens signed with the new KMS key immediately after rotation; auth-service does not accept previous key signatures because keyset cache was not updated/retained.
Key evidence: auth-service rejects list includes key id k-20260308-1; token-provider logs show tokens referencing k-20260308-1 issued at 02:11 UTC while auth-service keyset still referenced k-20260307-2.
Reproducer confirmed on staging by simulating KMS rotation and querying token issuance + verification sequence.
Scope: affects self-hosted runner pools that rely on short-lived tokens (TTL 10m). Hosted API tokens unaffected.
Risk analysis: high for in-flight CI pipelines during rotation windows; low risk to security (no key material exfiltration detected).
Applied hotfix to auth-service to accept tokens signed by previous key for a configurable grace window (default 15 minutes). Deployed 2026-03-08 02:54 UTC.
Restarted r2-large runner fleet in phases to allow token re-registration; this drained the backlog without causing new rollout collisions.
Updated KMS rotation runbook: require 'ci-token-safe' precheck and pre-warm token-provider key cache before initiating rotation. Document added: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/12345/KMS+rotation+runbook
Implemented follow-ups: token-provider change to delay issuance of tokens signed by the new key for 60s and to pre-fetch previous key material; added monitoring alert on token verification error rate > 1% in 5m.
Post-incident tasks: (1) change default short-lived token TTL from 10m -> 15m to reduce churn during rotations; (2) add runbook step to coordinate runner restarts when rotation is unavoidable; (3) schedule an internal dry-run of KMS rotation next month.
Status: all immediate mitigation applied and validated. Postmortem to be published; follow-ups assigned to infra and release-eng for Q2 sprint.
payload.summary: Short-lived CI tokens evicted leading to intermittent runner job failures during KMS key rolling update

payload.description:
Multiple engineers reported that the internal CLI key-broker process hangs during SSO login. The broker initiates Okta OIDC flow, receives redirect with session cookie, then stalls waiting for token exchange. Issue started after edge-proxy upgrade (cookie header trimming) and affects teams using the CLI for runbook and deployment actions.
1) Use latest internal CLI (v2.14.0) on macOS or Linux
2) Run `redwood-keybroker login --sso`
3) CLI opens browser for Okta SSO, authenticate with corporate SSO
4) Okta redirects back to localhost callback; edge-proxy forwards request to key-broker service
5) Key-broker stalls at "`/auth/callback`" waiting for cookie/token exchange; no tokens returned
Login window opens but CLI spinner continues indefinitely
No service account token is returned to CLI
Browser shows successful redirect to localhost callback with 200 from key-broker
Key-broker logs show cookie header length mismatch and then no token exchange attempt
Key-broker completes OIDC code exchange and returns short-lived service token to CLI
CLI prints 'Login successful' and persists local credential
2026-03-10T15:04:12Z key-broker auth:recv callback request id=3f2a7 - Cookie header length=8192
2026-03-10T15:04:12Z edge-proxy http:trim_cookie - original Cookie header truncated to 4096 bytes by set-cookie-sanitizer
2026-03-10T15:04:12Z key-broker auth:error - missing 'session' claim in cookie, aborting exchange id=3f2a7
2026-03-10T15:04:13Z cli keybroker:spinner - waiting for token (pid=11342)
Initial report from infra team coincided with edge-proxy 2.8.1 rollout that enabled a cookie trimming filter
Hypothesis: proxy truncation removed Okta session cookie (cookie size exceeded 4k) which prevented key-broker from validating session claim; broker code treats missing claim as unrecoverable and stalls waiting for callback
Reproduced in staging by enabling CookieTrim filter on edge-proxy and running CLI login; observed identical log pattern
Confirmed browser receives full redirect URL including code, but key-broker fails before initiating token exchange due to malformed cookie parse path
Temporary change: key-broker retry path added to treat missing cookie as 'continue-with-code' allowing token exchange; workaround requires broker change and additional validation against Okta introspect endpoint
Security review: bypassing cookie validation has risk; must ensure code verifier is validated to avoid CSRF. Will pair SRE + security on mitigation design.
~25 engineers across infra, security, and SRE affected (unable to obtain CLI tokens)
Blocking runbook access and short-term operational tasks relying on key-broker tokens
Ticket flagged for on-call escalation due to P1 business impact

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 16:10 - SRE-OnCall: Verified edge-proxy 2.8.1 introduced CookieTrim filter. Rolled back filter on us-west canary; observed successful logins from 3 test users.
1) SRE to perform controlled canary rollout of key-broker fix (with PKCE verification) in us-west
2) Edge-proxy team to patch CookieTrim filter to preserve Okta session cookies or increase header size threshold
3) Security to complete sign-off and update runbook for cookie-truncation scenarios
4) Postmortem scheduled after mitigation: capture scope, timeline, and permanent fix plan
Users can: 1) use browser-based personal access token (PAT) for short-term operations, or 2) re-run login from a host behind an unaffected ingress that doesn't trim cookies
Edge-proxy rollback to previous config restores full functionality for affected hosts
Mitigation in staging validated. Awaiting controlled canary rollout to prod and edge-proxy config patch. Temporary workarounds available. Postmortem to follow after prod rollout.
Key-broker updated to not fail on missing cookie if valid OIDC code and PKCE verifier are present; edge-proxy team will release patch to CookieTrim filter. Follow-up: add telemetry to detect cookie truncation events and alert earlier.
payload.summary: CLI key-broker login hangs after Okta auth cookie truncation by edge proxy

Issue summary
- The scheduled backup CronJob deployed via Helm in staging is failing immediately due to missing RBAC permissions.
- This blocks our nightly backup verification and is causing noise for on-call.

Impact
- Staging backup schedule is effectively disabled (no successful backups since enabling the chart values).
- No customer impact (staging only), but this blocks Day-2 ops hardening and restore drill automation.

Environment
- Cluster: private-staging-us-east-1
- Namespace: redwood-private
- Chart: redwood-private (backup CronJob enabled)
- Backup storage backend: S3 (staging bucket)

Symptoms
- CronJob pods crash with "forbidden" errors when attempting to enumerate resources required for control-plane backup.

Steps to reproduce
1) Deploy/upgrade Helm release with backup enabled:
   - values.backup.enabled=true
   - values.backup.schedule="0 2 * * *"
2) Wait for CronJob to create a Job.
3) Inspect logs for the Job pod:
   kubectl -n redwood-private logs job/<job-name>

Observed logs (redacted)
- E0122 02:01:14.123] error: failed preflight: unable to read cluster state: secrets is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:redwood-private:redwood-backup" cannot list resource "secrets" in API group "" in the namespace "redwood-private"
- E0122 02:01:14.124] error: failed inventory: redwoodtenants.platform.redwood.ai is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:redwood-private:redwood-backup" cannot list resource "redwoodtenants" in API group "platform.redwood.ai" in the namespace "redwood-private"

Expected behavior
- Backup CronJob service account should have the minimal RBAC required to read backup inputs (config/state CRs, configmaps, select secrets or secret references) and create the backup artifact.

Notes
- This appears to be a Helm chart RBAC template gap (service account is created, but Role/RoleBinding is incomplete/missing required verbs/resources when backup is enabled).
2025-01-22 02:18 (Sean Gallagher): Paging noise started after enabling scheduled backups in staging. Job pods failing with RBAC forbidden. Attaching command output:
- kubectl -n redwood-private get pods | grep backup
- kubectl -n redwood-private logs job/redwood-private-backup-28947281

2025-01-22 03:02 (Sean Gallagher): Confirmed serviceAccountName on the pod is "redwood-backup". RoleBinding exists but Role only includes configmaps. Looks like it never got secrets + Redwood CRDs.

2025-01-22 09:41 (Bruno Silva): Taking this. I suspect we templated RBAC for configmaps only and missed the CRDs used by the backup inventory step. Will diff staging rendered templates vs latest chart and propose minimal RBAC.

2025-01-22 12:10 (Bruno Silva): Root cause: RBAC template for backup CronJob uses a Role that does not include:
- core/secrets (needed for reading the backup config secret + optional S3 credentials in staging)
- platform.redwood.ai/* custom resources (redwoodtenants, routingpolicies) that the backup CLI inventories for a consistent snapshot
Also RoleBinding was conditional on .Values.backup.rbac.create but our staging values only set backup.enabled.

2025-01-22 12:23 (Bruno Silva): Proposed fix (staging hotfix):
1) Set values.backup.rbac.create=true
2) Expand Role rules to include:
- apiGroups: [""] resources: ["configmaps","secrets"] verbs: ["get","list","watch"]
- apiGroups: ["platform.redwood.ai"] resources: ["redwoodtenants","routingpolicies"] verbs: ["get","list","watch"]
- apiGroups: ["batch"] resources: ["jobs"] verbs: ["get","list"] (for status reporting)

2025-01-22 13:05 (Sean Gallagher): Applied temporary patch by manually creating Role/RoleBinding (see below). Next scheduled run succeeded.
Manual patch (staging only):
- kubectl apply -f rbac-redwood-backup.yaml
- verified with: kubectl auth can-i list secrets --as=system:serviceaccount:redwood-private:redwood-backup -n redwood-private

2025-01-23 10:18 (Bruno Silva): Opened/update in helm charts (PR noted in ticket). Added:
- sensible defaults: when backup.enabled, also create rbac by default
- tightened permissions to namespace-scoped Role (not ClusterRole)
- docs note: if your deployment uses external-secrets, add read-only to those CRs (optional)

2025-01-24 08:27 (Sean Gallagher): Pulled updated chart into staging, removed manual RBAC objects, confirmed CronJob succeeds. Marking resolved.
Resolved by updating the Helm chart to create the backup Role/RoleBinding when backups are enabled and to include the minimal namespace-scoped permissions required by the backup CLI (core configmaps/secrets + Redwood platform CRs). Staging was unblocked by a temporary manual RBAC patch while the chart fix was rolled out.
Staging-only workaround prior to chart fix: create a namespace Role/RoleBinding granting the backup service account get/list/watch on configmaps + required Redwood CRs, plus get/list secrets if S3 creds are stored as a secret. Verify with `kubectl auth can-i` before re-running the CronJob.
Add a Helm template test (or CI render check) that asserts backup.enabled implies creation of ServiceAccount+Role+RoleBinding with expected rules.
Update the internal runbook to include an RBAC preflight section: `kubectl auth can-i` checks for the backup SA.
Confirm backup process does not require reading secret payloads beyond explicit backup config/credentials (align with security decision: prefer secret references; avoid backing up secret material).
Add an SRE alert in staging for CronJob consecutive failures > 2 runs (non-paging during maintenance window).
payload.summary: Staging: Private control-plane backup CronJob failing with RBAC "forbidden" (cannot list/get secrets + Redwood CRs)

Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Retail, enterprise) has requested a targeted export of session logs and associated request/response payloads for a pending third-party security audit. They specifically asked for sessions touching a set of customer IDs and date range (2026-02-20 through 2026-03-05).

Impact:
Potential exposure of customer-identifying fields if redaction is incomplete. Request requires coordination across SRE (log extraction), Security (KMS & key access), and Legal/Compliance (contract & audit scope). Time-sensitive due to audit window; customer flagged as enterprise SLA.

Requested deliverables:
- Extract full request+response records for session IDs provided by customer or for the specified date range and customer IDs.
- Provide redaction metadata and confirmation of PII removal (or fields retained with justification).
- Delivery method: secure SFTP to customer-managed location OR temporary signed URL with strict expiry; Legal prefers SFTP to their auditor account.
- Audit trail: who accessed, query filters used, and KMS key IDs used to decrypt artifacts.

Why this is tricky:
- Production logs live in an encrypted S3 path with KMS envelope encryption and are indexed by a streaming pipeline; naive extraction risks including KV cache or non-redacted traces.
- Previous tickets (INT-4312, INT-5789) flagged gaps in how partial redaction was documented. We must avoid ad-hoc manual copies without an auditable workflow.

Customer-specified scope: customer_ids: [ACME-92, ACME-239], date_range: 2026-02-20 to 2026-03-05, include request and model response payloads, include request metadata (IP, timestamp, route). Delivery: SFTP to auditor@acme-audit.example.com; retention: 30 days; encryption: at-rest AES-256; requester: Acme legal - contact: sarah.liu@acme.com
Logs are stored in s3://redwood-prod-logs/session-archive/ and indexed in ES cluster logging-prod-3. Extraction pipeline must use the authorized read role 'log-extract-audit' and an extraction job should run from the support-runner namespace to ensure RBAC and egress controls. KMS key: projects/redwood/cryptoKeys/prod-logs-kms (access control required).
1) Confirm exact session identifiers or confirm customer IDs and date range.
2) Open a temporary gated extraction job in staging extraction-runner to validate query filters (use sample data).
3) Run extraction against production with logging enabled and 'dry-run' flag first to list objects that would be exported.
4) Apply redaction toolchain (redact-utils v1.3) to extracted payloads and produce an audit manifest listing redaction rationale for each field.
5) Coordinate with Security to provision SFTP credentials to auditor account and provide single-use passphrase stored in Vault.
Dry-run output: 1,236 objects; several payloads include 'user_email' and 'billing_account_id' fields that must be redacted.
KMS policy: prod-logs-kms currently allows decryption for roles: 'log-reader', 'support-ops'; 'log-extract-audit' missing decrypt. Proposal: temporary policy grant scoped to extraction job with automatic revocation after 72 hours.
Redaction tooling: redact-utils v1.3 flags ambiguous fields named 'acc' or 'acctId' - need mapping to canonical schema to avoid misses.
SRE recommends: export pipeline produce two outputs: (1) raw encrypted bundle for internal audit under stricter controls, (2) redacted bundle for customer/auditor. Keep manifest linking originals to redacted artefacts in Vault-only access.
Nina Morales (Support) - 2026-03-10: Created ticket after intake call with Acme. They supplied an initial CSV of session IDs; asking for ETA and whether PII redaction can be certified.
Ethan Brooks (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Will validate KMS access and run a non-destructive dry-run. Noted that 'log-extract-audit' role currently lacks decrypt permission for prod-logs-kms. Raising to Security to request temporary grant.
Dara Chen (Security) - 2026-03-11: We can approve a scoped grant but require Legal sign-off on auditor identity and a short-term IAM binding. Need Confluence page signed: Compliance/Third-Party-Audit-Checklist.
Liam Patel (Legal) - 2026-03-11: Requested confirmation that sensitive fields (credit_card, ssn, full_email) will be redacted. Also asked for copy of auditor NDA; customer to provide.
Ethan Brooks (SRE) - 2026-03-12: Performed dry-run; found 1,236 matching objects totaling ~8.3GB. Dry-run manifest attached to ticket (link: s3://support-temp/INT-8591/dryrun-manifest.json).
1) Legal to confirm auditor identity and NDA (owner: Liam Patel).
2) Security to approve temporary KMS decrypt grant and create short-lived IAM binding (owner: Dara Chen).
3) SRE to run extraction with dry-run approved filters and produce redacted bundle using redact-utils; produce audit manifest (owner: Ethan Brooks).
4) Support to coordinate delivery and update customer with ETA once all approvals are in place (owner: Nina Morales).
Pending approvals: legal and security sign-offs required before extraction. No delivery until redaction and audit manifest validated.
Create a reusable runbook for targeted log exports that standardizes dry-run, redaction, and delivery steps (owner: SRE).
Add automated KMS grant playbook for time-limited decrypt access to reduce manual overhead (owner: Security).
payload.summary: Customer session export + compliance SOP for third-party audit request
