Issue summary:
A subset of vendor payouts scheduled for the 2026-03-01 automated weekly payrun were excluded during the payrun selection step. Root cause appears to be a mismatch between supplier ledger codes in the procurement system and the finance ledger mapping table used by the payrun scheduler.

Impact:
- 7 vendor invoices (value ~$48k) were not picked up by the automatic payrun and remained in 'Pending' state.
- Finance manually intervened to avoid missed payments; this increased operational load and risk of duplicate payments.
- Affects scheduled weekly automatic payrun for the US East region; no customer-facing outages but internal SLA missed.

Initial hypothesis:
Ledger mapping service returned a null mapping for a group of suppliers that were recently migrated from legacy vendor records. The payrun scheduler treats null/unknown ledger code as 'exclude' by design.

1) Use production DB snapshot (2026-03-01 02:00 UTC).
2) Query suppliers with vendor_origin = 'legacy_migration' and ledger_code IS NULL in ledger_mapping table.
3) Trigger payrun selection dry-run for weekly payrun for us-east.
4) Confirm those vendors are omitted from selection list and flagged 'mapping_missing'.
[2026-03-01T03:15:12Z] payrun-scheduler.INFO selecting vendors for weekly_us_east run_id=wr-2026-03-01
[2026-03-01T03:15:12Z] ledger-sync.WARN missing mapping for supplier_id=SV-9987 ledger_code=NULL
[2026-03-01T03:15:13Z] payrun-scheduler.INFO vendor SV-9987 excluded reason=mapping_missing
[2026-03-01T03:16:05Z] finance-ops.INFO manual_payment_created vendor=SV-9987 ref=MP-20260301-7
Found 7 supplier records with ledger_code NULL in ledger_mapping; all have vendor_origin='legacy_migration' and recent vendor_id renames.
Ledger-sync job (daily at 00:30 UTC) showed errors for these supplier IDs between 2026-02-27 and 2026-02-28 — stack traces indicate unique constraint failure when writing to mapping table; job swallowed error and did not flag for re-run.
Payrun selection logic currently treats any non-resolvable mapping as exclusion. This is intended but means silent omissions if mapping sync fails.
Finance team confirmed manual payments were initiated on 2026-03-01 to avoid vendor impact; no duplicate payments observed so far but reconciliation pending.
Related PR in payrun-service attempts to make selection more verbose (https://github.com/redwood-inference/payrun-service/pull/1420) — aligns with this issue but does not address root mapping write failure.
Hannah Li (Reporter) [2026-03-01]: Noticed 7 vendors missing from payrun snapshot; finance ops created manual payments. Please triage ledger-sync immediately.
Marcus Nguyen (Assignee) [2026-03-01]: Acknowledged. Pulling logs for ledger-sync and payrun dry-run.
Found the constraint failure traces; escalating to infra team for DB write retries.
Elena Park (Finance Ops) [2026-03-02]: Manual payments created and queued. Reconciliations team will compare against automated run once ledger mappings fixed.
Request: flag any future payruns with 'mapping_error' to be surfaced on the finance console.
DevInfra (by ticket) [2026-03-03]: Identified that the ledger_mapping table shard had reached 95% utilisation causing occasional write deadlocks; increased capacity and re-run ledger-sync for missed vendors.
Marcus Nguyen [2026-03-04]: Re-ran ledger-sync for the affected supplier list; mappings now present. Triggered payrun dry-run — vendors are included. Scheduling follow-up to harden error visibility.
Finance Ops [2026-03-05]: Confirmed vendors were successfully paid via manual run and will now be marked as reconciled once GL entries post.
Workaround/mitigation: DevInfra increased table capacity and re-ran the ledger-sync job which restored mappings for the 7 vendors. Finance executed manual payments on 2026-03-01; those payments were reconciled against bank statements on 2026-03-05.
Permanent fix: Engineering to add explicit failure alerts to ledger-sync (notify #finance and create INC when mapping writes fail), and update payrun-service to surface 'mapping_error' items on finance console instead of silently excluding. PR for improved payrun logging submitted (PR 1420).
Status: Temporary mitigation applied and payrun behavior corrected for this run; follow-up engineering work scheduled (see follow_up_tasks).
ENG-Task: Add error propagation and alerting in ledger-sync pipeline (owner: Marcus Nguyen) — target 2026-03-12.
ENG-Task: Update payrun-service to surface mapping_error vendors in finance console and create a review queue (owner: Payments team) — target 2026-03-19.
FIN-Task: Reconciliation checklist update to include 'mapping_missing' audit after each automated payrun (owner: Elena Park) — target 2026-03-10.
OPS-Task: Database shard capacity monitoring to prevent write deadlocks; add autoscaling policy (owner: DevInfra) — target 2026-03-08.
payload.summary: Supplier ledger code mismatch preventing automated payrun inclusion

Employee start-date risk: inability to access paid developer tools (JetBrains, VMware), delay in laptop delivery (estimated 5-10 business days), risk of exposing work to non-compliant key storage if we instruct use of personal encryption. Potential escalation to HR and legal if start is missed.
New hire ID: RWI-2026-312 (HR record). Offer accepted with relocation assistance. payload.description: Issue summary: Users approving access requests via the Okta mobile deep link (iOS/Android) sometimes see the console show the approval as successful, but the temporary role never materializes in RBAC and the access remains in a 'pending' state. Impact: Affected employees cannot perform just-in-time elevated actions (e.g., runbooks, support tools) even though the approval UI indicated success. This affects ~3-5% of mobile approvals in us-west during the window observed. Environment: Production (auth-service v2.14.1), Okta SSO, mobile deep-link flow, us-west region. Steps to reproduce: 1) From support portal, request temporary elevated role (JIT). 2) Approver opens Okta approval notification on mobile and taps the deep link. 3) Okta completes approval and redirects to redwood://auth/approval?token=... 4) Console shows approval success; approver receives success toast. 5) Requester remains in 'pending' with no RBAC grant. Observed behavior: Console shows success but backend audit events show the approval callback was received with 202 Accepted and returned before the RBAC engine applied the grant. In some cases the callback processing retried later and succeeded; in others it remained pending until manual retry. Initial logs show a race between the approval webhook handler and the role-propagation queue consumer. Expected behavior: Approval via mobile deep-link should result in the same synchronous or reliably-queued propagation path as web approvals, with RBAC grant applied within SLO (~30s). Investigation notes: - Spike in incidents correlates with auth-service deployment v2.14.1 (rolled 2026-03-09). - Mobile deep-link flow appends an auth callback parameter that hits /api/v1/approvals/callback which was refactored in v2.14.1 to return 202 early for mobile UX improvements. - The refactor moved role-propagation responsibility to an in-memory queue that can be GC'd if the approval handler instance scales down immediately after returning 202. - Reproducible in staging when artificially introducing pod scale-to-zero within 5s of callback. - Linked incident INT-472001 notes a similar approval callback race for SSO flows last year; potential overlap in the queueing logic. Temporary workaround: Avoid approving from the mobile deep link; instead approve from the web UI which uses the synchronous propagation path. Engineers can manually trigger a propagation retry via the console action "Reapply approvals" on the request. Next steps: 1) Revert the early-202 behavior in v2.14.1 for the approval callback OR persist queue messages to Redis (durable queue) before returning 202. 2) Add end-to-end e2e test that simulates pod scale-down during callback processing. 3) Add monitoring alert for approval callbacks that return 202 with no subsequent role-propagation audit events within 60s. 4) Patch and roll back with canary to us-west. Workaround rollout: Support agents notified to instruct approvers to use web UI until fix is live. Postmortem owner: Marta Nguyen.
payload.summary: Mobile SSO deep-link approvals leave temporary access in 'pending' despite console confirmation

Issue summary:
Several internal users report that the approval UI shows 'Grant approved' for Model Inspector access requests, but the users still get 403 when opening Model Inspector. This started after an Okta SCIM provisioning change and a recent identity-proxy rollout (2026-03-11).

Impact:
- ~12 engineers across multiple teams cannot open Model Inspector despite approvals in the console.
- Affects internal runbook lookups and emergency debug flows during oncall.
- No external customers affected, internal-only tooling.

Timeline (local):
- 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC: identity-proxy v2.7.1 rolled (header canonicalization change).
- 2026-03-12 16:05 UTC: intermittent SCIM sync errors reported in metrics (okta->scim queue spikes).
- 2026-03-13 09:10 UTC: first support report received from SRE team.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) User requests Model Inspector access via internal console (approval flows).
2) Approver clicks grant in the approval queue; UI shows success.
3) User attempts to open Model Inspector and receives 403 with RBAC denial message.
4) Console logs show the entitlement claim present but with a namespace prefix mismatch (e.g., "ent:models:inspector" vs expected "ent:tool:model_inspector").

Observed behavior:
- Approval event exists in audit logs and Okta SCIM shows group membership.
- RBAC service evaluates claims and denies due to claim key mismatch/namespace rewrite.
- Some users see session cookies with older namespace and need re-login to surface any change (but re-login alone does not fix when claim namespace differs).

Expected behavior:
- Approval should result in effective permissions in RBAC and user should access Model Inspector immediately or after short propagation.

Initial hypothesis:
- identity-proxy header canonicalization introduced a claim-key normalization change that, combined with SCIM provisioning race, created duplicate entitlements under a different namespace. RBAC lookup uses the canonical key and does not match the new claim.

Immediate business workaround proposed:
- Manual RBAC reconciliation job to map both namespaces for affected accounts (temporary).
- Revert proxy canonicalization if root cause confirmed and no quick reconciliation exists.

References:
- Audit event examples and links are attached in investigation_notes.

Audit query: SELECT * FROM approval_audit WHERE resource='model_inspector' AND created_at>='2026-03-11' returned 18 events with status=GRANTED; corresponding RBAC evaluations show 'no_match' for claim_key lookup.
Okta SCIM logs (2026-03-12 15:58 UTC): transient 503s from scim-provisioner queue; retry loops caused near-duplicate group patches for some accounts.
Identity-proxy PR #1128 (deployed 2026-03-11): replaced '.' with '_' in claim namespaces and lowercased header keys; change introduced 'ent:tool:model_inspector' -> 'ent:tool_model_inspector' in some paths.
RBAC service policy lookup code expects claim key 'ent:tool:model_inspector' and does exact-string match; no fallback or fuzzy match present.
Affected users sample: ['sasha@redwood.com','dev+infra@redwood.com','mike.t@redwood.com'] — observed duplicates where one account has both namespace variants in the token store.
Grafana dashboard 'scim-provisioner/error-rate' shows spike 2026-03-12 16:00 UTC (3x baseline).
2026-03-13 09:35 - Support (Aisha Patel): Ticket opened after SRE escalation. Collecting list of affected users and request IDs. Notified #internal-support and oncall.

- Potential data exposure if devices assigned to departed contractors still have active credentials or KMS access.
- Developer friction if hardware earmarked for rotation is not available during the onboarding wave starting 2026-04-01.

Background / Context:

Summary: Since 2026-03-09 ~03:00 UTC a subset of newly provisioned users are getting 403 when calling the ModelObservability API. Initial triage shows users exist in OKTA and have expected groups, but the RBAC role lookup in auth-service fails because group identifiers in the incoming auth claim are integers instead of strings after a recent Okta mapping change. Impact: Affected SREs and ML engineers cannot access model observability dashboards or runbook actions; blocking incident response in us-east for customer-impacting alerts.
1) Create or modify an Okta user with group assignment via provisioning (SCIM).
2) Wait for scim-sync job to run (0-5m).
3) Login to console and call /v1/model-observability/metrics (or open dashboard).
4) Observe 403 and no role in auth-service logs for the user.
Expected: role lookup succeeds and 200 returned. Actual: 403 denied due to missing role mapping.
auth-service warning: role-lookup: claim.groups value types: [123456, 234567] (type: integer)
expected mapping key types: "123456"

example token claim (decoded): {
  "sub": "00u1abcXyZ",
  "email": "eng+test@redwood.ai",
  "groups": [123456, 234567],
  "iss": "https://okta.redwood.ai"
}

auth-service debug: mappedRoles=[] for user 00u1abcXyZ at 2026-03-10T03:12:07Z
model-observability-api access denied: headers: { x-rw-user: 00u1abcXyZ } response: 403 {
  "error": "unauthorized",
  "reason": "no-matching-role-for-groups"
}
Timeline: change window 2026-03-08 22:00 UTC when Okta admin updated group import mapping to emit numeric IDs (Okta API update). Hypothesis: identity-proxy and scim-sync historically normalized group ids to strings; the new mapping produced integers and our role index uses string keys -> lookup misses.
Findings:
- scim-sync stored groups in DB as strings when coming from canonical SCIM paths, but identity-proxy forwards token claims verbatim.
- auth-service role lookup code compares claim group IDs with role-index map (string keys). No type coercion.
- Reproduced locally by forging token with numeric group values; role lookup returns empty.
- Not all users affected: only those provisioned after Okta mapping change (group ids numeric). Older tokens remain as strings and continue to work.
Evidence: logs above and successful reproduction in staging by creating token with numeric groups.
Mitigation attempted: temporary canary: identity-proxy will coerce numeric claim.groups to strings on ingress; deployed to canary cluster (canary-2) 2026-03-11 18:30 UTC.

Additional notes:
Hotfix: identity-proxy change (PR #498) coerces all group ids in the token claim to strings on ingress and emits a metric for any non-string group values. Auth-service change (PR #1257) added defensive coercion for role lookup as backup. Canary results: successful requests for previously affected users on canary-2. Rollout plan: staged rollout to prod us-east 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC with monitoring and immediate rollback on elevated error rates. Root cause: Okta mapping change that started emitting numeric group ids; our code assumed string typed ids.
1) Add schema validation on identity-proxy (block incoming tokens with unexpected types and alert).
2) Create automated unit test in auth-service for claim type coercion.
3) Ask IAM team to revert or document Okta mapping change and add approver workflow for mapping modifications.
4) Postmortem to be authored in Confluence and linked here after incident closure.
Assigned to: Diego Morales (follow-up engineering items) and Priya Kapoor (postmortem coordination).
payload.summary: Role resolution fails after Okta group id type change; ModelObservability API returns 403 for newly provisioned users

Issue summary:
Ephemeral environment bootstrap for experimental-llm-sandbox is failing during credential exchange. The credential broker attempts to construct an assume-role ARN with the role path URL-encoded, which does not match the canonical ARN expected by AWS STS when passing session tags from GCP WIF.

Impact:
- Oncalls and SREs cannot provision ephemeral sandboxes for ML debug jobs via the web onboarding flow.
- Several data-science jobs queued in staging are blocked; blocking developer productivity.
- Affects both staging-us-west and some prod-us-east onboarding requests routed through the new broker.

Environment:
- Credential broker: infra/credential-broker v0.9.3 (k8s deployment in staging-us-west)
- GCP WIF pool: projects/ops/pools/ephemeral-wif
- Affected AWS accounts: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ops/ephemeral/debugger
- Terraform runner and web UI bootstrap paths both observed failing.

Expected behavior:
- Broker generates assume-role ARNs that exactly match AWS role resource names (no extraneous encoding) and STS AssumeRole succeeds with session tags preserved.

Actual behavior:
- STS AssumeRole call returns AccessDenied with message referencing a non-existent role ARN. The ARN in the broker log contains percent-encoding for the role path ("%2F"), while AWS expects plain "/" in the role resource path.

Notes on scope and novelty:
- This is not the classic session-tag truncation (see INT-860351) nor a WIF audience mismatch; the call reaches STS and is rejected due to name mismatch. The broker is building ARNs using url.PathEscape() semantics in Go, which is causing the mismatch.
1) Start web onboarding flow for ephemeral environment 'experimental-llm-sandbox' in staging-us-west.
2) Broker exchanges GCP WIF assertion for STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity to target role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ops/ephemeral/debugger.
3) Observe broker logs: the generated 'RoleArn' field is 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role%2Fops%2Fephemeral%2Fdebugger'.
4) STS responds with AccessDenied / role does not exist error.
2026-03-11T09:14:02Z broker pod credential-broker-5f6c9: DEBUG building RoleArn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role%2Fops%2Fephemeral%2Fdebugger
2026-03-11T09:14:02Z broker pod credential-broker-5f6c9: ERROR assume role failed: AccessDenied: The role with name 'role%2Fops%2Fephemeral%2Fdebugger' cannot be found\n\tat aws-sdk-go/service/sts.(*STS).AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
2026-03-11T09:14:03Z kube-apiserver: pod restarted credential-broker-5f6c9 (OOM not observed).
11-Mar 10:00 - Reproduced locally by invoking broker with a sample WIF token; observed same percent-encoded RoleArn. Hypothesis: broker uses url.PathEscape() instead of plain concatenation.
11-Mar 13:30 - Manual assume-role via AWS CLI using canonical ARN succeeds: aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ops/ephemeral/debugger --role-session-name test -> SUCCESS.
11-Mar 15:05 - Confirmed terraform-runner and web UI both call same broker endpoint; failure surface is identical.
11-Mar 16:20 - Checked AWS account policy: no deny on tag keys; denies only trigger if role name mismatch, reinforcing ARN mismatch theory.
12-Mar 09:45 - Temporary workaround test: created a duplicate role with encoded name 'role%2Fops%2Fephemeral%2Fdebugger' (for testing only) and observed STS call succeed (proves encoding is the root cause).
Maya Chen (Reporter) 2026-03-11T10:12: 'Filed after paging oncall; high impact for ML productivity in staging. Adding SRE and infra owners.'
Liam O'Connor (Assignee) 2026-03-11T11:05: 'Taking ownership. Reproduced locally. Suspect credential-broker string handling. Will add unit test and patch.'
Patel, SRE 2026-03-12T08:20: 'Checked cluster; no recent org-policy or IAM policy changes. Logging suggests code-level issue.'
Elena Rodriguez (Infra Eng) 2026-03-12T14:55: 'Created hotfix branch in infra/credential-broker; replacing url.PathEscape with explicit role path join. Running staging deployment smoke tests.'
Create temporary alias role without path components (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ephemeral-debugger) and grant same trust policy to unblock teams.
Directly run AWS CLI assume-role with canonical role ARN for critical one-off debug sessions until broker fix is deployed.
Merge and deploy PR to credential-broker that normalizes role ARNs without URL-encoding (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2187).
Add unit+integration test to catch encoded ARN regressions (exercise GCP WIF -> STS flow in CI).
Run a small canary rollout in staging-us-west then promote to prod-us-east; monitor for AccessDenied regressions in STS metrics.
After deployment, remove the temporary alias role and the test encoded role created during investigation.
Add an observability alert in console: high rate of STS AccessDenied errors with RoleArn containing '%25' or '%2F'.
IN-PROGRESS: Hotfix branch created and PR opened (infra/credential-broker#2187). Staging canary passed basic smoke tests on 2026-03-12 15:20 UTC. Plan: deploy to staging rollout channel on 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC, monitor for 2 hours, then deploy to prod-us-east. Post-deploy cleanup tasks documented in linked Confluence page. Temporary alias role will be removed after confirmation.
Audit credential-broker code for other uses of url.PathEscape that may impact IAM ARNs.
Add integration test in infra-ci that validates role ARN equality (unencoded) across multiple onboarding paths.
Document the expected canonical role naming convention for onboarding and include in runbook (confluence).

Issue summary:
A travel advance reimbursement for contractor vendor code ADV-TRAVEL-2026 (claim TR-2026-0047) was ingested into AP as a vendor invoice (INV-TR-2026-1123) and therefore blocked by the vendor-payment validation workflow. Impact:
- $4,320 advance reimbursement stuck in AP queue; would normally be paid in next contractor payout cycle.
- Creates cashflow issues for contractor and increases CS churn risk.
- Manual intervention required to reclassify and release payment.
Environment:
- Production ingestion pipeline (claim-processor v2.7.1)
- Region: us-east
- Affected payment batch: CONTRACTOR-PAYOUT-2026-03-11

Steps to reproduce / observed behaviour:
1) Contractor submitted travel advance via expense UI on 2026-03-07 with attached receipt and bank details for reimbursement. Claim created: TR-2026-0047.
2) Ingestion pipeline picked up payload on 2026-03-09 and created an AP record labelled INV-TR-2026-1123 instead of an expense reimbursement record.
3) AP validation flagged mismatched GL code and put record into BLOCKED_PAYMENTS queue.
4) Finance attempted manual release but backend disallows payout until record type is invoice (manual override not permitted for contractor advances).

Logs / Evidence:
- Ingestion log excerpt (2026-03-09T03:12:45Z): claim_processor INFO "mapped claimant_bank_details -> ap.vendor_bank; record_type set = vendor_invoice"
- AP ledger export: INV-TR-2026-1123, amount 4320.00, status BLOCKED_PAYMENTS, note: "classification: vendor_invoice (auto)"
- Expense UI entry: TR-2026-0047 (attached PDF receipts, claimant id: contractor-1982)

Additional notes:
Hypothesis: A change to the ingestion mapping (deployed 2026-03-01) increased precedence of vendor mapping when claimant_bank_details were present, causing expense claims with bank info to be misclassified as vendor invoices. Confirmed by tracing mapping rules and ingestion logs: rule 'bank_details_to_vendor' evaluated before 'expense_claim' rule for claims with 'advance' flag missing due to a UI variant used by contractors. Additional contributing factor: contractor mobile UI omitted explicit 'advance=true' flag for contractor-1982 due to legacy client app version 1.9.4.
Evidence:
- Deploy diff: claim-processor v2.6.9 -> v2.7.0 (rule reordering in mapping_config.yml)
- Ingestion logs show direct mapping decision path that assigned record_type = vendor_invoice when bank_details present and advance flag null.
Next steps taken:
- Performed targeted backfill to reclassify affected records in production (tested in staging first).
- Patched mapping rules to require explicit claim_type == 'vendor' to map to vendor_invoice, and ensure 'advance' boolean overrides vendor precedence.
- Created quick validation in claim ingestion to flag missing 'advance' boolean for contractor clients and route to manual review instead of automatic vendor mapping.
Workaround / fix applied:
1) Production backfill executed 2026-03-13 15:00 UTC: reclassified 7 records in CONTRACTOR-PAYOUT-2026-03-* batches (including TR-2026-0047).
2) Payment for contractor-1982 released via expedited ACH. Finance confirmed funds posted 2026-03-13 16:45 UTC.
3) Mapping config rollback/patch: rule 'bank_details_to_vendor' demoted; now requires explicit claim_type == 'vendor' or confirmed vendor account_id. Patch deployed 2026-03-12 22:30 UTC (claim-processor v2.7.2).
4) Added validation: claims from mobile client < v1.10 now flagged for manual review if advance boolean missing.
5) Follow-up action created: FIN-REQ-2026-17 to run audit of ingestion-mapped vendor invoices vs expense claims for last 90 days.
Follow-up items / Owners:
- Ingestion team (Anika Patel): monitor ingestion metrics for misclassifications for 7 days, produce dashboard alert.
- DevRel/Client SDK team: notify external contractor cohort to upgrade mobile client; add safeguard in mobile app to include explicit advance flag.
- Engineering: create unit-test guarding mapping order and add regression test in CI.
Status: Ticket moved to In Progress while monitoring; payment released and immediate impact resolved. Further monitoring and audit required.

Issue summary: When engineers connect to corporate via WireGuard while also enabling a phone tether (iPhone or Android hotspot), some clients exhibit a change in route/DNS precedence that causes internal artifact registries (artifacts.redwood.internal) to fail name resolution or route to the public internet. Impact: Multiple engineers reported inability to download CI artifacts and docker layers; CI jobs started failing when builders were on shared tethering. Environment: macOS and Windows laptops using WireGuard client + split-tunnel policy (internal routes routed via wg0), phone hotspots on AT&T and T-Mobile. Intermittent across home and cafe hotspots.

Initial hypothesis: The tethered interface sometimes inserts a default route with higher metric or pushes DNS via captive portal, causing the OS resolver to prefer the cellular DNS or public route and bypass wg0. This results in DNS lookups for internal hostnames either failing or returning public addresses that are unroutable.

Business impact: CI failures for nightly and PR builds for some engineers, blocked deploys for small teams, increased support load.

Connect laptop to corporate WireGuard (wg0) with split-tunnel config that routes 10.0.0.0/8 and internal suffixes via wg0.
Enable phone hotspot (iPhone or Android) and connect the laptop to the tethered SSID.
On the laptop, confirm interface list (ipconfig / ifconfig) shows wg0 and the tether interface.
Attempt to resolve internal registry hostname: nslookup artifacts.redwood.internal
Attempt to curl a known internal artifact URL or docker pull from internal registry.
Toggle phone hotspot off/on and observe behavior changes (sometimes fixes until next tether).
DNS resolves to public or fails; connections to artifacts.redwood.internal time out or route incorrectly. Sometimes TLS handshake fails because SNI/goes to public host. Behaviour is intermittent: works immediately after a fresh wg reconnect, breaks after hotspot reconnect or when mobile operator pushes DNS via captive portal.
When wg0 is up and split-tunnel routes are configured, internal hostnames and routes should resolve and traverse wg0 regardless of tethered/mobile interfaces. No leakage to public DNS or default route should occur for internal prefixes.
Mar 10 08:12:23 laptop-desktop wg0: peer xxxxx: handshake complete
Mar 10 08:12:31 Resolver: search list: redwood.internal local
Mar 10 08:12:38 DNS query artifacts.redwood.internal -> 8.8.4.4 (via tethered interface), NXDOMAIN
Mar 10 08:13:02 curl: (7) Failed to connect to artifacts.redwood.internal port 443: Operation timed out
Packet capture (tcpdump): SYN to 52.24.11.9 (public) from tether interface, no path to private range
Support reproduced on macOS 13.5 and Windows 11 when using iPhone hotspot; behaviour differs by phone OS and mobile carrier.
Windows observed to prefer cellular adapter DNS when its metric is lower than wg0's resolver metric; macOS has resolver ordering quirks with SCPreferencesDomains.
WireGuard config shows allowed-ips includes 10.0.0.0/8 and search domain redwood.internal; client routing table contains correct routes but resolver lookup uses different resolver (OS-level behavior).
Tested workaround: setting wg0 interface metric lower (higher priority) and pinning system DNS to internal resolvers prevents leakage on some clients.
Hypothesis: Mobile operator/captive portal or phone DNS proxy is being pushed to the laptop via DHCP over tether; the client OS sometimes installs that DNS as system resolver ahead of wg0.
1) Reconnect WireGuard after enabling tether — immediate temporary fix in ~60% of cases.
2) On Windows: Increase priority/metric of wg0 adapter or add internal DNS server entries under adapter settings.
3) On macOS: use scutil to set resolver order for redwood.internal to use wg0 nameserver: 'sudo networksetup -setdnsservers <service> <internal-dns>' or create /etc/resolver/redwood.internal file.
4) Recommend engineers avoid phone tether for CI-critical runners until fix applied; use home router or dedicated mobile hotspot configured without operator DNS push.
In progress: Engineering networking team (Diego Martinez) to propose client-side guard rules and update WireGuard client configs to push DNS via a link-local resolver and use WG DNS handling (avoid OS-level DHCP DNS overrides).
Follow-up: Add platform docs for 'Hotspot + WireGuard' troubleshooting and per-OS steps (Confluence page linked).
Long-term: Scheduler to add CI runner affinity to skip builds triggered from tethered networks (policy), and evaluate bundling a small VPN client helper that enforces resolver priority across platforms.
If a specific engineer hits this frequently, escalate to IT for device-specific config or provide a USB-based workaround (Ethernet via phone) as stopgap.
Aisha Patel (Reporter) [2026-03-10]: Hit this in the morning — PR build failed in CI because docker pull timed out when on my phone hotspot. Attached tcpdump and nslookup output.
Support (Diego) [2026-03-10]: Reproduced. Collecting system-level resolver order and adapter metrics from affected machines. Can you confirm phone OS and carrier?
Aisha Patel [2026-03-10]: iPhone 15 Pro on AT&T. Also saw on Android Pixel 7 on T-Mobile for another engineer.
Network Eng (Diego) [2026-03-11]: Working hypothesis updated in investigation_notes. Will prototype a wg client change to prefer link-local DNS from wg0 and push change to the client-config repo. PR referenced above.
SRE (Marta Lopez) [2026-03-12]: Noting CI impact. Adding a temporary check in the runner that validates internal DNS resolution before pulling artifacts and fails fast with a descriptive error so engineers can switch networks.
payload.summary: Cellular tether (phone hotspot) causes route/DNS precedence break -> internal artifact registries unreachable

payload.description:
Issue summary: Legacy Grafana instances (grafana-legacy stack behind auth-proxy) are not receiving Okta role claims after an Okta claim_whitelist rollout. Impact: dashboards that depend on role-based folder access show as blank or 403 for ~12 internal teams in us-west. Intermittent for newer Grafana v8+ instances (they are fine) but consistent for grafana-legacy.

Environment: prod (us-west), grafana-legacy service version v2.7.1, auth-proxy v1.13.0, okta-claim-service v3.4.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Sign in to grafana-legacy via SSO (Okta) using a test user with role claim "analytics_viewer" in Okta.
2. Observe GET /api/orgs/:orgId/folders returns 403 and UI shows no dashboards.
3. Inspect the auth-proxy token forwarded to Grafana and confirm role claim is missing.

Observed behavior: Okta assertion contains roles, but claim_whitelist in claim-service filters to a shorter allow-list. The legacy Grafana expects claim key "roles" (array) and "analytics_viewer" present — it is absent because claim-service returned only the new "app_roles" claim.

Expected behavior: claim-service should include legacy claim keys (roles) when the application (grafana-legacy) is configured as an allowed recipient or when a mapping exists.

Logs/Traces: Auth-proxy request id 2f9b8c7a shows token payload forwarded with claims: ["sub","email","app_roles"]. Claim-service audit log shows transformation rule applied: "apply_whitelist: [sub,email,app_roles]" (rule created during 2026-03-10 rollout). Okta assertion raw SAML contains attributes: roles=["analytics_viewer"].

Business impact: Internal users in product analytics, salesops lost access to critical dashboards during business hours; mitigated by temporary token bypass for a small subset of users (see workaround).
Initial hypothesis: recent claim_whitelist change was applied globally instead of per-application scope, causing legacy apps to lose previously forwarded claims. Verified claim-service config: global default whitelist set on 2026-03-10 via deploy tag v3.4. Policy lacked exceptions.

What we checked:
- Okta SAML assertion contains roles attribute for test user (confirmed).
- auth-proxy instrumentation shows it receives token with missing roles claim.
- Claim-service configuration contains global whitelist and app-specific mapping for grafana (was empty).
- Grafana-legacy expects 'roles' claim; new grafana instances read 'app_roles'.

Next steps identified:
1) Add app-specific whitelist entry for grafana-legacy to include 'roles' and 'email' temporarily.
2) Backfill mapping in claim-service so it copies 'roles' -> 'app_roles' for newer apps while preserving 'roles' for legacy.
3) Create a small deployment to canary the fix to us-west only.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 08:22 - SRE Oncall (Marco Li): Can we scope the rollout to us-west first? Traffic there is majority. Also request a post-deploy smoke test plan.
Workaround applied: added grafana-legacy exception in claim-service whitelist (manual change) to restore 'roles' claim for affected orgs in us-west. Longer-term fix: merged PR to add per-application whitelist and mapping logic to auth-service. Rollout plan: canary to us-west 2026-03-14 10:00 UTC, monitor 30m token flows and dashboards; full prod by 2026-03-14 12:00 UTC if no regressions. Postmortem owner: Priya Kapoor. Follow-ups: update runbook to include claim whitelist change checklist and impact assessment, and add automated integration test covering legacy app claim expectations.
Security review required before full rollout; ensure no PII is re-introduced in claims. Keep customer teams notified via #internal-support and send status email to affected owners.
payload.summary: SSO claim whitelist prevents legacy Grafana instances from receiving role claims

payload.description:
Issue summary: After Okta IDP started deprecating the 'location' custom attribute used in our SCIM to RBAC mapping, a subset of engineers can no longer see or toggle flags in the Feature-Flag Console. Impact: ~12 engineers in product and QA report missing 'feature-flag-admin' permissions while the same users retain other console permissions. This blocks scheduled canary rollouts and a hotfix deployment.
Operational: scheduled canary toggles for release 2026.03.11 blocked; Team productivity: ~12 engineers impacted; Security/compliance: no escalation required but role inconsistency could confuse access reviews.
1) User signs in to Feature-Flag Console via Okta SSO in prod-us-west. 2) Post-login, service evaluates SCIM-provided attributes and maps to RBAC roles. 3) If 'location' attribute is absent or mapped to 'N/A' the role mapping path erroneously skips secondaryGroup assignment. 4) Observe that 'feature-flag-admin' checkbox is not present in the UI and API returns 403 for /api/v1/flags/:id/toggle.
Affected users authenticate successfully but receive 403s when attempting toggle API and do not see admin controls in UI. Audit logs show successful SCIM patch with 'location' set to '-' or omitted. RBAC service logs note 'group mapping fallback missed' for these identities.
When the IDP deprecates an attribute, SCIM and RBAC should fall back to alternate attributes (e.g., 'department' or Okta groups) and preserve existing role grants until an explicit change is made by the admin.
- Feature-Flag Console auth trace (auth-trace-2026-03-11-14:22): shows SCIM->RBAC mapping call returned 200 but mapping result omitted secondaryGroups array.
- RBAC service warn: 'mapping:secondaryGroup not found, no fallback configured' at 14:22:05 UTC.
- Okta SCIM audit (okta-audit-2026-03-11): entries show attribute 'location' marked deprecated in metadata and some userProfile patches containing 'location': null.
Manual grant: Admins can temporarily assign 'feature-flag-admin' to affected users via the console user management page. We documented a one-off script (scripts/grant_flag_admin.sh) to mass-assign rights during the incident window.
- Hypothesis A: SCIM connector removed 'location' from user payload after an Okta schema cleanup.
- Hypothesis B: RBAC mapping code treats an empty string or '-' as a sentinel to remove secondaryGroup assignment.
- Verified: SCIM connector code (commit: github.com/redwood-inference/scim-connector@b2d4f9e) changed handling of null attributes two weeks ago; no fallback mapping was added.
- Coco (oncall-auth) reproduced locally by setting user.profile.location to null and observed identical 403s.
- Related tickets: INT-202406 (group-encoding mismatch) contains notes about mapping fallbacks; INT-531246 mentions SCIM rate limit but not relevant.
Aisha Patel (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed several engineers can't toggle flags during morning deploy. They authenticate fine, but UI is missing admin controls.
Miguel Ortega (Assignee) - 2026-03-10: I can reproduce with a test account by clearing 'location' on the Okta profile. Adding logs and routing to auth team to confirm SCIM payloads.
Jules Park (Auth Eng) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed SCIM connector updated handling of nulls in commit b2d4f9e; we didn't add a fallback mapping. Proposing quick patch to RBAC mapper to check Okta 'groups' list before dropping secondaryGroup.
Samira Chen (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Deployed temporary admin-script to grant rights to the affected list; recording in runbook. Will coordinate with SOC for audit trail.
Miguel Ortega - 2026-03-12: Patch prepared: rbac-mapper now treats missing 'location' as non-fatal and consults 'groups' -> PR #1237 opened. Running canary for 2 users in prod-us-west.
In progress: PR #1237 for rbac-mapper fallback behavior created and under code review. Temporary mass-grant script used for immediate unblock. Final resolution will include adding unit tests and a rolling deploy, then coordination with Identity team to update SCIM connector behavior.
payload.summary: Okta attribute deprecation causes partial RBAC grant for Feature-Flag Console

Issue summary: After depot battery replacement on several refurbished MacBooks we observed that FileVault escrow (institutional keys) fails to upload to our KMIP-backed escrow service. This prevents DEP/MDM finalization and blocks device check-in for end users. Impact: Devices remain in 'Pending Escrow' state, fail MDM policy application, and cannot complete AAD/AzureAD registration for corporate network access. Environment: Depot-imaged devices (staging) and small sample from production depot-us-west. Reproducible on devices that went through physical battery replacement and SMC/PRAM reset flow.
1) Receive refurbished MacBook from depot after battery replacement
2) Boot to staging image using our depot netboot and run automated imaging sequence
3) Complete OS install and corporate provisioning agent runs, attempts FileVault escrow upload
4) Provisioning agent reports KMIP upload error and device remains Pending Escrow
5) Attempt manual upload using kms-client returns TLS client cert validation error
ProvisioningAgent[2026-03-09T10:12:03Z] ERROR vault-escrow: kmip upload failed: TLS handshake error: certificate missing for client identity
kms-client --upload --device-serial ABCD1234 exit code 1: client certificate not found in Keychain: 'com.redwood.kmip.client'
system_profiler SMC: hardware: SMC firmware version: 2.58f11; NVRAM: 'boot-args' cleared after SMC reset
Initial hypothesis: depot SMC/PRAM reset during battery replacement cleared the local KMIP client certificate entry from the system keychain
Checked keychain on repro device: institutional KMIP cert absent under login/system keychains; provisioning agent expects cert at /Library/Keychains/com.redwood.kmip
Observed that imaging workflow attempts to re-import a device-private cert from /var/lib/provisioning/kmip_backup if present; backup missing for affected devices
Reproduced by intentionally removing KMIP cert before running agent; same error returned
Staging fleet ~5/300 recent repairs affected, correlated to repair vendor batch 'RV-17' which used a different SMC-reset toolchain
Manual re-enrollment: run 'sudo security import /opt/repair/kmip-client.p12 -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain -P <pass>' then restart provisioning-agent; confirms KMIP cert present and escrow upload succeeds.
Engineering to add an idempotent step in the depot imaging sequence to detect missing KMIP client cert and import a freshly generated device-scoped cert from our secure artifact store. Patch PR opened (see related_github_prs). For immediate mitigation we've instructed depot team to preserve /var/lib/provisioning/kmip_backup during battery replacement. Long-term: update vendor repair SOP to avoid SMC tooling that wipes system keychain entries, and add automated cert import to imaging flow.
1) SRE/Imaging to roll the provisioning-agent PR to staging (PR #842) and validate with 20 repaired units - target 2026-03-16
2) Depot ops to audit last 300 repairs from vendor RV-17 and run manual re-enroll script for affected serials - target 2026-03-15
3) Security to rotate escrow MFA key if we detect any missing cert anomalies during audit - target 2026-03-20
4) Create vendor-facing repair SOP update to prevent keychain wipes - assigned to Sofia Martinez - due 2026-03-22

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 08:30 Security (Ethan Ross): Recommended temporary escrow key rotation window if audit shows >10% affected. For now sample rate below threshold but monitor closely.
payload.summary: Missing KMIP certificate after battery replacement prevents FileVault escrow and DEP key upload on refurbished MacBooks

payload.description:
Issue summary: After a scheduled IdP attribute rename (department -> dept) performed by the identity team, users belonging to delegated Okta groups used by the oncall approval flow are not being recognized. Impact: approval requests for runbook elevation and temporary oncall access are stuck in the internal approval queue and cannot be auto-routed to the delegated approvers. This affects multiple teams' ability to escalate runbooks during maintenance windows.

Observed behaviour:
- Requests appear in the approval queue with 'no approver found' instead of routing to the delegated group.
- Affected users still have the expected Okta group membership in Okta UI, but our SCIM-derived group mapping table shows empty 'department' attribute for those accounts.

Business impact: Potentially blocks emergency runbook escalations for 3 SRE teams across us-east region during the incident window.

Additional notes: IdP change was scheduled and communicated, but the downstream SCIM mapping rule that populates the 'department' column in our identity cache expects the old attribute key. The change wasn't coordinated with the SCIM mapping rollout in our proxy glue service.
1) In Okta test tenant, rename attribute 'department' to 'dept' or change attribute mapping.
2) Wait for SCIM sync to push profile changes (or trigger manual sync).
3) Submit an oncall runbook approval request that relies on delegated-group routing.
4) Observe approval queue: request shows 'no approver found' and routing logs show failed lookup against identity-cache column 'department'.
auth-proxy[2026-03-11T09:14:02Z] ERROR lookupDelegatedApprover: no match for department=''. identity-cache rows returned=0
scim-sync[2026-03-11T09:12:58Z] INFO profilePatch: user=alice@example.com attrsUpdated=['dept'] oldAttrs=['department']
approval-service[2026-03-11T09:14:05Z] WARN routeDelegatedGroup: fallback to manual-queue because delegated_group_lookup returned empty
Initial hypothesis: SCIM schema change broke downstream mapping. Confirmed: IdP attribute was renamed at 2026-03-11 09:10 UTC (change request IT-2026-0311). Identity-cache assembly code expects 'department' key. SCIM logs show source attr 'dept' but our mapping layer filters for 'department' key strictly.
Actions taken so far:
- Pulled recent SCIM payloads from Okta to verify attribute keys (confirmed only 'dept' present).
- Replayed mapping job in staging with new payload to reproduce behavior.
- Short-term patch: updated mapping translation table in identity-cache service to map 'dept' -> 'department' for lookups (hotfix applied to prod-us-east at 2026-03-11T12:30Z).
- Verified routing resumed for 70% of queued requests after hotfix. Remaining 30% follow-up required: some cached entries were tombstoned and require full re-sync.
Root cause: lack of backward-compatible attribute mapping in SCIM consumer when IdP attribute key changed.
Applied an emergency mapping translation in identity-cache to map new attribute key 'dept' to the expected 'department' column. For users with missing cache rows, triggered a targeted SCIM full-profile re-sync for affected users (jobs queued). Instructed support to triage pending approval requests and perform manual approver assignment where needed.
Hotfix deployed to identity-cache to add key translation and fallbacks. Scheduled full SCIM re-sync for affected user set (completed 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC). Approval queue routing now returning to normal; monitored for 24 hours. Post-incident action: add attribute-rename detection and automated compatibility layer to SCIM consumer, plus update runbook to require identity-team change advisory for attribute key renames.
Follow-ups: (1) implement attribute aliasing in the mapping service (PR opened), (2) add schema-change webhook from IdP to alert on renamed keys, (3) update oncall-runbook to include manual-assign steps.
2026-03-11T10:05Z - Maya Patel (reporter): Noticed a backlog in the approval queue after the IdP change window. Opening ticket and tagging identity team.
2026-03-11T10:32Z - Sean Riley (identity): We pushed an attribute rename earlier; did not realize SCIM consumer had strict key checks. Investigating possible fast rollback or compatibility fix.
2026-03-11T12:35Z - Luke Moreno (assignee): Deployed temporary translation to identity-cache mapping. Confirmed partial recovery for queued requests. Scheduling full re-sync for remaining accounts.
2026-03-11T14:10Z - Oncall SRE (ops-team): Manual approvals processed where hotfix didn't catch; customers notified via #oncall and #support bridging channel.
2026-03-12T05:20Z - Luke Moreno: Full SCIM re-sync run completed. Monitoring metrics for routing success; error rate for delegated lookup dropped from 42% -> 1.2% in prod-us-east.
2026-03-12T09:00Z - Maya Patel: Closing out immediate operational impact; leaving follow-ups assigned to identity and platform teams.
payload.summary: Dept attribute rename in IdP causes approval queue to lose delegated-group mapping for oncall runbooks

Issue summary: Support operations have introduced three new SLO buckets for internal SLA measurement (P0-P2 incident routing windows). The support routing scripts (route-decider) and the analytics ingestion pipeline (support-metrics-collector) are not yet aligned to emit the new SLO labels, resulting in missing SLO flags in internal dashboards and automated runbooks. Impact: On-call and triage tooling continue to show legacy SLO groupings which causes incorrect escalation windows and missing automated snoozes for long-running support work. This increases cognitive load for L2/L3 engineers and delays time-to-first-action. Scope: Affects routing decisions and SLO reporting for internal-support issues created after 2026-03-04 in prod us-east. Not customer-facing directly but affects SLA metering and internal paging. Goal: Update routing scripts to apply new slo_bucket tags at creation time, instrument analytics pipeline to accept and persist slo_bucket, and add nightly backfill job for issues created since 2026-03-04.
1) Create a new internal-support ticket with priority P1 in prod us-east using the internal-support UI or API. 2) Observe ticket metadata in routing-engine logs: the slo_bucket field is absent or set to legacy value. 3) Check support-metrics-collector ingestion logs: no datapoint recorded for slo_bucket dimension. 4) Open Support SLO dashboard: ticket count by slo_bucket does not reflect recent issues.
route-decider logs: s3://redwood-logs/routing/2026/03/11/route-decider-us-east.log.gz (matches missing slo_bucket for events 11:00-13:00 UTC). Analytics ingestion error trace: support-metrics-collector stderr (k8s pod collector-7d9f) referencing schema mismatch for field 'slo_bucket' (schema_v3 -> expected). Example event id: evt-0a9f3b2c. Query used for dashboard: SELECT count(*) FROM support_events WHERE slo_bucket IS NOT NULL GROUP BY slo_bucket.
Initial hypothesis: schema rollout for support-metrics-collector (v3) was deployed on 2026-03-04 but route-decider remained on v2 tagging. Confirmed by correlating deploy tags: route-decider image: support/route-decider:2026-02-28 (no slo_bucket field), support-metrics-collector image: support/metrics-collector:2026-03-03 (schema_v3). Secondary finding: routing-engine template library contains conditional that wrote 'slo' instead of 'slo_bucket' for internal tickets created via API shortcut. Affected code paths: quick-create API and the webhook handler for infra alerts.
Manual enrichment: run the enrichment script tools/enrich-slo-bucket.py against affected tickets (backfill). For new events, an ad-hoc K8s sidecar can emit slo_bucket as a temporary shim (patch applied to support-api deployment). Both are temporary and operationally heavy.
1) Patch route-decider to include slo_bucket mapping and release v2026-03-15. 2) Update routing templates used by quick-create API to set slo_bucket correctly. 3) Add compatibility layer in support-metrics-collector to accept both 'slo' and 'slo_bucket' keys for one release window. 4) Implement nightly backfill job (lambda or k8s CronJob) to reprocess tickets since 2026-03-04. 5) Add unit and e2e tests to pipeline for schema evolution.
- Stage: patch route-decider in staging and run integration tests (2026-03-12). - Canary: deploy to 10% of prod us-east traffic and validate slo_bucket presence in logs (2026-03-15). - Full rollout: 2026-03-16 after 24h canary validation. - Deploy compatibility patch to metrics-collector in parallel. - Enable nightly backfill during low-traffic window (03:00 UTC) on 2026-03-17.
If new tagging causes unexpected routing churn: revert route-decider to previous image and disable quick-create changes. Compatibility in metrics-collector ensures dashboards remain stable. Backfill job is idempotent and safe to abort.
- Risk of mismatched tags causing duplicate escalations if route-decider and escalation service interpret tags differently. - Backfill may produce spike in metrics ingestion; we must throttle writes and monitor ingestion lag. - Potentially missed tickets created before 2026-03-04 if older schema variants exist.
1) Add integration test that simulates hot-path quick-create API and verifies slo_bucket propagation. 2) Update runbooks to reference new SLO buckets and update paging windows. 3) Schedule a post-deploy audit of SLO counts versus backlog (endpoint: /support/slo-audit). 4) Retro note to internal-support on lessons learned.
payload.summary: SLO flagging: update routing scripts and analytics pipeline for new support SLO buckets

payload.description:
Issue summary: After a routine IdP metadata update at customer identity provider (partner IdP), a subset of internal users report successful console login but do not receive any RBAC roles (403 when accessing modelobservability and runbook tools). Impact: Blocks developers and oncall engineers from running elevated commands and accessing dashboards. Incident first observed ~2026-03-10 09:12 UTC for ~12 users across multiple teams.

Observed behavior: Authentication (SAML/OIDC handshake) completes and session cookie is issued. Console shows "Signed in" but requests for protected pages return 403. The user session contains an authenticated subject but roles claim is empty.

Expected behavior: Roles derived from group claims in the IdP assertion are populated and RBAC grants appropriate permissions.

Affected scope: ~12 users (internal), intermittent pattern depending on which upstream SP/IdP connector the user hit; primarily users whose Okta profiles contain a new attribute named `x-org-attributes` which is a JSON blob (array) rather than the flat list of group DNs our claim parser expects.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use Okta account with `x-org-attributes` set to a JSON array string (example payload attached).
2) SSO to console via SAML redirect flow.

Issue summary:
  SLA cohort labels that drive routing policies have drifted between the routing-engine config and the reporting/alerts pipeline. As a result: some P1 customer tickets are being routed to the wrong escalation path and SLO dashboards show inaccurate cohort-level breach counts.

Impact:
  - Incorrectly attributed escalations for ~8 customers in prod (noted in Support Slack #support).
  - Daily SLO rollup for SLA cohorts shows 12% fewer breaches for the last 48 hours in the analytics dashboard compared to raw event count.
  - Potential missed followups by on-call for high-priority customers.

Observed behavior:
  - Routing-engine picks cohort "enterprise-c" for requests with tag "ent-c-eu". Reporting pipeline and alerts read the same tag as "enterprise-c-eu" and map it to cohort "enterprise-ce". This mismatch means alerts and routing use different cohort identifiers.

Expected behavior:
  - Cohort tag -> routing cohort mapping should be identical across routing-engine, reporting pipeline, and support tooling templates.

Additional context:
  - Noticed after a config push on 2026-02-19 that updated cohort template parsing (author: infra-config-bot).
  - Affected customers are on dedicated and private tiers; some are on eu-west region.

Steps to reproduce:
  1) In prod-us-east, send synthetic support request with metadata tag: "ent-c-eu".
  2) Observe routing decision in routing-engine logs: routing decision shows cohort "enterprise-c".
  3) Search ingestion pipeline (analytics) for the same request id; reporting ingestion emits cohort "enterprise-ce".
  4) Reconcile the two outputs in the support-escalation service logs to see different cohort keys.

1) Generate a test ticket with metadata tag 'ent-c-eu' in prod-us-east. 2) tail routing-engine logs for the request id. 3) query reporting ingestion topic for same request id. 4) compare cohort mapping fields 'routing_cohort' vs 'reporting_cohort'.

Hypothesis: a partial rollout of the cohort-normalizer lib (support-tooling v1.4.0) changed canonical keys but the routing-engine was not redeployed or its config not backfilled.
Logs (redacted):
```
2026-02-20T09:07:14Z routing-engine INFO request=rc_1234 cohort=enterprise-c decision=route:escalation-team-c
2026-02-20T09:07:14Z reporting-ingest INFO request=rc_1234 tag=ent-c-eu cohort=enterprise-ce
```

Issue summary: Following depot repair and battery replacement, a subset of returned laptops enter a provisioning failure state during Autopilot/Intune enrollment. Devices repeatedly fail device attestation and drop into BitLocker recovery or are marked noncompliant, blocking automated post-provisioning tasks.

Impact: 18 devices in the NY depot cohort; customers' engineers and SREs experienced delays in replacing hardware and reprovisioning. Automated fleet reimage pipeline blocked for affected serial batches.

Environment: Production autopilot flow, us-east, affected builds include latest corporate image (2026-02-15), devices repaired at vendor depot (third-party).
1) Receive device from depot after NVMe swap / RTC battery replacement.
2) Boot to OOBE / Autopilot flow with company network (corp-wifi with DHCP).
3) Device attempts Autopilot + Intune attestation.
4) Observe attestation failure, event ID 1001 in provisioning logs and Windows falls back to local account or BitLocker recovery.

Repro rate: ~90% for devices repaired during 2026-03-05 – 2026-03-08 depot batch.
[ProvisioningAgent] 2026-03-10T09:12:03Z ERROR Attestation failed: time-drift-exceeds-threshold (delta=372s)
[WinSVC] 2026-03-10T09:12:04Z WARN TimeService not synchronized, NtpClient returned error 0x80072ee7
[Intune] 2026-03-10T09:12:05Z INFO Device attestation rejected - TPM PCR time structure mismatch
[BitLocker] 2026-03-10T09:12:10Z CRITICAL Recovery triggered: PCR0 mismatch
DHCP lease details: option 42 not set; network NTP server missing
Initial triage (2026-03-10): Support confirmed correlation with depot repairs (same vendor batch). Devices showed RTC drift of several minutes on first boot. BIOS reported hardware clock behind wall time.

Hypothesis 1: Depot replacement procedure omitted re-sync of firmware RTC after battery install, leaving CMOS clock skewed. This causes measured PCR values tied to system boot time to diverge from expected values during Azure/Intune attestation.

Hypothesis 2: Corporate network DHCP scope removed option 42 (NTP) briefly on 2026-03-05 due to DHCP server config change; combined with disabled Windows Time Service (policy conflict from a scheduled baseline) devices could not auto-correct clock before attestation step.

Data points: Serial range affected: 7D0A0000 - 7D0A0111. Timedatectl on a repro device showed RTC=2026-03-05T02:01:12 whereas wallclock=2026-03-10T09:20:00. Depot image logs show battery replacement ticket IDs. Linked to INT-9276 (previous RTC attestation investigation).

Temporary mitigation tested: manual time sync via admin network console (w32tm /resync) allows attestation to succeed and provisioning continues. Verified on 3 devices.

Root cause: Combination of depot RTC left unsynced after battery swap and a transient removal of DHCP NTP option in corp network prevented automatic correction prior to attestation window. TPM PCRs used by attestation include time-related measurements causing the mismatch.
Support (Jordan Lee) 2026-03-10: Customer-facing depot reported 12 returns failing autopilot. Collected serials, repro’d one device in office lab.
Depot Tech (Marta Gomez) 2026-03-10: Confirmed RTC battery replaced on all serials in batch; repair checklist item 'sync RTC' not ticked for these tickets.
SRE (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-11: Observed DHCP config change on 2026-03-05 removing option 42 during maintenance window — reverted. Correlated with affected serial range.
Action: re-enable DHCP option 42 and confirm NTP service reachable from corp network.
Engineering (Priya Kapoor) 2026-03-11: Provisioning agent updated to add a pre-attestation NTP check and an NTP resync attempt (w32tm /config /syncfromflags:manual) before starting attestation flow. PR linked.
Support (Jordan Lee) 2026-03-12: Verified fix on 18 affected devices; all progressed past attestation and completed autopilot successfully.
Workaround applied: Depot instructed to run 'timedatectl set-ntp true && timedatectl set-timezone UTC' and connect repaired units to a staging network with reachable NTP prior to sealing. In prod: DHCP option 42 restored and monitoring alert added to detect missing NTP servers.

Permanent fixes: 1) Provisioning agent change merged and rolled (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning-agent/pull/472) to perform NTP sanity check and force a one-time resync before attestation. 2) Depot SOP updated to include an RTC resync step and checklist enforcement. 3) Fleet health dashboard updated to surface devices reporting time skew > 60s.

Postmortem actions: create a short runbook for 'attestation-time-skew' (confluence page created). Outreach: notified depot vendor and internal procurement for process compliance. Ticket closed after verification on 2026-03-12.
SOP: Depot RTC resync step added (owner: Depot Ops)
Monitoring: Alert for DHCP option 42 removal (owner: SRE)
Engineering: Backfill unit tests for pre-attestation time sync (owner: Provisioning Team)
payload.summary: Post-repair clock skew causing Intune device attestation failures and provisioning stalls

Issue summary:
Several release pipelines in prod became stuck in 'Pending - Waiting for runner' after the scheduled runner token rotation. New ephemeral runners register successfully but are immediately rejected by the CI scheduler because the runner label validation path rejects normalized labels when tokens include a legacy prefix.

Impact:
- Multiple release pipelines (build+e2e) blocked for the last ~2 hours, affecting two teams.
- Customer-facing deploys delayed; one internal canary was missed.

Environment:
- Prod CI cluster (us-east-1) using ephemeral GitHub Actions runners managed by runner-provisioner service.
- Secrets rotation completed at 2026-03-12T01:15:00Z via vault-rotation job.

Steps to reproduce (observed on prod):
1) Trigger typical release pipeline that requests runner with label 'release/canary-v2'.
2) Runner-provisioner spins up ephemeral instance and registers runner with token that contains rotated prefix 'rk_'.
3) CI scheduler performs label sanity-check and calls normalization routine. The routine checks token metadata and applies a legacy-path branch which strips slashes incorrectly producing 'release-canary-v2'.
4) Scheduler rejects runner because configured pool expects 'release/canary-v2' labels. Job stays pending.

Observed behavior:
- Runners show as active in provisioner logs but in CI scheduler metrics they are 'rejected_label_mismatch'.
- No 5xx errors from provisioner, but scheduler enqueues jobs without assignment.

Expected behavior:
- Normalization should preserve label separators or perform canonical mapping consistent with pool config. New runners should be accepted and assigned to pending jobs.

Immediate workaround tried:
- Manual re-assign of pending jobs to a healthy pool (manual override) — allowed one deploy to proceed.
- Rolled back runner token prefix normalization in a staging branch for testing (did not roll out to prod).

Logs & traces:
- Provisioner logs: /var/log/runner-provisioner/2026-03-12.log entries show successful registration events with token_meta: "rk_20260312_...".
- Scheduler logs (grep): "rejected_label_mismatch: runner_id=eu-3281 token_meta=rk_20260312".
- Kibana dashboard: https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/discover#/doc/ci-scheduler-logs/_search?query=rejected_label_mismatch

Notes on scope:
- Only pools that rely on exact slash-delimited label matching are affected (release/* pools). Other generic pools accept runners as expected.

Hypothesis 1: the vault rotation changed token format which triggers a legacy branch in label normalization (token_meta string contains underscore 'rk_' leading to fallback).
Hypothesis 2: recent change in runner-provisioner (infra PR 4218) added token metadata parsing that interacts with scheduler normalization.
Quick checks performed:
- Verified token strings in provisioner logs (confirmed 'rk_' prefix).
- Replayed normalization routine locally with sample token_meta: produced 'release-canary-v2' (slash removed).
- Reviewed PR 4218 — added token parsing but did not change label transformation; however, scheduler's normalization code (ci/scheduler) recently got a small refactor in PR 1192 that tightened validation.
Next steps in investigation:
- Add additional logging in scheduler label-normalizer to capture incoming runner labels and normalized output (temporary prod debug flag).
- Coordinate with infra on token rotation format to see if rotation job can emit compatibility header.
- Validate backlog of pending jobs and count how many can be assigned to alternative pools.

Additional notes:
Fixed in prod by patching scheduler label-normalizer (ci/scheduler PR 1198) to canonicalize labels deterministically regardless of token_meta format. Hotfix acceptance tolerance was removed after verification. Backfilled 9 queued jobs via normal assignment. Added compatibility header to vault rotation output (infra PR 4223).
Add integration test for token metadata + label normalization (CI test suite)
Alert on rejected_label_mismatch rate > 5/min
Update runner-provisioner docs to document token metadata formats
Schedule retro with infra and release-eng to coordinate future rotations
payload.summary: Pipeline jobs stuck pending: runner provisioning label sanity-check rejects newly rotated runner tokens

Impact: on-call unable to acknowledge alerts during a paging window. Scope: single contractor account provisioned this morning via automated SCIM job.

Observed behavior: After successful Okta authentication, the application receives the user attributes but the RBAC service rejects the role claim and the session terminates. The UI shows 'SSO error: invalid role payload' and an HTTP 401 is recorded in the auth gateway logs.

Issue summary:
Several newly provisioned Dell XPS 13 (9310) units in the corp provisioning lab fail to resume from hibernate (S4). Machines appear to power on (fans/charging LED) but the display remains black and user input is unresponsive. After ~30–90s some devices show recurring Network driver resets and kernel/driver rebind logs, which correlate with the black screen condition.

Impact:
- Blocks completion of automated provisioning validation (image QA jobs) for affected XPS devices.
- Prevents new devices from being handed off to employees until a manual power-cycle and driver rollback are applied.
- Affects ~6 of 24 test devices in the lab; intermittent across firmware revisions.

Environment:
- Image: windows-image-2026-03 (corporate build, Win11 23H2-based)
- Lab: corp-provisioning-lab, us-west rack A3
- Device model: Dell XPS 13 9310 (i7, Intel Ethernet via USB-C adapter on test bench)
- Drivers: Intel Ethernet driver package intel-net-26.3.0.1 (shipped in image), Dell BIOS 1.14.0

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Flash windows-image-2026-03 to XPS 9310 test unit via provisioning rig.
2) Apply corporate policies and restart; initiate hibernate (S4) via powercfg /hibernate on + shutdown /h.
3) Resume via power button.
4) System fans spin, charging LED on, but display stays black and no input accepted.
5) Watch provisioning rig console: repeated EventLog entries where e1qexpress (Intel) reports "Device Reset/Link lost" then driver rebind attempts.

Logs & artifacts:
- Collected full WindowsEvent log extract (attached in imaging artifacts folder): Event IDs 7026, 219, and repeated kernel-driver unload/load timestamps clustered at resume time.
- Photos of external console showing black screen and probe outputs available in /shared/internal-support/INT-714159/artifacts.
- Live kernel-mode dump captured on one unit (small memory dump) and uploaded to imaging bucket.

Notes on reproducibility:
- Issue is intermittent but reliably triggered on some firmware/driver combos. Not all XPS 9310 units repro. Units that were updated to BIOS 1.14.0 + intel-net-26.3.0.1 show higher frequency.

Immediate impact classification: workstation provisioning blocker for a subset of XPS models in lab.
Initial hypotheses:
- Power-management interaction between Intel Ethernet driver and Windows resume path causing a DPC/block that prevents graphics driver init.
- Race between USB-C/Thunderbolt controller resume and display driver initialization on these units.

Actions taken so far:
- Reproduced on 6/24 lab units. Captured event logs and small memory dump.
- Rolled back intel-net driver to intel-net-25.8.0.0 on one repro unit: resume succeeded and no black screen observed across 5 repeated tests.
- Swapped to Dell BIOS 1.13.2 on one unit: repro rate dropped significantly.
- Verified not related to BitLocker (BitLocker not yet enabled during image validation).
- Eng (kernel/drivers team) performed static analysis of dump; noted blocked worker thread waiting on NIC driver completion during init.

Open questions:
- Is the issue specific to the intel-net 26.3.0.1 package we recently added to image?
- Are the USB-C NICs being enumerated as late devices causing display init to stall?

Data points & links:
- Imaging CI job logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/imaging/1234 (last failing run attached)
- Dump and log bundle: s3://redwood-internal/INT-714159/dumps.zip
- See linked: INT-41256 (wake-from-lid issues) which had a similar driver / resume pattern.
Workaround (short-term):
- For staging/provisioning lab: pin intel-net driver to intel-net-25.8.0.0 in the imaging package. Update provisioning rig orchestration to apply driver rollback step when model == XPS_9310 until a formal fix is released.
- Instruct bench techs to perform a full AC disconnect + power-button hold (10s) as a manual recovery for units in the field.

Planned permanent fix:
- Drivers team to produce a patched intel-net package that defers certain power-management completion paths on resume (PR referenced below).
- Imaging to build a new windows-image-2026-03.1 with the patched driver + optional suspend/resume stress test in CI.
- Coordinate with Dell to validate BIOS behavior; if required, mark older BIOS 1.13.2 as recommended for provisioning until firmware fix is available.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Drivers team to ship a candidate driver and open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/drivers/pull/1034 (in progress).
- Imaging to run full lab validation and confirm fix by 2026-03-17.
- Create advisory for bench SOP: "If XPS 9310 fails resume, apply driver rollback and escalate to imaging team".

Status: In Progress — workaround in place in provisioning lab; pending driver patch and image rebuild.

Issue summary:
We have a contractor (email: aisha.oliver@redwood.ai) who is converting to a full-time engineer effective 2026-03-15. She currently has a contractor LDAP profile (contractor/aoliver) and a short-lived service account used for a shared GPU lab. HR requests a clean merge into the new full-time employee identity (employees/aoliver) rather than creating a brand new separate employee identity to preserve project history and reduce breakage in historical Git commits and CodeSearch links.

Background / why this is tricky:
- Contractor account was used to provision access to several Git repos (private infra repos), GCP service bindings, and a shared Dedicated cluster namespace.
- The contractor laptop (asset tag RWI-55431) was issued under the contractor profile and currently has disk encryption tied to the contractor's SSO MFA device and KMS key reference.
- Security wants to avoid key reuse across identities and prefers rekeying and reprovisioning for full-time hires. Hardware/Workplace Ops would like to reuse reimaged laptops for new hires when policy permits. HR prefers retaining commit history and internal ticket links under a single identity if possible.

Impact:
- Delaying access transition will block Aisha from completing her first-week tasks if full access is not granted by 2026-03-15.
- Aggressive merge without rekeying risks token/secret exposure between contractor-scoped resources and employee-scoped ones.

Requested outcome / acceptance criteria:
1) Contractor LDAP profile merged into employees/aoliver with preserved email alias and commit history updated (if needed) with minimal disruption to repo ACLs.
2) Asset RWI-55431 handback scheduled on 2026-03-16 for reprovisioning. Device must be reimaged and have disk encryption rekeyed to the new employee identity and KMS policy.
3) Update IAM bindings and service account ownership where contractor@example-service-account was used; introduce employee-scoped service accounts where appropriate and rotate keys.
4) Document the change in HR onboarding ticket and link to audit log entries.

Steps taken so far / preliminary investigation:
- HR (Jordan Kim) approved preserving commit history and requested the merge.
- SRE (initial investigator) listed affected repos via gitshortlog and found 8 private repos where contractor is the primary committer.
- Security (Priya Desai) flagged that the laptop encryption references contractor's MFA device; recommends rekeying rather than reusing disk keys.

Proposed plan (low-disruption):
A) Pre-merge tasks (by 2026-03-14):
   - Create employee identity employees/aoliver and add email alias aisha.oliver@redwood.ai. (Identity team)
   - Generate mapping plan for Git authorship preservation (git-filter-repo plan) with a read-only mirror to validate. (DevTools)
   - List service accounts and secrets tied to contractor profile. (Infra/SRE)
B) Cutover (scheduled for 2026-03-15 09:00 PT):

   - Run Git author rewrite on mirrors; after validation, apply to primary repos during a low-traffic window.

C) Device handback (2026-03-16):
   - Aisha returns asset RWI-55431 to Workplace Ops. Device is wiped and reimaged using corporate image; disk encryption rekeyed to employees/aoliver KMS key.
   - MDM re-enroll with new SSO MFA binding and new device certs.
D) Post-cutover validation (by 2026-03-17):
   - Verify CI/CD pipelines and scheduled tasks still run and are not tied to the contractor's service account.
   - Confirm audit log entries for merges and key rotations are present.

Outstanding questions / policy decision required:
1) Is a full git history rewrite acceptable for these repos, or do we prefer to preserve history via commit-author mapping without rewriting history? (security / devtools tradeoff)
2) Can Workplace Ops reuse a reimaged device for other hires in the same region after rekeying, or does policy require Hardware Escrow for 6 months? (policy clarification requested from Security & Legal)
3) Are there any billing/entitlement implications when preserving an alias between contractor and employee identities?

Additional notes:

Service account audit shows usage by CI job 'gpu-lab-runner' — scheduled rotation required and update to CI config to use new employee service account.
No active outstanding incidents found in past 90 days tied to contractor service accounts.
