Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 08:40 PST a subset of clients in the San Francisco office intermittently lose connectivity to internal services. Symptoms look like Wi‑Fi drops followed by failure to re-establish the WireGuard tunnel (zero-trust agent), which requires a manual restart of the agent to recover. Impact: ~12 users across two APs (floor 3) experienced repeated disconnects during the morning standup. Affected services: internal git, slack VPN-resolved flows, access to k8s API. Scope: office employees on macOS and Linux laptops using the corporate-ssid.

Impact: Internal productivity hit for on-site engineers; no customer-facing services affected. Outage window observed: 08:40–11:30 PST.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect company laptop to corporate-ssid at SF office APs SF-AP-23 / SF-AP-24.
2) Authenticate via 802.1X (Okta SAML -> RADIUS/EAP-TTLS).
3) Observe periodic deauths in system logs and zero-trust agent reporting 'interface down' and failing to resume WireGuard session.
4) Manual workaround: restart zero-trust agent or toggle Wi‑Fi to force reauth – this temporarily restores connectivity for the session.

Observed logs and evidence:
- AP syslog (SF-AP-23) around 08:43: "MFP policy mismatch: client RSN IE does not indicate MFP capability; rejecting management frame encryption negotiation; deauth/disassoc flood starting".
- wpa_supplicant (macOS/Linux) snippets: "supplicant: received deauth - reason 15, RSN: MFP required by AP but not supported by driver".
- Zero-trust agent (wireguard) logs: "wg0: interface went down due to link loss; handshake failed after reauth; route table entries flushed".
- Packet capture near AP: retransmitted deauth/disassoc frames, RSN IE mismatch visible in beacon and association response frames.
- AP controller shows recent configuration push at 03:00 UTC: SSID 'corporate-ssid' MFP policy set to 'required' as part of a security hardening roll (change-id cf-2026-03-13-03).

Initial hypothesis: Recent wireless baseline hardening set 802.11w (Management Frame Protection) to 'required' for corporate-ssid; some clients/drivers (older macOS kernel modules, older Linux Wi-Fi drivers, and our zero-trust onboarding images) do not advertise MFP capability properly leading to association but failing protected management frame negotiation, resulting in frequent deauths. When the client temporarily rejoins, the zero-trust agent's interface down event causes routing flush which WireGuard's automatic handshake does not recover from until agent restart.
Timeline:
- 08:45: CSI alerted from #internal-it Slack about multiple disconnected users on floor 3.
- 09:00: Collected AP syslogs and client logs from affected users (macOS 12.6.7 and Ubuntu 22.04 kernels). Observed consistent RSN IE differences.
- 09:20: Correlated with a controller change: config push cf-2026-03-13-03 set 'MFP: required' on corporate-ssid. This was part of a security sprint (PR: github.com/redwood/infra-config/pull/512).
- 09:35: Reproduced locally with a test Linux laptop: toggling MFP policy on AP between 'required' and 'optional' changed client behavior; 'required' triggered deauth storms on certain drivers.
- 10:10: Confirmed that zero-trust agent (wireguard) does not always gracefully recover route entries after multiple rapid link flaps; handshake stalls and session keys are not re-established until agent restart.

Hypotheses tested:
- MFP requirement causes client not to support protected management frames -> repeated deauths. Supported by packet captures and client RSN IE.
- Zero-trust agent's reconnection logic does not handle rapid link churn -> requires manual restart. Reproduced by simulated flaps.

Mitigation attempts:
- Temporarily set MFP policy to 'optional' for SF AP group (SF-AP-23/24) at 10:50 to stop deauth storms. Immediate decrease in incidents observed.
- Eng SRE pushed zero-trust agent update to improve reconnect logic (edge fix) on a test host but full rollout postponed pending QA.
Priya Raman (Reporter) 2026-03-13 09:02: Noticed 3-4 folks on floor 3 reporting repeated disconnects. Collected client logs. Adding AP controller team.
Janelle (Network Eng) 2026-03-13 09:18: Found recent config change cf-2026-03-13-03 setting MFP required. Rolling back MFP to optional for SF AP group to test impact.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee) 2026-03-13 10:55: Rolled MFP to optional for SF-AP-23/24. Immediate drop in deauth events. Will monitor for 2 hours.
SRE (Marco) 2026-03-13 11:30: Observed wireguard hang reproduction on test host after repeated link flaps. Created stub PR to add a hard restart/backoff in reconnect logic (github.com/redwood/wireguard-agent/pull/78).
Liam O'Connor 2026-03-14 09:15: Confirmed rollout plan: AP controller firmware/config baseline to set MFP to 'optional' until client fleet updated. Scheduled agent rollouts for next week. Marking Incident resolved after config change and monitoring window.
Security (Priya K) 2026-03-14 12:04: Noted that MFP requirement was a security hardening ask. Approving temporary relaxation with plan to re-enable once clients updated and agent fix shipped.
Temporary rollback: MFP policy changed from 'required' -> 'optional' on SF AP group (SF-AP-23/24) at 2026-03-13 10:50 PST which stopped deauth storm. Long-term fix: (1) Deploy zero-trust agent update v2.8.0 with improved reconnect/backoff and MFP capability reporting (PR #78) – rollout planned 2026-03-17. (2) Push AP firmware 7.2.1 and updated controller profile that allows 'optional' MFP with compatibility mode and clear rollout tests. Change window for re-enablement of 'required' MFP will be scheduled after fleet verification. Incident closed after 24h stable monitoring on 2026-03-14.
Roll out wireguard-agent v2.8.0 to all endpoint images (tracking: infra-deploy ticket INT-935102)
AP controller firmware update to 7.2.1 and new SSID profile that negotiates MFP compat mode (change request CR-2026-03-20)
Add monitoring alert: spike in deauth/disassoc events per AP -> auto-create incident (alerts #net-deauth-spike)
Document compatibility matrix for MFP in internal runbook (confluence: /network/runbooks/mfp-compatibility)
Security review to sign off on re-enabling 'required' MFP once 95% of endpoints have updated agent/driver support
payload.summary: 802.11w/MFP policy mismatch causes deauth storms and breaks zero-trust (WireGuard) reconnects in SF office

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We need a production-ready 'claim-broker' service that lets internal teams request and claim a pre-approved Slack namespace (channel prefix + template) with timebound access. When a claim is approved, the system should provision a Confluence space seeded with the team's templates, attach a Jira project stub (optional), and emit audit snapshots to S3 for compliance.

Impact:
- Faster pod onboarding (goal: reduce manual provisioning by 70%).
- Keeps access timebound to reduce lingering privileges.
- Provides audit trail for security/compliance.

Requirements / Acceptance criteria:
1) Self-service portal (web form or Slack modal) for claim requests with reason, owner, TTL (default 90 days).
2) Approval webhook to designated approver group; approvals must be recorded in Jira as a compact audit entry.
3) On approval: create Slack channel namespace and invite owner/service-accounts with ephemeral membership (SCIM/Okta integration preferred).
4) Seed a Confluence space with team templates and initial 'runbook' page; permissions mirror team owners.
5) Emit a signed audit snapshot (JSON + SHA256) to S3 and create a retention policy entry.
6) Provide a 'renew' and 'relinquish' flow handling TTL extension and proactive expiry notifications.
7) Configurable guardrails: deny if sensitive data tag present, require security review for vendor-facing namespaces.

Environment:
prod (primary), staging for initial rollout; target regions: us-west, eu-west.

Steps to validate in staging:
1) Open Slack modal via /claim-namespace (staging bot) and submit sample request for "team-signal" prefix.
2) Approver in group 'pod-admins' receives Slack approval DM and web console notification.
3) Approve request; verify Slack namespace created with proper naming and default channels (#team-signal-general, #team-signal-ops).
4) Confirm Confluence space created at /spaces/TEAM-SIGNAL with seeded runbook page.
5) Check S3 bucket s3://redwood-internal-audits/claims/ for audit snapshot and SHA256 file.
6) Trigger TTL expiry simulation and confirm notification flow to owners and automated archival proposal.

Observed errors / logs (staging):
- 2026-03-04T15:12:02Z ERROR claim-broker.lambda create_confluence_space 403 Forbidden: API key rejected (service-account lacking 'space:create').
- 2026-03-04T15:12:05Z WARN claim-broker.lambda invite_scim Okta throttling: 429 (retry-after: 30s).
- Sample webhook payload (redacted): {
  "request_id": "cb-20260304-7f3a",
  "prefix": "team-signal",
  "owner": "m.chen@redwood.ai",
  "ttl_days": 90
}

Notes: scope of work intentionally excludes full SSO integration for external partners — that will be follow-up.

Additional notes:
2026-03-07 - DevSecOps (Security reviewer): Security review required for the seeding templates. Any template with 'vendor' tag triggers manual security sign-off. Also request that audit snapshots be immutably stored with Object Lock (where available).
2026-03-08 - SRE: Noted potential concurrency issue when many claims are approved concurrently; recommend using a queue (SQS) and idempotency token to prevent double-provisioning.
SCIM vs Okta group invites: SCIM has faster invite flow but requires Okta provisioning setup; alternative is using Slack admin invite API with fallback to manual invites.
Confluence API requires 'site-admin' service account for space creation. We need to scope that account and rotate keys monthly.
Audit snapshot format: JSON with metadata (request_id, approver_id, timestamps), resources created, and a SHA256 signature; retention 7 years for enterprise customers. Need to consult Legal for retention policy variance.
Rate limiting observed in staging when creating >10 spaces in short interval (429 from Confluence). Plan: exponential backoff + per-region rate buckets.
Planned rollout path: 1) PoC hardening in staging (1 week): fix service-account scopes, add idempotency tokens, implement SQS queue. 2) Security gating (3 days): template review and Legal sign-off on retention. 3) Canary in prod (us-west) with 3 pilot pods (2 weeks monitoring). 4) Global rollout and automation docs + runbook (follow-up ticket for partner SSO).
Action items created:
- infra: provision s3://redwood-internal-audits/claims + KMS CMK (owner: infra-team).
- auth: create rotated Confluence service account with just-in-time elevation (owner: auth).
- dev: implement queueing and idempotency (owner: automation team).
- sec: review templates and approve vendor gating (owner: DevSecOps).
Post-deployment follow-ups: add fine-grained reporting to Console, add renewal email cadence, and schedule quarterly audit of claimed namespaces. Target full prod rollout by 2026-04-16.
payload.summary: Deploy 'claim-broker' flow: delegated Slack namespace claim + timebound access + Confluence project seeding

Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 at ~03:40 UTC automated anomaly detection flagged a surge of admin-scoped API requests originating from a freshly onboarded vendor OAuth app. The app had been granted only 'read:user' and 'email' scopes during onboarding, but tokens observed in logs were accepted for admin-level endpoints.

Issue summary: GreenPlan (dedicated customer) reports intermittent model unpinning for tenant 'greenplan-prod' during a scheduled canary that uses an SLO-driven throttle. The unpinning results in traffic falling back to an older, higher-latency variant and occasional 5xx error bursts.

Impact: Multiple customer-facing endpoints serving critical analytics pipelines see increased 95th and 99th percentile latencies and ~1.8% error rate spike for 20-40 minute windows during canary throttle events. Business impact: delayed reports and one customer SLA alert triggered.

Environment: production (us-east), tenant: greenplan-prod, dedicated pool id: dp-42, canary config: weight 5%, SLO throttle enabled (latency target 250ms).

Observed behavior: During an autoscaler-triggered SLO throttle (latency breach), orchestrator moves a subset of canary cohort to a protected low-throughput bucket. Shortly after, edge logs show session affinity tokens for the tenant are removed or replaced and requests are routed to an older variant (llama2-13b-redwood-v1) instead of the pinned quantized variant. Some requests then time out and return 5xx.

Expected behavior: SLO-driven throttling should reduce throughput but preserve tenant-level model pinning and not evict affinity leases. Fallback routing should only occur after explicit model health or capacity signals, not as a side-effect of throttle-induced cohort migration.

Steps to reproduce: see steps_to_reproduce field.

Attachments: partial logs, sample request IDs, control-plane snapshot links included below.
1) On prod us-east, schedule a canary rollout for model llama2-13b-quantized-v1 with weight 5% and SLO enforcement on latency target 250ms.
2) Generate load that increases tail latency above the SLO (synthetic traffic at 1.5x peak for 10-20 minutes).
3) Observe orchestrator perform SLO throttle and shift canary cohort into low-throughput bucket; monitor control-plane snapshots for dp-42 cohort placement.
4) Inspect edge-proxy logs for tenant greenplan-prod session affinity token churn and routing decisions for the same session IDs (should see variant flip to llama2-13b-redwood-v1).
5) Verify downstream responses: increased latency and occasional 5xx errors for affected requests.
2026-03-12T14:17:03Z request_id=8b2f3a cid=greenplan-prod cohort=canary slot=low_throughput edge_token=abc123 action=route model=llama2-13b-redwood-v1
2026-03-12T14:17:04Z request_id=8b2f3a controlplane: cohort-migrate tenant=greenplan-prod from=normal to=low_throughput reason=SLO_THROTTLE
2026-03-12T14:17:04Z request_id=8b2f3a edge: affinity-lease-evict tenant=greenplan-prod token=abc123 cause=cohort-resync
2026-03-12T14:18:01Z request_id=c1d9ff cid=greenplan-prod model=llama2-13b-redwood-v1 response_status=502 latency_ms=312
2026-03-12T14:22:12Z controlplane snapshot: dp-42 cohort assignments: tenant=greenplan-prod -> low_throughput bucket (5 nodes)

2026-03-12 15:00 — Support (Maya): validated customer timeline and collected request IDs and control-plane snapshot references.
2026-03-12 15:30 — SRE (Diego): reproduced cohort migration by triggering SLO throttle in staging and observed edge affinity eviction during orchestrator snapshot apply.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 17:05 — Observed that fallback routing policy treats low_throughput bucket as incompatible with quantized runtime (quantized variant not prewarmed in low_throughput), so routing falls back to older non-quantized variant.
2026-03-12 17:40 — Preliminary root-cause candidate: combined effect of (1) affinity eviction during orchestrator cohort resync, and (2) bucket-level runtime mismatch causing automatic model-variant fallback.
Applied temporary tenant-level static pin via control-plane override (force model=llama2-13b-quantized-v1 for greenplan-prod) and disabled SLO-driven cohort throttle for dp-42. This stabilized routing within 5 minutes and reduced 5xxs. Note: static pin is an emergency setting and requires manual revert after fix.
Mitigation in progress. Engineering to implement two changes: (A) make orchestrator cohort migration a lease-friendly operation that preserves tenant affinity tokens; (B) add a runtime-compatibility check before treating a bucket as 'incompatible' fallback to avoid silent variant swap. ETA for deploy to staging: 2026-03-18. Patch PR referenced in comments.
2026-03-12 18:05 GreenPlan Support Contact (A. Lim): Thanks, traffic looks normal. Please advise when a permanent fix is scheduled.
1) Deploy orchestrator patch that preserves edge affinity tokens during cohort migration (PR #582).
2) Add compatibility prewarm step for low_throughput buckets to avoid variant fallback when a tenant is pinned to quantized runtime.
3) Add guard in control-plane: do not trigger SLO throttle that moves cohorts if static tenant pin override is present.
4) Postmortem and runbook update: document this class of interaction between SLO-throttle, cohort migration, and model-variant compatibility.

Issue summary:
We observed a sudden cost spike in dedicated/staging during 2026-03-11 03:00–06:00 UTC. SRE needs temporary, least-privilege access to the billing export BigQuery dataset and associated storage/pubsub objects to complete a root-cause analysis. Org policy prevents broad roles (Billing Admin) from being granted; we need a narrowly-scoped role with an 8-hour TTL and proper audit bindings.

Impact:
- Investigation blocked: SRE cannot query billing exports (permission denied) and cannot view Pub/Sub push logs connected to export pipeline.
- Potential billing leakage or misconfigured job remains unresolved.

Requested change:
1) Create project-scoped custom role "redwood.billingReader_temp" with the minimal permissions:
   - bigquery.datasets.get, bigquery.tables.get, bigquery.tables.getData, bigquery.jobs.create (read-only pattern) scoped to redwood-billing-export dataset
   - storage.objects.get on gs://redwood-billing-exports
   - pubsub.subscriptions.consume (read) on billing-export-subscription
2) Create a timebound binding (8 hours) that adds group:eng-sre@redwood.com to the role in the billing export project using temporary-access-broker (or equivalent short-lived grant mechanism).
3) Ensure KMS audit and Data Access logs are enabled and routed to security-log BigQuery dataset for retention.

Security controls required: justification memo attached, 2FA enforced on group members, action logged with requestor identity, and the binding must auto-expire.

Notes: This is internal support (no customer data exposure) but access touches billing data and must follow least-privilege and auditable path.
1) On a staging operator machine (gcloud auth via SSO), attempt:
   bq --project_id=redwood-billing-export query 'SELECT project_id, SUM(cost) FROM `redwood-billing-export.billing_v1` WHERE DATE(_PARTITIONTIME)="2026-03-11" GROUP BY project_id'
2) Observe permission denied.
3) Attempt to list export bucket: gsutil ls gs://redwood-billing-exports — returns AccessDeniedException.
4) Check IAM bindings in the billing export project: no temporary binding for eng-sre group found.
Sample errors captured in operator session:
- BigQuery: Access Denied: Permission bigquery.tables.getData denied on table redwood-billing-export:billing_v1 (or the dataset)
- GCS: AccessDeniedException: 403 Forbidden (caller does not have storage.objects.list access to redwood-billing-exports)
Audit traces in Cloud Audit Logs show DENY entries from org policy for roles/billing.* for the operator principal (policy forbids project-level billing viewers unless via approved custom role).
Hypothesis: org policy prevents granting built-in roles, but a custom role scoped to the dataset + bucket will pass policy check.
Action attempts: attempted to add roles/bigquery.dataViewer to the eng-sre group in project redwood-billing-export; blocked by org constraint (requires approval).
Terraform module: infra/iam/roles/billing-temp (WIP) — PR opened to add custom role and timebound binding. See PRs listed.
Risk: If we create a role too broad, security will reject; conversely, too narrow will require iterative rbac changes and delay investigation. Proposed start: create role granting get/getData/metadata and storage.objects.get, test with one operator, then expand if needed.

Additional notes:
Action plan in progress: (1) Security to sign-off on custom role template by 2026-03-15; (2) Apply Terraform to create custom role and delegated timebound binding in redwood-billing-export/staging on 2026-03-15 02:00–03:00 UTC; (3) SRE to validate read-only queries and report findings; (4) revoke binding at TTL or manually earlier if investigation complete. No permanent changes to org policy planned.
payload.summary: Timebound billing-reader role and cross-project bindings for rapid cost spike investigation

Issue summary: After docking/undocking or plugging an ethernet cable while connected to corporate Wi‑Fi, some Windows laptops lose the VPN split-tunnel routes and the corporate DNS search suffix for the active interface. Impact: Users cannot resolve internal hostnames (e.g., console.redwood.local) and cannot reach internal services despite the VPN status showing 'connected'. Environment: Multiple Surface and MacBook devices observed but reproduces reliably on Windows 11 corporate image with Agent v2.14. Observed behavior: - VPN connection remains connected but traffic to internal subnets is routed to the LAN interface and then dropped. - DNS queries for short names stop appending the corporate search suffix, causing NXDOMAIN for internal names. - Reconnecting VPN or toggling Wi‑Fi does not restore routes until user reboots or runs manual interface reset commands. This blocks internal console access and developer workflows.
1) Boot Windows 11 corporate laptop and connect to office Wi‑Fi (corp-wifi).
2) Establish WireGuard-based VPN via corporate client (Agent v2.14).
3) Plug in docking station or direct ethernet cable (hotplug) which brings up the wired interface with lower metric.
4) Observe that VPN shows connected in client UI, but internal hostnames (short names) no longer resolve and services on 10.40.0.0/16 are unreachable.
5) Run 'ipconfig /all' and 'route print' to inspect missing split-tunnel routes and missing DNS search suffix on the active interface.
WireGuard client log excerpt (2026-03-12T10:14:02Z): peer=10.8.0.1 handshake ok; added routes: 10.40.0.0/16 -> wg0
Windows System event (2026-03-12T10:15:05Z): Network profile changed. Interface ethernet0 metric set to 10.
Subsequent WireGuard log (2026-03-12T10:15:07Z): routes flushed for interface change; no re-add of split routes due to client error 'IF_STATE_MISMATCH'
DnsClient service (2026-03-12T10:15:09Z): DNS search list cleared for interface ethernet0
Initial hypothesis: Client is not re-applying split-tunnel routes and DNS suffix on interface change; likely race between Windows network binding change and our agent's interface watcher.
Packet capture on affected host shows internal DNS queries sent to gateway DNS (192.168.1.1) after hotplug; WireGuard encapsulation still present for other traffic but no specific 10.40 routes.
Reproduced on Windows 11 with fast-APM networking driver; could not reproduce on macOS Catalina test node (suggests Windows-specific client/OS interaction).
SRE ran live debug: triggered hotplug while tailing agent logs; agent logged 'interface_added' then 'interface_removed' rapidly and skipped route re-apply due to debounce logic set to 8s.

Additional notes:
SRE-oncall (2026-03-12): Captured pcap and logs. Confirmed DNS queries going to local AP and not our resolver. WireGuard remains up but split routes absent.
Mitigation: Published a temporary PowerShell fix script in #internal-support slack and deployed Agent v2.14.1 to staging with reduced debounce time and extra check to re-apply split routes when a new interface appears with a lower metric. Permanent fix: Client-Eng to merge PR #1218 and add test automation for interface hotplug scenarios. Rollout plan: staged rollout to 10% of Windows corp fleet by 2026-03-16, monitor DNS resolution metrics and internal access error rates. Follow-up action: update runbook to include the quick-fix commands and add an automated endpoint remediation script in the Console.
payload.summary: LAN hotplug causes split-tunnel route removal and DNS search-suffix loss — internal service failures

Summary: After an org-level change to AWS SSO (IAM Identity Center) default session duration on 2026-03-09, external operators intermittently lose credentials while performing Dedicated provisioning workflows. Impact: several dedicated onboarding runs failed between 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-12 with STS assume/refresh errors; provisioning of new GPU pools delayed ~20-40 minutes for affected customers. Scope: observed in prod-us-east for external operator principals that authenticate via SSO and then call our dedicated-provisioner service which assumes roles into customer-linked accounts.
1) Login via AWS SSO (external operator account) and obtain temporary session (okta -> SSO) with permission-set A
2) Trigger dedicated provisioner job to create reserved capacity in customer account (calls AssumeRole in target account with DurationSeconds=3600),
3) Observe that token used by provisioner is rejected by STS or expires earlier than DurationSeconds resulting in access denied or token-expired errors mid-run
4) Re-run after re-authenticating via SSO and sometimes job completes if reauth gives a fresh session - but failures are nondeterministic and cluster around the recent org policy change
2026-03-11T01:12:23Z provisioner ERROR assume-role failed: STS AssumeRoleFailure RequestId=abc123efg region=us-east-1 error=ExpiredToken: The security token included in the request is expired
CloudTrail snippet: eventTime=2026-03-11T01:11:58Z eventName=AssumeRole awsRegion=us-east-1 userIdentity.type=AssumedRole sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName=external-ops@example.com
SSO audit: 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC: org-config changed: default session duration from 12h -> 1h (admin: infra-org-owner@example.com)
Hypothesis 1: Org-level SSO session-duration reduction causes source SSO session to be shorter than DurationSeconds requested by our AssumeRole chain, causing STS to return ExpiredToken during a long-running workflow.
Hypothesis 2: Some permission-sets are still attached to legacy session-duration profiles; provisioning path does not validate source session expiry before requesting long-lived downstream creds.
Evidence: CloudTrail and SSO audit records show session-duration change on 2026-03-09. STS errors cluster ~55-65 minutes after operator login. Reproduced by setting SSO session to 1h in test account.
Root cause: Combination of (a) sudden org-level session-duration reduction, and (b) provisioner requesting DurationSeconds without verifying the operator's source session remaining lifetime.
Mitigation implemented 2026-03-13: org-session-duration for affected permission-sets temporarily restored to 8h to stop ongoing customer-impact while code fix rolled out. Fix deployed 2026-03-14: provisioner now caps requested DurationSeconds to the source session remaining lifetime and to a safe max (3600s) and retries on ExpiredToken with exponential backoff. Follow-ups: create infra-as-code guardrail PR to require change-control for org SSO session-duration (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5432), add dashboard alert for STS ExpiredToken spikes, and update runbook with steps to detect and mitigate SSO session policy changes. Ticket remains In Progress until monitoring confirms no regressions for 72h.
1) Monitoring: watch STS ExpiredToken metric and oncall alert threshold for 72 hours (owner: SRE)
2) Documentation: update Dedicated runbook to include SSO session-duration mismatch checks (owner: Docs)
3) Policy: submit change-control proposal to lock default org session-duration changes (owner: Security/Infra)
4) Postmortem: if more than 5 customer-onboard failures occurred due to this, trigger a short postmortem (owner: Support)
5) Close ticket when monitoring clears (72h) and guardrail PR merged
Asha Patel (reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed three separate dedicated onboarding failures this morning. Correlated with SSO session renewals. Opening ticket to track root cause and mitigation.
Liam O'Connor (assignee) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally by setting SSO session to 1h then starting provisioner job. Provisioner requests a longer DurationSeconds (3600) but underlying SSO session lifetime can be shorter when SSO issues a shorter source session -> token chain breaks. Investigating codepath that sets requested DurationSeconds.
SRE (Maya Ruiz) - 2026-03-12: Confirmed CloudTrail shows STS responses with ExpiredToken at ~55-60 minutes after initial auth, consistent with session duration change. Quick mitigation: advise operators to re-auth before long-running jobs; planning infra change to cap DurationSeconds requested by provisioner.
Infra Owner (Samir Khanna) - 2026-03-13: Reverted org default session-duration to 8h for external operator permission-sets while we deploy code fix. Noted as temporary; will follow up with policy that prevents unexpected org-wide session overrides without change control.
Liam O'Connor - 2026-03-14: Deployed fix in infra repo to cap requested role DurationSeconds to min(source_session, 3600) and added retries on AssumeRole failure. Monitoring for regressions.
payload.summary: AWS SSO session-duration policy change causing external operator sessions to expire mid-provision and breaking dedicated capacity onboarding

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Users intermittently see a 401/403 from the internal analytics dashboard (console) immediately after an Okta profile change or a forced session refresh. The auth flow fails during the token refresh step: the auth-proxy exchanges the refresh token but the returned ID token appears to contain stale group/role claims, which the console then rejects due to tightened RBAC checks deployed last week.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers reported inability to load analytics dashboards since 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC.
- Affects internal dashboards and tooling only (not customer-facing APIs).
- Productivity hit for dashboard users and oncall when trying to verify incidents.

Environment:
- prod - us-east cluster serving internal-console routes.
- Okta as IdP, auth-proxy (v1.8.3) sits between console and Okta.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Log into console with a session established earlier (long-lived).
2) From Okta admin, update user's group membership (add/remove from analytics-admin).
3) Trigger console session refresh (browser refresh or wait for automatic refresh).
4) Observe 403 with "insufficient_role_claims" or 401 with "token_mismatch" in logs.

Expected behavior:
- After Okta claim change, the next refresh should either pick up new claims or gracefully fall back to previous session until the user reauths.

Actual behavior:
- Race condition: auth-proxy serves an ID token which appears to be from an older claim snapshot while backend RBAC service has the updated state, resulting in immediate denial.

Logs / evidence:
- auth-proxy logs (excerpt): "INFO exchange_refresh_token: returned id_token issued_at=1616161616 claims_version=42; cache_version=41"
- console logs: "ERROR access_check: claim_version_mismatch user=priya.shah@redwood.ai required=42 provided=41"
- Okta system log shows successful group update at 2026-03-10T09:02:14Z for affected users.

Business impact:
- Internal only, but P1 because it impedes oncall incident verification and slows engineering work.

Workarounds observed:
- Manual sign-out + full reauth resolves the issue for users.
- A temporary mitigation is to revert the strict claim_version enforcement in RBAC service (risky; requires rollback and careful rollout).
Initial hypothesis: identity cache/claim snapshot used by auth-proxy is behind Okta event processing or the token exchange pipeline; caching layer (claim-cache) may be serving stale claim bundles during refresh windows.

What we checked so far:
- Verified Okta event shows groups updated before auth-proxy token exchange.
- Replayed token exchange in staging: auth-proxy returns id_token with claims_version from local claim-cache, which is updated asynchronously by a background worker.
- Background worker shows occasional processing lag when claim updates are frequent (observed timestamps gap of up to 90s under burst).

Hypothesis: claim-cache update is eventual and not coordinated with token issuance; when RBAC service enforces claim_version strictly, short windows cause 403s.

Next steps:
- Add a short TTL invalidation on claim-cache on Okta webhooks (owner: auth-proxy team).
- Add defensive logic in RBAC service to accept id_token if issued_at is within 2m of claim update OR prompt reauth rather than 403.
- Add metrics and an alert for claim_version_mismatch rate > 1/min.
- Schedule a patch release for auth-proxy (v1.8.4) to synchronously refresh claims on token-exchange when webhook events are present.

Owners assigned: auth-proxy (Liam), RBAC (Sofia Martinez), SRE (Carlos Vega).
2026-03-10 10:12 - Support (Priya Shah): Created ticket after oncall reported that several engineers could not access the analytics dashboards following an Okta group change. Attached initial logs and user repro steps.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 08:45 - Support (Priya Shah): Communicated manual sign-out + reauth workaround to affected users. Tracking impacted users for postmortem.
(in progress) Mitigation steps applied to canary: increased claim-cache worker concurrency and temporarily relaxed claim_version enforcement in RBAC for 2-minute drift. PR for auth-proxy cache invalidation submitted. Full rollout planned once PR passes tests and security review. Will follow up with post-incident notes and longer-term plan for end-to-end identity propagation guarantees.
Deploy auth-proxy v1.8.4 with cache invalidation and sync fetch on token-exchange
Add incident runbook entry for claim_version_mismatch
Create alert for mismatch rate and Okta webhook processing lag metric
Review RBAC strictness and release guardrail for claim drift tolerance
payload.summary: Identity propagation delay prevents dashboard session token refresh for internal analytics console

Redaction rules: remove request.prompt_raw, replace user_id with HMAC-256 pseudonymization (per runbook), mask any detected IPs and emails, strip any KVs labeled as 'sensitive' in the trace schema. Deliverable: gzipped NDJSON with per-line JSON objects (sanitized) and an audit manifest recording redaction operations. Access: temporary S3 presigned URL to Legal with read-only permissions; copy to legal bucket is OK after audit logs recorded. Constraints: No full privileged console session access. Justification: subpoena; Legal (contact: Maya Kapoor) has provided the paperwork. Time sensitivity: expiring legal deadline in 8 days. Data minimization: prefer sampling (1k sessions) and prioritized by sessions flagged for "CustomerX" only. Approver(s) requested: Security lead (SRE Security), Compliance Officer, and Head of Legal.

Additional notes:
Checked serving-runtime retention and trace indexing: traces for the requested window are archived in prod S3 prefix s3://redwood-prod-traces/2026/02/.
Ran schema scan on trace objects (sample): fields present include request.prompt_raw, request.prompt_summary, response.text, kvcache.* and metadata.user_id. There are existing 'sensitive' KV flags in ~2% of traces for PII markers.
Validated that HMAC-256 pseudonymization utilities exist in internal/tools/pseudonymize and are approved by Security for legal exports (see GH PR linked).
Audited prior privileged extractions: previous approval flow required Security + Compliance sign-off and an audit manifest. Followed similar checklist from INT-12456 example.
Confirmed that streaming responses may include partial tokens; will redact request.prompt_raw and include only prompt_summary field with length threshold applied.
Cost estimate: extraction job for 1k sampled sessions ~0.5 GPU-hours for transformation; S3 egress negligible to internal legal bucket.
2026-03-11 Security approved conditional access: ephemeral job to run in VPC with KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222:alias/legal-export-key and write to s3://redwood-legal-staging/INT-15243/.
Applied redaction rules: removed request.prompt_raw, replaced user_id using HMAC-256 with salt stored in Secrets Manager (access logged), masked IP and email regex matches, stripped KVs flagged 'sensitive'. Added a 'redaction_version' field = 'rv1.2' to each output object.
Sampling decision: 1,200 sessions prioritized by CustomerX session flag and highest-likelihood relevance (per Legal). Full sample list exported in manifest (manifest includes original object keys hashed for traceability).
Access granted: Legal team (maya.kapoor@redwood.ai) given presigned URL valid for 72 hours. SRE retained IAM role 'legal-exporter' for job execution. All access and object copies logged and exported to compliance log index 'legal-exports'.
Follow-ups: Remove staging bucket contents on 2026-04-10, rotate export KMS key access, and file a short post-action note to Confluence. Also schedule a debrief with Legal and Security to review whether pseudonymization satisfies subpoena terms.

Issue summary:
A bulk asset-return import (CSV) into Inventory Service marked ~120 devices as 'returned' and triggered an automated deprovisioning workflow that inadvertently removed badge access for 18 active staff and locked the staging dock gate (Dock B). Several outbound vendor couriers were held because scanning the associated shipment manifest flagged assets as 'already returned'.

Impact:
- 18 staff unable to access Dock B or Staging Room 3 for morning shift (affects on-site engineer team and courier handling).
- 6 outbound shipments (GPUs, monitors, SSDs) placed on hold pending manual verification; SLA for same-day pickup at risk.
- Temporary inability to accept incoming returns that require manual staging.

Timeline (local time):
- 08:12: CSV import started by ops-tech (automated job).
- 08:18: Inventory Service completed import; deprovision job enqueued.
- 08:22: First badge access failures reported by morning team in #facilities.
- 08:35: Staging dock gate automatically entered locked state when badge validation returned null for badge mappings.
- 08:50: This ticket created and pager escalated to Facilities and Infra.

Environment:
- Inventory Service v3.5.1 (prod, EU region).
- Access-Control lambda (badge-sync) v2.2.0.
- Warehouse gate controller (vendor: SecureGate) API v1.9.

Steps to reproduce (suspected):
1) Reproduce locally by importing a CSV with mixed 'returned' statuses and missing badge_id fields into Inventory staging endpoint.
2) Ensure badge-sync job runs with 'cascade_deprovision=true' flag.
3) Observe badge records removed and gate controller receiving empty badge mapping payload.

Logs / evidence:
- Inventory import audit: https://logs.redwood.example.com/q/INV/2026-03-12/imp-2789 (CSV checksum: 9f3a1e)
- Badge-sync run (08:19): https://logs.redwood.example.com/q/AC/2026-03-12/sync-4471
- Gate controller alert: SecureGate event 0x7f3b: null badge handlers
- Slack thread: #facilities (link: https://slack.redwood.example.com/archives/C06FACIL/threads/1612)

Initial investigation notes:
- Preliminary root cause hypothesis: import CSV contained rows for assets that were already soft-returned but had badge association nullified in the CSV; the deprovision workflow did not validate active_user assignment before removing badges (regression introduced by infra PR 9705).
- Badge-sync currently treats missing badge_id as an instruction to remove mapping rather than skip. This is a policy change introduced in v2.2.0.
- Gate controller treats absence of mapping for a user badge as 'user unauthorized' and flips to lockdown when multiple invalid scans occur within 60 seconds (safety fallback).

Temporary workaround applied:
- Rolled back badge-sync to v2.1.8 at 09:05 which prevents cascade removal.
- Manually re-enabled badge mappings from snapshot backup (inventory snapshot taken 2026-03-12T07:50Z) for 18 affected staff at 09:22.
- Gate controller manually reset by on-site vendor tech at 09:40; dock unlocked and courier pickups resumed at 09:55.
- Placed affected outbound shipments on manual verification list and notified carriers; all pickups rescheduled to same day where possible.

Immediate next steps / owner actions:
- Marcus Reed (Facilities) to coordinate vendor gate health check and confirm SecureGate firmware logs for 08:22-08:40 window.
- Priya Nair (Infra) to open PR reverting the cascade behavior and add validation to inventory import pipeline to skip rows with null badge_id for active-users (tracking PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9812).
- Inventory team to add an import preview and dry-run step to prevent accidental bulk deprovision.
- Ops to run an audit of all 'returned' status changes in last 72 hours and confirm there are no further impacted users.

Acceptance criteria for resolution:
- Badge-sync prevents removal of active user badge mappings when CSV row omits badge_id.
- Gate controller no longer enters full-lockdown from transient multi-scan null-mapping events (fail-safe changed to log + notify).
- Post-mortem with runbook updates published in Confluence and shared in #facilities.
payload.summary: Bulk asset-return CSV triggered mass badge deprovision cascade; staging dock locked and return shipments on hold

payload.description:
Issue Summary
During several customer-impacting events and internal incident drills, incident-bot v2 telemetry context cards intermittently rendered as empty or partially complete. Slack threads showed repeated “Telemetry query timed out” messages. Investigation indicates the bot can generate bursty query patterns (multiple responders + retries + interactive actions), which saturates the telemetry query service and triggers timeouts. These timeouts are most acute under incident conditions (elevated error rates + higher on-call activity), which is exactly when the bot is relied upon.

Impact
- On-call responders lost fast access to saturation signals (GPU util / queue depth / KV cache pressure), increasing time-to-triage.
- Telemetry query service experienced elevated p95/p99 latency; in worst cases, query workers hit concurrency limits and began failing fast.
- Secondary impact: dashboards and ad-hoc queries in the same time window degraded (shared query infrastructure).

Environment
- Production (primarily us-east, eu-west)
- Affects Slack channels: #incidents, #eng-oncall
- Affected service(s): telemetry-query-service (internal), incident-bot (Slack app)

Customer / Data sensitivity
Internal issue. No evidence of customer data exposure; failures were timeouts/empty cards only.

What we observed
- Bot posts initial incident context, then multiple responders click “Refresh signals” / “Expand details” within a short window.
- Slack interactive action retries (due to ack deadline + transient network latency) caused duplicate calls.
- Bot performed per-card, per-signal queries with limited coalescing; same incident/thread triggers repeated identical queries.

Symptoms (from bot / logs)
- Slack card banner: “Saturation signals unavailable (telemetry query timed out). Showing dashboard links.”
- telemetry-query-service logs: request_id spikes and increased “deadline exceeded” counts
- p99 latency spikes correlate with incident start + the first 10 minutes of heavy responder traffic

Steps to reproduce (reliable in staging with load)
1) Start a simulated incident thread and trigger bot context cards.
2) Have 5–10 users click “Refresh” and “Expand” within 60 seconds.
3) Observe telemetry query latency and bot timeouts, particularly if the telemetry cluster is already under moderate load.

Investigation notes
- Primary driver is burst concurrency and lack of request coalescing at the telemetry-query-service boundary.
- The bot also issues some high-cost queries (wide time windows + high-cardinality labels) when the incident metadata is incomplete (missing route/service scoping), causing fallback to broader queries.
- Slack retry behavior: interactive actions must ACK quickly; when upstream query exceeds budget, the bot may retry, amplifying bursts.

Mitigation / Fix
Implemented a multi-layer approach:
1) Cache + request coalescing for telemetry queries used by incident-bot
   - Short TTL caching (target 30–120s depending on signal class)
   - Per-(incident_id, region, service, route) de-duplication to collapse identical queries
   - Serve stale-on-error during incident windows (prefer last-known-good + links)

2) Rate limits + circuit breakers on diagnostics endpoints
   - Token bucket per bot identity + per incident thread
   - Hard cap on concurrent in-flight queries per region
   - Circuit breaker: when telemetry p95 exceeds threshold, bot switches to degraded mode automatically (links + cached summaries)

3) Tighter query budgets + bounded time windows
   - Default windows reduced for “first 5 minutes” cards
   - If incident metadata lacks scoping, bot displays an action to “Select service/region” instead of fanning out

4) Perf canary for telemetry query latency (bot-critical queries)
   - Synthetic queries run continuously
   - Alerts on sustained p95/p99 regression and timeout rate

Resolution
- Rolled out caching + timeout handling improvements in incident-bot.
- Added server-side rate limits/circuit breakers in diagnostics endpoints.
- Deployed telemetry query latency perf canary and alerting.
- Verified during two internal incident simulations and one production incident: bot returned cached summaries quickly and did not amplify telemetry load.

Verification
- Success criteria:
  - Bot context card render within 3s p95 (degraded mode allowed) in prod during load tests
  - Telemetry query timeout rate < 1% for bot-critical query set (sustained)
  - No >2x increase in telemetry-query-service QPS attributable to bot refresh bursts
- Observed (post-change):
  - Bot “saturation signals” card returns within ~1–2s when cached, ~2–4s uncached; falls back to links after budget expires
  - Telemetry query p99 no longer spikes linearly with Slack action bursts

Follow-ups / Action Items
- Document query budget and allowed label sets for incident-bot (owner: Allison Grant)
- Add guardrail test to prevent introducing high-cardinality dimensions into bot queries (owner: Nadia Rahman)
- Confirm bot’s Slack retries are idempotent across all interactive actions (owner: Devon Price)
- Update on-call troubleshooting playbook for empty cards to reflect degraded-mode behavior and where to check perf canary (owner: Rafael Mendes)

Comments
2025-02-18 (Miles Thornton): Creating ticket after multiple reports that incident-bot v2 saturation cards are timing out during bursts in #incidents. We need a fix before expanding beta beyond SRE rotation.

2025-02-18 (Logan Wright): Looking at telemetry-query-service. Seeing concurrency spikes + deadline exceeded clustered around bot activity. Suspect missing cache/coalescing. Will propose TTL caching and a per-thread rate limit.

2025-02-19 (Jacob Stein): From bot logs, Slack interactive actions retried when ack arrives late. We’re not fully idempotent on refresh path; duplicates are generating identical telemetry queries.

2025-02-20 (Nadia Rahman): Confirmed some queries are unbounded when route/service labels missing. Recommend forcing scoping in bot UI or using safe defaults with narrow windows.

2025-02-24 (Logan Wright): Implemented server-side throttles + circuit breaker config in diagnostics endpoints. Initial load test: QPS is capped; bot falls back to cached context + links.

2025-03-03 (Aisha Bello): Adding perf canary to catch regressions earlier; alert will page obs-oncall only (not #incidents) to avoid noise.

2025-03-06 (Miles Thornton): Verified during drill. Cards load reliably; when telemetry is slow, we get cached summary and deep links. Closing as Resolved.
payload.summary: Telemetry query timeouts triggered by incident-bot bursts in #incidents (v2 context cards) causing slow/empty diagnostics

comments: Namespace: redwood-system (control plane), redwood-runtime (data plane), monitoring (Grafana/Prometheus)
payload.description:
Issue summary
- Customer completed Redwood Private install (including the “observability minimum pack”). Grafana UI is reachable and Prometheus is scraping targets, but there are no Redwood dashboards visible under Browse/Dashboards.

Customer impact
- Customer platform team cannot validate runtime health post-install and is blocked on their internal acceptance checklist for go-live.
- No production outage, but reduces operational visibility and delays launch.

Customer environment (as provided)
- Deployment type: On-prem / air-gapped
- Installer version: redwood-private-installer v1.12.3 (offline bundle)
- Helm charts: redwood-helm-charts 1.12.3
- Observability pack: included in offline bundle (customer unsure which pack version)

Additional notes:
- Grafana: 10.4.x (from our bundled chart)
- Prometheus: kube-prometheus-stack (bundled)
- StorageClass: longhorn
- NetworkPolicies: enabled (customer baseline)
What’s expected
- Redwood-provisioned dashboards should appear automatically (Runtime Overview, Control Plane Health, GPU Fleet, etc.) in Grafana under a “Redwood” folder (or similarly named folder) after install.
What’s observed
- Grafana is up and login works.
- Datasource exists (“Prometheus”) and can query basic metrics (up, kube_pod_info).
- No dashboards in the Redwood folder; in some cases no Redwood folder at all.
Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Install Redwood Private with observability pack enabled using offline bundle.
2) Access Grafana -> Dashboards.
3) Observe no Redwood dashboards.
Initial hypotheses
- Dashboards ConfigMaps not present in cluster (missing from offline bundle or Helm values disabled).
- ConfigMaps present but not labeled for Grafana sidecar discovery.
- Grafana sidecar for dashboards disabled or misconfigured (watch namespace/label selector mismatch).
- Grafana provisioning path not mounted / permissions issue.
- RBAC preventing Grafana sidecar from listing ConfigMaps in target namespaces.
Key customer-provided snippets
1) kubectl get cm -n monitoring | grep -i redwood => (empty)
2) kubectl get pods -n monitoring => grafana-xxxxx Running
3) Grafana logs (excerpt):
   - "logger=provisioning.dashboard t=2025-07-18T16:02:11.913Z level=info msg=\"Starting Dashboard provisioning\""
   - No subsequent "Dashboard provisioned" entries
Support request
- Identify whether dashboards were packaged/applied.
- Provide a workaround to get dashboards installed in Grafana for air-gapped cluster.
- Confirm the correct Helm values/settings for the minimum pack and whether any known issue exists in v1.12.3 offline bundle.
Resolution summary (final)
- Root cause: Grafana dashboards were included in the cluster as ConfigMaps, but Grafana’s dashboard sidecar was watching only the monitoring namespace and a different label key than what the Redwood dashboard ConfigMaps used in 1.12.3 offline bundle. Additionally, RBAC was missing list/watch on ConfigMaps in redwood-system/redwood-runtime.
- Fix: Update Helm values to (a) align the sidecar label selector with the Redwood dashboard ConfigMaps and (b) allow cross-namespace discovery OR copy dashboard ConfigMaps into monitoring. Applied RBAC fix and restarted Grafana.
- Outcome: Redwood dashboards appeared under folder “Redwood Private (Minimum Pack)” within 5 minutes; customer confirmed panels populated.
Workaround / customer steps (executed)
A) Confirm dashboards ConfigMaps exist:
- kubectl get cm -A | grep -E "redwood|observability|grafana-dashboard"
B) Update Grafana sidecar + RBAC (preferred) via values override:
- Set:
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.enabled=true
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.searchNamespace=ALL
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.label=grafana_dashboard
  - grafana.sidecar.dashboards.labelValue="1"
- Add RBAC for grafana sidecar service account to list/watch ConfigMaps in redwood-system and redwood-runtime.
- Helm upgrade kube-prometheus-stack / grafana release.
C) Restart Grafana:
- kubectl rollout restart deploy/grafana -n monitoring
D) Validate:
- Grafana -> Dashboards -> folder appears
- Prometheus datasource queries for redwood_* recording rules and runtime metrics return data
Notes
- If customer security policy blocks searchNamespace=ALL, alternative is copying the dashboard ConfigMaps into monitoring namespace with the expected label (documented below in comments).
2025-07-18 09:12 (Dev Patel - Support)
Created ticket from customer email + #support handoff. Requested environment details and installer/Helm versions. Asked for: `kubectl get cm -A | grep grafana` and Grafana pod logs around provisioning start.
2025-07-18 10:03 (Customer - Northbridge Health Analytics)
Install finished successfully and health checks passed. We can log into Grafana, Prometheus datasource works, but there are no Redwood dashboards. `kubectl get cm -n monitoring | grep -i redwood` returns nothing. We are air-gapped and used the offline bundle from Redwood. NetworkPolicies are enabled cluster-wide.
2025-07-18 10:26 (Bruno Silva - PS / Private Deployments)
Likely either (1) dashboards not applied because the pack values were off, or (2) dashboards are created in a different namespace than Grafana’s sidecar is watching. Can you run `kubectl get cm -A | grep -i grafana` and `kubectl describe deploy grafana -n monitoring` (look for sidecar args)?
2025-07-18 11:02 (Customer - Northbridge Health Analytics)
`kubectl get cm -A | grep -i grafana` shows:
- redwood-system/redwood-private-observability-dashboards-1
- redwood-runtime/redwood-runtime-dashboards-1
Both have labels:
- app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm
- redwood.ai/observability-pack=true
No label like grafana_dashboard=1.
`kubectl describe deploy grafana -n monitoring` shows sidecar enabled but label selector is `grafana_dashboard=1` and namespace is monitoring only.
2025-07-18 11:20 (Dylan Brooks - Dashboards/tooling)
That explains it: our dashboard ConfigMaps in 1.12.3 are labeled `redwood.ai/observability-pack=true` (not `grafana_dashboard=1`). Either update sidecar label selector to match our label, or (safer) add `grafana_dashboard=1` label to the existing ConfigMaps. Also, sidecar is only monitoring namespace; if ConfigMaps live in redwood-system/redwood-runtime you need searchNamespace=ALL or copy the ConfigMaps into monitoring.
Proposed immediate workaround:
1) Label ConfigMaps: `kubectl label cm -n redwood-system redwood-private-observability-dashboards-1 grafana_dashboard=1 --overwrite` and same for runtime.
2) Set sidecar searchNamespace=ALL (or copy CMs to monitoring if ALL is disallowed).
3) Restart Grafana deployment.
Longer-term we should align the Helm chart defaults/labels for private minimum pack.
2025-07-18 12:05 (Bruno Silva - PS / Private Deployments)
Customer prefers not to run sidecar across all namespaces due to security review. Suggested option: copy dashboards ConfigMaps into monitoring namespace.
Commands:
- `kubectl get cm -n redwood-system redwood-private-observability-dashboards-1 -o yaml | sed 's/namespace: redwood-system/namespace: monitoring/' | kubectl apply -n monitoring -f -`
- Repeat for `redwood-runtime/redwood-runtime-dashboards-1`
- Label the new CMs: `kubectl label cm -n monitoring <cm-name> grafana_dashboard=1 --overwrite`
Then restart Grafana.
Also asked customer to confirm Grafana SA has list/watch on ConfigMaps in monitoring (it does by default).
2025-07-18 14:18 (Customer - Northbridge Health Analytics)
We copied both ConfigMaps into monitoring and labeled `grafana_dashboard=1`. After restarting Grafana, we now see a “Redwood Private (Minimum Pack)” folder and dashboards are present. Panels were initially empty; after ~2 minutes they started populating. This unblocks us.
Question: is there an official supported fix so we don’t have to maintain copies after upgrades?
2025-07-18 15:01 (Dev Patel - Support)
Confirmed the workaround is acceptable short-term but we want a supported path. Looping in SRE/Telemetry to confirm recommended values for private minimum pack. Also linking runbook: private observability day-2 operations (Grafana provisioning section).
2025-07-19 09:42 (Rafael Mendes - SRE)
Recommendation for supported installs: either (A) keep dashboards in monitoring namespace to avoid cross-namespace watch, or (B) explicitly enable cross-namespace watch and add RBAC for grafana sidecar. For Private minimum pack we should default to (A) in air-gapped bundles to reduce security friction.
Also noted we’ve had a similar CI failure in INT-11804 where dashboards weren’t discovered due to label mismatch.
2025-07-19 11:10 (Connor O'Brien - Release/packaging)
Checked offline bundle manifest for 1.12.3: dashboards are included, but labels differ from kube-prometheus-stack defaults. This is tracked for backport in the private installer/helm wiring. Suggest we point customer to upgrading to 1.12.4 once released (will include corrected labels and/or chart values).
2025-07-21 16:30 (Dev Patel - Support)
Customer confirmed stable after 48h. No further action needed on their side until next upgrade. We provided guidance for keeping the copy step as part of their upgrade runbook if they remain on 1.12.3.
Closing ticket as resolved with workaround + upcoming product fix.
Internal follow-up: ensure minimum pack dashboards ship with `grafana_dashboard=1` (or chart default label is updated) and install places dashboards in monitoring namespace for air-gapped installs.
Resolved via workaround: copied Redwood dashboard ConfigMaps into monitoring namespace and labeled for Grafana sidecar discovery; restarted Grafana. Customer validated dashboards present and populated. Product follow-up identified to align labels/defaults in subsequent Private releases.
If you upgrade Redwood Private before the label/namespace fix is included, re-run the dashboard copy + label step (or opt into cross-namespace sidecar watch with RBAC). We will notify you once the supported default is available in a maintenance release.
Validate and backport dashboard label alignment for Private offline bundles (air-gapped) so kube-prometheus-stack Grafana sidecar discovers Redwood dashboards without manual copy.
Update Private day-2 runbook to include detection steps: where dashboards ConfigMaps live, required labels, and namespace watch settings.
payload.summary: Private install: Grafana loads but no Redwood dashboards (minimum observability pack)

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Intermittent connectivity observed across multiple clients in the LAX office on 2026-03-10 morning. Symptoms: Wi‑Fi clients lose connectivity while roaming between APs, obtain new DHCP leases multiple times in a short window, and WireGuard VPN sessions drop and fail to re-establish until manual reconnect.

Impact:
- ~10–15% of developers in LAX reported disconnections while moving between floors/meeting rooms (Slack channel #it-help showed ~12 distinct reports between 09:30–11:20 PST).
- Internal services (git pushes, terminals using VPN) experienced failures or hangs for affected users.
- Productivity impact: meeting interruptions and degraded remote access during the window.

Environment:
- Location: LAX office (primary floor 5 & 6).
- SSID: Redwood-Corp (802.11r enabled initially).
- Controller: Aruba Mobility Master (firmware 8.5.1-build-12).
- APs: Aruba 630/640 series, mixed firmware.
- DHCP: On-prem ISC DHCP server, scope 10.77.5.0/24, lease time 1h (configured), max-lease-count 200.
- VPN client: WireGuard (wg-0), internal configuration using static peer keys, allowed-ips = 0.0.0.0/0, keepalive 25s.
- Affected device types: macOS (M1/M2), Windows 11, and some Android devices.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. User walks from floor 5 to floor 6 or between meeting rooms where AP handoff occurs.
2. Client attempts 802.11r fast-roaming between APs (FT).
3. Controller shows transient duplicate client MAC entries and sends deauth/reassoc sequences.
4. Client loses IP/gets new DHCP request shortly after; WireGuard detects network change and drops the session. In several cases the client does not re-establish automatically.

Observed behavior / logs:
- DHCP server logs (excerpt): multiple DISCOVER/OFFER/REQUEST/ACK cycles for same MAC within 30s windows; lease time renewed but new lease assigned (different IP) 3–4 times in 10 minutes.
- Controller event log: "Duplicate client MAC detected on AP-06 and AP-21" and several "FT key negotiation failed" messages at the same timestamps as user reports.
- WireGuard client logs: "peer unreachable: network change detected, endpoint reset" followed by repeated handshake failures until manual restart.
- Packet captures (sparse): witnessed reassociation frames immediately followed by DHCPDISCOVER from same MAC; DHCP server responding with OFFER for same pool.

Initial triage and hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: 802.11r (fast transition) misconfiguration between APs with mixed firmware causing FT negotiation failure and duplicated MAC entries on controller, leading to transient disconnects and DHCP churn.
- Hypothesis B: DHCP server configured with aggressive lease reclamation or scope fragmentation; when client briefly disconnects it is assigned new IP causing WireGuard session to drop because endpoint/public keys are tied to previous src IP in some internal routing rules.
- Hypothesis C: AP roaming timers or radio knobs (DTIM/roaming thresholds) are misaligned across APs producing flapping.

Investigation notes:
- Cross-checked controller firmware list: several APs on 8.5.1, a handful on 8.4.x due to missed staged upgrades. Known compatibility note in Aruba KB about 802.11r inter-op across minor versions.
- Reviewed DHCP config: lease time is 1h but DHCP server shows rapid re-assignments due to AUTH failures (server sees client as new due to changes in 'chaddr' content on reassoc frames). No exhaustion of address pool.
- WireGuard config: peers are not IP-bound in server config, but NAT traversal and stateful firewall rules in the office edge expect stable client source IPs for some legacy routes; this contributed to sessions not recovering automatically.
- Reproduced in lab by forcing FT fail on a test AP pair; observed identical DHCP churn and wg handshake fail pattern.

Actions taken during incident:
- 2026-03-10 10:45 PST: IT turned off 802.11r (FT) on SSID Redwood-Corp as immediate mitigation across LAX master controller. This reduced roam-related deauths in the next 20 minutes.
- 2026-03-10 11:10 PST: Increased DHCP lease time temporarily from 1h to 12h to reduce churn during roaming until full fix deployed.
- 2026-03-10 12:00 PST: Deployed sticky client setting (client anchor) on controller to prefer same AP where possible for short periods.

Root cause and resolution summary:
- Root cause: Mixed AP firmware versions caused unreliable 802.11r (FT) negotiations. Some APs failed FT key exchange leading to reassociation errors and duplicate MAC state in the controller. The reassociation sequence changed the client 'chaddr' observation resulting in the DHCP server treating the client as a new request and issuing additional leases. WireGuard endpoints and edge firewall expectations of stable source IPs caused VPN sessions to drop and fail to auto-recover.
- Permanent fix deployed 2026-03-12: staged firmware upgrade to uniform Aruba firmware 8.5.3 across all LAX APs (completed during maintenance window). Restored 802.11r, validated FT success across AP pairs. Reverted DHCP lease time back to 1h after confirming stability. Adjusted edge firewall to avoid tightly coupling session handling to client source IP for WireGuard peers.

Resolution / rollout notes:
- 2026-03-11 02:00–04:00: Staged firmware upgrade on non-peak APs and validated roaming metrics.
- 2026-03-12 01:00–03:30: Completed firmware upgrades on remaining APs and re-enabled 802.11r.
- Post-upgrade validation: roaming tests with macOS and Android devices showed no DHCP churn and WireGuard sessions remained established during handoffs.

Follow-ups and action items:
- IT to add automated AP firmware compliance check to weekly runbook (owner: Priya Desai).
- Networking to add DHCP/DNS correlation dashboard to detect rapid lease churn (owner: SRE - Tom Becker).
- Update internal runbook section "LAX Network Runbook" with steps to mitigate roaming issues and how to perform zero-downtime AP firmware rollouts.
- Consider moving WireGuard peer handling to be resilient to client source IP changes (networking + security design review).

Attachments / evidence:
- DHCP log snippets, controller logs, sample packet captures uploaded to internal S3 bucket (links added to Confluence page).

Suggested postmortem tags: networking, wifi-roam, dhcp, wireguard, infra-hardening
payload.summary: Intermittent office Wi‑Fi roam causing DHCP lease churn and WireGuard VPN drops in LAX office

Issue summary:
During a scheduled snapshot restore of historical routing policies into the staging config-store, the routing policies editor surface continued to show the pre-restore (newer) rule set while the serving runtime and reporting pipelines started enforcing the restored (older) rules.

Impact:
- Customer-facing routing mismatches: requests served under incorrect routing policies for ~22 minutes in us-east.
- SLA enforcement flags (priority escalation macros) reverted to older values leading to unexpected quota throttles and at least one P1 customer support escalation.
- Reporting and analytics showed dropped metrics for the newer rule IDs because the serving runtime used the restored snapshot IDs.

Environment:
- prod/us-east (primary config-store cluster), routing-editor v3.8.1, config-store (consul) cluster 3.2.0, rule-engine v2.4.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Trigger a snapshot restore via the console snapshot UI (selected historic snapshot created 2026-03-08T02:00Z).
2) Simultaneously have two engineers editing routing rule drafts in the editor (autosave enabled).
3) The restore applied to the backend config-store. Serving runtime pulled the restored snapshot on next poll (~30s).
4) Editor UI kept rendering the in-memory draft / cached policy (user-facing preview) until autosave conflict resolution completed, creating a divergent persisted policy state.

Observed behavior:
- Serving runtime enforced restored snapshot rules immediately after its poll.
- Editor preview showed newer draft rules and allowed publish attempts that failed with a 409 because the active config had a lower sequence ID.
- Reporting pipelines ingested events tagged with restored rule IDs, causing customer-facing dashboards to show mismatched rule exposures.

Expected behavior:
- Snapshot restore should acquire a global apply lock or otherwise quiesce editor autosaves until restore completes so editor preview matches persisted active rules.
- Publish attempts during restore should surface a clear blocking error and not permit conflicting drafts to be published without sequence reconciliation.

Logs / artifacts:
- Serving logs (rule-engine): "applied_snapshot id=20260308-02:00 sequence=1124" (2026-03-09T13:04:06Z),
- Editor client console trace: "cache-miss -> rendering draft(seq=1130)" (2026-03-09T13:04:12Z),
- Config-store events: restore job logs (config-store restore-id=restore-20260308-0200, duration=18s)",
- Reporting sample: dashboard spike showing ruleset change at 2026-03-09T13:04:20Z (link: https://observability.redwood/reports/route-diff/46290)",

Initial triage (Priya): Correlation of timestamps shows the restore completed ~6s before serving runtime poll but editor autosave/draft machinery continued to present a newer sequence. Hypothesis: snapshot restore does not currently set a 'restore-in-progress' coordination flag in the config-store, so editor and runtime can diverge briefly.

SRE (Diego): Pulled consul event stream; found race between 'apply_snapshot' and per-editor autosave reconcile job. Editor reconcile attempts attempt a blind merge when sequence mismatch occurs, which can leave an in-memory display different from persisted state until user refresh.

Rule-engine team: Confirmed serving runtime correctly applies the persisted snapshot; however, analytic tagging uses rule-name -> id mapping cached by routing-ui service which was not invalidated by restore, causing reporting pipeline to backfill with older IDs.

Security/QA: No unauthorized changes detected; restore request came from a scheduled operator job (not automated third-party).

Root cause (working): Lack of a coordinated restore-lock and stale cache invalidation between editor UI, config-store restore paths, and reporting ingestion. There's a missing step that marks a 'restore_in_progress' key and forces editor to show a blocking banner and prevents drafts from being published until reconcile completes.


Additional notes:
Temporary workaround implemented (2026-03-09): instruct ops to run restore during a maintenance window and to notify editor users to refresh; manual verification checklist added to Route Snapshot Runbook.

Fix rollout (in progress as of 2026-03-13):
- Backend: config-store PR to set/clear a 'restore_in_progress' coordination key during snapshot apply (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/config-store/pull/782).
- Frontend: feature-flagged banner and publish-block changes merged to staging (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-ui/pull/942).
- Runtime: added immediate cache-bust notification to reporting ingestion on snapshot apply (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-engine/pull/2314).

Post-deploy follow-ups (assigned):
- Add e2e test that runs concurrent autosave + snapshot restore to prevent regressions (owner: QA, ticket INT-46810).
- Create alert when serving/runtime sequence != editor/latest-seq for > 30s (owner: Observability, ticket INT-46812).
- Update runbook to include manual restore verification steps and communication checklist (owner: Support OPS).

Status: patch set merged to canary; monitoring in place. Planned full rollout after 48h canary observation if no anomalies.
1) Complete canary rollout and monitor the alert for sequence divergence for 48h. 2) Close linked customer cases after confirmation from CS. 3) Convert feature-flag for UX blocking into default once backend lock is in stable release. 4) Document the snapshot/restore coordination pattern in the Rule Engine design doc.
Fix in progress; workaround and runbook updated; monitoring set.
payload.summary: Routing policies editor: snapshot restore applies stale SLA/route flags causing mismatched active rules

payload.description:
Issue summary: The ephemeral credential broker that bridges GCP Workload Identity Federation (WIF) to AWS STS for the dedicated LLM debug proxy is intermittently failing policy checks when network tag conditions are present on the target AWS role. Impact: Internal SRE/Platform engineers intermittently cannot assume the debug role in prod, causing inability to reproduce customer-facing Dedicated provisioning failures and blocking live debug sessions. Scope: observed in prod us-east for the dedicated control plane; affects debug/trace sessions for multiple LLM models. Hypothesis: a tag-based condition on the AWS role assume-policy combined with our broker's session tags causes role policy rejection when the broker attempts to pass truncated or non-canonical tag values. This is surfaced only when requests route through the LLM proxy because the proxy injects environment tags and request metadata before assume-role.
1) From a GCP service account configured with WIF, call the internal LLM debug proxy with --debug-auth=jit flag. 2) Proxy attempts to exchange WIF token at the broker to assume an AWS diagnostic role with tag condition (e.g., 'x-org:session-owner=*'). 3) Observe STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity response. 4) Failure mode: AssumeRole denied with 'Condition check failed' and 'Tag value mismatch' logged in AWS CloudTrail. 5) Repeat without proxy injection of metadata (direct broker call) — often succeeds. This reproduces ~6/10 attempts in prod under current traffic patterns.
STS assume-role calls intermittently denied. CloudTrail shows Condition statement failure referencing aws:TagKeys or aws:RequestTag. Broker logs show session-tags payload that include duplicated 'env' and 'request_id' keys; in some cases values are truncated to 32 characters. Proxy adds a 'proxy-origin' tag with URL-encoded path which causes the AWS policy string comparison to fail.
Broker should reliably forward canonical session tags that match the AWS role's condition checks. LLM debug proxy should not mutate or truncate tag values in a way that violates assume-role policy conditions.
Selected log snippets:
- broker-prod-2026-03-10T21:14:02Z: WARN assumeRole failed: MalformedTagValue or Condition check failed; requestTags={proxy-origin=/debug%2Fsession%2F1234567890, env=prod-us, request_id=4f7b...}
- aws-cloudtrail: EventName=AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, ErrorCode=AccessDenied, ErrorMessage=Condition checks failed for tags: request-origin
- proxy-prod-2026-03-10T21:14:02Z: DEBUG injected_metadata={env: prod-us, proxy-origin: /debug/session/1234567890}
Correlation IDs: req=4f7b-9a2c-prod
Initial triage (Maya): reproduced locally with a minimal proxy + broker pairing; confirmed that proxy URL-encoding triggers percent-encoded values which our broker does not decode prior to calling STS. Diego: identified an edge case in internal tag dedupe logic — when the total tags payload > 8 entries, we compact tags and may truncate strings to 32 chars. Hypothesis chain: (1) Proxy injects encoded path; (2) broker dedupe/truncate code shortens value; (3) AWS role condition expects full canonical value; (4) policy denies. Observability gap: request-level tag snapshot not persisted in long-term traces. Temporary mitigation applied to increase broker debug logging for tag payloads. Also verified the role policy is strict by design due to compliance constraints (see linked confluence).
1) Short term: revert proxy metadata injection for debug sessions in prod by toggling feature flag 'proxy.inject_debug_meta' -> false. 2) Add temporary retry logic with backoff in the broker when AssumeRole returns Condition failure, coupled with expanded logging (already rolled out to 3% traffic). 3) For urgent ad-hoc debugging, SRE can create a time-limited AWS role without strict tag conditions and request ops to map it to the session (requires approval).
1) Update broker tag pipeline: ensure URL-decoding of proxy-injected metadata prior to dedupe; preserve full tag strings (remove 32-char truncation) and enforce canonicalization rules. 2) Add deterministic tag order and stable hashing to avoid duplicate keys. 3) Harden unit tests for tag serialization/size limits and add end-to-end test covering WIF→broker→STS with proxy injection. 4) Small IAM change: add a 'proxy-origin-normalized' attribute to role conditions and support both forms during phased rollout to avoid immediate access breakage. 5) Security review: require secops signoff for IAM condition change. Estimated engineering work: 3s — 1 week to implement + 2 days for rollout and verification.
- Stage 1 (canary): deploy broker tag pipeline changes to staging and a 1% prod subset; monitor assume-role success rate and CloudWatch/CloudTrail errors for 48 hours. - Stage 2 (ramp): 10% for 24 hours, then 50% for 24 hours. - Stage 3: full rollout with IAM role conditional allowance for 'proxy-origin-normalized' for 24 hours; then remove temporary allowance after verification. - Rollback: revert broker change (toggle feature flag) and re-enable proxy injection if failures increase > 3x baseline in 15-minute windows. - Post-deploy: run conformance job that simulates 1k assume-role exchanges per minute for 30m and validate zero Condition failures.
- Security: secops@redwood.ai signoff for any IAM condition change. - Compliance: verify that adding 'proxy-origin-normalized' does not open policy bypass vectors. - SRE: approval for toggling proxy injection flag in prod during mitigation. - Product/Privacy: confirm debug path metadata is acceptable to PII policy. Contact list: @Leah Singh (SecOps), @Omar Patel (Compliance), @SRE-Oncall.
- Create automated trace snapshots for broker tag payloads (owner: Diego). - Add e2e test covering percent-encoded metadata (owner: infra-qa). - Update runbook for JIT broker failures (owner: Maya). - Schedule postmortem if incident recurs within 7 days after full rollout.

Additional notes:
Leah Singh - SecOps (2026-03-11): We need to ensure IAM change doesn't widen trust boundary. If feasible, prefer broker change only and avoid changing role conditions. I'll review PR when available.
SRE Oncall (2026-03-12): Toggled 'proxy.inject_debug_meta' flag to false for prod; observed immediate reduction in Condition failures. Rolling this flag change back will be part of staged rollout after broker fix.
payload.summary: JIT credential orchestration gaps: GCP→AWS role chaining and network-tag authorization for LLM debug proxy
