payload.description:
Summary: Jobs that bootstrap dedicated GPU provisioners via the auth-proxy intermittently fail to assume the target AWS role. Errors show AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRole or downstream permission checks fail when role session tags parsed by the provisioner are missing expected attributes. This started after last week's auth-proxy update that changed WIF-to-STS attribute normalization. Impact: Several Dedicated onboarding runs and internal automated repro jobs failed, blocking a small number of customer onboarding tasks and delaying a production scale test. Intermittent: ~10% of assume-role attempts in the last 48h failed.
Dedicated provisioning jobs intermittently fail to assume AWS roles; blocks internal repros and delays a handful of customer onboards. Estimated affected jobs: ~12/day during peak.
1) Trigger the dedicated onboarding pipeline that uses GCP WIF->AWS role federation through auth-proxy
2) Observe the auth-proxy logs for request->response attribute mapping
3) In failing cases, the provisioner logs show downstream permission errors referencing missing 'env' or truncated 'role-session' attributes
4) Re-run with verbose STS debug: CloudTrail shows AssumeRole succeeded but session tags truncated/rewritten; provisioner denies due to absent tag guardrails
Auth-proxy change on 2026-03-08 started normalizing multivalue attributes into a single JSON-encoded string; this appears to exceed AWS STS tag length in some flows
CloudTrail evidence: 90% of failed AssumeRole calls return 200 with AssumedRoleUser but the session tag list is shorter than expected (missing 'env' or 'team')
GCP audit logs: WIF token contained attributes 'environment=prod' and 'team=platform', auth-proxy forwarded 'attributes' as 'attrs:{"environment":"prod","team":"platform"}' string which STS interprets as a single tag 'attrs' instead of separate tags
Provisioner enforces tag-based RBAC: expects 'env' and 'team' top-level tags; when tags are absent permission engine rejects requests
Reproduced locally by issuing WIF with long attribute payload -> AWS STS drops tags beyond 64 characters per tag key/value limit
Hypothesis: two contributing factors — auth-proxy JSON-encoding of attributes and STS per-tag length/truncation behavior. Some attribute values combined in a single tag causing guardrail checks to fail.
1) Temporary rollback of auth-proxy normalization to previous behavior — confirmed immediate reduction in failures in a small canary cluster
2) Short-term change in provisioner RBAC to accept 'attrs' combined tag (risk: weakens policy precision) — tested in staging, allowed repro jobs to proceed
3) Manual re-run of blocked onboards after rolling back auth-proxy in controlled window
Primary fix: update auth-proxy attribute mapping to emit individual STS session tags per attribute (key->value) and ensure each tag respects AWS limits (max 128 characters for value, 128 for key). Add explicit truncation/validation and a feature-flag to opt-in. Secondary: harden provisioner to parse combined 'attrs' tag as JSON only after verifying tag presence, emit a telemetry metric when fallback parsing is used.
Change must be rolled out to auth-proxy instances in all regions. Rollout steps: (1) add validation and flag disabled by default; (2) enable in canary in eu-west-1 for 24h; (3) monitor CloudTrail and provisioner RBAC metrics; (4) progressively enable across us-east-1 and other regions. Provisioner RBAC fallback should be maintained until full rollforward confirmed. Backout: revert to previous auth-proxy image.
In progress — a patch branch has been opened that splits attributes into individual tags and enforces per-tag length limits. Canaries scheduled for eu-west-1 on 2026-03-12. Full rollout pending successful 24h canary. Temporary mitigation (auth-proxy rollback) reduced failures; provisioner fallback parsing remains as secondary safety net.
Assign PR reviewer and merge small fix (auth-proxy) — owner: Aisha Patel
Schedule canary deployment (eu-west-1) and monitor for 24h — SRE oncall (Miguel Santos)
Update dedicated-provisioner to add metric 'session_tag_parsing.fallback' and a dashboard tile — owner: Platform Eng
Communicate to internal onboarding owners about short window where manual retries may be required

Additional notes:
SRE Lead (2026-03-12): Please include CloudTrail event id sampling in the canary run so we can correlate per-request traces.
payload.summary: Intermittent assume-role failures due to mismatched session tag attribute encoding between GCP WIF and AWS STS

payload.description:
Issue summary: Request to deliver a tag-driven onboarding gateway that provisions Slack channels, creates a matching Jira project bootstrap, and links a Confluence space using a single claim flow. Impact: currently team leads create channels and projects manually which leads to inconsistent metadata, missing owners, and unclear archival schedules. This prevents automation (retention, billing attribution) and increases support burden. Request: build an automated gateway (bot + Jira workflow + Confluence template) that accepts a small set of tags (team:, sensitivity:, lifecycle:) and performs: 1) create Slack channel with metadata and default channel settings; 2) create Jira project using 'team' tag and attach standard issue templates; 3) provision a Confluence space from the 'project bootstrap' template and add channel link; 4) register ownership and automated archival TTL based on lifecycle tag. The gateway should support claim-by-owner, request approval for private channels, and generate a traceable audit entry in the admin log. Security notes: private channel creation must require approver from security for sensitivity:high. Acceptance criteria listed below.
Minimal UX: slash command /create-project-boot or a self-service form in the provisioning portal. Tags accepted: team:<identifier>, sensitivity:{low|medium|high}, lifecycle:{ephemeral|standard|longterm}, purpose:<short text>. Default rules: ephemeral -> 30d archival TTL, standard -> 180d, longterm -> no auto-archive. Channels created under prefix team-<identifier>. Jira project key auto-suggest, Confluence space key aligned. Audit entry must include requestor and approver and link to created artifacts.
1) Slash command or portal triggers channel+Jira+Confluence creation in a single flow. 2) Created Slack channel contains pinned message with metadata tags and owner claim instructions. 3) Jira project created with template 'Project-Bootstrap-V2' and initial issue set (onboarding checklist). 4) Confluence space created and linked back in Slack channel and Jira project. 5) Audit log entry written to admin-runbook and visible in ops-dashboard. 6) Sensitivity:high requires manual approval before private channel is created. 7) TTL enforcement runs and archives ephemeral channels after 30 days if unclaimed.
- Spike conducted by platform-infra on 2026-03-05 validated Slack API scoping for channel metadata and discovery. - Confluence template requires minor adjustments to inherit project key. - Existing Jira provisioning lambda can create projects but lacks tag-driven inputs. - Approval flow best implemented via GitHub-style SSO+approver webhook or simple Slack modal with approver list. Hypothesis: combination of Slack bot + infra lambda + Jira API + Confluence REST will be sufficient. Potential blockers: mailbox for approvers, rate limits on Confluence creation during onboarding events.
Risks: accidental creation of private channels without approval, mis-specified lifecycle leading to premature archival, privilege escalation via bot scopes. Mitigations: require approver for sensitivity:high, preview modal with TTL warning, limited bot scopes and audit logs, implement permission checks in Jira project creation lambda.
Design Slack modal & slash command
Extend provisioning lambda to accept tags
Add approval webhook and approver list config
Wire Confluence template to bootstrap flow
Add audit logging to ops-dashboard
Create runbook for support escalations
Week 1: design and security review; Week 2: implement bot + lambda extension; Week 3: integrate Jira & Confluence creation; Week 4: QA in staging and runbook; Week 5: gradual rollout behind feature flag.
Maya Chen (reporter) - 2026-03-12: Filing this to reduce repeated support load from ad-hoc onboarding requests. See linked Confluence pages for templates.
Liam O'Connor (assignee) - 2026-03-12: Picking this up. First step: sketch Slack modal and identify required bot scopes. Will coordinate with Security for sensitivity:high approval flow.
Ravi Patel (Platform SRE) - 2026-03-13: Spike results show Confluence rate limit at 10 calls/min for space create in our cluster; we should queue creations or use exponential backoff. Also recommend caching team identifier namespace to avoid key collisions.
Ana Gomez (Security) - 2026-03-13: For sensitivity:high we require approver with security role and an email audit. We prefer approvals via the provisioning portal using SSO rather than ad-hoc Slack approver lists.
Liam O'Connor - 2026-03-14: Implemented PoC for Slack modal in staging at https://staging.redwood.com/provision/preview. PRs opened: see related_github_prs. Next: integrate Jira project key generation and approval gating.

Issue summary:
A recent rotation of the device attestation signing key (identity-service) appears to have invalidated existing CLI session bindings. Developer CLI clients receive repeated MFA prompts and then a hard 'session mismatch' error that prevents access to multiple internal tools (devtools-cli, runbook-runner, internal-grafana-proxy).

Impact:
- ~45 engineers unable to run infra CLI commands or access runbook tooling from corporate devices.
- Automated runbooks triggered from CI intermittently fail due to inability to exchange ephemeral session tokens.
- No broad user-facing customer impact, but critical for oncall and incident response workflows.

Environment:
- Prod control plane (identity-service) in us-west-2.
- Affected clients primarily macOS and Linux corporate laptops with device-attestation enabled.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Attempt to login with devtools-cli from a corporate laptop with device attestation enabled.
2) Complete MFA challenge when prompted.
3) Observe repeated MFA prompt cycles followed by: 'ERROR: session binding mismatch: attestation-signature-verified=false' and 401 from cli-proxy.

Expected behavior:
- Attestation signing key rotation should be seamless: new key should be trusted by the control plane and clients bound to prior attestation should either be re-chained automatically or receive a clear recovery prompt.

Actual behavior:
- Clients loop on MFA then fail with session binding mismatch. Manual logout and login sometimes works after several attempts but not consistently.

Logs / error excerpts:
- cli-proxy: "WARN session_verifier: signature_check_failed key_id=attest-2026-03-10 reason=unknown_format"
- identity-service: "ERROR attestation: signature-validation failed for device=host-2345 status=untrusted-key"
- devtools-cli client: "session binding mismatch (attestation-signature-verified=false)
  token exchange failed: 401"

Temporary workaround:
- Some engineers can bypass device-attestation by using a personal device (not allowed by policy for many oncall flows).
- Support can issue a one-time session token via internal support console for immediate access (manual, rate limited).

Next steps requested / acceptance criteria:
- Determine whether new signing key was rolled out without updating the control plane truststore or if clients are sending an old key reference.
- Reproduce on staging and identify minimal rollback or hotfix path that restores session binding for corporate devices.
- Provide mitigation plan that restores oncall access within 4 hours or an agreed mitigation that allows runbook-triggering from CI.

Install devtools-cli v2.3.1 on a corporate macOS laptop with device attestation enabled
Run 'devtools login' and follow prompts
Complete MFA when prompted until the client fails with session binding mismatch
[cli-proxy] WARN session_verifier: signature_check_failed key_id=attest-2026-03-10 reason=unknown_format
[identity-service] ERROR attestation: signature-validation failed for device=host-2345 status=untrusted-key
[devtools-cli] ERROR session binding mismatch: attestation-signature-verified=false

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 09:10 - Security (note): Need approval for any rollback of key rotation; rollback decision requires cataloging keys and audit records. Security has been looped in.
Identity team deploy log shows key rotation job succeeded but truststore config applied to cluster via templated configmap may have had a YAML encoding mismatch (base64 vs raw).
Metrics show spike in 401s from cli-proxy at 02:05 UTC, aligning with the deploy window.
Partial hotfix accepted legacy keys on one replica only; suggests config propagation or bootstrap ordering issue during rotation.
No evidence of compromised keys; rotation initiated per schedule. Security audit required before any full rollback.
Hypothesis: templated configmap failing to encode key metadata correctly for a subset of replicas leading to signature parsing errors.
Workaround in place: manual one-time session tokens and temporary legacy-key acceptance on limited replicas to restore oncall workflows.
Planned next steps: coordinate truststore reconciliation patch (small config fix) and gradual rollout to replicas with monitoring. Schedule window: 2026-03-15 04:00-05:00 UTC.
Follow-ups: add end-to-end integration test for key rotation (CI job), add alert for post-rotation 5xx/401 spike, and update runbook with explicit rollback criteria.
Security will sign off on reconciliation plan prior to full cluster change.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During our automated provisioning task sequence (SCCM-based) that performs an in-place upgrade from Windows 10 to Windows 11 22H2, the integrated fingerprint readers on several device SKUs stop responding post-upgrade. Devices finish the TS successfully, users can log in with password, but biometric login and Windows Hello setup fail and the fingerprint device does not appear in Device Manager or appears with an exclamation mark.

Impact:
- ~180 corporate devices in the last 48 hours (primarily Dell/Lenovo/HP fleet) unable to use fingerprint login.
- Blocks onboarding flow for some new hires; increases support overhead for re-provisioning or manual driver reinstalls.

Environment:
- Provisioning flow: SCCM task sequence that runs Win10->Win11 22H2 in-place upgrade image, then installs OEM driver bundle from package driver-bundle-v5.
- Affected region: us-west production provisioning pool.

Observed behavior:
- Windows Hello fingerprint setup throws: "No fingerprint devices are available".
- Windows Biometric Service (WbioSrvc) fails to start consistently.
- Device Manager shows biometric device either absent or as "Unknown device" with code 45/28.

Expected behavior:
- Biometric device present post-upgrade and OEM drivers loaded; Windows Hello setup available.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Pick affected Dell Latitude 7540 with Windows 10 21H2 baseline image.
2) Run SCCM task sequence that performs in-place upgrade to Windows 11 22H2 and applies driver-bundle-v5 and company-provisioning.ps1.
3) Complete TS and OOBE for corporate user.
4) Attempt to setup Windows Hello -> Fingerprint.

Repro rate:
- Intermittent but ~40% on same SKU in the last run. Less frequent on HP fleet (~10%).

Relevant logs and artifacts included below.

1. Execute SCCM TS: TSID 2026-PR-012 (Win10->Win11 22H2 in-place).
2. Ensure driver-bundle-v5 is applied (current package in distribution point).
3. After first user login perform: > sc query WbioSrvc and check Device Manager.
4. Capture: msinfo32 export, pnputil /enum-devices, Get-WindowsUpdateLog, and provisioning logs at C:\Windows\ccm\Logs\smsts.log.
Sample event excerpts:

Application: Windows Biometric Service (WbioSrvc)
Timestamp: 2026-03-10 02:14:37
Message: Service failed to start. Error 0x80070005

System Event ID 1536:
Device USB\VID_138A&PID_00XX not migrated due to partial or mismatched driver stack. Status: 0xC0000185

smsts.log snippet:
[2026-03-10 02:04:21] Downloading package: driver-bundle-v5
[2026-03-10 02:06:03] Driver install returned code 0x80190001 (driver package signature mismatch)

Initial triage (Aisha): Confirmed correlation with driver-bundle-v5 application stage.
Hypotheses:
- The OEM driver bundle includes legacy Win10-signed drivers incompatible with 22H2 driver-signing changes.
- SCCM applies drivers before the new kernel driver store hooks are initialized, causing PnP migration failures.
- Windows Biometric Service configuration gets corrupted and fails to start due to missing provider DLLs.

Reproduction tests (Marcus):
- Re-ran TS with driver-bundle-v4 (older) -> biometric works on 2/3 Dell units but fails on one.
- Manually reinstalling OEM driver INF via pnputil /add-driver ... /install temporarily shows device then WbioSrvc still fails to start with Access Denied when service startup attempted.
- Checked signature via Get-AuthenticodeSignature on OEM driver INF: shows SHA1 and SHA256 signatures but timestamping inconsistent between vendor certs.

Next steps planned:
- Create a trimmed driver package with only the biometric driver and signed cert chained to Microsoft (test package: driver-bio-trim-2026-03-11).
- Run TS with the trimmed package and add a 30s pause after upgrade to allow kernel post-upgrade hooks.
- Engage OEM support with vendor-signed driver artifacts and request a Microsoft-signed driver or guidance.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:03 - IT Field Ops (Carla N.): Reported two users at 03/10 new-hire orientation had to skip fingerprint enrollment; ended up enrolling PIN only. Will provide serials and imaging job IDs.
Workaround and remediation plan in progress. Actions taken so far:
- Created trimmed biometric-only driver package 'driver-bio-trim-2026-03-11' which restored biometric functionality on 80% of canary devices.
- For devices that still fail: manual re-stage via pnputil + restart of WbioSrvc, followed by user-driven Windows Hello enrollment, works in many cases.
- Plan: staged deployment via SCCM over next 48 hours in 3 waves (Canary: 20 devices; Wave1: 60 devices; Wave2: remainder ~100 devices). Rollback: rerun TS with driver-bundle-v3 if regressions found.
- OEM engagement: opened case with vendor (Case ID: OEM-2026-334) requesting a Microsoft-signed driver and confirmation of compatibility with 22H2.
- Post-deploy checklist created: verify Device Manager enumeration, sc query WbioSrvc == RUNNING, and successful Windows Hello enrollment.
Follow-ups:
- Solutions Eng to create a short KB article for field support with pnputil and service restart commands.
- Hardware team to audit failing serials for unusual firmware revisions.
- Re-evaluate current driver-bundle packaging process to prefer vendor-signed drivers chained to Microsoft.
payload.summary: Fingerprint reader becomes unresponsive after Windows 11 22H2 in-place upgrade during provisioning

Issue summary: Platform team request to create a reusable project gateway that provisions a timeboxed 'partner-collab' Slack namespace, scaffolded Confluence space, and a light-weight Jira project template for short-term audit / partner engagements.

Business impact: Teams onboarding external partners currently create ad-hoc channels and spaces which creates long-lived guest access, inconsistent retention, and manual archive handoffs. This template should reduce manual steps, improve auditability, and ensure channels/spaces are auto-archived after a TTL while preserving an export snapshot for legal/audit.

Requested features: automated Slack workspace/channel scaffolder with RBAC snapshots; guest invite timebox (Okta linked); channel TTL with auto-archive and reason tag; Confluence mirror created at provisioning time with metadata page and exported channel transcript stored (attachments limited); permission snapshot (who had access) posted to Confluence space and retained for 365 days; Jira template for tracking turnover/closeout tasks; approval flow (manager + security) before provisioning for enterprise tier pods.

Who requested: Platform product manager (partner integrations) and Security.

Urgency: P2 — not blocking infra but high friction for partner rollout and audit readiness.
1) New 'Partner-Collab' provisioning button in the internal portal that creates a Slack namespace (scoped channels), Confluence space with a metadata landing page, and a Jira project from template.
2) Guest membership is time-boxed (default 30 days) and automatically removed at TTL; TTL configurable during provisioning.
3) Channel TTL auto-archives channel and posts an audit snapshot to the Confluence space (list of members, pinned messages, exported thread attachments).
4) RBAC snapshot stored as an immutable Confluence page (read: audit-only) and accessible to Security and Compliance.
5) Approval step recorded in Jira with approvers and timestamp; provisioning blocked until approvals complete.
6) All actions are logged to the central audit log and retain an immutable entry for 365 days.
2026-03-02: Reviewed Slack APIs for enterprise GRID features — channel export requires admin-level scopes and may be rate-limited for large channels. Confluence API can store HTML/PDF export blobs but we need to confirm retention policy with Legal.
2026-03-03: Security raised question on storing message content in Confluence (PII risk). Proposed approach: redact user emails and only store thread text + attachments metadata; full export gated to Legal/Security approval.
2026-03-04: Spike run to prototype automation using existing 'channel-provisioner' Lambda. Found two blockers: (1) channel export requires 'Discovery' scopes that are only granted to workspace admins with E-Discovery enabled; (2) Okta guest provisioning API exists but requires a dedicated integration client and consent from Identity team.
Prelim estimated effort: 5 engineer-days to wire approval flow + templating; 3 engineer-days for Slack export integration with rate-limit backoff + queuing; 2 engineer-days for Confluence export & immutable snapshot page.
Maya Chen (reporter) — 2026-03-01: Opening this request after three partner rollouts where manual cleanup was missed. Example: Partner ACME project had 12 guest accounts remaining after project ended.
Jonas Patel (Security) — 2026-03-02: Security: need to confirm Legal signoff before storing message-level exports in Confluence. Can we instead store a hashed transcript + metadata and link to E-Discovery export behind access control?
Avery Kim (Platform Eng) — 2026-03-03: We can scaffold the Slack + Confluence resources via the provisioning API. Channel export requires discovery scopes. I'll open an integration request with Identity for the Okta client.
Action: Avery to prototype with small test channel and report rate limits.
SRE (Alex R.) — 2026-03-04: Note on rate limits: we should queue export jobs and use exponential backoff to avoid throttles. Also recommend retention TTL enforcement via a scheduled job so archive is robust to bot failures.
Maya Chen — 2026-03-05: Updated acceptance criteria to require immutable RBAC snapshot and 365-day accessibility. Please include GSuite/Okta guest mapping in the export so compliance can trace accounts.
1) Platform Eng to validate Slack export scopes with Workspace Admin and Identity (Okta). 2) Legal to confirm allowed export content and redaction rules. 3) Build approval workflow prototype in Jira with required approvers. 4) Deliver PoC automation for a single partner template (no exports) to validate provisioning flow, then iterate to add export + Confluence snapshot.
Owner: Platform Eng (Avery Kim). Target: prototype by 2026-03-20.
Draft plan accepted; implementation gated on Legal approval for message export. Provisioning automation without message export can be piloted for one partner while approvals are pending. Will convert to action tasks once spike confirms API scopes and Identity integration.
Manual checklist: Platform Ops can create a Slack channel, invite guests with expiry, and manually create a Confluence page with a CSV list of members. Documented in the partner runbook linked above.
This ticket should be routed to Platform Eng and Security, and tracked from the Onboarding epic once approved. Retain visibility in #platform-ops and #security-review channels.

payload.description:
Issue summary: At ~2026-03-10T08:22Z monitoring alerted on a 15-minute spike in SCIM provisioning events originating from a third-party HR onboarding connector (vendor-hrflow). The majority of created accounts were standard employee accounts, but ~22 accounts were created with a non-default role label that maps to the 'developer-repo-admin' IAM binding. Impact: Potential unauthorized creation of privileged collaborator invites across multiple orgs; risk of lateral privilege escalation if accounts are active. Environment: Production tenant, us-east region. Observed behaviour: Sudden jump from ~2 SCIM events/min to ~240 events/min; provisioning API tokens used exclusively by the vendor connector. Sample events indicate use of a custom 'role' attribute in the SCIM payload that the provisioner incorrectly accepted and mapped to an internal role. Steps to reproduce (investigation steps): 1) Query SCIM audit events in /api/v1/scim/events from 2026-03-10T08:00Z to 2026-03-10T08:40Z. 2) Inspect provisioning token owner: vendor-hrflow@partners.redwood. 3) Replay a sanitized SCIM payload in staging to verify role mapping behavior. 4) Check recent changes to scim-provisioner mapping rules and vendor-facing docs. Logs: See attached audit snippets (log ids scim-20260310-0823-a .. scim-20260310-0835-c) for examples of the rogue role attribute. Initial mitigation performed: Disabled vendor-hrflow SCIM connector token at 2026-03-10T08:28Z; placed an emergency validation rule to reject non-whitelisted role attributes at 2026-03-10T08:35Z.
Timeline: 08:22Z alert triggered by infra-alerts on provisioning rate. 08:25Z triage by on-call SRE (Arya Patel). 08:28Z token disabled. 08:35Z emergency validation pushed. Findings: - The vendor recently rolled out a 'role' extension to their SCIM payload to request initial repo access. Our mapping table in scim-provisioner treats unknown role strings as 'closest match' using a fuzzy map and a fallback heuristic that in this case selected 'developer-repo-admin'. - The vendor connector made ~4,100 API calls during the 30-minute window; 22 resulted in privileged-role assignments. - No sign of direct credential compromise of the vendor account; vendor support logged a misconfiguration on their side that sent extended attributes in bulk after a CSV import. - Audit trail indicates no privileged actions executed by the newly created accounts (no pushes, no IAM changes) as of investigation time. Hypotheses: (a) Vendor misconfiguration unintentionally forwarded role attribute; (b) A malicious CSV uploaded to vendor portal caused attribute injection; (c) Attack chain via vendor admin account compromise is possible but low confidence. Data collected: SCIM payload samples, token metadata, IP addresses for vendor flows (range 18.197.0.0/16), temporally matched auth logs, and recent deploys affecting scim-provisioner mapping code (deploy ef12ab3). Next steps: 1) Validate whether any invited accounts accepted invites and completed SSO; 2) Force expiry of affected invites and require re-provisioning via manual SR; 3) Run a privileged activity scan for the affected accounts (pushes, permission changes); 4) Engage vendor security (ticket #VND-1924) for root cause and audit; 5) Prepare post-mortem if evidence of compromise found.

Additional notes:
Mitigation steps applied: - Revoked vendor-hrflow SCIM provisioning token and blocked their IP range temporarily. - Rolled back fuzzy-role mapping commit (ef12ab3) and deployed explicit role whitelist in scim-provisioner. - Expired all pending invites associated with the 22 affected provisioning events and required manual re-issue. - Requested vendor rotate their integration credentials and provided remediation guidance. - Performed a privileged-activity scan (no suspicious actions found). Follow-up actions: - Security and IAM to implement permanent deny-by-default mapping and new unit tests for scim attribute handling (owner: Liam O'Connor). - Schedule joint post-incident review with vendor (owner: Maya Chen). Incident remains open pending vendor RCA and completion of follow-up items.
Implement deny-by-default role mapping in scim-provisioner (owner: Liam O'Connor)
Add unit and integration tests for unknown SCIM attributes (owner: Platform QA)
Vendor RCA and credential rotation confirmation (owner: Vendor Security)
Confluence post-incident writeup and customer notification draft (owner: Security Communications)

Issue summary:
Support team noticed that the approval button on internal access request flows (Support Portal -> Access Requests) returns a 200 UI response but does not advance the request status when the requestor's Okta group membership includes a recently renamed group suffix. Impact: approvers click Approve; the UI shows success toast but the request remains in Pending and downstream provisioning does not run.

Impact:
- Internal access requests for a subset of employees are not being completed automatically by support tooling.
- Delays in provisioning MFA devices and runbook elevation for ~12 engineers in prod-us-east.

Environment:
- Production (support portal, region: us-east). Okta SCIM connector v2.1.4; identity-service v3.8.0; support-portal v1.6.2.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Identify a user with an Okta group that was renamed in the last 24 hours from suffix "-contractor-temp" to "-contractor-temp-v2".
2) Open Support Portal -> Access Requests -> pick a request submitted by that user.
3) Click Approve. Observe toast "Approval recorded" but request status remains Pending after refresh.
4) Check identity-provisioner logs for the request correlation ID.

Expected behavior:
- Approve transitions request to Approved and triggers identity-provisioner job.

Actual behavior:
- UI indicates success, but state backend does not persist transition. No provisioning job visible. Identity-provisioner receives no webhook for that request.

Logs / Observed traces:
- support-portal produced 200 for POST /api/requests/12345/approve. Response payload: {"ok":true, "message":"Approval recorded", "request_state":"pending"}.
- identity-service audit log contains: "received approval callback request: request_id=12345, user_groups=[\"eng-team\", \"infra-contractor-temp-v2\"]" and then "no matching group mapping for scope 'infra-contractor-temp-v2' -> skipping role resolution".
- SCIM-connector logs show group rename event processed ~22 minutes before the first affected approval attempt.
- No provisioning record created in provisioner-db for request 12345.

Initial hypothesis:
- Group suffix rename changed the normalized group-key used by our RBAC mapping table; the approval handler validates expected group keys and rejects role resolution silently (returns success to UI but does not persist state). Might be a gap in group canonicalization path after SCIM rename events.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally against staging SCIM snapshot: approval handler path returns success when canary flag "web-approve-no-fail" is true and logs a non-fatal role-resolution-mismatch. That flag is set in prod for backward compatibility.
- Identity-team mapping table currently stores canonical_group_keys without a normalization pass that strips historical suffix variants. SCIM rename event writes a new group record instead of updating canonical, leaving stale mapping referencing old key.
- Support-portal approval flow persists state only after role-resolution returns at least one resolved role. If no roles resolved, code path treats operation as idempotent and returns 200 without a backend state update.
- Affected requests correlate to users whose only mapped role came from the renamed group. Users with other groups succeed normally.

Temporary workaround:
- Manual approval by admins via identity-admin console persists state when forcing roles. Support runbook: use identity-admin -> find request -> click "force-approve and assign roles". Documented workaround ID: RB-2026-01. This requires SRE/operator action.

Proposed mitigation / next steps:
1) Short-term patch: change approval handler to persist request state regardless of role-resolution result (and mark request with a diagnostic label) so provisioning can be retried once mapping is fixed. Target: deploy hotfix to prod-us-east by 2026-03-04.
2) Medium-term fix: update SCIM rename handler to preserve canonical group keys or emit a mapping alias when rename occurs. Identity-team to create migration script to backfill alias entries.
3) Add telemetry/alert when approval processed but no roles resolved (new metric: approvals.role_resolution_misses).
4) Postmortem with runbook updates to prevent silent approvals.

Owner: Diego Alvarez (identity-service).

2026-03-01 10:42 - Support (L. Patel): Reported issue after approving 7 requests; 3 affected. Attached screenshots and one correlation ID: req=12345. Marking high visibility for oncall.
2026-03-01 11:05 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): I can reproduce with a staging SCIM snapshot. Initial guess: group canonicalization mismatch after SCIM rename. Investigating identity-service mapping table.

Additional notes:
2026-03-02 09:12 - Support (L. Patel): Applied manual workaround per RB-2026-01 for affected users; all requests now show Approved. Recording steps in the internal runbook.
In progress: hotfix PR created to persist approval state and surface diagnostic labels; identity-team preparing migration to create alias mappings for renamed groups. Manual workaround used for immediate cases.
Merge hotfix PR and deploy to prod-us-east (owner: Diego)
Run alias backfill migration in maintenance window (owner: R. Singh)
Add alert and dashboard panel for approvals.role_resolution_misses (owner: Observability)

Issue summary: New private deployment onboarding for customer 'BeaconHealth' requires cross-account IAM roles in both AWS and GCP, plus KMS key access and scoped S3/GCS read permissions. Impact: deployment cannot be completed for Dedicated/Private offering until credentials and role delegation are configured. Environment: private control plane connecting to customer VPCs in us-east-1 and europe-west1; staging and prod clusters use separate AWS accounts and one GCP project for telemetry.

Requested by: Solutions Engineering (Lena Novak).

Desired outcome:
- Create/approve cross-account IAM role in Redwood AWS org with limited assume-role trust to the Private deployment account and SolutionsEng principal.
- Grant KMS:Decrypt and GenerateDataKey for the specific CMKs used by private deployments in prod and staging.
- Create GCP service account with Workload Identity binding and allow impersonation from Redwood control plane service account.
- Attach least-privilege policies for S3/GCS read access to model artifacts buckets, and logging write to dedicated logging buckets.

Business justification: Customer onboarding is schedule-bound (integration window next week). This is an internal support access request tied to a paid private deployment contract.
1) Attempted deployment via private-deploy CLI in staging: command fails during artifact sync step.
2) Error: 'AccessDenied: not authorized to use CMK arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333:key/xxxx' and 'PermissionDenied: serviceAccount X cannot impersonate'.
3) Verified that the service account/role mapping was not present in target customer-connected accounts.
4) Reproduced in both staging and prod accounts with same failure patterns.
aws-cli error snippet: [2026-03-09T16:12:04Z] botocore.exceptions.ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User: arn:aws:sts::444555666:assumed-role/rdw-private-deploy-role/session is not authorized to use key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333:key/xxxx.
GCP error: permissionDenied: Service account projects/-/serviceAccounts/rdw-control@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com does not have permission to impersonate serviceAccount:beacon-private-sa@beacon-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- Confirmed via AWS CloudTrail that assume-role attempts reach the target account but fail on kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey due to CMK key policy (key policy currently restricts to account root + explicit admin role).
- Checked IAM role trust policy: Redwood role exists but the principal list omits the SolutionsEng role in some staging accounts (race during templatized account bootstrap).
- GCP: Workload Identity pool binding present in prod but not in staging; service account impersonation permission (roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator) missing for rdw-control SA.
- Hypothesis: recent bootstrap changes to account templates removed automatic KMS key grants and Workload Identity bindings for private deployments. See infra commit 1a2b3c linked above.
- Risk: If we grant broader KMS permissions, we could exceed least-privilege. Need to patch CMK policy with explicit role ARNs only for the deployment role and time-bound elevation where possible.
Lena Novak (Solutions Eng) - 2026-03-10: Customer integration window is 2026-03-17; we need confirmation of ETA for role creation.
Aisha Patel (IAM/Security) - 2026-03-10: Adding this to internal access queue. Will validate least-privilege policy draft and return with required ARNs.
Dana Ortiz (SRE Lead) - 2026-03-11: Noted inconsistency across bootstrapped accounts. Team will prepare a small corrective repo change; prefer role-only CMK policy updates rather than opening key to account.
Marco Liu (Cloud Infra) - 2026-03-12: Created PRs for role mapping and KMS policy adjustments. Need review from security. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/872 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/iam-roles/pull/211.
Aisha Patel (IAM/Security) - 2026-03-12: Reviewed PRs and left comments requesting time-limited condition on assume-role and audit tag for every assume. Also requested GCP service account binding template for reproducibility.
Workaround: Solutions Eng used a manual temporary admin API key in staging to complete artifact sync for BeaconHealth while infra prepared least-privilege fixes. Permanent fix steps applied: 1) Updated CMK key policy to include explicit allow for rdw-private-deploy-role ARN in both prod and staging CMKs, with kms:ViaService condition to reduce blast radius. 2) Applied roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to rdw-control@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com on the Beacon GCP project for the beacon-private-sa service account and added Workload Identity binding template. 3) Deployed infra PRs that patch account bootstrap templates to include KMS grants and Workload Identity bindings for future accounts. 4) Created follow-up ticket INT-5390 to add automated verification in account bootstrap CI.
Post-action verification: deployment completed successfully in staging and prod for BeaconHealth on 2026-03-12. No further permission errors observed.
Follow-ups: schedule a cross-team review (SRE, Security, Solutions Eng) to standardize CMK key policies and Workload Identity templates.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Request from Finance (Cost Analytics team) to grant a third-party consultant (ClearView Analytics) temporary access to our AWS billing and cost telemetry in the production AWS Organization. Goal is a 2-week audit to validate cost attribution and assist with Reserved Instance/commit recommendations.

Background:
- Consultant is not an employee and cannot be added to our IdP.
- Existing procedure prefers cross-account IAM roles with a permission boundary and short expiry.
- We have runbooks for vendor access but previous requests lacked permission boundaries and caused escalations (see linked issues).

Requested access:
- Create an AWS IAM role in the Redwood-production account (redwood-prod-analytics-role-extern-clearview) assumable by the consultant's AWS account ID 987654321012 via sts:AssumeRole.
- Attach a restrictive inline policy scoped to read-only billing/Cost Explorer/Cur/Tags/S3-billing-bucket-listing and Athena read on billing datasets. Example actions: "ce:GetCostAndUsage", "s3:GetObject", "athena:StartQueryExecution", "athena:GetQueryResults".
- Enforce a permission boundary that limits any escalations (explicit deny for iam:CreatePolicy, sts:AssumeRoleTo, s3:PutObject, kms:CreateKey, and any write/delete actions across billing/data buckets).
- Maximum session duration of 1 hour and automatic expiry of role trust after 14 days.

Impact:
- Low risk if scoped correctly; high sensitivity around billing buckets that contain project identifiers. Must avoid any write access.

Security considerations:
- Consultant identity proofing completed by Finance and Security (email thread attached in comments).
- Require CloudTrail entries enabled for sts:AssumeRole with an alert to #sec-ops and #cloud-ops on first use.
- Require a short-lived credentials audit and a deprovision checklist executed at expiry.

Steps taken so far:
1) Finance requested access 2026-03-10.
2) Security provided vendor assessment summary 2026-03-11.
3) Draft IAM policy prepared in infra repo (see related_github_prs).

Proposed timeline:
- Role created and trust policy applied by 2026-03-15.
- Acceptance test: Security and Finance validate they can assume role and run a sample Cost Explorer query by 2026-03-16.
- Automatic trust removal day 15 after creation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Consultant can only read billing-related resources, cannot modify or escalate privileges.
- Trail logs show sts:AssumeRole events and there is an alert in #sec-ops.
- Role is automatically disabled after 14 days and a deprovision checklist is recorded in Confluence.

Next steps / owner actions:
- Assignee (Rishi) to review draft policy and create IAM role.
- Security (Reviewer) to sanity-check permission boundary.
- Cloud-ops to wire alert to #sec-ops and verify CloudTrail event retention.

Notes:
- If any additional Athena or S3 prefixes are required beyond the billing bucket, they must be added via a change request and reviewed by Security.
- Do not grant Organization-level read unless absolutely necessary; prefer account-scoped permissions.

Additional notes:

payload.description:
Issue summary:
After an automated KMS key rewrap for the S3 bucket used as the CI build cache (s3://redwood-ci-cache), CI jobs started failing to fetch cached layers. Runners report cache decryption errors and several release pipelines have been stuck in the 'Prepare' phase for ~3 hours.

Impact:
- Multiple release pipelines (canary + stable) are blocked and cannot proceed past dependency fetch.
- Queue length for release runners on prod-us-east increased from ~10 to ~65 pending jobs.
- Increased build times for affected jobs (cold builds) and risk of missing release windows.

Environment:
- Environment: prod-us-east
- Components affected: CI runner pool, artifact cache (S3), KMS key used for SSE-KMS, release pipelines

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Trigger a release pipeline that uses the cached build layers from s3://redwood-ci-cache.
2) Runner attempts GET object with SSE-KMS; S3 returns 403 and logs a KMS:Decrypt failure in CloudTrail for the envelope key.
3) Job enters retry loop and eventually reports cache fetch failure and keeps the pipeline stuck in Prepare.

Relevant logs and signals:
- CloudTrail shows Decrypt failures for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333444:key/abcd-efgh-1234 at 2026-03-10T02:14:03Z.
- S3 access logs show x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id changed at 2026-03-10T01:58:12Z (rewrap event).
- Runner logs (build-rt-03) excerpt: "ERROR: cache decryption failed: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key ..."
- CI queue metric: runner_pending_count.prod-us-east increased to 65 at peak.

Hypothesis / initial investigation:
- An automated KMS rewrap job rotated the envelope keys for the bucket. New key policy/aliases introduced a tighter principal restriction that excludes the CI runner role used by self-hosted runners. As a result, S3 objects now require the new key for decryption but the runner IAM principal lacks kms:Decrypt on the new key.
- Alternative hypothesis: the key ID alias moved to a different account (cross-account rewrap) and the runner role's trust policy is missing a condition.

Temporary mitigation observed to work:
- Restoring previous key alias (alias/ci-cache-prev) allowed runners to decrypt objects again for a subset of objects that retained the old key metadata.
- Manually granting kms:Decrypt on the new key to the runner role allowed a single test pipeline to proceed (verified by SRE:ened).

Workaround applied so far:
- SRE temporarily added kms:Decrypt permission for role arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ci-runner-prod to the new key policy to restore immediate pipeline throughput. This is a mitigation only; revert requires discussion with security.

Investigation notes:
- Security change log shows an automated rewrap executed by the key-rotation Lambda at 2026-03-10T01:55Z. The Lambda replaced the CMK alias and updated key policy according to the new template which restricts decrypt to a narrower set of principals.
- There is a gap: key-rotation Lambda repo (github.com/redwood/infra-key-rotation) PR #78 changed the policy template; linked PR reference: github.com/redwood/infra-key-rotation/pull/78.
- A runbook for KMS rewrap exists but does not include a validation step to confirm CI IAM principals are listed in new policy.

Next steps / proposed remediation:
1) Security & SRE to coordinate a controlled update to the key policy: re-add ci-runner-prod role as delegated decrypt principal and add automated verification test that simulates runner decrypt request.
2) Update key-rotation Lambda to include a post-rotation validation step that runs a decrypt check using a staging object and the CI principal.
3) Backfill: scan S3 objects to identify those re-encrypted under the new key and verify access patterns. Confirm if any objects lost previous key metadata.
4) Add a pre-rotation change-control gating in Confluence and Slack (#infra-ops) to notify Release Engineering 24 hours before rewraps that impact shared caches.

Related links:
- CloudTrail event sample: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail/home?region=us-east-1
- Key rotation repo PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra-key-rotation/pull/78
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/KMS+Key+Rotation+Runbook

Resolution status:
- Mitigation in place (temporary key policy change). Full remediation pending policy update and CI validation automation.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 03:42 - SRE Oncall (Ravi Kothari): CloudTrail shows KMS:Decrypt AccessDenied for new key. Suspect key policy change during automated rewrap. Temporarily applied kms:Decrypt to ci-runner role to get pipelines moving.
2026-03-11 09:18 - Security (Ivan Cho): Key rotation Lambda PR #78 introduced tighter policy. We will coordinate to add the ci-runner role back, but need an audit trail and post-rotation validation steps.
Key-rotation Lambda changed key alias and policy without running a decrypt validation using the CI principal. CloudTrail confirms Decrypt failures started immediately after alias swap. There is an existing review step in the rotation PR but no automated verification. SRE verified temporary policy grant restores functionality; security wants formal change and audit log. Will add a preflight decrypt test to the Lambda and a Confluence change notice. Expected ETA for full remediation: 2026-03-16.
Temporarily granted kms:Decrypt on new CMK to role arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/ci-runner-prod. This restored pipeline throughput. Workaround is temporary and should be revoked after policy fix and validation are in place.
1) Security to approve adding ci-runner role to key policy with audit comments. 2) Infra to patch key-rotation Lambda to run decrypt verification and rollback on failure. 3) Release Eng to be notified 24h prior to next rewrap. 4) Post-incident: add test to release pipeline that validates cache decrypt during PRs that touch infra-key-rotation.
Mitigation applied; awaiting permanent policy update and automation.
payload.summary: CI build cache decryption fails after S3 SSE-KMS rewrap; release pipelines stuck in Prepare stage

Issue summary: After a change in Okta group id formatting in the SCIM sync (rolled 2026-03-11), multiple internal tools are unable to resolve RBAC roles for users who are members of affected groups. Impact: Users see 403s when accessing the internal model-insights and debug-runbooks portals; just-in-time elevation and impersonation flows fail. Environment: prod | us-east | identity-proxy v3.18.1 behind edge-proxy v2.6. Steps to reproduce: 1) Confirm a user is member of an Okta group that was recently updated. 2) Call /v1/internal/resolve-role using user token (or review request headers from an affected service). 3) Observe role resolution error. Observed behavior: Identity proxy receives X-Okta-Groups header with group identifiers that include a new prefix and url-safe base64 encoding; RBAC service stores canonical group ids without the prefix and without padding which causes lookup misses. Expected behavior: Group IDs should canonicalize to the same identifiers stored in RBAC and Okta SCIM, or the identity-proxy should normalize incoming group ids before calling the RBAC service.
1) Use an affected user account (member of updated Okta group).
2) Trigger a login to model-insights (or inspect a failing API call).
3) Check the request headers on identity-proxy (X-Okta-Groups) and compare with RBAC store entries.
4) Attempt role resolution via internal admin endpoint: /internal/admin/roles/resolve?user=<userid> and note missing roles.
[2026-03-12T08:14:02Z] identity-proxy: INFO incoming headers: X-Okta-Groups=[ok_UG9zZF9iYXNlNjQ%3D, ok_X3Jvb3Q%3D]
[2026-03-12T08:14:02Z] rbac-service: WARN role-lookup miss for group id 'UG9zZF9iYXNlNjQ'
[2026-03-12T08:14:02Z] model-insights: ERROR 403 user uid=alice@example.com missing roles
(Notes: header values appear URL-encoded; RBAC store entries use plain base64 without 'ok_' prefix or percent-encoding.)
Okta SCIM team confirmed a deploy on 2026-03-11 added an 'ok_' prefix and started emitting url-safe base64 with padding stripped for group IDs to support a new internal index.
Edge-proxy (v2.6) percent-encodes some header values when forwarding; identity-proxy decodes but does not strip the 'ok_' prefix or re-pad base64, so RBAC lookups fail.
Reproduced locally by simulating header values from Okta and observing RBAC lookup flow; adding a normalization step in identity-proxy fixes lookup in our test harness.
No evidence of user account creation or deletion; this is a canonicalization/regression issue rather than a permission removal.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 14:40 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Edge-proxy is percent-encoding header values when proxying to identity-proxy; that combined with 'ok_' prefix causes double-encoded values to reach RBAC. Suggest identity-proxy should perform decode -> strip prefix -> re-pad base64 -> lookup.
Workaround applied: identity-proxy v3.18.2 (hotfix) deployed to prod-us-east with a header normalization middleware that URL-decodes X-Okta-Groups, strips the 'ok_' prefix, and pads base64 strings before forwarding to RBAC. Long-term: coordinate Okta SCIM change with RBAC canonicalization and add an integration test in identity-proxy suite.
Hotfix rolled at 2026-03-14 03:12 UTC to prod-us-east; observed role resolution success for previously affected users. Okta SCIM team will add a compatibility header for 2 release cycles; we will revert normalization once all services are migrated or a mutual canonicalization strategy is agreed.
1) Add integration test for Okta group id variants in identity-proxy test suite (owner: Aisha).
2) Schedule coordinated change-window with Okta SCIM for canonical id rollout (owner: Priya).
3) Audit other services that consume X-Okta-Groups header for similar assumptions (owner: SRE).
payload.summary: Okta group identifier format change prevents RBAC role resolution for internal tooling

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During Dedicated customer onboarding (acct: rw-dedicated-205), newly-created ephemeral IAM roles and cross-account bindings are not being recognized by the Dedicated provisioner for ~10-30 minutes after creation. This blocks instance bootstrapping and agent registration, causing onboarding to stall.

Impact:
- One enterprise Dedicated onboarding is delayed (customer facing).
- Provisioner repeatedly times out creating GPU pools and fails health-checks.
- Risk: SLA miss for Dedicated onboarding window; engineering time spent manual-troubleshooting.

Environment:
- Dedicated provisioning pipeline (k8s provisioner service) running in prod us-east.
- Affected cloud accounts: AWS: 111122223333 (customer-managed), AWS: 444455556666 (ops bridge account).
- Identity paths used: cross-account assume-role via ops-broker, STS sessions created with session tags.

Expected behavior:
- New IAM roles and role-attachment policies should be immediately available for assume-role flows; provisioner should proceed without manual retry.
1) Trigger Dedicated onboarding run for customer acct 111122223333 using provisioning job v2026-03-12.
2) Provisioner creates role 'DedicatedProvisioner-ephemeral-<random>' in ops bridge account and attaches trust policy.
3) Provisioner attempts sts:AssumeRole into the new role for instance bootstrap.
4) AssumeRole fails with AccessDenied for 10-30 minutes, then begins to succeed without other config changes.
Provisioner logs (excerpt):
- 2026-03-12T18:02:14Z ERROR assume_role failed: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::444455556666:assumed-role/ops-provisioner-session is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/DedicatedProvisioner-ephemeral-7421
- 2026-03-12T18:07:33Z WARN retrying assume_role (attempt 5)
- 2026-03-12T18:12:21Z INFO assume_role succeeded
Associated CloudTrail events show role creation at 2026-03-12T18:01:58Z and subsequent PutRolePolicy calls. No admin revokes recorded.
Initial hypotheses:
- IAM eventual consistency / IAM cache window in AWS for cross-account trust changes.
- Org SCP or IAM propagation lag due to recent org policy changes (we rolled org tagging enforcement yesterday).
- STS session tag truncation or size causing policy conditions to not match immediately.
- Provisioner using a cached credentials path / role ARN that needs refresh.

What we've checked so far:
- Verified role exists and trust policy includes ops-provisioner ARN.
- CloudTrail shows role and policy put events before failed AssumeRole attempts.
- No deny entries in Access Advisor or service control policies at timestamp of failures.
- Tested manual assume-role from an ops engineer machine immediately after creation: initially received AccessDenied, succeeded ~11 minutes later.
- Confirmed provisioner retries succeed without code changes.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Updated provisioning runbook to wait 15 minutes after role creation before first assume-role attempt when creating ephemeral roles. This is live for current onboarding runs.

Next investigatory actions planned:
- Open AWS support ticket with Cloud Support to verify backend eventual-consistency windows for cross-account trust changes and tagging conditions.
- Add extra diagnostic tracing: capture IAM/GetRole and sts:GetCallerIdentity immediately before and after create to compare policy eval.
- Audit recent org-policy/tagging changes (rolled 2026-03-11) for any propagation impacts.
- Consider switching approach to pre-create ephemeral roles earlier in pipeline and promote to active state via a toggle to avoid on-the-fly creation race windows.
2026-03-12 | Marco Liu: Took ownership. Reproduced locally using a sandbox account; observed same ~12min gap. Added debug to provisioner to emit full assume-role error metadata.
2026-03-12 | Elena Ruiz (Security): Confirmed no org SCP denies at the time. Raised that we changed org tag enforcement policy yesterday; could be related.
2026-03-13 | Marco Liu: Filed AWS SR 789203423 (internal reference). AWS support requested CloudTrail snippets and role ARNs; provided. AWS acknowledged this may be an eventual-consistency window and is investigating internal replication logs.
2026-03-13 | SRE Oncall (Carlos Mendes): Implemented temporary 15-minute pause in provisioning CI for ephemeral role path and reran the onboarding job; job progressed to agent registration after pause. Logged workaround in runbook section 'ephemeral-role-wait'.
Workaround applied: provisioner now enforces a configurable wait (default 15m) after creating ephemeral cross-account roles. Long-term: engineering to implement pre-provision phase and consult with AWS on fixing replication/propagation. Pending AWS SR outcome and internal follow-ups.
payload.summary: Cloud account permission propagation delay blocking Dedicated onboarding — ephemeral role grants not visible

comments: 2026-03-10T09:42:00Z Maya Chen: Received multiple reports from on-site engineers about SSH sessions dropping after moving between desks. Repro steps and initial tcpdump attached. Marking P1 due to repeatability.

2026-03-11T03:15:00Z Lena Brooks: Emergency changes applied (DHCP lease increase + conntrack timeout bump). Applied to dhcp-prod-01 then synced to dhcp-prod-02. Monitoring in progress. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/networking-config/commit/4f3d2a1 for dhcp template change.
2026-03-12T09:10:00Z Maya Chen: After MDM push of new WireGuard keepalive, no further reports during 48h monitoring window. Closing incident. Action items added to backlog.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Corporate laptops roaming between SF-HQ APs sometimes get a new DHCP lease while the WireGuard VPN is active. When the client receives a different internal IP from DHCP and the VPN reconnection sequence runs concurrently with Wi-Fi reassociation, established TCP sessions (notably SSH to bastion) reset.

Impact:
- Affects ~12 engineers intermittently at SF-HQ during high density times (lunch/standups).
- Active SSH sessions to internal services drop and need re-authentication.
- Productivity interruption; considered P1 due to repeated disruptions for on-site engineers.

Environment:
- Office: SF-HQ main floor (AP pool: ap-sf-main-*).
- VPN: WireGuard managed by internal profile (wg-redwood-corp).
- DHCP server: isc-dhcpd cluster behind haproxy (dhcp-prod-01/02).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Connect corp laptop to SF-HQ wifi (ap-sf-main-21).
2) SSH to bastion (bastion.sf.redwood.ai) and establish long-running session (e.g., tail -f, tmux).
3) Walk across to a different AP coverage area or cause reassociation (open/close laptop lid).
4) Laptop triggers Wi-Fi roaming; shortly after, DHCP lease renew/REQUEST occurs and client gets different internal IP.
5) WireGuard tries to refresh peer endpoint and re-establish tunnels; ephemeral NAT/conntrack mappings on edge firewall are torn or mismatched -> TCP sessions reset.

Observed behavior:
- SSH sessions drop with TCP RST from client side.
- WireGuard logs show quick rekey/reconnect but the timing overlaps with DHCP grant.
- DHCP logs show lease assigned to same MAC but different IP within seconds.
- Firewall conntrack table shows short NAT timeout entries for ephemeral ports and drops on new mapping.

Expected behavior:
- Roaming should preserve VPN session continuity and existing TCP flows should survive short DHCP renewals or the client should rebind without breaking active connections.

Initial triage notes:
- Verified with tcpdump on client: captured DHCPREQUEST/DHCPACK followed by WireGuard handshake.
- Checked DHCP server logs (/var/log/dhcpd.log) around event: multiple rapid lease events for the same MAC (30s lease window).
- Firewall (edge-fw-01) conntrack timeouts were default (60s for ESTABLISHED NAT buckets), which allowed mapping expiration during reconnection window.
- AP controller (Aruba) logs show fast reassociation (<200ms) but client-side DHCP client triggered full lease refresh due to aggressive client config (dhclient scripts).

Attachments / useful artifacts:
- tcpdump snippet (redacted): DHCPREQUEST from 00:16:3e:ab:cd:ef -> DHCPACK 10.10.32.45 at 2026-03-09T12:14:21Z
- WireGuard debug logs (redacted) showing handshake at 12:14:22Z and immediate endpoint switch attempts.
- DHCP server excerpt: "lease 10.10.32.45 { starts 3 2026/03/09 12:14:21; ends 3 2026/03/09 12:15:21; binding state active; hw-address 00:16:3e:ab:cd:ef; }"

Business/owner impact:
- On-site engineering velocity degraded during peak hours. No customer-facing outages.

Next steps planned during triage:
- Short-term workaround: apply DHCP reservation for corporate device OUI range and increase lease time for corporate scope; bump firewall conntrack timeout; increase WireGuard keepalive to reduce race window.
- Long-term: adjust client DHCP client scripts to perform graceful rebind instead of full release/renew on roam; coordinate with AP controller team to tune roaming hints; add conntrack-sticky rules for corp device ranges.

Resolution summary:
- Applied emergency change 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC: increased DHCP scope lease for corporate devices from 30s -> 3600s and added a DHCP reservation rule for corp device OUI block.
- Increased conntrack timeout on edge firewalls from 60s -> 300s for NATed wireguard sessions (firewall rule id 2107).
- Pushed WireGuard client config update (keepsalive=25) via SSO-managed MDM the morning of 2026-03-12.
- Post-change monitoring for 48h showed no recurrence for affected users.

Follow-ups / remediation backlog:
- PR created to update DHCP server template with corporate scope defaults (see related_github_prs).
- Engineering to update client roaming script: ticket INT-892001 created to track graceful rebind change.
- Confluence runbook updated with diagnostic commands and quick remediation steps.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:05 - SRE (Lena Brooks): Collected dhcpd logs and edge firewall conntrack snapshot. Observed 30s leases on corporate scope and premature conntrack churn. Hypothesis: short DHCP lease plus client behavior causes IP flip during VPN rekey. Will test increasing lease for corp scope in staging.
2026-03-10 16:20 - WiFi Vendor (Aruba Support): Confirmed AP-side fast roam is functioning; suggested tuning client roaming aggressiveness and verifying DHCP helper behavior across controller nodes.
2026-03-12 11:45 - IT Ops (Omar Patel): Created follow-up ticket INT-892001 to implement client-side graceful rebind logic and updated Confluence with runbook edits.
Diagnostics performed: client tcpdump, dhcpd logs, AP controller logs, firewall conntrack dumps. Key observations: rapid lease renew (30s) in corporate scope; DHCP server returning different IP quickly even for same MAC (likely due to aggressive scope/rotation setting in DHCP template); WireGuard handshake occurs immediately after DHCPACK and new internal IP causes NAT mapping mismatch leading to TCP reset. Temporary mitigation tested by increasing DHCP lease in staging and observing no session loss during roaming. Firewall conntrack sticky rule verified to maintain mapping when new handshake arrives.
Emergency remediation completed: DHCP lease for corporate scope set to 3600s, DHCP reservation rules added for corp OUI block, firewall conntrack NAT timeout extended, WireGuard client keepalive increased via MDM. Monitoring showed zero reproductions after fixes. Recommended medium-term tasks: change client dhclient behavior to rebind, add DHCP reservation for registered devices, and add unit tests to DHCP provisioning code (PR created).
payload.summary: DHCP lease rotation causes VPN client IP flap after Wi-Fi roam, resetting SSH sessions

payload.description:
Issue summary:
- New hire (promoted to manager) cannot reach Admin Console after Okta group promotion. User sees SSO redirect loop or 'session invalid' page intermittently. Works for some engineering managers but not others.

Impact:
- One engineering manager unable to access admin tools (user management, billing view) during ramp. Potential operational risk if more promotions fail. No customer-facing outage, internal productivity impact.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east) using Okta OIDC SSO integrated with Redwood Console. Affected user session created via browser (Chrome Mac). Okta groups are used to map to console RBAC roles.

Steps to reproduce (reported by user):
1) Engineer added to Okta group 'eng-managers' by People Ops.
2) User clicks 'Open Admin Console' link or navigates to console.redwood.ai.
3) Okta redirects to Redwood SSO callback.
4) Console returns 'Session invalid' or redirects to login again (sometimes works after several retries).

Observed logs / error snippets (extracted):
- auth-service: "WARN session: token mismatch for user s.patel@redwood.ai; expected session_id=abc123 got=none"
- okta-logs: "200 OK /authorize -> /callback; user_groups updated: [eng, infra] (delay=4s)"
- browser console: "Failed to set cookie: SameSite attribute mismatch"

Investigation notes so far:
- Confirmed user appears in Okta group within 30s of promotion, but the group attribute in the ID token appears inconsistent on first callback (sometimes missing).
- Token introspection shows correct groups when requested manually, but the initial OIDC response occasionally omits groups due to Okta provisioning delay.
- Auth service expects groups present in ID token to assign RBAC on session creation. If groups missing, user gets base role and console denies admin routes.
- Repeating login within ~20s usually resolves because Okta includes groups on later callbacks; suggests a timing/race between People Ops add and Okta group propagation to token.
- Not a browser-specific bug (reproduced in Firefox).

Workaround for customer (manual):
- Re-run SSO sign-in after 30s-60s; user then receives correct role and access.
- Support can trigger a forced session re-issue via internal admin tool (path: /internal/sessions/refresh) for immediate fix.

Immediate actions taken:
- Reproduced locally with a test user and measured a ~2-6s window where groups are missing in ID token immediately after group add.
- Opened a ticket with People Ops to stagger promotions during business hours and notify support for immediate re-sign-in assistance.

Issue summary: During the 2026-03-10 evening release window, a subset of self-hosted CI runners transitioned to a permanent "Pending" state and did not pick up jobs. Root cause appears tied to agent bootstrap tokens that expired during a staggered key rollover, causing the runner's registration to become semi-valid (registered but unauthenticated for job assignment). Impact: blocked ~18 release CI jobs across multiple services, increased queue latency, and manual reruns required for the release train.
Release jobs stuck in queue; 18 jobs affected across infra and product teams. Estimated 40 minutes extra release time and manual intervention for affected jobs.
1) Configure a self-hosted runner with standard bootstrap flow connected to vault-backed token provider.
2) Trigger a key rollover for the bootstrap token provider with staggered rollout (canary then remainder).
3) Allow agents to refresh token during the rollover window (forcing token expiry and re-request).
4) Observe runners in CI dashboard showing 'Pending' and logs with 'token validation failed' while registration superficially remains present.
Runners remain visible in the fleet but report 'Pending' and never claim jobs. CI orchestrator logs show repeated 401/403 during job assignment after successful initial registration handshake.
Runners should renew bootstrap credentials transparently or fall back to reconnect flow and resume picking up queued jobs without manual re-registration.
[2026-03-10T21:14:03Z] runner-agent[abcd]: INFO registered as runner-33 (ttl=900)
[2026-03-10T21:29:07Z] runner-agent[abcd]: WARN token refresh failed: remote auth returned 401 - invalid grant
[2026-03-10T21:29:07Z] ci-scheduler[main]: ERROR assignment failed for runner-33: unauthorized (403)
[2026-03-10T21:32:11Z] runner-agent[abcd]: INFO heartbeat OK but assignment blocked by auth
Hypothesis: The vault-backed bootstrap provider rotated its signing key using a staged rollout. Some agents attempted refresh during an overlapping window and received tokens signed with the old key while the scheduler validated against the new key set, causing ephemeral validation mismatch. Observed TTLs: agents requested tokens with 15m TTL; the provider returned shorter-lived tokens in the middle of rollout causing early expiry. Cross-check of provider logs shows a 2-minute gap between key activation in authz service and cache refresh in CI scheduler.
Actions taken so far: collected runner agent logs from affected hosts, pulled provider audit logs, and validated token signature timestamps. Checked scheduler's key cache TTL (configured 5m) which likely exceeded the activation gap and produced stale validation results.
1) Manually re-registered affected runners to force fresh bootstrap handshake (mitigates immediate release-block).
2) Bumped scheduler key-cache TTL to 0 (hotfix) and restarted scheduler to force immediate key reload.
3) For upcoming rollouts, flagged provider to perform out-of-band key activation with a 10m overlap window and coordinated with infra team.
1) Update scheduler to use a jwks-refresh-on-401 flow to proactively fetch new verification keys when assignment fails due to auth.
2) Reduce bootstrap token TTL defaults or add jitter to refresh windows to avoid synchronized expiry.
3) Add preflight validation step in rotation playbook ensuring scheduler key cache is refreshed before switching active key.
4) Add automated smoke tests in release pipeline to catch runner re-registration impact during key rollovers.
Work in progress. Immediate release impact addressed by manual re-registration and scheduler restart. Engineering change requests filed: infra-config PR #2121 to adjust cache settings and release-scripts PR #489 to add pre-rotation checks. Follow-up tasks assigned to Release Engineering for rollout procedure updates.
1) Merge infra-config PR and schedule controlled rollout (owner: @infra-sre).
2) Implement JWKS on-401 refresh in scheduler (owner: @ci-platform).
3) Update runbook and run a dry-run rotation in staging next week.
4) Notify release teams of new rollover windows and update alerts.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple internal users intermittently receive 403 when loading the analytics dashboard (analytics-portal). Symptoms appear after recent Okta group membership changes; affected sessions are not picking up updated role claims until a hard re-auth.

Impact: ~12 engineers (observed) unable to access analytics dashboards or Jupyter notebooks for ~3-10 minutes during incidents; blocks troubleshooting and data exploration. No customer-facing impact but blocks internal ops during high-churn onboarding windows.

Environment: prod-us-east, internal VPC, analytics-portal behind sso-proxy (session cache + jwt-claim-middleware).

Steps to reproduce (intermittent):
1) In Okta admin, add user to a role-mapped group (e.g., data-analysts).
2) Trigger SCIM user-group update (via automated sync job or manual add).
3) Within 1-2 minutes, the user attempts to open analytics-portal while still having an active session cookie.
4) Portal returns 403 and shows "Insufficient role claims" in UI.
5) Clearing cookies or forcing SSO re-auth immediately restores access.

Observed logs and notes:
- sso-proxy logs show cached session token verified successfully but claim set does not include updated "redwood_roles" attribute.
- Identity webhook logs show SCIM user.update event delivered at 2026-03-10T15:18:43Z for user alice@redwood.com. sso-proxy logged session validation at 2026-03-10T15:18:45Z returning old claims.
- Okta system log entries indicate SCIM delivery latency spikes (~700ms) during churn windows.

Initial hypothesis: race between SCIM webhook delivery and session-claim-refresh path. When Okta updates group memberships, the SCIM hook correctly updates internal identity store, but the sso-proxy uses a session-bound cached claim snapshot and does not re-fetch claims until TTL expiry. If the SCIM update arrives before the session cache invalidation event, the portal continues to serve requests with stale claims leading to 403.

Temporary mitigation: Added a forced revalidate link in the portal UI (users can click to force a re-auth and refresh claims). Support instructed affected users to hard re-auth as a workaround.

Next steps: implement claim invalidation triggered by SCIM webhook (or push invalidation message to session cache). Also add metrics to correlate SCIM update times with session validation timestamps.

1) Add user to Okta group that is mapped to portal roles.
2) Immediately attempt to use analytics portal without logging out.
3) Note 403 with "Insufficient role claims".
4) Force re-auth -> access restored.

Additional notes:

2026-03-12 09:20 - Engineering (Priya Rao): Drafted change to session invalidation endpoint and opened PR to notify sso-proxy on SCIM updates (see related_github_prs).
Workaround applied: UI revalidate button and support-run forced re-auth flow. Short-term: lowered session claim TTL from 5m to 30s for analytics-portal while fix is deployed. Issue summary: Multiple Redwood employee accounts showed near-simultaneous creation of new privileged web sessions (console/API) immediately after receiving an external marketing email with a remote-hosted image. Sessions were from geographically diverse IPs but tied to identical OAuth token IDs. Suspected compromise vector is an image-hosted redirector that triggered a third-party token exchange path in our SSO integration.

Why this ticket: escalate to SRE/Sec to triage scope, contain compromised tokens, and validate whether any service accounts or elevated actions were taken.
At least 6 employee sessions observed (developers, infra engineers) activated within a 2-minute window. No confirmed data exfiltration yet; several console actions attempted and blocked by our step-up MFA rule. Potential lateral movement risk until tokens are revoked. Affected users are all internal; no customer-facing endpoints observed to be accessed yet.

2026-03-12T09:06:40Z - Support triage: initial correlation to recently received external marketing email with embedded image tag (tracking pixel) sent at 09:03:21Z
2026-03-12T09:12:02Z - Security created temporary blocklist rule for image-host host: img-analytics.example.com

2) Browser or email client makes GET to image-hosting domain which triggers a 302 to a redirector that includes open-redirect parameters
3) Redirector executes a client-side fetch to an endpoint that performs implicit token exchange with our SSO (observed via referrer headers), producing a short-lived session cookie
4) New session appears in logs as created with matching oauth_token_id across different user agents and IPs.
Auth logs: oauth_token_id 'otk_3a9f...b12' seen in six session create events; token signature valid for our client_id but refresh token flows show nonstandard user_agent 'ImageFetch/1.0'
Inbound network: multiple GETs to img-analytics.example.com from office and remote IPs within seconds of email send; host resolves to CDN provider used by third-party marketer
SSO provider (IdP) logs: conditional consent bypass returning success when referrer matches 'track.example-redirect.com' — open-redirect parameter present
No API keys or service account tokens observed to be used in conjunction with these sessions; console actions attempted were blocked by policy 'high-privilege-stepup' which requested MFA and returned 401 when automated agent couldn't continue
Related indicators: IPs 198.51.100.34, 203.0.113.120; redirector domain track.example-redirect.com; image host img-analytics.example.com
Preliminary hypothesis: third-party marketing redirector abused an open-redirect that allowed an automated client to trigger an IdP implicit or token-exchange flow resulting in valid session tokens being minted and propagated to various clients.

2) Create a detection rule to flag any future oauth_token_id reuse across distinct user-agents/IPs within a 5-minute window
