payload.description:
Issue summary:
A subset of service-bot sessions are failing to acquire RBAC roles when signing in via Okta SSO. The auth stack reports a JSON parse error when parsing the service metadata claim. The claim payload contains escaped sequences (e.g., backslash-escaped quotes and control characters) that the RBAC parser does not tolerate.

Impact:
- ~12% of service-bot login attempts into internal consoles return 403 or result in ephemeral session creation failures.
- Affects internal automation that relies on service-bot tokens (deploy hooks, scheduled oncall runbooks).
- Customers not impacted (internal-support only) but oncall and infra automation reliability degraded.

Environment:
- Production (us-west cluster), observed since 2026-03-09 03:20 UTC.
- Okta -> proxy -> console-auth -> rbac-service flow.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger service-bot login via Okta app (service-bot is provisioned via JIT).
2) Inspect SAML/OIDC assertion: service.metadata claim contains escaped JSON string (e.g. "owner": "team\"infra\"").
3) auth-proxy logs a parse exception when passing the claim to rbac-service.

Observed logs (snippets):
- auth-proxy: "Failed to unmarshal service.metadata: invalid escape sequence at offset 137"
- rbac-service: "role mapping aborted — parse error, rawClaim='\"owner\":\"team\\\"infra\\\"\"'"
- Okta system logs show the assertion delivered as application/x-www-form-urlencoded encoded JSON in the claim.

Initial hypothesis:
The Okta provisioning flow is embedding an already-escaped JSON blob into the claim string. When the proxy attempts to re-interpret the claim as JSON it encounters double-escaped characters, leading to a parse failure. Alternate hypothesis: an encoding mismatch during assertion transformation in our SSO adapter (URL-decoding vs JSON-unescaping).
2026-03-10 10:12 - Reproduced locally with a synthetic assertion that includes backslash-escaped quotes; parser fails with same exception.
Examined Okta app mapping: attribute maps 'service.metadata' to a custom profile field containing JSON serialized server-side. Mapping looks unchanged since last deploy (no rollouts around 2026-03-09).
Auth-proxy versions: 1.4.7 (prod). RBAC service version: 2.9.1. No recent changes in parsing libraries, but proxy uses a JSON library that treats backslashes literally unless explicitly unescaped.
Cross-checked SAML vs OIDC assertions: both show escaped payloads when the source metadata includes nested JSON strings (we have a handful of older service-bots still using legacy metadata encoding).
Threat model: malformed claim could be exploited to bypass role mapping if parsing were coerced — low immediate risk but should be hardened.
Telemetry: spike in parse exceptions from 2026-03-09 03:22 UTC; 18 distinct service-bot client IDs affected, all created before 2025-10-01.
Maya Thompson (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed this after a scheduled deploy didn't run; our deploy hook reported 403 from the console API. Opening ticket so SRE can triage.
Evan Brooks (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Assigned. Initial reproduce and logs collected. Suspect double-escaping on older service-bot profiles. Will attempt quick mitigation in proxy to tolerate escaped JSON.
SRE Oncall 2026-03-11: Applied rate-limited mitigation to auth-proxy in us-west: added a tolerant-unescape wrapper before RBAC parse. Monitoring for regressions.
Platform Eng 2026-03-12: Confirmed mitigation reduces 403s from ~12% to ~1.2% for affected clients. Preparing a proper fix in auth-proxy to normalize claim decoding. PR reference posted below.
Maya Thompson 2026-03-14: Please include a short runbook entry for teams that onboard older service-bots so they understand encoding requirements.

Issue summary: Several on-call engineers are unable to get temporary admin elevations via the console approval flow. The approval requests remain in 'Pending' and the approval webhook to Okta returns a 504 timeout.

Impact: Blocking on-call rotations and emergency escalations for engineers across multiple teams (SRE, Platform). Estimated ~12 users have pending approvals since the rollout.

Environment: Production (console-api cluster behind new ingress rewrite; Okta org: redwood-prod). Problem started after a routine Okta webhooks/policy change rolled at 06:12 UTC on 2026-03-10.

Steps to reproduce:
1) As a non-privileged user, open Console -> Access Requests -> Request temporary admin (duration 1h).
2) Initiate approval via delegated manager.
3) Observe request in Console UI stuck in 'Pending' and approval webhook logs show a 504 from Approval Service to Okta.

Observed behavior: Approval Service posts to Okta webhook endpoint and receives 504 gateway timeout; no retry is attempted and request remains pending indefinitely. Users cannot escalate to respond to pages.

Expected behavior: Approval Service should receive a success (200) or implement retries/backoff in case of transient timeouts; Console should offer manual fallback or admin override for stalled approvals.
Login to console as non-privileged user
Request temporary admin elevation
Trigger manager approval flow
Observe pending state and check approval-service logs for outgoing webhook 504
approval-service outgoing POST /okta/webhooks/approve 2026-03-10T06:15:14Z -> 504 Gateway Timeout
ingress-controller (ingress-rewrite) traceId=abc123 routeLatency=1200ms
console-api error: approval_update_loop: no response from webhook after first attempt

Additional notes:
Initial hypothesis: ingress rewrite introduced a connection timeout or removed keep-alive causing Okta to drop long-running webhook responses. Evidence:
- Ingress traces show routeLatency spikes >1.2s and connection resets around 06:14-06:18 UTC.
- Approval Service logs show single POST attempt that stalls until 30s then receives 504 from upstream.
- No recent changes in Approval Service code; change window coincides with LB/ingress rewrite.

- Coordinate with Okta to validate webhook best-practices and set SLAs for webhook responses.

Issue summary: Research team requests short-term access to a sampled, de-identified set of production inference payloads to calibrate a new hallucination-detection scoring heuristic.

Impact: Low risk to live production; moderate privacy risk if PII is not successfully removed. This request is time-sensitive for an upcoming conference demo but must follow privacy guardrails.

Request details: Access to sampled tokenized prompts and model responses (no raw user metadata) for a 48-hour window. Samples should be drawn from production ingestion between 2026-03-08T00:00:00Z and 2026-03-10T23:59:59Z, with a sampling rate ~5% stratified by endpoint and latency buckets.

What is being requested: Short-lived read-only mount of the sampled payload set to the research team's ephemeral workspace; IAM role to be scoped and time-limited; automated redaction/hash of any PII tokens prior to provisioning.

Rationale/justification: Model calibration to reduce false-positive hallucination alerts; internal research (no customer-facing publication planned beyond anonymized metrics). The new scoring heuristic requires realistic, anonymized model outputs to tune thresholds.

Expected deliverables: A short report summarizing calibration results, metrics before/after thresholding, and a statement confirming no re-identifiable data was retained.

Compliance constraints: Must adhere to data minimization SOP, Security's ephemeral-access playbook, and Privacy review sign-off. No raw session IDs, no IPs, and no attachments containing customer files to be included in the dataset.
Model calibration to evaluate hallucination rates on real in-domain prompts; engineering research team needs limited traces to validate a new scoring heuristic.
Provide only tokenized prompts and model responses; run automated PII filter to redact/hash flagged tokens; remove user identifiers, IPs, auth tokens, and session IDs; sample 5% of sessions using stratified sampling by endpoint/latency; store results in ephemeral S3 bucket with 48-hour TTL; no external downloads allowed.
Grant short-lived IAM role (duration = 4 hours) bound to researcher identities, require MFA, apply read-only S3 policy, restrict network egress, log every read to audit index, and require signed acknowledgement of data handling by each researcher.
All provisioning events and object reads will be recorded in CloudTrail and forwarded to the audit index; object access will emit datapoints with requester, timestamp, and object key; audit logs retained for 90 days; security will run a short review within 24 hours of access completion.
1) Research sends finalized sampling selector and filter config in this ticket.
2) Privacy runs automated PII policy on selector to confirm redaction coverage.
3) SRE creates ephemeral S3 bucket with lifecycle policy and scoped IAM role.
4) Data engineering runs extraction job, applies redaction filter, and writes tokenized samples to bucket.
5) Security performs quick sanity scan and signs off in ticket comments.
6) IAM role credentials issued via short-lived STS tokens and distributed to approved researcher IDs.
7) After 48 hours bucket is auto-deleted; security validates deletion and posts confirmation.

Additional notes:

Pending final approval from SRE after redaction test passes and IAM role prepared. No data has been provisioned yet. After approval, SRE will document the exact STS token TTL and the extraction job schedule in this ticket.

Issue summary:
Several ephemeral self-hosted CI runners in prod(us-west) failed to pull container images immediately after a routine robot-account token rotation in our internal container registry. The symptom was ImagePullBackOff/Unauthorized on new ephemeral jobs; some jobs succeeded intermittently depending on node scheduling.

Impact:
- ~18% of ephemeral-runner jobs in the us-west pool failed to start over a 45-minute window (2026-02-28 09:12-09:57 UTC).
- Release pipelines that create short-lived runners (canary builds and nightly releases) were blocked or retried multiple times, increasing CI latency and causing customer-facing release delays.

Environment:
- Cluster: gke-release-us-west1 (GKE autopilot; nodepools running ephemeral-runner DaemonSet)
- Registry: internal-registry.redwood-inference.com (robot account token rotated via Vault transit)
1) Rotate registry robot account token via vault write auth/registry/rotate
2) Trigger a release pipeline that provisions ephemeral runners (release-canary job)
3) Observe pod events from ephemeral-runner-created pods; many show ImagePullBackOff due to Unauthorized from registry
4) On same cluster, schedule pod to a node that previously had successful pulls and observe success (intermittent behavior seen in production)
kubectl describe pod release-canary-runner-xyz: Events: Failed to pull image "internal-registry.redwood-inference.com/release/runner:sha123": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Error response from daemon: unauthorized: authentication required
docker log (node-12): time=2026-02-28T09:22:11Z level=error msg="GET https://internal-registry.redwood-inference.com/v2/ : 401 Unauthorized"
vault audit: 2026-02-28T09:10:03Z user=automation/registry-rotations action=rewrap token_id=robot-reg-14 rotated=true
kubelet (node-7): time=2026-02-28T09:23:02Z msg="credential provider cache miss; using node-level image pull secret version v1"
Hypothesis: The registry robot token rotation updated the secret in Vault and the central k8s secret via the rotation job, but nodes (kubelet/docker) continued to use a cached credential or an older k8s secret reference for a short period. We observed that pods scheduled to nodes which had recently performed a successful pull (cached credentials) succeeded, while pods on nodes that had not refreshed credentials failed with 401.

Findings:
- The rotation job updated the k8s secret (registry-robot-token) at 2026-02-28T09:10:15Z.
- Kube-controller reflected the new secret, but kubelet credential handshake with container runtime showed cached old creds for ~10-15 minutes on affected nodes.
- The ephemeral-runner provisioning flow creates ServiceAccount->imagePullSecrets; when a pod schedules to a node with stale cached credentials the pull fails.
- No Vault failures or KMS errors were found; root cause is cred propagation delay + docker/kubelet cache behavior during immediate high volume of ephemeral provisioning.
Aisha Malik (Support) 2026-02-28T09:28: Support reported spike in ImagePullBackOff from release pipelines; preliminary triage points to registry 401s.
Jonah Kim (Infra) 2026-02-28T09:35: Confirmed token rotation ran. Spun up held nodes to repro; observed docker daemon returning 401 on nodes that hadn't pulled in last 30m.
Miguel Santos (Release Eng) 2026-02-28T09:47: The ephemeral runners create imagePullSecrets per-namespace. Suggest forcing a rolling restart of ephemeral-runner DaemonSet to repopulate node caches as quick mitigation.
Jonah Kim (Infra) 2026-02-28T09:55: Applied rolling restart to ephemeral-runner podset and manually refreshed k8s secret on affected nodes. Failures subsided after ~12 minutes.
Priya Desai (Reporter) 2026-03-03T10:10: Verified pipelines resumed; marking resolved pending follow-up automation.
Mitigation applied: 1) Recreated/rolled the ephemeral-runner DaemonSet to force pods to re-init and use the updated k8s secret; 2) Manually refreshed the registry-robot-token k8s secret on nodes where the cache appeared stale; 3) Restarted docker on 3 nodes that persisted 401s.

Permanent fix implemented: Created automation pipeline that runs immediately after any registry robot-token rotation: it updates k8s imagePullSecret, triggers a targeted rolling restart of ephemeral-runner DaemonSet, and warms node credential caches by performing a lightweight authenticated pull on each node. Added telemetry to detect >5% ImagePullBackOffs post-rotation and auto-run the remediation.

Runbook and link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Registry+Credential+Rotation+for+Runners

No rollback required. Post-mitigation monitoring for 24h showed normal job start rates and no repeat occurrences.

Issue summary:
Customer reported that during a scheduled downscale of their dedicated GPU pool, requests for a pinned model (lumina-bert-v2.3-pin-2026-03) started returning responses from the older v2.2 model for ~20% of requests. The customer had pinned v2.3 at the route level for a canary rollout (10% weight), expecting only the canary traffic to hit v2.3. Instead, roughly a subset of pinned sessions were routed to v2.2 intermittently.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: Mixed model outputs caused data quality regressions in two production features (document tagging and entity extraction) for LuminaAnalytics customers.
- Scope: Affected ~15k requests over a 45 minute window in prod-us-east.
- Business: Lumina flagged as P1 due to incorrect data for paid customers on dedicated capacity.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) in us-east; autoscaler configured to downscale at 03:00 UTC with graceful drain timeout 300s.
- Route config: route_id=lumina/entity-extract, model_pin=lumina-bert-v2.3-pin-2026-03, canary_weight=0.10.
- Serving runtime version: 1.21.4; autoscaler version: 0.9.8.

Steps to reproduce (as observed by customer):
1. Lumina triggered a routine scheduled downscale at 03:00 UTC.
2. Within ~3 minutes, some pinned sessions began returning v2.2 outputs (no explicit unpin request from customer).
3. Attempts to re-pin via API returned 200 but client continued to see mixed outputs until routing cache was flushed 40 minutes later.

Logs and evidence:
- Router traces: http://dashboards.redwood/internal/routing-traces?trace=SUP-27458 (shows fallbacks from pins to default group)
- Autoscaler events: scale-down triggered; nodes marked for drain then marked unhealthy while EVP drain state still present: autoscaler logs snippet: "node-cc-17 drain_started=2026-03-10T03:01:02Z drain_complete=\"\""
- Serving logs (example): "[2026-03-10T03:03:12Z] route lumina/entity-extract: session 0x7f3 pinned_model=lumina-bert-v2.3 but routed_model=lumina-bert-v2.2 fallback_reason=pin-owner-unavailable"

Initial hypothesis:
- During scale-down, nodes that were draining moved to a transient unhealthy state. The routing layer treats the pin owner as unavailable when the node health is not yet marked drained, triggering fallback routing to the default model group. A race between drain and health-state transitions can therefore clear pin mappings for in-flight sessions.

Supporting observations:
- Traffic heatmap shows coincident increase in connection churn during node termination events.
- PKI: No TLS errors observed.
- No quota or rate-limit events recorded.

Recommended immediate mitigation (customer-facing workaround):
- Re-apply pin via API after scale-down completes (observed to fix most sessions).
- For scheduled downscales, increase graceful drain timeout to 600s as a temporary mitigation to reduce race window.

Longer-term fixes under consideration:
- Ensure pin ownership is decoupled from single-node health and validated across routing metadata layer before triggering fallback.
- Autoscaler change to mark node as "draining" in healthcheck path rather than immediate unhealthy.
- Add metrics and alerts for "pin-to-fallback" ratios during scale events.

03-10 04:00Z: Reviewed router and autoscaler logs; found multiple nodes transitioned from draining->unhealthy within 20-40s.
03-10 04:30Z: Reproduced locally on staging with forced node termination and confirmed routing falls back when pin-owner health shows unhealthy before drain completion.
Observed that the routing cache TTL (30s) allowed stale entries to be invalidated while drain still ongoing; when invalidated the fallback logic chooses default model group.
Elena Martinez (Support) [2026-03-10T05:12Z]: Notified customer and collected request IDs and example responses; Lumina attached response samples showing v2.2 outputs.
Marcus Liu (SRE) [2026-03-10T06:01Z]: Started timeline correlation between autoscaler events and routing traces; suspect health-state transition order causes pin eviction.
Asha Patel (Platform Eng) [2026-03-10T08:20Z]: Created staging repro with forced termination; able to reproduce 2/5 runs. Filed PR to adjust health state semantics for draining nodes.
Lumina Support Rep (customer) [2026-03-10T09:05Z]: Confirmed re-applying pin fixed the immediate issue for active sessions; asked for ETA on permanent fix.
Marcus Liu (SRE) [2026-03-12T11:00Z]: Rolling a canary patch to autoscaler (PR #722) to mark draining nodes with health=draining; routing patch to tolerate draining nodes until drain_complete in PR #1867.
Elena Martinez (Support) [2026-03-12T12:15Z]: Updated customer on canary rollout and recommended increasing drain timeout as stop-gap.
Mitigation applied: temporarily increased default graceful drain timeout for Lumina dedicated pool to 600s and re-applied pin mappings per their request. Engineering has deployed a canary autoscaler change (PR #722) in us-east with routing tolerance (PR #1867). Next steps: monitor pin-to-fallback metric for 48h, if stable schedule full rollout. Postmortem to be drafted if recurrence >1 in 7 days.

Issue summary:
Users who recently enrolled macOS/iOS passkeys (FIDO2) are able to sign in via Okta, but the resulting SAML/OIDC assertion to Redwood's identity proxy does not contain the expected AMR (authentication method reference) device-trust claim. When affected users attempt to elevate to on-call runbook actions the runbook service rejects the request with a 401 and body: "error: device_untrusted - missing_device_trust_claim".

Impact:
- On-call engineers using passkeys cannot perform elevated runbook operations (approve/execute) for ~30% of passkey-enrolled accounts observed.
- Affects production runbook approval flow and on-call remediation during incidents.
- Immediate operational risk during active incidents; manual bypass is possible but slow.

Environment:
- Production (prod-us-west) identity proxy + runbook service.
- Okta org: redwood-prod (Okta release channel: continuous -> passkey rollout enabled 2026-03-05).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Enroll a new passkey on macOS with the company Okta Verify / WebAuthn flow (recently migrated from legacy device authenticator).
2) Sign in to console and authenticate successfully.
3) Attempt to elevate in runbook UI (click "Request Elevation" -> approve).
4) Observe 401 from runbook-service and check auth proxy logs for incoming assertion.

Observed logs / snippets:
- Identity proxy log: "okta_assertion_received user=jane.doe@redwood.ai claims=[sub, email, groups] -- amr missing"
- Runbook rejection: "level=warn service=runbook msg=ElevationRequestRejected user=jane.doe@redwood.ai reason=device_untrusted missing_claim=device_trust"
- No errors in Okta system log for the authentication event other than attribute mapping not applied (no explicit failure).

Investigation notes so far:
- Replicated with a test account that recently created a passkey: Okta auth event shows factor=WEBAUTHN but token does not include the amr/device_trust claim that legacy device flows included.
- Historical baseline: our device-trust logic expects amr to contain one of ["device", "device_trust", "fido2"]. New passkey tokens currently return amr=[] or omit amr entirely for certain enrollments.
- Started a scoped capture of SAML/OIDC tokens for affected users; confirmed token payload variance between legacy device flows and passkey flows.
- Quick mitigation attempted: forced re-enrollment via legacy device authenticator for one user; after that the token included amr and elevation succeeded. This is not a workable org-wide fix.
- Okta tenant setting: Passkey rollout flagged as GA on 2026-03-05; our attribute mapping for the Okta OIDC app maps the custom claim device_trust <- amr[0]. When amr is absent the mapping silently drops device_trust claim.

Hypothesis:
- Recent Okta passkey implementation does not populate amr by default for certain registration paths. Our OIDC mapping relies on amr presence. This is a mapping/compatibility gap rather than a Redwood runtime bug.

Temporary workaround:
- For impacted on-call users: instruct to use a legacy device authenticator or the mobile Okta Verify app for elevation until mapping is fixed. Documented in support playbook.
- For urgent incident remediation: support can temporarily toggle a runbook-service feature flag to relax device_trust check for the single-service code path (requires a deploy and risk review).

Proposed permanent fix:
- Update Okta OIDC app attribute mapping to fallback to inspect id_token auth_time/enrollment metadata or to map a new Okta custom claim (e.g., oktaDeviceTrust) populated via inline hook.
- Open ticket with Okta to confirm intended amr behavior for passkeys and request guidance for mapping.
- Add regression test in identity integration suite that simulates passkey tokens without amr.
- Add observability: alert when auth tokens arrive without amr for users in groups that require device_trust.

Next steps / action items:
- (Owner) Priya Singh: prepare Okta mapping change RFC and risk assessment. Target: 2026-03-16.
- (Owner) SRE (TBD): implement temporary runbook flag and deploy if leadership approves.
- (Owner) Support (Aisha Patel): notify on-call rotation and publish step-by-step temporary workaround.
- Contact Okta support case created: OKTA-CASE-2026-0312-77 (ticket opened during triage).

Resolution notes (to be filled after fix):
- Record mapping change, rollout window, and post-deploy validation steps.
- Update runbooks and add automated test.
payload.summary: Passkey sign-in omits AMR device-trust claim; runbook elevation returns device_untrusted 401

payload.description:
After a scheduled rotation of the GCS service-account JSON key in Vault, a subset of self-hosted release runners started failing artifact uploads with 403/permission errors. New jobs can start, but steps that persist artifacts to GCS fail consistently on affected runners.
Several release pipelines (mainly canary and nightly builds) are failing at the artifact upload step. End-to-end CI completes for ~60% of jobs; ~40% fail depending on runner pool. This is impacting release cadence for two teams and blocking one canary rollout.
1) Schedule a job on an affected self-hosted runner pool (label: release-runner). 2) Run a job that produces artifacts and pushes to GCS via the platform artifact uploader. 3) Observe upload step fail with 403 and 'permission denied' in upload logs.
upload_error: google.api_core.exceptions.Forbidden: 403 The caller does not have permission
  at artifact_client.upload (uploader.go:142)
  Runner agent logs: token refresh ok; vault fetch success; gcloud auth activate-service-account failed with: 'invalid_grant' in a small subset of requests.
Rotation of the GCS service-account key introduced a timing window where some runner agents kept a cached, now-revoked credential and attempted to use it to obtain short-lived tokens; cluster-level RBAC or IAM binding change might have been applied concurrently, causing inconsistent permission sets across runner pods.
- Vault rotation job executed 2026-03-12T03:10Z and wrote new key:ss: gcs-release-sa. - We observed two behaviors: (A) runners that restarted after rotation pick up new key and succeed; (B) runners that continued running show vault fetch success but gcloud auth operations intermittently fail with 'invalid_grant' or 403 when exchanging keys. - No global IAM role changes detected in cloud audit logs at rotation time. - Artifact uploader config unchanged. - Affected runner pods share the same node pools as healthy ones; not a node-level network issue. - Related Slack thread: #ci-ops (link). - Linked issue INT-48917 (ephemeral-runner-vault-rewrap-decrypt-failure) investigated vault rewrap before; not identical but useful for pattern comparison.
We reproduced the failure by running a small job on a pre-rotation runner (did not restart runner), confirming that artifact upload fails until runner process is restarted. Restarting the runner agent pod resolves the error in reproduced runs.
- Restart runner agent process on affected hosts (kubectl rollout restart daemonset/release-runner-agent) to force a fresh VAULT fetch and re-auth. - For critical release pipelines, temporarily route jobs to runner pools that have been rotated and restarted. - Notify teams of transient failures and recommended rerun after restart.
- Performed targeted rolling restart of release-runner-agent on 8 affected hosts, which restored artifact uploads for ~95% of failing jobs. - Updated rotation runbook to include mandatory runner agent restart step until hot-reload is implemented.
1) Patch the runner agent to detect service-account key rotation events in Vault and automatically re-auth without a full pod restart (hot-reload). 2) Add a post-rotation orchestrator step that performs a rolling restart of runner agents after a key rotation completes. 3) Add end-to-end test in rotation pipeline to validate artifact uploads after key rotate.
- Implement hot-reload in agent (small binary change) and ship to staging. - Run key rotation in staging and validate. - Deploy to prod behind a staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with monitoring. Risks: if hot-reload has an edge-case, some agents may still require restart; fallback is rolling restart orchestrator.
Hot-reload agent patch target: 2026-03-20. Complete rollout and rotation automation update by 2026-03-24.
- (OWNER: DevInfra) Implement agent hot-reload and add unit/integration tests (PR TBD). - (OWNER: CI Ops) Update rotation runbook to include canary restarts and validation job. - (OWNER: Security) Review rotation procedure to ensure zero-window guarantees if possible. - Create postmortem if production impact > 4 hours.
payload.summary: Self-hosted runners unable to upload job artifacts after storage service-account key rotation

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple employees report that corporate VPN (WireGuard SSO onboarding) fails during initial device provisioning when devices roam between the guest SSID (office-guest) and the corporate SSID (redwood-corp) while the captive portal is active. Impact: ~12 users unable to finish device enrollment and obtain machine/user certs between 08:30 and 11:45 PDT on 2026-03-12; blocks VPN SSO onboarding and access to internal services. Initial triage indicates SCEP enrollment requests are timing out or returning incomplete cert chains. Suspected root cause: HTTP AIA/OCSP retrieval from CA is being blocked by an inline ACL on perimeter firewall when traffic hits the captive-portal redirect path, causing the client to fail to build the certificate chain and abort the EAP/SCEP flow. This appears to be triggered by SSID roam events that change VLAN and transiently route enrollment traffic through the guest-path enforcement chain.
1) Connect device to redwood-corp SSID, start onboarding (MDM enrollment triggers SCEP).
2) While enrollment is in progress, roam the device to office-guest SSID or force a VLAN switch via AP controller.
3) Observe SCEP request (ACME/SCEP POST) leaving device, then captive-portal HTTP redirect intercept occurs.
4) Client reports 'certificate chain incomplete' or times out after 30s and onboarding fails.
5) Repeat on macOS and Windows 11 — issue reproducible on both client types.
Sample logs:
- AP controller syslog: Mar 12 08:34:21 AP-02 roam: client 44:55:66:77:88:99 moved from VLAN 201 -> 120 (redwood-corp -> office-guest)
- Firewall (PA) traffic log: Mar 12 08:34:22 rule 'guest-web-redirect' allow http 10.8.34.112:80 -> 192.0.2.10:80; rule 'deny-http-to-external-ca' blocked 10.8.34.112:80 -> 198.51.100.5:80 (AIA)
- Client (macOS) Console: SCEP: 'Server responded but returned no CA cert chain'
- WireGuard onboarding: 'client enrollment failed: certificate verification error (chain incomplete)'
2026-03-12 09:00 - Initial report from ENG desk: several reports from hot desk area near AP-02.
2026-03-12 09:15 - Confirmed pattern: failures clustered around roaming/vlan change windows; when devices enroll staying persistently on redwood-corp SSID enrollment succeeds.
2026-03-12 09:40 - Packet capture on AP-02 uplink (pcap saved to /var/logs/pcaps/INT-714332-ap02.pcap): SCEP POST goes to CA but subsequent GET for AIA URL is rewritten to captive portal and never reaches CA.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Firewall rules audit: found legacy rule 'deny-http-to-external-ca' added 2025-11-01 to prevent outbound HTTP to known third-party CA host list; rule evaluated before captive-portal exception.
2026-03-12 10:30 - Tested adding temporary allow rule for 198.51.100.5 (CA AIA host) -> enrollment succeeded for repro device.
Hypothesis: captive-portal HTTP redirect + ordering of firewall ACLs causes AIA/OCSP fetches to be blocked during transient VLAN path; client cannot fetch intermediate CA or perform OCSP stapling checks, so SCEP fails.
Next steps: 1) Apply temporary targeted firewall exception for CA AIA/OCSP hosts for internal DHCP pool during onboarding windows. 2) Update AP controller to mark SCEP enrollment destinations as exempt from captive-portal redirects when EAP/SCEP flow is detected. 3) Run broader test across SF office APs and schedule a config change window.
Applied temporary firewall rule (PA rule id fw-temp-714332) to allow TCP/80 and TCP/443 to CA AIA and OCSP hosts (198.51.100.5, 203.0.113.44) from internal DHCP ranges for the duration of onboarding. Instructed on-site team to avoid roaming during enrollment as temporary mitigation. Pushed MDM policy to retry enrollments automatically once device returns to corp VLAN.
Mitigation implemented on 2026-03-12: temporary FW exception allowed SCEP/AIA traffic; immediate onboarding failures stopped. Planned permanent fix: reorder firewall ACLs to evaluate captive-portal redirect after exceptions for cert-enrollment endpoints, and create explicit AP controller bypass for SCEP/MDM enrollment flows. Change request CR-2026-0315 filed and scheduled for 2026-03-16 02:00-03:00 UTC maintenance window. Follow-up actions: update runbook with this failure mode, add monitoring alerts for certificate enrollment failure spikes, and whitelist known CA AIA/OCSP hosts in infra config repo PR referenced below.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 07:30 - Security (Aisha Rahman): Reviewed whitelist list for CA hosts; approved temporary allow and CR plan pending change window.
payload.summary: Roaming between guest & corp VLANs breaks SCEP certificate enrollment -> VPN/SSO onboarding failures at SF office

payload.description:
Issue summary: After the nightly secrets-rotation job ran (vault-rotate-cron), our self-hosted GitLab runners lost access to the secrets path used by release pipelines. Impact: Release pipelines for multiple services stalled/failed, blocking a planned hotfix rollout.

Request: Help reprovision runner credentials, verify rotation tooling, and schedule a safe window for re-rotation.
Trigger release pipeline for service 'inference-gateway' on main: job 'prepare-release' attempts to read /secret/ci/runners/inference-gateway and fails with 403.
Check runner logs (runner-01): repeated 403 from Vault API when fetching token, stack trace shows 'permission denied: token role mismatch'.
Inspect vault rotation job: vault-rotate-cron reported success but Vault audit shows token revocation events for 'ci-runner-role' at the same timestamp.
Initial hypothesis: rotation job revoked long-lived runner tokens without writing updated credentials to runners.
Found that kube secret 'ci-runner-creds' was updated but runners use projected service account tokens; the rotation job changed role binding on Vault side but did not update k8s service account annotations.
Observed GitLab Runner registration token still valid, but Vault policy now denies 'read' to the previous secret path; runners were not reprovisioned.
Related automation PR (infra#1427) added a Vault policy change last week; suspected to be mis-scoped change.
[2026-03-11] Maya Kaur: Noticed multiple failed pipelines at 02:14 UTC after scheduled rotation. Creating this ticket to coordinate remediation and rollback if needed.
[2026-03-11] Jamal Rivera: Assigned. Sharing runner logs and Vault audit. Asking Infra to confirm last infra PRs that touched vault policies.
[2026-03-12] Priya Desai (Infra): Confirmed PR infra#1427 adjusted policy-to-role mapping. We see policy 'ci-runner-read' removed for 'ci-runner-role' at 02:12 UTC — looks accidental.
[2026-03-12] Jamal Rivera: As immediate mitigation, re-added policy binding and manually generated a short-lived token for runner-01; pipeline succeeded after we redeployed runner pod with new token.
[2026-03-13] Maya Kaur: Customer-facing release was paused; need timeline for full audit and permanent fix so rotation doesn't require manual steps.
Manual mitigation applied: restored Vault role binding and redeployed affected runners with short-lived tokens. Next steps: patch rotation job to update k8s SA annotations or rotate projected tokens, add Canary rotation test to CI, and schedule coordinated rotation window with Release Eng. Action items created in INT-9032 for automation fix.
payload.summary: CI runner credential reprovisioning after automated secret rotation blocked release pipeline

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We observed an anomalous spike in authentication events where IdP-issued JWTs (SAML->OIDC pipeline) were used to exchange for short-lived service tokens. These exchanges originated from a small set of IPs that are not common for our workforce and targeted multiple internal service and user accounts.

Impact:
- Potential credential or token re-use affecting 3 internal accounts and multiple service tokens issued to CI/CD runners.
- No evidence yet of data exfiltration, but some high-privilege service tokens were minted and used to call internal admin APIs.
- Could affect deployment pipelines and onboarding workflows if tokens are revoked without a coordinated mitigation.

Environment:
- Production SSO (IdP: corporate Okta) federated to Redwood SSO proxy in us-east-1.
- Time window: 2026-03-12 03:12:00 UTC -> 2026-03-12 03:45:00 UTC.

Observed indicators / logs:
- Auth audit logs show ~180 token exchanges with IdP-signed JWTs in the 33-minute window.
- Source IPs: 34.120.12.87, 34.120.13.192 (ASN / cloud provider observed).
- User agents: headless-bot/1.2, python-requests/2.31.0 (some variance).
- Several exchanges returned service tokens with admin-scoped claims for infra-ops account.
- No immediate 5xx or runtime errors observed on admin APIs; however, token usage patterns were unusual (burst requests to /v1/admin/keys).

Steps to reproduce (for validation):
1) Query auth audit index: query by event_type:token_exchange AND source_ip in [34.120.12.87,34.120.13.192] AND timestamp between 2026-03-12T03:00:00Z and 2026-03-12T04:00:00Z.
2) Correlate returned token IDs with internal token-usage logs in service-audit index.
3) Verify Okta org logs for suspicious OAuth/OIDC grant activity for the same time window.

Initial mitigation actions taken:
- Rotated affected service keys for svc-data-ingest and infra-ops.
- Forced SSO session revocations for implicated human accounts (alice@redwood.com).
- Throttled token exchange endpoint for non-corp IP ranges and added temporary WAF rule to block the two IPs.
- Opened an incident bridge and notified Legal and Product Security.
- Created this internal-support ticket to capture investigation and follow-up remediation tasks.

03/12 03:20 UTC - Alert from auth-monitoring: token_exchange_rate > 25/min for SSO proxy; triggered oncall.
03/12 03:25 UTC - Confirmed 180 exchanges from two external IPs; fetched raw auth logs and correlated to service-audit.
03/12 03:28 UTC - Hypothesis A: credentials/token capture from phishing or compromised CI/CD runner. Hypothesis B: misconfigured third-party integration replaying JWTs.
03/12 03:34 UTC - Checked Okta sign-in logs: no interactive human sign-in from these IPs, but several token-grant events via service app client. Opened ticket with Okta support for additional metadata.
03/12 03:40 UTC - Identified a CI runner artifact that had environment variable containing long-lived client assertion; rotated that credential and invalidated prior tokens.
03/13 09:00 UTC - SRE ran forensics on the two IPs: both map to ephemeral cloud VMs; abuse reports filed with provider.
03/14 10:30 UTC - Security team requested expanded audit retention for token_exchange logs and started payload-level parsing to extract JWT ids for replay detection.
Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-12: Initial detection and mitigation steps listed. On-call will coordinate rotations.
Diego Morales (Assignee) 2026-03-12: Applied WAF block for observed IPs and forced session revocations for implicated users. Continuing log correlation.
Priya Shah (Product Security) 2026-03-12: Requesting Okta export of app-level grant logs and list of affected app client IDs; also advise rotating any CI client assertions.
Samir Gupta (SRE) 2026-03-13: Found a Jenkins runner in project 'release-automation' with a stale service assertion. Rotated and removed hard-coded token from job config. Investigating whether token was exfiltrated via job artifacts.
Legal 2026-03-13: Please collect timeline for any external communications; we'll prepare a notice template if customer-facing impact is discovered.
Diego Morales 2026-03-14: Filing for a post-incident review once we confirm no further exchange spikes. Recommend making token-exchange rate limit permanent for non-corp ranges.
Complete full token lineage mapping for all exchanged tokens during window and mark any sessions/tokens for permanent revocation where appropriate.
Coordinate with Identity team and Okta support to determine the exact grant flow used and whether the client application was configured with overly-broad scopes.
Implement a permanent rule in API gateway to restrict token_exchange endpoint to corp IP ranges and known CI egress ranges, with an allowlist for validated third-party integrators.
Schedule a postmortem (blameless) with SRE, Product Security, and Build/CI owners. Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/INT-130001-Postmortem
Assess whether additional EDR/forensics on implicated developer workstations is warranted based on CI findings.
Partial mitigation complete: affected credentials rotated, WAF blocks applied, Okta support engaged. Full root cause pending confirmation of whether token values were exfiltrated from a CI artifact or replayed by a third-party integration. Postmortem scheduled. No customer data confirmed accessed at time of last update.
Revisit rate-limiting thresholds for token_exchange endpoint as a platform configuration item for Q2 roadmap.
Add automated alert for abnormal ratio of token_exchange events to interactive sign-ins for any given account.
Ensure CI templates do not accept raw client assertions and add linting check in internal-tools repo.
payload.summary: Unusual spike in IdP-signed JWT usage across multiple internal accounts

comments: 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z Priya Kapoor: Acknowledged receipt from customer and requested request/response traces and pcap. Escalated to SRE because symptoms suggest runtime-level blocking.

2026-03-10T11:03:00Z Marco Alvarez: Reproduced locally on a staging dedicated replica with node client. Observed event-loop stall in worker process when large multipart parse occurs concurrently with generation. Attaching staging traces to ticket.

2026-03-11T08:15:00Z Marco Alvarez: Hypothesis: synchronous file parsing in the upload handler blocks the event loop thread that's responsible for streaming token flushes to the websocket. This is exacerbated on dedicated nodes when CPU contention is high.
2026-03-11T17:40:00Z Dev: Implemented prototype offloading: move multipart parsing to a background worker thread pool and ensure websocket writer uses a dedicated async IO path. Created PR #4287.

2026-03-12T09:55:00Z Marco Alvarez: Patch rolled out to canary (10% traffic) for us-west cluster. Monitoring for stalls; no new reproductions observed on canary after patch. Rolling to 100% scheduled.

2026-03-12T12:10:00Z Priya Kapoor: Informed customer of rollback-safe patch and asked to verify. Customer confirmed that after attempting the previously failing flow on a canary endpoint they no longer see stalls. Marking as resolved and will follow up for 48h monitoring.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports chat streaming sessions (WebSocket) stall mid-generation (no tokens emitted for >60s) and eventually the client sees a connection close (1006). This consistently reproduces when the same client session uploads a large file (>50MB) to our attachments endpoint while a long-running streaming response is in-flight.

Impact:
- Affects NoteAI Labs production customers using Dedicated cluster in us-west-2.
- Observed on multiple accounts inside NoteAI with high severity (in-progress chat flows drop).
- Business impact: live note-taking sessions are interrupted, user-visible failures for editors using upload+chat simultaneously.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster (dedicated plan), prod us-west-2
- API path: /v1/chat/stream (WebSocket upgrade) and /v1/files/upload in same session token
- SDK: node-redwood v2.3.1 and direct WebSocket clients
- Serving runtime: 2026-02-28 build (kernel v3.4), websocket-proxy v1.9

Steps to reproduce:
1) Open a WebSocket chat stream to /v1/chat/stream and start a long-generation prompt (~1k tokens expected).
2) While generation is in-flight, in the same authenticated session upload a 60MB file using /v1/files/upload.
3) Observe chat stream: token emission halts after ~12s of activity. No error messages are delivered to client. After ~90s, client receives a 1006 close.

Observed behavior:
- Streaming output pauses (silence) mid-token; server shows no 5xx in API gateway logs for the chat request.
- Websocket connection remains ESTABLISHED from the proxy perspective for ~60-120s then unclean close.
- Upload request completes successfully and storage acknowledges file upload.

Expected behavior:
- Upload should not impact in-flight streaming generation. Both requests should make forward progress concurrently.

Logs/Errors/Artifacts:
- Customer-provided client logs show no application-level exception; final close code 1006.
- Gateway metrics: no increased 5xx for chat route; connection count for websocket proxy spikes during upload and CPU on proxy pod increases ~20%.
- Serving runtime logs show a single worker thread blocked in protobuf parsing at the same timestamp as the stall.
- tcpdump on proxy shows continuous POST data for upload while upstream ws packets cease after the stall moment.

Workaround (temporary):
- Ask customers to avoid concurrent large uploads during live streaming sessions.
- If unavoidable, perform uploads on a separate session/token so requests are routed to different backend workers.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 14:28 - Customer (NoteAI): Provided websocket debug logs and pcap. Confirmed reproduces on their production cluster only when using same session token for both requests.
Reproduced using Node SDK v2.3.1 and raw WebSocket client; failure only when same session token used for both concurrent requests.
Strace and async traces show main thread blocked in parse_multipart() inside upload handler; worker uses shared process for websocket flush callbacks.
CPU profile: spike on main thread; websocket writer uses same threadpool due to legacy synchronous flush path.
Proxy observed increased connection multiplexing and head-of-line behavior but proxy not dropping packets; root cause localized to serving runtime process.
Related to internal convo INT-5591 where we previously discussed offloading heavy request parsing; reuse of that design work sped remediation.
Root cause: synchronous multipart file parsing in upload handler blocked the event-loop thread responsible for websocket token flushes on the serving runtime. Concurrent large uploads in same process led to head-of-line blocking and unclean websocket closures.
Fix: offload multipart parsing to a thread pool and ensure websocket flushes run on a dedicated async IO executor. Implemented in PR #4287.
Rollout: canary deployed 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC (10% traffic), monitored for 12h, then promoted to 100% at 2026-03-12 11:00 UTC across us-west. No further reproductions reported by customer after canary test.
Postmortem action items: 1) Add e2e test for concurrent upload+stream flows; 2) Add telemetry to detect event-loop stalls >200ms on serving runtime; 3) Update SDK docs to recommend separate session tokens for heavy uploads until fully rolled out (temporary).

Issue summary: Several scheduled ACH payments for supplier 'Caldera Analytics' are in 'Held' state in the payments queue. The bank reconciliation feed shows the payments were created but failed to post to the corporate bank due to a payee identifier mismatch. At the same time, the invoice import pipeline rejected the invoice-to-PO match for the same supplier because the EDI invoice header omitted the PO number.

Impact: Three scheduled payments ($42,300 total) are blocked from releasing; month-end reconciliation is affected. The supplier sent multiple reminders via support@caldera-analytics.com and has asked for confirmation that payment will be released this week. Risk of late-fee penalties and supplier relationship impact.

Background: Caldera recently updated their banking details in the vendor portal last week. Finance updated the Vendor Master record on 2026-03-02 with the new ACH routing and payee tax identifier (TIN). On 2026-03-03 we ran a batch of scheduled payouts which now show 'Held: Payee ID mismatch'. The AP inbox contains an EDI 810 invoice for PO 78219 that was processed on 2026-03-04 but failed auto-match.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Vendor Master: vendor_id V-00948 shows payee_tin=12-3456789, routing=021000021.
2) Payments queue (payments-service): payment_id P-20260303-77 created for V-00948 scheduled 2026-03-03 17:00Z.
3) Bank gateway returned code BK-415: "Beneficiary identifier mismatch" during pre-send validation.
4) Automated PO-matcher logged: "PO_NOT_FOUND: EDI 810 header missing PO#" for invoice INV-20260304-119.
5) Reconciliation feed (bank-feed-us-east) shows pending but not posted.

Observed logs (sanitized):
- payments-service[2026-03-03T17:00:02Z] ERROR payment_validator: payee_tin=12-3456789 != bank_record.tin=21-9876543 for payee V-00948; code=BK-415
- edi-ingest[2026-03-04T02:15:10Z] WARN matcher: invoice INV-20260304-119 header[PO]=null; fallback_route=vendor_reference

Expected behavior: Updated vendor bank/TIN should be accepted after Finance confirmation; scheduled payments should move from Held to Processing. EDI invoices containing a PO reference should auto-match to PO 78219 and flow to payment.

Actual behavior: System prevents payments due to discrepancy between Vendor Master and bank's stored beneficiary id. EDI pipeline is treating missing PO as non-match and routing to manual review queue.

Additional notes: Caldera's accounts payable team provided a bank confirmation PDF (attached to the ticket) and a copy of the original PO showing PO 78219. Finance believes the Vendor Master update succeeded but suspects there may be a duplication of vendor records with different internal vendor_id.

Attachments: caldera_bank_confirmation_20260302.pdf; edi_810_INV-20260304-119.raw

Suggested initial triage steps: Verify vendor duplicate records; cross-check bank-held beneficiary id with bank portal; check change history for V-00948; surface payments queue more detailed audit for the affected payments.


Additional notes:
2026-03-08 11:11 - AP Lead (L. Chen): Drafted workaround: manually reconcile and reassign payment to vendor id V-0912 after Treasury confirms bank update, execute single urgent ACH via wire transfer for $12,500 to clear supplier priority invoice. Need approval from Head of Finance.
2026-03-09 09:34 - Head of Finance (A. Gupta): Approved one-off wire for priority invoice. Requested permanent fix for vendor merge and EDI header validation to surface missing PO to vendor upstream.
Preliminary root cause: duplicate vendor records (V-00948 vs V-0912) with inconsistent bank TINs created race between Vendor Master updates and bank-held beneficiary id. EDI ingestion also lacks strict PO header validation allowing non-PO invoices which complicate auto-match. Treasury confirms bank record hasn't been updated so bank rejects ACH due to beneficiary identifier mismatch.
1) Treasury to request vendor-submitted beneficiary update form (in progress). 2) AP to execute approved one-off wire for priority invoice and mark remaining payments as pending reissue. 3) Engineering to open PR to add a pre-send check that links payment vendor_id to bank-held beneficiary id and surface detailed error with reconciliation guidance. 4) Engineering to patch edi-ingest to reject EDI 810s missing PO header by default and notify vendor via standardized rejection message. Target ETA for code changes: 2026-03-17.

Issue summary:
Request to build a delegated, self-service provisioning service for an internal Research Fellow program that creates paired Confluence spaces and Slack channels with: templated space scaffolding, per-space RBAC, automated scheduled transcript export to an S3 bucket, timebound channel and space archival, and built-in audit logging and service-account rotation.

Impact:
- Current process for spinning up research sandboxes is manual, slow (~3-5 business days), and error-prone. Research Fellows and managers wait, creating friction and lost time.
- Lack of enforced archival/export means long-lived ephemeral channels and spaces accumulate sensitive notes and PII, increasing risk.

Requirements (high level):
1) Self-service portal (internal) with two-step approval: Fellow requests sandbox -> manager approval.
2) Creates: Confluence space using a Research template, and Slack channel (private) with standardized naming and membership sync.
3) Applies templates: space page tree (README, experiment-log, results, infra-notes), standard page permissions, and a designated audit channel for ops alerts.
4) Lifecycle policy: default 90-day TTL from creation, with automated reminders at 30d/7d/1d before archival. Archival should: make channels read-only, export Slack thread transcripts and pinned messages to a tenant S3 bucket, and snapshot Confluence space export (HTML/PDF) into the same bucket.
5) Audit & compliance: all provisioning actions logged to ELK and a per-request entry in CloudTrail-equivalent; service-account credentials used for exports must rotate every 30 days.
6) Opt-in extended retention for enterprise projects with manual approval flow.
7) Minimal privilege principle: provisioner service should operate via a short-lived service token minted by the infra token broker.
8) Integration points: Slack SCIM for membership, Confluence API for space creation, S3 target with encryption, and a Confluence rollback link.

Proposed workflow:
- Research Fellow opens portal and fills form (project name, manager, expected TTL, data classification).
- Auto-validate manager email and model tier.
- Send manager approval link; upon approval, provisioner creates Confluence space + Slack channel, injects onboarding scaffold pages, posts pinned onboarding message, and attaches lifecycle metadata.
- Provisioner creates a JIRA ticket in a monitoring project (INT-provision-audit) with links to resources.
- At TTL thresholds the provisioner triggers reminders and then runs archival/export playbook.

Steps already taken:
- Stakeholders: Research Org, Security, Platform, and Legal identified and informally agreed on requirements (meeting 2026-03-02).
- Security shared S3 bucket naming, KMS key ARN, and auditing requirements.
- Prototype mockups for the portal are in the Research Figma board.

Deliverables expected from this ticket:
- Implementation plan and runbook for the provisioner (includes service account model and rotation).
- Terraform/CI config to create the provisioning lambda/k8s job and necessary IAM roles.
- Confluence template and Slack onboarding message YAMLs.
- Playbook for archival/export and manual restore steps.
- Smoke test plan and rollout schedule.

Risks/Notes:
- Need privacy/legal signoff for automatic transcript export.
- SCIM writes require coordination with Identity team to avoid group collisions.
- Ensure rate limits of Confluence API are accounted for in heavy onboarding days.

Requested due date: 2026-04-17

A documented self-service flow exists with request and approval steps captured in the runbook.
Provisioner can create a Confluence space from the research template and a private Slack channel, with membership synced and onboarding content inserted.
Lifecycle TTL metadata is attached and automated reminders are sent at 30/7/1 days prior to archival.
Export workflow produces Slack transcripts and a Confluence space snapshot into the specified S3 bucket with encryption and audit logs.
Service account credentials are rotated on a 30-day cadence and rotation process is documented.
End-to-end smoke test for create -> reminder -> archive -> export passes in staging and is scheduled for production rollout.
Security and Legal have signed off on automatic export and data retention behavior.

2026-03-14 - SRE Lead (Jon Park): Suggest rate-limit backoff and jitter for Confluence API; recommend queued workers for bulk onboarding days. Also recommend using short-lived tokens via token-broker for Confluence/Slack calls.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
When a dashboard time range spans the ingestion retention boundary (e.g., 'now-90d to now'), large panels that fan out multiple series return a completely blank panel in the Console UI. Traces and raw events for the same timeframe are still queryable via the Trace view and raw exports. The blank panel occurs intermittently and appears correlated with panels that run queries hitting older hourly/rollup tables plus the recent hot partition.

Impact:
- Customer-facing dashboards appear empty for large time ranges crossing retention cutoffs.
- Users at Zypher Analytics (enterprise, heavy historical analytics) report inability to reconcile metrics with exported CSVs.
- Affects dashboards with >10 series across combined storage layers; can impact downstream alerts that depend on panel series.

Environment:
- prod | us-east (primary reports), also observed in eu-west during repro.
- Console version: web-2026.03.01
- Query-service: q-2.8.4, retention-worker: r-1.5.2

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login to Console as org admin for Zypher Analytics (org-id: zypher-001).
2) Open Dashboard 'Customer Latency — 90d Overview' (contains 12 series, split by route/model).
3) Set time range to custom: now-90d to now.
4) Click Refresh.
5) Observe panel rendering: some panels display, the large latency heatmap panel remains blank with no error.
6) Switch to Trace view for the same timeframe -> traces are visible and exportable.
7) Repeat with narrower window (now-89d to now) -> panel renders correctly.

Observed behavior:
- Blank panel (no series, no error message); browser console shows XHR 502 occasionally from query-service that is not surfaced in the UI.
- Query-service logs show a short-window SQL planner fallback and an upstream 504 in a small percentage of fanout shards.
- When blank occurs, panel-level alerting for missing series does not trigger because the UI treats the response as empty instead of error.

Expected behavior:
- Panel should render series where data exists. When one or more shards/time-partitions fail, the UI should surface a clear error and optionally render partial results. Alerts that depend on missing-series detection should consider query errors as failures rather than silent empties.

Logs / diagnostic artifacts attached to issue (customer-provided):
- Browser console HAR (redacted)
- Panel query payload and response snippets showing 502 from q-service
- Customer CSV export for same timeframe that contains non-empty rows

Additional notes:
- Customer only sees this when the query triggers cross-layer aggregation (hourly rollups + live partitions). Panels that query single layer (fully hot or fully rolled-up) do not reproduce.
- Initial hypothesis: query fanout to rollup tables uses a promisified fetch path that swallows a non-fatal shard error and returns an empty payload to UI renderer.

03-10 10:45 - Support (Maya): Received report from Zypher CS rep. Collected HAR, panel query and time range.
03-10 11:10 - Eng (Rory): Reproduced in prod on us-east with synthetic dashboard; able to reproduce ~30% of runs.
03-10 12:05 - Eng: Found query-service returns 502 for specific shard range (hourly_rollup_2025-12 to hourly_rollup_2026-01) when fanout includes both rollup and hot partitions.
03-11 09:20 - SRE: Identified that the retention-worker triggered a compaction job touching rollup metadata on 2026-03-09 which increased query latency for older shards for ~10m windows.
03-11 11:00 - Eng: Added extra logging around shard responses; observed that HTTP client layer treats 502 as recoverable and returns empty series to caller.
03-12 08:30 - Eng: Created PR to change error propagation policy so shard errors surface as recoverable partial-fail with explicit error waterfall to UI (see related_github_prs).
03-12 09:15 - Eng: Temporary mitigation: add UI-side guard to surface 'Partial data — check query logs' when any shard returned non-200. Patch deployed to staging for smoke tests.
03-12 10:00 - CS: Notified Zypher of investigation progress and recommended narrow time window as temporary workaround.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports blank panel affecting executive dashboard; provided HAR and CSV exports. Awaiting triage.
Rory Patel (Eng) 2026-03-10: Reproduced intermittently in prod. Query-service 502s observed for mixed-layer fanout. WIP to add shard-level error bubble to UI.
Alisha Rao (SRE) 2026-03-11: Compaction job coincided with incident window; verifying if compaction scheduling can be staggered to avoid hotspots.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer accepted temporary workaround (restrict range to not cross retention boundary). Requested ETA for permanent fix and note for runbook.
Rory Patel (Eng) 2026-03-12: PR opened and smoke tests passing in staging. Targeting canary deploy for prod tomorrow.
In progress. Temporary customer workaround: avoid dashboard time ranges that cross retention boundary (e.g., use now-89d). Engineering patch to propagate shard errors to UI has PR opened and staged. Post-deploy follow-up: runbook update to alert on shard 502s and ensure alerts treat query errors as failures for panel rendering. Will update ticket when canary completes.

payload.description:
During routine depot repair and reprovisioning of returned encrypted laptops we observed repeated failures when applying NVMe/SSD firmware updates. The failures correlate with devices that had BitLocker enabled and where the TPM owner was re-provisioned as part of the repair workflow. Failure mode: firmware tool exits early with device busy / access denied and task sequence stalls in WinPE.
1) Receive returned device with BitLocker encrypted OS volume.
2) Boot to WinPE from depot imaging station.
3) Run repair task sequence which: re-enrolls device into Azure AD/Intune, reapplies company provisioning profile, and runs vendor SSD firmware updater (Dell/Lenovo FW tools).
4) Observe firmware update step timeout/failure and subsequent task sequence error.
5) Attempt to re-run update: vendor tool reports device locked or unreachable (error codes shown in logs).
Example error lines copied from depot imaging logs:
[2026-03-09T08:14:22Z] fwupdate.exe --nvme-update --file NVME_2026_03_09.bin --target 0 --errorCode=0x80070005 --msg='Access denied to device handle'
[2026-03-09T08:14:22Z] TaskSequence: Step 'SSD FW Update' failed (exit 5).
WinPE logs: device enumerated as "Disk 0", but CreateFile on \\?\PhysicalDrive0 returned ACCESS_DENIED (0x5).
On-host PowerShell (after reprovision): manage-bde -status returned 'Conversion Status: Fully Encrypted', but protectors list showed new TPM protector GUID different from original device entry.
TPM event: EventID 15 - TPM ownership change detected during provisioning.
Vendor tool (DellCCTK) output: 'Device busy - NVMe controller report failed'.
Initial hypothesis: During repair we run an automated TPM reset / re-provision step (to clear previous owner's keys) which, combined with BitLocker still present on the OS volume, leaves the NVMe device in a state where firmware updater cannot open a raw device handle from WinPE. Possible causes: driver/locking interaction when TPM ownership flags change, or the imaging sequence ordering triggers an I/O quiesce race.
What we checked:
- Reconstructed the depot task sequence in staging and reproduced failure on 3 of 6 test units (models above).
- Verified that suspending BitLocker (manage-bde -protectors -disable) before FW update allows the vendor tool to complete successfully.
- Confirmed that if TPM ownership reset happens after BitLocker is suspended but before firmware step, results are nominal. If TPM reset happens during or immediately before WinPE firmware attempt, update fails.
- Cross-referenced with vendor KBs: Dell/Lenovo note that some NVMe FW update methods require exclusive device access and may be blocked if low-level security state changes occur.
- Looked for similar past ticket: INT-50321 (assetdb mismatch) referenced as related but not the same root cause.

Conclusions: Ordering in the depot runbook is the proximate cause. The repro is deterministic when TPM re-ownership occurs in the same boot cycle as FW update attempt.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 09:30 - Security (N. Patel): Concern about leaving BitLocker suspended across reprovisioning. We need to ensure suspend window is minimal and re-enable protections after firmware update and before shipping.
2026-03-13 15:02 - Eng (S. Brooks): Will add detection in imaging-scripts to check for BitLocker status and automatically suspend before fw step. Also adding automatic re-enable and TPM protector re-create after firmware. PR reference added.
Mitigation (applied 2026-03-14): Updated depot task sequence to: 1) Detect encrypted OS volume and suspend BitLocker protectors (manage-bde -protectors -disable). 2) Run vendor SSD firmware update in WinPE. 3) Run TPM re-provision / protector re-creation and re-enable BitLocker.
Permanent fix: Engineering to merge imaging-scripts PR to add idempotent suspend/resume helpers and a check that TPM re-ownership does not occur until firmware step completes (INT-432111).
Follow-ups:
- QA to run extended validation on affected models across us-west depot.
- Security to validate that suspend window is logged and limited; add audit entry to Confluence runbook.
- Ops to monitor depot throughput and reopen if regression observed.
If mitigation proves stable after 72h of samples, move ticket to Resolved and file INT-432111 for the automation work and INT-432112 for runbook update review.
payload.summary: SSD firmware update blocked during depot repair due to BitLocker/TPM owner change, causing reprovisioning failure

Issue summary:
We need a short-lived, auditable bridge that allows oncall engineers to open an interactive shell session from a secure bastion into production database hosts across both AWS and GCP. This is specifically to support fast troubleshooting during incidents where cross-cloud replication or connectivity issues are suspected.

Impact:
- Oncall is currently blocked from live triage of cross-cloud DB issues without raising a full access request and waiting for manual provisioning (30+ minutes).
- Delayed triage increases time-to-detect and time-to-mitigate for replication/consistency incidents affecting customer-facing services.

Background and constraints:
- The DB fleet includes replicas in AWS and primary instances in GCP for certain customers. Debugging often requires jumping from an oncall laptop -> bastion (audit-proxy) -> host in either cloud.
- Security requires session recording, MFA, JIT short-lived credentials (<= 1 hour), and least-privilege RBAC.
- We must avoid long-lived IAM credentials and require keys be bound to a recorded session.

Requested change / scope:
1) Create an IAM role pair and a provisioning flow that:
   - Issues an ephemeral access token for AWS via STS AssumeRole with a 1-hour max session and condition limited to SessionTags specifying ticket ID.
   - Issues an ephemeral signed IAP/OS Login session or short-lived service account key for GCP with comparable lifetime and session-scoped audit metadata.
   - Provides a unified CLI wrapper (internal tool) that exchanges SSO credentials for the ephemeral cloud tokens and opens an SSH session through the company bastion that supports session recording (tty+logs).
2) Implement a guardrail: access is only granted if the engineer has a valid PagerDuty oncall and a request is stamped with a SUP/INT ticket id.
3) Ensure CloudTrail and Cloud Audit Logs contain the session_id and user_id linking back to the ticket and the engineer's SSO identity.
4) Add automatic revocation after timeout or manual revoke from the Console.

Acceptance criteria (tests):
- Oncall engineer can start a recorded session to a target prod DB instance in either cloud within 3 minutes of request using the CLI wrapper.
- Session recordings are stored in the audit bucket with metadata that includes INT-820199 (or new generated ticket id).
- No long-lived creds are created; IAM roles exist with conditions and max session duration 3600s.
- Audit logs show AssumeRole / IAP login events with matching session tags.

Security controls & approvals required:
- Security review from InfoSec (approved by A. Patel) required before granting prod scope.
- Use KMS-wrapped session-recording encryption keys, and retention policy mirrors incident retention (90 days).
- Require MFA via SSO for the CLI exchange flow.

Expiration and cleanup:
- All temporary roles granted under this ticket must be auto-expired after 1 hour; any privileged resources created for debugging (temporary jump hosts) must be automatically terminated within 2 hours if unused.

Notes on urgency:
- Requested by oncall due to recurring cross-cloud replication incidents in the last two weeks; this will reduce escalation to EngInfra and speed root-cause triage.
Validation checklist once implemented:
1) Engineer with pagerduty oncall runs: redwood-crosscloud-shell --ticket INT-820199 --target db-prod-01 --cloud gcp
2) CLI requests SSO MFA, exchanges for ephemeral GCP session token, opens IAP SSH -> confirmation 'session-recording-id: sr-2026-03-12-0001'
3) Confirm session recording exists in gs://audit-recordings/prod/INT-820199/sr-2026-03-12-0001.jsonl
4) Repeat for AWS target: redwood-crosscloud-shell --target db-replica-aws-02 --cloud aws -> STS AssumeRole -> session appears in CloudTrail with sessionTag.ticket=INT-820199
5) Verify no long-lived keys created under the engineer's service account or IAM user.

Sanitized example traces collected during recent incident:

[2026-03-03T01:12:03Z] oncall-start: user=laura.chen@redwood.company action=attempt-bastion-login target=db-replica-aws-02 result=blocked reason=missing-crosscloud-role
[2026-03-03T01:12:45Z] escalation: slack=#incidents message='Oncall blocked; manual role needed'
[2026-03-03T01:16:10Z] manual-provision: infra-team role=debug-provision-temp user=miguel.torres issued_for=laura.chen duration=2h

Issue summary:
Request to create a reusable Confluence space template for team oncall runbooks and an automation that creates a temporary Slack channel + Jira incident project whenever a team rotation starts. The automation should provision channel permissions from the team's oncall groups, create a linked Confluence runbook page pre-populated from the template, and annotate the associated Jira project with the rotation metadata.

Impact:
- Reduces manual work when rotating oncall leads and ensures consistent runbook structure and permissions.
- Improve response time by ensuring channels and runbooks exist at rotation start.
- Potential security surface: automated channel creation requires granting a service account rights to create channels and invite groups.

Requirements / Acceptance criteria:
1) Confluence: a space template named "Oncall Runbook (templated)" with variables for Team, Rotation Start, Rotation End, Oncall Owner, PagerDuty schedule link, escalation paths, runbook sections (triage, mitigation, rollback, postmortem notes). Template must include a macro to display linked Jira INC- issues.
2) Slack: automation that creates channels with naming convention #oncall-<team>-<YYYYMMDD>-<rotation-id> and sets channel topic to include rotation owner and Confluence runbook link. Channels should be auto-archived after the rotation end + 30 days.
3) Permissions: channel membership should be inherited from existing SSO groups: team-<team>-oncall and team-<team>-eng. The provisioning flow must require an approver from Security or Platform for teams classified as "restricted".
4) Jira: create a light-weight Jira project/issue template for incident coordination that is automatically created and linked to the channel and runbook when requested.
5) Auditability: every automated action must produce an audit log entry (Confluence page created, Slack channel created, Jira project/issue created) with the service-account identity and rotation metadata.
6) Rollback & safety: provisioning should support dry-run mode and a manual approval step for first 5 team rollouts; provide a revoke action that removes channel invites and unlinks the runbook but preserves artifacts for postmortem.

Requested by: Platform Engineering on behalf of multiple pods.

Notes on scope and constraints:
- Prefer implementing automation via existing internal provisioning API (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/provisioning) rather than new bots, reusing service-account and scoped OAuth tokens.
- Security requires a short (30d) token rotation window for the service account used; consult IAM for least-privilege role.
- Confluence template must be created in the "Platform Runbooks" parent space and use page properties for automated indexing.

Suggested rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Build template and a manual provisioning playbook that SRE/Platform can run to create the first 3 team runbook spaces and channels (dry-run mode available).
- Phase 2: Implement automation with approval gating for restricted teams. Document RBAC and IAM required.
- Phase 3: Gradual enablement for all teams; add metrics (time-to-provision, number of created channels, manual approvals) to Console.

Additional notes:
Checked infra repo for existing automation patterns: found channel-provisioner service in infra repo but it lacks Confluence integration. https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/provisioning/channel-provisioner
Audit: We will reuse service-account 'provisioning-bot@redwood-inference' with reduced scopes; IAM ticket required (INT-739201 style).
Identified Confluence page property approach for indexing and automatic link embedding using page metadata macro. Need Confluence admin support to enable the required macro on platform space.
Pending - awaiting design sync and IAM approval. Proposed owner: Platform Automation team.
Workaround until automation is live: run documented manual provisioning checklist in Platform Runbooks and tag pages with rotation metadata so oncall owners can be found via the console search.

Issue summary: Customer QueryFlow reports intermittent empty result sets from reranking endpoint accompanied by p95 token latency spikes. Impact: Several production queries for rerank returned empty candidate lists or truncated partial responses; user-visible degradation for a portion of traffic. Environment: Dedicated tenant in us-east using dedicated routing through the new proxy compaction feature rolled last week.
1) Use QueryFlow test workload: 500 parallel rerank requests (batch size 32) to /v1/rerank with embedding payloads assembled by in-house proxy compaction. 2) Observe ~3-7% requests returning empty candidates or single-candidate responses. 3) Re-run with proxy compaction disabled -> behavior stops. 4) Run with canonical client sending explicit embedding-format header -> mitigates failures.
2026-03-10T14:22:11Z ERROR reranker: received embedding payloads count mismatch (expected 32 actual 28)
2026-03-10T14:22:11Z WARN proxy: compacted-segments reordered; missing segment-metadata header for request id=cf-7e3b
2026-03-10T14:22:12Z ERROR serving-runtime: fallback to CPU-ann due to ann-shard-miss; p95 latency 1240ms (baseline 210ms)
Initial hypothesis: payload compaction introduced by proxy optimization occasionally interleaves sparse (sparse-indexed) and dense embeddings without annotating per-segment encoding. The reranker expects consistent orientation per request. Reproduced locally by toggling proxy compaction flags: when compaction reorders segments and drops per-segment 'emb-format' metadata, the reranker sees mixed dtype/orientation and either filters out candidates or triggers a CPU fallback path causing high latency. Observed correlation with proxy release v1.14.2 and with multi-model routing where text-embedding-legacy-v1 coexists on same route. Confirmed presence of requests where Content-Length matched combined segments but segment-header-count was lower than actual segments (off by 1-5).

Additional notes:
Eng lead (Marta Li): Adding a defensive check in reranker to validate per-request segment headers and reject mixed-format payloads with a descriptive 422 so we can avoid silent empty-sets.
Customer (QueryFlow - Tom Nguyen): We saw this as intermittent failures across our night jobs; major impact to nightly syncs. Thanks for quick triage.
Jonah Park: Canary rollback of proxy compaction in us-east started 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC; monitoring for error-rate decrease.
Marta Li: PR created to add header validation and a metrics counter for mixed-format events: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reranker/pull/215
Disable proxy compaction for the affected tenant or set 'embed-format: explicit' header at the client to force per-segment annotations. Canary rollback applied to us-east; customer confirmed reduced failures.
1) Merge reranker validation PR and add a 422 response path for mixed-format payloads (PR #215). 2) Harden proxy compaction to always emit per-segment metadata; add integration tests that simulate interleaving. 3) Create an alert (SLO) on mixed-format counter and empty-rerank responses. 4) Run a rollback incidence review with proxy team and schedule full rollout after tests.
Partial mitigation: Canary rollback of proxy compaction removed majority of incidents in us-east. Patch PRs opened for both proxy and reranker; full fix scheduled for 2026-03-16 release. Assigned INT-4521 to proxy team for backfill integration tests and a follow-up postmortem.
