Issue summary:
Users are receiving HTTP 400 / 'invalid_request: token_too_large' responses when attempting to sign in to the internal Feature Flags admin console. The problem began after an Okta configuration rollout that enabled stricter token size enforcement on SAML/OIDC assertions.

Impact:
- Engineers cannot access Feature Flags admin UI to modify rollout rules and emergency feature toggles.
- On-call workflows (hotfix rollouts) are blocked for any team that relies on the console.
- Incident response window lengthened due to inability to temporarily flip flags.

Environment:
- Affected app: feature-flags-admin (internal console)
- Environment: prod-us-east (internal tooling network)
- Identity provider: Okta (org-wide policy change rolled out 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Navigate to https://internal.featureflags.redwood/ and click 'Sign in with Okta'.
2) Authenticate through Okta SSO flow for a user with > 20 group memberships (common for platform/admins).
3) Okta redirects back to identity-proxy with SAML/OIDC token; the proxy returns 400 and the browser shows 'invalid_request: token_too_large'.

Observed behavior:
- Immediate 400 response from identity-proxy with message referencing token size limits.
- No user session is created; UI shows login error.
- Okta admin audit logs show policy enforcement events coincident with the timing of failed logins.

Expected behavior:
- Successful SSO exchange and creation of an internal session for the console.

Initial hypothesis:
- Okta recently enabled a new token-size enforcement rule for assertion length (related to group claim expansion). Users with many group memberships produce tokens that exceed the new limit; identity-proxy rejects long tokens leading to 400s.

Relevant links/runbooks/logs:
- Slack: #support (thread t/okta-token-size-2026-03-12)
- Okta admin audit: https://okta.redwood/admin/audit?event=token_enforcement (internal)
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/internal/runbooks/identity-proxy-token-failures (internal)

Temporary mitigation attempted so far:
- Reproduced with a test account and confirmed group-count correlates with failure.
- Support temporarily re-routed a small subset of requests to fallback-idp (unavailable for most internal apps) — partial mitigation for one team.
- Okta admin contacted to confirm the policy change and request a rollback or scoped exception for internal tooling while we implement a fix.
- Confirmed timing matches Okta org policy rollout (2026-03-12 04:00 UTC).
- Token length correlates with number of group memberships; test accounts with <10 groups succeed.
- identity-proxy has an internal maximum accepted token size of ~12KB in middleware (limitation introduced by the SAML parsing library upgrade in 2026-02).
- Options considered: 1) Ask Okta to rollback/scoped-exception, 2) Increase identity-proxy token size ceiling, 3) Trim group claims (claim reduction) at Okta or proxy.
- Risk assessment: Increasing proxy token size requires a careful memory/DoS review; claim-trimming on Okta requires policy changes and may affect RBAC resolution for other apps.
- Reproduced locally with an assertion fixture; created a test PR to add logging and guardrails to identity-proxy parsing (github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1423).

Additional notes:
Triage complete. Okta granted a 72-hour scoped exception for ff-admin-client to restore access. Staged an identity-proxy code change to increase token ceiling to 32KB with monitoring and memory guards. Next steps: prod canary rollout, formalizing claim-trimming plan with IAM, and add long-term mitigation to identity runbook.
Prod canary rollout of identity-proxy token ceiling change (03:30 UTC 2026-03-13)
Add claim-trimming policy to Okta for internal apps and plan for phased rollouts
Finalize PR review and post-deploy monitoring dashboard for token-size metrics
payload.summary: Okta token-size enforcement causing 400s on Feature Flags admin console login

Issue summary:
Users are intermittently unable to complete passwordless SSO (magic link) sign-in for the internal analytics-runner console. The magic link validation returns a generic "invalid token" response in the UI and the session is not established. Impact: multiple internal teams cannot access analytics dashboards during the window.

Impact:
- ~20% of magic-link attempts for analytics-runner fail during peak morning hours (08:00-09:30 PT).
- Affected users see "invalid token" in the UI and are prompted to request a new link; re-request sometimes succeeds.

Environment:
- Prod authentication stack behind identity-proxy (us-west-2).
- Okta configured as IdP; passwordless flow issues are not present for standard username/password SSO.

Steps to reproduce (intermittent):
1) Request a passwordless magic link from analytics-runner console for a user with Okta session disabled.
2) Click link within 2 minutes.
3) Observe UI: sometimes shows successful login, sometimes shows "invalid token" and no session cookies are set.

Observed logs (examples):
- identity-proxy: "token validation failed: signature mismatch" (2026-03-10T08:14:02Z)
- auth-service: "token-not-found in key-rotation-catalog" (2026-03-10T08:14:03Z)
- browser console: 401 from /auth/callback with cookie not set

Notes: tokens generally succeed if link clicked within 30s or retried. Failures cluster during short windows that align with our hourly HMAC key-rotation job.
2026-03-10 - Support (Aisha): Initial ticket opened after Ops reported multiple login failures for analytics-runner during morning spike. Captured example logs and user timestamps.
2026-03-10 - SRE (Miguel): Reproduced intermittently in prod proxy logs. Hypothesis: race between magic link issuance and scheduled key rotation. Added detailed traces for affected tokens.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - SRE (Miguel): Deployed temporary mitigation to extend key acceptance window by +45s on identity-proxy. Monitoring for reduction in failures.
2026-03-12 - Support (Aisha): Customers (internal teams) report marked drop in failures after mitigation; still seeing rare hits around 08:00 PT. Keeping ticket open until root cause fixed.
2026-03-12 - Security (Lena Park): Requested audit of rotation logs and asked for timeline of full fix; flagged potential for transient auth audit gaps.
Correlation detected between failure spikes and hourly key-rotation cron (key-rotator v2.1) starting at :00 UTC-7.
identity-proxy currently caches accepted verification keys for 60s; key-rotator rotates keys and prunes old keys at 45s after rotation, leaving a small contention window.
Some magic links are generated with the 'old' signing key but validated after rotation prune, causing 'signature mismatch' or 'key-not-found'.
Tested local reproducer by triggering rotation immediately after link issuance and was able to replicate invalidation consistently when prune delay removed.
Mitigation (prod): increased identity-proxy accepted-key TTL to 105s; observed reduction from 20% to ~2% failure rate in morning window.
Long-term options: (A) change rotation job to mark old keys as valid for longer before prune; (B) include key id (kid) in magic link payload and fetch old key from key-rotator service on demand; (C) move to dual-signing (new+old) for a grace period.
Security review: must ensure grace periods do not open replay windows. Recommend signed counter/nonce and one-time-use enforcement for magic-links if grace is extended.
Mitigation applied: increased identity-proxy accepted-key TTL from 60s to 105s and added telemetry around key acceptance counts. Post-mitigation monitoring shows failure rate dropped from ~20% to ~2% during morning spikes.
Next steps: engineering to implement option B (include kid and fetch fallback key) with a design PR targeted for 2026-03-18 (tracking PR created). Security to review design for replay risk. After rollout, revert TTL extension to avoid longer acceptance windows if safe.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We need a recurring automation that reconciles project-level Jira permission schemes against the corresponding Confluence space permissions for the same product/team scoping. Where permission drift is detected (users/groups that have access in one system but not the other, or mismatched group roles), the automation should: 1) post a concise summary to the owning team's Slack channel; 2) create a Jira remediation ticket assigned to the project's admin group with the drift details and suggested action; 3) record an immutable snapshot of the permission state to an S3 bucket (or Confluence audit page) for audit purposes.

Impact:
- Current permission drift creates risk of overexposed documentation or denied access for on-call engineers.
- Manual reconciliations are ad-hoc and miss monthly compliance checks.

Request / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement a scheduled job (monthly) that:
  * Enumerates Jira projects with tag or custom field "ownership_team" and finds matching Confluence spaces (by space key mapping).
  * Compares group memberships and permission grants (including role-level grants like admin/edit/view).
  * Produces a structured diff per project/space and stores a gzip JSON snapshot to s3://redwood-internal-audit/permission-snapshots/YYYY-MM/INT-145287-<project>.json.gz.
  * Posts a short summary to the team's Slack channel (uses channel mapping source from /confluence/team-mapping page) with an action link to the created Jira remediation ticket.
  * Creates a remediation Jira ticket with the "remediation" label, links back to the snapshot, and assigns to the owners group.
- The automation must support a dry-run mode and an immediate run trigger via a simple web hook from the Console (URL).
- Provide a short runbook in Confluence describing how to interpret diffs and close remediation tickets.
- Ensure we have minimal PII in snapshots; redact email addresses where possible.

Proposed schedule:
- PoC run in staging: 2026-03-20 to 2026-03-22
- Production rollout (monthly schedule): 2026-04-01

Owners / stakeholders:
- Reporter: Hannah Liu (Platform Ops)
- Assignee: Diego Alvarez (IAM / Platform Services)
- Secondary reviewer: Priya Shah (Security Compliance)

Security & privacy considerations:
- Snapshots must be stored with server-side encryption and access limited to the security-audit role.
- Redact or hash email addresses in the snapshot JSON.
- Tickets created should contain only necessary context and link to snapshot in S3 rather than embedding full user lists.
Monthly job enumerates projects and matched spaces and produces diffs
Slack notifications posted to mapped owner channels with remediation ticket link
Remediation tickets include snapshot link and assigned owner group
Snapshots written to S3 with SSE and namespaced path
Dry-run and manual trigger endpoints are available for operators

Issue summary: We have ~18 legacy Confluence spaces created over multiple years for various experiment pods and research projects. These spaces have overlapping topics, inconsistent permission models (individuals added to page-level groups, expired service accounts, and external guest users), and duplicate content. Impact: Searchability is poor, audits for compliance are noisy, and new team members cannot find canonical guidance. This creates risk for compliance-heavy projects that need strict ownership and retention rules. Background: Past attempts to manually merge spaces caused page permission regressions and lost edit history. Request: Create a migration plan to consolidate legacy spaces into a smaller set of topic-hub spaces, implement a permission-translation bot that maps page-level permissions to space-level groups where possible, and produce a one-click rollback plan. Include an archival policy for low-value pages and a content-owner verification flow for all merged pages. Acceptance criteria: - Target topic-hub spaces created with appropriate templates - Bot translates at least 90% of page-level permissions to space-level groups without granting broader access than original pages - Migration preserves page history and attachments - Content owners notified and given 7 days to review/opt-out before final archive - Documented rollback and post-migration audit checklist

Full-run: schedule phased migration windows for remaining spaces with pre-migration backups
Archive: apply archival templates to pages flagged as low-value and set retention metadata
Audit: run post-migration access reports and reconcile with dry-run outputs
Rollback: if critical issues found, restore from backup and rollback bot changes

All migrated pages retain edit history and attachments
>90% of explicit page permissions mapped to reusable groups
Content owners confirmed within 7 days or pages flagged for team review
Post-migration audit report published to Confluence and linked in ticket

Week 2: Dry-run on pilot space with SRE and Security watching
Week 3: Pilot migrations and owner verification
Weeks 4-6: Phased migrations (2-3 spaces per week) with nightly backups
Week 7: Final audit and close ticket

Issue summary: A recently hired PM cannot access the internal DataViz console after completing SSO and SCIM provisioning. The user record appears in Okta and SCIM logs, but the console returns 403 with a message 'no roles assigned'. Impact: New hire onboarding blocked (cannot run dashboards or join pairing session). This is delaying a planned sync meeting tomorrow with the product team and is time-sensitive. Environment: Production (us-west), internal console behind identity-proxy, SCIM ingest pipeline v2.2.2. Steps to reproduce: 1) Invite new user via HR-provisioner -> Okta created profile. 2) Auto-provisioner runs SCIM PATCH to identity service. 3) User signs in via Okta SSO and is authenticated, but the console shows 403 and the support-runbook 'check-user-roles' returns empty role list. Observed logs: SCIM PATCH succeeded (200). Okta event shows user assigned to group "prod-dataviz-users". Identity-proxy log shows upstream call to authz service returned 204 NoContent. The console auth middleware logs: "role_lookup: 0 roles for subject=okta|12345-abcd". Hypothesis: crosswalk mapping between Okta group displayName and internal role key is failing due to a legacy transform that strips punctuation and lowercases; some groups created by IT include a trailing non-ASCII hyphen which is not normalized and therefore fails match in the role catalog.
Create Okta group with non-ASCII hyphen in displayName
Assign user to that Okta group
Allow SCIM provisioning to run and then attempt SSO login to console

okta: event=group.assignment user=ava.test@redwood.com group=prod-dataviz\u2013team (note: U+2013 EN DASH present)
authz-service: GET /roles?group=prod-dataviz--team -> 404 (no mapping)
console: role_lookup: 0 roles for subject=okta|7321-abcd
03/10 09:45 - Support triage: confirmed user exists in Okta and SCIM; console role lookup returned empty list
03/10 11:30 - Pulled role-catalog dump from authz-service; entries contain 'prod-dataviz-team' (ASCII hyphen) but not the en-dash variant
03/10 13:10 - Replayed provisioning PATCH locally with displayName normalized to ASCII hyphen; role mapping succeeded and console access granted in staging replay
03/11 08:20 - Reviewed transformation code in identity-proxy: uses python unicodedata.normalize('NFKC') but then strips '-' only for ASCII. Non-ASCII hyphen characters pass through unchanged, so lookup key does not match catalog.
Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-10: Initial report from hiring manager — new PM cannot access DataViz; confirmed 403 with 'no roles assigned'
SRE (Devon Patel) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in a staging replay. Logging indicates mismatch in group name normalization. Will attach role-catalog snapshot
IAM Eng (Priya Nair) 2026-03-11: Asked for sample Okta group displayName with hex for the dash. Provided: 'prod-dataviz\u2013team' (U+2013 EN DASH). Suspect normalization bug in provisioner pipeline.
Support (Ava Chen) 2026-03-11: Customer-facing note prepared for hiring manager with workaround: manual role assignment until fixed.
IAM Eng (Priya Nair) 2026-03-12: Confirmed fix prepared: normalize group displayName using unicode NFKD + replace any dash-like chars with ASCII hyphen before lookup. Preparing PR and rollout plan.
Role mapping relies on exact-match keys derived from Okta group displayName. Some Okta groups created by IT contained non-ASCII dash-like characters (e.g., en-dash U+2013). The SCIM/provisioner and identity-proxy pipeline did not fully normalize these variants to the canonical ASCII hyphen, so lookup against the role catalog failed, returning no roles.
Temporary workaround: manually assign the 'dataviz-viewer' role to the affected user in the admin console (documented in the support note sent to the hiring manager). Permanent fix deployed: PR #1724 normalizes incoming group displayName by applying unicode NFKD normalization, mapping common dash-like characters (U+2013, U+2014, U+2212) to ASCII hyphen, then lowercasing and collapsing whitespace before performing role lookup. The fix was rolled out to identity-proxy and provisioner v2.2.3 on 2026-03-12 in us-west with canary at 10% then 100% after 30 minutes. Post-deploy verification: recreating the original user flow now yields correct role lookup and console access.
Add unit tests for dash-like character normalization in identity-proxy and scim-provisioner
Run a catalog-scan job to detect existing Okta groups with non-ASCII punctuation and create a remediation plan (automation or guided IT cleanup)
Add telemetry alert: spike in 'role_lookup: 0 roles' per new-user provisioning events to catch regressions
Document workaround and update onboarding runbook to include group name normalization guidance for IT

Issue summary: Users cannot sign in to the internal Sentry-Bridge UI via Okta SSO. The application rejects the SAML response with a certificate/thumbprint mismatch error.

Impact: All internal Sentry-Bridge sessions requiring SSO are blocked for engineering and oncall teams in us-east. This prevents error triage and alerts access. Estimated ~25 users affected concurrently.

Environment: prod-us-east (sentry-bridge internal proxy + idp-proxy cluster: idp-proxy-prod-01..03).

Observed behavior: Attempts to sign in redirect to Okta then return with an error page: "SAML validation failed: signature verification error (certificate thumbprint mismatch)". No new sessions created; 401 returned from idp-proxy.

Expected behavior: SAML responses should validate and sessions should be created per usual.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Visit https://sentry-bridge.internal.redwood.ai 2) Click "Sign in with SSO" 3) Authenticate in Okta 4) After redirect back, application shows SAML validation error.

Relevant runbooks and links: Confluence runbook: SSO-IdP-Metadata-Rotation (link below). Slack incident thread: #support-sso (internal).
Open an incognito browser session to eliminate cached cookies
Navigate to Sentry-Bridge internal URL and click 'Sign in with SSO'
Authenticate in Okta and observe redirect back to Sentry-Bridge where the error page is shown
2026-03-13T09:12:02Z idp-proxy-prod-01 ERROR SAMLValidation - signature thumbprint mismatch: expected=3F:2B:...:A4 actual=null
2026-03-13T09:12:02Z idp-proxy-prod-01 WARN MetadataFetcher - metadata last-fetched=2026-03-13T06:05:12Z (TTL 6h), fetched_cert_thumbprint=3F:2B:...:A4
2026-03-13T09:12:02Z sentry-bridge ERROR auth - SAML response rejected, upstream status 401 from idp-proxy-prod-01
Checked Okta system log: IdP certificate rotation completed at 2026-03-13T08:10:00Z (thumbprint changed to 9A:7C:...:E1).
IdP metadata in Okta reflects the new cert; idp-proxy metadata fetch shows last success at 06:05UTC due to a runtime cache TTL of 6 hours.
idp-proxy configuration expects a single active thumbprint and rejects responses signed by any certificate not matching the cached value.
scim-sync is unrelated; no SCIM changes observed. No code deploys to idp-proxy at rotation time per GH deploy log.
Temporary workaround tested: hitting /admin/metadata/refresh on idp-proxy-prod-01 reloads metadata and allows a successful sign-in for that instance, but other instances still had old cache until restarted or refreshed.
Manual mitigation applied: Forced metadata refresh on idp-proxy-prod-01..03 via admin endpoint and zero-downtime rolling restart of idp-proxy service. Verified successful sign-ins after restart on two instances.
Short-term rollback not possible because Okta cert rotation is external. We coordinated with Okta admin to confirm rotation completion and confirm no rollback planned.
Engineering fix in progress: idp-proxy patch to accept multiple active cert thumbprints during a rotation window and to proactively fetch IdP metadata on 5xx/401 thumbprint mismatch events (PR referenced above).
Rollout plan: PR -> staging smoke tests -> canary on prod small subset -> full roll. Expected deployment 2026-03-16 after additional tests.
Follow-up actions: add alerting for repeated SAML thumbprint mismatches, reduce metadata TTL to 15 minutes, add playbook step to force metadata refresh cluster-wide after certificate rotations, and update runbook with Okta rotation checklist.

Issue summary:
Employee A (emma.jenkins) is being seconded to another team for a 6-week project. Instead of provisioning a loaner, the teams plan to do an in-place device handoff: Emma will transfer her company-managed macOS laptop (encrypted with company KMS-backed FileVault keys and enrolled in MDM) to Employee B (omar.ali).

Impact:

- Compliance/security question: what is the minimum safe window to rotate credentials and update KMS ownership for an encrypted device during a short-term handoff?
- HR asks whether we should use the standard deprovision/reprovision flow or follow a lighter-weight 'handoff' process to avoid blocking project work.

Background/context:
- Emma is full-time SWE on Platform; Omar is contractor on Data team doing a 6-week engagement.
- Device: MacBook Pro (company asset tag CB-78932) enrolled in Jamf, FileVault using customer KMS key alias: projects/redwood/keys/employee-laptops.

- No suspected compromise; this is pre-planned.

Requested decision/questions (need answers / recommended steps):
1) For a temporary 6-week handoff, do we require full device reprovision (wipe + reinstall + re-enroll) or is an in-place KMS alias re-assignment + account cleanup acceptable?
2) If in-place handoff acceptable: what credential rotation window is required for:
   - long-lived deploy keys (deploy-staging-key)
   - SSH keys used for bastion access

3) Do we need to create a new KMS key alias and re-encrypt the FileVault key material, or can we update ownership metadata on the existing key? Any HSM/KMS steps required?
4) Auditability: what logs/artefacts must be retained to show chain-of-custody during the handoff?

Steps already performed:
- HR and manager approved the handoff for 6 weeks (email thread linked below).
- Emma confirmed she has no personal SSH keys or private keys beyond company-managed ones on the laptop.

Relevant links:
- HR approval thread: https://slack.redwood/#hr-approvals/thread/CH45xk2
- Jamf device page: https://jamf.redwood/devices/CB-78932
- Internal runbook: https://confluence.redwood/display/Sec/Device+Handoffs

Please advise recommended course and an ordered checklist we can follow during the handoff window.

Issue summary: Several engineers report they are unable to re-authenticate to the Redwood Console after an IdP-initiated logout (Okta) and token revocation event. A subset of these users then trigger CI deploys (via internal CI runner) which fail during service-account token exchange. The session appears 'orphaned' in our session-store: the browser retains a session cookie that the auth-proxy accepts, but downstream services reject due to revoked tokens.

Impact: Multiple CI deploys failed for the infra team (2 blocked deploys in last 6 hours). Several users locked out of web console until a manual cookie clear. Potentially affects any workflow that performs token-exchange (service-to-service operations) when Okta revokes an access token and the session-service does not clean up in time.

Observed behavior: Users see a 403 on the CI job step 'exchange-token' and console shows 'Sign-in required' but the browser still has a console session (stale). Support note: this is not classic 401; the web session superficially looks valid which confuses users and on-call triage.
1) Have a user with an active console session (session cookie + access token in session-store).
2) Trigger IdP-initiated logout from Okta for that user (admin revoke via Okta admin console or use revocation API).
3) Observe webhook delivery from Okta to /webhooks/idp/revocations is acknowledged (200) but session-service does not immediately remove internal session record.
4) User attempts to run CI deploy which performs token-exchange; auth-proxy forwards the stale session cookie, but token-exchange fails with 403 from token-validation service.
Initial triage (Support): Verified Okta shows revocation events for affected users. Webhook delivery shows 200 from our load balancer logs.
SRE hypothesis: webhook processing acknowledged but session-service hit a transient DB timeout and skipped deletion; session remained in store but marked with revoked=true inconsistent with cache layer.
Found pattern: when webhook and parallel session refresh occur within ~500ms, cache mismatch leads auth-proxy to accept session_id from cookie while token-validation queries identity-service which sees revoked token -> 403.
Reproduction on staging: able to reproduce by issuing revoke and immediately triggering a token-exchange; root cause points to ordering/race between webhook handler, session-store TTL, and the in-memory session cache used by auth-proxy.
Related code areas: session-service deletion path, idempotency for revocation handlers, auth-proxy cache invalidation hooks.

2026-03-10T08:32:14Z session-service WARN cleanup_worker failed to find session by token_id=tok-3f2: race_condition_detected
2026-03-10T08:33:01Z auth-proxy INFO incoming request cookie session_id=sess-41 accepted
2026-03-10T08:33:01Z token-exchange ERROR exchange failed status=403 reason=token_revoked user=matthew@redwood.com request_id=rx-11
Support (Marta Lopez) 2026-03-10: Customer reports two blocked deploys; asked for logs and browser cookie screenshots.
SRE (Ravi Shah) 2026-03-10: Noted webhook 200s, started a focused runbook to reproduce. Tentatively calling this a race-condition between webhook and cache invalidation.
Platform Eng (Lina Chen) 2026-03-11: Instrumented session-service to emit revocation-handled events to Kafka; observed duplicate delivery in one case causing a transient DB lock. Adding idempotency guard.
Support (Marta Lopez) 2026-03-11: Provided workaround to affected users: clear console cookies or open an incognito window to force full re-auth, and re-run CI. Users confirmed temporary unblock.
In Progress - temporary mitigation applied (manual cookie clear recommended). Engineering to deploy idempotency and cache-invalidation fix; post-deploy will monitor for recurrence and close the ticket.
1) Push hotfix to session-service: add idempotent revocation handler and explicit cache invalidation event to auth-proxy (PR #4821).
2) Add instrumentation alert when webhook-delivered-revocations are not reflected in session-store within 2s (SLO breach candidate).
3) Run canary in prod-us-west for 2 hours, verify no CI token-exchange 403s correlated with revocations.
4) Follow-up: create a postmortem if recurrence > 1 within 72 hours.

Issue summary:
Customers (internal Redwood employees) submitting per-diem claims via the Redwood mobile app are intermittently creating duplicate reimbursement entries in the expense ledger. Investigation shows the mobile OCR pipeline normalizes receipt timestamps to UTC incorrectly when the device timezone differs from the account profile timezone, producing slightly different receipt hashes and causing the deduplication step to fail.

Impact:
- Multiple duplicate per-diem payments recorded in finance ledger for same day expenses.
- Approximate exposure: small-dollar but frequent (est. $800–1,500/month) and creates reconciliation noise.
- Affects payroll/accounting reconciliation and automated fraud flags for duplicated receipts.

Observed behavior:
- Two claims submitted by same user on same calendar date with identical images are persisted as unique receipts in ledger.
- OCR metadata shows different "captured_at" values when device timezone is non-UTC and app is offline then syncs.

Expected behavior:
- Receipt hashing and dedupe should ignore timezone-only offsets so identical images map to the same canonical receipt ID regardless of capture timezone or delayed sync.

Notes: preliminary triage points to a timezone-normalization step added to OCR metadata in mobile-sdk v2.4.0 that coerces captured_at to UTC but uses local-device offset inconsistently when sync occurs after midnight in user-local time.
On device with timezone set to America/Los_Angeles, create an account profile with timezone Europe/London.
Open mobile app v2.4.0, photograph a standard per-diem receipt just before local midnight (e.g., 23:58 PDT).
Disable network (airplane mode), wait until after midnight local device time, then re-enable network so app syncs.
Observe two receipt records in the expense UI and two ledger entries after automated sync (one with capture timestamp shifted).

Issue summary: During an automated migration to standardize Vault KV-V2 mount paths, a subset of ephemeral CI runners started failing to receive injected secrets. Impact: multiple release jobs (nightly and some canaries) returned credential-errors causing build artifacts to fail and downstream deploys to stall. Affected tenants are internal release pipelines and a handful of engineering projects that use ephemeral runners with Vault-based secret injection.

Observed behavior: ephemeral runner pods start, init-containers return healthy, but the in-pod vault-agent reports 404 when trying to read /secret/data/projects/<project>/ci-token after the mount path rename. The runner then exits with 1 and job marked FAILED. No broader Vault outages were reported.

Expected behavior: vault-agent should successfully read secrets from the new KV-V2 mount path, inject credentials into the runner environment, and allow jobs to run to completion.

Immediate business impact: blocked nightlies for two teams and delayed one minor release. Workaround required manual job rerun using a temporary templated secret path mapped in CI.

- Elevated blast radius when community-developed integrations request wide OAuth scopes.

- Security wants least-privilege guardrails and better install provenance.

- A documented API and playbook (Confluence) to request a scoped install.
- Templates for at least 3 common use cases (internal bot, alerting webhook, SMS/notification bridge).
- Install records automatically populated in Confluence page with links to Jira request and GitHub code repo.
- Admins can revoke or rotate app credentials centrally.

Issue summary: After the Okta attribute deprecation change rolled out to identity-proxy (2026-03-09), some CLI SSO-authenticated sessions are resolving to the wrong service account. Impact: Engineers lose access to internal-runner and Grafana dashboards; workflows that trigger model evals via support CLI fail. Environment: production in us-west; affects self-hosted and Dedicated customers' internal tooling integrations. Observed behavior: When a user's Okta externalId differs only by case from an existing service account (e.g., 'svc-Eval' vs 'SVC-eval'), identity-proxy's casefolding normalization collapses them to a single key and maps sessions to the first-match service account. Expected behavior: ExternalId should be matched case-sensitively for service-account resolution, or a clear collision detection should surface and reject ambiguous mappings.
1) Create two Okta service accounts with externalId="svc-Eval" and externalId="SVC-eval".
2) Deploy identity-proxy with the 2026-03-09 attribute-deprecation behavior (casefold normalization).
3) Authenticate via support-cli using SSO; exchange token for a session tied to 'svc-Eval' identity.
4) Observe session subject in authz logs and Grafana role mapping; note that some sessions are mapped to the other service account intermittently under load.
Auth trace samples: authz.trace_id=trc-20260310-7a9c, auth.log: "resolved_subject=service-account:svc-eval (id=sa-1024)" then later "resolved_subject=service-account:svc-eval (id=sa-2048)" for different requests. Splunk search: https://splunk.redwood.internal/en-US/app/search/search?q=authz.trace_id%3Dtrc-20260310-7a9c (internal). Identity-proxy container logs: last-deploy commit abc123def, config flag okta.casefolding=true.
- First-pass: correlation between the 2026-03-09 deploy and onset of incidents.
- Hypothesis: okta-sync pipeline now normalizes externalId to lower-case (casefold) to align with Okta deprecation changes; this introduced non-unique keys when service accounts differ only by case.
- Repro on staging with the same config reproduced ambiguous mapping under concurrent requests; race due to in-memory map insertion order.
- Related commit: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy@abc123 (okta attribute deprecation).
- Quick mitigation: toggled okta.casefolding=false in identity-proxy rollout to restore prior behavior; affected sessions began resolving consistently to expected identities (temporary).
- Long-term: require a migration plan to either enforce canonical externalId uniqueness (case-insensitive) or maintain case-sensitive exact-match behavior for service-account resolution and add collision detection to sync pipeline.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Engineering (Oliver Grant): I reproduced locally on staging by creating two service accounts that differ only by case. Behavior follows: identity-proxy normalizes and returns the first matched account. Adding to in-progress.
2026-03-10 13:30 - SRE (Diego Rivera): Rolled back okta.casefolding flag to false on canary; observed consistent subject resolution. Recommending temporary rollback in us-west while patch is prepared.
2026-03-11 09:20 - Security (Aisha Khan): This is high-risk for impersonation vectors if left; recommend enforcing uniqueness policy and adding detection alerts.
2026-03-12 15:00 - Engineering (Oliver Grant): Draft PR created to add collision detection and prefer exact-case match for service-account resolution; see related PR link below. Planning patch release 2026-03-14.

Additional notes:
Mitigation applied: set okta.casefolding=false in identity-proxy to restore case-sensitive resolution as a stopgap. Next steps: merge PR that adds explicit collision detection, a fatal error on ambiguous externalId mapping for service accounts, and a migration script to canonicalize or rename colliding service accounts. Issue summary: Multiple Surface Pro (ARM) devices reporting sudden loss of access to internal services immediately after roaming between 2.4GHz and 5GHz SSIDs. VPN (WireGuard) remains 'connected' but traffic to internal subnets (10.10.0.0/16) no longer flows. Impact: several engineers working on private repos and internal dashboards were blocked. Scope: 6 confirmed machines in SF office, same Wi-Fi AP cluster, mixed OS build 22H2 on ARM.

Expected behaviour: roam completes, VPN stays connected and internal routes remain pinned via split-tunnel rules.

Observed behaviour: after roam, Windows chooses different physical adapter and flips interface metrics; WireGuard continues with handshake but system route table places default for internal subnets via physical adapter that has no corporate VLAN reachability, causing traffic to leave on guest VLAN and be dropped by edge firewall.

1) Start WireGuard client connected to corporate split-tunnel config (internal subnets pinned).
2) On Surface Pro ARM device, trigger 2.4GHz->5GHz roam (walk between APs or toggle radio to force handoff).
3) Observe Windows network interface metric and route table immediately after roam (use `Get-NetIPInterface` / `route print`).
4) Attempt to reach internal service (e.g., git.redwood.internal:22 or 10.10.5.12) — connect fails despite WireGuard reported as connected.
5) Compare traffic path with packet capture on client (Wireshark) and AP logs.
6) Reboot or manually set interface metric back and confirm connectivity returns.
Selected excerpts:
- WireGuard status: peer=corp-peer latest-handshake=0s transfer=12.4 MiB/1.2 MiB
- Windows Event Log (NetworkProfile) 2026-02-24 09:18:12: Interface metric changed: InterfaceIndex=23 old=25 new=2
- netsh interface ip show config (post-roam): Ethernet 23 (Wi-Fi-5G): Metric 2, IPv4 DHCP, DNS suffix not set
- route print (post-roam): 10.10.0.0 mask 255.255.0.0 192.168.50.1 if 23 metric 2
- AP Controller logs: client A: roam success to AP-B bssid=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, assigned VLAN guest (300) due to NDP mismatch

Additional notes:
2026-02-24 14:05 - Windows sysadmin (Liam): Verified Windows behavior: on ARM build 22H2 with specific Qualcomm driver v4.2.0.13, `Automatic metric` flag toggles on roam, recalculating interface metric and reordering route table. Confirmed that persistent split-tunnel routes remain but traffic egresses via interface with lower metric to non-corporate gateway.
2026-02-25 09:12 - Repro test: Disabled 'EnableReassociation' on AP and forced roam — metric flip still occurs but VLAN remains corporate; suggests dual contribution: both AP transient VLAN assignment and client metric recalculation necessary to cause outage.
2026-02-26 10:00 - Vendor engagement: Opened ticket with Qualcomm driver team; they acknowledged a known issue where NDIS 6.70 events trigger metric recalculation on 802.11r handoff for certain NIC firmware. Vendor provided a beta driver that pins interface metric.
2026-02-27 16:30 - Mitigation test: Applied local Group Policy (script) to set interface metrics to higher priority for corporate SSID; confirmed successful mitigation on 5 test devices.
Support - Liam O'Connor (2026-02-24 09:35): Acknowledged, investigating. Asking for affected device model list and timestamps.
Network - Diego Ramos (2026-02-24 11:20): Looked into AP controller logs; saw transient VLAN assignment during reassoc. Noted sticky-client policy triggered on AP-B.
QA - Mei Chen (2026-02-25 10:10): Reproduced with debug build; metric flips observed only on Qualcomm NICs on ARM Surface. Intel x86 devices unaffected.
Root cause: Interaction between AP controller transient VLAN reassignment during roam and Qualcomm Wi-Fi NDIS driver behavior on ARM devices that triggers automatic interface metric recalculation. This allowed split-tunnel routes to be overshadowed by a lower-metric gateway on the guest VLAN.
Immediate remediation: 1) Deployed a client-side mitigation: Group Policy to set explicit interface metric for corporate SSID and a PowerShell script to re-assert routes for 10.10.0.0/16 on network change. 2) Updated WireGuard client to 1.2.3 which rejects ephemeral route replacements for pinned subnets. 3) Adjusted AP controller sticky-client policy to avoid transient VLAN flips during 802.11r handoffs on the affected AP cluster.
Permanent fix / follow-up: Qualcomm to release driver firmware with NDIS fix (vendor ticket QC-29812). IT will monitor and schedule driver rollout after vendor QA. Created follow-up internal task INT-356802 to track vendor driver validation and fleet upgrade.
payload.summary: Surface Pro (ARM) dual-radio metric flip during roam causes WireGuard split-tunnel to lose internal routes

payload.description:
Issue summary: After a recent company-wide BIOS configuration baseline pushed via SCCM, a subset of laptops connected to corporate USB-C docks intermittently fail Power Delivery (PD) negotiation and do not enumerate peripherals. Impact: Users experience no charging while docked, external monitors not detected, and some devices fail to complete enrollment during zero-touch provisioning, blocking new-hire workstation setup and on-desk productivity. Environment: Observed on Dell Latitude 9440 and Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Gen 11 devices in prod-us-west and prod-eu-west. BIOS baseline applied on 2026-03-09. Problem first reported by onboarding team 2026-03-10.
1) Start with device on battery (20-60%). 2) Attach company-branded USB-C dock (firmware v1.3.2). 3) Observe power LED and battery state; watch dmesg/syslog and Windows Event Viewer for device enumeration events. 4) On affected devices, PD negotiation fails within 3-8 seconds and laptops remain on battery; on others PD succeeds. 5) Reboot or hot-unplug/re-plug may temporarily restore PD for some devices.
Windows Event IDs: Kernel-PnP 219, Kernel-Power 41 (some occurrences). UEFI logs on affected units show ACPI: PD_PORT_HANDLER error codes and USB PD negotiation timeout. Dock debug logs (partner) show 'NO_SINK_CAPS' followed by repeated 'PD_RETRY' entries. SCCM deployment logs show BIOS baseline applied successfully to host IDs prior to failure window.
Hypothesis: New BIOS baseline flips an ACPI/PD compatibility flag (DisableLegacyPD) which interacts poorly with Intel PD controller fw 2.7.1, causing the host to advertise incompatible sink capabilities. Evidence: Repro on multiple units with identical PD fw; units with PD fw 2.8.0 unaffected. SCCM logs show BIOS setting toggled at baseline rollout. Vendor dock logs show 'NO_SINK_CAPS' which aligns with host failing to respond to PD contract requests. Next steps: (1) Create test group to revert BIOS setting on small cohort. (2) Coordinate PD controller firmware flash to 2.8.0 on failing devices. (3) Request dock vendor to provide tolerant fallback for legacy hosts if possible. (4) Add hardware inventory check to provisioning pipeline to avoid blocked autopilot with known PD fw versions.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 17:10 - Security (Jessie Kwan): Confirmed no data exfil or security alert correlated; this is a hardware/UEFI negotiation regression.
Workaround: Reverted BIOS DisableLegacyPD flag in SCCM for impacted device collection and queued a staged rollback for devices with PD fw 2.7.1. For immediate onboarding, provisioning team used USB-A chargers and manual imaging for 7 affected hires. Permanent fix: Coordinated with hardware vendor to produce PD controller firmware 2.8.0 image; SRE scheduled PD firmware update for affected asset tag range and added post-flash verification steps. Also updated the BIOS baseline playbook to skip toggling PD compatibility flags until PD controller fw compatibility is validated. Follow-up: Runbook updated and a small audit scheduled to detect devices with PD fw <=2.7.1 before future BIOS pushes.
payload.summary: USB-C PD negotiation failing after BIOS config push causing dock/charging/provisioning disruptions

Summary: Several headless workstations in the depot (model: RW-Edge-1500) failed provisioning after the scheduled corporate SSH certificate rotation. The provisioning-agent reports 'server certificate unknown' and aborts before SCCM check-in. Impact: 8 devices in current repair batch failed to complete imaging and remained in 'awaiting-enrollment' state, causing repair SLA misses. This appears limited to headless units that rely on the depot's pre-seeded SSH CA chain rather than interactive machine enrollment flows.
Repair pipeline blocked for 8 devices (RW-Edge-1500). Depot throughput reduced ~12% for the 4-hour window. No customer-facing impact but internal SLA breaches for depot repairs.
1) Start with a headless RW-Edge-1500 with factory SSD replaced and default image applied.
2) Boot to depot network (VLAN 1201) and trigger provisioning-agent v1.12.0 with --autoEnroll.
3) Observe agent attempting SSH handshake to provisioning gateway (provisioning-gw-us-east.redwood.io:2222).
4) During handshake, provisioning-agent fails with 'server certificate unknown (public key not accepted)'.
5) Agent exits before SCCM/Device-Enrollment step; device remains in 'awaiting-enrollment' state in depot UI.
Mar 05 08:14:22 agent[2154]: DEBUG ssh: starting handshake to provisioning-gw-us-east:2222
Mar 05 08:14:22 agent[2154]: ERROR ssh: server certificate unknown: fingerprint mismatch (expected: SHA256:abcd..., got: SHA256:ef01...)
Mar 05 08:14:22 agent[2154]: ERROR provisioning: aborting because SSH server identity verification failed
Mar 05 08:14:22 systemd[1]: provisioning-agent.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Rotation of the corporate SSH CA replaced the host certificate on provisioning gateway with a new chain. Depot headless provisioning images expect the previous host fingerprint pre-seeded in /etc/provisioning/known_hosts-ca and do not accept CA-signed chains that were rotated unless the CA root is present. The timing of the cert rotation and a deferred CA root rollout to the depot image caused the mismatch.
08:30 - Confirmed scheduled ssh CA rotation (engsec runbook) at 2026-03-05T04:00:00Z. Rotation included issuing new host certs for provisioning-gw-us-east.
09:10 - Pulled /etc/provisioning/known_hosts-ca from an affected image: file contains explicit host key fingerprint pointing to old host cert (SHA256:abcd...).
09:35 - Verified provisioning-gw-us-east now presents host cert with new fingerprint SHA256:ef01... (matches PKI rotation PR).
10:00 - Reproduced locally by booting a golden headless image in lab: agent v1.12.0 fails unless /etc/provisioning/known_hosts-ca is updated to include the new CA root or host key.
10:45 - Cross-checked with interactive laptops: those route to same gateway but perform interactive trust-on-first-use flow and succeeded; hence issue isolated to headless autopilot of depot images.
11:20 - Checked codepath in provisioning-agent: uses strict known hosts verification by default with no fallback to CA trust unless explicit CA file present (see github PR comment).
11:50 - Manual update: pre-seeded /etc/provisioning/known_hosts-ca on 8 affected devices with new fingerprint; devices re-run provisioning-agent and completed enrollment (workaround).
12:30 - Applied temporary network ACL rule to allow affected devices to use interactive enrollment gateway (int-enroll-us-east) as fallback; increased depot operator overhead.
13:40 - Notified EngSec and PKI team to fast-track CA root distribution plan for depot images.
Scheduled SSH CA/host certificate rotation replaced provisioning gateway host key. Depot headless images contained a hard-coded expected host fingerprint in known_hosts-ca; provisioning-agent v1.12.0 performs strict host-key verification without a CA-root fallback for non-interactive flows. The combination caused verification failures on re-imaged headless devices that had not been updated with the new CA root.
1) Short term: updated depot golden image to include new SSH CA root and refreshed /etc/provisioning/known_hosts-ca; re-imaged queued devices and cleared pending repair backlog. 2) Medium term: merged github.com/redwood/provisioning-agent/pull/1428 which adds a CA-root fallback and a configurable 'ca_roots_path' for headless flows; will ship v1.12.1. 3) Runbook: added 'SSH CA rotation' checklist to Depot Provisioning Runbook to pre-seed images + orchestrate agent rollout before PKI rotation.
Hotfix applied: golden image updated and 8 devices re-imaged successfully. provisioning-agent v1.12.1 released to depot fleet; continued monitoring for 48 hours. No escalation to Execs required. Workarounds and runbook updates published.
- Release provisioning-agent v1.12.1 with CA-root fallback. (Assignee: Ravi Patel, ETA: 2026-03-09)
- Rebuild and redeploy depot golden image with updated CA bundle. (Owner: Depot-Ops, ETA: 2026-03-08)
- Add automated CI check to detect hard-coded host fingerprints in golden images. (Owner: DX infra, ETA: 2026-03-16)
- Schedule a pre-rotation verification window for future PKI rotations; include Depot/Ops in EngSec rotation emails.
Maya Chen (Reporter) - 2026-03-05 08:45: Initial ticket opened after depot ops reported batch failures. Attached failed device IDs and timestamps to ticket.
Ravi Patel (Assignee) - 2026-03-05 09:05: Acknowledged. Spinning up a lab repro with golden headless image and gateway mirror; suspecting SSH CA timing issue.
Depot Ops (Liam O'Neal) - 2026-03-05 11:55: We manually injected the new host fingerprint into the 8 affected units and re-ran the agent; confirmed enrollment completed. Pushing this to ticket as workaround.
EngSec (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-05 12:20: We confirm a scheduled CA rotation; we will provide updated CA bundle and coordinate with Depot to pre-seed images. Apologies for the outage window.
Ravi Patel - 2026-03-06 16:02: PR #1428 adds CA-root fallback. Running integration tests now. Will cut v1.12.1 once green.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customers using Redwood Private (VPC) are seeing intermittent failures when starting long-lived gRPC streams (chat/streaming API). The TLS handshake completes from the outside but application-layer ALPN negotiation fails and the connections fall back to HTTP/1.1 or are reset. Impact: Streaming sessions fail to establish ~5-15% of the time for affected customers in eu-west-1, leading to degraded UX and increased retries. Environment: Private deployment in customer's VPC, control plane peered to Redwood, running serving nodes behind internal NLB. Observed since 2026-03-09 04:00 UTC.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From a client inside the customer's corporate network initiate a streaming generate() request to the customer's private endpoint.
2) Observe handshake completes but server and client disagree on ALPN selection; gRPC library logs 'no application protocol' or 'ALPN mismatch'.
3) Repeat under different network paths (direct corp network, via VPN) — issue frequency varies.

Observed behavior:
- TLS ClientHello appears to be truncated mid-extension list (Wireshark PCAPs show ClientHello length shorter than expected, large extension fields cut).
- Server selects default cert or negotiates HTTP/1.1; gRPC handshake fails with status UNAVAILABLE on first attempt.
- Artifact fetches and control-plane RPCs are unaffected; issue limited to new long-lived streaming session establishments.

Expected behavior:
- Full ClientHello delivered; proper ALPN negotiated (h2), gRPC streams established reliably.

Logs/Artifacts provided:
- Customer PCAPs (s3://momentumfin-support-pcap/pcap-2026-03-09.pcap) showing ClientHello truncated after ~512 bytes.
- Redwood serving node TLS debug log snippets (attached) showing negotiation fallback.
- Trace id: trace-eu-20260309-78ab (control-plane traces show normal auth flow).
- Slack thread: #support-momentumfin (link shared with SRE team).

Initial hypothesis:
- On-path corporate DPI/NGFW is rewriting or enforcing a max TLS ClientHello size and dropping the remainder, removing ALPN extensions and optionally SNI or other extensions.
- Truncation causes servers to not see required ALPN (h2) and fallback triggers.

Business impact and urgency: Customer is enterprise, private deployment, experiencing production user impact. Requested priority escalation and support for a mitigated workaround.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:38 - MomentumFin Engineer (customer): We pushed a change to client TLS stack to reduce extension list temporarily; observed reduced failure rate but still seeing resets from some office locations.
2026-03-12 16:00 - MomentumFin (customer): Provided firewall policy export; confirmed an 'inspect-tls-ext' rule enabled for outgoing TLS sessions that truncates oversized ClientHello beyond 600 bytes for deep inspection performance.
Verified truncation boundary: packets consistently drop extensions after ~600 bytes in ClientHello. This removes ALPN (h2) in certain client stacks that send ALPN late in the extension list.
Reproduced locally by configuring a test DPI instance with 'inspect-tls-ext' rule; when rule set to truncate TLS ext >600 bytes client hello became truncated and ALPN disappeared.
Temporary client-SDK mitigation: reorder extensions so ALPN appears earlier in ClientHello; we created a small patch build to test on customer devices which lowered failure rate but is intrusive and not recommended long-term.
Long-term: Recommend customer disable truncation or increase threshold, and work with DPI vendor for a fix that preserves ALPN/SNI while performing inspection. Redwood to publish guidance for firewall tuning for private deployments.
Cross-check: Control-plane auth uses shorter ClientHello and is unaffected; issue is sensitive to client TLS implementation (OpenSSL vs BoringSSL variants differ in extension ordering).
Workaround applied: Customer disabled the 'inspect-tls-ext' truncation rule in their corporate DPI during a maintenance window (2026-03-12 22:00 UTC). Post-change monitoring shows stream establishment success rate returned to baseline (~99.9%).
Next steps and follow-ups:
- MomentumFin to engage DPI vendor to obtain patch that preserves ALPN while still allowing inspection (owner: MomentumFin network ops).
- Redwood: publish an internal runbook and a public KB article 'Firewall DPI truncating TLS ClientHello causes gRPC ALPN failures' with recommended firewall rule adjustments and SDK mitigations (owner: DevRel/Docs).
- Engineering: propose optional SDK change to advertise ALPN earlier in ClientHello for customers who cannot modify DPI immediately (low-risk experimental flag; owner: SDK team, ticket created: INT-9202).
Status: Awaiting customer confirmation of vendor patch rollout. Will transition to 'Resolved' once vendor patch is deployed and stable for 48h or if customer declines vendor fix and chooses to keep rule disabled permanently.
payload.summary: Intermittent TLS ClientHello truncation by corporate DPI causing gRPC ALPN negotiation failures on private deployment

Issue summary: After the scheduled bastion host SSH key rotation on 2026-03-09, a subset of CI runners began failing git fetch/clone operations with host key mismatch errors. Impact: ~12% of builds that need to access private repos via the bastion experienced checkout failures, causing release and nightly pipelines to flake. This appears limited to ephemeral runners that had previously cached known_hosts entries, and the failures started immediately after rotation.

Observed error sample: 'WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED!
IT IS POSSIBLE THAT SOMEONE IS DOING SOMETHING NASTY!' followed by 'Host key verification failed.'

Business impact: Delays to canary release jobs and CI congestion as retries accumulate. No customer-facing outages, but blocking release cadence for two engineering teams.
1) Provision ephemeral runner that will route git traffic through bastion egress proxy.
2) Ensure known_hosts for bastion present in runner image (from prior successful checkouts).
3) Rotate bastion host SSH key (performed by infra schedule on 2026-03-09).
4) Trigger pipeline that performs 'git clone' of internal repo. Observe host key mismatch and checkout failure.
run-2026-03-10-12:14:23 - git@bastion.internal: Permission denied (publickey). Host key verification failed.
runner-ephemeral-xy12 - ssh: handshake failed: host key mismatch: got 'ecdsa-sha2-nistp256' expected 'rsa-sha2-512'
proxy-audit - 2026-03-09T03:02:15Z - bastion-key-rotate: new-key-published, old-key-removed
03/10 09:00 - Triage: Correlation between bastion key rotation window and spike in runner checkout failures. Not all runners affected; pattern tied to runners that retain known_hosts across warm pool cycles.
03/10 10:22 - Hypothesis: Ephemeral runners reuse filesystem layers or cached /home/runner/.ssh/known_hosts entry created before rotation; SSH client refuses new key causing immediate failure instead of interactive fingerprint acceptance.
03/10 11:05 - Verified: New long-lived dedicated runners (fresh instances) do not fail; ephemeral warm pool runners with preserved workspace show failures.
03/11 14:30 - Found CI image build step that pre-populates known_hosts using 'ssh-keyscan' at image bake time. Image bake predates rotation and therefore contains stale key for affected runners.
03/11 16:00 - Cross-reference: linked infra runbook for bastion rotation (CON-BASTION-ROTATE) lacks a step to invalidate runner caches or trigger pool recycle. Added as follow-up.
Short-term: Add a pre-check job to affected pipelines to run 'ssh-keyscan -H bastion.internal >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts' before git operations; rolling patch applied to two failing repos as a stopgap. Medium-term: Update runner warm-pool lifecycle to clear ~/.ssh/known_hosts on start and ensure image bake process does not bake static bastion keys.
Work in progress. Emergency mitigation (pre-check ssh-keyscan) deployed to release pipelines on 2026-03-11 which reduced failure rate to <1%. Follow-up tasks created to bake image fix and to update bastion rotation runbook. Will close ticket once warm-pool fix is deployed and monitored for 48h without regression.

Additional notes:
SRE - Priya Shah (03/11): Confirmed bastion rotation executed 2026-03-09 03:02 UTC. No other network changes. Suggest running 'ssh-keyscan' as temporary workaround.
BuildME - Jordan Lee (03/11): Applied ssh-keyscan pre-step in repo 'infra/deploy-svc' and observed successful run after one retry. Recommending org-wide mitigation rollout.
1) Merge runner-images PR to remove baked known_hosts and push new AMI (owner: Diego Ramos).
2) Update bastion rotation runbook to include a runner warm-pool recycle step (owner: Priya Shah).
3) Add automated CI smoke test that runs ssh-keyscan against bastion in prelude for pipelines that use bastion egress (owner: Jordan Lee).
4) Monitor failure rate for 48 hours post-deploy and close ticket if stable (owner: Support Team).
payload.summary: Runner SSH known_hosts cache causing intermittent git fetch failures after bastion host key rotation

Issue summary: New employees and contractors created after a recent change to the Analytics SAML app fail to receive the expected 'analytics:viewer' or 'analytics:editor' roles via Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning. Impact: Affected users can authenticate via Okta SSO but land in the analytics console with no roles and 'access denied' when attempting to load dashboards. This blocks onboarding and on-call access for a subset of infra/ops engineers. Environment: prod (us-east).

Observed behavior: Users successfully SSO into the Analytics UI, but the internal identity service logs show JIT provisioning rejected due to SAML assertion audience mismatch or missing role attribute. Expected behavior: Okta SAML response should be accepted and JIT should create the user with roles derived from the SAML attribute mapping.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a test Okta user in the same group used for new hires (okta-group: infra-analytics).
2) Trigger SSO to https://analytics.internal.redwood.ai using Okta (SAML redirect).
3) Inspect identity service logs for the SAML Assertion handling and JIT flow.

Observed logs: see 'logs' field. Temporary workaround: Manual user creation with roles via identity admin CLI and short-term rollback of the proxy entityID change applied to the analytics SAML app. Workaround applied 2026-03-13 18:40 UTC restored access for ~70% of affected users; remaining accounts require manual role grant.

Investigation summary: The analytics SAML app's entityID was changed on 2026-03-12 as part of an internal routing change (added ':proxy' suffix to support multi-tenant routing through a reverse proxy). The JIT handler validates the SAML Audience/Recipient strictly against a single accepted entityID ('urn:redwood:analytics') and therefore rejects assertions with 'urn:redwood:analytics:proxy'. Additionally, when the SAML assertion is accepted by a fallback path, the role attribute mapping is occasionally absent for SCIM-provisioned contractor accounts, causing a no-role state. The combination of a stricter audience check and inconsistent role attribute mapping explains the partial rollback success.

Next steps / proposed fix:
- Short term: Expand JIT acceptedAudience list to include 'urn:redwood:analytics:proxy' and run a reconciler to grant roles to accounts created without attributes. (Owner: identity infra)
- Medium term: Update Okta app metadata to standardize entityID (preferred) and remove proxy-suffixed entityIDs; update routing so proxies preserve original entityID in the SAML flow. (Owner: infra)
- Add an automated smoke test for JIT provisioning during deploys and a post-change reconcile job to find accounts with no roles.

Impact metrics: ~18 affected accounts identified so far (mix of full-time and contractors). Severity classified Sev2 due to operational but not company-wide outage.

Initiate SSO to https://analytics.internal.redwood.ai

Issue summary: Security team is onboarding an external auditing partner and needs a timebound collaboration surface that includes a Slack workspace scoped to just the audit engagement, a Confluence project for evidence exchange, and automation to provision guest accounts, enforce RBAC, and auto-archive after the engagement window.

Background: Current partner/onboarding flows are manual and across multiple tickets. Security requests a gated, auditable pattern with templatized channels/pages, just-in-time guest invites, and a retention/auto-archive lifecycle so evidence does not remain indefinitely. This ticket requests a one-off provisioning flow and an automation template the platform team can reuse.

Impact: Without this, onboarding the auditor requires multiple manual steps from SRE, Security, and Platform which extends audit start date and increases risk of mis-scoped access. The auditor requires access by 2026-03-10 to keep the engagement on schedule.

Requirements: 1) Create a new Slack workspace or workspace-like channel namespace named 'partner-audit-2026' scoped to auditing vendor group. 2) Create a Confluence project 'Partner Audit - Q1 2026' with a pre-populated evidence page template and access controlled to the vendor group + security + PO. 3) RBAC: limited guest lifetime (30 days) with expiration and a self-revoke link; no ability to export channels or pages. 4) Automation: a provisioning workflow (Slack invite -> create Confluence space -> generate service account for webhook-> attach retention policy) triggered from a Jira transition or a short form. 5) Auditability: action log export for audit trail and notification to #security-audit on creation/close. 6) Post-engagement: automated archive of Slack channels and Confluence space with snapshot export to restricted S3 and removal of guest accounts.

Acceptance criteria: - Workspace/spaces provisioned and accessible by named vendor accounts. - A templated Confluence page exists with placeholders and share link. - Guest accounts have TTL and are automatically disabled at expiry. - Automation can be executed via an approved Jira transition and completes end-to-end in <15m. - Security confirms audit trail visibility.

Security considerations: Follow Third-Party Access Checklist (see links). Use tenant-scoped service accounts. All secrets stored in KMS. No external file attachments permitted in public channels.

Ops notes: Prefer using existing ephemeral-workspace automation runbook; if missing, create new reusable playbook.

Issue summary: After a recent office CAB change at the SoMa satellite office we started seeing a sustained increase in VPN session failures and SSO timeouts for users on the office Wi‑Fi. Impact: ~12-18% of users at SoMa experience intermittent 403/SSO timeouts or are unable to reach internal services that normally resolve via VPN private IPs. Service impact is localized to the office LAN and affects employees using company Wi‑Fi and a subset of developer services behind policy-based routing. Initial hypothesis: an intermediate bridge/AP that was re-provisioned to 'NAT' mode is rewriting source addresses causing VPN policy lookup to fail, triggering mis-routed traffic and SSO token validation errors.
1) Connect a laptop to SoMa corporate Wi‑Fi (ssid: Redwood-Corp).
2) Establish Redwood VPN (WireGuard client) and authenticate via SSO (Okta).
3) Attempt to curl an internal service at 10.11.20.5: expect success; observed: connection resets or 403 responses.
4) Observe device local IP (e.g., 192.168.50.34) and the outbound NATed IP as seen by internal services (packets show 10.100.200.1 source after NAT rewrite).
Clients on office Wi‑Fi see internal service requests fail intermittently. Packet captures from service frontends show source IPs mapped to 10.100.200.0/24 (bridge appliance SNAT pool) instead of clients' VPN-assigned 10.8.0.0/16 addresses. Okta SSO validation rejects token assertions when source IP does not match expected corporate ranges, causing auth flows to fail.
Traffic from VPN clients should preserve VPN-assigned source addresses. Office bridge should be in passthrough mode for tunneled traffic so policy-based routing at the gateway can correctly match flows and SSO sees expected IP ranges.
2026-03-10T09:22:13Z firewall[gw-usw-1]: policy_lookup: src=10.8.12.45 dst=10.11.20.5 matched=internal-web-cluster action=allow
2026-03-10T09:22:13Z app-fw[web-01]: tcpdump: in.ether src=10.100.200.14:52344 > 10.11.20.5:443 SYN
2026-03-10T09:23:01Z okta-proxy[auth-01]: token_validation: ip_mismatch user=jared@example.com expected_range=10.8.0.0/16 seen_ip=10.100.200.14
- Confirmed bridge device model: Ubiquiti UBB‑Edge v2 (serial: UB-1212). Reprovisioning on 2026-03-09 set its WAN mode to 'Gateway (NAT)' instead of 'Bridge'.
- tcpdump on web-01 shows multiple connections with SNATed sources 10.100.200.0/24. When testing from a home client via remote VPN this does not occur; home clients preserve 10.8.x source addresses.
- ip rule list on gw-usw-1 shows policy routing keyed on src network 10.8.0.0/16. Because SNAT rewrote source to 10.100.200.x the kernel falls back to default route and packets get dropped or mis-routed to edge ACLs.
- Quick check: ssh to bridge admin UI -> Network -> NAT Mode = Enabled. CLI 'iptables -t nat -L -n' shows POSTROUTING MASQUERADE for bridge LAN range.
- Hypothesis validated by temporary change: disabled NAT on bridge -> source IPs preserved -> internal service connectivity restored and SSO token validations succeed.
pcap snippet (web-01): 10.100.200.14.52344 > 10.11.20.5.443 Flags [S] seq 0 win 64240
pcap snippet (after fix): 10.8.12.45.52344 > 10.11.20.5.443 Flags [S] seq 0 win 64240
On affected office bridge, re-enable 'passthrough/bridge' mode or add a NAT-exemption rule for VPN-assigned subnets (10.8.0.0/16). As an immediate mitigation, network ops applied a bridge-level configuration that disables MASQUERADE for src 10.8.0.0/16 which restored service for all connected clients.
Temporary mitigation applied on 2026-03-11: NAT exemption rule added to bridge and config pinned. Next steps: schedule coordinated firmware fix and update CAB provisioning template to ensure edge bridges are provisioned in 'bridge' mode for corporate VLANs that host VPN clients. Postmortem to be created and template change rolled out to 5 remote offices.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:05 - SRE Oncall (Riley Morgan): Did quick checks, observed SNATed sources on web frontends. Asking networking to verify bridge provisioning state and recent CAB changes.
2026-03-10 13:12 - Networking (Diego Alvarez): Confirmed bridge was reprovisioned yesterday as part of patch window; default image set WAN mode to Gateway/NAT. Preparing rollback of NAT change and plan for NAT-exempt rule for 10.8.0.0/16.
payload.summary: Office edge bridge in NAT mode rewriting source IPs and causing VPN policy routing failures and SSO timeouts

Issue summary:
A scheduled payout to supplier 'Greenwave Logistics' (vendor ID V-003412) for invoice batch MARCH-02 was blocked when the payment engine posted the cleared remittance to a suspense GL (4000-SUSP) instead of the designated vendor clearing account (2100-AP). This appears tied to a cross-currency settlement step where the USD -> EUR FX conversion name did not match the ledger mapping key, causing downstream allocation to fail and the upcoming ACH batch to be held by the payments scheduler.

Impact:
- One scheduled ACH payout (net ~USD 38,500) is on hold and shows as pending-cleared in the banking integration UI.
- Finance cannot close the vendor month-to-date balance for Greenwave; month-end reconciliation is impacted for AP.
- Risk of late payment and supplier escalation if not resolved prior to next attempt (scheduled 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC).

Environment:
- Production payments pipeline (payments-service v3.8.1), connected to bank connector 'StripeBank-Prod'.
- Vendor: Greenwave Logistics (V-003412).
- Invoices: INV-2026-0032, INV-2026-0033 (multi-PO allocation across PO-7781 & PO-7785).

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Finance uploaded remittance file CSV (remit_ref: GW-0310-USD-EUR) via AP portal at 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC.
2) Payments-service consumed the remit file and started FX conversion task using fx-profile 'standard-usd-eur'.
3) Conversion completed but ledger mapping failed: fx-profile label did not match GL mapping key (expected 'USD_EUR_STD' vs received 'standard-usd-eur').
4) The allocation step defaulted to 'suspense' when mapping lookup returned null. Posting created GL transaction to 4000-SUSP and flagged payment as 'cleared-suspense'.
5) Scheduler recognized cleared-suspense and withheld ACH batch until manual review.

Expected behavior:
- FX conversion should map to the configured GL account 2100-AP (or vendor-specific clearing account) and allow normal payout processing.

Actual behavior:
- Posting to suspense account blocked the scheduled payout; finance must manually move the GL entry or re-post with correct mapping.

Logs/attachments:
- Payment service logs (payments-2026-03-10.log) lines 1242-1270 show mapping lookup result: "mapping_key_not_found: standard-usd-eur".
- Bank connector trace id: bank-trace-9a7c3f.
- Uploaded remittance file: attachments/GW-0310-remit.csv (secure).

Business notes:
- Vendor is on a net-30 cadence; missing this payout may trigger expedited freight fees.
- This vendor has multiple POs on the batch; allocation mismatch could cause multi-PO unapplied balances.

Temporary workaround:
- Manual GL reclassification from 4000-SUSP -> 2100-AP for the single transaction allows the scheduler to release the payout. Finance-run manual journal recommended as interim.

Urgent ask:
- Engineering to validate why fx-profile labels are not normalizing to expected mapping keys and provide a hotfix or safe mapping override so the upcoming scheduled batch (2026-03-13 02:00 UTC) will not be blocked for other vendors.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:10 — SRE (Slack #payments): Linked bank-trace-9a7c3f to trace in observability. No downstream network errors; mapping null returned upstream from ledger service.
2026-03-10 14:00 — Initial triage: Payment ingestion and FX conversion succeeded; ledger mapping returned null due to mismatch between fx-profile label and GL mapping key.
2026-03-10 16:10 — Hypothesis 1: Recent rename of fx-profile in config (human-friendly slug changed) without corresponding GL mapping update.
2026-03-11 08:45 — Hypothesis 2: ledger-mapping service does a strict string match; it does not consult profile aliases.
Ledger mapping is implemented as a strict key lookup against fx-profile labels. A recent change to an fx-profile display slug ('USD_EUR_STD' -> 'standard-usd-eur') was not synchronized to GL mapping configuration, causing allocations to fall back to suspense account.
2026-03-12 07:30 — Prod config change: Added mapping alias 'standard-usd-eur' -> 'USD_EUR_STD' in ledger-mapping service config via deploy PR #finance/ledger-mapping-fix. (see related_github_prs below)
2026-03-12 08:00 — Finance completed manual reclass for Greenwave transaction; scheduler allowed payout release and bank connector shows ACH submitted at 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC.
Status: Partial fix — mapping alias prevents new occurrences, but root hygiene requires a stronger mitigation to avoid future slug/name drift.
Create a governance task to ensure fx-profile renames require a mapped alias or automated mapping sync (owner: Finance/Payments).
Enhance ledger-mapping service to accept canonical IDs in addition to human slugs to avoid string-drift failures (owner: Payments infra).
Add alert when posting to 'suspense' exceeds threshold (e.g., > $10k in a day) — integrate with PagerDuty.
Run reconciliation sweep for last 30 days to detect similar mapping mismatches and reclass any outstanding suspense postings.
payload.summary: Cross-currency remittance posted to suspense GL, blocking next scheduled payout to supplier

payload.description:
Users in the SF hotdesk area reported repeated WireGuard disconnects and inability to reach internal services. Affected clients retained an IP for a short period, then the local address changed and WireGuard reported peer unreachable. Multiple devices across adjacent ports were impacted. Initial triage suggested a VPN/client issue but symptoms pointed to layer 2 instability on the access switch feeding the hotdesk bridge VLAN.
Multiple engineers at the SF hotdesk (approx 12 seats) experienced frequent VPN drops and intermittent internal service access over an 8-hour window. Productivity impacted for hotdesk users; no org-wide impact. Automated synthetic checks for the hotdesk subrange showed elevated ARP/cache churn.
1) Connect a laptop to any port in the hotdesk bay (ports 41-52 on switch sw-sf-hotdesk-01)
2) Join corporate Wi-Fi (corp-net), ensure split-tunnel WireGuard config is active and route default via local ISP not over VPN
3) Start a WireGuard session to the Redwood internal Gateway (wg01), leave idle for ~2-5 minutes
4) Attempt to access an internal service (git, jira) or tail logs over SSH; observe dropped sessions and new local IP allocation or ARP timeout messages
5) On the switch, run 'show mac address-table' and 'show arp' to observe MAC flapping or duplicate entries tied to the hotdesk VLAN
Client WireGuard log (macOS): 'peer wg01 unreachable, handshake timeout', followed by 'replaced local address 10.10.55.24 -> 10.10.55.234'
DHCP server logs: lease for 10.10.55.24 assigned, then released 45s later with client MAC still present on switch but different port
Switch syslog (sw-sf-hotdesk-01): 'Port 46 security violation: MAC address limit exceeded', 'STP topology change on VLAN 210 detected on Gi1/0/46'
Network edge logs: 'ARP storm detected for subnet 10.10.55.0/24, suppressed 120s'
03/08 09:25 - CS observed repeated WireGuard drop reports from 3 users. Triage: confirm scope and reproduce.
03/08 10:00 - SRE captured switch syslog showing 'security violation' events on several hotdesk ports. Not all affected ports raised alarms simultaneously.
03/08 11:15 - Reproduced locally. 'show mac address-table dynamic' showed the same MAC moving between Gi1/0/45 and Gi1/0/46, then cleared by port-security.
03/08 12:00 - Hypothesis: port-security with sticky MAC or low max-mac setting plus edge mis-wired patch caused MAC flapping; STP topology changes triggered transient blackholing and DHCP rebinds leading to WireGuard re-handshakes.
03/08 13:30 - Verified patch panel: ports 46/47 were connected to a temporary unmanaged patch leading to duplicate L2 path during desk reconfiguration (hotdesk moves).
03/09 09:20 - Confirmed DHCP snooping and port-security interaction: when port-security triggered a violation, the switch shut the port for a short time (err-disabled) and the DHCP lease was released, causing clients to get a new IP on reconnection and WireGuard to rebind.
03/09 10:00 - Scoped: only ports in hotdesk bay VLAN 210; other office areas not impacted. No software bug in WireGuard detected.
03/10 15:45 - Mitigation applied: disabled port-security enforcement on the victim ports and removed the rogue patch cable. Monitored for 48 hours; ARP churn subsided.
03/11 09:00 - Permanent fix scheduled: update switch template to increase max-mac for hotdesk ports to 8, enable BPDU Guard, and add patch panel labeling to avoid future ad-hoc cross-connects.
Reference artifacts: Slack #infra-sf thread (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/INFRA-SF/p03Jq1x), Confluence runbook 'sw-hotdesk-port-template' (https://confluence.redwood/infra/switching/hotdesk)
Related config change PR: github.com/redwood-infra/switch-configs/pulls/87
Mitigation: removed rogue patch cable and temporarily relaxed port-security on hotdesk access ports to prevent err-disabled state. Permanent remediation: template change applied to sw-sf-hotdesk-01 and sibling switches - increased max-mac to 8, BPDU Guard enabled, DHCP snooping binding table validation added, and updated patch panel labeling/process. Communicated change to Facilities. Change PR: github.com/redwood-infra/switch-configs/pulls/87. No firmware upgrade required.
Nisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-08: 'Multiple folks in hotdesk reported WireGuard disconnects this morning. Started a ticket. Will attach screenshots of client logs.'
Ravi Kapoor (Assignee) 2026-03-08: 'Acknowledged. Triage in progress. Asking SRE on-call to collect switch syslogs and DHCP logs for the 10.10.55.0/24 subnet.'
SRE OnCall (Marta Li) 2026-03-08: 'Seeing port-security violation entries on sw-sf-hotdesk-01. Noting some MAC flapping between Gi1/0/45-47. Pulling depth counters.'
Networking (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-09: 'Found an unmanaged patch cable connecting two ports on the panel causing two forwarding paths. Temporary mitigations applied (partial shutdown of duplicate port).'
Ravi Kapoor 2026-03-10: 'Applied mitigation: moved affected desks to spare ports, disabled strict port-security on hotdesk ports, removed rogue cable. Monitoring.'
Nisha Patel 2026-03-11: 'Monitoring looks stable. No new WireGuard complaints from hotdesk users. Closing as resolved unless reoccurs.'
