Issue summary:
GCP-based CI (ml-ci) jobs that provision ephemeral AWS instances via workload identity federation began failing to assume the target AWS role. This prevents model replay jobs and nightly validation runs from starting.

Impact:
- CI pipelines for model replay and integration tests failing (~60% of ml-ci runs in us-east).
- Delayed validation and onboarding of new model builds; potential downstream deployment slowdowns.

Environment:
- GCP project: redwood-ml-ci-staging / redwood-ml-ci-prod
- AWS account: rw-infer-prod (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-ephemeral-provisioner)
- Federation mechanism: GCP Workload Identity -> AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity via OIDC token

Observed behavior:
- GCP jobs obtain an identity token successfully but AWS STS returns AccessDenied when calling AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. Error seen in logs: "Error: AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity" and "The principal is not authorized to assume the role".

Expected behavior:
- ml-ci pod/service account should exchange GCP identity token for temporary AWS credentials and assume role ci-ephemeral-provisioner to create ephemeral EC2/EKS resources.

Temporary mitigation:
- Manual run by infra on a dedicated bastion with long-lived credentials; limited capacity and not scalable.

Notes:
- This ticket covers investigation and permanent fix to restore the federated path and update any IAM conditions or identity configuration that caused the break.
1) In a test GKE pod with workload identity bound to service account ml-ci-sa, run:
   gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=sts.amazonaws.com
2) Attempt AWS exchange:
   aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-ephemeral-provisioner --role-session-name test-session --web-identity-token <token> --duration-seconds 3600
3) Observe STS error: AccessDenied / principal not authorized

Notes: reproduces in both staging and prod project service accounts when using the current audience/issuer values.
[2026-03-10T09:12:04Z] ml-ci-runner: obtaining identity token for sa:ml-ci-sa
[2026-03-10T09:12:05Z] aws-sts: assume-role-with-web-identity failed: AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity	status code: 403
[2026-03-10T09:12:05Z] aws-sts: request id: b1f4c2d3-example
Additional context: Token audience was 'sts.amazonaws.com' and issuer 'https://iam.gserviceaccount.com/..'

Timeline:
- 2026-03-10 09:30: Initial customer-reported failures in ml-ci backlog; alerted via #internal-support.
- 2026-03-10 10:00: Verified STS AccessDenied from a reproducer; confirmed tokens being minted.
- 2026-03-10 13:00: Cross-checked role trust policy (AWS) and GCP Workload Identity pool config; noticed an IAM Condition referencing 'aud' claim equality that had been tightened during a recent audit (INT-120999).
Hypotheses tested:
- Hypothesis A: Audience mismatch due to new audience format -> reproduced when using older audience string; AWS rejects because condition enforces exact match.
- Hypothesis B: Role trust condition now restricts source account or principal tag which ml-ci doesn't provide -> tested by adding permissive condition to a test role; assume succeeded.
Findings:
- Root cause: A recent housekeeping change to the AWS role trust policy added a StringEquals condition on "sts:Audience" and/or a tag condition on "aws:PrincipalTag/ci-runner"; GCP identity tokens emitted by ml-ci do not include that specific tag and the audience string uses a new issuer URL.
- Related change: a Terraform change in infra repo (PR #7421) updated the workload-identity provider audience formatting to include the full issuer; inadvertently changed token 'aud' value.
Next steps:
- Reconcile audience values between GCP Workload Identity config and the role trust policy.
- Decide whether to relax the StringEquals to StringLike or to update GCP token audience formatting back to expected value.
- Patch Terraform and roll out to staging first, verify ml-ci runs, then prod.

Additional notes:
WIP: Temporary fix tested in staging by relaxing the AWS role trust condition to accept the current audience format. Permanent fix to be implemented by aligning GCP workload identity audience formatting with the AWS trust policy in terraform (PR ready: infra PR 7445). After code review we'll roll to prod during low-traffic window and monitor ml-ci runs for 24h. Follow-up action: add automated integration test that exercises assume-role-with-web-identity on PRs that touch workload-identity/iam modules.
payload.summary: Restore GCP->AWS federated assume-role path for ml-ci ephemeral provisioning

Issue summary:
AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity sessions created by the GCP->AWS token-exchange path for 'prod-fence' debugging are being denied when evaluated against tag-based IAM Conditions. We traced the denial to truncated role-session-names which lead to missing/incorrect session tags used by org-level IAM Condition statements.

Impact:
- SRE/debug sessions in prod-fence cannot access SecretsManager/ParameterStore keys they previously had via JIT short-lived roles.
- Several on-call debugging attempts were blocked (3 reported) for customer-impacting tenant investigations yesterday.
- Workflows that rely on session-tag gating for audit and least-privilege enforcement are failing, causing potential operational slowdowns.

Environment:
- Private deployment: prod-fence (customer-isolated VPC)
- AWS account: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-jit-bridge
- GCP identity provider: workload-identity pool redwood/ci-pool
- Region: us-west-2

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create OIDC token from GCP workload identity federation with long principal subject/session name (our CI token exchange generates names like 'svc-debugger-prod-fence-2026-03-10-xxxxxxxx').
2) Call AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity to assume redwood-jit-bridge with the token and request session tags via TagSpecification.
3) Attempt to access a secretsmanager:GetSecretValue guarded by an IAM Condition: StringEquals: aws:PrincipalTag/env = "prod-fence".

Observed behavior:
- STS returns a successful AssumeRole response but CloudTrail shows roleSessionName truncated to ~64 chars (roleSessionName truncation appears to be performed by an intermediate token-processing step).
- aws:PrincipalTag/env is either absent or contains a truncated value (e.g., "prod-fence-deb") which fails the Condition and results in AccessDenied.

Expected behavior:
- Tags requested during AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity are present and match the full expected value. Tag-based IAM Conditions should evaluate to true when session tags are correct.

Initial hypothesis:
- RoleSessionName length limit in our token exchange path or in a dependent library is truncating the session name. Because our provisioning logic derives session tags from session-name (we append env info to session name), that truncation propagates into tags and fails tag-based conditions.
- GCP->AWS token exchange code path (redwood-ci/token-exchange) does not explicitly set TagSpecifications in the final AssumeRole request in some cases, relying on roleSessionName-derived tags which get truncated.

Logs / evidence (excerpts):
- CloudTrail eventId: 2b9f7d44-0a6b-4c2b-8e3d-EXAMPLE showing AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity; roleSessionName: "svc-debugger-prod-fence-2026-03-10-abcdef1234567890..." truncated to "svc-debugger-prod-fence-2026-03-10-abcdef1"
- CloudWatch auth logs: AccessDenied for secretsmanager:GetSecretValue, condition failure: StringEquals aws:PrincipalTag/env != "prod-fence"
- Token-exchange service logs: request.session_name length=96, no explicit tagSpecification found in 12% of exchanges.

Workaround applied:
- Temporary fix: Updated the token-exchange consumer in the ops playbook to generate a shorter session_name (trim to 32 chars) and to explicitly pass TagSpecifications in AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity for required tags. Deployed to staging and then to a narrow prod canary for the debug service.

Next steps (planned):
- Patch redwood-ci/token-exchange to always set TagSpecifications explicitly and not depend on session-name parsing. (owner: infra-token-team)
- Add validation & tests for session_name length and tag propagation in our e2e token-exchange tests. (owner: infra-ci)
- Review org SCP/IAM Conditions that rely on derived tags and consider a migration to explicit claims-based conditions or tag policy that doesn't depend on session-name parsing. (owner: security)
- Roll out patch and monitor CloudTrail for tag propagation success rate >= 99.9% for JIT sessions.

Create a long session name token from GCP workload identity federation (example generator in redwood-ci).
Call STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity without explicit TagSpecifications (simulates current failing code path).
Attempt to call protected AWS APIs gated by aws:PrincipalTag conditions and observe AccessDenied in CloudTrail/CloudWatch.
CloudTrail(eventId=2b9f7d44): AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity roleSessionName="svc-debugger-prod-fence-2026-03-10-abcdef1234567890..." -> truncated to "svc-debugger-prod-fence-2026-03-10-abcdef1"
CloudWatch(auth): AccessDenied: secretsmanager:GetSecretValue - Condition failed: StringEquals aws:PrincipalTag/env != "prod-fence"
token-exchange-service: request.session_name length=96; tag_spec provided=false
Reproduced locally by invoking our token-exchange mock with a 96-char session name; confirmed AWS truncation behavior in the returned STS roleSessionName field.
Confirmed that IAM Conditions rely on aws:PrincipalTag/env which in our infra is derived from session-name in older token-exchange implementations.
Found 3 user-reported incidents in the last 24h where engineers hit AccessDenied for JIT debug access in prod-fence; all share long session-name pattern.
(in progress) Short-term workaround deployed: token-exchange trimmed session names and explicitly sends TagSpecifications. Long-term fix: force explicit TagSpecifications in token-exchange codepath and add e2e tests. Security to review tag-based gating.
payload.summary: AssumeRole session tags truncated by role-session-name length limit causing JIT permission mismatch for prod-fence debugging

Issue summary: Multiple engineers on macOS M2 devices using CalDigit TS4 docks report losing access to internal services after their laptops wake from sleep. The zero-trust (WireGuard-based) tunnel shows established, but traffic to internal IPs is routed out the dock/AP link instead of the tunnel. This appears consistently after authenticating to our guest/corporate captive-portal SSID when the dock is connected. Impact: Productivity impact for ~6 engineers across SF office; internal services (git, internal API, vault) unreachable until manual fix or reconnect. Environment: macOS Ventura 13.5 on M2 MacBooks, CalDigit TS4 / Thunderbolt docks, corporate Wi-Fi (802.11ax) with captive portal that performs HTTP redirect authentication, zero-trust agent v1.8.2 and WireGuard kernel tunnel (utun). Observed symptoms: - System shows global IPv6 prefix from AP via SLAAC and a link-local address on dock interface. - Default IPv6 route gets assigned to dock interface with lower metric than utun, client resolves internal hostnames but packets leak to AP, causing connection failures. - Re-establishing zero-trust agent or toggling Wi-Fi fixes temporarily; unplugging dock also fixes. - Repro after sleep/resume is deterministic when dock + captive portal flow are present.
1) Connect MacBook (Ventura 13.5) to CalDigit TS4 dock into office USB-C port.
2) Join corporate Wi-Fi which redirects to captive portal and complete authentication.
3) Confirm zero-trust agent establishes WireGuard tunnel (utun interface visible).
4) Put MacBook to sleep and wake after ~30s.
5) Attempt to reach internal service (e.g., curl https://internal-api.redwood.local).
6) Observe connection hangs or DNS resolving to internal but TCP/UDP flows fail (packets egress via dock/IPv6 path).
Mar 10 09:12:05 macbook-pro kernel: utun1: Flags 0x2<UP> mtu 1472
Mar 10 09:12:06 macbook-pro system: WireGuard: peer xxxxx handshake complete
Mar 10 09:12:22 macbook-pro networkd: en7: IPv6 Router Advertisement, prefix 2607:f8b0:4012::/64
Mar 10 09:12:23 macbook-pro networkd: route add ::/0 -interface en7 metric 5
Mar 10 09:12:24 macbook-pro system: zero-trust-agent: tunnel up on utun1 (peer=x.x.x.x)
Mar 10 09:12:49 macbook-pro network: attempt to connect to internal-api.redwood.local timed out (tried via en7)
Mar 10 09:13:02 macbook-pro console: user unplugged dock -> connectivity restored
Initial hypothesis: IPv6 default route from AP/dock is winning over utun route due to interface metric and macOS route selection on dual-stack, causing asymmetric routing and stateful firewall drops inside corporate network.
Confirmed reproduction on two different MacBook M2 machines and one Intel Mac; appears OS-agnostic but more frequent on Ventura 13.x on M-series.
Zero-trust agent currently does not set explicit route metric on macOS for utun interface when tunnel is brought up after network interface changes (sleep/wake + captive portal flow).
Captive portal changes base interface properties (RA + new prefix) after tunnel establishment; timing causes the kernel to prefer the newly advertised prefix/interface.
Checked server-side: no change in peer keys or session — traffic is arriving at edge but source IPs show external interface, so responses are dropped by internal firewall rules expecting tunnel-sourced addresses.
Packet captures show TCP SYNs leaving via en7 and not being NATed through the tunnel gateway; returning packets never reach utun.
Related tickets: INT-302999 (similar post-sleep multihoming behavior) — differs because that one was primarily DHCP/MTU related, while this is IPv6 RA metric ordering + captive portal timing.
Ava Martinez (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Logged after two engineers in SF reported inability to reach internal git and vault after waking laptops. Workaround was unplug/replug dock.
Jamal Singh (Assignee) - 2026-03-10: Reproduced in lab with TS4 and Ventura VM. Captive portal RA arrives ~1-2s after utun up; kernel prefers en7 route. Collecting netstat/route and tcpdump.
SRE Team (#infra-help) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed that internal firewall blocks non-tunnel source IPs. Suggested forcing higher metric on physical interfaces or programmatically re-asserting tunnel route on sleep/resume.
Security - 2026-03-11: Need to avoid creating a fallback that leaks internal traffic to external networks. Any fix must preserve no-split-tunnel policy.
Jamal Singh - 2026-03-12: Drafted short-term agent patch to run a route preference adjustment on macOS when utun comes up. Testing patch v1.8.3-pre1 internally.
Workaround deployed: zero-trust-agent v1.8.3-pre1 (canary) now forces a higher-priority route for the utun interface on macOS immediately after tunnel establishment and re-applies after sleep/resume. For affected users we pushed the canary to the SF office and instructed to report if issue persists. Long-term: engineering will add deterministic route metric management and explicit IPv6 route rules in upcoming v1.9.0; also evaluating changing captive portal RA behavior with networking team to avoid late RA after auth. Follow-up: create a user script to run on login/sleep hooks for older devices and add test case to our CI that simulates RA arrival after tunnel establishment.
payload.summary: Post-captive portal: dock interface + IPv6 RA causes WireGuard tunnel route takeover after sleep/resume

Issue summary: Several employee expense claims uploaded on 2026-03-01 showed valid attachments in the UI but failed to map to expense lines during payrun generation. The payrun PR-2026-03-04-42 was blocked with 'attachment_type_unknown' errors and several claims were left in 'pending' state. Impact: Upcoming supplier reimbursements and corporate-card reimbursements for the March 4th payrun are delayed (~€37k total). Internal audit checklist demands attachments for reimbursements which increases manual workload until resolved.

Observed behavior: Attachments for ~12 claims are present in the employee profile but backend ingestion records show truncated filenames where the file extension was removed (e.g. 'receipt_12345' instead of 'receipt_12345.pdf'), causing the file-type sniffing routine to return 'unknown' and skip OCR/line extraction. This leaves the expense matcher unable to reconcile transaction lines, so claims are excluded from automated payrun inclusion.

Business impact: High — payrun blocked and finance must triage claims manually to avoid missing supplier deadlines.

Requested outcome: Identify root cause, apply temporary remediation to unblock the payrun (re-ingest or re-queue affected attachments), and implement a durable fix in the file-upload service to preserve extensions and validate content-type on ingest.
1) Employee uploads expense attachment via Expenses web UI (tested with Chrome 112 and Safari on macOS).
2) Attachment appears in UI with preview enabled.
3) Run internal ingestion job 'attachments-processor' or wait for scheduled ingestion window.
4) Verify DB record for attachment shows filename without extension and file_type = null.
5) Trigger payrun generation job; claim is skipped with 'attachment_type_unknown' and payrun enters 'blocked' state.
Uploaded attachment retains filename and extension or has valid content-type recorded in the attachment metadata. Ingestion should process PDF/JPEG/PNG and OCR should extract lines so expense matcher can reconcile claims into payrun.
Attachment metadata recorded with truncated filename (no extension) and file_type null. attachments-processor logs 'unable to determine mime type' and claim remains excluded from automated processing.
2026-03-01 09:12:07 attachments-processor: INFO processing attachment id=att-9f8e size=142014
2026-03-01 09:12:07 attachments-processor: WARN filename truncated detected: original='receipt_ÄÖ-12345.pdf' stored='receipt_ÄÖ-12345'
2026-03-01 09:12:07 attachments-processor: ERROR mime sniff returned empty for id=att-9f8e; skipping ocr
Hypothesis: UTF-8 characters in filename plus our legacy S3 key normalization is dropping trailing '.pdf' when names include non-ascii characters. Edge-case occurs when upload path length + normalized name crosses 120 bytes triggering substring operation that drops suffix.
Checked S3 object keys for affected files: keys exist and objects intact; object metadata 'Content-Type' is set to 'application/pdf' for some, but ingestion relies on database-stored filename for quick type decision — mismatch surfaced when filename lost extension.
Reproduced locally by uploading filename with surrogate characters via web UI and observing filename normalization routine in file-upload-service: url-encode -> utf8-normalize -> truncate(120) -> write. truncate(120) currently operates on bytes, not chars, causing suffix cut-off.
Temporary remediation applied: modified ingestion worker to fall back to S3 object's Content-Type header when filename does not contain extension. Re-queued affected attachments for processing (queue id: q-attachments-20260304-7).
Risk: Fallback increases processing latency but reduces manual interventions; permanent fix should be in upload service to avoid per-claim fallbacks.

[file-upload-service] 2026-03-01T08:59:44Z info saved key='uploads/2026/03/01/receipt_%C3%84%C3%96-12345' size=142014 content-type='application/pdf'
[payrun-generator] 2026-03-04T03:10:12Z warn claim c-78123 skipped reason='attachment_type_unknown' payrun=PR-2026-03-04-42
Ava Kim (reporter) 2026-03-01: Filed after finance noticed 10+ claims missing OCR output during payrun prep. Attached sample affected claim IDs and screenshots in internal thread #finance-helpdesk.
Liam Patel (assignee) 2026-03-01: Acknowledge — triaging with SRE and platform eng. Will try re-queueing ingestion and test uploader truncation edge-cases.
SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-02: Confirmed truncation occurs when UTF-8 encoded filename bytes > 120. Created a sandbox test to repro. Recommended quick fix: attachments-processor should consult S3 Content-Type before skipping OCR.
Platform Eng (Meera Singh) 2026-03-03: Patch prepared to perform truncate by characters not bytes and to ensure suffix preservation. Raised PR #4882. Will coordinate Canary deploy to us-east then eu-west.
Finance Ops (Olivia Chen) 2026-03-04: Thanks — please prioritize fallback. We have payment windows on 2026-03-06. Manual processing for affected claims will add ~3 hours of workload if not automated.
1) Re-queued affected attachments to attachments-processor with s3-metadata-fallback enabled (queue q-attachments-20260304-7). 2) Finance ops will accept payments for claims where OCR still fails via manual verification (guidance doc shared).
Merge PR #4882 and deploy to file-upload-service with char-safe truncation and extension preservation.
Add automated test for non-ASCII filenames crossing the byte-length threshold.
Add monitoring alert: Ratio of attachments with null file_type > 0.5% for 15m should page Platform team.
Postmortem to document root cause and update expense ingestion runbook.

Issue summary: During an org-wide deprovisioning job (safety cleanup for inactive contractors) we observed a race between Okta session revocation and our token re-issuance path. This caused a subset of ephemeral CLI tokens and long-running service-runner sessions to be rejected, preventing internal tooling authentication for affected users and automated jobs.

Impact: ~120 developer CLI sessions errored with 401/403 in us-east and eu-west; several nightly model-eval runners failed to start. No customer-facing inference endpoints were affected.

Business impact: internal dev velocity degraded, delayed nightly evaluations and blocked a small on-call escalation workflow.

1) Ensure user has an active long-lived CLI session (issued >12h ago) and a service-runner job with token refresh configured.
2) Trigger the scheduled Okta deprovisioning job that revokes sessions for users marked inactive in LDAP (internal cron: identity-sync/deprovision/weekly).
3) Immediately attempt an API call with the existing CLI token or perform token refresh for the service-runner.
4) Observe auth failures (401 / 403) even though user shows as active in our local cache for a short window prior to sync completion.
Tokens that were issued prior to Okta deprovisioning are intermittently rejected during the deprovisioning window. Identity-proxy logs show a short window where our cache still returns the old user state but Okta responds 'revoked' to introspection calls, leading to a race and final rejection. Some retries succeed after ~30s when caches reconcile.
Either a graceful transitional state where existing sessions remain valid until rotated OR near-immediate propagation with consistent revocation across our token introspection and session caches so clients receive deterministic responses.
2026-03-10T02:04:12Z identity-proxy[auth-introspect] INFO token_introspect user=svc-runner-27 token_id=abc123 status=active
2026-03-10T02:04:13Z okta-sync INFO deprovision: start batch=contractors-20260310 count=187
2026-03-10T02:04:13Z okta API DEBUG introspect token=abc123 response=status=revoked code=401
2026-03-10T02:04:13Z identity-proxy WARN reconcile mismatch token=abc123 cache_state=active okta_state=revoked
2026-03-10T02:04:13Z cli-client ERROR api_request user=bob@example.com error=401 Unauthorized
2026-03-10T02:04:45Z identity-proxy INFO cache-refresh token=abc123 reconciled_state=revoked
Initial triage (Aisha): correlated spike of 401s with scheduled deprovision job at 02:04 UTC.
Hypothesis: identity-sync performs bulk Okta revoke then emits user status events; our identity-proxy uses a short-lived in-memory cache that can respond before the event stream processes the deprovision message, creating a TOCTOU (time-of-check time-of-use) window.
Observed that token introspection calls to Okta return 'revoked' while our local cache still marks session active for ~20-40s.
Reproducible locally by running deprovision job against staging Okta and issuing concurrent token introspection + cache read.
Applied an emergency server-side check: identity-proxy now performs an Okta-introspect call when cache indicates active but the token age is >6h OR when a bulk deprovision event is in progress. This reduces false-positives for invalid active-state responses. Deployed hotfix to prod at 2026-03-11T18:10Z.
Ongoing. Hotfix reduces rate of failures by ~95% in short term. A durable fix (see follow-up tasks) will change event ordering and add a coordinated revocation phase to avoid races. Change to be implemented in identity-sync and identity-proxy coordination layer.
1) Implement coordinated revocation handshake in identity-sync so Okta revokes are gated until identity-proxy acknowledges event sequencing. Owner: Miguel. ETA: 2026-03-19
2) Add canary/deferred-revocation mode to weekly deprovision job to reduce blast radius. Owner: SRE team. ETA: 2026-03-24
3) Improve observability: add metric for 'introspect_mismatch' with labels (region, job_id). Owner: Observability. ETA: 2026-03-14
4) Postmortem and runbook update: document fallback policy and emergency mitigation steps. Owner: Support. ETA: 2026-03-16
2026-03-10T03:00:12Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Noticed 401 spike after scheduled deprov job. Correlated with identity-sync logs. Opening ticket and assigning to Miguel.
2026-03-10T05:22:40Z - Miguel Ortega (SRE): Reproduced in staging. Confirmed TOCTOU race between Okta introspect and local cache. Will assemble quick mitigation.
2026-03-11T18:15:03Z - Miguel Ortega (SRE): Hotfix deployed to identity-proxy to perform introspect for tokens older than 6h or when deprov job in progress. Monitoring impact.
2026-03-11T19:05:27Z - Sophie Lange (Platform Eng): Observability shows 95% reduction in 401s tied to this window. Still seeing rare residuals in eu-west; investigating backlog processing timing.
2026-03-12T09:32:11Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Affected users advised to 'rehydrate' sessions by re-authenticating if they see 401. Support playbook updated with temporary workaround.
2026-03-12T11:00:00Z - Miguel Ortega (SRE): Created PR for coordinated revocation handshake: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-sync/pull/482. Planning review and rollout in two-phase canary.

Issue summary: A recent vendor consolidation (merging two vendor records: VEND-7432 EMEA and VEND-19821 APAC) as part of the global vendor tidy-up has resulted in inconsistent tax jurisdiction codes stored across ledgers. Impact: Multiple vendor invoices for the consolidated entity are stuck in 'Pending Finalization' and failing payrun validation due to conflicting tax jurisdiction (VAT vs GST) and mismatched tax rates. This is blocking three scheduled payment batches (weekend payrun), affecting vendor settlements and month-end reconciliations. Environment: Production, EU and US ledgers. Issue summary: Deployments to Dedicated cluster in prod are blocked because the infra provisioning pipeline cannot obtain cross-account credentials for the GPU fleet. Impact: New dedicated node pools could not be created; rolling deploys were delayed ~3 hours for a single customer onboarding. Environment: prod (aws us-east-1) using GCP CI runner (us-west1) that federates to AWS via workload-identity and STS assume-role chain.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger infra provisioning pipeline from GCP CI (service account A).
2) Pipeline exchanges workload-identity token for AWS STS credentials via our identity-broker (assume-role-with-web-identity).
3) Broker then calls AssumeRole to target account role with session tags.
4) Observe failure in the broker logs and pipeline stops.

Observed behavior:
- Broker logs show repeated failures: "AccessDenied: SessionTags cannot be larger than allowed size" and "AssumeRole chain rejected: Tag truncated -> role condition failed".
- The infra task fails with exit code 2 and error: "Failed to assume target-role: AccessDenied".
- Affected runs show 100% failure for jobs that request more than 2 session tags.

Expected behavior:
- Broker should successfully exchange identity token and assume target account role, propagating necessary session tags (team, ci-run-id, env) so audit/AWS condition checks succeed.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- broker stderr: "ERROR: sts:TagLengthExceeded: session tag payload length exceeded 2048 bytes"
- pipeline output: "aws:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed: InvalidIdentityToken" (followed by tag-related message in broker)
Hypothesis 1: Broker concatenates tags into one serialized payload that exceeds AWS session tag size limit -> confirmed by reproducer.
Hypothesis 2: Recent change in infra agent started including full commit message and long branch names -> traced to infra agent v2.4.1 (commit 8f3a12) which appended full run context into 'ci_metadata' tag.
Findings: AWS enforces combined tag payload limits and also truncates tags in the assume-role chain; our role condition required exact tag equality which failed after truncation. Affected flow: GCP OIDC -> identity-broker -> AssumeRole -> AssumeRole (target account).
Related risk: If tag truncation occurs silently, role-based conditions may deny sessions leading to intermittent access failures for automation.
Hotfix deployed to identity-broker: stop serializing run_context as a single tag; instead send compact tags (team, ci_run_id, environment) and strip long fields. Release: identity-broker v1.7.2.
Terraform change: add validations to pipeline that reject job metadata containing fields longer than 256 chars before kicking the broker. PR: infra/pull/4987 merged and deployed to staging/prod.
IAM change: relaxed exact-string conditions on target role trust policy to allow prefix matching for ci_run_id and added CloudWatch alarm for STS:TagLengthExceeded errors. PR: iam/pull/212.
Post-action verification: three consecutive provisioning runs in prod succeeded; monitoring shows no further STS tag errors.
payload.summary: Cross-cloud role assumption failing due to session-tag truncation on assume-role chain

payload.description:
Issue summary: During an automated credential rotation (Vault AppRole + CSI driver) the projected serviceaccount token file used by ephemeral GitHub Actions runners became shadowed by a stale inode. Impact: runners intermittently fail uploads to internal artifact gateway with 401/403 during job teardown, causing archived artifacts to be missing and release pipelines to fail. Scope: ~12% of ephemeral runner pod restarts in us-east-1 across the last rotation window (2026-03-09 03:00 - 04:30 UTC).

Observed behavior: After the CSI driver rewrote secrets, the runner-agent continued running but artifact uploads to s3-gateway returned 401/unauthorized. Restarting the runner pod consistently restored uploads. No image-pull errors were observed.

Expected behavior: Rotation should atomically replace credentials such that long-lived processes either see the new token or failover gracefully; runner agents should not retain a stale token reference after a secret re-mount.

1) Deploy a ephemeral GH Actions runner pod with projected serviceAccountToken (k8s projected volume) and an image that uploads artifacts to internal s3-gateway.
2) Trigger Vault secret rotation for the AppRole bound to the CSI driver and let the driver re-mount the updated secret to the runner pod's projected volume.
3) Initiate a job that uploads artifacts at pod shutdown (typical release pipeline step).
4) Observe that upload returns 401/403 while runner process still runs; pod restart restores upload ability.
runner-agent[2345]: INFO initiating artifact upload to s3-gateway: /artifacts/build-1234.tar.gz
runner-agent[2345]: ERROR upload failed: http status 401 Unauthorized (x-request-id: rwd-9f3b)
s3-gateway[proxy][pid=1142]: WARN auth: token validation failed: token issuer mismatch or signature invalid
kubelet[572]: INFO volumeMount: CSI driver finished write, performing remount /var/run/secrets/csi-vault/runner-tokens
kernel: inotify: watch removed (wd=102) for /var/run/secrets/csi-vault/runner-tokens/token (inode changed)
runner-agent[2345]: INFO detected token file path /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token -> inode 14576 (pre-rotation)
runner-agent[2345]: INFO token refresh check: token file inode changed to 19802 but file descriptor still points to old inode
Initial hypothesis: Vault CSI driver wrote new token with non-atomic write -> file inode changed; kubelet projected token refresh left symlink to old FD used by runner process leading to auth failures.
Confirmed with kernel audit: inotify events show remove+create semantics rather than atomic rename, so long-lived FD kept referencing removed inode.
s3-gateway logs show token validation failed with 'iss' mismatch for tokens minted during rotation window; tokens themselves were valid when read from new file but the runner process continued to use an already-open FD pointing to deleted inode containing the old token value.
Repro on staging by forcing CSI driver to write via tempfile+rename vs direct write: using tempfile+rename (atomic) removes the inode churn and prevents stale-fd reads.

Additional notes:
In Progress — temporary mitigation is to restart affected runner pods which forces runner-agent to re-open token file descriptor. Engineering work: (1) patch runner-agent to watch token path inode and reload token on change; (2) patch vault-csi-driver usage to perform atomic replace (tempfile + rename) when writing projected secrets; (3) coordinate with kubelet upgrade/ops to reduce remount races. Planning a controlled small-window rotation once patches are live.
1) Backport small inode-watch token reload to runner-agent (hotfix). 2) Update Vault CSI driver to write secrets atomically (tempfile + rename). 3) Add pre-rotation draining of ephemeral-runner node pool or coordinate rotation with a short runner restart wave. 4) Add automated post-rotation verification job that validates artifact upload end-to-end.
Patch runner-agent and ship hotfix Canary (owner: Diego Alvarez)
Merge CSI driver atomic-write patch and deploy to staging (owner: Infra: Connor Li)
Schedule controlled rotation re-run and verification window (owner: Priya Sharma)
Create runbook entry for post-rotation artifact validation (owner: Aisha Mendes)
payload.summary: Kube projected serviceaccount token shadowed during vault-driven secret rotation; ephemeral runners lose auth to artifact gateway

Issue summary: Several engineers reported 403s when attempting to use the Delegated Developer Portal (devtools.redwood.com) after a scheduled SCIM attribute normalization run. Impact: ~12 users (engineering, platform) unable to perform impersonation or access feature-flag tooling; blocks oncall troubleshooting. Environment: production / us-west / private identity sync from Okta -> SCIM -> identity-proxy. Observed behavior: New and existing users receive 403 with 'identity_alias_not_found' when hitting /v1/impersonate. Expected behavior: Identity alias normalization should preserve existing alias mappings or provide deterministic alias remapping so delegated sessions work. Triage summary: Not a console bug; root cause appears to be attribute canonicalization change in SCIM pipeline that split the single 'ident' claim into two aliases for a subset of accounts, causing token->alias lookup failures in identity-proxy.
1) Create or identify user with legacy 'ident' claim (prior to normalization).
2) Trigger SCIM normalization job (manual or scheduled run).
3) Attempt to initiate an impersonation session via devtools portal UI, or curl POST /v1/impersonate with Authorization header from Okta session.
4) Observe 403 with error code 'identity_alias_not_found' in response body and identity-proxy logs showing 'resolved_aliases=0'.
identity-proxy (2026-03-12T09:12:04Z) TRACE id=trace-9a7: lookup_alias_for_token(token=xxx) -> not found; returning 403
scim-sync (2026-03-12T08:45:12Z) INFO job=normalization: user=eng.alex@redwood.com changed ident->[eng.alex, alex.eng]
okta-system-log link: https://okta.redwood.com/admin/logs?query=user%3Aeng.alex%40redwood.com%20eventType%3Auser.lifecycle.update
Support (Aisha): Customer reported via #internal-access Slack at 2026-03-12T09:20 saying 'can't impersonate, 403 identity_alias_not_found'. Added initial ticket and escalated to Platform SRE.
SRE (Priya): Confirmed 403s and reproduced locally using staging SCIM snapshot. Initial hypothesis: SCIM canonicalization created duplicate aliases and identity-proxy lookup index was not updated.

Additional notes:
SRE (Priya): Applied a hotfix mapping in identity-proxy to accept both alias forms (deployed canary to us-west). Verified immediate reduction in 403s. Pushed full rollout and informed support to validate.
Support (Aisha): Customer confirmation: 12 users reported success after 2026-03-13T14:00. Closing follow-up tasks to create runbook and add reconciliation job.
Product (Marcel): Requested postmortem items: add a feature flag around SCIM normalization and an automated smoke test for delegated-portal impersonation after sync runs.
Checked SCIM normalization commit history: scim-service@main introduced new tokenization for 'ident' on 2026-03-11 in PR #482.
Identity-proxy stores alias index keyed by 'primary_alias'. When normalization split the alias into two values we failed to migrate primary_alias for ~1.8% of users (all with legacy dots in username).
Reproduction: Used staging SCIM snapshot + live identity-proxy to repro 403; adding a secondary_alias mapping in-memory allowed lookup to succeed.
Metrics: error rate for /v1/impersonate spiked from 0.02% to 7.4% between 08:40-09:20 UTC on 2026-03-12 in us-west. Traces linked: trace-9a7, trace-1f3, trace-2b9.
Hypothesis validated by hotfix: adding reverse-mapping immediately reduced errors to baseline within 12 minutes in canary region.
Root cause: SCIM normalization change created a second alias variant for a subset of users without migrating the primary_alias index used by identity-proxy. identity-proxy treated the normalized alias as a new alias and did not resolve tokens issued before normalization.
Immediate workaround: Deployed an identity-proxy hotfix (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/482) to accept both alias formats and perform a best-effort reverse lookup for 72 hours.
Permanent fix: Rolled back the normalization rollout, authored targeted reconciliation job to unify aliases and update primary_alias for affected accounts, and reworked the scim normalization feature behind a feature flag to do staged migrations.
Rollout notes: Hotfix rolled canary -> full region on 2026-03-13 14:00 UTC. Reconciliation job ran 2026-03-13 16:30 and fixed 1,147 accounts. No further 403 spikes observed as of 2026-03-14.
Follow-ups: (a) Create runbook: 'scim-normalization-impersonation-check' (Confluence page created) (b) Add smoke test to deploy pipeline that performs an impersonation attempt post SCIM run (c) Add monitoring alert on impersonation/403 delta > 0.5% above baseline.
Status: Resolved and monitoring active. Ticket closed pending retrospective documentation.
Create feature-flagged rollout pattern for SCIM normalization (owner: Diego) - due 2026-03-21
Add impersonation smoke test to CI for identity-proxy and devtools backend (owner: Priya) - due 2026-03-18
Update incident runbook and Confluence page with reconciliation steps (owner: Aisha) - due 2026-03-17

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A subset of internal users attempting to sign in to the Redwood Console are stuck in an access-request loop: the console shows "Waiting for device approval" and the platform repeatedly creates new pending access-request records instead of updating the existing request. Approvers are not receiving stable notifications, and on-call pages are being generated for duplicate requests.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers across two squads reported inability to complete console login via SSO (device approval required).
- Flood of duplicate access-request tickets in the admin queue causing approver overload and delayed approvals.
- Temporary manual approvals required for critical oncall responders. No production compute or model serving impact observed.

Environment:
- Prod sign-in flow through Okta + Device Trust + internal SSO bridge (sso-bridge). Region: us-west. Affected users appear to be on iOS-managed devices and a few macOS devices with the latest MDM profile.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. User attempts console sign-in via Okta SSO from managed device.
2. Okta returns device-challenge required -> device-trust-service triggers an approval request to the approver queue.
3. The user approves on-device; device-trust service signals success, but sso-bridge polls the approval endpoint and receives intermittent 202 / empty payload due to a race with the approval indexer.
4. sso-bridge treats the response as "no approved record" and re-creates a new access-request entry (new request_id), producing duplicate pending items.
5. Approver webhooks and email notifications are rate-limited and deduplicated imperfectly, so notifications are inconsistent.

Observed logs (snippets):
- sso-bridge.log: "[2026-03-11T14:22:03Z] warn: approval-poll no-record for device-req token=abc123 polling=3"
- device-trust-service.log: "[2026-03-11T14:22:02Z] info: approval indexer wrote request_id=R-20260311-7"
- auth-proxy.log: "[2026-03-11T14:22:04Z] error: duplicate-access-request created new id R-20260311-8 for user=j.lee@example.com"

Hypothesis:
- A race condition between the approval indexer and the sso-bridge polling leads to a transient 202/no-body response that sso-bridge treats as "not approved" and creates a new request instead of waiting/backing off.
- Notification/dedup logic in admin-queue assumes stable request IDs and does not correlate repeated requests for the same user/device.

Immediate mitigation (already applied):
- Manual approval of critical oncall requests by SRE to restore login access.
- Temporarily increased visibility: added a dashboard query to show access-request creation rate and duplicate_count per user.

Proposed fixes / next steps:

Additional notes:
- Medium-term: Harden approval indexer to emit a pre-write lease or a transient marker so pollers can detect in-progress writes.
- Long-term: Improve admin notification deduplication by matching on user+device fingerprint and recent requests (rolling window).
Attachments / references:
- Slack thread: #support (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123456)
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OPS/Device+Trust+Runbook
2026-03-10 16:05 - Oncall (SRE): Temporarily approved affected users manually. Noted 4 duplicate pending items for same user in admin queue. Investigating logs now.
2026-03-11 11:30 - Eng (device-trust): Confirmed indexer writes can be delayed by up to 600ms under heavy load; we currently do not expose a 'write-in-progress' marker. Idea: emit a temp-token header to signal in-progress write.
payload.summary: Device-trust approval delay triggers repeated console access-request loop

Issue summary: After rolling BIOS 16.2.8 to a batch of Dell XPS developer laptops, devices consistently start with the fan-curve set to 'locked' state during provisioning. Thermal calibration step in our imaging workflow reports 'fan profile unmodifiable' and the node is marked failed.

Impact: Blocks provisioning of a subset (~18%) of new/returned XPS laptops in the prod-us-west staging fleet. Affected devices throttle under load because calibration cannot adjust fan curves; delays onboarding and increases repair queue.

Observed behavior: Fresh devices or devices returning from depot with BIOS 16.2.8 applied show the same behavior. Fan control still responds to ACPI calls (fans spin) but the firmware rejects profile writes from our calibration utility (exit code 5). Event logs show BIOS message: 'FAN_CURVE_LOCK: vendor lock enabled'. Older BIOS versions (<=16.1.4) do not show the lock.

Hypothesis: Dell OEM firmware introduced a new secure fan-curve lock flag in 16.2.8 that prevents vendor tools from writing calibration profiles unless an OEM signed token is present. Our calibration utility (support-scripts/fancal) uses standard WMI/ACPI calls that used to work. The firmware change may have been rolled out silently with 16.2.8.

Temporary impact mitigation: Manual workaround available at depot: use Dell Diagnostics > thermal override to apply a temporary profile. Not scalable for fleet onboarding.

Next steps requested: Eng (firmware/bios) to confirm whether flag is intentional and whether a signed token or vendor handshake is required. Provisioning team to adjust imaging workflow to detect locked fans and route to repair queue automatically. Hardware team to identify affected serial ranges sent to partners in last 30 days.
1) Start with a Dell XPS 15/17 with BIOS 16.2.8 installed (factory or updated)
2) Boot into provisioning image (PXE->WinPE->imaging task sequence) and run support-scripts/fancal --stage=calibrate
3) Observe fancal exit with code 5 and log entry: 'FAN_CURVE_LOCK: write access denied'
4) Check Windows Event Log: Application > FANCAL > Error 0x05; check BIOS serial log via vendor log collector for fan state
5) Reflash to 16.1.4 (rollback) and repeat; calibration succeeds and device completes provisioning.

Additional notes:
2026-03-09 10:02 - Reproduced in lab on 3/3 devices with 16.2.8; rollback to 16.1.4 fixes. Captured bios debug region via fwtool (attached to artifact bucket).
2026-03-10 14:33 - Eng hypothesis: OEM added a signed lock bit. Reached out to Dell partner rep; case #SR-992183 opened. Requested firmware release notes and whitelist process.
2026-03-11 11:47 - Provisioning team updated imaging pipeline to detect fancal exit code and tag device for manual handling. Reduced batch failure rate to 2% (edge cases where rollback not possible).
2026-03-12 16:20 - Hardware identified serial number pattern S/N prefix "DXP-00C" present in 60% of failures; forwarded to Dell SR to prioritize investigation.
1) Depot manual: Use Dell Diagnostics thermal override to set a temporary curve so imaging can complete.
2) Rolling back BIOS to 16.1.4 allows our calibration utility to succeed (applies to devices where rollback is permitted).
3) Imaging pipeline change: Detect fancal exit and auto-move device to 'requires-firmware-review' queue to avoid repeated failures.

1) Firmware Eng: Coordinate with Dell SR-992183 to confirm whether 16.2.8 intentionally introduces fan-curve lock and request guidance or signed utility (ETA requested by 2026-03-17).

Issue summary:
Dual-NIC laptops (docked Ethernet + Wi‑Fi) intermittently lose access to internal services after waking from sleep. Traffic destined for internal subnets is routed to the wrong interface causing a silent blackhole — the OS chooses the Wi‑Fi gateway but the corporate split-tunnel policy expects WireGuard bound to the Ethernet interface.

Impact:
- Multiple engineers in the SF office reported inability to reach internal CI, internal dashboards, and LDAP-protected services after resume.
- Symptoms: TCP connections hang (no RST), SSH sessions freeze, and http requests timeout despite VPN status 'connected'.
- Affects ~5–10% of docked macOS laptops (M1/M2) observed over the past week.

Environment:
- Client: macOS Monterey/Big Sur variations (12.x/11.x), Redwood wireless + wired docked setups.
- VPN: WireGuard-based zero-trust agent (internal build r2026.03.01).
- Network: Office LAN with split-tunnel routes provisioned by agent.
- Affected region: us-west (SF office).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Dock MacBook to ethernet dock while on corporate Wi‑Fi.
2) Agent starts and establishes WireGuard tunnel bound to the Ethernet adapter.
3) Put laptop to sleep (close lid).
4) Wake laptop, rejoin Wi‑Fi; OS sometimes reorders interface metrics and moves default route to Wi‑Fi before agent rebinds tunnel.
5) Requests to 10.0.0.0/8 (internal) show routing to Wi‑Fi gateway instead of WireGuard, resulting in packet loss.

Observed network state example (post-resume):
- netstat -nr shows default route via 192.168.1.1 (Wi‑Fi) with metric 100
- WireGuard interface wg0 present with peer handshake OK, but route for 10.20.0.0/16 is missing or points to wrong dev

Sample traceroute to internal app (user machine):
1  192.168.1.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.1 ms
2  * * *

Logs collected from client (attached in ticket):
- /var/log/wg-agent.log excerpt:
  [2026-03-10T08:12:02Z] wg-agent: peer handshake OK
  [2026-03-10T08:12:03Z] wg-agent: applied routes: 0 entries (expected 3)
  [2026-03-10T08:12:03Z] wg-agent: interface bound to en0 (Ethernet)
  [2026-03-10T08:12:04Z] netlink: interface change: en1 metric 50

Expected behavior:
- After resume, the agent should re-apply split-tunnel routes and ensure internal prefixes are routed through wg0 regardless of default route metric changes. WireGuard should bind to the active interface used for corporate traffic or use policy-based routing.

Temporary workaround used by users:
- Manually run: sudo wg-agent restart && sudo route -n add -net 10.20.0.0/16 -interface wg0
- Toggling Wi‑Fi off briefly restores correct routing.

Notes:
- Issue appears racey: sometimes agent reapplies routes correctly. Suspect timing between OS network stack reordering interfaces and agent's post-resume handler.
- A small subset of affected machines are using third-party 'Ethernet Dock' drivers that modify interface metrics on attach.

2026-03-10 | Support triage - Priortized by Alex Kim: Confirmed multiple reports from SF office. Repro steps requested from affected user. Assigned to Jordan Patel.
2026-03-11 | Customer (internal user) - Rahul S: Attached tcpdump and wg-agent logs. I reproduced by closing lid for ~30s. Toggling Wi‑Fi off fixed it for me.
2026-03-12 | Jordan Patel (SRE): Collected additional traces. Observed netlink events where en1 (Wi‑Fi) gets metric 50 and becomes default before wg-agent reapplies routes. Hypothesis: agent listens to sleep/wake but race with OS route update. Planning to instrument a test build that delays route application until stable network state is observed.
2026-03-13 | Jordan Patel (SRE): Deployed instrumented agent to 3 volunteers. Initial data: in 6 resume cycles where issue would have occurred, delayed reapply fixed 5. One failure correlated with third-party dock drivers changing metrics after 10s post-resume.
2026-03-14 | Alex Kim (Support): Notifying desktop platform team to escalate dock driver compatibility. Opening follow-up internal ticket for packaging vendor communication.
Collected artifacts: tcpdump, wg-agent logs, netstat -nr, route outputs from 7 affected devices.
Hypothesis: race between OS network reorder and agent route application. Agent assumes active interface immediately after wake; sometimes the system updates interface metrics afterward.
Confirmed: restart of wg-agent or toggling Wi‑Fi forces correct routing. Suggests route application is the corrective action.
Repro rate on instrumented devices: ~83% prevented by delaying route apply until no netlink changes for 5s.
Edge case: docks that hotplug drivers modify metric after we consider 'stable' - need driver-aware probe or retry loop.
(In Progress) Workaround: users can run 'wg-agent restart' or toggle Wi‑Fi until fix published.
Next steps: 1) Engineering to ship agent patch that waits for netlink stability (5–10s) before applying split-tunnel routes and adds a retry loop for late metric changes. 2) Desktop team to contact dock vendor to confirm driver behavior; consider vendor-specific mitigation. 3) Add telemetry to detect prevalence and log metric-change timelines.
Planned rollout: staged canary to 5% of macOS fleet 2026-03-20, full rollout if no regressions by 2026-03-25.
payload.summary: Dual-NIC route priority creates split-tunnel blackhole after macOS sleep/resume

Issue summary: Multiple employees reported seeing OAuth consent prompts requesting access to 'View and manage Google Drive files' and 'Manage service accounts' after downloading a DOCX attachment labeled 'Q2 Prospect List' from a cold outreach email. Users who clicked the link were routed to an external consent page that pretended to be our IdP.

Impact: Potential unauthorized consent grants and ephemeral tokens issued that could be used to enumerate service accounts and read linked Drive files. At least two users approved the prompt before being stopped by security. No confirmed data exfiltration found in the first 48 hours, but suspicious API calls were observed from two employee sessions.

Environment: Prod SSO (Okta) federated to GCP and Google Workspace. Affected users primarily in us-west office; cross-org emails originate from external vendor domain.

Observed behaviour: After opening the DOCX, users reported a browser popup requesting they "Sign in with Redwood" and then an OAuth consent screen for a third-party app named "Marketing Asset Importer" requesting elevated scopes. The consent screen used our logo and a subdomain that looked similar to our IdP. Two users granted consent.

Expected behaviour: Downloading internal prospect lists should not trigger any OAuth consent flows. Legitimate Salesforce/marketing integrations are pre-approved and use our internal app registry.

Initial evidence:
- Okta system log IDs: okta-log-55512, okta-log-55513
- Google Workspace OAuth audit entries: gw-oauth-20260310-01, gw-oauth-20260310-02
- Affected users: j.diaz@redwood.ai, m.ross@redwood.ai (redacted in ticket)

Recommended immediate actions already taken:
- Reached out to users and instructed them not to interact further with the file/link.
- Blocked the sender domain at gateway and quarantined the original email.
- Revoked the two recently issued OAuth tokens via Google admin console.
- Initiated short-term conditional access policy to require re-auth for web OAuth requests from unknown subdomains.

Receive cold outreach email with DOCX attachment 'Q2 Prospect List'
Download and open DOCX in browser or Word—document contains a visible link labeled 'Import to Drive'
Clicking the link opens a browser tab pointing to hxxps://drive-import.redwood-verify[.]com/oauth?app=marketing
Consent page displays Redwood branding and asks for Google Workspace and service account scopes
If user approves, OAuth grant is recorded in Google OAuth audit logs and tokens are issued
2026-03-10 10:12 UTC - Triage started. Identified OAuth grants with app name 'Marketing Asset Importer' created 2026-03-10 09:58 UTC.
Browser forensics: the DOCX contains a link to hxxps://drive-import.redwood-verify[.]com/oauth which resolves to 198.51.100.42 (malicious host). The subdomain includes our company name to add legitimacy.
Okta logs show an external redirect to hxxps://auth.redwood-verify[.]com that is not in our IdP app registry. No SAML assertions from our IdP were generated for these events—this was a direct OAuth page to Google.
Google OAuth audit shows scopes granted: openid, email, profile, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloudplatform.readonly (service account token exchange scope).
Affected assets: two user tokens revoked; audit of Drive files accessed shows read operations on a shared marketing folder by IPs 203.0.113.27 and 198.51.100.42, both external and not on allowlist.
No evidence of data exfil beyond listing and metadata reads. Investigating whether service account exchange requests succeeded—pending GCP audit logs retrieval.
Cross-references: related to INT-70319 (repeated-token-exchange-requests-from-geo-diverse-ips) for similar token-exchange pattern observed previously. Also flagged under phishing campaign cluster in SIEM (cluster id phish-202603).
Containment: blocked malicious host at perimeter, applied URL block in user agents, added domain to organization-wide denylist. Notified legal and compliance to prepare customer notification checklist if PII access is confirmed.
Revoked all OAuth grants associated with 'Marketing Asset Importer' and forcibly rotated refresh tokens for the two affected users. Blocked the phishing domains at perimeter and engaged hosting provider for takedown of 198.51.100.42. Implemented a temporary IdP policy requiring Okta MFA for any new OAuth consent that requests high-privilege scopes and blocked user-initiated service-account scope grants. Delivered company-wide advisory about the specific phishing lure and added an automated inspection to email gateway that flags DOCX files with external OAuth links. Follow-ups: schedule a tabletop with Support/SRE/IR to update runbook and add automated OAuth grant anomaly alerting to SIEM.

CISO (Evelyn Park) - 2026-03-11: Approve user-scoped token revocations and organization-wide short-lived token policy. Notify legal if any PII access found.

Issue summary: Customer (NovaChat Inc.) reported an increase in 5xx responses on their dedicated tenant beginning ~2026-03-13T18:05Z. Errors were concentrated on the /v1/embeddings and /v1/chat/stream endpoints and correlated with a simultaneous heavy embedding upload + live chat traffic spike.
Multiple production clients observed token-generation failures and stream disconnects. Aggregate 5xx rate for the tenant rose to ~18% during the peak window (18:05Z-18:28Z). Tail latency increased (p95 from 420ms to ~3.6s). Several upstream runtime pods restarted due to NVML driver resets, causing additional request amplification and a sustained elevated error floor.
Dedicated pool: dp-wn-02 (4 x A100s), autoscaler policy: conservative node add (cooldown 120s), apigw config: keepalive 60s, max-connections-per-worker 1024. Tenant traffic mix: concurrent small chat (low-token) streams + large embedding batches (single request sizes up to 10k sparse vectors).
1) Submit multiple concurrently interleaved requests: many small streaming chat sessions (20-50 rps) AND a few large embedding uploads (2-4 requests with 5k-10k vectors) from the same tenant. 2) Observe apigw connection churn and burst in accept queue. 3) Verify kvcache eviction & runtime GPU memory allocation spikes. 4) Watch for NVML reset events in runtime logs and subsequent 5xx responses from upstream.
- Apigw logs (18:05Z): accept_queue_wait > 2s, connection resets up 4x baseline.
- Error rate: 5xx jumped from 0.6% baseline to 18% at peak.
- Runtime logs: repeated NVML_ERROR: device is lost + kernel abort messages; container restarts 6 times across three nodes.
- GPU telemetry: sustained 98% memory utilization, occasional driver OOMs and ECC errors flagged.
- kvcache: eviction rate spike and lock contention metrics increased during the same window.
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant/tenant-dp-wn-02?from=2026-03-13T18:00Z&to=2026-03-13T18:30Z
- 18:03Z: NovaChat schedules large embedding preprocess job.
- 18:05Z: Apigw accept-queue grows; first 5xx observed.
- 18:07Z: Runtime reports NVML reset on node worker-03; worker restarts.
- 18:11Z: Autoscaler attempts node add but cooldown prevents immediate recovery.
- 18:18Z: We applied temporary tenant rate limit to embedding endpoints. 5xx rate begins to decline.
- 18:25Z: Additional runtime restarts observed after another embedding chunk completed.
- 18:28Z: Error rate settles to ~1.2% after blocking large uploads and scaling dedicated pool by +2 nodes.
Hypothesis: concurrent mixed workload (many long-lived streaming connections + large embedding uploads) caused connection thrashing at apigw leading to hot spots in the accept queue and amplified retries. Upstream runtimes experienced rapid memory allocations and NVML driver contention, triggering device resets. Lock contention in kvcache prefetch paths increased GC and eviction activity, contributing to runtime instability.
- Immediately applied tenant-level soft rate limit on /v1/embeddings for NovaChat.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive short-circuit retries on apigw for streaming routes.
- Scaled the customer's dedicated pool by adding 2 nodes (manual override).
- Notified SRE on-call and opened runtime hotfix PR to add defensive NVML reset handling.
- Customer notified with mitigation steps and temporary workaround (stagger embedding uploads).
Amelia Carter (Support) 2026-03-13T18:22Z: Notified SRE; applying tenant rate limit now. Customer reporting partial recovery.
Diego Morales (SRE) 2026-03-13T18:27Z: Seeing NVML resets on worker-03 and worker-04; driver logs attached. Autoscaler cooldown prevented immediate replacement — doing manual scale.
Ravi Shah (Solutions Eng) 2026-03-13T18:45Z: Advised customer to stagger embedding jobs and reduce batch size as short-term workaround. Monitoring error rate post-throttle.
Customer (NovaChat) 2026-03-13T19:05Z: Confirmed that error rate dropped and chat sessions resumed; will implement upload staggering today.
Combination of apigw accept-queue saturation from connection churn (mixed long-lived streams + large embeddings) and upstream runtime GPU driver instability under immediate high-allocation pressure. The autoscaler cooldown and conservative add policy delayed capacity recovery, allowing retries and restarts to amplify the failure.
Temporary mitigation: tenant embedding rate-limited and dedicated pool manually scaled; streaming retry policy adjusted. Customer workaround: stagger embedding uploads and reduce per-request vector counts. Engineering PR opened to improve NVML reset handling and add admission control to reject expensive embedding uploads during streaming bursts.
Merge runtime PR to catch and gracefully handle NVML resets + reduce automatic hard restarts (PR #2523)
Add admission-control / cost-estimate step in apigw to reject or queue large embedding uploads when a tenant has active streaming sessions
Tune autoscaler policy for dedicated pools: reduce cooldown for emergency scale-adds and add burst-mode override for P1 tenants
Investigate kvcache prefetch lock contention and add per-tenant prefetch throttling
Create a tenant-level best-practices doc for mixed workloads (confluence page draft)
Improve observability: synthetic mixed-workload load tests and alerting on accept-queue latency > 500ms for >2m
SRE to backfill logs and attach core dumps to this ticket (Diego)
Runtime team to finalize PR #2523 and run canary on staging (assigned: Priya)
Product to scope apigw admission-control (owner: Maya)
CS to follow up with NovaChat on upload scheduling adoption and confirm stability tomorrow (Amelia)
Schedule postmortem meeting after full resolution
Mitigated (temporary) - tenant rate limiting + manual scale. Permanent fixes planned as listed in long_term_fix_plan.

Issue summary: BeaconMaps reports intermittent 429 responses for a subset of ingest workers immediately after a scheduled credential rotation. Impact: ~15% of batch uploads from their orchestrated ingester fleet fail with 429s for a ~1–3 minute window during rotations; customer sees increased retry loops and missed SLA on a handful of jobs. Frequency: Observed across 4 rotation events in the past 48 hours (2026-03-08 22:00 UTC, 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC, 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC, 2026-03-11 01:45 UTC). Customer environment: Dedicated pool (BeaconMaps-prod), long-lived orchestrated upload workers that rotate ephemeral API keys via our key-rotation endpoint. They run 12 parallel uploaders per region with staggered rotation schedule under their orchestrator.
1) Configure a dedicated pool with orchestrated ingesters that rotate ephemeral credentials every 1 hour.
2) Start 8–12 parallel upload workers in us-west using multiplexed connections.
3) Trigger a rotation with overlapping refresh windows (small stagger <10s between worker groups).
4) Observe 429s in client logs during and just after rotation window.
Notes: reproduction requires parallelism + overlapping/closely-timed rotations; single-worker rotations are not reproducing the problem consistently.
[2026-03-10T02:30:01Z] upload-worker-7 POST /v1/ingest -> 429 {"error":"too_many_requests", "x-rate-limit-window":"60s"}
[2026-03-10T02:30:02Z] auth-rotator INFO swapping keys for worker-group-A (old_key=ak_...123, new_key=ak_...456)
[2026-03-10T02:30:03Z] proxy-conn-218 counted token for key ak_...123 against tenant BeaconMaps (window_start=2026-03-10T02:29:30Z)
[2026-03-10T02:30:03Z] proxy-conn-219 counted token for key ak_...456 against tenant BeaconMaps (window_start=2026-03-10T02:29:30Z)
[2026-03-10T02:30:05Z] upload-worker-3 RETRY attempt=1 after 429
[2026-03-10T02:31:10Z] upload-worker-7 SUCCESS POST /v1/ingest -> 200 (after backoff)
Initial hypothesis: overlapping rotation causes brief double-counting of tenant tokens because both old and new API key tokens are charged to the tenant window concurrently.
Checked rate-limiter logs: saw simultaneous token increments from two different API keys that both map to BeaconMaps inside the same refill window. No evidence of upstream proxy misrouting.
Observed that the customer's orchestrator triggers refresh for small groups in <10s buckets; heavy parallelism (12 workers) increases probability of >1 key being active in same 60s window.
Verified config: tenant-level window is 60s with 6k token burst configured for BeaconMaps dedicated pool. During rotation, instantaneous token counts spike above configured burst due to duplicate counting behavior.
Correlation: 4 rotation events where rotations were tightly clustered coincided with 429 spike windows on customer traces. Healthy rotations with >30s staggering did not reproduce.
Checked for related changes: no recent ingress-proxy releases in customer pool; key rotation code path change was deployed to control plane last week (PR linked below) but not directly in serving runtime.
Engineering note: candidate fix is to ensure rotation handoff marks the old key as draining (prevent new requests using both keys concurrently) OR server-side de-dup that maps rotating keys to same tenant ref and performs per-tenant dedup of near-simultaneous token accounting.
2026-03-10 04:12 - BeaconMaps (support@beaconmaps.com): We're seeing intermittent 429s right after our hourly key rotation. It affects only our mass-upload workers. Can you confirm if something changed?

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 05:03 - BeaconMaps: Sent sample request IDs and their worker rotation timestamps; confirmed they stagger by ~5s between groups.
2026-03-12 02:10 - Engineering (PR): https://github.com/redwood/ingress-proxy/pull/1425 submitted (adds rotation-handoff flag + per-tenant accounting dedupe). Requesting rollout approval to BeaconMaps pool.
Short-term workaround provided to customer: 1) Increase stagger between worker-group rotations to >=30s. 2) Schedule rotations during off-peak windows. 3) As an immediate platform-side mitigation, we increased their dedicated pool burst ceiling by 50% for 2 hours around rotation windows to avoid transient 429s.
Platform change merged to ingress-proxy that marks keys as 'draining' on rotation and performs per-tenant near-simultaneous accounting dedupe. Customer pool received the mitigation patch and a configuration update to ensure rotations are fenced for 30s. 429 events returned to baseline on next rotation window after patch rollout.
- Rollout steps: merge PR https://github.com/redwood/ingress-proxy/pull/1425 -> canary to internal test cluster -> deploy to BeaconMaps dedicated pool (done 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC).
- Post-deploy monitoring: 48h sliding window showed no rotation-associated 429 spikes.
- Follow-ups: update public rotation best-practices doc and add a console alert when tenant rotation density exceeds threshold.
- Owner: Marcus Nguyen (SRE) for rollout + postmortem.

Issue summary: Customer reports multiple short stalls in streaming chat sessions where the server stops emitting tokens for 2-10s, then resumes mid-response multiple times before completing. This started after a deployment on 2026-02-28 and appears correlated with idle connection keepalive rotation at the edge. Impact: UX degradation for long-form streaming replies (clinical note generation). Customer sees 2-6 oscillations per long response, causing timeouts and duplicate reconnection attempts on their client. Environment: prod | us-east-1 | dedicated pool for NimbusHealth. Observed on both SSE and websocket clients.

Observed behavior: the stream does not fully close, but output halts for short windows and then continues from the last token. Sometimes the client triggers a reconnect after client-side inactivity timer and receives duplicate tokens before the stream finishes.

Hypothesis: combination of edge-proxy keepalive reset, HTTP/2 window/flow-control interactions, and worker preemption (eviction) causing short write stalls. Potential coalescing in upstream LB leads to partial buffer flushes that the client treats as silence.

Severity/priority rationale: P1/Sev1 because production customers are affected and there is measurable UX impact and increased client-side timeouts.
1) Use a long-context prompt that triggers >20s generation time on redwood-14b-v2.
2) Open an SSE or websocket streaming session through the customer-dedicated route (NimbusHealth token).
3) Ensure client sends default keepalive heartbeats and allows connection reuse.
4) Wait for a generation that crosses an idle/keepalive reset boundary (observed after ~60s of token gap).
5) Observe intermittent 2-10s token silence followed by resumed tokens (repeatable with load and after edge config change).
2026-03-01T09:14:02Z edge-proxy INFO conn=0x7f8 keepalive reset for conn_id=abc123 ttl=60
2026-03-01T09:14:04Z serving-runtime WARN worker=wr-22 write-stall duration=2300ms request_id=req-9912 model=redwood-14b-v2
2026-03-01T09:14:07Z kv-cache INFO checkpoint completed shard=3 latency=12ms
2026-03-01T09:14:09Z edge-proxy DEBUG flush-partial payload_bytes=4096 conn_id=abc123
2026-03-01T09:14:12Z sdk-client ERROR client-timeout triggered after 8s silence request_id=req-9912
Initial triage: Support reproduced the oscillation in our staging cluster by toggling edge keepalive to match the production config. Correlated worker preemption events (k8s pod eviction for spot reprovisioning) were visible in the same timeframe as stall windows in logs. Edge team observed small partial flushes from the upstream HTTP/2 connection followed by a short pause while flow-control windows were updated. Engineering hypothesis: race between edge keepalive rotation + HTTP/2 flow-control + serving runtime's write path that treats partial flush as an in-progress write and blocks subsequent flushes for a short backoff. This combination produces the 2-10s audible silence.

Reproducibility: High under simulated keepalive rotations and spot-worker preemptions; low under steady-state load. Customer reports started after Feb 28 deploy which changed edge idle timeout tuning.

Temporary mitigation tested: disabled HTTP/2 connection pooling for the customer route and increased accept-window in edge-proxy; this reduced oscillations in test runs but not acceptable cluster-wide without further validation.

Related signals: spikes in client reconnects, increased request latency percentiles (p95 -> p99) for streaming endpoints, small uptick in 5xx in downstream logs when clients retry rapidly.
Aisha Khan (Support) 2026-03-01: Raised by NimbusHealth CS; they have multiple long chat sessions hitting the issue intermittently.
Marco Diaz (SRE) 2026-03-01: Reproduced in staging by toggling keepalive. Captured worker eviction events aligning with stalls.
Elena Park (Edge) 2026-03-02: Investigated HTTP/2 flush path; noted partial flushes coinciding with keepalive rotation. Working on PR to change flush semantics.
Customer (NimbusHealth) 2026-03-02: Provided sample request ids and client logs. Notified that clinical note generation workflows are impacted during peak hours.
Marco Diaz (SRE) 2026-03-03: Rolled a canary config to the customer's route disabling connection reuse; initial telemetry shows 80% reduction in stalls for the canary pool.
Aisha Khan (Support) 2026-03-05: Notified customer of progress and temporary workaround; monitoring continues.
Workaround applied: edge-proxy config for NimbusHealth updated to (a) disable aggressive HTTP/2 connection reuse on the dedicated route and (b) increase keepalive handshake grace window. Edge change deployed to canary pool 2026-03-03 and expanded to full customer pool 2026-03-04. Serving runtime patch (see PR 1056) adds non-blocking flush fallback when upstream partial flush is detected; merged 2026-03-04 and rolled out to dedicated nodes. Outcome: observed 85% reduction in oscillation incidents for this customer in 48h post-rollout. Customer verified improvement and reduced client reconnect events.
INT-4421: Add metric 'last_stream_chunk_age' and alert when >3s for streaming endpoints.
Edge PR 289: revisit HTTP/2 flush semantics and add feature flag for per-route connection reuse control.
ServRuntime PR 1056: add non-blocking flush fallback - monitor for regressions and load impact.
Document recommended client heartbeat guidance for long streaming sessions in Support KB and add to SDK defaults.
Postmortem runbook update: include worker eviction detection as a gating signal for streaming SLOs.

Background
- We are rolling out Dedicated throughput SLOs + tiered commitments. Support/CS needs a consistent, pre-approved external communication workflow for SLO breaches (or potential breaches) that can be executed quickly by oncall.
- Current gap: no standardized Status Page templates for Dedicated throughput SLO degradation (customer-facing wording, update cadence, what we can/can’t promise, and when to mention credits/remedies).

Problem
- During recent throughput investigations (see SUP-18422, SUP-18510) comms were ad-hoc and inconsistent across Support, CS, and SRE.
- Customers (esp. enterprise Dedicated) are asking for “in writing” acknowledgement of SLO misses and clear timelines/updates; we need a repeatable workflow aligned with SRE incident policy.

Request
1) Create Status Page incident templates specific to Dedicated throughput SLO breach communications:
   - Initial notice (Investigating)
   - Identified + mitigation in progress
   - Monitoring
   - Resolved
   - Post-incident summary (optional, within 2–5 business days)
2) Define operational workflow:
   - When to open a Status Page event vs. keep comms 1:1 (account-specific)
   - Who owns posting (Support oncall vs. SRE oncall) and approval path
   - Update cadence targets (e.g., every 60 min while active, then at resolution)
   - Links/fields to include (customer-facing dashboard references, if any)
3) Add “do not say” guidance:
   - Don’t share exact committed tokens/sec floors, internal headroom numbers, or affected customer list unless approved.
   - Don’t attribute root cause prematurely (e.g., “GPU shortage”) without SRE confirmation.
   - Avoid implying SLA remedies/credits unless Finance/CS policy is triggered.

Proposed scope for templates
- Dedicated Throughput Degradation (Tier-wide / Regional) template
- Dedicated Throughput Degradation (Single-customer deployment) template (generally avoid Status Page unless multiple customers impacted; prefer direct comms, but template should exist)

Acceptance criteria
- Templates added to Status Page tool (component: “Dedicated Inference (Throughput)”) with pre-filled language + placeholders.
- Workflow documented in Support runbook (link added to Dedicated throughput SLO escalation playbook).
- Approval list explicitly named: Support oncall owner, SRE oncall, CS lead on duty, and escalation to Commercial Counsel if remedy language is included.
- Training note posted in #support and #customer-success with where-to-find templates and when-to-use guidance.

Notes
- This ticket is about comms + operational workflow only (not SLO definition changes).
- Target date: before broader Dedicated tier enablement rollout.
2025-02-19 10:22 Dev Patel (reporter)
Created after reviewing recent Dedicated throughput cases where we lacked a consistent external comms pattern. Need something lightweight but enforceable before more accounts get tiered SLO language.
2025-02-20 14:05 Rachel Kim
+1. For enterprise accounts, CS ends up drafting emails from scratch during an incident. Even if we don’t post publicly on Status Page for single-account events, having approved language and cadence guidance will reduce time-to-first-update and de-risk legal wording.
2025-02-21 09:48 Rafael Mendes
From SRE side: we’re fine with a Status Page template as long as we keep it generic and don’t publish per-customer metrics. Recommend: only post if (a) multiple Dedicated customers in a region, (b) sustained SLO burn-rate alert indicates likely breach, or (c) SRE declares customer-impacting incident. Otherwise use the 1:1 template.
2025-02-24 16:11 Kira Thompson (assignee)
Drafted template set v1 and shared in #support-ops for review. Open questions:
- Do we name specific regions in the public post (e.g., us-east) or keep it broader?
- Do we mention “throughput below expected” vs “increased queueing / reduced capacity” wording?
- Who is the final approver if we include credit/remedy language placeholder?
2025-02-25 11:36 Laura Bennett
For remedy language: keep as “Customer Success will follow up regarding account-specific remedies where applicable.” Do not mention credit % or formulas in Status Page posts. Any compensation details must be handled 1:1 by CS per policy.
2025-02-26 13:02 Sean Gallagher
Suggested aligning triggers with SLO semantics:
- Status Page Investigating when we have a confirmed platform-side capacity/throughput impairment affecting more than one Dedicated deployment OR a regional pool saturation event.
- Use ‘potential SLO impact’ phrasing until breach confirmed by the evaluator window.
- Add a line that measurement excludes customer-side throttling/misconfiguration to avoid self-inflicted reports being treated as platform incident.
2025-03-03 15:28 Dev Patel
Reviewed templates. Requested two variants:
(1) ‘Dedicated Throughput Degradation (multi-tenant pool / multiple customers)’ for Status Page
(2) ‘Dedicated Throughput Degradation (single customer)’ for direct email + ticket update
Also asked to include required internal links: dashboard panel and escalation runbook.
2025-03-05 10:17 Kira Thompson
Implemented changes and added workflow section. Final template text pasted into Status Page as saved templates under component group “Dedicated Inference (Throughput)”. Posted internal enablement note draft for review by Rachel + Rafael.
2025-03-07 09:04 Dev Patel
Enablement note posted to #support and #customer-success. Marking resolved. Follow-up: we should add a short checklist to oncall handoff doc (separate ticket if needed).
Saved Status Page templates created for Dedicated throughput incidents (multi-customer / regional). Direct-communication template created for single-customer Dedicated deployment throughput degradation. Operational workflow documented and linked from Dedicated throughput SLO escalation playbook; update cadence and approval guidance defined. Internal enablement note posted to #support and #customer-success.
