Issue summary: Intermittent failures when obtaining ephemeral cloud credentials for sandbox/test environments. Requests to the identity-broker are denied with AssumeRole/Permission errors when session tags are included, resulting in developers being unable to access ephemeral namespaces for ML debugging.

Impact: Blocks multiple platform and ML engineers from running reproduce workflows in ephemeral environments (staging-like sandboxes). Affects oncall rotations for debugging Dedicated provisioning flows and slows down private deployment troubleshooting. Not a customer-facing outage but reduces developer velocity and delays incident response.

Environment: identity-broker service (k8s cluster: infra-idbroker-prod), ephemeral JIT flow used by dev and ci runners, affected regions: us-east-1 and europe-west1. Problem appears in prod only; staging not affected.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger ephemeral STS/AssumeRole workflow via the dev portal (Request ephemeral role for project: ml-experiments, env: sandbox-us-east).
2) Identity-broker calls STS:AssumeRole with session tags derived from portal metadata (team, env, requestor-email).
3) STS responds with AccessDenied. Broker logs show tag-aware policy evaluation failed.
4) Retry without tags or with truncated tag set succeeds (returns credentials).

Observed logs / errors:
- identity-broker logs: "AssumeRoleDenied: SessionTagConditionMismatch: env tag 'sandbox-us-east-2026' not allowed by policy"
- AWS CloudTrail: "AssumeRoleFailure - principal=broker-sa@example.com - error=MalformedSessionTag" (intermittent)
- GCP IAM audit: ephemeral-impersonation RPC returned PERMISSION_DENIED when tag translation enabled
- Portal UI: shows generic 403 and "unable to provision credentials"

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Session tag values exceed character limits / contain characters not normalized by the org policy (dashes + timestamp suffix). Tags are being programmatically appended with deployment suffixes, causing policy mismatch when org policy expects canonical env names.
- Hypothesis 2: The broker's tag normalization routine truncates or silently drops tags longer than 128 chars, causing required tag predicates to fail (we saw "MalformedSessionTag" in some STS failures).
- Hypothesis 3: Recent tag-normalizer change (PR #github.com/redwood/infra/commit/2b8f1c) introduced new regex anchors that fail on env names with numeric suffixes.
- Reproduced locally in a controlled run by injecting altered env tag values; removal of the timestamp suffix allowed AssumeRole to succeed.
- Cross-checked with org-policy logs; policy evaluator logs show failed match on "env" attribute when value contained trailing digits and hyphenated zones.

Workaround applied:
- Temporary mitigation: Identity-broker configured to strip non-alphanumeric characters and drop timestamp suffix before STS call for affected projects. Deployed at 2026-03-11 17:30 UTC to infra-idbroker-prod (feature-flag: relax-session-tagging). This reduces tag fidelity but restores developer access.
- Manual emergency policy exception created for the ml-experiments role to accept broader env tag patterns until permanent fix ships (ticket INT-314271 referenced for org-policy exception).

Root cause (current best understanding): A regression in the broker's tag-normalization code combined with a stricter org-level tag matching policy. The change made tag matching more strict and did not account for auto-appended deployment suffixes, causing legitimate session-tags to be rejected by STS/org-policy.

Permanent remediation plan:
1) Roll back the tag-normalizer regex change and add unit tests to cover env name variants (owner: infra-auth, ETA: 2026-03-15).
2) Update identity-broker to validate and canonicalize tags consistently with org-policy (implement a mapping table for known env aliases).
3) Release a phased deploy: canary in us-east-1 then eu-west (rollback window 30m).
4) Run a migration job that normalizes historical ephemeral requests for auditing and update Confluence runbook.
5) Security review of session-tagging policy changes and sign-off from SecOps prior to widening tag acceptance (owner: SecOps, ETA: 2026-03-18).

Next steps / action items:
- Samir to open PR to revert/adjust regex and add tests (ETA: 2026-03-13).
- Infra oncall to schedule canary and monitor STS/CloudTrail metrics for error rate regression (ETA: 2026-03-14).
- SecOps to review temporary policy exception and confirm expiry/cleanup (ETA: 2026-03-16).

Related notes and evidence:
- Identity-broker pod logs snapshot: s3://redwood-ops-logs/idbroker/2026/03/11/ephemeral-403.log
- Git diff suspected change: github.com/redwood/infra/commit/2b8f1c (see comment in linked PR).

2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Support (Avery Chen): Customer reported developers unable to obtain ephemeral creds; capturing initial logs and triaging to infra-auth.
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Infra (Samir Patel): Reproduced in prod using curl replay. Observed 'MalformedSessionTag' in one STS call. Adding more log context to broker and elevating to P1.
2026-03-11 16:45 UTC - SecOps (Marta Ruiz): Noted org-policy changes last week. Temporary exception approved for ml-experiments role until 2026-03-17. Please ensure audit trail for the change.
2026-03-11 17:35 UTC - Infra (Samir Patel): Deployed temporary relax-session-tagging flag. Verified that token issuance resumed for impacted flows. Monitoring metrics.
2026-03-12 08:20 UTC - Infra (Samir Patel): Preparing PR to revert regex and add tests. Will schedule canary deploy; posting PR link in related_github_prs when ready.

Issue summary: Internal support tooling contains diverging SLA template names and duplicated routing rules introduced during the Dec 2025 rule-engine migration. This has caused inconsistent SLA enforcement across internal queues (some P1 tickets are not being escalated to SRE on 30m schedule).

Impact: Partial enforcement of P1/P2 SLAs for internal support channels; potential missed wake-up pages for on-call SREs. Affected teams: Internal Support (triage), SRE runbooks that depend on canonical SLA labels, and the automation that generates SLA reports. No customer-facing incidents reported yet but internal SLAs are the source of several PagerDuty misses in the last three weeks.

Environment: support-tooling (prod), routing-engine v2, rulebook index: /opt/support/rules/v2 (internal).

Steps to reproduce:
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOOLING_API" https://tooling.internal.redwood/api/v1/sla_templates | grep -i P1
2) Compare template names returned against routing rule config: /etc/support/routing_rules.yaml
3) Run the reporting job (support-sla-reporter) for the last 14 days and observe tickets that should have triggered P1 escalation but show no escalation action.

Observed behavior: There are at least three templates that appear semantically identical but have different slugs (e.g. "P1-30m", "P1-30m_v1", "p1-30-min"). Routing rules sometimes point at older slugs. The SLA reporter aggregates by slug, so metrics are split and alert thresholds are not being hit.

Logs / dashboards:
- Support tooling audit log: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/abcd-support-tooling/sla-audit?orgId=1
- Reporter job run: https://ci.internal.redwood/builds/6543 (last failed run referencing missing template)

Initial hypothesis: Migration created duplicate template entries; the rule-engine accepted both old and new slugs without normalization. Downstream reporter was not updated to canonicalize slugs, fragmenting metrics and preventing escalations.

Proposed short-term mitigation: Add one-off reconciliation that maps legacy slugs to canonical slugs and backfills missing escalations for the last 7 days. Medium-term: enforce schema validation in the rule-engine CI and add a pre-deploy lint that rejects new/duplicate SLA slugs.

2026-02-11: Pulled template list from tooling API; found 47 SLA templates, 6 appear to be duplicates by human-readable description.
2026-02-12: Cross-referenced routing_rules.yaml; 4 rules reference legacy slugs that are not present in canonical mapping table.
2026-02-13: Re-ran support-sla-reporter locally with normalization flag; metrics aggregated correctly when normalization applied.
2026-02-15: Confirmed reporter failure in CI due to nil-pointer when template slug missing (see CI build 6543).
Marcus Lee (Reporter) 2026-02-10: Opening this task after noticing split metrics in weekly ops report. Assigning to Priya for ops-side remediation and coordination with rule-engine team.
Priya Nair (Assignee) 2026-02-11: I will scope the reconciliation script and schedule a short maintenance window. Can SRE confirm any on-call escalations missed in the last 72 hours?
Jules Park (SRE) 2026-02-11: Confirmed two P1 tickets on 2026-02-09 that did not escalate; raised pagerduty incident PD-7759. Linking here for visibility.
Eng (Routing) 2026-02-12: Noted that the rule-engine accepts arbitrary slug strings; we can add a validation hook in the next release (ETA 2026-02-28).
Priya Nair 2026-02-16: Reconciliation script drafted (support-tooling/reconcile_slas.py). Need review and sign-off from Routing and SRE before running in prod.
(Work in progress) Plan: 1) Approve reconciliation script and run in dry-run mode to produce mapping and list of affected tickets. 2) Backfill missing escalation actions for tickets created in last 7 days. 3) Merge a CI lint that enforces unique SLA slug registration and adds a test that canonicalizes slugs in reporter. 4) Update runbook and add automated rollback if any escalation deficits are detected. Target production run: 2026-02-20 02:00 UTC.
Routing team to provide canonical slug list and confirm preferred names (due 2026-02-17)
SRE to review backfill plan and approve PD runbook changes (due 2026-02-17)
Priya to open PR for reconciliation script and CI lint (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/support-tooling/pull/1423)
Schedule prod dry-run and full run in maintenance window (target 2026-02-20)

Issue summary:
We need a self-service onboarding flow that provisions a new Jira project, a matching Confluence space (based on a chosen template), and a Slack channel with enforced naming conventions and retention policy. The flow must include an automated gating/approval step that checks requester attributes against Okta groups and a lightweight risk scorer before creating resources.

Business justification / Impact:
- Current project creation is manual and causes 2–3 day waits for teams and inconsistent metadata.
- Missing templates lead to scattered documentation, inconsistent permissions, and audit gaps.
- Security/compliance wants a centralized guardrail to ensure PII/data-classification-sensitive projects require additional approvals.

Proposed solution overview:
1) Build a Jira service (internal-facing) where users submit a project request form that captures: project type, sensitivity level, primary owners, estimated lifetime, and required Confluence template.
2) Integrate with Okta to verify requester is in one of the allowed org groups; if not, route to manager approval.
3) Run a risk check (simple rule set: sensitivity + external-collab flag + billing tier) that returns low/medium/high. High-risk requests require SRE/Sec approval via an automated approval queue.
4) When approved, run automation to: create Jira project with standardized key prefix, create Confluence space from chosen template and apply page hierarchy scaffold, create a Slack channel with enforced name and retention settings, and set initial access permissions based on group mappings.
5) Emit audit event and create a confluence page stub listing owners + lifecycle notes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Form in Jira or internal console captures required fields and validates Okta group membership.
- Risk scoring outputs an explicit "approval required" flag for high-risk requests.
- On approval, Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channel exist within 10 minutes and follow naming/permission conventions.
- Created artifacts include metadata tags: "created_by", "sensitivity", "lifecycle_owner", and link to the approval ticket.
- Audit log entries land in central logging/observability (link to Confluence runbook).
- Security sign-off checklist included for high-risk projects.

Implementation plan / technical notes:
- Use existing automation runner (platform-automation) to call relevant APIs: Jira REST API, Confluence API, Slack SCIM/Conversations API, and Okta.
- Use a serverless workflow (short-lived job) to orchestrate: validate, risk-check, create resources, and apply permissions.
- Store mapping table in internal config repo for template -> Confluence template ID and Okta group -> permission role.
- Ensure idempotency keys for retries and guard against partial creation by implementing a compensating cleanup step.

Rollout and testing plan:
- Stage 1 (dev): build end-to-end in staging with a small set of templates and two Okta test groups.
- Stage 2 (pilot): enable for three internal pods, track time-to-create, failure modes, and manual override frequency.
- Stage 3: full rollout with internal docs and a short training session.

Risks / open questions:
- Slack SCIM permissions: do we have the authority to programmatically set retention policies for channels? Need confirmation from Security/Legal.
- Confluence template library: who will own long-term maintenance of templates? Suggest Product Docs owns templates and Product Ops owns scaffold updates.
- Billing and lifecycle: how will we tag projects for eventual archival? Need retention + cost center tagging fields.

Related artifacts and runbooks:
- Confluence: internal-runbooks/automation-onboard-template (requested for linkage)
- Slack: #platform-automation channel for webhook alerts

Estimated effort and resources:
- 2 engineers (backend + infra) for ~3 sprints, 1 security reviewer, 1 product-docs owner for templates.

Requested by: Hana (internal POD onboarding lead)

1) Request form validates Okta membership and required fields. 2) Risk check produces explicit approval requirement for high-sensitivity requests. 3) Successful creation of Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channel within 10 minutes of approval. 4) Metadata and audit events recorded and searchable. 5) Compensation/cleanup handles partial failures.
1) Draft request schema and UI for Jira/internal console. 2) Implement Okta lookup and permission mapping. 3) Implement simple risk-scoring lambda with configurable rules. 4) Build orchestrator to call Jira/Confluence/Slack APIs with idempotency. 5) Add observability: request logs, success/failure counters, and emitted audit events. 6) Run staging tests and a pilot with 3 pods. 7) Publish runbook and template ownership doc.
Stage 1: dev/staging (1 sprint). Stage 2: pilot with three pods (2 sprints). Stage 3: full rollout and docs (1 sprint). Post-launch: 30-day review to capture failure modes and adjust rules.
payload.summary: Create self-service gated Jira project + Confluence space + Slack channel onboarding flow with templated compliance checks

Issue summary: Internal service-to-service impersonation that relies on Okta group claims is failing when the impersonated principal has long namespaced groups. The identity proxy appears to truncate or drop group entries containing namespace separators (e.g., org:team:role), causing RBAC evaluation to deny impersonation.

Observed since 2026-03-10 07:40 UTC during the nightly runbook sweep. Affected operators cannot escalate runbooks that require cross-tenant impersonation and several CI jobs that create ephemeral service tokens are failing with 403.

Impact: High — oncall runbook escalation and scheduled internal automations are blocked. Manual workarounds are slow and error-prone.

Initial triage: Reproducible with a manual curl that includes a long X-Impersonate-Groups header. Short group lists succeed; long namespaced groups are either truncated or completely missing when they arrive at the auth service for RBAC evaluation.
Multiple internal runbooks blocked, CI-scheduler failing ~8% of nightly jobs, oncall escalation fallback being used. Estimated to affect 12 teams in us-east.
1) Create a service account A that will impersonate user B with groups that include namespaced entries (example: org:platform:runbooks, org:platform:ci-runners, org:infra:admin).
2) From the identity-proxy edge, POST to /v1/impersonate with header: X-Impersonate-Subject: service-A and X-Impersonate-Groups: org:platform:runbooks,org:platform:ci-runners,org:infra:admin
3) Observe response from auth service: 403 with RBAC deny. Check received headers at auth: the X-Impersonate-Groups header is shortened to "org:platform:runb..." or missing namespaced segments.
4) Repeat with a non-namespaced group list (team-members, infra-admin) and request succeeds.
5) Reproduce intermittently by increasing the total character length of group header; failures correlate with header byte length and presence of ':' characters.
Curl example: curl -H "X-Impersonate-Subject: svc-ci" -H "X-Impersonate-Groups: org:platform:runbooks,org:platform:ci-runners,org:infra:admin" https://proxy.internal.redwood/v1/impersonate
identity-proxy (2026-03-10T07:42:11Z): incoming headers size=734 bytes, X-Impersonate-Groups="org:platform:runbo"
auth-service (2026-03-10T07:42:12Z): RBAC decision DENY - missing required group org:platform:runbooks for impersonation request from svc-ci
nginx-proxy (2026-03-10T07:42:11Z): client_header_buffer_size=128, client_max_header_size=4096 (observed truncation when combined with internal rewrite)
Hypothesis 1: identity-proxy or one of the upstream proxies has a header-size/encoding bug that truncates values containing ':' (namespace separator).
Checked proxy config: nginx edge has client_header_buffer_size set to 128 for legacy vhost used by some internal tenants — likely inherited from an old template.
Captured raw TCP between proxy and auth: header bytes are truncated before reaching auth-service; observed truncation point aligns with 128-byte buffer boundary when long namespaced group strings are present.
Tested bypass: hit auth-service directly (bypassing proxy) with full X-Impersonate-Groups header — RBAC succeeds. Confirms proxy-level mutation.
Triage action: increased client_header_buffer_size temporarily to 2k on staging vhost and validated that impersonation with namespaced groups succeeds consistently.
Risk assessment: change to edge nginx template impacts many internal vhosts; need controlled rollout and verification for potential memory/latency impacts.
Next steps: prepare PR to update nginx vhost template to conservative buffer sizes, add unit tests for header pass-through, and add regression alerts for header truncation errors in identity-proxy metrics.
2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (J. Kim): Confirmed multiple customers internal teams reported 403 on runbook escalation. Escalating to infra-ops.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 02:05 - SRE (L. Gomez): Deployed staging nginx change (client_header_buffer_size=2048) and validated with long namespaced groups. No additional errors observed. Preparing infra-config PR for review.
Workaround: route affected service traffic to direct auth VIP until nginx template updated. Rollout plan includes canary on 1 host, monitor 5m auth-deny rate and header-mismatch logs.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A recently onboarded customer sandbox created a GCP service account for Private deployments, but the cross-cloud access broker (identity-inventory) did not index the new service account. As a result, when the dedicated provisioner attempted to populate assume-role mappings for AWS-side resources it used an out-of-date identity map and the STS token exchange failed.

Impact:
- Provisioning flows for the customer's private environment fail intermittently (5/20 attempts).
- Oncall escalations from Solutions Engineering during onboarding.
- No direct customer data exposure but blocks new private environments for this customer.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Create a new GCP service account via onboarding script in customer project (logs show SA created: sa-llm-provisioner@cust-123.iam.gserviceaccount.com).
2) Trigger provisioning from the dedicated API (provisioner v2.4.1).
3) Provisioner calls identity-inventory service to generate AWS assume-role bindings. identity-inventory does not return the new SA.
4) Provisioner falls back to a cached mapping entry which lacks the SA; token exchange fails with 403 from token broker.

Observed behavior:
- Token broker returns: "AccessDenied: token-exchange failed - principal not found in mapping"
- identity-inventory logs show no create event for that SA in the 10m window after SA creation.
- Cloud Audit logs from GCP show the SA creation event is present.

Expected behavior:
- identity-inventory picks up the new GCP SA within the sync window (<= 60s by design) so provisioner can build cross-account assume-role mapping and token exchange succeeds.

Relevant logs & IDs:
- GCP audit entry: projects/cust-123/activity/2026-03-10T14:02:11Z (createServiceAccount)
- Provisioner trace ID: trace-provision-20260310-77a9
- Token broker error stub: ERR-TOKEN-2039

Additional context:
- The customer is a Dedicated-tier customer onboarding a Private (VPC) deployment.
- Onboarding script uses short-lived service account creation; SA names follow our onboarding template.
- identity-inventory is built to react to Pub/Sub change notifications + periodic full sync. The pubsub topic for cust-123 shows delivery latencies ~30s but inventory still misses the SA in this case.

10-Mar: support triaged; reproduced with staging onboarding flow. Missing SA only when creation + immediate provisioning happen within ~20s window.
10-Mar: checked identity-inventory logs: Pub/Sub ack for cust-123 topics present, but worker reported "skipped - unknown resource type" for the message payload containing serviceAccount.create event.
11-Mar: hypothesis A - deserializer in inventory rejects new SA events when payload contains additional 'labels' field introduced by onboarding script (edge-case schema mismatch).
11-Mar: hypothesis B - race between event processing and full-sync TTL pruning: if worker sees transient resource missing it prunes, and subsequent persistence uses older index snapshot.
11-Mar: confirmed GCP audit shows create event at 14:02:11Z; pubsub delivery 14:02:22Z; inventory worker processed at 14:02:23Z and logged 'skipped - unknown resource type'.
12-Mar: pulled worker binary v1.9.7; deserializer change in v1.9.6 added strict schema checks for labels field. Onboarding script added a new 'redwood_onboard' label in customer template on 2026-03-09.
Sophie Nguyen (Support) 2026-03-10: Initial ticket opened after SE reported repeated provisioning failures for cust-123 during onboarding.
Diego Ramirez (Infra) 2026-03-10: Assigned for triage. Will reproduce in staging and check inventory worker logs and deserializer behavior.
Diego Ramirez (Infra) 2026-03-11: Reproduced in staging. Inventory worker v1.9.7 skipped event due to schema validation error. See log excerpt: 'event_deserialize_error: unknown field "labels" in serviceAccount.create payload'
Priya Shah (Onboarding SE) 2026-03-11: We added the 'redwood_onboard' label to onboarding scripts last week. That label is meant to help troubleshooting; didn't expect it to break inventory.
Diego Ramirez (Infra) 2026-03-11: Immediate workaround: revert onboarding script to not inject label or run a manual full sync after SA creation. Implemented temporary manual sync for cust-123; provisioning succeeded thereafter.
Ella Park (Security) 2026-03-12: Confirmed no security impact; label content non-sensitive. Recommend adjusting deserializer to accept unknown labels rather than failing.
Diego Ramirez (Infra) 2026-03-12: Pushing a hotfix PR to identity-inventory to relax strict schema checks and log unknown fields instead of erroring. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-inventory/pull/1124
Manual trigger of a full identity-inventory sync for the customer's project after SA creation. Revert onboarding label injection for immediate onboarding runs.
Hotfix merged to relax deserializer schema validation (log unknown fields instead of rejecting). Deployment scheduled to prod identity-inventory on 2026-03-13. Follow-up: bump integration tests to include onboarding labels and add end-to-end test for create-then-provision within 10s window.
Deploy identity-inventory v1.9.8 with deserializer fix to canary and monitor for missed SAs (2026-03-13).
Add integration test coverage for new label fields and sub-10s create->provision race condition (owner: infra/testing).
Update onboarding scripts to avoid adding non-essential labels until inventory compatibility is confirmed (owner: SE).
Schedule brief postmortem and add checklist item in onboarding runbook for verifying identity indexing (owner: ops).
payload.summary: Ephemeral IAM inventory mismatch: newly created GCP service account not indexed by cross-cloud broker causing AWS assume-role failures

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple employees on macOS laptops that are docked (USB-C dock providing wired Ethernet) are observing intermittent failures when calling internal Kubernetes-backed APIs (gRPC timeouts and 502s from the auth-proxy). Impact: Broad internal impact for office-based employees using the docked wired interface; affects engineers and support staff. Suspected root cause: laptops are receiving a duplicate default gateway via DHCP on both the VPN interface and the dock Ethernet with conflicting route metrics, producing asymmetric paths to our k8s cluster nodes which drop TCP connections from unexpected return paths. Timing: Started 2026-03-10 09:20 PST after a DHCP lease policy change rolled to the branch site DHCP server.
1) Connect MacBook to office Wi-Fi + WireGuard VPN and confirm normal behaviour
2) Plug USB-C dock with wired Ethernet (DHCP) into laptop while VPN is active
3) Run: ipconfig getifaddr en0; netstat -rn; scutil --dns to inspect route/gateway configuration
4) Attempt to curl internal-config-api (gRPC) or open /internal/dashboard and observe intermittent 502s / timeouts
5) Run tcpdump on laptop (udp/tcp) and on k8s node to observe SYN from one interface and SYN-ACK returning to a different interface.
6) Reproducible when dock Ethernet and VPN both advertise default route with equal metric and asymmetric return traffic occurs.
gRPC connections to internal-config-api either timeout after retries or return immediate connection resets. Traceroute from laptop shows outbound packets going via VPN tunnel but return packets to k8s node reach the office gateway then back to the dock interface, causing stateful firewall on the node/edge to drop the connection. Intermittent: 30-70% of requests fail under load.
Packets for established sessions should follow symmetric paths so that TCP state is preserved. When VPN is active, return traffic for internal API connections should flow through the same interface and tunnel the request was sent on, preserving connection state and preventing firewall drops.
laptop tcpdump snippet: SYN src 10.66.12.34:54328 -> 10.10.5.12:443; SYN-ACK src 10.10.5.12:443 -> 10.66.12.34:54328 received on different local IP
k8s node iptables: conntrack shows ESTABLISHED entries with mismatched src/dst pair causing resets
vpn logs (wireguard): peer shows inbound packet but no corresponding conntrack entry on node side
dhcp server lease change log (branch-dhcp-02): 2026-03-10T09:15:21 - rolled new default-gateway metric option to ethernet scope
09:35 - Collected netstat -rn from affected host: two default routes present, one via wg0 (10.66.0.1) and one via en3 (192.168.50.1) with identical precedence metric -> kernel chooses based on interface ordering, causing flips.
10:00 - Confirmed DHCP change on branch DHCP cluster rolled a new option that made wired interface advertise default-gateway and metric 0 (previously metric 100), resulting in identical metrics across interfaces.
10:30 - Reproduced locally: ip route show table main demonstrates alternating next-hop based on interface binding, traceroute confirms asymmetric return path.
11:05 - Hypothesis: stateful firewall rules / conntrack at k8s node validate reverse path; unexpected return source IP causes connection reset. This matches observed SYN/SYN-ACK mismatch in tcpdump.

Issue summary: After the scheduled cutover of the inference compiler and pinning the dedicated customer's fleet to redwood-7b-quant-v2, SlateDocs reported elevated chat session startup latency. Impact: customers see 5–12s TTFB for the first streaming token; some sessions time out at 30s and retry logic triggers duplicate streams. Scope: affects ~8% of requests from the customer's dedicated pool in us-east following the 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC deployment. This appears correlated with the compiler handoff and model binary swap.

Observed user-facing symptoms: slow initial handshake, delayed first byte, intermittent 504s for chat streaming, and increased request duration tail.

Why this ticket exists: to capture support investigation, mitigation steps applied, and remediation plan for the customer and internal stakeholders.
Create a chat session against customer's dedicated endpoint (prod/us-east) using SDK v2 with streaming=true
Send a short prompt (e.g., 'Summarize: Redwood platform advantages')
Observe time between request and first streaming token; repeat ~50 times to surface distribution
Optionally toggle model pin to prior variant to compare (redwood-7b-quant-v1)
api_gateway: request_id=az7-991, latency=11.8s, upstream_status=200, bytes_sent=512
serving-runtime: session_init_ms p50=1200 p90=8200 p99=11500 (post-cutover baseline pre-cutover p99=2200)
compiler: kernel_swap events spike at 2026-03-10T02:03:12Z concurrent_with model_loads=24
scheduler: batch_wait_ms increased from median 5ms to 320ms for dedicated pool nodes
kafka/metrics: routing_failures increased by 3x around cutover window
customer logs: client recorded stream handshake start then no bytes until 9–12s; multiple clients logged 'stream timed out after 30s' followed by auto-retry
03/10 03:15 UTC - Initial triage by Support: confirmed customer repro and captured traces; escalated to SRE and runtime on-call
03/10 04:00 UTC - SRE: checked node CPU/GPU metrics; no sustained GPU saturation but CPU-steal on some nodes during model loads
03/10 05:10 UTC - Runtime Eng: observed increased KV cache misses immediately after compiler swap, resulting in extra RT operations for prefix handling
03/10 06:30 UTC - Network: no packet loss on VPC level; TLS handshake times normal; hints point to in-process stall rather than external network
03/11 09:20 UTC - Hypothesis #1: kernel selection path introduced an extra synchronous I/O on first request to a freshly-loaded model which blocks streaming initiation
03/11 12:00 UTC - Hypothesis #2: scheduler batching threshold changed in compiler roll that increased initial batch wait time for low-QPS sessions in dedicated pools
03/12 14:00 UTC - Mitigation test: forced fallback to prior compiler runtime on a canary node; TTFB p99 dropped to ~2.4s on canary vs 10.9s on upgraded nodes
03/12 16:45 UTC - Correlation: incidents match nodes that experienced concurrent model cold loads plus kernel swap events
A newly-introduced synchronous kernel initialization path in the compiler cutover caused blocking on the serving thread during first token emission when combined with concurrent model binary swaps and cold KV cache state. This increased batch wait times for small sessions and manifested as elevated TTFB and streaming timeouts for affected dedicated pool nodes.
Rolled back the compiler change on the customer's dedicated pool nodes and applied a hotfix that converts the kernel init path to async+prefetch. After rollback and hotfix rollout to the pool, TTFB p99 returned to prior levels (~2s). Deployed canary test to validate fix before wide rollout. Customer notified and incident mitigation steps documented.
For immediate relief, we temporarily pinned the customer's dedicated pool to the previous runtime image (compiler-v1.14) and disabled eager kernel swap on low-QPS nodes. Customers on hosted tiers are unaffected by that pin. Documented steps provided to CS for reconfiguration.

SRE-1210: Add an alert for 'serving-runtime.session_init_ms p99 > 3s' for dedicated pools
DX-404: Update runbook with steps to pin runtime image and disable eager kernel swap
QA-678: Add regression tests that simulate concurrent model load + compiler swap with low-QPS sessions

Issue summary:
Product Partnerships requested a reusable automation (Partner Collaboration Gateway) that provisions a scoped, timebound collaboration environment for external partners: a Slack channel (private, invited guests), a Confluence dossier pre-populated with templates and an audit manifest, and a corresponding Jira project template for action items. The automation must enforce RBAC, run a PII redaction pass on exported content before long-term storage, and automatically archive + export assets at a configurable TTL.

Impact:
- Manual channel/space provisioning for partners is error-prone and inconsistent; setup time averages 3+ days.
- Security team wants per-channel audit manifests and automated PII redaction on exports to meet data-sharing agreements.
- Partnerships team wants a self-service button to create partner workspaces with built-in templates and timebound guest access.

Request details / requirements:
1) Self-service 'Create Partner Workspace' endpoint in the admin console that creates: Slack private channel (prefixed partner-<org>), Confluence space with the Partner Dossier template, and a Jira project with issue templates.
2) Approval guardrail: creation requires one Approver from Security or Legal; requests enter an approval queue.
3) RBAC snapshots: capture membership and permission sets at creation and on closure for audit.
4) TTL lifecycle: workspace expires after N days (configurable per request); on expiry run export pipeline: redact PII, generate an audit log bundle, upload to secure archive, then archive/delete workspace.
5) PII scrubber: integrate an existing redaction microservice or run a redaction lambda to remove/replace emails, phone numbers, SSNs, and API keys from channel history and Confluence pages in the export.
6) Slack policy: limit guest invites to enumerated domains; prevent file uploads from guests if requested by partner.
7) Observability: create an event log (created_by, approver, TTL, snapshot location) and surface in console under 'Partner Workspaces'.

Acceptance criteria:
- Admin console exposes a form and returns a request id.
- Approved requests result in Slack channel + Confluence space + Jira project being provisioned within 15 minutes.
- RBAC snapshot stored in secure audit S3 with link in Jira issue.
- Export pipeline produces a zipped export and redaction report; report confirms no PII pattern matches remaining.
- Demo run completed with Partner Beta group (3 partners) and Security signoff.

Additional notes:
Identified existing building blocks: Slack provisioning via SCIM + Slack admin API; Confluence space templates exist for Partner Dossier (confluence key: PART-DOSSIER); internal redaction microservice 'redact-svc' is experimental and only supports email/phone - needs extension for API keys/SSNs.
Slack export constraints: workspace export requires Enterprise export privileges; channel export for private channels must use Conversations.history with token of a workspace admin and obey rate limits (recommended: 1 req/sec with exponential backoff).
Confluence export: Use 'export space' API which returns HTML/XML; we should run redaction on HTML text nodes, then re-package as a sanitized archive.
RBAC snapshot plan: capture Slack channel membership via Conversations.members at creation, Confluence space permissions via space API, and Jira project roles via REST API; store JSON manifests in secure audit bucket with signed links in Jira issue metadata.
Approval flow options: (A) use existing Jira approval workflow with Security approver group; (B) use a small self-serve portal that posts an approval request to #security-approvals and waits for a +1. Recommend (A) for auditability.
Data retention & TTL: default 90 days TTL; allow partners to request longer TTLs (requires Legal signoff).
2026-03-12 - Workplan established, dependencies mapped. Next steps: implement PoC for incremental Slack + Confluence export with redact-svc integration. Security to expand redact-svc capabilities and provide test patterns. Platform to build console form and a Jira-based approval webhook.
Temporary workaround for immediate partner onboarding: manual provisioning checklist created in Confluence + RBAC snapshot saved manually to secure audit bucket. Use manual redaction by Security on exports until automated scrubber is ready.
Owner: Omar Kim (Platform) responsible for end-to-end delivery; Security owner: Luis Fernandez; SRE: Tara Nguyen for export reliability and rate limiting.
payload.summary: Provision partner collaboration gateway: gated Slack channels + ephemeral Confluence dossier + PII-scrubbing export

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers on Private deployments behind an appliance WAF (mod_security variant) observe SSE streams cut off mid-response for outputs containing large embedded payloads (long base64 inline images or multi-thousand-token code blocks). After the TCP teardown the client reconnects and the platform attempts an SSE resume, but the resumed stream lacks the final terminal event ("[DONE]"/closing JSON chunk). In addition the customer's conversational state shows the user message duplicated once after the reconnect, causing downstream logic to run the same generation twice.

Impact:
- AcmeHealth production users intermittently receive truncated assistant responses (missing closing bracket or end marker) for long responses.
- Reconnects sometimes cause duplicated user entries in conversation state, triggering duplicate side effects in the customer's application (e.g., duplicate DB writes).
- Incident spikes are correlated with large payload responses and occur only when the customer's WAF is enabled in their VPC path.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC with sidecar edge proxy)
- Region: us-west-2
- Model: redwood/gptx-13b-quantized-v2 pinned by customer
- WAF: third-party appliance (customer reports ModSecurity ruleset customized)

Expected behavior:
- SSE stream produces final terminal event and client receives complete JSON/markdown output.
- Resume should reattach and continue without duplicating conversation-turns in convstate.

Actual behavior:
- Upstream connection receives a FIN from the WAF path when a large data chunk is emitted. Redwood edge proxy logs 200 then short TCP FIN from downstream; platform sees abrupt EOF.
- Resume path sends a resume delta but the delta processor drops the terminal event in a race with connection-close handling.
- Session-token rotation logic during resume causes a duplicated user-turn entry in conv state for some sessions.

1) Customer config: private deployment with edge-sidecar routing through WAF appliance that performs content inspection.
2) Use chat completion with long output: include a large base64 inline image (~80KB) or ask for multi-file code output (~3000 tokens).
3) Observe stream from client: stream runs for ~2-6s then connection terminates with truncated JSON; client reconnects and requests resume.
4) Check conversation history via customer API: sometimes the original user message appears twice and the assistant output remains incomplete on first resume attempt.

edge-proxy (us-west-2) tail:
2026-03-10T15:04:32.123Z INFO  conn_id=abc123 client=10.1.4.22 upstream=10.2.9.10 status=200 bytes_sent=81920
2026-03-10T15:04:34.859Z WARN  conn_id=abc123 downstream=10.1.4.1 event=received_FIN_from_downstream reason=WAF_close_on_inspection
2026-03-10T15:04:34.861Z ERROR conn_id=abc123 stream_id=st-789 abrupt_eof detected; resume_token=rt-55a drop_flag=true
2026-03-10T15:04:35.002Z INFO  session_resume session=usr-42 resume_request=received; delta_seq=1024
2026-03-10T15:04:35.004Z ERROR resume_processor session=usr-42 dropped_terminal_event race=conn_close_handler
2026-03-10T15:04:35.150Z INFO  convstate update session=usr-42 user_message_id=msg-900 duplicated=true

Customer-side WAF logs (redacted):
2026-03-10T15:04:34 Rule 942100 matched pattern payload_size > 65536 -> action=close_connection (silently drop)

2026-03-10 16:10 - Support (Aisha Kaplan): Initial report from AcmeHealth. Customer pasted streaming transcript and edge-proxy logs. Customer reports duplicated user messages correlated with reconnects.
2026-03-10 17:01 - Eng (Tomas Rivera): Reproduced locally with WAF rule simulator. Observed FIN sequence from simulated WAF during large buffer flush. Filed reproduce harness in repo and linked PRs.
2026-03-11 08:33 - SRE (Maya Chen): Noted that resume delta processing uses a non-blocking cleanup path that can run concurrently with conn-close; race can drop final event. Added instrumentation to resume_processor to capture terminal_event lifecycle.
2026-03-11 12:44 - Customer (AcmeHealth - Anil Patel): Provided sample request payload and confirmed mitigation when decreasing inline image size below 64KB. Asks for recommended workaround until fix is deployed.
2026-03-12 09:20 - Eng (Tomas Rivera): Patch candidate created to serialize resume delta finalize step with conn-close handler. PR attached to linked_github_prs. Planning rollout to private channel for validation.
2026-03-12 13:02 - Support (Aisha Kaplan): Notified customer of in-progress fix and recommended immediate workaround: avoid embedding base64 > 64KB or enable WAF passthrough for streaming endpoints.
Findings summary:
- Root cause: interplay of customer WAF terminating downstream TCP on large payloads and a race in our resume_processor that finalizes terminal events asynchronously. When the conn-close handler and resume finalizer interleave, terminal event emission may be dropped.
- Secondary issue: session-token rotation during resume flow can cause convstate append to run twice if resume ack path is retried; this is a separate race in session-store write-after-ack code path.
- Reproducible with WAF simulator and large streaming payload (>= ~65KB chunk emitted).
- Affected only in Private deployments where an intermediate appliance can issue a silent teardown; Hosted customers not impacted because our edge removes/controls WAF behavior.

Telemetry:
- ~12 confirmed incidents this week for AcmeHealth, correlated to payload size and rule 942100 in their WAF.

Mitigation implemented in two parts:
1) Immediate customer workaround recommended: reduce inline base64 attachments > 64KB or configure WAF to allow passthrough for /resume and streaming endpoints. Customer acknowledged and applied temporary WAF override.
2) Engineering fix: serialized finalize() in resume_processor to ensure terminal event is emitted or transactionally recorded before connection cleanup begins. Added idempotent guards to convstate append to prevent duplicate user-turns on retries.
3) Patch rollout: patched edge-proxy and resume_processor; integration tests added to simulate WAF-driven FIN and validate terminal emission. Patch PRs: edge-proxy/pull/721 and serving-runtime/pull/1184.

Deployment plan:
- Canary deploy to private customers who opt-in for next 48h.
- Monitor metrics: stream_terminal_emitted ratio and convstate_duplicate_rate.
- If canary is green, schedule global private-channel rollout next week.

1) Avoid embedding large inline base64 blobs in streaming responses. If images are necessary, return a hosted URL instead of inline base64.
2) In customer WAF, whitelist or passthrough streaming endpoints (/v1/stream, /v1/resume) and disable size-based silent-close rules for those paths.
3) Short term: use non-streaming completion API for very large outputs until patch is validated.
payload.summary: SSE stream terminated by customer WAF on large payloads; resume omits closing token and reconnect duplicates user prompt in convstate

payload.description:
Issue summary:
CI (terraform) provisioning step that creates a KMS KeyRing and CMEK key in project redwood-prod-dedicated failed with org-policy DENY on keyRing.create and serviceAccount.impersonate. This blocks onboarding of analytics-replicator-sa for Dedicated environment and prevents terraform apply from completing.

Impact:
- New Dedicated capacity onboarding is blocked (analytics-replicator service) delaying customer migration.
- CI pipeline failing on every run; engineers cannot complete infra changes requiring CMEK.
- Risk of manual key creation and out-of-band grants if not resolved quickly.

Environment:
- GCP project: redwood-prod-dedicated
- CI: github-actions self-hosted runners in prod-us-west
- Terraform version: 1.6.8; google provider: 4.79.0
- Affected regions: us-west1 (primary), us-east1 (replica)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Checkout branch infra/cmek/onboard-analytics
2. Trigger CI workflow .github/workflows/provision-cmek.yaml or run `terraform apply` with service account impersonation from the runner.
3. Observe error during `google_kms_key_ring` creation step.

Observed logs / errors:
- iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob denied for impersonation attempts (logs attached in CI run).
- Error: "googleapi: Error 403: Permission 'resourcemanager.projects.create' denied by organization policy 'constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation'" (note: message varies depending on provider call).
- Audit log excerpt: orgpolicy.v1 DenyViolation on projects/redwood-prod-dedicated: constraint=constraints/gcp.restrictResourceCreation, denied_action=cloudkms.keyRings.create

Investigation notes:
- Org policy audit shows a recently-applied policy (GCP Org Policy: restrictResourceCreation -> permittedResources limited to team-managed projects) that blocks programmatic creation of KMS KeyRings unless the request originates from a whitelisted principal.
- CI runner uses impersonation of ci-service-sa to perform terraform; the org-policy expects either an approved infra-service account or a signed approval tag on the request.
- Cross-referenced with INT-572913 which flagged a similar deny pattern for a different project; that ticket included an org-policy change by Security on 2026-03-01.
- Hypothesis: Security applied a tightened policy during the compliance sweep; Dedicated onboarding path did not get the required exception.

Temporary mitigation / workaround:
- Manual creation: Infra can manually create the KeyRing and CMEK via an owner account and then grant the required roles to analytics-replicator-sa. This is sensitive and requires audit entry and rotation plan.
- Alternative: run Terraform with a privileged admin service account (not recommended long-term) and then reduce privileges after provisioning.

Proposed remediation steps:
1. Confirm with Security whether the org-policy change on 2026-03-01 is intentional for all projects or scoped to org-folder.
2. If intentional, request a scoped exception for projects/redwood-prod-dedicated for the resource types cloudkms.keyRings.create and cloudkms.cryptoKeys.create for the infra provisioning principal (ci-provisioner-sa) for 48 hours to allow onboarding.
3. Update infra onboarding docs to include the required pre-created resources and the approved SA impersonation list.
4. Post-fix: run terraform apply from CI and validate audit logs show the provisioning principal and not a human owner.
5. If exception is not approved, plan documented manual provisioning runbook and AM/PM rotation for keys.

Next steps / owners:
- Reach out to Security (tag: @security-org-policies) to validate policy intent and request exception.
- Infra/Platform (assignee Priya Natarajan) to prepare justification and minimum-scope exception request and to test manual create steps if required.
- Compliance to log the manual intervention if chosen.

SLA notes:
- Customer impact: internal onboarding delay only, but flagged P1 due to pipeline-blocking nature.
- First response due by: 2026-03-10 (same day triage).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several devices returned from depot repair are exhibiting repeated MECM client policy oscillation and failing AAD hybrid join intermittently. Suspected root cause is duplicate Machine SID left on disk image leading to identity collisions in on-prem inventory and policy evaluation.
Multiple users (approx 12 devices observed) unable to complete policy-driven provisioning steps. Affected machines receive conflicting MECM assignments causing service config churn, blocking application deployment and onboarding checks. No external customer impact, internal fleet only.
1) Reimage device using depot standard image produced on 2026-03-05 build
2) Run sysprep/clone sequence used by depot team (observed step that preserves SID),
3) Device checks into MECM and attempts Hybrid AAD join
4) Observe MECM client policy flipping between 'CompanyResourceConfig' and 'WorkstationBaseline' every ~5-10 minutes
5) Hybrid AAD join often times out or reports 'device already exists' during token exchange
MECM client shows rapid policy re-evaluation. AAD join fails with HTTP 409 / deviceConflict or times out after retries. Inventory in assetdb shows duplicated machine_identifier and identical machine SID values for two different asset tags (one repaired unit and another active unit).
Each reimaged device should receive a fresh, unique Machine SID and stable MECM policy assignment. Hybrid AAD join should complete on first attempt and device should appear once in assetdb with correct asset tag.
MECM client log: PolicyAgent::EvaluatePolicy - lastPolicyId=abc123 newPolicyId=def456 (flip)
AAD join log: HybridJoinService - 409 DeviceConflict: existingDeviceId=asset-49321 incomingDeviceId=asset-50218
imaging script output: sysprep step skipped due to marker file /var/local/skip_sysprep (unexpected)
assetdb: machine_sid= S-1-5-21-1122334455-66778899-10101010 appears on asset-49321 and asset-50218
Initial triage by onsite depot engineer confirmed that a custom disk preparation hook was introduced in the 2026-03-05 image that avoids SID regeneration for perceived faster provisioning. We identified a 'skip_sysprep' marker being created by a deprecated OEM script during NVMe firmware update step. Cross-checked assetdb historical records and found collisions between devices that had overlapping manufacturing serial batches.
OEM provisioning hook intended to accelerate imaging inadvertently bypasses sysprep/SID reset when NVMe firmware flash completes. That leaves duplicate SIDs in the fleet causing MECM and AAD identity collisions.
1) Quarantine affected devices by moving them to MECM collection 'Repair-Quarantine' which disables automated deployments until SID reset.
1) Boot device to WinPE, run 'sysprep /generalize' to regenerate Machine SID and re-run OOBE
2) Re-enroll device into MECM and re-run hybrid join script
3) Confirm unique machine_sid in assetdb and stable policy assignment for 1 hour
1) Suspend deployment of 2026-03-05 imaging build and audit other recent images for skip_sysprep marker
2) File PR to imaging-scripts to remove OEM 'fast-nvme' hook and ensure sysprep always runs after firmware flashes
3) Run fleet-wide scan query in assetdb to locate duplicate machine_sid entries and schedule remediation
4) Update depot runbook to include SID validation post-repair
5) Notify service desk and depot teams and schedule a hotfix window
Root cause postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-15 10:00 PT
Action owner: Priya Desai - remove fast-nvme hook (imaging-scripts) and add automated SID check
Action owner: Depot lead - reimage affected inventory and confirm enrollment

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - DepotEng (Rafael Ortega): Found OEM NVMe flash hook added to post-image phase. Will stop pipelines temporarily and provide patched image by EOD.
2026-03-12 - SRE (Maya Patel): Ran fleet dup-sid query; found 18 matches across last 30 days. Created MECM collection 'Repair-Quarantine' and applied hold policy.

Issue summary:
After a deployment of the new LDAP bridge (v2.3.4) on 2026-03-12 02:40 UTC, multiple users reported that recently granted Okta group memberships were not reflected in Redwood RBAC. The reconciliation job appears to skip group updates that the bridge just wrote.

Impact:
- Several oncall and infra service accounts did not receive elevated roles for ~30-90 minutes after group changes.
- Affected internal consoles: analytics-portal, observability-runbooks, infra-deploy.
- Users experienced 403s when attempting role-elevation flows and just-in-time access.

Environment:
- prod - us-west (identity-sync cluster ids: id-sync-3, id-sync-4)
- LDAP bridge v2.3.4 (new release, change: timestamp serialization refactor)

Steps to reproduce:
1. In Okta, add a test user (jdoe-test) to the "oncall-rotate" group via the admin UI.
2. Observe SCIM/LDAP provisioning logs in identity-bridge.
3. Trigger RBAC reconciliation (manually via /admin/reconcile or wait for periodic job).
4. Check user role assignment in Redwood console and test elevation flows.

Observed behavior:
- identity-bridge logs show group update events with lastUpdated=1650001234567
- RBAC reconciler treats timestamps as epoch seconds; when it parses 1650001234567 it interprets as 1.650001234567e+12 seconds (far future), causing the reconciler to mark the record as "not ready for reconciliation" and skip processing.
- Reconciliation resumes only after a periodic backstop that clamps dates, causing ~30–90m delay.

Expected behavior:
- Timestamps from the LDAP bridge should be serialized in seconds (1650001234) or reconciler should robustly detect ms vs s. Group changes should be applied within normal reconcile window (<30s).

Logs / Evidence:
- identity-bridge id-sync-3 log excerpt (2026-03-12T02:42:11Z): "groupChange: user=jdoe-test group=oncall-rotate lastUpdated=1650001234567"
- rbac-reconciler log (2026-03-12T02:45:05Z): "skip: incoming_ts > future_threshold: 1650001234567"
- User ticket: several 403 screenshots attached in support thread #support (Slack).

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 03:35 - SRE: Confirmed reconciler codebase assumes seconds (int64) and lacks guardrails for >1e11 values; unit test coverage missing for extreme timestamp values.
2026-03-12 05:00 - Security: Verified no privilege escalation occurred; delay caused temporary denial for intended role holders but no unauthorized grants.
2026-03-12 04:30 - SRE oncall (Anjali Rao): Deployed reconciler patch to tolerate ms timestamps (clamps >1e11 to ms->s conversion) as a safety measure; added metric to track 'future_ts_skips'.
Mitigated: rolled back the id-sync-3 instance to v2.3.3 to stop new malformed timestamps. Deployed immediate reconciler tolerant parse for ms values to prevent future skips. Hotfix merged into identity-bridge (PR #1287) and rolled out to prod canary on 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC, full rollout 2026-03-12 11:30 UTC. Follow-up: add strict timestamp schema validation in bridge, add unit tests for ms/vs-s handling, and create alert on 'future_ts_skips' metric.
payload.summary: LDAP bridge timestamp unit mismatch causes RBAC reconciliation to skip recent group changes

Issue summary:
Users on corporate Wi‑Fi intermittently finish 802.1X/EAP authentication but are placed into the guest VLAN by the NAC server. Devices in guest VLAN cannot complete VPN onboarding (agent registration + device cert fetch), causing blocked access to internal services and failed onboarding flows for new hires and reprovisioned devices.

Impact:
- Affects ~12% of onboarding attempts in corp Wi‑Fi during business hours in us-east-1; affects both macOS and Windows devices.
- New hire device provisioning fails to retrieve device certs; SSO flows time out.
- Customer-facing demo environment unreachable when presenters use corp Wi‑Fi.

Environment:
- SSID: Redwood-Corp-Enterprise (802.1X, WPA2/WPA3 transition)
- NAC: ClearAccess v4.2 (RADIUS proxy + policy engine)
- RADIUS backend: FreeRADIUS cluster behind haproxy (auth and CoA)
- Identity provider: Okta SSO -> RADIUS proxy (EAP-TLS and EAP-PEAP tested)
- VPN: WireGuard-based zero-trust agent with onboarding over TLS to onboarding.redwood.internal:443
- Affected clients: macOS 13.x, Windows 11 x64, occasionally Linux dev VMs

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect client to Redwood-Corp-Enterprise SSID and authenticate with EAP-PEAP (username/password) or EAP-TLS cert.
2) Observe RADIUS authentication logs show Accept for user/device.
3) Confirm client gets DHCP & IP on guest VLAN (192.168.240.0/22) instead of corp VLAN (10.20.0.0/16).
4) Attempt agent registration to onboarding.redwood.internal:443 -> connection times out; cert fetch fails.

Observed behavior / logs (excerpt):
- RADIUS server: "Auth: Accept: user=ajones realm=redwood internal="
- NAC policy engine audit: "PolicyDecision: TAG=guest_vlans; assignment=192.168.240.0/22; reason=policy-match: device-profile=unknown, posture=unscanned"
- DHCP logs: "DHCPACK yiaddr=192.168.240.55 to MAC aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff via VLAN 240"
- Onboarding server logs: "TLS handshake from 192.168.240.55 timed out; client failed to present expected bootstrap cert"

Hypothesis:
- NAC policy mis-evaluates posture for successfully authenticated devices causing fallback to guest VLAN when device posture check times out or returns unknown.
- Intermittent timeouts between NAC and posture service (hosted on separate k8s namespace) cause race where authentication completes before posture result arrives, leading to default-to-guest behavior.
- A mismatch in RADIUS CoA handling may fail to move some sessions after posture completes.

Investigation notes:
- 2026-03-12 09:15 (Diego): Correlated increased rates with periodic posture-service GC spikes; saw 5–7s latency spikes in posture API during rolling node autoscaling.
- 2026-03-12 10:02 (Priya): Captured packet trace from AP showing Access-Accept followed by RADIUS Change-of-Auth not applied for session 0x7a3f.
- 2026-03-12 11:30 (SRE): Hapoxy logs show occasional 503s to posture-service endpoints during scale events; backlog of requests queued.
- 2026-03-12 12:00 (Network Eng): NAC policy has explicit default assignment to guest VLAN when posture result absent after 3s.
- 2026-03-12 12:45 (Security): Reviewed recent NAC policy change (#472) that lowered posture hold-time to 3s to reduce auth latency for BYOD; this increases chance of defaulting to guest.

Temporary workaround applied:
- 2026-03-12 13:10 (Priya): Increased posture hold-time back to 8s via runtime flag on NAC policy engine cluster (deployed config patch ci-ops/patch-2026-03-12).
- 2026-03-12 13:15 (SRE): Scaled posture-service HPA min replicas from 2 -> 4 to reduce tail latency.
- Result: Guest VLAN misassignment rate dropped from ~12% to ~1.5% in the monitoring window (10:00–14:00).

Next steps and action items:
- Short term (Priority): Patch NAC policy repo to set posture hold-time to 8s permanently and add feature flag gating (#priv-ops-553). Owner: Priya Shah. ETA: 2026-03-14.
- Medium term: Improve posture-service autoscaling to rely on CPU+queue length and add readiness probe to avoid sending requests during GC/scale windows. Owner: SRE team (linked PRs). ETA: 2026-03-21.
- Long term: Update onboarding flow to support re-provisioning via HTTP proxy fallback when devices land in guest VLAN temporarily and to support CoA retries when posture completes. Owner: Security/Infra. ETA: Q2 2026.

Attachments: packet captures, haproxy logs, NAC policy audit snippets available in linked Confluence page and s3://redwood-support/INT-531234/

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:45 - SRE Team (sre-oncall): Found GC spikes on posture-service causing 5–10s tail latency. Scaling to 4 replicas reduced error rates. We recommend increasing hold-time on NAC.
2026-03-12 17:05 - Security (Amira Liao): Confirmed this change reduces risk of leaving corporate devices in guest VLAN. We should document CoA retry behavior and add test coverage for posture latencies.
Timeline shows correlation between posture-service latency spikes and spike in guest VLAN assignments.
Haproxy logs show 503s to posture endpoints during cluster GC/resize windows.
Packet capture demonstrates Access-Accept followed by no CoA and DHCP assignment on guest net.
Recent change lowered posture hold-time to 3s; revert to 8s reduces misassignments.
Noticed AP firmware 5.6.x had inconsistent CoA behavior; recommend upgrade to 5.7.2+ where CoA handling improved.
Temporary mitigation: increased NAC posture hold-time to 8s and scaled posture-service to reduce tail latency (2026-03-12).
Permanent fix in progress: PR created to update NAC policy repo to 8s hold-time and add configurable default behavior; add regression test for posture latency windows. Owner: Priya Shah. ETA 2026-03-14 deployment to staging.
SRE will implement improved HPA metrics and readiness probe for posture-service to avoid serving during GC/scale events. Owner: SRE. ETA 2026-03-21.
Network team to validate CoA handling on AP firmware 5.7.2+ and schedule upgrade for devices still on 5.6.x.
payload.summary: RADIUS NAC VLAN misattribution: EAP authentication succeeds but guest VLAN applied, blocking VPN onboarding

Issue summary:
A support engineer received an alert from the automation-queue consumer that a vendor DOCX uploaded to the partner intake bucket contained an embedded JSON Web Token (JWT). The ingest automation parsed the DOCX for metadata and inadvertently extracted the token which matched our internal automation matcher, triggering an automatic temporary service-account creation and granting of limited IAM roles.

Impact:
- One temporary service-account (sa-temp-0342) was auto-provisioned and used by downstream CI automation for ~7 minutes before flagged by monitoring.
- No sensitive data access logs observed beyond the automation's expected behavior (list and get on non-sensitive config buckets).
- Potential for an attacker to weaponize similar uploads to trigger unwanted provisioning.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (automation queue, ingest-service v3.2.7, iam-provisioner v1.8.0)
- Partner intake S3-like bucket: s3://partners-ingest-prod

Steps to reproduce (initial):
1) Vendor uploads DOCX to partners-ingest-prod via partner-form API.
2) ingest-service extracts text and looks for structured tokens per metadata matcher.
3) Extracted token matched automation rule: "provision-temporary-service-account" and invoked iam-provisioner.
4) iam-provisioner created sa-temp-0342 and attached role:iam.read-only-temp.

Observed evidence / logs:
- ingest-service log (2026-03-13T09:12:16Z): "extracted_metadata: {\"embedded\":true, \"payload_preview\":\"eyJhbGciOiJI...\" }"
- automation-queue trace id: aq-20260313-9a7c
- iam-provisioner audit (2026-03-13T09:12:22Z): "created serviceAccount sa-temp-0342 by automation-rule 'provision-temporary-service-account'"
- CloudTrail-like logs: role assignment and limited get/list calls from sa-temp-0342 from IP 18.215.42.33 (AWS AZ us-east-1a)

Immediate actions taken:
- Blocked automation rule "provision-temporary-service-account" (rolled to false) at 09:18:00Z.
- Rotated token/signing keys used by the ingest metadata matcher to prevent reuse.
- Revoked sa-temp-0342 and removed IAM bindings at 09:20:35Z.
- Snapshot of partner object (partners-ingest-prod/v2026-03-13/vendor-8923.docx) copied to investigator bucket for forensics.

Evidence artifacts location:
- investigator bucket: s3://sec-investigations/INT-612345/
- automation trace: aq-20260313-9a7c
- ingest-service logs: splunk://redwood/prod/ingest-service/2026-03-13

Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-13T09:32:00Z: Raised after on-call alert. Attaching initial logs and object path. Requesting security triage.
Jordan Kim (Assignee) 2026-03-13T09:40:12Z: We've paused the rule and revoked the account. Pulling full audit trail; adding SRE and SecOps to thread.
Maya Singh (SecOps) 2026-03-13T10:05:03Z: Forensics pulled the DOCX. Appears the token is base64 and wrapped in an HTML comment inside the docx XML. No evidence yet of exfil prior to provisioning. Collecting file hashes and vendor metadata.
Evan Brooks (SRE) 2026-03-13T10:22:45Z: Noted a spike of 3 provisioning events matching the same matcher in the last 48 hours. Correlating with partner uploads from vendor-8923 IP range.
Jordan Kim 2026-03-13T14:01:00Z: Adding mitigation plan: input sanitization on ingest-service, stricter matching, and require operator approval for any rule-triggered IAM provisioning. Draft PR ready.
Maya Singh 2026-03-14T08:15:00Z: Confirmed no lateral movement. File contains a JWT with a claim set pointing to an external URL; token signature uses HMAC with leaked shared key (rotated now). Recommend forcing rotation across other automations using same matcher.
09:45: Evidence: DOCX internal XML showed <!--TOKEN: eyJhbGciOiJI...--> inside word/document.xml. The ingest parser treats HTML comments as safe text and included in metadata extraction.
11:10: Hypothesis: An attacker embedded tokens in commonly uploaded docs. The provisioning matcher did not validate token origin or require operator confirmation for high-cost actions.
12:30: Confirmed two other vendor uploads from same vendor account earlier this week that contained similarly structured payloads but didn't match the exact regex; we patched regex to be more conservative.
15:00: Correlated provisioning IP 18.215.42.33 to a CI runner previously associated with vendor-8923; vendor outreach initiated to confirm intent.
Next steps: complete PR to require human approval for IAM provisioning; add a sanitization step to strip tokens from extracted text; run a retrospective search for other docs containing 'TOKEN:' pattern across partner buckets.
Partial mitigation applied: automation rule disabled, service-account revoked, signing keys rotated, vendor contacted for explanation. Longer-term controls in progress: input sanitization in ingest-service (PR ready), operator-approval gating for IAM provisioning, monitoring rule to alert on token-like patterns in uploaded artifacts. Ticket will remain open until PR is merged and retrospective search completes.
SEC-1: Merge PR to add sanitization and stricter matching to ingest-service (assigned to infra-team)
SEC-2: Implement operator approval flow in iam-provisioner for rule-based provisioning (assigned to iam-team)
SEC-3: Run retrospective scan across partners-ingest-prod for token-like patterns and report findings (assigned to SecOps)
SEC-4: Vendor outreach complete: get signed attestation from vendor-8923 and rotate their partner API keys if necessary
payload.summary: Embedded JWT in vendor DOCX triggered internal automation to provision temporary service accounts

payload.description:
Issue summary: LyricPay experienced a production outage beginning ~2026-03-12 03:15 UTC where a sudden client retry storm combined with an intermittent DNS failover caused token-queue saturation on the edge gateway. Saturation prevented requests from being admitted into the serving pipeline which in turn pushed bursty load into a subset of GPU pools, triggering autoscaler backpressure, long-tail queuing, increased 5xx responses and streaming stalls for streaming-enabled sessions. Impact: complete request failures and truncated streams for ~40% of LyricPay traffic in us-east-1 for ~2 hours, degraded latency for remaining requests, and noticeable billing spike due to request retries and duplicate completions.
1. Simulate transient DNS failover for edge gateway subdomain (client resolves to new IPs intermittently).
2. Replay high-concurrency client retries with identical session keys and streaming enabled (2000 rps sustained).
3. Observe token admission queues growing on edge gateway and reject rate increase to serving-runtime.
4. Verify autoscaler did not provision capacity quickly due to cooldown policy and detected backpressure propagated to GPU pools.
2026-03-12 03:10 UTC — LyricPay monitoring alerted on increase in 5xx and stream truncation (customer alerted support).
2026-03-12 03:18 UTC — Support acknowledged, P0 declared, SRE and on-call routed to #inc-lyricpay channel.
2026-03-12 03:25 UTC — Investigations pointed to edge-gateway token admission queue growth; DNS flapping observed in client traces.
2026-03-12 03:40 UTC — Applied short-term mitigation: temporary per-customer adaptive throttling and increased edge gateway admission window to drain queues.
2026-03-12 04:05 UTC — Autoscaler parameters relaxed for LyricPay GPU pool; additional reserved nodes brought online (manual scale-up).
2026-03-12 05:30 UTC — Traffic normalized; streaming sessions resumed. Continued monitoring and gradual rollback of emergency limits.
2026-03-12 12:00 UTC — Customer call with LyricPay CS and engineering to review root cause and immediate mitigations.
edge-gateway: token_admit_queue_size spiked to 48k (steady-state ~300) for lyricpay-customer-id
serving-runtime: gpool-us-east-1a queue-lengths exceeded 95th percentile, kernel thrash observed on redwood-7b-quant instances
autoscaler: cooldown prevented scale from +0 -> +8 nodes due to recent sync at 02:58 UTC
dns-resolver: multiple NXDOMAIN/TTL expiry events recorded from LyricPay CDN between 03:12-03:22 UTC
Hypothesis 1: Client-side retry/backoff misconfiguration combined with transient DNS flapping leading to synchronous replay of requests against a small pool of serving nodes.
Hypothesis 2: Edge gateway token admission has a degenerate path when admission queue exceeds threshold that results in rejecting instead of shedding gracefully — explored and reproduced in staging.
Findings: Reproduced admission-queue growth in staging when replaying LyricPay traces; autoscaler cooldown policy kept scale from reacting quickly enough to the burst profile. Edge gateway lacked customer-specific admission shaping which amplified the fan-in.
Impact quantification: Peak affected sessions ~42% of LyricPay traffic; estimated duplicate-completion billing exposure ~0.9% of daily spend for LyricPay (billing team notified).
Aisha Khan (Support) — 2026-03-12: Customer reported streaming sessions truncated and saw increased errors. We escalated to SRE.
SRE On-call (Rita Patel) — 2026-03-12: Confirmed admission-queue spike and DNS anomalies. Initiating temporary per-customer throttling.
Marcelo Ruiz (Infra Eng) — 2026-03-12: Manually increased LyricPay GPU pool by 6 nodes, adjusted autoscaler cooldown to 60s for affected pool. Monitoring continues.
LyricPay Engineering (J. Moreno) — 2026-03-12: We changed client retry logic yesterday; cooperating to share logs and DNS trace. Appreciate the quick mitigation.
Support Lead (Ellen Park) — 2026-03-13: Preparing formal post-incident report and a credit proposal to customer; flagged for billing review.
Immediate: applied per-customer adaptive throttling, increased admission window, and manually scaled LyricPay GPU pool to absorb burst. Autoscaler cooldown temporarily reduced and a short-lived override allowed fast scale-up. Long-term: implemented customer-specific admission shaping, adjusted autoscaler heuristics for bursty retry storms, and added detection rules to alert on token-queue growth earlier. Billing: finance approved a one-time usage credit for LyricPay equal to the estimated duplicate-completion exposure.
1) Engineering: Deploy edge-gateway admission-shaping v1 (customer-scoped token caps) — owner: Marcelo Ruiz — due 2026-03-20.
2) SRE: Update autoscaler runbook and allow emergency override path for dedicated pools — owner: Rita Patel — due 2026-03-18.
3) Telemetry: Add token_admit_queue_size anomaly alert with 5m and 1m thresholds for P0 customers — owner: Observability team — due 2026-03-16.
4) Support/CS: Customer action plan and RCA call summary to be sent to LyricPay, include timeline and credit details — owner: Aisha Khan — due 2026-03-13.
5) Product: Consider public runbook snippets for client retry best-practices in dedicated docs — owner: Product Docs — due 2026-04-01.
payload.summary: LyricPay: token-queue saturation at edge gateway caused GPU pool backpressure, streaming stalls and P0 escalation

comments: 2026-03-09T00:00:00Z Priya Nair: Acknowledged receipt and requested sanitized logs and exact SDK versions.
2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Liam O'Connell: Reproduced in staging with HSM emulator. Scoped to salt swap race across SDKs. Opening engineering follow-up.
2026-03-12T00:00:00Z Priya Nair: Sent customer temporary dedupe recommendations and sample middleware to add idempotency_key in tool metadata.
payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicated external tool executions after a reconnect that occurs concurrently with a hardware-backed idempotency salt rotation. This is a private deployment using an HSM-backed key manager where salt rotations are performed automatically every 24h.

Impact:
- Multiple duplicate downstream webhook/tool executions observed (billing/side-effects).
- Affects long-lived streaming sessions that span a salt rotation window.
- Customer observed 2-3 duplicate callback executions per affected session.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) with HSM KMS integration.
- SDKs in use: Python client v1.9.2, TypeScript client v0.12.0, Go client v0.8.7.
- Region: us-east.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Start a long-lived streaming session that issues an external tool/function call which triggers a downstream webhook (e.g., payment capture).
2) Force a reconnect by throttling the client connection (or trigger a token refresh).
3) Rotate idempotency salt in HSM (customer reproducer rotates salt mid-session).
4) Resume stream; server and SDKs disagree on per-request idempotency hashing, leading to duplicate tool invocation.

Observed behavior:
- When rotation happens during reconnect, the server accepts what client believes to be a retry as a new request (new hash).
- Downstream webhook receives multiple identical execution requests.
- SDK logs show the client re-sending the tool call; server logs show distinct idempotency-hash values for what the client believes is the same logical operation.

Expected behavior:
- Retries and reconnects should be treated as the same logical operation when the client indicates it is a retry (idempotency scope preserved). Salt rotation should not invalidate in-flight retry semantics until apps can observe success/failure.

Customer-provided logs (sanitized):
- client-python: "INFO stream: sending func_call idempotency_key=op-492a; header-salt=base64:AQAB..."
- client-go: "WARN stream: reconnecting; new-session-salt not yet attached"
- server: "INFO req: computed idemp_hash=sha256(op-492a|salt-v2)"
- server (earlier): "INFO req: computed idemp_hash=sha256(op-492a|salt-v1)"

Workaround applied by customer:
- Temporarily disabled automated salt rotation window for the private deployment.
- Implemented an application-level confirmation callback to deduplicate downstream effects for critical operations.

Notes:
- Customer reported this first on 2026-03-09; replicated in staging on 2026-03-10 with an HSM simulator.
- They rely on HSM rotation policy for compliance; disabling rotation is not a long-term option.

Initial triage performed by Support: reproduced in staging by forcing a salt rotation during an active streaming session. Behavior differs across SDKs:
- Python SDK attaches idempotency-salt at request creation and preserves per-request id field consistently across reconnects.
- TS SDK currently swaps the global salt asynchronously on rotation; if a reconnect happens in the swap window the outgoing headers can be missing or have the new salt unpredictably.
- Go SDK reuses a per-connection derived salt and on reconnect computes hash using the new global salt in some code paths due to non-atomic swap in the http2 header injector.

Hypothesis:
- Mid-session rotation + non-atomic swap of the salt value in SDKs causes computed idempotency hashes to diverge between the originally sent request and the retry, so the server treats retry as distinct.

What we've tried:
- Reproduced using HSM emulator and a controlled rotation pulse.
- Instrumented SDKs to log exact salt value used per-request.
- Confirmed server calculates different hashes matching the new/old salt values.

Next steps (short term):
- Advise customer to apply runbook: temporarily pause rotation during maintenance windows for long-lived sessions and enable application-level dedupe for critical side-effects.
- Provide a quick-fix guidance: set an explicit idempotency_key in the tool-call metadata so server can treat requests equal independent of salt rotation.

Next steps (engineering):
- Patch SDK-TS and SDK-Go to perform atomic salt swap for any in-flight session or attach session-scoped salt headers derived from a rotation-epoch token. PRs opened: see related_github_prs.
- Add e2e test that simulates salt rotation during reconnect to prevent regressions.
- Add runbook to Confluence and link in ticket.

2026-03-12: Eng has started work on SDK-TS and SDK-Go fixes; SDK-Python confirmed to be already tolerant but will add more tests. Customer is applying temporary dedupe callback while we patch. Working on internal rollback/patch plan for private deploy customers who cannot disable rotation.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 - Frostbyte SRE (customer): Provided logs and a reproducer script that toggles salt via the HSM emulator. Confirmed duplicates for 12/20 runs.
2026-03-11 - Eng (sdk-ts): Noted non-atomic global swap in lib/crypto/salt_manager.ts; drafting atomic-swap patch.
2026-03-11 - Eng (sdk-go): Observed header injector re-use; proposing to add per-session salt header until rotation epoch boundary. Will reference PR when ready.
2026-03-12 - Frostbyte SRE: Confirmed they applied the middleware and observed zero duplicates in 50 runs while awaiting SDK patches.
payload.summary: HSM-backed salt rotation during long-lived stream causes mismatched idempotency hashes and duplicate tool invocations across Python/TS/Go SDKs
