payload.description:
Issue summary:
BlueRidge Analytics (vendor ID BR-904) invoice BR-2026-0310 for $18,450.00 was queued for scheduled ACH today but the payment was held by Payments due to lack of a confirmed remittance address in the vendor profile. The vendor has requested same-day payment to avoid service interruption.

Impact:
- Immediate financial exposure: vendor services (data pipeline) scheduled for renewal tomorrow may be paused.
- Operational: Procurement and AP workload increases as we need to expedite verification.
- Number of invoices affected: 1 (this invoice).

Environment:
- Internal ledger: PROD; Vendor record resides in Finance Vendor Master (VEND-DB prod-us-east).
- Payment method: ACH (domestic).
- PO referenced: PO-48231 (fixed-price monthly).

Steps to reproduce / How this presented:
1) Procurement submitted invoice BR-2026-0310 and attached to PO-48231 on 2026-03-09.
2) Automated matching passed but profile validation flagged missing remittance_address_verified flag.
3) Payment scheduler put transaction into HOLD queue pending manual verification.
4) Payments team attempted to reach vendor contact but initial email bounced.

Logs / Evidence:
- Payment scheduler log (payments-scheduler-2026-03-11.log): "HOLD: vendor_profile_missing_remittance for BR-904, invoice BR-2026-0310"
- Attached: invoice_BR-2026-0310.pdf, po_48231.pdf, vendor-email-emily-stone.eml

Background / Notes:
- Vendor onboarding for BlueRidge was completed in 2023 but remittance verification was flagged incomplete during a previous vendor validation sweep (INT-7654). Procurement believed verification had been completed; Finance automation suggests the verification flag is still false.

Investigation notes (so far):
- 2026-03-10 09:20 (Rajiv): Checked vendor master; remittance_address_verified=false and the remittance_address field is populated but not confirmed.
- 2026-03-10 11:05 (Sophie Li, Procurement): Found an email thread with vendor confirming bank details but no proof-of-account or signed remittance confirmation attached.

Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 08:12 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses at the API gateway for a single dedicated-tenant (AcmeDocs) during their traffic warmup. Impact: customer observed 20-40% error rates on short chat requests and failed large embedding uploads. Root-cause chain is not confirmed but initial signals point to prefetch cancellation amplifying NVMe compaction I/O which caused upstream runtime watchdog resets and connection churn, producing apigw 502/503 waves.
1) Simulate tenant warmup: steady mix of short streaming chat sessions (avg 300 tokens) plus concurrent large embedding uploads (batch size ~1000 vectors). 2) Force prefetch enabled on tenant and trigger autoscaler scale-up of ephemeral pool. 3) Observe prefetch eviction/cancellation events in kvcache and concurrent NVMe compaction tasks. 4) Watch for runtime watchdog resets and apigw 5xx amplification under hedged retries.
- apigw 502/503 spike starting 2026-03-13 08:12 UTC, peaking 08:20-08:35 UTC.
- runtime restarts correlated with NVMe iowait spikes (iostat: avg await 120ms -> 450ms).
- kvcache eviction rate increased 8x; prefetch cancel events spiked.
- hedged retry traffic amplified connection counts at apigw by 3x.
- sample error trace: runtime watchdog SIGABRT after async nvme compaction task timeout (see runtime logs at /var/log/runtime/tenant-ACME/2026-03-13.log lines 1248-1264).
08:18 UTC: SRE observed iowait spike on nodes serving tenant shards; correlated with kvcache compact activity.
08:22 UTC: Runtime team reproduced async nvme compaction overlapping with prefetch invalidation causing excessive CPU blocking in the runtime main thread on test cluster.
08:30 UTC: Api-gateway hedged retry policy amplified backlog when upstream started failing - retries caused more concurrent connections and accept queue pressure.
Hypothesis: combination of aggressive prefetch + background NVMe compaction on hot shards caused runtime main thread stalls which tripped watchdogs; watchdog restarts caused partial connection tears and apigw to surface 5xxs. Hedged retries and autoscaler warmup contributed to amplification.
Customer correlation: AcmeDocs was initiating a large scheduled ingest at the same time as chat warmup which increased embedding IO and prefetch churn.
2026-03-13 08:25 - Support (Aisha): Notified customer that we are investigating and requested request IDs and sample timestamps.
2026-03-13 08:32 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Observed NVMe compaction task overlap; isolating compaction window and throttling compaction now as temporary mitigation.
2026-03-13 08:40 - Runtime (Liam): Pushed hotfix to disable async compaction during heavy prefetch windows on a small canary pool.
2026-03-13 09:05 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed error rates dropped to ~5% after mitigation but asked for timeline for permanent fix.
2026-03-13 11:10 - Product (Evelyn): Requested follow-up to add a scheduler-level circuit-breaker to prevent compaction during tenant warmup.
Mitigated: applied immediate throttling of NVMe compaction on affected shard pool and temporarily relaxed hedged retry settings at apigw for AcmeDocs routes. Customer error rate reduced from ~35% to ~5% within 30 minutes. A runtime hotfix was deployed to canary nodes to avoid long blocking compaction during prefetch invalidation. Full rollout pending validation.
1) Temporary: Throttle background NVMe compaction on tenant shards during detected warmup windows (applied 2026-03-13 08:35 UTC).
2) Temporary: Lower hedged retry aggressiveness for affected routes to reduce amplification (applied 2026-03-13 08:50 UTC).
3) Hotfix: Runtime change to make async compaction cooperative and cancelable when prefetch invalidation is in flight (canary deployed 2026-03-13 08:40 UTC).
4) Monitoring: Add alert for joint signals: kvcache prefetch cancellation rate + nvme iowait > threshold + runtime watchdog restarts.
- Postmortem write-up and RCA (owner: Liam) due by 2026-03-17.
- Product to evaluate scheduler circuit-breaker for compaction vs prefetch (owner: Evelyn).
- Modify autoscaler warmup policy to avoid simultaneous burst of embedding uploads and streaming route warmups for dedicated tenants (owner: Infra).
- Roll out runtime hotfix to all zones after canary validation (owner: Runtime).
- Update runbook and customer guidance for large ingest + warmup events.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer OrbitalAI reported repeated GPU attach failures and unexplained node ‘unavailable’ signals in their dedicated pool during the 09:00–10:30 UTC peak window. Symptoms look like short-lived GPU scarcity events (~30s–2m) that trigger the autoscaler to scale up aggressively, then immediately scale back down.

Impact:
- Affected customer requests experienced increased p50/p95 latency and intermittent 5xx attach failures for ~90 minutes across multiple model routes.
- Customer observed degraded throughput for batched workloads and saw spikes in request requeues.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: OrbitalAI-reserved-cluster-42 (us-east-1)
- Node agent: allocator-agent v1.8.3; node kernel driver v5.11-custom
- Autoscaler: v2.4.1 (adaptive-window enabled)
- Routes impacted: /v1/generate (rw-7b-v2), /v1/chat (rw-13b-qlora)

Observed behavior:
1) Node allocator logs show heartbeat timestamps drifting by 5–15s relative to control-plane metric timestamps, then recovering.
2) During drift windows, attach requests receive transient "attach rejected: node-report-mismatch" errors and are retried, producing short allocation storms.
3) Autoscaler interprets the attach rejections and short attach latency failures as capacity pressure and spins up extra instances; new instances register but are quickly marked unhealthy and drained when latency normalizes.
4) Net effect: repeated attach churn, elevated p95 latency, increased token cost from frequent scale events.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Target the customer's dedicated pool with a small steady-rate warmup (50 concurrent short streams, 1–2s inference).
2) Introduce a small jitter to the node-agent clock (observed in production as NTP jitter due to noisy host CPU).
3) Observe allocator heartbeat delta / attach reject logs and autoscaler behavior described above.

Logs / key traces (excerpts):
- allocator-agent: "heartbeat sent=2026-03-10T09:12:04Z observed_control_ts=2026-03-10T09:11:49Z delta=15s"
- serving-runtime: "attach rejected: node-report-mismatch (node-heartbeat=2026-03-10T09:12:04Z, control=2026-03-10T09:11:49Z)"
- autoscaler: "scale event: reason=attach-failures delta=+3 replicas; scale-back after 45s reason=healthy-probes"

Expected behavior:
- Heartbeats should be within <2s of control-plane timestamps; attach should succeed or be rate-limited gracefully without triggering aggressive scale cycles.

Notes on uniqueness: This incident centers on heartbeat timestamp skew causing false-positive capacity signals, rather than pure noisy-tenant CPU/GPU hogging or prefetch/slot fragmentation.
2026-03-10 09:25 — Support acked and asked for allocator logs and node heartbeat metrics (Amina).
2026-03-10 09:40 — SRE (Diego) pulled allocator and node-agent logs; observed correlated heartbeat deltas across 4 nodes in the dedicated cluster.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 10:25 — Reproduced locally in staging by introducing CPU steal on node-agent; allocator then produced identical attach-reject pattern.
2026-03-10 11:00 — Confirmed autoscaler interprets attach-rejects as capacity pressure; adaptive-window parameters (min-window=30s) cause oscillation because rejections resolve faster than the window.
Evidence collected:
- Node metrics (host-cpu-steal spikes coincident with heartbeat drift).
- Kernel driver trace showing scheduler latency spikes on worker nodes.
- Repro playbook used in staging (linked in comments).
Immediate mitigations tried:
- Temporarily increased allocator heartbeat tolerance from 2s -> 20s for OrbitalAI pool (config flag at control-plane) — mitigated churn within 5 minutes.
- Raised autoscaler min-window to 90s to avoid immediate scale-backs while a more durable fix is prepared.
Open questions:
- Root cause of host CPU starvation: noisy snapshotter or host-level cron?
- Are other dedicated pools at risk? Quick scan showed 2 additional pools with transient small drift but not sustained.
2026-03-10 09:31 - OrbitalAI Support Contact (Elena K.): No scheduled maintenance. We did trigger a bulk model-parameter warmup at 08:55 but it should be within normal ops. Attaching request traces (uploaded to customer-attachments).
2026-03-10 10:12 - Engineering (Jin Park): Confirmed autoscaler algorithm currently treats attach rejections as a proxy for capacity pressure. Proposing two changes: (1) soft-filter attach-rejection-derived events if heartbeat-delta > 5s; (2) backport allocator tolerance flag. Preparing PR.
2026-03-10 11:50 - OrbitalAI Support Contact (Elena K.): After the temporary config change things look stable. We still saw a single 5xx at 11:15 but no repeated churn. Thank you.
Mitigation applied: increased heartbeat tolerance for OrbitalAI pool and adjusted autoscaler min-window. Engineering patch (allocator PR #512) implements smoothed heartbeat acceptance and mitigates false attach-rejects; staged in canary 2026-03-12.
Planned next steps:
- 2026-03-12: Canary rollout to 10% of nodes in us-east-1 (in progress).
- 2026-03-13: Full rollout if canary shows <0.1% attach rejection rate increase.
- Investigate root cause of host CPU starvation (snapshotter/cron jobs) with infra team; will add to follow-up ticket if confirmed.
Status: In Progress — customer mitigation successful; awaiting full rollout and infra root-cause confirmation.
payload.summary: Allocator heartbeat skew causes repeated GPU attach failures and autoscaler misreads during peak window

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple ephemeral API keys were observed being issued for a Redwood service account (sa-ingest-01) in a short time window. Initial alert triggered by anomalous token creation rate from CI-related IP ranges and a spike in privileged ingest.put() calls. Investigation showed a recent OAuth grant to a third-party CI integration (BuildPulse) initiated from a Slack message link.

Impact: Potential unauthorized access to internal ingest pipelines and telemetry. No confirmed exfiltration of PII; elevated write activity to event_ingest.topic detected. Affecting one service account: sa-ingest-01. Scope currently limited to prod us-east cluster.

Timeline: 2026-03-12 09:03 UTC - SRE alert for unusual token issuance rate for sa-ingest-01. 2026-03-12 09:08 UTC - Support ticket created by oncall after Slack reports of strange message from #dev-integrations. 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - OAuth grant recorded: external app BuildPulse (app_id: bp-73a2) was authorized by user e.id=shawn.kim@redwood.com via slack-clicked link. 2026-03-12 09:25-09:40 UTC - Automated CI runner IPs issued three api-keys for sa-ingest-01 and performed high-volume ingest.put() calls.

Environment: prod-us-east, service: ingest, service-account: sa-ingest-01, integration: BuildPulse (third-party CI), communication vector: Slack message with link.

Detection: Alert rule "token-issuance-rate" fired (threshold 5 tokens/min) in Alerting -> Security. SRE observed tokens created by our token-service with user_agent header matching BuildPulse and originating from ci-runner-ops static IPs. Audit logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/q=token-service%20sa-ingest-01%20%22bp-73a2%22 (internal link).

Steps to reproduce (observed): 1) A user clicked a Slack message link in #dev-integrations that redirected to BuildPulse OAuth consent. 2) OAuth granted BuildPulse limited scopes including token:create for service accounts via a delegated CI flow. 3) BuildPulse used CI runners to call our token-service and created short-lived API keys bound to sa-ingest-01. 4) CI job triggered high-volume ingest calls.

Evidence collected: - Token-service issuance logs (timestamps and request ids) - CI runner IP connection logs - Slack message permalink: https://slack.redwood.internal/archives/C013XXXX/p1678698623000200 - BuildPulse OAuth audit entry in admin-portal (bp-73a2) - stacktrace of ingest.put() call anomalies - Screen capture of OAuth consent prompt cached in SSO audit.

Initial containment actions taken: - Disabled BuildPulse app oauth client in internal oauth admin at 09:32 UTC. - Rotated the tokens for sa-ingest-01 and revoked all active API keys at 09:40 UTC. - Temporarily blocked CI runner IPs in firewall allowlist while we validate runner images. - Issued org-wide Slack advisory to not click unfamiliar build/ci links and to report messages to #security.

Open questions: - Which user account authorized BuildPulse and did they have permission to grant service-account scopes? (initially appears to be shawn.kim@redwood.com) - Were any persisted credentials or configuration files in CI systems leaked to BuildPulse? - Did the BuildPulse app escalate beyond intended scopes?

Required next steps: 1) SRE to audit all token issuances for the last 48 hours across service accounts. 2) Identity team to review OAuth consent policy and restrict service-account scope grants to a allowlist of apps. 3) SecOps to run a forensic snapshot of affected CI runner instances. 4) Postmortem and communication template for leadership and legal.

Additional notes:
Hypothesis: A malicious or misconfigured BuildPulse connector requested and obtained excessive delegated scopes due to overly broad consent screen, enabling token: create for service accounts.
Logs show three api keys created at 09:25, 09:31, 09:39 UTC. Each key had a 10m TTL and was used for 2-10k ingest.put() calls before revocation.
No downstream data export detected in outbound egress logs; however high-volume writes could have masked other activity. Need to preserve logs for longer retention window.
User shawn.kim had team_admin role which allowed him to approve third-party integrations in the past; identity policy gap identified.
CI runner images currently under analysis for potential compromised tokens or leaked config; preliminary volume indicates automated job triggered by BuildPulse webhook.
Correlating Slack permalink timestamps with oauth grant shows click at 09:19:47 UTC; oauth token exchange at 09:19:58 UTC.
Recommend immediate hardening: require MFA for consent to any app requesting service-account scopes; add admin approval flow for service-account oauth grants.
Containment completed: BuildPulse oauth client disabled, all active API keys for sa-ingest-01 revoked, CI runner IPs blocked. Ongoing forensic analysis of CI runners and token-service audit. Identity team implementing temporary allowlist and admin-approval flow for service-account OAuth grants. Final postmortem to be produced after full investigation.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer NoteWise reports intermittent stream interruptions when using server-sent events (SSE) and WebSocket streaming for text-generation. The client sees partial output (truncated tokens) and the client SDK automatically attempts to reconnect but resulting resumed streams either duplicate fragments or resume from a later token — producing incoherent final outputs.

Impact:
- Affected customer: NoteWise Analytics (dedicated tenant on us-east)
- Several production jobs for realtime summarization fail to produce coherent final responses; customer reports ~8% of streaming calls in the last 24h were affected.
- Business impact: loss of generated text quality, increased retries, potential downstream data corruption for archived transcripts.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted Dedicated capacity (us-east GPU pool d-42)
- Client SDK: notewise-js v0.8.3 using EventSource for SSE and native ws for WebSocket fallback
- Models observed: gpt-redwood-13b (primary), gpt-redwood-7b-q4 (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Initiate streaming chat generation with streaming=true, max_tokens=1024, and a long prompt (~8k chars).
2) On SSE path expect token-by-token events.
3) After ~3-10s, stream stops with no final_done/event. Client receives no final finish event but receives a close event on the underlying TCP connection.
4) SDK attempts reconnect (backoff 250ms) and receives a resumed partial sequence which either overlaps existing tokens or jumps ahead.

Observed logs (customer provided):
- client: "event: message\ndata: {\"token\":\"the quick brown\" }\n...\nevent: close\n"
- server (gateway): "WARN connection=conn-7b2d: downstream reset while streaming to tenant=notewise code=ECONNRESET"
- streaming-proxy: "DEBUG stream-session=ss-324: resumed session after 312ms, last-kv=0x1a3, resume-offset=576"

Additional context:
- Customer uses long-running sessions with KV cache enabled. They previously reported a separate issue (SUP-4689) about occasional duplicate tokens during canary rollouts; might be related.

Request from customer:
1) Root cause analysis for disconnects and explanation of reconnect semantics for SSE vs WebSocket in our platform.
2) Short-term mitigation and recommended SDK changes/workarounds to avoid partial outputs.
3) Long-term fix plan and ETA.
2026-03-12 10:12 - Support (Ethan Rivera): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE for immediate investigation; requesting request IDs and sample request timestamps from the customer.
2026-03-12 10:27 - Customer (NoteWise - Maya Chen): Provided three sample request IDs and a short screen recording of the client behavior. Request IDs: req-20260312-77a, req-20260312-81f, req-20260312-90b. Noted that failures spike during peak ingest between 09:00-11:00 EDT.
2026-03-12 11:03 - SRE (Aisha Patel): Investigating streaming-proxy logs and gateway traces for the provided req IDs. Found ECONNRESET events for two of the three requests; correlating with a transient overload on the d-42 GPU pool at 10:05 EDT.
Summary of checks performed:
- Correlated request IDs against gateway and streaming-proxy logs; two requests show TCP resets during active token streaming.
- Checked node-level metrics for pool d-42: observed CPU scheduling spikes and elevated network retransmits at 10:04-10:06.
- Streaming-proxy reports resume-offset values that do not match last-sent token offset for the session; suspect mismatch in resume token bookkeeping when there is an in-flight cache eviction.
- Reviewed SDK behavior: notewise-js v0.8.3 will attempt reconnects and requests a resume token header; if resume fails, it opens a fresh session but merges messages naïvely which can create duplicate fragments.
- No evidence of auth/permission failures. No error codes from model process; model continued producing tokens until process closed the connection.

Hypothesis:
1) Under transient resource pressure (GPU or network), the serving runtime or the streaming proxy can force-close downstream TCP connections (ECONNRESET) to preserve headroom.
2) The streaming-proxy's resume bookkeeping for long sessions with KV caching has an off-by-one condition when an eviction or compaction occurs mid-stream, returning an incorrect resume-offset.
3) The client SDK's reconnect merge strategy is insufficiently defensive: it attempts to stitch resumed tokens into the existing buffer without verifying server-provided sequence numbers, causing duplicated/truncated outputs.

Immediate investigative artifacts:
- Gateway trace links: https://internal-ops.redwood/gateway/traces/req-20260312-77a
- Streaming-proxy debug snippets: captured in /var/log/streaming-proxy/2026-03-12-10.log (attached to ticket in the console)
Short-term mitigations applied (2026-03-13):
- Applied a temporary throttle on intensive background jobs in pool d-42 to reduce transient overloads.
- Pushed a server-side guard in streaming-proxy: if ECONNRESET occurs mid-stream, mark session as non-resumable and emit an explicit final_error event to clients to avoid silent truncation. Deployed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proxy/pull/214 (hotfix v0.9.1).
- Notified NoteWise to upgrade notewise-js to 0.8.4 which includes safer reconnect handling (verify server sequence numbers before merging; prefer fresh session if server indicates resume gap).

Long-term plan:
1) Implement robust resume token verification and stronger invariants in streaming-proxy to ensure resume-offset is validated against last-sent token metadata (ETA: 2026-03-27).
2) Add server-side telemetry for resume success/failure rates and surface on Redwood Console per-tenant streaming health (ETA: 2026-04-10).
3) Improve SDKs: a) default to conservative reconnect behavior for long sessions, b) expose hooks for app-level idempotency/merge strategies (ETA: 2026-03-31).

Customer communication and next steps:
- 2026-03-13 09:00 - Support (Ethan Rivera): Notified NoteWise of the hotfix and recommended SDK upgrade. Asked customer to run a 2-hour smoke test during non-peak window and share results.
- Follow-up: monitor resume-related telemetry and reopen if recurrence >1% in next 7 days.

Ticket status: awaiting customer confirmation of SDK upgrade smoke test. If customer still observes issues, SRE will attach full pcap and escalate to runtime team.
Pending customer smoke test confirmation. Hotfix deployed to streaming-proxy and SDK patch released. Root cause likely combination of transient pool overload causing ECONNRESET and a resume-offset bookkeeping edge-case in the streaming-proxy; SDK reconnect merge behavior made the symptom worse. Full server-side resume validation planned.

Issue summary: Vendor 'GreenLayer Logistics' submitted invoice INV-2026-409 that cites PO-2019-77 (legacy). The PO was superseded in our system by PO-2025-142 but the vendor billed against the old PO number. Impact: AP has put the invoice on hold to avoid payment to wrong cost centers; vendor has flagged overdue and is requesting payment. Estimated exposure: ~$24,800 gross.

Details: Invoice has three line items allocated to distribution centers A/B/C. Receiving records in Warehouse DB show goods received under PO-2025-142 with different line splits and a credit memo applied for distribution center B in 2025 Q4. The vendor portal shows INV-2026-409 tied to PO-2019-77. No automatic three-way match occurred.

Steps to reproduce / validate: 1) Search AP ledger for INV-2026-409 and related payment holds. 2) Cross-check PO-2019-77 and PO-2025-142 in Procurement system (ProcureOne). 3) Confirm GRNs in Warehouse DB for dates 2025-11-02..2025-11-07. 4) Review vendor portal shipment and invoice history. 5) Re-run three-way match in AP tool with manual override logging.

Relevant attachments/links: ProcureOne PO records: https://procure.redwood.internal/PO/PO-2025-142, Vendor portal thread: #vendor-greencare on Slack (link internal). AP ledger snapshot: s3://redwood-finance/ap-snapshots/2026-03-09/inv-2026-409.csv.

Requested outcome: Confirm correct PO to pay against, issue payment or partial payment where appropriate, update AP/Procurement records to avoid reoccurrence, and notify vendor of next steps.
[2026-03-10] Maya Chen (Reporter): Logged after vendor escalation. Put invoice on hold in AP to prevent accidental payment. Requesting Procurement to confirm which PO the goods should map to.
[2026-03-10] Priya Nair (Procurement): Procurement confirms PO-2019-77 was superseded by PO-2025-142 in Jan 2025 after contract renewal; vendor should have been notified. Will check the vendor onboarding record to see if notification was lost.
[2026-03-11] Ravi Kumar (AP): Attempted automated match; mismatch on line-level quantities for DC-B. System flagged a credit memo (CM-2025-88) that reduced payable amount. Holding payment until reconciliation. Attaching AP export.
[2026-03-11] Liam Patel (Assignee): Performed preliminary three-way match with manual overrides for DC-A and DC-C only. Generated a partial-payment recommendation: pay $12,400 now for matched lines; hold remainder pending vendor reissue or credit memo confirmation. Sent vendor a formal request to reissue invoice referencing PO-2025-142 and to attach the CM for DC-B.
[2026-03-12] Finance Ops (Automated): Accruals adjusted to reflect partial payment recommendation; created task FIN-2026-121 for month-end reconciliation. Notifying Legal for contract trace if vendor disputes.
Findings so far: 1) The vendor is billing against a legacy PO number that was superseded — root cause likely a vendor-side reference error plus a missing outbound notification in ProcureOne. 2) A previously-applied credit memo (CM-2025-88) reduced liability for DC-B but vendor invoice did not reflect that credit. 3) ProcureOne retains change history showing PO supersedure but vendor communication log is incomplete; likely a process gap in vendor notifications during contract renewals. Evidence: ProcureOne changelog (2025-01-12) and Warehouse GRNs match quantities for two of three lines. Next diagnostic steps: obtain vendor invoice attachment PDF, request vendor to reissue or provide credit memo evidence, run a full GL tie-out for Q1 accruals if payment deferred.
Workaround implemented: Partial payment recommendation created and accrual updated to avoid month-end mismatch. AP will issue payment for the confirmed matched lines once manager approval is recorded in AP system. Procurement to request vendor reissue with correct PO number or attach CM-2025-88. Follow-ups: 1) ProcureOne to add an automated notification on PO supersedure (owner: Priya Nair, due 2026-04-02). 2) Finance Ops to run FIN-2026-121 month-end reconciliation. 3) Vendor onboarding doc updated to include step for verifying PO numbers on invoices (owner: Vendor Ops).
Procurement to confirm communications history with vendor and request reissued invoice (due 2026-03-16)
AP to prepare partial payment run upon approval (expected 2026-03-13)
Finance Ops to track FIN-2026-121 and report final GL adjustment before month-end close

Issue summary:
Since the org signing key (team-release@gpg) rotation on 2026-03-09, the nightly release pipeline run by self-hosted release-runners is failing during artifact verification. The GPG step reports 'BAD_SIGNATURE' on multiple signed artifacts and aborts the pipeline, blocking all release promotion jobs that require signed artifacts.

Impact:
- All release promotion pipelines from the staging branch are failing in prod-us-east.
- No releases can be created or promoted; estimated user-facing impact: none immediate, but blocker for planned hotfix release.
- A subset of release-runners (hosts tagged release-runner-prod-*) are the first to hit the failures.

Environment:
- CI: GitLab self-hosted (runner group: release-runners-prod)
- Artifact registry: internal OCI registry + GPG-signed tarballs in S3 (us-east)
- Key management: internal key-rotation process (ops-runbook), public key published to internal keyserver at keys.redwood.internal

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger release pipeline for release-candidate commit SHA XYZ.
2) Pipeline downloads signed tarball from S3.
3) run `gpg --verify artefact.tar.gz.sig artefact.tar.gz` inside runner container.
4) gpg exits with status 2 and prints 'BAD_SIGNATURE' and 'no valid openpgp data found'.

Observed logs/snippets:
- Runner logs (release-runner-prod-07): "gpg: Signature made ... gpg: BAD_SIGNATURE gpg: invalid packet (ctb=0x0)"
- Pipeline job trace shows immediate failure at 'verify-signature' step.

Hypothesis / initial findings:
- The rotated GPG key was pushed to the internal keyserver with a new key ID and fingerprint. Some runners have an outdated keyring cached and still trust the old key fingerprint, while the artifacts are signed by the new key.
- Some signing tooling may have re-encoded signatures with a different packet format (we saw 'invalid packet' in gpg output) — possible gpg version mismatch between signing host and runner containers.
- The keyserver index propagation may be delayed; runners that used a cached lookup received a malformed response.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Ops pulled the previous GPG public key from backup and added it to a temporary allowlist on three runners (release-runner-prod-03/04/07) — pipelines for those runners succeeded for a single build (hotfix candidate).
- Bumped the runner container gpg package from 2.2.20 -> 2.3.8 on a canary runner; that canary now fails with 'invalid packet' while older gpg accepted signature, suggesting a compatibility issue.

Next steps planned / asked from infra team:
- Confirm the exact key fingerprint used by the signing process (artifact-signer job) and compare with keys published to keys.redwood.internal. (Assigned to Release Engineering)
- Force-refresh keyring on all release runners via staged job that pulls explicit public key file from S3 and imports to gpg keyring. (Assigned to CI infra)
- Validate gpg binary versions across signing host and runners; if mismatch, plan either to downgrade signing host gpg or upgrade runner containers. (Assigned to Security/Infra)
- Temporarily allow fallback verification to previous key for releases created in the next 24 hours while we fully roll the new key. (Requires Risk approval).

Cross-references:
- Slack: #release-engineering thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02RELEASES/p1640
- Runbook: Confluence GPG Key Rotation Runbook (link above)
- Related incidents: INT-23011 (previous key rotation fail), INT-23350 (runner keyring drift)

- Pulled signing host logs: artifact-signer@build-01 shows sign command using gpg 2.2.20 and key-id ABCD1234.
- Verified public key published at keys.redwood.internal shows fingerprint that does not match ABCD1234; shows new key EFGH5678.
- Compared signature packets with pktdump: some signatures created by gpg 2.3.x include new signature subpacket format that gpg 2.2.20 accepts but older container images have varying behavior.
- Keyserver response on 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC returned a header 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' causing our naive keysync microservice to truncate key exports; this produced a malformed pubkey blob on some runners.
- Reproduced locally by fetching key export via existing keysync service: got truncated payload resulting in 'invalid packet' on import.

Additional notes:
Partial: key rotation publishing pipeline returned truncated key blobs due to improper handling of chunked transfer from internal keyserver, combined with gpg version mismatches across runner images leading to inconsistent import/verification results.
Partial mitigation applied: temporary rollback of signing host to previous key for immediate hotfix, and targeted keyring refresh jobs run on three canary runners. Next steps: patch keysync service to handle chunked transfer correctly, schedule controlled rollout of new public key to all runners with checksum verification, and standardize gpg version in runner images. Will update once full rollout complete.
Patch keysync service to validate Content-Length/Checksums on key export (owner: infra)
Add key fingerprint validation step to CI key import job (owner: release-eng)
Upgrade runner base image gpg to 2.3.x in next CI image release (owner: ci-team)
Publish rollback decision and timeline in Confluence (owner: security)
payload.summary: Release pipeline failing: GPG verification errors after team signing-key rotation blocking runners

Issue summary:
A new Backend Engineer hire (international, work-visa pending) has a delayed start date due to immigration paperwork. HR requests a temporary shared workstation and a managed set of software seats so the candidate can begin restricted onboarding training remotely. LDAP account provisioning via Okta is currently blocked until the candidate's identity verification completes; we need a documented, auditable temporary access path and clear owner for license allocations.

Impact:

- Onboarding schedule risk: orientation tasks fall behind if we don't provide alternative access.
- Potential license oversubscription if seats allocated and not reclaimed promptly.

Environment:
- Affected systems: Okta SSO -> LDAP sync, internal license pool (JetBrains, Slack paid seats, Confluence), loaner workstation inventory (NY office), asset tracking sheet (Google Sheets).

Steps to reproduce / current state:
1) HR submitted standard new-hire request on 2026-03-05 with start-date placeholder and visa note.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Request from Applied ML (privacy team) for a short, auditable access window to a small, de-identified set of inference input/output pairs to validate a new automatic redaction transform.

Impact:
- Low production risk if handled per controls below, but the validation must use live workload distributions to catch edge-cases.
- Customer data sensitivity: potential PII in free-text prompts; must ensure strong redaction and minimal exposure.

Environment:
- Production inference traces (us-east) sampled during business hours for the past 72 hours.

Request details / Scope:
- Provide up to 250 inference records (input + output) containing examples where the new redaction logic triggered or was expected to trigger.
- Records must be de-identified using the approved pipeline: token-level masking, email/SSN regex scrub, and hash-only user/session IDs.
- Timebox: access for 48 hours from provisioning. After that, copies must be destroyed and S3 artifacts permanently deleted.
- Consumers: Applied ML (aisha.patel@redwood.com), Privacy Review (tbd), and one engineer from serving-runtime (liam.chen@redwood.com).

Data fields requested:
- request_id (hashed), user_id (hashed), timestamp, model_name, prompt_text (de-identified), model_output (de-identified), routing_metadata, inference_latency_ms.

Justification:
- New redaction transform introduced in PR #4521 needs validation against production prompt phrasing to confirm no PII leaks and acceptable false-positive rate.
- Prior staging tests missed a rare customer prompt pattern observed in prod.

Controls requested / proposed safeguards:
- Approved users only (listed above) with temporary IAM role (AssumeRole duration 1h; multiple assumes allowed during 48h window).
- Data stored in a dedicated S3 path with SSE-KMS; access limited to role principal.
- Artifact TTL enforced by lifecycle rule + manual verification of deletion by SRE after expiry.
- Audit log export of all S3 access and role assumes forwarded to Security (sec-audit@redwood.com).
- No local copies allowed on personal machines; only EC2 bastion with encrypted volume may be used for analysis.

Approvals required:
- Privacy Lead (Olivia Ramirez)
- Security (SRE lead: Marcus Holloway)
- Legal (if dataset contains >1 confirmed PII instance)

Deliverable format:
- NDJSON file with each line representing a single de-identified record.

Desired timeline:
- Approval decision within 48 hours (business days).
- Provisioning within 24 hours after approvals.

Additional notes:
Sampling query run: SELECT top 1000 from inference_traces where timestamp >= now() - interval '72 hours' and model_name in ('redwood-2.7b','open-llm-v1') and redaction_score < 0.95 order by rand() limit 1000.
Initial checks:
- Confirmed 12 candidate prompts with email-like tokens and 3 with SSN-like patterns.
- Redaction pipeline (staging) applied token masking and regex scrub; confirmed no raw emails remain in the sample preview.
- KV-cache references were removed and session IDs replaced with HMAC-sha256(user_id, salt).
- Logs: audit log for sampling query recorded at https://splunk.redwood.com/en-US/app/search/jobs/7089123 (access restricted).
Hypothesis:
- New redaction thresholds are too conservative for short-form prompts, causing false negatives. Need production distribution to estimate precision/recall.
Open questions:
- Do we need to include model logits or only final output? (Privacy prefers no logits).
Pending final privacy sign-off. Interim actions taken:
- SRE created timeboxed S3 path with SSE-KMS and lifecycle TTL 72 hours; KMS policy updated to allow assume-role for listed principals.
- Uploaded 5 de-identified sample records to the preview path for Privacy review.
- Security logged the permission change (ticket SEC-1142) and scheduled a follow-up audit.
Planned final steps after approval:
1) Run sanitized export job to produce NDJSON (max 250 records) into s3://redwood-internal-privacy-exports/INT-63249-<timestamp>.
2) Notify principals and hand off an IAM role with 48h window and 1h assume duration.
3) After 48h, SRE will verify deletion, run object-delete verification, and produce an audit report linking to this ticket.
4) If >1 confirmed PII instance found in the full set, Legal will be engaged and a wider remediation plan will be created.
Follow-ups / Action items:
- Update the data-extraction SOP to include HMAC-based user_id hashing as a mandatory step (owner: Applied ML).
- Add an automation to generate short-lived role credentials rather than manual creation (owner: SRE infra).
payload.summary: Time-boxed access to de-identified inference snippets for privacy validation of new redaction rules

payload.description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (first observed by Acme Retail) reported intermittent high p99 inference latency and occasional 504 timeouts when re-sending identical conversational turns (immediate replay of the previous user message). Impact: Replayed prompts that should hit warm prefix/session KV entries are falling back to cold-path lookups, causing expensive shard reads and downstream per-token tail latency spikes (~600-900ms additional per-token at p99) and occasional request timeouts. The issue is customer-facing for enterprise customers in us-east and correlates with a recent TTL sliding-window change deployed in kvcache two days prior. Environment: prod, us-east-1, mixed dedicated and hosted routing for the affected tenant. Observed against both redwood-open-3b and redwood-latency-optimized-7b variants.
1) Create a conversational session with the customer account in prod us-east-1
2) Send a prompt that includes a ~1.2k token context followed by a short user utterance; record response latency
3) Immediately re-send the identical user utterance (simulate replay/duplicate user action)
4) Observe that the first replay frequently has warm-path latency but subsequent replays within a 2-5s window hit p99 spikes or timeout, rather than consistent warm hits
5) Reproduce several times and capture serving/runtime logs and kvcache trace ids
2026-03-10T15:02:11.248Z [serving-runtime] req=abcd1234 warm-prefix-hit=false kv-lookup=shard-17 duration=372ms fallback=cold-path
2026-03-10T15:02:11.620Z [kvcache] key=session:acct:acme:ctx:hash123 ttl_remaining=1.2s shard=17 returned=false
2026-03-10T15:02:12.045Z [serving-runtime] req=abcd1235 duplication=immediate replay=true p99_inc=+820ms status=200
2026-03-10T15:02:13.111Z [proxy-gateway] req=abcd1236 upstream=serving-runtime timeout=504ms route=fallback-to-durable
2026-03-10T15:07:05.331Z [kvcache] resync shard-17 ttl-eviction drift=+1.6s reason=sliding-window-adjustment
Initial hypothesis: hot-key evictions or prefetch thrash. Observed different pattern: TTLs for session prefix keys are being decremented inconsistently across shards after the recent TTL sliding-window change (PR #2398).
Trace correlation shows the same session key sometimes present on initial request and missing on immediate replay within 1-3s—suggests per-shard TTL slip (race) where the key is treated expired on the replaying shard but present on requester shard, causing a cold-path backfill even for identical prompts.
Metric signals: kvcache cache-hit-rate for affected customer drops from 98% -> 72% for the replay window; p99 token latency for affected workloads increases by ~0.6-0.9s during miss storms.
Reproduction on staging with controlled shard mapping reproduces the miss when TTL update batching is enabled + high small-burst traffic. Disabling TTL batch commit removes the effect.
Immediate mitigations tested: enabling aggressive prefix pinning on routing reduces observed p99 by keeping requests on shards with warmed session keys (workaround only; not ideal for multi-AZ).
Support (Sonia Alvarez) 2026-03-10: Customer reports intermittent 504s and high p99 on replay. Captured logs and sample request ids attached. Asking SRE to triage.
SRE (Marcus Patel) 2026-03-10: Assigned. Initial triage points to kvcache TTL behavior after last deployment (runtime PR #2398). Kicking off deeper trace correlation across shards.
Customer (Acme Retail - Eng) 2026-03-10: Impacting recommender UI; users see repeated 'slow' playback on re-try, trying to mitigate on their side increases complexity.
SRE 2026-03-11: Replayed tests on staging show TTL commit batching + high burst leads to inter-shard TTL race. Opened PR to make TTL commit atomic per-session-key (kvcache #441).
Support 2026-03-12: Notified customer of interim workaround: enable session_pin routing flag or increase session TTL to avoid sliding-window expiry during bursts. Planned production rollback of TTL sliding-window change if PR does not land quickly.
Workaround: For impacted enterprise customers (Acme Retail) we enabled session_pin routing (keeps requests to the warmed shard) and temporarily increased session TTL to 30s. This reduced p99 spikes by ~85% for the observed workload. Long-term fix: landed atomic TTL commit in kvcache (PR #441) and are rolling to prod in a controlled canary starting 2026-03-13. Post-rollback plan: if atomic commit is delayed, revert the TTL sliding-window change (runtime PR #2398) across us-east. Follow-ups: add end-to-end trace that tags TTL update origin so we can trace per-key TTL mutations, add an alert (kvcache.low_warm_hit_rate) to catch >10% drop for customer sessions, and run a blast-radius test prior to future TTL algorithm changes.
payload.summary: Session TTL slip causes hot-key cache miss storms and intermittent p99 latency on replayed turns

payload.description:
Issue summary: After several template renames and bulk imports last week, the SLA dependency graph that derives effective SLA weights for autoroute macros is returning stale parent bindings for a subset of templates. Impact: internal routing is mis-prioritizing support queues for about ~2.3% of incoming internal tickets causing delayed escalations and inaccurate SLA reporting buckets in the ops dashboard. Scope: internal-support only; no customer-facing queues affected, but impacts internal on-call SLO reporting and automated escalations. Hypothesis: when template_registry entries are renamed or re-keyed, the dependency graph reconciliation job sometimes fails to update in-memory binding indices, leaving older template IDs referenced by compiled macros. This yields an effective SLA weight mismatch between computed routing decisions and the persisted template manifest.
1) Create a template 'HighTouch-DB-Migrations-v1' with SLA weight = P0 (10) and bind to macro 'db-migration-alerts'
2) Bulk-rename template to 'HighTouch-DB-Migrations-archived' via template-import job (template_registry import v2) and create new template 'HighTouch-DB-Migrations' with a different ID and SLA weight = P2 (3)
3) Trigger reconcile-run (manual run of sla-dependency-reconciler) but observe logs: job reports 'partial-sync: 37/49 reconciled' without error code
4) Send a test internal ticket matching macro 'db-migration-alerts' and observe routing: ticket routed with previous P0 priority instead of the new P2 weight
5) Check in-memory dependency graph endpoint /internal/debug/dep-graph?macro=db-migration-alerts and note parent template ID still points to the archived template ID
6) Query DB: SELECT * FROM template_bindings WHERE macro='db-migration-alerts' shows both bindings present; reconcile job should have pruned the archived binding but did not.
2026-03-09T22:11:03Z sla-reconciler INFO partial-sync: reconciled=37 total=49 duration_ms=12430
2026-03-09T22:11:03Z sla-reconciler WARN missing-template-id=tmpl_0f3a98 referenced_by=macro_db-migration-alerts
2026-03-09T22:11:04Z routing-service DEBUG decision=route_to_queue queue=oncall-db weight=10 computed_weight=10 source=dep-graph parent_template=tmpl_0f3a98
2026-03-10 - Initial triage by Maya: reproduced locally using staging copy of template_registry; confirmed reconcile reports partial-sync without throwing exception; suspect batching window in reconcile job is skipping orphaned bindings when import metadata contains 'rename' marker.
2026-03-11 - Ethan injected additional logging into sla-reconciler: discovered a race where template-imports create a tombstone + new template in same transaction; reconciler iterate over listing but uses cached index that is lazily refreshed every 60s, causing missed pruning of tombstones.

Issue summary: After an AP firmware push to office Wi-Fi (Cisco 9800 series), a subset of laptops experience TLS upload stalls when sending large payloads to Redwood Private endpoints over WireGuard. Impact: Engineers on-prem cannot push large model bundles or uploads to the private deployment; operations and customer-facing work slowed. Intermittent: small requests succeed; large uploads stall during TLS handshake or mid-upload and eventually time out. Behavior began ~2026-03-09 22:00 PDT shortly after the AP firmware rollout.

Impact: Several internal deploys to the Private cluster in us-west failed; developer productivity affected. No public customer impact reported yet (private deployments only).

Observed behavior:
- Uploads of tar.gz > 1.4 MB hang during TLS handshake or during the first data packets after handshake.
- Application-level logs show stalled HTTP/2 streams and long tail latency on token pushes.
- WireGuard tunnel remains UP per wg show; control plane reports no peer downtime.
- ICMP Fragmentation-needed messages were being dropped by the office edge firewall, but only after the AP firmware change.

Additional notes: This looks like a PMTU/MTU interaction between 802.11ax A-MSDU aggregation, the AP's new fragmentation behavior, and the WireGuard overlay which increases packet size by ~80 bytes (UDP + WG headers).
1) Connect to corporate-ssid on affected AP cluster (office floor 4).
2) Establish WireGuard tunnel to private deployment (wg0 to gateway 10.10.0.1).
3) Attempt curl --upload-file large_model.tar.gz https://private-us-west.redwood.internal/upload -v --http2
4) Observe TLS handshake stalls or stall during first POST packet exchange for payloads > ~1300 bytes.
5) Running tcpdump on client shows initial SYN/SYN-ACK, TLS ClientHello, then no progress; server logs show half-open TLS session.
tcpdump excerpt (client):
14:12:03.123456 IP client > gateway: UDP, length 1420
14:12:03.123789 IP client > 1.2.3.4: TCP 52344 > 443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
14:12:03.124012 IP 1.2.3.4 > client: TCP 443 > 52344: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
14:12:03.124200 IP client > 1.2.3.4: TCP 52344 > 443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1381, ack 1, win 64240, length 1380
14:12:03.124500 IP 1.2.3.4 > client: ICMP 1/4 Fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu = 1350)

Edge firewall (ASA) logs: "Unable to deliver ICMP dest-unreachable frag-needed to host 10.24.12.45, policy drop".

Application log (uploader): "http2 stream stalled: no DATA frames received after ClientHello; retrying; attempt 3 failed: i/o timeout"
2026-03-10 09:40 - Support triage: Confirmed multiple reports from floor 3/4 seating areas. New AP firmware v17.4.2 pushed 2026-03-09 21:55; rollback window open until 2026-03-12.
2026-03-10 10:10 - SRE checked WireGuard; peers show steady handshake counters and no rekey storms. No packet drops visible on wg endpoints in cloud.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Network Eng performed controlled repro with a MacBook: success when client MTU forced to 1350 locally; failure at default 1500. Suggests PMTU path discovery failing to propagate.
2026-03-10 12:20 - Packet captures on AP showed A-MSDU aggregation creating frames that exceed downstream MTU after WireGuard encapsulation. AP firmware changes now appear to allow larger aggregated frames without honoring DF heuristics; combined with edge firewall ICMP filtering, clients never learn lower MTU.
2026-03-11 08:30 - Tested temporary mitigations: enforced MSS clamping on office edge (ASA) for TCP sessions to 1330; this restores upload success for affected clients. Also validated forcing client MTU to 1350 works around issue.
2026-03-11 11:00 - Cross-team sync: Wireless team confirmed firmware change adjusted aggregation thresholds for HE frames; vendor acknowledged a regression and provided beta patch to disable aggressive aggregation per SSID.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Engineering created a short-term policy to enable MSS clamping on edge for user VLANs and disabled A-MSDU aggregation on corporate-ssid via AP config.
John Miller (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed several deploys failing with 'http2 stream stalled' errors. Happens only on office Wi-Fi; home tethering works fine.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-10: Triaged and escalated to Networking. Collected failed pcap and sample client config.
Network Eng (Miguel Ortega) - 2026-03-10: Reproduced locally. Suspect PMTU discovery not propagating due to ICMP filtering + AP aggregation increase. Will test MSS clamp as workaround.
SRE (Sophie Chen) - 2026-03-11: Deployed MSS clamping on edge and requested Wireless to push a config to disable A-MSDU on corp SSID. Noted upload flows recovered for test clients.
Wireless Vendor Rep (Cisco) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed firmware regression in v17.4.2 affecting A-MSDU behavior with overlay tunnels. Beta patch available to toggle behavior; scheduling controlled rollout.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-12: Notified impacted engineers of workaround (use wired or set MTU 1350) and tracking permanent fix with Networking.
Sophie Chen - 2026-03-12: Leaving ticket open while vendor rollbacks/patches are validated. Plan: roll back AP firmware on non-critical APs Thu 2026-03-12 window; full fix requires vendor patch.
AP firmware v17.4.2 changed 802.11ax A-MSDU aggregation thresholds such that aggregated frames after WireGuard UDP encapsulation exceeded downstream MTU. Edge firewall was configured to drop outgoing ICMP "Fragmentation needed" messages to internal hosts, preventing PMTU discovery. Result: TCP MSS not adjusted, causing TLS/data packets to be dropped and uploads to stall.
Short-term mitigations applied: 1) MSS clamping (1330) on office edge for user VLANs; 2) Disabled A-MSDU aggregation on corporate-ssid; 3) Guidance to staff: use wired network or set MTU 1350 on client if experiencing issues. Vendor provided beta patch to correct aggregation behavior.

Planned long-term fix: Vendor patch scheduled for controlled rollout week of 2026-03-15 after validation. Post-deployment: remove MSS clamp and re-enable optimized aggregation. Follow-up: add test to CI that repros large TLS upload over WireGuard overlay in office environment to catch regressions.

Issue summary:
A Redwood engineer cannot access internal notebook workspaces after SSO sign-in. The Okta SAML assertion authenticates but the session is tied to a secondary internal identity that has no notebook role bindings.

Impact:
Single-user (internal) access loss to notebooks; blocks debugging and scheduled runs for the engineer. No widespread service degradation observed, but the identity inconsistency could affect other users after provisioning changes.

Environment:
prod-us-west - notebooks service behind identity-proxy with SCIM provisioning from Okta.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Sign in to console via Okta for user alice+infra@redwood.com (sign-in prints success).
2) Attempt to open Notebook -> redirect completes but authorization to workspace fails with 403.
3) Navigate to support tool and inspect user identities. Two internal identities present: alice@redwood.com (primary, no notebooks role) and alice+infra@redwood.com (has notebooks role but not linked to SSO session).

Observed behavior:
- SSO/SAML assertion NameID shows email alice@redwood.com (lowercased, plus-tag stripped) while Okta profile externalId still contains plus-tag form.
- SCIM events show a recent canonicalization change that normalized email by stripping "+" tags; reconciliation job did not merge the two identities.

Expected behavior:
SSO/SCIM canonicalization must be consistent such that SAML/NameID maps to the same internal identity that holds role bindings, or automatic reconciliation should merge duplicates and preserve bindings.

Logs / Relevant traces:
- SAML assertion (trace-id: saml-7a2b): Subject: "alice@redwood.com"
- SCIM provisioning log (trace-id: scim-21f8): PATCH /Users/1189 - changed email to "alice@redwood.com" from "alice+infra@redwood.com"
- Notebooks auth log (trace-id: nb-9c3e): authorization failed - no role binding found for session principal id 0x4e2b

Temporary workaround:
Manual reconciliation applied by identity team: merged the two internal identities and re-attached notebook roles to the canonical account. User was able to sign in and access notebooks after a forced logout/login.

Additional notes:
Checked Okta profile for alice+infra@redwood.com - externalId unchanged; SCIM patch later normalized email to alice@redwood.com.
Identity-proxy change on 2026-03-09 introduced email canonicalization (strip plus-addressing) to comply with downstream analytics. The change was rolled out without updating the reconciliation schedule.
Reconcile job (identity-service/reconciler) was rate-limited by Okta API throttling between 2026-03-09 22:00 and 2026-03-10 02:00 which left duplicates unresolved.
Notebooks service expects principal.email to match existing role bindings exactly; mismatch results in lookup miss and 403. Consider switching to principal.internal_id or adding alias lookup.
Potential edge-case: users who used plus-addressing historically may now have two entries if SCIM normalization runs after a user used Okta initial provisioning with plus-tag.
Applied manual merge of the duplicate identities for the affected user and re-attached notebook role bindings. Asked the reporter to sign out and sign in to pick up the corrected mapping; access confirmed. Rolled back the email canonicalization rule in identity-proxy for the next 24 hours while we prepare a controlled migration. Created a PR to add an alias lookup fallback in notebooks-service and to harden the reconciler with exponential backoff and Okta retry logic (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-service/pull/1524). Follow-ups: schedule a controlled canonicalization migration with a reconciliation run and add a post-migration audit to Confluence runbook.
Create migration playbook to normalize addresses and run reconciler with quotas (owner: Olivia Nguyen)
Implement alias lookup fallback in notebooks-service to avoid authorization misses during migration (owner: Marcus Li)
Add Okta rate-limit handling and retries to reconciler (owner: Identity Team)
Postmortem note and runbook addendum on Confluence - link added to ticket

payload.description:
Issue summary:
During the EU morning peak on 2026-03-10 (~07:12-08:05 UTC), Quantumiq experienced degraded streaming responses and an elevated 5xx rate (~12% 5xx on customer route) caused by sustained inflight request queue saturation. A sharp increase in long-context generation requests (avg seq length ~8k tokens per request) from a single customer key triggered retry amplification and queue buildup in the local reservoir queue.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: intermittent streaming silence, truncated chunks, and increased 5xx/502 responses for ~53 minutes.
- Business: Quantumiq reported product disruptions for internal demos in EU region; support escalation to CS and Sales.
- Billing exposure: tracked as potential overbilling for replays and retries; credit pending.

Timeline (high level):
- 07:12 UTC: Spike detected via route-level SLO alert (p50/p95 token latency increase + 5xx surge).
- 07:17 UTC: Automated graceful-degradation policy attempted fallback to quantized variant but observed backlog amplification.
- 07:25 UTC: Autoscaler did not provide immediate relief due to GPU slot starvation and quota caps on the dedicated pool.
- 07:30-08:05 UTC: SRE engaged; applied temporary per-key concurrency cap and disabled fallback routing for the affected prefix.
- 08:05 UTC: 5xx rate returned to baseline and streaming resumed; remediation actions rolled forward.

Steps to reproduce (repro recipe for engineering):
1) Issue a sustained burst of long-context generation requests (prompt + 8k tokens target) with client-side 3xx retry policy, concurrency ~120 per key, to the Quantumiq route in eu-west.
2) Observe sustained growth of inflight reservoir queue and KV cache thrashing leading to repeated request cancellation and 502 responses.
3) Reproduces when per-customer concurrency caps are higher than pool allowance and autoscaler backoff windows align with the burst.

Relevant logs & links:
- Route dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/routes/quantumiq-eu/overview
- Trace sample: span IDs: trace-77a3.., trace-77a4.. (attached in telemetry bundle)
- Slack escalation: #support-quantumiq (thread TS03K9J4Q)
Measured queue growth: reservoir inflight queue for the Quantumiq route grew from baseline ~20 to >110 concurrent inflight requests during peak (sustained for ~18 minutes).
Autoscaler behavior: GPU pool autoscaler did add nodes but new nodes became usable only after scheduler slot warmup (~6 minutes) due to container cold-start and model warmup time (KV cache population).
Retry amplification: client-side retry policy (3 retries with jitter) caused effective request fanout; combined with long per-request tokenization time this amplified inflight count.
Fallback routing side-effect: graceful fallback to quantized variant attempted to reduce latency but routed additional requests into a smaller reserved pool, causing a local hotspot and backpressure loop.
Telemetry gap: exact trace for earliest 07:12-07:17 window is partial due to sampling; full telemetry captured starting 07:18 when sampling rate was increased.
Immediate mitigation: applied per-key concurrency cap for Quantumiq (50) and disabled graceful fallback routing for the route. SRE drained the reservoir queue via a sliding drain script and temporarily increased pool capacity. Medium-term: merged PR to add early-reject policy for requests with sequence length >7k tokens when router-level concurrency exceeds threshold (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891).
ACTION-1: Product to define new fallback throttling rules (owner: Lena Rodriguez) - due 2026-03-25
ACTION-2: Engineering to implement sliding drain + early reject for extreme-context requests (owner: Marcus Chen) - PR merged; rollout planned 2026-03-14
ACTION-3: CS to coordinate customer communication and confirm acceptability of per-key caps for Quantumiq (owner: Maria Gomez) - follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-13
ACTION-4: Billing to review retry/amplification exposure and propose credit calculation (owner: Priya Nair) - due 2026-03-16
ACTION-5: Observability to increase sampling for route-level traces during high-error windows (owner: Telemetry Squad) - checklist added to runbook
Proposed credit: 15% of March billed usage for Quantumiq's dedicated pool window intersecting incident (pending finance approval).
Customer notified during incident, follow-up postmortem shared on 2026-03-12. Quantumiq accepted temporary cap and requested permanent guardrails; CS scheduled executive briefing for 2026-03-15.
payload.summary: Inflight queue saturation during EU peak causing degraded streaming and 5xx spike for Quantumiq

Issue summary:
Service scheduled jobs that kick off LLM inference runs are intermittently failing with authorization errors after a change rolled to the identity-attribute normalizer. The scheduler can no longer assume the expected principal pattern for several service accounts, and KMS/decryption and model-launch steps are denied.

Impact:
- Several hourly inference pipelines in prod-us-east and nightly experiments in staging-eu-west fail to start (~12 failing runs/hour across teams).
- Customer-facing batch features are not directly impacted yet, but internal retraining/validation jobs are delayed and oncall is paged.

Observed behavior:
- Scheduler logs show authorization failures when exchanging principal identity for downstream roles. Example: "AccessDenied: principal arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/scheduler-runner/session not authorized to kms:Decrypt".
- GCP side shows 403 on IAM Bind when the scheduler attempts to bind a temporary service-account identity: "PermissionDenied: serviceAccount not found for normalized-identity=svc-runner-normalized".
- The identities observed in logs are transformed (normalized) by a recent internal service that rewrites attributes: identity_namespace -> identity_domain and replaces displayName with a short hash. The scheduler expects the pre-normalized displayName pattern.

Environment:
- Scheduler: kubernetes cluster run-scheduler-prod (prod-us-east), run-scheduler-staging (staging-eu-west)
- Auth stack: internal-attribute-normalizer v2.1.0 (rolled 2026-03-09), auth-broker v1.8.3
- Affected resources: KMS keys used to unwrap model secrets, IAM role bindings used by llm-runner, scheduler ServiceAccount -> cross-account assume-role mapping

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Submit a scheduled inference job via the scheduler in prod-us-east.
2) Observe scheduler requesting identity translation from attribute-normalizer.
3) Scheduler attempts to assume downstream role using normalized principal string.
4) Downstream role checks fail and KMS decrypt is denied.

Logs / key excerpts:
- prod-scheduler (2026-03-11T04:12:22Z): "ERROR auth: assume-role failed: AccessDenied for principal 'svc-runner-6a1f' -> expected 'svc-runner-ai-prod'"
- gcp-iam-proxy (2026-03-11T04:12:23Z): "WARN identity-normalizer: rewrite identity_namespace=orgA -> identity_domain=corp.org and display->hash(6a1f)"
- kms-audit (2026-03-11T04:12:24Z): "DENY principal:svc-runner-6a1f action:kms:Decrypt resource:projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/models/cryptoKey1"

Initial hypotheses:
- The attribute-normalizer v2.1.0 introduced a rewrite rule that changes the canonical principal string used by the scheduler to look up role mappings. The lookup fails because the role-mapping table still contains pre-normalized names.
- The role-mapping service does a strict string match and does not consult alternate identifier fields (e.g., originalDisplayName).
- Org policy or a recent org-level migration may have caused some accounts to be rewritten while others keep the old pattern, producing intermittent failures depending on which SA the job runs as.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Rolled attribute-normalizer back in staging to v2.0.5 and staged-scheduler runs resumed in staging.
- For prod, added a hotfix in auth-broker to perform a best-effort reverse lookup mapping normalized hashes back to legacy names (temporary shim). That reduced failures from ~12/hour to ~2/hour.

Next steps / owners:
- SRE (Miguel Ortega): finalize and deploy reverse-lookup shim to prod and monitor for 24h.
- Identity platform (Ruth Chang): audit normalizer rewrite rules and produce a migration plan to expand role-mapping to accept both normalized and legacy identifiers.
- Scheduler product (Aisha Patel): implement fallback lookups in scheduler when role-mapping lookup fails, and add feature flag for strict vs tolerant matching.

2026-03-11: Traced failing runs to attribute-normalizer rollout. Pattern shows jobs scheduled under accounts that were migrated by org-policy earlier this month. 2026-03-11 18:00: Rolled back normalizer in staging; staging runs recovered. 2026-03-11 20:30: Hotpatch auth-broker in prod to add reverse-hash lookup using previous displayName cache. Need a persistent fix: expand role-mapping keys and add unit tests for new normalizer behavior. 2026-03-12: Observed residual failures tied to archived service accounts that were not present in displayName cache. Consider seeding cache from identity-store export.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 02:45 - SRE oncall (Harpreet Singh): Pager triggered; confirmed KMS denies and correlated with normalizer rollout at 01:30 UTC.
TBD - temporary reverse-lookup shim in prod reduced impact. Permanent fix requires identity-platform to expand role-mapping keys and scheduler to add tolerant lookup. Plan: seed role-mapping table from identity-store export and release coordinated rollout with feature flags. Target: complete migration and remove shim by 2026-03-20.

payload.description:
Requester: Security Engineering (Kevin Osei)
Service/Area: Usage Insights export (CSV) + signed download URLs

Background
Security review for Usage Insights beta flagged that our existing audit events for downloads are missing required context to support:
- Customer requests for “who exported what, when, from where”
- Restricted workspace controls (cost visibility + exports)
- Incident response / forensic workflows when a share link or signed URL is used

Problem
The current audit log entry for export downloads only records a generic “download” action and user identifier. We need additional fields and consistent event naming so that exported cost data can be traced and reconciled.

Request
Add/extend audit log events for Usage Insights exports with additional fields.

Proposed event names
1) usage_insights.export.created
2) usage_insights.export.downloaded
3) usage_insights.export.failed (optional but preferred)

Required fields (minimum)
- event_name
- occurred_at
- actor_user_id
- actor_email (or actor_principal if SSO)
- actor_type (user | api_key | service)
- workspace_id
- project_id (nullable)
- environment (prod/staging)
- export_job_id
- export_type (route_model_breakdown | top_cost_drivers | other)
- time_range_start, time_range_end (ISO-8601; timezone explicit)
- filters (stringified, canonical order; see notes)
- resource_scope (workspace | project)
- rbac_decision (allowed | denied) + denied_reason (if denied)
- request_ip
- user_agent

Strongly recommended fields
- file_name
- file_size_bytes
- row_count (if available)
- signed_url_ttl_seconds
- download_method (console_ui | api | share_link)
- share_link_id (if download initiated via share link)
- region (where the export job executed / where the request was served)

Notes / Constraints
- Avoid logging raw prompt text or any customer content.
- “filters” must not include high-cardinality user-provided strings (e.g., arbitrary route names pre-normalization). Prefer logging:
  - route_template (normalized)
  - model_family + model_version_bucket
- If filters are logged as a single string, they should be stable and parseable (e.g., key=value pairs in sorted key order).

Acceptance criteria
- A successful export flow results in:
  - created event on export job creation
  - downloaded event on file retrieval (including when using signed URL)
- A denied export attempt logs a denied audit event with rbac_decision=denied and denied_reason.
- Audit fields are present in our central audit sink (same place other console security events land).
- Fields validated with 2 test cases:
  - user with Cost Viewer permission exports from console
  - user without permission attempts export and is denied (audit logs show denial)

Customer/Compliance drivers
- Supports enterprise security questionnaires and audit requirements (Northstar Fintech-style asks)
- Supports internal escalation path for discrepancies (ref: SUP-24811 - customer asked for export traceability when totals didn’t match invoice)

Links
- PR implementing export job + signed URLs: sources/github/redwood/pr-23148-export-csv-endpoint-and-signed-downloads.json
- RBAC gating PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-23160-rbac-gating-for-cost-and-export.json

---
Comments

2026-01-27 (Kevin Osei)
Creating this as an internal support task from the security review thread. Current download audit events don’t include workspace/project, export_job_id, or IP/UA. We need this before enabling beta allowlist beyond the initial handful.

2026-01-28 (Kaitlyn Nguyen)
Ack. I’ll coordinate with Dylan/Chloe to ensure the export endpoints emit an audit event at both job creation and download. Question: is “filters” acceptable as a JSON blob? (We try to avoid nested payloads in audit sink.)

2026-01-28 (Kevin Osei)
Prefer a stable string field over nested JSON for now. Key ordering matters; we’ve had issues searching audit logs when the formatting varies. Also please include rbac_decision in the event so we can prove access control enforcement.

2026-01-30 (Dylan Brooks)
We can emit:
- export.created when the async export job is queued
- export.downloaded when the signed URL endpoint is minted (or when the object is fetched?)
We currently mint URLs server-side; actual object GET happens on storage.

2026-01-30 (Kevin Osei)
For beta, minting the signed URL is acceptable as “downloaded” if we also include signed_url_ttl_seconds and file_name. Longer term we may add storage access logs correlation, but not required for this milestone.

2026-02-01 (Kaitlyn Nguyen)
Implemented audit payload additions in the export service. Added denied event for permission failures. Sent PR update request on pr-23148.

2026-02-04 (Kevin Osei)
Reviewed staging audit sink: events present with workspace_id, export_job_id, IP, UA, and rbac_decision. Filters are in canonical key order, looks good. One nit: actor_email empty for SSO users; can we populate actor_principal?

2026-02-05 (Kaitlyn Nguyen)
Updated to include actor_principal when email absent. Also added download_method=console_ui. Merged into pr-23148.

2026-02-06 (Kevin Osei)
Confirmed in prod-like environment. Closing.

Follow-ups
- Consider adding correlation ID between signed URL mint and storage GET (if/when required by enterprise customers).
- Consider export.failed emission on warehouse timeouts (nice-to-have).
payload.summary: Request: add additional audit log fields for Usage Insights CSV export downloads

payload.description:
During onboarding of a new Dedicated customer cluster for Private deployments, the automated provisioner failed at the KMS step. The flow expects to create an encrypted configuration blob using a customer-scoped CMK and call kms:Encrypt. The call is blocked by an organizational SCP that denies kms:Encrypt when requests originate from the 'infra-provisioner' principal path. Error surfaced in provisioner logs and blocked the onboarding flow.
Onboarding blocked for one new Dedicated customer (private deployment). This prevents spinning up the customer's isolated infra and delays go-live. No production serving traffic affected yet, but customer-facing SRE/CSR escalation happened. Estimated delay 24-48 hours without workaround.
1) Trigger onboarding job: repo infra/provisioner -> pipeline run 'provision-dedicated-onboarding' for tenant 'tenant-phi'.
2) Pipeline reaches step 'encrypt-config-with-cmk' which calls AWS KMS Encrypt API with key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh.
3) Call fails with AccessDenied and org policy evaluation log indicates an SCP deny matched for action 'kms:Encrypt' on principal path 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/infra-provisioner'.
Commands used during repro:
- aws kms encrypt --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh --plaintext fileb://config.enc --profile provisioner
- aws sts get-caller-identity --profile provisioner

Provisioner stderr excerpt:
2026-03-09T15:12:02Z ERROR kms:Encrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/infra-provisioner/session-xyz is not authorized to perform: kms:Encrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh
(org-eval-id: ORG-EVAL-2026-03-09-1)
AWS CloudTrail sample event id: 9e8f7c6a-1b2c-4dbe-99a4-0f1a2b3c4d5e

Initial hypothesis: CMK policy restricts kms:Encrypt to a narrow principal set.
- Checked CMK key policy and found it permits account root and key-usage-role but no explicit allowance for infra-provisioner role.
- Policy simulator against the provisioner assumed-role shows org SCP deny as highest-priority decision. Example SCP snippet we found in org root:
  {
    "Effect": "Deny",
    "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*"],
    "Resource": "*",
    "Condition": {"StringLike": {"aws:PrincipalTag/role": "sensitive-*"}}
  }
- Provisioner role does not carry the expected tag; it is evaluated as matching the deny due to a tag inheritance quirk introduced in recent org policy rollout.
- Temporal repro: when we ran the same encrypt call from an ad-hoc admin role (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/platform-admin) it succeeded.
- Cross-check: no VPC endpoint or KMS key policy logs indicate a service-side deny; decision explicitly from org SCP evaluation.
- Eng-runbook referenced: confluence: 'private-deploy/onboarding-kms-guardrails' which notes SCPs are enforced at account eval time and will override key policies.
Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-09: Customer onboarding job failed during KMS encrypt. Raising P1 because onboarding blocked.
Marco Chen (Assignee) 2026-03-09: Captured CloudTrail and org policy eval. Looks like an org SCP deny — submitting to OrgAdmins for temporary exception. Will attempt delegated-key workaround.
OrgAdminBot 2026-03-10: Confirmed org SCP 'deny-sensitive-kms' was applied 2026-02-28 as part of hardening sweep. Condition uses PrincipalTag role prefix; infra-provisioner role update planned but not yet rolled out.
Marco Chen 2026-03-10: Applied temporary workaround: created a scoped IAM role 'provisioner-kms-relay' with explicit allow for kms:Encrypt and ensured session is assumed by a short-lived admin broker which is exempt from SCP deny via tag-based exception. Tested encrypt call successful. Notified CS and left follow-up ticket to remove workaround once org policy corrected.
Security 2026-03-11: We agree short-lived workaround acceptable for one-off onboarding. Need audit trail and retention. Raised request to OrgAdmins to refine SCP condition and add explicit allow-list for our infra provisioning pipeline.
Temporary workaround: a short-lived relay role was created to perform KMS encrypt operations and was limited to this onboarding run. The onboarding completed successfully 2026-03-11 using the relay role.
Permanent fix plan: (1) OrgAdmins to update the deny SCP to exclude the infra provisioning principal path (or require a tag pattern that the provisioner will explicitly set); (2) Update infra/provisioner to attach required PrincipalTags on assume-role sessions and add an automated validation test in the provisioning CI that simulates KMS encrypt under current org SCPs.
Follow-ups: INT-947663 (related assume-role chain failures) referenced for org policy remediation; create new RFC to add an integration test gating onboarding PRs.
payload.summary: Org-level deny policy prevents kms:Encrypt for dedicated onboarding agent, blocking Private deployment provisioning
