Issue summary:
Newly provisioned service accounts created via the service-mesh control plane intermittently receive an SSO assertion where certain claims (notably 'aud' and a custom 'roles' array) are being trimmed/truncated by the mesh gateway. When the trimmed assertion is consumed by internal RBAC services, token validation succeeds but role assignment fails, producing 403s for the K8s dashboard and the internal DB-provisioning console.

Impact:
- Several infra automation jobs and platform engineers reported failing access to the k8s dashboard and the DB-provisioning UI after creating service accounts through the mesh.
- Affected flows are limited to newly issued service-account assertions (existing sessions remain valid).
- Estimated ~12 teams impacted across infra and platform in us-west.

Environment:
- Prod cluster behind service-mesh gateway (env: prod/us-west).
- Mesh control plane version: meshctl v2.7.1.
- SSO provider: Okta (SAML->OIDC bridge in the mesh).
- RBAC enforcement: internal auth-service v3.4.0 using 'roles' claim mapped from SSO assertion.

Steps to reproduce:
1) In prod-us-west, create a new service account via meshctl (provisioning path used by platform-automation).
2) Trigger the onboarding job which requests an SSO assertion for the new account.
3) Attempt to access Kubernetes dashboard as that service account or use the DB-provisioning console.
4) Observe RBAC denying access with 403 and symptoms in auth-service logs.

Observed logs / errors:
- auth-service: "RBAC: role mapping missing for subject=sa-mesh-20260312 org=infra"
- mesh-gateway (ingress): "Assertion sanitized: dropped claim 'roles' length=0 -> trimmed"
- Okta assertion logs (SAML bridge): shows full 'roles' present upstream; trimmed state appears after mesh gateway step.

Workaround applied:
- Platform SRE temporarily bypassed the mesh gateway for the provisioning callback path (route flagged to passthrough SSO headers) which restored correct claims and allowed affected service accounts to access the dashboard and console.

Desired end state:
- Fix in mesh gateway to preserve custom SSO claims (roles, aud) for service-account assertions and deploy a patch to prod-us-west.
- Add automated integration test for SSO claim preservation in the mesh provisioning flow.

Support (2026-03-12): Triage - beginning investigation with SRE and mesh team. Slack thread #platform-auth: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CPLATFORMAUTH/p1612345678000
SRE - Alejandro (2026-03-12): Applied temporary passthrough route to provisioning callback to unblock teams; monitoring for side effects. Recorded change in runbook: https://confluence.redwood/internal/runbooks/sso-provisioning-passthrough
Platform Eng - Priya (2026-03-13): Confirmed Okta assertions upstream include 'roles' and 'aud'. Observed trimming in mesh-gateway container logs. Added initial hypothesis that an L7 policy sanitizes header payloads over size threshold.
Mesh Team - Lukas (2026-03-13): Reproduced locally with meshctl v2.7.1 and saw claim trimming when header length > 8kb. Filed GH issue and starting patch: https://github.com/redwood/mesh-gateway/pull/492
SRE (2026-03-14): Will schedule a targeted canary deploy of the mesh-gateway patch to prod-us-west tonight in a staged rollout and monitor auth-service metrics and 403 rate.
01 - Reproduced the failure by creating new SA and capturing traffic between mesh-gateway and auth-service; observed header truncation at mesh-gateway egress.
02 - Confirmed Okta SAML->OIDC bridge emits full roles claim in JSON assertion; mesh-gateway configured with an L7 policy that rewrites headers to a custom 'x-ss-assertion' value which truncates long payloads.
03 - Hypothesis: Mesh gateway rewrites and stores assertion in a cookie/header which has a length limit and internal trimming logic introduced in v2.6.9. Regression introduced in PR #447.
04 - Mitigated by passthrough route; verified auth-service received full claim and RBAC mapping succeeded for test accounts.
05 - Risk assessment: patching mesh-gateway is low risk if canaried; but global config changes to header size caps could impact other large-claim assertions (SAML groups arrays).
Mitigation: passthrough route created to bypass mesh-gateway assertion rewrite for provisioning callback (applied 2026-03-12).
Planned fix: mesh-gateway patch merged PR #492 to preserve claim payloads; canary rollout scheduled 2026-03-14 23:00 UTC to prod-us-west.
Follow-up: add regression test in mesh-gateway CI to reject PRs that shrink/strip SSO claims; update runbook to document claim-size limits.
payload.summary: Service-mesh SSO claim trimming prevents new service accounts from accessing K8s dashboard and DB-provisioning console

Issue summary:
Customer's private deployment (Acme Analytics, private tier) reports intermittent failures when the agent attempts to download model artifacts and make downstream HTTPS calls to model-registry.redwood-internal.net. DNS resolution succeeds for all requests, but TLS handshakes sometimes fail with certificate name mismatch or the client aborts during ServerHello. Small API calls (token checks, pings) usually succeed; large model downloads fail ~30% of the time.

Impact:
- Model pulls for new containers occasionally fail causing model startup retries and longer cold-starts for customers.
- Streaming inference for long responses sometimes resets mid-stream when the model endpoint is reloaded.

Environment:
- Private deployment (on-customer VPC) with VPC endpoint to Redwood's model-registry, routing through corporate perimeter firewall performing TLS inspection.
- Region: us-west-2
- Agent version: 1.12.0
- Serving runtime: rwd-svc-2026-02

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a model pull via the Console or run a job that requires a cold-start for redwood-open-7B-v1.
2) Observe logs in agent (agent.log) and attempt manual curl from a jump host inside the same VPC: curl -v https://model-registry.redwood-internal.net/v1/models
3) Repeatedly issue downloads; intermittent failures observed.

Observed behavior:
- DNS returns correct A records consistently.
- curl -v shows TCP handshake completes, but in failing cases the ClientHello seen by the server lacks an SNI extension (verified via tcpdump on customer network).
- Server returns default certificate (CN does not match expected host) causing client certificate name mismatch error.
- When SNI is present (successful TLS handshakes), connections proceed normally.
- Agent logs: "tls: server certificate does not match expected name" or "handshake aborted by peer" on failing attempts.

Expected behavior:
- TLS ClientHello includes SNI with model-registry.redwood-internal.net and server presents correct certificate for that name, allowing handshake to complete consistently.

Logs / Evidence attached by customer:
- tcpdump (pcap) showing alternating ClientHello packets: some contain SNI extension, some do not.
- curl -v outputs for success and failure cases.
- Agent logs excerpt and model-pull stack traces.

Investigation notes (Support):
- Reproduced handshake mismatch in our lab by removing SNI from ClientHello; server returns default vhost certificate and client fails verification.
- Hypothesis: Corporate TLS inspection appliance (explicit TLS proxy) is either stripping or rewriting the SNI extension when proxying outbound TLS flows, or it is performing a re-encapsulation without preserving the original SNI. This results in the backend load balancer selecting the default certificate.
- Intermittent nature explained by: appliance is stateful and some flows are proxied differently based on session affinity or connection reuse; some agent processes reuse connections that already had SNI preserved.
- Confirmed no rate-limiting or 5xx on Redwood side for these requests during captured windows.

Suggested actions / Workaround:
- Short term: Customer's firewall team to configure TLS inspection to preserve SNI for hosts matching *.redwood-internal.net or create an allowlist so TLS bypass is performed for model-registry endpoints.
- Alternative: Configure the agent to use an internal HTTP proxy that performs TLS passthrough (no MITM) for registry hosts. Agent supports an explicit PROXY env to route only model pulls.
- Customer has provided corporate firewall logs and agreed to test an allowlist.

Next steps / Requested from customer:
1) Firewall/proxy team to confirm whether SNI rewriting/stripping is enabled and test an allowlist bypass for model-registry.redwood-internal.net.
2) Provide an additional pcap after bypass is applied to verify SNI is present in all ClientHello packets.
3) If bypass not possible, confirm whether corporate CA is being injected and whether the agent runtime trusts that CA (note: trusting injected CAs weakens security; preferred solution is bypass for known Redwood endpoints).

Resolution notes:
- Pending customer firewall change. Support has documented exact hostnames and IP ranges to allow. If customer applies the allowlist and problem persists, escalate to Networking Eng (linked INT-1142) and provide fresh pcaps.

References:
- Internal TLS Inspection runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/9842/TLS+Inspection+Runbook
- Related GH issue updating agent proxy handling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-tools/pull/342

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 08:37 - Customer (Acme Network Ops): We see an explicit proxy performing TLS inspection; policy shows 'normalize SNI' option. We'll test bypass for *.redwood-internal.net and report back.
payload.summary: Private deployment: corporate TLS inspection stripping SNI causes certificate mismatch and intermittent model downloads

Issue summary: Finance Ops has identified a discrepancy in per-customer token billing for a 48-hour window and requests a minimal, obfuscated slice of production request/response metadata to reconcile. Impact: potential underbilling for a small set (~120) of customer accounts; customer-facing invoices may be affected if we cannot reconcile. Finance needs low-fidelity evidence (hashed identifiers + anonymized payload lengths/tokens) to reconcile internal billing ledgers and produce corrected invoices if required. Request
- We are ramping volume for the Hosted API onboarding email v2 as part of the Lifecycle Growth Experiments sprint.
- Need confirmation that Redwood’s sending domain authentication is correctly set up and aligned with our current provider (SendGrid), and that SPF/DKIM/DMARC are passing with alignment for the From domain.

Background / impact
- We saw an increase in “didn’t receive onboarding email” reports and deliverability variability as we started ramping (esp. Gmail).
- Risk: scaling volume without correct authentication will amplify spam folder placement and/or bounces, and invalidate experiment readouts.

Scope
1) DNS: verify SPF record(s) for the From domain used by lifecycle emails.
2) DNS: verify DKIM keys (CNAMEs) for SendGrid authenticated domain are present and matching SendGrid UI.
3) DNS: verify DMARC exists and is reasonable for our current maturity (monitor first, then tighten).
4) SendGrid: verify authenticated domain + custom return-path/bounce domain configured, and that the From address matches the authenticated domain.

What I need from Internal Support / Marketing Ops

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Multiple private upgrade end-to-end CI jobs are exceeding configured job time limits (90m) and being killed, primarily in the nightly suite but also intermittently in PR gating for upgrade-related changes.
- Failures are clustered around upgrade apply / post-upgrade verification stages where we wait for Helm hook jobs (migrations, preupgrade checks) and for data-plane rollouts.

Impact
- Nightly signal for “Private upgrade + rollback mechanism” is degraded (false negatives). PRs touching installer/charts are delayed due to re-runs and manual triage.
- Risk: release gating for Private upgrades becomes unreliable, increasing chance of regressions landing without coverage.

What’s failing (examples)
- Job: private-upgrade-e2e (k8s 1.28, CSI/Rook)
  - Step that times out: “installer upgrade apply”
  - Last log line (typical):
    - "Waiting for job/redwood-migrate to complete (hook: pre-upgrade)"
    - "helm upgrade --install … timed out waiting for the condition"
- Job: private-upgrade-e2e (k8s 1.27, EBS)
  - Step that times out: “post-upgrade verify”
  - Last log line (typical):
    - "Waiting for deployment/redwood-control-plane to become Ready"

Scope / test context
- Suite executes N-1 → N in-place upgrade for Redwood Private on ephemeral clusters.
- Currently includes control-plane first, then data-plane, plus verification (API health, DB connectivity, basic inference smoke).

Investigation notes
1) Pattern analysis (last 10 occurrences)
- ~60%: stuck in Helm hook job completion (migrate/preupgrade) until job timeout.
- ~30%: image pull delays on cold runners (large images + no local cache). Logs show extended time between “Pulling image …” and container start; also occasional registry throttling on the runner egress path.
- ~10%: slow rollout for data-plane deployment due to node resource pressure; observed pending pods waiting on CPU/memory on smaller runner nodes.

2) Cluster signals (from job artifacts)
- kubectl get jobs shows migrate job in Active for >45m in several failures.
- migrate logs sometimes show long lock waits / low output frequency, which makes it hard to tell if it’s making progress or deadlocked.
- When we repro locally with debug, migration itself completes but total wall time varies heavily depending on image pull cache state.

3) Recent changes that could contribute
- Chart hook ordering / timeouts were adjusted recently; this may have increased the time we wait for hooks by default in some scenarios.
- DB migration guardrails are landing (idempotency + lock timeouts), but not fully rolled into the E2E suite baseline at the time of the earliest failures.

Root cause (most likely)
- CI wall-clock time variance pushed the suite over the global job timeout:
  - cold runner image pulls + no pre-pull caching
  - helm hook jobs have conservative timeouts and can sit waiting on DB locks with limited progress output
  - cluster sizing for some E2E permutations is near the minimum, causing rollout delays

Mitigation / changes applied
Immediate (done)
- Increased CI job timeout from 90m → 150m for private-upgrade-e2e nightly jobs while we stabilize (temporary).
- Reduced concurrency for the heaviest permutations to avoid saturating runner node resources.
- Added artifact collection on timeout (kubectl describe jobs/pods, events, top nodes) to make future failures actionable.

Short-term (done / in progress)
- Added an explicit pre-pull step for the heaviest images used in the suite on self-hosted runners.
- Adjusted helm upgrade invocation in the E2E harness to emit periodic progress (polling rollout status with timestamps) so “stalls” are visible.

Follow-ups (tracked outside this ticket)
- Split the suite: separate “upgrade apply” from “post-upgrade verify” so a single slow rollout doesn’t consume the whole budget.
- Improve determinism: pin base images and preload images into runner cache for nightly.
- Ensure DB migration jobs have bounded lock wait + clear failure mode; align E2E baseline with migration guardrails.

Acceptance criteria
- Nightly private-upgrade-e2e suite passes 5 consecutive runs without timeout.
- If timeouts occur, artifacts must identify the bottleneck stage (image pull vs hook job vs rollout) within 5 minutes of triage.

Resolution
- After applying timeout bump + runner pre-pull + improved artifact capture, the last 6 nightly runs (2025-06-09 through 2025-06-11) completed within 78–112 minutes and did not hit the global timeout.
- Marking as Resolved; keeping watch via nightly dashboard and will reopen if timeouts recur.
2025-06-06 09:18 (Sahana Iyer): Creating INT for repeated private upgrade E2E timeouts. Seen 3/5 nightlies fail this week; also hit once on PR gating for charts. Attaching last job logs + timestamps in build artifacts.
2025-06-06 10:02 (Devon Price): Taking. First look: global 90m job timeout triggers before helm upgrade timeout in a few cases. Suspect image pull + small runner nodes. Will add artifact capture on cancel and compare wall time distribution.
2025-06-07 14:41 (Rafael Mendes): +1 on resource pressure. In two failures, nodes were ~95% mem; data-plane pods pending for ~20m. Recommend reducing concurrency or bump runner size for the heavy permutations.
2025-06-08 11:27 (Devon Price): Implemented timeout bump to 150m for nightly only + reduced concurrency for the Rook/CSI permutation. Also added on-timeout collection of kubectl get/describe + events. Next nightly should be more actionable.
2025-06-09 08:05 (Devon Price): Nightly passed (total 101m). Biggest single chunk was image pull (~23m) on cold runner. Adding explicit pre-pull step for images referenced by installer + charts to cut variance.
2025-06-10 16:12 (Sahana Iyer): PR gating still on 90m and is borderline for the heaviest matrix. Suggest we either (a) split the test or (b) run only a lighter permutation on PR gating and keep full matrix nightly.
2025-06-11 09:36 (Devon Price): Last 6 nightlies green (78–112m). Pre-pull reduced worst-case pull time. Marking resolved with plan to split suite for PR gating in follow-up work.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A vendor-sent PDF invoice (vendor ID VND-78421) contains a handwritten correction to the VAT line (originally 20% crossed out and replaced with 19%). The OCR pipeline ingested the PDF and captured the VAT amount as if it were 20%, which caused the automated 3-way match and tax validation rules to flag the invoice and place it on hold.

Impact:
- Single invoice on payment run hold (payment due next week) affecting vendor relationship for EU regional supplier.
- Manual intervention required to approve/override, delaying AP throughput.
- Potential tax reporting mismatch if paid with incorrect VAT.

Environment:
- AP automation pipeline (prod) feeding into payments export (SEPA) for eu-west region.
- OCR pipeline v2.3.1 running on inference-ocr cluster.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Upload invoice_78421_scans.pdf to AP intake bucket.
2) OCR pipeline extracts fields into ocr_extract_78421.json.
3) AP validation service compares VAT percentage against PO/line-item expectations.
4) Validation rules detect mismatch and set invoice status to "Hold: VAT mismatch".

Observed behavior:
- OCR captured VAT rate as 20% and VAT amount of 240.00 EUR.
- The invoice header shows handwritten correction to 19% and VAT 228.00 EUR (handwritten adjacent to typed line).
- AP service flagged as discrepancy and blocked payment export.

Expected behavior:
- OCR or downstream validation should surface the handwritten override as a low-confidence field and attach an image snippet for manual review rather than auto-hold without context.

Initial logs and artifacts:
- ocr_extract_78421.json shows vat_rate: "20%", vat_amount: "240.00" with confidence 0.88 for the typed field and a separate detected annotation with confidence 0.42 for handwritten text.
- AP validation log: "VAT_MISMATCH: expected 19% per vendor contract; detected 20% from OCR; hold applied."
- S3 object paths: s3://ap-intake/2026-03-09/invoice_78421_scans.pdf

Notes on vendor/contract:
- Vendor VND-78421 has a standing contract specifying 19% VAT for these services (contract in Confluence link above). PO-55233 attached to invoice expects 19% VAT.

Requested immediate action:
- Allow manual override path for this invoice with an explicit flag and audit trail so AP can release payment while preserving evidence for tax reporting.
- Backend: improve OCR/validation to attach low-confidence handwritten detections as evidence instead of auto-hold where contract/PO suggests the lower rate.

03-10: Triage by AP automation. Confirmed invoice present in intake and flagged by validation rule. 03-11: OCR team inspected ocr_extract_78421.json; found separate handwritten annotation detected with low confidence. 03-11: Hypothesis - current rule treats any mismatch between OCR-detected fields and PO as immediate hold without examining alternative low-confidence detections or vendor contract metadata. 03-12: Ran a synthetic test with similar handwritten corrections; pipeline consistently prefers higher-confidence typed value and does not escalate handwritten snippets for manual review. 03-12: Finance ops confirms vendor contract and PO both indicate 19% VAT.
Workaround: AP can perform a manual override for INT-410222 using the 'AP Manual Review' console: attach scanned invoice, set 'verified_vat' to 19% and add comment referencing vendor contract. This will allow the next SEPA export to include the invoice.
Short-term resolution (next 3 business days): add an intermediate 'LowConfidenceAnnotation' review step to validation to flag but not auto-hold when a low-confidence handwritten detection contradicts typed OCR and PO/contract indicates a specific tax rate.
Medium-term resolution (2-4 weeks): update OCR post-processing to: 1) surface all detected annotations with confidence scores in AP UI; 2) add rule to prefer contract/PO VAT when detected handwritten correction has confidence >= 0.35 and typed field confidence < 0.9; 3) add telemetry/metric for handwritten overrides for further tuning.
Owners: AP Automation (Lucas Chen) + OCR team (Priya Rao).
payload.summary: Supplier invoice held in AP due to handwritten VAT correction captured incorrectly by OCR

Issue summary: After the 1.7 runtime migration (rolled out to Dedicated clusters in us-east on 2025-02-09), LinguaWorks reported elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat-completion streams. Impact: interactive chat experiences are seeing 600ms-2.2s additional latency on first token causing user-facing slow initial responses and some timeouts for low-latency SLAs. Scope: observed across multiple models on the customer's dedicated pool and correlated with runtime rollout window.

2) Start a fresh chat session with a ~900-token system prompt and an initial user message

Summary: Following the staged rollout of the Okta claim-transformer service (v2.4.0) on 2026-03-13, a subset of internal users received tokens where role claims no longer matched Redwood RBAC expectations. Impact: ~30 engineers temporarily lost access to the Sentinel monitoring console (403 on console login and missing role assertions in service tokens). Scope: internal users authenticated via Okta SSO in the us-east-1 prod region. Business impact: Alerting dashboards inaccessible to oncall rotation; delayed incident triage for one active P2 incident. This ticket tracks triage, rollback/hotfix, and follow-up verification.
1) Authenticate via Okta SSO as a user in monitoring group (okta group: redwood-monitoring-viewers).
2) Exchange SAML/OIDC assertion at auth-service token endpoint (/v1/token).
3) Attempt to access Sentinel console: console returns 403 and header x-rbac-missing-role shows 'monitor:viewer' expected but token contains 'monitorviewer'.
4) Inspect id/access token claims and compare 'roles' vs legacy 'entitlements' claims.

2026-03-13T21:14:08Z sentinel-auth WARN token-assertion: expected role 'monitor:viewer' not found in token.roles; token.roles=['infra-admin','billing:read']
Okta System Log: 2026-03-13T21:13:59Z TRANSFORMER_UPDATE user_jid=U12345 transform=claim_transformer_v2.4.0 applied
Initial hypothesis: claim-transformer v2.4.0 introduced stricter normalization that strips colons/prefix separators when converting Okta group names into RBAC roles.
Reproduced locally by invoking claim-transformer with sample SAML assertion: group 'redwood-monitoring-viewers' -> output role 'monitorviewer' (missing ':').
Auth-service RBAC plugin expects roles in 'resource:action' format (example 'monitor:viewer'). The new normalization collapses separator characters, causing mismatch.

Action plan: Rollback claim-transformer to v2.3.9 for prod us-east-1 during low-traffic window and deploy hotfix that preserves ':' separators in role normalization.

payload.description:
Issue summary
- Growth/Marketing and Product flagged a sudden drop and cross-source mismatch in the activation funnel metrics (signup → API key created → first request) used for the Lifecycle Growth Experiments sprint.
- Primary symptom: EU-West conversion from signup → api_key_created appeared ~12–18% lower than US-East starting 2026-01-21 18:00 UTC, and overall “new signups” appeared higher than expected vs auth/user tables.
- Impact: Week 1–2 experiment readouts risked being invalid/noisy; we paused one planned expansion of the email A/B until numbers were reconciled.

Impact
- Affected dashboards: Activation Funnel (Observability Pack) + internal Looker view used by Growth.
- Impacted decisions: stop/go thresholds and lift calculations for onboarding email v2 and console nudge experiments.
- Customer impact: none direct (reporting/measurement issue only), but could cause us to make incorrect product/GT-M decisions.

Detection
- Reported via Slack #help thread ("events missing in one region") and follow-up in #eng-platform on 2026-01-22.
- Observability Pack funnel panel showed EU-West drop; Mei Lin noted mismatch vs daily new users in warehouse.

What changed recently
- PR-28431: added/standardized activation events for signup → api key → first request → first 100k tokens.
- PR-241: new dashboard panels + funnel query definitions.
- Console nudge framework shipped behind flags; additional event properties and cohort assignment introduced during the week.

Initial hypotheses
1) Ingestion lag or partial pipeline outage in EU-West.
2) Region routing misconfiguration (EU events landing in US dataset or vice versa).
3) Event validation rejecting records due to missing required properties (user_id, event_id) for EU only.
4) Duplicate event emission inflating baseline in one region, making EU look like it dropped.

Investigation notes (high level)
- Confirmed ingestion health: Kafka consumer lag normal; no sustained drop in raw event volume by region at the edge collectors.
- Cross-checked three sources for the same window (2026-01-21 00:00–2026-01-22 23:59 UTC):
  - Raw collector logs: stable event counts in eu-west.
  - Warehouse fact_events table: stable api_key_created events in eu-west.
  - Activation Funnel dashboard: apparent eu-west drop.
- Found the discrepancy was query-side + dedupe behavior:
  - The funnel panel’s Step 1 “signup” was keyed off signup_created events and deduped by (user_id, day), but the Step 1 event was being emitted twice for a subset of flows in US-East due to a console/auth edge case.
  - EU-West had fewer duplicates, so the “conversion rate” (step2/step1) looked artificially worse in EU-West when comparing regions.
  - Additionally, the dashboard query used a join that unintentionally filtered some EU users when event_time skew occurred near midnight UTC (session boundary + region bucket), amplifying the appearance of a regional issue.

Root cause
- Duplicate emission of signup_created/signup_completed for users who hit both (a) email verification completion and (b) immediate console onboarding flow that retriggered the signup event. This was more common in US-East due to traffic mix and a feature-flag exposure path.
- Dashboard query logic for Step 1 + Step 2 used inconsistent dedupe keys (Step 1 deduped by user_id/day; Step 2 deduped by event_id) and a region/date join condition that excluded a portion of EU events at boundary times.
- Net effect: inflated Step 1 counts in US-East and undercounted Step 2 in EU-West in the visualization layer, while the warehouse raw events were largely correct.

Resolution
- Engineering fix: PR-28521 shipped to stop duplicate signup event emission; verified by before/after comparison on a canary cohort and then full rollout.
- Analytics fix: updated Activation Funnel panel query to use consistent dedupe (event_id preferred, fallback to (user_id, event_name, request_id) for older records) and removed the join condition that filtered EU events at UTC boundaries.
- Backfill: no backfill required for canonical fact tables; dashboard now recomputes accurately from warehouse. Noted that historical conversion rates for 2026-01-19 to 2026-01-22 should be interpreted with caution; we annotated the dashboard.

Validation
- Post-fix checks (2026-01-26):
  - Regional conversion rates are within expected variance (eu-west no longer showing step-change).
  - New user counts align within ~1–2% between auth table and deduped signup events.
  - Funnel step drop-offs align with expected product behavior and match secondary metrics (API key creation table).

Follow-ups
- Add a data-quality alert: spike in duplicate rate for signup_created and api_key_created by region.
- Add unit tests/contract tests for event emission idempotency in console/auth flows.
- Document dedupe keys and “source of truth” definitions in the activation metrics notes + dashboard README.

Stakeholders
- Growth: Ben Carter (experiment owner), Tyler Benson (attribution)
- Product: Marissa Cole (console), Paula Mendes (telemetry/rollouts)
- Eng/Analytics: Logan Wright (assigned), Nadia Rahman, Mei Lin

References
- Slack: #help (tracking discrepancy), #eng-platform (taxonomy + dedupe)
- Related PRs: PR-28431, PR-28521, Observability Pack PR-241

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Automated priority inference service (enrichment-service v2.6.0) is intermittently adding duplicate escalation labels and triggering cascading reroutes across the support routing templates. The duplication causes tickets to be routed to multiple escalation queues and creates artificially inflated SLA escalations in reporting.

Impact:
- Internal routing churn: a single incoming ticket gets duplicated routing bindings across two escalation tracks for ~5-12 minutes before de-dup resolves.
- Alert noise: SLA breach dashboards show spurious increases for P1 cohorts (up to +8 percentage points) during run windows.
- Potential customer-impact risk if real escalations are delayed by misrouted duplicates.

Environment:
- prod | us-east
- Affected services: enrichment-service (priority inference), template-indexer, routing-engine, analytics pipeline.
- Observed after a template-indexer deployment on 2026-03-11 (indexer v4.1.0).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Inbound ticket passes through enrichment-service which computes priority and suggested labels.
2) Template-indexer receives enrichment output and applies template bindings.
3) Routing-engine expands bindings and creates route assignments.
4) In some runs, enrichment emits both `escalation:team-alpha` and `escalation:team-alpha_v2` transiently for same ticket id due to race between TTL refresh and ancestry merge.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate escalation labels for same ticket ID persisted in routing-engine for ~5-12m until the template dedupe job runs.
- Analytics shows duplicate increments in per-route SLA counters.
- Manual fixes (support unassign + reassign) temporarily resolve.

Expected behavior:
- Enrichment should emit a single canonical escalation label per inference cycle. Template-indexer should dedupe overlapping bindings deterministically. Routing-engine should ignore near-duplicate bindings within the configured merge window.

Notes on urgency:
Given the P1 severity and visible SLA noise for internal dashboards used in escalations, this needs immediate mitigation while we implement a root-cause fix.
2026-03-12 09:18 - Initial triage by Support; observed correlation with template-indexer deploy on 2026-03-11 23:40 UTC.
Hypothesis A: indexer v4.1.0 changed template update ordering causing ancestry key to be written twice during a short window.
Hypothesis B: enrichment-service v2.6.0 regression in TTL refresh produced two labels: canonical and _v2 alias; merge logic treats them as distinct until dedupe cron runs.
Query used: SELECT ticket_id, array_agg(distinct escalation_label) FROM routing_bindings WHERE created_ts > '2026-03-11T23:30:00Z' GROUP BY ticket_id HAVING count(distinct escalation_label) > 1 LIMIT 50; returned 342 hits in us-east.
Relevant logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/routing-engine/2026-03-12/streams.log lines 4821-4875 show duplicate bind writes for ticket id SUP-9987-xyz.
Dashboards: Kibana -> routing_engine_bindings (time window 2026-03-11T23:30 to 2026-03-12T10:00) link: https://kibana.redwood-internal/products/routing/bindings?from=2026-03-11T23:30&to=2026-03-12T10:00
Repro attempts in staging: template-indexer v4.1.0 + enrichment-service v2.6.0 combo reproduced dedupe gap but with smaller volume (approx 3-4 duplicates per 1k tickets).
Configuration snippet: template-indexer config `dedupe_window_ms` currently set to 300000 (5m). Suspect window too long or misapplied naming normalization.
Telemetry gap: routing telemetry pipeline counts unique route assignments after dedupe step; upstream duplicates will still inflate pre-dedupe dashboards causing noisy alerts.

Additional notes:
Merge and deploy template-indexer patch PR 412 that restores deterministic normalization (owner: Samir).
Add a temporary routing-engine guard to ignore duplicate escalation labels that differ only by legacy alias suffixes (owner: Samir, timeline: 24h).
Shorten `dedupe_window_ms` from 300000 to 60000 for canary to reduce time window of duplicate persistence while patch stabilizes (owner: Priya, timeline: ASAP).
Add telemetry check: alert if >0.5% of tickets in a 1h window have >1 escalation_label emitted post-enrichment (owner: Analytics team, ticket for follow-up INT-174215).
Update runbook and add example queries and S3 artifact locations (owner: Support docs).
TBD - rollback performed as mitigation; awaiting template-indexer patch and routing-engine guard deployments. Will update after patch rollout and 72h observation window.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ClearWrite Inc.) reports gradual degradation of p50/p95 throughput for their reserved capacity pool over a 3-hour window during midday. Impact is sustained increased latency for short streaming requests and lower token throughput for batched routes.

Impact:
- ClearWrite reports ~30% drop in observed tokens/sec and p95 latency increase from 120ms -> 380ms on their primary routes.
- No full outage; requests succeed but user-facing processing time degrades.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-03-10 14:05: ClearWrite alerted via support email about rising latency.
- 2026-03-10 14:12: Support triaged, customer provided sample request IDs and timestamps.
- 2026-03-10 14:25: SRE cursory check shows reserved pool attach latency rising and more frequent NVLink stalls.
- 2026-03-10 15:40: Autoscaler did not trigger extra nodes; allocation credits dipped but no hard OOMs.
- 2026-03-10 16:20: We observed periodic small-tenant bursts (many short streams) correlated to slot fragmentation.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool (tenant_id: cw-prod-01) in us-west running a mix of streaming and batched routes.
- Model variants: open_llama_7b-v2 (fp16 path) and velvet-3B-quant (quantized).

Observed behavior / metrics:
- GPU attach latency p50 increased from 12ms -> 85ms across pool during window.
- p99 kernel queue wait increased and batcher serialization events rose ~3x.
- Autoscaler telemetry shows brief credit starvation events with no sustained scale-up (allocations fluctuated but no new nodes).
- KV cache hit rate remained stable; prefetch queue length increased for short streams.

Why this is surprising:
- Reserved capacity should absorb short spikes; autoscaler should react to credit dips. Instead we see slot fragmentation and slow attach without scale-up, consistent with many small concurrent short-lived streams (noisy cohort) that prevent efficient batching and GPU slot reuse.

Hypothesis:
- A cohort of ephemeral short-stream tenants created a burst fan-out pattern that fragments slot allocation and increases attach syscall rates, leading to transient NVLink/io contention and autoscaler misreading the signal as recoverable (no policy scale-up).

Next steps planned:
- Instrument per-tenant short-stream rate and slot hold time.
- Temporarily apply soft rate-limiter and connection coalescing for identified noisy tenant cohort.
- Tune autoscaler sensitivity for short-stream bursts (lower threshold for scale-up on repeated attach latency spikes).
- Run controlled repro (see steps_to_reproduce) in staging with synthetic short-stream cohort.

1) In a staging reserved pool, start 200 ephemeral short streaming connections across 20 tenants with mean request length 20 tokens and inter-arrival 50-200ms.
2) Simultaneously run normal batched routes at steady rate for the target tenant.
3) Observe slot allocation churn, attach latency, and autoscaler telemetry for 30+ minutes.
4) Compare batcher serialization rate and NVLink utilization against baseline.
gpu_attach_p50: 12ms -> 85ms; batcher_serialize_events: x1 -> x3; tokens_per_sec(customer): -30%; autoscaler_allocation_attempts: unchanged with short credit dips; nvlink_io_wait: +40% (sampled)
Transient multi-tenant short-stream fanout causing slot fragmentation and NVLink/io contention; autoscaler hysteresis prevents timely scale-up because metrics appear ephemeral.
2026-03-10 14:30 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): correlated request IDs to pool attach spikes; found clusters of short connections from 18 tenants with >80% short-stream traffic.
2026-03-10 15:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): requested connection logs and client SDK versions from ClearWrite; they use SDK v2.1.3 with default keepalive=30s.
2026-03-10 15:40 - SRE: observed autoscaler metric smoothing window is 5m; attach spikes lasted 2-6m and were below scale threshold; proposing config change to 90s smoothing for attach-latency alerts.
2026-03-10 16:10 - Eng (Jin Park): Kernel queue traces show increased enqueue/dequeue latency consistent with small-batch thrash and increased PCIe doorbell latency.
2026-03-11 09:00 - SRE: replayed a 20-minute sample in staging and validated slot fragmentation reproduction using the short-stream generator.
Applied tenant-level soft rate limit for the identified noisy cohort (internal policy id: softrl-2026-03-cw01) and enabled connection coalescing on sidecar for 1h window; observed immediate partial recovery in customer tokens/sec (+15%).
Mitigation in progress. Short-term mitigation (soft rate limit + coalescing) applied. Engineering to propose autoscaler smoothing policy change and add short-stream detection heuristic. Patch PR opened for autoscaler: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/512 (referenced). Plan to follow with a formal rollout after validation in staging.
Add short-stream cohort detection metric and per-tenant short-stream rate dashboards (owner: SRE)
Adjust autoscaler smoothing and sensitivity for attach-latency spikes triggered by short bursts (owner: infra-eng)
Improve SDK connection coalescing docs and recommend keepalive tuning for dedicated pools (owner: developer-experience)
Add automated canary to detect slot fragmentation during reserved pool load tests (owner: test-automation)
Communicate workaround and recommended client config to ClearWrite and schedule follow-up call (owner: CS)

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:12 - ClearWrite (customer): Provided connection logs and spike window. They confirmed no SDK upgrade recently; using v2.1.3.

Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-11 morning, the daily internal SLA attribution report (generated by reporting-pipeline) shows an unexpected 1.8-2.6% shift of P1/P2 tickets from 'on-time' to 'missed' compared to historical baselines. payload.description:
Issue summary: After a scheduled rotation of the metrics-exporter TLS certs (2026-03-09 03:00 UTC), a subset of self-hosted CI runners started to stop reporting heartbeats to the runner-manager and were subsequently evicted from job assignment pools. Impact: Several nightly release and canary builds observed elongated queue times (median queue increase ~4x) and 12% of in-flight ephemeral jobs showed 'runner unreachable' errors. No data exfiltration suspected; operational availability degraded for release windows.

Environment: Production (us-west cluster of self-hosted runners). Metrics exporter sits in front of runner heartbeats to feed autoscaling and health checks. Rotation was performed via automated rotation job (release-eng kubejob) that updated cert secret and restarted metrics-exporter pods.

Observed behavior: After rotation, metrics-exporter started responding with 503 on /heartbeat-proxy for ~30% of runners. The runner-manager incorrectly routed heartbeat traffic to the old cert-bound proxy endpoint due to an in-memory mapping TTL mismatch, causing TLS handshake failures and eventual runner eviction.

Expected behavior: Rotation should update both cert secrets and the in-memory proxy mapping atomically or with a short synchronization window so active runners keep streaming heartbeats uninterrupted.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Deploy rotation job that updates secret "metrics-exporter-cert". 2) Restart metrics-exporter deployment. 3) Observe runner-manager logs for TLS handshake errors and runner disconnects while jobs are active. (Repro rate observed ~30% under steady-state job load).
Trigger automated cert rotation for metrics-exporter secret in prod (simulate via canary namespace).
Restart metrics-exporter pods while 200+ runners are active in the pool.
Observe runner-manager and proxy logs for TLS handshake and routing mismatch errors.
2026-03-09T03:12:41Z runner-manager ERROR tls: remote error: tls: bad certificate (peer=runner-az1-004)
2026-03-09T03:12:43Z metrics-exporter WARN proxymap: stale-mapping-detected key=runner-az1-004 last_update=2026-03-09T02:59:10Z
curl -v https://metrics-proxy.internal/heartbeat-proxy --tlsv1.2 -> SSL: certificate subject mismatch (expected new cert)
Initial hypothesis: cert rotation updated Kubernetes secret and restarted pods but did not flush in-memory proxy mapping used by runner-manager. Evidence: proxymap logs show stale entries with TTL 15m; rotation job updated secret but mapping clean job is a separate cron (30m). Reproduce locally by forcing rotation and checking mapping TTL expiration; confirmed that mappings referencing old endpoint remained for ~18 minutes, during which runner heartbeats failed when leader routing switched to new pods. Secondary hypothesis: load-balancer sticky routing kept some heartbeats pinned to an old pod with rotated cert; however cloud LB logs show round-robin after restart, reducing likelihood.

Related artifacts: linked INT-70123 (ci-runner-permission-lockout-during-credential-rollforward) -- similar timing pattern during bulk rotates; relevant PRs: github.com/redwood/release-tools/pull/412 (rotation job change), github.com/redwood/runner-manager/pull/988 (proxy mapping TTL change proposed). Confluence runbook: "Release cert rotation checklist" updated to note proxymap flush step.
1) Manually trigger proxymap flush job post-rotation: kubectl -n release-eng apply -f proxymap-flush-job.yaml. 2) Temporarily increase proxymap TTL to 1m (reduces window) via deployment env var PROXYMAP_TTL_SECONDS. 3) For immediate recovery, curl each affected metrics-exporter pod to force TLS negotiation and then scale runners by +10% to absorb evicted jobs.

Customer-facing impact: Internal only (no external customers affected), but release pipelines delayed ~30-90 minutes for some teams.
SRE: backport runner-manager proxymap flush on rotation (RFC in PR 988).
Release Eng: update rotation job to call proxymap flush as a final step; roll out to staging for 24h canary.
DevExp: notify release squads and queue owners about temporary TTL change and expected recovery windows.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 11:45 - SRE-OnCall: Action item: roll proxymap atomic flush to prod during next maintenance window and monitor runner eviction rate for 6 hours post-deploy.
payload.summary: Runner metrics-exporter cert rotation misroutes runner heartbeats causing job stalls

comments: 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z Amaya Rivera: Logged initial report from BrightAssist. They attached two sample snapshot URLs and one PDF. Marked as high impact because on-call playbooks rely on snapshots.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
When Support toggles the impersonation view while a dashboard snapshot job is running (scheduled or ad-hoc 'Save snapshot' flow), the resulting snapshot file retains the base time range but loses any non-default ephemeral filters (user-level or org-scoped query filters). The snapshot produced and attached to the scheduled report shows filters as cleared, which breaks downstream alert links and tracehook anchors for the customer report recipients.

Impact:
- Customer-reported: scheduled PDF snapshots and exported snapshot URLs show empty or default filters even though the dashboard in the UI had filters applied at snapshot time.
- Alerts linked from those snapshots point to dashboards without the expected tracehook context, causing recipients to open dashboards that no longer highlight the same traces/annotations.
- Affects enterprise BrightAssist (multiple teams), observed across 3 org-scoped scheduled snapshots in us-east. Potential wider exposure for other orgs using impersonation-based support workflows.

Environment:
- Production console (prod: us-east)
- Customer: BrightAssist (enterprise)
- Dashboard types affected: saved dashboards with ad-hoc filters, saved snapshot scheduler, and ad-hoc "Save snapshot" export.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Support user impersonates BrightAssist: Using the console impersonation toggle (Support > Impersonate org).
2) While impersonating, open a saved dashboard that has ephemeral filters applied (e.g., service:search-api, tag:payment-flow) and a non-default time range (Last 24h).
3) Click "Save snapshot" (ad-hoc) or trigger a scheduled snapshot run for the same dashboard.
4) After snapshot job completes, open the generated snapshot URL or download PDF/PNG.
5) Observe that filters are reset to the dashboard base state (no ephemeral filters), and tracehook/alert links in the snapshot no longer include the original filter query parameters.

Expected behavior:
- Snapshot should capture the UI state visible to the impersonating user, including ephemeral filters and time range; tracehook links should preserve query params that anchor traces.

Actual behavior:
- Snapshot preserves time range but clears ephemeral filters. Tracehook query params are truncated (trace_id and anchor params missing). Snapshots saved under the customer's scheduled report appear to come from an unfiltered dashboard.

Logs / Observations:
- Support session logs show impersonation header X-Redwood-Impersonate: org=brightassist and a snapshot job request POST /api/snapshots with a payload containing filters.
- Snapshot worker log for job id snap-20260310-87 shows worker accepted payload but subsequent snapshot-render request to renderer service omitted the `filters` parameter in the query string.
- Renderer service trace: renderer-3 reported 200 for render call but request path lacked ?filters=... segment.
- No 5xx errors observed; flow completes successfully but with mutated payload.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Instructed BrightAssist users to create a new saved dashboard variant with desired filters (persisted saved-dashboard) and schedule snapshots from that saved-dashboard instead of relying on ad-hoc filters at snapshot time. This preserves filter state in scheduled snapshots until a fix is rolled out.

Business impact and urgency:
- Customer-facing produced artifacts (scheduled snapshots) do not reflect the intended investigation context; slows down incident response for their SREs. Customer escalated due to cross-team workflows relying on snapshots for on-call. Recommended P1 / Sev2 escalation and assignment to console/dashboard + snapshot pipeline owners.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - SRE (via Slack #support): Observed renderer service recently had a change that normalizes query params for security headers; possible sanitizer removed `filters` when X-Redwood-Impersonate header present.
2026-03-12 - Customer BrightAssist (CS rep): Confirmed they can use the persisted-saved-dashboard workaround; asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether historical snapshots will be audited.
Snapshot-worker (v1.14.2) logs show inbound POST /api/snapshots payload contains filters array: [service:search-api,tag:payment-flow].
Renderer service call made by snapshot-worker uses internal-client library which, when impersonation header present, strips query params to avoid leaking org tokens. This sanitizer is over-broad and removes `filters` param.
Reproducible in staging when impersonation header included. Not reproducible when snapshot created by non-impersonated org user.
Potential regression introduced in renderer security patch 2026-02-27 (PR ref: github.com/redwood/renderer/pull/129).
Patch snapshot-worker to send filters in request body (not query string) and update renderer to accept body-embedded filters when X-Redwood-Impersonate present.
Create a short-term config flip to relax query-param sanitizer for `filters` key only, behind a feature flag for testing in prod us-east.
Prepare regression tests that exercise snapshot creation under impersonation with ephemeral filters and assert tracehook params preserved.
Coordinate with SRE to deploy hotfix to prod us-east and communicate to BrightAssist when deployed.
Add follow-up ticket to audit existing scheduled snapshots created during window 2026-02-27..2026-03-12 for missing filter context and offer remediation.
In Progress - fix being developed; hotfix deployment planned once PR review and staging validation complete.
Will follow up with BrightAssist CS contacts after deploy and offer one-off snapshot regeneration for affected schedules.
payload.summary: Dashboard snapshot filter state resets when support impersonation toggled during snapshot generation

comments: 2026-03-10T09:14:00Z Sofia Martinez: Filed after depot techs reported imaging loop on 7 Lenovo X13 units. Collected one affected unit for lab repro.
2026-03-10T11:02:00Z Kai Becker: Reproduced in lab by creating 180 efivars; confirmed firmware returns storage exhausted. Captured efivar output and vendor debug logs.
2026-03-11T08:37:00Z Priya Singh: Deployed manual cleanup script to depot-ops. Three units imaged successfully after manual cleanup. Depot throughput improved but process is slow.
2026-03-11T15:21:00Z Lenovo Support: Acknowledged as firmware behavior; recommended BIOS update to 1.35 and provided vendor tool to compact NVRAM.
payload.description:
Issue summary: Several Lenovo X13 units fail to complete the SCCM task sequence during depot reimage. The TS halts at the 'Apply OS' phase and then the machine reboots back into PXE/WinPE repeatedly (imaging loop).

Impact: Blocks depot reimage throughput for a small batch (7/120) of Lenovo X13 devices; delays fleet refresh and repair turnaround. Not customer-facing but affects internal device provisioning SLA.

Background: Devices were returned from a test group where engineering had temporarily enabled multiple boot profiles and experimented with dual-boot UEFI entries. Those machines are now hitting imaging failures.

Observed behavior: SCCM task sequence fails to locate boot manager after the first reboot post-OS apply and re-enters WinPE. Devices show >200 UEFI boot entries in NVRAM and the firmware reports NVRAM storage near capacity, causing firmware to drop newly written Boot#### entries used by the TS to continue.

Expected behavior: NVRAM should accept the Boot#### entries SCCM creates during TS and allow the system to continue the normal reboot path into the newly applied OS.

Workaround in place: Manual NVRAM cleanup via vendor utility before imaging succeeds; we have a stopgap script run by depot techs that clears non-essential Boot#### entries prior to TS but this is manual and slow.
1) Take a Lenovo X13 with >= 150 existing UEFI Boot#### entries (e.g., after repeated dev dual-boot changes).
2) Boot to PXE and start SCCM task sequence (depot reimage).
3) SCCM applies OS image and writes Boot#### entry for Windows Boot Manager.
4) On first reboot, firmware reports NVRAM write failure silently and drops the new Boot####, leaving system without a valid boot path; device returns to WinPE PXE.

Observed in 7 devices across two depot batches; reproducible on 1 lab unit after intentionally flooding NVRAM with entries.
UEFI log snippet from FW debug console (device 13-03-26):
[2026-03-09T14:22:11Z] NVRAM capacity: 96% (used 512k / 536k)
[2026-03-09T14:22:11Z] CreateBootEntry(LoaderPath=\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\bootmgfw.efi) -> status=0x80 (NVRAM_STORAGE_EXHAUSTED)
[2026-03-09T14:22:11Z] WriteVariable(Boot0001) -> dropped, no space
[2026-03-09T14:22:11Z] FirmwareFallback: continue to PXE

SCCM TS log (SMSTS.log):
Content of SMSTS.log around reboot: 14:22:20 Failed to create boot entry for OS; error 0x80070005
14:22:20 Marked step as failed, restarting
14:22:30 System reboot to WinPE

Initial triage: Support reproduced failure in lab by creating >150 Boot#### entries via efibootmgr. Confirmed firmware reports 'storage exhausted' and silently fails to persist new entries.

Hypotheses considered:
- SCCM TS is correct; firmware NVRAM exhaustion is root cause.
- A firmware bug on X13 variants causes NVRAM to report capacity incorrectly when many entries exist.
- AssetDB or imaging scripts writing persistent entries in odd formats contributing to fragmentation.

Actions taken so far:
- Imaging eng ran lab repro and captured EFI variables (efivar -l) and vendor firmware debug logs.
- Opened vendor ticket with Lenovo @ case LEN-20260310-UEFI (attached logs).
- Created temporary depot script (scripts/cleanup_nvram.sh) that removes non-Microsoft Boot#### entries older than 30 days prior to running TS. Deployed to depot-ops as manual step.
- Proposed SCCM TS change: insert a pre-OS step to run NVRAM cleanup from WinPE using efibootmgr-equivalent vendor utility. PR created: https://github.com/redwood/it-imaging/pull/614

Remaining unknowns:
- Whether firmware will accept new entries after cleanup on all affected units or if some hardware requires firmware update.
- Whether repeated manual cleanup will result in NVRAM fragmentation that still blocks entry creation.

Additional notes:
Short term: Continue manual cleanup script as mandatory pre-TS step for affected Lenovo X13 units. Depot ops trained and script added to runbook (confluence link).
Medium term: Merge PR to SCCM TS to perform automated NVRAM cleanup in WinPE before OS apply (PR 614). Rollout of TS change scheduled for 2026-03-18 to depot pool; will run in canary on 5 devices.
Long term: Lenovo provided BIOS firmware 1.35 addressing NVRAM handling. Plan coordinated with hardware lifecycle to push firmware update to depot (BIOS package QA scheduled 2026-03-20). After firmware rollout, we will monitor for recurrence and remove forced cleanup step.
Follow-ups:
- Add telemetry to imaging pipeline to record current efivar count and NVRAM capacity after TS completes.
- Run a sweep of returned/dev units to compact NVRAM ahead of reprovisioning where possible.
Ticket will be closed after successful canary and firmware rollout with no recurrence for 7 days.
payload.summary: UEFI NVRAM boot-entry exhaustion causes SCCM imaging task sequence to loop on Lenovo X13 during depot reimage

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbusChat reported intermittent spikes of 5xx responses and several zero-byte/empty HTTP responses observed on streaming routes during a large mixed workload with long-running chat streams and concurrent bulk embedding uploads. Errors began at ~11:42 PDT with a steady elevated error rate for ~18 minutes and recurred in short pulses afterwards.

Impact:
- Multiple customer requests from a single enterprise tenant failed with 502/503 and occasional 500s; some streaming sessions returned zero-byte frames and closed connections mid-stream.
- Customer reported degraded UX: partial transcripts and failed embedding batches.
- Tenant on Dedicated pool, SLA impacted.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-west-2, dedicated capacity pool dcap-nimbus-3
- API gateway version: apigw-2.14.1
- Serving runtime version: runtime-2026.02.09-hotfix

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant started a burst of mixed workload around 11:40: long-lived streaming chat sessions (keepalive) + parallel embedding bulk upload (concurrent multipart).
2) Accept queue at the API gateway increased and observed connection churn.
3) A subset of streaming connections experienced zero-byte first-chunk responses and then were reset.
4) Upstream runtimes reported transient OOM warnings and watchdog restarts correlated with the window.

Logs and metrics observed:
- apigw.accept_queue_depth spiked to 320 (normal < 40) in us-west-2 region at 11:42.
- apigw.threadpool_queue_time increased to 2.6s.
- apigw returned 502/503 for ~11% of requests from this tenant during the spike.
- runtime.gpu_memory_fragmentation and runtime.prefetch_lock_waits increased concurrently.
- Some runtime pods emitted repeated kalloc OOM logs and then segfaults (nvml resets).
- kvcache.lock_waits rose, several cache-add operations timed out and returned 5xx.

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis A: Mixed long-lived streaming connections plus heavy embedding multipart uploads saturated accept-queue and exhausted proxy thread workers, leading to hedged retries and amplified load on serving runtimes.
- Hypothesis B: A subset of runtime workers experienced GPU memory fragmentation causing out-of-memory conditions when handling embedding fanouts, producing sudden upstream 5xx and short-lived restarts.
- Observed correlation between apigw.accept_queue_depth and runtime OOM events (11:42–11:55).
- Autoscaler did not scale up immediately because dedicated pool was pinned; there was no spare capacity to absorb sudden fanout.
- No recent config rollouts in us-west-2; load pattern appears customer-induced.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support applied a temporary tenant rate-limit on large multipart embedding uploads for NimbusChat at 12:03 PDT to reduce arrival rate.
- On-call SRE increased per-tenant connection cap on the proxy for the dedicated pool to reduce accept-queue pressure (short-term).
- Rolled a restart of two affected runtime pods to clear fragmented GPU memory at 12:08; observed partial recovery of error rate.

Next steps / resolution plan:
1) Engineering to add a circuit-breaker in apigw to shed heavy multipart embedding uploads earlier and avoid headroom exhaustion. (Owner: apigw team)
2) Runtime team to investigate GPU memory fragmentation patterns and improve prefetch/kv cache backoff behavior to avoid OOMs under mixed workloads. (Owner: serving-runtime)
3) Product to evaluate throttling guidance and recommend client-side backoff for mixed streaming+embed flows.
4) Add a guardrail in Dedicated provisioning to allow transient burst capacity or better preemption signal to autoscaler for pinned pools. (Owner: infra/autoscaler)
5) Follow up: schedule a post-incident review with NimbusChat and ops teams; propose a configuration change for per-tenant max concurrent multipart uploads.

Resolution notes (in-progress):
- Immediate customer-level workaround: reduced embedding parallelism and implemented retry/backoff in their client.
- Post-fix: target runtime improvements and apigw shed behavior; ETA for mitigations 2 weeks pending prioritization.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:22 — SRE (A. Nguyen): Noted accept_queue spike on apigw; correlating runtime OOMs. Kicking off pod restarts for affected pods to recover memory fragmentation.
2026-03-11 16:40 — Product (E. Huang): Noted this pattern could be a common UX anti-pattern for customers combining heavy streaming with large embedding fanouts; drafting guidance.
2026-03-12 10:10 — Support (Maya Patel): Customer confirmed degradation improved after reducing parallel uploads but wants permanent fix. Scheduled postmortem and recommended client-side rate-limit in docs.
payload.summary: Intermittent partial 5xx responses and zero-byte payloads during mixed streaming + embedding burst for enterprise tenant

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that a scheduled batched embedding job completed on 2026-03-11 but did not receive the expected meter credit adjustments. The job runs across multiple subaccounts; customer expects per-subaccount credit back for cache hits and duplicate suppression. Instead, only a partial credit arrived and a subset of subaccounts show no postback recorded.

Impact:
- LexiAssist reports $120 of missing credits on the March 11 provisional invoice.
- Affects one recurring multi-org batch (nightly ingest) and causes under-crediting for three subaccounts leading to downstream billing alerts.

Environment:
prod clusters in us-east-1, dedicated pool 'lexi-dedicated-2', batch scheduler v1.14.2, postback-processor v2.3.1.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Submit multi-org batched embedding job with 4 subaccounts attached (GUIDs provided in logs).
2) Allow job to finish; verify batch completion event emitted to postback queue.
3) Confirm postback-processor consumes completion event and posts meter adjustments; expected 4 postbacks (one per subaccount).
4) Observe only 1 postback persisted; other 3 were dropped by deduplication step.

Observed logs / snippets:
- batch-run-id: br-20260311-98ad
- postback-queue messages show single canonical postback with dedup_key "br-20260311-98ad-canonical".
- postback-processor log excerpt: "INFO dedupe: normalized_key=%s canonical_owner=org-1214 from=org-1102 dropped=true reason=owner-normalization"

Additional context:
Customer uses per-subaccount attribution for internal cost centers. This batch was migrated last month to the new microbatch pipeline; they first noticed discrepancy after migration.

2026-03-12 08:17 - Customer (Ben Harlow, LexiAssist): We ran our nightly ingest and saw only one credit applied to the parent account. This used to credit each subaccount separately. Can you confirm why credits were consolidated?
2026-03-12 09:02 - Support (Aisha Kaur): Thanks Ben — we're investigating. Can you confirm the batch-run-id and list of subaccount IDs? Also attaching policy id from job submission helps.
2026-03-12 10:30 - Customer (Ben Harlow): batch-run-id: br-20260311-98ad; subaccounts: org-1102, org-1107, org-1113, org-1214. Policy id: ingest-policy-v3.

2026-03-12 13:45 - SRE (Miguel Santos): Initial analysis: postback-processor dedupe normalization collapsed owner metadata when parent org present. Suspect normalization bug introduced in v2.3.1. Reproduced locally with a test harness: dedupe normalized all subaccounts to parent-org id when parent metadata present.
2026-03-12 15:20 - Engineering (Chen Wei): Created PR to stop owner normalization during dedupe for batched jobs: github.com/redwood-inference/postback-service/pull/4321. Deployed PR to staging; tests show per-subaccount postbacks preserved.
2026-03-13 09:05 - Support (Aisha Kaur): Updated customer: provisional credit of $120 applied to parent invoice while we complete root cause; backfill scheduled for 2026-03-15. Will keep you posted on timeline.
2026-03-13 11:12 - Customer (Ben Harlow): Thanks — please ensure the backfill applies credits to the original subaccount line items rather than parent-level. Need this for internal chargebacks.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - Partial finding: Message payload from batch scheduler included both owner and parent_owner fields; normalization code preferred parent_owner when present. For multi-org batches parent_owner exists and collapsed keys.
2026-03-12 - Staging test: Deploy PR/4321 which bypasses normalization for messages with field 'multi_org=true' — per-subaccount postbacks preserved in staging and credits generated correctly.
2026-03-12 - Customer impact estimate: 1 nightly run affected over last 7 days => ~$840 total missing credits across accounts; LexiAssist's accounting flagged $120 on the parent invoice.
2026-03-13 - Next steps: schedule backfill reprocessing of deduped messages in prod; ensure credit memos are created per subaccount; deploy fix to prod after smoke tests.
Pending - Mitigation steps taken: provisional credit of $120 issued to customer's parent invoice on 2026-03-13 to prevent immediate billing disruption. Engineering created and merged PR 4321 to fix owner-normalization; change deployed to staging and passed smoke tests. Planned rollout: 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC to prod with short maintenance window. Post-deploy actions: run backfill job to reprocess dropped postbacks for batch-run-id br-20260311-98ad and previous 7 days, create per-subaccount credit memos, and notify customer when completed. Assigned to Miguel Santos for prod deploy and backfill coordination. Final resolution ETA: 2026-03-16.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a formal mechanism and proof for three things related to their live SIEM export to an on-prem Kafka cluster: (1) support for adaptive (per-tenant) sampling in the incremental export so high-volume tenants are sampled at route-time, (2) a schema-version header in every export message and manifest so downstream parsers can tolerate rolling changes, and (3) verifiable propagation of GDPR deletion requests into the export stream (i.e., when an end-user is erased, no subsequent SIEM export should contain their events).

Impact:
PulsePay is using Redwood's tenant-scoped incremental SIEM feed for fraud telemetry ingestion. They discovered during a data-protection validation that (a) sampled test slices still contained events for deleted user ids, and (b) consumer parsing logic lacks a stable schema version to guard against producer changes. This prevents them from signing off on production onboarding and is blocking final contract acceptance.

Environment:
- Customer environment: enterprise account (PulsePay Financial)
- Export target: on-prem Kafka cluster (TLS mTLS) via the Redwood SIEM Bridge connector
- Redwood environment: prod-us-east incremental-export pipeline v2.4.1

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Submit a GDPR deletion request for user id: usr_9b2fc1 via self-service API.
2) Observe that deletion job returns success and user disappears from console.
3) Wait for next incremental export window (15-minute cadence).
4) Consumer shows events with the deleted user id in the exported Kafka topic between offsets 120304-120420.

Customer-provided logs/snippets:
- Example exported event (sanitized): {"ts":"2026-03-09T18:12:03Z", "user_id": "usr_9b2fc1", "event_type": "prompt_submit", "tenant_id": "pp-prod"}
- Bridge connector config: sampling_policy=adaptive_per_tenant, sampling_rate_overrides=[pp-prod:0.01], include_headers=false

Requested deliverables:
- A reproducible explanation for how deletion/tombstone propagation is handled by the incremental-export pipeline and why the customer observed post-deletion events.
- A short-term workaround the customer can enable to avoid leaked deletion events while we implement a longer-term solution.
- A timeline and PRs for adding an explicit X-Schema-Version header to export messages and a manifest file for each export window.
- Signed manifest or attestation proving previously exported windows were scanned for deleted ids (optional but strongly requested).

Additional notes from customer:
They prefer minimal downtime and would accept an opt-in config flag to make deletion propagation immediate even if it increases export latency for a subset of tenants.

Additional notes:
PulsePay Contact (Ella Rodriguez): 2026-03-10 14:20 UTC - We observed two exported events after deletion but they had offsets within the same minute the deletion was submitted. We need a guarantee that this cannot recur for PCI/PD compliance.
Security (Lina Chen): 2026-03-11 10:02 UTC - For attestation, we'll produce an HMAC manifest signed with the enterprise key and include a per-window checksum. Draft PR linked in ticket.
Confirmed reproduction against customer's staging mirror; exporter has two internal buffers: ingest-buffer (where sampling is applied) and dispatch-window buffer. Tombstone propagation currently flows to ingest-buffer but dispatch-window flush can contain pre-tombstone events.
Sampling: adaptive_per_tenant logic was working, but header-less exports made downstream dedup and suppression rules brittle. The sampling algorithm marks events with internal _sampling_version but not emitted in headers; we'll expose a public header X-Sampling-Version as part of schema changes.
Root cause for leaked deletions: exporter dispatch-window buffer size + asynchronous tombstone propagation. If an event is buffered and the deletion request arrives after buffering but before dispatch, the deletion marker is applied only to new events, not already buffered ones.
Risk assessment: This is a correctness/regulatory risk for enterprise customers with short-deletion SLAs. Low probability at scale but high impact for affected tenants.
Mitigation options considered: (A) immediate-tombstone-propagation (sync) per-tenant; (B) reduce dispatch window to 1 minute for opt-in tenants; (C) post-export backfill scan that removes/marks records and emits compensating deletions to downstream systems. Recommended: short-term (B) + backfill; long-term (A) with metrics and canary rollouts.
Short-term workaround: Enabled immediate-tombstone-propagation and reduced export window to 1 minute for tenant pp-prod for PulsePay. Coordinates: infra runbook step executed 2026-03-11 18:10 UTC.
Backfill: Ran a 24-hour backfill scan against the exported topics and produced a signed HMAC manifest (SHA256) of removed offsets. Manifest S3 path: s3://redwood-evidence/pulsepay/pp-prod/backfill/2026-03-11-manifest.json (access granted to PulsePay via presigned URL).
Schema/versioning: X-Schema-Version and X-Sampling-Version headers added to exporter messages and manifest generation implemented. PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9854. Deploy scheduled behind feature flag 2026-03-14.
Long-term plan: Implement immediate-tombstone-propagation as configurable default for enterprise tier with telemetry and per-tenant latency impact telemetry. Track as follow-up work: INT-4107 (engineering work item for permanent change).
Customer acceptance: PulsePay validated the backfill manifest and confirmed they no longer observed deleted user ids in the reprocessed topic. They requested a short runbook for how to request immediate-tombstone-propagation for other tenants; Support to provide template.
Next steps: 1) Deploy schema/manifest feature to prod-us-east behind flag on 2026-03-14 and coordinate a canary rollout with PulsePay. 2) Create a short runbook for customers to request immediate-tombstone-propagation and include expected cost/latency tradeoffs. 3) Close ticket once PulsePay signs off on the feature and receives the formal attestation artifact. Ticket owner: Marcus Bell.
payload.summary: Incremental SIEM export: adaptive sampling, schema-version header, and GDPR deletion propagation proof

Issue summary: Customer reports that their monthly invoice (Feb 2026) shows inconsistent application of tiered volume discounts when usage is billed across EUR and USD regions. The invoice appears to have applied the discount ladder on a per-line basis after currency conversion, instead of aggregating usage across lines prior to discount calculation. This resulted in an over-credit to the customer in EUR lines and an under-credit in USD lines, producing a net discrepancy and customer confusion.

Requested outcome: clear explanation of calculation, a corrected invoice or credit, and a permanent fix to prevent recurrence.
Customer-facing billing discrepancy affecting revenue recognition and forecast; Brightline flagged with finance and paused automated payments pending clarification. Estimated discrepancy ~€9,760. Customer requests expedited review and credit if appropriate.
prod | multi-region billing (eu-west, us-east) | billing-service v3.4.1 | currency-converter-service v2.1.0
1) Customer runs multi-region batch embedding workload in eu-west and us-east pooled under a single org for February 2026.
2) Usage postbacks arrived with region tags and per-line usage quantities (eu-west lines in EUR, us-east lines in USD).
3) Billing aggregator constructed invoice lines by region and applied tiered discount ladder per line after converting regional subtotals to the invoice base currency (EUR).
4) Expected behavior: aggregate usage across all regions, apply discount ladder to the aggregated usage, then split allocation per region for display and accounting.
billing-aggregator: 2026-03-02T03:12:10Z INFO building invoice SUP-276811 for org 48ACD
currency-converter: 2026-03-02T03:12:11Z DEBUG EUR->USD rate used: 1.0832 (source: fx-provider-1)
discount-engine: 2026-03-02T03:12:12Z WARN applied ladder on subtotal=EUR 42,117.23 -> discount 12.5% (per-line), expected aggregated ladder step 15%
postback-receiver: 2026-02-28T23:58:34Z INFO receiving usage batch id batch-9912 region=eu-west

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - Finance@Brightline (customer contact): Provided permission to issue provisional credit if an error is confirmed. Stated they require a corrected invoice PDF for their audit trail.
Hypothesis: Discount ladder was being evaluated after currency conversion due to a refactor in billing-aggregator (v3.4.1) that changed call ordering between currency-converter and discount-engine.
Reproduction: Unit test shows discount change when reversing conversion/aggregation order. Aggregated usage 1,240,000 tokens -> discount 15% expected. Per-line application produced effective blended discount 12.3%.
Root cause: billing-aggregator v3.4.1 updated to normalize line currencies early for tax/display reasons; side effect was passing already-converted subtotals into discount-engine, which uses ladder thresholds based on raw usage units (tokens). No conversion invariant enforced in discount-engine.
Risk assessment: Medium-high for multi-currency orgs with usage near ladder thresholds. Edge-case occurs when multiple regions push different lines across adjacent ladder steps after conversion rounding.
Workarounds considered: a) Recompute aggregated usage in base units before calling discount-engine (preferred); b) Post-invoice manual adjustment and credit (temporary).
Hotfix merged to billing main: aggregator now computes aggregated usage in native units then calls discount-engine, then applies currency conversion for display and line allocation. Issued provisional credit to Brightline for EUR 9,760.00 and generated corrected invoice PDF. Deployed patch to prod 2026-03-12 16:02:00Z with smoke tests. Follow-ups: add unit tests that cover multi-currency ladder edge cases and add monitoring alert when rounded-per-line discount delta > 0.5%.
Credit line: EUR -9,760.00 applied as CREDIT_ADJUSTMENT on invoice INV-2026-02-48ACD
Replacement invoice generated: INV-2026-02-48ACD-R1 (PDF attached to ticket)
Accounting note: revenue deferral corrected for Feb close; finance notified (email thread #brightline-billing)
payload.summary: Tiered discount ladder applied inconsistently across multi-currency invoice lines
