Issue summary:
Customer BrightChat reports an increase in 5xx error rate for production requests that use large batch submissions with streaming fan-out to multiple sub-requests (chat + retrieval + reranking). Errors began ~2026-03-10T08:05Z and recur under high batch+stream concurrency. Affects dedicated pool in us-east-1.

Impact:
- ~8-12% of batch requests return 5xx on affected endpoints during peak bursts.
- Customer reports user-facing errors and retries causing cost spikes.
- No data loss reported; failures are transient but frequent enough to disrupt service.

Timeline (high-level):
- 2026-03-10 08:05Z: BrightChat first reports increased failures.
- 2026-03-10 08:12Z: Support triaged and escalated to SRE; initial mitigation to throttle per-route burst.
- 2026-03-10 09:00Z: SRE observed correlated autoscaler events + serving-runtime restarts.
- 2026-03-11 02:30Z: Added temporary routing fallback to smaller model variant for heavy fanouts.

Observed behavior and error signals:
- HTTP 503 / 502 returned from API gateway and from upstream serving-runtime.
- Serving runtime logs show "worker OOM" and "connection reset by peer" on some request shards.
- Autoscaler shows frequent scale-up then immediate scale-down cycles during bursts (thrashing).
- KV-cache miss rate spikes during fanout; cache thrash inferred.

Why this ticket is different from past 5xx spikes:
- Failures strongly correlate with combined pattern: large batch sizes + streaming fan-out to multiple downstream tasks (retrieval, rerank).
- Not a pure GPU overload—some nodes show low GPU utilization but high CPU and IO for worker coordination and cache activity.

Current severity: customer-impacting (P1 / Sev1).
1) Submit a single batch request that contains 80 conversations (or >5000 total tokens) with streaming enabled.
2) For each conversation, the pipeline triggers retrieval and reranking sub-requests simultaneously (fan-out of ~4 sub-requests per conversation).
3) Repeat with concurrency of 20 simultaneous batch requests from a single client at peak time.
Expected: Stable responses with occasional tail latency.
Observed: Elevated 5xx rate, intermittent upstream disconnects and worker restarts.
2026-03-10T08:09:12Z runtime-02 ERROR worker 2143: OOM while handling request shard id=shard-9923
2026-03-10T08:09:14Z gateway-01 WARN Request id=req-7f4: upstream returned 503 for /v1/responses (x-retry: 1)
2026-03-10T09:02:40Z autoscaler INFO scale-down triggered: pool=dedicated-us-east-1-3 cause=idle-burst-backoff
See attached snippets in Confluence page for full traces and gzip’d stderr logs.
5xx_rate: peaked at 11.8% (5m rolling) for customer route /v1/batch:2026-03-10T08:05Z
p95_latency: increased from 420ms -> 1.9s during incidents
GPU_utilization: avg 42% on affected nodes; CPU load avg 87%
kv_cache_miss_rate: 72% during fanout bursts
autoscaler_events: 18 scale-up events and 16 scale-down within 30 minutes (thrash).
03/10 08:30 SRE (Rohan): Verified pattern reproduces in internal staging with similar batch+fanout. Identified worker OOM traces that align to shard handling code path for rerank step.
03/10 09:15 Eng (S. Liu): Observed per-shard memory allocation spikes when streaming + multiple sub-requests are active; per-request coordination increases pinned CPU and socket usage.
03/10 10:00 SRE: Autoscaler aggressive cooldown config allows quick scale-up but scales down when small number of nodes appear idle (thrash). Buffering/backpressure not applied to fan-out sub-requests causing many concurrent shards to land on few workers.
03/11 02:40 Support: Applied routing policy to send heavy fanout routes to a dedicated smaller-model pool; observed immediate drop in 5xx to ~1.2%.
Hypotheses: (a) Combination of high per-shard memory + coordination overhead causes workers to hit OOM or reset connection; (b) Autoscaler thrash amplifies transient overload by removing capacity before shards fully finish; (c) KV-cache thrash increases IO and CPU, exacerbating worker instability.
Next tests proposed: Increase per-worker memory limit in a canary pool; apply backpressure at gateway to cap concurrent fanout per-request; increase autoscaler stabilization window to avoid immediate scale-downs.
2026-03-10 08:14 - Support (Ava): Received initial customer report. Asked for request ids and sample payloads. Customer provided 4 failing request ids and logs.
2026-03-10 08:22 - SRE (Rohan): Triage started. Noted OOM traces in runtime logs; escalating to runtime team. Added priority P1.
2026-03-10 09:05 - Eng (S. Liu): Confirmed reproduction in staging with large batch + retrieval+rerank. Working on a small fix to the shard allocation code; will run canary.
2026-03-10 09:45 - Support (Ava): Communicated temporary guidance to customer to reduce batch size to 30 per request and disable streaming as workaround; customer agreed to test.
2026-03-11 03:00 - SRE (Rohan): Rolled out autoscaler cooldown increase on a canary pool (stabilization from 60s -> 300s). Observed reduced thrash and lower 5xx for canary routes.
2026-03-12 11:20 - Customer (BrightChat - ops): Reported that applying suggested changes reduced errors to acceptable levels; requested ETA for permanent fix and guidance for production traffic shaping.
Partial mitigation applied: routing heavy fanout routes to a dedicated smaller-model pool and increasing autoscaler stabilization window for canary pool. Customer advised to reduce batch size and disable streaming for highest fanout cases as immediate workaround.

Planned next steps:
- Runtime team to land guardrails for per-shard memory accounting and connection handling (PR #842 under review).
- Autoscaler config change to be rolled to all dedicated pools after validation (target: 2026-03-15).
- Add gateway-level soft backpressure counter to cap concurrent fanout per request.
- Follow-up runbook update and postmortem to be drafted in Confluence.
payload.summary: Intermittent 5xx surge during high-volume batch + streaming fan-out causing request failures

Issue summary:
NimbleHealth reports an unexpected change in the applied rate tier for a set of hours on the invoice dated 2026-03-09. The invoice line shows a temporary lower per-token rate applied for hours 02:00-04:00 UTC, which later corrected in downstream records. The billing pipeline flagged the discrepancy and placed the invoice into a provisional credit hold while we audit the raw meterings.

Impact:
- Customer sees a confusing invoice line and a provisional credit hold preventing automatic payment routing.
- Risk of incorrect revenue recognition and a customer trust issue if not resolved quickly.
- Affects one dedicated tenant (NimbleHealth) for a 2-hour window only.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity in us-east (prod).
- Model: redwood/pythia-12b-quantized-v2 served from dedicated pool dhp-us-east-3.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Customer ran sustained traffic spike between 02:00-04:30 UTC on 2026-03-08 using pinned model variant.
2) Our metering-batcher aggregate job produced hourly buckets.
3) Billing pipeline applied rate-tier smoothing and generated invoice lines.
4) Downstream anomaly detection identified a mismatch between raw token counts and billed tier, and set invoice to provisional hold.

Observed logs/indicators:
- metering-batcher logs (producer) show job start times at hh:59:30 UTC for affected window (link below).
- Raw token counts from ingestion show consistent totals but split across two buckets instead of a single hour.
- Billing anomaly detector rule: rate-tier-flip threshold triggered at 2026-03-09T07:12:34Z.

Provided artefacts:
- Customer CSV of request IDs and timestamps (uploaded to ticket attachments).
- Relevant log snippets and aggregation timestamps (S3 links in comments).

Customer request:
- Explanation for what caused the apparent rate-tier change.
- Request for provisional credit until audit completes.
- Ask to confirm any long-term risk and remediation plan.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 - Customer (R. Patel - NimbleHealth): Accepts provisional credit pending confirmation. Asked for ETA on resolution and whether this will affect their committed reserved capacity billing.
Metering batcher (v1.14.2) started using cronlib v3.2.0 during 2026-03-07 deploy; cronlib changed interpretive behavior for non-zero-second entries. Several hosts started their hourly aggregation at hh:59:30 which split high-throughput windows across two buckets.
Raw ingestion records show total tokens for the 02:00-04:30 window equal to billed usage, confirming no token duplication or data loss; discrepancy is in bucket boundaries used for rate-tier calculation.
Rate-tier smoothing algorithm uses per-hour buckets to determine tier thresholds; when a spike is split, per-hour peak appears lower for an early hour producing a lower temporary tier; later correction re-aggregates but initial invoice generation used the split results.
Billing anomaly detector correctly flagged out-of-band tier change and placed invoice on provisional hold per policy.
Workaround and fix applied: provisional credit equal to the delta caused by bucket misclassification applied to NimbleHealth's 2026-03-09 invoice (details emailed to customer). Immediate mitigation: reverted cronlib upgrade in canary and pushed schedule normalization patch (PR #6289) to all metering-batcher hosts. Long-term remediation: update CI tests to include cronlib behavior lockfile, add integration tests that simulate high-throughput cross-boundary spikes, and add a billing pipeline re-check that delays final invoice generation by 1 hour if anomaly detector fires during aggregation. Postmortem scheduled and linked (CON-OPS-2026-03-metering-window-drift). Follow-ups: INT-33245 assigned for infra rollout validation and SUP-36321 referenced for related billing smoothing work.
payload.summary: Hourly usage-window drift caused apparent rate-tier misclassification and provisional credit hold

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports hourly buffer credits for specific hourly windows not applied to their finalized provisional invoice. The credits appear in internal logs as 'escrowed' and not released to invoice lines after a tag-namespace merge and a rate-selector cache flush during a region failover window.

Impact: BrightServe AI (enterprise) shows a $14,720 provisional credit difference on the 2026-03-07 finalized invoice. This blocks their finance team from reconciling month-end and may trigger a billing dispute. Customer reports they lost expected hourly-buffer credits for six hourly windows during a cross-region replay.

Expected behavior: Hourly buffer credits should be attributed to the customer invoice and appear as applied credits on the provisional/final invoice within the normal postback reconciliation window.

Observed behavior: Credits are present in the postback-reconciler logs and marked as applied to tenant tags, but an intermediate ledger entry was created with status "escrowed:tag-merge" which prevented application to invoice lines. The escrow state persisted after the rate-selector cache was flushed and after automatic reconciler retry.

Timeline:
- 2026-03-07 02:14 UTC: Region us-west-2 edge proxy failover; queued postbacks replayed to reconciler.
- 2026-03-07 02:16 UTC: Ops ran scheduled tag-namespace merge to resolve duplicate tenant tags (part of planned housekeeping).
- 2026-03-07 02:18 UTC: Rate-selector cache flush deploy rolled out to address rate-override bug.
- 2026-03-07 02:20–03:30 UTC: High postback replay volume; several postbacks processed with tag metadata in transitional state.
- 2026-03-07 08:00 UTC: Customer noticed provisional invoice lacking expected hourly buffer credits.

Steps to reproduce (dev env):
1) Seed simulated postbacks for tenant with hourly buffer qualified tag.
2) Trigger tag-namespace merge during a short window of postback replay.
3) Flush rate-selector cache and restart postback-reconciler.
4) Observe ledger entries: some credits transition to status 'escrowed:tag-merge' and are not consumed by invoicing job.

Logs & artifacts:
- Postback reconciler traces: /var/log/postback-reconciler/2026-03-07/replay-usp.log (attached).
- Ledger excerpt: shows entries with note 'escrowed:tag-merge' for tenant brightserve-123.
- Console screenshot: provisional invoice comparison (attached).

Business impact: Customer finance team delayed closing month; potential credit dispute escalation to enterprise sales.

Requested outcome: Immediate manual application of missing hourly buffer credits to the customer's account and a permanent fix so tag-namespace merges do not leave credits in escrow during active replay windows.

Additional notes:
2026-03-09 08:00 - Ops (Maya): Reproduced locally with the reproduction steps. Created a failing test that demonstrates escrow creation when tag-namespace merge and cache flush overlap with replay. Linked PR to add locking/atomic swap for tag resolution step.
2026-03-10 13:55 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed provisional adjustment reflected as expected on 2026-03-09. Customer requests timeline and RCA; asked for ETA for permanent fix.
Hypothesis 1: Tag-namespace merge produced temporary alias mappings; postbacks processed during this window used aliases that were not resolved to canonical tenant tags, leading reconciler to mark related ledger entries as escrow until alias resolution completed.
Hypothesis 2: Rate-selector cache flush returned empty/unknown rate for alias mappings for a short period; reconciler guarded against applying credits with unknown rate, leaving items in escrow.
Finding: Ledger entries include metadata 'resolved_tag_id=null' and 'escrow_reason=tag-merge' for the affected postbacks. Postback timestamps align with the merge + cache flush window.
Reproducer created: added unit test that simulates alias transitional state; current reconciler allows escrow state without re-queueing after alias resolution.
Temporary mitigation tried: manual ledger reconciliation utility applied credits; mitigation requires finance sign-off and audit trail.
Proposed permanent fix: ensure rate-selector and tag-resolution are performed atomically for postback commit OR add a reconciler job that re-evaluates escrowed ledger entries after alias-resolution events. PR#842 implements reconciler re-evaluation loop and idempotent apply.
Applied manual invoice credit of $14,720 on 2026-03-09 15:30 UTC after finance approval; annotated account ledger with 'SUP-112233 manual apply'. Customer notified and verified provisional invoice now matches expectation.
Manual credit applied as stop-gap. Engineering PR#842 submitted to add re-evaluation pass for escrowed credits post-alias-resolution. Target deploy to staging 2026-03-12, canary 2026-03-13, prod 2026-03-15 pending QA. Follow-up: update runbook to block tag-namespace merges if active postback replay rate > threshold and add runbook step to drain replay queue prior to cache flush.
Merge PR#842 after review and run regression suite (assigned to SRE).
Update runbook and add pre-merge check to prevent overlapping operations during high replay load (assigned to Ops).
Billing to close manual audit trail and confirm final invoice adjustments (assigned to Connor Briggs).
Customer RCA and timeline to be delivered by 2026-03-11 (assigned to Support).
payload.summary: Hourly buffer credit held in escrow after tag-namespace merge during rate-selector cache flush

Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent garbled tokens and truncated embedding payloads partway through SSE streams when calls traverse the customer corporate mobile network. Problem correlates with short-lived TLS session resume (0-RTT / renegotiate) events during mobile carrier handoffs.

Impact:
- Multiple requests from FinGrid are returning partial text followed by malformed base64 in the embedding chunk.
- Customer-facing application displays '…[decoded error]…' and treats the generation as failed, causing degraded UX for >5% of streaming sessions in their fleet during the incident window.

Environment:
- Customer: FinGrid Analytics (enterprise, dedicated SLA)
- Region: us-west-2
- Path: client -> corporate mobile carrier NAT -> customer CDN -> Fastly edge -> Redwood ALB -> edge-proxy -> serving-runtime
- Client SDK: browser-based SSE adapter v1.2.1 with reconnect enabled

Steps to reproduce (observed by CS using the customer's repro):
1) Initiate streaming SSE generation with embeddings+text payload targeting redwood-7b-instruct.
2) Move device from wifi to mobile (carrier A) to trigger short TCP/TLS session pause and 0-RTT resume on subsequent requests.
3) Observe SSE stream progress; error appears ~4–7s after resume with corrupted tokens and partially-base64 embedding chunk.

Observed behavior:
- SSE stream continues but text frames contain garbled UTF-8 sequences and the final embedding item is truncated, producing invalid base64.
- Server-side ingress logs show normal downstream write attempts; edge-proxy logs include a TLS session resume event and a subsequent 200 stream chunk containing non-UTF8 bytes.

Expected behavior:
- SSE stream should continue cleanly across short TLS resumption events without introducing byte corruption or truncation.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- Repro script (curl+sse) and a few raw sse captures attached to the ticket (file names referenced in comments).

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Route streaming traffic through a stable connection (lock to wifi) or disable 0-RTT resumption in their corporate mobile proxy for the short term.

Notes on urgency:
- Customer is enterprise with SLA; business-critical feature impacted for a subset of users. Escalated to SRE and serving-runtime on call.
Timeline & findings:
- 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC - Customer alerted CS about repeated corrupted streams. CS created this ticket and attached capture files.
- 2026-03-10 15:01 UTC - Edge-proxy (on-call) searched Fastly and ALB logs for request IDs provided; found matching session IDs with TLS session resume markers.
- 2026-03-10 16:30 UTC - Reproduced locally in staging with mobile emulation and carrier-like NAT: observed non-deterministic byte corruption when L4 connection migrated and TLS session resumed with zero-round-trip data.
- Binary analysis: corrupted bytes align with SSE chunk boundary positions where our edge-proxy performs chunk coalescing. Hypothesis: on TLS session resume with 0-RTT, upstream TLS record reassembly causes shifted framing that edge-proxy's chunker misinterprets (mix of origin keepalive and application data), leading to splitting mid-UTF8 sequence and breaking base64 stream atomically.
- Serving-runtime verified no model output corruption pre-ingress (captured original payload from the runtime shows correct UTF-8 and well-formed embedding bytes). Corruption appears after edge-proxy / TLS layer.
- Early repro suggests issue more frequent for multiplexed SSE sessions where multiple logical streams are interleaved by the customer's CDN plus our proxy.

Logs & traces referenced:
- Fastly edge request IDs: fst-20260310-987a, fst-20260310-987b (see attached excerpts)
- ALB request ids: alb:abc-99321
- Edge-proxy trace: ep-20260310-5512 (linked in PR)
- Serving runtime: sr-20260310-5512 (clean payload)

Hypotheses prioritized:
1) Edge-proxy chunk coalescer incorrectly handles TLS 0-RTT resumption record boundaries during connection migration (high confidence).
2) Customer-side corporate proxy rewrites or buffer-shrinks during carrier NAT transitions causing mid-chunk truncation (medium confidence).
3) Rare kernel-level TCP reorder on the carrier network (low confidence).

Initial mitigation taken:
- Deployed a temporary patch in edge-proxy that disables chunk coalescing across TLS session-resume events for new connections in us-west-2 (canary, 5% traffic) to validate hypothesis.
- Notified FinGrid of workaround (disable 0-RTT on their corporate proxy) while validation runs.

Additional notes:
Workaround applied and verified; a patch to edge-proxy that avoids chunk coalescing across TLS resume boundaries was canaried and then rolled out to the customer's region. Customer re-enabled 0-RTT and confirmed repro no longer occurs in their tests. Next steps: backport fix to websocket handling, add unit tests around TLS-resume chunk boundary handling, and update streaming runbook. Refer to INT-4442 for rollout notes and follow-up tasks.

Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13T18:10Z we observed an elevated 5xx rate from the /v1/embeddings route for customers on dedicated pool dsp-6-us-east. Error surface: predominantly 502/503 returning from the API gateway with upstream runtime exits. Impact: multiple batch embedding jobs for NimbleSearch failing, ~12-18% request error rate for the tenant, visible increases in retries and customer timeouts.

Impact: Customer-reported batch uploads failing; customer-facing retry storms exacerbated backend pressure. Several internal alerts fired: apigw_5xx_rate_high, runtime_unexpected_exit, dsp-6_gpu_util_spike.

1) Submit concurrent embedding batches to customer-specific route (tenant id T-NIMBLE-22) with 8 parallel workers and batch size 256.
2) Observe rising 502s at the API gateway within 5-7 minutes.
3) Check runtime pod logs for SIGABRT / 'pthread_create' errors and thread pool exhaustion warnings.

- apigw: 502 rate rose from baseline 0.4% to 15% between 18:10 and 18:25 UTC.
- runtime rtm-04 (dsp-6-us-east) logged repeated: 'error: pthread_create: Resource temporarily unavailable' and 'fatal: cannot spawn thread' at 18:12:34 UTC.
- kernel/messages show 'task: pid XXXX killed by SIGABRT' around same window.
- GPU util for pool spiked to 92% and NVML reported frequent driver resets for a subset of nodes.

Initial hypothesis: aggressive prefetching + apigw hedged retries caused connection and work-queue pileup leading to thread exhaustion in the serving runtime.
What we checked: thread counts, ulimit/nproc, runtime threadpool settings, recent config sweeps. No recent runtime code deploys in us-east at incident start; a config bump to prefetch.window_size was rolled out globally at 17:55 UTC (INT-331002 linked).
Findings: rtm-04 hit process-level thread limit (nproc soft limit reached) while other nodes showed high accept-queue lengths. The apigw retry backoff was not honoring the reduced capacity threshold; hedged retries amplified work.
Possible contributory factors: customer workload with large batches (size 256) producing many short-lived threads per request path; the dedicated autoscaler lagged behind request surge.

2026-03-13T17:55Z - config sweep: prefetch.window_size increased (internal change INT-331002).
2026-03-13T18:08Z - first apigw 5xx alert for dsp-6-us-east.
2026-03-13T18:12Z - runtime rtm-04 logs thread create failures.
2026-03-13T18:20Z - Support engaged SRE, opened temporary rate limit on tenant route.
2026-03-13T18:35Z - Autoscaler scaled up 2 nodes but observed some nodes still in crashloop.
2026-03-13T19:05Z - Hotfix PR merged to add backpressure respect in apigw retry logic (github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3842).

Applied immediate mitigations:
- Scaled dedicated pool dsp-6 by +3 nodes to absorb burst.
- Added tenant-level temporary rate-limit to 60rps for NimbleSearch routine jobs to stop retry spin.
- Rolled back global prefetch.window_size for dsp-6 to previous value to reduce work amplification.
- Enabled apigw soft-backoff so hedged retries won't flood runtimes while autoscaler warms up.

Root cause addressed by a two-part fix: 1) runtime hardening to allocate a bounded worker thread pool (prevents unbounded pthread_create) and better nproc fallback handling, and 2) apigw change to honor backend capacity signals and avoid hedged retry amplification. Hotfix (infra PR #3842) deployed into us-east on 2026-03-13 19:05Z and runtime patch rolled on 2026-03-13 19:40Z. Post-deploy: 5xx rate dropped back to baseline ~0.6% within 20 minutes.
Resolution steps recorded and communicated to NimbleSearch. Incident declared mitigated at 2026-03-13T19:50Z; full resolution pending follow-ups.

- Create a runbook entry for 'thread/worker pool exhaustion' and include detection thresholds.
- Adjust autoscaler warmup policy for dsp-* pools to be more aggressive for batch-heavy tenants.
- Add tenant-level preflight checks for large-batch embedding uploads with recommended batch sizes.
- Audit prefetch config rollout gating so we don't apply global prefetch increases without region-specific safety checks.
- Add metric alert to detect 'pthread_create failure' log pattern and auto-throttle affected tenants.

2026-03-13T18:22Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer NimbleSearch reports repeated failures when uploading large batches. They see '502 Bad Gateway' after ~3-5 minutes. Added as P1 and escalated to SRE oncall.
2026-03-13T18:30Z - Marcus Li (SRE): Observed pthread_create failures on rtm-04. Suspect runtime worker explosion. Temporarily rate-limiting tenant and requesting immediate scale-up. Investigating whether nproc/u limits are being hit.
2026-03-13T18:40Z - Eleni Georgiou (Serving Eng): Confirmed runtime spawns >800 threads per process under current settings for this request shape. Preparing a bounded-pool hotfix; will coordinate patch and restart strategy.
2026-03-13T18:50Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer accepted temporary rate limit as workaround; reported immediate reduction in failed uploads after limit applied.
2026-03-13T19:10Z - Marcus Li (SRE): Hotfix to apigw to respect backend capacity merged and deployed (PR #3842). Monitoring for downstream improvement.
2026-03-13T19:45Z - Eleni Georgiou (Serving Eng): Runtime patch deployed to 6 nodes in dsp-6 set. Nodes stable; watching for any regressions. Post-patch logs show no further pthread_create failures.
2026-03-13T20:00Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Notified customer NimbleSearch that incident is mitigated. Customer requested postmortem and guidance on safe batch sizes.
2026-03-14T09:00Z - Marcus Li (SRE): Follow-up note - autoscaler warmup policy adjusted for dsp-6; will monitor next 48h for any drift.

## Issue summary
Customer (Proxima Bank) reports a sharp increase in HTTP 429 responses starting ~2026-01-20 09:10 PT on /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings. They believe this correlates with Redwood’s recent “priority routing / capacity protection” changes.

## Impact
- Customer batch + online traffic intermittently fails with 429s, causing retry storms on their side.
- Reported elevated end-user latency due to retries; some requests fail after their max-retry budget.
- Customer concern: enterprise tier expected fewer 429s, not more.

## Environment
- Hosted API, prod
- Region: us-east
- Routes: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings
- Auth: enterprise API key (account: PROXIMA-ENT-014)

## What customer is seeing
- 429 response body includes Redwood reason codes (examples pasted by customer):
  - "reason": "overload_protection_admission"
  - "reason": "quota_exceeded" (less frequent)
- Response headers observed:
  - Retry-After: 1 (sometimes 2)
  - X-Redwood-Request-Id present
  - X-Redwood-Throttle-Reason: overload_protection_admission (most common)

## Customer notes
- They run bursty workloads: 10–30s spikes during market-open events.
- Client currently retries immediately with fixed 100ms delay and no jitter.

## Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Send ~800–1200 RPS bursts to /v1/chat/completions with streaming disabled.
2) Concurrently send embedding bursts (~2k RPS) during the same window.
3) Observe 429 rates rising from <0.2% to 6–12% during bursts.

## Expected behavior
- Enterprise priority should protect them during fleet pressure; customer expects either stable acceptance or clearly defined, predictable throttling limits.

## Actual behavior
- Customer sees throttling during burst windows and requests clarification on:
  1) Why enterprise traffic is being rejected
  2) Whether the 429s are overload shedding vs quota
  3) Whether Redwood can grant a temporary burst exception / larger budget

## Initial support response (guidance provided)
- Confirmed that the new system returns distinct reason codes and customers should key their retry/backoff behavior on:
  - "quota_exceeded" (respect quota windows; reduce steady-state rate)
  - "overload_protection_admission" (transient overload; respect Retry-After; use exponential backoff + jitter)
- Recommended changes:
  - Use exponential backoff with full jitter; cap concurrency; do not retry immediately.
  - Honor Retry-After; treat 429 as a signal to shed load client-side.

## Investigation notes (internal)
Hypothesis: us-east protected-route capacity protection enabled for Proxima allowlisted accounts; per-route/per-tier admission control is active and may be gating bursts more aggressively than intended for this customer’s contractual traffic shape.

Checks performed:
- Correlated spike with protection annotations in hot-route dashboard (SRE): overload protection activated for route-group "chat" + "embeddings" during a concurrent regional pressure event.
- Confirmed most 429s for this account carry reason=overload_protection_admission (not quota).
- Verified no corresponding 5xx spike; p99 latency for enterprise class remained within SLO during event, indicating protections are working for fleet health but customer’s burst profile is being clipped.

Open questions
- What is Proxima’s contracted peak/burst behavior (RPS and token/s) for these routes?
- Is Proxima being routed to a stricter per-route budget due to route-group defaults?

## Requested outcome
- Explain semantics and provide an actionable plan.
- If eligible, grant a temporary burst exception with guardrails (time-boxed, monitored), or propose a dedicated capacity option.

Additional notes:
2026-01-20 10:02 PT - Customer (Proxima Bank): Shared 12 request IDs and headers. Majority show X-Redwood-Throttle-Reason=overload_protection_admission; a few quota_exceeded. They confirm current retry policy is fixed 100ms, no jitter, up to 10 retries.
Resolved with (1) customer education on 429 reason codes and correct retry/backoff behavior, and (2) a time-boxed, region-scoped burst exception for PROXIMA-ENT-014 on chat+embeddings (14-day expiry) with automated rollback guardrails. Customer to deploy improved client-side exponential backoff + jitter and concurrency caps. Separate guidance provided for quota_exceeded events (smooth usage / avoid end-of-window spikes).
payload.summary: Proxima Bank: unexpected spike in 429s after enterprise priority routing rollout (chat + embeddings)

1) Log in as a user with access to multiple organizations (tested with an account on QuantaHR orgs: quantahr-prod and quantahr-staging).

Issue summary:
We need guidance for a recurring scenario in which new hires are starting as part of a staggered onboarding (multiple cohorts sharing hot desks / loaner devices) and Security requires that elevated service accounts and corporate-managed keys are activated only after completion of mandatory training and SSO enrollment. HR wants devices shipped to site A, but the employee will be colocated at site B for week 1 and use pooled devices for day-zero tasks. We need a documented, repeatable process that balances (a) zero-day productivity, (b) least-privilege activation, and (c) hardware logistics for shared desks/loaner devices.

Impact:
- Delays in first-week productivity for engineers and PMs if access is fully blocked until training completion.
- Risk if privileged credentials or KMS-wrapped secrets are issued to pooled devices without additional controls.
- Operational burden on IT to physically coordinate device handoffs across sites when cohorts are staggered.

Environment:
- New hires across US-West and EMEA offices; some hybrid employees who will use shared desks in week 1.
- Standard corporate laptops (encrypted), a small set of loaner GPUs and docking stations maintained in central pool.
- Identity provider: Redwood SSO (SAML + OIDC). KMS: customer-managed keys in AWS for service accounts.

Questions requested (high level):
1) Can we implement timeboxed, scoped shadow/service accounts that grant only non-privileged access (email, docs, internal Slack channels) on day 0, with automatic elevation after training/SSO enrollment? What is the recommended lifecycle (duration, revocation hooks)?
2) For pooled loaner devices used on day 0, are there recommended controls to ensure they cannot access KMS-wrapped secrets or be used to cache credentials that would later allow privilege escalation?
3) Are there existing IR (incident response) or audit runbooks we should link to when a pooled device is lost or reused without a wipe?
4) What documentation and labeling should IT include in the device manifest to make cross-site swaps low-friction (e.g., tenant tags, cohort IDs, staged activation tokens)?

Steps already taken:
- HR and IT discussed a possible "staged activation" flow: create a user account in disabled state, ship a laptop with local OS account and a one-time enrollment token for SSO that becomes active only after HR marks training complete.
- Security proposed removing KMS decryption permissions from default service accounts and requiring a short-lived IAM role to be requested via the console after SSO MFA is completed.
- Inventory team trialed labeling loaner devices with QR codes that surface a web form to confirm wipe and enrollment.

Logs / evidence:
- N/A (policy/process question).

Desired outcome:
A short, prescriptive runbook that we can operationalize immediately for the next cohort (March 23 start), plus any policy changes required for scoped day-zero accounts and pooled device handling.
2026-03-10 10:14 - HR: Hi Maya—we started seeing this with the engineering cohorts. We need a repeatable path; can Security and IT provide guardrails?
2026-03-10 13:02 - Security (Leah Ortiz): Initial thought: allow a low-privileged 'day0' role with no KMS decrypt and block creation of long-lived API keys. We should also require device attestation (certificate) before granting network-level access to internal services.
2026-03-11 09:41 - IT (Samir Patel): We can ship laptops with autopilot imaging and a temporary local account. For pooled devices, we have current stock of 25 units. I'll confirm wipe procedure times and whether we can add a kiosk-mode enrollment link via QR codes.
2026-03-11 12:30 - SRE (Jonas Meyer): Suggest we add a 'just-in-time' IAM role broker for KMS access that requires SSO MFA and a short TTL (e.g., 1 hour). This avoids granting decrypt permission at day 0.

Additional notes:
Confirmed current loaner wipe SLA: IT can fully wipe and re-image a pooled laptop within 6 business hours when device is on campus and imaged via PXE/autopilot.
Inventory labels: QR-based manifest prototype returns device asset id, last-wipe timestamp, and assigned cohort id. Works with our internal asset service API (inventory-redwood/v1).
IAM constraints: existing service accounts hold KMS:Decrypt on 'redwood-dev-secrets/*'. All teams agree to revoke those permissions for new accounts and route through STS AssumeRole with MFA for sensitive operations.
Potential friction: non-corporate networks (coffee shops) may block SSO enrollment steps if we require corp VPN or device certificate ahead of SSO. Need fallback for remote hires starting offsite.
Workaround and proposed policy: 1) Implement 'Day-0' cohort role template: read-only access to core docs, Slack, and internal ticketing; no KMS decrypt and no long-lived API keys. 2) Add a short-lived IAM role broker (STS) for KMS access that requires SSO MFA and an explicit justification field; TTL default 1 hour. 3) For pooled devices: mandatory automatic device wipe on check-in/out with QR-scanned manifest that logs user, cohort, and timestamp. 4) For remote hires without corp network, provide an encrypted enrollment package (USB or pre-provisioned MDM token) that is valid for 72 hours only. 5) Update onboarding checklist and Confluence runbook; HR to withhold privileged role activation until training completion event is marked in Workday (automated webhook).

Security to draft short 'Day-0 role' IAM template and STS broker requirements (owner: Leah; due: 2026-03-14).

Request: Provision a scoped Slack automation that can (1) read Confluence page metadata for project/channel mappings and automatically apply channel topic/tags, and (2) produce a daily digest of active threads in specified channels and post a summarized thread into a pinned channel.

Impact: Reduce manual tagging of channels, improve discoverability for cross-pod collaboration, and provide lightweight async summaries to reduce meeting load. This will be used by runbook/ops channels and a few product pods on an opt-in basis.

Requirements:
- A bot service account with least-privilege scopes (read channel metadata, set channel topic/purpose, read pinned messages, post messages).
- Confluence-to-Slack mapping configuration: a Confluence page or page-space that contains a table of channel -> metadata (tags, retention policy, owner).
- Daily job (09:00 UTC) that aggregates top 10 active threads per channel, runs an extractive summary, and posts a single digest message with links.
- Ephemeral channel lifecycle hooks: when retention TTL set in Confluence mapping expires, send an automatic ownership ping and a 7-day deletion warning to the channel.
- Audit log entries written to an internal Confluence/ops page and a Jira ticket for each deletion action.

Acceptance criteria:
- Slack bot created and visible in org apps with documented scopes.
- Admin page (Confluence) editable by ops to control mappings and TTLs.
- Daily digest posts in #ops-digests and can be disabled per-channel via mapping.
- RBAC: only approved admins can modify mappings; bot cannot escalate permissions.

Notes: This is an internal-support automation; sensitive operations (channel deletion) must be gated and logged. We prefer a phased rollout: start with 5 pilot channels (ops-runbooks, infra-alerts, platform-rt) before broad enablement.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 - SRE Rotation (oncall@sre.redwood.ai): Please ensure digest jobs have retry/backoff and exponential jitter to avoid thundering herd when summarizing many channels.
2026-03-12 - Security: Suggested service account with short-lived tokens and KMS-encrypted credentials stored in vault; flagged channel deletion workflow for manual approval step.
Planned: (A) Create bot service account with scoped pilot permissions; (B) Publish Confluence mapping page and grant ops-admins edit access; (C) Implement digest lambda with summarization model (extractive), add jitter/retries; (D) Create deletion workflow that opens a Jira ticket and sends 7d/3d/1d warnings before deletion; (E) Run a 2-week pilot on 5 channels and capture feedback. Owners: Slack-ops (implementation), Platform Ops (pilot), Security (approval). Pending work: org-admin approval for channels:manage and final KMS/vault integration.
payload.summary: Enable contextual channel-tagging and daily thread-digest Slack bot with Confluence metadata sync

Environment details: CI runners are fleet of ephemeral GCP VMs (image: rwinf-ci-runner-202601), using systemd unit to spawn runner processes as user 'ci-agent'. Artifact storage is S3-compatible objectstore behind internal gateway (artifacts.redwood.local).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reported repeated 5xx spikes for a tenant on dedicated capacity. Errors surface as 502/503 from the API gateway and are followed by upstream runtime restarts. Pattern is periodic (~3-5 minute cadence) and correlates with a burst of short-lived streaming and embedding requests. Impact: customer experiencing elevated error rates and degraded throughput across several routes; production traffic impacted for NovusAI during business hours.
Elevated 5xx rate for NovusAI (dedicated pool). Intermittent complete request failures for streaming and small-embedding routes; customer reports timeouts and aborted streams. Estimated 18% request failure rate during waves, sustained for 8+ windows over the last 2 hours.
Dedicated GPU pool in us-west region. Instances running serving-runtime v2.14.1 with proxy v1.6. Healthchecks set to 10s interval, no jitter. Autoscaler configured with warm-pool size 4, ephemeral workers enabled.
1) Replay customer traffic pattern (short streaming sessions + embedding small-batch mix) against dedicated pool.
2) Run at the same QPS and concurrency mix used by NovusAI (documented in replay payload).
3) Observe accept queue depth on proxy and socket backlog metrics; watch runtime memory and connection counts.
Proxy accept queue grows rapidly in short bursts and then collapses, creating a 'resonance' pattern. During peaks, the serving runtime shows a concurrent spike in open FDs and KV-cache thrashing leading to OOMs and runtime process restarts. API gateway surfaces 502/503 while upstream cycles. After restart, the pool warms and pattern repeats.
- API gateway error rate: spike to 35% 5xx during windows (2026-03-10T14:22-14:27 UTC).
- Proxy accept_queue_size metric shows sawtooth with period ~180s.
- Runtime memory usage climbs to >92% before OOM; dmesg shows cgroup OOM kill on runtime PID.
- netstat on proxy shows many sockets in SYN_RECV and CLOSE_WAIT during peaks.
- Relevant traces: trace-id=trc-20260310-9b3a (attached link in Confluence page).
Initial triage: customer request pattern includes many short-lived connections followed by bursts of embed uploads and short streams.
Hypothesis 1: Lack of healthcheck jitter + synchronous prewarm created alignment where many ephemeral workers accept at same moment, amplifying backlog.
Hypothesis 2: Proxy backlog default (somaxconn) underprovisioned for dedicated pool; kernel socket backlog and accept queue interacting with app-level accept loop causes resonance.
Reproduced locally with replay at 0.9x QPS: observed accept-queue resonance and then runtime process OOM after sustained backlog.
Temporary mitigation tested: adding jitter to healthchecks and reducing ephemeral worker churn prevented immediate resonance in replay.
Observed that runtime prefetch module allocates large KV pages when many connections reach prefetch; combined with concurrent restarts this increases memory churn.
Attached artifacts: flamegraph, heap snapshot, proxy accept-queue time-series (links in related_confluence_pages).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 15:10 - NovusAI (Customer): Provided sample payloads and timestamps; confirms impact reduced when they temporarily rate-limited inbound embedding jobs.
Applied short-term mitigations: increased proxy accept backlog (somaxconn/accept_queue tuning) for affected dedicated pool, added jitter to healthchecks for NovusAI route, and deployed a runtime guard that limits concurrent prefetch allocations during high churn. These actions reduced the observed 5xx windows and prevented immediate runtime OOM restarts. Customer verified improved stability.
ENG-12345: Implement rate-limited prefetch in serving-runtime to avoid large concurrent KV allocations during connection churn (owner: Maya Lopez).
OPS-9876: Add adaptive accept-queue tuning and monitoring alarm for accept-queue-resonance pattern (owner: Ravi Patel).
DX-332: Update customer runbook to recommend healthcheck jitter and connection reuse settings for dedicated pools handling many short-lived streams.
Perform scale test with realistic mixed workload to validate changes and ensure no regression in latency or throughput.
payload.summary: Socket backlog resonance triggering periodic 5xx waves and runtime crashloop

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (OpenFinch Labs) reports intermittent 5xx responses when sending mixed chat+embedding requests at sustained rates (~250 rps) to the hosted API. Errors manifest as short spikes of 502/503 and occasional runtime exits on upstream workers. Problem started 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC and recurred during evening traffic windows.

Impact:
- Several production endpoints returning 502/503 for 30s-3m windows.
- Customer reports degraded UX and increased retries.
- A subset of upstream runtimes report SIGTERM then restart loops.

Environment:
- prod - us-west
- Customer on Dedicated pool tenant ID: ofl-dedicated-71
- Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/embeddings/batch

Steps to reproduce (observed at scale):
1) Send mixed workload from same client: 60% streaming chat sessions, 40% embeddings bulk upload (batch size 64).
2) Traffic ramp to ~200-300 rps over 2 minutes.
3) Observe proxy connection handoff latency increasing (long TCP/TLS setup times).
4) Upstream runtime processes receive SIGTERM and restart; 502/503s spike during this period.

Observed behavior / logs (excerpts):
- api-gateway logs: "2026-03-09T23:12:41Z proxy: handoff latency=789ms route=/v1/chat/stream tenant=ofl-dedicated-71"
- proxy logs: "handoff delayed, queue_depth=87, accept_wait=421ms"
- runtime syslog: "2026-03-09T23:12:44Z runtime[pid=2145]: Received SIGTERM, reason=parent_graceful_shutdown"
- runtime exit reason: "watchdog: preemption timeout during kernel swap"
- customer-reported: spike started ~23:10 UTC and repeated 23:30-23:40 UTC during their evening jobs.

Hypotheses so far:
- Proxy handoff latency (accept queue/backpressure) causes graceful shutdown logic in the runtime to fire (SIGTERM) while worker is still handling long-lived streaming connections, producing a cascade of exits and 502/503s.
- Noisy embedding bulk uploads are pushing accept-queue depth and causing large tail latencies; combined with tight graceful shutdown timeouts this leads to churn.
- Potential misalignment between proxy backpressure thresholds and runtime graceful shutdown thresholds (race condition).

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Rolled out a temporary accept-queue throttle bump on the tenant route for ofl-dedicated-71 at 2026-03-10T02:15 UTC (increased conn backlog limit + extended handshake timeouts).
- Suggested customer reduce embedding batch size to 16 as a short-term workaround.

Next steps:
- SRE to verify proxy -> runtime threshold alignment and increase graceful shutdown window for affected pool.
- Engineering to validate runtime shutdown logic under backpressure and check for stray SIGTERM triggers during kernel swaps.
- Ask customer to run reduced-batch test and report if 5xx stops.

Related artifacts:
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenant/ofl-dedicated-71/acceptqueue
- Incidents / runbooks referenced: CON-acceptqueue-backpressure-runbook

Support - 2026-03-10: Maya Patel: Acknowledged report and triaged. Informed customer we are prioritizing as P1. Requested pprof traces and runtime logs for the 23:10 window.
SRE - 2026-03-10: Aaron Li: Observed repeated accept_queue spikes for tenant ofl-dedicated-71 matching customer's timestamps. Queues peaked at ~120, avg handoff latency >700ms. Increased backlog soft limit on edge proxy as stopgap. Gathering kernel swap telemetry.
Engineering - 2026-03-11: Priya Desai: Preliminary debug indicates graceful_shutdown() path receives SIGTERM due to autoscaler preemption combined with proxy perceiving the worker as unhealthy (handshake timeouts). Propose: extend grace window by 6s and add hysteresis on preempt decisions during heavy-accept-queue pressure.
Customer - 2026-03-11: Jordan Hale (OpenFinch): Confirmed reduced batch size to 16 eliminated 5xx spikes in a 2-hour test window. Requested ETA for permanent fix and prevention for other tenants.
SRE - 2026-03-12: Ethan Brooks: Implemented canary with extended graceful shutdown + adjusted preempt hysteresis on 2 nodes in the pool. Monitoring for 48 hours. Initial signals show acceptqueue depth still high but no SIGTERM cascade after change.
Mitigation in progress: canary deployment extended graceful shutdown + preempt hysteresis. Customer workaround validated (reduced embedding batch size). Follow-up: engineering to harden runtime shutdown logic and add metrics to trace handoff latency -> shutdown triggers. Postmortem to be scheduled after 48h validation.
payload.summary: Persistent sporadic 5xx correlated with proxy handoff latency and runtime SIGTERM churn

2) Enter credentials when prompted for 802.1X (EAP-MSCHAPv2).

07:58 IT push: security team applied new baseline (NetworkAuthRateLimit) to SF-HQ OU to combat brute-force attempts; rollout targeted 150 machines.

Issue summary: Ephemeral GKE namespace creation succeeds but rolebindings fail intermittently during ML CI runs, leading to 'permissionDenied' errors when the canary deployment attempts to access GCS buckets and secret volumes.

Impact: Several CI-driven canary rollouts in staging have failed for the last 18 hours; developers cannot validate model rollouts and a few scheduled smoke tests are blocked. No production impact observed so far.

Environment: Staging cluster (k8s-ml-staging) in us-central1. CI runner uses workload-identity service account mapping to GCP service accounts. The failure appears tied to ephemeral namespace rolebinding automation that assigns iam.workloadIdentityUser and storage.objectViewer to the namespace SA.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger model canary CI (ci/canary-deploy with ephemeral-namespace flag).
2) CI creates namespace ns-ephemeral-<timestamp> and service account sa-ci-<id>.
3) Automation calls internal IAM binder to create RoleBinding and IAM policyBinding on the GCP service account.
4) Deployment pods mount secrets and attempt gsutil ls gs://model-artifacts-<staging>.

Observed behavior: RoleBinding creation API returns 200 but subsequent GCP IAM API responds with 403 permissionDenied when binding storage roles. Pod logs show accessDenied when reading secrets/GCS.

Expected behavior: Ephemeral namespace automation should complete rolebindings and GCP IAM policy updates within CI window so that pods can access required resources immediately.

Excerpt from CI run (timestamp 2026-03-12T14:22:03Z):
- binder: POST /namespaces/ns-ephemeral-16432/rolebindings 200 OK
- gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding model-ci-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role roles/storage.objectViewer -> ERROR: (gcloud.iam.service-accounts.add-iam-policy-binding) PERMISSION_DENIED: Caller does not have required permission iam.serviceAccounts.setIamPolicy

Kubernetes pod error (2026-03-12T14:22:41Z):
- error: failed to fetch secret redwood-gcs-creds: accessDenied: Access denied to secret manager resource projects/12345/secrets/redwood-gcs-creds

Initial hypothesis: recent org-level constraint change or a condition on the GCP Organization's IAM Deny policies introduced a new guardrail that blocks service account policy changes from the CI service account. Checked Cloud Audit Logs for 'SetIamPolicy' and found DENY entries with policy name 'deny-unscoped-service-account-mods' starting 2026-03-12 13:50Z.

What we checked:
- Cloud Audit Logs: denied SetIamPolicy calls from CI service account with policy ref org-policy/deny-unscoped-service-account-mods.
- IAM Binder service logs: binder is authenticating as svc/ci-binder@infra.redwood.internal; binder has iam.serviceAccounts.setIamPolicy in its role historically.
- Recent Terraform change: infra/iam/org-policies.tf rolled out constraint to prevent unscoped service account IAM changes; PR merged 2026-03-12 by infra-ops (PR #5402).

Interim conclusion: Org policy now blocks binder's action unless call includes 'resource.name' matching a whitelist or has a precise principal. Binder calls are generic and therefore being denied.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 - Security (Liam O'Connell): Need justification and timebound window for exception. Recommend temporary exception with audit logging and follow-up to change binder to use impersonation with precise principals.
Workaround applied: Infra ops created a timebound, narrowly scoped exception to org-policy for the binder service account limited to projects 'redwood-staging-*' and service 'svc/ci-binder@infra.redwood.internal' until 2026-03-20. Additionally, CI was modified to call an infra-runbook job that performs bindings under infra-admin credentials for pending jobs.
Permanent fix plan:
- Modify binder to perform IAM operations using short-lived impersonated credentials that include the required 'resource.name' attribute resulting in allowed SetIamPolicy calls (owner: Miguel Santos, ETA 2026-03-19).
- Add integration test in ci-configs to validate org-policy-compliant binding flow (owner: Priya Desai, ETA 2026-03-18).
- Postmortem and documentation update to runbook and Confluence page (owner: Security team, ETA 2026-03-22).
Follow-ups created: INT-587000 to track binder code changes; INT-587001 for org-policy exception audit and removal on 2026-03-20.
Add code change ticket for binder impersonation (INT-587000)
Update CI templates to include explicit project-scoping for policy binds
Schedule org-policy review with Security and Infra (invite sent)

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports periodic P50 latency spikes for requests pinned to us-east despite overall throughput and P95 remaining stable. Impact: Intermittent customer-facing slowdowns for chat completions and embedding lookups during control-plane residency refresh windows. Environment: Dedicated pool for ClarityHealth in prod-us-east; single-tenant reserved capacity with token-level residency stamps enabled. Observed window: spikes occur in short bursts (~10-30s) roughly aligned with pin refresh cadence.
1) Use customer API key scoped to ClarityHealth dedicated pool (token-scoped residency enabled).
2) Send steady stream of small completion requests and periodic embedding requests (approx 50 rps).
3) Observe p50 latency for requests over a 30 minute window and correlate with control-plane pin refresh timestamps.
4) Note: issue reproduced only when client connections are long-lived (HTTP keepalive) and when pin TTL refresh occurs during active connections.
2026-03-10T14:05:20Z edge-proxy[proxy-12] INFO connection-hand-off user=ClarityHealth token=tok_XXX src_ip=34.201.1.22 dest=us-east-edge-3 reason=pin_refresh
2026-03-10T14:05:21Z routing-service WARN route-change user=ClarityHealth old_path=us-east-edge-3 new_path=us-east-edge-7 latency-delta=220ms
2026-03-10T14:05:21Z serving-runtime INFO request-id=abc123 model=open-llm-13b-v2 exec_ms=45 total_ms=340
Client-side metric sample: p50 increased from 120ms baseline to 340ms during handoff window; p95 ~ unchanged (420ms -> 460ms).
Initial hypothesis: pin refresh causes control-plane to rotate residency stamp which triggers soft-handoff between edge proxies; long-lived keepalive connections may get proxied to a new edge that requires a TLS rehandshake or route reconnection leading to added 150-250ms on p50.
Correlation found between control-plane 'pin_refresh' events (every 15m by default for this account) and observed p50 spikes in request logs.
Observed that requests using HTTP/1.1 keepalive (no re-open) still experienced routing change at edge (proxy-level stream reattach) which added an extra hop: edge -> new-edge -> serving, compared to normal edge -> serving path.
No evidence of GPU contention or scheduler queueing during the spike windows (serving-runtime exec_ms unchanged).
DNS resolution times stable; TLS handshake logs show an increase in short-lived rehandshakes tied to the proxy handoff window.
Temporary replication of the problem in staging by forcing pin refresh confirmed the handoff reproduces p50 delta when connections are long-lived.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports P50 jumps to ~300-350ms during 'rotation' windows. They see this across small completion and embedding calls. They are concerned about user impact for chat UX.
Arjun Patel (SRE) 2026-03-11: I reproduced in staging by triggering a pin refresh and keeping connections open. Logs show proxy handoff adds ~200ms due to short-lived TLS rehandshake and extra routing hop. Raising to control-plane to discuss pin refresh behavior.
Lena Ortiz (Control Plane) 2026-03-11: Current pin refresh is implemented as a soft-rotate to balance control-plane leases. We can consider keeping connection affinity for active keepalive sessions until the session idle timeout to avoid immediate handoff. Filing INT-4472 for a control-plane change proposal.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-12: Shared preliminary findings with customer and suggested workarounds. Customer requests a short-term mitigation and asks for timeline for a permanent fix.
Short-term mitigation provided: advised customer to set client keepalive timeout < 30s to force client reconnection outside of pin refresh window OR set pin TTL to a longer value on their dedicated config to stagger refreshes (support can apply a temporary TTL override on their account).
Workaround applied for ClarityHealth: Support extended pin TTL for their dedicated pool to 60m for the next 72 hours (temporary config change) — reduced observed p50 spikes in monitoring by >80% during the next rotation window.
Long-term plan: INT-4472 created to change control-plane behavior to avoid breaking affinity for active keepalive connections; control-plane engineering to propose one of: a) honor active connection affinity until session idle, b) perform zero-downtime in-proxy transfer without TLS rehandshake, or c) coordinate rotation during low-traffic windows.
Follow-ups: assign control-plane owner to INT-4472, update runbook for residency pin rotations, and include a KB article describing recommended client keepalive and pin TTL settings for dedicated customers.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports intermittent 429 responses from the streaming text-generation endpoint when performing high-concurrency streaming sessions during daily traffic spikes. They are using a client-side token-bucket implementation to pace outgoing frames and believe the server is still enforcing additional quota checks that result in 429 bursts.

Impact:
- Intermittent user-facing errors in production for a subset of streaming sessions (~2-3% of requests during peak).
- Degraded UX: streaming sessions restart or fail to attach.
- Customer wants prescriptive configuration advice: how to tune client-side token-bucket parameters so they avoid server-side 429s and when to request quota increases or dedicated routing.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (dedicated pool for BrightCart)
- Region: us-east
- SDK: rwinf-js v1.4.2 using websocket-streaming mode
- Observed during peak business hours UTC 14:00-16:00

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Open 200 concurrent streaming websocket connections that each send an initial prompt to rwinf-7B-stream and then request 128 tokens at a time with backpressure disabled.
2) Each client uses a local token-bucket: refill rate 50 tokens/sec, bucket size 200 tokens.
3) Within 30s of traffic ramp, ~4-6% of connections receive a 429 and disconnect.
4) Server returns 429 with body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded", "retry_after": 10}.

Logs / headers captured by customer sample (sanitized):
- Response headers on 429: X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 1615800000
- Body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded", "retry_after": 10}
- Client-side: many streams show bursts of token consumption when user events batch on the client.

Customer request:
- Explain how server quotas and per-connection limits interact with client-side token-bucket throttles for streaming API.
- Provide tuning recommendations for token-bucket parameters and backoff strategies for streaming frames.
- Confirm whether dedicated pool configuration or quota increase is recommended as the long-term fix.

Desired outcome:
- Prescriptive config guidance the customer can apply immediately to reduce 429s.
- If config changes are insufficient, clear next steps for quota increase or Dedicated pool autoscaling adjustments.
Initial triage performed by Support:
- Reviewed customer request logs and our frontdoor metrics for their API key during the reported window.
- Confirmed pattern: X-RateLimit-Remaining hitting 0 concurrent with spike windows.
- Observed that dedicated pool still enforces API-level per-key quotas to prevent noisy-customer impact; separate per-connection concurrency ceilings exist on websocket handlers.
- Found customer client token-bucket is tuned for average throughput not burst smoothing; local bursts (e.g., many users triggering at once) can still cause short term outflow greater than server per-key burst allowance.
- No errors in serving-runtime other than expected 429s; no 5xx.

Hypotheses:
1) Client-side bursts exceed server-permitted short-term burst capacity even though average rate is under quota.
2) Websocket multiplexing behavior leads to many parallel frames being flushed when a user event happens causing temporary spike.
3) Dedicated pool autoscaler may be reacting but not fast enough for minute-scale bursts; server quota controls still throttle.

Troubleshooting actions taken:
- Asked customer to capture sample trace ids for a failure window (provided).
- Checked rate-limit headers and per-key metrics in Console; validated X-RateLimit-Remaining hitting zero.
- Reproduced locally with a small harness that mimics their burst pattern; confirmed 429s when many streams flush simultaneously.

Support findings summary:
- Server enforces both sustained quotas (per-minute, per-hour) and short-term burst allowance. The token-bucket on the client can mask sustained heavy usage but doesn't change server-side burst enforcement.
- Recommended immediate client config changes reduce 429 frequency in reproduced testing by ~80%.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 12:40 - Support (Miguel Alvarez): Received logs and started triage. Requested trace IDs and peak-minute counts. Reproducing against a staging dedicated pool replica.
2026-03-11 09:05 - Support (Miguel Alvarez): Reproduction succeeded locally. Preliminary recommendations posted in ticket. Asking customer to try conservative client changes (increase refill interval, enable backpressure, jitter).
2026-03-11 14:22 - Customer (BrightCart Engineering - Priya Rao): Applied suggested changes: refill 20 tokens/sec, bucket size 80, added randomized 50-200ms jitter on frame flush. Observed 429s drop to ~0.5% during next peak. Curious about server-side config and whether quota increase would help further.
2026-03-12 08:30 - Support (Miguel Alvarez): Noted improvements. Proposed follow-ups: request dedicated per-key burst quota increase or enable per-customer smoothing proxy rule. Opened INT ticket to evaluate autoscaler policies for the customer's dedicated pool. Recommended formal quota increase only if sustained traffic grows beyond current commit.
2026-03-12 11:00 - SRE (Aisha Patel): Linked INT-4121 created to review autoscale thresholds and websocket handler concurrency ceilings. Will report by 2026-03-16.
Partial mitigation delivered: customer applied client-side token-bucket configuration changes (lower refill rate, smaller bucket, jitter, enable client backpressure) which reduced 429 occurrences by ~90% in reproduced tests and initial production peaks. Next steps:
1) If BrightCart traffic grows sustainably beyond current commit, advise formal quota increase for their API key and/or increase dedicated pool capacity.
2) INT-4121 (SRE) to review autoscaler/concurrency settings for BrightCart's dedicated pool; potential small change to short-term burst allowance.
3) Provide a short playbook to BrightCart ops: recommended client config, monitoring dashboards to watch (rate-limit headers, per-key 1m/5m rates), and contact for quota requests.
Ticket remains In Progress until SRE recommendations are confirmed and customer is sent the final playbook.
- Send BrightCart the playbook and sample client-code snippets showing token-bucket and jitter implementations.
- Coordinate with SRE (INT-4121) for autoscaler and burst policy changes.
- If SRE recommends permanent change, schedule a controlled increase in per-key burst allowance and monitor.
- If customer requests, prepare formal quota increase request with finance approval and updated DPA if needed.
Advice to customer: start with client-side smoothing (smaller bucket, lower refill, randomized jitter on flush, enable backpressure) before requesting quota increases. Monitor X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers to confirm behavior. For sustained growth, request quota increase or additional dedicated capacity.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a dedicated deployment are observing 'stuttered' token/frame sequences when a transparent proxy path-change occurs mid-stream. After the client's SSE connection rebinds to a new upstream route, the resumed stream sometimes omits the final footnote (closing paragraph) and intermittently repeats a short prefix. Behavior is more common for long-running responses (>20s) and when the edge-proxy performs a quick connection swap (keepalive probe / health check).

Impact:
- ComposeAI reported ~7% of streaming requests for a specific dataset lost their closing footnote or returned duplicated 1–3 token prefixes after a route change.
- Customer application displays 'incomplete answer' to end users and retries which amplifies cost.
- Seen only on dedicated Tier deployments behind our edge-proxy; not reproducible in staging.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated (customer-managed) via redwood edge-proxy in their VPC egress path.
- Region: us-east (customer route uses two upstream edge nodes with active health probes).
- Models: redwood-chat-13b (primary), redwood-open-7b (fallback).

Steps to reproduce (observed / minimal reproduction):
1) Start a long streaming generation call (prompt size ~400 tokens, expected token stream ~500+).
2) While streaming, trigger a transparent route swap by briefly failing the primary upstream (simulated by toggling health check to fail for ~1s on edge node A).
3) Client re-establishes SSE to a new upstream (edge node B) and issues a resume request with last-ack offset.
4) On resume, output sometimes contains a duplicated 1–3 token prefix, and the final footnote (closing paragraph) is omitted; in other cases, the stream ends normally.

Observed logs & traces (high level):
- Edge-proxy: frequent 502->200 transition logs during the window; connection handoff shows short TCP close followed by new socket; no TLS handshake error. (see edge-proxy log snippet attached in comment).
- API gateway: resume request acknowledged, async resume flow shows 'partial-kv-primed' events and a small delay (~120–300ms) between resume ack and first resumed token.
- Serving runtime: a small set of workers logged 'kv-cache-not-prime' during resume which correlated with missing terminal footer.

Initial hypothesis:
- The resume logic and KV cache priming race: when the client reconnects to a new upstream quickly, the worker may start producing tokens from a partially primed KV cache resulting in a short duplicated prefix and the downstream end-of-stream marker being suppressed due to an early EOF/close during final write aggregation.
- Transparent edge-proxy route swap can coalesce/mangle keepalive/heartbeat frames causing a misalignment of the resume offset vs the primed state on the worker.

Requested customer impact data:
- Provide 3 example request IDs and timestamps where this occurred (ComposeAI supplied two in the first comment).

Investigation notes (timeline):
- 2026-03-10 09:45 (Support): Case opened after ComposeAI filed via support portal citing missing closing paragraph on 4/60 streams.
- 2026-03-10 10:30 (SRE): Collected edge-proxy trace for customer's egress group; observed route swap at 10:12:15 with a 800ms probe-induced socket reset.
- 2026-03-10 12:00 (Eng - serving-runtime): Identified resume paths that do not block on KV priming when the resume offset is within the current session window; added instrumentation to log 'kv-primed-state' for resumed sessions.
- 2026-03-11 02:15 (Support): Reproduced locally by orchestrating deliberate health-check toggles between two test edge nodes; saw same duplicate-prefix + occasional missing terminal footnote in ~12% of runs for long responses.

Mitigations tried so far:
- Short-term: Advised ComposeAI to enable 'resume-grace' 250ms client-side delay before reconnects; reduced incidence but did not eliminate it.
- Platform: Deployed additional logging to identify 'resume-without-full-kv' on resumed sessions (PR referenced below).

Next steps (planned):
- Engineering to add synchronous KV priming check before resumed token emission for resumed sessions where the resume offset matches the worker's recent window. This will be gated behind a feature flag to limit latency impact.
- Edge team to add brief drain window (100–300ms) on route-swap for SSE sessions to allow graceful handoff of in-flight streaming sessions.
- Validate fix in a dedicated canary environment that mimics ComposeAI's multi-node egress path.

Attachments / references:
- Customer-provided request IDs: compose-req-20260310-1102, compose-req-20260310-1128
- Related support tickets: SUP-214159 (similar resume delta investigation), SUP-314271 (edge route swap behavioral notes)
- Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/783 (instrument resume kv-priming)
Start a long SSE streaming generation (prompt ~400 tokens; expected output 500+ tokens)
Trigger a health-check toggle on the primary edge node to force route swap (~fail for 500-1000ms)
Client reconnects and issues resume with last-ack offset immediately
Observe resumed stream for duplicated 1-3 token prefix and check if final footnote/closing paragraph is present
2026-03-10 09:50 — ComposeAI (via portal): 'We saw missing footnote for request compose-req-20260310-1102 and prefix duplication on compose-req-20260310-1128. Customers see "Answer incomplete" and we have retries enabled.'

Additional notes:
Edge-proxy health-checks often flip for this customer because of short probe intervals configured in their egress group.
Resume logic currently optimizes for minimal latency; it does not always wait for a full KV prime when the resume offset looks recent.
Partial KV prime leads to re-emission of a small token prefix because the worker's local state lacks the last few KV entries and generates a short overlap before realigning.
Serving-runtime metrics introduced: resume_attempts, resume_kv_partial_count, resume_emit_delay_ms. Correlation found between resume_kv_partial_count spikes and customer incidents.
Temporary workaround: Recommend customers introduce a 200-300ms randomized reconnect delay (applies to ComposeAI) — documented in support reply.
Planned fix: Add synchronous KV priming barrier when resuming sessions where the resume offset is within active worker window (feature flagged).
Edge mitigation: Experiment with a 150ms drain window on route swaps for SSE sessions in canary environment.
Post-deploy validation plan: Run 10k long-streamed resumes in canary with intentional route swaps; target <0.5% missing terminal footnote rate before enabling broadly.
payload.summary: Stuttered frame sequences after transparent proxy route change — final footnote missing on SSE resume

payload.description:
Issue summary:
ClearPath reported a sustained increase in 5xx responses for a subset of API requests tied to their tenant during a period of steady medium concurrency. Symptoms included 502/503 responses from the API Gateway and rapid cycling of several serving-runtime instances for the tenant group.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: intermittent failed requests for embedding and chat endpoints (~3-8% error rate over a 45-minute window).
- Affected customers: ClearPath Analytics (enterprise) — business reports degraded UX and automated ingestion failures.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east-1 region.
- Tier: enterprise tenant pinned to redwood-rlhf-legacy model with fallback to gpt-medium-8k.

Steps to reproduce (reported by CS):
1) Replay customer production traffic at ~120-150 RPS with same request distribution (short chat + embedding bursts).
2) Observe 5xx increase after ~10-20 minutes concentrated on requests routed to tenant priority queue.
3) Runtime logs show repeated graceful-drain and restart cycles for some worker processes.

Observed behavior:
- API Gateway returns 502/503 for a subset of streaming and sync requests.
- Serving-runtime processes for tenant enter graceful-drain repeatedly, then fail health checks and are restarted.
- KV cache eviction spikes prior to the first failures.

Expected behavior:
- Traffic shaper and priority queue should preserve fairness; runtime instances should not repeatedly fail during steady-state medium concurrency.

Immediate logs / snippets (redacted):
- apigw: "upstream returned 502, host=runtime-xxxx; queue_wait_ms=842"
- runtime: "[WARN] draining due to priority-seat starvation; inflight=128; max_inflight=256"
- runtime: "OOM-like memory pressure detected in tenant sandbox; heap_used=1.8GB; restart scheduled"

Initial hypothesis:
- Priority-queue fairness imbalance caused head-of-line blocking for lower-priority work which increased request latencies. Increased inflight requests caused KV cache thrash and higher memory churn in the tenant sandbox, triggering runtime health failures and restarts which propagated 502/503s through the API Gateway.

Workarounds attempted by Support/Oncall:
- Short-term: temporarily raised per-tenant concurrency cap for ClearPath to smooth request queuing (apigw policy) and routed a percentage of traffic to fallback model variant.
- Restarted affected runtime pool with staggered backoff and increased socket backlog.
- Flushed a small KV cache partition serving the tenant to reduce eviction storm.

Next steps planned:
- Deploy a scheduler patch to better rebalance priority queues and avoid starvation (PR linked).
- Add a metric for per-tenant queue-age to alert earlier.
- Postmortem and runbook update with recommended per-tenant knobs.

Additional notes:
2026-03-13 10:05 - SRE (Priya Rao): Increased per-tenant concurrency cap to 180 for ClearPath and staged a graceful restart of runtime pool (stagger 10s). Error rate dropped from 7% -> 1.2% over 12 minutes.
2026-03-13 11:12 - Customer (Sarah Lopez, ClearPath): Confirming partial recovery; ingestion jobs completed but some backfill failed. Asking for timeline on permanent fix.
Timeline summary: 09:10 alert from ClearPath; 09:25 repro harness validated queue_wait and runtime drain; 09:40 increased per-tenant cap and restarted runtimes; 10:05 observed error rate decline; 13:40 hotfix PR created; 02:22 next-day canary validated.
Findings:
- The apigw priority queue implementation allowed a small set of long-lived high-priority requests to monopolize execution windows under this tenant traffic pattern (fairness weight enforcement bug).
- When priority-starvation occurred, request latencies pushed more in-flight contexts into the runtime which caused accelerated KV cache eviction; this amplified memory churn in tenant sandboxes (small memory leak in legacy model path) and triggered health restarts.
Evidence:
- Per-tenant queue_wait histogram and runtime heap usage graphs (links attached in Confluence).
- Similarity to SUP-62111 noted in linked_issues — same tenant-level throttling patterns but different root cause.
Mitigation applied: increased per-tenant concurrency cap, flushed tenant KV partition, and performed staggered runtime restarts which brought immediate error rates down to <=1%. Hotfix (scheduler weight adjustment) merged and canaried (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2481).
Permanent fix: scheduler change to enforce stricter fairness and a follow-up runtime patch to close the small memory leak in the legacy model path scheduled for 2026-03-20 deployment.
Post-incident actions:
- Create an alert on per-tenant queue_age > 250ms.
- Update runbook with steps to increase per-tenant cap and trigger graceful restart sequence.
- Inform Customer Success to follow up with ClearPath for impact credit discussion if requested.
Ticket status: Resolved (mitigation verified in canary and prod); postmortem in progress.
payload.summary: Elevated 5xx rate for ClearPath during priority-queue fairness imbalance causing runtime failovers

Issue summary:
Users report that Access Request approvals show as 'Granted' in the Support Console but the target internal service (runbook/console) still returns 403. Happens after the recent Okta issuer domain swap (okta-old.redwood -> okta-new.redwood).

Impact:
- Internal engineers cannot escalate to runbooks or use the console automation tooling after approvals.
- Blocks oncall workflows during testing; affects ~12 engineers across multiple teams.

Environment:
- prod (us-east) - internal console + identity-proxy + okta-new.redwood

Steps to reproduce:
1) Submit Access Request for runbook elevation in Support Console using existing flow.
2) Approver approves the request (shows Granted in UI).
3) Attempt to open runbook — receives 403 with 'missing RBAC grant'.
4) Inspect auth logs on identity-proxy and console-service.

Observed logs/snippets:
- identity-proxy: "ERROR auth: issuer mismatch: token_iss=https://okta-old.redwood/oauth2/default, expected=https://okta-new.redwood/oauth2/default"
- console-service: "RBAC: no matching grants for principal: user:12345 issuer=https://okta-old.redwood"

Notes: This started after the Okta issuer domain migration rolled earlier this week; some tokens/approval links still carry the old issuer in their assertion/redirect flow.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 12:00 - SRE oncall: Canary at 10% shows successful provisioning for previously-failing users. No obvious regression in other flows after 3h.
Initial hypothesis: RBAC grant lookup keys include issuer, so any token with old issuer won't match grants issued under new issuer mapping.
Checked audit logs: Access Request approval events authored at 2026-03-09 23:xx still contain 'iss' set to https://okta-old.redwood. Approvals created after 2026-03-10 02:00 have new issuer.
Identity-proxy currently rejects tokens whose 'iss' does not match configured accepted_issuers list (single value).
Support Console's approval token generator signs a short-lived JWT with an 'iss' claim set to the Okta issuer configured at time of generation. Some queued approvals were created before migration and delivered post-migration.
RBAC datastore keys: grants are indexed by (principal_id, issuer). When issuer changes, previously-created grants are still stored under old issuer namespace; provisioning call attempts to read grants using issuer from assertion.
Attempted local repro by forging approval JWT with old issuer and calling provisioning endpoint — repro'd 403 with same logs as production.
Short term mitigation: Deployed identity-proxy update to accept both https://okta-new.redwood and https://okta-old.redwood on the access-request/provisioning endpoint only. This allowed in-flight approvals to complete normally without touching global token acceptance.
Medium term fix: Backfilled RBAC grants for recently-approved requests by running migration job that normalizes grant keys from old issuer to new issuer for approvals in the migration window (2026-03-09 22:00 -> 2026-03-10 04:00). PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-tools/pull/57
Long term: Update approval token generation to include an 'orig_iss' claim and update provisioning to canonicalize issuer during lookup. Add explicit migration step to retirement playbook for future issuer changes. Added unit tests for multi-issuer acceptance in identity-proxy.
Follow-ups:
- Security to review acceptance window (Ethan & Claire).
- Rotate any long-lived service tokens that may embed old issuer references.
- Run additional audit to ensure no external tokens accepted accidentally.
