payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer sends a single batched request that includes three tool/function calls in sequence (pay-authorize -> record-ledger -> notify). In ~1% of requests during high concurrency the final two actions are executed only partially: pay-authorize succeeds once, record-ledger runs twice or not at all, and notify is missed. Impact: inconsistent financial and notification state for customers, visible as duplicate ledger entries or missed notifications.

Observed behavior: Walkthrough of a failing trace from PayFlux: the Go SDK client constructs a single multipart request with per-action metadata (action nonces and a per-request transaction-id). Under an autoscaling event, the request appears to be split across two serving replicas (replica A returns an ack for action1 and action2, replica B returns for action3) — but due to nonce rotation on client retry and KV cache warmup on the runtime, a second execution of action2 is observed downstream (duplicate ledger row) while action3's webhook did not fire. Expected behavior: either transactional ordering with single execution per action (at-most-once) or clear guidance that batched multi-tool sequences are not atomic and require customer-side dedup/compensation.

Environment details: Go SDK v0.9.3 (enterprise fork), network: TLS via customer-managed VPC peer, Redwood serving-runtime v2.6.1, autoscaling policy with burst pools enabled in us-east-1.

1) Customer sends a single API call using Go SDK BatchFuncCall that contains three tool invocations in sequence with per-action nonces and transaction-id header.
2) Load generator sends 2000 concurrent batched requests to the same route with short inter-arrival times to trigger autoscaling/burst routing.
3) Artificially inject a transient 500ms delay on replica A's response path (to simulate GC/warmup) using test harness.
4) Observe downstream systems (ledger DB and notification webhook) for duplicates/missing events and collect request/response traces.
5) Compare SDK client-side retry logs and server-side request routing traces for matching transaction-id and action nonces.
CLIENT: [2026-03-10T16:12:43Z] tx-id=tx-89c3 action=pay-authorize nonce=na-17 attempt=1 -> 200 OK
CLIENT: [2026-03-10T16:12:43Z] tx-id=tx-89c3 action=record-ledger nonce=na-18 attempt=1 -> 202 Accepted
CLIENT: [2026-03-10T16:12:44Z] tx-id=tx-89c3 action=notify nonce=na-19 attempt=2 -> 200 OK (no webhook received)
SERVER: [trace-id=tr-45f] routed to replica-A, batch-part: actions [pay-authorize, record-ledger], cache-miss, runtime-kv-warmup=95ms
SERVER: [trace-id=tr-46g] routed to replica-B, batch-part: actions [notify], owner-retry=true, runtime-fallback=stream-to-nonstream
DOWNSTREAM: ledger DB shows two rows for tx-89c3-record-ledger (ids 10087, 10088) with identical payloads.

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 14:10 UTC - PayFlux (Customer): We rely on batched sequences to be effectively ordered for accounting. Duplicate ledger entries cause reconciliation errors. Can you confirm whether batched multi-tool sequences are atomic?
Hypothesis 1: SDK-side nonce rotation on per-retry path causes idempotency-key mismatch when parts of a batch are retried to different replicas.
Hypothesis 2: Serving runtime can split batches for load reasons; split parts carry the same transaction-id but action-level nonces are expected to be stable; we observed mutation of nonce header on client side during retry callback path.
Logs show replica-A returned accept for first two actions while replica-B later processed the third action; mismatched attempt counters on client show action3 was retried with a different nonce value.
Cache window: idempotency cache TTL is 30s for route; when replica-B was cold the KV cache warmup delayed dedup check long enough for second execution to be accepted (race).
Repro: Deterministic repro achieved in lab by enabling burst pool and injecting 200ms processing jitter; duplicate ledger row & missing webhook reproduced 7/20 runs.
Workaround provided to customer: 1) Disable burst pool for the impacted route (via Console -> Routing -> RouteSettings -> allow_burst=false) to avoid mid-request split; 2) Set SDK to use stable per-action idempotency keys (client must not rotate action nonces on retry), recommended field: ActionIdempotencyKey derived from transaction-id + action-index.
Short-term platform fix: engineering to add server-side normalization that prefers per-request transaction-id when available and treats missing/rotated action nonces as identical for a short grace window. Patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1224 (WIP).
Long-term: design doc proposal to document transactional guarantees for batched multi-action requests; options: explicit 'transactional' mode that pins request to a single replica, or stronger at-most-once semantics via global idempotency index with cross-replica coordination. Draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Batch+Transaction+Spec (in review).
Customer follow-up: CS recommended a reconciliation-safe pattern (idempotency token per high-level transaction + idempotent downstream writes using transaction-id). Customer accepted workaround; will schedule a follow-up after platform patch rollout.
Status: monitoring patch rollout to staging; recommend keeping ticket open until PR merges and customer verifies in staging.
payload.summary: Batched multi-tool request: partial side effects when retry splits actions across replicas (Go SDK)

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer observed a sudden P99 latency spike for small-batch embedding requests. During the window (~2026-03-12 09:15-09:35 UTC) requests that should have egressed in eu-west were routed to ap-southeast, adding ~220ms network RTT and causing downstream timeouts in their ingestion pipeline.

Impact: Production ingestion pipelines for Streamline Analytics degraded (10% request failures, 25% higher token latency). Affects users pinned to eu-west and using batch-embeds endpoint.

Environment: prod | eu-west (tenant: streamline-prod, customer-tier: enterprise)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send concurrent small-batch embedding calls (batch size 8, concurrency 40) to /v1/embeddings with tenant API key from EU.
2) Observe egress path in edge logs and p99 latency in Grafana.
3) Repeat during off-peak — issue appears correlated with higher control-plane heartbeat jitter.

Observed behavior: During burst, control-plane reports for tenant showed delayed residency stamp refresh; edge selected nearest healthy edge (ap-southeast) as fallback for some connections. TLS handshakes and auth token validation retried against APAC edges causing auth retries and additional latency.

Expected behavior: Requests from eu-west pinned tenants should egress through EU edges unless strict residency is unset or explicit fallback policy permits cross-region egress.

Logs/metrics referenced: grafana/dashboard/embeddings/tenant-streamline-p99 (snapshot attached in comments), edge-proxy logs (edge-eu-01, edge-eu-03), control-plane healthcheck timeline (2026-03-12T09:14:50 -> 2026-03-12T09:16:20). Slack thread: #support-streamline-212022

Temporary impact mitigation: Workaround applied to pin tenant to eu-central-edge pool to avoid dynamic fallback while we investigate.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:02 - Support (to customer): Temporary pin applied and connections restarted. Asking customer to validate. They reported immediate improvement to baseline latency around 10:10 UTC.
2026-03-13 08:05 - Customer (Streamline Analytics): Confirmed mitigation worked for now; asked for RCA and preventive measures.
Data collected: edge-proxy traces, control-plane residency refresh logs, DNS logs from eu-edge NAT cluster. Pattern: intermittent delay in control-plane TTL refresh for residency stamp (~35-90s) under high concurrent embed churn. During that window, edge token validation path falls back to 'nearest healthy edge' bucket which currently includes APAC edges by proximity metric when EU edges show transient auth timeouts. Hypothesis: a combination of DNS rebinds at NAT + control-plane heartbeat suppression triggers transient stamp expiry and fallback-routing. Reproduced in staging with synthetic churn at ~40 concurrent batch requests. Correlated with increased control-plane GC pauses in the same timeframe (GC activity in control-plane host cp-14).
Mitigation: Reapplied tenant strict pin to a dedicated eu-edge pool and performed graceful connection drain -> immediate latency return to baseline. Root cause: transient control-plane heartbeat lag combined with NAT/DNS rebinds allowed the residency stamp to be treated stale, which triggered fallback routing logic that selected APAC edges. Permanent fixes planned: 1) Increase control-plane heartbeat alerting and reduce stamp expiry threshold; 2) Harden fallback routing policy to prefer region affinity longer when stamp is near-expiry; 3) Network ops to investigate NAT/DNS rebind frequency and patch; 4) Deploy control-plane GC tuning PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/9876). Follow-ups tracked in INT-451900 (engineering task) and SUP-742913 (similar customer case).
ENG: PR#9876 - GC tuning and heartbeat backoff (target release 2026-03-20)
NETOPS: Investigate NAT/DNS rebinds on eu-edge cluster (ticket INT-451901)
PLATFORM: Add residency-stamp-near-expiry metric and alert (runbook update)
CS: Share postmortem with customer and schedule 1:1 RCA call

Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring short windows (30s-3m) of elevated p95/p99 token latency and intermittent 504s immediately after long idle periods followed by traffic bursts. Behavior started after customer's migration to Dedicated pool with autoscaling enabled; reproducible in their prod us-east cluster.

Impact:
- Several API calls timed out (504) for a subset of requests during burst.
- Observed p95 rising from ~120ms to 800-1500ms and p99 up to 3s for 20-60s windows.
- Affects latency-sensitive features (live doc previews) for NimbleDocs; customer reports user-facing UI flicker and failed saves.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) in prod-us-east
- Serving runtime version: 2026.02.18-release
- Continuous-batcher service image: cbatcher-1.7.0
- Autoscaler: proprietary-pool-autoscaler v2.1

1) Ensure a dedicated pool with zero recent traffic for >5 minutes.
2) Send a burst of ~200 small generation requests across 5 concurrent connections (prompt length ~20 tokens) at time T0.
3) Observe p95/p99 over next 2 minutes in Console per-route latency.
4) Repeat with different idle durations (1m, 5m, 15m) and note correlation with severity of spike.
Extracted excerpts (prod-us-east) 2026-03-01T14:02:11Z - 2026-03-01T14:05:00Z:
- continuous-batcher: INFO span=cbatch/window:start idle_window=312s chosen_window_ms=50
- continuous-batcher: WARN span=cbatch/dispatch delay_ms=810 queue_depth=37
- serving-runtime: WARN span=runtime/kvcache miss_rate=0.72 cold_kv_initialization=true
- api-gateway: ERROR 504 upstream_timeout route=/v1/generate status=504 trace_id=...
- autoscaler: INFO pool_scale=0 -> 2 reason=burst_detected scale_latency_s=28

2026-03-01 15:00 - Support triage: Verified customer p95/p99 spikes aligned to bursts after idles; reproduced in repro cluster with same runtime and cbatcher image.
2026-03-01 16:30 - SRE observed that continuous-batcher chooses larger batch window after long idle: chosen_window_ms grows from typical 20-50ms up to 250-500ms in initial burst phase.

Additional notes:
2026-03-02 09:10 - Tested a patch toggling aggressive idle backoff (PR linked). Initial patch reduced p95 by ~60% in isolated test but introduced slightly increased token fragmentation (tradeoff).
2026-03-02 11:45 - Observed KV cache cold-start contributing to per-request overhead; requests routed to freshly started workers had additional 150-300ms overhead while KV tables populated.
2026-03-02 14:20 - Correlation found between autoscaler scale latency (>20s) and severity of p99 spikes; when pool was warm (no scale up) spikes diminished.
2026-03-03 09:00 - Decided to implement a combination of faster initial batch timer, early-pass fast-path for tiny workloads, and proactive worker warmup hooks tied to autoscaler events.
2026-03-02 12:30  NimbleDocs (Customer): Provided traces and consent to test fixes in their dedicated staging pool. Customer asked for temporary mitigations while fix rolls out.
Partial mitigation deployed (2026-03-03):
- Canary release of cbatcher patch that shortens initial batching timer after idle and enables a tiny-workload fast-path.
- Added autoscaler->worker warmup hook to prepopulate KV caches when new nodes start scaling for a detected burst.
- Added Circuit alerting in Console: 'cbatcher.initial-window-ms > 200 && p99 > 1500ms' for prod-us-east.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customers on a Private deployment (SigmaDocs) reported intermittent truncation of gRPC streaming responses when requesting long-form outputs (models: gpt-xl-32k, opt-30b-stream). Partial transcripts are returned and the client receives gRPC UNAVAILABLE or INTERNAL after a partial stream. Impact: Production traffic experienced degraded UX for users performing document synthesis; approx 7% of streaming requests fail for large responses during peak windows. Environment: Private deployment in us-east (VPCE + corporate L7 inspection proxy in front of VPCE egress). Steps to reproduce: 1) POST /v1/streams generation request for a prompt that induces >30k tokens of output using model gpt-xl-32k behind customer's L7 proxy. 2) Observe partial streaming followed by a final gRPC error (UNAVAILABLE/14) or HTTP/2 GOAWAY in proxy logs. Observed logs/metrics: - Serving node logs show stream closed with transport error after ~30s of streaming. - Customer's proxy (Bluecoat) logs show GOAWAY frames emitted with last_stream_id set; reason field empty/NO_ERROR. - TCP captures show no TLS alerts and connection remains open for a short time after GOAWAY. - Client shows okhttp errors indicating stream ID exhaustion or stream reuse attempts. Temporary workaround used by customer: 1) Route streaming traffic through a proxy bypass (direct VPCE egress) eliminated the failure. 2) Lowered chunked token window on client to force more frequent flushes (reduced failure rate but not fully mitigated). Investigation summary: Hypothesis: Customer L7 proxy is configured to aggressively insert GOAWAY frames when concurrent HTTP/2 stream count or stream lifetime thresholds are hit. For long-lived, high-throughput streaming (large models) proxy sends GOAWAY which causes an in-flight stream to be terminated mid-response; some client stacks mis-handle the transition leading to partial transcripts instead of a clean retry. Evidence: - Proxy logs correlate GOAWAY timestamps with truncated streams. - Increasing "max_concurrent_streams" on a test proxy reduced occurrences. - Bypassing the proxy eliminated failures. Root cause: Proxy-level HTTP/2 lifecycle management (GOAWAY injection / stream limit enforcement) combined with client library behavior leads to non-idempotent partial results when long-lived streaming responses are terminated without graceful handoff. Next steps and remediation: 1) Customer to update L7 proxy config to: a) disable GOAWAY injection for VPCE-to-Redwood control plane/streaming endpoints or b) increase max_concurrent_streams and stream lifetime limits. 2) Redwood to add a server-side guard: detect GOAWAY mid-stream and emit a clear final trailer indicating retryability where possible, plus guidance in our private-deploy runbook. 3) Recommend customers configure ALPN passthrough / avoid HTTP/2 rewriting for streaming routes. Resolution: Customer updated proxy to allow HTTP/2 pass-through for /v1/streams and increased max_concurrent_streams; the error rate dropped to <0.1% during the monitoring window. Follow-up: Engineering PR created to add clearer final trailer when terminating streams (see related PR).

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:20 - SigmaDocs Network Admin (customer): We tested bypassing the corporate proxy for a subset of traffic and saw no truncations. We'll test increasing max_concurrent_streams and share results.
Test harness: replayed large-model streaming workload against customer-like proxy (Bluecoat) with configurable concurrent-stream limits. Observed direct correlation between GOAWAY emission and truncated streams. Confirmed bypass and config change mitigations. Proposed fix for runtime: emit explicit 'retryable: true' trailer when we detect forced mid-stream termination to help client-side retry policies.
Customer reconfigured corporate L7 proxy to pass HTTP/2 streams for /v1/streams and increased max_concurrent_streams; Redwood delivered a runtime change to add a clear trailer on forced stream termination. Monitoring shows issue resolved (failure rate <0.1%).
Merge and deploy PR to emitting canonical termination trailer for forced mid-stream closures
Add runbook entry and preflight checklist for Private deploy customers with L7 proxies
Share guidance with Solutions Engineering for pre-prod verification steps
payload.summary: L7 proxy GOAWAY injection causes intermittent gRPC stream truncation for large-model streaming on Private deploy (us-east)

comments: 2026-03-10T10:15:00Z Aditi Rao: Customer opened after noticing large 99p spikes. Provided initial diagnostic checklist and asked for pcap and SDK config.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent multi-second slowdowns for generation requests from their service that appear as long tails (95-99th percentile spikes). These spikes correlate with a high number of client retries and a rise in 5xx/timeout retries logged at the API gateway.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat experiences show delayed replies for ~15% of sessions during peak traffic windows, causing SLA alerts and user complaints.
- Revenue-impacting for ChatFlow’s paid tier (enterprise contracts).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod), region: us-east-1
- Customer SDK: redwood-js v1.11.2 (HTTP/2 enabled by default in their environment)
- Backend models used: rwdl-phi-2.1 and rwdl-psi-1.0 (mixed workload)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Run steady stream of short prompt requests (avg tokens=30) at ~300 req/s using SDK default client configuration.
2) Observe 95p/99p latency spikes after ~20–40 minutes of sustained load.
3) If maxConnections is increased locally, spikes reduce.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Gateway logs show a pattern: burst of new request attempts, followed by rapid client-side retry storms (exponential backoff starting at 100ms, max cap 10s, no jitter).
- SDK metrics: socket churn increases (many short-lived TLS handshakes), concurrent in-flight requests exceed pool size, HTTP/2 stream queueing increases per connection.
- Serving runtime traces show normal token generation latency once request reaches rack; delays are pre-rack (transport/queueing).

Initial hypothesis:
- Combination of aggressive deterministic backoff (no randomized jitter) and conservative HTTP connection pool sizing leads to head-of-line blocking. With HTTP/2 multiplexing, long-lived streams and socket churn reduce available streams on existing connections and new requests queue behind inflight/blocked streams. TLS session reuse disabled in the customer's infra increases handshake overhead and short-lived sockets.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally by running redwood-js v1.11.2 with maxConnections=6 and backoff policy: fixed base 100ms, multiplier 2, no jitter. Observed identical 95p spikes after ~25 minutes.
- Turning on jitter and increasing pool to 40 eliminated the spikes in load test.
- Packet captures from customer (pcap) show many TLS handshakes and RSTs when pool is saturated.
- Related logs: API gateway trace IDs 20260310-ARK-0091 through ARK-0098 attached by customer.

Mitigation / workaround provided to customer:
- Immediate: bump SDK client maxConnections to 30 and enable HTTP keepalive with 90s idle timeout; enable randomized jitter (uniform or full jitter) in backoff. This reduced 99p from ~3.8s to ~420ms in customer staging.
- Short-term: recommend SDK upgrade to redwood-js v1.12.0 which defaults to jittered backoff and safe pool sizing heuristics.
- Long-term: SDK team will ship telemetry to detect "pool saturation patterns" and warn users when default config may cause head-of-line blocking.

Next steps / open action items:
- SDK: ship v1.12.3 patch to make jitter required and to change default maxConnections heuristic for HTTP/2 heavy clients. (assigned SDK-ENG).
- Customer Success: confirm customer applied recommended config to production (ChatFlow to confirm by 2026-03-16).
- Observability: add dashboard alert for "client retry ratio > 5% and new TLS handshakes per second > threshold".

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 09:30 - ChatFlow Ops (Elena M.): Applied recommended bump to maxConnections=30 and enabled jitter; reported immediate improvement in staging. Will roll to prod tonight.
Mitigation applied by customer (increase pool + enable jitter). SDK patch scheduled (v1.12.3) to make safer defaults. Monitoring alert created to detect recurrence. Case to be closed after 72h of stable production metrics.
payload.summary: Keepalive/backoff misalignment + HTTP/2 multiplexing causing head-of-line blocking and perceived inference lag

Issue summary: After initiating a tenant geo-split migration (ClearSight Analytics) to move production traffic from us-west to eu-west, a subset of inference requests continued to egress via us-west for ~10-30s windows, causing p95 latency to jump from ~120ms to ~850ms and sporadic TLS renegotiation errors. Impact: Customer reports degraded latency for EU-based users and elevated error rate (502/524) during cutover. Environment: Production, dedicated tenant on Redwood Dedicated using strict residency=true and model redwood-gpt-large-v2 pinned. Expected: All traffic for tenant should egress in eu-west after migration cutover. Observed: Intermittent cross-region egress and TLS handshake retries correlated with our control-plane maintenance window and edge cert rotation.
1) Customer triggered geo-split migration using console 'Start region migration' for tenant ID T-7391
2) Control-plane rollout initiated pin refresh and edge coordinator scheduled edge cert rotation
3) Observe traffic during cutover windows using customer's p95 latency dashboards and our tokens/egress logs
2026-03-10T02:14:31Z EDGE-LB: selector=eu-west-1 -> routed to us-west-2 (fallback) reason=pin-refresh-expired ttl_remaining=0
2026-03-10T02:14:34Z TLS: handshake error: remote_renegotiate during connection to 44.210.11.72:443, retry_count=2
2026-03-10T02:14:35Z CONTROL-PLANE: residency-binding refresh start for tenant=T-7391, change_set=geo-split, rollout_id=rl-2026-03-10-02
Initial hypothesis: residency pin-expiry and edge healthcheck flapping during cert rotation caused routing fallback to nearest capacity (us-west-2) despite strict residency flag set.
Checked control-plane logs: refresh requests for tenant T-7391 completed, but there is a 12s delay between control-plane commit and edge-lb binding reconciliation during the rolling upgrade.
Edge LB telemetry shows NAT session affinity causing existing upstream TCP sessions to persist to us-west-2 while new sessions prefer eu-west-1; combined with cert reissuance we saw TLS renegotiation and short-lived 5xx bursts.
Found a codepath in edge-lb that clears residency binding when healthcheck returns soft-fail during certificate replacement; this allowed fallback routing even though strict residency should block egress to non-resident regions.
Reproduced in staging with smaller window by simulating cert rotation while forcing healthcheck timeout; observed identical egress behavior and p95 jump.
2026-03-10T03:00Z - Aisha Patel: Customer reported initial spike at 02:14 UTC. Attached their p95 chart and sample request IDs.
2026-03-10T04:20Z - Marco Ruiz: Correlated with our scheduled edge cert rotation at 02:12-02:18 UTC. Creating follow-up with edge-lb team to validate healthcheck behavior.
2026-03-11T09:15Z - Priya Shah (SRE): Verified staging repro. Raising severity to Sev1 due to customer P1 impact. Patch proposed to add grace window for residency binding during edge maintenance.
2026-03-12T13:30Z - Marco Ruiz: Patch merged to edge-lb (PR 4872) that prevents residency binding clear on soft-fail during cert rotation. Deployed to canary clusters in eu-west-1 and us-west-2.
2026-03-12T18:45Z - Aisha Patel: Customer validated with synthetic traffic and reports stable p95 ~130ms post-patch. Still monitoring for two full maintenance cycles.
Workaround/Fix: Deployed edge-lb patch that preserves residency binding during certificate replacement and extends pin-refresh grace window by 30s. Adjusted control-plane requeue to shorten reconciliation lag during rollouts. Customer validation: ClearSight ran two synthetic cutovers — no cross-region egress observed and p95 returned to baseline. Follow-ups: 1) Add metric 'residency_binding_reconcile_lag' and alert for >5s, 2) Update geo-split runbook to pause cert rotations during tenant cutovers unless zero-downtime mode enabled, 3) Postmortem scheduled with edge-lb/infra teams (link in related_confluence_pages).

Issue summary: Customer reports SSE streaming sessions ending with a trailing silence and an incomplete final JSON object after an iOS client (managed device) reconnects. The client receives a partial JSON payload (closing bracket missing or truncated final text) but the stream does not emit an explicit terminal event. Impact: Customer's app shows 'incomplete' responses for ~5-15% of long-running streams on iOS 15/16 devices behind the Apple HTTP proxy used in their MDM. This affects Generation and Chat endpoints and causes user-visible corruption in message endings. Environment: prod-us-west, customer using our hosted API via SDK v1.12.0, mobile network: corporate Wi-Fi with Apple HTTP proxy/transparent caching. Observed: - Session logs show a short idle period then a socket rebind/hand-off from device path manager. - Edge logs include: "connection: id=sk-8765 partial_close=true late_fin=true" and serving-runtime logs show "stalled-flush: true" for the stream session. - Client-side: SDK reports reconnect, normal resume handshake, then receives no explicit "[DONE]"-like event or end-of-stream marker; final JSON block is truncated. Steps to reproduce (customer-provided): 1) Start a long streaming generation (>120s) on iOS device on corp Wi-Fi. 2) Background the app for ~10s then bring it to foreground. 3) Observe stream reconnect and final payload missing trailing characters. Expected: stream resumes and emits final terminal event or complete JSON. Observed: trailing silence and truncated final object. Additional notes: Issue more frequent when device OS performs a connection warm-up (path negotiation) or when Apple HTTP proxy inserts an intermediary probe. This appears different from standard proxy chunking issues we've seen previously because the connection close code sequence is unusual (delayed FIN coalesced with keepalive).
[edge-2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] x-request-id=7f9c2a session=ss-04f3
[edge-2026-03-12T14:02:12Z] connection: id=ss-04f3 partial_close=true reason=idle_probe_coalesce code=SOCKET_MIGRATE
[serve-2026-03-12T14:02:12Z] stream_id=ss-04f3 stalled-flush=true kvcache-primed=true last-frame-offset=18432
[client-logs] sdk.v1.12.0: reconnecting, resumeToken present
[client-logs] received chunk: "{\"choices\": [{\"text\": \"...and finally we recommend\"}\n\n(EOF)\n"
Initial hypothesis: Apple HTTP proxy on managed networks sometimes coalesces an idle-probe FIN with a subsequent TCP migration, which the edge treats as a definitive stream close before the serving-runtime has flushed the trailing buffered tokens. Differences vs known issues: not classic proxy truncation or chunk reordering; here the edge emits partial_close marker and we see a stalled flush rather than an explicit RST. Reproducer verification: Support able to reproduce locally using an iOS device simulator + a transparent proxy that delays ACKs. Correlation: request ids with partial_close show higher incidence when keepalive interval on client > 20s. Temporary mitigation: instruct customer to enable websocket fallback in SDK or set keepalive to 15s. Observed workaround success: websocket fallback avoided truncation in 30 test runs (0/30 truncations).

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 16:30 - ScribeNow (Customer): We can enable websocket fallback in our app, but would prefer SSE to be robust. We rely on SSE for analytics pipeline compatibility.
2026-03-12 08:45 - Ingrid Müller (Edge Eng): Hypothesis: edge-proxy currently converts unusual FIN+probe sequences to partial_close and notifies upstream synchronously. Proposing instrumentation to defer terminal event emission by 250ms to allow flush. Preparing a small spike PR to toggle via runtime flag.
2026-03-13 15:45 - Ingrid Müller (Edge Eng): Preparing PR with flag gated by label 'defer-terminal-on-coalesced-fin'. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1423. Plan: deploy to canary for 48h then progressive rollout if no regression in connection counts or memory use.
Workaround: customer enabled websocket fallback in their app (short-term). Engineering created a canary server-side mitigation (defer terminal emission by 250ms for sessions that match Apple HTTP proxy heuristics). PR opened and canary shows significant reduction. Follow-ups: - Monitor canary for 48h (Liam/Edge team). - Add more robust detection for coalesced FIN patterns and extend test harness to include Apple HTTP proxy behavior (Ingrid). - Postmortem if rollout proceeds to prod to capture metrics and potential regressions.
payload.summary: Trailing silence and incomplete final JSON when re-establishing SSE after iOS connection warm-up behind Apple HTTP proxy

Background: Multiple platform and product teams have asked for a standardized, short-lived integration playground that bundles a Jira project, Confluence runbook space, and Slack channel. The goal is to give cross-functional teams (eng, QA, infra) a consistent place to run integration tests, onboard third-party tools, and exercise deployment hooks without creating ad-hoc spaces that are hard to track.

Request: Create a templated, self-serviceable integration-playground offering with the items below and sensible defaults for lifecycle and security. This ticket captures the provisioning and automation requirements; implementation should be reusable and parameterizable for teams to request via an internal portal/Slack bot in a follow-up story.

Impact: Low immediate risk but high operational value — reduces setup time for integration experiments, reduces noisy ephemeral channels, and centralizes auditability for guest access and CI webhooks.
Jira project: key INTGPLAY, project template = Software Project (Kanban) with issue types: Task, Bug, Experiment. Default components: integration, infra, ci-cd.
Confluence space: 'Integration Playground - INTGPLAY' cloned from a thin template that includes: incident playbook, runbook checklist, onboarding steps, and a 'CI webhook manifest' page.
Slack channel: private channel #intg-play-<team> created automatically during provisioning, members synced from Jira project roles; naming convention enforced.
Service account: 'svc-intg-play-bot' with scoped tokens for Slack app and a GitHub webhook user (rotated monthly).
Automation: on-create hooks that wire a repo webhook to the Confluence CI webhook manifest, and add an issue automation rule to create a runbook page when a 'Release Test' issue is transitioned.
Guest approval flow: external guests require approval from two project owners via an automated request; approval should appear as a Slack message with Approve/Decline buttons that link to Jira request.
Lifecycle policy: default expiry 14 days; channel/space/project archived at expiry and owners emailed 72h before; owners can extend once per archive cycle.
Observability: create a lightweight audit log entry (Confluence page link) summarizing provisioning params and the GitHub repo receiving the webhook.
RBAC: Project role mappings: Owners (can add guests), Members, Read-only observers; Slack members mapped to Jira roles; Confluence restrictions mirroring Jira project roles.
1) Provisioning script must use existing org templates and run with a single approval in Jira. 2) Create a GitHub webhook using a scoped service account and store the webhook secret in the vault. 3) Slack channel creation via Slack provisioning bot with membership synced from Jira project role groups. 4) Add scheduled job that checks for expired projects/spaces/channels and triggers archive workflow plus notification email. 5) All actions must be idempotent and provide human-readable audit output (timestamp, actor, params).
- Owners group: team leads + oncall engineer (default).
- Members group: users explicitly added by Owners.
- Guests: external vendor accounts require 2-owner approval via Slack interactive message.
- Service accounts must be created with least privilege and have an automated rotation policy (30 days).
- No anonymous or public group permissions on Confluence or Jira pages created by this flow.
- Webhook secrets must be stored in Vault/KMS; never placed in Confluence pages.
- Service account keys rotated automatically and usage logged.
- Provisioning job must run in a restricted runner and require token with narrow scope.
- Audit events for create/archive must flow to central audit stream (link logs to observability pipeline).
A templated Jira project INTGPLAY can be provisioned via the internal UI or automation script with parameters for team name and expiry.
Confluence space is created from template and contains runbook and CI webhook manifest page with placeholder fields filled from provisioning parameters.
Slack private channel is created with correct name and membership, and visible in Slack for all members. Approval flow for guests functions end-to-end (request -> 2 approvals -> guest added).
A GitHub webhook is successfully created against a specified repo and triggers a test payload that creates an entry on the Confluence CI webhook page (test harness).
Expiry job archives the Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channel and sends owner notifications 72h prior.
1) Requestor opens a short form (internal UI or slash command) with params: team_short, owner_emails, repo_url, expiry_days (default 14). 2) Controller creates the Jira project and maps Owners/Members groups. 3) Confluence space cloned from thin template and placeholder fields replaced. 4) Slack channel created and membership synced. 5) Service account and GitHub webhook created; webhook secret stored in Vault. 6) Notification sent to owners with links and a 72h pre-expiry job scheduled.
- Use platform-provisioner library for idempotent resource creation.
- Parameterize template with: team_short, owner_emails, repo_url, expiry_days.
- Vault path: secret/intg-play/{{project_key}}/webhook.
- Use existing Slack provisioning bot but extend membership sync endpoint to accept Jira role groups.
- Add unit tests for webhook lifecycle and a staging dry-run.
- Coordinate final rollout with Security and Compliance for service account onboarding.

Additional notes:
Priya Ramesh (Security) (2026-03-11): Security: dedicated service account recommended. Also require monthly key rotation and audit hooks. We'll add review for vault access policy.
Diego Alvarez (Infra) (2026-03-12): Noted. I can add the webhook creation/job into the automation repo. Will need the template Confluence space exported or a short doc describing required pages/variables.
Create internal portal UI story to call this provisioning flow (separate ticket).
Add telemetry: count of active playgrounds and avg lifetime for observability dashboard.
Run a tabletop with two teams to validate guest-approval flow next quarter.
payload.summary: Provision 'integration-playground' Jira project + Confluence space + Slack channel with CI webhook and guest-approval gate

payload.description:
Issue summary: A single payment from vendor BrightArc (vendor_id: V-9982) was applied to PO-7789. The vendor submitted two partial invoices that shared the same vendor_reference token (BR-INV-2026-03). One invoice belonged to PO-7789 and the other to PO-7810. The payment engine matched the vendor_reference and auto-applied the whole payment to PO-7789, leaving PO-7810 unpaid and creating a $24,600 GL misallocation in account 2201.

Impact: Financial misstatement for March close if not corrected; downstream payment failure to PO-7810 blocking goods receipt and potential vendor escalation. Affects month-to-date AP aging and reserve calculations. No customer-facing outage but material for finance (>$20k).

Environment: Production finance dataset, BrightArc vendor profile, payments settled via payment-processor StripeConnect integration on 2026-03-02 14:12 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (how support triaged):
1) Reviewed BrightArc AP ledger and vendor invoices.
2) Searched for vendor_reference BR-INV-2026-03 and found two invoice records with different invoice_ids (INV-22011 and INV-22012) tied to different POs (PO-7789 & PO-7810).
3) Queried payment application logs: payment PAY-70321 matched on vendor_reference and applied to INV-22011/PO-7789 only.
4) Confirmed PO-7810 remains open and goods receipt was processed on 2026-03-01.

Logs & attachments: payment-apply.log excerpts (attached in ticket), screenshot of AP ledger showing duplicate vendor_reference, CSV export of invoices for vendor V-9982.

Initial findings & hypothesis: The auto-apply heuristic prioritizes exact vendor_reference and then earliest invoice date; because INV-22011 had an earlier invoice_date, the full payment was applied there. System did not detect duplicate vendor_reference across open POs. No evidence of duplicate payment from vendor. The payments-processor returned a single settlement.

Immediate risk mitigation performed: Placed a temporary hold on any further auto-applies for BrightArc by toggling vendor.auto_apply=false for vendor_id V-9982 (temporary config change recorded in change log). Accounting team alerted and advised to hold close-entry of affected GL account until reversal is processed.

Requested action: Finance ops needs a manual reversal of payment PAY-70321 from PO-7789/INV-22011 and re-apply $24,600 to PO-7810/INV-22012. After reallocation, request a short reconciliation report and journal entry guidance for GL 2201 adjustment.

Next steps owner & ETA: Assigned to Sophie Ramirez (Finance Helpdesk) to coordinate reversal with Payments team and AP system owners. Target to complete reversal and re-apply by 2026-03-10 to meet period-close timelines.

Additional notes:
2026-03-05 10:02 - GL Team (Maria Chen): Provided journal entry guidance for GL 2201: debit account 2201 $24,600 and credit clearing account 1205 $24,600, and then re-post after allocation. Please confirm once reversal is posted for final entries.
Manual reversal created (RM-881) and posted 2026-03-09. Payment PAY-70321 re-applied to INV-22012/PO-7810. Journal entry JE-2026-03-78 created to correct GL 2201. Vendor profile updated to require unique vendor_reference per PO; follow-up task created to add duplicate-reference detection in payments service.
Create a ticket for engineering to add duplicate vendor_reference detection to payments auto-apply (owner: payments-team)
Update vendor onboarding docs to mandate unique invoice references for multi-PO billing (owner: vendor-ops)
payload.summary: Ambiguous invoice reference caused payment to be applied to wrong PO; request reversal and reallocation

Request to add/update standardized RFP response snippets in the Generic Response Tool (GRT) used by AEs/SEs.

Background:
We are refreshing the Enterprise Security Enablement Kit and need GRT to reflect the same approved language. Field is currently copy/pasting from older docs, which is causing version drift (esp. ISO wording, data residency nuance, and audit log export claims).

Request scope:
1) Create a new snippet pack: "Enterprise Security (2026)" with curated blocks by category.
2) Deprecate/redirect older snippets tagged "Security FAQ 2024/2025" to reduce accidental use.
3) Add guardrails: a short header on each snippet reminding users to not modify compliance claims without review + link to evidence request process.

Categories + required snippet titles (exact):
A. Security Program
- "Security program overview (SOC 2)"
- "Vulnerability management + penetration testing (approved wording)"
- "Incident response + breach notification (non-contractual overview)"

B. Data Protection & Data Use
- "Data use: no training on customer data (definition + caveats)"
- "Data retention + deletion (deployment-mode specific)"
- "Subprocessors + DPA request pointer"

C. Encryption & Key Management
- "Encryption in transit"
- "Encryption at rest"
- "Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) by deployment mode"

D. Access Controls
- "SSO/SAML + supported IdPs"
- "SCIM provisioning"
- "RBAC model and granularity (Console + API)"

E. Audit Logging
- "Audit log coverage (events)"
- "Audit log export (SIEM/S3) + limitations"
- "Audit log retention controls"

F. Deployment Modes / Shared Responsibility
- "Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: shared responsibility summary"
- "Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) security overview (approved)"

Non-goals:
- Do not add any roadmap or "on-request" capabilities that are not supported today.
- Do not include contractual commitments; only describe current capabilities/processes.

Content source of truth:
Snippets must match the latest approved language in the Enterprise Security Enablement Kit (Confluence/Drive). If any conflicts are found, pause and escalate to Security/GRC for clarification.

Acceptance criteria:
- All snippet titles above exist in GRT under a single pack labeled "Enterprise Security (2026)".
- Each snippet includes a "Last reviewed" date and owner line.
- Each snippet includes a link to the Confluence index page for canonical references.
- Older "Security FAQ 2024/2025" snippets are either removed from search results or clearly marked "Deprecated - do not use".
- Sales/SE users can filter by category and copy snippets without losing formatting (bullets preserved).
- Audit log export snippet explicitly states supported export destinations and avoids implying every event type is available in every deployment by default.
- ISO snippet language does NOT claim certification; it must be framed as alignment-only unless explicitly certified.

Requested due date:
By 2026-02-18 (needed for Nordbank and Aurora Financial questionnaire/RFP workflows).

Approvers for snippet content:
- Security/GRC: Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov
- Product Security PM: Naomi Feldman
- Messaging: Camila Reyes

Notes:
If GRT cannot support per-snippet "Last reviewed" metadata, add it as the first line of the snippet body.

Additional notes:

Added per-snippet "Last reviewed" + owner line and canonical link to Confluence index/evidence request process. Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 we observed repeated spikes in privileged API calls originating from IPs not associated with our known vendors. Each spike followed a new webhook registration event for the same third-party integration name. Impact: Potential unauthorized use of a service account (svc-webhook-consumer) and elevated API activity that may expose data or state changes. Initial triage suggests the webhook registration flow allowed a callback URL that later triggered server-side token refresh behavior.
Multiple high-privilege API calls (read/write) executed for short bursts over 3 distinct windows. No confirmed data exfiltration yet; potential risk to confidential customer metadata and internal job scheduling. Affects two regions' serving clusters; autoscaling also triggered additional GPU allocation during bursts.
1) Create a new webhook integration via Console > Integrations > Add Integration using name 'thirdparty-webhook-ops'
2) Provide a callback URL hosted on a third-party domain and select 'svc-webhook-consumer' as the associated service account
3) Trigger a sample event from the third-party site and observe server-side token refresh and subsequent API calls in request logs
4) Confirm activity correlates to the time of registration in audit logs
a) Request logs: multiple POST /v1/internal/jobs from svc-webhook-consumer token at 2026-03-12T09:21:13Z (ip=45.120.33.8)
b) Audit trail: integration.create events for integration id intg_98a7 at 2026-03-12T09:20:49Z by user automated-bot@example.com
c) Auth logs: token refresh events for svc-webhook-consumer at 2026-03-12T09:21:12Z and 2026-03-13T02:14:02Z
Hypothesis: The webhook registration flow inadvertently allowed third-party supplied metadata to influence token lifecycle behavior (callback URL triggered handshake causing server to refresh/retain token).
Observed IPs do not match any on our vendor allowlist; reverse lookup shows fastly-like provider hosting transient payload endpoints.
No obvious lateral movement detected from the service account; calls mainly invoke internal orchestration endpoints and a small set of read operations on customer metadata buckets.
SRE confirmed autoscaler reacted to higher request rate, creating temporary capacity in us-east which increased our cost footprint during bursts.
1) Disabled new webhook registrations for 'thirdparty-webhook-ops' pattern and paused automated integration onboarding (2026-03-12 10:10Z)
2) Rotated svc-webhook-consumer API keys and revoked all active tokens for that service account (2026-03-12 10:45Z)

5) Notified Product Security and Compliance; initiated targeted audit of recent webhook registrations (2026-03-12 12:00Z)

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightLearn reported a sudden elevation in 5xx responses (502/503) for API routes serving small prompt requests starting ~2026-03-10T15:12Z. Impact: several customers experienced failures in chat completions and short embedding calls; BrightLearn (dedicated tenant) saw 40% of requests failing for a 6-minute window. Environment: prod-us-east (dedicated cluster for BrightLearn), models: redwood-open-13B and redwood-opt-7B.

Observed behavior: Around 15:12 UTC the apigw error rate rockets from baseline 0.2% to 28% within 90s. Accept queue length climbs sharply on edge proxies; upstream serving runtime pool reports rapid worker creation, OOM-like logs, and frequent preempt/restart events. Simultaneously, the scheduler performed a configured batch-queue flush job (scheduled maintenance task) that triggered eviction of queued requests.

Steps to reproduce: 1) On prod with tenant BrightLearn, trigger a batch-queue flush for small-payload routes (test route: /v1/chat/complete?tenant=brightlearn). 2) Ramp a steady small-payload traffic at 300 rps (simulated client). 3) Observe apigw accept queue and runtime worker churn.

Logs & metrics (highlights): - apigw: 2026-03-10T15:12:31Z "upstream unavailable" spikes; 15:13:05Z many 502s with upstream reset. - runtime: repeated "worker init failed: EV_RETRY_LIMIT" and "pagefault: vm_prefault_failure" around same timestamps. - scheduler: scheduled job "batch-queue-flush" executed 15:11:58Z on cluster brightlearn-prod-01. - infra metrics: accept_queue_length from 12->780 in ~45s; runtime_active_workers doubled in 60s; kernel pagefaults and GC pause increased.

Hypothesis: The scheduled batch-queue flush created a synchronized eviction of long-tail queued requests causing a rapid flood of short-lived requests onto the serving runtime. The runtime's ephemeral worker pool attempted to scale up aggressively, oversubscribed local resources (CPU/memory) and caused worker init failures and pagefault spikes. The API gateway then observed unhealthy upstreams and returned 5xx errors. Additional factor: tenant-weight rebalancer had recently migrated a small fraction of traffic to this cluster which reduced headroom.

Issue summary:
Customer LexiconAI reports an unexpected credit reversal and a net charge on their finalized monthly invoice for Feb 2026. They were previously issued a provisional +$1,420 credit on 2026-02-28 labeled 'aggregate-metering-warmup-credit' which was applied to their invoice on 2026-03-01. On 2026-03-05 the credit shows as reversed and an invoice adjustment of -$1,420 appears as a charge.

Impact:
- Customer budgeted around the provisional credit; reversal caused immediate negative balance and a billing alert to the customer finance team.
- Customer is on Dedicated tier and reports downstream reconciliation failures with their accounting system.

Environment:
prod - us-east (dedicated cluster dcap-lex-01)

Initial hypothesis:
Preliminary triage suggests a change in metering fingerprint generation during a policy refresh on 2026-03-02 caused hourly aggregation keys for a subset of embed jobs to be reclassified. That reclassification made previously grouped warmup microbatches look like distinct meter lines, triggering duplicate postback suppression logic to misattribute credits and then cause a retroactive reconciliation that reversed the provisional credit.

Customer statements (from email thread):
- "We saw a provisional credit and then it vanished; our ledger shows a negative line item for Mar 5."
- "This affects month-end close and we need a full audit trail for our finance team."
1) Customer runs large concurrent embed warmup job across 10 nodes using org key X.
2) Metering service aggregates hourly postbacks into fingerprint groups.
3) On 2026-03-02 a config push expanded fingerprint inputs to include 'quantization_profile' for policy reasons.
4) Same warmup traffic now hashes to two different aggregation keys across the boundary, which triggers dedup and credit reallocation paths during nightly reconciliation.

Observed result: provisional credit applied then reversed with corresponding invoice adj.
Expected result: provisional credit persists or is reconciled without reversal for identical logical traffic.
- Ingest logs: s3://metering-logs/prod/us-east/2026-03-01/lexicon-embed-warmup.log (contains duplicate batch headers)
- Reconciliation run: job-id reconciler-2026-03-05-03:14 (attached CSV snapshot available on request)

- Slack thread: #support-lexicon (ts 1619.2026)

2026-03-10 09:20 - Billing eng: Replayed reconciliation for customer with original and new fingerprinting rules. Found that ~6% of hourly postbacks changed key due to quantization_profile defaulting from 'none' -> 'auto' in the policy push.

Preliminary root cause: Policy refresh expanded fingerprint entropy without safe backfill; reconciler logic doesn't treat provisional credits as idempotent across fingerprint splits.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses for a single enterprise tenant (AcmeRetail) routed through the us-east-1 API-Gateway cluster. The traffic pattern correlated with a spike of large multipart/chunked uploads from that tenant. The API gateway proxy started allocating large per-connection buffers while parsing malformed chunk metadata; this drove memory pressure on the ingress proxies and led to upstream runtime processes (serving-runtime) OOMing and restarting. Impact: ~18% 5xx rate for the tenant across multiple routes, intermittent streaming disconnects, and several customer-facing requests failing for ~40 minutes during the peak. This is customer-impacting and blocking their QPS-critical ingest flows.
Customer-facing elevated 5xx across text generation and streaming endpoints for AcmeRetail. Observed increased retry storms from client (hedged retries), and temporary rate loss for 2 internal services depending on tenant-specific routing. Estimated ~1500 failed requests during event window.
1) From a client in us-east-1, send a POST to /v1/streams with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and intentionally malformed chunk sizes (e.g., send an undersized chunk length header followed by larger payload).
2) Attach a large file part (~30–200MB) in a single chunk frame while keeping connection open.
3) Repeat at ~5 concurrent connections to reproduce buffer growth quickly.
4) Observe api-gateway proxy memory climb and serving-runtime OOM logs in ~30–90s.
[2026-03-10T03:21:05Z] apigw-proxy-12: parsing chunk header failed: invalid-length '000aX'
[2026-03-10T03:21:06Z] apigw-proxy-12: allocating buffer 32768 -> 104857600 for connection tenant=acme-retail
[2026-03-10T03:21:22Z] ingress-proxy-7: memory pressure high: rss 92%
[2026-03-10T03:21:28Z] serving-runtime-3: runtime OOM: failed alloc 104857600
[2026-03-10T03:21:30Z] serving-runtime-3: watchdog restart triggered (exit code=137)
[2026-03-10T03:22:10Z] apigw-metrics: 5xx_rate tenant=acme-retail window=5m value=0.18
[2026-03-10T03:58:01Z] apigw-alert: resolved: proxy memory normalized
Initial hypothesis considered DNS/timeouts or backpressure amplification. After correlating access logs and buffer metrics, the pattern pointed at malformed chunked bodies causing the http parser to fallback to a slow-path that accumulates data in memory until either a full delimiter or timeout. The parser does not enforce a strict per-request content-length cap for Transfer-Encoding: chunked, so large or malformed chunks can cause the proxy to allocate progressively larger buffers. The ingress-proxy runs in the same node pool as serving-runtime processes; when the proxy RSS climbed, kernel OOM killer targeted runtime processes rather than the proxy (smaller oom_score_adj), causing upstream restarts and 502/503s. Heap snapshots from a warmed serving-runtime instance show large slab allocations immediately before OOM.
1) Immediate: added an ingress rule to throttle and reject chunked uploads > 16MB for the AcmeRetail tenant via per-tenant rate-limit policy (applied at 03:30 UTC).
2) Rolling restart of ingress-proxy pool with tightened ulimit and earlier buffer reclaim behavior applied (03:45 UTC).
3) Customer advised to stop large multipart uploads and switch to signed pre-signed object uploads to S3 for large files; support provided sample client code (03:50 UTC).
Partial mitigation applied and service returned to normative 5xx levels by 04:10 UTC after ingress throttles and restart. Permanent remediation tracked in follow-up tasks: tighten the parser limits, ensure proxies are preferable OOM targets, and add per-connection chunk size cap. No long-term data loss detected. Incident remains open pending code fix rollout.
Ingress HTTP parser allowed malformed chunk metadata to drive unbounded per-connection buffer growth under Transfer-Encoding: chunked. The ingress proxy and serving runtime co-location led to memory pressure killing upstream runtime processes, producing elevated 5xx.
Apply tenant-scoped content-size and chunked-upload rejection rules. Recommend customers upload large blobs via object-storage workflows instead of embedding large multipart uploads through the API gateway.
- SRE/Runtime: implement a hard cap on per-connection buffered bytes for chunked transfer (PR proposed: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521) - Target: 2026-03-17.
- Gateway: add parsing defensive checks and early 4xx on malformed chunk headers. Target: 2026-03-16.
- Ops: move ingress proxy to dedicated nodes (isolate from serving-runtime) as a medium-term deployment change. Target: 2026-04-01.
- Product/Solutions: document recommended large-file ingestion patterns for enterprise tenants. Target: 2026-03-20.

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 10:15 UTC - PM (Liam O'Connor): Requesting prioritized rollout of parser guard rails due to enterprise customer impact.

Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout of gptx-13b-rev1 for NimbusHealth, a subset of tenant sessions were intermittently routed to a fallback model. Investigation shows the root symptom is a divergence between KV prefix caches on different multipath routes, causing session pin decisions to disagree and the routing layer to oscillate between pinned and fallback variants. Customers reported mixed outputs and increased latency for a small cohort.
Approximately 3% of the customer's traffic in us-east experienced mixed-model responses and elevated tail latency (p95 increased from 180ms to ~750ms) over a 45-minute window. No data loss. Customer-facing quality regressions for affected sessions; higher error rate observed in orchestration logs (HTTP 502/504) around the same timestamps.
1) Start a canary rollout for gptx-13b-rev1 with multipath prewarm enabled and cohort sampling at 2%.
2) Send a consistent stream session for a tenant with session affinity pinned to the canary cohort.
3) Observe the edge-proxy logs for parallel prewarm probes; watch KV cache keys on two different routing paths (edge A vs edge B) diverge in TTL/state.
4) When one path returns a stale/missing prefix entry while the other has a prewarmed prefix, orchestrator's pin-consensus logic can fail and route to fallback variant intermittently.
5) Reproduce by toggling a simulated prewarm delay on one path (see test harness in PR 4591).
Attached excerpts: edge-proxy logs show alternating route decisions for session token=eyJ... between route-72 and route-88 at 2026-03-12T14:03:21Z; serving-runtime shows KV cache miss for prefix 'tenant/nh-42/session/abc' on route-88 while route-72 reports cache hit; orchestrator emitted 'pin-consensus-mismatch' traces and returned fallback policy 0x3 at the same time. Relevant trace IDs: trace-7a9f2c, trace-7a9f2d. Full logs uploaded to s3://redwood-support/SUP-704555/log-bundle.tar.gz
2026-03-12 13:52 UTC - Canary roll started for NimbusHealth cohort
2026-03-12 14:02 UTC - Support alerted by customer about mixed outputs
2026-03-12 14:10 UTC - Initial triage: spike in fallback rate and 502s correlated to canary cohort
2026-03-12 14:28 UTC - Engineering reproduced divergence in internal staging by enabling multipath prewarm delay
2026-03-12 15:05 UTC - Temporary mitigation applied (disable multipath prewarm for cohort)
Hypothesis: multipath prewarm optimization causes non-deterministic ordering of KV writes and TTL updates across parallel edge paths. Orchestrator expects eventual KV consistency within pin-grace window; when divergence exceeds grace window pin consensus fails and fallback routing is selected. Additional contributing factor: health-probe-induced eviction on one path produced a cache miss while other path retained warmed state. Reproduced with local harness by introducing 150-400ms write delay on one prewarm worker. Correlation with edge-proxy version v2.18 where multipath batching behavior changed.
2026-03-12 14:15 - Support (Aisha): Notified NimbusHealth and requested traffic sample and session tokens. Asked customer to reduce canary percentage while we investigate.
2026-03-12 14:40 - SRE (Diego): Reproduced in staging with simulated prewarm delay. Confirmed mismatch in KV TTL writes between parallel paths. Creating INT ticket to track orchestration fix.
2026-03-12 15:06 - Support (Aisha): Applied mitigation for NimbusHealth (disabled multipath prewarm for their cohort). Customer reports reduction in mixed-model responses within 3 minutes.
2026-03-13 09:22 - Eng (Priya Rao): Patch in runtime to add a short pin-consensus barrier and align prefix TTL writes. PR 4591 opened for review and backport to 2.18-hotfix branch.
2026-03-13 12:04 - Customer (NimbusHealth - Ops): Confirming improved behavior after mitigation. Asked for timeline for permanent fix and whether dedicated clusters require config change.
Mitigation: disabled multipath prewarm for affected cohort and forced single-path routing for NimbusHealth while fix is staged. Permanent fix: engineering implemented pin-consensus barrier and TTL-alignment in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4591; this prevents consensus mismatches during prewarm writes and handles transient probe-evictions gracefully. Hotfix deployed to edge-proxy v2.18.1 in us-east and rolled to affected dedicated clusters. Observed fallback rate returned to baseline within 8 minutes of deployment.
1) Backport hotfix to previous maintenance branches and schedule rollout to eu-west where multipath is enabled.
2) Add an automated runbook check to detect KV TTL divergence across edge paths and create an alerting rule.
3) Update canary configuration docs to recommend single-path prewarm for cohorts with strict pinning requirements.
4) INT-2107 tracks adding a consensus health-check during orchestrator snapshot commit.
Merge and backport PR 4591
Runnightly canary with multipath prewarm disabled by default until backport is in all regions

payload.description:
Issue summary: Oncall runbook execution for private deployments hit a blocker when our ephemeral Workload Identity Federation (WIF) -> AWS debug proxy fails to assume the target AWS role. Impact: SREs cannot access customer-dedicated resources (S3 + KMS) to complete a live debug, delaying incident resolution for a Dedicated onboarding automation failure. This ticket requests a timebound, minimally scoped debug-proxy IAM role in target prod account(s), plus a short runbook update describing correct audience and token parameters for WIF->AWS chaining.
1) From GKE pod with workload identity enabled, call STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity using the token from metadata server
2) Observe 400/InvalidIdentityToken from AWS STS in logs
3) When forcing a successful STS call using a manually minted token with audience=sts.amazonaws.com, the role assumption succeeds but KMS:Decrypt is denied for the assumed role
4) Attempt to decrypt an envelope key with aws kms decrypt -> AccessDenied
5) Reproduce occurs only for private-deploy worker accounts in eu-west and not in self-service staging accounts.
GCP metadata token request: GET http://metadata/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/identity?audience=https://iam.googleapis.com/&format=full -> 200
AWS STS response: {"Error":{"Code":"InvalidIdentityToken","Message":"STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed due to token audience mismatch"}}

Additional notes:
CloudTrail (AWS target account): No successful AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity events; KMS:Decrypt attempts logged for assumed-role/redwood-debug-proxy but denied due to condition aws:SourceAccount mismatch
Initial hypothesis: OIDC/WIF audience mismatch. Our token requester uses default GCP audience (iam.googleapis.com) which is not accepted by the WIF trust configured in target AWS accounts that expect audience 'sts.amazonaws.com'.
Secondary finding: When AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is forced to succeed (using corrected audience), KMS denies Decrypt because the KMS key policy conditions restrict decrypt to the dedicated account's principal or a specific source account; our ephemeral role comes from a different account (redwood-debug), causing aws:SourceAccount condition to fail.
Observed that staging/private account trust mappings diverge: staging has permissive mapping allowing multiple audiences; prod dedicated accounts were locked to only sts.amazonaws.com for security reasons.
Risk assessment: Creating a cross-account trust for debug-proxy increases blast radius if not timebound and constrained to specific principals and keys. Preferred approach is to change token minting in our debug proxy to request the sts-compatible audience and negotiate a short, auditable WIF session, plus add minimal key policy exceptions for the ephemeral role with expiration tags.
Repro playbook attached to this ticket and linked PR with token change: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8041
2026-03-11 14:40 - SRE PagerDuty: Confirmed we can reproduce with a local token minted via metadata server; STS fails with InvalidIdentityToken. Suspect audience mismatch as first pass.
2026-03-11 16:05 - Security (Priya Rao): Security note: any temporary role must be short-lived (max 8h), have strict key and S3 ARNs, and be tagged. We'll require an approval thread for accounts that contain customer data. Linking security review checklist.
2026-03-12 12:30 - Security (Priya Rao): Approved the scoped temporary role creation; requested Confluence update to runbook and to add automation that revokes role after expiration and emits audit event to #security-audit channel.
Temporary debug-proxy role provisioned in affected prod eu-west account with minimal KMS and S3 scope and strict trust policy to the redwood debug OIDC provider; role was timebound (8 hours) and tagged. Token minting in debug proxy updated to request audience sts.amazonaws.com (PR merged). Runbook updated with WIF->AWS checklist and automation to revoke ephemeral roles and post to #security-audit. Post-action: schedule a permissions hardening review to explore making the WIF audience mapping explicit in onboarding to avoid ad-hoc role creations.
Merge runbook changes into Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/16822/WIF+to+AWS+Debugging+Runbook
Create an automation job to verify WIF audience mapping on new dedicated accounts at onboarding (ticket INT-995300 assigned to infra-onboard team)
Post-mortem with customer success for ACME Corp onboarding delay; capture timeline and mitigations
Add unit test in platform repo to assert token audience when spawning debug proxy pods (covered by PR #8041)
Close this ticket after role expiry verification and runbook merge.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
A senior individual contributor (IC) is being promoted to an engineering manager. We need a staged access transition that preserves ongoing project access for 7 days while enabling manager-level privileges for a subset of systems immediately. The request includes reassignment of the existing work laptop to the manager role owner pool after an inspection and re-image window, and coordinated handoff of 2 service accounts used by the engineer's automation scripts.

Impact:
- If access is removed too early, backlog PRs and on-call rotations could be disrupted.
- If elevated privileges are granted without revoking certain IC-level service accounts, there is risk of permissions creep.

Background/context:
- Employee: Rahul Mehta (engineering)
- Current state: IC, has multiple service accounts (svc-ci-deploy, svc-data-sync) and a company MacBook Pro (asset tag RW-AP-9932).
- Promotion effective date: 2026-03-15. HR has requested access changes to start on that date.

Requested outcome:
1) Grant manager-level group membership in Okta and add to manager-specific Slack and LDAP groups on 2026-03-15 morning (09:00 PT).
2) Keep project-level repo write access and CI deploy rights for 7 calendar days (until 2026-03-22 23:59 PT) to finish in-flight work.
3) Transfer ownership of automation service accounts to the new manager (Rahul) after a credential rotation and audit; svc-* accounts must be rotated and access logged before final transfer.
4) Schedule laptop handback inspection and re-image to corporate baseline after 14 calendar days from promotion (window 2026-03-29 to 2026-04-02), then return asset to manager device pool.
5) Document the sequence in Confluence runbook and notify Payroll/Facilities of scheduled pickup date.

Constraints/policy questions (see 'policy_clarification' below):
- Current internal policy allows up to 72 hours of overlap for role changes; business requests for longer overlaps require approval. Requesting explicit exception for 7 days.

Attachments: asset manifest export, HR promotion email (redacted), list of service accounts and recent last-used timestamps.
1) Confirmed asset RW-AP-9932 serial matches inventory (AssetDB entry exists, last checked 2026-02-10).
2) Checked Okta group schema: manager-group grants access to /admin-console and payroll reporting service; these are compatible with requested elevation.
3) svc-ci-deploy and svc-data-sync are currently bound to Rahul's personal SSH key via vault token; tokens need rotation. Last rotation timestamps: svc-ci-deploy 2025-12-02, svc-data-sync 2026-01-08.
4) SCIM sync runs nightly at 02:30 UTC; immediate group changes must account for propagation lag across systems (estimate 5-15 minutes post-sync).
5) Need sign-off from Security for credential rotation window and from People Ops for overlap exception.

Preliminary recommendation: approve 7-day overlap conditional on recorded sign-off in ticket and on credential rotation schedule and logging enabled for both service accounts.
Question for Security/People Ops: our default role-change overlap is 72 hours. For manager transitions where continuity of in-flight work is business-critical, is there an established escalation/use of 'short-term overlap exception' (formal approval cadence)? If not, can we provision a documented one-off exception for Rahul with People Ops + Security co-approval? Please confirm required approvers and any audit trail requirements.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 13:05 - Security (via comment): We need to rotate credentials for svc-ci-deploy and svc-data-sync before any ownership transfer. Please provide last-used audits and a proposed rotation window where CI deploys will have a fallback user to avoid deploy disruption.
2026-03-11 09:40 - People Ops (Nora Simmons): Support the 7-day overlap pending manager confirmation. We require Rahul's acceptance of the manager role and acknowledgment of device return policy by 2026-03-14.
Pending: awaiting Security and People Ops approvals for 7-day overlap exception and execution of credential rotation. Post-rotation validation and asset re-image outcomes will be recorded here. Final closure steps: confirm SCIM group changes, post-rotation deploy smoke tests pass, asset re-image succeeded, Confluence runbook updated, and notify Billing/Facilities.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Service-side authorization tokens issued for delegated impersonation are expiring earlier than the console expects, causing on-call engineers to lose the ability to "impersonate" service accounts via the internal Runbook Console. Impact: several engineers reported immediate 403s during live incident response, preventing escalation and execution of debugging playbooks.

Impact:
- Multiple on-call engineers unable to escalate or run automated remediation via Runbook Console for ~3 hours during a production incident window.
- Manual intervention required to rotate tokens or escalate privileges in IAM console.

Environment:
- Production cluster: us-west primary identity-proxy cluster behind edge-auth.
- Affected clients: electron console (internal), runbook-executor service, service-proxy v1.12.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Sign in to internal Runbook Console with SSO (Okta) as on-call user.
2) Attempt to use "Act as service account" feature on a long-running runbook (session lifespan > 45m).
3) Observe immediate 403 from identity-proxy when starting the impersonated action.
4) Check identity-proxy logs and Okta token introspection for expiry timestamps.

Observed behavior:
- identity-proxy returns 403 with body: "delegation token expired or invalid".
- Okta introspection shows issued_at and expires_at with a 20m window for tokens minted by the proxy under a specific client_id.
- Console shows an "authorization expired" modal and suggests re-authentication which does not help for long-running tasks.

Expected behavior:
- Delegated impersonation tokens should match the Runbook Console expected session lifetime (configurable default: 2 hours) or the proxy should automatically refresh tokens for active runbooks.

Relevant logs / errors:
- identity-proxy logs (2026-03-12T09:22:13Z): "delegation token validation failed: expiry 2026-03-12T09:41:02Z < now"
- Okta introspection trace: client_id=runbook-proxy, token_ttl_seconds=1200 (20m)
- Runbook Console trace id: trace-runbook-0x8f12f

Additional notes:
- This appears to affect only tokens minted via the legacy proxy code path (service-proxy v1.12). Newer v1.18 proxy in staging uses a refresh flow and is not impacted.

Hypothesis 1: legacy proxy issues short-lived tokens (20m) due to default TTL override in v1.12.
Hypothesis 2: clock skew between identity-proxy host and Okta token issuer reduces effective validity window.
What we've checked:
- Confirmed proxy config on affected hosts uses token_ttl_seconds override set by a deploy in Jan 2026.
- Queried host NTP status: most hosts show offset < 3s, but one host (id-proxy-3) shows ~70s drift and had identical errors.
- Staging proxy v1.18 uses active refresh; not affected.

Next steps:
- Roll identity-proxy (v1.12) hosts through a config change to align TTL with console expectations.
- Patch host id-proxy-3 NTP and re-evaluate.
- Create short-term policy in Runbook Console to surface token TTL to on-call users.
On-call: start a new console session and select 'elevate now' to re-request a fresh delegation token. If runbook requires >20m runtime, split into smaller steps or use CLI impersonation flow that refreshes tokens. Engineering workaround: temporarily increase token_ttl_seconds in proxy config for affected hosts (requires deploy).
1) Patch identity-proxy v1.12 to default token_ttl_seconds=7200 and add a refresh endpoint for active runbooks (backport from v1.18). 2) Roll id-proxy hosts safely with canary (1 host) and monitor runbook-success-rate and 403 rates. 3) Fix NTP on id-proxy-3 and add NTP healthcheck alert. 4) Add automated test asserting delegated token lifetime >= console session lifetime.
Target: hotfix deploy to prod within 24 hours, full backport in weekly release.

Additional notes:
2026-03-14 07:42 - Tomás Reed (Security): Confirming no auth policy violation with extended TTL for delegation tokens; security approves temporary 2h TTL for on-call delegation until backport is merged.
payload.summary: Service proxy authz expiry prevents delegated console impersonation for on-call runbook

payload.description:
Issue summary: Several HelixCare tenants observed sustained routing 'hold' during a canary rollout window where their explicit model pin did not commit and traffic did not fall back to the configured secondary variant. The control plane reported the canary cohort as in 'snoozed' health-probe state and suppressed fallback behavior.

Impact: Customer-facing production requests were routed to a single degraded canary pod for ~18 minutes, causing increased latency (p50 -> ~1.2s to 2.8s) and some 5xx spike for streamed sessions. Estimated ~0.6% error uplift across the customer's traffic during the window.

Observed behavior: - Orchestrator logs show cohort marked as "probe_snooze" which sets a local flag suppressing automatic fallback. - Pin commit handshake never progressed from PREPARE -> COMMIT for affected tenants. - Edge continued to route to the canary cohort due to sticky route lease being extended by the snooze path. - Manual force-commit restored normal routing.

Initial timeline: 2026-03-12T09:04 UTC - HelixCare first reported increased tail-latency. 2026-03-12T09:08 UTC - #support Slack pinged and ticket opened. 2026-03-12T09:22 UTC - On-call engaged; preliminary mitigation applied (manually force-commit pin). 2026-03-12T09:42 UTC - Observed routing normalized, metrics returned to baseline.

1) On a dedicated cluster with an active canary (weight 5%) enable health-probe-snooze feature flag on orchestrator config for a short window.
2) Trigger a gradual rollout that requires pin commit for tenant affinity.
3) Simulate canary pod health flapping to cause orchestrator to mark cohort with probe_snooze.
4) Observe that tenants with explicit version pin remain routed to canary and fallback logic is suppressed until manual intervention.
[2026-03-12T09:18:03Z] orchestrator: cohort=tenant-helixcare-42 action=mark probe_snooze=true lease=extended request_id=01FZ9TQJ9XK
[2026-03-12T09:18:05Z] control-plane: pin-handshake tenant=helixcare state=PREPARE seq=1123 request_id=01FZ9TQJ9XK
[2026-03-12T09:25:21Z] orchestrator: fallback-suppressed cohort=tenant-helixcare-42 reason=probe_snooze request_id=01FZ9TQJ9XK
[2026-03-12T09:26:10Z] control-plane: pin-handshake tenant=helixcare state=PREPARE -> ABORT (timeout) seq=1123 request_id=01FZ9TQJ9XK
[2026-03-12T09:33:02Z] support: manual_action force_commit_pin tenant=helixcare operator=diego request_id=01FZ9TQJ9XK

Hypotheses considered: 1) Orchestrator's health-probe snooze path is setting a suppression flag that also prevents fallback triggers — this is expected for short probe windows, but a race occurs when pin handshake times out while snooze is active. 2) Edge sticky-lease extension logic did not honor pin-handshake ABORT and kept tenant affinity to canary. 3) A recent config roll (orchestrator PR #589) modified the probe_snooze TTL behavior and may not have backoff for handshake aborts.

Findings: - Confirmed a code path in orchestrator where probe_snooze sets fallback_enabled=false for the cohort. If pin-handshake remains in PREPARE and then times out, fallback_enabled is not re-enabled until the cohort exits snooze. That window can exceed handshake timeout causing tenants to be stranded. - Edge lease extension uses cohort.snooze_ttl to extend session affinity; combined this held traffic on canary. - Reproduced locally with a simulated TTL of 15s and handshake artificial delay -> routing hold reproduced consistently.

Metrics checked: - routing.affinity.held_count increased by tenant. - controlplane.handshake.timeouts spike at same time. - Serving runtime logs showed increased queue depth on canary pods.

Additional notes:
SRE (Marta Chen) (2026-03-12T09:30): Manual force-commit observed to restore routing. Suggest we collect orchestrator and edge lease debug traces for the 09:10-09:35 window.
Linking to Slack thread: #support-helixcare (https://slack.redwood/support-helixcare)
Product (Ravi Singh) (2026-03-12T11:05): Related PR 589 changed probe TTL behavior; need postmortem to consider reverting or adding handshake-coexist checks.
Mitigation applied: manual force-commit of pin for affected tenants and rolling restart of the canary-coordinator process to clear snooze flags.
Permanent fix plan: 1) Patch orchestrator to ensure probe_snooze does not permanently suppress fallback when a pin handshake aborts (PR to add explicit re-enable on ABORT). 2) Add safe-guard: edge should not extend sticky-lease beyond max_handshake_timeout when cohort is in a transient snooze state. 3) Add synthetic regression test exercising PREPARE -> TIMEOUT while probe_snooze active.
Rollout notes: Patch PR target branch release/2.8.1. Expect to ship hotfix within 72 hours pending review.
Follow-ups created: INT-9921 (orchestrator patch), INT-9922 (edge lease TTL change), and SUP-223345 (post-release validation with HelixCare). Customer notified 2026-03-12T12:00 with interim mitigation steps and will be scheduled for validation during their next maintenance window.
Metrics to monitor: handshake.timeout.rate, cohort.snooze_count, fallback.invocation_rate.
payload.summary: Tenant routing hold during canary health-probe snooze prevents fallback and leaves traffic stuck
