payload.description:
Issue reported by employee via #security-helpdesk: received a targeted phishing email, clicked a link, then observed an unexpected active session for their account from a foreign IP. This ticket documents triage steps, containment actions, and next steps for forensic analysis.
Potential credential exposure for one SSO-enabled account. No confirmed lateral movement; some API keys associated with the user were briefly active before being revoked. A subset of internal console sessions were observed originating from a foreign IP (unknown device).
1) Employee received email with subject 'Invoice overdue - Redwood billing' containing shortened link. 2) Employee clicked link and was presented with a fake SSO prompt that resembled our Okta page. 3) Employee reported to #security-helpdesk at 2026-03-10T09:18:00Z. 4) Security observed a new session from IP 185.66.124.241 at 2026-03-10T09:22:10Z for the same user.
auth.log lines of interest (redacted):
- 2026-03-10T09:22:10Z AUTH SUCCESS user=j.smith ip=185.66.124.241 ua='Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)' session_id=abc123
- 2026-03-10T09:23:03Z SSO TOKEN ISSUE user=j.smith client_id=redwood-console token_id=tok-45f
- 2026-03-10T09:24:12Z API KEY USE key=redact-*** resource=api.v1.generate model=gpt-redwood-light
SIEM event id: SEV-7621. Packet capture reference: pcap-20260310-09-22 (stored in secure evidence bucket).
2026-03-10T09:18Z - Employee reports phishing to #security-helpdesk.
2026-03-10T09:20Z - Security triage starts (Aisha).
2026-03-10T09:22Z - New session seen from 185.66.124.241.
2026-03-10T09:25Z - Password reset enforced and user session revoked (Liam).
2026-03-10T09:30Z - All active API tokens for the user revoked; suspicious tokens flagged.
2026-03-10T10:00Z - Initial containment complete; forensic snapshot taken.
2026-03-11 - SOC confirmed no additional accounts observed with same IP. Forensic team awaiting results from disk image analysis.
2026-03-13 - Ticket escalated to incident review; containment stable.
Preliminary findings: the phishing email used a legitimate-looking domain (redwood-billing[.]info) with a redirect through bit.ly. The SSO prompt was a credential-capture page that POSTed to a third-party domain. The session IP (185.66.124.241) geolocated to Eastern Europe and matches a set of previous malicious indicators (threat intel tag: THRT-2026-03-EU1).
No new service principals were created. The user did not approve any OAuth grants. API key usage observed came from the legitimate CLI token; timestamps show a brief window (09:24-09:27) before revocation. We found one suspicious header: X-Forwarded-For: 10.200.45.67 (internal range) which likely indicates proxy manipulation; need infra to confirm NAT logs.
Hypothesis: credentials were phished and used immediately from a foreign IP; attacker attempted to leverage active CLI token for quick API calls. No evidence of code exfiltration or model weights access.
- Immediate actions (2026-03-10): forced password reset for j.smith, revoked all active sessions, rotated affected API tokens, disabled legacy CLI tokens, blocked IP 185.66.124.241 at WAF and infra ACLs, created SIEM watchrule for THRT-2026-03-EU1.
- Communication: notified user, sent company-wide advisory (no compromise detected beyond single account), posted summary to #security-ops and #incidents.
- Evidence preservation: captured session logs, exported relevant pcap, saved mailbox headers and the phishing message to secure bucket.
- Longer-term: SSO provider support ticket opened to review token issuance logs and phishing-resistant MFA options (push-based or hardware for admin tier).
Containment achieved: compromised account credentials invalidated, suspicious tokens rotated, and attacking IPs blocked. Forensics in progress (disk and memory imaging for the affected host). Postmortem scheduled; action items include improving phishing-resistant MFA rollout and updating the security awareness training to include this phishing template. Ticket remains In Progress until forensic report and postmortem are complete.
payload.summary: Unusual session activity after employee reported suspicious phishing email (triage & containment)

Environment: Production identity for SCIM/Okta; seats should live in the main Redwood SSO org and be isolated via group membership. Deadline: 2026-03-18 (POC kickoff prep). Steps to fulfil (high level): 1) Confirm contract and NDA reference numbers with Sales (#SL-3319). 2) Create seat pool in SaaS licensing console named 'vendor-trial-engineer-2026-03' with expiration policy and seat cap 25. 3) Add provisioning SCIM mapping to create group 'vendor-trial-engineer' and configure Okta group push. 4) Configure billing tag/chargeback to cost center 3-DS-POC in licensing system. 5) Raise KMS access request to Security (this ticket + KMS request payload) and scope keys to read-only export. 6) Prepare PR for terraform licensing (infra repo) to make the pool auditable and revertible. 7) Notify vendor and Sales when complete.

Licensing console does not currently support TTL-based auto-deprovisioning for third-party vendors; workaround: create scheduled job (licensing-cleanup) to remove group membership and revoke SCIM tokens at expiry. Ticket created in infra ops backlog if approved.
Confirmed Okta group push is already enabled for similar pools; will reuse mapping pattern 'group:vendor-.*' in SCIM mapping. Need to ensure SCIM provisioning uses attribute 'costCenter' mapping for billing tagging.
KMS notes: Security prefers HSM-key for vendor telemetry exports. Requesting temporary key alias 'vendor-trial/ds-exports/2026-03' with strict IAM policy limiting Decrypt and GetPublicKey to service account used by vendor exports.
Billing: Finance has asked to attach forecast tag '3-DS-POC' and set an alert threshold of $1500 for run rate. Will include billing owner in PR.
Related infra PR created to add terraform resource redwood_license_pool.vendor_trial_engineer with metadata and lifecycle ignore for expiration automation placeholder. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821
Pending: Security approval for KMS HSM key and sign-off from Finance on billing tag and alert thresholds.
Workaround prepared: if HSM access denied, configure envelope encryption with vendor-provided key and restrict exports to S3 bucket with KMS encryption using a Redwood-managed key and lifecycle policy. This will be documented in the PR.
Next steps: 1) Security to confirm KMS policy (assigned to Priya). 2) Marcus to merge infra PR after Security review. 3) Run licensing-cleanup job on 2026-04-02 to revoke seats automatically (or earlier if POC ends). 4) Notify Sales and vendor once pool is live.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
There is an inconsistency in per-diem rate tables between the expense system (Expensely) and payroll rate lookup used by the finance ledger. Employees on expense reimbursement workflows for international travel are receiving different per-diem calculations depending on which legal entity the claim routes through.

Impact:
- ~120 outstanding expense claims are stuck in AP review with flagged rate mismatches, delaying reimbursements for employees (total estimated hold ~ $8.6k).
- Reimbursements that have processed in the last pay cycle show two different per-diem rates for identical trips for users assigned to different payroll entity mappings.
- Risk of incorrect tax reporting if reimbursements are posted to the wrong entity.

Environment:
- Production expense pipeline; multi-entity setup (US and EU).
- Systems involved: Expensely (expense submission), PayrollSync (entity mapping microservice), Finance Ledger (posting engine), AP dashboard.

Steps to reproduce / Observed behavior:
1) Employee in EU submits travel reimbursement in Expensely for a 3-day domestic trip in Germany. Expense uses per-diem profile "DE-EU-Std" (configured at employee profile).
2) Expense routes to entity mapping: employee legal entity correctly set to Redwood EU Subsidiary Ltd.
3) PayrollSync lookup returns per-diem rate key "DE-STD-v2" (value 90 EUR/day) for EU entity.
4) Finance Ledger receives payload and applies fallback lookup which incorrectly resolves to global per-diem key "DE-STD" (value 80 EUR/day) because entity prefix is missing from the request.
5) AP flags mismatch between submitted expense amount (calculated at 90 EUR/day) and ledger posting (80 EUR/day). Claim gets queued for manual review.

Logs / Evidence:
- Sample claim IDs: EXP-2026-1184, EXP-2026-1217, EXP-2026-1229 (attached exported CSV).
- Expensely submission JSON (redacted) shows per_diem_profile: "DE-EU-Std".
- PayrollSync service logs (2026-03-09 10:22:14 UTC) show entity->rate mapping returned "DE-STD-v2".
- Finance Ledger trace (trace-id: fl-20260309-9a3b) shows incoming request missing "legal_entity_prefix" field.

Investigation notes so far:
- Initial hypothesis: recent schema change in Finance Ledger v3.2.1 introduced a stricter key resolution that expects a prefixed rate key (e.g., "EU:DE-STD-v2"). If the prefix is absent, it falls back to an unprefixed lookup which resolves to an older baseline rate.
- Confirmed mismatch in nightly mapping job between PayrollSync and Finance Ledger rate tables; mapping export shows both prefixed and unprefixed keys present.
- Pull request references: finance-infra#412 includes the ledger change logs.
- No signs of data corruption in Expensely; submissions contain correct profile id. The gap appears in the translation layer between PayrollSync output and Ledger ingestion.

Temporary workaround / mitigation applied:
- AP configured a manual override rule to accept per-diem when submitted profile and ledger posting differ but amounts are within 15% until fix is deployed (applied 2026-03-11). This reduces manual escalations but still requires reconciliation for audit.
- Triggered a one-off mapping sync between PayrollSync and Finance Ledger to align prefixed keys (run 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC).

Proposed remediation plan:
1) Patch Finance Ledger ingestion to accept both prefixed and unprefixed keys while we standardize the mapping format (owner: Ledger eng, ETA: 2026-03-15).
2) Add input validation to PayrollSync output to ensure legal_entity_prefix present in payload (owner: Payroll infra, ETA: 2026-03-14).
3) Run a backfill to reconcile claims posted with the older baseline rate between 2026-02-01 and 2026-03-09 (owner: AP + Finance Ops, ETA: 2026-03-22).
4) Update runbook and Confluence doc to include the new canonical key format and create an automated daily mapping check with alerts (owner: Finance Automation, ETA: 2026-03-18).

Open questions / blockers:
- Is finance comfortable with an automated patch that accepts both key formats for 2 weeks prior to full migration? (Need sign-off from Head of Finance).
- Are there other downstream systems relying on the older unprefixed keys that we need to notify?

Requested actions / next steps for assignee:
- Confirm which engineering owner will deliver the ledger ingestion patch and add a link to the PR when available.
- Coordinate with AP to identify high-priority claims for immediate manual processing.
- Schedule a short meeting with Head of Finance to approve the temporary acceptance window.
payload.summary: Per-diem rate discrepancy across legal entities causing expense reimbursement delays

payload.description:
MedLex reports that after they enabled encrypted SAML assertions on their IdP, users can complete the SSO redirect flow but receive 403 Forbidden when calling the Redwood private API. A subset of users (all SSO-authenticated users) are unable to map roles and therefore cannot access the private deployment. No 5xx from the serving runtime; failures are authorization-level (403).
1) Configure private deployment with customer SAML IdP metadata (IdP sends EncryptedAssertions).
2) Perform SP-initiated SSO login using SAML with encrypted NameID/assertion enabled on IdP side.
3) Observe redirect back to identity-proxy -> session established -> attempt to call Redwood API -> 403 returned.
4) Check identity-proxy logs for decryption/signature verification messages and RBAC mapping traces.
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z identity-proxy[auth] WARN failed to decrypt EncryptedAssertion: keyName mismatch (expected key alias 'medlex-sp-enc', got none)
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z identity-proxy[auth] INFO SAML Response validated (signature ok) but Subject/NameID extraction failed
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z access-checker ERROR no principal email extracted -> role mapping failed -> returning 403
Initial hypothesis: signature/JWKS rotation issue. Logs show signature validation succeeded but decryption failed.
IdP is sending EncryptedAssertion elements with KeyInfo/KeyName that did not match the customer's uploaded decryption certificate alias in our onboarding bundle.
Private identity-proxy version 1.12.2 requires KeyInfo.KeyName to map to a keystore alias; if KeyName is missing or mismatched the assertion remains encrypted and NameID cannot be extracted.
Customer confirmed they recently enabled 'encrypt assertions' in Okta and uploaded a new public key but left KeyName blank (Okta default).
Reproduced on a staging private cluster by toggling encrypted assertions and removing KeyName from metadata.
2026-03-10 15:03 - Support (Ava): Hi MedLex — thanks for the report. Can you confirm whether your IdP is sending EncryptedAssertion elements and whether the SAML metadata includes a KeyName?
2026-03-10 15:20 - Customer (Sarah L., MedLex IdP Admin): We turned on Encrypt Assertions for PII. We uploaded a public encryption cert via the Okta UI but did not set a KeyName. We see the login redirect succeed but then 403s.
2026-03-10 16:40 - Support (Diego): We reproduced the failure in a staging private environment. identity-proxy was unable to map the decryption KeyInfo because KeyName was absent; NameID remained encrypted and role mapping failed.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Eng (Diego): Deployed hotfix in identity-proxy (PR #487) to fallback to matching KeyInfo.X509Certificate when KeyName is missing. Also added a clear debug log when encrypted assertion cannot be matched.
2026-03-11 12:20 - Customer (Sarah): After the hotfix was deployed to the private tenant and we re-ran a test, SSO users can access the API. Thank you.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Support (Ava): Closing ticket; created follow-up to update onboarding docs.
Hotfix deployed to identity-proxy to support certificate-only matching for encrypted assertions; customer re-tested and confirmed access restored.
Applied identity-proxy patch: fallback to X509Certificate match if KeyName missing (merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/487).
Rolled patch to MedLex private cluster (us-west) as a targeted config update during low-traffic window (2026-03-11 02:00 UTC).
Customer onboarded to recommended checklist: either include KeyName in IdP encryption KeyInfo or ensure decryption cert is present and matches X509Certificate in metadata.
Added diagnostic log lines to aid future debugging: logs now include which KeyInfo match path was attempted (KeyName vs X509Certificate).
Follow-up action: update Confluence onboarding page and add a new test case to private deploy e2e for EncryptedAssertion without KeyName. (Action owner: Diego Martinez, due 2026-03-19).
payload.summary: Encrypted SAML NameID decryption mismatch causes 403s for SSO users in private deployment

payload.description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 morning, a number of employees on the Floor-4 corporate Wi‑Fi SSID experienced short VPN disconnects and application failures. Symptoms were correlated with packets showing the client removing the default route after failing to locate the corporate proxy PAC (wpad/proxy.pac).

Impact:
- ~12 developers (floor-4) reported intermittent drops while working on remote repos and internal dashboards.
- Typical user impact: sudden 10–30s application failures, followed by VPN reconnect or manual re-auth.

Environment:
- SSID: Redwood-Corp-Employee-Floor4 (VLAN 204) via Aruba AP group floor-4-controller
- VPN client: OpenVPN-based corporate client v2.7.3 (configured for split-tunnel with proxy auto-detect requirement)
- PAC hosting: internal proxy service proxy.internal.redwood (behind nginx/reverse-proxy, served from us-west datacenter)
- DHCP: VLAN 204 uses DHCP relay to central server; DHCP option 252 expected for WPAD

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Join Redwood-Corp-Employee-Floor4 SSID.
2) Launch corporate VPN client (auto-connect policy enabled).
3) During PAC discovery, client attempts WPAD via DHCP option 252 then falls back to http://wpad.proxy.internal/wpad.dat.
4) When PAC lookup fails or times out, the VPN client removes/rewrites default route and triggers reconnect, resulting in application errors.

Observed behavior:
- Windows and macOS clients on that SSID fail PAC discovery ~15–40% of attempts.
- tcpdump from an impacted client shows DHCP OFFER without option 252 on the floor-4 subnet intermittently.
- Traceroutes from client to proxy.internal show intermittent ICMP timeout when routed via the AP controller's relay path.
- AP controller logs show SNAT to management IP for some relay requests.

Expected behavior:
- DHCP option 252 (WPAD) reliably delivered by DHCP relay; PAC file fetched; VPN keeps routes stable.

Logs and artifacts attached (referenced below):
- tcpdump snippets (client): wpad DHCP DISCOVER/OFFER without option 252 (see tcppcap-2026-03-10-floor4.log)
- AP controller relay logs: relay-logs-2026-03-10.txt
- VPN client debug logs from a consenting user: vpn-debug-ashley-2026-03-10.log
- nginx access/error logs for proxy.internal around event window

Temporary workaround used by impacted users:
- Manual set of proxy to http://proxy.internal:8080 in browser until reconnect stabilizes (not ideal).
- Moving to wired port on floor-4 eliminated the symptom (indicates wireless relay path-related).

Request:
- Investigate DHCP relay behavior on VLAN 204 and AP controller configuration for WPAD delivery.
- Confirm PAC server availability from the AP controller routing path and ensure no intermittent SNAT/ACL is blocking HTTP requests to wpad endpoint.

Additional notes:
2026-03-10 11:20 - NetOps (Elena Gomez): Uploaded relay logs: relay-logs-2026-03-10.txt. Observed that some relay requests are being proxied via the controller's mgmt IP when CPU is high.
2026-03-10 13:45 - SRE (Omar Khan): Confirmed that proxy.internal returns 200 for wpad.dat from the datacenter. No errors on upstream. But nginx shows occasional 499 (client closed) when requests traverse AP controller.
Ran tcpdump on three affected clients. Observed DHCP OFFER sequences missing option 252 when AP controller showed CPU load >85%.
AP controller has a legacy DHCP-relay implementation with a known issue for large concurrent relays; vendor doc mentions option truncation under high load.
Confirmed PAC server reachable from core network; timeouts correlate with controller path where nginx logs 499.
Hypothesis: when PAC lookup times out, VPN client aborts proxy auto-detect and rewrites routes which triggers the observed application failures.
Tested forcing direct DHCP relay via a controller policy for VLAN 204 which reduced repro rate dramatically (from ~30% to ~2%).
Next step: schedule full controller firmware upgrade and audit DHCP relay configuration on other office VLANs to prevent recurrence. Also consider VPN client safeguard to avoid route removal if PAC not immediately found.
Mitigation applied: Temporary controller policy pushed to force direct DHCP relay for VLAN 204 which reduced incident rate to acceptable levels. Canaries for controller firmware upgrade completed without regressions. Long-term action items: full firmware rollout scheduled 2026-03-15, vendor bug submitted referencing relay implementation behavior, and a follow-up ER (Engineering Request) to add a VPN client option to tolerate transient PAC lookup failures. Monitoring set for 72 hours post-rollout.
Complete full firmware rollout for AP controller across all floors (scheduled 2026-03-15).
Open engineering ticket to add VPN client resilience to PAC timeouts (ref: GH PR above).
Add synthetic PAC fetch monitor from AP controller path to alert on >5% failure in 15m window.
Document workaround in internal KB and notify floor-4 users of scheduled maintenance window.
payload.summary: Intermittent route flap when corporate PAC not discovered on specific office Wi‑Fi VLANs causing VPN default-route drop

payload.description:
Issue summary:
We need a secure, auditable mechanism that allows engineers and SREs to obtain short-lived AWS console/CLI access in prod by federating from a GCP workspace identity (workstation or CI) without standing long-lived IAM users or an always-on bastion.

Impact:
Currently on-call engineers sometimes need to perform quick debug steps in prod AWS accounts, but provisioning emergency access today requires manual ticketing and SSH bastion sessions that add latency and risk. This ticket aims to design and provision a federated path that:
- Enforces least-privilege via scoped AWS assume-role with session tags,
- Issues sessions that expire <= 1 hour,
- Records audit trail (CloudTrail + KMS-encrypted session metadata),
- Requires step-up auth (MFA or approval) for sensitive roles.

Goal / Acceptance criteria:
1) A documented, automated workflow for exchanging a GCP short-lived credential (Workload Identity Federation token or OIDC assertion) for an AWS STS assume-role with session duration <= 1h.
2) IAM policies are scoped to a minimal debug policy (read-only EC2/ASG/logs + ability to run ephemeral diagnostics) and use condition keys to restrict by request tag and source IP ranges.
3) All assume-role actions are visible in CloudTrail with session tags that map to the requestor identity and ticket/incident ID.
4) The workflow is covered by a runbook and unit test in infra repo; a canary request path is deployable to staging first.

Background / constraints:
- Redwood uses GCP for SSO/workstations. We want to avoid creating long-lived AWS users or maintaining a separate bastion fleet.
- Existing internal tickets reference similar needs but either rely on privileged bastions (INT-30421) or ad-hoc service account impersonation (INT-63124). We must be distinct: federated OIDC approach (GCP -> AWS) with strict condition rules.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Create an AWS IAM role per account: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNTID:role/ProdDebugFederatedRole.
2) Trust policy allows sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity from GCP Workload Identity Provider ARN.
3) Role session tags required: "redwood:identity", "redwood:ticket", "redwood:reason".
4) Inline policy scope: read-only for compute/logs, plus temporary ssm:StartSession and ssm:SendCommand limited to a diagnostics command set. No IAM management or KMS key policy changes allowed.
5) Enforce MFA/approval for any role that contains write privileges via an AWS IAM Condition or an approval lambda that injects a session tag after approval.
6) CloudTrail configured to write assume-role events to dedicated S3 bucket with lifecycle and to our observability pipeline for rapid search.

Implementation steps:
- Step 0: Pick pilot AWS account (prod-us-east-infra) and a staging account.
- Step 1: Create Workload Identity Provider in AWS (requires GCP project OIDC metadata).
- Step 2: Create IAM role with trust policy and restricted inline policy.
- Step 3: Add terraform module in infra repo and open PR for review.
- Step 4: Add a small helper CLI script (or extend existing 'rwd-access' tool) that exchanges GCP token for AWS credentials and emits session tags, fails if session length > 1h.
- Step 5: Hook assume-role actions to a lightweight approval flow for write-level roles (Slack-based approval via /approve command calling an API gateway which writes a tag).
- Step 6: Test in staging with canary user and audit logs.
- Step 7: Roll out to prod and deprecate older bastion procedures in runbook.

Rolling back / mitigation:
- If federated paths cause failures, revert by removing the federation provider trust or disabling role trust in AWS (fast). Keep the existing manual ticket-bastion as fallback.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Over-broad policies. Mitigation: Start with explicit allow-list for API actions and perform policy simulator checks and a 48h policy review.
- Risk: Audit gaps. Mitigation: Add automated CloudWatch Events -> SNS -> observability to ensure assume-role events surface in alerting.
- Risk: Identity spoofing. Mitigation: Rely on GCP Workload Identity with audience checks and signature verification.

Required approvals / stakeholders:
- SRE (oncall): @Evelyn Park (assignee)
- Security: @Marco Alvarez (please review policies and audit plan)
- Platform infra: @Priya Nair (terraform review)

Notes on policy snippet (example to be checked into PR):
-----
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "ec2:DescribeInstances",
        "ec2:GetConsoleOutput",
        "logs:GetLogEvents",
        "ssm:StartSession",
        "ssm:SendCommand"
      ],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": {
          "aws:RequestedRegion": "us-east-1"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
-----
(Policy above is a minimal example — will be tightened per resource ARNs.)
Initial attempt to configure the AWS OIDC provider in staging failed with 'Invalid audience' errors when exchanging a GCP signed assertion. Hypothesis: the GCP workload identity provider in our project emits an audience that contains the full service account email instead of the expected client ID. Action: request the GCP project owner to add 'audience' mapping or update the workload identity pool provider configuration. Also verifying that the trust relationship in AWS uses the exact issuer URL from GCP and that the thumbprint matches. Logged CloudTrail assume-role failures in staging account S3 bucket: s3://redwood-staging-cloudtrail/logs/2026/03/14/assume-role-errors.json
(Work in progress) Resolved the audience mismatch by updating the workload identity pool attribute mapping and re-registering the provider. Terraform PR #4128 includes the updated provider resource and role module. Post-merge tasks: run terraform apply in staging, run canary assume-role, verify CloudTrail entries and session tags, then schedule production rollout during low traffic window. Final closure after 72-hour policy review and security sign-off.
1) Marco to finalize KMS key policy and sign-off on audit flow (due 2026-03-16). 2) Priya to open infra PR and include terratest for assume-role flow (PR #4128). 3) Evelyn to rerun staging canary and paste CloudTrail sample event into this ticket. 4) After staging success, schedule prod apply and update runbook; deprecate legacy bastion steps.
- Terraform module merged and applied in staging.
- Successful assume-role in staging with correct session tags and CloudTrail visibility.
- Security sign-off documented in ticket comments.
- Runbook updated and a short internal training (15m) run for oncall engineers.

Additional notes:
Do not grant iam:PassRole to anyone in the pilot role. All role session tags must include 'redwood:ticket' referencing this issue key. Ensure terraform state access is limited to infra owners.

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BrightMap Analytics, dedicated tenant) reported seeing mixed model outputs and a sudden spike in fallback routing to the canary variant during a slow, weighted rollout. Tenant had a model version pinned for a subset of sessions; several of those sessions received responses from the new canary variant for short windows (~10-30s) before affinity restored. Impact: inconsistent inference outputs, user-visible quality regressions for affected sessions, and a brief increase in token costs due to replayed requests.

Impact:
- ~120 sessions observed mixed routing over a 24-minute window (2026-03-13 02:08–02:32 UTC).
- Customer reports downstream quality alerts and a rollback request.
- No full outage; requests completed with increased latencies and occasional 5xx spikes correlated with the event.

Environment:
- Redwood prod (us-east-1) - dedicated capacity pool: dp-09b4
- Edge tier: edge-v3-proxy cluster (ASG edge-us-east-1-3)
- Canary rollout: weighted rollout 5% -> 25% over 2 hours; affected sessions were meant to remain pinned to stable variant via session affinity (lease TTL 60s).
- Customer pinned version: rw-infer-v2-medium@2026-03-10, canary variant: rw-infer-v2-medium@2026-03-13-canary

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Begin weighted rollout and verify canary weight increasing (5% at 01:50 UTC).
2) Simulate long-running sessions that rely on affinity (session token kept alive).
3) Introduce a synthetic edge-proxy restart/rolling restart (we observed an internal edge-restart job at 02:06 UTC).
4) Within ~2 minutes after the restart, sessions intermittently lost affinity and routed to canary for a single request before re-binding to original pinned variant.

Logs / Observations:
- edge-proxy logs (edge-us-east-1-3) show lease_renewal_rpc latency spikes from ~12ms baseline to 1.2s at 2026-03-13 02:07:34 UTC.
- Router metric `session_affinity_miss` spiked from 0.3/min to 18/min during the window.
- Serving-runtime returned canary variant for requests that carried the original session token; token verification succeeded but affinity lookup returned 404 for a short period.
- No auth/SSO rotation events for the tenant in the timeframe.

Hypothesis:
Primary: Edge-proxy lease renewal requests timed out due to transient RPC backpressure during the rolling restart, causing the affinity store to drop or fail to return binding for a narrow window. Router fallback policy allowed requests without confirmed binding to be routed via the canary path (safe default), resulting in mixed outputs.
Secondary: A TTL/lease-reconciliation race between the canary-controller's cohort rebalancer and the edge's lease-renewal path surfaced because of accelerated canary weight change combined with pod restarts.

Temporary mitigation / Workaround applied:
- Support manually pinned the tenant at the router layer to force stable variant for 30 minutes and initiated a controlled drain of edge-proxy hosts that exhibited high lease latency.
- Canary rollout paused (canary weight set to 0%) and an emergency config was applied to increase affinity lease TTL to 180s for all dedicated tenants.
- Customer notified and asked to hold heavy evaluation traffic for 1 hour.

Next steps / Action items:
1) SRE: Investigate edge-proxy restart job logs and autoscaler activity around 02:05–02:10 UTC (Omar).
2) Runtime: Add additional logging around affinity-store RPC failures to capture call path and error codes (Maya + Helena).
3) Reconciler: Review lease-reconciliation logic for races when pod restarts coincide with weight change events; propose a backoff or hold window (PR referenced).
4) Product: Consider defaulting to rebind-to-stable policy for pinned sessions during rollout windows for dedicated tenants.
5) Follow-up: Run a controlled repro in staging simulating edge rolling restarts + gradual rollout to validate fixes.

Owner: Omar Patel (SRE)
Priority: P1 / Sev1

Attachments / Links:
- Grafana: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/affinity/lease-renewal?orgId=1&from=2026-03-13T02:00:00Z&to=2026-03-13T02:40:00Z
- Edge logs (scrubbed): s3://redwood-support-logs/SUP-402321/edge-proxy-us-east-1-3-02-07.gz
- Reconciler PR for investigation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/1427

Additional notes:
Mitigations: paused canary, increased affinity TTL, forced tenant pin at router. Next steps include autoscaler cooldown tuning and reconciler race fix. Postmortem scheduled and patch PR opened.
payload.summary: Affinity lease renewal lag triggers mixed routing and unintended fallback during gradual canary rollout

payload.description:
Issue summary: BrightChat reported a sudden increase in 5xx responses (502/503) on their chat streaming route (/v1/chat/stream) starting ~2026-03-10 18:30 UTC. Impact: ~18% error rate across their tenant for 20 minutes, user-facing disconnects, and message duplication from client retries. Environment: BrightChat on Dedicated pool in us-east-1. Behavior: API gateway returned rapid 502/503 spikes; upstream runtime processes entered a blocked state with high thread counts and elevated syscall wait times. Support notes: customer observed multiple mobile clients rapidly reconnecting after a mobile SDK update.
1) Simulate ~2000 short-lived websocket reconnects to /v1/chat/stream over ~2 minutes from the same tenant. 2) Monitor API gateway 5xx rate and upstream runtime thread blocking and accept_queue length. 3) Observe keepalive pool exhaustion and increased fd usage on ephemeral proxies. Expected: graceful handling and bounded 5xx; Observed: accept_queue growth, rapid apigw 502/503s, runtime watchdog kills and restart loops.
- apigw logs (2026-03-10T18:30:12Z): upstream response 502
- runtime stderr (2026-03-10T18:30:22Z): threadpool busy=256/256 blocked_on=socket_read

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete their compliance ingest verification without precise field names, types, and examples.
- Onboarding delay of 2+ weeks if they must reverse-engineer fields from raw exports.

Request details / Desired deliverables:
1) A field-level catalog (CSV or table) listing field name, type (string/ts/int/boolean), sample value, retention semantics (e.g., PII, redaction guidance), and TTL/partitioning hints.
2) Two short ingestion examples:
   - Splunk HEC mapping / props/transforms example for timestamp, tenant_id, event_type, and request_id normalization.
   - Snowflake copy into / staged file parsing SQL with a recommended target table DDL for efficient querying (partition by event_date, tenant_id).

- They also asked whether event payloads contain prompt text or model output under any default logging regime.

Issue summary: ClarifyAI (dedicated tenant) experienced sustained p99 and 429s for short streaming requests during midday window in eu-west. Root observable: a set of many small fanout streams (chatlets) with aggressive prefetch behavior caused a cascade of KV cache prefetch leases across multiple GPUs in the reserved pool, producing localized GPU thinness and slot fragmentation.

Impact: Customer observed elevated p50/p99 and intermittent 429s on their dedicated routes (~10-15% of requests in the 12:00-13:45 UTC window). Throughput to other tenants in the same reserved pool degraded modestly (3-7% p50 increase), and autoscaler failed to rapidly provision additional capacity due to a combination of cooldowns and fragmented slot availability.

Timeline (UTC):
- 11:57: first small fanout increase from ClarifyAI (many short streams, high keepalive)
- 12:05: kv-cache prefetch lease growth observed on pool-mgr logs
- 12:13: autoscaler sample shows elevated slot utilization but below scale-threshold due to fragmented free slots
- 12:22: support alert triggered by customer; 429s and p99 spikes visible in console
- 12:40: mitigation applied (temporary burst limit change and pinning)
- 13:05: partial recovery, p99 lowered but still above baseline

Observed metrics & logs: (excerpt)
[pool-mgr] 2026-03-13T12:06:11Z pool=eu-west-dedicated-5 lease_prefetch_count=124 slot_free=18 total_slots=256
[autoscaler] 2026-03-13T12:09:03Z pool=eu-west-dedicated-5 util=68.3% fragments=32 cooldown_remaining=420s decision=NO_SCALE
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-13T12:15:45Z route=/clarifyai/stream code=429 reason=slot_unavailable latency_p99=1120ms

Steps to reproduce (probabilistic):
1) Use a client that opens many short-lived streaming sessions (fanout 8-20 per conversation) with long keepalives and prefetch enabled.
2) Set model to gpt-medium-4o-q4 and run burst traffic at ~200rps for 10-30 minutes targeted at the dedicated pool.
3) Observe kv-cache lease growth across GPUs and increasing slot fragmentation; autoscaler increments do not trigger immediately because global util remains below the strict scaling threshold despite local fragmentation.

Initial hypothesis: aggressive prefetch logic combined with many short streams is allocating prefetch leases across GPUs leading to slot fragmentation. The autoscaler thresholds use aggregated utilization signals and a cooldown that prevents rapid response to fragmented availability. Noisy-neighbor behavior is not a single large tenant hogging GPU memory but many micro-streams scattering prefetch state and holding slots.

Immediate mitigation applied: increased ClarifyAI's allowed burst quota (to reduce failed requests while we investigate), temporarily pinned a small shard for their highest-throughput routes to limit pool-wide scatter, and raised autoscaler max-provision for pool eu-west-dedicated-5 from 4->6 to give headroom. These changes reduced 429 rate and lowered p99 by ~30%.

Recommended long-term fixes: tune prefetch lease lifetime and per-tenant prefetch limits, improve autoscaler signal to include fragmentation heuristics (free_contiguous_slots), and add a guard that converts many short streams into multiplexed connections to avoid slot-hogging.

References: Slack #support-eu thread https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SUPPORT/p1643_prefetch, infra PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8421 (autoscaler fragmentation metric), confluence runbook linked above.
Engineers pulled heap and lease metrics from pool-mgr, scheduler, and serving-runtime. Confirmed pattern: kv-cache prefetch lease_count correlates strongly (r=0.82) with slot fragmentation metric. Autoscaler logs show NO_SCALE decisions during the peak because global util stayed under threshold while free_contiguous_slots count fell below allocation limits. Checked GPU memory and drivers: no OOMs or kernel faults. No driver restarts in window. Hypothesis refined: prefetch leases are being spread across devices (fanout), preventing the allocator from finding contiguous slots to place new batches. Longer keepalives amplify the effect.

Action items from investigation:
- Collect sample of per-tenant lease distribution over next 48h (assigned to infra-monitoring).
- Prototype fragmentation-aware autoscaler rule (small PR drafted: see related_github_prs).
- Recommend customer apply client-side limiter (reduce fanout or enable multiplexing) as stopgap.

Notes: We saw similar mechanics in SUP-314159 but that incident was triggered by a different traffic mix; this ticket's distinguishing factor is many small concurrent streams with prefetch enabled and long keepalive, rather than one large noisy tenant.

Additional notes:
ClarifyAI Ops (2026-03-13T12:30Z): Confirmed they rolled out a recent client change enabling eager prefetch in 2.1.0 of their SDK. They can toggle prefetch off for testing.
Mitigations implemented: shard pinning + increased pool cap + customer burst uplift. Partial recovery achieved; p99 down ~30% from peak and 429s reduced to baseline-ish for most routes. Root cause: prefetch-cascade + slot fragmentation + autoscaler cooldown/aggregation semantics. Next steps: validate fragmentation-aware autoscaler in staging (infra), finalize client guidance to limit prefetch concurrency (support/solutions), and schedule a follow-up postmortem with ClarifyAI and infra team in 1 week. Owner for permanent fix: Marco Ruiz (SRE) and Nadia Patel (Infra).
payload.summary: Small-fanout prefetch cascade leading to localized GPU thinning in eu-west reserved pool

Issue summary:
We need an automated mechanism to propagate role/group membership changes from the central directory to multiple Slack workspaces and simultaneously bootstrap a Confluence space with a small set of templated pages and initial permissions.

Impact:
Currently, when we update pod reviewer groups or oncall role mappings, engineers must manually update membership across three Slack workspaces and then request a Confluence space creation with manual permission granting. This causes delays in onboarding, inconsistent permissions, and occasional missing runbook pages during incident responses.

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement an automation that listens for updates to the central group registry (LDAP/SCIM source) and propagates role changes to Slack workspaces: #runtime-ops, #model-evals, and #platform-pods.
- Create a Confluence space provisioning task that, when a new pod/team is onboarded, will create a space from a seed template containing: Incident Runbook, Oncall Roster, Playbooks, and Ownership page.
- Ensure the Confluence space creation sets space-level permissions aligned to the propagated Slack role (e.g., "pod-reviewers" => Confluence group pod-reviewers with edit access).
- Provide an audit log (linkable) showing which automation run applied which changes and an ability to rollback the latest change.
- Expose a one-click trigger in the internal admin console to run the provisioning for a team with a dry-run option.

This request comes from recent cross-pod incidents where runbooks were incomplete and channel membership lagged behind directory changes. We have an initial IAM mapping for groups, but no reliable propagation mechanism across multiple Slack workspaces or a templated Confluence scaffold. Existing manual process is error-prone and scales poorly as pods grow.

Proposed constraints and non-goals:
- We are not changing SCIM/LDAP itself; this should consume changes from the existing source of truth.
- This task should not attempt full org-wide Slack consolidation; only propagate mapped groups to listed workspaces.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Time-to-onboard new pod reduced from ~2 business days to <30 minutes for initial channel/space creation and role mapping (dry-run measured).
- Zero manual membership edits required for role changes in 90% of cases over a 30-day pilot.
- Confluence seed page completeness verification script reports 100% presence of required runbook pages after provisioning.

payload.description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when resuming a long streaming SSE response after the mobile client is backgrounded and then restored, the last sentence of the assistant reply is sometimes missing even though server logs show the stream continued.

Observed behavior: After a reconnect and resume attempt the stream emits duplicated earlier tokens, the client deduplicator drops the overlapping suffix and the stream terminator (end marker) is not observed by the client, which results in UI showing an incomplete final sentence.

Expected behavior: Resume flow should deliver the last contiguous sequence of tokens including any closing punctuation or explicit end marker so the client receives a complete sentence and the stream terminates cleanly.

Customer impact: NimbusDocs notes frequent user-facing truncation on their mobile app during short background/foreground cycles. This affects around ~8% of streaming sessions for them according to their metrics and is blocking their launch of an in-app summarization feature.
Partial outputs lead to bad UX and increased retries. Customer reports ~8% failure rate on mobile app background/resume. Dedicated customer with reserved capacity — high priority for launch timeline.
1) Start a streaming SSE generation (chat) using redwood/gptx-3.2b on prod us-east with client_mobile SDK v1.6.2.
2) Let the assistant generate a multi-sentence paragraph (~120-200 tokens).
3) Put the mobile app into background for ~5-10s to force socket close / OS suspend.
4) Restore app to foreground and allow SDK to perform resume handshake with the server.
5) Observe client UI: sometimes final sentence(s) are missing even though server logs show tokens emitted after resume.
Relevant server traces: resume request id=tr_9f2e3bd, client_resume_offset=115, server_resume_applied_offset=37, resume_state_hash mismatch logged. Worker migration events around 2026-03-10T14:03:22Z. Attached excerpts from request traces and cloudlogs query: log://prod/serving-runtime/trace/tr_9f2e3bd and dashboard link https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/resume-traces?var-trace=tr_9f2e3bd
Initial investigation (SRE): reproduced with mobile SDK v1.6.2 on a test app. When the client resumes, it sends an offset which the resume handler accepts but an older worker instance (recently restarted / migrated) replies with a truncated prefix window due to stale KV cache. Observed behavior: the server emitted a small duplicate prefix and then emitted the remaining tokens, but the resume response did not always include the canonical stream terminator event (end-of-response marker) in the same sequence number after a duplicate overlap. Client-side deduplication removed the duplicate range and, due to an ordering edge, dropped the subsequent terminator event.

Hypothesis: race between resume accept and worker-local KV cache priming during worker migration / autoscaler scale-in leads to a transient resume-offset snapback where server reports an earlier applied offset. Client deduplicator and event coalescing presumed monotonic sequence numbers; the overlap triggers a path that discards the final end marker.

Reproduction notes: added interleaved keepalives and introduced a 200ms artificial delay on resume path; reproduces ~90% locally. Observed related metrics: increased resume_retries and resume_overlap_count in prod for NimbusDocs in the last 48h. Cross-reference channel: #support-nimbusdocs thread (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C06SUPPORT/pt2g3r8).

Additional notes:
2026-03-11 Customer (NimbusDocs): Provided prod timestamps and agrees to test a canary rollout. They are on a Dedicated contract and can accept a short maintenance window.
Workaround: Ask customer to enable a short client-side post-resume jitter that waits for 150ms before applying deduplication window; this temporarily reduces observed omissions.
Fix rolled: Serving team implemented a guard in the resume handler to canonicalize applied_offset based on authoritative KV checkpoint and to always emit a synthetic end marker when overlap is detected. Patch deployed to canary on 2026-03-12 and promoted to full NimbusDocs pool after 2 hours of clean metrics.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5482. Follow-up action: add a probe test for resume ordering under worker restart and add metric resume_overlap_count alert (SLO playbook updated).
1) Add automated e2e test for resume ordering and worker restart to CI (assigned to eng/core).
2) Instrumentation: emit resume_state_hash and applied_offset to traces for 100% of resume attempts for 48h after rollout.
3) Update mobile SDK docs to recommend a small post-resume jitter until fix is fully rolled out to all customers.
4) Postmortem draft in Confluence and notify NimbusDocs once PM approves schedule for long-term mitigation.

Issue summary: At ~08:20 PST on 2026-03-10 a subset of employees across the SF office reported inability to join CORPORATE-SSID (WPA2-Enterprise / 802.1X). Affected clients fell back to GUEST-SSID or had no network. Concurrently, several users reported their VPN (CompanyVPN / OpenConnect) failed to re-establish after being kicked off by the Wi-Fi drop. Impact: ~120 users intermittently affected (most on macOS 13/14 and some Android 13 devices). Core services (git, Slack, internal apps) were inaccessible for those users. Environment: production corporate Wi-Fi using Mist APs, RADIUS cluster (FreeRADIUS) behind HA proxy, Okta as identity provider for EAP-PEAP/MSCHAPv2, OpenConnect VPN appliances for remote access. Timeline: 08:00 — automated cert rotation for RADIUS completed; 08:18 — first auth failures; 08:22 — ticket opened; 08:45 — temporary mitigation applied; ongoing. Observed behaviour: RADIUS rejects EAP exchanges with TLS handshake failures referencing certificate trust or SAN mismatch. VPN clients do not prompt for re-auth and remain in CONNECTING state or immediately drop. Expected behaviour: seamless re-auth to WLAN and VPN after cert rotation.
08:25 - Confirmed rotation job ran at 08:00; new RADIUS leaf cert issued by internal CA with expiry 2027-03-09.
08:30 - Observed mismatch between RADIUS server cert SANs and the hostnames used by HAProxy health checks; some APs are configured to validate a different FQDN.
08:35 - NTP skew detected (~6 minutes) on radius2 (10.10.2.24) causing client TLS validation failures on devices strict about time sync.
08:40 - Okta SSO console shows no policy changes; certificate chain presented to clients missing intermediate CA on one RADIUS node (radius2).
08:42 - Cross-checked cert bundles: radius1 and radius3 have full chain; radius2 certificate bundle was missing intermediate due to packaging script bug in rotation job.
Hypothesis: Incomplete cert chain on radius2 + NTP skew caused a subset of APs (that prefer radius2 via session stickiness) to return validate-failed responses, leading clients to drop and VPN clients to fail reconnect without prompting.
08:45 - Temporarily rolled back HAProxy pool to exclude radius2; auth success rate on APs increased to normal within 90s.
09:05 - Reissued complete cert bundle for radius2 with intermediate included and corrected NTP (systemd-timesyncd restarted and compared to ntp.redwood.net).
09:15 - Reintroduced radius2 to HAProxy with weight reduced; monitored for 30 minutes — no TLS errors observed in logs post-fix.
Workaround for users: Connect to wired network where available or manually select GUEST-SSID then reconnect to CORPORATE-SSID after 2-3 minutes; VPN users can kill and restart OpenConnect to force credential prompt if needed.
Partial resolution applied 2026-03-10: radius2 cert bundle reissued with correct intermediate chain and NTP resynchronized. HAProxy restore completed at 09:15 PST and auth success rate returned to baseline. Follow-up remediation planned: audit and harden cert rotation job to validate bundle completeness, add pre-flight checks for NTP across radius nodes, and add health-check to HAProxy to fail a backend when cert chain validation fails. Owners: Infra Sec (cert rotation) and Network SRE. Postmortem scheduled and linked (see related_confluence_pages).
payload.summary: 802.1X authentication failing on CORPORATE-SSID after RADIUS certificate rotation; VPN connections not re-establishing

During a scheduled PKCS#11 HSM key rotation the cosign signer on CI produced valid signatures but subsequent verification by the promotion job failed with epoch/time-window errors, preventing any container images from being promoted to the release registry.
Issue summary:
- What happened: Automated container promotion jobs started failing verification immediately after the HSM key rollover window. The cosign signing step reports success, push to registry succeeds, but the promotion verification step (post-push policy) rejects the image.
- Impact: Blocked promotion pipeline for all releases targeting the us-east release cohort. Approximately 12 release candidates queued; customers on internal canary cannot be promoted. No pod rollouts happened.
- First observed: 2026-03-13 02:17 UTC when nightly canary promotion aborted.
- Temporary scope: prod us-east artifact-registry and the cosign signer instances used by CI runners.

1) Trigger standard build pipeline that signs with cosign (PKCS#11-backed key).
2) After HSM rotation window, run the promotion job that invokes 'cosign verify' against the registry entry.
3) Observe verification failure with epoch/skew related message.

Observed error: 'cosign: signature verification failed: verification time 1678793820 not within validity window [1678797600, 1678801200]' (timestamps are examples).

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Northshore Analytics (Private deployment, us-east) reports production latency spikes and periodic request stalls that correlate with failed model shard fetches and control-plane auth timeouts. Root cause appears to be an SRV-record based conditional forwarder on the customer's branch DNS appliances that forwards _redwood-control._tcp lookups to an internal forwarder which then re-delegates back to the VPCE resolver, creating a recursion/loop and UDP truncation to TCP. TCP53 is blocked by a corporate opaque proxy on the branch path which causes a long fallback timeout and repeated TLS client hello retransmits leading to TLS handshake retries and grpc stream retries on serving nodes.

Impact:
- Multiple production requests experience 5-30s stalls before failing or retrying.
- Token refresh and control-plane auth exchanges occasionally time out, resulting in short-lived degradations and falling back to stale cached credentials.
- Serving node KV/prefix cache misses spike during the periods.

Environment:
- Customer deployment: Redwood Private (VPCE + TGW peering to branch offices)
- Affected network: Branch office forwarders behind SD-WAN -> corporate proxy -> TGW -> VPC Endpoint (VPCE) resolver
- Observed on: us-east serving and control plane endpoints

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) At branch office, run: dig +short SRV _redwood-control._tcp.example-delegation.local @branch-forwarder
2) Branch forwarder returns delegation to internal resolver A; internal resolver attempts to forward to VPCE resolver which returns large response (DNSSEC/EDNS0 present) causing UDP truncation
3) Branch forwarder downgrades to TCP but corporate opaque proxy blocks TCP53, resulting in a 20-30s timeout before fallback completes or fails
4) During this window, control-plane handshake (mTLS) opens but client reattempts TLS ClientHello several times; gRPC streams reset and serving node reports TLS handshake retries in logs

Logs & diagnostics collected:
- tcpdump from a serving node during incident: repeated SYN->SYN-ACK timings align with 3x TLS ClientHello retransmits
- customer-provided branch-forwarder logs show repeated delegations for _redwood-control._tcp to internal resolver A
- VPCE resolver metrics: elevated NXDOMAIN/TC rate for the customer's resolver namespace between 13:12-13:34 UTC
- Serving node metrics: KV cache miss rate +1.8x and grpc retry rate +3x in same window

Hypothesis so far:
- The SRV conditional forwarder chain creates a DNS resolution loop that triggers UDP truncation to TCP. Blocked TCP53 along the branch path causes extended lookup latency which cascades into TLS handshake timeouts and gRPC retries. The opaque corporate proxy that blocks TCP53 is the gating factor.

Immediate customer workaround suggested:
- Update branch DNS forwarder to short-circuit lookups for _redwood-control._tcp to return the VPCE resolver IP directly (avoid delegation) OR configure the forwarder to allow TCP53 to VPCE resolver.
- Temporarily increase local DNS cache TTL for the delegated name to reduce frequency of recursion while remediation is scheduled.

Notes for engineering:
- Ask infra to provide VPCE resolver full response size and headers for the queried SRV to validate EDNS0/DNSSEC behavior.
- Evaluate whether returning smaller response or EDNS0 fallback is feasible for the control-plane SRV to avoid UDP truncation in customer's pathological chains.

Follow-ups/next steps:
- Customer to confirm branch firewall/proxy policy on TCP53 and provide a packet capture from the branch egress appliance.
- Support to request VPCE resolver logs for the specific query window and SRV name.
- If customer cannot permit TCP53, propose configuration template for short-circuit A-record override in branch forwarders for control-plane endpoints.

Additional notes:
2026-03-15 09:12 - SRE (internal): INT-4128: VPCE logs attached, response for SRV contains DNSSEC and additional TXT entries, response size 2080 bytes, TC set. Confirmed truncation at UDP and TC flag set.
payload.summary: Branch DNS forwarder SRV record recursion creates intermittent TLS handshake retries to control plane

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Between 18:05-19:40 UTC on 2026-03-10 we observed a sustained spike in 5xx responses for a subset of ClearMind AI traffic on prod/us-east-1. Symptoms: rapid rise in API gateway 502/503/504 rates, long accept-queue length, followed by upstream serving-runtime processes entering a watchdog restart loop and GPU-related worker evictions.

Impact:
- Customer ClearMind AI (dedicated) reported ~35% error rate on chat and embedding routes; multiple streaming sessions terminated.
- Platform-wide latency tail increased for the us-east-1 partition; some other tenants experienced transient elevated latency but not sustained 5xx.

Initial hypothesis:
Autoscaler slow warm-up + accept-queue backlog caused amplification: API gateway queued requests, proxy replay/hedged retries increased fanout to runtimes that were still cold. Prefetch/kv-cache contention + heavy embedding uploads caused runtimes to hit a watchdog threshold (long GPU stalls) and restart, causing upstream 5xx amplification.

Context / why this is unusual:
We have seen 5xx waves before, but this event correlates strongly with a rapid ephemeral scale-up path where warm workers were delayed by quota throttling and NVMe checkpoint I/O spikes. The serving-runtime responded by evicting tasks (watchdog) rather than graceful shedding, producing runtime crashloop and persistent 502/503 errors at the gateway.

Full incident notes and timeline are below.

From prod-us-east-1: Run simultaneous workload: continuous embedding upload (5000 small vectors/min) + 250 concurrent short chat streaming sessions to chat-3b-opt for 20 minutes.
Set a temporary autoscaler quota / slow warm path to simulate resource provisioning delay (reduce warm pool growth to 30% of normal for a 5-minute window).
Observe accept-queue depth in api-gateway, worker prefetch latencies, and serving-runtime watchdog logs for GPU stall thresholds.
2026-03-10T18:05:12Z apigw[edge-01] WARN accept_queue_size=620 route=/v1/chat status=queueing
2026-03-10T18:07:01Z autoscaler[controller] INFO scale_event=requested=18 provisioned=6 reason=quota-throttle wait=120s
2026-03-10T18:08:45Z runtime[worker-3] ERROR watchdog: gpu_stall=12.8s -> evicting task id=xx34; initiating process-restart
2026-03-10T18:09:03Z apigw[edge-01] ERROR upstream_response=502 backend=serving-runtime-3 trace=trace-9f2a
2026-03-10T18:15:22Z kvcache[embed-shard] WARN eviction_lag=340ms prefetch_lock=true
Checked autoscaler logs: multiple scale requests were queued; cloud quota API returned 429 for instance creation between 18:06-18:10 UTC.
Serving-runtime logs show repeated watchdog-triggered process restarts with stack traces pointing to long GPU kernel stalls (nvml timeout observed intermittently).
NVMe iowait spikes correlated with background snapshotting of embedding shard at 18:04-18:09 — this increased prefetch latency and caused request processing backlog.
API gateway metrics show hedged retries increased 8x as accept_queue > 500; gateway retries contributed to runtime fanout amplification.
We reproduced a smaller-scale version in staging by throttling warm pool growth; results matched production behaviour (accept queue growth -> runtime eviction).

Additional notes:
2026-03-12 11:02 - Runtime team: Deployed hotfix to runtime to delay watchdog eviction threshold by 30% and add a soft-shed path to return 429/503 gracefully before process restart. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
Temporary actions applied: (1) Emergency per-tenant rate limit for ClearMind AI on embed/chat routes; (2) Rolling restart of affected runtime workers to clear GPU/NVML state; (3) Increase prewarm pool for us-east-1 to reduce cold starts; (4) Customer-side backoff recommended. These reduced 5xx rate from ~35% to <2% for the impacted routes within ~25 minutes.
SRE: Work with cloud provider to remove transient quota throttling and investigate instance creation latency (owner: Marco Ruiz).
Runtime: Analyze core dumps and GPU driver traces to determine root cause of nvml timeouts (owner: Jillian Kim).
Autoscaler: Add a better backpressure signal from api-gateway accept-queue to the scaler to avoid scale amplification (owner: Priya Desai).
Product/Platform: Add route-level automatic graceful-shed path to return 429 when accept_queue exceeds configurable threshold (owner: Tom Nguyen).
Work in progress. Immediate customer impact mitigated with temporary rate limits and prewarm increase. Hotfix to graceful-shed behavior merged and scheduled for canary rollout (us-east-1) on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. Awaiting deeper analysis of NVML timeouts and cloud quota events for permanent root cause. Pending follow-ups tracked in action_items.
payload.summary: Evening 5xx surge: API gateway backlog + autoscaler slow-warm causing upstream runtime crashloop

payload.description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightPath Analytics observed a sudden increase in 429 rate-limit errors during a scheduled bulk embeddings job between 02:10-02:37 UTC on 2026-03-10. The job processes ~15M text segments nightly.

Impact:
- Multiple customers using the same public API key (shared SaaS workload) experienced transient 429s and retries, causing the BrightPath job to stretch from its normal 25 minutes to ~3 hours.
- No data loss reported; retries completed but with degraded throughput and higher cost.

Environment:
- prod-us-east
- API: /v1/embeddings (hosted public API)
- Customer tier: self_serve (BrightPath)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Kick off large multi-threaded embedding job (15M text segments) using our public API key and default concurrency.
2. After ~5k requests, clients start receiving intermittent 429 responses.
3. Client-side retry logic succeeds but with exponential backoff, dramatically increasing overall run time.

Relevant logs & metrics:
- Spike in 429s visible on token-level and route-level dashboards starting 02:10 UTC (correlates to a short latency increase on api-gateway).
- Route rate limiter logs show a surge of allowed burst requests then enforcement; a small percentage of requests hit per-account rate limits before the global rate limiting enforcement stabilized.
- No corresponding spike in CPU/GPU of serving-runtime nodes; autoscaling did not trigger.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: a misconfigured burst window in the API gateway combined with an unusual traffic burst pattern from a handful of high-concurrency clients.
- Related config: recent gatekeeper change (K8s configmap) rolled 2026-03-09 adjusted per-route burst thresholds for embeddings-route.
- Correlated with a scheduled third-party ingest that started at 02:05 UTC from BrightPath; their job concurrency briefly exceeded expected limits.
- Observed that token-bucket refill rates applied per-route and per-account had overlapping enforcement which caused an oscillation when many clients retried simultaneously.

Workaround applied:
- Temporarily raised per-account burst allowance for embeddings-route for affected customers (BrightPath + two similar accounts) at 03:00 UTC, which reduced 429s and allowed the jobs to complete.
- Enabled a short-lived adaptive backoff on the API gateway to smooth retry storms.

Next steps / proposed fix:
- Short term: keep elevated per-account burst allowance for 24 hours while we complete a root-cause analysis.
- Medium term: introduce a jittered retry guidance and client-side SDK update to spread retries, plus a soft-queue on the gateway to absorb retry storms.
- Long term: rework rate-limiter coordination between per-account and per-route token buckets to avoid oscillatory enforcement under large concurrent retries.

Related artifacts:
- Related GitHub experiment PR: pr-4217-experiment-adaptive-batching-simulator (used for load modeling).
- Confluence runbook referenced: CON-8234-embedding-route-rate-limiting (link: https://confluence.internal/CON-8234).
payload.summary: Unexpected rate limit spike causing 429s for bulk embedding job

Issue summary: Several staff on floor 3 (printer island A/B/C) report intermittent failures when submitting print jobs. Jobs appear in the client queue but never reach the printer; sometimes jobs error with a network timeout or 'printer not found'.

Impact: Low-medium operational impact; employees are using floor printers for contracts and physical sign-offs. Reported across 6 users over the last 48 hours; not a full outage but recurring and disruptive.

Environment: On-prem office network, wired VLAN 12 (office-devices), printers are HP LaserJet managed via local print server (windows-printsvc-03). Office DHCP and printer IPs appear stable. Printers are assigned static reservations.

Steps to reproduce:
1. From a macOS or Windows client on VLAN 12, submit a 20-page print job to Printer-Island-A.
2. Observe that the job appears in the local client queue.
3. Wait 30-120s; some jobs remain queued and eventually error with timeout OR disappear from client queue without printing.
4. From the print server, check active spool and filter logs for job id.

Logs/observations:
- Windows print server (windows-printsvc-03) shows frequent 'spooler timeout' entries around 10:23–10:45 on 2025-11-11.
- Printer diagnostics show occasional small packet loss on management interface (snmp ping latency spikes to 300ms) but connectivity returns.
- No DNS changes or recent network maintenance recorded in the ticket history for that time window.
- Affected users are both wired and wireless on the same VLAN; guest VLAN unaffected.

Hypothesis: Intermittent network congestion or managed switch flaps on the office floor are causing SMB/LPD sessions to drop mid-spool. Alternatively, print spooler on windows-printsvc-03 may be hitting resource limits under specific job sizes.

Temporary workaround: Ask users to re-submit smaller batched jobs (split larger docs). If urgent, use the single-office color printer with direct USB queue (manual).

Next steps (proposed):
- Engineering: collect and attach spooler logs for 2025-11-11 through 2025-11-13 (Miguel).
- Networking: enable interface error counters and port-level logging for switch-shelf-3B for 72 hours (NetOps).
- Ops: attempt a controlled restart of windows-printsvc-03 spooler during low-hours (overnight maintenance window).

Related artifacts: link to temporary diagnostics doc: drive:shared/office-it/printer-diagnostics-2025-11 (placeholder).

Additional notes:
2025-11-14 - NetOps (Liam O'Connor): Observed CRC errors on switch-shelf-3B port 12 at 10:24 on 2025-11-11. Port flapped twice, correlated with one reported failure. Will enable granular port logging and monitor for 72h.

Issue summary: Several branch builds on the internal CI pool intermittently fail during the `docker pull` step with transient 502/503 errors from the internal registry. Impact: ~10-15% of branch builds on the shared staging agent pool fail, causing developer churn and reruns. Not hitting production yet but reproducible on feature branches. Occurs since ~2026-03-18 after a routine registry config push. Expected: agents pull base images reliably. Actual: docker pull exits with non-EOF network errors and occasional TLS handshake failures.
Trigger a branch CI build on staging using the shared agent pool (e.g., feature/* PR).
Observe the pipeline step that performs `docker pull` for base image (node:18-slim or our internal base).
Failures are intermittent; rerunning the same job often succeeds within 1-2 retries.
Mar 20 09:03:12 agent-17 docker[1234]: Error response from daemon: received unexpected HTTP status: 502 Bad Gateway
Mar 20 09:03:12 agent-17 dockerd[998]: pull failed: Get "https://registry.internal.redwood/api/v2/": net/http: TLS handshake timeout
Mar 21 14:21:04 agent-03 build-script: WARNING: docker pull returned exit code 1; retrying (1/3)

Proxy logs show increased 502 responses aligning with increased pull concurrency after 04:00 UTC (scheduled nightly matrix jobs).
No auth failures in registry logs; upstream connectivity to artifact storage (S3 backend) shows transient 503 errors around the same timestamps.
Mitigation: increased proxy replicas and added a conservative client-side retry in the CI job manifest. Long-term: plan to decouple heavy nightly matrix builds to a dedicated pool and harden registry backend retry behavior. Work remains: track and validate for 72 hours, then schedule a follow-up change to move large dep pulls to a cache layer.

Issue summary: Customer reports that their March invoice contains an unexpectedly large charge attributed to text-generation tokens. They claim most of their workload is embeddings and a small streaming chat integration.

Impact: Potential billing dispute, customer is evaluating whether to pause Dedicated capacity. Financial impact reported ~$9k over expected month-to-date.

Environment: Dedicated tenant in us-east running pinned model gpt-4o-redwood-13b for chat routes; embeddings routed to embedding-ada-2 via a separate endpoint.

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Customer runs batched embedding jobs (low token usage) and intermittent chat streams (small convo).
2) Billing report shows large generation token counts starting 2026-03-02.
3) Customer supplied request ids and sample request timestamps (included in comments).

Investigation notes / logs:
- Initial billing export attached by customer shows line-level usage matching request ids: request-20260302-7a2, request-20260305-1f9, request-20260312-cc3.
- Internal query of request logs shows multiple replayed requests from the routing proxy between 03-02 and 03-05 (suspected retry storm).
- Proxy logs show 5xx responses to client followed by automatic client-side retries that were not deduplicated by the gateway, leading to repeated generation calls.
- Embedding endpoint logs appear normal.

Preliminary hypothesis: a client-side retry loop combined with gateway behavior caused duplicate generation requests that were billed. Need to confirm deduplication and idempotency semantics for streaming calls and check accounting aggregation windows.

Next steps proposed:
- Support: collect full request id list and timestamps from customer (actioned).
- Eng (api-gateway): validate deduplication logic for long-poll/streaming routes; check if retries are recorded as billable.
- Billing: run reconciliation to aggregate duplicate request ids and flag potential credits if duplication is confirmed.

References: related internal issue INT-332 (routing-retry-analysis), and a recent experimental PR pr-4217 that changes adaptive-batching timeouts (might be relevant).

2026-03-17 Eng-sre note (L. Chen): Pulled gateway logs for 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-06. Observed repeated 500s from a rate-limited downstream and subsequent client retries. Need billing to check whether each retry was billed separately (likely yes).

payload.description:
Issue summary: Third-floor shared printers (two devices: HP-LaserJet-3A and Brother-MFC-3B) intermittently drop from the office network and DNS. This causes print jobs to queue and fail, impacting ~10-15 users in that zone.

Impact: Blocks printing for small teams and interferes with on-site demos and hardware sign-off. Not affecting production services, but causing recurring user support tickets.

Environment: On-prem office LAN, Cisco switch stack on floor 3, DHCP+internal DNS, VLAN 20 (office), static IP assignment via DHCP reservation for printers.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Print job submitted from Mac or Windows workstation on VLAN 20.
2) Job queues for several minutes, then fails with "printer unreachable".
3) Devices show as offline in the printer UI and respond to pings intermittently.
4) After 2–10 minutes device returns to network and queued jobs print.

Recent logs and observations:
- Switch logs (03/12-03/16) show short flaps on ports 3/21 and 3/22 correlating to HP-LaserJet-3A and Brother-MFC-3B (link-state flaps 10–30s).
- DHCP server logs show lease renewals around same timestamps.
- DNS entries briefly fail to resolve to the reserved IP, client fallbacks attempt direct IP which also times out.
- No power cycling observed in camera footage; both devices have latest vendor firmware (checked 2026-02).

Attempts so far:
- Rebooted printers and switch stack (03/11 restart) — temporary improvement for ~24 hours.
- Replaced patch cables for both printers (03/13).
- Confirmed firmware up to date and vendor known issues check (no known matching bug).
- Scoped DHCP lease durations; increased lease TTL to 24h as test (no effect).

Hypothesis: Intermittent link flapping likely due to switch port or SFP module; could be temperature-related or power-supply hiccup on switch. Alternate hypothesis is ARP/DNS cache misbehavior on the DHCP/DNS server causing short resolution outages.

Next steps / proposed remediation:
- Swap the switch SFP/module for stack member A to isolate hardware (owner: Networking).
- Move printers temporarily to spare ports on different switch member and monitor for 72 hours.
- Enable enhanced debug logging on DHCP/DNS server for VLAN 20 for another 48h.
- If hardware swap doesn't resolve, schedule vendor support ticket with switch vendor and open SUP ticket for DHCP/DNS investigation.

Owner / point of contact: Elena Martinez (Facilities/IT); please coordinate with Networking (A. Chen) and Office Ops (M. Lopez).
payload.summary: Office printer network flapping on 3rd floor - intermittent DNS failures
